name: Red Solstice 2: Survivors
detailed_description: SEASON PASS About the Game Plan your strategy and undertake real-time combat missions, in this sequel to the best-selling tactical game Red Solstice! Welcome Executor! It's the year 117 After Earth and you have a very important mission. You were awakened to lead the Cell, a secret taskforce that was assembled to counter the threat of the STROL mutant invasion. Take command of your squad to fight the mutants and find a cure to the virus that threatens to end mankind. Across both a deep strategy layer and engaging real time combat missions, you'll need to make decisions quickly to survive in this hostile world and determine the fate of the planet. Choose your mission, select your loadout, take to the battlefield, and lead your squad to victory. Playable in single-player or co-op with up to seven friends, Red Solstice 2: Survivors combines tense claustrophobic action with careful strategic planning to create a sci-fi experience like no other. KEY FEATURES Red Solstice 2: Survivors is playable with the classic Real-Time Strategy controls. These controls provide a lot of freedom, more control and they allow the player to learn proactive actions which are to plan, execute and improvise. Survival Strategy: Red Solstice 2: Survivors combines tactical missions with ongoing survival against the STROL virus. Explore the entire planet in a campaign that expands over time with a single goal - survival of humanity. Research technologies: Research and upgrade new technologies and use them on the battlefield. Real Time Tactical Battlefield: Fight in an open battlefield in real time, while adapting and making plans on the move. Combat Missions: Deploy alone or with other players into combat missions to contain the spreading biomass infection. Manage your resources, explore an open map and secure areas in order to save humanity. Three Mission Types: Over 15 main missions and more than 20 side missions, with each having a different mission type (exploration, stealth and survival). Unique Classes: Choose between 6 classes, each with a unique gameplay experience – Assault, Demolition, Heavy Support, Marksman, Medic and Recon. 8 Player Co-op: Join campaigns and combat missions from other players – or let them join yours. Play together and work towards the survival of the planet. Powerful Weapons: Cause mass destruction, wipe out battlefields and decimate entire colonies. Biomass Infestation: Fight the spreading threat which changes the environment and adapts to your actions. 'It all looks like fighting StarCraft’s Zerg, only up-close and personal...' Rock Paper Shotgun 'In other words, it seems to be taking the base-operating and mission elements from titles like XCOM.' WCCFTech

_childDocuments_.review: So far I'm really enjoying it.Graphics are good for a game like this.I'm here for the multiplayer. _childDocuments_.review: This game is so underrated! I held so long on buying it because of mixed reviews. If only I knew!This is action xcom! And there is loads of action.As someone that loves strategy the geoscape layer with resource management and research and mission prioritization was an awesome surprise. I thought I had bought a pure top down action game. Instead I was surprised with a great implementation of the xcom type strategy. The story has all the usual tropes but it does not disappoint one bit as the cheeziness actually gives it charm.Lots of classes and hundreds of equipment/skill combinations.Totally recommend this game!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is quite unique, I think its one of the most boring game I've ever played.The part that is unique is that it is deceptive, on the surface it seems polished and well made, but oh boy... the actual game feels made by someone that had some checkboxes to tick but no idea of what the fun part of the game was supposed to be.You can afk for the first 12 hours of the game on normal difficulty, literally just click on a spot to go, your marine group will get there and do everything on their own without any input from you. Every map 12 hours in is the same, upgrades feel meaningless, since there is no challenge curve. You are dropped into these maps where there is exploration to be done, a bit of a sandbox, but there is barely any reward for exploring.  You have an inventory of 5 items, the items are again meaningless given the lack of difficulty scaling, and none are fun.So when I say its deceptive, I found myself giving the game more patience because it felt like there was more there, perhaps I just have not understood the game loop, perhaps when the difficulty rises actions are meaningful. It has a strategic layer that feels unique xcom like. But nah, 12 hours in there is nothing new nothing interesting, just rinse and repeat send your marines, they will constantly get attacked by uninteresting enemies, go to the waypoints, extract.If steam gave awards to bad games, this would no doubt win the most boring game ever made, don't waste your time there is nothing here for you.

The more you learn to use the AI in Solo the better each mission gets and you can really start to knock out those side quests they throw at you past wave 10+

_childDocuments_.review: I'd rate this game as neutral if I could. I used to love the Night of the Dead map on WC3 back when I was a kid. This game definitely has those vibes, but also has a few annoyances.First, the tutorial stuff. It sounds like this has improved a lot since launch (reviews say there way no tutorial before), but the tutorial stuff is incredibly dull. Rather than learning by doing, you are bombarded with notification screens. You get into the world map on the campaign and immediately have to click through 9 notification panels. Then you get to a mission and have to click through 3 more. Then your soldier setup and there's another 2-3. This is NOT how to teach people how to play your game. Let me get into the game, and let me learn by doing with a gradual buildup in complexity and some highlights showing players where the key things are on the screen. DON'T give me a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ novel to read.Second, there seems to be some annoying technical issues. I put this game on my HD rather than SSD and it takes an age to boot up. I tried using the Steam feature to migrate the game to my SSD and the move failed. I don't have that issue with other games. In the game itself I've not encountered any bad bugs/glitches though.Third, the practices of the devs are really questionable. They put up a post recently saying all DLC is out and now they're focusing on addressing feedback etc. Wtf guys, how about addressing feedback and making a solid game first, rather than letting the game languish for over a year, sat at middling reviews. I got this game on a really good sale; no way I'd have taken the chance of buying this for full price given the reviews. Devs, might have a decent playerbase to sell DLC to right now if you took the "make the game good first" route, rather than trying to nickle and dime the couple hundred(?) active players with DLC when the game's full price already feels like too much.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Solstice 2: Survivors

_childDocuments_.review: This is currently my favorite game to play. There is just something so satisfying about positioning your AI team in a building while using the combat engineer to set-up a series of cannons, drones and electric fences to attempt to hold back the tide of the infected. The wave system is insanely fun and it really makes each deployment feel like a ticking time bomb of impending chaos. I have had several close calls with extractions that look straight out of a movie: hundreds of mutants while my team is rappelling back up to the dropship. Straight out of Starship troopers. I haven't tried multiplayer yet.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: The original review can be found below. I am glad to see that a Developer has taken a keen interest in my review. It is always nice to know that sometimes reviews reach out to the right people and can be addressed. In all fairness, I would like to update my review to reflect the changes made and the communication by the development team. Seeing as how my initial review pointed out balancing issues in multiplayer and an option has been implemented, I would recommend RS2 for co-op. I rarely purchase games for single player content and felt that it was important that the host and I could start with the same progress. So I'd like to thank the development team for adding this feature. As far as skirmish missions go, it is nice to see that there is different task to complete. Overall, I would recommend this game.Found this game on the Steam Store page and thought I would give it a try. After messing around for a few hours, I've come to the realization that this game is not worth $30. I say this because it's actually disappointing for the price. When you first start a campaign and run through the tutorial, you get a sense of the basic controls and finally make your way into the campaign menu with the over-world view. It's here that you can go into the armory and customize your character. Seemingly, the only two classes that you start with are Assault and Medic. Which would be fine normally, but as I was playing multiplayer with someone; I began to see how unfair and unbalanced it is for campaign. The host has to research various things through the campaign to unlock the other classes and weapons, while the player who joined the campaign match can level his profile and have things unlocked from the start. There is a work around where you can just fast forward time by scanning and making the timer go down to have the unlocks before you start missions, but then the infestation level becomes too high. Making the missions more difficult for two players. Especially those new to the game. So then I tried Skirmish mode. Much to contrary of the campaign issue, both players can fully customize their character from the start. Great. Now the only problem with that is it then became boring. Activate overwatch and right click your way through the map as you escort a convoy. Most of the weapons are not great and it sounds like having everything at your disposal had taken the fun away, right? Wrong. What was fun about the campaign was the objectives on the missions and the length. If the multiplayer concept had been developed better, I might would recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Tried so hard to look past the issues, but they're glaring and unacceptable for a full release. Games livelyhood is its multiplayer, and even though it's literally unfathomable to me how their Closed tests performed better, the servers since full release have been absolutely atrocious between the lag and just straight bugging out. Can't place nukes if i'm host.. why? How? Wasn't an issue in testing... so many little things just clutter the bigger picture to the point where it's entirely gone.Spent 40-60 hours across multiple tests, and 150h+ on the first TRS, loved all of it and the testing just led me to believe we were going to be getting a more fleshed out version of it. Somehow, all of the bloatware mechanics they added with story just brought the entire rest of the game down however. I truly don't understand the focus on the single-player content when the games main draw is its strategic team-play. The "strategy layer" is basically just a badly done x-com overworld map, a lot of the systems are badly explained and it's a trial-and-error experience, was frustrating but whatever, skirmish is what I wanted so sub-par single is perfectly fine if not expected. Boy does that singeplayer look like a nice healthy apple in the middle of a famine now, I truly don't understand how the mark was so completely missed. Had my concerns after learning Terminator(fav from trs1)/Hellfire were getting delayed past launch but having played multiple tests, I knew(hah) the game would still be amazing and the wait would be worth it. That turned around fairly quickly. Just so sad to see the state of this launch especially after the 7 month delay from their first delay.Hoping future patches fix up server stability and improve on the numerous bugs. I get the feeling even if the game does get completely fixed it'll be dead at that point however. Really needed a strong launch to bring in a variety of new players, as is it's just going to follow the route of the first game and fade into obscurity which is a shame because when the game actually works it's wonderful, it's just few and far inbetween currently.

_childDocuments_.review: I find this game to be very interesting and fun. If you play it single player it's basically like star ship troopers meets Xcom. Fighting hordes of mutants in an XCOM like campaign setup. Like literally Xcom. I have not gotten far into the game but the little bit that I have played is really enjoyable. The campaign map regions are spread across the entire planet so seemingly there is alot of content to try out. I look forward to trying out the 8 player coop. Only thing that made the tutorial worth playing was learning how the movement worked. It is a point and click to move while either manually aiming or having your character in "overwatch mode" which auto fires at enemies. Which may sound lame but its pretty cool. You auto aim your secondary and then manual aim your primary weapons. (chain shotguns, missle launchers, snipers, flame throwers). While navigating a warzone rescuing, escorting, destroying, stuff.Having played a few multiplayer matches I can explain the general idea. Basically you drop into a map and have various objectives to complete.Prior to this you select the Skirmish mode and then can either host or join servers. It seems to be a smaller community but you have no issues getting a full group of 8. The real issue is that the host will not be able to start the match until all 8 people hit the ready button making some people hold up the lobby potentially. Past that the various classes all have their perks, pros and cons and play styles. Heavy is slow but can be good with crowd control. Medic literally keeps everyone alive. Snipers can deal MASSSIVE damage. Recon grabs everyone resources etc.Speaking of classes from what I understand your profile levels up as you play both single player and online. You then get points to give out in your multiplayer load. This is how you unlock the desired class you want to play and give it perk, weapons and abilities. I find that the reset your perks is to costly and should be reduced to not effect you. There have been times where I just got to level 50 or something and gone down to 49. I do not think they should penalize you for trying to explore classes. BTW settles on HEAVY. mini gun go's bRRRRRRRRRRRThe team compositions seem to always be random, missions + difficulty + resource management REALLY effect the success of the team. Basically the best way to do early game is split off into smaller groups and loot all the houses so you can have gear/ammo for situations later on. Then once the hordes REALLY start coming to form up and work together.I really really really enjoy the game play. With time I hope they fix little bugs and certain pieces of equipment that bug out. Add more missions and game modes. and improve performance. (cus why not)I think with time and updates this game will only get better.

_childDocuments_.review: I've gotten some play time out of this and enjoyed it for the most part, so I'll give it a thumbs up, especially for its price tag.If you're fine with lots of bugs, some balance issues and weird issues with new content releases which are fixed between a week to a month later, then this is a pretty solid game.  It'd be an awesome game if it wasn't constantly tripping over itself with every content release.Singleplayer is serviceable with bots if you build them and use them right.  There are a lot of "wrong" builds which will make playing singleplayer with bots miserable until the "right" builds are discovered.  Every game mode can also be played online coop with friends or strangers, which tends to make the experience more interesting.The DLC isn't necessary unless you want to play the new classes. Everything else can be experienced by joining someone else's lobby.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Solstice 2: Survivors

_childDocuments_.review: Campaign side will likely take a bit of time for several to get use to, especially as the host has to plan out their actions from choosing their battles down to how they wish to plan out things for the war against strol forces overall. With the added the satisfaction of going in there to take out stroll with either your friends or troops in a real time battle. You even get to test out several suits and to their abilities, getting use to it even before you unlock them all in the profile tree skirmish side; so you get an idea of how that functions with enough time unlocking them camapign side by researching it. You also get to build up your profile points on top of things even whilst doing the campaign.Skirmish side to coop side, you can jump right into the battle or link up with others before they're heading out to combat the stroll. If you're looking for a more classic TRS survival to multiplayer, it'll be more on the skirmish side as you get more objectives to complete on randomized maps, whilst focusing on your primary mission chain which will likely lead to overrun fights as you fight through the hoard up till evac; on top of whatever you wish to make it even more challenging. Such as increasing the infestation level for rougher times on biomass and its expanding influence, down fixed waves to add a lot of differing foes for everyone to engage with them coming out in larger hoards to numbers as time goes by.Overall its going to be a blast going through things.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Solstice 2: Survivors

_childDocuments_.review: There's a really solid co-op game experience here, but it's buried under an enormous mountain of jank. Not only is it still bug-ridden after over a year of patches, it still shows major signs of incompleteness, like missing or incoherent ability descriptions. Combined with some ill-advised changes to gameplay mechanics, I'd say that RS2 has actually become less playable over time. I really wish I could recommend this game, but right now the jank outweighs everything good about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Solstice 2: Survivors

_childDocuments_.review: RS2 is an amazing example of a game where the devs clearly had a dream....but lack and real leadership talent to shape that dream into something. instead....they just pooped out this blob...of sadnessThe problem? the game is effectively divided between the single player story line and co-op. in theory the two are supposed to mesh well. in reality... they dont.the single player story line suffers from just god awful writing, voice acting and makes no attempt to really hook the player into caring whats going on. on top of that the story line is supposed to take place while the player is supposed to be desperately fending off the infestation of the enemy across the planet. its supposed to be a delicate balancing act that always leaves the player on the edge. it doesnt.....the terrible story line leaves you mad that you are having to waste your time fighting back the infestation for a planet you just dont care about. by the end....if you make it that far.... your attitude is just nuke them all and let god sort them out.this balancing act was a tall order even for the best game devs...these took a dive into the deep end of the pool and flat out drowned.so now half the games resources have been wasted on a crap single player mode.the co-op is where this game should have really shined...but it didnt. with all  the dlc included you have whats called a "skirmish" profile with a vast array of a bunch of abilities and talents you can level up.  theres a lot of rewarding grind here...but its all wasted. what little of co-op there is in terms of maps difficulties what not is in fact pretty goodafter awhile you start to notice the dead ends of co-op. ability trees that lack balance, classes that are more usesless than anything really. it becomes pretty obvious that resources that could have been used to flesh out the co-op into something pretty respectable were instead stripped away to beef the god awful single player campaign. so now you have a co-op that is at best meh.DLCto be fair at the start the devs promised a lot of dlc campaigns and they 100% delivered. the problem? the campaigns are just as garbage as the main story line. they just puke random events and call it story mode that makes little to no sense and it becomes increasingly clear there was not enough bank to make a decent DLC story, so you just have a handful of meaningless missions.is there any reason to get it? some of the DLC offers pretty good classes and gear for your skirmish profile worth the pick up.in the end... the game died. theres virtually no-one online for skirmish maps and the few that are are usually die hards running max diff missions.had the single player campaigns been dumped for a full co-op campaign similar to HellDivers,  the game might have had a meager life and the short comings could have been more easily over looked.the Verdict? if you can get it for free or for 5 bucks pick it up...other wise dont waste your time.

_childDocuments_.review: These days I can't recommend the game anymore, the playerbase has dropped to double digits.The gameplay is still good but there's still longstanding bugs that others and myself reported like 2 years ago, such as the hellfire bot just randomly becoming unresponsive or bots sometimes randomly dissapearing from the game entirely, enemies getting stuck half in the floor, enemies getting bunched up on each other or objects on the map, missions breaking if you interact with a world object too early... the list goes on.I'm pretty sure the publisher has pulled funding for the game and assigned the studio to do other things instead, because while the devs still say they'll do this or that, it's been what feels like 2 years.The combat does feel good though and so do the rpg mechanics and progression system, some people might enjoy the game.So I guess you could get it on like a 75%-80% discount if you're up for enjoying a pretty decent singleplayer squad management game, especially since you can do skirmish with 3 personalized bots under your command as well.-------------------------------------------------------Old review here:I've put about 5 hours into the game now and it's everything it was during the demos/betas but better, more enemies, more sound effects, better fleshed out UI.There were some multiplayer issues on launch day, but what game doesn't have that these days and they released a hotfix the same day to resolve most of it.For what it's worth the campaign is pretty flawless, haven't run into any bugs yet and the fact that it gets randomly created missions thrown in (which other people can join) makes it very replayable!I think compared to TRS1 this will make it a lot more appealing to the general crowd as well, by simply being more accessible and easier to use.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Solstice 2: Survivors

_childDocuments_.review: The game isn't finished and it released too early, It should probably still be listed as early access. Balance changes are being made among weapons and classes, chunks of content that probably should have been present at launch are in development. Lots of mission ending bugs still around. The devs seem to patch pretty often and have an active discord so maybe they'll get it hammered out.My experience was 100% in solo campaign mode and it just wasn't well put together. The campaign mode is an Xcom 2 map laid over what feel like multiplayer quickplay missions. Outside of the few main story set-piece missions, they're all randomly generated with 1 main objective and infinitely generating side missions as you do the actual top down shooting. I'm OK with that as a concept but there's like 5 of these objective types and they all boil down to go here and shoot. There's even fewer maps to do these limited number of missions on. I ended my 30 hour campaign when it became 5 runs of an identical mission back-to-back as my colonies got infested.The combat might as well be a timed on-rails shooter, because the longer you take the harder enemies the game spawns. Which forces you to run as directly to objectives as you can because of the second big problem, the bot companions. The AI companions leave the player to do 99% of the heavy lifting. They don't do enough damage or have enough skills to deal with anything bigger than trash enemies without direct player intervention. Doubling down on this is the enemy mechanics where you have to debuff harder enemies' insane healing or armor before you can kill them. The bot classes generally can't debuff at all, and mostly fail to do so correctly even if you bring a bot that can. This would be mitigated in multiplayer where you can synergize classes but the bot classes literally do not have the same options available as the player. They get simple versions of some of the class skills, can't carry as big of weapons, have limited suit upgrades and can't use items at all. To top it off you only get 3 of them with you, restricting your choices further.The biggest issue with the game is that nothing is explained, players are left to guess at huge portions of game mechanics. Infestation on the campaign map, what research does, what rewards you get from missions, damage types, debuffs. The game doesn't even tell you how to get ammo for your companions, because apparently they run out of ammo and that isn't mentioned anywhere. (They get magic ammo from opening lockers)I don't want to count the number of times i had to search the dev's discord for information about things that absolutely should have been explained in game or been in the tutorial. I have hundreds of hours in similar games and this game had me blindly guessing at core gameplay features the entire time.I really like the idea of this game and bought into it because of its Warcraft III / Starcraft 2 custom map heritage but it's just disappointing. There's no way i could recommend this to any of my friends in its current state.

_childDocuments_.review: The latest incarnation of the old NOTD mods for Warcraft/Starcraft; I, and many others, have enjoyed this punishing, real time, tactical, squad based mission game type that is rarely replicated elsewhere, so there is bias -- there are a number of fans that would accept nearly any game, even if in piss poor state, if it contains this gameplay.That said, this game is not in piss poor state, but it does have some aspects that you must be able to look past if you want to fully enjoy it.The gameplay/modes are difficult -- success is rare in full skirmish mode with proper difficulty settings.  There are bugs, sadly -- I have not run into major ones, but others certainly have.  Devs made some strange design choices related to coop experience in campaign and progression -- it seems more designed right now for drop in coop rather that a full coop campaign experience (skirmish was always the favored default mode of the game, though; campaign, and with coop to boot, was always seen by the community as a bonus).Regardless, this is, thus far, one of the best implementations of the NOTD style gameplay, both in technical terms and in accessibility.  Great, challenging, multiplayer heavy, tactical experience that you simply are not getting anywhere else.

_childDocuments_.review: Red Solstice 2 is a fantastic and successful iteration upon Red Solstice. It is spiritually and mechanically the same game, with the rough parts sanded/smoothed/insert appropriate metaphor here. If you liked the first one, stop reading here and just buy it and play it.Red Solstice 2 is still something of a "slow start" game. There's a distinct learning curve and options at the beginning are fairly limited. A lot of the negative reviews have less than 2 hours of playtime in a game that takes at least 4 to really get rolling. RS2 doesn't really spend any time holding your hand and keeping you safe from the bad things (ammo mismanagement, explosively happy teammates, bad choices, bad loadout design, etc). The flipside of this coin is that, as a player, you have a huge amount of freedom to dictate how you interact with the game.Where RS2 shines is in the freedom for the player to dictate how they interact with the game through their loadout choices. There are several roles that need to be filled on a squad to see success, and the devs let players decide how to fill those roles (Medic is probably the only real pigeon holed class). In an attempt to avoid overloading the player with choice and information, the initial choices presented to the player are fairly limited.An important thing to understand about Red Solstice 2 is that it is a multiplayer game that can be played single player (but is infinitely better and more fun by dragging more people into it), but because there's a "campaign mode" people are expecting that to be basically stand alone (it can be, but its missing the magic of what makes RS2 good).Waxing on, the campaign brings a delightful amount of variation to the content experienced in the skirmish multiplayer. The missions are shorter (one of the big issues from RS1 is that games are typically 40-90 minutes long) and more varied. One mission involved pushing across an infested dam in a tight, intense experience.As a final point, the devs are extremely active and responsive to the community. Most of the day one reviews (with playtimes under 2 hours) were complaining about bugs that were fixed within 24 hours of launch. They chat with the community, offer personal tech support, discuss design and ideas, it's everything you could ask from a dev team.Overall, RS2 is just a better game than RS1. I struggle to pick a specific area where the first one outshines its successor, maybe just the price tag?

_childDocuments_.review: Red Solstice 2 reminds me of the good old days from Warcraft 3's custom game - Night of the Dead (NOTD).It can be challenging on the harder difficulties with good coordination needed between teammates.Its can be fun playing solo but the game emphasized on teamwork so it becomes amazing with friends with great replayability in terms of challenge.Now to note, Red Solstice 2 is NOT a twin stick shooter like Alien Swarm. The camera controls are like the controls of most modern RTS or strategy games like Total War - WSAD and you mainly control 1 character in the likes of most MOBAs with point and clicks while using abilities and items through hotkeys. You can manually aim your shots like the skillshots in some MOBAs.In terms of gameplay, you either join or host your own session with up to 8 players, choosing the map, difficulty and other parameters. Currently there are around 5 maps (iirc). Difficulty ranges from Easy > Normal > Hard > Very Hard > Nightmare. You choose your class out of 6 different classes each with their own abilities. You select the weapon and abilities that are suitable to your playstyle and head into game.In game, you collect equipment and complete objectives and side missions while enemy spawns with an ever increasing number and varieties as the game stretches on. How fast enemies spawn and how many enemies spawn are dependent on the settings.In terms of progression, you gain experience as you play and you can use the points to unlock classes, weapons, abilities and equipment.Overall, I would say Red Solstice 2 is a great game and I hope to see more contents developed for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Red Solstice 2, a very interesting take on the stratagy/rpg genre, and a good one at that.While the game has some bumps, it is certainly a stride from its lesser counterpart.Yes there are some bugs, however not very many that make the game unplayable.Aside from that, the multiplayer aspect seems on the down low at the moment, though regardless, there is a single player mode that makes the game withstand-able while we wait for the future updates.There is a fairly large (in some aspect) arsenal of weapons, skills, gear, and system upgrades to work with. However there is no weapon customisation (in case you were wondering).For a recently released game in 2021, it certainly has met a higher mark then many others, though still has a ways to go content wise.In all, a strong foundation with a stronger open road ahead of it.This is defiantly a game I didn't see myself playing as it isn't apart of my normal genre preference, though regardless, it meets a well placed expectation.I suggest picking it up if you haven't played any genre like this before, or are looking for something more hands on then Helldivers.I look forward to what this game has in store for us in the future.Let it be said that this game is by no means Easy.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommended!TRS2 is an awesome Isometric, sci-fi, class-based, cooperative PVE strategy game. The multiplayer (skirmish) feature of the game supports up to 8-player teams, you control a single "hero" in a fireteam who's role and combat suit are all of your design. TRS2 also has campaigns, which can be played cooperatively with friends as well.I'm not sure what to call the genre, I think of them as "strategic RPGs." There's not a lot of games out there that offer the experience the Red Solstice series provides. If you played the first Red Solstice, or are familiar with some of the co-op maps from Starcraft Arcade or WC3 such as the multitude of NOTD versions, you'll definitely know what to expect from this game.I put a lot of time into TRS1 (one of my favorite games on Steam), it stubbornly took me a couple years to finally give TRS2 a serious try. I'm only about 60hrs in and still quite a "rookie"--which is something I enjoy about this genre--the amount of game knowledge required for a good chance of survival in higher difficulties. TRS2 is definitely a bit more forgiving in this regards though, which I think makes this title more appealing to a larger audience. Some key differences that stick out to me immediately, compared to the first title:- Fog of war <3- In depth mission/session difficulty customization- (Very) Dynamic suit/class build system- Built on a modern game engine--extremely improved visuals and sound design- Shorter sessions, on average 30-40 minutes in my experience (but can be longer depending on mission setup)- Ability to hot-join games in progress (!!!)- Mistakes and errors in game-play are a bit more forgiving- Faster player revives- *Very* easy-to-manage bot-players the lobby host can control, if you're lacking human-players- New weapons, classes and skills (along with the classics)My overall impression is that TRS2 favors action-oriented game play, over the slower-burn strategic feel of the first game. They're both excellent games though. I recently picked up the DLC as well, which I do not regret. For the amount of time I foresee investing into TRS2 and the entertainment it will provide, the store price tag is really quite modest.I'm really excited to see what Ironward works on next!

_childDocuments_.review: It offers RTS and WASD/Twin-stick controls, you are able and sometimes even should switch on the go to tackle different obstacles.The Game gives you the Bare-bones of a Tutorial introducing you to the controls, cover system and item usage. It does not take you by the Hand and flood you with information, but instead give you a codex with all Information you can read if you need it. This is a learning by doing/failing experience if you don't have someone showing you the ropes.Cooperative multiplayer allows for up to 8 players to play together, especially the higher difficulties needing teamwork and coordination.The game offers a wide array of customizable classes, each with unique abilities and play styles, allowing players to tailor to their preferred strategies. While it is playable Solo with 3 Bots it is a different and sometimes quite difficult experience, and i wouldn't want it any other way as this Game is clearly made for Co-op.Yes there are DLCs and no they are neither a cash-grab nor pay-to-win. No Micro-transactions.Each of the DLCs contained in the Season Pass (Howell-Barrax Inc.,Condatis,Insurgents,MERCS) add a Campaign story of that Faction or their Point of view on the whole conflict and Maps for the skirmish Mode (Both Campaign and the Maps can be played if you join someone who has them)- Combat Engineer (Class)- RIVNIK (Heavy Weapon)- UBAS (usable if it stands around unmanned)- Psychic (Class)- Crusader (Melee Weapon with Shield)- Weapon Modding- Driveable Vehicles (usable if someone else calls them)Again None of it is Pay-to-Win. The Classes and Weapons give way for other play styles and are not overpowered. The Weapon Modding give the option to increase the performance of a weapon, giving drawbacks in return as well as change color and pattern of the weapon.While the Vehicles give great firepower you have to manage the fuel and increased difficulty as each Vehicle counts as one or more Players increasing the amount of Mutants. (Scout car 1, APC 2, Tank 3)tl;trThe Game is Great but

_childDocuments_.review: Game was gifted to me by a friend who was really hopeful of the game. We've all since stopped playing.I got excited when I read reviews that said this was like NoTD (Night of the Dead) from Starcraft 2 arcade , and it is in the same shape yes. You go into a map with a squad , fight zombie like aliens (and a large assortment of mutant dogs for whatever reason) , you do somewhat random objectives , and you extract , earning XP to level skills , buy modules , weapons etc for different classes of space marines. Graphics are pretty good , performance is also good. But that's about where the good things end.Lacking tutorial doesn't teach you anything but basic movement and camera controls. Confusing UI , lots of things lacking quality tool tips. I have no idea what alot of things in the tech/skill tree do or require cause the tooltip doesn't tell me anything. Lots of bugs , seen the spent cartridges from people shooting miniguns cause lag , got trapped in a drop ship once. Campaign story is just some C tier alien colony gone wrong story , and requires having played the first game. You need to have 4+ friends with you to enjoy this game otherwise you're hoping one of the 100 people currently playing join you or host a lobby. Ranking up requires doing certain "challenges" however you cant see what these challenges are until you actually host a game and change the game's settings to whatever is required for the challenge.My biggest complaint about this game vs the Starcraft 2 Arcade map is that in that FREE arcade map enemies (especially bosses) are more than just walking HP bars with varying move speeds. The bosses in NoTD have actual mechanics. Meanwhile just about everything in this game except for one boss is just a big walking HP bar.Season pass costs more than the base game , so that should tell you the direction this is going.

There's a really cool "overwatch" feature that keeps your guy reacting automatically to enemies, so you don't flay around frantically.However I don't agree with other reviewers in here that the game doesn't need other players - IMO the AI players are kinda annoying at most and I would recommend having at least one friend to play it with (which I don't have sadly).However I'd say it's "easily" solvable by having some kind of control over them. _childDocuments_.review: I got this expecting something like Alien Swarm but with more interesting mechanics, but it just isn't fun in the same way. Normal weapons can't friendly-fire so there isn't the same zany fun, and the death mechanic is quite anti-fun: you can respawn on a timer, so everyone respawns individually and dies to the same thing that just killed everyone else. The "co-op campaign" isn't really very co-op: it's more like a game of X-Com that one person plays while the others play as the soldiers.It's a well-executed game: the interaction is pretty smooth, the graphics are reasonably pretty and quite readable, and I didn't find any important bugs when playing. We just didn't really have much fun playing it as a group.

_childDocuments_.review: It's everything I was hoping for in a sequel. Yes, the launch was a rocky, at best. That said, the way the devs responded to the players, and corrected the issues with immediate patches for the most important issues, makes me more hopeful for the future of the game, if anything.Being able to suddenly drop into a friend's Campaign missions to provide extra fire support through a hard section is awesome. Having a team with a friend and 6 other players tearing through swarms of aliens is awesome when it all works right.The looting is almost exclusively for items that are lost at the end of the match, with limited space, so you're encouraged to improvise and use them as you go, or pass extra items to teammates. The game was obviously built with a co-op experience in mind, and it does it well.Bots can currently only be used in the Campaign, but work better than most NPC support I've seen in games. You have the ability to level them up, spec them a bit, customize their equipment and appearance, and give them some rudimentary orders during battle. They're effective enough, that I'm sure they could support you through the Campaign on some difficulties. That said, playing with other players makes the game a lot more fun, and generally works well.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decent squad-level top-down RTS.   Basic Gameplay Overview:  Click to move.  There is a constant visible reminder of where your mission waypoint is, so moving in that general direction is advisable.  However, there are often side missions in the maps for you to find and complete for bonus rewards.   You can turn on "Overwatch" which will make your soldier automatically target and shoot at enemies.  If you manually target an enemy (and you will have to, frequently, as Overwatch does not prioritize enemies efficiently) it detoggles Overwatch.  The enemies are numerous and you will run out of ammunition if you don't scavenge lockers and lootables around the map.  Complete the various objectives in a mission and then extract to complete it.  If a soldier dies or is downed a certain number of times they are permanently dead.   There's a tactical map, like in XCom, where you can select missions, complete research, arm yourself, etc.  I haven't done much with it and it's not as intuitive as I'd like.  I'm enjoying the game thus far (it says I've played for an hour, that's incorrect, more like 3.  Not that that's a lot or anything, but yeah) and look forward to playing it with friends.  The class system is interesting and you can customize your soldier's class/armor class with different abilities and passives.   Having 3-4 people in a squad will be a blast.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very much a contender for "Favorite game you suck at" in the steam awards. It can be quite challenging, but I never felt like I couldn't have done something different to improve my odds. Through experience you learn how to play better much like other games; Monster Hunter for example. Like Monster Hunter; I wouldn't expect a groundbreaking story or anything, but it's far from the worst I've heard. The DLC has a good amount of quantity and quality for the price; I would still recommend the season pass however.The music may be repetitive after 40+ hours but it is definitely fitting. I find I turn the music down and put my own music on in the background now; but that isn't to say don't listen to it. You can play campaign solo, or with friends, or even randoms. You can play "skirmish" which is the multiplayer style mode; but can play without anyone except bots if you want, but also with friends or randoms as an option. The classes feel unique and useful in their abilities where they could go it alone briefly, but ultimately work better in pairs or more and are fairly interchangeable. There is no "You need this on your team." meta I find; yeah a medic is nice, but you can account for the lack of one with items or your loadout in a trade off for firepower or support abilities for example.It's a solid gem in the rough of game that are spotty with their long term support, or buggy as hell. I think I've only had 2 crashes, and I'm pretty sure they were my fault for multitasking my computer too hard. It's a labour of love and a solid top down "stick shooter" style game with strategy instead of hectic carnage.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has potential. Sadly that's wasted by the devs' poor design choices and a toxic community that is somehow incapable of seeing any flaws whatsoever, preferring the tried and true rhetoric of "git gud" and "cope." Things that stand out to me about this game are:#1 the lack of a meaningful progression system.Ignoring the campaign as its progression is totally separate from the other game mode: Skirmish, we have the tech tree. The tech tree has many short branches in different categories. These branches have increasing point costs in an attempt to slow down "progression." Don't be fooled, though. Although I have not tested everything, some higher tier unlocks are worse than their predecessors. Take for example the minigun. A staple of any shooter, yet Ironward thought to shake things up and make it utter garbage. Although on paper the dps is higher than the lmg, the minigun has horrific accuracy. Does this accuracy get better after spinning up? YES...after emptying 75%+ of your magazine. I've done some calculations and the effective dps of the minigun at a moderate range is lower than the lmg. Now carrying on to other aspects of progression, we have the combat suit tech tree. Pitiful really. one of the main instances of solid progression and the numbers are just incredibly low. Extra health? 5 points per rank (with those increasing costs per rank remember) which may be acceptable... IF you had 100 hp base. Nonono...the Heavy for example has 500 hp. that is a WHOPPING 1% increase per rank. Remember that, it's a pattern. Status resistance is 3% per rank, and there's one branch that should be split into dedicated ones, and that contains a 1% speed boost, a 2% damage increase (iirc. it might also be 1%), and a couple small damage resistance upgrades at I believe 3% each for... two? ranks. Now let's move onto the bestiary. Probably more of a late game endeavor, but one can capture monsters in missions for a small stat bonus. There are multiple types of bonuses one can obtain from captures, but the maximum is of course still quite limited. Perhaps 10% damage and similar degrees of boosts to a couple other stats. Sounds good on paper... In reality it's a lot of work for not much reward. Even if it's one of the highest non-module buffs you'll obtain in this game. And last we have the player ranks. There are both ranks and levels in this game. Ranks giving you ever so slight stat buffs like +0.5 energy. While the latter is completely meaningless. Alright so that's the progression system now let's talk about...#2 the difficulty.In my brief foray into what this game has to offer, I have tried the campaign and skirmish, with both having drastically different challenge levels. The campaign seems to feature a slow burn where things start off incredibly easy and ramp up over time. However Skirmish is something else entirely. Multiple times I have tried putting it on the easiest possible difficulty through various mission settings, and yet every time I find little to no ammo, a constant stream of enemies, and frequently disproportionately difficult enemies such as a behemoth on wave 2 and some enemy I failed to identify as a pack of them just ROLLED ME revive after revive with my lmg doing so little damage to them I suspect either their hp regen was 90% my dps OR they just had absolutely MASSIVE health pools. These enemies were also invisible and to kill them was the first objective.Once again I shall mention that I can see the potential of this game. It looks good and has some good shooter rpg elements, but it just flops. The one saving grace could have been a modding community, but this game is unmoddable. There is a built-in anticheat that removes any meaningful modded content. But even if you're like the rest of this garbage community and think "yeah, no cheats in my game!!", that's simply not the case. It is already possible to google a cheat table for this game and EASILY use it in multiplayer. The difference is all the wonderful content that could have been added to the game and even community fixes for poor base game content like the progression system. Honestly it's sad. anyway I'll leave you at that and hope I helped you on your path to find a good game. Cheers.Edit: increased hours due to modding. I am working on getting this game on nexus because I believe mods will make this game 100% more enjoyable for the casual player and expand the small community this game has. At first I failed to realize how limited the anticheat measures were. There's so much more to change than class stats, so although their variability remains elusive for now, it's all good. Excited to see what people come up with. Keep an eye on the nexus for when the page goes up soon!

_childDocuments_.review: A Quick Overview as to this game:TL;DRIf you enjoyed S.W.A.T. Aftermath (the Classic Warcraft 3 Game) or Night of the Dead, or any of those other style games from Warcraft and Starcraft servers then this game is for you. Longer Version:Red Solstice 2 is a tactical squad based primarily MULTIPLAYER centric experience meant to be enjoyed with others.The community is vibrant and friendly, and the developers seem to really be focused on delivering a fun, addictive, fast paced squad based experience that can be tailored to all different challenge ratings.This is a game that if you are into those prior games, or in general RTS Squad Tactic games with some Shooter Elements, it is for you. If you are looking for a Stealth game, or a Detailed Single Player Campaign like Command & Conquer, you are better off looking elsewhere.. although the Campaign does seem very in depth and nuanced, and according to the community the first game had a legendary story that this one is following up on.The Graphics are beautiful and use the Unreal Engine to its full potential, outside of Triple A titles you won't find much better.The game itself is stable, and most of the quality of life enhancements have already been implemented at this 1.0 Release time. The Grind although very existent, is rewarding and worthwhile and you do not need to put in 40 hours to start to contribute. If you are a skilled player, you will easily find yourself welcome and dominating in any setting outside the highest difficulty ratings.There is an extensive perk tree that allows for much customization within the existing classes, with plenty of room and potential for the Devs to expand and grow this system naturally as the game becomes even more threshed out.It is absolutely worth its $30 price tag if these type of games interest you. Thanks and big ups to the Devs for taking this great formula and making it into a Full Title that can be expanded upon and bring more players into this particular Cult Classic Genre!

_childDocuments_.review: Eh, since we're already "Mixed" on release day I'll leave my review here, even though I'm less than 10 hours in. I bought this for multiplayer with friends, first and foremost. I played with one friend tonight and plan on playing with more when we're all online.The way the character unlocks in multiplayer is a little odd. Whoever is the host, and therefore at the beginning of the campaign, has a limited number of unlocks - because it's the beginning of the game.  Whoever joined that game, though, has a long list of available things to unlock - because it's not their game. Honestly this is the right way, because it allows people  to have full access to the game. These people exist, I have one friend who will only play this multiplayer - he'll never touch the campaign on his own. The person hosting, then, is limited to some extent - but they're also unlocking and progressing in their campaign while everyone else who joined is not. They get to perform research, the missions they want, etc. It's a reasonable trade-off. I saw a dev comment they may add an option to allow everyone who joins to be at the same limited level as the host. This may be good for some people, but IMO only if that campaign progress ends up carrying over to all the players. Since there does seem to be static story missions (along with the random missions) if that mode allowed everyone to progress their story mission along with the host, that would be good.  Otherwise it's fine just how it is.As for the gameplay, it's fun. It's real time X-Com with a good number of elements and variables to make the game unique for each person who is playing. And, 8 player co-op!!  This is huge and that alone makes this game fantastic.We experienced no bugs tonight. The game ran well.  Ultimately no complaints whatsoever. If things change as we play more I'll update the review.People who have 1 hour gameplay and leave a negative review about "the amount of content" are tools.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, please, please listen to me before you start judging this title on face value alone.This is a new release, with a small team, they work tirelessly to improve and create content that makes the original seem like caveman paintings. With stunning lighting effects, beautiful weapon and ability effects, solid voice-over acting, and clear dedication to a plot, this game is a solid play, if you truly want to believe in it.On launch day (l a u n c h   d a y), I had only encountered two bugs, only one was gamebreaking. When you or the host would seemingly tab out during the loading process, the ambient world would load in, but the random placement of barricades and cars and fences, wouldn't sync with the rest of the lobby. It was immediately patched and fixed shortly afterwards, and I have never encountered it again.People complained about not being able to hit ready in a lobby. This is only an issue, when the host has yet to fully set up a mission to hit ready, please stop being impatient, and wait for your friends. ♥The Red Solstice was a game I played with one of my best friends before he passed away, we dumped hours into it because we had the time of our lives. He never unfortunately was able to see the release of TRS2, but I know he would be proud of this. Please stop giving this game negative reviews because you were inconvenienced by something that was immediately fixed shortly afterwards, this game is worth it. Give it a chance, you won't be disappointed.Play it with your friends online, or play it through the story. It has a myriad of things to do. I'm very picky about my games. _childDocuments_.review: TRS2 is a continuation of the Red Solstice series, which started as a mod for Starcraft, evolved into it's own game as TRS1, had a brief interlude twin stick shooter game called "Solstice Chronicles: MIA", and is now TRS2: Survivors. At every step of the way, the game has gotten better and matured. The quality, look, gameplay, and smoothness have all seen great leaps forward.TRS2 introduces many new abilities and map types, as well as a strategy map layer. Since the missions/maps themselves are randomized within each biome, it leads to great replayability. With a fleshed out single-player campaign, with missions that can be joined in co-op by friends, as well as the general online skirmish mode, TRS2 offers a lot of options for people to play.Veterans of the XCOM series will adapt quickly to the new strategy map/globe layer, which allows for research, exploration, manufacturing, an armory for customizing yourself and followers if playing in single-player, and important campaign informtaion.Overall, TRS2 is a great game for those seeking a neat real time, top down shooter game with classic Real-Time Strategy controls in a sci-fi setting where you can blast aliens with friends... or alone.Just don't get separated or overrun, or it's your friends who will be alone.

_childDocuments_.review: Real-time tactical XCOM fighting  space zombies.At it's core, it's a game about tactically surviving against hordes of enemies in a deserted Martian hellscape. Work towards saving the remains of humanity from the STROL menace and to attempt to reclaim the Earth after surviving Mars.The campaign may give you the impression that the game is relatively easy and unenventful, but on higher Infestation levels, things get VERY intense the longer you have to stay in missions. Craft your Operator build with tons of different passive and active abilities, choose your weapons and prepare to run, loot, shoot mutants and run away screaming from the horde chasing you. Bring your shotguns, your flamethrowers, your plasma rifles. You'll need them. The campaign alternates between this tactical view with a VERY XCOM-like global strategy map that you have to manage the resources of to advance. You won't be able to save everyone, or do every mission, so make every thing that you do count.On the multiplayer side, there's coop play of campaign missions that you can do with friends, or Skirmish single missions. That's what most people play, but I must mention there are  people playing this at any given time, so filling out an 8-player lobby for a 20-minute Skirmish mission might be hard. I hear gaming sessions are organized in the game Discord server, so you can always try that. All in all, it's a good game still in active development and support by the devs, with a fun multiplayer and a hardcore campaign.

_childDocuments_.review: [Note: Even after 100 hours I am not even done with the Elysium campaign and I am still an overall noob]This game sure is a doozy and can be complicated to explain to others but lessgooo;Red Solstice 2 is an RTS MOBA tactical rpg top down shooter with strategy metagame elements.Still confusing? Ok, I'll try to explain further.The game is mostly split into two parts: Campaign and Skirmish.Playing the campaign gives you an almost X-COM feel for the world as you expand territory, research new stuff and face new threats while uncovering secrets.You will also recruit new soldiers to your cause in order to both help you in mission and on that strategy metagame level.Note that pretty much every "story" DLCs switches faction from the one in the base game (Elysium) and are balanced differently (as in more difficult!).The cool thing with campaign is that you can play through pretty much the entire story up to 7 players giving an 8(!) player coop campaign which is quite damn impressive.Although, here we come to the difference between Campaign and Skirmish.When playing the campaign the host has the option upon starting said campaign wether the Campaign will be "coop or not".What this means is that if you have "coop enabled" all connected players will have to use whatever the host has researched in the campaign so far.Since the game took a lot of flak for this Campaign design decision, "disabling coop" is now available- allowing people to unlock their own stuff to bring to the campaign.Which leads us to Skirmish, which just like RS1 is where most of the meat is. Most players are not in for the story in the campaign but want an challenging coop session (note: bot support is available).When playing skirmish you have to unlock classes, weapons, gear and mods for personal use.Note that the game has class restrictions for both Campaign and Skirmish though, so you can't bring multiple Terminators to a mission!Plus with skirmish it is easier to coordinate level ups and daily challenges compared to campaign mode, so you may see way more people playing Skirmish rather than Campaign.Ok, so that's the gamemodes- what about gameplay?Red Solstice 2 plays mostly like an MOBA so you will unlock whatever skills you equipped on your suit (we'll come to that later) during the mission, so it's hard to unlock everything max level in one mission- you need to decide what's important!Mainly the game uses an rts control scheme with hotkeys for your abilities but you have the ability to aim manually with your weapons. A quite recent update added proper WASD controls for those who want it.Speaking of, secondary weapons are forced to be manually aimed.Although if you want, you can enable "overwatch" with your primary weapon which causes your character to attack anything in range (not recommended for advanced play though!).This makes it tense when moving around a large map since you may need to focus on walking to the next objective but need to put down threats along the way.Ammunition is a scarce commodity but the class included in the Howell-Barrex dlc, the Engineer, can produce ammo and defensive measures.If you play coop you can also share ammunition with each other, so it is important to check your ammunition with your friends before heading into a large battle.So what are the toys in the game? Well, in this game you play as highly advanced soldiers in power armour.These suits come in different flavours as I call "classes": so you may play as the well rounded Assault, the useful Medic, the sneaky Recon and the mighty complicated Terminator.Pretty much all classes are well balanced but some cracks can be shown amongst them: Recon and Marksman are so-so and so was Demolition (which was recently buffed thanks to community feedback!).So yeah, these suits are kinda like the Space Marine power armours in 40k mixed with Iron Man's suit.You can install different modules and skills which may drastically alter how gameplay plays out. For an example the Heavy can have a auto-turret on it's shoulder while focusing on launching rockets, or becoming a mobile turret by itself!All these modifications require energy so you need to min-max until you have something you feel good about. A good comparison would be the mech building part in the Armored Core series of games.Next- GUNS GUNS GUUUNS!There are plentyful of guns to mess around with in RS2!Primary weapon examples: Rifles (both auto and semi automatic), light machine gun, minigun, autocannon, pistol, submachine gun and flamethrower to name a few.Secondary weapon examples: Sniper rifles, cold thrower/freeze gun (mostly used to capture enemies), grenade launcher and rocket launchers to name a few.And here is the cool thing about the suit customization: You can pretty much use any of the above weapons for any class, I won't stop you from trying to bring a rocket launcher with your recon!Also the weapons are quite well balanced and are constantly balanced by the devs. Don't ignore the normal assault rifle just because it is the first gun you see, it's still useful!Although, to unlock all these things you need to level up and here it gets complicated;You have an XP (experience) that always goes up when you play a mission and successfully kill enemies.Collecting enough XP's will give you a skill point which you can spend on a giant skill tree. While most unlocks are only for Skirmish (or non-noop Campaign) there are some that affect both, be sure to read before you choose!Which brings us to ranks, remember me noting level ups in Skirmish? This is it.Along with the skill points to collect you can also increase your rank which gives slight stat boosts and more colours for your suit customization.Here is the crazy thing about ranking up though: you need to perform certain challenges during a mission or over multiple missions!It's hard to explain exactly why but it is way easier to plan out a rank up challenge in Skirmish rather than in Campaign. Trust me on this.Another quite recent update added something else that can be brought between both Campaign and Skirmish: Medals.There are medals you can unlock by during certain challenges, some for a specific class, some for other requirements.I personally have not unlocked any of them as of yet but trust me, those can be hard to unlock without a proper team.Those medals have complete stat changes that can further even more how your build works. As an example a medal might lower your hp but increase your ailment resistance.So along with your powerlevels you also have to take into account what negatives a medal can accidentally bring.So ending (TLDR section);It's a weird mix of RTS, MOBA and top down shooter in an explorable world with a ton of unlockable stuff.Playing this game solo is not recommended from me, so if you are searching for people then go visit the Red Solstice official Discord!Bots can make the game playable but they are more acting as dumb mobile turrets. With players you could split up and cover more ground.The Campaign can be extremely slow at times and it shows that most development has been spent on the Skirmish mode.Extremely high customization how your character works in-game gives it a unique personality, kinda like an RTS MOBA of Armored Core with Space Marines if anything! I have not seen anything like this game in a long time! This makes me think back to the late 1990's and early 2000's when devs risked to create something unique!I highly recommend picking this one on a sale since it has it's weird design quirks, get some friends playing together and have a good time!PS:While this is the second mainline game it doesn't feel like you need to play the earlier Red Solstice games (RS1 and MIA) to understand the story.If you are playing campaign there is a glossary you can read up on lore which explains which character is who and what he or she has done in the earlier games.

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun and challenging top down action game.  you kit out a powersuit wearing spec op (think master chief) VS an abomnible force (think the flood or tyrranid or necromorphs) as you play in Falling cities and research facilities completing various missions and side missions, from defend and escort missions, to head hunting tough enemies.  the game excels when played with others since the surroundings steadily get more dangerous with time and each class can bring its own unique qualities to bear. from the steady damage and durability of the assault class, the impressive longevity granted by the medic, the undeniable DPS and crowd clearing of the heavy to the artillery barrages and orbital strikes of the recon(and other classes as well), there are many ways to wage war against the enemy.  if you are looking for a military sci-fi game to play with friends or others, I highly recommend, but if your a solo gamer this may be a poor fit, since the more consistent and diverse the firepower, the greater your survivability and longevity.

_childDocuments_.review: Again "mixed" from me. It's a 50/50 yes it's very, fun but it has a lot of flaws. However if you're good with learning things and you got friends to play with, then it's worth a look. Personally **I like this game**, but after finishing the main campaign I can't recommend this to others as it has a lot of flaws.This game is a top down "helldivers 1" with a bit more freedom of customization and such. The problem with helldivers 1 (which I still like, don't get me wrong)  is the camera is locked to the whole team, meaning people can't move around the map as they please, they can't get into positions easily, people can be left behind, etc etc...., in this game, each online player has their own camera, so it's better on THAT front only.However the devs took some... REALLY weird choices in gameplay, mainly campaign stuff and understanding things.Seriously, someone could scoop this game up, change a ton of things, and make it into an amazing top down multiplayer game.Basically someone who could mod this game? You could make this game ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ great! Remove the campaign gating, smooth out the difficulty increase over each map. And add maybe another passive slot without EN cost for people to play around with.Pros and cons+Fully Customizable Character (stat wise)- You slot upgrades in your suit and each class has a different number of slots.+Bunch of classes with variety of skills. A LOT of useful skills.++8 player games... holy crap, that's nice.++The ability to play in RTS mode or WASD mode and able to swap modes with a button press.+Overwatch mode -> basically you can bring up menus, use the bathroom, check the map, etc. And your character will continue to fire with their main gun, but it takes some max energy away from you.~If you can't gather 8 people to play with you, you can still play with NPCs (3 of them) and you can control them. You can assign them to a friend (hidden thing) but your friend can't control them like you can.Addendum bonuses: +You can take NPCs you train by fighting alongside and send them to help zones you control.+NPCs can be customized some, not as much as you though.+You can control NPCs kind of RTS style.Okay the downsides...---The campaign is WAY too repetitive. Like holy crap can you ease up on the number of repeat battles between story segments? Don't get me wrong, I don't mind building up things, but there are some really really bad gates to be able to advance the story, like not having enough supplies to build a comm center to expand your scan range or such. There should be like 2-3 side battles between stories. Cause at a certain point you can max out EVERYTHING in the research area and then be like "okay okay can we move it along here without having to defend the wall and save a colony from exploding for the 20th time?" (yes you have to at leastkeep colonies from getting destroyed or it's a big setback)-Due to the length of the campaign, having a bunch of friends who all want to still play it... well.... might be difficult.-Main player/host is the only one that can control the between gameplay XCOM management stuff. Your friends can sill work on their loadouts, but that's all.-Main player can bring in items but friends can't-Main player can play as a "hidden class" in the campaign, but friends can't.-DLC has weapon customization, which I was happy with at first but a lot of the customization choices had too severe penalties.-Heavy difficulty spike. Each map starts easy, then gets really bad. Gameplay spends too much time in the either too easy or too hard sections. You start from character lv1 on each map and have you level up your suit. There's a story reason for this of course but it feels kinda eh.-Vague or unclear effects or a bunch of useless feeling skills. While there's a LOT of fun skills and such, there's a lot that are a bit cryptic to "how is this good?" due to cost of installing the skill in your build. It almost feels like some of the skills should be added as extra passives.Example of a vague boost: "Gives +0.01 crit"  wait is this a % or a 1% crit boost due to how math works, or ... what? this looks like a typo that needs fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very underrepresented game which I greatly enjoyed. Originally, I expected this to be more like XCom, for some reason, but it plays more like Diablo with guns. Still, the gameplay is very engaging; the variation among enemies and equipment allows for a lot of replayability and the game doesn't get stale, despite the repetitive elements. Graphics and audio are pretty neat, as well.Two gripes I have with the game is the rank advancement (purely cosmetic) demanding you to play skirmish mode, instead of being fully unlocked through campaign alone. Its a minor thing most won't even care about, but I find that annoying and immersion-breaking. The second gripe is the ending of the main campaign... which is entirely dependant on several VERY obscure and easily-missed key moments during certain campaign missions. Putting 60 hours into campaign and getting the very bad ending which kinda invalidated all of my efforts feltbadman.Regardless of these relatively minor things, however, the game is definitely worth its price and its a great fun to play, both by yourself and with friends. Considering that devs still update and closely watch the game, I am totally recommending it.

_childDocuments_.review: TL/DR version: Unexpectedly shallow game play that lacks the enjoyment of the original. You're much better off playing the first one through again.Longer version:As a huge fan of the original Red Solstice I went into this expecting more of the same, and from the trailers it looked oh so promising. Unfortunately as far as single player campaign goes, the delivery was decidedly lackluster.The main issue is you only get control over a single unit, with the rest of your squad (7 members eventually) all controlled by the A.I.While this wouldn't be an issue normally, the game lacks any kind of ability to take direct control over your A.I companions, or even order them when to use their special abilities or even when to switch to secondary weaponry. All you get for control over them is "follow" and "move to designated location. (What's the point of giving you a sniper who uses a generic assault rifle as his primary gun and then deny you any actual ability to control when and where the unit uses said sniper rifle?)Combine this with a relatively low level A.I for your teammates, and no active pause/bullet time ability to let you effectively manage your squad in the thick of combat, (They are no where near smart enough to take up solid support fire positions or seek cover without your direct orders.) and the fun is quickly sucked out of the game after a few missions.I wanted to like this game, and gave it almost 2 hours to see if it got better further in (sadly it doesn't) but at the end of the day the single player campaign left me shaking my head and requesting a refund.As far as the other bits go:Graphics: 7/10 (There's some nice eye candy to be found, but the lack of any zoom function on the camera and the angle being a bit too birds eye makes it hard to really see the details like you'd want.)Sound/Music: 6/10 It's there, but nothing especially memorable compared to similar titles?Storyline: 5/10 A watered down X-Com 2 feel, minus any actual character development of your units or NPC's. Controls: 9/10 Nicely functional with all keys able to be remapped for your convenience. Only downside is the lack of a zoom feature and the camera feeling just a little (about 25%) too zoomed out for comfort.Bugs: 4/10 Some nasty ones, from lost progress, to crashes to desk top, and serious problems with getting videos to play (Work around is replacing and renaming all the video cut scene files with the intro video.Also worth noting there's no save in mission feature, so if you need to leave in the middle of a map, you're starting over from before you launched the mission.All in all, wait for a steep (70%+ Off) sale, or just give this one a pass entirely, it lacks the charm and fun factor of the original.

_childDocuments_.review: I would say treat the negative reviews with a grain of salt.  Many of the complaints I saw were about the first few hours of the game going live.  Most of those bugs were fixed within the first 12 hours of the game going live.  That said some of the other complaints were people believing this game was a different style.  This is a live action game.  You have to work as a team with the other players in the lobby to make it to the end.  The whole idea behind this game is TEAMWORK.  At the very early stages of the multiplayer rounds you can wonder off a little and find supplies.  However, you really need to find a few battle buddies and stick with them!  90% of the time if you run off on your own and stay alone...you die.  You can be revived but it's not easy as the team has to hold your dead position while you're revived.  Share items, share ammo, fight the undead horde and complete your objectives.  GAMEPLAY:The best way to describe the game play of this game I would say is to think of MOBA meets Starcraft.  Don't get the wrong idea as you don't fight other players.  You fight the undead horde only. You control your soldier and can set up a build with talents and abilities.  You level up during the match you join and put points into those abilities as the match goes on.  There are different classes that all have strengths to help the team.  If you enjoy team based games you will likely enjoy this one.  I've not really run into a negative or toxic player yet.  After all you're all trying to do the same objectives together!

_childDocuments_.review: Game is fun, haven't encountered many bugs so far, played a few hours. There was a bit of desync in one mission so far, but it wasn't really that big of a deal, was caused by NPC vehicles on the map, and went away once that section of the mission was complete. Mostly played MP. This is basically real time XCOM, if that doesn't sound fun to you, you're not going to like the game. It's a good time if you know what you're getting into and enjoy that type of game. It's not really a coop action game, it's a bit slower and methodical. There's a lot of running around the map to get to where you need to be, especially if you're doing the secondary missions, traversal takes some time and you will be backtracking a bit to complete objectives, dealing with waves of enemies as you go. I think a lot of the negative reviews come from people not knowing what to expect from the game and it not being as fast as they were expecting. Progress is tied to host, so keep that in mind if you're playing with someone else as host, it's fine if you're just wanting to play the game coop, but you will do everything twice if you want to progress yourself without your hosting friend. If real time XCOM sounds fun, I recommend it, if you want something fast paced and high octane, you'll probably want to skip. The tutorial and first mission are enough to decide if it's your kind of game or not, and won't take long, so you can always refund it if it's not your cup of tea.
