_childDocuments_.review: Interesting concept if the developer was a bigger team it could be an exceptional 3-D platformer. As it is, its an atmospheric game where you are an explorer in an experimental craft dropped in mysterious environments. Use its unique movement system to travel the alien landscapes to the destination. If you enjoy a nuanced minimalist game you'll love it. Going for achievements will enhance the experience.+/- This is an "experience" type game. Very short. Its more about the way it makes you feel on the journey. Their is no failure. It certainly isn't going to be for everyone.+Movement Mechanics. The vehicle adopts an entirely unique movement system where you activate its gravity drive to force you down creating speed. Use the terrain to slope up hills to launch into the air and switch to gliding through the sky.+Atmosphere/Sound. The vehicle being of alien design in origin, the environments, the sound, and the super short cut scenes depicting the Jupiter disaster deliver a constant feeling of mysteriousness.+Achievements. Many of them don't come naturally giving you something to actually shoot for besides reaching the destination. Getting you to explore and find ways to break the sound barrier, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know where all the gaming press hype comes from. It's not a bad indie game, it's just it peters out very, very quickly and probably can be finished before Steam's refund timer if you grok the craft motions quickly. It's a nice and novel idea for controls, but it is not without its flaws. Camera code can't keep up after you learn to control the craft which sucks the fun out of it right when it should be the beginning of having fun. Zero replayability value. Story is non-existent, just a few dialogue lines with annoying randomized word-like gibberish. Music - also sparse and practically non-existent. Sound effects are OK. Too much film grain to my taste (luckily adjustable) and an un-toggleable overlay annoying with "camera crosshairs".It's an "experience", but a fleeting and forgettable one. It would benefit from supporting VR though, like Race the Sun does.While it's not deserving a negative review, it is "meh" at best.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a peacefull challengeless contemplative journey of 2-3 hours (3 if you're achievement guy or smth).This review contains spoilers about levels and atmosphere.If you want to feel it fully by youself - do NOT read below.To the author.Thank you for this journey, for making me rethink the gorgeousness of Jupiter and for reminding me of people who look into the abyss and further. And, of course, making my evening a bit brighter.About the aspects:What I loved- Sounds- Cubes and other solid obstacles- Lights (except the second, icy planet)- Clouds- THE concept. Wow- "No energy" level- Thumb down review to this game saying that the guy was thinking that this game was about you flying in the ufo destroying cities or smthWhat was meh- No message about out of energy on level with no energy and electric storm- Barely to no water reaction on any collision with ship or with huge rolling sphere- Last level of speed (kind of inverted colors). Previous speed effects - awesome, but last one looks not mesmerizing but horrifying to me, like something bad is happening.What I didn't liked-Green level (mostly because too much "just roll up the *smth*", too linear)(Seems like first water level was the hardest one, everything below is about that level)-Splashes of water too lo-fi-Waves have top and bottom level, leaving huge squares of plane water not reacting to the waves-No returning mechanic when you try to go down as much as possible, cought first and only bug there where my ship was rotating

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, the music really sets the tone, and everything you do seems to flow smoothly, i'm glad i bought this game, i didn't feel rushed, instead, i felt like i wanted to keep playing up until the very end, and not only that, but the credits were calming, I could control the camera while they rolled so i always had something to do.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so super cool. It's a really different experience. The gravity-pull-onto-hills-for-momentum gameplay isn't a completely original idea, but this is the BEST version of that game I've ever seen. The controls feel incredible (with the exception of one short level gimmick). The visuals are INCREDIBLY GORGEOUS. The music is BEAUTIFUL. The story is lightly sprinkled throughout and oddly grabbed me really strongly despite being not particularly revolutionary.Simple ideas almost perfectly executed is a good formula.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game that took me about 3 hours to play through.  The beginning of the game is a bit overwhelming because you feel like there is no direction and you have no backstory.  These two things are quickly overshadowed by the immense beauty and calmness of the landscapes of each planet you visit. Eventually you figure out there are landmarks to follow to complete each planet.  I did not think I'd be into this game but I found myself feeling zen playing this.  Almost therapeutic.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most beautiful games I've played in recent memory. The combination of the music and huge, breathtaking maps made me feel awe and amazement in a way that I have not felt for a long time, at least in terms of video games; this is more of an experience than a game. Even though it is pretty short, I finished it in less than 180 minutes, this is firmly one of my favorite games of all time.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: This game makes the physics-fan part of my brain really happy. It's also gorgeous even on lower end PCs. You can play this game casually as you explore the vast maps in a mesmerizing playthrough, or you can play technically to learn the speedrun with many play-throughs. The developers did an exceptional job designing around both styles. Soundtrack is top-notch.The second half of the game does lean into technical challenges and leaves casual players yearning for the early-game simplicity. It has some fun elements like ramps and boosters, but they could have done more with this. The story is a bit cryptic and intrusive. The 2-hour playthough is pretty short for the price, but again it's pretty re-playable like an arcade game.If the trailer makes you want to play it, I think you'll love this game.Warning to those sensitive to flashing images and plain-white screens.I recommend buying with the soundtrack, because it's pretty good ambient instrumental music.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: one of the most beautiful games i've ever played, played it 3 times over now and will totally replay multiple times more, would buy any dlc they'd make for it too. music is 11/10 movement is so good and it's only flaw is that it's too short. outer wilds is the only thing that feels this unique but outer wilds is much more challenging and mysterious. buy it and play it multiple times.

_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Cool idea, graphically pleasant, but ultimately an unsatisfying experience. The concept is nice but the game never really fully lets you enjoy it. A game about momentum but you always feel like you're being artificially limited, and railroaded in a certain direction. The trailers show you bouncing and zooming around amazing mountain scenes but more than half of the game has you pointlessly skimming across water or clouds or almost flat ground, none of which is thrilling or exciting unless perhaps you've eaten a fistful of mushrooms beforehand.There is some attempt at story but actually it's just an annoying distraction between loading screens, and is totally impossible to understand. It's not even interesting enough to make me want to look it up.The game is very short too, I was tabbed out for like 2 hours of my play time for reference.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Not bad. I'm disappointed that there isn't more content, but that's the sincerest form of flattery, I suppose. The game mechanics are simple and very fun. I just wish the playground was bigger. Exploiting the physics to gain tremendous speeds is super fun.This game could really benefit from a level editor. Giving players the ability to create and share levels that allow them to do tremendously ridiculous things in the engine would be incredible.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Bold, strikingly beautiful and entirely ambiguous from minute one..Exo-One feels more like the start of an incredible career more than anything. Jay Weston and co flex their inner passion for aviation with every sound-barrier break and swooping bullet dive straight into the depths of sparkling blue oceans, warp drives and the steepest of banks, all specifically curated for eye watering speeds.The game relies on the physicality of the world more than it does with any other aspect. The player-controlled object flying through the world is but a current of energy (electricity almost) that is constantly dependant on the line (the world) that supports it's predetermined path. Despite the unintentional, frustrating breaks in momentum that the game suffers from (in mechanical form) Exo One is absolutely breathtaking to watch and be a part of, especially when it starts firing on all cylinders. The presentation of levels and environmental story telling on show here impresses me greatly also. As well as the sense of scale which I struggled to comprehend with on a number of occasions. This thing is an eye opening delight....Perhaps a little too short? And lacking a little in quality of life features and options? Despite all this, the skeleton for an even more ambitious game is lurking upon the horizon and I am so eager to see this man and his vision on an even grander scale next time around. Bring. It. On.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: So....do I recommend this game? It's fun, and I like the vagaries. It reminds me of the kind of "game" you'd play as a kid, putting your hand out the window and feeling the wind flow over and under it. It's enjoyable, and relaxing.But it is not worth $15. There simply isn't enough gameplay. If there were some kind of endless mode with randomly generated worlds, that would be something. But I finished the game in 3.5 hours, and there really isn't any reason to play again. even the remaining achievements are "go high on this world" or "go fast close to the ground on this world". Nothing else to find, or to see. There's not even any reason to "explore" the worlds that I could find. At any rate, I'm glad I played it, but wish it had been cheaper.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: I tried to describe this to a friend, I came up with:Imagine ["Second Reality" demoscene masterpiece creators) Future Crew watched Flight of the Navigator, cranked Unreal Engine 4 to 11 and wa**ed out a fever dream of Science Fiction 2001/Interstellar skunk-visions.A little crude I know but it fits.  On my modest 2014 i7 and GTX 1650, it looked *glorious*; each planet was a distinct place ranging from verdant mountains to asteroid fields to a stormy sea-scape.In many ways this felt like a tech-demo, almost a portfolio of graphical prowess.  It is true that the story is perfunctory and ultimately doesn't matter, but I appreciate its inclusion as it did lift my experience above that of a tech-demo.  The length of the levels and the well-timed introduction of new gameplay mechanics (there are a few and I liked them all) means Exo One never started to wear out its welcome.Above all, the mechanics and physics are nailed, it's a joy to play which of course is the most important part of anything one does for pleasure and it feels *great*.  The weight that causes the speed-up and the exhilaration of the flight into the sky, glorious.One run through took me around 2 hours and 30 minutes, it was a perfect game to play in between longer console titles for me.I played this with an XBox 360 game pad and it was great, didn't try with mouse and keyboard.  I would say that if you can play this natively on a big television, then do so as it's the perfect visuals to lean back and drink in.Great stuff, very well made.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: A very unique experience unlike anything I've played before. The visuals are out of this world literally. Excellent graphics and and game play. Flying the spacecraft is fun and satisfying. Achievements are fun to unlock and it's hard to get bored even just flying around. I lost my breath a few times flying high up in the air or going under the ocean. This game feels super realistic and runs smooth. The story is vague but haunting and leaves you loving the mystery. I would love to play an EXO TWO because it just wasn't enough.

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost; This game is short.It took me 2 1/2 hours from beginning to end credits.  If this is a problem for you, don't buy this game.That being said, it's a pretty cool experience.  There's an over-arching story, but that's just the sprinkles on the delicious cupcake that is rolling and gliding as an interplanetary space marble.Do I feel like there could have been more?  Yes.  I think there's more that could have been explored with this gameplay mechanic.  Like I already mentioned; It's short.If I had to compare this game to another, I would say Abzu or Journey.  Just a simple, chill, exploratory experience with an interesting method of locomotion.Something about the aesthetic of the game makes me think it's like a playable version of that early, abstract, 3d rendered artwork from the 90's.  Kind of like what you might have had on your binder in middle-school back then.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know, it just wasn't for me. I played the demo a year or two ago and then bought the game based on the fun I had in those few demo minutes. Ultimately, though, while the gameplay was fun for half an hour (again), after the fourth planet, I felt that something was missing to keep me motivated. I did not master the controls as well as would have been necessary to remain fast and moving all the time, so I bumped into icebergs, had to struggle to reach some of the power-ups, and overall felt like I had to work hard in a game that was marketing itself as casual and relaxing exploration. The idea is still novel, and the planets (so far) have been stunningly beautiful despite their simplicity, but the story did not catch me at all, and overall I just seem to have lost interest. A shame. I still respect the effort.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, maybe the idea bihind this art project is quite good and interesting, but implementation as a game has its flaws. Considering the screenshots provided, it should look like a free flight through beautiful scenery, vast landscapes, beatiful skies with clouds and various weather effects - everything is in there, but without freeflight for me, mostly flying low above the ground/water with frequent "flight" recharging (except for the level with flying islands with green forests - that one was really nice).If you want to speed up to fly high, you need to "dive" first to gain momentum, but it is not always easy to figure out the right moment to do that - you simply cannot see what is down below exactly to fall on a downhill instead of uphill.The "glide+dive" option also not quite predictable - you either not "dive" long enough and not gain enough speed, or it turns into an uncontrollable tailspin. Also awful control of flight on the "pink clouds" level - instead of flying strait with small corrections you either glide up or dive down following your guide.The level with asteroids is the worst considering mechanics - it is obvious that you need to fly from one asteroid to another, escaping their gravity fields to be caught by the next one and be pulled to it, but when the planet is right above you and you cannot fly to it it is confusing as hell. Here I just thought that game needs some visual confirmations of gravity fields and your actions (as either color halos or smth else changing according to your actions and environments), without it playing experience is kinda negative.Though I should say that visuals and sound are really nice, pity you can't enjoy it in full without proper game mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: So this is one of those games that is more of an experience but is a lot of fun to play. Just gliding around while using gravity to build up momentum is such a freeing experience. I would love to see a level select menu so I can just go back and glide through some levels and experience them again without having to play through the entire game again. My only complaint is that I feel the price is a little high for what it is, I think I would feel more comfortable to pay around $10 for Exo One, but all-in-all it was an enjoyable experience and I would buy it all over again. This is just one of those games that has what I'm looking for, a special experience. Would recommend. If you don't feel like paying full price then I recommend wishlisting it and waiting for a sale, it's a short game but worth the experience it gives. So if you get it set aside a couple of hours and let this game take you on a journey.

_childDocuments_.review: That was quite a journey. If you're looking for a story-driven game like Firewatch, this is definitely not it. The story plays a rather secondary role to the feeling that develops as you travel through the different areas. The levels don't feel empty, even though you catapult your space frisbee from one place to the next with Mach Weeeeee and have plenty of time to take in the surroundings while listening to a very idyllic soundtrack. If you liked the game Journey, Exo-One is very similar, except you have a space marble-frisbee-transformer that regularly breaks the sound barrier.

Apart from the epileptic inducing flashing lights, you're welcomed to a smooth and relaxing journey across different planets (biomes).Albeit short in length it offers up a simple yet engaging gameplay, which have enough depth in the mechanics to let you experiment with optimizing your flight paths for a truly exciting pace through the diverse landscapes on future playthroughs.If you enjoyed games like "Journey" and it likes. _childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Exo One is a game that caught my eye one day before it's release. Curious, I tried out the demo and loved it, a few days later, bought it and absolutely adored it. It's Zen game play, gravity mechanics, Delightful graphics and great soundtrack really made me happy with the overall package...sort of. The story I would say is a bit of a miss, but isn't much of a issue in my case as I expected the story to be lacking, but just wanted to bring it up.The pricing for what you are getting is also a bit much. 23.95 Australian dollars totalling over 2 hours of game play, which is a shame with how enjoyable the rest of the game is, and I would totally the price is way too much for what you are getting. Unless we are getting a huge content update that gives us more levels OR maybe even some mod support? (that would be neat, would totally be into seeing that.) I would also like to see in a update also a Level select, even games like Journey had in some way a level select without saying it did, so I could master levels I had trouble with without having to restart all the way to the beginning of the game.An overall very enjoyable game. But, if you are money conscious or don't think it's worth the price, get it on discount. Hope to see more stuff from this developer in the future!

_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful and moving journey.   It was amazing to explore the various planets that make up the levels and simply take in the breathtaking views.   The game play consists of rolling, jumping, and gliding through an assortment of gorgeous vistas to reach a monolith that takes you to the next level.  Along the way there are canyons, ramps, cliffs, clouds, ancient structures, etc that allow you to utilize the game's physics the reach incredible speeds and heights.  There is no combat, and there doesn't appear to be any way to lose such that you have to start a level over.  There is nothing to collect outside of the occasional power-up to your speed/gliding length, so additional exploration is only for the enjoyment of the views.   This is a chill game that somehow had me feeling excited the whole time rather than relaxed. I enjoyed it greatly.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: I loved almost every part about this game. The scenery is beautiful, there were some crazy ass moments that were amazing (won't spoil, you'll understand what I mean if you play the game), and the mechanics were fairly easy to grasp. Although some of the levels were meant to be played at literal supersonic speeds, some other levels would feel excessively long when you were forced to mostly travel near or at ground level. If you're okay with having to travel a bit before reaching your destination, I think you'll enjoy this game to the fullest extent.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. I actually audibly said "wow" a bunch while playing this game. The developers have a way of crafting a kind of wondrous, ethereal experience, where you're genuinely in awe of the world they've created. Really special. Early levels were kind of slow and 'getting' the game was hard (I question putting a water level without being very explicit about what you need to do there- I spend most of the level just rolling along the bottom of the ocean, with no idea what I was doing wrong) but they seem to be getting better the farther the game progresses. And I mean a LOT better. Wow.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful and relaxing experience, I have played through it a few times now and it never fails to impress. There's no time limit, no evil aliens or guns. I often play games like this after a rough day at work, The game is very simple and easy to control, I would say it is rather expensive considering you can clear it in about 2 hours if you explore like I did. But as many of you know the completion time isn't everything unfortunately, the game does not change on a second or third playthrough. Maybe I am missing something, there could be more out there. Most short indi titles usually offer a new challenge with each successive completion. But I sill feel like there is more to this game. It reminds me of Race The Sun a little, only there is no pressure and the environment is not constantly trying to end you.  The game should run on a potato and there was a Demo available so please give it a try. P.S. CAN MORE DEVELOPERS PLEASE OFFER DEMOS FOR GAMES.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely blissful experience.You're a spherical craft, able to flatten yourself to glide, flying through the universe.Short, but an absolutely wonderful, relaxing and addictive experience.Visuals are beautifully done, controls are responsive, sound design is great.Good game for speedrunners.Loved it, would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Take this as a... neutral review.Gameplay-wise it's pretty fun; the movement mechanics are well-made and engaging... however, it's constantly held back by very hit-or-miss level design. I often felt like the levels were preventing me from reaching high speeds, doing cool moves and intuitively showing me where to go. There are some really cool levels as well, but I often felt there was a lot of room for polish.The story is... I don't know. I don't care. It's very... present in everything going on and reminding you it's there, but it never tells you much and you don't know any of the characters in the story, so... who cares, you know?Finally, visually, it's... a bit all over the place. Some things are like... some of the coolest ♥♥♥♥ I've ever seen in a video game. Gorgeous shader-work, really cool planet designs, massive vistas stretching beyond the horizon... And then you get close to the terrain and it's kinda flat, low on details and the hills just look like someone went nuts with the terrain tool.Overall... maybe get it on sale, or if you're in need of nice shader references, or you just want a simple game to play around in for a while? I don't think you'll be disappointed by the purchase, but I don't know if it will fill the void in your soul either.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Exo One is a game about atmosphere and aesthetic.That's  it is. If you want to know whether you'll like this game, search for "Exo One: Prologue" which is its free demo. If you play that, you think, "Yes, more of this, please," and are willing to part with however many dollars in exchange for two-ish hours of (very pretty) new levels, then by all means go ahead.I personally found the flashing images and the looped garbles of the dialogue kind of irritating, and I wasn't satisfied with the ending. The game is unique enough, and pretty enough, that I'll give it a thumbs up in spite of that - but I  hope the developers add options to disable all of that stuff and just let you play the game uninterrupted.Recommended  you play "Exo One: Prologue" and are comfortable with the price point for a two-ish-hour campaign.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible given the circumstances surrounding the development. I couldn't believe how blown away I was started playing. The semi-complex story threaded in between the relaxing yet challenging game play was not what I expected while I was following the development of this game. It exceeded any expectations that I had and I couldn't be more happy with this game. I highly recommend this game to anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: This game was fun. I was disappointed when I finished it and realized I couldn't just aimlessly roam different worlds with my obtained power. You can go back and select previous worlds you've played, but you just wont have everything you gained before. I enjoyed it regardless so I'm giving it a positive, but this really needs to have a sandbox mode.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: This experience has many similarities to "Journey", another atmospheric and contemplative title with similar hovering and gliding mechanics. Unlike Journey, however, Exo One is the most underrated title of 2021. Hands down. The entire experience, I was speechless, even moreso than 2012's Journey (developed by Thatgamecompany, Journey is their flagship title alongside the multiplayer experience "Sky" (Sky is only available on mobile devices, Nintendo Switch, Playstation 3, 4 and 5)).Each planet gives you such a unique sense of  A feeling that whatever you see is the first time it has ever been seen by human eyes. You  feel like an alien probe, your indestructible and unexplained nature causing you to feel no fear while exploring the breathtaking vistas and landscapes of these untouched-by-mankind planets at supersonic, impossible speeds.The sensation of speed in this game is  frequently breaking the sound barrier and hearing the rest of the world slowly fade out as you outzoom sound itself. Gaining speed and launching off the various slopes, divots, crevices and aerial slipstreams, blasting through the air like the fastest Jetplane ever to exist, it's...  I frequently found myself unconsciously leaning closer and closer to the screen, letting the screen take over my vision and seeing the speedlines fly past my peripheral vision and I see a vapor cloud form around me with the  of the sound barrier breaking, wanting to feel every moment of that speed with full immersion and have my heart thumping out of my chest, you feel For an experience that lasts just barely over two hours if you casually play, maybe 1 hour if you just go to every Transporters and explore nothing, this is my GOTY for 2021. Any other game that came out in 2021 does not compare to Exo One and I am  exaggerating. I can only hope that this dev team makes a sequel, because... my god, this speed is more addicting than F-Zero X.If you want speed, and feel like an interplanetary Christopher Columbus (minus the colonization, theft and pillaging) and fill yourself with cosmological wonder and curiosity,
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Exo One´s atmosphere is best described as a mix of Stanley Kubrick's "2001 a Space Odyssey", Denis Villeneuve's "Arrival", Christopher Nolan's "Interstellar" and Randal Kleiser's "Flight of the Navigator".In my opinion Exo One is a bit too short, but otherwise a very good game. I mean i played it around 4.5 - 5 hours and I went through it 2 times aside from that, I was taking my time. Much of the negative Reviews are refering about Exo One's short playtime and in my opinion they aren't entirely wrong. But just because it's short doesn't mean it's bad. In all other aspects Exo One is stunning, has amazingly atmospherical effects, a great soundtrack and super smooth controls. It's not a game for everyone but if you just want to lean back and enjoy a meditational trip trough time and space I definitely would recommend it to you.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: It just finished it right now, and nothing else to say than : just do it. It's a pleasure to watch, it's a pleasure to play. The first minutes I just couldn't get how I could get into the game so fast and easily, then I played a bit more, and just understood that it was a good game, with nothing else to offer than a good relaxing and mind refreshing moment. Thanks for your work dear devs, it will be a real pleasure to come again to Exo One.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: If you're ever in a bad mood, play this. You'll be so much calmer in about 5 minutes. It's relaxed, you can't lose/win you just experience the fluid movement of guiding your ship from a to b moving from planet to the next. I don't know how long the game but the next time I'm feeling a bit tetchy I'm putting on this game. Don't know how I haven't finished it yet I'm grumpy as f**k!
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: This game is hella dopeAnyone saying it's not worth the money, has no concept of value. (But it is short)The visuals - stunning, the music & sound - divine.Heavily influenced by Journey. Wish once you've completed it, you unlocked a free play mode. Maybe where you got some sort of propulsion. Best parts of the game are where you use the clouds to gain altitude, then dive to break the sound barrier, sonic boom and all. More of that please.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: I'm at a loss of words. The beauty of this game just can't be described using some letters on the screen. You have to see and play for yourself, only then you will understand. And combined with the marvelous soundtrack. This game is just... perfect.edit: An level select after you have finished the game would be awesome (nvm there is one now)
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: On its surface, Exo One is a chill game about exploring various planets and moons. And it can be that because the movement, in my opinion, feels just right. The "spaceship" ball/disc behaves in ways I'd expect it to. You can pick your own path to a degree.The real fun begins when you practice and try to go as fast as possible, though. You can stay at incredible speeds and do the levels in ways you wouldn't have considered possible before. This is a great speed game.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Exo One is easily one of the most intriguing titles i've spent time with. I love anything space related, and this nails planetary exploration in a way any of us can only imagine. I bought the game on sale, but i'd say it's worth whatever they are asking for.  The mechanics are simple, but they really are a joy to play with.  Once i was finished the game, i was glad to be back on earth. Easy 9/10 for what this is.  Great graphics, great gameplay, just the right length. Would recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: The mechanics are fun and even though the game does not have traditional objectives (go here, do this), it's very rewarding to just drive around and glide in the clouds. You will encounter various landmarks integrated in the planets, which will guide you through the game, but simply getting the hang of the mechanics for the first time and then spending your time speeding around the planets, reaching new heights while gliding and finding new points of interest is where most of the gameplay (and fun) seems to be.The only thing I would appreciate having is some sort of an in-game map; for now, I am a bit lost on each planet, without any good sense of direction and discovering POIs feels a bit random. Apart from that, the game is very well made, runs smoothly and is very responsive. No bugs or crashes.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Unique game that reminds me of "Journey" where the only objective is to work your way towards a beam of light in the sky. Soundtrack is great. The game alternates between "relaxing" and "I've had my thighs clenched continuously for the last 20 minutes as I try to time the gravity right". Story line is meant to be mysterious and thought-provoking I suppose? But it almost lacks too much to where you don't particularly care about it. During the initial play through it can be frustrating on some of the more difficult levels to learn how to generate energy. But if you intend to gun for achievements odds are you'll need 3-4 play-throughs anyway and it becomes more fun as you progress through. Recommended at full price, but definitely on sale as well. Overall 8 out of 10, and that's mostly because of the lack of story line. I think had they gone with a little more in depth to keep the mystery but explain more background, 9 out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed this experience; it's something between a short-sci-fi-story + physics/graphics demo + a dream or perhaps a poemi was briefly disappointed when i discovered the craft used a type of inverted gravity drive (basically you can drastically increase your mass/gravity then use a kind of centrifugal force & aerodynamics to propel yourself at break-neck speeds) but after a moment to acclimate i absolutely loved the feel of itthe music, the vague plot, the dream-like worlds were all fascinating - the super-sonic travel was somehow both exhilarating and calming simultaneouslymy first play-through i only faintly comprehended the plot, but primarily due to the stunning visuals and exuberant gameplay - so i played through again immediately and now "get it"...and it's just *chef's kiss emoji*it's a very good, short, beautiful adventure which i cannot recommend enough edit: just two small changes devs should consider (1) if i'm totally honest i did not really notice any changes the "upgrades" made if they made any at all (2) there is a level with nearly zero-g that, while exploring and investigating an object, i inadvertently transported to the next level - the "exit door" for that level needs to be MUCH less sensitive
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an amazing, unique eperience. I've always wondered how it would feel like flying among the clouds and over the seas. I think this game will be the closest I will get to that feeling.I have a couple of suggestions:- After finishing the game, add chapter select so we can jump on the experience we want, with the end-game stats :)- Make all cutscenes and dialogues skippable. At least for the chapter-select.Pros:- Spectacular visuals and atmosphere!- Controls are good- Sounds are good- Feeling of flying is amazing- Interesting gameplay mechanic- Intriguing story premise.Cons:- A bit short (~2 hrs). I wanted to fly more! :D- Not the clearest story. But it's not a story-heavy game. And it might be meant to be that way- I personally didnt like the "gibberish" voiceover to the subtitles. But it might not be a problem for everybody.Overall, thank you for this game. I'm glad I bought it and if there is ever a chance of a sequel, I will be thrilled to play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Good game.  Gliding/gravity mechanic was well done.  Environments were varied and had some visually stunning moments.  Collectibles and interactive environment bits were cool, I would have liked more.It took me about 3 hours to complete a run.The game could use some work on artistic direction.  I felt the flashing pictures were overdone and mostly a distraction.  I think just having the scenes in between levels provides enough story.  I would also like the Exo One to look more like a space craft of some sort rather than just a sphere and ellipsoid.The camera also could use some work, especially when on the ground.  Quick maneuvers on the ground sometimes led to aggravating camera repositioning that would cause me to lose the momentum I was trying to gain.The good parts vastly outweighed the bad though.  The game was at its best when I was surfing clouds or skimming water over long distances, jumping between the orbits of large bodies orbiting a sun, or .This game has a ton of potential and I hope the devs keep refining it.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Exo One provides a simple, enchanting and effortless gaming experience thanks to it's high velocity mechanics, massive structures and smooth controls; the lack of replayability, vague story and short duration however may hinder the title from reaching truly exceptional heights.Interested in my reviews? You can follow my curator page here;
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: A great concept, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, is this game short. The review time is literally how long it took for me to beat this game from start to finish. There's even an achievement for beating it in an  Overall, not worth the $21.99 CDN this game is asking for. If there was more to do than replay levels, like different gamemodes, I would see how it could be worth at least $15, but people aren't kidding when they say this game isn't a long one. Wait until it's on sale to get your money's worth.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Well, that was neat.  :)  Fun mechanics, very unique game experience.  I really enjoyed the design choices for keeping you going in the right direction... I felt relaxation, apprehension, confusion, mild frustration, satisfaction and overall just a neat sense of 'whoa, this is pretty cool' through the whole game.  Short, but fun!  Good stuff, doing something outside the box and making it interesting and enjoyable to play through.I don't know if it would have much replay value for me, but going through the story once was worthwhile.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: What a remarkable piece of art, a journey of dreams, wondering around and falling in love with the landscapes, the speed, the story which it wasnt from the first run always so clear but i had an idea, and that mystery made me want to play it again... and again... and try to make it faster and faster and rip the skies... Simply. one of he greatest gems I ever played the last years, PLEASE MAKE A SECOND JOURNEY
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Akin to sticking your hand out of a car's passenger window and "flying," except instead of your hand flying past cars and over trees, you control a morphable ball-shaped spacecraft that explores breathtaking alien landscapes on a mysterious interplanetary mission. A simple, but beautiful dream-like game and a new favorite.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Fall, find a mountain, increase your gravitational acceleration on slopes, release it on climbs, cross the speed of sound, soar in the ascending winds of clouds.This is all a drug, and like Nina Simone : I am feeling good.You guys have the killer app you were looking for so long.+ Amazing mood and graphics+ Best meteor locomotion system ever- I would love some nice hand crafted level designs to ride like a meteor.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: VIBES. VIBES. VIBES. So cool and very satisfying gameplay. The visuals and the soundtrack is insane. Story is vague, you sort of only sense there is one - but it works imo. Very rarely do you get an artsy game that also has fun and innovative gameplay. I find that most games in that category are walking simulators - but this is a very fun exception. Can definitely recommend. It made me want to make video games.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ▰▰▰▰▰▰▰▰▱▱ Never have I ever had an experience where a game was able to make me feel anxiety and a sense of overwhelm to a sense of peace and calm in a second. Incredibly unique game.The gameplay is easy to pick up and fun, the beginning felt a little overwhelming and anxiety inducing but later levels are great to "zen" off to. Gaining momentum and launching yourself faster than the speed of sound is always satisfying. The graphics overall look great, the terrain textures look flat and lacking in detail but the lighting effects, atmosphere and clouds make up for it. And while the plot was interesting, it felt disconnected from the gameplay and didn't offer enough to form a full story, only to leave speculation and vague guesses.The soundtrack is great but I really wish that it played more often. You usually only hear the soundtrack when you reach a high enough altitude, leaving a bunch of sections completely void of music. But whenever the soundtrack does play, it gives you a sense of serenity. I also really wished this game was longer, or at least had a level selection/sandbox mode as currently you are unable to select a specific level and have to play through the first few panic attack levels to get to the good ones.Although I brought up quite a few negative points, I still believe that Exo One is a truly unique experience and I am really glad that I tried it. This game left me wanting more and I'm really hoping the developers will add more onto this game in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot deny how serene this felt to play through, even if it only lasted a couple hours.  That said I still have 19 other achievements to get so I suppose I'm not done yet!  Also, I'm not sure if it's because it's so lonely or so beautiful, but either way I nearly cried playing this.  I'm shook, SHOOK I TELL YOU!  10/10 for what it is.  Very replayable too, just for the views.  I can only imagine how this would look in 4K at the highest graphics settings...
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: I'm conflicted on if this is a good game or not, I enjoyed the experience in parts but it does get repetitive in some of the levels. Oddly Id actually trim a few levels out to help it be more streamlined, the levels where you are against the elements is fine but there is a water level that I thought was quite short and a little annoying enough for me not to complete the whole game in one sitting. Finishing the game offers no continue or supposed other endings that I could think of. The story is there but you have to piece it together from the fragments of messages you get when you submerge yourself in water or run around in the cloud layer, collecting the orbs that increase you ships power don’t really help explain how much faster or longer you can fly. There are some strange crosses that cover the screen as well which considering we are viewing the game from the outside seems a little odd. Maybe if there had been a first person view from the beginning to choose from and that had the markers it would make sense. The design of the levels are also great at high speeds but getting too close does shows just how low poly the environment looks. I think this an interesting space story that fits in with games like Echo, where you don’t know everything that's going on and that's OK, you there for the ride. However unless there are unlockables I haven't found or something will be added later this is a one and done type of game. Maybe if you get high and just want to fly about you'll get some pc and chill vibes. I give it a B+ the scores for the nice visuals and relaxing music but the repetitive gameplay might put some off, also its a one story experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: A journey through space and time. The graphics are just stunning and the soundtrack hauntingly beautiful. You may feel alone and lost as you travel amongst the planets and stars but you will be compelled to keep progressing. This game is an experience and a fun one at that. First time you fly up through the clouds on an alien world as the sun sets it is just a sight to see. Highly recommend this. Worth the 5 year wait.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: A quick game that can be completed in under two hours, but you shouldn't play it and refund it.You can tell the love that was put into this game, and the interesting mechanics that are thought out, but simple. Not simple in a bad way where they get old.This isn't a game for everyone. There's no "action" per say. It's nice to put on and play, while you have Netflix on the other monitor, or are you just looking to relax.Either way, I can't recommend this project enough from a solo developer who's progress I have watched.Congratulations on an awesome game.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Ball go brrrr whoosh make brain go :)The gameplay, visuals, and sound design are all fantastic, you really feel like a ball cruising along alien planets. The sense of speed and momentum is incredibly well done and the visuals are genuinely beautiful. The music compliments the visuals perfectly with it being chill af. The story is just kinda.. there.. I couldn't really make sense of it and it feels somewhat like an afterthought and actually jumpscared me a couple times when I was focused lol, but it doesn't detract at all from the game. Personally I wish there were more structures and whatnot, it'd be so freaking cool if there were like remains of buildings you could zoom through or like giant skeletons or something. I do wish the game was longer for how fast (pun intended) you cruise through it, as at just under 3 hours it doesn't really feel like you get your money's worth.My final verdict is this: The game is incredibly fun and incredibly beautiful, I bought it for $14 during the winter steam sale so it was at a slight discount, I just wish it had something like workshop support so there can be more levels. For such a short game I don't really think the $17 price tag fits, but the game is still great nonetheless and if you're looking for something chill to play in an afternoon this is it.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: It's finally out. And it is a beautiful, hypnotic, intelligently designed gaming meditation. While they tell you the controls of the ship, that's all. It's designed so intuitively, you just know where to go without the game saying a word. It's systems work, as designed. The skill floor is so accessible, so easy to pick and you are already playing. But the fact that you learn what gets you more speed, more distance, like diving and quickly flattening for a visceral boost to your sense of speed and distance.I love it. I LOVE IT. PLEASE, I NEED MORE OF THIS GAME.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful experience with very satisfying movement mechanics.My favorite experience of the year.3 inputs is all you need-Gravity Drive-Glide-Double JumpSimple controls yield to complex mechanics in getting and maintaining speed, great for speedrunning. This isn't crucial during the first playthrough, as the experience is quite enough imo.Expect the first playthrough to last between 1-3 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: has to be one of the strangest and most unusual games I've ever played.  It is difficult to liken it to other games because it's actually quite unique.  If I had to, though, I'd mention a likeness to  and , two games in which flight plays a vital role.  So maybe I should describe  as a kind of flight simulator.You control the movement of an alien craft that can alternate between two shapes - a sphere and a flat oval - and propels itself forward by means of a gravity drive.  It took me two to three playthroughs to fully grasp and master this very basic but unique propulsion system (that's just me though).It's a visually attractive game.  You visit ten planets, all with different landscapes and moods, with strange structures, floating islands, weather systems, otherworldly formations and hints of other lifeforms.  The alien beauty of it all can be hypnotic.  Breaching the sound barrier is a kaleidoscopic experience.The objective is to reach the teleportation structure on each planet - indicated by a thin blue line - that will transport you to your next destination.  You may be aided by the weather and flight-boosting devices on your way. is dedicated to those astronauts who were lost to humanity, as well as the powerful attraction that space exploration has on the human psyche.  May we never stop dreaming of what we may find out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: This game in one word is phenomenal. The visuals are very pleasing, the music is just absolutely amazing, it plays very well, it’s something you can play all the way through in just a couple hours, the story is amazing. Everything about this game is great. There’s definitely some scary elements to it. If you have thalassophobia theres a couple parts that  will get you, it did for me for a total of like 45 minutes. Nyctophobia is also a thing for only about 15-20 minutes. It makes it more interesting and it’s amazing. Seriously go play this game, it’s not expensive, it’s beautiful, the soundtrack is good, controls are amazing, and it’s all round fun. Branch out like I did and take a chance with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard not to recommend this game as it's different to most other games with it's unique movement mechanics and interesting audio/visuals. It has a great feel to it and it's almost worth it for the ride alone. I wish I could give a neutral review as there should be more games like this and I don't regret playing it.It  by being a one-track experience where you go from start to finish, with the only one single other objective being a power-up boost that you may or may not need. The maps are large and have a lot of surface level intrigue but really don't reward exploration; many maps can be literally flown over without missing much. There is no level select option in case you liked a map and want to revisit it. Level selection will probably be added in later patches but it's simply not worth slogging through cutscenes to get to the "fun" parts again. It feels like another tech demo phase rather than a full game at the moment.The gameplay hinges on one single mechanic- the spaceship you fly, and that's it. Different maps will remove or give some very slight variation to its functions, but it's the entire focus start to finish, which makes it feel like a linear walking sim. The story has a severe case of indie-game-itis where it's vague and only very loosely pertains to the actual gameplay. It actually detracts from the experience in some cases, where you're having a relaxing romp through a tropical paradise and it jumpscares you with a random image to hint that you have some sort of "mission". It would be nice to be able to straight-up disable the story in later patches.It's not for everyone but it's a good pick as-is, maybe even a great one for people that just need something to roll around in and relax. For others that like exploring or varied mechanics though, it's pretty shallow. A single run through the story will amount to around two hours, which for its current price point and lack of features tips the scales for me. If just the thought of breaking the sound barrier gets you excited, give it a try- if you want something deep/compelling that will keep your attention for more than a few hours, hard pass.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Great, short game (<3 hours) about speed and efficient motion as you explore grand, alien landscapes and towering black monoliths that bounce between worlds that are, beautiful, desolate, awe inspiring and terrifying, in an Arther C. Clarke inspired sci fi setting. (2001: A Space Odyssey)The story is fed through flashbacks and disembodied voices. The game has some beautiful landscapes for you to roll and glide through. Moments in the game made me stop in awe of my surroundings. Some graphics are a bit rough around the edges with geometric clipping (rolling through trees with no effect) that kinda took me out of the immersion. I really wish there was more to the game after beating it. A new game+ where you have all your upgrades would be nice, or even a level select or free roam mode. I do wish the landscapes were a bit more interactive.I don't know if the hamster ball on Daramulum was supposed to make me incredibly motion sick or not, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ did I almost not make it through that... I'm not looking forward to reliving that segment of the game.Coronides was an amazing sequence, jumping from asteroid to asteroid.Coelus... One of my favorite landscapes.The game ends and you're left with satisfaction, but also... disappointment and wanting more... I hope the developer updates the game to give it more life. Otherwise, it's an enjoyable, planetary exploration game that feels truly alien in every aspect.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Crank the video settings up to ultra and you'll truly appreciate the visuals of this game (1440p works perfectly with it too). The sound, the levels, and the mechanics are all fantastic.Yes it is a short game, but you have to think that 1 person developed this by himself. There's plenty of secrets and achievements for people who are so inclined. If you appreciate a game for visuals/art/feeling, this game is a must play (and well worth the original price).If you appreciate a game for playability and complexity/story then I would buy this when it comes on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a "kinda" option for reccomendation. The game is very short, has no level selection, and no endless mode, which I feel is nessecary for a game like this. The gameplay is fun and satisfying, but there isnt really any reward for exploration and it doesnt have much replayability since you have to go through the water world and jungle world to get to some of the better ones.If they add secrets and a level select it would be worth buying at full price, with an endless mode it would be probably the best time waster/relaxing game on steam
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: I am really surprised to see so many positive reviews for this game. If I had to guess without looking, I would have expected many more negatives. Unpopular opinion I guess.This an unfortunate case of unachieved potential. The game has a control scheme that is legitimately fun to use. What it lacks is levels that use that the control scheme in fun ways. It seems like the thing to blame for that deficiency is the story and that's a problem on its own.The story is esoteric and nearly impossible to follow. I feel like I could figure out what was happening in episode 1 of Star Wars faster than this. A few comments mentioned Journey as a comparison. That game had almost no text, if any, and managed to deliver a story with identifiable beats that I still remember. Exo One, on the other hand, does the opposite. I have reached the end of the game and I still can't explain what happened besides a few words that establish a vague setting. In contrast, I can give you a rough idea about why a cloth person is hangin' out with floating cloth creatures in Journey. There is an entire sea of things that I can't explain in Exo One. Why is the player being brought to different planets? What are the energy balls I am collecting? Why does every line of intangible dialogue sound like it's being played in reverse with a crap ton of reverb? Why the hell does the game insist on flashing images into my retinas when I get close to an energy ball or go fast? Seriously, what's the point of that? It's like paint was just flung at a wall and a viewer is supposed to get something more from it besides "that's splashes of paint on a wall." If the game is going to supply a story, that story needs to be understandable. If nothing is understandable, why should a player get invested? If a player doesn't get invested, why should they care to continue? I certainly didn't, and I find the lack of a skip cut-scene button ironic, because it's one of the instances where I would have actually used it. For reference now and in the future, here are the percentage of players that completed this game vs some others. The achievement name for completion is to the right of the game. Let the data speak.And the worst part, what really gets a kick in the nuts is the maps. It's as if the maps are fighting against the player controller in some instances. Here are some clips as examples. Spoilers? Idk, I couldn't spoil it for you if I tried. , , , . Besides the brief touch of the ol' PP-Bizon provided by the asteroid level [2], which ended as quickly as it began, many levels are a drag to traverse. They are anywhere from sitting on a bench to a stool with nails. Each of them just feels like another place to sit and none fit the mold of the player controller's ass just right. Why aren't there massive hills with interesting curves that the player can roll the ball down? Why aren't there huge ramps in the sky that that the player is supposed to use in combination with each other? What about cloud highways to race on? Why aren't large portions of levels clearly crafted to make the player controller feel awesome? Instead, most of them lack any such intent. Fundamentally, most of the levels scream tech demo rather than game and it seems like so much more is possible. That's a shame considering the player controller is quite fluid and it's why I labeled this as unacheived potential at the beginning of this half review half rant.Why doesn't it provide it? I can't back it up, so I'll leave this as an afterthought. The setting of the story seemed like it stopped the levels from going down this route. There are direct counter arguments to this though: huge floating cubes, insanely powerful boost gates, strange large warp structures, etc.. Then again, would mega roll the ball tracks be too far?
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: It feels good to shut down all these half finished "pay to win" games released by big companies and just enjoy a game like Exo One. Beautiful music, amazing texture and a short but very interessting story behind it. The mystery of the story got me easily hooked and I played through the game in the middle of the night instead of going to sleep. No Man's Sky developers should have hired Jay Weston. He alone could have saved the game on the day it was released.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: This game is super re-playable, very fun, and very well designed. It's extremely therapeutic for my anxiety and really glad this game has released. It's short, but this will be a game I will continually come back to just because of how the game feels so...freeing. No other word to describe it. Love the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game as a relaxing journey into beautiful cosmic scenery accompanied by sweeping ambient tunes. You'll never see an enemy in this game, but you will see a lot of interesting landscapes, fun level features, and a fairly unique gravity system. This is an easy game to kick back with for 20 minus and forget everything else. Or 2 hours, your choice.Two hours is about what it took me to beat the game. That's about the price of a two-hour movie ticket, so that's how I think of the price. It's definitely replayable, but you'll get bored after your second or third run.I only have two complaints, and I rate them both as minor complaints. One: the game features graceful movement and blistering speed, but occasionally you'll run into the side of a hill or something that will eat all of your momentum and make you start from scratch. A Sonic-like spindash move would get you back up to speed quickly. The other thing is the story. I am happy being an alien ship that skips its way across the galaxy. I don't need low-value cut scenes of some astronauts that are metaphysically entwined with the alien ship I'm flying. It does absolutely nothing for the core value of the game.Okay, I spent way too much time criticizing it - it's actually a ton of fun and there are so many beautiful sights to behold. I recommend it at the $15 price.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Exo One was quit enjoyable. Short but sweet. I would consider it more of a vibe than a game, with its atmospheric and particle effects very hypnotic at times. If you're looking for something to enjoy with some good tunes, this is a fun play. I do wish they included alien life of some kind on these planets that have you playing on.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: mmm, that was a game, kindathe gameplay was fun, really fun, i cant overstate how fun it is. visuals are interesting, overwhelming, sometimes confusing but it all works in the setting mostly. theres a story, kind of, well not really, theres a random string of phrases based loosely around the theme of space travel. there are ofcourse bug-out-your-ship glitches.then just as the game gets going, you get a long but pretty cut scene and are dumped in to an endless stream of clouds.also the pause menu stops working so when you finally figure out youre in a post credit endless runner, or i guess endless flyer, because the pause menu doesnt work, you have no way to exit the game past alt tabbing and closing it down from windowsi dont think i can recommend it, which is sad, but ive come out of it feeling like ive just played one long tutorial for a bunch of really well made mechanics, that never got to be used in a full game. i dont regret purchasing it, theres defiantly no reason to refund, but i also dont think its worth £15. i guess, a really cool tech demo might be a good way of describing it.-------------------------------------------------------Edit: there are a lot of arguments for this game being considered either an exploration game or an art gamethis isnt an exploration game, huge levels with nothing in them are not exploration games, this is an much an exploration game as any procedurally generated rouge like in that case. no mans sky original had the same issue of being an exploration game without exploration, if you can go through a level for 5 minutes and you have seen everything that level has to offer twice over, you are not playing an exploration game.this isnt an art game.... what are you talking about? all games are art, this has as much artistic merit as any other game
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: When this game released, I reviewed it with a No, not because it was bad, but because my PC was pretty bad and the game crashed a lot, making it impossible to finish it for me.Now I have a new PC that's not bad at all, and I finnally got to finish the game, and with great graphics and all!Yes, this is a good game. A short one for sure, and a simple one also. But it has great replayability, and if you like Clarke, Sagan or Lem, then for sure this will be interesting for you.PD.: Sorry for the original bad review. I erased it time before this one, but I know it is not justified.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely gorgeous and VERY fun to play....For the very short duration that you can play it. Look this game is a gorgeous work of art that the creator poured their soul into. I'll still play this game here and there when I'm bored. However I do have a few complaints. The planets are to few in number is the first issue I have, nobody wants a game FILLED with filler planets that have no content but you need SOME fluffed content in games to make it worth the persons money and give them plenty to do. Honestly my other complaint is music. GREAT soundtrack...the first time I heard it. I'm not sure how the music is obtained or licensed but I would consider a SIGNIFICANT increase in playlist size. What music is there is very good, so however it was obtained keep that method. Overall, the game is hella fun and gorgeous to boot but it's just to short, you can roll around a planet forever but there is only so much per planet before its all the same. Due to this and the price I'll not recommend it for now. Drop the price to $10 (no less) or add more planets.(if this game had randomly generated terrain and planets I'd EASILY pay $25 for this.)
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: I think I found the perfect game that is both relaxing and exhilarating. If you're into sci-fi and wonder what it would be like to be a fast moving probe gliding across the landscape of an alien planet and taking in the wonderful views. Then this is the game for you. There is enough here to keep yourself engaged while you seek how to best maintain the best speeds most effectively. This I recommend.  I have not finished yet but I did already make a game play video with the song Might Wings from Top Gun in it to match the visuals.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: This one is a gorgeous adventure odysey that I personally enjoyed the physics-based traversal.  The story is a bit all over the place, but considering how breathtaking the visuals tend to be, I'd say it doesn't matter at all.  The price reflects the length of the game though... it doesn't last long.  But hey, I played it more than once and I plan on playing it sometime when I want a little scenery candy!
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to keep this very brief; since I saw the demo (and subsequent Prologue) for Exo One earlier this year, I was hooked. It's just the right blend of surreal, sci-fi, and story-based to have hooked my interest, particularly since much of the story is only inferred as you play. It's gorgeous to look at (so many wallpaper opportunities) and remarkably easy to play. It's almost a game that you can relax with, just skimming about a planet's surface or atmosphere to unwind after work.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: I had no idea WTF was going on throughout this entire game. That said, it was surprisingly Zen.Probably some kind of abstract thing going on here? There's no real connection between anything. You're just a ball rolling through a planet until you get shot to another planet where.. you roll about. It's interspersed with.. not really dialog, that doesn't seem to have much connection to what you're actually doing/meant to be doing (whatever that is).Thumbs upping it, purely because there's no neutral option.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: i thank the developer for this art of creativity. the sound, the atmosphere and construction is superb. i played it since the demo already for many hours. good job! I'd also love to see this with a high texture pack or something, that would be even more better than it is :) i bought the game at full price on steam to support the developer in the first place and then the publisher as well of course.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: , a simple gameplay idea wrapped in beautiful scenery and a short sci-fi story.You can manipulate the gravity affecting your spherical spacecraft, and as simple as that you’ve created a satisfying mechanic, increasing gravity near slopes to rapidly accelerate, and relaxing it to be shoot off once you encounter a ramp or dune, add in the ability to glide and a triple jump for more precise course adjustments and voilà, you’ll have an incredible relaxing game, also carried in no small part by the ambience it creates with vast sprawls of land and great sound effects.Now, the pricetag may be a bit high since it’s a short experience, coupled with the fact that it doesn’t seem too polished may dissuade you from buying this.I personally recommend it, especially if it’s on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game! It appeared to be one of the best VR experiences for me! It can be run with VorpX. Absolutely stunning! Author must release native VR version.Please complain that it is a short game but for me it is not about getting to the end but enjoy the atmosphere. I can endlessly fly over the Aquarius ocean without any rush to complete the level.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: This is what a masterpiece looks like.Marble madness meets Flight of the Navigator meets Interstellar in the shadow of a 2001 a space odyssey monolith. (Or Journey meets super monkey ball? Lol Idk!)When you invent a rolling/flying mechanic that feels this good to play, and then you make it look as good as this. And *then* you play with the rules on each exo-planet you visit to add variety. And then you add some nice story too. Well... It's just brilliant! It even got me in the feels at the end.Soundtrack is suitably epic.If I had to be really picky, I'd say that dam section when you are in the "big ball" in one of the earlier levels could be more polished, because I did manage to get it wedged somewhere it couldn't move. Other than that the whole game is pretty perfect.If I had one (actually 2) request(s). they would be... "could you make this work in VR please?" followed by... could you make an option so I can use the mouse to move and look around using keys (or my vr headset) so I could use a trackball to roll around!I waited for a sale, but it is actually totally worth the full price, so I bought a second copy for my brother.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: You know those momentum based hill games you play on your phone? This is that. I was hoping for an original idea and this is unfortunately not that. It is however very, very pretty. There is no story. If you want an art game I may instead recommend Manifold Garden as it actually has gameplay. Pick it up on sale. My review is neutral.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: Well worth the purchase. If you're after something where you can simply chill out and enjoy the experience, this is the perfect game. It's a short game, but I played it in small amounts over a long period.Exo One provides a nice mental cleanse between the competitive shooters, RTS, and RPGs where action and violence is the focus. The environments are vast and beautiful, and the audio and music compliments them perfectly, with just enough of a cryptic "story" unfolding to proved the idea of what's happened while remaining mysterious and frankly quite odd.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely beautiful; the music and sound are fantastic. At first it's a little bit confusing what's going on, but you can figure it out fairly quickly. You are this little marble rolling, bouncing and gliding your way across various planets as you solve problems to keep going. All the while trying to unravel a greater mystery. I will say it's not very long ~2-3 hrs. and replayability seems low to me, but I really enjoyed it.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

_childDocuments_.review: A strange signal… an alien craft… Exo One is an interplanetary, gravity-defying journey through space and time. Master a truly alien traversal system and move through enigmatic and desolate landscapes in ways you’ve never experienced. Use gravity and momentum to reach colossal speeds and exhilarating heights.
_childDocuments_.name: Exo One

name: SCARLET NEXUS
detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Edition The Deluxe Edition includes the SCARLET NEXUS full game and Brain Punk Bundle, along with 2 bonuses. Ultimate Edition The Ultimate Edition includes the full game, Season Pass, Digital Artbook & Soundtrack, an Attire Set, an Additional Attachment, and Plug-ins. About the Game In the far distant future, a psionic hormone was discovered in the human brain, granting people extra-sensory powers and changed the world as we knew it. As humanity entered this new era, deranged mutants known as Others began to descend from the sky with a hunger for human brains. Highly resistant to conventional attack methods, extreme measures needed to be taken to battle the overwhelming threat and preserve humanity. Those with acute extra-sensory abilities, known as psionics, were our only chance to fight the onslaught from above. Since then, psionics have been scouted for their talents and recruited to the Other Suppression Force (OSF), humanity’s last line of defense. Featuring a dual story, begin your adventure with either Yuito Sumeragi, an energetic recruit from a prestigious political family or Kasane Randall, the mysterious scout whose power and skill has gained great notoriety among the OSF. As their different experiences interweave with each other, it is only then that you will reveal the full story and unlock all the mysteries of a Brain Punk future caught between technology and psychic abilities in SCARLET NEXUS. Kinetic Psychic Combat – Using psycho-kinetic abilities, the world around you becomes your greatest weapon. Lift, break and throw pieces of your environment to build your attack combos and lay waste to your enemies. Exterminate the Others – Deranged mutants that descended from the sky, highly resistant to conventional attack methods and defenses. Tormented by the constant pain of their mutation, they seek brains of living organisms to calm their madness. Discover a Brain Punk future – Explore and protect a futuristic Japanese landscape that combines inspirations from classic anime and western science fiction. A Dual Story Experience – Dive into a complex story of bonds, courage and heroism, crafted by minds behind the iconic Tales of Vesperia.
