_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is fun if you like hack and slash. The one thing that bothered me is how dull the characters can be sometimes. In certain parts of the game the main character will be like "oh no are you okay" when obviously the character who got hurt is not Okay!Ill give this game a 8/10  wish we had a tales of arise demo :(
_childDocuments_.name: SCARLET NEXUS

_childDocuments_.review: So you have telekinesis, what can you do? Other than throw things at monsters, nothing.How about something other than fighting monsters to do in the game? Like bank heists, building structures, lifting yourself off the ground and flying to other destinations. Go wild with the things you would do if you could move objects with your mind!Another problem I have is locking skills & items behind story progression points. Like it would mean so much to me if there was a JRPG where you could see the $1,000,000 sword at the beginning of the game, you may not have enough money for it but you can at least see it's for sale at the shop. It's 2021, stop locking items behind "Oh I've been working on this in my shop for you" cutscene.The bad news: I got exactly what I expected from this game. A hack & slash monster hunter game with telekinesis but you can only use it in battle.
_childDocuments_.name: SCARLET NEXUS

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews but i think this one deserves it.36 hours into the game and i JUST finished the story playing on Hard Difficulty, which made it extremely fun.Combat system is VERY fun, i was actually surprised and it goes quite in depth with the crazy BS you can do later down the line, i'm a sucker for Hack and Slash games so i'm very picky with that, it keeps and keeps surprising you with stuff, not even exaggerating.It's quite a LONG game, so you get your money's worth, i barely did any idequest and i completed it with the girl so haven't even touched the other character yet, and it will follow his side of the story, and there's a LOT that i didn't see of the other character in this playthrough, they go through different routes so it's not just a character swap with the same things. etc  Oh and the music is so good, do yourself a favour and turn music slighly or all the way up, the soundtrack is a banger.What else... idk dude this was such a fun game, still gotta play more, recommended 100%
_childDocuments_.name: SCARLET NEXUS

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for an anime game with polished graphics and good combat + a good story, this is for you.My only problem with the game is what everyone else is saying: This game is NOT for mouse and keyboard. You HAVE to play with a controller. It's the only way.Besides that, the combo system and visuals are great. I'm actually liking the way the long dialogue parts are filled with the game's aesthetic. It makes the whole experience more pleasing to the eye.Executions are my fav part. All of them look cool.Kyoka Eden is hot.
_childDocuments_.name: SCARLET NEXUS

_childDocuments_.review: Scarlet Nexus is an oddity to me. I played it, binged it infact, finished both sides of the campaign and completed all the achievements in less than a month and it made it into my 2022 Steam Replay as one of my most played games. And yeah, I thoroughly enjoyed my time playing it. The story was interesting (a bit darker than I imagined, but hey I like depressing stories for some reason), the gameplay was good and the music some of the best I've heard in a game released recently.However once I finished it, it kind of slipped from my mind. It just didn't leave that big of an impression on me and I kind of forgot it existed up until I saw it in my Replay.But I would still recommend it to anyone who is on the fence about trying it. The story is interesting and the gameplay has some unique ideas to differentiate itself from other hack'n'slashers. Just don't expect it to blow your mind.
_childDocuments_.name: SCARLET NEXUS

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first game I've ever felt compelled to review. I bought the deluxe edition and this game is worth every penny of it. The story kept me on my toes the entire time with how meticulously convoluted it is and how it sticks to it. I have yet to experience Kasane's story so I can only speculate but Yuito's story is currently a ride and a half. On top of the amazing story, the characters writing and design keeps the pace with it. They all feel very fleshed out in their bond episodes and I can actually feel like I'm getting to understand and like them better as genuine people. Each character has their own personal problems and they all get the time to explore and deal with it inbetween the main story. The enemies, while little in variation, are all very well designed too and the combat, while repetitive, is still fun for me in the late game. Seeing Yuito brain crush a Auger Ritter is still as cool as it was the first time. I know this is a very shallow review but I can't coherently express how much I've enjoyed every aspect of this game. If you like stories that are like Durarara in their levels of convolution, amazing characters and a bumping soundtrack, get this game. Bandai Namco really knocked it out of the park with this one.
_childDocuments_.name: SCARLET NEXUS

_childDocuments_.review: This was my first "anime" game with 2 storylines to choose from and I give it a 8/10. The story was hard to piece together at certain areas, and I told myself to see it through till the end. Overall the story was aight (Note, I only played Yuito's storyline, and I felt pretty exhausted so I'll probably do Kasane's in the future)The art style was also amazing, I really enjoyed the visual and graphics, the ambience and scenery. The character designs are also unique .The fighting mechanics however was outstanding, I found it very fun to pull combos and slice the ♥♥♥♥ out of the enemies. After that I came home and played Scarlet Nexus.
_childDocuments_.name: SCARLET NEXUS

_childDocuments_.review: The game is nice, has great graphics, and an enthralling story... but the combat is repetitive and boring. All you do is just do the same 3 hit combo while flinging everything you can find at your enemy. Psychokinesis is one of my least favorite fantasy abilities which makes this whole game a drag. All they would've had to do is let you play as the other characters that actually have cool abilities and the game would be amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: SCARLET NEXUS

_childDocuments_.review: This game is only for those die hard manga fans that would love to sit there for hours watching manga style cutscenes with a little combat thrown into the mix. I am really trying to enjoy this game but I have never been the die hard anime type. Wish I could give this a mediocre rating because thats what it deserves.
_childDocuments_.name: SCARLET NEXUS

_childDocuments_.review: I love this Game.It has a pretty interesting combat-mechanic.The story is also very good.The characters are nice, but pretty streamlined JRPG-stereotypes.The Music is fine and so is the english syncro for the voices.There is just a tiny bit of grinding which is rare in JRPGs in my experience.The ONLY things which are bad are for one, most bossfights, because of being cheap (beatable of course but badly made) and two, an occasional bug, that freezes the game in a way that makes it necessary torestart the PC, so SAVE OFTEN !!!But besides the two negative things, the game is a top buy recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: SCARLET NEXUS

_childDocuments_.review: I already knew this was going to be a great game before it came out and was not surprised at all after getting the chance to play it, and yes this is a great game.The story is split between two main characters, Yuito and Kasane and you get to choose who to play as in the beginning. I don’t think it really matters who you play as first or in which order as they’re both great though I played the Yuito story first and then played the Kasane story because I somehow felt like doing it. Also another thing regarding the story, it would be best if you played BOTH characters and stories if you want to get the complete story, since both characters have their own unique story lines and scenes that intertwine and connect, and thus there may be gaps in the story that you may not understand if you only played one of the stories. The story itself is alright, I found it a bit weird at times but still fine for the most part.The gameplay is excellent. The fighting and combat in this game is top tier in a way that you can perform many different kinds of attacks and combinations using different powers and abilities creating a dynamic, fun and engaging variety of methods to take out enemies. The combat also encourages the player to make use of their surroundings to their advantage like using certain objects around the environment to attack enemies in very cool ways. It is addicting and I never got bored of it at all and this is where this game shines the most in my opinion.The characters are interesting and their bonding events are also equally interesting as you learn more about their personalities and their other selves. The environment is also very cool looking, especially the city area and the soundtrack is also pretty decent.In regards to the two main characters, personally I think Yuito has a better combat and attack style while Kasane has a better story perspective and personality. Either way, they’re both great characters.However there seems to be some criticism from people who claim that there is too much dialogue in this game and it feels like it’s a visual novel at times but personally I don’t see the big deal. Most anime games tend to have a lot of dialogue and overall the large amount of dialogue in this game doesn’t take away the game’s immersion at all as the dialogues are also quite interesting. But if you’re the person who doesn’t like reading and listening through plenty of dialogues, then I suppose I can understand why you might not like this game.Overall though, the pros outweigh the cons here and this is definitely something worth playing, for both anime and non-anime fans, though anime fans would probably appreciate this more.
_childDocuments_.name: SCARLET NEXUS

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what a game. I'm really impressed with this complex ga- experience rather. This is what next gen should look like. High octane action, gripping story, plenty of visual options to switch the style up. Gameplay: 9-10/10 depending on how much you like deciphering maps and running around stages.Graphics: 10/10 beautiful with unique character designsPerformance: 10/10 on a typical modern gaming PC. No hiccups or crashes.This game deserves every penny it asks for, and all the time required to play it to completion.
_childDocuments_.name: SCARLET NEXUS

It is well made and keep the flow of stories goes smoothly.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most fun action RPG releases in recent years. The gameplay is definitely where the game shines and the sheer amount of combos you can perform with different party members keep combat exciting. Although the plot starts out really well, it unfortunately drags on during certain sections of story-line and the ending felt rushed. Nevertheless, the gameplay will keep you entertained till the end. Even if the ending felt a bit rushed to me, the plot is still very unique and will keep you interested till the very end.Overall 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not one to write reviews as i just can't be bothered most of the time, but i am.In the small time (soon to grow) that i played scarlet nexus i have thoroughly enjoyed most of it.The combat is great, very reminiscent of Nier automata and anyone familiar with that game or it's combat style will feel right at home, there is also a hint of bayonetta in the mix, with perfect dodges and abilities reminiscent of witch time. The only thing hampering the combat is the absolutely trash control scheme for mouse and keyboard (my faulty for not having a controller so disregard it if you have one) where you often get stuck on targeting one enemy and the camera is nigh uncontrollable.Other than that, which can be solved very easily with any controller the combat is a solid 9/10 for me.The story is divided into two campaigns, one playing as Yuito Sumeragi and another playing as Kasane Randall.You need to play both campaigns to truly understand the story, but it wont leave you completely clueless as to whats going on like some people are saying.I'm playing the Kasane campaign and never once have i felt completely lost, on the other hand there are plenty of twists and turns to keep you on your toes.Overall the story is solid and a fresh take on this type of narrative, 8/10.The music is a bit repetitive and weird at times, where you're about to fight some others and you have this overly happy tune in the background, that can be rather weird and anticlimactic, but when the music choice actually corresponds what's happening its quite good. 6/10Graphics are good for a JRPG and i'm pretty sure that a potato could run this game thanks to it's stylised aesthetic. If you like this sort of look in a game you will definitely enjoy what's on display in scarlet nexus since the graphics are very good. 8/10Overall i think this game is most definitely worth a shot if you have the cash to spare and nothing to do for 30-50 hrs.Final score: 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Would rate this meh if I could. Downvoted only because I feel like it's not as fun as other games at 80-85% positive. Get on discount if you're going to, and I think there's other stuff that's more worth your time unless you're specifically into this kind of gameplay like a more recent Tales game. The combat is stiff until you get about half way through the game and doesn't really flow well until the last quarter of the story. There's apparently some postgame stuff to use all the things on, but i'm not super motivated to do it since the combat got a bit repetitive and particularly consistent fun after a bit of having roughly all the abilities due to the way some enemies work. The story is very predictable but adequate and never felt particularly painful since it does actually progress rather than spinning wheels on the same point like many mediocre plotlines do. The characters are standard anime archetype personalities done well enough with some fun gags. Of the two main character companions, the Yuito group seems to be more kiddos plus one old guy, while Kasane's group is somewhat more mature in attitude overall but still early twentiesish level of maturity at most. The plot reflects this relatively teenager-minded cast so don't expect serious time travel psychological drama out of it.Nothing notably bad about the game's build quality other than levels are reused more than I feel was appropriate. You visit an uninspiring construction site like 5 times for story reasons. What's there works, didn't run into major issues, etc. It's just not really inspiring unless you really like generic younger shounen anime with an occasionally neat but underused aesthetic/theme.

_childDocuments_.review: I am about halfway through with Yuitos story, and dang, I really love this game. It will make the wait for Tales of Arise a lot less painful. It has beautifully designed characters, both visually and, well, characteristically. I can listen to their problems and stories for hours. You can see how much work the team put into this, they want you to love the cast, and they did it. Except for Gemma I even love all the choices for the english dubs. It can be cringy sometimes but that is to be expected from an anime game. I cannot really say anything about the story yet, since I have not finished it (Phase 9). So far it had a lot of twists and events that just left me more confused than before, yet always coming back to see what happened next. Definitely not the strongest point of the game but bearable. And now, the big one. Combat. You have SO. MANY. OPTIONS. The combat is insanely polished, a lot of different features that can be used. It feels a lot better than any hack and slash anime game. I don't want to spoil anything, but the amount of commands, combos and attacks you can execute is just crazy. In some battles I find myself not pressing any button combination twice. And if you do not grind and play the game on hard you also get quite the challenge, however it gets a lot easier once you revisit old areas and gain some levels and unlock more skills. All in all this has to be the hidden gem, the must-play game of the year for me. BIG recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is very good. The game play loop is similar to games like persona but dumbed down. Instead of a dungeon or what have you, you're just exploring earth as a whole. You will do storyline 'missions' which are separated by 'standby phases' where you socialize with your group, give gifts, watch bonding episodes like those in  Xenoblade Chronicles, and do side quests. Fortunately nothing really seems too time sensitive quest wise but I was not a completionist by any means. I did however play both main stories. You do get what is essentially the full story on one playthrough, but with most games like this the ending is the same for both stories, it's the first 75% where there's some differences primarily in the 'missions' each protagonist goes on and some individual story bites, as well as the team members you are forced to use for that portion of the game. I will say that if there's a secret ending or something to unlock by meeting some criteria I definitely didn't do that, so correct me if I'm wrong there. The game does use new game + features, and the normal game comes with a no lose button (an accessory that prevents you from going below 1hp) as well as a 2x xp multiplier so if the typical daunting grind of a jrpg is holding you back, it helps.Overall I'd give this an 8/10 the combat is unique and refreshing in some ways but at the end of the day it's a lot of damage sponge enemies and gimmick enemies, and really the combat loop does become boring, granted I played both stories back to back so it might just be over exposure. The mini map shows icons of intractable stuff in the level and literally calls them gimmicks which is a bit funny, at least they recognize it.You'll be seeing a lot of your typical anime tropes in this game, and they deus ex you a few times, but it's an original enough concept and the characters are all likable enough that overall its a good experience. The story could be better, but it isn't glaringly cringe by any means. If you like linear games with an OK story and entertaining combat it's an alright new IP. They left enough in there to make a sequel or prequel without making it a cliffhanger. If you don't like games that force social ♥♥♥♥ on you though you will be handicapping yourself by not doing it, so keep that in mind, too. It's not difficult, just a lot of unskippable scenes.Overall it's worth a buy, likely not at full price but it's good enough to drop 50 hours on if you enjoy the combat.

_childDocuments_.review: Scarlet Nexus definitely has little bugs scattered around the place, but it's a solid bi-linear action game, nonetheless.The game is lengthy - I clocked 26hrs, though it's a bit less considering that includes menu time and time figuring out where the damn Exit Game button is! My 26hrs only includes ONE playthru, and NO quests (they're kinda pointless). I was ready to finish the game after 20hrs in, yet the gameplay and story keep you engaged til the end.Combat has way too many buttons to keep track of, but it's core design is excellent. The different attack options are wonderful, and the graphics match very well. It's always satisfying to get a nice finisher in on an enemy.The game is available in a native Japanese or English setting, which is a plus to some. Voice acting is very good as well.One thing that urked me was the item they throw in your inventory right from the beginning - a "You can never die" god item. Having such petty options in a game always seems tasteless to me. ANYONE can boast they beat the game in X fashion, while we may never know if it's true or not.I certainly recommend this game to any action game fan.

If you value your time, then maybe pass up on this game till you don't have any others. If you don't mind using a lot of time, or don't have the money for mutiple games in a given time, it might be a good one to get It's not the best dense and most enjoyable at any moment of experiences, but it does keep you decently entertained and intersted for a good long time. The abilities, movement, and combos all feel really good with the exception of some "hold the button" abilities, and unlike some of the other reviews here, the story and bond episodes are what kept me the most interested in this game.a solid "That seems to be the spot" out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: SCARLET NEXUS is an action RPG with a great emphasis on story. Overall, the gameplay and story are good enough for me to start and finish a second playthrough.The general combat plays like NieR: Automata plus Control, you have light, heavy and aerial attacks plus a dash as your dodge, you also have the ability to throw environmental objects at your enemies. The real fun of SCARLET NEXUS' combat system comes from the SAS, basically you can temporarily borrow your friends' superpowers and incorporate them in your combat. For example, borrowing Pyrokinesis gives your attacks more damage and the ability to burn enemies; borrowing Invisibility lets you recover safely or set up a strong backstab; borrowing Hypervelocity gives you super speed by slowing everything else around you etc. Your success in combat hinges on how well you can combine your friends' powers together, at first you can only borrow 1 power at a time, but later on with some upgrades in the skill tree you can borrow 4 powers at once. Using SAS itself is also visually satisfying and the small animation it plays still doesn't get old after my second playthrough.The story of SCARLET NEXUS has an interesting take on storytelling as there're 2 protagonists with different perspectives here, meaning you'll have to play the game twice to get the full picture. Gameplaywise there isn't a huge difference as in 1 is way stronger than the other, and the in game description of their playstyles is fairly accurate. Personally I really like the story, especially the character design. Each character's superpower matches their personality and weapon pretty well, like it's ironic to have a lazy character with super speed or have fire powers and uses a torch as weapon. The plot itself is fine and is easy to follow, there're some twists and turns here, nothing too ridiculous, and most of the important plot points will also have a recap message later on just in case you’ve missed something.There’re some design choices here I don’t mind but some people might take issue with. Combatwise the game isn’t really challenging, as most superpowers are strong even by itself, you can imagine how easy the game can get once you can combine 4 powers at once. This isn’t a huge problem for me because being overpowered is part of the fun of having superpowers to begin with. Another problem with the combat is how healing is handled, much like in NieR: Automata, your healing in combat relies on consumable healing items that can be purchased endlessly. There’re 6 types of healing items and each can stack up to 10, if you stock up on healing items in the end game you can have up to 38 health bars restored. Again this isn’t a huge issue for me because it’s a single player game and my focus is on the story. Storywise most of the game’s cutscene are in still image and will auto scroll to the next image after finishing some dialogues. I don’t really mind the comic book feel of it and I even turned off auto scrolling in the options menu for better readability.That being said, SCARLET NEXUS does have some rather obvious issues. Although there’s a lot of maps in game, both protagonist’s campaign somehow requires you to revisit the same map multiple times, the worse example is in 1 campaign where you’ll be fighting a nearly identical boss in the same area twice. Speaking of bosses, besides the end game bosses which are both interesting and memorable, most of them aren’t that inspiring and have very few attack variations. Especially the human bosses, they will be doing the same attack strings as if they’re your active party members, I find that very boring and comical. Though there’re a lot of side quests, most of them requires you to kill mobs in a certain fashion, and the rewards of the side quests just aren’t worth the trouble at all. While I really like the actual content of the bond episodes, the context behind those episodes featuring the opposing factions felt really forced and even with them stating they’ll ignore which side they’re on, it just makes the whole situation more jarring. Finally, an option to disable tips and tooltips would be nice, especially during cutscenes the skip button prompt is always visible, that really ruined the immersion and made it harder for me to appreciate the art.Overall, SCARLET NEXUS is a good game with some flaws to it. The combat is flashy and fun, the story is decent, the character design, visuals and music are superb. I got this game on a 30% discount and without knowing anything about it beforehand I’d say it’s well worth my time and money, I 100%-ed Kasane’s story (max bonds+all side quests) first at around 34 in game hours then started NG+ to finished Yuito’s story (max bonds only) at around 60 in game hours. If you’re looking for an RPG with solid gameplay and story it’s worth giving SCARLET NEXUS a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately sunk 50 hours into this game.Positives: -Visuals. This game is truly stunning artistically. The art style is crisp, the designing work is diverse between the human characters and monsters, with the monsters having extremely cool, whimsical designs that make them feel almost dreamlike. There's lots of use of consistent symbols and motifs that create good ties from a plot perspective as well. The cinematics, both in cutscenes and in battle are stellar. 9/10 on this front. -Audio. While the music wasn't super my cup of tea, it did serve really well to carry the mood in the game. Voice acting (I played English) was pretty good, too. 6/10. -Crafting system. A decent amount of things you want in the game like cosmetics and gifts to give to party members are going to require crafting with parts obtained from monsters. While simple, it encourages a bit of grinding and keeps you from just buying your way through everything. 6/10.Negatives: -Story. This one actually caught me off guard. I went in not really expecting a good story, but this one actually builds up and becomes really interesting, before falling extremely flat. It's hard to say specifics without spoiling, but the story was making itself out to have a lot of intrigue before ultimately falling back on some empty history and "friendship is magic" stuff. There was multiple themes brought up but never explored in a significant way that could have really made the story impactful. To it's credit, they didn't do the "friendship is magic" in a poorly written and "this happens because plot" sort of way, it was actually done using something the story had already well established. 4/10. -Combat. It uh...it's just messy. It encourages weaving of psychokinetic and weapon attacks, kinda making unlocking weapon combos feel pretty obsolete. There's 9 abilities but only 8 slots to use them, meaning you have to go into the menu in mid-battle to change it if you wanna use your 9th ability. The main interesting thing the combat has going for it is the enemies each having specific weaknesses to specific abilities, requiring you to utilize your full skillset across your encounters. 5/10 serviceable but kinda poorly designed imo. -Skill Tree. Frankly, it feels kinda underwhelming. Most of the skill tree is passive buffs that don't feel super impactful in practice. There's a few that grant you noticeable new abilities, which are definitely cool, but they're far and few. 3/10.-New Game Plus. This is mostly just a design flaw and warning, but make sure you don't save over the file the game gives you right after beating the final boss. You may think you can load that file, play a bit, and save normally while keeping the "completed" tag functional, but it will only let you use a -freshly- beaten file to begin your new game plus, so make sure to keep that as a separate file. Overall, I wouldn't call this game absolutely terrible, but I don't think it's worth picking up. I'm usually pretty determined to go full completionist and get all the trophies and challenges but this game is overall so underwhelming I'm not bothering going into new game plus. The main thing this game has going for it is its beautiful art, but...that's really about it.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to try to get into this game. It has the hallmarks of what I normally like, action based combat and an anime aesthetic, but the game shoots itself in the foot right when I try to like it. It dumps almost every character you will have in your party on you at the same time, so it feels hard to keep track of who's who and remember names. The combat, after 4 hours, doesn't seem like it's going to gain any kind of depth to it, as I am still using the same moves and tactics I used in the first 20 minutes. And the cutscenes all have a "Tales of" approach, with most of them being static images with the characters talking. Might just be me, but I felt there were a lot of things in the game holding it back from keeping me playing.

_childDocuments_.review: So far so good! 4 hours into the game and I'm really enjoying it. I have not come across any bugs or graphic problems. I've never played a Bandi Namaco game before so I can't compare it to Code Vein like many others are doing, but the story keeps me interested and it's visually appealing, especially during combat. I wish cut scenes weren't always like a "graphic novel" because it would have been beautiful if everything was a normal cut scene, but I've played many graphic novels so it doesn't bother me. Combat does feel fast with all the skills they give you since you can "borrow" each party members powers, but it does make every fight fairly easy and fun. The only complaint I have is the side quests that you can randomly pick up throughout the city (and can hardly tell they're there. Only difference is a bigger darker square). There's no real way to "track" where to go to complete the quest or how/where to find specific Others to fight. I know there's a log that is kept on which Others you have killed and where to locate them, but it would have been nice to look at the world map and know where I can track it down without having to do research on it, especially since every time I take a side quest it tells me to activate it. Also, 4 hours in and I've done the main story quest on the same two maps several times. I don't know how big the world map is supposed to be but it does get boring exploring the same areas. Other than my nitpicking I really do enjoy the game and recommend playing it at the price point. I'll probably replay the game as the other character when I am done!

oh yeah...Persona.aaaand lastly before i get to my verdict the cutscences:There are a few cuts but mostly they use Static pictures with talking protagonists at the sides.Many people argue that "This is cheap in 2021..." okay...BUT This style AGAIN gives me Persona Vibes.Verdict:♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ i love this game, didn't regret it a second and while i still wait for Persona 5 to come to PC i play Scarlet Nexus, vibe with the music, enjoy the combat and chill with my companions.DLC:oh boi...i wished for new Content, new Episodes and new Stories but....20 Bucks again for Bond Episodes? I think the description is not transparent enough, how many Bond Episodes? How many time can i spend in them? That are all factors on how im considering to buy it  but without these key points im tempted to give it a pass since im not into the attire business.

_childDocuments_.review: Scarlet Nexus is a fast pace hack & slash RPG that's kinda good. You play as either Yuito, Kasane, or both as they fight against others and find their own reason to fight. The story overall is fine but I'm not sure if everyone would like the visual novel style in the cutscenes and some of the characters can feel a little generic but if you do their bond episodes they do flesh out their characters. Gameplay is probably the best part of the game you have so much options to deal with enemies like with your telekinesis, SAS, or brain drive. The worst part of this game are the side quests they're just killed this amount of enemies or use this ability sometimes. They're just really not worth if your're not a achievement hunter. Overall I think Scarlet Nexus is a decent action RPG that is definitely one of the better games of 2021.

_childDocuments_.review: Overview: A fun game that becomes repetitive toward the end in terms of both story & game play. 75% of the game is fantasticStory: I followed Yuito's story, he is a very boring character. There isn't any romance between the characters but there are undertones of it. You spend standby phases hanging out with your platoon members in order to increase your bond with them similar to trials in the sky steel series, this gets boring & repetitive quickly. Out of the platoon members the only ones I liked were Genma, everyone else felt like brats or spoke in mysteries. The ending is terrible, and defeats the message the main characters were trying to make. There might be additional endings via NG+, but pushing through the end section would not be worth it. The majority of enemies don't match the game theme at all and the lack of gore is off from what the story entails.Game play: Uses a system called SAS which allows you to use the powers of your platoon mates in order to battle. The combat isn't to messy, and is enjoyable. The ending is awful, tons of boss enemy spam, prepare to spam max heal items in order to progress, damage is literally unavoidable.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent Gameplay, Atrocious StoryThe gameplay is fantastic, and does a great job at slowly introducing mechanic after mechanic without overwhelming the player. You can get away with just using abilities on cool down, or figure out optimal ability and combo rotations for MAX DEEPS! (dps)The setting is well imagined, and has a great cyberpunk borderline-magic aesthetic that feels unique. Although I question the effectiveness of holographic guard rails :p . Excellent sound design, and decent music round out the visuals and audio.The story is hot garbage, and there's a lot of it. All of the VO's are great, but the characters are not very interesting, particularly the female lead who has about as much character as a brick wall. The story is full of nonsense, plot holes, and characters acting with zero common sense. One minute you'll be fighting a rival team to the death, and the very next scene you'll be happily chatting over tea with members of said rival team.Or a character gets "infected" with a condition. Your character joins the people that caused this condition, with no guarantee that they will fix your friend, only being told that working with them is the best way to fix their friend. Well, they don't fix your friend, and SURPRISE!!!! the leader of this group is evil. So why were you working for this OBVIOUSLY EVIL group? ... ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ i dunnoIt's like the writers wanted to capture the essence of Nier and Final Fantasy storytelling, but only the awful confusion and contrivances. None of the substance or interesting characters.Update: The story, characters, and dialog were SO BAD that I couldn't do it anymore. I have changed this to a thumbs-down.

Is that Former Major General Fubuki? We should talk to Former Major General Fubuki. Guys, I need to do this for Naomi. Naomi would want this. Naomi is the reason for my actions, because Naomi would want me to. Naomi, is that you Naomi? Naomi I'm glad I found you Naomi.)- 90% of the game's cutscenes are presented in a visual novel style. _childDocuments_.review: First off, I picked up this game primarily for its anime-style art and animation. Damn, those really surpassed my expectations! When it comes to these aspects, I'm utterly speechless. The combat become better and better once you get midway through the story, since that's when you start to unlock more of the skill tree. It's a bit odd that the basic attack is so limited when you're at a low level - especially since this is a JRPG. This could make sense if it's for skills, but here, even the basic attack is minimal. Nevertheless, I found the final boss battle as my best play in this game, unlike other tedious boss fights. It truly pushes the limit of skill, which is challenging and precisely why I enjoyed it. Furthermore, the soundtracks are catchy and quite pleasing. My favorites are "Scarlet Nexus" (yes, this is the soundtrack name), "Suoh," and "Broken Promise.". And the last for good part in this game, the enemy character design is another high point - shoutout to the design team. It may be a bit too much for JRPG, feeling more suited for a horror game, but it works.However, this game has alot of unbearable things. You may have already seen other reviews mentioning this: the main story can fry your brain if you take it too seriously. The early premise had me hooked, after phases two or three, the plot become worse and worse. It feels like the story was penned by multiple authors with different storytelling styles. Moreover, this game has two unique perspectives or walkthroughs of the story that initially intersect slightly, but eventually merge into one. One perspective is from Yuito Sumeragi, with his team, and the other is from Kasane Randall and her squad. But because the creators likely wanted to deliver different experiences with limited resources and budget, the execution on this aspect fell short. In the end, both stories become unbearable to play and almost every chapter or phase has an odd start and finish, at least to me. Given that Yuito and Kasane each have their own teams, the roster of characters is extensive, yet each character lacks depth or uniqueness other than their backstory and voice acting. Speaking of which, the voice acting is notably poor in this game, similar to AI-trained generated voices that lack chemistry with their respective characters. As for the animation, while it's superb as I said before, most of the game's dialogues are on par with powerpoint slideshow. At first, I thought this unique 'slideshow' approach could give different experience, but overtime it becomes monotonous due to the characters' lack of expressiveness. The game has lot of maps, and each is fairly huge, but they feel empty and underutilized in the main story. Finally, I skipped a lot of the "bond episodes" because they were simply too boring. I gave the first two couple attempts a shot each characters, but they just weren't engaging enough.In conclusion, it seems like the game's direction shifted frequently during development, given the promising premise but poor execution. Well, if you're just looking for casual play and don't care too much about the story, you can give it a try. But if you're like me and you love good story in your JRPGs, you might want to pass on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I took a chance with Scarlet Nexus because I wanted to start giving new IPs and new games in general a chance. So many times do we as consumers simply stick to what we are familiar with at the detriment of new ideas and creativity. However, after playing through Scarlet Nexus, even without finishing the game entirely, I can say there is a LOT to be desired. Let me start off by saying the combat is the most enjoyable part of the game. If you like fast moving combat that requires on your feet thinking, then you'll have fun with this combat. That said, there are still a lot of problems with the combat that could be made better. Mainly, the fact that you can't dodge during an animation. This isn't a gigantic issue, as even with my terrible dodging skills, I can still eek out victories without too much problem, though some fights almost require you to master the perfect dodge mechanic, which is just silly considering how precise you need to be to do it. Being able to cancel a basic attack animation to dodge would take a lot of stress off the player when fighting larger enemies who can eat your hits without getting stunned. Making the perfect dodge window wider as well would help a LOT during certain bosses or against specific larger enemies. The fact that most enemies have aimbot precise attacks as well doesn't help. Yes this is a factor of git gud, but it could be tweaked to be easier without sacrificing the complexity of the combat. Beyond that, being able to combine powers is really enjoyable, and allows for a super fast gameplay that will make Devil May Cry style fans happy, or at the very least content. Using items mid combat is pretty easy, though the fact that you can only hold ten of each item can make missions still feel stressful, especially if you get into a harder fight and aren't good at the dodge mechanic (Or if your teammates just get bullied). If they were to make more games like this, the combat would be the area they need to change the least, with just some minor adjustments going a long way to make for a very fluid and enjoyable system.After that though, almost everything else in the game begins to break a bit. Lets start with the story. Overall, it's nothing amazing, but not terrible either. It's a very safe story that focuses on two major paths, one for Yuito and one for Kasane, going through the choices of each MC as they try to solve the major overarching problem. The concept is interesting, but nothing particularly new or inventive. The only major addition to the story style is the main focal point of the game itself - Psychic Powers. These powers are what connects everything together, serving as both the problem and the solution to the game in a way. Of course there are other factors to the story I won't spoil, but prepare to hear a lot about Brains, Powers, Information and Governments surrounding them for the entire game. You won't fall asleep listening, but you won't be having any emotional responses to it either. Going along with mediocre story telling comes mediocre characters. This personally makes me the most upset. Characters can make or break a story driven game. Even if your story isn't revolutionary, good characters can hold it together and make it feel more unique than it might actually be. Sadly, no character whatsoever stands out. Every single character is the same cardboard cutout version of a character trope. Yuito is the good boy who trusts everyone and wants to do his best. Kasane is the cold but kind hearted girl who is so loyal to her sister that she basically ignores everything else. Tsugumi (who is one of my favorites in the game) is the stereotypical shy girl who doesn't have many friends, Shiden is the stereotypical "I'm better than you" ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, etc, etc. The only character I think comes close to being unique is Kagero, and even then it's only because a mysterious character has the benefit of being mysterious. Outside of that, he's nothing special either. What makes matters worse is none of the characters really feel like they grow, they only just become closer to one another. Being friends is fine and dandy, but characters feel one dimensional without any significant growth. Tsugumi at the very least went the typical "Shy girl is more determined and stubborn than she appears" route, which shows some nuance to the character, even if it's only basic. No one else matters, no one else grows or changes, no one is memorable. It's kind of funny in a way, the bad character design can even almost be reflected by their voice acting. This shares the issue with the story of being not bad but not great either. I can barely feel any emotion in any of the character's voices. They don't sound like robots but also don't sound like they really care. Tsugumi might have been the only one I liked because the soft spoken voice does well with a determined demeanor because you can feel the effort behind the voice. There's a reason she's my favorite in this game. I don't blame the VAs honestly, they probably weren't super aware of how to be these characters yet. I feel like if they did a redo on the voices for the characters and tried to fit the emotions of the scenes a bit more, they'd do a better job. Lastly, I want to talk about content. Mainly the side quests. The side quests in this game are awful. The worst I've ever seen in an RPG honestly. They're unimaginative, boring, difficult and irritating. Unimaginative because all they tend to consist of are kill quests or fetch quests. Boring because again, kill or fetch quests plus you can only have one active at a time. Difficult because they require you to do very specific things sometimes that the game doesn't easily explain to you how to do without trial and error, and irritating for similar reasons but also because your allies can completely screw you up. I just did a side quest where I had to kill a specific enemy using a combo assist, but using that combo assist was really difficult without first nearly killing it. This resulted in me having to wait for quite a bit of time simply to allow the enemy to get weaker so I could actually kill it the way the game wanted me to. These honestly felt more like challenges than side quests, something to do to show you can, not because you should. The rewards you get for them are also usually worthless, and thus doing them isn't really worth it, but there are so many that you feel compelled to do them for completions sake or simply to feel like you got your money's worth.I truly cannot say this game is worth sixty dollars. I'd dare say it's only worth 30, maybe 40. Thus, I can't recommend the game as it is, because it's just a mediocre game. If you want something to waste time, go for it, it will definitely waste some of your time. But wait for it to go on sale first. And Bandai, if for whatever reason you read this review, do better than this. Take the feedback and improve. I honestly think this universe could be super interesting, but you need to work to make it stand out. The psychic/information based setting isn't enough to hold it up. Make better characters, make a more compelling story, and add some side quests that truly make the world feel alive. If you do that, this could be a really popular JRPG series. TL;DR: Not recommended. Mediocre game with too many flaws weighing it down to be worth full price. Wait for a sale to try it out. Try again Bandai. 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: SCARLET NEXUS is 2021's most underrated RPG! I enjoyed it's NieR meets Astral Chain meets Control style gameplay, premise, and lore and SCARLET NEXUS is a big time recommendation for those of you who enjoy either of the three forementioned franchises and potential hog heaven for those who enjoy all three of those franchises combined. For those of you that are Persona fans this game has bond episodes you can do while playing either of the two playable protagonists with the side character companions and all as well as gift giving to them. Also each character you have on your teams have abilities so think of it as what if My Hero Academia heroes were in a more militarized police force thus had more simply basic powers. Again this is 2021's most underrated RPG and you all should check it out!

_childDocuments_.review: Lets start with the terrible combat.-Lock on doesn't actually lock on-Attacks essentially has no weight to them outside of your character spamming the psychic attack.-It's really hard to gauge the range on the girl's attacks as the lock on doesn't work.-Enemies for some god forsaken reason will usually only target you and rarely your ai teammates. This targeting still occurs even if you are across the room and your teammates are next to them. This becomes an absolute chore to deal with many flying enemies.     -Your ai teammates also tend to stand next to enemies and do absolutely nothing even if set on attack mode.Now you'd think with such terrible combat, maybe the story would be better, but alas you would be sorely incorrect. The majority of the cutscenes are powerpoint slideshows with animated faces at times. There are also times where it would go from powerpoint->real cutscene->powerpoint, making it extremely unimmersive. The plot is predictable and at times very frustrating to see characters make terrible decisions with no consistency as to their respective powers' strength.I honestly wouldn't recommend anyone buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game features fun, fast-paced combat and a decent, although relatively short story. However, I found most of the value or "content" in the the bond system with your teammates, adding to the seemingly bare-bones story. There are a lot of exclusive cut scenes and certain "sides" & character development that you can only see of your teammates depending on which character your play (I highly recommend playing as Yuito's story is more straightforward and Kasane seems to compliment Yuito's perspective and is mainly to help fill "holes" that you may have on the plot). I suggest playing one full-play through, start an EX-New Game so you have the option to carry items & your level over to the new game if you wish to skip the grind.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10. Game would be a solid 5/10 due to the writing but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ does this game feel good. The gameplay is worth the cost alone but the story... make no sense. On a surface level its really good with nice yet predictable plot twist, and some less expected ones. However the way the characters deal with the changes makes no sense.     Imagine someone who you are on decent terms with gets told something about you... so they start trying to kill you, you ask them why and try to deescalate but it doesn't work. So you beat em up and they run away. Then this happens 2 more times but on the third you finally manage to start talking after beating them up, but they only explain some of the current events, but not why they want to kill you. Then you have a migraine and they get really worried and start asking if your okay? Then they run away? Character motivations make sense some of the time but the rest of it just doesn't match up. People your fighting ask you out on "dates" and talk about your fighting as if its no big deal and it can wait. The characters don't realize the stakes in their own story and it really pulls you out of it. And before anyone says "they don't actually want to kill you so that's why they are worried about you" then why would they try to attack you when you show no signs of hostility and are actively trying to negotiate and understand whats happening. Its terrible writing is all it is.    Once again the game play is hella good, super smooth and has that fast paced hard hitting anime feeling to it which is hard to get right, so overall definitely worth it. However the story and writing leaves much to be desired, not to mention pretty much every character is some sort of cookie cutter anime trope. Its not about having to make everything original because that's impossible at this point, its just that some of those tropes are pretty bad/boring. Some of the ones here are pretty cringy, and all tho there are a few done well in this game its not many.   So all in all if you want good game play here it is, and if you like your stereotypical anime characters and nonsensical writing then this game will be the only thing you play for the next year or so.

_childDocuments_.review: [EDIT 2/2023: this plays fantastically on Steam Deck, max settings, at a perfect 60fps] dope game. played thru both campaigns multiple times. the party-based combat is pristine, but the average gamer will surely need to up the difficulty if they want a challenge. in my initial playthru i found the cut scenes - w all their familiar jrpg cheese, anime grunting, and inch-deep PG-13 drama to be irritating; but in all fairness i am an actual adult and not really the primary target demo for that stuff. i reference the anime story aspects here cuz of the other comments i've read from users aka other non-children who understandably didnt vibe w it. cuz upon my following playthrus i am ashamed to admit that the wholesome yet ham-fisted coming of age YA life lessons, evolving relationships of your party members, and the execution of story managed to override my eternally cold black cynical heart and mind ♥♥♥♥ me into actually not aggressively insta-skipping all the cut scenes like i did in my first play thru. in all fairness the story is a bit slow at first and the initial interpersonal conflicts are objectively obnoxious. but once it gets going, it all starts to click, and imo the sci-fi concepts are pretty rad for the genre. the reason i'm shilling for this ♥♥♥♥ here is because the combat/gameplay loop is fantastic - so dont let the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ get in the way of playing this. honestly this might be my 2021 goty. the complexity of the combat and the difficulty is very well tuned and scales perfectly with the skills you unlock and the increasingly nuanced enemies you battle. by the end of the game you'll be in full control of a frenetic epilepsy inducing full screen of anime chaos. and for all the jrpg melodrama, there is a really well made game inside some rad plot devices, and who knows u might even end up watching all 26 episodes of the anime on crunchyroll

_childDocuments_.review: Let's be upfront: to like this game, you will need to have some tolerance for some typical quirks of Japanese RPGs. The story is an incoherent mess, breathlessly jumping from one major revelation to the next plot twist in such a tempo that seemingly important plot points quickly are forgotten. The cutscenes simply are too long and strain your patience. And the levels are mostly overly linear and full of reused assets.But had I fun? You'd bet I had.First of all, I actually enjoyed the characters. Your companions don't avoid all tropes but still are a lot more nuanced than they seem at first glance. (You'll have to sit through a lot of cutscenes to get there, though…)And the combat is a joy. It manages to remain fun and engrossing up to the end, and is almost perfectly balanced throughout (on normal difficulty, at least).I only finished one of the two sides of the story so far (which took me about 38 hours, playtime of the demo included – the  progress carries over). I will probably play the other story as well, but only after a break.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore my playtime on here as I played and finished this game on the PS5. As of writing this, I have finished Yuito's story and started my second playthrough already with over 46 hours clocked in. I'll just give the rating first and it is a good 8.5/10. I do recommend it. Be sure to read my last two paragraphs if you choose to stop here after the rating. The combat is great and fluid with a lot of interesting ideas and combos but with a few small issues. - Locking on can sometimes be wonky as in the character refuses to attack in the direction of the enemy I locked on to or simply locking on to the wrong enemy, This messes with the flow of combat severely and can definitely ruin some moments in game that requires fast reaction. - The combos and attacks are great and varied but required a long time to get and even longer to get the power combos. In fact, the best part and most fun you can get from the combat only comes after 20 hours due to them requiring skill points to unlock movement skills and bond points to unlock powers. All this is fine if not for the super tedious amount of grinding needed to get all the movement skills and powers. In short, you will most likely only be able to experience the best the game can offer near the end game and by then it's been a long journey of sub-par combat. - Unfortunately, there are not much weapon varieties. In fact there are basically none for better or worst. The characters you choose are strictly one playstyle of weapon which is different between the two main protagonist. Yuito uses swords while Kanase uses throwing knifes. Both are restricted to those weapons and that's it. Any weapon you purchases from the shop are only straight up bigger numbers to damage and a cosmetic change, nothing more. Now this isn't 100% terrible because while it does kinda suck to be force to play with one weapon the whole game, the benefit of doing this by game design is that these weapons are very fleshed out. There are so many movement skills and power skills that can be mixed together to create some truly fun combat. The maps and locations in game are decent. It's what you can expect from Bandai style anime games with linear maps and forces you to go in one direction and maybe a few rooms with little bonuses if you choose to go there. - The aesthetic of the game in general is pretty good and the locations are mostly good as well. Just don't expect anything mind blowing or amazing but nothing bad or terrible either. - The locations are obviously based off Japan but there are also a lot of European inspired locations as well. For the soundtrack and music, it's absolutely great. While not on the level of Nier Automata, it's doesn't need to be to still be good music. It's good enough that I went and bought the Vinyl record for the game. Now the main reason I mostly buy these type of games in the first place is the story, weird I know but i'm the type of guy who watches porn for the plot.  But this time I have to say that the story is pretty terrible and disappointing. - Yuito is a terrible character. He's a goodie-two-shoes but to the extreme. To summerize, take your typical 2011 style wholesome anime MC tripe and make it worst. Bad things happen but he downright ignores it and sometimes acts non-human. - Kanase is the better of the two mcs. I won't say much more than that.- The plot itself is probably the worst offender here. It has to be one of the most contrived plots I've seen in anime in recent years. It's safe to say it's downright terrible with little to no redeeming factors. It's literally one plot twist after the other and I've actually lost track of how much plot twist there were. The pacing is also terrible because you would be bomb shelled by one huge plot twist only to immediately and I say that as in THE VERY NEXT SENTENCE be bomb shelled by an even larger plot twist that ain't related to the previous plot twist. - That's another thing, the story is a contest on who can have a bigger plot twist but the opponent is itself. It constantly tries to outdo itself with nonsensical plot twist and horrible directions which is a shame because if you just stood with one and kept it that way then everything would be kinda fine. It's even worst when everything started off really good too but just slipped off a mountain and continued to roll downhill at increasing speeds. - It's also funny when you think about it because if you took out 90% of the plot twist, the ending would've still make sense and probably for the better too. There were just so many things that didn't need to of happened but for some reason it did and some of them don't even have a conclusion meaning it literally happened for the sake of it happened rather than progressing the story or plot. Some of it are literally ignored and never brought back or even fully explained.But even with all these negatives, I still gave it a high score and a recommendation because it's just simple fun. The negatives while horrible, doesn't really take away the fun factor of this game which is the gameplay. For me, if the story is absolute ass but the gameplay holds up then I can give it a free pass but that's just me. Though for those who value story, character, and plot more then I wouldn't recommend this title at all especially to those who can get very angry at nonsensical stories and characters with a lack of common sense. For those on the edge, I recommend you wait for a discount or sale of at least 30%-50% percent. Only buy this at full price if you've seen some other reviews and gameplays and still want to get it. Other than that, thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: Writing this review just after completing my first playthrough (I picked Yuito first), and all I have to say is WOW.  I didn't expect to be hooked on this game like how I was, I couldn't put this game down.  The gameplay itself seems pretty basic ARPG, but once the game really gets going, it feels VERY satisfying to play.  I have a few gripes about the camera sometimes (honestly a recurring theme with any ARPG in general) but nothing serious that ever made me want to quit the game.  I also wish there was some form of dash cancel for some of the really long attack animations, but the game still feels quite fast-paced despite the lack of it.The characters are somewhat stereotypical JRPG school-life, but I find them to be very well-rounded and well written, especially in a game that's fairly dialogue heavy.The music is great, not amazing or anything you'll be obsessing over, but good enough to keep your attention and mood right.  The story itself honestly impressed me the most, while I don't find it necessarily breaks any barriers, I think it was done well enough to keep you drawn to the progression of the story.  I find it odd that the game splits the 2 main characters' stories as 2 different playthroughs when I imagine they could have been merged (I imagined something close to Yakuza 0's Kiryu/Majima flips).  That said, I don't think it's necessarily a bad decision overall.Overall, this game was probably one of the best ARPGs I've played in years, and I'll be doing a 2nd playthrough as Kasane very soon.  My final score: 9.5/10.  The only thing this game is missing is a real dash cancel for all your attacks, but perhaps the main characters would be WAY too powerful with it, so it's more of just a personal gripe.  DEFINITELY pick this game up if you're a fan of ARPGs.

_childDocuments_.review: Cannot believe a $59 game in 2021 uses power point slides rather than animations to tell the story, especially a game from Japan. The story itself sucks. Although it is somewhat innovative to tell the same story from two sides, nothing can save a terrible story from itself. Without spoiling the story, let me just say that without being silly and intentionally and unnecessarily keeping key intels in the dark, there would not be a story at all. One side of the story is being nice but stupid, the other side is being smart but mute. And I, the player, seem to be the greatest fool. By the way, some of the requests are simply stupid, for example, one request asks you to kill a creep in brain drive (you need to accumulate energy to enter brain drive state, and once you have enough energy, you enter brain drive immediately) that commits suicide once they see you. Another example, another request asks you to kill three of a certain type of creeps by throwing back the fireballs they throw, but you first need to dodge the fireballs close enough then use mind power. Even worse, the description of requests can be vague. It feels like the only goal for these requests is not making players enjoy the game but to passively make them spend more time on the game so the statistics will look good. Remind me of Fate/Grand Order and many other Japanese games, they are really good at doing that. Also, the optimization sucks. In some maps,  I lose frames badly on my RTX3080+i9 10 gen laptop. However, this game has some merits. First, the game has a novel and complicated fighting system. In the meanwhile, the guidance is wonderful. So, I really enjoy the combat without getting confused by different elements in the system. Also, the game makes materials in all maps important in all time and, the creeps in all maps level up with the characters. Therefore, it is not all that boring to harvest materials from early maps. I want to make up three, but somehow end up with two...Right, the third one is that the animation is also released. If the animation can tell the story better, I will keep it in this paragraph, and if not, then I have to live with buying a game with 4 5 demerits but 2 merits. Good for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I reluctently give this game a thumbs up.Because it has potential, but wastes most of it on annoying decisions, forced gimmiks and wonky balancing.The only thing I really can not complain about are the easthetic and general style. Beautiful graphics, amating animations, freaky enemy design. The game is a visual masterpiece.The core gameplay is pretty great. Basically a Character Action game like DMC. But the problems start already there.Enemies can get really annoying and all of them require the same strategy of activating your teleport/ time freeze/ invisible ability and defeat the enemy.Most of the game is fine, but especially endgame is full of enemies that are invincible if they notice you.You can not animation cancel. In a character action game.Most hits I received felt extremely unfair, thanks to being animation locked most of the time.Not to mention that this game suffers from the greatest mistake in the genre, enemies attacking you off screen. Which is annoying by itself already, but a lot of enemies have extremely damaging special attacks that they can also use while off screen. Which results in a massive amount of frustration thanks to sometimes ridiculous ammounts of damage that you can not avoid.Another thing that highly annoyed me was the amount of cutscenes.Yeah, the game trires to tell a complex and deep story, but personally lost me half way through thanks to the lackluster and slow presentation.90% of cuscenes are like the no-animation cutscenes in bayonette, but even less animated and 4 times as long.I often just wanted to play through a level, but the game constantly throws you from one cutscene to the next. Often letting you walk just a few meters with nothing to do in between multiple cutscenes.The ballancing also is pretty wonky. You get pretty OP over the game.New combos, new abilities and special skills you get from raising the friendship level of your companions.At the end of the game you are a near indestructable power house with tons of options to kill your enemies.But that's not the OP part.Getting to a high enough friendship level you unlock special attacks that randomly trigger in battle that just DECIMATE your enemy. Not to mention that you literally can upgrade yourself through a Skill Tree, one of the Type that allows you to get everything in it, to be completely invincible during your Ultimate state, basically the devil trigger of this game, which lasts like 30 secons and further increases your damage output. And if your Friendship level is high enough there are AGAIN random triggers where your friends increase your duration of your ultimate while in it.I was able to beat 3 bosses in a row with  this, without having to leave the ultimate state.The game, sadly knows this and just starts throwing bs at you during the final chapters..Lastly, I want to mention how this game doesnt have a single fun Boss fight.They are eather annoying and unfair or annoying and boring, relying on stupid and flat out unfun tactics to beat them.And whoever designed Dominus Circus does not deserve to work in this industry anymore.Final Verdict,I really hope this game gets a sequel where they improve on the combat.Less story, more gameplayAnimation Canceling, better enemy AILess annoying enemy design and better bossesand voila, it would be amazing

_childDocuments_.review: BANDAI obviously has some very talented people working for them. The soundtrack alone makes this game worth playing; breakcore, electronic, piano medleys, simply an ear feast with catchy tunes that'll make you look up the soundtrack for streaming simply because it's that professional. The gameplay has me exclaiming "woahs" and giggles by sheer viscerality and impact. Art direction is uniquely dystopian with an incredible sense of character clothing style. Characters actively comment on things you do during combat and even as I'm typing this review, I have the game open in the background, with characters in my party making comments on how it's important to rest, if their hair ties are dirty, and other quips. Once again, the soundtrack coupled with the new-age city tech environments is simply eargasmic. If you were looking for a more serious iteration on something like Genshin Impact, you've found it. I'm more of a gameplay and atmosphere person but the story had a sort of Wolfenstin: New Order "human cruelty tragedy" to it, and I felt sympathy towards particular characters. It also helps that the characters are diverse in their attitudes and personalities, even though some aren't that in-depth. It gets funny and spunky sometimes, if you're not used to games having a dignified serious attitude that's sometimes naturally poked at by a teammate's comic relief due to a mentally stressful situation. This game takes queues from games such as Tom Clancy's The Division and mixes it with a hyper-pop electronic sheen. Gorgeous.

_childDocuments_.review: Summary: Good combat, interesting story ,and cool use of multiple story routes. Completionists be warned, the game can be annoying, tedious, and not fun to 100%.A solid action JRPG. It feels similar to Astral Chain in combat and difficulty where the game will reward you for understanding the mechanics while also presenting some challenges. The best part of the game are the boss fights. While the game is straightforward in how to beat the boss, the bosses have some interesting abilities that keep it challenging and rewarding for when you do beat them. I was worried about the story because I knew there was an anime released alongside it as I feared it would be barely strung together. The story is acceptable. Its not amazing like Final Fantasy or Tales Of but its better than most anime. The fact that you have two characters to play as makes the story really interesting becuase each play through you get to see different parts of the game but also a different side to each major event in the game. The game is not great for completionists. The side quests aren't really quests, they are tutorials on how to use various parts of the combat system. While it's a good idea in teh beginning, most of the quests, even the ending quests, are all combat system tutorials. It's annoying, tedious, and sometimes frustrating depending on the piece of the combat the game wants you to use.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is... Strange  I don't hate it, but I don't recommend it if it isn't on sale. And this is for three reasonsThe story has no clue what it wants to be and starts like 50 different plot threads. And wraps them all up in the most unsatisfying way by the time the game ends.Scarlet Nexus starts as something like a cop drama, you play as one of two protagonists Yuito or Kasane.  Both characters get there own specific campaigns until about halfway through the game. Until the story suddenly switches on what its actually about. More on that laterBut during the sort of cop drama phase you wander around the city as a futuristic cyber cop hunting aliens called Others.Throughout this opening, you'll see so many interesting plot threads.  Government conspiracy, exploitation, classism, Dictatorships. The whole nine yards of classic Cyberpunk tropes. And when the game is covering that. I would argue its amazing. Watching things go up in flames and lines being drawn as the two protagonists pick different sides and are forced to fight each other in a war is interesting to watch. And honestly fun to experience as you will fight either side in a boss battle several times.Whats frustrating about all of this... Is its Scarlet Nexus's B-plot. And honestly? that's an insult to B plots since they drop everything the minute the A plot starts.  And the A plot is straight up awful, even when it was set up all throughout the game its so underwhelming and frankly boring that it hurts the game as  a whole.The A plot is a time travel story.   A time travel story that fits about as well as  rotten tuna on a fresh hamburger.And the worse part is all the interesting things from the B plot. Just get resolved off screen. Every single thing resolved not because you the player resolved it. Or you the player were there to see it resolved.  You the player watch a cut scene of someone travelling back in time and hearing the resolution second hand in a line of dialogue.The time travel rules are awful too. No real follow up, needed I just wanted to say that.Finally to wrap up the story, the time travel lets in so many plot holes Just by existing you wonder if the script was written by chatgpt or  a block of swiss cheese.  But to be honest I think chat gpt could have written a plot with less holes. I cheddah believe that until the day I die.Next Characters: Some are good, some are alright some are the most generic monstrosities that Bandai Namco have ever createdYuito is you're classic dough eyed anime protagonist #69He wants to help everyone do the right thing blah blah.  The game tries to give him depth in multiple points, but by the hog tying his development to the time travel you create a messy charcter that has no beginning middle or end.  His arc is equivalent to a soggy spaghetti noodle. Spoilers for various plot points regarding Yuito: The other characters tend to fare better there nothing new, and the more interesting characters get shafted on screen time. But there still interesting enough that I would say there a decent selling point if you want that classic power of friendship game.Finally we arrive at combat...Its good. but messy.Its good as a 3d action fighter. Following in the footsteps of games like Dmc and bayonetta, you're not gonna see some kind of sick combo video but the game is serviceable enough.  The main draw is the psychic powers, using telekinesis to throw cars and swing around huge wrecking balls and excavators never gets old. Later you can link with you're party members and use there powers. And these new powers can be super fun, at first. Until you realise most of them just = do more damage for some time.  And all you're upgrades are just going to go into getting uptime on these skills.Its not bad, but its flawed and poorly balancedThe game isn't bad? Its fairly unique, but just cause its unique that doesn't make it good.  When playing the game I couldn't get the thought out my head if there wasn't a better game left on the cutting room floor. And that's not good for the game, if I'm playing a twentyish hour game. And am wondering if there wasn't a better game lost in some poor developers disk drive.If the games on sale pick it up I don't regret my time for the most part. But as a side if you want to avoid being disappointed if you even get just a little bit invested the moment you get to the level where you climb a mountain.  Alt f4 out of the game open notepad and write a fanfiction about what happens next.  It doesent matter how good you are at creative writing. you will come out with a better story

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished Kasane's route and I'm planning to go right back in with Yuito's route. This game was such a great experience. The combat was fun and satisfying, a lot of the environments were beautiful and atmospheric, and it wasn't difficult at all on normal. Very well tuned to my preference these days. Somehow an ARPG helped me relax every day after work. I don't have much else to say about the positives of the game; I'm just really happy with the overall experience. I am however, going to point out some issues below, and it's a shame they'll probably consist of the longer component of my review. I just want to make sure they're crystal clear, in case they weren't abundantly clear from the top rated reviews here.1. The game's story and areas are ultimately very linear. While you do have free time between story phases, areas progress in a straight line with minimal branches from the main path. This will bother some more than others. Personally, I don't mind this kind of design (I loved Final Fantasy XIII, to give some more perspective).2. The new photo mode is a fantastic addition, but after all this time, they still haven't added an option to hide the UI for it and the skip button. So it'll be on your screen 99% of the time and you'll just have to get used to it.3. The side quests are extremely lackluster and add nothing to the world other than extra experience with the various combat mechanics the game introduces. However, this ultimately doesn't help, since there is also no option to disable tutorial tips. The game was still telling me how each ability worked as I activated them during the final battle... lol.4. The requirements to raise bond level seem to be ambiguous and heavily dependent on gift giving and story progress. Why the game is unclear about this aspect in particular but holds your hand everywhere else baffles me. This issue is amplified by the fact that certain rare drops from enemies (required for some gifts) are brutal to farm unless you have a someone's () level 6 SAS bond ability (even then it sucks lol).With all that being said, the game still easily earns a thumbs up from me. I just don't understand how some of these very obvious aspects of the game weren't addressed before release (or a year afterwards...).
