_childDocuments_.review: Reviewers said Scarlet Nexus' gameplay was comparable to the iconic action rpg style made popular by Platinum games, so i had to check it out. First impressions were bland, the artstyle was uninteresting and the story immediately threw way to many made up terms and concepts at my face. After playing for a little while longer, the gameplay turns out to be great. The fluid, flashy, fast-paced combat felt really fun and rewarding. Like the reviews described, it really did feel like a game made by Platinum games. The combat provides a lot of options, which can feel a bit overwhelming but the game introduces them at a nice pace. Combining all these different options and techniques feels really good. The animations go a long way, the way Kasane pulls her knives out when starting combat, or the way she puts them back, go a long way to making combat feel cool. But the best part are the way characters enter the screen when using the SAS or the flashy goly kill like finishing moves the protagonist uses. These great animation make the combat feel really dynamic and rewarding. Even though the bland cell-shaded anime artstyle and edgy, abstract, uninteresting and confusing world created with it did not leave a good expression at all, the UI and animations were amazing. Subtle details in de HUD make the game feel alive. A lot of games try to go for this cyborg, glitchy UI style, but only a few pull it off in a way that feels nice, looks good and is functional all at the same time. I see Platinum games' Astral Chain (great game btw) as a great example of this UI style, and it feels like Scarlet Nexus takes a lot of inspiration from this. Overall great UI.All in all, after the 7th act i started skipping all dialogue and cutscenes becaues they were just boring and made no sense to me and i turned the mediocre music off in favor of my own music. But after doing this the game was really fun and felt great to play. The difficulty is challenging enough to keep you wanting to try again and never feels unfair.Not worth full price, but a fun game to check out on sale!

_childDocuments_.review: First time I saw the trailer of the game, I wasn't so hype at all, knowing it would be similiar as Code Vein. But infact, I was “TOTALLY WRONG”. The game was suprisingly impressive in many ways. This game is not “Souls Like” at all, it’s a JPRG similar to Final Fantasy including a visual novel which tells a lot about the storyline of this game. Now lets breakdown deeper inside the game, I’ll try to review the game as far from spoilers as possible. Also please keep in mind, that this review I given is “from my own based experience”, and mine is not may the same to you guys may encounter.+ Remarkable story+ Great character design, world visualization, enemy design+ Overall combat is decent, but requires a fair amount of upgrades, farming and development+ Great character bonding+ Good cutscenes+ Oh boy, great OST/Soundtracks+ The game offers good replayability, if you get into the story deeper like me- Side quest is kind of boring, and the majority rewards is given can be obtain from store or story progression- Camera FOV can be annoying in certain fight- Lack of variant enemies- Alt-Tab at Fullscreen mode may cause black screen or even game crash. Just use Borderless Window.1.	StoryThe game offer two main protagonist, which is Yuito Sumeragi and Kasane Randall. Keep in mind that these two protagonist had a different storyline, combat style, and personality. Some of the plot twist in this game would make you shock or even confused. I would recommend to play both sides to understand the twist of the story. I also mention that this game combine a visual novel effects into the game, which I don’t recommend for you to skip it even though sometimes it’s boring to watch, but in the end it will tell what’s going on within the game.2.	Character DesignTwo main protagonist given in the game offers a great visual and also different personality. Like example, Yuito Sumeragi had a optimistic personality while Kasane Randall more towards into cold personality.3.	CombatLike I said before, overall combat is decent, but requires a fair amount of upgrades, farming, and progression. What type of upgrades is used for the combat? Skill tree. There are 5 types of branch in the skill tree, “Expand”, “Enhance”, “Support”, Brain Drive”, and the last is “Brain Field”. Keep in mind that not all skill tree are available to upgrade at early of the game, these are based on progress orientation. You can also freely roam or even farm level to get upgrades of your character level and points to spend for skill tree.Another good combat stuff they add into the game is called “SAS”, which allow you to use other NPC power that will influence/help players in combat. For example, you can use Shidden Ritter’s Electrokinesis power to boost your attack converted into electric, Tsugumi Nazar’s Clairvoyance power to see invinsible enemies and many other companion powers. You can also combine their powers to create a variety combos for you to use.Last but not least, your/character ultimate power is called “Brain Field”, which will gives buffs to your attacks, but with a limited time to use.4.	Character BondingThis feature that is given is actually rewarding. Don’t get me wrong, you’re not just going to sit and watch every other character personality, back past story, hobbies and etc. Instead, if you managed to level up your bond to certain character, they’ll be more usefull in combat and the great bonus is it will increase the effect, duration, and even better upgrades of SAS power on the relatable character.Should you get this game? If you are a fan of JPRG, yes you should. This game may not be a masterpiece, but I definitely can this game worth to buy from your pocket. By the time I review this game (01-10-2021), they keep adding content, such as cosmetics, upcoming bond episodes, and many other improvement. The game itself offer a good replayability and pretty enjoyable.

Trust me when I say a good anime style combat game is hard to come by and this one by FAR takes the cake.

_childDocuments_.review: i got this for discount and wanted to try it out, i love anime, and Tales of Arise is one of my favorite anime games ive played some of, but this game? no, not even if it was free would i play it again, id recommend against it if you love fluid combat game play, the animations and SFX look fantastic but they are keyed to your placement in repeating motions, NOT aimed in attacking an enemy like a floating blade bird thing should do, its got lock on but what good is it if you are not jumping and slinging at the same time, enemies move around nice, its all good and well, but fighting them was just an mental stress over load, im use to playing some darksouls on consoles, and even elden ring, im no pro but im not wet behind the ears in dodge timing, i was able to get perfect dodges a few times playing here but it was so off putting when it slowed you down, like why? im not bullet timing anything, theres no special benefit to slowmo me in a dodge, Fromsoft knows better, dont slow mo someone dodging, its jarring to deal with in combat, just give the I-Frames and let the combat flow best it can. and at the combat i tried to engage in was weak. fighting enemies with knock down stun locking was the worst thing for this, and if you dont go right for the skill to get back up when down you have to wait so long to get back up you could be hit AGAIN, and stunned AGAIN. what is with this kick to my face in combat. if you play elden ring like its a kids game to you, sure play this, but if you want to play an anime game thats casually fun or a little difficult to jostle your jimmies, dont play this, it will stress you out trying to combat 4 enemies that can stun lock you in the start of the game making it hard to engage at the start. and theres also the healing and market, nothing to say for its equipment but a weapon and 3 modules to give you a little edge, and then cosmetics so mediocre id rather waste my cash on whale bait games like vindictus or black desert. theres no long to the games story, the cut scenes are cut aways to picture plays that fly about the screen left and right, the effort to get you involved in the cut scenes is hard to find, and its not like they cant do decent cut scenes and put effort into animations and voices, they did great for that, but said screw it for cut scenes, and instead pitched it off to some middle rate graphics designer that took stills and just flick back and forth like an indie animation studio, and in the near start of the game, THEY DO ANIMATE A CUT SCENE LIKE MOMENT, theres talking matching mouth movement, they know how to do it but they instead mainly did picture cut scenes? why? why do they put effort into half the game like it doesnt really matter to them? Ugh, Take my words with a grain of salt and see it for your self, either dish out the money and play it or watch youtube videos on what goes on in the game. but my opinion, they just cash grabbing with this.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not that there is anything outright bad about the game, it's just exceptionally mediocre in almost every aspect.Two-thirds of the game are cut scenes presented mostly as still images, which basically turns the game into a visual novel. That wouldn't be bad if the writing was interesting but not far into the game I lost all interest in what the characters do or what happens to the game world. Combat mostly is about cycling through the skills on cool-down, fighting the same enemies over and over again just in different combinations of enemies pitted against you. Map exploration is practically non existent because there is nothing interesting to be found. The music is bordering on something playable in an elevator. The only well done thing was the visual design, which wasn't always translated that well into art assets.Verdict: not terrible, just forgettable.

_childDocuments_.review: As an anime, action RPG this game is quite solid. The combat has a unique take on the tried and true "break" system many action RPGs are a fan of using. This one involves using abilities of your MC and party members to whittle away at an enemies weaknesses and possibly trigger elemental reactions to really push their break. Once the enemy is broken you essentially get a prompt to get to execute the enemy (and rather stylishly too I might add). I personally found that the combat become a bit of a drag for me later in the game. Some fights just felt like the enemies had way too much health or just wouldn't break and that's probably more on my misunderstanding of how to get the most out of the combat system but it still caused me to lower the difficulty as fights were no longer becoming a fun part of the experience.The game is quite visually appealing in combat and just walking around. I wish they took advantage of this more and took the time to make more talking sequences into full cutscenes because there really can be a lot of talking in this game. I've come to expect this from anime RPG games at this point so I went in expecting this but it's really boring watching stock expressioned faces with moving mouths talk rather than characters with full motion moving around and conversing in a space. We tend to get the anime art itch scratched in these games with the dialogue also in there but then we're just staring at faces vomitting text. Maybe they could get away with this 10 or so years ago but anime production has been increasing in quality and these games need to step up and commit to keeping up with the times.The story is anime quality and nothing to swoon over but it is solid and I found it interesting enough to keep me going most of the time. This is a game that requires at least two full playthroughs to get the full story as the game has you choose between 2 MCs to start with and you are locked into that one for that playthrough. I played them alongside on another and would swap whenever hitting a new act/chapter or when it felt like I hit a good milestone in the story.The music is also rather fun and interesting. I have no idea what genre to classify it as but it reminds of a mix of what Persona 3 and 4 had to offer with upbeat tracks that sometimes have vocals but you're not really sure why as they tend to be nonsensical lyrics (not bashing it just trying my best to put into words what I was hearing). Overall though the tracks are all fun, unique, and set the mood effectively. I'll recommend overall because I do see the potential for others to enjoy the combat especially. I really do think it was just a personal issue I had with grasping it. As I found out though if you can't enjoy the combat, the rest of the game doesn't have as much to stand on. So try it on a free weekend or the demo if that's still up and make sure you enjoy the combat before committing to a full purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: For starters, this game probably isn't for everyone.If you're on the fence on buying, here's your checklist:- You like fast paced, yet semi-thoughtful combat. - You Enjoy anime art style - Linear game play does not make you want to poke your eye out- Your imagination is capable of dialogue developing the story rather than full motion movies- You are a fan of the weird - creepy characters, dark themes.- You don't mind cliches. Like the female anime protagonist that doesn't who doesn't give a care about anything and never smiles- You're okay using a game controllerThat being said: This game is captivating for me .The story is interesting, yet not very deep, but the they managed to capture what I feel is very important to me in a JRPG, character and story development. It's visually fun to look at. I wish there was a 21:9 aspect ratio option but this is typically left out of Namco Bandai games (disappointing but understandable) at the beginning of this game the combat felt a little sluggish and every time I got knocked down It felt like an eternity to get back up and only get knocked down again. After a few hours and getting skills that allowed me to bounce back quickly and learning the motor skills of combat, I often felt like a  bad-ass which is a great sign the game developers focused on this. To sum everything up: If you like fast paced games like DMC  but with AI teammates, mixed in with a slew of mild skill tree development and some cool anime mini-scenes, building relationship with characters that feel thought was put into, all along a linear path, then this is for you.If you can't tolerate any of the above it will probably feel average, but you will at least feel the developers put some love into it.It's a must buy for me but I have very selective tastes.

_childDocuments_.review: I mean, its fine? Combat feels satisfying, but a bit simple later on, and some enemies end up being either too tanky, or just rely on a gimmick that forces you to use a certain power that defeats them near instantly. Soundtrack slaps, but the plot is kinda a mess. There's a lot of good ideas, but it introduces too many things, and then never follows up on all of them correctly. Might have worked better if they used the two playable characters like SA2,s Hero and Dark stories, with each campaign being a lot shorter, but having much more unique gameplay and story content, with a final campaign that ties everything together. Still pretty fun to play, but has a decent amount of issues, and DEFINITELY isn't worth the full 60$. Also ignore the DLC, its overly expensive and doesn't seem to actually add much worthwhile content for the price.

_childDocuments_.review: [NO SPOILER REVIEW]Aight I just beat the Yuito story of Scarlet Nexus... which is literally only half the game and it took me roughly around 36 hours on hard. I will say these small things since I haven't fully completed it yet but I feel like it needs to be said (Keep in mind most of this was from me playing on HARD):- I urge you to play this game--- If you're an experienced gamer, --- If you just want story, play on normal--- Game is boring on easy- This game is actually REALLY good- The combat is a solid 9/10 for me--- Combat is EXTREMELY satisfying and your teammates actually do something for once in a video game--- The game forces you to think critically about what you should do next and what powers to use and combine--- You must assess your surroundings and make sure you know what you're going up against or else the game will punish you for slacking- The music sounds generic at first but once you hear it enough times in isolation, it's phenomenal- With a huge cast of characters that this game has, it's really saying something that I can remember everyone's names- Those of you that play English dubbed can be at ease, the dub is REALLY good- The story is REALLY good- Hanabi - This game is animation dependent most of the time--- This means that in order for you to continue your next action, you need to wait for your first animation to finish--- There is no animation cancelling in this game- Combat can be glitchy --- Instant kills on the player--- invisible projectiles and entities stun-locking and blocking the player--- The revive button--- That one boss you all heard me talk about before--- Luka's ability not working like 10% of the time-  (Just an opinion, not gonna say anything other than a short phrase of what I think about it)--- Even though i'm only halfway done with the game with 36 hours in... it honestly feels like I was 60 hours in the game. Which is a great thing. I'm sucked into this game's universe and I want more.If I were to give this game a rating right now, it's a wobbly 8/10 and I think it's a game people should play if you feel up for it, or just browsing your list of games wondering what to play. Honestly color me surprised but I thought this game wasn't gonna be that good but it was A LOT better than I thought it was gonna be.P.S: Just in case you guys wanted to know, I was playing on hard the whole time and my death count is: 2...I'm pretty sure you know why

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about this game, but I feel as though the bad outweighs the good points of this game. The bad: 1. the camera is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mess. So much so, to the point where it becomes nearly impossible to keep track of the enemy/enemies, leading to your attacks not connecting properly.2. during a certain boss fight, I actually started falling through the world... after the cutscene. Had to boot the game up again.3. There's a certain degree of disconnection in regards to the combat. What I mean by that is, your attacks don't feel as strong as they appear. If that makes sense.4. This one isn't as bad as the other three - if anything, this is just my personal take; cliché anime tropes. Guy conveniently likes things the girls like, girls fall in love with guy. Guy doesn't notice. Please. Please stop this.5. The story is... odd. Certain decisions were made regarding the male main character (in-game) that would otherwise be unrealistic and just downright ridiculous. This is just another personal take on it, so you may see it differently. That's all I can say right now since I'm only 16 hours in at the time of writing this.Now, the good:1. The music. The music carries the combat at times, however.2. The graphics. Although I'm not a fan of the art style for anime-like games, this time around it's done surprisingly well.The game certainly has its charm and maybe that's why I keep playing it. Just wish the camera was less problematic.

_childDocuments_.review: I have only completed one characters story and I intend to go back for the other at a later date (so I don't burn myself out).I can't say much about the story without potentially spoiling anything, but if you're used to anime then you should be fine with it. They throw enough twists into the plot to keep you interested, though some are predictable or the characters seem to conveniently forget to mention something until its relevant five minutes later. The main cast of characters are rather trope heavy, but do have some depth to them and they aren't there purely to push the protagonist forward.You get to explore the cities which is nice, but quickly loses its appeal when all you do is look for side-quests and items strewn around the place. While some of the NPC's can be interacted with, they don't offer anything insightful. Shopping and saving are both done by one NPC, and the equipment is mostly generic stat boosts.When it comes to the combat, it is heavily reliant on your psychokinesis and companion abilities, as your weapon attacks don't seem to do a great deal of damage on their own. This isn't necessarily a bad thing, as it keeps you from mashing the attack button the whole game and you are able to use the aforementioned abilities regardless of your team composition.There is a skill-tree to make the combat flow better and feel more fun. While some are simple percentile increases, they do make an impact if you invest in the right ones. Your companion abilities can also be improved by increasing bond levels.This section is purely self-indulgent and for things that, in my opinion, could change:1. Add invulnerability frames to the dodge, or widen the 'perfect dodge' window2. A guard ability3. Multiple weapons for the protagonists that have special effectsWhile the game isn't perfect, it is certainly an enjoyable experience. It's just a shame that Bandai Namco have delivered an interesting world but don't delve very much into it's lore (just like Code Vein).

_childDocuments_.review: Set in alternate future, Scarlet Nexus takes place on a version of Earth that has advanced technologically and physiologically concerning the human brain. This physiological advancement has given way to humans with superpowers. Yuito and Kasane are the two protagonists within the game recruited into the “Others Suppression Force” or OSF. The OSF is a defense branch made up of people with supernatural abilities. Others are cruel brain-craving monsters that appeared on Earth prior to the current events of the game. Although there seems to be a common enemy perceived by the citizens, shadowy behavior goes on within the separate factions of Earth. New Himuka where the game initially takes place has an Orwell-ian state going on while the sister city of Seiran continues to “advance” medical technologies, and then there’s the mysterious religious state of Togetsu in the snowy mountains. Each state has conflicting views on how the safety of the Earth is handled. Discrepancies lead to an intersecting threat placing all of humanity in harms way. For all the players in the game, you would think that this would make some solid intrigue, but in the end it tasted like a flat soda. Flavor with no bite. What Scarlet Nexus excels at is team building and intrapersonal relationships. Some of the best and most heartfelt writing is in the pieces shared in-between missions. Each playable character has a different relation with the team. Once both characters are played it feels as though the whole story of the teammates come together. Stories vary from learning how to convey feelings to finding meaning in life after OSF. This game is a solid example of how to build up a cast that you can get behind and care about. The action combat is easily one of the strengths of Scarlet Nexus. The action mixes RPG elements (i.e. skill trees, combat enhancement powers, upgradeable gear) with stylish combat. Combat is typically fast paced and frantic. Enemies have their health bars as well as “crush” bars. The crush bar is essentially a stagger meter with the added ability of rewarding you with OHKO opportunities no matter where the enemy health gauge is. The exception is only bosses. Typically, the crush gauge is tough to burn, but with abilities granted by teammates you can exploit weaknesses that melt the crush gauge. Learning the weakness of your enemies rewards you with the satisfaction of slicing through them at accelerated speeds. Bosses, although unique in move sets, are just enemies with a larger health bar. Here the game ask you to exploit the weakness pointed out during the battle so that you can take a large chunk of health off using “Brain Crush” (the OHKO move used on regular enemies). More times than not, the rule of 3s apply here and now the boss is dead. What the bosses have going for them is some truly creepy designs, akin to Del Toro and Junji Ito. Its just disappointing that once you understand how to make the most out of either Yuito or Kasane even bosses are light work on harder difficulties.  Being straight forward with you, there are 26 across both characters (13 each), with a handful of side quest that are of the “go here and kill the thing” variety. The most frustrating thing is that half of them are the same just with the POV of a different character. You would think that seeing the different POV for the separate character would be reason enough to play those missions over again, I assure you they are not. I could’ve lived with doing the alternate missions only on the second playthrough. What is worth it though is what I mentioned above, the “bond episodes”. The bond episodes see you forging relationships with your team and connecting on a personal level. These bonds are progressed normally throughout the game and accelerated by giving them gifts you can make within a crafting menu or get during side missions. Challenge missions are offered, but I did not partake in them because my interest with the game was wanning Scarlet Nexus boast tunes that had me think back to the days of SEGA Dreamcast techno-anime tracks. Most were catchy! Most importantly, it captured the feeling of the game. Scarlet Nexus has a busy futuristic setting, and when you’re in those areas, It captures that. Other times it has you going to quiet, slow peaceful areas had matching music that felt in line with the game. The art is standard anime cell shaded art. A tried-and-true style also reflected in performance of my game that never saw it dip below 144FPS. What was different was the way Scarlet Nexus did its cut scenes. They opted for a comic book style telling which had me wanting more of the real time cut scenes they had sprinkled in throughout the game. The real time cutscenes were high action anime in the vein of the average shonen.

_childDocuments_.review: The game's very well made, in terms of the story, it has many twists and unexpected parts that are not revealed. Only at the last or second last chapters do they start to reveal these pieces of information which really fills in the gaps in the story.The best part of the game is the combat experience, I can tell that many many hours has been put into making the combat unique only to this game. With the extremely cool and vibrant particle effects, it truly makes me want to play the game more. I especially like the SAS, instead of allowing us to switch between the main character and other side characters, they lend us their abilities which makes it another aspect for us to learn and become more skilled in.  Lastly, the effort put into the graphics and every unique environment of every chapter is something that must be take note of. The graphics of the ever changing environments and the different stages you can go to grind some levels during the rest time, are astonishing. Every part of the stage is different in theme, a construction site, high-tech headquarters, a factory that has so many paths that it is like a maze. Every stage has a different feel and additions special to only that stage.However, one thing that they have to improve would be the keyboard and mouse support. At the start of the game, I tried to play the tutorial with a keyboard and mouse. It was unbelievably bad, the mouse sensitivity was very low even at the max sensitivity and the whole feeling of moving my mouse felt off. The keyboard did not have very good binds to the different actions of my avatar, I could not access half of my initial abilities and could not pass the tutorial...Also, the support on different controllers can be improved. When I changed to controller after knowing that it supports controller better, I was clueless for a period of time. The only controller I had was a nintendo switch controller, and the prompts I got during the tutorial did not match every button of my controller. All in all, Scarlet Nexus has been an eye-opener to me as my first Bandai Namco game. It has numerous of features that can definitely keep you hooked for at least a week. However, there are definitely problems with the controller support which I hope they can improve in the future. F.Y.I you may want to wait for a sale before buying this game, I had to spend 2 weeks of my allowance for this :c

_childDocuments_.review: Scarlet Nexus is a linear JRPG that focuses heavily on dialogue and story. While the game features a stylish combat system, its implementation suffers from myriad of issues and ultimately feels repetitive and stale once the initial spectacle wears off.At the start of the game you choose to play as either Yuito or Kasane, both of them have different combat styles as well as their own roughly 15 to 20 hour campaign (or more if you do the side missions). Campaigns intersect and converge at certain points, but outside of these moments there is a lot of unique content to be experienced for both characters. In order to see the full narrative, you need to complete both campaigns but I have to admit that after beating the game as Kasane - I don't really feel like playing it again, as the quality of the game takes a massive plunder in the latter chapters.What surprised me the most about the game is its setting and the narrative, which takes influences from japanese and western sci-fi, handles some of the themes commonly seen in cyberpunk and even mixes in some supernatural elements. Unfortunately the story, storytelling and its delivery, pacing and the hamfisted reliance on anime and JRPG tropes ultimately fail to do justice to what could have been an amazing setting along with some solid world building.What I liked about the game:- Monster designs- Soundtrack is excellent, even if sometimes poorly utilized during the game- Setting and world building- Art direction in overall is excellentWhat I didn't like about the game:- Lack of enemy variety is an issue and it actively ruined the last few chapters for me, as you are constantly fighting the same 3 or 4 enemies that are relatively spongy.- Combat starts off as stylish and impresses with its spectacle, but ultimately ends up feeling shallow and stale imitation of a mediocre fighting system from a character action game. Particular issues with the combat are how repetitive it is, constant offscreen attacks in multi enemy fights, poor targetting, poor camera and animation locking that makes combat in general feel rather clunky.- Side quests are not worth doing and are poorly designed in general- Level design is poor and consists mostly out of linear tunnels that have occasional optional dead ends you can visit to pick up a consumable item at.- Poor pacing, alternating at roughly 60/40 to 70/30 ratio between dialogue or cutscenes/gameplay.- Excessive usage of anime/JRPG tropes: Fights you cannot win due to reasons, power levels, "No time to explain this critical piece of information which if explained would actually resolve this plot thread instantly", characters suddenly becoming extremely incompetent when cutscenes demand it and last but not least the power of friendship taken to such extremes that it completely defies any form of logic.- Chapters 10 & 12 drag on for way too long and serve as an excellent example where the excessive padding sours the experience.When it comes to the state of the PC port, I would say it is functional but comes with a lot of issues such as:- Shadows seem to disappear occasionally and won't return until a save is reloaded- Keyboard and mouse has a lot of issues including menu navigation problems, in general I'd definitely recommend using a controller.- DualSense (ps5) controller support of the game is bugged: You can either disable Steam controller support which makes the game display correct button prompts but unfortunately all the buttons are completely messed up making the game unplayable. Alternatively you can use Steam controller support but in this case the game displays Xbox controller prompts but at least functions properly.- Alt + Tab seems to be a big issue for the game particularly in the full screen mode, while you can tab out you might not be able to tab back in. Particularly on multi monitor setups, the game might actually tab back to wrong monitor if on any monitor at all. Which forces you to kill the task.That being said, I think Scarlet Nexus is a 6.5/10 or a 7/10 game - there are a lot of things to like but also many issues that bring down the entire experience. For now I would recommend waiting for a sale and even then I would recommend buying the game only if you have a huge tolerance towards repetitive gameplay and anime tropes.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay starts off fairly basic, and takes time to hit its stride (about 5-6 hours into the campaign). The combat system's biggest strength is the ease with which you can pull off flashy moves and switch between styles on the fly. When in full flow, you can get up close with your melee weapon, fling psychokinetic projectiles, or borrow your party members' abilities to buff your attacks or exploit an enemy's weakness. It all looks and sounds more complicated than it really is, which is to the game's credit. Another one of the game's strengths is how there are times when more than one ability (or a combination of abilities) can be effective against a type of enemy. One such example is how you can either slow down time, turn invisible, or use teleport to tackle an elusive enemy. Fighting waves of enemies is a lot of fun in short bursts, as you switch between abilities to target enemy weak points and set up finishing moves that are satisfying to pull off. I say 'in short bursts' because the game loses steam in the later areas when battles take priority. You will have to kill wave after wave of the same enemies with very little variation. This is where the best action/hack-and-slash games excel, and this game falls short. Some creativity put into the level design, set pieces, enemy type combinations would have helped the gameplay loop not feel as repetitive. Introduction of a few new enemies here would have helped keep things fresh (entirely new enemy types, not bulkier versions of old ones). However, to the game's credit, It only starts feeling repetitive in the last few levels. The boss fights are more creative and memorable, helping reduce the tedium a fair bit. The side quests aren't meaningful or engaging in any way. It basically boils down to "kill 3 of 'enemy type A' with X move/ability to get Y rewards".  They are as bare bones as side missions can get, and the rewards are often not interesting. The upgrade/skill system is fairly linear, more like a standard action slasher than an RPG. As fun as all the abilities are in combat, I wish they could have been implemented into free roam and platforming better. The game isn't just fighting monsters, you spend a fair amount of time bonding with the side characters. The side characters themselves are wholesome and worth investing time in. Bonding with them will also unlock new abilities. The story is also engaging, and *almost* worth playing just for the plot. My only gripe with the storytelling is the lack of animated cut scenes during key moments. The comic book style is fine during conversations, but the character models look amazing when they are moving around and emoting during action sequences. The music is great and never gets overbearing during combat. The graphics are very good, and will age well over time.Final thoughts: Fun mix of hack-and-slash and lite RPG. Not deep in either aspect but combines them seamlessly. I would not personally get it for the gameplay or the story alone, but they work well together to deliver a memorable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly downloaded this game by complete mistake, I own a good few Bandai RPGs so there's that. I intended to install Code Vein but I mixed up the names therefore here I am. I came in with ZERO expectations as to it's quality, art design, story telling etc. And quite frankly I was left with a bitter taste in my mouth after beating the game as Kasane. I will probably not do a playthough as Yuito as I really didn't enjoy the game.Credit where credit's due; SN is a beautiful game with amazing art and environment design. A dedicated and high quality english VA cast which I greatly enjoyed. Finally it's one of those games where the difficulty falls off a cliff and your appreciation soars above when you fully understand the mechanics. (Kinda like Neir, and Souls games but not really.)    However that's where the praises end. The aforementioned points the game has can't push the game past a solid 3/10. I am not going to be kind to the game from this point onward and I suggest you play the demo if you are interested in the game, as it's not good. I take issue with the simple, repetitive combat; painfully annoying characters; atrocious plot-holes; and most importantly the user experience (Camera control ruins a lot of the scenes too.). Full disclosure I played start to finish on Steam Deck.UX: SN's UX can be described as lazy and sloppy. Menus are slow, loading (ssd) is slow, camera is restrictive, character tutorials repeat over and over on certain maps, frame rate can affect the gamespeed. All of these issues are annoying at best and detrimental at worst. Then there's how SN handles cutscenes and conversations.The devs (Who are Tales Series Vets) decided to go with this ugly and jarring voice manga panel style. The team has very talented animators, who make amazing animated cutscenes. However every tense moment is always undercut by this slow impact-less manga style bogging down the pace of each plot point. A plot that isn't very good at that. Then there's the 20 min length of many interactions. They were so long my Deck would almost go to sleep as I watched them. Also there's NO pause option only a skip, and often they take away the ability to skip line by line instead skipping the entire scene.Characters: I hate Kasane. I hate Naomi. Why? Kasane makes literally every situation worse actively, to the extent where I wanted the game to end with her committing -spoiler-Suicide-spoiler-. The game wears all it's twists on it's sleeves, and as a rule Kasane always has to choose the worst option for the sake of drama. Now Naomi on the other hand was a character that screams -spoiler-"I'm going to die right now"-spoiler- and she was unrealistically annoyingly nice and well liked by everyone. Thankfully she got Fridged so hard that I cheered because it meant maybe the story could begin to move. (it didn't)Shiden the RivalTM ended up being my favorite character because you could actually tell he changed on the inside. And actively pushed to be someone who wouldn't hold down the crew. All in all his character was written as the most human of all of Kasane platoon, and left me feeling touched on a personal level. However it doesn't offset the 25 hrs I spent to get there. (Steam didn't track playtime correctly I have 35 hrs on my save file.)Plotholes: Don't write time travel if you don't understand what a grandfather paradox is. Heck, don't write time travel if you don't have a concrete version you want to use. Don't make time travel the main plot point for the main villain's goal if the MC's only exist because the main villain using time travel. Oh this is just the beginning of the issues with the plot, characters just do whatever they want with no concequences. The story made no sense, and really pushed no moral premise. It attempted to ask deep questions, but gave shallow answers. This game is one of those with a nobody's the bad-guy endings. Honestly it feels like you control the accidental bad guys who genuinely screw over everyone else, and do a poor job of cleaning up their mess at everyone's expense.Combat: Combat is inbetween Nier & and a Tales game. However it doesn't do a good job at copying either even if what came out is consistent. Combos are simple since you only have 5 attacks in total when you begin the game and about double the attack limit by the end. Another issue I encountered is that the combat can cause frame dips which change the game speed for several seconds, affecting the timing of dodging and even shutting down telekinetic throws which are one of your most powerful attacks. Furthermore basic functions for a Neir style game are missing like a double jump, no sprint, alternative combos from swapping from heavy to light attacks. Some of these are features you can unlock later like the double jump. But the game still feels restrictive due to the exclusions that would make movement more fluid and the clunky camera and lock on. Then you get your Tales style hard limits on combos, weapons you can use, party size, item capacity, etc, which don't exactly elevate the gameplay. Though thanks to its roots as a Tales game there are some neat link effects (Powers/SAS) you can use, but nothing like Arts or Combo Arts from the Tales games. These choices all add up as you play the game and result in unexpected jank. Powers: However I'm going to move on to the powers. You have a cool suite of powers in Kasane squadron; Telekinesis, Duplication, Electrokinesis, Superspeed, etc. However they are typically under utilized by both the writers and game-play designers. This is a problem because these powers don't have described limits, so it leads to me asking why humans are even under threat to these Others in the first place. Especially with Karen being as OP as he is. Telekinesis for example is super OP, you can manipulate ANY physical object with your mind. If you've seen Mob Psycho 100 or any ESP. focused anime you know how broken it can easily be. In Kasane's case you see she can easily manipulate several tens or hundreds of tons and I'd guess she can use it with the dexterity of a human hand (the knives are my reasoning). She can do all of this at the beginning of her story, as a super elite who's been trained since she's 8. Kasane quickly learns she's not OP and still has a ton of room to grow. So why doesn't she just learn to lop these things into peices like Lucy from Elfen-lied? The game really loves to make a point that she's growing stronger and more experienced but she doesn't have any notable changes to her moveset from the start. Why can she fly in one level but not the rest? Why can she manipulate the monsters directly in brain crush but not before hand? Why can she do that in a cutscene but not in game, and vice versa.Again the powers are under utilized, where Shiden is the only character who makes sense to have trouble, and is arguably the most useful SAS link. He has potential but he's weak and has to continueously train to not hold back the rest of the group.  Furthermore he is scared of his powers and won't use them to their fullest extent. In game play his attacks don't always work to stun enemies nor does he have the capacity to instantly kill anything, unlike Seto can in the story (who he admires). The other characters don't have an excuse. Either in the story or in the application of their powers they feel underwhelming or plain stupid. In conclusion: This game really sucks, like royally bad. I can stomach the combat and I enjoyed the artstyle (Even if it's style over substance). I just think there are better games out there. Like Code Vein the game I installed after I beat this game is way-way better than SN for a lot of reasons. Big reason being, in CV You as a player have the agency to decide how the story ends even if it's only superficial. Your crew doesn't only make bad decisions for drama. SN is like some ugly love child of two better franchises by comparison.TLDR: IDK how TF SN nearly got a GOTY, its bad.

_childDocuments_.review: After some deliberation I decided to give it ups (and yet another game that shows steam should have at the very least yes/no/neutral scale).Make no mistake, this is basically JRPG with significant skew towards action combat - of which the most similar is probably Nier.From primary issues this game so far has:controls:- camera sensitivity is largely broken - it's tied to fps + it's tied to whether your character is moving; people say it's bad both in controller and kb/m context; prepare to crank up DPI- most useless implementation of a gamepad workaround called target lock - no target tracking with camera, while your camera is stuck in one direction; what the bloody actual ♥♥♥♥ ? You can unbind that key, as nearly the whole game you will be fighting packs of mobs either way- as usual, lack of camera relative attack direction (aka camera lock)- kb/m controls - as usual - inherit controller limitations; so get ready to cycle through items to use (by 1) and cycle through sas shortcuts (by 4)- unable to bind key combinations, so forget anything cleverWhile the standard kb/m failure sting, kb/m still beats the ♥♥♥♥ out of gamepad here - as quick and precise camera control is very good thing to have here and target lock is utter garbage in SN.other:- complete and utter lack of any fanservice whatsoever; you can literally smell that stink of Soyny and "muh western standards" ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥On a positive side, the game actually has likable (mostly ...) characters and passable story - which gets better later, though don't expect steel logic and plotholeless plot. Combat also gets notably more interesting later, especially when you get access to full SAS set. All in all I enjoyed my time, despite some quirks and issues. I'll prooly play the other char's route in due time.Ah, make sure to play on highest difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: Really obviously made on a tight budget but they managed to get a good game out of it. While most of the story is told in slideshows as a trade-off, pretty much every non-npc line of dialogue in the game is voice-acted and very well, and there's a LOT of it too.  The story itself is alright, veers off into crazy 90s JRPG territory but that's kind of inevitable when you're trying to sell a high-concept story on a budget of 10 bucks and some gum. There's also two protagonists with entirely different stories & parties and they frequently cross over, adding heavily to replay value.Also you get a neat base that slowly fills up with crap you gift your teammates(and they will start adding their own junk as you get closer with them) which is fun. Giving your gardening friend some plants, for example, ends up with flowers and vines all over the place. Give someone a booze set and bottles will show up in the kitchen. They'll also goof off with this stuff in their spare time, too. It's a nice bit of characterization on a budget. Gameplay itself is decent enough though somewhat hard to get used to, it's mostly about managing a suite of buff-like powers that alter your moveset in subtle or overt ways. Every action is very committal(for a character action game) and enemy damage is pretty high so you need to know your enemies' weaknesses and prioritize threats to effectively fight. Of course there's also a lot of items to help brute-force your way through so it's not TOO punishing on lower difficulties. Having different party members(and thus powers) most of the time means that both playable characters approach combat situations very differently too. Both characters do share a power in psychokinesis, which typically means weaving hurling junk at enemies into your combos but occasionally manifests in rad ways like surfing a bus through a crowd of enemies. Overall it's not super in-depth but it's good enough and doesn't overstay it's welcome.Anyway it's not a life-changer or anything but it's a high-concept story told decently well on a budget and is an easy recommendation to buy if you like good ol' anime action games.

_childDocuments_.review: Just came off of finishing my first playthrough (Kasane) and I plan to do Yuito's next. I honestly was surprised by just how much I enjoyed this game both from the style, story, and characters. Going in I expected a fun romp, with some decent sci-fi story and I got way more than that. The characters are written and executed so well, and everyone feels alive within the world itself. There are typical JRPG themes that are followed, but it very much strays from that and leans into the sci-fi genre where the world moves with the characters and the characters are not the sole source of conflict and change. The overarching plot is very much a mystery thriller, with a lot of information left for the player to either observe or learn later. Some have complained there are plot holes but I personally fail to find any. Any answers you might want seem properly there in the game itself. I really appreciated feeling connected to the character's sense of "what in the ♥♥♥♥ is happening" because there were still more mysteries to uncover. The gameplay itself is nothing to scoff at either, once I really hammered down how to utilize my allies' abilities and the way the flow of battle went I found myself really enjoying every fight. It really helps that the game enables you to feel like you're directing an action sequence with the way the cut-ins, and other sfx, weave their way in. Solidly recommend, there's even a demo and your save data gets imported into the full game. Music also slaps. Creative direction as whole, very slaptastic.My biggest complaint is how ♥♥♥♥♥♥ the localization is. I'm not fluent in Japanese, but playing with JP audio and ENG subtitles, I really saw just how little effort they gave into actually capturing what was said. This extends far enough that some things are just objectively incorrectly translated. Also, the amount of grammar mistakes....sure, nitpicky and a bit petty but come on. You couldn't proof read a single time before you shoved it in there?

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing games for over 25 years and at a certain point during that time I began to lean more towards western developed games. However, as I grow older I find myself going back to Japanese developed games to the point I barely play any western games anymore. Why? One reason: game-play. Video games can be a lot of different things offering different kind of experiences and that's wonderful. But when it comes to action games it seems like Japanese developers have a better sense of what makes them fun. Timing, movement, attack patterns, character and combat progression systems. You can be assured that a lot of thought is going to go into these aspect in a Japanese action game, resulting in a  truly compelling and immersive action experience, and this is totally the case with SCARLET NEXUS. In contrast Japanese games can often be found lacking in the narrative and story-telling department. That's why I was pleasantly surprised when SCARLET NEXUS's story picked up quick revealing a fairly compelling twist that put me in the edge of my seat, and left me curious for what would happen next. Often the story in a Japanese action game is there only to serve the purpose of getting you from point A to point B, but this is certainly not the case here.P.S.On release day some people were review bombing the game because it did not met their technical expectations. I play the game on max settings, 2K resolution, 60FPS, with a game-pad and I've had zero(0) technical issues or complaints.

_childDocuments_.review: I used to live in Japan for many years and at first I loved anime and manga, but over time I lost interest as it's just too much and everywhere. _childDocuments_.review: I thought Tales of Arise had bad writing, characters, and story, but man, Scarlet Nexus is just as bad, if not worse than ToA. You have no sense of exploration, due to the fact you are locked into a small, confined central hub where you talk to your companions (ultimately it amounts to a few rooms one may wander around in). Not only is this game much smaller than many JRPG counterparts, one is NOT allowed to walk around the map when there is no ongoing story mission, and the areas in which you explore are extremely boring, small, and uninspired. The characters are just as trope-y, one-note, and dull like in ToA, but the voice acting is pretty decent here. I do like the look and style of certain areas in Scarlet Nexus, but with such little direction for the character(s), a terrible story, and lackluster level design really hamper what could have been  a pretty decent game in a year filled with crap. One of the few redeeming factors of this game is the combat, but even then its sluggish and can be a bit boring. Enemies can be extremely OP even when one plays on easy, making one question whether they even play-tested their game to make sure it was balanced properly. With so many problems, this game is average at best and very below average at worse, which is why I'd rate it a 4/10, only slightly lower than ToA. Why? The game is shallow for a $60 asking price, and their DLC policy is becoming just as egregious as ToA's is. Overall, I'd pick this game up when it goes on-sale for 50% or more off. I personally do not recommend this game; many indie titles are more deserving of ones time.

_childDocuments_.review: May update this when I finish the other route (Kasane), but that'll depend on if I remember or not.It took me about 40 hours to complete the first route I did give or take as I'm sure I probably left it running unattended while I got up to do things a few times or to take a break.Overall this is a solid game with a good story and a pretty unique and interesting combat system. I like that there's two routes and that you get to see the other protagonist's side of things. They seem to have done this well as far as I can tell as each protagonist will primarily fight different bosses and experience different things.Story wise it's your typical anime game story about the "power of friendship" but with the brainpunk futuristic twist. It takes it a few phases (what the chapters of the game are called) for the story to really kick off, but it kicks off and it doesn't stop. In terms of Yuito's route and problems specific to him I felt that they weren't tied up as nicely. There's one issue that just kinda comes to a head and then they just kinda shrug it off the rest of the game. There's also another issue where it's this big disagreement and the resolution to it just feels like a quick fix because they wanted to move the plot along. These few things do detract from the story, but that doesn't make the story bad. I enjoyed the story quite a lot I just wish they'd resolved a few things better.Combat is a mix of weapon attacks and psionics (what the psychic abilities of characters are called). You have the protagonists which is psychokinesis and this sees you throwing objects or using objects in special ways to attack enemies (it depends on the object). The objects that allow for special attacks mainly have QTEs that are *very* easy to complete and give a lot of time to resolve the event. Sometimes it's moving the left stick in a direction, both sticks in a direction, spinning the left stick in a direction, mashing a button, etc. On top of that you can borrow the powers of others in a system called SAS in-game. At first you can only do one but there are abilities in the skill tree that allow you to use two and then four at the same time. This allows for a lot of different combinations to try by the end of the game when you have 8 psionics to pick from.Lastly during the standby phases (basically rest time between chapters) you quickly gain the ability to hang out with the people who are with you. You'll get bond episodes with the various members of your team as your bond level with them grows. Growing these bonds is also helpful to battle as it adds abilities to combat situations (for example, their SAS ability recharges faster or they'll block incoming attacks sometimes). These also lead into interesting side stories with each character and getting to know them better as well.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very good at looking good but it doesn't feel as good as it should, nor does it speak as well as it should. I know my hours aren't reflective but I've actually completed 85% of the game on Game Pass and am doing a full 100% run of the game on Steam. But after hearing the story again, I can't help but voice my gripes with it.I come from a background of Nihon Falcom games like The Legend of Heroes series and Tokyo Xanadu, and the Bandai Namco Tales of- series. I'm used to stories where the protagonist and his team aren't in the loop and slowly unravel it over the story. Where they are just pawns in a story and turn into Kings in the end fighting against the people who thought they were in control the whole time. It's an overused trope in this scene but when executed well, it makes for a fun ride.Scarlet Nexus is not one of those games. Constantly, this game seems to insult your intelligence by giving you half-baked context to every occurrence with the subtle promise that when you play the game from the other character's perspective, everything will make sense, or when you push further along in the game, everything will come together nicely. It will, but it doesn't feel good. A movie that does that well is Inception or heist movies, where you thought you had the whole plan in X, but really it was all Y and har har we got you.Instead of feeling good about what happened, it really just feels insulting because it's not written well. I'll spoil one point of the game below that just annoys me.Kasane and Yuito build such a great relationship but early on in Yuito's story, Kasane is caught with a knife in hand over his father's dead body and it proceeds into a battle between the two. She doesn't explain herself or justify, only to say a statement like "i promised you i would kill you". Then over the course of the battle she says ♥♥♥♥ like "I don't need to explain anything to you". I'm left baffled. Then after that, something like that is brushed off and you're left to bond with this seemingly heartless character with no explanation as to how something so terrible can be ignored.Simplified, it really feels like the story is rushed, the story moves into points of the game that the writers want, even if its not good storytelling. Where you're left thinking "wait that doesn't make sense, why's that?" and the writers just say "♥♥♥♥ you that's way, keep playing." It's one of the most frustrating stories and writing in main story video games I've ever encountered.The world is interesting. The combat style and interactions are cool. But it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥ over by some pretty terrible writing and story direction that seems more concerned with rushing things too fast to explain why the character constantly doesn't get a chance to understand anything until later on. You're left feeling like you're chasing after the story, and only until you get all the pieces will you realise that, well, it's not a good story.The game with the story included is a 7/10. Held up by its interesting combat, some characters, cool animations and textures, held down by its story, writing, and honestly terrible dodge system. If the writing was better, it could honestly be a very easily be an 8, maybe 9/10. But because it really isn't as bad as many other games out there, I'll have to recommend it because maybe the story frustrations aren't so bad for others.EDIT Post Clear:My opinion still remains true. The story is riddled with "well just because". It's not good, at least compared to its peers in the RPG space. The combat is fun (even though the dodge is ♥♥♥♥), its flashy and cool to look at, but the writing in the MSQ is honestly not good. An easy 6/10 for story MAX. If the game wasn't held back by its story, it would have been monumentally better.

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, this is a game about blowing up monsters using cool psychic powers. It's a game that makes "throw cars at people" one of your basic buttons. Your combat progression is almost entirely based on upgrading new superpowers and combining them together in ever-larger ways. By the endgame my staple combo was summoning clones then stopping time to freely team-blast a tough enemy with lightning.If that sounds cool to you, then I think you'll like this game. If not, then you'll probably be better off elsewhere.The plot itself is an earnest helter-skelter B movie with all sorts of things going on (don't be fooled by the slow start of the demo). I enjoyed it, but it's no artful realist piece if that's what you're after. I recommend against worrying about the fine details.There's an interesting gimmick in that you're asked to pick between two protagonists from whose viewpoint you'll see the story, but neither character sees the complete picture. I played through both characters simultaneously chapter-by-chapter, and I recommend it; I imagine some plot points will seem confusing or abrupt otherwise.(For completionists, note that there are some achievements you can only get by playing through the other story in NG+, though I'd still recommend playing through in parallel.)The first few chapters of the game have an annoying number of pop-up tutorials, made worse by applying to both stories, though I wouldn't think it a dealbreaker.The game also has some very pretty & outlandish scenery and enemy design going on, and it really helps to sell some of the dramatic moments. I hope the artists had as much fun as it looks they did.

_childDocuments_.review: Scarlet Nexus is a high quality JRPG for anime fans. The storytelling and character development is well done, with the critique that the more minor characters are very linear and predictable in their development. The story is well-presented, the world is fleshed out pretty well, and the characters are relatable on a personal level (no Kirito-syndrome for the MCs). The two MC paths you can take offer a very unique experience similar to the different routes of Nier Automata. Speaking of which, the combat is very fluid and has a comfortable skill ceiling. There is certainly a level of mastery to be achieved, and the combat easily carries the game to its end. The music is solid, but nothing to write home about. The graphics are top notch, I love this art style. The voice acting is good, but nothing exceptional or outstanding.The biggest gripe is the linearity of the dungeons/levels. It's very clearly "go here, kill these, do this." Fortunately, the combat is fun enough to make up for any lack of interesting level design. The boss fights are all very unique with lots of fun mechanics. The ally-system for swapping abilities and doing realtime events is very satisfying as well.And of course, the "dating sim" part of the game is well-made, without being overbearing or too weak. Some of the connections are superficial, but most of them are satisfying enough to scratch the itch if you're into that.If you are not into anime, this is probably NOT a game for you. Expect a lot of standard anime tropes. "The power of friendship", "the MC always wins", "the MC can go super saiyan", etc. But if you're comfortable with the usuals, then this should be a no-brainer title for any JRPG/action game fan.

_childDocuments_.review: Buying this game taught me the value of impulse control. If you're someone who can tolerate "anime" dialogue (dialogue that can only be taken seriously within the context of anime) then you're better off just watching the anime as it airs if you care about the story. The character writing isn't worth 50+ hours of your time and $60 of your hard earned money. On the gameplay side of things, it's trying really hard to be a Platinum Games title, which is why it feels so stilted and awkward when it fails to do that. Not only is it far less fluid and freeform as something like Nier: Automata or Bayonetta, it's often outright unresponsive. This game had a lot of potential, and I'm pretty sad I ended up hating it as much as I do. If you're looking for another game like this (and happen to have a Switch), I'd recommend Astral Chain. It's got a similar setting, it's polished as hell, the combat feels buttery smooth, and the writing is pretty solid. If you have to buy Scarlet Nexus though, PLEASE, for the love of God, wait for a sale. I'd say this is worth $20 bucks tops, and even that might be too generous.

_childDocuments_.review: Scarlet Nexus should be called anime the game, every anime trope is present. So while the story will lose you very quickly the gameplay takes a lot longer to finally tell you to get rekt as well.The combat itself is rewarding, slick and fun. There is plenty of enemy variety that is ruined by the decision of the developers to make the game as long as possible. Levels have bland layouts and drag on for ages while you defeat wave after wave of enemies. It starts to grind you down bit by bit and the final level commits the cardinal sin of having you play the entire game again.The bond system is nice but once again is stretched thin by how long the developers decided to make the game. There are good ideas here executed poorly. People now days want games to be longer but developers have exactly the same length of string to play with so to speak.What you end up with is the developers have created 10 - 15 hours of actual content, the rest is padding. There is much to like in this game, the soundtrack, the cell shaded visuals and the voice work are very good. Had the developers focused on delivering 10-15 hours of focused story and gameplay Scarlet Nexus would have been an excellent game.By the end of it all the story is a meandering, convoluted mess and game has stopped being engaging to play. Having played one half of the story there is absolutely no way I am going to play the other side.

_childDocuments_.review: Ultimately, a slog with your face pressed against the glass.I love anime, so I really wanted to love this one. Sci-fi? Check. Magic powers? Check. But I just can't. It felt needlessly arduous, and it fell into the old Japanese game trap of 2012, where they wanted to create an action game with a fighting game's combo system. Maybe that appeal is lost on American audiences, but much of the game felt like a carrot on a stick, and I was never going to get the carrot.If you've played Phantasy Star Online 2, there's a lot here that will feel familiar, old warts and all.The good:+ Great soundtrack. I feel like this is something Bandai Namco does well.+ Voice acting is great. Play with Japanese or English voices. Both teams did a good job.+ Interesting character and enemy designs. Enemies reminded me of Bayonetta + circus.+ Two characters to play. Ranged-ish and sword-melee are your options.+ Combos look neat. Fighting can be flashy, especially finishers.+ Interesting color design. They lean into the red/black motif, but they pull it off pretty well.+ Side characters are quite interesting.+ Environments looks nice.The bad:- MCs are forgettable. You have a Tsun and a loyal dog, and that's all they'll ever be.- Lack of practical variation between MCs. I opted for the ranged-ish character, and it still mostly felt like a melee character. The sword character can still levitate and throw objects, so other than the weapon animations, not a lot of difference here.- Side quests suck. They're barely even fetch quests. More like, "Do your main mission, but also, please pick me up some milk, which you will find randomly on your mission anyway. I'm too lazy to get it from the grocery store myself, but I'll give you a pat on the back for your troubles."- Combat feels pretty much the same after a short time. Do your main combo, enemy dead. Slightly different enemy, do a gimmick to weaken it, do your main combo, enemy dead. Repeat ad nauseum.- Feels like fighting with marionettes. Hits have no weight. You slash a monster, it flinches. Maybe it sometimes falls down. You get hit, you fall down, you hop back up (with the right ability). Are you doing good? I dunno, but your pals are now screaming at you to do the combo thing, so maybe.- General controls don't feel good. Tiny, limited environments, invisible walls, goofy jumps, all lend to feeling like a game from 2012.The unforgivable:-- Show, don't tell. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, this is 2023! Great game designers have been introducing "How to play" into tutorial missions for yeas, so you barely realize you're doing a tutorial. Why are you interrupting every moment I get to play with a two-page explanation for a new ability that I have to read? All of this should have been in some kind of "Episode 0" training mission.-- Do you like menus and submenus? Because the devs sure do, and good luck locating where to quit. I seriously spent a couple minutes on this. Not okay.-- The camera is terrible. Enjoy getting pinned by an enemy on a wall with the camera pointing anywhere but where it would be useful? Targeting helps, if you happen to target the right enemy, otherwise, it involves a combo press to switch targets, which may eventually get to the one you want.-- The camera is terrible. I said it twice. It was not fun babysitting the camera. It felt too close, even when I was given a ranged view. Maybe the character was placed incorrectly, but I always felt claustrophobic, like my face was pressed against the glass.-- The controls were made for a controller. You are releasing a game onto Steam. There shouldn't be two different ways to exit various contexts (Esc or Backspace). I don't mean you can use either/or. I mean you can only use one or the other, and it's not always the one you expect. Publisher should have spent some time investing in a proper control scheme port.-- You don't get to really play for long. You spend less time fighting than you do in the overworld or watching dialog scenes.

_childDocuments_.review: The combat in this game is a real let down. You are rooted in place by most of your actions and that is a really bad thing when you are fighting 6 or more enemies at a time and nearly every single attack that hits you will knock you down or stagger you. Enemies will rarely stagger and instead will simply stop attacking for short periods of time. The ability to dash cancel out of an attack would do wonders because i'm constantly taking damage from an attack that I can see coming but aren't allowed to react to. The "fix" would be to not attack as aggressively but the fights can already take a while because even the weak enemies have a lot of health. Fighting powered humans in this game takes all the above and makes it 3x worse. It's kind of like nero fighting the boss at the start of dmc5. You don't think that you are supposed to be able to beat them, but it can be done. The last 2 encounters were literally just survival matches. There are good points to this game though. The art style is fantastic in my opinion and was my main draw to this game. Everything to do with the world is pretty and interesting. Performance wise this game is one the best running titles I have played in a good while. I have not had a single hiccup, fps drop, bug or visual glitch using my radeon 5700xt. Load times are fairly short on my nvme ssd and only happen when fast traveling. The story so far isn't very deep  but that's all right. I really wish that there had been a demo on steam for this because it wasn't until the 3-4 hour mark when I figured out that I just wasn't going to like this game. They lock basic moves like an aerial dash behind the skill tree so I guess I should have known sooner but I really wanted to like it. It's on sale at the time of this review so if you wan't to give it a try anyway then I would sugggest blasting through as much as you can in the first 2 hours and really give that combat a good test run. If you decide you like it after that then start a new character to take in the story.

_childDocuments_.review: Scarlet Nexus is a fast-paced action JRPG featuring Yuito and Kasane, two adept soldiers with exceptional powers capable of combating the brain-eating beasts roaming the lands. With a cast of eccentric and likable characters, I found myself becoming invested in their woes. The story can be hit or miss, but overall it’s good enough. Fans of anime might notice commonly used tropes and character archetypes, but I don’t think it’s a negative since it isn’t overly in your face. All in all, this new IP from Bandai Namco surprised me with how much it burrowed itself in my heart.   In this futuristic adventure, you play as either Yuito Sumeragi, a trusting young man belonging to a powerful political family, or Kasane Randall, a pragmatic individual with ties to an influential household. Both are gifted "Psionics", a term for talented people with the ability to tap into the fullest potential of the human brain. When humanity is threatened by a horde of dangerous "Others", a species of mutated monsters, Yuito, Kasane, and their stalwart companions answer the call to protect their world. Having a dual perspective is a great way of introducing two distinct points of view and adds to the replayability. Once you’re done with one character, you can switch to the other in new game+, making your second playthrough feel fresh. It also has a wonderful and colorful cast of personalities whom I have fallen in love with. The protagonists, Yuito and Kasane complement each other well, with the former being the more emotional one, and the latter, the logical one of the pair. Their dynamic, alongside their compatriots, is one of the highlights for me. The story somewhat falters when the main antagonist enters the fray because they are shown to be this undefeatable force, but the final encounter was underwhelming. This character had me rolling my eyes every time they had a cutscene. Besides that, the plot is enjoyable enough, and it covers meaningful real-life issues, like climate change, tastefully. However, it does love dumping exposition every chapter, and it can get overwhelming in later parts.Yuito and Kasane do not vary too much.  Yuito fights with a katana, requiring him to be closer to his opponents, while Kasane attacks with multiple knives, enabling her fighting style to be close to mid-range. They have the same power, psychokinesis, which grants them the skill to use the environment against their enemies. I slightly prefer Kasane since her knives cover a wider spread than Yuito’s weapon, but I’ve noticed that he can connect with aerial opponents better than her and has a faster weapon speed. They both have access to the skill tree called the brain map and can consume brain points to improve their battle prowess, notably gaining perks such as improved dodging or increased attack. Additionally, they can induce a brain drive, a temporary power-up that augments attack/defense/weapon speed, for a minute or so. It is kind of annoying that you can’t independently activate a brain drive, but you can trigger a brain field at will, a concentrated version of a brain drive with a longer cooldown.Enemy encounters are often chaotic and fast-paced, so an assortment of powers is readily available to Yuito and Kasane. This is where the SAS is useful, and I love this system because it allows them to neurally link up with their teammates, adopting their unique capabilities for a short while. For example, if Shiden, an ally who can manipulate electricity, connects with Kasane through the SAS, she can coat her weapon with electric damage that can stun enemies. Only one can be activated by default, but as the playable characters grow, they can trigger multiple powers simultaneously, creating opportunities to break through the enemy’s guard and activate impressive finishing moves capable of one-shotting non-boss enemies with large health pools. Most of the locales are fairly straightforward. Unfortunately, they don’t encourage exploration too much, and except for the final areas, there aren’t many detours you can take. I was disappointed by this considering there is so much worldbuilding throughout the story, but the dungeons are so linear in comparison. There is an attempt to hide special trinkets and key items behind passageways that can only be opened using a teammate’s powers, but I would have loved more elaborate dungeon designs. Being a constant theme of the game, the bonds Kasane and Yuito form with their allies play a significant role in how effective they are in battle. By giving your friends gifts, you strengthen your relationship, and at higher levels, they can unlock special effects through the SAS and can even revive the main characters more frequently. Comrades like Luka, a fighter with teleportation expertise, can defend Yuito/Kasane from critical harm or even do follow-up attacks, damaging the opposition considerably. It is a nice touch that every present that our teammates receive is displayed throughout the base, giving the hideout a more homely feeling.For context, my specs are RTX 2070 Super, i7 4790S, 12 GB RAM. Playing at 2160p resolution.The anime-style graphics are quite endearing and beautiful to look at. Although the locations are linear, they are detailed and robust, bringing life into a world torn by meaningless fighting and deadly creatures. Cutscenes feature a visual novel structure, which can be off-putting to players who are not familiar with the style. However, I think the transitions between the still and animated cutscenes were done in a way that isn’t intrusive to the flow of the story. The model designs of the enemy creatures are also grotesque and haunting but surprisingly great in depicting just how altered these monsters have become. I didn’t come across any bugs and only had a performance dip at a particular location called the Heino Mountain. It has a snowy terrain, and bringing the camera down to glance at the icy floors throttles the framerate into the 30s. I believe the framerate dips are due to unoptimized reflections, and the only workaround I found is bringing the resolution down to 1440p. Other than that area, the framerate usually hovers around the 50-60s, depending on how busy it is.With 45+ hours of gameplay during the first playthrough and another 30+ hours in the next one, Scarlet Nexus provides its players a substantial amount of content to enjoy. I am completely enamored with its characters and their growth, making me truly invested in them. The soundtrack is also a big plus for me, as it harmonizes with the high octane nature of the game. I highly recommend Scarlet Nexus, and hopefully, you’ll enjoy it as much as I do.-- --If you have some time, check out my adventures in Scarlet Nexus!

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game, I'd say a solid 8.5/10. if the story didn't feel so rushed I'd almost give it a 10. That said, the story is still pretty good (if a bit confusing at times). The main reason to get the game is the combat. I'm over halfway through each campaign and I still haven't gotten bored of it. Despite the repetitive enemies (which seem to be mostly reskins of earlier enemies) the combat draws you in by introducing new and interesting mechanics to approach combat with. Some of this is by getting new team mates and combining your powers, while some of it is more internal like unlocking double-jumps and aerial attacks.I was expecting Code Vein 2.0 but the more accurate comparison would be to Nier: Automata with elements of Fire Emblem, such as developing the bond with your squad to get stronger.
