_childDocuments_.review: Love love love this game, praying and begging for a sequelWhen you start you're given an option to play as Yuito or Kasane (And then you can play through the other route later) I did Yuito->Kasane and in hindsight that feels the most natural/'correct' to me, either way you'll get the full picture regardless of order, with the exception of the opening bit (as it's essentially the same for both) each path is unique once the two MCs split upThe OST is a banger, not much more to sayThe combat is a lot of fun, you control the MC and borrow the powers of your party members for a fun mix/match of abilities that keeps combat fresh (tbh the MC power alone is cool, telekinesis is goated) speaking of MCs, for me Yuito felt the best to play but that could just be personal preferenceThe graphics/vibe might not be for everyone but I liked it a lot, I think it looks good and everyone looks coolI think the main thing that is definitely a bit jarring is between missions you hangout with your squad mates at the hideout (which is fine - you can give them gifts to increase your friendship with them and you get a lot of cool dialogue/interactions with each character - And there is also specifically 'team' bonding which is really sweet!) but every now and then characters you are beefing with will invite you to hangout at a neutral zone - It's not too bad since they do acknowledge the overall situation but yeah can definitely be a bit ???

_childDocuments_.review: If you like games like Astral Chain, you'll love Scarlet Nexus. It has a compelling story, strong supporting characters and nutty combat. It's not a perfect game however, as it lacks long-term replayability after finishing the main story (which the devs seems to be addressing with DLC challenge rooms) and has boring MMO-style side-quests (kill this, collect that, use certain skills on this monster etc). You should also know that most cutscenes are not animated but use static images instead (but fully voiced). Long story short, I really enjoyed this game and am really looking forward to a sequel. Play it for the main story and side character stories and you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Going into this game, I didn't know much about it other than it's cool anime art style and fun combat when trying the demo Bandai released on the consoles. In all honesty I was planning on skipping the game all together because while fun, the demo didn't really click. Boy am I glad I pulled the trigger and bought the game because I had a really fun time!Scarlet Nexus takes the combat you love in NieR: Automata/Replicant with a twist in character abilities and combines it with a bond/gifting system that is reminiscent of Persona and Fire Emblem. The game also borrows the "Plug-in" feature you'd see in Automata. The story and characters are great. Every character has their own style, personality, and story that really shines when you level up their Bonds and hang out with them. There is also 2 characters you can choose to play as(Yuito and Kasane) and both characters have very different story paths that converge so it's worth playing both routes to see all the different scenes you otherwise wouldn't see if you just stuck with one playthrough.I recommend this game to anyone who loves the combat in the NieR games, Persona/Fire Emblem's bond system, or just a straight up anime fan. Scarlet Nexus is definitely worth the pickup. Don't sleep on this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Combat is about the only redeemable feature of this game. It might be a bit repetitive, but still very satisfying. Everything else was disappointing.Bland characters with shallow development; the sort you always see in a generic anime or manga series.Boring side quests that seem closer to mini challenges than actual quests. They're just "beat an enemy with this method" or "collect this item then return it to quest giver".Horrible EX New Game (NG+) design; imagine spending hours grinding for the best equipment, only to find out there's no level scaling in this game and everything dies in one hit.Overall Score: 6/10I wouldn't recommend anyone - even JRPG fans - to buy the game at full price in its current state. Either wait for a sale, or don't bother with it at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game globally thanks to the combat mechanics and how smoothly it runs.The gameplay mechanics and handling is really easy and very satisfying, with some decent challenge. It does use cheap gimmicks to balance the game. The downside of an easy to handle gameplay means a very limited experience of diversity of skills. There isn't much like code vein, god eater or tales of diversity. The only minor variant is the protagonist and which one you will play. It's really easy to handle on both a controller or keyboard and mouse combo.The shiny items are easier to notice, finished the glowing star on the ground to pick up manually.The dodging mechanics are really based on timing, so don't get too frustrated.There is no point raising your level to an obscene level. The game auto compensate by putting enemies at a higher level then you or increase their HP and DMG.The side quests are the most boring ones i've seen. Waste of time as they are not interesting at all to do. Basically kill a certain enemy in a certain way.The graphics are getting better and better, fitting the style more and more, while not having a big toll on the hardware. It does require an SSD to avoid popping objects and loading of assets. But it's not a glaring issue like some games. So, if you got a dedicated HDD for gaming it will be fine.There is a very limited graphics controls, you don't have the really advance tweaking you would love to have. Which is a small downside but since it's not hard to run it isn't as bad as one would think.The sound and music is really good. For me it is fitting the universe and there isn't much to say more about the sound.The environment design is really good at first, some missions are just corridors of boredom. Sometimes you wonder if there was any attempt to push that more. Especially on the principle of the 2 different POV narrative, as this will get very repetitive and not much interesting. I feel that this is one thing they still lack, meaningful and fun environment, this is just eye candy but nothing else but a straight path. There could have been different path to reach a target, but they didn't both protagonist will trace the same path in the story. (except for story exclusive areas but those can be counted on 1 hand), offering little replay and exploration value.The open world options are really limited and barely brings anything.Let me go over a few things that are minor annoyance but still annoyance.OP video at launch of the game cannot be deactivated and is just annoying to always have to see it or press skip (just a small thing).Cannot deactivate tutorials. Really annoying, especially when you will do the second playthrough to see the different perspective.Beware if you install the game on 2 different PC, the steam cloud deleted all my saves, even trying to go directly on steam to recover those was in vain. So be careful to backup your saves just in case. I lost around 33h of gameplay, luckily I had a backup but it still gave me a stroke.Let me address the elephant in the room, the story itself has a lot of potential that was barely touched upon.This part is spoiler free:You have 2 choices, 2 different perspective and 2 different protagonist, there is no romance which I appreciate. As this story is full of cliche and would make the romance between those 2 so forced beyond justification it would be borderline a cringe fest.There isn't a specific order to play the game, the best one would be to progress both at the same time in parallel. But there is no load save options for easy swapping. You must go back to the title menu to do the swap.Honestly, many points of the story deserve more development and more attention but it is not really elaborated.Without stating much, you will hate the male protagonist trope and girl protagonist trope. This evolve for the better later on, but it is still heavily based on tropes that the anime/manga industry relies on.The dual narrative could be push even further. Especially for the current pricing. Honestly, at that price I won't recommend it unless it's around 45buck or less. Not enough push to be worth the full 100usd of a deluxe edition or basic 80USD.For a narrative driven game, it's way too weak to put such a high price tag.There is no replay value except for those who wants achievement or challenge.It feels that their interview on learning from past experience such as: code vein, tales of, god eater and dark souls amount to little. They gave birth to something that doesn't know what it wants to be. Not making use of strength of those titles.Currently a second title or DLC would make me wary to even bother. The trailers was promising, but that's all there is honestly.Here are my rants hidden as it is spoiler heavy.

_childDocuments_.review: Played this during the free weekend. Put about 9 hours into it and expect to be about halfway into the playthrough for the first character. Pretty much feels like a cookie-cutter JRPG.I think the highlight of the game is the voice acting, story and characters, though they all come across as a bit inconsistent and mashed together. Felt like you weren't given enough time to get to know characters before major events or before you 'bond' with them in game. But overall enjoyed these aspects of the game the most.I suspect the combat will be what determines if this game is worth playing for you. Mostly linear corridors with enemy encounters relatively frequently. Different enemy types that call for somewhat different tactics but imo not significant changes in how you fight. Basic attack combos wore me out pretty fast, even the 'brain field'/'brain drive' overpower modes. The most interesting aspect of combat was the 'SAS' mode where you adopt powers of your companions - the strength of which is also dependent on your bond level with them - for a limited period of time to target enemy weaknesses.Ultimately felt like the combat and game levels were filler-ish to drip-feed the story and I got impatient. Combat felt mostly mediocre, fought certain major enemies multiple times, revisited certain levels etc when it felt things could easily have been condensed a bit. Definitely curious about what happens next but not enough to put another 20 hours in. Probably will read or watch what happens elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: Not bad, but not great, worth it if you like anime JRPGs in general, but not at anything higher than 20-30 dollars. Not worth full price definitely. It has a lot of potential but terrible writing and a lot of weird design choices bring it down.Story was mostly pretty bad, with all anime cliches and tries way too hard to be something deep. Most of the dialogue was pretty awful and the characters were anime tropes, not badly written but nothing interesting. Story does improve a little bit by the end but overall, it's not the reason why you'll be playing this game. Yuito is also a pretty lame protagonist.Story isn't helped by the way it's told either. Telling the story via still pictures and portraits talking was a pretty weird decision that left me mostly uninterested in what is told in front of me. Please don't mention Persona, because in it you can at least see character models moving on the screen, while here it's all still pictures after still pictures. This honestly screams lack of budget or laziness more than art direction. This game has an unnecessary anime released at the same time, so why couldn't they make full 3D cutscenes ? really ?Combat is why you'll be playing this game, and why it's worth any money. With ton of movement, powers, attacks and allies, there're ton of fun to have here, and a lot of ways to change your style and try new things and different combinations all the time. There're 9 powers that you can use in total and they're fun and can be combined together for great combos.The only problem the combat suffers from is that the game is very easy even on hard. I played the entire game on hard and I only suffered in very, very fights, and nothing more. With the amount of powers, skills and abilities you keep getting as you progress, it's hard not to become overpowered in this game. Not to mention the healing items are abundant and very easy to get/buy. However, this doesn't hurt the fun you'll get from the hack and slash gameplay. I would have liked it if I can switch to other characters but it's not a big deal.Environmental design is mostly solid and good to look at, but it's very linear. Exploration is pretty limited and the game is mostly you moving from one combat scenario to the next. A little more open areas would have been nice. With that it's basically linear action game.English voice acting was pretty meh. Not terrible, but I felt most of them were phoning it. Some did well but for the majority I really felt they weren't interested in this at all and just in it for the money, either that or they're not that experienced. A lot of dialogue came out pretty lifeless as if who's saying it is a robot and not a human. Don't know anything about the Japanese voice acting. The graphics and character models are all superb which is a shame how it's wasted in still pictures rather than 3D cutscenes. The few cutscenes in the game were very good, but they're pretty rare as I said above.Overall, as I said, get it for 20-30 dollars max and you'll probably be able to forgive its faults and enjoy it for what it's. Anything more and you might disappointed. It's not a bad game, but just a huge wasted opportunity for me. Very good combat that gets interrupted by terrible story told by still pictures. Shame. Still don't regret playing it that much as I had some good fun with its combat.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a really decent game not good nor bad, with epic finishing moves and interesting battle mechanics, the battle mechanics sometimes feel clunky and overwhelming at the beginning but is just matter of getting used to it. The music and sound design are.. decent. Don't really have much to say about that since I've only really stopped to hear the soundtrack in-game about... 6 times. It's got some nice tunes for sure, and it gets the job done, same with the sound effects. The combat is pretty good, with interesting upgrades to it and the SAS system was really fun while I was playing, linking SAS upgrades to bond level with your companions was a good way to get interested in your party and see their backstories. I loved the artstyle of the enviroment and the character designs, the japanese voice cast did a good job. Overall an interesting game with a pretty fun combat system that really suffers from cliche anime story.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished Kasane's story in ~20 hours on normal.The combat is very flashy and fun, with plenty of room for strong combos as long as you utilize SAS abilities and psychokinesis properly. If you ever wanted to feel like an OP anime protagonist, this is the game.Combat is a bit weird to get a hang of first but once you realize you should be alternating physical attacks and psychokinesis attacks the game flows much much better. Utilizing special objects in the environment (such as slinging a train along a railway or blowing up a gas truck) is fun as hell too. I do wish a lot of the combo improvements, such as longer combos and more psychokinesis energy, weren't given so late in the skill tree though. Overall I'd say if you like anime-JRPGs like Tales Of games or God Eater you'll like this. The plot is B-grade, with some plot holes here and there (such as bond stories with characters you're currently enemies with at that point in the story) but the characters and their bond stories are very enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: I ended up enjoying this game a whole lot! I could easily write a small essay, but I'll just quickly sum up my opinion:+ The gameplay, including all of its mechanics are absolutely amazing, you can do some really nasty SAS activation combos+ While the enemy variety could use some work, each enemy requires a different tactic to beat, especially on hard difficulty+ Speaking of which, to me, the difficulty on Normal felt just right, it's easy to die if you don't pay attention(, though for the most part you can just spam your healing items), but it's a lot easier if you know what you're doing, so if you want real challenge, play on Hard+ The characters are pretty tropey at first, but they all have a nice character development throughout the game, it's overall a likeable cast+ The story is a bit messy at times, but it was actually pretty interesting and it came together nicely+ I liked the skill tree this time around, it doesn't focuses on raw stats, but provides you with even more tools in (or sometimes even outside of) combat, which is very fun+ Visually pleasing+ Great Japanese voice acting, decent English voice acting- Boring and later very annoying side-quests that barely reward you- A lot of boring looking locations- Not enough enemy variety- Locking into, and actually hitting a target with normal attacks can be a problem sometimes- Some questionable character moments (Kasane is a huge hypocrite for example, but I won't spoil the rest). These aren't too much of an issue, because... anime- The story can be too anime for some (for those people, I have a good suggestion: just don't think about it)- The music overall is a bit flat, but it still fits the tone of the game, though there definitely are some tracks I really liked- I wish every cutscene were animated, because the ones that are actually animated look awesomeI really hope this game is going to get a sequal, because I had an absolute blast playing. It practically begs for one because of how it ended. If you like action games, I think it's worth even at full price, but if you can get it on a sale, this is a must buy for fans of the genre. Also, do yourself a favor and play both Yuito's and Kasane's story, it's worth the extra content!

_childDocuments_.review: It takes only 30 minutes (into the game) to experience the meat of the combat and so my review will be based on this, since combat drives this game. It's not great. The lock-on "function" is typical of more generic AA Japanese Action RPGs, wherein the character does not forward face who they're locked-on to which is extremely frustrating for ranged classes like Kasane Randall who needs to always be facing her target in battle. What's worse is the active dodge system; it shares the same button as sprint which would not be an issue if we could hold the dodge button to enable sprint, but this is not so. If the developers could take this as critical feedback and make the necessary changes, that would be appreciated.In short:- Fix the lock-on system to have the PCs (playable characters) track their enemy (forward facing, unable to change movement directions as long as lock-on is enabled) so as to make dodging and psychokinetic combat fluid and actually playable- Change the functionality of the dodge and sprint buttons/keybinds (simple: hold dodge to sprint, tap dodge to dodge)Everything else is cookie cutter JRPG goodness of a AAA game. Lovable characters, a good passives tree, incredible skills system, beautiful aesthetics (granted, not a fan of the film grain but this is the style), a much appreciated visual novel styled dialogue system, and the music is God tier. Like, almost on the level of Shoji Meguro. Hayata Takeda deserves a lot of credit for their incredible compositions!  Scarlet Nexus could be a sleeper hit if the devs can fix the two most critical issues. Besides them, I absolutely recommend this gem of a JRPG! Please, Bandai, take this AA game to a AAA game with these two simple fixes <3

_childDocuments_.review: This review is based on only nearly completing (at this point I'm forcing myself) one of the two protagonist's stories after 22 hours - I have not played the other story yet, though I don't know that it will affect my recommendation. There might be light spoilers in here, but I left out any specifics. I want to start off by saying that this game has some of the most enjoyable, flashy, stylish, an exciting action combat that I've played in a long time. The powers you can borrow from your companions are diverse and flashy in their own ways, even though some of them achieve the same things as others. The Brain Map (skill tree) has some fun upgrades that help you feel like you're consistently getting stronger.Even the sound production is high quality, from the music, to the sound effects, to the voice acting (I played with Japanese voices). Unfortunately, the amazing combat is brought down by the overall storytelling and character development. Cut-scenes that start out as fully animated are abruptly switched to static character profiles and stills, often times as soon as actual action starts which really tears you out of the moment and just leaves you wanting more and wondering why they bothered animating at all. These animated moments are few and far between.Huge plot points that should be major revelations to the characters are just glazed over like it's some casual conversation and isn't a big deal. Characters turn on each other but still ask to hang out the next day like nothing happened. They imply a lot of world-wide repercussions to events in the story, but none of that is ever seen because there are like 5 NPC's in the main city hub and you never see them again after the first few chapters - the world feels like it only exists for the MC's and their friends. Granted I have only played one of the two protagonist's stories, I can't imagine much will change playing the other. After every chapter they end up meeting and exchanging notes about what happened to each other, so there is almost no mystery in what I would get out of the other story. The character bonding episodes feel like pulling teeth towards the end of the game because you have to power through all of them one at a time, and only between main story chapters, which really turns them into unnatural drags of time; a majority of which aren't particularly interesting or endearing. Not to mention the obnoxiously long time it takes to give a gift to a companion, especially after crafting all the newly available ones. Side quests are few and far between, usually only one or two are available between each chapter, and are rather tedious and don't provide any extra side story or valuable rewards (you can "exchange" monster parts for almost everything they provide, so there is not much of a point in doing them unless you want to collect all of the cosmetic items). TL;DR - amazing combat, terrible story delivery and character development. If you can get through slogs of text and shallow story development to get to the exciting and flashy combat, or really REALLY enjoy anime style story telling, you may enjoy this game. Unfortunately for me, it just leaves me wanting to finish the game so I can uninstall it.

_childDocuments_.review: Grinded to get 20 levels over the enemies. Still got beaten the hell out of it. 8/10Word of advice? Levels are aesthetic on this game. Learn to use the right SAS to exploit Other's weaknesses. And learn to both be patient and perfect dodge on bosses.Scarlet Nexus is a good action RPG. The SAS and Brain mechanisms are nice and keep the combat fresh. You also can't just "HULK SMASH" through the enemies - unless you want an early game over.The equipment is very simplified so you focus on the story and combat. Weapon and plugin upgrades are clearly sequential and easy to follow - I spent little time on equipment management thanks to that.Story-wise all party members have their problems and personality, and they do evolve and improve as you get to know them. The main story is nice, however personally the last 4 phases lost its logic to me.They also overly abused the power of friendship, to the point that assassins and spies are trusted 30s after they say that they won't do it again. They also abuse classic clichés such as "no time to explain this" or "one day you'll understand". It doesn't ruin the story, however it clearly push the boundaries of common sense.The story is very linear, and broken down into 12 phases. I personally don't see a problem on that, as I like both linear and open world games. If you prefer to roam freely, then this game is not for you.Overall Scarlet Nexus has a good action gameplay and mechanics with a convoluted story and crippled RPG features. It is interesting if you are willing to invest half of your gameplay time into "bond episodes" to get to know your teammates and learn more about them, and eventually jump into a fast-paced, dynamic combat with Others using your friends' powers through the SAS.

_childDocuments_.review: Scarlet nexus was a blast to play.It goes through a lot of cliche anime tropes, but the story is well made and there's a twist at every corner. Despite how much the game info dumps toward you, it's never too hard to follow... until the end, when it can get kinda confusing.Combat is very fun in scarlet nexus, mixing and matching abilities as well as finding out effective combos makes for a surprisingly in depth combat system. I thought at first that the combat would get boring, that it was going to be shallow, but each time it was about to get stale, a new mechanic was added to keep things fresh.Each side character has support conversations, much like Fire Emblem, only problem is that you can spend up to 2 hours between each phase just doing supports. It gets very tedious toward the end of the game, as the support density doubles. I found myself skipping a lot of conversations.This game supports plenty of visuals too that can show off your edgy side, dorky side, and even furry side. I was very satisfied with the amount of character customization you could do, though you can only equip 3 visuals at a time, and i've found myself wanting 5 or more for some outfits. Doesn't affect gameplay though, so it's not a huge issue.All in all, try the demo first, it makes a pretty good impression of what the rest of the game will be like. If you like the demo, you'll like the main game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible and deserves way more attention.Combat 10/10 - Best Action RPG combat, maybe even Action combat period, in any game I've ever played. The game gives you so many cool tools to use, and the enemy arrangements create a combat puzzle that you really have to pull out every tool in your toolbox to conquer. Not to mention everything feels super satisfying and extremely flashy to pull off.Music 7/10 - A lot of the music was very catchy and good, but I was never blown away. I did bob my head quite a bit in a couple zones thoughStory 8/10 - Presentation is a hybrid between a Manga and and Anime. Sometimes it will zoom into the "Manga panel" and start an anime-style cutscene. Story is quite interesting. It gets a little convoluted at the end of the middle of the game with what seems like an M-night twist every hour, but it eventually irons itsself out to a very satisfying conclusion. Most of the character bonding sequences are also pretty interesting and function a lot like Confidants in Persona 5. This is also where the side characters get some much needed character development. I liked the direction they took with almost every character. Minus points was strictly because of the tangled web it wove in the middle of the game.The dual pro-tag approach also works very well. The two characters are experiencing two completely different stories for most of the game and getting to see both sides is really compelling. PLAY AS YUITO BEFORE KASANE PLEASE.Visuals - 8/10The graphics are incredible. Best anime presentation by far. Some of the environments can be a little drab though. There's a couple areas in particular that you spend a lot of time in that are 2 or 3 colors and get old, pretty fast. The characters, animations, and actual anime style is executed better than any game I've seen, though.Overall - 8.5/10. The soundtrack could have been more consistent, the story eventually ironed itsself out but got convoluted at one point, and the level design/environments can get drab in some areas. However; the visuals, combat, and presentation are absolute 10/10s. Please give this game a shot if you're on the fence. You won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Scarlet Nexus is a "brainpunk" action RPG that delivers some fantastic combat alongside a serviceable story and decent albeit somewhat tropey characters. I particularly enjoyed using psychokinesis abilities to hurl all kinds of miscellaneous objects at my foes, which I feel is the selling point of this game. The story, while interesting on its own, is unfortunately told through mostly still images like a more fancy pseudo-visual novel. I would have liked to have seen more dynamic events and animations in the story segments but I guess I can technically get that experience by watching the anime adaptation. All in all, this is an easy to recommend game for anyone looking for a good anime action RPG to play. Oh, and don't forget to check the anime for the codes that can be redeemed in game. There should be one code each week the anime airs.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall:Tepid Recommendation - The plot is insane and dumb, and mostly serves as a sequence of excuses to run down hallways to kill groups of enemies. Is the moment-to-moment gameplay good enough to justify that? For me, it is.Great:Visual design - The clothing designs are pretty appealing evolutions of modern tech-wear, and the use of in-universe augmented reality interface to contextualize the HUD is pretty cool.Good:Combat - The combat is simple and straight-forward hack-and-slash action, with the addition of a crush meter, which something akin to sekiro's posture meter. Most enemies have some kind of weakness that builds the crush meter much faster than you can drain their hp, and it is pretty satisfying to get that execute.Animations - A major part of why combat feels nice. Everything is well animated and flashy. The Hideout/Bond Episodes - A pretty fun change of pace from the regular gameplay. Without them, most of the characters are pretty lacking. That sounds like a bad thing, but making them optional for those who are uninterested is fine with me.Neutral:Combat - The 'dodge' mechanic does not have i-frames, and until you unlock 'Perfect Dodge Attack' you don't have any reason to try to perfect dodge. It's risky and does nothing for you. Once you do have it unlocked though, you have just enough incentive, but it should be treated more like a parry.Environment design - The themes of some of the levels are not super interesting and/or they overstay their welcome. Its not like the levels are super long, but within a level, everything looks too similar. Abandoned Construction site with no twist. Highway ruin with overgrown tree roots. Urban ruin with neon wires. Subway ruin. Abandoned hospital. A snowy mountain pass (boring if not for the ice statues) A bunch of metal blocks. Enemy design - A bit of a mixed bag. I like how crazy and unique many of the enemy designs are; the combination of mechanical industrial with organic, plant and animal mix is probably the most visually interesting part of this game. The third motif of enemy design is honestly bewildering. There's like weird fetish stuff in half of the designs. Corsets, bare legs and stilettos. Mannequins in thigh-high stockings or long latex gloves. Two torsos conjoined at the waist in some sort of bondage gimp-suit. WHY? Also the designs of the Others feel very out of place, and there's no in-universe justification for why they look the way they do. Bad:Writing - Don't bother paying attention, because its not worth it. The story is convoluted and unsatisfying, as you may expect from time-travel shenanigans, but also the dialogue is pretty anime-like, in the most derogatory sense that I can possibly mean. With teenage protagonists and even the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ "power of friendship" cliche. The voice acting is fine, but the lines are often stupid.Cutscenes - About half of the dialogue is delivered in static panels instead of animation. I would be okay with this if they did anything fun or artistic with it, but they don't.Combat - The game likes to have large enemy groups that impossible to all keep on screen at once, and they off-screen enemies are still free to attack you, and their projectile attacks make this very annoying.Level design - Hallways between arenas for enemy encounters. Pretty much the only way you interact with the environment is for you to just run through it to fight enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game. I really like the anime style paired with the cyberpunk setting, the Japanese voice acting and most of the characters are very likable with a nice dynamic between them. But then, after a few hours (I played the demo before buying the game at a discount): - Combat starts feeling repetitive. Even the huge skill tree isn't enough to prevent this since we're fighting the same enemies over and over again. It also doesn't help that the game levels are very similar to each other. It's always a "keep going forward but maybe also go to all the dead ends too so you can loot X item that is used to craft... stuff...?" thing. Which is a shame, because graphics are really pretty. - The plot is already all over the place, with  It's like the story raises many questions at once – too many questions – without giving me any real reason to care. - On that matter: underdeveloped characters. Pacing is odd since we're very quick to jump to action and I still don't know much about my partners or about the character that is supposed to be a childhood friend. I could think of a few more issues like the slideshow-esque cutscenes or the lack of a log system to read past dialogues during those relaxing visual novel moments, but these are the ones that prevent me from continuing the game. Again, a shame.

_childDocuments_.review: This game could be so much more, but it chose not to be.Story kinda shallow and underwhelming. Everything is predictable, characters are cute but their personalities are kinda cliche. The plot are hit and miss. Play Yuito's story first before Kasane. A lot of Yuito's plot twists are ruined if you play as Kasane first, and sadly it doesn't apply for the other way around.Gameplay is solid. Not amazing perfect 10/10, but it's solid. Combat felt like DMC meets Tales, SAS is decent but Yuito's squad and Kasane's squad's SAS doesn't feel different from each other, skill trees are straightforward and not confusing. But sadly, the combat doesn't offer much incentive for experimentation. You just spam one combo and you can plow through the entire game.Kasane and Yuito are marketed as feeling different from each other, but other than Kasane playing from range using her floating knives and Yuito favors close-and-personal combo attacks, they don't really play that different.The environments on both the dungeons and towns looks amazing and practical. You always know where to go, and never got lost. Towns are very useless tho. There's literally nothing to do in town except for story reasons and taking sidequests. Soundtrack is the only thing I would give a 10/10, comparable to Persona.If you're just looking for mindless fun and don't mind spending 80 hours (40 hours for each character), go ahead and grab this game on sale.7/10. Could be so much more.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is fun. Pretty good battle system. Sick looking enemies. Walking around town and dungeons gave me Shin Megami Tensei vibe a bit, which is cool. They should also have history text, so players can check dialogues that they missed/not understand during dialogue cutscenes. A la otome games, you know. I'm actually surprised the game doesn't have this when it's so dialogue heavy. As of now, player can only skip dialogue.I played with English voice. A few are great (Yuito, Arashi, Kagero). Most are okay. Hanabi's voice isn't great. It doesn't suit her personality. That cutscene where she jumped on Yuito's back in the hospital--that was the flattest shout I've ever heard. And I never knew a shout can be flat.All in all, a great game, with minor setbacks.

_childDocuments_.review: Score: 8.5/10Pros:+Graphics with great art style and amazing aesthetics+Good combat system. SAS, Combo Vision, Brain Crush and Brain Drive ensures that the combat isn't just another generic Devil May Cry styled game+Great music+Good lengthCons:-They definitely cheaped out on the cut scenes as a good majority of the cut scenes (minus the major events) are styled like a VN-There's a lot of talking in the cut scenes. Too much, even.-Not enough enemy variety-Too many invisible walls which hinders exploration-Kasane was not a likable playable character. She has the personality of a wooden plank and her weapon/combat was inferior to Yuito's.When I first saw this game's unveiling trailer, I was instantly drawn by its art style. I'm a big fan of games that utilize 2D-esque visuals such as games made by ArcSys, so naturally I was a big fan of Scarlet Nexus' graphics from the beginning. They're honestly some of the best, if not the best, anime styled visuals in any video game and I hope that future games utilize similar aesthetics.Scarlet Nexus is overall a fun, action JRPG with a good combat system and competently in-depth skill tree. If you have ever played Astral Chain on the Nintendo Switch, this game shares many similarities with the latter and those who enjoyed Astral Chain will certainly enjoy Scarlet Nexus. What hurt this game's combat is that there's not enough enemy variety. Enemies you see in the beginning are ones you'll see throughout the game's entirety. Sure, they'll have variations, but there simply isn't a good amount of variety. There's a lot to like about this game. From its great visuals and music to its fun and quirky features like character bonding and gifting. The story imo was nothing amazing, as it was the run-of-the-mill JRPG filled with your typical anime tropes and ends with heroes beating the villain with the power of friendship. That being said, I enjoyed most of the characters and the game makes you care about them.For me, the biggest flaw is that the game developers decided to cheap out on the cut scenes. As I mentioned above, they're reminiscent of something you would see in a visual novel and there's definitely a lot of talking and dialogue involved, which may bore players at first.Overall, I really enjoyed this game. I'm glad I bought it and experienced it and for those who are hesitating to buy it, I would certainly recommend it. It's a shame that there's no demo on PC, however.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally got through this one. This was my favorite game of 2021 and the combat still holds up today. If you are a fan of spectacle fighters like Astral Chain this is the game for you.My main pros for the games is:1. The Combat is fast, fun, and top notch, not overly difficult but still has a decent skill ceiling.2. The interactions with the cast of characters is pretty good you will be sure to find a few you like to have in your party.  That and brainpunk world they made was fun to explore and I'd want to see more. 3. Value, this game is always on sale and even down to $10 at some times so it's worth it.My main cons:1. Repetitive combat, I personally took a good year brake between playing both characters in this game and even then it was a little tedious. The different psychokinesis objects you can through add some much needed variety but I can see how some people would quit at around the 30 hour or so mark. 2. The whole game can seem like one giant hallway with enemies. Some variation in the environments is here but not enough for anything to stand out except the last level in the story. I say Astral Chain has more varied designs.  3. This is a personal one but there wasn't enough character customization. They give you a few outfits but most of them are just recolors and not a lot of variety except a couple DLC outfits.All in all this is a great game for anime fans and people who love the action rpg genre. I enjoyed going through and finishing the DLC's and playing Kasane's story on very hard which brought some much needed challenge to the experience. Overall great game I'll definitely play a sequel if one is ever announced.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute treat from start to finish. Fantastic pacing on both the story and gameplay elements. They do an exceptional job of implement tools to your arsenal one at a time, emphasizing their use in the short term, and then considering them as a useful/necessary part of your kit overall, and this loop continues for a majority of the play time. This leads to a great sense of power scaling and progression, to the point where the final segment of the game you feel like an unstoppable super hero-god king. The story was surprisingly well done for the type of game that it is, and manages to avoid many of the pitfalls and predictability of both animes and the type of games that spawn from those works. I recommend playing the game as the dude first, as his story feels much more cohesive, and Kasane's (the girl) serves more to fill in the gaps, and provide a similar feeling, but ultimately different, gameplay experience. You will probably be surprised how hard it is to put this game down once you stop. I certainly was.

_childDocuments_.review: Scarlet Nexus is a fantastic game with a few issues, but not enough to warrant not playing it. At the time of writing this review I have 50 hours on my save, and have finished only the male character's route, and a small part of the female character's route 44 hours of that was spent on the male character.First let's talk about the positives. The combat is very fun; it's fairly fast paced and the enemies hit hard, but you're given so many tools to play around with. Almost every enemy has a weakness which makes them extremely vulnerable and allows you to exploit the game's crush mechanic -- essentially a stagger gauge that once emptied gives you an instant kill attack on the enemy -- finding these weaknesses can be very enjoyable and satisfying once you figure them out.The Free Time sections are very enjoyable. If you like Persona's social link system, you'll almost definitely enjoy the character bonding sessions. After most phases (chapters) you'll be given a free time, where you can go around and pick up side-quests, and roam areas freely; but most importantly you can talk to your party members in your hideout. Talking to your party members allows you to give them gifts, and sometimes watch Bond Episodes; extra scenes where you get to see a little side story between your main character and the party member. The gifts in particular are the reason I like these free time sections so much. Whenever you give a new gift to your party member, the actual gift is added to their area of the hideout. Not only are you actually able to see the item you've given them in the hideout, but they actually use them! Each time the hideout is loaded, the characters will be performing randomized animations, and most gifts you give them come with an animation of them using the gift. It's a really great addition and it makes the gifts feel extremely satisfying to give.The music is enjoyable. I tend not to notice music in games unless it's either extremely good or extremely bad. This game is no exception. The majority of the music is just okay. I'm sure I could go into more detail if I paid attention to the music more, but the main thing is that there were no bad tracks that I can think of. There was a good track however. The opening theme for the game is fantastic. It's a track called Dreaming Drive by THE ORAL CIGARETTES, a Japanese Rock band that also did the opening song for the anime Noragami. It's a track that I've actually listened to outside of the game, which for me is fairly rare.Now onto the issues. There is . While I don't think that in itself is a necessarily bad thing (though I'm sure many people would consider it too much), almost every line is fully voiced. I like to let the voices play out when I play a game, but I simply could not recommend doing that in this game. The amount of dialogue is simply too great for letting the voices fully play out. I'm not joking when I say that it added literal hours onto my game time. The voice acting itself (in Japanese) is phenomenal, and I seriously commend their voice actors for putting in so much quality work; but there's just too much. The Bond Episodes in particular is where this comes to light most frequently. I generally love side stories with characters in games, but the bond episodes often felt like they just went on for too long, and it's purely because I allowed the voice lines to finish. What should be a 2-3 minute scene turns into a 5-10 minute scene, which over the course of the game adds up. Post Credits The cut-scenes are generally not great in my opinion. The majority of them are what I'd call pseudo-cut-scenes. Essentially just a set of still images with dialogue. This is fine for the majority of them, since they're generally just characters talking to each other, you don't really need a full cut-scene for that. But sometimes there's more action, and that's where they fail. Every now and then you'll get a proper cut-scene, full motion like you're used to in almost every other game. These cut-scenes are fantastic. However, the majority of the time the pseudo-cut-scene style will still be used. It ends up looking like a 4-frame stop motion video The sounds play out as normal, but you'll see a series of still images depicting what's happening. Personally, I think this is a poor decision. Considering how much dialogue is in this game, it feels like animation took a back-seat to it.The side-quests are mundane. There's nothing to them. They all consist of kill x enemy with y attack -- some of which are extremely frustrating to complete. There isn't even any real reason to do them. The rewards they give are often easy to get, and actually easier to get than going through the side-quest. When you pick up the quest there's 3-4 lines of exposition for an in-game reason that the quest should be done, and that's it. You don't even get any resolution to the quest, since the only way to turn the quest in is to go through the menu. Returning to the NPC that gave you the quest just results in them asking you to hurry up and finish the quest.To get the full experience, you  to play both the male and female characters routes. Playing through only one will leave you with a few unanswered questions, and a feeling like you missed out, since some of the chapters are drastically different, and you learn entirely different things. This combined with the sheer amount of dialogue is fairly daunting.The story has a fairly slow start. It takes a few chapters for the story to get actually interesting. I don't really have much to say on this matter, but the first few chapters nothing of note happens. It's only at the end of chapter 4 that it gets really interesting.Overall I'd say Scarlet Nexus is worth a play, but I definitely would not recommend letting dialogue play out unless you  like the voices, nor doing the side-quests.I'd give this game a solid 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: While this game shows potential, and shine in some aspect, its downside more than compensate for those, which prevents me from recommending it.- The story is divided in a complementary ways between the two playable characters, Yuito & Kasane. But outside, it is a generic anime trope with bad pacing, and starting a lot of story elements that it never resolves.On top of that, the story is mostly presented through weird still image dialogues, which only managed to give me a slight nausea during my longest session, my first time for any game, mostly due to their transitions from one to another. The fully animated cutscenes are much better, but much less present.- The gameplay should have been the redeeming feature, but it isn't the case. It is action RPG where every action from the player has high commitment, and cannot be cancelled. If the game was balanced around that, it would be fine, but that is unfortunately not the case. Many enemies, especially smaller ones, can play out their entire attack animations while the player's is still in progress. Moreover, should both sides attack one another, the player will lose, as they would get sent flying, but enemies wouldn't, in most cases.The game offers a nice gimmick, where the player gets access to the abilities of their teammates, offering various buffs or other moves. But while they could let the player play with those in a way they enjoy, they chose to create numerous enemies that require you to use a specific buff to beat, in a rock<paper<scissor fashion.When everything goes well, the combat does look really nice, but it only felt "okay" at best, due to my being punished heavily for any misstep, instead of being rewarded for doing well.I went for all the achievements, and I had moments I enjoyed here and there, like most of the interactions with the teammates, or the overall visuals. I wanted to find more elements to like, but unfortunately didn't find enough to balance the negative aspects of the game.Overall, this game felt more like the developers wanted you to experience it exactly in THE way they designed it, rather than letting you play through it with the tools given.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best ARPGs to come out in 2021. The combat is inspired by NieR: Automata, but I personally find it to be an improvement. The moveset may not seem too extensive at first, but as you play the game and unlock more options, you'll discover that there are many, many interesting ways to put it all together. This game may be an RPG, but it definitely wears its character-action DNA with pride. Now, on to the story: if your main focus in a game is its story, then you might want to look for something else. The story is good and the characters are all entertaining, but it's nothing extraordinary. That said, the main draw of the game is its combat system, which I could not recommend more highly.

And honestly, it's a JRPG, if you didn't expect convoluted as hell that's on you- Music is pretty goodBad:- No ultrawide support without mods, even though 3440 x 1440 is listed as a resolution in settings- Crazy difficulty spikes; the regular gameplay and boss fights are essentially 2 different games- It is a bit repetitive. The entire game is basically go from point a to b, fighting everything in your way, watch a cutscene, fight a boss, end of chapter. That said, it's an action JRPG, so the combat and the cutscenes are really what you're here for anyway. _childDocuments_.review: This game takes way, way too long to get going, while simultaneously expecting immediate perfection from the player.The best gear is locked behind finishing the game in 15 hours.Core parts of combat are blocked by story progression, to the point where the initial flow of combat feels like waving a marionette around, while later combat flows with much fewer issues. But it retains issues, such as offering an extensive combo system that can't be used until you progress far enough in the story to unlock super armour.Speaking of which:The story appears to be completely nonsensical at first glance, but pulls multiple "Nomura"-esque "plot twists" that don't really deserve the name. Things only make sense in hindsight, which isn't all that fun if you have to play 20 hours to finally understand the first 2-3. The narrative only comes together after completing both story campaigns, which is not a hallmark of a good story.Overall, this game is not a fun experience until you have invested multiple dozen hours.

_childDocuments_.review: The aesthetic, combat, level design, story, characters etc, are all wonderfully woven together. I put this up there with Nier Automata in how it's all executed.SAS abilities and combo vision attacks add a lot of style and variety to combat. They are also key in efficiently disposing of enemies.One SAS power may not work against a certain enemy or prove to be inefficient, so using a different one will get the job done. You can also use them in conjunction with each other. For instance using Arashi's Hyper Velocity, Kyoka's Duplication and Shiden's Electrokinesis can melt an enemy's health bar.The story took many unexpected turns, so calling it weird, weird in a good way, is the best word to describe it. There are some areas where it faltered, such as The characters can be tropey, but it wasn't a real bother for me. It's still a lively cast I don't see myself forgetting.Scarlet Nexus is straight forward in it's design: there are phases (mainly consisting of combat) followed by phase breaks which allows you to grow bonds with allies in a Persona-esk way, minus the dialogue options. The higher the bond level, more an advantage you'll have in combat with them.Scarlet Nexus isn't without it's faults however, so I would love to see the ideas more refined and built upon in any possible future entries.My main complaints are the following:-Enemies constantly spamming projectiles can deincentivize aerial combat altogether.-The lack of dialogue options in bond episodes.-There's no option to disable tutorials.-Every attack is a commitment that cannot be canceled out of, nor are provided with sufficient i-frames. To elaborate on the last one, it's very frustrating constantly getting knocked down. I played the game from start to finish on hard mode, so at times it was infuriating,Compared to Tales, Scarlet Nexus is more linear, and while that may be off putting to some, for me it's one of the game's strengths because it's thought out and fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of people seem to enjoy the combat, but from someone who like stylish and skill-base combat systems like DS series or Code Vein, this feels incredibly janky and awkward.  I really don't understand why camera lock on gives so much freedom it seems like there isn't a lock at all, until you try to look at something else and it jerks your camera back.  There aren't really any combos except for the one they teach you in tutorial.  There's also no animation cancelling, so the character feels very unresponsive at times.On the plus side, I suppose animation looks pretty good.  Story seems pretty okay from what little I've seen so far.Overall, I think it should be a decent game, but the weird combat system really turns it off for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Classic Bandai Namco game. Extremely fun and promising start that falls flat in the second half.Mixed feeling about the game. Dropped in the end because I lost interest.The story starts up asking some interesting questions and mysteries but then quickly just starts dropping the "plot twists".  Its one of those cases where I would rather not have had any twists, as they mostly twisted the game in the wrong ways. Also the emotional beats suck a lot. There is one point in the game where Gameplay is the main reason I stuck with this game as long as I did because damn its fun. Plays actually pretty similiar to Tales of Arise. The SAS abilities are extremely fun to use and I really liked the enemies requiring different SAS activations to beat. However, as you get closer to the end of the game you need to use this less and less. It would have been much healthier for the game in my opinion if they kept the SAS abilities more limited than giving you all of them by the end and 4 to be activated at the same time. Also seeing that anime cut that stops the whole game really discouraged me from switching between them often.I have very mixed opinions about the Brain Drive feature. Its cool and I like that it kills you if you don't exit it on time, but damn its the most frustrating gameplay feature by far. If you do not upgrade it, you are actually kind of weaker than normal while inside of it, and if you do upgrade it fully the whole game becomes even more boring as you can't combo and its just button mashing.Music is outstanding. Really liked the tracks in the game. Gave me heavy Kekkai Sensen vibes with the instrumental tracks. Characters are good. Some are kind of basic, but some have had a surprising amount of depth to them and have had very fun interactions. Some of their actions in bonding events also didn't match their reactions in the actual story which was very off putting.Sidequests are ass. They sometimes feel worse and more pointless than an MMO quest. Its kill 3 of this or kill 5 of that. They have no substance. Skip them if you can, unless you are going for all achievements.All in all I would usually recommend you play the demo first as the data can be ported over to the main game. The problem with this game is that its problems only start to show in the second half, and they become glaring by then.

_childDocuments_.review: Stepping into the era of modern hack and slash genres, Scarlet Nexus welcomes you to its brain-punk world of technology and supernatural powers. It’s a new entry for fans of iconic hack-and-slash franchises like Devil May Cry and Bayonetta. On a side note, I’ve reached phase 2 of the game in less than ten hours of playtime (6.2 hrs to be exact), and I believe it's a good start to share my initial thoughts on Scarlet Nexus. So, prepare yourselves as we move things and ratings around in this spoiler-free review!Immersive Sounds and GraphicsAs we immerse ourselves in the world of Scarlet Nexus, the game unfolds a captivating audio and visual experience for our inner weeb. The game welcomes you with striking and immersive background music that sets the tone right from the start (I’ll leave that to you!). The choice of sound effects for every button press and menu selection enhances the overall user interface experience. Whether opting for the Japanese or English voices, the emotions conveyed are spot on! The game also has a dynamic soundtrack; seamlessly transitioning from chill background music as you start to explore and navigate to intense background music as the tension also heightens during combat scenarios. The sound effects, including those for attacks, finishers, powers, and enemies, contribute to the immersive experience of the gameplay. Notably, the satisfaction derived from the sounds of throwing and smashing objects at enemies also takes the game to the next level. The game's environment feels similar to watching a 90s anime, thanks to its art style that immerses players in the game. However, there is room for improvement in the texture used; a slight enhancement could elevate the overall visual impact. Mysterious and Compelling StoryAside from the captivating audio and visual experience, the story of the game also has an engaging narrative. Imagine this: you are in a brain-punk world with advanced technology granting people psychic powers, however, humanity faces a threat from deranged mutants known as Others. As humanity’s last line of defense, it's up to you and your team to take extreme measures.Moreover, I like how there are separate storylines, which you must complete to uncover all the mysteries in this brain-punk world. As I’m currently in my first playthrough with Kasane (the one on the right), I’m still unsure how different the storylines are or how much they  would impact them. Nevertheless, I hope it’s something worth the wait.Memorable CharactersBut what’s a mysterious and compelling story without memorable characters? In Scarlet Nexus, you get to choose your protagonist between Yuito Sumeragi or Kasane Randall. Let’s start with Yuito Sumeragi! He is a typical anime bright, pure-hearted, and positive-minded male (or young recruit in the game). His power is psychokinesis, which allows him to move objects using his mind. Also, he wields a katana for he specializes in close-range combat. So, for those players who love to go crazy with their katana and go straight into the frontlines, Yuito Sumeragi might be the one for you! The next one is Kasane Randall (my favorite actually)! She is a typical anime kuudere who only shows her soft side to the one she trusts. She is also a new recruit who has  a strong bond with her sister, Naomi Randall. Like Yuito Sumeragi, she also possesses the power of psychokinesis,  More than that, she wields flying throwing knives, which splits into six! Pretty good for mid-range combat. So, for those players who love dancing and slicing with their throwing knives, Kasane Randall might be your perfect match! The other characters in the game are just as fun and interesting as the ones I’ve previously mentioned. Most especially if you're a fan of characters typically  portrayed in anime, I assure you that this game will truly unleash your inner weeb. Since Scarlet Nexus offers a wide diversity of characters and personalities , I'll let you discover the remaining ones!Personal Opinion and Rating In addition to my previous review of the game, here are some pros, cons, and good features based on my observations and opinions.Pros:JRPG Party System:The game features a JRPG party system, where having a party is a must, especially in combat. You can also change their combat tactics/behavior based on your strategy in the party settings.Various Characters/Party Members:The game offers a variety of characters who can join as one of your party members, each having a unique power. You can share and combine powers with your party members, boosting your attack power and gaining various status effects. Thus, you can create different party/power combinations depending on your strategy, or you could simply stick with your waifus or husbandos.Character Enhancement:Characters in the game can level up through "bond episodes" where you spend time with your chosen party member. This enhances their power and status effects, resulting in a stronger attack power. You can also upgrade their status using plug-ins (buffs) acquired from shops, missions, or defeating enemies.Enemy Designs:The enemy designs in this game are so weirdly good! They are impressive because everyday things turn into weird, creepy, and satisfying monstrosities. For instance, a flower pot head with ostrich-human legs in stilettos is considered somewhat normal in this game, which again is really good!Everyday Things as Weapons:Do you want to throw and use everyday things as weapons? Well, I present to you the Scarlet Nexus! They have every single thing you can imagine. You name it! Whether it's cars, posts, boxes, pipes, tables, or chairs, everywhere and everyday things are weapons in Scarlet Nexus!Cons:Camera in Combat is Difficult:Maintaining a stable and following camera during combat is sometimes challenging. For instance, when focusing on attacking one of the enemies, you can be attacked from all sides without even noticing. The camera may deviate from your desired angle, making it tricky to focus on your targets.Difficulty Achieving Perfect Dodge:Every time I attempt to perform a perfect dodge, I still end up getting hit. It's frustrating because a perfect dodge can be achieved when a projectile, an object thrown at you, or an enemy attack is extremely close in a matter of seconds. Sometimes, there is also a slight delay. Even so, how I wish it was just my reflex issue.Limited Power Choice:Throughout the story, you only have psychokinesis as your power. Since all characters have distinct powers, I wish players could also try other powers. Although it's good that you can somehow grasp other powers and enhance your abilities by sharing with your party members, having the option to choose your power would be a valuable feature.Good Features:Loading Screen:One outstanding detail during loading screens is that when you are solo, it's just you displayed. However, when you are in a party, both you and your party members are shown on the loading screen.Transition of Cutscenes:Another impressive detail is the transition of cutscenes, which is combined with three types: storyboard panel, cinematic, and combat mode. All of these elements are incorporated very well, significantly impacting the overall game experience. I find this feature superb, especially since it was my first time seeing it.Cosmetics/Character VisualsYou can equip your character AND YOUR PARTY MEMBERS WITH A VARIETY OF COSMETICS. AND! THESE COSMETICS CAN BE SEEN DURING CUTSCENES, WHICH IS SOOO SATISFYING.With its pros, cons, and impressive features, Scarlet Nexus, despite minor issues, stands out as a remarkable brain-punk game. It successfully demonstrated its potential in the modern hack-and-slash era. Unlike other games in the same genre mainly focusing on melee-based weapons, Scarlet Nexus innovatively incorporates powers into traditional hack-and-slash gameplay. With everything that has been said, I give it a final of 8.8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a big game taking about 40hours to clear if you explore each map and not care to much about side missions. But then you can run the game again as the other main character to get their point of view for another 40 hours. So it can become a really big game if you want. It does feel abit slow early on in the game before you get all the moves and party members to play around with, Which is what makes starting the second round abit difficult to get into. Sure you will have 25h - 30h of new insight of the lore. But then you also have about 10 - 15hours of the same stuff you already seen. Same issue I had with Nier Automata, but in Nier it was worse as you do pretty much the exact same thing twice before you get the 3rd round with new lore. So it isn't bad atleast it start off with new lore right away. Would also have to say the game is very anime, not just graphic but the lore screams anime and the way they is like the anime cheesy style aswell. Which in all honesty I quite enjoy. Not sure what it is about it, it's just funny cuz it's stupid. If you do enjoy that random anime styled conversations I would highly recommend it as there is alot of it in here.The combat in the game is also quite enjoyable, as I mentioned before the early game is quite slow you do the same moves over and over again. But atleast they give you new party members every now and then so you can do new combo attacks with them. So there is something new to play around with while building up your tech tree. The enemies in the game can give you quite a fight aswell, giving you abit of a souls like fight but a easier version of it ofcourse. I never really had a struggle to get through the fights in thegame. The fights could be difficult and did die a few times but it was never like hitting a brickwall with a pillow and slowly tearing it down.I do however wish there was more to do with the party members, you do get special cutscenes as you give them gifts but felt like it was lacking something. Like would be nice if you could actually improve their skills aswell, similar to the tech tree your character got. I know they're working on more content with the party members and excited to see what they will bring. Saving my second play through for them to release the added content. I have mentioned the tech tree a few times by now but never actually touched on the subject, so guess it's time I say something about it. As you progress through the story and fighting monsters you get points you can use to unlock new moves, like extra movies in your combos. increasing your def and atk. Or unlocking how many party members you can combo moves with at the same time. It's not a massive tech tree but it's big enough to keep you working on it through out the game. You don't really have to be all to careful what you choose to unlock, it's not difficult to get enough points to get most things on there by just running the main story. If you put in some side quests in there you would be able to max it out with ease. In the end I would highly recommend this game if you enjoy some anime styled rpg game, with some good souls likeish combat. With a story that hooks you in and making you want to know more. Can't wait for a second game to see more of what they didn't get into in this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Scarlet Nexus is an action rpg with a lot of Nier Automata vibes (just to be clear from the start, don't expect a Yoko Taro-kind of story here, though). You can play as one of two predetermined protagonists, a melee focused swordsman or a ranged focused flying-blade wielder. You are part of a psionic combat unit that defends humanity against the monstrous "Others", deformed creatures that invade the world very often and literally eat people as a snack. The struggle is quite desperate but the army of which you are part is full of psionic combatants like yourself. The beginning of the game is spent in relatively ordinary military activities, but the stakes go up very fast, with a lot of shocking events taking place very soon. The game certainly doesn't waste time getting to the good parts of the story, Please do note that the two protagonists have a different story to tell so to enjoy all of it you need to play both of them.Gameplay-wise, Scarlet Nexus is very fun. You are a PSI warrior that dashes around the battlefield, hitting enemies, dodging, charging your PSI attacks and unleashing them. You have a series of AI squad mates that join you in many occasions and that, depending on how close you are to them, allow you to use more PSI abilities. PSI abilities interact with both enemies and the environment, making for some very fun, exciting combat. Controls are very smooth and responsive, giving you a great feeling of speed and power.This game is still an RPG so you have the usual inventory management / skills / experience points & levels business you get in many other games. Nothing particularly surprising here, but you will notice you level up VERY frequently. This is not bad and I think it's connected to the fact they would like you to play the entire game twice. If you had to majorly grind to level up twice I think the game would feel like a chore.Finally, there is a whole bonding system with your squadmates. When you are at your base, you can spend time with your favorite teammates and deepen your relationship with them. When your relationship levels up, their borrowed PSI powers become stronger and they will help you more in battle. The Bond Episodes give also additional pieces of the story so it's good to not skip them. It's cute, it works.Speaking of story, it's narrated through some cutscenes but mostly through some very smooth visual novel like system, but with an amazing level of quality. Since the visual novel is partially animated, it looks like you are reading a very advanced 3D comic book. It's a bit weird to describe, but it just feels really good. As a negative sidenote on the story, if you have played a lot of JRPGs it's possible you will find it a bit derivative: some of the characters have very clichéd motivations and some of plot twists are a bit obvious. It has not personally bothered me very much because the game is really well put together, but if you are demanding in this sense you might not appreciate it.Bottom line: PSI warriors fight weird monsters. Big mistery behind the world. Humanity under siege. You fight in a really cool way. For me this is a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game gave me a very mixed experience.  Some parts seem very well designed and thought out while others seem like just filler. The battle system can be fun, but there are certain times where the game throws tons of enemies at you on screen and it's hard to keep track of anything, it just turns into a mess.  Fighting one big giant monster was usually fun though.  The default dodge is garbage though and really hurts a game with this kind of combat. Story and characters were ok, although the plot seemed rushed at some points.  Overall: There's parts about this game that are great, but I can't really recommend it due to how repetitive and tedious some areas became to fight through.  I had to just lower the difficulty all the way to very easy from normal towards the end of the game to see the ending, not because it was too hard, but because there were just too many waves of the same enemies the game kept throwing at you and it became very tedious and boring.  I played all the way through the male character's story and have zero interest going back and playing through the female's story just due to the tedious slog of samey enemy waves.  I think they probably could've cut about 1/3 or so out of many of the dungeons and the game would be better for it.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve tried twice to give this game a fair shake and all I can say is what I’ve played of it is so generic, so bland it just feels like I’m wasting my time playing it.I could overlook the boring story, cliched writing about the power of trust and friendship and the, frankly, terrible graphics (you’re lucky if you look at a character and they actually have a shadow half the time) if the gameplay was at least fun but it just isn’t.It seems the developers wanted to make an action RPG but got half way to a good combat system and suddenly changed their minds. It seems they actually made semi-decent combat mechanics and then intentionally gimped them for the sake of making you work through a skill tree to completely unlock it. Want to be able to heal mid fight without waiting for an animation to play? Spend some skill points. Want to be able to recover from being hit? Skill points. Want a four hit attack combo? Believe it or not, skill points.The combat feels clunky, and the main culprit is there is no dodge cancelling: once you commit to an attack you’re in it until the animation finishes playing and combos almost seem to queue like a JRPG. Hit the attack button 3 times and you’re firing off that combo, even if you’ve stopped pressing the attack button long before the 3rd attack starts. It frustrates the flow of combat to no end, encountering situations where even though you’re pressing other buttons the game just seems to ignore the fact you’ve asked for it. So many times I’ve tried to pull an Arial launcher by hitting X+A only for my character to just stand there and take a shot to the face. Things only get worse when you take in to account that there’s a perfect dodge mechanic where the window for dodging just doesn’t seem consistent: some attacks will only trigger a perfect dodge window if you dodge a nanosecond before an attack hits you, where some will trigger so early that it’s actually possible to miss an enemy with a follow up attack and they just plough right in to you. The baseline dodge also inconsistently has no iframes, so if you dodge but the enemy is still within attack distance there’s a chance you’ll still be knocked down. I say it’s inconsistent because it really makes little sense: giant horse enemies have an AOE attack that delivers consistent damage if you stay in the zone but you can chain dodge out of it if you get caught, only taking damage between each dodge, but Brawny’s (weird mechanical gator enemies) can hit you mid-dodge during an emergence animation. Then there’s the psychokinesis attacks which are your special, and require you to use a chunk of a gauge to perform. The game explains to you pretty early on that following up attacks with psychokinesis, then following them up with another attack is a good way of chaining damage against an enemy and breaking down any armour they may have, but your attacks rarely interrupt enemy movement or attack animations and these follow up attacks will usually fling you straight in to an enemy attack that will knock you on your ass.In addition to this, you’ll usually find yourself with 1 or 2 party members in combat but their AI is absolutely brain dead, doing the bare-minimum of attacks and taking absolutely no steps to defend themselves from attacks. They seem like they’re just there to act as a minor distraction when you’re facing a gang of enemies, but even then 9/10 times the enemies will aggro to you with laser like focus. Fighting enemies with AOE attacks will annihilate your team mates because they just run at the enemy and in to the attacks like they’re suicidal, which leads to situations where you’re spending most of your time picking them up off the floor so you can use their SAS abilities. You can change their default behaviour in the party menu but I’ve found it does little to their survival instincts.This probably wouldn’t be so bad if you could control them directly: they level up just like you do and can be kitted out with weapons and augments just like you and probably would have made the combat system far more engaging than it actually is, but again this seems like something that has had the bones of established but the developers just gave up on.Consider all of the above with the rest of the problems the game has which just seems to point to a poor plan of how to make an enjoyable game and focusing resources in the wrong areas and I just couldn’t play it anymore after 6 hours. I found myself sticking the EXP booster on with the intention of just getting through the game quicker before I took a step back, realised I’d done it because I wasn’t enjoying myself and finally decided in turning the game off and walking away.It’s obviously had some care put in to it, but to me it looks like they’ve put that care in to the wrong parts of the game: there’s been great effort put in to the design of the games neon-futuristic aesthetics, but the graphics, especially for environments, are bad, the hub city is a few streets with absolutely nothing to do in it other than get meaningless text box exposition from random NPC’s (“OMG this Arashi poster looks so cool!” ~ Arashi Fan), the mission maps are long, empty and ugly looking corridors with basic healing items as your reward for exploration, the enemies are weird (stupid weird, not unsettling weird) and are limited to 6 or 7 base models, the cutscenes are 99% in-engine storyboard stills because it was cheaper than animating actual scenes, the characters are textbook anime tropes but have incredibly bland designs and boring powers, all the female characters have a wide-on for the male protagonist despite him having all the personality of plained timber that someone has sharpied a face on to, the female protagonist is  a walking “Im cold to everyone but my sister” trope and the story is so monumentally dull I was picking up my phone to check Reddit during cutscenes after the first couple of hours. I could have powered through if they’d actually made a good combat system - the reason I finished Chorus despite its myriad of problems was because getting in to fights was actually fun and it made me want to keep playing. But it’s so frustrating to almost see the potential of what it could have been and see the game completely go in the opposite direction for some reason, possibly rushing to release as a next-gen launch title when it would even be considered a mediocre last-gen game. FF7R was a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ PS4 title and it does every single one of Scarlet Nexus’s elements better by orders of magnitude. And with that I come a realisation about this game: the combat system, the pseudo-futuristic aesthetic, the concentrated linear progression - it all just seems like they wanted to do their own spin on FF7R, started make a last gen game, but saw an opportunity to rush it out to hit the next gen launch window.And in the end what we ended up with was one big grey lump of meh with some red neon resting on top.
