_childDocuments_.review: This checks all the boxes for a tabletop campaign game - difficult enough to be interesting, strategic, interesting multifaceted leveling system, the ability to make choices that affect your story. On top of all that, they transferred it seamlessly onto PC. As someone who played the tabletop game first, the PC version solves my main problems with the tabletop game - setting it up and taking it down. It works beautifully as a PC game and at a much better price.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the most brilliantly designed combat I've ever seen in a table top game / crpg.It is brutally challenging, though, and you'll have to spend a lot of time with learning the ropes.Even then you will FAIL frequently, so every conquered map feels like an incredible accomplishment.I can't count the times where I thought it to be outright impossible to beat a specific scenario, but in the end I've beaten them all. Due to the game's difficulty, I need a break now and then, playing more casual titles like Solasta or Poupup Dungeon, but I keep coming back to this "king of tactical games" to play a few scenarios and having a blast.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: Moderately amusing game that took me almost 300 hours to unlock the character I was waiting for the most, only to find out one of it's key builds/cards is bugged and doesn't even work.3 patches later, on a game that isn't even actually newly released, and they keep fixing multiplayer bs and ignoring this basic character bug.And HEAVEN FORBID if you try and find message board support on the issue and do something even slightly wrong so that the Spoiler Police spend all their energy enforcing a stupid meta-rule than actually help explain things.Obviously fun enough to spend almost 300 hours on but not making sure all your Classes actually work correctly has definitely made me Salty enough to down-vote.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely my favorite online boardgame, and one of the most fun and challenging tactical games I've ever played.  The biggest improvement over the physical copy is that pets can't try to eat the pieces while you're playing.  Scratch that, everything's a huge improvement: the game plays faster, shuffling decks isn't as fiddly, ally and enemy cards are very easy to flip through, and sources of error in calculation and enemy movement are greatly reduced.  Also, soothing Scottish accents.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this. I've played the board game regularly before.Too much RNG. Had a miss come up... and then come up immediately again for a burned card and burned item that would've ended a dangerous target. Even side scenarios you "win" along the way are too random.Scenarios take too long, even sped up.I cannot currently recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: I never played the table top version but a friend and I took about 100 hours BLASTING through every nook and cranny of the main campaign and came out absolutely satisfied. Would recommend to anyone who is into the genre. Has some flaws but they are quickly being worked out. 10/10 game. Remember, this is more of a PUZZLE game than anything else. Manage your resources.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve played the physical board game of Gloomhaven a few times, and I can confidently say that the Steam version is far superior. The setup/takedown of the physical game alone can take an hour, and this removes that entirely. I’ve played with a friend group for close to 80 hours at the time of this review, and it’s been a blast. The gameplay is like if  Divinity Original Sin 2 was mixed with a deck builder, and it works really well. Fans of the board game will love this, and anyone who enjoys turn based strategy games (best played with friends) should pick this up. Totally worth it at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: I played the physical game and I assumed enchantments lasted between characters. They do *NOT*. This makes enchantments a huge waste for all of your characters and drastically changes how I would have approached the game.I spent hours and hours preparing for my characters retirement (playing a sub-optimal setup with enchantments rather than purely items), and all of that work is wasted.EDIT: They have since patched the game and enchantments can be made permanent. This is an awesome change and renders my previous complaint null. Awesome change :)!
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: 10 hrs in and loving this unique strategy game. Never played the board game but am having alot of fun with the puzzle element to an my usual turn based tactics. The element of time pressure is great as it is tied into the number of turns you have, it almost eliminates camping / setting up. Also many of the cards at the lower levels are next turn setup combos making planning 1 turn ahead crucialWould love this type of system added to more games
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: Love the game. The guild master mode is a nice change up that lets you explore the game faster than the campaign. The campaign is the board game digitally. This game has progression and all the character building you would want, but it is also very much a strategy game if you like a challenge. It isn't forgiving, so you have to like to have to take time and think out synergies, etc. If you like that sort of thing, you really should give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: I have the board game and played it for years. Friends in other states hated me for always teasing them with photos of our game sessions they couldnt be included in. The digital version changes that. Now I play with friends and family from Florida, Texas and Hawaii. While its not as immersive as playing the board game, it is still fun to play with others. We had random disconnect issues at one point in multiplayer before we figured out that the player had syncing to the cloud turned off.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: Don't buy if you're trying to play co-op, it's apparently been broke for almost a year now.  Everything seems to function fine, until players start to lose parity (which takes 5 - 15 minutes), and then the wheels fall off the damned thing.  Core functions stop working, like the undo button or the settings menu, and crashes/disconnects are far too frequent.  Sad that I bought in after Saber destroyed what is otherwise a really good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: The early access build scratches the Gloomhaven itch, and I'm excited for when the game gets fully developed. Due to the limited amount of content right now it can get repetitive, but I overall enjoy the gameplay and how it takes a lot of what makes the board game a chore out of the equation. If you haven't played the game and are interested, there's a wealth of tutorial information (which is optional, so if you know what you're doing it's not a hassle to skip it) that breaks things down into digestible chunks.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: Honest Review,A lot of people don't understand early access. Which is just people not understanding game development and most of the critiques come from that blinded view. For example one guy didn't understand the durability system on some items. While this can suck, it is a balance system on items and characters in general since they have a shared gold pool as well. This system is just for the adventure mode which is just a small campaign mode really and not the main story/campaign.The game is fun, and very challenging in its current state. It is not a 1 to 1 with the board game right now as there is no campaign mode(story mode) at the moment, which is expected as that is going to take a lot of time as the campaign in the board game is quite extensive. There are bugs as with all games and they will take some working to fix but if you send in support tickets/report them on the discussion post under bugs they seem quite receptive and the patches seem to fix a lot of bugs if you look through the latest patch notes.Overall, for a gloomhaven experience/strategy/turnbased rpg combat, the game passes with flying colors. Again, it's not the campaign/story mode and if that's all you want then you should wait and multiplayer will also be released later. If, however, you want to support a fun game with much promise and an active indie studio through my personal experience has been quite friendly purchase now. In the long run you'll probably save yourself 20-50% of the final product cost as with all Early Access games.I hope this review helps someone. Overall the game is highly recommended and look forward to the progress being made to the point I can experience the story with a few friends and wonderful graphics.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: Want to give this an positive review to offset some of the unfortunate negative reviews.  For an early access game this is everything I expect.  Game shows great promise.  Devs are on the right track.  Yes, the content is light, but that is why this is early access.  Yes the game is hard, but it faithfully is interpreting a board game with a cult following.  If you like Gloomhaven, support this project.  If you like meaty digital board games, support this product.  If you like awesome fantasy settings, support this product.  Excited to see the game develop and happy to support the early access work of these devs.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: a slog for stress fetishists with too much timeThis is one of those games that makes you feel inhibited ever step of the way.The skill card system is different and a nice idea: Every combat round you choose two of your 10 or so cards; every card has a top and a bottom ability, and if you choose the top of one card, you have to go with the bottom of the other. However, the skills hardly ever seem to complement each other and are extremely situational; what's more, the game periodically forces you to remove cards from your active deck for the rest of a mission, and once you end up without two cards to choose from, you're out, so it all gets really stressful. The RNG and overall randomness factor is also high, and not in a good way.I've lost most of my patience over the years and the progression in this game is slower than the Second Coming. Every mission feels the same, though the enemy variety is okay, I guess, and the tilesets are varied and nice-looking. The narrative seems fine at first, but you it turns out to be quite bland and linear pretty quickly, so don't expect much in that department. The characters are different as far as their gameplay roles, but they have no personality.I guess this just isn't the game for me. Buy it on a budget, if you're starving for something to do, I guess.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of the actual board game I can say that is game is a perfect alternative for anyone who wants to play Gloomhaven without 1. All the set up, and 2. Cant get together around a table. So far its just as enjoyable as the real thing and I cant recommend it enough to anyone looking for a great RPG time with some friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: The price for the table-top game has always been putting me off from trying it. Now, after playing this, it's still putting me off, but I can forgive myself if I ever do end up buying it. One of the best table-top games ever made is now on PC, and me and my wife love playing it every single day. My machine is somewhat (read a lot) out of spec, so the visuals are wasted on it, but the core gameplay is what's important in these type of strategic, turn-based rpg games. And it's pretty good. Also, shout out to the tutorial makers, job well done, thank you very much!
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: i write this after requesting a refund.The game is good but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ PLEASE know what you're getting into. This is not what I thought it was. This is puzzle game where your actions are timed by your cards. Your not so much playing against the enemies as you are against the number of rounds until you've burned through your cards.I DESPISE this mechanic and it's core to the game loop.This does not mean that the game is bad it just means that I should have done my research first. I commend the devs for making something that so many people love and with such obvious quality.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: Not for the faint of heart. This game's campaign is extremely hard. I enjoyed the game at first until I realized that pretty much every mission plays the same. You stumble into an area with a multitude of enemies and you spend all your time clearing them out, only to find another room with even more. I have beaten 6 missions and so far they get harder and harder to where at the end, I only have one card left. I'm playing on normal btw. I wouldn't mind the difficulty so much if the game didnt try to force your character into a specific playstyle. Example: I play Tinkerer and Mindthief and I really wanted to go for a summon playstyle. Well, it's not viable at all and you are usually burning cards for no reason as the summons die way too quickly anyways. So, now I have to play stun lock Thief and Multikill tinkerer otherwise I lose. Even if I do play optimally, it seems that I am always at the cusp of losing no matter what I do.  Slay the Spire is a deckbuilder that lets you beat the game with more playstyles than meets the eye and it handles difficulty very well with scaling enemies. This game however, it throws frustrating enemies right at the start and continues to scale up even more than it needs to be. Sun demons and Wind Demons come to mind. The thing is, I want to enjoy this game but at the moment it's too much trouble to stress for every single mission.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: Been enjoying this in mulitiplayer with a group of friends for sometime.  I notice a few people have said multiplayer is a mess - I've been lucky enough not to experience this so can't really comment.The RNG does seem to sometimes kick you in the balls, but I don't think it's out to get you, just seems that way at times.Lots of fun and saves tracking progress and dealing with moves etc... like you do in the board game.  Would be nice to gave more or the characters to chose from rather than them being unlocks, not too sure on the benefit of this as they are all kind of similar (yes some have better powers based on playstyle etc...)The LOS can appear a bit janky in doorways, but the game does follow the targeting system well, it just sometimes doesn't look it due to graphics/walls around doorways and stuff.Enjoying it so far and the fact we are so faar away from completion doing 2 or 3 missions per sitting means we have lots to look forward too.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: I did not buy the board game because it would be hard to gather people, learn the rules, set up and keep track of all the maths. This ticks every box. I love being able to jump into missions, get the same strategic depth and teamwork when playing with others. I'm awful at the game, but I love it. A superb way to experience the board game when you do not have the resources to host.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: Update 10-21-21: With full release i can stand by my initial recommendation! Started the campaign and being familiar with the tabletop version, was pleasantly surprised, that all matches up as it should, so far so good! -------------------Love the table top version and look forward to long weekends when me and the missus get to continue our ongoing campaign day and night. Now i finally have a way to play while waiting for those weekends! Really looking forward to see how they implement the actual campaign, as that to me is where gloomhaven really shines! Loving everything so far and dont really have much criticism to offer. Personally dont see any issues with the UI or the number of clicks others have mentioned as gloomhaven has so many moving pieces in the tabletop version im not quite sure how it could be streamlined while adhering to the original rules and mechanics. keep up the great work!
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: If you have ever tried to play the board game, or wanted to play the board game, I recommend you instead play the digital edition. While there is the annoying mechanics/interface that does not always let you 'undo' an action when normally you'd be able to; it is not enough of an issue where it detracts from the entire game. The laborious rule following and turn taking of the table top version of this game do detract from the game experience of Gloomhaven.Fun solo, fun as a group.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: Not my cup of tea.Its sold as an turn-based tactical RPG (like Fallout Tactics, Battletech or Gears Tactics) but actually plays as a puzzle turn based game (such as Into the Breach).Battles are slow and the game will punish you severely for every non perfectly optimal move you make. Most tactic games, allow variety of sub-optimal choices that will somehow work in battle. In Gloomhaven, you pick or discard the wrong card or make the wrong move and thats it, you will lose the entire battle.Other aspect I didnt liked at all is the randomness in your attacks. A tactical game with "negative crits" shouldnt be called tactical at all, but rather "BS simulator". When you level up your characters instead of getting skill perks like "X skill gets more range" or "X skill now deals +1 damage" you get to "remove some negative crits" from four attacks. Basically, as you level up, less random bs will happen. Yay! (?)I cant see how people played this tabletop. Battles lasted ten hours (to kill just 4 enemies)?
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: While still in Early Access, the game is shaping up very well. Just know that the only playable mode right now is not the main campaign of the board game, but the game follows the board games rules pretty closely and accurately. The updates are huge when they happen and the developers have really been listening to the community on how to improve. I have no doubts the finished product will be all the developers promise.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a few dozen scenarios of the big box gloomhaven and finished the Jaws of the Lion campaign over the board. I really really enjoy the digital game for it's automatic draws, calculations, monster movement, etc. The UX really allows you to focus on the core of the gameplay without the hours of setup, organization, etc. Highly recommend both versions, but the digital will definitely be how I replay with anyone new to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: I know many folks love this but my experience of it is that it ultimately collapses under the weight of its own cleverness: essentially, the game is just is too board-gamey for my tastes. I was hoping this would feel to me like Warhammer Quest or For the King, and instead it feels mostly like Puerto Rico with a combat system.My real complaints here are that the there are just too many aspects of the experience which break verisimilitude, like you only collect gold + treasure chests if you end a turn on them... rather than just picking them up on your way out of the cleared-out dungeon. The merchant has two helmets to sell at the start. Characters can't share gold (this feature in particular I understand, but it's an imposition that again takes me out of the experience).I wanted more of an RPG experience and this delivers a boardgame experience. It's not a bad game at all, but it isn't to my tastes and therefore I can't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: This is my favorite board game (no contest), and taking it to PC has made it even better. Even though I miss painting my minis and playing a physical board game, cutting out the tremendous amount of unpacking and setup and the time-consuming delays of remembering the complex ruleset and looking things up every few minutes has made this a possible weeknight activity. Having the computer facilitate this game has taken out all the work and made it so much easier to get in and play without needing to make a huge event of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: This game has come a long way since it first released in early access. If you like the board game this will be an easy way to play the campaign together with your friends, without all the time sink it takes to setup. I thought they had planned to release the Campaign this July but we are still pending the official release!
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: Once you understand your characters will get beat up badly and you learn how to make the best use of the different cards the game becomes much more manageable than it might seem at first.  Not sure if you can successfully play with less than 4 characters just given the number of enemies encountered, etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: I get that you're trying to have some added funding while this game is in progress.But really, devs?? to call this game an early access would still be an atrocity! this isn't even 10% of the game! would be amazing if this game can even release in 2020!Edit 12 December 2019: this game is updating nicely, even though there's still some bugs. Still hoping for multiplayer coop.Edit 3 March 2020: played a few more hours, loving the updates, changing my review to thumbs up even though there's still a lot of updates to be desired. but overall, a nice game.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing the boardgame for a while and so far, I've felt really frustrated with the implementation while playing this version.  I feel like it's tedious to mouseover every card individually to see what it does instead of being able to look at all the cards side by side on a turn.  Because that review is tedious, when I've picked one of the two cards, I just want to click it, so I don't forget, but then I have to click the cards in the right order to set the initiative, which I've forgotten to do, and thus completely messed up a turn multiple times now.  I'd rather see a layout where I can compare all the available cards at once on 1/2 the screen, with the other 1/2 being maybe a mini-hex map of where your character and the enemies are.I feel like the gameplay is sacrificed for fancy graphics.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't care for the original board game. It was fun, but it took forever to set up and take down and the rules were pretty fiddly, leading to a large FAQ and time spent between turns looking up edge cases in the rules.Thanks to this app, none of that exists anymore! You can just play Gloomhaven alone, or with friends online and it takes care of everything; enemy movement, elements, EVERYTHING. It's great. Buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely addictive...for the right players.Tl;dr: You're going to fail. A lot.I had to play through the first mission four times to get it.Follow through, grab those gold piles, grind that experience and learn how to optimize the deck and plan your turns. Fun assured if you're up for that challenge.Being selfish in the encounters can give a lot of immediate rewards and helping the world out tends to accumulates rewards later. Choose wisely.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: I own a physical copy of Gloomhaven as well, and I thought when I bought the digital copy that I would mostly use it with friends to play through the original campaign while we couldn't get together due to the pandemic.  However, I've mostly been using it to play solo through the Guildmaster mode, which is a brand new campaign not included in the physical version.  I love it, and if you enjoy strategic RPGs, I think you will too!  The only warning that I have for prospective buyers is that the game is very processor heavy, so if you're going to play it on a laptop with poor ventilation/cooling (like I do), you'll probably have to turn down the display quality settings (like I have).
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: Gloomhaven is a horrible, inaccessible, overly complex game with too many rules, too many modifiers, too many cards... like some AD&D nerd went crazy masturbating his dungeon master brain to come up with the most complex train wreck he could muster because no woman would let him touch her titties, except for his fat cousin who's 50. Calm the ♥♥♥♥ down.  Yes, i'm sure there are people who LOVE to spend 5 minutes figuring out if they should move to Hexagon 1 or Hexagon 2, but then i would say, "what's wrong with you?  Life is too simple?  You're a multimillionaire with your dream house and wonderful family that you got 10 hrs to burn on doing 5 things in a game?"  If you want to spend this much time thinking about tiny, little minutia things, go do it for something that really matters.  Go cure a disease, fight poverty, feed the hungry, start a small business, anything.. just don't do it on this ♥♥♥♥♥♥ game.  I'm telling you, it's not worth it.Pass times are supposed to be light, fun, simple... because that's what they are supposed to be.. PASS TIMES... unless you can figure out how to make a Career out of playing Gloomhaven, I'd say PASS.  Too much.  Shame on you Gloomhaven creators, go wipe up your gloomhaven spoodge now, it's messing up my floors.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: There are a few loading freezes but that may just be my pc and not the game itself. The starting faze of learning the mechanics of the game are very beginner friendly while also not wasting time for gloomhaven vets. Whether playing alone or with friends this game is a lot of fun and can be quite a challenge with great rewards for those who like to play strategy based games
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most innovative, creative, replayable board games of all time. And the video game version reproduces it just as you'd expect. All good things to say about this one. Just don't forget to bring your friends. Solo is perfectly fine too, but can be a challenge for one human to keep everything in your mind at once. Friends help spread the load.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: Some context before the review:-I've played Gloomhaven (Physical board game) before trying this version. Roughly 20 hours. Unlocked our first new class and got the enchanter started late because we did a lot of side missions.-I've played this version since its release on Early Access-I love strategy, fantasy, and D&D-like dungeon crawler gamesThat said, if you agree/resonate with any of my statements above, you will probably love this game. It emulates the classic board game really well, and gives you completely optional quality of life changes to help make some of the more challenging, or rather annoying, aspects of the original a bit more managable (summon mechanics, monster targeting rules, etc). I love that it can be cooperative with friends, or solo. It is a fraction of the cost of the board game and breathes life into the series with wonderful animation, sound effects, voices (a lovely narrator for scenario text, and fun battle noises for each character's abilities). I can't express how great this has been as an option to play virtually during the pandemic, or if someone is just too far to come over. I hope you give it a try if you're new to Gloomhaven or have tried the board game- it's a really fun time! Have fun exploring!
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: Early access turn-based dungeon crawler, quite nice already.I haven't played the board game but this digital version is easy to get into and game mechanics are explained in the tutorial missions. Took around 50 hours to complete the main adventure quests with 2 characters. 6 other characters are available to play and mechanics are different between each character so there is some replay value.Character progression is nice. Relatively slow but steady with perk points, new gear, additional enhancement or character level-up which unlocks a new card: your character won't change much from one map to another but each little improvement adds-up.Very few bugs overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: This game just keeps getting better and better. Communication to the community is great and each update brings both new things, as well as pieces of the tabletop game to life. If you're a fan of the tabletop, you'll love this; if you've never played tabletop GH....why not?!?! LOL - seriously, go do that...but this is an excellent strategy RPG even if you haven't played the tabletop version.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, love how every decision has a true consequence, weather that be now or later. The characters are incredible, the abilities, the combos, the tag team combos, i love it. Thank you for bringing this to a pc where i can play and not have to lay out a big ass board in my house and my wife look at me like im some sort of alien from another planet. Lots of bugs still but thats what early access is all about. Cant wait for future content releases leading up to full release.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: I like everything about this game. Can't wait for it to be finished with all the mercenaries and full campaign. Also looking forward to there being all the other content that Gloomhaven has to offer in the board game world for this digital platform. This game puts a grip on you and sucks you in fast. 60 billions stars out of 5.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: Though there still isn't a, "campaign," according to the game, there is. It's just not the board game campaign yet. Haven't delved into multiplayer as of yet since it seems you need a code or players you know in order to do so; however, there is a single player campaign to do. You can play 2-4 heroes by yourself and if you've played the tabletop version you will absolutely love it, and hope for more to come.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: I was really turned off by this game.  Nowhere does this game say it is a deck builder.  Frankly was completely bored out of my mind in about 30 minutes of game play.    If a game cannot capture your attention in the first 30 minutes I doubt another couple of hours will help.   This was the first game I have ever asked for a refund in 25 years of gaming on Steam.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: The voice acting and animation are awesome - fit the setting perfectly. I think being online/automated speeds the game up significantly and shows how well the board game can be played as a video game. There's so many things to unlock and loot to plunder I could keep playing this game for hours on end. I really couldn't get that interested in the tabletop version of Gloomhaven but this game is killer
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: I tried playing the physical version of the game and I enjoyed it but it was SO much to keep track of. This keeps all the best parts of the original game while automating all of the tedious parts, which is great. Sometimes the UI and descriptions are a little vague and you have to screw up a few times to figure out some secret rules, and the lack of an undo button in certain situations can be a bit frustrating. Overall though I really love the game, it just definitely has a learning curve.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: DO NOT BUY THIS IF YOU PLAY ALONEThis game is a horrible drag when played solo and I would not recommend this ever.It's takes too long and the RNG is stacked against you in a classical manner where seemingly impossible things will happen, just like in X-COM, except that enemies don't play by the same rules and spam the same ability OVER AND OVER.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: An almost excellent adaptation of the boardgame Gloomhaven.  However, the digital version is riddled with bugs and errors.  The enemies do not focus correctly, which in this game can absolutely RUIN your turn.  Some of the scenarios are just not playable.  We just finished (SPOILERS)  Toxic Moor, and the Drakes whirled around and destroyed the tree... which if you have played this scenario you know is /not/ how it is supposed to work. (END SPOILERS)   The animations are alright, characters have 3 animations for attack, using an item, or using an ability.  It's fine, it works.  The environments are also fine, recycled from what looks like 3-4 tilesets to build each scenario.  None of that is super important, as long as the game actually works.  As a veteran of the actual tabletop of this game, I cannot recommend this digital version in it's current broken state.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: Like every game with a good amount of effort and content it can be a bit confusing at first to manage all your players and cards, However once you get the rhythm down and start to understand where the skill factor comes into play it is a very fun and challenging game. If you like the strategy style of Divinity Original Sin 2 you will like this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the game, that is the board game. Played countless hours with that one and around 1.5k with the digital version. While I prefer the real thing, playing campaigns is a tedious job, setting up scenarios, not making mistakes during the plays etc, is not easy, you need a pretty big table and a reliable group who doesn't abandon the campaign. The digital version helps with this a lot, no more setup, no more mistakes etc, I think it looks pretty nice , I'm even ok with the controls. It was quiet buggy at the beginning but most of them were fixed. There is one thing that ruins the game for me though, and I can't look over it, and that is the rate of pulling curses and misses on high brutal+ difficulty. I played the game a lot of times, but I'm still enjoying it with a friend and we still enjoy playing it on very high difficulty, however it looks like the developers using different algorithm to decide what cards we pull from the attack modifier on different difficulty. This is prety damn annoying. And I'm talking about pulling a miss with 1-2 characters out of four, for about 4 rounds every turn. Now, according to the rules, whenever you pull a miss, you supposed to reshuffle the deck, the chances to pull 4 misses for several turns continuously.. well they are very low, but somehow it keeps happening on every scenario with us. The enemy also seem to pull every single curse from their deck when they have 4-5+ curses. It's just really not realistic, and even if you put Maths on the side, I played a lot with the physical board game, it's not happening. This ruins the game for me, I want to finish it on Brutal and Deadly but even with a deck, with no negative modifier other than the miss, I pull a miss 5 times in a row... BS.Not sure how it is implemented, but it really feels like on higher difficulty, the algorithm is different, which is just stupid, you have increased damage and HP for enemies and traps, just stick to that, introduce more difficulty levels with even more damage + hp, but changing the "luck" element of the game is a joke.I really want to recommend the game because the rest is ok or really good, but I had enough. Luckily Frosthaven is out!
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: The board game is a lot of fun. If you like that you'll probably like the digital version too despite it's flaws. The camera is awful  and you'll constantly be fighting the auto camera for control. The enemy ability cards don't seem to fully cycle through the deck properly. Also don't expect the cards to be the same from the board game to digital. Both monster and mercenary cards have been tweaked in some instances. AI pathfinding can be bad at times. If you're not careful and you make an accidental button click, you can completely waste a turn.If you can look past those issues, it's worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: Tutorial is unskippable. Pacing is extremely slow. Doesn't feel punchy or rewarding to win. When you run out of cards, you lose. Even if you don't waste time, you can still lose if the procedural dungeons are too long, but you won't know this until your 20-30 minutes into a dungeon. Might improve, but basically, not fun at it's core.---Update:Came back to this to try the DLC and see how things ended up. This is hands down my least favourite RPG on steam. I really dislike everything about it, from the pacing to the convoluted systems. None of it adds depth. Something as simple as picking up items from a chest (oddly difficult), may net you an item or it may put that item in the town 's shop, for you to buy later (bizarre). Character classes are locked behind hours of play and the whole experience is like controlling a group of rpg characters via marionette strings. I cannot fathom why this game was made this way or for who. It haunts me.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: I find this game unnecessarily difficult, I mean right from the very first quest, it's hard.  So far I've beaten 7/15 quests and I feel like I've just barely managed to finish each scenario by the skin of my teeth....and yet despite this, I am still on the cusp of purchasing Jaws of the Lion DLC.  As I level up and unlock new skills, there is a sense of new hope (that this game will get easier, via my continual learning) and so I press on.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of the board game, this is an excellent adaptation.If you haven't played the board game, this is an excellent tactical, turn-based rpg.  The primary mechanics revolve around card hand-management mechanics with tons of unlockable items and classes.Co-op also works great! Hope expansions are adapted!
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far the hardest table top game I have ever played. First, it was hard to understand the mechanics, then tactics came into play but after that (and with the help of my smarter comrades) the game really opened up for me. It's challenging. It's beautiful. It makes you use your brain for once. The amount of content quest-wise and character-wise is huge. Can't be certain, but I reckon it may take up to 300 hours to try out every max level character with all perks and cards unlocked and beat all 95 scenarios.I would especially like to note the work of the narrator. Boy did he deliver an outstanding performance! And yes, as many before mentioned, it's better with friends. You will fight, argue about choices and laugh at your stupidity, basically having a great time. There's one technical issue though that could ruin the fun: the game is VERY sensitve to your internet connection so if you have a bad one prepare yourself for frequent disconnects.Other than that, highly recommend and do hope to see more content soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: I love the boardgame, and so I decided to try the digital version for solo play. For the digital version, I especially like the fact that you get different scenarios than the boardgame, and also I love the summons coming to life. What I dont like that much, is that new classes are unlocked too quickly in my opinion - no time to wonder about whats to come (which is one of the main reasons boardgame Gloomhaven gets so addictive).
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: Best game ever, in my opinion. I slowly fell out of love with video games in the last few years and this one brought me back. It's been a while since I found myself thinking and talking about what I've played hours after I ended the session... and long time since I woke up in the morning with my first thought being to try again that last mission I failed the night before. Like many people that wrote here, I wanted to buy the physical game, but was discouraged by the ordeal of setting it up every time I'd want to play. On the other hand this is considered the best board game of all time for a reason (there are ranks that attest to this) and I really wanted to try it. The digital version of this game was a must... and it didn't fail. Best played with a friend... the way you have to plan, strategize and cooperate adds a lot to the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: Gloomhaven is based on a board game.  The board game is excellent, highly tactical, and engrossing.  The computer game is wonderful in that you don't have to set up the board (which takes ages), and is getting more of the interesting features of the board game with every patch.  If you understand that Gloomhaven is trying to bring the board game to life and like that idea, this is for you.  If not, you may not like it.  An added advantage is that the computer game is far cheaper than the board game.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: Love the board game. Played this; got a refund. I'm fine with an Early Access game lacking polish but having most of its content, or lacking most of its content but having a polished system, but Gloomhaven has neither. When I played, in addition to having very bare-bones content (no card upgrades, items didn't work right, only 4 classes had been implemented), there were a ton of bugs, way more than there should have been for what is ultimately just a digital board game.Granted, this was in 2019, and they've been steadily adding content since then, but things were so buggy at the time I'm going to wait at least another year to give it a second shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: Still pretty early on, maybe 4 missions out of the tutorial.  The game has happily surprised me.  I was not expecting much in the early access, but the Guild Master campaign mode has a LOT of meat to chew on.I just picked up Gloomhaven: Jaws of the lion and was very happy with that so thought I would give this a try to practice when my wife is busy.The game is GREAT.  Only one really well handled crash, got an exception regarding an undefined pointer and it just bounced me to the title screen, when I reloaded I happily found that it saves every turn so I barely lost any progress.The tutorial is really well done, not too hand holdy like so many games.  It teaches you a few tricks then gives you a little puzzle to solve with some cards and lets you fail at your own pace experimenting with the design.  A few things I know because of having read the manual for the physical game that I am not sure if they were explained enough, mostly how the persistent abilities work.  And there is a symbol I don't understand in the perk tree.  But overall very happy with the onboarding for what could be a pretty complicated game.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: Never played the board game, but I hear this is a good adaptation. Fun game with friends and certainly challenging at times. Definitely requires some strategy and coordination, but missions are achievable and short enough to make for quick online sessions after work. A few bugs exist in the game, especially in the campaign with system lockups, but overall it's a well built and fun game.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: I get that this game is only in EA for about a month. And in that regard it is really decent. Of course there is not much to do yet which is understandable. But what is there works properly and looks good. So much for the Pros. Now the negative stuff which there really is not that much of to be honest. But why on earth has this game to try and come up with it's own rules? There is no durability system in the board game. And apparently for a reason because here it just sucks. Maybe it is just to give players something to do while there is so little content in the game. If that is so I would be fine with this as a temporary mechanic to stretch out the content a bit. But then dear developers please let us know about it.And more importantly the core game is balanced for random dungeons being compiled of three rooms. No more and no less. Just adding more rooms messes with the balance far too much. Please stick to the source material a little more closely because these two aspects alone take away a lot of what makes the original so great. So in conclusion: I understand that sometimes it is hard to move a source material to another medium. But this is only true when it is also moved into another system like converting a board game into a first person shooter. Gloomhaven the board game already works almost exactly like a video game, so please for the love of gaming stick to it's rules to the t. I also imagine that coming up with new rules costs resources... so please stop wasting them. I am only speaking for myself here but I bought the game because I wanted a faithful recreation of the original game and not an hommage to the game that is only loosely based upon it.This rating will be a thumbs up as soon as the game gets the rules correctly because the fundamentals are really good and look very promising.Edit: Changed my review to thumbs up due to the answer I received from the devs regarding the differing rules.

_childDocuments_.review: Gloomhaven delivers the turn-based top-down dungeon crawler experience through the limitations of a ~10 card deck. Your deck diminishes over the course of the dungeon, using cards for actions or movement. Taking excessive damage will also cost you cards, sometimes more than half your deck in a single turn if you are very unlucky, which can make your run very short.The idea of fusing movement and actions into a limited set of action cards is novel, but ultimately given the games aggressive RNG this will mean most players will exhaust their turns part way through a dungeon. There are certain classes with the ability to restore discarded cards, which my party relied on heavily.The game itself is designed to be punishing, but mostly not in a way that can learned or overcome. In our experience, rolls typically skew unfavorable. Using one of your ~10 cards for an action doesn't mean it will happen, often you will fail a dice roll and just waste one of your precious cards. Our party began at Normal difficulty, and after failing to clear the first mission more than 6 times, we tried other missions, and also failed all of those. Eventually we began periodically lowering the difficulty which allowed us to finally progress. There appears to be a massive disparity between the games easiest difficult and all other difficulty settings. Ultimately we had to choose between an unchallenging easy difficulty and an unassailable Normal difficulty. As you progress the game does become somewhat manageable as you can afford items and unlock new cards.The game also has "encounters" which occur between dungeons. They involve a bit or story followed by a binary choice. Regardless of the choice, most encounters will hurt your party, either by taking away your progress towards action points, money, or giving your party a debuff at the start of the next dungeon. There is no way to predict which choice will provide what detriment, the only way to learn this is through experience and repetition. There is also a chance that encounters can benefit a party, but these appear to be extremely uncommon.Playing with friends, the game needs to be reset roughly every other dungeon due to technical issues such as desync, crashes, and other bugs. The game has a dedicated bug report menu, which our host used frequently. The game does not allow players to rejoin mid-turn: you have to wait until turns are over, so the host ends up having to play many of other players moves. Rejoining is not a guarantee that users will be able to retake control of their characters and we experience several soft locks where our only solution was to kick all players and stream the hosts perspective in a voice call.I write this review after having narrowly completing an escort dungeon by one turn before exhausting our last standing players deck. We are not sure if it was a deliberate design choice or buggy pathfinding AI, but the NPC we were required to escort would not move if any enemies anywhere in the dungeon were positioned in a doorway space. It took many turns during the session to even understand how to get them to move, as they just stood by at the entrance turn after turn.The game is not bad, I personally think the aesthetic of the game is wonderful. The dungeons feel somewhat underwhelming in design, but the game definitely captures a tabletop map and deck game motif. The abilities are varied and choosing which card to play definitely involves understanding, strategy, and a degree of chance. It definitely involves a different mindset. The games story is largely driven by each dungeon, episodic and sparse. The game does provide art and narration.This is perhaps one of the few games where I do not feel a sense of accomplishment when overcoming difficulty, and unfortunately felt strongly enough to leave a negative review. It's a nice game if you're a glutton for punishment, but I do not think most people would find this game enjoyable. The game will roll the dice, and bad rolls are extremely punishing and will make your experience short.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr : Overall this is a great bang for the buck game.Very true to the boardgame. You do not have to know the board game to enjoy though.If you like turn based fantasy play, this is for you. If you have a friend or three to join youyou'll have a great time. That will be full of difficultchoices, and laughable mistakes. Along with a few mistakes that make you made at yourself.But when you one hit and elite drake and three of your friends cheer... It's magical too.Speaking of magic it's a card based system of play. you have a limited size deck, too manycards and always a few regrets. You will want a crowbar for one more card. _childDocuments_.review: Way better than the board game. Does it sound fun to move and manage every single enemy on the board, paying close attention to managing all of the complicated rules and quirks, or would you rather let the computer do it? _childDocuments_.review: Would I say it's better than the board game? It's close. On the one hand you got the close interactions with friends, on the other the 2 hours to set it up and tear it down make it a chore. Plus this streamlines the game so much, that you can play a scenario in 2/3 of the time, even if you are uber fast in the boardgame (for most people the digital is 1/2 of the time per scenario).It's an extremely good adaptation, I could literally not ask for more.The game itself is exceptional, one of the best games (not just video games, or board games) ever made, even though it looks like a dungeon crawler, it's more of an optimization / puzzle game. It may appear hard, but it's really not after you grasp it. In addition you are the weakest at the beginning, so after getting some perks / items, and most of all experience with the card system, it gets much easier. With my board game group we could consistently win on hard and some times we would even find it easy (some scenarios are easier than others -while the escort missions are super hard even on easy!)If I could propose some improvements, those would be quality of life specific, like a bit more undos (eg after selecting the tile that you want to move to, you should be able to undo everything since no "dice have been rolled"), as well a tiny bit more UI to show you the current state of your character (gold, experience, number of burnt and available cards).I wholeheartedly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Gloomhaven is a unique card base legacy RPG that can be quite challenging. Aside from the fact that this is a Work in Progress, I really do enjoy the digital edition more than the paper edition. What the digital edition does better than the paper edition is managing all the little stuff for you. Setting up can take a massive amount of time.Each character feels unique and can delve into different play style as you progress the character. What I really like about this game is the way health work. Each character have their base HP that increases as they level, but in addition, they also can burn cards from their hand or discard them as they use it. This leads to making riskier plays and thinking hard about what to do now, so that you don't limit your options too much later. When a character burn too much cards, they become exhausted. And if a character takes heavy damage, they can opt to burn their cards. This means that the card practically functions as a stamina system. Some character has a bigger card pool as well. Balance wise, I feel every character has their own unique style and can perform on par with one another in their own roles, though certain character combination might be really good or at worst, somewhat bad but doable.All in all, I would recommend playing the tutorial, and making your own decision from there (whether to refund or not) before committing to the game. I personally like it, so I recommend giving it a try at the very least!
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: It would take a bit of an essay to properly explain why I don't like Gloomhaven, because the mechanics are the problem and they are quite convoluted.To put things in a nutshell/simplify as much as I can: actions in the game revolve around a deck of two-sided cards that slowly exhaust, and you must choose wisely when to play each card and which side to play. The problem is that very basic actions, such as moving and looting mobs, are all actions on this limited and ever-exhausting pool of cards. I find that such things essentially all sharing the same AP pool is fundamentally at odds with fun. It turns a tabletop RPG into something different; it turns it into a puzzle game.Is this a bad thing? Not necessarily. Gloomhaven might be a lot of fun for you. Most RPGs are optimisation problems in disguise and perhaps, unlike me, you don't find it jarring when this reality isn't concealed. Or perhaps you just really love puzzles. I review based on what I like though, so it's "Not Recommended" from me.

_childDocuments_.review: ***SPOILER FREE REVIEW***Gloomhaven is one of the best board games ever made.  Period.  The game plays as a dungeon crawler and uses a Card based action system that is simple to explain but extremely nuanced in its complexity.  Each round you play two cards and then, when it's your turn in initiative, perform the top action of one card and the bottom action of the other.  It's that simple but there are ten thousand reasons why it is actually more complex than that.  Which top action do you choose (for you are not locked in to an action until you perform it)? What do you target with your attack?  What is the enemy doing?  What are your allies doing?  Should you use one of the game's many powerful items?  Should you use all of your items in one bombastic turn thus sacrificing yourself in a white, hot blaze of glory?  The possibility space is nearly unlimited and thus this game's main mechanic is just perfection.  I simply cannot rave about it enough.  You NEED to play this game!So, all this digital version has to do is adapt the board game faithfully without any game breaking glitches.  Gloomhaven digital does succeed at that but not perfectly.  I've played a lot of this game by now and I would say one out of every dozen play sessions something goofs up.  That's only a 8.33% failure rate but still, it can be frustrating.  Most frequently it just requires a reboot but occasionally my play group and I have lost progress.  Never huge amounts of it but we have lost multi hour long play sessions to the ether forcing us to replay scenarios.  So, do I recommend the game?  Yes, I do.  I would also recommend that you, or someone in your play group, back up your saves.  Speaking of play groups, this game is enhanced greatly by playing it with others.  I would still recommend the game if you are forced to play it alone but it's worth playing at a slower pace just to accommodate friend's schedules.  Good luck friends!-B9

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic adaptation of the board game, but also a fantastic tactical turn based strategy RPG even newcomers. The digital version is able to abstract away a lot of the more tedious elements of Gloomhaven (mainly setup and managing enemies) to let you focus on the fun parts - picking cool cards, making clever plans, and screaming because that 12 damage hit you queued up got nullified are you kidding me I literally burned two cards for that hit ahhhhhhhAlthough the heart of the game is really playing co-op with a small consistent group of friends, the solo mode is still a lot of fun. So far we've encountered a few frustrating problems - it's easy to ♥♥♥♥ yourself over with a single misclick, there are a handful of bugs that can desync what each player sees, but generally both solo and co-op are a fresh and accessible take on Gloomhaven physical. The game may say early access, but it feels very polished.The big thing it's missing is a lot of the story/lore. Gloomhaven is more than just a very cool tactical strategy game, it's also got lots of interesting questlines and scenarios with cool twists that I haven't seen much of in the digital version. Hopefully we will see more of that as the game develops.Highly recommend

_childDocuments_.review: I have played the original boardgame and Tabletop Sim Version, as well. _childDocuments_.review: It pains me to not understand the fandom this game has garnered. I couldn't possibly hate Gloomhaven more. More confusingly, are from the few negative reviews this game has gotten; nobody appears to address any of the complaints I'm about to bring up. I got your back!There is plenty to pick apart, but I've narrowed down my disdain to these insufferable aspects...--- STAGES [] ---Lets start off by stating the obvious, the card "burn" mechanic is f*cking obnoxious! Yet, it is made far worse whenever exploring a stage for the first time. Are there three rooms? Four? More? Who the hell knows! But, you better hustle because you'll eventually run out of cards. Or, don't hustle, because alerting too many enemies is securing doom. Who knows? Certainly not you, on the first run. Don't despair, keep losing your progress and you'll eventually come to...--- STAGES [] ---Now you know the stage. Might have taken a few tries, but the mystery is gone. There isn't any randomization for: corridors; room size; enemy type and layout; traps. It's beyond dumb and feels like the game could have saved me some time if it just revealed the layout. But, what's the fun in that right? Though now you're subjected to just...--- STAGES [] ---Once you've figured out what works for the layout and characters, just repeat the same strategy. RNG might change things up a bit but for most situations, you'll figure out the best opener for a particular level and when to have that "push" card on standby for pushing monsters into traps you know they'll be standing adjacent to. Hopefully this redundancy won't be boring for you because...--- STAGES [] ---You will be stuck on the same levels multiple times during the early game. This won't always be the case as you gear and level up, but when it does happen, it will test your f*cking mettle in ways few games of this nature ever do. Good luck!--- ENCOUNTERS ---Having to endure encounters isn't an issue rather it is the perceived choice they claim to offer. Play the game long enough, you'll memorize which choices have idealistic outcomes or offer lesser punishments. Why even bother? I'd much rather the game would randomly give or take crap from me. Don't insult us with the illusion of choice, when I already know choosing option 'B' will always give me reputation, whereas option 'A' would have robbed me. These options are fixed. They don't offer a percentage outcome of risk or reward. Oh, and take note, be prepared to lose a lot of progress until you familiarize yourself with the correct answers.--- COIN ---Wow! Sh*t gets crazy expensive in this game. It's already challenging enough trying to complete a level in the hopes that the cards won't burn out before the area can be cleared. Yet, I'm expected to squat on gold piles or utilize loot cards to collect what starts off as paltry amounts? This doesn't appear too unreasonable until you unlock card upgrades. I took a look at the cost of those and decided for everything else this game has pissed me off about, I'm done grinding my way through mediocrity.

_childDocuments_.review: A bare-bones version of the board game that captures the magic of the card-driven action system I've come to love, but every other aspect of this game is grossly underdeveloped.  The sheer amount of work required to elevate this project to something functional and fulfilling is staggering to think about.Scenarios (the combat events of the game) are engaging but horribly imbalanced.  Serious play testing is needed, especially on harder difficulties.  Playing scenarios grants you gold and exp which can then be used to empower your heroes.  The sad part is that - at the moment - gold is almost entirely useless. Items available in the shops are nearly worthless and, worst of all, uninteresting.  Not to mention the infuriating item decay system.  Items you aquire break after a short time, even when unused.  Gaining new cards after leveling remains satisfying and meaningful, but even this system needs an overhaul.The UI is gross.  Reading your cards is time-consuming and frustrating in the game's current state.  I can only read the text of one card at a time when selecting from a hand of 10-11.  Inexcusable. Attack modifiers, a major source of tension in the board game, are displayed microscopically.  Embrace the board game aesthetic and display them on colored cards that flash up after every attack. The current system only leaves players confused and frustrated.  Even if you love the board game, skip this.  In it's current adolescent state it's just not worth your time.  Darkest Dungeon, Icarus, Slay the Spire, and many others scratch this same itch in a far more effective way.

_childDocuments_.review: For an early access game, I am impressed.  Had no issues in the first four hours of play - mainly just got through the tutorial in that time. Strategy is definitely key here.  Overall, I like what I've experienced so far.  Looking forward to seeing what the full campaign will be like.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. I played through Jaws of the Lion with the physical board game, and it took almost a year and a half, with an average of 3 hours per scenario. _childDocuments_.review: The game does a great job of replicating the board game, and likewise will be more fun playing multiplayer.  The graphics, music, and audio are on point, and the text in the encounters is suitably whimsical.  The mechanics of the game itself feel very fresh relative to other games I've played, as you constantly have to weigh risk versus reward in how you play each card and level up to add more cards to your deck.  In an era where it feels like games are too easy, here is one where you need to really think about each move and plan multiple moves in advance.  I'm really looking forward to see how the game develops, the devs are on the right track so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: My primary concern with this game is how unstable it is.  It crashes frequently, and disconnects in multiplayer.  A lot of players have experienced a large load time when getting into the game that makes it seems like the game has frozen (you just have a wait several minutes to see progress).  That's a bad sign.  But additionally, while I can see why this game would be attractive to a very particular kind of gamer - I doubt the vast majority of people will like it.  There's several odd quality of life issues with the game, including the obvious need for an "undo" button for a misclick (which would never happen in the board game).  And the difficulty curve of the game is not at all welcoming.  The game clearly expects you to learn by a multitude of failures against a single scenario - especially in the early game - instead of easing you in.  It gets boring quite quickly, and I doubt many players will want to bash their head against the wall so often.  In truth, the mechanics of the game may be overdesigned, or at least incorporated into the game far to early for a natural learning curve.  I cannot recommend this game, even for folks who like strategy RPGs.  It's a technical annoyance, as well as full of gameplay frustration.

_childDocuments_.review: Can't speak about Multiplayer.Not knowing the board game single player was somewhat tough to begin, but the card mechanics etc are soon learnt and one is very soon drawn into this game's somewhat tough tactical combat. Replayability is mainly using different class combinations, items, enhancements and card combos, the bulk of which are unlocked as one progresses through the game. RNG does play a part too, especially in combat where it can be quite cruel. Characters don't so much die but become exhausted and disappear from the scenario one's playing and are available again for any retry or the next scenario if the rest of the crew make it through; so there's no perma death or serious repercussions for a wipe out and the characters get to keep gold and XP etc they gained prior to the wipe. In that sense the game's user friendly. But it's a tough tactical game none the less. Unfortunately the characters are the bog-standard generic fantasy types with very little new about them for players of fantasy dungeon crawlers. Same can be said of the animations - the standard fare whose novelty wears off rather quickly. Music is pleasantly unobtrusive and weirdly makes my canary start singing; so anything that keeps her happy deserves a thumbs up despite the game's somewhat minor failings.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: If you like D&D, turn-based combat, or a good RPG experience, I highly recommend Gloomhaven. This is a board game adaptation that plays exactly like the physical game. I have gone through 2 1/2 campaigns in the board game with over 150 scenarios played over about 350 hours. The game is very well balanced at 2, 3, or 4 players and allows you to increase/decrease the challenge. This virtual version removes the hardest part about the physical board game, setup (can take about 30min in the board game) and monster movement (very specific rules that have a lot of edge cases to learn).The game has a different approach to most turn based combat which has a % RNG mechanism as it is all card based instead of % based. It will take some time to learn all the rules, how/why something happened and at times that can be a bit frustrating when something goes differently than you would expect. If you make the wrong choice, choose in the wrong order, or forget something it can be punishing just like most other turn based RPG's as there isn't always an a way to undo. The forgiving aspect however is that you are not expected to win every match/scenario the first time you play. When you fail, you keep any XP and gold you earned, can go back to town, level up if you reached the xp amount, and go back and try again until you succeed. LIkewise you can turn the difficulty down if necessary as well.This game is incredibly good and once you get the hang of it, it will start to feel natural after 2-3 scenarios. There are also over 15 classes to play and when each character reaches its objective, they retire and unlock a new class to try out. This allows you to become attached to the character but for only as long as you meet their goal meaning you will go through 3-4 through an entire play-through.The co-op is flawless and allows you to play with a friend(s). I highly encourage this as you need to play with at least 2 characters and learning 2 characters at the beginning can increase the learning curve. Overall expect a ton of hours of gameplay (each scenario is 1-4 hours with each player increasing time to play).

_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: Apparently according to the other reviews the problems the game currently has are recent.I have only recently started so I don't know what the previous state was but right not it is a problem.This game has one job above all else: be a digital copy of the boardgame.Not with a twist, not inspired by, as far as rules go, a 1:1 copy.And right now it just isn't.The boardgame is a precarious balancing act with a rulebook with 80 pages and it assumes all of the rules are being followed in its balancing.But the game straight up violates the rules time and time again.So even if you don't care about the boardgame, the balance of this very hard game is broken since the rules are not followed.One example: you can give yourself the ability to draw 2 cards instead of one and pick the better card for the damage.This is something you usually need to setup so it requires a decent payoff to be worth it,I have seen the game pick the card that is worse multiple times.So if you have the choice between +2 damage and a critical miss then the "advantage" you get is to miss.Right now, coming from the boardgame with experience, I can still finish the scenarios and nothing gamebreaking has happened yet. But I don't need to softlock myself to say: wait till the recent reviews start talking about fixes. And get the game on tabletop simulator.
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: Obviously I love this game! Gloomhaven board game is by far the best board game of all time and according to boardgamegeek ranking it is not even close.  The digital version is true to the board  game with very good graphics that visualize the characters and monsters in a captivating way. The new Guildmaster mode offers many many hours of gameplay and allows players to test different character combinations and item combinations. I would describe this mode as an XCOM-like experience within the gloomhaven universe, since you can freely choose which characters to take at a mission. The developers are dedicated and take feedback from community very seriously. They are very responsive to fans via the discord channel. Of course such a complicated game takes time to complete, it is a long process. The ways that all different character abilities affect each other and are affected by items creates the need for careful testing and constant bug-fixing. I am not at all bothered by the pace of development, every update clearly gets us closer to the end of early access which will coincide with the full campaign release. We even seem to be relatively close to the multiplayer release. I highly recommend this game both to all fans of the board game and all fans of turn-based strategy games.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent adaptation of the board game. Many of the bugs have been fixed with updates and a number of quality of life features have also been added over time. _childDocuments_.review: Oh boy... Gloomhaven is definitely going to be my "heartbreak game".I dearly loved the board game, definitely my favourite co-op. Alas, nobody is playing with me anymore. It runs ok enough on my Linux machine, so I started playing.Sadly, all the magic, mystery and appeal of the board game is gone. The PC version feels like a somewhat tedious puzzle game, and holds little to no charm for me anymore.Why did I give it a thumbs-up anyway? Well, I don't want to see people skip this gem just because it has lost some of its shine for ME. So, give it a go, see how it holds up for you. I still believe, that there's a solid and enjoyable game here, regardless of my own personal journey.

_childDocuments_.review: Best digital board game adaptation I've seen, even in its current EA state. Since I already played the board game, I don't care to replay the same campaign over again anyway, and Guildmaster mode is perfect as new and replayable content.Some requests: - option to speed up animations- during action resolution, a faster way to skip my turn entirely if I don't want to do anything- for singleplayer, UI option to see your whole parties' hands at the same time. _childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful, perfect adaptation of what turns out to be a rage-quit-inducingly difficult board game campaign...You know how once in a while a game seriously miscalibrates its difficulty levels, and makes it so hard to play than even when you swallow your pride and go down from 'normal' to 'easy' and then after that 'easiest', it still has you pulling your hair out in frustration? The Gloomhaven campaign is apparently one of those. However, I can't fault this as an adaptation. It's gorgeous, slick and I didn't notice any bugs in 77 hours of playing. The Guildmaster mode Asmodee have wisely added is significantly less brutal than the campaign and I would recommend it just for that mode. I just wish they'd gone one step further and adjusted the difficulty defaults for the campaign mode to bring them in line with other turn-based combat games.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's get the most important part out of the way first: this is a 1:1 recreation of the tabletop game with fancy graphics. The various tags like "RPG" ad "Strategy" are accurate in this context, but if you come here expecting a "video game adaptation" of Gloomhaven, you're going to find it stiff, limited, and disappointing.If, like me, you came here for a digital conversion of Gloomhaven, you're going to be thrilled. The eye-candy makes the game crisp and easy to follow, all the rules and updates are there and interactively explained. And the game a LOT of the bookkeeping for you. No more lengthy setup and pack down, no fumbling through rulebooks to resolve edge cases, no forgetting a step or losing a piece. This automation takes solo mode from "technically possible but boring as hell" to a legitimate way to enjoy the game, and makes multiplayer run super smooth - perfect for groups that can meet up online more often than in person.In short, I can 100% recommend this as a way to experience Gloomhaven the tabletop game, alone or with friends, and Gloomhaven is something that deserves to be experienced. The game itself is lengthy, with oodles of content, branching mission paths that require more than one playthrough, and the new Guildmaster mode is a great learning experience that massively expands on even that. Just be aware that this is a digital board game and may fall short if you're expecting the scope of a "videogame".
_childDocuments_.name: Gloomhaven

_childDocuments_.review: This review is for the digital implementation of Gloomhaven and not for Gloomhaven itself. Go read reviews on boardgamegeek if you want an in-depth discussion on class/monster/item balance and how vague/binary the city/road events are. The good:-At least you don't have to muck around with monster AI manually and setting up the board compared to regular gloomhaven.-The voice acting and music.The okay:-The board, monster, and player textures    -However it can get hard to tell what's an obstacle versus background flavorThe bad:-No Undo last action so long as no modifiers have been drawn, necessitating a round restart if you misclick a bottom move/top attack action.-Terrible Line of Sight tool that should just be hold button at a hex and it highlights tiles that are in/out of LOS -Hexes are sometimes highlighted showing that you can possibly target an enemy in an AOE attack, when you actually can't target them at all unless the card is fully enhanced for additional hexes.-Related but minor quibble is that you should just be able to click on an enemy when you are choosing an AOE attack and just be able to rotate around or let the player know if there is only one configuration where you can target the enemy you want.-Guildmaster mode having an unlimited cap on enemies unlike the boardgame, removing door rushing, and inadvertingly buffing enemies that spawn other enemies when they were already kill on sight -inability to switch host mid-session -There should be a setting to skip animations for enemies/players/allThe dealbreaker for actually playing this over tabletop sim:-The AI is very unoptimized at higher target/mini count, taking ~3 minutes per monster to act. With an average of 8-10 enemies on the board, you're sitting there for a good 20 minutes for some scenarios waiting until its your turn again with no player input and the fastest animation speed. At that point, you may as well just do the monster AI yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: this game can give a very negative first impression as the difficulty of the 'normal' level is off the charts hard for anyone who is not very familiar with the board game.  It is just excessively difficult and after failing the first missions over and over I think a lot of people will just stop playing and trash the game - that is what i almost did.  But I sucked it up and after reading a ton of complaints about the difficulty I bit the bullet and did 'easy mode'...  That is much more what I expected 'normal' to be -  and it is not easy at all, but i can do most scenarios in less than two tries.  It is like buying a chess program that only has AI setting for GM. I know, white knights will point out a video showing someone crushing the hardest difficulty, but i can point them to Magnus Carlson crushing GM level chess... most players are not Magnus.... As a new person to the 'world' it should be common sense to play 'normal' difficulty and win the early battles in a try or two. I think they are really doing the game a disservice by making the early game so difficult. I recommend the game because if you can stomach playing 'easy mode' it offers a lot of content and is a good value for the price - but i can also see giving this a big thumbs down as the first impression is terrible.  it also suffers from the tight restrictions on card use making it a must that you highly optimize every card decision - but the first run of 'dungeons' you will not have a perfect optimal move path etc. and so it is very punishing for first time thru a level as you will fail often due to running out of cards toward the end.
