_childDocuments_.review: The Rift Breaker is a good game brought down by a lack of automation.The basic gameplay loop is good fun with some nice simplification from a game like Factorio or Mindustry. You will spend most of your time in a loop of finding resources, expanding, researching, and then be directed to finding different resources so you can start the cycle over again. It's a fun if somewhat common game loop. I would consider this to be a solid 7/10 however it's innovations bring that score up to an 8/10. For example, the game simplifies the annoyance of having to cart around numerous resources through having everything connected through wormholes that connect all of your physical resources to each other. Strangely, you still need to build a bunch of pipe and power lines to connect things to each other but resources that you mine or gather are automatically transported around for you.Having said all of that, this game ends up at as a 6/10. At this point the game quickly becomes annoying to play due to several design decisions that detract from what is otherwise a fun experience. The following are the biggest gripes I have with the game as it stands at time of review.1. The game is missing automation when it comes to upgrading things. For example you'll manually run around back and forth upgrading a turret here, a solar panel there, or mine over there. This is okay but rapidly becomes annoying as you have multiple bases, a large interconnected network, or thousands of power plants and turrets that needs manual upgrading. For the love of God, please just let me set a minimum amount of resources to maintain and then let me prioritize automatic upgrading by building type. 2. Depleated buildings should really scrap themselves. Currently, the game will happily tell you that a Carbonium mine is depleted and wait for you to manually run over and scrap the thing. This is annoying as your base grows larger and larger. Most of the time I can't find the individual mine that's depleted or be bothered to truck halfway across the map to scrap an individual mine. Instead, the game just continues to alert me that a mine has depleted when it's been depleted for hours and hours in game. This leaves me thinking "I'm aware it's depleted and I don't CARE!". 3. The resource names are straight up silly. Carbonium? Ironium? You're playing a character from Earth you can just grab actual elements off the periodic table and use them. No need to invent names like this... You know, since you've kept using Uranium and the like.4. I never found a need to change out tower types. You can easily just stick to the basic turret and upgrade it all the way. Adding in hundreds of turrets is as effective as having 10 of the ones the game belives you should be using. There are other issues but those are the top 4 I have at  the moment. In closing this game is fun but at 16 hours played I've beaten it on the hardest difficulty setting, found it easy, and I'm probably done with this game forever unless they add something new to the gameplay loop.

_childDocuments_.review: looks great and is fun to play, no doubt about that, but its setting must be eligible for an award in tastelessness. You play as a member of a technologically advanced force that invades a foreign planet, starts strip-mining it for resources, and brutally slaughters any native inhabitant they come across. If that sounds like a scifi take on everything bad about colonialism and imperialism, it's because that's exactly what it is. It doesn't matter that your player character is constantly prattling on about wanting to find ways to coexist with the natives, and that she can have a last-minute change of heart. The former rings hollow because she never stops killing everything that crosses her path. The latter is pointless because it happens at the very end of the campaign, practically right before the credits roll.Long story short: if you're morally flexible enough to stomach 's blatantly xenophobic, human supremacist agenda, have fun playing it, and then take a minute to seriously contemplate your moral compass. Otherwise, don't spend any money on this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that has serious potential to be amazing, and if it had released as early access, then I would have recommended it.  Unfortunately, for a full release game, it suffers from lack of polish, major bugs, crashes, and lack of balancing in every possible category.  I'll break it down further:- Graphics.  This is probably the best aspect of the game, but even that is mediocre by modern standards.  The fact that the textures are not optimized causes low framerates on even high-end graphics cards.  The interface is buggy and inconsistent.  Sometimes things work and sometimes they don't.- Value.  This game is way too expensive for what you get.  There is, as of yet, not much content here.  It starts well but ends up very repetitive pretty quick.  Plus the fact that they skipped early access and went straight to full release leaves a bad first impression of the company.  I may be wrong, but based on normal small-studio trends,  I suspect that they did this so they can cash grab some 'Horse Armor' DLC asap.- Story.  The game uses its campaign mode as a tutorial.  Unfortunately, it fails to explain many of the basic concepts and controls.  And the main quest line is broken for a lot of people.  The Voice Actors for the game do a decent job, but scripts are poorly written.  Even some words are pronounced incorrectly.  It is difficult to 'fix' voice acting, so if you are going to use it, then you need to make sure to get it right the first time.  They mostly just use it to yell at the player that something bad is about to happen (which seemingly every 5 minutes or so).- Gameplay.  This game is basically just an updated re-texture of the classic arcade game 'Berserk'.  It has some elements of production and tower defense.  It is mainly a grindy slog of getting resources to make resources so you can put up defense towers to fight waves of alien monsters.  Those looking for a Factorio level of production won't find it here.  It is simplistic with resources getting where they need to go by space-time bendy magic.- Tedium and Frustration.  The game has these both in spades.  From awful weather events that break half your base and require lots effort to fix to the incessant, overwhelming waves of monsters that are intent on making everything you did for the last hour meaningless.  Most of what happens in the game is beyond the player's ability to control.  There is not much skill to be learned.  No real replay value, as the game wants you to build only what you need when you need it and punishes you harshly if you don't,  So it will be exactly the same every session.Overall, this game was not ready for full release and should have spent some time in early access.  Bugs are understandable on any game release, but the foundations have to at least be solid.  If things get better down the line, I may revise my review.

_childDocuments_.review: Decided an easier way to review is to look at some of the criticism and assess my thoughts. I'd like to be fair to a wide range of thoughts.  As far as what I like about the game. I think the action is still just as top notch as the previous game and makes a lot of marked improvements. The mobility options (Dashing, Double jump from the beginning) add a nice sense of momentum to the game. The story does seem to be more fleshed out so far. while people might argue that it's more obtrusive and pace killing than the previous game I for one am very biased as I will always favor a game with a good story than one without. I get it. DOOM isn't about the story. Some people want that constant moving forward. If that's an issue for you I understand but it isn't for me.     I'll admit I don't think it's a complete home run. I think a few of the battle Arena's are too cramped and narrow and some of the platforming feels a little awkward. These don't ruin my experience by any means but I figure it's worth mentioning. Aside from that I ran into a couple glitches but nothing major. Some of the criticism is how low you are on ammo. As with the last game this is definitely an intentional choice by developers to force the player to change their guns around and use every bit of their arsenal. Perhaps it's a little more unforgiving than the first game but I don't think it's to a level that people can't get used to.Also it appears some players seem to have a hard time keeping their health up in this game. I'll say this is my first time playing the game on Nightmare and I've died several times. It's definitely not an easy game but I believe the rush of victory actually getting through the fight and hitting the checkpoint is one of the best feelings you can get. I understand some people want a more streamlined experience but if that's the case I suggest either playing on the easier difficulties or play this game in short bursts to avoid burnout. Overall if you want an experience that imo is similar but also a noticeable improvement on the previous game than DOOM Eternal is absolutely a must play.EDIT: Upon finishing the campaign on Nightmare I can safely say this is easily one of the best experiences I've ever had  in a video game. The action is beyond perfect.I can understand why some people might have a problem with this game. IT IS HARD. There is no shame in playing on a easier difficulty. take your time try not to burnout and I guarantee this will be one of the best action games you can play.

_childDocuments_.review: I was trying to savour this game but I couldn't stop playing it whenever possible. Well it's over now(going back for collectables missed a few) and I gotta say I think this is even better than Doom 2016. Early game ammo was a problem and It took me awhile to get used to the new flow of combat, but once I hit the mid game I was having a blast. There isn't as much liberty in dispatching enemies as some might like, you need to play how the devs intended, but I prefer this because otherwise I'd prob had been lazy and just spam super shotgun like I did in the previous game. Rotating through weapons constantly was def an issue early game but once I upgrade my ammo cap I was able to use the weapons I enjoyed most more often but still there are just "the right tools for the job" on many enemies which is good and bad. I see alot of peeps hate the marauder but I actually really enjoyed the dodge and waiting for him to attack mechanic it's more intense than most enemies and requires patience. The level design was pretty linear for the most part but a huge open world doom game wouldn't be very good imo this is how it should be it's a good balance. The game looks and runs amazing no surprise there but always nice playing a game and just being fully immersed and not getting distracted by lost frames. I did encounter a few bugs I got stuck a few times and I lost 10 extra lives when escaping the base after the heart puzzle thing which was really annoying. I just kept respawning and was trapped in the lightning and couldnt move. Ultra Violence was the perfect difficulty for me not too easy and not super hard I felt very satisfied when I finished a tough battle/boss. The last boss and ending is very meh imo underwhelming mechanics and really drawn out. The ending just kinda happens like okay guess that's it lol. The music is dope as always the guttural chanting fit the games atmosphere perfectly. I see a lot of complaints about too much acrobatics and stuff but I thought it created some much needed space between fights. Everything considered; on the whole the gameplay is what matters with this and I had a good time. Rip & Tear 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Occasionally you hear about some rock band that goes into a studio to record an album, disappears from reality, then emerges pasty, malnourished and unshaven.  They mention how during the process they nearly literally killed each other as they deliberated on all the details and facets of the work.And the album? It turns out to be their finest work ever.Now I'm not saying Doom Eternal is id's best or most influential title; that's an indefensible opinion I'm not even sure I agree with.  What I am saying is that the product here is of a rare and unmistakable quality, and that's obvious going in.  These guys deliberated, sacrificed and yes, I imagine probably suffered to make something that's absolutely peerless.Instead of ranting endlessly (which I could do) about why I love this game, here's a few highpoints:I could go on further, and I may update this at some point.  But I think those are the highpoints.  I just completed my 5th run and 3rd Nightmare run, and I'm already itching to get back for more.There are a handful of pieces of media I've encountered throughout my life that I choose to re-experience on a regular basis.  I play Super Metroid once a year. I have music albums I've listened to hundreds of times.  I have books I've reread dozens of times.  I never get bored of them.Doom Eternal might have found a place beside them.Update Incoming

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love this game, I really do.  For the things I love, this game is hands down beautiful.  The scenes portrayed feel like something horrifying and crazy is happening, yet are painstakingly beautiful.  You can see that much work went into the graphics system and they knocked it straight out of the park.  The game engine runs smoothly and I did not have any types of stuttering or lag while playing where other games, even including Doom 2016, I had stutter in places that could kill you in game.  The music feels truly appropriate for each location you hear and it can make what would be a small uninteresting place enjoyable just from it alone.  The creativity of the creatures and scenarios you find yourself in also enhances this game in amazing ways.  Hell, even the multiplayer is a fun experience that even with the Demons being the more likely ones to win, playing as the Slayer is still enjoyable.  However, the actual combat mechanics, and to a much lesser extent, the story KILL all these experiences.  Let’s start with the combat as they’ll probably be some spoilers in the story line of this.  If you enjoy Doom 2016 and are coming straight from it, your experience of the game will almost certainly be harsh at best.  I understand that many people enjoy hard games and even I have enjoyed harder games such as Dark Souls on my consoles.  But I can say this coming from Doom 2016 myself and that is the difficulty spike between the two is absolutely absurd.  This is a game in which you are the Doom Guy, but within a life-based system around a large damage income and low health and shield recovery.  It ultimately will leave you feeling like some random guy who put on the Doom Guy armor and it’s the only reason you are even surviving rather then being the full-on Doom Guy who the demons of Hell fear so much.  You are expected to use every single alternate ability to it’s fullest and if you are not fast enough or familiar enough with these abilities, you will die quickly even on the lower difficulties.  This incentivizes you to have some of the highest reflexes I have ever seen required for a video game and can be very harsh on someone who is not quick on the draw.  Weapons of the game feel a bit down trodden.  The punch mechanic of the game is nerfed to be almost completely useless taking 10-20 punches to kill even a basic zombie that a single gunshot could remove unless you have a blood punch charged up.  In addition, there is no pistol so the two fall back weapons of previous Doom games are completely removed by these actions.  Your selections of weapons come back to some well-known Doom weapons, but their ammo reserves are so incredibly low that after a few shots you will find yourself running on empty and being unable to fight.  For best example, if you fully max out the ammo increase in this game your Shotgun ammo still does not even reach the first ammo upgrade in Doom 2016 for the shotgun.  In order to combat this, you are expected to make full use the chainsaw on small enemies which will then drop ammo.  It quickly becomes apparent that this is a painfully bad game technique as you are required to quickly kill the larger enemies while leaving the small ones alone. Any enemy in this game can deal serious damage to you so if you leave too many of the small ones around you will be over run as they keep spawning until the large enemies are dead.  However, if you kill too many you will find yourself out of ammo and most likely dying to larger enemies while hoping a small one spawns for a new ammo cache.  Enemies are enjoyable for the most part.  Some of the new additions such as Whiplash and Gargoyles are annoying as Hell itself, but they feel like good additions and fit well into the system.  Marauders though DO NOT and they ruin the experience of the enemies.  This here is a creature that does not fit into any rhyme or reason within the gameplay.  If you are too close, it shoots you with a super shotgun.  If you are two far it blasts you with energy.  If you are standing the perfect distance from it, it will attack you with an energy axe.  If this was all the Marauder did, it would be a strong enemy and a unique one to the game.  Nope, they decided to give it a shield that it can bring up and negate all damage at any time.  Think you’ll one hit kill it with a BFG or Crucible attack, nope it’s immune to both of these one hit kills.  So you have a very attack driven and defensible enemy now.  What more to give it?  How about a large amount of health requiring several shots to kill when you are able to hit it?  How about a summoned dog that spawns and attacks if too much damage is dealt to the Marauders shield by you or by other enemies.  This enemy felt like it should have been a boss fight and for one of the stages it is, but then they just throw it in as a casual enemy in locations with several others in a wave spawn.  There was no reason for this other than to artificially create a difficulty that could have been obtained without this enemy and still felt fair and normal in the game.  At last, the story.  If you do not want any potential spoilers, please end your reading here.  TLDR of this, the story went off the rails like a freight train having a head on collision with another train.  Starting this game, I loved the story.  It seemed as though it was following up from Doom 2016.  There were a lot of questions such as who really are these priests, who are the Makyrs, what exactly are the sentinels, etc.  This game started explaining and answer these questions, you got to see how the Priests behaved, what had happened to the Sentinels homelands, even explained the downfall of the Sentinels.  The story was going great.  Then you get towards the end of the game and you have to rescue Hayden.  Here, the story shifts from an interesting story to “wtf, you threw out everything you just setup”.  Hayden seems to know everything that happened to Doom Guy.  He knows the machine that was used to give him incredible powers, he stole Father to make Vega, he knows the prophecies of the Makyrs from all I can see and find in game were never wrote down or shared with the Sentinels or Demons.  Everything in this game points to him being the rogue Makyr that created Doom Guy, but yet we know from everything in Doom 2016, Hayden was born a human, made the robot suit which others helped work on, and transferred himself into it so he could be a deadly disease.  How is in Doom Eternal this robot is now something that no one has ever seen the technology for and they cannot access it? There are so many questions here that I can’t even begin listing them all as it makes so many contradictions to the Doom 2016 and most of the Doom Eternal storyline when it gets to the end.  Maybe if there was something more clean to this I wouldn’t have issues as I do with the story and all problems would be solely with the combat.

_childDocuments_.review: And with him lies our salvation. For as he gains in strength, so do they fall in numbers. The Priests command the armies to the North and South but he controls the fight. The inner circle of death is where he resides - hunting them at the far reaches of the earth and beyond. I am a believer now - I feel it is in DOOM that I have faith. The Slayer is the spear that stabs at the heart of our attackers, and those that would seek to harm us should feel warned - for there is only one dominant life form in this universe and it carries a steel barreled sword of vengeance. All hail the coming of the Destroyer - the Slayer's time is now.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This game is about only one thing: killing demons. It does that well enough to cover any other flaws, and the upgrades you get with each hour of gameplay multiply the fun. I can now recommend this game, especially to any fans willing to get past the first 4 hours or so.ORIGINAL NEGATIVE REVIEW:These are my very early impressions (<1 hour played so far):This feels like a modern adaptation of a 90s Doom game. 100% action, 0% story. Quite a departure from the deeper narratives of Doom 3 & DOOM (2016).Pros:+ Refines the fluid, fast-pasted arena combat from early games and DOOM (2016) - out of the gate you can double-jump and weapons don't need reloadingCons:- No story to speak of- Environment is just a backdrop / obstacle course; no narrative elements to give it meaning / depth- Strange ammo limitations / high reliance on chainsawIn summary, this is a 90s Doom game brought into the 20s. Maybe that's not a bad thing... just not at all what I expected.Will update my review once I've put at least 10 hours into the game.UPDATE #1 (3 hours in): After coming to terms with the lack of story and just focusing on enjoying this as a mindless arena shooter, I've been pleasantly surprised by the game's progression.New Pros:+ Environments, while remaining a soulless backdrop, vary a lot and are nice to look at+ A steady supply of codex entries begin to describe the world and your place in it+ A rechargeable grenade & flamethrower upgrade you unlock within the first ~2 hours resolve the most frustrating balance issue called out by many negative reviewers: the possibility of running out of ammo & chainsaw fuel and losing all means of dealing damage to foesNew Cons:- Combat is still fun, but there's clearly a 'meta' - not sure how I'd be fighting arachnotrons and cacodemons without the sticky bomb shotgun upgrade- I purchased an ammo capacity upgrade, hoping it would alleviate my biggest gripe with the game. It increased my shotgun ammo capacity from 16 shells to... *drumroll*... 18 shells. *:|Leaving the overall review as negative for now because it's still a huge step back from 2016.UPDATE #2 (8 hours in): I think I finally get it.

_childDocuments_.review: DOOM Eternal delivers spectacle and a solid core gameplay loop that is enjoyable for multiple playthroughs. The shooting of DOOM Eternal is by far the highlight. It is greatly improved and nicely balanced with its slew of new weapon mods, weapons, and abilities. The helps add to the game's telltale immense scope which it delivers plenty of. While the aesthetic and story are not nearly as strong as DOOM 2016, they serve well enough to deliver on the strengths of the title --- i.e. move fast kill big. However, the pacing is bumpy in some of the parkour sections. The multiplayer is fun but doesn't last for long.Overall: 4/5

_childDocuments_.review: 7.8/10, too much purple sludge.Being serious, it's a bit tough to recommend this game to just anyone. It's not as easy as just saying "If you liked the previous Doom games, you'll enjoy Eternal." It is fairly different from previous entries in a lot of regards. These changes, such as the extremely fast and aggressive ai, the low ammo capacities, and the new suit gimmicks are going to feel awkward at first. After a few hours of dedicated playing, the game should eventually click for you and will start to get really, really good.That being said, it's still not a game for everyone. If the sound of combat that is so hopelessly chaotic at first that you can hardly keep up sounds repulsive to you, perhaps Eternal just isn't for you. There's no shame in that, in the same way you shouldn't feel ashamed for not liking turn based combat for being too slow.

_childDocuments_.review: Played it for about an hour:+ Music, still pretty good+ Retro style: Feels like the older games+ Decent game: It runs well and set settings to current keyboard, something that doesn't occur often.- Doesn't grab you. Remember the previous game's start? Don't find that here- Too cartoony: Sure, still gore and stuff, but punching a zombie's head in it's torso and it looks at you big eyed? Nope. Glory kills which made previous well... glorious... are not satisfying here. That's a big part missing.- Tutorials everywhere. Getting in the flow? Nope, got to tell you what an objective marker is or how to spiderman climb. perhaps less later or able to turn off, but inside affraid I'll miss something.- Chainsaw reliant: Burn through ammo and forces to chainsaw (which doesn't work above grunt level). Punched a zombie for a minute, didn't blink. - Atmosphere: First one showed a story in the levelbuilding (corpses, ...). It's apocalyptic Earth and looks too bright and clean... All in all: Not a bad game, but not worth the current price. Just play the previous game till it gets a decent discount. Haven't noticed anything new yet (an hour in) that makes me want to play more, but urges me to play the previous game. More little stuff that each unnerves me a bit, but in the general keeps me from wanting to plow through it to reach the (possible) better game later.

_childDocuments_.review: What blows me away is that the game starts with story exposition right off the bat. The last one made it very clear from the onset that it was a game first and dealt with story with indifference. If you wanted to, you could stand by and listen or just plow right thru with glee as you painted the walls with demon. Now, however, it makes the point that there's a story to this world. Which again is perfectly valid, but instead of feeling optional the game makes it clear that it's now an integral piece to the experience.Fine! I can deal with that, no problem. At least it wouldn't be if the pacing didn't feel like it suffered from both it and other issues. The entire tutorial level uses every bit of bad game design to halt you in your tracks, which is ironic in a game with no walk, sprint, or reload buttons.Now, maybe I just suck but I felt like I ran out of ammo an infuriating amount of times while murdering demons. Part of me suspects it's because the game starts you off with just a shotgun, which I immediately started using on everything including the really basic shuffling enemies. Like the previous game, there are ammo boxes laid out across the levels, but your main refill comes from using the chainsaw. And when you're completely empty, the game automatically switches you to it, without warning.It's fun to get those up close kill animations as you slice a demon in half, that is if you have the fuel to do so. Regular enemies take one fuel but the larger enemies –that the game throws at you from the start– take all your fuel. I can deal with the paltry amount of ammo the game gives for each chainsaw kill a sit adds to the strategy of the game loop, the bigger the enemy the more ammo you get. But it's incredibly jarring to run out of ammo and then instantly teleport to 15 feet away. Even more odd is that my decision to run past those shuffling zombies instead of killing them comes down to the fact that they're immune to melee damage... They should drop with one punch, two tops! You can leave them alive as it seems they still don't count towards progressing to the next area. It's as if they were designed to just waste your ammo even quicker.Maybe it's just me, but there were a number of times that the level design felt somehow off. There were many times I'd go thru an area that had few enemies in it to suddenly an entire battle happening before me. And this stood out more when I got the first map download and saw that now there are areas that are discreetly marked as battle locations, even before you get to them. Sure, I could chalk them up to an in universe explanation that the random AI helper, VEGA, marked them ahead of time. But that doesn't stop it from feeling odd.In Doom, you knew that every area you went to was going to have enemies spawn all over the place, it was part of the fun. Often, more would spawn the further you progressed thru an area to always keep you on your toes. It made each encounter in each area feel carefully planned out by the developer to always keep a focus on the action. Likewise, the times where there weren't enemies in an area, served as breathers for you as you navigated around the world.In Doom Eternal, I just feel like I'm moving toward one direction, even if it occasionally snakes around itself. It's not like it shows me something I may have missed when I see the area I just came from, rather it confirms I've definitely moved forward.It all just serves to break the pacing that was established in the last game. Run forward, shoot, kill, repeat. Run forward shoot, melee kill, repeat. Now it's run forward, get halted by an on screen pop-up that tells you what to do, shoot, kill, run out of ammo, throw up from telekill, lose health while locked in kill animation, get a little of it back after the kill, repeat until you're out of ammo, you die, or everything else has stopped moving.To be clear, it's not as messy as that, there were many times where I could run around and clear an area the good ol' fashioned way. But the times where I got interrupted just seemed to persist. I don't need a hard cut to show me a door opening after I've cleared the enemies in an area. Especially not if there's an objective marker always on the screen! I don't need to be halted do the game can tell that the colored item I just picked up opens same colored door a few feet away from it.Sure, a lot of this could be forgiven and looked past as just standard player on-boarding. Eventually the game will drop the training wheels and let you go off to scrape your knuckles on your own. The game looks great and runs just as solid as the previous iteration. But that's where I think the heart of the problem stems from. This is a sequel to a fantastic game and it feels like many of the issues come from sequelitis. There's this feeling of an unquenchable desire from this game that it needs to be bigger and better than everything from the last one.I had hoped the game would take the approach of the last game and have a moment where it taunted you with new and complex mechanics before Doomguy gives it the finger and rushes off to stick his shotgun up a demon's butt. Instead it just keeps constantly stuffing your screen with objective markers and blips while pausing the momentum for some random cutscene or needless tutorial box.

_childDocuments_.review: THE GOOD-Another brilliant green flash etches across the angry red sky, accompanied by a bone chilling chorus of inhuman screeches as their twisted, motley flesh boils alive. Most of the unfortunate targets explode in a shower of blood and meaty chunks, leaving only a few bruised and bloodied nightmare spawn behind. Without considering the now slick ground, you steamroll headfirst into the nearest behemoth, hoping to briefly stun it. It pays off! The wretched thing staggers back as you launch your left fist into its beefy jaw. In a smooth motion, you rear up, grabbing hold of its shoulder with your right, then slam your arm mounted blade directly up through its chin to the top of its skull. Fresh blood drips down your arm. Perfection.The corpse burns away, but your next target is your only thought now. Its bloated form stands atop a nearby pillar, but it doesn't appear to have quite recovered from its recent deep tissue baking. Taking advantage of its slower reflexes, you deftly pull your rocket launcher from your back pocket and lock on. One, two, three steps backwards and... click! Just as many rockets burst forth from their steel cage and puncture the beast's massive core. Once more The Father has blessed you! The explosive rounds were just enough to stagger it. With a quick bound, you close the gap and plunge your blade deep into its chest. It returns from the meaty cavern with a most hearty decor. A dull grin spreads across the beast's face as you force its mouth open and spoon the still undulating organ in. Leaping back from the creature, there is a beat or two, then a stream of thick fluid erupts from its mouth and it collapses in a pool of its own blood.The final one catches your steely gaze as it attempts to flee around the corner of the bizarre ruins. Not today! You quickly swap for the only weapon for this particular job. Another delightful metallic click, followed almost immediately by a fleshy impact, seals the straggler's fate. By the Maykrs! Another perfect performance! You glide elegantly through the air towards your latest victim. Then, as though the crack of the retracting chain was a conductor's queue, you sweep its legs out from under it. The bowed creature, doing a perfect 180, goes head under heels. Heels which you grasp firmly and separate left from right, bottom to top. Glorious victory is yours once more!The second part-reboot, part-origin-story, part it-doesn't-matter-because-it's-time-to Rip and Tear already! is another worthy entry into the DOOM franchise that provides a visceral, well, Rip and Tear experience! One that cannot be described in mere human linguistic etchings. Every environment, every weapon, every movement, every demon, every shiny powerup is tuned and polished to a dazzling gleam for that most splendid, malevolent, artery reverberating violence. It screams and pulses with an energy that feeds one of the most driving, daring and dangerous feedback loops in gaming to this day.The three part (with DLC) campaign is a wild, drug trip of a journey across some truly spectacular vistas and awe inspiring biomes. Scenery which you will only be able to appreciate briefly between those juicy, intense, skill-testing encounters the series is known for. Only a heck of a lot more so, because what has been lovingly crafted this time around is a combat loop unlike any you have likely ever experienced in any game. Period. A combat loop that somehow manages to make even the previous DOOM entry, along with many other top tier FPS games, look like sloppy, mushy messes by comparison.From the re-imagined chain saw, to the absolute god of all overkill tools: the Super Shotgun's Meat Hook, DOOM Eternal's core gameplay is on another plane of reality entirely. With each demonic roar welcoming you into another pristine arena, you are drawn into an encounter that will clutch your heart and lungs in its fiery embrace until the last corpse hits the ground. If you managed to find a way to squeeze in a pause or two during encounters in the last game, such a thing won't happen this time around. The cast of red hot horrors has been reinforced so that every, nook, cranny and corner, is thoroughly covered. The only way to succeed is to find the quickest route to your next glorious skewering, whilst not being beheaded yourself. It's a deadly game of tag that demands you fly without wings, dance without feet, and make perfect shots without time to scope.I doubt it needs to be said, but the soundtrack and effects are orchestrated so well, they blend perfectly with the action. Rising and falling with each beat of the fight, your very blood will be pumped through your body as though it too is under the pursuit of the hellish hoards.DLSS, your friendly neighbourhood sharpening agent, makes a splash in this one. Perfect for squeezing every last bit of detail you can out of your monitor, it makes the awe inspiring architecture dazzle and gleam. Even more so when used in the super sampling configuration to drive the game above native resolution. The effect works so well, that you only notice shimmering jaggies while looking closely at the exceptionally slow camera pans in cut scenes. Who says you need a higher res panel?THE BAD-I can hear the fanbase loading their super shotguns already: what is a section like this doing in a review for this game? Hold the firing pin! The issues I found here were minimal and few, but worth noting.Amongst the many magnificent encounters, there were scattered a well paced helping of bosses. These almost always seamlessly added in a few unique mechanics to the established combat loop, often serving as introductions to tougher demons that would later become commonplace. There were two notable bosses, however that stood out in a bad way. One such boss played with the dynamic of slowly shrinking the playable area with a "floor is lava" style technique. The issue here is that it effectively blocked off the fodder demons, making resource farming nearly impossible, while also punishing mobility. Resource farming by intermittent quick kills, and remaining highly mobile, are core teachings of every encounter, so to have a boss mechanic actively punish these behaviours was beyond counter-intuitive and resulted in a notably less satisfying final victory.Another boss combined this restricted play area, though to a lesser extend, with an arena design that made movement too broken and disorienting. By relying solely on free fall and teleporting to maneuver, the arena did not provide sufficient line of sight, nor the briefest of gunfire runway. It was a cool looking fight, but it required a very different play style than the one the rest of the game so skilfully hones and trains you for.The correct way to amp the pressure, as shown in every other boss encounter, is to increase the number and level of the demons, along with ever more insane combinations (Marauder with a side of armoured Baron, anyone?), not by restricting core mechanics that have been thoroughly established and rewarded throughout the campaign. What can I say? They took some risks when tweaking the formula for bosses, most of the time they paid off quite well, sometimes they fell flat: becoming wholly incompatible with the established combat loop.THE VERDICT-Unless you simply refuse to play first-person shooters, Doom Eternal is an essential entry in your line up. It is a nearly flawless, unbelievably addicting, hyper speed artery accelerator from beginning to demonic end. Now, grab those fist-sized shells and eviscerate some demon abdomens, soldier!

_childDocuments_.review: This Doom title steers away from what made Doom 2016 great. You worry more about lack of ammo more than anything else. I like to compare the levels I played to Mirror's Edge in a way, since the levels have a parkour feel to them. If you miss a secret and progress too far, you cannot go back. Then there's the Anti-Cheat implementation. Bethesda is a toxic gaming company with no morals beyond profits.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall the game is great. It takes everything that you loved about Doom 2016 and turns it up to 11. The way the developers designed the game really makes you think before you rip and tear, but still manages to keep the fast paced over-the-top feel that we love.... for the most part that is (I elaborate later in the review.) It offers more of a challenge than Doom 2016 as well as better more fluid traversal. The only thing I dislike is the moments that halt the fast paced demon slaying gameplay Doom is known for. These moments include the purple goop which slows you down and takes away your jump and dash abilities (which are essential to combat.) Under water traversal which has poisoned water and for some reason is difficult to jump out of. Lastly we have the Marauders. In a game that prides itself on its fast paced over-the-top combat they throw in an enemy that completely slows the combat down, making you wait for an opening to attack him. How this enemy type got past play testers is beyond. They are by far the worst thing about this game. Other than that the rest of the game is phenomenal.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a 45 yo father, probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am a single father to my Son, who is 14 now. My son got this game for Christmas in 2021 from his uncle, so we installed it on his computer and he started playing. By the end of the week he had 24 hours on this game. This was horrible for me, as it was already hard for me to find ways to spend time with my son, as he is always out with his friends or just watching YouTube. So i decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. I loaded into the game, picked my character and world and started playing but I was stuck on what you where supposed to do. I asked my Son for help and he hosted a game for me to join. I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my Son since my wife had died. This game has ever since brought me and my son closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house together as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my Son many happy memories.

_childDocuments_.review: It's DOOM 2016, but better (the single player). It's exactly what you'd expect, from blood and gore, to smooth and well designed Quake style gun play. It has introduced a new method of platforming with the addition of dashing and monkey bars to swing on, which brings an opportunity for colossal level size.  The new guns and gun designs are fantastic. My only complaint: The multiplayer is worse than 2016's. 2016 had a great PVP mode with large teams. Not sure why snap map was removed, now that the level design has become more complex, but oh well. It's DOOM, most don't come for the multiplayer.Fantastic game
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM Eternal

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest, I enjoyed DOOM 2016 so much more then this one. But the reason is simple. The fights were not for me.This is such a fast paced game that I just couldn't keep up. I know that there are people who like this sort of stuff, I don't. 2016 Doom had it figured out much better imo. When playing it I felt like a monster, absolutely destroying everything in my way however I pleased. In Eternal you have to juggle through all the weapons you have, and my god it's so many of them. You'd think that's good, but if you HAVE TO use them all you quickly run out of fingers and brain power to manage that. As I said, it might be just me, so I completely understand that someone else will think the game was perfectly balanced, as all things should be.In terms of upgrades, collectibles and stuff to unlock this game made it really well. There's a lot of stuff to look for, collect, grind and generally do. It was cool.Tthe problem is that I don't really want to go replay the maps, cause I didn't enjoy fighting in this game. Puzzles were fun. Not fighting. And that's essential. So yeah.Story I don't think matters, it was whatever, the end boss was a cutie tho.Overall I think it is just DOOM 2016 squared, some people will love that, probably most of them, but I just quite didn't fit in. Still was fun. Just not as much.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is solid, although not as fun and focused as Doom 2016, and with a UI and front facing design trying too hard to be quake that's really unpleasant to look at.Can't recommend buying it on PC, after they patched in a rootkit anti cheat that's a severe security concern for the user.  My main problem with it is that it was patched in after release without notice.  I wouldn't have bought the game if I had known Denuvo was included.  I'm sitting at more than 2 hours played so I can't refund it, but I uninstalled.

_childDocuments_.review: The more I play this game, the more I dislike it.  On a technical level this game is fine. Graphics and performance and audio-visual design are great. However, the gameplay isn't nearly as fun as DOOM (2016). The pacing of the game just seems off. The combat can be fun, but the intensity of it is exhausting and then it all comes to a screeching halt with annoying platforming sections. So you are either doing 120% hectic combat or dumb, irritating platforming. I was super excited for the game. But now I find I don't want to go back and finish it, because the gameplay feels like an irritating hassle rather than the lighthearted expertly paced fun of Doom (2016). Very disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom Eternal! The follow-up to Doom 2016, possibly the greatest Doom game ever made, possibly the best reboot ever made. Nothing could possibly--I'll rip the band-aid off and say I didn't enjoy Doom Eternal. I wanted to. I really wanted to. But I didn't.Eternal is an unbalanced, jumbled mess. When it shines it's great, but you have to fight the game for those moments. In a game about power fantasy, I never really felt powerful, just harried. They give you a ton of neat equipment items to use, but it isn't about getting to use them, you -have- to use them. Constantly. Perfectly. Or you die. They aren't a carrot, they're a stick. And there's a lot of them, plus all the weapons and their attachments, and you'd better be using the right one at the right time or you get the stick. It's too much crap. You can get used to it all, but it's still too much crap.The lives system is a thing. It's pretty bad, and lead to poor game design. From what I can tell they use them as an excuse to throw combat balance away. Enemy damage is incredibly unforgiving, your ammo supply is laughably small, and enemies feel like they take way too much to put down. According to the game though, it's all totally fine because you can regain armor, health, and ammo more-or-less at-will. But what it really comes down to is you, the Doom Slayer, render of demons, will run away and hide and hope you can set something on fire and punch it where no one is looking so maybe you can get some more hits in before you repeat the cycle. This is made more frustrating by enemy AI, which is good but has a strong desire to pin you into a corner and body-block you. With the game's design of "Move or Die", you tend to just randomly die from this before you know what happened. But hey, you have extra lives, right?Another issue I have is level design. Eternal is thus: jumping puzzle, arena, jumping puzzle, arena, repeat until level is over. I think I spent more time playing at parkour than I did killing things, and the jumping puzzles are generally awful or the intended direction is poorly shown to the player, which doesn't help. The arenas are their own issue, which flows back into the general problem Eternal has - balancing. They only balanced for the arenas, so everything is feast-or-famine. You'll be near dead, then back to half health. Out of ammo, then some ammo, now near dead again. It's this constant, wild, janky sea-saw of have and don't have, and it just feels awful to play through. They saw those big, keystone moments of awesomeness Doom 2016 had and went, "what if we just made the whole game like that and threw everything else out?" Great in theory, but anyone old enough to buy and eat nothing but cake realizes it's a bad idea. Apparently Id didn't get that memo.For good stuff, the story was neat. I liked learning about Doomguy, though I'm on the fence about Doom's protagonist getting a more filled-out backstory. Still, it was fun. Not as good as 2016's demonic recounting of how he tore his way through Hell, but still fun. The music was decent, I didn't really notice anything that stood out to me other than maybe the title music. Nothing unseated BFG Division or anything. The areas were interesting, it was pretty cool to see something other than Mars and Hell.Doom Eternal was a pretty big disappointment for me. Considering the other reviews it's pretty obvious I'm in the minority, and that's okay. I really didn't enjoy the experience, but that doesn't mean other people are wrong for having a good time with the game. Honestly, I wish I got the same vibe others did. I was looking forward to a great time.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to begin by saying that the single player campaign of this game is phenomenal and, were it not for the decisions made with this most recent patch, it would quite easily be my favorite game so far released this year. The people responsible for the artistry and functionality of this game should be proud, because it's very, very good.Regrettably I cannot recommend it as long as it is bundled with Denuvo Anti-Cheat; to boil the issue down for those not technically inclined, DAC is an incredibly over-zealous and risky program that operates at and requires access to the very lowest levels of your computer's functionality. You might ask why this is risky; surely a huge company like Bethesda and a friendly developer like id wouldn't intentionally bundle a dangerous program with their product?DAC operates at what is called 'ring-0' or 'kernel' level, watching every input on your device for evidence of potential cheating. This sounds great, surely no cheater could get around a watchdog at the very core of their computer! Unfortunately, this also represents a risk to your PC's security and privacy; because of the way Windows restricts kernel-level access, DAC must be launched as a service, a constantly-running piece of software that is obfuscated from the user.One of the properties of a service, regrettably, is that it's much more difficult to shut down than an application. Because of this, when you launch DOOM Eternal with the latest patch applied, DAC starts...and does not stop when you close DOOM Eternal. Not only does this represent a security vulnerability (it's pretty easy to hijack a service designed to monitor inputs and use it to collect, say, password inputs) it also represents a privacy vulnerability (even if it's not sending any of that data across the internet, it's still recording it, and that recording can then be seen by any program that knows where to look) and a draw on your computer's resources. It's worth mentioning that DAC has a history of overdrawing on computer resources and causing things like kernel instability (a problem that can only really be solved by a clean reinstallation of your operating system).With all of these things in mind, I have to strongly recommend against the purchase of DOOM Eternal, at least until such time as this root-kit in the guise of an anti-cheat program is removed. DAC has an incredibly bad reputation in the data security community; I cannot imagine that anyone with any understanding of data integrity or security was involved in the decision to package such a dangerous and unstable 'solution' to the problem of cheating into this product.TL;DR: There's a really bad sub-program packaged in with the last patch; I don't recommend spending money on this game unless and until it's removed.

_childDocuments_.review: could once claim to be my favourite game in its venerable series, but it’s now going to have to share that spot with . The MO of this sequel is expansion; there’s simply more of everything, for better and for worse. The previous system of gunplay peppered with chainsaw kills and finishing moves that respectively recover ammo and health has been augmented with new melee options and a shoulder-mounted projectile launcher that includes an armour-restoring flamethrower. Furthermore, the incredible variety of enemies have been given unique weaknesses, and the system has been tuned to ensure your entire arsenal is useful, if not crucial for survival. It’s pushing just up to the complexity limit for a game this fast-paced – most of my early deaths were caused by choice paralysis more than anything – but the result is FPS gameplay that’s undeniably gripping from start to finish.The production values are also top-notch. Aside from the general brutal splendour of the visuals, the extensive “destructible demon” physics and animation variants for melee kills go a long way towards keeping players engaged. Additionally, the industrial metal soundtrack is one of AAA gaming’s best, with pulse-quickening riffs and an uncommon electronic dissonance that distinguishes it from its peers. The controls work perfectly as well, which is surprising considering all of the new aerial movement abilities they have to accommodate. The image of the Doom Slayer gaily swinging from bars and climbing walls is an unusual one, and, along with an increased emphasis on story, it’s emblematic of a shakier tone this time around. The latter inclusion is especially misplaced, because the game isn’t very good at  its story.Finally, the standard multiplayer offerings of  have been replaced by a chaotic asymmetric setup that attempts to replicate the “one vs. horde” feeling of the campaign. It’s where several of Eternal’s new ideas (as opposed to ideas that are just new to ) have been placed, so it’s a lot more interesting than its predecessor. Unfortunately, it’s also ludicrously unbalanced; almost every match I played ended in a blowout.

_childDocuments_.review: You can see the framework in DOOM Eternal for a game as great, if not better, than it's previous incarnation. Then the publisher stuck their thumb in it and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ it all up. Right away, the game felt off. It didn't need a battle pass, cosmetic character options, and the combat had changed to make glory kills an essential part of each combat, which gets really repetitive really fast. The story tries to be serious, and continuously undercuts itself with extra lives, and software that gives you "cheats" when replaying a level. And the option to replay a level is done in-game as well from a hub world where you can get the latest updates from Bethesda. Then, when it came out this week that Mick Gordon had his soundtrack remixed without his permission, it all fell into place. These decisions that made the game feel off were not made by the development team, but by the publisher. So, at this point, I can't recommend it in good conscience. There are significantly better ways to spend your money.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fresh migrant from the Bethesda Launcher, I feel it’s my job to add yet another review to the pile and let everyone know my feelings about Doom Eternal. I obviously had high expectations when I bought the Collector’s Edition to get a cool helmet that doesn’t fit my head and a cassette tape of weird monster sounds, but at least now I don’t have to look at the Bethesda Launcher anymore.However, to light things up and get them nice and controversial, let me begin by saying – I think Doom Eternal is better than Doom 2016. Doom Eternal is Better Than Doom 2016: That’s a lot to say because I loved Doom 2016 for its ability to revive the franchise and deliver the feel of the classic raucous and visceral experience while still bringing something entirely new to the table. It’s a game that made the Doom Guy into the Doom Slayer and didn’t even stop to let you ask why. Doom Eternal didn’t have to build that transition though. The developers could have just taken the template they established in 2016 and slapped more content on it and few would have complained. Yet, they chose to craft a game that demanded more interaction, rewarded skill and practice, and paid off by capturing the vicious excellence of the previous game while giving dedicated players the challenge they always wanted.Doom Eternal expands on the skills of the Doom Slayer by giving him tools like the flamethrower and the blood punch – while also adding weak points to the familiar set of enemies. They also created level design with much more verticality and gave the Slayer a significant increase in maneuverability. These features let the player learn to use these tools skillfully to create a much richer gameplay experience. On top of that, the combination of an expanding base/hub that steadily unlocks with your success and an exploration of a still relatively small but interesting story made the game addictive almost immediately. Even with its overwhelming assault on the senses and significantly increased challenge, it was hard to put down.Of course, since my initial rampage through the campaign and subsequent cooling over the past two years, I haven’t explored recent changes as thoroughly. My early experiences with Battlemode were enjoyable and gave me quite a few additional hours in the game, but overall, it was clunky and involved an unexpected amount of lead-in time for only three players. It almost seemed as though you’d spend as much time picking characters, loading, watching intros, and waiting to start as you would in the actual match. Sometimes the inactive parts were even longer if one side was particularly skilled (or unskilled) – which was fairly common. “Best of Five” would usually just be a three-match sweep that might not even make it that far with rage-quits.Playing Battlemode more recently, they have taken some steps to improve the flow, like eliminating the “vote” section for rematch or shuffle which rarely ever resulted in an additional match. However, time is almost always the enemy of a healthy multiplayer population and that means longer waits for matches, a higher chance of mismatched skill levels, and sometimes matchmaking giving you nothing at all. Even with the additional Demon class and tons of balancing changes, it’s still a dice roll whether you’ll get a competitive match with shifting tactics or a demoralizing stomp.Luckily though, id Software added more than just some updates to their sole multiplayer mode. They’ve also tossed in a few more extremely challenging master levels as well as a new “Horde Mode.” This was the replacement for the “Invasion” mode which would have worked like the familiar Dark Souls invasion where a player would show up in your game to try to kick your ass – except this time with Demons. The Horde Mode, however, sort of works vaguely similar to Doom 2016’s Arcade mode, but is more focused on ‘arena’ fights and a limited variety of events like platforming, coin collecting, and demon blasting under some unique circumstances. You’re also required to progress through this mode with limited weapons that unlock as you go. All of your actions in this have point values with the goal of achieving a worthwhile final score – though given my score’s placement on the leaderboards, I definitely need some practice.  However, this provides a unique challenge for those that have become intimately familiar with the campaign and master levels.With these noteworthy changes, the already robust core game, the two story-centric DLCs released, and of course, a soul-melting soundtrack, Doom Eternal went from GOTY level of quality to something truly legendary. It’s great to see a sequel that breaks new ground rather than safely iterates to prevent shocking their playerbase. Even though it lost some of the gritty feel from the original, it gained so much gameplay variety and overall breadth that it was a worthy tradeoff. My only hope is that id Software continues to be unafraid of the scrutiny that comes with change and builds the future of this franchise with as much of a focus on powerful enthralling gameplay. Until then, we can all continue to enjoy the rich game that Doom Eternal has become.

_childDocuments_.review: DOOM Eternal is a solid sequel to DOOM 2016 in that they avoided doing more of the same and created a unique product that completely changes many of the gameplay mechanics found in its predecessor.  Limiting your players ammo, forcing you to constantly be switching between weapons, power ups, and evasive tactics trains you to battle massive hordes of demons, and eventually massive bosses WITH massive hordes of demons.The level designs are brilliant and I know people say they didn't like some of the platforming in the game, but honestly some of the most fun I had was trying to find secrets just like the DOOM of old.  The settings you play in feature all kinds of neat little details and you can tell the level designers had fun putting the frills in.The weapons all feel great but of course running out of ammo quickly is always a burden, but like I said, it mixes up your tactics enough that you're constantly performing in a ballet of death to come out on top.  The Fortress of Doom was a nice touch and overall the game feels like a bigger achievement than DOOM 2016.In the end, was it fun?  I certainly had plenty of fun, exciting, and nail biting moments, but there were also some heavy moments of frustration the last few levels.  They really crank up the difficulty and I ALMOST knocked down which mode I was on, but I prevailed.  Is this a great sequel?  Absolutely.  An improvement on the last game in an unexpected way.  Will it be for everyone?  Absolutely not.  The difficulty and high skill demand may turn people off.Overall, a great installment for the DOOM franchise.  Just don't expect to breeze through this one!8/10 Doomslayers would rip and tear again

_childDocuments_.review: 22 hours into the game, played on Hurt Me Plenty. Read almost all the complaints and I'll advocate for both sides. But I'm mostly on the side of not particularly liking the changes.I think Doom Eternal is by no means a bad game. Not at all! But... there are so many small changes the game could do to make it go from good to great. Let's talk about those issues people have. Keep in mind these gripes are very much subjective, you'll either hate or love them but those haters can and should arguably learn to adapt beyond 2 hours of the game. 6 hours +, not enjoying it? Completely understandable.The great chainsaw ammo economy:Major hint: Chainsaws regenerate 1 bar all the time.Yeap. That's a thing. Where other games have reloads with individual weapons your chainsaw is your reload.  After playing the only available master level over 4 times, clearing up and collecting half the missions again and adding up my ammo capacity it does feel like a problem that gets mitigated over time. What doesn't however is the fact that I need to use the chainsaw now, instead of complementing my combat flow it's just something that I HAVE to integrate into my combat flow. No, I can't just use it when I want since non fodder require 3 bars to use it up but I guarantee you my ammo will run out before I can fully utilize all the ammo that the larger enemies can give. So the gripe I have with the chainsaw is that I can't just use it when I feel like I wanna do something badass or end off my fight with a shabang because I will most likely not have the chainsaw fuel (x3 bars) to kill off said large enemies.Weapon variety and versatility:On my first whole playthrough of HMP outside of the cacodemons I thought "eh, screw enemy weaknesses, if I get em. I get em. who cares". I'd occasionally try to burst a revenant's jetpack every once in a while but 7/10 of the times I'd just ya know, brute force my way down to his HP.However after trying the whole weakness system I found it being too effective. Enemies that were major threats to your HP like Mancubus, arachnotrons quite literally get there threat levels down by 80% I wish I was exaggerating but everytime they spawned you can easily decrease there threat with 2 placed Precision bolt rounds. That 7/10 of the times went from 10/10 times for every revenant, mancubus, arachnotron. This just gives off that feeling where some weapons are far more effective than others in almost every situation. If I were to give a good example of making you choose different weapons without completely overshadowing others it'd be the Doom Hunter. He's really weak to plasma weapons but he's not completely useless when you exploit his weakness either, he can still pose a threat until he's dead. Can't say the same for Mancubus', Revenants or arachnotrons. Map design and "linear" design:Another critique that people have of Eternal is that it feels more linear or straight foward compared to 16. Which... I might agree with. MIGHT. I haven't played 16" since 2 years ago so I'm going based off my memory. But I do recall that I could deal with certain maps like the Foundry in ways that I wanted to deal with first, do I deal with the gore nest here first or the one over there. Or maybe get a key card way over there. It was mostly up to me. With Eternal sure the maps are bigger but they're not always better, you go slightly off the path, invisible wall, wanna jump over to that section that has something you can land on? oh no no my friend lose HP, get back and spawn where you just started, or spawn back up even further back. In a game where it encourages you to go off the beaten path it also feels like you're being hand held by another person in that regard. "Try exploring over there b-but wait! that's too dangerous, come back here right now young man!" is what I felt like most of Doom Eternal's exploration is like. However, the actual polish and look of the maps is 10/10. Each place looks varied with myriads of scenery, gothic castle areas, Warframe's void like towers, hell on earth. A lot's there in terms of map variety so you don't get the samey feel of the orange mars and orange hell in 16".I brought most of these critiques up since I completely understand both sides, while I like the game, I really do, I just can't bring myself to enjoy it as much as I did 2016. Overall a 7-8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an decent game, but I won't recommend it to Doom2016 fans or for impulsive purchase. Wait for it to be on a sale.You start the game and feel like you missed Doom2017, Doom2018 and Doom2019. I am... on a ship? Darth who? Maykir what? Old King Cole ghost says what? Ghost knight gives me Oreo for what?Okay, maybe future will shed a light on all that obviously-meaningful-and-important stuff. But the game gives you tl;dr pages written in CAPS LOCK using the font that was truly forged in the hell: my eyes start to bleed and game tells me that I should do my homework as those questions will definitely be in the finals.... and then the game starts pulling tounge-and-cheek jokes making me even less involved in that obviously-meaningful-and-important-lore. And yes, some of the jokes are spot on, but you can't expect player to take anything seriously at that point.   - Bethesda, can I reap and tear?- Yes, but only after you do your chores And there's a lot of chores that always is going to interrupt the flow of game. Worst offenders are mandatory parkour sections. You all sure loved that section from Doom 2016 where you climbed that tower that felt like it was an eternity. Now you'll get that a plenty.  Chainsawing in Doom2016 was like a christmas. Now it is just another chore to add to your list. Ammo capacity (even it can be upgraded) is too low for long rip-and-tear sessions, regular demons are bullet sponges, so you have to keep a couple of cannon fodder in reserve to avoid sad end with 1v1 against mancubus with 1 pip of fuel and no ammo. Speaking of bullet sponges, now they all have "weak spots" and "recommended strategies". But in reality that means if you don't want to play by the rules "cacodemon eats a nade, dude with shield eats a plasma" you'll get punished by spending LOT of resources and damned to perform even more chores. Doom2016 was all about freedom.Finally, not to mention Bethesda Online Services that are constantly getting offline and you got interrupted from your single player campagin to see that modal "Oopsie, bethesda is bethetic again, online services won't be accessible. Okay?" just to close it and get back to the game.* * *Again, this is an decent game - the pacing could be suffering at times, but arena fights still has that doom 2016 drive.  of new gimmicks are fantastic addition to the combat like  blinks or meathook swings. Backgrounds and arenas are stunning in design. New enemies are really fun. But because of aforementioned reasons, you might be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome and fun game with a lot of action and fun game mechanics.I personally love the weak point system in that there is more strategy in your fights. The game  also supports the idea of quick-switching in fights, which is a very fun mechanic and works very well with the flow of the battles. I also think that the levels all looked great and had a nice atmosphere to them.But I have to say, that the last two boss fights were the biggest letdown in the game for me.I played this game for the first time on Ultra-Violence and throughout the game, I felt the difficulty was just right for me and was very consistent. But the Khan Mayker boss was laughably easy. Simple quick-switching between the Precision Bolt and the Ballista and the fight was done in like 3 minutes.. Also the Maykr drones on headshot drop so much, so health has been never at issue.The final boss, Icon of Sin, felt very tedious and wasn't much fun. I might just not that good at this game, but I couldn't concentrate on any of the fights. Throughout the fight you have to destroy the armor of the boss and then just shoot it.Simple enough.But the game constantly spits enemies at you, which in the first phase is not that bad. But in the second phase, the game throws at you bunch of annoying Heavy demons and you become overwhelmed very quickly. And of course the boss attacks too, so that makes dealing with these heavies super frustrating. It’s really just a 20 minute clusterfrick that isn’t fun at all.  The rest of the bosses such as the Gladiator or the Doom Hunter were great fights and not too overwhelming as the final boss fight.Ignoring those two bosses, the game is absolutely worth the money and I would definitely recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom Eternal is a MASSIVE improvement to Doom 2016 in almost every way, i was expecting it to be good, but not this good. It takes everything 2016 did and improves on it dramatically. The fights are so much more intense, and there's a lot of fun fanservice for old school Doom fans.PROS:- Movement is quicker, you can dash around arenas now to dodge attacks.- The maps are HUGE, this can be a detriment to some, but every level is different so there's a lot of variety. It's not like 2016 where it's almost all on mars.- The game is more challenging, you'll die a lot more.- Fights are shorter than in 2016, so you're not stuck in an arena forever.CONS:- Some platforming sections are tough as hell- You get bombarded with tutorials at the very beginning so it can be hard to remember everything.9/10 game though.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a typical shooter. It deviates from the norm even more than doom 2016 did, but it's an excellent game nonetheless. Feels almost like a character action game like that of Devil May Cry or Metal Gear Rising, in that you have so many unique weapons and abilities and actual mastery of the game comes from understanding and being able to weave between them at a moments notice.EDIT: Game completed, and I think my favourite thing from it all was the set pieces and level design it had me run through. Lots of tiny secrets here and there. There's some set up for the DLC story campaigns which is kind of disappointing, I was hoping they'd be proper optional content as opposed to potentially extremely important story details, but we'll have to wait and see on that front. The game definitely gets easier at the halfway mark, and its lowest points are those first few levels where you don't quite know how to stay in the gameplay loop. Just remember, the Chainsaw button refills at least 1 pip all the time. Don't ever hang onto that pip unless you're intentionally collecting fuel to one-shot a heavy demon. It's a free ammo button. USE IT.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay has changed up a little bit from its predecessor with a couple of new features.1.  It now has a minimum of 1 gas that is always regenerated. This encourages the use of the chainsaw on smaller enemies throughout the game to gainammo back, especially with lack of ammo compared to 2016, which I personally liked a lot. 2.   The dash feature adds a new level of maneuverability to the game where you can get out of a sticky situation very quickly,or use it to your advantage in some of the various platforming sections in the game. I found myself using this feature a lot in the fighting sections of the game. Another movementrelated change that was added was the hook on the super shotgun, with this feature you can hook to enemies from certain distances away and use that to swing around the arena to gainanother tactical advantage. This feature was so cool to use as you were flying around the map with your dash, and double jump. 3.  one of my personal favorite features in the game is the utilization for EVERY weapon in your arsenal. In Doom 2016 I found myself resortingto the Super Shotgun and not using anything else in my arsenal, unless I ran out of ammo. In Doom Eternal I constantly was switching weapons, utilizing every weapon for certainsituations and I absolutely loved it. I felt variety and its great. Especially with how enemies now have weak points you can destroy to your advantage. ranging from the rockets on the revenants,the cannons on the mancubus, and even the plasma shields on the demon soldiers. A very welcome feature to me.  Does it live up to the hype Doom 2016s soundtrack gave us? The music in Doom Eternal is something I’ve been anticipating since Doom 2016s soundtrack mesmerized me. This soundtrack, in my opinion, is even better than its predecessor. And that is saying a lot, because Doom 2016s soundtrack was my favorite videogame soundtrack.With the haunting screams from the Metal choir ringing in the background, To the glitchy, ear deafening Djenty guitars that Blair over your demonic carnage. Mick Gordon has somehow outdone himself and it is insane. This soundtrack is something I will be blasting constantly once I’m able to get my hands on a physical or streaming copy.  I’m not going to get too much into the story, but I thought it would be good to at least say something about it. Hell has now invaded earth, Doom guy must stop it. That’s the gist of what I’m going to go into the story itself. It was cool to hear some more voice acting, and even see the Doom slayer himself in some cutscenes but overall, I don’t think a lot of people come to Doom for the story which is fine, because for what it is, it’s not bad! And the most important thing is it doesn’t take anything away from the gameplay. I personally thought it was fun and a cool change of pace to the simplistic story of Doom 2016.Edit: still relevant and even better than how the game launched + ray tracing!

_childDocuments_.review: Well, how could they possibly beat the astonishing predecessor which Doom (2016) was?I didn't know but they somehow did it! Doom Eternal is bigger, fast, fatter, richer and more badass in nearly every aspect compared to its prequel. The gameplay, consisting of fast action with many different weapons, mechanics and enemies, is one of the smoothest i have ever played in an egoshooter. They also hit the perfect sweetspot between brutal modern reality and arcade-style shooter like Doom 1 and 2. I especially had fun with the many unlockable weapon mods, challenges, cheats and soundtracks which felt like a few thousands! Only the story leaves a bit to be desired, but lets be honest, who plays Doom for the story anyway? :D Still, the backgroundstory and anecdotes we got fill the great world of the "new" Doom universe really well.The multiplayer is way better than the Quakecopy from the 2016 franchise release as it's build around a new "one Slayer vs. two Demons" gamemode, which works quite well. Yet is still recommend this game exclusively for the great singleplayer!9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;Dr I think it's an evolution upon DOOM 2016 on most of the aspects, and overall an amazingly entertaining game.I waited to finish the game once before posting this, so I can be as fair as possible with ID Software's work. Every game mechanic was required in order to rip and tear properly, but I feel the gunplay has reached an optimized flow on all the difficulties - my run was on ultra-violence and it felt challenging but still fun.I find it more fun, more violent, more aggressive and more polished than the previous installment. The level design is opened and enlarged, the environments are beautiful. The music is as good as our headphones allow. The story is much developed and I found myself interested in the lore codex. The mechanics may require attention at first but you will find you need every bit of armor and ammo you can muster :) The animations are smooth and fast, even the wall grab feels good. Mobility has been upgraded via double dash combined with double jump, dash recharge, swings and even a meat hook!Doom Eternal allows for aggressive or passive style of gameplay, since every gun has 2 different upgrade paths and a mastery perk. There are a lot of secrets throughout the game; you will find some personal customization in your homebase and even an old school PC :)P.S. I am glad to see the continued support in content, from the dev team.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM Eternal

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best FPS I have ever played and the best modern campaign-based FPS in existence. I dont compare it to the multiplayer FPS giants like COD, CSGO, PUBG, etc. Apples and oranges. Now there are a lot of super fun story-based FPS out there. The Borderlands games, MGS V, Ghost Recon Wildlands, etc. Doom Eternal just does everything better. It's everything I want in a shooter: Insane graphics and gore, killer soundtrack, scalable difficulty, minimal grinding, variable and fluid combat options without being bloated or too complex, glory kills (these might be the game's crown jewel), interesting story that takes a background seat and doesnt force you sit through endless cutscenes, leveling system that generally makes sense, and the Doom Slayer himself is just a bad motherfluffer. The M.O. in Doom is you never stop moving. Power-ups and ammo are almost exclusively gained from kills. About to die? better chainsaw or glory kill a feeder demon. I will say the game is HARD. Not Souls-punishing hard, but on the high-tier difficulty you can make very few mistakes. I'm not an expert FPS player and I found plenty of challenge on normal and even easy modes. Some of the jump-and-grab sections are a bit frustrating, or maybe I'm just old. But not unfair in any way. There is no perma-death, and checkpoints are also fair. For as good as it looks it's oddly not a hardware hog either. I got splendid framerates on a 2070/i7-8700k.TL;DR: stop thinking and buy this game. Aggressive, frenetic demon-slaughtering satisfaction.

_childDocuments_.review: The main issue with this game is that Doom 2016 was damn near perfect, but ZeniMax/Bethesda wanted to cash in on the newly revived franchise.So they went to id and said "Make it more" - "Make it more what?" - "Just make it more".Now how do you improve upon a near perfect game? A problem id couldn't solve either. More enemies, more difficult, more story, more movement, more platforming, more convoluted maps, more ♥♥♥♥♥♥ multiplayer, more always online, more carrots on a stick (cosmetics).Don't get me wrong, this is a fine game (albeit a step back from Doom 2016), but where to go from here? Ideas had obviously dried up towards the end of TAG 2 when the final boss was just a reskinned Marauder and increasingly gimmicky arcade elements were eclectically thrown at the player. Time to take a deep breath, join Doomguy in his casket and ponder...
