_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe I'm writing this, because I really thought this would be incredible, especially after the masterpiece that 2016 was. Basically, 2016 Doom was my favorite shooter of all time, and instead of addressing that games few flaws, which let's be honest, were really just nitpicks, they took a sledgehammer instead of a scalpel to the operating table.First, in addressing the Super Shotgun spam from the first game, they basically over penalize the use of any one weapon, to the point where certain weapons are basically useless against certain enemies. Then, they provide such low ammo levels (even with upgrades)  that near constant Glory Kill and Chainsaw spam are required to even maintain baseline levels of ammo. Essentially, you are forced into the play pattern that the devs want you in, not one you actually want for yourself. I can completely understand incentivizing certain weapons against certain enemies, but you are penalized to the point of uselessness. I actually like the idea of GK and CS alternating to replenish, but it is required nonstop to the point of annoyance. To be honest, it feels like the devs are saying "we know better than you, so you're going to play this way or else."Second, the platforming is completely ridiculous and overdone. The first game had too many arenas, so instead of slight tweaks to the layouts, they went full on Super Mario insane with confusing maps and overly elaborate platforming sequences. And they are EVERYWHERE. Had they been once in a blue moon, I could have tolerated it, but it seems like they way overdid the criticism of the original. Third, It somehow looks worse. Far more cartoony and less visceral than 2016. In all fairness the performance is liquid smooth, but everything just looks less sharp and brutal. The cheese is ramped up to 10, instead of the grit. Make no mistake, this is a good game, and I appreciate what Hugo and his team were going for, but in doing so completely overcompensated in addressing the concerns from the first game. 2016 didn't need a complete heart transplant, it only needed a couple stitches and bandaids. In all honesty, this might be one of the most disappointing games I've ever played.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm fairly new to the Doom scene. The last Doom game I played was Doom 3 back in 2004. I decided to get this game when a buddy of mine suggested it during the summer sale. I wasn't really interested but I went ahead and bought the game. I was not disappointed. From the start, the game throws you in without any tutorials and you begin your quest to kill all demons. There are some hints to show you some game mechanics but if you don't want help, you can easily turn them off in the menu. The music is amazing! I loved every single encounter I had because the music pumped me up to rip and tear everything in my path. You can't catch your breath for a sec without something spawning in or fighting in a mini arena. The story is a little weird to me but only because I haven't played the first Doom(2016). The controls are really good and I enjoyed dashing around and flying in the air. You really have to plan your moves carefully to get the most out of your weapons. There is a multiplayer which I have only played about 10 times. It's a lot to take in but having a friend who can dumb it down helps. It's basically a 2v1 match where the demons must kill the doom slayer while they spawn in demons for help. Over all I had lots of fun and played it again just to grab all the collectibles. Did I mention the music is insane? If you're not a fan of metal, you will be by the end of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! But seriously, watch some reviews before you buy it and realize that this isn't Doom 2016. I am almost done with my Nightmare playthrough and I am eager to go back and play again.Combat is a system. This game is to shooters what Dark Souls was to 3rd person action RPGs. Yes, the game expects you to utilize the weapons and ammo management in a particular way. No, it's not something that needs a balance patch. If you don't like it then it's not the game for you. When played correctly, it feels so smooth and challenging. It's an action puzzle and I can't get enough.Here I want to address some of the negative reviews I've read.1. Tentacles. They CAN be avoided. They have pits in the ground which you can see from afar and be prepared for. Either shoot quickly or use the dash function to avoid their attack.2. The Marauder. He's challenging, but he's not overpowered. Just keep him at mid range, use the super shotgun when his eyes turn green, and dash left and right in-between green eyes. If you run out of ammo, he ALWAYS spawns with fodder demons to chainsaw for more ammo.3. The cutscenes. They can literally all be skipped.There are some things that I don't like, though.1. The story. Yes, it can be skipped, but if you don't, the story itself is weak, cheesy and irrelevant to a Doom game. However, the classical Doom method to a story is, "it's like the story in porn; just enough to make sense but not enough to get in the way of what's really interesting." Unfortunately, I don't think the story here is just enough to make sense. It ended up feeling too serious and too much of it is hiding in codex entries. Therefore, I wish it wasn't included at all.2. Short and sweet, this feels like a Quake 1 spiritual reboot with Doom 2 being the mother and Doom 2016 being the step-father. The biological father is unknown.3. The purple tar pits. Unless I'm missing a mechanic, once you're stuck in purple goo, you're stuck. No dash, no jump. I hate this goo and it's not fun nor challenging.4. The  integration needs to f off. ----tl;dr not perfect, but definitely groundbreaking. If it's too easy or too slow, your difficulty is too low. If it's too hard, it's one of two things: 1. you're playing it wrong / aren't practiced enough; or 2. it's not the game for you. It's definitely a good game, but it's not for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't describe how much i love this game each demon has a specific role from the charging Pinky to the towering behemoth of a Tyrant and each gun has a specific role to help you kill the demons use the arbalest to kill the Cacodemon quickly or use the meat hook to gain higher ground.As far as the difficulty goes play as you want as long as you have fun but the difficulties does give a better chance for re playing and your first run of this game will bust your balls.If your coming hot off the heels of DOOM(2016) this will be different each demon now has a weakness and each demon has his own quirkiness to it.The platforming does feel like a chore sometimes but its better than walking down a boring hall.As you probably heard the story has been given more attention unlike most doom games and i can say if you want the full package don't skip the cutscenes there is tons of lore you can dive into if your into that kinda thing.The DOOM dance has been altered from 2016 you'll have less ammo and there's more emphasis  on chainsawing.The grenades hold a bigger role unlike 2016 but you'll see everything that went into this game is a more refined better version of 2016 packed with content.i think a bethesda account is necessary which may come on as a turn off but this is a must play and overall is the best shooter i've played in decades 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanna say this game is great. This game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fantastically done. Everything about screams wanting to be perfect.Yet there are these tiny flaws that most people overlook and I just find it like.. All too rear up its ugly Titan head.Gameplay feels slower, with dashes feeling really clunky when it doesn't wanna work, getting stuck between demons when you really want to get the heck out of there. Enemy AI is there, it works, but holy heck, why do all the enemy attacks track even while you're mid-dodge? Movement speed feels slower too, the wall grabbing half-works, monkey bars are break the pacing when they're in the arenas.. It's all those little things that feel like they don't agree with me. We also got the new drop system, with ammo coming from chainsawing fodder. Which honestly sucks. You're just given so little ammo to work with in spare, it hurts. Why am I able to super shotgun 12 times only? How come I only get 10 rockets? It feels so little and the chainsaw kills get old pretty fast with how long they take, sometimes even getting you killed as the demons suddenly swarm up on you.Guns.. Those guns man, do they just feel like.. I don't know, it doesn't feel like they do much. As insane as it is for me to say it, the guns in this game just don't feel like they do much in comparison to 2016. The Ballista just feels like a far weaker Gauss Cannon, the mods all feel very meh, with the precision ones giving you the best results just because of the weakpoint system, which I mean, sure cool? But that goes back with the gameplay being slower with the system set up to reward hanging back a bit more and taking precise shots more versus those that run in, shotgun blazing, and can still get out without taking too much damage.Marauders. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Marauders. What is this enemy and why does it exist. Why do I have to deal with a demon that blocks EVERY SINGLE ATTACK at range, chunk you for a ton of damage, DASH, summon a wolf that chips away your HP if you forget about it cause you're dealing with adds, and takes a ton of punishment. No really, why does the enemy have a patience way of defeating it? Every single enemy can be killed in less then a second if you're really good with your fingers and know your weapon match-ups. Why do Marauders SLOW down the gameplay more then it should be? Why are they so tedious to fight against? C'mon idSoftware, this enemy is cool in concept, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is the execution of this enemy just outright horrid. At least they make you fight them one at a time in the base campaign.Other nitpicks include not moving during examination animations when you pick up a secret! Secrets in general feeling a bit less, especially since there is no hidden levels. Initial replayability since as of this review we only have campaign, master levels, and battle mode, which is the PvP of this game, not interested in it to be honest.At the time of this writing, I have completed the campaign on Ultra-Violence. The level design is great. The soundtrack is outstanding. The overarching gameplay is fast and action-filled. All the levels and details are fantastic, but there are some little things that really crawl up under my skin. I will eventually do a Nightmare run as well as do the Mastery levels, but for now, I need a break from Marauders. Good grief.Updated to finally go through the Nightmare levels. Just going to be brief.Coming back to it with a fresh mindset helps. Optional encounters are painful on Nightmare, but at least they're optional. Do I still recommend this? If you haven't played 2016, play this. If you have played 2016 fresh, give it a bit before jumping into this one.I'd love to switch to a neutral stance for this game, but Steam reviews only has yes and no.

_childDocuments_.review: + Quite long and replayable campaign+ Insane graphics+ Mick Gordon+ Fantastic combat+ Secrets and easter eggs+ The story and characters are actually ok+ Mmm... tasty glory kills+ Doom 1/2 as a bonus +/- Multiplayer is forgettable... I'll take arena style DM over this anyday+/- Low amount of weapons... altho they can be upgraded to function like a different gun+/- I know that this is semi-fantasy game but some moments are really unnecessary (ex. the infamous 'player bullet')+/- Other weird changes to punching, chainsaw, double jumping mid-air dashing almost flying... whatever... not fun- Frustrating number of new mechanics, upgrades, things to learn and remember... I literally forgot about perks and flamethrower 10 seconds after they were introduced- Platforming and wall-climbing sections are just stupid- Too heavy dependent on chainsaw and glory killsDoom Eternal feels like improvement in every single department... HOWEVER... its a prime example of 'getting too much is bad' thingy. Instead of adding sooo many new mechanics they should just add new weapons (and monsters, which they did), scrap multiplayer, make some sort of coop survival mode... and get rid of that ridiculous climbing sections.9-/10

_childDocuments_.review: RIP... AND TEAR.... UNTIL THE JOB.... IS DONE.OK so first off, this is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing game. Absolutely worth full price. It's all the high-adrenaline, DOOM action you could want.However, this game plays very differently to DOOM (2016). This game is all about the combos. If you're not killing, you're dead. It's the only DOOM game I play on the easiest difficulty, because I'm just looking to enjoy the carnage, and otherwise I find it too challenging.This game absolutely shines visually. Like the huge storage requirements, this game eats VRAM. Luckily I *can* run it at 1080p max, with ray-tracing, on a 2060 SUPER with 8GB, but with older cards you'll be severely limited by your VRAM. 4k is a no-go for my system, but I imagine at 4k, without the upscaling graininess from my display, it'd look even better.The music is phenomenal. DOOM (2016) had one of my favourite game soundtracks ever, and this game tops it. Deep, growling guitars meet some awesome electronic effects. It's just a shame it can't yet be bought as DLC on Steam.In all, this is a fantastic game. I'd recommend it strongly, and if it's on sale, it's a no-brainer. If you like FPS's, this is an essential.

_childDocuments_.review: most of negative reviews come from people annoyed by some company/payment management regarding some audio tracks in-game... I didnt and I dont care about reading about it. But this is not a review for the company's management. Its for the game. And its awesome. It doesnt feel like doom, its like playing chess against monsters and you need to grow some extra fingers to pull all the crazy gadgets and weapon combination this has. But if you are willing to learn deep mechanics (not doom-like at all) while also being a violent demon slayer then you will enjoy this game A LOT. Thats exactly why I didnt buy this game on release. I loved 2016, it was reaching with a few extra mechanics but it was OK. When I found out ETERNAL was that multiplied by 5 in terms of mechanics and tactics I refused to buy it because it was obviously not a "DOOM" game... I got it now full with every dlc highly discounted and man its good. 10/10 fps, the lore doesnt botter and its basic and cool, music literally rocks, graphics makes your head spin (it gets insane and fast), gunplay is superb, when you get used to its "rock paper scissors" nature you feel like a machine.I played 32 hours now. Only now I can honestly say im getting somewhat good at the game. Combos, quick switching, resource management, prioritization, movement, etc. And this has to be the best SP FPS experience ever made. I think about combos and my finger movement while trying to fall asleep. I want to get a good night rest so my brain capacity it high the next day to perform and get a little better the next day. Its just awesome. I wish everyone undestood what this game is really about.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly the best example of what a sequel should be.They could have easily made another DOOM 2016, but instead they looked at what they had done and sought out to improve everything that was wrong and further improve what was right.No more long hallways filled with nothing, here's a platforming segment to keep you engaged.No more using the same weapon, ammo has been restricted and you MUST swap to keep going.Chainsaw is more predominant simply due to the fact it refills on its own, easing the tighter ammo.Each and every level stands out far more than they did in 2016, rather than have everything be varying shades brown and red, you see a much wider variety of colors and environments.All of the bosses stand out, with some even joining the enemy pool later in the game. Remember the Hell Guards in 2016? Of course you don't.Even the music is far more varied than 2016, as good as it all was all of the tracks blended into each other.All of the weapon mods are far more useful than in 2016, with each feeling like a valid option. The good ones from 2016 stayed and were improved while the useless ones were replaced with a more viable option.The story is there for those who care, and as someone who does care, I personally think it's great and I can't wait to see what happens next in the upcoming DLCs.While I haven't played too much of Battlemode, I can say it's much better than what 2016 had and always has me catching my breath whenever I play.I thoroughly enjoyed DOOM 2016 and to see the devs take everything they learned from it and make the best game they could is honestly something more game companies should do nowadays.10/10, please buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Engine-wise, this is probably the most well made game I've ever played.  I've cranked all visual settings to Ultra Nightmare at 1440p resolution, and my frame rate still blows my monitor's 144hz refresh rate out of the water - never even coming close to dropping below 144 frames. My rig has i7 8700k and Aorus 2080ti, but still, I have not played many other FPS games that are optimized as well as DOOM Eternal is. Gameplay-wise, this is the most fun I've ever had playing an FPS campaign. This game has a certain style of play that id clearly wants you to utilize, and they are very successful in making you adopt that style of play. If you aren't running and gunning, using your entire kit, constantly weapon switching for specific enemies, using the environment for kills and movement, and ripping and tearing as much as you can - you die. Quickly. The gameplay and design is conceptually perfect. My first playthrough is on Ultra Violence, to get my sea legs, and I'm actually excited to replay the game again on Nightmare - maybe someday Ultra Nightmare. DOOM's push forward combat is so intense and actually exhausting, that I've only been able to play (at most) one level at a time; sometimes having to take a break after a Slayer Gate because I'm so drained from 5+ minutes of non-stop, action packed, ultra violence. But the game is incredibly satisfying, and one-shotting a level's final arena or a Slayer Gate is insanely gratifying. You feel like some kind of primordial force of doom - a feeling no other game has ever given me.DOOM Eternal is the most badass game ever made.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom Eternal is the latest and most violent game in the Doom series, which practically popularized first-person shooters in the world. Available on PlayStation 4 (PS4), XOne and PC  and Steam), the launch was not exactly groundbreaking, but it has everything needed to be a legitimate representative of the genre and also one of the best examples of how to create a narrative linked to gameplay. Did not understand? Full review below:Doom Eternal is a natural continuation of 2016's  following its story of demonic invasion of Earth, with alien airs. _childDocuments_.review: It's far from being a bad game, but I find myself tremendously disappointed in comparison to DOOM 2016 in nearly every aspect. My plan is to simply list my personal issues and do my best to articulate why I feel that way. Some of the larger complaints I have are as follows:Your ammunition reserves have been severely restricted in favor of a recharging chainsaw. It's heavily encouraged for the player to burn fuel on fodder units every couple of minutes or so. I found it to be incredibly cumbersome having to frequently disengage from heated firefights in order to seek out additional fuel containers or a lower-tier enemy to burn a single bar on. Despite being considerably more capable than in the previous installment, I feel like I'm performing a much more defensive dance in Eternal by comparison.Eternal trades 2016's "If it has a head, it's a weak spot" mentality for a more complex weak spot system. Higher-tier enemies have their own unique weak spots, such as the Revenant's shoulder-mounted missile launchers, for example. Eternal introduces each of these weak spots by abruptly pausing the action and telling the player through a pop-up tutorial exactly where to shoot and the best weapon for the job. Method of teaching aside, I think this idea is fine on paper. But considering a single shot of the scoped Heavy Cannon can instantly knee-cap a fair portion of the enemy units, I think this was a fumble in execution.Staying on the topic of enemies, I find the Tentacles and Marauder to be particularly obnoxious additions. To my knowledge, there's no way to preemptively kill tentacles while they're underground, so you just have to slowly kill them as they spring out of their nests one-by-one. They're not difficult, but they're entirely unnecessary. The Marauder, on the other hand, demands all of your attention when he decides to join the dance. In order to get past his shield, you have to bait a specific attack from him which requires you to be standing at "medium range" and only "medium range" lest you be punished with one of two projectiles.Again, not particularly hard, but tedious, slow, and incredibly annoying. I feel that these two enemies clash with the fluid, non-linear, almost-improvisational combat design introduced with 2016.While platforming was definitely an integral part of 2016, it was still fairly muted and secondary to the ripping and tearing. In Eternal, however, the platforming is increased to a suffocating degree, especially annoying when coupled with the odd focus on puzzle-solving. Rarely have any of the dedicated puzzle/platforming segments been all that interesting, but they've definitely been consistent on slamming the brakes on my momentum. And if I'm being honest, the 'Objective Complete' cutscenes that have to play every time you complete every minor task, story cutscenes, and hub world all do a fine job of doing that on their own.I won't say much on it for spoiler reasons, but the final boss was kinda awful, too. Mostly just fighting standard mobs while the boss exists in the background.And 2016's Multiplayer was good. People were way too harsh on that thing.I have a few more personal issues with the game that I consider to be a bit more mild:First off, I started on Ultra-Violence and found it pretty effortless outside of maybe a couple encounters and that was almost entirely due to ammunition woes. I did begin a Nightmare file just to get an idea of what it was like and found the enemy damage output to be a bit higher than I would have hoped. Probably wouldn't be as big of a deal if it wasn't for the lower ammo reserves and frequent narrow, low-ceiling combat spaces. Additionally, early game can be a bit of a slog until you get the few upgrades that make you less sluggish. Either way, it's entirely doable, but not nearly as fun (or genuinely challenging) as 2016's Nightmare. The upgrade systems were a little silly, too. There are like four(?) different methods of upgrading you can do that all take their own unique currency to activate. I think they could have been more homogenized overall, and maybe some upgrades could have been cut in order to beef up some of the others, like ammo capacity for example. I still find it odd that they would restrict runes to only three slots considering how lame some of the options were; I stuck to the initial three that I unlocked for the entirety of the game. I personally would have restructured everything other than the weapon mods.I've touched on this a bit already, but I would have been happier with less meters to worry about. I'm already having to frantically look at my dwindling ammo count every few seconds, so worrying about my chainsaw, grenade, sword, blood melee, etc., just creates a strange situation where I'm dying because I don't have an ability, rather than making a genuine mistake. I think I'd rather have physical weapons replace some of the abilities/equipment in the Slayer's kit and have more ammo overall as a result, but hey, what can you do.Lastly, and this is probably the most throw-away complaint, but I wish the story would have picked up from where 2016 left off. It was really jarring to just hard cut to Hell on Earth and the Slayer's silly spaceship without a mention of what happened in-between. And other than those two exposition dumps in 2016 that dragged on way too long (you know the ones) I enjoyed the story's delivery method in that game and would have liked to see it return over Eternal's implementation of more typical narrative cutscenes. You can actually skip these though, so pros and cons, I guess.TLDR: the game's not bad, and clearly the majority of people really enjoy the changes, but 2016 was much closer to my taste and there are definitely aspects, such as the emphasis on platforming, that could be a huge turnoff for certain people out there.

_childDocuments_.review: It's more of the same, fast-paced combat, with brutal fighting sections, punishing level ending bosses, as well as more reasons to explore the environment than 2016, with multiple difficult encounters hidden throughout each level. While the overall move speed definitely feels slower in comparison to Doom 2016, when you combine it with the increased Glory Kill distance rune, the new Dash mechanics, and starting with the double jump, it feels like a reasonable trade-off. I will say that while it's not overtly more difficult in terms of how hard the enemies are to kill, which work differently to how they did in Doom 2016 (Don't expect to be able to consistently Super Shotgun Hell Knights to death), there are definitely many, many, MANY more demons in the game than 2016. The difficulty in this game, in contrast, feels like it comes from adding exponentially more enemies, while restricting the size of each arena to laughably small cubes where twitch reactions, ammo conservation, and picky chainsaw/glory kills will most likely be the best way to succeed. Seriously. The Slayer Gates are a true challenge, and were the first time that I started to get frustrated with the difficulty. However, I'm kind of a masochist when it comes to playing games, so this was a plus, and felt that much more rewarding when I do finally manage to beat them. The ammo/armor/health mechanics in terms of how different types of kills give you different resources are actually very nice, but harder to manage. It feels like you can really get almost anything you need on demand, as long as you have the movement and placement to get it. Another plus is that different demons all have special weaknesses and you can break certain parts of demons to make them easier to deal with, or toss them on the backburner while you deal with more immediate threats (ex. blowing up Arachnotron turrets). It truly feels like you have a reason to use other guns besides the Super Shotgun, and it feels surprisingly good, in a way I didn't expect. Also, while the soundtrack has a lot of controversy, rest assured that in game, it feels f&%@ing fantastic in every way. All the crunchy and aggressive tunes that you need to slaughter literal hordes of demons. However, I do feel the Mick Gordon tracks play a little better (Super Gore Nest and Meathook in particular). All in all? The experience of the Singleplayer is 100% worth it when the game is on sale. Definitely not worth playing on Bethesda Net though, so be careful when you see sales on certain websites, cause I fell into that trap. Do yourself a favor and get this if any of this appeals to you. Also, for the completionists, the secrets feel a little easier to find, but more difficult to get to, which feels more rewarding imo.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably a good game, but I came in expecting more of Doom (2016). It isn't.Gone are the carefully crafted maps, the carefully crafted music, the carefully crafted mechanics. It feels like a shell of the previous doom.The most annoying things so far: * Melee does no damage. What?* Weapons and keycards and upgrades no longer feel part of the world.. they just float there. * Same for lore and secrets. No pads or secret levers, just floating pages and floating giant question marks. It's no longer an immersive world.* Running out of ammo. Constantly. Having to use the chainsaw every 5 enemies to get ammo. It's stupid. Edit: even after upgrading to maximum ammo, it's still not enough. The shotgun only holds 12 shots, for example. There is some strategy involved in when to use which weapon, but with only 4 ammo types (5 if you count bfg), once you run out on one weapon, you'll also run out on the other. Final edit: ok, the chainsaw refills itself. Ammo is never an issue anymore, because you can just keep chainsawing forever. This gets very tedious, however.* Platforming. A little bit is okay, but you're supposed to jump from ledge to ledge and if you miss, you're dead. Also, jumping from wall to wall is almost a puzzle as it's barely visible which walls you can jump and which you can't. edit: I'm a bit further in the game now and it has progressed to double jump to double dash to recharge dash in mid air to dash some more to jump to horizontal bar to jump to dropping platform through fire and electric barricades. I wish I was kidding.I'll continue to play to finish the campaign, but I wanted to throw this out there for people thinking about buying it in the summer sale: this is not the greatness of the previous doom. Wait till it's at least 75% off.Final edit: Ok I have now finished the game. My points all remain the same. I'll give the game one thing: it is very pretty. The environments are amazing to look at.But it's just not as fun to play as the previous doom. The music never goes to 11, I never got the "this is awesome!" feeling, the entire game feels like a chore. The story is.. whatever. They retconned Samuel Hayden's character and some other stuff. Half of the story is just loads of text that you have to read in a crappy interface (tip: read the codices on the wiki instead of ingame).Maybe it's me...Final final edit: F you id/Bethesda for the extent that you screwed Mick Gordon over. I knew something was wrong but holy crap. No more money for you. Ever.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This is the best first person shooter I've ever played in my entire life. BFG 9000/10I loved DOOM 2016, and as soon as I saw the second story trailer for this game I pre-ordered it. To say it was everything I asked for is an understatement. ID software turned the everything up to 11 with this game. I beat this game on launch day, and as of writing this review am on my fourth playthrough of the game.The game's combat is the most engaging part of the game. The combination of resource management and fast-paced movement; along with the abolishing of pace-halting reloads makes slaughtering demons as enjoyable as possible. Your weapons have a flesh tearing impact that makes them each feel like capable killing machines, the brilliant sound design also makes for loud impactful fire.Speaking of sound design, Mick Gordon does it again. The hard crunching music of DOOM 2016 comes back full force in this game. The music delivers the most brutal concierto of badass metal riffs mixed with all-new chants and synth combinations. This all combines to create the most headbanging metal soundtrack I've ever heard in a game.I do wish there were slightly less cutscenes in this game, but the fact that they're skippable makes this criticism almost negligable.If for the combat alone, the game is fantastic. With a dash of platforming, fantastic art direction, and a brutal challenge (ultra-violence and nightmare), DOOM Eternal is a game I would recommend to anyone who likes fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic, some folk don't seem to understand the basics of this game, so let me explain.This is a game where you move.Learning to move and dodge the enemies in this game, and learning to effectively use different parts of your arsenal is the entire idea behind the design, and the harder difficulties.You CANNOT simply use one gun and assume it will take you through the whole game, the weapons have been balanced to all be useful for different situations.Some say that the dash is too slow, to which I say: Get the upgrade to make it faster.Some say that the Marauder is impossible, to which I say: He really isn't, there is a combo that works for me, you can probably look it up if you can't figure it out, just be fast at weapon switching. Also, fight him on flat ground, last time I played, uneven natural ground seemed to make his AI a little wonky.All in all, this is a game you have to play at it's pace, not yours. If you can't handle going very very fast while paying attention to many enemies at once, this game may not be for you.Be mindful of what demons you're facing, and Don't. Stop. Moving.I'm leaving my original negative review below for historical sake, but Denuvo Anti Cheat has been REMOVED as of this edit._____________________________________________________This is an amazing game which I truly love.Gameplay, Graphics, Storyline, All fantastic.But, the newest update added Denuvo Anti-Cheat, which is a kernel level anti-cheat program.What this means is that this program can alter your computer in any way it wishes, or alternatively it can be attacked by other malware to gain total control of your PC.Basically, Denuvo Anti-Cheat can delete or modify any file on your computer, or add new ones.Not to mention Denuvo Anti-Cheat doesn't run on Linux, so people who bought this game for their Linux computers cannot even play the game they spent 60 bucks on anymore.They say it can be uninstalled, but if you do that the game won't start until you allow it to reinstall.At the very least they've stated it only runs while DOOM does, so in theory it can't affect your PC in any way unless you're playing DOOM, but this is brand new software which hasn't even been cleared by Microsoft's security as far as I know.Think of it this way, how many times have you bought a new game and had it be absolutely flawless with no bugs?Denuvo Anti-Cheat is brand spankin' new, and with any new software, there likely will be security holes, glitches, exploits, and more.All in all, Kernel level Anti-Cheat programs are against proper coding practices for Microsoft systems, which is why they often cause system crashes, and are very easy targets for malware developers.DOOM Eternal is a fantastic game and I enjoyed every minute I put into it, but I can't recommend it with this massive security risk required to run it._____________________________________________________Thanks for reading this, but Denuvo Anti Cheat was removed, it's all good now.

_childDocuments_.review: I like DOOM 2016, but DOOM eternal is not DOOM 2016. So of course, I had some concerns about the game, therefore I will try to be as honest as possible. This lengthy review contains NO SPOILERS, unless you count revealing game mechanics, which I WILL BE going through. Also, before writing this review, I stubbornly bashed my head against the demons on ultra-violence and finished the game without changing the difficulty (you can switch the difficulty settings during the campaign up to a point). I’m not an expert in FPS games, but I’m not terrible either.DOOM eternal is different. At least it plays out quite differently than DOOM 2016. Is it good or bad is really just a preference, but in all honesty. I think DOOM eternal takes the cake from all the recent and current FPS games out there. Here are some reasons as to why I think so. Some have raised concern that you run out of ammo constantly, while it is true, it is also wrong. One big difference is that in DOOM 2016 you could joyfully blast through the levels with 1 or 2 of your favourite weapons. And so, in DOOM eternal, it really feels like you are constantly switching guns because you don’t get that much ammo drops. But you would be WRONG, because in DOOM eternal, ammo is also eternal. The chainsaw is there with you, and it auto refills on a cooldown to chomp fodder demons. Heavier demons require you to save your chainsaw fuel, but I don’t really recommend in doing so. When you enter a fight, the game procedurally spawns “a set of demons”. Until you rip & tear through the set, the game spawns constantly additional fodder for you to introduce your chainsaw with. Therefore, the ammo drops that you are missing, are the fodder demons just waiting to be brutalized for your ammo refilling pleasure. The game makes sure you need to use the chainsaw much more often and provides the means to do so. Between the devastation and carnage, pretty much every level has platforming “puzzles” after each big battle. I personally don’t find these parts that appealing, but they do provide time for you to drink your beer that has been sitting next to your monitor unattended for the duration of indiscriminate violence against all demon kind. These parts are however usually quite short, although somewhat difficult at later levels (difficult for my fat fingers at least). This is also the part where you do most of your exploring. Many secrets are hidden in these stages and require you to utilize the mobility of the slayer to get to. In addition, the platforming parts allow you to wonder how visually beautiful the levels are. There are no secrets that you will miss. At the end of each level you unlock the RPG fast travel™. With RPG fast travel™, you can get back to those secrets you missed. Luckily, most of them are not that difficult to find, and unlike open world bullsh1ttiness, they don’t require you to walk all the way there and back again to get to. And just like that, the level design is very linear, which is a good thing. That way, the action and the platforming occur when they are supposed to. The levels guide the player in an interesting and engaging manner. The battle areas are well thought out, in a way that they really let you use your mobility vertically and horizontally. With the mobility, you get the feeling of fighting in a very open space. For this there are mobility objects placed throughout each level. There is the pole vault pole (aka forced jump) and the climbable wall (aka ladders), that let you move more freely. You can also grab ledges if your jump is about to fall short. But luckily, all of this is done smoothly and turns you into an expert monkey in no time. The essence of DOOM is of course to dispense as much righteous violence as possible. And for this, the game provides you with plenty of opportunities. At first, the battles feel very chaotic with demons spawning left and right with no end in sight. Especially during the slayer gate challenges. You will also find that most of the heavy and super heavy demons are bullet sponges. For this, the game provides you with kind of like a rock paper scissor system. Many of the demons have weaknesses. For example, feed a cacodemon a pineapple (grenade) and it will stagger for you to perform an instant melee glory kill. This encourages the player to get as many weapon modifications early on as possible. You need to utilize the tools you are provided with. You have your regular grenades, freezing grenades, flame thrower, blood punching, and the aforementioned chainsaw. I found using these constantly to compensate my lack of mobility skills. Although, regardless of skill, you should be using these tools anyway, as they will make a great difference in the game difficulty. What this means, is that you need to react to different enemies in a certain way. You need to be able to do glory kills and set demons on fire to get health and armor in tough spots. You need to switch between your guns and use the chainsaw. You are given plenty of tools to find the order in all the chaos. There are tons of things for you to collect. Many of them provide you with a point in here or there to spend on an upgrade. Some collectibles help you cheat (without consequences) in the “mission select” where you can return to previous missions and do those challenges you might have missed. Some of these collectibles (and the mission select) you will acquire from your mission hub. Yes, there is a mission hub! And just like the RPG fast travel™, I found the mission hub a bit ridiculous for a DOOM game to be honest. Also, in your mission hub you can visit a demon prison to “punish” demons, which I didn’t quite understand, since you will be punishing demons as you go through the campaign anyway.  Many DOOM eternal upgrades are the same as in DOOM 2016. Most of them upgrade your gear, health, armor, ammo capacity and so on. Then there are the runes, which I liked in the 2016 version where you got certain runes after certain challenges. Now in eternal you can freely choose from the beginning which you unlock. Meaning that when you get your first 3 runes that you really like, you are not that excited to gather the rest. Also, just like in DOOM 2016, you upgrade your suit and weapons. However unlike in 2016, you don’t punch the poor thing for a weapon mod, but just gently pick up your mod. After that, you unlock upgrade points by killing stuff. The more you kill, the more you can put points in your guns. Then, once unlocked, you can try to go for the mastery upgrade which is a challenge similar than in 2016, i.e. kill a bunch of demons in fabulous fashion related to the gun and weapon mod. The only thing in the weapon mods I found wonky was when you got the rocket launcher lock on mastery. After that, I never quite figured out how the lock on worked properly, and for fast moving enemies (such as the archvile teleport move) it was downright painful to shoot. There is a story? I personally found it confusing, and that the slayer has much more patience than before. I could’ve used more breaking of consoles than forced cutscenes. Not my cup of tea in a DOOM game. The music is the same djenty style heavy metal (during the application of violence) and atmospheric gloomy sounds (think original quake soundtrack) during the platforming, which is perfect for the game. But now, that Mick Gordon actually knows what he is doing, it all sounds more thoughtful and engaging. The music is preposterously good, and the sounds are fabulous, and I didn’t feel anything out of touch except maybe a bit with the plasma gun rapid spifififififi sounds. Best FPS game there is currently. Everything the story lacks is made up by the gameplay and awesomeness that is killing demons.

_childDocuments_.review: DOOM Eternal feels like a classic case of the "Too-many-things" Syndrome. There's a lot of good to be had in the game, but unfortunately it seems that it's just so packed to the brim that various core mechanics suffered. Whilst the game is good, it just doesn't make you feel like Doomguy, as you're weaker than you were in DOOM 2016 and so are several weapons within your arsenal.Some of the design choices made for the game feel as though they were purposely made so that the developers could force players to use something they personally like, or keep players from using things in a similar fashion to the way they did in DOOM 2016. These changes are extremely evident in how they handled various aspects of the game. Whilst I do have a lot of criticism for the game, I did at least enjoy my time with it.For this review and others like it, please check out my Steam Curator page if you'd like! What's good:- Map design. Areas are lively and dynamic, allowing for much more exploration and secret hunting than in the previous titles. Maps are super expansive with gigantic arenas at times, and encourage you to explore and go off the standard path to find every single item and secret.- The player map. The 3D map for the games expansive areas are really well done, and show you almost everything as you fill them out or if you acquire the automap.- Sound design. Sound design is wonderful in this game, from everything in the environment making various little sounds due to wind or you stepping on them, to the squelch of demonic gore-covered terrain mechanics moving in the background just out of sight. Weapons sound chunky and fitting for their uses, and overall everything seems to fit. This does not include the soundtrack, and I've touched on that further down.- The Doomiverse. Doom has never particularly explored its universe outside of a contextual storytelling setting, so seeing the various new races and other characters which are integral to the Doom universe is incredibly interesting. There's a lot of contextual storytelling and lore to be found as well from the various codex pages, and if you're interested in the lore you won't be disappointed.- Optional Encounters. Arguably for me these were the most enjoyable experiences in the game. Slayer Gates and the optional Gorenests just bring the combat to the forefront and make it shine whilst relying upon your own skill and nothing else to conquer what you've gotten yourself into. Many are more intense than anything else in the game, and are truly rewarding if you do all of them.What's ok:- Combat. Whilst the combat in DOOM Eternal at times did have me smiling as I flew across the room, there were numerous times where I found myself saying "Are you serious?" with a grimace plastered across my face whilst fighting. Eternal should be held up to the same standard of quality DOOM 2016 set, and whilst it's not bad and at times is comparable, it unfortunately does not reach the same level.Many things lend to this overall feeling regarding the combat, but the primary one is the ammunition drought felt throughout the entire game. Core combat mechanics have been changed to where it feels like there's this lame Rock-paper-scissors mechanic as you're forced to juggle utilizing various things rather than playing how you personally feel like.- Platforming. Something that doesn't necessarily add to the game, nor is it really a detriment. It's fun to swing around on a bar and then fly across an expanse, but at the end of it all, it's just kind of a "Why was this necessary?" type scenario.- Soundtrack. Whilst normally I'd throw this into the same section as sound design, this felt like it deserved its own segment as DOOM 2016's soundtrack made the battles feel much more intense. In Eternal there are some interesting musical choices, and some of them are good, but there's also a lot of double-dipping upon DOOM 2016's soundtrack success by throwing the most impactful songs from the previous game in at some of the most intense moments.- Dashing. Dashing feels incredibly freeing at the best of times, and at the worst of times can be the primary factor leading to a majority of death. It works very well whenever you're off the ground and at the height of your jump, but if you're slightly below that there's a lot of raised objects and various other level geometry that will catch you up and stop you mid-flight.- Equipment launcher. I constantly found myself forgetting about any aspects of the Equipment launcher in the same way I forgot about Frags in 2016. They're not bad, but they don't feel as though they particularly add anything or are so integral to the experience that you need to use them.- The upgrade system. From the Sentinel Tokens, to the Sentinel Crystals and more, the upgrade system just felt tacked on at times. Very few upgrades felt as if they were actually beneficial, and only 3 of the 9 runes actually felt remotely helpful throughout the entire game. Many of the upgrades or runes just make you wonder "Why would I want this, when I could have this?", or are disappointing in their upgrade capacities such as the ammo capacity upgrades giving you two more shotgun shells for each upgrade.What's bad:- Anti-fun and Anti-skill mechanics. There are so many of these in the game that range from a variety of things, with one of the key points of contention being The Marauder, as how he is designed is directly anti-fun. There's purple goop in some levels which go against the core design element of the game which says "You're supposed to be fast and strong", which basically brings you to a crawl and feels like a way for them to have padded sections so they take longer. Enemy projectiles home in on you at least slightly for almost every projectile, which feels like it's to directly counter the dashing mechanic.- Ammunition drought. There is almost NO ammo economy in this game, to the point that early on it feels as though you're struggling to do anything which has more than 12-15 demons in it. Glory kills no longer drop ammo like in 2016, and you're forced to use the chainsaw rather than keeping it on your person and using it as you like. Regardless of how much of a sure-shot you are or how good at the game you are, it will punish you with a lack of ammo in almost every fight as the drops are so scarce.- Doomguy is weak. Sadly, Doomguy is weaker than he was in 2016, to the point that the game just doesn't thematically feel right. You throw punches like you're hitting someone with a wet pool noodle, and to put any enemy into glory-kill HP range you have to have an 8 round boxing match with them, REGARDLESS of what they are. You're slower than you were in the previous game, and just overall it doesn't feel as awesome as it once did.- Boss fights. Throughout my playthrough of the game I enjoyed only two boss fights, and neither of them felt particularly integral to the game. Bossfights devolve into this mess of fighting with mobs and clearing out almost everything before eventually focusing on the boss, and even then the mobs endlessly spawn which just takes away from the awesome feeling the boss fights could have. Endlessly spawning enemies are a result of the lack of ammo as well in boss rooms, which feels lazy.Final Score: 7/10Worth $60? For me personally, I feel it's worth $40 and not much more.Closing thoughts: Personally I feel that all games which are a sequel should be held to the same standard that their predecessor set, and sadly DOOM Eternal just doesn't deliver on a lot of aspects and fronts that DOOM 2016 did. I personally feel that if this had been the first release within the DOOM "Revival" project that the game would be received with glowing reviews, but as it stands as a sequel it sadly doesn't deliver on all fronts. Had this game been the revival of Quake or something standalone, it would be much better.

_childDocuments_.review: Upon the 2016 DOOM release, it was the 6th game in the series at the time.  Its inception was responsible for re capturing the 1990's classic first person shooter genre, including returning the series to its former glory.In 2020, DOOM Eternal, the sequel to the 2016 DOOM and 7th in the family tree, once again puts the player in control of the DOOM slayer. The game received positive reviews from critics and outlets alike, with 91% positive of 154,000 reviews on steam alone.  Like DOOM, its core emphasis was robust and relentless combat, encouraging the player to aggressively dominate its enemies. Doom Eternal continues that of its predecessor, with the player engaging in a variety of arenas, sometimes to a point of being overwhelmed by Hells forces, you must rip and tear as if the monsters will come through the monitor!DOOM Eternal being a sequel, As the Doom slayer you are to remove the demonic forces of hell from earth with a vengeance. However, DOOM Eternal introduces more to the table than previous. New weapons, new movement mechanics, which now collectively cause the player to rethink their strategy when coming across a multitude of different demons, i.e like the infamous Arch-vile. There are also newly added demons with different fighting abilities. The player must think on the fly incorporating many weapons, tactics and movements to dominate a vast array of organic killing machines. The player can also effectively reduce certain demon capabilities using certain weapons to give the Doom Slayer an advantage. There is also a hub in between missions where the player can unlock gear, abilities, bonus weapons and view in game collections.The game is long, the levels are  beautifully created and still sets a solid benchmark for FPS in modern gaming. The graphics are amazing, the soundtrack will almost certainly release that extra dopamine and make those demons afraid of you! Simply to put it, words can only have so much effect, the game is a requirement. DOOM Eternal keeps as close as it can within its realm of infamy, much is kept intact here and not much divergence, keeping to its traditional roots. It is still now an incredible nostalgic and psychological feat, not only that, it really touches the souls of many of us, who played that very first level of DOOM 1 on MS DOS in 1993 some 30 years ago.  The DOOM franchise Is one of the very last, most successful, most influential and memorable gaming line in existence without a doubt. To simply ignore or detest this is simply delusional.   Ive seen a lot of games come and go in this world.... but Doom is eternal.

_childDocuments_.review: The biggest problem with this game is that you end up in situations where you have to master your cool downs. This is not a run and gun game. It is not "Doom". You run out of ammo, health, and armor really fast and all your skills have cool downs. If you are not playing on the easiest mode you end up in situations where you have no choice but to run around spamming chainsaw for ammo and flame attack just to keep fighting. It takes the fun out of it because all you are doing is trying to barley survive while doing those rotations with many of the encounters.  You feel weak if you do not play how they want you to play. I feel like how I felt when playing WoW because if I forget to use a cool down in my rotation then it might mean life or death. More of a remembering your skills vs shooting stuff. This is not a FPS in that fashion.  Basically you are forced to play a certain way and if you don't you will not have a good experience. If this doesn't bother you then this game is great. I personally hate the game play style and I am not sure if I will finish this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom Eternal over-engineered mess full of bad design choices. As it turns out, the shortened dev cycle for 2016 (after needing to start from scratch with the cancelled Doom 4 Half-Life 2 clone) was what gave the game it's tight gameplay loop and minimal story.When given a full dev cycle, the designers stuff in too many mechanics under the pretense of 'complexity'. It bills itself as a 'combat puzzle', but it's a puzzle in that you stuff the square peg in a square hole. See a Cacodemon? Launch a nade in it's mouth. Fighting the most insufferable FPS enemy of all time The Marauder? Be sure to stay in what the devs called "The Fun Zone" and quick swap between the SSG and Ballista. Be sure to not get too close demons either, as iD didnt like how 2016 players would get point-blank to Mancubi or other enemies to quickly take them out. So now a number of demons have an AOE attack to keep you in The Fun Zone. Every time a overengineered demon shows up, the game comes to a standstill and tells you which shape to fit through what hole.2016 was about forward momentum and carving a path through demons. Eternal is about regularly falling back and finding trash mobs while your MOBA skills refresh their cooldown. Boss fights are miserable and the game throws so many upgrades at you despite many of them being unnecessary. Remember how games journalists and streamers made the soy face at the Doomguy funko pop in 2016? Well now that is a whole library of doom funko pops that will leave your mouth and beard agap. Remember how 2016 was praised for it's distant but kind of neat story? Well now you can enjoy it's expansion into arguably the most embarrassing writing and worldbuilding put to ink.The soundtrack is forgettable, and compared to 2016 sounds like Royalty Free background metal.Multiplayer was a damn hoot during the first week, but ultimately it is an unbalanced mess with a 45 second intro each game.  This game is bad and an absolute mess. iD did not like that gamers didnt play Doom2016 the way they wanted, and this game is a result - the FPS equivalent of Simon says. The devs are not going to learn a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ thing from it, which means the next doom is going to be an even more miserable slog.Also, never tell a dev they are funny, because you get stuff like Hipster Archville and the Coffee shop.

This sequel amplifies the intensity, pushing you into a fast-paced, brutal combat environments that keeps the adrenaline pumping from start to finish. With a focus on movement and precision, the game challenges even seasoned players, making every battle a test of skill and strategy.The story of DOOM Eternal takes the Doom Slayer on a journey across dimensions to prevent the complete annihilation of humanity. The narrative is more expansive than its predecessor, offering deeper lore and more cinematic moments that immerse players into the world. The stakes are higher, and the scope is grander, giving the story a more epic feel while staying true to the series' roots.Gameplay in DOOM Eternal is a masterclass in first-person shooter design, combining speed, fluidity, and brutality in a way that few games can match. The addition of new weapons, abilities, and enemies creates a constantly evolving combat landscape that requires quick thinking and adaptability. The game encourages aggressive play, rewarding those who can maintain momentum and execute well-timed kills. The resource management system, where health, armour, and ammo are tied to specific kills, adds a layer of strategic depth that sets it apart from other shooters.Visually, DOOM Eternal is a stunning display of technical prowess and creative design. The environments are diverse and richly detailed, ranging from the ruined cities of Earth to the hellish landscapes of other dimensions. Each level is meticulously crafted, offering a mix of open arenas and tight corridors that keep the action fresh and varied. The demons are grotesque and terrifying, brought to life with incredible detail that enhances the game's intense atmosphere. Complementing the visuals is Mick Gordon's phenomenal soundtrack, which perfectly matches the game's relentless pace and dark tone.Overall, DOOM Eternal is a remarkable sequel that surpasses DOOM (2016) in almost every way. It offers a more expansive story, refined gameplay mechanics, and a visual experience that is both awe-inspiring and terrifying. The game is a must-play for fans of the genre, delivering a visceral, challenging, and deeply satisfying experience that sets a new standard for first-person shooters.DOOM Eternal gets a 9/10.For more reviews check my Steam profileHope you enjoyed my review, god bless you

_childDocuments_.review: DOOM returns in this excellent sequel to the already great DOOM (2016). Earth has been completely overrun by the legions of Hell, and its once again the Slayer's job to clean up the mess and avenge Earth. This time, the slayer has more to play with in his arsenal, such as the shoulder-mounted flame thrower and the ability to dash. The demons this time around aren't to be underestimated. They're much smarter and more precise with their attacks than the previous game, but that only makes them more satisfying to rip apart. Thanks to the new abilities such as swinging from bars and climbing walls, there is a lot of platforming throughout the game that works surprisingly well and can be fun. The music is still godly, and the animations of the glory kills are very fluid. Ammo is more of an necessity this time, since the max capacities of your weapons are much lower, which makes your chainsaw much more important (which now auto-refills its first bit of fuel). The bosses are also much more entertaining and unique this time around. Overall, this is a very solid, well-detailed and refined DOOM game that I HIGHLY recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom Eternal wasn't exactly what I was expecting and is a lot different than Doom 2016.  Initially I was really disappointed in the first few hours because I was still clinging on to old ideas instead of trying to embrace the new stuff and take the time to fully understand each demon's weaknesses along with making full use of all the tools given to me.  Once I got a better understanding of the game's systems, the fun really multiplied as Eternal is much more challenging than 2016 and you have to play faster and smarter than in the previous game in order to win.  Eternal is a good followup game if you are part of the hardcore crowd that gets their jollies playing Nightmare mode and you think 2016's Nightmare mode was too easy.  You can no longer overly rely on one weapon for an entire fight due to lower ammo pools and you have to use your chainsaw more to stay on top of ammo reserves.  This change along with adding weaknesses to enemies makes a world of change, where some might have preferred the more simple system of Doom 2016, here it has changed the game radically and there is more setplay involved with making sure you use x ammo for y enemy.  You really have to drop most of your Doom 2016 knowledge and be ready to jump in to a harder game, maybe get kicked around a bit before things start to click.  If you wanted a harder more challenging game than Doom 2016, you should pick this game up.  If you liked the more simple style of 2016, approach with caution and MAYBE wait for a sale or watch some videos to see if it's something you want to get if you were mainly an easy/normal difficulty type of player in Doom 2016.

_childDocuments_.review: All I see when I close my eyes and when I sleep now are the glory kill highlight, chainsaws, weapon combos and demons.Please helpDo not let the appearance of the game deceive you. Doom Eternal is a resource management strategy game in the skin of an FPS. If you are going in from Doom 2016, or another FPS, prepare for a different experience. Doom Eternal ditches the typical FPS formula and builds you from the ground up. Other FPS's (incl. Doom 2016) allow you to win the game with any basic play style or any weapon. Doom Eternal requires you to learn a specific set of rules in order to survive. Your arsenal is a giant tool box used for different situations, which you need to assess and react to really fast. No weapon is useless, or becomes defunct as the game progresses.The main philosophy of this game is: Every encounter, every weapon and every monster are either here to teach you, or to challenge you.The early game experience differs from the late game experience. You are started off with only a single gun, and get taught vital resource management skills. Afterwards, the game grows in size and complexity, and you are encouraged to experiment and formulate tactics using all tools you've obtained in order to succeed. Every encounter is either to introduce a new concept you will need to survive, or to test your knowledge of what you have obtained thus far. If you didn't learn something properly, or didn't execute it properly, that is why you die.By the end of the game, you will formulate weapon combos, using all of the 7 main weapons, and mastering the game's tool box rewards you with fast kill times. Use the right tools for the enemy to succeed. Does this sound similar? Yes, this is literally the same game loop and progression as a Real Time Strategy game.The exploration aspect of the game is often under looked by the people who are just in the game for the combat loop. I feel the exploration of Doom Eternal is dialled in just right. There are enough collectibles and upgrades for exploration to feel satisfying and rewarding without taking out from the main experience.The upgrades are different from typical FPS games. In other FPS games, upgrades allow you to become min-maxed, and obsolete the game challenge. In Doom Eternal, the max upgraded player is just the full tool box, and you need to unlock upgrades to obtain those tools in order to succeed.The story of Doom Eternal is simple, and not a cinematic masterpiece, but doesn't need to be. It is unserious, often times humorous. I can't give a full review on the game's lore because I never really took the time to read all of it. I don't usually take game lore seriously in general anyways. The games story is simple enough to drive the arcade action into play, and is satisfying enough.In conclusion: Doom Eternal is a satisfying Resource Management Strategy Game which takes a fresh spin on the FPS genre. It is not a game of click the bad guy to win. You have a diverse tool set needed to be learnt and mastered in order to simply survive and make it to the next challenge. It is ironic that at a distance, the game appears to be mindless. The digital manifestation of violence (which it still is). Yet as the player, it is an extremely strategic and calculated arcade type game, which is extremely satisfying once you have learnt how to operate within the game's structure.

_childDocuments_.review: is everything a sequel to 2016’s  needed to be, and that alone would be impressive enough. And yet somehow it manages to be even more.  is the core concept of  amplified tenfold, but it wears its own identity plainly: this is a game of power-ups, health potions, and secrets, finding a sense of purpose in the arcade worlds of games past. The fundamentals of that ingenious reworking of the  formula, however, are intact. The combat remains thrillingly visceral, meaning you’ll spend your battles dashing between enemies, peppering them with bullets, plasma, rockets, and more to induce the stagger state and perform that life-sustaining glory kill you will so desperately need.And you will need to do this again, and again, and again. And again.Repetition is a really interesting concept to me, as it’s something games rely heavily on to properly function. Games test your patience and attention by insisting that you repeat the same essential tasks over and over, often for hours at a time. It’s especially true of the first person shooter, which fixes your perspective behind a hand and a gun and asks that you spend the overwhelming majority of your time pulling the trigger on bad guys. I don’t think that actually sounds particularly appealing when thinking about entertainment value, but games have found a way to make that repetition not only attractive, but downright .I don’t think there’s a point during the 23 hours I invested in the game where I didn’t want to do the thing  wanted me to do (actually, that’s a bit of a lie…). In fact, as I write this, fresh off my victory over the final boss, I want to close the document and go submit to those repetitions all over again.But first let me tell you about the lie. I started  on ‘hard’ difficulty as I recalled spending the final stages of  wiping the floor with Hell's legions. I thought of myself as something of a badass, and I felt confident I could handle whatever  threw at me. This was not the case; Hell had returned prepared. The initial fights were gruelling and not in the way they were meant to be. I struggled and pretty early on I found myself not having fun, which is generally a bad sign. I wondered if it was something wrong with the game itself – that id had tinkered so much with those aforementioned fundamentals the scales had tipped in the wrong direction.Well, no. The problem, as it so often is, was me. Apparently I'm not a badass at all, so I had to take it down to 'normal'. Some balancing has taken place between the games, meaning ‘normal’ difficulty is arguably more of a challenge. I still died every now and then, but my fun had been amplified and I felt capable of dealing with the numerous obstacles the game presented.Sadly, difficulty does not impact my ability to correctly time jumps, so I died just as often there. Jumping? Yeah, there’s a lot of it! Too much, honestly. The Doom Slayer is a big, clunky instrument of war, and the game too often demands some frustrating acrobatics. Or perhaps the problem is still me? We’ll never know. Good luck with your own jumping. is a bigger game in every sense, and nowhere is this more evident than in its enormous levels. It’s easily the most varied in the franchise, finally taking us away from Mars and depositing us on Earth to repel the demon invasion fans have been clamouring for since 2004. But what’s most striking about  is that it’s not in the least content to settle there, taking us on a dimension-hopping adventure through ancient ruins, cultist strongholds, frozen wastes, alien cityscapes, and a bunch of other places new to .The succession of new environments is mighty impressive for a franchise that’s relied on the dual red landscapes of Mars and Hell since its inception. It’s less impressive when you consider that environmental variety is just a given in most other series, but as it’s , you know, well done. You left Mars. Perhaps once they realised it wasn’t such a difficult step after all, they whispered amongst themselves that they could try doing it again -- in the . So, Hell may have come to Earth, but thankfully the secret to its undoing lies elsewhere in the cosmos.It’s a feat made possible by the game’s eagerness to embrace and then vigorously expand its mythology. I have to admit that  lost me here. It’s so deeply submerged in its own lore-laden world it mostly forgets to tell a story. I don’t think there’s a whole lot to care about, plot-wise. There’s Khan Maykrs and Sentinels annnnd you lost me. It’s all a bit too serious; the premise is bonkers, and I feel lightening the tone in places would have mitigated some of the mythology's stuffiness.Its best moments are found not in the inane ramblings of Hell Priests, but when it’s able to mock its own fetishisation of the Doom Slayer. There’s a point roughly halfway through the game that relies on a creatively insane use of the BFG. It’s inventive and quite funny, but it’s also something more important: it’s the essence of the game perfectly distilled into a single moment. A moment that, to me, is where these games need to be – not in the wilderness of arcane jargon.In the absence of relatable, compelling characters or a clear thematic purpose, I switched off to the comings and goings of the plot and surrendered to the sweet, sweet thrill of making demons bleed and blowing ♥♥♥♥ up. I’d watch cutscenes and moments later I couldn’t tell you what happened in them. I had the same experience with , too. It’s like being in a Warhammer codex instead of a narrative, and that’s not really my jam.So, is that a problem? It’s a good question. If the game wanted me to care about its world, it failed. As it is, I’m not sure it does! It rarely acted as impediment to enjoyment. The real narrative is the one you spin yourself between battles, elevated to sheer poetry when cracking an arena to best counter the relentless horde of foes. What’s the best combination of runes? Which weapon upgrades do I prefer? These are your concerns, and for the most part  knows it.If  had proved to be more of the same, I’d have been pretty content. id have unlocked something raw and powerful with their vigorous, demanding combat system, and I was (commander) keen to see more of it. Fortunately,  is both much more of the same  surprisingly fresh where it counts. As a game it’s repetitive. Deeply repetitive. And in that repetition is its success; it has cracked the code to the perfect manoeuvre, one I'll never tire of repeating, and its name is the glory kill.So when it comes to killing things, there's nothing quite like . With it,  has at long last reclaimed territory it ceded decades ago.

_childDocuments_.review: DOOM Eternal, developed by id Software, thrusts players into an adrenaline-fueled, demon-slaying rampage that stands as a testament to the frenetic brilliance of the first-person shooter genre. With its heart-pounding action, brutal gameplay mechanics, and immersive world, DOOM Eternal delivers an unforgettable experience that will satisfy fans of the series and newcomers alike. However, it's worth noting that the game may lack extensive replayability for some players.First and foremost, DOOM Eternal's combat is a ferocious dance of destruction that sets it apart from its peers. The combination of relentless gunplay, visceral melee attacks, and the ability to execute glory kills creates a gratifyingly aggressive and fast-paced experience. The introduction of the "Destructible Demons" system adds an extra layer of strategy, as players strategically target specific enemy body parts to gain advantages in combat. The depth of the combat mechanics ensures that each encounter feels exhilarating and rewarding, encouraging players to experiment with various weapon mods and abilities.The level design in DOOM Eternal is a masterpiece in itself. The intricate and visually stunning environments take players on a tour through hellish landscapes, ancient ruins, and futuristic facilities. The levels are ingeniously designed, offering a perfect balance of exploration, platforming, and intense combat scenarios. Secrets and collectibles are scattered throughout, rewarding players for their keen observation and curiosity. The level of detail and craftsmanship in each location is a testament to the developers' dedication to delivering a rich and immersive world.Furthermore, DOOM Eternal's heavy metal-inspired soundtrack is a true work of art. The pulse-pounding rhythms and aggressive guitar riffs perfectly complement the breakneck speed and intensity of the gameplay. Each track pumps adrenaline into your veins, driving you forward in a relentless pursuit of demon obliteration. The audio design, from the bone-crushing sound effects to the guttural roars of the enemies, further immerses players in the chaotic and otherworldly atmosphere.While DOOM Eternal's campaign offers a thrilling and satisfying experience, some players may find that the game lacks extensive replayability. Once the main story is completed, there may not be enough incentive for players to revisit the campaign. While the addition of collectibles and hidden challenges adds some replay value, it may not be enough to fully engage those seeking a robust post-campaign experience. However, it's important to note that the game does offer a multiplayer mode called "Battlemode," where players can engage in intense 2v1 battles as either a fully loaded Slayer or a pair of demons. This mode can provide an additional layer of entertainment for those seeking competitive multiplayer experiences.In conclusion, DOOM Eternal is a relentlessly exhilarating and visually stunning masterpiece that excels in delivering fast-paced, demon-slaying action. The game's combat mechanics, level design, and powerful soundtrack come together to create an adrenaline-fueled experience that leaves players breathless. While the game may not offer extensive replayability beyond the main campaign, the sheer quality of the gameplay and the immersive world make DOOM Eternal a must-play for fans of the series and anyone in search of an electrifying first-person shooter experience.
