_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece, plain and simple.  There are numerous other reviews explaining why the singleplayer campaign is amazing, and all of them are valid.  What I want to review here is the game's unique multiplayer experience, "Battlemode" (or BM for short).BM is an asymmetric 2v1 game mode that pits one player who takes on the role of the Doomslayer against two players (and their NPC minions) who take on the role of playable demon characters (as of the time of writing this, 5 demon characters were playable).  There have been many players who most likely tried this mode a few times and didn't enjoy it.  I'm not here to say anyone is wrong for having an opinion, and certainly everyone who plays this mode competitively knows that there are some problems that need to be fixed.  But I'm here to tell you that BM is absolutely amazing and is by far the most fun I've had with any multiplayer game released in the past 10 years.  One of the core design principles that the developers used to guide their development of this game was the concept of a "fun zone," which is to say that they have a vision of what "good gameplay" looks like, and they design the game to reward habits and behaviors in line with that vision and punish those outside of that vision.  It is my opinion that a majority of the players who view BM in an overall negative light are those who have most likely not yet experienced the "fun zone" of this game mode.  It needs to be stated that playing BM requires all of the singleplayer campaign skills as just a fundamental baseline - to really play successfully and against truly skilled opponents, you need to elevate your skills beyond just the level needed to play the game in singleplayer.  In fact, playing BM at a high level is the most challenging thing this game has to offer.  As such, players who want to push the limits of skill and creativity and who have a competitive mindset will naturally be able to find an extreme amount of satisfaction from playing and mastering this game mode, but ONLY if they give it enough time to realize that they need to learn more advanced skills than what works in singleplayer.  And that's only talking about playing the game as the Slayer; when you play a demon character, you have a whole new skillset to learn and master that is different from anything you've ever seen in a Doom game.Now a word on some of the current flaws in BM.  The biggest one is lag/latency issues.  It's impossible to know how much is due to the game's netcode itself versus the natural latency that occurs based on the geographic regions of the players connecting (i.e., if you live farther away from a server, your ping is higher which means lag affects you more).  There is simply nothing that can be done to fix geographic latency and it is not the game's fault that this exists.  But due to the fact that this game allows for some very fast actions, when a player's screen doesn't accurately reflect every action, it can be frustrating.  Luckily, the developers have been quite open and engaging with the BM community and have stated that they are working to fix these issues.  We also know that they are working to add a ranked mode (presumably after the lag issues are fixed) and additional demon characters.  Given the current situation with COVID-19, I see these as positive steps and am willing to accept that implementing these things may take more time than what we impatient gamers might normally expect (or demand) from the developer who took our money and promised us greatness.  You are entitled to your own judgments about this.  There are also still some balancing issues, though the devs also release hotfixes every so often to try to address community concerns (the bigger problem is that the community in general is the same as all other gaming communities and tends to overreact to everything, but that's just gamer logic).  Overall, I am pleased with the effort the devs have shown in addressing the flaws of BM and am willing to be patient as they work to implement changes over time.But even with the flaws considered, my experience with BM has been exceptionally fun.  I play this game almost entirely for it's multiplayer content now, as I enjoy it even more than I enjoy the singleplayer campaign (though do still replay the singleplayer, because it is indeed very awesome and well worth the price).  I encourage everyone to give BM a try with an open mind, realizing that it requires different skills than what you may have acquired from just singleplayer or from prior FPS titles.  All of the top tier BM players are very welcoming to new players and many of them stream BM content, making them good resources if you want to ask questions and get a better understanding of the "fun zone" of this game.  You don't have to become a godlike player to find the fun in this game's multiplayer, and once you do, you'll realize that there is nothing else like it on the market today.  In that respect, I personally am grateful that id Software made the decision to create this game mode rather than rehash the classic deathmatch that has been done over and over again over the past 30 years.  Battlemode is unique and it stands out, but because of that you will have to put in more effort to master it because not all of your prior skills will translate over to it.  To me, this is a strength and makes it worth wanting to play and master.  If you share my opinion, give it a try (especially if you have a friend to play with), and you might also come to realize just how much fun the Doom Eternal multiplayer really is.

_childDocuments_.review: I went in expecting more of Doom 2016, which was a big mistake on my part. The three hours of gameplay I had prompted me to refund this.The game is messier with level design, with more invisible walls and unexplorable terrain which looks explorable, while also featuring less enjoyable platforming sections. The combat is solid, but seems a lot less polished than Doom 2016 due to the introduction of more combat mechanics.The levels and graphics do look amazing, but the amount of detail in each level seems lacking when compared to the previous title. Exploration also takes a back seat in this game, making collectibles and secrets feel much less rewarding.The game does feature timed events and challenges which can grant alternate skins, which seems pretty pointless in a game that is primarily a singleplayer first person shooter. Doesn't really bother me, but I don't really see the point of having it in the game to begin with.The story is noticeably more obvious than the previous game, which was incredibly jarring to me. I enjoyed Doom 2016's cutscenes much more than this games, as they felt a lot less restrictive, were much shorter, had more personality, and didn't appear so frequently. Also, the game forces the Doom Slayer to stop moving when interacting with objects such as the toy collectibles, killing any momentum you may have had previously, which was not present in Doom 2016.At this point in time, the UI is terrible. The HUD in game is easy to get used to, but everything else needs a rework. The main menu seems like it came from a generic multiplayer title, the codex menu is overly clunky making information difficult to read, and the weapon upgrade and armour upgrade menus are too bogged down and could use space more efficiently. The inclusion of timed events do not help in this regard.The inclusion of a player hub also seems fairly pointless and seems ridiculous considering the character. The Doom Slayer has a satellite base similar to the Justice League's Watchtower. I couldn't help but laugh at the idea, while also being disappointed that the game hides player upgrades and skins behind locked doors in this area. It also has a "prison" arena where you can fight more demons, which at worst seems pointless, as that is exactly what you're doing all game, while at best it has the potential to be a good time waster. At the very least, you might find some funny throwbacks to the classic games that'll keep you entertained here.The first thing this game asks for when you before you can play the game is a Bethesda account login. You cannot play the game without one as far as I'm aware. I can't say I'm a fan of this decision, especially after the numerous issues Bethesda has had regarding user information and general security.The game could be a solid experience, but I cannot recommend this title while it is still at full price. Maybe when the game sells for $30 aud or less, but not $99.95

_childDocuments_.review: now THIS game, oh boy this is a game alright (a good one at that). i'll try to keep this brief:pros:- faster and more intense combat than doom 2016- you actually have to use your whole kit to survive- game is harder than 2016 which i personally think is great (i played both games on ultra-violence difficulty)- the places you visit look cool as f*ck- looks good and runs really well- larger variety of demons, and the guns still feel as good as ever- they went bigger on the lore/story of this universe and i personally think its pretty cool- the game has some cool cinematic moments- whoever thought putting a grapple hook on the super shotgun was a good idea needs a raise- the slayer gates are the best part of this game, they're ridiculously intense and satisfying to complete- movement feels really good and most platforming sections feel fine- the soundtrack is just as good if not better than 2016, mick gordon certainly did not slack off- there's zero microtransactions...cons:- ...but why is there a f*cking battle pass?- SOME texture pop-in- a little buggy, me or enemies would get stuck in terrain causing me to restart (this only happened twice)- my game crashed once in the last level but that's just me- invisible walls during some platforming sections suck- whoever thought that purple slime sh*t was a good idea needs their nose broken, it is not fun to be in at all (thankfully it only happens a few times and they are very short-lived)- SOME platforming sections are straight up bad- the low ammo count and harder difficulty may turn off some (i was fine with it though)- the UI is not that good looking but i eventually got used to it so whatever- the hub world is bigger than it needs to be- while i think the story/lore is cool, most of it is still told through data logs which is counter-intuitive to this game- the big increase in cutscenes may turn off some people, and some of the voice acting is kind of cringey - the bosses, while not bad at all, are a little underwhelming. i preferred 2016's bosses- the final boss was cool as f*ck as the scale of the fight was huge but i felt like what i was doing for most of the fight was clearing out demonskeep in mind my pros significantly outweigh my cons, and some of my cons are a bit nitpicky. this game is definitely worthy of being a sequel, and i still had a lot of fun playing it. i haven't tried the multiplayer yet, and i know there's more content coming but going off of just the campaign, this game is worth it if you enjoyed 2016. i have seen people who loved 2016 but not enjoy this game and that's fine, i sort of get why but i f*cking love this game. its not a 10/10 by any means, but this is a VERY strong 9/10.this is probably going to be my game of the year.EDIT: i have tried the multiplayer, its better than 2016's multiplayer as that game's MP was an absolute mess and was super fast paced but had very slow TTK (time to kill). eternal's multiplayer is actually pretty decent and surprisingly well balanced.

_childDocuments_.review: DOOM Eternal is a Masterpiece and marks the end of this generation of Ego Shooters. In that regard, it may just be the best shooter currently on the market. It is flawless, packed with content and does not support greedy monetising methods like paid skins, exp booster or even loot boxes. Eternal is in many ways the greatest achievement of id Software and I can only hope they will get all the support and freedom with their next project.But as every entertainment product, this game also has it's target audience, which is why I cannot recommend it to everyone. Eternal demands you to learn its rules; manage your resources, constantly reposition yourself, learn enemy behaviour and which weapon works best in your current situation. And if you can't; it's on you. The game is fair but brutal. It - in almost every way - improves on its predecessor, which is why I recommend you to play through DOOM (2016) on a higher difficulty to  to play this game. After which, you won't be able to go back and play the worse 2016 game.If you like a challenge, enjoyed DOOM (2016) but thought it wasn't very demanding or even enjoyed the mechanics of Quake, then this will be your new favourite shooter.I, for one, am having a blast with it.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM Eternal

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews because the public seems to develop an opinion on the game and everyone hears about it quickly and knows what's up.This is one of the few exceptions.Note that I played this on Nightmare from the get go and this review is based on that first playthrough.Doom Eternal is the perfect follow up to Doom 2016. Eternal builds upon what has already been established in 2016's entry. Platforming feels great and isn't really intrusive as some would think. Going from cliff to cliff feels great.As far as everything else goes, Eternal eases you in with a small number of tools to work with. As you progress, you add more and more into your arsenal. With so many tools at your disposal, you have so much to work with and so much variety that you should probably start thinking about what works best against certain enemies and what kind of ammo to pop off first.The pacing, the enemies, the guns all feel amazing. You have 2 types of grenades, a flamethrower, and a huge arsenal of weapons to switch through you sometimes forget you had. How you use these weapons play a big part in your success. You're rewarded for hot swapping and comboing weapons and grenades with each other with massive damage. Knowing when to use what is half the battle. My only nitpick about the combat is that I wish you moved just a tad bit slower to make things even faster than what it is. Doom Eternal is just a giant gorefest with nonstop action that gets addicting the more you play. As soon as I beat the game, I went straight back in with everything I had to do it again. Everything encounter feels like a dance that you need to adjust to. Where you go and what you use ultimately determines your success.The only other single player FPS campaigns I really think come close to this level of fun would be BioShock 1 and DusK. That's a big claim I'll happily stand behind.Tl;dr - Super fast paced shooty shooty that doesn't give a ♥♥♥♥ about story. Buy if you likey smash boom boom blood parties.

_childDocuments_.review: Was a solid game until the latest update decided to add a driver-based anti-cheat for the online mode that I never have and never will play. _childDocuments_.name: DOOM Eternal

_childDocuments_.review: Ladies, Gentlemen,The latest update introduces a new denuvo Anti-Cheat, a mandatory service (yes, even when only playing single player) that grants itself full access to your PC. Not surprisingly, the priority of ensuring the legitimacy of the "single player experience" leaves you, the consumer, at a disadvantage. This includes a variable performance impact while playing the game, and a computer that as a whole is now more vulnerable to security exploits. The latter is a result of the amount of privileges this new anti-cheat comes with.It's sad enough that this game -requires- a Bethesda account to play. It's more pathetic that this is introduced months after its release, as this effectively prevents consumers who didn't agree to this when they initially purchased at launch from a refund.100% avoid this game until this is addressed and resolved.05/21/2020 - Devs have stated the supreme anti-cheat will be removed in next update (for  sp only I believe).
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM Eternal

_childDocuments_.review: Sneaking malware tier "anti-cheat" software into your game silently as possible months after release when most of the people who have already purchased it can no longer get a refund is a new low in unethical behavior by game publishers/devs. EA and Activision don't even pull stuff like this. If Valve cares about their customer base at all they'll honor refund requests regardless of play time or purchase date.Update: I wasn't able to get a refund using the normal refund request (It's largely automated and my request was denied because I had over 2 hours game time) but after opening a normal support ticket explaining the situation they agreed to a steam wallet refund. Not perfect (I would have preferred to just get my money back) but better than nothing.Update 2: Bethesda has replied to my review informing me that they have removed Denuvo anti-cheat from their game, and while this is a welcome change it doesn't change the fact that it's a fix to a mistake that never should have made in the first place. I hope other players who already own Doom Eternal enjoy the game and have a good time, but I cannot in good conscience recommend any game that comes from a developer or publisher that engages in this sort of behavior and only fixes their mistake after *massive* player backlash.

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of DOOM 2016 and the original DOOM games, I can confidently say this is one of the best, if not THE best first person shooter campaign I have ever played.The game does "almost" everything perfectly. While you might struggle with the limited ammo as you are first learning the game, once you get used to the new mechanics and pacing you will enjoy it just as much as any other part of the game. Instead of using the same weapon repeatedly, you will find certain weapons and even specific weapon mods are best strategically used against certain enemy types, or even stages in the fight.Before long you will be strategically dashing, jumping, hooking and rocketjumping around a fight, leaving lesser demons to survive as a source of ammo (from a chainsaw kill) or armor (from a blame belch kill effect) after you use your initial health pool and resources to tackle the first wave of heavies. The talk about the "Doom combat dance" is so true, you are never stopping, always looking to use specific weapons to hit certain demons and their weak spots. The movement is fast, MUCH faster than Doom 2016 and at points even surpassing stuff like Quake.One of the best factors is that the combat is so polished, so varied and deep, that regardless of how good you are, you can always make improvements, going back and repeating levels as you get better. The first time you meet a Marauder, you might get your ass handed to you a few times, but later in the game you'll be facing off 2 or 3 at once while fighting off an army of demons at the same time, without breaking the rhythm of the combat loop.Needless to say, the music is fantastic, never skipping a beat. There are even some really atmospheric deep sores in some of the more "mysterious" parts of the story, differing from your typical rip and tear soundtrack, but still fitting perfectly. Talking about the story, there's plenty here, and while it may not be the "best" story ever made, it does a really good job of going deeper into the idea of who the doom guy is and why he is so badass.As usual for a Doom game, there are plenty of secrets and metagame ways of playing, such as unlocking "cheat codes" to be able to go back to previous levels and play with some fun effects and modifiers which really add to the game's replayability. There's a nice additional feature where you can find a location ingame where all your collectables will be displayed as you progress through the campaign, and you can even play music disks which you find throughout.All that praise aside, I have two issues with the game. The first is that while the gameplay, pacing and level designs are fantastic, at times, especially on your first playthrough, you will enter some platforming or "environmental challenge" sections which completely grind the pace of the game to a halt. It's really jarring when you go from gunning around at 200 miles an hour to being forces to walk slow speec, unable to dash or jump while trying to find that specific hidden thing to press to progress to the next section. These moments are relatively rare though and I can only think of two in the 14+ hours I spent to complete the game on the hardest difficulty. The rest of the platforming is done rather well.Secondly, the multiplayer is "meh." While It's a creative concept to have 2 demon players and 1 doomslayer face off, it gets old quick and the matchmaking seems way off base. Not only that but there is considerable lag in these games. Definitely the least enjoyable part of Doom Eternal.In conclusion, this game is a true masterpiece, and I highly reccomend everyone to get out there and RIP AND TEAR!10/10 (excluding multiplayer)

_childDocuments_.review: 666/10 would slay again...but actually it's a pretty amazing game. Feels like a weird mashup between DOOM 2016, Metroid Prime, and (at times) Dark Souls (yeah, seriously).Oh, and the music is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing (as per usual -- Mick Gordon has gone full industrial Meshuggah or something).When I started...I wasn't really sure about some of the new direction.  The interface is *weird* and has this odd 80's vibe or something (no complaints there -- just weird to see in a DOOM game).  The gameplay felt way faster and more intense than DOOM 2016 and I just wasn't sure if they were making a DOOM game or Quake 5.Turns out they were just making a really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ brutal DOOM game.By the time you get all the core mechanics unlocked you start entering this wild flow state in every major battle (and you kinda *have* to in order to get through everything -- played on Ultra-Violence and I think that's probably the "definitive" way to experience the game). You start to figure out how all the enemies work and you figure out strategies for how to handle pairing of enemies.  That last part is why I mentioned earlier that it feels like a FromSoftware game -- if you've played any of those (and I recommend you do), you realize individual enemies (save for bosses) are manageable. You can deal with them even when you just start the game (I'm excluding Bloodborne from that statement -- you kinda get dropped into some intense fights in the beginning of that one). It's only when the game starts throwing interesting *pairings* of enemies at you that you start to realize "oh, this is *really* hard".  DOOM Eternal is like that -- you can handle individual enemies -- the rooms they throw at you are what make it interesting.By the time you finish, you really will feel unstoppable (well, kinda -- the final two boss battles are HARD and you have to figure out the playstyle the developers intended which can suck because the rest of game you need to manage resources -- by the end it's just a "♥♥♥♥ it -- LET'S RIP AND TEAR"...which is hindsight sounds pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rad).In summary: the meta strategy is *insanely* developed, the story is somehow badass as ♥♥♥♥, and if you *at all* enjoyed DOOM 2016, you should definitely buy this.

_childDocuments_.review: Biggest ripoff of this year.After Bethesda decided to add Denuvo Anti-Cheat, the game won't launch (I'm on Ubuntu 20.04). I would speculate this anti-cheat technology is an attempt to protect their precious micro-transactions they'll inevitably be rolling out later this Summer because it wouldn't make sense to add such a controversial and divisive piece of software for a game-mode that makes up maybe 10% of the actual game-play. This is fundamentally a single-player game. Why does it need anti-cheating? Between what happened with this and Fallout76, I'm done; I won't be purchasing anymore games from Bethesda, which is unfortunate because I was previously enjoying it very much.EDIT: I'm glad Bethesda has corrected their error, but I still cannot recommend this game. I understand these decisions are not reflective of every employee at the company, but this violation of trust between a software proprietor and its patrons is more severe than I am willing to tolerate. It never should have been an issue in the first place. Copyright law grants certain privileges to software developers, and I do not tolerate abuse of those privileges. I will be continuing my boycott.

_childDocuments_.review: The invasive Denuvo aside, Doom Eternal is a decent arena shooter.  But it is a terrible Doom game.  The new enemy art design left me wondering if i wasn't actually fighting the Strogg at times and the story and worlds (especially in the earlier levels) made me think i was playing a first person mod of the Darksiders.  Only a couple of times in this game did i "feel" as if i was fighting the denizens of hell, but instead i usually felt like I was fighting multi-dimensional and highly technologically advanced aliens that had weird names for their stuff.  The player felt as if he was moving at a snails pace a lot of the time (i'm assuming to make the dash useful in combat).  And it may have just been me but on the higher difficulties it felt like i was running away from enemies 60% of the time waiting for my chainsaw to recharge so i could get some ammo from enemies and get back into the fight.  I guess Doom guy is pretty forgetful.  He forgot his flashlight in Doom 3 and in Doom Eternal he forgot his backpack.Don't get me wrong, Doom Eternal is still fun on a first play through in terms of combat but i fear that Doom Eternal has completely forgotten what (in my opinion, the father of FPS games) Doom, really was.  In short Doom Eternal is a better reboot of Serious Sam then it is of Doom II.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR:Overall: 9/10Campaign: 10/10TAG1: 9.5/10TAG2: 8/10Battlemode: 7/10My rambling review: This game was so much fun from start to finish, everything from the soundtrack and graphics to gameplay and level design is just fantastic, you can get so immersed in being the DOOM SLAYER - especially when you get to grips with the mechanics and balance of Chainsaw - Flamethrower - Execute to restore your ammo, armour and health respectively. I got all but one collectable because the last one was a right pain, so probs add on about 3 hours in secret hunting and level replays - maybe another hour because i got stuck at a few points and boom a 20 hour or so campaign with lots of lore if you want it but can skip over if you don't. Absolutely fantastic.edit1: I played TAG1 the first week of March 2021 to give you an idea, as I know some things changed with certain updates. I think TAG1 was a fantastic addition to the series, the difficulty increased with the addition of turrets and whiplash spectres was great, and the blood makyrs were a pain the arse - a cross between the drones and the khan makyrs. The level designs were fantastic, a real difference from main campaign, especially the swamps. There's the addition of spirits as well, which possess other demons and make them super-powered - they're definitely ones to prioritise, i found them more difficult than a buff token, demons are faster and stronger and chase you relentlessly, the possessed marauder was a lot of fun, can't believe I didn't die on that.Once you kill the possessed demon the spirit is exposed and you have to microwave them with the plasma rifle, finally making that mod useful.The final boss for TAG1 is pretty difficult, because you have to take out 2 spirit possessed demons before you do damage to him, i didn't struggle with the first round but the dread knight + pain elemental was difficult.TAG2 was fantastic conclusion, i enjoyed the pacing and even more challenges - it built upon mini scenarios that it introduced in TAG1 where it'll spawn in like 30 of 1 type of demon, but with the ammo type that perfectly counters them. My favourite was walking into a room of like 50 boxes of shotgun ammo thinking OOO ITS ABOUT TO GET REAL and it spawned in loads of stone imps which you have to kill with auto shotgun, you don't even have to take your finger off the trigger for the whole encounter just run around picking up more ammo and keep smashing those imps.Speaking of stone imps, they're 1 of three new enemies, others are cursed prowler - if it hits you you get 'cursed' can't dash and take damage over time, only way to break the curse is to blood punch the cursed prowler, a real challenge in the middle of a fight. Also armoured baron, break armour immediately when mace flashes green or gradually with plasma rifle then just shoot him til he dead before the armour regenerates.There's also riot shield guys, they're easy, just soldiers who's shields don't break, shoot a rocket or grenade behind them and don't even blink twice. Last of all there's screechers, ambient zombies but if you kill them they empower all demons around them for like 20 or 30 seconds or something, AVOID, they're designed to throw you a curve ball of 'hey actually maybe don't shoot everything in front of you'. I love it.I was a little disappointed with the dark lord's design, i didn't find him particularly imposing or intimidating, and the boss fight i thought was really easy for what is meant to be the real big bad - i struggled more on the icon of sin.After all the original game and both DLCs I'll give it 9/10 overall.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom Eternal is a challenging and intense single player arena FPS, with a large focus on resource management and intelligent play.  The game has some great arena movement with additional; dashing, double jumping and a grapplehook, (meathook).  The game also requires you to juggle 8 guns, two grenade types, a flamethrower, a demonic sword, a chainsaw and your fists, to slaughter hordes of demons. Demons have their own weaknesses and tactics.  Certain enemies have powerful ranged weapons that can be destroyed with precise fire, certain weapons will do increased damage to specific demons.  This all accumulates to a late game that involves encounters regularly involving 1-3 mini boss type enemies, 4-5 large demons, 1-3 support demons and a constant steam of, "fodder", demons in some really interesting arenas. You'll want to strategically focus down on the larger demons while tactically moving to avoid being surrounded.  If you're not intelligent in your play you'll find yourself desperately scrambling around trying to isolate a lowly imp to chainsaw. Yes, the game does have multiplayer but it was pretty much DOA.  While I liked the asymmetric mode, it's not for everyone and very frustrating to play due to it's small playerbase and huge skill gaps.  As a new player you'll likely find yourself waiting for 10-20 minutes for a match that will involve you being obliterated and back searching for a new lobby in under two minutes.  I will say the SpiceyDemon's Discord community is great and almost mandatory to join if you want to really enjoy the multiplayer aspect of the game. Graphically, the game is a masterpiece.  When I first played the game I spotted a flying demon high up in the distance.  I took a shot and was stunned as a chunk of it's flesh tumbled down to the ground and landed at my feet. Yes, when you shoot demons their skin and meat tears away from their bodies! Not only does this look fantastic, it serves the purpose of being able to gauge how much HP demons have remaining. This game is an absolute visual treat, with it's vivid colours really helping with identifying enemies and pickups at high speeds. Sound wise, soundtrack is yet another masterpiece from Mick Gordon, guns sound great and the demons have their own recognisable and blood curdling screams. It sounds like an orgy at Satan's personal nightclub. Difficulty wise, the game is seriously challenging on higher difficulties.  At this point the game also has Horde Mode and plenty of Master Levels that push the difficulty to it's absolute limits.  There's also Ultra Nightmare difficulty that challenges the player to complete the entire game on the hardest difficulty without dying once. If you're more of a casual player, the game is still playable! Put it on easy and you'll still be faced by the same hordes of demons but with less aggression and much less damaging attacks. The game has also some light RPG elements, that basically power you up throughout the game and let you have some perks to customise your play style. The AI is pretty good, it all feels right. Sneaky enemies will constantly try to flank you, ranged enemies will find vantage points and close quarter enemies will rush you. The level design is pretty good but overall sadly it's mainly a linear string of arena battles. Still a pretty high standard of great looking levels but besides the simplistic secret hunting, there's not much in the way of exploration or alternative routes. Some people are up in arms about the platforming but there's around 2 minutes of pure platforming in the entire game and it's very simplistic, particularly when compared to the platforming and aerial manoeuvres you'll be performing during the late game combat sections. If you can't handle doing a couple of dash jumps between arenas you're really not going to enjoy having to meathook launch yourself into the air then double-dashing and ballista boosting to a jump pad while raining your arsenal down on demons. TL;DR

_childDocuments_.review: Summarizing DOOM Eternal as DOOM 2016 only better, unfortunately, does not do the game justice. And with that I mean DOOM 2016, because Eternal is a tedious and tangled mess. The level-design, while varied and generally wonderful is also very linear in the sense that it feels like a corridor shooter. The narrative... well let's say it this way. While "RIP AND TEAR" is a great tagline, making it the centerpiece of your narrative by repeating it over and over in the dialogue comes across as overly juvenile and puerile. Somehow the guys at id Software decided that fleshing out the world of DOOM with a "real" story and some "real" lore was just what the game needed. Unfortunately, the end result is a "Codex" section filled with endless sections of jejune high school writing. See, the trick (like in DOOM 2016) is to NOT slap the player across the face with what an awesome intellectual project the game is supposed to be. As it stands, the player gets drowned in a sea of lore that nobody is really interested in and nobody will ever read. The end result comes across as immature and fatuous and is extremely tedious. Leave something to the player's imagination.Now the actual gameplay. It is faster—which is nice because DOOM 2016 felt like "ripping and tearing" through a group of disabled wheelchair-wielding demons—unfortunately to the point where DOOM Eternal is just a mess. The game skips the combat pistol altogether and gives you a shotgun right from the start. However, you will also encounter legions of ranged ADD enemies right off the bat. Thus, a general fight looks like a scene from a Bagdad 1991 night bombing during Operation Desert Storm—with tracers, bombs, missiles and bullets flying everywhere. Instead of prioritizing and strategizing your way through the combat arena's, all you'll do (all game long) is spamming the dodge button—which is surprisingly effective in negating any damage. This also means that there's also extremely little thought-process involved. Whereas DOOM 2016's combat felt more like a fine waltz, DOOM Eternal's combat flows more like a ballet while being administered electro-shocks. The hardest part of the game is actually dealing with it until you unlock the dash ability—which serves as a downright lobotomy.Multiplayer consists, during the time of writing, solely of the new BATTLEMODE, which is a doommarine vs demons, 1v2 PVP mode. The flow of it is really nice, but it's not really something that can tickle my fancy for a long time. The game really misses a team-based multiplayer mode (like DOOM 2016's TDM) to hold player's attention for a longer time. Perhaps the season pass will introduce some team-based multiplayer modes—but I doubt it. DOOM 2016's multiplayer was implemented as an afterthought without any anti-cheat or dedicated server support for that matter; I doubt they'll divert money and resources to a DOOM Eternal TDM mode from the season passes.So in conclusion, is DOOM Eternal a bad game? No, not really. Overall, I had a good time dashing around the map, shotgun-blasting and chainsaw-mêléeing my way through the game. Halfway through I decided to just ignore the callow in-your-face backstory of the "Makyrs". The overall experience is, unfortunately, lackluster. It improves on its predecessor in some area's; in others it's a complete step back. The lack of any decent multiplayer means you will most definitely and without a shroud of doubt only play this for the singleplayer campaign. The campaign is of decent size, but does not warrant full price. Get it discounted, ignore the season pass, chew through the first couple of levels and rip and tear through the campaign after that. 7/10EDIT: 01/07/20 After reading the privacy policy myself I must say I'm absolutely disgusted by the amount of information Zenimax wants to gather; it seems like selling privacy information is becoming their core business. Welcome to the USSRA comrad.After editing, Steam actually tells me they have to verify this review to make sure there's no "links to websites that attempt to steal information". Yeah imagine... oh the irony.

All in all I know most people came to this game for the campaign. Well all I can say is it is amazing, the level design is phenomenal(except for a couple very short underwater portions). All of the enemies are fun to kill(maybe not the Marauder, but I will discuss this later). I love the challenge of scarcity of ammo, health, and armor and having to chainsaw, flame belch, or glory demons to get them. It adds more depth than Doom 2016, and you are constantly thinking and planning your attacks. I honestly can't tell you how many adrenaline highs I got off of this game. This and Doom 2016 are games you must play if you are a fan of FPS!SPOILERSSo my thoughts on the Marauder...When you first meet one you think it is like a mini boss.After learning his weak spot you seem to think you have to kill everything else before you kill him(he kinda kills the flow of gameplay). I think the Marauder is very cool, I love his design and lore and I hope he is in the next game, but.........He definitely needs to be changed, his shield is OP, and I really hate that dog he summons.When he comes into an Arena I feel like "Great, now I have to kill this guy, which may take longer than I would like." Overall I would give this game a 9.5/10. There are flaws, but every game has them. It was and still is one of the best FPS experiences I have ever had along with Doom 2016. I am heavily looking forward to the DLC for this game!

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to begin by saying that I did play through several hours of this game and, while there are elements I like about it, this is NOT the game I expected by quite a long shot. I can't express how truly disappointed I am in what came from a long awaited sequel.  From the advertisements and the gameplay footage on the pre-release end, it sounded like a  fantastic experience and would add anything the original DOOM was missing, but what it delivers is an entirely different game. Allow me to elaborate:The feel of the game from even the title screen is extremely different, sacrificing the "welcome to Hell" vibe the original DOOM 2016 had for a more "trendy" feel I've come to associate with the rinse-and-repeat COD style of game.  The art style steps away from this rich, immersive style of design and transitions to more cartoony play where the HUD is bulky, colorful and menu options seem like cheap, half-hearted design.  The combat itself requires a certain...style of fight; in essence, each demon and enemy you come across has to be fought a certain way otherwise they just drink ammo.  This take the "kill everything, take no prisoners, rip and tear" vibe and gives it a platformer element that feels extremely awkward given the genre and pre-existing universe.On that note, the pre-existing universe is lost somewhere in the translation as Doomslayer somehow has a ship-castle thing with no explanation and VEGA, who, mind you, belongs  to the UAC is now your AI and you are effectively playing Destiny style missions where you are teleported into the world to complete a task to then fight your way to an exit portal, taking you "home".  The game spoon feeds you weapons while witholding ammo, forcing you to use the chainsaw constantly to have ammo/health, holds your hand through tutorials and forces you to comply with specific character building early on in the game, punishing the player for choices outside of the requirements by making enemies exponentially harder to fight.  The original DOOM 2016 style of finding weapons on bodies, or earning the BFG through solving a puzzle is lost, weapons are literally green, hovering as massive gun icons and screaming "COME GET ME".  To add insult to injury, every new killing skill acquired takes you OUT OF THE GAME and teleports you to some tutorial room to walk you step-by-step through how to use the skill while major platforming skills are just awkward pop-ups with a paragraph of text and little demonstration, so the teaching-learning ratio is extremely unbalanced.  More to that, the animations are redundant for glory kills and the melee in this game is essentially ONLY glory kills unlike DOOM 2016 where you could still punch your way through zombies to save ammo.  The game seemingly punishes the player's attempt to snipe or pre-clear an area at a distance by making the enemy AGGRO way too high; I had enemies virtually across the map attack me when I couldn't even see them, let alone hit them.  Stealth is NOT an option in any areas.  While I understand the idea of the game is to RIP and TEAR, it would be nice to actually get the drop on some enemies like you could in 2016.  Comparing DOOM 2016 and DOOM Eternal is like comparing the prodigal son to the accidental pregnancy of a one-night stand.

First, sometimes the path forward in the story isn't clear--it doesn't happen often, but there was a couple times where I was looking around the same area multiple times trying to figure out how to progress.  Second, the ammo reserves are very small which requires a ton of weapon switching.  Don't get me wrong, switching weapons for different situations is one of the great parts about DOOM, but this feels forced--I think they overdid it just a bit.  Anyway, very small and minor gripes with what is otherwise an amazing game.

_childDocuments_.review: DOOM Eternal is a game that takes first-person shooting to an entirely new level, with stunning visuals, heart-pumping action, and an epic storyline that will leave you on the edge of your seat. As the Slayer, you are tasked with battling the forces of Hell and saving humanity from certain destruction. And let me tell you, there is no shortage of demon-slaying in this game.From the moment you pick up your weapon, you are thrust into a world of chaos and destruction. The graphics are stunning, with every detail meticulously crafted to bring the game to life. The sound design is equally impressive, with every shot, scream, and explosion feeling like it's right there in the room with you.The gameplay is fast-paced and intense, with a variety of weapons and abilities at your disposal. There is no shortage of demons to fight, and each one presents a unique challenge that will keep you on your toes. The game is incredibly satisfying to play, and there is nothing quite like the feeling of ripping apart a demon with your bare hands.But what really sets DOOM Eternal apart is the level design. Each level is a masterpiece, with stunning visuals and intricate layouts that will keep you exploring for hours on end. There are secrets to uncover, challenges to complete, and hidden areas to discover, all of which add to the game's replayability.As for me, I can't help but goof around with the game. Sure, it's intense and challenging, but there's also something incredibly satisfying about goofing around with the physics engine and watching demons fly across the room. I've spent hours experimenting with different weapons and abilities, trying to find the most creative ways to take down the hordes of demons that stand in my way.Overall, DOOM Eternal is an incredible game that is not to be missed. It's an adrenaline-fueled, demon-slaying masterpiece that will keep you on the edge of your seat from start to finish. And if you're anything like me, you'll have a blast goofing around with it too. So what are you waiting for? Grab your weapon, suit up, and get ready to save humanity from the forces of Hell. The only thing they fear is you.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: This whole issue has been fixed with the removal of said Anti-Cheat tool. Therefore I remedy my prior recommendation.Writing this review is a really though decision for me to make. Usually I do not write reviews (mostly becauseI am too lazy to do so), but in this case I feel as if I have to.First of all: DOOM ETERNAL, as in the core experience, is an amazing experience, worth every buck. The core gameplay is tight, the flow between fighting and exploring is seemless. The changes to the weapon system from the first game gives every weapon a reason to be used whilst streamlining the ammo system at the same.Performancewise DOOM ETERNAL is a technical marvel and a treat to enjoy due to the great implementation ofthe Vulcan API. The graphical fidelity is quite higher than in Doom 2016 yet keeping the demand in hardware quitemoderate. Good Job! The game puts you in the same trance/rampage state just like Doom 2016 empowering you and making you feel as if you ARE the Slayer. This immersiveness combined with the general gameplay loop and flowis so much fun if you are into this rather old school "run-and-gun" Shooter type of game that puts gameplay aboveall else. For this I would recommend the game to anyone who enjoys these kind of games. No second thought here.HOWEVER, as of now, May 16th, 2020, Bethesda released an update which includes Denuvo's implementation of an Anti-Cheatthat uses kernel-level drivers to enforce that purpose. The reason for this is supposedly to stop cheating in the MP portion of this game. I will not indulge into the details on what a kernel-level driver is, as this can be easily done with a couple of searches in a search engine. My biggest issue with this is: - This impacts the performance, tanking the FPS on many system including mine. (RTX2070S + i7-9700k)- This breaks the support Linux/Proton, making it impossible to play this game on my laptop running Ubuntu- Having access to the kernel, is like having the keys to the castle. You have to put faith into some company    somewhere in the world that they will do you no harm with this kind of access or keep their services save    from any third party access that could the enduser by proxy. - The inclusion of such an invasive software after the release and people spending their money on this, without    any kind of prior notice except for a simple remark in the patchnotes is just bad practice. On top of that a lazy    solution to a problem in MP that also impacts SP. Which is, in my opinion, the core focus of the game. Not the MP.Simply put: I came here to buy a Game that has a great Single Player experience. I don't care or buy DLC. I don't care or play Multi Player. I can, just barely, stand with Denuvo Anti-Tamper. KNOWING this I dropped 60€ for this on release just to have some simple SINGLE PLAYER fun. And now, after just a month, I have an update forced upon me that includes a software driver, that never was part of the the deal and I refuse to install, for a mode I don't even play. In conclusion:Would I have known, that this lazy "Anti-Cheat" would be part of the game in the first place. I would not have bought this game at all. Despite it being so great...I urge everyone to not purchase this game unless this issue is addressed. The game is broken at this point on a technical standpoint. People are locked out of the game because they are hustled to submit access to their whole PC which wasn't even part of the deal in the first place. Business practices to include such invasive measures well AFTER launch (possibly to avoid press backlash) is yet again a slap to the face to paying customers and overall a very shady and unacceptable business.Thank goodness I didn't buy this on the stupid Bethesda Launcher and can at least hope to get a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of stuff has been said about Doom Eternal both by hardcore fans and by the whole crowd of people preferring Doom 2016 and it is important to understand where both arguments come from. Doom Eternal is closer to a character action game like Devil May Cry than to regular FPS and actually it was this way in Doom 2016. Doom 2016 attempted to promote combos of weapons and equipment and utilizing mobility and verticality in its arenas. Overall fighting demons in the last game was a rather complex technical process involving both tactical thinking and reflexes. While Doom 2016 allowed people to just bang their heads to heavy metal, blasting demons with double-barreled shotgun or gauss gun, it still was a game with much higher requirements to player's skill than the majority of FPS game of that time and as a sequel, this is the aspect Doom Eternal doubles down on, not mindless violent fun the series is known for.This is the reason a lot of people don't like this game - it has a set of rules players have to abide by and for those who don't understand those rules ... well, the game can be enjoyable, but not on Doom 2016 level. And I'm not saying they're wrong, I'm saying they come with a perspective that they shouldn't be forced to intimately learn the game they're playing and that for them this kind of stricter rules are a sign of bad game design, they feel that a game punishing them for playing it wrong limits their agency and I wholeheartedly think that it is a valid perspective.I also disagree with it completely.Once a player learns the rules of the game, once he understands the interplay between weapons, abilities, and enemies Doom Eternal becomes vastly more enjoyable than Doom 2016. It's so much more complex, dynamic, fast, and filled with adrenaline that in harder arenas you feel like an action movie hero despite - and even because of - the fact that you're usually one mistake away from death. Limitations inherent to game's rules (being it stricter ammo limit and bigger emphasise on cooldown-based abilities and mobility) actually promote creativity and technical skill of using different tools and weapons - if you don't believe me, compare videos of how the game was played at release and how it's played now, how less popular mods and weapons caught second wind when players start experimenting with them. Honestly despite being more punishing Doom Eternal has much more variety in combat than 2016. But it all takes learning and getting used to, player has to suffer for some time to overcome the entrance barrier and get into a mindset and skillset where the game becomes incredibly fun and some people just don't want to put time into the game to get there, which is completely their right.And no, despite being a huge fan, I don't think the game is flawless. It stumbles a lot, has some questionable level- and encounter design decisions both in the vanilla game and its DLC. Platfroming is mostly fine apart from some parts of some levels. The storyline is pretty much a mix between Warhammer 40k fanfiction and silly anime at this point and bosses were mediocre at best, but all of it didn't ruin the game for me at all.Overall the "Am I going to enjoy Doom Eternal?" question boils down to "What kind of a sequel to Doom 2016 do you want to play?". The one where you can bang your head even harder to even louder industrial metal and rip even bigger demons while tearing their even bigger guts without almost any thought about cooldowns, ammo counts, and specific algorithms for killing specific enemies? Eh, turn the difficulty down and go ahead, the game is still fun and actually EXTREMELY accessible on lower difficulties, so much that even a new FPS player can beat it no problem. Just be prepared that some parts will be frustrating or even downright infuriating.The one which expands the last game's combat system and puts you into the environment where you HAVE to use your every move, manage every ability with its cooldown, every weapon with its limited ammo count, the one that makes killing enemies even more of a technical process? Are you one of those who caught the DMC-Esque vibe from Doom 2016 but found it a bit too surface-level to become really great? Well, this is a game for you. It certainly was for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game a ♥♥♥♥ ton on the Microsoft version of the game, and I have to say it really is one hell of an experience.During my time playing, I started getting in the combat more and more and "mastered" stuff like quick switching, movement (ballista boosting, but still working on bhopping), etc. I'm not sure whether this is what ID software intended when making this game but it flows together very very well. They outdid themselves on gameplay with this game. However I noticed the fair share of some of its flaws as well.Eternal combat wise is really good, and dare I say it as one of the best, but a lot of really nice features 2016 had was stripped away. Like the really good atmospheric tint and some dark shadows. It looked awesome in 2016 and I understand why it wasn't in eternal (Playtesters for the game said they couldn't see the demons much). A lot of the sound effects (not to be confused with the music/soundtrack) were pretty toned down and subjectively didn't sound as good as it's 2016 counterpart. The super shotgun sounded very weak compared to 2016 shotgun (Thank god for the mods). I also think the story was very weak. I understand that Doom was always combat based but they tried lore and world building yet the base campaign didn't sell me out on that regard, and just putting a bunch of codex paper entries throughout the map to collect and read does not express lore to casual players. 2016 had voiced testaments to make up for the lore papers and that was more immersive as it dived into the stories of the slayer and his foes. I know that there were some audio logs for eternal but they just felt generic and didn't actually add anything to the slayer's lore or anything and is just speculation from the scientist thirsting (lmao) over the slayer. 2016 seems as a predecessor to doom 3 which was great but eternal feels like the predecessor of the first and second doom games. Which is why I felt 2016 was more gritty and eternal felt retro. It's a great game and definitely one of the best first person shooters. I do suggest you buy it at sale price as buying this at full price is in my opinion not worth it as it doesn't carry much replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: DOOM Eternal truly improves upon the 2016's DOOM. The set pieces are varied and packed to the brim with detail, enemies are well modeled and animated, everything looks awesome and runs very stable. This year's DOOM is way more colorful and more true to it's previous, old school games. The sound design is phenomenal, including the yet again amazing soundtrack from Mick Gordon. I haven't experienced any game breaking bugs, apart from a game crash at the Fortress of Doom when trying to play the original DOOM games on the Slayers PC.The gameplay is really hectic and takes time to get used to. Eventho similar to the previous title, it's very different in certain aspects and balance of game mechanics. After playing the game on Ultra Violence difficulty, I can say that it's one of the hardest games released lately. I really don't like the forced platforming, I wouldn't mind it at all if it was used as a way to get to secrets and side missions, but the way it is implemented now completely breaks the flow of the game and sometimes punishes the player for it itself being clunky. The other thing I don't like is the sheer amount of things you can (and have to) control. With the added dashing, the Crucible, Chainsaw, switching between grenade types, flamethrower and god knows what else, there isn't really a lot of space to customize your bindings as there is simply too much to assign.Some enemies can feel cheap and unfair but usually each and every one has their weakness and way to be dealt with. The lack of traditional multiplayer really disappointed me and I can imagine that after i finish the game to its 100% and collect everything that there is, there won't be any reason for me to launch it again, until some time in a few years for another walk through.All in all, the game has it's few set backs but all things considered, DOOM Eternal is one of the best FPS Campaigns I have ever played. Fully recommending to anyone who likes the genre and the Doom series!

_childDocuments_.review: By no means bad, but the trends here with the online components are a bit worrisome and overall, it's not quite as tight and masterful as the original. Additions are either middling or are a step back from the first entry. is definitely just as fast as the first  Re-remake, but with more juggling and a lot more strange out-of-body shifting storytelling. Not a huge deal, but it's like a super fan of the first game directed this one and sort of jammed in some light humor and "ultra mega badass moment" third person cut-scenes. Again, not horrible, but aside from shoehorning in multiplayer, the first game pretty much hit all the right notes. is definitely visually beautiful, and it runs very well even when settings are maxed out. Music's decent but it's all starting to sound the same this time around, and I haven't hit a "BFG Division" moment (though funny enough they just throw it back in here). Story has taken the serviceable one from the first and shot itself in the foot a few times with the "I don't actually get what 'cool' is but I'll be damned if I can convincingly write it" gun— left the story in a good place, but  just carts multiple things all at once while the Doom Slayer routinely pauses to listen to someone talk about his past. Why is an Earth defense force that was founded after the invasion defending Mars? Dunno! Why'd they take a high ranking member of the old cult? Dunno! Why they using his tech? Dunno! This is definitely the weakest part of . It doesn't seem like it had the same writer this time around, like a mid-season writer switch on a TV show or something. I beat the game, and in starting the DLC I've realized that this problem is not going to improve.The juggle-fest combat loop from the first game is expanded by now throwing in another kind of grenade and a flame thrower, and the "blood punch" melee thing. These seem required at first, but as you upgrade your health, armor, ammo, runes, weapons and abilities the juggle is more of ammo rather than anything else, and that just seems like a formality. I get the idea, they want us to swap weapons still, but I'd argue that the first game did that just fine, and it's time to get something new on the plate to encourage weapon swaps (like combo effects, etc). The game tries to foist complexity upon the player, but in reality running in a circle and firing infinite amounts of frag and ice grenades (and flamethrower spurts) circumvents the punishments of the mechanic, so what's the point? Some weapons are "better" for some enemies, but the weakpoint mechanic is fairly shallow and doesn't really drive the need to switch weapons. Other pointless additions include monkey bars that you can swing from as a environmental double jump that can chain into your own (just give us small platforms to land on), a dash that also works in mid-air (this is okay, but over-tuned), and climbing walls for the Doom Slayer to scamper up and down like some sort of battle koala. There's some other change ups in weapons and enemies, but it feels familiar to the first game. Marauders, however, are a decent addition to the game; they actually do feel like threats that have counterplay outside of "run around until they die".It would be dishonest to call  a bad game, but it doesn't seem like a great iteration of the franchise. Not to say I hated my stay, but the deviations it took from the original's formula served only to distract from what made the original so great and it's kind of disappointing. Here's hoping  goes back to its "roots" (for the second time) the next game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is almost a masterpiece but it has a couple of small flaws which I will discuss below. First, a few disclaimers.This game was played on a 6750XT system. Max settings, 1080p, consistent 144fps at all times. The multiplayer portion for only played for about 45 minutes tops. I did not grow up playing the classic doom games. Doom 2016 was my first one and this was my second.The good :Gameplay : This is very fast paced, hearth thumping, action packed first person shooter gameplay. No, it's more than action packed. It's over the top, gory, bloody, with an amazing soundtrack. There's a lot of weapons to use and a ton of different ways to kill the demons. Glory kills are encouraged by the gameplay loop itself. Glory kills are basically take downs and the game is designed in a way where it's basically necessary to perform them if you want to regain your health and have a short recuperation period during the action. Gameplay is king here and some of the best fast paced first person shooter gameplay you will ever experience. The guns, the sounds, the environments, and the glory kills are high points of this game.Soundtrack : Probably one of the best soundtracks in any game period. Recorded by Mick Gordon, the music alone is worth atleast half the game's full price.Story : The quick, simplistic story is easy to grasp. There is quite a bit of lore involved behind the scenes that you can read about and dig into which is awesome but if you don't care about that, the basic premise is enough to get you going. Some points do go a bit....off the rails for my tastes but overall, another high point of the game.Variety : There are a lot of different varieties of demons for you to kill. Some weapons are more effective than others at killing them so you'll have to get a bit creative. Regardless, there's small, big, wide, short, tall, hard, and easy fodder for you to get through.Content : Campaign is average length but there are a bunch of secrets and collectibles and weapon upgrades to acquire and challenges to complete. There's enough to keep you occupied. See my "campaign length" point below for additional expansion on this topic on the "lacking portion" of my review. Otherwise, there's enough here but I personally expected a bit more. Take this as a good and bad point.The bad :Multiplayer : Welp, it's basically a 1 vs 1 type of deal. I only played for about 45 minutes. What's there is polished and fits the games premise but it's just a team of 2 demons against the doom slayer. It's not terrible and it can be fun but it's more of an afterthought than an actual part of the game. Regardless, it's surprisingly polished and plays very well. It's fun playing as the various demons but it's not something I'd regularly play.Enemy types : So this is a bit of a controversial point for some people but for me, there is quite a difference between your weapons effectiveness in this game versus Doom 2016. In Doin 2016 you can use any gun against anybody and the game doesn't really restrict you from doing so. However, in this game, while you can use whatever whenever, the game tends to structure the enemies in a way where some weapons are really bad to use against a specific enemy, almost forcing you to break your "flow" and forces you to change things up which can be an annoyance for some people.Length : This is a mixed bag. The campaign is long enough but once you beat it, the joy is to go back and play it again at different difficulties. The replay value is enormous from replays and speed runs to finding collectibles and secrets. However, I personally feel the campaign should've been a bit longer for a fast paced single player focused game like this.That's it. The criticisms are still just personal nuisances but overall, this game is a solid 9/10. Definitely worth every penny at full price and will be remembered as one of the best first person shooters of all time.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a very good FPS here somewhere. Unfortunately, it is buried under layer upon layer of useless upgrades and skill trees, forced platforming, and worst of all, the ever-present resource management: ammo, health, and armor are intentionally scarce, and you are forced to use special attacks to refill. To some that may be fun, to me it just makes the whole experience feel incredibly clunky and unnatural, interrupting the flow of the game rather than adding to it. While we are on the subject, the number of special attacks is excessive: chainsaw, flamethrower, glory kills, blood punch... keep it simple will you? It's a Doom game, I came here to blast demons away with a double barreled shotgun, I don't want to have to memorize half a dozen key bindings. Then there's the platforming: I like the idea of double jumps, climbing, dashing, somersaulting. Those are all things which, in moderation, would have been a great addition to the game, but sadly they got carried away, and often you find yourself spending more time jumping than shooting - again, this is a Doom game, I came here to fry hordes of demons with a BFG, not to re-enact Nadia Comaneci's perfect 10 at the Montreal Olympics. Probably as a consequence of this forced platforming, the levels also feel very linear.The story is also a significant let down: they turned the tech-occult theme of previous Doom games into a sort of dark fantasy mishmash with kings, priests, gothic churches, and similar elements which might have been great in another game, but which simply do not blend at all with the Doom lore. The main character himself is disappointing: in Doom 2016, through some excellent use of environmental storytelling and brief cutscenes of the Slayer punching and smashing his surroundings, you felt like fury incarnate. Here... meh. The storytelling is also subpar: in 2016 you knew who the main villain was within minutes of starting the game, here, I've played the game for seven hours and I'm still not sure who or what I'm trying to find - something to do with some priests?Overall, Doom Eternal feels bloated and clunky. That said, it is not a terrible game. It is a major step back in the series, and it is also a major disappointment, given how much potential was wasted due to poor game mechanics, but it is definitely not all bad. There are some enjoyable moments here and there: when the fighting picks up and you don't immediately run out of ammo, it can be entertaining. Just don't buy it at full price.---Addendum: I forced myself to finish the game. I only did the campaign because I don't care for multiplayer. I stand by what I wrote: when you are in the thick of the fight it can be entertaining, and once you get the hang of it you even stop running out of ammo (protip: dash, dash, chainsaw), but the glaring issues I saw in my first hours of play only got worse.The platforming and puzzles became so annoying I almost quit several times. I do not know how much time overall I spent jumping around like a frog, or frustratedly looking in every direction, searching for a climbing wall or a horizontal bar that might get me to the next cluster of demons, but it definitely felt like hours, and it probably was. All that time spent not shooting anything and engaged in activities which would have been better suited to a Mario game, was time in which Doom Eternal was failing utterly at its main purpose: being a first person .Then there's the whole "you must only play the way we want" attitude. This was already evident in the forced chainsaw-flamethrower-ice bomb mechanics, but it became even more annoying with the marauders: they're really not that difficult to kill, they're just... boring: there is a certain distance you have to keep, and there is only a specific time window during which they are vulnerable to your attacks. There is absolutely no room for doing things any way other than what the developers decided. And don't even get me started on the Khan Maykr. Once again, the experience feels incredibly mechanical and artificial.The story and the atmosphere... eh. More priests, more fantasy environments, some clichés about . It's all a convoluted mess. Where Doom 2016 was almost lovecraftian in hinting at the unseen and the unspeakable ("They promised me so much"), this was in-your-face and comic book-ish, and I cringed every time the UAC hologram talked. Even the "evil priests" sound petulant rather than scary, definitely not something you would expect from literal Hell. All this nonsense is canon in the same way that midichlorians are canon: it simply does not fit with the rest of the story, it severely hinders suspension of disbelief, and I hope it will be quietly ignored in future games. Speaking of disbelief: what's with "empowered demons" who "killed another player"? This is a single player game, I don't want to know about other players, this has to be the most immersion-killing thing I've seen in a game! What were they thinking?To conclude: several times while playing Doom Eternal I had the distinct feeling that, in some posh executive's office at id/Bethesda, some of the suits decided that rather than improving upon the previous game, the surest way to sell more copies would be to expand the target market by including gameplay elements which may attract people new to the franchise or even to the genre. Unfortunately, the end result is a Frankenstein monster of a game which tries to be too many things at once, and fails to deliver the kind of experience a lot of older fans have come to expect. There are still moments of absolute brilliance, namely when you are given lots of guns and lots of very angry, very mobile targets, but that just adds to my disappointment, because if this game had just tried to be Doom, instead of Doom Raider or Assassin's Doom, it could have been really good.

_childDocuments_.review: One year ago I wrote a short review citing Doom Eternal's restrictive trifecta design made it an inferior game to D2016. I was wrong.It is easy to draw a comparison between Doom Eternal to anything that includes a learning curve, it's low hanging fruit, it's not a secret that this game is difficult. What I admire about the difficulty is how the game circle strafe around it with its mechanic design, encounter design, enemy design, level design. In some ways each encounter is an improvisational puzzle piece where you constantly prioritize targets and plan the next move base on where you are and your resources. Should I grapple straight up to the Baron and shoot him for a few armor bits, freeze him, delete him real quick then turn back and tank the damage from PE with shield and burn all my chaingun ammo on him, or I should just sling shot myself and kill PE first since Baron can't reach me while I'm up in the air, then I would just blow him up with plasma rifle's microwave? I made it sound more complicated than it should be, but it often does work like that.This is how the fluffs that make Eternal less "immersive" tend to be that, just fluffs. The pop-up tutorials that tell you about weak points? They only appear once for each new super demon, all take 1 minute at max for a game that lasts 20 hours. The fact that the HUD are all colorful and objects like keycards, ammo and weapons appear as huge floating blobs in corners? They just cut down on unnecessary pick up animations, and I personally prefer when games make in-game objects more readable. Eternal sacrificed environmental storytelling for expanded scenery and levels that are more comfortable to traverse in, with more verticality and old school platforming, which for me are totally welcomed. It spends the majority of its time in combat, beautifully designed, magnificently paced combat, and it made every bit of its majestic corner shine like african diamond in every second you engage with it.And then there's the elephant in the room: the trifecta. At first just like the majority of Eternal's critics, I wasn't fond of how the game limited ammo count and force you to chainsaw more than usual, and I disliked the amount of glory kill and the way the flame belch was implemented feels contrived. But just like the fluffs above, these are all fluffs. It's actually insane how flexible these tools make combat encounter feels, as they help you in how you prioritize targets, reward reflex and quick decision making. You already know about lighting a horde on fire then shoot them, but how about flying above a horde, lobbing a grenade at them, then LIGHT THEM ON FIRE RIGHT WHEN IT EXPLODES? It's so shortsighted of me to not use every tool available as I'm an arena shooter enjoyer, where quick switching between lightning gun - rocket launcher - railgun became second instinct. It's the same in Eternal, it's arena shooter-ish level design with enemies coming in waves give each encounter a different beat and a playground for you to master in short term. I win a fight in this game, not with craving the satisfaction of gore bursting out of demons, but because my confidence and my skill granted me that satisfaction, and that's something incredibly valuable in video games these days.I believe this is also why Eternal often gets a bad rap from some players. It's a difficult sequel to a relatively breezy casual game that was more free form in how it played, one that was often criticized for running out of steam in the final third. Eternal feels grueling in the first levels as you don't have all the tools available, and the weakpoint tutorials and the trifecta design gave it an impression that it's a "restrictive" game. But it also proved that great video games are the ones that know where to put limitation on players and let them know what they can do to overcome those limitations. In my opinion, games that let you do anything with no repercussion are cheap, shallow power fantasy. There's nothing wrong with that, but I appreciate the effort in making the power fantasy something you really earn, rather than from a meter and achievement pop-up. My most favorite games of all time include Spelunky, Devil May Cry, the Souls and Sekiro games, Kingdom Come Deliverance, classic RPG, games that give you no mercy unless you're willing to be a part of their relentless system. And now Doom Eternal becomes one of those. I feel powerful after every fight, because I made sure I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ earned it. Doom Eternal made me realize how I deeply love challenging games and challenging myself in games. I put it on Nightmare, failed so many times in the first couple Slayer Gates, but never have I found frustrated with it, because the game made clear that some few mistakes, not my entire inability to beat the fight, was responsible for those deaths, and mistakes can be erased and improvement will come through practice and familiarity. There are still some design decisions I don't really agree with, mainly with how glory kills still feel a bit too long for their own sake even with the fasten animation rune, and the Makyr Drones should appear in more levels given how useful they are at supplying ammo. But as a whole, I just can't stop thinking of how elegantly, forward thinking designed this game is. It almost feels like an enigma not just for the genre but for mainstream AAA video game scene as well, because you don't find many games build on huge production value that's not afraid of its own identity and infamy like this these days.

_childDocuments_.review: While being accustomed to stealth and assassination games; FPS isn't exactly my strongest genre, but I do enjoy them nonetheless. Definitely worth the money and expect to constantly die if you play on Ultra-Violence or harder. There are a lot of secret content to find and I still haven't found them all with my first playthrough. Enjoy metal albums and collectible figurines. Climbing and swimming is a bit wonky, but nothing short than being mildly annoying. One word of advice, watch out for those ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Marauders. Splash damage them with grenades and missiles. The Marauder is probably the worst enemy in the game capable of making you ragequit within the first few times. Fortunately, once you learn how to kill them, you stand more of a chance. I have no idea what the devs were thinking with the Marauder. Horrible design on that demon.Boss battles are more fun and takes strategy to beat. _childDocuments_.review: Doom Eternal is the perfect FPS. (This is a statement and it's not up for debate)I thought that it was nearly impossible to improve doom 2016's formula, well... they ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ did it!Doom eternal is not just a doom game, it let's you go into the doom universe for the first time and goes even beyond, making some fan theories true and adding new incredible enemies for the slayer.It's really a different game from its predecessor, it's more cartoony and more colorful; the gameplay loop is masterfully designed to be fun and engaging at any time, with new brutal ways to glory kill demons and new incredible sounding weapons; your ammo is really scarse and you have to rely to your chainsaw to refill your weapons, this makes it a lot of fun to combine all the different things into the "combat puzzle" that is doom eternal, your chainsaw also refills itself after some time so you always have a mean to get ammo, as long as there are demons to cut up in half; it also adds some platforming which i find to be a nice way to explore and catch breath between fights.Unlike doom 2016, where the super shotgun was the only weapon of choice for 1/3 of the game, weapons have their strengths and weaknesses for every demon type making them all useful and requiring to switch between all of them to overcome the demon horde.Oh and yeah... the music from Mick Gordon is back and better than ever!For having incredible looking and detailed environments this game runs beautifully, with a gtx 1080 in 1440p max settings i was going 90 to 100 fps with minor stutters during some intense battles.I just have two complaints: the boss fights are not really good compared to 2016's boss fights and the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Marauders...
