_childDocuments_.review: As Hugo Martin promised, this game makes DOOM 2016 feel obsolete. Every aspect of that game is done better on this sequel, from managing resources to keep you alive with the new Flamethrower giving you armor, chainsaw still being the same ammo resource as before or a good tool to delete an enemy that is giving you a problem, And amazingly added mobility to this whole game that just makes the combat feel much better. You now have these poles that let you maneuver around and airdashes that just work so great for the flow of battle, it helps you dodge out of enemies' ways and just makes Doom feel like a Character Action game. It really shows how much the Original Vision and the Director loves games like DMC and Bayonetta. The same trials from before are here but in a much different style, they're not gimmicky anymore. They're a REALLY TOUGH WAVE of enemies that you have to conquer with your Tools for the job. Enemies have Hard counters from certain weapons, which makes you think a lot more during combat and it just feels a lot more rewarding. It's not so much about the power trip that 2016 was, it held your hand too much, this game wants you to learn from your mistakes a lot much like you did in the original doom games. It's also such a love letter to how the story came out of a Tabletop RPG session of the Id studio guys, and it just oozes awesomeness all around. It also runs much better than 2016 which is a big plus for me. My pc is the lowest recommended hardware for this game and it somehow runs the game on high somewhat fine, but a high medium gives it the best performance.If you loved the first game and love being engaged in combat, with a game that respects you instead of holding your hand, you'll have a great time.Having now finished the game I can stand by what i said and this game only gets better and better as you go on. the Core Gameplay just works so damn well.PS: If you get all the cheat codes you can play Doom 1 and 2 on the Dosbox inside the Doomguy's room.

It feels like a deception, whether intentional by Bethesda or not.The issue here is because the driver has so much privilege, it could be doing anything. It could even just be a buggy driver and cause your computer to bluescreen. Either way, it's scummy to force people to have to use this, even in singleplayer, when the game had been anti-cheat free for nearly 2 months now.

_childDocuments_.review: So I just beat the campaign for the first time (Will definitely do it again like I did with 2016) and as a person who owns all of the doom games and has played them for over a decade I would like to give my thoughts on it and also address a lot of the points I see in many of the negative reviews. So let's start with a simple pros and cons list, any major spoilers will be blacked out. Before people call me a pleb and say I play on ITYTD I didn't, I played on Ultra-ViolencePros* Fantastic combat, everything is really smooth and is much faster paced than Doom 2016* Movement, just everything about it* Upgraded visuals* The chainsaw isn't useless anymore (Played through Doom 2016 3 times, never used the chainsaw once.)* It seems a lot more skill based especially with the addition of the dash mechanic. I get hit in this game a lot less than in 2016 because it's less likely you'll be unable to move out of the way of a fireball in time.* Upped enemy count from Doom 2016 (At least on ultra-violence)* Better puzzles, solving some of them made me feel big brain. * Cutscenes can be skipped instead of having to wait for Hayden to shut the hell up.* Imps no longer eat ~2-3 shells unless you literally shove the shotgun barrel up their tight * That final boss fight, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that was intense, way better than the spider mastermind. (Won't spoil it, just know it's fun)* Slayer gates, these are fun, wish they were harder though as I didn't die during them at all.* UI, bear with me here, I know the neon is awful but in the in-depth section on UI I will explain why this ended up in pros.Cons* That ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ purple goo ♥♥♥♥, why was this added, at least these sections are short and rare.* SOME platforming sections* Underwater sections, this is just a personal preference and nothing to do with the game's execution. I just hate underwater sections in any game, luckily these are also short and few and far between.* Low ammo counts which is complained about a lot and while i'd like it a bit higher I only ran completely out of ammo once and had ammo for all guns about ~99% of the time.In depth section: Don't click black boxes if you don't wanna be spoiled.I'm going to start off with the combat. Overall the combat is greatly improved from 2016 and I had a lot more fun killing demons in this game. I will leave a disclaimer though, THIS GAME IS HARD, like really really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hard, however it isn't unfair and I got through it with only 2 deaths, both of which were absolutely my fault. I will now address the ammo count issue I see in many negative reviews. This can be mostly mitigated with good aim and on point use of the chainsaw (Which now regenerates fuel automatically to one pip and does so quite quickly), kill one enemy with it and you've pretty much got all your ammo back for all guns. The ammo upgrades while seemingly useless for the shotgun are actually quite good for other guns and give you a fairly large surplus of ammo towards the mid-early game.  As a matter of fact I found myself in arenas with tons of unused ammo pickups because I was already full on everything. I also didn't have an issue with the reduced count during combat because enemies are generally less spongy in this game with imps and soldiers now taking 1 blast from the shotgun instead of 2 for the imp and like 3-5 for the soldier. With this reduction in bullet-spongyness also comes a welcome increase in enemy counts, basically dialing the amount from Doom 2016 up to 10.Another point from the negative reviews i'd like to address is being shoehorned into a certain playstyle. I saw people complaining the precision bolt is imperative, however after getting it I never used it, and only really used the heavy cannon when I got the micro-missiles. They say it is necessary for the revenant's cannons or arachnotrons gun, however I found the sticky-bombs of the shotgun to be far more effective for this, and I was a lot more accurate with them, this isn't even considering the fact that it sometimes only take 3 stickies to kill a revenant outright. When it comes to the mancubus I also used the stickies for their cannons but found that rockets, the heavy machine-guns base and precision fire mode, and the ballista also do a fantastic job of this, or if your don't care about weaknesses just blast them a few times with the Super Shotgun and you're good. Every combat encounter has many approaches that can be taken and there is no "correct" way to go about things. I for one never used flame belch or the grenades. However there are likely people who use these all the time and the cacos also get 1-shot from the frag grenades out of the shoulder cannon. Melee does zero damage. Kind of annoying but was replaced by dash. Dash into weak enemies once or twice to instantly stagger them, no ammo required.Now on to movement, the movement in this game is incredibly fluid, seemingly more so than the last game. The dash mechanic is undoubtedly the best part of the movement improvements and allows for so many new ways to move around the map and dodge enemies. It also regenerates incredibly quick, to the point where if it would regenerate while you were in the air you could literally fly. The "monkey bars" while seemingly gimmicky are actually very handy and fun to use to your advantage and I found myself keeping a height advantage over the demons a lot more in this game. It also allows for creative ways to explore the map and discover secrets.Cutscenes, unlike 2016 where you had to sit through Samuel Hayden monologuing about Argent Energy or some ♥♥♥♥, I don't even remember I wasn't paying attention, in this game these sections are skipable. I don't care what you say, sitting in Hayden's office for 5 minutes listening to him talk about crap, without being able to leave, breaks up the flow and IS A CUTSCENE, just because you still are in first person and have control of the character doesn't make it not a cutscene, that part and the others like it all feel and play like cutscenes in 2016. At least in this game they are skipable if you don't want to hear Samuel Hayden jack off about how he watches Rick and Morty or some ♥♥♥♥ like that.Tutorials, luckily can be disabled.UI, Ok like I said bear with me, the default neon green UI is kinda doo-doo i'll be honest. However it is highly customizable in the options menu and this pretty much negates it being a con and lets it get into the pros territory. Giving more choice to the player is generally a good thing in my eyes.Platforming, oh boy here we go. Platforming in this game is a mixed bag. While I prefer it to the "walk in a straight line for 30 seconds, arena, repeat" formula of Doom 2016 it can sometimes be quite frustrating. I got particularly frustrated with it in  when I was trying to get to  and they had the wall climbing drone ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ so far away that you could barely reach them and I ended up falling a couple of times, luckily though falling only takes away 20 health or armor. These sections could get tedious sometimes, however there were some sections it was used well, generally involving pathways to secrets.TLDR; Obviously the game isn't perfect. However, I personally feel it is worth the money and a step in the right direction from 2016. Combat is fun and engaging, and almost everything that broke the flow of the game in 2016 can be skipped or disabled in this game. On the other hand I feel base ammo count could be higher, base movement speed could be a bit higher, and they could reduce the amount of platforming between fights a little bit or make it less tedious.Hopefully this cleared up any questions, just know it takes more than loading in, shooting one imp, then refunding the game to actually know how it plays and make a good review.Overall Rating: 8.5 - 9/10 Improved on 2016 but still can do more to improve.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't overstate on how much the Doom franchise is important to me. I play it since my childhood and just by thinking on how much it grew and evolved brings me joy. Doom really is a long-lived iconic classic with diverse styles in its various games, some titles being horror focused (such as Doom 3, Doom 64 and Doom PSX) and some titles being heavy packed with unrelenting action.   Doom Eternal obviously carries the flag of the latter mentioned style and does it very well with its elaborate combat system with a defined weapon variety, enemy variety and count, strategic resource management, advanced movement mechanics and a kickass soundtrack. Doom Eternal, while being arguably a hard game, its a very accessible one with its difficulty variety, while also being very lenient with different playstyles, combined to weapons mods that gives your well-diversed weapons a secondary fire to accompany your playstyle.  And last but not least the atmosphere with its beauty and diversification is jaw dropping. Travelling from dimensions beyond is astoundingly varied. From the very depths of hell and to the very ruined realms of a decaying and dwindling extra-dimensional race, to the acidic bog of tortured souls of the Blood Swamps, you travel and fight with one objective in mind: To kill and murder every single demon you face. In revenge for what you've lost and to protect what remained. This franchise made history back in the 90s, delivered numerous titles and even after 25+ years of existence it keeps delivering the most fun I've ever had in any videogame title out there. Can't recommend it enough!

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant sequel to Doom 2016 that is only let down by a wet fart of a final boss. Absolutely worth your time and money if you have any love for shooters.The game more or less plays like Doom 2016. It's fast, precise and oh, so very violent. That being said there are a number of important changes from 2016. First, your powerful weapons (like the super shotgun and Gauss cannon/Ballista) now consume much more ammo, meaning they'll be something you switch to to deal with a big demon rather than using them as your main weapons like you could in 2016. This seems to have annoyed a lot of people and I sort of get why; you no longer have that care-free anti-demon rampage the previous game was praised for, since the devs wanted to make this game harder. That being said, it encourages and rewards people who are willing to put the time in to learn how the game is meant to be played. Getting stuck on an encounter for a while can be frustrating but it makes it so much more rewarding and satisfying when you actually do complete it. You feel like you have accomplished something and your skills have improved (and if you want to play with as little interruption as possible that's what the easy difficulty is for). Ammo is also reduced overall, but your ammo-generating chainsaw now recharges on its own and the game goes out of its way to spawn trash-mobs for you to chainsaw when you run low on supplies, so it balances out the difficulty as long as you can count (or at least can see the colour red). The second big change is the addition of platforming. Now, a lot of people seem to be complaining about this and I personally don't see the issue. Sure, it's not Mario 64, but it's really not bad at all. It's perfectly serviceable and there really isn't that much of it. It's more of a way to mix up the gameplay between combat encounters as opposed to the corridor walks of 2016. You'll be jumping, dashing, swinging on monkey bars and climbing occasional walls to get from place to place. It's all very easy for the most part, but a few secrets require more precise timing of jumps and dashes. They're hardly frame perfect requirements, though. The game knows that's not what you're there for, so it keeps them brief and (usually) very forgiving, with big platforms and short distances between them. Sometimes there will be a light puzzle accompanying the platforming but it's never more complex than "push button then platform then punch box to reach new area then platform more."Lastly, there is more story focus this time around. Gone is the unbroken first person perspective of 2016. There are now many more traditional cutscenes. The story itself is on the same level as 2016. Doom Slayer needs an excuse to go to the next place he can kill demons, so a maguffin or bad guy is placed in a level so Doom Slayer can go after it. Not terribly complex but there is a bit more story to sink your teeth into should you want it this time around, mostly revolving around worldbuilding and telling us more about the slayer itself. It can all be ignored if that's really not your thing.Traditional PvP is gone and has been replaced with Battlemode. It's a 2v1 mode with two players controlling some of the powerful demons from the campaign trying to take down one Slayer with a full arsenal. And the Slayer is still at advantage. I haven't played much of this mode but I have enjoyed what I have tried. It requires coordination from the demons and the Slayer has to be on their toes. It's fun and tense and doesn't seem to have any OP ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ so far.If you liked 2016 you'll probably like this. In my opinion it's a much better game than 2016 and I so hope we get another one after the story DLCs are out

_childDocuments_.review: What is Doom Eternal? Short answer. Pure unadulterated badass demon slaying action!Long Answer. A well executed spin on the shooter genre, that aims to teach both new comers and veterans a different and unique way of approaching encounters, not only in this game, but all FPS out there. It excels at everything the 2016 Doom introduced and pushes that to a highly more adrenaline fuel rush than anything you've experienced before. It's faster, it's bigger and it's more Doom. It's a true blast to play! There is far more to unravel in Eternal than just "here is gun, make demons go boom". The game requires strategy and reflexes. When you hear that heavy metal music, it's time to fight like hell with both brains and brawn.At first glance you might think the combat is chaotic and all over the place, and truthfully that is how it's going to feel at first because you are just starting to learn "The Doom Dance". Allow me to explain. The combat in Eternal is a rhythm of satisfying executed weapon swapping, dashing, jumping and kills that puts the player in a coordinated mindset to always be on the move, shooting and managing ammo, health and armour. And this dance will be learned and understood the more you play. Don't let yourself be discouraged. You will get the hang of the visceral nature of Doom Eternal. It may at first feel the game is forcing you into a certain play style, it's actually teaching you to better manage and control the situations you are faced with.Until something finally clicks. It's going to happen. And when it does, you will be are aware of every demon, every weak point, and every weapon. You are going to be fully immersed and be completely addicted to the combat. This masterpiece of violence is going to be all you're thinking of when you are finally ready to use every tactic you've learned along the way. It's a grand spectacle of fantastic audiovisual communication to the player. The idea that no matter how much you replay it, the game challenges you to invest the time and experiment and use different methods of clearing each arena, proving how well the new formula works where you want to perfect these mechanics because they reward the player and feel accomplished for their effort. Very good game design on all fronts, and the soundtrack is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fire!One of my favorite games of all time.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom 2016 is dethroned honorably from the mountain that represents most intense single player FPS experience ever. This game crushes you atleast a dozen times if you are not some regular arena shooter semi-pro. Coming from someone who played all DOOM 2016 arcade levels on Ultra-Nightmare with a slayer rating (highest level rank 215).You will have to manage your resources, use the proper weapon and gear combos, prioritize weapon and suit upgrades, position correctly, hit your damn rails (ballista) and switch tempo on the fly to match ever changing situations. This game is not for those that wish to spam one weapon throughout the whole fight, kill demons with whatever and however. Days of DOOM 2016 stun bomb spam are over, player has to adapt or die.Loads of collectibles, secrets, slayer gate arenas and mini combat challenges to complete for various resources. These can then be used to upgrade your suit, weapons, open new areas in your home base and select active rune modifiers.Enemies are extremely varied and each require a different tactic and/or weapon to take out effectively. Combat chess explains this core gameplay perfectly. You will not fight the same fight in this game.Doom Eternal is a game worthy of the pioneer title within FPS genre, standing tall next to such giants as Half-Life 2 and Quake. Every shooter game afterwards will be measured by the extremely high margin that Eternal has set for vast amount of interconnected play pieces and choices available to the player throughout the fights. After this more "normal" shooters like COD series or even the great Titanfall 2 feel like glorified whack a mole machines with no depth.This is the Dark Souls of FPS, you will die, adapt and overcome... or post a review whining that there is no ammo.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly it's an extremely good game, but personally I'm not feeling it enough to foam at the mouth like others have with the game. I get it, all the gameplay quirks and the flow of combat, but it just isn't for me. It's annoying for me to constantly be looking at my abilities and meters to know when I need to set a demon on fire or chainsaw them. I get it's supposed to be replacing pickups, but I just think it's a chore to always be looking out for it and I personally prefer the pickup system more. The whole platformer aspect is annoying too and makes sections without demons annoying as ♥♥♥♥ to play because when you're not ripping demons limb from limb you're jumping around like a monkey swinging on branches and ♥♥♥♥.Music isn't as good as Doom 2016 imo, but that soundtrack was kind of hard to follow up.  Bethesda also decided to not pay Mick and ♥♥♥♥ with his music, but at least they hired Andrew Hulshult to write music for the DLCs, so I'm not too mad with the music in the end. Speaking of Doom 2016 and being better than this game, I prefer the tone of the story in the first game way more. Everything seems a little too serious in Eternal, which wouldn't be bad on its own, but compared to 2016 it just falls short.That's all the personal issues I have with the game and they're all very subjective. Let's talk about what's better than 2016: weapon variety, level variety, enemy variety, more challenges, more perks. It's a whole ass smorgasbord of new content compared to Doom 2016. Performance is insanely good too, even with the new patch adding RT reflections. The game already ran smooth as butter on my gtx 1080 and 7700k (iirc around 180 fps on ultra/nightmare settings at 1080p), and now with my 9900k and 2080ti I get around 130 fps at 1440p on ultra nightmare, highest RT settings and DLSS set to quality. Even if you run this game without RT, it looks very impressive and runs extremely well on basically any hardware from the last 8 years.So yeah that's it for the review. The game has issues for me, but I'll still try to finish it at least once. Besides all of the issues I have with the game are very subjective, and even with those subjective faults I still think this is a very well made game that is 100% worth the asking price. I just don't think this game is as good as some reviews make it out to be.

_childDocuments_.review: First off I will say it's not a "bad game", just as much as I wanted to like the game I don't enjoy it much. I powered all the way through to the ending in hopes I might start liking it more, but it was honestly a chore. Half my playtime was spent with the game paused while I did other things.The devs' design approach to this has a very narrow concept of how the gameplay loop should work and anything outside of said loop doesn't work. So you either love it and find it a blast to play, or you just don't. It's not a difficulty problem it's a design philosophy one. Everything is designed around pushing the player to handle things in one specific way from the way the ammo is handled, to the way tools are handled, and all the way to how maps are handled with invisible walls being everywhere. You do it the "right way" or you don't do it at all. It's a love it or hate it experience all in all. If you're looking for something closer to an old school FPS where the only thing you have to do is navigate the levels and keep an eye on ammo while slaughtering enemies... This probably isn't the game for you. If you're looking for a follow up to 2016 that is more of the same this probably isn't for you. And if you want immersion this definitely isn't for you. HOWEVER if you want a fast frenetic almost "arcadey" shooter with a focus on "rip & tear" style play and a gameplay loop that revolves around you chaining all the various tools at your disposal.. you'll probably have a blast with it.

_childDocuments_.review: This right here, is not only one of the best DOOM experiences that has ever existed, it is also the most fast-paced action packed fun FPS game I have ever played. There are some major gameplay changes in comparison to DOOM 2016, you might like or dislike some of them; this is definitely a more arcade-ish DOOM but it's resource managing mechanics make it a much more dynamic, swift and brutal dance. Once you settle the muscle memory for getting ammo/armour via chainsaw and flame belch, even the HUD becomes unnecesary, the gameplay flows so perfectly that you will never find yourself not knowing what to do on a battle. The platforming parts might feel underwhelming at first but once you realise they make the journey through the immense maps much more enjoyable AND watchable, the replayability of any level increases exponentially. Unlike its predecessor, enemy spawns are always the same, which makes memorizing them an easy task and every time you re-play a level you are bound to completing it on a much more perfect pace. The story exists, but it is up to the player to read it and understand it, it is, by all means, possible to complete the game without understanding the whole context of what's happening. DOOM ETERNAL establishes, once again, a new high standard for videogames of the genre to try and tackle down, it is, 25 years later, yet another revolution for the FPS industry. The art, level design and soundtrack are absolute madness, nothing I can say that has not been said about it. It may not come flawless to the eyes of some players, but once you get used to all the decisions and gameplay mechanics, DOOM becomes the best game to be playing in 2020. By all means, I recommend playing this game if you are fond to relentless awesome turbulent shooters, RIP AND TEAR until it is done.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Doom game in name only. It's a nice action game no doubt but it simply isn't a great or even a good Doom game. I could give Doom 2016 some artistic freedoms but Eternal is just ridiculous. There are numerous design issues which make it really weird game to play. Its primary sin is being a shooter where you don't really have ammunition to freely shoot.You're expected to chainsaw demons which changes the way it was used in Doom 2016. Now you're forced to use the chainsaw a lot more and much more frequently especially on Ultra-Nightmare difficult I'm playing the game on. Watching these action interrupting rip n' tear animations every 30 seconds or so get really old and annoying after the first level.You cannot use the chainsaw in bigger staggered enemies now either. This really messes up with the flow of the combat. At least until you've unlocked all the stuff. There are upgrades for upgrades for upgrades, weapons, skills, etc. there is a guarantee upgrade for it. Being able to carry full ammunition and have full health and armor are all upgrades you have to unlock by playing the game.Visual style and design is in my opinion inconsistent. I think even the Hell looked better in Doom 2016. The whole game is much more comic book like now. But there are a lot of great visual art in the game and the game does look very pretty. But I'm not sure if it looks better than Doom 2016.UI and UI font are not all that well designed and it's hard to read some of the menus and sizes are clearly intended to be read from a TV screen.There are these Super Mario like platforming sections which I'm not fond of. I like Mirror's Edge but I don't like Mirror's Edge in my Doom game which is the reason I'm not going to recommend this game.Technically the game runs superb on my system. This is despite the fact that I have newer GPU but much older CPU which for sometime has been a bottle necking performance in some other new games. Audio and music is just insanely great.These are my initial thoughts so far.Oh and I really hate the idea of arcade style lives. The biggest single progression in game design the original Doom introduced, was dropping the Wolfenstein 3D style lives in FPS games. When you spend a live you respawn to the point where you died and if you run out you go back to checkpoint but don't get your lives back. It seems like a really redundant idea.Also they've removed the starting pistol and replaced it with a nerffed version of the shotgun. It makes this more like Quake but also a lot less like Quake. I think the starting pistol in Doom 2016 had unlimited ammunition but I'm not entirely sure.Now it's not all that clear how to proceed once player runs out of ammo, especially if you've run out of chainsaw gas. I guess player is expected to whack the regular zombies but they will not drop ammo that way. Instead the glory kills give you health boosts. Burning the regular zombies with flamethrower gives player more armor shards.Also there isn't a Doom style 4-player Deathmatch with server browser and community hosted dedicated servers. And no community made mods or maps.Furthermore  network features are crap and don't seem to work properly half the time causing you not getting your XP and progression unlocks to work or whatever it's supposed to do.Also the movement speed is slightly down from Doom 2016. The running in Doom Eternal is now a must-have upgrade which then grants you faster movement speed when you perform a glory kill.Furthermore apparently because of technical limitations of the aging game consoles... there now seems to be less monsters to fight than in previous Doom games (albeit their polycount to me looks higher). Guys at id have compensated this by making them tougher opponents which in-turn makes them a bit bullet spongy and shooting less fun.Arenas feel much more tightly packaged with more walls and smaller corridors. Some floors literally deny player freedom of movement and force slow walking for "cinematic reasons" I guess.There are cinematic cutscenes every now and then but those can be skipped. It's a missed opportunity because it would have been more interesting to see Doomslayer react to things with this arms like in Doom 2016 from the first-person perspective.Over the half of the gameplay time in this game, player spends watching pre-animated sequences during which you do nothing for a few seconds because you're forced to do so. Not because you choose to do it for fun every now and then. The novelty wears off very quickly and I'd rather spend those seconds shooting demons in every fight.All this is because they took the worst aspects of Doom 2016 and made them have bigger share of the gameplay loop.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom - a game series with ups and downs for 30 years now and there aren't that many games that can look back on such a long history.With Doom Eternal and the two expansions The Ancient Goods Parts 1 and 2, the story also finds its (“worthy”) end for the time being.Yes indeed. However, this wasn't even thought about until Doom 2016, and it's even more complex than many people might think. Anyone who has carefully followed the monologue in Doom (2016) and read all the codex entries already knows this story and has enough background information to be able to enjoy Doom Eternal to the fullest.Anyone who hasn't played the predecessor should definitely do so before Eternal and anyone who is willing to absorb the information provided in the game will then know the story.For those who are interested, I posted a summary of the story in the comments due to its length.Eternal begins shortly after the events of Doom (2016). However, this time difference is not precisely defined. The Slayer has moved into the Fortress of Doom in space, which serves as his main base. How this happened remains as much a mystery as what happened in the meantime. With the support of the AI VEGA from the predecessor, the Slayer is now hunting the hell priests who are the masterminds of the demon invasion on earth. But that won't be the only thing that will keep the Slayer busy on his way because as the game progresses he will repeatedly be confronted with his past as well as his first battle in which the Doom Marine became the Slayer we know and the famous sentence “Rip and Tear, until it is done” comes from.In addition, Eternal, unlike its predecessor, relies on more cutscenes in which the Slayer himself is actively staged and the principle of an active story telling is applied. This reveals more background information about the actions of the demons and the circumstances and the player is confronted with stories and explanations that primarily serve to give the whole thing a framework for the actions that are about to take place. There is also a lot to read. For those who have no real interest in the story and don't want to read every codex entry, you will find out the most important things in the various cutscenes and the messages from the characters.In this game, the formula of its predecessor has been expanded again. The double jump is available from the start and the Slayer also receives a dash that is not just intended for reaching secrets or game passages. This will become a good friend and offer even more mobility in battle. In addition, the Glory Kill mechanics and the chainsaw continue to celebrate many broken bones on the battlefield.Especially when it comes to the double jump and the dash, there is an incredible, unique and fluid combat feeling in which long-range fire and brutal close combat alternate. Covering or retreating is completely pointless here. If something like ammunition or armor is missing, there is only one right path: moving forward inexorably.Thanks to the new movements and swinging on poles, the arenas now offer significantly more vertical action because the fighting areas are often crossed by high platforms or take place on a large cliff where you fight your way from top to bottom. Many of these elements can be used to outmaneuver the demons and attack them from the side, behind or above. What's pretty cool is that there are several runes that either improve movement in the air or slow everything down when you press the alternative fire button, which leads to really spectacular slow-motion maneuvers when jumping.The range of facets of the carnage are almost endless thanks to explosive or frost grenades and the alternative fire modes that are unlocked as upgrade boxes in the areas and can be swapped out at the touch of a button, adding to the already great weapons.But not only the challenging combat but also the level design and the variety can score even more here compared to its predecessor. The locations are just visually great and really offer something to look at in a wide variety of settings. The game isn't dark, in fact it's brightly colored, which is really great because it covers the same grey-brown soup with colors that don't harm the hellish design in any way.The Fortress of Doom is also fantastically designed and, in addition to storing the unlocked secrets, also offers enough excitement to explore. You can also use the collected Sentinel batteries to unlock upgrades for weapons and the Preator suit, and there are skins for the suit like the super cool outfit of the Marine from Doom (1993)A big difference to Doom (2016), which was missing towards the end, is the variation in the gameplay. While in the predecessor you ran from arena to arena, Eternal also requires more skill. Since you can climb special walls here and the double jump and dash are ideal for overcoming large abysses, there are sections in which the game plays almost like a classic action adventure. Boxes have to be moved, switches have to be activated, simple environmental puzzles have to be solved and tricky jumping passages have to be completed. And that's damn cool, but unfortunately in some cases it's sometimes too much of a good thing. At least for my taste because in some passages you don't know how to jump until you get to the next platform, which then - oh wonder - falls into the lava after a while. But when what feels like the hundredth jump-and-run passage comes along, then at some point it's enough.But this slows down the quick arena shooting a bit, giving you time to breathe and concentrate on finding secrets. In addition to collecting items, soundtracks or cheat codes, there are also valuable upgrade points or crystals for the suit, the locations of which are automatically displayed on the clear and freely rotatable map so that you can easily return to the secrets you have not found.Whether you think Doom is good or bad. The games all have one thing in common. They always run perfectly, the controls are precise and the weapons feel really good. And here, if you belong to the Slayers Club, you will be rewarded with various things for playing. The Slayer, the Hud and everything that has to do with it can be adapted to your own wishes and you will literally be showered with free cosmetics. When it comes to this, some other game developers could take a good look at this, because everything is available here at no additional cost. In addition, the game is always up to date and work is constantly being done on it and that is more than just exemplary.For me, Doom Eternal is one of the best shooters of this generation with a unique flow in combat, great arenas, extensive weapons, numerous and different enemies, impressive locations and a brutal soundtrack, which takes arena shooters to a new level.✔ great level and monster design✔ great soundtrack✔ smooth and uncompromising gameplay✔ clever AI✔ precise controls✔ Effective weapon modes and upgrades✔ interesting mythology✔ lots of humor✔ extensive campaign✔ many hidden secrets✔ many customization options✔ Photo mode✔ tactical and quick battles✔ optional time trials and battle arenas✘ Story is told weakly✘ partly monotonous corridors✘ too many acrobaticsRevised and reposted: January 15, 2024

_childDocuments_.review: Doom Eternal has spoiled my experiences for First Person Shooters forever! something about it just feels right, from the well balanced difficulty, to mastering the extremely challenging but satisfying loop of managing the Doom Guy's arsenals aka his fists and flamethrower, Doom Eternal just oozes with polish and attention to game design. It is a detachment from Doom 2016 to be sure, with a more casual approach to the game, making pickups float and glow like an arcade game which may cause some people to question as to why ID Software did that. All I know is it just works, for me at least, I believe the departure from the more serious tone allows Doom Eternal to have more fast paced fun intense encounters. With the introduction of Dash and the way the encounter areas are designed, the game does encourage you  to utilize EVERYTHING in your arsenal to stay alive! I found myself constantly bobbing and weaving about, zipping around the area sending demons back to whence they came, rotating from grenades, flamethrower and glory kills....its a rush, and there is some strategic layer to it if you are playing on harder difficulties. Not only that, since power ups are just floaty pieces in the world, picking it up mid-fight while still maintaining the rapid flow of battle is just easy and feels satisfactory when you nail it, which contributes to how fun and exciting the encounters in Doom Eternal are.Overall, i think the game does a lot of things right in what a sequel should be. A lot of games seem to make a sequel yet the only thing that changed is the narrative, they don't add anything new to make the gameplay loop feel much better or improved in any sense, but with Doom a lot of adjustments and fine tweaking has been made to the gameplay to make it feel like its own game rather than JUST a part 2 of the story. Speaking of which, the story is surprisingly rich and deep with a ton of lore for you to explore! so its nothing like Doom 2016's "i'm mad, kill demons" story. Really good stuff!Of course its not perfect in any way, I don't particularly like the platforming sections. But that's probably just me.  Overall, I really liked the game and I am definitely getting the DLC when its on sale! Can't wait to see what ID Software cooks up next! Wait is temporary but Doom is Eternal! (I finally get to join this trend)

_childDocuments_.review: TDLR version: Eternal isn't nearly as good as the 2016 DOOM due to a lot of highly questionable design choices. It has moments of being really good, but it has a tendency to get dragged down by various small things. A lot of deaths feel like your got screwed instead of you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ up. If you have held off this long, continue to hold off until it is on sale or reduced.It comes down to this: In the previous DOOM, I rarely felt like my death was to the games fault, be it from a glitch, unresponsive controls, BS enemies, etc. I felt like I was in control, that if I died, I could have done better to avoid it. In Eternal, I get frustrated by deaths that I couldn't avoid. The chainsaw not locking on when the enemy it just a bit off the center of my screen, so you get melee'd to death instead. Not grabbing onto ledges despite having a lot of platforming sections (which themselves are annoying and stop the pace), so you fall and lose a bit of health. Your dashes stopping if you so much as graze an enemy, instead of sliding around them or bouncing off a bit. Weapons running out of ammo and auto switching to awkward weapons, for instance: Super shotgun often switches to rocket launcher. Because obviously when I was using a point blank weapon, the next closest weapon I want is a rocket launcher that will kill me with self-damage. Which brings up the ammo problem, except for the BFG, don't bother saving ammo. You are expected to constantly be switching weapons as they run out of ammo, when you run out, to go find a small zombie that they spawn in fights, chainsaw him for a shower of ammo, and continue. It is an annoyance, a chore. Then several enemies are incredibly frustrating to deal with. Prowlers (Teleporting Imps) are incredibly annoying, since they can teleport right next to you and instantly melee. Not much damage, but every time it happens, it takes me out of the game in frustration. Bonus points for when they spawn behind you while you are backpedaling away from an enemy, so when you try to dash, surprise, you get glued to them and your back gets clawed while that hell brute comes up to have a word with you.Then you have marauders, which are the most frustrating enemy I've encountered so far. It is like whoever designed the Hell Guard (the worms in the stone golems) from DOOM was allowed to make a semi-common enemy in the last half of the fight. You basically have to wait for them to attack you (flashing green eyes is the tell) when in sort of medium range and then do a burst of damage. Repeat several times. If you are too close, he will shotgun you in the face, too far, he will just throw projectiles. Attack him when he hasn't given the tell and he will just block your shot, including the BFG. He can also spawn a ghost dog that will ♥♥♥♥ you up if it gets too close and if you happen to get the super shotgun swapping to the rocket launcher automatically... well you are probably going to lose a lot of health. Meanwhile he can dash around rapidly at times, including right into your face and pull out the instant shotgun for some BS damage on you. Basically, it is an aggravating enemy to fight at worst, a chore to fight at best. I don't feel satisfaction on defeating them, I feel relief that I can move on to a different fight.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic sequel to the rebooted Doom 2016. Doom was always about the single player experience - I've never cared for the multiplayer aspects so my review will not be about that (though from what I have played, ID can do better).This game is worth it for the single player alone. Games these days tend to come with a well thought out storyline as a way of keeping their users engaged, while providing context of the character(s) and their choices in game. Doom 2016 & Eternal are no different, and they do not disappoint.ID mentioned they were building an entire universe for Doom, and that's exactly what they've done. The story picks up ~10years after the events of Doom 2016. The Slayer arrives to see Earth fighting a losing battle against the forces of Hell, and his journey to save them takes him across the universe, into Hell and 'Heaven'.We learn a great deal more about the history of the Sentinels & Argent D'nur - and while this game answers a lot of the questions we had after Doom 2016, it has now left us with more questions!------------------POSITIVE ASPECTS -------------------- The graphics/sound remain incredible and true to Doom.- The storyline is very in-depth and well planned out(see my lore guide).- The monsters/weaponry have been improved (although they were already awesome in Doom 2016).------------------NEGATIVE ASPECT  -------------------Doom Eternal introduced wall climbing, as well as a few platforming options such as 'monkey' bars to swing off, and hovering platforms to jump across.The wall climbing works, and they have been plausibly added to the landscape. However the monkey bars and hovering platforms are simply out of place and don't logically fit in.-----I've seen other players complain about the minimal amount of ammo - this isn't an issue if you have a very basic ability to manage resources. There are plenty of pickups around and heck, use the chainsaw on a demon once and you most of your ammo back..

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the previous game. So I was very much looking forward to this game. I rarely buy games at the full intro price, but this one I did based on the last games impression and level of satisfaction.However, this one is different in every way I hate. I hate the ridiculous amount of platforming and all the overwhelming amount of jump and dash mechanics. I feel like I'm spending more time trying to get through platforming sections than fighting enemies. Not only that, but I will find 5 1up's and lose them all to platforming falls rather than enemy fights.Fighting the enemies doesn't feel satisfying either. It's more of a chore. And you don't get but one or two enemies killed before all ammo and health is depleted. So you are then stuck trying to find one of the many ways to launch into some other kill mechanic to try and get health or ammo or shield, all of which require a different means and are often not available because of a cool down or lack of fuel. It's so much to manage in the fast pace and it doesn't flow well.The game has so many things to keep track of in terms of special little things that unlock this or that, that again feels overwhelming and takes away from just the pure visceral shooting I was hoping for from the last game.The enemies are stupid hard and I only went to the 2nd difficulty. The game atmosphere is also off. I can't put my finger on it, but it doesn't match my expectations based on the last game.All in all the game is not fun, just frustrating. I'll probably be forced to play it at the lowest difficulty going forward, which is disappointing as that robs me of any feeling of satisfaction.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of DOOM since the original back in '93, but this ends up being the first DOOM game that I genuinely don't like...even DOOM 3, which had plenty of faults, was more enjoyable than this.I can't summon the willpower to recommend this, as it's clear that this game has been tailored to appease a VERY specific crowd. If this game is for you, then more power to you, have a ball. But from what I've seen, that amounts to only about 20% of the people who have played it...I did NOT try BATTLEMODE, as I dislike online competitive in general. This is strictly from a single player campaign standpoint.MINOR SPOILERS AHEAD, just a heads up.1. WAY too much platforming, and it adopted the "Uncharted" (Which I also dislike) formula as I call it: Platforming - Arena Battle - Platforming - Arena Battle so on and so on.2. CONSTANT resource management for EVERY fight - Juggling between setting things on fire for armor, glory kills for health, and chainsaw for ammo, AS WELL as almost having to use a specific gun for EACH enemy, WHILE needing to keep moving and not getting caught on the environment (Which happens often) is just too much. DOOM 2016 hit a nice balance imo where you still had to keep moving and it was still frantic, but you didn't have to constantly worry about your inventory or swap weapons for EACH enemy type.3. Ammo is a CONSTANT problem, since every enemy higher than the basic soldier zombie takes a LOT of ammo to kill. On the other hand YOU die in like 1-2 seconds.4. Speaking of ammo, you waste shots on fodder zombies which SHOULD just die from a basic punch or 2.5. WHY does the Slayer NOT use his arm blade for melee? The regular punch is useless anyway.6. There is a HUGE bug that they STILL have not fixed to this day, where you are "in the floor" when you load up a checkpoint and can't fire or attack at all. The only solution is to do the ENTIRE level over again. Happened to me twice on 1 playthrough.7. Infighting is ENTIRELY for show, the demons don't even hurt each other.8. MAJOR difficulty spike between "I'm too young to die" and "Hurt me plenty", while higher than that the changes are minor.9. No Fast Travel when you revisit the level, so you have to do the whole level again - even though the game TELLS YOU to revisit when you get to your first Slayer Gate...10. Now comes Ancient Gods, where they add even MORE mechanic handling per fight, and they TOOK AWAY one of your primary weapons. They've added enemies that require a SPECIFIC mod in order to kill them, adding yet MORE juggling to each fight...11. They've also added another platforming mechanic, this time only with a specific gun equipped...12. In Ancient Gods 1, there is a mechanic with Oxygen when underwater, even though in the main campaign you could stay underwater forever. Ancient Gods 2, it's back to unlimited oxygen again?13. Marauders suck. That is all.Lastly, the story...HOO BOY was that an outright disaster. Even the diehard fans of this game won't be able to defend that. There's so many plot holes that it will trigger Trypophobia in people who don't even have it.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom 2016 was truly a return to formula, and for me Eternal went away from that formula a bitI don't really like any of the combat mechanics they added. I feel like the protagonist was weakened in order to push them. I'm certain that they especially increased enemy damage in order to support the new "extra life" mechanic. I mean I'm supposed to be a badass slayer yet death can become a regular part of combat, I only actually died a couple times on the normal difficulty and finished the game with over 20 of them, but still they should have just omitted it entirely and had the player focus on health and armor Instead of nerfing the protagonist to add it. I think the contributing factors to this is all of the other combat options they give you. The flame belch, the ice bomb the crucible, everything probably contributed to a overall feeling of being weaker, and they didin't all gel together in combat for me at all - especially considering that 2016 Doom stood out on simplicity. Ammo also just felt horribly nerfed. I get that I needed to upgrade it but I felt like did this to really push the chainsaw. In 2016 Doom, I was using it so I could get back to the weapons I liked the most, rather than desperately going around looking for an enemy that requires one fuel bar so I could continue fighting - even in a ton of boss fights which was super immersion breaking. I felt like Ito upgrade whereas before I felt like it just made me even stronger - mind you, playing on the same difficult across both games.Boss fights took a huge hit as well for me. I've never seen a game give you nothing but a boss, a giant health bar, yourself and say "good luck", which is what 2016 Doom did. In this game, every boss and even new enemy came with a tutorial which took me away from the gameplay big time. Some of the bosses had a huge "wait to attack" base, which is something I never thought they would add, and it's not what I looked forward to.All of my complaints stem from comparison with the 2016 Doom though. This is a fantastic game and the soundtrack is 10/10, it is easily worth the $30 I paid for it.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has played all the original games extensively over the years as well as made mods, I can say with confidence that this has perfected the FPS formula and I would argue is even better than the original games. The combat is incredibly fast and addictive, the music is fantastic, the level design is quite frankly the best I have seen in a very long time, the story is actually interesting with plenty of fan service and the platforming sections are actually really good and add some nice variety.The visuals are excellent and I love that they recreated a lot of the old sprites from Doom 1, 2 and 64. The game runs really well too and feels very smooth to play, had some minor bugs but otherwise flawless, especially without any day 1 patch.The only things I wish for is; 1. Modding support, mods are the one of the main reasons Doom 1 and 2 have such an active community and are still played extensively today. Add modding support and this game will last just as long.2. A DRM free version, I would much prefer this over the combination of  and Denuvo, customers should be able to play the game without DRM hindering them and should be allowed to actually own the games they buy rather than glorified renting, I will happily buy the game again at full price for a DRM free version.All in all, absolutely fantastic game that i had the absolute pleasure of playing and will continue to play extensively.

_childDocuments_.review: I gave up on FPS as a genre quite a long ago, after both seeing what happens there on average and especially after playing some titles that everyone praised as "nah this one's really good bro, not like the others" but that were, in fact, also generic as hell — like Titanfall 2.Well, this one is  good.At first I was prone to avoid the new Doom games because of their seemingly useless and casual glory-kills, but when you turn something from a mere cheap spectacle to a vital game mechanic, magical things start to happen. Unlike the regular formula of shooting the bad guys and picking up ammo in-between, this game limits your max ammo in a way that you're encouraged to not only use different weapons (which adds variability), but also watch the ammo count and replenish it mid-battle by chainsawing the enemies, as well as heal yourself by finishing off the enemies with your hands (both of which pushes you out of the comfort zone and adds the so, so needed tactical aspect of a certain kind).A lot of midwits criticized the game because of this, because they can't just circle around the arena and shoot endlessly at the enemies anymore, but who in their right mind would still want that same old mindless shootfest? Don't get me wrong, I love the old Doom games, but they are still always there to play if you want to scratch that itch, and adding a layer of modern graphics on top of it isn't gonna improve it in any way that matters.Developing a new game is always a chance to introduce new things to the formula — a chance to do things differently —  a chance that is usually not allowed to be taken in the current sorry state of the game industry, in which any new ideas are branded as "too risky", "too unprofitable", "too unconventional". For the first time in fuсking decades the stars have aligned and the higher-ups at ID / Bethesda allowed the developers to make something new, fresh and actually fun, and you bitсh about it because you act like the FPS genre has already been perfected whereas, in reality, there's still so much new additions and mechanics to play around with? Go fuсk yourself.Anyway. The game is not without its faults. The final boss is garbage and the progression of skills / upgrades hits a wall a bit too early (I maxed almost everything out at like 60% of the game), but it doesn't matter. That's not what the game's about. It's about the good old demon killing, but now in a more stylish and diverse way than before, and the game succeeds at what it wants to be.I'd even go as far as recommending this game not just to fans of the FPS genre in particular, but to anyone who appreciates and enjoys good game design and action games in general. Not buying this at a discount would be a foolish thing to do.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my initial review for this game and I will update it as I progress in the game. Currently completed Doom hunter's base as of this time of writing. Haven't played multiplayer yet.Intro:I'm not a fan of FPS genre, I'm mostly a solo RPG, hack and slash or sometimes turn based gamer. However, when I was a kid, I was able to play the Doom 1993 version, and seeing Doom eternal getting released caught my interest. Although, I haven't completed the old version yet, I decided to take the plunge and try to complete the new one this time. The graphics and gameplay looked cool to me, and therefore gave it a shot.Actual review:Gameplay: 10/10Being new to FPS genre, this game just set a golden standard of FPS gaming for me. I won't probably play any other FPS game that isn't like Doom Eternal. I love how fast-paced action this game can be. Btw, I play Ultra violence difficulty and will probably play the game again in Nightmare mode on my second walkthrough. To those who didn't like the game play, they are most likely playing on easy difficulty. I totally recommend harder difficulty as it will force you to play the game the way it is intended. You simply don't stop moving around, because if you do, you're dead. I love how the game makes you to remember each demon, as there will be a specific way of beating each of them. Other games don't usually do that. I don't usually bother what my enemy is, all I just know is that it is an enemy that I needed to kill, the end. But here in Doom Eternal, that brain dead enemy killing will get you killed instead. I love how awesome the combos you can execute the moment you mastered your weapons, skills, mods, etc. and to which demon you can do those combos at. Even in harder difficulty, I feel powerful and unstoppable, as long as I have the knowledge of each of the demon, and each of my weapons in my arsenal. I love everything the gameplay system offers. Everything simply makes sense, and none of them are gimmicky. The wave of information about weapons and skills may be overwhelming at first, but once you get used to it, you'll love them as well. Finally, I love how this game brings out your skills as a gamer. Even if you're a total noob at first, as long as you want to get better, this game will help you in your FPS journey.Graphics: 10/10Well, this is a triple A game. A beautiful stunning graphics is pretty much given on this type of game. I'm playing at maxed graphics and @100 fps on average. The environment, enemy and slayer design are all well done. The insane amount of gore and violence is pretty much what would you expect for a Doom game. It's about Rip and Tear after all.Sounds/BGM: 9/10The sounds are good enough that it can put you in the "zone" while slaying some demons. I love how awesome their battle sound themes and it matches the gameplay really well. I only gave it 9 because I think they can improve the sounds each weapon makes. It lacks the "oomph" factor. I want my shots to sound explosive and ear tearing sounds. That way, you can totally feel like you're in a battlefield, not in a Star wars movie.Story: 8/10Well... It's a Doom game. It's main purpose is to get players up and running, while keeping story telling and lore in the sidelines. I get that. That's what devs have said as well. However, they can do it better rather than writing it on codex. It feels like a Tomb Raider game would usually do. But, I do read the codex because I'm interested on how the story plays out, but I doubt there's even half the player base that actually reads it. One way of doing it, is to get Slayer's assistant to talk about the lore as you play. This way they can make places in the game more memorable, and you don't even have to bother reading codex anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: is a first-person shooter that mixes fast-paced combat with an ever-increasing difficulty steep and platforming to navigate the terrain. The game's main idea appears to be always to keep moving and is an action title that features a crazy amount of weapon and weak points to exploit in your enemies. There is a lot of detail to appreciate in its gameplay and is one of the best first-person shooters. If you are interested in slaying demons at high speed and enjoy crazy good shooting, keep reading!In  enemies have weak points that can be exploited to either make them easier to kill or disable a capacity in them, such as long-range weaponry. The attention to detail here is astounding, as you keep searching for these during combat and start to learn their weaknesses. Targeting a weak point is the difference between killing a demon with few bullets or an entire magazine! It is satisfactory, too, as you get to hear a "bing" sound every time you hit a weak point.This mixed with the game's high-speed pace makes it like an adrenaline-filled experience in which you must shoot lots of demons while also trying to search for windows to exploit their weak points. The maps are filled with pickups to obtain and platforming so you can navigate around while in combat. It is so fast that at first, it was hard for me to keep up, but you eventually get used to it and start to become better while playing, so it has a steep learning curve and just went it starts to become comfortable, it adds new enemies or mechanics to keep you in your toes.I wouldn't say I liked the system for weapon switching as I found it to be quite awkward in my opinion, you can only go back between the last two weapons you selected previously. Besides, you have to open a wheel to select any of the other guns, and while time does slow down during it, my take on it is like navigating a menu mid-combat. Since there are many tools to use, I would have preferred a more intuitive and straightforward system to select them.Speaking of the different weapons, one of the things that impressed me the most is an absolute bonkers number of upgrades and mods! There were so many that I did not know what to choose at times and are very useful! You can turn a shotgun into an automatic terror that keeps going until it is dry or add grenade launchers so demons can chew on them while you kill them. There are also upgrades to the suit, which can help you locate things in your map or lower your abilities recharge.The campaign is replayable, and there are many reasons to play it again, from collecting all collectibles to getting all upgrades. They also added twists to make it more attractive on a second run, such as cheat codes that can influence the gameplay or different modes such as arcade with lives.It can be exhausting to play at times, as I did suffer a bit of fatigue, with some missions being able to last 20-40 minutes. During my time with the title, I would usually play sessions of 1-2 tasks and then pause to make this more tolerable; I don't mind them being long, however. Also, I don't particularly appreciate that platforming seems to be implemented oddly in some sections, like having to break a wall. Simultaneously, it can sometimes lead to falling off, or some jumping platforms can make you lose momentum if you dash.The strong point of  is that it is a first-person shooter with tons of things to discover. There are many challenges, secrets, and exploration to do, and should you do; Then you can be rewarded with upgrades or weapons to add to your arsenal! It adds an extra layer to shooters with the addition of chainsaw enemies to recover armor and have to pay attention to details to come victorious in its vicious combat! Executions have gore visuals into them, and with the high-speed chaotic formula, it doesn't get dull at any moment save some platforming bits.The weak point of this title is that there is no incentive to try the more formidable difficulties. During my playthrough, I choose the one after what would be considered normal, but there was no reason to go beyond that. There are no achievements or significant rewards for beating the game at the max difficulty, and I think this can take some of that replayability I mentioned before. The story did not impress me either, as it boils down to you, killing demons while higher demons tell you to stop, and you ignore them. It could have been more interesting if we had a more interactive main cast, perhaps.It was tested on an RTX 2070 S, during my experience as of this review; there were no crashes. I would have loved if the chainsaw ran out of fuel as you use it rather than being an automatic cleave, as that could make it more gore like while adding skill to using it! There are tactics the game doesn't tell you as burning a demon before executing it still gives you armor to pick up or that you can hook to a monster, and instead of shooting it, chainsaw him to get ammo while traveling long distances. Ammunition being colorful in contrast to the blood theme of the world of  is amusing and looks sick, so I appreciate that detail! is an outstanding title with one of the best shooting I have experienced in gaming, It is a superb title with almost no flaws and adds diverse layers to an established genre. There is a lot to do while exploring the levels it features, and its gameplay is always filled with adrenaline and the exhibition of how good you can be while playing it. I had a great time with it as I went from being scare of demons to punching them out of existence! If you like this review, give it a thumbs up! If you want to add your own opinion or share something informative, do it below in the comments!

_childDocuments_.review: My heart is broken. When Doom 2016 was announced, I was excited. I'd spent nearly a decade playing through "gritty realism" FPS games galore, with restricted weapons and scripted events. The announcement trailer gave me a lot of hope. When the game finally came out, it took me nearly 24 hours to download it. But I played it for months on my old PS4. The game was everything I had been missing from FPS games for years and it truly made me feel as though I'd recaptured a bit of my youth. Fast forward to 2020 and the second installment of the rebooted franchise was due to launch. I waited patiently while issues with DRM and so on were straightened out, the summer sale came and I finally decided to buy it. 30 Minutes. It took less than thirty minutes for them to destroy what I'd spent four years dreaming about. The fast paced, in your face shooter I spent many a summer night playing was gone and in its place was some sort of hybrid mess of video game ideas. I walked right out of the first area with a shotgun and 16 shells. There was a voice que, "Rip and Tear" until its done. Unfortunatly, you can't. The game gives you almost no ammunition, what I thought was a free starter gift of 16 shells turned into literally the number of shells you can carry at a given time. Within 13 minutes I already had found two gun drones and had both of the options for the shotgun in terms of specials. One of which is a full auto option, that would be fun if you could fire it for more than three seconds before running out of ammo. Jumping platforms? The chainsaw now refills, glory kills are the only way to get health and I've seen almost no armor pick ups. The story, well right off the bat, 4 minutes into the game you cutscene kill a boss, resulting in "33% of the deamon infestation dealt with"I got to a point where I found the MG, and sure enough, "60 bullets is all you get." I turned it off. Now I'm sitting here, researching the game on steam, reddit and other places. As I read the thoughts and opinions of others, it seems that there is just so much about this game that isn't DOOM. I'm to the point of trying to decide if I want to refund it or not. And it hurts. It's been ages since any game came out that looked like it was something that a team put hard work into and even longer since I saw a game that felt like it wasn't an attempt at some company to squeeze as much cash out of me as they possibly could. This was my hope, and it's been nothing but a let down. I recently even went back and played some D16 to compare, and it's no contest for me. The 2016 game is not only superior, it's the King. Before you decide to buy this game, my advice would be to watch some gameplay videos on youtube and to research the game online. If you're expecting D16 but better, you won't find that here. It's up to you to decide if you want to get it, but even on sale, my personal feeling is: Pass.Additional Information: Ultimately I have decided to seek a refund for this product. As I continued to play the game, I found each new area more annoying than the first. Weird jumping puzzles, strange mechanics that require you to spam glory kills and grenade/ flamethrower kills to get more health and armor. I noticed as more new enemy types were added, the screen becomes cluttered with awful UI, low ammo and low health warnings galore. It's not fun to have these guns, but then have to spend your time conserving ammunition as if we're suddenly playing RE. The chainsaw doesn't give much in the way of ammo either, and I would notice that I quickly run out of ammo once more after having just filled it up again. This really does hurt. I feel like they took a box full of ideas and just slapped a price sticker on it and called it good. The game truly is inferior to the 2016 game in almost every way. The ammo and jumping system kills all of the flow the original game have, I found myself having to start stop, start stop, over and over again. Card keys had unique animations and were hidden in clever places all around the UAC facility on mars, but in this game they just hover in the air, in seemingly random locations. I feel like they didn't even try. I'd like to add a note about bugs as well. I played for a little over 1.7 hours and encountered no major bugs. That said, I still saw several instances of terrible AI, in addition to a number of hit detection problems. I had some screen tearing early on, but that seemed to clear up once I fiddled with the settings.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom Eternal is meh and has lost track of much of what made Doom (2016) fun.The game's graphics are beautiful and its performance is extraordinary. At 4k with HDR on and all settings maxed I get > 100 FPS. Other games that look worse struggle to do half that. Unfortunately this is in the service of terrible level design, with constant invisible walls and objects you should be able to jump on that you just can't. There are lots of props, but few can be destroyed. You can't even shoot out windows! It feels like you're killing monsters on a movie backlot.As for combat, there's no cover, no reloading, and you're constantly swarmed by enemies and have to keep moving not to die; this is all perfect and exactly what the last game got right. Now, however, you're overwhelmed with detail beyond just glory kills and sawing monsters in half for ammo. The chainsaw refills its own fuel and you have half a dozen other new abilities that do similar to refill this and that, and because the gameplay is designed taking that into account, constant micromanagement in combat encounters is required just to survive. The "kill X guys in Y way" challenges for weapon upgrades in the last game added to the variety, but there's so much going on in every fight now that the frantic spontaneity is ruined.Also: jumping puzzles! I can die in the same combat encounter a dozen times and go back for more. I wouldn't have as many hours in this game as I do if this wasn't the case. After a couple falls into the same pit, though, I'm done. Very few first-person games get jumping puzzles right, and Doom Eternals's no exception.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom 2016’s reinvention of the franchise was a success story no was really expecting, reviving old school shooting mechanics with modern technology to create an intense and invigorating shooter. Doom Eternal expands on every aspect 2016 revitalised, bringing a bigger yet more refined shooter that excels in every category. Eternal is a textbook example of the ideal sequel, building upon all of the ideas its predecessor introduced without invalidating the experience of the original  game.The star of Eternal is its extremely fast and intense gunplay, creating a perfect sense of flow unmatched by most shooters. Eternal immediately emphasises movement, evidenced by dashing and very open environments littered with climbing equipment. Doom wants you moving at all times, which creates a constant chaotic tension as you need to route your way through environments while under attack to avoid death. Thankfully, the game also provides plenty of resources to help combat enemy threats. Plenty of lifeline equipment is available at all times to provide the player with health, armour, ammo or even just a quick escape from a hairy situation like the blood punch and ice grenades. This means mistakes aren’t overly punishing, as there's always a way to easily return to the fast paced shooting antics and their constant availability regardless of your equipped weapon makes them extremely useful throughout the game.The equipment systems work great with your impressive arsenal. All weapons return from 2016 but are improved with various new upgrades that are dotted out across the campaign, meaning you’re constantly finding new powers to play with and building a memorable experience as you slowly power up. Every weapon brings a unique joy to the table, and the limited ammo encourages constant experimentation as you are forced to switch up your playstyle. All of these elements make Eternal’s gameplay an absolute treat as you have to manage a constant barrage of offense and defence, forcing a frantic amount of energy from the player. Boss fights unfortunately stagger at times, usually becoming serviceable at best and tedious at their worst, but the larger demonic horde battles were endlessly enjoyable as Eternal trusts you with fighting more and more powerful groups of foes.It would’ve been nice to have more reasons to return to the game, master levels was a neat idea that hasn’t been played with enough and some extra mechanics like a ranking system would've been fun to play with. Eternal’s gunplay is refined to near perfection, with more than enough variety and potential experimentation provided, the game remains enjoyable for as long as you need it to be.Eternal’s fights can get very intense, so it’s great that quiet time is also handled superbly. Fights are broken up by traversing each level, giving the player time to hunt for secrets or just explore the environments, and what beautiful levels these are. 2016 focused on drab ruined facilities with the occasional dip into hell, which made for some awesome levels, but it could feel a tad repetitive. Thankfully, Eternal’s levels feel far more diverse, there's a huge variety in environments through colour and geography, as well as some amazing background detail that sells the scale of the demonic invasion.The secrets are really well implemented too, they’re just the right amount of hidden and the player is free to search for them uninterrupted. There’s important gameplay buffs found hidden in each level as well as challenge rooms to test the player, but I loved finding the secret collectables that take fun forms, such as the vinyl songs or floppy disk cheat codes. They play into a solid retro feel that Eternal braces, often paying homage to the old games with the classic health pickups and modern interpretations of classic enemies.Visually, Eternal is a treat. Environments and models are richly detailed, but it never takes a hit on performance, allowing the game to look and feel deadly without compromising on performance. Demon designs too are brilliantly detailed, all looking beautifully unique from another, but all maintain a deadly and threatening aura. The animations especially are finely crafted, glory kills are quick and brutal, which sells the power of the Doom Slayer without interrupting gameplay. Demon animations too, all have very clear sells of what attacks they’re about to use, conveying vital information to the player. Eternal stands as a good game with it’s shooting mechanics, but the outstanding quality of the world that surrounds the combat is what makes the game greatDoom’s never needed a story to justify rampaging across hell, but I really appreciate the extra effort these modern entries take into crafting one, even if it doesn’t always pay off. The delivery of the story really synergises with Doomguy’s attitude within the narrative, Cutscenes are brief and always get to the point immediately. You can ignore the story as much as he does and just be treated to cutscenes that are crafted with such care, the voice acting and writing resulting in many memorable lines.Yet for those who want to get invested, the expansion of Doom’s world feels pretty well crafted. It’s nothing revolutionary, embracing a classic good vs evil narrative, but it does an amazing job of setting up massive stakes against you. There’s plenty of codex pages to flesh out the world and learn more about each new interaction that seemingly appears from nowhere, but there’s also a lot of fun found in embracing Doomguy’s role as revenge-ridden rampager. I don’t think I’ve ever seen a silent protagonist justified so well, it's always cool seeing exposition or villainous plotting being rebutted  with a cold glare and a shotgun ♥♥♥♥.However there are times where I think the plot can get too detailed. I think a lot of Doom didn’t need to be justified, it’s why Doomguy is so fun to embrace as a protagonist, but Eternal feels insistent on telling more than it should. While I like the introduction of the Makyrs and Night Sentinels, I feel like at times we delved far too deep into them, making the factions just seem a tad generic at times. The worst example is Other elements of the plot set up in the previous game also feel completely ignored. I wish we’d gotten to focus on humans a bit more in this entry, 2016 had a good dynamic with how Hell’s Argent Energy was being used by humans and placing them in danger, but they’ve mostly just taken a back seat in the conflict this time. Samuel Hayden particularly, was such a disappointment. He was such a  great opposition for the player in 2016, being set up fantastically, so to end as such a useless expository character was a real shame. Eternal’s story still allows for plenty of good moments, but I think it could’ve been taken further in keeping the world consistent from 2016.Doom Eternal is an incredible FPS that does an outstanding job dedicating itself to a particular style by refining every element of the game. It’s absolutely worth playing if you want to enjoy a shooter that pushes the boundaries, but more than that, it’s just really fun.
