_childDocuments_.review: Devs: get bullied into removing denuvoEveryone else: wE diD it BoIsJokes aside, props to the devs for actually listening to the community.My old review: 9/10, good game. Nightmare is the way to go to fully appreciate it. Like the dev said, once you go Nightmare you can never go back. Doom Eternal is unforgiving at first but it really tries to make you a better player. Everything they throw at you has a counter, you just have to learn it. Once you start learning how to manage your ammo, you'll often find yourself stocking up on 3 pips of fuel.Most of the pros have already been said so I'll just say my cons. My biggest gripe is that the amount of respawning fodder enemies (specifically ranged ones) is a little overboard in some of the last missions. I get that the idea is to give you an infinite ammo source, but that is already handled by having just normal zombies. Seems counterproductive that the entire point of the Marauder, taken from Hugo Martin himself, is to have you kill all the other demons before you can focus on him, only for the game to just keep spawning ranged fodder enemies that snipe at you.Also, unnecessary cutscenes. There absolutely does not need to be a 5 second unskippable cutscene to show you that a door 3 feet from you has opened. And speaking of unskippable, for some reason in the second last mission half of the cutscenes are unskippable. This doesn't matter on first playthrough, but it definitely gets annoying during replays.Not refilling ammo when replaying missions is a shame. It seems very inconsistent. Half the time going into your base gives you back ammo, but half the time some of your ammo types are only 25% filled.Minor critiques, but it was also a strange decision to exclude the enemy introductions on the final version. I don't know why you would bother animating that stuff for pre-release just to exclude it. I also don't get what's up with the amount of tutorials. Leave it in codex entries, but having it as a tutorial pop-up to tell you how to defeat the enemy is dumb. I really feel like that stuff was made to appease bad game journalists...

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay here is pretty straight forward. You’re on an island, and it’s your job to build and populate it how you see fit. The level of detail and the amount of things that you can do is pretty staggering. And it’s all done with a level or adorable that is infectious, which given the times we find ourselves, is a much needed distraction.All of the content is rated E for Everyone, and you won’t find anything offensive or objectionable in the game.The controls are mostly very easy to use and quick to learn, even for kids.The short version is that you combine resource gathering and management, with crafting new items, building homes, and customizing every detail of your community. From building waterfalls, to going fishing, and decorating the interior of your house. There’s a lot of detail in all of these things, and you’re free to create at will.One of my favorite details is the day/night cycle which in sync’d the to Switch’s internal clock. So it’s morning in-game, when it’s morning in your timezone. It’s dark when it’s dark outside for you... you get the idea. It’s just a nice touch in-game.You can also play online with friends, allowing others to enter your town and send them messages in-game. Likewise you can visit a friend’s island remotely, or in-person through local multiplayer.10/10 would highly reccomend this game to anyone looking for a peaceful getaway for a while. :)

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to give this a 'No', but it feels like too much of a departure from the feel of Doom. I loved Doom 2016, I wanted a sequel to Doom 2016. This is something that uses Doom 2016 as a reference only. There is less feel of sci-fi horror. The art style is too bright, too comic bookish/cartoony. The fights are not about raw brutality. Extra lives are a thing to collect and fight difficulty even at Hurt Me Plenty is tuned to make you use them, Glory Kills are now something you must do if you want to keep your health up, chainsaw kills are required to gain ammo due to extreme ammo scarcity for even the basic weapons, switching weapon types to match monster 'weaknesses' is required to not run out of ammo trying to just gun them down, and worst of all (imo) is the introduction of a monster type that requires fighting at a specific range and timing your attacks as counter attacks. I'm sure some people will enjoy the new feel of the fights and the new art style, but it isn't for me. As I approach the end of the single player game I find the fights more frustrating than fun. If another Doom sequel is made in this same style I'll definitely pass on it.On the plus side, the technical execution of things has been fantastic. I've run into no major bugs or crashes.EDIT: I guess Bethesda now replies to negative reviews? You guys doing ok over there? Thanks for telling me my reasons for not digging the game style are invalid because you wanted to make the game more challenging, but in the words of The Dude "Yeah? Well, you know, that's just like uh, your opinion, man."

_childDocuments_.review: I still remember looking for and watching all the coverage i could leading up to the release of the game. I was even fortunate enough to play the "Mars Core" portion of the game early at QuakeCon. I couldn't wait for it to release. Let's start with the base game. There's an overabundance of third person cutscenes, which in my opinion feel out of place. It just feels forced as a means to let you see your custom Slayer skin in action, nothing more. The cinematography isn't anything special to justify this either, and the best cutscenes are in first person. That one moment in the initial reveal of the game where the Slayer steps on Phobos is such a masterfully executed scene, all in first person. It gave the Slayer a powerful presence by conveying how much fear he strikes into everyone. Unfortunately, they over-convey this in the final game, which overall hurts the gravity of his presence and feels like fan service. The game doesn't think once or twice is enough and overdoes it as if no one understood the first time the Slayer is dangerous - this principal of overdoing certain ideas is felt throughout the game. The UAC spokesperson for example, functions as a representation of companies with no remorse for real people, and it works to good effect. Eventually, the dialogue dwindles into a gimmick. It just doesn't hold back. The story of the campaign itself, i don't really care for. I've tried to, but as with 2016 it loses my attention over time. This doesn't bother me at all, as long as i know i'm here to rip and tear, and nothing silly happens. This game tries really hard to realise its gameplay mechanics in every way it can. Something i've rarely seen in any game. Each and every thing is meant to have its place in the game, with one infamous culprit known as the chainsaw. The chainsaw is intended as a means to replenish your ammo, which you have to do very often when you first start the game. I know it annoyed many people, but i personally didn't mind it. Why? The small ammo amount acted as a means to push players to use their arsenal to their full, instead of sticking to their favourite weapon - something i was guilty of in 2016. In other words, the game says "f you play this game our way and use all the weapons", and to be honest it's better that way. I suggest learning to weapon-switch on the fly instead of relying on the weapon wheel, it's incredibly satisfying if you let the game pull you out of your comfort zone of sticking to a few weapons. It's just a shame the chainsaw animation is as repetitive as it is, even against the heavy demons. There's also the platforming sections, some people hate these parts. I don't see why. The platforming sections help you understand how to manoeuvre better in the air, which comes in handy during combat. To summarise combat mechanics, you have your basic weapons, flame belch for armor drops, glory kills for health, bombs and blood punch for some space, BFG for even more space, the freeze grenade is rather multifunctional, and of course there's the double jump and double dash for manoeuvrability. It's all really simple and you constantly rotate between everything, it's just a lot to juggle and requires your full attention as you go up against many types of demons with different weaknesses to tackle. It works to great effect overall, forcing you to be strategic and process everything that's happening around you constantly. Now, on to something i genuinely despise. The bosses - referring to the main bosses here, no recurring mini-bosses such as the Marauders. This is one area where the 2016 game blows Eternal out of the water. This is where the approach to the combat mechanics falls apart for me. As a side effect of the small ammo management and lack of an infinite ammo weapon (such as the pistol in 2016), you're stuck fighting bullet sponge bosses while you constantly refill your ammo. There was still a simple solution to this - have your bosses drop ammo after taking certain amounts of damage. Instead, this game wanted to lean heavily into its combat mechanics and didn't see another way about it. I really liked 2016's bosses, and wanted more of it. A personal fight with you and the boss, a vastly unique enemy type that will test you differently and more intensely. Unfortunately, Eternal's approach is "run around and chainsaw a grunt, shoot boss, repeat". That's not fun at all, i really wanted to like the few bosses we get here but i just couldn't.  Everything else about the base game is good. The level design, the soundtrack, the enemy designs. I really love the Mars Core mission in particular, with Super Gores Nest coming second. The level design is a huge improvement over 2016, where nothing about the levels stood out to me and there was no variety. The addition of the grappling hook for the Super Shotgun is also really nice. I even like going up against the Marauders, though they could be handled better. It seems to be impossible to avoid taking any sort of damage from them, even if you maintain the right distance. I wish there were more master levels, it's been more than a year, but only four master levels - two of them feature a classic mode which lets you start the level with just the combat shotgun, you re-unlock the rest of your weapons as you navigate through the level. It's a really fun mode, just a shame it's only available for two levels. The replayability could be far better with more master levels. Also, fix the damn customisation options. It's annoying to have a demon skin i can't apply for the campaign, and i don't care for Battlemode at all. Eventually, the first two story expansions dropped and i decided just recently to finally play through them. Just a few more hours worth of missions. Should be good, surely? Wrong. Level design was straight up boring to me in the first expansion, being a chore to push through a mission. And of course there's the Spirits, a horribly executed enemy. Remember how i said the game likes to overdo certain things? Well the Spirits are new enemies that take it way too far to the point of being super obnoxious. Let's see, they possess demons and make them around three times tougher than before, as well being much faster. The weak points of the possessed demon are removed completely. They cause a huge imbalance in the expansion's difficulty as they don't constantly appear. Oh, and you're required to use a rather boring weapon mod with enough ammo reserved to kill a spirit once you've forced it out of a demon, or it will possess another demon. So, what's good about Spirits exactly? They throw any demon's weakness out of the window, and then you have to use a dull weapon mod on them to kill them. It's very boring design. Oh right, and the final boss in the first expansion is somehow worse than any of the bosses in the base game.As for part two of the expansion, i actually enjoyed it - awkward writing aside. Level design was better, and Spirits were mostly replaced with a better enemy: the Screechers. These are harmless zombies until you kill one of them, which causes them to lift the stats of demons around them. That's basically it. It doesn't overdo it while still managing to push the stakes in battle. The other new enemies were also fun. I can see others finding them annoying but i didn't mind them and i especially liked the Armoured Barons. The final boss was far better than any other boss in the game for me. It might've been a beefed up Marauder, but it was at least more of an actual boss for once, just a poorly written one.I usually don't have time to write reviews, but i woke up really early and couldn't fall back to sleep. Needed something to do :D
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM Eternal

_childDocuments_.review: Titles like these, with such hype and expectation often end up lacking in some way shape or form. They may not meet our expectations, they may be something other than advertised, for better or worse. Doom Eternal had big shoes to fill, after the incredible reboot of few years back. Post finishing this game, I can't really view this subgenre of shooters the same as I did before, and I've been playing them since original Doom came out. This game surprised me in such way that it goes to the top three SP shooters I ever played, and easily among the best games I had pleasure of going through.Aesthetically this game differs from the last one. Most notable difference is that pickups are more how they appear in Q3A, big glowing neon floating above the ground. In last game you picked up a gun off the ground, or from a crate, or some such. Here the thing will be oversized neon model that is impossible to miss. Take that as you will. Demons got a slight makeover, and added a ton of new ones to the roaster. I personally care little for these comparisons or discussions. Make your own mind up on this end by watching few clips.Structure wise the game plays nearly identically as the one from few years ago with few changes. You go into a mission, complete the linear objectives while fighting a ton of enemies required to progress, looking for secrets, items and so forth. The core overview is the same, the difference is that you go to a hub after you complete a mission. So you don't go from one area that leads into the other as it did in Doom 2016. Here you go from one place, teleport home, then teleport to another place. Take that again as you will.The big thing about this game is how the main gameplay partition was designed. Forgive me in advance but this topic is too large to go over in a review. I'm still in awe how well this was done and how much I enjoyed it, but here it goes. You will fight demons using your set of weapons. You like in previous game upgrade your weapons with mods, upgrade your suit, health/armor/ammo etc. That part is the same, however how they interact in the combat loop differs significantly. To better understand this, in most games in this subgenre you amass weapons, which while all may be useful generally let you pick what to use at your own pleasure. You end up stocking up on ammo and going for it. Now not that this is bad, but it does create few balance issues. One you will get things that are simply better or more efficient than others. Like in previous Doom super shotgun was simply one of the best guns in the game with hardly any drawbacks, and you could beat anything late game with Gauss Cannon's Siege mode using a specific rune found in the game. You could trivialize the game even on nightmare difficulty with this...This game simply WON'T let you have that.The game balance is designed in such way that to survive you are forced to use ALL your tools. Your maximum ammo pools are small, so if you lean too much on one gun you will run out. However because you have soo many tools, including new equipment launcher, the godly blood punch and dash mobility, you can do far far more than you realize. The game opens up avenues how to tackle problems. One you technically have infinite ammo (bar superweapons), since your chainsaw's last charge is on a cooldown. Using a chainsaw will refill some ammo for all ammo pools. Chainsaw however can't one shot every enemy like it did in previous game. This is to make it balanced. (you get other ways to do so). Each combat scenario you approach won't let you pick a gun and roll with it. You will be making constant decisions, each choice you make will have to lead into another one that flows from it, that capitalizes from what you did. Do you tackle a problem by leaning more on skill and efficiency or do you use a more ammo intensive approach that is easier to handle. Can you take time to refill your guns, or can you continue with what you have in that instance. You have many cooldown abilities and all of them can turn the fight in your favor.Then there is control. You in essence will have to control the battlefield. This means both eliminating choice targets quickly and knowing how to manage bigger targets. What falters what demon, how do you stop a dread knight for a second, how do you quickly kill a whiplash. Take this for example Cyber Mancubus can be dealt with by simply shooting rockets at it. Use lockon mod on it twice or so, and you solved that problem, fire and forget, easy. Also used up 6+ out of your 13 (max) rockets. Or you could decide what he has around, shoot one rocket that falters it, as you approach, blood punch to remove its armor and then blast it back to hell with super shotgun. Or you could freeze it and pound it with ballista/auto shotgun, or you could use a superweapon, or you could simply chaingun it to death. Each enemy, each problem has many solutions, some more skill oriented, some easy, and each will create risk and affect how your next action or set of actions go from there. You will constantly make these decisions because you will be overwhelmed. You will have to balance efficiency versus ease to tackle the problem. This wouldn't be anything special if the game wasn't difficult. It is. I played on nightmare and to put it simply, you have to constantly do something, constantly switch, constantly adjust, move, shoot, prioritize. The moment or two you lag can end you.  I'm not sure how the game was designed or balanced for lower difficulties, but I simply can't imagine not playing on nightmare. it's really what pushes the player to do better, to be quick, to be aggressive and relentless. Use all your tools and learn how powerful they all are.I'm simply in awe how much this combat system pushed me, how much it made me constantly think what to use, what to do. I haven't had this sort of feel since Playing Team Arena Master in UT2k4 (or CA in Quake Live). It's that kind of thing but in singleplayer. All this has to be done fast, you can't take time to breathe and think, you have to go go go. Once you get a grasp, it is adrenaline pumping fast paced bloodbath where demons are stuck in the room with you. "They are rage, brutal, without mercy. But you...you will be worse"As I stated prior, this is one of the best games I played. I love shooters, I especially love these type of shooters. Where twitch aiming is necessary and improvisation is king. When I heard people who played it before say it will redefine the genre I scoffed, but honestly after I played it, I simply have to agree. No other shooter in this subgenre took balance and mechanics to this level. No other SP shooter pushed the player to learn and adapt. To overcome the immense difficulty and live up to the legend that the Slayer is. Honestly, after pulling this sort of ♥♥♥♥...he more than lives up to it. This isn't that the character is badass because the story or game tells you so. No he's badass because you EARN IT, you own it through and through. The 20 some hours I spent completing my first run on nightmare was among the best campaign shooter experiences I ever had. Raze hell people. Rip and tear until it is done.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was not what I expected it to be at all.  And I could not have been happier for it.Huge fan of the OG Doom, loved 2016, expected more of the same for this one.  To my surprise, ID revamped the entire core gameplay loop.  However, they did it in a way that resulted in more engagement.  As the player, you can't just lean a few personal faves in your arsenal and simply run-and-gun.  Enemies are more aggressive and threatening than ever, and you are constantly being challenged to make choices about what to use and when to use it.Health, Armor, and Ammo aren't necessarily scarce, but now you have to work to manage your stacks - there's always resources to be had, but it requires that you take out enemies in a specific way to earn them.  Working that into your flow is part of the fun and essential to your survival.The introduction of weak-points adds a new dimension to threat assessment and management as well.  Whether you decide to first neuter a Manc by taking out his arm cannons or focus on and freeze that Whiplash rushing you down is a huge part of the game.  One isn't necessarily always a better decision than the other in every situation, but it is ALWAYS important that you make a choice quickly, because enemies will be all over you if you can't take the shot.Bottomline, DOOM Eternal forces the player not just to be skilled, but to play smart and make good decisions.  It's a type of engagement I have never seen in an FPS, very akin to that of a character-action game like DMC or Bayonetta.  The game will punish you for not playing the way it teaches, but once you understand what it is asking of you and execute that, you'll experience an unprecedented rush that no other game can bring you.I cannot overstate how much I love this game and how much it pleasantly surprised me.  I think we'll be talking about this one for a long time.Like the name suggests, this game proves that DOOM is Eternal.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of what I said about 2016's DOOM can also be said about this one. The combat is fun and fluid, the game is well designed and the environment is always a marvel to look at. You cannot run and hide in this game, you must always be shooting and staggering and glory killing in order to refill your health. There is some new additions; such as a flamethrower that will make enemies vomit armor shards at you which is a great idea, I wonder why they didn't have it last time. If you liked the 2016 game then you'll probably like this one. I do have one major complaint.When the game remembers that its a corridor/arena shooter, that's when I'm having the most fun. However, I'm not sure which design team got it in their head that there needed to be so much ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ platforming here. A negative review mentioned that this game is about 30% platforming which concerned me, and it turns out to be fairly accurate. A certain level of platforming is acceptable for environment traversal, and I'd be more fine with it if that mechanic was mostly used to hide further secret pathways but as it stands, every level has multiple points where the game comes to a dead stop for you to do a bunch of double jumping. Falling into chasms doesn't instantly kill you but it does punish you for mistakes as it will stab out ten health every time you fall.It's such an irritating show stopper and I never really thought this is what Doom fans wanted. We came to rip and tear, not jump around like Mario. I am not good at platformers, and if I wanted to I'd go play your Marios and your Metroids. That's not what I'm here for.Ultimately it's just a temporary (but common) irritation this game throws at me. When it remembers what it is, it's great.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom 2016 is a masterpiece. Doom: Eternal is alright, it just doesn't reach the same level.DoomGuy gets a face lift, and we get a face reveal.He also feels like he's put on 50Kg and the pace seems to have gone from frantic madness to "Hey, we've implimented a dash feature... slow down so it's useable yeah?"Oh melee? yeah that does literally zero damage now. You can wail on the weakest enemies in the game five or six times and they shrug it off before giving you a love tap and dropping your health by 25%.Graphics are incredible. Some levels do genuinely feel like the afterlife. The health/ammo pickups being aracde like are extremely frustrating. Everytime I see them I get a weird "What the hell is this?" feeling.The levels are incredible. The sheer scale of them is mind-bending and they've got that old-school Doom "Now I've got to go back there, I slaughtered everything there earlier BUT OH GOD WHAT IS THAT?!" feel to them. That being said, the platforming is just... nonsense. DoomGuy is now George of the Jungle and they can rapidly turn into a slog. Some of the levels will rip your arms off and hit you with them because the level design is wonky (see: platforming in FPS) OR because it feels like spawning some snake dudes and a mancubus on your head... and trust me, your muscle memory is going to mess up and you're pulling out the rocket launcher and not the machine gun because the pistol is now missing from your inventory...Speaking of weapons, they all feel like they're a little too crap. You put shotgun rounds into somethings face, it dies... not so with D:E - Now it ensures you use all the pretty weapons they've made for you. No, You can't have more than 15 shells on your godlike body at any one time, why would you want that? - Seriously, Ammo capacity is awful, Enemies are either sponge-laden or your bullets are .22LR instead of 7.62s. I guess it's all to do with the new "Bad guys have special weaknesses" nonsense they've introduced (It is fun to snipe a mancubus's cannons off and watch it spit teeny tiny fire at you from afar though.) It's a mechanic that, I guess works? But you need to stop, slow down, take aim... AND GET SPEARED THROUGH THE CHEST BY EVERY DAEMON WHILST YOU WAIT FOR THE WEAKSPOT TO APPEAR. Endlessly frustrating.Oh and the storyline? I'm just arriving at Dr Haydens and I have zero idea what's going on. There's a spacestation. There's an invasion. The Codex seems to be telling me that Hayden returned to Earth just in time... then it's telling me he made new energy before the invasion? Get the lore right if you're going to write something. There's some big bad angry angels that are either allied with/or rule Hell but I can't quite get that figured out. Doom 2016 had the wonderous ability to ignore storyline for the sake of gameplay, this one definitely can't go more than fifteen seconds with giving you an expose on the metaphysical hellscape battles.GIZMOs. Christ there's a lot of them. Now there's a grenade launcher, glory kills, flamethrowers, dashing around, double jumping. TOO. MANY. GIZMOS. Doom 2016 had the perfect amount of madness going on.Collectables. Yeah, Bethesda went "PEOPLE LOVED THE DOOMGUY FIGURES. MAKE ALLLL THE COLLECTABLES" and turned this into Assassins Creed apparently.It's an alright game. It's not a touch on Doom 2016.Will I continue playing it? SureWill I complete it? More than likely, but not this pandemic weekend.Will I play it again once I'm done? Honestly, no. I'll go back to Doom 2016. That knew what it was. This one feels like it's had a bit of an identity crisis during development and it wants to be too much now. Feels like Bethesda sat on Id and said "Make new pretty stuff for new pretty game" and Id rolled with it... thus the weirdness of this one.Do I recommend this game? No. Honestly. You want Doom? Go play 2016 or the originals. This doesn't feel like Doom.Edit: "Git gud scrub" doesn't justify anything you say. I've done Doom 2016 on Ultra-Nightmare. I'm good, this game is just bad.I shouldn't have to chainsaw every five seconds because I need more ammo for guns I don't want to use. I don't want to snipe bad guys... I want to tip and tear with a shotgun. But I can't.Final Edit: I tried to complete this. I couldn't be bothered in the end. Slog fest after slog fest. The final straw was platforming in Urdak. This game isn't Doom. it's Doom's half-brother who got confused with 1990's platforming. The dev's should be ashamed of this game. It's awful.Super-Final Edit: Tried again in December 2020. It's still awful. Doomguy weighs more than he did in 2016, the guns feel like limp noodles, enemies are bullet sponges and the soundtrack doesn't live up to its predecessor. I wanted to love this, but I just don't get on with it. Too much pandering, not enough play testing.

_childDocuments_.review: There are things that people won't like, which is fine. A lot of people don't like the idea of having less ammo (pro tip, use the damn chainsaw) platforming, the "puzzles" if you really want to call them that...but for me it works. This is still DOOM, anyone who says it isn't at it's core either hasn't played past the first 15 minutes or believes it's defined by just shooting without having to think.The combat it still fast. It's still a gorefest. I know this is a dangerous word to use, but it's an evolution of DOOMs formula when you put the new mechanics and ideas into place. Are all of them perfect? No, but it never once took away from the fun of slaughtering demons. It was a pretty challenging experience that I plan on playing over again on the higher difficulties. Most importantly, through all of my 35 current hours I had a LOT of fun for most of it. I also liked the more apparent story and the lore that comes with finding collectibles, but that will (and already has) differ from person to person. That being said: while battlemode is honestly very fun minus the lag and some balancing issues that id needs to work out, I'd love to see a more traditional multiplayer mode return, even it's just simple deathmatch on the current battlemode maps. With how smooth the gameplay and gunplay are, they're sitting on goldmine as far as that tradition arena shooter PVP goes.Same goes with Snapmap. People made some really awesome maps and co-op modes in DOOM 2016 with those tools, and it would only be better with the new environments and mechanics that Eternal offers. Hopefully it could return in the future.Overall: game fun. shoot demons. made me smile. Rip and tear.

_childDocuments_.review: DOOM Eternal surpasses its predecessor in every way and is the best FPS I have ever played. Everything about it is so fast paced and fun, the combat, the music, the exploration; all of it is perfect. The people behind the game were so passionate about what they were making and it shows in the finished product. I beat the game and all the slayer gates on Nightmare difficulty and it was one of the most satisfying experiences I've ever had in gaming.The game looks beautiful, performs almost perfectly on my ageing system and I only encountered 1 minor bug in my over 20 hours of playtime. And all that is packaged in under 40GB of space! (Other developers take note.)The only area where DOOM Eternal stumbles in my opinion is the story, which feels like we missed a whole other game's worth of story before this one started.DOOM Eternal is an absolute 10/10, a reminder of when games were actually fun and is the frontrunner for my game of the year.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to be a heretic and post a negative review. Objectively this is not a bad game, but I feel like it is a step backwards from Doom 2016. The main thing I dislike is that in this game, you spend a lot more time dodging/running than you do shooting. If you're the type of person that likes bullet hell games (Binding of Isaac, Enter the Gungeon, etc) and would like a great fps version of that then this is a great game for you; crank up the difficulty and have a blast in hell lol. However, to me the dodging and running around can get tedious because most of the time you are running around to find health and ammo to fight back. In this game every ammo type is shared by 2 guns, so you effectively you have half the ammo compared to Doom 2016 and way more things to shoot. Even when you've upgraded your ammo capacity to the max you feel like you're constantly fighting to not run out of ammo. Additionally, the chainsaw is capped to 3 fuel the entire game. In Doom 2016 you could save up fuel and use the chainsaw strategically either for ammo in long fights or for taking out certain key enemies, but in this game it's basically a 'press-C-next-to-fodder-enemies-for-ammo' button. This makes the gameplay essentially boil down to 1. Shoot for 30 seconds 2. Look for fodder enemy to get ammo 3. Repeat over and over again. There are plenty of new mechanics in this game but most of them feel half baked: the flamethrower is basically a press button for armor mechanic that you will forget to ever use. The melee weapon you get (no spoilers) is super cool and could've been a really cool mechanic but it turns out to just act like a more ammo-efficient chainsaw. The runes and weapon mods are significantly more balanced but as a result are less interesting to use. The runes in 2016 could be stacked in certain ways to create some really broken stuff like infinite ammo towards the end of the game; here they're just little bonus perks. Towards the end of the game you actually encounter a certain enemy that encourages you to actively switch weapons and weapon mods mid-combat which made the game a lot more fun for that whole level, but then you no longer encounter that enemy and return to the same tedious loop which shows that these mechanics really could've been much better with some more thought put in. This game is far grander than Doom 2016, the levels are gorgeous, and the enemies you encounter are far more numerous and diverse. However, perhaps due to this grander scope, the progression and game mechanics feel far less thought out to me and make the game tedious towards the end, even though the essential aspects of the game like the controls, shooting, and movement are fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: A symphony of destruction and chaos; a ballet of blood and bullets. An orchestral display of viscera and fear. You are the DOOM guy, and you will rip and tear... until it is done.It's been a very long time since a game has rekindled that nostalgic joy of what playing a video game should feel like and DOOM lit the spark that fueled an almost instant playthrough in one day. It's got all the ingredients to a perfect video game; secrets and 1Ups littered around that made me want to explore off the beaten track, gratuitous violence and carnage that satisfied me after every encounter, challenging arenas that relied purely on your own skill to complete and rewarded you for exploring earlier with huge boss battles littered in between. It's almost the perfect video game. They really, really outdid themselves. Graphically brilliant, smooth animations, excellent arsenal of weapons to use in every possible situation and varied, staggered gameplay with fantastic pacing. I don't believe a sequel has ever been done as well as this one. DOOM 2016 was also a brilliant experience, but DOOM Eternal blows it out of the water. A MUST-play if you're an FPS fan, and DEFINITELY worth the time if you're on the fence.Multiplayer is very "meh" compared to DOOM 2016 though, and it's the only criticism I really have for this game. The rest is Grade A, unfiltered beauty.9.5/10

Most likely not but why would you ever want to add another avenue of attack that someone else might use to infect your device. No thanks. Bethesda is a steaming cancerous turd in the game industry and it's a bloody shame they have their hold on Doom, the actual developers (id) are absolutely amazing. Do not buy if you value your privacy.

_childDocuments_.review: First I will say that I love Doom 2016. This is not the sequel I was hoping for. However, this is still a great game. While I don't agree with all of the design decisions, I can respect them. Just because it doesn't fit my vision does not make this a bad game. Things I like: Fast paced.Tons of shooting, tons of killing, the combat is pretty smooth.The game is genuinely difficult. I also like being able to generate health, armor, or ammo depending on how I kill an enemy.The game runs great. Easily maintains high framerate at 2K. Very pleased.Visuals are top notch. The background landscapes are phenomenal.Unlocking cheat codes that don't prevent progression when replaying missions. The cheats are a lot of fun. It's satisfying to go back to very difficult levels and destroy them with ease because now you've unlocked unlimited ammo. Very cool and fun feature.Things I dislike: The lowered total ammo quantities. I am constantly out of ammo. It sucks. This forces you to use the chainsaw frequently. Not inherently bad, just not my preference. There is a lot of platforming in this game. Not my bag, I'd really rather just shoot stuff. I absolutely hate the sections with the purple sticky crap on the ground. It's not fun to have your mobility COMPLETELY removed. Literally cannot jump or dash. You walk at an agonizingly slow crawl. This is not how I want to experience Doom: a game that thrives on fast paced shooting and movement. I did not enjoy a single section of this.Conclusion: This game is fun. I recommend it, even if I disagree with some design decisions. I can live with the things I dislike.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best shooters of all time. I didn't think it was possible to top Doom 2016, but here we are. Everything is improved: Gameplay is much more strategic (you cant rely on just one weapon). The story and lore is expanded (especially if you dig deep into the readables).The graphics are beautiful, and gorgeous with HDR.You can now see the Slayer's biceps. Anyone complaining about more story emphasis can just simply skip the cutscenes and not look at the readables.Anyone complaining about the new strategic gameplay needs to get good.I do have three minor gripes: 1. You can't punch enemies and do damage anymore regularly. I understand they want you to wait for blood punch but really, the muscled up slayer should do SOME damage with regular punches.2. While the new arcade like design is great, having weapons and secret items not be found naturally in a level and instead just be a floating icon is disappointing and feels lazy.3. I also think that the crucible and the bfg could have been done better ammo wise. Theres no fun in only having a select few ammo to find for the crucible in the last levels and it makes it so you will practically never use the thing. The bfg is similar but you do find more of this ammo type and in most levels. Also there are barely any powerups compared to 2016.Update: Just replayed the whole game, both DLC, and all Master Levels on Ultra-Violence.What a great challenge and still a 10/10 Main Campaign. Ancient Gods 1 is a 10/10, and Ancient Gods 2 is a solid 8/10 (Too much open space in the maps, and the ending is a bit of a letdown). Every Master Level is great and a worthy challenge except Arc Complex which doesn't have a lot going on. Horde Mode is a 5/10Also I never touched multiplayer in my original review. It's alright as long as you're not fighting a pro slayer who weapon swaps and kills you instantly.It's nice that the events recycle yearly to allow all players a chance to get all the paid cosmetics for free. I wish I did not have to play MP just to get their exclusive season rewards though.

_childDocuments_.review: DOOM 2016 was such an amazing experience that the devs wanted to double down on everything with DOOM Eternal.It's a good sequel, but it lost itself somewhere. Whole action feels less like "I'm the baddest badass" and more like a grasshopper jumping and dashing around while juggling a handful of different weapons to utilize the weakspots of his enemies. I didn't like that they made ammo very scarce and the best way to refill it is by killing your enemies with the chainsaw. Or replenish your armor by sprinkling demons with the flamethrower before killing them.it's a fps, I should just go in and blast everything with whatever I want, but I had to juggle all this crap in every single fight. The whole gameplay is so methodical. For this demon you use this weapon, for the other one you use this weapon and so on. You have so many options, but on the other hand you have very few.Levels are gorgeous, but I dislike how segmented every single area is. Simple puzzle->Platforming->Arena with endless demon spawns->Platforming->Puzzle->Arena.... etc.. and it's the same x100 times.The last boss of The Ancient Gods - Part Two is the best example of what this game really is. it's not a hard boss once you get into the rhythm, but you have to be picture perfect in dashing, jumping, use only a few weapons (because nothing else works) and time everything perfectly while doing so. And the devs made that boss as an exaggerated version of the most frustrating demon in the game. Ugh.66/100

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, even though I recommend this game I don't think its as good as Doom 2016. If Doom 2016 was a 10/10 I think this is about 8/10 or 8.5/10. Its by no means a bad game, just not as good in my opinion and here is why:*I think there is to many systems at play. At first when playing through the first two levels I bounced off pretty hard and didn't like it at all. But as I kept playing I eventually got in to the rythm of things and understood how I was meant to play. The game is also much harder than what I remember Doom 2016 being. While not necessarily a negative it kind of suprised me.*While the levels are really involved and much much bigger than Doom 2016 I don't think they make as much sense. I might be misremembering but when I played Doom 2016 the levels felt like a real place that had a catastrophe brought upon it. The platforming made sort of "sense" in the game. Here it doesn't in the same way that the levels in Super Mario Bros doesn't make any sense as in existing in a real world. I personally preferred the more "realistic" take in Doom 2016.*The cutscenes. From what I remember in Doom 2016 you never really left the perspective of the Doom Slayer so everything unfolded from the player perspective which I personally feel is more immersive. In this game there are cutaways and thirdperson cinematics which I don't enjoy as much. Also, many of the cool setpieces that take place you don't really have any control over but is instead scripted canned events, which is a bit of a bummer in my opinion.*The character of the Doom Slayer. In Doom 2016 it was presented quite clear that you as the Doom Slayer didn't give a ♥♥♥♥ about anything and just ripped and teared through everything with no respect or revenance to anybody. Just an unstoppable killing machine hell bent on killing every Demon in sight. In this game however the Doom Slayer actually has respect and doesn't feel as ruthless. If you read through all the codex entries this is sort of explained and make sense but I still think it feels a bit "wrong" and not quite in line with the character I learn to knew in the first game.*Speaking of codex entries, they certainly stepped that up. At point it feels like the codex entries and the lore in them almost rivals a contemporary RPG. Now, I though the codex entries in Doom 2016 where pretty damn great. The first entry for every enemy and so on were usually somewhat "serious" but the second entrie and forward usually was quite humerous and dripped with a dark humor. I remember at some points laughing out loud and I don't laugh easily. That humor is completely missing from this game which I feel is a shame. There is a sprinkle of it with an UAC announcer here and there in certain levels but they are not anywhere near as funny in my opinion. This game feels like it takes it self way more serious than it ought to as I see it.* The music is also not near as good as in Doom 2016. It is by no means bad and doesn't pull you out of the game but it doesn't really amplify the experience either. In Doom 2016 I remember really feeling "♥♥♥♥ yeah" and getting energized by the music. Not so much here. It's just...there.All of my complaints above are by no means a deal breaker. They are just things that rubbed me a little the wrong way and knocked the game down a few nothes. The game is still really fun to play though and expertedly paced. The game is gorgeous and really well optimized. It runs like butter and the framerate is solid. There are also some awesome set pieces and environments. The platforming is quite fun and I personally didn't have any problem with it.If you liked Doom 2016 there is a really good chance that you are going to like this but be prepared that some stuff has been changed and, in my opinion, not necessarily for the better.

_childDocuments_.review: The sequel to the excellent Doom 2016.The good:ID Tech 7 is an incredible engineDemons can be torn apart as you fight themVariety of very different looking locationsSuper responsive fast-paced combatThe bad:Sound mixing is poor, following one of the best sounding games of all timeArt style of 2016 has been traded for a more cartoon based lookCartoon sound effects cannot be turned off unless you change all gun soundsEnemies are spongier, the new "shooting chunks off Demons" feature only exists to try and and make hitting enemies still feel responsiveThe ugly:The game is far sillier than DOOM 2016The focus of the game has shifted from blasting demons to managing several cooldownsThoughts:This is a sequel where nearly every aspect of the game was attempted to be improved, but changing things that already work as well as DOOM 2016 did is just an crazy idea.Lets talk about the presentation.  The engine upgrade allows far more polygon pushing and better lighting.  Unfortunately you will only notice the polygon pushing, the better lighting feels wasted because the art style of Eternal has a colorful brightly lit cartoony style.  Though the engine is capable of far better lighting than DOOM 2016, I thought that 2016 consistently looked better.The music rarely (if ever) fits the locations you are fighting in, and if you look up what the composer has to say about the game then you will know that is exactly what happened - id had him try to make music before there were any finalized level concepts and even told him they weren't going to use the music he gave them.  On top of that, the sound mixing is weak.  Comparing individual sounds to their DOOM counterparts has them comparing favorably, but in actual gameplay nothing is balanced properly.  The music is less than half as loud as in 2016 (of course you can fix this in the settings, and you should!), sound effects sound tiny and pathetic compared to the enemies, you have essentially gone from a rocking power fantasy to a weaker impression of it.The gameplay loop of DOOM 2016 has completely been replaced.  No longer are you simply staying mobile and trying eliminate large numbers of demons as quickly as possible (though it may look like that at first).  In Eternal you are actually avoiding killing all weaker enemies until one of your several cooldowns to turn them into health/ammo/armor is up.  Weaker enemies seem to have less health than before to facilitate this, but this just further hurts the new loop - nearly all of your weapons are too strong on them, and you will kill them rather than staggering them for glory kills (you cannot melee them like in DOOM 2016, your melee does no damage at all unless you have a cooldown up).You are given new mobility options (dodging, leaping off trapeze bars) so that you can go airborne and escape large groups of demons easily (mainly to facilitate this "deliberately leaving enemies alive" mechanic).  Because your new traversal options are so fast, they drastically lowered your running speed.Larger enemies are all intended to be killed with a few specific methods.  This is not like DOOM 2016 where you weapon swapped to deal damage at different ranges, or because you needed AOE - the game expects you to weapon swap with every large enemy you face, and efficient combat actually requires weapon switching after firing a single shot to avoid recharge/reload animations.  Being "efficient" is more important than in 2016, as Eternal limits your ammo to less than half what you had in the first game.  On top of all of this the strongest enemies in the game are all traffic lights - you cannot damage them except for in the half second after they flash green, meaning you have to kite them around avoiding weak enemies while not even shooting.  In Doom 2016 when a powerful enemy came into the arena I always was pumped to take them on, but in Eternal I struggle to think of an enemy I actually enjoyed fighting.  It feels terrible to constantly flee weak enemies because you need to save them for pickups, the exact opposite of the power trip 2016 was.I have seen the new loop described as "combat chess."  I don't agree at all.  This is more like that game children play when they learn their shapes, putting different cut pieces of wood into a box with cutouts on the lid.  You may be able to put a piece in the box through the wrong hole, but it would have been easier if you just used the right one.  You may be able to kill a demon with a weapon the devs did not intend, but you should have just used the ones they wanted you to.I have seen people claim that there is a rhythm to the new cooldown based system, but there isn't, the core mechanics of the game actually prevent it from being in a rhythm.  The cooldowns are there to give you armor, ammo, and health.  Only armor does not quickly despawn, meaning that the only cooldown you can use "in rhythm" is the one that gives you armor back (but if you want to use the armor gaining CD in a rhythm, you actually need to avoid getting an ability that will pick up armor at full armor and apply it towards another cooldown).  You are not always going to get hit, using your health gaining CDs in rhythm will get you killed.  Using your ammo gaining cooldown in rhythm means that you will use it too early, and be unable to refill your heavier hitting weapons when the game spawns in multiple heavy demons that require the same types of ammo at once (which this game does often).The end result feels less like a DOOM game than I hoped.  Your survival revolves around managing your cooldowns and avoiding weak enemies.  When I play it I just wish I was playing 2016 instead.  I really preferred it when DOOM felt like a celebration of the simple core mechanics that FPS games used to be all about.All these absurd issues combined with the terrible new story/lore feel like extreme whiplash.  Doom Eternal is exactly the kind of game Doom 2016 was making fun of.  It makes no sense to see it here advertised with the same name as its predecessor when it is ruining everything the earlier title stood for.To put everything as nicely as possible:  I remember several individual encounters with enemies in DOOM 2016, and even how I approached them.  Despite Eternal having more variety in setting, I cannot remember a single non-boss encounter.  All fights muddle together feeling the same - you avoid packs of weaker enemies, use whatever weapons meet the weakpoints of the heavy enemies spawned, then farm ammo armor and health out of the weak ones.  Though the game is more than competent in every aspect, it is less than the sum of its parts, and I disagree with so many of the changes made.Verdict:  I think I would have enjoyed this a lot more if this were not the sequel to DOOM 2016.  I hate that this has turned into just another game where you spam your dodge button and manage cooldowns.  Some people may like that.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom Eternal accomplishes what it sets out to do as a sequel with flying colors. The fast paced combat that feels like an intentional dance with death. The blood pumping music to back it all up. This is easily one of the best shooters ever released. However, it does come with some issues.The combat can be a bit overwhelming at first. You can get used and you will have to in order to survive. Though the amount of tools you have compared to the amount you are required to use is really confusing. Weapons mods from 2016 are here though a lot of them can feel useless to you. For example, the shotgun comes with either a grenade launcher or a full auto mode. While the full auto mode is fantastic at dishing out damage, the grenade launcher is just the better option overall. You can destroy weak points with it and it is practically required to efficiently kill cacodemons without wasting a ton of ammo. It begs the question, why include different weapons/tools if I have no reason to use them all? Switching mods, even after upgrading the speed of swapping, doesn't feel all too fast either. Minor in the grand scheme of things, but still thought it was worth mentioning.The tools at your disposal are all requirements however. You will need to constantly use glory kills, chainsaw kills, flame belch kills and grenade kills alongside using the right weapon for the right demon. All these systems feed into you staying alive and it can feel pretty overwhelming to the point where you forget you had a certain tool that you should've been using like the flame belch which grants you armor from those set ablaze. I can say I didn't start using every tool at once until near the end of the game. It can just be a lot of things to focus on at once. Battlemode is meh at the moment for me personally. I don't want to judge it too much right now but all the matches I've played has been the demons rushing me down and spawning everything at once to completely halt my movement or as the demons not really used to the controls. I'd recommend swapping the button to use your summons because LCTRL, the default bind, is just a weird bind for it. I'll play it more to see if my opinion gets any better about it.HOWEVER, do not let these minor complaints get in the way of what is genuinely a fantastic shooter and love letter to Doom and its fans alike. Once you learn to use all your tools and are constantly swapping weapons, finding fodder for ammo, tearing apart demons for health and armor then the game truly shines as one of the most well crafted and fine tuned shooters to date. There are tons of collectibles from id and Doom history. A lot of little easter eggs for those who love past Doom lore and the fortress hub is a great place to just kick back and revel in it all. As for the story, this game has a pretty good one. A lot of people have complained about the story taking more of a front seat and that is partially true? The story is in the moment and rarely interrupts the gameplay and your goal. The presentation is top notch and it is a wonderful journey from start to finish with tons of codex entries in between for those who want to learn more about this fantastic world. The cutscenes, though quite few and far, are also a welcome addition for me. The skins are overall a fun extra and I'm thankful you get to view them in the campaign cutscenes as the look of the Slayer is intense. I love seeing this character in different costumes and having the world take the original Doomguy armor seriously. The cutscenes themselves also add a lot of extra character to him as well. If you don't want cutscenes in your Doom, however, then just skip them. They are 100% optional and you don't get much of the story in them anyways.I've seen people saying this doesn't feel quite like Doom (2016) and that is correct for the most part. Compared to this game, though, makes me feel like 2016 was playing it safe so that if it failed they could shrug it off. I will admit that the glory kills do seem more toned down with their intensity and that's kind of upsetting but with the flow of combat the longer, more complicated kills would've probably been a bother.Overall, yes. Do not go into this expecting Doom (2016) type gameplay and narrative. In my opinion, you're getting a far more complex and complete package but some feel otherwise. It's all fair criticism too. If you want a game that is demanding and challenging to its core then this is it. I'm happy to say the hype was real for me. I loved every moment of this game even when it got insanely difficult near the end. If you're a fan of Doom or shooters in general, this is a game you must, at the very least, play. Rip and tear.EDIT (as of 3/27/20)After playing Battlemode more, especially after finishing the campaign, I can respect what it is trying to do, but it also has very glaring issues.To start, the only thing you really have to do to win is rush down your opponent.As Slayer: Take different routes each round, though the portal to get behind the demons at the start is an easy choice, hook onto one of the two with the meat hook, get him to low health by quickly swapping between super shotty and rocket launcher, target the other demon and do the same until both are low health, find fodder to replenish armor/ammo, kill both demons with minigun easily.As Demons: Hide your outline as soon as the match starts, watch for Slayer route, surround with demons asap and unload everything.For demons it IS harder to pull off because the slayer can easily break out of a fight but it depends on who you're going against.This obviously ignores the demons you can summon in the game. There is a serious balance issue if I can willingly ignore the summons and target only the players and win. The strategy aspect is immediately lost.Video of this problem in action:  Part of the problem with this as well is the demon keybinds. The slayer gets instant access to each move just by pressing a button. The demons, however, have to switch through summons with a single keybind and then activate them with another. Why? I get that you could eliminate spam by doing this but... you can still spam easily. If the slayer has easy access to each ability then the demons should as well.Speaking of easy access, the health summon is TERRIBLE. You spawn a box you have to be inside of to heal while the slayer can just shoot fodder once or twice, glory kill, bam health. By the time you're going to want to use your health summon anyways the slayer is right behind you ready to finish you off because you're low. A better option would be to immediately or time heal the demon for a certain amount of health, that way the player can heal as quickly as the slayer can and the slayer isn't guaranteed a kill if one of the demons gets low on health.Maybe also buff the damage of the demons a bit? It never feels like I can hurt the slayer as fast as they can hurt me.When you get a match with players who know what they are doing though, hoo boy get ready to be there for awhile. It is a constant game of cat and mouse until the slayer decides to finally attack you.I like this mode for what it is trying to do, but changes are in order here. Battlemode does not detract from the campaign however, which is worth the price of admission alone.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh, boi. I loved Doom 2016. But this game is a total different breed. Not in a good way.First, the positives.- Awesome graphics- Total banger soundtrackThe negatives include the fact that a lot of things that made D2016 great are missing.  I, personally, find this more colorful approach unfitting to doom. D2016 had a dark and gritty tone.The gameplay has a lot of platforming sections. It even rivals Super Mario Odyssey. I am not kidding. If you, like me, want to play a fun shooter and just kill things, then the amount of stupid platforming puzzles will annoy the hell out of you. If I would like to play a platformer, then, well... I would just play a platformer game and not doom.The gameplay has also undergone some changing. Mostly, it became very strict. In D2016 you could rip and tear with the weapon you liked the most. In Eternal, however, the game basically forces you to use X, Y weapon, or else you will just end up wasting your ammo. Overall, Eternal is not a bad game. Not even a bad Doom game. It's simply just not Doom. If you want to have a real Doom experience, then I can't recommend the game. But if you just want to play a kinda restrictive, platforming shooter, then go for it, you will enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: While the developers of games like Ultrakill ask themselves "What new mechanic can we add to the game to expand the combat variety and amount of possible playstyles?"the Doom Eternal devs go "How can we force everyone into a specific playstyle that we've deemed to be the best?"On top of that: - Collectibles have been extremely dumbed down and are straight up just shown on your map, - There's invisible walls everywhere cause the level designers decided to go for looks over logic so you'll find yourself constantly seeing places that are easily accessible only for you to be blocked off by an invisible wall or for you to "fall off the map" and be respawned,- The game has quite a few bugs from my playtime, the most annoying of which was several instances of elevators glitching out and making me fall through them so i had to blow myself up to reset,- A large majority of my deaths were as a result of being instakilled as soon as the Glory kill animation endedOn the plus side the optimization and graphics are still fantastic but that doesn't do much to save it.I'm extremely glad that new indie boomer shooters have decided to take inspiration from Ultrakill and not so much Doom Eternal.Doom 2016 is a better game than Eternal is.I absolutely despise player freedom being gimped in a pursuit of what the developers deemed "correct gameplay", if you don't mind it then you'll probably enjoy this game a great deal more than I did.

The only single thing that Doom 2016 beats Eternal is with the art style atmosphere. Regardless, both are masterpieces.

name: MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries
detailed_description: BE YOUR OWN WEAPON OF WAR Welcome to the year 3015! It’s a hell of a time to be alive. Humanity has colonized thousands of star systems spanning a vast region of space known as the Inner Sphere. The golden age of cooperation and advancement is now a distant memory, and humanity has once again splintered into disparate factions all vying for supremacy. In the midst of these Succession Wars, power hungry Mercenaries like yourself are in a privileged position to capitalize big time. It’s dangerous work but that’s why you’re here, right? If you’ve got an itch to blast, wreck, stomp and go all out ballistic, step inside and become your own weapon of war! STORY As the inheritor of a once-prominent Mercenary company, reborn in the flames of its near destruction at the hands of conspiring factions, your quest for glory and revenge will stretch light-years as you chase threads of interstellar intrigue along your journey to becoming an elite MechWarrior and mercenary commander. THE INNER SPHERE Home to thousands of star systems and an array of stunning biomes, the Inner Sphere is alive with activity, purpose, consequence, and variety. Systems will be captured and reclaimed, major events will unfold, and new technologies will come to light. The rigors of war will be seen with each passing week as your relationships with the various factions fluctuate according to the relentless Succession Wars and your choices as the leader of a Mercenary outfit. GAMEPLAY The battlefields of the future are dominated by BattleMechs, hulking machines of war capable of leveling entire cities. As a BattleMech pilot you’ll rain havoc upon enemy ‘Mechs and targets, including tanks, ground vehicles, aircraft, advanced defenses, and reinforced bases. Few things can withstand the power of a ‘Mech for long, and the worlds of the Inner Sphere are veritable playgrounds of destruction awaiting your shielding defense or crushing devastation. BATTLEMECHS 'With over 50 unique ‘Mech chassis and hundreds of sub-variants, all fully-realized with high-fidelity models, damage states, and equipment, no two ‘Mechs are the same! Whether acquired from scouring the markets of the Inner Sphere for rare and valuable chassis and equipment, or salvaging directly from the wreckage of your annihilated enemies and the spoils of war, the maintenance and operation of your BattleMechs will be vital to your success both as a MechWarrior and a Mercenary outfit commander.' THE MERC LIFE Off the battlefield, as the leader of a Mercenary company you will need to manage all the key components of running a unit. You’ll need to maintain and acquire ‘Mechs and equipment, hire and field MechWarriors from throughout the Inner Sphere to join you on the battlefield, and manage your relationships with the Great Houses of the Inner Sphere, all of whom are vying for your contribution to their staggering war efforts. Of course, with each Contract comes negotiation, and with each victory comes consequence. OTHER FEATURES With the vast scope of the Inner Sphere and its complex system of world generation providing huge variety and replayability, the MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries experience offers no end. Outside the campaign, a fully-featured Instant Action system will allow you to customize and kick off isolated missions at any time, free from campaign restrictions. With four-player co-op supported both within the campaign and the Instant Action system, you can experience the full breadth of the MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries universe alongside your friends. Mods extend your game even further! Unlock the boundless creativity of the community to alter and expand the game in amazing ways. With a full editor and interface supporting gameplay mods out of the box your creativity will know no limits.

_childDocuments_.review: INCREDIBLE GAME...WITH MODSHad to get that out of the way. I've been a MechWarrior/Battletech fan since I was 5 years old, sitting on my dad's lap watching him play MechWarrior 2: 31st Century Combat. That game was *so* good. The visuals, the music, the AI assistant who chirped at you when you took a critical hit, all of it was so compelling and inventive. I've played every single entry in the series, as well as the MechCommander and Battletech games. I have some perspective behind my opinion on MechWarrior 5!I, like many, waited awhile for MW5 to hit Steam. As far as I'm concerned, the poor folks at the EGS were beta testers. Early iterations of MW5 were plagued with bugs, terrible enemy spawns, and a general lack of polish and variety. The base game experience now on Steam in 2022 is *much* improved. Don't get me wrong, there are some head scratching design decisions and omissions here, but that's what mods are for and oh man, there are some good ones on offer.Here are the ones I heartily recommend:- Advanced zoom (for that MechWarrior 3/4 style 4x popup zoom window)- Better lighting hangar, which restores the original PC lighting in the hangar that was removed for the console releases- Better crates, so you actually get useful items from salvage crates you randomly encounter on missions- Better spawns, because spawns are still borked in the base game. You WILL encounter magically appearing enemies within 100m of your mech without this mod. I don't mean turrets popping out of turret ports, I mean tanks and mechs appearing out of thin air. Absolutely unacceptable, this is a must-have mod- Coyote's Missions, adds much needed mission variety to procedurally generated contracts- Dropship Recolour, I like black- Expanded Logos, for more mercenary company banners- Fahad's animation tweaks, to make him less...uncanny- PGI Infantry, an official mod that adds enemy infantry. Great for MW3 immersion- Infantry tweaks, to make infantry not glow like Power Rangers- Infantry outline, see above- Max Tonnage, so you can take a legitimate lance with you on missions and not be arbitrarily restricted- Mech Shader, to make damaged mechs look less plastic- Missile Trails, so LRMs leave beautiful black smoke trails. The battlefield comes alive with this one!- Mod Options, so you can adjust certain mods and their parameters- More Enemy Mechs, so you can fight something other than Firestarters and Locust- MW2 Betty, so your audio assitant has some personality and variety! So good for immersion- MW5 Compatibility, forgot what this one does but it is useful- No dialog HUD, so you don't have crudely drawn pictures pop up constantly when the enemy are ♥♥♥♥ talking you- Paint Schemes of the Inner Sphere, adds hundreds of quality paint jobs and patterns to the mechbay- Pilot Overhaul, allows you to rename, customize, and promote pilots. Adds a ton of depth to your hired hands!- Purchase Salvage, so you can pay the difference in C-Bills between the 28 salvage shares you were alotted, and the Atlas that costs 30 shares.- QOL Upgrades, lots of nice tweaks like a repair all button for the mech bay- Repair Bays, adds repair bays to large garrisons on missions. Adds immersion and a useful tactical option- Salvage Percent, so you can actually salvage that Warhammer you legged, instead of it being absent from the salvage screen- Scary Tanks, adds variety to enemy ground vehicles including new types and variants of existing types. Also makes them more resilient as in Tabletop- Smooth Lasers, beautiful new laser FX- TS Music Mod, adds in Timothy Seals soundtrack. MUST HAVE MOD, the base game's music is so generic and completely lacks soul. Timothy's covers of classic tracks add a ton to immersion, especially Gotterdammerung-TRulez AI mod, MUST HAVE MOD. Adds more lancemate command options and makes them less stupid- Ultra Visual and Weather, makes the game look more modern- Unlock hidden colour schems, like Paint Schemes of the Inner Sphere- Dropship weapon rebalance, makes your dropship useful in combat- vonBiomes, MUST HAVE MOD. Adds numerous, quality biomes to the random contact missions.- WAR FX, MUST HAVE MOD if your system can take the heat. Adds a ton of great particle effects and turns battles into legitimate chaos- Weapons Shader, pretty- XenoPax Optimize, greatly enhanced my rig's performance (I9-9900k, 2080ti, 3440x1440p)With those items installed, I love this game. Without them, the game lacked variety and lacked the heart of what made MW2 and MW3 so good. Base game is slick, no doubt about it, but these mods really add so much to the immersion and fine detail that the Battletech universe has. I would highly recommend this game with that fat disclaimer!

_childDocuments_.review: Moving onto the singleplayer review:Have spent a decent amount of time playing this game on a competing game service:[Deleted link in case it hid my review, it was a screenshot, but I have 3d, 16h, 26m and 9s clocked in on said service]MW5 is not a perfect game. MW5 has a bunch of drama surrounding it. MW5 won't cure cancer, but neither is it the embodiment of Satan. MW5 is decidedly...  Worth 30 bucks? Frankly, yes, I'd say so, even if you knew nothing about the Battletech universe. Easily worth that if you do and you'll recognize all the mechs, weapons, and factions in the game.It lacks an engrossing narrative campaign like in Mechwarriors 2 (and expansions), 3, or 4, though there is... some body of one there. But it serves little purpose other than to give you additional motive to pump up your company and not just sit in the initial low-level area. While on that note, MW5 is very focused on that aspect of the game, with mixed results. If you aren't a fan of running a bunch of procedurally-generated missions to incrementally upgrade your arsenal and mech roster to take on incrementally harder missions with more and deadlier opponents, awesome, go ahead and leave this game behind. If you thrive in a sandbox environment, don't go away just yet.You fly around the Inner Sphere, doing procgen missions for the 5 Great Houses of the Inner Sphere. If this means nothing to you because you don't know the lore, all you need to know is it's basically like a 5-way civil war where everyone's stabbing everyone else in the back. You're a flagless mercenary commander who signs up for whoever has jobs. You can keep doing jobs for the same faction for loyalty perks (more “negotiation points”), but that's about the extent of that. Said negotiation points are used when taking mission to select bonuses for your pay, salvage rights, or insurance for damage taken (higher rate than points for base pay, but you ONLY get money for damage your 'mechs sustained). Salvaging mechs requires an all-or-nothing value of points, you can't bank parts like in HBS's Battletech, but as you gain loyalty and/or select the right (i.e. multi-mission) contracts, it will give you ample points to afford the heavy cost of mech salvage. Otherwise, weapons and gear take one or more points, with a 'tier' system giving subtle bonuses between weapons of the same type (i.e. a Tier 5 Medium Laser is functionally identical to a Tier 4 one, but has slightly better range, damage, lower heat generation, and so on).There's a healthy amount of debate about MW5 “dumbing down” the customization from previous titles, about its canonicity, people pointing at the tabletop manuals and arguing about random excerpts... look, the long and short of it is, MW5 has a different paradigm from the previous games, even 4 which was a departure from the TechManual. Where 2 and 3 had the really generous reading of “if it fits crits, it sits” rules from the TT experience and you could shove a bunch of lasers into the legs or something if it made you happy, MW5 opts for a more fluff-oriented approach of battlemechs having a set role. 'Mechs will have, say, 3 "Large" Missile slots, which can each fit up to an LRM-20, or any smaller size of the same family (an LRM-15, 10, or 5, or any size SRM). It's a one-to-one hardpoint swap -- you don't "double up" on smaller sized weapons. A slot's a slot, fitting one and only one weapon; it just has a maximum size that'll fit.I preferred MW4's system, myself, as it made weapons a bit more abstracted in size (wasn't just small-medium-large, but different numbers of 'sockets' taken per weapon, and components having a number of 'open' sockets that you could fit accordingly), but either way I personally consider it better than MW2 and 3; you may not, and your opinion is perfectly valid, too. My take on it is, if a 'mech is meant to be a missile boat, it's a missile boat – you can't just arbitrarily decide it now carries twin AC/20s. This means that you're forced to prioritize salvaging or purchasing 'mechs (or variants thereof) specific to the roles you want them to serve, rather than the old way of 'mechs basically being “choose your favorite-looking/most-meta-hitbox'ed one” and only using that. I prefer it that way. You may not. But, weapons aside -- No Ferro-Fibrous nor Endo-Steel. If you know what this means, you know, and there's much gnashing of teeth and wailing of women at this. Again, call me a shill, but I equivocate it with the lore: At this point in the timeline, FF and ES are both Lostech. And, funnily enough,  Similarly, engines can't be changed in rating, nor can you mount Light/XL engines (Again, something something lore something something Lostech). Again, again, some variants actually have XL engines, 'hidden' from you seeing them on the interface. They even take crits.The game is set roughly in the 30ish years prior to the Clan invasion. What does this mean? Well, if you have passing familiarity with the BT franchise and consider yourself a salty veteran because you played MechAssault once or twice, this means you won't see Timberwolves (“Mad Cats”), Stormcrows (“Ryokens”), Mad Dogs (“Vultures”), or any of the other Clan-designed 'mechs, nor will you see any of the Inner Sphere Clantech-derived designs that have been 'poster mechs' like the Bushwacker or Uziel. The game does feature a subtle time progression mechanism, such that as you play the game (and progress in the timeline), 'mechs with more powerful weaponry, or later variants (with different weapon slots) will begin spawning as opponents and in shops.The game, at least at a surface glance for the purposes of this review, DOES appear to just... FEEL better than the pre-patch version. There are a bunch of UI tweaks that clean up a lot of what you're looking at, and a bunch of subtle immersion stuff like character lipsyncing has been added. Dumb, I know, but have to say it because there's a committed force of trolls ranting and raving about how it's literally the same since day 1. I've been playing on and off since day 1. It's not.I return to my first rhetorical, do you like sandboxes? If you don't, then you probably won't like this game, but that doesn't really mean the game is objectively bad, it just means you don't like sandboxes.

_childDocuments_.review: Without mods this game is aggressively "meh". PGI needs a swift kick up the arse. They got very complacent because nobody else is making Mechwarrior games, so what are you gonna do, not play? If you're not going to mod this, or are getting this on a console, get it at a deep sale.THAT SAID, with mods this becomes so, SO much better, it's not even funny. My main recommendation would be either YAML (haven't personally tried that one out) or MercTech (the one I'm running rn). They add so much customizability and potential to the otherwise slim base game.Want to drop the engine down from a 340 to a 320 on your Victor? Sure. Or maybe you want to slap in a 380 clan XL into your Banshee and give it a pair of hatchets? Go nuts! New weapon calibers, new equipment, unlocked customization, slap in the TTRulez AI mod and give your lancemates battle roles! Change your mech's cooling to double! Give it Ferro-fibrous armor! The possibilities are, uh, not exactly endless, but it sure beats the ♥♥♥♥ out of whatever the base game is doing.The game itself is, like I said, pretty mid. The story is uninspired, more or less just there to have an excuse for things to happen. The gameplay is really good though. There's nothing quite like sitting into a 100 ton avatar of death and destruction, accompanied by 3 other 100 ton avatars, and beating the snot out of other 25 - 100 ton goons. Weapons sound and feel good (and could sound and feel even better with mods, cough cough), the mechs feel good to pilot, having enough of the signature weight and inertia to really make you  like Batman. Piloting a mech.One major downside of the game is the braindead AI. Mods make it tolerable, but it's still pretty bad. In vanilla though, your lancemates will sniff fuel and eat glue while the enemy pilots are divinely inspired marksmen that have trained since their inception to land a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ gauss slug in between the asscheeks of a mosquito at 1000 meters away. BLINDFOLDED. It is so frustrating to watch your team do the poopshuffle in place while you're getting dismantled by omega cracked enemy AI. To be honest, if there was no mod support, I'd flat out not recommend this game solely for that reason.At the end of the day, there are much worse games out there. And if you want Mechwarrior, it's either this, Online, or trying to fiddle with getting the older games to work. Beggars can't be choosers I guess.
