_childDocuments_.review: 10/10. Best -not a- golf game. Miraculously "putt"s together dozens of mechanics from dozens of games yet still feels original. Game never runs out of surprises. I suggest playing with a controller, mouse controls were a little flicky for me. I originally played this on apple arcade, best input method could be a touchscreen, but controller is a close second.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: A great way to make people laugh is to surprise them, and What the Golf? is almost constantly surprising. Golf is almost never just golf: It becomes soccer, driving, bowling, first-person shooting, archery and more...When you think you've got a handle on things it'll switch it up on you, so instead of your bow shooting an arrow, it'll shoot 100 arrows or it'll launch you through the air instead. Just great, hilarious barrage of gags. If you want to get away from the boredom of life and leave a smile on your face, maybe it's time to play What the Golf?
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot of golf in What the Golf? Like, tons. You never stop golfing. You golf at one hole, and then you golf at the next hole, and to get from that one hole to that next hole you golf your way there. Even when you're done with What the Golf? the golf doesn't stop. Want to read the credits? You have to golf your way through them.At the same time, there is very little golf in What the Golf? because What the Golf?'s golf is almost always something other than golf. Sometimes it's soccer or bowling, sometimes it's a first-person shooter or an interplanetary physics simulation, sometimes it's snowboarding or a driving game, and sometimes it's a cowboy spitting into a bucket while electric fans try to blow his loogie off course.It's also lovely and funny, has a delightful soundtrack, is full of secrets and references, and is occasionally quite challenging. It's a journey through a strange and surprising world where everything is golf even when it isn't. And when you finish What the Golf? you don't so much feel as if you've won at golf as you have defeated Golf itself.What the Golf? has one simple system you learn immediately: Pull back, aim, and release. This same control scheme is used in every level of the game, and for moving around the map between holes and levels—though when golf turns into bowling, cycling, archery, soccer, or any of the other things it routinely turns into, finishing the level is rarely as clear cut as simply pulling back and releasing. Sometimes there are explosive barrels. Sometimes kids kick your ball away. Sometimes the pole you're aiming for flees. There are, quite often, cats. Sometimes you're a cat! (Other times you're a crab, or a moon lander.)It's a hilarious and surprising game. Every time something funny happened I recorded it, and now I probably have about forty-five damn minutes of footage that I'm not going to put in gif form (with the exception of the handful you see here) because the surprises are much better if you discover them yourself. Sometimes what you think you're going to be sending across the "golf" "course" isn't what actually moves when you release your mouse button. Sometimes there's a silly pun that fills the screen when you've finished a level. I laughed a lot while playing.Each level also has different ranks. Hit the flag with the golf ball (or whatever it is you're flinging across the level at any given moment, which can be a ball, a club, a hat, a house, a bomb, a bicycle, a horse, yourself, or a dozen other things) and you can optionally try a more difficult challenge, usually to complete the level in a certain amount of moves or within a time limit. There's also a final challenge for each hole that awards you a crown, which is often a twist on the level itself or a completely different activity, and it usually isn't more difficult than anything that's come before. Complete each level on all three ranks and you'll unlock a nice little trophy, like a chicken or a spaceship or, oddly enough, a trophy.In addition to the ever changing not-quite-golf levels, there's a bunch of other video games delightfully incorporated into What the Golf?, including Portal, Guitar Hero, Metal Gear Solid (yes, there is stealth golfing), Flappy Bird, and plenty more. Golf is a game, but now all games are golf, too.The only issue I had with What the Golf? is on certain frantic, reflex-based levels which are a bit more awkward to control with a mouse than I imagine they'd be on a touch-screen. Steering a speeding car down a narrow patch filled with explosives isn't the easiest thing to manage with a mouse, and as for a banjo I had to bounce over an Old West-style town (I can't explain it further than that), I still have no idea how I was meant to properly control it. I succeeded by accident on that level.What the Golf? has been in development for a while—I feel like I've tried it at several indie game events over the past few years—but now that it's out I'm delighted to see its a fun, funny, extremely inventive puzzle game and a pleasure to play from the first hole-in-one to the final cat-in-seven.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: What the Golf! feels amusing and original initially. It is incredibly casual and perfect to dip in and out of when you don’t have a lot of time. Essentially it is golf, even if they say it isn’t, but a pitch and putt version where the ball has been replaced with a whole host of objects, ranging from household items to animals. When I first started playing, I was having a blast. It concentrates on being humorous and entertaining. Everything is set up to make you smile. The novelty slightly wears off as you progress but the game still does a great job of throwing in a few surprises and curveballs even towards the end when you think you’ve seen it all.I would say ninety percent of the games are fun and challenging, but fair. However, there are a few holes where the mouse control is extremely frustrating to use and this mars the experience slightly. There is quite a variety in the holes you play. Some require you to complete them in a certain amount of shots, some are timed and some have multiple layers. These elements make the holes a lot more difficult and then it becomes a bit less casual and a lot more frantic. Speed and accuracy are needed with a slice of luck to complete these. They can be extremely difficult and will take you multiple attempts.The hole is always the same, so you can learn from your mistakes and try a different approach next time until you complete it. It is quite rewarding when you finish a hole that has taken a long time to defeat.There are numerous comical touches sprinkled throughout the game from the theme tune, to the wonderfully named holes. Even navigating around the lab can be funny with some choice quips and jokes all berating golf.There’s about ten to fifteen hours of gameplay if you try to play every hole and dabble in everything it has to offer.The projectile you need to get in the hole is controlled by mouse movements. Pulling back with the LMB sets the power and release it to shoot the object. Sometimes it can be very difficult to set the power correctly, especially when you are on a timed level or controlling a car or similar object that continually moves at pace. There are also other levels that can be frustrating due to annoying mechanics, but thankfully these are in the minority. There are four main sections which are career mode, sporty sports, challenges and party mode.This is where you’ll spend the majority of your time. There are twenty-one themed zones to navigate in the lab including outer space; football; athletics; exploding barrels and driving themed levels. There is quite a lot of variety in each zone and it mostly keeps things fresh, considering the ultimate goal is always the same.Each area will have a varying degree of holes and there are three tiers to every hole. The first tier is simple and just involves you hitting the object into the hole with minimal resistance. Tier two is harder and will introduce new elements and difficulty into the hole. For example, there might be trees, moving cars, cats and boulders waiting to ricochet your “ball” into oblivion. Tier three is usually bonkers and the most difficult to complete. This tends to be very silly and can be completely different to the previous tiers. It could introduce a timed element or ask you to complete it under par. If you finish all three tiers you are awarded a crown. Get a crown on every hole in that section and you’ll get an achievement.Here is a video of the three tiers. As you can see, they are often very different from each other and vary in difficulty. You will need to complete at least one tier on every hole in the area to move on to the next zone. There is a computer blocking your path until you meet the criteria to pass. Once you meet the quota you then play a mini game where you have to defeat the computer to gain access.Occasionally, the zones have small puzzles in that you need to solve. For example, in one area the holes are hidden behind trees and you have to go to another level to collect a circular saw to chop them down before you can play. There are a few instances of this which makes navigating around the lab a bit more fun, but nothing too difficult. There is a teleporting option once you have reached these areas and you can fast track to any zone you have entered, which is perfect for achievement hunters.This will take around an hour to complete and is all sports themed. It’s great fun and surprisingly varied. There are daily challenges where you can compete on a leaderboard. There are other challenges you can try also. This is just a versus mode where you can race each other and the winner is the first one to complete the hole.Visuals are basic but very colourful and comical. They don’t feel out of place in this type of game which is crazy and cartoon like in nature.The sound adds a lot to the gameplay including an amusing theme tune, some memorable moments during play and lots of great special effect sounds.Curator Info:

_childDocuments_.review: You adjust the power of the swing, aim in the direction you want to swing the club and click. This gameplay mechanic is very simple in theory, but what's exciting about this game is that it takes it to the next level with a barrage of creative, wacky and charming ideas. You use this basic control scheme to drive a car, make a chick flap it's wings, fling a man, move a house, kick a football, clip clop as a horse and many many more. There's a lot of surprises in this game as it experiments with perspectives be that 2D or 3D. It replicates gameplay mechanics from other games, while making it's own ways to mix up the simplistic control scheme. You can do a 2 player competition mode against a friend and make your own maps, as well as getting through the singleplayer mode that features a hub world and collectibles to unlock. With how many levels there are, the game almost feels endless when you start playing for the first time. There's also more bonus content for you to find once you've completed the story mode and the game has daily challenges too! 10/10 Extremely accessible, unique, fun and confident in it's own creative vision and it's so easy to recommend this game to others because of this. The music is great the visuals are colourful, minimalist and pleasing to look at and the gameplay is great from start to end. It's a very welcoming game for everyone...WHAT A GAME! Definitely worth £15.49

_childDocuments_.review: + A hilarious game that makes you laugh 100% of the time+ It has a surprisingly reasonable amount of content+ A lot of references to other famous games + Extra challenges to make your life even more difficult+ A funny memorable soundtrack+ Daily challenges that can be the reason for the players to come back to the game from time to time- Sometimes the game carries way too far from the golf and it stops being funny-Some courses are really boring and weak compared to the creative onesYou should probably know that kind of games where the main goal of the game is to make players laugh. It’s not about the skill or the rich story or insane graphic solutions - no, it’s all about having fun and a really good laugh. Those games are a rare thing nowadays, but when they hit the market, it’s usually a blast.What the golf? Is the exact example of the game I am talking about. It’s funny and silly in a good meaning of this word, it makes you laugh all the time and it’s a chill experience in general. The only question I still have stuck in my head is “Why did they even create this game?”. I mean why did they take golf as a starting point and why did they escalate it so much. I guess those developers must be really in some weird relationships with golf, that’s for sure. At first glance, on the very first course, What the golf? Looks like a classic golf game, where the player has to drag a mouse or release the key button on the gamepad to point the arrow and send the ball to the hole. But then in the next stages, you will find yourself playing as a golf player itself who has to be delivered directly to the hole. And on the next hole, you have to control the big house that is rolling around the village with a hole at the end of the course. And then all of a sudden you just have to drive a mini car to the hole.This is what this game is all about, the main idea - they take the general idea of the golf game, and then they do whatever it takes to design the most creative and weird courses to make people laugh and have a good time playing the game. There is no point in the detailed description of the game courses because it will simply ruin all the fun and spoil some really good and unexpected moments. The only thing that you have to know is that this game is full of surprises - you think that you will hit the ball now but then something weird happens. And what’s really good about What the golf? is that it has tons of those creative and funny courses. I was expecting that this game would be much shorter and that I would be bored of it pretty quickly, but it turned out to be a massive game with a reasonable amount of content. When I say reasonable - I really mean it, because you never feel like you are tired of it or you didn’t have enough of the game, it just has a perfect amount of courses. After the short introduction to the game, the player finds himself on a map with different mini-games. Each map section is divided into different themes, such as sport, video games, countryside, wild west, space, and many others. The player has to complete each level at least one time to proceed with the story, but if you are the completionist, you have to beat the level at least three times to get the crown. The second and third level of the course is usually a bit trickier than the first one.In order to proceed with the story, the player has to finish the required amount of the courses and hit the button to open the doors to the next section. After that, the player has to play a fairly easy mini-game that reminds me of Arkanoid against the evil Computer. This evil Computer is the main boss of the game that will remain the biggest threat to the player till the end of the game.  The main campaign can be finished in around 3-4 hours and when the player is done with it, they can always play some extra levels or focus on finishing the game on 100%. There is also a daily challenge event that tests the player’s skill and can be a fun reason for the player to log in to the game from time to time. The goal is to complete a few golf courses using as little as possible pars. After finishing it, you will see a leaderboard and a position of yours on this daily challenge. You can also play it with your friends in a local co-op.The developers already work on the content update of the game and plan to launch the ability to create your own courses to share it with the community.What the golf? Has pleasant 2D flat graphics with mild warm colors. Some golf courses change the perspective to 3D and it looks fun and unexpected with this kind of graphics. The soundtrack is one of my favorite parts of the game - those funny and silly sounds really make the atmosphere of the game. It also has a pretty memorable song with a men choir that you will constantly hear during the game.What the golf? is a really kind and non-stress game about the golf mechanics that are used in everything that is not connected to golf at all and this is extremely funny. This game can be a perfect choice for someone who is looking for a light and nice game to spend an evening or Saturday afternoon. It’s highly recommended to people with a good sense of humor and to someone who hates golf. Obviously.

_childDocuments_.review: is a wacky game that's not really golf, but still maintains the golf theme in every stage that you play one way or another. Don't look at this game and think you will actually get to play a real golf/minigolf game, that's just not going to happen.It starts off benign enough, with the standard thought of using a player-selected direction and force to get a ball to a flag/hole. It doesn't wait very long before it gets out of hand, however, when the flag starts moving, or the thing that you need to get to the flag becomes a golf club, your own playing character, or even the direction/force arrow.The game is broken down into different sections, each with smaller sections that have doors that you can progressively open by completing the available levels. Some places will require you to do the additional challenges associated with the stages present. Every stage has three different tasks for you to accomplish, and some of them get pretty tough.Not long after diving into the main campaign, you will start encountering other sections where the game parts/levels are inspired by other games, such as  etc. Pretty soon you will find yourself trying to use the baseline golf concept to complete other sports objects, such as volleyball, soccer, track and field, bowling, and so on. And of course you are going to be trying to perform some ridiculous tasks such as well, stuff that you never thought you would be doing, like throwing office equipment or boxes, or uprooting your whole house.At the beginning of some levels, it's not clear what your objectives are or what you are supposed to do. But fiddle around a little bit and pretty soon you will be on your way to trying to make it through a potentially funny, wacky, silly, or frustrating level. I did a first-look video of this game when I started, and it was just mostly me getting used to the game and playing through the first of three sections of each stage, you can see it here:I thought that the other two sections of each stage was actually meant to be the same thing, just a little bit tighter restrictions, but later on I found out otherwise. They are all different.Who knows what was going on in the heads of these developers when they managed to put this game together. However they managed and ended up with an absolutely hilarious non-golf golf game that's going to be boatloads of fun, especially if you are playing with your family and friends watching. Everyone is going to have a good time.Another thing you can expect to see is a lot of puns, some funny, some corny, some just plain trying too hard. But whatever, it's just part of the game, I am really enjoying seeing what it's going to throw at me next, or at least make me throw next.In addition to the main campaign, there are also daily challenges and leaderboards. You can use the level editor to start making your own ridiculous levels as well. For those creative minds out there, you could probably challenge yourself and see what levels you can come up with that are more ridiculous than what the developers managed.You will also find a local 2-player Party mode that also supports Remote Play Together, and I think as a party game, this has a lot of laughs and discussions to contribute.You can play the whole game with just your mouse, so the other hand's good for holding a beer.Simple low-poly artwork that works pretty well with the ridiculousness of this game.It's got some catchy tunes and generic sound effects. Overall works well together.Not for everyone, there are quite a few levels/challenges that have timed components or various levels where you need to act fast. So people who do not want to see these kinds of levels might get stuck in some frustrating areas. If you hold down the mouse click time slows down, so that might be helpful. But if you absolutely cannot deal with time-sensitive levels, then you will probably be more frustrated instead of having fun. If you wanted a real golf game, well, this has almost every aspect in life in the game, with minimal golf, so play at your own risk. If you already have seen some gameplay videos and want to try it out just to have some laughs with friends and family, then absolutely, check it out.Its base price is $19.99, but during the launch-week sale right now, you can get it for 30% off, so that's a pretty good deal. is as ridiculous as any screenshots, videos, or reviews you may have read about on this game. It's not a golf game, so don't expect that. But it has every other aspect of life in low-poly representation that offers a really memorable experience.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: is a "golf" game for those of us who hate golf. Really.You don't need to know a single thing about golf to enjoy this. It might even make you a bit sad if you love the real sport, since the game makes an absolute mockery of golf in so, so many ways that its almost criminal.When you start the game, it looks deceptively like the real thing. You quickly realize that this is no ordinary golf... Everything you knew about the sport is thrown out of the window fast, as you progress through the levels. You would think that golf here was about putting a ball in a hole. You would be wrong.It's hilarious how the game keeps subverting your expectations up to the very last bit of content. You don't even really strike a ball for most part. What you do strike instead is something I'm not going to spoil that much since it's part of the appeal to discover that yourself. Suffice to say that it's ridiculous, silly, surprising, and sometimes even a bit evil. So many genres are parodied that it is a joy to discover just what nefarious plans the developers have for each level. My favorite levels involved those resembling SUPERHOT and first-person shooters. Yup, this game even is an FPS. Technically. The sheer silliness of the concept works brilliantly in the games favor.Interestingly, while the game never wastes a chance to mock golf, it is entirely, unashamedly, a game of golf. Literally *everything* you have to access in the game is through you playing golf. Want to get to the next level? Putt your ball in that hole. Want to open a door? Hit that switch with your ball. Of course, this assumes that you are controlling a golf ball to begin with... which you may not. Your golf "ball" may be a cat. It may be a bomb. May be a car. Or even a house. And why not a crab while we're at it? The targets you have to hit are even more bizarre than what you hit them with. It's also jam-packed with more puns than you could ever think about golf. So. Many. Puns.What surprised me the most (aside from the usual "expected" surprises) was the sheer volume of  the game has. Sure, if you rush through the game, you can finish it in less than 7-8 hours. But if you want to see  the game has to offer, including the daily challenges and extra levels added by later updates, it'll take you more than 15 hours to do them all. The main campaign consists of themed segments each with a "boss" (yes, you defeat bosses in this game). When you reach the end and defeat the final boss, it feels like winning in the sense of defeating the sport itself. Which is a grand thing. You can tell the developers had and are still having a lot of fun designing all the unique gimmicks of each level. Ever since being released the game also got some major content updates and even community-made levels.It is quite relaxing and very Zen-like in the sense that you can just play a bit every day to chill. Sure, the harder levels are practically puzzles where you have to figure out the right way to win, but even those aren't that punishing.This game was originally released on Apple Arcade for iOS devices. It was basically the best game I played there when my subscription lasted. Not a big fan of renting games so I was happy to buy it a little bit more permanently on a superior platform. This steam version is the best one just because of the more precise mouse controls and that you won't lose access to the game when your subscription runs out. Would love to see a sequel someday.

Trading the long, meticulous bore of real golf for bite-sized minigame-type levels based on simple hooks and references to past decade indie and AAA greats like . _childDocuments_.review: It’s very simple to make a silly game that does many things and pokes fun at different genres and mechanics. It’s very hard to make it consistently great. Luckily, WHAT THE GOLF? almost never misses.I suppose, you could call this game a physics-based parody game and evoke comparisons with something like Goat Simulator or Amazing Frog, but in reality What the Golf is much more than that. This game doesn’t simply take the basic mechanic of golfing, so often found in countless golf video games (aim and set power of the swing), and apply it to other genres. It does it in a way, where the results are surprisingly fun on their own. Racing games, stealth, FPS, precision platformer, physics-based puzzle game – there are so many unexpected mixes in this title and almost all of them actually work.Every next set of levels is a surprise. And so very often more surprises hide inside the sets. The game isn’t shy about how silly and full of dumb puns it is, it shows what it’s all about at the very beginning, where it teaches you how to play. Put the ball in the hole? Nice, now put the golfer in the hole. Now put the hole on the flag. Now ride a horse while shooting exploding barrels. Yes, you’re still playing the same game, keep playing.It’s also great that the main progress of the game is nicely balanced with never an annoying or dull moment. To complete the game itself, all you have to do is to finish each level once to finish the set and move on to the next one. But each level flag has two additional challenges you can complete, which are presented as harder versions of what you’ve played in the main level, but in reality are often completely different levels and experiences altogether. Completing those gives you additional rewards, but it’s completely optional and if you feel like some of the levels aren’t fun for you, don’t feel like you’re missing out on something.Sadly, some of those optional levels are really unfun and in all those very rare occasions it’s because the game tries to turn its chaotic random gameplay into a challenge. Most of the time, it’s done in a way that’s still entertaining and is sometimes even easier than the original level. But in a few bizarre moments the game requires impossible precision with its own imprecise mechanics. And strangest of all, in all of those cases the level could be turned into a fun experience by just tweaking the “challenge” numbers and adding one or two additional tries, or tweaking the timings a tiny bit.Those moments are also tied to the least fun sets of levels and that’s another point worth mentioning. There are quite a few genuinely amazing mixes of gameplay ideas in the game, yet most of the truly fun ones are easy and quick to complete. Yet, some of the really unfun ones are unreasonably long (the cars segment just kept on going, for example). Perhaps, some of those really fun sets will be revisited in the future as an update or a DLC, since the game now has an extra mini-campaign based around sport, which wasn’t there at the start.Either way, WHAT THE GOLF? is one of the most enjoyable and entertaining games I’ve played in a while. It’s really fun, really funny and consistently surprising. And I would highly recommend checking it out.

_childDocuments_.review: I know a game like this tends to be filled with joke and meme reviews, but I really wanted to try and write a somewhat serious review because honestly, this game is great, and it deserves the praise it gets.I feel like this and Untitled Goose Game fill the same general, I don't know if you'd call it a genre per se, but maybe a  "space"? Games that are casual, full of humour, don't take themselves too seriously, but at the same time, are well made and fun to play.WHAT THE GOLF? is essentially a collection of mini-games centered around a common control scheme and a vague sense of golf. The controls are the same for all the games: you click and drag to aim and adjust "swing" power. What ultimately happens though is dependant on the level itself. I don't want to spoil anything, but all the levels have themes. A lot of them are video game themed and a lot have a more broad theme (like "music"). The levels and challenges are mostly well designed (there's one or two levels which are kind of poor). While some levels can be frustrating, I don't think any of them are so extreme that they're impossible.Overall, I would definitely recommend WHAT THE GOLF? if you're looking for a casual, absurd, and mildly puzzle-y type game. It has some of the most creative levels I've ever seen in a video game and I actually found myself saying "What the f***?" on more than one occasion.

I could see the younger audience having a lot of fun with it and the bizarre levels and ideas it throws around.

_childDocuments_.review: (My playtime on Steam is not indicative of my time with the game. I played it when it released on Epic a year ago)What the Golf is an incredibly silly game. Every level does a great job at taking your expectations, and throwing them out the window. Within the first 5 minutes, you will puck a man, a house, and try to score into a moving hole. Some levels are parodies of famous games like Angry Birds, and others will have you navigate the gravitational pull of a planet.The main campaign is a lot of fun, and most of the times it does a great job and changing up the gimmicks. Every level can be replayed in a few alternative modes. Sometimes they will have you do the same thing with only a specific number of hits allowed, while others will strap a rocket to your ball and tell you to destroy hot dog stands. It can be pretty crazy.You can be sure that the game will have you constantly giggling. And that's where my enjoyment comes from. The game isn't exceptionally hard, but can get tricky at times.The new Steam features are welcome. A silly local multiplayer mode, a pretty intuitive level editor etc. The game has a bunch of nice features to fill it out.There isn't really much more to say.It's golf, but funny.Despite the silly premise, the game is actually very well done. You can tell a lot of love went into every aspect. The music is fun, the aesthetic is charming, and the physics work very well with the ideas.If you like golf (or maybe not?), check out the game!  I think it's a very relaxing and funny game overall!

_childDocuments_.review: A goofy golf game with cute visuals, silly gameplay and plenty of fun content. The game revolves around the concept of golf obviously, though from this it plays from regular kind of golf, putting the ball, various objects or even yourself towards the hole/flag, to playing different parodies of games like mario, donkey kong and flappy bird. Various genres are also found such as platforming and racing, which does further give a mixture of gameplay to this physics element oriented game. Along with the many, many levels to go through, there are also a bunch of different game modes that can be played, from local co op, daily challenges as well as a level editor which is in progress. Create your own as well as play ones that others have made. Having included the feature of steam remote play is also a nice addition, as it then allows the option to play with friends online. The humour in the game is a highlight of the game, with the puns, weird gameplay and the dopey visuals. Several kinds of environments are also played in too, with suitable visual backgrounds and music. Playing in the winter snow or playing in big arenas are quite fun as you explore the campaign and adventure modes. Overall, it is a great and funny game with a lot of charm to it.

Levels are also based on many other games such as Portal, Metal Gear, Mario, Guitar Hero, Flappy Bird & Angry Birds.The insane amount of variety in humour and gameplay is commendable and the game still has more episodes on the way. There are plenty of challenge levels that escalate well towards mastery and completion. Secrets are always well-hidden; never too obscure to access.This game will constantly churn a chuckle out of you. If you are tired of games that make you sweat, try this one that makes you laugh!

_childDocuments_.review: If you don't care about achievements, this game is awesome and you should buy it. But as an achievement enthusiast, this game is a pain in the ass. It's already annoying enough to come back to finish the game again when the new achievements are added, but for those achievements to be unobtainable without ridiculous workarounds? I have to give this game a negative review out of principle.The first time was when they added Thanksgiving levels and achievements for getting them. The problem was that they were only available for a limited time around Thanksgiving time, and I found out about a week after the levels were removed. I had to wait a year to go back and finish the game again. Now they added a new achievement about a secret in the main campaign, but you can't get it if you already finished the campaign! The only way to get it is to replay the game to this point again (which is like 70% through). Yes, I could download a save, but I shouldn't have to."You're really giving the game a negative review over achievements?" I'm giving the game a negative review for not respecting my time on multiple occasions. Either don't add new achievements, or if you do, make sure they work. And if they don't work, let your community know you're fixing them. Why would I ever buy another game from this dev after this precedent they've set? If they actually fix the glitches with the achievements, I'll be happy to change this to a positive review.

_childDocuments_.review: At first looks like an innocent simple golf game, but after playing it for the first few minutes you can easily see what is really happening here. There is a "campaign" mode in a golf game where you play as the ball. You go through different sections with different themes where for each section there are 15+ different levels (and each level has minimum 3 sections). And each of the levels contain a gimmick. In regular golf games, the level design changes from level to level, there are new obstacles etc. But here for example instead of shooting a ball to the hole, you sometimes shoot the "hole" in to a hole that has a shape of "ONE" and when you successfully finish that level, you get a success message saying, drum roll..... Hole in One. I think that this explains so much about this game. Besides the gameplay, soundtrack was fitting and fun. My only non-positive comment is that you can't get one achievement naturally, you need to download an older version and do some stuff. So a fix to that problem can result in a perfect game for its price

_childDocuments_.review: What the Golf? is listed on Wikipedia as a game in the "Sports" genre. On one hand, that can't be further from the truth, but on the other, I can't blame the wiki editors because it's hard to pin down great comparisons for this wholly unique experience. The closest game to this in spirit that I can think of is WarioWare; it doesn't have the timed element of WarioWare but it does have the humor, wackiness, and constant improvisation. Indeed, the greatest strength of the game is all the curveballs it throws (golfs?) at you. You really never know what crazy idea they've cooked up next.But man is it FUN. I can't remember the last game that made me laugh out loud this many times. I was just so happy my entire playthrough; everything is so silly and insane that you can't help but incredulously think: "this is so ridiculous" as it throws you from one absurd minigame to the next. I want to list notable examples of its comedy in my review but I don't want to spoil the magic; a big part of the fun is seeing the zany concepts for yourself.One thing that jumps out the screen is how much fun the developers must have had making this game. So much fun, in fact, that they've released a bunch of (very high quality!) free DLCs post-release. Some of these DLCs are actually the most polished levels in the entire game so make sure to check them out. The amount of content overall is stunning, honestly. Not only is the main playthrough quite lengthy, but there's a Vs. mode (which is pretty fun!), multiple DLCs, a level editor, and daily challenges. An impressive package; they didn't have to do this much and they did.As for difficulty, the game is appropriately easy. There are a handful of tricky stages that you might need to replay a few times, but the vast majority you'll beat on your first or second try. Losing is just as much fun as winning in this one though; sometimes you lose in the funniest ways imaginable so you can't help but laugh either way.Presentation is appropriately hilarious. The art is as dumb and funny as it ought to be; I love it. The music is similarly absurd; with various riffs of the same overarching theme. Great stuff.As for flaws, there aren't many. This game is really good. But, at least for me, 3 of the minigames are broken. Like, they simply don't work. There are hundreds of minigames, so it's not a big deal in the grand scheme of things, but it's kind of a bummer that my completion is stuck at 99.9%. I think you could also complain that the physics and controls aren't quite as sharp as they could be, but the game's relative ease makes that a pretty minor concern. Sometimes the wonky physics make it all that much funnier, in fact. You can cheese your way through a ton of the stages if you understand some of its finer mechanics (Soccer levels are pretty guilty of this; you can just spam shots and zoom across the stage), but again, because the game's focus is on zaniness, all in all this doesn't really make the game any worse. Finding a funny way to break a minigame is part of the charm, if anything.Overall, I'd give this game a high, high recommendation. I also think it'd be a great game to give to someone who is new to or unfamiliar with video games. So much of what is here validates what makes video games as a medium so special to begin with. Tons of fun; please support this game! Love it.

_childDocuments_.review: Only get this game on a 50% or more discount if you want to try it. This game's rating is obviously pushed by a fan base living in another world. What should be a fun little "party" game with references to other games turns out to be a physics and buggy frustration getting worse as you play. Sometimes you get a good laugh at what some levels offer but later on the game chooses difficulty over those fun little moments. Simply getting around the map becomes a struggle as the mechanics behind hitting objects in the game rely on position of the object and your mouse cursor not just your mouse. Control requires time to practice and slows down the game quickly such as gravity effecting your ball in different directions.It only took about 5 hours to see this game could be so much more but is plagued by the mess injected into it. A lot of it is good then the bad parts come in the worst way ruining the experience. The levels with "Par" challenges can be overly frustrating due to RNG and the physics choosing whether your object will roll one way or bounce another. In fact, some levels are just constantly trying to get the good RNG for a set up at finishing the level. All the while the same music and sound effects happen over and over until it's near too much.As of writing this I have 29/50 achievements and will try to finish all of them. There's some good things going on in the game so it's worth looking at some more. However, there's gotta be something better our there for you to spend $20 on if you're looking for a great gaming experience.Edit: Wanted to add one more thing. The reason I even wrote this review is the car levels. The  car controls horribly as it will turn left or right for no reason. When it hits something sure but send it a direction then watch it veer left or right. The devs should know better. Good luck.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really enjoyable not-golf game.   The only connections to golf games this has are 1) some levels do in fact have golf balls and holes and 2) you control your "swing" by pulling away from "X" (where X can be a golf ball, but also literally anything else that's not a golf ball).   More accurately, the game is 90% puzzles and closer resembles a Warioware game.  If you have not figured out from the videos and screen shots, you are rarely actually golfing, and each stage does a pretty good job at subverting your expectations for how the level is supposed to work.  More often than not the simplest solution is usually the correct one, but not always the most obvious one.  The game is pretty forgiving and let's you experiment as much as you want.  The only exception to this is during challenge levels, where you may be limited by time or the number of actions you have per turn.  The game has a pretty lengthy main campaign if you are completing all levels and challenges.  I'm 6hrs in and at 70% completion.  It's a nice casual pick up and play game, and I'd highly recommend for something off the ordinary to play.

_childDocuments_.review: I once read on a reddit post recently "How can we make golf fun again? Add defense!"This game is exactly like that, but in a fun, original, clever way. The controls are easy, just point, click, hold back for how much power you're hitting your 'ball' and repeat until you reach your destination. The concept is clever with a touch of goofiness, you really won't expect what will happen next! The visuals are vibrant and fun, sometimes I will pause and just look around to get a good chuckle, such as the satire'd versions of Mario, Floppy Bird, & Angry Birds.So far I have had no issues with the PC port, this game really POPS out from your monitor. Definitely the best experience I've had playing 'WHAT THE GOLF'.This game is made for you if you're looking for something chill, challenging, and relaxing. A perfect nightcap game where you can visit daily to climb the daily leaderboards.P.s: Please make an album! The music is the icing on the cake!10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't aware golf needed to be fixed but this game has convinced me. If you're expecting just some silly golf jokes, you're in for a little more of a treat. It's a level of humor you'd be familiar with if you like Katamari Damacy. There's no plot but there's a lot of homages to some of your favorite games that'll make you feel pretty old.It'll also make you feel like a little kid. I've somewhat fantasized about throwing the golfer rather than the golf ball so this is a pretty imaginative game that tickles my fancy.Other than offering a good party game aspect, there's also a main game that isn't boring or impossible to play without your buddies. You can sink into that golf zen when you want. Another huge draw is a level builder. I haven't done too well tinkering in it myself, but the temptation to create levels is a huge one. Allowing for a game like this to have our custom content be playable by others is very alluring.Of course there are some drawbacks. I found the soccer- sorry, football levels to be somewhat buggy. Sometimes the hit box on the ball was overly sensitive and exploded with a touch I didn't even see. That's okay, I guess I overestimated things...but that didn't seem so sensitive in other levels. Anything involving those evil little cultists- I mean delightful children enjoying youth sports seems to be cursed somehow. It's probably just me. I probably just suck at that.This also seems to be best played in bite-sized amounts. Sure you could just binge the whole solo part of the game, but there's three parts of a single hole to conquer so you can get a little crown and prove you are worthy of wandering around this spiffy lab...and possibly wrecking the joint with your superior golf powers. Take it easy so you don't go into golf rage. Unless this is your sort of thing. I'm not gonna tell you how to enjoy your not-golf-golf.

I have been playing using both mouse and controller and swapping my input depending on the demands of the level. Overall this is a very clever game with a lot of variety and heart in it. Each different "world" here has a unique theme and often sub-themes, many of which pay tribute to mechanics from other games (SUPERHOT, for example). _childDocuments_.review: The first time I actually have to say "I want to like this game, but can't." It is an interesting concept and a lot of (large) parts of the game are actually very fun. It references a lot of popular games, from multiple time periods, from indie games to Valve or even Nintendo. BUT: Every level-flag has 3 different challenges. And you can tell it was just forced and out of principle in some places. A lot of twisty challenges just aren't fun anymore, they are just some Par number that can only be achieved if every mouse movement is 100% perfected, with perfect timing or some random limitation like "pacifist" in a SUPERHOT-themed level (a shooter game) where there are perfect-aim-enemies standing around everywhere and you just have to "figure it out".But maybe you're fine with just skipping about a third of the content because it is ridiculous, or you think "I like to grind, I can do that". OK. I would normally consider myself one of those people as well. But there's another factor that makes it harder. In those places where the gameplay is extremely difficult, you generally have to make fast and precisely timed movements. But the game's controls almost literally backstab you. If you pull your mouse to far up to go backwards ("down"), it just flips around to forwards again - the literal opposite of what you wanted to achieve.I don't know why this is, but it feels like something someone would have had to think "Hmm, that's a good idea" and intentionally implement. It is not a good idea. It is confusing, almost always unexpected and makes those already extremely hard, forced twist challenges even harder.

_childDocuments_.review: Yet another golf game. But What The Golf? is unlike any golf game you know. It’s golf, and at the same time it’s not. What do I even mean? Read on!Even if you do not know the rules of golf, if you’re a regular gamer then it’s likely you have at one time in your life played a round of virtual golf. Realistic or arcade-y, it doesn’t matter: get the ball into the hole in as few swings as you can, we all know that. Easy.What The Golf? does this as well, but with some fun and surprising twists and takes on the sport. Neither the course, the ball or the club are what they seem. The only thing that’s pretty much consistent throughout the game are the physics. Yes, logically you could say, but also because of the many crazy ideas the game throws at you. Naturally you should be able to get the ball, or whatever in this case, into the hole with precision and therefore it’s of such importance that the physics all work as they should, even if the game doesn’t seem to take itself seriously. Imagine instead of swinging the club you’re actually swinging the person holding the club. It becomes a whole different ballgame (pun intended); it’s completely crazy. Welcome to What The Golf?. And that’s just one idea.The game has you play as a golf ball that can be swung into any direction, with any force and with complete precision by using the mouse. As a golf ball you’ll navigate through some sort of overworld first where you can find and enter many courses. The overworld also has many different areas with different themes and although the game is pretty short it stays fun and fresh all the way through because of these different takes on the sport. Despite the overworld having different kinds of areas you only get to play in these settings with those kinds of zany ideas and physics when you enter the level itself. Some fun examples would be having to play in space or play from a 2D game perspective like Flappy Bird or Super Mario. And there are many, many more ideas just like this, almost all of them fun to play. But many of these areas and levels are locked until you complete a specific amount of levels so you can’t just go to the parts that sound or look more interesting to you.Levels are usually completed in a matter of minutes. But you can try to beat the par score afterwards to unlock another level. Finishing that level will ultimately award you with a crown, letting you know you’ve done everything you can in that specific level. Now, the game isn’t hard per se - with the exception of a few levels - but beating the par scores can sometimes get really frustrating. It’s better to skip it for a little while then and get back to it later. Somehow - for me at least - you can always get it done when you’re not trying so hard and just let it come naturally.There are hundreds of levels and unlike the Apple Arcade version the Steam version comes with an included level editor, providing even more hours of fun. Completing the game should take most us around four hours, but to do everything you can easily double that number, or at least make it to seven hours.And even with the crazy amount of levels, physics and ideas I never ran into any technical problems.Visually the game is quite pretty, with a mix of colorful 2D art as well as 3D models that look okay-ish. The 3D models aren’t very detailed, but they’re clear enough to make them out just fine. Just don’t expect anything amazing on that front. The 2D graphics are a whole lot better, however. The animations and physics are all excellent.There’s no voice acting since there’s no actual story. The sounds effects are all great, though. And the music isn’t brilliant or anything, but is still perfectly fine.It’s ridiculous, it’s frustrating, it’s fun, it’s dumb and it’s insane. The game manages to evoke quite some emotions during your time with it. If you don’t think it’s funny - or fun - the first 30 minutes you play this then it’s probably not for you. If you want something else in your golf game, however, it doesn’t get any better than this. What The Golf? is golf game that *does* reinvent the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a fun singleplayer experience, the game is somewhat enjoyable if you only do the bare minimum number of mostly optional challenge missions. However, it's also extremely short lived for its price and a lot of the gimmicks are going to run really, really dry really, really quick.The floaty, imprecise and inconsistent physics it presents though, make any of the challenge missions (especially the more tedious ones) insanely frustrating, unrewarding and generally unfun. Like trying to enter the grand prix in a unicycle falling apart, you feel cheated because you're losing an uphill battle. These challenge missions can sometimes scream precision or speed in environments where you're provided little to none, making an extremely poorly designed and awful experience.If you still intend to go through with some of these, avoid any of the par missions... They're usually AWFUL and suck all fun out of the game.Though if you do manage to get the optional challenge missions done, what do you get? Some extremely boring figures in a museum that you'll never see again and get no use out of. Terrible rewards to go with terrible challenges.If you're just going in this for the singleplayer then avoid this game outright. Even if it was 75% off, it's not worth it as you're getting an extremely short set of base challenges and if you ever go for the optional ones they're going to be so frustratingly awful that you'll wonder why you ever bought the game.So what about the multiplayer experience?Well, it's actually really great. With some extremely big caveats.First of all there's no online multiplayer. At all. For a game of this price tag, during a global pandemic, that is outright unacceptable. You'll be stuck with Steam Remote Play which, for this game the quality of my remote play sessions (just for this game, generally i've had no issue with remote play before) have been pretty garbage.However the 1v1 multiplayer itself has been really enjoyable and presents a nice amount of variety. Maybe they'll consider using that Apple Arcade money to actually put some online multiplayer in?It's also limited to just the two players. For... Well, i've honestly not found a reason. Why there's no 4 way PvP i'll never know, but it's also a huge negative to the game.So if you're interested in multiplayer, should you pick it up? Yes... At a heavy discount, because it's sure as hell not worth the price tag it's asking for. Maybe wait for a sale, though i'd dip no lower than 60% off on this one unless you're REALLY desperate and none of your friends own it.Overall I can't recommend unless it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: In 1988, the ultimate anti-golf game was released. It was simply titled "Will Harvey's Zany Golf" and the game was so much fun because each hole and each thing you had to do was completely unpredictable. You had to adopt a new strategy for each of the 9 holes and if you made it to the secret 10th hole, Mystery, you knew you had accomplished a great feat. (until I found out you could shoot the mouse's eyes on the 9th hole when they turned red and you would go automatically to the 10th hole). 32 years later, we have a worthy but try-too-hard sequel, in WHAT THE GOLF? I see this as having a lot of potential with a slight caveat: Play more to people who hate golf, like me. "I'm hitting a cat!" "I'm hitting a vase!" "I'm hitting a TV with a VCR!" is cute but it doesn't really strike me as funny after the 10th time I do this. I've heard people say that certain other genres like role-playing games and FPS's will be lampooned and one reason I like this game is that it took on a trope of Super Meat Boy. That is genuinely fun and I like what I'm seeing. That said, I'm thumbing this one up for what it could be, rather than what it is. Simply focus on the parody aspect. You don't need to hit a couch to be funny. You've got this, so make it happen.

_childDocuments_.review: A great game about "golf." And by "golf" I mean whatever was going on in this game. _childDocuments_.review: Golf is inherently a boring, degenerate sport. What the Golf? seeks to remedy those two inherent crippling aspects of the game, and does so in pretty much the best possible way: by embracing absurdity. I have rarely had as much pure fun playing a game as I have with What the Golf?, despite the escalating challenge of the late game curve. You play Ball, a golf ball who's been putted into the Golf Lab, a weird place run by a series of linked AIs, all doing their best to figure out how to make golf, which again is inherently boring, fun. pitches start off more of less normal, but get weirder and weirder as you go along, and though the ball is usually on the screen, it's not always what you're hitting toward the hole; other objects include remote controls, TVs, couches, the golfer himself, cars, bicycles, and at least one type of livestock. It's nonsensical comedy sports gaming done right, very much in the style of Katamari Damacy (which I would be very surprised to learn was not among the inspirations for this game), and very much a breath of fresh air. Give What the Golf? a try and if you don't enjoy yourself, then you clearly should seek medical help as you appear to have been born without a soul.

_childDocuments_.review: Generally a really fun game about "golf" with tons of dumb and crazy ideas spread out in 11 areas. It's filled with many refrences, way too many puns about golf. It's really hard to get bored of this game, since gameplay is almost always different. Sometimes you are a flying explosive barrel trying to knock down the pins and sometimes you are playing with time and outmanoeuvering your enemies in "Super Putt".Not everything can be perfect, since the biggest problem comes from level variations. So each level has 3 variations and those quality can vary. Sometime there is a new gimmick added to a level which completely changes how it's played or it can be a brand new level with new mechanics never to be seen anywhere else in the game. Other times it can be pretty much the same level again or just a restriction of how many moves you can do. Games like this should always be pretty easy, that's because they are about different ideas, experiences, jokes and gimmicks devolopers came up with. Which this game for the most part is, you can beat like 95% of levels withing first attempt and that's great! Unfortunately there is still that 5%, most of them aren't a problem they just require a bit more attempts and some of them are Incredibly frustrating. There are levels which require pretty much pixel perfect shots or INCREDIBLE LUCK, those levels really put you out of this fun experience. For no reason at all there is a big con for achievement hunters, because of the achievement that requires you to beat 18 daily mission's. In a game that you beat in 1-3 sittings you have to play everyday for 18 days. What's even bigger downside are the daily missions themself, because they are really lazy. It's literaly just 5 random levels from main story connected together.Overally it's a good game and it's worth playing, if you can get it for cheap you get 3-7 hours of joy.Just remember to be carefull with level variations and be patient if you want all the achievements!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute joy. Endlessly creative, profoundly funny, and on the main very finely crafted. _childDocuments_.review: Well, I must say...it certainly is Golf-like...but that's where it throws everything else (and the kitchen sink) not just out the window, but at the HOLES!If you're looking for something fun, mindless, and just-challenging-enough, along with just enough extra stuff (like trophies, hidden commentary, cats...CATS!) then this is for you. The physics is good for this type of animated game, you never really count any strokes (unless completing "challenge versions" of holes to get crowns on your way to trophies), and more than anything else, it's just FUN. Oh, and if you have a sense of humour, and have played the odd other video game here-and-there, you will DEFINITELY enjoy the "homage" levels (Portal, anyone?) strewn throughout the game, and the pop-culture nods distributed throughout.Overall, lots of fun, and I recommend it highly!

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game from start to finish. From the very start it's fun and kind of addicting and doesn't lose this momentum it gains at the beginning. I absolutely recommend this game, however I do have a few gripes with it.The positive:- Fun and addicting gameplay from start to finish (as I've said above)- The game doesn't overstay its welcome. The campaign doesn't feel drawn out and keeps innovating throughout itself to keep things interesting- The hub worlds are cool- The themes of most of the sub-areas are cool- The extra episodes are great- Some puzzles can be solved in multiple ways- The humor and references are good- Easy to 100%- Simple but effective art direction- Runs wellThe neutral:- The "boss fights" were fine. They got the job done but they could've been more of a challenge i think- Some challenges were really fun and difficult in a fair way, some were just either a bit ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ or completely luck based and some were just kinda whatever- The daily challenges are okay but I don't know what purpose they serve other than to pad out the game time for achievement hunters- The gimicks can get rather predictible- LGBT flags randomly appear in some maps. Thought this was worth a mention for some people, I don't care about this tbhThe negative:- I don't think the game is worth it at full price. Buy it on sale- There are advertisements for the studios newer game in this game- I don't like date specific achievements, soI wasn't fond of the daily quest and thanksgiving related ones. Thankfully these can be completed any time if you change the date on your computer.- The soundtrack gets very boringI think this is a good game overall and the main campaign deserves a playthrough at least once.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is alright, not really worth the full price. The whole game is divided into tenths of themes, each again divided into tenths of mini levels that each are very similar but with slight difference. The aesthetics are very beautiful, each theme shows off something different that might keep you interested enough, the music is quite decent too, and there are quite a few collectibles/trophies/secrets to explore after main game.The thing is, comedy is subjective. If you are a naive (?) person like a child, you might be entertained throughout the game and had a really good laugh. For me, the best most of these levels can get is slightly more airflow out of my nose. (Eh or maybe I'm just a depressed ass without humor.) I admire the game for its multiple play styles and references, but hardly entertained by the memes/jokes. The game is still worthy for a thumbs up, especially with the occasional free updates that add more content, and there's a level editor under development that has a huge potential.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like dad jokes that get old after about 10 minutes, terrible controls (dpad and start button don't work in menus), cheap ripoffs of other games, annoying sound effects, absolutely nonsensical "lore", and a golf game that has no golf, buy this.Even if you like difficulty, there's no satisfying movement in this game. Controls are muddy, plus they've managed to choose the most dissatisfying amount of friction on every level. Level selection is beyond irritating - to move quickly you want to buffer inputs, but the "confirm" and the "hit ball" button are mapped to the same button, so if you're a bit impatient, you end up entering a random level that you never wanted to.... dozens of times. Some levels are also unplayable on controller and require mouse because the game just doesn't respond to inputs (no it's not the controller, since other precision games seem to handle the inputs just fine).

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 27.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ing minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you

_childDocuments_.review: You might say that this is just a golf game, but it's much more. It's a view on society. We might say we hate golf, but we play a game entirely based on it. The computers in the game can be argued to be one's problems, and destroying them would mean overcoming these problems which is what we all strive for. Even though you might think that with such a simple concept of golf that there would not be any kind of creativity, but you would be mistaken. _childDocuments_.review: This game can't decide what it is. Is it a party game? Not really, the campaign is far more singleplayer oriented. Is it a singleplayer game? Yes, but the quick holes that service a punchline at the end would be more enjoyable if the game were more party oriented.Is this challenging? Not really. The majority of holes are over suuuuuper fast, and the ramped up versions of the holes aren't usually even the same level. Most levels are either too simple to be fun, or too frustrating to make finishing them enjoyable because the physics are annoying. Strangest of all, most holes don't even have a par challenge. You just kind of finish them, read the 'joke' and move on. Even the ramped up versions usually are just "this isn't hard....just really slow or really long".The overworld map is also annoying. Each hole has, usually, one hole, then you're back to putting to the next hole in a map with tons of items strewn about that prevent you from smoothly navigating to the next level. It sounds like a challenge all its own, but it's just another annoyance.This isn't really golf. It's just a large series of toys, only sometimes serving any pressure or challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is right on the cusp of 'recommend', but I'm going with 'no' for one simple reason.But before I explain that, I'll say first that the overall reviews for 'What the Golf' are spot on. The graphics are winsome, sound design is pleasant, and the humor is like a Mel Brooks film: when you pump out a dozen gags per minute, some will land and some will fall flat. No harm there.The developers invest admirable effort--there are no heights too high, no depths too low--in levels that last barely ten seconds and serve no purpose other than to deliver a terrible pun. Truly, you have no idea what will be thrown at you next.As others have pointed out, if you are a completionist or an achievement hound, you are in for a rough ride. While you can skim the levels and finish the game with little trouble, some of the 'par' and 'crown' levels are absolute trash, difficult primarily because they are awful. Another gamer gave wise advice: you'll have the best experience if you try the extended levels once or twice and then walk away from the rubbish ones. That's what I did.And I had a good time. A few laughs, a bit of fun. The game was on sale for under $7, which is about the right price. More than that is too much for the goods on offer.Why the thumbs down then? I discovered this game because the developer's new game, 'What the Car', showed up in my recommendations and looked interesting, so I took at look at their (small) catalog and ended up buying 'What the Golf'. And after playing 'What the Golf' I can say I have no interest in playing other games from this team.The actual gameplay is so thin, as shallow as a birdbath, the variety ultimately superficial, the novelty spent, that it's most fun when, through imitation, it reminds you how fun other games can be, and that you should probably play those games instead. And so you should.There's value in reminding us of great games, but not enough for a recommendation, as it is also a reminder of what this game is not.

_childDocuments_.review: Once again Steam's review system fails to offer the necessary nuance for a great-but-flawed game.What the Golf? is equal parts fun, joyful, surprising, tedious, frustrating, and hateful.For every level where it surprises you with a unique or brain-twisting idea, there is another where the twitchy controls or excessively harsh requirements cause acute anger. Every giggle of surprise is matched by a sigh of weariness.Panic and frustration can be great when competing against other players. Everyone has to deal with the same randomness and silly controls and arbitrary goals. But when playing solo it makes you curse the developer for not tightening up the puzzles a little.It settles into a routine. First part of a stage is quirky, 2nd part oscillates between strict and extremely unfair, and the 3rd part is silly. But over time, the 2nd parts start to taint the other two. So I fully recommend about 82% of this game. But the other infuriating 18% make me think I should never play it.

_childDocuments_.review: A golf game for people that don't like golf games.The premise of this game is rather simple: It is a joke game that is a parody on golf games with unexpected twists.The thing is: it's not fun. The jokes are by far the biggest selling point of the game, but thing is: They just aren't that funny. One type of jokes are the puns that appear when you put the ball/hit the goal of the level. Sometimes good for a small chuckle, but most of the times on the level of 'can I haz cheesburger'/meeminess. The cheesiness is off the charts. And then I'm talking about the original ones that appear in only one or two levels, if the makers couldn't think of something, it's something like 'parfect'. Maybe it's someones cup of tea, but this level of cheesiness just isn't mine.Besides the puns, the other type of jokiness is the unexpectedness of what you're supposed to do. The archetype: You see a guy about to hit the ball, you fill the meter, release to hit and suddenly, the ball stays still but the guy ragdolls towards the flag. Again, this is sometimes good for a chuckle, but such a huge part of the jokiness of this game is build on this one premise, that it soons becomes old. Time and time again the game throws this joke at you: 'Oh you thought this would happen? Ha ha! Another thing would happen.' I'm all for unexpected humor, but here it becomes predictable that something entirely unpredictable happens. And even worse, all the jokes are repeated like 3-6 times each, so maybe it was kinda funny the first time, but the last time, it certainly isn't anymore.The worst thing is, these jokes are such a big part of the game, that each joke is dragged out just a few more times to really make you feel: 'See how funny we are. Right? Right?' Some jokes are good for a chuckle, but the rest of the game (which is 90% if I'm being generous) you're still playing some lame golf game while the game is all over your face desperately trying to be funny. And that is a lot of time that I see myself in the reflection of my screen, just sitting there, going from one lame joke to another.The game is not unlike an annoying 12 year old on your aunts birthday party where you were forced to go to who is showing you all the memes he and his friends thoroughly enjoy. Sure, one or two of these memes aren't all that bad and maybe one is rather funny, but you're still spending your saturday afternoon with an annoying 12 year old while you could be doing all these more enjoyable things, like taking a nap.I have refunded the game. I see two possible audiences for this game: people that really really love incredible and repeated cheesiness and young teenagers (the annoying 12 year olds I talked earlier about). Maybe they would like it, I didn't.

_childDocuments_.review: Are you tired of religious missionaries always knocking on your door? Well, for $20 and about 8 hours of their time, you can fix that! Just make them play this game, and then ask them what merciful god would allow it to have been made. But actually, $20 is lowballing it - you might want to put aside a few extra grand or so for potential therapy costs, anger management courses, and a new computer monitor, not necessarily in that order. So yeah, it might be more cost-effective to just tell the missionaries to go away.Alright, now that that's out of my system, onto the actual review.First, the positive, which I can fit into a single paragraph: Some of the levels are actually pretty innovative and clever. The idea of "Golf, but it's a different game entirely" had a lot of potential, and if you're not trying to 100% the game, it might be a fun way to kill a few hours.But... if you are the type who tends to go for 100% when playing games, you will want to keep reading, that you may save yourself.The developers were very proud of the title they came up with for this game. It's in the store description, it's in the background music, it's in the lyrics of the sing-a-long level, and sometimes when you go out of bounds, you'll hear voices going "WHAAAAAT" like this game invented the word "what" because it's so random xdddzs. I actually had to turn sound effects off for one level because that voice was grating on my nerves so much.Speaking of failing levels, let's talk about that. The hit detection is awful. You'll be playing a hole with a par of the exact same number of shots it took you to clear it the first time, but you're inexplicably unable to make it in that number of shots again, often times because you'll miss the hole by half a pixel on your last shot. Oh, but the exploding barrels that usually send you right out of bounds, THOSE you can hit from two feet away! And when you fail to make the par, it doesn't say "You Failed" or "Failure" or anything like that, it just says "Fail", like a little kid who just discovered memes and watched you miss the trash can while throwing away a paper towel. I get that it's a troll game and it's meant to be annoying, but there's a limit, especially at the asking price of $20.And if the extra objective on a hole isn't a par, it's usually something that will make you wish it was. Like a monkey paw but for every finger that curls, two more sprout in its place. And don't even get me started on the damn sheep. Instead of "What the Golf?", this game should have been called "If I See That ♥♥♥♥ing Sheep One More Time...".So, yeah. It might be worth grabbing on sale for a quick laugh, but I'm very glad I didn't pay full price, because then I'd probably be even more angry.

_childDocuments_.review: My main complaint with the game is that it very often relies on "subverting your expectations" in ways that aren't really fair. Like the hole that moves the minute you hit the golf ball. There's no way for me to know it's going to move before I play so it feels a bit unfair. It's not a huge deal to have this experience once or twice in a game but it feels like half of the levels rely on this sort of gameplay. You're basically expected to just try hitting your ball/object for a bit, see what happens, and then restart the level and actually try. It gets really old really fast.A few other nit-picks: The game relies a LOT of references to other games/sports and often sacrifices fun and engaging gameplay just to make a joke. Your shot power is dependant on the distance between your mouse and the controlled object which sometimes backfires when the controlled object rotates around something besides it's center with a feedback loop that makes it nearly impossible to aim the way you want since move the mouse by a few pixels starts to swing the object widely in a different direction. It also causes problems when the object doesn't stay fixed on the screen like if the object is moving fast the view smoothing often causes you to be unable to fine tune adjust your power because the location of the object on screen is rapidly changing. The ending of the main campaign was really weird in my opinion. I'm not sure if there is a proper "story" that I am missing out on but I definitely felt like the ending was entirely random and not very fun either.
