_childDocuments_.review: This is a review from someone who has just 100% completed the campaign. I've had to give this game a thumbs downs for reasons explained below, however I would honestly recommend this game to anyone. Pro's:1. Creative use of a single mechanic means the game rarely feels like it's becoming stagnant. 2. Levels are short and give instant satisfaction upon completing them, making this game incredibly difficult to put down for too long. 3. Map creator built in along with daily achievements4. The game never dwells on one gimmick for too long, so if you do not enjoy certain maps they tend to be over before you know it. This does however have the downside that really fun gimmicks like SUPER PUTT are also short lived. However, I'd say there is a lot more good than bad and it all evens out into something positive. Cons:1. This is only really only relevant if you're looking to 100% the campaign. The game has a lot of janky mechanics which while often fun, sometimes in the extra levels, the difficulty is ramped up to a point where the cracks in the game really start to show, the horse and crab levels come to mind in particular. There are good reasons why most people do not think "Getting Over It" is a worth while game outside of torture and while I never got stuck for more than 10-20 minuets on a single level I feel I have to make a point that objectively bad movement options + difficulty only lead to frustration, not fun. 2. Many of the extra levels are simply getting par on the exact same course you've just gone through, which feels a bit like padding. Sometimes I would get the Par in my first try only to have to do the exact same thing again. This is the only part of the game where I felt it stagnated. Honestly it's a very fun game and the two cons above never fully interfered with my enjoyment of the game. The reason I have to give this a thumbs down is due to 1 set of levels in the space zone, where you're in an inverted planet that's spinning and you're trying to kick some balls into a goal. This level on purposely attempts to make the players feel physically sick with the spinning screen and judging by the coy message at the end of the third level, the developers know this. I have no other way to interpret this than as malicious intent by the developers. While I was mostly fine with it, many people suffer from motion sickness and trying to induce it on people playing your game is frankly a d*** move and a slap in the face of the people who unwittingly paid money for it.I honestly feel that this level should be taken out and the developers should apologise.

_childDocuments_.review: Initially, I had some fun with this game, mostly because of the subversions to typical golfing, as you may see in several of the videos and pictures surrounding this game. However, its charm fell apart when I accidentally stumbled upon the "Crown" levels. These levels, while "optional" (in the sense you don't actually need to complete them to progress through the "main" part of the adventure mode), were questionable in their ability to be fun.Now, to some extent, due to the optional-ness of the "Crown" levels, they could be seen as a challenge of sorts. The unfortunate reality is that they're either "fun and easy" or "the worst thing ever multiplied by cancer". The fun ones were like the normal holes you had to do normally, and were no big deal. The  ones were nowhere near the same idea as the fun ones. Their design had little direction, and little control, or had constricting mechanics, sometimes combined with all three and then some. If you want to make a "challenge" you don't make it a deplorable or frustrating experience on the player. Specific "Crown" levels that could be rightly called torture:"Par" levels. (Probably makes up 50% of "Crown" levels) Levels where either the object or screen move to exploit the clunky controls, resulting in either unintended and/or frustrating movement. (There is at least one of these, and that already should be grounds for capital punishment)"Fragile" levels ie: If you touch something or anything you start over; barrel or vase levels to a major extent, or "Super Putt" levels to a minor extent. (These are interesting in theory, but the controls make it abhorrable)Some other minor tidbits:Why does a resume button exist on the pause menu if clicking the background does the same thing?Why are some of the floor plans to get  a level a frustrating experience? The space section does not count, and was actually interesting in that regard.Why does the pause menu not have easy access to the options? I have to back all the way out to the main menu to even try to adjust something as simple as  Not to mention the option menu for such things isn't immediately available upon first starting the game.tldr: Game is fun at a glance, but if you want to utterly complete it, you'll hate it before it's even done.

_childDocuments_.review: WHAT THE GOLF? is a mobile app that's been dumped on Steam as if it was a real PC game (it's not)... it's a cash grab from greedy mobile devs.  This mobile app is a different kind of spin on the general slingshot flinging game, Angry Birds.  The slingshot mechanic is at the core of this mobile app, but instead of birds and pigs, it's loosely golf themed as you fling a ball (or club, person, clubhouse etc) towards the goal, with unusual interactions on each puzzle level with various objects like cats, cars etc.The amusement factor of the "Oh, that was unexpected" is certainly "there", but you could get that from watching someone play it on their iPhone on Youtube, so we can disregard that.  And taking that out of the equation you just have an (admittedly well polished) low poly Angry Birds ripoff.  Yes, I know it's golf themed, so how can it be an Angry Birds ripofff?  Because just like Angry Birds, 100% of the game is still putting your finger on your iPhone screen, dragging it back just enough, choosing just the right angle, and letting it go.  Angry Birds is not what I spent almost 5 figures on buying a bleeding edge gaming rig for. From a technical perspective, as a mobile app, this doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.The mobile app features lazy low-polygon "retro" assets, making this look like a barely functional 3D game from the 1990s.  It's unclear why the developers weren't able to arrange high quality, high polygon count contemporary assets for the mobile app (although the requirement for this to run on low end mobile phones is a factor), and also irrelevant... what matters is that this looks bad as a result of their decisions, a compromise PC gamers shouldn't have to put up with.Because this is a mobile app, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the iPhones that the mobile app was designed for.  These are unfortunate handicaps and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was an afterthought for the iPhone developers who are to blame for this.  The mobile app is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for mobile phones forces upon a game.  Once more, mobile devs have made gaming worse for everyone.  I didn't spend thousands on building a gaming rig just so I could pretend it's an iPhone.These technical defects push this mobile app below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.Once more we see greedy mobile devs trying to scam PC gamers. On Steam, this is an eye watering $20 USD (TWENTY BUCKS FOR A MOBILE APP), on app stores, it's about $7 USD. Mobile devs must learn PC gamers are not here to be gouged, and can't be expected to pay MORE THAN TWICE THE PRICE premium for a simple kids mobile app just because it's been lazily dumped on Steam.  This is unacceptable disrespect for PC gamers.  Because this is a mobile app, is priced to insult and gouge PC gamers, and because of the other defects, it's impossible to recommend.Just who do they think we are?

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine a Monty Python-esque absurdist comedy show about golf - that is 'What The Golf?' in a nutshell. You may start out putting a ball into a hole, but you will soon be putting the hole into the ball, a cow into a shed, a bike-rider cross country into a flag, and bombs into bowling pins. Then it gets deeply weird.What The Golf? is filled with bad puns, insane moments and complete absurdity from start to finish. The soundtrack is entirely a cappella, the graphics minimalist, and the game play is not merely off the wall, you will be putting the wall, trying to golf with a detached wall, or a house, or any object you can imagine. The game will take you through references as wide as Katamari Damashi all the way to bowling and The Olympics - frankly, there is almost no end to the inventiveness on display. This game is absolutely worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is specially made for those who like to get all the achievements in games (minor spoilers ahead).What the golf is a mix between a golf game and a sandbox physics game, with a lot of variation between levels: the objectives and objects used for the “club” and for the “ball” are frequently not what you’re expecting. The game has a lot of short levels divided into chapters in the main game but also several different modes/content that you also have to complete.The graphics are very simple and low budget, but the level and randomness and creativity present in the levels ends up making up for it. Despite the poor graphics, the physics engine seems solid, with objects behaving more or less in a realistic way.Completing the levels is rather simple most of the time but the goal of the game is more about being surprised and having a laugh than really completing it. From all the levels and their two different extra challenges, I only found one to be hard to complete in the sports level pack, as it requires dexterity and good timing and is very easy to fail shooting in the right direction in the required time window.It also has a local multiplayer mode where two player compete against on another that is even more fun than playing alone, but has less variety when it comes to levels available.   63 Achievements. Around 15 hours, with a little help or the more obscure achievements. This time needs to be spread around 18 days for you to complete 18 daily challenges. Easy, all the main levels are easy to complete.  Easy, but there is a harder level that will require some practice and several tries, unlike the rest of the game. Some of the hidden achievements will require a guide too. What the golf is a goofy golf/physics game that is fun to play in small doses and will often surprise you with its randomness and creativity. The levels vary a lot and are very different from each other, even more so in the extra level packs.b]Join and follow my group  for more suggestions and reviews of enjoyable indie games to get all the achievements.[/b]

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun and clever casual game that features several laugh out loud moments as you start a challenge for the first time and only by trying it discover what it's all about.  For example, you may have a man with a golf club standing over a ball, and when you draw your mouse back, a power arrow appears behind them to indicate how hard you will swing.  But when you let go of the left mouse button, it might be the ball, the club, the man, or even the power arrow that goes flying (or tumbling) down the course.  Or it might be a couch, an office chair on wheels, a house... it's unpredictable and hilarious and a lot of fun.  The challenges are easy enough to be casual, but sometimes you may have to retry them quite a few times until you're successful, so there's enough of an occasional challenge to keep things interesting.Fun references to Nintendo properties abound, from the Wii Golf-inspired soundtrack to obvious nods to Mario and Donkey Kong in some of the early challenges.  To keep things fresh, there are daily challenges that are every bit as silly and fun as the "campaign" mode.All in all this one gets a solid thumbs up.  It's even stream-worthy because it's almost as much fun to watch as to play.

_childDocuments_.review: the game as a whole is a fresh take on the classic mini-golf genre. almost every level has a unique gimmick, plus 'par' and 'crown' versions of each level with a twist (and pun) of their own. the sheer number of different ideas they came up with and crammed into a single game is nothing short of impressive. there are definitely some flops in there, but for the most part each level is fairly well executed.all told it took me a little over 5 hours to 100% the campaign. beyond that there are several smaller campaigns/level-sets and daily challenges and such. despite the constant new twists, it all started to feel a bit stale by the end of the campaign. me stubbornly insisting on 100%ing each level certainly didn't help, though.the controls are mostly adequate, but I kept finding myself switching between controller and mouse on tougher levels. some felt impossible with one while being almost trivial with the other. some alternative input settings within the options menu would have been much appreciated.in the end it was well worth the $5 I spent on it for 5+ hours of entertainment.

I beat the main game 100% in just over 5 hours, and my second playthrough to mop up achievements that were added and didn't pop retroactively didn't count. Game's also got a couple of strange bugs, such as my save datas corrupting, overwriting each other, and boosting me up to 252% in one of the save files. Highly recommend the game, just go into it knowing it's a wee janky, and if you want to fully complete the game, know achievements won't pop retroactively, and they may keep adding them so you'll need to go back again and again to maintain 100% completion.

_childDocuments_.review: What the golf is a welcome satire that has an very rich pool of references to pull from. The levels are fun, and while some are tad repetitive, they find ways to change the mold almost every time. The only knock I have against the game is that playing with a controller is actually a disadvantage on timed levels. Playing with a touch screen or M&K can get through most of the timed levels easily meanwhile a controller will struggle immensely if not outright be impossible do to the slower "draw" time per shot that is used so controller players have more control over how hard they shoot (This was my experience on the steam deck at least). Aside from that though, the game was a very fun experience and would recommend it highly to anyone that isn't expecting a PGA tour clone.As far as what to expect on the levels, the most simple answer is that you will be surprised almost every time. If something was decently popular in the last ten years, there is probably a reference to it in here, and the game play itself is easy to understand, aside from a few levels where the puzzle itself is to figure out how to score.Calling the levels puzzles is probably the most accurate description. Sometimes its a race, a puzzle, sometimes just a normal golf hole, etc. Saying too much beyond gets into spoiler territory, its worth experiencing for yourself!

_childDocuments_.review: WHAT THE GOLF? Is such a cute indie game from Triband, and is spun as, "The golf game for people who hate golf." It lives up to that title in the most unique way. You play as various objects in short levels, putting yourself to the goal, each level having a unique spin on the oft generic formula of golfing, whether it is sneaking through a box past beacons of light a-la Metal Gear Solid, or launching yourself via toaster to a goalpost. The achievements of this game can be quite aggravating to achieve, especially the Thanksgiving achievement, which can only be accomplished on or near the date in question. Overall this game is a great romp and a fun one to dust off every now and again.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: What if golf but [blank] was the question, and these people went all AdLib on it. There's some classic golf gameplay, spliced in with lots of interesting weird ideas (also the greatest popular game references). I pretty much fully finished everything without rushing in 6 hours-ish, as the game has additional "adventures" when you finish the main story. There's even some hidden lore in there believe it or not.Apparently there's some trouble with 100%ing the game but if that's not a problem for you and all the things above sound good, I'd strongly recommend getting it.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: Collection of physics based minigames. Stretches the definition of "golf" to unrecognizability (in a good way). The joy of the game comes from seeing what kind of crazy new thing is going to happen in the next level - you truly never know what you'll get. Minigames run the gamut from jokes/puns to a few genuine challenges that take many attempts to get right. There are stretches of easy minigames that blend together and can become tedious (though few are completely trivial). Difficulty curve is fairly flat and resets on each world, so even late-game you won't be challenged (but arguably challenge isn't really the point of the game). The definition of a "casual" (in a good way) game. A relaxing experience that asks very little from the player and will feed you a constant stream of surprise and delight.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game if you're overwhelmed and are in need of some silliness to get you through. _childDocuments_.review: - Cute and cartoonish graphics abound. I like how the 2D and 3D portions of the game feel distinct but still cohesive throughout- The music is pretty catchy too. Nothing that'll get stuck in your head for a long time, but it's still pretty good- There's sort of a story there about beating evil computers for some reason. I don't really remember because it had nothing to do with the golfing- And that's probably okay. I don't think like my enjoyment of of a parody golf game was deeply impacted by the lack of a rich narrative- It's a fun, goofy, casual game- It's putatively golf in that the goal of every level involves moving an object to a specific location, but it's a fairly loose interpretation of golf- Each level has 3 variants that typically feature increasing difficulty surrounding a central mechanic or theme. These increases in difficulty may involve things like adding additional obstacles or a par restriction- I don't know if I can think of a reason to replay any levels after completing them. I don't plan on revisiting the game until the Thanksgiving achievement is unlockable again. Sure there's daily levels and stuff, but there's not much point in playing them until it's possible to 100% the game again- This title definitely fulfilled my desire to play a completely unserious casual game. No stakes, only "golf"- Ran very well on the Steam Deck; no issues whatsoever- . Don't expect anything deeper than a silly, casual time. It's a high-quality silly, casual game, though, so it's pretty easy to recommend

_childDocuments_.review: Don't be fooled by the game's lighthearted graphics, it is much deeper than it appears.The game begins with a simple question: "What is golf?" What follows is a profound adventure through many of life's most complex and pressing issues. From gun violence to the housing market, and even virtual reality, "What The Golf?" has something to teach us about every one of life's experiences.You'll laugh, you'll cry, you'll develop complex feelings on one of literature's most common themes "Horse vs. Sheep."I originally waited to get it on sale, but after playing through only the main campaign (and there is so much more content beyond that), I can confidently say it's worth every penny at full price. Go on, buy the game and discover for yourself what a complex and enlightening game golf can truly be.

_childDocuments_.review: WTG (What the Golf) is a great indie game. It doesn't reinvent the wheel but it just throws a lot of cool little ideas at you without much downtime. Its fun and provides a play experience that is relatively rare. If you personally aren't a big fan of golf games this should still be entertaining. It feels more like a WarioWare style mini game bundle rather then a golf game.The game offers a single player campaign that I beat 100 % within about 7 to 8 hours. There are also some extra game modes which I decided not to get into for now as well as community levels. Overall this game is absolutely worth it for its price tag. The game isn't overly hard but if you go for 100 % it can throw some nasty levels at you from time to time. It can be as hard or easy as you want it to be. It can get repetitive, especially if you are going for 100 % but if you do everything at your own pace or come back to it from time to time it should still be a really great experience.One last thing I wanted to note is that my kid loved watching me play the game and try out some of the easier levels. Its a pretty family friendly game in that aspect.Overall What the golf exceeded by expectations and I highly recommend it to almost anyone to buy it even at its full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing this game vaguely reminded me of taking care of someone’s pet cat. It’s cute and clever in some little ways, but it’s often more irritating than you'd expect. Put simply, What The Golf was much more enjoyable when I was b-lining to new stages and basically treating the game as a one-button WarioWare affair. Expecting precise gameplay from the player during the optional tasks doesn't work so well within a funny physics comedy context.The game’s humor is far more energetic than it is competent. Think around the same level as a “hip” diner that uses manufactured dad puns for all their menu’s items’ names. To that end, bootlegging a recognizable game mechanic and writing 'tactless reference' across the screen upon completing the level might be the most video-gamey way to repeat a punchline. (Although in fairness, many of the “inspired” gameplay twists are executed very smoothly.)I think the all-caps implied exclamation of the game’s awkward title nicely summarizes its predictable personality and frantic attempts to get your attention back with a weird new mechanic. Even though nearly all the novelty of wacky golf wears off shortly after the fantastic introduction finishes, What The Golf spits out such a volume of moderately interesting bits that it’s easy to get lost in all the putting. Not a personal favorite, but I’m always eager to jump on the “golf sux” bandwagon.

_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: Very silly game, good for all ages. Though many of the references will work better on older millennials, I could see a young kid being way in to the goofy and novel gags which this game has in spades. It is quite easy to blaze through the levels in a couple of hours, with a few more tacked on if you want to take on the optional harder challenges. Some of these are quite frustrating in their difficulty though, so completionists might find the game to wear out its welcome. However, it is worth playing through everything at least once to see all the creative ways the team has subverted the idea of "golf." It kind of reminds me of a WariorWare game actually, with a very short completion time on each game and a goofy, anarchic sense of humor to compliment each vignette. Lots of puns too, if thats your kind of thing. 7/10: once you've played it there isn't much reason to ever go back, but the creativity on display here is hard to be mad at.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is great but the PAR stage before get to the crown stage is near impossible without luck or 100% accuracy shot and it's very repetitive. I have to do the exact limited shot (PAR mode) before i get to the crown stage to beat the stage 100% on certain maps and it gets boring and old very quick. Just play the normal game mode and don't even bother to get PAR mode and crown mode because you will always need 100% and have to do it over and over again with slight different golf.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: While it looks like a very meme-y game (and on some level it definitely is), this game is beyond amazing. Most games have at least some core identity, but What the Golf? manages to cycle through new ideas over and over so quickly, it's almost disorienting. Highly recommended, especially if you're into fun physics, silly humor, acapella soundtracks and everything that isn't golf. Not recommended if you want to play golf.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really smooth game - a highly interactive hub world and a seriously large amount of inventive content with a small palette. I really enjoyed it and completed the main story to 100% over two sessions, totalling just under 6hrs.There are many extensions to the main campaign that I am sure I will enjoy (there seems to be a smaller, second world to explore!)I must admit I was getting a bit burnt out on the 100% completion grind - every level is effectively 3 levels with some permutation - but if I spaced it out I think I would have enjoyed it more. That's just a testament to how addictive the gameplay is!9/10 for me when considering this was a small team's passion project.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: I almost wouldn't even consider What The Golf? to be a golf game, because it manages to play with and stretch the limits of the simple stroke and power bar mechanics as far they can possibly be taken unlike anything I've seen. It's also both a celebration of and love letter to all different kinds of games, as it's numerous level and mechanic designs draw direct inspiration from so many others.On top of all that, this game absolutely oozes with charm in nearly every aspect from the music/sound design, to the level design, art, and of course, puns! What this game masters, though, is the art of expectation subversion. Many, many times over the rug was pulled out from under me in the most clever and laughable ways, and I audibly cackled every time.Just breezing through the levels, the difficulty is more on the casual side. If you are going for 100%, some of the levels get ridiculously frustrating, mainly any involving ragdoll physics combined with par time or par shots. But the more aggravating ones are far and few between.9/10  I'm begging you, PLEASE play through all the bonus adventure levels!
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: I just saw this game on the store page while on sale I just thought that it would be a great time. I was right, this is a incredible puzzle game that just flips the concept of golf on its head. the gameplay is fun and innovative, the sound track definitely fits with the game they were going for. I'd say its worth the price even not on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: Quality game, and when I say quality I MEAN QUALITY. Every single level is made with complete perfection. It is a mix of all the games you know and love wrapped into one big gift. If you ever wanted to play golf with any other object this game is right up your alley. Endless amount of fun when you include the workshop levels. Even the amount of levels in the game currently is worth it. I am sure you, your family, your future grandchildren, and their grandchildren will love this game with a burning passion. I rate this game a golf/10
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10A silly and funny physics game of "golf".This is really the kind of game that is better experienced without knowing as little of it as possible, but the best description I can give about the game is that it's a game of golf where you're rarely just trying to hit a ball into a small hole, as the object you're hitting (or the goal you're aiming for) are different on each level, along with whatever else is happening in each level as well.The game obviously has a lot of focus on the use of physics: balls will roll, but a person will wobble on the ground, a chair with wheels will slide along the ground, etc. Hitting something will also cause an impact that affect the trajectory of the object you're hitting and/or cause the object you've hit to move, fall over, etc.But the game's chair relies on how silly it is. It never takes itself seriously and it's constantly doing something new, very often catching the player unprepared for what happens next, and it's just a really funny experience all around. And while it's not a specially long game, it still has quite a bit of content with 2 challenges for each level besides the "base" level itself (and challenges can be quite different from what the level is), in addition to extra campaigns, multiplayer, daily challenges and a level editor (though the level editor is currently on early access).I had a blast with the game for the most part, with the exception of a few challenges that were pretty frustrating to complete, but hardly anything that turned me off from the game.Easy recommendation, even at full price.

_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a fun little time waster if you are looking for something fast and casual. It got a few laughs out of me and some of the mechanics were pretty creative and were entertaining to toy around with.It did feel at times that some of the levels got a bit repetitive, where it felt like they existed purely to pad playtime. It was fine since it is hard to expect consistent quality throughout games like these, but I wish developers would stray away from the ideology that you NEED to have a long game in order for the customer to warrant the purchase. I would rather have 5 hours of great gameplay than 5 hours of great gameplay AND 5 hours of filler (not to say that this game didn't have 5 hours of filler because it doesn't, just an example.) Still, the ideas and mechanics it presented made for a few relaxing evenings of fun, so I would give the game big ups for that overall.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: I love how this game is golf... but not really golf. Hahaha...if that makes sense? If you're a lover of indie/variety games, this game has the most random rounds that bring nostalgia. You have the main storyline and you have plenty more to do if you're a completionist. They seem to have added many other courses too, so I guess the $20 may be well worth it. I highly recommend this game if you're a fan of games like Donut County and Untitled Goose Game. It's just pure humor and fun!
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: Entertaining for the first couple of hours but it gets boring pretty quickly. Most of the levels are mid, but some of them are outright unfun to play and feel as if they were never playtested. The music gets tiring pretty quickly too, with some tracks that are as annoying as the levels themselves. Overall would not recommend outside of a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: What the Golf? cares very little about rules of golf and is lot wackier game because of that. You better expect the unexpected as there's no way to know for sure what happens after the first strike. Rules are bent so far that sometimes what you're playing is not really golf.Luckily rules are easy to figure out. Just expect to fail hilariously at first.I won't spoil what kind of things to expect as it's fun to get surprised. Levels are short, getting back to where you failed doesn't take too long. Hardest levels might require quite many retries, but game is fun enough that you still want to try just one more time. I have managed to finish the "story" of the game, so most likely you can too. 100% completion needs bit more effort I suppose.On top of everything else, expansions are free. No need to think if season pass is worth it. It's so fun to play despite of some of the frustrating parts (bowling especially). Give this game a chance and try it out.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: A really nice game.It has the right balance of fun and frustrating. I lost track of time several times, like I thought I played for about 20 minutes when it was actually 2 hours. The parodies of other games are extremely funny and you'll find extremely low amounts of cringe - which is always good. I laughed audibly several times.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: What the Golf is a super fun game with lots and lots of references and super funny jokes. I really love the fact that there's a multiplayer option with multiple maps, characters and many levels. I also like how it has so many different features and how each side campaign is built on a different feature, yet contains elements of the different ones as well. This game plays super well and runs smoothly. It also has super unpredictable jokes and gameplay mechanics that will for sure make you laugh. However, I dislike how the game sometimes updates spontaneously and may remove really weird stuff about certain levels. For example, a level where pots were brown changed to white or sometimes speed changes as well. These are very minor changes and rarely affect your experience. That is my only complaint. In summary, I highly recommend this game on Steam due to its easy controls and smooth gameplay, as well as its hilarious and unexpected jokes and refences.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: Its a cute physics game that resembles what you might get if you fused Warioware with mini golf. The developers have consistently supported the game with new content and events. I tried to 100% it but found a handful of challenges too frustrating, but going through casually and completing each hole once will give you plenty to do with lots of varied game play.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: Aesthetically pleasing to the eye and soul. I would laugh randomly (and sometimes loudly) at this game, the joy was immeasurable. Very satisfying game play, and a world of fun. Would definitely recommend if you're a fan of a little puzzling and some comedy. Not to mention the soundtrack is *chef's kiss* (in my humble opinion).
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: In my years of playing video games I have found that comedy games give off a fun first impression, but soon after I find myself getting bored with them, especially if they are single player. However, What the Golf is not only funny, but creative in almost every level. The levels aren't very long so it makes you want to beat just one more to see what weird stuff they do in the next one. I will say the final boss is very lack luster and a little disappointing for me compared to the wild originality of all the levels that came before it. I can easily recommend this game when it goes on sale. Give it a shot, or maybe a stroke.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: It's honestly impressive how a golf game can be anything but golf.That's what made the game the so enjoyable to me, knowing each level was going to try and throw me off made a fun game of if i can guess the the gimmick.There are loads of level to begin with in the base game as well as little secrets to find and explore, the game loves to reference other things In the form of levels, surroundings or the little phrases you get upon completing a level.If you've beaten the base game maybe to 100% completion there are other games modes and little adventures that can keep you entertained for a little longer.The only complaint is the achievement for playing for 10+ hours now, I have played for this long now and still haven't gotten the achievement. However I do plan on playing a little bit longer thanks to the daily challenges so this problem might fix itself.Thought this might be worth mentioning anyway.If you do end up buying the game, enjoy, its definitely worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a weird game. If you're expecting an experience that is in any way related to golf, you are barking up the wrong tree. It started good, but quickly grew tedious and annoying. By the end, you're relying more on luck than skill. There's an old saying i'll paraphrase; Games are fun when you're wasting your time, not when your time is being wasted. This game starts at one end of this spectrum and almost reaches the other by the time you complete the main campaign. Make of that what you will.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: When I started up What the golf I had no idea what to expect and a few hours after starting that feeling stayed. What the Golf is an absolute gold mine of clever fun, inventive levels and genuine humor. This deceivingly simple golf game had me absolutely hooked on every new area and each new mechanic. From putting around a makeshift Mario level to catapulting your ball across space, What the Golf offers a variety of absurd challenges moment after moment. If you want to play a golf game this may not be the one. if you  just want to have fun then definitely give it a try
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really nice and relaxing game with lots of creative and funny levels. The game takes about 4-6 hours to complete, if you go for all of the achievements, it might take up to 10 hours (since one achievement requires you to spend 10 hours "in game" which actually means that you should spend 10 hours in the campaign mode). The developers also updated the game regularly adding lots of new maps. All in all, the game is worth your time and your money.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: While the game is mostly fun and enjoyable. Occasionally, a level is thrown in there when the broken physics engine makes playing painful, frustrating and soul-crushing. That is not what I'm after. Stay away unless you don't mind repeating some levels until you accidentally finish them, because there are levels that simply has no trick to them but random chance.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played a better golfing game. It's enjoyable, funny, cute, and not too challenging or rage inducing. It gets harder in a manageable slope. It always has something new and exciting. The bosses and story were always fun to fight and follow. The music is topnotch. One of the best parts however, is that you can actually control it without wanting to scream. 10/10 will play again :)
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: This is a unique experience that although not usually difficult, did give me some good laughs here and there and is overall pretty solidly built. I only encountered 1 or 2 non-game breaking bugs, and it's really polished overall. It also has a ton of puns and references, many of which were quite comically done. I bought it on sale for $7 or so and it's definitely worth it at that price. The game isn't incredibly long, but I had fun the whole way through.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: I would wholeheartedly recommend this game *on discount*, based on gameplay, graphics and the odd bug here and there, I wouldn't want to buy this for more than 10 euros. _childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really really fun and inventive. I'd recommend this to anyone because there really is no difficulty to it. This game is just pure fun and you can play with a friend. However, the game did not properly close, so it says I played for 8 hours when I really play for one and a half and went to bed.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun game that is best played in small portions at a time. Multiplayer mode is great too. The game has plenty of references to other game series which bring different playing styles and levels into the game. This keeps the game entertaining and ensures the levels won't feel repetitive.Majority of the levels are easy, but there are a few challenging ones too. Thanks to the level editor there are more challenging levels available.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: It would feel wrong to give a negative review to a game with this much loving effort put into it, but just know that this praise is qualified.I didn't like the inconsistent physics, wonky controls and the immovable camera which combined to give many of the challenges a frustrating and unfulfilling feeling.With that out of the way, the game design is great, constantly introducing new concepts and fleshing them out enough, while not having them overstay their welcome. The humor is hit and miss for me, but i appreciate that they don't linger on a joke for too long. The fast pace in both the game and humor gives it an addicting feel, and despite my frustrations, I did want to see what came next, and I didn't have to wait long to  see that.I 100% the campaign in ~6 hours, and while I had fun, I'm not itching to hop back in. A fun distraction that is worth experiencing at your own pace.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: This is easily one of the most creative and lovely games that I've ever played. The simple graphics are very cute and fit the game very good and the music is funny as hell, with those people singing the name of the game :DThe stages are always doable, well some of them are quite challenging, some even had my hands break sweat, but they are never unfair in any way.WHAT THE GOLF? is the kind of game which let's you feel how much fun the developers had in the making.10/10: Get this game ASAP!
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: Usually i'm not one to give a review 'cause of laziness, but this game was too much of a fun wild ride to pass up not leaving a good-ass review! This game is one of a kind and amazing, wonderful references, and great concepts, While there are a few stinker levels, the good out ways the bad in ore ways than one. To anyone out there looking for a wacky 9-10 hours of fun, and possibly more with the side stuff, and the custom maker that's coming soon. Then this is the game for you!

_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: This game geniunly makes me so happy you do such goofy things like maybe your golfing an actual person or a barrel. Not to mention the really cool references like levels inspired by portal super hot and stuff like that. The only thing is that sometime the challenge levels can get a bit annoying but besides that an amazing game I'd reccomend to anyone casual or serious.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most hilarious game I have ever played. I have never enjoyed and laughed more at a game in my entire life. Every level presents a new challenge that is equally as hilarious such as racing sheep, cooking food and bowling but while you're also playing golf. It's great. Get this game if you need some comic relief in your life and just a fun laid back game.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game for myself and my boyfriend when it was on sale for under 7 €.We've been playing this together for hours and it's SO much fun! ♥ My favorite game of the year so far~This is a Remote Play game so you only need ONE game when playing with someone! (: But it's worth it having an own copy, you never know when you wanna play again or with who!10/10 would recommend! :) There is so much to play, areas have different themes and this is NOT a plain 'n' boring golf game.This has made us laugh and smile and have fun memories together online! :D
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend this to people who actually want to try it, it is really fun and interesting.However trying to 100% complete the game I would not recommend, it is way too inaccurate on some maps and could take 1 try to 100's of tries. I was able to beat the game fully in 7 hours 45 minutes. However it really feels longer because of the amount of resets I had to place upon the tracks.Still a great game I would recommend. If you wish to go through the hell which is 100% GO AHEAD.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: Low-key GOTY.  Not even joking 💯At first glance it looks like zany streamer bait, but there's a ton of creativity, humor, and homages to other video games.While all levels are at least tangentially golf-like, there are several unique worlds to explore... some sports-related (e.g. soccer, racing), some related to a specific game (e.g. Superhot, Portal), and others just themed around a fun concept (e.g. outer space, stealth).Definitely a pleasant surprise, and one that I will come back and play again sometime.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of the negative reviews mention the game being too difficult towards the end and a lack of creativity and copy and paste levels. I just 100% the game in 4.5 hours and i couldn't disagree more. I don't think i was stuck on a level for more than 5 minutes to be honest. maybe i'm just a chad gamer i don't know. Any levels that are somewhat difficult are also completely optional so it difficulty shouldn't be a reason not to buy this.The games broken up into lots of areas. these areas have usually 5-8 levels depending. each level usually has a unique twist, whether small of big. and then each of these levels have 2 more optional sub levels which usually involve having a stroke limit, a time trial or just doing something different with the same idea as the original level.Personally none of the twists or gimmicks overstayed there welcome.I had a smile on my face the entire time and i don't think I've played a game that's made me laugh as much as this one did.I binged this all in one day but even as just something to kill time or if you need a break from competitive and just want to have a quick laugh, for half price i'd say this games a steal. This game was on my wish list way before release and exceeded my expectations, It does exactly what it sets out to do and does it well.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, and very funny. However, some of the levels feel borderline untested and are very frustrating and unfun. Lots of the Superhot levels are just annoying and not fun, and likewise, many of the par levels will require 50-100 attempts as the par has been set for borderline absurd levels of perfect. Expect to spend somewhere in the ballpark of an hour+ for every single one, as you'll need to hit like 8-12 pixel perfect shots in a row. Pretty fun game overall, but I do wish a bit more testing had gone into some of the levels.

_childDocuments_.review: 🟊☆☆ - In the end credits there's text that reads, "Different team members worked on different parts" -- I wouldn't condemn the game for this, it just makes it incredibly uneven. The first two levels had me grinning from ear to ear, but the middle game is kind of broken. There are levels that are the definition of casual fun and amusement, and there are levels that are agonizingly stilted.Fortunately, the levels are structured like this:  -- The Fun are the only ones required, so you can reach the end without much grinding your teeth.But the challenges range from naturally expected to, "ARE YOU KIDDING ME?!" So I gave up on getting 100% almost immediately: I have to worry about my blood pressure. And the real shame of that is that I'm never going to see a lot of the "weird" parts. There's a lot of puzzles that are just straight up luck because of the physics engine. All of these could be fixed by adding just one or two strokes to the par. For the hundredth time, None the less, I had a lot of fun. I think if you can grab this one on sale, it would be a lot of fun for the first time player. It's the kind of game where you'll hand the controller to a friend who "Doesn't play games" just to see their reactions. But, you'll want to take the controller away after the first few levels.

_childDocuments_.review: What the GOLF? is a fantastic and unique game. The gameplay never gets stale as the developers will constantly throw new levels with features that completely change the way you play the game. _childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fun time, especially when taking turns with a friend. The gameplay is always changing. The game is a little short, though. I 100% it in 9 hours, ignoring the achievements that relied on gameplay time and daily challenges. The music is relaxed and the controls just work. The animation is fluid. There were 1 or 2 difficult levels to complete, but overall, the game was not too challenging.The game has a simple story. I guess it was just a commentary on advances in technology. You don't really play a game like this for the story, though. The unique gameplay for each level is the major selling point, and the game does this part well.Give this a try when it goes on sale. You won't be disappointed. There's even user-made levels and a few extra DLC that can extend playtime even more, if you really are enjoying the game.

_childDocuments_.review: A beautifully simple premise: What if everything was golf?It isn't a game about beating impossible odds, or getting stronger, it is like watching a really good comedy sketch anthology. It is a really refreshing take, that I haven't seen many in other games.I highly recommend playing this beautiful game!  Especially with someone who you can take turns playing with.Sometimes the controls with the mouse were a little fiddly, and the first person segment caused a fair bit of motion sickness, but I would happily play those segments again for a game as special as this!

_childDocuments_.review: Many of the game's challenges are either so easy they feel pointless or so punishingly hard that they're not fun to complete. I don't mind playing games that take lots of attempts to finish, but the wonky controls that make the easier levels funny don't translate at all to ultra-precise movement. Still, my overall experience was not entirely negative. There's a lot of heart in this game, and I really did appreciate the variety of challenges offered - including some fun homages to other games. What The Golf isn't a bad way to spend a couple rainy afternoons, but for the price (and from the trailer) I expected more.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this with a warning. What the Golf is funny, has nice physics, and has several gaming references that will hit home for a lot of people. Yet the game is quite empty. The vast majority of What the Golf is using the simple vector and power mechanic to get one object to reach another, filled with a plethora of puns and wacky situations in between. Each level has three versions of varying challenge, but I felt challenged only once briefly throughout the game. There are a few exceptions that were refreshing to see outside of this mechanic such as first person shooting, and odes to angry birds, flappy bird, mario, superhot, portal, and the like, but not enough to make it feel varied often.That being said, if you are in this for the jokes/parodies I would say go for it on sale. Otherwise you might be disappointed. For a better game with one golf mechanic try Golf Story. For a better mini or microgame collection try WarioWare.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a funny indie game I happened to see on Youtube one day and I'm so glad I did because it is a treat! WTG will make you question what golf truly is as you go from simply playing golf to playing many different genres of games in a golf setting.The complete charm of this game is the randomness of it and how when you really think about it, everything is golf. The first few levels will have you simply hitting the ball to the flag. Then it will be hitting a person into a flag, or a house, or a turtle. Next thing you'll be playing golf as a platformer, or a race, or even an FPS (no, I'm not joking). The sheer amount of different ways the creators made for you to play is phenomenal and hilarious at the same time.The main story mode will have you exploring a facility where then are different "zones" and levels for you to play. Each level has 3 sets of challenges for you to complete in order to 100% it. The first one will be a simple, "get to the flag" challenge. The second one usually consists of "get to the flag with X amount of strokes" or a time limit. The third challenge tends to be a weird zany one. This game has the Super Meat Boy feel in which some of these challenges are hard and infuriating, but hey aren't too bad to the point to where you want to give up. I finished the game with 98% as there were only two challenges I couldn't finish, which is pretty impressive for me. On top of that, the creators have 2 more campaigns, and you can even make your own levels to play and share with others. You can even go to the workshop to see what other's have created and try out their levels. I could say my gripes are that some of the levels are super infuriatingly tough, but it's only for if you want to go for the 100% run. I never found too many of the levels to be crazy. There is a hint of RNG since the game is physics based, but that's also what makes it funny too. Just know if you're going for a 100% run, there's gonna be pain...Final verdict? Check this game out if you want a silly golf game to play. I think the creators did a fantastic job of exploring every possible avenue they could with golf and there are so many gaming easter eggs and call outs that will make you smile. I think one of the ending computer terminals said it best, "Maybe life is golf..." Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: Claimed to be made by people who know nothing about golf.FALSE.The devs CLEARLY know EVERYTHING about golf. _childDocuments_.review: An absolutely hilarious series of golf-themed minigames. _childDocuments_.review: WHAT? This is not golf! This is better. This is fun. This is funny!This is a golf game where you are not actually playing any golf. Not really. Instead you are playing a parody of golf in the style of everything not golf. The creativity in this is insane and it never gets boring. This is actually a game where I will likely go back and spend time to achieve the "best" "scores" on each "course", as the variations are as creative as the courses themselves.The final boss (yes, really) is as much a parody of video game tropes as the rest of the game and it's absolutely delightful. Highly, highly recommended for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: This review has been completely changed from my old, sucky, and unhelpful review.You start with the Main Campaign, which starts off relatively simple. You read the Golf Notes, you destroy the computers, you play the levels... but then things start to change.In 03 (I think), a wreckage blocks everything off. The Golf Notes are more cryptic. You eventually get to 01. And you beat it. And then...Meat juice stuff everywhere. You finally get to the hole. And you beat the Frog King.You did it! You beat the game... right?Let's start with Sporty Sports. The only other campaign with Crown Levels so far.It's really fun, but can get tough. Especially the rhythm ones.Then there's It's Snowtime.A nice fun snowy one, with a story of two Turtles trying to get pizza. And you deliver the slices.Lastly, so far is A Hole New World.It has holes, and a Final Boss. Not as crazy as the Frog King though.And then Party Mode, for 2 Players.It hasn't been updated with new levels (yet), but is still fun.This mode was first introduced on Nintendo Switch.Ok, after Campaigns is Challenge Me, and Daily Challenge.Challenge Me is always the same I think... Daily Challenge is where the fun is.You have to try to beat the given levels in as few shots as possible to get in first place.Now, that's practically it for this game on every other platform for now... Except Steam.Because it's Early Access, it's a Steam Exclusive for now. In this mode, you can create your own levels! This hasn't been updated in a while as well, but it's still fun.In earlier versions, you could glitch out the camera as well, and have really odd ball placements. But that's patched now sadly. I have a few levels that feature these glitches, like A Topdown Experience.There's also a demo, so you can see what the game will be like. You get to play through the first chapter of the Main Campaign, and create levels too! The only thing is you can't save them.That concludes my review of WHAT THE GOLF. You can decide whether to get it or not now.And for people who already have the game, keep not golfing!And to the devs, thank for making this masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: Cheery and cheesy, it's a refreshing take on a few classic game mechanics used throughout. Some levels are deceptively difficult where others are fairly easy. If you're looking for a game to not take too seriously and practice your quick-click mouse skills, this might just be the game to pick up.
_childDocuments_.name: WHAT THE GOLF?

_childDocuments_.review: What The Golf is a perfect game to play while having a podcast in the background and relaxing.  Each new section of the map adds a unique mechanic that doesn't wear itself out; platforming, first-person shooting, SUPERHOT timestop, etc. Each level includes 3 objectives, the first is always simply getting the ball (or other random object) to hit the flag pole, the second is usually a par challenge where you complete the level within a certain number of hits, but there are sometimes different challenges instead of par, and the third challenge is something so random and vastly different than the other two that it always keeps you guessing. What the Golf has a wonderful sense of humor and plenty of things to do. My only criticism is that it can sometimes get a little tiring after long play sessions, but that just means this game is best enjoyed in bite-sizes. A delightfully silly and relaxing golf game, and my favourite golf video game ever made.

name: Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos
detailed_description: A dark evil stirs beneath the once peaceful land of Tasos… Deep within the four Great Dungeons, the ancient seals that hold the Titans at bay are gravely weakened and their minions have unleashed terror upon the world. The Goddesses who forged the seals long ago have made a desperate plea for a band of heroes to come forth and save the people from a terrible fate… You are one of the heroes tasked with saving the realm of Tasos from the terrifying Titans. Whether you choose to take on your mission solo, or with up to three friends is your decision to make. Do you have what it takes to save Tasos? Key Features 4-Play Rogue-lite Adventure: Play solo or in co-op with up to 4 players to take down the Titans! Remember that death is not the end; rise again, upgrade your hero and venture out once more, stronger than before! Tackle Procedural Dungeons: With its procedural engine, no two runs are the same! Each room has hand designed layouts, traps, puzzles and enemies all with randomised configurations, making every run feel fresh and different. Classic Weapons: Rogue Heroes features classic top-down swordplay with a large range of tools, spells, and weapons to use as you explore Tasos and tackle the Great Dungeons. Locate classic weapons like a Bow, Boomerang and Grappling Hook to use at your disposal. Rebuild your Town for Upgrades: Spend your hard-earned loot on new buildings for your village of Intori. From Weapons Smiths to fisheries, each can add new ways of adding to your abilities and arm you with the tools to return to the fight. Multiple Classes: Each with their own unique abilities, find which character suits your style of play and take back Tasos!

_childDocuments_.review: Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos is hands down one of the best Co-op roguelites I have ever played. It takes dungeon crawling, Zelda-like gameplay and mixes it with modern roguelite elements like an amazing progression system and awesome combat.And so how the game works is that you create your save, pick your class, and then go into dungeons. There is a story that kind of brings you to the first dungeon and explains the game and from there you go through these elaborate dungeons to try to get to the end, and gain a ton of gems for out of game progression.And the dungeons are easily one of the best parts about this game. Each room can be filled with enemies that pose serious threats. And the combat in this game is really great. It feels super smooth and responsive which is what you want. Sometimes you will accidentally touch an enemy which can hurt you but the better you get the less you tend to do that.There are items you can find in the game like bows, magic wands, grappling hooks, and more. Some of them use your mana and some use their own separate ammo like the bow and arrows. On top of that each dungeon is filled with traps like pressure plates that trigger arrow traps, or bombs falling from the sky, and sometimes good things like giving you a ton of other gems.There are also a ton of secrets you can find and one thing this game does that is really cool is that every room in the dungeon can be cleared. And that's mainly just means like killing all the enemies and discovering any secrets. So you might have to light all the torches in a room which will spawn a chest or press on certain pressure plates in a room.When you’ve cleared a room it changes color on the map and you get a notification which turns every room into an entire objective as you want to make sure you get all the awesome loot and find all the hidden secrets instead of just running as fast as you can from room to room.And like I said earlier the dungeon crawling in the game is so fun especially if you are playing co-op. And all of my experience with the game so far has been with me and one other friend online and local. The dungeons appear like they can be completed perfectly fine solo but they are also designed in a way that subtly promote cooperation between all the players.And if one of you dies you drop your skull and if your friend brings it carefully to a sacrificial altar you can get revived. But that is way easier said than done.Overall the game is very challenging. I have played for several hours and I am not even going to lie, we haven’t even scratched the surface of everything the game has which is a good thing. I can tell there is so much this game has to offer and you could play this game for hundreds of hours. And the main reason why is the progression.The progression in this game is fantastic. So all throughout the dungeons you are collecting tons of gems. And these gems are the main currency for all the out of game progression. So you keep respawning in this little town and you can actually build up the town with your gems. So you create a nurse building to gain health upgrades, a blacksmith to get damage upgrades, a gym to increase stamina, a clothing store thing to unlock new classes you find cloth for, and a ton more buildings. And there is so many things you can focus on progression. There are like 10 different buildings all with several simple but deep perk trees that you can subtly improve your character with. There are also several buildings that are really unique like a fishing dock or a place to brew potions, or a farm to grow crops. The progression system is baked into a simplistic town management idea which makes the progression feel natural and grounded in the world instead of random characters giving you random upgrades like in other roguelites. So overall I don’t have a ton to say about the game mainly because I am still exploring it as we speak. It is so awesome because you can play the co-op local multiplayer or online even with Steam remote play if you have a good enough internet connection. So the fact that I now have a roguelite game I can just pop on when friends come over where we all have our own progression yet we are all on a team makes me so happy. And I touched on it a tiny bit but the way the game handles progression with multiple players is great. So when anyone finds gems in the dungeon everyone gets the same amount for the most part but how you spend your gems is however you want. So my friend could use his versions of the gems he got to upgrade his damage a ton and go to a thief class to do a ton of damage while I could go a mage class and focus on upgrading my magic and getting wands and stuff.And I have to say this is one of the best local multiplayer roguelites I think I have ever played and I am so happy to continue playing it constantly. So I would highly recommend this game if you have some people to play with whether online, local co-op, or steam share, but also I do think this game can be enjoyed a ton as a solo experience. You might be at a slight disadvantage but I think its still doable and enjoyable.And if you love Roguelites as much as me then  for more reviews and videos about them :)

_childDocuments_.review: At best its a fun little game, but it has too many problems for me to recommend.If all you want is a mindless little hack and slash to play with friends then go for it, maybe wait for it to be a little cheaper but keep in mind the following.Classes are pointless, they work mostly the same as each other with a few buffs and debuffs, the specials all work similarly and fill the same roll with only slight mechanical differences.Playing anything other than melee is going to have you underpowered. I played a mage, and maxed everything out i could and had low defense. Because i had to depend on mp, my resources were limited and my damage output was barely a fraction of my melee co-op partner. Playing anything other than melee also means that you are going to have to swap to your main tool and that brings me to the next major point.Inventory management sucks. it starts off okay, but soon your toolbar is so bloated cycling to anything, especially in the heat of combat takes forever. You can pause, navigate to the equip window, select the item, unpause. and honestly that's fine in single player but ruins the flow in multiplayer and can get annoying for who you are playing with as they cant even access there own pause menu while you are in yours. There is a quickwheel but.. is only for emotes, not that it works consistantly in the first place. So soon your inventory will be full of things like a seed bag, and a watering can that are only used in the farming part of the game that honestly can be entirely ignored more so in multiplayer, it feels really tacked on. Exploring feels kinda pointless, as while i have found a few neat things for the most part i seem to end up in dead ends and have no reward. There are power spheres to collect but they nothing/so little as to not be worth it. Several times my progress has been hindered by bugs, in fact in one area i couldn't progress because of a bug, but another bug made me warp right past where i needed to go, so i was lucky but what it amounts to is that there are too many bugs.If the game is going to be updated some of the improvements i would like to see are.Make the classes more distinct, maybe replace the sword with a unique attack that works for the class.Add more spells, give users the ability to target what they want instead of a bat, the other side of the room behind 5 obsticals... that it seems to want to do right now.Make the inventory managable. either add in an item wheel for quick select or just allow users to hide items from the rotation.The game is okay, but I was hoping for more especially when it came to classes.

_childDocuments_.review: I've followed this game for a little while since it seemed to have all of the elements I was looking for in a multiplayer experience, and I can say definitively that it did not disappoint. It isn't without a fair share of bugs and glitches, but based on the competency of the development team (who, to my understanding is just two dudes) within the rest of the game, I cannot imagine that it'd stay that way. It's chock full of stuff to do/see/find/farm/grind. It's almost exactly what you think, too. It's basically LttP but with multiplayer and randomly generated dungeons. Almost every item has a skill tree which really makes it to where you can play however you want. Classes could use a bit more definition regarding what they bring to the table, but that's a pretty minor complaint.The multiplayer, though honestly rife with glitches and desync issues, has been a blast with my friends. We've had a couple of instances where two of us would get kicked if the third party member equipped a new class. We've had occasions where someone spending gems at the health store spent all of their gems regardless of price. But, even though they're frustrating, they're not enough to remove from the overall experience.Exploration is exciting and fun, and you don't just get new items via dungeons. We'd completely forgotten about areas only to go back through and find a super useful main-stay secondary item in a cave that seemed fairly inconspicuous. That, and a bunch of collectible stuff gives you a great incentive to get out there and really get into the world.Combat is pretty basic, but fairly punishing until you figure out how to get into the groove. Dungeons are riddled with all kinds of traps and puzzles that are doing their best to kill you, and a lot of times you'll find yourself fighting enemies while also trying to navigate a floor-spike puzzle. It's fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: I have not played the game for a bit but giving it a bad review feels bad considering the potential of the game. I have to say that I comend the developers for trying to fix the buggs and hopefully the buggs and balancing issues can make the game worth another go. I recommend it but only for a certain type of gamer. If you like like, couch coop, Zelda-like games! However the game has some huge flaws/bugs that can really suck the fun out of the game. I played local coop.The game has about 10 - 12 hours of gameplay, about half the time for us went into re-doing dungeons because we could not get zap cores to make a super rudimentary item called a shovel.Cons1. 17 hours in, all bosses defeated, all other items acquired, all dungeons done several times, endless dungeons done, but still no godforsaken shovel!!!!! We just do not get any zap jellies and the few times we have seen any zap jelly monsters, they drop very few. To give you guys an idea how bad it was...we have played 17 hours and only received 5 zap cores and you need 6 to make a shovel. We got every other item but never a SHOVEL, really?! It is one of the first things you should be able to get. Why? Why would you make zap jelly so extremely difficult to acquire. What is the point in farming if you can not get a shovel? 17 hours in and only 5 zap cores! Why?!- Dungeon rooms are randomly generated but there is very little variety. There really is no real reason for the game in this state to be randomly generated, maybe only the endless one.- Bosses are too easy to just spam to death.- Skills are way too unbalanced. Why use magic or arrows that are super hard to aim, have very limited ammo, cost a fortune to level up and still do very little damage in comparison to the sword and grappling hook. All other items except the sword is useless.- Too many items to cycle through, in the end it is 16 items on one button. Therefore it requires you to pause to find the item you need. - Many of the items work in rather uncreative or weird ways, wand and bow is basically the same weapon but with different ammo. Boomerang is nice but why does it need mana? bombs explode a bit too fast in my opinion. - I wish you could zoom in on the map a bit more, I often had difficulties seeing where I was and where I should go. Spending hours running around in circles. It is weird how the third zoom is only of your town and that it always works.- I wish that there was more incentive to explore and find stuff on the map. Like the crystal ball collectible things you find in chests everywhere, what is the point of them? Why do I care?- Would be nice with more quests. - Also If you do a quest together I wish everyone got the reward instead of only one person. like the bottle and fishing rodPros-- Fun to level up the character in inte beginning before you realize that most upgrades are kind of boring.- Still a nice balance between puzzles and combat- Zelda like

_childDocuments_.review: March 26th review: Still rough around the edges. I was blocked in one spot because I couldn't push a tablet out of the way, but they fixed it in the next update. It IS fun, but it still feels like early access. Regarding quests, follow each step in order, I tried to get to a nearby village after a wayward villager told me I needed a special item, but I had to do a step in the quest chain first that was the opposite way to the town.April 14th review: Yep, the game is buggy all the way to the end, not enough to ruin the enjoyment, but enough to frustrate me. In fact, beyond the end of the game seems to have its bugs too, one of the developers seems to have a typo in one of the two places they are credited towards the start of the credits, and afterwards I gained an unexplained new ability that doesn't work with any consistency. Farming seems a wonky add-on, and the upgrade guy calls out that he can upgrade your watering can, bu there's no spot for it among the upgrades. I would advise skipping it, don't invest in it early and don't rely on it as a source of gold. Gold is really only useful for purchasing health potions within a dungeon and maybe getting some of the treasure boxes if you're absolutely loaded with gold. Yes, I still recommend Rogue Heroes, but it still has the feel of a game that belongs in early access. The most glaring bug for the intrepid swimmer is the climb-out point that launches you clear to the next zone north, pretty much every time without fail. I'd report everything in full detail, but I'd need to get a QA credit and a paid invoice because QA is a job for me, not a hobby. And don't mind not getting the fishing rod completed, there's an enemy that appears in the 3rd boss dungeon that drops the part you probably don't have yet. Likewise, I think it was the same area where you get the parts to finally complete the bow. It looks like there's 4 slots for potion bottles, but I found the first 2 early on and none after for the rest of the game. To optimize gameplay, just pay into sword, health, and stamina upgrades, as well as threads, everything else is pretty much secondary.
