_childDocuments_.review: Kind of underwhelming experience of game. To preface this, I have not played any sort of legend of zelda topdown games but have watched gameplay of them. The exploration part of the game in the over world is really dull and there's hardly any interesting npcs that you meet or puzzles to do other than shoveling for treasures. The puzzles in the dungeon were definitely designed to be played with 2 or more people as it will take forever to complete by yourself, even though you will get the 1 player version of them. Further in the game in dungeon 3 and 4, there were puzzles where it was clearly impossible to complete solo showing lack of polish in this game. To further this issue on the game's polish, I got locked after defeating the second boss because he was underground and not in enrage form before he died. After beating the final boss, the game rewarded me with absolutely nothing useful other than an amusing bug where the NPCs dialogue didnt trigger properly and gave me a weird message after interacting them from behind. It fixed itself after I reentered there area. I've included a picture of the encounter here. The game gives you too many tools that are straight up clogging up the usefuls ones you need, taking forever to swap to the one you need if you dont use the menu. If the dev's actually play tested this fully they should really have made a function to remove useless tools that are not needed currently in the swap bar. The only tools i found useful outside of their interaction for puzzles were the fireball wand because of its fire debuff DOT and range. You get spells like magic missile and frostbolt but those are just garbage spells you find in the overworld. The other tools than the wand just take too much gems to be good when you need to pump a lot of gems into your sword which is your main damage dealer.The other classes are absolutely useless other than the knight with his ridiculous stats, apparently their fixing this in a later patch to make the classes gimmick's actually work. You dont really unlock any cool techniques like I've seen in zelda game like the spin move or having ranged slashes at max health. As a sort of roguelite type game I dont think It's worth buying since the level design feels very weak and uninteresting to play if you do it solo, but there also seems to be a lot of bugs with the coop side which i've never tried.

_childDocuments_.review: Solo = goodMulti = mixedSolo has great UI and can pause the game whenever you want. Multiplayer has limited UI and when one player pauses the entire game pauses until the player unpauses. Camera pans out when players move but is limited to one screen. I'm not used to that restriction of freedom and find it very annoying. When one player moves into a new area the entire party goes along with it, causing all items to disappear when you want to go back and interrupting what that player was doing.The gameplay is fun in itself, the stamina system allows players to time their attacks. Building the town is enjoyable and farming brings wealth, as well are the upgrades for your character. Sharing gems in multiplayer is a new experience for me, I find it enjoyable when bantering with friends.I would like to think that the single screen is just a core part of the game, reminiscent to TLOZ Four Swords and Adventures. Although I would like to argue that in TLOZ Four Swords and Adventures, each player had their own separate cameras when exploring throughout the map, allowing more freedom for each player to do as they please.

_childDocuments_.review: With the time I've spent on this game. I think I'm able to give my point of view on it. I've completed the game (as far as defeating the last boss currently available) and may delve into some optional content.Although I'm currently recommending this game, it is not without its many, many issues. Please don't take my words as a personal swing; that is not my intention. I just want people to know what to expect if purchasing this game.I'll start with the cons first then follow with the pros:1. The desyncs. I didn't have it terribly bad but I've heard some bad scenarios. The worst I got was that I was forced to run the first dungeon three times cause my friend kept glitching through the door right at the end. Other than that, most of our desyncs have been in the overworld; mainly he wasn't able to destroy the bushes so he was stuck while I almost had to go off camera every time just to get to the next zone. I put this at number 1 because it is a major issue, though with word that it's being addressed, it likely won't be a thing soon.2. This is a very dumb-downed look-a-like of Legend of Zelda. Everything feels cheap and not really unique. I'm honestly convinced that the "Procedural" Dungeons actually harmed the game way more than it helped it. Too many rooms, enemies and puzzles are recycled from dungeon to dungeon. I've seen the same areas likely over ten times in my playthrough. Hell, I've faced the same skeleton mobs in all four major dungeons (haven't touched the Endless Abyss yet). My personal recommendation was for the dungeons to be static and be unique to their themes. The Procedural bit could've been an Extra after beating the game or just tied to the Endless Abyss.3. Nothing was a challenge. My buddy and I decided to not pick up any health upgrades at all to even give ourselves some possibility of dying. The second we did though, nothing could even come close to killing us. The most difficult boss, simply because we had nothing at that time, was the first boss.  I feel that the upgrade system kind of made this game too easy since every dungeon seems to be geared towards if you don't have many upgrades at all. Even when we beat the final boss, I literally said to him "That's it?". It just doesn't feel satisfying at all.4. The puzzles were a joke. I don't consider myself smart, but some of these "puzzles" are just simply: Go stand here and there. I'll give some credit, some puzzles had me think for over five seconds, but those were the rooms where the entire thing was a puzzle. Those were the ones where I felt the most rewarded, and that's not a good sign.5. The Overworld was a wasted opportunity. Not only was it even easier than the dungeons, but apart from doing specific quests and exploring for the sake of "hey! what's over here?" It's almost completely pointless. Every time a dungeon was finished, I could not wait to get to the next one and once more, the same bit was recycled again (You can't proceed cause you need X item, go find it in this remote part of the area or talk to a fella, then come back and now you can do it). Honestly the swamp area felt the most unique of the four.6. And the bugs, by jolly, the bugs. Most of it I imagine I can contribute it to the desyncs, but I've encountered issues such as getting stuck randomly on objects, clipping through walls and, without even trying to glitch the system, walking on water. That's not a good sign when one part of the world basically just transforms you into Jesus and the only way to save yourself is to run against a specific cliff.Boy that was a lot of negatives, so why am I even recommending this? Well...Pros:1. Despite all the failings and missed opportunities, I enjoyed the ride with my buddy and may play again with others in the future. It is a good game to play with your friend(s), mainly to hang out and laugh, love and live. It's nothing that's going to make you sweat as failing means you can come back even stronger so you can relax while playing this one.2. For 20$? There's little that you can go wrong here. I've got 9ish hours at the time of this review and that's with me beating the base game and doing I'd imagine most of the optional content.3. Maybe I'm a fool, but I have a soft-spot for these kinds of games and the fact that these fellas even attempted something like this makes me happy. I've always enjoyed games like A Link to the Past and more-so Four Swords Adventure. I guess I could call this one of my guilty pleasures.4. Most of the major issues I've mentioned (such as the desyncs and bugs), are being addressed so I imagine in due time, they will be fixed and the game will be far more stable. Anything about the difficulty or gameplay I've mentioned honestly can be more opinion-based. Your experiences will differ from mine; you may like what I didn't.That is my review! Good luck to the team behind this and I hope for the best of them.-Wigglezz

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing concept for sure hands down.  Pros:  Besides the concept, the "classes" are a cool idea but it really only changes one ability.  They're basically all the same besides that.  Such a missed opportunity here.  Up to 4 player coop is definitely really cool if you have someone who will slug through this boring mess of a game.  Cons:  World design is meh at best and at worst feels lazy.  There doesn't seem to be a reason to explore the map to find useless collectibles that have no affect on your play through.  Magic lacks variety.  2 spells are for environmental manipulation you might never need except one area, and the other 3 spells are exactly the same.  You could be shooting fireballs from start to finish with no reason to use the other spells.  The leveling system.  At first leveling seems fun but you'll run out of meaningful things to spend gems on by the 3rd or 4th dungeon.  The worst part is you might not even feel strong in your class even with your favorite tool or spell maxed out.  The aiming of spells and bows feels pretty random and you will be missing most of your shots because of how the game selectively auto targets.  It's a little frustrating.  Lots and lots of glitches.  I can't tell you how many times I've clipped through a wall or back into the same entrance I just exited.  Also, its silly to walk into a dungeon room and immediately take damage due to enemies flying around the door.  It feels extremely unfinished.  TLDR I'd give it a 5/10.  Not a terrible game by any means just very plain and feels unfinished and boring at times.

_childDocuments_.review: Rogue Heroes is a criminally overlooked indie title, and it's easily one that deserves more active players and continued support. Building off the foundation laid down by Link to the Past decades earlier, this game improves on LttP's gameplay elements in every way. Fluid movement, wide and aimable attacks, useful tools (in both traversal *and* combat), varied class abilities, and more! The overworld is also designed around these elements, with tons of secrets and extra items scattered around its many environmental areas. Add in some engaging randomized dungeons and much-needed skill tree options, and you have an indie game that will satisfy adventure fans for a long time to come. My issues with Rogue Heroes are mostly nitpicks, so I'll list them below rather that include them in the review proper, but I will mention that the music leaned more atmospheric than memorable. It's not bad by any means, but I'd be hard pressed to remember much of anything outside of the main village theme. Regardless, this is a must-play for any roguelite fans or Zelda-style adventure-game enthusiasts, *especially* if you're looking for the perfect co-op game (multiplayer, whether local or online, makes this game 150% better). Now, I think I should provide some constructive criticism on some nitpicks I have with this title. As of early January 2023, I'm still waiting on an update to fix these issues (and I hope the developers will stick with Rogue Heroes long enough to see it perfected):- No controller configuration is a HUGE oversight. The default controller configuration is pretty good, but not having *any* kind of customization for that is a significant fault on the part of the developers.- There is also a lack of Quality of Life features, although not with the core gameplay as much as the unique content. Little annoyances like a severe lack of Power Stone markers on the map (once you've obtained each stone), the map not updating with in-game terrain changes, not being able to move houses or clear unused land in the village. This little things add up over a complete playthrough, and can be more than a bother if you're going for 100% completion.- I was additionally disappointed to find out that completing the Fishing Log, Farming Quest, and mastering the Bestiary only rewards you with an achievement, instead of a useful in-game item or ability.  - The online multiplayer has some glitchy bugs, especially when players don't have the strongest connection possible. I've run into some serious warping and screen-blackout issues on occasion, when playing with friends.- There are a handful of rooms that have some needlessly complicated or time-strict puzzles that should not gatekeep progression in the dungeons. Rooms in Fyrotek Castle and the (optional) fish dungeon come to mind.- This is a reach, but there is (sadly) no risk/reward mechanics for the tavern minigames, which makes them nearly useless (beyond an initial run of each minigame).

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving Rogue Heroes a thumbs up because there is a lot to like about the game, and I want it to succeed. But the game has its flaws, and it still feels like early access.Pros:- Large overworld that's fun to explore and full of secrets.- Engaging gameplay loop of dungeon crawling and upgrading in town.- Strong Legend of Zelda: a Link to the Past vibes with a roguelite and co-op twist.- Online co-op lets you explore with friends.- Active developers who listen to the community, fix bugs, and make the game better.Cons:- Feels like early access.- Some items are almost never used and feel pointless.- Meta progression easily gets out of hand and takes away the challenge.- Bosses, puzzles, and dungeons feel too simple.- The story and the NPCs are completely uninteresting.- Playable character classes all feel the same.- A few soft locks and one crash to desktop over 18 hours of play. (Reported to devs, who seem good about fixing bugs.)The randomized dungeon layouts are a major design choice that I feel is a double-edged sword. On the one hand, it keeps things fresh as you replay a dungeon, which is part of the roguelite experience. On the other hand, it means that every room is self-contained and can be fully understood and solved in isolation. The rooms never work together, for example having to enter a room from different sides to solve it, or activating a switch in one room to affect another. The result is dungeons that feel simple and random rather than interesting.I really want to love this game. There is a lot to like, such as the overworld, where I had many hours of fun exploring. However, I'm hesitant to recommend the game in its current state. If you want to enjoy some of the Link to the Past nostalgia, or go dungeon crawling with friends for a bit, this game is fine. Nothing amazing, but you can get 10-15 hours of enjoyment out of it, which to me is worth the price.If you're looking for outstanding dungeon and puzzle design you'd be better off with an RPG like Cross Code. For outstanding roguelite co-op combat, I'd just go play Children of Morta again, where the bosses are challenging and all the characters feel very different to play.

_childDocuments_.review: What you expect in the best ways possible.---Going in, I was concerned that the game would be too simple and too much of a Zelda clone, and while it does have those hallmarks - looking at you, hookshot - Rogue Heroes has me enamored. The randomized dungeons haven't gotten old after 10+ hours and the natural progression of the game allows you to pursue other things if a particular venture is boring you. That simple Zelda styled feeling of reward when you explore, discover, and ultimately return to areas with new abilities and knowledge to unlock things you missed previously are all here. Is it cheap and easy? Yes. Does it work every time? Yes.Playing solo is plenty of fun, and I never felt like I was missing out on anything by not having party members. That being said, I could totally see this being a go-to couch co-op staple; the party dynamic and dungeon crawling is very reminiscent of Gauntlet, and I'm quite tempted to rope some friends into this one.Some of the life-sim elements are fairly underwhelming, however, and really prevent the game from having that ultimate RPG feel. Farming is dirt simple (get it?), home decorating is tacked on, and the inability to customize your character's appearance beyond skin tone, hair colour, and cloak colour is quite disappointing - especially for a game with 4 potential friends' personalities running around on the screen at once.The story is completely forgettable, but to the game's credit, it is not at all the focus here, and thankfully, any mention of the story is kept short, so you and your potential party members won't be stuck reading paragraphs when you'd rather be dungeon delving. Just the standard fare of something evil corrupting the land, and you, the chosen hero(es) are here to restore things to pleasantry; it's all just an excuse to set up the exploration-action-adventure you came here for.Far and away my favourite idea the game has is to force the players to lose their gems in order to enter a dungeon. At first, you will recoil at the notion of losing your loot, but this subtle requirement creates a fantastic pace to the game and its progression by incentivising you to spend your wealth on upgrades or buildings rather than horde it. After all, the few gems you'll be unable to spend that get lost to enter a dungeon are made back after clearing a room or two, so once again, the players are encouraged to attempt long, deep runs through the dungeons in order to maximize the profits.Overall, this is a well thought-out game that captures that nostalgic feeling of when games were complete on release, polished, co-op, and simple fun. Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos doesn't break the mold much on the classic old-school Nintendo RPG format, but it doesn't really have to when the formula is as tried and true as this. Despite this game deriving obvious inspiration from the pixel Zelda games, I - a not so huge Zelda fan - find myself struggling not to spend all of my free time playing this game. I'm just over 10 hours in and there feels to be around 20+ more hours of content, making the price here an easy purchase.If you dare to give it a try, I doubt you'll regret it.

I understand there's a bug on it right now.*2- The different classes skill does not add any difference to the gameplay. Basically defend with shield and attack with sword. Each class should have had more depth and additional unique skills.*3- Village customization is very boring, for example: you can't turn around objects in your house. And you can only put few houses that will get blocked, even though you have spaces available.*4- There are no "final items", like a better shield, sword, etc.*5- Some classes need to be balanced, for example: the Reaper and Knight are OP, while Ranger and Witch are very weak.

_childDocuments_.review: A rare treasure. If you loved classic Zelda, this is the game you've been waiting for. It starts slow. You have to earn a few tools and character upgrades, which are not intuitive at first, but once you realize that you're supposed to die on the dungeons, it gets super fun with great exploration and tons of hidden treasures. Lots of clever new tools, character roles/job aren't that interesting, but there's a mix of procedural dungeons and fully designed dungeons so you can self-pace but you can also enjoy some cute puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: Do not mind the 79% positive reviews! This is an excellent game that I definitely recommend.It looks like the negative reviews are mostly:1) Early access reviews when the game wasn't finished, calling it... unfinished..I just fully completed the game and can guarantee there's tons of content here, I got almost 20 hours out of it, and I get bored quickly.2) Multiplayer complaints (old?), I can't say anything about that because I only played single player, and I don't think I've seen a single bug or issue.I had a lot of fun playing this, it's very Zelda'ish with obvious references and flat out ripoffs of it, but who cares, it's a different enough game and it works.Lots of classes, but they all work pretty much the same unfortunately, this could have turned this game into a masterpiece if you could actually get more variety, as it stands you usually just use the same old sword throughout the game, with really poorly designed secondary weapons that run out quickly and don't even do much damage.I really liked the overworld and exploring the little nooks and crannies and going to every last inch of the large map. It's too bad you don't really get rewarded much, most rewards come from grinding the dungeons (that are random and fun).I do recommend you give this a try, you will definitely see the value in this within the refund window.

_childDocuments_.review: Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos offers an addictive roguelike experience with procedurally generated worlds and the option for cooperative play with up to four players. Overall, the game deserves 4 out of 5 stars.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a functional game, very fun gameplay but horribly broken.You will encounter bugs all the time, specially as you progress further. Bugs which either softlock you or force you to reopen the game and lose progress.Here's some of the many bugs me and my co-op partner met during our 12h play session:* Game has constant issues with desync during co-op. * Game will constantly and randomly warp you to lategame areas where you have no way of leaving, forcing you to restart the game to respawn at the bed. Easily reproduceable if either player plays Thief, for some reason the game breaks whenever you play that fast class.* Druid is also unplayable on co-op. If co-op player attacks while Druid is shapeshifted, the Druid also attacks. It WILL get you killed because Squirrel has a lunge attack, and you will be forcefully lunged at enemies.* Game aiming with magic is broken, focusing targets far away and ignoring targets in front of you. No way to turn off.* Game will desync badly if both of you try building something at the same time.* Game dungeon puzzles can softlock you, forcing you to restart the game not to complete the puzzle, but to leave the puzzle room itself.* Aside from the 4 main dungeons, all optional dungeons have no revives for co-op. Hilarious because the Reaper class is a co-op focused class and one of its upgrades is to make it easier to be revived.* Game will desync badly for no reason randomly.Now if that wasn't annoying enough, you WILL get warped to random locations every 30 minutes when leaving a cave. It just happens more consistently with fast moving classes but happens regardless. Exploring a new area but found a cave? Pray it doesn't lead to you being thrown on a glitchy ocean forcing you to restart your game and having to backtrack all the way from where you left off.The game is just barely playable on co-op. I'm sure it works better on single player but co-op is just broken in all sorts of ways. Really cute graphics and really fun to play, but the sheer amount of bugs you will encounter make it too frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun to play with friends.  It's a great LoZ experience with multiplayer aspects that makes the game challenging and fun.  The puzzles aren't too difficult but remain fun to solve with the presence of enemies to interrupt your problem solving attempts.  The world is interesting and fun to explore with a plethora of upgrades for your gear.  A nice QoL that make the game even better is that it tracks quest progress for everyone in the session.  You don't have to worry about repeating missions in your own game (unless a bug pops up which I'll get into shortly).  All in all, a fun game worth the price tag.  Though the game is great, there are a few things that still need to be ironed out and hopefully soon.See, despite all of that good stuff, it's still pretty rough around the edges with its multiplayer.  My friends and I have encountered a couple funny glitches and that's all fine and dandy, but the worst offender of a bug is when the game decides not to auto save quest rewards.  If you suddenly have connection issues or have to drop from the game without being able to select "save and quit", chances are high you will lose out on the reward and it's happened a couple of times to date.  Now, the game keeps track of quest progress for ALL members regardless of who's hosting as I mentioned.  However, in my case I lost out of a quest reward and cannot repeat the quest (because Comcast is awful).  It was a pretty significant item but won't mention it in this review.  If you can get over the hurdle of risking your quest rewards online, I wholeheartedly recommend this game to fans of LoZ, and those that want to get into this kind of game.  Take care and have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos is a charming yet imbalanced action-adventure game that leans heavily on its dungeon-crawling roots. The difficulty curve feels uneven, starting out challenging but becoming easier as you accumulate damage upgrades, which eventually mitigate many of the threats you'll face. This progression can make the game feel less rewarding as you become overpowered fairly quickly.The game offers five main dungeons, each with a boss at the end, alongside an endless dungeon for players seeking additional content. The overworld includes puzzles and quests that unlock new character classes. However, I found this to be the weakest part of the experience, as I was more interested in jumping straight into dungeon action with friends than solving overworld puzzles.That said, Rogue Heroes truly shines when played with friends. The cooperative multiplayer elevates the experience, and if you enjoy teaming up to tackle dungeons, it's easy to recommend. For solo players, there’s still value if you find the core gameplay in the demo enjoyable, but the experience is undoubtedly more engaging with a group.All in all, Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos has some pacing issues but offers a fun co-op experience, especially for fans of dungeon-crawling action.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Fun game that can be played with friends both online and locally but DO NOT spend more than a couple bucks on it, either wait for a 90% discount here on Steam (that's how I got it and I suspect it gets discounted regularly) or get a key from the usual key dealers. It's unfinished, full of bugs (some inconvenient, some gamebreaking) and apparently abandoned, if the price gets lowered to around 5€ this could've possibly been a positive review but I just cannot reccomend it for 20€I won't point out all the negatives simply beacause there's so many that I just can't remember all of them, just know that there's issues with pacing and clunkiness and a lot of bugs, this is essentially an early access title with some unfinished content that never got added/fixed for some reason, you can still get 100% completion thoughI never tried out co-op personally, only single player, so my thoughts are mostly relevant for single playerSome of the most problematic bugs and design issues:-The randomly generated dungeons can bug out and softlock you, either by spawning chests that block your movement or by failing to generate doors to other rooms (happened to me in te 4th one), both prevent you from progressing and force you to abandon the run (=the same as dying and respawning) from the main menu-Sometimes you can't get out of the water, the docks simply don't work and you are forced to wait for your stamina to run out and die. Water exploration is unclear and sketchy even when it works, could use some more guidance-Ranged combat is very unpolished and underdeveloped, you can't aim precisely and the projectiles fly all over the place, it's just not worth the effort and basically never needed, it's not unusable by any means but unless you want to challenge yourself on purpose there's no reason to ever use your bow or wand for anything other than dealing minor chip damage when your enemy is too far for your sword to reach-Some things are just never explained or explained incorrectly and cannot be figured out unless you stumble upon them randomly or specifically look for guides online, I'm mostly referring to I liked most of the secondary, non-randomly-generated dungeons and some of the bosses, especially the , the general mechanics and gameplay loop are fun which makes sense considering it's essentially the exact same as the classic 2D Zelda games

Bosses are not interesting in the slightest. Game is a walk in a park at normal difficulty.- Swamp navigation is terrible.- Underwhelming classes and especially magic. Melee is just so much better its not worth it to even invest in magic.- Music is generic and very repetetive.Overall this game doesnt have much, its pretty shallow and its average at best but thanks to co op it shines just a bit brighter.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun experience that does a good job of capturing some of that Zelda magic, specifically Link to the Past. Has an enjoyable roguelite approach to dungeons that, while gimmicky, does keep it a bit fresh on each visit. Minor gripes would include annoying instances of taking contact damage and largely uninteresting upgrades to gear that boil down to stuff like "+1 damage" and "+1% armor".However, I wouldn't grab this for full price. I got it for 5 bucks on a sale and that's really the most I'm willing to pay almost purely because of the terrible netcode. If you're playing solo or local coop, great! It's a super fun game that'll keep your attention. Playing online however is a nightmare. I don't have the best internet in the world but it's definitely not as bad as this game makes it out to be. Heavy delay, teleporting, cave exits teleporting you to , and copious amounts of desync are to be expected.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start of by saying i WANT to leave a Thumbs up.. But i can't.Let's start with the good! The graphics are cute, and animations are beautiful. This gives HUGE Legeng Of Zelda: Link To The Past vibes and it's so much fun to play. It has some pretty simple mechanics, but the retro style of gameplay actually keeps the game Semi challenging.. mainly because i'm an idiot and i like to run into enemies..The village building aspect of it is cute, and i like the idea of being able to build up your town with new NPC's who can sell different items to help you along your adventure. I like the idea that you only gain gems and currency AFTER you have been killed in a dungeon.. but.. this leads to a problem which i will talk about later in the review.Multiplayer is so much fun! Playing this game with friends adds some more depth to the game, as it increases the dungeons difficulty, depending on how many people are playing. Also, throwing things at eachother is so much fun to do. Because the other player automatically catches the item, it's fun to catch them off guard! though that being said.. Throwing a bomb when it is 1 second away from blowing up and your friend catching it is... well.. it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ funny. When a player dies they have the ability to float around as a ghost and posses items that they can throw at enemies once they get close enough, and the resurrection aspect of the game is great, giving players a chance to redeem themselves! But.. don't play catch with their skulls too much.. if you throw their skull.. it can break.. leaving your friend a moaning, floaty ghost forever! It's pretty fun.. But.. this is only when the Multiplayer works..Now.. the bad..The De-Sync and Disconnection issues in this game are absolutely unforgivable. And i know, everyone and their dog is complaining about this. It wouldn't be SO bad.. if you didn't lose EVERYTHING when you get disconnected. If you've just collected a total of 1400+ gems in a dungeon and you get disconnected.. yeah, say goodbye to those gems. THAT'S the most infuriating part of it.  This is also the reason i haven't had a chance to defeat any bosses. I don't want to play this game on my own, i want to play it with friends.. But i can't even reach the boss without being disconnected.Opening your inventory forces the game to pause for everyone else.. Why? I literally do not understand this design choice. it's annoying, and it makes you feel like you can't check your inventory, or the bestiary to read about enemies without the risk of annoying whoever you are playing with. It just seems very counter productive. This also goes hand in hand with talking to NPC's. As this too, will stop the game for everyone else, and actually is one of the main causes of the game Soft Locking, causing everyone to need to restart and rejoin he game. And this NPC is right at the very beginning of the game.. Not something that should be present in an early access game.. let alone a full release.As soon as these connection issues and De-Sync issues are fixed, this game will be perfect and i'll absolutely change my review.i would like to say.. The fact this game was made by two people is astounding. I do not want to discredit the work they have done so far, it's amazing.. But these issues NEED to be addressed, as i'm sure they will be in future. It's just a shame i bought this game on day 1 release, and can't play it as much as i really want to.Also, There is a discord for this game. Don't dare go in there and tell them of the problem.. because they will defend the fact they got given a broken game, and then they will kick you :) Pretty dope place.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't in good faith recommend this to anyone. TLDR: Game is very short on content and the content that is there is bland and uninspired.There's very little content in pretty much all aspects of the game. Few enemies and most of them act exactly the same, just run at you or shoot and run away from you. Very little variety in rooms, puzzles and traps to the point you'll see over 80% of them on your very first run. This wouldn't be a problem except the dungeons are randomly generated every time you enter similar to a rogue-lite.The classes all play very similarly with slight stat variations, the upgrades are all beyond boring flat or % stat increases, no new abilities or gimmicks.Village building is a joke, building placement doesn't matter, what you build doesn't matter as you're not allowed to have any duplicates, you don't need to worry about the residents and most of them don't even do anything.The bosses are all very simple and boring, you're not forced to use any of your tools in those fights.Multiplayer adds very little, you'd have just as much fun if not more fun just playing Uno or battleships with your friends.

I had one floor that I needed a key and there was none to be found (likely enemy drop that fell to narnia). I had another floor where I seemed to get put underneath the layer of where the objects I needed to interact with were. I enjoyed my time with it...the bugs were only one part of the game that wasn't necessary for enjoyment.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this one and look forward to them finishing the remaining areas because I'd like to play more of this game.I purchased this on sale along with the Bomber DLC class. It plays similar to "The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past" but the right stick attacks in the pressed direction allowing you to attack while you retreat. I used the Bomber DLC class, which can also kick bombs like "Bomberman," until I replaced it with Knight and later, my favorite, Reaper. Total playtime at time writing is just over 26 hours, local co-op with my son plays well but the screen expands too slowly leaving you vulnerable at screen edge and we had issues with quest progress since we didn't start from scratch together. Even when his character was P1 and we were using his town my progress threw some events off.The game appears to have been made by a two person dev team and right now feels like it was finished just enough to release, but it lacks polish. There are four areas that are locked out on the map, or are only partially accessible, that appear to be for future expansions, but the Kezar Fist could just be replaced by the hammer and Mastery of the Book of Beasts doesn't feel rewarding yet, for example.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sure that this type of game appeals to certain people, but I am not one of them. The gameplay grew repetitive and rote fairly quickly, and was a mix between very easy and very difficult rooms. The city management and roguelike aspects could have been fun, but they were fairly simplistic filler between different dungeon runs.  The exploration was nothing to write home about, and the different characters had little discernible differences between them. There are many other games in the genre that you should go to before this one.

_childDocuments_.review: If I have to be honest... the game is honestly not the best. I've been playing this with some friends of mine, and even though all 3 of us have fairly good PC's, one of them seems to keep getting stuck between doors repeatedly to the point where he had to basically stop playing with us. As for me and the one friend, we have managed to get soft-locked in ridiculous situations a total of 2 times....The idea of the dungeons is cool and all, but some of the weapons end up being completely worthless to use, to the point the only real weapons to kind of use is Sword, Grappling Hook, and Wand. The music isn't anything to write about. at least the boss music is decent, and the Froggy music is probably the best theme in the entire game.... and It's only played in that one Mud part of the game. Oh... and I almost forgot... there is no cross platforming so if you have a friend on a PS4- PS5, or a Nintendo Switch, or any console related game, you will not be able to play with them. Overall, this game is absolutely meh... I'd give it a 5/10 or a solid C grade. the soft-locks are just random and kind of funny at the same time... but I'd say... play it with friends. It's more fun if everyone enjoys the random stuff the game has to offer you.

_childDocuments_.review: I played solo. Its a nice little distraction for a few hours, a mix of classic zelda with the breath of the wild stamina system. Though it is short if your decent at the game. Theres 4 dungeons to conquer and then a final boss fight. Currently there are 3 dungeons that have not been released yet but those are optional. Its not a really deep game and if your looking for a crafting system look elsewhere. Its possible to grind one of the additional dungeons for fast gems and max all stats making the game much eaiser. I did not have the DLC bomber class to rate that however all classes have their own stats and one special move which is usually a charge/dash of some sort. Id advise against the bomber class even though I didnt play it on the grounds of classes being almost the same and the base ranger class being more then enough to beat the game.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Multiplayer Zelda (but the puzzles are easy) and it's pretty buggy. Also make sure to play with friendsI got this at a deep discount, and I probably would not have paid full price if I knew nothing. After playing through juuust about the whole game and DLC, I'd recommend it for the full price (and I'm a cheapskate!). For the skeptics, let's start with the cons.Cons:It's buggy. Very. There will be game breaking stuff, there will be funny ones, take that as you will. It only detracted from my playing experience once or twice, and the rest of the time it was funny to me and my friends.Difficulty is wack, and so is balance. Certainly feels as though some classes (and upgrades) are a better choice, but it doesn't detract from the gameplay imo. This game is at its most fun when you're playing it casually, and trolling your friends a little. I think we played it on the difficulty above base, and it felt like a healthy challenge.UI is also a lil wack, but with some practice it's managable. Devs if you're reading this, I think this is a pretty simple fix. Maybe be a little more transparent about what the book does as well? I wasn't able to find an answer online on the benefit of "mastering". Generally, be more transparent with stats and all the like, gamers will love it. I understand it's difficult to toe the line of simplistic design and informative HUDS, but maybe add some hover effects :^)Pros:THE IDEA ITSELF! Multiplayer roguelike zelda is an excellent gimmick. Super fun with a full lobby of friends, but I can't imagine it'd be too much fun singleplayer.An adorable art style I love. We had a player who had no mic, and the expressiveness of the characters and emotes were enough to send us reeling. The soundtrack is pretty good, but nothing to write home about. Sound effect design, and the overall satisfying bits of the game really give the aesthetic its pop and make you feel rewarded when you pick up good stuff.Some humorous moments, albeit rarely from the story. There are some goofy mechanics you'll love if you aren't taking the game *too* seriously. Frog flute is the pinnacle of game design. You will laugh playing this game if you have the right people. Troll your friends a little, this game makes it soooooo easy.A playpace that knows exactly how to toe the line of exploration and progression. It's easy enough you'll probably always know what to do next, but the game rewards you a lot for exploring the massive open world, and it's an awesome break from when you're tired of the main quest. It's also got achievements and collectibles that will entertain the collectathon fan/achievement hunter for hours more than the game itself. You don't have to be grindy, but you certainly can be.Overall, a great game! PLAY WITH FRIENDS!

_childDocuments_.review: Game just does not work for multiplayer.  Constant lagging, glitchy camera, etc.  At one point one of my friends got slightly desynced from the rest of us and had us constantly warping 3 rooms back where he was unable to move any longer.  Honestly, even if it weren't for this the game is kinda meh.  Classes have practically no point to them beyond slight stat changes and a movement ability that I honestly never found a use for. _childDocuments_.review: I heavily recommend this game. It truly feels like a 2D Zelda game in the style of A Link to the Past. Combat feels great, progression feels great, and the world has a lot of personality. Music, graphics, and level design work together well to create the world. The Rogue-lite elements are used really well without making things too repetitive. A sort-of Stardew Valley style town-building system keeps you motivated to collect more and more gems.

_childDocuments_.review: Can I give it two thumbs up? One does not seem like enough! I wish I payed full price for this game I enjoyed it that much. I guess I will settle for buying copies for friends on sale to spread the love for this game! It has so many things I enjoy in a game such as class changes, town building, an expansive, fun world to explore, fishing and farming, though optional as well as having a Zelda like approach to dungeons and landscapes but still feeling like it's own world. It is funny though I did not learn about certain aspects of the classes till near end of the game. I didn't know the reaper can roll and be immune to spikes and such using his movement ability. Man all the spike deaths I could have been spared! Or that the witch could fly over them with her broom or the pirate can do so as well with his bird. So many class aspects I overlooked but now that I have completed the main part of the game it makes me want to go in and do the other dungeons I didn't finish with different classes. See how far I can get with a class out of my comfort zone. You can die in a dopey way at times but  it has this great Hades feel to where even if you die you progress because you keep gems to buy abilities and such. I started this game playing in an online group and that was fun as well. It can make the dungeon's more challenging puzzle wise but also can make you laugh as you lug your dead friends head back to a raise point. This is a a game I know I am going to keep going back to over time. Heck I am fighting the urge to get back into it now because I am writing this! I have beaten it and yet still have much left to do if I want to and I actually want to! There is one thing I will say that I did kind of blunder. After you get to a point where you can go into an endless dungeon. I thought I had to go through at least 25 levels to get to the last boss because I saw the achievement for 25 levels... well I got to 26 and no go... thankfully I looked it up after and found out all I had to do was walk into the statue at the start of the endless abyss and you get to the last boss... derrrp. On the 26th floor after getting the achievement I just went to the entrance of that floor walked into the statue and beat that sob! Well least I got an achievement! ^_^ I will definitely try to get 100 for this game as an excuse to get back in and to display it on my profile page.   Do not miss out on this adventure. Also expansions have come out for it already with additonal classes and areas so its an ever expanding world. You can't lose with this one in my opinion. Do yourself a favor and give Rogue Heroes a try! P.S if you are going to fish I looked up a video on it and doing it with a keyboard even though I played the game with a controller was a lot easier for anyone getting frustrated with it. Good luck and enjoy the game!  Remember when games were fun? This is one of those kinda games! ^_~

_childDocuments_.review: A heavily inspired Zelda-like, rpg-lite, puzzle-dungeon, rogue-lite adventure with its own unique twists that successfully make it stand on its own. It is charming, fun, very addictive and surprisingly casual for the amount of deaths you will encounter. Some slight grinding is required, but does not feel like work! Dying forces you to spend your collected gems and gems equal upgrades! Upgrades mean less dying, therefore the fun lasts longer! Lots to do and explore and the forced world progress keeps things locked away just out of reach to make the gameplay loop bring you back for more to make yourself more powerful at every step of the way.Quite lengthy if you really allow yourself to explore every nook and cranny of this delightful journey.

Which I don't mind, but don't expect this to be a farming simulator to max your entire profile out. I lost interest once the story/dungeons were over.

_childDocuments_.review: All bugs aside, it's a fun game. _childDocuments_.review: We bought this game 5 days after it was released and played it for 4 hours. Here are some things to note, and things that I came to understand:1. Game is very Buggy in online co-op, our friend walked up an invisible bridge as an example, another one of our friends took out 2 wooden archer towers on his side, whilst they were up for the 3 of us and we were unable to take them down.2. The Class system is unbalanced, the only differences between the classes are stats and 1 ability which is either a dash or a jump, classes do not get unique weapons.3. Menu system sucks on online co-op as well as going to a different area or tile.4. When increasing mana or health, the bar would go outside of the bar's area for a bit then reset5. Sometimes we were randomly soft locked, luckily one of our friends went to the door and reset the area for usThe great things about this game however far outweigh the problems listed above.1. Great Experience and is fun with friends2. Interesting system with upgrades and town progression3. Cute visuals as well as very detailed areas4. Randomized dungeons and different layouts make it daring and exciting5. Only for 20$ not too shabbyFor all new players who are interested in looking and playing through this game, although it may be buggy now i'm sure the developers are looking towards fixing and bettering the game. I found this to be a great game with friends as listed above with a lot of stupid and funny moments, obviously this would be great solo as well as it feels similar to Zelda: Link to the Past but with its own twists and progression.

_childDocuments_.review: Great coop Zelda game! I have mainly played it in Local Mode, over Parsec (so, remote local). I did not see any bugs.The game does summon a lot of the Zelda A Link to the Past nostalgia. Now, I would not play it alone though. The game does lack a compelling story, and I don't believe the game is meant to be played single player. Also, the dungeons are semi-generated every time you enter them. So if you die in a dungeon, and go back to that same dungeon, it will, in fact, not be the exact same dungeon. In that regard, it is not like ALTTP for example.If you are looking for a game in ALTTP style, but with more story, then I can suggest Blossom Tales.But for a coop Zelda, I don't know a better game! It can truly be fun. And with at least 2 players, this works well! The way the game works, this is a little bit of a "you will have to die a few times before you can start to win" kind of game. But it's all in good fun. In fact, when you die, you can get stronger (you can to train more skills). While there are not a lot of puzzles that truly require a ton of cooperation, completing dungeons in coop can be a lot of fun. And playing as a group starts to make more sense once you can change classes.

_childDocuments_.review: Only grab right now if you're willing to deal with potential bugs.Fun, but buggy, especially for multiplayer. Even in singleplayer there ARE a couple puzzles you won't be able to solve yourself, if RNG isn't kind to you. Luckily the devs have been both rolling out patches and been in contact with the players, including problem-shooting.Plays like older Zelda titles with rogue-like upgrade skill/tool trees via a minor town building system. The game has a pleasant visual and audio aesthetic, so it shouldn't be taxing on wired-potato systems. There's several different classes that have slight to major play differences, but sword & board is the prevalent mechanic. There's a very, very minor 'farming' system, but it lacks impact on actual gameplay. Story is run-of-the-mill adventure game in a monster-troubled world that the 'hero'(PC) must save. Along with updates and patches, the devs have mentioned rolling out new content, including the cut/inaccessible areas and quests; along with possible DLCs and classes down the road.

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely pixel art roguelite game that's super fun. Your goal is to defeat four temples before confronting the final boss. Dungeon rooms are randomly generated, containing a mix of puzzles and monsters so you never know what you're going to get. As you progress, you collect gems to enhance your stats, abilities and, class. Gems are also used to upgrade your town and unlock new buildings. When you die, spend your gems in order to get further on the next run. My only slight criticism is that the fishing and farming sides came too late on to be of any real use, but overall a gem of a game. Great fun in co-op.

_childDocuments_.review: When i first played this game i was confused why it was only at 78% positive reviews on steam. After a little more time with the game i understand but will still cautiously recommend this game. The first 6-8 hours of gameplay in this game are really good. It is retro zelda gameplay, with a big overworld and dungeons to explore. After a death (or victory) in the dungeon you get to upgrade your town and yourself. There are new characters and tools to be acquired and a bunch of sidequests and secrets to hunt down if you are tired of the dungeon gameplay. And it even has multiplayer, what is there not to like?Well the game is extremly shallow at times and feels kinda unfinished.After a while the dungeons get really boring because neither the puzzles nor the fights provide a real challenge.The differences between the character classes are too small for them to be considered character classes.A lot of items and tools are used only a couple times, almost as if the developers forgot about them.Gardening and fishing really serves no purpose as there is no depth to it.There are plenty of softlocks and out-of-bounds glitches all over the game.One achievement is currently impossible to complete and is glitched since May of last year.Neither keyboard and mouse nor playing with a controller feels very good, selecting items is a hassle as there are just too many and the quick-select options are mediocre at best.Despite all that the game is just fun to play, you go into a dungeon and mindlessly kill a bunch of enemies and solve some puzzles for an hour and it is a good time.At the time of this review the developers are working on a big patch that should solve a lot of the issues the game currently has. _childDocuments_.review: Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos is a rogue-lite adventure that's starting as a fun game and ends quite dead. It's buggy, lacks variations in classes, has unfinished content and is overall unrewarding. Halfway through you come to a point where you either ditch the game or finish it because you feel like you've wasted your time already so just might do it till the end. neat, classic old-style adventure type. Just exactly what you would expect from the genre. it's there but it's also easily forgotten after. Nothing special, but at least it's not annoying. not deep or unique, common for the genre. lacks content (as-in, there are dull placeholders for cut out or unreleased content). There are places you can't go and things you can't do yet the game is not an Early Access title (experimental patch 1.7 at the time of this review). I don't think there was a way to change the difficulty unless I totally missed it. As it was, it's unbalanced from my point of view. Starting curve was good: you lose, you grind for upgrades, you progress. About 40% into the game you become too powerful with some classes making you nearly invincible while you keep on getting tons of resources for further upgrades. Turns the second half of the game into a walk in a park. bad. Lots of tools without easy navigation through them. You have to scroll through them without any way to rearrange them or access specific tools quicker. And those are not optional, you have to use them often. You can't get some information about the game elements through UI (spell descriptions after you've acquired them, for example). there are collectibles hidden around the game world which are utterly useless except for achievement hunters. There are game breaking bugs that make you abandon your run and start dungeon over. buggy game that's either unfinished (you can finish the story line but there are lots of placeholders still lying around) or implies that there would be paid content for what's missing (if it's free, see p1.). Fun level drops too fast, can't recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Get ready for nostalgic joy!!! Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos is retro top-down SNES "Zelda: A Link To The Past" goodness with MORE features and an art style that's perfect for the experience.This game does an incredible job of paying homage to "Link To The Past" while adding things you never even realized you wanted to increase re-playablity. With rogue-like elements such as procedural dungeon generation and buff collection exclusive to individual runs, no 2 dungeon dives are quite the same.Spend the gems you earn in each dungeon to customize your character's strengths via health, magic, weapon, and tool upgrades and more. Collect special items to unlock different classes with special abilities (not all features of this are active just yet), and brew potions using items from monsters you've slain.If re-playable dungeons and character customization weren't enough, there's also building of your town, upgrading and decorating your house, gardening and selling crops, fishing (a must for a Zelda style game), and more. There are also additional "mini-dungeons" and of course plenty of puzzles and quests.This game can also be a multiplayer experience, which I have not tried yet.  It is my understanding that there are currently some issues with multi-player that are being ironed out as quickly as possible; we've already had the first patch just 2 days post launch and the next is on the way.Free updates are planned per comments from the developers. Currently there are at least 2 areas of the map that are not even explorable yet, so there's still more to discover and conquer in the future! It's my hope that the developers will continue to expand this game and satisfy my never-ending itch for top-down pixel art adventures. There are so many great things they have implemented that I can't wait to see expanded upon.Lastly, I'd like to give a shout-out to their team for their caring and responsiveness - I experienced something I thought might have been a bug and their support team responded to me with a solution in just a couple of hours ON launch day. It turned out to be a very easy fix through file repair in Steam, so it wasn't even something that was their fault, but they helped me solve it anyway and in record time!TLDR: Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos is a blast to play (and re-play) and has more content on the way! Rejoice in the satisfaction of a "never-ending" retro style action puzzle adventure! Praise the developers for having the insight (that Nintendo apparently doesn't) to give us the throwback we wanted and needed with expanded features and the genius addition of rogue-like elements!As for the negative reviews regarding multiplayer issues, etc. - keep in mind that this is an indie game that just launched, and the developers are incredibly responsive and resolving issues as quickly as they can. They are also implementing player suggestions for improvement coming as soon as the next patch/update. I genuinely think we can count on them to continue to refine and make this game as great as possible!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is about 90% of the way to being a classic. The gameplay is good, the exploration is rewarding, the items work as you'd expect and the enemy variety is perfectly acceptable. I love the upgrade system - there's a lot to like about the game.However, I have a caveats to that.Firstly is the art. Yes, it's a style - but let's be honest here, if 16 bit tiles looked *better* in the 80s than your current gen ones, you should probably consider altering the game's art style. It is, by design, more or less flat - but that does not IMPROVE the game. It doesn't make it worse, but it doesn't add anything - and a charming aesthetic could certainly accomplish that. You already have all the tilesets and such programmed. Why not change the style to something that will be more eye catching, and less forgettable?Secondly, characters. IE, there are *none*. You don't care about anyone in this game, because they have no character, and have no actual distinct appearance. Yes, yes I know they *technically* are different - but they're not different enough to matter. Writing alone couldn't fix this, either, because the characters just don't look distinctive enough to really lodge in your brain. It's bad enough that it even makes it a little tricky to remember who upgrades what, early on. If the characters were more distinct, had more unique behaviors - maybe had more dialog - and had a look that stuck with you, it would go SO FAR towards improving the game.Third - item favorites. You need an item favorites system. There are WAY too many items if you want to scroll through them all without opening your menu. Implement a favorites system where you favorite four things from your inventory, and have those be all that scrolls with L and R. Do that, and the gameplay would be *rock* solid.Overall I still highly recommend this game, but actually caring about the characters in it would work wonders. I want to care about those four goddesses, and see a unique appeal in each of them that's WORTH fighting to release!

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks beautiful at a glance, and if I'm not paying much attention to detail, it's truly a game that grabs my attention(I love the art style). But, there is such wonky things that will ultimately keep me from coming back.Going up stairs... Why is it so slow... And the character going up the stairs left and right just looks horrible lol, he walks off the edge of the stairs, yet the character is centered, just move him up a few pixels so he's not centered on the stair sprite.F is the default to continue speech... Really? Couldn't use something easier? space, click, or even E would be better.What's with the GLASS equipment. They couldn't just explain that you lose equipment on death? They had to go all out saying it was glass and shatters on death? A glass bomb bag lol....There is frame drops through the game that get worse as you play (memory leaks?), I'm assuming it's because of AI in far off distance performing actions when player isn't around, because the longer you run around, the more bogged down it gets. I have a fairly good PC set up too. Played for a little over and hour, and it seems like 15ish minutes is where the laggy framerates start to happen, dying solves the problem, but dying to frame rate drops is pretty sad, and annoying. Roguelite games are where you want to die due to skill, not lag.There is also confusing things, some NPC's will ALWAYS have an exclamation mark above their heads, even without a current quest, making me think I'm missing something, when in fact, there is nothing.There is no way to skip NPC dialogue. When they yammer on and on and on, and the only way to continue their dialogue is F, which is also the key to TALK with them again, if you press it one too many times, you get back in their loop, which is soooooooo annoying.Throwing the boomerang uses mana, but using a bow doesn't? Using the lantern to light stuff costs mana, but if you equip the lantern and bump into the stuff, it will light without mana cost...The first class which I admittedly didn't play for long (I switched to the thief/hunter class pretty early on...) has a WIND-UP to his class skill, the other characters don't (I played the mage for a bit too). There's a good 1-2 second delay before he dashes, and it would be useful if you go in a straight line a lot, but you don't. The dungeon was twisty and turny, and once you get the teleport locations, there is no use for the first classes skill, which is kind of dumb since a lot of players will probably stick with that instead of rushing to another class like I did.Losing all your "gems"(rupees) upon entering the dungeon is pretty ridiculous seeing as most of the time you'll only lose 10-100ish (adds up over time) and really only annoys me that you're making me re-earn them when I shouldn't lose them in the first place.Also, gems, AND coins? Why would you make it complicated like that, ditch one for the other, and WHY are coins permanent when gems aren't? They're only ever used in the dungeon, if ANYTHING, it should be the other way around for losing them on death. Because they're used in the dungeon... And most of the time, they're used to open chests that give gems, why the hell is that even a thing?Honestly, this game just put me off within the first hour of playing it due to clunky gameplay, and bad game design(purposefully?)It looks beautiful, and for the most part, there is some really cool things in the game. I may try it again in a few years to see if anything has changed, but I really doubt that anything will.Thanks for reading my experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally play RPGs like this, but When I used Parsec on a friend's PC, this was a must-buy for me. I LOVE this game. Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos is a dungeon-crawling multiplayer roguelite, heavily inspired by the top-down Legend of Zelda titles. You can play this game either by yourself, or with up to 4 players locally, or online with Co-op.Gameplay: 7.5/10Game feels extremely solid in terms of movement, combat, and usage of powerups and abilities. Super well done. I've never played Four Swords like other people have, but I HAVE played LTTP, and this feels 1-1 with it. You have access to 1 class as you start, and you can unlock 7 other classes (1 of which is DLC, but it's worth it.) in-game. Each class gives you special abilities based on who you pick, like Hero having a charge attack, Bomber having bomb jumps, Pirates having a parrot companion to save you from traps, Witches with potion specialisation, etc. Not only do you possess different abilities, but to balance out the game better, each class has different stats, which let you mix and match upgrades of your choosing, like weapons, tools, potions, stamina, health, etc. The upgrade selection is very proficient and nicely done. Being able to increase your attack speed, reach, strength and stamina consumption goes a long way. The game lets you build villages and other buildings that service different purposes, Like gym's for Stamina, Hospitals for Health, Shops for resources, etc.My other issue is how the camera gives you fairly little room for being able to see with multiple players on screen, whether it's co-op local or online. If each player got their own screen, that'd be amazing. But for now, it's kind of a big problem to me. Although I understand why they went this route.Graphics: 8/10Very cutesy and adorable, centred around small pixel art-based characters, environments, objects and enemies. Fairly simple yet effective.Story: 5/10 The game tries to centre the game around you, the main character, and your journey to saving Tasos. Nothing insane to write here in terms of plot. Just your standard "save the world" cliche. No princesses to save, so that's a refresher.Online: 7/10 This game has a pretty good functional online system. It plays great, and it's fun with friends. My only reason I'm giving it a 7 our of 10 is cause this game does have a couple of issues with regards to online. First one, which does hinder progress sometimes, forcing you to abandon your run: Getting teleported in random places. So me and my group of friends decided to grab the Kezar Glove to go to the barn and grab a watering can. As soon as we got into the dungeon, we teleported to the top left of the map (The Arctic) and got lost. This does hinder progress as we walked all the way up to the Kezar caves, for our friend who didn't have the glove yet. This has also happened on a couple of different occasions, but for the most part, the glitch has been consistent. Even though the online is there, take it lightly with a pinch of salt when I say: This is the only Early Access part of the game that should've put the game back into it's EA state. There may be a couple of bugs that hinder the experience a fair amount, but i feel like in due time, this will be addressed. Hopefully.Final Score: 7.5/10Rogue Heroes: Ruins of Tasos is a Zelda-inspired roguelike with multiplayer elements and a healthy amount of content for its price-tag. From its solid gameplay to fairly decent multiplayer, i'd encourage you to buy this on sale, simply from the bugs I've encountered online. Otherwise, if you look past it, Rogue Heroes is a really fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: First things first, I completed everything in 30 hours and I rate the game 6/10. Fun little game to play with friends. Game is most definitely balanced around multiplayer rather than single player. What I mean by this is that bosses and such have the same amount of health and do the same amount of damage, regardless if you're solo or with 4 players.I have some gripes that just really ruined a few things for me, but doesn't drag down the entire game. So here they are:1) Honestly too many 'Equipment' things to have on the scroll wheel, and the 'Favorite' wheel is clunky.2) Don't bother with Thief as a class - You can't crit bosses, and you take 1.5x damage for no benefit.3) Don't bother with Mage as a class - The wand picks a random monster to attack, not caring about aim.4) Don't bother with Ranger as a class - The bow requires more upgrades to matter, and the sword is always better, with less cost.5) Don't bother with Witch as a class - The entire shtick is potion effectiveness, so unless you're going with a group of 4 and want them to be fairly worthless except giving you stronger potions, I'd avoid it.6) Circling back to points 1 and 3, specifically the Equipment:a) The Boomerang is entirely worthless. The grappling hook does everything it does, at no cost, and is your traversal tool.b) The Lamp is just annoying, because you always set yourself on fire too. Just instead make it have an interaction function on items that require it, like the wood blockades.c) The Book of Beasts is just a monster tracker, and if you farm enough with it, tells you what they drop...but you already know that when you kill them.d) The Temporal Scope is an item you'll never use outside of leaving the dungeon you get it, and to 100% the game. It has a total use of 4 times, and that's me counting a room in the Endless dungeon generation.e) Bombs are fun, but entirely 100% optional unless you want to 100% complete the game.f) Hammer and Kezar Fist should've just been the same item to reduce clutter. Same as lamp, just make it have an interaction instead of an actual thing to scroll through.I know the list is long, but they were serious downers for me. There are some other little nitpicks here and there, but the above list is what I truly wish would've been fixed before the game lost update support. I still recommend the game for a group of friends, especially if its on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. However, I bought this game purely for its multiplayer function, since well, I could just play The Legend of Zelda if I wanted a singleplayer game like this.Now onto the actual bug:At multiple locations where you exit a room back into the overworld (ex. exiting a cave), you get teleported to the corner of the map. This softlocks you since you end up either walking on the water out of bounds or in the snow biome, where you don't have the necessary gear to get out of said biome because you weren't supposed to be there yet. I'm astonished this has not been fixed since it is completely game breaking and you will encounter this bug even if you are just going through the main story line - i.e. no exploring hidden paths, no checking the cracks etc.I waited over a year to buy it hoping they would fix this bug. Alas, I am greatly disappointed.

Having a bunch of essential collectibles scattered through the world is a bit tedious given the world’s maze-like layout. Even if not for the achievement, these collectibles are necessary for improving your class perks. Having progression locked behind collectibles in a game like this is rather questionable. At the very least they should have given the player Something that did tire me out throughout this game were the block puzzles and everything revolving around them. They were fine at first, but given the repetitive nature of this game, you will encounter the same handful of block-related obstacles over and over again. There was one instance where I would actually softlock myself because I couldn’t reset nor move the block from the exit, trapping myself in a small space.Despite the fun factor, I would suggest getting this game with a discount. _childDocuments_.review: I read the other reviews and was, like, okay, how bad could it be? And yeah, it’s about a little south of “meh” right now. This is not a “finished” game and it should be considered early access. The story (or lack there of), the dungeon levels, the RPG progression, and the “Stardew Valley”-esque elements are so half-baked and forced together it is almost confusion. When playing, you want the game to make sense but it doesn’t. Why does it take so long to get the fishing rod and what is the point of that and farming? Why use any other tool when the grappling hook is clearly the best item in the game? (uses no stamina and no ammo) What is the point of building all these generic homes for the generic townspeople in the bland land of Blands-ville?Wait, so there are only like ~20 different enemies the game? For a $20 game? I’ve gotten better value from a free mobile game. Why the artificial difficulty spikes? The most punishing thing in the game is when you bump into an enemy or trap. The dungeons are waaaay more difficult than the “bosses”. I literally stood still and grappling hooked my way through most boss fights. And and and yeah more. All that said, I played through solo and I know that’s not the intended experience. I wanted to test the game out before recommending my girlfriend and I play it and I just ended up hate-finishing while hoping it would get better and it did not. I feel like I saved my girlfriend from this experience. My verdict: I’ll come back when there is an update or when it’s more polished but I’ll burn all of Tasos to the ground if it’s paid DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: Having fun with it thus far.  I get Link to the Past x Binding of Isaac vibes with some persistent upgrade elements thrown in.  Definitely on the lighter side of roguelite.  Good enemy variety, interesting exploration and abilities/items that enable further exploration.  If it's too hard you can grind a bit and buff up your dude with some upgrades.  Nice art direction and dungeons have puzzles that are on par with Link to the Past - nothing too difficult but might take a minute to figure out.  Nice little town building mechanic with light farming elements as well.  Couple different currency types that are used for different things.Some notes for improvement:- Limited variation between classes- Exploration - once the waypoints are unlocked it would be much more convenient to be able to teleport between them whenever you want vs the current system of only being able to access the waypoint system when you are at a waypoint.- Item selection needs to be streamlined, maybe something like hold down a key/bumper to open a radial menu for item selection.  As it stands scrolling one-by-one or opening the main menu to select an item is too cumbersome as they begin to accumulate.- Dungeon rooms - The algorithm needs to be adjusted, on multiple occasions I have left one dungeon room only to go to exactly the same dungeon room.  I find it's not uncommon to see the same room multiple times in a single dungeon run.- Town building - Would like this to be expanded, I had everything in the town built before I even accessed the second dungeon and there are still a bunch of empty lots.  This would also serve as a gem sink for later in the game once you are pretty much maxed out on persistent upgrades.  Let me relocate buildings, further customize my house, and maybe some options for purely cosmetic items/decorations and buildings that can be placed in empty lots.- Also, when moving on ice I experienced some instances of inability to move.  I thought my controller was running low on battery but it seems when sliding into a wall sometimes it will freeze your movement for a second.Overall have enjoyed the game.  Can't comment on the multiplayer as I've only played solo.

_childDocuments_.review: is an indie love letter to the  franchise. Equal parts  and , this RPG integrates some roguelike mechanics into its dungeons to make a product that balances the retro gameplay with modern mechanics nicely. It suffers from a severe lack of polish and a litany of bugs (some game-breaking), but if you can look past some of these quality issues you'll find a fun, casual RPG.You play as a nameless denizen of the continent of Tasos, which is beset by monsters summoned by four invading demons. With the blessing of the goddess in tow, you must go on to fulfill your destiny by clearing out four procedurally-generated dungeons. Invest the loot you earn from dungeon crawling in a variety of upgrades to power your character up and improve your chance of success. With town customization, minigames, sidequests, bonus dungeons, a class system, collectibles and more,  has a lot to experience.Perhaps the game's most unique feature is its optional co-op.  offers both a campaign playable in singleplayer or up to four-player local or online co-op. The game does a pretty good job at straddling the line between being small enough to suit one player and large enough to fit four; dungeon maps, for instance, have enough space to allow multiple players to distinctively move around, but players are mobile enough that traversal never feels like a grind. The level balance is loose, since there are too many permutations of playersThe roguelike elements are more of a mixed bag. While it is true that dungeons are procedurally generated, there is a very limited amount of rooms for each dungeon that the game pulls from. Thus a player of average skill who takes maybe 3-4 trips to finally complete a dungeon will likely encounter almost every single room from a dungeon's pool, just in different orders. Beyond making repeat runs feel samey, the level design can rarely introduce a game-breaking bug: since players can enter a room in any direction, you may get stuck in a room that can only be unlocked by defeating an enemy which you can't reach. As there's no room reset option upon saving/exiting standard to other roguelikes like , you always risk losing a bunch of progress anytime you attempt a dungeon.Speaking of bugs - this game has a lot of them. Twice the game broke during dungeon attempts due to level design flaws (the aforementioned unbeatable enemy, and once my character got stuck behind a level prop). The game also frequently allows the player to walk through breakable objects. Music would cut out until the game was reset. Certain enemy hitboxes were inconsistent. Some additional QA would've gone a lot further to give the impression that this game was made as well as possible.The other major selling points are mostly irrelevant. The minigames are easy to miss entirely, the farming element progresses far too slowly and there is little incentive to complete it, the character classes all play too similarly to offer replay value, town customization is limited to placing buildings on a grid, and the collectibles are frustrating to keep track of because the game never erases the clues for where to find them after they're collected, forcing players to waste tons of time backtracking or to remember each of the hundreds of locations they've already visited. In short, if you're playing , you're doing it for the core RPG gameplay. makes a valiant effort to capture the spirit of  and the gameplay of  fused with roguelike gameplay and other modern types of side content, all to a mixed-positive result. The core RPG gameplay is impressively adaptive to the standard singleplayer experience as to the zany chaos of multiplayer co-op, though the roguelike feature is underdeveloped and exposes the game to some serious bugs. Temper your expectation a bit when comparing this game to the inspiring  classics, and an enjoyable adventure will await.  gets a B-.
