_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - Buy Binding of Isaac instead.The game has a good art style and a decent idea of what the game should be. But there are also a ton of design choices that become annoying and frustrating the longer you go in the game.And a lot of the time, I just think back to the Binding of Isaac, and how much I wish the devs had just straight up copied some of the design philosophies from it.For example, you can see what minion/follower/companion you're getting before acquiring it in Binding of Isaac, and you almost always remain in control of it. In Neon Abyss, it's ALWAYS random. You can get a minion/follower/companion that may be very detrimental to your run, which just leaves you wishing for the little bastard to just die already. And not only that, you have actually no control of them. You need a health pick up? Race your little buddy to it or they'll grab it to try and give you shields. Need money? Grab it before Mini Trump snatches it up before you. Need to hold your fire in order to not corrupt a crystal chest? No worries, your lil' buddy managed to land a shot on it through the power of chaos theory.In my opinion, never pick up eggs at the start of a run, they're a big part of the game but not worth the hassle.A lot of the pick-ups are what I'd consider borderline useless. And even worse still, is the sheer number of them. So plenty of pick-ups to choose from, but very little of value to be had. And the good pick-ups are all basically the same. Extra jump or the ability to fly along with weapon damage, fire rate and bullet/projectile count. In over 30 hours of playing, never once have I been happy or found it useful to get an item that either increases my melee damage or gives me a chance to get a crystal/heart/shield or whatever when I manage to get a melee kill. The melee is bad, and none of the upgrades address it or fix it.The game leaves me wishing they would have carried over more of the good ideas from Binding of Isaac. "Angel rooms" in Neon Abyss are the only ones really worth it as it can be obtained for free. Meanwhile, the "Devil room" in Neon Abyss, is absolutely atrociously bad. You MUST take damage consistently to obtain it. You MUST sacrifice a heart container to even be able to see which items are on offer. Items that aren't even necessarily exclusive to the "Devil room". It's just not worth it unless you NEED to go and defeat Ares.Meanwhile the devil rooms in Binding of Isaac has you able to see all the items on offer before you make a purchase with the exception of a rare floor curse. Devil rooms in Binding of Isaac are also less costly to get to to begin with, in  Neon Abyss it dictates that you HAVE to take repeated instances of damage to fill up the meter, no devil room until it's full. In Binding of Isaac you work with less guarantees due to it being based on a percentage chance of getting one, but you can influence that percentage, and doing so is also way less costly in terms of health & play style. In Neon Abyss it's frustrating how easily it can be to accidentally turn towards Devil rooms despite trying to avoid it, and reversing it towards Angel Rooms is an uphill struggle at best. If you're unfortunate and collide with an 'evil' crystal chest, door or whatever.. you could be half-way to an Angel room and it'd reverse your work to the point you'd be half-way to a Devil room now, but doing the reverse of using a 'good' crystal item, does nowhere near that much, meaning pure RNG can almost block you into a Devil room, where it'd straight up be faster to just work on obtaining the Devil room to clear the bar, rather than trying to slowly reverse the damage. It's not fun, just frustrating. And you don't feel like you're in control of the circumstances leading to it a lot of the times.I don't know if this is something the Devs eventually patched in or I unlocked from progressing in the game, but the starting levels of the game got harder enemies in it now. Normally I don't mind a challenge, but they all seem to come in a variety of long lasting invincibility where you then get a small time frame to deal damage before going back to being impossible to kill. They're not really a challenge, they're just slow and tedious to deal with.The game does have a large unlock tree, but one so large and costly that in order to see it to the end of it, you'll likely be driven to stop playing due to the shortcomings of the game. In Binding of Isaac, you'd have some fun and interesting though of course also sometimes annoying and tedious tasks to complete in order to unlock some things, but it at least gave you something to do and some variety, a tangible goal to work towards. Only thing left to do in Neon Abyss is to just play the game some more as the unlock tree works with currency obtained from defeating bosses.Did Binding of Isaac ever make areas impossible to get to unless you had some special mobility items? Yes.Does Neon Abyss do it a lot more often than Binding of Isaac for less reward? Yes.Biggest advice I can give a new player is to keep your browser open with the game wiki's full item list. Because even when you get the item pick-up that actually lets you read what an item does in-game, it doesn't work in the shop where you have to buy it first, for some god awful reason.The game does have good potential, but it needs a lot of work to get to that potential.

_childDocuments_.review: Another Update: I want to like this game. I dusted it off, added another 6 hours after a friend said it was updated. Read below for previous reviews. Overall, back to a Yes, sure i'll recommend it. The tunes are catchy, I hate that music style but, even I bob around to it.They fixed the bomb/explosive thing from what I can tell.. There's also some story, it's not as infuriating blowing yourself up every 2 seconds (though most of my upgrades were reset so maybe it still happens?  Some runs though are crap, You can say it's RNG if you want, sure. It might very well be, though I'd love if there was more cross-play between the items. The items are very unique and well thought out there are times though where your pick-ups are worthless. Or could be amazing, but only if you get a different or upgraded gun that never comes.  Now I know the game is supposed to be a bit rogue-like (or so it seems) and i've cruised through all the bosses (great designs) but I dont want to grind.  suggestions: Constructive criticism. Two untouched rooms should activate the Wisdom bar rather than a chance of not finding a purple chest/door until last room (if then).  Make an option where both bars activate simultaneously, but you can only choose one of them as reward. Wisdom/Athena bars get penalized still (maybe?) but let the damage stack for Ares.  Or, make it a transition rule. If you get hit in a room, Ares will fill Next room hit in, if you don't get hit Wisdom/Athena gets filled next time you aren't hit through a room.  Generates a skill style that seems to already be there but doesn't cause a negative, sliding back on a bar/skill/gameplay is such a game breaker.My 2 cents, take it or leave it.----------------------------No Review--Go ahead and read below if you want my original "positive review" I have to change it, new items new unlocks etc etc all focus on that same mechanic that is infuriating bombs, chained negatives and teeny tiny tweaks wherein the game gets worse the more you unlock. I would get my money back if I could. Even at the sale I bought it on, don't.---- Original "Positive" Review ---Sure i'll recommend it - be prepared for some irritation. It isn't hard, it isn't long but it is frustrating. Its the explosions. They need to redo it, even mines auto explode when dropped touching blocks or even a non-explosion regular chest. Your Wisdom/Fury bar wipes if its full after you kill the boss and leave. It's a fair game for what it is, I'm glad I got it on discount. Some people might like these aspects - but I don't feel its a challenge to be 2 pixels away from not blowing yourself up its just irritating. Not to mention their "quick restart" not really that quick.Hey though, if you like unlocking things this is your game, if you like a bunch of items this is your game, if you like EDM soundtracks this is your game.

_childDocuments_.review: Free: gifted to me by a friend. Edit: I have since unlocked everything on the "skill trees" and beat all the bosses, and had fun doing it!  Recently (Jan, 2022) there was another free content update with some new bosses, so I paid to buy the DLCs.  The extra characters are....meh....but I think they deserve some money out of me for all the fun I've had.  Have not reached the new bosses yet but I'm working on it!  Original review follows:Roguelite platformer/shooter with zillions of items and guns, and quite a few pets too. Shoot the badguys, and don't get hit by their shots.  It's nice that many enemies don't damage you on-contact, just from their actual attacks.  At the end of each stage there's a boss fight, and after several stages, there's a big boss called a manager.  So far I only beat the first one. 5 types of 'currency' in the game:-HP, which you can sometimes pay directly or indirectly to buy things or access new areas. Restore them by picking up full/half hearts. Moldy hearts may heal or harm you. -coins. Gain them as copper(1)/silver(5)/gold(10)/larger-keys-grenades / explosions, there are plenty of obstacles that will only disappear/open from explosions. -crystals, which you can think of as MP. They are used to power your RMB special ability. Some doors/chests can be opened for 3/2 crystals, or you can shoot them to turn them into a 'spiked' version that instead costs 0.5HP to open. On a run you can find big yellow coins, which go towards unlocking things on a skill tree including new characters.  Some of the skill-trees end in a one-time-use bonus that seems pretty dumb...the longest skill tree ends in double-jump (one-time-use), though you can sometimes get that, or even flight, from RNGesus during regular gameplay. There are several characters you can unlock in-gme (and more you can buy as DLC), they vary in health/shields/keys/grenades and their special abilities.  I like the black guy (default version) that lays landmines.  At the risk of hurting yourself, you effectively have infinite explosions.

_childDocuments_.review: Very nicely made game. The challenge is appropriate for a roguelike and offers great replayability via all the unlockable items and guns. If you're experienced with these games, the best I can offer as a description is the gameplay from rogue legacy, isaac, and gungeon all mixed together in the setting from hades with an artstyle that is uniquely its own. Movement is responsive and clean, I always get what I expect on the screen when moving around and the movement in general feels fluid. The game is tough but offers a lot of opportunity to solve small puzzles for items and consumables if you're careful not to obliterate everything in sight when entering/clearing a room. I have not felt supremely underpowered on any run that I've done in my 40 hours so far; you will find yourself stuck without keys, frags, money, or crystals occasionally, but usually not all at the same time.I like the pet system from the game which can reward good play by pets surviving longer, evolving, and giving better benefits. These kinds of variety are what keep the game interesting and replayable. I do hope that they add more pets in the future.All that being said, the game's animation and artstyle are amazing. I love the unique take: Cyberpunk Hell.........Where else are you going to see that? The music compliments the game fantastically and the DLC is all reasonably priced and adds actual variance to the game. Overall, I would give this game a 9/10 with definite room to grow to a 10 with updates or significant DLC. That being said, very glad I found this gem of a game, I'm sure 40 hours is just the beginning!

_childDocuments_.review: To be completely honest, this game feels like it was made by someone who has never played a rougelike in their life. Everything in this game just feels bad, and there's no flow in the game play. This game is quite literally this: lets fill the screen with as much ♥♥♥♥ as possible. The vast majority of the mechanics just feel like they're missing something.Positives: you want to see big number, here you go! This is a pretty mindless game, so it's good for when you don't really want to focus or pay attention. The artstyle is nice too, and the progression system is fine. If you want an easy game, here you go.My absolute #1 complaint is the fact that in the later parts of the run, you're literally not able to see anything because of all the flashing gun lights and whatnot, making it impossible to actually try and dodge bullets. This bothers me so much- there's no option to reduce the amount of effects on screen or highlight enemy bullets- THIS NEEDS TO BE A FEATURE YOU ARE LITERALLY UNABLE TO PLAY THE GAME. LITERALLY EVERY RUN I CANT SEE ANYTHING BY THE END OF IT IT'S NOT FUN. The game is quite literally is unplayable at this stage.There seems to be little to no skilled game play as well, pretty much every run boils down to this: get as much damage as possible. Very braindead gameplay.Another negative is that all the characters practically feel the same. Just in general all the runs tend to feel like a repeat of the previous, it's just an endless cycle of the same exact run. Who wants to play the exact same run over and over and over? Whenever I play this game I feel like I'm slamming my head into the wall over and over and over.And more than anything- the game just isn't fun. When I get hit instead of feeling like oh I could've dodged that or I could've outplayed it, I often feel cheesed and just annoyed.Honestly there are so many better rougelikes to play. This is the most watered down baby rougelike thats not fun or skillfull. I honestly don't know why this is so highly reviewed, if you're an actual rougelike player stay away from this game. I'm a real hardcore rougelike player and my opinion is that this is a bottom of the barrel tier rougelike. Don't waste your time with this game.

By far are the biggest issue with it in general in my opinion is the general room design (primarily that it leads to a lot of unavoidable damage rooms). There are a few specific rooms and combos that cause particular grief. Any room with a bomb wall that requires you to throw the bomb while falling (usually next to a jump pad) is extremely frustrating, because of how little control you have over bombs. They throw out horizontally at a specific angle and it can be extremely easy to waste bombs in these rooms or damage yourself. The other is any room with a staircase that spawns the enemies that fire two bullets downwards then split and move horizontally. Visually, it seems like standing on the lower level of the staircase would make this pass over you - it does not, and you will get hit.Rooms also tend to pen you into one corner with the monster spawn locations instantly. A lot of the design decisions of this game are more or less taken from top-down roguelite games, but because this is 2d with gravity to contend with many of these decisions do not work well.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me begin by stating that I did enjoy the game while it lasted, however I have no desire to play it any further. This review is also going to mention The Binding of Isaac (henceforth referred to as TBOI) a good number of times, so it'll be clearest if you've played that. This review is based upon the game without the DLC.The gameplay is pretty straightforward when you look at the tags. It's a 2D roguelite shooter, you move through levels consisting of non-randomized rooms placed randomly next to each other in a grid system. When you reach the last level (up to nine) the run is over and you're reset back to the starting hub. Every level has 1 boss room, 1 item room containing an item, 1 shop room and 1 duel room which rewards the player with another item. To get stronger the player collects these items, which give the player various bonuses ranging from straight up more damage to making it so bullets bounce off of walls or explode. The game uses 6 types of resources, hearts and shields, which are the players' health, bombs and keys which can unlock areas and chests, coins which are used to buy items in the shop, and lastly crystals which can be used to use your weapon's active ability (if it has one) or use certain purple objects.The game obviously took inspiration from TBOI, which also has the rooms listed above, coins, bombs, keys, hearts, shields (soul hearts in TBOI). However, I would never call this game an isaac clone, as the gameplay is too different from TBOI.The crystals are part of the game's most interesting feature: Wisdom vs Violence, this game's version of TBOI's angel vs devil system.Throughout the game you will find various purple doors, chests and crystals. Shoot them and they will turn red and spiky. While purple, you can use crystals to activate the object and start the wisdom meter. Activate more purple objects or finish rooms without getting hit to fill up the meter. While red (and spiky) you can touch the object, which will hurt the player and initialize the Violence meter. Fill it up by activating red objects or getting hurt in rooms (once per room). Once full, you can teleport to another room not connected to the rest of the map. If you went for Wisdom, you can choose between 2 items and get one for free, for violence the player will have to sacrifice a heart container and get to choose between 3 items (up to 5 later in the game). The game also has an egg/pet system, which evolves TBOI's 'babies' (which are mostly pretty useless) and turns them into an integral gameplay feature. Eggs can be found throughout the run and can later 'hatch', which will either result in "hatch failed", which gives the player nothing or it can hatch into a random pet which can do anything from just shooting at enemies to picking up coins and dropping random pickups. Okay, so you're playing the game, you've reached the final level a couple times, what do you get? Neon Abyss uses a system a lot of roguelikes use in the form of a currency (Faith Gems, in this case) earned throughout each run and are the only thing not lost upon the end of the run. Faith Gems are gained upon defeating a boss and are used to unlock new items, characters or dungeon upgrades.This is the second biggest issue the game has that limits its replayability. In TBOI item unlocks all have different requirements, like "Beat X Boss with Y Character" or "Finish level X without getting hit". In Neon Abyss, everything is unlocked using the same currency, gained in the same way.This is pretty personal, so take it with a grain of salt. At time of writing, I've played the game for exactly 8 hours. In this time I've beaten every administrator including Ares and Athena. I have only gained enough Faith Gems to unlock 1 of the 6 unlockable characters, meaning progression is very slow, not to mention that later upgrades get more expensive. Slow progression is fine, but not when it's so linear and uninteresting. I've already mentioned that a lot of rooms can be cleared by standing in the entrance, this problem is magnified if you have a weapon with long range, as you can kill most enemies without them even being able to hit you. This is also true for hard mode. I did like the game for my time with it, learning the (limited amount of) rooms, (limited amount of) bosses and (less limited amount of) guns but it simply lacks the replayability of a game like The Binding of Isaac because of its boring items and progression system. I also want to mention here  that you can't rebind actions to buttons like 'Mouse4', 'Mouse5' or the 'Shift' key for some reason, a truly baffling decision. Not recommended for it's current price or even half off. I would pick it up if it ever drops to 5$ or less.

_childDocuments_.review: Because Steam doesn't let users post reviews in terms of score, I'm forced to give a not recommend because the gameplay is just not that good, though it's still at the least a 6/10.  After defeating a boss, you can pick up upgrades, but these mostly affect either your DPS or health and not radically alter gameplay like Enter the Gungeon -  a game that serves as obvious inspiration to this game.  While this ensures that all boss drops are useful  to an extent, it reduces the replay value of the game, a poison for roguelikes.  The guns all have infinite ammo, so that's one less aspect of resource management for those seeking them out.  The massive downside is that you can only ever hold one gun at a time. This makes combos non-existent and the game very unengaging. In fact, there is a character who can specifically combine two weapons into one as a bandaid solution for this very problem, but the way the combination works is just so lazy and unimaginative it's not worth mentioning - just a combination of those two gun sprites shooting both types of bullets at once.In terms of quality of life, the game actually does most its job well, with remappable everything and difficulty selection anytime in the hub area with no penalty, you can also customize the weapons and passives to disable the garbage you accidentally unlock, so no more Dead Cell BS here.  The one biggest gripe I have, however, is the translation quality. Without mincing words, it's honestly atrocious, combining broken syntax with wrong grammar. While this is mostly limited to the character selection and not item description from what I've seen, it's still grating to see them in-game.Edit: I have maxed out my gears and unlock all characters by modifying my saves, just to see if the game does increase in variety in the late game as some have said. That is unfortunately not the case for what I described above. Of course, apparently I'm just a guy complaining about the translation quality of another language IN ENGLISH, and not the language that I intend my criticism to reflect, take it with a grain of salt.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game, it has too many issues at the present which I’ll outline below. – The whole game is repetitive and a grind. To advance the game, you have to defeat ‘managers’ which are the final level bosses. The first manager is found at the end of level five. After you beat it, an additional level with another manager is unlocked. But you don’t get to advance to the next level straight away, you are forced back to the beginning, and now you have to beat six levels to unlock the next manager. Rinse and repeat until there are eight levels.After that, you still have to run through all the same levels, but now you have to get to a special room to find a token that drops randomly so that you can access the next two managers. This wouldn’t be so bad if these were optional bosses, but it is necessary to beat them to advance the game.I’m sorry, but who thought that this was good game design? You play well enough to get to the room, but no token? Guess what? You might as well start a new run grinding through the same levels that you have already played multiple times at this point. Like I said, repetitive.  – For the first couple of runs, the music is ok. But OMG, after several runs it becomes repetitive and grating. For the love of God, please add some more variety to the music! After several runs, I got burnt out on the soundtrack. Anyone who says the music is great should reevaluate after 10-15 hours of play. I can almost guarantee that they will change their opinion of the music. Come back after 15 hours and see if you still think the music  is good. – Often times there is so much on the screen it is difficult to make out what is damaging you. Not only do you have your own bullets flying around the screen, (often flying in multiple directions at once), you can also have multiple pets that follow you around attacking enemies and firing their own projectiles. (I’m not sure how many pets you can get, but I have had several runs where I have had 20 or more.) At the same time you have multiple enemies and their projectiles, not to mention the background which often has flashing elements. In between you, your pets, the enemies, all of the projectiles and flashing background elements, it can become very difficult to see what the hell is damaging you. The overall game feels like they made the game and weren’t really sure what direction to take it, so they just started to add stuff to it. They even have an in-game joke about this.There are other frustrating elements to this game which I won’t go into. But I will say that most of this game's faults become very apparent around the 10-15 hour mark. I think that most of the positive reviews that have less than 15 hours playtime should reevaluate and see if they feel the same way once they hit 15 hours of playtime. Due to the game being repetitive and a grind, among other issues, I cannot recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't a bad game at all, i don't recommend it but i don't don't recommend it either, the problem is Steam doesn't propose another choice so i put a thumb down because, as a rogue like (and considering the other rogue likes on the market), this one is frustrating.Frustrating because it has a great potential. There's a lot of bosses in the game. They're all pretty neat, nice mechanics, sometimes hard and not very fair but still fun because the core gameplay itself is very nice. Running, jumping, shooting: it all feels great. Grenades are pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up tho, but after some time you'll get it. Visually, well, it's well made but not very diverse. It gets boring after a few runs only. Not a lot of environnements AT ALL but there's a lot of "secret or bonus rooms", and they're very funny sometimes, pretty creatives. Soundtrack is boring, sadly. Not a lot of diversity in terms of ennemies either but i don't know if it's a big problem because it's already hard to understand what's happening in game. Lot of ennemies per rooms, A DAMN LOT OF PROJECTILES so you reeeaaally need to pay attention to everything. It's fun. Not easy, but fun.So yeah. Great gameplay, pretty creative and original game when it comes to all the bonus rooms, secret rooms, bosses...But there a problem. A very big one in my opinion and the reason why i give the game a thumb down instead of a recommendation. Items. They are awfully boring, the very vast majority of them. Sure, there's many different weapons. Most of them plays the same BUT they are kinda still different and some of them are very unique. They can change the gameplay a bit. But the items... IMO, items in a rogue-like like this are very important. In this game, they almost NEVER change the gameplay. What's fun about Binding of Isaac for exemple, is that there's always this excitation when you're about to get a new items. What is it gonna be ? How is it gonna affect my gameplay ?Sure, in Enter the Gungeon for exemple, only the weapons are really gonna be big changes but all of them are incredibly unique so they don't need to spice it up with gamechanging items. Weapons aren't like this in Neon Abyss, so you need items to make everything more diverse. But they don't. 90% of them are something like "get hit by [insert something] and have a chance to drop [insert drop like bomb or key]", "kill ennemies and have a chance to drop [insert drop like bomb or key]", "use [insert drop like bomb or key] and have a chance to drop [insert drop like bomb or key]". THAT IS SO BORING.Items are either like this or like that -> "get one more heart" or "drop more something". I mean, yeah items like that are also in Isaac but they are not 90% of what you are gonna get, in Neon Abyss it is waaaaaayy too much, way way too much. It's very rare to get something a bit fun like an item that will add a projectile to your weapon or making your projectiles bigger. Very, very, very rare. I mean sure it's fun when it's happens but waow it almost never does.And it makes the game honestly boring, most runs are just the same, the gameplay rarely changes. Except, it's the point of rogue-likes like this. So, thumb down for that because the game has the potential, it's just sad that it fails in the one essential category.Oh, and i forgot about eggs. Yeah but you know what, you'll forget about them too. Eggs sometimes get you familiars, but you will never really see them. I mean, they do stuff, they hit ennemies, they shoot ennemies, but there's already so much happening on screen that you won't pay attention to your little familiars at all.So yeah, the game isn't bad, but, when you can play Gungeon, Isaac and such, i don't see why you would spend time on Neon. So far, it's not competiting. But it might soon, because they make updates, so keep an eye on this one, the potential is there.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who plays so many roguelikes, this game is not something I cannot recommend.  As a lot of the the other negative reviews of pointed out, this game makes a great first impression, but unfortunately , it fails to keep that charm moving forward into the game.  A lot of my issues come from their choice of gameplay and pulling from other popular games like Binding of Issac and Enter the Gungeon.  I would call the gameplay itself grindy and disappointing.  The balance of resources feel fully random with no logic at all.  I can go levels without finding explosives to unlock various areas.  I can even go a whole level without finding a key to unlock the treasure area.Everything in this game is locked behind progression, which seems like a great aspect for roguelike, but is actually one of its worst features.  A lot of the layout changes to the dungeon can only be unlocked via resources dropped by the bosses.  Currently bosses drop one token no matter how far you have progressed.  A full clear (at my point in the game) will net 7-8 tokens.  Most unlocks are anywhere from 5-30, with the average being between 10-15, meaning currently, I can do a full clear and yield nothing from that run,A lot of the mechanics of the game go unexplained.  What is the bar at the bottom right?  I figured it out myself with the difference between the red and purple bar on how to progress them.  One thing that is nice, when you do unlock a new gameplay item (passive item) you get to try it for free on your next run to get a general understanding of how it works.I love the art style of the game,  but given the bullet hell nature it becomes quite a busy and I frequently lose my crosshair in the fray of it all.  There is no option to change your crosshair to make it more noticeable or even just the colour.Use and Melee are both bound to the same button and share the same button map, meaning you cant seperate them.  This is a huge chore as there are items in this game that you can interact with,  but if you aren't in the exact spot to interact with it, or the use activation is still on cooldown, you will instead melee it, changing the cost of the item to health instead of currency.  Also again, your character will automatically melee when near an enemy but in 90% of cases, your gun will always do more damage.Picking up other guns to me, has no incentive.  13 of the 14 hours I've played this game have been with the default gun.  It is reliable, does good damage, and scales well.  Other guns work in unpredictable manners, or statically or just worse than the default gun.   The incentives to other guns are the secondary powers they offer.  Such as flying, granting health, etc but again all are worse than the default gun (with the exception being the gun that increases your damage for one room),I almost forgot the pet system!  This system is high variance with very little incentive to pick up the eggs.  They offer to only be an annoyance.  A majority of the pets operate like bumbo from BoI.  They will pick up a specific items (Health, Coin, Crystal,  etc) and turn it into another random item.  THERE IS NO WAY TO GET RID OF A PET.  I capitalize this because I have lost multiple runs because I had a random pet that was taking every heart, or would out race me to every coin depleting my resources.  These resource pets can also generate a random currency of the one they pick up (which doesn't make any sense).  There are also offensive and defensive pets as well.  The offensive pets I don't mind, they shoot at your enemies till they die, it helps.  The defensive pets function like cube of meat from or any other orbiter from BoI.  These pets orbit you and block bullets, damage enemies etc.  EXCEPT FOR ONE that is a ball that blocks YOUR BULLETS (and enemy bullets).  Why does it function like this?  I had a run where my bullets exploded on contact, naturally I would want to avoid the orbiter the blocks my bullets.  But because of the random nature of pets I just hatched one randomly with no control over it.  This ended my run almost instantly as I couldn't shoot anything without risking my own damage.I've explained to most of my friends why this game is poor.  For someone who is really into roguelikes and a huge fan of BoI and EtG I am just left feeling disappointing.  This game would of heavily benefitted from early access and input from its player base.  Because a lot of what I listed above feels like it was all implemented with lack of testing from unbiased third parties.  I had a lot of these reservations at the 5-6 hour point of the game but really wanted to give it a shot.  But doubling my playtime didn't improve the game at all and instead just frustrated me further.  This is a game made by the developers for the developers, not for the players.  As a result I will be uninstalling.I have so much more to say but truly just don't care and don't normally post reviews for things.TL;DR : Game is appealing for the first few hours of gameplay but becomes uninspired and grindy in an attempt to increase the longevity of the game while sacrificing the enjoyment.  Without significant improvements and input from the community I cannot recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game a has a few issues I believe hurt it's replay value.- Too many keys.  Not the actual key item, but to open a door it could either be a key, money, crystal, bomb, or health.- With too many keys, there are often times you can't find enough or any of the type you need and are leaving a whole floor of loot behind.- Items don't tell you what they do before you pick them up, so you have to do trial and error, and you can't plan a build around things unless you remember what it did.- Eggs are underwhelming.  It's rarer for an egg to not be a failure hatching.  You can get several eggs following you, and only 1 or 2 might be a pet.  Just did a run where all of them were failures.- Pets are underwhelming and don't feel like they contribute very much.  Plus they take damage and disappear very quickly because they roam off on their own and you can't really save them.- Too many restarts.  I understand roguelike, but you have to get to the first boss beat him, then start over, so that build you were working on goes away.  Next time you can potentially go through the first boss to the second.  Restart.  Go through the second to third, etc.  It's just not the restarting of a rogue like I was expecting.- Unlocks are underwhelming.  I've played for 7 hours and just now got enough crystals to unlock through to the next playable character.- Dancing is broken.The game is fun, but not for a long period of time.+ The colors and art are great.  It's very attractive smooth running game.+ The music is good and keeps you in the neon rave groove.+ The number of item pick ups is crazy.  There are a ton of items and weapon combinations.+ Bullet size is proportional to weapon damage and can make for some crazy fighting.Overall I wouldn't get this game again at the current price.  It just doesn't hold enough replay value, and when I'm staring at the pit deciding whether or not to jump back in, I frequently find that the pay off is not worth the time put into the run.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an okay platformer roguelite. It suffers from being blatantly unfinished and full of bugs and design flaws. Hitboxes are atrocious, with enemy animations not lining up with their attack or movement state, i.e. an enemy will damage you the frame it starts a bite attack, with the actual bite animation being a full second later. Enemy spawns appear to be mostly random, meaning that they can spawn on you and create undodgeable attack patterns very quickly. It is entirely unclear if an enemy will deal contact damage, sometimes they have spikes (obvious) sometimes they just look like balls and still contact damage you anyway, despite the game telling you to your face that most enemies don't deal contact damage. Runs are samey, there's five hundred items that barely do anything, and many that will completely screw you over and encourage you to quit your game and restart rather than delay the inevitable death by self-damage. The music is uninspired and forgettable, and the art itself is probably the only saving grace. That being said, I have yet to play a single run in which I did not see an art-related bug, such as texture seams not lining up properly or sprites getting ordered wrong and showing up behind things they shouldn't.Despite all these flaws, the game also manages to be completely devoid of challenge. I pumped up the difficulty to max and won my first run handily, and all runs afterwards, save for the ones that were ruined by a "screw the player" item (why would you even put these in the game?) or boss attacks with unclear telegraphs or damage sources, like making the floor damage you without any animation to indicate such. This is because, while many of the guns are jokes and do nothing, there are enough guns that erase enemies so quickly that there is no need to dodge anymore. You simply damage enemies too quickly and any damage you take is quickly mitigated by the pickup balancing being out the window. I have ended all my runs with more consumables / hearts / shields than it was possible to spend in the run, it really needs some resource rebalancing.There's definitely some real replayability somewhere deep in the game loop, but the developers haven't found it and I think it's clear the game needs at least another year in the oven.

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to 'Enter The Binding Of Dead Cells'. If you've ever wondered (and who hasn't) what a game would be like if you combined the guns of Gungeon, the ridiculous items of Isaac and the platforming of Dead Cells, well... wonder no more!So far, I would say this is a decent enough game to warrant a positive recommendation. Early signs are good that the Devs want to keep supporting and improving the game, and it looks like there is already an update on the way which aims to address some of the community's most requested changes/fixes. I'm personally not too sure about the whole 'hatching' thing (I don't really want a dozen eggs following me round the room thanks), and I hope that they tweak the unlocks system to be less grindy. Overall though it's a fun, stylish game and I like it.This game could be destined for greatness. Let's see if it gets there.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game, but only for a while. A huge negative point is that there is not much variation in gun upgrades and most items feel like either direct stat boosts, or nearly useless. It is a roguelite, so it does get very repetitive after a while, and as I said earlier it does not have a lot of longevity due to the items/upgrades, but you can have a lot of fun with it. Overall, I'd give it about a 6.5/10. You should try it cause it has a good price.REVISION: After playing the game for the first time in a while, and with the latest few updates, it has gotten SO much better. There is a new endless mode in the Chrono Trap DLC, and there are a few new bosses, titans, and titan variations, along with some new guns which are very epic, an overhaul to the item system, which includes upgrade badges that replaced some stupid items, and a new feature that allows you to use angry sprites to do your bidding. _childDocuments_.review: It's good! Very reminiscent of Enter the Gungeon with some new unique gameplay mechanics, such as the eggs, which hatch into familiars. There are some issues that I've noticed, but I am confident that this game will continue to be perfected in future updates. Bosses are also a weak point so far, but the platforming and enemy variety makes up for it. Glad to have a new Rougelike to play!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the Best Rougelike games on the market.This Review is based heavily on the exp patch for the game and i would ignore all of the negative reviews with 40hrs or less of playtime. They are most likely people annoyed with features that have been removed in the Exp patch. The Developers listen so much on the discord and ive never seen so much dev feedback from a small team. i would 100% go drop into the discord and see for yourself. Now for my actual game review.Positives:+Game has a huge skill tree that allows you to pick the items you want at the pace you want. i cant stress how different the game is on skill tree 5 than on skill tree 1.+Feels rewarding and unlocking characters means an entirely new way to play.+Endless amounts of synergies like nothing ive ever seen before.+Fantastic item and weapon design.+Perfect mix of slow and face paced game-play.+Gorgeous Visuals and art style i cant fault it at all.+Its just very fun and fluid to jump into and blast out a few runs.Negatives:-Core gameplay loop can be a bit tedious until you get to grips with the game.-Music can be quite choppy and repetitive and unless you get an enjoyable weapon to listen to they really do clash. -Lack of Bosses, overall the amount of managers and bosses is just too few.-Too easy even on hard. I hope they add harder modes to make it more challenging.Summary:In short the game is amazing and only held back by very minor issues and flaws. with the amount the devs are listening at the moment i dont see why this game cant be the next big rougelike it has that much potential. The game is a totally different beast when you get to late game and getting the perfect items just feels amazing. you can make the game harder for yourself now but i cant wait until the devs give us an insane difficulty with more managers and bosses. overall i feel like this game is totally worth the money every penny.Its not too fast paced and just hits you in the sweet spot making you want to play one more run just to see if you can get that amazing rainbow show on the screen. items are perfectly synergised and you feel like a god when you get that perfect seed. almost all of the issues have and will be addressed in the future on the exp build for the game. i cant stress how important it is for you to use the exp build in the beta section of steam properties. it totally changes the game. All in all i think this game is a hidden gem and is totally worth the money final score 8.5/10EDIT: So they have added abyssal mode and i have to say after running with it this is the absolute way the game is to be played. it makes the game allot harder and allot more rewarding if you can finish a run. with the addition of this mode and all of the stuff on the Exp Patch the game is easily 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Warning: This game is addictive, if you play you may not put it back down, you have been warned.Just to make clear I was a creator who has been provided a key to produce content prior to release. I had played the demo and requested a key due to my keen interest. First this game is a roguelite, if you haven't played a roguelite you die, a lot, it's part of the game! What make this a roguelite though is that you do have some overarching progression that persists after you die. This is in the form of an unlock tree that requires a currency you obtain after defeating a boss. These unlocks can vary from more OP items, weapons and even game rules! The item and weapon variations were okay, a lot of the items just provide a straight damage and speed buff. I'd like to see these become more unique in the future patches. They are varied enough however that each run is completely different, one run you may struggle and the next you may face roll every boss. These have not been balanced and for a good reason, it allows you to become overpowered because it's fun! The game has varying difficulty levels (easy, normal and hard) these difficulty levels do not have an incentive however, but the incentive is to challenge yourselves. What would be nice to see is some leaderboards in the future for people to try and compete against each other. Perhaps more difficulty levels added in the future too.Neon Abyss is exactly what it tries to be, fun! I'd like to see more content in the future and a little more polish in a couple of places. All in all I think it's a great game, has plenty of replayability and is worth every penny.Now get your character onto the dance floor and press E to dance!

_childDocuments_.review: I think I could recommend this game, but it has a few frustrating things that are holding it back. I think if these few things changed, it could easily make the game way more fun and less frustrating. -Your own pets block your shots and grenades. This not only gets in the way of you shooting enemies, but you can waste precious grenades only to blow yourself up. I got one item that made your shots explode, and of course my run was cut short by my damn minions blocking my shots repeatedly and me blowing myself up. Super frustrating, and there's no point to this. -Charged Beam weapons lock your aim in place after you fire and that feels absolutely awful. Let us move the beam around or make it a not channeled attack. -Charged weapons get interrupted when you take damage. These weapons are generally not advantageous to begin with, but when you constantly need to recharge your attack for taking a hit it's incredibly frustrating. -One of the most frustrating things in Binding of Isaac is getting to a power up room and not having a key. Not because of having wasted it prior, but because there just hasn't been any dropped or available to you. In Neon Abyss, this is a problem x10. Not only do you have to worry about keys for power up doors, but there are also locked chests behind rock walls that you need a grenade to blow up which is equally as rare as a key. Make these more common, having to complete a level and skip a power up room feels like you are being ripped off. -Grenades need to be able to be held down and show their path. Way too many times I've wasted my only grande only for it to miss the rocks I'm aiming for and land on nothing. Nothing like losing a precious resource for nothing. -In this game it's class based whether or not you can read item descriptions prior to picking it up. So you either pick a character explicitly to know what it is you are picking up, or you're forced to blindly pick something that could be trash. Alternatively, you would just go google the name of the item and it's effects and waste your time because of this design choice. Make this a feature, not something limited to a class. There's also a number of bugs that need fixing. If you play with a controller, you cannot use the upgrade bar without restarting the game and using the mouse to do so. Gameplay is jittery pretty constantly.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a bright, colorful game, well animated, excellent music, lots of items and lots to unlock, but it's simply not on par with many of the other roguelikes out there owing to the extreme reliance upon RNG and said colorful nature making for confusing visuals.Keys and grenades are often the resources used to open containers and get loot, but said containers seem to have no minimum value for the contents.  Sometimes a grenade's used to open a stone chest and inside is another stone chest, which itself contains a single coin or the like.  Similarly, sometimes random crates will hold a key or two, or even grenades.This problem would be frustrating enough were it not for the way that late game fights tend to get extremely confusing.  As a bullet hell, it's typical that the player's projectiles are colored one particular way and enemy projectiles are very distinctly something else.  In Neon Abyss, the first couple levels will stick with this, but as more enemy times become available and more weapons find their way into the player's hands, there's the propensity to have stuff flying everywhere and to be seemingly randomly taking damage from the incomprehensible nature of the visual clutter that results.It's a fun game to chip away at, but I'd recommend one of the Gungeon games over this one if you're looking for a bullet hell roguelike.

_childDocuments_.review: In the current state the game is in, I wouldn't recommend it. Few reasons why-The dungeon generation can be kind of frustrating as it will generate many chests/stone wall blocks and at times not give you any keys or bombs to get through them. Also the generation at times doesn't make sense in the beginner levels. Why they expect me to be able to go through a treasure chest room full of 9 treasure chests all blocked by stone walls on the first dungeon (unless you're unrealistically lucky on the first floor to get a rocket relic and a key gun) is beyond me. What's also annoying is that many rooms will generate platforms that have chests that are literally too high for you to reach in one jump, requiring a flying relic or a two jump relic, which are incredibly rare and most run throughs you never get. If the player can't get to it why generate it? makes no sense to me. If the devs wanted to make sure that the player gets less chests then literally make it so less chests appears instead of pointlessly making them inaccessible or just for the very lucky ones? This doesn't make the game more difficult in any way, just makes the game more based on luck. Making chests more rare would definitely make the game more difficult if that's what their goal is, unless their goal is to make this game about luck. Either way, a game based on luck frustrates many. And the generation isn't exactly random. It's basically the same rooms, just in different orders. I've seen the same exact rooms 10 times over, which makes the game look really shallow. This was a tangent, continues below.-hit boxes aren't accurate,-can't crouch/dodge, feel like in a game like this you should be able to crouch/dodge something, any ability to evade really besides wasd really. -Many ways to do cheap damage to you such as teleporting monsters, at times these monsters will teleport behind you from off screen, meaning you have no sign that they are coming to you and you will 90% of the time take damage, as well as monsters spawning on you or right in front of you in some rooms, where you will take damage from no matter what. -Seed dungeons don't count as a real run, wish it told me that.-the crystal/damage meter that gives you a free relic empties on defeating the boss and leaving the dungeon if It's filled up all the way. Why? It doesn't empty when It's not full and sometimes when you defeat the boss room without being hurt it fills up and if you decide to just go through the portal as one normally does the free relic room goes away and the bar empties. ???-There needs to be more variety in each run, and for the love of god different music. Every run the same music repeats itself over and over and over, and every run It's literally the same mobs, same rooms, just generated in a different order. This game is as wide as a ocean and as deep as a puddle. -Some of the weapons are just utterly useless or impractical-The way you unlock more perks/items is pretty slow and boring. I literally haven't seen the items unlocked by my progression tree even once after unlocking them. It's kind of a joke. Hopefully they will change this, it just seems incredibly un-finished. -Not an incredible amount of content, you beat the last boss and it unlocks the next last boss, there's only 6 of these. You could possibly beat the entire game in 6 runs. Now going after unlocking the entire perk tree would probably bore a person to death fighting the same bosses 50 times over.-almost every character is locked behind really grindy wallsThe good things about this game-A-lot of items/relics, so there's that-It's pretty fun to see what you'll find every run and see what synergies you can create-eggs are cool-that's kind of it. I would say the gameplay is nice and smooth, but it's crippled by the mobs. no joke. The way mobs shoot out bullets is incredibly obnoxious. I get that they're supposed to hurt you, but there's almost no room to enjoy the actual platforming and movement of the game because of this.

_childDocuments_.review: Very decent 2D rogue-like, where you have to clear rooms full of enemies using a huge amount of different weapons, perks and companions. These companions can be earned by finding eggs, which have a chance to hatch if you clear a room. Each companion has a unique ability and can increase in level if you can keep it alive long enough.Neon Abyss does a lot of things right: the controls are great, there's a huge variety in weapons, perks, enemies and bosses, the pixel-art is beautiful and the soundtrack is amazing. On the other hand, as in many rogue-likes, your chance to win depends heavily on the weapons and perks you find. Some of the weapons are really strong and can kill even the final boss without any effort. Other weapons require more precise aiming, and that's not easy in this game because the screen is often cluttered with bullets and your companions.This said, I had many hours of fun with this game, so I can definitely recommend it to anyone looking for an arcade-style experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is such a mess.. where to even begin..The gameplay is garbage, you get swarmed by random projectiles that are half the size of your character, with no way to actually dodge other than running and jumping, which are both very underwhelming. It just results in you taking hits that feel unfair, because you ended up having 40 bullets shot at you with no physical space to avoid them.None of the items or weapons have an explanation until you pick them up, and even then it's barely any info at all. You have no idea how much damage you deal, or any of the guns for that matter. The bosses are poorly made, they pop into existence with no warning, while already making an attack on you in the first frame they magically appear on your screen. Then, they spend most of the fight repeating one attack 5-6 times, half of which are off-screen projectiles that end up hitting you because you have almost no vision on them.Secrets and chests are often locked behind environment that you have to break with your very very limited grenades, which you have no way of aiming, and can easily end up wasting your last grenade trying to unlock something, that you just miss because they are poorly placed..The overall design of the game in terms of aesthetics is a joke.. it makes no sense, there's no logic, you're a dude with a gun running through a dungeon with torches and neon lights, magical runes, platforms with magical runes, and mechanical beasts.. it's a mess!The game is just a cluster of random things thrown at it with no real vision. This is someone making a roguelite game for the sake of just making a roguelite game, with a bunch of random mechanics shoved in there, because yay minigames. Spare yourself the torture, go play Dead Cells, Rogue Legacy, or any of the other really well made games, avoid this trash with glowing lights as the main feature.

_childDocuments_.review: : Discount Isaac/Gungeon with little to no price advantage, better save up your time/money for something else.Get the beta build if you insist on this one as it makes the game much more bearable.It's one of those games that give you amazing first impression yet the more you play the worse it gets.1.  Imagine getting a hair dryer and all it does is increasing your fire rate which is identical as like 20 other items in the game. This eventually leads to the fact that 99% of your winning runs are the ones where you simply stack up 30 damage upgrades and end up one-shotting everything without any mental process.Also part of why I'm concerned that this game won't get much better in the near future. The only scenario to fix this is when the devs care enough to reinvent and replace the effects of all those stuff.2.  There's several unlockable final bosses (like the Isaac situation, runs become longer as more are finished), as well as a whole ass unlock tree including characters/items/in-game mechanics. However as someone who gets hit basically every room I made it to the true ending before even getting two thirds of the unlockable contents, and mind you this is done with the beta build where beating the final boss gives you something equivalent to 2-3 extra unlocks, so in the current official version it's even 10 times slower! On top of that, if you can rarely beat the game it just takes forever to see literally anything new!!3.  A fair amount of items have something to do with your melee attack but literally nobody uses it; Yeah there's like 2 characters that are supposed to focus more on melee attack, one of them is an endgame unlock, which combined with the grinding system means nobody I've seen has unlocked it yet, the other is a paid DLC, and from my observation people only utilize her katana dash as a free double jump lmao  Another thing that's dumb is that you have very little control over your own character, in the sense of not having a reliable way to negate incoming damage; There should've been a dodge dash like what Hollowknight and Cuphead did (One character sorta has it but can only perform it on ground), or they could've just made the player invincible while jumping like Exit the Gungeon. It's frustrating to have enemies coming at you from all directions and not be able to not take damage cause you can't kill'em immediately.It doesn't help that you can even hurt yourself with your own bazooka, like why is that a thing?Bonus: Not that it matters at all but you can tell it's made by a Chinese team when you can hardly find any western media reference in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Almost 80 hours into this game. Time for a review!VISUALSAce, really good pixelized cyberpunk feeling. Each level has its own designg, same with the bosses and casual enemies. Enemies that DO contact damage actually have visual clues to this.SOUNDThe soundtrack is dope, but it gets repetitive because there's only 4 stage compositions and 6 boss themes. A unique composition for each level would make it way better.Sound design overall is really cool, loving the sound effects for weapons. But, again, these could use some diversity. Re-using same sound effects - unedited, just plain same, - is bad practice.STORYThere... isn't any. Sorry. I just couldn't find it. Or it went completely over my head. COMBAT/BALANCEWhack-a-moles should cease to exist. I had enough of them in the Binding of Isaac and I'm getting tired of them here. Otherwise - pretty good. Enemies get harder retroactively, yet they all telegraph their abilities. The characters are interesting, my all-time favorite being Zack. R-6, on the other hand, is the most underwhelming one - not only does its gun has no knockback, it only has an upper limit of 8 shield containers, compared to every other character that can have way more than that (i think it's 10 for HP and 8 for shields?).Also, during combat, a stray bullet - either your own or your enemy's - can hit a crystal or a crystal chest and drop all of your Athena Deal progress, replacing it with Ares Deal. Not cool. Resource hoarding is another problem. Starting from Floor 5, the amount of keys and bombs you need to open certain doors is doubled, so is the amount of HP you lose when you get hit. Sometimes you may never come by a single key or a bomb. It happens.Items could be better. My main issue is that almost every single item in the game follows into one of these categories:- The more Y you have, the more of X you get- You can use X if you don't have Y- You get a chance of getting X by doing something (killing an enemy, using a key, etc)- Jump items- Weapon upgrades- Bomb upgrades- Stat UpgradesThat would be okay with me if the synergies were INTERESTING. As far as I can judge, every run has its own gimmick. There could be a Key run, a Shield run, a Jumping Item run and so on. The diversity this game promises is usually absent and I end up having almost the same sh*t each time I finish a run.TECHNICALSometimes bugs happen, most annoying one being the crawling spiney monsters appearing out of nowhere and then dropping your HP just because they can. Other than that - no complaints, the game runs on mediocre PCs pretty well.OVERALLItems need a rehaul. And they need it drastically. Best solution would be to add workshop/modding support - it helped the Binding of Isaac and it will help this game. But on its own - it's a good rogue-like platformer.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Bundle for September 2021. If you are interested in the game and it's before October 4th, 2021, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Our first rogue-lite of the night.  Players are thrown into the abyss and have to fight their way out.  The game just oozes style and feels like a Binding of Isaac design philosophy with a little Dead Cells platforming and deep weapon system, but every weapon is a gun.  The levels and gameplay are fantastic and working your way through levels and boss encounters are fun.  Though a big piece of the game is the items you get and the synergies between them.  There’s a decent amount of luck involved with the game as well, as my two deep runs had amazing item lists, and I struggled for about thirty minutes across four runs to get beyond the second level possible due to some bad luck, or possibly grinding permanent upgrades. Still, this feels polished and well designed, even if a decent amount of that is just Binding of Isaac’s rules snuck in there.  I have seen it’s not the longest rogue-lite, and with a heavy reliance on luck that might upset some rogue-lite players.  There are three difficulty modes so new players can choose the right one for them. Pick this up if you somehow aren’t overloaded with rogue-lites.  I have over a hundred rogue-lites myself, and I can still somehow find myself playing this.  It’s solid, but also I question if I need yet another rogue-lite.If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: Feels VERY  Early Access :♦ Melee System :  Absolutely useless - you WILL get hit when attempting to Melee as the enemies have to be touching your face for the Melee Action to trigger.♦ Weapons :  Most weapons are gimmicky and useless.  Example : Guitar Gun and Lullaby.  Rocket Launchers do less damage than your default starter weapon.♦ Pets / Familiars / EGG HATCHING : Pets do  minimal damage to enemies and die easily.  Egg Hatching is RNG, so your Eggs may or may not hatch.  A useless feature due to the low damage output from Pets and Eggs not a guarantee hatch.♦ Character Hit Box : You cannot crouch / duck in this game.  Bullets / projectiles will hit your head, even though it didn't touch any part of your character, approx. several "inches" above the character.♦ Violence / Wisdom System : A VERY flawed system - WISDOM : just insert a blue crystal into certain doors or floaty diamond...things and if you does this enough, you get a Gateway to an RNG room with 2 helpful items.  VIOLENCE : Costs you Half a Heart to unlock a Corrupted Door or Floaty Diamond thing which unlocks a gateway to a SACRIFICIAL ROOM with 3 items that PERMANENTLY.  PERMANENTLY removes a Heart Container.  Like , WTF ?!!!!!  It already costed you half of a heart  EACH time to contribute to the WISDOM / VIOLENCE meter and now you have to PERMANENTLY lose a heart container on top of that?!!   Seriously, unbalanced mechanic.♦ Resources :  Keys , Grenades , Money are rare.  Like, I went through an entire dungeon without finding a single key.  That dungeon had 4 Golden Chests that ALSO require keys, I could not open any of them due to me Starting that Dungeon with 0 keys.  This is  a serious problem with the game - it really kills the motivation to play when you're stuck with the default gun for 3 dungeons in a row.♦ Aiming Reticle :  The aiming reticle is VERY difficult to see, especially in combat.  I constantly lost the direction i was aiming due to the reticle being blended into the mass of Enemy projectiles , Pets / Eggs , etc.  ♦ Teleporting Enemy types :  Some enemies teleport , not a problem...unless you just entered the room and you don't see them because they're outside of your view box, then BAM!! they teleport to you and slash you before you have a chance to assess the environment.  CHEAP SHOTS , MUCH ?!!♦ Enemies Spawing on Player :  Yes , enemies will spawn on a player when they enter a room , causing damage before you even have a chance to react.  CHEAP SHOTS, AGAIN ?!!!♦ Puzzle Rooms :  I have yet to see one of these Advertised " Puzzle Rooms "  shown in the trailer.  Is it all a lie?  Probably....♦ Player Skill Shop :  When you defeat a boss, they will drop a Golden Diamond, which you can use to purchases items in a Skill Tree located at the Bar before each Dive into the Abyss.  The problem , however, is that most of these Skills are a ONE TIME USE item.  Really....Just......UGH......  ♦ In conclusion , this game has some things it does right , however, the negatives overshadow any positives I'd be willing to list.  The game is a Grindy , Unrewarding CHORE.  Save your Money - play a game that rewards and respects your time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun roguelite with satisfying item combinations and a rewarding gameplay loop. It has decent enough music (although not enough of it, in my opinion) and a pleasant pixel-art style, with some more modern graphical flourishes like cell shading (does that still count as modern?).The movement physics are solid, but require some precision when it comes to jumping.  It can be a little frustrating to miss some jumps, but mastering the nuances is rewarding in and of itself. The same goes for grenade throws. They are unintuitive at first, but satisfying once understood. The movement is not so momentum based as something like the Mario series, but more reminiscient of older Apogee titles such as Duke Nukem, Bio Menace or... Word Rescue. The grenade mechanics also evoke those old Apogee titles.When it comes to originality of mechanics, there is some heavy borrowing going on. Not outright plagaristic, but let's just say if you've played any amount of The Binding of Isaac, then you will experience a sense of deja vu while playing Neon Abyss. The bomb and key metagame of using bombs and keys to unlock certain rooms, or gain access to resources is very similar. Many of the pets of NA are near identical to the familiars of TBoI. NA has an angel room/devil room mechanic similar to TBoI. NA does however add it's own flourishes to these mechanics, such as the crystals, which act as another resource along with bombs and keys to access rooms and loot, and play into the devil/angel room mechanic. The mechanics and weapon combos aren't as detailed as TBoI and don't have as many cool edge cases, but TBoI is a game that has been expanded with numerous DLCs and I believe NA can get there eventually.That last paragraph may seem negative, but the truth is that Neon Abyss is a solidly built game that is very satisfying to play. After putting about 6 hours into the pre-release demo, I bought this game seconds after release and have not been disappointed. It may not be the most original game, but it's just FUN. I have faith that the developers will release more content to expand the complexity of interactions available in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: GOOD, BAD, UGLYI'm not recommending this game with the caveat that in the future with some work it could be great. I'll wait for patches before revisiting.THE GOODThe game has a high level of polish. The design aspects and vaporwave aesthetics look great. It looks like a finished product. The core mechanics are polished, requiring a good handle on situational awareness along with some enjoyable gunplay.The soundtrack hits all the right notes. It feels "cool" as you play and really builds on the universe of the game.Personally, I enjoy the bosses as a whole. While mechanically they aren't complicated and in some cases mimic one another, the sheer chaos is fun. It feels rewarding mastering a boss pattern. Not to mention they look great on screen.THE BADRuns seem to go one of two ways: you either stack up weapon upgrades and/or land a good weapon early or you get stacked with mediocre to bad passive upgrades that have no real meaningful impact on the game. The passives are uninteresting. If you don't see movement, damage, range or rate of fire upgrades, most barely move the needle on the gameplay.Enemy spawns are a problem. They will spawn where you are or will be firing as they spawn and you will take damage. At face value that's bad, but more on that below.Enemies aren't terribly varied, and the rooms themselves are just a set of platforms. You lack the ability to engage in combat when you struggle on the Y axis due to limits in jump height and character speed, and in many cases you are simply swarmed as a result of beginning in a corner of a room with no chance to move to safety. Alternatively some rooms you never see any danger as you fire comfortably from above or below. Neither is a good look.Your hitbox is obviously larger than your character. On many occasions you will move or jump in reaction to a projectile in a tight window only to be hit by said projectile. You will see it happen and you will scratch your head.Large rooms with enemies that blink to your location are frustrating, offering no chance to be mentally prepared beyond simply spamming jump when you enter the room. Enemies off screen engage without your knowledge. This is probably the least frustrating aspect of this game.THE UGLYThe game relies on a core mechanic of managing one of two types of bars. Purple is "Wisdom" which when full offers a teleport to a room to decide between items. The alternative is "Violence" which operates in a similair vein, only you sacrifice health for a chance at an upgrade. Wisdom is managed by using crystals and avoiding damage. Violence by shooting crystal objects and taking damage when touching them/taking damage in rooms in general.This would be fine were it not for the way these items you can shoot would not spawn right after a firefight right where you are shooting. Once you shoot a crystal chest, you are now practically locked in on the violence path, which removes your agency. Your pets that follow you will also shoot these crystal items, a system you have next to no control over. Plainly speaking: it's bad design.The pet system, ooooh the pet system. You will obtain eggs that will hatch (or not) as you clear rooms. Some of these pets are highly beneficial, providing cover from bullets or killing enemies themselves. The real problem comes from negative pets, and as this is a core mechanic to the game, it's just awful for gameplay.Some pets will snatch up coins before you see them, offering little in return. Some will take hearts, offering a degraded version that can harm you. Some toss grenades constantly, creating a chaotic situation where you are bounced (not damaged) around creating poor positioning you could not control. You have no control over this. You either get lucky or don't. That is one of the most infuriating aspects of this title.Runs either snowball into laughable boomfests or devolve into a long, drawn out but inevitable demise. While that can be the case with some titles in this genre, the best reward players for fighting through the pain and coming out the other side. You CAN win any run, but it feels far less likely than a standard poor Isaac run given all of the other issues around it.

_childDocuments_.review: is a roguelike arcade action game in the vein of , , or , although its clear strongest influence is .  Specifically, on the surface it plays like " does :" it's a 2D side-scrolling platformer with firing the player's  firearm mapped to the right stick or mouse, with light platforming and resource management metagames.Artistically, the game is striking but inconsistent; the whole thing has a vague "vaporwave nightclub" aesthetic with rave glowsticks festooning Grecian statues and columns, in service of a very barebones plot about how new techno-Gods representing modern ills like pharmaceuticals, fast food, beauty tips, and TikTok have supplanted the old Greek pantheon.  You're an agent of those old deific powers killing the new Gods so that the old Gods can reign once more.  The designs of the new Gods are very chaotic and imaginative, with a squishy feel to them similar to the work of Paul Robertson, and their designs are where the game gets closest to 's intentional grossness.  As a side effect, the game practices an implicit traditionalist dogma -- [sic]  -- but because the theming is so lightweight, loose, and inconsistent, it manages to dodge feeling like a weird Twitter trad with an anime profile pic most of the time.The game's economy is easy to summarize, and also where I run into problems with it.•  are your standard 'blaster,' have limitless ammo, and determine your attack pattern.  You can only have one, and picking up a new gun drops your old one.•  are the primary currency, can be stacked limitlessly, and are used to participate in minigames or purchase things in the shop, just like in .•  are thrown to damage enemies or (more frequently) blow up obstacles, just like in .•  can open locked chests and doors, again just like in .•  hatch into little companion characters called  who perform a simple automatic behavior to aid the player, just like the babies in .•  are a secondary currency after Coins.  You have a very low cap (5) of Crystals, and they can be used both to unlock special crystal-only doors and chests in place of keys, or to power certain items and abilities that rely on Crystals.  The low cap encourages you to keep them in constant rotation; they're "use 'em or lose 'em."  Crystals are the game's main addition to the  formula, aside from turning it from a top-down  arcade shoot-em-up into a side-scrolling  arcade shoot-em-up.And lastly...•  are objects of power that can be purchased from shops or a key-gated item room, which give the player additional powers, modifiers, and abilities.  There are hundreds and hundreds of items, allowing for theoretically tens of thousands of combos.  Exciting, right?In practice, not really.Where  hugely flounders is that many of its items follow a rote, formulaic design approach that frankly isn't exciting.  In  or comparable games, many items feel like a radical modifier that changes something observable like shot pattern or consumable logic, with a fair amount of filler that just do simple stat-ups or background effects like "gain a damage-up for every key you have."  In ,  items follow this kind of stat-futzy, "filler" approach.  Typically, when I pick up an item, it does something like "you can use bombs in place of keys when you're out of keys," or "when you use a bomb, there's a 25% chance to gain a key" or "when you use a crystal, there's a 10% chance to gain a coin."  In aggregate these are marginally useful effects that give you more options in how you navigate the dungeon, but they don't  substantial, in large part because individually each effect is so niche and so background.  There are a  items that radically change playstyle, like the rare item that lets you fly instead of jumping, but the  majority of all items in the game follow this simple economics-manipulation model that makes them feel like they were designed by filling out quotas on a spreadsheet.In , like in other games of this genre, luck is more important than skill when it comes to getting the right combo of items for a successful run, but the difference is that in those games, frequently a "broken/successful" run is visually bombastic, with the player filling the screen with projectiles.  That  happen in , but more frequently it takes the form of my first "perfect run," where I got an item that let me deal more damage for every coin I had, and another item that let me spend crystals for coins, and another item that let me generate crystals on a regular timer.  I just farmed crystal-coin-damage boost until I was an unstoppable juggernaut, but there wasn't anything  interesting about it; I just fired the same basic buster bullet and demolished all the bosses.YMMV, of course.  Maybe you played  and wanted the combos to be less about cool novel effects, and more about background inventory and resource management.  But for me, despite some high points like the boss designs and aesthetics,  is a swing and a miss.

_childDocuments_.review: At this point, cannot recommend.  The game has a good start, but sadly that is about it.  I wanted to play this and for the first couple runs enjoyed it.  The overall game play quickly soured with the issues I started regularly facing.  Grenades are terrible, just terrible, to rare, to hard to aim, and far to necessary.  It felt to me that way over half of the chests i found required some form of explosion to access, and then also a key after. The payoff would rarely be worth the cost.  Key also suffer from being overly rare.  Chests should have a minimal amount of value.  opening a chest to receive 1 gold feels bad man, and it happens way to often.  The items are overly repetitive.  In a single run my first three item rooms gifted me with flight items.  Flight is a great ability and i like the way i changes the game, but you do not need three different items giving the same ability.   It is worse when you start to notice how many of the items are just a mix of a couple different modifiers such as "weapon lvl up" and "increases weapon dmg".  There are many items that are just bad or useless.  While i do think that games like this should have some bad items that you need to decide whether to take or not.  In most other games that this mimics, the "bad" items just tend to be the ones that are hard to synergize with, but in rare circumstances can help win you the game.  Here some of the items are just absolutely useless (literally any of the "small chance to gain [consumable] when [egg/pet] does [x]" items).  Worst of all has been the constant run killing bugs.  Couple of examples have been the game locking itself in a minimized state, getting stuck in between rooms. and random controller disconnects.  With no save system, your run will just be over.... at least you can take the metaprogession coin back to the bar.... but you cant buy anything because the bar is glitched out because I'm using a controller.  So, then i need to restart again in keyboard mode in order to make any purchases... I would estimate about 40% of the runs ended this way.  All i can say is this game has potential... but it needs work...BAD.FAMILIARS NEED TO BE DISMISSABLE!!!!
