_childDocuments_.review: Neon Abyss has the potential to become a great game, but it is not there yet. While I have had a lot of fun playing so far, I would definitely recommend waiting for an update before buying the game. I'll try and list out some of the things I like and the things that I think really need to be addressed before the game is worth buying.Pros:-I like the idea of gun leveling. This makes it so that even the starting gun can be a viable weapon and also creates a feel of progression even if using the same gun for a whole run.-I like the basis of the angel and devil system and I think that being able to choose which path to go for makes for an interesting game mechanic.Cons: -The level and enemy variety are extremely small. It is basically impossible to tell what level you are on without looking at the transitions between levels. -The unlock system is not very fun. Unlocking things is done by using yellow crystals which drop whenever you defeat a boss. The cheapest that an unlock costs is 5 crystals and many two times that. With a full run bringing about 7-9, that means that sometimes it can take forever to unlock even a single item. Beyond that unlocking items this way isn't very interesting and makes progression feels too grindy (as opposed to objective-based unlocks like in the Binding of Isaac).-I am not a fan of the egg system. Eggs hatch into tiny companions that have a variety of effects. The problem with the system is that the effectiveness of these companions vary and are sometimes actually actively harm your run. In addition, you get so many eggs in a single run that it is hard to really keep track of which companions you have. This also makes it very hard to intentionally keep them alive or use them in any meaningful way.  The eggs seem like something that could be an interesting mechanic, but ended up being something that I ended up mostly ignoring.-The chest system seems very unbalanced. Both keys and bombs are a scarce resource on many runs and spending an entire key or bomb in order to open a chest seems like it should be pretty rewarding, but chests never seem to contain anything worth the price. Using up valuable resources only to get an egg or a couple purple crystals makes it so that the trade is rarely, if ever, worth it.-Upgrades lack oomph. The most useful upgrades are usually just straight up stat increases. Apart from the popcorn item that causes your bullets to explode or the item that creates a mine every time you jump, there seems to be a severe lack of "zaniness". Yes you have upgrades that give you flight or extra jumps, but too many of them seem to be "give you random consumable if you get enough kills or when your egg or pets hatch." Most upgrades have very little change on the feel of a run and if it weren't for how each different gun acts, it would be hard to tell one run from another. -This may sound like a small issue but the angel system seems too delicate. It only takes a single shot to turn an any angel device, door, or chest into its devil form. This would be fine except for the fact that enemy bullets also affect them too, meaning that even if you avoid shooting at them, they may still be changed just because an enemy shot at you.Smaller Issues:-The use key is bound to the same button as melee attack. This wouldn't be a big problem if it weren't for the fact that angel devices turn into devil devices on a single hit. This has caused me on multiple occasions to attack the angel device when I am actually trying to activate it.-Without upgrades most characters have very little movement options. This is a problem because a lot of the boss patterns seem to be balanced in a way that makes it extremely hard to avoid hits without movement upgrades.-Active abilities are directly tied to guns. This is more personal preference but I feel like this definitely affects run variety, as there are many guns that either don't have an active ability or the ability is not worth using in most cases. -The hitbox to collect items is too small. In order to pick up an item you have to be at the same exact level as the item. This is  most noticeable when you have flight and can only pick up coins with your feet.tldr: Neon Abyss has potential but is held back by a severe lack of variety and poorly implemented mechanics. With a few changes the game become one of the greats but I would not recommend buying the game in its current state.(Disclaimer: The devs have begun to try and fix some of these problems in their experimental test branch, but seeing as the changes have not made it into the real game yet, I have not taken those changes into account within this review.)

_childDocuments_.review: Edit again: I want to like this game, but there are just so many small things that drive me crazy. The biggest annoyance for me if how much this game relies on difficulty through obfuscation, which I find incredibly frustrating. Even things which the game does tell you are not presented particularly well and are often very easy to miss. Just poor UX. The end of a challenge room sometimes drops 2 items that you pick between, but it's only a small portion of the time, and there is absolutely no indication that you can only pick one.After defeating all enemies its still possible to take damage, but if you hatch an egg the game covers up half your screen. There is a method to ban enemies, and there is literally a single enemy I would like to ban. Can't find it in the list of enemies. Can I not ban this enemy? Who knows. Feedback from being hit is not good, and late game visual clarity is awful. There is a menu where you cannot navigate down from the top menu item and have to go up to get to the bottom.Edit: I saw an update to the game and decided to give it another go. There is now a lot more content and the runs feel much more distinctive than they did at release. Overall, a lot of positive changes and a big improvement IMO. I think the core gameplay loop is fun, but a lot of the roguelike systems around it could use some work. Early gun variety sucks, with several guns that just seem worse than the starter gun. The progression system seems off to me, since most of the unlocks are for potential new items and you need to use a currency to get unlocks. Yes, you get to try the item the first time you unlock it, but that seems like a pretty lackluster reward to me. If I need to grind for currency I would like to see tangible upgrades with my unlocks. I much prefer seeing new items locked behind challenges and achievements. I feel like the biggest problem is that there's a ton of overlap between item effects, with many different items that give a small damage boost or extra health. Very few of the item upgrades really feel special or unique as a result and they all just feel like minor stat upgrades. Hopefully some of the later items are more interesting, but if that is the case, then I think gating the interesting items was a mistake.

_childDocuments_.review: To me, what makes or breaks a Roguelike are two thing: How many hours can I get out of it and how easy it is to break the game with some insane build. This game lacks both.First of all, it's deceivingly short. You start with 5 stage that eventually grow up to 9. They're pretty straightforward and very rarely will a combination of stage and enemies be tough enough for you to be scared so it gets boring really fast. The hours of time I logged into this was to reach all the way to the alternate bosses but I left it after that because I can't find any motivation to get back into it.Second, you don't have enough time to become powerful enough to really enjoy this game. Yes, there are weapons and items that are insanely OP (like with every Roguelike) but the issue here is that, even if you manage to buy everything in the shops, pass all challenges for bonuses and get every power up in front of you, by the time you reach the final bosses it still doesn't feel like you're very powerful and it's a struggle. The amount of items here is crazy but it's a perfect example that quantity doesn't equal quality.All in all, as far of Roguelikes go, this one doesn't cut it for me. If the stages were longer and tougher BUT with a highest amount of powerup drops and more combinations that make you hilariously OP after a while, then I would be more behind it but as of now I don't really like it, I don't care for its DLC and I don't recommend it.I don't want to leave without saying anything positive so I'll say the graphics and design style are great. The music is good and some of the item rooms are very clever and fun. It's obvious the people behind this game are very creative so I congratulate them for it. Hopefully in the future we'll agree on another creation of theirs

_childDocuments_.review: I wish i could say it's a good game. i really could.strange controls, (cough cough, f to throw grenade), gravity pulls a bit strong for a bullet hell game with this camera angle, making it super hard to dodge anything, health drops are rare in a bullet hell game, 90% of chests that steal health if shot are accidentally shot before you know it exists, the more fun way of getting extra items requires taking a ♥♥♥♥ ton of damage and also steals max health from you, crystals are so abundant that you end up leaving floors with 50 of them on the floor because the game rarely generates ways to use crystals, etc.you can go roughly 20 rooms without finding any money. when you do, it's about 3 cents. you need about 100 to buy a single item, and that price only increases over time. there's enemies that simply appear under you without any visual cues, audio cues, or anything, they simply appear. those enemies also shoot bullets in every single direction after appearing. oh? that isn't the only enemy to do that?items? garbagió. most guns(that you spend a whole run's worth of money on) are something like "hmm, your starting gun, but ummm, it fires 2 bullets at once, each dealing 51% of the normal bullet's damage."there's a ton of non-gun items that do the exact same, and ones that actually are fun are way too rare to even consider praying for.fun fact, almost every single egg i've opened has had literally nothing inside of it. no money, no pet, not even a single speck of anything that might do anything.another issue i have is how strange it is to move about in a room, and many times you have to do so while under constant fire to reach the last enemy in the room, which promptly teleports across the room.DID I MENTION THE COPIOUS AMOUNT OF BUGS? _childDocuments_.review: Neon Abyss is a great little rouge crawler. Distancing itself from the traditional fantasy elements of the genre and embracing a futuristic neon retro-80s feel and art style with a good sound track to boot. Though the game had a bit of a rough start on release the dev team are very kind and hard working, releasing new content and updates all the time. Bugs are taken seriously and fixed in reasonable time and suggestions are seriously considered, resulting in new bosses and extended levels for longer gameplay per session. With lots of items and numerous weapons to create varied combos and play styles Neon Abyss is good choice if you are looking to get familiar with RNG rogue dungeon genre, though veterans may feel the game is too easy. (Personally, I think they need to finish the game on Insane mode before they have the right to call it easy. Most haven't.)I do ask the dev team to kick whoever it was that thought the Abyssal Veteran achievement (999 dives into the game) was a good idea. It wasn't. I hate you, specifically.

_childDocuments_.review: My playtime is higher, but since I started out as a pirate it doesn't show xDSo far I enjoy this a lot more than i.e Dead Cells, even with the small quirks that are currently present.The biggest annoyance right now is one of the pets can/will block your shots, and if they explode on impact, you'll take damage.Depending on the weapon it might even constantly block it, so you have a short beam shooting out and you're unable to kill enemies.Enemies can spawn close to the entry point, so if you rush in (just a handful of frames) it'll hit you no matter what + some enemies like to despawn (mechanics) and respawn right on top of you - Super annoying.People gripe about how grindy it is - It's a Roguelike game.. That's the nature of the game.People whine about the price not being worth the current content - It just released: Give it time.The music is AMAZING, the various items can be GODLIKE and really complement a run.There's a good selection of weapons, and various characters to choose from.There's a violence/wisdom meter which leads to a "Secret Area" (Wisdom = Find a crystal door, or "crystal cache/thingy-ma-jig" or a chest and insert crystals in it. Violence = shoot said crystal things, bump into them and take damage and that'll fill your violence meter) that acts as a bonus item room.I've made it up to the 4th boss/manager and there's still more to come.There's a, sort of, skill tree that'll unlock certain benefits or 1-run only items.I'm pleased with having spent 19.99£ on it - I haven't made this big of a steal since the latest Yakuza game released, or getting the new SUPERHOT game for free <3

_childDocuments_.review: 7.5/10Neon Abyss is a rogue-like platform shooter that is a combination between the Binding of Isaac and Enter the Gungeon. The game is really fun and there is quite a lot of GAME content, but there are a few things that bother me:1. There aren't enough weapon drops or even weapons as a matter of fact.2. _childDocuments_.review: While this review is indeed still positive; Neon abyss is a mediocre game at best.To keep things short I would say only buy this game at a heavy discount and if you are a real roguelike/lite fan.There are some things the game certainly does well such as adding a neat feature to disable a small amount of enemies from future runs, or being able to collect small lore cards troughout your runs. Furthermore a lot of weapons are pretty cool or have cool effects going on.The general gameplay and artwork is decent as well, the story is kinda neat too.But this is pretty much where all the positives end, everything else in the game is just mediocre or downright frustrating.I got all major unlocks in the game and have almost all achievements, meanwhile I also took notes of most issues I found.So lets list them all in a wall of misery!- The game has decent music, issue is that it often feels like there are only 3 songs most of the time- A bunch of bosses suddenly spawn in bossrooms and have a high chance to telefrag you when they spawn in, getting a free hit unless you memorise where each boss spawns.- Very low enemy variety, most are just previous versions of themselves but they fire an extra projectile or something as an example.- Some of the lowest variety between floors I've seen in a roguelike/lite, almost feels like recolors at times.- Certain endgame special bosses have annoying requirements to reach them, making getting certain endings you may want to get on a run often impossible.- You can upgrade your weapons 8 times with items, these items upgrade all your weapons you have and pick up in the future, yet these items keep dropping after reaching weapon level 8. These upgrades replace other rare item drops and thus can screw you over in the long run if unlucky.- Probably the biggest problem in the game is that while a lot of the player weapons look pretty awesome at times, many weapons absolutely FILL the screen with their projectiles/beams etc. to an extent that most of all hits you take in the entire game are from enemy projectiles turning invisible because your own projectiles just completely overlap everything. - There are a bunch of difficulty settings which is neat, sadly the actual difference between all difficulties is quite minor.- The majority of enemy visual design is just goofy at best and uninspired at most.All things said and done, Neon Abyss is very mediocre but I guess it is still good enough to warrant a positive review.
_childDocuments_.name: Neon Abyss

_childDocuments_.review: Ehhhhhh. The game itself definitely pulls you in. The desire to collect all of your hard earned rewards in each room, to progressively annihilate your enemies as you become more powerful - it's very addicting.Dying is part of making progress in the game, which is FINE, except for that you must start at level 1 after each time you die. Once you've beaten a boss on levels 5, 6, 7, it becomes very cumbersome to start all the way over again, and compulsively have to re-upgrade yourself each run. You waste a lot of time doing that because you want to be as prepared as possible for the final boss you have to beat this round.  The rewards you can buy are quite silly as well. The game runs off of collecting basic resources (keys, gems, bombs, coins, hearts, shields). All of the upgrades you purchase with your hard-earned death money go into carnival-like game add ons that just throw these resources at you in different ways, which doesn't solve the earlier problem of wasting so much time on the early levels of the game over and over. I got it on sale, and it's fun, but I wouldn't pay full price

_childDocuments_.review: It's with a heavy heart that give this game a thumbs down.  It has the foundation to be a great, great game but, as others have stated, it feels very, very incomplete.  While it's common to come across games on Steam that are all but complete but masquerade as Early Access titles to avoid criticism, Neon Abyss flips the script and is an Early Access game masquerading as a full release.It has all the signs of being a game that isn't finished.  There's a "boss tree" that stops unlocking new bosses after number 4 despite having visual displays for at least 2 more.  There's huge balancing issues(enemies that teleport to your location, deal contact damage and give no visual indicator that you're in danger...rng "followers" that actively make you worse...etc.)  There's game breaking bugs(you can't spend your "crystals" to unlock new weapons if you don't use your mouse as the first input the game recognizes upon startup.)  There's no ending, even in the loosest sense of the word.The game has tons of potential, but it's not there yet.  There's an "experimental branch" that claims to have hotfixes attached, but unlike games that properly label themselves as "Early Access", I didn't pay for a game listed as a full release just to act as a beta tester.  Keep an eye on the game and see if its issues are resolved.  If they are, it's worth a purchase as it could turn into a gem.  Right now, however, it's just a disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: There are better roguelikes out there.Neon Abyss starts off as a really fun game. For the first ten hours or so, I loved what I was playing. As the game went on though, the flaws became very apparent and ruined my enjoyment of the game.Gameplay:Running and shooting enemies is fun for the most part. Attacks make sense, and every enemy attack pattern can be learned. Melee weapons on the other hand, are effectively worthless on anything but the weakest of enemies. Hitboxes on melee weapons never felt like they worked correctly, and these weapons rarely did enough extra damage to be worth it.Getting Stronger:The fun of every roguelike comes from the crazy items and synergies built up over a run. Neon Abyss has a very respectable 400 items to play around with. However, acquiring the items is just as important as the items themselves, and this is where the game falls apart completely for me. Typically, each floor has an item room with a choice between two items, a shop which sells one gun and one item, a boss room that drops a stat boosting item, an arena which may pay out with an item, and minigames that pay out with items. Oh, the minigames...The minigames destroy the balance of the game entirely. These games are all timing based and have nothing to do with the core gameplay of Neon Abyss. This would be fine as a distraction, but these minigames pay out with items on every victory. Some of these minigames can be played over three times per floor, allowing for insane amounts of items in one run.Characters:Every single character felt the same to me. Each character has a slightly different starting weapon as well as a unique ability. Outside of the character who could carry two guns, I never found these unique abilities to be particularly useful and was more successful when I just ignored them completely. I fail to see the purpose of alternate characters if they don't have anything substantial to differentiate themselves from the default.I want to like this game, but I find it really hard to enjoy it when it feels like every run comes down to blind luck and hoping I don't botch the super hard timing minigames to get items. Maybe it's just a skill issue on my part, but this game felt like it leaned too far in the luck based direction for my liking.

_childDocuments_.review: Great Game! I'm having quite a blast. High difficulty has 3 grades and on the third one, it's a helluva ride!A lot of people compare this freshly out of the oven game to Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth+, without recalling that there was a Binding of Isaac 16 bits that came out first and 3 major expansions/releases after to become as polished and finished as it is now.Well, Neon Abyss is in the state of the Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth (no +). It has a wide variety of Weapons, which some uses Crystals, Coins, or just have a Cooldown before reuse. Passive items are affected by your Keys, Coins, Crystals, Pets, Bombs (Grenades), Hearts, Shields, name it. So it's up to you to get the best balance between your actual Ressources and reinforcing your Damage/Fire Rate by having More or Less of said Ressources.Make the most out of each playthrough, although, sometimes it might backfire. Rockets have impressive damage and blast destructible... your face is also destructible. You'll learn it the hard way and curse as much as I do when I forget.On the down sides, the game has some bugs, nothing game breaking so far and nothing too frustrating. You will learn to play with Explosives. But first, you will think it's the game's fault, not yours. I did it, until I gut gud. Some mecanics need some tweekings and balancing, but that's to be expected on a brand new game. The music, although matching the universe created here, could have more variety, based on the different "biomes". It's mostly 2 musics (neutral state / combat state) + a Boss battle.More content is expected in the (near?) future, which is great news as this game has a lot to offer.The mini games are a great addition and I'd recommend the Devs to develop the current ones a bit more (more classical tunes, for example. I've seen/heard 3 and I doubt there're more) before creating new Mini Game rooms.24 hours in, still discovering new Enemies, Rooms, Weapons and have about 30% of the Unlocks (and probably 0 big game twist ending secret that I'll discover when finishing with all characters on Hard Grade 3)I love it, so should you!

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the few reviews where I wish there was a "Meh" button. Fundamentally, it's a good game. However, if you are a veteran or you're familiar with the rougelike/rougelite genre, then you might as well skip this one and play something better like Hades or Isaac. This game is a baby's first rougelike given how much the game gives you per run and how easy the game is in general. Other than that, the game has it's flaws. The runs don't feel much special, the gameplay gets a bit generic at times, unlocking features is a bit tedious, the guns don't really feel special the more you collect, the game pampers you with so much upgrades, etc... But yeah, not a bad game, but not really a good one either the more you play. If you're new to the genre, go ahead and try this game, but like I said, you could play other better one's like Hades. If you really want to get this game, I'd say wait for a sale. The game isn't really worth 20 bucks as of now due to the flaws and how easy and bland it is.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an average game but I'm pushing it into Not Recommended due to a few more negatives then positives.  The positives are music and visuals of the game with a well done neon/techno aesthetic that becomes a bit dungeony near the end of runs.   The gameplay is somewhat addictive and fun for a while; I usually don't like joystick shooters but this game did it very well.   The negatives are the items not getting descriptions when you're trying to decide what to take, no thank you I don't want to memorize all the effects of the hundred guns and hundreds of power ups.   The guns and power ups are honestly kinda lame and not as creative as you'd expect.  There is maybe a plot, I'm not sure and I think neither is the designer.  The alternative characters are mostly so bland I wonder why they're included.  The worst negative is the screen often gets filled up with so many projectiles both from you, your little ally things and from enemies that you can't dodge them because you literally can't see them, that's just poorly designed at a certain point.  I'd be willing to overlook those negatives because the game is somewhat fun, but then i beat some bosses and did some stuff and the achievements for it didn't work.  Call me a sucker I don't care but I do actually care about showing what I've done in games and most games get this to work without a problem. Get it on sale for a bit of fun, but overall you'll just end up getting frustrated trying to complete obtuse requirements to get to certain bosses and by the lack of visual clarity and sucky sidegrade enhancements or suddenly becoming a God if you get some of the busted enhancements.

_childDocuments_.review: At first I wasn't too sure if I liked this game.  It does start a bit slow, I didn't understand the value of exploring, and I found the mini-games to get bonus items and weapons overly difficult.After playing much more, I absolutely love this game and highly recommend it!  The pace picks up very quickly whenever you get a new weapon.  Exploration is heavily rewarded.  They have a genius teleporting system that allows you to bounce between explored rooms every 2-3 rooms, which makes back-tracking a breeze.  There are tons of items, weapons, and pets to acquire.  The colours are beautiful, the sound effects are awesome.  And before long you become an overpowered wrecking machine.  Upgrades between levels unlock more characters and special rooms.  Once you get the hang of the mini game rooms they become quite easy to get very powerful abilities and weapons from.  The RNG in this game isn't that bad at all.  If you fully explore every floor you will become overpowered very quickly.  The challenge seems right on the money, not too hard, not too easy.This is also fun to play with the kids and is kid friendly.Would recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: I've follwed Neon Abyss for a bit and was quite hopeful that while I generally loath platformers, that it would win me over and I'd have tons of fun. It appeared to have lots going for it--touting things like; numerous unlocks, numerous weapons, abilities and just general content to entertain you for months if not years all while having some of the best looking pixel artwork ever. Color me interested! It sounded like a perfect match for me. This game would of greatly benefited going into Early Access first rather than just releasing. Everything about it feels unpolished. Menu's are bare bones. Settings are bare bones. There is no stat tracking--anywhere. Oh.. There is a bestiary I've found but like everything else this game offers; requires many many hours of grinding to unlock. Level variety feels the same and is lacking. Enemy variety suffers this as well. Bosses largely feel uninspired and tacked on. There's lots of unnecessary cluttter going on during encounters from the bullets, debris and enemies jumping up all around. Each enemies bullets take on different colors and patterns making it hard to dodge/counter and only serve to frustrate the hell out of you. Music for the game is lackluster--generic techno that only serves to keep an tempo. The ability variety you'll unlock as you play is limited and doesn't change playstyles enough to make much difference. Pets, one of the supposed mechanics to separate this game & define this title from others in the same genre are sadly just standard abilities with fancy skins slapped on. They also suffer the same issues that your standard abilities do in that they lack variety and make little difference to your run except that they have an added nuance in the 'hatching' mechanic. There's more characters to unlock but they don't vary enough to be impactful and lack incentive for you to unlock and the main nail in the coffin for me with this game is..All the bad reviews about this game being grindy hold up. It's a grind fest. It's yet another roguelite game that somehow got insanely good reviews for terrible mechanics-- This game, like Gunfire Reborn is just a grind to win game.. grind until your eye's explode game.. grind until you grind so much you develop stockholms syndrome and begin to enjoy grinding so much--game...At least with Gunfire Reborn, there's a little bit of incentive added. You know for sure after you expend months of your precious life you'll beat that game, not on skill, not on wit, but because you're a savage that not only throws away money, but precious time of their life too! I don't know if you'll get the easy, cheesy win after you do all you can do with this game, that remains to be seen and I am not going to find out. I just loath that it's like this and wish people would stop praising games--especially ones attempting to be 'rogue-anything' for using them. I've talked enough--let's get down to the nitty gritty of things.   I am disappointed to say the least as I did have higher expectations that what we got here. I rarely give bad reviews and I am not quite sure this really deserves one-- I will say, don't just write this game off. I am going to hold faith that devs will put in some extra work, some additional polish and make this game worth it's entry price and hope you do too. It's got a lot of potential and a great foundation to build on. I WILL definitely recommend you follow the game and watch to see what gets added over time. Just as far as throwing $20 on it, I do not recommend it yet--hopefully soon--just not yet. Needs more time in the oven unfortunately.

_childDocuments_.review: While I have enjoyed some of this game and would prefer to give it a neutral review, I'm skewed towards the negative.This game is very much like Binding of Isaac, sharing many of the positives and all of the negatives.It also tries to put its own spin on a lot of it, ultimately coming out all the worse for it.Take the 2D perspective for example, while it has been shown to work by plenty of other roguelikes, Neon Abyss' characters limited mobility, bad level design and unfair enemy placement/types make it significantly less fun. It takes many elements of all of these things directly from BoI without really considering how well it works in 2D, resulting in an overall frustrating experience.Run variety, one of the most important factors of a roguelike and something that BoI in particular excels at, is also abysmal in Neon Abyss. The reasons for this are the lack of item variety and Neon Abyss trying to reinvent the wheel with new systems.Guns in particular significantly limit variety, where in BoI you just had basic tear projectiles to start with, you had a wide variety of items that completely transformed how they work and look, in Neon Abyss that is mostly achieved with guns.There are many different guns that all work somewhat differently, however they have very little synergy with items.You can get items that increase damage, projectiles, range, firing speed or add a chance to shoot additional projectiles with different properties, however your gun will still fire the same mechanically.For some this is a positive as you can always just switch your gun out for a different one mid-run, but ultimately this significantly limits item variety as none of them can fundamentally change how you fire each gun.Another thing Neon Abyss takes and ruins from BoI is the familiar system. In Binding of Isaac there was a category of items that granted you a (most of the time) invulnurable familiar that followed you and helped you in various ways, like shooting enemies or dropping items for you.Neon Abyss instead has the egg system, where you can pick up egg pickups that over the course of a couple of cleared rooms have a chance to become a familiar. these familiars work in much the same as BoI aside from one key difference: they can be killed. Whether it be by enemies, projectiles or traps, if your familiar takes enough damage it will die and that's that. This feels like a complete downgrade from the familar system in the most frustrating ways. Eggs more often than not fail to hatch, and even when they do, chances are the familiar you get isn't any good anyways, and even on the off chance that they are, if you aren't particularly careful and having a great run, they'll get killed anyways.Finally a third feature that I feel is a straight up worse version of something in BoI is the faith system.Where in BoI you had Devil Rooms and Angel Rooms, special post-boss rooms that rewarded you for not taking any damage per floor with great items, Neon Abyss exchanges that for a faith system.Now you have to rely on crystal items (chests, doors, etc.) to get the process going, where you activate said item with crystals that you pick up to fill up the "angel" side of the bar, or damage it and let it deal damage to you to fill up the "devil" side of the bar.You can then also fill up said bar by either not taking any damage for each cleared room for the angel side, or taking damage each room for the devil side. This would not be an issue at all save for one important detail, only one side of the bar can exist at a time.As you might strive for angel rooms as those align with not wanting to take damage anyway, you might happen to accidentally damage a crystal item, either by shooting it mid-fight with enemies or having your familiars shoot it with no input from you. This results in your faith bar instead getting changed to the devil side with a lot less of the bar filled up, essentially wasting all your effort and forcing you to either abandon that mechanic until you find another crystal and start over or force yourself to keep taking damage for devil rooms.This is one of the most frustrating aspects of the game.As you keep trying to do no damage runs for extra items, which is already frustrating enough with the level design and enemies in this game, now you also have to contend with crystals being obstacles in every other stage where your already flawed and fragile familiars are now an active threat to your run.This is a major issue in a game like this that heavily relies on items to make it fun and exciting, when the vast majority of the ones you get being nearly useless or incredibly situational, every chance at an additional item is crucial for having a good time and saving a run.This could have very well been a great game but the devs insisted on trying to change mechanics that already worked incredibly well in their main inspiration for significantly worse versions of themselves, making this game a lot more frustrating than it is fun.If you don't mind bashing your head against the wall for that one god run where you destroy everything then this might be for you, otherwise save yourself the trouble and find another roguelike.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon Abyss is overall a really fun new roguelite. It has a really awesome visual style and really awesome music and the gameplay is a mix between Binding of Isaac and Enter the Gungeon.You can find different weapons and passive items that make you even stronger and the items synergize together really well. You can make some crazy gun combinations just like in Binding of Isaac.The movement is a little stiff but I got used to it after awhile.There is a really cool gimmick with finding eggs that hatch into pets, the only problem is that late game they can actually be harmful so it kind of defeats the purpose of them.My biggest complaint with the game is that the progression is obnoxiously grindy. It takes like 5-6 hours of just beating the same bosses over and over and over again to unlock new characters and it makes it feel like you aren't actually making much progress. Also there is day 1 DLC which is super scummy in my opinion.Overall this game is fun if you only expect to have a max of like 25ish hours of playtime. This does not have the replayability of say, Binding Of Isaac that could keep you playing for thousands of hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon Abyss is a roguelike shooter that combines a modern cyberpunk aesthetic with an environmental setting inspired by Greek mythology. You start of at the Cerberus bar where you can unlock new gameplay mechanics and characters, browse through your unlocked items and pets, select your character and do some other nifty things (like dancing).Runs are started by jumping down into the abyss, where you will face randomized rooms filled with various enemies, treasures, shops and puzzles throughout multiple levels in a classic rougelike manner. Every level also features a boss fight, which needs to be defeated to access the next level. As you continue playing you unlock new levels and bosses, as well as cursed forms of previous bosses that require following certain paths to be accessed. When it comes to gameplay mechanics, Neon Abyss doesn't reinvent the wheel, but that isn't a requirement for an enjoyable roguelike in my opinion. You collect keys which are used to open locks and bombs which are used to blow stuff up.Health comes in the forms of heart containers as well as shields, with shields being used up first. An interesting mechanic are pets, which players can hatch from eggs found across the levels. These eggs hatch after clearing a few rooms but might fail to hatch as well. Pets come in various forms, from protective pets to offensive pets and also in the form of pets that collect certain pickups and drop other stuff in exchange. These pets can also level up and become stronger throughout the run, however they also come with their own health and therefore can die.Killing bosses drops a badge that cycles through various upgrades and boosts your stats in certain ways depending on the badge you end up grabbing.There are hundreds of different items to be founds and a fair amount of guns as well, however many of the guns exist in multiple forms which end up being the exact same gun but with different active effects. I found quite a few of the guns to be very annoying to use because of strange bullets patterns and because every gun exists in multiple forms you ultimately end up with not thaaat many different guns for a shooter roguelike. When killing bosses you unlock faith gems which are used to unlock new gameplay mechanics, rooms, secrets and characters in the aforementioned bar. Each character comes with 2 different "costumes" (if you own the respective DLC) that also grant them different abilities and i found the character variety to be pretty neat, some of them come with very unique playstyles.However, the part where Neon Abyss falls pretty short is the end game in my opinion. Some of the late game content seems a little rushed and most of the cursed bosses are just different forms of former bosses that feel like bullet sponges in most runs. To get to these cursed bosses you also need to rely on RNG to some degree since you need to follow specific requirements in every run that can easily be messed up. There also are no achievements for killing any of the end game bosses which once again reinforces the feeling of rushed end game content. Also, the screen tends to become very cluttered towards the end of runs as you find many items and pets which can make dodging very hard since you need to stop shooting to even see whats going on.Neon Abyss also has its fair share of clunky mechanics and bugs (you can't rebind all keys, weapon upgrades cycle in an annoying and unpredictable pattern, elemental effects overwrite each other, the minimap doesn't show all objects, occasional crashes when entering a new level, errors in the English translations and so on). From what I can tell the game is no longer developed and while I wouldn't call it "abandoned" it still could use quite a bit of polishing in its current state.At the end of the day this is one of those games that make me wish steam had a "mixed feelings" option besides recommending or not recommending a game. Overall I still enjoyed most of my time in the abyss and if you are a roguelike fan then you will probably find some joy in it as well. I would definitely recommend playing all the other top tier roguelikes first (such as Isaac, Spelunky & Gungeon) and if your rougelike itch still isn't satisfied then you can't go wrong with picking up Neon Abyss, although I would recommend doing so during a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Stunning visuals, amazing music, and the exact gameplay loop you want from these types of games. There are many different builds you can end up on in a run, and the most powerful ones are absolutely ludicrous. Get the right items, and the game becomes a neon explosion. A persistent upgrade tree makes every run feel rewarding, even if you lose.My only criticism is that the game encourages you to brute-force through bosses. A lot of them become trivial when you have a really powerful build going, leading to me not actually fully understanding some of the encounters because I always seem to melt them before I have to pay attention to mechanics. That can be offset by increasing to a harder difficulty, or just by enjoying the sheer chaos of feeling unstoppable.Great game, I recommend it to any roguelike and roguelite fan out there.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a number of issues with this game, but I will start with the pros to maintain good faith. The TL;DR, however, is that I wouldn't buy this for any more than 10 dollars, because the controls feel off and the chests that require explosions to open are more challenging than most enemies.Pros:+Good initial concept, the idea of cyberpunk'd Greek gods was what got me to buy the game in the first place+At the beginning of every run, you are able to fully customize difficulty, RNG seed, what items are banned from spawning, and even which enemies are able to spawn, though setting a seed manually or making too many changes to item/enemy spawning will disable achievements+The rocket launcher (or at least the only one I found in my playtime) doesn't explode when it hits walls, only enemies, which is a nice QOL thing.Cons:-I honestly did not have fun playing. I am a fan of rougelikes and roguelites in general, but the movement and gunplay in this one felt wrong. You have to pay 10 of the "floor bosses drop 2 each" currency that many of these games have to unlock the only character with a dodge ability.-The game is very easy on the Normal difficulty. The primary challenges I ran into were trying to open awkwardly placed stone chests without getting hit by my own grenades, finding out my bullets now explode and dying in the next room due to every bullet I shoot damaging me, and the occasional "You wanted to open this chest with crystals? Too bad, it's spiky now!"-The ratio of eggs that hatch to eggs that don't is very low, and when you actually manage to get a pet from the eggs, it dies in 3 or 4 hits (whether it's bullets that hit me, or bullets that hit my pet, I can't tell). Even if they were beefier, there's no way to have cute floating pets killable that doesn't feel crummy.-The final straw was when I ran into a third floor boss that was a recoloration of a first floor boss. A slightly more difficult bullet pattern, but aside from that he was just a sunburnt version of the original.

_childDocuments_.review: So the game is great, i love the aesthetic and is pretty fun, plus also some humor and references on the side is a nice touch. I only have 2 criticism for the game:1.- On the later half of any given run the chaos on the screen becomes.. too much and is hard to distinguish enemy projectiles and it becomes a bit overbearing to dodge everything, deal damage and distinguish my bullets from the enemy's, which is only made worst when you have the occasional enemy that can shot through walls so yeah.. Ideally i would like to see a better contrast from the background and the color of the enemy bullets so its easier to read the screen and react in time.2.- At the time of the review i just finished a run killing Athena (dont know if this is related) and one stage before getting to the final stage, a mistery stage appeared, so alright pretty cool, like surprises. However this was something called "chaos room" or the like, in which basically is.. f0ck any of your decisions you made through your run, you are stripped of all your power ups (except health, shields and pets) and now you have to fight any the first bosses 4 times every 3 rooms, each room you will get a random upgrade, make it through you get to a room which maybe you expect based on the sign at the start you get all your items back plus get to keep all the new ones.. no... you get a bundle of upgrades and thats it, so you have to pray the final build (which is COMPLETELY RANDOM) is equal or better in power than whatever you been building so far. WHY? WHY!? i had a disgusting awesome build, my weapon was basically a minigun of death that i tried my best to build up to the few times i got choices and then out of nowhere the little agency i could have is stripped away from me and forced to comform to whatever random roll of the dice coocked for me??WTF.. if i made it so far as to the final stage chances are im pretty happý with my build or proficent enough to have a chance at winning my run, whats this senseless idea of throwing everything out the window and force me to use whatever when i might have adopted a particular strategy early on to sustain my build up to that point and had to do sacrifices in the middle? Dont get me wrong im not salty because i lost, actually i won my run (tho it was a bit on the edge) but the sheer feeling of betrayal and sourness in my mouth completely killed off the run for me. So now i have to go into every game hoping either A) if this happens again i get a better build or B) this doesnt happen at all. So great, getting a 50% chance (allegedly) of not knowing if my knowledge of the game becomes useless around the end or god forbid, i somehow craft something weird but fun and want to try its viability towards the end game and the suddenly be like: "hahahahahaha NO"..I do recommend the game, but i honestly wish they changed this 2 main grips i have with this.

_childDocuments_.review: Game seems fun at first, but once you're over the honeymoon phase, you're hit with the realization that the game was barely QA'd. The things that are meant to appeal to you end up working against you and 80% of the time, you're being punished for things outside your control. The other 10% is your skill and the final 10% is the game being nice to you. Reading the top negative reviews will give you a detailed insight of why this game works against you as a roguelite. Not worth full price and potentially never until they change certain game mechanics (probably won't happen).Edit: It's been nearly 2 months since I left this review. Not much has been done on making the game more fun. The update seems to mainly focus on fine tuning the RNG elements of the game to just be right on the middle of being tolerant, or not fun. That's it. I don't like to throw accusations around but the devs seems to be so heavily invested in keeping their RNG mechanics over making the game have any semblance of enjoyable replayability. Whenever I try to pick this game back up and try to enjoy it, I'm frustrated right on the first level, and it doesn't get better. Killing bosses, beating runs, have barely any satisfaction in them. Only a masochist will play this game. If you like playing roguelites where you absolutely have no control over your run, go for it. What I wouldn't give to purge this game from my game list.

_childDocuments_.review: The fortunate upshot of systematically going through the exhaustive list of titles that I have on Steam and reviewing them is that I keep coming across questionable titles from unknown sources that either amaze me in their design or profoundly irritate me to no end.  does neither, really. I'm not even sure I'm going to remember this title outside of reflecting over my reviews and wondering if I did enough justice in conveying my opinion of it. is by no means a terrible title so much as it's... well, it's there. It has the unfortunate position of being played after I completed , which is infinitely a better title. Which reminds me, this title actively compares itself to  as a sort of meta-commentary within the actual game, and that in an of itself makes me want to cast aggressive criticism toward it. But I'm getting ahead of myself here.To keep it relatively brief,  is a roguelike platformer bullet-hell mash-up where you, the player, continuously progress further into the depths of some sort of dungeon to defeat the "New Gods", which are a cyber-punk mess of pun concepts realized in pixel graphics. From the outside, this concept works effectively enough, to a fault. I want to say this title feels a bit half-baked, like the developers just through things at a wall and worked with whatever stuck. The controls aren't exactly functional, and some of the menus don't react properly to pressing down without pressing up first, which seems like something that should have been fixed early on. The artistic choice works to a point, but it also becomes incredibly difficult to discern what's going on when you're trying to dodge a hail of projectiles while there's a stream of eggs following you around like the end of Snake.That is by no means the only fault that this title suffers from. The RNG that the title employs is a bit broken. You can have a dozen attempts through the dungeon where every buff is completely useless before you get a single run where you're practically set up to be completely indestructible before you complete the second floor. For instance, I had a run where the shop continuously reset, taking damage dropped money, killing things dropped more money, and explosions made money. By the end of that run, I looked like Liberace fell into a vat of technicolor acid, became supersized and ate steroids for breakfast while rainbows literally spewed out of my anus. I won't apologize for the bizarre image that might plague you from that description.With all that being said, I didn't hate the experience. I'd call it bland before I would claim that I enjoyed myself, but there were some positive aspects to the title. The music, for example, is quite well orchestrated. The weird minigames in the form of secret rooms were a pleasant change of pace from "bounce and shoot". Even with the scenery becoming an indiscernible blob of bright flashy colors and literal Easter eggs, the bosses aren't so difficult as to detract from the experience. Mind you, getting beyond the first eight bosses or so is more grind than its worth, but still.I don't really know where to put this title. I didn't hate it, but I didn't enjoy it enough to warrant a recommendation on my part. As a sale purchase it would seem fine, I suppose, but it doesn't really deserve much in terms of commendation at all when there are other titles out there that do the exact same thing but slightly better. Perhaps this title would have done better with more development time or a bit less whimsy on the developer's part.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to rate this negatively, because it has so much potential and I did enjoy it, but this game feels very incomplete. It should have released in early access, perhaps. There's been major balance issues, a lot of frustrating design decisions around negative pets and items, extremely grindy skill tree which includes unlocking other characters and not just abilities, and including temporary buffs/items in the skill tree? That feels like a major waste of an already scarce reward.But then I reached the end of the game, defeated the boss......... and there's nothing. This game has no real ending, nothing rewarding or providing a feeling of completeness once you've 'won'. All that's left is grinding to unlock other characters and rooms, and I'm not interested.Why does the Office exist above the bar? I had assumed all along that would be part of the ending or post-completion reward, but it does nothing?It just feels incomplete.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just plain fun.  The difficulty is little too easy, but that does not stop me from coming back to it quite often.  There are a million RNG items that you get to choose between when you get a power up.  However, every few runs you can still create a really focused build, and when you cant they still combine in so many ways as to keep the game fresh and fun.  Some of the items and mini games are annoying/tricky.  That said, you can customize what elements show up in your runs if you really do or dont like something.  The progression system takes the form of unlocking bonus items that show up across your runs, so you always start them feeling a bit under powered, but the more unlocks you get the faster your power level ramps up.   As stated above, you get OP fast, so the runs dont feel overly hard, though if you pick up the wrong combination of itmes, you can at times do more harm to yourself than the enemies do.  Overall this is just a lot fun to play, and for the amount of time I've spent in it, the regular price of $20US is vary fair.

Replayability is amazingEvery fan of rogue-lites should give it a try, especially when they're bored of fantasy settingThere's tons of upgrades that you can buy with currency that drops from bossesAlso there's a lot of easter eggs, even in the item descriptions! Apart from that there's great egg hatching system which is fun and random, every time you get an egg you have a chance to hatch it by completing the enemies rooms and the sprites that hatches from them give you bonuses. Game is a blast, it was in bundles before, get it and you won't regret it!

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly, I have to give this one a negative review, because the game just feels like it doesn't like the player at a few too many corners. Don't get me wrong, the overall gameplay could be a lot of fun, and maybe it will be in the future, but compared to some others in the genre this one just makes me feel like it actively wants me to not be happy. This ranges from room with 5 enemies immediately rushing you without space to dogdge and important systems like grenades, egg familiars and the violence/wisdom thing being infuriatingly designed, to actual situations where a boss seems to take no damage at all, for no apparent reason whatsoever.As it is, for this game, I just don't ever get the 'just one more run' feeling, instead I'm kinda just thinking 'I'm good for now...', and that's really strange for a roguelite.However as a positive note, the devs have started experimenting with changes in the right direction already, so I'm hopeful for the future and will change my review if the game manages to win me over again. Sadly, that day seems to be well in the future at best...

_childDocuments_.review: Neon Abyss is a 10/10 rogue-alike, neon-colored, side-scrolling platformer version of Binding of Isaac.All of BoI's mechanics & features are translated directly to the side-scrolling platformer genre and in a good way:From a locked golden door with a free item on every level to hidden rooms that need to be bombed, keys & grenades, being locked in a room until you kill all the baddies, many pick-ups & mods for your weapons that change you visually & the effects of your weapons, pre-fab rooms with proc-gen placement in the map & proc-gen filled with baddies, each level ending in a boss room, bosses aren't bullet-hell-frustrating (*ahem* Enter the Gungeon, ugh), several unlockable characters, optional use of seeds, and...The most important feeling for a rougealike to generate: that  instead of anguish when you die.Neon Abyss also goes farther than BoI and adds good features such as difficulty settings, some rooms having a minor puzzle in how you move & blow up barrels to get to extra treasure, the ability to ban items or monster types for runs, an upgrade/"skill" path to unlock features with tokens you get from boss kills all to suit your gameplay preferences.(These bits remind me of the customizations that Streets of Rogue allow, which I love.)The other important thing to mention is that movement, platforming, jumping, and aiming with the mouse all feel good. You're not too slow, you're not sluggish, the speed of everything you do/control is appropriate.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun roguelite at first, but the gameplay loop quickly becomes repetitive and boring.The game also suffers from gated progression, bad RNG mechanics, and questionable design choices.I'd recommend Binding of Isaac, Risk of Rain, Enter the Gungeon, Dead Cells, or Gunfire Reborn to name a few alternatives.

_childDocuments_.review: Great rogue shooter. Plenty of weapons and pets to collect, mini games are great too. The game can get a bit repetitive at times as you'll notice the same room layouts and enemies. It can be hard in the early stages to manage the resources as you can spend valuable coins on a weapon that is terrible as there's no indication of what it does beforehand. The RNG can be brutal too with low key/nade runs, this results in a lot of running back and fourth trying to find the best way to use the utility which makes an already bad run drag on too long. Overall worth a go if you like rogue style games and can pick it up in the humble bundle.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon Abyss is a side-scrolling rogue-like platformer that shamelessly rips off The Binding of Isaac. And that's exactly what makes it worth playing. It has similar itemization, similar room types, floor layouts, health system, followers, pickups, and characters. Unfortunately, it's not executed as well as Isaac. It does a poor job at rewarding the player's game knowledge, some questionably useful items, poor transformations, and less variety in room layouts, floor types, enemies, bosses, and characters. All that said, I still recommend this to fans of rogue-likes. Don't expect anything ground breaking and enjoy the cyberpunk atmosphere.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of Roguelites, and it took me a while to understand why I did not like this one as much. Despite the points I'll put, I do still think this game is not bad. But for me personally, I feel the gameplay is extremely mediocre. The art is good and the style is very appealing, there's no denying that. The issue with this game is gameplay. Roguelites are based a lot on luck, and rolling the dice to the see if you get the weapons, abilities, and other such items that you like, while also learning how to roll with the punches. Despite the random aspect to this genre, there still needs to be a sense of familiarity after a while with the player. The item/weapon pool in this game is MASSIVE, which on the surface seems really good, until you realize that you've done a hundred runs and can still hardly remember what anything does. I never found myself having moments where I went "Oh! Yes I love that weapon! This is a good run!" or the opposite "Ugh I hate that item, I'll leave it.". Most of the time I just sorta found myself picking up anything and going "Oh, that's what it does." and then never seeing that item/weapon until 30 runs later, where I have forgotten what it does. This game could benefit from not having such a large pool of items/weapons available at the start. Dead Cells handles its large range of weapons by having very little available to player at first, but slowly by unlocking everything, the player becomes familiar with everything and has a sense of control, despite the random nature of the game. Not to mention that there's also an egg mechanic where players can get eggs that hatch into little allies that do random things, and there's a bomb mechanic, and a violence vs wisdom mechanic; there is just too much. Nothing meshes that well, and it feels like the devs just threw everything at the wall, but never took anything off. In the end, you can get a bunch of half baked concepts.I feel like the style and concept of the game is very solid, and the gameplay is almost there, but there is just too much of everything. If you're looking a game with good art and a lot of luck, then you'll have fun. But if you want something you can actually nail down, then I suggest something like Dead Cells or Nuclear Throne. 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: First off, let me start by saying I love this game so far. It has a great aesthetic and manages to capture that feeling that made Binding of Isaac such a great game. That said, It has one glaring bug that makes it all but unplayable for anyone playing with a mouse on a duel screen PC. If you're frantically clicking away shooting at enemies and you click off your screen the whole game minimizes. There's no option for non-windowed full screen, either. So you can't bind your mouse to stay just in the game window. Fighting bosses was incredibly frustrating as in the panic and excitement your screen would just seemingly minimize out of nowhere, completely ruining the experience. If they get this glaring UI oversight fixed I'll happily change my review to recommend this game.** Update ** Despite this having been reported by many people and the assurances of the devs (such as the one on my review here) a week has gone by and there's still no patch.This should have been something that was hot-patched a day or two after launch. Since the game is unplayable in its current state I am requesting a refund and will never know if they ever actually fix this issue so the review stays.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon Abyss is a fantastic rogue-like, bullet-hell metroidvania.While you may occasionally run into a bug or two, and there is a *lot* of RNG involved in how successful you are in finding good loot for completing a run, the fun far outweighs the small annoyances.The memes and jokes are fresh and relevant. It's even making fun of games in development while this game was in development. The artwork is slick and well suited to the atmosphere. The music is poppin.But the thing that really sells this game is the  available. I've pumped nearly 50 hours into the game as of this review, and I've still only found about 2/3 of all the available weapons and items. The potential for varied gameplay and experimentation is nearly unparalleled. While it's easy to draw comparisons to Hades (even the game itself makes some tongue-in-cheek meta commentary on its similarities), Neon Abyss more than stands on its own legs as rogue-like with a ton of replay value and between-run progress.If you're looking for a fast-paced rogue-like you can really sink your teeth into, don't sleep on Neon Abyss!

_childDocuments_.review: Roguelike ‎Neon Abyss from Veewo Games is an innovative roguelike that combines elements from traditional dungeon crawlers with modern aesthetics. Unlike other roguelikes, Neon Abyss offers a colorful pixel art design and a stunning soundtrack crafted by 2-time BAFTA Award winner Danny Baranowsky and an impressive selection of special abilities, weapons, and items that offer an extra layer of depth to the action. Players can explore dungeons filled with enemies, bosses, and loot while ascending each level with progressively more powerful gear and abilities. Fans of the genre will be delighted to find that Neon Abyss also employs challenging roguelike elements such as permadeath and randomly generated levels.Neon Abyss is an excellent example of a God-tier roguelike. The colorful art style and original soundtrack combine to create an exciting atmosphere that immerses players in the game’s procedurally generated world. With plenty of secrets and new content to discover, it’s a great game for fans of the genre. The roguelike elements work harmoniously together, rewarding skilled players for their strategies and providing an engaging experience for newcomers and veterans alike. Neon Abyss is an excellent roguelike experience that is definitely worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Art direction, having a ridiculous build is fun and almost guaranteed, reasonable amount of content.Cons:One of the easier roguelikes out there, if you're new to the genre/bullethell in general I might recommend it. The main problem is the difficulty fails to pace with the content, you have to use currency from runs to purchase the ability for certain rooms to appear, and I managed to reach the credits without having unlocked many types of rooms, and those that I did unlock often proved inferior to the rooms I already had, and left me wishing I just hadn't bought them. The main way you'll die in this game is getting a gun/build so ridiculous that its shots fill your screen and you have trouble dodging enemy bullets, which IS fun, but the issue is that the variety of items is such that almost every one is just flat increase to stat(s), goofy or double edged sword items are few and far between.

_childDocuments_.review: A more forgiving and better looking (in my opinion) Binding of Isaac.Even though I had fun playing The Binding of Isaac I never really got into it. That game is pretty hard and to me it got repetitive relatively quickly because I usually fought the same monsters over and over again and died at the same stage.Neon Abyss on the other hand is more forgiving (I'm playing on the normal difficulty level). Additionally there are a bunch of very entertaining mini games that break up the combat sections and the graphics are fantastic.I also enjoy the progression system. When you unlock a new power-up you get that power-up for free in your next run, essentially making you a bit more powerful from the get go which helps you progress through the bosses.
_childDocuments_.name: Neon Abyss

_childDocuments_.review: I've never seen such utter lack of originality in an otherwise pretty well-made game. Yeah, I've played Binding of Isaac too, dear Veewo Games, you could be more subtle about lifting almost EVERYTHING from it. Hearts, keys, bombs, similar enemies, crates, casino machines, rooms that you can only enter by taking damage, secret rooms you need to blow up walls to see, the whole map, the power-ups system — all that is straight up stolen from Isaac. And developers haven't added anything from themselves, no new ideas, no new style, nothing. Story is laughably basic and boring, graphics are generic pixelart with a few good backgrounds, artstyle is a mess — game want to be cyberpunk-ish, but forgets about it 5 minutes into first level.Other than that, the game works perfectly fine, it is moderately fun, gameplay loop is nice. Upgrades are random, wacky and interesting. Guns all feel unique, but not all feel usable. On the later stages the screen becomes really cluttered with all the effects, projectiles and enemies. Bosses are too easy (played on Normal). Default control scheme is bizarre (left trigger to jump - really?).Overall — there is nothing really wrong with Neon Abyss, it is just so painfully average and generic. I see no real reason to play it over dozens of other amazing roguelikes out there.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd only recommend you get it on a sale if you're just dying for a roguelite. Could use some biome diversity and maybe more varied music.It's a fine enough game, but with how many great roguelites there are out there, you have better options.

_childDocuments_.review: it's unnecessarily grindy and not that fun.  You have a bunch of characters, and *each* of them are supposed to kill all bosses, which is like 70+ runs. That's fine if the game is good, but it's strangely not. The characters's classes feels more annoying than useful, like one character can lift things... what can you lift and why you lift them? Can't tell. Another character can revive pets by hurting yourself... except they died very easily and the game itself rewards you for NOT TAKING DMG. Which means that character is useless for a no dmg run by default.  And then there the upgrades... some of them are good, others are very situational and some downright breaks your build. Also I feel that either you are dominating or you feel weak, not much in between. Also mobility is king but it's rare to get those items. And the environment traps are more pointless than challenging, especially your pets can died to trap dmg as you try not to take dmg.The entire game is full of these weird design choices, it's almost like the devs don't want you to have fun.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fine. Main reason I stopped playing was more because the music was getting annoying than anything else. There's a solid roguelite here with all the usual features and plenty of weapons and items to discover over the course of countless playthroughs. The feel of the game is a bit off though. It's weird to have 360° aim on one stick and 8-way movement on the other with no analogue sensitivity for movement speed. Jumping with the left trigger always feels weird too (though admittedly I'm not sure what to map it to considering your right thumb should be on the right stick almost constantly). All and all it's still a fun game, so I recommend it if you're bored of your other roguelites. But if you haven't played Hades, Dead Cells, or The Binding of Isaac yet, definitely get to all of those first.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon Abyss is a crazy, frantic, action-packed roguelite which I feel will grow even better with time as the developers seem to actively engage with the community for feedback. I'll go ahead and summarize some of the positives and negatives of the game from my experience so far.+ Fluid movement and shooting mechanics+ Vibrant colours+ Plethora of room designs+ Lots of different enemies that increase with progression+ Great pixel-graphics+ Plenty of pop-culture references+ Interesting and diverse synergies+ Solid soundtrack + Learning curve that isn't too steep+ Progression based rewards (items, characters etc.)+ Unique experiences across runs+ Decision making is incredibly important (investigating room layouts, usage of keys and grenades)+ Strategy is equal to mechanics and skill+ Addictive gameplay-loop- Some rooms are incredibly goofy and seemingly impossible not to take damage in- Luck proves to be a major part in progression at times (critical on hard and abyssal)- Hatched eggs prove much more detrimental than beneficial regularly- Small bugs occur from time to time (etc. Ghost enemy stuck outside of screen view, almost ended a great run)- Portal network isn't available in every room of a level- Bosses can be a little too similar at times (etc. Johnny + Kimmy)In conclusion the positives outweigh the negatives pretty heavily so I would definitely recommend neon abyss to anyone looking for a new adventure in the roguelite scene.

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game to others who like roguelike 2d shooters, however this game has some obvious flaws as well. The most glaring flaw is that the screen can become very messy as your character spams a bunch of projectiles and bosses/enemy projectiles aren't always distinct enough to make them clear in all the mess. They should really have a brighter red outline like gungeon on most enemy attacks to make it clear what is going on, for instance the second end boss has some attack that drop stars or something that is almost impossible to see through all the clutter. It doesn't help that you can have an army of pets adding to the clutter.Also not having the ability to dismiss pets, at least not as I have found, is rather annoying and can lead to very cheap deaths. I was low on hearts, entered a room with hearths but I had to clear an obstacle to get to them. One of my pets just rushed over and ate the hearts turning multiple hearts into half a shield. This happened multiple times.I also ended up having pets that spammed bombs that kept getting me hurt because they knocked me around, I ended up having to spend as much time dodging my own pet's bombs as enemy projectiles.Overall good game but could benefit from some improvements, in particular more clarity on what projectiles will damage you and what won't

_childDocuments_.review: I will divide this review in the following categories :- Game atmosphere- Actual Gameplay- What I believe that should be prioritized in the upcoming updates- My personal suggestions to the devs- Final ReviewGAME ATMOSPHERE   When you begin the game, you're sitting besides what seems to be a pixel Keanu Reeves, who will introduce himself as Hades and tell you that a bunch of guys killed your family before offering you a drink. Next moment, you're in a strange bar ready to jump into the Abyss to kill a god...Or perphaps just to take a pause and enjoy the music of a rave as your character rocks the dancefloor.    And that's pretty much Neon Abyss, as you explore the dungeon, you won't be able to forget that rave feeling as your weapons turn into a light show the more you pump it up and you might have a taste of American Gods as you defeat the final bosses, while the ones that come before them are funny sketches of consumism and critics to modernity (ex. god of pills, god of mobile videos...).ACTUAL GAMEPLAY   I believe anyone that had a past experience with roguelike games will be familiar with most aspects of Neon Abyss and might find it pretty casual. It consists of getting through many rooms, collecting coins, bombs, and keys to open special rooms and chests ( sounds familiar? ) in order to get items and weapons that will make your character stronger.   So, what makes this game different? It has has two unique systems that you'll be able to encounter early in game : collectable pets which can fight on your side and a " faith " system which allows you to get more items by being damaged or killing enemies while avoiding damage ( I know it sounds confusing when put like this, but just take my word for now that it's pretty cool and experiment by yourself )   Aside from that, you'll find a tech tree in the game which allows you to unlock special rooms such as mini-games or more ways to spend your in-game resources, characters and items. Which means that there is always a reason to do "just one more run",UPCOMING UPDATES PRIORITIES   I think that the features and changes that were shown to be tested in the experimental branch fill pretty much any gameplay demand I could have with my experience so far. Good work devs!PERSONAL SUGGESTIONS   These are mostly about character customization : the game has awesome looking items, and I wish there was a way we could control which items are actually being displayed over our characters or not, since we can collect so many of them. So maybe displayed items could have special frames in our inventory and we could scroll through them in order to select and unselect what masks, hats and weapon mods we have currently on.   The second suggestion would be adding some kind of wardrobe in the bar where we could change special skins collected by defeating the game bosses. We would be able to firstly unlock skins of the used character and, if we had all of his unlockables skins so far, we would start getting skins for other characters.FINAL REVIEW   This game has been released 6 days ago at the time of this review. It has bugs, it could use some changes - and the developers are already showing that they will work for these changes. The game has a refreshing amount of items and weapons, 10 characters, and all the unlockables and side-content keep making each run a new surprise everytime you play. I definitely reccomend and believe that this game could be a great introduction to anyone who is curious or want to get into the roguelike genre.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really well made game with some really annoying design decisions that made it not recommended to any kind of casual player. I wish I could give it a middle thumb. As you can see, the art is great, controls etc are on point. However, there are a plethora of items and they choose not to tell you what they are. So either you can take the time to memorise (or note) what they all do, while taking risks on an item that *only* has a picture and a name, no description. Or you can just play it with the wiki open. All seem suboptimal. Also RNG, there is a lot of RNG, from chests that may or may not open if you put money in, to what items do (because if you haven't memorised it and don't use a wiki, then it's RNG basically. On top of that it is pretty punishing in terms of HP. Sure, that's ok, but if you finally get deep into a run, they suddenly ramp up the damage that *everything* does. Suddenly any source of damage will do twice what it did. Overall this is a great game if you're willing to invest the time to memorise everything and get ultra sharp reflexes. Otherwise it's probably best to just pass and find a more forgiving game.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon Abyss is a 2d platformer twinstick-shooter roguelike, it's one of very few that I haven't uninstalled as it feels good to do individual plays through with. However the considerable lack of variability with each run, other than tied to character, certainly hold me back from reviewing this as an absolute must.I've got a lot of close friends that are major rogue-like/lite fans, me personally I've been a fan of only a handful but probably more than the general populous, this doesn't make me a resident pro or anything and I want to make that clear (I'm not paid to play games, I just love gaming as a means of downtime) however for all the pros of this game I feel the random aspect almost wears this game thinner than it should feel. Yes I'm aware of what the genre entails but for all the good aspects this game is weighed down by the negatives of the rogue-lite.Yes come at me if you think Rogue-like and Rogue-lite are appropriately different genre's because to me they are evidently different. Roguelikes should be completable on run one f you're good enough and the RNG is in your favour, rogue-lite's generally favour an approach that it's far less likely to achieve first run through and they provide universal upgrades between runs.Hate me on my views, but please I'd rather a discussion on what the genre differences are.Again simply put, I really do like this game but my positive review comes with a tonne of caveats and the concerns that I don't feel this is as a fun a game as it could be.
