_childDocuments_.review: A point and click adventure focussed on jokes, weird occurrences and a detective having to deal with it all, acting as a Sequel to the original The Darkside Detective.The game consists of multiple cases you’ll complete one after the other. Each of them features some spooky occurrence in a unique location, which you’re tasked with resolving. To do this, you can move between different screens making up the location and collect junk, which you’ll then combine in order to solve puzzles. From time to time, the game also throws in a minigame to shake things up. As you work through these cases, you’ll encounter a multitude of characters, who provide you with hints as to what you need to do, while also providing a couple of humours lines of dialogue. Many of these characters are encountered throughout different cases, giving some nice continuity and fleshing out their personalities. Some characters from the first game also return, which I very much enjoyed.You once again play as Francis McQueen, his jokes as dry and self-aware as ever, often joined by his loveable Partner Patrick Dooley, being just as goofy and easily distracted as in the game’s predecessor. These two, along with the other characters, provide a nice mix of light-hearted humour, which kept a smile on my face throughout my time playing the game. Jokes are often self-aware or referential, which works surprisingly well.Each case felt quite distinct to me, providing puzzles that were somewhat obscure, yet not too challenging to solve. The non-grid-aligned pixelated look works well for the game but at points feels too static, with few animations. While certainly rather absurd, the world created by the game feels consistent and scenes feature a convincing atmosphere.All in all, this is a good sequel, which retains the strength of the original, but sadly doesn’t really change things up much. Nevertheless, I still recommend you buy it, along with the first game in the first game.

_childDocuments_.review: Lets talk about how a very simple-looking game can have such a rich world."DsD Fumble in the Dark" and the "Darkside Detective" before it, are consistently well-written; the humor flows naturally, the side characters are treated with backstories making them memorable and fun to interact with. The pixel art is great, the music is appropriately soothing (and vintage) the game interface was very easy, I never "got stuck" due to the lack of cues (nor was I force-fed the cues) and that to me means well-thought game logic and leveled feedback to the player. The Cases are unlocked in a linear manner, complete one to tackle the next. There are 3 bonus cases which players can start, pause to go back to the main story if they want, then return to continue working on the bonus case.  I think that the intended way to experience the story is by playing all the cases as they unlock, then moving on to the bonus area. The linear nature of the cases works for the story narrative, since we get many recurring characters in the series, even from the very first case of "Darkside Detective".Each case is a tongue-in-cheek, fresh and interesting take of a cult reference. They all take place at different city locations so the game can not get repetitive unless intended (bird bones). This brings replay-ability value if you are hunting for achievements and will be revisiting the cases.The game's achievements is actually where my one pain point is, some are a little punishing. It helps that cases are very short to play through once you have solved them once and know what to do. But, you also have a lot of (great but seen) dialogue to click through. All cases can be accessed after completing the main case, that is also a great help, but for example, I missed the Camp Counselor achievement twice because of one rushed click out of the screen. I kept this part for last as it probably doesn't interest most. I was very happy with the good-nature of our characters being evident in the small things. I am a fan of the anti-hero as the next person, however and without spoilers, here is a small example of what I mean here: at some point our Detective discovers an open invitation to a birthday party hidden among some information brochures. After confronting the person stationed at the information booth about it, our detective confirms the employee sneaked their birthday invitation in the brochures, and concludes "We'll be there," and by now we know he means it. These small touches are consistent and bring to life the concept of this open-para-minded small community in the big city, plagued by paranormal havoc and obsurdity but still remember to be human to one another. Definitely give this game (series) a try. It kept me very entertained, for longer than I expected (a good 20 hours according to steam, without achievement hunting). This also includes some long, un-pauses as the game waited patiently while I got distracted, having the background music keeping me company :). Great work!
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Like the first game, the detective cases are creative and blend comedy and the supernatural well. A lot of care is put into the dialogue and interactable objects. The two main characters have a great chemistry that makes a lot of banter found in the game enjoyable. And I also like the simple minigames thrown in so that progression isn't 100% dedicated to just point-and-click. They don't offer much of a challenge but it definitely helps break up monotony and their some of them are pretty creative.Overall this has become my favorite modern point-and-click adventure game series. I really hope a 3rd game is planned for the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed the first game? Here's more!Cases are a litttle longer this time around. Sometimes the lampshading/metahumour does get a little bit predictable or repetitive, but overall this is a worthy sequel. Once again, the puzzles are perfectly balanced on that sweet spot of frustration and satisfaction, and despite the wacky antics, the game does not involve moonlogic and even often times foreshadows its solutions subtly. It's less of a breath of fresh air this time around, but if you want more Darkside Detective, this'll definitely deliver.

_childDocuments_.review: The fun continues in this sequel to the Darkside Detective. The writing is still clever and funny, the puzzles longer, with more parts, but still avoiding some of the worst elements of these style of adventure games. I just love everything about these games, to the fantastic pixel art, the amusingly worked in references, and even to the characters and world. It may be simple, but it's a delight. Treat yourself to a little more fun in Twin Lakes. And I can't wait for another!

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy sequel to the first game, using the same structure of mini case files to work through. There's a more content here than in the original, which is great, and it continues to be fun meeting characters (new and old) throughout the absurdly spooky city of Twin Lakes. Some of the puzzles in this one take place over a lot of different areas as well as generally being a little more challenging than the first game - which I can imagine could push some players towards a guide. The 4th wall breaking humour did get a bit tiresome at points for me but there's plenty of genuinely good jokes in here too.

_childDocuments_.review: A bigger and better sequel with more cases with more length to them, more puzzles and more comedy.  The very basic pixel art is charming and colourful, the writing is humorous and the challenge feels about right, if a bit on the easy side for adventure game veterans.  The music and settings are good and although quite basic, the full screen puzzles are a nice addition.  There are some truly terrible, groan worthy puns and the 4th wall breaking jokes do get a bit dull after a while, but there’s enough charm, wit and variety to make each case entertaining and a joy to solve.  I found it to be a comfortable and rewarding game which I enjoyed very much.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: The game has the same pixel charme as the 'first season' game 'The Darkside Detective', the almost same level of pun-ishment (only later in the game the puns and funs tend to seem more forced and repetitive) and the almost same kind of weird use-a-with-b-to-get-c-and-apply-to-d-to-achieve-e puzzles (here the puzzles are even a bit more difficult than in 'The Darkside Detective')... and interesting substories of the individual cases... a worthy continuation of the first season with lots of funny details to discover. The uneven crime scene investigator team(s) still make fun to play, mostly because of their cartoonic stereotypes and the ones of the persons they come across in their adventures.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing sequel to the unforgettable Darkside Detective. I discovered this game way back in the day when it was still in the process of creation and it has since been my absolute favorite thing. I'm so happy to be seeing this many people discover and enjoy this game the same way I did and I completely recommend it to everyone. It is filled with fantastic characters who have a surprising amount of depth, but it manages to keep a lighthearted and fun attitude as you solve through various puzzles. I came here for the gameplay, but stayed for Dooley and McQueen.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: A great sequel, I enjoyed it. Very story rich, hilarious and meta (as in 4th wall breaking). There is no voice acting and it is text heavy, so I played this game bit by bit. There's usually a little quip or blurb to discover in a scene that's entertaining but personally I wasn't able to play for too long in one sitting. It doesn't flow as smoothly as a story in a book or the flow of a fighting game. But it is very fun and I enjoyed it.I believe it references to the first game a few times so play that first. Not much of a hardship lol

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the first one you'll love this one. _childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: This is why I hate the Steam rating system because this isn’t really a thumbs up or a thumbs down game. This, overall, is an okay game. I really liked the first one as was hoping for more of the same.This is very similar to the first one in art and game play. But, the first game had a plot and was fulfilling. This is just a hollow set of mini-adventures with some references to the first game.I like the graphics and humor, but I didn’t like the unconnected mini adventures. I was hoping that they would tie together in some fashion for a “grand” reveal or at least some connection between them to make a coherent story of some sort. Unfortunately, they do not. So, what you get are a bunch of little mini-adventure games that have the same protagonists without any story or overarching connection.Although, I might sound pretty down on this game. It is a semi-fun adventure game and I’d be thrilled if the developers made another, especially if incorporate a story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Very entertaining! This edition is in my opinion a bit more complicated than its predecessor. Frustrating at times, but also fulfilling when you finally get it. That said I needed a guide for one of the cases after an hour of clicking and combining everything I could and a still not figuring it out. The solution was very far fetched and put me of the game for a few days. Also a fun point, the game is self aware enough to be entertaining and not become tedious regarding it. The dialogue is, as always, brilliant and entertaining. The creators have given the (main) characters a personality that I can empathize with and want to know more about. I have honestly fallen in love with the familial/professional relationship between McQueen and Dooley. Its sweet, funny and something to aspire to. Love it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Exactly what I want from a modern point and click adventure. Not too obtuse, great nostalgic art and feel. Unique, lovable characters, great world building, interesting stories. Everything complex enough to get the brain churning, without being so challenging as to be frustrating. Stories are on the short side, so they don't overstay their welcome. Genuinely a masterpiece of its style.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Point and click adventure like they used to make back in the old days (both quality and graphic wise).Puzzles are not to hard but are not baby level, dialogue is very clever, the jokes usually hit the spot and the vibes are overall cool.If you like P&C you will love this one and even if you find the genre too boring, the humor and writing are still worth the price, especially if its on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, albeit simple game. Really charming in terms of the artstyle and writing. A bit too easy for my tastes, but on the other hand that just means the devs are really good at making all the puzzles logical and clearly highlighting the interactible objects. Captures the spirit of the original. Here's hoping for Darkside Detective 3!
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: It has worse puzzles than the first game had, at least for me. Differently from the first game, I seldom can see a logic string of my actions. ('Vinegar on a painted lever = lever' is the most extreme negative example)Shame, because this game made many many improvements to the predecessor and I don't feel you can see them without guides' help
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Reviewing even though at current only 8 of 6 cases (2 bonus) are available:Fantastic sequel to The Darkside Detective, which I highly recommend playing if you haven't already, as there are a lot of references to it in A Fumble in the Dark. Much of the same humour from the first game is reflected in this installment, although I did get stuck in a few places where, for instance, it wasn't clear there were additional exits in a room. Most of the puzzles are definitely fair, or at least fair in the sense that ok, yes, it's moon logic, but it's also moon logic repeatedly spelled out by the characters if you talk to them again. (Cute referencing both This is Spinal Tap and Stranger Things in the same line of dialogue!) There's also a fun time-travel section, which is a rare thing to do well, and something I'd like to see more games try in the future! (pun not intended)
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I'd really say I liked this game, but there were some parts that I really felt would be impossible to figure out for most people.  They made it incredibly far fetched to figure out what some of the solutions are.  You have to not take this game seriously at all.  You have to remember that many of the solutions are silly. If all else fails, go for the trial and error route.  Attempt to combine everything you have with everything in the world, and if that doesn't work, attempt to combine everything with each other. Funny jokes, references, and gameplay could use more practicality.  I'd give it a 6.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed every aspect of this game, its challenging and fun to play with new and old exciting characters such as Nigel, Dooley and so many more!The design of this game makes it feel as though you are part of the story, solving these intricate and well thought out cases each with a rewarding ending makes the game feel real. I adored every second of this game as its like nothing I have ever played before, I highly recommend this game to whoever may be considering buying it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: The Darkside Detective returns! In a whole new series of cases, which I found to be just as fun, if not more, than the first!((If you haven't played the original, go check that out first, then come back!))After leaving off at the end of last game on a cliffhanger...The game picks right back up, launching into its story. This game follows the same format as the first, so if you liked that one, rest assured you'll probably enjoy this one too! I found the best parts of this game at all times to be the self-aware humor, always with a little nod to the ridiculousness that is going on, but never losing sight of telling an entertaining story. If you like weird, supernatural, and funny games, and if you like the point-and-click style, I think you'll really enjoy this game. For me, I'd say better than the original by far, and I'd be excited to play more episodes, or even a third iteration! This is definitely my favorite series of point and click adventures, and definitely one of my top recommendations to my friends!
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of this review I've only completed 3 cases.  The first case was a fantastic continuation to the finale of the first game.   The next cases have had a few puzzles that did not click with me and I had to resort to the ol' combine everything in my inventory with everything else routine to make progess (teddy bear + tape recorder?).  I very much enjoy the continued writing, wit, and premises surrounding the Detective and Dooley's adventures, but as of right not I think I prefer the simpler charms of the first installment.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark is a great sequel, with cases that are much longer, for better or worse, some amazing pixel art with glorious colours and much funnier than the first game. While DSD felt like a small project, this one feels like a proper game, with proper puzzles and somewhat of a story. The soundtrack is as great as ever, really building the atmosphere in each case.The cases being longer can have their bad sides, since I feel like a couple tend to drag for too long and, especially in the first case, it throws way too much stuff at the player that requires the player to keep a mental reminder of way too many objects at once. For example, the make-up item, you can interact with it but it has no special dialogue to hint that it may be used later and you can't pick it up, but later when you need it, it is most likely long forgotten by the player.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a lot of fun, like the first.  Several interesting mysteries to solve.  There aren't multiple ways to solve a case/puzzle and there are no different outcomes.  It's pretty linear in that regard.  However, the point-and-click style doesn't get old in this game.  The dialogue is pretty funny and hints are adequate, but not too revealing.  Game and case storylines intermingle with the previous game.Took me about 13 hours to complete the game and bonus cases, including 100% achievements.  A bit short, really, but totally worth it when it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Another brilliant installment in the Darkside Detective series! As fun, witty, playful, creative, and engaging as the first game and with longer cases this time. I did get stuck a few times but it wasn't anything some running around didn't fix. The hugging animation added 10 years to my lifetime, as did the amazing soundtrack, dialogues, and background art. Very excited for case 9 and/or a third game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Great series of games - humor (witty dialogue, cultural references) , difficult (But not impossible) puzzles with enough subtle hints to keep you progressing and a very nostalgic (think Lucasarts classics) graphics style. Highly recommended point and clicks.A bonus (literally) is that free extra content gets released occasionally such as new episodes/  cases , which is always welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: If you played the first one of these Darkside Detective, you know what you are walking into. It is a really well done point and click 8-bit adventure. The cases get tougher here and a few times I got stuck and needed to look for help. Some of the dialog gets lengthy and will discourage you from clicking around aimlessly over time. Still I recommend this game if you like point and click adventure games.EDIT: The last case was released and it was much like the previous 8 cases. This time I played it exclusively on the Steam Deck and it worked perfectly. Can definitely play this game on the Steam Deck and it all plays exactly the same.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: The first game was pretty good and this one is pretty much the same with longer and more complicated cases.If you liked the original one, you will definitely enjoy this one. It's more expensive but definitely worth the price for the more complex cases.All the stories are well done and I personally think the humor got much better in this one as there were much less cringe moments like in the first one. Dialogues were better while the plots are still fun and interesting.The cases are much bigger than in the first game and span many screens and locations unlike the first game which contained some very short cases. This makes the puzzles a bit more complicated but you are never truly lost and can always go the good old way of clicking everything, combining everything. I felt overwhelmed in one or two cases but the others were pretty linear in which you unlock additional locations while you advance the story.There is a little less  theme going around but all the stories are great and well-written, maybe even better than the first one especially since I felt the dialogues were a tad more mature and less childish slapstick humor, at least one main character doesn't feel completely brain dead/opposite of sanity.This is a must buy if you loved the first game. It's a good buy (especially on sale) if you liked or enjoyed the first one. Otherwise I would advise people to buy the first game which is much cheaper to get a taste of the story/characters/difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played the original Darkside Detective, and you liked it, you're going to enjoy this as well. I do have to admit, it's not as fun as the original, only because the puzzles aren't as difficult. Other than the puzzles being easier, everything else about AFITD is better than the original: Soundtrack is great, dialogue is spot on, puzzle depth is top notch, and the DLC's are excellent. Ghosts of Christmas Passed is by far my favorite puzzle. If you like satire like Twin Peaks, and puzzles that are difficult, but not Elden Ring difficult, you'll enjoy this game. Also, click on everything, a lot of time went into all of these eastereggs, take the time to enjoy them.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: First game was somewhat fun, but this sequel is truly remarkable in many aspects.It was like playing an old-school point'n click adventures such as Monkey Island, Sam'n Max or Day of the Tentacle.Puns are funny and there are many references to popular culture. Dooley is funnier in this game.I truly enjoyed every case (except bonus cases) and puzzles were somewhat challenging.It took 12 hours for me to beat it. I recommend the game to every veteran adventure lovers and to beginners to genre.I feel pumped for the next sequel.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game series, with the oerfect amount of comic relief.The right amount of challenge per casual game play. I had AFITD in my wishlist before the first game. but bought them as a bundle and played n order (recommended). The first one I couldn't stop from the moment I started until the moment i 100% it. The second one, I found myself taking a small hiatus from (no particular reason) and then just opened it back up last night and ended up staying up most of the night to complete it. So, with that being said, it is a bit slower than the first, but it does pick up, and all is worth the entire playthrough. great game series. I want to think that the ending of AFITD leaves speculation that there is going to be a 3rd?? oh, please?
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Was looking for a serious detective game and found this. Not at all what i was looking for but oh my god do i love it. If you love point and click, inclusive and diverse language, awkward humour and loyal friendships, you will love this game. You will probably also love it if you don't. I just wish they had eyes...
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adored the first game and immediately bought the sequel the moment it was out.I love the Darkside Detective adventures SO SO MUCH!!!They're not only pretty to look at and have a banging soundtrack - the writing is what makes these games real gems! The references, the humor, the clever puzzles! They even released an additional Christmas case!I want so many more new cases, I never want them to stop coming, I love love LOVE these games, I can't stress enough how awesome they are! And everyone should play them! :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes everything I liked in the first game and does more of it, better! The characters are funny and charming, the puns are terrible (as puns should be), the puzzle minigames are fun, the plot is weird (as plots should be), and the cases are a good length each. I hit a few points where I felt stuck, but it was the kind of stuck solved by pacing around a little or by taking a quick break. I can't wait for the next two bonus cases to be released!
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Much like it's predecessor, the Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark is a hilarious point-and-click adventure game that explores the supernatural side of the police sector. Its dialogue is witty, intelligent and never gets old, while the cases are long, challenging and exciting, giving one much value for money spent. What I love about the sequel, in comparison to the former, is the extension of the cases in terms of rooms, challenge and overall story. These cases exist in a bigger realm, with more areas to explore and in a more diversified backdrop to the action. A great game, would recommend to everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Oh my goodness, where do I even begin? This was such a fun game to play! I enjoyed it from start to finish! Nicely paced and amazing humour! Had me giggling through and through. The characters really grow on you, old faces from the first game make an appearance and even the credits are still hilarious. Not everything is obvious and takes some thinking. I had such a great time with this game. In my opinion? Well worth the price! It's short, but so good. As someone who is currently unemployed, I'm very picky with where my money goes when I have some saved by for myself and this? No regrets at all! Really hope to see more from these guys. Detective McQueen, please come back soon!
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: I am enjoying the sequel much more than the original game. The humour is still hit and miss for me, but they added love to the characters and the world building gets a better shape. I mean, even when I did not enjoy it I would still follow Spooky Doorway through because The Darkside Detective itself got better as it progressed, but this one starts really strong from the beginning. A beautiful game that knows its strengths.Now, I am going to edit the review to highlight what I find most irritating about this game and the previous one: the dialogues are full of really bad, overlong, overexpositioned and even pedantic puns. Like the worst kind of Family Guy pop culture wink mixed with unintentionally creepy innuendo and generally a lot of stuff that I feel like I need to skip. But then, out of that enormous amount of trash there can be a clue, which is the only part of the dialogue that is fairly related to the world building, to the story or to anything that makes you advance through the game. I believe someone here thinks that they are very smart, intelligent and know how to write well, and I am pretty sure they are and they can... with someone that reads them for filth when they are so out there in the writing, someone they trust. Meh whatever the game is cool anyway.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed the Darkside Detective, or humorous point and click adventures, this is the game for you. While not too challenging, the puzzles are always logical. The dialogue is crisp, to the point and always funny, while never suffering from not being voice acted, as the characters themselves bring enough personality with them.Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful, magnificent, endearing and incredibly funny. Very worthy sequel to The Darkside Detective.Can recommend this to everyone who likes Point & Click games (and played the previous game).The characters' dynamic is again wonderful, and they get a lot more depth. The cases are interesting and original, the soundtrack is very nice and the jokes are on point.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the first Darkside Detective, and A Fumble in the Dark is more of the same in all the best ways. The humour is great as always and the cases are a great way to enjoy the game in bite-sized chunks, but meaty enough to be satisfying individually. Highly recommended to anyone who enjoys pixel art and humourous point and click adventure games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: If you like humor (slightly on the dark side) and point and click adventures in short bursts, then this is the game for you.While I like big adventures with long and winding story arcs, it's really nice to have a game you can start up after work, play an episode (or try finding what you missed in an older one) and be done for the evening.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Great game if you're a fan of classic adventure games. It has good humor, no no-win scenarios and worthy sequel to the previous game.To update, I am back one year later after completing the cases in the final update. The team put a lot of thought into how much we'd enjoy Dooley's dialogue and it shows.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the original, this was an instant buy. It's more of the same (not a bad thing), great pixellated art, various music scores (that doesn't get tedious) and of course the humour. It's obvious the developers have a passion for their game and updated it with additional cases.  Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the first Darkside Detective game, then it's a no-brainer - you'll like this. It's more of the same puntastic banterrific puzzley click-click adventure gaming, in the  same universe, with the same graphic style, with the same protagonists. And I can't get enough of it. If you haven't played the first one yet, well, start there and see  how it goes. If you're into adventure gaming that leans heavily on puns and slightly off-kilter character interaction, and you have a hankering for old school graphics, definitely try it out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great, especially for the price. The logic puzzles are really interesting because they involve putting items together that you wouldn't initially think of but make total sense. If you want super heavy graphics or a really serious detective drama, then this isn't for you. But if you like light-hearted puzzle-solvers, then this should be right up your alley.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Essentially more of what we had from the first game. Fun characters and writing and an enjoyable experience, overall. Cases are still not that difficult when compared to other point-and-clicks, but they are a bit longer this time around. If you liked the first game, you'll probably like this one, too.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe I'm shallow or have a low sense of humor but it just makes me laugh.  Some of the puzzles are so confusing I can't imagine how anyone could have put this together without a guide which, admittedly, I used a few times but I made it through most of the game fine.  it's short, charming, and relaxing.  If you liked the first one you'll like this one6/10 - a little above average, it's very simplistic but in that it has as sort of charm.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Fans of vintage Lucas Arts point-and-clicks as well as Thimbleweed Park and Jenny Le Clue, this game is everything you hope it will be. Irreverent and funny, it's wonderfully well-written, with characters you'll root for and laugh with (and at) and references to your old favourites as well as new ones (the subtle Stranger Things nod was a highlight). Puzzles are perfectly balanced: interesting, challenging but not frustrating, and you never feel that you've solved something by happenstance o forcing combinations and not through deduction. The sequel to The Darkside Detective, you of course want to start there, but come here straight after. And come back soon, when there will be more cases added. Because that's just the kind of dedication you get from these Brightsiders...
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Reviewing every game I own #172Not as funny as the first game. Relies too heavily on fourth wall breaking and "um, so THAT just happened" style internet humor. Still worth playing though. I would also like to apologize for calling the devs british in my review of the first game. They're actually irish
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Exciting opening and satisfying ending. Nice music and art. Really expect the new chapters. The game will be better if some selection windows can be adjusted, and if there is an option to skip some conversations and descriptions since the game could requires repeated investigation. Hope the Chinese option can be on soon.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: A great second instalment in the series. The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark is just as fun, just as unique, and just interesting as the first Darkside Detective game, but provides players with a larger story and more context for the world we are introduced to. I am looking forward to the bonus cases, and any possible future games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: This was my first jaunt into this punderful, cheeky, geeky & fantastical world of McQueen & Dooley (who btw, have one of the best relationship dynamics ever).If you love games such as Thimbleweed park and Dropsy, you'll love TDD:AFITD It's got a great sense of humour, enjoyable game design, hilarious dialogue and more geek references than you can throw a stick at, with some being so obscure it made me squeal with delight.I highly recommend you play it. Do it or Geoff will come and eat your butt.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Although it's a separate game, this could have been launched as DLC or expansion for the first game, as there are no improvements, only new cases.If you liked the first game as I did, it's just more cases so nothing can go wrong here. No new mechanics, no new user interface, almost no new characters. Again, feels more like a DLC for the first game rather than a sequel. It's still good though, as good as the first game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Very good follow-up to the first game. The writing is still the star of the show: I find myself clicking on everything, even things that I know won't advance the plot, just so I can read whatever quip or skit it triggers. The pixel art is very well done. The inventory puzzles are good, finding that middle ground between "logical enough to actually figure out" and "not the same boring puzzle again." There are several mini-games, none of which stands out on its own but do serve to break up the point-and-clicking and add variety. I would like to see the "crazy conspiracy theory investigation board" be fleshed out into a recurring mini-game and was a little disappointed it was a one-off. Takes about 8-9 hours to play through.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: This review will cover both this game and the first, since I bought them as a bundle.These games are a wonderful callback to some classic point and click adventures (sometimes explicitly - I'm looking at you Bobbin Threadbare reference). The puzzles are fairly simple for the most part; there are a couple of times I've struggled and got a little frustrated as it didn't feel clear what I was aiming for, but that's only once or twice in 10+ cases so far. The puzzles in Fumble in the Dark definitely feel more sophisticated, and the minigames in FITD are really a joy; no spoilers, but the telephone exchange sigil/cable puzzle was really good fun.  I'd say the best thing about the game has to be its sense of humour. Spooky Door's jokes and cute 4th-wall-breaking consistently get a chuckle out of me. The jokes are well placed and spread evenly in the cases and it never feels like they fail to land.I love Pastor Farrelly, but my favourite characters have got to be the Bloodwolves. Leaving the TV studio and seeing Emily on the car really made me smile.Good job Spooky Door!
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent sequel to the first Darkside Detective, having all the things I liked about the gameplay of the first game with even more funny in-jokes and cases. I don't know what else to say, just that this game is clever, witty, and a total throwback to all of those flash games I stayed up too late playing to get myself through the hell years of middle and high school. If that's your vibe, you'll love this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: some puzzles are hard for my simple minded brain (cant handle it without a guide)overall FUN!!! i miss Dooley.if you havent played the first one its ok, youd miss alot about the characters and some of the story especially Nigel( Nigel's a real sweetie ).i love love love this game. the mini games are alot fun, i didnt mean to break the clown car though im sorry.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: So fun, funny, and addicting! I can't wait for more cases and I hope there will be a third game afterwards. Can be very tricky to figure out what to do with certain items. Highly recommend this series for point and click lovers. This probably won't melt your graphics card or your wallet so give it a go
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: A long-awaited sequel to a game I love? Sign me up! Just like the first game, the writing is phenomenal. The puzzles are interesting, the characters are fun, the graphics are great. .  . Basically if you want a classic style Point and Click, this is well worth your time and money. Sorry to say though, if you wanted an RTS, this game does disappoint.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Just like the previous Darkside Detective game, this is a delightful game. I do have to admit that sometimes I need a guide to jump through some of the weirder hoops of this game's puzzles, but then again, I'm not that used to point-and-click games. I do highly enjoy the humour of it all, though. Would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Another kickstarter success story!If point and clicks are your thing then this is definitely a must play. The dialogue is witty, the puzzles are wonderfully well balanced and intuitive and each piece of pixel art is beautifully crafted. I actually love the approach taken with using limited animations with the characters, having the characters move to perform actions is totally unnecessary and it's clear that what you get in return for that small sacrifice is a much more beefy game in terms of content. These days it's rare for a point and click to be as large as the point and clicks of the 90's and this definitely delivers with its 7 chapters, each one feeling like its own stand alone Darkside Detective game.Please keep em coming guys! I'll be buying every one of them.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Darkside Detective Francis McQueen and stalwart partner Pat Dooley return for more ridiculous pixel adventures in Twin Lakes, the most supernaturally spooky town in the continental forty-eight.  As in the first game, the comedic writing is solid and often downright funny.  Dooley gets the funniest gag sequence this time around, snagging the crown of lulz from Emily of the Bloodwolves, whose relative lack of action is this game's only true downside.  Needs More Emily!In truth, point-and-click adventure aficionados cannot do better than this collection of offbeat, spooky buddy cop mysteries.  Prepare to laugh, puzzle and occasionally smile wryly to yourself for 8 to 10 hours of supernatural sleuthing in good old Twin Lakes.  Mic check in 3...2...1... take it Dooley!
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: The game was a great, now i usually tend to be rather picky with games, specially with how some characters are written or how some puzzles tend to be. But coming from the first game this was a great continuation, or even better than the last one! I played this with my friend and we had a great time reading the text and trying to solve the puzzles. Can't wait to see what comes next for the game! <3<3
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: OMG I liked the season 1 so I instantly played the season 2, EVEN BETTER!! I can tell that they have improved a lot (I know it's all pixel-imaged but gameplay, storyline, etc. Overall quality had been improved). Season 1 and Season 2 are connected to play the first season first. It didn't take long time to finish the first one. I only finished the first case from the second season and already adoring it so much. I want to play this slowly so I will not be running out cases to solve instantly. 100% recommend :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly think the Darkside Detective series is one of the best puzzle game series. I tend to be very picky about the games I play; however, I have never had a moment in DD2 so far in which I have felt bored or uninterested by the story. The puzzles are of a decent difficulty -- typical adventure game style -- and the characters are incredibly memorable.I know the dev team is relatively small, but I hope with success on their first two games they'll be able to branch out and make more classic point-and-click adventure games :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: This is the sequel I definitely wanted to Darkside Detective. While playing the first game isn't necessary, it definitely carries some basic plot and jokes through into this second game so I would recommend playing both. The first couple of cases are a little long, but I was motivated to complete them because of their connection to the cliffhanger from the first game. After that, the cases go back to being more stand alone. The jokes are funnier, the fourth walls are broken more. This is exactly what I was hoping this game would be,
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: A fun sequel to the original Darkside Detective game.  Fans of old point-and-click adventures (i.e. anything by Sierra in the 80s) will love this, especially with the tongue-in-cheek genre references and heavy fourth-wall breaking.  It's also nice that the chunky graphics are large and bright enough that you don't have to play pixel hunt to find clues.  Figuring out what the hell to do with the clues is another matter, however.  Luckily, unlike in the 80s, there are walkthough guides readily available for when you really can't figure out what to do next.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Even funnier than the first one!  Each "case" has a lot more variety too, and is more challenging.  Definitely got stuck a few more times, but mostly felt pretty fair.  I think my only real complaint is that I wanted more Raxa!  I hope she makes more appearances in any future cases and/or additional sequels.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: I was overjoyed to see that the Darkside Detective was back for another round of point-and-click adventuring.  If snarky wit, urban fantasy, and retro gaming is your jam - and if you're reading this, I bet it is -- I wholeheartedly recommend picking up this game.  I very much hope this won't be the last chapter in the adventures of Detective McQueen and Dooley; I've grown very fond of them and this setting.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Even better than the first game. I laughed harder, I was more intrigued by the plot (because now there is one) and I spent exactly the right amount of time solving the puzzles (long enough to feel like I'd achieved something, but not long enough to get frustrated).Also, you can pet the at least three animals.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:+Same crisp pixel art+Puzzles are definitely a step up and each case is a lot of fun in it's own way+The story and characters are a step up from last timeCons:-If I had to say something, music wasn't bad but I can't remember much outside of the main theme and the loading jingleOverall just a really solid point and click adventure/puzzle game with a fun premise and setting. Definitely pick it up if you're into that.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Very good little point-and-click game. One small criticism: sometimes you will know what item you need to use to advance, and even have good idea of how to use it, but won't know exactly what to use it with. And McQueen's reaction to trying to use an item is usually a binary works-doesn't work thing. In some of those situations, the game should either accept multiple correct solutions or else give you a different response to indicate that you're close.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: I'm halfway through the game but i can already say that it's pretty good, even better than the first one which i really enjoyed. Don't expect hyper-complex puzzles, this game is not that, it's all about the point and click magic and cool 80s references (?) Even if you don't get the references, the humor is good :)Update: I finished the game, still very recommended but i must say a few puzzles are a little too far fetched and can get a bit frustrating (mostly because it's not that the puzzles themselves are hard, it's just that some don't make sense and you end up solving them out of randomly combining stuff.). It's not constant through the game but there are a definitel 2 or 3 moments where this is an issue. In every other aspect, i liked this better than the first one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: I waited a long time for this game, it was thrown into my wishlist as soon as the steam page for it had become available and it comfortably sat at the very top at slot number one. I would have gladly paid for this game but my girlfriend surprised me, she bought it for me before I woke up on launch day (such a sweet and sneaky surprise). This game was well worth the wait. _childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Very much more of the same as the first game, which is simplistic point-n-click game with delightful writing. Really, like 90% of your enjoyment of these games is derived from whether or not you enjoy the writing. Art is great, music is good, but no voice acting, which is ok. but barely any sounds and animations at all. lots of punny and 4th wall jokes. _childDocuments_.review: What a brilliant game. I played the first one and I absolutely loved it and the second one is even better. Cases are so funny and interesting. This game will keep me entertained for days and days. The dialogue is hilarious and has very detailed stories to go along with them. Struggle to find a game like this that has as much detail and effort put into it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Review made at 6 hours played and 2/6 cases solved.Another instant classic!With myriad creative point n click puzzles, a great musical score, more puns and wordplay than you can (or should) shake a stick at, I'd recommend this game for any fan of the genre, and probably for a lot of people looking to dip their toes in it.  The game is designed to be easily digestible by splitting the story into (for now) six separate cases you have to solve, so it's also easy to put down and pick back up again!Can't recommend this game, and its predecessor, enough. Get'em both!
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the first game and was looking forward to when the second one released and was not disapointed. It's a point and click game with a great sense of humor and while some of the puzzles can be challenging, in my opinion it does not suffer from the far-fetched solutions that many other point and click adventures nowadays suffer from. It is rather short (around 13 hours for full completion, including all achievements) but since the price matches this, I can fully recommend giving this game a try.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: On the second to last mission and it's been a lot of fun! This was the first time I bought a game close to release because I was so excited to join McQueen and Dooley on more adventures! If you enjoyed the first game then you are sure to enjoy this sequel! Each mission is much longer and more complex than the first game, I've had a few head scratching moments but have always been able to find the solution! The writing and plots of each case are very funny, and as before I love the art style!
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: A truly excellent followup to first The Darkside Detective.You get more fun and longer cases filled with witty puns and "hidden" things.The cases in this one is longer which is nice.If you enjoyed the first one you will really enjoy this one. I do recommend playing the first one not only because it is good but there are references back to the first one here and there and you will understand them more. You can of course still enjoy the game without it.Only have good things to say about it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful sequel to a wonderful game.  I love Detective McQueen's deep love for Officer Dooley.  When he pretended to not be able to turn the crank, when they recited their school motto together, when in the flashback we see all the places that Geoff was... This game has so much heart, so many fun puzzles, such good writing.  I urge you to buy it, you'll fall in love.
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely stunning sequel with even better dialogue, puzzles, and Dooley-isms than the first! I highly recommend to anyone who loves their point-and-click adventures with a hefty dose of puns. Thrilled to see the first case is a bit longer, as the longer cases in the first game were my favorite kind. Congrats to the team on another amazing game!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: A solid sequel!  If you enjoyed the first you can't really go wrong here, especially with that ending, you're not gonna just leave that hanging, are you?The stakes have been raised, the scale of most of the cases feel much bigger, and for the most part they flow more easily and can feel quite dramatic!  I did get stuck 2-3 times and those times were very frustrating because when you're missing something there are no hints to help you out.  I was either missing a tiny object that didn't look like I could collect it, or a "walk left" screen that I had no idea was there.  but, I got there in the end without help, just took a while of pixel hunting!
_childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of the series since I played the demo for Darkside 1 and honestly this did not disappoint. Absolutely had a blast playing it, getting stuck for half hour and puzzles and then cursing myself for not seeing simple solutions Lmao. Gotta Love point and click adventure games. Things that made This a highlight though: Heart wrenching story about losing and finding your best friend, visiting exotic locations like Ireland, pixelated butt, the fact that there's different ways McQueen tells you you're not doing things right based on chapter, dunking on *lon M*sk, escaping toxic relationships and the power of karaoke. _childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Still going through the game, but I can tell it is all I could have ever hoped for. This series has found a place in my heart since I played the demo of the first game years ago. The humour, the charm, the style, the story, everything. It doesn't drag itself to the point of pandering to little kids with potty humour, it has it's own personality that I implore anybody interest in point and click games to at the very least try it. _childDocuments_.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the original and love this game too, clever puzzles to figure out, and while sometimes you're left wondering around trying to figure out the solution, it's almost always logical enough that you're left going "Ahh, that's what I needed to do" rather than "Well how was I supposed to figure that out?" which is a downfall these kinds of games often fall into.Fans of the original will be glad that the hilarious writing is still here in force, and it's still incredibly funny!I'd say check out the original game first, there's a free demo of the first case and by the end of that you'll either be bored or sold. _childDocuments_.review: After 30 hours, I've gotten all of the achievements and cleared the game twice. However, due some balancing abuse cases, this game should actually be longer and, arguably, much more difficult later in. I'll explain that after some praise.I like the dark aesthetic, theme, and intentions behind the concepts. This game is grim in all things, especially the sacrifice mechanics. Since your daughters never heal naturally, and can only be healed by the sacrifice of another one that is equal or higher level in power, this sounded like a tough choice. And it is for your first or second attempt. Though it's technically possible to beat the game in a single shot, you're not meant to, and it's highly unlikely you will deduce the methods to do so on your first try.The game is challenging starting out. You don't have vitae to dump into memories or germination, and enemies are formidable. This continues on, and the bosses can be tricky with limited resources and power. You want a well-balanced team, and to stay as healthy as possible. Your goal every battle is to kill everything before it can hurt you, or minimize damage taken. There are reaction skills that cost HP, but are ultimately intended to prevent you from taking even more damage in a bad situation, or turn the tide.After you wipe a couple times, you'll have enough shards and Remembrances (perks you can activate for your next restart) to finish the game. The further you push, the more powerful you'll be in your next playthrough, so you're inevitably going to be strong enough to beat the game, regardless of tactics.-------------------Now some negatives:1.) VarietyThis game is not massive in scope. The development team is on the small end, and you'll notice a general lack of variety, primarily in missions. Layouts get reused, a couple tracks are kinda boring to listen to repeatedly on some missions, and the mission type variety is limited--particularly early on. This comes with the territory and doesn't bother me much, though some more layouts earlier in the game, or randomized starting positions would be better. There's missions that have identical enemy and daughter placement, including later enemy spawns.2.) Specific balancing issues (Spoiler for making the game way, way, WAY too easy)There are some very specific abuse cases in this game that were clearly not intended, or an oversight into how effective they are. Soulslingers and Scythedancers (obtained much later) become utterly busted and break the game. In the case of the former, they gain a skill at level 7 called Spirit Burst that costs them 30 Initiative units to move another daughter up 20 units. This, in its base form, isn't really overpowered, since the timeline will keep advancing in a negative loop. However, later in the game you can add memories on that increase the Init. bonus by 10-20, and it becomes very broken at this point. The skill has an insane cast range that isn't limited by line of sight, and your AP pool can jack up considerably late game with the right traits. You can run 2 Soulslingers that have enough AP to trade +40 Init buffs AND attack at least once in the same turn. You can literally freeze time on any boss that isn't capable of fighting back by late in the game.This gets worse once Scythedancers come into play. Each class gives a bonus to the daughter you sacrifice it to. They aren't game breaking, except in the case of Scythedancers. When sacrificed, they increase your starting position on the timeline and reduce the end-of-turn delay. It's possible to get Soulslingers to ~31 turn delay, and Scythedancers to 20. So, now you have Soulslingers freezing time by trading buffs, and getting in free shots with no reprisal.The last domino in the broken Soulslinger issue is the Shadow Round skill. At first, this seems pretty average. However, Shadow Round fires once for each attack any daughter does before the Soulslinger's turn comes back. Trigger a boost to push your turn back as far as possible, and then have another Soulslinger unload 4+ attacks for 4 additional Shadow Round attacks--there is no cap on how many times this ability can activate for more damage, and it's only a 5% HP cost (which is nothing late game). To top this, you can equip a memory with it that will increase the target's damage taken by 15-30% for 30 Init. units, and this debuff begins on the Shadow Round shot. This memory stacks onto itself, and you can chain bosses into taking over half of their HP in a single hit from all of the debuff stacking. I actually broke one of the bosses doing this by skipping multiple phase changes and a cutscene completely by accident. All of these abuse cases completely trivialize the mid-game through the end, and I highly advise NOT using them.Lastly, the Scythedancers are cool and, aside from their sacrifice bonus, are okay. Except one of their final skills, The Harvesting, is overpowered. Assuming you get to 15 to snag this, it trivializes virtually every mission thereafter, including parts of a few bosses. An instant skill that hits every enemy on the map for a substantial chunk of damage, and doesn't even automatically push the Scythedancer into a burst. Two Scythedancers with their reduced turn delays bulldoze an entire map, and I've literally loaded into one and killed every single enemy on the very first turn and had to wait for more to respawn.3.) BugsI encountered very few bugs, actually. There's some shenanigans with damage values, and explanations on mechanics could be better. I do wish the UI contained certain information more accessible, especially in battle. (Forgetting which daughter has which memory in combat is annoying.)--------------So, as you can see in that block, there's some balance issues for specific things. Most everything else besides the aforementioned is quite balanced for the game. I think overall delay and armor options need tuning against each other, but otherwise you'll find the endgame very difficult if you skip these cheesy tactics. Even Scythedancers aren't overpowered in and of themselves (besides sacrifice bonus and Thar Harvesting).The game has a lot of replay value in imposing challenges upon yourself. I'd expect someone casually moving through this game to 100% it in 25~ hours, maybe a little less, with no self-challenge runs. I discovered and abused these cheesy tactics and cleared it on my third Recollection (restart; I died once to two different bosses). The game would likely be longer and more brutal with some balancing done.I do recommend this game for fans of things like XCOM. Whether you want to wait on a patch or not is up to you.

_childDocuments_.review: A thoroughly stressful and vexing kick in the nuts. Defeat is always lurking around every corner and it creeps up on you slowly. Every scratch, every missed hit, every slight miscalculation piles up to an unpayable debt that will kill all of your precious daughters and send you right back to the start of the level. Defeat in this game is slow, frustrating and bitter. Victory is cheap, cheesy and ill deserved. Cool art, cool music, cute daughterfus. And all in all, a pretty cool game.

_childDocuments_.review: 3 hours in, you think this review may be kind of unorthodox- However I MUST recommend this game. First of all the devs are STILL UPDATING THE GAME! Second of all, this game if you play on how it's meant to be played (Nightmare) it will be one of the hardest Strategy games you'll ever play and it is worth it! The gameplay loop is rewarding and punishing all at once! And as you go through the game and it's lore, you can get attached to these daughters and it makes every death kind of thunk against your heart. Especially ones you grow attached to. The story thus far is amazing and the gameplay loop is more than worth it for the story you receive. If I had anything to kind of like- Give you an idea of what this game is like- Imagine Bloodborne and XCOM had a baby, then called it Othercide and asked the Hades art team if they can clothe the baby. Then Hades put the baby in unique clothes fitting it's parents, an that baby said: I'm Othercide, and ima make the Bloodborne story pale in comparison to me whilst following a similar theme. That probably made no sense! Just know, it's worth full price and half price, get this damn game!

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, as I like this genre and the graphics seemed really appealing to me. However, I've ultimately requested a refund for this game as some of the issues with the controls, UI and game features are simply lacking or too poorly implemented to make the game fun to play. It feels like a chore. There doesn't appear to be any efficient way to view the range of movement of enemies, and the range of movement doesn't really factor in the AP cost of attacks. Making it feel like home work to have to count how many tiles an enemy may move, and what kind of attack he could use. The controls just appear silly making the whole process take for ever. The UI lacks clarity, I would often try to use an attack, and be unsure if it's going to be an AOE, ranged, delayed, and sometimes couldn't figure out who I was targeting. The controls don't make this easy either as there seems to be an inconsistency with how the controls operate on various skills or targeting. If this game had massive improvements to the UI and control schemes I would perhaps recommend it. But unfortunately the issues make the already slow paced genre of game even slower and tedious. :(

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly high quality for what it is, but suffers from some obvious faults.As far as what's great about the game, enough cannot be said about the aesthetics. The black and white with splashes of red is reminiscent of Sin City. The progressive soundtrack is similar to those of FFXIV or Doom, with an emphasis in growing and swelling when combat is at its most dangerous, or when you've pissed off the wrong boss.The combat is a classic turn based system, with the ability to overspend a character and go into burst, allowing for more actions. This system is critical to the enjoyment of the game, because it really lets you go wild when you need the damage, and allows my Prudence to absolutely dunk a whole squad of enemies by herself. The manipulation of the turn system is similar to the likes of FFX or DOS2 where you focus on delaying the enemy while speeding your own units up.I've read some comparisons to Dark Souls and XCOM and various other franchises here but I think that those are somewhat derivative suggestions. Saying it's like Dark Souls is saying Cuphead is like Dark Souls. It's just difficult. And not difficult in an unfair, or probability based manner, like XCOM (which of course I love as well) but rather in your preparation and planning. Some other people suggest that the game is too grindy, but I think that is to overlook the systems at play. I mean the game let's you restart each run with multiple old characters. That alone allows you to easily get back to where you were with your previous run with the addition of even more leveled characters. I would encourage those of you who think the game is too hard to look closely at some of the systems available to you and abuse the mechanics for what they are. Lure faster enemies to you by clustering your characters out of range and LoS, forcing them to outrun their teammates and fight you sooner. Abuse reaction commands like Interrupting Shot and Immovable Stance, because being able to act during your opponents turn allows you to steal it. And for the first boss, please don't kill all his boys. Thank me later. As far as the bad for this game, it simply lacks the polish of a triple A budget. Some skill descriptions are confusing and force you to try the skills out to figure what they really do. Some classes are stronger than others (cough blademaster cough), and there aren't that many classes to begin with.AND FINALLY. My god the voiceover is worse than Central in XCOM. It is so bad. Please do yourself a favor and turn off the voiceover after your first run. It isn't going to help you with the game, it is just going to make you wanna crank up the Linkin Park and cry yourself to sleep. It is super depressing, super pretentious, and above all, it does nothing to over you more information about the game.If you wanna do things my way, have your best blademaster eat your best shieldmaster and watch her tap dance on enemies graves while taking no damage. I think it's worth a buy, even at full price; the devs clearly put a lot of love and care into this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Othercide is a thinking man's game. If you can conceptualize a winning strategy, the game won't stop you from using it. It doesn't matter if this trivializes the encounter, because you win by learning, not by getting lucky. If that sounds boring to you, well, to each their own. All I can say is that Othercide is the first turn-based game I enjoyed  of its turn-based combat, rather than in spite of it.The game tells you exactly what the rules are, it doesn't restrain you, doesn't pull cheap tricks on you. There’s practically no randomness involved — you only lose when you make a mistake. Figure out the mechanics, make correct calculations, and that's all there is to it. You can complete entire missions without taking a single hit. That's the beauty of it: an overpowered combination that would be considered an exploit in other games is completely valid in Othercide. However, none of this means the game is cakewalk. Every mistake you make has serious consequences, both immediate and delayed. Damage taken during one mission may spell your doom during the next one.The game has excellent visual style, majestic soundtrack (except for some of the vocals), and great overall atmosphere. There is a story, but it’s nothing to write home about. There’s plenty of in-game lore, and there are dramatic cutscenes to set the mood. There are rogue-lite elements, and that’s probably the only objectively bad part of the game — it doesn’t improve the experience, it’s just used to pad out game time. The campaign would probably take less than 10 hours to complete if it wasn’t balanced to encourage the player to start over at least a couple of times.Unfortunately, Othercide has some technical issues: there’s a somewhat rare bug that lets melee enemies hit you when you’re supposed to be out of range. It’s been a very long time since the devs promised to fix this, I don’t think it’s going to happen. I still recommend the game, because when it works properly (which it does, most of the time), it’s an absolute joy to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Neat little game I got on a steam sale, definately worth the sale price. Turn based tactical combat. I absolutely love the grey scale with red color, creates a dark vampiric feel to the game. Unique combat system based on action points. Here are some tips for beginners :- Can not regenerate HP even between missions, except if you sacrifice a characer of same level or higher. Level some characters just for the sake of life regen your main ones.-Tactics include LOS behind objects to prevent range attacks, side attacks (flanking) and Backstab (attacks from behind) get bonus damage. Delay enemy attacks by knocking them back on the attack timetable through abilities. Kill enemies before they can attack to prevent any hp loss. Sacrifice small % of life to prevent damage on self or ally and do damage back.-Generally use only 50 ap per turn so you can react easier to enemy movements. IF you are going to kill an enemy or delay it from attacking can be worth it to use all 100 AP, but this means you will be put at the very end of the attack timetable which means u have to skip the next attack round. Key point is use all 50 ap or 100ap per turn as any left over doesnt help you, the only reason not to use up to those points is if positioning is important. -Try to face your enemies to not let them attack from behind or from the side. Move close enough toward enemies that they cant attack you next turn but have to move within attack range; that way you can attack right away on the next combat round. If you have aura bonuses stack your characters together to get the bonuses.-If you have killed all or most of the monsters, sometimes you can get away with using all 100ap for movement before the next group of monsters spawn.-always do rescue mission if you think you can beat it, and collect the reward of resurrection at the end so you can resurrect a high level character.-Start by leveling 1 ShieldBearer (tank) and 2 SoulSlingers (range dps). The Blademaster (melee dps) is weakest in my opinion at low levels, once you get sidestep and lightining strike BladeMaster gets good. Blademasters are good against high armor/hp units or bosses since they have high damage single attack. Once you get higher level characters you can carry a BladeMaster to level up.-it may be tempting to skip era once unlocked, but if you do so you could miss some rescue missions and some easy exp, memories and vitae.-try to keep at least 6 sisters active at a time so you can do multiple missions before the next day if they area available, cause they do get harder as the days go by. -use the codex to read up on new enemies so you can learn their tactics.-get extra exp for each kill on the specific character that does the killing.Great game for the price (on sale)! Few things that could be better - more music and sound bites variety, more and dif types of missions, more classes to play would be great maybe as an unlockable feature, more customization of characters skills cause it seems like you have the same choices all the time. The story is not exactly forthcoming, could be a bit more clear.

_childDocuments_.review: Imho it's a bit light on content for its current price.The aesthetics work well, and are tied into the story. My main complaints would be:the strategic layer in-between missions is very light, most decisions aren't decisions as much as obvious clicks to do and it goes by quickly. You'll be mostly in mission.the tactical missions are repetitive. The game features a "fail-and-restart-stronger" mechanic in the strategic layer with ironman only, meaning you'll be replaying some of the tactical missions after failing to a boss. But even without those, you still need to do 4-8 identical missions before each boss, with repeating maps, enemies, slight variance in difficulty. This smells of padding. The tactical battles aren't complex, some stuff deals damage, there's initiative determining order, there's armor, and abilities that execute a small timewindow after you've started them. It's a 2d map in terms of how you move, and you can avoid ranged attacks behind obstacles but other than that there's no cover system, no terrain modifiers ("set the place on fire" etc).You take 3-5 daughters into combat. There are 3 classes, and about 4 levelup choices of additional abilities (2 choices per). You can also add "memories" to each ability to tweak them. There is no customization beyond this. Daughters get traits that add stats, but you can't impact them directly. You can sacrifice a daughter to heal another daughter (the ONLY way to heal, even in strategic layer) giving you a special trait. Missing from this equation: there's no visual customization, there's no item layer. The sisters all turn out almost identical depending on their class.The bosses are real challenges and I would consider them the highlight - they got their own little bit of taunting pre-battle, multi-phase battles, just feel very well executed.All this considered, the game feels a bit grindy. Either because you're working your way to the next boss through identical missions, or because you failed the boss and have to do the same missions again. (ps. once you beat a boss you can re-start after the boss, with higher level daughters etc)
