_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I wanted to say that I am  and recommending it.It has everything I want from the games: amazing soundtracks, difficult choices to be made, great looking visual effects/graphics and a lore to be explored. Mother (player) is leading her army (daughters) against evil forces (The others) which trying to torture and then destroy the world.1. you will fall and will be destroyed just to rise again even stronger;2. you will be forced to make hard choices such as sacrificing your daughters for the greater good;3. timeline and your position on the battlefield are the keys to victory;4. game will punish you for every mistake you made;5. there is autosave onlyYes, that is correct. The game wants you to fail just to follow the path of the phoenix such as "you give everything you have got, you die and you become even stronger after rebirth". This rebirth can be activated manually (next recollection) or automatically when all of your daughters were killed (same recollection mechanic).The next recollection will reset everything you have achieved except remembrances bonuses (for example, +15% of health for all daughters), special currency for buying remembrances and 3 strongest of your alive daughters. Also, last 32 dead daughters will be saved in resurrect chamber to be revived for special in game coins.This is the main idea of the game: you have to sacrifice daughters to win a battle and this war. This sacrifice can be made by:- holding the enemies to let other daughters and/or bright soul escape- sacrificing daughter to heal another daughter (there are no other way to heal daughters in nightmare mode)By doing the sacrifice you are not just healing daughter but also give her part of her sister power called traits (for example +532 HP and +1% of evasion). So as mentioned in item #1 by each loss you become stronger.The timeline in this game is dynamic and each move/attack/ability might change the order of turns and possible outcome of the fight. Your daughters are always outnumbered (sometimes 4 or 5 times) and sometimes outgunned (enemies are stronger) on the battlefield. This are your main disadvantages. In order to defeat your enemies you should:- keep your daughters united and enemies separated to face it one by one or wave by wave (use terrain features and timeline management);- analyze each your move and keep an eye on enemy attack range;- remember that each hit your daughters take will move you closer to a hard choice of sacrifice.As mentioned in previous items, each action has a consequence; each hit will move you closer to a needed sacrifice; each death of your daughters will lower your army number. So keep that in mind when you play this game of thrones scenario;Action has consequences and you cannot escape it by shutting down game and reloading last save. Every move you make, every action you do will be registered for the only one goal: to face the outcome of your choices.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often review games, but I had to post my comments on this.  People have called this a hidden gem and I agree. _childDocuments_.review: Mechanically, it's an interesting twist on turn based tactics, the timeline system makes you think differently from standard turn initiative and will likely make you adapt and change your play style. If you play a substantial amount of games in this genre like Xcom, Mechanicus, Wartales, etc this is a good thing because it may force you out of your standard style you usually apply to these sorts of games. The sacrifice mechanic is also an interesting twist on more standard permadeath. You should not play in the easy mode, you would be missing a primary point of the game. The Daughters are literally made to die and be sacrificed for the greater good and is in alignment with the theme of the game. The story is a bit odd, it's delivered in a way I would describe as 'dreamlike' and leaves a degree of interpretation open, although the main core of the story will be fairly clear. None of the characters are supremely deep, if nothing else just due to limited exposure, but most will still leave an impact. Especially the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Deacon. Aesthetically, quite frankly, it's very edgy. This is not a bad thing in itself, it's not a type of edgy that is dripping with nihilism and bitterness that would turn me off. It may initially seem that way, but once you get deeper in there is a core idea of enduring suffering towards a good purpose being worthwhile. The aesthetics reflect this, and are pretty cool IF they dont instantly turn you off, which I wouldnt blame you for. It's a pretty exacting style they've got going on. One other neat thing is that due to the format of progression, once you beat the game you can go back and fight any boss at any level tier freely, which I'm not sure I've seen before. My main critique is in amount of grinding necessary, paired with the number of maps. You get to a point where the fights get pretty samey about halfway to 2/3 in because you start to see the same map+enemy layout frequently enough that you just go through the motions once you recognize it. A handful more maps would make a substantial difference. The music is also worth highlighting, most of the boss tracks are unarguably excellent, though lyrics in a boss track are always a bold choice and dont always work. I personally enjoyed those tracks too, but it did strike me as weird when they first kicked on those boss fights that had that kind of theme,. Not all the tracks are metal, but if you hate metal you probably will not be enthused by the game in general.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've ever thought, "Hmm, I love FF Tactics and MCR, how can I blend these into an interactive story experience?", Othercide is your answer. This game does a good job of telling a lovely and emotional story interwoven with interesting gameplay. The choices of playable classes for your characters is a bit limited, but you can pretty quickly build a good roster and change team compositions to suit the particular mission requirements.The combat mechanics benefit from player choices with character skill customization and items, which gives each player a way to tailor the synergy of their teams to suit their taste in play-style. One thing I did enjoy was the inclusion of the combat timeline, a HUD feature that shows you when your character will be able to act if you take certain actions, when delayed attacks will trigger, when enemies will move or take actions, etc. At first blush the content might seem a bit shallow. I think there are 35 - 40 "days" to play through, but each "day" has multiple missions to play unless it is a boss mission. You are probably not going to get through the full game on your first playthrough though, and the game is designed with that in mind. All told, I clocked around 67 hours to get most of the achievements and beat the final boss, which was a satisfying amount of playtime for me.I would give this game overall a 7.8/10, and definitely recommend to anyone looking for a tactics-style game.** DISCLAIMER **- I got this game at a significant discount during a sale (picked it up for just under $10), but having now played the game through to completion, I assure you that the price point has zero influence on my recommendation. -** SECOND DISCLAIMER **- I am not going to hide the fact that the overall aesthetic of this game is going to bias my opinion significantly. I love the art style, the atmosphere, character design, and soundtrack of this game. Deal with it. -

_childDocuments_.review: Othercide was a diamond in the rough for me. It took me a bit to... "get it", so to speak. Once I did, I absolutely loved it.The game is a slow roguelite, so I didn't really get what it was going for for the first run, I still enjoyed the turn based tactical combat and the aesthetic (visuals, sound design, music and voice acting are all top notch from the get-go) but gameplay wise it wasn't really clicking for me. With only 3 character classes and only 3 abilities each, the variety in the combat was a bit limited, and there were enough mission types to keep me going but not to have me feeling hooked.It wasn't until I got utterly destroyed by the new enemy types that appear after beating the second boss that I started to understand the gameplay loop of the game. After losing (or choosing to start a new Recollection), you are given the option to activate "Remembrances", which are passive buffs or bonuses that make your next recollection easier and more dynamic, while allowing you to start the game at a later stage, to not have to play the early levels over and over again (which I still did because I wanted my Daughters to level up and be a little OP to face the bosses, cause they can kick your ass pretty quickly if you aren't well prepared).Once I got my Daughters to level up and unlock new abilities I started realizing the cool combinations you could create to control the tide of battle (especially by equipping Daughters with Memories, which improve their base abilities with a variety of cool bonuses), and the game completely clicked for me after Recollection 3, which I had to start after the third boss  (which was cool because I got to start again with the coolest surprise the game throws at you, ).I absolutely recommend this game, even if the start may be a bit slow and confusing. The whole vibe of the game is wonderful, the main story is pretty cool and the side story that you unlock as you play got me in the feels, really well written stuff. I loved the game and will probably play it again on Nightmare mode one day (yes, I played on Dream because I like my games to be fun, fight me).

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game, if you easily form headcanon for characters in games, this essentially feels like watching a squad of recruits gradually become stronger and make their way in a dangerous mission to save the world. The thing is, some of your girls will fall by the wayside and die, some new recruits will serve as fodder to heal up the ones you care about via sacrifice, then the rare few will distinguish themselves through experience and acts of valour. In most games this would be a blessing, and it is, it's also a risk. Having one character make it to level 10 whilst the rest are hovering around level 7 means she won't be receiving ANY healing for the forseeable future - so you'd better keep a resurrection token just in case. But make no mistake, watching your favourite become leader of the pack, able to solo some missions, guide newbies through others, or team up with her 'second in commands' in your next 2 strongest and take on the horrors ahead is great. The attachment you feel to your units is what makes sending them into danger meaningful. And restarting a run never feels like the end, it feels like anticipation of building back that strength and resurrecting a pseudo-saint to show the new batch of warriors how it's done.The bosses also feel extremely fair and reward slowing down and thinking. Just hitting them really hard with your strongest units isn't always how you win. Can't recommend it enough.

It's actually quite a difficult game to complete with lots to get frustrated at, so if you have a disposition of getting frustrated easily, I would definitely avoid.PERSONAL NOTEI was sucked in by the cool artwork, stayed because it's actually a good game... _childDocuments_.review: Another hard game to judge. Purely on tactical combat it's decent. My MAJOR ISSUE is that it was a drag towards the end. Also don't look at my play time, I was alt tabbed playing league of legends most of the time on this game, which is a testament to how i felt about it at the end. If you enjoy SRPGs, tactical combat, progression systems that make you feel stronger, and moderately difficult game-play then this game is an instant buy. But, and BIG BUTTS ARE HERE, it gets a little repetitive at the end and the challenge evaporates. There is no narrative what so ever to keep you interested (this is no fire emblem) and the customization is bare bones but what is there has meaningful decisions to be made. The core of it is this -  the rougelite elements detract from the game utterly. The randomized levels don't do much to elevate the game but rather hurt it. These drab samey levels with similar enemy placement. The game is also a very player phase oriented with powerful abilities reserved for limited use on enemy phase.  Overall really a decent SRPG with decent style. I wish i could give a mediocre review, but I'll thumbs up because i think it was a good effort. But I will ultimately forget this game in a few months. _childDocuments_.review: HelloThis is personally for me one of my favourite games to date. The art style and environment of the game is something that appealed to me straight away. Its dark, gloomy and really portrays the concept of little hope. The game itself is a tactical turn-based game. Roguelite only if you fail but considering the game can be completed in a single remembrance according to the hidden achievement. This would make it just tactical turned based if you can achieve it. The Daughters are each unique in how they should be used and the combos you can pull off are satisfying when you get it just right. The main complaints for this game as that is what should be important to comment on. I wish there was more than 4 Classes, but it was Ok. The maps do get repetitive with some maps only used a handful of times. More maps, more enemies, more classes, more skills. Just more of everything and id love the game to 10/10. As it stands the repetition does begin to show itself. Important points i think should be mentioned. Game is separated into 4 Era's (Sections). When you complete one, then if and when you fail you don't have to start from the beginning. You can select a remembrance in game to start at the beginning of the Era you failed with stronger daughters. Your second run will be Recollection 2. Things by design are harsh, first encounters will sometimes end badly and sometimes you just have clearly the wrong build for the mission you entered. An example one of the bosses loves its armour, if you enter without a means to shred it, it will be quite difficult. While other bosses have no armour at all, then it’s pointless to take armour shredding. Don't be afraid especially if you failed once already to just start boss fights earlier. The game by design each fail you come back a lot stronger. I’d say 1st Recollection Brutal. 2nd Recollection is Hard. 3rd Recollection is Normal to Easy. (In fact, I found it too disappointing at Recollection 3. It really was way to easy). I strongly believe only if your going for the single recollection run, then skipping nothing matters. Maybe i will attempt this in the coming days. Kind Regards

_childDocuments_.review: The weakest possible recommendation.It's by no means a bad game, but it feels very same-y after a few hours. _childDocuments_.review: A good T-RPG / rogue-lite with a dark story and a wonderful art style.From the first second when the game lauches, up until its end, the only colors displayed are red and shades of grey. This gives the game that dark tone and greatly helps with the immersion. The character design is on point too, both for allies and foes. The environments are original, quite mysterious sometimes, but always really pleasant to look at. The voice acting is correct although very few voice actors participated in the recordings. The sound design makes a great job at giving a feeling of power in every attack, as well. The soundtracks for boss fights are excellent, the mixer makes good transitions from one part of a song to another as you fight to add some epicness to your actions. In short, every artistic aspect of the game is wonderful.The lore is nice (but mostly dark), it is explained through cinematics, dialogues, and notes to unlock. The lore doesn't unlock itself in chronogical order, so it's best to finish the game first before looking into it.The gameplay is nice, it uses a turn-based approach with a chronological order to determine who will act next. One needs to have strategy both in terms of placement and chronology-wise. Acting too much at an instant will result in more delay before the next action of the character, but also allows to have an increased damage output or to make buffs last longer. Each character can counter-attack and react to some specific event, allowing for devastating combinations. Enemies are strong and often benefit from a numerical advantage to force damage-control situations. Everyone's abilities are clearly explained, leaving no space for unfair surprises mid-fight. From a run to another, the rogue-lite elements make a huge difference in difficulty, and no real grind is necessary to unlock all of them. Bosses won't go down without a tough fight on their first encounters, too. The sisters' classes choice is permissive, one can survive most fights with any team composition, which is nice.Unfortunately, the game is plagued by a few bugs. It happens extremely frequently that the display of two attacks' ranges get mixed together for some reason, or that AOE attacks tiles remain stuck with danger indications when there really isn't anything there, which hides real danger indications. This gets slightly annoying against AOE heavy bosses once the map is covered in red skulls that indicate nothing. After a few dozen hours of gameplay, the enemies' behavior appears to be simple as well. The only real difficulty comes from the number of foes that spawn at once, and strategies might get repetitive over time. In some cases, elements of your save might get deleted without a warning as well. Some lore related elements got deleted on my second completion of the game. Make backups of your saves just in case something like this happens to you.A specific setup with a boss will lead to an infinite loop of chain reactions mid-fight, one-shotting your whole squad and ending your run abruptly, or softlocking you.  Beware.Overall, the game is good, I would give it a 7/10 for the looks, lore, and nice gameplay ideas. The 3 missing points are due to the amount of bugs one may encounter while playing.Also, it was made by a French game studio, what more can we ask for ? :)

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Crunchy XCOM-like tactical combat without the annoying base management. Many missions can be played perfectly with smart play and the right combination of caution and aggression. Pulling that off feels great. Unit skill options support different playstyles, and I often wish I had a different skill, no matter which one I chose (they're all situationally useful).Cons: Feels like the limited map and enemy pool should result in repetitive game play, but the combat loop is so good it doesn't. A few glitches (like double-voice-triggers playing audio over itself) are annoying, and some can detract from the gameplay until you learn to account for them (mostly related to boss AOE ground indicators getting out of sync with where the effect will actually land).???s: The setting leans hard into the tropes, and plays it straight. Probably not for everyone. Art style is similarly polarizing, though the scarves turning gray is a nice touch. The unit customization allows for a lot of unique setups, but there's no characterization; they all feel replaceable. Having same-class units with different skills can get confusing ("oh, shoot, they don't have the teleport I built the plan around..." etc.).One of my favorite games in a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: Noir Claymore with a Lovecraftian twist.'Othercide' is an ingenious name for this game. Gameplay is brutal initially and seems unfair since you cannot heal any of your daughters without sacrificing another (she has to be the same level or better to be sacrificed), but it gets easier as you learn the mechanics and your daughters level up. _childDocuments_.review: interesting project, with dark theme and tactical combat. there will be plaguebearers\doctors, spirits and all other kinds of monstrosities, the enemy design is rather gruesome, stuff for nightmarescombat is turn based, one misstep may cost you a unit or a big hunk of unit HP, so you have to get used to enemy AI patterns for optimal play and understand your own strenghts and weaknesses.progression goes by Eras, each Era lasts 7 days. each day has a set of available battle encounters for which you can participate, each encounter after success locks out particiapting units until next day. you unlock boss encounter midweek which you can do anytime to progress to next Era or wait till 7th day where you'll haveno choice but to confront boss.progression system suggests that you are expected to lose over and over, starting over from the beginning (and if you managed to kill some bosses - skip some Eras that you alrady played through). basically, Game Over is not exactly that, but rather a New Beginning. you get special resources (Shards) that are accumulated from encounters you cleared and which can be used only after starting new Recollection, which is caused either by Game Over or by player deciding that enough is enough. in new Recollection you get to spend Shards to use unlocked Era skips and various power ups to support your progress3 unit types at the start (more unlocked further as you progress). Tank unit, Melee unit and Ranged unit. all have their pros and cons and skill development. Most encounters have 3 units max lockout, but some will have you take max 2 or max 4+. game suggests synergy between units, so its good if you can learn how to do combos (e.g. one unit pushes enemy close to another unit that used interrupt ability which causes them to automatically do damage when enemy enters melee range with them)what game really lacks is narrative. it is there, but it isn't at the same time. nightmarish setting probably suggests for mistery, it doesn't feel like a mistery, rather "♥♥♥♥ happens, we are not telling you why and to what end, just bear with us"overall, good game. totally recommend

_childDocuments_.review: Is Othercide your next strategy game? I'd say the answer is "maybe," but leaning towards "yes."First, the good.The game's presentation is top-notch. The art style is absolutely gorgeous, the animations are all convincing, and while the soundtrack can appear muted but serviceable in standard battles, it gets cranked up to 11 for each boss fight, each of which being extremely well-designed with unique strengths and weaknesses. The game's enemies are predictable in their behaviors, meaning that with time and practice you can anticipate their moves and counter them like a master playing chess. The story, while initially told in piecemeal fragments, is also exceptionally well-written. The challenge the game presents is significant, but it never felt truly insurmountable, and the usage of the timeline system to alter when both friendly and enemy units take their respective actions was always consistently engaging in every fight.Then we have the not-so-good.The enemy design in Othercide is, in a word, fun. Your initial enemies are horrifying to behold, but (mild spoiler) in the end stages of the game, you'll find yourself going up against beefed-up versions of those same units. In the same vein, the stages you find yourself fighting in are rarely noteworthy, and while they might be put together in interesting ways, they have a tendency to repeat. There's also the matter of sacrificing your Daughters - your units - to heal your other Daughters. At first, the decision of who to give up and who to save was interesting to the point of choice paralysis, but I found myself growing numb to it over time. With all that in mind, I would still argue that Othercide's positives outshine its negatives. This is, at its core, a game that has been put together extremely well. It isn't perfect, but what we have at the present is more than enough to get me hopeful for a sequel, and despite its comparative brevity to some games (I was able to beat the game and unlock the entire story in about 30ish hours), it was an experience that'll stick with me for quite a while to come.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just... WOW! Such an incredible gem! First of all the art direction is astonishing (especially if you like the macabre theme). The black and white setting with splashes of red makes for a very authentic world. Those visuals are supported by more than commendable audio (shrieks, whispers and VO). The whole package is a real audiovisual treat.Secondly, and of course more importantly, this game is just a blast to play. Lovely turn based tactics and combat, where you can pull off some splendid tricks. I literally finished levels with one mouse-click (bring your Scythedancer to level 15 and you'll understand). Perhaps the gameplay isn't as unique as the art but it's rock solid nevertheless. Where the game really shone for me was the initiative order and recollection system. No Xcom-alike heroes first and enemies second setup, but a combined initiative order which can be manipulated (you feel so smart doing that). The recollection system grants you extra options and possibilities once you have to start over. It's a lovely system that balances the game for you no matter your skill level.Lastly, I really liked the 'point of view' the game has on (the) main characters. You're playing with a team of Daughters so no masculine, pumped up, brainless machos here. It felt like a fresh wind of air. Because you're Daughters all look like very fragile schoolgirls, it was even more impressive when they sliced some monstrosity in half. :)The only downside of the game is its size. There aren't that many levels, so there is an element of repetition involved (didn't bother me that much because I just luuuv it). So, devs, make my day and create some DLC!!!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good. But it's hard to learn. The new attacks aren't explained well & it's difficult to know how memories affect attacks in real terms. That means you end up looking for info online & land on quite a few spoilers. Which is a pity. It would be nice if the interface was more clear about how to use it.Also notifications don't go away after being visited. That's confusing because you feel like you're still missing something.I'm still trying to understand if there is an advantage to keeping action points for the next turn queuing system. They really need a tutorial for all those intricacies.Boss is super hard. I died from a boss & it restarts & my daughters are reset to starting level. Only recollection buffs remain. But honestly, I'm going to have to restart countless times to get the buffs to defeat even the first boss. Either that or I don't understand the interruption system.Also, it doesn't really say how many daughters you need. & there doesn't seem to be much info about how sacrificing one does anything useful. If you have enough daughters, you don't need to sacrifice to heal? Just use one that isn't damaged? & Sacificing for skill adds almost nothing compared to the cost of sacrifice. That isn't well balanced. Makes it feel like it's more worthwhile sacrificing for health & stacking all experience on 3 daughters. But then daughters that have played a mission, it doesn't seem that they can play a second mission in that turn? Again, this is not clear if adding health would reset their turn playing ability? So again. Don't really get the point of sacrificing daughters for health. Another not well explained or not well balanced game mechanic.So it's hard. It's not well explained. But I'm still keen to try a bit. But right now seems to me like you can't pass the first boss without restarting the game 7 times. Not sure if that's the whole point. If I've picked the wrong skills doesn't it mean the skills are not well balanced?

_childDocuments_.review: So I may not have played this game for the longest time, but I absolutely love it. It is just my niche of weird and creepy, while still being really fun and engaging on the strategy game front. First I'll start with what attracted me to the game: the art style. Now obviously this will be subjective due to the nature of it being so stylised, but oh my god I love it. I didn't even know this was an art style I loved until I saw it! If it was just the monochrome black and white I wouldn't care so much, but just that splash of red does so much to bring out everything and make it as visually appealing as it is. While I'm on the superficial stuff, there's a particular song that's made its way into a couple of my playlists, and some of the VA is chilling. I'll admit, lines can get repetitive sometimes, but there's a few voices (the Deacon is coming to mind) where the delivery of those lines are just... disturbing in the best of ways. Now let's get to the meaty bits: mechanics! At a surface level it all seems rather simple. You control 3-4 units (called Daughters... did I mention this game gets weird?) each having one of three classes. The Blademaster, the damage dealer of the three, just don't let it get hit.The Shieldbearer, the tankiest of the three as well as the one most capable of controlling crowds. Mobility is on the low end though.And the Soulslinger, dual wielding pistols to provide ranged support to her sisters.Every Daughter and active enemy unit on the map gets placed on a timeline, which dictates when they get to act. Each Daughter has an amount of action points, you spend them to move and use abilities, end turn to move down on the timeline. Use up only half your action points, and you go halfway down the timeline, use up over half your points however and you end up all the way at the end of the timeline. Seems simple enough, but it's one of those systems that's easy to learn but has plenty of depth to master. How well you can manipulate and manoeuvre yourself around the timeline will dictate how successful you'll be. Though there is one thing I have yet to mention: health. What could be so special about that you ask? I'm glad you did! Your Daughters will have access to certain skills that, rather than having an action point cost, have a health cost to activate. Now you may be thinking "oh that's not too bad, you can just heal them right?" to which I'd respond with "you poor naive fool." Y'see, you can't just regain health in Othercide. If you want to heal your Daughters, you have to sacrifice another one. The health of your Daughters will not be regained in any other way. (IMPORTANT NOTE: There is an optional difficulty setting where Daughters will regain a portion of health each day. There is no shame being on this setting! It's the one I play on after all)So that then begs the question: what happens if you do lose all your Daughters? The answer is easy: you try again. Armed with the knowledge of what you now know, as well as your choosing of buffs that you can apply to your next run to give you more of a fighting chance, you keep fighting. Again. And again. Just because you have been defeated doesn't mean all is lost. The veil has been torn, time has ceased to work, reality has been fractured, so what's a few more attempts to conquer Suffering between a mother and her daughters?I am aware that last sentence probably made no sense... did I mention this game gets weird?To summarise, the foundation of this game is a solid turn based strategy game that's easy to learn with plenty of depth to master. The decoration is an absolute treat to the eyes, the story is all sorts of weird and fascinating, even if a few of the voicelines won't leave my head. Just don't be discouraged if you fail, it's almost encouraged to fail at least once!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: I would recommend this game if you like XCOM and Darkest Dungeon. As for tactics games, it adds a cool initiative timeline system with the concept of taking a half turn. Also, you can never heal your units between battles without sacrificing others. You will lose units, you will lose and have to start over, it is brutal just like Darkest Dungeon.The good:Excellent art style! The scarves that your daughters wear are also HP bars. They lose their red the closer they are to dying.The timeline, with delayed moves and windups this makes initiative more than a roll.Not being able to heal units, Sounds bad, but makes HP a limited resource. It also adds strategy between fights.Boss fights are hard, and if you fail you have to start a whole new game. High stakes!The bad:Unfortunately, it gets a bit repetitive quickly.Not a large array of maps.High stakes game, just like Darkest Dungeon. If you don't like Darkest Dungeon you won't like this.Only 3 different units.The ugly:Nothing!Wrap up:If you like Darkest Dungeon and you like XCOM, you will like this. The only real downside is that it feels repetitive faster than Darkest Dungeon and XCOM do and I'm not sure why. Still worth the money, even more so if it is on sale!

_childDocuments_.review: A very cool idea misguided by an artistic direction that tried a bit too many things at the same time making the gameplay suffer because of it.The game is good, at least the concept of it, I like the "bloodborne-ish" setting, the very vague explainations of the victorian setting and how the timeline works, both in combat but also in the overall managment of the game. Unfortunately the gameplay is barebone to say the least. I think the developers don't understand what makes these strategy game such as X-Com work, and I think it's the fact that the player has to navigate an enviroment and move forward on the map. All missions I've played so far are the opposite in this game. You just sit in the middle of the map and defend from swarms of enemies that come to you, which devolves very rapidly into "camping the center" and waiting for them to be close enough to be attacked but not close enough to attack you, by moving your units so that they are just 1 square away from the enemy, so that when they approach they can't attack. And that's literally it when it comes to gameplay. Thow your characters at the game till you have strong enough characters so you can revive them in the next run and start advantaged so you can progress further, but there is absolutely NO skill in how the game is played, it's incredibly boring.The art direction, while cool, also is boring. The black and white style looks nice for 1 hour, then the brain starts begging for colors and VFX which are nowhere to be found. I like the short cutscenes that play sometimes during combat, but they are very repetitive as the amount of em is limited and gets old quickly.One thing that I really, really dislike is the Darkest Dungeon rip-off Narrator. They just hired a lady to spout a couple of "cool" phrases, very much like DD Narretor does. The problem here is that these phrases aren't cool and the language isn't interesting, they sound flat and uninspired. The fact that they are very few makes it even worse. You'll costantly hear the same 3-4 phrases repeated over and over and over during gameplay.Overall, I strongly suggest NOT to buy the game, not even on discount, as the core gameplay is boring, repetitive and grindy. They attempted to create a mix of darkest dungeon and roguelite with x com elements in it, which is amazing on paper, but entirely failed to understand what made these games great.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a game that takes advantage of multiple other games' themes, go for this one. First and foremost, there's the combat; a timeline is always nice in turn-based games. You can use memories, which are essentially perks, to adjust how your Daughters (Your team characters) play. For instance, you have a standard attack that would normally just swing once; add a certain memory and it now slows the enemy, making it so that they have to wait longer before they can make use of their turn. Mix this with other characters that can punish the foes because they have extra time to attack and you create deadly combos.Seeing just how far you can develop your characters gives you a strong sense of power as you progress. Similar to that one time you decided to go to the gas station at 10pm because you were just aching for a doughnut that late in the day, you're overcome with a sense of satisfaction upon completing a combat that you needed to think through, debating whether or not that next move will be the end of you.You WILL lose your sweet princesses on the battlefield. That's a promise. Whether it be because an insect decided to spit one too many times on them, or she just cleaved in two because of a frightening guy holding scissors, you're bound to part ways with the teammates that you spent so much time using. That's why there's a system just so the players can become sociopaths! Let it be known that you can't heal naturally. There are no skills, no special items, nothing. That's when you finally give in and say, "She only has 12hp left out of 3,000, let's SACRIFICE her to heal my other character that is halfway full already!" Kind of brutal, kind of nifty. Bear in mind that you will lose a character that is of the same level (or higher) if you decide to sacrifice in order to heal another.Then we come to the story. Overall I've been enjoying it, well enough to know that I'll strive to make it to the end of the game. The boss battles are punishing, so it's rewarding to find out just where the game's direction goes. If they don't add more content I will honestly be surprised. I've already noticed from the beginning that the lore is deep, assuming you're willing to read the pages in the codex. With that in mind, it's good, and seeing more bosses, maybe even mini-bosses in future patches/updates will only help the game. Overall, Othercide is an excellent turn-based, rogue-like, female-protagonist, strategy game. Final review: 8.8/10 great game.

Sure you can change her hairdo, eyes and what-not, all of which are indistinguishable in-game. Here it's just the opposite, you're urged to keep every one on the same level, with basically the same tried-and-true team composition every game, and favoritism is severely punished. _childDocuments_.review: is a turn-based strategy involving some future event, and the need to produce daughters to circumvent this event that seems to be at some point in the future or past, during the opening of the game. Gameplay involves a good bit of grinding at its core concept. You can gain points to invest into direct abilities, and unlock things in each zone as you go along. Losing a few times is actually not such a bad thing in this game near the beginning, since you will accumulate more to spend on some of your unlocks, which you can then use to give you a slight edge.I want to make one thing fairly clear though. The game itself is not actually extremely difficult. I do not consider this roguelike either. Permadeath is there for your current run, but it doesn’t really fit many other qualifications for the genre. I would say the difficulty is in a sort of , meaning it’s grindy, and time-consuming to raise your daughters, of which there are several classes with varying abilities. The learning curve is the only problem, then it becomes somewhat clockwork in nature. Some of the daughters were unbalanced when I played last. The big issue with the way the grind system is set up is that inherited traits of classes are the same for each class type, and you only get one, which is in red on your skills for the daughter that received the benefit from a daughter of a higher level, where the lower level will inherit the said trait. This is why the game is so grindy. You can also pick up random debuffs/buffs to stats that can be permanent, or practically permanent based on things your characters do while in battle. Another thing upon leveling is you gain extra usable battle skills. You can choose one or the other and it can vary depending on which you want to keep, given the situation.There were several types of situations one might end up in, ranging from surviving all waves, to reaching a goal, or escorting missions and some other various types. You may choose to skip right to bosses, bypass bosses altogether, or do other things depending on how far along you are in the game. I thought some of the bosses were hard, but once you learn what they do in each phase, you can find ways to take certain counter-measures. Most are not too hard to figure out, but there was a bit of randomness and trial and error for me. Supplementing with a guide for ideas on how to effectively play is useful, since the game didn’t really explain it too well at the time I played, in my opinion.Pretty graphics, with a noir and red style of background. The daughters reminded me a little bit of 2B or something similar, and the music paired well with the game’s overall feel and mood. The setting and plot are hard to understand much about, but things get revealed to you as you go, and there are sections to examine for unlocks, extra enemy information (which I cannot stress the importance of enough, as it reveals attack patterns, weaknesses and strengths to take advantage of), and other such things, which can be viewed in the menu any time once you’ve unlocked them.You can gain other abilities which can be applied manually to your daughters when you meet the right conditions. They are usually chance-based, but if a condition meets all unlock requirements, it’s possible to get these orbs which can be later added. They are removed after a game ends. Your daughters you lose can be resurrected as well later on as you open up more abilities, so a complete wipe isn’t necessarily a bad thing in many cases in this game. Early on you probably won’t really  be worried about specific daughters, and may instead try to get a few with some good overall stats, since these can vary.While I think the game is good, I also think there is a lot of untapped potential in what is possible with this system and the way it was done during the time I played this game.Lots of customization is possible. More is possible with further optimization and unlocks, further adding to possibilities.Nice graphics, and the gameplay is fun early on, as I got introduced to the game. It can get a little bit repetitive, due to only a few classes of daughters to choose from, thus limiting your movesets.I liked the counter-attack system, and the attack time grid at the bottom of the screen. This could be somewhat exploited early on, but as far as I’m aware, most instances of this have been hit with the nerfbat.Decent amount of variations, and different ways to play, based on how you choose to set up your party. Good to strategize, since you can only fight once per day and need a rest with daughters. There is an easier mode where resting gains life. I never tried the other mode as of yet though.The game could use more enemy types, varied attacks, and different characters and encounters. While the game is fun, it is still tedious and a bit predictable at certain points, depending on how familiar you get to creature habits and how to move your daughters efficiently to get the most out of them.The roguelite elements are only having to do with earning extra currency to buy more skills as you unlock them with progression. This value only decreases in the current game, and you continue to gain more as you fail.Very grindy when I played. This is what ultimately made me take a break from playing. I still don’t really feel like finishing this yet, but I do believe it will be enjoyable to jump back into playing again sometime and see how it is now compared to when I played it in October or November.The battle speed was a bit slow too. Even speeding things up, it was a bit of an annoyance to wait on everything to finish turns.Just felt inefficient and unbalanced having to grind and keep levels close, so I could then add stats in sacrifices.Good foundation here, but I see a lot that could be built upon. I personally felt that this game should have been in Early Access or beta still when I played.Way too expensive for the amount of material in the game, however it still feels like a higher quality game than many out there, most likely thanks to publishing and development making polished and crisp graphics a big priority. The scenes and action bits are quite nice in presentation, so I did enjoy some of the cutscenes.Some of the voicing would mess up, be silent, or overlap. Not sure if this was corrected or not.  It’s also a bit repetitive since there are not a huge amount of phrases.No 9S in this game. Why can’t there be some dudes around?! I’m probably out of room now, but this one is tough for me to swing one way or the other. Paired with the expensive price, I recommend this but with some caution. It’s not a game for everybody, and the tags are a bit misleading. Buyer beware! Still a nice game overall, but I hope there have been some improvements since I last played. I’ll update if I decide to finish the game and go for all the achievements! All in all this one is worth a go, but do not run into it with majorly high expectations!Game curator review made possible thanks to  for allowing me to review this, courtesy of

_childDocuments_.review: My first impressions:TL;DR:Othercide is a blend of genres that isn't seen very often,but works surprisingly well. On the one hand there is the Turn-Based combat that can almost rival XCOM in terms of depth. It's easy to learn but hard to master. Making full use of all the options given will require lots of strategic thinking. This paired with the punishing difficulty makes prevailing here hugely satisfying.And while it is certainly hard, it doesn't feel unfair. Looking back at a turn, you can almost always identify something that you could've done differently to prevent a characters death, due to the large amount of options the game gives you, in terms of skills, movement and special character traits.On the other hand you have a lot of Roguelite elements sprinkled in there, that will allow you to make progress and get stronger even if you fail. And you will fail - but like any good Roguelite, Othercide mixes things up from run to runby having a degree of randomization, as well as allowing the player to shape the outset of a run.Add to all of that the unique, dark aesthetic and you have yourself a recipe for greatness.An experience that I recommend to anyone that even remotely enjoys turn-based combat games!

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly? This game was hard to get into. The fact that it became repetitive after 2 hours due to the lack of variety in the maps made it feel weird. However this game grew on me the more I played it. Don't get me wrong it does feel repetitive at times HOWEVER the gameplay is what carries this game along with the unique artstyle that accompanies this game. This game is less intense compared to XCOM. I would say this game is comparable to a game of chess. Every unit u control and move must have a move planned ahead of time to ensure success in missions. The mechanic of using AP which decides what u can do per turn helps elevate the feeling of playing chess across this game and it's what got me hooked despite it being repetitive. The gameplay mechanic of having your daughters heal only when you sacrifice another daughter adds a layer of depth that I didn't think was possible. Do you heal the lower level daughter to invest into her development? Or do you keep the high level daughter despite her having low health. Such questions are asked while you are playing the game. Trust me you are meant to die but through each death you adapt your tactics, get more powerful daughters, get more powerful relics to start each run. Each run that you do in this game has a purpose and certain elements are carried onto the next run. This is a very good roguelike game worth your money. Yes it will get repetitive but the feeling of killing your first boss after multiple runs is so satisfying I would compare it to dark souls. This game is harsh, annoying, anger inducing but man I am having one hell of a time with this game and the atmosphere and lore behind it

_childDocuments_.review: It was hard to click "no" on this one because it's such a mixed bag for me.  I love, love, LOVE the style of this.  The aesthetic to it, the music, the voice acting... it's all just so freakin' cool.  I want the Warhammer people to see this and give this developer a license to do fifty Sisters of Battle games, they've nailed how that should look, feel, and sound.Ultimately, though, it pains me to admit that this just quickly becomes not that fun a game.  I'm a big fan of tactical turn based squad games but this one becomes both repetitive and convoluted very quickly.  I was impressed by how novel the whole system was of pushing units around on the initiative line, but it wasn't meaningful enough to be all that useful.  And the interaction and complicated chain of events that could be set up between all the units and enemies interacting, especially in the boss battles... well it could have made for a chess match but instead it just gets so weird and convoluted that I feel like I need to put my data analytics training to work and build a machine learning algorithm just to figure out how to take my turn.  Information can be difficult to dig out of the interface (I'm still not sure if there's a way to view individual unit trait effects during a battle and that can be important) so you end up either having to remember or keep notes.  And I found myself having to do entirely too much math in my head to figure out what kind of combos I might be able to pull off.  What could have been cool if the information was presented effectively just became a chore.One little change to the whole RPG combat trope that I thought was great was how hit points don't regenerate between battles.  You can win the battle and still lose the war, I thought that added and interesting element to it.  Unfortunately that's coupled to a grind that's designed for you to fail.  You play a bunch of missions, you fail but win some bonuses, and then you try the same thing again.  That doesn't make for a satisfying game loop, because you don't feel like you won.  You just come away feeling like you persevered long enough that the game eventually felt sorry for you and gave you enough bonuses so you could proceed.I liked the haunting nature of the story but that suffers from obfuscation and complication as well.  I'm sure it all ends up being some kind of deep metaphorical look at mental trauma or something like that, but it's presented all abstract and weird so you spend more time trying to guess what's going on than you do enjoying it.  Maybe it all makes sense in the end but the journey purposely just leaves you a little too lost and confused for my taste.I love this as a collection of novel ideas.  I adore it as a piece of art and style.  I wish I could say I liked it as a game, but I just don't.

_childDocuments_.review: Similar to the XCOM franchise, this is a turn based strategy game. Due to it being an Indie game, it has not been advertised widely. But it is a hidden gem of a game.The game has a medieval horror setting, but it is not overdone. The in-game animation, art and soundtracks are done perfectly. Especially, the use of only three colours throughout the game (black, white and red), which perfectly conveys the desolate and unforgiving vibe in the game.The game expects you to lose, you cannot finish the game in a single run. But it rewards your run by progressively unlocking more powers and levels on your daughters (the heros that you control) in your subsequent runs. I recommend the 2nd difficulty mode for getting the true experience( there are two difficulty modes - 1st one heals your daughters for 10% hp at the end of each day, while the other doesn't). In the 2nd difficulty, the damage taken by your daughters are carried forward to the subsequent missions. The only way you can heal is by sacrificing other daughters of a similar or higher level. Even some of your stronger skills in mission require you to sacrifice hp to perform. So you have to weigh the cost/benefits. The monsters are also well designed and the boss fights are epic. You also can't abuse the save option as the game auto-saves and doesn't allow you do do manual saves.The in-game story and lore are also engaging and keeps you hooked. If you are a fan of the turn based strategy genre, definitely give this game a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is good.Replayable. I thought it would get boring, but it really does not.Innovative unit level-up mechanics too.You are forced to 'blend' your units into more powerful combinations to progress deeper into the game. Its pretty cool. Starting squads will all die, you cant beat bosses with starting units. But what game forces you to do, is take your starting squads, get them killed, and combine survivors into more and more powerful characters... And so it goes. And as you get deeper, you collect trinkets that let you skip the level grind of fresh characters. After boss 1, your units start at level 4. After boss 2, units start at level 7. And so on. And you can skip bosses as well on your subsequent runs. Clever.Combat forces you to think for once. its not a steamroll at higher levels. Key abilities like overwatch, stuns and interrupts cost health, not action points. And there is no healing in the game (other then blending in the character management screen). And you can only blend units of equal level. So yeah, your characters have a shelf life, they are NOT expendable, and it forces you to think which unit to take into battle, because you have to keep multiple copies of toons roughly in equal levels - spares are used in healing/blending. No powerlevelling for U, in other words.Anyways, its a fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start with what the game does very well, and that's its style. It has incredible visuals and music, my tense battle against a boss where both sides were being beaten down and it could absolutely go either way, was far more epic than anything I encountered in X-com or x-com 2. In that regard it's amazing. Unfortunately, and this is why I don't recommend the game, the actual overall gameplay is designed really poorly. Not the tactical part of battles which are decent though not amazing, but the overall strategic layer ruins the whole game.The only way you have to heal any of your characters from the damage they take in battle is to sacrifice another character of the same level as that character. Which has a few consequences, you need to grind up throwaway characters so they're a high enough level to use to heal your good team, you are penalized for using many of your abilities that pay with health to use in battle, receiving any damage at all in battle is catastrophic. In my case I had an amazing fight with a boss, lost one of my team and the other two barely survived. That battle was an amazing experience... unfortunately trying to continue the game after that was futile, new characters were not high enough level to survive missions to grind up to heal my good characters who were on death's door. Even if I managed to level them up enough, I would just be putting all that time and effort in just to throw those characters away, it just all feels so pointless and a huge waste of time.There is some mechanic in the game that I didn't use, as it feels like cheating. You're able to restart the game but you get extra bonuses at the start, the effect being that you're essentially able to use cheat codes of increasing power every time you start the game over again. This again feels pointless, because if you do that your success in the game is determined only by how long you play and not how well you play, eventually you will just have enough bonuses to win.It's a shame because the visuals, music and atmosphere could make an amazing game if the core gameplay was any good

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing, short (25-ish hour) game that I would recommend for anybody who likes turn-based, squad RPGs like XCOM.This game doesn't have quite the same amount of gameplay choices and strategic depth as XCOM, and the map variety gets kind of stale due to the way the game is played. However, the story in the game is very well done, the themes and tone are relayed extremely well, and there are a lot of satisfying emotional beats as you discover the story of the Mother and the Child. The music in this game is particularly outstanding, and I often play the tracks to the boss fights when playing other games.The game is absolutely gorgeous despite not having the best graphics, in part to the wonderful aesthetic that is put into it. The designs of the Daughters and Monsters are really well done, and the sound design is on point.The boss fights are amazing, tense, and difficult the first time you do them. I finished the game in 4 recollections, though. I would imagine as you get more remembrances, the game gets a lot easier. I think I one-shot the first boss during my final recollection. The aforementioned amazing music and design only heightens the amount of fun you have playing.Overall, I really really loved this game. Even though the gameplay itself isn't as special as say, XCOM or even Troubleshooter: Abandoned Children, the atmosphere, story, music, and boss fights were unique and scratched an itch that I really needed in gaming.EDIT: Forgot to mention that I did recieve this on sale for around $22. Looking at the current price, it is a bit much for the amount and quality of gameplay, so I would wait to get on sale. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I actually had to switch my review from down to up, I can own up to speaking too soon.I originally thought that the game loop revolved around one boss (the one at "7 days"), and it would seem pretty repetitive/pointless to keep having to replay just those 7 days to kill it and be done. I was wrong, there was several bosses after him (each 7 days after you beat one boss), and for every step different enemies and maps open up.I loved the style and some of the improvement over your conventional tactical turn-based approach (you can do more each turn, but it will cost you "initiative" which means the next turn for that character will came later), but there is one: One, the interface is very poor, you never really know what things mean, or even what traits are active. Sometimes one of your characters have an "aura", but ... which character? what aura? you have to find out moving around. It is somewhat complicated, I think a small icon for each aura/passive skill on the character bar would be a huge improvement.The game is somewhat repetitive but each play is different in the way that you will have to build up your "daugthers" again, and there is a lot of random traits and skill you get along the way. You can revive "daugthers" from previous runs, but it is kind of costly so you will probably do it with only one or two.In the end, other than the interface lacking some information value, since this is a game where every bit of information is important, is a little distracting, but it just makes you the more focused on thinking your moves thorugh.

_childDocuments_.review: One hell of a game, pun intended. The replayability of the game stems from failure as the player has to start all over again, but the game is bit forgiving as it accumulate tokens from previous game to spend on future game. On topic of New Game +, game can get repetitive when you know the mechanics and have farmed enough tokens to overpower new game +. Overall it is a very stylish and fun game that respects the players intelligence and rewards risk taking. Well worth the money I spend on Othercide.

_childDocuments_.review: So I don't often write reviews for games, but I feel for this one I really should try to inform people who are looking to buy the game...I see a lot of the negativity around this game based on the fact it's a bad Rogue-lite game. Let me make this super, super clear. This isn't a Rogue-lite. No where in it's marketing does it call itself a rogue-lite, no where on it's website or Steampage does it call itself a Rogue-lite, it's just the community who has slapped that title on the game. The confusion around this comes from the fact the game plays off of a Time-loop where if you reach a game over, you go back to the start of the game to try again with a new unit roster and a new chance to approach challenges that might of cost you a lot previously with new strategies. For example, if you find in a stage a monster has thorns and melee units get hurt by attacking him, you might want to build a more solid ranged team to overcome that on your next run. The game isn't perfect, but I think it's a really solid Tactics game, and a lot of the critisism I see against it is really misplaced and silly. Complaining that this game is a bad Rogue-lite is about as useful as complaining that Ocarina of time is a bad FPS.

_childDocuments_.review: Reason i'm not recommending it is because its niche and does not cover Roguelite tag (which i personally picked up because it had one) it's misleading.Each tl;dr will have more detailed explanation down below, but my current statement is that this game is worth only half the price of it's original. It looks polished, but when you play you notice its design is scaled in a fashion that forces you to rebirth with additional boons that help you scale accordingly. Lacks actual rogue style elements and strongest impressions it gives are first couple of hours, each boss and the ending. It has very little to no replay value.TL;DR what's wrong, what's right ?The right stuff,Theme (world end, last hope of humanity, apocalypse, the last stand) with stylistic presentation, music, ui, character models, animations and even map designs (details that go beyond boundaries of play field) all of it is fresh, unique and well made.I absolutely adore xcom unit treatment system. No matter how much you invest in a unit, he's not immortal. All it takes is couple of slips and you're caught in regret of investing so much in one character. Each character with minimal characteristic differences grow differently and you get attached to them, maybe you start playing "doll house" and imagine them interacting with each other or bonding as they go trough missions and handle hardships. Them being veterans they soon  lead team of newcomers just to form new bonds as mistakes become memorable events that change dynamics and fill pages of story that entail them all. Emotional gymnastics and biased decisions i make as i'm being tormented by difficult decisions is what i love. Being emotional masochist this game caters to my needs.Most memorable, memory,  being first boss fight, all daughters in range of a deadly aoe attack. Only one daughter can move before it goes down, she can move boss, but only in 2 directions. Either she dies, or other sisters. Being my favorite and grown attached to her i made my decision with a heavy heart, it was a calculated and best one i could have taken ... is what i kept telling to myself. Just as memorable were equal level veterans sacrificing themselves to squeeze out more progress out of a run.The wrong stuff,While not excessively, everything else. Replayability, for average player getting trough whole story takes 40-50hours. Once you are done, you are. There are no roguelike random elements aside from 1 measly buff for that days missions (which is called an "Event"). Skill enchant system (memories) drop from specific mobs at certain percentage chance, traits (that give characters minimal boosts) are condition based with chance percentage once meeting conditions. Maps are hand tailored (assuming as i've done several new saves and noticed a lot of repeats) mob spawn locations are also handpicked. Mission types differ minimally between each type. It's the same thing every time, go to a mission, clap some naughty sister cheeks without getting hit and you're done. Repeat.Also bugs, convoluted/unclear inspection system with half predictive stats making first 20 hours very "shot in the dark" experienceDespite this game having so many rewards and good reviews i'm pretty sure they were given on same basis as i sung praise for this game in earlier stages of the game. I got hooked up on it, but as i slept on it soon this impression dissipated. Visual style is done right, theme and premise, story, additional lore is done in concise simple, but also captivating way. Few music tracks, like mainscreen "Soulswap" , first boss phase switch is absolutely on point and immersive. It feels like a proper masterpiece, but it falls short in progression, depth and clarity aspect gameplay wise.As you progress you meet enemies, after reaching certain milestone you meet next tier version of said enemies that coincidentally have (on average) twice that stats previous tier had and once you get to the next one, same thing applies. Thus restarting shortly after every milestone is unavoidable as you can't keep up with the numbers. Missions from each other differ in their completion objective, but overall will feel just like any typical Hunting mission.I'm not exactly sure where the randomness comes in that's attributed as key feature for rogue genre. Maps are hand crafted and so are spawn locations. At times in predictable patterns. Scaling, gearing, improving system. Each character upon its creation has different starting stats. (Minimal difference, but because of slow rate of growth, could be significant in order to min/max) As one levels up they gain skill at certain levels. They have a choice between 2 every time and a slot which can boost stats by equipping "memory". Which most of the time doesn't show how they interact with it. Or that this skill is being affected by the boost or have one to begin with, there are no indications when you are on about in the battle. You have no idea, unless you document it. Outside of memories and skills there is trait system. Minor buffs which are obtained by completing certain conditions you are not told (wiki has all documented), some of them despite meeting conditions still have percentage chance. Couple more desired traits have counterintuative conditions. Aside from this there is Remembrance system. Boons you obtain by fulfilling conditions. These conditions are mentioned in the journal. To acquire them you need to finish missions which give a currency and you have to rebirth to redeem the said currency. This is effectively is a catchup mechanic, giving ridiculously strong boons. Both stat and mechanic wise. From which (damage percentage boons) are not displayed into calculation until the moment you strike the enemy.Ui and clarity. It's awful as mentioned before some memories don't display their stat effects when hovering over the skill. Neither do the boons from remembrance system. Worse is when timeline in battle doesn't show duration of the buffs, debuffs of your units or enemy, but wait, it gets worse. You have the ability to click on the enemy in battle and review their skills, range which most of the time (the range) doesn't show up or is misaligned. Enemies in journal have tips about their behavior, but some of them change between different tiers making it convoluted.  Now the fun part, the bugs.I didn't experience any bugs or issues for first 20 hours, then they started popping in or i just started to notice them. In a boss battle i lost the ability to move my map around with wasd. This lead my battle against the boss significantly harder as enemy behind it (which was my desired target) could not be targeted as i hovered over it, boss stat information window would popup and hide it behind it ... Another instance, or more like recurring one is when enemy units sprawl over intersections of the fields. Meaning. Unless i however over the right quadrant, i don't know which one is he on visually. I've also had a bug where enemy would grow 4 times it's size in the background as my unit attacks something in the foreground and stays like that blocking half the map behind it. And making it virtually impossible to see attack range of the enemies behind it. In other news, i've had a instance where enemy spawns in without character model, being invisible. (I failed that battle and redid it with another group) This time, literally the same culprit as before would spawn in (note when enemies spawn in, if they are ranged they can only move, if they are melee and spawn next to someone they can attack, but generally move if there is at least one square inbetween without attacking) popup behind a unit thats over 20 squares away, perform a backstab attack of over 1k and return to his spawning location.All these reasons add up to me not recommending this game, but honestly, for me at least, it's worth the experience. I feel problem to me is that once im done with it ... it's just going to sit in my library as a ... memory

_childDocuments_.review: + black / white / bloody styling+ interesting combat system+ various combinations / combos / synergies of individual daughters+ intimate atmosphere+ music- simple and repetitive over time- minor UI shortcomingsOthercide is a turn based roguelite game with a stylized simple story. The player, with his characters of female daughters, fights hordes of cultists and demons to defeat materialized Suffering. The game has 2 difficulties, while one is original and it is not possible to heal your characters other than by sacrificing another. Which is not a particularly bad thing from a long-term perspective, because the character thus healed takes over the time of power from the victim.The player then spins in a series of repeated attempts to conquer the game, while he can, to a very limited extent, revive the characters he has lost and who keep their traits and levels throughout the game.Combat system is interesting and not too complicated, the daughters are 4 types of classes, where each during its development have a choice of a pair of skills. These skills can be modified with memories gained while playing.There are a really large number of combinations of skills, their modifications and combinations of individual characters.The game is really hard at the beginning, but with gradual repetitions, the individual characters become indestructible killing machines, which sweat really only with interesting bosses.Great music is also worth mentioning.

_childDocuments_.review: On the onset, the twists on the X-Com format Othercide takes I thought were pretty engaging and unique. And they ARE unique. But, as I played on, restarted the campaign a few time (which is a built-in mechanic), the mechanics that set Othercide apart, for me, quickly grew tedious.Personally, the biggest appeal  for the turn-based, squad oriented tactics games is taking a rag-tag group of soldiers and watching them grow and become attached as they become powerhouses, losing some soldiers here and there. X-com excels particularly well at this - it's what creates the battle to battle drama and tension.Herein lies I think the main problem with Othercide, while at the same time I acknowledge it as probably what  they intended to be their defining and most unique gameplay feature. See, due to the mechanics of failure and progression, your soldiers ("daughters") are largely expendable. In order to heal a soldier after each encounter, you have to sacrifice (kill) another one. Granted, killed daughters aren't gone forever. They go to the cemetery, which carries over to each playthrough. But each new playthrough you get 3 new daughters, which, again, you will grind to level up and inevitably have to sacrifice to heal others in order to have a healthy team for boss encounters. Now, there are mechanics that allow you resurrect dead daughters, who retain their stats, traits, etc. That, in essence, is how you go about creating a "powerhouse" team, through a long cycle of sacrificing and resurrecting your soldiers across many restarted campaigns. But, though an interesting mechanic, I think its a mechanic that is ultimately off-putting. You can see how this then becomes a tedious cycle of grinding cannon fodder, until they are leveled up enough to be able to be sacrificed to heal your actual priority daughters - that's how it actually ends up being played out - and it just takes away the attachment and tension X-com creates while making the game (at least the first 15 hours or so) kind of a bore. There are unlocks and such as you play that alleviate a bit of this, but it never got to a point where the actual slog was all that circumvented..The traits system is fun and done well (sacrificed daughter imparting traits onto the ones they heal) and of course, its got a well done aesthetic and visual style. The 'timeline' turn order mechanic I think is interesting and good take on the typical 'turn-based' gameplay, allowing for some fun decision making. Ultimately, I just think the cyclical nature of the game brings it down too much for me to recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Othercide

_childDocuments_.review: Othercide is a turn based tactical roguelite with an interesting setting and an excellent visual style. While the monochrome art with red highlights might be off putting to some, I found it to fit the setting very well and the artists have done a good job of balancing the contrast by focusing on darker colors, while white & red are used for details and highlights which makes it a lot easier on the eyes.Gameplay consists of a grid based tactical combat, but some of the core mechanics are a little different from most of the other games in the genre. Every turn you're given a base AP of 100, but if your AP drops below 50 you enter a burst state that consumes your next turn - in a way this could be seen as a chance to use 2 turns in a row if the situation calls for it, which adds a nice layer of strategy to the combat.AP is consumed by moving and casting abilities, although some special abilities such interrupts etc. use a % based value of characters HP instead. Which brings me to the 2nd twist mechanics wise, the only way to heal your characters in the game is to sacrifice another character of an equal or higher level. While this sounds rather harsh, it adds an element of risk to the game - although later on you're able to mitigate this a little by being able to resurrect a certain number of characters upon restarting a run.Due to being a roguelite, failing your run is something to be expected and often you've unlocked some new things to start out with during your current run. Which in turn allows you to have a stronger start and eventually you're able to maintain a team of characters you carry through your runs.While the visual presentation is great, the audio side has some issues in particular with the repetition of voice lines over the course of the gameplay. Music of the game is pretty good, but often a little too muted in the background. Sound effects do their job but do not really stand out in any way and while the voice overs are delivered well enough, the game has an unfortunate amount of repetition when it comes to in combat commentary - after hearing "They collect pieces of broken souls" and other melodramatic lines for hundreds of times, they get really annoying.And speaking about issues with the game in general:- While the setting of the game is great, the overall story is abysmally boring and bland.- Repetition: There isn't a whole lot of enemy variety in the game, environments are repeated often and the roguelite aspect of the game introduces some amount of grind that further highlights how repetitive some elements of the game are.- Very little replay value: Due to the grind and the repetition, there isn't a whole lot of incentive to do additional runs.- Balancing of the game is badly affected by the roguelite aspect of the game, this starts to be particularly noticeable around the end of the 3rd recollection and is especially highlighted in the 4th & 5th recollections where the difficulty spikes up a lot until you unlock specific things to mitigate it a bit.- Skill design often clashes with the mechanics, in particular with the boss battles where some skills are practically useless due to bosses having hard counters to them. Which is a shame as it punishes you for choosing specific skills.- Grind used as a padding to extend the game length- Final boss of the game is horribly designedOthercide is one of those unfortunate cases where the game starts up as a fun and enjoyable experience, but ultimately ends up having enough issues to sour the experience - in this particular case some additional QoL features and better balancing would already go a long way. For now though, I wouldn't recommend buying the game - instead wait for a sale and see if the developers patch some of the issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Now, this was an odd one. I'm a big fan of turn based strategy games such as XCOM and Fire Emblem, so to see one sneak under the radar with such a grim art style that looks straight out of Lovecraftian horror was a much welcome surprise.Othercide is a roguelike take on the XCOM formula that takes a back seat on the base building and unit upgrading, instead going straight into the combat focusing on unit placement and individual abilities between a rather limited but unique set of classes. Each class has its tree of abilities that you have to carefully consider as each unit can only have one ability over another as they level up, making each unit feel a lot more unique considering there are no customization options available. That said there is an interesting trait mechanism that is based on the personal experience of each unit, if they perform well then they gain more confidence in battle and gain positive bonuses. However, if they sustain too much damage but live, they may be hit with some devastating debuffs. Making each decision you make in combat a lot more involved, this is made even more important at the end of each mission. Units don't recover their health in between missions like you'd come to expect, instead you need to sacrifice the lives of other units to heal another. In other words when things go bad, they go real bad very fast. For me what sets this game apart is its brilliant art direction and a solid soundtrack, that said this game isn't made for everyone. If you aren't a fan of games that Othercide takes inspiration from then I really can't recommend this since this game is a lot more punishing if you don't have the patience for it. hat said if your gonna take a shot in the dark then this game earns my strong recommendation. this is a welcome breath of fresh air for me and I hope to see more.
