_childDocuments_.review: It's quite good. Given more resources, I feel Lightbulb Crew could unseat XCOM as the undisputed best within the genre.I enjoy the aesthetic, although it does feel a little try-hard and troublesome at times. They were going for melancholy/Lovecraftian, but I don't think you have to go 90% grey scale to do it. Sometimes the environments, enemies, and animations feel washed out in the grey on grey on grey palette. This is a shame because it sells the artistry a bit short in what appears to be a ham-handed way to achieve the feel they wanted. In the end it's very unique, especially within the genre. The artists who worked on Othercide are fantastic, but I believe the nuances of their work would be more appreciated if the grey scale dial went from an 11 to maybe a 9.I suppose you could call this game "unforgiving" or "not newbie friendly", and you wouldn't be wrong. There isn't a lengthy tutorial. Some of the more complicated mechanics are left for you to get experienced with mostly on your own. It's a game you will need to lose in order to win, if that makes sense. I'm not sure if this is a positive or a negative. I view it as mostly positive, but I could see it turning some new players off. I thought the design of the UI was intuitive enough to not need a full lecture on how to do everything. If a turn-based tactics game isn't just a disgustingly brutal emotional curb stomp, then I personally am not interested, but maybe I'm just a filthy masochist.My only other complaint I don't even really feel is all that valid because I don't think it would be there if this game had more of a budget behind it, but I'll mention it anyway:I just wanted more. More customization, more weapons, more attacks, and so on.That short list contains all the negative things I could say. Fundamentally all the things you need from an enjoyable TBT game are there. I couldn't help but feel that even if these developers don't choose to pursue the genre and expand on this universe, eventually they are going to create something special and genre-defining. Othercide isn't quite that IMO, but it is a damn fine game that got remarkably close while still being indie. Worth every penny and every bit of time you put into it. I'm excited to see what the future holds from Lightbulb Crew. They've made a fan out of me.

_childDocuments_.review: Got it on sale for $12 and love the genre. Have been pretty disappointed so far after being excited to play this one for awhile.This game suffers from moderate design issues and severe, experience killing UX/UI issues.A roguelite's biggest hurdle is not making things feel grindy - each run should feel distinctly different, even if slightly. So far this game hasn't offered me that at all. Upgrades are largely passive bonuses (+dmg%, +hp%, etc.) and so each run just feels like you're a little stronger - you hit harder, you can eat a little more dmg, etc. - but the core gameplay mechanics, interactions, skills, etc. have hardly changed at all for being 6+ hours in so far. Beyond that, there are lots of little things that drive me insane. For example, the game shows tiles when new bad guys are going to spawn in and where. Fine so far. But you don't know what KIND of bad guy is going to spawn in. Beyond that they get to move and attack the same turn they spawn. So you basically have to just stay miles away from any new spawns or risk getting bad RNG. In an unforgiving roguelite with permadeath, that sort of mechanic is just insanely frustrating and adds nothing to my experience. There's no strategy for the player to relate to the mechanic.That's whatever though, I can enjoy a game with those flaws. The killer for me is that WITH that design approach of lots of character improvement via passives or skill augments (e.g. teleport to a square is the base skill +add armor when landing on the square is the bonus), the game communicates these things extremely poorly. Nothing in the UI is clearly communicating which skills have perks and bonuses. Character armor is not visually represented on health bars, but only appears on the character/enemy pop-up card. The art direction is cool, but I'm constantly having to read the name of my character to figure out whose turn it is. The menus for managing your squad are cumbersome and require too much clicking. Again, the visual style causes extra energy to be spent trying to identify the characters you care about and those that don't. I really appreciate the attempt here and wish I could recommend the game, but if you're a fan of the genre you'll find constant small annoyances that will wear you out.

_childDocuments_.review: Two hours in and my number one thing that I want to make note of is that this is not XCOM and I think any comparison to XCOM is doing Othercide a huge disservice. For me, Othercide is a lot of fun and I'm eager to complete it. For anyone who likes board games, this feels very Kingdom Death: Monster, especially when you get to the bosses. I like it.

_childDocuments_.review: Product acquired through humble choice. Spoilers for everything but the lore, the reading of which in game takes a substantial amount of time to unlock, is actually a decent read, and is entirely optional.A roguelite tactics game. I don't think I've seen the two types put together before. I feel like the outcome is that the roguelite elements extend the game's length past its welcome. Not enough changes per run to justify the resets, and you will master the mechanics long before you are able to beat the game. I had fun some of the time, but a huge chunk of the time just felt like mandatory grinding and for that i can't recommend it. I think I would've been happier with it if it were about half as long. I should note here I played on the difficulty where you don't have to regularly delete your units, which I strongly suspect already made the game shorter.There are four unit types (but it takes a long time to unlock the fourth), each unit type has ten different skills. They start with two, and as they level up you can make a choice of two skills at certain levels, which is then fixed. If you're like me, you'll quickly decide which one is better and then forget the other one exists, so every unit has up to six skills (you will wait a very long time for skills five and six). Missions are for two to four units (except the final boss which is five), most are three, and there are very good reasons to run one of each. What i'm really saying here is you're going to take the same team of three units to the same ten stages to fight the same ten enemies (if you don't count enemy upgrades as new enemies), until you've played the game long enough to be able to buy the stats to survive to the end. Buying upgrades really is mostly about the number of missions you've run, since the currency used to buy the permanent upgrades is always given in the same increment from normal missions. The permanent upgrades have to be unlocked, but the unlocks come either from overall run progress or things that happen randomly over time, so you don't have to think about it or do anything different, just run about a hundred missions. That's not a joke or exaggeration- you get 25 shards per shard dropping mission and I had 3000 at the end. For your own sanity, hit the "faster gameplay" box in settings to speed up the enemy animations.When you actually get to the end, the game stops pretending balance is fun. In the end, you develop the ability to nuke the entire map at the same time, god hatches from an egg, and you kill him before he's allowed to take a turn. This is not me saying the boss is easy because you get too strong at the end. On the contrary, everyone who complained about the boss being too hard is right- I don't know what game it's playing but it's not the same one as you. If it takes a turn, it will just sit at the top of the initiative list taking actions and blowing up your units until maybe one of your units gets to take a turn, then it'll do it again. your action counters don't even work, you just lose.Instead of dealing with that, just spawn camp it and abuse the attack reaction mechanics to hit it thirty times before it can move. Did I mention attacking the final boss deals damage to your entire party, so even this strategy leaves you half dead? I hope you brought the map-wide nuke to trivialize phase one. It's the max level scythedancer skill.Your reward for getting this far is the opportunity to read the lore and trivialize the gameplay.I think the most fun I had along the way was the third boss. That was the only time where I felt like it was my fault I died rather than that I needed to come back with more stats. If you aren't set on finishing the game by then just stop, it doesn't really get better than that. The only actual new thing that happens is the monster enemies get replaced with evil copies of your own units, and you already know how those work.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I'd say the game is worth it.  Visuals, music, and sound effects are strong and immersive.  I found the noir color scheme to be very easy on the eyes.  I do agree with one of the other reviewers who complained that voice lines were kind of spammy.  Gameplay is 70% combat, 25% management, 5% story, which is great.  This is a turn-based tactics game, not an RPG or a 4x.  The story provides a sense of universe to the game, and doesn't try to do more, and I'm happy with that.  On the subject of mechanics, I like the timeline system used in this game in that it allows a unit's turn interval to dilate and contract, with sometimes even small changes one way or another having a huge impact.  The game's difficulty is pretty self-balancing, since you power up every time you restart, and thus you are able to reach further into the game each run.  I also like that reactions cost life to activate, which makes it so that you always have to weigh the consequences of using these abilities, some of which can be incredibly powerful, but also incredibly costly if untriggered.  My biggest con is how limited unit specs are with respect to ability choices.  As units level up, you get to unlock new abilities for them.  You get to choose one of two options at levels 1, 5, 10, and 15.  In most cases, there is a right choice and a wrong choice.  One ability will be one that you make huge plays with every fight, and the other will be one that kind of just has a cool name that you can look at from time to time.  In some cases, the right choice will not be obvious, but through experimentation you will come to learn that there is indeed a right choice, and you will then become very familiar with the respec mechanic of this game, which is called "sacrifice."  As far as replayability goes, this game doesn't even come close to that of an open world title, but it doesn't need to in order to succeed.  It succeeds by presenting you with difficult choices to make in order to progress.  It's nice to see that people still make games that are concise in scope in the 2020's.  You can pick this game up, level up your squad, learn all the cheesy moves, wreck all the bosses, and then set it aside for a while.

_childDocuments_.review: Full disclosure here: I originally bought the game on Switch, and played it there in my first playthrough. It was so much fun and I was so pleasantly surprised, that I decided to buy the steam version while not on sale to support the developers and to show my appreciation. Othercide finds its niche into a niche genre, roguelike, that somehow manages to be too crowded while not offering near enough titles, if that makes any sense. I feel like very few games have managed to add something to the genre in the past years, while maybe only Darkest Dungeons, Dead Cells and Hades fully succeeding in this.Otherside does a massively amazing job at telling a story that, like it or not, it's beautifully told and there to be found by those players who like to read and discover it. You don't HAVE to, and you won't be FORCED to by the game, but if you like it, go and get it. In a way it reminds me of the way titles like Dark Souls and Bloodborne tell their story, without falling into the soulslike genre.It's a really good game, that has massive opportunities for expansion (DLCs, sequels, prequel) while still offering a product completely worth its price and the time you're going to spend on it.You like to powerplay your way into games, finding neat combos that will wreck havoc among enemies? You can do that.You like to roleplay and savor your games slowly? You can absolutely do that.You have less time available and would like a game that lets you get up from the PC, go around do your stuff and come back in a few hours/days without giving you that "how the ♥♥♥♥ did this thing work" feeling? This is the game for you.You like to delve deep into your games, devour them and then replay with new choices, maybe using different combos to see how does it go if...? Yes, you can replay the game and have a completely different playthrough if you so desire.I'm replaying it on PC and loving every single moment since the very beginning.

_childDocuments_.review: I hope this is a temporary thumbs down, as there's quite a lot I like with this game but at this moment there's one big flaw.Let's get the theme and artwork related stuff out of the way: I really dig the horror setting of this game (it's NOT a horror game but a strategy game in a horror setting), love the visual style and enjoy the soundtrack. I'm not someone who's into such stuff normally but in this case they really add to my motivation to play and enjoyment.I also really like most of the design decisions in the game, most certainly including the idea of healing as well as how skill synergies work. I like that instead of having a long and linear campaign, it's designed to be replayable (though not evergreen, there's not much randomization and once you solve the system you are done with this game. Do not expect a Militia 2 or Auro here but rather Crying Suns).So what's the problem? Balance (of the initial segment). The game is split into parts that correspond to different enemy types and a final boss. The huge balance problem that exists in the game as it is now is that the initial "normal" missions are extremely easy. And you NEED to do about 10-12 of those before you can fight the boss battle, which at least in the beginning looks quite hard. So in essence, the game poses a very interesting tactical problem with that boss but then asks you to grind about 2-2,5 hours of very easy missions. And you have to do that every time you lose after the boss battle. Now after your loss, you might think "this is impossible" but then realise some interesting tactical possibilities that might actually beat it. But to try that idea the game asks you to go through hours of drudgery. Absolutely unacceptable. And also absolutely fixable, so I hope the devs do a balance pass to make the early parts of the game similarly as exciting as that first boss battle. Until then, I don't intend to do drudgery for something I paid to entertain me.

_childDocuments_.review: 2/5. Great atmosphere, utterly game breaking final boss fight. The game dives headlong into the grimdark, and nails the aesthetic. It’s too light on lore, even from a ‘hidden lore’ angle; it’s just too obtuse.The tutorial does an excellent job setting you up for the entire game, it really is a necessity. When you have a grasp on the mechanics, the game becomes a wonderful puzzle to figure out. It’s stressful yet rewarding, because when you click you can utterly devour bosses on your first try if you’re careful enough. That all come crashing to the ground when you get to the final form of the final boss.I’m not sure if this is a glitch of some kind, or the game is “working as intended,” the final boss fight is a 15-minute interactive cut scene of watching your girls die. The final boss can stun-lock your girls. All of them. All the time. Fortunately, you can unlock upgrades that make your girls immune to stun-locks.The boss stun-locks you regardless. It doesn’t care if you’ve buffed your girls out to be 200% immune to stun-locks, it doesn’t care if you have abilities that move them up the turn-based time line, the final boss will lock you out and take back-to-back-to-back-to-back-to-back-to-back-to-back-to-back turns until you’re dead. Who play tested this? It feels like nobody did. They just threw together a boss, said “how can we make this too difficult?” and then broke every single game mechanic they had.This used to be a fun game. I thought I had ways to prepare my team against the final boss, and it didn’t matter. This isn’t pulling the rug out from under you, it’s pulling the entire foundation of the house out from under you. If this is a bug, it needs to be fixed. If this *isn’t* a bug, the balance team and the play tester need to be drawn and quartered.

_childDocuments_.review: Othercide takes a bit of getting used to even for fans of rogue-like-ish games.First is the healing mechanic which isn't really a healing mechanic in the usual sense but part of your long term strategy. Healing one daughter requires sacrificing another of equal or higher level. The kneejerk reaction here is "this is stupid and wrong". The thing is that sacrificing one daughter permanently empowers the healed one and as you play you'll receive permanent unlocks that allow your fresh daughters to come with a higher level and to resurrect dead ones. This makes it easier to "feed" sacrificial lambs while also grooming your "champions" in the long term even if they die.The above is all connected to basic gameplay where you need to maximize efficiency in combat to lose as little health as possible while also wisely using your hp draining abilities for maximum effect and doing your best to prepare your "A-Team" for the boss battle so they go into it as healthy as possible. The first paragraph of enemy entries in the Codex describes their movement and attack patterns, reading these is very helpful for predicting and exploting enemy behavior. The game seems a bit sadistic when you first start but things come together after you get the first few unlocks, higher starting level, resurrection, more hp for all daughters, etc. It's an interesting system you don't see often that takes a bit of time to wrap your head around.The UI could be better in some cases. For example, once in combat you can't see which memories (ability enhancements) your have equipped so if you have multiple daughters with the same class it's very easy to forget who has what equipped.   It's a rogue-like with meta progression so obviously there's grind involved though not as much as you'd think from the first impression (thanks to unlocks). Whether it's too much or not is up to you. The game does have an option to speed up combat animations and such. Othercide doesn't have the complexity and sheer variety of something like Iratus but the combat and progression mechanics are solid and fairly unique and the aesthetics are quite stylish in a dark, edgy, French anime-ish kind of way.
_childDocuments_.name: Othercide

_childDocuments_.review: Fun gameplay for the most part, but there are too many issues that bring it down.-I appreciate trying a different art style, but the color scheme is hard on my eyes sometimes, and I frequently can't tell the difference between some of the characters, or between the types of terrain.-The dialogue in missions gets repeated so frequently I wish there was a way to turn it off.-Sometimes your abilities get locked out of use for no reason, you have to fiddle with the controls to regain access to them, and sometimes that doesn't work.-The between mission interface is f**king abysmal. There is a codex for characters, lore, upgrades etc. and each of these pages is just one long-ass list that you have to slowly scroll through, so whenever something new is added, you have to spend forever to get to it. You can upgrade abilities using items called memories, and it has the same problem. There is a huge number of memories, and you have to scroll through one smallish window to access them. They also are named in a very unintuitive fashion. Everything is called things like "purpose" and "mercy" but the names don't correlate to their function. Additionally, a memory that gives say +50 to damage is called something completely different from another memory that gives +55 to damage. So there is no way to infer a natural progression of memories, you just have to scroll through them one by one. It's stupid. When you start a new run, you can turn on bonuses called remembrances, and every run you have to turn on every single remembrance individually, and there are dozens of remembrances. I don't understand how they didn't think to let them stay on between runs.The biggest issue is the balance. Classes are not particularly well balanced with each other, and skills within classes have very clear superior choices. There really is no need to have a well rounded group of characters; once you learn the best choices for each class, there is no need to deviate. Additionally, the enemies are just plain unfair at times. Sometimes the enemies will push your character's turn back, allowing other enemies to go before you get a chance to respond. If multiple enemies with this ability target the same character, you get stuck watching your character die without being able to do anything. There is no real way to stop this; it's just sh**ty and not fun. Most of the bosses have a mechanic like this too, where if you do enough damage, they immediately get to skip to their turn, then they can do multiple actions in a row. Having one boss with this would be fine, but every single boss fight having this mechanic sucks.If something between thumbs up and thumbs down existed, that's what I would rate Othercide. I like some parts of the game like the theme and (some of) the combat, but there are too many frustrating/lazy elements for me to fully recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Great: - Puzzly feeling of trying to balance skills and abilities is A+ in my opinion.  - Gives SERIOUS Kingdom Death: Monster vibes (an excellent boardgame about managing a settlement in a horrific hellscape and fighting terrifying monsters/bosses for resources and whatnot.)  - Rivals Divinity Original Sin 2 for turn-based combat; I really am digging the timeline and how I'm able to interact with it. It's taken me a few hours to really get to see things and progress (and thankfully, I still feel like I haven't discovered most yet! Still a bunch to do.) - Soundtrack is S++ (and I personally like the art. One of the biggest draws to this game from other Roguelites.)Good:  - Runs smooth! No hiccups or anything (as of yet, but not looking like I'll encounter any.) - Monsters are spook.Meh:  - The UI could use a little love, it's not always intuitive and I've found myself lost a handful of times... BUT it's not unplayable awful, nowhere close, but when I first started I needed to focus a little more to make sure I knew what I was clicking and where I needed to click.  - I wish there was a little more diversity among the skills. I'm hoping and praying that'll be something that will come in an update or expansion. I do like the customization with augmenting abilities though. _childDocuments_.review: Okey, here we go. Just pros and cons.Pros:- Great artstyle. Cool and simple. Really, it`s just a piece of art. - Nice music on boss fights. Moments when the music changes following the boss stages can touch your very soul.- Cute girls. Maybe too cute for a warriors but great anyway. I`ll be honest, they’re the only reason I made it through this game.- Iniciative based combat mechanics. This "timeline" stuff plays pretty fun.- Pretty hardcore. I don’t remember another game where the price of a mistake was so high.Cons:- Most of gameplay. Someone told the developers "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love rogue-lites" and they made "rogue-lite" mechanics. Yeah. But unfortunately none of them understood what it meant and they did not bother to find out. So gameplay is just a repetitive grind. No randomness at all. Same maps (there are very few of them), same enemies, same enemy placements, same girls, same skills, over and over HUNDRED of times and tens of hours. And then you meet a boss with counter-intuitive mechanics, wiping you out on the second turn and guess what? Yeah, grinding again. And thats not all. The icing on the cake - most of cool skills wasting your HP, but you can`t heal your girls in this game, so you can only afford to use them on bosses. What it means for you? Yeah, grinding via two skills. You can move and you can chop, thats your gameplay here.- Bosses. Maybe I'm too dumb, but I haven't found a tactic for any of the bosses. They have different skills, different stages and... i have no idea how to counter them or play with it. So It`s all about abusing reaction attacks and interruptions no matter wich boss and what it`s going to do. Same tactics for everyone, everytime.- Ambient sounds. I mean these random voiced lines. They are good, they create the atmosphere, but why do they come out SO OFTEN? "Memories hurt... memories hurt.... memories hurt..." - continuous annoying spam dozens of times in a row. I’m sure ì`ll hear them again in my nightmares. Her lips...her legs...her lips...her legs...her lips.... Aaarrggh! Overall: This game is great as a piece of art and mediocre as a game. So if you don`t mind of some tactical grinding enjoying the dark atmosphere and cute warmaidens - this game is just for you. But if you are looking for good rogue-lite.... go look somewhere else.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an masterpiece!Othercide is an turn based game. You command an Army of daughters (1-5 per match) against the forces of darkness. There are 4 classes of daughters. Every few levels they learn an new ability and they also get traits and you can upgrade them with memories which are dropped from enemy monsters.It features an unique artdesign, mostly white/black/red which fits realy well with the setting.This game is like Xcom, set in a creepy "all is lost" world. The game starts of to be very challenging. The chances are high that the first boss will Rip off your Face and you gona post "NERF IT" on the forum, just to realise a few runs later, that the boss is completly harmless if you play it right.The game is crafted in such a way, that the more you play, the stronger you get. If you lose the game, you keep your earned shards which are used to enable different buffs. And these buffs are crazy....like +80% Total Hitpoints for every daugher you have.If you play long enougth, its completly possible to make a new run and one shoot the first boss. Talk about revenge! Because of the buffs, you can also customize your run. Currently im playing a new run with lvl 1 daughters, with no ressurects allowed, but they all get +50% exp (buff) to level up realy fast and have lots of hp + damage (again buffs).This leads to a classic "Xcom" like gameplay. Another example: i could start a new run, ressurect my strongest daugther and try to finish the wohle game with her alone.There are two things which make the game go from "Its ok" to "HOLY MOTHER OF HELL!"1. Is the Soundtrack. its creepy, haunting, with an apocalyptic feel.2. The boss fights. Seriously, i played LOTS of games but these bosses.....bloody hell, i want to meet the guy who designed them. Overall i rate it 8/10 because it can get a bit repetive, cos there are no random generated maps and only a few maps per "Era".

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful crafted game, weird and atmospheric, makes one think and feel, very few games out there that do that. That said, game is somewhat short and the ending lacks closure, hints to a part 2 or dlc. Overall this game you should get . ( better with a discount ). However, word to the wise, you will cry for your daughters. On the gameplay side, imho this game cant be compared to xcom or wasteland 3, because of the hiting chance. While the enemy can and will dodge your atk sometimes its no big deal, as most basic atks are 3 in 1 ( soulslinger ), and each char has a generous ap pool wich can be further enlarged with traits. I recommend for the end game team 2 soulslingers, 1 blademaster, 1scythebearer. For the last boss just add another soulslinger. There are other viable builds but i found this one to be the most forgiving in terms of mistakes. Prolly a pro gamer ( wich im not ) will finish the game in less than 30 hours. In my opinion worth the money aslong as you pay max 20 euros. There is also some replay value here, as you cant complete all missions in one given chapter, not even with 2 viable teams, wich anyway you cant build sooner than closer to the end of the game. Anyway thats my 2 cents, cheers, may your favourite daughters survive, and if not, ressurect them :)

_childDocuments_.review: Two months after original review:The developers have released one major update since launch alongside several hotfixes designed to address bugs. The Dream update included a new difficulty setting as well as some more traits that can be obtained by your characters. Some skills and traits have been re-balanced. For the time being, I would consider this to be final state of the game.The game itself has excellent art and story direction. I think the atmosphere, music, and art style are all excellent additions to the game. Some of the voice acting is out of place (especially end-of-game buddy voice overs), some of the lines trigger much too often, but I can honestly say that I'm impressed with how much effort they went through to get the music and art for this kind of story.Gameplay-wise, there is potential that the game ultimately falls short of delivering. The developers tried to balance the game around losing and seem to have looked at producing a rogue-like experience where your characters can gather different traits each playthrough (most like Darkest Dungeon). Characters can choose different skills as they level up. There are game-altering options that you can purchase upon losing / starting a new playthrough that change how the game plays. Unfortunately, that's where it stops. The skills are mostly one-sided or redundant for most of the characters. The playthrough modifiers mostly just make the game universally easier - instead of changing how the game plays, it's just a difficulty slider that increases your characters' health, increases damage to enemies, increases experience gain, or skips chapters. With how the game is balanced, you go from playing a game where any damage is lethal, to one where characters can just walk through enemies. Instead of offering new ways to succeed at the game, it just lets you play dumber. There's not much fun in replaying this.While unintended, the game still has a number of unacceptable bugs for a $35 game. Especially as an iron mode game, where the game constantly saves automatically, save data loss of corruption is unacceptable. This is still a frequent phenomenon according to the discord channel, that plagues players and wipes hours of play (from a game that is already designed to make you restart). Beyond that - the save state compromises, in that quitting to menu in the middle of a map will reset the entire map. This is very easily abused, but even if you have no intent of abusing this design decision, if the game crashes (which is not uncommon) then you will reset any decisions you may have made on the level. Melee range enemies can occasionally hit you from across the map. The recent update added a new bug where damage calculations are universally higher than actual damage output. With that said, I would not recommend purchase at full price. I would be happy playing this as an indie developer game with all its bugs and design flaws for $15-20, but at $35 the expectations for a fully fleshed out game are higher. Original review:Othercide is an extraordinarily atmospheric game with excellent writing, design, and soundtracks. The first few hours in the game were excellent. Having said that, I cannot recommend it to anyone else, . There are substantial game-breaking performance issues with the game. I'm using an Intel i7 laptop with a GTX1080Ti eGPU. It can run XCOM2, Fallout 4, modded Skyrim, Sekiro, etc. at over 40 fps. When Othercide runs, it runs at a stable 60fps at maximum resolution and settings - but periodically the game freezes (about once every 45 minutes). Sometimes the game will chug through like nothing happens, other times it hard freezes the computer - not CTD, no task manager interrupt. Worse, on two occasions it has corrupted saves with >15 hours of play. I've played with the settings to try and mitigate this, but it seems that I've only been able to lower the frequency of these crashes - low shadows, VSync off, no AA.Besides the game-breaking crashes, Othercide has a surprising amount of polish in some areas, and lack thereof in others. The soundtrack, atmosphere, codex, and lore are rich and entirely different from the waifu simulator some have jokingly called it. The noire, pseudo-Eldritch story is excellent. The entire game revolve around sacrifice and loss. The game is balanced around defeat. However combat UI, enemy behavior, and boss battles are all bugged: enemy delayed actions don't properly display if the enemy has changed position; some AoE delayed attacks don't display correctly regardless; killing an enemy next to another blows their model out of wack; starting turn doesn't allow actions if your character has negative initiative; one boss's cutscene can bug out and soft-lock the game... these are only some of the ones I've experienced. Ultimately this turns a difficult but rewarding combat system into what feels like an unfair slog of repetition, especially when the game freezes.I'm putting the game on the shelf for a month or two in hopes that the developers will address these bugs. It has a lot of promise, but I would advise waiting some time for the game to develop.

_childDocuments_.review: Othercide is a  fun tactics game that has a lot of strategic depth that will keep you coming back. The closest comparisons I could make would be the X-Com series (but you actually can hit your targets), Turn based combat games like Divinity (with less RPG elements), and toss a bit of spice from something like Amnesia for the astheticThe lore and worldbuilding is captivating and fits well with the minimalist color pallet. If youre a fan of grim, emotional settings you will enjoy this. The visual clarity is on point and there's rarely ever trouble understanding what you're looking at. The boss fights are where this game shines. Difficult encounters that really require you to think carefully before acting. I've wiped a few times against the first three. It has a few problems- Repeating voicelines, sometimes overlaping voicelines (especially at the end of missions)- Occasional bugs in combat including: Permanently getting stuck (must alt F4), Monsters gaining infinite range or otherwise breaking the rules, cutscenes breaking and not completing (must alt f4)- Lack of information in the UI (getting better as of the last update, but still has a ways to go. I would like to be able to see what memories my daughters have equipped mid mission for example) These problems have not been bad enough to stop me in my first 20 hours of this game. Any of the situations that require you to close the game don't lose you too much progress (you return to the start of the mission you were on) All in all, very happy with my purchase. Would highly recommend to anyone who is a fan of difficult strategy games.

I would describe the combat as being similar to that of Child of Light, with a heavy emphasis on the ability of a player to control and plan around the 'turn timeline.' I found it very satisfying to do this, especially during certain boss fights. One thing I will say is that the stages between boss fights can get repetitive. Though the player can choose to take on relatively fewer of these missions (synapses) if desired, they're encouraged to complete as many as possible to grind for XP, vitae, and shards. This was fine by me, because I really liked combat and enjoyed maxing out all my daughters, but it's something to consider before buying if you don't feel the same. P.S. Ending boss very hard for me at first, get everybody near its spawn as the nucleus is about to hatch, put "menacing stance" on a blademaster or two before whaling damage from every other character. _childDocuments_.review: Othercide is a beautiful looking turn-based RPG games with heavy rougelite elements. Every move will definitely decide how each mission will goFor a sale's price it's definitely worth it. If you are a turn-based  BDSM gamer who loves punishment and pushing your thinking brain to the test - then buy this game ASAP.Humanity is on the brink and it is up to an army of sisters bound together to rid the world of demons and monsters; you have three classes: Melee, range, and tank; these classes work together in synergy; use combos all the damn time, do not be afraid to take risks, but also know your limit. This game has heavy x-com vibes as well....With that said there are a few key issues that you must be aware of: 1) The difficulty on "Original" and "Dream" are VASTLY two different mindsets; Nightmare difficulty will push even the veteran turn-base gamers to their limit, as the game will throw everything at you. Dream mode however is essentially a walk in the park; basically a traditional turn-based RPG game; i recommend playing it on Dream mode to better understand the game first before playing it on original2) Group size missions must be definitive and not just "Okay, one mission is 3, and another 4" because, yes while it may be a game design choice or cheese; on original mode the game is extremely hard and will insist that you clear the 7 days before the boss attacks. And guess what? If you die, then the current run will end -- yeah no. 3) During combat there is no instant click. So like for example there are "overwatch" type abilities that will watch for enemy patterns - here's the thing though, You have to CONSTANTLY click on the soulslinger; it's not just a one click type of deal which is an odd design choiceAudio & visually it's a breathtaking game, and I recommend the soundtrack.As I mentioned, it's a sale game; however, if you really want more Turn-based games in your library at this current moment then this is a full buy right now.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, the grim dark aesthetic is amazing, concept is original and the gameplay is generally sound.Easy mode can be challenging but I enjoyed my experience in Original more, while it might sound masochistic xd.I felt that every time I lost, afterwards I found that organising the Daughters and understanding enemy types became far easier.Heres pros and cons.Pros:Story! I love the lore in this game, the abhorrent enemies, the sick and twisted bosses and gradually uncovering the truth of the past. The game also feels original, which is a breath of fresh air in this age of sterile media.CombatFast and brutal, for both enemies and Daughters.AestheticFlawless, there is nothing in this area in my opinion that needs to be changed.ConsStory... I know its in my pros, but I found some aspects hard to understand, especially the Memories. Also I'm still confused as to what the Chosen One truly means, what the Suffering is and what Others are. Combatyes its also in my pros xd, but I ve found it can be frustrating for no reason. For example, on many occasions, ive had plague butchers and plague guard strike Daughters from across the map, which I assume is a bug. In addition, Infected spawn and immediately shoot a daughter, which due to the fact they can do it across the map, frustrates me. However, I think the worst experience Ive had are the Painslingers, simply because of Corrupted Haste. It wouldnt be a problem if they only used it once, but when there are a pair of them, they use it on each other and have 4 turns before you get to a Daughter's. Unless you re capable of killing one as soon as they spawn (Which can be difficult considering they have 3000+ health), it can completely overrun the mission.In addition, actions that can counter interruptions would be great for both enemies and Daughters, as I feel that any action or ability in a strategy game needs a counter to feel immersive.DaughtersI think this has been repeated a lot in the reviews, but more customisation would be nice. Memories are one thing, but I do get attached to the Daughters ive had for several Recollections. Moreover, Shieldbearers don't work in Nightmare, at least they feel like the worst class. This is due to several reasons, one they can't aggro enemies, they can t generate armour without using hp, they do less damage than every other class (Yes even Soulslinger because they get Shadow Round.) which wouldnt be a problem if they could soak up damage like an actual tank. The biggest problem is healing, they need a way to regain health during missions, perhaps as an attack so you couldnt do it every turn. Having a big hp pool is useless if you cant use it. More classes would also be amazing, I'd love to have one with an axe or maybe a musket to have another ranged class.RepetitionI have autism, which results in me finding games like Warframe and FF14 enjoyable to play, even after hundreds of hours of gameplay. I would say for Othercide though, having more items to collect would be a boon.Voicelines.After hearing 'Give life to our Daughters' and 'A clean cut.' a million times, some more voice lines would be great, and help with the repetition.ConclusionI love this game and I am intent on buying any content that comes out for it. Despite some problems here and there, I find myself enjoying Othercide immensely. I am looking forward to it's future.

_childDocuments_.review: A tedious, unfair game built on infuriating mechanics, making it a repetitive mess.Visually the game seems pleasing, but after a while the monochromatic with red accents seems overdone.The soundtrack is great for an indie game, the voice acting as well at times, underwhelming other times.The story is skippable as it adds nothing to the game.The UI isn't very helpful:-There isn't any indication on how long an effect lasts; i have been rooted seemingly infinitely with 3 characters while the "maggot" that cast root, was long time dead already, creating a slow wipe for my team.This cast was from across the battlefield, leaving no way to defend myself.-skill explanations of enemies seem lacking clear information.-Stats aren't clear during battle, enemies have 150 block for example, i have 300 damage, i attack, 0 damage every time.. how does the calculation actually work?-The same goes for dodge: scavenger has 15% dodge, i do a total of 15 attacks, 3 hit, he dodges everything else.-buffs aren't very clear which are active and what the effects are.-The enemy stat screen overlaps part of the battlefield making you pan to select the target. Add to this that after an action the camera pans back so if you want to attack a second time, you have to pan again, quite annoying.The mechanics are somewhat unique, yet make the game overly grindy in an absolutely tedious manner:-"daughters" get attacked, don't ever heal automatically and the only way to heal them is to sacrifice higher or equal level units. Start grinding to possibly heal decent units.-add to this that any decent "combo-worthy skill" what the game tries to promote costs actual health percentage, makes this mechanic insufferable.-once skills are set, they are permanent. Want to replace skill on a decent unit? wipe it, start a new grind.The game feels unfair, especially during rescue missions, mostly at chapter 4 and up.-infinite spawns that trigger when reaching a point are acceptable, except when adding trashy enemies with OP mechanics like "maggot" with its root ability, making you rush towards it, creating 10 to 15 spawns at once, basically wiping your team, since it's impossible to survive this, not by fighting or by rushing to the exit.Hunt and ritual are acceptable missions, but survival depends on rng where and what spawns, including the exit.Boss fight entirely depend on cheesing by abusing certain game mechanics and feel like chores.They also have several Ridiculously OP moves that once performed wipe in 1 to 2 turns.Now the wipes wouldn't be necessarily bad if the resurrect mechanic was good.When getting wiped during a boss, the game resets, all your daughters die, your set memories are all wiped.This way you barely will know what u did wrong, being it a wrong skill on a unit, having to regrind a unit to hope that next time she will be what you need for the fight or being it a wrong set of units. I didn't even finish the game, i just quit during recollection 3, chapter 5.I didn't even lose the last battle i played, i haven't tried the 5th boss which was reachable for me at this time, but i just had enough of the bland, monotonous, frustrating  grindfest that is the core of this game.After chapter 3 you've experienced all there's to experience, only a grindy, tedious gameplay loop remains.The looks, the sound at first pleasing, exciting became what i eventually hated about this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying I'm not a fan of the rogue genre... I don't like the idea of putting in the work for a game that's just going to inevitably rob me of my efforts. Othercide does not do that at all.Othercide is a nightmarish fantasy, roguelite, and mysterious tactical RPG with a lot of subtle RNG seeding well worth the work put in, once you grasp all of the mechanics. Even when assigned 1 of only 3 roles each character can play as, it takes a while to master, but once you do you can craft yourself quite the team and since each class has to choose an exclusive skill every few levels, one will feel different than another of the same class. This game starts out feeling like an uphill battle grinding just to stay alive with minor rewards but along the way you increase your shard max and your next few playthroughs feel less like a survival suicide roguelite and more like tailor-suited tactical RPG with a team you've grown attached to and won't let you down. Keep in mind as difficult as it was that I never lost, so it is far from impossible to beat, and my second playthrough feels exciting. I voluntarily (you can at any time you choose) ended my first playthrough and start a new one over with my hand-selected hard-earned permanent bonuses. The story is somewhat shallow, with each battle lacking substance as far as that is concerned. As with your roster of Daughters, however, the story fleshes out bit by bit and becomes a mystery to unravel and, so far for me, is rewarding. The progression has a depth to it that makes up for the lack of story interaction. The game is worth the buy, especially on sale (got it half off!), but it leaves you craving more... and not in a bad way. To me Othercide has the best aspects of Darkest Dungeon and XCOM 2 combined. I loved both of those games for different reasons but was also disappointed in them. This does not contain the same disappointments. Hopefully there will be a sequel with more depth, but the bleak (satisfyingly so) atmosphere, akin to Darkest Dungeon, of the game is always nice to hop back into and will keep me coming back for a while. It's a unique experience everyone should try out.

_childDocuments_.review: Did they send me daughtersWhen I askedFor sons?They did! And these daughters totally rule! Othercide is a tough as nails tactics-game that immediately jumps at you with its distinct visual presentation. The main hook of the game is your squad of Daughters, heroes and warriors who will battle the demons for and with you. They come in various classes which fulfill your standard rock-paper-scissors role but with an interesting spin to it. At certain levels you will choose between two abilities, although I must say that one choice seemed superior more often than not.During battle the order of actions is determined by a clever mechanism of initiative. Each daughter has action points and using half of them means she can act again in a certain amount of time. Using all the action points means you can move further or attack more often but comes at the heavy price of your next turn taking twice as long to come around and so the game has you planning those crucial turns and weighing the decision of having one Daughter stranded after going on a rampage. Even moreso because later enemies will not take as long until their next turn!Should your Daughters take damage in battle, you will find yourself faced with Othercide's next defining trait: Its healing system. When playing on Nightmare difficulty, which is the standard difficulty, your daughters do not automatically heal after combat but only if you sacrifice, yes kill, a Daughter of equal or higher level. A part of her stays with her comrade in the form of a permanent buff, but the game will still force some heavy decisions upon you this way. You can resurrect some of your team, but only at the price of rare tokens, so that decision becomes equally tough!SIDENOTE: The game offers a second mode in which each Daughter heals 50% of her health after each overworld turn and since each Daughter can only go on one mission per such turn, most of them will usually be at full health. I imagine the game would be no less punishing inside the missions but I played it using the standard mode. Just an fyi.The bosses in the game provide interesting combat puzzles although the community has come up with some ways to absolutely bully them. I would still recommend going in blind on your first try and failing miserably! It's a learning experience!Should you fail a boss mission or if you choose to do so between missions, you end your run and bank the metaprogression currency of shards, which are used to activate buffing trophies, Remembrances. These will give you all sorts of benefits from your Daughters having more health or starting at a higher level to outright skipping one or more of the game's five stages. While some of the Remembrances felt very strong, none of them seem mandatory to beat the game, so the game does not feel grindy in that way.All in all I would highly recommend Othercide for any fan of tactics games. It's a real nailbiter at times but feels highly rewarding when you bring a boss down. And while the story seems a bit cryptic and to be happening on a meta or possibly psyche level, it provides an engaging backdrop which gives your Daughters their reason to fight.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played only a few Xcom-like games, and this has so far been one of my favorites. The enemy variety switches things up with each new era you progress through, and you can easily get attached to certain daughters and there's thankfully a way to always bring her back if an untimely death comes her way. I've yet to get to the end game, but so far I haven't felt the need to grind. Many powerful and permanent bonuses can be unlocked to make new resets much easier. However, I've noticed that if you are an above average player, you can easily unlock nearly all the important upgrades after only 2 or so resets. Once you've done that, the only thing left to do is to try and get as many traits as possible onto every daughter. And if you end up not being good at the game, that is when the grinding will likely finally show its face.The class variety is sadly low though, and many skills just aren't as good as others. You may find yourself making tons of the same daughter rather than unique ones.There have been a few bugs however. Tooltips and the codex don't always line up. Some enemy logs say they do X, but in reality they do Y. Sometimes the movement phase of characters can be visually buggy, requiring you to swap between all their actions until it correctly shows where you can actually travel. Red danger zones on the ground seem to stick around for longer than they should, which can get confusing when an entire area is nothing but red and you're unsure of what's actually safe.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the first things this game does is admit that this game is flawed. The game genuinely says be prepared to lose your favorite characters because they will die to B.S. They're right.The game is hilariously unfair, even with the easier difficulty mode. Get used to your girls dying in just two hits because every single enemy is overpowered. You'll have 700 HP at the start of the game with one girl for example and a hit from an enemy is 350 hp. How is that good game design? Why do you want our characters that you want us to build up and keep die so ridiculously quickly? Horrible game design. The BIGGEST PROBLEM with this game is it's AP system. You are only allowed to use FIFTY of your one hundred AP points. If you use more than fifty you are PUNISHED. THAT IS SO INCREDIBLY STUPID AND A TERRIBLE GAME MECHANIC. Moving takes so much AP so moving to an enemy usually uses your first 50 and then you're screwed if you use anymore because if you go above 50, the game punishes you by pretty much forcing your character to wait double the amount of turns before you can do anything again. On top of that attacks cost 25+ AP so combat is a terrible chore that isn't fun. Does this even sound like good game design? No, it doesn't. It is flawed and horrible and yet they decided to keep this garbage in the game.Game also allows enemies to pretty much outnumber you every mission but you're only allowed to bring up to 3 girls, sometimes 4. This is the worst, especially during rescue missions when the enemy amount is doubled. No, that's not fair. Stop restricting us with poor game mechanics and decisions and let us have fun. _childDocuments_.review: 10/29/23 I beat the game. It as like a wave crashing against a wall. I finally eroded it. It was just a combination of things... but just... did it. It was hard and took time. I had to abuse the crap out of boosters as much as possible. Interrupting Shot. Saving Grace. Dance of Binding. The last boss was difficult. Truly, you just have to make sure to get its HP down so hard that it can't use it's HP expending stuff. It will use them, but like you , you can't use an HP expending skill once your HP drops to a certain point. Same with bosses and monsters. :) It is not for everyone, sure, but like people who want to kill Ruby Weapon in FF7, or fight Omega weapon in Ultamecia's castle in FF8, you know you can, and it is  hard, but it is HARD. Definitely felt the pain getting to beat this boss. The reward for getting lv 15 daughters is beating the game. I think it should have been earlier so that you can prepare for the boss fight. :/ That way you can change out skills on a new daughter and try it out instead of having to grind them out for that last skill, level, up, etc. We need mod support. We need more maps. We need more enemy variation. We need new skills. We need a longer story. We need an Othercide 2. I like this game. I appreciate this game. I'm not saying I don't like this game because of my recommendation.For me, it is a 7/10[] Music        The music sets a great tone and I do like how "hopeless" you feel at times in the fight due to the soundtrack.[] Art Direction        The black/white/red all over makes some things pop out. The death animations and zoom in flanked kills are really cool.[] Graphics        The game looks nice and I have no issues, at all, with how this game looks. [] Steam Deck Compatibility        I played it on steamdeck and it works just fine.[] Stable Frame Rate       Stable, no issues. Well made.[] Sound Design       Shots and skills have a good sound to them. Gives you a good thump for every gunslinger shoot. They don't hold peashooters[] Overall feel and aesthetic       I like when games take risks on how they present the game and , since it is a personal thing, the game delivers for me. Some people like shiny rtx. Some people like anime goth girls and nekos. I will eventually get through the game completely and do all the things, get all the memories, etc, but it will be painstaking. I played and beat Doom Eternal on Nightmare on Run 1 and Resident Evil 8 on Village of Shadows. I like the hard difficulty, because, yes. I'm that kind of person. This game gives me that feel and I like it. It punishes me for being greedy and underestimating my enemies. _______________________________________________________________________Where this game may be the deal breaker for other people, but not for me.[] Storytelling is alright, but sometimes the in-battle dialogue can be very repetitious. The cutscenes are cool. The rouge-like gameplay does not help with repetitions, but there are "speed up actions" settings in the menu.[] The difficulty settings are simply just allowing healing between missions. Otherwise, you sacrifice a daughter to heal another. Sacrificing is a mechanic that brings other enemies upon you for your decision. I don't mind the mechanic and it is part of the general gameplay direction of the game. It adds to the grindy-like gameplay. For someone who has a hard time with failing, being constantly punished, and feeling like they aren't making any traction in the game, this would be the kick in the pants.[] Mod support isn't available, which would be amazing in a game like this, extending the game's life by allowing more units, more varied maps, and battle conditions. While the devs said something that they didn't forget on the forums, we've yet to see anything come to fruition. The amount of content for other games on Steam Workshop or Nexus Mods really allow games to flourish, not because the devs are shortsighted, but because they provide a platform for creativity to emerge and a community to build exponentially.[] Grandia and other games have the time bar at the bottom. Delaying moves and delayed actions are not new to the gaming scene. Many people have expressed, and I have experienced, the obscene amount of enemy attacks in maps later on, citing the final boss to have that issue. Before Boss 4, I experienced multiple combat situations where I have 4 daughters and am thrust into a battle where 8 combatants have 2-3 moves each, sometimes halfway killing my team before we have a chance to act. While players may have a hangup, this is where skills like interrupting shot (interrupt enemy attacks), saving grace (Swap places with an ally and retaliate the incoming attack), and stance skills (enemies finishing movement in melee range are struck). This consumes 5-10% HP (which is the a severe cost at times, gameplay wise). With multiple enemies spawning in, the timeline for turns can be heavily saturated. It seems ridiculous at times. Functionally, yes you can counter the enemy, but sometimes, it is just annoying. [] The maps are limited, the "Days" are your timer before the bosses, and you get a mechanic to skip them. What can be annoying is that you are gated each day within the "Era". With skipping mechanics, you just have to grind out earlier missions with a B team, revive your A team with revive tokens, level up/attach skills to the A team, complete rescue for revive tokens for your A team, and send the A team to kill the boss. You just end up Sacrificing B team members with good bonuses to the A team to make sure they're buffer. You feel like you're getting incremental progress and while that's part of the Rogue-like , it feels really slow. A new player will simply just not beat the game in one fell swoop on Standard Difficulty. It is designed to force you to engage with the mechanic. Example: Dark Souls Players (fine with taking the punishment and death isn't permanent) v. Not Dark Souls Players (very much does not like to lose and takes a failure more personally as an attack on their skill level, rather than hapchance). [] The gameplay loop has some "physical obstacles" that do provide some tactics, but not to the degree of XCOM, including destructible cover, defense bonuses and just serves as a line of sight from ranged enemies buffer. Some enemies have a 'charged shot' ability that can be broken if line of sight is gone. I would have liked the first half of the game to have more dynamic stages.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this strongly enough. It has some flaws, but it's an unforgettable experience. I didn't pick it up until it was on sale, but having played it, it is absolutely worth buying at full price.As a tactical RPG roguelite, you're going to find yourself in very similar encounters every run, but the game punishes you harshly if you don't get everything *perfect* considering how hard it is to heal or revive so the level of challenge keeps it interesting. The atmosphere is wonderful and the black/white/red art style suits it perfectly, complemented by an amazing sound track. Your Daughters don't have any voiced lines, but they gain traits under certain conditions (and possibly with certain probabilities attached?) which can make you pretty attached to the ones that you keep using. Between that and Mother's lines praising them, you get truly attached to your girls... and the healing mechanic means you eventually have to either sacrifice them or let them die. I don't think I've ever apologized to a video game character before, but I felt so awful each time I had to do it.My only complaint is that it felt a little too easy on Nightmare difficulty, especially the boss fights; I was able to finish it on my 4th run, clearing both the fourth and fifth bosses on my first try, with my blademaster able to skip entire phases and she also made it to the final boss completely unhurt. Looking at community posts, it does seem I had an easier time than most, however.It didn't quite scratch my itch for the truly punishing game I was expecting, but it was still a wonderful experience overall.

Both sides get a fair dodge chance that can be built up, you dont feel like that 99% hit chance youre told about is actually a 50% hit chance.The AP system, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ yes. The combos you can create are amazing, no more of the usual: move up, shoot and enter quick shot mode. Or move up, miss shot and stand there like a idiot that will now die next turn. You can get so creative, do you keep 50+ AP so that your characters turn occurs sooner at the cost of you maybe doing less for this turn. Or maybe you move up next to an enemy, shoot the ground whilst flying to a square 6 tiles away to then shoot once more, now with no AP you use 5% of you HP to enter a vanguard mode allowing you to interrupt the enemies next turn if he tries to attack an ally. HONESTLY, WTF IS THIS BADASSERY I NEED MORE OF IT IN MY LIFE. The way you have to throw away this idea of getting attached to a character is amazing too. No more grinding your favourites to the top, some have to be sacraficed to keep others alive, whether in battle or after to heal another character. Eventually some become too high level that it gets too hard to keep them at full HP as you have to grind another to the same level in order to do the healing. So you sometimes have to sacrafice the higher leveled character to help heal the lower leveled but easier to keep full HP characters.The art style and soundtrack are just perfect. Already praised to death in the reviews thus far so I shall leave it at this, i never buy soundtracks or art books anymore...but this one has made me break that long streak ;) Really would love it if the main menu theme was in the battles too but hey it means it feels even more enjoyable booting the game up and seeing/hearing that menu screen.Only cons I can think of is that the UI and button presses can be buggy, sometimes dont work and will need you to back out and try again. Thats literally it, just a minor pain that doesnt change the experience whatsoever.9.8/10please add that main music theme even if its for a DLC boss or whatever, JUST GIVE ME IT!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is such an underrated gem, it's a shame it's not more well known. Overall, I've really been enjoying this game and would recommend it to people who love punishing turn based strategy. However, it's not without its flaws that will put some people off, but I think the core game is fresh and unique and well worth a go. I'd love to see a sequel at some stage.PROS:* There is such a dark but engaging atmosphere to this game. Your decisions, losses, and sacrifices all feel very gritty.* The permadeath of units adds so much tension to the game, leading to some tough decisions as you progress. As a huge XCOM fan, I love this.* There are some great moments of unit synergy once you understand how they work and can be exploited. It's a great feeling when it all comes together.* The initiative timeline is a cool and unique mechanic, and the initiative boosts + delays give some good strategic options.* The art direction is amazing and really accentuates the theme of this game.* The soundtrack is amazing, particularly for the bosses.* The game is brutally difficult and you certainly feel the costs of your mistakes.* The voice acting is fantastic - although the lines do get repeated quite a lot.* The different kinds of missions, while limited, are interesting and diverse enough.* The animations are fluid and the short cutscenes for some abilities and for some killing blows look great.NEUTRAL:* Sacrificing your units to heal and upgrade others is a great concept. However, I think it is underutilised and the requirement of sacrificing a unit of greater or equal level largely makes it an unviable strategy as you progress.* It seems some abilities look good on paper, but are far less useful than their alternatives in game, so they seem like traps to new players. I find myself selecting mostly the same abilities across all units because they are objectively better than the alternatives.* There are only a limited number of maps, so you will see the same ones fairly often. I think they could have padded this out a bit better with varying the starting locations, enemy configurations, randomly distributing the obstacles, etc.* I think the rougelite mechanic is a little bit lacking, and it seems to be used more for saving overall progress rather than unlocking new and exciting things.CONS:* Boss fights can be incredibly unfair and almost impossible to predict or even plan for. If you don't know in advance what you're fighting against and you bring the wrong team comp, the fight is almost unwinnable.* Normal enemies spawning near your units is such a pain point. The melee units are largely predictable, but the ranged units can just spawn and immediately shoot your units and you have no real way to mitigate this.* Some normal enemies are horrible to fight against. They have their turns too often, do too much on their turn, and there's no real way to counter them.* There are some major things lacking in the UI that really  should be there. Particularly around what traits and memories your units have - it makes it difficult to build your team comp and utilise them in battle if you don't know what your units do.OTHER:* I'd love to see more classes, more useful abilities, and a greater diversity of missions. Essentially, just more content.* I'd like to see a better way to manage your units turns, particularly when they are all in a row. You're at the mercy of the imitative bar and often you want other units going before others to properly utilise some skills and setup combos. Perhaps a simple delay initiative ability would be useful.

_childDocuments_.review: This game should be called "Othercide : Guess what the enemy will do" The AI is so inconsistent, yet you have skills that rely on them doing an action.  For example: There are two enemies within range of two of your daughters, instead of attacking them they just move past and try to reach your third Daughter.  You move that daughter away, they switch to the other team members, but by then you used your AP and didn't want to waste another 10% or 5% of your HP for a "reactionary" skill. This gets even more frustrating during boss fights. Otherwise, the mechanics are pretty solid, the customization of characters' skill as well as the added "memories" are well thought-out,  the roguelite portion of the game is really cool, saving HP and planning ahead is a great concept, except the inconsistency of enemies make it more of a chore than of strategy. Overall I wouldn't recommend this game as there are better turn-based strategy games out there deserving of your time and money. 5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a good pace, and once you understand the controls, is easy to play. I use a remote, which has been a lifesaver! You know, minus the perpetual dying. But as the game tells you right from the start, it is designed knowing full well that you will die a LOT, as that is the only way to make progress. They have two different modes--Nightmare and Dream. Nightmare mode is the original gameplay, where once you lose your warriors, they are toast! You can, however, bring them back with resurrection tokens. You do't get many of these, so good luck with that! The other mode allows them to heal while resting, and they get back 50% of their total power when they do. Playing Dream mode is still murderously difficult, but you can get things done more easily, and level up your fighters quite a bit more before you willingly sacrifice them to start all the way from the beginning. But no worries! That sacrifice means the world, and you can start to get your favorites back as you begin again. All in all, this game is amazingly fun, and comfortably hard!

_childDocuments_.review: Storytelling in Othercide is akin to a cross between Transistor and Dark Souls, minus Transistor's occasionally pleasant monologue spoken to Red. Effectively, almost all of the "plot"/character content is conveyed via journal entries, so figuring anything out will be like reading the Final Fantasy XIII journal entries to get more information. If that appeals to you, then great, but if you prefer actual storytelling, show-don't-tell moments in fiction, etc., then Othercide will devolve into just a case of gameplay and visual aesthetic.Gameplay-wise, the game felt very grindy during my time with it. You have kill quotas and certain tasks to complete to unlock bonuses you can equip to give yourself better chances of surviving future runs. I can only imagine the most turn-based strategy fans enjoying this game, which is why it surprises me to see that so many people recommend the game. Then again, I can't "blame" them for doing so since we aren't given a "score" system to rate the game with individually. You either recommend it, or you don't...either a 0% or 100%, which is disappointing. I will say, however, that while more than 80% of players recommend this game on Steam...only 6.4% of the game's players have completed it based on the global achievements list you can check on Steam. They might like the game, but they aren't interested enough to finish it after it's been out over a year and a half (or it's too difficult for them; either/or).I just couldn't get into this game as you go into a map, kill everything and leave, or reach an extraction zone, then move on to a boss, while spending time at a menu in between each map. The maps are dreary and uninteresting. While Sin City looked all the cooler in black and white, the lack of color in Othercide's locations is to their detriment. It makes the bland maps even more bland and unappealing. I couldn't get into X-COM, but at least I thought the maps looked nice and had a little memorable variety to them. The entire time I was playing Othercide, I wanted to stop playing. I could have (and have on some games) stopped playing after half an hour and written enough of the issues I have with the game, but I pressed on to give it a chance, and it doesn't have a single thing I enjoyed.Well, that's not true. There is ONE thing I enjoy: the title screen music. Do a search online for the Othercide title screen music and enjoy. That song is awesome, the visuals on the title screen accompanying it are great as well, and really liked everything about that title screen. beyond that, though...it was a complete wash for me. Avoid this game unless you basically like every game, or you can't get enough of turn-based strategy games.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, I really had fun with Othercide, but at the same time the game did leave me frustrated & burnt out quite often. Towards the end, I dreaded opening up the game and powered through only to finish it.Othercide is a pretty good game, especially towards the middle. The art style is captivating, and conveys this bleak, hopeless tone perfectly. The story, and the world in general is unique, interesting, albeit a bit fragmented since you start to decipher things only towards the end with codex entries. That can be a positive for some too though, as it really feeds this mystery as to what the hell happened. The combat is generally engaging, with an intricate initiative system & abilities revolving around said system. Also, since you cannot heal your units without sacrificng other units throughout the run, the combat really encourages planning ahead. The game makes information about all the enemy moves and AI available to you, so you are encouraged to try to do perfect combat encounters.This is all great at the beginning, but does get tiresome over time since the unit variety is not very high especially at the start, and each run has you juggling 3 classes with a limited number of abilities. The more interesting abilities and  unlocks towards the middle-end of the game, which makes the grind more and more frustrating before you unlock mid to late game abilities. And ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ does this game require grind. New enemies DO unlock, and the game does get more difficult, but to get there you have to repeat the same maps over and over. Not to say that it was boring; most of the time the game was very satisfying since it felt like trying to solve a puzzle to win an encounter without getting hit. They just overstayed their welcome at times, especially when you started to see essentially the same encounter multiple times.So yeah, the game encourages perfection. However, the UI/UX to try to predict what will happen is pretty bad, both design wise and bug-wise. Sometimes indicators just get left on the screen, cluttering the map especially with large AoE attacks. Reading the enemy abilities themselves can also be frustrating at times, requiring multiple clicks and juggling tooltips. MY worst complaint is that the game is quite buggy, especially the bosses.  Another boss for example,  after casting an ability that should make her face a single direction, and then getting hit by an ability to face the direction of the attack, will actually turn towards the attack, but only after the attacker has moved or ended her turn!? These are just some of the examples, and bosses have a much larger chance of bugging out than regular encounters, making the whole thing really frustrating sometimes.Anyways, I did enjoy the game most of the time. The restarting mechanics were interesting, and allowed you to skip the earlier parts of the game as well as get power ups. The sacrifice mechanics, the traits, and late game abilities were all engaging. You really can do some pretty good combos etc. in the game, but not too much until towards the middle-end. In the end, I must say that Othercide is enjoyable only if you are willing to power through some parts and are generally not easily frustrated due to bugs/UX.I just wish it didn't rely so much on pure stat grind. The skill tree is limited and mostly has wrong and right choices. After a while due to low variety you kinda just "figure out" the game and must now keep grinding to get the stats you need. Or you can try out some "cheesy" strats, which was kinda fun for me tbh.
