_childDocuments_.review: A nice turn based game with a good story and an incredible artstyle.Gameplay wise it's a bit like XCOM with Bloodborne aesthetics. Your characters (daughters) are always majorly outnumbered and there is a fairly steep difficulty spike from the enemies at the third chapter but your daughters rapidly become stronger to the point that a single one will be able to clear a whole mission. Each daughter has 50 action points and an extra 50 called "burst" that will let her do more things her turn but delay her next turn significantly so you always need to make a decision whether you will be able to kill all the nearest enemies fast enough. Daughters can't be healed unless another daughter of equal or higher level is sacrificed so it's best to not overlevel any individual one. Enemies come in many varieties and work well off each other, with each prerfering to attack a specific daughter (lowest hp, farther a;ways, certain class etc.). Bosses are well designed, each one demanding a certain strategy to beat. At some point you will come to be unable to proceed as you are and will have to start a new recollection (new game). When starting anew, you can use certain upgrades that you earned from the last walkthrough, like having your daughrers start at higher levels, giving them more health or skipping a whole chapter. It helps but can get tedious for some people.Music is atmospheric and enchances the gothic mood of the game. Special mention goes to the first and fourth boss themese, these are incredible and remind me of Metal Gear Rising's OST, the songs become more intense as the battle goes on.Story is told through memories you unlock as you play and while confusing at first, will become clear later.There are some QOL features that the game still needs, for example the HUD doesn't always factor in all the buffs and debuffs that are active on a daughter and can make some fights have more guesswork unless you keep every single stat and effect in an excel spreadsheet.Overall a good game that I would recommend more for the artstyle and story than the gameplay. While by no means bad, the gameplay might seems tedious for some.
_childDocuments_.name: Othercide

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know... on the one hand I've spent 25 hours on this game ... on the other hand I mainly did it to prove a point: that I could beat it. Did I have fun? At times. Was it frustrating? Also.Othercide is turn based tactical combat game not unlike XCOM, but instead of getting 2 AP to move and attack your units move along a time line alongside the enemy. Actions cost different amounts of AP, so you can either try and finish an enemy off and hope for the best or you can take it slow and hope that that works out. This feature is cause for my first gripe: You cannot see the enemy's AP or what actions cost how many AP. It's guess work or simply trying to remember a lot of different movement patterns.The enemy design is gross and great, movement animations are so so ... however, there are some enemy types that just do not gel with the combat formula imho. One can shoot you across half the map and constantly buffs other enemies to move quicker and thus murder you instantly, the other runs away from you (!) and then roots you to the spot from across the map (literally). That basically means you either have to rush that dude and possibly leave yourself wide open or you might end up in a spot that you can't even kill him, because he also likes to encase himself in a shield that can't really be pierced by 1 or 2 of your units. And the mirror image enemies are also pretty lame, since your whole advantage on the battlefield is your versatility and movement speed, which they just copy ...The maps are boring and very repetitive. You'll soon have seen them all. Enemy placement will be familiar, etc. Bosses are VERY interesting, but also VERY confusing (especially with constant buffs to act sooner than you think) and the music is in my opinion just very moody and great. That being said, some bosses are unnecessarily hard, some are just ridiculously easy. That also depends on your setup.The gameplay "loop" itself is: Fight random enemies to level up your daughters and unlock power-ups and bonuses to use in later runs. Yes, this is a rogue-lite and I think that is a real shame, because to me it makes no damn sense. The only way to heal your daughters in regular mode (they've added an easy mode that should trivialize the whole game) is to sacrifice others of the same or higher level. Any daughter that was killed or sacrificed can also be resurrected, keeping all her traits and her levels as well as skills. This is only possible with resurrection tokens, which you rarely get during gameplay, but you also get one after defeating each of the bosses for future runs. You also get several powerups that give you more health, damage, higher starting levels, etc.After my 3rd run I was basically "set". I had enough resources to unlock everything. And that's where the game falls apart. At its core it's a good game, just not a good rogue-lite. And because it's not a good rogue-lite it turns into a bad game.The 2nd recollection already got boring. You basically start over again and push new units in the beginning, which you have to level up again, but the first zone barely gives you any XP. You could skip it, but you also need the resources to power up your daughters during a run, you want them to get new traits, you need to collect more power-ups, etc., so you run through the same maps over and over again, trying not to take any damage, because taking damage is bad. And when you've finally beaten the final boss, the game let's you start at level 15 with all skills unlocked ... just ... there is no reason to play the game anymore. There is no "new +" or sth like that. Just the same combat loop that you're probably sick of by now.Another thing that makes me scratch my head is the decision to implement % health skills into the game. These skills are almost essential, at least during boss battles, but 5% or 10% of your health is a huge deal during a fight, especially once your units start having 5k to 10k health or more. You start to wonder, why even use the skill? The boss deals less damage than I'd do to myself to interrupt his attacks. So that on the other hand means you could/should respec your daughters to take other, more useful skill, except you can't. You have to raise a new one for that, but that one would actually need the % health skills. I think it's a bit of a mess, especially since the final boss just doesn't really require interrupts that much ... I know my daughters did interrupt him, I just don't even know WHAT they interrupted. Once you get to that boss you will understand its questionable design. That is, should you make it past the first boss, because that one is imho by far the hardest one in the game when you're just starting and your units are barely level 5. The game is snowbally ... at the beginning you feel threatened by everything, later on you oneshot even the strongest enemies and can facetank most hits without immediately dying. You get more AP, more damage, more health, more versatility, but you still have to fight the same old battles. And the story is presented via some weird cutscenes and finding text fragments ... only you don't find them in order, but randomly. Why should I care about a story that is not coherent while I play it?I'd give it a 6/10. If it weren't a rogue-lite, but closer to XCOM's progression system (following a story, but with random missions to level up and get resources basically) then I think it would be more interesting. This way I feel that 75% of the time I've spent on it was kinda wasted.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun playing Othercide. It's one of the few strategy games that actually lets you strategize. The battles were always fun and satisfying to win. The art style and atmosphere is beautiful and the music had me headbanging. There are, however, a few problems with this game that hold it back from being really good. Most of these problems are completely solvable with an update tot he game.My biggest problem with the game was the descriptions of the abilities. The writing was not nearly specific enough. I found myself constantly questioning what abilities did. For example, one of the bosses has the ability to interrupt either a melee or ranged attack and deal damage back to the player. The definition of "melee" and "ranged" was very vague, which lead me to use attacks that I thought were safe, but actually weren't, and not use attacks that I thought would get interrupted, but were actually fine to use.There is a card game called Dominion. My recommendation to the developers would be to play Dominion and draw inspiration from that game on how to describe abilities. I think that would help a lot.I really enjoyed the story. As someone who has been through a lot in life, it really hit home for me. I do agree with some of these reviews that say the story was vague and hard to follow, but despite that issue, I understood it well enough to appreciate it. The themes of suffering and darkness were well depicted. I love how those themes were integrated into the gameplay. A lot of games have a disconnect between the story and the game itself, but not this game.Despite the game's small issues and bugs, I genuinely had fun playing Othercide. And because of that, I highly recommend it.

My units die, but I BRING THEM BACK.Failure is an option, but you get strong and fight each time! You only lose when you stop playing...

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, i'll definitely recommend this game to the fans of genre.This game is pretty good, even with some design problems.Without further ado.What is good:1. Visuals and sound. These guys really tried to convey the atmosphere of the game and they did it.2. Interesting mechanics that try to make the game brutal and force you to make tough decisions.3. How do enemies become stronger as you progress. They are not just deal more damage, their mechanics are getting more and more complex.4. Just bonus point. Feeling when you do your first boss fight. You will understand.But there are flaws of course:1. Last few hours become gridning as you need level up your daughters and collect memories before try to fight final boss.2. "Sacrifice daughter" mechanic is ... optional and that's disappointing. Why should you level up and sacrifice daughter to heal another one when you can just restart reflection, start your new run in the last unfinished era and resurrect your favorite daughters for "free"? Yeah, you will lose memories but it's not that hard to get them.2. With  you can just one-two shot every enemy on the map (not bosses tho) on 15 lvl. With that, you can complete some missions just in 3 sec (meme with facepalm here).3. AI is bad and it's flaws easy to exploit. What about two enemies who just buff each other every turn and totaly ignore their allies and you? Or enemies who use all of their action points to just get close to you without "thinking" you'll just shoot them down on your next turn?3. Last boss is frustrating. He is not really strong or difficult, especially after you figured out the tactics. Without spoliers: you are looking at his moves 45 sec just to do yours in 5. And so EVERY turn. _childDocuments_.review: An interesting and fun tactical RPG (sort of also "puzzle-like") with a cool style and story.Do yourself a favor and play the game on Nightmare, not Dream mode. _childDocuments_.review: I love X-COM and other games with tactical battles. This game seemed to have it all and plus some: unique setting, cool aesthetic and squad based combat.After defeating the first boss, I cannot say I want to go on. The game has a very unique design where in order to heal your squad member, you need to sacrifice another of the same level. This is conceptually not a bad design - it adds on another layer of decision making and forces the player to try new tactics. Practically, though, there is nearly not enough of skills and classes for variety so it comes down to grinding low level characters up to the strongest character level to heal it. There is way to resurrect your characters, but it involves a rescue mission so..Since on the topic of missions, they are very boring - kill everything, move NPC to the zone, or have characters kill a certain amount of enemies. There are no twists, or some kind of variety so the repetitiveness sets on quick. The enemy design is very basic and a bit uninspired at times. For example, there is this huge worm that burrows towards your units and starts an AOE attack...from which you just move away from before it's setts off. That's it.The combat itself feels unpolished. There is line of sight, but  it's underused. There are obstacles but no apparent covers. Abilities are uninspired and usually just do damage. Not that there are a lot of them.It feels like it could have been a great game, but also feels it's only halfway there. It needs more interesting skills, more classes and overall make combat have more interesting decisions.Lastly, the UI is lackluster. It fails to remind you of what perks your characters have (like an Aura for example) or what passive bonuses are active. Nope, none of that, so you better have memorized all of that before the battle.There is also a roguelite element which strengthens your future runs, but I simply don't have the will to go through this grind again.
_childDocuments_.name: Othercide

_childDocuments_.review: Two things that I love about Othercide are the uncompromising emo style and fittingly cruel gameplay. Mistakes quickly spiral into death, and the many bosses of the game can chew through units after units until you crack their strategy. Yet the systems can be learned, and their depth enables real mastery over the game. You have to learn what sacrifices are necessary, which fits the theme of the player being a "mother" to their warriors.The thing to be wary of is that the game has a lot of repetition. Many battles are very similar, there isn't that much unit variety and the voice lines, oh the repetetive voice lines. It really comes down to if the gameplay and the style click with the player. I recommend giving the game some time, since the strategy elements really come into their own after the first chapter.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is actually pretty fun, but its inconsistency is too frustrating to give a recommendation.  There are a slew of bugs and other unpredictable inconsistencies that riddle this game, which is a huge problem in an ironman game with permanent health loss.  A lot of abilities are extremely vague or just don't do what they say on the tin (scythedancer's deadly dance), and others bug out or simply don't work a large amount of the time (shieldbearer's saving grace).  The timeline, the turn order of units, shows at the bottom of the screen with each character's turn in order from left to right, and their initiative number on the bottom (lower initiative is better).  You can use the timeline visual to quickly determine the number of enemy actions that will take place between your character's turns.  It's a pretty cool system...  except when it doesn't work, because for some reason characters will be placed incorrectly on the timeline, so a low initiative (fast) character will be on the far right and appear to be going later, or vice versa.  This can have dire consequences in game if you don't notice that the little white number at the bottom of a character's icon doesn't match its neighbors.Enemies will spawn in and not attack you the first turn they spawn, because that would be kind of dumb for them to damage you in a game like this with no chance to react to it.  Except, of course, for when they do for no particular reason that I can tell.The game will tell you how much armor an enemy has, so you can calculate how much damage you should do to it when you run up and target it.  Ability damage - armor = damage dealt.  Except when it doesn't calculate correctly, and your 200 damage attack that is being used on an enemy with 100 armor deals 0 damage.You can upgrade your abilities to have certain effects on hit, such as breaking enemy armor after the attack.  This is a cool way to add rider effects to "utility" abilities that you don't care much for the actual damage of.  Except when it doesn't work, and even though it shows the "armor breaking" animation, it doesn't actually reduce their armor.Believe it or not, there's actually even more that I haven't listed here such as melee enemies sometimes attacking from range, being unable to move despite having enough AP to do so, camera controls locking and more, but I think I've gotten the point across.  It is so bad that I verified the game cache because I was convinced my install must be bad, but it came back clean.  The game is legitimately pretty fun when it works correctly - hence why I have 40 hours in it at the time of this writing - but I can't recommend getting invested in it while it is in this state.

_childDocuments_.review: It has been said better in others reviews, but the problem still persist even after giving time for the game to get polished. I expected a lot of problems to have been ironed out with the "Dream" update, that allow healing of units every day up to 50% for free. It should have allowed to experiment more, especially for people with limited time.Unfortunately, the UI gets in the way. The problems there are constant: damage aren't the same between displays and seems bugged toward dealing less damage. You have reaction skill and can do a number of things, except it's an absolute pain to predict which of your unit will get attacked, even after reacting the codex that straight up tells you the monsters behaviours. Monsters will without consistency attack or not at the end of their move, ranged units will screw you, armour will ruin your day. Worse, you can equip "memories" that can change significantly your attacks (such as allowing to remove armor)... but you can't tell what memories are attached to what skill during battles. You don't remember which skill on which daughter has armor-removal? There is no way to tell, none. You essentially have to write down on paper what your daughters have.This last example is one bit of clunky interface among a lot of problems that means even fans of X-Coms, Fell Seals and so on are better off ignoring this game. _childDocuments_.review: Really fun tile-based RPG that plays a bit like XCOM, so if you liked that, chances are you will like this. The game is really successful at setting up a grim tone through the art style, enemy design, killer music and interesting color play. The gameplay loop is pretty satisfying, and the game does a great job of making you care about your choices, both inside and outside combat. You're meant to repeatedly tackle the game and fail a couple times, gaining buffs for subsequent runs. Health loss is permanent, and there's no way to recover except for by sacrificing other equally powerful units. This can have you sometimes heroically satisfying your favorite units just so you can make it a little bit further. You can always revive lost daughters, so you never completely "lose" your units. You'll spend a couple ruins beefing up your A-squad and then tackle the bosses.Good stuff-It's fun-Satisfying when your units get stronger-Cool combos between the various classes, if you set it up right-Great ambiance-Great musicI really like this game, but there's a couple things I would point out as flaws.-Needs more map/enemy options. All the fights are scripted events, with sometimes slight variations. With how much you re-encounter certain fights, even in the same run, it can get easy/uninteresting. Gets better as you get further.-Some bugs need fixin'. I've encountered a couple cases where melee enemies gain infinite range for no reason and a big part of this game is managing where your enemies are and when they can attack. Free hits suck, that damage can't be recovered without sacrifices. Aside from that, some annoying UI situations where you can't cast spells for a bit, warning tiles for attacks not going away. Had one crash to desktop but no progress lost.

_childDocuments_.review: at its core it's a great (and obviously gorgeous) game, the timeline & interruption/reaction mechanics are unique and offer a lot of depth, and the whole healing/sacrifice thing is unique and challenging, but not to everyone's taste. it's avoidable with the easy difficulty but it makes the game far too forgiving with the amount of healing you get and there's no middle ground if you want a challenge but not a total ass whoopingwhen you first start the ui feels clunky - ability ranges sometimes don't show when you hover them, menu transitions are slow and info boxes can cover enemies that you're trying to target, but you eventually learn to work around that (i didn't know wasd/arrow keys could pan)ultimately i think it's worth picking up just to play (and unlock the pretty points shop backgrounds, hehe) and quit when you stop having fun. personally if you don't feel like playing it when it's too hard it's only worth it at a discount, which is pretty common now that the game is old. i couldn't justify paying full price for the amount of time where the game would remain fun if you don't like being punished. the gameplay it offers at the beginning is great, it's just held down by balance problems, grindiness and lack of variety later on. don't feel bad about quitting the game after playing it for a while, because it runs out of stuff to show you eventually.one thing to note is that it doesn't have to be grindy if you're smart about things, i got way farther than expected in 3 recollections by using some borderline cheesy strategies (soulslinger op). another thing is that i enjoyed approaching the game as more of a puzzle to solve which meant i often restarted levels to try and find a near perfect way to finish them, which is probably going to be extremely unfun for most people

_childDocuments_.review: Turn-based strategy/tactics is one of my, if not my absolute, favorite genres. In that regard I tend to be biased towards liking them, even if they're just mediocre. This one just completely failed to grab me. The Rogue-lite elements are tedious and add nothing to the game beyond repetition. The lack of any real choices between missions does nothing to break up the monotony of grinding the same missions over and over until you unlock the ability to spawn higher level daughters. Ultimately that's the only thing that really matters once you figure out the proper tactics. Once you have a good strategy, the only thing that can stop you is that you're under-leveled or too injured for any given fight you're in. So after a while you get the ability to spawn daughters at level 4 instead of 1. So you can skip straight to the boss of the first era or just pay to skip that era completely. Later you unlock the ability to spawn level 7 daughters, which means you can fight the first two era bosses. There are two more unlocks in that section... I'm gonna go ahead and assume they allow you to generate level 10 and 12 daughters. Ultimately, these are the only abilities that really mattered in my time with the game.There are some neat ideas here, like using health to cast your most powerful abilities. It changes your perception from "how can I deal as much damage as possible" to "what's the minimum amount of health I can expend to prevent losing even bigger amounts to an enemies attack?" But even this ends up just having an obviously "best" strategy, so instead of adding a layer of depth, it just forces you to do the same thing over and over.Plenty of people seem to like this game, and maybe it would be more fun in shorter bursts than I was playing it in, but after a while it just made me want to play different tactics games with more depth.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm enjoying the game.  Thus far it has been very fair. The "Burst" system of using all your characters action gauge offers some good risk vs reward and allows you to potentially maximize abilities that use HP rather than actions points.Having to sacrifice your characters of a same or higher level is a bit off-putting. _childDocuments_.review: The tactical gameplay is really solid so far. It's like XCOM, but the initiative timeline is flexible. Controlling it is important, and you set-up combos with instant actions, delayed actions, and interrupting actions. I haven't played nearly enough to see all of it yet, but it looks like a strong system for a game.On the downside, there does not appear to be any strategic layer beyond managing units. No base-building or anything. That's the same thing Gears Tactics did. And much as I loved Gears Tactics tactical gameplay too, it eventually got stale when there was nothing to break it up. Hopefully that won't happen here. Back to positives, the game is stylish as hell and seems to have some pretty in-depth lore (there is a codex). So far it does appear to be off-brand Adeptus Sororitas battle Chaos (and specifically Nurgle in Chapter 1) after the Warp enveloped a 19th century city. But I'm totally on board for that.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that isn't as smart as it thinks it is.The central premise is that you'll die, and die, and die again. There's meta-progression in that every failure results in some bonuses for your next playthrough. This is just not a very fun concept; while it might sound interesting on paper, the end result is that you'll have to keep on grinding the same battles over and over and over. The missions are not even strategic, and often reuse the same battlefields that you've seen countless times before. Thus, the game's difficulty boils down to trial-and-error + dumb grind, rather than genuine strategic thinking.Bosses are outright unfair if you've playing blind, but are stupidly trivial if you have any experience with them. Othercide is the sort of game to reward metagaming knowledge, rather than tactical acumen. Again - this game is not as smart as it thinks it is. Othercide also only gives you 4 classes, and within each class, all units learn the exact same skills at the exact same levels. In other words, there's almost no customization or variety here. You'll begin and end the game using the same units and strategies. I like the atmosphere and vibe, and I wish I could say more positive things about Othercide. But unfortunately, it's just not a very fun or interesting game. There are plenty of great roguelite TBS games out there. This is not one of them.

_childDocuments_.review: Othercide is a strategic/tactical rogue-like RPG. This game is challenging, and will encourage players to take careful consideration in every decision they make. For starters, here are some pros and cons... Pros: +Fantastic artwork and graphical design. +Incredible replay value. +Unique tactical mechanics that grants players multiple facets to think ahead, and control the battlefield. +Every mission has variety of different enemies which keeps maps engaging to play. +Detailed lore descriptions in the codex that aid players in preparing for future combats.  +The skills in the game encourage players to try different combinations between daughters base on how they want to play.  +Daughters are the extension of a player's will. +Events that appear in the game keeps player's on their toes.  +A multitude of different skill upgrades(Memories)Cons: -Maps sometimes repeat themselves, especially hunts. -Combat can get redundant. The game encourage players to fail and fumble to make of the "Recollection" system. Essentially, players can restart their run at anytime to return stronger with buffs that are unlocked from playing the game. Every buff is potent and could give players the strength they need to take down their upcoming challenges. However, the game will still punish if you make a mistake. This is why I would like to offer a few tricks. Tips: *Recollect just before the seventh day to get the most shards out of each run. *Check the codex to see how enemies behave. Each enemy has a different way of attacking your daughters. *Make sure to keep the amount of graves in the cemetery to a minimum. Forget daughters to make sure your strong daughters aren't forgotten forever. In other words, if the cemetery is full, then daughters that die per recollection will not be buried and will be gone permanently. *Make use of the sacrifice/regeneration to grant daughter bonus stats and restore their health. Keep in mind that a daughter can only obtain the stats of one daughter or can only have daughter's soul. For example, if you gave a daughter extra damage and try to give a daughter extra health as well, then the daughter that grants health will override the previous stat or part of a daughter. Overall, I would highly recommend buying this game. It's an incredible tactical experience that is appealing, and a blast to learn. I hope you give this game a try!

_childDocuments_.review: Othercide is a strategy combat game with several interesting twists that almost add a puzzle element to it.  You enter combat with three "Daughters" and can chose from initially three (and later four) "classes" (A Tank, a Ranged, and a melee DPS).  The enemies are strong, but a bit slower than the Daughters.  The key is to set up offensive and defensive strategies in order to succeed in the various mission types.  For example, you can have your ranged sit back a bit and use their "interrupt" skill, allowing the to negate an enemy attack and do damage at the cost of some health.  These "reaction" skills are a good addition to the game and add some strategy.  You can also opt for a Daughter to essentially take a double turn, which allows her to do more on her turn but causes her next turn to come at a delay.You can eventually sacrifice your Daughter in order to heal and slightly empower another Daughter, giving you an easier time at the next attempt at progression.  In addition, you unlock bonuses that can be applied to their sills as well as other bonuses that can give you passive abilities.  The more "points" you earn from runs, the more of these you can apply...making progression even easier (although never too easy).The bosses can be a bit tough your first time, since you need to figure out what their main mechanic is.  After that, they tend to be easier.   Your memory may be better than mine, but it may not hurt to take notes so you can remember the best strategy for each boss.These small additions make for an interest strategy game.  The game looks amazing, but my laptop fan definitely stays running at full speed.  In addition, there are some very minor bugs, such as sometimes your movement range not being highlighted for you.  The atmosphere of the game is great...it can be a lot of fun to puzzle through the lore.Overall, this is a great game.  If you are a fan of tactic based games, with a hint of puzzle elements, then this game is a no brainer...especially if the atmosphere strikes your fancy.  I didn't beat it (I'd imagine I'm about half way through), but someone else who is really into this genre probably could sink their teeth into it even further than I did.

_childDocuments_.review: Darkest Dungeon meets Transistor. If you enjoyed the game play loop and appreciated the permanent death of Darkest Dungeon, and are able to maintain that ruthless, commander mindset -- rather than becoming attached to your heroes -- then you should definitely play this game! The main menu music is the best track.Levels are small and few in number.  Each era is slightly different, but the reuse of a limited number of layouts makes the game somewhat repetitive. _childDocuments_.review: Really good concept, quite creative. However, it is a lazy outcome. If the key concept is the sacrifice, it is really not much for exploring or try out. Basically, after maybe half day exploring the sacrifice system, what has left is but mechanical/boring combats and boss fights which we have seen in everywhere. _childDocuments_.review: I bought Othercide because I'm a turn-based strategy addict. If aliens ever invade, and only engage in turn-based tactics, Earth will be safe. I got you covered. So when I fired up Othercide and enjoyed the lovely tutorial I was all set to defeat the forces of darkness. Then the game says it wants you to fail. And you will fail. At least it is beautiful while pulling out your soul through your spleen.This was where my familiarity with XCOM failed me. You can't lose to the aliens! But Othercide has roguelike/roguelite mechanics which were new to me. The idea of losing, and restarting was, at first, unappealing. Then you start to unlock stuff. Cool stuff. Stuff that makes your Daughters go from fragile warriors of light to slightly less fragile warriors with awesome fashion sense and giant swords with flames and...oh my. I need to sit down.In short, it's a gorgeous piece of punishing turn-based strategy. Buy it if you like those things.
_childDocuments_.name: Othercide

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DRVery enjoyable roguelite with a really wonky difficulty curve. I can sincerely say I enjoyed my ~25 hours with this game - a very rare gem these days. I hope they continue to add more content; and frankly I wouldn't mind paying for it.The game plays like any other strategy RPG like: XCOM, Divinity Original Sin, Final Fantasy Tactics, etc...It's a turned based game where you have a certain amount of Action Points per turn to accomplish something. This games unique edge is their "timeline system." Nothing bleeding edge, but essentially a order of events too occur - player turns, enemy turns, specific actions. Once you learn how to abuse it, things become very easy. The GoodI really liked the aesthetics and music. The characters, the bosses, the units, were all designed very well and fitting for the style of game.I very much enjoyed the game play. Personally I love the aforementioned games above, so this was easy for me. Again though, it's nothing really new, it's still a good implementation. I liked the different classes and the way they played (but see caveat below in "The Bad"). The length is just about right and just feels like a nice game to spend a few hours on.The BadThe classes are pretty skewed. It's very possible that I could be playing wrong, but I tend to min/max things. And it was very easy, clear, and wide what was min and what was max. The difficulty curve is very weird. Starting from very easy, to fairly challenging, to hard, to downright wtf. Some of the bosses, felt like it was scaled specifically for multiple repeats - I get this is the roguelike archetype, but it felt very forced. From my perspective, I enjoyed being challenged, but I hate artificial challenges like invulnerability phases, one-shot kills or other unavoidable cheese mechanics. It can certainly be argued those are valid gameplay challenges, but I just don't like them.The WhateverThe roguelite aspect I think goes a little too far. It marginalizes a significant portion of the game - most which can be achieved via 1 run. The game has a trait system that allows your units to gain peculiar bonuses, but it's semi-random and not always good. I like the idea but the randomness too it just doesn't feel good. This is hard to explain without spoiling anything but it also actively dissuades playing units in a particular fashion when there is nothing to force the opposite or appropriate fashion.There are some abilities that absolutely trump the alternative for some units.The VerdictI very much enjoy the game. If you like a simple roguelite similar the games mentioned above I think it's an easy decision. Though I did get this on sale for 50% off. I would probably pay full price for it though, but would just recommend watching a video or two to see if it interests you.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Never has a game been more style over substance for me. Not to say it's bad! But it needed another pass to be great.The good:-Visually distinct, with a great atmospheric moody feel drenched in some good ol' gothic-eldritch horror and a sin-city style color pallet. -Interesting ideas for mechanics, enemies, challenges, story, etc. -Each class has a role to play, meaning no class feels left out, while at the same time most compositions are fine so you won't need-Trait system where units get buffs (and occasional berfs) depending on chance and what happened in a mission (though the list could stand to be expanded and have codex entries to explain said criteria rather than players having to guess)They variable:-The story is interesting, but dripping in edgy, tropey language that makes things ambiguous. If you like piecing the story together from codex entries, then you'll like this, otherwise you'll just have to ride the tropes/general vibe.-Numbers are very big and wide ranged. Some people like this. I prefer my tactical games to have smaller, more accurate numbers for quicker calculations on whether something is lethal or not. -Fully capable of exploiting the game's mechanics-Permanent damage but impermanent death: The only way to heal is to kill another of your units in sacrifice, but you get several things that give you revive tokens to rez your dead characters, even between runs.-Very much rogue-LITE. While you begin a new run when you run out of characters, you get tons of stuff that not only heavily buffs you, but lets you bring those characters back, at the exact way they were when the died (minus a few equipables)The Bad:-Desperately, desperately needs quality of life adjustments. I understand not wanting to compromise your visual style but in a tactical game I should be able to figure out my enemies' movement and attack ranges without having to try and memorize or compare to scenery instead of being able to just toggle it on. What scenery blocks line of sight for attacks? Why doesn't the AI behave the way described in the codex? Why do I have to go in and out of a menu 2-3 times to make the "you've got something new" notification go away. -Gameplay is slow, movement and positioning cleverly is discouraged over a more general turtle strat-Not enough class variety. The choices between skills meant to diversify within a class will often have obvious right answers, especially since many skills consume hitpoints that can never be regenerated making them boss-only skills. -A lot of information could stand to be made clearer-The achievement for perfecting the tutorial is weirdOverall, I give the game a slight recommendation, like a 6/10. If it got a big patch to address the QA and information issues it'd be a 7 or 8. The question you've got to ask yourself is do the things I listed in variables sound like things you enjoy, or things you hate. If you like those things, and I like a good chunk of them, you'll get some fun out of Othercide despite it's style over substance.
_childDocuments_.name: Othercide

_childDocuments_.review: Here is a game that is proud to show its influences on it's sleeves.If you are looking for an XCom beater, this isn't it. However, if you are looking for a deceptively deep turn-based strategy - this is sort of it. Once you have the mobs you are fighting figured out, it gets a whole lot easier.Graphically the whole thing is inspired by Silent Hill and Schindler's list - Black, White and Red are basically the only colours you'll see (And those three mixed together). But they are quite striking.The concept of a time-loop has been done before, but here it tells an interesting story - one you have to dig to really understand a-la Dark Souls.A word on grind - yes, this is a grindy, grindy game. But I don't mind those on occasion.Advice: Buy, and enjoy!EDIT: I never really bother 100%'ing a game. And yet, here we are. That's how much I enjoyed this!

_childDocuments_.review: Well, if anything this is "Depression: The Game"... You are "Mother" a Memory of a once great Soul who fights for the mind and well-being of "The Child", which has suffered from illness, mistreatment, and misleading. Your daughters, all beatiful and fierce women each one specialized in one particular weapon. Every mistake costs you, as you are not able to just "heal up" with medkits or through "magic". Every injured daughter stays injured unless another daughter of the same strength sacrifices herself to heal and buff another one. Reviging is even more difficult as it requires innocent souls to do.You can never "truly loose" but you will be set back to the beginning. Strengthend by the recollection and memories of the last run.The graphic, sound and overall setting are just brilliant, and unique. Sadly the voicelines repeat often, depening on what memories (something like loot) you find. Some bugs appeared. I had the regular occurence of markings on the map not being removed, once the unit was displaced or moved somewhere else. Leaving me to just think of the new location etc. Nothing game braking but annoying.The difficulty level even on the higher "nightmare" difficulty feels absolutely fair. Harsh, calculating and sometimes depending on luck, but completely fair. Especially given, that your daughters are in fact much stronger than any of the enemies.Once a daughter reaches level 15 she gains a really powerful ability, especially the Scythedancer, which makes most battles trivial.If I get to rate I would give it something around 4,5 out of 5. Fix the mentioned minor bugs and repeating voice lines and it is just perfect.Finished in 20h on nightmare difficulty (harder of the two choices).
_childDocuments_.name: Othercide

_childDocuments_.review: Othercide is a dark and gritty turn-based combat game that focuses a lot on the game's combat timeline. Through success and repeated failure, your Daughters will grow and become more and more powerful. There are a few different classes that offer variety in tactics and each milestone in leveling them up gives you two options to further specialize your daughter to your playstyle. + Othercide is actually quite difficult. At the beginning, even clearing the first of several bosses is a monumental task. As you progress, the game gets more surmountable. It always maintains its difficult posture, so when you are able to beat it there is a lot of satisfaction.+ Othercide really just gives you all the information to work with in order to defeat enemies. It shows you how far enemies can move, the range of their attacks, and what all their skills do. When they activate an ability, it also shows up on the timeline letting you know how long you have to avoid or prevent it. If you hover over the tool-tip on the timeline, it also brings up the monster stat card to display the ability directly.+ The game tells its message of suffering very well. Whenever you take damage, the damage is permanent throughout following maps. While any one combat may be easier than others, one hit can mean trouble further down the road of torment. It really makes you feel bloodloss as you make your way through the many levels. Even certain abilities, such as ones allowing you to protect another Daughter, cost health instead of action points. + Othercide has a very unique story and world that you slowly learn more of as you unlock "Memories" by defeating opponents. Its exciting to receive these drops as each one is like another page in a book you are trying to collect. While these drops aren't part of the main story per se, it just provides a further look into the world that is Othercide. You lead your Daughters through the trials that The Child has faced and understand and hate what happened to him more and more.+ Babes.- While each boss fight is very unique, has several phases, and is just a joy to face, the maps working towards them is a lot less so. The maps themselves aren't super varied and while there are several enemy types, about half of them are re-skinned upgrades that only have inflated stat cards. In terms of the variety of maps and monsters, the aesthetic (while I enjoy) might have been a limiting factor in making things a bit more unique, but that is only counting a color palette. Spawn points on each map seem set as well, so the combats largely play out the same.- I really love that everything you do moving from map to map matters so much if you want to get as far as you can or even clear a "Recollection". Now, what is less satisfying is when something seems to break the rules a bit. Typically when an enemy spawns in, it can move, but won't attack during its first turn. Occasionally, an enemy will spawn in and hit one of your Daughters after moving anyway. With it happening infrequently, it always feels like the game cheated you. Sometimes it can also spawn an enemy right next to you, who then hits you for free, without you having the ability to even know it was coming. While this does occur infrequently, if you are going through the game very strategically, it can be enough to put a bad taste in your mouth.- Some of the balance is...questionable. The game offers a variety of skills and classes, but there is always an optimal choice. Many skills just aren't comparable. For instance, the Soulsinger and Blademaster have a "chain" ability where you will strike an enemy that is damaged. If you have a squad of Daughters that each have this ability, you can sky rocket the amount of damage a boss is taking with each attack. I just wish the other skill in several instances was worth taking.- The boss fights are fantastic bar none I would say. However, even with the bosses pretty much always remaining challenging, you do get to a point where the regular maps are anything but. I understand that with the amount of them they need to be easier, but I frequently found myself not being challenged at all by them. I was grinding out the monster maps to level up my daughters and try to get more memory drops. That was it. It was very much like walking into a shop, grabbing something, and leaving. With the repetitive maps and monsters, the lack of a lot of the challenge in regular maps made them increasingly more stale.Overall, I really enjoy Othercide. Some people don't like the aesthetic and I'm in the pool that does, but everyone has their preferences. I found it extremely fun to plan everything out and even take on overwhelming numbers of enemies. As I mentioned, you feel very weak when you start out and just feel more and more powerful the longer you play. It is a very satisfying game to beat if you can make it through its repetitive nature. If I were to suggest anything to the Devs, I would ask them to make more skills worth taking and make more varied enemies. The repeated maps are not too much of an issue as they are well designed, but random spawn points could liven those up as well. In conclusion, if turn-based combat is a style you enjoy, I would greatly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely make reviews, but Jesus Christ, if you like turn-based tactics game, do yourself a favor and grab this one. At full price, even. This is one of the greatest games in recent memory.The story is abstract, but made much more clear as you progress.Even with that abstraction, though, the two primary characters- the protagonist and antagonist- are fantastic characters that I'll be thinking about for a long time.The visuals are incredible- very slick, stylish, and cool, while maintaining a quick pace. It's the textbook definition of "spectacular;" it's a literal spectacle.And, finally, the music goes hard.The only warning I'll give is that this game is TOUGH, even on the easier difficulty setting. There are a few cheesy exploits you can either find or google if you really hit a wall, though. This is one of my favorite games I've played in years, and I'll be keeping a close eye on the devs from now on.

_childDocuments_.review: This and XCOM: Chimera Squad are now my go-to turn based tactics games. Great art, music, and combat. Only issue is that the game can and will get repetitive, but that's kind of the theme of the game at the same time. _childDocuments_.name: Othercide

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game, but not great as well. Not much content, but the last boss is really hard, and dying to it involves a huge punishment in having to revisit the same content again. I could kill the last boss in my sixth try save scumming, otherwise I would have stopped playing the game if I lost to it again. Also, as you play, you start learning that some upgrades (traits) are not possible to be achieved for some daughters (your warriors) in certain conditions, and the only way to get them is leveling up new daughters from level 1, after the game gives you the option to have daughters at higher levels without those upgrades and you probably already started leveling them.You get to level cap before reaching the last boss, so you can’t really farm before fighting it very much, which makes the roguelite mechanic of restarting the game become somewhat pointless and annoying. Skills are few and they are divided in either essential or useless, and you can choose between two of them at level up. If in your inexperience you chose a useless skill over an essential one, depending on the circumstance, that character is almost useless afterwards, and imagine that on a character full of good traits. The story fragments I could put together doesn't seem appealing, the game seems to be about emotional trauma, which to me is too sentimental and I’m already saturated with this kind of talk.Graphically the game is beautiful, and have a great soundtrack. The idea of making a game almost completely black and white was great as well, it worked. But the levels repeat too much, specially for a game that is already repetitive. Sometimes I would fight two times in a row in the same arena. Considering how difficult the last boss is, it can become very repetitive if a person tries to follow the rules by the letter, like not backing up their saves and only allowing the daughters being healed by sacrificing another daughter. I think that a person that does this can spend probably over 50 hours playing the same content. Anyway, I saw the end of the game, I’m happy for that, and because of it I recommend the game. But it’s too expensive for what it offers.
_childDocuments_.name: Othercide

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game. It feels kinda bad that you have to sacrifice daughters of equal or higher lvls to heal up others since you get very limited ressurects. The game has amazing strategic play which is why I still recommend it even though its a bit rough to get into. Also there's a bug where changing the location of a boss who is casting a delayed action doesn't update the action's "danger" highlight so sometimes you get out of the area and still get hit or viceversa. Over all good game, but it will make you cringe with a few of the decisions you'll have to make.

The voice acting was good in places and not in others.  The story was abstract, but interesting enough.  Getting through the first two or three bosses took effort, I really had to force myself to keep playing to see where the game was going, but the repetitive nature and lack of character diversity actually builds itself into having more strategy than you'd think at first.  ... meh ...

_childDocuments_.review: I would love to recommend this game, but I just can't. In its current state it just not as enjoyable as it could be, and could use some changes.The first major change I would like to see is to have "trigger" type abilities fade on an initiative of 100. This means that a full initiative cycle will pass before the HP I just sacrificed is wasted. Got real annoyed using the Gunner's overwatch ability just to have her be the next unit in initiative.The next is diversity. Its possible that I just haven't gotten far enough in the game to get to see other classes, but so far all I have seen is blademaster, shieldmaster and soulslinger and it gets repetitive quickly.The last is I think many people would enjoy this more with an "easy" mode where you can regenerate Daughters with Vitae instead of sacrifice. This mechanic reminds me of Darkest Dungeon and I didn't like the stress mechanic in that either.

_childDocuments_.review: The game basically a TBS rougelike, like XCOM but quite a bit more difficult. Very fair though, you are usually overwhelmed by the enemies but they behave in a consistent manner, so the trick is to figure out how they will react. It can get a bit repetitive because of the roguelike element, but within reason. What really sold the game for me though is the art style and the soundtrack, both of which are awesome and create a magnificent atmosphere. Probably top 5 most atmospheric games I've ever played. For that alone the game gets a big recommend from me!
_childDocuments_.name: Othercide

_childDocuments_.review:
Othercide is a horror-themed turn-based strategy game where the lore and game mechanics are tightly intertwined to deliver a twisted, dark and challenging experience. Enter a brutal world under assault from terrifying creatures from another dimension, hold back the tide with limited resources and endure brutal conditions in visually stunning world.

Experience dynamic turn-based combat and a new way to anticipate enemy movements to perform a flawless tactical plan. Using the Initiative Sequence System and unique set of skills, you will be able to interrupt an enemy attack, plan a delayed action that will be triggered later on in the timeline and use reaction skill to respond to any threat.

Prepare to suffer and face close calls in our terrifying and ruthless universe. With roguelite features, deadly missions, limited resources and permanent death, there is no room for errors.

Level up, unlock new skills and collect memories from the death of your enemies. A limited number of these bonuses can be implemented to your skills to boost their stats. But choose wisely as once implemented, you can't take them back, unless... you decide to sacrifice your Daughter!

Make dramatic choices and endure with your Daughters traumatic experiences which will make them stronger or weaker.

Othercide invites you in a ethereal monochromatic dimension with only dashes of crimson red where your worst nightmares come to life.

name: Dungeon Munchies
detailed_description: Buzz Discord : About the Game Hunt down monsters to cook and eat them! You’ve been revived in a massive underground complex and you must leave this bizarre facility. Aided by the undead Necro-Chef Simmer, you must stay safe, get fed and find a way to get out. Dungeon Munchies is a side-scrolling action RPG with a focus on hunting down creatures, cooking them, and eating dishes to gain certain abilities. The combination of dishes you choose to eat will impact your entire play style. Features: Big Menu for a Big Stomach With a stomach that can only take seven dishes, you must put together a meal that maximises your abilities. Guava juice, grilled shrimp, or crab stirfry may mean the difference between health recovery, damage output or a watery shield. Tools of the Trade Craft all kinds of deadly weapons out of the animal and plant parts you can't eat. Pair them with your favorite dishes to create the most overpowered combat combo. Farm-fresh & Locally-sourced In this day and age, ingredients are hard to come by. You should be prepared to face off electrical snails, razor-sharp shrimp claws, and laser wasps to get the delicious parts you need. Something Doesn’t Feel Right... From the self-professed-AAA-license-holding necro-chef, to the diabolical voodoo “Lord of the Forest”, to the radical revolutionaries of the fruit revolution, everyone wants you to do their thing, but no one's really right in the head. What’s really happening down in this dungeon?

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeon Munchies is an interesting game. At first it looks like nothing more than you usual unity-engine sidescroller. Sure the art looks funny, but nothing to write home about. But then you see all the positive reviews, and you go "sure, why not, worth a try". You carry that same air of ambivalence to the first few parts of the game, the stages seem basic and the combat is nothing to write home about. The characters seem a little cool, you guess, but not worth getting attached to. Seems a little overblown by those reviews.But oh. The game continues.Combat? A min-maxer's dream. Platforming? Mario odyssey eat your heart out. Story? THE STORY? Every expectation you didn't have about this unassuming title is blown out of the water. You are making connections and firing neurons and that damn art and writing just gets better and better with every level. You are scrounging each level for the secrets and extra weapons not because you'll use them but because of how good this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game is. Each character is a close personal friend and you want to see them succeed and thrive. You have gone through the five stages of grief and your own ego death and come out the other side as a true appreciator of Dungeon Munchies, and what can you possible do after all that? Well, you can make a review like this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: ExceptionalDungeon Munchies is a side scrolling dungeon crawler with flavor. And yes, pun intended. You awaken by means of necromancy by the necro-cook Simmer. And you're put straight to work! You make your way through the massive underground facility, fighting creatures along the way. Each creature drops items you can use to cook with. And each cooked or crafted item is added to your inventory or abilities for use and lasts forever. This unique pixel art game has humor and life that isn't all that common today. The game play is tight and responsive. There are a lot of things to fall in love with here! I hope you enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: What. The. Hell.I expected: Dungeon Meshi, Happy anime treats, metroidvania with some cooking elements and wacky weapons!What I got: Junji Ito's Body Horror Nightmares given flesh. And bone. And vegetable. Twists, Turns, a giant SCP, several SCPs, more nightmare fuel, earnest tales of loss, revolution, coups and realpolitik.And all that only covered chapter one and half of chapter two. You owe it to yourself to play this incredibly odd, heartfelt, amazingly weird and horrific game. Go for easy mode if you have to, but you have got to see how this ride goes, and where it ends. It is a dish that is so very much more than the sum of its ingredients.

_childDocuments_.review: (Editing in my chapter 2 Opinions below my original review)Dungeon munchies was an unexpected gem I found while browsing the up and coming tab. Combat was easy to pick up, story was decent and the food mechanic was quite interesting. Though for all the praise I will give this game, there are some flaws in it (note: this is still early access, so some of these problems might get fixed later on).PROS:- combat is easy to pick up and the difficulty of mobs and bosses scale really well.- all of the enemies in the game has its own unique charm. Personally, I love fighting the final boss.- the game isn't too "grindy" compared to other titles.- the comedy might be a hit or miss for some people, but it gives the story a decent amount of flavor.- the food buffs appearing on your character is a pretty nice touch.CONS:- music was good, but wasn't really memorable in my opinion.- since its early access I won't be too harsh, but its really disappointing that you can cheese the 2nd boss by manipulating its ai using dashes- this game is made for mouse and keyboard, using controller in this game is possible, albeit harder. Had to switch to mouse and keyboard on the final fight.- story was pretty "eh" most of the time, didn't pay much attention to the story until the end where they forcibly fed you all the information in one go.All in all, I think its worth the price. Yes it may be incomplete as of now but the amount of content you do get more than makes up for the money you spent on it. I might have missed some details in my review, but I will probably address those when the game is finally finished.CHAPTER 2 REVIEWAlthough it took a while, chapter 2 has been released! New recipes, enemies, and bosses to experiment and play around with. Gameplay has stayed pretty much the same, but the devs added new weapons and mechanics and the tone of the story shifted drastically compared to the first one. (Similar to my previous review, ill add a pro and con to quickly summarize the changes.)PROS:- Combat has been improved with the addition of new recipe buffs and upgrades, giving viability to other styles of combat.- The "gun" archetype is a nice addition, albeit a bit too powerful in my opinion.- Some of the newer bosses are incredibly fun. My favorite of the bunch is mercury one, a unique bosses that changes between arena battle and side scrolling platformer depending on its current phase.- the story is better paced this time, giving the player time to digest the information rather than shoving it all in one go like last time.- some of the newer tracks are a banger.CONS:- the game is still a bit buggy. In my playthrough of the second chapter, I abused the "reload" glitch.- the comedy from the first half of the game was toned down by a lot (this can either be a positive or a negative)- the balance scaling is not great. The difficulty between the first escort quest (hard) and the first 2 bosses after(easy) is quite jarring. - more into balance scaling, some bosses are just glorified damage sponges.- the game is still made for mouse and keyboard.Overall, I think the second chapter was great. It gave better insight on the overall goals of the main cast and was better at world building compared to the previous chapter. It has a few bugs and problems here and there, but combat has greatly improved. I would still recommend this game and it's still well worth its price.

_childDocuments_.review: A weird ass game with SOUL.Terraria-ish combat with a lot of build variety by equipping food items. Mostly linear with a little bit of side paths for extra recipes. The story is... much more than you expect from the game, and from the first few hours.What starts as a truly bizarre game about celebrating cooking and eating things that were all alive, including plants, quickly becomes an existential dread simulator featuring body horror. To say the game undergoes a tone shift isn't quite accurate. It's more like a tone catapult.The writing can sometimes be a bit too corny as characters will talk at length about >THEMES OF THE GAME<, but it's heartfelt and the characters have great chemistry with each other. The comedy has a lot of good usage of art assets, too. It's a fun, rather breezy ride.I do think there's more design than what meets the eye in the bosses and platforming, but the player becomes so horrifyingly strong, and easily, that even on master chef it feels like the game falls over without too much issue, the bosses largely because of one food item that lets you delete projectiles via dashing, and the platforming because the obstacles simply aren't threatening enough.Either way, a fun romp with fun characters and it has Simmer, so 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeon Munchies. A fairly bizarre but attractive game has been released on Steam. It's a 2d side-scrolling action game made by maJAJa. The player was resurrected as a zombie, but with the help of the undead Necro-Chef Simmer, you gained special abilities. It's cooking! Hunt dungeon creatures, get ingredients, and cook them. The player then gains the unique abilities of each dungeon creature. The interesting thing is that you can not overeat. There are various dungeon creatures, but there are limits to the number of unique abilities you can absorb. This makes gameplay more interesting and addictive. When exploring dungeons, required special abilities and equipment are required for your own strategy. Especially, the boss battle is quite challenging!Dungeon Munchies. It's still early access, but it has plenty of potential. Until I hit the first boss battle, I could not stop playing this game. Cartoon-style characters are really cute and humorous. It is extremely addictive, fun and challenging! Controls need adjustment, but that's not much of a problem. If the balance and optimization progress with content updates, it will definitely be a good game. Highly Recommended!*The review score criteria from Nyanco Channel will be rated according to price, genre, early access, and so on. Furthermore, most of them are Nyanco's own thoughts, so these reviews may be different from the the general users' opinions. Thanks![Steam] Nyanco Channel ヽ(=^･ω･^=)丿

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR:  It’s alright, 20 USD as of coming out of early access for something you’ll finish in a playtime of 10-20 hours.  Personally recommend picking this up on sale.    Context: Followed the game's updates for a few years casually after watching a playthrough of the first chapter during early access.  Played both major story updates when they came out during the early access period, and it’s been more or less the same, a solid 2D hack and slasher.    Gameplay:Gameplay itself is as stated, a solid 2D linear metroidvania-lite with an assortment of standard faire melee, ranged, and magic options available to you.  Along with a perk, “magic food”, system to give you modest build variety of your preference.  Wherein you would settle into a favored niche of a dual-wielding blender, out of kilter crab cyborg mage, or dual wielding shotguns, all with the freedom to change them freely at checkpoints.    A few personal gripes with the gameplay:- The semi-frequent double/triple jumping doesn’t work as intended.  Extra jumps simply gain you no height and you just "spurt" in place.- In fights with tons of magic particle effects flying on the screen make it occasionally hard to keep track of what’s going on.  (Skill issue for some maybe.) :^)- On exceptionally rare occasions it feels as though some weapon/perk builds may or may not have their numbers bugged when amidst the hectic action going on the screen, almost as if the game struggles to work through it all at once.    Story/Art:Story is delivered to you via Visual Novel-esque text at certain points of the story.  It’s cute, comedic, grows dark and edgy, then grows into waxing philosophical existential crises.  If you like the sound of that, it’s exactly what you’ll get.  As for the art, if it’s the anime cartoonish art style that grabbed your attention, you’ll get more of it as you play through the story.    Stability/Port:No major issues on my end from playing on my old Intel CPU and GeForce RTX 1070 desktop system during multiple points in Dungeon Munchies early access.  Same deal today, no issues on my stronger rig using a mid-range CPU and 3070 GPU.  Granted this game has the graphical intensity of a Newgrounds flash game.If you skimmed through any of this, I hope it helps informing you on whether you'd like to try this game out for yourself, take care and take it easy.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a true hidden masterpiece, it's been years since I've experienced a game with such beautiful writing, it knows when to take itself seriously and when to parody both media and real life, ranging from enjoying life to existential dread, what makes us human, society, power, etc.All of this is presented with fun and perfectly balanced gameplay in which you can create ANY build that suits your playstyle, funny relatable main and side characters which had me exhausting every dialogue option and enjoyable level designs that introduced new mechanics in each new area; one thing that let me down a bit was the music, in my opinion it sounded a bit generic and non-memorable, other than that this game is a true 10/10.Please, play this game, it is truly a labor of love.I can't wait to see what the developer will publish next, thank you so much maJAJa for existing and creating this wonderful experience.

_childDocuments_.review: It's unfinished but I've enjoyed it enough already that I feel I got my money's worth. I'm excited for more to come out! They also pushed a big update very recently, so the project isn't dead like lots of early access games might be. Just note that boss fights can end up ridiculously easy if you pay attention to what food you equip. I shake up my loadout regularly to try and appreciate the many different playstyles (there's lots!), and I've found that pretty much everything breaks the game. XD The final boss in chapter 1 for example went down in ~1 minute for me, completely without damaging me because I nullified all damage. It seemed like a very well made and fun boss fight... unfortunately I didn't experience it because I was able to just ignore everything and hit the boss really hard.I literally have never died in this game properly using the power ups. axe + hatchet + speed food = 500DPS and damage immunity. Maxing out poision and bleeding with a dagger and I'm doing 300+ poison damage for every hit, I slap an enemy once then run off and watch them just die at a distance. I'm playing at Normal (Souse Chef?) difficulty, so maybe it's better in hard mode?

_childDocuments_.review: Blew every expectation I had for it out of the water. Each chapter was better than the last and chapter 3 in particular was just perfect. It's not super innovative or new gameplay but I love min-maxing so seeing my DPS spike as I got new builds definitely gave me a massive boost of serotonin. I freaking LOVE the story and characters. It starts out small and linear but bit by bit a greater picture comes into focus and it's definitely worth the wait to see it. The dialogue is that perfect balance of satire but tinted with actual emotion where things feel natural given the interactions rather than just "guys we're so meta this is peak comedy am I right?" Would recommend this game 100% as it's one of the best surprises I've had in a while

_childDocuments_.review: The first impressions of this game are tough, as are the first hours of playing it. The beginning doesn't leave a good impression.But, only the beginning of it.I can see why different people don't recommend it with that little hours they played it, and I agree. Like I said already, my first impression of the game wasn't good either. The start is slow, really slow. The first hours seems unsatisfactory, the weapons are too, especially the ranged ones, the combat and the gameplay seem slow too. After 4 hours of it I told myself "Maybe I should've refund it, I hope something better is around the corner" and such, because the only things I liked of this game was the characters, and not even that much. BUT.But, after the first chapter, for absolutely no reason, everything became more enjoyable. The gameplay was more dynamic, the weapons more interesting, the passives more intriguing, the characters were more charming and there were new too! (Simmer still best girl though). The OSTs, the story too...I found myself reading a specific dialogue and having literally chills from it, with a little of sadness too, to the point where a tear was about to come out. Then, a minute later, another line of dialogue made me laugh with the dumbest smile of my face for how it killed the vibe from some minutes before. The devs really know how to put a smile on your face, and how to turn sad moments into funny and cute ones, this is definitely the main grit of this game.After chapter 1, everything changes. the backgrounds and the vibes too. I feel like this game took inspiration both from  and , because the monsters and the theme really reminds me of them, the sound effects and the background noises too, somehow...So you can expect a creepy and unsettling vibe; well, more unsettling than creepy but it's surely something that you wouldn't think about when you first start this game; at least I didn't. I expected just a funny and cute environment, but the story and the atmosphere is serious and later on, even dark.So in conclusion, the game is worth it in my opinion, especially if on sale (two hours are not enough to understand if you like it or not, unfortunately. You just have to trust that the more you'll go on, the more you'll like it). The platform is fine, OSTs great, characters lovable and wonderful (Simmer ♥, and Grill too, best dinamic duo), the story is good too and it always get better as you continue it, it's truly a climax; art is cute and funny, dialogues too...I do agree that some stuff could be improved; the menu is still buggy when you open it (not a big of a deal but annoying), some bosses are confusing. But at the end of the day, I do not regret buying this game.

_childDocuments_.review: So, first off, don't pay attention to the fact I have 27 hours on this game. That was because I left it on during the night and most of the day by accident. My playthrough itself was around 6 hours, and mind you we're talking with collecting all hidden recipes, seeing all the dialogue and going for 100% completion. And I must say, it was a great experience.Let's start off with my shorter list - grievances. It mostly boils down to two things - the music, while pretty well-suited for the scenes and stages it was accompanying, was mostly forgetful. The one track I can remember is the whistling tune that plays before and after you fight the first boss, in the stage you fight him at.The second, and somewhat larger con I had with the game, was the uneven pacing of story. It starts off kind of goofy, what with you being a zombie resurrected by the spirit of a college student necromancer chef (named Simmer, which I appreciate). You get little tidbits of story, mostly the background of Simmer and her more prominent skeleton servants (Khamul the Weaponsmith with an Existential Crisis, Tyler The Big, The Bad, The Clumsy, and Emma the Necromanced Necromancer who also happens to be Tyler's girlfriend), and some story on the why The Lord Protector and Simmer are on bad terms, and with a small bit of exploration and speaking to NPC's you also find out some other plot points (not gonna spoil them). But then you get to the final parts of Chapter 1, and an avalanche of story is being thrown at you. Not a lot, mind you, and some such info does answer questions instead of creating new ones, but compared to the ratio of "gameplay to storytelling" of the earlier parts of the game, the balance falters as the chapter ends on mostly "Go here, read this".Oh, there's also the fact that the first two dishes basically become useless a bit further into the game. Since you get permanent double jumps and the Fried Mosquito doesn't give you a third jump, there is literally no reason to equip it later on, and the Mean Grilled Fish makes you faster in water, but there's literally never a reason to need to be faster in water. I'd be happy if those were buffed a bit. At least the Fried Mosquito.Now, onto the Good Sides of the game (and I'll say each one much more shortly):All in all, this game is already great, and it's still in , first of 4 chapters. And if all of them are this kind of quality... Well, let's just say this indie darling will definitely become a hit.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably one of my all-time favorite games now. _childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly endearing platformer.Without saying too much, the story goes to some REALLY unexpected places and i ended up reading every bit of dialogue i could find because the characters were interesting and likeable.I'm a bit torn when it comes to gameplay however: the main gameplay mechanic of eating differents foods to obtain passive and active abilities is very fun and lets you come up with some crazy (downright unbalanced) combos, but the stiff character movement and awkward jumping hold the game back pretty significantly.It's no game of the year contender, but its janky charm had me hooked from start to finish.
