_childDocuments_.review: A charming little indie game in which you play as a zombie powering up through the power of questionable recipes and eating dishes made from the various monsters you kill throughout the game. Gameplay-wise it is a 2D hack and slash with a sprinkle of some bullet-hell. While I found that the build variety was serviceable, I did enjoy all the options and play styles available to the player. The game is quite easy in terms of a creating synergistic build that will be able to carry you to the end of the game.There are some platforming challenges within the levels but they are not challenging at all considering you can just brute force your way through without dying.The combat itself was not very challenging due to later enemies basically being HP sponges to whittle down before you move on to the boss/next areas. The bosses were slightly more enjoyable as they had move sets that needed to be dodged and bullet hell sections where you only focused on dodging. In terms of level design, the game is quite linear with usually a branching short path that leads to a hidden collectable recipe or weapon every now and then. The game is not grindy at all as going through a level and killing most of the enemies will get you enough of the materials naturally in order to craft a specific dish/weapon that needs the materials found in that level. Overall the linearity of the game was a small detriment but I did not mind as it was still an enjoyable experience as there was minimal backtracking. The games art is pretty good, with a nice pixel art and anime style with the visual novel dialogue sections. The real standout surprise of this game is the characters and story. The characters are all quite charming and entertaining and the story was more than I expected for a small indie like this. The game manages to hit a good amount of comedic story beats and dialogue in a way that isn't just cringy humour. Some of the emotional story beats were quite solid as well. Overall this game was a pleasant experience, would recommend it if you enjoy the aesthetic of a 2D anime hack and slash with a focus on cooking and zombies.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write reviews.  Just not me.  But there needs to be some dissenting opinion here.  This game is decent, but far from the overwhelmingly positive score it has somehow earned.It's got some promise, including a framework for great mechanics, a fascinating world, and a lot of fun dialogue.  But it never really delivers.  The level design, and potential for exploration therein, never really develops, and there's only a tiny handful of explorable hidden areas.  The cooking, and related perks and bonuses, ends up feeling rushed and kinda thrown together by the end of the game.  The story itself is left totally unfinished.It was neat, but overpriced and undeserving of the score it currently carries.  I blew through it in 7 and a half hours, liberally taking my time and exploring, and was left feeling noticeably dissatisfied and letdown because of the high expectations set by the other reviews.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. This was, uh, not exactly what I was expecting to get in to when I first stumbled across this. Note, I did play this on the Steam Deck and had basically no issues running it (other than some minor bugs mentioned below), though I can see how playing with a mouse may be easier.I watched Ceres Fauna play part of chapter one, and it came across as a happy-go-lucky little metroridvania with cute art and little jokes. You can make weed as a food, isn't that cute? You're a funny little zombie guy, isn't that funny? The necromancer lady is cute and make funny faces, aren't you charmed? The combat is nothing to write home about, but ultimately it works.But then it all kind of hits you. Your plot goes from "We're gonna cook some magic food" to "The crazy cult is going to destroy the world as we know it and only you can stop them." I don't want to really spoil anything because it's 100% worth experiencing for yourself, but I will let you know that the art direction only continues to improve as time goes on. The writing stays great, the gameplay stays kind of mid, but the aesthetics and gravity of the situation get better and better.My only complaints are that the boss fights can be a little ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ down the line, very quickly going from pushovers to full on touhou levels of projectile spam. The fact that they get shields in order to do their special phase transition moves feels a bit cheap, but I can kind of see the need for it when you can otherwise totally mow them down. Summons especially are pretty overpowered. I was also annoyed at some minor bugs, where some weapons would just straight up not work or you would randomly lose the ability to use one of your arms or something, but overall you can work around those things. Lastly, the way the story is structured it did kind of feel like the game was ready to "end" three total times, which always kept me on edge and feeling like "Jeeze, how much more do I have left?". This is probably due to the game initially coming out in three unique chunks (which explains the continuing rise in quality), and on one hand it kind of kept me going because I always felt like I was getting close, but on the other it does feel like I was getting edged too hard.But those small complaints aside, I think I loved my time with dungeon munchies. The writing was always fun and engaging, and having three cute anime girls running around with me is always a big plus. As the devs mentioned in the final area, I am in fact looking forward to whatever they put out next. Thank you for this roller coaster of an experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't simply describe it as a bad game, there's actual effort in it and certainly serves some niche well.But if you're looking at the overwhelming positive rating and think to yourself that this might be worth playing, be careful about what you want from this game.The best thing you can get out of this game is the Story. The overarching story is interesting with some weird twists and eldritch horror involved (which only one of the screenshots slightly suggests). But the moment to moment jokes which makes up 90% of the game is a hit or miss.If you're considering playing this game, please for the love of god . And maybe you will find the story interesting enough to justify your playthrough.The gameplay just isn't great.The controls are super janky for a supposedly precision platformer, and that's a red flag. The level design is straight up bad and gets way worse further into the game, accompanied with janky controls leads to one of the worst gameplay experience I have in my whole life.Keep in mind, the platforming is not hard, just frustrating. You can easily tank through the environmental hazard even on higher difficulty, but that doesn't justify the bad level design.The general combat is serviceable but the design only comes down to attack until all enemies are dead and spam dodge button in the meantime to mitigate damage.Boss battle. Ugh.It started out OK. Not like super fun but as good as a typical side scrolling game could be.But then the devs slaps bullet hell onto bosses.The bullet hell pattern is just uninspiring and isn't really designed around the idea of "learn the pattern and avoid it." You can't, it is at no point designed to be avoidable and the janky control doesn't help at all.When bosses start spraying bullet hell they also become invulnerable which isn't explained at all. The super unreadable visuals, microscopic boss health bar and invulnerability countdown aren't helping either. It took me four hours into the game to figure out this is a thing.Most importantly the whole game is designed around M&K control scheme even though there's a switch release of this game. The final encounter is just a mess if you're using a controller, and the devs bad at explaining their game ain't helping at all.I would love to give this game a "meh, but recommend" if not for the boss design.The devs pour their soul into making this game and I can feel it, but I'd rather take a visual novel version of this game stripping out all the gameplay.So that's why the best I can do is warn other players to check it out using the lowest difficulty. Only with further lowered damage of lowest difficulty, can the level design and bosses become tolerable. And maybe, just maybe, the game will serve you better than it did to me.I hope the developers won't get burned out by this project and hopefully comeback someday to deliver that same bizarre story but with actual enjoyable gameplay in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is based on Early Access version 0.1.18.3. I mention this because the developers are working very hard on this game and only chapter 1 is in the game at this moment. Everything I say here is based on this version. I'm sure they will add more achievements as well since the current achievements are all for chapter 1.  This is an action platformer with a lot of darkish humor. I like the jokes a lot and the game looks amazing.  You are a zombie who just woke up because a necromancer summoned you. You are her new project to whom she wants to learn all the recipes she knows. Some of the required ingredients are hard to get and she will not get them for you, that is your job.  You'll fight your way through enemies to find those ingredients and you'll cook new recipes or make weapons with them. It sounds weird to make weapons from ingredients, but the claws of a crab are multi-functional!The most fun thing is that every recipe you make will go into your stomach and will give you a buff as long as you keep that recipe in your stomach.  You can switch during the game and can combine to a total of 8 active buffs. You will not have to make an old recipe twice because if you know how to make it you can just add it to your stomach.  Some examples for buffs are: more health, doing extra damage over time when using a melee weapon, produce every few seconds a poisonous cloud that will hurt enemies. I like this game a lot. I never thought it would be so much fun to hunt ingredients! The boss battles feel a lot harder than the normal monsters. I really needed a few tries with the first boss which has a big difficulty spike since you just left the training ground aka the tutorial. The second boss is also giving me a hard time and I haven't been able to beat it yet even though I've was very close two times.This game shows some promising stuff and I'm looking forward to future updates. This game has a variety of achievements. Think about achievements for beating the different bosses but also for making all the cooking and crafting recipes.  One of the hardest achievements will be to beat chapter 1 without dying. Chapter 1 seems to have 3 boss fights which will make that one a real challenge.  I'm a bit afraid that they will add achievements for not dying in the entire game and if that is the case I hope there will be some sort of chapter selection.  + Addictive gameplay+ Fun darkish humor+- Challenging boss fights

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I recommend it, mostly for the good story and characters. Nicely above average here. Definitely finished it feeling satisfied and happy with the characters and story, and would recommend it to many people. Compared to the last big budget game I just finished that started good but the ending left me feeling very unsatisfied... I liked this game much better, and it's story and characters will probably stick around with me a lot more strongly for a lot longer.That said, it's got it's ups and downs.Pros: Humor... it'll be hit and miss but there's a lot of humor here.Characters: Some nice characters that you'll probably like, or not... but at least find interesting and they do develop, not just being 2 dimensional.Story: It does do a few jumps as you go, so expect some surpises, a few parts you can start seeing coming, but not all of it. It's more interesting than you'll expect when you start, though it does take some time to really get good or interesting.Cons:- Gameplay is... only ok, but early on before you get more weapons and options it's not great, so a rather slow/tough start on the game. Push through it, gameplay gets ok to decent later, but the story is what you want to stick around for.- Bugs, more than a few of these. Frequent ones like the armor break debuff icon sticking around longer than it should, or just getting stuck on the screen, up to more serious ones like the final boss often just insta killing me with random attacks that at least normally don't do that and shouldn't have the damage required to do that. Honestly very annoying, final boss I died like 10 times, only two felt like they were my fault. I'd have 160 health, suddenly die not even sometimes seeing me take a hit/collide with anything... and my UI still says I got that much health/shield left.- Story, at the start. It does well once you get to know characters, go through changes in the story with them, and thus get invested in and actually like them. At the start, for that first hour or two plus it's... very simple, characters are just kinda... meh with forced comedy, and it's not that good of a start. Again, later on they develop, you learn why they are the way they are, and it gets better, but the start of the game... honestly felt disapointed and wondered if I'd bother keeping to play since early story, gameplay, characters, everything... felt pretty sub par like a cheap indie game made by relatively unskilled/capable devs. So ya, push past the start, was the weakest part of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished this game and feel like I owe it to the devs to take the time to write this out. I had an absolute blast with this game, start to finish.It has a surprisingly good story, one that takes on tones and themes I was not expecting given the humorous nature of the beginning. The game never loses that humor though, thankfully. It inserts it masterfully even in the most serious of moments. I laughed out loud a couple of times which is a great indicator. I came to genuinely care for pretty much every character that ends up in the main squad and was significantly invested in them by the end of the story. Lots of good commentary and pokes at humanity as a whole is sprinkled throughout as well.Really enjoyed the art of the game. Really detailed pixel art combined with the large variety of more fleshed out character art for the conversations made for a very nice atmosphere. Character design in general was top tier! So creative and expressive. Monster design was also crazy good and disturbing at times.Gameplay was super fun and more engaging than I was expecting. Tons and tons of build opportunities, and ample methods to get extremely strong. Progression felt great.I LOVED THE SOUNDTRACK. So much variety in the genres present in the soundtrack and it was such a blast to listen to. Bought em all to support the artist and devs.Thanks for this game. It was such a pleasure to play through, and I'll always be hoping for a sequel. I want to see the crew again!

_childDocuments_.review: Artwork----- [8.5/10]Story----------[9.5/10]Gameplay---[6.5/10]There is A LOT of miss able sprite work throughout the game that overall is added for just a bit of flavor or tone setting. Additionally, the developer took the time to make sure there are a lot of unique sprites and expressions for all characters.  Lastly the music has a solid +60 tracks for your enjoyment. This game is an incredibly funny romp that is interspersed with a lot of really funny quips and genuinely touching moments. The fact that this is translated and still keeps its snappiness is being no small wonder. Despite 90% of the dialogue being in support of the humor I was surprised to find I genuinely cared for almost every single character by the end. So, you are going to experience a bug or 3 in a full run of this game the most notable I experienced was a spawn death bug that I had to restart for. Additionally, there is a severe difficulty curve you are going to experience in the later half of chapter 2. Unless you are a pro gamer™ or are trying for the achievements I would recommend dropping the difficulty to easy. In order to beat the game on hard I had to run all but 1 of my food slots towards defense and still struggled quite a bit. This would normally be a big deal breaker but I was honestly just having such a good time with the story and secret collecting that I just made it work. If you are determined to persist on normal/hard into the late game highly recommend

_childDocuments_.review: Normally like to log more time to have more to say about this game, but the sale I got it on is only going on for like another 14 hours, and it's good enough I feel it deserves a plug while it's running.Game seems really really great so far. It's "core" graphics are low res to a degree I'm not even sure I'd call them charming (like don't expect Dead Cells or something) and I'm mildly concerned about the difficulty curve going forward, but... I can't really even think of any other complaints? Aside from a couple translation gaffs (and honestly, not many... it's pretty impressively well-translated considering I'm guessing the team aren't native English speakers... even the humor comes through well), the story is a mix of legitimately clever tongue in cheek humor with a surprisingly decent amount of characterization... like it's rather minimalist so far, but a lot of bang for your buck, as it were. Likewise while the "gameplay" graphics are a bit "meh", the animation is fairly fluid with solid hitboxes etc, and the cut scene portraits are very well done... Simmer's plethora of images in particular are very amusing and cute, plentiful and good quality in concept and execution. The music/sound is a bit utilitarian, but not bad at all.And that's about the closest I can think of to negative of neutral feedback a bit under an hour in... I've basically nothing but glowing praise for the rest. The game uses simple mechanics, but implements them in ways that they function with shocking elegance... in essence, the cooking system is less a "survival game" mechanic so much as the game has RPG elements that work off crafting... enemies drop items that you turn into gear that give you skills covering everything from active combat moves to passive buffs to traversal abilities. Water level getting you down? Equip a swim-speed up food. Getting knocked around a little in combat and not sure you need the double jump at the moment? Swap it out for a food giving extra HP. It puts a hard cap on "Grind to reduce difficulty", which I can't say I love as someone not super into high-intensity twitch reflex difficulty and such, but it's actually a cute, theme-appropriate means to add some complexity of "character build" in a novel way.Meanwhile, the combat at first seems like it could be a bit one-note, but expanding my repetorie into more gear, movement foods, and active move foods made me realize combat is actually quite versatile... You can really approach fights from a lot of playstyles and strategies, despite the fairly straightforward mechanics of "Primary, secondary, roll, jump/move" that creates the basic system. Dual handing swords with an uppercut manuver feels a lot different that rolling with a fast dagger that applies DoT in melee and a shield to do a "ping and turtle" strategy, or a heavy spear and a ranged weapon to stick, move, and harass at a distance. The hitboxes felt very clean, enemy attacks predictable and telegraphed enough to feel fair while complex enough to not be easy, and my own motion blended enough control and lack thereof to leave my mistakes feeling like my fault but also easy enough to make. I was really expecting something clunky and utilitarian ala Starbound for this game's combat, but it's honestly more crisp and well done than most dedicated action titles, from what I can see so far. All in all, cute game, fun writing, serviceable-to-good quality visuals and audio, simple but satisfying RPG mechanics, very well implemented action gameplay, this game is honestly pretty top notch as Metroidvania's go... I was a bit on the fence about it picking it up even on sale, but super glad I tried it, definitely reccomend even at full price.Adendum: Finished currently released content (chapter 1 of 4, as I understand it?).Gameplay continues to be top notch, only getting stronger if anything. Difficulty also grows, but not to unmanagleable levels so far.Meanwhile, story becomes less minimalist, which I'd say is indisputably a good thing (you can always hit Esc to skip if you're not into it, after all). Story is surprisingly heartfelt, raised some legitimate feels for me along with some interesting philosophical questions. A lot more novelty  and complexity to the plot/setting than I was anticipating as well, very interested to see where it goes moving onward... it's a real clash of divergent concepts that comes together to very interesting effect, taking everything from sci-fi to high fantasy to college slice-of-life to Lovecraftian cosmic horror, maybe even a little political thinkpiece... all while maintaining the excellent humor established from the start. While the graphical limitations persist, I'll also point out that it manages some pretty excellent ambience around the end of this first content installment... the final areas and the opponents there are so off-putting, it's a bit chilling.My initial review was already meant to convey a glowing opinion, if that wasn't clear... but if the notion the writing might be too sparse or silly to tell a real story was a turn-off, know it very much gets around to getting serious, given time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so close to excellence, but misses it on just too many points to recommend.Among the list of poor features are: level design, combat balance, boss design, polish, and worst of all, a third act that has less than a third of the content of the other two acts, but attempts to wrap up every thread as quickly as possible.Don't get me wrong, there are really good elements here; the art direction, music, and story (up to the third act) are fantastic.So first, the level design. None of the levels are exactly memorable and I found the parkour challenges both out of place and not very fun. For example, there are trains that pass by for a few seconds, allowing you to move forward before waiting for it to pass by again. Except there's not any reason why the trains are there (as they phase through the walls) or add anything of interest. There's some nice secrets, but it was never very interesting.What did pique my interest was the weapons and food "accessories" you could make and equip. There's a huge variety that makes collecting things fun, just because you have a new toy to try out, but continuing to experiment will find you with builds that are extremely broken, turning the game into a cakewalk on the highest difficulty. With so many choices there's bound to be some better than others, but it reaches the point that you can near one-shot bosses by the end if you have the right build. Then there's the boss fights. I enjoyed a few of them, but too many of them can be easily broken. For example, Clifford, can be forced to teleport to turn around, so if you dash through him, then dash back, you can practically stun lock him and trivialize the majority of the fight. Other than the fact that they're not exactly well designed, the bullet-hell phases that all bosses have don't  work. Movement is way too fast and the projectiles require precision, so you end up attempting to dodge bullets but end up never quite able to miss all of them. The biggest disappointment in the game, the final boss, is genuinely terrible; it flails around a lot while you have no weapons and compared to the rest of the bosses, is just boring to fight. It glitches the menus and other weird things like breaking the screen, but it left me more confused than excited.In general, this game has a lot of weird quirks. The crafting system doesn't seem to work some of the time (?) and in general attacks and hit-boxes feel a little off, but I can't say it's terribly by any means.What really let me down was the final chapter. For context, Chapter 1 consists of 49 recipes and 45 weapons. Chapter 2 has 42 recipes and 42 weapons. Chapter 3 however, has 11 recipes and 21 weapons. The story and content is just much lighter here when it needed to be the heaviest; the story leaves so many questions open by the end of Chapter 2 that get resolved extremely quickly with very little emotional payoff. Then it's all just happy, wrap a bow on it and game ends.I wish this game had been developed a bit more— I  to love this game, but its speedy conclusion stripped all emotional connection I had— which I definitely had by the start of Chapter 2— but there's too many flaws to recommend this game. Perhaps you'll be able to look past its flaws, as the vast majority has, but after finishing it and reflecting on it, I couldn't.

_childDocuments_.review: Seems alright.So you kill things, get resources off of them, and you use those resources to "cook" which is essentially a 1 time recipe you can change out any time that contains some sort of buff or new ability for your character. You have 7 food slots in your stomach, otherwise you're "full"... Yeah, it's one of those games where there is as many food related puns as possible.Anyways, you can mix and match abilities, areas that require a certain ability that you may have swapped out will grant you that ability anyways, for example... A platforming section that requires double jump, you'll get it on your character through story related means and not have to use a slot for it anymore.If you don't stay up on going  back and cooking up new weapons, you'll die a lot so basically any time you collect a few new materials you should fast travel back to the nearest section and check your recipe at the various stations.Like I said, seems alright. Platforming and combat, they did it just fine.Personally though, too many puns/ too heavy on the word play.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on a whim and wasn't prepared for how much I loved it.The gameplay was juuust right. The movement and combat were just the right level of engagement to keep you interested and entertained the whole way through with lots of build possibilities if you're feeling creative and some absolutely broken ones if you just wanna smash through everything.The crafting system also hits exactly the right level because it fully gives you the feeling of accomplishment for collecting the materials you need for each recipe but never makes it feel like you're grinding for drops.The main appeal for me was the stellar story and writing. It genuinely made me feel emotional at times. There were lots of very heartfelt conversations between characters that are so easy to love. The casual interactions between this group of friends just felt so comfortable and fun and the dramatic talks and arguments pulled super hard on the heartstrings. The comedy was also absolutely on point. The game is frankly absurd, but it never feels tired or overdone. The jokes keep changing up and it never runs out of things for you to chuckle about. Surrounding the laughs and the tears, the story starts out simple enough, as most stories do, but goes a lot of places I wouldn't have expected and kept me completely enthralled in learning more about this world and what might happen to it. There's also a fair share of commentary about a whole lot of subjects without ever feeling preachy or anything and I can respect that. Serious things happen, but overall chill vibes.I should also mention that this game has very cute art. The character art and the pixel art, it's all fantastic.I had a much better review earlier, but I accidentally refreshed and lost it, so I made this one a little quicker and rougher. The important thing for me to convey though is that this game is great and I absolutely would recommend it.

For example, the "intellect point" system, which functions sort-of like a currency for creating meals and weapons from the monsters and plants you kill. Never at any point did I have so few intellect points that I was gated from making either, making me question the point of the system at all.- Not a bad game overall but not worth the price tag ($14.00), especially in its unfinished state

_childDocuments_.review: According to the Michelin Guides, a rating of two stars is "Excellent cooking, worth a detour." That is exactly the score I would give Dungeon Munchies. It's absolutely worth checking out.At the time of being gifted this game, I was in something of a dilemma between buying this and Metal: Hellsinger, which was on sale at the time (I also highly recommend that game as well), and being gifted this game ultimately let me have both by buying the then-discounted Hellsinger myself. If I'd known even half of what was in store for me with Dungeon Munchies though, I wouldn't have hesitated to buy this instead, not for a second, and I fully intend to gift a copy back to the sender both so they can experience Dungeon Munchies as well and also to financially support the game. It isn't perfect - I'd give it a low 9/10 overall - but let's talk about the good for now and circle back to the bad later.There will be some trivial spoilers past this point, though. Nothing related to the plot will be directly spoiled (that isn't already obvious just by looking at the store page's screenshots), but the things I say may skew your expectations of what's to come vs how they would have been had you gone into the game completely blind, since I do bring up some of how I felt at various stages of the game.Dungeon Munchies is clearly a game with the somewhat cliché "most important ingredient of all": love. The graphics and soundtrack are respectively pleasant to look at and easy on the ears, but the boss health bars could stand to be a bit more visible. I didn't even realize bosses HAD health bars until fighting the Lord Protector near the end of Chapter 1. Setting that aside, the visuals in the game are overall easy to digest, and the dialogue portraits range from cute to hilarious. The soundtrack never feels intrusive at any point, but I also have trouble remembering most of the songs once I close the game. There's all sorts of tunes in it, though the ones that stick out to me the most are both in Chapter 2, since the vibe of both the songs and the areas they're meant for hit you out of nowhere.The gameplay has just the right ingredients for something simple yet distinct. Rather than getting more stats or something like that, a player's build is made up of seven foods with various effects (some of which DO increase stats, but most don't) and two weapons. This allows for some experimentation or mixing and matching, but around the middle of Chapter 2 it starts to feel pretty clear that not all builds are cooked equally. In my personal experience, it felt like axe builds were simply better than everything else because you could easily purée everything that looks at you funny without much trouble, up to and including the final boss of the entire game. I'm also going to talk about bosses real quick, since the game never explains what I'm about to say.At certain health thresholds, bosses will enter a bullet hell phase, very much akin to Touhou's spell cards for those familiar. During this time, the boss becomes nigh-invulnerable, taking maybe 10-15% of the damage they'd normally take, and a gray time bar appears underneath their health bar (it's directly under the boss, again, this should be more visible). Damaging the boss will reduce this time bar, but it seems that you also need to do some amount of damage during these "spell card" phases to get them to stop. There's a lot of little things like this that the game could stand to be more transparent about, but aside from some small hiccups - most notably the boss mechanic I just talked about - the gameplay is solid, but nothing to write home about.This might be a weird take, but I think this "it's a game that plays, but the gameplay itself is nothing incredible" works in the game's favor. Because it lets you focus more on the real meat & potatoes of Dungeon Munchies.The biggest selling point of Dungeon Munchies has to be its story. There's no shortage of indie action platformers, but where the stories of most that I've played feel like more of a side dish, the story of Dungeon Munchies is a three-course meal of comedy, tragedy, and things that make you feel unsteady. And I do mean that almost literally - rather than just inserting yet another culinary term into this review because haha food words in review for food game - since the game is divided into three chapters, with the tone of the game notably shifting from one chapter to the next. I do think Chapter 3 in particular needed a bit more time in the oven, since it tries to wrap things up with not enough time to actually do so, and just one or two more zones would have been massively beneficial to this rushed feeling. It makes sense that it feels rushed I suppose, for story reasons, but still. Otherwise, it's a story I fully intend to play through more than just once, with a nice, feels-good ending.That's all the good about this game. Nice graphics, an unintrusive soundtrack, solid gameplay that usually keeps itself fairly simple, and a story that threw me deeper into the pits of despair than any other game, only to pull me back out again. Now I'd like to take a moment to address the things that left a sour taste in my mouth.Having already talked about the bars & mechanics of boss health, I'd like to talk about two other things that left a bad impression. A few bugs in the UI that are mildly inconvenient but incredibly annoying, and the final boss. The UI has two persistent bugs that gave me no end of frustration. When opening the options menu, for some reason, a lot of the time the game's language will reset itself to Chinese. This is easily resolved by a single click to set it back to English - or a few additional clicks if you'd prefer a different language - but it was quite annoying to have to roll the dice on if I'd have to fix that or not every time I wanted to adjust something else. Additionally, the food menu can be a bit buggy. When you make a new food with an empty stomach slot, the animation and sounds for eating that food play, but you don't actually eat it, which can be confusing. Weapons auto-equip when you first make them, so why does food not behave at least somewhat similarly? Trying to upgrade a food from the bar of equipped food can cause the UI to instead display the info for other foods as well, namely one of the first two dishes in the game. You'll still upgrade the food you're trying to upgrade, but this can - like other interface bugs - be somewhat frustrating.And then there's the final boss, who you technically fight twice. The first fight isn't really a fight at all; you're supposed to run the hell away from it instead. This is despite in-game dialogue implying you have the option to fight, and despite the area immediately preceding this encounter - an area you're stuck in with no transport shrines, by the way - having food & weapons stations, making it feel like you're SUPPOSED to fight but are simply boned if you don't have any builds that can down the boss. Even my funny axe blender build didn't down the boss, so if it can be "killed" here I have no clue know how on earth you're supposed to do it. The second encounter, the REAL final boss battle... is horribly disappointing. The whole fight left me with an overwhelming feeling of "That's it?" It was an incredibly easy battle in my experience, despite the fact that it was difficult to impossible to make the most of the Tomato Soup that made my build a menace to virtually every other boss in Chapters 2 & 3.Despite these shortcomings, Dungeon Munchies is one of the best video games I've experienced lately, and I'd readily recommend it to anyone who enjoys platforming, cute anime waifus, funny humor, or unexpected waves of stomach-sinking despair and/or cosmic horror. At the end of the day, Dungeon Munchies has just the right ingredients for a fun game that grabs hold of you and just won't let go until you're finished. Delicious!

_childDocuments_.review: This game made me create a real steam review for the first time. ! Ghost anime waifu helps you learn how to cook endangered magical species and monsters beyond human comprehension. Surprisingly great and hilarious writing, but a falls a little flat with repetitive combat and stiff movement. Highly recommend this game if you want a great 12 hour story and seeing your weapons make big funny damage numbers.Anime ghost girls? Tons of weapons? And cooking? Whatever else could you need! Dungeon Munchies is a combat focused action platformer with a gimmick surrounding collecting materials from defeated enemies to create both weapons and foods. Foods in this game act as passive effects you can equip that will make certain weapon types stronger. Do you want to do shoryukens with a sword? Become a spinning machine of death by dual wielding axes? Or just not do anything and have a army of minions do your work? All of these builds are possible by experimenting what combinations of both foods and weapons you have at your arsenal. The fights in this game eventually become a mash fest of swinging your weapons around until the enemy and dashing towards the next area. I highly recommend playing this game with a  as aiming with a controller is much more difficult for most weapons.The best part about this game. The story of this game starts off slow and small but definitely ramps up after Chapter 1. The characters are very charming with some hilarious character portraits and witty dialogue. I can't say much without spoiling but the world building of this game is done wonderfully and had some very intense moments where I had no idea where the story would go. Everyone in the main cast of this game are very fun and I love them to death. I highly recommend beating at least Chapter 1 before deciding whether or you want to continue playing this game or not. When crafting with materials you got from defeating in enemies they . So don't feel like you have to grab an extra 6 shrimp claws when they're not used in craftingThe movement in this game is a bit stiff as you're either moving at  or . I personally had no issues with the movement of this game but I have heard other people find it too difficult to play because of it. Throughout the game you'll find hidden recipes that can help you create even more weapons and foods, you can access these hidden areas through platforming, air dashes, or wall climbing as the game progresses.Bosses in this game have . Usually during the final phases of mid phases during boss fights the boss will take only 1 damage from attacks and you must chip them down with lots of hits before they're defeated. Sometimes they're just straight up  and you must dodge through a horde of attacks and projectiles to finish the fight/get to the next phase.The developers of this game obviously put a lot of passion making this so I want more people to play and know about this game if possible.  I feel like this game could've became much more if given more development time and resources.

_childDocuments_.review: This is from the perspective of someone who played this game at full release. I didn't play this during early access.The best side scrolling dungeon crawler I've played in a very long time. The path you take is linear aside from some side paths with some hidden items to find. The hidden items are not very well hidden but I prefer it like that because having to use a guide or trawling back through a level is just wasting time not doing something fun.The combat system allows you to equip 7 passive abilities and 2 weapons allowing you the freedom to try many different builds. The only drawback is this is best played on mouse + keyboard, using a controller doesn't allow you to move and aim your weapons independently.The story and art is the best things about this game. The characters are charming and funny, while the art fully reflects the mood the writers were going for. The story starts out simple and evolves in to something grand and exciting.If you take all the parts of the game, combat mechanics, sound design, art etc and examined them individually you could easily pick out many games that have done it better, but combined together this game is much greater than the sum of its parts.

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeon Munchies is a very cute and fun Metroidvania with a great humor and story, that offers a very unique take on a post-apocalyptic Earth.You wake up as a zombie raised from the dead by Simmer, the Necrocook, to be her "assistant". Your job is to explore and go gather food from the monsters in the dungeon. Sure enough, the "soon to be food" will fight back and you will have to defeat them to get the materials needed for equipment and the dishes you can cook out of them.Those food items act as passive skills for your character and fill up your recipe book, which will be upgraded after beating bosses or finding the recipe in hidden and/or previously inaccessible areas. Completing it will grant you the possibility to customize your character how you want, when you want, since you can change your spec midway through in a few clicks.The combat is very different than any other metroidvania as you need to "target" with the cursor where your attacks land. It's a bit weird at first, but as you play you get more and more comfortable, as the controls are spot on. You will do what you input, which is useful for those "jumping puzzle" you get during the game. Dodging through attacks with the dash is really tight as well, you can do it at the very last moment and it will proc, which is very satisfying. I would recommend playing with mouse+keyboard as it's much more responsive this way in my opinion.It's a very artistic oriented game, both with the pixel art graphics and story the game provides. It's sometimes silly, but it's also the point of the game to not take everything too seriously and all the characters are lovable and cute. The gameplay and mecanics are unique enough from other metroidvania while keeping the essence the genre.I'm really impatient for the next chapter of the story, and I think the devs really deserve support. If you are looking for a fun, 6 to 8 hours long game for pretty cheap, I would definitely recommend you check this one out, as it's a good hidden gem.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is fun although a bit repetitive after a while, however what really sells the game is the story and character interactions. The story is a really interesting take on an apocalyptic future, that just takes you on a wild ride starting with talking veggies and then slowly along the path you find twists and dark turns that makes you question if you are indeed still playing the same seemingly cheery game you were a few hours ago. The characters feel so genuine and full of emotion, and it is a genuine pleasure to get to explore the depth of the characters as you progress. This game makes you laugh and cry pretty damn well.With that being said, while this is a roller coaster of emotion, the ride doesn't last very long currently. I finished what is out currently in about 5.6 hours (not 100% completion but caught up with the main story), so definitely will have to wait for the rest of the story. I'm excited to see what more is to come for this game!

_childDocuments_.review: It started as a cheerful, funny, colorful action game game. I was not expecting that. With it being set in a world of talking plants, chef-necromancers, and even waifu skynet, I didn't expect many of the things that happened in this exceptional game. I still loved it though.Every part of Dungeon Munchies is . It starts off cheerful, colorful, and simple, but both its story and mechanics quickly gain depth -- yet it never loses its unique humor, and it is always fun as hell to play. This game somehow stayed cheerful and colorful even as it reached Warhammer 40k levels of "Oh my god that's messed up and " which is  impressive.--I hadn't touched a platformer for years before I left my comfort zone  and bought this because of the good marketing and excellent reviews. I'm glad I made the exception for this game. The gameplay is utterly fantastic, with slick combat and incredibly deep build customization. Playing on the hardest difficulty, each boss fight is a battle of fine-tuning and combo-creating just as much as it is a test of reaction time. I cannot encapsulate the brilliance of this masterpiece's design with words (at least, I cannot do so concisely), so all I will do is implore you to find out for yourself.But this game's true strength is its story. It's story of struggling to survive and stay sane in a miserable, mad world (very timely, honestly). It's a heartwarming story of friendship. It's a tear-jerking tale of sacrifice. And it also has a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hilarious sideplot of revolution and a few other things which I won't hint at here. The banter between the two characters on the cover art is excellent, the world is interesting, the morality is nuanced... I simply can't get to it all. Nor should I. You can get to it all once you scroll up and click the "add to cart" button.Go do that or I'll make you into a meal and eat you for an attack speed buff.--Final note: this is unironically Game of the Year for me (though I haven't played Elden Ring yet).

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a bad game, but the difficulty spikes are absolutely ridiculous.Why are there enemies in the S.U.C. That can shoot me with a death ray from 2 screens away through multiple solid steel walls/platforms, taking most of my life with the first shot, and easily killing me before I get to them?  Why is there an enemy that can stun me, leaving me highly vulnerable to damage, and the only warning I get are two tiny yellow arrows over my yellow head?  Why are these tiny yellow arrows the exact same yellow as the enemies' highlight colors and energy attack colors?All combat in this game, including all of the bosses (except the first one), amounts to doing DPS spam faster than the enemy DPS spams you.  The only difference is all of the bosses (except the first one) I made it to also had a 30 second invincibility cycle that produces bullet hell in a game that lacks the controls (or actual bullet patterns) to make it reasonable to dodge them, and after you beat the boss you get one last bullet hell before your victory counts.What makes it frustrating is a lot of the game is kind of fun and I like the story/characters, but it feels like I am keeping my head down and dragging myself through the insane parts where apparently the tester only used one build to confirm it was doable.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll cut to the chase: This game is incredible and I absolutely endorse the opinion that it's worth your money, full price or otherwise.It's honestly even difficult to describe this game. The story is completely off the wall and yet strangely compelling, somehow meandering through sentient fruit-rebellions, the iron grip of government authoritarianism, and nihilism made manifest all while being both upbeat and sincere. I'd like to underscore that last bit, because in this day and age it seems like way too many authors try and hide behind glib irony and detached cliches, as if afraid to say that their work really believes in something. That's not the case here; all the characters are invested and committed to the story, and that's very refreshing to me.Visually the game is stunning, with a ton of enemy variety, excellent boss design, and progressively better level artwork. The pixel art here is superb, which is something I have always loved, and the game is just beautifully brought to life in that style. It's also quite good in my experience with regards to visual clarity, it was very unusual for me to lose track of my character or get hit by an unseen projectile. This is good because the late-game can get quite chaotic.As far as audio design goes, this one's also a winner. The ambient music is fantastic and really suits the strange calm of a doomed world, and ramps up appropriately as the plot intensifies. Not much else to say really, I didn't hear a single bad track and I didn't tire of the ambient music even in long levels.When it comes to game design, Dungeon Munchies gives the player a ton of options, with the ability to customize your perks via a wide variety of food choices, and your weapons with a wide plethora of options within a few set categories. There's lots of playstyle options whether you want to be more of ranged damage dealer, up close and personal, DoT effects, or even summon-centric builds. The criticisms I have of this game are almost nil. There could have been a little more cleverness in level layout, and maybe a few items/foods could use balance tweaks, but generally speaking this is an amazing game at a great price point. I'd absolutely recommend everyone give this one a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a wild ride, the story is completely wack and throws like, everything at you. _childDocuments_.review: I absolutely ADORE this game. I've rarely seen a game with so much heart, and that puts so much effort into its characters, backgrounds art, lore and general story. Seeing minor characters show up early, and then come back later in the game with some sort of character growth or transformation makes the world seem so real. Gameplay wise its a very competent action platforming RPG with a lot of customisation via the incredible amount of weapons and food items you set up for your build. Reasonable level of difficulty, with the occasional spike in both possible player power and difficulty. if you're ever having a tough time, revise your build! There are also 3 different difficulty settings to choose from if you want it easier or harder.There are a few minor bugs and typos you may experience in its current state (as of september 2022) but most of them are incredibly minor, like getting extra double jumps if you time them properly after a rising flame slash. I'd just recommend not revisiting major boss fights after chapter 1. Story triggers mid boss fight don't like to activate a second time, so things get wonky.Also Simmer and Grill are cute.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, it's pretty fun. The character's movement is jerky, almost like the characters are locked to a pixel grid but the camera isn't? Not sure what's going on with that, but I could definitely see that causing headaches. Also, there are some aspects of boss design that I would go as far as to call objective design errors. The Clifford boss taking reduced damage in his later phases doesn't add anything other than making his health bar completely useless. Just make the boss have more health and show it in his health bar. Bullet hell sections are more annoying than fun as well, as the movement system clearly isn't designed for that type of challenge so it just feels awkward, and it seems that dodge rolling through an enemy or boss only works if the roll ends with the player hitbox entirely past the enemy, which makes it feel inconsistent (almost feels like one pixel was the difference between taking 2 full hearts of damage or taking none). It's definitely a long way off from a finished game, but it's a fun concept and I'm excited to see what it becomes.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm very much right on the border of recommending this. It's an overall good game and worth the asking price. If it looks interesting to you, I'd recommend buying it.Unexcpectedly good writing and genuinely likeable characters are the main draw of the game. Especially the main heroines are all nuanced and have much more personality than you see in most games. The game has a lot of optional dialogue, and you'll likely want to read all of it. The localization is also top notch. Story and plot are simple and serviceable, but are made more interesting by great artwork that unambiguously demo the narrative as you play.Two major issues. It's a floaty platformer that lets you arbitrarily go anywhere on the screen, albeit imprecisely. The weapons in the game are all broken and litter the screen with effects, making it difficult to know exactly what's going on in combat. Sound effects are poor, and you don't get much feedback when both taking and dealing damage. Combat gets boring early, and this is a mid-length game for casual play,  Second major issue, some of the music is, alright? It's primarily a mix of chill-pop and post modern rock that very rarely aligns with the gameplay. The music seems to be a point of pride with the developer and switches on the dime with boss battles and narrative events, but it always felt out of place and distracting for the entire length of the game. The issues with gameplay and the audio is why this doesn't get a thumbs up from me, although I will play the developers next title. The writing and artwork are almost good enough to carry the entire game, but the average gameplay and mediocre sound makes the in between forgettable.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, this is a cute platformer with a decent collection element, and lots of little nooks and crannies to find secrets in.  Surface level, it's a fair fun game, if a bit on the easy side.  Especially if you get some particularly powerful combinations of upgrades going.  The story is interesting, if rather off the rails at times.  I was eager to see where it went with all its wild twists and turns.However, the end boss was a complete mess.  A bit too inspired by Undertale, the end boss not only completely glitched out on me at one point and failed to transition to the next phase, forcing me to restart, the fight itself is just insufferable as movement is incredibly difficult.  You have to jump between slowly falling platforms.  The problem is, they fall at roughly the same speed you do.  Meaning it's nearly impossible to actually land on them and then make progress up.  There's also various things that can get your character stuck on, and be unable to avoid when the boss does one of his massive damage attacks.As a note, I played with a controller, though the game seems more geared for mouse and keyboard.  Even an analog stick can only aim in 4 cardinal directions, making some weapons difficult to use effectively.It's not a perfect game by any means.  And the ending left a very bad taste in my mouth.  But most of the game was fun enough.  Not a classic, but something you could be happy wasting a few hours on.  My run of the full game was about 8 hours, and that was taking my time to explore everything.

I would hold down left and right click; the boss would die before it could kill me, so I really don't even know if bosses other than the final one actually had different attack patterns (will be checking later). Now this wouldn't be that much of an issue if I was just sitting and grinding for hours, but I only back-tracked twice (for redwood and a crab claw, both for shields coincidentally enough) which took total probably 5 minutes. While I'm not saying it should be ridiculously hard, I feel that it should take the player a few times to get through it. Honestly, while number buffing is usually not the way to go, maybe just a health buff to the bosses and slight buff to damage.Another, but much smaller, issue is a visual bug where when the mouse is placed too close or under to the playable character, their legs begin to freak out.TLDR; Great game. _childDocuments_.review: Some information to get out of the way, I played through the whole game after it exited early access on the hardest difficulty (executive chef) using a spear and shield combo for most of the game. Be aware that this likely affected my view on the gameplay to a degree.The game has some ups and downs. I'll start with the best and move towards the worst.In my opinion, the art's honestly the best part of the game. The characters that come up during dialogue look great, and the enemies and environments are well made. It's clear that the devs put some time into making everything look good. There wasn't any time I was annoyed or disappointed by the visualsWasn't bad, but I honestly wasn't a fan. I don't want to spoil anything so I'll keep it VERY simple. The game starts lighthearted without much direction and some funny jokes and banter. Eventually a serious plot springs up out of nowhere, but the game tries to keep the lighthearted feel at parts. It honestly feels like the devs didn't have any plans, realized they needed something, and rushed a main plot while haphazardly filling any hole they left. That said, my standards for story are usually pretty high, so if you like what you hear from other reviews then don't be afraid to buy the game for the story. The characters were well written, especially Simmer, Grill, and the skeleton crew. I could see them carrying the story for someone who thinks they'd enjoy it. Sadly wasn't enough for me though.Honestly the biggest reason I can't recommend the game. As mentioned above, I played on the hardest difficulty, so that without a doubt played a part in my experience. The best part of the game is the combos of food and weapons. It's fun to mix and match things and see what works. Not only that, but you have a good spread of different weapons and food that can give you completely different play styles.That's sadly where the positives end. The fights and areas between the bosses are pointless. They're not challenging or fun, even on the hardest difficulty. All the enemies in these areas can be killed nearly instantly, and I had no trouble tanking through literally every platforming part. Remember, this is on the HIGHEST DIFFICULTY. I honestly don't even know if I should complain though, because the movement can be sorta jank at times. You get a number of mobility abilities later in the game, like dashes, extra jumps, and the ability to climb walls. Sounds fun until you realize that the movement isn't very smooth. There were times I dashed and still got hit, or other times I tried to use my second or third jump, only to not have it work.The bosses can range from being insanely easy to annoyingly unfair. Every boss can have their health shredded immediately, only for them to go into an invulnerable bullet hell phase for some reason. Now, I like bullet hells, but you need good movement to make them work. Remember the movement problems I mentioned before? Now add in some unfair patterns that can't be dodged if the boss decides to stand in a bad spot. Suddenly you have a horribly obnoxious fight where you're replaying the same boss, waiting one to two minutes to get to the second bullet hell phase, only to die from something that isn't your fault and have to do it again a number of times. The game is best at the beginning, and as you progress the chapters it honestly gets worse. The final boss is a joke, but the bosses before it are way too difficult, mainly due to the annoying RNG bullet hell parts and clunky mobility I talked about.Just some minor pet peeves here. They don't matter enough to affect the gameplay or story, but still annoy me a little. Feel free to ignore them or read them. They honestly shouldn't change whether you'd buy the game or not.To start, the achievements are broken. I got and made all the recipes in the game. There's an achievement for that, and I got it. There's another achievement for making the FIRST meal you can make. I don't have this achievement. Why don't I have this achievement? I don't know. I made the first meal, I have the achievement for making all the food in the game, which only ~4% of people have. But I don't have the one for making the first meal, which is required to progress in the game. ~80% of people have it, but I don't. Not only that, I beat the third chapter on executive chef difficulty, but I didn't get the achievement for that. Sorta annoying not to get it after putting all that effort into it.Insight points. You get them from killing enemies and reading dialogue. They're used to make meals and weapons, as well as upgrading meals later on. They're pointless in the first half of the game, you always have too much. The dev clearly put them into the game as a currency for making things, realized they had no purpose, and tossed in upgrading to make them useful. Now, that doesn't bother me. What bothers me is that they still required insight points to craft things. It's annoying to spend all your points on upgrading a dish you already have, only for you to not be able to craft the new dishes/weapons you just got because they need 2k insight. Honestly not a huge problem, it just sucks to not have enough insight and skip a dish for the current area, only to have it immediately one-upped by another in the next.Minor typos in the text, especially in the last chapters. Nothing big or worth complaining about, but they are there.Game isn't bad, but I personally wasn't a massive fan. Be sure to read through some other positive and negative reviews, especially one that played a lower difficulty, to see if you'd enjoy it. If you think you'd like the story you might want to consider buying, but DO NOT buy it just for the gameplay. There's tons of similar games with better gameplay, and if you won't like the story you'll probably dislike the game like me.I'd recommend buying the game when it's on sale, preferably for less than $9.99. I don't think the game is worth $20, but I'd be fine with what I got out of it if I paid less than ten bucks.

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeon Munchies is quite an experience. You don't play this game for the gameplay, you play this game entirely for the story, the characters, and the worldbuilding. The worldbuilding in particular is top notch, including things such as: the emergence of a fascist, eugenicist state as the first-choice governmental option by sentient vegetables; a well-paced mystery of human societal collapse which becomes more comprehensive in each subsequent chapter (there are 3 chapters); the consequences of a society where food is outlawed for being a gateway to magic and happiness; deep characters who have deep, consistent, and deeply human narratives and grapple with existential questions. If I had to come down on something, it is that the gameplay is... clunky. It is a simple side scroller with light platforming and questionable balance. The "normal" SS Gestapo Pumpkin enemy was a significantly bigger pain in the ass (killed me a fair number of times) when compared to the final boss (who I killed without even realizing it?). Hitboxes are generous, if you're an enemy vegetable. There were many times where I would take a mouthful of damage from some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that was undodgeable or poorly telegraphed or definitely not touching me. Movement is pretty smooth, but the dashing mechanic can be frustrating at times (love accidentally activating sticky keys in the middle of a boss fight). Fortunately, the game makes up for this for making some weapons and their associated recipes absolutely useless. Why would anyone ever pick the melee weapons? You have to get inside the hit ranges of enemies that can 1 shot you to do baseline negligible damage. If you want to get swiss cheesed, build sword. Best weapons are the magic staffs that fire on each click, meaning if you click super fast you can stack ALL your DPS in a single second or two, charge up for another 2 seconds and repeat. Combine these with a secondary weapon that auto-shoots when the right mouse button is pressed and you can basically 1 shot any set of enemies that you come across. This is great, because it meant I could worry less about the jank combat and move on more quickly to the rest of the story.A couple other minor points of observation: 1) I came into this with minor expectations foisted from "Dave the Diver." I expected something where I could kill the enemies, take their ingredients, and then actually make food to power myself up. I had limited expectations in being able to throw ingredient together and create bizzaro combos that would be unique. Instead, you just collect the ingredients as simple enemy drops and then just click in a menu to activate different powerups. Was a little disappointing considering how much the  of cooking was rendered central in the story. 2) The ending was comparatively underwhelming and felt rushed when compared to the rest of the story.  That said, I really think the story and worldbuilding is top-notch. Consider this a relatively interactive (and demanding, and jank) anime. It is some of the most creative writing and explicit worldbuilding I've had the pleasure of experiencing through video games, and is quite unique. I think $20 is a little on the high side, but I appreciate the small (if not solo) developer team behind this project, and consider the writing just worth it enough (although I do wish it were less jank). I hope they can improve the core gameplay loop for what is a clearly set up sequel, and can maintain the quality of writing and worldbuilding. I'd love less jank platforming, less ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hitboxes, better balanced weapon + food combos, more interactive engagement with cooking. But I can tell I'm buying the sequel regardless just to close out the story.

_childDocuments_.review: Bro i haven't even finished this damn game and i want to tell everyone about it. The characters are amazing and scratch my itch for cute but serious girls that slowly unravel their inner selves as the game progresses. Combat is very fun and the build diversity is insane, every time i get some new fancy upgrade to a build, i think it can't be topped with the insanity, and 30 minutes later a new fat upgrade is added to my repertoire! I highly suggest you go in as blind as possible and definitely expect the unexpected. It might not be as cutesy and fun-filled as you'd think... Will update this review after i finish the game, but a singular play session was so damn fun i had to write a review about it!Edit 2 Days later: Just finished the game on Executive Chef Mode and 100%ed it, and had an absolute blast. I highly highly recommend the game to anyone with a smidge of interest in it. However it isn't without flaws.Noticeable flaws: - Sound design in some areas either wasn't working or just glitched out. Was playing a summoner-like build so honestly might've been part of it. Some areas had amazing soundtrack to it, but others were lacking or just...silent? Some areas have silence on purpose but others also had it randomly. Coming back to those areas and the sound was restored.- Final Boss is kinda chaotic in a bad way. It was all over the place and things weren't really well telegraphed. It was a pretty meh fight, although i enjoyed most of the visuals. Definitely not the highlight fight of the game.- Story is really hastened in the final chapter. The final chapter has such a massive about of loose ends to tie up, that it rushes through hastily and drops bombs onto you back to back without much time to comprehend it. I partially understand how the story went, but i had to go back and really think and re-read some parts to piece other parts together. The story overall though was FANTASTIC and had my interest piqued the whole playtime.- Builds are Diverse but some really just overpower others. My Summoner build revolved around me sitting still to purposefully take damage to spawn orbs that i could detonate for over 4000k damage each time. Also spawned one per enemy killed, so it was just massive chain reactions of devastation. I tried out NG+ for a bit with a new build, but couldn't really find anything nearly as overpowered. Closest i got was the 1 HP build with the Lower HP=More Damage item, but some attacks go through shields so it was a bit pointless.-Bugs that need squashing. There are a bunch of bugs still in the game that haven't been fixed. The most notorious being a bug where when highlighting over the language button, it changes it all to Chinese until you change it back. There are a lot of small bugs i encountered whilest playing. A few to mention are the training dummy bugging out and being unattackable at certain times, Some enemies making their noises even after they were dead (very noticable in the final few levels) and once or twice NPCs being uninteractable until restarted.Listing these bugs since i figured i'd make a point that the game isn't perfect. I love this game and all the characters it's created. I hope to see a sequel or more from the devs as the gameplay was fun and the humor was great too. Thanks for taking the time to read my review :]

_childDocuments_.review: Gonna be honest, having completed the game, the Overwhelming Positive score is pretty surprising. The game isn't terrible but gosh is it not great. I'd been waiting years for this game to come out of Early Access and I guess I should have paid more attention to its development because it feels like the team radically changed their minds about what the game would be after Chapter 1 (of 3).The combat feels like it belongs in a Flash game. You just sort spam wildly at enemies until they aren't there anymore. The game begins incredibly easy, and at around the 1/3 mark decides to start throwing much higher hp enemies en masse, and cranks up the projectile spam. It's not easy to read, it's not particularly interesting to fight. Then you get to the boss fights, whose healthbars are genuinely blatant lies, as they unleash big ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mass AOE bullethell attacks while sitting at 0 hp.The writing has sparks of humor but there's a lot of unsatisfying crunch to get through it. The cutscenes play somewhat like a light novel, but without any dialogue options so you're just sort of around for the ride while these characters have existential crises in front of you. As you near the end of it you're somewhat beat over the head with information that was pretty easy to infer, and some dialogue goes on for much too long.Combined with this is the unsatisfying pacing. The game doesn't take long to shed its veneer of quirky dungeon-cooker and throws itself into eldritch horror that is, and I can say this from very personal experience, just SCP fanfiction. Suddenly you're fighting waves of flesh monsters and there's no real point to it, because the materials they drop is near worthless and the XP you gain from combat doesn't have that much value.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a review for Chapter 1 of this game ( it's in Early Access, so this isn't the full game yet ) So far, this is very good stuff. The pixel work is nice, the characters are nicely designed for the cut-in dialogue.The main premise is : you are a zombie, and you need to eat cooked food. The reason is, having these cooked foods in your belly gives you powers, attacks, moves, stuff like a double jump, an upward shoryuken style attack, and then there's the crafting which uses enemy parts to create a main weapon ( melee usually, although I found a bow later on ) You also hold a secondary weapon, these can be anything from a shield to another dagger, or short sword, maybe a wand to cast a magic attack, or something to throw poison spores on enemies, there's a lot so far. This is  a linear game, metroid-ish but you don't really backtrack for anything. There are secret areas, though.You can only hold so many " cooked meals " in your stomach at a time, and some foods give you skills needed to advance ( such as the double jump, which later on becomes a permanent upgrade ) The meta is arranging them in a way to get what skills you need, and what stuff you want; like maybe an attack boost or effect or something to raise your dps. controls with a gamepad are quesitonable, but not impossible. The game is setup like a dual stick side scroller would be, except this doesn't use the R stick for anything, so the secondary weapon ( which is aimed with by your L-stick ) is mapped to the same stick you move your character with.I think D-pad for moving left and right ( or L- analogue stick ) and using the R stick to aim the secondary weapon would be a much better solution.Using mouse and keyboard works exactly as you would think it would. Mouse aims the secondary weapon and main attack and it's smooth as butter.promising early access entry, price is worth it as this is Chapter 1 of a much-larger game.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Great art design, enemies, environments. very creative.- Challenging bosses with bullet hell sections (similar to Rabi Ribi)- Lots of weapons and perks available, all sorts of builds and approaches.- Fun platforming sections, great variety in the environment, secrets and such.Cons:- Endless boring unskippable story sequences.- Story overall is pretty standard and uninteresting and takes up at least 50% of play time.- Combat and movement overall feels very janky/floaty and unpolished.- Unbalanced difficulty (most sections are too easy, then suddenly certain enemies/bosses are nearly impossible).Not recommended at this point, though it's borderline. I really liked the game, but some of the flaws were a bit too painful. It's still early access, the dev will likely improve the game, and also I can imagine that a lot of people will still love this game. If I was enjoying the story/visual novel sequences then I probably wouldn't be so critical.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a very interesting concept executed poorly. The level design isn't the greatest and just feels very rushed. The boss fights are the biggest flaw in this game. I never felt like I was using any real strategy. Every boss fight is the same, extremely easy then the boss enters a bullet spam mode which is extremely annoying. I felt as if I was dodging half the bullets that were supposed to hit me, or you get hit by waves of bullets that are basically impossible to dodge. Meanwhile the boss is completely invulnerable. So while you basically defeat the boss you're forced to go through a really annoying bullet spam mode, which is stressful when you have next to no hp. Why not just give the boss another stage where he powers up and actually let us fight him instead of running away and hoping you manage to dodge the massive wave of bullets. Also, the way you climb walls is just really annoying. You climb walls without wanting to most of the time and it really makes the game feel clunky. Makes it really difficult to play the game at a fast pace. The end of the game, the gameplay itself, makes absolutely no sense either. Just feels like the developer was trying to add a little more content to make the game longer. The combat is okay but not good enough to make this game worth it. The boss fights are just too awkward.
