_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't terribly impressed for the first hour or so of this game; it seems to focus primarily on meme centric, cheesy dialogue initially. This slowly evolves through chapter one, ending with a dark turn and instilling in you the impression that you're no longer playing a silly, lighthearted game. You're not left entirely in the dark thankfully, as the slapstick, off the wall humor persists throughout the whole experience, offsetting the dark tone of an inevitable disaster slowly approaching.Customization is king here, and much appreciated. Builds are easy to plan and a sound strategy for whomping enemies and bosses comes fairly naturally. I sort of just stumbled into a scythe build with soul explosions, coupled with a dps secondary and it worked like a charm. Every recipe and ingredient has a clever bit of lore with it along with well made sprites. Combat is not terribly challenging, as long as you have a proper build to champion your way. Bosses don't feel unduly difficult and are each unique, bringing new mechanics to each fight.I cannot emphasize enough the depth of the story experience here; while the game starts off silly, it quickly progresses and sinks you deep into a world filled with strife, sadness, and peril. Dialogue interactions can become very heartfelt quickly, cutting through any lighthearted tone set just minutes before. Characters are unique and interesting, each with their own piece of the overall puzzle to add, making for convincing interactions. There's just an absolute grab bag of references, philosophy, and rationale to mull over when viewing some of these scenes. While the absurd character designs can be a bit distracting, pulling you out of the moment and asking such questions as "why the hell am I listening to a living pineapple ponder the meaning of it's place in society and have an existential meltdown while being slowly crushed under the tyrannical rule of a living ice cream cone?" I've found those moments only serve to enhance the charm of the game.If you like DEEP story combined with fast paced, satisfying combat, platforming, and build customization, it's the perfect game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot of inconsistencies to this game. Most of the time I enjoy my time playing this game, however I think it's still important to highlight the parts that I think can make or break the enjoyment of playing this game.First, the story. It started with plenty of jokes and light-hearted moments, but then the story gets too serious it ruins the pacing and immersion. Right now I'm 2/3 done with Chapter 2, and I don't know if the plot will get better once I finish it. Second, the movement. This game isn't advertised for platforming, so I expect the game not to be too punishing if I get the jumps wrong. However, the movement is pretty janky; I expect to be able to double jump after hugging a wall, but the game sometimes only let me do one jump. Because of this I took damage in places where I shouldn't, and it's really annoying.Third, the difficulty. I'm playing on normal difficulty but I feel like it's too easy. In first chapter I died a few times because of the builds aren't that great, however once you transition to mid-game, the builds decimate enemies in seconds you barely take damage. Boss fights can be trivialized too, I barely get to see the boss does normal attacks as I shred their HP too quickly, I only had to react to their bullet-hell moments where they are immune to any damage until they are done with it.Maybe grab the game during a sale, because $20 doesn't seem to be worth it considering the game isn't that long and with the problems mentioned above.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a blast and a half to play! I haven't had this much fun in awhile, I highly recommend this, especially for the 20$ price tag (or even better if it's on sale).The gameplay is fun, chaotic, fast paced at times, and the difficulty progresses at a reasonable pace so you don't feel like you're hitting random difficulty spikes that ruin your momentum. You start off as a lowly zombie, slowly making your way through the games story and world while collecting different items and weapons to make yourself more powerful. You also walk and move around on this 2D plane but as you progress you gain tons of freedom for movement throughout the game, which is something I liked a ton! You go from walking around to basically flying everywhere across the screen.The weapon and item varieties are very fun and allow plenty of different play styles, whether you like ranged or melee or even magical weapons. I found myself mostly playing with the spears, guns, and magic the most because of all the fun passives that work with them from the items you can craft. The passives you can get from items modify your gameplay a lot as well, whether giving yourself new attacks with weapons, more mobility, more damage/effects, and other useful passives.The characters are also very well done, with everyone you run into having their own distinguishable personality even if they're a random side character. The humor with NPCs and Item/Weapon descriptions throughout the game is also top notch, I was stuck laughing a good bit at many different times, just to screenshot something someone said and show a friend because it was that good. My personal favorite being Captain DUI, a real american hero. It never feels over the top or too forced as well, the story in the game has a good mix of its being silly and being more serious moments too. I usually am a dialogue skipper but I found myself not doing that for this game, and actually going along with the characters and reading what they had to say, and it was definitely worth it. I'm even going back and trying to earn all the achievements because I enjoyed it that much.

_childDocuments_.review: My video review if you prefer that:What an amazing game. Having a blast so far. Although the mechanics feels a bit clunky at times, controller in inventory is buggy and some of the bosses could have been better. I also it feels that the balancing isn't quite there yet, it starts super easy (invincible if you choose the easiest difficulty, at least until before the last chapters), and gets much more difficult in the last part of the game with overwhelming bullet-hell boss fights.That being said, it is challenging until you discover some very powerful builds that make things much easier. The game felt a bit more liker Returnal 2D, at least when it came to boss fights. Things I like the most are the weapon variation and crafting to unlock new passive skills. This  leads to a variety of different playstyle and powerful synergies that can be a tons of fun to play and experiment with.Levels look unique and interesting platforming is well design, well-written story alongside great music. There are so many things the game does right and it all compiled into a fantastic side-scrolling/platforming gameplay experience. Overall, highly recommended, and I hope the few annoying things with the controller and the UI would be fixed in the next update. Get the game, it's well worth your time and money spent and there is lots of content as well. I recommend playing on the regular difficulty at first as the easiest one is not really a challenge. Have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: So some thoughts now that this is done.Overall:- Highly interesting build design. Not only is there a lot of ways you could viably play, but often times weapons that you would typically forget about from earlier in the game have the potential to become build enabling hyper-competitive weapons again upon unlocking a new ability. Most notably, you can hotswap your builds at any time so when you get stonewalled by something you experiment to get past it.- Charming world.This is one of those games where I found myself trying to find *all* dialogue I could, simply because it was enjoyable.- Rough early game.The first chapter has very little audio, and less polished fights then the rest of the game. The first two hours give a highly negative impression compared to the rest of the game.- Rough audio balancing.Sometimes enemy audio can be too quiet or too loud by impressive amounts, key story moments do have decent audio usually though. There may be some bugs here, since some weapons I used in the beta had sounds but were silent in my current playthrough.- Interesting boss mechanics.Bosses have spell cards where for a time they do dramatically more interesting and character appropriate new attack patterns while upping their damage resistance, even if your build has massively overblown damage bosses can still take advantage of yourprobably lacking survivability to stay challenging. Sometimes you need to adapt your build to address the difficult of these.Mind you, they are never damage immune and hitting them still helps. Overall, it keeps the game fun when minmaxing is done, and is far better then any other implementation I have seen of this. No straight immunity phases that you have to fight through.- Solid story.Its a little rough, but this story actually has a point, is well connected/planned, has good velocity, and keeps total control over its tone at all times even if the developers regularly shock you with how rapidly the tone shifts._______________________To the developers.If you ever plan on patching this game more, I highly recommend polishing the first two bossfights to be closer to the standards of the later bosses. This isn't that I want them to be more intense, but rather I would like it if their animations and sounds actually matched what they were doing better since the lack of audio for these fights is borderline jarring compared to later. One common bug with the first one is that they face the wrong way when doing attacks directed at you.Something similar could be said to all the audio-less act one weapons and enemies. The later parts of the game are impressive, but the beginning being this raw compared to the rest is likely going to result in a lot of new people being confused as to why anyone likes this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: After having finished the final chapter just now I can definitively say that this was a great experience all the way through.The characters are cute, unique and interesting.The story is interesting all throughout an develops nicely with multiple twists and turns and no matter how serious it gets the devs always found a way to throw in a pun or two.The visuals are stunning, one of the best pixel art I've seen in a long time, the backgrounds are the icing on the cake. The characters are well drawn and designed with fitting and funny expressions.The combat can feel a bit whacky at times but overall fits the feel of the game nicely and doesn't get in the way of trying to beat anything. Plus with the update that introduces the final chapter, they have improved the way the character moves and feels which helps greatly when exploring and fighting enemies.The difficulty feels nicely balanced, based on which overall level you decide to play, nothing seems too far out of reach at any given point. The boss fights are well designed, very unique from one another and offer enough of a challenge not to be overly aggrovating or acting as a complete hard-lock nor are they too easy to just steam-roll through (mainly due to their timed-sections).The grinding for materials to craft and cook each individual weapon and recipe feels just enough to be neither annoying nor tedious, yet still satisfactory.The level designs are interesting and bring several new mechanics, enemies and secrets to the table with each new area. It makes for a damn good feel when trying to find every recipe and resource there is.The soundtrack adds a nice touch to each area and boss fight, it's an amalgamation of several different music genres that combine into one... "experience" let's call it.All-in-all Dungeons Munchies is money well spent in my opinion.It is a rather short game, even when farming for every unlockable but offers enough content to not feel like a rip-off. Plus, if anything, the experience is what counts and I personally enjoyed my time with the game.I can wholeheartedly recommend this game, even to people who may not be a fan of manga or anime as, aside from the character designs, it has little to do with anything "anime-y".

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeon Munchies is a very entertaining game. At first it looks like a resource gathering and survival game, but the resources are not used up when you craft things, so you never really need much of them. The focus is instead on the crazy and interesting storyline and finding cool combinations of buffs and weapons that "break" the fighting mechanics. The first and second chapter are very well written and executed. The third and final chapter is a little unsatisfying in comparison. Overall a very good game. The Lickspittle theme was my favorite.

The design of making different designs of combat through the way certain foods synergize with what weapons you use was a masterful design choice. Truly love this game.

_childDocuments_.review: A fairly fun metroidvania with slightly clunky controls and a quality story.Dungeon Munchies doesn't do anything life changing, but I enjoyed myself quite a bit.  Would I start a religion around it?  No.  But I will praise it for being consistently enjoyable and interesting, albeit a tad jank.The english translation has a few minor spelling errors (like using the word "confide" instead of "confine") but functions just fine.The story delves in some interesting directions, being both optimistic and pessimistic.  Humanity is cruel and unkind, and the world will probably just trample over you without care, but there's still hope.  There's always some hope.If you want a pretty fun game then I'd recommend this.  Its worth 20 dollars for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: A very solid game, well worth the price tag, especially on sale. This game will probably take between 5-7 hours to complete. Maybe like 8-10 hours if you wanna collect all the secrets and make all the foods and weapons. (there are currently 2 chapters, at the time of this review)tldr: would recommend 8/10. Has great potential.story:The lore is suprisingly deep and the story is actually quite good. I went in expecting a cutetsy anime girl cooking game, but its much more of a hack and slash platformer with an actually fairly dark story. The games writing is also very good, its entertaining and I read every line, didnt skip a single one. This game actually made me do some deep thinking, which is not what I expected going in.Art:the hand drawn art is definitely much better than the pixel art. the pixel art isnt bad but it isnt like exceptional either. The animations are kinda strange and once you start having many foods equipped at once, you start looking like an absolute abomination, kinda like the binding of isaac. I wish the background characters had some sort of idle animation or something, they just stand absolutely still and its not very immersive.Gameplay:Its basically like a hack and slash platformer where you equip different weapons and foods with different effects. I found making synergies between different foods and weapons very fun.Difficulty:The games not that hard if you spec out a build with good synergies its relatively easy, you can kinda faceroll most of the enemies if you build for it. there were a couple hard bosses that took me a few tries but thats it. I died like 20 times throughout the course of both chapters. The combat in this game isnt very hard. It is pretty satisfying though.Music:The music in chapter 1 isnt that great, I barely noticed it, but the music in chapter 2 slaps, I liked it.Bugs.Due to this being an early access game and a game translated to english from chinese, theres some strange working and translation errors it seems. The translation in the story seems professionally done and is overall very good, but the item and food effect description translations seem a bit weird. I couldnt really tell what they exactly did by reading them and had to go test them out. Also there are some bugs, like theres this item that says you take 10% increased damage but you actually take 100% increased damage. pretty big difference. Just from the description the item is op, but in reality its really bad. So theres just a few small things like this, I didnt encounter anything game breaking though.The only thing I really wish they did differently was explain who tf the character you played was. Throughout the whole game I had no idea who the character I played was, I was mainly just watched the other characters develop and killing ♥♥♥♥ for them. You play a zombie so you have no personality, you also have no idea who you are except for like one 5 line flashback.

_childDocuments_.review: Well i just played for 4 hours straight in my first sitting if that says anything. _childDocuments_.review: Excellent little gem! This game is surprisingly good quality in every area. The graphics are adorable and fun! Its story is charming and shifts between being lighthearted and tragic. The gameplay involves killing enemies for ingredients and inspiration which you use to cook buffs that fill slots and craft primary and secondary weapons. There are several synergies and they all have cosmetic effects which make your character look like they're a crazy cosplayer. While the soundtrack is not near the calibre of Christopher Larkin or Jeremy Soule, it has some fairly catchy jingles that are consistent with the tone of the story.My singular critique is that many of the weapons and food buffs are poorly balanced. There are too few defensive buffs (inc regen) and some weapons (swords) get much more love than others (hooks, spears and magic); the former enjoying MANY more buffing foods and interesting combos than the latter.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: Bosses are difficult but they're not too difficult, you can usually find a pattern or a blind spot pretty easily. Now I'm saying that it's hard because I went through the 2nd chapter only using the foods from the first chapter so I don't know if it should be easier than it already is. Explosion staff + Chili gun = big dpsGameplay-wise, it's fun, me being the casual player with next to no iq points to put in the complicated combos. I got carried thorugh the game with a shield-spear combo. After that, I used the rgp+chili gun combo. They send you the new enemies by themselves most of the time and they're tanky enough for them to exhibit all their attacks, if there's a large quantity of one enemy you've never seen before, then you can expect them to be the cannon fodder of the bunch. There may be major jumps in difficulty in certain areas though. Art is also a major highlight.
_childDocuments_.name: Dungeon Munchies

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game. At the current price it's a bit steep given the relatively short length. You can blaze through what I guess counts as the first chapter in 3 hours. But I feel I got my money's worth. It's a nice enough story, plenty of humour, decent controls and sound with okay music. Main gameplay loop is pretty nice. I like the combat though it feels like it could be... snappier somehow. Localisation is solid with a high quality translation which I was a bit worried about initially, unjustly as it turns out. I spotted maybe three typos in the script throughout but the language and humour are excellent. Makes me wonder if the original script is in English even, so no worries there. And the art, it almost goes without saying, is amazing.Devs appear to be a three man team who are providing reasonable updates and while there have been some delays it seems a big update is coming soon. So happy to have purchased this and recommend others do as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeon Munchies is a fun little platformer with a lot of customization for weapons and skills, despite being a shorter game. As a zombie, you are created by Simmer, a grand Necromancer spirit, with the intent that you will follow in her footsteps as a chef and learn all of her magical monster recipes. Using these recipes, you can gain stat boosts, buffs, weapon abilities, and the beloved double jump. As of now, the game doesn't really have a set ending but the "Final Boss" fight was really impressive and the overall story followed through really strongly.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing title, had me hooked right off the bat.  The characters are lovable and funny, the story is compelling while still providing good laughs, and the ending cliffhanger will have you begging for more (as of 5/2020).The combat is comparable to a more developed version of Starbound, including dodges and high customizability.  I found that for a majority of the game damage over time was the best build for me.  You gain new abilities and increase stats with each meal you eat, but you're limited to how much you can fit in your stomach, so if you wanna trade, you need to cough something back up.  (You can regain the previous dish's effects without reconsuming the ingredients).  Mobility is satisfying, and it never got to a frustrating point thanks to the ease of control.  This game has been an absolute blast and I look forward to seeing more from it.

_childDocuments_.review: Played a single run through. I don't enjoy these kinds of games, so I didn't get 100% (no deaths run), but got all the other achievements.Loved the story, reminded me of Undertale with its shift in tone. I also really enjoyed the art and characterisation of the main characters and the slow reveal of their backstory. Felt organic, akin to Hollow Knight.Gameplay is organically taught, which is the best kind of learning. Think similar to original Mega-Man games where the level was the storyteller, teacher and content. It was really impressive in that regard.Cooking and Weapon upgrades felt... okay? Gimmicky, yet essential. There is definitely a meta way to play. Devs are working on it supposedly. A little slow to respond to inputs some times and some mechanics are hard to understand.Overal, I was extremely impressed with this game, if only for the story. I'll be waiting for the full release to see how the narrative plays out.

_childDocuments_.review: Where to start. hmmm, how about the hour per dollar principle. Generally speaking, I don't play video games unless they offer at least an hour's worth of playtime per dollar spent. This game I only played for about 3.5 hours, yet I'm reccommending it for full price. Why?It's good. Real good.Not that kind of good that you play through without getting engaged. It's the kind of game with virtually zero flaws. The game isn't punishing, yet it could offer so much challenge with how smooth the combat system is. It's very solid, as it avoids putting barriers between the player and the actual combat. Normally games like this game playing very difficult by injecting combos and complex inputs. This game defies that convention, making complex movements easy and simple. It also adds several playstyles that are all viable and engaging. Surprisingly enough, the combat isn't the best part.It's the writing.The game does an excellent job of slowly building up the characters over time. I felt genuine emotion several times, and I also sympathized with the characters. When something awful happened, This surprised me as the story starts off as very goofy. At the same time, it isn't lacking in depth. They explore an utterly abusrd premise, and the developer does so with an unflinching resolve. This creates an execution that's elevating; it makes the story shine brighter than it should.So despite only getting 3.5 hours out of the game, I still would reccomend it as it was a breath of fresh air. These are the kinds of games I remember, and I cannot wait to see how the developer decides to finish the story. Excellent work on your parts. Really well done.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game in early access. This game is a rollercoaster of emotion, and overall an interesting take on cooking! I love the art, the character, and combat. The game goes into three basic categories, all of which have their ups and downs; Movement, Combat, CookingMovement: Throughout the game, your ability to move will become faster, and versatile. Sometimes it's a little sensitive, but most of the time it's fair to the player. Combat: Combat is a little iffy with what enemies do more/less damage, while also being odd in what weapons do more/less for the player. Some weapons are direct upgrades, other weapons have niche's that the devs probably wanted to try out. If you've played bullet-hell type games, you should have an easier time avoiding numerous enemies. Otherwise, be prepared to dodge and attack frequently.Cooking: Cooking is a mechanic shown in the first video for this game and it shows off what cooking does only a little. By killing monsters you get resources, and with those resources, you can cook various dishes with them. Each dish grants you some kind of ability or buff. These dishes are vital to not only overall movement but combat as well. Conclusion: This game is still in early access, so treat it like such a thing. Games in early access are still in development, so supporting them by buying the game is always appreciated, for ANY game. The game might have a small amount of playtime or replay value right now, but as the game finishes development, that should increase. Optimization will also increase. I don't know if anyone else has noticed, but these are clearly foreign developers that not only have to help code the game but translate it and put the updates out for us, the players. This game has already met my expectations as being a funny take on cooking, involving necromancy and fighting. The emotion from characters chat is in most cases hilarious, while at other times being dead serious. Be prepared for a lot of emotions, and hopefully a joyful necromantic experience. P.S. Simmer Best Girl

_childDocuments_.review: Let me just start off by saying this is an unfinished game, and this is an unfinished review. When the game is finished, I will give my full review. This review is subject to change.Now, with that out of the way, I think it's best to begin at, well, the beginning of the game. When you first load up the game, you are presented with the menu. It's a pretty bare bones minimum menu, but it gets the job done while looking nice. Go ahead and jump right into the game. First things first~The movement:There is nothing special about the movement. I think the movement system can definitely be improved upon. It is as generic as jump, walk left, walk right, along with a roll to dodge. That’s it. There is absolutely no momentum to be found. The second you stop pressing any buttons, you are stopped dead in your tracks. It feels very lacking and just all around isn't fun. This is a hack and slash platformer, it needs good movement, but it just doesn't have that.The combat:The combat really isn't bad at all, aside from the movement aspect, the weapons you get throughout the game feel rewarding. One of the only problems I have with the combat, is that it gets way too easy late game, specifically during and after  This game is based around synergies. Basically you have weapons and you have upgrades that work together to from a great combo. Upgrades in this game are very interesting, and it is a take on upgrades I have never seen before. They aren't even really upgrades, in the sense that you can pick and choose exactly what upgrades you want when and where. You aren't locked into your choice the second you make the decision to go with say, a health upgrade. You can always swap out for a damage upgrade later on if you want. Which brings me into~The crafting:This really is an interesting category, because usually when you think crafting, you think “ugh grind for materials.” But there is little to no grind in this game at all. Most of the crafting recipes (and yes, I really mean actual recipes) only require the materials you would get going through one specified area one time, to craft either one weapon, or cook one dish. If you make something, and decide you don't like it and want to try something else, then is when you would need to go back to the area again. This means, the only real grinding you would do in this game would be for the achievement for crafting and cooking everything.The upgrade mechanic:One of the main selling points of this game is being able to unlock new upgrades by eating food that you have cooked from materials gathered through killing unsuspecting plant (monsters?) and sometimes bugs and fish. The catch here is that you only have 7 slots available in your zombie stomach. With there being 49 foods, it starts to become more interesting the more you play. You are presented with pretty early on in the game, the dilemma of being able to change what upgrades you have at any point. Something interesting here is that there are mobility upgrades, such as faster speed, or double jumping. In any other normal platformer these would be with you throughout the entire game. However, in Dungeon Munchies, you have to option of say, replacing your double jump with a damage, or defense upgrade. One problem I have with this system, isn't necessarily with the system itself, but a side mechanic called “surgeries” which  This mechanic is fine, but personally I don't like the specific surgery  It would have made the game more enjoyable to me personally if that surgery never existed, because I would actually have to think about my next move and what upgrades to tack on along with it to be efficient enough. Which leads me into the difficulty~The difficulty:This category I find the most disappointing. The game feels way too easy. What is the target audience of this game? Obviously it is meant for more mature audiences, what with the  But I think, for the target audience, the difficulty is very lacking. It is a very easy game to blast through, but it presents itself as something that should be tough, and have you dying at LEAST 100 times throughout your journey through the dungeon, however, in my playthrough, I only died 10 times The sound design:This isn't anything special, the music generally matches the mood of the locations you are in, but during the boss fights, all the momentum of the situation quickly fades away. Personally I feel there needs to be more action in the music when there is something intense going on. None of the music is very memorable, but it adds flavor.The story:The story is very interesting. I won't add any spoiler tags here because I am not going to talk much about it, and if you already played the game, then there is no real need to see a recap of what you just played. If you want to go in totally blind, I recommend skipping this part, but nothing major will be mentioned in this part. The story focuses around two old friends turned nemesis who have different viewpoints about the situation happening in the dungeon. Both sides have their own fair arguments, which is what makes the story so compelling to me. There is a dispute going on, and neither side is right or wrong, just different. I won't get too much into this, but if you are looking for an interesting story, and don't care too much about the (negligibly) bad movement, this is probably a good investment.There you have it. This is my review for what is out of the game at the moment, and I will be changing it based on future updates. For what is given in this early access game, the game is actually pretty polished, it is just missing a few key details.TL;DR: The movement and the sound design needs to be worked on, along with the surgery mechanic needing to be tweaked.

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to just state, that I clearly havent put a lot of time into this at all. Because i literally got as far as picking up your bag in the tutorial area and from what I see, the PS4 touch pad does NOT work to bring up the bag. A Small complaint really since you dont really ever use your bag per say. And id also like to point out that aiming and moving, is tied to your left analog stick. Basically like the old school metroid prime on GC as an example. It basically makes it impossible to use any aimed range attacks like the seeds you pick up cause you have to aim and move at the same time. The aiming itself is kind of wonky as well. Not very fluid.  If i remember right the keyboard doesnt have these issues. But Either way, these are just a few things ive noticed so far and not even 10 mins into the game. That said, I know this is Early access so im not trying to bash the game. Just giving feedback as far as the ps4 controls go. maybe look into it when you got some time and come up with a better controller layout. Or at least allow button mapping in the future.Now on to my review. I played this straight for roughly 5 hours and got to the end. I will say I really enjoyed the humor and artwork in this game. I feel like 13$ was a pretty good price for the amount of content. The game plays really well for keyboard and mouse, compared to ps4 controller at least (Idk about xbox controller). Its an Early access title but truthfully it played really well overall. I didnt have any kind of game breaking bugs, or glitches to speak of. I really just played through it all in one sitting and i thoroughly enjoyed it. I would recommend this game if youre looking for a breathe of fresh air as far as an rpg goes(along with the unique humor and setting). I dont know if this would be classified as a rouge like, as it seems to have its own qwerky dark story. But theres really no penalty for dying, its like the devs took what makes a rouge like/lite good, the abilities, the gameplay, variety,  and blended it with a unique story and artwork.. Its a very dark kind of humor overall as well, but i enjoyed it. I say this is worth 13$, but i do hope to see more content coming out in the future. Lastly, i will mention i actually liked the soundtrack in the game. I felt like it really set the tone for the areas you were in. Especially when the game got a little bit more serious. Overall, as i said earlier, i think this is worth 13$. Its a fairly short game though, so if youre expecting a long game, as of now, or a truly challenging one (im not the greatest gamer and i managed to beat it in 5 hours so...), this probably isnt for you. Just yet at least. cause who knows where the devs will take it in the future. I do see promise in this game and Ill be following this to see where it goes.

_childDocuments_.review:
Hunt down monsters to cook and eat them!

You’ve been revived in a massive underground complex and you must leave this bizarre facility. Aided by the undead Necro-Chef Simmer, you must stay safe, get fed, find a way to get out.

Dungeon Munchies is a side-scrolling action RPG with a focus on hunting down creatures, cooking them, and eating dishes to gain certain abilities. The combination of dishes you choose to eat will impact your entire play style.

Big Menu for a Big Stomach
With a stomach that can only take seven dishes, you must put together a meal that maximises your abilities. Guava juice, grilled shrimp, or crab stirfry may mean the difference between health recovery, damage output or a watery shield.

Tools of the Trade
Craft all kinds of deadly weapons out of the animal and plant parts you can't eat. Pair them with your favorite dishes to create the most overpowered combat combo.

Farm-fresh & Locally-sourced
In this day and age, ingredients are hard to come by. You should be prepared to face off electrical snails, razor-sharp shrimp claws, and laser wasps to get the delicious parts you need.

Something Doesn’t Feel Right...
From the self-professed-AAA-license-holding necro-chef, to the diabolical voodoo “Lord of the Forest”, to the radical revolutionaries of the fruit revolution, everyone wants you to do their thing, but no one's really right in the head. What’s really happening down in this dungeon?

name: Per Aspera
detailed_description: Reviews About the Game The surface of Mars is littered with Humanity’s failed attempts to colonize its surface. This time will be different - this time there is no room for human error. Per Aspera is a planetary simulation game that combines hard science fiction and base building and takes the experience planet-wide. Step into the role of AMI, an Artificial Consciousness with the prime directive of terraforming Mars for human colonization. FEATURES: Balance a complex well of resources to build interconnected structures that span the entire planet. Customize your planet with branching research trees that allow players to tailor their terraforming plan — Develop new technologies, steeped in real-world science, to create a thriving interplanetary civilization. Uncover the mystery of a threatening presence on Mars and defend your colonies from unknown and combative forces. Immerse yourself in a rich, compelling narrative or take your time and craft the perfect Martian landscape with Sandbox Mode. Includes the immersive voice acting talents of Troy Baker, Phil LaMarr, Laila Berzins, Yong Yea, Lynsey Murrell, and Nneka Okoye. Terraform Together with Friends (up to 4 players). Sandbox Mode Only. Using scientific theories proposed by real space agencies and geographical data directly from NASA, Per Aspera presents life-like conditions and challenges steeped in theoretical science. Per Aspera contains a rich narrative that presents players with difficult decisions with planet-wide consequences. See the world through the eyes of an infant AI as it traverses a complicated ocean of self-discovery and shapes the fate of the human race. Navigate your ever-evolving programming to adapt to morally challenging concepts and forge relationships with the human colonists that look to you for their continued survival. The choices you make will impact how your mission ultimately concludes. Keep your wits about you as this is not the first time humans have tried to tame the Red Planet. Expose long-forgotten relics of Humanity’s failed attempts, learn from their past mistakes, and uncover a looming menace that threatens to see you fail at any cost.

_childDocuments_.review: I had fun with this game and would recommend if you are looking for a fun terraforming simulator.  The story line was good and the play was straight forward.  I found the combat frustrating but the opponent was not tactical so it was fine and fit with the story.  The charts and graphs with so much seemingly useless information, unlabeled, no trending information, were also lacking but you got the point I guess.  Definitely sad to reach the end and not get to use your new terraformed planet as a base for further colonization/ exploration, but that's probably for the next game or DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: Summary - While I understand the mixed reviews - and I read most of them, I find this game solid.   Many reviews talk about the UI being clunky - yes, and I would add lacking in some areas but its still quite polished.  The "value" is arguable at its current price and "development," but also consider I have played 50+ hrs in less than a week - this is MY kind of game.  So over all - THUMBS UP!   I do not regret the purchase of Per Aspera.Detail - there are some very unique aspects in this game.   In over 200 games in my library, this one is completely unique in so many ways - and most of my titles come back to this general genre. There is a story line and plot that allows choices instead of strictly linear, so its not a 1 play.  And its not predictable.   The full game design is intriguing.This is a very grindy game.  If you don't like grind, then probably not your game.  This is not a game to sit down and finish in one day.  Also, not a game that you can walk away from: stuff happens, key choices that can affect the game later.I don't show this game is still in development some but some key pieces are missing - like a basic tutorial. The plot provides a bit of a walk through, but there are key points in the game that you are left to just figure it out.  An additional challenge by design?  Possibly.  The in-game knowledge base is somewhat helpful, but I found it lacking.  Mouse over labels would be helpful since the UI is very full.  If you prefer detailed instructions, then this also may not be something you will enjoy.  After the time invested, I am still figuring out the UI.Make no mistake - the game IS completely playable.  If you do any kind of simulation/base building/colony sci fi sim, then you won't be disappointed in this title.  The graphics are eye catching - the developers spent time on detail. The game presents layers and while you could argue some things were missed or could use improvement, there is a lot of complexity to mechanics and game play.I see there is much room for future development, which is definitely a positive.  Arguably, I could see an ongoing series that takes players through the solar system and beyond, tracking future space exploration.  There is a lot of unused material here and hopefully they will run with that.

_childDocuments_.review: Find a different terraforming game. Early game is interesting but is lacking. Mid game makes you want to restart because you didn't build everything 100% correctly and removing buildings is the most annoying thing in the game. Late game is just watching your screen for 5 hours as the nitrogen pressure goes up. Dont build near the south pole as it will blind you whenever its winter, and dont use 50% of the planet without paying them 6$. Dont upgrade roads in mass as you cant cancel road upgrades. Dont land a new lander in an area you already scanned. Yeah this game has some bad mechanics that make you feel like you can do whatever you want but you cant. Also the story-lines dialog gets extremely political and boring as all get out.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine Creeper World, but without the Creeper. This isn't exactly like that, but it's pretty close. The base-building is a bit more complex, and there are more resources to manage, and the tech tree is a more-important part of the game, but this is essentially Creeper World without the Creeper.Having said that: this is a really fun game. Lemme rephrase. This is a very interesting story, with a very playable, very solid computer game as its medium. If you take out the story, the game loses a significant amount of what makes it fun. Of course you can't take out the story, so the game is really fun.At its core, Per Aspera is a city-builder, and that's pretty much all she wrote. There's nothing surprising or innovative about the gameplay; it's just a solid city-builder. Collect resources, use resources to make stuff, use the stuff to make buildings, use the buildings to collect more resources. You Mine things to craft stuff, then you craft stuff to mine things.Honestly: if you don't care about the story, the game is pretty boring. I like the story, so I really enjoy the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I took a bit of time to think how I should write this review, after playing through the game. So if you want a detailed version read bellow. Tl;Dr 8/10 beautiful graphics and music, more for relaxing gameplay, if you are looking for a colony builder that’s semi idle this is the game otherwise I recommend looking for other games.Beware gameplay spoilers ahead!!!!Now the long story:The game has truly stunning views and music, the atmosphere of the situation can truly take you to any sci-fi fanatics’ heaven, sadly the game part does not deliver such a “punch”. The game is a casual style strategic resource manager with one problem almost 0 resources. They show you hot spots of recourses and the maximum amount you can find in them is around 10k of that recourse in cluster that contain from 500 – 2000 after that you are screwed if you can’t quickly establish a route to another hot spot, while recourses that you discover like uranium, can be so far away that you will never reach them, and you will never use it or the tech that requires it. Now the tech tree some parts are vital, like nitrogen import (since you can’t get it any other way), and some tech will never be touched (no reward for using it other than just having it) the army tech is one such example. The tech tree is limited would wish for such tech as deep drilling or something resembling it for infinite or near infinite recourse production in late game. Now about getting RP (research points) don’t go to ? for the recourse just build colony’s much more efficient, don’t need special placement, generate more than 10 times more, the only benefit of the ? is the lore you get. You would think what more can be wrong with the game, the combat OMG the combat, you get an opponent that comes out of nowhere(also disappears into nowhere) with an army so big that he can destroy you in a few minutes if you don’t throw your resources at that moment into defense,  which sits idle(using up energy and resources) for a long time till he reappears a long time later at which point your army is so big you just remove him from the face of mars in a second do to always living in fear before, since the appearance and disappearance of the enemy comes as a surprise with no warning. Now the tech tree of the army is one of the biggest in the game but used only just for 2 combats, which brings me to question why have an enemy in the first place. To sum up if you’re a casual gamer looking for a Zen game and never wanting to truly spend hours or days on paper planning to just be disappointed you found your game, if you’re a hardcore strategy game fanatic with tens of city builders and strategy games in library run away, you will be mad at this game, you will rage, you will want to delete it, just because you ran out of Iron or aluminum or any other resource and the closest instance of it is on the other side of the planet and there is no way you will reach it and even if you reach it and mistime when your enemy appears well kiss your hard work goodbye as it blows up to an enemy you could not expect or just break down from not enough repair drones which need the resource in the first place to be built. To finish this review, I am truly sad the game is what it is and not what I expected it to be a realistic mars transformation game. But I am willing to wait a year, a decade, to give the devs time to fix it, make it better if not, well it is going to be just another game in the shelf.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I enjoy this game. _childDocuments_.review: So do you like waiting? Do you like watching numbers tick? Then Per Aspera is the game for you! Now, that's not necessarily purely the fault of the game, being somewhat endemic to city-builders in general. You put down a building, you wait for it to finish. Either that requires time, your peasant to do the work, or in this case, a bunch of robots to gather stuff and pile it into one place to assemble the thing in question. Okay, fair enough.What is somewhat problematic is how *much* the game places an emphasis on the hurry-up-and-wait aspect of the genre. Every step in the process feels like it's elongated for its own sake. A single unit is a full load for a worker, so erecting your factories is dozens of trips. Each factory or resource generator requires someone to take it to storage or another building for it to be consumed. Each worker only takes a load so far before having to hand it off to someone. So you can have resources to build a planet of factories, but it'll take ages simply for the game to shuffle it slowwwlllyyy across your little base before it's built. Were it just that, then eh, maybe that's not so bad, other city-builders might be worse. But as other reviews have noted, there's a research tree and over-arching project to be done: terraforming Mars. Alright, that sounds exciting right? It would be, but much of this ends up being researching something, putting the game on fastforward for a half hour, then starting a project that puts your research into motion. These are for all intents and purposes like watching the progress bar of a large file download. At the latter stages you might have to maybe fine tune a few things, but this is allocating a few buildings to doing a few things repeatedly while you watch the numbers go up. Or down. Very slowly. To a certain extent that's understandable; you're terraforming Mars! It shouldn't even be possible, and it borders on magic. But that's not really compelling game play. You might have a plan on how to melt the polar ice caps. If you have your industrial base built properly, it's literally select a project and wait. Whee. It's probably fun to do the first time, but having beaten it, gotten one of the endings (which is likely a single choice you make 18 hours in), I feel like there's no rush to go back into it and see the rest of it. The story is interesting but the main plot points can fit on an index card and I only kinda felt invested in the outcomes, despite the voice acting doing a very good job of trying to sell the emotional aspect to me. If you're addicted to city builders and like a near-future sci-fi setting, give this a try. You can overlook a lot in that honeymoon period when you first fire up a game, and that might push you to the end through sheer momentum. But I honestly don't see myself returning to this any time soon, and I am a dork who likes it when number go up. Also, shame on Steam for not letting me put in a mixed rating, because not every choice is binary. I'm going to say "recommend" because if you're looking at this you're already in the mindset I imagine, but I'm not going to recommend this to a lot of people in general.

_childDocuments_.review: I adore this game. The story and voice acting is incredibly interesting and I love the way you are along for the ride as the ai develops consciousness. _childDocuments_.review: I would love to give this game an ambivalent review, since it's not really a bad game, but since Steam only asks whether I'd recommend the game or not, I'll say no.Early on the game feels like a fun logistics game, but as the game creeps forward, new options don't feel exciting anymore, and the sheer scale of up to 1550 buildings means that you aren't really encouraged to optimize, at least on standard difficulty. On higher difficulties I feel like optimization would be required, but it would also be tedious due to the sheer scale and the weirdness on how drone hubs work,  having only one drone each for some weird reason. I feel like the game might have had way more ideas than the developers had time to implement. The Blue Mars DLC adds in my opinion pretty pointless stuff, while the game desperately would've needed more variety in terraforming: Where are the animals that you can even research? Don't the humans need any real infrastructure ever?I think the concept of the game is brilliant, but the execution is mediocre. More depth in terraforming and perhaps a different system for logistics and it would've been great.

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this over the October weekend promotion on Steam after looking a bit into the description, and opting for the extra OST, Audio Drama, and Art Pack. The sale meant that I picked this all up for about $18 USD. It did not however include the Blue Mars DLC at the time.First playing the product I opted for a challenge, Astra Mode, since it came with a campaign mode and I wanted to be told a story of how exactly I was going to proceed along with terraforming Mars. My play method was cautious initially, so expansion was slow. I ended up getting wiped during a specific section of the story line, and wanted to restart. On the 2nd round, I aggressively expanded and made sure to correct my previous lack of defenses. This process on Astra Mode took three days of play; about 20 hours total divided between those days. Not my best decision.My first impression was this game rewards patience, and tends to encourage grinding away at special projects. This is not something I as a player like. One way I think Tlön Industries can correct that, is to allow special projects to be distributed across multiple spaceports. A player would spend more resources, but get more done more quickly. This I feel was especially important in the later half since I was stuck waiting for CO2 to convert to O2, and N2 to backfill. I never encountered issues with O2 running rampantly high in the atmosphere, and I'm not sure how a player could push that, since most atmosphere factories only contribute microbars over a few sols in the Martian month, and to alter that atmosphere would easily take decades of simulation time (hours of play time). On the other side, it was hard to push plant life since by the time I reached stage five, it seems that any attempt to alter the ocean levels was for naught; all my games so far I ended up underfilling the ocean by a 100m of stock or so.I think this game could use more work. I would agree with players that the Blue Mars DLC should have been part of the stock game, and I'm sure players would pay $30 USD for that plus what's in the game now. (Whether enough players pay to make it worth to Tlön Industries that I don't know, but that's also not the player's problem to make a game worth buying :-P)Here however I have a suggestion. Terraforming Mars is fun and all, but once this gimmick runs dry, what is there left for the player for replayability? Find out if you can burn the planet with pure O2 atmosphere? See if you can make a waterworld by stocking up as much ice as possible? Turn the planet into another Venus with runaway greenhouse? I haven't attempted these, but I'm not sure their possible either based on how the game is implemented using terraforming stages. I don't think it's that open, but those might be good marketing draws to keep the product valuable.Ultimately though, this brings up my suggestion. Once Mars is terraformed, what else can you do as a player. Is it possible to target other worlds? Venus? Jupiter's Eurpoa? Saturn's Titan? Those would be interesting challenges and something I would love to see in a DLC or expansion. Those are things I would pay for at the right price.Unfortunately though, the offical website for the game seems lackluster, and I think that's perhaps because the attention is upon leveraging Steam's connection to a large playerbase. The company website however indicates it's a very small development team, so based on that information, I don't think we'll see as players any major changes anytime soon. But that doesn't mean we may not see those changes at all.Overall, I'd recommend this game, but only when it's on sale for under $20. If Tlön Industries desires to focus on improving the game or expanding upon the lore they've built in the campaign story, I'm sure they could make it worth more to players.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: The more I played this game, the less fun it became.Per Aspera has a really cool foundation and pulled me in quickly. Unfortunately, all of its problems build up and up the longer you play and don't really become problematic until you're outside the refund window...I struggled with the user interface and it battled me more and more as my base grew. The number of menial and repetitive tasks you need to complete only grows as you play - there is no automation, no copy/paste, no building templates, no delegation of tasks to AI, no technology to research that lessens your cognitive burden. You're supposed to colonize an entire planet here, but none of the game mechanics work  you on this. There are no signs or labels or user-created districts to help organize your base or offer any aid in visual recognition. There are no hotkeys for building, and every single building you place needs to be situated within numerous zones of influence - you will have to toggle these, one-by-one (where's my filter?), and pre-position your cursor because some of the overlays don't even allow you to place buildings at all!I struggle to see which buildings or swarms I've selected. I struggle to respond to in-game alerts and notifications and locate their sources. When your buildings break down, you have to zoom in to see either the damage or the icon to spot it - and when your base is half a planet wide, you zoom in and out and in and out and in and out. When important events happen, the game fades to black, and then fades back in, with no prompt or notifications or voice effects or  to indicate what has just taken place. Voiced lines play out-of-order with regards to story revelations from minutes ago. To top things off, I had four crashes to the desktop, and one PC hard-lock in the ~8 hours I've played.It's a mess. This game doesn't feel playtested  What it feels like is a trap, and even having purchased this on sale I don't feel it was worth it, and I'd refund if I could.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDRIf you wanna zone out and play a building/terraforming game, this is for you.  It's relaxing, but can get monotonous.I played 3 runs.  1. I played the campaign for a bit.  Story is interesting.  AMI keeps talking so as keep you 'engaged' or 'immersed', but felt a little much after a while. The tutorial is good.  AI is fine and getting a decent set-up isn't too bad.  2, Reload and try again, campaign from scratch.  Blow throw all the stuff and get my colony to explore another part of the planet and think 'oh boy!', but am a bit disappointed because it's almost just like repeating the very beginning tutorial again.  3. I try one more time, this time in sandbox. The beginning is fun and getting everything set up, but each time there gets to this very critical point once all the set-up in the beginning is mostly 'running smoothly' that is just becomes boring.  I never even made it to flooding the planet just because waiting forever for the research was so tedious. There was hardly anything 'urgent' or even 'necessary to do.  It does run smoothly, just wish the gameplay loops had a bit more variety/tension to it.  Just feels like 'build a million mines and factories and oh some people are here now.'

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely amazing, it also gives you real pause for thought on some situations that may actually arise during a mission to terraform. _childDocuments_.review: There's some problems with the design of the game.Firstly, you basically just build things on resource nodes and then as long as everything's connected up stuff will kinda just work. There's no interesting logistical problems to solve, every problem you come across can basically just be solved by building more of the same thing. The only real upgrades to these factories/mines you can get are for more production and by a few hours in you've got enough of everything so these upgrades feel useless, you're basically waiting around for the right asteroids to be detected or for some meters to go up.The story is kinda forced upon you and sometimes feels a bit overbearing, I don't think it was really a needed addition to this game as you just kinda sit there and listen to a bunch of different people be unreasonable and deceitful to you. like I can see what they were going for because it's an interesting premise but by halfway through my play-through I was hoping to just terraform this planet in peacesome progression is kinda weird, there's a limit on buildings you can have which you can only increase by doing more research - which if you've left it too late can require more buildings to speed up, so you just kinda sit there on 16x and wait. New portions of the map are locked behind story progression which is really annoying. I kinda wish this game just gave you the planet and told you what the levels were supposed to be and just let you figure it out with interesting planet wide factorio-like logistics, but instead it's kind of just a railroad of checkboxes with an annoying story bolted to the top of it, which is a shame because the game is great in a lot of other respects - it's competently made, runs well, is scientifically accurate where it needs to be and its graphically pretty enough, like the effort is top notch it's just not that fun to play.

_childDocuments_.review: The combat and Musk references both put a damper on an otherwise really fun experience. I'll keep playing, but the whole battle UI is a real hassle to wrangle. *edit after more gameplay*The game is decent, but is missing to many ease of life features to be good. There is no way to cap manufactured resources which stops you from building any form of efficient system without running out of raw mats. The whole terraforming progression is also unsatisfying as there are no noticable consequences for any actions. Blowing up a bunch of nukes or crashing a moon into the planet should do more than just raise the temp a bit. The whole water system is also a bummer, there is no stats showing how much potential water there is on the planet. This means that you must either just wait with terraforming to build on flood areas or just ignore those places. The pathfinding of deconstructing buildings is really bad so building a base and then later deconstructing it to move away from water is tedious and frustrating. There are a bunch of things I could overlook if the core gameplay was more polished, but as of now the game has to many annoying moments to make me overlook that sort of stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: Aesthetically excellent, I love both the UI and the world rendering, the smooth transition between zoom levels, and the visual effect of the slow terraforming.Mechanically okay - doesn't stray very far from similar games, like Surviving Mars, though it has less hazards and may be too "hands-off", degenerating into a waiting game later on.I played it on release and it had game-breaking problems in the working drones in the mid-to-late game. The colony would fall apart due to drones getting stuck in incorrect tasks. I'm happy to say it has since been resolved, and I've played the campaign from start to finish without issue.Managing a single "colony" is fine, but when you get the option to add additional and isolated "landings", things kind of fall apart. The new colonies are very slow to get going (requiring the same loop and build order every time, and the resources produced/demanded become unclear for each specific colony). This should have really been solved with an additional mechanic to start a colony with more resources (even if it cost more to prepare them before deployment). Narratively ambitious - but ultimately unsuccessful, and this unfortunately kind of kills the game. The game tries to tell a good old science fiction story, in the classic sense, and I love it for it. If it succeeded, it could be a truly unique entry in the genre, a must-play.But the narrative isn't well implemented with the gameplay in several respects:- the pacing is completely off, with segments very dense with narrative, followed by long (hours) periods without any narrative; - parallel plot lines can get out of sync, so the same character is speaking to you very angrily in one moment, almost severing relations, and seconds later it is talking to you as if nothing had happened, kindly telling you something about a mission; - the game gives the illusion of choice (especially when it comes to combat, attacking a colony or not), but it completely ignores your actual actions. The dialogue asks you for an opinion, and at one point reprimands you for a past action, like attacking a colony. But right afterward, if you refuse to attack, the game doesn't acknowledge it at all; in fact, the colony you were supposed to attack vanishes completely once you reach a new terraforming stage, and the dialogue plays out as if you had attacked it. It's really badly implemented - and this may also have been one reason for the bad pacing; maybe the game was waiting for me to attack to advance the story. Needless to say, the opposing colony presented to real threat, as I had more than sufficient defenses, so it posed no threat, and thus no real imperative for me to attack.Ultimately, the problems are two fold: - pacing and sync issues (for example, at some point I reached stage 5 of terraforming, but the story was congratulating me on finishing stage 4);- treating the player as an agent with free will, but then not providing any actual mechanical choice, instead expecting a single choice and ignoring any other action.Soooo yeah. I'll still give it a positive because I kind of enjoyed my time with it, and I am interested in what they come up with next. I fully support its ambition, but am forced to recognize how it fails to realize it.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: First off, Per Aspera is an automation/building game which is abstracted to nodes and workers. At first it looks very basic, but I'd say it grows on you as you create large networks. The mechanics are relaxed, as far as I can tell there is very little chance to get to a fail state and most of the game will be a slow wait as you grow towards various objectives. The audio and visuals support the chill vibe, while the story themes are also largely contemplative and existentialist.Indeed, the catch is that this is a story driven builder game.  It's good news for underserved fans of hard sci-fi, as the narrative is relatively grounded, and explores terraforming with the aid of a possibly conscious AI. Not wholly groundbreaking per se, but it does hold a good amount of mystery and intrigue. I also thought that it was a nice touch that it starts from real life lore surrounding Mars exploration missions, and then expands them into a fictional future. My criticism here is that the voice acting can be uneven, ranging from good to melodramatic, and often feels too chatty to the point it overstays its welcome. Meanwhile, at times the dialogue/monologue can become a tad redundant when it circles round into existential AI territory. I found the story started strong and ended a bit shakily, and while it suffered from second half pacing issues, I'd say that overall it was enjoyable. About a 6-7 out of 10 as far as SF goes for me, and considering how rare decent hard SF is, I'd say that's not too bad.Overall I'll give it a thumbs up because it was a pretty different experience, though I'd caution you to only try it if you're armed with patience and prepared to be quite generous to a small game which is rough around the edges.

_childDocuments_.review: I am very glad I was able to play this game as part of the free weekend. The game itself is decent as a base/city/planet builder. I played my first (and only game) in realistic mode, and I eventually quit out of sheer boredom.The game is simple. Natural disasters like asteroids impacting the planet are the only opponents I found in the game. There is a whole military branch, and one "opponent base" which was effortlessly destroyed soon after I found it, and learned how to move my drones.Any base you build is doomed to eventually die of mineral starvation. Drones (worker, maintenance, military) cost non-refundable resources, and can not be recycled. They all naturally wear out over time - workers are automatically destroyed after a set time, maintenance drones are destroyed after they've repaired a certain amount of repair points, and military drones are destroyed if they get shot by an enemy. These are permanent losses of resources, and there is no way to get more resources.The planet has a certain amount of resources, and that's it. You build drones - which require a lot of different resources, and those resources can never be returned, nor required. This means every base you build will eventually die of mineral starvation. Your goal is to beat the scenario before you run out of your resources.This is a very slow game. I was playing the last several hours on 16x speed as I simply waited for the terraforming to be completed (Since I didn't want to spend my limited resources to speed things up - things like aerobraking asteroids, or importing green house gasses are a permanent loss in resources).For people wanting a few hints:1) Assault drones can be moved by clicking on the triangle above then which displays the number of drones you have. This isn't something you're told, and only reading other people's comments can teach you.2) When you find something that must be researched, the way you do it is put enough food and ice into the research station, then find a colony and turn it off. This is the only way to populate research stations. Be sure to turn the colony back on once the colonists reach the research station.3) Water treatment facilities, water packing plants, crater farms, and biodomes are the only way to survive once you start running out of resources needed to make food. These facilities create food and ice all by themselves. This'll help slow the eventually mineral death of your colony, but due to building drones - which is required - your base is still doomed to a slow death. If only you could retrieve your drones and recycle them... but you can't.In short, on realistic mode, I had no difficulties. There is absolutely no challenge to the game... This is just a waiting game, and a minor story is mixed in... but hours upon hours of waiting. It might be interesting to people who like to build bases, but since every base is doomed to mineral starvation, even they may hesitate to play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I don't understand all the negative reviews. I think a lot of players simply fail to understand what this game is.It's a solid colony builder with just the right amount of micromanagement. The tech-tree is not overly complicated but that's totally fine. The challenge is to maintain a steady flow of resources which forces constant expansion. So there is never a state of build-it-all or a perfect colony layout or something of that sort.The graphics and overall aesthetics are well made and suite the story quite well. It's an interesting combination of a lean, computerized, functional management interface with just a little bit cartoony flair when it comes to the humans. I think this suits the game and its mood very well and I kind of like it actually.But what makes this a true gem is the non-linear story mode. It's well paced and the story itself is actually quite intriguing. It gives you choices which actually matter and therefore this is one of the few games where I want to play the campaign multiple times just to see what happens if I had decided differently. That's rare and absolutely awesome in a colony builder.I guess the negative reviews are the result of the fact that this game diverts expectations of  many players as it is a unusual combination which gives it some depth but keeps game play very casual. I think that's quite rare and makes this game a true gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Suffers from the exact same problem as so many other sim games does nowadays. In the "goods old days" you could not simulate every single worker and transport individually, but now you can. That however means that the AI for transporting must be impeccable. Games like Factorio avoids this since the logistics IS the game, but in this game you cannot do the detail controls of it and it quickly would get out of hand. There are also a lot of other problems with the interface. The mini graphs for things are nice and all, but should be production and demand rather than amount in inventory. Also for the love of doG add construction requirements to demand so it is 3/month + 247 or something. Also would very much like to have a specific icon for empty resources, power off works, but that should also be removed from potential production, otherwise the potential need and production is good.When you use the map locator it would be handy to move the screen so the object is in the middle of VISIBLE screen, now it ends up right under the menu. Also nice to still see all information about it.Building roads is also hell and they are not listed in the production list or anything, so it is very hard to get any oversight, but it is so important for getting a working logistics sytem.But yeah, if it wasn't for the troublesome logistics system, like all other games like this, it could be really enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: This is a weird game to suggest because it has some really good and really bad elements.The good of it is that its a really nice game to play while doing something else on your other monitor.  The game is mostly about setting systems up and then waiting for them to process through a queue of some sort, so it doesn't require a huge amount of interaction to play this.  That's not a style of game that's for everyone, but I like it since I can "play" it while I work on something else.I wish it gave you a bit more information on how the systems worked, it needs a tier 4/5 logistics building, and the late game balance is a bit wonky.  But at its core it does the whole "set systems up, do something else for bit" genre well.  Also the game itself is beautiful and its really cool to see Mars get visually terraformed.Now for the bad: the plot, which is ironic because that's what the developer seemed to think was the high point of this game (and they tell you not to spoil it, whoops!).You play a hyper advanced AI that was given the personality of a not very intelligent high school girl with some *very* severe mental disorders.  None of this has any impact on the gameplay whatsoever, but you're forced to listen to the AI constantly talk to itself and a few other people.   These conversations are some of the most cringy stuff I've ever heard in a video game - particularly the conversations that you have with the "bad" guy - head of the western hemisphere's Air Force, Lt. Dominguez (yes, that's right, he's a lieutenant).  It really feels like the AI is a self insert for a writer with some severe mental health disorders where the conversations with the bad guy were taken straight from conversations they had upon being involuntarily committed, while the conversations with the "good" guys in the game are how they had wished those conversations had actually gone.I watched a few youtube lets plays on this before buying it and all of the LPer's stopped playing at the exact same part, which is when the conversations transcend from normal cringe to mega-cringe.  So I knew what I was getting into and I enjoyed the gameplay enough to still recommend the game.  But be aware that you're going to have to sit through hours of the AI whining about how it wants to be popular, find someone who understands it, have babies, AND HOW IT IS BEAUTIFUL AND PERFECT JUST THE WAY IT IS AND HAVING A "FRINGE CONSCIOUSNESS" SHOULD BE CELEBRATED, NOT TREATED.Although there also is a sandbox mode that is just the normal mode with the plot removed so you can also play that, but I don't know, it just feels wrong to play that mode when there is a campaign mode available - even if the campaign is just a strictly worse sandbox.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: A management with a good story Per Aspera will keep you engrossed for a very long time.  There is some replayability but it is limited to maybe two or three games.  Furthermore the game is a fair bit longer than its tech tree so expect to be max tech long before you complete the game.  I hope the devs add more content in the future but we'll have to wait and see!  At the time of writing on DLC (Green Mars) has been released and was a welcome addition to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Having played this and Surviving Mars to completion, I prefer Per Aspera. It gives a view of a grander scale, fitting for the task of moving mountains. The art direction and graphical style is just perfect for the setting. The story kept me guessing, accompanied by wonderful voice acting. The sci-fi felt much more grounded, and consequently, more impactful than Surviving Mars's story lines. The science of the game is lovingly rendered in wonderful detail, which gives your play through precisely the texture you'd want out of a game about change over time. New gameplay elements are introduced as you progress to keep you engaged and on your toes, right up until the mid to late game, where things start to slow to a grind. I finished the entire game over a weekend in one sitting, which I would call a pretty good review.I really enjoyed this game, so if I had one complaint for the developers, it would be the lack of fine grained control, which I feel would have been fitting, considering the AI protagonist. There were several times I felt that more precise tracking of efficiency, usage, supply and demand, and drone movement, would have been useful, or at least interesting. That being said, I finished the game without any cataclysmic consequences due to their absence, so perhaps it would have just been purely window dressing. If I had two complaints, the second would be the lack of fanfare for the release of animals. Perhaps I simply researched things in the wrong order, but from what I could tell, nothing changed when the atmosphere was made suitable for animal life. If I had a few more complaints: The characters should have aged. The combat was lacklustre. I wish we had more colonist characters to give the mission more weight. Why can't I predict or view the change in the water table into the future? It's important for planning, and surely a calculable value!
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. Lack some instructions for new construction gamer such as me. I didn't even know how to remove the build... And there is no notice to tell me that it will cost sometime to remove all the factory and the ruins. I love the storyline since player is an AI. I hope there would be more interesting plot in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Not as good as Surviving Mars, even with Surviving Mars problems, but this is meant to be a different type of Mars game.  A very lot of game time is spent just watching resources being transferred among nodes.  The entire campaign might be a nice long story (I did not finish it), and the planet size to build on is very large size. Considering Surviving Mars base game was given away for free sometime past and considering its sales plus sale-bundles, this game seems worth no more than 75% off ($7.50 US including Green Mars), and I think Blue Mars seems to be needed (for maybe $1.50 US more) considering some Mars in-game flooding that is supposed to come later.  Even then, you must like this style of game compared to Surviving Mars, which is more fun, to even consider buying this.  Hope this game gets better later, but I am not sure if the developers want to later make big change improvements to the game's current style. I was unable to create a multi-player lobby for co-op, I did not debug that much, and I am not sure if no-multiplayer was planned or not for the Steam Free Weekend.
