_childDocuments_.review: First of all something good about this game. The story is really interesting. Now for the annoying parts.It has some bugs which drags out the game time a lot.Some examples:When you grow large enough, you will encounter a supply-chain-bug. Turning buildings off and on again will fix this only some times. If the building that needs the supplies is under construction, you have to deconstruct and reconstruct it for it to work again. Cannot be done while paused, some game time have to pass.Hyperloops that can form a triangle will shuffle resources back and forward without any real destination.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I had a great time with this game when it first launched. The story was intriguing with an AI forced into deriving it's own moral code and decisions as the player which could alter the trajectory of that story. Not what I was expecting of a city builder/colony sim. The initial launch had a few rough edges, but it was not enough to keep me from playing avidly. And this studio did a great job of addressing issues in a timely manner. The organic growth that emerges as you aim your colony layout towards the resources that you seek is very compelling, and provided me personally with a continual "just 5 more minutes" mindset. The game also does a good job with events that force you to revise your strategies along the way and re-evaluate what you need to do next. The elements around enticing colonists to Mars and satisfying them well enough to stick around was straight forward enough, but needing them not for their labor but for their creativity was a great twist. A lot of the elements came together in a complementary way.I went back after a few updates and found additional enjoyment with the game and the latest updates are drawing me back in once again. The additional metrics and analytics that they added to the game really helped to clarify what was going on in your inevitable colony sprawl. I am looking forward to the ability to define districts and see how that "local" perspective helps you drive sustainable growth. A lot of good stuff in this game and it still has more room to grow.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: So I've done two playthroughs--one in the story campaign and one in sandbox--and overall, it's a decent game.  I adore the visuals, and I literally got emotional at seeing clouds and running water and oceans and green fields on Mars.  So let me give the strengths and weaknesses here.Strengths: Once you get past early game, it's very zen at times.  The music is very enjoyable--I've been considering getting the soundtrack and adding it to my general playlists, especially for writing and the like--and there's a good emotional core with AMI and her voice acting that I very much enjoyed in the story campaign.  Also, I really like the exploration feel and watching things develop.  The new water system update added a great deal of late-game content that was sorely needed and it made it possible to sustainably develop Mars for settlement that wasn't available in the initial release and made deciding what to do with craters more interesting--I had a bunch of crater farms in central locations and then adapted less-useful sites into animal sanctuaries and composting sites, but it made it all interesting.Weaknesses: The core gameplay loop is too front-loaded on early game.  The early logistical loops to get the basic worker units up and running is THE most complicated logistical setup, and you have to do it all in the initial setup; once you've got that going, everything else is much less complicated, meaning that mid-and-late game projects are basically a matter of "place a thing and wait for the workers to construct it" because once you hit a certain point, it's just a matter of waiting.  And there will be waiting.  Prepare to spend a lot of time on 16x speed waiting for processes to get going, and expect to start up subsidiary bases at various spots around the planet just to give yourself something to do.  Overall, I will recommend the game, but with the note that this is basically a low-pressure, slow-paced base-builder.  I felt very much like I was building a garden and watching things sprout and bloom, and while that was nice, you have to be both in the mood for it and temprementally suited for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I've been watching and waiting on Per Aspera for quite some time, and didn't want to buy it until it had received some much loved TLC from the Devs, however the game is everything I expected it to be in regards to colonising and terraforming Mars. Its also great to see the Devs pumping out patches and paying attention to their players in regards to QOL improvements and future implementations!Worth Buying!
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Its a bit rough around the edges and the late-end game is badly balanced. But overall its pretty relaxing and enjoyable.Resource system is very basic. Most advanced refining is carbon + iron = steel. So don´t expect this to be Factorio on Mars. You have almost no control over supply and transportation as this is done by automated bots. Basically it comes down to constant expansion by spamming mines, hubs and solar panels. Very little planning and thought required.Same goes for research, military and terraforming. Very basic systems.  The story line is not paced very well and long stretches of nothing is replaced by hectic contact between the different characters. End game is very badly balanced and turns into to a massive grind where you basically alt+tab for 15-30 mins, alt-tab back to press 1 button and then you have to repeat this 30 times. (This is where I put the game on hold waiting for a patch).Despite all this I found the game pretty relaxing and enjoyable. Devs seems active and I´m sure they will fix the issues given some time.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: While it's have a great concept, the game itself feels so empty. Forget about playing it on sandbox mode, this game will be so boring without humans and their dramas.The developer should add more game mechanics to this game, like human happiness. Humans who can afford food, oxygen, cloths, education, and entertainment are happier than those who don't. As an AI it is our job to keep them happy. If the player fail to do so, the population will plummet over time producing big penalty for productivity or even better... they rebelled causing mayhem here and there to keep player on their toes. We can also have several rival colonies from Earth arrive after you terraformed Mars, you must  annex them or make a peace with them, trade, etc, Endless possibilities....I recommend this game because of endless possibilities it has, great story and overall great concept for a game
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I got so invested in the story/terraforming project that I prefered to finish my run with Per Aspera than to check out the Cyberpunk, even though I've had it installed already.It's a really interesting game, I enjoyed the slightly more macro resource & expansion management than the usual colony builder gameplay. The storyline and voice acting were pretty darn cool too.As for the downsides - the end result of terraforming isn't as satisfying as I'd like it to be, which is something that you're working towards the whole game, so I'd love to see this game stage / planet look developed a bit more. But it's something that I was prepared for, as it'd be a tough task to fit that in with the rest of the game properly.The graphics are pretty nice, especially when you zoom out a little. The first few bits of terraforming progression also look pretty cool. Unfortunately the music gets repetitive really quick.TL;DR: i've had a blast with this game and was pleasantly surprised. Though if you're expecting a regular colony builder you might be disappointed.PS. Don't build level 2/3 factories and mines in your new outsposts, you won't manage to get the base self-sustained before everything breaks down.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: There are quite a few problems with this game.First, the campaign, makes absolutely no sense. They wanted to tell the story of an AI awakening, but it doesn't fit here. Astronauts get years of training, same with city planners, etc. An AI expected to do all of that would also get years of training - it would not be sent to Mars before being turned on for the first time. So yeah, completely unable to suspend disbelief there.I tried sandbox mode, but there just isn't much there. The game is just a scaffolding for their story in campaign mode; it's not enough by itself to be anything but boring.So no, I would not recommend this game to anyone, ever.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Played game during Free weekend. I purchased it after for discount.To gamers:Yea, I can recommend the game. starts slow, gets faster, then gets slower again. Go in expecting dialog trying to provoke thoughts on AI rights, and what it means to have thought. odd pacing on some things. It has Co-op but no idea how that plays, I played solo entire time. read below for more information, should be spoiler free to anyone who hasn't played the game and gotten to a point it would be understandable.To Devs: (it kind of bounces around some)I think the game plays too slowly, I went to x16 and rarely ever left that speed. Issuing commands for combat, and during select dialog options being the 1x times. Never had performance issues though, so that's nice. I personally think it'd be more thematically fitting to have 16x speed be base speed, and 1x become 1/16 speed thus when AMI says I can perceive time differently due to being a robot it makes it seem like a human life is a very short time as an ageless robot, and when you need to take a lot of actions at once you're able to pause time (aka send out 100s of actions instantly) or perceive time more slowly to represent you being able to think something through so quickly.Some tech feels like it's placed oddly. Notably:-Water handling being so early made me think water was going to be a thing VERY early, while it wasn't super late still felt odd. I think I had ability to pull up and move liquid water for 30-40 years prior to ever using the tech.-Geothermal Power felt too late, make it less powerful but earlier, by the time I had it unlocked with how rare thermal spots are it felt very...underwhelming... I had to move 2 buildings to be to place them and found 2 others I could use without moving, and then only a few others around all of Mars in random locations.Logic in the game feels weird. It's like your trying to go for a "realist" terraforming process but you have no ability to remove N2 from atmo, so you could accidentally get to an atmosphere of several bar while earth is ~1 bar. I understand you suggest ~1 bar of N2 by having ~400 mbar of CO2 releasable from Mars itself, thus only having a 1.4 bar, but it's very easy to set 8 space ports importing N2 and forget or look away for a bit and have 850mbar N2 (which I did), or say 5bar N2. I then set up 20 O2 capture plants and lowered O2 + CO2 to 22% resulting in about 1.25 bar.You can have liquid water on the surface at -20C and 100mbar which makes none sense. I know you have ice graphics on north and south poles, so isn't unreasonable to have ice build up depending on T/P ratio. Alternatively just have water build up in atmosphere until conditions for liquid water are meet thus the great rains happen. checking phase diagrams seems like these conditions would simply cause all H2O to evaporate/sublimate, but I might be mistaken on this.It feels REALLY bad being so heavily iron starved while on the surface of mars with all that rust everywhere, would recommend a building at the start that works best at the start and gets worse over time in one area and as you start growing plants on that area of soil. this would make early iron vastly more abundant but require you to keep spreading out or run out of iron. I felt that early game Steel was the what I waited for the most, and Iron being the cause of that.For Story: uh, didn't finish the Tekkie ending but [Good Robot] felt kind of annoying due to how long it takes to get O2 up and CO2 down. Free Ami felt silly, I think I took another 10-20 years to finish the fleet and yet, never had retaliation after first directive was completed??? you'd think with the given dialog they'd try anything at all when the first directive in Tekkies path is build array.In regard to [Good Robot] I think giving a hint in how to more quickly modify CO2 into O2 or allow for CO2 Capture. I had 25% planet coverage growing to 45% but couldn't get much higher then that. I had I think 573m of water but never felt the desire to bring in more ice. is that the problem? I don't know if more water = more plants = more O2 faster. I assume so, but until you get the [Good Robot] achievement it didn't feel justified to bring in more water, but by that point I'd have to delete like 100 building and rebuild them a few times to keep water intake, which sounded like more of a hassle then it was worth, when I can just wait and watch YouTube on another monitor.For QoL I'd recommend a button you can press to enable auto-upgrading roads to next tier that are >[slide bar]% saturation, a button to build all hypertubes possible at that time. If you have upgraded roads between 3 buildings and remove the middle building losing the road feels annoying since you loss upgraded ways for distribution that you then have to upgrade other ways for, why not just have the upgraded roads snap together? non-upgraded roads *poofing* away is fine but losing the investment of time and resources on your road infrastructure feels annoying. why can't I keep F1 open while upgrading ways?Idk if this was a me problem or something others have had, but after researching magnetic dipoles I couldn't find where to build them for like 10-20 years, I would have had them completed easily prior to entering stage 4 but just never saw the build location. I ended up seeing the achievement on my steam library page as one to be unlocked and realized I might have missed it in space, and it turns out I didn't zoom out enough and didn't pan far enough to the sides.Lastly, Make it more apparent you can research the bottom circles immediately, I hit 50/50 buildings really quick, then thought I had to research both the engineering upgrades to raise limit so ended up waiting a while to get them then found out I could have just immediately researched it saving a 1-3 years of time since I was only at 10-25 research/month, I don't  remember, but almost quit at that point since all progress felt walled behind an arbitrary time wall, and I had nothing to do for so long at the start of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Ever played on your mobile the simple looking game Achikaps and you like that much? Than, as I think, you like this game too. As PC game looks Per Aspere the much bigger further advanced brother of Achikaps. May-be this is not a game for every one, it's a matter of taste if you like this game more than "Surviving Mars", being developed by the makers of Tropico. I have played this game already several hours and have seen many YouTube videos and I like this game a lot. The Mars game map is not generated randomly but is hand created by the developers, it's a 100% realistic Mars map, for that is much info from NASA used. In Per Aspera you are not as in Tropico El Presidente but a self-aware artifical intelligence robot (a kind of Mister Data AI life form known as in Star Trek) created by the team of Doctor Foster and sent to Mars to make the planet fit for human life. Creating on Mars the first mile stone for our peaceful inter planetary civilization. That's Doctor Fosters plan.. but.. are we alone on the Red Planet or is there later in the game an unpleasant Grey? surprise waiting for you? Remember in the ancient Roman religion Mars the bringer of... war.

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful and interesting perspective on the Mars theme city-builder genre.  It grabs you similar to the 'one more turn' meme of the Civs series.  Here it is one more building, one more research, or one more task.  In my first play, I found myself getting too heavy in the terraforming and in the 3rd or 4th hour getting crushed by the opposing colony.  (Oh, by the way there is combat).  It is different than other Mars games where the hard part is the start, here the challenge slowly ramps up.  Making at least so far from what I can tell, the mid-game, as the challenge.I will admit there is some quality of life issues that need to be worked out (sometimes hard to find that one silicon mine that you placed in some place 90 mins ago or to deactivate a structure priority via a scroll list) but I am happy to see a decent full game (non-Alpha/Beta) with decent replay value.  It might be the one highlight to 2020.

All the mechanics for the actual terraforming  are WAYYYyy off.  The game is a good idea but it was implemented poorly. _childDocuments_.review: Really needs more nuanced prioritizing options. Its all supposively about automation; but falls flat due to the chaotic nature of the workers deciding to do their own thing before everything else that should be more important... Forexample: My silicon mines are stuck with full mining stock piles, but my electrical factories are starving of silicon, yet no drone hubs nearby is doing anything about it; unless i hit the prioritization button which basically says all drones should be on the task which remove them from doing something else equally important somewhere else in my huge base. Sudden a mine runs out of something and something else starts lacking, because i was too busy trying to fix another chain and not expanding my base to the next nodes.Its micro management game without nuance and more about just placement, that its obnoxiously slow yet absolutely chaotic at higher speeds.Combat becomes just blobing up a huge assault drone fleet with defense towers here and there. and is definitely not the main focus.At the start the game is manageable, but as you start expanding between sectors and have to balance your atmosphere composition with microing the absolutely massive base which will eventually crawl down the gameplay as you forced to play at slower speeds or risk death spirals.Suggestions- Give us the ability to set alerts for specific levels of production or when efficiency for a set of buildings go down or if resource production levels fall below a level, especially ability to slow down the game if something is triggered. We are an AMI after all.- Conditional Power off / Power On of buildings.- Stockpile management needs a lot more work especially when once starts working with large units of resources- Allow us to assign drone hubs to specific buildings instead of area.- Should be able to assign mines/factories to stock piles instead of a resource, to avoid drones from going all over the place- No way to convert oxygen back to carbon dioxide. This should be simple, we already do it here :) and stockpiles of carbon is available. Currently too easy to get stuck at 95% oxygen and going into a death spiral since everything is on FIRE and silicon and chemicals get completely drained- Give us the ability to have multiple graphs of  resources up at the same time.- More variation in music... it gets a tad monotonious.Bugs- I can get calls from the same character while I'm still talking to the same character. I get these are conversations that may have happened, considering the timeframe. Slow the game down perhaps when such have been accepted to avoid such?- Research completions interrupts story elements and can get jarring.- Story elements do not stop the game from running in the background. Had all the psych evals WHILE i was in 16x mode and I think that screwed me up in the end game on my second play through attempt

_childDocuments_.review: *Update* They released an update over 2 years later that fixed the only imperfection in the story. Love it.I bought this for the city-building and terraforming, and that aspect of the game is good. The colonists just need food and water. If they don't have that, they leave, when there is enough, they stay. No mass graves because your water pump shut down for a day.But, HOLY POOP the story is amazing. I'm 10 hours in, and, like every good thriller, I have no idea how this will end. It is hands down, the absolute best AI narrative in any medium that I've experienced. *UPDATE* 20 hours and finished. The whole story is great, and worth looking into some of the other options.I'm also so happy to see Yong Yea's voice acting career picking up.

_childDocuments_.review: Of all the games allowing you to colonise Mars (and teraform it into a Green Planet), Per Aspera is most likely the best one. The storyline gives you a few branching paths, but the beauty of the game reside in the ability to play on a global planetary level, explore previous missions site (including some of the real ones) and watch how your progress impact this no longuer barren world.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: While the game was a bit buggy on release, I love Per Aspera, and how it traps you in exploring mars. It's so, so beautiful to be able to see mars slowly turn green by your hand. And the story is beautiful too.It was fun going through the first stages of the game, slowing building up a base, expanding outwards, reading the story, and while the logistics system can sometimes be a pain in the mid- to late-game, once you get the hang of it, it's not all that bad. The orbital projects too make everything even better. Can definitely recommend to any fans of citybuilders and factorio.

_childDocuments_.review: Ugh, I want my weekend back.On paper I should love this game, and I played as far as I could up until a game breaking bug prevented me from finishing :(  It's not just the bugs though.  There is little to no challenge (even at the second highest difficulty) the base building is quite un-rewarding and becomes choreish very quickly.The story has some interesting bits to it, but pacing is crap, from a bit of reading there are a lot of "triggered story events" so if you don't go after things in the order they expect, you can have very long periods of not much happening, followed by a lot happening that you're massively over-powered for.The dynamic of water appearing and flooding a lot of stuff is also super annoying, not fun and can break story elements as well
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a fun gameplay concept that is however very shallow and towards the end frustrates by not being rewarding and throwing a hundred little stones into your path for being unrefined.The story is okay. It starts out fine, but it tries so hard to make us care for overdrawn, one-dimensional characters that however instantly default back to normality the moment the plot needs to advance. The game gives you choices, but almost none of them seem to really matter. One big conflict that threatens to tear the very protagonist apart somehow disappears into the void later on, even if you never chose to resolve or confront it. Poof, gone!But the biggest problem will certainly the be the sprawl. You will find your base hopelessly overgrowing, because resources run out so you need to keep building mines and expanding your reach. But the old mines need to be deconstructed manually and production needs to be either moved along or you need to rely on one of the worst logistics management in a base-building game: none. You cannot influence the way the game paths resources. So one worker will be overburdened with dozens of orders while the worker in the next sector idles peacefully because the orders do not go or from a building in its sector. You can put buildings into priority mode so they get preferential treatment when goods are moved, but if you have for example one area where a lot of water is being extracted and one area rich in chemicals, you cannot have the game path those resources together where you want to turn them into food. Only put the food factories into priority mode individually. And when another resource then gets pathed by those food factories, you will see all your other projects grind to a halt because your worker drones will prioritize the food resources over whatever else is needed. This can be resolved with clustering production, but it feels more like working *around* the bad game pathing rather than clever base design, and it will slow down your production. The only thing you can do is basically give every mine and factory its own worker, at which point you can enjoy the framerate grind to a halt, because running anything other than x16 speed is horrible (most sound effects aren't played on that speed so they won't keep building up to a deafening drone) which also cuts your framerate in half. I found myself spending more time on de-sprawling the planet towards the end, while the actual endgame presented no actual challenge.And if you want to hunt down the food factories to un-prioritize them, have fun, because unlike every other game like this that I have played, icons do not stay the same size when you zoom out, so you to scroll across literally the entire planet looking for this tiny symbol next to every building. This also goes for drone swarms in the laughably shallow military aspect, where biggest swarm always wins. Want to know where your huge swarms are? Well, have fun checking every single defense tower. How do you find them? Well, let's go for icon-hunting again!Only engage on your own volition. It is addictive, but not rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sure other reviews have covered most of this. Despite really looking forward to the game, and it being in theory one of the kinds of games I really enjoy, I just found the whole thing to be quite lacking. The core loop of mine-build-expand lacks both detailed feedback and any way of really getting "better." Compared to something like Factorio, despite the apparent presence of a resource management aspect, there's almost zero depth. It doesn't have to be a Factorio clone, but the fact that resources dry up so quickly means that you're mostly just trying to expand all the time.Starting second bases is a problem. For a start the ships you send out have almost no resources, so you're forced to make another bootstrap base even if you have the long-distance hyperloop system. This means that while you may think it's a good strategy to send out a lander, build a hyperloop and connect it up to your main resource stockpile, you cannot do this, and are stuck going through the exact same aluminum-steel-parts process to bootstrap a base to get a hyperloop connected. Also, once you have researched higher-level mines, as they are set to the default build option at the beginning, you can find yourself being unable to even build a starter aluminium mine in an expansion until you work out how to select the lower levels.One of the resources you run out of soonest is water, and despite crashing whole asteroids full of ice into the planet, you are always running out, unable to get water from the literal oceans you create.The terraforming process is also incredibly shallow and, as others have pointed out, often means you end up with an excess of oxygen and no way of generating what you need to counteract fires. The notion of carefully guiding the Martian atmosphere with the right amount of CO2, O2 and N2 from the beginning seems to be alien - why? Why would you need to spend years making O2 only to discover that you need a shedload of N2 later on? Why wouldn't you want to be balancing these emissions from the beginning? It makes no sense and is just frustrating.The story is good, but the painfully slow mechanism of sending out landing sites, bootstrapping them, building research outposts means most of the story is simply too much of a pain to unlock, or you end up unlocking it out of order. A real shame given the work that was obviously put into this side of the game.All in all it feels like a game that needs more playtesting, more depth, a balance overhaul, and a revisit of the whole core loop to give you something to do and optimise in your base. I hope it will be a good game in a year's time and look forward to seeing if the developers can rescue it.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly a  good game. Don't get me wrong, it needs some work. Fortunately, in the last couple weeks the devs have been listening to the community and are making rapid improvements and fixes. Construction and research choices, as well as dialog choices, can seriously alter the game. Some choices can send you on a mission to destroy the very colony you built, or getting deleted, while others can flood the planet, while others can lead to immortality (for AMI at least). Worth your time. Fun to play, with a really good story. That said, here's my list of gripes:  It is  difficult to house more than 1000 total colonists. Most of that limitation is from water scarcity. Even after you have sections of your colony drown, you'll still be mining ice, and using it up, rather than doing any recycling. That wouldn't be so bad, but for two things:1. your research comes from colonists so it takes 3 to 5  to research higher level tech with 1000 colonists.2. Half of a whole tech tree is dedicated to buildings that you can't use. Who needs to be able to build colonies that can support 1000, 5000, or 20000 colonists, if you can't even feed 1000? Another issue tied to the tech-tree, and the story progression. You can't progress to techs to balance your oxygen until you're already over dangerous levels. Worse, it's gonna take  of time to research what you need to get the levels safe again. By the time you've done that, there's no need for the unlockable trees and animals... Trees would almost certainly spike your oxygen again, and it's much faster to research and finish teraforming than to research plants and animals. There's a lot of poorly ordered dialog. Make a new discovery, and 10 minutes later you get a phone call wondering what that discovery might be. Melt the ice caps, then spend the next hour getting  calls and thoughts about we might soon melt the ice caps. The worst one is near the end. A few good dialog and construction choices, and you can uncover the secret of . Later, you find a dangerous thing, that does the same thing to your own colonists. Not only is this rather silly, but it becomes a serious plot point "if I had known what the danger was, I could have taken precautions." Worse, the fate of the colonists doesn't actually line up with the uncovered secret history on the origin of Carmine.

_childDocuments_.review: Aggressively dumb story, fun gameplay with mods (which disable achievements). So, borderline thumbs up on sale.Story: the game is about an AI sent to supervise the planet-wide infrastructure for the colonisation of Mars. The space part of the story is fine, great even. The game wears its Kim Stanley Robinson influence on its sleeve, and is the better for it. There are some issues with the impact of certain choices, but nothing major. 9/10.The story dealing with the AI is aggressively dumb (and a huge chunk of the game). The AI monologues and does things which are massively dumb, while commenting on its own logical precision; massive soap-operas are born because the AI doesn't talk to the humans to ask advice or more information.The story arrived out of order multiple times, e.g.: the AI argues with a character, they get very upset, and they no longer speak to the AI. 30 minutes later, the character cheerily contacts the AI with no reference to the prior discussion.There are mods which stop the AI monologues but I found that the AI dialogues were a bigger headache. I advise playing the sandbox mode, which has no dialogues or monologues.So, the story is infuriating, but the option exists to remove it: 3/10.Gameplay: I started playing with mods reducing artificial restrictions and micromanagement (but I disabled my achievements by enabling mods). And I had a great time, smooth and fun gameplay while watching Mars transform around me. If Skyrim can get rated on how it plays with mods, then so can Per Aspera. The controls are somewhat poor, and are especially bad in the battle UI (e.g. left-click select and attack). 8/10.Stability: finished the game in 22 hours, I did get the game stuck once for 10 minutes(!) when placing a building. Most people would've closed the game and lost 10-20 minutes of play. So... it's decent, but I'd like at least an option to save according to real time, as the game only autosaves according to in-game time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a horrible game..Good things about the game: The graphical design is very well done, it is impressive and they obviously did an amazing job on it. The sound design is also so well put together that it fits seemlessly into the game, nice work.Bad things about the game:1: Limited basic resources like iron, coal and silicon... There are mines on earth that has been in use since the bronze age and geologists estimate that many of those mines will be exploitable for several thousand years into the future even with modern mining methods... Now we look at Mars that has never been exploited before. Mars has several craters on it's surface and most asteroids contain a boatload of minerals, the game however does not let the player exploit the craters but instead ignores them for stupid gameplay reasons (artificial difficulty). In real life there are so many basic resources on Mars that you could run fully modernized mining operations there for thousands of years and there would be barely any end to the amount of resources that would be exploitable.This kills the immersion, this absolutely destroys the atmosphere of the game. The whole story becomes nonsensical. It's like the AI (PLAYER CHARACTER) is so dumb that it doesn't exploit the near endless amount of resources on the actual surface of Mars. The game only lets you have like a few mines here and there WITH LIMITED AMOUNTS OF MINABLE RESOURCES IN THEM. THIS IS RIDICULOUS. There is enough iron within one of those asteroid craters to fuel the whole earth's iron industry for several decades. But somehow it's not enough to fuel a few little drone industries with drones that fly around and move things/repair things.. Are you kidding me? This is absolutely idiotic game design.2: Absolutely idiotic gameplay when it comes to your worker drones: So the drones which repair your buildings cannot be recycled and break after a few months, they are completely useless but costs a fortune of VERY LIMITED resources to construct. You need them to repair your buildings because if you don't your buildings break. But they barely get the job done and then they break. The game does not even let you recycle them, it doesn't even give you a chance to re-use those resources that were lost with the drone. When you have STUPIDLY LIMITED RESOURCES for the most idiotic gamey reasons these drones quickly become a huge thorn in your side. You have to produce massive amounts of them over and over again whilst you are forced to build a million other buildings and transport drones. You will be forced to micro-manage several dussins of factories eventually because of the limited resources, you have to individually turn them on and off at the right times in order to not waste resources which becomes EXTREMELY tedious after just a short while.3: The game pretends to be sandboxy but there is a time limit in the game. The time limit has been converted into STUPIDLY LIMITED RESOURCES. Because you have to build production chains you need specific resources for different production chains but since the base resources are STUPIDLY LIMITED you will eventually run into a dead end where you run out of that specific resource. Which soft-locks you from the rest of the game. Sandbox huh? More like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.This is some of the most stupid game design that I have ever seen. Don't get me wrong, the sound design and the graphical design is great, well done. But holy smokes.. The gameplay is horrendously bad and completely nonsensical. The game claims that you play on the surface of Mars, but on the surface of Mars you would have near limitless amounts of minerals. THE WHOLE REASON AS TO WHY THE PLANET MARS IS RED IS BECAUSE THE WHOLE DAMN SURFACE IS FILLED WITH IRON DUST.... OMG HOW THE HELL IS IRON A LIMITED RESOURCE, ARE YOU KIDDING ME?This game made me sperg out completely regarding realism. This game does not play out on Mars, it does not play out in anything that we could even compare to the real world. Most if not all fictional universes has simple laws and rules that makes those universes relatable to us. But this game just ♥♥♥♥♥ on your face and tells you "NO, THERE IS NO RESOURCES ON MARS, YOU WILL HAVE TO SCRATCH THE SURFACE IN DIRE HOPES OF FINDING A SINGLE GRAIN OF IRON, SILICON OR COAL."I will never play this game again, refunded. DO NOT BUY THIS GAME, it makes no sense what so ever, the gameplay is stupid, the game is stupid. Don't buy it. Unless of course you are just looking for a mediocre challenge with some really dumb logic to it, maybe then this game will fit you. Whatever entertains you is up to you.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Most people quit before getting through 1/10 of the game, solid DO NOT BUY! The early game is intriguing with interesting characters, a story that is told in through a unique perspective and unfolds with the choices you make throughout. The game is admittedly slow but it can't be that way all the time right? That assumption was oh so wrong. I have 20 hours in and many problems are technical but the majority, the vast majority, is the padding. Let's start with the resources, they are randomly found, generally far away and creates a burden to get them constantly. I played on normal and the resource veins were a lack luster pittance but everything and I mean EVERYTHING is expensive not just in materials, but power to. This probably padded out 14 hours of my play time. This has been a problem from the get go and it's obvious it isn't fixed which is a major problem in my eyes but the biggest technical bug is one you do not notice when things are on micro scale and that is the worker drones. The worker drones AI are still bugged, just check the forums to see the problems with that and again it's a problem that's been there since release. This only become glaringly apparent when you go to the macro scale of the city management and it only gets worse the more you do. Such as I would set a priority build and my drones wouldn't work on it cause if I had something else building that needed the same resources but it wasn't a priority. The AI couldn't figure out where to put the items and so worker drones would shuffle them around like a paid by the hour worker with no over sight and were just trying to run out the clock to the end of it's shift. Frustratingly the clock is your time and this caused my economy to tank so I had to use a cheat engine to increase the yield of the ore veins. That worked to fix the supply issue and let me continue play but the overall issue of the AI of not working only made me wait longer and longer to get things done and that is not acceptable. That problem was probably the next 5 hours of game play so that leaves the last hour to story. Yep, 20 hours and maybe an hour of story. I also got achievements that only 34 some odd percent of the player base has gotten and this has been out since December 2020 with a mostly positive? How?!? The game had 4k player in December 2020 (steam spy btw) but it hasn't broke 300 since Feb 2021. That along with the low achievement's given out means that this game is abandoned long before I quit playing. I am the exception not the rule and it isn't hard to see why. There was something interesting here at first but the dev's are either too focused on their vision to keep the game interesting, flowing smoothly and unwilling to compromise the padding or they're too inexperienced to know any better. Either way the game lacks vision, lacks engagement beyond the first couple of hours, doesn't respect the players time and they lack the technical expertise to fix what is broken. Period. Do not buy this.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine a version of Surviving Mars where each drone hub can control one and only one drone.  And building more hubs only shrinks the area of control of the hubs around it.  And drones won't cross over other hubs to help out in busy hubs.  In this colony builder/resource management game you're often trying to play around the strange and somewhat broken AI of the worker bots, and the resource management system in general (if you upgrade the roads between buildigs A and B so workers move faster between buildings, then you build a new building C between A and B those upgraded roads disappear entirely.  There's no way to hook new building C into the existing road network.  Don't ask me why this was left in or seen as a good idea.)The tech tree is unbalanced and backwards.  For example, you can unlock wind farms early on, but they won't help you until you get on with the terraforming, and by then you should have access to nuclear fission power plants anyway.  Meanwhile building hyperloops basically is a complete game changer and should absolutely be rushed.The RTS elements are poorly executed.  I wasn't sure what the purpose of drone hives is, since my swarms seemed to gravitate to worker hubs just as often after combat and the drone swarms seemed to be able to operate far away from hives with no loss of capabilities.  If the Drone Hives are only spawn points, why include a Drone Factory building as well?  Also the control system for the RTS elements were annoying and that whole element was poorly balanced (I was able to crush enemy bases with little effort and hadn't even researched half the military tech tree, while playing on the hardest difficulty setting).Also, the main game mechanic is at odds with the other mechanics.  When you terraform the planet you lose access to a lot of resources and research sites that disappear under the ocean.  You won't get much benefit from terraforming (no open-air farms like Surviving Mars) so I didn't see any point in rushing it.  I wasn't sure what half the bio techs were doing (yay now the colonists can have animals on Mars.  How does that help me out?)  The bio tech tree seems really unbalanced with the broken resource-gathering mechanic.  Researching the bio tech tree allows you to have massive colonies of a hundred thousand inhabitants, but I couldn't swing a colony of more than a few thousand due to the limits of the worker bots in moving resources from mines to factories to colony sites.Finally there's not much in the way of replay value.  The Campaign seems to unfold the same way upon subsequent playthroughs and your choices don't seem to have much impact.  For example Carmine will still appear even if you use the most peaceful ways of terraforming the planet.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, I love it.  It's ambitious and well worth it.  You def want the blue Mars DLC.  It's been a while since a game sucked me into it this much.  I'm near the end (I think) of my first playthrough.  Base game is a colony management / terraform Mars sim.  It's fairly epic in scope; this isn't just "drop off a terraforming package and watch it green up." It takes time to build your base(s), develop tech, and build your tech that has an impact (pun intended) on the planet.  On top of that is story mode where you have conversational choices to make, people count on you, secrets are gradually revealed, loyalties shift, and *things* happen.  There's even a little bit of "combat."  Along the way we explore several ideas such as the nature of consciousness and personhood and a few others, but that's easily skipped/skimmed if you'd rather.   I'm looking forward to finishing up story mode, though I love it, so I can also try other modes.I don't have a lot of nits to pick.  Foremost in mind is the tech tree structure strikes me as a little strange, but that's not much of a problem beyond suspension of disbelief.  Another is that some story event triggers also sometimes seem to happen at odd (late?) points but again not a dealbreaker.  I could wish that it was easier to find a particular building on the map, like maybe a search function with filters - late game you can have a lot of buildings (*EDIT - nm, found the building list! Helpful.).   And that's about it.  Graphics are pretty and detailed, story engaging, and the UI and mechanics make sense.  Voice acting is well done.If you read the description and think you'll like the game, you probably will.   Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: Have to thumb this down sadly. A cool game certainly, with some original ideas in there, however its got some major flaws which I would argue mean its not worth a buy. I've done one entire play through on the second highest difficulty. I mostly enjoyed it however that is the most I will get out of the game. The story I thought was really cool, until the ending. Could've had some epic in game implications that were lazily not implemented.-Firstly, and most glaringly obvious. Combat?!?!?! Why does this game about terraforming Mars have combat? I like a good space fight as much as anyone else but the execution of combat was absolutely ♥♥♥♥, a total add on/afterthought that did not feel tacked onto the plot/game at all. Incredibly boring, incredibly simple. You can easily win the game by only researching 1 military tech, the rest r unnecessary (for context there is like 30). The enemy AI will always have a pitifully weak army that is easily destroyed. Cool idea, IF implemented wayyyyyyyyyyy better. Bit of a joke.-Game felt poorly designed. Hard to optimise your production lines at all, robot workers take resources wherever instead of where their needed. You cannot streamline/optimise properly, the no.1 best tactic to win fast is just expand constantly and rapidly, throw efficiency to the wind and just build ♥♥♥♥ until the planet is covered with your mines and factories. Feels lazy, and gets very repetitive.-The actual terraforming process is bugged and weird. Might have just been my play through, but the planet terroforming process constantly felt strange, I was pulling wayyy ahead meeting certian targets while lagging behind on others. You could say Im bad, and your probably right, the the terrible UI descriptions led me researching and investing in tehcs that did nothing or where the opposite of what I needed at the time. Story and voice acting were cool, though at time the story confused the hell out of me. This AI intellegnce (the player) is given enormous and total control over terraforming and ultimately controlling mars. Felt very odd with how little oversight the characters gave me, felt like Mars was an afterthought for them. For e.g. the mars colony was quite literally under attack, with humans dying, annndddd.... nothing. I repaired the damage and then a call came in months later that mentioned the attack as a bit of a side note. Like what??? Aliens/whatever/something just attacked humanity on Mars and I am not instantly contacted about wtf is going on? seems odd. this dev team had a cool vision I can see, and with a rating of 88% most players r clearly enjoying it. I certainly did at times, however felt like the game has way to many enormous flaws, oversights and plain poor design to recommend it.
