_childDocuments_.review: This game has some annoyances, but the detail on the planet surface and the terraforming process are second to none.The atmosphere has the partial pressure of different gases and you can move the concentrations to what you want. The sea level fluctuates somewhat based on the atmosphere properties, but it's also up to you to decide how wet the planet should be.The bad bits? Nice story, but annoying to listen to a second time after you paint yourself into a corner on the first playthrough. If you don't expand resource production aggressively it's easy to spiral into failure.Also, there's no sense from terraforming actions what the outcome might be. Some early decisions you make can cost you hours to reverse later.Tips: Grow fast or die. Don't use scanners, they discover few resources and prevent landers from finding basic resources. Use lots of landers, both as a means to expand and find new resources. Be careful how much CO2 you add (if any) - yes it's a good greenhouse gas but you will eventually have to convert it all back to oxygen.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Bought it on Friday, finished on Sunday. Perfect game for "need something to do in the week-end".Gameplay: 8/10Graphics: 7/10Audio: 10/10Replayability: 6/10Innovation: 9/10Value for money: 8/10Overall: 80%... and it was just enough length in the game to keep me interested. The feeling of really making a difference on an entire planet, made this game stand out. The storyline was just long enough, and did end just in time before I felt it became a chore. The difficulty for the normal storyline was pretty easy. There might be some replayability in trying other ways of completing the storyline. But I doubt this is a game I will play more than a couple of times. There is no base design in this game, as you just plop down mine after mine, and try to set the factories not too far away from the required mines. So it just boils down to making sure you have power-, repair- and worker coverage for everything. It is not a game you play for min/maxing. Just do tasks and enjoy the story.Graphics is functional, but the gui had some annoyances. Some elements was hidden behind other elements, and it could be a bit difficult to understand what was where and how to access certain features. The audio on the other hand is spot on. Nice music. The voice acting is very good for a game like this. I had expected some cheesy stuff, but some of the characters are really believable.So would I recommend it? Hands down, yes. The theme terraforming mars has been used in other games, as well as the well as board games. But I feel this game really is spot on, combining science with a fictional story, and good voice acting.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Boring game!It lacks the tools to analyze your efficiency if you want to play it hardcore. It drags too much for casual play. The story is good, its even better than the gameplay loop. Which is a terrible thing for a city-builder. And the story is not THAT good.I like the start, but gets boring and repetitive real quick. The game does not even force you to try to do something efficient. You have way too much everything. There is supposed to have a building count limit - doesn't matter - the limit is so high, you will never even get near it. There is supposed to have limited resources - doesn't matter, there are so many of them, half of the time you wont produce because you have tons of the said item. You are supposed to research new ... power building (e.g.) - doesn't matter you can just make 100 of the first tier power building, not a problem.What was supposed to be the challenge here? Not dying from boredom?This game allows you to do the most stupid layouts and the only thing it costs is a little time. And is not even fun to do stupid things in the game. Devs - stay away from identity politics (machine-person and such). Just make art..... Entertainment suffers enough IP and SJW themes. At least you had some reason to do it. But even in this case - its stupid and takes away from the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game with great story. Base building is interesting and looks good but lacks a depth of some other builders. You definitly want to play this one for a story not for base building aspect. Overall had fun but it's a kind of game where you finish campain and move on to new title. This isn't bad thing though.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I mean, it is an alright game, I did finish the campaign. It would be disingenuous to not recommend, I did have fun and it was quite nice to look at.I am kind of curious to see how the choices really affect the gameplay or if it is just a "different ending" kind of deal. But I don't feel the urge to go back and do mostly the same thing for ten more hours to find out.I'd say the biggest drawbacks for me were that the choices could be quite frustrating (either no nuance at all, or even sometimes an overly opinionated response when the choice text seemed fine), and that the story feels a bit forced and preachy from the very beginning.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: The problem with binary choice. I don't hate it but can't say I would actively recommend it. On the positive side, the scale of the game is quite impressive - allowing the entire planet to be unlocked and worked on. I also appreciate just how grounded in science the developers tried to make the game. There's a lot of useful tidbits of general knowledge and might even recommend it in an educational setting. That brings the other side of the coin. It has some serious pacing issues. It seems to be a direct consequence of both the subject matter (terraforming is not a quick job) and just how "scientific" the game is meant to be but for a colony management type game, there are some lethally boring segments - especially in sandbox mode, where the decent story and acting is nowhere to be found. A little dynamism and random surprises would go a long way in that regard but perhaps will be put in at a later date. Actual colony mechanics are a little shallow as well with production chains not needing much thought to manage and your biggest challenge will likely come from not noticing that one of your extractors ran dry and scrambling to put things back in order. Even that carries little risk though (unless you run out of aluminium, which is used for absolutely everything... including an aluminium mine),The closest comparable game would be Surviving Mars and I couldn't necessarily say Per Aspera outshines it in many regards other than letting you work with the entire planet as opposed to just a small piece as in Surviving Mars. For some reason, it's also made me want to play Rimworld more - likely due to me absolutely starved for some dynamic events apart from a falling meteor or twister here and there.There's a (slightly unfair) dichotomy between educational games and traditional games with the former often being seen as boring or non-engaging. Per Aspera helps show that there is in fact a spectrum of games in between and games can teach as well as engage. This particular game just doesn't do enough of the latter for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: The good: nice campaign and story, simple yet deep game mechanics, some replay value.The bad: user interface gets in the way (mainly selecting wrong building) and lacks quality-of-life features you would expect, but nothing game-breaking. Also, FPS drops considerably as you progress with the game. Personally, I disliked the early- and late-game pacing, but your mileage can vary. Also, it felt too easy on max difficulty.At the core, the game somewhat resembles Banished, Planetbase etc: the units, workers, are not under player's control. In Per Aspera, their task is to move resources between buildings and they do so following their own algorithm. Facility placement serves as the primary means for the player to influence worker's performance. You will be building and maintaining logistic chains, adjusting things as mines dry up and scale goes up. Overall, Per Aspera is a nice game, though not without problems at this point. Buy if you like the (sub)genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: This game is right up my alley in terms of genre.  I love space sim/colony/builder/survival type games.  I started playing the game yesterday and all of a sudden it was 3am... this is exactly the effect a decent game should have on me.  I love how the tutorial is woven into the campaign story, and everything about this game is unobtrusive.  The voice acting is good and not over the top or cheesy like you get from a lot of games, it's all very professional sounding.  The background music is good, and I say good because I didnt even notice the game HAD background music until about 4 hours into play.  That's what I like... not having to immediately go into settings and adjust audio volumes.  I also really LOVE playing as the perspective of the AI.  I'm excited to see how my choices affect my game later down the road.  I'm hoping HOPING that this can be a sort of Black & White type thing where I can be a benevolent AI, or I can be an evil domineering AI overlord.The game mechanics are not too complicated if you've played games like this before.  There is no "hand holding teach you to move, shove info down your throat" type tutorial, and that's OK because the game is simple enough to figure out on your own.  The UI is not busy and in my opinion is well organized.  I can already see that this is going to be a game that winds up with hundreds of hours of gameplay.To the devs, great job!Feature requests:-Add a technology to maybe increase the worker drones per worker hub from one to two.  Late game and I'm having some load issues despite cramming in new hubs everywhere.  This load issue is even after I rebuilt half my base to keep resource chains in close proximity in an effort to be efficient.-Some of the AI "reflections" seem a bit repetitive.  I was already building up atmospheric pressure and was almost at 300mb and the AI was STILL rambling on about the microsuns.-I like talking to Houston and the Commander.  Can maybe add in a feature where I could initiate communications with them at will instead of them just randomly calling me only when there's some event?-Allow me to set the transfer colonist task at the spaceport to auto-expire instead of having to sit and stare at the progress bar waiting for it to get back on Earth and only then can you cancel it.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: After a long deliberation, I unfortunately cannot recommend the game. I was on the fence, but progressing further in the game you see more and more janky features. Cancelling roads is impossible, if some road decided to put over your prospective mine, bad luck - you cannot build a mine anymore.Resource distribution with workers is made complex busywork, you need 30-50% of buildings to be workers... Mines are somewhat odd - there are few at start, and later there are deeper mines, but they are clustered together in "resource villages". Also resources are finite and depending on your luck, you will always be low on one resource. Repair is another micromanagement stuff, you have to put a lot of repair buildings. And in some building views you do not see if there is resource spot where you are putting your building. You sometimes find it out after placing a building and have to press cancel building quickly.Scanning is a bit of busywork too, which goes very slowly even with 10 built towers.Game is okay, 6/10. Maybe get on sale when you have finished rest of strategies.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the kind of busywork logistic games where you set up supply lines and watch them go, but don't like the constant math and optimization that usually comes with the territory, this game is a nice change of pace. In the normal campaign mode you quickly reach a point where you have resources in abundance and meticulous planing is no longer necessary. While a lot of people might enjoy the mathematical optimization aspects, they usually just drag a game down for me. Add to that a story that is carried by mostly amazing voice acting, and you have a relaxing yet engaging game.The only downside is that there are still some issues like questionably worker drone pathing or dialogue triggering in ways that feel unnatural, as well as a lategame that mostly comes down to waiting for enough resources to be deposited in X. These flaws are easy to live with though thanks to the rest of the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: The workers are frankly broken. They're basically uncontrollable. While the game nominally allows you to assign a prioritization for tasks, the worker drones seem to love just completely ignoring that. I'm sitting here watching my Martian civilization die a slow death, because despite the fact that I've allocated literally every possible task to a lower priority than the "make more workers in the worker factory", they're all running around doing basically anything other than moving the damned gears that need to get from the warehouse to the factory that's right bloody next door. Meanwhile, these mindless drones are slowly dying off, and none of them seem to be willing or able to do a damned thing to replace themselves. Oh now it's been five minutes, not only are they not moving the gears from the warehouse to the factory, some of them have gone and taken the gears from the factory and moved it elsewhere. Why? Who the hell knows. No, of course you can't manually control them when it's important, that would be *insane*. Who would want to be able to actually fix a problem? The game doesn't even let you reassign the area where you want your workers to be focusing on. You just need to kinda build these "hubs" and hope what workers you have pick the right ones to move to and to start doing the jobs you've actually assigned as high priority. Instead of, I dunno, stockpiling 1000 units of polymers just for the hell of it. Very important.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I came for the base builder, stayed for the story! While I can nitpick a couple improvements I would've like to have seen like being able to run water pipes from the treatment plant or an easier way to filter by buildings that were empty or destroyed, all-in it was a great base builder. But the real story here was the story, I loved that I was an AI running things with options that lead me down various paths. I found the storyline quite engaging and didn't want it to stop. I won't say any more to avoid spoilers, but this gets an easy 2 thumbs up from me!
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing a play through on the hardest difficulty, I have to say: This is not a colony builder, this is not an rts. This is a resource management-RPG. Everything is a resource, the aluminium, the iron, the colonists. What is important is to find more and more, while developing your character, literally. You are an infant AI, learning to be a grown-up. Everything in this game serves that agenda. If you approach it as a colony builder, you won't like it.  You have to approach this game from the perspective of story telling and making a character. If you do that I'm sure you'll have fun, deciding whether to be the arbiter of peace, or the genocidal villain, is what the game is about. Both having direct routes, each decision having a logical path that you discover as you play.The end game can get pretty slow, so don't worry about slowing down your mission for the sake of the story too much, like I did. You have plenty of time to get everything you want done. It can get pretty boring after you finish with the story aspect otherwise.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Take a city builder and sprawl it across an entire planet at a reasonably believable scale! The terraforming DLC enhances the base gameplay enormously, letting you reshape your gamespace in a very satisfying way that I haven't really experienced since the days of Sid Meier's Alpha Centauri. Also! It was a brilliant choice having you play the AI responsible for the terraforming project, across the years, and centuries, and following Frostpunk's lead in seasoning the potentially dry city-building with continual little reflections and decisions!
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: It gets a solid I guess of a recommendation as it will scratch a certain management itch. It has a story mode as well which isn't bad. Doesn't get my highest vote either but it isn't bad. The gameloop suffers a bit due to some gameplay elements like the resource transporting system and the finite resource nodes but overall an enjoyable experience and its moddable so any complaint you may have with it could be solved by someone's mod!
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Game is addicting.Gameplay is all about juggling resources and efficiency, all in the name of that huge goal -- terraform mars. I love how the planet changes dynamically to how you influence it. Once you get an atmosphere, wind will blow across the martian surface and you'll see the blue glow from your orbital perspective.It has an immersive quality that I love. You are an AI in mars orbit and that's why you see everything the way that you do. There is a worldbuild behind it too, one that you'll really only get into if you seek it out. The story is a feature that I adored and was a perfect change of pace to the regular base building.If you are one of those people who spent a ton of time with cities skylines or satisfactory, I'd really recommend this one.Very good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a lot of these types of games and I usually never play the campaign and go straight to sandbox mode, but I am actually playing and enjoying the campaign in Per Aspera because of the unique twist that you are an AI and was actually interested to see what would happen.  The base planning/building, management and exploration are all fun as well.  Good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the game. People complaint about resources being scarce and logistics are a problem but... This game a resource management game guys... I am on my 20th hour in the game and this is still my first play through. I am playing on the realistic difficulty and never ever thought the logistics are being a problem or had a headache from resources. It is really fun to see the red planet become green slowly.My only complaint about the game is the lack of tutorials/explanations about drone attack ranges, hyperloop connectivity, road upgrades. I thought that hyperloops connect by themselves about an hour :D
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Updated Review 06th December 2020 :I initially provided a positive review for the title, unfortunately the current state of the game requires that I leave a negative review highlighting the issues i'm seeing : 1) Road construction AI : There needs to be a way to control how roads are built to create a more linear transport network. See point 22) Worker transport AI : As a result of the bugs with the road network the drones will commonly go into a death loop, getting perpetually stuck between two buildings. Drones are the lifeblood of yr planetary network, there inefficiency, coupled with long construction times results in most of your production buildings grinding to a halt due to full storage capacity3) Despite well placed worker hubs and storage depots, the workers will dump random resources at production buildings. 4) No way to store resources for an emergency or specific future project. 5) Maintenance Hubs : The drones are consumed upon doing the repair works. This is a redundant game design choice. Why would a sentient advanced machine produce expensive drones that comsume themselves? Rather use resources that create nanites that the repairs drones consume. we can then have a supply of nanites close at hand to supply these hubs.. Or build this into the Hubs functionality. 6) Resource pocket quanities. The recent update increased the spawn rate but there will need to be a buff to overall resource quantities per node. 7) In general the game is not forthcoming with info letting you know when you have issues with production.Summary : The AI is the worst part of this game right now and as the player taking control of a sentient AI machine, you cant fall in love with the system because you constantly faced with the glaring errors of the drone AI network. There needs to be far more control for yr drones. I see no other way than to allow the player to create their own road networks so the drones are forced into set paths to achieve efficient logistics systems.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game.   A nice story, and overall I quite enjoyed my first playthrough.  Unfortunately, it doesn't really have any replayability -- generally once you have figured out that you do X, Y and Z -- the difficulty levels simply affect the speed in which you reach the goal, but the path seems to always be the same.    I think with some effort they could release a "planet generator" where you get a random gen planet, add on some fantasy story such as "woke up and your colony ship went off course to an uncharted territory" + add in some random events -- planet-wide dust storm for 10 years, solar flare, planet-killer asteroid, etc.     Or start from a hot titan-like planet and need a different path.. or a ice-ball, or living on a cloud-platform in venus, or, or or.   Some sort of variation would add replayability.     I still recommend this game, but know that once you have finished the story, you are basically done.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice game of being the most advanced artificial intelligence that ever didn't walk the Earth. Instead, it remotely (not 100% sure) controls an army of things that are absolutely enormous compared to what size you'd expect them to be. The army contains carrier bots and buildings whose purpose is to terraform the planet to such a state that it becomes habitable without any suit! That is your main goal because people will sooner or later be involved as well. You are responsible for keeping them - the researcher-scientists alive by delivering them food and drink while watching over power, maintenance etc., searching for new raw materials because the veins DO get depleted, selecting interesting research and much more. Headmaster of the company which programmed you is giving you the necessary advices to bring the mission to a good end. You response in short answers YOU chose and sometimes even (when you like think and hear your mind's voice) the woman AI voice asks a question to itself/herself which you answer. That is a part I especially like because most of those games of terraforming another planet don't have such a thought through story. The army of the automatically and unconsciously controlled machines even includes groups of flying drone-soldiers you can command to attack wherever, whenever and whichever team of enemies you like.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: SPOILERS WARNING!!!This game has a very steep learning curve so prepare for that! I really enjoyed the first 10 hours of constant challenge but the last 4 hours I just sat and clicked a single button and waited for the ships to be built.I found the story was good with a few nice twists thrown in. If you are after a challenge terraforming your own world, I definitely recommend this game, In the end give yourself some other goals to tide you over though.This game could use with some more development on balancing and resource availability, there was a quite a few times I had to deconstruct key buildings in order to progress which was annoying at worst. The worker bots are broken and do make logical decisions at all. They will travel halfway around Mars to pick up a resource that is literally right next to them.Art style is clean and informative using standard topographical lines to show elavation as well as the 3D is very nice. The way the planet physically changes as you progress is awesome! I loved watching the oceans slowly rise.All things considered I would rate this game a 6.5 out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very good and very hard. If you like resource management and if you would like to be challenged then this is a perfect fit for you. Every action you take as implications in the long run so you need to choose what to build (or not build) and which actions to take and benefit or suffer for it later.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Man, this is a game that's disappointing to dislike.I'm a pretty avid city builder/strategy nerd.  I appreciate very heavy games like what Paradox produces, lighter games that are well executed like Banished, and everything in between.  This one just isn't good unfortunately, well below my low bar.The good:The voice acting is very good, and the story is somewhat intriguing.The bad:The game play is really poor.  Honestly it reminded me of an idle game I might play on my phone, except I had to watch it the whole time.You land on Mars and immediately are interacting with 95% of the available resource types within 5 minutes of the game starting... and those interactions are going to remain virtually unchanged for the next 20-30 hours.  This might be forgivable if it went somewhere... but it does not.  Initially you will feel like it might be going places: there are little prompts with temperature and oxygen levels and when you hit a couple of different milestones the planet undergoes a neat little transformation.  But after that... the game virtually stops.  There are a few more parameters to tweak but not only is it mechanically very tedious it doesn't *feel* like you are effecting the planet anymore.  I got the "congratulations mars is terraformed!" message when the planet was -1.8 degrees C, the water level was still well inside what was obviously supposed to be the ocean boundary, and the planet was still entirely red and dead looking.  There are endgame techs you think might be cool that are literally pointless, like open air cities.  The whole game just provides none of the mechanical joy I would expect out of a game of this genre, and none of the wonder that you might get out of a building game like Cities Skylines... It just isn't very good as a game.  There is a light combat aspect in the game that is also largely pointless, which ties to a plot element I wont spoil.  I suspect that system pulled a lot of attention away from the rest of the game, which would have been far improved by a more linear game play loop with a focus on the headline mechanic of terraforming.  Kind of a classic example of not knowing what your focus in development is.Very rarely do I leave poor reviews, but this is a thumbs down.  I wouldn't even pick it up on sale honestly.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game if you enjoy city builders, it follows a lot of real-world concepts regarding terraforming Mars I was very impressed with the single-player sandbox. I took Mars from a desolate red rock with one lonely landing site to a sprawling connected web of resource generating buildings spanning and entire green and blue planet. To the Devs: One tiny issues with with removing resources from scrapped buildings to preserve building limit. Perhaps add an option to sacrifice the resources to removing the building pad.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: It's fine. Has some good ideas, but the end result is "fine".Don't worry about how your cities look. It will always form a blob of buildings and streets running all over the place. Looks awful, and resources reach where they should eventually anyway. It has some combat, just make a blob bigger than your enemies and throw it at them.Transport of stuff is a serious problem in this game. Because this is ThE fUtUrE, you can't have a train, truck or any reasonable medium of transportation. You have pods. Each pod can transport ONE resource through ONE road, so resource transport is slow and bottlenecks are frequent. Just add more pods to the blob until flow of resources resumes, so not a terrible thing. The problem is the hyperloops. They are ALSO pods, just faster, so they suck and are usually a bottleneck. Put normal roads on top of the hyperloop, and normal pods will transport resources that the hyperloop going and coming full speed trasnporting ONE RESOURCE EACH TIME just can't. The Blob keeps growing. If you ever wondered why we don't have hyperloops, play this game.Besides that, there's some cool ideas here, but the core of the game is... fine. It's fun for a while.Oh, also, the plot. It's also fine. Promises a lot, but I feel it doesn't do a lot and it kinda ends.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to buy it after the free weekend, but I binged it.  Near zero sleep.  It was so good.  However, I finished it.  It is very worth the full price.The game synopsis?  Most of what makes it great is the narrative story that comes along as you play.  If not for the story it would be a typical, not terrible, but not great, Mars terraforming game.  The narrative makes you feel like the game is alive and draws you in.  Most of the "choice" in the game is moral thought that acts more of a self-analysis than anything related to the game.  It's like a nice coffee chat with someone who likes deep conversation about human psyche.I might come back later and buy it when I want another play through.  However, I need sleep and, thankfully, the free weekend is nearly over.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Great idea that needs much more work. Story is interesting. Visuals pleasing. But the UI is such an unreadable mess that the game eventualy evolves into spawning everything everywhere randomly. Its impossible to locate the weak links in your net of mines and factories, so just plop more. Just to keep incomes over demands. Its something thats definitely possible to fix over time, thus positive review.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Good idea for a game but unfortunately rather poor implementation. Too much focus was put on the "story" aspects, such as the game asking me how I feel about decisions...every decision... It is obvious that the game doesn't include QoL features seen in Factorio or Dyson Sphere Program. Some examples of poor QOL I experienced in just a handful of hours:- Every building in the game you want to build must be clicked on. There is no hotbar, no "smart key" to build a building you are hovering over, etc.- There is no way to run an electrical, repair, or worker hub network. You cannot click and drag to place multiple of these spaced neatly apart at maximum range like you can power poles in Factorio / DSP.- There is no way to mass upgrade road networks, it is an absolutely painful process.- The view which gives you details about traffic on your road network CANNOT be viewed while upgrading roads. This made me feel like the devs don't play their own game honestly.I tried to play past the lack of QoL just to get through my first play through but after having no challenges presented to me with the game running on max speed it felt like a waiting game. I would spam click buildings to expand as fast as I wanted and just wait... Got bored. May return just to see what Mars looks like terraformed but besides that this game is a pass from someone looking for Factorio / DSP on Mars!
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: It's actually a rather simple builder game, however there are some impressive simulations going on in the background making it a bit more interesting. The story line felt a bit simplistic in the beginning, however as it evolved it got me more and more hooked, and now I just have to know the ending! I think this is one of the few builder games that I've actually wanted to complete in a very very long time. The story is really what makes this game worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: As mentioned in the review (like from Slug), the UI in this game is terrible.Nothing not in priority get done. I had assault drones factories to be build for 10min, only built when I prioritized them. THEN for 15min more they didn't build a single assault drone due to lacking input.I had over 125 drones and they are at the main base, factories and storage are 10 tiles away at max.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: For an indie game, yes it was pretty good. I really liked the story and the characters - it was in fact the best part of it......but the meat of it was quite thin once you had achieved self reliance. I kept on expecting more of a challenge, and then it never came. I prepared anally for something that never happened. Ending was quite disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Per Aspera is an interesting game about terraforming Mars, with you playing the part of an AI which has to oversee the process.A lot of thought has been put into the needs of a colony on Mars, which necessitates inter-related building and resource-gathering.The gameplay can be quite involved as you advance, and it isn't always intuitive. For example, at one point I couldn't place any more buildings, and I couldn't figure out why - but luckily someone had posted in the Steam forums about the same problem (doing research into engineering was the answer).The voice-acting in the game is well done, especially the voice actors for the AI (female) and the Earth-based scientist (Dr. Nathan Foster).If you like civilisation-building games, then you might want to give Per Aspera a try.(Note: I played this game on a free weekend.)
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: It starts out nicely but the story doesn't really feel related to the terraforming progress.The story is actually interesting, but for me at least, it ended half-way though the game (in "story mode", mind you).My way was probably not the only way one most certainly not the fastest way, because the last phase was just long and boring.It would have been nice if researching locations would give unique bonuses.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very impressive and addicting game, great time killer. You've got the entire Mars on a birds eye view topographical map.As the game progresses, more and more areas open up to you and allow you to slowly cover the planet in buildings and trees.I find a lot of the mechanics of the game to be fun and creative, some areas being flood zones and having the danger of being out of reach to explore the rovers, artifacts is a good addition, and the orbital view for projects looks dope, but it does definitely has its lackings.Farms' food production pales in comparison to the food factories. The game does not create bridges over the rivers when water levels start to rise, which looks strange at best. As such, some buildings definitely need a buff or work up.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that you WILL be sucked into if you like basebuilding/citybuilding games. There are threats, and there are disasters, and you will want to punch your monitor when an asteroid lands RIGHT WHERE IT KNOCKS OUT ALL THE MAIN POINTS OF INFRASTRUCTURE RIGHT AS THE GAME AUTOSAVES.... But it makes me feel like I am running a Mars Terraforming effort, and that is DAMN impressive.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I can't in good conscience recommend this game. The sound is buggy, the story is stupid, and the game's constant need to wrench control away from you at all times is a right pain in the ass. Additionally, there's no quick way to sort through all buildings of the same type planet-wide, the atmospheric handling is fiddly as hell in a way that it really doesn't need to be, and it's just not very good. Make a better game next time.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: *This review contains no spoilers about the story*I completed my first playthrough and successfully terraformed Mars! Woop! Definitely a fun game and very unique compared to other builders I usually play (Cities Skylines and Factorio mostly, SimCity games in a previous millenia).This game is beautiful and great for space nerds and builders alike. The easy mode for the story (what I did) was great for a low-stress playthrough and more of a guided story experience. I won't reveal what happens in the game, but I really appreciate how story mode introduces you to the more complicated aspects of what you are allowed to do on the planet as you go. My only complaint here is that I could tell when I spent 'extra' time in a certain segment of the game or rushed the next milestone too quickly because I ended up either not needing the advice given or found myself painted into a corner that required lots and lots of work to get out from.I would say the game is pretty fun but if you get yourself worked into a corner it can take a considerable amount of time to work yourself back out of it. Lots of hurry up and wait in my game. My playthrough took ~30 hours to complete and I definitely spent close to 8 hours today just watching the game play on a second screen. Planned a whole base and let it build it up and chug through research all with extremely minimal involvement (basically clicked the next tech in the tree).All in all, it is a fantastic play through and definitely worth the $ for just enjoying the story, acting, etc. My suggestions are to play it on easy knowing that you're going to play it again and expect it to take a long time to finish the story. I screwed up in my play but would expect most people to make a similar level mistake at some point. Expect a 25 hour game the first time through and make adjustments to your play once you know the whole game dynamic. Also, this game looks fantastic on higher resolution displays and especially ultra-widescreen displays.Developers: You need to let me continue playing after I beat the game though! I love the pan around of my terraformed Mars, but I'd like to add some water and alter the temperature to shape it more toward my 'ideal'. I know that there is a sandbox mode for this, but would you mind simply turning my story game into a sandbox after it is over? My last save is right after finishing the final stage and the game auto-completes without letting me finish my personal goals for the planet.And please let me queue techs in the tree. There are times when I want to be able to plan a strategy, save and leave the game and then forget what I was doing when I return. Planning some future research would help me along the way in remembering the strategy.The UI it pretty intuitive (just click on things if you would like to know more) and extremely informational but there are even more nerdy things that I wish were included. Like, could I have rates of change as an option for charts rather than just the value alone?Also, for late game, can we see the addition of 'fixit' type technologies that let you deal with resources and research that you may have missed due to expedited circumstances?
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: This game is freaking awsome, once you get the nuts and bolts of it. It took me a while to get to the point where mars actually turns green but I did it in the final hour of my first playthough. The biggest con' is that some of the mechanics (road upgrade, i'm looking at you) are not explained at all. The story is fun, with the multiple endings and all :)
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Could this be?  Finally, a worthy successor to Outpost 1 and Moonbase??  No.  No it is not.  For the first few hours, emotionally, this fit all the positives I felt as a child playing space colonizers for the first time.  But after that, the gameplay gets so boring and repetitive that I couldn't keep playing.  Cool narrative but I'd rather read it as a novella.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Played on the free weekend.The game is ok. Resource management and city building are right up my alley. The campaign could use some work. You're building everything up and then an objective comes up, 'go explore the other side of the planet' and you've barely built out 1/4 of your first sector. It kind of pressures you into building really big, really fast.Then, after a bit of an initial build-up you just kinda hoard resources by playing on 16x speed before your next big push into base development. The game quickly turned into, base-build for 10 minutes then do nothing at 16x speed for 5-10 minutes.Edit: I wrote this and discovered that an additional landing zone could be created. I've been sucked into this game. It's great. Buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, managed to win it during free weekend, one ending atlastThere were some things i would like tweaked, AI sometime takes bizzare-longer routes and is not using hyperlanes often enough if you ask me.Combat and unit control is another thing i found extremly unintuitiveBut overall ill give it 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: A really nice RTS strategy city builder about turning the red planet green.  Plays really well and doesn't get too boring. Went in expecting just a planet city builder not expecting to have some combat in it, even if the combat was quite easy. Took just over 12 hours to complete my first run from start to completion. Would be nice if there was more heads up on how some researched buildings would help before being researched and adding polymers to the advanced landing site to drop a hypertube straight off the bat for faster planet traversal to remote bases.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: A good idea but a bad implementation. I am kinda used to play this type of games but the way it's made make it more of a headache that an enjoyment. The AI which is manipulating the resources it's flawed, after 6 hours the AI stop producing workers due to the fact that it was missing an item even though in the storage AI had 300 pcs of certain item. Even though i started to prioritize that item it would still not go in the worker production facility even though it was prioritized( i still had 18 workers).
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Resource management terraforming simulation on a beautiful render of Mars. The game has a decent story, which is surprising for a res-man sim. If you watch someone play this at mid-end game, it can look daunting, but the game progression is simple and gated quite well, despite the campaign having a bit of a slow pace. The terraforming process can take 100+ years but the NPCs don't age or die, but that's the balance between "scientific realism". Because at the end of the day, you're trying to add an atmosphere, water, and the right mix of oxygen, nitrogen and carbon-dioxide to make the planet liveable. Based on this pace, and the fact combat is very light, the game is quite relaxing. Unfortunately the difficulty is non-existent, there's very little you can do to "lose" the game. Definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on a whim expecting a simple terraforming game where I could just watch the gradual transformation of Mars into a paradise. I wasn't expecting anything major out of it, just a few hours of entertainment and logistical planning while doing other things. Color me surprised when I came into a rather indepth and cleverly written story ruminating on concepts such as AI agency, independence, and the nature of what it means to be sentient.While the core loop is simple, it's engaging enough to keep you going to put you through the rather interesting story and the mystery at the core of the game. Though relatively short, it is entertaining enough to be worth the experience. Additionally, the game is very beautiful and well crafted visually. While I do hope the devs include more complex, layered mechanics in their future endeavors, it is very clear they have talent to form an engaging narrative.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Very much enjoyed the game. Having Mars in all it's glory to explore with all the tidbit's of former mission sites and future mission sites was exciting. I think the most amazing part of the game was working to get the first liquid water and then watching as the water levels rose and filled in all the desolate and dry areas. That part of the game and he way it was implemented blew my mind.  Later on seeing the surface turn green with a balance of the atmosphere was an accomplishment.   The story that goes on behind the scenes is well written and pulls on the heartstrings at times.  I would recommend this game to anyone interested in Mars and its terraformation, to anyone that needs a pleasant distraction with a simulation/game that is not to hard and can come back to at any time.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect experience (if you buy on sale). Not overly complicated, kinda cozy, good story that doesn't get in the way. This is the best game to play if you like not being overly challenged while still scratching the anno type strategy-city-builder itch. Watched streams while I played and felt like my attention could be easily divided between the two
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Very nearly beat the game, was on the last stage of terraforming to create a magnetic field, but the late game lag and breakdown softlocked the entire system and lack of management tools meant I couldn't fight it.Full of tedium, horrible management, you have a single "priority" order on a per-building basis, breaks down late game into a laggy, buggy mess and workers fail to deliver produced resources to necessary buildings. The whole "flooding" system is ridiculous too, if you want to interact with the water mechanics at all before you have fully flooded the planet, be prepared to rebuild stuff over and over as water rises because you CANNOT build water pumps inland. It started out so strong with an interesting story but the game just fell apart underneath me late game.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Despite some negative reviews, I really like the game so far. It looks like a mixture of the Offworld trading company (minus trading competition) and Surviving Mars (minus some boring micromanagement) and perhaps something else. The pace is slow, but I would just call it a relaxing gameplay (similar to Cities Skylines). You can set the game speed to x16 anytime if you like. In general the game looks well made and well polished. Perhaps it is just not for everyone, but for me it is the game I always wanted to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: At first I loved this game but I became more and more frustrated the more time I spent with it.Logistics become a nightmare. The game is based on scaling your base on a planet wide scale but the games system and algorithms simply don'T allow for that. At some points I had 1000s of ressources and production buildings and omes that complained about missing ressources.The pacing of the story is completely wonky. Somethimes you have to wait forever to get an event, sometimes they come so fast you have no chance to react. They also appear out of sequence in some cases screwing everything up.Terraforming is interesting but wonky as hell. I managed to get my planet to have 80% O2 atmosphere because the necessary nitrate tech was far deeper in the tech tree letting me get into an unsalvageable position.This game has some great ideas but the execution is just maddeningly annoying when you come down to it...Update after the newest updates: It has gotten much better in many quaolity of life features...
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun colony sim/city builder. It slows down significantly when you get the actual terraforming part though. If you're not careful you can easily flood the areas you've built on and runaway oxygen production is catastrophic. Careful planning is an obvious solution here but your first time through is likely blind and you'll make a lot of mistakes. You're also not warned about ice reserves melting when the planet goes above zero degrees C. Again, in hindsight it's obvious but it's a game so you're not thinking it can even happen at all until it does.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: In short, it's a charming blend of story and resource management that takes the tedium out of the supply-chain genre.  Engaging for one playthrough (~20h), though the Green Mars and Blue Mars DLCs are required to enjoy the game.It's worth it for the strategy fans who need a more relaxed experience without it being dumbed down.  The only way to lose is if you stop expanding, run your mines dry, and start to doom spiral.  I didn't find the gameplay to be repetitive, as I was discovering better strategies throughout my playthrough
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: There's a decent game in here somewhere but the catastrophically bad way of how it currently handles logistics makes the experience insufferable. No matter how many hubs you spam down, 90% of the time, mining and production buildings will be at a stand-still due to being filled to capacity. Here's an example:4-5 worker hubs with fully upgraded roads outside miners leading to both factories and supply depos are halted.. "Uhh, just rearrange the roads and stuff". I'd love to, but the game doesn't let you. Everything is hard-locked to being automatically attached to each-other via circles which right out of the gates creates a minimal spacial inefficiency of 11-60% on-top of looking like spiderweb diarrhea and the AI also has a tendency to not take the best routes. This becomes particularly annoying because once mines are depleted, you're encouraged to scrap buildings.... Which disconnects the roads.In a similar brain-dead fashion, power generation & maintenance is also restricted to circles with buildings also requiring constant maintenance so every single time you want to reach out to get resources somewhere, the project goes from being a single building with a road (maybe a cargo hub) like other actual good management games to:Once you put a few hours into the game, you also realize just how incredibly simple it is. No complexity, only occasional "threats" that randomly destroy stuff and the obligatory "research" element that involves you waiting for 10 hours before getting another toy to play with.Disappointing mess.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game in its present state. I had voice over lines cut short, I had missions that fired randomly or not at all. The logistics/building part of the game is slow and extremely tedious, and the bots that carry stuff around can rarely be counted on to do their job efficiently. The research tree is rather dull, with only the hyperloop being an actual game changer. Running out of minerals and resources is frustrating as you have to make longer and longer "tentacles" of droid bases into the unknown for just one or two resource nodes. I spent most of the time playing at maximum speed, and it still felt like the game was absolutely crawling. The soundtrack is also extremely repetitive which I shouldn't have noticed having only played the game for 4 hours, but just sitting and staring at the bots moving steel plates from one side of the base to the other leaves nothing but the soundtrack to appreciate, and I didn't appreciate it. I thought the story was weird and incomprehensible at times, but that might just because the game randomly cut short dialogue or skipped entire conversations on me. Ultimately what you spend a lot of time on in this game is staring at your base and waiting for resources to either be made or moved without any satisfaction. It's not like Factorio where you get that cool moment of making something really efficient or you get to the next research tier. There is just nothing to look forward to.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Engaging main campaign! Definitely found myself thinking about the story decisions I made later when I wasn't playing... wondering if I had made the right call... always a sign that I really will enjoy playing it again. Not sure how sandbox mode or multiplayer will progress quite yet, still early for me in the game, but so far it is getting two thumbs up... I will reserve judgement (an anticipated tip of the hat) until I get through each game mode, but I am excited to play more.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: This game is nice - but I cannot recommened it at this time. Every action takes ages! The game has multiple speed ups (from 1x to 16x) and you can only enjoy this game on 16x. Every mine takes ages, a single building will take minutes at the highest speed to be built and every space mission also.A management game that is soooo slow is not enjoyable. Even with the interesting mechanics or plot. Most of the time you are idle and waiting for the next thing too happen.Please reduce the timers by half for everything or decrease the resource costs drastically. Rebalance it to be enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Can't recommend this game because I'm almost two hours in and have yet to make a real choice of any kind. I just place the obviously needed buildings wherever, or on their resource sites, and move along. There's no decision-making, no resource balancing, no bottlenecks to overcome or supply/demand flux to worry about. There's seemingly no consequences for making too many or too few of a given building. Rather, buildings are easily replaced so fixes are wand-waving easy.It's pretty and the writing is cool but there's just no GAME here. It might as well be called "paint-by-colors the colony-builder."
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game! Conquering Mars, scientifically accurate, never been so detailed and great.But, to be more specific some pros and cons of course, technicals etc.GRAPHICPros:- Mars is perfect. Scientifically accurate map, very detailed. Looks amazing. And when terraformed - also good. Zooming, orbital view - precise and smooth.- Interface - clear, good design - nothing to complain.Cons:- buildings are not enough different from each other. But this is reasonable. Mines would be similar, right?SOUNDPros:- climatic music,  many tracks, good choices.- voice acting - perfect! Great actors and voices!Cons:- noneGAMEPLAYPros:- if you like base building games - Per Aspera has everything you need. Building, resources, production chains etc. - Terraforming aspect is just perfect. Focused on so many details like atmosphere pressure, temperature and other aspects. For example - crashing Deimos on surface is raising temperature! Same with comets. It's obvious for some people, but not for most :) More pros about terraforming would be to spoilerous, so I can't gave any details, but for sure - they are so real!- AI developing. You are AI, and you make moral and conscious choices. You can be more or less "alive". Great aspect and so emotional for me :)- Plot and stor is very good. Few turning points, many mysteries - good played dev team.Cons:- I played once getting ending "good robot". I will play again to get oppose ending. But not sure if there is room for more replayability.OVERALLBuy, play, terraform! Bring humanity to stars, starting from Mars!

_childDocuments_.review: So, what to say about Per Aspera. I played for a couple of hours so far and I’ve been quite entertained. The basics of building a colony on Mars seems quite simple, but as I started to go deeper and deeper, new mechanics appeared which got me rethinking my strategy every time. Slowly the planet starts to be populated, first by drones and eventually by humans. I also noticed that at some point there will also be flora and fauna spawning on the surface, as well as oceans that will spread across the planet. So far I’m really enjoying the game, although sometimes the progress is slow, the rewards are worth the wait. I’m also eager to try out the MP coop as soon as I finish the main campaign.

_childDocuments_.review: One day in and love it! Yes the learning curve is steep but if you're into hardcore strategy game lover its perfect! _childDocuments_.review: fun game.ai can be a bit annoying but you can skip all the dialogue so idk what these other people are complaining about.another reviewer mentioned that there is a 50 building limit. yes, there is a 50 building limit at the very start of the game and you can increase it by 100 within half an hour. there are techs that increase your building limit so idk what that moron was talking about, they just didn't read the descriptions that are in big bold letters. it's not the games fault if you are too stupid to read.

_childDocuments_.review: If you come into this expecting a management game you will be disappointed. In reality it's an idle game that uses a very hands off management system with a very light graphic novel style story with a touch of philosophy.The extent on the management side of things is placing building and setting a building to priority. That's it. Early game building placement is important for efficiency when you have few workers but by the mid game the ai has it's own ideas about efficiency and moves resources randomly. Regularly you'll notice you're low on a resource but the harvester and factory are next to each other, both full, just not being used... so trying to play the game as a management game is just infuriating. Whereas if you see it as an idle game while doing something else it becomes a lot easier to tolerate. As you can imagine terraforming a planet takes a lot of time. As does researching the technology to do so. So there's a lot of time gates. You can do little things to reduce this but things like needing to research the ability to place more buildings just slows the game down even more. There's also a total building limit so by the end game you do reach a limit to what you can do so all that's left is the wait a few hours for the numbers to go up by themselves. There's also some very tacked "combat" with a whole research tree dedicated to it. It almost feels as if this tree is here to distract you and slow you down more, since it's only used twice (sometimes thrice depending on ending) it's a huge time investment in something with no use. The story kinda happens at you. Yes there's a lot of dialogue options but they don't change anything. Doing side objectives can unlock addiction endings which are the only real choice in the game. The story isn't anything new or particularly interesting if I'm honest. There was only one twist in the whole game that was actually a surprise and it was one of the endings so there's a good chance 2/3rds of people won't see it anyway. All in all, there is very little to this game but for something running in the background it's alright if you can get it cheap. It's a nice idea but nothing feels finished. It's like it touches on ideas but they never got around to flushing them out.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Game is great but has balance issues. 20 hours in running out of water  for the food. Story line in good and has alot of twist and turns  to it.Giving it a thumbs down for now due to balance issues which hope will be fixed soon.After the game has had several new updates and content added now have to say the game is better and more balanced.Great game

_childDocuments_.review: So i gave this game a go on the free trial, but I'm so not sure what to think of this game. The concept is promising, but there is so much that doesn't suit me here that I dont know if i'll purchase a full version .. The positives are , the idea of the game, resource management and overall good choice for people who like resource management colony games and you have played all the others on the market. For the cons :  First of all the navigation and controls are just awkward , from panning to moving across the map to the UI , which is super unintuitive and you will be stuck with having to figure things out often .  The most annoying part were the random dialogues, which would interrupt you during game play, i often found myself just clicking it away to be gone . The AI concept is interesting, albeit i feel it didnt deliver. It was often super annoying with all the awkward choices and i found the voice dub the most awkward of them all , had to mute the voices in the settings after an hour.I've been put off by the long waiting times for everything to be built also . I may give the game a go in future but its highly unlikely it will be anytime soon.Overall i do recommend to people to at least try it if they like resource management games, but its defo a shelf stacker game for me.

_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: To sum it up in a single sentence: This game is conceptually fantastic but mechanically infuriating.The idea of Per Aspera is very appealing. Watching Mar slowly gain an atmosphere, watch surface water slowly begin to spread and even greenery begin to blossom is incredibly satisfying. It is obvious that a great deal of care and attention has gone into recreating Mars and there's a lot of fun to be had just rotating the big red ball and admiring all the craters and canyons.But as a game, Per Aspera is infuriating. For a game primarily about base management, I feel I have very little control over how my base is run. So much of core gameplay is left to the whims of the AI and frankly it isn't up to the challenge. It becomes difficult to focus on further terraforming when basic things like keeping Drone Factories working, Maintenance Hubs and Colonies can fall apart if you look away for too long. I would kill for a little more micromanagement. Just the ability to tell a worker "Your job is to take food from this factory to this colony and nothing else." Especially with resource placement being so random that you've got no guarantee that the resources you need will be anywhere near each other. Considering the story is suppose to revolve around an AI fully in control of the terraforming mission, you can often feel helpless watching your workers skirt around at random.I'd be lying if I said I didn't have fun playing Per Aspera, but at the end of 20 hours of playing my frustration with the mechanics quickly began to outweigh my enjoyment. This is an impressively ambitious game, and the story seems to suggest an amount of replay-ability, but the mechanics need a lot of work before I'd consider playing it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: This is the type of game my autistic a.ss. always wanted. You are set with the task of making Mars liveable. To do so you build a sprawling mass of roads, mines, colonies, and the facilities to run it all. You then have some research trees which the colonists can put their minds to work on. It's all very satisfying to watch your progress over the years in game and see the little projects you've completed along the way become part of the unique layout for your colonies. WARNING: Flood zones flood! Now, you can build there but make sure you are ready to leave. The sea takes all and you cannot stop it once you start the terraforming process.I wish the building limit was higher (or just gone tbh with a warning about it being unstable). Game ran pretty well for me, unmodded that is. However the longer you play the lower the fps gets. It will be stable but it will sink.Overall, if you like the idea of being in charge of bringing life to Mars, and making a massive blob of buildings and roads, then I'd recommend it. The game is slow and your first two hours are pretty much like the rest. Watching your base and the Martian landscape slowly change. That's the selling point for me, especially on sale.TL:DR - Game good, take forever though so put a few days aside.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Greate game concepts, but currently contains at least one annoying game breaking bug for me. Some ressources manufactured in buildings are not transported to storage sides. The output buffers of those buildings are full such that they do not produce output any more. Please fix that soon. Currently I cannot recommend the game until the bugs are fixed.Edit - 25.12.21Dear Per Aspera team,thank you for your kind response. I gave the game a second change and played it for some hours. I must admit that logistics now does work a lot better. I also enjoy the new content. Great work so far. However, there are still certain situations where I don´t know whats going on. For example, there are mines producing goods and there is free space in a warehouse. However, none of the resources are transported to the warehouse. But apart from that there is a total gamebraker which rellay killed the fun for me. That gamebraker is managing multiple districts. It is really cumbersome to get an overview of all your districts and the amount of goods that are produced there. I know that there is a special overlay where you can jump to the district and see the resources beeing stored there. However, when this overlay is active, you cannot place new building, edit old buildungs and so on. It would be nice if you just have the option to show the ressources within a certain district and still be in the normal unrestrictive gaming mode.I know, you spend a lot of work in the game. And I encourage you to keep up with the good work. I think that all problems are solvable and the game-design is quite good.Have a nice christmas,Tom
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed Per Aspera for what is it trying to achieve, but I hesitate to recommend this game at full price. I'm giving it a thumbs up because I had fun and wanted to keep playing, but the game did feel like a chore at times. The user interface needs a complete re-do, and there's a lot of missing features that other citybuilders have that I could consider core. Things that filter what you see on screen so you can find certain buildings easier. That was the most frustrating thing for me.I would be very keen to play this again if an overhaul update comes out that improves a lot of the friction in the endgame when your city is huge. The story was quite good and I was always intrigued by the characters and plot. At endgame, the performance did suffer a bit, but being such a slow-paced game, it was completely fine to play at 30fps. I think the simulation was tanking the performance more than the graphics at that scale. If I completely populated every inch of Mars, I am sure it would be completely unmanageable and the simulation would cripple my computer.Despite that, it's actually a good game, and I got my money's worth. I hope to get more if the game gets any improvements down the line. If you're looking for a citybuilder that doesn't have a lot of micromanagement, but has an engaging story that ties in with your progression, you'll probably enjoy this. I did, even though I recognise its shortcomings.

_childDocuments_.review: The first time i saw this game, i was really weirded out by the scale of things. even though you can zoom out a lot and mars is really big, it still felt like every single building is kilometers long, and for some reason you have to leave dozens if not hundreds of kilometers between each building.thankfully this weird feeling quickly faded away, and left place to a gameplay that is really interesting. it is not perfect, there is some clunkyness in the UI, but overall it really feels like you are terraforming mars. Some steps reeeeaaaally take a long time though, so be prepared. you see my fourty hours ? that's just one playthrough.if you're into simulation/management games, and also are a space enthousiast, i strongly recommend you buy this game, the good clearly outweigths the bad.So now to talk about the issues: the first thing that annoyed me, and the only one that  is the issue of finding resources in early game. at the beginning you will have everything you need close to your landing site, but each mine exctracts ressources pretty slowly. this is not a problem past the early game because you will have plenty of mines, but at first your ability to expand will be severely limited by the rate at which you can produce steel and aluminum (and in turn, electronics). it took me a long time to find a second aluminium deposit and frankly waiting for one to be detected was a drag. but past that point everything was moslty okay.now the UI : most of it is again, perfectly fine. but the window that (should) allow you to track temperature, CO2, pressure, sea level and so on is... confusing. Rather than having one single gigantic graph, the thing is split by phases in a mess i still do not understand. the reduced indicator you will have in your main view is sufficient, but i was really confused about my oxygen levels and why so many guildings were on fire depite having only 2% oxygen, and that graph was supposed to inform me. it did not.On a similar note, you have different overlays that show you the range of your power grid, maintenance buldings and so on, they are all fine except the one that is for checking temperature, biomes and moisture. at some point in the game you will unlock "biodomes" which are what you use to seed plant life on the planet. they do not output anything during regular use, unlike GHG plants that clearly indicate what they release for each unit of chemical they consume. so i build them but for maybe half of the time of my playthrough, i just didn't understand what they did. actually i don't even know if they were properly working for most of that time, but i noticed near the end that you can see what they do in the biome and moisture overlays. as for the temperature, you can see the gradient from the poles to the equator, but when you hover with your mouse, there is no indication on how hot or cold the place you're hovering over is. near the end of my playthrough, the average temperature of mars was like +8°C (because of the poles stay cold), but looking at the equatorial regions where my pet humans live, i could only assume that the temperature was scorching hot because everything was red. maybe it was just 28°C, maybe it was a hellish 55°C, we'll never know. also clearly the oceans do not work as a heat buffer and that is a shameand lastly the visual aspect of terraformation is... very underwhelming. At the very very end of the game you will see some of the ground turn green-ish but i was hoping to see trees, birds, fish and so on. nope. Oh so  you decide to respect the scale, game ?again, overall, this was a very nice experience, it truly feels like you're terraforming mars over a hundred years, i really like how you (as the AI) expand on the planet like some sort of blob made of robots and factories, starting small but eventually extending your tentacles over a good 3/4 of mars.EDIT: the way the worker bots function is strange, granted, but they work correctly. if your logistics are falling apart, it's either because you do not have enough drones, because they are placed improperly, . there is a logistics overlay that show the bottlenecks, build more drone hubs where you see red unless you think it's transitory.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Wait on it. The game relies on an AI that is completely incompetent.The game has massive potential and after a few patches it might be pretty good. As it stand now however, do not buy it unless you're a big fan of endless frustration. It's a game that demands efficient supply lines and base construction while offering next to no tools to actually achieve those things.Logistics are a total nightmare for even a midsize colony. Thanks for wasting my resources and worker load.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like Per Aspera. The UI and visual design is beautiful, with the sleek, geometric style being right up my alley. Playing an AI slowly discovering it's own will was an instant sell for me. This was one of few games that I instantly bought after seeing early gameplay and binged for hours at a time.Unfortunately, it's kind of a wreck. It's not playtested or balanced well at all. The worker AI is atrocious, likely as a result of workers trying to be boxed into specific sectors. There's very little the player can do to control the workers: a prioritize button button that can make a building suck up way too many materials, or controlling each resource's target output tasks with sliders which honestly doesn't seem to do much. It's way too easy to just get stuck in this game, where one can spend all of their starting resources in the beginning playing around or later on when scripted events and random meteor impacts alike can cripple a base beyond recovery without much the player can do about it, and that's even before the military-defense component is introduced. By then, a base can get bogged down so heavily that even if it has a healthy stock of materials and several key resources have redundant extractors and factories, it can be nearly impossible to get the Drone Factory and Towers up in time. That's even assuming it's not your first playthrough, in which you'd have no idea where to build your first Tower(s) for proper defense.As for the story, it's clearly suffered for the lack of playtesting as well. Occasionally AMI, the AI that the player takes the seat of, will chime in to herself to reflect on the current events. Except, due to poor flag tracking, it will often not be the current events at hand. "I wonder if I should use the nuclear warheads on the polar caps?" she muses to herself after the player has already accomplished that. "The sudden base failure, was it a sabotage?" she wonders after the threatening transmission from an unknown entity confirms its presence and influence. It's quite a mess. The nuclear weapons mentioned earlier are framed as a quick method to go through the first terraforming step, Bootstrapping, which involves raising the temperature and pressure enough that all the dry ice at the poles completely sublimates and floods the atmosphere with a boost of CO2. The problem with this framing is that reaching for the nuclear weapons takes far more resources and commitment than a simpler alternative that requires just a handful of techs researched. All in all, I wish Tlön Industries the best. This was clearly an ambitious undertaking, and one that I hope in the future can meet up to industry standards. For now, I must recommend passing on this: it is a rough gem still entombed in stone and wants for far more polishing.
