_childDocuments_.review: This is a really great game, especially from a narrative perspective. Gameplay is motivating and addictive, also thanks to the way the developers make you invested in the story and your mission to colonize this planet. The AI storyline is a nice spin and its deeper than you would expect from a management game. But there are some really stupid bugs (Or at least I think their are bugs): - Sometimes the workers max is not equal to the number of hubs built. Saving and reloading fixes the problem- I am not sure if this is intended but I think not: The first mission of the spaceport, brining in colonists can not be halted or canceled. But there is only one spaceport per sector? How can I unlock the next sector if I can not halt the other mission when there is only one mission allowed at once per spaceport?- Also at some point suddenly all my workers were gone. Maybe there is decay on them and you just have to constantly put priority on your factory to produce new ones. But this was not really communicated like that. Maybe give the player a hint that your worker production/decay ratio is negative, because if you have a huge Colony and suddenly there are no more workers, you have trouble recovering from that.Edit: With almost 20 hours in and a complete restart of the campaign I have to add some things:This game really feels like an early access, there as just so many small bugs and things that don't work properly. There are so many tooltips missing and sometimes you really have no idea what some things mean, so you have to guess it. Most annoying is, that workers rather use the streets than my beloved hyperloops and makes them feel useless at points.I still had a lot of fun playing this game and I am curious where the story leads but I thanks to all the unexplained problems I probably won't play anymore for now. Maybe with a patch.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I would post a more positive review but the drone combat management is pretty bad.  I made the mistake of combining drones from several bases to take on the initial drone attacks from the SA-1 area and after the battles, there is no way to easily return drones to their respective bases.  There are no command options (supposedly u can 'shift' and designate a number of drone to split off, but doesn't work (at least for me).  Really disappointed in this design and makes me dread going forward with the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: It was a slog, but I managed to finish the game.  It's very much of a grind at times, and then a lot of just waiting for things to happen... even at 16x speed.  There were a lot of interesting and unique concepts, but the gameplay just did not allow them to shine through.  The lack of a proper tutorial was also very frustrating, and I found myself starting over a couple of times because I did not have enough information to make good decisions at the beginning.  The only thing that kept me going was the story, and even that ended up being disappointing.It was a decent effort by the developers, but some poor design decisions pretty much killed the overall enjoyment.Just a side note:  My game took about 93 Mars years to complete which is almost 180 earth years.  During that time only one in-game character aged at all.  She went from a newborn to 20's or 30's.  Also, Mars' light gravity allows rivers to run down one side of a crater (or elevation) and up the other.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Per Aspera is a wonderful game in concept but falls incredibly short content wise.Positives? The story is very intriguing and you'll discover more of the story and setting via dialogue and text as you progress the game. The layout and UI are simple and easy to learn and use while the overall colour and design of the game is quite easy on the eyes.Negatives? The game lacks any significant amount of content, with some aspects being very quick and others sluggishly slow, meaning there will be long stretches where you do absolutely nothing! You'll reach build limits quickly and your resources will build up quite quickly which means you'll achieve mission goals very quickly with limited difficulty. Research is incredibly slow and reliant on colonist arrivals, which is also slow, so you're waiting for long stretches of time for research to complete so you have something to do. With 3.5hrs of play time on a single run, nearly an hour of waiting for something to happen occurred, usually in 5-10min blocks. Long wait times isnt a new for long haul strategy games but there is usually some kind of fluff to fill in the space between major events to make the game feel fuller. Sadly this is absent from PA making the game feel very empty and not worth paying full price for. But that being said I did mention it had a good story so if you dont mind the wait its worth picking up when on sale
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: My favorite part of the game was the story. Lots of moral questions. Too bad you have to grind your butt off to get there. Most of the game is waiting for things to happen while having the game at 16x speed.As others have mentioned, the stage 4 and stage 5 terraforming takes literally hours. Finding new resources  is watching a bar go up. Doing special projects is "click start project", then wait. Populating new colonies is build it, then wait for people to move in. Getting new people onto mars, is start that special project then... you guessed it, waiting.The systems in the game hide enough information from you that it gets really frustrating to play. Simple things like how your workers decide to do things is mysterious. Let's say you deploy a new base somewhere else on the planet, and want to see how much iron it's producing. Well, you can't do that. The section tool only shows absolute values. So good luck managing that. Ok, later on you get said new base up and running, "oh did I remember to build a steel forge?" time to stare at that section of map and hope I spot it.I could whine more, but this game does have great ideas. I just wished I didn't have to wait for the sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I loved playing this game on Saturday evening while watching Netflix on the background. The gameplay might be simple, but you really start feeling the accomplishment as forests start appearing and Mars slowly changes into a green world and you end up with settlements all over the lunar surface. A great management sim.Also, my inner Mark Watney loved the focus on real science and hard scifi. The "Terraformation Plan" feels authentic to my layman knowledge. Combat, on the other hand, is borked. It feels like a feature added just before cutoff release to add a bullet point. You are only going to need military units on very few instances of the game. And their controls are the inverse of any other strategy game released in the last 20 years. double click to select, click to move, right click to deselect. I could not rely on my muscle memory to control units and constantly made mistakes on the few instances I actually needed to muster my units.Overall, very fun and very chill experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: If I could, I would give this a neutral review.  The story, voice acting, and visuals are all very strong.  The game really endeavors to capture the grandeur and mystery of Mars and it succeeds at that.What holds the game back is the gameplay.  To be frank, for a colony-builder / resource management game, it falls flat.  Sometimes I wonder if the devs playtested the game at all.  Even after several patches, the user interface feels cluttered, and it can be difficult to find relevant information to your tasks.  For example, at the beginning of the game you are limited to a small amount of total colonists.  But you won't know that unless you stumble across it in a tooltip or infer it from a tech tree research option.  If too many colonists show up and you hit the limit, colonists start to leave but the game won't tell you why.  It's that sort of baffling oversight that frustrates me.There's a distinct lack of clear feedback on what you should be doing to between major story beats, and the best ways to avoid resource problems.  The tech tree is a real let-down, as none of the researched options really change your core gameplay loop for most of the experience.  Most of the research boils down to "do what you were doing before, but a little bit better, faster, or deeper, but visually the same."  Big terraforming projects are cool - but they aren't exciting to execute.  You just assign the newly unlocked project to a spaceport and everything happens automatically.There are a number of other gripes and nits I could list that stopped me from fully enjoying the experience.  That's a shame, because the good parts are really exciting and enjoyable.  What tips this review to positive is the heart and effort by the dev team.  They've put a lot into post-launch support and it shows.  I want to see what their next project will be.  But I do hope that next project will strike a better balance between engaging minute-to-minute gameplay and story.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Similar to Surviving Mars, this game shines in that the map you are on is the planet Mars itself. There is amazing detail on both the topography as well as the sites where we have already landed rovers. Buildings in lowlands get destroyed as you raise the ocean water level -- a great touch and you really feel like you are there terraforming. The science is pretty realistic. Watching plants slowly expand across the surface of the planet is mesmerizing.It doesn't have quite the complexity as Surviving Mars and while the story is great, there's only the one campaign story (less replayability). However as a terraforming sim its by far the best I've played.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Outstanding.Fantastic soundtrack, visuals and storyline. Not sure if I was just 'lucky' or the game pacing is precisely crafted, because everything was timed perfectly.It feels like devs have dedicated a lot of time and thought, no only into the game itself, but into the 'experience' of it. With so many bland titles nowadays, if you really want to play something different, give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, although I'd very much say it's a work in progress and doesn't feel finished. I didn't finish the game as at the end it turned into a grind for resources and the logistical side was confusing. However, I enjoyed the hours I spent, and am curious how this game will develop. I'll be coming back for sure, the roadmap for development of this game promises lots of interesting stuff. And the map of Mars is beautiful!
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: It was released as an unfinished game. I had to quit because it was so broken. I waited for all the updates and yea they fixed a lot, but its still not a fun game. I love city-builders and resource management games, but this is just frustration on Mars. The whole backbone of the game, workers and their hubs, is a buggey ridiculous mess. This game is BEAUTIFUL! The story line is awesome with great voice actors. But the core of the game is just frustrating. Honestly I don't regret buying it cause it is an amazing 3D render of Mars.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Overall 6 out of 10.Good simulation game for the price.Story is ok but as you progress you lose track of whats happening especially the/in base.I dont know if im doing this right or not but my base is a cluster of icons that i dont know whats what anymore, i have to zoom in/out to find out each icon.The stages of terraforming doesnt tell you much about how to do it other than "do this/that to complete", somehow i manage to get to stage 4 but i have no idea how to complete this, there are buildings that tells you what are they for but their effect dont have much either you build a bunch of them (takes resources that takes forever to get/make) or you will take forever to finish the stages.Also, why is it giving me directives to investigate/research outpost or buildings thats hellllaaaa far away, how do you even get to them? build a bunch of worker hub, maintenance and power?
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Good game with a a great narrative. I'd pick this up happily for 30% off. The game is perfectly playable, some people just have a misconception of how many worker's hubs they should need. Rather than learning from this observation and just building more, or upgrading travel speed, they decided to review the game poorly.For those *not* choking on an infrastructure system where you literally don't even have to give orders, this game isn't just mechanically cool - it's *philosophically* cool.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: The game seems interesting to play, especially in sand box mode. I just began my first campaign mode in easy to get to know the ropes. There is some sort of enemy on the planet that sends out drones to attack. However, the algorithm the programmers put in have it attacking me faster than I can rebuild and faster than I can build my own defense or attack drones. I am spending all of my time defending and rebuilding only to have hundreds more come in before I can even rebuild what I lost in the last battle. If this is the easy mode, then I don't recommend this game for anyone. Easy should give you a chance to feel out the game and not be stressed to losing the entire thing in the first few years. You need to fix that problem or I will continue to not support this and give bad reviews.Part 2 of reviewAnother review on the game. I started a new campaign and go through the issues above. That story line is ridiculous as an AI is not going to forget something like that, but that is all I will see about it. Once I made it past that I then suffered catastrophic failure of all of my buildings at the same time. Part of the story and I get that. I had 146 buildings at the time and every one of them suffered. The problem I have is that it wouldn't build maintenance drones to fix those problems. I had 8 maintenance facilities and put them as priorities, I went 8 years game time at the time of this writing and in all of that time it built me maintenance drones only a handful of times and only 3 at a time. I started losing my worker robots so I took priority off of everything and set my worker factory to priority. My supplies were very high, but I went game time several months before it finally brought me 1 supply of glass to build another worker. Priority evidently doesn't mean anything to the system. Still in easy mode. It appears that the programmers expect you to fail, and if you aren't, they will make you fail. I am still playing to see if there is a way to beat these very obvious programming fails or to see if they will fix them in an update. I like the premise, just not the story the programmers want to tell. I won't change my recommendation until these are fixed and you quit taking the joy away from the game.I had for a moment thought to give this a thumbs up as they supposedly fixed issues. Turns out the core issues are still failing. Either all of the maintenance stops at the same time so you can't repair things for a long time. Or I have tons of energy one month and the next 100 negative and I didn't build anything. I look at the weather and it shows bright hot sun, so it isn't dust storms or sun that is causing the power fluctuations. Then when I look at my research speed, I have 235 people and I have 2 points per month in research being created and another time I have 35 people and 10 points. There is no logic. Unfortunately the research points per month go down just when I have to research the  military stuff, so I can't build enough drones to repel attacks and my place gets destroyed. I think I have played enough hours on this to say, they don't want you to win and will do everything they can to make sure your colony never survives, even in easy mode.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Wish there was more resources and power/maintenance buildings would have their range be 2x what they are now because that's really the only thing that annoys me about this game. Their range way is too short and hampers base building how I want. Also small piece of annoyance is I don't get why they hide information from you when you actually click on a building. Why do I have to hover to see what's actually going on with the building?Outside of that the game plays nice and relaxing. Haven't encountered any major game breaking bugs yet, just some UI funky fun on the terraform screen.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: This game is thoroughly unfinished. It's got some depth, but not nearly enough story to justify its playtime. The only reason for the difficulty system presently is to pad incredibly underbaked and unbalanced design overall. I wish I could speak better of this game. Buy on steep sale and to the devs: consider telling people this game is not actually finished, storywise, mechanicwise... anywise. This is pretty damning to your product to not indicate. It is inherently dishonest to call this a 1.0 product. The story just... ends with no resolution to much of anything, no credits roll, and no indication there is anything further beyond the tolerance of the player. I hope you eventually finish the game. As the product stands, wait until they release some form of complete edition, as there's just not enough to work with here for a fully conceived title.POST: My friend Erbkaiser's review is now up as I got him into this game. He made very different choices and got a very different ending to me, one with a credits roll I did not receive. I will update this again if I find out that there is difficulty-locked dialogue as that would just be absurd given how little happens in stages 3 to 5 with the choices I made.. He also took quite a bit longer than I did. I would say do not take any play time for gospel, it can vary drastically. This does not change my lack of recommendation until the devs fix some of that rather glaring issues with pacing. I would like to... but there are too many problems for me to recommend it. This can and possibly will change if the devs address and fix the issues, as I do intend to check it out again when the next major expansion drops in January.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun, but the UI makes the logistics a nightmare. The UI that shows resources, for example, becames completely useless as soon as you get a second settlement, because it only shows you global resources across settlements, not how much is in each settlement. This would be fine, except that there isn't any trade between settlements. So basically, you get a big number that means nothing. Like, I have 500 aluminum rn, so it looks like I'm rich, but one of my settlements is actually out of aluminum and I had no idea because nothing actually shows the local tally.Update: after completing the game, I have to say, I look back on my playthough with great fondness. Once I got over some of the pains of it being an indie game, I found it addictive. The story is great (and has interesting and meaningful choices that make me want to go back and play out the what ifs of going the other way on big decisions), and I loved that you play as a globe spanning AI rather than the typical commander.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: The game certainly does have potential, however it does feel like it is only tapping that potential and not using it at its fullest.With the story mode, I felt the game really made me engaged with the world and story that is unfolding as you terraform Mars. The gameplay also lends itself to be interesting and fun, however the game kind of really bogs down mid-late game. The limit of buildings, resources, and lack of variety pretty much slows down the game and it just becomes a loop of finding more resources. Combat does exist in this game too, however, its pretty basic and it just becomes a which side can outproduce drones and mass it all in one go. Really if I had a option to vote a middle thumbs, then I would go for it as this game is at best middle line. The story is engaging, but the gameplay is somewhat lacking in terms of options, and replayability. I will leave my recommendation as a yes for now in hopes of seeing a sequel that is far better.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Insipid. This game is insipid. The gameplay's thin, the design's clumsy, the scientific gloss flakes off with a mere fingernail's touch, and the writing - God, the writing! - feels like it came out of a mid-tier creative agency staffed exclusively by Reddit. Expect to spend most of your time with Per Aspera daydreaming about what a good colony-building sim with an AI-driven Mars colonisation story might look like while you wait for the game to stumble over its next boring revelation.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I got Per Aspera in a bundle a bit ago and figured I’d give it a shot as it seemed up my alley. Per Aspera is a fairly standard colony simulator except it has a story that is actually pretty interesting. You play as an AI who is tasked with terraforming Mars to make it livable for humans. It’s not the most in-depth story but it kept my interest and does have some interesting twists, which I was not at all excepting from a colony sim. The Story is fully voice acted, which is nice, although at certain parts of the game it can get annoying how frequently voices pop up to talk to you. Additionally, even at 16x speed, there can be times where you just sit there waiting for buildings to complete or tasks to finish. The game is also very poorly optimised. You don’t need tons of frames for this type of game, but it is annoying that I can’t even hold 30 fps when neither my GPU, or my CPU is maxed out. All of my CPU cores seem to be in use, but not a single one is above 70% usage, with most of them being closer to 40% usage.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great. It maintains it's pace throughout the entire game with an incredible sci-fi story. If you liked Surviving Mars you will like this.Just finished the game. Oh man it's sooo good. Please play it. To the Developer:Bravo!Make way/road upgrading easier, maybe drag and drop a circle and all roads in that area are improved? Make the space elevator more relevant. I assume it's like a hyperloop but at a global scale. But it's unclear in game. Population a little more relevant. Make me responsible for their happiness. Build parks, hospitals, schools etc to keep them sane. How many different endings are there? Can't wait for a sequel!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: The voice acting and story would be superb - if it actually played in a coherent sequence. The campaign is so poorly paced, unbalanced, and full of bugs that it's hard to imagine it was play-tested at all.The overall gameplay is quite fun at first, until the mid-late phase of the game turns your well-thought logistics network into a nightmare web of exhausted mines, inactive factories, and broken-down power generators. The game offers no way to automate or eliminate the micromanaging tasks that become extremely tedious over time, nor any tech options to reduce the sheer quantity of buildings that you have to maintain. The priority system is also extremely basic, and once you have 200+ buildings, it becomes impossible to manually assign priorities, turn buildings on/off, or even remember which facilities are located where. Lots of potential - could even make a neat multiplayer game - if the bugs & usability issues are addressed.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Its fun and I've played a bunch of it.Its a novel and interesting game in many ways - the integration of the narrative elements is probably the most interesting part - the second personality test is fantastic and the high point of the game.As per sci-fi tradition hte final wrap up isn't the strongest, but the rest of the narrative is excellent - i really enjoyed how you can steer the character you are playing as to get their personality to develop in different directions, i still dont understand functionally how that is implemented (and i build these kind of systems for a living) - its just a very interesting system.There are a few annoying characters, and some narrative missteps - i feel like a bunk of plot was awkwardly cut in the handoff between the lab lead and her daughter - in general managing all the loose threads of the open story gets weaker as the game progresses and there are occasional missteps.And it almost starts comically nieve but then deepens as it goes which is quite enjoyable once it gets going i was telling my wife some of the character lines and we couldn't decide if it was satire or not.The actual sim aspect of the game is also interesting and engaging, there are still some quirks in how the drones work (which is the real core of the game) - mainly that I'm not 100% on how long distance resource transfers are scheduled and how they interact with the hyperloops, which has kept me from having great success scaling colony's into the late game, but there are more recent patches and definitely more for me to know.I know one of the newer patches addressed some quirks in how mines worked that would have been my next comment.The only other complaint i would have would be a bit of a lull in the pacing right out of the gate when you are playing on the harder difficulty level - its clearly tuned for normal diff (which makes sense and is fine for this kind of game).All around its fun - I recommend to sim game fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: The concept of the game is fantastic. You get to terraform Mars. There are already hundreds of games out there that have that exact premise. But none of them have a well-crafted and fully voice acted story to go along with it. Terraform a planet is a monumental task and that really shows in the game.Which is also unfortunately the immediate and major downside of the game. I played the game on the free weekend for a few hours over the course of three days. But on the third day I was actually just browsing my phone while I waited for the game to complete certain tasks. My bases were able to sustain themselves perfectly fine so I had no intensive whatsoever to keep building more bases. So I just waited, and waited, and waited for certain events to happen. While waiting, the story also completely halts so there's little to no interaction anymore. Which is a shame because I really wanted to know how the story would end.In the end though, I think I can recommend this game although it's more of a "maybe" because I certainly had fun playing it up until the mid/end game.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Per Aspera is a really great game with an interesting story that unfolds during the course of the campaign. The game has been improved since its release with even the addition of a free DLC (Green Mars) or even a multiplayer mode.I recommend it for any lover of city building games as this one is a really good take on the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: At first, the game looks a bit boring and becomes a bit too hectic for the new players, and the world looks a bit dull...at first. Then you get engulfed in the the world being slowly terraformed with your actions, with a surprisingly enticing story that kept me wanting to learn more and more. I managed it in around 15 to 20 hours on normal difficulty, but know that this game will also have multiplayer soon (in time of writing this), and can realistically be expanded to other worlds / moons too, not just Mars.All in all, worth the money, and really fun. Highly recommended
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: The core concept here is really appealing. The high level concepts are good - terraforming, logistics, managing projects. But the execution results in a fiddly and boring gameplay loop. The story seems interesting, but not compelling enough to deal with the fiddly resource management (which isn't well explained and online guides suggest has some bugs still as well). It isn't bad, it just isn't good. In a word, I'd say bland.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: It was hard to decide what to say... I'd give it 3/5. It is almost more of an interactive story than a game. Everything is extremely easy, except for the tedious stuff. Upgrading things is way too annoying, especially roads, since there is no mass upgrade option. The resources are completely unbalanced, so only a couple kinds of resources are annoying to produce, and you just spam buildings for them. It is hard to call it a city builder when it is just narrative with an unbalanced economy. Since the game is 3 years old, I doubt much will change. I think they'd be better off either focusing more on narrative and getting rid of the complex micromanagement stuff, OR investing much more into the economy and challenges of actually building. The game has a lot of potential and interesting ideas, but it really isn't optimized at all. If it were a major studio, I'd definitely give it a thumbs down. Worth buying on sale if you are interested in AI and sci fi. Not worth it if you just want to build a colony.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Could be good, even addictiveHowever it is lacking key feedback elements for the amount of ever growing stuff to manageI end up frustrated, always looking for this an and that building/resourceIt needs a highlighting buildings by type feature and dependency route highlighting featureIt needs better feedback on important issues (like missing resources, destroyed building)It needs better priority systemAnd why do building icons disappear when you're close?!I don't want to play Where's Waldo!
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Pro:- nice way finding and management options. lot of charts and controll mechanism- whole mars as map- good story- nice grafic- "one more turn" effectcon: - not really a reason to play it again (but i had 55 hours fun, thats ok)- stupid enemiesreally nice game which i have  a funny time with. I played also surviving mars and if you like that, you will like Per aspera for sure also. Special gratulation for the amazing management functions, inovativ controll options and the overall more then normal feeling of playing a "think to the end" game.Little warning. In the beginning go strait to more workers, due to its otherwise little bit boring in the beginning.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: The game is definitely interesting for a few hours. The graphics are interesting and the zoom in / zoom out at a planetary level is neat.The core loop is simple and mostly mindless. You put a node on a resource, the roads automatically connect and your drones auto mine it. You place a few of the factory buildings out randomly to provide the next tier of resource, and then after that you put a few of the terraforming buildings out randomly. A large part of the game is waiting on research to uncap your building limit or unlock the next buildiing, so you put it on 16x speed and wait.Something as simple as making you manage the roads / logistics could have probably gone a long way to make the game feel more engaging.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game invokes the wrong expectations in people. For those expecting a Factorio level of logistical neatness, this game is not for you. Its systems have enough meat in them to justify its core gameplay loop, but not enough to make the logistical megalomaniac blush.What it does satisfy is the fantasy of terraforming Mars. The graphs and the systems that track your progress are satisfying to complete, and feel realistic enough to fulfill your fantasy. The story that happens in the background enriches this fantasy by inserting the game in a plausible conflict we may see in the future. Watching Mars slowly grow green as you carefully balance the elements is a treat that satisfies the brain of a very niche type of nerd. If you want that, buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Do not buy--until they fix the software bugs!  Because, right now, here's what you get when you purchase Blue Mars DLC: (1) game-killing lag through all phases of play and (2) a broken tech tree that doesn't let you research water-based capabilities.  The only thing blue about Blue Mars is how you'll feel after playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Rather enjoyable to see Mars change over time, I am happy enough to say this game deserves a thumbs up. Although, it has some flaws, it's easy enough to work round them. The hardest part is figuring it all out, and not over extending into the flooded area's like I did. It's a game where you can take things as slow or as fast as you like, and you don't feel any pressure.I've always enjoyed terraforming games, and I can say this is one of the more in depth ones. It's hard to compare it to games like surviving mars and the planet crafter, but Per Aspera was worth my time and money.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute gem!Graphics, sound, soundtrack, stats, complexity, gameplay, stoyline and game idea is a absolute gem! This is a gem I have had my eyes on for a while. I have thought "another indie with big ambitions" and havent really deared to dip my feets in my own big expectations. But finally I did! Now I can say one thing: Game is better than trailer =) Its so damn delicate and satisfying that I dont want to speed up anything. I just enjoy my micro adventure in the "slow pacey" (with really enjoyable music) and look forward to next space deliviery of colonists within some years (its kind of realistic).
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: On it's way to becoming the premier Mars Terraforming game, surpassing Surviving Mars.Pros: Sheer scope of the game, and fidelity to martian geography.It's fun!Cons:In my opinion, the storyline is the most hit or miss part of it, but I vastly prefer sandboxes, so I won't hold it against Per Aspera. The logistical system in the game takes some getting used to (and some downright trickery sometimes, and would be the only other area I would urge devs to improve.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Less complex colony-builder (city builder with a twist) than some others on the market. It is not assembly line simulator like Factorio or Dyson Sphere Program, so you'd not have to frantically scale up your production each time you research new thingy to build.There is a plot with several possible endings that depend on few (single digit number) of your choices, which are all actually surprisingly not bad at all. Was expecting much less interesting outcomes. SPOILER FOR ALL OF THEM: Gameplay is pretty standard for the genre - building foundation, getting first colonists - spreading their habitat, terraforming the planet. There is also a tiny bit of combat aspect - just making drone swarms in factories - sending them to guard towers and when attacked, responding with those drone swarms. Fight is on auto, so the one who got more numbers win, unless you have not researched defence\speed\attack for drones at all, that's the math of fights.Sound is ok, graphics is fine too, not most visually impressive game, but it does the job. The one DLC that's not free adds some new mechanics, that could help quite a bit, but as lots of ppl commented - those could very well have been in base game.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR - interesting plot (at least what I saw), initially fun, but AI seems to randomly fail to do what needs doing, and even when it is working the late game is slooooooooow.  Also the graphs and management system are often too high level making finding that one problem item/building in the mess painful.  Also, lotsa busy work needed.Main review:I was actually enjoying this game a fair bit in the early stages but once I hit late middle to early end game (Green Mars stage anyway) things just got silly...For starters, everything slows to a crawl as you wait forever for a counter to tick up to finally reach the next milestone.  It also gets fiddly as water consumes things near it and you have to rebuild on and off as it expands.  Unfortunately you need to build things like water treatment plants actually near water, which means they often get wrecked.  Why can't I build a floating or water resistance treatment plant?  Ditto for  other things that must be in or near water.But the real killer (like in Surviving Mars) is the AI just implodes periodically and given this is a hands-off management game that is a real problem.  When I gave up my run  I had a large number of buildings desperately needing resources or waiting to be built but they were not getting resource snot matter what priority I set them to.  Then the game decided (for the second time but I somehow unstuck it the first) that despite the above issue it didn't need worker drones so while I previously had ~80 of the things I suddenly only had 16-18, and none near where they were actually needed!  I also could not get them  to move glass - the core resource most of my stuck or broken buildings needed - even though I had 900 units in stock.  I built hyper loops to try and allow what few drones I had to move them from more distant stockpiles to where they were needed, but they just wouldn't do anything.So I got stuck with a bunch of dead buildings.  Technically I could have actually just left the game running for hours on its own and probably cracked the next stage as my atmospheric mix was (glacially) heading in the right direction and the colony was stable, but man, how boring would that be?  Not fun! Also the graphs and management system are often too high level making finding that one problem item/building in the mess painfulAlso, there is a lot of busy work.  You want to build some new useful buildings or setup a new outpost.  You will need to build all the basic support junk again as you are invariably out of range of the prior infrastructure base.  *Sigh*.All this is a pity, because the plot was looking interesting.  And early on, it does all work ok.

_childDocuments_.review: For AI you have no management options for optimization such as priority resources production and transport. No option that a road will spawn or not, upgrading a road that splits and uses part of the other road that has been upgraded will downgrade to upgrade again, or the portion that this does not happen will 'upgrade' at same low pace.I was hoping to see the big upgrades in animation, like space mirrors in action, or aerobreaking a comet trough the atmosphere. Nothing. The only thing I see is a Rocket launch for advanced landing sites and Rocket landings from other places, and a colony space elevator arrival. Go play Terraforming Mars a strategic tabletop and you will have more fun then this so called simulator. _childDocuments_.review: Voting No because there isn't a Maybe option on Steam.Per Aspera offers itself as a factory-logistics game wrapped up in sci-fi story of terraforming Mars. To this end you are Artificial Intelligence/Consciousness known as AMI, assigned by ISA space cadets to work the machines on Mars. The story features some interesting premises, and plays to them with a serious weight. I am interested in seeing where it goes, but I have not gotten far past terraforming stage 1.The gameplay of Per Aspera is where the blood is getting drawn.It is problematic in the kindest words to say, and crippling otherwise. The fundamentals of the game are as follows: you setup mines to gather raw resources, your workers then transport these resources to factories. Factories refine the appropriate resource, and workers take as the factory pops it out to wherever they're needed. Simple idea. Per Aspera has a ... bizarre way, of handling this throughput.Every worker needs a 'hub', every hub only has 1 worker. These hubs create 'traffic zones' around themselves automatically, and that hub will only work whatever is in its respective zone. Workers are soft locked to these zones, though they can step outside to do other tasks sometimes. So long as a complete production chain is inside one traffic zone, it will function without issue. When production chains are broken across multiple sectors, it breaks down quickly.Workers will transport materials through their traffic zones, leaving them at the border of another zone for that zone's worker to pick up materials. This 'daisy chain' is how material is moved for the most part throughout your entire planet-scaling base. However, workers must do all their other tasks in that zone, in addition to handling material transport. This can result in supply chains sitting stagnant for literal ingame years as the drones prioritize their zone's production facilities.Additionally, workers suffer from ignorance of how to work with cross-zone functions. Resource storage hubs act as overflow, however only the worker in their zone will feed into them for the most part. They can be neighboring a mining zone of 7 mines and none of the overflow will go into them by either zone's workers. There is no way to setup priority supply routing for central storage or creating 'factory areas', as the daisy chaining effect above simply prevents it. Similarly factories will starve of resources because they are too far from the mining locations and too many work tasks by other drones prevent materials shipping in. Supposedly this is not an issue, given worker load is 40-70%?These fundamental issues have left me a bit flabbergasted. As it stands I cannot really say the game has functional logistics, because it's a simple work queue that goes through its tasks without player intervention. The most you can do is 'higher priority' by one tier a building, where it is pushed to the front of the work queue always. This can cause problems as it greedily gulps down whatever it takes and starves other facilities elsewhere. Increasing drone count is seemingly the answer, but the traffic zones and their fussy behavior make scaling that up rather troublesome. If the zone is too small, drones sit around doing nothing. If it is too big, they are always busy working. If it is just right, they're still busy working in their own space.Perhaps there is some secret sauce I am missing, but even peering down the tech tree, looking at youtube videos, and so forth, I really cannot find it. The logistics model is not intuitive, communicates what it wants/needs poorly, and is hard to come to grips with. I am hopeful these issues will be addressed, for as it stands I am quite miffed at my purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a tough call, but after some deliberation went for a positive review, simply because the game has kept me nicely entertained for 15 hours.In the game's current state, if there was a 'neutral' review option I would have gone for that.As above, the game is entertaining, but there are some issues:- some things don't seem to be explained well (new landing sites, how to choose)- some UI issues (building population versus 'real' researched population limit)- some bugs (weird negative research values and some others that I can't tell if bugs or lack of explanation)Positives:- some of the best voice acting I've heard in a video game- graphics are very nice and you can really see the planet changing- runs well on my system (Ryzen 7 3700x with GTX 1070)- interesting story line and concept- good core game play - has the 'just a few more minutes' vibe...At this point, I will likely try and finish current game then mothball the game until patched further in 2021.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this game is designed very well, The  player assumes an AI role to terraform Mars by developing resources and building bases, etc. The "Base" building aspect is automated mostly in that the player just has to select the building and location, subject to constraining resources, and the interface automates the connections, "roads", etc.  A well thought-out aspect.  The graphics and voice acting are good and overall game play is straightforward. There is much to do with objectives to achieve, a bit of a learning curve as the game advances, options for terraforming, researching and overall management.Interestingly, the game also touches philosophically on issues concerning terraforming Mars and the role of an advanced artificial Intelligence in that task and in interfacing with human colonists offering the player chances to think and make choices related to these issues.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on launch because the demo left THAT much of an impression on me. Unfortunately, currently I can't recommend it for the following reasons:1. And for some reason you can't send resources from your main base to this offshoot, which was frustrating because my main base had the raw materials to spare.2. YongYea is a voice actor in this. On the realm of "this person is a toxic scumlord AND they don't bring any talent to the table" when it comes to voice acting in video games, this is somewhere between Ronda Rousey as Sonya Blade and whatever Jontron was doing in A Hat in Time. Seriously Tion It looks like there's a decent roadmap of content coming as of the time of me writing this, but how much of it is actually new content and how much of it is quality of life improvements that are sorely needed is a little unclear. _childDocuments_.review: Really wanted to like this game. I played Surviving Mars and didn't really enjoy the fact that it was basically just a city builder with a Mars theme. This game poses as a logistics science game with a cool narrative to drive it (AMI the AI). However the logistics/economy of the game just isn't that great. It also trips you up as you go along, with the pacing being wildly all over the place. Water levels started rising and flooded whole areas I'd hoped to mine with little warning - dialogue being somewhat out of step with events - long lulls in story progression with not much to do but wait for the badly designed logistics game to catch up. The story is ok, gets a bit cringe for me at the end and the directions your 'reflections' go are a bit tame/human. But early on it does pose some quite interesting ideas to you. But by the end its lots of A or B questions that deserve much more nuanced answers. I'd kind of recommend it for its story telling and visuals, and I'd like to see something like this again. _childDocuments_.review: I am very mixed on this recommendation. Overall, I liked the story, the characters were decent, and the voice acting was much better than I expected. The base building is very satisfying to see the end result with a fantastic visual aspect.That said, I am mixed because: the game itself is really wonky. You are ostensibly on Mars to terraform it, however that goal is secondary to your own survival. Most of the time I found progressing through the terraforming requirements wasn't important, and took my time doing it. This ludo-narrative dissonance wouldn't be so bad, except the way you progress in the game is tedious.All resource deposits run out, which means your only survival strategy is to constantly expand. Expanding is critical, as later game projects require too many resources. Setting up secondary bases, and then linking them to your primary base, is all you will do in this game. And the tools for doing that will leave you wanting. You will just power/worker/maintaince/storage walk in a giant line to the base you just slapped down to link them so you can feed your primary base.Each base you create? It will do the exact same bootstrapping process you had done from the beginning. Every single time. Managing production quotas is impossible, though there are plenty of tools for visualizing how your production is failing. Not much you can do to effect change.As the game goes on, performance drops, and the number of resources and robots you needs climbs fast. You need to constantly be expanding to afford all the projects, keep your colonists alive, and more. It becomes a real chore.Here are some improvements that would have a big impact:1) Remote bases are not fun to manage. Starting with more drones on a new base, linking power over greater distances, and having more starting resources on the new base (that don't need buildings) would reduce the repetition. 2) I want to set per-region resource min/max, not per base. Once I had 40 bases or more, I don't want to go through each to manually set resources max, or turning off the steel factory at each base that I needed to get that outpost through the bootstrap phase. Being able to define a "region" of linked bases and setting production quotas would help.3) The grind is too long. You need thousands of carbon, iron, and more resources for various projects. I wasn't even sure the defense network was necessary. The story hinted an attack would come, but once built, the network was never "tested", so it felt pointless. The space elevator was underwhelming for its cost.4) Space ports should be nameable, and clickable through the mission selector. The dropdown is too small.5) Managing pop influx was frustrating. You have a small window to remember to cancel more pop from coming in. You can "cheat" this by turning off the space port, forever freezing the colonist ship in place, and also locking up your space port. Just let me set a max pop or something and have the ship make its own trips, or anything than the current way it works which is frustrating.6) If I have hyperloops, why do colonists take extremely slow airships? Waiting for a colonist ship to spend *months* moving to a new, story required outpost (of which there are many!) is agonizing when I have a globe spanning hyperloop network that can transport water in a few in-game days.7) Upgrading roads is tedious. If I remove a building in between (so as to free up building slots), the upgraded roads are removed.8) Terraforming has no in-game benefit or drawback. It doesn't affect wind or solar output (shouldn't more atmosphere make wind turbines better? Solar worse? Should the mirrors make solar better?). Water on the planet isn't drinkable, apparently. Forests and animals aren't food. By the time you can get open air bases or whatever, the game is past its welcome in terms of grind, and the bases before then can support more pop than I can deliver resources to, let alone generate enough water/food/chemicals.9) Losing pop has no discernible impact on the game. If you starve your people, they just peacefully leave. No impact on the AI whose only job is to...make Mars for humanity. Yes, it makes research slow, but you'll be spending so much time grinding base expansions and other objectives that it doesn't matter. The characters won't even remark on hundreds of pop leaving.10) The only cool tech in the tree are space elevators and hyperloops. Everything else is underwhelming (or just simply required, and thus neutral). Military tech is the least inspiring. 11) New-game plus would be wonderful to experience the other stories. For now, it is too much grind.12) The required amount of sprawl, while obviously carries a strong story component, feels overly forced and annoying. It makes expansion feel necessary only for the story, rather than the stated purpose of your character, which is to terraform. I suppose this ties into the feeling that terraforming is only a goal, and loosely ties into all the events and things happening.I know I had a lot of criticism to provide, and I really did enjoy my time with the game. But I had hoped for more, and these many flaws prevent me from playing it again, rather than spoiling the experience I had.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful city builder/planet terraforming game that unfortunately has glaring issues in logistics and a ton of bugs. This game will, for seemingly arbitrary reasons, sometimes completely cease to function and you'll be forced to just accept it and have to remove and replace buildings from time to time to get things rolling again. There are plenty of features that are just completely broken and should not be used under any circumstances - these include Storage Chests and secondary landing sites. These will 100% break your production and are NEVER worth using under any circumstance. There are other features, like Hyperloops, which will increase productivity overall but require a restart every so often as they tend to get stuck bouncing items back and forth.The campaign has decent writing with good voice acting. I have no complaints on that front (so far at least, I'm at terraforming stage 4 at the time of writing)This game has plenty of potential as terraforming Mars into a habitable planet over time is a really enticing prospect to build your city around. Unfortunately the plenty of issues that are in the game that will frustrate you for hours detract from the interesting premise and makes this a difficult game to enjoy. I got this as part of a Humble Bundle and would not have paid for it normally, and I wouldn't recommend anyone else to do so either, hence the negative review.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played for 4 hours and I have had a *magical time of it*. The story so far is hauntingly beautiful, and full of self-discovery. It's pretty cerebral, but without being inaccessible. The art style is simplistic, yet I loaded up the game and gasped, as I realised my colony looked like a neural map- the more connections I made, the more Mars begins to look like a living, breathing thing. This game is going to have to *SERIOUSLY* have a terrible ending for me to not consider it one of the best, most engaging games I've ever played.10 hours in, I have to say the background music is simple, but soothing. _childDocuments_.review: If I'm forced to give this either a thumbs up or thumbs down then the scale just barely tips towards thumbs down. On a scale of 1-5, I'd rate this as 2.99.On a Scale of 1-5* Gameplay 4 - I did enjoy it.* Graphics - 2 - Would have been considered state of the hard 10 years ago. Low resolution and not a whole lot to say "wow"* Story line - 1 - plus, there are many numerous bugs which cause the game to crash. * Sandbox mode - 3 - very limited.* User Interface - 2 Very Glitchy, Glitchy and Glitchy!!! Did I say Glitchy? You click on one thing and the nearby thing is selected. Plus the controls are maddenly wonky, they just don't want to behave. I'd say they rushed this before release was ready and didn't do a whole lot of testing. Simple example of this is that when you quit, you can't save the game in the same stroke, you have to save first then quit and then it complains that you'll lose progress. Likewise, there is no way to reload the game without shutting it down completely and waiting for the horrendous load time. Other minor annoyances is a crude file name interface. On the subject of graphics, you would think that 4K would be in the cards. NOPE!!! And while I'm at it, when one zooms out, all of the artifacts get in the way of clicking on the objects underneath. Zooming and scrolling is messy. Plus, you can't look south. The other thing that got old quickly is the lack of icon filters. After more than a few hours of game play, you're looking at a cluttered mess of icons. Last but not least, no manual. I mean really? I guess that's because it's a foreign studio where they don't have English as a first language speaker. All in all, this game studios inexperience in game design shows. I've seen smaller studios produce a much higher quality product.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid game that makes you feel in control of terraforming the red planet. The amazing story and graphics are definitely the highlight while watching the oceans flood the world and plant life grow, while the basebuilding and logistics feel pretty average when compared to games like Civ, Factorio, and Rimworld.

_childDocuments_.review: For someone who is really into autistic 4x games this is one of the better ones I've played. While it technically isn't 4x, the city-building mechanics have significant overlap and the early game feels incredibly intuitive. As you unlock more tech and hit more story beats, more mechanics are added for you to juggle at a steady pace. While the difficulty never "spikes" it does add a constant and daunting difficulty slope that just keeps on ascending and challenging you to keep up. Fortunately there are time controls so you can speed up or slow down the game to match your level of immediacy, regardless of difficulty settings. Everything from the story presentation, music, mechanics and visuals are incredibly polished and high quality. For the asking price I could not recommend this game enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Props to the studio for making this game free to play for a weekend.  I read the reviews first, which were mixed, about 1/3 to 1/2 said that the basic gameplay loop was some variation on boring/grindy.  I really love the idea of this game, and so decided to check it out. [minor spoilers follow]I picked the second easiest difficulty, and was off to the races.  I didn't read any faqs beforehand, though I have played other basebuilding/"Mars" games in the past.I thought the tutorial was good up to a point, and then left everything to the player to figure out.  Using the journal/notes helps, and I suppose in this day and age the internet faqs are the best bet.The GoodI thought the opening sequence was excellent from a storytelling point of view.  There's a mystic/mythological feel that many classic Mars books talk about, and it became clear eventually that the writers/game designers were generally well read people.  The sounds, voice acting, and the look of a tiny little outpost settling on Mars were very cool.The PotentialReally this game has tremendous potential.  I found combat to be clunky, but not a huge challenge at below-normal difficulty.  A little tweaking here could add a lot.Visually the look of a city spreading across the surface is great.  Having real place names really made it feel like a tour/educational experience of Mars's geography.  The Grind?I play RTS games like Warcraft III quite a bit.  I took it as a challenge to try and 'macro' better.  That worked up to a point, that point being roughly when I got my first colony going.  At that point there were many conflicting directives as the story really got going.  Rapid expansion meant that stuff was just plopped down.  I had to run on x16 speed just so that research would finish in a reasonable timeframe.  It did feel that gameplay fell into a pattern of building the same set of structures over and over again, and there were moments (alluded to in the story) where it felt like this ugly blight was taking over the pristine Martian surface.  The story also felt... odd towards the end of stage 3, where I stopped playing due to the weekend being over.  There were echoes of HAL, and strange culty people.  The history of the past expeditions was also interesting, but maybe could have had a different mechanic?  I found it annoying that the process consisted of a 'rocket launch' followed by the same repetitive process of building a new base, occupying the research site, and waiting.  One of the research sites was underwater, and I couldn't figure out how to access it (and trying to lower the sea level by refreezing the ice caps just seems silly).Overall, I would rate this game about 75%... not quite my cup of tea, but could easily be someone else's

_childDocuments_.review: A fun automation game with a great story-line, though the transport network lets it down. With limited transport options and congestion problems the game drags a bit. Terraforming the planet is a delight and a fun challenge to balance, though with care and the guidance of the game I got pretty earth-like conditions on mars with mirrors, greenhouse gases and 20% oxygen / 80% nitrogen.It has really gorgeous and appropriate graphics, good UI and great voice acting. I couldn't stop playing it, it is quite relaxing and addictive. But having reached the end credits there were long periods with little to do. Much of the game is mechanically quite repetitive, building the same structures in a similar pattern but in different places.Most resources are found in shallow mines which cease to function relatively shortly. Most last about 20% of the game. This mechanic makes most of your early structures redundant as the game moves on. While that pushes you to expand to new areas, it is also somewhat tedious.You'll hit the building limit and need to scrap much of your base before you finish the game, clearing out old mines and transporters. Some building sites will get flooded as you melt and introduce water to mars. There are minerals and research sites you might lose access to (due to underwater) if you don't plan well.The game doesn't seem to use multiple CPU cores well. It also doesn't seem to render and simulate in different threads. This means you will experience frame drops as your factory grows into the second half of the game. That gets extreme if you accelerate time.The pacing is indeed lacking at times, fortunately there is a 16x time acceleration which (while running at 3 FPS lategame) helps a lot. I get the feeling that I was too efficient for the story-line, with the military aspect being trivial for me and the whole planet was green well before the end. Even a couple of military upgrades and every part of your base under the umbrella of a defensive drone hive made it a toddle.You will need to take care to stop production of certain items. Specifically Polymers and Parts (they look like cogs) which permanently use up chemicals (needed for food instead), carbon and steel. If you don't turn off Part production early on, you might end up with thousands of useless parts and none of the steel you need to survive. It would be nice if you could set global production targets, with reasonable defaults like 10% of all items (limit of 100 if you have 1000 items, etc). Perhaps all stores should default to a limit of 50 for each item.Terraforming with the bio-domes and their sea eqilivent are poorly explained. Look in the built-in help guide for details. The basic version is that every base should have a couple of these, preferably in the orange/red temperature zone. You'll find getting enough oxygen very easy once the planet has plenty of plantlife.I look forward to see what the developers make next. I really enjoyed the mix of epic story-line, relaxing automation game-play and the meta-progression of terra-forming.

They seem devoted to fixing the issues and making the game the best it can be and ignoring those issues mentioned, what's here is really fun. You get to slowly build up and the story kept me interested, wanting more the whole way through.Overall, I'd recommend the game but for those who aren't already interested in this type of game, waiting for a sale maybe be best.

_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend this game for what it is -- a fairly chill, fairly linear colony-building game. Unlike many games at its price point this is a complete and stable game with a moderate feature set and a solid presentation. I like it specifically because it doesn't take my full attention; it's not an idle game, as some reviewers have said, but it's absolutely a 'while watching a show' game and occupies the same cozy niche as desk Legos. Of course I would like a more nuanced and physics-based terraforming sim but I don't think that's reasonable at this price... the only major con for me is a poor UI (if there's something as simple as a way to select multiple buildings of a type, or get a list of all depowered buildings, I haven't found it). Certainly worth at least picking up on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: So at 11 hours I feel pretty comfortable and ready to actually try to take on Mars. It's a surprisingly crowded niche with 2 near peer competitors with the Paradox's one and the new early access one. This feels meaty and well crafted though. While I did enjoy the paradox version, this one has some passionate developers and doesn't feel as chained to the paradox dlc model. I have not tried the new early access one yet but I'm going to let it bake a bit longer while I get into this game. I feel like at 11 hours I'm scratching the surface as it is a very slow burner but with the improvements to UI I'm seeing the depth better, but just one small nitpick. Games should allow you to play peacefully if we so desire (Minecraft and Factario come to mind), sometimes after kids have destroyed your freshly cleaned kitchen you want to just chill and build with out anything kicking over the castle but the tide or the sunrise in the windows.  I look forward to where this game goes and the plans the devs have in store for post launch support.

_childDocuments_.review: A cracking game, really immersive experience, you can lose hours with this one.In my opinion a very accurate simulation of terraforming Mars, with a surprisingly well voice-acted story thrown in. The science is good, and will appeal to fans of Kim Stanley Robinson' Mars trilogy, also those who like the equally excellent Surviving Mars, and Terraforming Mars board game. This is perhaps a touch more abstracted than Surviving Mars, but has a more 'global' feel, however the true scale of the process feels more obvious here.One issue though - and I would say a significant flaw. I'm now about 30 hours in and have come across an issue that means I probably need to restart the game. This is not a bug as such, more of an issue with the reality of terraforming and how the devs have chosen to structure the tech tree. Without spoiling anything I'll just say that nitrogen needs to be a little more easily available at this stage of the game. I suspect this will be tackled in forthcoming balancing / new content however.All in all, currently a flawed gem - but I suspect one that will soon be polished to brilliance.

_childDocuments_.review: NOTE: I am heavily CONFLICTED on this game.It took me 31h to finish a game on simulation. Yes, that's ONE singleplayer campaign although the last 5h was spent on 16x (max speed) waiting for final terraforming process to complete. It could be possible that I just suck at the game or lost interest by that point.Combat:Story:There is a disconnect between time passing and the actual story. It felt like the story took place over months while the game time counter soared past 50 in my final hours. Do humans routine life over 100 in this universe?Interface and game play:I won't spend much time here. It's excellent. Downright excellent. The UI is a work of art and the stats and balancing of resource management is exceptional. Full marks.Time respect:Here is where I'm heavily conflicted on this game. I LOVED the first 18 hours. The 13 hours after that were a HORRIBLE drag, yet the skinner box design of short and long term goals with a dash of uncertainty kept me hooked long after I stopped enjoying it. Truly "Per aspera" lives up to it's name: "Through hardship". Conclusion:I value the experience, I LOVE the game design (UI specifically), but I hate that I spent 13 hours extra just to finish it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've finished one full game, and I'm unlikely to start a second one. Maybe after a few patches and changes to the mechanics, but that's a stretch. The concept is great, and the AI story/decisions is interesting. However, it's too unpolished in its current state. Lots of projects or items don't have useful descriptions, so you can't always make informed decisions. I won tonight by building something which honestly seemed like a stepping stone to other things. No save, no option to continue. Just....game over. The logistics system is incredibly frustrating, and you mostly poke at limited priority controls and hope that things get to the right places. In practice, your robot workers are stacking random things instead of delivering the things you need.  No controls for managing overproduction of any materials, outside of micromanaging individual factories.Resource spots run out quickly enough that you'll spend most of the game just building out to grab more resources. That's laughable at times, such as when you are scrambling to find ice resources while staring at a giant ocean.Many things on the tech tree are traps, where you really need later techs before you start using the ones you've already unlocked. That's most commonly when converting co2 to oxygen, where you need the nitrogen coming in soon, or some other way to balance co2 and oxygen. It's made worse by many of the space projects being broken - you can't repeat them without saving and restoring the game.Anyway, many aspects of the game just aren't terribly fun in its current state. It feels like early access still. YMMV.

_childDocuments_.review: I cant exactly pin down why I love this game so much. The peaceful cheerful sounds as the little robots deliver their goods to their destination. Logistics is handled by the game and you just build things and just give it time and it will build. I like that expanding harms the growth bacteria and trees. You don't necessarily want to build everywhere as that prevents growth. Nitrogen is your main concern. Trucking it it from Titan seems like the only way possible. I like how there are many cool sci-fi ideas on how to terraform mars that made me google and ask questions.Storyline: This was clearly written by different people at different points. It isn't cohesive and the characters aren't very believable. In one breath the AI doesn't like the idea of ISA using mars as a mining station and in the next is willing to rape and pillage Titan for its resources.(Titan is one of the only planets with liquid oceans of methane and might actually have life that is very different from Earth, a slim chance but still worth probing) There are 1000 inconsistencies or just stupid dialogue that makes no sense but suspending that the game is really enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: I am really mixed about this game & would say the negative points are more on a subjective level. Played it during its free week.Positive Points:- Absolutely beautiful story for a simulation game. Voice Acting is very nice and the story feels really good. The story is not intertwined mechanically into the game play, but it still doesn't feel out of place. The time that progresses works for both gameplay and story. It was really my main reason to continue this game. That said, it is not something unseen. Feels like a good doctor who episode.- It looks really good (Sadly the looks don't support the gameplay, will comment on that in the negative section)- It is fun for about 2 hours and then again when ressources get scarce. I played it on the recommended mode and the difficulty is on the lower level, but not totally uninteresting, it's definitely a game that you can let your kid play (minus the story).- Traffic System is kinda fun, once you see the logic.- New Game Mechanics unlock at the right time in the game, it was always the moment I was bored that something new got unlocked.- I love the historic stuff they put in there, would be great to get a bit more information on it. I also _love_ the lore they built, their world feels really round (Even though a bit black and white)Neutral Feedback (For me, these things were bad, but some people might enjoy them):-  It is definitely a slow game, I mostly played on the highest speed setting.- No micromanaging possible due to missing informations and options.Now to the negative. None of this is something that can't be improved, but I fear a lot of these are very major things:- My biggest pet peeve: You absolutely can't see what the different buildings are doing, even the icon overlay barely helps. This is something a lot of sci fi simulators have to fight with, and it annoys me a lot. There is no overlay for highlighting certain type buildings (This is _absolutely_ needed and I won't turn my review positive / buy the game until it happens. This is a serious threat!) and in general the UI is not really good. It looks good, every kind of overview/menu misses some information that you need to make a good decision. You also don't have options to e.g. upgrade all streets/ buildings of a certain type once you unlocked the upgrade via your science tree. If your mines are empty, you need to zoom in very closely to see that they are not producing anymore. You never have an overview over why something is missing - Did I just build a bazillion buildings that need this resource, or are all my mines dead? I guess I will just make a few new mines and never find out.Just give me some overview where I see all my buildings and other stuff. Every single other simulation game has this. This is really taking the fun out of optimizing your game.(*I didn't finish the story, which is partly about keeping information from the player, so it would be a great twist if in the end these kind of data are unlocked. But then hint at it more. This way is just frustrating)- Fighting is very basic (which I like!) but kinda unintuitive. Partly due to the reasons mentioned above; I have no idea why sometimes my drone armys combine and sometimes they don't. Still, due to fighting happening only a few times during the story, you're probably either completely overpowered (like I was) or underpowered when it happens.- There should really be side stories / interesting things that you can research or just... do while youre waiting for your ressources to fill up. Just make them textbased or whatever, but right now, research sites that are not relevant to the main plot are absolutely uninteresting, so these would be a great start. Right now, the game is a lot of waiting, and in later stages you are partly waiting for the plot to catch up to you. - Give me more speed. Please, a x32 speed option would be kinda needed. If you only drag out the time your players are playing by limiting their speed, then you really need to think about whether the game you made is actually fun.Right now, I cannot recommend this game. I would love to, I will put it on my wishlist, but until the UI is fixed, it's just not my game. The other issues, especially the speed, are definitely weird game design choices, it almost feels as if the game devs purposefully tried to do things different than in "usual" simulation games. But why tho?

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed the game.  The hardest difficulty was hard, but not super hard.  The writing is good and it has a good narrative and, good art.  Very few bugs, and only a few quibbles.  Well worth it if you are into Mars terraforming, or games like this.Quibbles:Pacing seems a bit off at times, especially tech cost balance, where sometimes they are blowing by way too quickly (early on), and then later there is so much waiting.  Ditto on the end game projects, I probably spent 4 hours just mindlessly clicking minimum.  They need to be simpler/quicker once you are there.  The game isn't really very respectful of your time at the end.Having the little points of interest give minor bonuses would be nice.  Would give the game some more flavor and give you some reason to go to them.  I did it for fun, but gameplay wise I think it is probably best to ignore them.Game badly needs an alert or goto for when a mine runs out, I spent at least a couple hours just scanning over mars for run out mines.  Probably could use some more serious external challenge at the end to.  As it went other than the first external obstacle, the rest were of only the most minor bother.Finally there were at times frustrating paths/priority decisions, when say a space elevator takes 1 month to fill up with 130/150 iron, then 5 years to fill up with the last 20 despite there being storage adjacent with hundreds of iron, and a thousand throughout the network.  I realize the pathing must be a pain for something like this where there are 10000+ buildings in global network, but it was quite frustrating and the priority system didn't do enough.Overall though really enjoyed the game!
