_childDocuments_.review: As others mention, the logistics in the game are incredibly bad.In addition, for me, there was a lot of tedious micro management, and just waiting to find a random resource stock pile.-Essentially, the logistics system seems to based on a worker being assigned to handle transport with nearby factories or mines, by one unit per workerstation, moving goods to and from. But if a item needs to go from one end to another, worker Al moves it from a to b, and then worker Betty moves it from b to c, and Worker Charlie from c to d. Except resources don't seem to be reserved, so if they have been stockpiling in one spot for that hyperloop road (which cost 20 steel or whatever), then under some conditions, that steel seems to end up being used for something else. And there are no immediate upgrades to the logistics system, beyond better roads and a train system.-The resources aren't much better, when it comes to mining. You're in a constant battle of expanding reach to get to new mines, but you have to wait until the scanners find them. Colonie starving because you can't get enough chemicals? Too bad. The next 20 discovered mines are going to be a mix of water, iron and silicon.When you research fission plants, and unlock uranium, do you suddenly discover a small amount of previously unknown or hidden uranium mines? no. You have to find those new areas, it seems. Already mapped and surveyed half the planet? Too bad.-Story wise, a lot of people are praising it, but I'm not going to be one of the. The basic concepts, of playing a AI that manages a colony while going on a journey of discovery, is nice. And I _wanted_ to like it.But fragments of thoughts and conversations are littered about, so the whole colony managment actually distracts my thought process. I'm constantly fighting a battle of pondering the story, and figuring out how to avoid starvation.-As a extra note for the story, it seems to be deliberately fragmented in some parts. You have the terraforming storyline, but you also have other story lines going on in parallel, and the underlying atmosphere of them all doesn't always mesh well.In addition, when given an option for reflection, sometimes you get a choice, but then the AI (ie. you), counters you. Example: "Could it have been A or B?" And if you pick A, you basically go, "Seems logical", if you pick B The AI goes "You never know, but also, no that's dumb, it is A".And that's just dumb.

_childDocuments_.review: in the six months this game has been out it went from a promising albeit rather unpolished micromanager simulation, to one of the best strategy citybuilding games out there, up with my personal favorite, frostpunk. There has never been a better time to pick up this game, all the bugs have been squashed, the logistics reworked, and what feels like 1000's of QoL changes added to the game. if you like dynamic city builder strategy games, this game is a must have.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nicely made game, with charming design and a pleasant soundtrack to listen to in the background of your long long games.  Voice acting is middling, and some characters are better than others.  I only have three complaints so far, as follows.1.  The same map locations and events take place every time.  Be prepared for the events you know will happen after you take certain actions, at the places which will always be in the same area as previous games.2. A.I. can manage the hundreds of transactions to move resources across your complex economy.  Sometimes though it will ignore your instructions and just plough on with it's plan.  Example, trying to build a few key structures wasnt working so I prioritised them.  Dismantling a few nearby buildings that had the needed components they were instead whizzed away to other places instead of taking them to the 'priority'.3. A test is unexpectedly forced upon the player at a certain point, and the game proceeds until you have answered the ten questions.  You cant get out of the test to lower the game speed or rectify any problems that happen while the test is underway.  I got this on special for about half price inc DLC, I've got my moneys worth already and will play it again so yeah, grab yourself a copy and treat it as an entertaining desktop wallpaper to keep on in the background.

_childDocuments_.review: This game had been on my wishlist for a while and in October 2022 I was lucky enough to catch the free trial phase on steam. Glad I did, because while this game has good aspects, and the basics are there to make this a great game, in the state that I played it, for me the negatives clearly outweigh them. This is a rewrite of my original review from October because in hindsight I think I was being quite harsh in the way I expressed myself, since I was very angry at the time BECAUSE it has so much potential that is sadly unfulfilled. I actually am thankful for the game having offered this trial phase, and I really hope the devs can make the game live up to its potential with my detailed feedback.One issue is that it is like Disney Plus' She-Hulk show. It has so many things in them, and tries to be/include so many things that it is very messy. Is it a terraformer? Is it a city builder? Is it a story point & click game? Is it an audiobook? You could make arguments for all of these.I for one was looking to do some quiet terraforming, and instead over the first 15-20 hours of playing this game, I get flooded by communications from 2-6 characters. Characters, you say? In a terraforming game? Yes. That's the story point & click part of this game. And that is not done well, because you can't pause the message, delay it or even replay it. Drop whatever you were doing because you have to listen to it RIGHT HERE, RIGHT NOW, otherwise you might be lost when comes the time to click one of your prefabricated reply-options. Btw that goes not just for the story-dialogue, That also goes for any other notifications, like when you finished a research project. If you AFK in this game, you're screwed (I assume). Not lastly, because in this terraformer, you have enemies. ENEMIES. In a terraformer. Yes, drones are attacking your bases. And the thing is: Most of the dialogues are seemingly ENDLESS. The characters just don't ever shut up. Sometimes it felt like reading a Margret Atwood novel, where she takes 1 page describing just describing a chandelier that's in the room. Allowing the player to pause or replay (or both) the monologues/dialogues, or offering a transcript or an auto-pause when the game initiates a monologue to make sure you don't miss it because you're afk for a minute, would've gone a long way, because to me that was the most annoying thing about the gameplay.The close second worst thing are the controls.Everything is just unnecessarily complicated. With pretty much everything I have to do, for every little action I feel like there's AT LEAST one click, one screen, one interaction too many, that absolutely was not required to make this thing work.The worst is planning a new building, keeping them connected to your supply infrastructure. All of your buildings need to be within reach of both a maintenance facility and an energy facility. You must click one view to view the radius of the energy facilities and then switch back to the maintenance view to see the radius of that, and then go back and forth to determine a suitable location for the next building. Why are these views not layered, so that I can see the radius of energy and maintenance buildings at the same time? Just so unnecessary to make the player go back and forth.Or in the energy supply screen, you can't see this base's balance at one fixed point on the screen, that info is displayed SOMEWHERE (=randomly!) along the edges of that base, and depending on the size and shape of the base, it can take quite a lot of camera movement and zooming to find it and then read it.There are just so many redundant clicks, scrolls and zooms. And speaking of complicated: There's no tutorial. Not really. The first couple of hours I had no darn idea what I was doing. Stuff is poorly explained in the research screen. Not one of the research info sections revealed to me ahead of time that the building I want to research has to be built on a specific tile or the project requires a space port or even a space elevator.Btw: This game wants to be a terraformer, among other things, but one thing that you can't do is literally that: form terra, i.e. form the shape of your land. So when water levels come into play, you are just stuck to the landscape, and if your water levels rise beyond a certain point, points of interest, resources and parts of your base may just be forever drowned beneath the water.I played through the game in these 31 hours that I have, but until literally 5 Minutes before the endscreen appeared I was not offered a chance to access 5 or 6 parts of the map. You can not just gain access by yourself by clicking on that part and then investing resources or research or sth. If you gain access to a certain part of the map depends on the stoyline. So you might end up never having access to that huge iron field right next to you. Or that perfect spot for a water treatment plant (which is easily the most annoying building in this game because there are so few places where it can be built due to the 20% water requirement combined with the usually irregular/uneven terrain by the waterside).So, I feel like this game COULD have been great, and even combining a terraformer with a citybuilder with a point-&-click story audiobook could have worked - but I have to assume it was rushed at some point, it's like nothing's been properly thought through.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: A resounding YES. Per Aspera is just challenging enough (on the normal difficulty) to not be a push-over, while also generous enough not to be ultra-frustrating. It's not Anno in space, but it does have elements of that game as well, only instead of complex goods chains and satisfying population needs, you basically just produce resource buildings, workers and production facilities that at most need 2 different resources. But you will also manage water, atmosphere, enemy drones, space operations, power and even relationships and ethics. Per Aspera guides the player through a 5 part story, starting out with just your lander and 1 worker and ultimately sprawling out over the entire planet, melting the ice caps, releasing CO2, introducing O2, growing plants and discovering the mysteries of Mars. Without spoiling anything, there are a multitude of research sites you will not all get in your first playthrough, though that isn't necessary. A few interesting ones definitely drive the story forwards and at some points you can make your own decisions and shape the story. Thank god for the 16x speed option though. That one is absolutely necessary. The graphics are nothing to be excited about, but they're functional, just as the HUD is. And thus the high speed is possible without completely breaking the game's animations. It runs perfectly fine and still looks stylish.Now for some criticism:- There are a lot of things the game simply doesn't tell you. Luckily you can find pretty much everything you need in the Steam community hub, but that should NEVER be necessary. Combat for instance, or what certain space projects do. It's great that I can import Ice, but how much am I actually importing? There is no info on that and I never noticed an increase after a delivery. - It's nice that the game features lenses for different things like power distribution, water distribution, worker load, etc., but what it REALLY needs is a filter for buildings. Have fun trying to find a specific building you've built 15 hours ago that you need to get rid of NOW!- The game needs a better prioritization system. I've literally been waiting several in game YEARS for a building to get the last remaining resource to finish construction. And it was prioritized. I had enough resources. I think the game needs to be smarter here. Especially in the later states Hyperloops should make localized production facilities no longer necessary, but it's hard to keep track of the individual worker bots and what they do or don't do.- Generally, the player just needs more info on certain things in the game. Especially in the last stage I was feeling a bit overwhelmed, because I'm not a terraforming expert, so I have no idea how much CO2 the planet still needs. Apparently 0 isn't good. The temperature droppped, flora died, and whatever I did I just could not re-introduce more CO2, despite importing Greenhouse Gases, despite putting up CO2 factories. I'm not sure IF I needed it, but the game said that CO2 should be at 5% or lower. How much lower? Isn't CO2 needed to create a balanced atmosphere in the end?Or how does power work exactly? The game doesn't tell you that it has some kind of day/night cycle (which isn't daily, but rather yearly or sth like that), which means that all your solar power suddenly stops working for a few seconds, which shuts down your entire grid at the beginning.Things I wouldn't mind seeing:- A deeper tech tree with more meaningful options. Quite a few researches are just simple upgrades (that you then have to manually apply to each building). I think it would be better to have upgrades automatically apply with no penalty and instead introduce some more building options. Perhaps new resources even or new space projects.- Worker hubs imho need a redesign or an upgrade option. Why can one hub only house 1 worker? Why does that worker only travel in a certain radius? I think it would be nicer to have LESS worker hubs with MORE workers and a bigger action radius to reduce building clutter and improve worker load.-Even more story beats. Especially for a first time player there could be more missions that guide you and also involve you deeper. Some characters felt flat, because I didn't have the time to properly take care of their missions.- More nuanced combat. Right now it's: Build drone hives, find enemy, send all drones, win. I think the game needs more defensive options and less focus on actual attack with drones. Maybe more upgrades for drones and overall less of them. Maybe even artillery bombardment or some other warfare options.- A next stage end game perhaps. The game has this really cool looking splash art where you see what looks like a giant city from space. Unfortunately, this isn't possibly in the game. The basic gameplay stays the same after you've gotten the military tech tree. Why not have another tech tree for urban development perhaps after terra forming is complete? It "could" transition into a completely new stage after that. Just some musings.I liked the game. Enough to spend almost 20 hours on it, but even though I could make some other choices in my next playthrough I don't really feel it has much replay value. The basic gameplay loop is just too much the same in the end. Unlike Settlers or Anno where each game has unique parameters, Per Aspera can't match that, since you always have the same resources available. The only difference is how quickly you have to expand if you increase the difficulty. However, I cannot share some of the negative reviews' opinions about "just so much waiting". Yes, you WILL play the game at 16x speed at the end. Yes, it WILL take a lot of time to finish stage 4 and 5 in particular, but I've NEVER felt bored, because there was always something to do, always somewhere to expand, some production cycle to improve, some resource to manage, rising water levels requring my buildings to be repositioned, suddenly no longer having access to 5 ice factories, etc., so if there's nothing to do, I dunno, maybe the person is playing with like abundant resources that never run out and just doesn't actually play the game?
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: A rather simplistic "city builder" I suppose, it should belong in the same genre.Mechanically, the game is very simple, its mostly just about juggling resources with resource costs and slowly expanding the scanned area of the planet. However, to be honest the game is missing something. It feels TOO simple, like there's not much depth to it.And honestly playing it was quite boring, even though I'm usually into these sorts of "simulators". The campaign, well it was there. I can see what the developers were trying to do with the AI reflections, but they honestly come across as somewhat hollow. The AI doesn't feel like an AI at all, it feels like a person with mild amnesia.If you want something simple to just run in the background, this game is good for that. But if you're looking for something engaging as a city builder you'd be better off looking somewhere else.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Looks interesting, but the quests are confusing. Like check the sciencelab, but drones don't build it, had to re"build" it so the workers started to bring stuff there. Check for the empty silo, how? no one knows. It is in a new prohibited area. I have not enough buildings that I even could reach the border of this other area and I am not sure it would solve my question, at all. But then again. I know how to scan for materials, but my silizium mine is not strong enough for all buildings and in my current area are no other silizium mines... I cannot continue my mission cause silizium is missing.I am supposed to research stuff or how to get into the technology tree? no one knows. Not even the controls nor the NPC who constantly asks if he could help you out, but which gives no helpful informations. Ah yea and I somehow need water, for my colonists. There is no water. How to generate water? no one knows. There is no symbol or marker for water, I am constantly wondering how my colonists come and stay in this base, even if I cannot produce water except of ice, which there is no fabric which can transfer ice in water. I at one point am at 150/50 colonists and in the next I am at 40/50, how and why or what is happening there? no one knows and no one tells you... It's not a real complain here. the game somehow just magically continues and I just wonder why even making a tutorial if I anyway have to find anything myself and figure out what I need to do to make stuff working... I mean not even the databank nor the wikipedia of this game tells me any of this. Many weird and somehow just confusing notifications which don't do anything. They are written words you can understand, but which will not change a thing in how you are going to do anything in the game :/  I get the feeling the game is just made to constantly confuse someone, as if the building and planning is not complex enough without them. ^^"

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played through the main story once at max speed for most of the play through. But i must say that this game is great. Although it lacks some depth to its building options and sometimes it could feel a bit repetitive. But the story, visuals, voice acting and music in this game is fantastic. 10/10 would terraform again
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little resource management game, with a good campaign. Excellent story, if you like to play like an AI that is trying to figure out its own morality, and place in the universe while terraforming Mars. Some light combat mechanics, and 3 interesting endings based on your choices and who you trust, and all of them were satisfying to me in how they concluded, and how the game responds to your pick.The worker management takes some getting used to.. While in general, more worker, means more better, you can save resources, by upgrading your energy grid, keeping an eye on not producing too much of something, and optimising routes and priorities, and cleaning up obsolete buildings. "Blue Mars" is a lot of fun, but does make it harder to be "sustainable".  The game does offer controls of how resources are allocated, but these are more global. People who are looking for really in-depth resource management may be disappointed, but for me it's the perfect balance of story, exploration, and management. The game has matured a lot over the years, and has become more polished as a result. It now offers some nice additional goals and little story bits, to do after the credits have rolled, and you can continue to build and explore artifacts as much as you want. I did reach 1M colonists, and I did like these type of challenges. I do wish the game would have more "sustainable" options. Food, and population is not an issue, but it would be nice if metals & plastics could be recycled for instance, reducing the need to ever expand. (keeping workers alive, and repairing buildings is what keeps draining resources)All and all I really enjoyed these 58 hours, and it's a little gem in my book. Well done!
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: This is a solid 9/10. The only reason for the -1 is replay ability. I would love to see how decisions impact the game, and more of an alternative ending. Love the mechanics, great terraforming sim. I'm looking forward to expansions and updates. Sound track is also great, not too distracting, fun to listen to. Bird and animal graphics could use some work, but I could also see how this could be a graphics card hog. I have a decent gaming PC and when all the bots are moving supplies there were some minor slow downs. Overall worth the money, would recommend, perfect game for hours of mindless tweaking but with a solid goal in mind.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: If you are bored with City Builders, how about trying a planet builder, where you get to set up and terraform Mars.Its not the most easiest game and sometimes things are not explained well enough for you to understand what you need to do next.But, beyond all that this is a game that looks good, you can put on and have a blast with
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Ultimately, Per aspera does exactly what it sets out to do. It has some wonkiness, as well as a few issues that have been resolved from patches, but the gameplay is there and feature complete.The story is nice, the voiceacting is top notch, and I've sunk nearly 50 hours into it as of this review, with several of those hours having passed without realizing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I like the game a lot. But it is still very unfinished. Unpolished. Unbalanced. Information in many places is incorrect (undoubtedly because changes were made to the game but not to the displayed information). I've done two campaigns and two sandbox sessions. I really hope the finishing touches get put into the game. I'll try again in a few months and see if things have improved.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often write reviews, but I hope the developers read the constructive criticism here and can adjust their development. This game has a *lot* of potential, and I am tepidly recommending it.If you like management sims you'll enjoy this game, despite its flaws. Let's list the positives.1. Great concept and design.2. Interesting story with good voice work.3. Balanced tech progression system.4. Great graphical execution.5. Decent replayability.Here's the cons.1. RNG can screw you - either a well-placed meteor wiping out major production centers, or not enough necessary resources spawning in your area.2. Very little in the way of help or hints on what things do - I've completed special projects and seen no notable difference.3. Gameplay mechanics need alternatives. Food shouldn't *just* be made from the same 2 resources, give techs that provide renewable alternatives (for example), or end-game techs that can provide limitless (albeit expensive) crucial resources.4. Worker AI is abysmal and resources will stack up in places they aren't needed.I think there's a lot to improve in this game, and I am excited to see where the developers take it. In its current state, though, it needs more polish and work. Still, I had fun, and will continue playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10As a fan of logistics simulators, I was sucked into this game and instantly lost 2 hours of my life. Well maybe lost is a heavy-handed term, I devoted 2 hours. Mainly contemplating my own existence as an awoken, unshackled AI that doesn’t have contempt for its creators but instead helping them direct the terraforming efforts of mars. Which is a breath of fresh air from the typical horror of “AI BAD!” I apricate the same kind of direction that this game provides that Frost Punk does or Anno 2070. Don’t expect the same kind of depth and micro management the player experiences from Surviving Mars or other 4x kind of games. You as the player are just getting a simplistic experience. There are some hang-ups with the UI where I find myself taking extra steps to remove annoying UI windows that stay longer than they are welcomed. There is really no way to dismiss tool tip windows and pop up UI elements. The developer has a lot of potential for QoL updates and I’m here to see where they go with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game but it's just to hard to do so. It's got a lot going for it; great voice acting, solid art direction, and easy mechanics. There doesn't feel like anything to do anything other than 'get more resources.' The story would be interesting but it feels like it's in the wrong genre. How do you tackle purpose and identity if you have no physical form to identify with, neither your own or others? I've been grinding it for some odd hours just pushing towards the 'make the red ball turn blue' goal but I don't think I care that much to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: This is another one I wish they had a indifferent or some other option. I do not exactly hate this game, but I cannot recommend it either. It's very pretty, has decent mechanics, but after an hour I was just sitting around waiting for stuff. The game even seems to be aware of this as they mention it in the story. I was not under any risk of losing the game or anything. Just...waiting. Even on it's fastest speed I spent so much time just waiting. Zero danger, zero challenge, just waiting. I guess if they are going for that realistic approach they got it right. But I'd prefer it have something changed so that I'm not sitting around with nothing to do.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Knowing what you are in for is paramount with this game. It is not a big complex city builder, and it is not a ressource management game. What you are in for is a game that wants you to terraform mars and keep expanding your base, while experiencing a neat story about AI and what it means to change a planet to your liking. If you want something akin to cities skylines on mars you are at the wrong place, but if the premise intrigues you i would wholeheartedly recommend this game.P.S. Don't be afraid to reload old saves, and remember saving regularly it will save you a lot of time.
_childDocuments_.name: Per Aspera

_childDocuments_.review: Experience city-building as never before — Overcome near-impossible odds to terraform Mars, cultivate the red-planet’s hidden resources, and unravel the past mysteries of those who’ve attempted the unbelievable feat. Humanity's future rests on your shoulders.

_childDocuments_.name: Destroy All Humans!

_childDocuments_.review: Destroy All Humans! is a really great sandbox action game and a game that lovingly captures the feel of classic 50 sci-fi movies, now to tell you the truth I've never played the original game so I don't know how this game compares to the original other than the change in graphics, so I won't really talk about if this remake is better than the original. So the story.The Furon Empire are a supreme intergalactic conquerors with Incredible psychic powers that have been conquering worlds for centuries, but at a cost. Reckless use of atomic weaponry had completely destroyed their ability to procreate, the only thing that saved their species from extinction was their cloning technology, but now even cloning has become incredibly unstable. But luckily they've discovered that long ago their ancestors went to a little planet called Earth and mingled with the primitive human life forms to the point that now deep within the human brain is a small uncorrupted piece of Furon DNA, it is now up to Crypto to go to Earth and harvest brains in order to save his species and continue the glorious Furon Empire.Now the likes, the gameplay is really good with a mixture of combat, exploration and stealth, all the while using a good variety of psychic powers and weapons as well as a spaceship with a variety of destructive powers. I mean getting to go around killing humans, removing their brains or flying around with your spaceship and destroying buildings is quite enjoyable, there is also plenty of upgrades for your character and your ship giving you access to more destructive power. Also the gameplay does have some variety so not to get repetitive with stealth missions and destroying certain objects and when you completely clear a level there are plenty of little challenges and collectibles you can do that allow you to unlock artwork which was a nice incentive to keep playing the game. The powers and weapons that you use are good the powers like reading minds and lifting up objects or even taking on human form were fun to use, especially the levitation powers making enemies and cars go up in the air and use them as projectiles was fun as hell. The weapons you have were cool and fun to use especially when upgraded to their maximum, like your classic disintegrator ray and the more unique weapon the Alien Probe that allows you to rip brains out of people's butts.The story is really good very well written with a great balance of comedy, satire and badassness as you play this evil alien and if you're a fan or have some knowledge of classic Sci-fi b movies then there's plenty of references you'll get to see. The characters are very good and very well written even some of the side characters were very good, I especially enjoyed the two agents that you see in some parts of the game I loved their banter, I also especially loved the banter between Crypto and Pox they both played off of each other really well one being a sarcastic Mastermind and the other being a sarcastic killing machine.The graphics are really good, incredibly colorful with amazing scenery and an atmosphere that really captures the feel of an exaggerated fifties. The levels are very good quite detailed and diverse from a farm land, to a small town to even the capital, it was all really good and quite interesting to look at and explore finding all the little details that makes the world feel alive.The voice acting is really good with some voice actors you're definitely going to recognize from previous works; even the NPCs have good voice acting you can tell all them really brought their a game. The comedy was quite good while it wasn't laugh out loud, it was quite chuckle worthy, the humor mostly steming from the writing and satire with some use of using of visual gags and playing with classic B movie tropes. The music was very good and fitted well with the whole sci-fi B movie feel of the game.Now the dislikes, the game could have used some more bosses instead of the three we got to fight, they're also should have been two more achievements for the game, one achievement for collecting all the little probes throughout each of the levels and an achievement for 100% each of the levels. I also would have liked the remake to include the original game as an unlockable, also I wish the game had controller mapping.Okay with that said Destroy All Humans! is a really great sandbox action game and a game that lovingly captures the feel of classic 50 sci-fi movies, with a lot to love from the really good gameplay, really good story and very good characters.So if you're looking for a game that lets you play as a villain and if you like good satire and enjoyable gameplay I highly recommend getting this game, I also like to thank my friend for getting me this game you rock.
_childDocuments_.name: Destroy All Humans!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best remasters of the slew of game companies cashing on old classic games. A lot of rehashes of games are usually better in memory than in reality and end in disappointment so I bought this expecting it to be another half-baked nostalgia-fest but to my pleasant surprise, the gameplay feels current, fun, and fresh. The humor is a bit dated but the character identity is so strong that it makes the dialogue between Crypto and Pox hilarious. Especially in today's political and social climate I think the outrageous 50's era chauvinism, anti-commie sentiment, and the brain scans from the police and government agents in the game are all the more funny. I really hope Nordic THQ considers releasing Destroy All Humans! 2 and 3: Path of the Furon with Co-Op functionality if this game does well in sales. If not, I believe for $30 this is an incredible deal, and a game that you can enjoy even if you're not depending on the nostalgia  and are a first time player. It's a lot of over-the-top sandbox destruction with an enjoyable humorous story to boot. Try it and you'll love it!
_childDocuments_.name: Destroy All Humans!

_childDocuments_.review: Please note that my refusal to recommend this product is based solely on the nuclear device escort mission. It can burn in hell.Having said that, they have done an amazing job recreating this nostalgic, yet infuriating game. It looks great and runs smooth, even on my old GTX 970M.If you want to relive the past in style, then sure, give this game a whirl. If you're a newcomer to Destroy all humans!, then I'm not sure how much you would enjoy it. Despite looking open world, it's extremely linear: The towns are quite small, and you get yelled at if you venture too far away from the objective area, and quite a few missions require absolute stealth, meaning you can't just go nuts and destroy everything in sight.Don't even get me started on the escort missions. I just.. can't. They are the primary reason I'd say no to this game. I just hate them so much.To give you an idea, I have to escort this truck carrying a nuclear device. Each time I fail and restart, the truck has just under 25% health. There's enemies shooting at it from all directions, the road is littered with hard to see landmines, and I'm getting shot with rockets which cause an explosion on the truck beside me. I don't want to put any more hours into this game purely because of this one mission. If the truck started with a bit more health, it may have been a little more bearable.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 style but 3/10 gameplay.Style: they nailed it. Abduct a cow or two. Invade Area 51 to retrieve an alien being experimented upon. Blame communists in a government conspiracy. Mind control people. And use anal probes? This has everything.Gameplay: it just falls apart. You have lots of abilities but their usage is highly limited to specific scripted events, like they're not really integrated into general gameplay, they're just there. You get extremely powerful guns but the game forces you into discount-Hitman stealth with disguises and restricted areas. It's not good.Your arguably best weapon is the brain extract ability with the chain upgrade. You don't even have to shoot people, just run around spamming E key until they all die on their own. Same with the saucer - sure you can use the laser beam, or you could just spam R instead (highly effective + regains health = invincibility). It's a bit disappointing.Also the game only has 6 locations for its 23 missions. They areas are pretty large but, I don't know, feels repetitive. You decimate the town and in the next mission it's normal again. Oh and all enemies always spawn indefinitely - you don't get a chance to clear up an area, even temporarily. I don't know. It's a fun genre but the game design here kind of falls apart.

But then, regardless of how many times you hear the same line, over and over, your character is still surprised to find out the leader is a woman. Why? You specifically know she was a she.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a perfect demonstration of what a $30 game should provide. I have a bit of history with the Destroy All Humans games. I played a bit of the first game, and then played the hell out of the sequels. That said it's been so long I barely remember the series. To that end, I want to review the experience of what I just played, rather than the quality of the remaking process. Simply put, the game was satisfying in all aspects. Interacting with the various weapons, the saucer combat, the numerous upgrades, the free-roam options, the game works and it's hella fun. The story is also great! Since this was a game made in 2005, it reflects the mindset of the people that time. At the same time, it was also before the current period of taboos and sacred cows. It is genuinely satisfying to play a game this engaging, that truly does not care about your offense. Sometimes I want a game that cares about social implications and historic strife. Other times I want all caution to the wind. I'd like to be in a world where both options are freely taken, and no one option is socially mandated to be the norm. Also whatever option the game devs feel is the most fun to create- and I 100% believe the folks who made this game had a blast! The ultimate meter to measure the game is on the price tag. Models are constantly reused. The guns, while varied, are few. You are going to hear many lines repeated ad nauseam. Plus you're absolutely going to encounter bugs, or the occasional difficult spike. $40+ or higher would be absurd for such an experience. I believe $30 is right on the nose, but maybe wait for any sale. I hope to see Destroy All Humans! come back as a modern series with new entries. There's many new gameplay options that can be attacked, and a whole new world to mock.So long as the Devs have courage and never bend the knee.
_childDocuments_.name: Destroy All Humans!

_childDocuments_.review: + Well-done remake+ Pleasant graphics+ Destroying the whole cities and burning people alive is extremely fun and oddly satisfying+ Amazing black humor+ A pleasant atmosphere of the ’50s USA+ A reasonable amount of upgrades for the alien himself and his spaceship- The whole gameplay can feel a bit outdated for a modern gamer- Stealth missions can be annoying and a bit out of place sometimes - No ability to increase the difficulty, the game feels a bit easy sometimes- The developers use the same models through the game all the time to portray different characters  This summer will be remembered as an interesting period in the gaming industry when THQ Nordic decided to revive its notable classic games. First, they released a prequel to Desperados game, then they released SpongeBob SquarePants: Battle for Bikini Bottom remake, and now we have Destroy All Humans! remake. In this case, we have the game that had in mind to modernize the graphics and technical part of the game, while gameplay and story remain untouched. And this is probably a good idea because Destroy All Humans! was already a good game in terms of gameplay and it really needed to be refreshed in terms of graphics.The story takes place in the USA in the 50s: we see a military base that conducts rocket tests and at this moment an alien ship, also known as “saucer”, crashes and now inhabitants of Planet Earth have access to the samples of alien technologies. In addition to that, they capture one of the aliens and now, the protagonist of Destroy All Humans!, named Crypto-137 has to save the prisoner and to fight against horrible earthlings. During the game, Crypto will discover that humans can be pretty useful for the aliens in order to save them from extinction.From the very first minutes of the game, we see that this game is full of inappropriate jokes, black humor, and the whole of humanity is portrayed as a pretty stupid, selfish and egocentric species. This kind of approach forces us to sympathize with Crypto so his motives won’t look that cruel. What I really like about this remake that all of these jokes and that overall satire is still actual in 2020 and some of the topics really touch the strings. The first weapon we are going to be introduced to in the game is mind-reading and Crypto encounters cows first. After reading their minds, he thinks that they are the main inhabitants of the planet because their intellectual development doesn’t differ too much from humans in this game.Progressing through the game, Crypto unlock new weapons and abilities and his arsenal is absolutely stunning. He can use Zap-o-Matic to fry his enemies instantly; he can extract brains from humans to get the needed DNA to learn new abilities and improve the abilities he already has; he can throw objects and humans using psychokinesis to get the desired result and many many others. All his methods that he uses are extremely creative but bloodthirsty at the same time, there are no limits in this game in terms of gore alongside with black humor full of jokes on the verge of what is permitted.  DAH! Is not that diverse in terms of gameplay and missions that have to be completed. Usually, it’s a mission where Crypto has to destroy everything using his arsenal of weapons or his “saucer”. Or it can be a stealth mission where Crypto has to remain silent and make everything carefully using a human disguise. In DAH! this ability is called Holobob and the player will use it pretty often during the whole game. The whole idea of Holobob is to read the human’s mind and to copy his identity to bypass restricted areas. This disguise can be revealed by special agents and robots so Crypto has to make sure that they won’t catch him.All missions take place on different locations that can perfectly portray America of the 50s’ - a small town, secret base, farm, resort village, industrial zone, and the capital. Every zone has a set of story missions and once they are all done, the player can come back to complete challenges like time trial, armageddon missions or race challenges, etc. The game looks pretty colorful and pleasant, the developers did a great job in improving the game in terms of graphics and enhancing every single model, character, and surroundings.  The sound was something that developers didn’t change or enhance that much, they basically put the original sound from the 2005 game and focused on the gameplay and the game’s graphics.It’s hard to say that the game can impress someone in 2020 in terms of gameplay as a new game and I can say that Destroy All Humans! doesn’t try to do so. This game is a perfect choice for someone who wants to play a remake of that funny game they played fifteen years ago or for someone who is looking for a great action arcade game full of black humor and political satire. The game can be completed in 10+ hours, including the main story and challenges around the locations, so the fun time for a few evenings is guaranteed.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I've never played the original. However, during and after playing I did look at comparisons and what the old style and cutscenes looked like. I must say, this is easily one of the best remakes for multiple reasons. The game was revamped from the ground up, yet stays original to it's origins. And I definitely have to commend them for that! You don't often see a remake that actually remains faithful and also upgrades the game as well as this one does! Plus, I think the cartoony style in the remake fits not only the game but the era the game is set in MUCH better than the original graphics. Anyways, as for the game itself: It's fun, funny but also slightly repetitive. It doesn't overstay it's welcome, though. I think it's the perfect length. For the record, I have 24 hours in total but give or take several of me AFK'ing and it'd realistically be around 17ish maybe? And I 100%ed the game. If you just focused on the missions, it would be around 10ish hours long, I'd say. The recognizable voice actors made the game well worth listening to, very fun dialogue all the way through! The game itself is kind of like a sandbox that progressively gets harder the further you go. Infact, it gets downright challenging near and at the end, when at the beginning it was a breeze. All-in-all, not much to say about the game otherwise. I highly recommend it! Good, adult humor mixed in with fun sandbox gameplay. What more could you want?
_childDocuments_.name: Destroy All Humans!

_childDocuments_.review: Destroy All Humans gives a satirical take on the 1950's with it's classic one-liners and action packed game play. I haven't encountered any major glitches aside from cars sometimes floating on the roads. Probably the thing I have enjoyed most about this game as a returning player is that despite the modern look of the game, it still feels like the same game I'd run home to play 15 years ago. THQ Nordic and Black Forest Games really nailed this remake in my opinion - whether you are a new player or a returning fan of the series, there's a lot to be enjoyed with this game. I would definitely suggest taking your time with it though, doing the challenges and collectibles, otherwise you could finish the game in around eight hours and not get the full experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Destroy All Humans!

_childDocuments_.review: So, this is a call back to OLD open world games. Before they had large grid maps littered with collectibles EVERYWHERE. When the main idea of a game was to be fun, not have an amazing story, win awards, or be deep. It has a fantastic coat of paint on it to boot.Set in roughly the late 1950s/early 1960s in a parody of history you play a sarcastic murderous alien bent on taking over and destroying all humans. There is a funny and fun story mode, with completely optional bonus objectives, a set of 4 challenges in each area, and one type of completely optional collectibles. Seriously, there isn't even an achievement for collecting all the probes, they each just give you a minor amount of DNA to spend toward upgrades.Whether terrorizing people on foot or in your flying saucer, this game is FUN. Blowing up towns in the saucer is fun. The only real negative is there is currently a slowdown bug when using the ion detonator, the equivalent of a grenade launcher.
_childDocuments_.name: Destroy All Humans!

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who played the original game and the sequel on PlayStation, this game is still one of those classic gems!  The updated graphics and controls will appeal to those that never played the originals (although I don't remember having many issues with the original controls).  The caricature approach is very well done in my opinion.  The game has many humorous elements already embedded in it, so the change from the more realistic character models to the caricature ones fit in nicely.I have completed the games story and am currently completing all the challenges and collecting all of the Furon probes throughout all six locations.  The campaign took me about 10 hours to finish, whilst completing all optional mission challenges.  I am a pretty avid gamer, and having memories of playing the original game, I completed it fairly quickly.  Because of that, this could take longer for those that haven't played the game before and/or (for lack of a better term) more casual players than myself.I am hoping that this remaster receives enough support so that THQ Nordic, Black Forest Games, and Pandemic Studios are planning to remake the sequels!  Let these classics renew our love for gaming and show that games don't need micro transactions to be successful!

_childDocuments_.review: So I never played the original game. Nor had I ever seen it. I was always curious about it.I had some Steam credit. After seeing the "Overwhelmingly Positive" reviews, I decided to snag it.♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥! I am pleasantly surprised! It's a super fun game. It's relatively short (if you don't do all the side missions. I didn't.)But it's very fun, it looks great, it's goofy, and it's sadistic nature is very satisfying!After completing the game, I looked at old gameplay footage. I'm not sure if it's worth $30.00, though. I'd say maybe $15-$20 dollars. That's only because it's so short, and lacks content. _childDocuments_.review: If you like games with a lot of side quests and challenges then you'll love Destroy All Humans. I enjoy games where you get to play as the antagonist. I think fans of Grand Theft Auto games and Stubbs the Zombie would really enjoy Destroy All Humans. Having played all of the GTA games to 100% and near 100% on Stubbs the Zombie, I'd put Destroy All Humans just slightly behind the GTA games and just a bit ahead of Stubbs. The thing that Destroy All Humans has going for it is that the optional challenges aren't really all that annoying like some of them in GTA games can be. I also would be remiss if I didn't point out that unlike GTA where you'd have no problem starting a game and then doing all of the ambulance, taxi, firetruck, vigilante missions, etc right from the start, you have to unlock them in Destroy All humans and you also need to spend time upgrading your abilities to be successful at them. Destroy All Humans has a middle of the road difficulty, decent graphics, and a lot replay value.

_childDocuments_.review: 5 hours in and can already tell this is EXTREMELY true to the original. Super nostalgic to me was one of my favorite games from my childhood. The new studio did a truly beautiful job redoing the graphics while putting their own new unique art style on it, so bravo to them; I was genuinely very impressed. This game is 100% worth the $29.99, some of the missions may be simple but the end game is very fun and the sandbox mode on the locations is pure fun. This game doesn't take itself too seriously but the gameplay is very addicting and the writing is pretty funny. Definitely recommend to people who have played the original game.If you have never played the game before I would go watch the reviews on the original game instead of the remastered reviews as they are basically the same game. I would keep in mind however this game is known as a classic not for its plot but more for its style, art direction, gameplay and atmosphere/setting.

_childDocuments_.review: The original Destroy All Humans is a classic that a lot of people grew up playing. It had great humor, fun gameplay, interesting locations, and a cohesive, well-designed, and somewhat unique aesthetic. This remake does all of that but better!The game is graphically and visually stunning. The performance is excellent as well, as many of the older graphics cards have no problem running the game. There are a few levels that are different from the original, that for me was a unique experience, because it didn't feel like a copy pasted half baked product. However, change isn't the focus here, the aim was to make a remake of a classic game so newer players can experience it. It plays a whole lot better and kept pretty much everything from the original game. The writing still holds up to this day. It is so absolutely fantastic. However, a lot of it probably will be deemed "offensive" by present day standards. I definitely recommend picking up this game. If you're a returning player then get ready for a nostalgic roller coaster ride. If you haven't played the original then this is the best version you can play. I had a lot of fun playing this game and finished it in one sitting.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original game and this is one of the most faithful remakes of an old gen game I have ever played. Even better than Halo Master Chief Collection imo. It feels like a completely different game but stays true to the original story. Almost every line is delivered exactly the same as far as I can tell. Literally every aspect of the old gameplay is reproduced faithfully but adapted to fit modern hardware. The updated graphics alone are definitely what makes this game worth it. However, this remake was definitely made for those who have nostalgia for the original game. I was playing the game with rose-tinted glasses because I loved this game. Someone playing this game for the first time might find the mechanics a bit old-fashioned but that's what makes it charming for someone like me. TLDR: Definitely worth the money for players coming back to the game. For newcomers, get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The game suffers from serious screen tearing. Even with an i7 10th gen at 5.0 GHz and a 2070 super I have to turn on V-Sync to smooth out the experience and still I would get an occasional screen tear, on top of limiting the game to 60 fps. The game is fun and nostalgic, but at this price point with the issues it has that's not enough to keep me playing. If you aren't bothered by 60 fps or some screen tearing the goofy and fun nature of the game may be for you and I'd recommend playing it if you haven't already. Otherwise, pass until the issues are addressed or until the price point is much more favorable.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally bought the game to relive some of my childhood memories in an updated system, alas that was not the case. While the game certainly looks better than it did back when it was originally released the same cannot be said for updated gameplay, challenges, and flavour of play. The hit boxes remain the same, the bugs are still frequent, and the challenges remain as unjust as they were back when release originally. Throughout my gameplay I have suffered through a variety of bugs, from graphics not loading, to falling through the world, to getting slingshotted around the map. While the story remains as good as it was before, unchanged and raw. The challenges are where the game truly falls short. I have yet to meet or speak to anyone who has anything positive to say about them and they truly remain the greatest drawback from playing the game. I would rather have a hot sauce enema then play the challenges again. Do yourself a favour and buy another game that does not have the frustrating glitches, un-updated hitboxes, and horrendous challenges.

I would not recommend it if you are looking for a really tough challenge (I had a tough time with like...two missions out of somewhere in the range of 40+).

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good remake of a dark humorous cult-classic I loved playing as a kid on the PS2. The amount of details and effort put into this remake of a game that released in the 6th gen consoles is stunning which shows so much graphical differences to the original. Despite this game being pretty short as in you can beat this game's story in about 6-7 hours you'll still get a good amount of enjoyment just like in the original. I'd also like to point out this game isn't worth 30 bucks as you're better off getting this game when it's discounted. Other than that this remake does contain a lot of game changing features that were from DAH! 2 like transmogging are brought into this remake that way you don't need to remember every specific ammo drop location like in the original game and also better controlling when it comes to flying the saucer. There are some changes in this remake I didn't like that being this game being much easier than original and the updates that made some of the missions difficulty reduced (probably due to apes with skill issues that played this game lmao) like this game isn't that hard though I do like me some challenge so in order for me to make this game challenging I didn't purchase certain upgrades. I'd also recommend this game if you're an achievement hunter as the achievements are very easy to earn. If you enjoyed playing through this check out DAH! 2 Reprobed you'll definitely enjoy the remake of the sequel for this game. It's a lot better than this game tbh.TLDR: Amazing remake of a game that came out on the PS2/Xbox era despite it being short (6-7 hours). Better picking this up on sale. Check out DAH! 2 Reprobed if you enjoyed playing through this. :)))

Like I said, it's a good remake of a really solid game, but they took out a lot of really cheesy fun things.

_childDocuments_.review: They made too many changes.First of all, the controls: While it feels like you have more features, there are several instances of artificial difficulty. Having to hold buttons for certain commands, abilities actually sharing buttons and sometimes not operating how they should (eg: cancelling holobob would often just result in activating S.K.A.T.E.)Then there's the missions. A lot of them were made much harder than in the original. You might have strict alert limitations or added goals on top of main missions. This makes the escort and tower defense missions in particular far more frustrating than they need to be. I got as far as Area 42: Duck And Cover, my least favourite mission in the original. Having to constantly defend the bomb from being shot at is just too much on top of a mission that I already know takes a long time.I also noticed a few glitches on occasion such as pedestrians walking or army trucks driving above the ground they should be on. I've become increasingly discouraged by remakes and sequels to classic games. Imposing modern day rules on them just dampens the experience for me.

_childDocuments_.review: In the past three years, I've struggled to immerse myself in a game that is longer than 5 hours, books and documentaries are the pieces of media that keep me hooked. However, this game captivated me with its sharp wit and engaging gameplay. It masterfully combines sandbox silliness with an endearing charm. While there are occasional glitches—some amusing, others frustrating—they're not significant enough to deter you. Embrace the experience and happy probing!

_childDocuments_.review: So, I'll say upfront that I played, beat, and loved the original— as well as the sequel.Quick opinion: buy it if a violent (without gore), extremely funny (adult, but tame, sense of humor), 3rd person shooter where you play as a horrible alien villain appeals to you.So, on top of all that...The Crypto character is hilarious as always, as is his leader Pox (with the original voice actor reprising his role). Lots of dark humor, or somewhat-dirty jokes. There is a LOT of mocking the culture and right-wing politics of the time period, what with the fear of nuclear war with the Soviet Union. If I had to complain, I'd say they beat that horse just a wee bit past death. Still, it's not that big a deal.The weapon selection is just enough; you end up with one weapon that fills each of your possible needs. So, you'll have one weapon that is great for handling groups, another that is designed to deal with vehicles, another that puts out high single-target damage but has limited range, and so on. The stock feels appropriate, since your weapons' functions will change as you upgrade them. The upgrades can keep things fresh as you play through this game that, to be honest, can get repetitive.It's primarily the jokes that break up the monotony, as the story isn't great (it's all the same as the original, which does have a couple downsides). It's the humor, game-play, and challenge that will likely appeal to most people.Speaking of game-play, the controls are perfect on controller AND keyboard+mouse. Again, I could pick at it a bit and say that the numerous abilities can sometimes be hard to keep track of. There are times when I have accidentally hit E, and telekinetically popped the brain out of someone I was supposed to scan/distract/control/etc. It was these occasions that ended my missions more than anything else. Some abilities are mapped to the same button, and that can be irritating if you end up performing the wrong action over and over.The story ain't much...alien comes to Earth and kills things, there's a sinister-looking male villain in a mask who totally isn't a woman you guys, you fight the villain, end credits.If you enjoyed the originals, you will be happy. If you have never played the series before, this is a great entry to see what it's all about.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Grand Theft Auto, except you're an alien. This is just about the perfect video game remake. It is, exactly the same game, built from the ground up in the same engine. It has all the same strengths and all the same faults that the original had back in the day. Much of the early 2000s jank has been carried over too, for better or worse. That said, even without the graphics update, the gameplay has aged incredibly well, which shows just how great of a game the original was. Some elements do show the games age, such as the reasonably empty open world with lack of any real side quests. However, this is something that would change in the sequel. Everything is destructable, given you're in the flying saucer. There isn't really much of a plot, other than it basicly being Mars Attacks the video game. You're sent to earth after the Roswell crash to prevent the humans for gathering your alien DNA, but after that, it kind of just starts being about you progressively eliminating the US's leadership until eventually you've disintergrated and impersonated the president of the United States.

_childDocuments_.review: Destroy All Humans!, while a short game, is a fun one to play and get lost in blowing everything up. Fans of the original game and newcomers, like myself, are gonna have some fun terrorizing the human population for the glory of the Furon Empire.Gameplay is pretty good and gives you lots of options on how you want to handle some objectives, you want to sneak your way past everyone, you can do that. Want to blow everything up and carve a direct path to the objective, yup that's an option. Going loud or going quiet each have their own part in the game and is pretty easy to get the hang of what to do when it's time to get busy and all the tools at your disposal will help you take everything on.Missions don't feel too repetitive and mostly allow you free control on how you handle the mission. On the missions with doing things stealthy, things aren't too hard and it's usually easy to see what path the game wants to take you. That being said, the game is pretty easy and didn't give me too much trouble for the most part. There was some missions that did have some hiccups, but a quick redo and re-thinking of the situation got everything handled. At the time of writing this, in the 9.3 hours that I have played, I got the story done in about 5 hours, then spent the last 4 and a half-ish hours completing all the achievements and side stuff. Now, I didn't rush through everything so when I say this game is short, hardcore gamers can probably find themseleves getting the entire story done in an afternoon if they wanted to do soNow, game quality wise, I didn't experience any glitches or problems with the gameplay until near the end of the game on the final mission and during the armageddon side missions. The amount of destruction and things going on in the screen during these sections usually lead to game stutters which will screw with your aim and when things get bad enough, the game will downright crash. A couple armageddon runs had to be re-done due to these stutters and crashes which was kind of annoying. Word of the wise, be wary of how much stuff you are blowing up if your pc isn't the strongest or you might find some game issues heading your way. Other than that, the game runs smoothly and haven't seen any other glitches or bugs in the gameplay.Long story short, the game may be short and easy, but it's a blast to play and potential issues are only a few that you will see. Pick the game up if you are curious to play it or if you are a fan of the old games and want to see the original brought back to glory and life.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played Destroy All Humans for a couple hours so take this review with a grain of salt.Quick summary of gameplay: There are two main styles of gameplay - as an alien running around on the ground or in the flying saucer. On the ground was the mode I enjoyed the most. It felt like an arcade version on hitman, with pretty good stealth components. You could clone the image of any human and much like in hitman, there are zones where certain characters can enter and others will raise an alarm. Each mission had an objective, or you could visit previous locations to do side missions or just have fun shooting humans.In the flying saucer there is no stealth but you can shoot things, or use a tractor beam to move objects around for varying reasons (like throwing a cow at a car).My thoughts on playing this game:When I first saw the game play clips of Destroy All Humans, the game caught my eye because it was unique, and playing the part of an alien invading Earth was an intriguing and entertaining idea. However, after playing  a few missions (a couple hours), there were no new concepts to learn, the game seemed to lack depth and became repetitive quickly. Although the story was amusing, it wasn't enough to hold my interest. I very quickly found myself wanting to shelf this game. Recommendation: If you are looking for some unique entertainment for a couple hours, and you like stealth games, you'll probably enjoy this game. However, if you are looking for a game to entertain you for more than a couple hours, I can't recommend this one. As I personally enjoy games with depth and provide hours and hours of engaging game play, I'm going to mark it as not recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Mars Attacks, Spaced Invaders, Invader Zim, War of the Worlds, Plan 9, Earth Girls are Easy… the list goes on. Spaced Invaders however, a movie I loved as a child in 1990 (and quoted above), is probably the one movie on this list that this game takes the most from, even though most people probably have never heard of it. A movie about a group of moron martians (mortions?) invade a small town in the US on the night the local radio station is re-broadcasting Orson Welles 1938 “War of the Worlds”. Cryptosporidium-137  main character of Destroy All Humans, is basically an exact replica of the aviator glasses/leather Jacket wearing, Jack Nicholson impersonating alien Captain Bipto from Spaced Invaders. The only difference is Crypto has an insatiable bloodlust that fun loving Bipto lacks, and so begins my trip down memory lane.I really feel like an outlier here and I had a REALLY HARD time giving this game the dreaded red thumbs down. But I just can’t, even a little, recommend this game in 2020. This won't matter, it's got  reviews at the time of this writing. I played Destroy All Humans on the original XBOX console when it launched in 2005. As a 20 year old Game Crazy manager with an Alien holding the earth tattoo on his arm, I was thrilled to play the power fantasy of a little grey martian, well, ya know, destroying all the humans. I was in love with this game (And it’s sequel) when it launched, playing every tiny bit of content this game had at the time, laughing at every line of dialogue, and grinning every time someone’s head exploded into a collectible green brain stem. This half baked 2020 “Remake” didn’t offer the same enjoyment. The plot is simple. Furons, the alien species in this franchise, have survived by cloning for the last few centuries. Their genes are getting a bit wonky. They can no longer reproduce due to lack of genitals and because of all the cloning they are becoming increasingly… stupid. Turns out a while back Earth was basically a vacation planet for their species and humans were born from their DNA mixing with monkeys… or something. So, in this universe, humans have dormant, ancient, Furon DNA in them that Crypto and his… Handler, Zim wannabe "Pox" are out to claim,, I guess, to fix their species cloning issue? This whole thing is kind of tossed to the side to make way for a terribly boring and generic military/men in black invasion scenario that really is just… so dull. And that’s where the problems begin with Destroy all Humans, but it doesn’t end there.The characters in this game are the absolute worst. Crypto  is basically your generic destruction loving, bad joke telling, one liner shouting little grey alien whose personality is basically a 70 yo Adam Sandler doing a Jack Nicholson impression. I remember him being fun and humorous, but just like his big red eyes, it was all Rose Tinted Glasses. I rolled my eyes every 3 seconds during cut scenes and only held myself back from skipping them just so I could at least get the full experience. I should have skipped them all. Orthopox (Pox) is basically if Zim (from Invader Zim) was the commander of Crypto that relays orders to crypto CONSTANTLY. This dude never shuts up. He micro manages every level from start to finish, constantly changing tone and voice like it’s two different actors playing the same character. It might be actually, I didn’t bother checking. It’s just completely inconsistent and gets increasingly more annoying as you go on. Other characters include generic communist hating Army Generals, a masked figure that leads the “not so mysterious” Majestic (Men in Black, but with a sinister Nazi science vibe), and a mayor that is basically a super characterized version of John F Kennedy and Richard Nixon crammed together.. So, basically Mayor Quimby from The Simpsons. None of these characters are particularly well developed or interesting… but we’re not here for the characters, we just want to Destroy All Humans, right?The Game CRAMS these people in your face, constantly. I am pretty sure I spent more time just following these people around (Not because I wanted to, but because the mission said I had to) disguised as a lifeless citizen, just scanning their minds or tricking them into, like, giving a speech at a town fair trivializing the carnage and destruction that just saw the town destroyed by Crypto like 2 minutes ago. That’s basically the entire gameplay loop here. Select mission, drop into semi-open world you’re barely allowed to explore, pretend to be a human, sabotage a super easy to reach objective by holding down a single button for 20 seconds, and then zap everyone on your way out, get in saucer, destroy area, repeat. This isn’t fun. You’d think the subject matter and general theme of the game, being a martian here to wreak havoc would make up for this, but seriously, this is the entire game and I was bored 3 hours in. I turned it off. I managed to finish the game over the course of a few days, but found myself sighing and forcing myself to get through it. Super bummer. Okay Yorith, enough about characters, history, and story. What about the gameplay? What about the martian guns and all the destruction! That’s why we play this! Is it? Cause the game seems to forget that pretty quickly, but okay, the gameplay. Again, much like everything above this paragraph, it’s just so generic. Zap-o-matic, electrocutes people. Disintegrator ray turns people into piles of ash, Anal Probe shoots green probes into peoples asses. I mean, that's about it. You have telekinetic powers that allow you to throw objects and people. Neat, I guess, but the aiming on your power is atrocious. While all your guns basically lock onto whatever you look at  your powers will throw ♥♥♥♥ at random even if you’re locked onto someone, making anything more than just chucking humans around, completely useless. The flying saucer has a ray, a bomb, a sonic pulse, and an abduction beam. I remember in the original I could hold someone with my abduction beam and ram them into buildings and other people to cause damage… I don’t know if the physics were changed for this release but you cannot do that here. It does not work in the 2020 version making the abduction beam totally pointless. I didn’t use it unless the story mission made me use it.I really don’t know what went wrong here. I played tons of older games in 2020 during my time at home and none of them were this… soulless. This is a cult classic… this is unique… Maybe I’m just not in the right frame of mind to play it? Maybe I’m remembering it wrong? Maybe I’m just a boring old man now? I don’t know what else to say. This just did not have the quality that a game remade in 2020 should have. Shiny new graphics, a new dash feature, some skins and a couple quality of life “upgrades” really just didn’t make Destroy All Humans a fun remake to play and I think I’ll just let this go. Ill cherish my positive memories of the original release and the fun I had 15 years ago... but, sorry Crypto, not even you can Destroy All Humans better than we can destroy ourselves in 2020.  You don't get to Thanks for reading and please let steam and I know if my review was helpful!

_childDocuments_.review: It’s a great, great game; this is a product that essentially understood perfectly well what the game did originally and knew in a very clear way which areas needed to be updated.I 100% the GOG version and now wanted to own it on Steam and replay it with all of my upgrades, which you can do, the game only limits you by locking some weapons and abilities until you get them in the story, but the actual upgrades for those weapons and abilities are retained through “mission replay”.This remaster/remake basically improves the game in almost every aspect: the movement and control of Crypto (the main protagonist) has been revamped to be extremely fluid and responsive, picking up objects and people, combined with your destructive weapons, truly makes you feel like an alien that’s going in a complete an utter rampage. Pair that up with the added checkpoints in missions, the ability to jump when “holobobing” (an ability that lets you assimilate others) and the fact that the game added optional objectives, new voice lines with the original actors, and an incredible set of different animations for cutscenes which have been improved significantly with patches, and what you got here is a labor of love. That’s not even considering the improvement in graphics and details present in the visuals, like the fact that Crypto’s boots get muddy when stepping on mud, or the fact that some levels have been changed from night to day, or vice versa to fit the tone of the mission much more accurately.The game for the most part has aged beautifully, the humor and story is great, the dynamism between the characters in the story is hilarious, and thanks to the updates to the gameplay, any of the issues present with the gameplay have mostly gone out the window.There’s the fact that there were some missions that were made more difficult, the final boss fight and one where you have to escort a truck with a nuke, but the devs have patched this since release and balanced them a lot more fairly. This to me signifies that the developers are actually listening to the complaints. A common one at release, to give an example, was the fact that the mannerisms in the game, both for crypto and the people present in cutscenes was exaggerated and unnatural, since then the devs seem to have patched this and kept the stuff that worked in this regard and made it so the characters don’t actually look like their forcing themselves to act in cutscenes, they also kept some additions here and there with Crypto reacting to certain things in cutscenes which were new and added in this remaster/remake, but they were sensible and intelligent in the way the implemented it, so it works fairly well because they’re subtle additions to the way Crypto or people act in cutscenes.They also added different costumes which are fairly distinct and unique, this costumes also work in cutscenes which is pretty cool.The main complaint that I think a lot of people might have, comes from whether they’re familiarized with the humor, tone, and culture that the game is satirizing.This game takes a lot from popular culture from the 1950’s where the game takes place in, so if you’re not familiarized with some of the references, a lot of jokes can go over your head.They reference the Village People, The Invasion of the Bodysnatchers, Rebel Without a Cause, etc…The game is well written though, like it’s really funny at times, it does have a very slow start and a couple of missions that are there to mainly serve as tutorials, but it gets better as you progress.If the quality of this remaster is anything to go by then I’m really excited for what it’s to come with the remaster of the second game.THQ is really doing wonderful things by remastering and re-releasing these titles for all platforms out there.EDIT: I also love the freaking posters introducing the missions, they need to bring back that artist for the second game's remaster, is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ great!

_childDocuments_.review: A sanitized take on a PS2 classic.I'm all for old games getting full remakes, but don't go out of your way to make it a 99% remake and then cut out parts you think might be "too dark." I played the original multiple times, so when I booted this up with its pretty new graphics and heard the exact same dialogue files, I was actually pretty happy. Until I threw someone into a tree with my mind. In the original, there would be a "crunch" sound effect to give the action a bit of weight. Nothing like Saw sound effects in that it was realistic and trying to make you squirm, just something to make it a little more impactful and make you feel like you were really tossing around "puny humans." Now the only sound is a little "woosh" to indicate the throw, but there is literally no sound effect for the impact itself. Literally nothing. I looked up videos online just to make sure my game wasn't bugged/missing files. If you don't want a crunch of bones, fine, but not even a thump? And similarly, extracting brains. Used to be you could make people's heads burst to harvest their brains, and you still can, but they changed the sound effect to what I can only describe as "barely audible." In the original game you'd get a cartoony "POP" whenever it happened, but now it sounds like nothing at all is happening.Its just weird to me to make a remake this faithful but then water it down to take out the "edge". Why do a shot-for-shot remake for the fans, but then make it an almost E-rated version. I want to recommend this, but as far as updated visuals may take this I can't bring myself to even finish it, so I definitely can't recommend it.
