_childDocuments_.review: "Destroy All Humans!" a 2020 release from Black Forest Games, is a remake of the classic 2005 game with improved graphics and features. The game lets the player take on the role of an alien named Crypto, whose mission is to invade Earth and extract human DNA to save his species.Pros:- The game has good humor and satire, making fun of the Cold War era but some may find it distasteful.- The gameplay is enjoyable, providing a variety of weapons and abilities to use to fight the humans.- The graphics and sound design are fine, the voice acting is surprisingly good while music is quite bland.- The game offers a good amount of content, including main missions, side missions, and challenges.- The game does a good job of capturing the spirit and style of the original game, while also improving on it.Cons:- The controls can be a bit clunky at times, especially when flying or using certain abilities.- The game can feel repetitive after a while, as the missions and objectives are quite similar in structure.In conclusion, "Destroy All Humans!" is a solid remake of the original game, providing an enjoyable and humorous experience for fans of the franchise or newcomers. While it has some flaws, the game's strengths, including its humor, graphics, and content, make it worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: From start to finish, it's been an absolute blast, filled with humor, action, and a delightful satirical commentary on our society. First and foremost, the gameplay mechanics are top-notch. The controls are intuitive, allowing for seamless immersion into the chaos of extraterrestrial invasion. Whether I was zapping unsuspecting humans with my Zap-O-Matic or wreaking havoc with the Anal Probe, every moment was an adrenaline-fueled joyride. However, what truly sets this game apart is its brilliant satire. The game cleverly lampoons various aspects of human culture, from the absurdity of consumerism to the hilarity of government bureaucracy. The witty dialogue and absurd scenarios had me laughing out loud countless times, making each mission a memorable experience. Moreover, the attention to detail in recreating 1950s America is commendable. From the retro aesthetics to the nostalgic soundtrack, every element contributes to the immersive atmosphere, enhancing the overall enjoyment of the game. In summary, "Destroy All Humans" is not just a game; it's an experience just like it was back in the day, where I used to play its PS2 version. It combines addictive gameplay with sharp wit and social commentary in a way that few games manage to achieve. Thank you for creating such a fun and thought-provoking masterpiece. I eagerly anticipate future installments and can't wait to see what hilarious adventures await Crypto-137.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, this game is a great remake of the original and worth the purchase for old fans, but also a great experience for newcomers. The biggest amount of effort has clearly gone into the overhaul of the graphics which are now in a stylised from but this works with the setting and tone of the game and has been done very well, the best evidence of this being the unlockable concept art that shows the original asset from the first game and the redesign next to each other. This effort has not gone to waste and the game's environments and effects look great in-game, simultaneously looking new but not changing things to be unrecognisable compared to the first game. The other main addition are new gameplay mechanics that while not significantly altering the gameplay loop from the original game, are a nice addition for returning players and brings the game up to what modern games are expected to have, like optional objectives, the dash/skate ability, Skins and the Repulse-O-Tron etc. Also worth mentioning is the good support for both controllers and MK+B with the ability to seamlessly switch between the two just by pushing a button on either, which also immediately updates the HUD and prompts. Personally I find the controller the best given that's how I played the original, but both are useable.There are downsides of course. In technical terms the cutscenes are a bit lacklustre with an often noticeable lack of ambient sound or score that makes things awkward, and the lipsyncing  in these scenes can sometimes appear off? I'm quite paranoid about audio and video being out of sync, so this may just be me. While no means bad, the audio effects in gameplay also seem a little less punchy than they should be, but this is very minor. Also annoying is the saucer gameplay in the new game. Mainly, the most noticeable issue is the rather low ceiling for the saucer which was obviously present in the original as well, but because the graphics are much more detailed and there are no technical limitations to justify it, it becomes more noticeable. The Repulse-O-Tron I also found difficult given the relatively small size of maps and the ability to lose the prompts in the chaos of destruction which pairs badly with the introduction of the drain mechanic for recharging the saucer's shields into the remake. Also, as far as I can tell the extras from the original game have been dropped which is a shame but hardly a turn off for the game.Ultimately the development team deserves as much kudos for what it hasn't done for what they have done. Namely, they have NOT dropped any of the dialogue or altered the tone at all and deserve praise for this decision. The game's tone and parody of 1950s America is undoubtedly the best aspect of the game and soul of its experience, and being able to experience it as an adult and actually UNDERSTAND the references and jokes is honestly one of the best parts of the remake. They have also amplified this tone by writing the Furon Handbook entries in the same tone and style.In conclusion, this game is a fantastic remake and should be upheld as an example for future remakes: A complete technical remastering that extends far beyond just updating particle effects and raising texture resolutions, the maintenance of the original's creative content, and the addition of just enough extra mechanics to create a unique experience compared to the original. It has been executed with care and passion, and I heartily recommend it to both old and new players

_childDocuments_.review: Summary: A Great remake for a classic game. DAH (2020) keeps most of the original in tact while improving the gameplay with QoL improvements across the board. Which can lead to scenarios where the player is struggling to find objects to make ammo in missions or boss fightsTelekinesis has been made greatly overpowered with the removal of the focus bar from the original. _childDocuments_.review: This is a fun mindless game....when it isn't being a rage-inducing nightmare. Sometimes you fail a mission every five seconds because the checkpoint system is garbage, and if you leave a radio tower or a vehicle you're escorting at low health, the checkpoint saves that amount of health, literally causing you to instant fail over and over again in the next wave. I'm not joking, some moments and missions of this game are downright aggravating. I've seen a lot of games restore a little bit of health during checkpoints like this, and I'm sure we can all agree that escort missions are just the worst. So imagine horribly a implemented checkpoint system, which erroneously serializes the health of what you're escorting, even if it's at like 5%, and then making you continue as if it's possible to actually escort or protect whatever that thing is.I know what you're thinking: "Just git gud". It's not like that. Go ahead, buy this game and have fun protecting those radio towers. I was basically caught up in an infinite loop of failure with that one. You'll see what I mean.Now let's continue. The weapons are good...except for the Anal Probe. I feel like something is broken about it, because it just doesnt want to fire some times. I don't know why, but it's like it has to pass some sort of check before it actually shoots, and you can sit there just constantly trying to shoot it, but it will just keep failing. Very poorly implemented, that one.I've encountered only one bug, and it's quite simply if you (I play with an xbox controller on PC), hold down the forward movement stick, then open and close the start menu two times, your character will literally glide without an animation until you release the forward stick or change direction. The character model basically T-poses, but without an actual t-pose. And like I said, this state lasts forever.I'm still recommending this game, because I am having fun with it. I just personally feel like it could be better. Simple things like giving us another upgrade that increases the amount of dna we get from harvesting brains. Things like that.7/10 from me. It's fun. But the escort missions and checkpoint system are absolutely dreadfully implemented.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game, it really made me feel like I was back in the PS2 era. I only have 1 minor problem, the game is too easy to 100% and there's not a whole lot to do after beating every side challenge and story mission. Then again the price tag was $30 so I can't complain. I hope these developers use the money earned from this to make a true modern Destroy All Humans game with more of everything that was in this game.Graphics 8/10: This game looks surprisingly good and not just in comparison to the original. Explosion effects look really good, and everything isn't realistic but just detailed enough to give off that feeling. The only mixed part is the human characters. The only 2 alien characters look so nice and fit in but the human character models look like exaggerated caricatures where as the original had a more realistic look. Either you love it or hate it, I personally love it because the dialogue is intentionally exaggerated so now the look matches the tone.Story 7/10: (Not much spoilers, everything I'm saying here you find out in the opening sequence so please look away if you atleast want to jump in not knowing a single detail)--The story I really like, it's pretty simple and straight to the point since the mindless destruction is the main course. The story is from the perspective of 2 aliens known as Furons looking to invade earth. The protagonist being Crypto-137. The story starts with Crypto's clone 136  being captured by humans on a scouting mission. They have found a way to become immortal through cloning but their DNA is degrading over time so they're looking into Earth because humans have an ancient Furon gene deep in their DNA. (This implies they made humans long ago to farm them, it's kind of dark and funny when you think about it). The rest of the game is what the title implies. Starting slow with throwing comes to finding yourself at war with the US Government.Audio, 8/10: The audio has been remastered for weapons, explosions, but the dialogue wasn't touched at all. They left that untouched. I think it's because the other alien named Pox was voiced by Richard Horvitz which if you don't know was the same person who voiced Zim in Invader Zim. Once you know this it is very hard to not hear Zim's voice when Pox talks. He's a top rated actor and I think they chose not to chanage the dialogue because there's no replacing him. But that does come at a minor cost. See the audio is very slow paced, fits in with a PS2 game but in this they made cutscenes try to match up with the audio. So you'll have awkward cutscenes where there's action. 1 quick example so you know what I'm talking about, there's a scene where Crypto gets knocked onto his butt, he makes a snazzy insult at some soldiers and the sound effect of him picking up his gun is like 10-15 seconds after that insult so he's animated to awkwardly look at the soldiers and he casually walks to his gun with no one shooting at him with such a big window to do so. This happens a lot, and keep in mind the first game came out when Metal Gear 3 was barely setting a new standard for video game filmography but like the human designs you either like it or don't. It feels very old school so you'll appreciate that if you're into that. Gameplay 9/10: This is the bread and butter of why people love this series. It's a 3rd person shooter where destruction is the only point of playing. I wish there were more games like this because the last total destruction game I remember playing was Prototype. You start with almost nothing and the game slowly gives you new abilities, upgrades, and weapons as you progress. You have telekinetic abilities, throw people around, throw a cow at a human, crush them with a car too. You can make people's heads explode to harvest their brains. You get a jetpack for more mobility. You have 4 weapons and a flying saucer that can crush cities.The big improvements they made I love. They changed a lot. You now have a dash ability and with the right upgrade you have access to S.K.A.T.E which is just hover boots to move faster and feel fun to use in combat. You can mix telekenisis with skate and weapons. In the original skate wasn't a thing and you can only do 1 thing at a time. If you fly with your jetpack you couldn't shoot, if you were lifting something with your telekenisis you couldn't fly or shoot. In the remake you can do multiple of these giving you more ways to approach enemies. They also added minor things like picking up rockets and grenades mid air to throw them back. The saucer had a button that works like a parry, pressed at the right time can send missles right back to whoever shot it. Boss battles were revamped and built from the ground up to work with these new features and mechanics too. They don't have the same attacks as before. They also got very creative with the boss fights like the final boss. Before the final boss you did fight a 50 foot robot and the same robot's remains are on the final boss arena. During this fight the giant robot uses his chest blast to scortch the entire area so you have to take cover to avoid damage. I loved that detail and it was never in the original game. The final boss in the original didn't have a lot of complex attacks because of limitations like player mobility so they went all in with this boss jumping around the arena, using cover, it was so fast past compared to the original. My biggest problem with gameplay is because this is a remake they didn't add in as much as they could have, they only added in what the devs couldn't at the time because of limitations with the tech. There's only 4 guns, so although they added what they could to make it feel like a proper remake it still feels like there isn't as much as there could have been. At the same time after beating the story it is so easy to go back and 100% the game. I'm not saying the game is lacking in content, it has plently for a $30 game but I am saying it feels like they could have done so much more. But what it does have I would recommend this game if you just want to switch off your brain and have mindless fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Normally games have you fight off aliens to defend humanity, this game is the complete opposite. Now YOU are an alien trying to take over humanity, what's more this is a recreation of the original "destroy all humans"!Pros:- Very nice Graphics, they pretty much hold up to today's standards.- Very nice voice acting (they even had the voice of Tank Dempsy in here, holy crap)- Fun gameplay mechanics, if you're in a mission there's several ways to play it, if not you can literally do whatever you want. Go crazy and go on a rampage! Or blend in and observe the humans.- Interesting story, the narrative wasn't too hard to understand and I felt it was an interesting plot (considering we're taking over the world)- Funny jokes (until you've heard them several times, covered in cons)Cons:- The voice lines sound a little choppy, the acting is fantastic but the audio quality from the voice lines aren't perfect. You can tell they've brought them in directly from the old version.- A bit of repetition especially in the stealth segments. You hear the same lines over and over, it gets a little stale. Eventually the repetition catches up and you just keep hearing the same lines even in combat.- The game isn't too long, and compared with the price tag I'd say wait for a sale. (I completed the game in 6 hours, the extra hour was from idling)- It's not been out long so there's a bit of an issue with optimization, especially at the end. I struggled with the second last boss simply because of the game freezing long enough for me to get spun about and run into hazards.Overall I'd say this is a very fun experience, something you should try out if you didn't play the original "Destroy All Humans!". Though, wait for a sale. It's not worth the current price.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the original game. Dev's, to there credit, did a great job of remaking it for modern systems, but they've also made a few radical changes and pretty much every update, change or improvement they made was either poorly executed, or unbalanced the game in some way. For instance, let's start with character models. When they updated to graphics, the devs decided to go for a more cartoonish look for the human NPCs, and I actually agree that this was the right move. Destroy all Humans is a silly game, and going for photo realistic look just wouldn't work. Problem is, they took it a bit too far. NPCs don't look cartoonish, they look like characteratures of cartoons, and bottom line, they're just really ugly. The rest of the world is gorgeous, just not the NPCsAnother example is the grinding.  In the original game, every so often, you would have grind for brain stems (basically the games currency) to continue the plot. This was a determent to the original game so I happy they removed it. Problem is, the grinding served a purpose. You didn't turn in those brain stems, you got to keep them to spend on upgrades. The brain stem grind was there to make sure you were properly prepared for the next level. You still have to grind for upgrades, in fact you have to grind more because the dev's added a bunch of NEW upgrades.  The only difference is that you decide when it's time to grindSpeaking of those upgrade. let's talk about the dash ability, and more specifically, the zero friction upgrade. This at first glance is a great QOL upgrade. One of the week game play points of the original game was how long it took to get from one point to another. even with the jetpack, the game really suffered without a dash or sprint ability. The Dash and slide upgrades are a great improvement, but the Problem is, the zero friction upgrade lets you run literal circles around enemies. With a bit of practice, you're pretty much unhitable, and since you can use your weapons and powers freely while sliding, you can mow through wave's of soldiers and majestic agent like they are nothing.But even without the zero friction upgrade, the game's just too easy now. NPCs with guns attacks are slower and easier to dodge. They took away the psychic majestic agent's ability to nullify you own psychic powers. Tanks can now be thrown via telekinesis just as easily as cars, which pretty much negates any threat they would have posed to you.  I'll admit, the original game could be frustrating at times, but the challenge was enjoyable for the most part. the remake has no challenge whatsoever, and no challenge, for me at least, means no replayability Overall, the games a good remake, but It just isn't as good as the original. I'm hoping take the mistakes they made to heart with Destroy All Humans 2. They really did try

_childDocuments_.review: Destroy All Humans takes place in an alternate universe where the practical medical uses for opium were never discovered, therefore many drugs such as morphine were never conceived. Because of this discovery... or lack thereof, war casualties were much higher than they are in our timeline but more importantly, the famous Romanian actor known for his role as Dracula, Bela Lugosi, never had an opportunity to become dependent on the drug morphine. Of course his sciatica neuritis would give him pain until the day he died, but it would not however kill him... unlike the morphine did.The timelines seem to be pretty similar, with Bela making many of the same mistakes he would have in our timeline, like turning down the role of Frankenstein's monster for the film Frankenstein adapted from the famous Mary Shelley novel Frankenstein, and Boris Karloff would still become immensely famous for the role of Frankenstein's monster in Frankenstein. This would leave Bela fading away into obscurity, until he would later meet up with the one, the only, Edward D. Wood.For those unaware, Ed Wood is known to be one of the worst film directors of all time, directing such anti-classics as "Glen or Glenda", "Bride of the Monster", and most famously of all; "Plan 9 From Outer Space". They are films to be enjoyed with your friends drunk on your ass on weekends, and for that Mr. Wood, I am grateful. Mr. Lugosi would star in all of these films, but as we know in our own reality, he unfortunately passed away during the filming of Plan 9. But in this alternate reality, Lugosi lives and stars as the antagonist of Plan 9, splitting our timelines in two, forever. You might think that in this alternate reality that Plan 9 is a good movie, yes? No... it's just as bad, in fact, it's even worse. But people saw the movie, and noticed the man they knew from Dracula, and people loved it. Loved it so much in fact, that they wanted a sequel. Ed Wood got to filming the sequel right away, and when it released it was also a hit. So they made more sequels, and more, and more and more and more. And each was worse than the last. Eventually there were 33 Plans from outer space, leaving us with the latest entry in Ed Wood's (s)hit franchise, "Plan 42 From Outer Space".And that's where our story as Crypto-137 begins. The Furons noticed all these horrendous works of film and wanted to put to a stop to it. How would they do it? Well, by destroying all humans of course. They could not for the lives of them bare to see a "Plan 43 From Outer Space" be excreted out into the universe.

_childDocuments_.review: **Review: *Destroy All Humans! (2020 Remake)***  *Destroy All Humans!*, the 2020 remake of the 2005 cult classic, is a nostalgic revival that manages to capture the quirky essence of the original while offering a polished, modernized gaming experience. Developed by Black Forest Games and published by THQ Nordic, the game puts players back in the shoes—or, rather, alien boots—of Crypto-137, an extraterrestrial invader tasked with harvesting human DNA and wreaking havoc on 1950s America.  ### Visual and Audio Overhaul The most immediate and noticeable improvement in the 2020 remake is the graphical overhaul. The original *Destroy All Humans!* was built on mid-2000s technology, and the remake updates this with vibrant, cartoony visuals that are perfectly suited to the game’s whimsical tone. The environments are more detailed, the characters more expressive, and the lighting effects add a dynamic layer to the chaotic destruction Crypto brings to Earth. While it’s not aiming for photorealism, the visual upgrades significantly enhance the playful satire that the game thrives on. The audio, too, has been remastered, with the original voice acting intact—a big plus given the stellar performance of Richard Steven Horvitz as the snarky, irreverent Crypto. His sardonic commentary, alongside the bombastic declarations of his superior, Orthopox (voiced by the iconic J. Grant Albrecht), add a lot of charm to the experience. The sound design complements the on-screen mayhem with satisfying laser blasts, explosions, and the occasional sound of terrified humans fleeing in panic.  ### Gameplay: A Faithful Remaster with Quality-of-Life Improvements In terms of gameplay, *Destroy All Humans! (2020)* sticks closely to the formula that made the original a hit, for better or worse. It’s an open-world action game with mission-based objectives, allowing players to use a variety of alien weapons and psychic powers to wreak havoc on humanity. Crypto’s arsenal includes a Zap-O-Matic for electrifying enemies, a Disintegrator Ray for turning humans into ash, and the infamous Anal Probe for, well, you get the idea. These weapons feel as fun as they did 15 years ago, with the remake enhancing their responsiveness and visual effects. There are also some minor quality-of-life improvements that make the game feel less dated. Crypto’s ability to use multiple powers in tandem has been streamlined, and the controls feel smoother. New mechanics, like the ability to use your jetpack more fluidly, make movement easier and combat more engaging. However, it’s worth noting that some aspects of the gameplay still feel a bit archaic. Enemy AI can be erratic, often charging directly into your line of fire, and some mission structures are repetitive by modern standards. ### Story and Humour The story of *Destroy All Humans!* is purposefully absurd, centering on Crypto’s mission to harvest human DNA and infiltrate the United States government—all while delivering a satirical take on 1950s Cold War paranoia, B-movie alien invasions, and conspiracy theories. It’s lighthearted and doesn’t take itself seriously, which works in its favor. The humor, often dark and filled with innuendo, still holds up remarkably well, especially with today’s lens of satirizing paranoia, government overreach, and societal norms. The game’s writing is laced with snark, and its parody of the ‘50s setting, complete with exaggerated accents and cultural tropes, offers plenty of chuckles. However, some jokes that played well in 2005 may feel a bit dated or tonally off in today’s more socially aware environment. Still, the over-the-top humour, when taken for what it is, contributes to the game’s charm and identity. ### The Downsides:Aged Mechanics While the remake does a good job of bringing the original up to modern standards, it can’t entirely mask some of its aged design. The mission structure, for example, often boils down to basic fetch quests or simply obliterating waves of enemies, which can become repetitive. The game is also fairly short by today’s standards, with most players able to finish the story in about 8 to 10 hours. There are side activities and collectibles to pad out the runtime, but they don’t offer much in terms of variety. Another downside is the difficulty curve. *Destroy All Humans!* doesn’t have much of a challenge, and enemy variety is limited, meaning that combat encounters can start to feel monotonous after a few hours. Although Crypto's weapons and abilities are fun to use, the lack of meaningful progression or complex enemies means that the novelty can wear off sooner than expected.  ### Verdict: A Fun, If Flawed, Trip Down Memory Lane *Destroy All Humans! (2020)* is a love letter to fans of the original game, offering a visually impressive and faithful remake that captures the spirit of its predecessor. It’s a fun, chaotic experience filled with irreverent humor, creative destruction, and a lighthearted tone that sets it apart from more serious, modern titles. However, beneath the shiny new coat of paint, the game’s age still shows in its repetitive missions and simplistic gameplay. For newcomers, it may not have the depth or sophistication expected from today’s open-world games, but for fans of the original, it’s a nostalgic romp worth revisiting. Despite its flaws, it’s hard to deny the simple joy of being a wise-cracking alien wreaking havoc on an unsuspecting human population. After all, who wouldn’t want to destroy all humans—at least for a little while?  **Score: 7.5/10** A solid remake that stays true to the original’s quirky charm, but some dated mechanics keep it from being truly out of this world.

_childDocuments_.review: Destroy All Humans (2020) is a from-the-ground-up remake of the PS2-era cult classic of the same name. This is a relatively ‘safe’ remake, meaning the developers have changed as little as possible from the original, though cut content has been added where appropriate. While its age may show with its simplicity and certain design choices, this third-person alien chaos simulator still manages to be a ton of fun, helped by its light-hearted tone, a great variety of destructive tools, and its quality over quantity approach to content. Breaking from the tradition of most save-the-world-type experiences we see today where you play as the saviour of Earth, Destroy All Humans places you in the shoes of Crypto-137, an alien seeking revenge on the inhabitants of Earth for capturing his brother. Think John Wick except the guy they just annoyed has zero sympathy for the entire race that wronged him. This simple goal gives your chaos a purpose, and even though this sounds like a setup for an alien invasion film you’ve seen before, it feels surprisingly unique as a video game since there are not too many linear experiences where you play as the undisputed bad guy. The writing is surprisingly funny, portraying Crypto as a spiteful force to be reckoned with, and conversely presenting the humans as incredibly gullible creatures who believe communism is responsible for Crypto’s existence. Further context is delivered through a series of mostly enjoyable, short and sweet cutscenes that occur within and between some of the levels. However, the transitions to these certainly show this game’s age, as they sometimes occurred without warning after you’ve reached an objective, which I found to break the momentum of the experience, especially as the narrative mostly takes a backseat here. Combat is split into two modes: on-foot playing as Crypto, and in the air flying a UFO. You’ll be on the ground most of the time, using Crypto’s array of weapons and telekinetic abilities to achieve the goal set out by the game’s title. You can chain shock multiple humans using a lightning gun, disintegrate them with a jacked-up ray gun, and fire incredibly volatile projectiles which can be thrown to create devastating explosions. Crypto can also throw any living organism and object in the environment, and both this and his weapons can be used almost simultaneously for maximum effect. There’s not much variety here, but what is on offer creates a very fun and gratifying power fantasy, helped by satisfying audio feedback from the weapons, and the hilarious reactions of your victims. Crypto can also move about by jetpacking, and can perform an endless skating manoeuvre which is equal parts a useful, fun, and unique method of traversing each environment. All of the above and your UFO can be upgraded by collecting currency from completing missions and killing humans by affecting them with an ability which primes their brains to be consumed. UFO combat is similarly basic but still plenty of fun. You’ve got your standard destruction beam, a powerful sonic boom attack, and the ability to drop mini-nukes onto the world below. The enemies, combat vehicles, and surface-to-air missiles that stand in your way don’t pose much of a threat until later on, so it is pretty easy most of the time, but this isn’t necessarily a bad thing. Not every game has to be super challenging to be fun, and Destroy All Humans smartly recognized that disrupting its power fantasy by weakening your destructive capabilities would have been a poor move. The campaign takes place across 23 missions which are launched from a mothership-themed menu. These are split between six open environments, all of which have a simple but distinct theme ranging from a farm to a classified alien research facility, and the objectives you have to complete are typically focused on a small part of one of these areas. After finishing your first mission in each zone, you are able to freely roam that world to complete some exclusive activities, or simply destroy as much of the area as you’d like to. There’s good variety here; you’re not just causing carnage throughout all of them, as you’ll sometimes be required to kidnap a target stealthily or infiltrate a guarded facility to gain some important information for Crypto’s quest. You’ll make use of the ‘holobob’ ability in a few of these assignments; this allows you to take on the appearance of any human on the map and walk around without raising suspicion. Whilst this does slow the game down significantly, I liked the change of pace that these offered most of the time. However, tedium set in during a couple of missions where the holobob ability was required whilst following a slow-walking human, as these don’t give you much to do while waiting. I also found it a bit frustrating that completing an objective’s requirements would sometimes cause the mission to instantly end, even during the middle of chaotic battles for no good reason. This could have been fixed by asking you to exfiltrate the area by reaching your UFO, and the small size of the maps means this wouldn’t have become repetitive for me.There are four types of hub-area activities, each focusing on a particular element of the game, and reward you with one to three stars based on your performance. Races require the fully upgraded SKATE ability and ask you to follow a probe to collect dropped resources from it as quickly as possible. Armageddon activities give you more opportunities to be rewarded for destroying the environment with your UFO. Both of these follow an identical format per hub-world, but remain consistently enjoyable as a result of their low quantity. Abduction activities require you to pick up a particular category of object and throw them into the tractor beam, ranging from humans to household objects, and Rampages ask you to kill lots of organisms as fast as possible, ranging from civilians to special agents, and even cows in one instance. These are all really simple, but absolutely feel worth checking out after you finish the campaign if you’re looking for more to do. It took me around seven hours to complete the campaign, completing all of the bonus objectives per mission along the way, and an additional two hours to clear up the remaining achievements. There are a series of collectable probes hidden throughout each of the maps, but obtaining all of these is not required to collect the achievements, only rewarding a bit of upgrade currency and some concept art for seeking them out. This made completing the game incredibly pleasant, as there were no annoying or repetitive activities that stood in the way of completion, and so the 100% experience is highly recommended. Performance-wise, the game ran at a buttery-smooth 60fps on high settings on my main machine (GTX 1660Ti, Ryzen 7 3700X, 16GB RAM). The ultra settings did not increase visual fidelity to the point where the performance decrease was justified for me. While I never played the original Destroy All Humans, I can easily see why it developed a cult-following as there are not too many mindless experiences that have quite the same setup as this game does. I’d highly recommend it if you’re looking for a straightforward third-person action experience that focuses on gameplay, and provides you with the freedom to endlessly level entire towns and their inhabitants without requiring much effort.Click  for more details about what my review scores mean!

_childDocuments_.review: What Black Forest Games and THQ Nordic have achieved with the Destroy All Humans! remake is impressive. It retains the same feel and the graphics are so well done. They have executed excellently and sets a standard for remakes. Old and new fans will love this. In some ways Destroy All Humans! shows its age, being a remake of a game that came out 2005, in a genre that's grown a lot in those years. But it's also got a sense of humour and parody of American life that feels more relevant today than when the original game first came out. That's a depressing reflection on the state of the world today, but it also means that the satire that underpins everything else in the game hits harder than the original creators ever could have imagined. This is definitely one of the funniest games I've ever played, I highly recommend this game for everyone. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I killed a boss with a weaponized anal probe, and you can too.This is one of the best remakes I've ever played - so much more than a graphical overhaul with a price tag slapped on, and yet it stays true to the original experience. IMHO this is how remakes *should* be made.The hilarious audio and level designs are intact (with a bonus "forgotten" mission), but the controls and graphics have been given a lot of love and a massive boost. I wasn't betting on keyboard + mouse feeling good since it's originally a PS2 game, but it handled great.All told, you're looking at 7-10 hours of main campaign, but there's plenty of challenge events, free roam and unlockable skins to at least double that playtime - so there's plenty of fun to be had. In fact, I challenge you NOT to have fun playing a wisecracking evil alien while blowing up buildings, throwing cows with your mind, and turning enemies into dust with alien weaponry.Definitely recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Short version:Pros:+ 50s setting is awesome+ Bright and colorful graphics+ Enjoyable story mode+ Voice acting is over the top and very enjoyable+ Plenty of upgradesCons:- Repetitive gameplay- Drags a bit towards the end"Long" version: is a third-person action game developed by Black Forest Games and Pandemic Studios and published by THQ Nordic. You follow the adventure of Cryptosporidium-137 in his quest to gather human DNA to save his dying race from extinction, as years of cloning started degrading its DNA.The story does not take itself seriously and is very silly, which I really enjoyed. Crypto is an okay protagonist, as he is unashamedly cold and apathetic towards humans, but his demeanor is a bit one-note, as it never really changes. It does work for the story, however. The other characters are just caricatures of real life political figures or stereotypes of 50s tropes, like the bimbo blonde with an exaggerated accent, the dimwitted farmer that mistakes the protagonist for an ugly wild animal or the idiotic FBI agents/army men that are terrible at their job. It does not come across as mean-spirited, however – more like self-deprecating humor.I felt like the story had a strong start but slowly lost steam, especially towards the end of the campaign.Gameplay shines in .You have two different types of gameplay – on foot, where you use Crypto, and you can also use your spaceship to fly around.Crypto controls well, as you have a wide array of deadly weapons and movement abilities. Each weapon has strengths and weaknesses and it was enjoyable to scroll through all of them and dispose of humansby the hundreds. Your abilities provide much needed versatility to your arsenal, as you will be able to fly around with your jetpack, slide across the map at high speed and lift enemies up with telekinesis and yeet them across the environment and against each other, for example. There are also several abilities that allow you to engage in a bit of stealth gameplay, which is nice.The flying saucer controls are okay, but I felt the game did not offer much in terms of variety when it came to spaceship missions. You usually just have to destroy everything – enemy forces and buildings – and cause as much mayhem as possible. While not necessarily bad, it did grow boring.You can upgrade your arsenal with a considerable number of upgrades, but most of them felt like basic stat boosts that did not change my approach to gameplay.My main problem with the gameplay only came up later, near the last third of the story - it grew repetitive. Pair that up with the story’s lack of focus I mentioned above and everything starts feeling same-y and uninspired.Graphically,  looks awesome.The color palette is vibrant, character models look silly (definitely intentional) and you get to explore different areas of the US with diverse biomes, citizens and enemies. Even the loading screens have a lot of personality and charm, which I really appreciated.Both the soundtrack and the sound effects are great. The voice acting is a lot of fun, as it leans into the cheesiness of the premise and makes fun of the humans.While I did not care much for the last third of the campaign and the side content (mission challenges) was very repetitive, I did enjoy . Overall, I think it is a fine game. It embodies the best aspects of early 2000s games, though it occasionally shows some of their flaws. It provides 10-15 hours of pulpy fun. While I feel like its base asking price is a bit steep, I totally recommend getting it on sale. The game plays well, has a strong art direction and does not take itself seriously.Final score: 8 out of 10.If you enjoyed this review, please consider following my .

_childDocuments_.review: Maxed this on Xbox and there are a lot of welcomed changes but there are some unwelcomed ones too. First off, the insta-death from touching water from the original game has been addressed here, you now get a chance to get out of the water before you die, thank you! Secondly, I love the jetpack changes, it's more versatile which I love. The cut content from the very original because of the space problem back in the days of PS2 like the missing 'independence day' like death Ray from the underside of your UFO is welcomed and the missing mission that had to be cut too. Healing your saucer by using humans and vehicles for their health is a great idea they took from the OG Destroy all Humans 2 idea of 'transmogging' if I'm not mistaken. Now, to the unwelcomed things I didn't like starting with the style of the graphics. Although back in the day there were limitations on the graphics, they still tried their best to resemble realism with their towns, people and vehicles but with this remaster they've gone down a more silly and goofy look to match the story and goofy gameplay but I'm just not a fan of it. Some line's and conversations along with animations aren't quite in line with how they were presented in the original and it's a little off putting and weird. Moving back to the visuals, the blood from the cows has been removed and the brains from humans that you collect are now glowing with green radiation or something which I don't like as well as the DNA points you get being the same amount whether the humans are dead or alive when you remove the brain which in the original, the brain was worth more when the victim was alive and halved when they're dead. I'm also not a fan of the telekinesis, it was done a lot better back in the day and it was fun throwing people up in the air to watch them fall to their death and hear the bones crack. I might have missed some things or forgotten some things, good and bad but they're just a few. Anyway, I love the work THQ has done here and keeping the original voice lines front he original and used them here is an absolute brilliant move by them, thank you so much for that. I highly recommend this game if you played the old one and to new players, you'd probably fall in love with this version. A definite ne 8 out of 10 for me!

Ha-ha, nope!Almost every mission starts with you assuming someone's disguise and ends with... sneaking into a base, lab, meeting, scanning minds on your way to maintain the look . Where. Is. My. CHAOS?!Oh, it's there... for like 1-2 minutes. DAH introduces one new ability per chapter and lets you upgrade it via revisiting previous levels. But don't rub your green hands in joy - you won't meet any oppression. Very-very colourful game. Lots of green and red explosions. Overall cartoonish and... boring to complete. . These heavily rely on your upgraded abilities and timed. At least somewhere you can destroy something.

_childDocuments_.review: If there was ever an IP I wanted its studio to remake because of how good it was and how good it still fulfills today's standards, it's without doubts Destroy all Humans! _childDocuments_.review: This is the first remaster in a while where I actually played the game growing up, so I was excited to see how much justice this remaster does to the original. Thankfully it does one hell of a job. This game is notorious for its humour, and the devs didn't hold back by censoring content. There's a warning at the start, describing that times were different but they wanted to keep the old content in which is highly respectable because a lot of snowflakes will probably cry about it. The newspaper transitions are especially brilliant, the headlines are always hilarious. Something I didn't experience as a kid was the ending of the game as I never beat it growing up.  Something I noticed in the intro cutscene was that Crypto's voice is way different, I'm not sure if it's a matter of original audio vs remastered or if the voice actor put on an accent and then scrapped it. Either way the intro cutscene plays out completely differently to the rest of the narration which is a little strange. One of my biggest annoyances with this remaster is that there's no restart checkpoint feature. There's only the option to restart the whole mission which is pretty useless. When doing the optional challenges I found myself just suiciding in order to restart, and this could have been easily streamlined with a restart checkpoint button on the menu. Speaking of optional challenges, I completed them all just to realise that the relevant achievements are bugged and won't unlock which was quite disappointing. Seems like a fix is nowhere to be found. + humour (newspaper transitions)+ didn't censor the original+ boss fights - checkpoint system- bugged achievements Rating - 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: great remake of a unique game. only downsides i can chalk up are that the pause menu only offers the option to restart the entire mission rather than also being able to restart from your last checkpoint, along with disguising tending to be a bit faulty ( though that was also in the og. ) other than that, lovely visuals, big ups.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played the original game and never getting around to finishing it, I can definitely say that this game is worth every cent compared to the original. The only time I encountered lag/stutters was at the final two boss battles where the game would freeze for a second or two then unfreeze and I'd be looking somewhere else even though I didn't move my mouse.The game runs smooth and should be able run on almost any computer as it is not hardware intensive.Yes the game looks a lot better in graphics wise, the dialogue could of also been improved for today's standard because there are a few lip syncing issues but for a 15 GB game I can look past that. _childDocuments_.review: I don't like how they made a remake of just the first one, it wasn't even the best one compared to others. It would have been better just to make a new entry to the series with new weapons and everything. But since they didn't do that, I'd be almost expectant of them to remake the others too.The graphics also kinda suck. Everything is super saturated with bloom and god rays (which I turned off later in the .ini files) and the new models for characters are kinda sucky. Crypto himself looks more like a celebrity recast with a facelift, which might be a good bit of irony, but he still had way more character on the PS2 because the jagged angles complemented his iconic evil smile, while here you can't even tell what he's thinking with that glossed over glare. The other humans were given a more cartoony caricature look too, which I think they did later on to make them fit into the higher resolution environment. They might have overdone it a bit though. The animation in cutscenes sucks, a lot of it was smoothed over to try to make it feel more 'natural' I guess but everyone just moves at the same speed no matter what emotion is being portrayed. In the PS2 version, you actually see Crypto have an angry breakdown in front of pox in the intro cutscene. Here, he just turns his head like he's pacing and the camera cuts a lot to make you think he's moving. One last final bit, a lot of audio was just taken out of the original game, so that also hurts the cruddy animation a bit, but they also had to bring Invader Zim himself back for more bonus mission dialogue, so you'll have some weird shifts in fidelity. He also sounds a bit old or tired to be doing the iconic voice anymore, so sometimes he'd do the flamboyant emphasis but squeak it out and it just made me feel kinda bad for him and want to give him a break. No disrespect to his career of course, he still did a decent job.So in terms of graphics, it's a pretty bad remake, but with gameplay, it's actually a pretty good upgrade from the original. Moving Crypto around in PS2 Land was like dragging around a garbage bag while drunk, and you could only ever fire your weapon and move at the most. Here Crypto gets to do all the cool dynamic movement and jumping he really deserved, and you can pick up a guy with TK and toss him at a tank while firing and ridding your jetpack through the air all at once and it's amazing, as it should be. A lot of weapons were reworked to be better but worse in parts though. The Zap-o-matic gets a huge upgrade, but it's now the only weapon I'd use half the time as it just became a DPS lazer with infinite ammo, and the Disintegrator ray just became this thing that shot heat seeking fireballs (how even) as opposed to the cool plasma gun from Doom 16 type thing it was. The Probe should have been removed all together, that's all. I think the Ion Detonator got nerfed, but I can't remember what it was originally like. Now it's this weird charge up distance thing that only goes half as far as it did, but you can still manually detonate it so that's cool. The saucer weapons are worse. The death ray is pretty much just the Zap-o-matic taped to the front of the Saucer, so it ends up being more flashy than it is an actual DEATH RAY. Neither the death ray or the Sonic Boom can take down a building any quicker than like 10 seconds, even with full upgrades, so you can't level half the town anymore in a few minutes like you could on the PS2. There's also way more stuff that attacks you in the saucer, like missiles which are nearly impossible to reflect in time given the game's default crappy FOV. I also don't get why they didn't add in the cloak for your saucer, just to give you a break from all the missiles.Either way, it's still a fun game. Go kill em all!

_childDocuments_.review: This is generally a good all round game. It could do with some improvement but works well enough. It's stable, interesting, fun and looks good. _childDocuments_.review: A beautifully done, nostalgic remaster of the original, this is perfect for the older or newer players, for those that want to add another perfect game to their collection, or for those looking to enjoy a mindless adventure of mass destruction.I won't give much away, but you play as Crypto, an alien from the planet Furon, who is wreaking havoc in both an attempt to save his species as well as invade Earth. Taking place in the US during the late 1950s, there's very clear references to both pop culture and the effects of the Red Scare, which results in many comedic quotes and moments. The game also features equipment you use throughout the game that can be upgraded to help aid you in your destruction.Seeing as this is a remaster, to say I have an issue with the game means I also have an issue with the original, which I don't. It's not much of a concern, but...There may be more, but it really isn't a big deal. It just felt as if they forgot to add in those achievements and I was left wanting more.As you play the game, all of the achievements become pretty self-explanatory, but one that didn't come to me right away was "Do Feed The Sharks". It makes complete sense, but if you're having issues, check out Dayngls' Game Guides' YouTube video, linked below...

_childDocuments_.review: To start off I have been a fan of Destroy All Humans since its first release back in 2005, while the 2005 version was not the best looking and had its fair share of issues with wonky and weird mechanics. The 2020 version takes the older version and absolutely overhauls and adds some of its own content that makes the game not only fun to play but also remains true to the original! From the very start of the game to the end it is pure nostalgic if you have owned and played the 2005 version hearing the voice actors absolutely nail the original voice lines from so long ago; I did find it weird there were a few script changes in the game but I suppose it was for the better since it feels more modern. Overall I give the game a 10/10 and hats off to Black Forest Games! You guys took a cult classic and remade it to where the old and new generation of Destroy All Humans fans will love and get hooked for years to come! Also please consider a remaster of Destroy All Humans 2 the game may not be as serious as the first but it still remains true to following the first game and it was a blast to laugh at all the wacky content provided and the seriousness that was a perfect blend for its time!Edit: So from what I have gathered the game has been a success to the point where Blackforest has released a trailer that hints at a remaster of the Destroy All Humans 2! This is big in its own right since Destroy All Humans 2 is a big fan favorite among the Destroy All Humans community! Keep an eye out Ladies and Gentlemen!

_childDocuments_.review: Destroy All Humans – Recommend for the setting and story, but not for the completionists-It’s weird. This game gave some really good first impressions. Can’t see the Furon Probes on the map, but no matter. Well, turns out that is a problem. You need the DNA for upgrades. Although it makes more sense to farm humans for it than these, and this is just one red flag in the game design. Which clearly wasn’t updated or improved, I didn’t play the original, no idea if it was like this then, but if it was, then this is terrible.The characters and story are definitely its strong point, as well as the setting and art style. It’s just goofy and that’s what makes it fun. Favourite parts of the gameplay was blowing things up. And the amount of tools at your disposal is amazing. It’s surprisingly simple too, but sadly this comes at a detriment when we factor in the following gameplay issues:Missions are too gimmicky. Whether it’s not being detected or doing something like, deflect projectiles, it becomes a pain. I’m speaking mainly on the optional objective side which I think grants currency rewards? They require a gimmick, not a use of assets. Some are stupidly simple and do allow freedom of choice, but others don’t. Stealth missions. These suck. Pretty much the opposite of destroying humans. For a one alien army, it makes no sense that you can’t go in and read minds to complete everything. Not to mention that this is really the only flaw in the story, why can’t Crypto just read minds to get info? Why does it have to be stealth or in one case interrogation? Gimmicky side activities. Races were okay, until Capitol Chase, and everything is literally a gimmick. You have to complete everything one way, rather than multiple ways, and it sucks. It feels so bad. It isn’t fun.No map markers for Furon Probes. For a remake, especially one released quite recently, I’m surprised there wasn’t a quality of life feature for this. It’s actually almost unheard of that a collectable item isn’t marked on the map. First (not sure why type of game this counts as) game I’ve played in years that hasn’t had this feature. Upgrades feel expensive. If you don’t have every upgrade before the final mission, you may struggle. It’s doable, but extremely stressful and easy to die. Navigation the Archives can be a nightmare. There isn’t any reminders that you can’t alert the military in some missions.That said, I’m really conflicted on this game. On one hand, it’s a strange sense of humour that works, an interesting story, and great graphics. On the other, you have ♥♥♥♥ gameplay design which absolutely craps over what this game had going for it. I was willing to 100% this game in the first 2 hours, but I ended up losing that motivation when these gameplay issues arose. I want to play the 2nd game to see what happens, but this was just disappointing. I’m always scared of inaccessible games. So I don’t recommend this. It’s a shame because it seems like a good remake. It just lacks a lot of polish. Thank ♥♥♥♥ it’s a singleplayer game though.

_childDocuments_.review: Destroy All Humans! is a remake of 2005 game and it's very close to original in many aspects. At the same time game looks amazing and (almost) perfectly polished.We play as an evil alien named Crypto-137 in 1950's USA (with all essential stereotypes included). Each mission takes place in a half-open location and is conventionally non-linear in most cases, but there is no great freedom of action either. There's a lot of hilarious cinematics that are mixed with gameplay sequences - humor is definitely the strongest part of the game. Unreal Engine 4 works great here and I've encountered only one issue with performance on one of the last bosses (RoboPres) where I had to reduce graphic setting to low to avoid weird lagspikes on phase 2-3 (definitely not a PC FPS issue). Every other technical aspect of the game was just great.It took me 6,5 hours to complete campaign with a majority of achievements and I suppose it would take another 3 hours to complete all the rest. There's next to no replayability beside completing achievements and a couple of additional challenges.  gameplay is a little bit awkward in some moments, because it kept most of original mechanics and I constantly had a nostalgic feeling that I'm playing an old game (not exactly 2005's original but old game in general). It was a good feeling most of the times but some mechanics looked too outdated and some actions that are supposed to be fun were kinda generic/boring.All in all,  is a great remake of a hilarious game that definitely won't disappoint people who played original game and wanted to experience it again while it could also entertain new players. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I adore this game. It's set in a 1950s era Nixon controlled neo-conservative USA with unquestioned allegiance to corrupt leaders and a deep-seated fear of the USSR (or the "reds" as they used to call them). It actually really feels good to destroy such a perversely twisted vision of America: whether it be the Nixon or Trump version.It has as total of 23 missions, and you fight either on foot or in a ship (or in some missions both). The ship has a huge collection of guns and defenses, and hand weapons have a similarly huge collection for ground attack. You start out with only the basics and gradually unlock new weapons and features as you complete missions and gather Furon DNA (as mission rewards or extracted from human brains). Furon DNA is the currency for buying upgrades.The game is an open world map with 6 cities. Each with its own style and culture and completely destructable buildings. As you play the missions the cities gradually open up. You can also play 4 minigames in each city with 3 levels of excellence to achieve. I spent hours collecting human brains with furon DNA and just antagonizing the locals.The most fun minigame is "armegeddon" where you have to destroy as much of the city as possible. Once you achieve the quantum destructor weapon you can blow up entire city blocks. The visuals are so stunningly viceral as you watch rubble and fire rain down all over the streets. It's a little like grand theft auto but only on foot and with far more destruction. Lastly the $30 price is perfect, actually it's almost too low as this game has hundreds of hours of replayability. So it's well worth it.

The textures also look a little glossy, which is fine on Crypto and the other aliens, but the humans don't look so hot at times and I would have liked if the buildings exploded into debris higher than 15 fps. _childDocuments_.review: To be honest, I didn’t care much for the original in 2005. I think I played it for an hour or so before abandoning it. It just didn’t resonate with me. 17 years later I got this one in a bundle and decided to give it another try. And to my surprise it is a solid and to this day pretty unique game. The mix between 3rd-person-shooting, stealth missions, all-out-rampage UFO-action and kinda funny cutscenes was good enough to make me finish the ~8 hours long campaign. In six hub-worlds across the USA consisting of backwater areas, several cities and secret military bases you go to war with all of humanity.The 23 main missions are linear with fixed objectives, still leaving some room for creativity with an interesting pool of weapons and skills at your hand that can be upgraded between missions. For example you can disguise as humans, control them to a certain degree or use telekinesis to manipulate matter. All in all the mission design is varied, but I didn’t enjoy the stealth missions as much as the action mission. Blowing up stuff is certainly the most fun you will have in this game. Gladly most of the game is about that. During the course of the game you will also unlock side missions in the hub worlds that add further challenge and volume to the game. Just don’t expect some cutting edge action game. Everything feels a bit unpolished and janky, but never too much to get in the way of the fun. It’s a good remake, especially the graphics and controls got a huge overhaul to make this feel like a modern game. This also runs pretty okay on the Steam Deck after fiddling around with some settings. But even on my PC the performance wasn’t always that great with some stuttering and frame drops here and there (ultra-settings @1440p on RTX 2070 Super). Still, I am actually surprised how much effort they put into this remake instead of just releasing an upscaled remaster. Some other publishers should take note.

_childDocuments_.review: The original Destroy All Humans was one of my favourite games of the 6th console generation, it was a stupid amount of fun, with so many memorable moments and with an engaging atmosphere.However I won't lie when I say it's dated compared to Modern Third Person Shooters from today, it's still a lot of fun, however I was looking forward to this remake a lot, wow it delivered big time.This review isn't going into much as the game as it's own, but more on the fact it's one of if not the best remake I've ever played.New controls for Crypto and the saucer, allowing for more intense gameplay since you can now use PK and your weaponry together, and the saucer can now swap weapons quickly for fast mayhem.Game looks fantastic, the new visuals and new details the devs added are great, like when the Farmer's wife comes out to find the Farmer on the first mission, only to see a grey smug face looking at her with her husband under his feet are very welcome.Has the classic music and voice acting from the original game, they haven't been replaced.Has a new Dash and Skate ability for Crypto, a very welcome power up, giving new mobility options for in and out of combat.The added cut mission is fun as well and fits into the game perfectly, if you told a new player it was originally not in the first game, it would shock them.Has a new skin system which allows you to customize CryptoNew side challenges during missions for extra DNA and special skins.The grind is nowhere as bad as the original game.Doesn't replace the original, I don't like it when remakes make their original games near or completely obsolete, like the Crash N-Sane Trilogy and CTR Nitro Fuelled, since there's no reason to go back to the original games for the average Joe since the remakes are just better in nearly every way, however the way this game controls compared to the original is night and day and offers a different gameplay style from each other because of it, which makes me very happy, since I have a reason to play the original besides just for nostalgia's sake.No skins for Saucer or the weapons, which is a massive shame, weapons weren't to be expected anyway, but with Black Forest adding skins for Crypto, a feature from Big Willy Unleashed and Path of the Furon, I was hoping at least the Saucer would get some too, but alas, nope, hopefully a DLC or something down the line gets added.I don't know if it's just me since I know the original game like the back of my hand or the new controls or whatever, but this game was very easy, I remember the original being a lot more harder.While bugs and glitches are rare, I've had the following...1. During the Mission Duck and Cover, I accidentally let a Radioactive cow destroy the escort, when it restarted, I got stuck where the mission would start from the checkpoint, only to be blown up by a cow within seconds, I had to restart.2. On the new/cut mission, there's a part where you need to find 3 officers, 2 are labeled/hinted on the map, the 3rd one isn't and is hiding in a corner with some soldiers.3. I spawned in Rockwell one time and just saw a car fly by, it wasn't stuck, it was flying like it was driving as normal until it touched the floor, then drove of... ok cool...4. During missions where I'm in disguise, stay in stealth and need to talk to a soldier or something, the game would randomly transmog an object BEHIND the person instead, leading me to fail the mission.5. A few texture glitches on some maps where you can see under the map, but these are rare and often nearby the boundaries.I've played many remakes, I've played remakes of many of my favourite games, and i can easily say, without a doubt, this is the best remake I have played, bravo Black Forest Games and THQNordic, hopefully another Destroy All Humans game or Remake is on it's way.

_childDocuments_.review: In essence you run around to "Destroy all humans" in a fantastical universe set in the 50s. You have different "cities" you invade which considering this is a remaster of a game from many years ago that's not super surprising but it helps give a nice open world feel to it, which you didn't get a lot back then. The "loading" time between each area is kind of annoying but that loading time will be more based on your computer than it will be the game itself.In essence you "learn" about the humans along the way by doing various things and studying to slowly work your way to end-game plot, at which you fight what I would define as a "broken" last boss due to the fact the game forces you to actually go back to some places to play the "challenges" and/or you have to buy very specific upgrades to make it tolerable and not boring and repetitive. Outside of that one gripe, basically you run around and blast stuff with various weapons, and of course a saucer. The graphics were updated so the explosions and stuff are cooler but does look like they took some fun elements out from the OG, but for the most part still plays like the original. Is it worth it at full price? No. Is it worth it on a 75% or more sale? Most definitely. $30 for an equivalent remaster with less than 15 hrs of gameplay(20 or so if you want all the achievements) isn't really worth it.TLDR: Mini challenges to play, short storyline that's a bit funny and good voice acting, and fulfilling ending after last end-game boss that's broken. Hint. If you do end up getting it, focus on SAUCER upgrades especially on the reflecting ones. So, a little bit of replayability if you're into that kind of thing but it gets boring kinda' quick. Personally not going to sink 5+ more hrs into this just to 100% the game as it requires you to do very time sensitive challenges and it's just not that worthwhile and fulfilling.

_childDocuments_.review: Destroy All Humans is a fantastic game which I played for the very first time recently.This game was gifted to me by a very good friend and I am glad that they gifted it to me! I actually never even knew that this game existed when I was younger.Everything about Destroy All Humans is perfect; The story is perfect, the gameplay is spotless - no gimmicks, no micro-transactions, no boring grindy repetitive quests.This is a 3rd person game. You play the role of an alien clone created to basically gather information on the humans in order to eventually subjugate them!As you progress through the game, you start to encounter much more difficult enemies. The end boss fight is like a cherry on top.I especially love the little snippets of newpaper articles that reflect on the carnage caused by you as you progress through the game - they make it seem like it's all an accident or some top secret military experiment gone wrong or something.Destroy All Humans isn't really that long, I was able to get through this game + do all the side quests and extra missions in under 20 hours.This game is totally worth it, if you are a fan of great narrative driven single player games. An absolute gem.

_childDocuments_.review: What do I say to a childhood game of mine easily a 9.5/10 so to talk about Destroy All Humans we need to talk how close is it to the source material and its basically 1:1 95% of the times. Let talk about the common complaints and that is the audio quality now its not great on the voice acting because it is lifted from the original game but that's not a bad thing because its exactly as you remember it. I do have audio stuttering and it seems to be a common problem and my rig does have that problem but its a fully cosmetic issue that does not detract from the game.People are gonna crap on this but personally I am fine with the original quality because its exactly how it was back in the day and I think the mixed reviews are people going in expecting a more modern representation of the old game. And that is just not the case you have to understand THQ Nordic are not trying to make a new game to appeal to modern audiences. There making this game to appeal to the dedicated fan-base of it that loved the original release so that is why I take review sites with a huge spoonful of salt this time.As for the game itself the core is left it exactly as it was with a lot of QOL changes to give the player much more freedom this time around. Crypto no longer has a limitation on his Telekinetic abilities as for the holobob its now tied to its own gauge and not to Crypto's Telekinetic limits that no longer exist that is replenished like the original by scanning thoughts. The agents of the game no longer just strip it off of you they now cause it to decay faster and the mini map now displays the radius of that effect. Any Distraction psi on or near them or a forget psi cast on them cause them to lose this Disruptive field temporarily. They have been side graded essentially while your given more tools and means of evading them whenever your in there field of disruption all PSI abilities do not work along with having to deal with that faster decay.Now the biggest QOL changes is an addition that's in the 2nd game that being the ability to drain vehicles while in the saucer for health. And the ability to transmog things into ammo making your tools and weapons now have much less restriction on the ammo as you can turn objects and vehicles into ammo (Even vehicles you drained) but all ammo and health pickups on the map are gone which is fine because its a change I greatly welcome. You can now dash and skate (Given you have been keeping on your upgrades...) The Probe tool imo has had the biggest overhaul though. In the original game it was a tool you charged and released it was fickle and hard to use but using gave you as much DNA as Extracting there brain mentally when they were alive.Now its a green whip (I am not going there, stop trying to put it there ya weeb >.>) that continuously does damage and yanks the brain out giving it to you instantly you can also extract brains mentally while this happens. Making the Probe weapon essentially the ability to make Crypto a literal Brain reaper with a little finesse. The best part is your shield starts recharging instantly now when you pick up a brain making it viable to do that very thing.I also hear people struggle with the difficulty now I am either a long standing veteran who is good with the series or people are avoiding any kind of grind they can get away with and skimping out on upgrades. (Gotta love that modern rushing gamer mentality...) But I found so long as you keep your upgrades up on integral weapons and especially your health with a little bit of grind with the saucers brain extraction, and you do not play recklessly you will get through the game fine for the most part. And this due in part to the QOL changes both to your options and control of Crypto also the game pretty much states this you DO NOT need to do all optional objectives in a single run that's what the Holo Deck was designed for so do not fall into that perfectionist mentality that you HAVE to do everything in a single run... Also the fact you can replay missions to your hearts content is a very nice replay ability feature also.I cant note everything its way to much to note here all I can tell you is its the definition of what a remake should be the same but better. So I recommend to those that play it do not treat this like a modern game because its not, its a old fashioned game with a new coat of paint and polish.Edit: It took me 15 hours to beat the main game and unlock all upgrades you will need to do some grinding if your not doing the challenges or finding all the drones. I recommend taking advantage of the Probes abilities because when you pick up a brain in this game and I did note this off somewhat in my original stance. It removes the recharge delay rechargeing the shield as soon as you pick one up. Also if a human has the brain extraction aura from extracting a brain from someone else as that is an upgrade of the brain extraction PSI. Killing them will automatically cause there brain to be extracted. By doing this you can essentially play Brain Reaper to keep your shields up through any aggressive weapon or through the probe.Now I did not die ONCE while beating the game all my mission failures are from failing the objective not from death. I will say I came close twice during the final boss but managed to pull through. The optional objectives are for the most part advantageous I will say I had two small points where they got in the way but the Checkpoint system along with the Holo Deck mitigated those instances.All missions are 99% accurate to the source material the voice acting's compression is only noticeable when the new lines, and old lines are said in close proximity to one another which happens like 2 or 3 times throughout the entire game. The bonus mission feels right at home with the others and furthers the continuity of the story of the game that when I first played it, it felt like it was or belonged in the original. And the dash ability one of the few new things in this game feels right at home and is an amazing addition along with aim gliding you have so much more movement freedom and freedom in general with the remake that the old game does not grant. Here's hoping the sequel drives the same kind of mentality that this remake had.

_childDocuments_.review: The 'Destroy All Humans!' remake by Black Forest Games and THQ Nordic is a nostalgic trip back to the golden era of gaming with a modern twist. As a long-time fan of the original game released by Pandemic Studios, I was ecstatic to see this classic reimagined with today's technology.Right off the bat, the most striking aspect of this remake is the graphics. The original game, while charming in its own right, pales in comparison to this version’s vibrant and detailed visuals. The art style chosen for the remake brilliantly encapsulates the 1950s B-movie vibe, which is a perfect fit for the game's theme and tone.Gameplay-wise, the remake brings much-needed quality of life improvements. The controls are more fluid, and the ability to use different powers while firing weapons adds a new layer of strategy and fun. Additionally, the inclusion of a mission cut from the original game is a delightful bonus for fans.All the beloved abilities of our alien protagonist, Crypto, return in full glory. Whether it’s using telekinesis, disguising as humans with Holobob, or wielding advanced Furon weaponry like the iconic disintegrator ray, the gameplay never loses its appeal. It’s easier to manage these abilities, making the experience more enjoyable than the original. Upgrading these abilities and weapons as the game progresses is immensely satisfying, turning Crypto into an unstoppable force.The mission design, while largely unchanged from the original, offers a mix of stealth, combat, and destruction. The stealth elements can be a bit rigid, but overall, the missions provide a good variety of challenges. The flying saucer segments are particularly enjoyable, allowing players to wreak havoc from the skies.The game's setting in the 1950s, with its many references to the Cold War era, is well-executed. The humor, although a bit dated at times, still brings plenty of laughs. The voice acting, especially by J. Grant Albrecht (Crypto) and Richard Horvitz (Orthopox), is top-notch and adds much to the game's character.In conclusion, the 'Destroy All Humans!' remake is a faithful and fun revival of a classic. It retains the core of what made the original great while updating it for a modern audience. For fans of the original or newcomers looking for a lighthearted and entertaining alien invasion experience, this remake is a must-play. Black Forest Games has done a commendable job in bringing back a beloved title, making it accessible and enjoyable for both old fans and new players.

You play for maybe five minutes, then there's a cutscene. You continue for maybe another five minutes and that's the end of the scenario, with yet another longer cutscene.
