_childDocuments_.review: I was a little wary of trying this game out given the reviews, but it's a genre I love and the art aesthetic is enjoyable. I opted to give it 2 hours and see what all the fuss was about, so to speak. The foremost flaw is just being thrown into it. The tutorial is not enough. Once I fully understood the basics I thrived, but getting everything to work was a bit troublesome. The important of mana didn't become apparent until I finally had spells I wanted to cast, for instance, upon which time I was in little position to regain it well. That sanity and health were 100 percent separate bars also took a few combats to understand. And the importance of A) forging items for minions with stats you need and B) stacking them with level up stats is something many people might not ever realize they are not doing right, which could be a big part of the perceived difficulty. (I didn't even realize what luck did until finally hovering over the icon, I would never have guessed it was just crit chance)Once I knew what I was doing, which was around halfway through the first floor, it was fun. But this is not a 'traditional' roguelike where you should struggle to figure out basic things, it's just frustrating. You have two hours to convince someone not to refund and leave a negative review, and I think this is the aspect that has made launch a bit cruel. Even for someone with thousands of hours of experience in this, it took over an hour for the fun and appreciation of the design to sink in.That said, here's actually constructive feedback:It's nice to have multiple teams of minions, principally for a sanity group and a physical group. Too bad you have no idea if you brought the right team or not. Seeing an icon of one enemy is quasi-helpful at best. This was mainly an issue upon starting floor 2. You ever try using a sanity attack team on 3 berserkers? I am not a fan of the 'lose a game to figure something out' thing. It was lazy design 30 years ago in Nethack, I don't like seeing it in modern games of the genre when I can lose time doing nothing wrong on my end. A scry spell to show you enemies and their health/sanity would be nice for whatever mana is fair.Zombies are so boring in spot 3 and 4. C'mon, give them one other skill to use. I regret building them. They are far worse than the brides. They don't particularly put out more damage in return for losing a lot.If there's a way to swap one spot to the left or right for using a turn, I can't figure it out. If there isn't, for the love of the undead, put one in. It's a huge sacrifice to reposition your team in this manner, which is more fun than using crappy skills since you have no way of getting back where you are optimal. Especially since some core skills to me move you, which just opens this weird can of worms where I can't use things in the way I'd like. (Example: Wraith's self buff. Why the heck does it move you forward?) Maybe make positional changes of certain sorts optional if you aren't going to let your team shift otherwise.All in all, I think it's a bit expensive for what it offers at the moment, but I didn't refund it. I'll be keeping my eye on it and hopefully the dev stays this active and engaging on making it a better experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a difficult one for me. I really do enjoy almost every part of the game I have played so far but one thing I just can't enjoy are the really unfun instant kill mechanics on some enemies. Regardless of your stance on difficulty and difficulty is something I am quite fine with, having an enemy instantly kill one of your minions from full health isn't really about the difficulty, it's about how fun the game feels to play. When you've put the time and effort into improving your minions, an instant death ability from any enemy is just a slap in the face that kills all of my motivation to continue playing. Instant kill mechanics are not fun and really aren't difficult, just frustrating and really unenjoyable, especially to a new player who doesn't know the enemies to enable them to counter them yet.TL;DR Instant kill abilities are very anti-fun and unenjoyable and are easily replaced by similar difficulty abilities that are less frustrating.Update: Since I first Reviewed this game there has been a lot of work on it and my main gripe with the instant kill enemy has been resolve with an ability that mere does a decent chunk of damage instead. With Iratus' full release the game has more features than it did when I last played and all of them have seemed to only improve the game from my initial experience. I can now very enthusiastically say you should buy this game, it's great, it's enjoyable and quick and easy to get into.

_childDocuments_.review: Since it's clear from the outset that this is a Darkest Dungeon clone what most of you will be asking is whether or not it's as GOOD as Darkest Dungeon. I would urge you to at least complete the first two difficulty levels before reaching this conclusion as it improves as you progress along its learning curve. My current feeling is that it IS, in fact, as good as DD and has the potential to become better than it. Even as it is it is an absolutely worthy purchase and there's not really a lot more to say about it than that as, if you are looking at it at all, you have a fairly good idea of the kind of turn based tactical game that it is.

_childDocuments_.review: You play as the Necromancer Iratus that have been ressurected and is now seeking vengance upon the world!The gameplay rogue-like where you level up your minions that you create from the parts you find as you defeat enemies. You'll also be leveling up yourself, Iratus, giving you additional spells to cast or passive abilities that increase your minions powers. Iratus is also well versed in the arts of alchemy, giving him the ability to create new parts from others, artifacts or even regain vigor or mana.You'll also be expanding your graveyard, the base of operations from where you send your minions out on missions, giving you bonuses and new capabilities to keep your minions alive.The game is a mouthful to grasp, and will take you some hours to get used to - on the surface it might look like games like Darkest Dungeon or Slay the Spire, but in truth it is even more complex.The graphics are appealing and the different minions each have a ton of abilities to use and modify, making the process daunting but in the end very satisfying when you find just the right combo!All in all the game is a lot of fun and hard to put down once you start playing - one more fight before bedtime.. just one more... I can highly recommend getting this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Iratus: Lord of the Dead is artistically fantastic, deep and a brutally challenging experience that is heavily inspired by Darkest Dungeon. The game is currently in early access but already has a promising foundation in place. However, there are some fundamental design decisions that could prove problematic as development persists towards release. Firstly, the atmosphere is severely lacking from an audio and gameplay standpoint. This makes battles feel rather flat and not very tense. On top of that, I didn't feel attached to my characters like in Darkest Dungeon which was a huge part of the experience. Instead of moving your army around a map which increases gameplay interactivity, all you do is choose a visible path like you would in Slay the Spire and fight battle after battle. There is a few things to do before and after fights in terms of preparations and upgrading elements but the game just doesn't feel very varied or engaging. There is definitely potential here but I am slightly concerned the overall design and whether this can be drastically improved or altered upon. I am not expecting a carbon-copy of Darkest Dungeon but Iratus feels like it's missing crucial aspects that made that game so successful. Worth keeping an eye on but I wouldn't buy this yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Iratus: Lord of the Dead

_childDocuments_.review: Big fan of similar games like Darkest Dungeon and Slay the Spire. Iratus definitely falls into this genre of strategy/math/roguelike. The big thing that makes Iratus stand out is that it is less random than these games, but also much more complicated. The end result is that there is a barrier to entry, though I would say it is worth the learning curve. If you want complex systems with a long haul risk/reward campaign, that's what this is.
_childDocuments_.name: Iratus: Lord of the Dead

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic gameplay and great ideas. Some of the worst balance I've ever encountered in a game. You routinely run into enemies that can kill you in 2-4 hits while it can take you upwards of 10-15 to kill them. Couple that with how abundant healing is for your enemies, and how non existent it is for you, makes for some real BS fights.I get it, your minions are disposable. But having them 2 shot when they are level 5, losing all the materials from making them and then basically losing the other 3 minions as well, since once you are down 1 party member, you are almost guaranteed to lose the fight.They say "strategy" is required, but when you have no idea if you are going to be facing enemies that buff tons, are immune to stress, have high def and every other form of advantage, strategy is impossible. The fight previews show you  enemy out of the 4 you fight meaning you can prep for that 1 enemy that is weak vs stress attack, build your party with that in mind, and then find out the other 3 are immune to stress damage.Virtually every single fight contains enemies that easily strip you of any and all buffs, meanwhile you have or 2 minions tops that can do the same. Meanwhile in these same fights, an enemy can strip you of all buffs, debuff you, and hit you for 1/3 of your hp all in one attack/action. And this same enemy can the next round give itself, block charges(immune to attacks besides crits) and buff it's crit% and attack damage again, all in one action. No big deal right. Oh yeah, practically every single enemy buff/debuff  in this game stacks. So if you try and wipe those clean, you are spending the entire fight doing that and not damaging anything, or you just don't have a minion who can cleanse those buffs/debuffs and you just die in a few hits.This game has a phenomenal approach, and a real unique mechanic. But, holy hell is it poorly executed. The enemies are overpowered, your minions are incredibly weak, your magic spells are either weak and take too much mana, or they provide buffs to the enemies when you use them. Your only support character than can reliably heal your characters is unlocked after a considerable amount of time in game, and heals you for x-y damage, and then the next turn it damages you for the same.RNG can be a PITA some times but, in most roguelike games you can work around it. In this the game is specifically designed to make it as unfair as possible. Difficulty is meant to feel challenging, not cheap.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Darkest Dungeons-like, but is not a cheap imitation, it is the real deal. It is every bit as detailed and intricate as DD, but it has its own twists, and somehow, I just seem to enjoy playing it a lot more. It's hard to even explain why, maybe because it is more forgiving, or doesn't take itself as grim-dark seriously. I like dark themes, but DD was so heavy-handed, I often found it grating. This game has a sense of humor, and it's very welcome in this genre.

_childDocuments_.review: After coming back to this game after it's been released and a few patches after that even.  I can't recommend the game.  There are some glaring mechanics issues, and balance issues.  The game seems like it's not finished.  There hasn't been too much changed in terms of play since early access just more minions added, level lengths increased, and a few bad design choices later we have another unfinished game.The bad: The price is a bit high for the game in it's current state (still broken).  The different monsters aren't balanced well as specific combos will wreck you (still broken)The game isn't balanced well level to level as there are spikes and complete cakewalks (still).The bosses are harsher than they need be (fixed but almost too easy). There are some very annoying enemy actions that bypass wards completely (kinda fixed).The voice acting is repetitive and needs more variety (still broken).The music needs more variety, and there needs to be more variety in the quests (still broken).  There is not much happening in your main chamber just dude staring at you, which gets old dude needs some other positions to chill in, and maybe have some animated actions happen. (still bad).Now that the game is out of early access it's clear it was rushed to it's current state.  I played a few hours on cakewalk, just to get my feet wet.  Switched to normal, and found that the game still needs a lot of work.  I'd say if you can get it for 50% off then it's a good time waster.  Just be prepared to be frustrated by mechanics that are still in the works. I mean you can log in and do two or three fights, if you are short of time and then log of again.But ... I am still at the beginning, but I already found myself more like: Okay, got 'em. So one more fight. Cool, got 'em again. Let's do one more fight. _childDocuments_.review: As far as i'm aware this is the first Darkest Dungeon-like game that has seen any amount of success (aside from the original of course). I hope this becomes a trend because the combat system has the potential to work quite well in all sorts of settings. Iratus adds new mechanics to the now familiar Darkest Dungeon style combat such as making your enemies go insane, single time use shields that block all damage from a certain type of attack, and spell casting that can be used once per round on any of your minion's turns.The out of combat management is expanded on somewhat from what is available in Darkest Dungeon. You create your minions from all sorts of different parts of varying quality; the higher quality the parts the more stat points you get to allocate into your minions various attribute fields. Iratus also implements a version of the hamlet from Darkest Dungeon by giving you Iratus' tomb to build out with different structures. These structures  give various bonuses such as healing a minion after combat if they're placed inside, or improving how much mana Iratus recovers after combat.The evil-side spin on the concept is certainly refreshing Iratus himself giving his musings about what's happening both in and out of combat is quite charming. The undead minions, despite being undead, all have personalities and little quips they send out during combat.It's clear that the developers saw Darkest Dungeon and didn't just want to make a carbon copy of it. I think this game really tries to stand on it's own two feet. Ultimately I can definitely say I had quite a bit of fun with Iradus: Lord of the Dead, but if I had pick out the most glaring flaw with the game it would be that it gets to be a bit repetitive towards the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Iratus: Lord of the Dead

_childDocuments_.review: I am impressed enough to actually write a review on the game.If you have been dying to play a similar style game to Darkest Dungeon, this is it and almost as impressive so far in the early access with lotsa potential down the road.  This would be the "evil" version of Darkest Dungeon as you are playing on the side of evil.  The voice over is just as amazing as Darkest Dungeon, the condescending and snide remarks are just as fun.  Just buy it and try it, you wont regret it.  You're going to keep going for "one more fight" until you realize how much you like the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Iratus: Lord of the Dead

_childDocuments_.review: (mini-review.)This game screams "Cheap Darkest Dungeon clone." and, in many ways, that's exactly what it is.  It's an extremely difficult rogue-like game, that is played by controlling a party of four fantastical characters that you upgrade/train over time, throughout the completion of a campaign.  Combat occurs in a turn-based fashion, like DD.  Graphics are 2D, like DD.  The game has a suitably dark and menacing vibe, like DD.  Most of the beats are lifted straight from its spiritual predecessor.Unlike DD, however, the game has a more forgiving range of difficulty levels and quality of life elements, including "insta-level brains", character component upgrades, and more forgiving necromancy character skills, allowing you to raise dead compatriots.  That only begins to touch the tip of the iceberg of a game with great art, fantastic voice acting, atmospheric music and fun/challenging gameplay.  This game may be a DD knockoff but in some ways, it exceeds its spiritual predecessor.Great for DD fans and strategy game/TBS buffs.  Highly Recommended.8.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Iratus: Lord of the Dead

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful rogue-like with great progression. Each run is a bit different and I enjoy experimenting with different builds of the necromancer and trying out different minions. I enjoy this game more than I ever enjoyed darkest dungeon. A+ game and improving with each patch. Latest beta patch is great and I am looking forward to unlocking the hardest difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: I looked this game up after seeing a few comparisons to Darkest Dungeon and I've had a lot of fun with it! _childDocuments_.review: I liked this game way more than darkest dungeon. It has way more options and mechanics, way more customizable parts. 1. The difficulty and learning curve...are properly designed. I started playing on "good always wins" right away and it was really challenging to complete. I think I won on my 4th try or so; the fact that I didn't have all the unlocks at the start and didn't know what enemies do certainly added to the challenge. The game was really hard in a most fun way. I had to make "scouting parties" which went into combat just so I could understand what enemies do (because monster (or rather human) manual is not initially unlocked). I had to carefully crunch numbers and calculate what stats I should upgrade. I had some tough "do or die" moments. I had to completely change my composition over the playthrough (I unlocked and tried every minion except locked dhampirs and ones which unlock after a win). What was viable early was not viable late; most compositions were not able to beat everything. I had to specialize and minmax minions a lot (e.g. I had 2-3 copies of the same minions with differently skilled talents/stats/artifacts). I had to constantly adjust my roster and to think about more than just 4 minions.Winning the game tasted supersweet after that.I hate games where you know you gonna win halfway into the game - because they are not tough. I also hate games where you know you gonna lose (eg. tome4 madness difficulty). This game was hard enough that I didn't believe I could make it till the very end, and yet I did it. It felt like a win against all odds. There certainly is room for error. I lost several upgraded squads with artifacts; the game is not over after that. However you hav to adapt and not do the same thing over and over.2. VersatilityThere are certainly many compositions and ways to play. There are so many synergies! There are ways to utilize anything, there are no useless items or units. Love it.3. ConsThe main issue: levels are certainly too stretched. They are designed similarly: at the beginning you are introduced 2-3 new types of minions, you fight them (probably get rekt). Then when you have just learnt how to deal with them, 1 by 1 new types of minions are added and you have to adapt. It is a nice concept, but it is a bit too slow. There are about 20 fights a level. I thing each level could be shortened to 14-15 fights plus a boss and it would be a more dynamic experience. In the last fights before the boss it is just grind; if you've progressed to the end of the level you already figured what to to and know how to deal with the enemy.4. Minor thingsI'd like the game to have:-more complex crafting. A bunch of simple recipies is just too few.-more spell variety; tbh many of them are too similar and serve similar functions5. Replayability Well, i think even if you play the game once, it is fun and satisfying and worth money spent.After finishing I am not sure I will play it again. On one hand, there are many things I want to try in this game. On the other hand, the playthrough took three days out of my life. The game is certainly too slow (geez, at least make animations slightly faster?). Probably I will play again to beat it at the highest difficulty but not soon.Overall, I had a blast; if you like challenge, get this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty good. It's constantly being compared to Darkest Dungeon. While it is a similar style game, I actually enjoy playing this from the Necromancer perspective a lot more. It's much more fun to drive others mad than to be the one driven mad. This game is difficult, but also quite enjoyable to play. I'm almost finished the game on More Pain mode, which is the second highest difficulty. Once this mode is complete, you have access to the highest difficulty. Unfortunately you don't unlock all the minions at the start, you have to earn them by completing the game on the more pain difficulty. I'm still missing 4 minions that will unlock once I beat the final stage and get a few more bones as drops. So far I've found quite a few strategies are very viable to win. For the first half of my run I focused on driving my enemies insane and giving them heart attacks with stress attacks. The main purpose of this was to unlock 2 minions; the vampire, by causing enemies to flee, and the wraith, by driving enough enemies insane. After this, I found a minion I enjoyed and built a team around buffing them. This was also very successful and I could often wipe out a full enemy team in two shots.

_childDocuments_.review: Very addicting game and thoroughly enjoyable if you like Darkest Dungeon or Tactical RPG/Rougelike games. The battle setup is obviously similar to DD and there are some light town management aspects here, but Iratus brings quite a few things to the table on its own. Mainly I felt there was more control over your minions and actions than in DD where sometimes bad stuff happened and you were just really screwed. There is less of that here. In DD you had to worry about stress but now the enemy has to worry about it and YOU get to inflict mental damage, which is a big change here. You can choose between physical, stress, or magic damage while mixing several different minion types to experiment. The addition of Iratus as a character that can be equipped with items and cast spells to benefit your party is really cool and another neat aspect that makes this game feel unique. The dungeon maps are sprawling with lots of events. My one playthrough took me just over 30 hours and I still have things that I would like to go back and get, so the replayability is nice. The game is difficult, especially in the later levels. If you have played games like this one before I would try it out on the second-highest difficulty and see how you feel first.

_childDocuments_.review: After 100 hours, I still cannot recommend this game.  It looks like darkest dungeon at the first impression, but the feel is very different when you are deeper into the game.  Unlike the heroes in DD, the minions in this game are very expendable.  With the right material, you can create an identical minion instantly.  The minions also have no attributes such as perks to make them unique.  I guess that's why I don't feel much when losing a long serving minion, which is pathetic. Difficulty is another problem.  The game has so many difficulty levels without meaningful differences, and learning from the outdated Diablo 3 doesn't do any good.  The first two difficulty levels are so easy that make the first two runs very boring.  It's a huge waste as the first run is most important to player's overall experience.Achievements are also designed with very low effort.  Most of the achievements are designed to kill X number of enemy in a level which are basically unnecessary grind.  To kill 1000 enemy in each level requires you to play about 12 runs and I probably only enjoy 3 or 4 runs at most.After all, the game actually has some potential but not best implemented in many details.  I wish the developers can put more thoughts into these areas and do better in the next game.

_childDocuments_.review: When Darkest Dungeon game out and rocked the RPG scene with its unique blending of mechanics and storytelling, one wondered if it could ever be replicated. And when Iratus: Lord of the Dead game along, that question was answered with a resounding; NO. And that's not necessarily a bad thing.While the game plays almost exactly like Darkest Dungeon, the key differences are that your units are far more expendable, you feel far more powerful, and the game eases up a lot on RNG which allows you to put together a truly terrifying powerhouse of a minion squad to pull apart any puny resisting mortals who happened to blunder in your way.The game of course isn't without its flaws; the difficulty spikes at times, some things aren't fully explained, and some balancing is just downright questionable. That said, the dev team seems dedicated and eager to listen to the community to fix what might feel broken, (And yeah, I'm sure you've heard that before, but this one is actually true). Overall, you're getting your money's worth for sure; an enjoyable and easily repeatable Roguelite RPG where, for once, the promise to play as the sadistic and creepy bad guys isn't an understatement. So if you liked Darkest Dungeon, but feel the pressure every time you boot it up, give Iratus a try for a more relaxed and experimental take on the genre. Just don't be surprised if you find yourself developing an evil laugh...

_childDocuments_.review: Its a great, satisfying itch for a game similar to DD. Animations, art, narration, music are all spectacular. Each unit has multiple abilities with 1-2 ultimate abilities that require a special resource from Iratus. I actually like this concept as it makes each play more strategic. Some of the units though are completely not worth playing, I'm looking at you Lost Soul.  She is actually really neat but the negative effects on the enemies do not even get close to out-weighing (or just making even) the positive effects she applies to the enemies as well. However, that's what early access is for and i'm certain things will get balanced out. My biggest complaint is the progression cycle. It gets old FAST.  Take DD, you had multiple options to progress and the paths weren't so linear. With Iratus:LotD, you only have one path, and if you fail its back to the very beginning for you. Now you do get to keep all the creatures that you've unlocked, BUTTT the cost to create them, level them and upgrade their parts completely destroys your run. When I reached the first boss, I had about 5 armed and level units, I beat the boss and lost all of them but 1. got enough materials to make a few new units they start at level 1 too, always. On the first battle of the second floor I lost my whole crew, and couldn't progress because you can't upgrade or obtain materials without WINNING battles. That is what kills it for me. In DD it hurt to loose your top units BUT you had ways to get them back up without having to start over. You had to grind and grind but you could get back and kick their ass.  In Iratus you don't, if you loose any of your top Units you are done, you'll slowly drain out until you have to start over. Once those level 5 units with Epic or Legendary parts that took ALL your materials on the whole first floor die you are screwed, and its not like you can go back and reload. DD punished you for mistakes but gave you time to learn and try again. Iratus Lord of the Dead, Punishes you, shoves you to the floor, kicks you in the balls/boobs. When you try to get back up it it jumps on you and cuts your head off. GAME OVER.Having such a major problem can ruin this game quickly, however there are several ways they could fix this that would be quite simple. I'm recommending because, it has huge potential, its the first day of early access and I want to give the team time to read the feedback and see what they adjust.  I don't want to have to change my recommendation to a thumbs down and I hope they truly listen to the feedback and make the appropriate changes. They have a great thing here and it would shame to see it crash.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recc. this amazing game. Really enjoy all aspects of gameplay and difficulty scaling / replayability to this game. If you're a fan of Darkest Dungeon, then you'll love this game, it's essentially the same thing but as the "bad guy". You learn to value your minions lives, even as undead and consider every move. The 3D Char. models have a little more gore detail to them than games like Darkest Dungeon, while the gameplay is super similar, the hub is similar to Darkest, but there's alchemy, raising the dead, and other rituals. On high difficulty you can easily get tons of hours battling in intense scenarios. My only complaint for this entire game is just actually the lack of map detail/variation with some stuff/lack of alt modes and some typos with some skilltooltips. I highly suggest having all DLC for all possible unit characters. 10/10 game, for the price, a steal. a MUST buy if you like Darkest Dungeon. High difficulty full runs could easily be 50+ hours and that's not even considering practice or redos, etc. Could really use a workshop and more DLC!! Basically darkest dungeon but opposite side

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderful game following the playstyle of darkest dungeon. I really like the minion designs, the skills and magical abilities are well developed and there are quite a few combos appearing to work in several occasions. The game is still in development so there are many additional features to appear but I believe the devs are heading the right way. I also like the addition of difficulty levels from noob to expert which is a very good element of the game. Finally I would like to see minions with healing abilities as the ones I have unlocked so far have offensive, defensive and supporting abilities (with the exception of vampires). I do not know if anyone of the locked minions can heal but if not, I would like to see this addition. Finally, as rng is rather important in this game especially in higher difficulties, I would like to see the choice to replay dungeons or at least complete the paths neglected in the first run. If you cannot rerun completed dungeons then I think that sometime in the final levels (or sooner) there may be a dead-end.

_childDocuments_.review: While its not finished, this is the spiritual successor for Darkest Dungeon; with the twist of playing for team evil while driving the heroes to madness and death. The game has terrific depth and tactics, with a fairly high learning curve if you're not familiar with the genre and style (ie if you've played Darkest Dungeon - its straight forward). Some thoughts on the good and bad; often comparing this to Darkest Dungeon if you've played it - (this is probably a mix of half review and half suggestions for the future).Novel twist portraying the villains (this can be a con for some). Though the villainy of the villain is left to the imagination, sure I'm bad and my enemies are elves and dwarves - but what awful thing is Iratus really doing? Without a story, it makes the necromancy more gimmick than story/plot (but fun gimmick!)Creating new undead is initially an interesting mechanic compared to DD and going to a wagon to recruit guys, but something still feels limited about it. There are static about mixing the same four parts to get the same undead every time. It has as many classes to pick from as DD, but there could be some more freedom or options here. When I first heard of the game concept that you'd collect parts from fallen heroic enemies to build your undead, I more imagined that assemblage of parts in random collections would build a sizeable variety of undead when instead the game let's you use four of eight basic parts (with standard MMORPG levels of rarity)  types to make statically similar undead from a set. Despite my original expectation; this system does work very well as done. I just think adding extra random parts to an undead, or building an undead without certain parts would add to things (A skeleton with extra bones gives extra arms and attacks, a zombie without a head is cheaper to make but lacks accuracy; etc).Along with the above, currently you can upgrade your undead with parts - but not downgrade them. One class (Lich) allows you to destroy your own undead in battle to gain an advantage - it would make more sense to plan ahead to destroy an old skeleton but remove its useful parts prior to the battle. Worse, if you do try to downgrade/unequip a part, its just permanently lost. Very annoying, feels more like a bug than a feature right now.Fights are very challenging, though the 3 available boss fights tend to be straight-forward once you figure out the strategy it takes to win (and the option of retreating is novel, letting you use teams to soften up tough foes or even scout out if you can trade some damage). Despite the name Iratus, you seem to do little more than cast spells from a distance while sending your minions into the fights. The "Quests" that come up let you choose an outcome - but there could be more done with the eponymous namesake of the game beyond wearing artifacts that give the occasional bonus to the team or casting spells from a distance. This could work with Iratus able to take the field himself as the result of some event (perhaps if the team is slaughtered, the cornered necromancer must fight himself with victory allowing the recovery of more parts). There really is no story line, its just evil necromancer breaking out of the mines and into a mansion filled with heroes set to oppose him. A more finished game should aim to flesh this world out, as ancient and evil as the necromancer is, some other hero/villain/rivals to overcome would give someone more emotional investment in the game. The game's crafting system adds nicely to the customization of the undead team, but here the limits feel even more confining - there are far too few items to craft, but combining parts for bonuses is very well handled. Turning items into mana or combining parts for greater rarity is well done and balanced it seems. Building the necromancer's cemetery lair is interesting, but archetect's souls are far too easy to come across (building an Obelisk feels pointless right now) and I like the tactical level of deciding if I need an undead fighting or in the crypts -- but storywise, I'm locked in the mines trying to escape so where exactly is this crypt? This game really needs a narrative cohesion - but if you suspend a desire for story it still can work. The mechanic of deciding if you want to damage foes or drive them insane is terrific and adds quite the depth to the game. Though it is odd to have a foe escape as a cursed male and return to your team later as a female vampire (small thing). The mechanics of how the game works is absolutely the best part, its clearly well-developed, complex, and yet easy enough to figure out within a short time of beginning play. The developers say it'll take hours, it took more around 30 minutes for someone familiar with this type of game.All this aside, it was a great way to spend about 15 hours playing through the released content so far. I'm firmly looking forward to more.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the game a lot. As a lot of other reviews say, it's very similar to Darkest Dungeon and if you like that game, you'll probably have a good time with Iratus.  It has a LOT of potential to be brilliant and it's definitely a beautiful gem to stumble upon, I'm hoping the best for the developers and as I write this review, I've already gone and bought the supporter pack not for the pretty goodies it comes with, but in hopes of giving them the funds they deserve to make an amazing game.All in all, everything's reversed in Iratus. You're the supreme bad guy, the necromancer, the big bad evil dude that wants to spread horror and mayhem everywhere. It's not just 'Darkest Dungeon but evil' though. There are plenty unique mechanics that you can get into that turn the game interesting; you craft your minions from parts instead, meaning you can control what you get, and each minion has a lot more unique abilities they can utilize, with various playstyles I'm discovering. Stances also apply a lot of interesting stuff to the game. If I had any critique whatsoever, then it'd basically just be anything you'd expect to hear for an early access game. Namely the difficulty. I have to play CAKEWALK to get any progress, and even then, I get ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ destroyed in some playthroughs. Thank god the devs havent made corpses a thing. (though id find it interesting if they did, since well, you're a necromancer.)
_childDocuments_.name: Iratus: Lord of the Dead

_childDocuments_.review: Necromancy? Darkest Dungeon style mechanics? Slay the spire esque aspects? SOLD!There's a LOT of potential here for a solid game. The good: - It's sort of reverse darkest dungeon only without all the overt "f**k you" mechanics being tossed at you endlessly save for a few elites it has "f**k you" moments but those seem mostly like teething issues of early access.- No corpses... I cannot state how awful that change to DD was. Simply awful. If you like DD but hate corpses this is for you.- In an inversion of Darkest Dungeon, you get to "stress out" enemies and have them flat out die or go insane and attack their own guys. But some enemies WANT you to stress them out and gain bonuses from being insane. Great fun! nice to be inflicting the stress for a change :P- It's aesthetically pleasing, if you like all the edgelord stuff and I do so +1 from me ;) - The devs are active on the discord and folks are on there talking strategy and being chill so nice playerbase. -  Insane potential with it's premise and marrying of two different sets of game mechanics that we all know and love/hate. It's early and needs work but it's fun as heck.- No needlessly censored and understated/hyper realistic female clothing. The monsters are monsters and the female form monsters are not bound by the "You need to have realistic armor!!!11!!!one" nonsense. They're reanimated corpses and bound spirits. It's fantasy and that's that. So it's artistically chosen to go with classical fantasy tropes in clothing. I missed this stuff.The bad:  - It's overtuned a little and "cakewalk" is not the cakewalk it states xD but it's still fun if you consider that normal mode. - The unlocks are a tiny bit grindy, stuff like damage your own minions or kill x amount of people. They're nice to have but they seem like an afterthought in some cases and in others teach you mechanics on how to use the minions better. I love the latter and dislike the former. I see what they were doing and it worked mostly but it's also annoying given a few of the starting minions are a little under-tuned or too fragile. In time that might be less of an issue. I'm used to terrible unlock systems and grind it's just irksome to see them done in a way that's not as interesting as they should be. Might change in future though.- The talent system is kinda full of fluff. You could remove half of the talents and no one would notice. Some being amazing, others feeling like they're in the way to something you could use. A ton of the talents should be baseline tbh, it would free up a lot of strategies early on and give a better range of options in how to use the earlier out of the box unlocked minions. - It seems to not know if it wants you to callously sacrifice your minions for victory or build them up for more competent strategies because of the permanence of death of minions. This is going to be difficult to balance and design around and I'm surprised it works this well already. Mainly because you can get "brains" which can be placed into minions in order to instantly level them up. But this is tied in with the iffy talent system and naturally this is sort of dichotomous with the item system, spending a ton of resources which are used to create new backup minions to create items only to lose them to a string of crits, leaves youwith the impression that items are for the most part pointless. Powerful but pointless. In short                                                                "Brains op. Equip items poop" - Me, just now.- The city building part is good but half baked at the moment. This is probably because there's no endless mode and only three of five floors released as it stands. You gain points on wins (altered again with... talents ugh) which allow you to sacrifice a minion and some points to gain long term bonuses, it could be that it's only three floors that this effect is hampered but... it's great, it's just not implemented as well as it could be. For one you have to sacrifice the minion AND then use another one to staff the building, whichever minions you use to staff doesn't matter. Only that you throw them in there and in a game where resources are tight until about the mid point of act 2 IF you build right. I can see some folks resenting the +10-50% chance increases to gains and the huge costs that if you neglect at all from the beginning. Are pretty pointless. Yet at times seem mandatory. I just wish it was implemented differently although it's NOT that terrible a system.  - There's a few small crashes here and there nothing major. This wouldn't be an issue only, if you crash out of an encounter just as you surrender out of one, you lose all minions deployed in the fight. So crashing + losing team entirely + scarcity of resources to make more + no brains (heh) = scrubbed run if you crash. Ah, early access. Think it's running on unity too, this is the RIGHT type of game for unity but unity will ALWAYS suck. Horribly suck. - There's a lot of "figure out out as you go along" and while I don't like handholding and enjoy finding out things. Being told what the mechanics of the sacrifice encounter tiles would help a ton. Knowing that each specific minion sacrificed will give you items that match the rarity if their parts AND a specific artifact which Iratus equips for entire run boosts. - Some of those artifact boosts don't work or don't work as expected... You might think it's for lich summon spam and sacrifice play which takes some set up to even get going for it's "every 3 minions that die grants you max mana" on one set of robes for example. Only it seems to either only work once per fight or... not at all on summoned minions dying. Tooltips need a massive going over. Artifacts have massive potential for fun and build complimenting but as it stands they're barebones. Heh, get it?- The alchemy system is pants, it compounds other issues or suffers as a result of them. It needs an overhaul but it's a nifty idea, just needs iteration and for the love of bob. A few "combine all of X" or "combine all to highest" so you don't have to spam clicks.This is all I can think of for now, bear in mind I adore this game and haven't stopped playing it since I got it. Not bad for a few Ruskies with a kickstarter :P Just pick it up, it's great fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Iratus is a turn based strategy game similar to Darkest Dungeon.  And by "similar" I mean HEAVILY inspired by. The position of your character affects the types of skills you can use and the position of your enemies affects the types of skills that can target them.  In Darkest Dungeon you upgrade your hamlet and in Iratus, you upgrade your graveyard.  What separates the two is the crafting of your characters rather than picking from the random offering of the stagecoach, and the theme of the game.  In Iratus, instead of playing the role of the heroes, you are playing the role of the evil horde attacking humanity.  Overall an enjoyable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy Darkest Dungeon but get frustrated by the random and capricious nature of the RNG-based difficulty spikes, then give this flipped version a try. Furthermore, the level of minion customization and skill-tree unlocks allows for great variation in strategies and play style. Overall, even though this can be accurately described as a Darkest Dungeon clone, I'm really enjoying the additions and tweaks made to the basic formula, and as a long-time fan of Dungeon Keeper and similar "evil is good" titles, this one definitely scratches an itch.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - While my vampire used her own blood to debuffed the wannabe heroes, I lost my ♥♥♥♥ when my goul chick simply ate the poor damaged bastards! While the ladies did the killing, my ghost dude simply floated there, buffing himself up to become unhitable... (is that a word?) Great game, highly recommend!May 2021 - I've followed this game since it early days, waited for the right time to approach it. Saw it on sale and bought the core game to try it out... 27 game hours later, the campaign is finished and I'm back to get the DLC and Supporter Pack. This is the kind of game and developer I'd like to support. You start the game on easy and get though a basic tutorial, once finished you get to continue on easy or start new and choose difficulty. I chose the middle way, normal difficulty and while there were some tough fights none of them felt unbalanced or unfair. The bosses were really fun and provided a different type of challenge than the ordinary level-fights, which in themselves also never felt tedious or boring since the constant mix of enemies brought different need of tactics.Your own creations/minions combined with the gear you find (loooooot baby!) gives possiblity to create optimal gear+minion+magic-tactics, but there was no need for that on normal difficulty. I simply played with the latest monster I unlocked, changed when they were low on life and made new ones or got new ones though the levels. You get plenty of material to make new monsters/minions should they die, but that happend very rarily.Progression felt OK as well, never too far away to unlock your next thing (on my first play through) will try again on difficult and see how the replayability is. And then there's the DLC for the additional level, and ending.Great game, have fun scaring the life out those poor puny heroes. Moahahahaha!

_childDocuments_.review: So as of now, the game has just gone into public Early Access, and is still very much a beta. I expect plenty of numbers to be changed as it develops.Traps are a neat mechanic that makes you value movement skills so much more. Sanity damage is fun to build around, and seeing you're enemies flee in terror or have a heart attack and die goes great with the atmosphere of the game.The ability to string together your army from the corpses of enemies is a great idea, as well as just slotting in a brain to make your units level up quickly. In fact everything to do with flavor is already amazingly on point and it makes the game much easier to get invested in.That said, this is definitely a beta, and there are lots of balance issues, the most glaring of which are golems and bosses.Golems have no sanity meter, and hit like a truck. When they are too far away to hit you, their move that pushes them up boosts their accuracy, So if you build with stress in mind, the regular golems are often harder than elite fights.Bosses are naturally quite strong, and are where you really notice the game's lack of healing. In a battle that lasts many many rounds chip damage and crits add up quickly. The first boss could be fine with some minor changes, but the second boss needs major changes.At this point anything extra would be rambling, So I will just end by saying that I do really enjoy this game, and am excited to see where it goes.

_childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes for this, but the end result is a game that lacks flavour beyond it's initial appeal. There's a lot of potential, but it just falls a bit short on depth compared to its competitors. There is very little variety after your first playthrough. While each minion is interesting as a base, there is really nothing that builds off that. They have no unique traits, so they all feel generic. The items are very samey and plain so growth feels stagnant. The parts mechanic could have been an interesting way to cobble together unique minions from spare parts, but instead they're merely flat stat points. You can experience everything the game has to offer in one run, easily unlocking nearly all the classes, and it unfortunately doesn't hold much for you after that. If they added more personality and depth it would be an easy recommend for me. If minions had traits or growth that separated them from others of the same class. If items were unique and build defining. If parts made a minion instead of feeling tacked on. If events were events instead of fights with a minor temporary buff if you win. If there were more unlocks or unique minions past the initial few. if. if. if.The setting is neat, the voice acting is great (notably the main voice actor), being the bad guy is cathartic, the mechanics *would* be appealing if they has substance. But all in all it just doesn't feel fleshed (heh) out. It could be worth it on a deep deep sale for a playthrough or two, but other than that I unfortunately can't recommend it when the competition is so stiff.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is almost good, but it has couple really horrible design decisions, that makes it really bad and boring.First time I was playing I completed the tutorial and started playing on hardest difficulty that was available, I made few major mistakes and lost pretty quick. After that I figured out I give a try on easier difficulty called "more pain".I got 1 single artifact that gave my units 6 armor, this caused most of my units to take any damage during combat and made the game way too easy, I used this item till 3rd dungeon. And it was just boring grind, not a challenging experience at all and game got really boring really fast.After this I figured out I change my strategy to use heart attacks against my enemies. This made the game little bit more interesting trying different builds for a time, but in the end everything I tried just worked and there was no challenge at all.All the combat was starting to feel really same and I started to wonder how long does it take me to finish my run.I ended up spending like 7 hours in fights that proved no challenge and was just a grind. The final boss fight was way too easy also, I just used my same group of undead that I had been using for long time and beat the boss on first try.I don't understand why game designers made it so that the dungeons are so long, instead they should have only like 3-6 fights before boss and more optional events with more interesting mechnanics.I feel this game would be much more fun if the runs would take only maximum of 1 hour and would only have 1 difficulty where the game would be balanced around it. I will probably give game another try on harder difficulty, but knowing that it will take ~7 hours to complete my run and losing all my resources will cause me to start from beginning...Also the mechanic of unlocking stuff is really stupid, I would have wanted to start expanding my graveyard more, but I didnt have specific units unlocked so I cannot still do everything if I start on the harder difficulty now.Everything should get unlocked after playing the tutorial.Looking at steam achievement stats, only 3% of the players have achievement "I'll Be Back!", that means player has lost a run, seems like most people probably got bored in the grind and stopped playing after finishing 1st or 2nd dungeon.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who plays a lot of Darkest Dungeon on my Switch and some on the PC I am a huge fan of the genre.  I have had my eye on Iratus: Lord of the Dead since it was first announced on Steam and so happy that it is now released to Early Access.The big stuff out of the way first: 1) While it shares a lot in common with Darkest Dungeon it does make plenty of changes that set it part and improve on the formula.   Normally I am not a fan of playing the bad guy but this game certainly makes playing the bad guy, "good".   Some people will think that the only difference between DD and Iratus is you are playing the Antagonist however that is really one of the minor difference.  So if that is your concern you can reset easy, it isn't just a reskin of Darkest Dungeon.  2) That game was completely stable during my 90+ minutes of playtime so far.  No crashes or bugs that I could tell.  I also didn't notice any mechanic bugs, however as I am still getting the hang of the game it could just be that I wasn't aware of them.The fun factor is there as is the, just one more turn factor.   The artwork is nice and the voice acting is good too and has plenty of humor.   Combat is pretty straightforward if you are used to Darkest Dungeon.  Like Darkest Dungeon if you go straight for the enemies health you may be sitting yourself up for failure.  The game is all about strategy and getting to learn your enemy.   Even after a few run-ins against the Doomsayer I still make a lot of mistakes against that particular character/class/enemy that would have had me pulling my hair out, if I had any.I am a firm believer in posting an initial review and then coming back after I have a fair number of hours under my belt and reviewing.  That said if my gaming time continues to be as fun as it has been so far then I feel that this is a game well worth the asking price and can't wait to see where the developers take it.

_childDocuments_.review: 🔥🔥  I am having a blast with this one! 🔥🔥      💀 Along the same lines as Darkest Dungeon with the same combo character related strategy and base town with upgrades. _childDocuments_.review: To me, this is a true Necromancer's dream. Unlike Darkest Dungeon, YOU get to be the antagonist to the 'heroes' of the world Iratus has risen in. While more forgiving (To a degree) than DD, it still does require a fine tune plan when tackling the various enemies you will encounter on each level. You are given hints as to what you are fighting, but unless you have fought these and memorised their abilities (I'm 90 hours in, and I've yet to.) it's going in just as dark as if you hadn't known the roster. Each undead has their own unique skills that can be morphed into a new one, with two choices to choose from. Some undead are better at striking at enemies sanity, some are better at tearing flesh and health, while some can be tuned to run a middle path and devastate both. Each minion has specific items tuned for them only, as well as a vast plethora of 'universal' items that any undead minion can use. With a recent DLC, potions were added to the game which can help tip the battle in your own favor. That's just the tip of the sword, as Iratus himself also has his own skill tree with spells and buffs, and a graveyard for upgrades... and the art style is one of the best I've come across(The Ghoul, am I right?). It is a nice breath of fresh, rotten air as I see myself coming and playing this roguelike more than I do Darkest Dungeon. It's worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: A rather poorly inspired attempt to show the other side of the Darkest Dungeon's mechanics. You will quickly find yourself in a defeat spiral because you are not allowed to backtrack, farm, and approach fights tactically. If you want to play a game where you will end up in an utterly untenable position and be forced into restarting the whole campaign because of one bad fight - even if you tried to scout the fight out and come up with a plan - this is the one for you. It's a grind monkey festival, albeit a short one, which is another thing not in the game's favor. Don't bother trying to play at higher difficulties at the start since the base building mechanic is tied to being a grind monkey and killing enemies in special ways to unlock the units you need to expend to achieve higher tier buildings.There's a lot of good in the game, but it is overshadowed by the misguided attempts to force replay value into a short campaign which boasts as its main difficulty point "bad loot RNG." Play Darkest Dungeon until the game is finished and if it is better.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very tepid recommend. Iratus steals a lot of good ideas and has some problems, but overall I enjoyed it for a while.Iratus is a turn-based dungeon crawl almost rogue-like. It isn't a true rogue-like, runs can take 10 hours or more, and the number of meta unlockables is very small, so it feels more like a permadeath run with little, or no, reward for failure than it does a rogue-like.This game borrows HEAVILY from darkest dungeon. As result I am going to say it right now, if you have not played Darkest Dungeon play that first and don't assume because you liked Darkest Dungeon you will like this. Iratus is not as polished and creative as darkest dungeon so the experience just is not as good (normally I would't compare two games like this but Iratus forces the comparison by taking so much from the prior).Gameplay wise the bones of the game are good. You have a dungeon you go through room by room, fighting enemies in 4 v 4 turn based battles, with lots of mechanics and resources to use and balance. All the interesting stuff, like the stress mechanic, sending your minions to town to rest, having to get used to losing characters often, is pretty much all taken from Darkest Dungeon. It all works and it can be pretty fun to plan your battles and then play them out.Art and atmosphere wise the game is fine. I found the production values to be pretty cheap but passable. Again they try to ape Darkest Dungeon by having a narrator comment on things going on but the voice acting and writing is nowhere near as good.I personally found the difficulty curve and the meta progression to be pretty bad and resulting in me quitting so early. After the tutorial I jumped into the highest difficulty it allowed me to. While the beginning was a bit of a struggle, it actually started to turn into a cakewalk by the end where I was drowning in resources that I didn't need. By the end of my very first run I had unlocked almost everything. I then played a new run maybe 10 minutes to quickly unlock the remainder. Then I start a run on a higher difficulty I had just unlocked. Those first few floors were great, probably the most fun I had in the game, but then I hit a difficult boss and I realized that maybe I had made a mistake in how I got here. 10 hours into a run where I was not going to unlock anything I realized that maybe I should have done things differently and should start over. No thanks. Without the incentive to unlock more there really was nothing keeping me around after needing to restart.Bottomline, I got 1 and 1/2 good runs out of my 20+ hours play time, had some fun, but ultimately I do think the game borrows too much Darkest Dungeon and really messes up its meta progression.

_childDocuments_.review: Many reviews praise this game for its difficulty scale being more logical and giving you more control than Darkest Dungeons, but I personally found the whole game loop to be quite repetitive and boring; The tutorial basically runs you through most aspects of the game, leaving little to discover on your own. What's worse, the difficulty scale in this game comes mostly from whether or not you're ready to read heaps of text and descriptions, for each available unit you control, and each enemy you will encounter. It's basically a case of memorizing what anything does, what weaknesses and strengths anything has, and applying it in battle. That's it.Some might say that's the premise of many, many games in this genre, but I feel like Iratus really is the worst offender in the category, as most learning has to come from studying the game rather than experiencing it.I dunno, might be fine for some, but I'd rather learn by doing rather than studying.

_childDocuments_.review: One design decision ruined the whole game.  Never written a bad review before but I hope folks read this so that if they are looking for a challenging roguelike game, they avoid this game.  ISSUE:  3 levels of difficulty when you start.  You are expected to grind out a complete run on one of the first two easier settings in order to unlock all the minions.  A couple of the locked minions are necessary for the last boss fight of the highest difficulty setting that's available to you (there is a higher 4th level of difficulty but that is locked).The problem is that even on easy, the length of the game is very long and so you are expected to grind out one of the two easy levels just to be able to beat the 3rd difficulty level.   Why is this a problem? because the easier levels are boringly easy and you won't realise this until the very last end game boss fight of the 3rd difficulty level. No matter how hard you manage to make it through the 3rd difficulty level, this decision only becomes apparent at the last boss fight and completely ruins the game.

_childDocuments_.review: All in all a worthy waste of your time ;)If you like Darkest Dungeon, but always wanted to play the bad guys, then this might be of interest to you.The core mechanics are pretty similar:You create a team of up to 4 evil minions, unlocking more and more the more you play. Each minion has a prerequisite to unlock it throughout all playthroughs.And each minion has different stats and skills, some being tanks, some buffers or debuffers, some damage dealers, etc.Many minions you unlock later can fulfill similar roles, so you can perhaps swap them out, but still play the same kind of combo.There are 3 different kinds of attack: physical, magical and mental.The first 2 are self-explanatory and mitigated by armor or magic resistance values. The latter is where the game starts to become fun, since stress attacks target the heroes' sanity (just like in Darkest Dungeon, only you are the one dealing stress ... and the attacks are much more devastating). I found this to be the superior strategy early on, since enemies tend to have a much lower stress bar than health bar ... and your minions generally deal more stress damage as well. With a few tweaks, stress attacks can induce "panic" very easily, which gives the enemy a nasty debuff of some sort.The more I moved through the levels though I found that a strong physical team is less fragile and more consistent, albeit a lot less fun. Which is imho the first real problem I've encountered with the game: It's a bit unbalanced. At least on easy (I imagine it's just getting worse on higher difficulties).My final team consisted of a werewolf, a ghoul, a reaper and a bride. I could have used a vampire for the bride instead, would have been good as well. A "shuffle-heal" team. The Reaper healed all allies after every kill. The werewolf healed automatically before every turn. The ghoul can also almost constantly heal and the vampire has an ultimate skill that lets her heal with every attack. Combined with some actual armor upgrades and this team was simply unbeatable.Around floor 4 I got bored with the game due to that reason. I "could" have tried out other combos more (I did try all minions at least), but I felt, why bother?Unlike Darkest Dungeon Iratus is a strictly linear game. You will inevitably advance towards your goal, unless you reset the entire floor. This is one of the main drawbacks compared with DD. DD is an "endless" game. You can just play a quick dungeon with whatever units you have available ... but you also risk it all. You have random encounters, secret bosses appearing, pitch black runs for more loot, challenging bosses to tackle, just vastly different arsenals and interplays, different biomes, different enemy compositions, etc.In comparison Iratus is just rather "boring". It's alright for one playthrough, maybe two if you really like, but it doesn't offer that same level of just "playing one more dungeon". Darkest Dungeon has the hamlet as an additional progression system, Iratus has, well Iratus. You can upgrade the necromancer in various ways, but most upgrades are spells ... which you can only use 1 or 2 times during a battle usually, unless you have a minion that gives you back mana. The items Iratus can wield are also rather limited. And at least I had him fully upgraded until the end, but actually didn't want 90% of the upgrades.The graveyard upgrade is another comparison to the hamlet, but also just stat boosts, I've had it fully upgraded almost by about the middle of the game. Then I didn't know what to do with my over 1,000 souls ...If they'd ever make a sequel I'd wish they'd invested more into actually making the gameplay more fun in the long term. Going from battle to battle got boring rather quickly, especially since enemy compositions were often the same. Animations are "alright", but nothing to write home about. Models are really nice though as well as backgrounds. The weird round shadows are unnecessary though. I'd like a deeper progression system (unit progression is fine) and a better alchemy system. I didn't bother using potions.And the unit roster UI needs improving. You "can" have 1 unit of each type, technically, but 6 or 7 will always have to be either in a healing or XP building in the graveyard to make room for the others (you can only ever have 16 minions present).It's definitely worth playing for, even if it's just to listen to Iratus' great voice actor! I just wish the game had more ... "theme"? In Darkest Dungeon every enemy is a masterpiece (and actually dangerous), here, most enemies just seem so bland, especially in the last floor, which lacks complete cohesion (though there is an in-game explanation for this).

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a great mix of Darkest Dungeon and other similar indie rogue-like games. It's niche is you are the bad guy this time, no sanity required.The grind has been pretty much completely removed as you progress in one big dungeon with a boss at the end of each floor with multiple paths without the ability to change paths or go "back" or any way of farming outside taking paths with more enemies than others.It has a lot of characters, it's voiced by the guy from Blood. Pros:*Lots of Characters, good level of tactics and different approaches*Nicely streamlined between moving units from working in your buildings, raising more units and progressing*RPGesque Talent system and ability to use Magic and actively helping your undead party is sweet*Fun, expansive. Great visual design with an awesome evil vibe.Cons:*Bugs, like multi-thousand critical strikes, Armor, Block & Ward calculations going wonky at times. The ability to lose resources by backing out of transmuting them/putting another item ontop of them.*Balance is needing a bit of a fix, but for early access is pretty awesome. The sanity battles need a bit of work tho'*The voice acting work while good, isn't varied enough. There needs to be more voice acted lines with Iratus speaking, and I really feel the writing in a lot of spots/the takes don't represent how great of a voice the actor has, also makes it feel very early access. I hope the devs got the budget for more voice acting. More lines, more jokes, much more variance is needed.Conclusion is that there is the makings of one of the best, friendly Roguelikes to come out. It's a streamlined, annoyance-removed, grind-removed tactical roguelike with a really neat vibe and potentially with more updates, extremely expansive and varied.Current state is a 6.5/10. But everything for a 10/10 is in the works. Buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to like about this game, but the UX is a poorly-conceived click-fest. It is straightforward, but inelegant. There's a lot of extra steps and pop-ups that all could have been done in a single pane. In a game where UX choices are the core gameplay, this is fairly unacceptable. Additionally, they have irritating grind achievements. I'm getting older, realizing I have fewer and fewer clicks left, so my tolerance for sloppy design choices has gone down.If you liked Darkest Dungeon, this is a fine purchase, but if you haven't played it, go get that first.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, this was a pleasant surprise. It's like Darkest Dungeon, but - by and large - fairer and more streamlined. Better grouping and presentation of information, for instance. Accuracy is tracked per combatant rather than per individual ability, so estimating enemy hit chances involves far less guesswork or wiki-delving.Also, you play as a sinister, conquering necromancer voiced by the delightful Stephan Weyte, whom greybeards like myself may recall as the voice of Caleb in Blood, or Nathaniel Claw from Captain Claw. The necromancer himself takes the place of the Ancestor from D.D. in providing narration during combat and otherwise. Instead of a hamlet, you restore a graveyard; instead of expeditions to dungeons with random encounters, you choose your own path through a smaller number of larger, Slay The Spire-style branching dungeons, fighting varied groups of highly questionable 'good guys' as you go.There is a large selection of minions, most of which are made available as you progress, and which then stay unlocked for subsequent playthroughs; each has its strengths and weaknesses, as well as variable growth potential; some minions can gain a lot of single-attack-nullifying Blocks and Wards, while others are focused toward permanent (albeit debuffable and bypassable) damage reduction or simply soaking up damage with high health and then recovering it. Still others are dodge-based.Enemies are much the same - the design is compassionate in that there are relatively few enemies who are simply powerful in every way. Rather, an enemy may have very high magical damage reduction, but no physical defence at all - or vice versa. Thus, with the foresight of examining the enemy types on the map before battle, and selecting minions suited to obliterating each of them while effectively defending against their attacks, you can often triumph handily.Similar to Darkest Dungeon, there is also a "stress" bar in addition to the health bar, which dictates whether someone will go insane (receiving a random impairing effect for the rest of the battle) or, eventually, die of a heart attack, regardless of their current health. Unlike Darkest Dungeon, in Iratus,  get to be the creepy undead bastards freaking enemies out and giving them heart attacks! Your own minions are, thankfully, not susceptible to stress. It all makes a nice change from the much-aforementioned game, and offers another avenue of attack which comes in very handy against many types of enemy, when compared to brute force physical or magical assault.The graphics are lovely, too; sure, "deliberately rough strokes" and "big black blotch over the eyes" and so forth are valid stylistic choices, but Iratus is  While still being quite gruesome and horrifying when it means to be. No reason not to look good while you're slaying the fools who oppose you, right? And they get to look good dying.Between the morally bankrupt opposition and the wonderful array of fearsome undead minions on offer here... not to mention all the spells! ...There are plentiful opportunities for maniacal laughter as you cleverly destroy one troublesome opponent after another. It's a game that is fun. Yes, some of the bosses pile on the BS rather high, but there are ways to defeat them as well, can confirm this even up to the expansion episode's finale at the third and final remotely sensible difficulty setting (though that took some doing, let me tell you)... but the game is, overall, fun. And that's something more games these days could stand to be.Heartily recommended to anyone who thinks it might be their cup of tea!

_childDocuments_.review: Iratus is a pretty fun game inspired by Darkest Dungeon. It abandons the lengthy campaign grind and hero stagecoach RNG; opting instead for emphasis on combat and creating your own minions as you prefer. Combat plays out similarly, with a caveat. You are expected to lose a lot of minions during your playthrough, so don't be frustrated! Minions are very expendable.If you were never great at Darkest Dungeon, you will struggle here. It's supposed to be hard. But once you find discover good party compositions, and understand the game mechanics, the game feels really rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a pretty entertaining game,  similar to darkest dungeon on the surface but honestly after playing it more I can say its a very different game. Its got some flaws with some unit compositions just being better than most others but overall the balancing issues I've heard about weren't as glaring for me personally when I went into the game myself. The reason most people compare it to Darkest Dungeon is because you have a vaguely similar formula in which you make a four minion team and send it up to fight some heroes, in this game though you are the one dealing sanity damage and so forth and on lower difficulties your minions are somewhat expendable. The higher difficulties  kind of have an issue where only a couple of unit compositions can really beat them realistically. The game is challenging but not to the point where its no longer fun, but you'll definitely want to tune your strategies up if you're going to do the higher difficulties.Regardless, it is pretty refreshing to have a game where you play as an unapologetic Villain too, not enough good games that play with that concept. The "evil" theme of the game is done pretty well and the minions you'll use all have some pretty fun and creepy designs. The game-play on its own is good but the theme and "soul" of the game is fantastic.Personally I hope the devs keep working with this title and continue to add more content for it, I cannot stress this enough but having "villain protagonist" games like this that don't suck is painfully rare.

This is done by traversing dungeons with varying themes.....Iratus does none of this and its just bland.Some idiot high on their own farts thinks we're all complete trash at games and need to be forced into journalist mode, so the initial game is just ridiculously easy. You have to complete the game several times...the pompous devs even have a disclaimer calling the game hard.....My god, how much more out of touch can one get?This makes the game incredibly boring. _childDocuments_.review: As it stands right now, I just can't recommend this game as it is way too frustrating to play. I've sunk hundreds of hours into Darkest Dungeon and can appreciate the inspiration from the game by the developpers, but some aspects of the game are just way out of balance.While the roster looks cool, you'll soon see that most of the available units are unreliable because the mecanics themselves are unreliable. You're gonna miss 90% chances 2 out of 3 times while the ennemies will double crit you on a 2% chance, you can't know for sure what you're gonna encounter in your next fight, some ennemies are just so brutal it's not even funny. The more you play this game, the less confidence you'll have in any action you take because the deck is so heavily stacked against you that winning is almost impossible. So what do people do? They find cheese strats or wonder comps that use "meta strats" to spam in every fights, because you just can't beat the game with legit casual play.And you know what? All of that is fine to some degree if your ressources weren't finite and losing your current run because you ran out of these ressources wasn't a thing.You're playing a game that tells you outright that your minions are replaceable but losing minions punishes you heavily. You're playing a game that takes inspiration from the greatest dungeon crawlers but also removes all forms of farming while still having the difficulty curve of a normal dungeon crawler.So many things are wrong with all of this and thank god the game is in early access and can be improved. Because it needs improving quite badly. The atmosphere is cool, the art is great, some gameplay mecanics are great and the bosses are challenging... but the core gameplay is frustrating, unfun, and not worthy of a good game.I'm not giving up on you, Iratus. But you're gonna need to work on a lot of things to make me go back.

_childDocuments_.review: If Steam had a 'meh' or shaky hand review option, I'd give this game that because it's not totally awful, it just doesn't really have much to recommend it, especially compared to its inspiration. If you really like old school fantasy aesthetics and Darkest Dungeon, you might enjoy it enough to ignore its faults. I personally could not ignore them so I’m gonna list them as I found them.Worst offender is that the game copies so much of Darkest Dungeon but copies it poorly or carelessly. It destroys Darkest Dungeon’s best feature, which is getting attached to your followers and their stories by turning them into generic undead troops with no real way to differentiate them. The game has also lost the pacing of Darkest Dungeon by turning the rhythm to a guaranteed battle-encounter-battle with no variation or suspense, with every encounter taking a handful of seconds and every battle taking way longer than it should.You’d hope that experimenting with build variety would be a lot of the fun of the game but while it starts well with a lot of buttons to hit to advance in combat, it trails off quickly. Each troop type has, generously, two viable builds and unlocking new troop types quickly reveals that there’s a lot of overlap, so even the process of building your squads becomes dull almost immediately.Finally, the choice to add roguelite advancement mechanics to a game with a 10+ hour campaign is baffling. The game is already so slow and repetitive that telling you to expect to play through the campaign multiple times, with every attempt potentially taking double digits of hours, feels like such a bad choice. But even that feels misjudged because despite the game’s marketing, it’s not that hard. I’m not much of a strategy whizz and I still never lost a battle or even came close to losing to a boss. So why the rogulite elements? Trend chasing, maybe?As an addendum, the game’s visuals are pretty uninspired, especially when compared to Darkest Dungeon’s stellar art direction, but also just very crass and distasteful. Every female minion and enemy has ample cleavage and generous jiggle physics and the only black character I saw had a voice line saying “sugah” and her description referred to her as ‘sassy’. Doesn’t take much thinking to realise that all of this could’ve used another pass.If none of that sours you, maybe pick it up on sale.
