_childDocuments_.review: edit: im changing the review to positive because I want this game to succeed and love the concept but im keeping my original one below ----vedit edit: THEY DID IT! Blocks/wards now affect crits! They listened! ahahahaThis is why you give games a chance boysOriginal review: ---vi really, really enjoyed this game and thought it was the game i was looking for until you get to higher difficulties.when you play on the game mode "good always wins" deaths seem to not root from mistakes anymore but instead getting your minions instantly destroyed by RNG, and then it inevitably snowballs out of the control because you have to play the rest of the fight from a disadvantage, or in cases like the Inventor (second boss) on good always wins, your entire team can get two-shot all at the same time by ONE of his attacks (not even counting his pylon which mimics the same attack) within under a minute. The only possible counterplay you think you can do other than hoping that the crits don't happen, is creating "blocks" or "wards" which flat-out prevent the next attack from damaging them, but guess what? Crits flat out IGNORE this feature so your team will be inevitably blasted to pieces regardless of whether you prepare ahead or not, and one of the solutions I can think of this would be crits being REDUCED to a normal hit while still consuming a block/ward, that way they would still be punishing but not to the point where your team all dies instantly within 2 turns in certain fights regardless of preparation. On the difficulty "more pain", lots of fights kept me on my toes and it was enjoyable and sometimes I didn't know if I was going to make it out alive, and none of it was because of random crits instantly slaughtering my team, for example lots of times it came where I had one minion left and I still managed to pull a victory out. I think this is the state the game should be in and it's actually enjoyable. But bumping up the difficulty doesn't really feel like it adds anything or any new attacks but just, bumps up the random crit chance and the game instantly becomes based on whether the dice rolled in your favorite or not and if it didn't WELP say goodbye and have fun restarting.It's sad to give a negative review because I really like the concept of this game and have been waiting for another hardcore turn-based game like Darkest Dungeon but the sheer amount of RNG that determines your fate and lack of skill and planning requirement on higher difficulties is just too infuriating and feels like throwing yourself at a brick wall over and over until the RNG gods bash you through. I'm sorry developers but something needs to change, like maybe add more tactical and different attacks and attack patterns enemies can do or make their AI smarter, or even just give them more health/damage rather than make it all based on random crits.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Revisited this game 3 years after, and boy have the devs have delivered. It has become one of the best rouge-likes I've ever played. Will buy the DLC shortly after I finish the story. Easily over 50 hours of enjoyment for the price.They included a quick save function, which is amazing to help you get your first victory and test the waters. The devs seem to have made all the right decisions. :)==============Just finished the Pyromancer (last boss, 3rd location) to finish the game on the easiest difficulty. I must say it was uber hard. I had a perma stun composition:2 back lines: bride of iratus2 front lines: skeleton giants (forgot the name?)I defeated her with the last skeleton giant with under 10 hp. My brides stun when hitting a critical, and I took all items and skills that buff critical to around above 70%. This was my 2nd time to try to beat her (counting only the times when I reached the boss). The trick for me was to use high damage attacks on the fire golems, and occasional AOE wrath attack by the bride to damage everyone, including the pyromancer, while the front line minions tanked. When the pyromancer starts using the shield, DON'T use any AOE. Or else you get hit by 30 magic damage, and the brides almost immediately die. That said, I REALLY think the difficulty needs to be nerfed down, or it will only appeal to the most masochist of players.Before this I had many compositions that failed. _childDocuments_.review: This game is like Darkest Dungeon, there are differences of course. But out of all the games that are like Darkest Dungeon, this one is it the most, and that's not a bad thing, but let the comparisons commence.The battles are extremely similar with the positioning of your troops and uses of buffs/debuffs playing way more importance than any other game of this kind. The one big difference between the two games in this regard would be the lack of corpses in this game, so killing an enemy will always bring them all forwards towards your position.There are more classes for you to use in your party but there seems to be a bit less variety when it comes to enemies and bosses instead.The city section is also quite similar but I found it a bit less useful here and mostly used the menus for crafting and creature customization.The map is a bit more like in Slay the Spire with a straight road with some branching paths rather than the usually also kinda linear, but occasionally labyrinthian levels of Darkest Dungeon.The artstyle is very nice, while not as striking as in DD at a glance, it all looks very good. Although it could have done with some more animations since while the characters all look good while idle or attacking, when they die they just turn into embers or something rather than having a real death animation, there's also no frames for blocking or such.At launch you have two out of four difficulty settings to play with, apparently you unlock at least the third one just by playing the tutorial but I dove into the second one which seems to be a medium difficulty setting. Right from the start I was feeling the game to be a fair bit easier than its predecessor and in the end I got the achievement for losing my first battle with a complete party wipe while facing off against the final boss (pre-DLC, since I don't own that yet.) I also had my second party wipe against said boss and then had to give up. The difficulty spike was pretty big, makes sense since it was the end boss, but while I did have some setbacks during the other parts of the game, even there the blows are made much softer because since you play a necromancer you constantly get body parts that can be used to instantly level up new soldiers, sometimes all the way up to where your fallen ones were at.TL;DRI think the game is pretty great but a little flawed.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun dungeon-crawling roguelite with several interesting leveling systems. The combat is very enjoyable and is very similar to Darkest Dungeon. The game has a lot of moving parts regarding its crafting and leveling systems, which makes the meta-game an enjoyable aspect as you manage your undead army. The art and animation is good and the game is an overall fun package. I would recommend this game! However, I can't help but feel like some of the gameplay aspects are too "phone game like." It's definitely not justified to compare Iratus: Lord of the Dead to a mobile auto-battler, but a combination of small details gives off that vibe. Overall though, I would say that this game is well worth it, especially on sale. It's an enjoyable strategy game with a fun premise that lends to the purpose of its well thought out systems. 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Very obvious darkest dungeon clone except that when your characters die you can just re-create them at the next checkpoint so you don't lose anything. That's probably the major selling point here. My main criticisms would be that each dungeon contains way too many encounters and they don't feel impactful, so you wind up feeling like you're just trying to click through repetitive screens. Things don't feel like they have the weight or impact of darkest dungeon. That said, if you enjoyed DD but wanted an experience that didn't make you want to scream when you got ambushed and your entire party suffered permadeath - this is a good alternative. I just wish there were fewer encounters that felt more interesting, than a bunch of encounters that felt trivial.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely cool premise very well implemented. There are so many possibilities with minions and spells, it's a necromancer's dream!The only flaw to me is that it's a bit of an RNG fest; the same battle can turn from a flawless victory to a crushing defeat, depending on which enemy uses what ability on whom. _childDocuments_.review: Fun game but it lacks depth. Great skeleton or backbone of a game here (pun intended) but to truly make it a great game it needs some work. I really want to love this game and I hope it continues to improve. _childDocuments_.review: Here's the real deal:Easier than Darkest Dungeon. Yes.  Easy to "fix a mistake".  NO.  People keep writing how it is "forgiving".  It isn't . It is MORE forgiving than DD, true, but you still can't really "recover" from some terrible wipes (if u wipe).   Let me explain.The game is a "Rogue LIte".  You get Minions (cool variety BTW) and you Follow a path to the "end"Cool, that's all self explanatory.   You can Make potions (if you have the DLC), which can compensate for some hard fights. You get Items (artifacts for your HERO, and Other Items for you MINIONS).   And they too can help your party if you do it RIGHT.   Artifacts can be REMOVED which means you can "change your build" when it comes to YOU (iratus)  but cant easily change the build for your minions. If you put an item there, then wanna put a new one in, the old one is gone. When you win a battle you get multiple types of 'xp'  (some for YOU, some for minions, some for anyone in one of your BUILDINGS that get xp... etc..)  You also get drops (Body parts to make stuffs... and Brains to LEVEL GUYS).    This is where there is CONFUSION on how to recover.  The theory is that you have a party of 4 guys lvl 30... and one die,, or two..  OOOPS.  Well no worries I probably got a brain or two laying around,  here's one at 28.. good enough, here's one at 31.  HUZZAH.  You make 2 new minions and throw them in.  Great,  Same level as before.Except NOT.   You still need to upgrade their BODY parts (which takes a BUTT TON of material you DIG up... ) and replace the two GOOD items you had on them.. So yeah, your guys are now the same level.. but their stats are way way way way lower.  And they don't have the good items.  There is no "replaying" a floor to get new items or farm stuff.  So you basically play with your party as is, and get more stuff (Hopefully) eventually.It's not as hard as it sounds.. At first.  On the first 2 difficuties, it's fun. You can try new minions, try new strats, try new builds etc... But all the maps, and all the fights are BASICALLY the same.  So no real variation.   When you get into the Third difficulty and beyond, there are VERY VERY few viable builds, for very few viable minions.   Youtube, and you will see.   So, you are kind of stuck running 1 of 7-8 parties.. and just doing the SAME map,  but against enemies that hit harder, and drop less loot.   Not great for replay in my mind.The voice acting is good, The graphics are good (for this obvious Mobile game ).. And the game is quite fun.   But don't go into it thinking "ahhh this should be easy, You can REPLACE GUYS"... you kinda cant... well not without an EXORBITANT cost.. (the brains are THE CHEAPEST of the things youd need).All in all, I'd say this is a 7/10  Definitely worth it on sale. DEFINITELY.Probably worth it full price too. You can get 20+ hours easily.  Maybe even 100 if you really wanna test yourself.  But again, keep in mind it is SUPER repetitive, It's just trying to do the exact same thing, against the exact same enemies, with the exact same minions.. but enemy does more damage etc...

_childDocuments_.review: Conceptually this is right up my alley: a dark (but funny) take on the Darkest Dungeon model. After playing through the tutorial and a bit of a normal run, I had to refund. TL;DR I wish I could give it a thumbs up but I can't. If you're a DD fan, maybe wait for a sale or give it a shot now if you're really hankering for something similar. Fans of Darkest Dungeon might find things to love here, but it lacks the polish of its inspiration. It makes up for that with its own character but its systems can't quite take it over the finish line. Definitely worth picking up on a sale, or after a few updates perhaps, but I can't recommend it in its current state. The combat is a bit slow compared to DD, and didn't pick up at all during my time playing. Minions are interesting, but upgrading them feels somewhat shallow / not very meaningful. In the end, your choices are mostly which stats (even in the abilities tree, which just increases stats and the attack's power type) and don't feel very meaningful. The expendable nature of minions lack the engaging character of DD--I always tried to keep my veterans alive and had a sentimental attachment to more than a few of those poor souls--whereas these minions are truly expendable with no meaningful differences between the next one you raise / sacrifice. This is a minor complaint, but: the voice acting for Iratus is REALLY awesome, love whoever they hired for it. That said I don't feel like I'm Iratus--or that I'm even supposed to feel that way! Who am I as the player? That might be a weird criticism, but I felt divorced from what story was there because of it. I wanted to see more but I wasn't willing to slog through the combat to get there.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a successor to Darkest Dungeon and I've got to say - I enjoyed this experience a lot more. Three major changes to the formula1. You are progressing your way into the world, this means you feel progression through a story faster and you're not just leveling up characters for the sake of making them strong enough to try the final dungeon.2. The sanity system is flipped, you can kill your foes with damage or stress and insanity checks occur on your foes. Much less infuriating and lets you build teams around a damage type instead of trying to heal stress3. Healing is sparce. Your team likely won't have a healer because what little healing options there are come with large drawbacks. Being the villain is great.

_childDocuments_.review: It is inspired in Darkest Dungeon, but I wouldn't compare them directly. This game is far less frustrating due to the nature of the game itself: - Here you're the Lord of the Dead and command hordes of undead units, not some guy in some town trying to be a hero in the darkest of times. - In Iratus, you craft your minions out of human limbs and they don't ask questions, they simply obey. In Darkest Dungeon you have a hard time convincing folks to fight incredible odds to ultimately die. - Your undead minions in Iratus don't panic, they fear nothing, they feel nothing, and would certainly won't bother dying again. When you start playing, go on for the Cakewalk difficulty (the 1st of 4 difficulties)  to learn the basics, then jump to the 2nd  to unlock units. The right way to play this game is on the 3rd difficulty, that is where the real hardcore tactical roguelike takes place. You'll enjoy figuring out how units work and how they do synergy together. There are specific units to counter specific enemies, you'll learn how to counter them. You won't get frustrated if one of your minions die, they were already dead anyway! You'll build new units to replace them.

_childDocuments_.review: Okey, this game has lots of potential, BUT, suffers from terrible design failures. 1. someone wrote a terrible RNG,Honestly, 118% accuracy vs 25% dodge will miss 4 turns continuously, 50% redirect will trigger 7 times continuously...so on and so forth. The RNG distribution is just terrible, in such a game, make a better distribution okey? The game actually knows about how bad its RNG works, so it offers a free "restart" battle option by quit current session and continue. well...if u KNOW how terrible the RNG is, u FIX the RNG, u don't waste the plyers time by restart every 10 minutes just because low percentage ♥♥♥♥ keeps happening. 2. horrible, horrible enemy design.It's okey u want every enemy to do sth different, and pose a different challenge. BUT, let's look at this random battle: barbarian, have to push it all the way back or it stuns your frontlines constantly.bard, have to kill her quickly otherwise it will just heal everyone back with no sweat.elven archer, u have to interrupt its stance, BUT it can also one-shot you if it decides not to use stance. so u have to kill it quickly. swordsman, this dude protects and also slowly gains damage buff, need to kill it before it grwos too strong. So in a word, the enemy design is simply that, "you have to kill this one first" on every enemy. Don't get me wrong, in "good always win", u can build your critter bride or whatever and quickly go through it. BUT, the design flaw makes the endless mode simply BS. Because EVERY ENEMY needs to be prioritized, i mean seriously, design some filler enemy that DOESN"T need to be killed in turn 1 or 2, so i can get my priorities proper. I worked in game industry for years and i know this pattern, it's called "ambitious deisgner". This is because the designer is afraid of designing something mediocre and unimpressive, so he made everything as impactful as possible. After some time when he gets better at game designing, he'll realise that, the game has to be composed by things that's impactful and things that's not. That's the healthy environment and a much better experience.3. monster talent pointsThis is very personal, but i have to be honest i like the previous iteration. Like we made a system, and then reading some feedbacks saying it's stiff. Instead of fixing it, we decided to simply turn everything into currency and let the player directly tune numbers. C'mon man, do more events/encounters, let player customize his minions through gameplay, don't let them customize by pouring currency(body parts) and tweaking numbers by "literally tweaking numbers". All in all, the game has potential, BUT terrible rng combined with "ambitious designer" makes the user experience awful. And then with certain systems i really don't like, my conclusion is a "not recommended".

_childDocuments_.review: I find the negative reviews regarding balance rather annoying, as most of the people giving negative reviews say they like/love the game but that it needs to be better balanced.  FFS people, it just released into early access and is very playable and fun. Of course it has balance and gameplay issues. Giving a game negative reviews because of something that's inherent in early access is only hurting the game and developers. Seriously, if you aren't up for playtesting the game in its early form just don't buy the thing. It's not complicated.As to my take, I love this game despite it's early access flaws. Obviously it is punishing, and needs work in terms of balance. That said, the core here is better than Darkest Dungeon imo. Not having to rely on RNG to build the groups you want to use is a huge improvement as are many of the "meta" level strategic elements that DD doesn't have (yes DD is a better game right now, I'm only talking about the foundation elements). Overall, right now, if you liked DD and have patience for a game in early access, this is a can't miss purchase. _childDocuments_.review: Due to the amount of effort from the Developers, a lot of the negative aspects already changed, and more changes are to come. Loot drops on medium and easy difficulties were increased, while abilities and spells that gave you loot were nerfed. Good change. Good always wins still needs to have loot drops nerfed though.Fortunately, one of the worst aspects of the game will be changed soon. This will allow a more strategic approach to the fights. I do believe, however, that a minor buff to enemies could balance things out.Developers that really care about their game is something that all players can truly appreciate. Developer and community engagement is def. something you can expect from this game.    Iratus: Lord of the Dead takes inspiration out of 2 very distinct games: Darkest Dungeon and Slay the Spire. You have the feeling of progression that Darkest Dungeon offers with the map layouts that Slay the Spire has. The problem with this is: Slay the Spire is supposed to be a game that you can play half an hour and then start over whenever you want, while on Darkest Dungeon, there's no limit to your progress. You can hoard as much gold and equipments as you want or just rush the game. I feel like this game should follow Darkest Dungeon's steps more closely, as the entire game is about progression, but you have a very limited run. My suggestion: Make levels bigger and make it a separate option. The easiest level of Darkest Dungeon makes dungeons smaller. On Iratus, there should be an optional difficulty setting in which you can make levels bigger.     On a game that is all about progress (minion unlocks, rarer materials, parts and so on), this just feels infuriating, and part of the reason why is because , which means that new levels will eventually come around and you'll have to start all over again to play them.     Now, I don't normally mind starting over a game just to play new content, but having my save deleted just after I finish the game feels like a good way to kill sense of progression. A good way to fix this would be to just stand still behind the gate after you finish the final boss, much like you do on the other levels before advancing to a new stage.     Well, not much to say here. You get 1 boss per level and that's it. The same boss, over and over. This is very detrimental for replayability as you'll easily get tired of these. As this game has an obvious inspiration on Slay the Spire, I suggest adding more bosses to the levels so you have a wider range of possibilities and strategies in which you'll need to use.    On Iratus: Lord of the Dead, you have natural resistances that reduces the damage taken, as well as shields that completely negates damage, but you lose them in the process. Crits bypasses both, shields and resistances. To me, this is sort of bad design since having 2 damage dealers with high crit chances can simply obliterate the enemy team before they can react. I suggest taking off the possibility to deal extra damage (as far as I know, you need certain upgrades to get extra damage) and just put something else instead. That's it. Again, the game is REALLY good and if you want to support hard working developers that are giving everything to make this game work, buy it!

_childDocuments_.review: Iratus is a turn based roguelike dungeon crawler that plays similarly to Darkest Dungeon yet has a lot under its hood that makes it really unique and different from it. _childDocuments_.review: I know what you're thinking: this looks edgy in a 2005 death metal frontman kind of way. Also, a ripoff of Darkest Dungeon. If that's what's bothering you, don't worry. Iratus might look like an laughable edgester, but he's also the narrator, and his voice and manner of speech are much more befitting a charismatic ancient necromancer. As for the ripoff part, nah. Since you're the forces of darkness this time, the gameplay loop is much different, and doesn't feel like DD at all. That's a compliment, if that's not clear. I liked this game, and after beating it on Normal, here's what I have to say. The game offers 4 difficulty levels. It forces you to play on Easy first with tutorial enabled, but once you get past that - which takes maybe 20 mins - you're free to start a new run on Medium or Hard. To unlock Hardest, you need to beat the game once. I played on Normal, and I gotta say, the game felt rather easy to me. I always had abundant reserves, my minions felt powerful, and I had a huge stockpile of material to raise new ones. Only the final floor and the final boss gave me pause, but for the most part it was smooth sailing. Which is not to say that it was boring. The enemies are unique, and so are your minions. It's fun to swap out minions from your squads to adapt to new combat situations. This minion for armoured enemies. This minion for debuffers. This minion for reactive enemies. Et cetera. Since you can fight your enemies both physically and mentally, stress is also a weapon, and combining hard-hitter with stress debuffing is so much fun.Another fun thing is that the game really makes you feel like a wretched warlock tinkering with body parts and magical reagents to create the best minions. Alchemy has many uses, for example you can produce finest quality body parts to produce strongest minions. And then implant them with your enemies' brains for instant levelup. Great stuff! This preparation mechanic is very elaborate, and you're given a lot of freedom of how exactly you want your setup to look like. I loved the feeling after an occasional loss, thinking "hmm... I'll need to improve the design on this one. Let's try again" and spending 15 minutes tweaking the minions' skills and stats just right.It's also very thematically coherent. Like I said before, Iratus (you) narrates his own story, saying things that you yourself are thinking, such as evil laughter on a crit, sighing on a downed minion, mocking your enemies on a swift victory. The music's a little monotonous, there is not much variety and that really sucks. Would be nice if the music would've changed depending on battle conditions or which chapter it is, but no. Oh, and if you're feeling squeamish about being an evil lord, don't be. Your enemies are shown to be the worst of humanity and beyond. Slavers, fanatics, greedy madmen. It feels very right to be purging those, it almost feels like you're the good guy here. (you're not, but you get the idea)What keeps the game going is the sheer variety of both your guys and your enemies. At the beginning, you have 6 types of minion to raise. There's some another 12 to unlock by achieving certain goals. Trigger insanity in x enemies, collect y bones, kill z bosses. Very exciting and after a while you have a good understanding of each minion's strengths and weaknesses. And you'll need them, as the game has 5 floors, each with stronger and stronger enemies, which are also thematically and mechanically different. For example, there are dwarves, many of which respond to stress by going berserk. This makes them take more damage, but also hit harder. Is it a good idea to use sanity attacks here? Up to you. Then, there are mages, which have naturally high magic resistance. So let's go with physical fighters this time, just make sure they don't die from strong spells. Those enemies block your attacks? So just pick a minion which has many weak attacks, so they can wear down their shields before you bring the heavy hitters. What I'm saying is: you want variety, there's plenty. My only complaint here is that the floors feel a little too long for what they are.If your fights are not going so well, you will eventually start losing minions, and losing body parts from which to craft more. It is possible to lose the game this way, if you run out. So it's a constant struggle. That said, I always had a massive stockpile, but I had in mind that a few bad fights and things wouldn't be so great anymore.Including the tutorial, the game took me 19 hours to finish on Normal. I might end up trying to play again on a higher difficulty, but I think I'm actually good. It was a great, complete experience. I invite you to try it out. Especially if you thought Darkest Dungeon was getting too hard later on.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of strategy games and rougelikes, Iratus feels like dream come true. It takes existing rougelike styles and takes an approach that ramps up the level of strategy and makes resource management a real component of the game. I managed to complete what currently exists of the game on my first run, but the allure of many minion types to play around with and the many build styles that come with that, along with higher difficulties to conquer, makes it likely I'll be sinking many many more hours into the game. The game is certainly difficult, but for the most part not unfairly so. And while the game needs balancing, the devs have been putting out balance patches on a fast pace and that is what early access is for. This game has plenty of content as is, and the roadmap the devs laid out for early access is promising even more minion types to try, more enemy variety, more dungeon levels, and just overall more variety to most aspects of the game that will further extend it's replayability. So far this is certainly early access done right.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:  Think of LotD as Darkest Dungeon, designed by a Euro company that puts out detailed city sims or RPGs with tons of complexity-by-design.  It is simular enough to be picked up rather quickly by a DD fan, but it is definitely different enough that you won't feel like it's just an extension of DD.  I find it enjoyable, but there is a bit of a learning curve that I think on hour 7 i'm just starting to realize what I'm missing...forget about actually playing well.DD has this game beat on style, story, mood, art, and a bunch of nebulous characteristics that I would call "cool".  But...this is still pretty good in those categories.  Looking at a video should give you all you need to know if you want to try it.  I definitely think if you like DD then this game does things differently enough that they don't cannabalize each other, and having both is enjoyable.So anyway, as to LotD itself?  The differences as I see it are "fiddley bits".  Like the difference between a German game and an American game.  There are lots more to fiddle with; town development is more complex, character levelling is more complex, combat is more complex, and there is the added difference from DD in that you as the master of your party can cast spells and carry your own items...you're not actually IN the battle, but you can affect it.This game puts a lot of focus on using fear/insanity effects, so you can either kill an enemy, or make them run.  Buffing is also a much more complicated process here; every class and every monster has a number of buffs...for themselves and their party.  It makes the puzzle aspect of the game more complex.One thing I wasn't a big fan of; I played this game a few hours when I first bought it, but skidded a bit a few levels in because I felt the added complexity didn't really add anything.  I returned to the game and the more I play it, the more I appreciate all the interrelated buffs and debuffs and counter-buffs and the multiple layers of combat, damage/avoidance/mental state, etc.What I didn't see is a tutorial.  I have done a cursory glance through the menus and it looks like after the first tutorial, you can't go back and do it again...not so cool  if you haven't played in a while.  There are also a lot of "oh, I didn't see that thing over there to click on it, it really affects the game".  It's almost as if the came has a search and click aspect with regards to the interface.  I still have a lot of questions on the interface (where do I see % to hit?) which I'm sure I'll get answers to in forums.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: It is fun!Without a doubt, this game will be compared to Darkest Dungeon (DD) and as someone who wanted to play DD, I could not withstand unfair difficulty using artificial over the top RNG situations and endless boring grind. With that said, I really enjoyed Iratus which is not just a copy of mechanics yet offers addition to the base formula of DD. In Iratus, player is the bad guy - Iratus the necromancer and player is opposing the good guys. Iratus doesn't have a volontiers for his army - he makes them from the remains of the defeated enemies. Better remains will make better minions and not only that - Iratus can replace parts of his minions if he finds the new ones. And there is a lot of different minions where player can make composition of minions with synergies he likes. Basic skeleton can have plenty of synergies with other types of minions depending how player wants to play. Iratus himself can cast spells directly but at the early game mana is scarce as well as wrath (wrath is Iratus' second type of mana used by minions for ultimate abilities if it makes sense). Each minion has 6 different abilities and combining them makes game amazing and urge player to try different parties. However, unlocking new minions is done through gameplay but remain unlocked for future gameplays from the start.There are some cute references like one boss is basically teenage Witcher Geralt with places of power!As for difficulty - it is not like DD! Player can start with easiest difficulty to learn the mechanics non frustrating way and then make a new run on the higher difficulty.Alchemy, cancilation, trinkets, consumables, sacrifices - all make sense and are easy to learn hard to master (on higher difficulties). Unlike DD, in Iratus, player has whole dungeons displayed in front of them to choose in which direction they want to go - similar to Slay the Spire. This way player might choose a path to get some random artefact/trinket but might loose valuable experience from the other path in some encounter. True, Iratus can craft some of nice trinkets but it is obvious they are very basic starting gear and already not that useful in mid game.Visual presentation is also very nice, well animated and voice acting for Iratus is a spot on! Music is also nice.Of course there is a room for improvement which I hope we will see in a form of a DLC or a sequel as the current game as a foundation simply inspires many possibilities. Like - we could maybe experiment with remains and create minions which are not in the necromancer's recipe cook book. Or maybe gathering rare materials to craft trinkets which are on par as those in the mid-late game if Iratus has enough skill unlocked in the talent tree (and forcing player to choose where to distribute Iratus' talent points more carefully).All in all - highly recommend it regardless if you are new to this type of games or not.
_childDocuments_.name: Iratus: Lord of the Dead

_childDocuments_.review: Long story short, it's Darkest Dungeon, but with the board swapped. You play as a Lich King who can summon undead villains to attack heroes. Heroes have stress bars, and will be driven insane if you can push them past the breaking point, and will have heart attacks if you push them further. The bad news is, Death's Door doesn't apply to your minions - they've already died after all. Even worse, your minions have few means of healing themselves as a full party. Expect your minions to die on a frequent basis, but be sure to keep them restocked and well-armed, as they still need to have hero-killing potential and your resources are steadily running out.

_childDocuments_.review: Very decent, challenging game that twists the Darkest Dungeon aspect over! While I enjoy being the bad guy and being able to dish out sanity to my enemies, there's a few points that bring the game to a crashing halt.1) Economy: This was my number one grievance while playing in the difficulties above "Cakewalk." If I lost my minions enough times, there was essentially no way for me to gain them back. While I appreciate that these enemies I've died to don't regenerate their health and such, if it's a boss, the player is left quite screwed.2) Minions: I liked that there were some which you only gained gradually as you progressed, what I didn't like was how overtly stronger some were compared to others. Skeletons and Zombies by nature make great cannon fodder and since they're starter minions, this was understandable. However, the synergy with Lich and/or Ghoul (a very overpowered minion) shouldn't be a deciding factor in my team compositions when there are numerous other minions to choose from. This could just be my lack in forethought how the other minions work, but I DO know for a fact none of my other minions do nearly as much damage as that Ghoul, not even the Dhampir/Bone Golem.3) Quests: I actually found myself planning my paths based on how many of these popped up. Lots of them were actually really cool, while others after effects weren't clear. For example, I received extra Vigor to Zombies, which appeared in upgrades for them. On the other hand I'd receive a debuff for -XX Vigor to enemies for my next two fights, but at the start of the battle it didn't seem all that apparent they took any hit to their Vigor. Another point to bring up is the lack of information on risk/reward for specific options chosen. The most regrettable one I made being to "Parley" with a group of mages only to have a decently worked on minion die for it. 4) Artifacts: This was implemented really well, there were quite a few combinations that really helped the player decide a playstyle. I didn't care for the two or three I'd get all with different names that did the exact same thing though. There's a particular one that gives 10% chance of extra body parts, and then another two or so that give the same effect, BUT go in the exact same slot. So what's the point? It also didn't help that depending on the random artifacts you start a game with, those felt as though they would push you to play a specific way. 5) Buildings: I feel this one is more of a "Wait-and-See" than any of the others, some buildings were mandatory (but only depending on your chosen playstyle). If you intended to do a lot of spell-slinging, there was a building for that. If you wanted to use ultimate attacks in rapid succession, there was a building for that. If you wanted to MAYBE get a few extra parts for WHEN not IF you lose some minions/waste your time MAYBE getting an extra minion item, there were buildings for that. Having an infirmary was a moot point, didn't feel like upgrading that whatsover. Aside from those buildings, I don't see the point of building something that allows me to build more buildings, when fighting enemies gives me the currency I already need to make that happen. Same could be said for the training grounds, there's an item that bumps my lvl 1 to a lvl 3-5 in an instant should I be willing to spend the EXP to Alchemy to more frequently attain said item. Tip for those reading this, the vampire spell made it easier to find "grunt workers" for your numerous buildings. All in all, great concept, but there's a lot of traffic jams that frustratingly cause players to need to start over if they distributed their resources incorrectly. For that reason, I can't say I'd recommend it to someone unless they're a glutton for the kind of punishment Dark Souls and Darkest Dungeon didn't explore...Start Over.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun but not as good as darkest dungeon:PROS:1. Strategy and good calculation needed, brutal attack usually does not work.2. Darkest and unique POV (You are the dungeon itself).3. Various of units and plenty of skills you can use.CONS:1. Per unit stats customization is a bad and dangerous design (DD does not have). First it is boring that you have to click unit one-by-one. Second it easily makes too strong/too weak combination which actually limits the possibility of the game and make balance much more difficulty.2. UI is not very friendly (at least not good as DD, although DD is not good either).Mixture:Stress attack/escape mechanism: Stress attack was something more fun than DD. But later I found it was not 100% what I like:(1) heart attack is by chance: for game like DD which needs careful calculation, random thing is fun but too random will ruin the game. I can accept something like I have 10% to miss the hit, but not like 80% chance not heart attack. I suggest we can greatly increase the sanity bar but once it closes to 0, chance to heart attack and at 0 surely die.(2) Escape mechanism: No farming is interesting design but you have to make sure the loots at a stable level. As the enemy escape, you lose loot which makes the later game more difficult. Sometime I have to kill the escaping enemy first in order to keep the loot. I don't think it is how this mechanism was designed.

_childDocuments_.review: I fell out of love with Darkest Dungeon and Iratus solved many of my complaints.One of my biggest ones is how DD encourages overly cautious play. You want to delay turns for extra vestal heals, spend extra turns removing stress, and err on the side of overpreparedness since failure means goodbye to many hours of progression. This makes an already long game longer, and I do not find "maximize combat length without the game noticing" to be fun. Iratus just lets me focus on having fun tactical battles. I also appreciate that because each battle is broken up, you can mix up teams much more frequently and combats can be harder in general.It is probably unlikely Iratus will ever fully get out of Darkest Dungeon's shadow, but for me it is a game I like to play whereas Darkest Dungeon is just a game I like the IDEA of playing (until I remember having to juggle stun locks and heals at the end of every combat).

_childDocuments_.review: I was afraid to regret my buy for THIRTY € as another scam like i did recently with Football, Tactics, Glory.Here I don't! _childDocuments_.review: Iratus Lord of the Dead really is a game that's a joy to play, the diversity of ally and enemy units and the interplay between them really makes you sit and think at times. _childDocuments_.review: Iratus is an awesome dark fantasy strategy/roguelike/squad turn-based hybrid game, but IMHO overpriced for what it currently offers. The combat reminds me the most of Heroes of Might and Magic and Disciples, and it shares a similar dark vibe with the latter, with a pinch of cartoony. I didn't play "Dankest Dungeon" yet so I can't compare it to this game. The game is still in early access and its biggest flaw is that it is currently unfinished. Your savegame will get deleted when you finish the game, although you get to keep the unlocks, because it is - after all - a roguelike hybrid. You can get around this easily if you really want it, though, by not going through the portal after the third boss on the map screen. If you like Necromancers (seriously, they are everywhere now from Diablo to ESO, though I'm not complaining because I love them), you shouldn't miss this.

_childDocuments_.review: Iratus is what happens when amateur game designers try to ape better, smarter designs.This is a mashup of Darkest Dungeon and Slay the Spire, both excellent games that created new sub-genres. Iratus is not an excellent game; it's not even a very good game. Its lack of polish is apparent immediately, from the amateurish art and voice acting to the unwieldy and unintuitive interface. Its lack of depth shows through after just a few rounds of battle. You might think there's something more to it, but there isn't. Yes, you will see more enemy types and unlock some new minions, but the fundamental gameplay is incredibly repetitive and these aren't big enough draws to make you come back. It was a slog for me to finish just one play through. Slay the Spire stays interesting because your deck is constantly in flux. In Iratus, your minions do not change. You're stuck playing the same boring characters with the same set of 6 moves for dozens and dozens of battles without anything shaking it up. If you're looking at this you're probably hoping for gameplay that reminds you of Darkest Dungeon, and Iratus absolutely does not. DD features complex layers of strategy with its choices about party composition and the way the different skills interact with each other turn each battle into an engaging dance of death. Iratus has skills that are themed to the party members, but have zero interaction or combo potential. There's nothing that mimics the feeling of pulling an enemy out of position with one character, to set it up for a devastating strike from a second character who's been buffed by a third. Instead, it's just a series of individual moves and random die rolls to see if you get insta-killed.Hard pass, this is amateur hour from someone who saw a good idea and tried to ride its coattails.

_childDocuments_.review: Would I recommend this game? Yes.The core gameplay mechanics of this game are solid and fun. The variety of minions leaves each playthrough feeling different.The art style is nice. I prefer it to pixelated art styles but the art and animations still remind me of less polished products. When I play this game I get the sense I'm playing adventure quest. UI could use improvements.Have a way to reset a skill or stat point that was just applied until the character sheet is closed or an applied button is clicked.Include a more practical view with each of the base locations (graveyard, alchemy, etc...). Clicking on alchemy, then clicking on a potion, filling the slots and clicking craft is not an intuitive system. At the time of writing this less than 25% of the player base has used the alchemy table (data based on the achievement). It fits the atheistic of the game but calling the stat vigor health and the stat dread magic would make the character building elements of the game more intuitive. Certain moves have two sources of damage. I would like to see the information available when I hover over an enemy to attack them of how likely the attack is to hit, crit, total damage range and is there a possibility to kill the enemy.So again, I would recommend this game. I also think there is a lot of room for improvement. If you want to play a more polished game in the same genre I would recommend Darkest Dungeon.

_childDocuments_.review: Iratus: Lord of the Dead is a game that I have to recommend for a variety of reasons.If you enjoy Roguelikes that are challenging, that require you to experiment with different party types, and that, yes, will punish you for making mistakes, then this is a game you'll enjoy. If you like the idea of playing the bad guys from Darkest Dungeon, then you will probably enjoy this.If you recognize that you like unlocking things through various playthroughs, then you will probably enjoy the fact that you only start with a basic few minions, and that others need special parameters to be unlocked, then you will enjoy this. And please note, that those unlocked minions are unlocked for all future playthroughs, so you don't need to worry about doing, say, 8000 damage to your own minions every single playthrough because you love the ghoul!That being said, it will be a learning experience. The bosses may **** you up. They may make you rage. But! Look at your minions, and the abilities that they can learn. More importantly, look at the upgrades, and recognize ways around beating the bosses. Trust me, it is very possible to beat them all, even on the harder difficulties.With all of that said: Most of all, if you like Early Access done right, you should enjoy this. These devs are some of the most responsive that I've seen in an Early Access title. Literally, go through the negative comments and see how many the devs have responded to with either a thank you for constructive criticism, or a desire for more information as to why a person does not like the game. So, as someone who's enjoyed playing the game, and messing around with the different game modes, unlocking the different minions, and killing lots and lots of humans, dwarves, and elves, I just want to say "Thank you" to the devs, and since this review is being written near the holidays: Merry Christmas and a Happy New Year.

_childDocuments_.review: Very playable in the current state, though if balance issues bug you, you should definitely wait for the full release.  Still, I see a lot of potential here.  I like the artstyle, Iratus himself is fun to listen to, and there's the makings of a pretty interesting resource management system. I will say that if you're coming to this after Darkest Dungeon, you should know you'll need to take a bit better care of your minions.  Your primary means of making minions is killing the living for parts, meaning if you ever get to a point you can't make more, you're screwed.  This isn't a complaint, mind you-- it helps with the feeling that Iratus really is desperately clawing his way back to power, and that this is a challenge even for an ancient necromancer.  But you will need to unlearn the "Well I can always get a new mook off the carriage" mindset.  That's kind of a delightful reversal, when you think about it: In Darkest Dungeon, life is cheap.  In Iratus, corpses are dear.Thumbs up.  I had misgivings about getting this game on early access, but I don't regret it at all.  If you don't mind dealing with the odd bug or balance issue, I'd say this is worth the money.  Can't wait to see the finished product.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this, but I struggled to come up with enough redeeming factors to outweigh the negatives currently facing the game.  Of course it's extremely similar to Darkest Dungeon, but where DD was somewhat elegant in the overall simplicity, this game seems to add some unncessary fluff mechanics to make up for the refinement of it's core gameplay.The result is core gameplay that still needs some balance tweaks and a lot of other features that feel lackluster or cobbled together.  Gameplay-wise, there are many similarities between DD and this game.  Besides the setting, the big difference is that you can actively damage enemy stress versus going  after health, and just like DD, if you stress-out an enemy enough, they will break and get debuffed (or in some cases, HEAVILY buffed).  Combine this health / stress mechanic with a two part armor system: There's physical armor and magical armor.  So now you're presented with the option of dealing normal damage, magic damage, or stress.  The game will throw various combinations of enemies at you that are (usually) good at resisting at least one of these things, so it's often you'll see enemies strong against magic who are weak to physical, or enemies strong against physical attacks who aren't strong against stress abilities.  Therefore your own party composition will generally need to alter from fight-to-fight so you don't get straight up counter-comped.  After all, it's pretty hard to be effective going in with a team focused on heaping on debuffs or stress when the enemy team is packing a member that will constantly heal stress and clear your debuffs as fast as they are applied.This emphasizes knowing the next fight and managing your troops accordingly.  It's hard to say if these troops are truly meant to be expendable or not.   There's not a HUGE difference between a level 1 minion and a level 5-6 (max) minion, although the game does emphasize leveling up a few teams and using them properly.  This becomes more difficult as very few minions can effectively heal, and so it's fairly difficult to preserve your forces.  They're not THAT difficult to replace, but unlike DD, it does appear this game has a final fail state once you run out of body parts to replace minions.  There's no "farming" or going back on old fights - you just go one way through the dungeon.This non-stop ramping up of difficulty then means losses to your A-Team or upgraded minions is extremely punishing.  Since there's no going back to farm anything back up, unless you already have a backup lined up, it's permanently going to set you back as you replace that minion with either something not suited to the composition, or simply something lower level (and thus more likely to die again).  Again, DD of course functionally has no fail state, but this just seems it's too easy to get painted into a corner from which there's no return.Lastly beyond minion creation, there's little upgrade equipment you stick on your minions, then upgrades you stick on the necromancer himself (but some of these are one-shot on the next fight only) so then you get to go back and re-equip necro after every fight.  Then there's this whole building / garrison mechanic, but your troops aren't doing stuff like relieving stress or learning abilities, some of them get healed, some level up, some do research for you, some dig up body parts, and so on.  This is ok BUT there's no summary screen like DD that shows what everyone is doing, or what their level is - so you get to click around to all of these UI elements to see if you accidentally parked your level 5 Skelly at the mortuary.Between the necro and the minions and the buildings and the lack of most any summary UI to see wtf is happening between all these little systems combined, it's definitely a game in Early Access.  A few improved UI elements and a balance pass or two would go a long way.   Most notably:  A summary screen to see what ALL minions are doing, and second, something that will display the potential next fight(s) so you can tailor your team accordingly.  Stress attacks too seem very random at times as to what they'll do or if they're going to be that effective.  It often seems easier to just club through armor and kill, even if someone is warded.Whether or not there's any change on going back to "farm" stuff or having that ability.  I dunno.  It seems there's a certain roguelike element to this that doesn't exist in DD.  In any case, for now I'd say wait until more changes go in to buy.  It's hard to tell exactly how this game will turn out.

_childDocuments_.review: I have won Iratus.  This game is nothing like Darkest Dungeons.  Other than both are games and they have 4 party members.#1  This game is NOT RNG.  This game gives you all that data you need before attacks and defends.  You also know what you are going to be fighting so you can bring the proper group on a PER FIGHT basis.  Thus allowing for proper strategy and tactics instead of getting "lucky" to face what your party is built for or "unlucky" and getting smashed.  This game is a heavily swayed by strategy and has minimum RNG.  Iratus would be like poker, and DD would be like playing a slot machine.#2  You are involved in the battles, you cast spells.#3  You can lose Iratus, you can make enough bad decisions that it is impossible to continue further into the game.  With enough time anyone can win DD.  You cannot grind your way to victory in Iratus.#4  Block and Ward, are a game changer.  You don't just have physical damage ratings, but also magical damage ratings, you have block and ward.  You must remove those or no damage is taken, unless... you have a minion that can bypass those defenses.  People saying skeletons suck have no idea how to build a skeleton to assassinate anyone for instance.  It's why the enemy focuses them usually.  Spells that attack all 4 enemies are also very helpful in tearing off wards.#5  Your Grave Yard is far better than DD.  You don't have some random jerk taking up a "rest" spot from your team.  Again, no RNG sticking it to you.  You don't PAY each time you use something you've unlocked, you pay upfront and that's it.#6  You choose the "best" path to go on each level based on your play style.  Want more artifacts?  Want more minions?  Want more instant levels for yourself?#7  You can find amazing artifacts that literally allow any minion to heal each round, or to bypass attacks, or ones for yourself that allow minions to get permanent buffs.  None of that is necessary, but they open up more party options.  A healing skeleton for instance, that can receive buffs...  wicked.  :)#8  Your skill tree drastically changes the game.  You can make sure to get all of the permanent minion buffs, or more parts, more attacks spells, more utility spells, or easier alchemy.#9  You have a book where you fill in each different enemy you face.  You literally take notes on exactly what attacks they can do from the 4 different positions, along with their stats.  You MUST use that to succeed on harder difficulty or have a great memory.Those are some of the major ways Iratus is far superior to DD.Now a big complaint is minions you have to unlock are often weaker than the starting minions.  Even at higher levels.  Each minion can be effective in the proper team vs the proper enemy.  For instance a minion that can only do stress damage is 100% useless vs things that aren't alive.  Some minions do best by moving around a lot, you must use other minions that go well with that strategy for it to work.  Most other games you expect the higher level, aka harder to get units to be upgrades of the lower ones and that is not the case with Iratus.I've won the from back to front with a Bride, Wraith, Skeleton, and Zombie.  Zombie wards vs physical and magic each turn, Skeleton shields and does sanity damage to anyone attacking it, Wraith has a 65% evade uses ability to put skeleton at about 40% evade and Bride,  Bride buff, then ultimate attack every single round, full wrath when it's her turn from my build.  Once that is done, mix in interrupts for stances from Wrath, Zombie, and Bride.  Skeleton mixes in unstoppable attacks.  There are other specific abilities and artifacts at play.  The point is even STARTING minions are are good enough.  With the proper design.Or you go with a Lich in the back, 3 tough shielded minions in the front, and have the Lich rain fire one your team and their team and burn them down.  Better have the right builds, but it works.  One of em dies the Lich or you can summon a new one in mid battles.So, many viable options for the different play styles.Truly Awesome game.  Stop insulting it by comparing it to DD, it's nothing like that other than the GUI and art.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't be dissuaded by the "Early Access", the game has a lot of fun, content and replayability already available and I have not run into any bugs. I heartily recommend the game even now in Early Access and am really looking forward to seeing what the full game is like. Gameplay seemed fairly balanced on easy and normal difficulty so far; maybe on later difficulties there is more unbalance.An update for re-balance and a new character comes out tomorrow, so this review is for the game as I played it for a week or so before the this update.So - obviously, this games takes inspiration from Darkest Dungeon, but playing as forces of evil against heroes instead. It's interesting and allows for some pretty neat classes and designs to select from for your party. While the comparisons to DD are fair, I think Iratus does a great job at establishing it's own identity. Instead of a long and grueling campaign with slow progression like in Darkest Dungeon, you instead have a short campaign through some dungeons where you can make a lot of progress and build up quickly.  Fail or pass, the available minions you unlocked carry over to the next run. Thus, there is huge replayability in trying out new minion compositions, ascending to higher difficulty for challenges, or just playing for fun because the core gameplay loop is addicting fun. Since the campaigns are short (my last campaign shows 39 battles played, and I deliberately took some longer roundabout paths to fight more battles), it's easy to play and complete one in just a weekend.In Early Access, there are 3 dungeons to conquer, with what looks like at least two more to be available in the full game. 18 minions (characters to form battle parties) are available with a 19th being added tomorrow. There are tons of items to find and utilize as well as spells/skills for Iratus to choose from. The minions themselves can gain up to 7 levels and with each level they can choose to upgrade a skill in one of two directions which have different side effects (i.e. maybe less damage than the other upgrade but now is able to stun targets) and also different stats. So even if you don't plan to use the skill for a build it may be useful for the stat boost. Then instead of equipment, minions can be enhanced by adding items to 2 item slots, or by crafting them (or replacing existing parts) with rarer parts that have stat boosts built into them.Iratus is a necromancer, so instead of getting free party members like in Darkest Dungeon, you must find parts in order to craft your party. You can use alchemy to transform parts into different kinds. Extra parts can become mana to use for spells instead. You find parts at the end of each battle and can boost the chances with some items you may find along the way as well. Like Darkest Dungeon, there are also upgradeable buildings to enhance the experience. These do not carry over through playthroughs though. The different benefits you can get from the buildings are:More exp for IratusMana regen for IratusWrath boost for Iratus at start of battle (Wrath is sort of like mana but for minions to use their more powerful skills. It renews in battle through damage taken and received or skills that directly give wrath)An arena to train up to 4 minions 2 exp at a timeA health regen facility to restore health up to 4 minions  left in the buildingAn item finding facilityA part finding facilityAnd lastly a building that boosts the currency used to make these buildings in the first place.A typical gameplay loop will be as follows:You start with one item, and 4 minions and some parts. You start at the hub where you can choose to upgrade Iratus (if have talent points from leveling up), upgrade the minions, move minions around to rearrange parties, place minions in buildings, make the buildings, craft new minions, craft parts through alchemy, etc.. From this hub, you can also select a map which has you enter the dungeons.The dungeons is an overhead view of a map where you can see what the next battle encounter is and plan your party accordingly. If you see you're fighting a golem for example, a stress party is not going to be helpful as golems don't have fear. At some points in the dungeon there will be a fork and you have to choose with path to go to. You can look ahead and see what is coming, but battle encounter more than one movement away will only reveal one enemy type. Also note there is no random encounters or replaying battles. There is no going back.Only forward or to the side. Not all paths are equal. Some can be longer and more rounadabout if want to grind for exp/items/parts, but this may also be risky and can lose your best minion before the boss. The boss will always be the final encounter on each dungeon/ Once you've played the boss once and seen how it works, it probably won't be too challenging in the future. Maybe this will be addressed in future updates.Battles are fairly similar to darkest dungeon. It is turn based 4 vs 4 system with  a health bar for yourself and a health and stress bar for the enemies. You have three different attack types: physical, magic, and stress. Fire also exists as a status and there are all sorts of buffs, stances, stuns and so on to fine-tune some strategy. Stress can lead to insanity and debuffs or possibly inspired and buffs which may ruin your day. So it can be risky, but in some cases, some enemies are dealt with easier via heart attack of too much stress or scaring them into fleeing. Anyways, after each battle, you are rewarded in parts and exp for both Iratus and the minions along with any bonuses from the buildings constructed. You are also returned to the hub. Thus between each battle encounter you can swap your party, send your hurt minions to heal over the next battle etc. So the game isn't quite like Darkest Dungeon where you need 1 party to survive many encounters. Instead, you can swap your party around and tune it to each encounter. However, the drawback is healing is pretty scarce, especially in the early game before unlocking later minions. Most of the difficulty comes from this. I had a really rough time in my jump from easy to normal difficulty because I was missing some key party members that make great self-healing tanks. I think my next run will go a lot smoother now that I've unlocked such.That said - the easy difficulty is indeed easy. If you were turned off from Darkest Dungeon by its difficulty you may still like this game on the easier difficulty.  If you like the challenge, this game definitely gets more challenging as you go up in difficulty. You can also impose your own challenge through your choice in party members. That said, no party member seems useless. They all have been pretty fun. But as hinted by the above, some do seem more crucial in alleviating the difficulty than others. Definitely recommend this game, especially to any RPG or dungeon crawler fans. It gets really addicting unlocking all the minions and I would recommend to try out each one at least once. On paper some may seem lackluster, but then when you combine them with another minion something clicks. For example, marking your allies to provoke them to be attacked more, then sending that ally into a counterattack/defensive/healing stance. The game stands out from Darkest Dungeon for the following:IMO, it is more accessible and easier to learn and get into, mostly due to the next pointShorter campaigns and easier to restart and play through in a weekendYou can cast spells to interfere with the battles at any point in your turn (once per cycle of all your minions)While Darkest Dungeon characters may be more iconic and memorable I actually really like the designs of the monsters. Especially love the Unfrozen, Damphir and Lich.  The aesthetic in this game is awesome, love the art direction.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an acquired taste. If you're really into dungeon crawling and you like Darkest Dungeon type combat, get it. The game is well crafted, the combat is quite alright if repetitive and the story is pretty much non-existent. Personally I had to force myself to finish the game to see if the story got interesting, but it didn't. Nothing is explained, it's purely "you are the bad guy, go kill some people". Maybe I've played too many games and maybe I'm burnt out, but I lacked any real sense of exploration or wonder at event occurrences.It's not a bad game, but I'd say 5.5/10 entertainment value. Which is a shame, because the art is nice and the setting has a pretty cool vibe to it. It's all just very shallow and it didn't feel inviting to me to explore further. It lacked that magic that janky games like Kenshi or Warband have. I would go as far as to say it lacked SOUL haha

_childDocuments_.review: Good Game. Decent replayability due to increasing level of challenge. Story is basically nonexistent if you care about such things. Its similar to Darkest Dungeon in that you have 4 characters with different abilities vs 4 other enemies with different abilities determined  by class. Its one long dungeon crawl as opposed to quick jaunts into dungeons. In Iratus, you are crawling out of a dungeon.There is far less RNG in Iratus, which i like. Yes you still miss key attacks, or roll low on damage, or fail the roll to make the item to upgrade your duder. However, the decision you make are far more impactful. You decide what your team is. You don't have have to wait for lich to show up in a wagon, you just make him. Also there is far more customization of your characters than in DD. You can turn your lich in crowd killing, he even kills your guys, power house or can make him into a stress dealer. You can make one minion into a solo duder with upgrades and items, forget bringing in 3 others.Overall, I like this game more. The pacing is solid, a campaign won't last for eternity but around 10 - 20 hours depending on how fast you take it.

_childDocuments_.review: A very interesting game.You can build lots of combinations of minions with very different potency - this is exactly what I like.You can build a team from interesting to effective or funny gameplay.Kill enemies by heart attacks, kill them with fire, kill them with old good claws/swords, turn them into bones and rags by magic ...Life is a disease ... and you have the cure!h.
_childDocuments_.name: Iratus: Lord of the Dead

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of Darkest Dungeon I always was on a lookout for any similiar games in an interesting for me setting. In general I really like the possibility to take a "bad guy" cape in video games (almost all of them only give you an option to be a boring boy-scout which gets tiresome at some point). And when I played DD I thought "I wish there was an ability to play the monsters or at least use them somehow" (and there was that possibility, with the help of some mods of course).I also love the idea of necromancy in games: controlling hordes of the undead, slaying everything in their path, only growing stronger with every battle and consuming all like a disease. That's the reason why I always try to build pet-oriented characters or at least employ some form of dark magic in games.And then I saw a trailer for this game and, o boy, it really seemed like a perfect fit for me. I patiently waited for its release and here we are - I finally got to play it (it's only an early access release, but oh well).What can I say right now? I like it. When you first play it, it certainly feels harder than Darkest Dungeon in some aspects, but when you get used to it and start to see a bigger picture, then it gets easier to enjoy the gameplay. Just gotta learn those enemy abilities, try on bosses and make up a fitting build to counter them. Not everything works though and the balance in this game is certainly in need of attention from the developers (and it looks like they're right on it - devs are active in the forums, they listen to feedback and rollout updates to change things up).The variety of available minions is to my liking (and there will be more), there are enough possible ways to create and use different builds and the progression is decent enough (not too grindy, not too fast).I like the art style, the music isn't too distracting and I find myself enjoying some of the Iratuse's remarks. What I would like to see added to this game: mod support, as mods really boost the game's life and improve the game in many aspects: players can add new content or improve the existing one and they can also change the balance how they like.I also would like a possibility to make it less linear in some way, for instance it would be interesting to have a way of exploring the whole map or be capable of backtracking to gather as many resources as possible to prepare for a boss fight. tl;dr: You probably will like this game if you enjoyed Darkest Dungeon and want to try something new with a different approach as there are enough gameplay changes that make this game less of a copycat and more of a DD inspired creation.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Darkest Dungeon's battle system but didn't like the grinding and the RNG, you'll love this game. You're a necromancer so you can build specific minions and set up exactly the squad you want from the start of the game, you can swap squads mid-level to combat specific threats, and you can cast one spell per combat round which can salvage bad situations, move your minions around without spending their turn, that sort of thing. Grinding isn't even really possible; there's a strictly limited number of fights in the game, and while you can restart a floor, it's a full restart and you lose all the stuff and exp you got. The planning and squadbuilding aspects are very deep and understanding how your minions work and how enemies work will make or break your run. Extremely enjoyable and has high replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: So far after a few hours I can tell this game should continue to appeal to my hardcore sadistic Darkest Dungeon rouge-like/lite mindset, but if that doesn't describe your style of play then it might be more frustration generating than fun.The key word here is "balance", and given the dev's quick response to player's concerns I assume there will eventually be a hardcore sweet spot along the road map.For now there may be rage quitting aplenty, especially with players being unfamiliar with some of the more extreme mob traits; for instance, in my last run there was a mob that didn't seem too threatening, that is until I saw that after a few turns it got a buff which couldn't be canceled that stated , and since I hadn't bothered to focus fire it from the first turn, I couldn't kill it in time, it was a total wipe, wiping away all of my characters' development to that point, and since I had decided to focus the majority of my resources on that now defunct squad, it was the end of my patience for this evening's Iratus session. Now given my affinity to the genre there wasn't any anger, but I just didn't feel like spending more time to get back to a similar point for the evening.So know yourself, and if you like the genre, this offering has enough activities outside of battle to develop your characters/avatar (including research trees), crafting, gear grinding, and travel map branch choices, to provide excellent replay value for the tactical squad focused micromanager gamer.
