_childDocuments_.review: Many moons ago there was a free fan made game called Doom RL, it was the perfect blend of the Doom universe and the genre that has come to be known as "rogue" or "rogue like" it was a passion project made by a single developer and the combination of the Doom universe and the rogue like game play meant it was an amazing game that I personally sank over 200 hours into. With many different strategies to try and a sadistically beautiful quality of game play that lead to that "one more go" mentality, it was truly a gem of an indie game... however, the developer was brought low by a cease and desist forcing them to remove the game from their website, a true tragedy for the indie game scene as it became lost to the ether. When I updated my computer, sadly it was one of the files that slipped through the cracks in the process and alas I was unable to track it down again, even though memories of playing it stuck with me for many years.Jupiter Hell is the spiritual successor to that long lost game, a lot of the same game play mechanics are there from Doom RL, the game plays exactly how I remember Doom RL playing, even down to the weapons and armour upgrades, the class system, the special harder levels with bigger rewards, and the character development system. If you like Rogue likes and you like SciFi demon killing, then this is the game for you.TL:DR It's Doom RL remade without the Doom branding due to copy right, and it has been given a lot of love.Buy it. NOW

_childDocuments_.review: A fascinating game marred by questionable design decisions.First things first; it's fun and interesting. The 80's zeerust aesthetic is excellent, and multiple types of enemies are difficult yet engaging insofar as finding ways to overcome them. The upgrade system is, perhaps, a touch more bare bones than I would like such a game, but understandable regarding game balance.The bad; those questionable design decisions reveal just how skin-deep certain strategic decisions actually are. Consider the following:You are in the early game and are using a weapon kit that involves, say, a grenade launcher, a shotgun, and maybe a autorifle, and are getting ready to go down to the next floor. The floor you are currently on has had a horrendous number of enemies who used grenade launchers, and you spent a great deal of time weaving around trying to avoid getting splattered. Congrats! You've successfully not died to a potential early game killer; however, you spent so long trying to avoid dying that the enemies, now dead, had managed to reload their weapons.And you can't unload them to get that rare-for-that-point-in-the-game ammo. Unlike other options in roguelikes, where a decision is made with a limited carry-weight or pack-size in consideration, the game has artificially restricted your available options. You can't move/drop relics, either, because they break on drop. To put it another way, certain complications on weaponry and relics exist solely to complicate their usage, and in certain situations simply mean that I am borderline forced to use a mediocre copy of the weapon I already possess simply to conserve ammo, since it is irretrievable once loaded.Progression is almost purely linear; there are branching paths on each planet, and each route may have a 'special' floor that you can return back to the route from, but those are exceptions. This, inherently, isn't a problem, but it makes the decision to break relics on drop even more baffling.So, yeah. There are the bones of a stellar, 10/10 game here. But there are a number of moment by moment decisions that turn an interesting experience into an aggravating one, and an aggravating one into an angry one. I gave the game 20 hours and I got to Dante, so I know enough to know that there were design decisions that broke this experience for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Jupiter Hell is what you get if you turned Doom into a top-down turn-based game. The game is glorious, difficult and rewarding. There are currently 3 classes and a good amount of skills to make your soldier into whatever type of killing machine you want. Devs really care about the game and are active with the community. _childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolutely amazing tactical, atmospheric, heavy metal, 90s action movie roguelike! One of the complaints of roguelike haters is RNG. However, this game brilliantly balances probability with binary (yes/no) tactical decisions. For example, a shotgun that has 33% accuracy on an enemy will inflict 33% of its max damage on that enemy (guaranteed). On the other hand, a single projectile weapon like a sniper rifle will hit with the given accuracy. For automatic weapons, a 33% chance to hit is applied to EACH bullet in the burst, so if your gun shoots 3 bullets you will hit with 1 bullet.200+ hours into the game and I keep coming back to it. There are so many variables for level branching, combined with a rich set of skills to customize and experiment with, add in mod-able proceduraly generated loot and weapons and baddies galore.In summary, this game has not reached a fraction of the popularity it deserves yet. I hope the developers keep working on it.That said, every game could be improved a bit. Some of my hopes for improvements follow:1) More diverse set of skills that help to differentiate play-styles for each character type.2) Better balancing and more testing to ensure that each build is viable all the way to the end boss. Currently, some builds make it near impossible to defeat the end boss. An example is Gun Kata master skill. It's super fun to shoot 2 pistols simultaneously with each move. However, you run out of ammo stupidly fast and it would not even be viable with the number of baddies on Hard difficulty. This is even true when getting skills that allow you to convert ammo types to equipped weapon. Also, Gun Kata will auto-shoot at the nearest enemy. In the final boss battle, minions are spawning every turn around the boss, but you cannot direct your fire to finish off the boss, so there is no hope of winning with this build. Additionally, a sniper build is not viable on Hard due to the shear number of enemies that are constantly rushing you and you cannot waste a turn aiming at a target to enhance damage. A lot of work can be done to test and improve balance.3) More information on the enemies would be extremely helpful. After 200 hours, I still cannot understand in what scenario the Medusa can reduce my HP max. And I have no clue what the white HP overlay is on the enemies (armor??). You can also suddenly be reduced to a pile of ashes without any warning because several enemies were prepping a simultaneous attack on you, or one enemy is targeting you for a special attack. So, some UI information on the estimated damage you will take on a given round could be nice. Or, perhaps this is a mod option on a combat visor that gives you a prediction of damage received on the next turn!Best of luck to the developers, I hope your game receives the popularity and recognition it so deserves!

_childDocuments_.review: Way back at PAX East 2018, I had an opportunity to demo this turn-based action game. It had this dark space setting with heavy metal vibes, and all in all, looked really cool. Now, I am a huge Doom fan, and not just the recent games. I grew up with them. Doom was one of the first FPS games I experienced. Anyway, back to the above game. It’s clear this game draws a lot of inspiration from Doom. I chatted up one of the devs at the show and he gave me a business card with the game’s name on it: Jupiter Hell. I am actually kind of annoyed at myself for not following Jupiter Hell after PAX (I did not have a gaming PC at the time so anything I enjoyed at the show that was slated for PC release was kind of forgotten). Connections to Doom aside, I just have to say: this game is a wild time.Developed by Chaosforge, Jupiter Hell “is a roguelike set in a 90s sci-fi universe.” You play as a lone space marine against hordes of demons on the moons of Jupiter. Wearing its influences on it’s sleeve like a tattoo on its forehead, this is a fast-paced (well, as fast-paced as turn-based can possibly be), in your face, hardcore, thrill ride.You actually can play as a lone marine, scout, or technician. I mean, you are still alone but you do not have to just play as a marine.The objective remains the same regardless of the class you choose: survive the hordes of demons and guards and mechs and drones and get to the next floor and the next floor and so on and so forth. Each of the three classes plays the same way with the exception of special abilities. The marine has a fury resource. He gains fury by killing, which can be used to activate adrenaline which allows him to heal a bit and ignore the pain for a few seconds. Scouts utilize stealth for short periods of time, which can help get to a better position for combat. And technicians have access to smoke bombs that break line of sight with enemies, which in turn allows for better positioning or easier escaping.Upon taking control of your character, you learn that you can only move in the cardinal directions: up, down, left, and right. Diagonal movement is done via two separate movements quickly like up and left or down and right. I said turn-based earlier, but it’s not as simple as games like Final Fantasy Tactics where there is a clear distinction between each side’s turns. If you have ever played Superhot, you will see some similarities. When you move, they move. You can choose to wait, which serves as a “turn,” and then they will move. Waiting is usually used to take cover and open fire once the enemy makes its move. The game shows your chance to hit so you can decide whether rushing in or waiting is the better option.There were a few times that I entered a room to loot a chest and could see four enemies approach. By waiting in the corner, I picked them off as they came into range. There is also an option to manually target, which comes in handy with the numerous explosive barrels throughout the levels.Your objective is to find the elevator to advance and get off each planet. Levels are completely randomized, but sometimes, you find the elevator almost immediately, while other times, you need to uncover every square inch first. You are free to leave right away, but exploration may be in your best interest. For one, this is how you improve your arsenal. You only start with one weapon, but you can find combat knives, pipe wrenches, shotguns, and even miniguns to name just a few. There is also armor pieces (head and chest), grenades, and multi-tools which have several uses.Throughout the levels, you come across terminals. These terminals do a number of things including revealing the map, marking enemies, providing weapon upgrades, health upgrades, and even disabling some enemies all at the cost of multi-tools. Exploration also helps you earn experience. With enough experience, you level up and gain access to perks. The perks are displayed in list format but they behave similarly to talent trees in other games with perks locked until previous perks are picked up.Perks range from health increases to dual-wielding to life leech, but their names are the best part. Names like Son of a Gun and Angry ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, or, my favorite: Rip and Tear (gee, wonder where they got that one from).What is funny is that Angry ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ can also describe the marine almost to a tee. For example, if you press the button to pick up and there is nothing to pick up, he will say, “There’s nothing here.” Keep pressing that button and he raises his voice to say, “I told you, there’s nothing here.” When you run out of ammo, you may hear, “Reload dammit!” or “There’s no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ammo!”Guess who also might get angry? YOU. This game is a roguelike. This is more like Rogue than it is like the roguelikes that have been released in the past two years or so. How so? When you die here, you die. Game over. There is no level-up screen to show what you earned to make the next run or the run after easier. You do see how you performed compared to your other tries, but that is it. The next run starts right from the beginning just like it did when you first started the game. If it is any consolation, you can save and quit to prolong the inevitable but every run is a brand new run.Replayability is extremely high in this game. In campaign mode, you choose your difficulty and then have to make it to the end. Levels have branching paths which make no run exactly the same. If the campaign is not your thing, try a challenge run or a trial. Challenge runs set parameters like limited inventory but increased movement speed or only grant rocket launchers as weapons. Trials change everything from removing all branching paths to playing forever/until you die, or even having every level available with the ability to choose where to go (you normally have to find either exit).Jupiter Hell combines one of the most popular genres of late and one of the longest-running and best-known series, and somehow, it just works. In fact, it works really well. Permadeath and that “one more run” feeling with the in-your-face and heavy metal vibes of Doom combined with turn-based, tactical gameplay make for an extremely enjoyable and fun as hell (PUN INTENDED) game. Side note: if you want all of the above-described action but without the foul language and cheesy 90s style, you can actually turn it all off!

_childDocuments_.review: A couple of quick things: 1. Jupiter Hell is a Traditional Roguelike. What this means is that it is turn based rather than real time, and much slower paced than the Action Roguelike, or Roguelite, style of game.2. There is a lot of swearing on by default. There are options to reduce and completely remove the swear words which includes the UI elements, voice lines, descriptions and messages. 3. The CRT effects are also adjustable. They gave me a small headache until I figured out the options to turn them off.Overall, the game is very easy to learn, with a lot more depth to be found once the basics are mastered. The branches are all interesting, with different final levels. Weapons, armor and creating builds with traits is very satisfying.The runs last from a couple of hours to 5-6 total depending on the paths taken, and how careful you are. It fits From the Difficulty options, to the various trials and challenge playthroughs, I can't recommend it enough for folks who enjoy Traditional Roguelikes, or new comers to the genre.Update for 1.3: The new early game options are absolutely fantastic and add a lot choice in how the early game plays out. No longer is Callisto a dull run through - you really have to pay attention to maximize your rewards.

_childDocuments_.review: This is ultimately a game about making hard decisions with limited resources and imperfect information. It manages to do this without putting the player under time pressure, which makes it extremely accessible to anyone that might have to drop a game mid-run. Just about every weapon in the game is really satisfying, and completing your first run on Medium isn't the end of the game, but the beginning of discovering its depth.Anyone that is a fan of traditional-style roguelikes and dispatching demons should play this without hesitation.

_childDocuments_.review: Very well made. Too bad it's a full (enforced) rogue analogue with no real meta-progression. The game itself is a downright brilliant take on DOOM if it was turn based, with nods to everyone and everything important from the era. There's the gravelly voice quipping "What are you waiting for - Christmas?" straight from Duke 3D, the absurd  mucho macho scripts, and even nods to earlier lore like the Grue eating people in the darkness. A dulcet soft-rock soundtrack, and surprising depth in character builds. I found the first few runs to be highly entertaining, tight and rewarding. I simply wish that there was a way to keep and develop a character, and take him on multiple runs. But yeah, its a rogue type game. So, very well made, fun, and well worth the price of entry.If I had a wish: a career mode with level-by-level character development and no permadeath.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a blast (both figuratively and literally). I grew up playing doom and nethack, so when I heard about D**mRL (Bethesda!), it sounded like it would be right up my alley. I was expecting to have fun with it, but it ended being one of my favorite games of all time. So when I found out Jupiter Hell (D**mRL's spiritual successor) was coming out, I was quite excited. I've only logged about two hours so far, but this game is scratching all the right itches, and I trust these guys to finish a game right. It's not an X-COM (squad shooter), but if you enjoy turn based games where you shoot guns 10/10.To the developers: I really loved the master traits in DRL and feel like they made character creation/leveling up a lot more interesting. I might not be far enough into the game yet to have discovered them, but I really hope assemblies also make their way into Jupiter Hell too. Keep up the good work, and I'm excited to see what you guys do next.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: best suited for die-hard fans of the roguelike-genre, this game fits all the traits of the classic definition of "roguelike", without taking in any of the innovations, such as adding progression.I like this game for its humour, quips, puns and simple heads-on brutality. The gameplay is turn-based chess-like movement mixed with intense combat and some RPG-elements, all in a heavily Doom-inspired setting, which I find quite intense and invigorating.However, after 10+ runs, the game comes to halt (or at least it did for me), since the only results of your runs and re-runs is the highscore on a score board. Even though the classic definition of "roguelike" never included any sort of progression, I personally feel the game is poorer without the progression. There is no story-rich environment or characters like in "Hades", nor any expansive gameplay like in "Stoneshard", both of which are also roguelike.There are 3 classes to play with, but despite the unique traits and gameplay, this just isn't enough, as the weapons, environment and the experience is still the same.In conclusion, I personally cannot recommend this game to anyone who isn't a die-hard classic roguelike fan, as I prefer games with some sort of progression, and there are plenty to choose from on Steam at the moment. I feel that the game is poorer without the progression, but I certainly appreciate the effort that the devs put into this project along with all their Kickstarter-supporters.Mayhaps I will revisit this game from time to time, when I just want some simple "run-and-gun" fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: First impression: the solid roguelike shooter base from D**mRL is still there, but with streamlined gameplay (no tediously emptying every weapon of its clip) and more tactical options like cover and aiming.BTW I use the term "roguelike" loosely here, since while this game and D**mRL are probably closer to Rogue, Nethack and Dungeon Crawl Stone Soup than a Diablo 1, Spelunky, Binding of Isaac or FTL, it's still very much streamlined an "lite" compared to its venerable  (which BTW are still incredibly fun and engaging to play today).Some details I find less positive such as the very limited inventory space combined with ammo still taking space in it - once it gets full you never quite know whether you'll be able to pick up a clip until you try, and with many weapon and ammo types it's really hard to pick what ammo to drop. Also, destructible walls seem to be gone, compared to the original.I also wish (and this applies to the original roguelike) that you could carry all weapons and their ammo at once like in Doom. Perhaps only one of each *kind* of weapon, i.e. only one pistol at a time. I think it would give the player more of a reason to use niche weapons that don't necessarily fit your build, like the chainsaw, and add variety to fights.Difficulty on Normal seems fairly challenging, I got killed on the second level on my first try. I like this, too easy is boring.Gamepad support is great, and this might be the only serious roguelike you can comfortably play with a gamepad. A bit surprised there's no keyboard+mouse support though (you can play keyboard-only), mouse would feel great for shooting. You'll be surprised that unlike most classic roguelikes, there's no option to "advance until an enemy is sighted" or to auto-explore the map. This means more tedium and the possibility to die because you got tired of moving with a pause between every step.Sound and music are pretty good, although some dynamic music that gets quieter when you're just exploring and shooting one or two enemies would've been appreciated. As it is, the constant metal riffs get repetitive fast.Graphics have nice lighting and reflective effects, serving the tense mood perfectly. However environments are very generic. In DRL you could imagine the environment to be whatever you want. Here it's mostly crates, doors and crates (or desk/plant/door/desk). It needs a smattering of unique props and rooms to spice things up visually, a bit like DCSS mixes-in predesigned areas of various sizes into the procedural generation.I'm not 100% convinced by the UI. It's functional, and I'm ok with its overall retro design which makes it feel a bit like a real HUD could look, but I think it has too much text overall which makes it hard to read things at a glance. It might be improved by the use of monochrome icons (perhaps in addition to the existing text) to display weapons, abilities, and the amount of clips left especially when using a weapon that houses no more than a dozen bullets - reading a number is especially bad for quickly checking how much ammo you've left, you want vertical bars or something of the sort.Overall recommended to experience a game that's quite a unique hybrid, although I don't consider it perfect.---Further thoughts about the graphics after reading some other reviews:Despite the obvious developer investment, I find that the graphics in this game are barely passable. I wouldn't describe myself as an ASCII purist, I enjoyed playing Skyrim and The Witcher 1-3. But if I just evaluate the net result of this game's look on my engagement, I'd say the net effect is: visual boredom. I didn't get this impression of moving in generic cold corridors with the DoomRL ASCII or tiles, perhaps because my imagination filled the blanks more, and the pools of water/acid/lava as well as the level destruction (none of which made it in this game) made the place feel more dangerous and dynamic.So for me this game is kind of in the Uncanney Valley of game graphics: it steps close enough to realism that your brain can't fill the details by itself anymore and starts demanding more details, which are missing.I'm mostly speaking about the levels BTW, some things are well-done like the gore effects.Now take the same game and []make it look like this[/url], or like one of the good action RPGs like Grim Dawn, and we'd be speaking.

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful, simply wonderful. In true roguelike nature, you’re gonna die… a lot. The amount of variety in maps, builds, weapons, etc makes you not care. Not 100% sure how the game exists without getting sued, but this is basically Rogue Doom. Doom rock music + cussing/catchphrase great voiceovers + infinite replayability + blowing up zombies and demons = HIGHLY ADDICTIVE
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This game is addictive and challenging in all the right ways. It's a bit of XCOM, a bit of DOOM, and a lot of roguelike with a K. I started playing this game during its early access and not only has it come a long way since it started but the developer was always active, engaging with the community, and rolling out big new features at regular intevrals.It's a roguelike that doesn't have a massively complicated controls, take way too long to play (runs are about 2 hours like an FTL run), or contain unfair deaths. The game design is well balanced and the gameplay loop is addicting as you go from killing, looting, and figuring out the direction you want your build to go as you step ever closer to the end boss.Enemy, weapon, and build variety are all present. There are dozens of different weapons to try and enemies to kill, with every new enemy you encounter offering a new kind of tactical challenge you must face and find good solutions to so as not to get worn down to death or quickly killed. There are three classes, and each has five different master traits to make a total of 15 different ways to play a run (or you can go masterless and do whatever you want).There are six difficulties, 4 chapters per run, over a dozen challenges, and several trials which are totally different ways to experience the game. Content is not lacking in this game by any definition and every run is a gripping ride from start to finish.Graphics and sound are what you would expect from a high production value game, not an indie roguelike, which makes this game punch a good bit above its weight class. The animation blending too means that nothing looks jank despite being a turn based, grid based game. It's beautiful, violent, and punchy in motion and always satisfying when you gib a demon or a zombie. Soundtrack is great and fitting for each chapter of the game, and the DOOM style carnage of the game in general.I highly, highly recommend this game. It surpassed my hours played for both XCOM and XCOM 2. This is from someone who does NOT normally like traditional roguelikes at all. This one is special.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Upvoting to support a roguelike without any meta progression.But unfortunately, while the core gameplay is very solid, the strategic gameplay is flawed.The core of a roguelike game is composing your build from the tools you randomly encounter on your way to the final boss.Here, builds are composed from a static list of abilities which are tied to the character class and never changes.So you can create the very same character every run.You don't adapt to the random drops.You don't balance survival chances to power potential.You are playing the game like it's not a roguelike, but a generic story-based game.In my opinion, it kills the entire strategic layer.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time fan of DoomRL I was excited the minute ChaosForge (KK) announced they would be making a roguelike based on their original IP. I backed it immediately and the final product shows how much experience the developer has in the genre, how much work was put in building their own game engine from scratch and how enjoyable a fast-paced roguelike can be. Looks great, sounds great, plays great and the dev is very engaged with his audience/customers regarding constant updates and plans for enhancements to Jupiter Hell for the foreseeable future. It's insanely addictive to play and the collectibles (uniques, badges/medals, etc.) make for a very long-tail of exploring everything the world has to offer. With (currently) 4 different "moons" to visit, each with multiple paths to choose from (which differ in difficulty and possible goody drops) along with "special" one-off levels during your journey, it almost seems like the possible gameplay variations are endless.You can blaze through a run quickly, making a hasty trail for each levels' exit or take your time plotting every move, killing every enemy and collecting every item. It's totally up to you. (I prefer to take my time, with complete runs usually taking me around 4 hours, but the loot you gather along the way is worth it). And we have even gotten to the traits/perks portion of the game. With 3 base classes, which eventually branch to 15 different "Master" classes, you'll also find more insane variance it play possibilities. Wanna take nothing but pistols on the entire run and amp up your character to accommodate this? Do it! Wanna blast everything with shotty??? Grab those weapons, apply those traits and go to town! Wanna get up close and personal with only melee weapons?? Of course you can! I've been playing DoomRL for almost 10 years and still have gotten nowhere near the depths of all the possible things to find in it and learn from it. The same can be said of Jupiter Hell. It's only been out a short while (although I've been playing since alpha as a KS supporter) but I can already see it also is going to provide years of fun as well.Oh, and do yourself a favor. Play beyond Callisto (the first moon). Give it at least an hour, because that's when you'll really start to see all the options the game has to offer and how much the replayability really shines.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Wow i didn't expect the game to be this good.It's basically turn based rogue like where you fight zombies, demons and robots with guns in a doom-like atmosphere.Mechanics are well thought, many different builds : three main classes then you chose a perk each level and a unique ability for your character at lvl 6. Lots of choices which really impact the gameplay and thus great replayability.Runs are a few hours long.Game feels well balanced. I suggest starting on medium, i'm currently trying to beat hard which is hard (but really fun) and there are two higher difficulties for veteran/masochistic players :)Very satisfying to play, 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: The best time I've had in a long time. One of the most accessible roguelikes I've played. It's great. Buy it.Update: The developer continues to tune this game, and I really appreciate it. Large focus has been placed on making builds and traits more flexible, removing the early release need to find the right weapons to match your build. Now it's much easier to continue a build while still picking up the coolest loot you find. They've also put a lot of effort into increasing the variability of the early game. Since you spend most of your time in the earlier levels this is much appreciated. The introduction of the grenade launcher and the mobs that wield it did much to break up the optimal grind through the first 2 planets as well.This just keeps getting better! Can't wait to get home and update to the Valhalla build.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Thanks God such games still exist!!! It seems infinite .... This game is going to be my #1 Roguelike/lite, whatever it is. Atmosphere is like Diablo 1, it even feels like it, sound, animations, however, it is even more fun since it has guns which I am keen on more. Furthermore, Its Chess indeed as well! I beg of you Devs, do not make it more casual and simple as some people will probably ask you, it is supposed to be HELL!! Do not waste your time for requests such as mouse support and stuff .. yes, I know you are already doing it .. Hail to Jupiter Hell!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first run. Died to the summoner. Digging it so far. Good content for the price. Early access, but you can play to the end. It's probably the perfect traditional roguelike for people new or curious about the genre. If you enjoy games like Spelunky or Binding of Isaac, give it a try, you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Fight, die retry. They are spot on with that one.A Doom style, rogue like experience, with a focus on gun play, inventory and ability management. Brutally challenging in places. Worth replaying over and over just for the experience. Cool music, interesting pickups and varied routes and maps. Runs can be slightly different.Technically a rogue like - but you can push along as fast as your like. (Good way to get killed) Quite a polished experience otherwise. Understanding weapons and abilities is crucial to success as they are not equal. Feels like there is a difficulty spike later in the game - but varied builds will help. Decent room clearing strategies help, understanding enemy weaknesses, but you can still get smashed just by a bad series of decision. One I’ll come back to for a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Criminal that the soundtrack isn't uploaded anywhere. High tier music for a extremely high-tier traditional rougelike.Gameplay is great, none of that stupid "deal with what cards the game gives you to level up and hope you get the build you want" bs i see in games today, just build the character the way you want. each weapon is equally satisfying to use in their own way. Melee is a shockingly viable option as well.Play if you have any interest in rougelikes whatsoever.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who absolutely stinks at turn based roguelikes and got my first win on my 20th run, this game is really fun. Mechanically it's very straight-forward game but it's got a lot of depth, with a ton of build options, it looks and feels great to play, and the ranged combat is really enjoyable. You are constantly making lots of small decisions that add up to whether or not you can manage the attrition the game throws at you.For the dev: please keep building on this game. I've absolutely gotten my money's worth already (and have only touched one of the three classes so far) but this is the kind of game that will only get better with more content. Nice work dude.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: The game has one major problem: The absence of an overall game design concept for player experience. Every part is there and not bad, but not combined as a gaming experience.The game has managed to kill me with a horde of enemies in the starting hangar under a few minutes on easy.When you die, it is not because of forgetting to reload or taking a wrong move: It is because of randomly occuring too much or too strong enemies or because of getting randomly garbage equipment or both.pros+ cool setting+ nice graphics+ cool console simulation+ good skilltree+ good atmocons- cannot avoid sudden deaths out of nowhere- graphics of enemies too vague- drops are seldom helpful- console can be annoying slow- maningless story snippetsI tried to establish a kind of strategy against the randomness but I have no clue how to make this game a fun experience.Some may say this is the game design: Stand against fate, then this is your game.Some bugs occured and made again progress impossible: impassable poisonous gas, not working ingame consoles, not getting upgrades.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This Jupiter Hell is a ton of fun! Its all the fun of the DOOM Roguelike in a beautiful skin!It takes a lot of extra influence from the DOOM comic and the modern games appearances. In true Roguelike fashion you can keep playing again and again for new and exciting adventures. A run can take three hours but to see all the content could take weeks!Love it! I will keep playing it for a long long time!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: If you like roguelikes in general, this is a pretty easy sell. It's tough, the RNG can be downright wicked, but so can the player once you get a good streak of upgrades going. You can find DoomRL floating around if you want to try it and see the depth that the premise can achieve.Personally, I'm looking forward to the continued development of JH: it's already an enjoyable title and it shows great promise that can be easily expanded upon.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: While I do enjoy the game experience quite a lot, the lack of control you have over the, well, controls, is a bit lacking from an accessibility standpoint.To switch to any weapon you're expected to have a completely dedicated button to it rather than using a specific "change weapon" button that for example might open up a menu letting you pick which weapon you want to equip. The game offers gamepad controls but because there's such an expectation for so many things to have a completely dedicated button, you actually can't even use a gamepad alone to play because the gamepad controls don't offer a way to swap weapons at all, nor can you use your character's special abilities.You can have up to 4 weapons, and you can potentially get 4 abilities, so that's 8 dedicated buttons you need just to either switch weapons or to use the abilities your character has. There's no way to swap guns from your inventory as far as I can tell, and there's no way to use your skills from it either. So you're relegated to always needing to use part of your keyboard to fully play the game rather than being able to play how you want to.I've been having a fantastic time with the game, but I can't say the same about the control scheme.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: If you ever played D**M the Roguelike, buy without hesitation. If not, but you're into roguelikes and want to see something fresh, where magic is replaced with technology - you should try it too. While Jupiter Hell is relatively new game, its foundation - DRL - with all rules, technology tree, challenges and much more - was polished for more than 10 years (it appeared in 2002, I discovered it in 2010, and it was developed for some time since then). One of upsides is that your character either dies from the start, or advances fairly quickly to let you have some fun. As for graphics, I miss ASCII mode of DRL and often catch myself looking at mini-map more than at the main screen. But I appreciate Kornel's effort to freshen the game's visual part. Also, as it was promised, game really adapts to how you play it: if you press arrows fast, it almost feels like real-time game instead of turn-based one (but you shouldn't forget that it's not, otherwise you will die soon).Big thanks to the Kornel for creating modern port of very influential (IMO) RL sub-genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I've found this to be a fast paced, turn based rouge-like.  Learning curve isn't steep if you've played anything like this before.  Lots of items to find, upgrade and agonize over trading for something better...is it better though?  Lots of skills to upgrade, unlock through skill combos and to agonize over choosing.All around, worth the money.  I plan on putting many more hours into this.  Thanks for a great game!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: A really wonderful spritual-successor to DoomRL.There's a few key differences, such as 'not' being able to move diagonally. But this game is so much more streamlined (in a good way), that I would highly recommend it to any true 'Roguelike' lover. For those unaware, it's essentially an old-school-roguelike Doom game. 5/5
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I will start this review by clarifying that this game is not a "Roguelike." It is in fact a genuine entry in the Rogue genre. If you like games like Shiren the Wanderer, Azure Dreams, or the Pokemon Mystery Dungeon series, then you like Rogues, and you will like this game. It's not generic, either, in that it places a ranged emphasis on the gameplay which is not a typical build for Rogue while still having some options for specialized melee builds. That said, there are still Roguelike elements in that you can unlock more options (challenges, trials, routes) with each run and it's not all just progressive forays into the same randomized endless dungeon. The game's atmosphere and story is reminiscent of and clearly heavily inspired by Doom. There is a mild lack of content in the limited classes or starting builds available even after unlocking much of the content, BUT WAIT. There is Steam Workshop Support and continuing Dev support and updates! Additionally, there are some great community resources available to inform some of the more nuanced choices once you get to the point that it begins to matter (unless you'd rather go in blind and learn for yourself which is also a great way to enjoy this game). I'm personally looking forward to hours more of challenge and enjoyment with this game and hope to see more like this in the future.  Sometimes it's okay to go back to the roots of a genre, and this is a case in point that shows it can be worthwhile.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This game plays and looks exactly how I want a modern traditional roguelike to. If your worried about the curved CRT-like HUD/screen, don't worry because you can turn it all off! I play it with my steam controller, I made my own settings as always and that worked great. By default there's 3 classes with plenty of build options for the scope of the game. If I could fault it for anything, it's so fun that I wish it was much larger in scope, but I feel like I'm easily getting my monies worth (tho I did get it on sale!). I'll be keeping an eye on this developer to see if they put out another game along the same genre for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: A fun game, but it does feel a bit lacking. I suppose its enemy variety and general gameplay. When you play something like Dungeon Crawl Stone Soup, ADOM, E.T.C, you get that expansive feeling that every start is new and crazy. For Jupiter Hell, it definitely feels very same-y. Its definitely fun and a nice spin on the genre as a whole, so I do enjoy it, but after playing about 5 hours over a few days I feel burned out, which isn't a lot of time to feel "Burned out" with.The game at nearly $30 CAD is too overpriced for what I feel it offers. I don't think its worth the cost - I've played games for 1/3rd the price that have caught my attention and kept hooked for much, much longer.Pick it up for maybe $5 - its fun. But $29? No. It doesn't have nearly enough meat for that.If some significant updates happen and some fresh content comes out, I could change this review, but I bought it a while back and haven't seen much of anything change.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This is turn-based doom, and it's fu**ing awesome.You go floor to floor killing demons, mercs and robots, trying to find new weapons and mods along the way.It's a tough but fair game, and since it's turn-based, you can take your time and optimize combat.There are three different classes with different passive and active abilities, and each time you level up (by killing enemies) you get to pick skills and buffs.The music is awesome and the VO for the main character is just perfect for the mood they're going for.Each run starts very fast and you never spend too much time "getting to the good part"; The game just STARTS. there's no boring build-up. Which makes it a perfect "one more run" game.If you like roguelikes and/or DOOM, then this game is for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This game has come a long way since the initial early access release. ChaosForge have done a great job.It might be a bit far-fetched to compare it to "The Binding Of Isaac", but the feeling of "meaningfully building yourself up" is present and accounted for, at least for me.Even though it's a bit masochistic, I really enjoyed the fact that you have to make full use of the game's mechanics at all times - if you get too cocky and try to skip them, or assume that the game will cut you some slack as it progresses, you will most likely die. Horribly. But that's okay.Interesting visual style, lots of different weapons (including unique ones, ), branching levels, satisfying character progression and a really well thought-out quest system that affects your run in a meaningful way. Also, Mark Meer talking ♥♥♥♥, can't forget about that one.10/10, like Skyrim with guns ~ IGN
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often play roguelikes but this modern take on the genre convinced me to give Jupiter Hell a chance.. and I am glad I did.I would not regret buying the game as it is. I enjoyed playing throught the official campaign, but the best content is yet to come. Once modding support is added into the game it will become even more awesome! Moreover, the author mentioned that he might open-source the engine one day, so it is clear that Jupiter Hell will only get bettern and it will stay with us for a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Alright bad news, soldier - we're gonna need you to crash land on a demon-haunted, rogue-AI-guarded, zombie-human-infested maze of a research station, and then basically spend the rest of your probably short life killing everything you come across. You'll get a class ability to start with, and a standard issue pea-shooter, and that's it.Good luck.You're gonna need it, obviously, but there's some things you can do to improve your luck. You can look for item and ability synergies, for starters. As you kill guys you'll level up, and each level grants a new upgrade. Some upgrades offer affinities for particular weapon types (miniguns, rocket launchers, shotguns, you know, the usual suspects.) Other upgrades encourage a particular style of play - slow and defensive, or aggressive and mobile. Maybe you get a bonus for hitting demons. Maybe you get a bonus versus robots.Now the deal is, the difficulty level of the enemies you face go up faster than your own levels do. The only way to get ahead of this ever-steepening curve is to stack synergies like a doomsday prepper, you need to absolutely hoard everything that has to do with enemies within a particular range, while wielding a particular weapon, and you need to STICK to that build element because otherwise you're never gonna make it.Oh hey, what's that on the floor, a shiny new things. It's a different colour than your other things, it's a BETTER colour... but maybe you should just leave it on the ground, floating gently in the blood of a thousand slaughtered demons, because you're all-in on the EVERYTHING IS ICE strategy, and this cool looking grenade launcher is just normal, not ice at all. That's a shame.Incidentally, did you notice the decor? Double shotguns? Rocket launcher? Pistol? Minigun? Hey, that's starting to sound a lot like... I mean, cyber demons, zombie marines, little floating eyeball guys... it's reminding me of something, it's like, you know that thing that like - that drives you, to want things? Like the basic drive that's making you want to do stuff, like kill bad guys?The proper term will come to me if I think hard enough about it but regardless, it's a nice aesthetic for a proper roguelike, and it's got cool cover and pain mechanics, and yeah, like I mentioned, synergies.Sorry, was I donig the thing where I pretended like I was delivering this review in-character from within the perspective of the universe?Am I still doing it?Do you like roguelike games? Then this one is pretty good.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: If DOOM was a classic roguelike. For fans of retro-feeling, punishing, turn-based strategy with a bit of a modern coating. The good:- Approachable, quick to pick up and addictive- Challenging and rewarding- Nails the classic roguelike feel but with a mixture of modern 3D graphics- Diverse play styles, broad and interesting skills, weapons, mods, etc- Forces you to make tough decisions and move purposefully- Smart game design decisions throughout - Theme and mood is a lot of fun- Works well with controller for laid back sessionsStuff that could be better:- Some UX improvements could be made throughout- Certain levels can have very poor visibility (can't see items or enemies against the environment)- Simply hitting the wrong button can screw your whole run (I liked the undo in Into the Breach- it wasn’t just a free “retry” every single time you made a bad decision, but was forgiving for when mechanics were not as expected or press wrong button) I had some frustrating deaths because behaviour was not really telegraphed or I just hit the wrong button.. e.g. when it looked like my grenade throw was unobstructed, but it actually hit the wall I was peaking round and killed me. I'll put this partly down to just how roguelikes are - screwing up and retrying is part of the experience, but I think there can be a better balance. - Storytelling, while I 100% understand it's not really the focus of the game, but honestly it has a lot of potential but ends up being quite limited. I liked reading the logs in the terminals and more environmental storytelling would be cool.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very unique - fast paced turn-based roguelike. I've never seen anything like this, beforehand I would've considered it impossible. But it captures the feeling of playing a fast paced old school shooter in turn based form, somehow. Everything is so fluid and feels very good. It's worth trying.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Don't balk at the pricing point, it's worth the money if you like traditional roguelikes.I was influenced into trying this from a friend of mine (thanks Tollo!) and I was totally blown away.  Standard roguelike movement with interesting talents and builds you can tinker with.  Fun loot to get killed by or carried by.  Will this rocket launcher kill the big bad around the corner?  88 percent chance to hit!  Is there a chance it'll hit the wall next to me and gib me?  ...yeah.  Did it?  Yeah.  I laughed and started over.  Another learning experience!  The next time I didn't fire near a wall and used splash damage to kill the big bad. The sound is great, you can hear the low hooting of bad guys scraping along the halls or robotic chittering.  You can use it to figure out what you're walking into or use it to stage an ambush!  The guns all sound great.  Reloading a shotgun chk-chk?  yep, it's in there.   The protag cussing and talking ♥♥♥♥?  check.The graphics are great for a traditional roguelike,  I'm used to ascii but what they've done is really clean and I think we need to ascend to this level of UI for a new audience to enjoy roguelikes.   Some minor things don't perfectly line up (like enemies dying before the bullet or rocket hits, some of the tiles being a little jittery sometimes) but it's really well done.  If you're easily frustrated there are difficulty options, but dying and learning is a very big part of roguelikes.  I hope this review helps if you're on the fence!  ...one more run.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game, but not for me. I loved the music and the game play mechanics. But it made me realise I prefer rougelites over rougelikes. I want to actually UNLOCK stuff as I progress. New classes, new guns that may drop, SOMETHING. Higher difficulties and trying new builds is not enough incentive for me personally to replay this style of game because I'm just going to play the build I know works. Why waste my time with anything else? So, while I refunded it, it's not the game's fault whatsoever. It's very good. You absolutely should buy it. It's just not to my taste. I'm going to stick with rougelites, like Binding of Isaac, Our Darker Purpose, or Dead Cells.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: DRL is probably my all-time favorite traditional-roguelike. (Looking forward to buying the commercial version on Steam as Jupiter Hell Classic.)So, with solid voice acting, sound mix, improved visuals and many other improvements, this one delivers LIKE HELL.If you love at least one movie from the golden era of VHS (Alien, The Thing, Predator, Evil Dead) and if you dig traditional roguelikes, don't think twice about it. You're in for a treat IN HELL.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Insanely good game. Everything is just right about it. The variety, pacing, difficulty, visuals, soundtrack - all amazing.The game offers lots of different gamemodes along with adjustable difficulty. Plenty of unique weapons to pick from and mods to upgrade said weapons with. Even though it's a turnbased game you don't waste time on min-maxing fluff keeping the game's pace dynamic.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I backed the Beta on Kickstarter and have been playing since it was made available to me. This game is simultaneously true to the Doom/90s sci-fi hell aesthetic and holds on its own amazingly. The polish and consistency of this game is great and it's been getting gradually harder as they add more stuff, but has never felt either unfair or boring. Like chess with shotguns indeed, but also auto rifles, fireballs, demons, and space stations.As a roguelike, it checks all the boxes (unless you're being super pure about ASCII graphics, in which case there is be an option for you (or there will be soon down the line). There is also an easy mode for you to learn the game, but even that will challenge you as you're learning the game. The devs are super great people, shoutout to the fun-loving and communicative Epyon and Chaosforge team. I know there's lots of content planned and I can't wait to play it.Edit: forgot to mention, the engine is custom and is very smooth and slick and cool.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: The classic ASCII rogues all suck.  They're fiddly, they're obtuse and new players are often instructed to dive right into a wiki because they're nearly unplayable.  They're nearly illegible given that 98% of their "graphics" are just random characters.This game Ol' Yellers those games.  This is the classic-style rogue I've always wanted.Took 50 hours to beat the first time (on medium).  It's fun as hell.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun. That's the most important thing to say about it. I've played plenty of rogue-likes but there is something about this one that makes me come back for more. Combat can be as fast or slow as you like, as the game is turn based, which is handy because sometimes you have to play very strategically. Controls are simple enough and make sense and the upgrades are great.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan ChaosForge's previous games, I've been anxiously waiting for Jupiter Hell.  The gameplay and overall vibe is fantastic. In my opinion it's the perfect next step for this kind of roguelike. The 3D graphics are gorgeous and the mechanics make for a fast-paced, exciting turn based gaming experience. My favorite roguelikes are DCSS, ADOM, and DRL. This game maintains the roguelike feel of these games, but this is really bringing something new. I anticipate spending many hours on this!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing it for like a week or so and it's been really fun. There's a lot of ♥♥♥♥ missing/not implemented but it's still very playable.One thing I've got to say is that it's sad to see some of the drama or whatever in the reviews. I know the dev wants to tell you to stfu normie, but he can't, and it really hurts my heart to see that. The game looks like it's meant to draw in a bigger crowd like some other recently release roguelikes, and that's cool. I know they have to be professional, but as a player, I don't.The spirit of of elitism and aristocracy in roguelikes will NEVER die. The ancient cult of 1000 ascended players will spearhead the extermination of all noobs regardless of race, creed, or beliefs. If you are a noob, savescummer, or clicker don't entry because you will be burned and died!I'm really tired of people who try to come in and infiltrate roguelike communities/roguelike discord servers/and roguelike steam reviews and try to push their agendas. The roguelikes discord has mods who have nothing to do with roguelikes whatsoever, ToME and DCSS were both ruined by a problem player who goes by the name "Minqmay", and lots of true roguelikes on steam are voted down because the player expected a roguelite. _childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give a neutral rating to this game since it's in early access and the developers seem like they are passionate and have every intention of making this game as good as possible. However, what's currently on offer here, especially for the price, I feel just isn't worth it. I was hoping for a more tactical/strategic game, but what is here like others have said, plays more like a twin stick shooter that is "turn" based. The enemies only move when you do similar to SUPERHOT, but that's really where the strategy ends. You'll try to get into cover or out of harms way depending on the enemies that are in a room, shoot them until dead, and repeat.As of now there isn't much progression, your character will level up as you kill enemies so you can pick perks. You can also find better weapons/armour in the levels. There aren't any permanent unlocks or upgrades to try to obtain, just move through the rooms, kill enemies, repeat. The areas all feel the same just with a different coat of paint so this got tiring for me very quickly.The UI also has room for improvement. Right now it's hard to quickly tell exactly what type of enemy you're looking at, their health, damage output, etc. The info for your own weapons isn't super helpful either, you have to go into the equipment menu just to tell the difference in damage, range, type of the weapons. Thankfully, there is an option to turn off the CRT effect that is on by default as I found it to make things even worse.It might seem like I'm pretty down on the game, but I think it's a solid base for what could become something great down the road. That's really the problem for now, it could be a great game, but what is currently here is very bare bones. It's a nice foundation and the developers will hopefully build on it and make it a fun, tactical, varied experience. My advice would be to hold off for now, but keep an eye on it to see how it progresses.

_childDocuments_.review: If I can use a neutral recommendation, I would. It is not a bad game, but not too good either. Very simple game where ever you see it. Probably I will find the time to finished it, after all I already buy the game, waiting a few more updates first.If you play games where you need to think, as I usually do, and you play Rogue-like (I mean a true Rogue-like). Jupiter Hell (JH) is the most simplistic game. I recommend it for the "Rogue like" newcomer, this Rogue-like is for the masses (with everything trimmed, and still steam kids complaint XD), if you already play real Rogue-like don't look here unless you look for a casual game.When you play a good RL game, you need to think, you win the game because you're thinking smart, because of your knowledge of the game and how you use the tools making improvisations to get out of trouble, using the different game mechanics, strategy and skills to win the game, but when you need to learn a set of skills to build your character and do it in the specific way to win the game, well, your strategy is summed up thinking when you shoot and when you cover.If you trace a line to compare Rogue-like games, where one end of the line you have Rogue (and all the game mechanics) and the other end of the line, Jupiter Hell. JH is at the far end, with all the game mechanics of a Rogue trimmed. In other words, Rogue (1980-1985) is still a more interesting game, and you can play it right now 2022 with tile texture. If you read someone said "JH is a true roguelike" that person does not know what he is talking about.- JH don't use 8-way of movement, just 4-way of movement, the combat tactic it is very cropped. Even Rogue-like console games use 8-way of movement.- JH don't have in deep tactic, beyond covering yourself and using some items. (Chess with shotguns, I don't think so)- the levels are short/small, adapted to the 4-way of movement, which basically means little exploration.- I died once because I didn't see something that was in front blocking my shoot, with ASCII you can know what's in front, with a clear tile texture or clear 3D you know what's in front, with isometric 3D view, with dark/shadows effects and visual effects sometime you can miss it, unless re-designed. (Maybe is me)- After writing it, I decided to remove more complaints about the game mechanics :DIf you trimmed too much the "Rogue game mechanics", without adding weight in other Rogue game mechanics, depends on the approach, you should have a roguelike focused on tactic combat, but if you trimmed more, you have a bland game with neither, that is Jupiter Hell. A bland, simple game not similar (like) to Rogue, or using the real "Lite" meaning (). JP is a Rogue-lite

_childDocuments_.review: Considering design it can't be much more straightforward I guess. Also sharing the thing that this genius slim'n'fast game concept would work flawlessly even on a retro iron like a Commodore 64. Part RPG, part turn-based strategy, and also none of them as all of the mechanics have been made more efficient than of a typical game representing these genres. Due to my occupation I travel a lot and Jupiter Hell is a pretty good option to turn the long travelling hours into fun.Just a footnote: Around 1995 I was involved in a game development on C64 called "Geister", making the music for that. All the sources were destroyed in a housefire. That was the end of it, you know back in time a game developer was often a single guy. Jupiter Hell and that ancient project had a couple of surprising similarities considering game concept. The project failed to reach the finish line and the developer died in 2020 so it will never come to be. The only memento remained was the pack of chiptunes on my old archive floppy disks.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, if you're reading this to find out if you should buy this, go grab DoomRL (or DRL, as Bethesdas lawyers forced them to rename it).  It's a rogue-like with permadeath and some RPG elements and a ton of fun. You're gonna die, a lot, but the fun is in honing your abilities as the player. There is a little more level variation between the two games, and the graphics clearly are different - I don't say "better" because 2D/3D is a choice these days, not a technological advancement like it was 25 years ago.It's still in beta, but that doesn't mean ♥♥♥♥ - other than the super occasional crash (I've only had 3 and they were back to back before the latest update) it is stable and I play the game at 100+ fps with everything turned up to max. A warning to nvidia+linux players: turn off framelock if the game keeps locking up to an unplayable level. It runs smooth, there are no input errors that I've seen and the controls are identical to DRL for the most part, and smooth. A lot of the levels look same-y but once you play you won't care in the least. If you're even remotely thinking about buying this but aren't 100% sure, go play DRL (DoomRL) made by the same dev - play it and imagine that it looks exactly like Jupiter Hell but with updated (better?) music and all the little details that 3D allows over 2D. That's an 85-90% accurate comparison.If you have played Rogue-likes before and like the video/screenshots, grab it. It's not even a risk. I love this game.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a certain type of person who will really like this game, and I was surprised I was it. There's a lot of small tweaks I very much would have loved, but take it for what it is: an action flick with a solid set of mechanics and a foul mouth. Were there cheesy references? You bet your Duke Nukem there were. Were there unexplained stats and obscure mechanics? Absolutely.Still: It isn't easy to make a game _both_ a solid follower of roguelike traditions, yes, down to not having unlockable permanent gimmicks, and explore the hallmarks of a Doom/Quake (or dare I say Blake Stone?) at the same time. The fun in gearing up with different combinations of the character abilities, affixes on gear, and tactics for navigating the map is a pretty compelling reason to play it if the idea of thinking up new builds and gambling that the right ammo or weapon will drop appeals to you. For me it did! And the translation of things like cover around corners, collecting clues as to what high-end items drop where within the world map, and the ability to specialize your class without slowing the pace of the game down - those are a real treat in a game that hides its cleverness behind cliche.

_childDocuments_.review: I have over sixty hours in this game, and I still feel like I can escape death if I press the keys quicker.I was unaware of DRL and AliensRL, the two roguelikes of which this is a direct descendant, when I first found Jupiter Hell in (very) early access.  Though those original games still hold up as incredible examples of fun, tight, ranged combat roguelike gameplay, Jupiter Hell is a revolutionary reimagining.Since Early Access, so much depth and cool stuff has been added that coming back to it at 1.0 felt not like a new game, but like I was entering a much, much larger world.Jupiter Hell is roguelike, distilled down to its essence, and imbued with style to burn.  It absolutely oozes style, from the retro scan-line display of the menus, to the beautiful graphics -- certainly the prettiest graphics you'll find in a classic, true roguelike -- to the satisfying sounds of gunfire, explosions, heavy metal and plenty of hilarious vulgarity from the narrator.It's a roguelike that you can win in under two hours (and probably much quicker, but that's as good as I've done), but never feels repetitive.  I have sixty hours and the stats indicate I've seen about a quarter of all the possible unique items, skills, and secret locations.  Every run is different, and presents a fresh set of decisions to make at every turn.It is not an ultra-complex roguelike like other modern takes on the genre.  Pick your guns, pick your skills, pick your upgrades, and blow stuff up.  It's quick, it's straightforward, and it might be the most plainly fun game in my Steam library.  And if you get tired of the main game, there are endless variations, challenges, and trials to toy with as you "level up" your player data.  This has no in-game effect, it's just for bragging rights.  And brag I shall!I have over sixty hours in this game, and I'm as excited to hit "New Game" now as I was the first time.I have over sixty hours in this game, and my hands still start shaking when I get near the final boss.I have over sixty hours in this game, and I still feel like I can escape death if I press the keys quicker.Something is wrong with me.

_childDocuments_.review: Strangely addicting and satisfies all the rogue-like checkboxes for me. I often find myself on the "You had died screen" lamenting on my characters untimely death to be spamming the A button on my controller to get another round going. I'd recommend playing a few rounds on medium to get a good feel for the game and characters and then bump it up to hard.Things I'd like to see:* Better support for Steam controllers (and joystick movements in general over the D-Pad). It works decently but I find dropped inputs and/or repeated inputs that happen. I have to switch back to the D-Pad for menus which while serviceable is a bit cumbersome. Manually targeting using the joysticks is way too sensitive at the moment and I have to switch over to the keyboard to accurately select my target.* More visual aids to tell what kind of weapons the "human" enemies have. An icon over the enemy head that has a symbol for the weapon equipped would be hugely helpful for target prioritization and strategy. Someone with a shotgun is treated very differently than someone with a rocket launcher and right now it is really hard to tell what weapon the enemy humans have until they pop a round off at you.* Better visual indicators on what type of ammo a weapon uses (maybe ammo icons on the equipped weapon hud). You have things like SMGs that use a variety of ammo types and although it is stated for some reason my brain likes to presume it's always 9MM.* More weapon types!Overall if you enjoy rogue-likes I highly recommend. Plenty of content and fun times to be had and I'm very interested in what additional content and polish they will be adding to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't put a ton of time into Jupiter Hell yet, but the time I have has been very fun and it holds up to good old D**mRL and AliensRL lineage.  Both of those games where true Roguelikes by the Berlin Interpretation and while some die-hard purist will argue that anything not ASCII automatically disqualifies a game as being a Roguelike, only the those without any willingness to give or take would not classify this game rightfully as a Roguelike.   I have seen some trolls trying to say that Jupiter Hell is not a Roguelike, but pay no attention to them because this game has what it takes to be classified as a true Roguelike and not just a Rogue-lite.   Sorry for my rant.As far as game play wise the game is very solid and runs smoothly.   While my game time so far is limited to just around a half hour, I had no bugs or crashes.  The game runs smooth without any lagging or hiccups.   So if you are leery of investing money in an EA game, you can rest easy that this game is already playing smoother than the majority of released games.As far as those who are upset with the price tag, you really need to find a job.  The game is priced a very worthy price for what fun you will get.  If you are one of those people that don't like paying for Roguelike games, well there are plenty free ones out there, including the predecessors to this very game.  However if you appreciate a great game with unlimited replayability and want to show your appreciation I highly doubt the asking price will change your mind in the least.  It is more than worth $25.The game has very nice graphics, sound effects and music.   I am one of those players that usually disables the music in my games because I find it annoying and breaking immersion, however Jupiter Hell's soundtrack is one of the few games that from the get-go I have enjoyed the soundtrack and haven't even considered disabling it.Oh, also if you aren't sure about the CRT mode, it is a setting that you can disable.  I have seen some people here and there ask about that.All in all if you enjoy Roguelikes then you owe it to yourself to pickup Jupiter Hell ASAP.* Update 8/1/19 @ 10:43pm CST * I have put about an hour and 15 minutes into the game so far and while I am mostly just speed running for the heck of it, the game is still a huge blast.  In normal RL fashion pretty much all of my runs (about 15 of them so far) have ended in a disaster of my own making, usually the getting cocky kind.    The game runs so smooth that it is very easy sometimes to forget to stop and think about my tactics.   It reminds me a lot of when I am speed running through Dungeon Crawl Stone Soup.   It has that same feel where you get into a zone and forget that a big bunch of mobs might just be around the other corner.     I love it when a game does that.   I love it when a game is fun and the biggest enemy to my completing a run is my own self, not the mobs.   In true RL fashion 99% of the time you really are your own worse enemy.    It is that feel that has always made DCSS one of my favorite games of all time and increases my love for Roguelikes in general.  And Jupiter Hell certainly capitalizes on that feeling.I have had to pull myself away.  That darn "just one more run" mindset is certainly engaged here. :)

_childDocuments_.review: It is fun. Until it isn't. lol It is VERY unforgiving. For the longest time I could never finish a game on medium (and easy is like "shame mode" to me, so I don't even bother with it). Must have tried 50 times before winning (with a Scout Gunslinger build). I always died stupidly. Most often than not, I died because I was slightly reckless and I often die with an inventory full of survival possibilities. I get caught in the action and sometimes forget to use the class skill that would have saved my life. It is fun, but nevertheless, losing hours of gameplay over and over again gets old (and depressing). Seeing a promising build die stupidly is always heartbreaking. This game makes me want to rip off the foam armrests from my computer chair with my teeth. This game is a very strong contender for the game that makes me alt-F4 the most often. But you know what? I still recommend it, because I hate you and want you to suffer as well. :) No, seriously, no matter how unforgiving this game is, it has a very addictive play pattern and you will eventually come back for more punishment. And you might even win as some point. Damn you, Jupiter Hell!Anyway, I find the turn-based system quite clever and effective. Each turn takes a set amount of time, but you might be able to take several actions per turn, and doesn't feel like a turn because everything is so fluid. Everything happens all at once. The loot system can be super generous and give you a huge boost right from the beginning OR you only get meh! stuff and sometimes the RNG will put you in a situation you simply cannot survive. You have to take risks to get better equipment, but it might kill you. Also, foregoing risk and not getting better equipment can also kill you. So taking risk is always best, I think. Other than that the music is great, the graphics are nice, sounds are satisfying. All in all, this game is both fun AND an excruciating  punishment. If that sounds good to you, I totally recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Before posting anything here I'll preface this by saying I'm a Kickstarter for this game. I also played a DRL prior to this.This is certainly an expensive roguelike by any measure and it is likely going to be a major turnoff to anyone looking to play this game. But I think there is indeed good value here for those looking for a really good roguelike. Graphically this is one of the more impressive titles on the market. Gameplay wise it has been streamlined quite well and excellently designed to work for players using devices that don't necessarily have access to a full keyboard. In respect to Traditional Roguelike designs one will find that this will probably tick enough of the boxes that one will fully consider it to be one. Content wise one will find that this is a complete game.In further describing this game, I will note that unlike other roguelikes it is a lot more fast paced. _childDocuments_.review: My first impressions vieeo: Roguelikes and particularly Roguelites have become a dime a dozen these days. Many are of the Lite variety because a lot of players prefer to have an element of permanent progression to go along with the inevitable many deaths. This is usually my preference too but when a game comes along that does the full on Roguelike formula super well, it sticks with me. Originally starting out as a mod for DOOM, this is basically if you took that, turned it intot a Roguelike and splashed some Duke Nukem style attitude over the top.You're a foul-mouthed space marine who crash lands on a procedurally generated station where everything's gone bad and have to fight your way out. You'll play one of 3 distinct classes, all of which have their own loadouts, abilities and skill trees to advance. Though the game is turn based, moving between spaces rapidly created a fluid, real-time like animation, which I quite like. Exploration and combat are the two main drivers, though fully exploring every level isn't necessary, though you can be presented with branching paths if you do. When you encounter enemies, you can quickly fire on what's in front of you or also manually aim your shots and take advantage of the environment.You have an inventory and there's a variety of weapons, armour, throwables and items you'll come across but this isn't like other games where you want to hold onto everything to either sell or scrap it. Take the best stuff you can get, leave and rest and move on. Despite being turn-based, elements like this keep the pacing up and make the game feel fluid and not overly sluggish.As I said before, this is a proper Roguelike, meaning when you die, you're back to square one. There's no permanent abilities and the only things you unlock are challenge stages which don't impact the main mode. And you will die a lot. This game is rock hard and requires smart play to get through. Being randomly generated, sometimes RNG won't be as much on your side as other times, though every seed is exposed to you so you can run the same layout again if you want. There are multiple difficulty levels but even the easiest level is still a huge challenge.This is a dark game by design but it still looks great and the soundtrack is sublime for this kind of title. I really hope it's offered for sale at some point. The protagonist is foul-mouthed and crass in the old-school way and though you can turn this off, I actually appreciated it. It's nice to see a game that isn't afraid to embrace its own identity and doesn't care about offending those who weren't going to be its customers anyway.If you've already decided you don't like Roguelikes, this won't make you into a fan of the genre. But if you're someone who thinks the right title could sell you on it, this is definitely a good one to check out.
