_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of Doom back in the day, and also a fan of turn based roguelike games, I was really excited to try this out. Unfortunately I just couldn’t get into it. It took me a while to figure out why.When I think of Doom I think of demons right up in your face being carved apart with a chainsaw. I think about frantic paced exciting action, running away from fights at low health only to come back again and kick some A. While this game makes a valiant attempt to recapture that feeling, I think it ultimately fails in what it is trying to achieve.Where this game succeeds is in the voice acting and in the music. However where it fails hard is in the presentation. The game screen is so zoomed out you feel completely detached from what is happening on screen. Everything is dark and underwhelming. Your character looks the same as all the enemies. The camera never moves from a fixed perspective.As a result of this, the game fails to take advantage of the rag doll physics, lighting effects, giblet effects etc that have been built into the game. When you fire a shotgun into a demon at point blank range and see it explode, it should be exciting. Instead it just feels underwhelming.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This brings back sweet memories of Doom and Duke Nukem. I wasn't too sure about it when I first started playing, it took me a hot minuet to get the hang of combat and what did and did not work. But I am finding myself enjoying this more and more as I progress deeper into the game. I often find myself wanting to clear one more room, one more corner, one more level and show the demon scum the short end of my boom stick. Hail to the king baby.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: A true rogue-lite! Great skill system and loot drop, but will ♥♥♥♥ you up because you didn't use a barrel or wait long enough to reload. Kudos to game developed. Enjoyable game, fun item system. I really had to think about upgrading my weapons because weapon/ammo drop rate was variable! But tutorial was ♥♥♥♥♥♥ explaning that when armor hits "0/1200" durability it just DISAPPEARS. Mods on weapons last forever, Mods on armor last as long as the armor!!I spent 10 hrs playing, only to lose on final boss in less than 10 minutes. Because my armor "wore out" and just dropped right off me without warning.  All the bleed effects and burning that was resisted over 4+ hrs was suddenly 'not there" and I died by a thousand cuts: Sort of like purchasing the game was!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good - I like audiovisuals, atmosphere, design and gameplay. Solid roguelike with three distinct classes each offering multiple valid builds. The loot is interesting too. Props for authors for balancing the game well enough, so it offers good level of challenge - the game can get very difficult especially on Hard and onwards. Medium is much more forgiving, but still changing.There are various modes, but I personally enjoyed main campaign on Hard/Medium and 'Endless dungeon' - I hope the authors give some polish to the latter in the future, because I think there is some potential there. Content wrapped as Sci-Fi on a distant planet filled with demonic presence which needs to taken care of.I rank the title as 8+/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Jupiter Hell is great, thinky fun, yet still retains its brutal roots in DOOM theme. There's lots of great tactical decision making about what class, upgrades, and guns you choose depending on your playstyle and objectives for a run. I always keep coming back for more to experiment with and there's always something new to experience here.The graphics are amazing for a traditional roguelike and you can really tell the amount of optimization and coding effort that went into the game. JH sets the standard for other traditional roguelikes to follow from an artistic standpoint and it stands heads and shoulders above the rest in its part of the rogue-game genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun rogue like concept that plays with the idea of the game moves when you move. The issue im having is how it just beats your ass suddenly for no reason. you can easily walk through the first two levels. Kill a few enemies. collect some weapons. Upgrade gear and skills.Then boom lvl 3. you take 3-5 steps outside the elevator and suddenly you got 6-7 enemies on you and not enough ammo or rounds to deal with them quickly. And since every attack and dodge is % based. It feels more like luck and hinesight then it feels like skill. In around 30 min I managed to do 3 runs. each run like 10 min each. And each run i felt like i steamed rolled everything up to the point of the game saying ♥♥♥♥ you and killing me.maybe i try it some more later. I can't say It's a bad game. but right now it doesnt feel like its for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Great fun and I learned new bad words!Update:  After putting some hours in, I'm really impressed with the following:-Dev updates - awesome patch notes and continuous improvements.  Due to this (and native Linux support) I'll be checking out everything this dev produces.-Replayability - the different skill allow you to replay with a good variety of diff playstyles.  Levels variety and randomness of path makes it feel diff each run-While it's not real-time, after you get guud, my runs tend to move very fast.....maybe thats why I die so much ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Used to play their old roguelike titles (especially loved DiabloRL!) and was sad back then when they announced they would focus their time on this project. That was quite some time ago but after all it was worth it.Great title and atmosphere (music is very nice as well) and good fun. Got to io before I was completely destroyed by some reavers, well, maybe next time.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Well I uh, I gave it a shot. I know I haven't played enough to warrant a full review, but at least I can leave my reason for my refund request here.On my second try after getting killed due to being overzealous with my medpacks, I finished the first level, and took the elevator to the next map.Right outside the second level's start, I found myself on a T intersection with enemies pouring out of every single door. I shot a few with the two weapons I had with me, all the while running trying to find a little cover. There were demons in every direction I ran to, catching me in an alley with enemies just going to town on me from both ends. I used all I had on me, but unfortunately, it was a losing situation. I doubt there would have been anything that I, now or 50 game hours from now, would have been able to do to salvage that encounter. Now imagine this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ happening at the tail end of a run.The reason I purchased Jupiter Hell was because I wanted to play a turn based roguelike game that isn't banking on being extremely difficult and unfair. This is the reason I tried this one and not The Pit, Quasimorph, Qud, or any of the alternatives, and well, I guess this game just tries as hard to be "hardcore" as them, because I am absolutely not going to give my time to a game that on the very second level has demonstrated to have this little interest in respecting it. At least it's forthcoming enough that I've been able to make that decision in under 30 minutes.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Good Rogue-like (no real cross run progression), that is set in a doom type universe. There are 3 "classes" each with a different perk tree with a few cross over perks between them. Mechanics in the Jupiter Hell are typical for an over the top tactical game with cover and line of sight implemented well. Weapons and armor have set values depending on type and then have a random rarity that goes from common to unique, additionally there are two gear slots that can also contain things to help build your character. Difficulty on normal seems appropriate though some builds seem to be vastly more powerful than others. That being said I feel like there should be more perks available for each class, which would allow for more builds. Overall I give it a 7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I don't review games but..As a spawn of the 80's and a person with a discerning budget adequate for indie games I quickly fell in love with Kisielewicz's interpretation of DOOM as a Roguelike, and have been following his work ever since. I've been a lurking supporter of ChaosForge since the early days of the beta on ITCH.IO and payed for this game twice on ITCH.IO and steam and  I tell you, it was worth every penny to be a part of such an amazing game and would do it again because this game is so well done for the price. This game is punishing yet enjoyable, to a degree you will loose time and burn food on the stove as if it wasn't an auto-pause style game. If you enjoy challenges and a fan of tactical top-down shooters with a DOOM style aesthetic, you will enjoy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: DoomRL/A Doom themed roguelikeOne completion on Easy, 1 Angel of Shotgunnery completion on Normal, 1 Angel of Vampirism completion on Normal, one Haste Trial completion on normal, 128 deaths to those 4 wins.- Great classic roguelike gameplay, complete with no meta progression, punishing overconfidence, and needing to learn to actually progress, with a bit of RNG that occasionally lets you do more than you normally could. (I definitely would have died in my Vampirism run if I hadn't gotten a Wavesplitter early).- Ingame supported ways to not go for the same build every time: Random/Fated has been really nice for keeping me from just trying to go Gun Kata Scout every run. If this option wasn't there, sure I could just generate some random numbers somehow and try to follow that, but I know myself well enough that I know I wouldn't do that.- You can just quit out of a run at any time and resume it later.- Unless you're saving your run summaries somewhere, there's no way (currently that I know of) to see what equipment and skill build you went on your runs. You also can't seem to tell if you were doing some challenge on the run.- The slightly tilted camera angle is a bit awkward for me, and I would really prefer it to be head on.- It's difficult to tell exactly how much cover is doing for you/you can't see how high of a chance the enemy has to hit you. I think the developer has said they're looking into this, so fingers crossed.- The game once told me to stop watching porn when I alt-tabbed for a while.- ASCII mode is a real blast from the pastI love this game even though I'm terrible at it. Even though there's only 3 classes and no real story to speak of, it doesn't feel stale.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I have very much enjoyed my time so far with this game. The focus on ranged being the primary method of combat (instead of the traditional melee combat used in rogue) really shakes up the formula in an interesting way.I've also noticed that balance seems pretty good. I'm yet to look at a master skill and think why would I want that and they all seem to have there place.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely satisfying Turn Based with some roguelike elements. The fluidity of the controls seamlessly blends TBS combat with exploration and movement. Controls are exactly how you would want them, akin to your traditional TBS. Re-bound my half-keyboard to have all the actions on it so I can play 1 handed FeelsGoodMan (new keybinds should be shown in UI, quick fix). The brutal feel of combat where boxes scatter or limbs fly gives a Crusader: No Regret vibes where you (or your enemies) inflict massive damage to each other and the environment. Graphics and theme are extremely polished and the theme definitely has some strong Doom vibes. Re-playability seems extremely high and there's numerous biomes to keep the areas fresh. The random encounters, tasks, and sidenotes actually give you mini-missions that could improve your run. Chest loot is exciting to find, always looking for that next piece of loot. Strongly recommend the game in it's current state. IMO, can only get better from here with more seeds, biomes, loot, classes and other procedural generation. Will update as I get a better feel, but I will definitely be logging some hours into this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This is a phantastic modern incarnation of a traditional Roguelike. It plays so well with a controller, which is a refreshing way to play such a game from a comfortable position further away from the screen. The size of the HUD elements and the adjustable map zoom accomodate this well. The aesthetics of the interface hits all the the right tastebuds for me, as a kid from of the 80's and 90's. I remember curved CRT screens and that very font from old textfiles. If you like old-school Quake and Doom, you will appreciate some content referencing those games, such as keycards, armor and health orbs. The gameplay heavily emphasizes tactics and positioning. The mechanic of cover is most important. Bits of lore is fed to the player via e-mail messages exchanged between staff members of the bases on Jupiter's moons. However the content of these messages are so vague, that I mostly can't make out much sense about what they are trying to tell me. From what I understand, they hint at good loot that can be found in branches, which can enable advanced players to aim for a certain exploration path and character build. The turn based nature allows for relaxing and cautious play. The animation of the turns is so fluid, allowing for faster play in less dangerous situations. You can get into a real rush of killing sprees! Gibbing the enemies feels so satisfying, as well as all the weapon sounds of shooting and reloading. The game is brutally hard, but the typical audience expects that and I like a real challenge. It took me over 30 hours to get my first win on Easy difficulty, even though I have many years of experience with Roguelikes. The game has no metaprogression system unlike several modern Roguelikes, but this adheres more to a traditional Roguelike. The graphics and the lighting are pure eyecandy with highest quality settings on a 4K monitor. Tough I am a passionate Metalhead, I play with the music muted, because the metal soundtrack is too repetitive and generic for my taste. Instead I use quiet playback of some Dark Ambient from outside the game, as this enables me to better hear the enemy noises and I also find it more atmospheric like that. The official Discord community is very friendly and helpful.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: NOT A ROGUELIKE!!! Just a turn based top-down shooter: low variety of items, feats and perks; procedural level generator makes clones and twins.TL;DR: no content, nice mechanicsUPD: Okay, this is a roguelike, although the roguelikeness here is at a minimum. It's more of a turn-based cover shooter (that nice person in comments is right). I changed the rating due to the fact that you can not give a bad rating to a game that you play over and over again.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I played this several months after it entered early access, was very dissatisfied with how dumbed down it was compared to it's predecessor, and my complaints were generally dismissed as elitist and premature. If it were any other devloper I would have gotten a refund but I'm a huge fan of DoomRL so I figured I'd leave it on the shelf and hope it got better. It has, but not in the ways it needed to.Go play DoomRL instead. It's so much better, honestly. It's full of unique enemies, weapons, and easter eggs. There's alternate fire modes for weapons and destructible terrain. The gameplay flows more smoothly because you don't have to wait or move one turn at a time and check for enemies, the game lets you move a long distance and only interrupts you if you spot an enemy. It has more interesting achievements that aren't just doing all the challenges on a given difficulty. The special levels are far more interesting with solid themes. It has a better UI that shows your character stats like movement speed and resistances properly. It has better combat balance, instead of limiting your sight range to significantly less than the effective range of half your weapons.The only things this game really has going for it are the graphics. It makes a lot of sacrifices so that it looks nice and can be played more easily with a gamepad. And while the game is pretty for a roguelike, there are better genres to sate that appetite.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Good Roguelike, keeps the core gameplay simple for a faster paced sort of play, but comes with plenty of build options for the 3 main classes, a variety of gear with different modifiers, and a crafting and modification system to really customise your pew pew to your playstyle. An isometric 3D perspective with explosions and lighting effects should also make it quite approachable for those who like Roguelikes, but dislike ASCII art.A worthy spiritual followup to DoomRL.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: With modern crappy business practices and overall tasteless designs in video games, roguelike genre is at least worth to try, offering endless replayability and a ton of memorable moments with no strings attached. Jupiter Hell is, in my opinion, probably the best way to introduce new players to this amazing genre. Set in the 90's sci-fi fictional universe heavily influenced by original DOOM, Jupiter Hell is quite easy to learn, but is very tricky to fully master with its tactical gameplay and constant decision-making: you have limited inventory slots, you have limited weapon slots, you can take different paths and use different builds on different characters, and all of this , always keeping you on your toes. Luckily, with average  run time of nearly two hours (compare this to my ~60 hours for a golden  ending), you can always start over and try a different approach.The game is visually appealing, with blood splats everywhere, barrels exploding, dead monsters falling off cliffs, and that's accompanied by heavy metal soundtrack. It even has a plot (), what else are you looking for?On the negative side, with such relatively simple graphics, you'll probably expect that this game can be played on low-end video cards (e.g. Intel), but as of March 2020, this is not the case.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely fantastic true-blooded rougelike. If you're a fan of old school rougelikes like Dungeon Crawl: Stone Soup you'll love this. It's hard, and a bit grindy to start, but there's a surprising depth to character builds and the many different branches make each run different enough that it won't get stale for a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute gem of a game. Plays incredible on the Steamdeck (crashes on exit but easy to fix before the game gets verified status). I was a bit put off by the music at first but the later stages of the game offer some great variety as well. Combat is tactical, fast, unforgiving and highly rewarding.Try easy, get a feel of the game, but quickly move to medium difficulty where the game really starts to shine. Terminal Emails and messages give hints as to which paths you can take, with some better suited to certain builds. Character development is straightforward but offers a lot to play with!9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun and I would totally get it perhaps if it were on sale.For me, after winning one run, on easy . . .  I was sort of done with this game. And the reason is, you will die often. And, you do learn from your mistakes, but sometimes you don't, like when an enemy hits you for half of your health and your run ends unexpectedly. A run, played carefully for me, takes about 4 hours. There is no metaprogression, and there is no saving, so dying in 2 hours after playing a very well thought out and maximized run just feels completely awful. This genre is super fascinating and fun to play. There is a lot going on, with item use and management. Planning for upgrades and there are quite a few routes to take within each of the 4 biomes to give you very diverse runs. Right now skills feel very specifically tailored to certain guns. I am not encouraged to take rifles or guns that use 7.62 ammo it feels. As someone pointed out, this game really forces you to play defensively. and that can often slow game play down. With that said, there are certain situations where things go downhill quick. for example, using a medkit takes an actiion. and while it is almost always a bad idea to use it during battle, it intuitively feels like the right thing to do even though I have died that way many times.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: So here we finally are, full 1.0 release. It's a hell of a roguelike, combat focused and stripped of a lot of the tedium you'd find in most classic roguelikes. The game looks great, runs great (minus making half the map explode from barrels) and has a ♥♥♥♥ ton of replayability. Which is good cause this game is also balls hard, it took me a good while to beat it on Ultra, but man did it ever feel good. The devs are great, open to communication, and were open to balance suggestions as well as bug fixing throughout early access. If you want a combat focused roguelike with extensive class based skill trees and Diablo like loot dropping look no further.As a side note, and touching on sound design a bit, the hero is voiced by none other than Mark Meer (Commander Shepard) and he is absolutely chewing the scene with his VO as a pseudo Doom Guy. Some might find it cringey, but I love it in the Doom comic sort of cheese-fest it is. It can be safely disabled though if wanted. Music is appropriate and mildly catchy but nothing to write home about, I've swapped it out a few times for a synthwave playlist. Jupiter Hell is a game I picked up a while back on a whim and has become one of my favorite roguelikes of all time.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: It's Doom the Roguelike. In 3D. That's all it is so far and that's all we ever really needed.It's a roguelike (generated levels with permadeath), with firearms and cover tactics, where you shoot zombies and demons in space. The tactics keep it challenging and the challenge modes and rank progression give you a reason to keep playing it over and over and over.The graphics are great: the "CRT" GUI and general presentation is wonderful, if a bit dark and oddly GPU intensive for a top-down game.The soundtrack is nice: unlike some other reviewers, I really like it especially towards the end.The gameplay is perfect, it plays like a more streamlined DRL, but all the tactical choices are more obviously visible.Clearly, there needs to be some more content added. It's missing some skills (I first beat DRL with a Marine shotgun build, which really isn't possible now with the current skill progressions), there's no levers/traps, it could use some more level branches, the special weapon builds aren't implemented yet (and they better be!), but the core is there enough to completely replace DoomRL as my roguelike of choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: It is pretty good until you reach Io. At that point if you didn't make a build that would be tailored for that moon enemies then you will suffer. Sadly, that limits your choices to a very few picks that are not exactly optimal for the content that precedes Io. Considering that this is a 2 year old game, you can expect this to not change.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. Managed my first medium win after about 12 hours I'd say.I really like the different classes and the "ultimate" skills you can work towards with each of them. The game gets brutally hard, but you get a lot stronger throughout the run to tackle the ever increasing difficulty. Loot is not entirely random as some locations drop loot based on your prefered weapon on the run.My #1 tip for progressing further: Running for cover is good! You get a juicy dodge bonus as you run and most enemies don't have excellent ranges so their hit changes as you get distance become noticeably worse.One trick is to not open doors manually but instead destroying them by shooting them from a safer spot. Even the wall right next to a door is better than being exposed and taking a turn to duck into cover. Also getting any of the movement speed skills can allow you to easily kite enemies as long as you have the space. It really helps to be faster if you are walking down a hallway and there is suddenly 6 guys coming your way.It's basically DOOM as a roguelike.The game is hard even on Medium difficulty. You'll die fast if you fight in the open.Note that there's no progression. If you die, you start all over from the beginning with nothing to unlock.I know it's basically DoomRL in a shiny wrapping, but it's a good wrapping.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game with loads of character build and path choices. This is not a roguelite but the true bonecrushing roguelike experience. no meta-progression ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, pure turn based tactical skill. To everyone that played d**mRL...this is the upgrade! Fancy gfx, more weapons, better (master)perks...i'm in love with this game! MUST BUY!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Jupiter Hell got me breaking down psychological barriers about the essence of gaming itself... We must play by the rules of a game, within the designed framework. If you're hesitant to learn new rules, you're hesitant to play a new game. It limits you to only playing games that are very similar to what you already know. If you wanna play games that are interesting and different, you're gonna have to learn new rules, and experiment with different or unfamiliar gameplay elements, and have the mindfulness to know you're not gonna know how to play the game instantly without investing some more time and attention to the experience.Any time and attention you invest in Jupiter Hell, you get rewarded for. There are multiple plateaus of game-knowledge. Every time you break through it's a satisfying confidence boost. But then almost instantly you get to see the next level of the plateau, and have a clear idea of how to get there. There are lots of options that seem overwhelming at first, but just reading through and playing, it all comes together quickly. If that cycle of mastery of mechanics appeals to you, this is a top, top-tier game for that experience. How I see it, Jupiter Hell is more than a game, it's like a toolbox. You are given full control over so many aspects of how you want to play- you can choose your own class, spec, guns, gear, route, and more- all huge varieties- and can build any type of run you want around the playstyle you're feeling for that session. The possibilities have my head spinning, even after 80+ hours played. I've never played anything like it. What's old is new again. If you're into roguelites and strategy games as a whole, and are looking for something fresh, IMMERSIVE and engaging, this is where you wanna start to get a taste of what a traditional roguelike can offer. You just have to be willing to maybe play by some new rules.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent roguelike! Easy to understand with short, yet informative tutorial. Pretty much what turn-based Doom would've been like.I'm honestly struggling to come up with much to say about Jupiter Hell. It's just a solid game all the way through. I have no complaints about much of anything. And all my questions and issues (had a bit of trouble running it in Vulkan) were answered by the developers on Steam forums. I've spent 16 hours in the past 3 days alone playing Jupiter Hell. If you like roguelikes and blasting monsters with a shotgun, then definitely give this game a try! Jupiter Hell is well worth of your time!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Atmospheric, spooky and tense as hell, this is the game that Doom 3 wanted to be. Every step taken and every door opened could be your last but it never feels unfair, just a chance to try again. Music is appropriate to the setting and will give you the one-more-turns long after you should've gone to bed. The weapons are all satisfying to use and the enemies are interesting and varied. The gibbing effect in particular is glorious.Game is not easy, so if you're new to roguelikes, maybe try DoomRL first as it's free and this game builds on that foundation. It would be nice if you could rename your character ingame but that's a minor gripe.Would rinse and repeat again.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This game, the closest to replicating the fun and excitement to the original rogue games in a long time, just imagine replacing ascii characters with some high resolution isometric models!  The nice graphic lighting in game adds some realism to an Alien-esque sci fi environment.  Would be cool if your avatar could be a female and look like Ripley from the movie Aliens!  I thought with so many ranged weapons this game would be too easy to win, but they made it challenging and fun with a plethora of options given the different character classes, items, and skills.  They put more variety than I expected in the game and I can foresee playing many many replays ahead!  Well done team! I look forward to future updates!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Really solid classic rogue like, what if a miniature ADOM met Doom.Visuals and music is really good, makes you with there was a little bit more variety - the exists assets are very well done.Gameplay is fun, there is learning curve and no a lot of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to deal with (which is a problem in many games like that).
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game. Loads of replay. I've played probably 20 rounds on easy and still haven't officially beat the game. I do have one complaint so far. I've played as technician through all of my runs. On my last run today, I did the best I've done so far in the game. On Dante 2, I full cleared the level and received the pentagram to go to the special dimension. Mind you, I'm loaded down with around 1000 plasma ammo and 3 stims, 3 small med, 1 mil stim and 1 large med. I full clear the special dimension only to find out that it goes to Dante 3 and gives me 6 chests full of random crap that doesn't help me at all. I'd say to the devs, that if you are at the final level and you do something like this and use all of your ammo and health to do it, just give me ammo and health as the reward. I'm assuming there's a special ending for completing this realm otherwise I don't see why anyone would bother doing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Superb game.  Has that retro feel and takes me back to my Alien Breed days but with a fresh take.  The turn based system is so slick that it feels real time, and it is brutal.  Slowly learning the game systems and how each class operates, but so many trait picks and routes to take that each run can be completely different so a lot of replayability.  I highly recommend, and also looks perfect for the Steam Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Loving this game. Normally I would not play games with unforgiving difficulty and perma death, but Jupiter Hell does a good job of ramping things up slowing and starting the game on the easier side. The gradual introduction of enemies and gives you some freedom to see what works and does not work, the perma death keeps you from getting stuck based on earlier mistakes (such as squandering resources early in the game). I was able to beat the game after 30 hours, with my 1st winning play through taking 4 hours. Upping the difficulty adds more enemies with better weapons, and I feel beating the game on easy, felt like it helped a lot for playing medium, and hard.There area a bunch of other games modes to switch things up. At first these are locked, but you can do a play through with only shotguns, do one with only grenade launchers and rocket launchers, as well as a large number of other. These also change the game slightly such as giving you the weapon to start with, and allowing you to convert ammo. There is also an endless more where random levels are generated endlessly, and a area mode where you are in a smaller area and waves of enemies spawn, you get rewards, and move to another area, repeat.Overall the game is pretty tight, allowing a lot of approaches worth trying, and making the focus much more on adapting to the evolving situation. While standing in cover and shooting some lightly armed guards is easy and simple, that changes if some demons hear you and come from the other direction, or maybe the guards have a friend with a grenade launcher who was out of sight. Higher levels have much more going on, with more issues to address.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interesting one. I'm generally a big roguelike fan, and a HUGE XCOM fan. Somehow, though, this game got old fast.There are a LOT of builds that you can try and what seems like infinite different weapons. At 13 hours, I still feel like I haven't scratched the surface of what's possible in the game (and I haven't beaten it, although I started on hard mode.) But despite that, the core gameplay loop and the graphics just seem to create a boring game. Encounter enemies (or what you think are enemies, based on poor lighting conditions and retro graphics), run behind cover, wait for them to step into the open and shoot them.Overall, I think this game is probably good, but just not for me. There may be a lot of choices in terms of itemization and perks, but the combat feels so straightforward that it makes it much less enjoyable. If you know that going in, I say go for it, but if you're looking for a deep combat experience or good visuals, go elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: Jupiter Hell might well be my favourite roguelike, but my recommendation* comes with a caveat.What the game offers is a deeply tactical and strategic experience, impeccably balanced and trusting of the player. You are a lone soldier in the familiar theme of 'all hell (literally) has broken loose, in space', but this time on the moons of Jupiter as opposed to, say, the clouds of Venus.The gameplay appears simple at first glance - it is turn-based, you can move in the four cardinal directions (seems limiting at first, but it works), and shoot at zombies, robots and demons. After killing a few of them, you level up and can select a perk. Level up a  times and you can select a 'Master' perk - and this is where things start to get interesting.Each moon has 5 possible paths through it - straight down the middle, or the option of one of three of four side-branches. Every branch has a special objective to discover, and you're rewarded for accomplishing it. Furthermore, weapons and armour found in a side branch have unique bonuses, which at first appear to be only minor, but in combination with perks and the ability to customise weapons and armour through 'modpacks', can become incredibly powerful. In addition to that, exotic and unique items can impart unusual and powerful abilities, if you're lucky enough to find them.But you are  at the mercy of RNG.Even the most overpowered build with the most astonishing luck, a few wrong moves and you're toast. It may be through attrition (you really failed 3 levels ago but didn't realise it), or a moment of hubris leading to a speedy demise; nearly every win or loss can be attributed to the player, and the decisions they make.You will lose a lot. Almost every run. No, you don't unlock a new weapon or gain some permanent bonus,  the permanent bonus of knowledge. As familiarity with the game increases, you learn to exploit its mechanics, how to leverage the RNG to produce an item you need, what the best way to fight a particular type of enemy is. As long as you don't fall to complacency, a win is possible.* So why the caveat? It's addictive. Not in an exploitative way - quite the opposite, but if you have a lot of stuff to do and are easily swayed into  doing it, Jupiter Hell could be that demon in your ear convincing you that it's .

_childDocuments_.review: Doesn't look like much on the surface, but once you start playing you come to realise this is an extremely well-designed roguelike. It has an absurdly deep strategy pool and steep learning curve for such a seemingly straightforward game, and it has enough game variants and challenge modes to keep things fresh.I should also heap a big helping of praise on the little things, the small design decisions that show the developer really knows their stuff. The tiniest details, things you might not even consciously think of as design choices, are all geared to keep the game flowing and avoid micromanagement.I strongly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: is a roguelike turn-based strategy game with procedurally generated levels and permadeath. The game is still in Early Access so expect some changes depending on when you are reading this review. The game is fully playable as it is right now according to the developers, which is nice.You start by choosing from three different classes, each with its own buffs. So from the beginning you have a slight selection for the type of gameplay that suits you.Like in may tactical turn-based games, you and the enemies will both be able to take cover behind objects. All of the fighting in this game is done from a distance, because you are firing guns at each other. You have to remember to reload your weapons too, and that's something I forgot often.You will have a limited amount to carry, so you have to decide what to loot from the drops of enemies, usually guns and ammo.There are also spawned items on each floor. There are not many, so you have to use them judiciously. These include med kits, armor, grenades, etc.I have no idea how many levels there are, because I keep dying in all of my attempts so far, even on Easy mode. I am still have a great time though.The game does come with a very good interactive tutorial, which is always appreciated.Currently there are two game modes and four difficulty levels. The game modes are Regular and Challenge. I think there are two more that are currently locked, and will likely unlock with updates in Early Access. Of the four difficulties, I played on Easy, and even that has been a challenge for me. The most difficult setting is locked until you meet certain requirements. Difficulty does not bother me because this is a true roguelike. is the spiritual successor of .This is especially notable for a roguelike, it is so very good. Everything is top-down in view. Some levels are a bit dark and can be hard to see at times.The music is not my cup of tea as it is very repetitive. The sound effects are good, though there's a lot of mature language. So be warned, do not play this game on loud from work, especially in the presence of little children.The game can be fully played with a controller or a keyboard.A little more than 10 minutes of sample gameplay can be found here:The price in Early Access at launch is $25 USD, in my opinion that is a bit too steep. Most roguelikes will cost a lot less. Though the game is quite fun and looks fantastic, so if the price is not a hindrance for you, definitely get it. Otherwise waiting for a sale is a reasonable thing to do as well. is a really good game, even though it's in Early Access. The launch price is a bit high, but I would still recommend it at this high price. It is always nice in these turn-based shooters to be able to take cover, and I really enjoy seeing that here. The gameplay combines the turn-based roguelike and the shooter genres. It is just a lot of fun. Like most other roguelikes, you may have to play and replay to get better. For me this is enjoyable, but for others, I know this can get frustrating.Overall it is a very good game with plenty of replayability.Leaving the price out, I would give it a 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: With this game nearing release, I figure it's about time I do a review here.  This has come a long way... for context, I was one of the backers on this one.  Normally I avoid Kickstarters like the plague, but I made a very special exception for this.  I'm glad I did, though it has been a LONG wait for it to reach this point.If you're not aware, this is essentially a spiritual sequel to DoomRL.  Like that game, it is very fast paced, and goes far, far away from many traditional roguelike concepts (thankfully, as I hate most of those).  No endless bump combat, no unnecessarily gigantic blob of skills/spells that you'll always cycle through in exactly the same order, and biggest of all (at least for me) no godawful unidentified item garbage.  It's that last bit that originally attracted me to DoomRL in the first place.  Well, that and it was based on Doom.  Duh.What I'm saying here is, if you've played more "traditional" roguelikes and found them to be overly convoluted, irritating, or just bloody stupid in some ways, this might be the one for you. Though it does have its issues nonetheless, but we'll get to that.Like DoomRL, combat is all about positioning, movement, timing, and cover.  As I said above, there's no brainless bump crap here.  If you're not considering all 4 of those concepts there, you're going to get smeared all over the wall.  It's fun, it's exciting, and it's fast paced, and it's a huge part of what makes this game what it is.And considering this game's lineage, it's all about GUNS.  The unusual emphasis on ranged attacks makes the game feel very darned unique when compared to basically any other roguelike out there, barring DoomRL itself, and it's a very nice breath of fresh air.   There are many, MANY weapons to pick from, and they are all good at different things.What's more, as the early access process has progressed, these weapons have become far more interesting.  If you'd seen the game in one of its earlier versions, you probably would have seen that most guns tended to be almost identical.  But not so now.  You'll find all sorts of screwball traits/abilities that your weapons can have, and this makes finding new ones extra exciting.  You'll love finding those glorious purple chests that signify a new and interesting way to obliterate demons.  You can hold only a couple at a time, so deciding what to carry at any given time is important, particularly as new enemies appear later in the game.  Some guns just arent good against some things.  If you've reached that one branch area full of CRI bots (big mech things), well, you better hope you have something that works darned well against armor, or you're in big trouble.  All of these things go for your armor as well, as that too has all sorts of unique traits.What's more, you're going to find all sorts of other items (grenades for instance), and lots of machines to interact with that can do different things, but are limited in how many things they can do at once.  Do you use that construction machine to build an advanced weapon in a particular class, hoping to get some good traits?  Or do you use it to make armor, or maybe a weapon mod?  Choices like this appear frequently, and with the game's very fast pace, there's never much downtime between interesting or exciting moments.There's lots of enemy types as well, though they can seem a little samey in some cases.  It might be neat to see some that have genuine unique abilities, as right now its mostly about their primary attack method, health, possible armor, and so on.  Then again, maybe that's all it needs, I dunno.  One way or another, you still definitely need to get a handle on what each horrid demon/robot/whatever can do.Lots of variety in the levels, too.  There are many floors, and a boatload of branch areas and special zones (which are optional).  Deciding just where to go whenever a choice is given to you is very, very important.  Like that CRI lab I mentioned earlier;  if you go there, you arent getting back out until you've gone all the way through, and that means LOTS of horrible robot things.  Think carefully about your current build before entering.  Same with any other optional zone.  Levels have interesting design too, making them more fun to explore... something I wish a lot of roguelikes would learn to pull off.  Look, I'm tired of the usual "random ultra thin corridors and equally random blocky rooms".  These levels are generated much better than that, and I love that.Also, the game is a visual treat.  Most of the time, I prefer ASCII for roguelikes.  And the reason is twofold:  First, I just like ASCII, but even moreso, most roguelike tilesets are butt-ugly.  Not so here.  Great visuals and overall aesthetic here, fitting the overall theme wonderfully and adding to the satisfaction of the combat, with things flying all over the place when blasted and stuff like that.Where the variety does falter a bit is that there are very few overall classes to pick from. Only a couple, really.  Each one has a great many traits to choose from when levelling up, but still.... it's definitely a weak point in the game.  And the Marine in particular could do with a change... his active skill, Adrenaline, is easily the most boring (low grade heal, and a short term buff).  The others are definitely more interesting, but... yeah, there's very little choice here.  At least each class has tons of build variety within itself.The other thing I'm not too fond of is the way that it handles ammo.  Perhaps you're having a run where you've got a focus on shotguns, right?  You've built one up with some mods, you've chosen skills that support it, and so on.  Well.... too bad the game doesnt tell you that shotgun ammo almost entirely stops spawning once you get past a certain point.  Why?  I have no bloody idea.  Look, I get that the game doesnt want you to just stick with the same couple of guns the whole way, but switching out a weapon for what is often a much WORSE weapon because "oh that type of ammo isnt on these floors, you WILL run out for good, better not use that weapon class anymore" is not exactly satisfying.  It can make progression feel outright backwards at times.  Surely there's a better way to encourage the player to change things up.  This aspect just feels unnecessarily forced.  It's been the #1 thing I dislike about this game from the very start.  It can also make weapons not feel quite as exciting to get as they COULD be.  Sure, that new gun you just got as a reward for beating that special zone is great and all, but... it sure isnt quite as satisfying when you know that its ammo type will stop appearing 3 floors down the line.But hey, that's just one issue, and maybe it wont irritate you as much as it does me.  And the rest of the gameplay more than makes up for it.  Super fast paced yet very tactical, exciting combat that never feels tedious, lots of interesting and tough choices to be made, huge variety in builds, weapons, areas, everything... also did I mention the frequent level-ups and the awesome "master traits"?  Yeah, that's pretty great too.Also, this is FAR more accessible than most turn-based roguelikes.  It isnt permanently set to "nigh impossible" as its only difficulty level.  Like Doom, there are quite a few to pick from.  And the controls/UI ARENT FREAKING TERRIBLE.  Certain OTHER games could learn from that!  You can even play with a controller (and boy am I glad for that one).  Which works wonderfully.  If you're a fan of Doom, if you like fast-paced and tactical games, and if you want something that actually dares to change up the roguelike formula instead of trying to be the 350969034742397th Nethack clone... yeah, get this one.  It's good.  And as of this review, it's nearly done... just a couple of months from full release.  What better time to give it a go?

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic roguelike. The core game has you picking one of three classes, each with their own skill tree.  You gain perk points for each level up, and can work towards one 'master' perk that defines your playstyle on that run and requires investment in multiple prior skills.  So far I have had successful runs with a dual wielding pistol and SMG build that fires extra bullets for each shot, and also with a shotgun based build that allowed my shots to pierce and work at a far greater range than you would expect.The base game mode is a relatively lengthy campaign that I would estimate lasts around 4 hours on average, although far quicker times are possible.  Each of the four main zones that you pass through consecutively have a number of alternative paths with their own themes, enemies and drops, and terminals dotted throughout the levels give you hints regarding what you are likely to find if you decide to go down one of the alternative paths.  This, once you get familiar with the possible routes, allows you to influence the rng and find the equipment that you actually need.  There is also a system in place where, by using, for example, a pistol extensively during your run, you make it more likely that you will get better pistols going forward.As you play, you unlock medals and ranks, and these unlock further difficulties, challenges and trials.  Challenges restrict your character in some way, for example giving you access to only 4 inventory slots.  Trials alter the game substantially; the Haste trial greatly reduces the number of floors that you need to pass through and alters the drop tables and XP to compensate,  Arena makes you face waves of respawning enemies, etc.  This all means that replayability is very high, and as the core experience is both satisfying and challenging, I can see myself playing the game for a long time to come.Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Frickin' good time. Evokes memories of playing Doom back in the day and all the tension and discoveries in there... Really dig the advancement system and the badges/promotions you can complete over multiple playthroughs.  Soundtrack slaps, more heavy music reminiscent of those days... And maybe most importantly the devs haven't left it so you have a self-destruct key adjacent to your movement that can perma-kill you any time if you misclick.  I will recommend virtually anything that hasn't wasted ten years leaving Windows key enabled when it leads to an instant loss, so bonus. Project Zomboid devs could learn from these guys.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following the plans and development for this game from even before the Kickstarter (and consequently, from before the moment Zenimax/Bethesda were required by law to protect their trademarks), and it has evolved into something so much more than just "Trademark-Friendly D**m The Roguelike" over that time. The story, told through emails left on long-forgotten access terminals strewn across the various satellites of Jupiter, is exactly as invasive as it needs to be: not at all. And that suits Jupiter Hell as a game down to the last, since everybody on this page likely remembers the slow crawls of text that the original D**m series would paste to the screen at the end of each episode. The gameplay is as fast or as slow as you need it to be. You can surge forward recklessly, dashing from cover to cover as you frantically search for an access terminal to lift a Lockdown. You can hunker down and enjoy a nice hot cup of coffee as you plan how to get past a squadron of high-powered security robots with only a crowbar, ten health, and a single red keycard.All in all, this game truly is the successor to "D**m, The Roguelike" that it always set out to be. Now if you don't mind, I've gotta find a way to Europa...

_childDocuments_.review: When I first got this game, I was reluctant.This was awhile ago, when the reviews were kind of mixed as they suggested "it's good, but basically just a graphically improved DRL which is free."I tried DRL, I liked it, but the screenshots here still showed a bit more and figured what the hell, give Chaos Forge some money to help them out, I've already sunk an unhealthy amount of hours into DCSS (another of their free classics).Since then, Jupiter Hell has with each new update become bigger and more amazing. Far more diversified weapons and enemies than D**M ever did, and in a way that feels more balanced too. Honestly one of the best of these kinds of roguelikes I've played, and the only one that scratches a certain kind of itch for a sci-fi shooty roguelike that games like Cogmind left unsatisfied. _childDocuments_.review: ** A letter of love for both DOOM and the true classic Roguelike genre **The game might sound like something unbelievable : taking a universe like DOOM, nervous, aggressive, fast-paced, and applying to it a turn-based gameplay implying strategy to avoid an unforgiving permadeath. These devs did it, and they did it well :Jupiter Hell offers the action and the bloody massacre someone would expect from a game like doom as its gameplay, visuals and also musics are immersive enough to get in action and take quick decisions.At first, you would obviously die, like a lot. Since like any traditional rogue-like, Jupiter Hell is not an easy game. Though unlike most of roguelike, the choice of difficulty can offer you the choice to just have fun running around and shooting as in lowest difficulty, the game would allow you to make mistakes in your decisions and choices.The game also offers three classes which are well balanced with their own resource to manage, activable powers and passive abilities. - Marine, focused on direct attack- Scout, focused on backstab and escape- Technician, focused on bulky stratsAlso, since we're playing a rpg, you'll have a system of leveling to unlock new traits to spice up the gameplay with new passive or activable abilities, combined with an important point of the gameplay : the gear.Maybe it's the only moment of the game in which the pacing might slow down but for the good sake as it would often occur after the gunfight when the area is cleared and all the time required to explore, think and relax is available, to be ready until the next level.And when the classic gameplay might feel too much, you can still enjoy the game with other original way of playing with the challenges or trials the game offers.Cherry on the top : if despite all the points mentionned, you are still not doubtful about the game or its content, you can still embrace the community which is active, fair, welcoming in addition to the dev team whose always listening at their players and modders.AND YES, I said modders : the game also provides a workshop with mods so you could add your own content in the game both in its gameplay and visual.In conclusion, Jupiter Hell is pleasant experience, a game which worth its price and deserves to be known and tried. If you love DOOM and love Classic Rogue-like games, this is for me a must play for the hommage it represents and the content it offers. And if you're a novice in rogue-like, this game is fair enough for a good introduction to the genre.Enjoy !

It's DOOM with critical thinking behind it...oh what am I saying it's DOOMrl and AliensRl's little love child!

Chalk it up to me not remembering the problems or there were some improvements with steam/game software--I'll list the Steam Deck issues below.Upon saving, the game will freeze (either a salt and pepper screen or just freeze what was on screen, audio will still play). Don't fret!  Just hit the "Steam" button and exit game, load back up and continue. I did this 4 times yesterday and it always loaded up where I left off. Not perfect, but not a huge issue.When you complete a world (Callisto, Europa, Io, Dante), the game will go to black screen and act like it is frozen but audio still plays. As soon as I hit the "Steam" button, my character would say something then I would load in on the screen.  Minor issue.An issue that I had previously that I did not test was when the Steam Deck goes to sleep while the game is running or the game is manually closed while the game is running. I am going to assume this is a still a problem, I play plugged in and my settings give me a good 20 minutes so I never organically tested this and was on a rip, so I didn't take a break.  I'll recommend saving and manually exiting the game if you plan on walking away for bit, don't manually put your Deck to sleep while the game is running.I believe there is now a disclaimer on this title for the issues described above, which is good. Still 100% like this game as a title for Deck as the issues are completely avoidable, but they are absolutely devastating if you aren't aware of them and lose your progress because of those issues, so that said, I keep by the motto of save often.-------------------------------------------------------------------------------Original:  Bought for Steam Deck, mostly play on desktop.It plays very nicely on Steam Deck but when saving, the screen goes grey. Sometimes it will become unplayable if the screen gets turned off/back on or goes to sleep.So, if you play on Steam Deck, save and exit often.  You'll have to force quit the game and reload save, but its better than losing progress.  If this issue gets resolved, I'd be ecstatic, because its truly a great Steam Deck title and I'd rather play this in bed vs at my desktop.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: It does what's advertised very well, the cover-based combat actually works, nothing is unbalanced, it flows very quickly, it's hard enough and the gameplay styles are pretty different. Possible cons are that it's attrition-based (you never get free heals after combat), isn't consumable-focused like classic roguelikes But that's mostly preference, and I prefer it this way, and I heard a year of content is on the way. Also doesn't have as many build choices as DCSS or StS, but  more than GKH.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Jupiter Hell is essentially if DOOM was a traditional rogue-like, it's a very approachable modern rogue-like and so far I only have two issues which are noted below.  Aside from these minor issues I'm really enjoying the game and I look forward to beating it eventually.1) PLEASE make it to where the numpad and enter on the numpad can be used to navigate all menus, I remapped the UI controls to be able to use the numpad to navigate menus but I can't rebind it to where I can use the enter key on the numpad so I have to awkwardly move from the numpad to my keyboard enter key when I want to select something.  This should be a very easy fix and I hope it comes soon, being able to use your arrow keys OR numpad should be standard in all rogue-likes.2) The game has really good graphics for a rogue-like considering ASCII was the standard for a long time and I really do appreciate the effort that went into it, but I would appreciate some mode to help make it easier to look at for people with substandard vision, whether that means introducing an ASCII mode or adding some kind of slight highlight to make it quick and easy to spot and differentiate your character and enemies.  While the graphics are nice, sometimes I find it hard to spot my character, especially when playing on a laptop, it's almost unplayable for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of the reviews already hit this on the head.It's a good game.It's an enjoyable game.But is it not a great game.Visually great, writing does the job it set out to do.It is a top down Doom without the complexity or skill cap of Doom.There isn't a lot of variance and a lot of the game relies on RNG.Which means on higher difficulties RNG begins to drain away from player agency.The result is a very shallow strategy game. Is there strategy? Sure.Is it complex or a major part of the game? No.I'd say this is a good get at $10-$15, but beyond that you really have to have a love for the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: For every thing Jupiter Hell does right, it does three things wrong... And yet, you want to play as this egocentric manly man in quest of uncovering the truth behind what happened to his ship, this guy that will not stop spewing obscenities and dropping the F bomb whenever he feels like it lol.This is a tactical roguelike RPG, and if I say Roguelike, you'd think: "I'm gonna die a lot, huh?"... But no, actually the game is only PART-roguelike. Let me explain; when you die it's permanent, however unlike roguelikes you usually play, your progression DOESN'T carry over! This in part (I think?) is balanced out by the fact that the game is very extremely easy, even on Hard mode. You play as a nameless rambo whose ship collided with another, and upon inspecting it, he finds himself fighting hordes of undead, Doom demons, parasite-infested marines and *insert any other sci fi horror creature you can think of*. He climbs up elevators to reach new areas and before doing that, he'd have to fight a boss for each area. The game follows a "crypt of the necrodancer" paradigm, in which every time you move to a direction (or perform any action really), the enemy AI also does the same thing and that's the tactical side of it. Don't worry, however, because the AI controlled unit are such trash that you will breeze through the game like it's nothing. All you have to do is carry around healthkits and prioritize getting Keycards; now these give you an edge on the map because they allows you access to unique upgrades available if you could hack into terminals! Then it's a matter of getting into cover, and waiting for an opportunity to empty up your machine gun unto the oblivious creatures that come through the corridor... It's very fun to see that happen. When you level up, prioritize grabbing upgrades that directly affect your "damage in a row" counter and you're good to go. Although the game is easy, the challenges are NOT! And although doing them over and over again might sound addicting, it's the graphics of the game and the annoying looping soundtrack that actually pose a problem. The graphics are very dated for a modern game, and the main character's movements seem forced and abnormal. The creatures are also badly designed and at some point you won't be able to distinguish between who's the enemy that poisons you and who'd just straight out shoot you... Jupiter Hell is a  experience to only go through once and never again.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game enough, especially to roguelike lovers - after all this time we finally have a breeze of fresh air in a genre. At first it was quite hard for me to get used to it, as I was comparing it to the previous product of ChaosForge - DRL, but now it feels really awesome to me.I deeply appreciate that the game works stable, despite being in EA and using the custom engine. The graphic part is very neat, and the soundtrack is just what would you expect from this sort of game! It also gives you a perfect feeling of simultaneous turns (which is hard to explain actually, you just have to try it).Now about the roguelike part. It's a bit less deep in tactical sense than DRL: you can't open doors manually, firing with shotgun in the darkness almost never works, diagonal movement is absent (which makes dodging more tricky), there are no melee weapons (at least I didn't find any yet), and finally you can't run. Despite this it adds few useful things, like a visualized covers system and various grenades, both can be a game changer in certain situations. Like in DRL there are many possible builds for your character and in-game achievements unlock new game modes.Now on the things I would like to be changed:1. Though adding realism, pain mechanics feels very annoying, especially when you're almost dead. I would prefer to make less damage than not doing it at all because of misses.2. In DRL I had a lack of medboxes only in the endgame, and here I have to hunt for them starting from Valhalla Terminal. Would be very nice if their spawning rate increased, at least on Easy level.3. There's no speech on double shotgun pickup, which feels very unnatural especially as character is quite talkative in all other situations :) Overall - nice work, keep going! Hopefully the game will become even better on full release.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent successor to the awesome DoomRL from back in the day. A very tactical rogue-like where positioning is crucial to making it through each level, particularly on the harder difficulty settings. I've been playing this since it was greenlit for open beta and have seen the game grow and develop to meet its potential as a contender for being the best tactical rogue-like ever.PROS* Addictive and highly replayable* Three distinct classes with many builds available within each classes' skill trees* Lots of fun loot that can be further customised* Multiple game modes with various challenge settings to add to replayability* Fun Doomesque setting with a 90s feel to the music and atmosphereCONS* Slightly janky FPS, at least on my ultra widescreen monitor* Melee builds are difficult to succeed with on higher difficulty settings. Maybe I just need to 'git gud.' :p* Needs more enemy types with distinct strengths and weaknesses. This can be easily remedied with additional content, howeverThis game from an indie developer ticks all the boxes for what makes an engrossing tactical rogue-like for me and thus earns a well-deserved recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a long time since I have regularly played a turn-based Rogue inspired game. I just didn't connect with any and was sticking to real-time Rogue games instead. This game has changed that and has shot up to the top of my play list. I foresee many many hours spent fighting the Forces of Hell on the Jupiter moons.The UI, dialog, music, gear and enemies all combine to set an excellent gaming experience with a point of view. There is a lot of swearing by default but you can turn that off. Also, for Roguelike purists, my understanding is you can go into the config files and remove the progression unlocking everything right away.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy successor to DoomRL- aesthetically, it's Doom 3 to Doom 3 to DoomRL's Doom 2, but in every other sense it's actually a gameplay refinement. There's room for improvement, and it's not what I'd call up to the level that was just YET- but the improvements are tangible and it's easy to see it getting further improved from here!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Another great game for new players of the traditional roguelike genre, which is also very satisfying to veteran players.  Jupiter Hell is a no-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ no-tedium streamlined traditional roguelike (turn-based, grid-based, permadeath, etc.) with 3D graphics, animations and a physics engine, making it truly unique and one of the more stunning titles in the genre to look at.  The game is primarily ranged combat and has a great tactical feel to positioning and movement due to its use of line of sight, terrain, and cover mechanics.  It has a skill tree (I'm a sucker for these) with each skill having a big impact, and a balance of loot and inventory space to make the experience one of the player making fewer but very important decisions, contrasted with other games in the genre that have the player constantly making small decisions with minor impact for cumulative gains.  Overall very satisfied with the game so far and it is well worth a look if you want a truly unique traditional roguelike experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I should start out with a disclaimer, I put many many hours into DoomRL, absolutely loved it, and still play it. I also think the developer is great, and I've loved everything he's put out that I've tried. That said, I just can't recommend this game and I really really hate to say that, especially since the list of things I don't like about Jupiter Hell is so short.This may be the only roguelike I've played that I think handled the transition from ASCII to visual well. The graphics are great and I'm glad to hear that an ASCII mode will be included at some point. I also think the small changes to the story/lore/etc were handled very well. The thing that completely kills it for me though, and I know it's a tiny detail, is the lack of diagonal movement. I wish I could get over it and adjust, it truly bothers me that I can't. There are a few other minor things, like not being able to carry extra equipment or unload guns, but the movement is the only real dealbreaker.I'm not planning on giving up on it, but every time I try to play it I just get so frustrated by that little detail that I have to put it aside for a while and go back to the original.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Unique and refreshing combination of Doom-ish themes and classic strategic roguelike gameplay. At first it can seem like some encounters can practically instakill you if you're not careful, but with a bit of experience you'll get a good sense of when you need to use some consumables or just GTFO of a bad situation. Your class and build can really change how the game "feels." Survivor Marine can dig in and take a lot of hits, the Scout variants can either focus on stealth, sniping, or extreme mobility, and Wizard tech can kick back and let the bots do the work. Really good game.Worth a try for fans of roguelikes, Doom and/or turn based strategy.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up with Doom and Doom 2, and sometimes I still play a modded Doom version In a roguelike way: launch a map generator to create a few random levels: if I die, then I quit and delete the .WAD.Jupiter Hell feels like Doom like no other game, in a roguelike fashion. - It's a roguelike: not a rogueliTe. No metagame bonuses carried over to the next run, every game you start over. It wouldn't feel like Doom if it wasn't this way, where every new game welcomed you with a pistol and the E1M1 map.- The atmosphere is very "Doomlike": nowadays roguelikes tend to have cartoonish or pixel graphics and simple music. That's ok, but as a Doom fan I would reject a tribute-game with such features. Jupiter Hell delivers realistic, dark colours with very nice light effects and shadows like every demon-slaughterer would expect. I don't like the "old LCT monitor" effect, but that can be desabled. And please let me praise the composer that created that masterpiece of a soundtrack. Notes and riffs are meshed together to create tracks that are not merely clones of the Doom ones, but instead they deeply share their soul (more with Doom 2, since it's metal, while Doom 1 had a more unsettling soundtrack). The composer really understood the spirit of the game and delivered accordingly. Download the free DoomMetal tracks, then listen to this game's songs and judge for yourselves.- All the characters of all my runs have been, are, and will be called "Doomguy"Let's move on to other aspects.Jupiter Hell is a turn based roguelike. Time ticks only when you move, but the devs made an incredible job about movement. If moving fast enough the game looks and feels like real time! Never seen such a smooth movement in a roguelike. You can choose your hero from three archetypes: the tank, the rogue, and the tinkerer, everyone with his own skill set, special ability and general gameplay. The levels' layout is procedural and consistent: no strange rooms or useless corridors. It's random but looks like handmade (premade chunks randomly arranged? or maybe "style rules" for the generation algorithm to follow?).Combat is ranged only, although melee will soon be introduced. I bet they'll add the chainsaw, can't wait for that! Overall it is satisfying, and the cover system introduces that little bit of strategy which is required in every roguelike, but not too much... it's an action game we're talking about! I like it. And I do because it's simple. Not too many weapons, not too many items. Every run I want to kill demons in Jupiter Hell, instead of spending dozens of minutes comparing stats and numbers. When I want deeper strategy or variety I play other wonderful games (like Synthetik) that cover those needs.The UI is clear, you know when you're in cover and when enemies are; items drop always in the nearest free floor tile available and are clearly distinguishable. There are a lot of destructible items: crates, barrels (which can explode and deal different kinds of damage, like fire, cold or acid). Enemies are different enough and unlike most other roguelikes (when they simply disappear or turn into a "corpse" sprite) they ragdoll nicely when they die. New mechanics are constantly added like hacking (enemy bots or terminals to open vaults, turn turrets to your side, or discover the entire map of the level): those add depth to the game, yet are not too complex.In conclusion: Jupiter Hell succeds to transfer the feel of action in the inherently static gameplay of a roguelike, with an atmosphere which will please for sure all Doom fans, but is not enchained by that bigger and more famous franchise.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: It started life as an AliensRL / DoomRL amalgamation. It has grown *so much* since then. Today, Jupiter Hell is an action packed, easy-to-play, hard-to-master roguelike with tons of options for replayability. It's games are between 30-60 minutes for a decent player, so it fits a nice timeslot for a "coffee-break" roguelike.Only, compared to DRL, this has TONS more content.Graphics are great, voice acting is hilarious (Thanks Mark Meer!), music is good and gameplay is top notch.I'm not gonna lie though...it's hard as balls. Do I recommend Jupiter Hell? HELL YES.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this at the kickstarter as I was big fan of their previous Ascii rogue like DRL, which provided a tactically interesting fast paced addictive rogue like and I have followed it through it's time in EA.It takes all the things that make rogue-likes good, cuts some of the cruft that can make them feel like work and then wraps it in a setting, sound track and visual design that makes it feel fast paced and tense, or slow paced and tense depending on your playstyle and your current situation.I highly recommend giving this a go
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Basically Doom as a Roguelike.Pros:-Feels like I'm playing turn-based Doom-Difficult and Challenging-Each class have different skill trees to encourage multiple builds and different ways of playing the game-Each level have multiple routes to choose from. You can view the messages in the terminals that give hints as to what rewards / hazards each route possesses so you can manage risk vs rewardCons:-Exalted / Elite mobs are a bit too powerful-Too many times you turn a corner, find yourself staring face to face with a group of exalted mobs, and that's the end of the run if you don't have any proper defensive items-Your character can't outrun melee so if you get swarmed it just becomes a slugfest-Last two areas are deliberately over-turned to deal with powerful builds. Enemies deals an enormous amount of damage in comparison to the previous levels.-Final boss swarms you with an endless number of summoned mobs while also spamming attacks on you.Don't get me wrong, Jupiter Hell is a great game and I honestly had a good time with it. But with runs being 2hr+ long, runs consistently ending due to rounding the corner into a pack of elite mobs and promptly dying along with the over-tuned final areas makes the game just too frustrating to deal with and ultimately feels like I'm wasting my time.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: One of the smoothest turn-based games I have ever played, if you were to watch someone play quickly, you may not even realize it is a turn-based game! Solid mechanics through and through, if you like traditional roguelike games, I can't think of anything to say other than well worth the money, quite obviously a labor of love.
