_childDocuments_.review: D**mRL and AliensRL are some of the top roguelikes, immensely playable and replayable. I’ve been enjoying them for years and backed JH on Kickstarter. JH is a cross-over and a further development of these, with controls simplified but not dumbed down. 3D graphics, music and speech only make the game better.Whole-heartedly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fairly hesitant positive review at the moment. It's strategically somewhat unique for a roguelike with its cover system, movement-dodge mechanic and its heavy focus on gunplay. The game certainly can be interesting when you reach tense moments. So far however, it feels like the vast majority of the time I'm just using rinse-repeat strategies on helpless basic enemies which is far snappier in a game without cover mechanics. I find myself taking damage simply because I don't want to run away to cover and wait for enemies to catch up eight times per floor. This game also definitely lacks the item management and variety of something like Dungeon Crawl or Infra Arcana. You're pretty much just managing your life bar, ammo and a few grenades here and there, while you hope for a good, mostly generic gun that suits the build you've locked yourself into.I intend to update this review after a bit more playtime, but I'm not particularly looking forward to replaying the first 10 or so floors before more difficult enemies start spawning on hard mode.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I just beat this game on MEDIUM after six hours. I had 5% HP left. And my heart was pounding through the entire endgame.Jupiter Hell takes a well-established genre—the roguelike, with its pedigree in console-based games of the 20th century—and spruces it up with graphics, guns, and a gosh-darn brilliant soundtrack. No, this isn't the FTL kind of roguelike; it's right down to the basics of the genre, with turn-based grid combat, permanent death, randomization, and punishing difficulty.Roguelikes of that sort have a reputation for being unforgiving. But Jupiter Hell does a great job of easing you in, with eye-popping three-dimensional graphics and a stripped-down core. This is what some call a "coffeebreak roguelike": short enough to play on a (very long) coffee break, but still meaty enough to sink your teeth into. The interface is at first slightly impenetrable, but you eventually learn to interpret what you need and remember the critical keystrokes—which are more expansive than simpler titles, like Brogue, but not so numerous that you're constantly pulling up a help menu. I was able to master the interface in the few hours my first win required.Jupiter Hell also eschews the melee focus of most roguelikes in favor of ranged combat, with mechanics that are simple to understand yet thought-provoking enough to drive the gameplay. Positioning is everything, as is weapon choice. It's a lot more interesting than the combat in some other roguelikes, which is simple enough that some games even automate it!Inventory space is also limited, so you're forced to choose weapons and other items to maximize your effectiveness. The items can get same-y after a while, but the game tries to mitigate this with occasional rare item drops with randomized traits. There are also multiple viable weapon builds, so you can get replay value out of maining a chaingun one run and a rocket launcher the next.The replay value comes from a large set of achievements and challenges, as well as a difficulty scale. For instance, one challenge mode requires you to use rocket launchers the whole game! And if MEDIUM is too easy, there's always ULTRAVIOLENT. It's more than enough to keep me coming back after my first win.A couple of complaints: The graphics aren't optimized, so I can only get about 10 fps on my integrated Intel chip even on low settings, while I can easily get 60 if I switch to my Nvidia discrete card. Jupiter Hell isn't a twitch shooter and the graphics are all eye candy, so it would be nice if the developers added a low-performance mode. Also, while opaqueness is a part of the genre to an extent, there are some spots where it seems pointless—for instance, why can't you see what kind of ammo a weapon uses until you equip it?Still, an excellent title; even after my first win, I'll be coming back for more. Jupiter Hell was highly anticipated in the roguelike community, and it has surely lived up to expectations.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this game regularly for the past 2 years and it doesn't get old. Essentially this is a sort of remake or spiritual successor to DoomRL with 3d graphics and commander Shepard's voice actor Mark Meer playing a one liner in human form (the amount of references in this game will make any 80s movie fan happy).Like any roguelike, dying and learning what you did wrong for the next run is part of the gameplay. If this is your first foray into the genre, don't get too attached to any of your runs and don't worry too much about "losing". Even a successful run will last about an hour and a half on average, so its a game where you'll keep playing over and over. Gameplay can change quite a bit depending on the class you picked and what build you went for, so replay value is pretty much a given.Overall if you like roguelikes you'll like this. If you like roguelikes and Doom, you'll love this. If you only like Doom, you might like it, so give it a shot.Pretty much the only thing i dislike here is that every armor is just a recolor of the old doomguy belly shirt, even the armors that are said to be a huge suit of combat armor in the description look like this. I'm hoping this changes somewhere down the line.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a couple of hours of content. It is possible to blow through the main game on Easy because the Easy mode does not require any more than the most basic of tactics. After reading the negative reviews, I feel that the posters had a couple of hours of fun, and ran into a brick wall. The basic tactics that got them that far or into a particular situation stopped working, and it caused them to stop playing. Other times they phrase it as "I've seen everything" with less than 5 hours clocked in. It could be they had a really good RNG run and completed a run on Easy pretty quick. This can happen in any roguelike albeit rare.This game is not for everyone. Also, it is labeled as a "traditional" roguelike, and won't have FTL style rewards for making it halfway through. So this could be the cause of some of the negative reviews, and that is understandable. Worth a buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: More then 5 hours in Beta, but Steam does not count them.Excellent TURN BASED Rouge Like. And I am talking here about true Rouge Like. From the same Guy who made DOOM RL before Bethesda tore down the game. Jupiter Hell gives you a highly tactical Rouge Like set in a SciFi setting where you fight Demons and Rouge AI drones in branching Levels. It looks good and feels good. Every action counts in combat. Shoot em, stab em, hack em, depending on your class and skill choices. Grab the epic shooty or better two hand guns? Charge into melee or use cover to you advantage. Misstakes can be deadly.Enjoy features like Trial mode and a profanity setting (Seriously, set it to max and hear Commander Shepard Dub Mark Meer do his best 90s Action Hero impressions). It is really well made, by a small studio that cares. And it shows.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello Im Skill Incarnate and Welcome to My Games Review Series.My reviews cover indie games that i have bought, had gifted to me and have been provided by developers for review.In This Episode we rip and tear on the red planet with Jupiter Hell of the Magister by new developer Chaos Forge.  Jupiter Hell is an Action PRG combining a Sci-Fi horror setting with turn based combat as well as roguelike progression. The player takes the role of a soldier with the task of investigating a colony on the planet Jupiter, which has suddenly ceased communication with earth. The colony is under seige from demonic forces destroying the colonists and threatening to spread to earthIn order to succeed you will need to master the Turn Based Combat system, utilising the environment and weapons to even the odds against superior numbers. This game takes heavy inspiration from the doom games and I highly recommend it for fans of doom and also strategy game enthusiastsPlease note my opinions are my own. _childDocuments_.review: It took a minute to get used to. For the first hour or two, you won't like the controls and think it's missing features (what? no analog stick?), but once you get the hang of things, you realize why they're not there. They went out of their way to ensure that there is nothing tedious at the cost of a few reasonable limitations.I've never played a game quite like it. It's turn based, but once you take action, the turn lasts just a split second. The pace is entirely up to you at every move. You can always stop to think about it, or you can finish a whole encounter in a second. There is NEVER anything time sensitive in either direction. No rush, and no delay.I always _want_ to like turn based combat games, but so often the menus and animation sequences just make it a chore. None of that here.A small thing, but you can save & quit anywhere, as well. I like when a game doesn't try to control my time.I do hope they add more camera control, though. I would love to be able to zoom in and out.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this on kickstarter and after a bit of a play of this early access version I'm already very happy. It's EA so obviously some things are missing (that's what an early access release is for), but the foundation is already solid and as is, it's a great modern roguelike, modern as in the good bits of classic RL design (the tension, buckets of it) mixed with much-needed ease-of-use improvements (slim UI, readability, fast-playing if you want to, no grind, you can play a complete run without sacrificing your night).TL;DR: great shooty bang-bang demon-blasting turn-based fun, pick up and play, tactically deep, and it's probably going to get even better as early access progresses.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I like it. Never played DoomRL, so this is coming from someone with nothing to compare it to. Has an old school feel, like doom and an old ascii roguelike had a child. The level up perks have a decent amount of variety so I feel like I can mess with different builds to an extent every time I die. Looking forward to seeing what improvements come down the pipeline.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: the best introduction to the genre. heavy focus on good positioning and decisionmaking. if you suck at roguelikes, just try this. it will teach you all the basics you need. and it's extremely replayable and balanced, with lots of nuanced mechanics and different playstyles. oldschool fun with modern ui and pacing. it's so much more than turn-based doom
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Jupiter Hell has gradually over the last year become my favourite game. It has been amazing seeing it grow over the early access period, patch by patch, from a clone of its predecessor DoomRL into a separate game of its own. It has incredible depth, with many game modes to choose from, and many styles of play which feel noticeably different. After 280 hours, I still feel I am learning new things which will help me do better on future runs.It is a traditional roguelike in the sense of being a turn based, grid based, pseudo-rpg with procedurally generated levels and permadeath. What it does better than any other traditional roguelike I have played is making highly tactical ranged combat seem smooth.Tactically, it reminds me of XCOM games with cover, accuracy and positioning often being more important than raw damage per turn output. However what sets it apart is the streamlined play allowing it to played at action game pace (if you choose). As someone who would usually play a roguelike with mouse, I was wary of hearing it was pure keyboard, but once I got used to it I think its control system is what make the combat side of things so enjoyable.Thematically, it is hard to miss the influence of Doom: Hunting zombies and demons across the moons of  Jupiter. The soundtrack is brilliant, fitting the feel well and not getting annoying even when playing for long periods of time. The voice acting is pretty memorable also.The item and crafting system and inventory management fall under the "easy to learn, hard to master" category, as does the skill system.My few complaints (lack of modding support, some information that can't be found in game so need to check the wiki for it, some of the newest systems to be added have a bit fiddly interfaces) are all on the Devs to-do list and I can't wait to see what comes next.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very solid. I've always liked both doom and roguelikes and this is a really nice take on the turn based genre, focusing on tactical ranged combat. It is simple and quick to pick up, but really makes you think during later levels how to approach each area of the map to have optimal coverage and escape routes in case things to south.The most fun things about the game are the trait system when you level up, and finding better weapons with randomly generated mods on them. I feel like your run depends heavily on them though, so if don't find anything great the demons will get you.The art direction of the game is great and the sound track is OK.I beat the game on medium on my third run, but there's still 3 difficulty levels to beat, and different challenge/trial modes. I don't know if there's a huge amount of replayability (for me), but at least some. For the price I think it's a good buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly an amazing unique roguelike that is simplified to be welcoming to beginners but has some depth to make it interesting to keep playing.My concern so far from what ive seen is two-fold1) Balance - I've finished a game as Marine - Survivor on normal on my 3rd run but felt that it would have been impossible to win without some sort of self-sustaining ability (Survivor negates death by one shot, and also allows passive regeneration. Functions similiarly to Guts from Monster Hunter series)Ive tried a few other builds so far, namely Scout - Ghost and Marine - Onslaught and i find that while cool, it might not be viable late game. With better understanding of the systems i hope it wont be a big issue.2) Variety - From what i've seen so far: There are a fixed amount of levels per region, with 4 regions in total. Each map has 1-3 special regions.There are also several weapon types with 1-3 specials per type.There are maybe 5-7 distinct enemy types i can remember. So far its still interesting but i suspect it will end up being kind of mundane in the long run. Adding in more content in the future would definitely be great. The only one i probably dont have issue with so far is the builds you can make (Though to a certain extent only Master builds modify your playstyle by a large margin)
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Being someone that played Doom on Sega many many years ago, just seeing people compare Jupiter Hell to it, I had to see what was going on. If Doom was made as a turn-based rogue-like: this... is... it... Jupiter Hell is an absolute blast that feeds my turn based strategy passion while keeping things moving with sudden enemies ripping my soldier apart with chain guns and fireballs. Not to mention all the random references to movies and other games: Warhammer 40K... Evil Dead... Equilibrium... The Easter eggs are aplenty. Grab this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Your point of view is a bit too far from the character who looks tiny on screen. The keyboard and mouse control is horrendous but if you are looking to play games from PC stoneage it's alright i guess plus it's turn based but gets really choatic with big waves coming at you agressively and during these times you really don't want to click on the wrong button using a controller so that might be another reason. Yet I still prefer to play it with a controller which feels bit weird for a PC culture rooted game, why can't we just use our mouse? For that alone I want to thumb down. The achievements list is made for the real completionnist, not for fun, not for me. The music is nice, cheery Doom-like, the gameplay is really neat, melee is brutal, the shotgun wipes floor, the sniper is death touch, so far so good. And there's lots of good quality loots where guns get their own twist and surprises, also last mention for the depth put into characters builds. Jupiter Hell is not an outlier, it's not the best either, but overall it's a good effort, I wished for more cinematics though, I liked the animation during the intro.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't meant to be a harsh review. I just didn't really enjoy the game. It's turn based by virtue of each action (a step, a shot, a reload, etc) is a turn. Example, as you take a step, the enemy takes a step at the same time. This isn't you move, you action, and then finish your turn and it swaps to the enemies. The gameplay, at least in the 40 minutes I played, was moving around darkened spaces, spamming the fire key whenever an enemy came in sight. To be honest, ammunition was so plentiful there wasn't any challenge. It was just boring. I didn't really like the interface, and the 'curved screen' effect on menus is just a bit off putting. I just found it a bit too boring to persist with.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly fun game, so much strategy and replayability. Combining different traits with different inventory-style preferences, stat enhancing armors, techno-chips, and demon bodyparts (so metal) will never get old. Not much in the way of story or conceptual reflection though -- beyond an incessant recognition by the game that life in an isolated military facility is even more hellish than slaughtering demons. Sometimes I wonder about whether these soldier or scientist-turned zombies ought to be afforded some respect after death, like a space-burial, but my shotgun doesn't seem to understand that I don't want to blow them to bits. Great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: It's metal. The systems are complex enough to make each run and build interesting and challenging, while not so deep as to make it difficult to learn. A really nice touch is you can learn how the mechanics work by default when looking at your level perks. They often describe how it works without the perk giving you clues into the deeper mechanics of the game and builds. The game runs beautifully and definitely offers a challenge, though you can quickly learn what works for you. The class options are another level of customization it offers for taking on another run. It's still in early access, but it's got me hooked wanting to explore. Do you enjoy randomized levels, path options? You get to choose your loadouts as you choose and can mod your guns to suit your play. Or try to get personal with melee.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: So.I'm twenty-one hours in, according to steam, and I can feel that I'm just scratching the surface.Frankly I'm only leaving a review in the hopes that it boosts whatever numbers steam uses to recommend games. Because if you know what Rogue, ADOM, AliensRL, ToME and the likes are, you know what this game is and isn't - It's a (worthy, and superior) successor to DOOM RL, it isn't a trad high fantasy roguelike...It's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥' good game is what it is. With a exellent soundtrack - my biggest gripe is that there isn't enough tracks. 21 Hrs is too short to cover the gameplay - I'm a slow learner, so I'm still experimenting with different builds and whatnot, still haven't got a win on my belt... But gods dammed it I'm having fun. This game has a setting to decide how much profanity there'll be in the mc's quips.This game will let you decimate roomfulls of demons with a shotgun.This game will crush you mercilessly because you spammed the "wait" key in the wrong place at the wrong time.And, frankly, this game needs more exposure, reviews, wishlisting and whatever else. So here I am. I'm not trying to get you to buy the game - I believe that if you've heard of it, you know whether you'll like it or not - I'm here to convince you to give it the publicity it needs to succeed. We are a (relatively) small playerbase, with a (relatively) few games to play, and this kind of competent, awesome, clearely loved game needs all the promotion it can get.So please. Leave it a review. Even if it's a negative one. Wishlist it if you're interested. Stream it if you do that kind of thing. Just give this labor of damned love the recognition it deserves - give the devellopers the means to not only bring this project to completion, but also the next.It's a good-looking, addictive, meaty, bloody, metal as all hells roguelike for the ages. And If that tickles your fancy, don't stop at playing it.The game can bring you joy. We can bring it success.Please, please do so.We both know it deserves it.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know what it is about this game that makes me love it so much. I've played other games like this and it just didn't have the same feeling Jupiter Hell does. The music, the environment, enemies, weapons and just about everything else just mixes together so perfectly. Creating different builds with different skills each run is amazingly fun. I don't feel like there is any meta to go with so each run feels so incredibly different and you're actually picking skills based off so many different factors that don't require a giant learning curve.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like proper roguelikes? This one was built from the bone fragments and ashes of an excellent fanmade (free) roguelike that was blasted apart in its prime by copyright lawyers. Get this game because they're excellent devs, and also the game itself is excellent.It's always nice to see a game finally come out of Early Access, and this is one i'll continue to play for a while now! Still modes for me to unlock!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: JH is money well spent. The replayability is excellent. The builds are balanced. There's enough luck to keep you groaning and even when you're kitted out with good drops there are still jams that you really have to plan your way out of. The weapons are fun and interesting and the pop culture references and nods to the video game canon is nice to see (and hear). This is not generally my type of game. I'm glad I took the chance on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I loved D**M, the Rogue-like and played it for hours. Jupiter Hell is a great spiritual sequel, polishing up D**M RL for the modern era while staying true to its heart. It's intuitive, strategic, and well-designed. The classes, skills, and weapons are very different, and many different weapon/skill builds and styles of play are feasible. The generated levels, difficulty options, and run challenges provide a lot of replayability.If you want a good turn-based rogue-like, or a good coffee-break game, check this out.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: My biggest problems with most roguelikes is that ranged weapons often feel like they lack impact. This game takes care of that by letting me gib a room of enemies with a single shotgun blast. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I'm having the kind of fun in the first two hours that I wouldn't normally feel until I've become super powerful in most other titles. Another element that really sets the game apart from other roguelikes is the cover system. Very simple stuff you've probably seen dozens of times in games like xcom, but for a genre that traditionally REQUIRES you to hold a choke point at the end of a hallway in order to kill dozens of enemies single file, it is a remarkable breath of fresh air!I anticipate many more hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Jupiter Hell hits all the beats that I loved about DRL. Everything is obviously prettier - DRL runs infinitely better on my tablet, sadly - but the style lends well to the gameplay. Nothing feels too weird despite the turn-based timing, and everything feels mechanically tighter... and so much tougher than I remember DRL being. If you haven't played DRL, this is a really pretty turn-based roguelike, truer to form than most, albeit with a focus on hitscan weapons. It does it well, though!I mentioned my tablet, which can only run this game at 1024x768x30 if I'm lucky. I'd love if this had a 2D tiled mode one day 🥺
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: tried again to like it. got closer, but too bad it crashes constantly on steam deck. so sad :(I really, really wanted to like this game. But it feels like it was built by the devs, for the devs. The tooltips are indispensable, but trying to learn the mechanics and get a bearing of how the game works is tediously stupid. I have absolutely no desire to sink hours into a game to figure out whether or not it'll actually be fun once you "get it". Especially when so many games make that discovery actually fun.And in the mean time the cheesy sound bites are just annoying. No thanks.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Hellishly good fun, also very refreshing, smart gameplay... the each action advances the clock system is really cool and lets you play as fast or as slow as you like without losing any sense of tension or bogging things down.  Of course if you are like me you get overconfident and start playing like its real time and then get yourself killed but it's pretty much always your own fault.  Very fair with scaling difficulty to make it as hard as you like.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those on the fence games. It is not bad, but I can't really recommend it. I have put 22 hours into the game, and will likely revisit it again sometime. It is deeper than some reviewers have complained about, but the branching system doesn't really make that much difference to the repetitive feel. It is very dark. The player and enemy models are small. The character classes do operate a bit differently and the skill system can tailor them a bit to taste, but they look and feel the same. It would be nice to have different models, voices, and flavor dialog for each. A female model and voice would be great as well.Gameplay-wise each level is most difficult at the start where there is a significant danger of getting mobbed. Once you overcome the early danger, it is generally a good bet you'll make it to the next level. This is a problem in other games as well, but it is worth mentioning.The number of ammo and weapon types is a bit overly complicated. I also don't like the use of 20th Century standards. It is hard to imagine a future colony system around Jupiter using 44-caliber or 12-gauge weaponry. No bugs or crashes encountered. Performance was not issue on a Mac Studio.It is a small thing to mention, but it felt great that the default keys are convenient for a touch-typist. I'm used to having to switch the usual WASD layout to ESDF so that my left hand sits properly over the home row. 'F' for fire, 'g' for get, 'r' for reload, etc. The default for movement is to have your right hand on the arrow keys (the game is not mouse-driven).Overall, it is no FTL or Dungeon of the Endless, which I continue to play (currently over 400 hours each). I'll say 6/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; What if a Roguelike removed all the tedious bits, and left behind only the intense bits?A successful run is relatively short, but more intense.  It's basically a heavily distilled essence of rogue.  There is no grind, no backtracking, no excessive detours - just alternate paths forward.In exchange for being shorter, each engagement is much more involved.  ALL enemies benefit from cover, some of which is destructible.  Half of the enemies will take advantage of cover to attack at range, while the other half rush you.  Between that and the limited hearing of non-robot enemies, even the simplist fights are more complicated than "whack enemy with a stick."  It feels very similar to XCOM in terms of positioning and scouting.Resource management is very involved.  You have precious few inventory slots to share with ammo, grenades, upgrade ingredients, healing kits, and special items.  Depending on RNG, you could hit a famine of any or all of those resources - so you have to choose what to stock up on.  You can only carry 3 weapons by default, but there are ~4 damage types (regular, anti-unarmored, anti-armor, anti-armor & robot), ~4 effective weapon ranges (melee, close range, mid range, long range), ~4 ways of dealing damage (high damage single target, low damage * multiple shots, multitarget, explosion radius), ~6 ammo types... you get the idea.  You will always have at least one weakness.Compare this to Nethack.  Excessive backtracking through dozens of levels, 90% of fights are zero risk, passive healing makes chip damage irrelevant, positioning is as simple as standing in a hall or doorway, and enough inventory space for 50+ items BEFORE getting a bag(s) of holding.  Other roguelikes vary in the specifics, but they all have a similar formula of 85% tedium, 10% risk of death by attrition, 5% risk of instant death.  This game is 90% death by attrition, 10% chance of a instant death.---If you ever feel like you've "mastered" the game (50 hours on medium difficulty got me my first win), there are a few dozen unique trials and challenge modes (including "you can't reload weapons, you have to pick up a new one" and "pacifist, lose max hp each time you kill an enemy"), all of which can be played on four difficulties (with the hardest being "deliberately unfair").  After that, there are personal challenges: 3 very different classes, with 5 subclasses each.  A handy and exhaustive list of medals is there to remind you of what you haven't mastered.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: A *real* classic rogue-like, the kind of games I like and Steam needs more!If you enjoy games like Tales of Maj'Eyal, Dungeon Of Dreadmore, Cogmind, Cave Of Quod but want or don't mind mind simpler mechanics/systems (usually called "coffee-break roguelikes"), this is going to be perfect for you!ChaosForge (and it's main dev) have been creating roguelikes for almost 2 decades. they know their ♥♥♥♥.It's already a good game, and I'm excited to see future content and features! These devs deserves support.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Went into this expecting it to play like DRL and was ready to drop it after two runs, but I'm glad I gave it another shot.Jupiter Hell requires a more deliberate playstile where you carefully have to plan your approach vector and your eventual escape route should things get a bit hairy as it very much relies on a cover system. You should generally try to never be caught in the open as opposed to DRL where you can just weave through enemy shots.The game offers a very good amount of build variety, multiple difficulties and several challenge modes. I feel like it's still a little bit lacking in replayability as of now, I'd really like to see more memorable side areas and a couple of cool boss encounters - the final boss also was a bit of a letdown and seems more like a placeholder.I think the price tag might be a little bit steep for what Jupiter Hell brings to the table right now, but I'm nonetheless looking forward to get back into it when the next content update releases. The core gameplay is rock-solid.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: It's the best game I've played for a few years. The AI is much deeper and complicated than appears at first glance. I used to complain that I wasn't doing well, but I have content for the next 400 hours of trying to overcome at the various difficulty levels. Also the developer puts out free updates continuously? I played for free for 100 hours,  I saw the new update and thought, "It's not like I don't like the game..." This game is this year's version of This Land Is My Land or Battle Brothers, at least for me. Highly, highly recommend, but I would warn that it will destroy your social life. Call it creative destruction.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: A weird, wonderful gem. I wasn't sure how much I liked the keyboard (or gamepad) controls and old-school CRT effects.. But, the tight tactical gameplay quickly won me over.In short, it's a bold, turn-based tactics game done really really well. Great music, great theme, great tutorial, and highly satisfying character progression. Every upgrade feels punchy and the gameplay is just buttery smooth - over just the first hour or two you'll go from bumbling around each room and item drop, taking  10-15 minutes to clear a floor, to tearing through an entire floor in 3 minutes.There are only a few classes that each sound a bit unimpressive from the selection screen.. But they have their own deceptively large, unique skill trees that will have you coming back for more.Tips:Open up the settings while you're playing through the tutorial and tweak them to your liking. I zoomed my camera in, enlarged the mini-map, and removed the CRT effects.. You'll almost certainly want to lower the camera distance some. Made a world of difference.You can also remove or reduce foul language and turn off being shouted at for being idle :)If you're on the fence, you can easily complete the tutorial and a run or two to decide if you like it within the 2 hour refund period.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Really good roguelike. Lots of build varieties and challenging gameplay. My only caveat is that there is a significant jump in difficulty from the main game to the final boss. I can get to the final boss pretty easily with most build combinations but usually die before I can kill it. The difficulty should be consistent across the game for each of the difficulty levels IMO. I would recommend a Scout Sniper as a good first build that will get you through the game and give you a fighting chance with the final boss.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: As of  August 9th the developers are still silent about how they acted towards negative reviews. For now I would wait until Jupiter Hell launches before giving them any money due to how badly they took negative criticism. Chances are that not a lot of people are going to look at this and give much of a damn, but if anyone needs proof of how they behaved, other reviewers and I documented the majority of what they had said before they edited/deleted comments.I'll update this review near the end of its early access or when it launches, going more indepth with other aspects my review didn't mention and updating others with how they changed at the end of EA.The camera perspective is terrible, since it's too zoomed out to tell similar enemies apart (is he carrying a shotgun or an autorifle? That not-imp looks a lot like that other not-imp..oh it moved twice in one turn and is murdering me in melee and  throwing fireballs) and zooming in means you can't see the geography up ahead and plan your movement. The worst part is the default zoom level doesn't zoom out far enough to see your max view distance, though at that point good luck trying to tell what is actively trying to murder you. This wouldn't be so bad, but the command for zooming in/out isn't listed in the controls section and also requires you to use the mouse as well, which can add up in time spent.To me this is a fundamental flaw that should have been squashed early on since being able to identify enemies accurately is a big part of roguelikes in general. Focusing on making enemies and their armament distinguishable from a distance (via enlarging the models or otherwise) should be prioritised, though I'm not sure how to go about it without redoing large chunks of the ingame models which may not be an option at this point for the developers.The UI looks out of place, considering the graphical style of the game, using ascii text. This isn't a huge issue in of itself, mind you. The mapping system however is terrible, since it's usually obscured by lit objects forcing you to squint to make it out, not to mention its placement means it's hard to glance at it in the corner of your eye to quickly check where you have/haven't been.Finally, one pet peeve I have currently is that it's very hard to bait the a.i into following you anywhere it seems. This makes it hard to utilise the cover system not to mention giving enemies free shots at you if you want to try to clear them out. Oh, also add onto it that you can't see the the cone of fire for shotguns.I enjoyed the hell out of D**MRL and was hoping for something that'd be it and more with this, but so far it's just an exercise in frustration and absent quality of life actions (unloading weapons you find on the ground for their ammunition as one example). It's still in early access (or just launched as early access rather), so things are subject to change and I can only hope a lot of these issues are addressed over time. For now though, I would say wait and see before purchasing.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Great rogue-like with a ton of depth. There are tons of weapons, armor, and perks to insure that no two runs will ever play quite the same. The game is initially quite accessible, with an in-game tutorial, but you'll need to consult the wiki if you want to get OP and maximize the damage you do on each run into hell.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not an expert in roguelikes, but it's a genre i'm well accustomed to and familiar with the more accessible choices, such as ToME or DCSS or ADOM .... Jupiter Hell came out as a very fun and fresh experience without straying too far from the classic formula, getting into it was easy and quick enough thanks to a functional and helpful tutorial that helps you with the basics but leaves out some few key details that certainly could've helped me more if i knew early, but, nothing too crazy that warrants yelling at the devs. There's not much for me to warn about for potential grievances, there's good enemy variety and an insane amount of juicy items and variants that spice up every run, 3 backgrounds and a lot of perks to choose from, there's a lot of options in terms of character progression. Jupiter Hell for me is an easy recommendation, easy to get into, fun and satisfying to play from start to finish, lots of variety in terms of game modes and challenges and a good team behind it that support the title with juicy updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Although I haven't been able to beat any of my runs, I am hooked. This is a great rouguelike. Can be tense even if it's turnbased action. Heavy metal soundtrack is great, graphics are suitable for this kind of game. Any PC-potato will probably manage it. I encoutered no technical problems or bugs. Randomness of the loot can kick you in the ass but it goes well the theme. A well deserved thumbs up from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Hell Yeah!I'm an old-time hand who grew up with Doom and Doom II as my childhood fond memories. This is TOTALLY up my alley, and heartily recommend it to any fans of the genre.  A friend roped me into the developer's early Roguelike version of Doom, now known as DRL and which I still play during the off hours at work. I'm very much enjoying the current iteration of Jupiter Hell and looking forward to everything else coming down the pipe!What, you're still standing there? Shut up and give them your money!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Bought it for Mark Meer's Voiceover.   Stayed for the fun game.   First off, the Developers are supporting the hell out of this title, and it just keeps getting better with every patch.   I enjoyed it immensely at the start, and am still enjoying it, especially with the new flavors for the various areas that they're working on.    This is Gauntlet meets Doom.   All that's missing is Mark muttering... "I need heals... badly..."  as such, it's a blending of two incredible old school flavors that go together in an olive oil and salsa kinda way.  Surprisingly tastier than you'd think.   This is a game for when you've got an hour or so and just want to blast away at the bad guys without thinking too hard about it.   Yeah there's a lot of fun strategems to explore, and they keep getting more interesting with every patch, but the catharsis of blowing away demons to obvious old-school Metallica (Before they cut their hair and sold out)  is a retro moment that those that missed the 90's are sure to enjoy. Plus you know...  Mark Meer.  If you like him here, I highly recommend you also Check out "Tiny Plastic Men", an Awesome Canadian TV show that was one of the first victims of cancel culture.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: A quick impressions review at less than 2hrs play.... a lot simpler and less interesting than I hoped. No traditional roguelike depth or emergent gameplay. No real chaos spirals or creative loadouts. Perk progression is slow and unexciting, lacking imagination.Just monsters running down corridors toward me. Very little tactical involvement. Comments re: 'Doom as Chess' feel misplaced when you're often simply sitting in cover trying to maximise DPS. AI is simple, aim system is simple, damage variation is simple. Shooting explosive barrels is the only tactical wrinkle in the first few hours, it seems.Visuals are adequate but unexciting. Kills aren't visually satisfying like those of - for example - XCOM2. Environments are dull. Writing sometimes aims for humour but usually misses. It usually presents the most generic scifi blather, at a bare minimum to contextualise tips for hidden loot.Perhaps far further into the game the depth expands, but I'm not sure I want to lose my refund opportunity on that gamble.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: It's very whatever. "Whatever" is the most i can say about this title. It's fine. The promise of rogue-like elements did not occur in my few sessions i went through. No unlocks, no changes, no customizations. I have to assume this may change later on, but I didn't encounter anything that would fall under the "rogue-like/lite" style of game.It is a poorly designed game. The UI is the least friendly UI that I have seen in quite a long time, and required multiple trips to google to figure some things out. The gameplay itself is as follows - take a generic twin-stick isometric shooter, then make it turn-based. Thats it.The rogue-like genre is packed with amazing titles, and this doesn't hold a candle to most of them.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Old skool gamer here. Game totally nailed it the spirit of the 90s Doom generation. the soundtrack is sick! Its all about plain "kick ass and chew bubblegum" fun, though i wish the protagonist referenced that in the game! sorry, but I laughed at the clean version language as an option.It actually push your skills to play, and the reason its roguelike because at each restart you'll find sometimes your quadshotgun you found never turns up and u have to change playstyle throughout. enemies might be puny this time, next restart suddenly they swamp you with grenade launcher. yeah sure you can argue to play safe, probably  its time to stop being a wuss and go in guns blazing! its really fun. its fun to get your ass handed to you by denizens of powerful enemies, then next round you obliterate them with you supershotgun! The levels arent repetitive, felt it probably because you die and restart alot at first, each place has a different feel, some small corridors, plenty of shotgun opportunity, suddenly next stage long corridors and very little cover provided. the random gun drop really get you to change gun tactics, one playthrough you plough through enemies, next they swamp you with you having only your tiny 9mm, next no ammo drop from enemies, next swamped by OP exhalted fiends, next swamped by bots, next hack the bots to attack everything on sight  - wait for the explosions to die down then BANG you've leveled up from standing still. yippekaiyay mofos! Theres a lot of variety in gameplay!I havent finished the game and already I hope to see more content, a sequel and more of them brutal heavy metal tracks! Well done ChaosForge!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: Great game, absolutely worth it.Pros:Simple control scheme. Easy to get muscle memory, gets faster the faster you play. Great feeling/powerful tech trees. Thought I had maybe 3 hours in it when I realized it was actually 12.Highly reccommend, runs well on Ubuntu 20.04 + Proton, therefore will make a GREAT steamdeck gameCons: Many things endorse melee, but the whole structure seems to punish melee strongly compared to cover-fire....just like real life I suppose.

_childDocuments_.review: The control scheme is from the early 1980's, pre-mouse era, as is the font.I'm not digging the 1990s CRT monitor look ( the developer copied a flickering, non-interlaced monitor, complete with curved distortion - who even bought more than one of those? Usually the first non-interlaced purchase was an accident, due to a smooth-talking salesman, and complete ignorance about computers ). The flickering was hard on the eyes and gave some people headaches. The developer is clearly trying to blind people. I turned it off in the display settings.The aesthetics were all over the place. The game combined a great opening, anime-esque cut scene intro, with a 1980's keyboard-only menu and tutorial ( I had flashbacks to using the "VI editor" on a Unix mainframe - fun times ) with hard rock music, that I instantly wanted to turn off. The font was ugly as ♥♥♥♥.You have to have some serious nostalgia goggles to think that this is a "good look".Me: How high were you, when you made this game?Developer: Yes. Me: How much of the purple juice did you drink as a kid? It was methylated spirits... methanol. You can go blind from drinking that stuff...Developer: Um...I wanted to uninstall and refund the game after seeing the 20 minute tutorial. The trailer was fake - this is a turn-based game. It's hard to see the game's appeal. This game might have been amazing in 1983.You can enable mouse control in the settings.

_childDocuments_.review: REVISION: full release definitely follows through on the promise of the earlier work. I started following Jupiter Hell as a fan of DoomRL... it is truly a worthy successor, a “pure” roguelike in an era where the term has been used and abused to the point of meaninglessness...But for people unfamiliar with classic roguelikes, it is definitely closer to "chess with shotguns." You can move as fast or as slow as you like-- and speedrunners can go VERY fast-- but the world and the monsters in it react only when you yourself move, sort of a more discrete, turn-based version of Superhot.There's a ton of replayability already, and the dev has proven he is dedicated to constantly updating and improving the game... DoomRL still gets updates more than a decade after release!BONUS: extremely profane vocal quips from Mark "Commander Shepard" Meer

_childDocuments_.review: I just beat the game on easy and I haven't had this much fun with a roguelike in a long time. I must admit the graphics aren't really my thing, and the Duke Nukem style one liners don't really do it for me either. Also the music really gets on my nerves, I muted it before I even finished the tutorial. Despite all that, I am having a blast with Jupiter Hell. It really strikes the perfect balance between a fast paced, action packed role-playing experience, and a true to the core traditional roguelike. This is a roguelike with meaningful character progression, fantastic item variety, exciting loot, excellent sound design, and most importantly, very slick controls. I played keyboard-only and it was super easy and intuitive. I don't really have much else to say, apart from that I think this is an incredibly well crafted game and an absolute must-have for every fan of the genre. Also, if you're intrigued by the idea of playing a traditional roguelike, but intimidated by the extreme complexity of games like Nethack, this might very well be your perfect introduction to the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: It's certainly fun and very faithful to DoomRL but there is very little variety throughout the first levels where you will be spending a lot of time as you try to get good. Something else to do besides shoot demons and open boxes would be nice. The moments I find one of those "unlock vault" terminals are a great reprieve for example.I am quite unhappy with the soundtrack - while the music itself is perfectly serviceable metal, it isn't used well - it's basically being blasted constantly which puts you into a mood where you want to go through the level as fast as possible, it's basically the main cause of my deaths. There should also be some more atmospheric tracks playing when there are no or few enemies around, so players feel comfortable taking their time - leave the high intensity stuff for high intensity encounters.The core gameplay is very good though, would recommend. Not sure if the price is worth it at this stage of development but I'm considering my purchase as payment for the free fun I have had with DoomRL in the past so it's fine for me

_childDocuments_.review: Jupiter Hell is a fantastic game and I really enjoy it. It's a turn-based, roguelike homage to Doom-style one-marine-against-the-hordes-of-hell, sci-fi horror. The game is lovingly-crafted, atmospheric and marvellously challenging, packed full of satisfyingly chewy heavy metal and carnage, well done sounds, visuals & many little details done right. I particularly like the keyboard control scheme and responsiveness and speed of the game experience - you can go as fast or as slow as you like.This kind of game isn't for everyone, but if - like me - you enjoy conquering punishingly difficult skill ramps, this game is one of the most satisfying I've played.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of roguelites for their sense of accomplishment and replayability, I have to say that as a genuine RogueLIKE this game was a complete blast of fresh air and an absolute joy to play. The soundtrack immediately pulled me in in tandem with the absolutely hilariously highly abrasive voice lines and pop-culture references. The gameplay is both fast passed and intense while still forcing you to stop, hold your breath while you analyse the situation and try to strategize as best as you can to survive a genuine challenge. Jupiter Hell is a game I usually use to separate myself for a run or two when I need a break from tasks, but also a game I can sit down for four to six hours doing multiple runs.Seven thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: Your patrol ship was suddenly shot down by your homebase’s own defense grid and you barely made it out of the battered wreck alive, only to find the hangar even worse for wear. Corpses pile up across the floor, demonic markings painted in blood cover the walls and your previous comrades snarl like wild beasts as they turn their guns at you. Does this setup sound familiar? The action may take place on Jupiter, but simply watching through the game’s introductory cutscene removes shadow of a doubt as to where it takes its inspiration from. It is only natural given that Jupiter Hell is a spiritual successor to DRL – Doom, the Rougelike.While many among you will immediately have an idea what to except in terms of setting, enemy design and interior decor – the gameplay is an entirely different beast. Jupiter Hell is first and foremost turn-based title presented from a top-down perspective. Every single action performed by the player takes a turn: moving a tile, shooting, reloading, using a medkit. Some among you may now argue that turn-based combat is an antithesis to fast-paced gunning mayhem of Doom, to this I retort – not in the slightest, outlandish as it may seem.The kicker is that all of the aforementioned actions may be performed in a blink of an eye, allowing the player to blast through a level in 2 minutes while also shredding all of the enemies on your way to the exit. A 20 minutes-long session can easily translate to several thousand turns and motion is fluid enough to make you forget that you have all the time in the world before acting.  Frankly, the game almost taunts the player to recklessly rip and tear until suddenly the protagonist is done, much to your disbelief, as the endgame screen delivers impassionate breakdown of damage from 6 hits at once you ate while rushing into the open.Satisfying as the fast-paced slaughter may be, it will come as no surprise that such angle of approach won’t get you far in Jupiter Hell. This title offers unique gameplay which takes patience and perseverance to even get started, let alone explore the depths which the game is able to offer to its veterans. For now, take my word for it – you really don’t want to skip the tutorial.Staying true to the rougelike genre, Jupiter Hell relies on repetition to extend its playtime. Why some rougelikes encourage the player to repeatedly beat the game in an increasingly extravagant manner, the title of the day induces repetition by beating... the player, to death and repeatedly at that. Bluntly put, Jupiter Hell is punishingly difficult – to the point where the first boss will likely seem ridiculously overpowered as you make your acquaintance. Those among you familiar with this type of games will also anticipate that the same boss barely makes for a speedbump once you learn the ropes.That’s where the perseverance comes into play. To make proper progress through the game, the player must engage in an extended period of “trial and error”, during which one will gradually familiarize themselves with myriad of different mechanics Jupiter Hell has to offer. There’s a lot to unpack too, weapons come in different calibres, optimal firing ranges and with an extensive modifiers system. Especially the latter deserves a separate mention. Upgrades may include anything ranging from mundane faster reload or increased range, through additional elemental damage, and rounding up with unique modifires operating vastly different from their ordinary counterparts (say, a self-charging rocket launcher shooting fireballs).No less complex are the levels themselves. At face value, each one is a small dungeon complete with loot, batch of enemies and usually some optional additional risk, which may yield greater rewards in return. It will come as no surprise that hellspawn-marked corridors of Jupiter base are best enjoyed in a leisurely stroll once all enemies nap peacefully in the dirt. However, the only condition mandatory for further progress is finding the exit elevator, giving the player a possibility of sneaking out of tough level mostly undetected. It doesn’t take long to find out that each biome has limited building blocks available. To remedy this, every chapter of the game includes randomized side branch of levels. They all come with a unique twist and offer best rewards if the player handles the extra challenge. You can probably see the pattern emerging by now, namely Jupiter Hell is a chain of risk vs reward calculations, where player needs to continuously brave ever greater dangers to keep racking up even better rewards. Overestimate your prowess though and the chain breaks.I hope the multi-layered wrapping of the game doesn’t come off as overwhelming as we are not quite done yet. The game offers 3 classes, each with unique active skill and dedicated set of abilities. Every class can offer a refreshing new twist on the gameplay and may open your eyes to an approach you didn’t previously take into account. However, not all abilities are equally powerful and in title like this one, consistency is the key. Take my word for it, in a game primarily about slaying demons, you might want to stick with combat-oriented Marine until you beat the game at least once.Let’s assume you’ve done just that – picked your best guns, found a favourite build and discovered branch levels which yield rewards fitting your playstyle. At long last, the game-over screen sums up performance not of a freshly baked corpse, but that of a victor. You might take notice that victory screen is followed by list of completed challenges and how you barely seen the tip of that particular iceberg. Once you have mastered the game enough to be able to beat it, there is a room for further ascendance which can easily fill hundreds of hours with whacky achievement runs, higher difficulty settings or challenge modes. Sky is the limit.More than deserving of separate mention is the overall 90’s touch to Jupiter’s aesthetic. Visuals are slightly curved at the edge of the screen as to imitate CRT monitor (or “brick” as some may call it) and the protagonist fills the time with cheesy quips often referencing action films (profanity filter is an option, however to my ears it would be a disservice). To yours truly, this is just the right corny touch which evokes adventurous spirit of both 90’s cinematography and games.Jupiter Hell is a tremendous game, nonetheless no matter how enthusiastically I would spin it – this title is definitely not for everyone, far from it. The steep learning curve will turn away all but the most patient players and not even the rougelike genre veterans are guaranteed to find purchase during the climb. Despite this, resilient enough to make it to the top will find an entire mountain range, offering countless hours of top quality gameplay. It takes time and intimate knowledge to truly appreciate it.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, I've reviewed this game before. It's good. But I really need to add that I've been consistently impressed by the updates this game has received. At launch? Good game. Since it's been updated? Awesome game. At the core it's still the same turn based shooter roguelike, but the additions it's received have added a lot of depth to your choices. Still playing the game, still loving the game.Original review below:Other reviews will cover the amazing voice acting and audios, and the visuals. The video side of things is well done, but I'm not sure the console overlay will be for everyone. I grew up with this stuff, so it's great for me.The selling point for me for this game is twofold:1) each run is short. Either because you freak out and make a bunch of silly mistakes because you forget the game is turn based, or because you get a good run and rip and tear your way to victory.2) the game is turn based, but doesn't feel like it. So when your child wakes up because she hears Mark Meer cursing over your speakers and have to settle her, you can just walk away from the game. You don't die, you don't time out. The worst that happens is Mark curses at your some more for wasting his time.I have a plethora of items in my steam library, and not too much time to play. This is one I'm glad I bought, and that I keep coming back to.

_childDocuments_.review: holy shotshells what an amazing fragging ride this turned out to be.checked out 'd***rl', found it surprisingly engaging. decided to risk sale price on jupiter hell. i have an astonishing lack of regret, 8.2 hours in. even if i never saw anything else new (which is unlikely because i've only seen a subsets of paths so far, and i have yet to get past the first floor of the third episode because i actually suck), i will consider this money well spent.it's unexpectedly pretty, with the detail of the models, the fluidity of the animations, and how the blending makes everything look like it's an action game. it's frequently exceedingly cinematic, usually right as i die because i was moving too fast.looking over the history of the patches, it also looks like the studio is improving the game at a remarkable pace for the size of the team.fantastic stuff. i look forward to experiencing more of it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my new addiction. Very similar to the dev's previous work, DRL (free to download), but still growing with content additions. Turn-based and keyboard only, but with 3D graphics and an engine that can play very fast - the mouse would slow things down. There are a few minor UI issues that can cause confusion and annoyance, but all together I'm adding to my GOAT list.Jupiter Hell is a true Roguelike with no "real" metaprogression; you do unlock new modes as you play the game, but in theory you have access to everything in the main game mode from the very beginning.  Actually encountering everything the game has to offer - let alone surviving it - requires many, many attempts, though... so not having metaprogression isn't really a downside.If you're interested in Jupiter Hell, I recommend trying DRL first.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm still bad at it, managed to reach Io a few times and get destroyed, got to the Beyond once (on Medium).That said, I really like this roguelike, snappy, action-packed but tactical nonetheless, the developer said more than once that he hates adding stuff that bogs down the gameplay with repetitive, grindy actions, the main one being unloading ammo from weapons on the ground for example.In a sense, when you look at other classic roguelikes, it's a bit of a streamlined experience, but there's no shortage of impactful decisions you make every game you start, ranging from what path you take, how you engage enemies, what to fill your inventory with, in other words, it doesn't detract from the experience at all, but enhances it. Also it looks gorgeous for what it is, get that ASCII out of my face.In short, it's tactical, but also fun, fast and satisfying, with an awesome soundtrack to boot.This is clearly a passion project and as such I'm happy to support it, it's a great game even though it's tough, try it out.EDIT: Just won my first game on Medium!

_childDocuments_.review: Original review 2021-10-21: The game is fun. The spooky, isolated atmosphere, and fun gunplay, and great audio is really cool.That said, it does feel "not quite done yet" : 1.Some of the levels are cool and fun, but many have a very similar "square with rooms" feel with very similar colors. More variety would be good - and devs are working on this.2. The classes feel very similar at the start of the game and don't start to feel really different until you get the Master Traits at around level 10. The master traits might be called "active skills" in other games. Generally for much of your first dozens of runs you will be doing "wait at corner, aim, shoot" until you get a Master Trait that you can use for fun.3. For some reason it's prohibitively difficult to play a melee character from the start. I think the idea is this is because the game is gun themed? Which is fine, but just feels a little odd that you get good at a skill you are not practicing and can only start it at level 10.Once you get into the swing of things, though, the game is indeed fun. The devs seem like good guys and are working hard to add content to the game.Edit, 2023-11-06: There's a little more variety in rooms and treasures now, but I still feel the main problem is that all characters play generally exactly the same until they get a unique skill near the end of the game. I feel the developer can fix this by putting the interesting active skills right at level 1.

_childDocuments_.review: Remember DooM? The feeling of alternating panic at hordes of demons coming at you and the power trip of shoving a double barelled shotgun in their faces and blasting them off?Remember DooM RogueLike, which captured that essense perfectly in ASCII-art top-down roguelike random-generated number-crunch-fest goodness?This is what you get when you debrand DoomRL. No, this is not Mars and its moons, this is Jupiter and its moons. No, you cannot copyright rocket launchers, demons, pentagrams or heavy metal, but just in case, everything looks and sounds legally distinct.It's still Kitchen Ace (tm).It retains most mechanics from DoomRL, including the challenge modes (Angel of Carnage, here I come), trick shots based off manual targeting, bajillions of gun mods and grenade types and, of course, the various skill trees. It also adds distinct classes patterned after Doom RPG's ones, probably, its own soundtrack (don't worry, it still sounds like the best fusion of Doom's 3D0 and PSX soundtracks one can hope for) and even an animated intro sequence!It's still the same amazing time-consuming game as before, except now it has spiffy graphics, and I am eternally glad I backed that Kickstarter.

_childDocuments_.review: What a great game. This is basically a more polished version of Doom RL in most ways, but there are certainly a few differences. At least tonally, DRL is Doom I and II and Jupiter Hell is Doom 3. However, the tone of the game is very silly and feels right out of an 80s sci-fi action film. There are plenty of weapons and variants of them, but not too many to be lost and forget about them. The three classes are fun to play and make you feel pretty cool. The controls are very intuitive (mouse free too!) and clear. You can certainly play as quickly or slowly as you desire, but playing fast and loose is a good way to die instantly. Overall, this is a wonderful game for fans of quick and strategic combat or the Doom franchise. While this is a roguelike, there isn't a crippling amount of RNG at play, and it's fairly easy to remember the item pool. Good stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fairly difficult (I am playing on easy and still die regularly). That said, it is fun and there are 3 diff classes (with different upgrade perks) and each class plays differently. Despite being difficult however, this game is actually fun (something I could not say for games like dark souls and their ilk generally).  Although it looks like it is real time, it is not...it is 1 for 1 movement (i.e. you do a move and then enemy does immediately after). It is easy to get overwhelmed so do not rush in, upgrade your guns etc. and my advice would be to just head to the different worlds (don't go to the special levels until you are more experienced in the game). For a few negative points i will say that the hacking tools seem useless...when you get to a terminal you need way too many of them to make them useful in the majority of cases (especially since you have limited inventory). Yes you can upgrade a skill to lower the hacking cost..but you need dmg/crit/health upgrades way more than some perk that requires heavy investment for a terminal that may only show up every few levels and even then may only have a small benefit in using it (which i don't believe is offset by the inventory space it takes up). My other gripe would have to be with the game itself when it comes to the different paths...normal paths (i.e. normal elevators, specialty elevators and then things like the anomaly elevator (anomaly is very hard but you can go there on after a few levels on the first world...game should warn you the enemies are much harder there (and unless you have some mad skills you are just going to get murdered). Despite those two negative points, this is a fun game, is generally well made and the community in the game is very helpful and willing to provide tips/advice on how to do progress in the game. Dev also participates as well, so I think they deserve your money...buy the game and see for yourself! you won't be disappointed :)

_childDocuments_.review: roguelike-lite game with demons and guns. Recommended? 80% yes, 20% no.I think the comparison with DoomRL is inevitable. Lets see what changed and how it effects the gameplay. -- it is more claustrophobic, more packed, the vision and the range is smaller. The first and foremost impression that it is not as good as DRL was. If you don't opt for a kind of enemy sense or if you don't have allies on the map you tend to get into ♥♥♥♥♥♥ situations while opening doors. You can shoot them, true, but half of my deaths came from door related things. Apart from that, most of the tilesets are look great while the rest are okayish. The map have their variations, although I think this is an area for improvement. Several maps tend to be too much packed (cave and Europa maps mostly) or you are struck with 1 corridors. Corridors are another kind of pain as usually you don't have cover, you have to open certain doors and if you don't have a smoke/gas grenade or a high dps you can get into trouble. (Turrets, high tier enemies, etc.) -- A mixed bag honestly. The AI is stupid if not in "Hunt" mode, moving in random directions if activated. Several enemies will seek out you if they hear you, but most of the time pulling them into a good position is a pain. In DoomRL you had blind fire (radar shooting) and gift dropping for pulls works, here you are mostly using the wait keys and maneuvering around the map and hoping for the AI to stay put. Enemy variation is okay, although I feel that several enemies are too powerful or designed to burn through your medpacks. ((Arch)Medusas for example). The mechanical-beast-demon-human balance is okay, monster infighting is fun. If you take the pulling into consideration I think DRL was better, without that, both games are fine and very good in this regard. Apart from a few difficulty spikes, balance is okayish. Certain builds will have trouble in certain places (ammo, armor, enemies...) but it is part being of a roguelike/lite game. -- Another mixed bag. JH has certainly a better itemization in my opinion as random weapon and armor traits allow for greater freedom. I still miss the crafting element of DRL thou. Exotics are more powerful and maybe a bit more plentiful, but a single rifle with 2-3 mods can get you very far in the game in JH. In DRL certain strategies were built upon a weapon, in JH weapons tend to change and rotate as you progress through the game. I think this is a positive thing. Skills? Quite similar to DRL, some are quite op (looking at you techie gas, wizard, remote hacking), some are lackluster (mostly marine ones). The classes are distinct enough, have different paths, so you have your options. It is different from DRL but I don't think it is strictly better. -- I play with music turned off as it is not my kind of music, so no idea how good is that. The ambient and weapon sounds are great, they create a good athmosphere for the game. Enemies has distinct sounds you can recognize and prepare for them. The graphical presentation is very good and detailed, whatever you do ingame will be seen on the monitor. (Dash, cover, etc.) The GUI effects are not my style, I found the CRT and the noise effect annoying (turned it off, you have several options for them), the camera handling is... well... annoying. The fine camera movement looks good on paper, but it looks awful with detailed/anisotropic textures ending up in moire patterns after you've moved. Fortunately you have the option to use a fixed camera mode that solves this. The GUI itself is a bit chunky by design I reckon, nothing fancy but utilitarian.So as a summary, if you loved DRL you most likely will love JH. If you are new to the genre, it might work for you. I think the transition to 3d removed some of the charm of DRL (Derek Yu's exceptional tiles), but JH has some merits of its own. The devs are good people, they listen to feedback so overall I am more likely to recommend the game for you. As a demo you can always try DRL, as it is free and runs on just about every PC/MAC of today. Beside these, JH is so much better in price/gametime ratio than most of games that it also tilts the scale... Don't get me wrong, JH is a quality game (rare nowadays), it might just not be perfect for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Another review likened this game to a cross between Doom and Rogue, with a splash of XCOM thrown in. I find nothing to argue with as far as that goes, and I feel it adequately captures the soul of Jupiter Hell.Jupiter Hell, like DoomRL before it, is a turn-based roguelike in which you set the pace: the flow of action and reaction goes exactly and only as fast as you want it to go. Whether you want to meticulously plan your moves like George Clooney and Matt Damon in Ocean's Eleven, or go all-in like Doomguy himself, you can tailor Jupiter Hell to your preferred playstyle with an expansive perk tree and enough weapons to make a Kentucky gun nut blush.Make no mistake, though: this is a rogue-like with a 'K.' There's no meta-progression, no chain of unlocks making the game easier as you go. You start the game from a clean slate every time, and it ends one of two ways: victory over your final enemy, or with your blood splattered across one of Jupiter's moons.This game is playable with either keyboard or controller; in this writer's opinion, it feels right at home on the controller. The buttons are laid out very intelligently and are (almost) completely re-bindable using the in-game menu. (The dev has mentioned at some point adding mouse support as an accessibility option; however, it will not be the recommended playstyle.) The game should never surprise you with an input that doesn't work like it "ought to."Graphically speaking, looking at JH you might immediately think that it was written in Unity or Unreal. Nope: Jupiter Hell uses an engine that was written from the ground up for this game. It includes dynamic lighting and shadow, partial ragdoll simulation and hard-body physics for you madmen who can't leave any bench unbroken. It supports both OpenGL and Vulkan rendering pipelines, and overall it looks as good as you'd expect to see from a commercial game engine.On the sound front, this game features a bespoke soundtrack that evokes the thumping soundtrack of its namesake -- or, rather, what it could have been had it not been limited by the hardware of its day. The mood of the soundscape changes as you transition between levels, and is never inappropriate to the act, no matter what you're doing.In perhaps an oddity for roguelikes, the main character has a voice: none other than Mark Meer. Taking a leaf out of the Duke's book, he is foul-mouthed, sarcastic, and incredibly 1990s. It isn't necessarily something you would notice as missing if it weren't present, but its inclusion serves the game exceptionally well.In closing, I won't try to assign a numerical score to this game, as I feel it cheapens matters to do so. I hesitate to even assign a "value" or a "recommended price point," as even that can feel awfully subjective. Setting aside as much bias as is possible for a person to do, though, this game is absolutely worth the $25 it asks of you.

_childDocuments_.review: Fight zombies, robots, and hellish demons in this Doom-inspired turn-based Roguelike.  It features a huge variety of weapons, equipment, and skills to upgrade, which allows for a huge variety of playstyles, as you level up your character to be able to face tougher and tougher foes.  The maps are randomly generated, so no two playthroughs are the same, with difficulty settings and challenge modes to provide something for players of any skill level.  Also features gorgeous visuals with smoothly animated monsters, and it's all set to a heavy metal soundtrack, with a wise-cracking protagonist who sounds like he could have come out of an 80's action movie.I've personally sunk hundreds of hours into the early access version of this game, and it just keeps getting better and better, with endless replay value, so I can highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game plays like old-school rogue-likes which is refreshing in the world of meta-oriented rogue-lites.Your meta progression is you _knowing_ the game better.Tactical layer isn't too deep, but its solid enough. "Take it slow", "choose your own fights" and "don't be afraid to run away" are the paradigms that surprisingly still found their way in a gun-based game.Strategy layer consists of managing inventory space, picking a skill build and managing weapons and armor.This is where it gets a bit hairy.Having access to all skills in every run and being forced to pick your build-defining Master perk somewhat early means that you'll probably stick to something that works for you and it cuts down heavily on replay-ability.Inventory space is always lacking and annoying to deal with and only good thing I can say about ammo management is that it organically forces you to slowly migrate from 9mm to 7.62 to plasma as the game goes on, because of the loot tables the mobs have.Armor doesn't get access to your damage reduction perks and with how scarce repair stations are, you not being able to field-repair it and armor effectiveness going down as it gets damaged, investing in something apparently made of paper that still manages to impede your dodge chance doesn't feel good.You can mod the weapons and armor mid-game, but it doesn't feel like it affects the game too much as by the end of it you'll find some unique weapons that are both unmoddable and much stronger than any of the stuff you can make as long as they are at least somewhat relevant to your build.Still, its fun to play and well worth the price tag and I haven't even touched the atmosphere, voice acting and memes.Go forth and slay the demon hordes!
