_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game enough to fans of turn-based action. One of the few early-access titles that has been worth my investment. It's also had regular major updates since it came out; it's had one of the most consistent development cycles I've seen in an early-access game. The developers have been continuously refining the product into a truly worthy successor to Doom : The Roguelike. Similar to its predecessor, it takes place in a sci-fi horror setting, populated by zombies, robots and all types of vicious demons. Games are approximately two to three hours in length, accommodating a wide variety of difficulty levels. The action is brutal and violent, emphasizing intelligent, tactical gameplay. Careful use of your resources is vital to success, and the game provides a massive arsenal of interesting weapons and items that can radically alter how you approach your run. It's extremely satisfying to chance upon an advanced energy weapon that can take you from barely surviving to massacring the enemy with relative impunity.There are three character classes and numerous difficulty levels ranging from simple to virtually impossible. Each character gets his own skill tree, the skills you choose will determine the way you'll approach the game.  There are a generous helping of additional challenge modes help extend the playtime of this game. I've already put over 200 hours into it myself. If you're a fan of the turn-based tactical genre, you'll want to check this one out!

There are many game modes and challenge modes that keep things fresh, although I haven't played them as much, as there is enough depth in the normal game to put in hundreds of hours.I played half my time about a year+ ago, came back to it again and found new boss, new branches, new enemies. _childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game, and I have barely scratched the surface at 2 hours in. Its inspired by many games, from Doom, Dead Space to System Shock (and I'm sure there's more), but it never leans on them for help. Its truly unique in game-play, and is more tactical than it appears, leaving you room to breath and learn, but also punishing you for being bold. You're all alone, and you can get help, but it will cost a lot, and you're forced to make tough choices like whether to access a floor, or hack security for drones to kill the enemies+themselves in the process. This mixed with data logs giving you clues to future floors and items makes for a good gaming experience where you want to keep diving. I haven't even cleared the first floors, yet have been enjoying it thoroughly, and really look forward to the branching routes you can take. This game could be described as a Doom-like game, but its far more interesting and slow paced, not to mention way harder.

_childDocuments_.review: Very, *very* highly recommended for anyone who liked the old DoomRL, or turn-based classic Roguelikes in general. There's only three classes, but each of the mastery skills wildly change up how the game plays - I've got ~60 hours in at the time of reviewing, and I'm still having fun tooling around trying new stuff on Easy! The difficulty ramps up significantly once you go past that point, so it's definitely worth learning the ropes on Easy before moving on.Also, I chainsawed the end boss to death, and it was *glorious.* The music and sound design is great as well! _childDocuments_.review: If you lack the demon killing reflexes to play Doom Eternal or if you just want to sip a coffee while ripping through space fiends, this game is for you.It is an overall very good Roguelike with constant Early Access updates. _childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a love letter to DOOM and classic roguelikes. It's gorgeous, easy to learn but hard to master, and flows so well. Jupiter Hell sets a new standard for modern roguelikes.The gameplay centres around intense tactical combat throughout a procedurally generated sci-fi hellscape. There's a powerful sense of progression as you level up, choose skills and find powerful modded weapons.The graphics are great, the UI is incredibly polished, the original soundtrack is phenomenal. There's classic DOOM-style voiceover lines from the voice actor that played Commander Shepard. Every single part of this game drips with polish and attention to detail. If you're a fan of DOOM, tactical shooters or you just want to gib some demons, I can't recommend Jupiter Hell enough.

_childDocuments_.review: After 50 hours and a lot of viscera everywhere, I can safely recommend Jupiter Hell. It's a challenging and entertaining game, it looks good and runs smoothly, the sounds and music work and fit well, the guns and items are fun and plentiful, it's inexpensive, and it feels fair for a rogue game!The short of it is, if you like rogue style games, you should try this game. It's classy, it's sassy, it's a bloodletting humdinger! There are not many games that can hook me hard enough to keep me interested in playing like this (50 hours in a week).First of all, it's a roguelike, which means that if you die, you're dead and the game is going to be a tough challenge in general. That is important to note if you don't like the permadeath, randomly generated, try again style of play.You don't ever get to keep the things you find and there are no unlocks outside of challenges, trials, and further difficulty from what I have seen so far. So, the game is only ever going to get harder, which may not be for everybody. Furthermore, .A run can take 3 or more hours when going at a steady clip and taking breaks. It may be longer for people who like to really plan their strategy and are very tactically minded in all their actions. This means that , which may be frustrating for players new to this genre or who prefer to win often.There is a variety of weapons and items in the game, as well as traits and effects, but . It can feel sad to be deep in a run and receive loot that is under-powered for where you are.Rogues are definitely long form, heavy thinking, RNG-heavy type games where . So a few of the things I highlight above are things that the game should do. You can find a lot of enjoyment with this kind of game because of that sort of accomplishment.While I have died over and over, it has never felt like a drag to die. It has felt like an eye-opening experience! I hear myself saying things like, "Ah, should've used this instead of that." or "Now I know that I cannot melee that enemy without some set up." or "I could've chosen X instead of Y earlier and wouldn't be in this particular situation now." , which I think is a very strong accomplishment in a genre known for insta-gibbing players. I also almost always want to jump back in and improve or try again or try something new.First of all, the . The main character is a corporate worker guy just trying to get his work done and finds themselves having to get the 'damn thing done' since corporate (probably, once again) has summoned demons and made a pact with Jupiter's version of Satan, or something. The character seems to believe, at first, this is someone's idea of a really crappy prank and it's an entertaining hook for this kind of plot as well as shows what kind of place was being run there and what kind of corporation it was. So, thanks for that bit of fun lore.Speaking of lore, there's a plot and story, even if it's a relatively simple one. It's fun enough and carries the weight of the gameplay and assets. Movement and animations in the game are gorgeous, and even though it's a turn based game, it's easy to forget that with how smoothly your character runs and performs actions, even on a potato PC like mine! The many different enemies and objects you find look good and explode even better. Yes, your character can move the body chunks around when running through them! You can destroy most anything that isn't hard cover in the game with your fists, and that can be quite fun to watch too. The weapons and the way they fire, the way they look when they fire, and the sounds they make when reloading or being shuffled about, are amazing. The animations and sounds have been very satisfying to experience. .The  to parse and choose! You are often presented with interesting decisions that may make or break your run. I think with enough game knowledge, you can mitigate a large majority of the RNG the game throws at you. You are able to, after some game play and wisdom gathering, choose to avoid or take certain risks for certain rewards and chances. Sometimes knowing which branch to take or whether to change weapons is more than half the battle. It might be better to leave rather than trying to find more loot or gathering more exp. Learning which options you can choose to help alleviate a tension point in your run is one of the joys and important skills of this game. In other words, , a lot, and that's great. that help make it an experience you will enjoy. There are a plethora of audio settings such as changing the protagonist's style of speech from Normal, foul-mouthed, somewhat humorous guy to super serious, but clean mouthed fella, and places in-between. If you don't like the character's quips, you can choose to turn them off or only be plot-related. I recommend turning off his dialogue if you are going to be idle for a period of time, since he likes to discuss you being idle and that can be jarring. You can also remove some of the graphical effects on the screen using the display options if you don't like certain screen effects.  and I play using one to great effect. The game is Alt-Tab friendly in my experience, so you can adjust your virtual play space to incorporate an additional screen or just go see what new message popped up or whatever before diving back in. EDIT: Something new! You can choose a 'random' class when playing now. Which I appreciate greatly.There are , and you only have access to three of them to start. The tutorial is very quick and taught the base game very well. I recommend trying it out and really delving in based on your comfort level from there. With new challenges, trials, and difficulties being unlocked as I play and not being forced on me, I feel like the game is encouraging me to take my challenges at my own pace, and that's awesome!I foresee many many more hours and sleepless nights thinking about whether I should pick up a new weapon, drop an item for another one, take cover or run, shoot or throw a grenade. Every decision I've made feels weighted in some way, even if it's unintentionally taking two steps when I should've taken only one. So, if you like that sort of game experience, you're going to find that in spades here in Jupiter Hell.I want to end with this. The game has a lot to offer you. You may not know if you like rogue type games. You may not know if you like tactics or strategy games. If you'd like to try one though, this is a fantastically accessible one that clearly has a lot of experience and love put into it. I have enjoyed all 50+ hours of game I have played so far and will likely put hundreds more hours into it. For the price point, that's an absolute steal of a deal and I recommend it for people who like long-form, high-strategy, turn-based, rogue-type games. If you like dungeon crawlers with high challenge, this may also scratch that itch.*Pops open a lemon soda*

_childDocuments_.review: I had put many hours into the predecessor DoomRL, and this game inherits its strengths. For a "real" turn-based roguelike, it is really quick to get into, e.g. doesn't require memorizing many keybindings, and a playthrough also lasts a couple of hours. Instead of adding complexities, it focuses on the essentials, which is the ranged combat in this game. And that is really fun and addictive, which is why after your first run you will want to do another. The hardest decisions in this game are which weapons to choose, in which skills to invest and whether to take the teleporter to the extra-hard level which might offer special loot.The biggest and most obvious difference are the nice 3D graphics with cool lightening effects and animations, which is rare for roguelikes. Crazy how such a small team, mostly a single developer, could accomplish that, as they had to develop a custom graphics engine. The result is that you can move quickly or slowly, however you like, the animations will adapt and will almost let you forget that it's a turn-based game, as you never have to wait for a turn to end. Together with the sounds it makes the world feel more atmospheric and "real" then in DoomRL, as though I am actually there. I still like ASCII graphics occasionally (why no ASCII mode?) and using my imagination, but the graphics really help with the immersion in the game. And it still feels fluid and runs surprisingly  well given my dated laptop which even a dedicated graphics card and runs on Linux.Still, I think some polish would help the game. Here some examples: The menu for example could be easier to navigate, e.g. it should allow to navigate by keeping the keys pressed and even though I admit the mouse is not necessary to play the game, I still think it would be useful in the menu and maybe some other places. I understand that a roguelike lives from the fun gamplay and does not need an in-depth story, but for the immersion it would be nice to have some animations/sequences or something that actually show that I am travelling between different moons of Jupiter and not just taking an elevator (e.g. look at in Crypt of the Necrodancer). It would be nice to have small icons above the numbers for the weapon slots, I always have to check the equipment menu. And maybe some icons for the abilities and skills. And all in all just more details to make the procedural world look less procedural. It is still early access, so I hope these things will be improved, which is why I post this here.Otherwise, great game and I am glad that I had backed it. I think that players that feel overwhelmed by other "traditional" roguelikes will enjoy this as much as I did. It is as action-packed as a rogue-lite (e.g. Binding of Isaac, Risk of Rain), but does not require reflexes, but lets you stop and think. If you want a complex roguelike, where you explore an open world while worrying about hunger, can customize your characters in crazy ways such as mutations and set your enemies on fire, you are better served with something like Caves of Qud, Cogmind, Unreal World, etc. I enjoy both, depending on how much time I have. This is a nice introductory drug.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a very fun game! It is an outstanding spiritual successor of DoomRl. You can play it as a fast-paced "break" roguelike with fast-paced runs during your breaks, but it also allows a slow, thoughtful approach.It is a hard yet fair game. The losses feel like they were your fault and caused by your overextensions instead of by unfair and unavoidable enemies. The high challenge makes the victories more gratifying. I still need to beat it, but I consistently reach the third area. The game has no meta-progression, meaning the improvement comes from within, not from unlocked mechanics. When you start the game, you will lose consistently. However, one day, you will beat it, and no meta-progression means no difference between your first character and your winning character. The difference comes from your own improvement.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing Roguelike games for many years. I think one of my first ones may have been Tales of Middle earth. Though I did heavily play Angband and variants and many many others. Always looking for a good game in the genre.JH is a great game for the genre if you know what it is. I would call it more of a coffee break Roguelike as a full game that you win, may only be about 2 hours (depending on your speed and difficulty). But that is something that I find attractive. Sometimes I only have a little bit of time and want to fire something up quickly.Now it may have shorter runs than some games, but there is a huge amount of depth and content to explore. No two runs will play out the same. You have three base classes and each of those has five master skills that greatly alter or enhance the way you play. You could go for Technician and get Wizard and have hordes of bots do your bidding, or maybe you like to be a wraith and move through your enemies unseen? Scout and Ghost has you covered. Or maybe Equilibrium is your favorite movie ever and you want to be Christian Bale? Check out Scout's Gun Kata where every time you move your guns shoot... Ooor, maybe you are more of a Bullethell type of person, well grab chaingun and pick up Marine's Bulletstorm.. The lead you can pump out is epic.Did I mention all the varied levels? You have special levels you can visit and you can't go to every one in a run so it'll keep you coming back. The shorter game length will have you saying just one more after a win (or loss). You can get achievements to unlock new scenarios (with special run conditions) or unlock higher difficulties.The UI is simple clean and easy to use, sound effects are good too. And the best part is the devs just keep adding more to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hidden gem. It has all the (real) rogue-like elements that we love from ADOM, with a little nostalgia from classic Doom. Don't be fooled by the name, the cover image or the cover video. Despite showing fast-paced combat in the cover video, the game is turn-based. It's hard, but has a good balance of RNG + skill.

_childDocuments_.review: Without additional modes, the thrill of Jupiter Hell began to wane after about ten hours. The counterpoint of making a true roguelike is the risk of gamers failing to evolve, or getting good enough to make progress, and becoming frustrated or bored. rank-style achievement system presents attainable goals for struggling players, including those like me who balk at only four inventory slots. Combined with ChaosForge’s roadmap promising additional features, I believe that the secondary modes make Jupiter Hell an accessible game even for roguelike newcomers. And yes, there are hard and nightmare modes for the sadists, as well.Full review at

_childDocuments_.review: Context: I played the -crap- out of DooMRL and enjoy traditional roguelikes.For the first hour or so of playing Jupiter Hell I thought I'd made a mistake in buying it. Lack of diagonal controls felt clunky and "simplified". Really felt like I'd bought a shinier but stripped back DoomRL.A couple of hours later and I've come around to the design decisions. The enemies are given the same restrictions of you and I'm finding myself having to constantly think a couple of moves ahead. The cover system makes a lot of sense after your first game, and the perk trees for the different classes look like they create some interesting builds. Enemy variation is diverse enough to keep things interesting and the various "branch" levels have their own quirks - being able to use terminals/emails to anticipate what's ahead (including rewards) is really useful and a great feature considering builds will often work with a certain weapon group.One thing you should know going in - if you've only recently gotten into Roguelikes, you might find the lack of "stat boosting" metaprogression to be a dealbreaker. Personally, I love that we've got a modern commercial roguelike in Jupiter Hell that doesn't have this (there are unlocks but they are for challenge modes) and consider it a plus.Price wise? The default price tag is a little high in my estimation (when compared to other games of its ilk), but considering how many hours I got out of DoomRL without spending a cent? I consider it backpay. Your mileage may vary.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing turn-based Doom themed roguelike. Just amazing. It is hard, to the point I lost more than ten times trying a certain build until it works, and rewarding, when you manage to beat the last boss. This game is not an action game or shooting game. It is a tactical turn-based game with three main classes with at least three different builds each to master in order to beat the game. If enjoy tactics, turn-based games, and roguelikes, there is no reason why to not try this gem. Well done, devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this. I love Doom, and I love Roguelikes. But this game isn't really enough of either to be worth it. Its much too simple to be an in-depth and good roguelike and not fast enough to be Doom.*Response to Dev'sI have played a lot of Rogue-likes and a lot of Doom-likes, and I stand by what I said.What makes a good rogue-like to me, is the depth of moment to moment choice, not enemy variety or build alone. That is what makes this game too simple for me in rogue-like terms. As you said yourself "you move, collect stuff, shoot/slash and try to not get massacred". For comparison, other rogue-likes have skills, puzzles, ranges of spells/ability's, usable items, etc. Each moment of game-play in a rogue-like should be an important choice out of a large list of options, and this is what this game lacks.The Doomyness of this game is more-or-less just theme, and there's nothing wrong with that. I was covering how when I see this game for sale, I see Doom, and I see a Rogue-like. I wanted others to know that Doom does not feature in its game-play much, and how it doesn't qualify; hence it being too slow to adhere to a core Doom fundamental and also obviously not an FPS.Ultimately I won't dispute if the game is fun or not for other people. I will however say that a core of a good rogue-like is once again moment to moment game-play options, and this lacks that.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This game rules. It's a great translation of Doom to a traditional roguelike. It took me a second to come to grips with the fact that you can only move in the cardinal directions, there's no true diagonal movement in the game. But since the game is designed around this choice once you get used to it it all comes together beautifully.There are three classes to choose from, but within each class there is a large amount of choice how you want to build your character. As far as I know there's no progression system in the game, so the only way to get further and start winning is to die and get good so beware.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful and tactical roguelike - perfect if you have no experience in this hard to delve into genre. Don't be afraid of the price tag as the game already has 100's of hours worth of gameplay potential from weapon choices, classes, skill trees, mods, and most importantly, well developed tactical skirmishes. Playing on easy mode is a trap, as you'll find its still very difficult- Hard mode is a completely different beast. One word of warning for lovers of DoomRL- this is NOT DoomRL. The gameplay is vaguely similar, as are the classes and a few enemies- but overall this is a brand new game with different mechanics and intentions. Compared to DoomRL this game is, in my opinion, far more tactical. You are not a godlike Doom man- you are a badass fellow who NEEDS cover and tactical expertise to come out on top of each and every encounter. Its just as fun, hell, I think its better, but my initial 5 hours were ruined because I relied so heavily on my previous experience. Only after I took a step back and thought of the game as more as a seperate entity and relearned, did I really start to improve and have fun.Remember- LOSING IS FUN!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Super good game if you enjoy traditional roguelikes (features such as turn based, grid based, permadeath, very high levels of difficulty).  If you're exclusively a rogue'lite' person, it's probably not for you.  Not a lot of metagame progression, not a lot of forgiveness for mistakes, etc.  Still, a super fun tactical roguelike that you will keep getting better at and learning new things the more you play.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This is first and foremost a rogueLIKE.  Don't be confused.  This game is tough, and when it chews you up and spits you out at the beginning it expects you to learn from your mistakes and carry forward.Jupiter Hell is one of my favorite roguelikes ever though.  Yes, you have the methodical turn based action, but it looks so good and the cover system ends up making ranged combat very compelling.  You have to really think about the environment and be wary of what's around the corner.  Good decisions and strong builds can get rewarded, yes, but there's always that fear that the next chamber you step into is going to eat through too many resources or cost too much health.For as sleek as this game looks, it still sticks to it's DoomRL roots by creating and keeping a lot of tension as you progress.  There is a good amount of enemy variety and each run has multiple paths you can take before trying to find out why the Jovian System has won the worst colony award for 11 years running.  Get it.  Play it.  Die.  Try again.  Get a little further.  Incremental progression is rewarded with very fun, methodical game play.  Easily recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: It's so deep and challenging. Once you get the hang of it, there is way more to do like the challenge modes and higher difficulties. I particularly like how the challenge modes force you to use a different strategy than you're used to. I got my first wins with marine vampire melee builds, and the challenge modes helped me branch out to other classes and master traits! I think it looks great, I really like the 3d. Plays AWESOME on steam deck. Up there with Doom 2016, Rimworld, and Project Zomboid for deck playability.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I've played enough roguelikes to know that there is a faction that abhors graphics in these games, and I get that. I've played my share of alphanumeric rogues; I came up in the late 70's and believe me, that was all we had. We ran them on printer terminals, too... So I can say with some authority that sometimes, it's good to just have something easy on the eyes. And this game is that, stylish, atmospheric, all that Fashion Week stuff translated into off-world Cyberpunk settings. The music is also moody and appropriate.Beyond that, the purists will be happy. The game is a classic roguelike. 3 character classes. Gear is all combat related - health packs, weapons, ammo, mods, armor and so forth. As you level you can get additional perks - extra life, dodge skill, aiming skill, that sort of thing - from a relatively brief menu. It's all focused on gameplay, is what I'm saying. Some roguelikes offer huge lists of pets, variant character types, skills, all the adjectives of character building. Not Jupiter Hell. Jupiter Hell is blasting things before they blast you, in spooky offworld levels with cool lighting and a moody soundtrack. It is the quintessence of roguelikes, a distillation of exquisite quality and taste for the cognoscenti. This game gives you classic tradeoffs - short range/high damade or long range/low accuracy, or moar bullets/faster expenditure? Choices that really put you in the classic roguelike mindset of desperately searching for and comparing supplies when you find them, because you can only carry so much... It engages you, pulls you in very well.Edit - Gripe about voiceover addressed, new weapons and damage types and skills added, kudos to the dev team!I highly recommend this game for fans of roguelikes. It's an instant classic.  Enjoy the game in the silence of space, if you have to. But enjoy it you will. :-)
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Jupiter Hell is a turn based roguelike in the style of Doom. The camera is overhead and every time you perform an action, all the AI performs a turn. If you choose to move, shoot, reload, or even just wait, the enemy gets a turn immediately themselves. It's not a turn based game like XCOM if that's what you're looking for. As a roguelike, there is no progression from one run to the next. You die, you lose everything and start over. You get further by learning how to better play the game.It is really fun but very challenging. It took me about 10 hours to beat it for the first time on easy. Looking at the Steam stats, only 13.2% of people ever even beat the game on easy. As a point of reference, 92.4% have at least played the tutorial so that's a very small percentage of people who have beaten it. You can easily die in the first couple of levels on any given run. The only reason I was even able to beat the last boss is because I had so many medkits I just focused on damaging the boss and taking hits myself, healing to full with large medkits when necessary.The graphics leave a lot to be desired. It's an overhead camera but I feel like with the fixed camera like this, they should have gone with a different aesthetic. It's kind of tough to tell what some enemies even are at times. The UI is pretty fitting though and looks like something from the 90s. There's also classic voice lines like you'd expect from a game like the original Doom series. The game certainly does do a great job at bringing the Doom vibe even considering the big camera change. The music is also awesome too, some solid metal tunes in there.If you like turn based games, this is a fun one. I'm not sure if I really want to continue trying harder difficulties because I feel like getting to the last boss will be incredibly infuriating at higher difficulties. I'm still glad I got it though, it was worth the price of admission!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don't care enough to review games, but this one holds a special place in my heart-Its been very satisfying to watch it develop from a free indie ASCii rogue-like (DoomRL), from an obscure corner of the internet, into a fully developed game on steam. I used to keep a thumb drive with the original, so i could plug and play it anywhere (I think I played it freak'n Haiti a few times, when i was trying to de-stress).For those who played the original, this will be a satisfying successor, will all the mechanics and play strategies refined/diversified. I think the only major difference is that you can only apply mods to weapons, but not construct specific 'named' weapons with mod combinations. But this is an actively developed game and the creators are adding content and re-balancing with some regularity.Fans of the Rogue-like genre in general should enjoy this game: it is DOOM re-imagined as a rogue-like, what more is there to say?
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: ChaosForge's legally distinct successor to DoomRL might surprise you if you expected more of the same. Its gameplay makes subtle but meaningful changes that result in it being more of a cautious and difficult experience overall. That said, it's a great fast-paced roguelite that's matured nicely through its Early Access period. Tough as nails but highly addictive to play, with a tongue-in-cheek tone and gameplay that's easy to pick up but has enough depth to sink into. Hopefully future updates can keep Jupiter Hell supplied with new content.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: It's honestly a pretty fun game. It's a decent follow up to DoomRL, and keeps the flavor of "What if Doom, but Roguelike instead?" You are gonna die quite a bit until you learn how cover and dodge work, but once you start getting the hang of leveling and weapon usage? It's honestly a blast, and the updates so far have been great. I'm stoked to see what weirdness gets added once the game releases.Recommended if you're a fan of Turn Based Gun RPGs at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: If you've ever played DoomRL, you know what to expect, just more of it. If not, Jupiter Hell is very interesting as a roguelike because it is purely turn based and can be played incredibly slow and tactically, but the game still runs as though it were a full paced action game. It's incredibly easy to get wrapped up in the action and start playing as though it were a real-time game.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: (Edited to address developer notes and comments)Ultimately it is at this point not quite to the level of DOOMRL, it has number of problems that will hopefully be addressed as development continues.  Such as the inability to turn the camera, this means that enemies to the bottom of the screen side are seen as many as 2 spaces slower than enemies at the top of the screen.  They have chosen to remove diagonal movement, which can be a little jarring coming from DOOMRL straight to this game  They have added an active skill mechanic to each of the classes and added the ability to upgrade the basic passive and active skills of each class.They have added a new mechanic [Pain] that degrades at minimum your accuracy against targets for a few game ticks and falls off rapidly. It can be interesting, forcing you to take a more passive role in fighting, hoping they miss an attack at longer ranges to look for the best opportunity to fire back, but enemies are generally aggressive enough that you won't get locked into anything completely unmanageable.They have also added Grenades, they are useful against monster closets stuffed with 4-5 enemies, so they're handy in a way say the rocket launcher is not because you can manually choose where the grenade goes. to place yourself out of the damage radius.They have also added a cover mechanic, it degrades accuracy for either you or your opponent if one of you is next to a cover that is "in the way" the game is pretty loose with the concept and I'm not certain it does anything else. It also amplifies it's impact based on your pain rating, as noted by the developer, furthermore, staying in cover doubles its benefit, encouraging pretty heavy cover shooting.  There is also an added benefit, using the [Wait] command will also increase accuracy, so finding a good sturdy wall corner and holding it can Greatly increase your ability to handle threats.They've committed to traits and perks in this game being very different from DOOMRL, almost none of the perks are straight numerical increases, they push Utility a lot harder in this game than in it's predecessor.  for good or ill is a matter of opinion, but I think it at least lessens the chance of a monobuild becoming dominant for me where I look to do the same thing every game.  Strong potential, getting better with iteration.Happily it is still in beta and will likely receive the love it needs to hit a mirror shine.  It is getting better patch by patch.  I still play DOOMRL quite a bit, but as this goes I could see letting the old dog lie.  Growing into a Good game, has a chance to grow into something far greater than what it came from with some careful attention to detail and a little imagination.recommended, for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This is a turn based rogue-like from the makers of DoomRL (which I never played). The game has much better graphics and more streamlined gameplay, at the cost of some minor player choices. The biggest issue right now is that you can't unload weapons on the ground, but to compensate the devs made the ammo drops more generous. There's also no diagonal movement which is fine with me.What initially drew me to even consider buying it in early access is the dev's clear middle finger to the Epic Game Store, which you can hear in the trailer. Epic has been bribing Kickstarter devs left and right to betray their customers for a paycheck, and hearing a dev have some integrity made me want to support them and try out a game that looked interesting. I'm glad I did because it is fun. What has further cemented in my mind that I made a good decision is that the devs are extremely active on the forums answering questions and concerns. This brings confidence that the game will continue to be worked upon and improved (that and they apparently worked on DoomRL for 10 years without even getting paid).Basically in the game enemies don't move until you do, so there is strategy involved in positioning, especially with the cover mechanic. The game obviously takes heavy influence from Doom which is no surprise, with demons, you being in space, and even going to Hell to kill the summoner.Being Early Access the game is obviously not yet complete, but the devs have stated they have plans for updates for years to come. I fully expect the majority of my gripes to eventually be fixed. Perhaps my biggest one is that the game is really hard right now. I haven't been able to get very far on medium, I have no idea how you're supposed to beat it on ultraviolence. But as new equipment and items are added, and traits are added and refined, it should get a little more balanced in player favor.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Jupiter Hell is quite literally LIKE Rogue, earning its title more so than a lot of other "roguelikes". To sum this game up, it's "Great Value Doom" with all of the charm and just as badass. In fact, I found myself feeling distinct "Doom 3" vibes from this game. It must be the locales and the liberal use of gorgeous bump-mapped textures. The graphics, in fact, are gorgeous and run very well. Good use of lighting and reflections. These eyecandy visuals, sprinkled with a liberal amount of gore, is accompanied with a soundtrack that sounds much more like classic Doom than Doom 2016/Doom Eternal.Jupiter Hell is a highly replayable roguelike with some tactical elements. You can choose from a number of classes, each with their own set of "traits" that you can acquire via leveling up. If you prefer running and gunning, there is indeed a build for that. Get the "Hell Runner" trait and pair it up with "Onslaught" trait, it increases your chance of dodging attacks and allows you to fire at nearby enemies while moving. Some traits are "master traits" which require you to learn and level up other traits in order to get them. This system is quite frankly excellent, and I never found any trait to be terribly useless or uninteresting. You really do feel like you're getting stronger.If that all wasn't enough, you get a large variety of weapons in true Doom fashion. Melee weapons, pistols, SMGs, assault rifles, chain guns/rotary guns, launchers, and even plasma variants of these weapon types. There are indeed special and unique weapons, which are very rare.When it all comes together, the weapon selection plus the progression system encouraged me to experiment more than many other roguelikes or roguelites. You can even dual wield pistols or SMGs, and even a combo of the two. You can gain "badges" of various types as a persistent reward, which grant you all kinds of goodies including special challenges. Really, Jupiter Hell comes together in one incredibly fun package!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, cryptBeer for everyone!Then, that game is awesome!Pros: - Marvealous metal music! - It's the spiritual successor of d**mRL - It's a really good Roguelike developed by a brilliant team! - Graphic are great! - The custom engine makes the game extremly fluid - The pace is as you want, you can go fast or slow! - Still jamming to the music! - The dev team are putting monthly update with full of content during the current BETA (Seriously, the berserker update was great)Cons: - You don't have it yet! What are you doing, click the button and join the fun! - I'm bad at roguelikes even if I love them.But it's enough about the game. If you like strong beers, but also like sweet beer I'm certain you'll like the Samichlaus beer. It's brewed in the month of December every years and is aged for 10 months in barrel before being bottled. It's a 15% beer and have similarities with ruby porto wines.Edit:Now that it's on 1.0 it's even better then when it started! Can't wait to finally kill that Final Boss, if I'm ever able to get good at it!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: It's Doom, but if Doom was turn-based! Try not to get confused by the smooth animations and fast play that are emphasized in the trailers and some of the other promotional material... you can play as slow as you like.I certainly tend to play roguelikes fairly slowly myself so even after four hours I'm still in the middle of my first run (streamed it, actually, with the devs in chat and archived ), though based on my experience with RLs and having reached half way to the end at this point (just Medium difficulty), I can already tell it's worth my time to explore Jupiter Hell's mechanics and classes (three of them each with various skill tree options and correspondingly different tactics) and of course procedural content and environments to mix up the runs.If you like the look of it and enjoy gunning down or blowing up demons and robots, finding and upgrading your weapons and armor (plus some light inventory management), maybe operating a few terminals here and there, and picking new skills as you raise levels (XP-based, but not really much grinding involved since levels are short and the number of enemies capped, at least on normal difficulties), then give it a shot. It comes with a very straightfoward tutorial and is pretty easy to pick up.The focus is on ranged combat and using various forms of cover to your advantage to come out ahead against greater odds, and although there's melee combat as well I haven't tried that yet (seems dangerous to let them get that close? :P)Note: Movement is four-way only! I think it works fine here since that's how the game was designed and balanced, though it's worth pointing out as it can be a dealbreaker for some fans of the genre.There's also no mouse controls yet, but I prefer keyboard myself anyway, and for those who don't, the game is also controller-friendly.There are definitely some QoL issues to iron out, but there are already quite a few settings options, no real show stoppers, and I know the devs are working at addressing requests in the near term while also expanding the content even further, so it's only a matter of time.What traditional roguelike is really done at 1.0 anyway? ;)Edit: So I continued my first run and won (Medium difficulty, took about 9 hours in all due to streaming w/chatting--second video ), and while the enemies did get tougher later on, the only hard parts were encountering a miniboss type of enemy on the second to last floor, and fighting the final boss itself, being not really sure what to expect and just dealing with it on the fly, down to my last resources.Considering I've only explored one play style with one class using a few of the available weapons, and the fact that branches offer more variety and extra challenge for extra rewards but I've only visited a few of those out of the total number available, it still feels like there's plenty more runs to try out here. That said, the gameplay loop is relatively tight and limited and as a result personally I find the tactics a bit repetitive once locked into a particular style, but maybe a higher difficulty will at least add more spice.Also I'd certainly enjoy playing in ASCII mode once that's available, since the visuals are fun but I've found I repeatedly have trouble spotting important features, like enemies, obstacles, and even my own Doom guy xD (sorry: Jupiter Hell guy...) Reportedly there will be more highlights available at some point, which would be nice. To be honest at this point Jupiter Hell feels kinda like it's still in Early Access despite having a full release, but again the "1.0" milestone is almost kind of arbitrary when it comes to traditional roguelikes that are constantly evolving, expanding, and improving, and I'm sure it will continue to improve over the coming months and year.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This deserves an updated review given how much has gone into it since I first recommended it. I'm a longtime supporter of this dev, ever since the wonderful "DRL" (Or, y'know, Doom: The RogueLike before they actually caught Bethesda's attention.) this game is the spiritual successor to. This was also one of the few games I've backed on Kickstarter, and one of the VERY few I haven't been disappointed in doing so.As expected from the description and source game, you get to strategically kill armies of corrupted soldiers, robots, and demons as an action-hero-grade space marine.There's an enormous variety of ways to play and weapons to use. You could easily put dozens of hours in before really getting into everything. The graphics aren't what I call spectacular, but they do a good job conveying the atmosphere of where you are, and just how badly you're blowing things to bits. The music, though...♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ the music in this game slaps.It's worth noting, though, this truly IS a Roguelike. It WILL kick your ass. Repeatedly. On top of that, the dev happens to enjoy making the highest difficulty settings into challenges for those who pretty much mastered his game. And yes, that's continued here. Trying to get the highest level badges (in-game achievements) will destroy your sanity.If you like roguelikes, ABSOLUTELY buy this.Now, I'm off to make even more space zombies do the Chaingun Cha-Cha™
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I loved DoomRL and this is much the same, only better. The top-down 3D graphics are amazing, the music and sound design very much in line with Doom and the gameplay is much like DoomRL but streamlined and very accessible. For roguelike fans who also like Doom this is a must-have game. Be warned though, this game is hard and unforgiving. You will die a lot, but as you play, you will get better at it and the difficulty is what makes progress so rewarding. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Good to scratch that itch of rogue + turn based dungeon exploring and killing in a sci-fi setting with guns instead of swords. Becomes monotonous after a while, but after taking a break you're drawn back again. Good at any price.EDIT: My enjoyment of the game has increased 300% by scum-saving (save the game files and restore if you die). Yes I know this is cheating, but it's enabled me to learn so much more about the game and I've gotten to the point where I no longer need it.EDIT2: After investing more hours into the game, the breadth of strategic options available for all 3 classes (Marine, Scout, Technician) is fantastic and offers much replayability. The map layouts do take some getting used to, but after you figure out how they are it's fine. This is a fantastic game and I daresay there are none like it out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: So! Let me begin by saying a quick thank you to the wonderful dev team. Not only did they send a copy of this game to me for free, but they were wholly understanding in the delays in me getting around to playing it (New PC, gpu issues, capture issues initially that were my fault, etc). Now, let's get into the meat of things!Style: I was initially a hint wary as this is not the sort of game I normally rush off to peek at, but after just a few minutes of game play? Oh, I'm hooked! Traditional turn based rogue styled mechanics - Inventory management, ammo, weapon changing and types (So far, we've found a variety of different guns using different ammo types and even melee options! I need to find that chaingun again whee!). There are different armor types as well (as I recently found out) and you can upgrade your weapons and armor with mod packs of different styles. The game play gets really interesting and customized as you progressMusic? Oh, it's great. Fun, engaging, creates a solid atmosphere and got me really into the mood for the game.There are presently 3 classes, each has a unique take on it. Yes, they all have the same weapon options, but they also have their own perk set ups for leveling, starting gear, unique traits and can impact the game heavily on play style. I have tested 2 of the 3 so far and have to say, I am seriously enjoying the variety just there and the randomization between runs.All in all? I say pick it up. It's damn entertaining and the profanity only adds to it in my opinion. (Yes, there is a clean language option for those sensitive to such). They really did think of almost everything here! I will keep playing the game in the upcoming weeks, test out new set ups, builds, etc. Best of luck in your runs and may the RNG Gods smile upon you!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: On its surface the game does look pretty basic.Playing the first hour you would think the game is all about taking cover while juggling the enemy out of his and nothing else, but once you start toying with the different character perks you will uncover the real game of:"can i make a sniper that one shots everything?""can i create a hacker that doesnt have to lift a finger and just let bots destroy everything?""can i be a ninja with a weeabo katana?"And the answer is: give it a try, see what happens.....if you succeed, there is always a higher difficulty mode to really test your mettle.The game also has interesting challenge modes to insitigate you into trying something different and unique.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: It's the plot of Doom but done as a rogue-like. Level up, upgrade and manage your equipment, kill everything you see and always try to make sure you can run if things look bad. Unlike perhaps most traditional roguelikes as a long grind through lots and lots of levels, it's more focused with a set number of levels (~30), no going back, no shop level, finishable at a couple-hour sitting. This is a plus and a minus - it's pretty short which creates a sort of fun dynamic, with the replayability in three different classes with lots of optional builds. It does however lack a bit of the same "epic" feel, and once you've gone through enough times, you'll be seeing the same places, enemies, items, and so on a lot, and this lack of variability will probably cause boredom in some players fairly quickly. I suspect some expansion with new places and things would not go amiss.It's slick enough, graphics and gameplay are fine.  I've had a couple of crash to desktops, but they are rare enough that it's no big deal. I don't have any problem rating this positive, but at the same time I do not think it is a work of greatness. £20 is a pretty reasonable price.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Jupiter Hell is a classic style roguelike from the creator of Doom the roguelike. This game is pretty much DRL with all the copyrighted stuff filed off and with pretty good 3D graphics.You are a soldier stationed on one of the moons of Jupiter and demons invade your base while you were out scouting, You get back and start killing the demons, eventually invading their homeworld and killing their boss. The game is divided into episodes and each episode is divided into levels. You can't go back to previous levels, unless you're visiting some small sub-level like a separate storage room or similar. You can find alternative exits to other parts of the station that can lead to better loot, but those paths are usually harder. The game has three player classes with different skill trees, multiple difficulty levels and there's a player profile progression system which unlocks more difficulty levels and extra modes.Jupiter Hell is a classic roguelike, which means there is no permanent upgrade system. Your character doesn't get permanently better stats or better starting gear. You can only rely on your own growing knowledge of the game. It is a fairly tough game, but on lower difficulties it is certainly beatable. One playthrough is fairly short, but there are multiple endings depending what you do during the game and what game mode you play. Depending on what skills you learn from the class tech tree and what weapons you use, the way you progress through the game can vary wildly.Jupiter Hell is a really good roguelike for the fans of the genre. It is a fast-paced, short game and notable for being one of the few shooting-based roguelikes out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: A brutal but fair, turn-based but fast-paced roguelike, it goes as fast as you do. Need a moment to plan out your next move? Free feel to take it. Want to speedrun? No need to wait on slow animations. None of the above? It'll animate just as fast as you panic.Sounds and controls are both fantastic, gamepad or keyboard.As many levels of difficulty as you need, but it doesn't stop there. As you progress further you unlock challenges that morph how you play and trials that morph how the dungeons play.For instance, in the Angel of Carnage challenge, you get to use only one weapon: a rocket launcher. In exchange, some ammo will be converted to rockets. Don't blow yourself up! Some example modes include Purity (no side branches, but more loot drops), Haste (half as many floors, twice as much exp), and Infinite. After 280+ hours I've only begun to see all the game has to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I have very little experience with 'classic roguelike' game (i.e. synchronous turn-based where enemies act when you do), but if Jupiter Hell is anything to go by, I need to check out more of them!It plays similarly to a XCOM, only you have direct control of a single character. It's all about utilising cover, calculating risks, and managing resources. There's a lot of variety in the levels you traverse, given it's all set on spaceships or the moons of Jupiter. There are 4 main 'levels' to progress through, and each one is split into multiple alternate paths to go down, ending in special rooms with difficult fights and better rewards.It took me 4 attempts to get to the end of the game on medium difficulty, and that took ~4 hours (roughly an hour per level). While there isn't a whole lot of difference between runs, the drops you find early on will tend to guide which perks you choose when leveling up. These perks have a significant impact on your playstyle. There are also 3 different classes to keep things fresh.Finally, the production values are the best I've seen in a roguelike game, which makes a change from the typical ASCII or low fidelity art you usually see from these types of games. There's loads of environmental and enemy variety, a good (but not DOOM level) metal soundtrack, and the guns and enemy SFX sounds satisfying.Jupiter Hell is fantastic, and worth a look if you're interested in a DOOM-like game that's slower paced and more strategic.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best roguelikes I've ever played.  This game is in the spirit of D**mRL, and made by the same person.  If you want a preview of Jupiter Hell, I recommend downloading and trying out D**mRL, which is free, as long as ASCII graphics don't bother you.  They are very similar games, though Jupiter Hell is superior in every way, in my opinion, and I'm sure there are people who disagree with me out there.If you like roguelikes, and you like Doom, you will probably like this.   Get it.

_childDocuments_.review: If you love roguelikes and you love dying over and over and over and over and over .... again, then this game is for you.Boy, just tonight in the span of four+ hours I died like 12 times and restarted runs at least 4 times, because of bad luck/rng. But damn son! The runs that lasted at least an hour or more, like the last one of today, were fun as hell and I didn't feel cheated or kept getting the short stick because of a ♥♥♥♥ RNG. Nope. It was great fun.Yeah, some of the runs I think I got unlucky in regards to RNG gods, but then again I only have to blame my trigger happy self, pressing forward and/or fire one too many times, when I should have instead retreated. Lessons learned. And my last run of the day went pretty far as a result of that.Great game. 11/10. Highly recommend it. Full price is totally worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: The short and sweet of it - It's a coffee break Rougelike. Not in the increasingly watered down meaning of Rougelike where it just means random levels with permadeath, but of the actual "Isometric RPG with depth and a quick trip to the mortem screen for not thinking". You'll either like it, or you won't, it's not the run and gun rampage of it's inspiration, nor drawing elbereth in the dust and waiting dozens of turns. It's quick, it's satisfying, and the developers are incredibly active within the community, what more could you want?UPDATE AUG 5 2021, 1.0 RELEASE: Wow, what a ride this has been! Exotics, Uniques, Master skills, and tons more, the dev team put in a *ton* of work over the years. Since my initial review, it plays better, feels deeper, and every win feels more satisfying than the last. Grats on the 1.0!

_childDocuments_.review: When they said this game was successor to DoomRL, they really mean it. I haven't messed around with the mods enough to know if there's special/unique "craftable" gear from the mod-pack combinations, but everything is a slick-stylized upgrade to everything that made DoomRL great and then some.Heavy focus on positioning and tactics in comparison to other roguelikes, and despite being more tactical than the original, the pacing is quite fast and snappy. _childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of traditional rougelike games like ADOM or Tales of Maj'Eyal, this is a good game in the genre to pick up. If you've ever played DoomRL, this game is basically a modernized and far more polished version of that with graphics.

_childDocuments_.review: A refreshing blend of theme and genre; Jupiter Hell is Earth Heaven one run at a time. This is a game I can see myself playing for years to come as the replay value is... is exactly the point!  It's a traditional styled rouge-like with turn-based tactical elements, in a 90's sci-fi horror, action game wrapper(TIP: I recommend the "serious" audio dialog setting as it makes the game more doomish rather than duke-nukish.  It's my personal opinion that a silent and strong space marine fits the game better than some loose talkin' flamboyant chauvinist punk, glad the developers added this alternative option). Jupiter Hell is a complete game as-is. I'm very happy I decided to purchase it on a whim. I enjoy variety in my gaming diet and this game checked a few boxes not often checked, and it hit the spot perfectly.  However, with a bit more added polish from future updates it could substantially increase longevity and positive buzz among players who may enjoy the addition of online challenges.  The game has an addictive run-based nature that makes good runs feel magical enough you might like to show your achievement to online friends & strangers(sadly there will be no public record or memorial for space marine "F*cker Carlson" who cowardly bled-out hiding in a corner from a bi-pedal ice-devil). It's a really good game from a heavily influential genre that doesn't come around often, if at all. Buy it, try it, be happy(until you forget to manually reload your shotgun). My only critique/suggestions at this point are merely additional polish and extra features:1) While I love the music and sound fx that are in the game, there seem to be some missed opportunities for additional sound cues related to in-game actions.  Example of places where cues would be welcome are; when a new elevator is revealed for the first time, or a musical cue when last enemy is killed(along with the quip that plays), stuff like that I felt could use another pass.  More bells and whistles, ya know, "video-game-it-up" a bit more. 2) Daily/Weekly Challenge feature with online leader-boards(same statically seeded level for all players).3) A replay feature at the end of each level(or floor) that allows the player to watch their run of the level in real-time from a cinematic camera(or tightly zoomed game-play camera). It would be awesome if these could be coupled with a daily challenge feature and/or could be uploaded/saved with your high-score.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun for a while - if you enjoy roguelikes it's worth picking up to see at least.But there isn't very much depth to it.The game feels like theres a lot of potential for fun choices in it, but all of that potential seems wasted by some very questionable design decisions. I'm sure the developers listen to their community, but I also get the impression the people they listen to might not understand what makes things fun to play.The cover mechanic is integral to the game - outside of cover you can expect to eat a lot of gunfire unless you have a build that lets you shoot while moving, maintaining a % dodge chance by doing so. What this results in though is most runs revolve around dancing out from a corner to get someone's attention by waggling your butt at them, then running giggling back to your corner to shoot at enemies one at a time. And while the cover mechanic seems to be what the game was built around, many of the recent updates have been introducing more and more content that specifically renders cover useless to the PLAYER. You can have a excellent spot of cover or dodge % and learn that the majority of lategame enemies simply... don't aim. Linear beams that penetrate walls, AOE blasts, and suicide bombers will be commonplace lategame. And even without them, expect almost every elemental enemy to leave a puddle of damage at your feet (acid, destroying armor, poison that stacks every turn, or fire that stacks every turn and causes you to leave a trail of fire... that also stacks on you) on the off chance one of them DOES hit you, forcing you to run either out of your cover or retreat down a hall - giving anyone within range free turns to deliver you a healthy lead supplement. Not to mention how many of their status effects are designed to stack insanely fast, and wear down by one per turn (poison deals its number then reduces by 1, can be removed with a medkit - and fire stacks, reducing down by one per turn... and cannot be removed anymore due to the fire pool mechanic they recently introduced). (EDIT: They recently updated and made it possible to remove fire pools with medkits or smoke generation - Haven't tested the new build, not really interested.)This isn't even including the pain and bleeding mechanic - taking damage causes pain, which reduces your accuracy by a sizeable amount. When bleeding, every few turns it ticks down by one, dealing its full damage and giving you pain equal to bleed stacks x 5 (and is often applied in stacks of 7-10, resulting in taking an enormous penalty to accuracy and around 30-40 damage over time if you do not happen to have a medkit handy). Most melee enemies apply an enormous amount of bleeding and pain on hit, rendering almost any melee build just completely useless instantly.As for builds, they seem interesting at face value but there is unfortunately less depth in the character skills than there could be - mostly focused around melee, boosting range/damage, allowing dual wielding or some form of ammo conservation. But also essentially forcing a player to decide within the first 5 player levels (or 3-4 stages) what build they must commit entirely to ahead of time. There is no room for improvisation, either you find a gun that works with what you are doing or it is garbage. The new unique weapons are fun but don't really add anything outside of being occaisionally an item that simply wins you a run with no additional effort.There exist a number of AOE options, mostly in the form of shotgun cones, grenades/launcher circular AOEs, but nothing else. for a scifi game there is very little weapon variation outside of unique/special variants of guns that usually only add things like "no pain penalty on aiming" or "+aim to crit chance", without adding any more interesting mechanics or effects.The majority of runs go as follows: collect a shotgun somewhere, wiggle your bum at enemies to draw them to your cover corner, stockpile as many medkits as you can (you will likely be spending most or all of them in IO or Dante to remove poison or attempt to mitigate fire), and grind through each level so you can put another level into whatever your chosen build for the run is. Most of the runs honestly have almost the exact same playstyle until around the third zone where you finally have enough gear and skills to have a more unique approach - hug corners, dance around looking for enemies to wiggle your butt at, run back to your corner, rinse and repeat until a level is cleared. Of course there can always be situations where you turn a corner and just ARE adjacent to a reaver - in most cases this is an instant loss due to the accuracy penalties from pain rendering you unable to hit anything in front of you, and their move speed being larger than yours rendering you unable to escape without the aid of smoke grenades or teleport kits, but outside of events like that gameplay mostly remains the exact same.Theres a lot of possible fun that could exist with the skill system and unique/rare weapons with possibly interesting effects, but as it stands the majority of design decisions for added content just keep adding new monsters (and bosses) that are specifically designed to render the tools given to the player useless.The new bosses for example: all of them have large AOEs that ignore cover, save for the ancient - when damage he simply teleports behind you to shoot you from a new spot, potentially one that has its own cover against you (he teleports fairly randomly, but more often than not negates your cover. Though if you made it far enough to get to him you will likely just delete him anyways - as far as bosses go he's considerably less threatening than the majority of hordes and enemies you faced to get to him)I've been following this since I heard it was in development after DoomRL, and while I had high hopes for it I am just... consistently disappointed by it.TL;DR - A unique roguelike with a cover mechanic, try it out but don't expect a lot of depth. stick to cover.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game! It's seemingly simple, but REALLY hard to master. I've only played in on 'Hard' and sometimes I die in the first room! _childDocuments_.review: It's about time I updated this review.A lot of updates have improved the diversity and balance of this game. It can be really fun to try out different builds and build routes, and see how different equipment will affect the way the build plays out. I'm a big fan of this kind of stuff. But in an almost ironic way, the game remains the least interesting in the moment-to-moment gameplay. There are some tricks you can learn for AI manipulation, but overall, you're either mowing through enemies repeating the same tactics that your build encourages, or you get caught out and you die.Items like grenades and certain actives try to alleviate the dying aspect, but even then it's reliant on you having them in the first place - which isn't a guarantee on Callisto and even sometimes beyond. I think it generally boils down to most of your actions consuming a turn, with you getting punished for reloading, running away, healing, or swapping weapons.Of course, it makes sense that you WOULD be punished for these things, but it makes you feel like your options are quite limited when trading shots with the enemy.I'm adjusting my suggestion to pivot toward giving the player access to new actives that give them more power over positioning. A dash, a jump, a slide, what-have-you - varied a little based on the class. A charge for the Marine to cover a few tiles in a straight line (and maybe offer some damage and a stun on a direct enemy collision), a small dodge roll for Scout that lets them move a couple spaces without consuming a turn, temporary cover for Engineer - stuff that gives the player a little more power to micromanage their engagements to their advantage at the cost of class resource.Honestly I still think it wouldn't be a bad idea to swap Running with Adrenaline as Marine's starter active. It's so much more versatile and would help him with his struggle of being caught out of position.
