_childDocuments_.review: I first heard about this game on Roguelike Radio Podcast #130, and snatched it up as soon as it hit Steam! Even more excited about the solid game engine and future content to come after listening to episode #154!I immedeately enjoyed the dark theme, gritty language, thumping metal which gave me that nostalgic early teen years feeling for listening to NiN and playing Doom ][ with friendsJupiter Hell is fun. The game loop is tight and gives a feeling of control during basic gameplay.Jupiter Hell is challenging. I thought after making it to Io on my 3rd run I was close to beating it. Hours later I'm still trying! I haven't even tried all the challenge modes etc, and just now developing my strategy after mapping out the various location paths. (e.g. if I haven't found the right weapons yet, I'll avoid paths which have more robot enimies etc...)Jupiter Hell is a rogue like. Don't let the procedural graphics fool you, the tyranny of the turned base grid is *real*! I've had fun trying speed run builds as well as clearing every level slowly and methodically with minimal ammo expenditure. But always I find myself opening a door a little to close to some big bad Reavers then who cares how many health packs I've managed to horde! lol  Time to develop my "retreat" strategy w/ smoke and gas grenades...One thing that made the game much more fun for me was learning about holding down the direction keys. It wasn't obvious, but you can just hold a direction and the guy will stop upon sighting enemies. Makes it play *much* faster and less tedious than watching the top right corner of my 4k monitor to see when an enemy is sighted. I would prefer a "shift + direction" automove personally (like Nethack etc) than holding the button, as I have multiple times mis-stepped after an enemy was in range wasting a round... nitpick i know... In terms of character builds, I'm most looking forward to some sort of dual-wielding pistol mechanic, as I can see having a fast run & gun character as being great fun, firing rifles at range has worked so much better that I always skip pistols until electric damage at least...Thanks for this entertaining game that continues to evolve and push the envelope of the roguelike genre!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Jupiter Hell feels like someone's first attempt at making a video game because of how barebones everything is. This is barely a traditional Rogue-like and feels more like a cover-focused turn-based shooter. It also has almost nothing to do with its obvious inspirations and intentionally controls poorly. I am really disappointed at how little content there is (and the quality of that content) for a project that the devs proudly proclaim they have been working on for five years, including Kickstarter *and* Early Access on Steam.All of the main line DOOM games are run-and-gun (yes, even sections of 3) and yet you will get absolutely perforated fighting out of cover even on the first floor sometimes (even on Medium difficulty). Targeting is automatic by default and the only time you want to manually aim is for shooting barrels, doors, or to target specific enemies flanking your cover. Doors are also frustrating to deal with because you can't interact with them without either walking straight into them (leaving you out of cover) or shooting them open (which can alert nearby enemies). Weapons are unsatisfying to use with poor sound effects and little variety. You'll find tons of the exact same weapon littering floors with the only difference being later levels having stronger weapons of the same type scattered everywhere. Movement is tile-based as with most traditional Rogue-likes and yet there is no auto-explore, running, or stop on enemy in vision. You have to manually move one tile at a time and "running" by holding down or rapidly pressing a key can give enemies free attacks if you're not careful. Movement is also restricted to cardinal directions and diagonal movement is simulated; this means you can move diagonally in the open but it'll cost you two turns. If for some reason you try to move strictly diagonally through an area that you can't move in cardinal directions for (for example, trying to squeeze through in the cavern tile set), it'll block your movement. The controls feel like they were designed for a controller and are as simplified as possible to the detriment of the gameplay. This alone makes the game a chore to play and bad controls are reason enough for me to drop a game.Everything else I've encountered in the game is bland and unoriginal. Human enemies use the same weapons you can carry so don't expect anything flashy from them. Demons will occasionally surprise you with special attacks or zone modifiers but there's still little enemy variety. Sound effects and music all feel like stock and the graphics I guess are impressive when compared to this game's inspirations. Even then there's bad texture tiling on the floors and lighting is often too dark even with the default gamma set to +2.4. I love DOOM and traditional Rogue-likes so I thought this would be an instant classic for me. Unfortunately, because of intentional bad design choices, this was a huge disappointment on all expectations. This is honestly the worst game I've played this year and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone. The only reasons I played past the refundable two hour mark was to really give it a chance and because I could play it at work.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I have had a lot of fun with Jupiter Hell. It's very unusual to find a game with traditional roguelikes mechanics and sensibilities along with nice graphics and good action. the overall cinematic design and sound really add to the experience, while still being a slow, thoughtful game if you want to approach it that way. The game manages to modernize and streamline the roguelike experience in a way that makes it a pleasure to interact with, which is not necessarily easy. My favorite part so far is customizing different runs, and customizing your weapons on those runs. You can emphasize different parts of the game and make a character that feels different than the last time you played, which is really important for me in roguelikes.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great Rogue-like. The classes are all distinct enough to have a few unique traits and quirks so they all don't feel like carbon copies of each other. The cover mechanic and pain mechanic are also nice touches to help stand out.For those completely unfamiliar with this, it's essentially a spin-off of Rogue Doom, D**m Roguelike, or whatever else name you knew it by. Essentially, it tried to make Doom into a turn-based Rogue-like. Turns out it was so popular it became its own thing. It was popular enough to get slapped with a copyright hit but by that time the team knew they had enough on their hands to make this Jupiter Hell.Unlike many other Rogue games, this one is heavily reliant on ranged attacks as opposed to melee. In fact, at the time of this review, I don't even think player melee even exists. The weapon meta is more or less geared towards sniping stuff far away (rifles) or letting them get up close and personal (pistol, shotgun, SMG). Each build is distinctive enough to differentiate. The Scout, for example, can spec into pistols and SMG's and go for an ability that sacrifices accuracy for damage. You know going into that build that you will need to spec accuracy to make up for the range penalty of the Headshot ability. That same Scout class instead can also spec into an ability that reloads the shotguns as you move. Since you reload for free when you move, you will naturally want to spec into abilities that provide better dodge bonuses.Some neat little touches here are the fact that the game screen has a "stretched" look to it like 1980's monitors had. The game also lets you know if there are still enemies alive so you know whether or not to let your guard down.As a Rogue-like, expect to be at the absolute mercy of RNG-esus. At times you are going to be in cover and yet still getting hit. At times you are going to miss high-accuracy shots. At times you are going to open a door and have 5 or 6 baddies asking if you brought the potato salad to the potluck. At times it will feel like you did everything right and still die. Hate to say it but welcome to Rogue-likes :\By no means is this a perfect game, but it's great none the less. Kornel and his crew are still good people and I am proud to support their hard work.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: edit2: Or so I thought; there's a lot of content to this game in terms of choices you can make during a run. No doubt that what I said in the first edit sort of stands, the base weaponry and combinations are what they are - but there's new modifiers now, as well as a ton of unique items and secrets to discover. =Make no mistake, the game itself is solid - I sunk ~10 hours into it before getting bored, where it was feeling 'samey'; but now I've just played 20 hours - and am hankering for more. The updates really did a wonder on replayability and making it all more interesting/decision based across the board.Recommended it when it first released, and definitely recommending it even more with all the updates it's had - with more to come on the horizon! <3edit: After about 5 hours, you discover all the game has - and while it's cool, the content and play (mechanically) is extremely limited at the moment. I think it's a very well produced game, and certainly fun for a while - and even past that - but, I have to acknowledge that things do hit a point where they feel repetitive; no matter what you do. The three different classes help keep it fresh, but the weapons and items always being the same (with minor random modifications if you're lucky - but even then, they don't feel different - just slightly "better"), things feel same-ish. :shrug:This game is a love letter to the Doom franchise, as well as turn-based combat/board games.It's simple(y) fun....and now I'm trying to decide; another run, or sleep? It's hard to want to put this one down for the night. The game is not only great mechanically, but plays extremely smooth and quickly - but if you think there's no decision making, or depth of play here - you're sorely mistaken.There's tons of choices to be made along the way, and they all feel valid. One wrong step, one poor choice - and you're going to be in for a world of hurt. However, the same can be said for your enemies - there's a real planning and execution, to how you approach each different room; and potential position of enemies.The music is spot on too, every step of the way.+ It's a labor of love, and it shows in each and every element.+ It doesn't get bogged down in overwhelming amounts of information or variables; and all the relevant information you need is on the screen as you play. [Sure, learning what augments do on the equipment you found takes opening the inventory once or twice - but, they all make sense - and they're easy to remember].+ If Doom were a turn-based combat game, this would be it.What more do you need?Oh, and knife/melee-based builds are not only possible, they're viable.Rip and tear baby, rip and tear. <3

_childDocuments_.review: edit: The majority of my concerns are being addressed with an upcoming update, and I am switching this to a Yes. Leaving the original up though as it's a reflection of the current state of the game.Another instance where steams yes/no reviews aren't good enough. I'm going to leave this on a No to hopefully bring more attention to some massive UI issues in hopes they get fixed. But I'll likely continue to bash my head against learning the game, as I'm enjoying everything else about it.---An improvement to DoomRL in a lot of ways, streamlining a lot of tedious and awful mechanics, but it's currently plagued with some absolutely awful UI decisions, and a lot of descriptions are sorely unclear about mechanics.In my 9 hours of playtime, I've thoroughly enjoyed experimenting with the variety of classes and traits, it feels like there's a lot more cool things to work with compared to DoomRL mostly being passive buffs. But while trying to learn the game, I'm frequently running into new things that just aren't explained anywhere. This leads to some frustration as I'm forced to basically die and see what effect this unexplained mechanic is just so I can learn it and be more prepared next time. Primarily seeing this from a new enemy just added, the Warlocks, which have an aura and a status effect they put on you. They don't even exist in the games wiki site yet. The existence of these UI quirks makes sense as this was for the longest time an early access game in a niche genre, but with a proper release they desperately need to be addressed for the sake of new players trying to pick it up.A simple ingame database detailing every enemy, their stats, mechanics, status effects would ease a lot of these concerns.---In my short time playing, my personal list of grievances so far is;If you get enough mods on your armor, their descriptions take up the entire info panel, and there is no way to scroll it down to see the stats of your armor. Surely there's plenty of input space available even for controllers (hold the minimap button to modify dpad up/down to scroll?)There is no info screen detailing your stats like movement speed, dodge while moving, etc.Trait descriptions like Assassination say your dodge is maxed after using it, which can be inferred as 100% dodge but you'll frequently eat an attack from the target you use it on so the only assumption you can make is that it's taking your movement dodge %, unless there's a dodge cap that isn't explained? I'm genuinely confused on this one.Terminals that offer to repair armor say they'll repair your armor and boots, but boots aren't an armor slot in this game, helmets are, which do thankfully get repaired.Bladedancer's description says it's a master trait, but it's not and you're not locked out of picking another master trait, and it's even a requirement for one.Some enemies have two health bars, some are colored yellow, some are grey, some entities like doors have two health bars, and none of them are explained anywhere.Status effects like Chilled and Frozen aren't explained anywhere. Are they penalties to movement speed, entire action time?Late game enemies get status effects and auras that you have no way of reading what they do. Receive a new status effect? You have no information as to what it does. Enemy has an aura? You have no information as to what it does.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute gem that is frequently updated and tweaked, and for some reason somewhat overlooked.ChaosForge weren't kidding about JH being almost like chess, because this bad boy requires you to think-- and a lot at that.Jupiter Hell is essentially the most puritan rogue-like there is, with a gorgeous aesthetic and an absolute s**t-tonne of replay value. Unlike games like BoI, in JH tactics are key and adapting your build and inventory to changes during runs is absolutely essential.If you want to rush and play something fast paced, this isn't for you-- you will be slapped about and spat upon by everything you come across if you run about without any strategy or thinking behind your movements. But at the same time if you want a casual strategy experience, then this isn't for you either as you'll soon find yourself wanting to rip your hair out due to how high-octane JH can get. It perfectly blends a thinking game with 'WTF is going on' moments that I only really experienced in FPS games such as PlanetSide 2 and RTS games such as Supreme Commander 2. In short, be prepared to be swarmed from every angle, with it being your job to save yourself and beat the foes while dodging literal walls of lead flying straight at you.Again, replay value is mad. I played for around 6 hours straight after work and not only I got so immersed that when I looked at my watch it turned for 4pm, to nearly 10, but also not a single time did I get the same experience. With each run having a different layout, different weapon drops, different elevator destinations, etc. At first I didn't understand how some people have 300 hours in this game already, but I get it now. There is A LOT of content in this one, and set up in such a way that if feels even vaster than what it really is-- which is brilliant, as it means when ChaosForge will keep releasing content, it will nicely blend in adding to the whole experience. There are dozens of weapons all acting in different ways, with dozens of different mods that can be applied, with dozens of different rarities along with unique variants-- which also applies to armour pieces, relics and AMPs (augmentations). All that on top of an RPG-like perk system which one tweak and your play style can drastically change. I also love the retro Doom-like take on the world as well, with everything from the UI to special effects and colour palette reflecting that overall vibe. Huge plus in my eyes as I'm not a huge fan of the newer 'make everything blindingly blue and orange' bandwagon aesthetics that Bethesda pumped out in the past few years with their reboots.Jupiter Hell is an masterpiece at what it strove to become-- an extremely well made rogue-like, with a massive array of content, vast opportunities for replay and a sick art style to boot. Absolute must buy for anyone into rogue-likes, Sci-Fi and strategy titles. Don't get me wrong it's not for everyone, but if you think 'rouge-like with a tonne of guns, near infinite replay value set in an 1979 Alien-like universe killing the possessed and demons' sounds awesome-- get it. For 20 quid, it's an absolute no-brainer.

_childDocuments_.review: This one has more depth than at first glance. The further you go, the more enemy and loot variety you'll come across, including item rarities, effects, mods, and even "levelable" special weapons (though don't expect this to be a turn based Diablo degree of loot or anything). Gun sound effects could use more punch, imo, and the shotgun effect looks more like spraying water than a gun blast. Mouse functionality is a nice, if currently experimental, addition. Enemy pathfinding gets wonky sometimes, I occasionally see enemies "bumping" into obstacles as if they're trying to move through them rather than going around or making some other logical action. And there's a decent selection of skills to choose from.Overall I've found myself really digging it more than I thought I would. Definitely a solid recommend if you're a traditional roguelike fan, and even more so if you enjoy the Doom-like aesthetic and cheesy action movie one-liners. (One recommendation is to turn on "Entity Outline" in the options, otherwise it's easy to confuse enemies on the screen, especially on a smaller screen like on a laptop.)
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: A definitive argument against Rogue-like purists who include ASCII graphics in their list (but really, I appreciate the fidelity to an interpretation of "true rogue-like" the designers chose to keep with)It's like ADOM if ADOM were DOOM, or something. Cool idea to make a rogue-like focused on ranged combat too. Heavy metal music, demon killing, and turn-based decision making while an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ space marine yells at you to make a decision cuz he wants to get going.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Essentially a Doom-themed Traditional Roguelike. It's a very enjoyable game with good execution, but it does admittedly feel a little content-sparse. Plenty of challenges and such for completionists to be sure, but the set pieces get a little repetitive and the ways you can interact with the world seem somewhat limited. Still, worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun, challenging, strategic and addictive little game. It's turn based, essentially each action is one turn, but all enemies take their turn while you perform your action, so you almost don't notice that it's turned based. However, it does give you time to think about your action, which you will need sometimes!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Doom's fast-paced and frantic violence translates so well into a roguelike setting I can barely comprehend it. This game is hard, metal as ♥♥♥♥, and one of the best games I've played in a long time. This game has a ton of replay value which will most likely suck far to many hours out of your life than reasonable. If you like Doom or roguelikes this is a must buy! P.S. _childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Glad to finally be playing the first game I ever backed on Kickstarter.Jupiter Hell is what Doom (2016) could have been if it was:a) a rogue-like, andb) a good gameAnd ignore the devs responding to reviews drama - for a game to be this polished in Early Access, they can be as salty as they wanna be.Personally, I cannot wait to see future iterations of this shiny successor to the one true D**M.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Devs did a great job. It's obvious how much effort and love was put into this game.Game designers on the other hand failed miserably - they managed to make a classic turn based rogue-like boring as hell (no pun intended). Looks like they were trying to make it appealing to to both audiences: people who never played any old-school ASCII games and those whose nostalgia can be monetized. To me they failed in both. The key feeling of "just one another turn" isn't there, because turns don't mean anything in this game, you can think about it as an action rpg shooter with auto-pause after every shot. Just imagine this: 3rd person doom game which pauses after every single shot. That would be it. Can't stress this enough: no strategy is required (or even welcome), you don't see enemy health and you just spam shoot button until everything dies.  You can imagine how boring that becomes after the first 100 turns. It would have been WAY better as a generic action shooter (which it already is) without any turn-based mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: A well done,  turn-based, pure combat roguelike. No meta progression by design, and I'm ok with that. It's a streamlined version of DoomRL. Based on some criticisms I've seen, I think Callisto (the first area) might take a little too long to get through for some folks, so you may think you've seen everything in a couple of hours. However, if you stick with it to Europa and other levels, try different classes and master traits, and read those emails, you'll find quite a bit of depth in the gameplay. The A.I. can seem a bit simplistic but this is DOOM after all!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I stumbled across this game while looking for the game DoomRL, And while I don't think it's as good a game as DoomRL I still rate it quite highly. Unlike DoomRL this game can be played with a controller, but also unlike DoomRL you cannot move diagonally. Another thing that's different is the cover system, You'll have to get used to picking your position carefully or else you'll take lots of damage while doing very little in return.I just completed it on the easiest difficulty after about 34 hours of trying and there's still quite a way for me to go with this game. I feel the player characters comments are a little annoying, he likes to swear a lot for no apparent reason but other than that the sound is top notch.Overall I'd say 8.2/10
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: While rogue-lites have provided a fascinating bridge between the methodical rogue-likes of old and the seat-of-your-pants reactivity of contemporary games, they nevertheless lose something in that from the ways of rogue-likes. Jupiter Hell, on the other hand, takes a different approach. Instead of removing the turn-based methodical elements of rogue-likes, it removes the tedium and abstractness of it all by never keeping you waiting to perform your next action, while still having a gorgeous and fully-realized visual representation of everything that's happening in the game world. Of course, the game itself is wonderfully engaging to boot, and borrows heavily from shooters, namely in that almost all fighting is done at range, leading to an approach much more dependent on clever use of positioning and cover to stay alive...or you can spec yourself out to feed on the blood of your enemies as you hack them apart limb-from-limb with a chainsaw. It is an RPG, after all.This has become my favourite rogue-like, and I would strongly recommend it to anyone.If you like rogue-likes, or the idea of rogue-likes, but always wanted something a bit more up-to-date in design, and without the focus on melee combat, Jupiter Hell is for you. If you like rogue-lites and are curious about their genre forebears, Jupiter Hell is for you. If you just like the idea of acting out the fight scenes from Equilibrium on the rogue's gallery of Doom, Jupiter Hell is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I have no clue how this game flew under my radar until the 1.0 launch because it is so damn good. If you're unsure about liking the genre but like the idea of the game I highly recommend at least trying it. Not to be sentimental but you can feel the passion behind the game immediately. The visuals, audio (both music and effects) and gameplay are all given the love they deserve. This game is a home run on every level for me and I hope more people try it.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to wait until I had beaten this game at least once (even if it was on easy), so that I could give a fair review.  I would have played a bit more, but I think this is a critical time where there are a lot of eyes on this game since it just came out.Long story short: I really like this game and I have high hopes for its future.Long Story:I've been checking this game out for a year since I first heard of it.  The prospect of playing a doom inspired roguelike had me giddy.  I waited and waited until the 1st of August rolled around and then I eagerly jumped on steam to check it out.  The price tag of over twenty dollars had me go "oof" and I stalled for a few days trying to make a purchasing decision.  I read the reviews on here and as you can see for yourself, most of them are positive (and deservedly so), but it was not enough for a cynic like me.  I browsed around the web and I found an interview where the developer said that there will be more content in the future.  I don't know why, but it just clicked with me.  This is obviously a passion project and I want to support that; even if the price seemed steep they will be adding stuff in the future right?I bought it and got hooked right away.  *The soundtrack by Roland La Goy is awesome and I sometimes just idle in a mission to enjoy the tunes*Mark Meer is the marine's VA so that's obviously awesome!*The graphics and aesthetic are very pleasing to the eye and rumble a nostalgic feeling in meBut the gameplay is the most important part since this is a game after all and I think that they nailed it.  I've gotten hours of enjoyment from experimenting with different weapons, learning the ropes, adjusting tactics, playing with different perks, and I've only played on one of the three classes so far.If I could think of a criticism it would be how annoying it can be with the protagonist constantly shouting cheesy one liners,  but guess what?  You can adjust the profanity filter and how often the marine talks.  So my only gripe that I can think of is null.The game is exactly what I expected and I believe it is totally worth the asking price.  I look forward to future updates and kicking more demon ass!   PS: The developers are very active on the Jupiter Hell subreddit and on steam.  So if you have any questions they are totally available and I find that really cool.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice roguelike. I remember playing ADOM back in the oughts, and this reminds me of it, just with (better) graphics, doom atmosphere, and much more streamlined gameplay. These days, having way way less time to play, I don't miss a bajillion little things and skills from traditional roguelikes (bridgebuilding, sigh..). Special shoutout for amazing voice lines, that's exactly what a doom guy would say! As for negatives: - I'd say three classes is too few. I want to try more different playstyles.- Some descriptions are really nondescript, like a pistol Death that says that the thing you shoot will die. It certainly will, of old age if nothing else, but some details would be appreciated. My build was not pistol-oriented at all, and enemies were dangerous enough not to fool around and find what happens, so I skipped it.- Story is kinda murky. E.g. what exactly is Dante station? Who opened the portal to hell again, and why? Sure it's doom, so run and shoot, but I can't help wanting to know more.Still, very much worth a try for anyone who likes turn-based roguelikes and doesn't have time for old-school stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: This is a refinement of a previous game by the same team, and after playing it for a bit (and playing the original a lot) I can say it's a really darn good one. The ranged-combat-focused roguelike creates a unique gameplay feel that you won't get from anything else, and it's one that they refined to a mirror finish. The 90s-shooter aesthetic still works well. The dodge system has been simplified (to the player's benefit) and in its place is a cover system which works quite well.There's a huge variety weapons and a huge variety of character builds (each of the 3 classes has half a dozen mutually exclusive "master traits" you can steer towards, which favor different weapons or playstyles).There's also still a wide, wide variety of challenge modes, and an acheivement system. If it's anything like its predecessor those acheivements will keep scaling up to provide challenges beyond the capabilities of most human beings if you're looking for them.Overall, roguelike fans should not miss this one.

_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: In the same way that DoomRL unexpectedly won my heart from ADOM, Jupiter Hell delivers an experience that you can't expect to be as addictive and fulfilling as it is... but once you let this demon into your life you and give it a chance to grow you too will find satisfaction in the well-calculated nuance of slaying your way through a techno-organic space apocalypse with nothing to lose and so much to gain.However this game is a difficult beast to master, with many options to explore mechanically and tactically. If you cannot bear the die and repeat learning of a true roguelike, you will suffer more than your Jupiter Guy. If you're still here, buy this game, it's a diamond for those who like it rough.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the spiritual precursor to this game and was excited to see the news of Jupiter Hell coming years ago.  It did not disappoint.  I believe that this game appeals to both newcomers to the Rougelike genre who don't like a heavy burden of knowledge and also long-time veterans of the genre.  Of particular interest are the ways that you can customize your difficulty to get the experience that you want.  Do you want to win most of the time?  No problem, play on easy.  Do you want more challenge?  Keep walking up the difficulty or use challenge modes until you feel the struggle.I am also looking forward to the future game planned by the developers to make something similar that takes inspiration from the Alien movies.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Instead of playing Jupiter Hell, You could spend hundreds of hours on cookie clickers as well. But there's a definite difference of intensity and meaning behind those hours.Basically Jupiter Hell Guy is a marine who thought that waiting for other's turns on XCOM was wasting his life, and started his own private alien slaughtering business on his own terms. While the game is turn/cover based firearms fighting, the game eats and animates commands so quickly and smoothly, that you could think JH is real time action.Mix in three different character background selections with numerous unique perks and builds, random generated maps, tough but fair difficulty, huge amount of weapon types, armours, modding capabilities threats and challenges on a very painstakingly balanced. Once you get the hang of it, this game starts to drain hours and hours.This game takes the legacy of DoomRL and rocketjumps it to my personal hall of fame.

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game.  The new update has made it even better.   Worth every penny.  If you play other roguelikes you know how frustrating it can be to get deep into the game and have to start over.  With Jupiter Hell your average run is only going to take 30 minutes to an hour so it's a lot easier to swallow when you die.  This game is not about being so complex as a game like DCSS or Nethack.  That said there is a lot more going on than is apparent at 1st and the game does have depth and strong tactical decisions to be made.  I think it would make a great 1st game for a player interested in the genre or an old pro.  Get it.

_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: . I am what you might call a professional reviewer. Jupiter Hell is a turn-based shooter from the depths of cosmic hell and I hope I can give you some insight into why this is one of the most original (and not to mention best looking) releases I've played in years.Much like in what other games have called "nightmares" and "drifting planes of nothingness" I spend much of the first few hours of Jupiter Hell playing this game entirely alone, and it's strange how time seems to fly by when you are enjoying yourself. Jupiter Hell is nothing like any game I've ever played and that's something that I'm really appreciating.Let me just say this from the get-go: Jupiter Hell is a masterpiece, and it's very hard to describe how brilliant it is, but if I were you, I'd at least drop everything you're doing to check out a demo. Just try it once. You won't regret it.***Do you hear what I hear? One of my favorite composers in gaming, Koji Kondo, has composed the score for Jupiter Hell, and I can confirm that it's nothing short of incredible. All the music in the game is a showcase for the genius that is Kondo. Even the background music is fittingly moody, creepy and tense. It's just all so incredibly stunning.It may not have been intended, but the music in Jupiter Hell perfectly compliments the gameplay. I was going to describe some of the themes in the game in this review, but there are simply too many to write about all at once. But I will say this: there is a track called "Prayer for Light" that will take your breath away. It has a truly haunting theme with some heavy bass and powerful drums.Anyway, this is game is what you would call a "rogue lite," meaning it is annoying to play if you want to make progress or not. The enemies come out in waves and they're pretty weak so you just do what the green-haired, shirtless demon hands you. In fact, much of what you need to know to win this game is already in the game, if you look hard enough, so I'll try to summarize some of the elements of the gameplay.The controls are fairly simple, but not nearly as simple as anything out there. You move and aim with the D-pad. Your basic movement direction changes when you take cover behind something, but the placement of cover makes movement in multiple directions a bit more.Part two of my review coming soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Just giving a heads up first that controller support does work. When I launched the game, it did not detect my controller at first. I turned off Steam Input and then it works fine. I guess the game probably has native controller support that doesn't play nice with Steam Input. My entire playtime is with an Xbox controller.I've never played DRL before, but I have tons of experience with other Roguelikes or Roguelites. As far as turn based games go, Jupiter Hell is very fast paced. What I mean is that you don't need to navigate menus for most of your actions be it moving or shooting - you perform them instantly with a press of a button (or combination of buttons). You also don't need to wait for your enemies' turn, since everyone moves simultaneously at the same time. This removes the tedium of waiting in turn based games, and it feels super refreshing to be constantly in the thick of things.As a roguelike, there is no progression and successful runs only rewards you with higher difficulties and unlocks challenges. Your only progression is your deeper knowledge of the game. It took me around 6 hours (including failed runs) for my first completion on the easiest difficulty, and it was a blast. There are also other classes to choose from, and many different weapons and perks to try out so the replayability is there.The atmosphere is great and I especially love the BGM. I never tire of it even when it's played on a loop. Jupiter Hell makes me feel like I'm playing a stop motion version of Doom. This is a real gem and I highly recommended it, even for the "modern" players who think turn based games are slow and tedious.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I really had high hopes for this game, but I'd really just recommend anyone who is interested play DRL instead.I find myself missing many of the things that made DRL special like, destructible terrain, alternate fire modes, assemblies, hazardous terrains, and the ability to carry around gear in inventory.  It feels really samey with all of that stuff stripped out.  This game still has stuff to offer, I like the changes to Traits and the utility slots, DRL had problems but this trade off doesn't feel worth it.I'm definitely not a fan of the new inventory stuff, it seems too cramped, like I can't carry around a lot of the more fun consumables without being at risk of running low on ammo, which leads to me just using the same weapon or two for every encounter, which is a shame cause a lot of the new consumables are really fun.This is more subjective, but I really wish things were more distinct sometimes, a lot of the humanoid enemies look similar but the different weapons they can sport can really screw you up, something that was never a problem with the distinct colorful sprites in DRL.  This game feels best when played at a higher speed, but the visuals are often too dark and muddled to make out clearly (even after you turn off the screen effects).  I also think that the item floor icons would benefit from some borders and heightened contrast.  On brighter floors they can blend into the floor and be harder to make out.I hope this game continues to improve, maybe one day I'll come back to it and be pleasantly surprised.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: I love the idea behind this but far too much falls into RNG. Every attack (except for a couple of explosives) are hitscan. Taken from its boomer-shooter roots, enemy shots should be projectiles so you at least can dodge them and be presented a choice: stand and shoot or move the character to dodge? Instead it's just a couple of dice rolls until someone falls. It just doesn't feel fun. Heck, even dodging is only accomplished by moving the character where you only receive a dodge percentage and another RNG opportunity. There really isn't a trade off between moving to dodge since the enemy is just going to shoot again.It's a hardcore rogue-like so, in theory, the runs should probably last a couple of levels and you die or reach the end in maybe half an hour. But in reality it's something like 18 levels and my game winning run on easy took something like 3 hours to complete, and since it took about +2 hours to just reach the 12th level, the game will just wipe your save and you need to restart.Rogue-likes usually will have some sort of mechanic that, through playing the game, you improve your initial start with better stats, better unlocked gear, or starting later in the dungeon trek (reach level 10 to unlock level 8 start and a basic loadout). Instead it's just level 1 again with a pistol.It's very disappointing overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like roguelikes? Do you like making meaningful decisions at almost every step you take? Then this is the game for you.Jupiter Hell does what many other games (even some of the greats of the genre) lack: it presents you with a number of options and expects you to (almost) always pick the best one to succeed. This might sound stressful, but believe me, it isn't. The way the game flows and how the gameplay loop (shoot, duck behind cover, move carefully) works, guarantees that the precise decision making expected of you to win a run will lead to a plethora of adrenaline packed situations which play out in seconds and - even though the game is turnbased - will feel like an action movie.There are 3 classes, each of them with a number of skills and "master traits", which basically function like subclasses as you can only pick one on each character and they significantly change how your run will play out. There's also a good variety of guns, melee weapons (although keep in mind that ranged combat is the focus of the game!), relics, exotics and special levels to find and explore.I could go on about how there's also terminals to hack, mods for your weapons, trials and challenges etc. but others have done that in great detail already.If you're a fan of roguelikes (no unlocks in this one that make your character stronger, only additional difficulty levels, trials and challenges) you definitely need to try this. I never thought I could love a game as much as I loved ADOM back in the good old days, but Jupiter Hell might be a strong contester for my personal #1 in the genre.Buy it now!
_childDocuments_.name: Jupiter Hell
