_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: The Metroidvania genre has been highly over-saturated for years ever since the release of Hollow knight. Many of them are simply ok, boasting the exact same upgrades and mechanics that Metroid and Castlevania created in the first place. Hollow Knight did a good job modernizing it but there haven’t been that many games that actually innovate anything in the genre considerably. It’s the same double jump, dash, grapple hook, type mechanics over and over again. Even the environments in many of these games are just the same damn thing over and over. It’s made the genre quite boring because every new game follows a very rigid formula. Obviously there are exceptions such as Ori or Blasphemous but most of these smaller indie Metroidvanias just aren’t unique. I can gladly say Animal Well is the best Metroidvanias to come out this year. The world is unique and vibrant. The cat chases are genuinely terrifying and the vibe of the game is just perfect. The mechanics and Items are all extremely unique, It's just a fun game. The best part is how non-linear it is. Most other Metroidvanias run on a lock and key system where you gain an Item that lets you progress further down one specific hallway. The problem that often occurs is that players forget or can’t find which hallway or room they need to use their new item on to progress, leading to hours and hours of backtracking. Other games such as Metroid Dread solve this by locking players into smaller areas or chunks of the map where they aren’t able to backtrack and waste as much time. Animal Well doesn’t really run into this issue however, sure you’ll hit some dead ends but all the necessary items to beat the game are available right at the start. Hell every area can be tackled in whatever order you want. It feels more open world than Metroidvania. I would say this is where the game definitely shines the most, the exploration, amazing puzzles, great score, and dark vibe.Animal Well does suffer from one flaw however (spoilers ahead), All that to say, aside for my one gripe, this is a great game. Anyone who likes Metroidvanias or wants to give the genre a try, this is a must play.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: 1 ½ cups (150g) graham cracker crumbs (about 10-12 full crackers)¼ cup (50g) granulated sugar½ cup (115g) unsalted butter, melted4 (8 oz) packages cream cheese, softened to room temperature1 cup (200g) granulated sugar1 cup (240g) sour cream, room temperature1 tsp vanilla extract3 large eggs, room temperatureOptional Toppings:Fresh berries (strawberries, blueberries, raspberries)Whipped creamCaramel or chocolate saucePreheat your oven to 325°F (163°C).In a medium bowl, combine graham cracker crumbs, sugar, and melted butter. Stir until the mixture resembles wet sand.Press the crust mixture into the bottom of a 9-inch (23cm) springform pan, using a measuring cup or flat-bottomed glass to pack it down firmly.Bake for 8-10 minutes, then remove and let it cool while you prepare the filling.In a large mixing bowl, beat the cream cheese and sugar together until smooth and creamy, about 2-3 minutes.Add the sour cream and vanilla extract, and mix until just combined.Add the eggs one at a time, mixing on low speed after each addition until just blended (don’t overmix to avoid cracks in the cheesecake).Pour the filling over the cooled crust and smooth the top with a spatula.Place the cheesecake pan on a baking sheet. (Optional: Place a pan of water on the lower rack to add moisture to the oven, helping to prevent cracks).Bake for 60-70 minutes or until the edges are set but the center is slightly jiggly.Turn off the oven, crack the door slightly, and let the cheesecake cool in the oven for 1 hour (this gradual cooling helps prevent cracks).After it has cooled, remove the cheesecake from the oven and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.Before serving, release the cheesecake from the springform pan.Add toppings if desired and slice into pieces with a warm knife (wipe the knife between cuts for clean slices).The cheesecake should be creamy and smooth, with a deliciously buttery crust and perfectly balanced sweetness.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game, exploration and puzzles are great. Lots of post-game content to keep you engaged long after the credits roll. I don't really have any big problems with the game at all, the only small gripe is that there is no key rebinding and the controls for keyboard suck, so you're pretty much forced to play with a controller.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well is fantastically creative as a Metroidvainia - there's a multitude of unlocks to help you traverse the map in new ways, however not one of them is a dash, double jump, or anything so mundane. You'll be getting new traversal methods all the way through completing the main "story", and the surprise of what new oddball trinket you'll get and puzzling out all the ways to use it is great.The post-game is extensive - and by and large great, though not without flaws. Without treading into ARG territory, there are 64 secret eggs to chase after. Most of these are fine, and I had a lot of fun chasing after them. There's a great puzzle difficulty curve - some of the endgame egg unlocks are combining all of your tools together in pretty satisfying ways.... but. The number of times you'll have to retread the map gets excessive. Really, excessive. Later unlocks become increasingly niche - you go from getting upgrades that can be used in nearly every single room to getting something whose sole purpose is unlocking 3 eggs tucked away in far corners of the map. So you'll end up retreading the entire map 4-5 times in the late game as you're drip-fed these last few upgrades, just spamming your new toy in hopes of finding one of the last few needles in the haystack.Definitely play, but maybe don't be shy to look at a map as you're creeping up to 15, 20 hours. There's an excellent spoiler-free map in the community guides.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great. The base game is just a cool experience of a metroidvania, but for those looking for a extra challenge, there are puzzles lining the map that are complex and rewarding to solve, with multiple ending for the deeper you go.This game was a adventure to play and I recommend new people coming into it to not watch any guides!
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: As a big Metrovania fan....I didn't enjoy this game....tbh, the game is pretty good. Puzzles are very clever, artstyle are unique, secrets well hidden, until you hit the unavoidable backtracking plateau, as the nature of a metrovania game.And naturally, when you hit a plateau, you open the map try to figure out where you haven't been in such game. But the amount of puzzles.... almost every single room has a puzzle, and a lot of them are well hidden. This made the backtracking extremely tedious.Usually, in a metrovania game's backtracking, you got to use all these new abilities dashing through the old stages, this offsets a lot of the tediousness and gives you a sense of progression.But not in animal well, your new abilities rarely have any effect on your traversal, and unreached path/puzzles are in every corner of the map. My speed of traversing literally have 0 improvement even tho I unlocked most of the items.For people who has a lot of time and energy to invest, this is probably a god tier game just based on sheer number of well hidden puzzles.But for me...I just can't take it man. I don't want walk the whole map 10th time on the same speed of game start.And the thing is, I don't even consider myself a "casual gamer".... I 100% every single metrodvania game I have played, except Hollow Knight cuz it involves speed running.Or maybe I'm just getting old...
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This game doesn't hold your hand. I mean this in a good way. I figured out a few movement mechanics that basically changed how I approached the game. I thought that I got my hand on a new exploit since so much of the platforming became so easy, only to be greeted with pretty difficult puzzles/platforming specifically tailored to said mechanics. I wouldn't have discovered these without it. Very clever!For a platformer, the controls feels incredibly responsive and has a good game-feel. I like the vibration feedback that I get from the controller.Ya made a great game, Billy and Jason/Dunkey.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Quickly became my favourite puzzle platformer, had fun all the way through while completing the 100% as well. Mechanics are super fun if that's your thing, and secrets are well hidden but not so hard that you wouldn't ever find them without a wiki. The eerie atmosphere created some tense moments, I just loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Animal well, was my first well type game.It is also the first real puzzle game I have ever played.It has been an unforgettable experience. First of all. You SHOULD NOT play this game for the insane puzzles that frequent the internet, Don't look up any guides, you are doing yourself a disservice.YOU SHOULD play this game because it is a master crafted learn-by-doing experience. Everything you do feels earned, every puzzle and every platforming sequence. The thrill of finally cracking what the game wants you to do or where you need to go is indescribable.All the tools you gain throughout the game are tailor-made for tinkering with how you want to approach each puzzle.The animals are amazing! They are scary, derpy, cute, weird and many other acronyms I currently can't think of, My personal favorites are the ostrich, kangaroo and the Dachshund.     Do not feel frustrated about puzzle's you don't crack, revel in those you do!All in all an amazing experience, highly recommend it, even for players with little puzzle game experience.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This game is ~INTERESTING~  It feels and plays like the best parts of other metroidvania games, but without the worst parts.  About an hour in you hit your first "okay, I need the double jump to get up there".  You expect to find some boots, a feather, or some tired & overused item.  You get a bubble wand instead. There's no story, no dialogue, just you exploring this world and solving puzzles.  One puzzle leads to the next, it all feels so fluid and organic.  That feeling you get when you're 75% way through a jigsaw puzzle or crossword.  Finding the next piece or word is made easier, because of your efforts. You get that this entire game. The graphics are great, the sound design is amazing, the gameplay is great. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy metroidvania games with a TON of hidden secrets and puzzles, definitely pick up this game. The "first" ending is short, it took me ~5 hours to get it, but there's so much in the game that I haven't even scratched the surface on.The soundtrack and art style are also phenomenal, creating a wonderful atmosphere that's mysterious and spooky.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an onion.  Don't believe anyone who says it's just a short, fun, little metroidvania.  I'm not a completionist, but I am the type of player that will keep trying to solve mysteries to tie up loose ends.  If this is you, prepare to fall deep, deep down the well.  It might not be bottomless, but they still haven't found the bottom yet (at least according to  Some of the puzzles could be signposted better, so even the most dedicated will probably have to start looking stuff up.  But when they land they're really satisfying.For fans of Fez, Tunic and good metroidvanias.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: It took me 6 hours to beat this game and then 14 hours later, I finally put it down. What started as a quirky metroidvania pulled me in deeper as I peeled back the layers until my second monitor was drowning in half jotted notes and my in-game map looked like I was writing a manifesto. When my brain was completely fried and I needed to look up answers, the game was still engaging enough for me to see the puzzles through to the end. Please give this passionate little game the chance to charm you! And make sure you have a printer.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of puzzle games and metroidvanias, and there really isn't a lot of overlap (at least to the degree I would like) in those two game genres. If I had to describe the game that this game reminded me of most, it felt like a 2D Tunic. Honestly starting out I was underwhelmed; I didn't know what I was doing and while nothing about the game was bad or going wrong, I felt like I wanted more. Then I found something I missed. Then I figured out a new way to move around. Suddenly I was finding things everywhere.This game scratched the itch that Tunic left after finishing it; I love exploring areas with new items, either gear or knowledge, that opens up things I hadn't seen before. Finding the layers to peel back on each visit was super satisfying. Definitely recommend if you liked Tunic, if you are looking for a straightforward metroidvania you'll get one but probably won't be the most satisfied.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Yeahhhhh... I didn't read anything about this game (only heard it got high reviews) before playing it. It looked like a great indie metroidvania. But it's more than just a metroidvania and that wasn't clear.This is an "arg" game with "arg puzzles", a term I've never heard of. I did play some of Tunic, but didn't get very far and didn't come back to it. The game doesn't make it clear that it has arg puzzles in it and that is the main reason I don't recommend playing this game, I felt like it wasted so much of my time before I eventually gave up and looked stuff up online and realized I could not have solved a lot of puzzles on my own by design. Which makes a puzzle game pointless IMO. Since you're just looking it up and doing what a guide tells you.I get the concept, it's interesting, it's kind of like a multiplayer single player game. And yeah it's kind of like a real time thing, when it first came out, if you were on Discord solving it with the community, sure that might be fun, but that's not what I want. And if the game had made that clear, I probably would not have bought it. The other issue is the game conditions you into thinking that you can solve all the puzzles by yourself, there is little to no indications that some puzzles are arg puzzles. The arg puzzles are intertwined with the single player puzzles, so that's a problem.It really sucks to spend hours to try and solve something just to find out it's not solvable by you alone. I feel scammed in that way. I found the game to be pretty pretentious in this way.The metroidvania portion of the game is just mid. It's got nice pixel graphics, but that seems par for the course these days as that's made easier by modern game dev frameworks, etc. The items are interesting and unique and not what you expect, so that's refreshing. But other than that, not sure I can even recommend this game even if you like arg puzzles, since most (?) of them have already been solved by the community, so you kind of missed the boat to participate in them?At least getting all the achievements do not require solving all the arg puzzles or speed running the game, which is nice.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I used to play Metroid games like it was heroin so another puzzle filled big map to explore is always welcome. Lots of secrets to find - still haven't solved it all yet. Highly recommend that you start taking notes from the very beginning of play so you're not going "Where the heck did I see that duck statue?" 10 hours after you passed it.

_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Great style and overall gameplay. The attention to detail and fantastic vibe that Billy Basso put his heart and soul into really show throughout this artwork. The exploration is enjoyable, the areas unique, and the animal encounters are so much fun. Each is different, one even managed to scare the ♥♥♥♥ out of me lol. I am nowhere near finding all the secrets (that we know of rn), but I am eagerly wondering through areas trying out new things, and I feel rewarded when I think of my own solution to a problem. The puzzles were enough to stump me for a bit, but never so frustrating that I wanted to put it down (tho once or twice I did need to look something up--more cause my own lack of observation). I plan to put many more hours into this game and I am more than happy with my 25$ spent.Its like Halo 2 meets Halo 3 ♥

The secrets were super fun to find and most of them were really well hidden (some of them are just almost impossible without insane amounts of outside perspective). The rush I got when i figured out new uses for items that I thought could only do one thing is indescribable. _childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This game reminds me of those old 8-bit computer games like Jet Set Willy, where to get an idea of what's going on and what you are supposed to do you must first explore the game world, attempting to uncover its many secrets. And Animal Well it's all about the joy of discovery. What counts here isn't just getting to the end, but also paying attention to the little details you're likely to miss. Billy Basso should be very proud of his effort: this game is one of the finest indie Metroidvanias ever made, and without a doubt one of the most unique, with a distinct dream-like, sometimes unsettling atmosphere. Basso also deserves credit for cramming such a game in just 30 megabytes... now that's what I call optimization!
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I've seen a metroidvania yet that, on the surface, plays fairly normally and easily, all the way to the credits but can, by and far, exceed the depth of La Mulana 1 and 2 combined.  Like getting all the achievements, which includes getting the "true" ending is just the beginning of the rabbit hole on how deep this goes.  But it's also a perfectly good time to stop playing if you don't want to invest in that, and you'd still come away from a complete fulfilling experience.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little puzzle-platformer that reminds me of the Alwa games. There's only a handful of items but they all have various clever interactions. Plenty of timing-based puzzles but nothing I've run into that requires serious reflexes yet, having picked up one of the four Major MacGuffin items. The game is extremely forgiving about saving progress even through death, which is good, because it's also very, very easy to die - sometimes a lot! ...but it's also often the case that if you're dying a lot, there's an easier way to do what you're trying to do. All in all: a delight. If you enjoyed the Alwa's games or Environmental Station Alpha, give this a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Hands down one of the best games I have ever played in my life.  I've beat anywhere from 5-20 games a year or so for the past 14 years.  This game is worth your time, and then some.  If you're a fan of metroidvanias like Ori, Shadow Complex etc and love to explore and discover and have a natural sense of progression I cannot think of a better game then this.  This game is the epitome of "a-ha" moments.  Don't get this game if you absolutely need combat.  There really isn't any but there are enemies you encounter that you need to deal with using your brain and the tools your given.I cannot recommend this game enough!!!
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Animal well is okay, but probably not worth it at full price for any non-collector gamer. Playing this game to the initial "end" is about 5 hours of pretty interesting metroidvania-esque platforming and puzzle solving. There's a bunch of secret collectibles and a really interesting meta easter egg that was fun to watch people figure out , but realistically is not something obtainable for an average gamer.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well is a must play.A fascinating entry into the metroidbrainia genre of games. If you enjoyed TUNIC, Animal Well is the perfect game for you. I implore everyone to take as blind of a dive as you can into this game, and experience it for yourself. You will find yourself coming back more and more after the credits roll to uncover the REAL secrets of the well. _childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I agree with many negative reviews. Visual is astounding, very polished and nice aesthetic. I've played a lot of metroidvania in my life of different complexities and subgenres. But there's nothing I dislike more than being forced to “learn the hard way” without explaining any of the initial mechanics, none. It's frustrating to spend time learning the basics without any reward being that the challenge should be the puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well is made by someone who appreciates the medium of video games, instead of turning it into something else. It is not a game that it filled with endless cutscenes that takes control from the player, or a ton of expository dialogue and tutorials that take away from pacing and suppresses your sense of discovery. It is a game that starts abruptly, you were asleep and now you're awake. It lets you take in the surroundings as you go, figuring out how to navigate as well as make sense of it. As you progress, it provides you with tools without offering any explanations of what you're supposed to use them for, which encourages experimentation and using your imagination to come up with different ways to use them, it feels really good whenever you discover a creative use for a tool and seeing what you were imagining was gonna happen when you use it that way actually happen.The game is beautiful, it is filled with little details and sounds that add so much to the immersion, the choice not to include much music and instead letting you hear all of the subtle and the less subtle sounds was really effective in allowing you to lose your self in the moment. In your time in the well you will find moments of beauty, peace, anxiety, joy and horror. Each element of the game blends together really well to create a really memorable experience. I haven't gone into detail about the specifics of the gameplay because in this type of game, figuring out gameplay mechanics is a huge part of it and it really should be experienced instead of just explained to you, as a video game should be. thank you reggie for this wonderful game, I can't wait to see what you come up with next

_childDocuments_.review: Animal well is a welcome game in the vein of games like La Mulana. I think it's an excellent one and well worth the price.What I enjoy most about the game is the complete lack of narrative. You really can go anywhere and get any item first. You will hit a roadblock in one corner of the map and receive an item in another that solves it. I like that there's no hand holding.The puzzles can be cryptic, but not indecipherable or requiring you to figure out what some note said like in other games.  It is amazing visually, the music and sound design is very enjoyable, and I love that there are tons of secret things to find.

_childDocuments_.review: It really is like Halo 2 meets Halo 3. Jokes aside, it's a pretty solid Metroidvania, I'm an avid fan of the genre and most of the new games tend to be too obvious or show too little and this game manages to make the gameplay mechanics simple so anybody can understand them and yet manages to make interesting puzzles, while secrets or hidden paths can still be easily recognized by just looking at the terrain.Also a huge plus for me was the lack of comba twhile still being able to receive damage, since the focal point of the game is it's puzzles but you can still screw up and have to go back to a check point, so you get punished for not thinking what you're doing.I have been progressing steadily through the game for two hours and I still feel pretty lost and that's a good sign of a good Metroidvania, since I have probably need to backtrack a little to remember where can I use a new "power-up" instead of going in a straight line only using the newest item adquired to solve everything.10/10, a pretty funny marketing campaing for an excellent game.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Reminds me of Fez. Good, but at a certain point it stops being a puzzle platformer and starts being a collaborative ARG, for better or for worse. Would still recommend. Maybe wait for a sale.The base-game is fairly short. 6-9 hours depending on how quick you play. The brunt of the content is in secret/post-game. A most of it is reasonable enough to figure out on your own, but is at least one post-game puzzle that is literally impossible to solve without outside help and a few more that rely on randomness or leaps in logic that rely on the fact that with the number of players playing the game somebody's going to stumble upon the answer. This might intrigue you, but for me, the core gameplay left a little to be desired and made the prospect of backtracking around and figuring out some of these more esoteric late-game puzzles a chore. Ultimately this means that the final puzzles aren't necessarily there for everyone to solve on their own, but to solve as a collaborative effort from the community as a whole. This isn't inherently a problem but it does make it tough when you aren't sure if a puzzle is something you can solve on your own or something you'd want to look up to save yourself the leaps of faith. I'd say about 3/4ths of the content is reasonable, even easy, but then 1/4th ranges from challingengly difficult puzzles that span the whole map to lucky-shot solutions with little to no hints or indications pointing towards them. Some of these puzzles are fun, some I wouldn't even call puzzles. If this would ruin it for you and you'd prefer a game with deep secrets and a 'hidden' late-game/post-game that you can actually find on your own and puzzles you can actually solve without outside help I'd recommend something like Hollow Knight or Environmental Station Alpha instead. Still a solid play, though, but maybe worth waiting until it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well takes a peculiar approach to the metroidvania genre. There are no combat per say but there are lots of ennemies to defeat, sneak past to, run from or simply outwit. Most of the game revolves arround solving puzzles to unlock new tools and progress further into the world. Those tools are incredibly original and have several clever ways to be used. However nothing is ever directly teached to you. The game does a perfect job of always putting you in a new situation and letting you figure out what to do with your current tools. Everytime you get stuck and think to yourself "Did I just softlock myself ?", you will find a new way to use something you already have and it is tremendously satisfying. The game world is simply gorgeous, it is eerie and hauntingly beautiful. The subtle soundtrack blends perfectly with the visuals and it's a pleasure to explore and discover new areas. The main "questline" last about 7-8h and is well worth getting the game for. However if you're the completionist kind of person and enjoy unravelling all the secrets hidden within a game then you're in for a hell of a ride.Without spoiling, once you finish the game, there are several "obvious" objectives you can challenge yourself to. They will lead you down a deep, deep, deeeeeeeeeeeeeep rabbit hole. People reference Tunic and Fez for good reasons. The game takes direct influence from those game for the scale of their Meta Puzzles and the sheer madness required to unlock everything the game has to offer. This is not my cup of tea but once I finished the game I took great pleasure in looking up guides online and watching people figure stuff out. Well worth checking out.This is a work of love and it shows all the way through.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Cruised through the main game in a few days, which I don't often do. That's a true testament to the game's quality, that you feel like coming back to it each day to try something new at the latest part you're stuck on. It's a game you think about while not playing it and then boot it up and sink a few hours into it until you're finished. Playing through this game at the same time as one of my good friends and excitedly discussing secrets, trading tips, and wondering what was to come made me feel like a kid all over again in a way that most games nowadays don't. Beautifully made, super fun and occasionally frustrating, but above all, inspiring.

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well invites you into a deep, labyrinthine world of exploration, where an ever-expanding toybox of tools helps you navigate its intricate secrets. There’s no combat; instead, the tools you find assist you in further exploration and help you avoid danger. While it may appear on the surface to be a simple puzzle-platformer, the deeper you delve into its mysteries, the more layers there are to uncover.With its stunning pixel art, the game is a delight to explore. Even after completing the main story, Animal Well offers plenty to do, revealing its true depth. Its densely packed with secrets that remain consistently engaging...just when you think you’ve uncovered everything the game surprises you with yet another layer. If you’re like me and craving a new FEZ-like experience, I highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: When I bought the game for $25, I was hoping for more than just a few hours of playtime, especially since $25 can be a bit pricey for a short indie game. I saw a funny comment on Reddit saying I took my time and reached the first ending and the credits-roll at around 12 hours of playtime. Some people have done it in 5-6 hours, so if you're just aiming for the initial "main" ending of the game, the game does indeed seem expensive. The achievements don't help much since most are easy to get before reaching this point (except for one that needed an extra 5 minutes of gameplay on a new save-file ).However, the first ending does not mark a particular end-point in both the Lore and in answering many of the mysteries of the game, hence why I put  in quotation marks. The only thing that suggests this is an ending are the credits. For this reason, continuing with the game past the credits feels very natural, as it also unlocks a few new areas (but also reveals many inaccessible ones) leaving you wondering what can be done to achieve them. I finally got what I believe is the true ending after about 60 hours of playtime. This makes the first credit-roll feel slightly confusing but also understandable, since the other "layers" of the game require a bit more willpower. Also, I did check Reddit and YouTube for help with some puzzles, which would otherwise add at least another 10 hours of playtime if I'd have tried to solve them all by myself.The puzzles and mysteries of the game are extreme, and if everyone who played the game was a casual like me, we would take years if not decades of figuring many of them out. However, I believe the devs slightly underestimated how far people are willing to go to figure something out, and the manpower of Discord- and Reddit-like communities made some amazing discoveries, with another couple hundreds of theories still on the table. As I said above, the first ending left me with more questions than when I started the game and I simply wanted to go for more. The game then also introduces some ARG puzzles and I became even more amazed.The puzzles and 101%-ing of the game do not feel forced like in some other games (I am looking at you, Psychonauts 1 - collecting hundreds of randomly scattered stickers was not fun). In Animal Well, I am actually solving puzzles for most of the things I try to obtain. I do wish, however, that the game stretched out its achievements to cover some of the later parts of the game, and not just the first few hours. I think hunting difficult achievements in a game like this could be a lot of fun.There is zero combat in the game (although you have to defeat enemies using different means) and so for people who like non-combat platformers filled with a lot of puzzles and find games like Hollow Knight overwhelming, this hits the spot perfectly.  Personally, the game is so much fun and longer than it appears to be. I am at 60+ hours and still don't know what the actual true ending is. Some people say the game starts after the first credit roll, but the game may be difficult to people not experienced with easter-egg hunting. Achievements are very easy to achieve and feel slightly disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well is an absolute gem! From the moment I started playing, I was drawn into its beautifully atmospheric world, full of charm and mystery. The art style is stunning, with its soft, glowing visuals and intricate environments that make every corner of the game a delight to explore.What really stands out is how immersive the experience is The sense of discovery is constant you never quite know what you're going to find next. The puzzles are engaging and well-balanced, and there's an incredible satisfaction in uncovering the game's secrets. The sound design is fantastic too, with subtle audio cues that enhance the feeling of being part of this unique world.The game play is soothing but also rewarding, with a great pace that keeps you hooked without overwhelming you.It's the perfect mix of relaxation and challenge. Plus, the attention to detail in the world-building shows the developer's dedication and love for the project.Overall, Animal Well offers a peaceful yet intriguing experience that I can’t recommend enough. If you love atmospheric games with a strong sense of discovery, this is definitely one to add to your library!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a life long Metroidvania fan, and this is easily one of the best I've ever played.  The game is CHARMING and ORIGINAL from start to finish.  The wonderful sense of exploration and connection never stops.  In fact the more time you spend in the world, the more interconnected you realize it all is.  This is truly an original game.  Sure it's a Metroidvana to the bone, but it does so many new things in that framework it feels different than anything I've ever played.  The puzzles are unique.  The tools (you dont really get weapons in this game) are different than anything I've ever used, and all of them have several uses.  Each time you figure out another function of one of your tools it's a eureka moment.  This all spurs interactions with the world and your enemies that play by their own rules.  Figuring out the rules and how the world works for yourself is as rewarding a thing as I have ever experienced in a video game.There are so many layers to the game, and the puzzles go almost literally as deep as you want to go with them.  For some, I'm sure they will go too deep, 98% of gamers wont find all of them without help from the community.  I think the Billy Brasso the sole dev made a bold choice there, but it works for this game.   It feels in keeping with the deep and layered nature of the puzzles and secrets.  That said, in a game as original as Animal Well is, where expanding your understanding of the game world, is such a key part of the experience.  Forcing players to search online sets players up for a minefield of spoilers.  Google at your own risk!The graphics are as beautiful as pixel art can get and the music and sounds are absolutely haunting.  The vide of this world is second to none.  Cloudpunk is one of my favorite games ever just to soak in the atmosphere, and the world of Animal Well is every bit as comforting to be in.  I love this game, I paid full price for it, and I got every penny's worth out of my purchase.  I am one ecstatic gamer.  Animal Well gets an almost unqualified recommendation.  Some of the platforming can be quite challenging and the puzzles go so deep completionists might also get frustrated if you don't want help from the community.  Bravo, and thank you to Billy Basso this is one of the best games of all time.

_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: A standout among metroidvainia platformers, Animal Well captivates with its unique tools and abilities, obsessive attention to detail, and sheer number of puzzles. This game is made for players who want to be rewarded for combing over every aspect of the environment, and discover how to apply a wide variety of abilities, that seem simple on the surface, to solve a variety of interesting challenges. Everything that looks conspicuous likely hides some kind of puzzle, and almost every puzzle has enough clues to solve it without looking the solution up () The visuals and sound design fit the world well, and the retro scanlines effect gives the game a unique look.If you're not the type of person who enjoys collectathon games, or likes all the mechanics of a game spelled out, this game probably isn't for you.

_childDocuments_.review: It doesn't reinvent the metroidvania/puzzle exploration genre wheel at all like some are saying, however it's quite good. The atmosphere is particularly good with a rare case of a well implemented scan line filter. The audio comes in clutch too, however the "main jingle" playing randomly is weird, I'm not sure how that fits. It respects your time for the most part except for when it doesn't want to, like in particular boss/chase scenes, and the odd case of a particular aim/jump/speed dexterity requirement, or hiding something in a cheap way. What I really liked is the playful aspect of some of the tools, solutions, designs, better to say less about this than to spoil the possible fun/things to gaze at away, and that it can be quite genuinely scary. Getting roughly 20 "optional" calcium carbonate :) items, almost all traversal/puzzle tools, 3 map tools, about 5 "candles", about 2 fast travel locations missed in 12 hours, that's not bad value. That means there's still a lot of nooks left in the mostly discovered map, and 12 hours for a run blind seems good in a -vania basically guideless (couldn't tell a secondary use of the "varia suit" lantern at the end) It is a title that's very much worth playing, the little details are mostly here, you get rewarded for noticing the little things, and creativity / sequence breaking is possible. I adore the art and hope to see more metroidvanias stylised like this.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, well, well, they really made Animal Well well. An instant classic.Very rarely is a game so well made, so intricately designed, so passionately crafted and so carefully presented in layers upon layers of revelation that exploration evokes pure joy in in spite of a complete lack of exposition, dialogue or hand holding. Animal Well is such a game.The soundscape drips with liveliness amidst an atmosphere of eerie mystique. Discovery is a delight as "death" is not punished; the map is astonishingly vast, the mechanics are novel and diverse. There's surprise and there's awe. The art is an impeccable amalgamation of retro pixels and modern smokiness.All of this in 34 MBs and from one single dev. Billy Basso - hats off, genuinely. We need video games like these. Thanks BIGMODE and Dunkey.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good schizoidvania, emphasis on puzzle solving and secret hunting over raw mechanical skill, with plenty of new tools you can discover, both in terms of items and special techniques. The art is beautiful, and the map just keeps filling in more and more and way more than you expect, so plenty of rewards for exploration and keen observation, as well as remembering things you've seen to go back to later. The tools you discover are pretty non-standard compared to most metroidvanias, but that allows for a lot more expressiveness as you discover the full potential of each item you find, even the ones which initially seem kind of pointless.The postgame and true ending is kind of a slog to get to in terms of combing and recombing the map to find the last few secrets (I got to 54 eggs before caving and looking up a guide), but you should definitely keep playing after you roll credits for the first time. This game is as deep as its namesake.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing metroidvania. Tired of every game always having the same type of upgrades like double jump, dash, grappling hook and whatnot? Or worse, something just plain boring like colored keys and contextual items?Well, animal well has by far the most original assortment of upgrades for traversal I have ever seen in a game of this type. I'm not even joking, this game has genuinely reinvented 2D world traversal and movement with incredibly creative items and gadgets, allowing you to do insanely fun tricks with a ridiculously high skill ceiling.Each item you find has many uses, often not spelled out for you requiring experimentation and thinking out of the box on how to make the best use of them. The game world is riddled with fun puzzles, challenges and secrets requiring understanding and mastering each of tool to advance. The exploration is very non linear and some areas seem able to be reached in several ways.So far, this is looking to be a new classic, expanding on ideas from other titles like environmental station alpha, the procedural animations of noita and the visual style and atmosphere of rain world. Not sure how deep the secrets rabbit hole goes, but so far it's been extremely enjoyable. Big win for Bigmode and Billy
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic. There's so much stuff to do and the game looks absolutely stunning. This game has a lot of puzzle elements that are very clever then some deeper stuff for the puzzle fanatics out there, which I personally couldn't be bothered to do so I looked it up but still had a great time. The map is by far the most useful, just seeing places that are open or have gaps on the map post game can be very useful for finding all 64 eggs to get the true ending. Of which by squinting at the map and just exploration I was able to find 53 of and 9/12 items which is pretty good. The simplicity of the game is simply charming and in certain sections require complex platforming with such simply tools. For a game with such simple tools it's impressive how much is able to be accomplished. The only real issue I have is the lack of save points in certain areas and how addicting the game is. The sense of finding new stuff has injected too much dopamine into me and I can't help myself from wanting more. Oh, also the keyboard controls feel awful to use. The best thing I found was to use the arrows keys with my left hand on ZXCV and SPACE. It's very clear this was made for controller which I prefer but it must be very weird to get used to for keyboard users. It is also very impressive to me how good the game looks, the impressive firecracker and smoke effects, as well as the slight glowiness added when using scanlines is simply immaculate. This game can run on even the lowest end horrible computers while still running great, props to Billy. Dunkey knows a good game when he sees one. But this has also intrigued me for what Billy may put out in the future. A well spent $25 that is also much cheaper in other countries (although at the moment it seems there are some translation issues, such as "board" the verb being translated to "board" the noun in Korean and a few others). A great purchase for any hardware!

_childDocuments_.review: What a surprise.The compelling pixel art is the main reason I bought this game. Before playing I've  heard news about hidden secrets and crazy ideas but I try to play blind, and stay out of spoilers, do as much exploration as I can and enjoy a relaxing journey - in fact, I was surprised by how peaceful Animal Well is.Platform seems to exist only for action games, previously popular games including Ori, Messenger and Hollow Knights etc., all are not easy to finish and bring tests on reactions and proficiency, rewarding player satisfaction after each boss. However, enemies in Animal Well won't chase you till the end and there's no mandatory bosses to fight to finish the 1st run. There are, indeed, some enemies but nothing too challenging, overall this game is super friendly to new players of action games, and surprisingly, offers the same level of satisfaction upon finishing.The pixel art is superb, with top-notch map design and mind-blowing multi-use of inventories, I can't praise enough how clever some puzzle designs are. There are some places where I got stuck so I had to check playthroughs to pass: (1) Use bubble gun on fish (2) Use yoyo on mouse (3) use fireworks on chinchillas, and (4) ghost cat chase. With a bit of help, this game is such a pleasure to play.I finished the 1st run in 9 hours with more than 20 eggs. Upon knowing there's more to discover, I earned extra tools and eventually doubled the amount of collectible eggs. I'm never good at finding secrets and not that keen on discovering everything, so after 14 happy hours as I discovered as much area as I could I decided to stop. I'm yet to find the use of that giant ring nor the clock, never seen the time capsule but every minute I've spent in Animal Well is pure joy. I wish in the future there will be new DLCs, and easier ways to reach the other endings, but for now I'm already satisfied with the content I've explored.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the best puzzle games ever. Do note that post-endgame content contains stuff that legitimately requires you to look up guides. And beyond that, 100%'ing this game requires you to go through so many different challenge scenarios it becomes an absolute chore. (whether or not that was the developers intent, I personally just don't find that kind of stuff fun).I bailed at that point. But most of the main game (i'd say like 85%-90%) I proceeded through on my own and had a ton of good "A-ha! I got it" moments. I love that stuff, so I really wasn't too bothered when that ran out towards the end of the game and I had to use guides to nudge forward and complete it. Some games bring that "need a guide" feeling in much earlier than that and it sours the experience. I didn't really feel that for most of the game, developer did a great job here.Amazing stuff overall, would highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Animal well is an amazing puzzle game with a lot of deep secrets for players to find. The art is beautiful, the sounds and music create an amazing atmosphere, and the platforming feels great. It feels like the pinnacle of metroidvania games, and does everything that it aims to do really well, however there is one thing I think should be pointed out. Before I played the game I saw a lot of people draw comparisons to games like Outer Wilds and Tunic, but to me this game didn't have that same sort of sense of discovery. The collectibles are fun to gather and the puzzles feel rewarding, but there wasn't anything particularly mind-blowing about them, and by the time I collected everything I was mostly just glad I was done. I would still recommend this game to anyone, but keep your expectations in check.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, it's pretty good. Perfectly spooky vibes. Fun to casually speedrun as well.I'm not a huge fan of metroidvanias recently, with the only other ones I really like being Hollow Knight (I mean, who doesn't like Hollow Knight), and The Messenger (and tbh I didn't really like it for the metroidvania part). So maybe it says something that I really did enjoy that side of Animal Well. Its a fun world to untangle, with secrets around every corner.I will warn that the main game, i.e. time to first ending, is pretty short (~5 or 6 hours). At that point, you will have seen a majority of the map. There's still quite a bit more to uncover after this, and I shouldn't spoil, but there is another big milestone I hit after another 5-6 hours, and lots of content in the world to find to get there. I understand there is even more after this, but it gets closer to ARG territory.That being said, even if it is short, the quality of that main 12 hours is really high. Strongly recommend to metroidvania enjoyers for sure, and also recommend to anyone who looks at the trailer and thinks *huh, this looks interesting*. Your hunch is correct. Give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best metroidvania's out there. Its one of the very few games that made me want to track down every little collectable and figure out all of its obscure puzzles. Really really fantastic. Do yourself a favour, do as little research as possible. Just buy it and figure it out. Once you've completed it, then yeah look at the wiki to find the obscure stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet, it takes about five hours for a regular runthrough, ten for 100% achievements, a little more for total completion using the community's puzzle-solving data.  You can likely see the credits without referencing a guide, but completion is at least a pen-and-paper affair.  You'll also likely want to turn flashing effects off, whether you have a medical reason to or not, because the flashbang effect is just unpleasant.  This game is extremely into backtracking and quadruple-checking every room for secrets, which is by turns charming and laborious.  Some of the rooms really get on your nerves after a couple times through, and it only gets worse if you aren't making detailed notes on your map.  But when you solve the optional puzzles on your own, it really does feel quite good.  I would have preferred more automatic tracking of fully completed rooms and missed-but-seen treasures, especially since the stamps easily overwhelm the small, blurry map.  A lot of care was put into layout and puzzle development, especially to check for softlocks in the highly open-ended exploration.  However, there is no concrete story or character to latch onto, this is a gameplay-first endeavor with an animal theme.  If you do not want to solve puzzles in a metroidvania style world, there is literally nothing else here, so don't buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played this game for 20 minutes but can already say with a high degree of confidence that this is a solid game. Animal Well oozes charm and runs incredibly well on all types of hardware. The gameplay feels really tight and responsive - the artstyle is unique and weirdly nostalgic. In the short time that I played I have found the map to be incredibly interconnected as well. Personally, I think this game is best enjoyed on a Steam Deck in front of the fireplace.A little gripe I have with the game is that is does not support ultrawide resolutions, nor does the framerate go higher than 60fps. Other than that this game is going to be an absolute treat for anyone that likes platforming and metroidvanias.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic game. I rarely play Metroidvanias but this one clearly stands out. It's a non-combat game that emphasises puzzles and platforming in order to progress. The game is stacked full of secrets, and although I've completed the game and founds most of the eggs, I've yet to even come close to figuring out all of the game's secrets and collectables, and I'm going to enjoy coming back to this game and finding even more content that I've missed.My only complaint is that the platforming (Jumping) can sometimes be a little too strict, it just felt slightly off at times. Other than that, the game is an absolute delight. The puzzles are fun, engaging, varied, and the world is absolutely enthralling. The items are extremely fun to use and encourage creativity. The atmosphere is top tier.I would recommend you go into this game blind. One of the game's main pillars is exploration so looking up how to find all of the collectables and secrets will probably diminish the experience (Unless you're just looking to finish off your collection.) .Only thing left to speak on is the pricing. The game is an indie title and so it's only £20.99. That was already great value BEFORE AAA games became obscenely overpriced. Nowadays, that value for money is just insane.In other words, there's really no reason not to pick up this game. Its great value for money, the aesthetics are great, the gameplay is great, the vibes are great. One of the must buys of 2024.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is nearly perfect for me. My gosh I was starting to think no one made an effort to make good games any more. Its all about 40-60 hours of painstaking tedious and boring filler where games drag on for an eternity. Games that blow their entire development budget on stupid graphic engines. Give me 10 hours of actual solid fun gameplay and you can have all my money. Stop filling games with crap and trying to make boring look pretty.One thing I never do with games is try to be a completionist. Mostly because I feel like games try and waste my time. But this game is so inviting and fun I actually find myself looking for the rest of the secrets. Its a testiment to how well its made. Its too bad that it is so hard to find good games like this, buried under a sea of mediocre companies with huge marketing budgets.Well done guys you created something pretty great.

_childDocuments_.review: How the f*ck is this game 33 MEGABYTES large??? I have Excel sheets with like 3 simple formulas that take up more space than this game.Awesome Metroidvania with many puzzles and secrets to explore.I really odn't want to spoil anything, so here's the best advice I can give:Buy the game, play it for 2 hours, and then decide whether you wanna refund it or not.I love the puzzles and exploration a lot and look forward to seeing what else it has to offer.Edit after finishing the game with all achievements:It took roughly 10 hours to finish, so on that front, the game is a little short. _childDocuments_.review: (***If you skip to the tl;dr at the end please first read the section with the marked asterisks as it is extremely important to note in my opinion***)I've never been so happy to be lied to by the marketing for a game.Everything I saw about this game leading up to it from the trailer and the publisher made it look honestly a little bland. It was cute and all but going into it I thought I was going to play a decent game and that my real money's worth was going to be supporting Big Mode to pursue publishing further nice indie projects at a time where indie games need to see the spotlight more.I was so wrong.You see my time played? At the time of posting this review it is 17.1 hours. That's a lot of time for a game that's less than 40mb and was published by a youtuber. So I've beat it what, 3 times? 5 times?Nope.0 times.I have gotten to a state where I would say I have finished the game 0 times so far. And I mean that in a good way because this game has definitely got a lot of replayability potential, I will be shocked if after I beat it I don't replay at least part of it once or even a few times. This game has squeezed some much content into a seemingly tiny game in far more ways than just the file size. To quote cousin Eddie: "Clark, that's the gift that keeps on givin' the whole year." I really don't want to spoil anything but there's so much that could be spoiled even a little bit of spoilers is basically nothing. I've played games in this genre before and it generally boils down to "the fun part" and "the tedious part" and while this game follows that pattern, the part that would normally be "tedious" is instead another fun part! It's not really spoilers to say that on its own since you can get an idea that will be the case from almost the very beginning of the game, but there's far more than you could have ever predicted. When the publisher and developer described the game like a lasagna that was the most accurate description or representation of the game that I could have imagined. I can think of hundreds of games that tried to do similar things to what this game does but this one does all of the PERFECTLY.I write game reviews primarily so my friends can see them and get a sense for the game from a perspective they are familiar with and so I'll put it this way to better illustrate my thoughts about this game: It is like a lasagna. I'm not a big fan of lasagna because I don't really like marinara sauce. This game is like a lasagna but all of the marinara sauce was replaced with different kinds of cheeses. You start out at the top with a nice mild mozarella, like a cheese stick. The only people who wouldn't enjoy a nice cheese stick are people that don't like any video games but if you can see this I have a feeling you do like them. It makes for a nice snack pretty much whenever you want a snack.Then you go for a sharp cheddar. Not too sharp though so I still get the feeling all of my friends will enjoy it but you'd be harder pressed to snack on it. I certainly could though, love snacking on some sharp cheddar cheese cubes but it goes much better in a full dish where all the ingredients together create an exquisite taste that leaves a pleasant after taste.Next you've got something along the lines of Gruyere. I can't stand the smell so it can be off putting at first but the flavour is much better than the smell, tasting very fancy and generally tasting like I'm eating something above my class, something that should be enjoyed by someone with more skill but I'm still lucky enough to get the chance to. I would not snack on this and I would be sure to eat it only when I have the most patience.I think there's more to come from where I am right now (almost done with the Gruyere) but I haven't gotten the chance to scrape the bottom of the pan and find out what delicious gooey cheese is down there. Perhaps it might even just be a victory lap. With a final ending credits.As I have gotten to the layer of cheese I'm on I find myself using a guide to help direct me in the right direction but the person who create the guide has graciously separate the "where to go" and "what to do" into separate spoiler tags so I don't feel as lost as I would have otherwise but the real gameplay part I still get to experience myself. The name of the guide was something like "A Traveler's guide to Animal Well" and it has been great, I would recommend not using it as much as possible as this game is EXTREMELY good at pointing you in the right direction as I was able to finish almost all of the sharp cheddar layer before I had to use the guide. Trust me, you'll know when it's time to use the guide and do not use it a second too soon, or too much.There are two criticisms I have with the game (not "main" criticisms, I think these two are literally all the criticisms I could think of, minus one puzzle that is extremely tough compared to the rest of the puzzles in the game but I found out I was missing a very helpful piece that is easy to overlook but not necessary enough to be required to even attempt it):1. For some of the puzzles in the sharp cheddar and the gruyere layers I often found myself finding a clue somewhere that made me think I had to go somewhere else to do the puzzle but I actually didn't. I am probably alone in this but I found myself far more frequently than chance getting a clue to a puzzle and thinking I'd solved it but I took it to where it made sense to me and it didn't work, making me think I had it wrong when I did have the puzzle right, I just had to do the puzzle elsewhere for some unknown reason. I probably just think very differently from the developer, i don't know, I hope no one I know runs into that problem as it made solving those puzzles hours later when I dipped into the guide kind of disappointing since every other puzzle has been EXTREMELY intentional about every little aspect (but not in a precise way, a good number puzzles can be completed in completely different ways)*** 2. There is a single puzzle in the game (in the gruyere layer) that CAN NOT be completed by yourself as far as I or anyone else can tell. It was kind of like an arg (the developer seems to have used a lot of those to entertain the community that has been following the production of Animal Well since before Big Mode got involved) and required 50 different people to solve. It is the  puzzle that you find early in the game but can't work on until later. You might think eventually you get the tools to solve it in game with how the game sets it up and though it does eventually give you a tool to help you solve it, you can not. At least, it's extremely unlikely considering  While other puzzles can get quite meta in very fun ways this one being impossible to solve on your own is not as fun. Luckily someone has made a handy tool to help you at least have some of the fun of solving it on your own! I have linked the page where you can still do the puzzle  (assuming I got the formatting right) or it's linked in that guide I mentioned earlier.Besides those things, the game is basically flawless.tl;dr: One of the best video games I've ever played in a genre that I typically am not a fan of. It has many layers and will keep you entertained as long as you want.ps: if you turn off scan lines you're lame >:(

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Metroidvania games, it's a solid entry. Certainly not the best, but decent. If your interest in this game is specifically in search of that genre, you'll probably get a good 6-10 hours out of it and you'll probably enjoy those hours. At that point, you'll have seen the credits.Unfortunately, the "meat" of the game occurs after the credits, where you're expected to comb through the same rooms and look at the same "hints" over, and over, and OVER, AND OVER in your search for increasingly obscure details. You will spend very little of this time actually solving puzzles or overcoming challenging platforming sections. Eventually, you will realize that you need to start spending a massive number of hours *outside the game* in search of clues/solutions.That's not my idea of fun, and if I'm honest, I genuinely despise it as a form of content. If I have to leave the game to play the game, then to me, that's a ♥♥♥♥ game.I don't regret my purchase. I wouldn't refund it even if I could. But, I do wish I had waited for a sale. The price is a bit steep for what I thought I was getting versus what I actually received.This isn't really a game for fans of Metroidvanias (that game is called Hollow Knight). This is a game for people that love Alternate Reality Games (ARGs). I recommend this only because what I consider to be the actual game (running around jumping and exploring) is still pretty fun and acceptably long. After all, even Super Metroid can be completed in under 10 hours on a first run.All I'm saying is, keep your expectations in mind. Is the thing you want the most another Hollow Knight, to keep you entertained until Silksong comes out? If so, you will be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s like halo 2 meets halo 3.In all seriousness, this game is so good. Here are some of my favorite things…The Atmosphere: So beautifully crafted. The times when it is “quiet” it is anything but. The silence speaks volumes when it is just cave noises, bugs, bubbles, whatever. Also the environment is highly interactive. Plants, lanterns, and more all move with you instead of blending into the background. The controller vibrations are super well thought out and sync beautifully with the audio to give a “deep bass” effect that is super cool. For reference I was using a first gen Xbox Elite controller.Open World (Well): For a platformer, this game feels like it’s open world. To be honest I have no clue if there are multiple endings or a linear path since I haven’t beaten it. It just lets you go wherever you can. No hand holding, you just experiment and explore wherever you want to.The Art Style: The fusion of retro pixel art with high fidelity effects all covered by a CRT filter is just so beautifully done. This game really shines on my OLED monitor and probably is the best way to experience it. The game has a lot of darkness so true blacks on an OLED are just stunning for this game.Such a good game, good price, if you’re even only slightly interested I say go for it.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like puzzle games and metroidvania's, so both should be great and they usually mesh with each other pretty well and makes for a lot of aha! moments which makes you feel smart for figuring it out. Animal well does not do that. There have been two instances now of the game just forcing me to guess how to progress. I was stuck in a dead end loop for way longer than I should have cause the game wanted me to do something its never even hinted at being possible. I get they want you to experiment and see what works, but the solution was just dumb. I didn't feel good figuring it out, I triggered it on accident and I'm glad I did because there was no way I was going to purposely do what I did. It's entirely possible I missed a clue on how to do it and wasn't very observant in a room I was supposed to be, but it was definitely a "how was I supposed to know I could do that" moment.The world is very interesting and I want to explore all of it, however traversing the map get tedious with the amount of backtracking there is and they lock fast travel behind finding secrets. Find enough secrets and you unlock a hub for fast travel. Why is this locked behind an optional objective? Some of those secrets are really hard to find too. I guess they figure you'll stumble upon enough of them to unlock it since you don't need very many, but still, its such a basic gameplay mechanic.I do really like the items in this game, they offer some fun traversal skills and you can do some pretty cool tech with them and get into areas early. That is a big plus though I do wish the first item you get could be set up easier to use to make traveling faster, but its very satisfying in rooms that allow for it.Overall its an okay metroidvania, the progression pushes you into a really specific way of going, so its not very metroidvania-y, but still fun. Ultimately I decided to switch my review to recommended because the rest was great, just a few really annoying things like community secrets that you are not ever going to figure out by yourself, but if you don't care about that, fire away.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Billy Blasso has, without a doubt, one of the strongest independent debuts in entertainment media. He belongs in the mount rushmore of 'devs whos name's i know'. Blasso is a 'mysteries' madman. There are some 'bunny puzzles' that have some of the most reality-bending solutions I've ever seen. If you don't plan on playing the game, you should at least look up some of these solutions . You will end up needing guides for the endgame puzzles, but it's very rewarding to do what you can without them during the "first layer" of the game (which you will know is over when you see credits roll for the first time). I just got the 'true final' ending last night, and i am still thinking about what happens at the very very end, and the insane lengths that Blasso took at a technical level. Couldn't recommend more if you are into the metroidvania genre. If you aren't a fan of puzzles, and give up on challenge quickly, you may want to skip.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a nothing burger. It's cool in concept, and looks beautiful. The gameplay mechanics are there, and they aren't bad. However... when I play games like this, I ultimately end up comparing them against games like Super Metroid, Hollow Knight, Bloodstained, and Ori. What ANIMAL WELL lacks is a drive to continue. There is nothing in this game that makes me want to pick up my controller and play it some more. The world does not pull me in and make me want to explore it in the same way that Metroid or Hollow Knight compels me to progress. ANIMAL WELL lacks the soul behind 2D Map-based exploration and puzzle solving. Beautiful on the outside, empty on the inside.

_childDocuments_.review: Technical marvel, terrible game design. Billy Basso created the entire game for scratch, as literal as you can interpret that without physically assembling the transistors in your computer: he built the engine, did the music and the graphics all by himself. It's a feat that's quite uncommon, especially for games that actually get published.Animal Well oozes charm. It has some of the best shading effects I have ever seen in a platformer. It radiates intrigue. Unfortunately the game feels very pretentious and devoid of much reflection. It's like setting a very talented but arrogant student on a project: the quality of the overall result will be high, but the actual objective they might have explained away in their head. Anima Well is a game that likes to be obtuse. It adds a plethora of puzzles the developer proudly calls "unsolvable" for singular players. It's supposed to be a "community effort". It is a very thinly veiled excuse to just not care, to just be pretentious without grounding yourself in the realities of game design. Foregoing responsibility.If you are the kind of person who feels enthralled with the whole atmosphere you might just be able to ignore this. If not, and you actually expect this to be a good game then unfortunately it will disappoint. The game is a mess: combining great, simple, well communicated puzzles with excessively obtuse ones that "aren't supposed to be solvable". Even if you paint half the canvas in the most beautiful portrait, smearing your feces over the other half will ruin the resulting product for me.Most pretentious game I have played in the last couple of years.

_childDocuments_.review: This is "Overwhelmingly positive" for a reason. I managed to go in pretty much completely blind, without even seeing most of the store page. If a mysterious and immersive metroidvania that lets you figure things out by yourself and doesn't patronize you sounds like something you might enjoy, I highly recommend it. _childDocuments_.review: I was kind of torn on how I felt about this game. I really like this genre of games with lots of secrets and mysteries to uncover and at least initially this game had me intrigued. It looks and sounds great and this contributes to the eerie atmosphere. There we also a few moments that gave me that feeling of excitement at gaining new understanding about the game's world or systems. However, ultimately my frustrations with the game wore me down enough that this wasn't an overall enjoyable experience. While I did finish the initial ending and found most of the first round of collectibles myself, I just couldn't bring myself to continue on to the deeper stuff. I think if Steam had a more granular rating I'd probably rate it as like a B or a C. Still passing, somewhat worth looking at, but not good enough for me to unequivocally recommend and certainly doesn't rank high in my favorite games. Some of my main problems with the game:1) It doesn't feel good getting around and taking actions. The platforming feels off. It's hard to explain, but there are all sorts of times when I slipped off a platform, barely missed a tight jump, etc that just made me feel like I didn't have as much control over my character's movements as I wanted. This platforming is at its worst whenever you need to jump past a screen transition. It's jarring suddenly changing views and often your jump just barely gets you to the next screen before immediately falling back if you have nothing to catch you. So you have to fairly quickly orient yourself to make sure you land properly. Your use of tools is also pretty finicky. A lot of the tools allow you to aim them with your directional input. But the 2 problems with this are that a) This is also you movement control, so sometimes you might screw up your positioning while trying to aim, and b) the aiming is 8 directional and it can be a pain to get the game to recognize you're aiming your stick at an ordinal direction.2) This is exacerbated by the fact that the game will ask you to backtrack through the same rooms a LOT, often requiring you to redo the platforming or in some cases even puzzles. This is just exhausting and several times made me not want to bother rechecking some areas for clues. You can eventually find some tools that make traversal a bit easier such as a teleport. However, the points you can teleport to are fairly limited and some areas of the map simply have no easy way to get to them without redoing a bunch of rooms. Plus the checkpointing is fairly inconsistent, making some platforming segments feel wildly more punishing than others. Sometimes you'll fall into some water and just instantly respawn on a nearby ledge and get right back to trying again or the last piece of solid ground was a few screens back and you go all the way back there. In some places, you might fall into a completely different area and have to either go back to a previous save or trek way back up. And the save points are also pretty scarce, so there were quite a few times, especially early on, when I wanted to stop playing for the night, but I hadn't saved in like 20+ minutes and I was struggling to get back to a save point or find a new one. 3) This one is a little nuanced, but I think the game doesn't do a great job at teaching some of it's core mechanics. I need to be specific about this point: I think it's good that the game doesn't have a bunch of text popups telling you exactly what the items do and how to use them. I think it's good that the game lets you discover some of the advanced uses for the items yourself. What I don't like is how the game doesn't present the rooms/situations where you get some items in a way that helps you learn what their basic use is. Ideally, you get the item, and to get back, the game should set up a puzzle that needs your new tool to solve it. The game actually does this for some of the items, but it either doesn't do it, or doesn't do it well for some others. Trying to avoid spoilers as much as possible for these examples: - There is one item which you get where you can just walk back out of the room after you get it. There is a way to use that item in the room where you get it if you notice, however, doing so serves no purpose. It just brings you back to another room you've already guaranteed gotten the item from and which is literally right next to that first room, so not even a shortcut. So I never thought to even try using it there because there was no need for it nor even something enticing me to use it. - One item I received I actually tried using in the room where I got it and later I found out through spoilers that there actually was something in that room that needed that tool. However, the tool is kind of random, so I just so happened to miss the thing I needed it to interact with.- In both of the above cases, I actually didn't find even the most basic use for the item for quite a while until I accidentally used them somewhere where they just so happened to do something. - One item I got actually had a room that required me to learn how to use the item to get out and it was actually kind of a cool puzzle. However, this gave me a wrong impression of what the item did. I was really excited after leaving the room, thinking that this item completely cracked the game wide open and now there must be a ton of places I can go and things to do. However, I was disappointed when I found out that the item's abilities were actually far more limited in scope than I thought.4) I was frequently disappointed by the rewards for my exploration/platforming/puzzle solving. The most exciting moments of the game are ones where you find some new tool or learn some new piece of information that lets you interact with the world in a whole new way. But of course that's not the only kind of secret/reward you'll find. Most of the things you'll find will be one of 3 kinds of things: - The collectibles: I've had similar collectible hunts in other games like this where I actually felt pretty engaged by them. Maybe it's just how many of them I needed. Maybe it's just how much effort was sometimes needed to get one. None of them offer a tangible reward or even a clue that can give you a hook to go do other things. I'd often hit a roadblock, spend a bunch of time looking for something I've missed, then I finally find something, think I've found a lead that will get me past the roadblock, then it's just another collectible and I'm a tiny bit closer to the goal with no new direction to help me feel like I'm not just stumbling around the entire map looking for things. - Shortcuts: I'd think I found something that will move me forward only to end up somewhere I've already been and I asked myself "WTF has that accomplished?" Think back to games like say, Dark Souls. That feeling of relief you had when you discovered a shortcut from some dangerous area back to a place of safety. I never felt that with the shortcuts in this game. It was always just confusion followed by anger at having wasted my time seemingly done nothing.- Health Pickup you don't need.5) I ended up spoiling myself on the postgame stuff because I was so sick of the game by then and I don't regret it. While there are some cool puzzles/secrets that I might have had some fun solving, There are a few puzzles that you literally do not have the ability to solve within the game itself, plus some unreasonably tough platforming challenges mixed in with them. And these aren't separate secrets or a final big secret as the cherry on top. These are part of the same pool of collectibles necessary for one of the endings. So even if I spent my time solving the fun/interesting/reasonable ones, if I couldn't get through the platforming challenges and/or didn't want to have to go online for some of the secrets, I just straight up would have wasted my time doing the ones I did complete.

_childDocuments_.review: Is an overall amazing game, with very enjoyable puzzles, graphics, etc, it would be easier to explain the few things I don't like.By the way, I'm not someone who plays puzzle games often or ever, so this might make me biased.I wish puzzles had a way of showing me whether I don't know how to do it, or whether I don't have an item for it, that would make it a lot more realistic and would make me enjoy the game more, as I know the puzzle II'm focusing on is currently doable with the items I have.I was able to beat the game and get around 40 eggs without any guidance, but after that I was just running around for hours, making no progress, and resorted to finishing the rest of the game with internet guides.
