_childDocuments_.review: So far it's been a stellar experience. Well worth the asking price. The game balances an incredibly chill atmosphere with occasional tense segments that you must learn to maneuver gracefully. The progression items I've unlocked so far are a very nice spin on the typical metroidvania items. No cliche double jump or speed burst or grappling hook, but items that actually feel like they are interacting with the world itself, making progression through the map feel very rewarding.The game opens up very nicely. It's a great mixture of unlocking new items, as well as trying to use the items you've unlocked so far to cheese your way through areas, until you hit a wall that you just barley cannot get over or a pit that you just barley cannot get across. But maybe you can, if you just cheese hard enough. There are definitely some areas where you do need specific items to progress, but the map feels very open and there is never one obvious path forward.The puzzles range between easy and mildly difficult. So far there hasn't been anything that was terribly difficult. The solution is either fairly obvious, or involves a bit of backtracking as you figure out your way through the handful of permutations of puzzle state. This is probably my biggest critique here, some of the puzzles have a pretty sever failure state or involve semi-precise movement or targeting. Not enough to make the puzzles feel skill based, but enough to make some of them very frustrating to repeat.My other big critique would be at the map. For one, I think the game would benefit from having an optional mini map, because I do often find myself in situations where I am pulling up the map repeatedly when making my way back to an area I haven't fully explored yet. I also find the map a bit difficult to parse. Especially the symbols you can place or the sketches you can make can be very hard to read. It would also have simply been nice to have proper markers for the more important places of interest.All in all I'd give it a solid 8/10 and probably the most fun I've had with a metroidvania since Hollow Knight.

_childDocuments_.review: The second I hit install the second it was download and ready to play, I was shocked!Billy Basso has crafted an amazing atmosphere in this game.  The song playing while you're on the menu gives the perfect vibe for the environment you are about to explore.  You will constantly be surprised with how some of the animals react when you use your gadgets around them.   The same applies for how your gadgets work as well.  You may think something has only one purpose, but the more you experiment with them the more you realize there are multiple different ways to meaningfully use each gadget.The puzzles feel very intuitive and satisfying to solve.  You are greatly rewarded for testing out your own ideas and thinking outside of the box to find the solution.  There is also the platforming which can feel like a puzzle in itself at times, but that brings a nice mix to the game.  Mechanics are amazing and well thought out with how it all works together.  Absolutely loved accidentally jumping onto the frisbee and discovering what happens when you land on it, that's all I'll allude too for this review.Once again, Billy Basso has made an amazing game, I hope to see more from him in the future.  Big thanks to him for making it and another thanks to Bigmode/Dunkey for putting so many eyes on the game.  Be sure to recommend Animal Well to your buddies who might not know about Dunkey, the more new faces, the more recognition for both Billy Basso and Bigmode for crafting and publishing such a unique game.

_childDocuments_.review: Great little metroidvania-style platformer with a lot to love. Billy Basso blowing us away with this adorable little gem, and Bigmode starting out super strong with a great pickup. Only downside I have is how short it is--or at least how short it seems. I'm just over 10 hours in and it feels like I'm closing in on the end already. It might have only been 10 hours so far but it feels much longer with how much is packed into the map to explore. If you don't like backtracking or you struggle with precise platforming than this game will be a struggle for you, but provided you're good with that stuff this game is a winner that won't soon be forgotten. One of my favorite things is how expressive the player character is with just a brown circle and 2 eyes. The little guy is adorable and I don't wanna see him get chased half way across the map by an angry ghost cat!But yeah. Game good. If it's as short as it seems than $25 might be a little steep, but I see myself coming back to this one for years to come so I'll definitely be getting my money's worth on it. Waiting on the eventual Dunkey video about this one, assuming he decides to make one. Hats off to Billy Basso, hope y'all are getting the success you deserve for this one!

A nice touch from the dev.Cons: Although the sound design is really good, some sections would benefit from having theme songs. The game has some well defined regions and each one has a specific and important area to progress. Adding thematic songs to represent these regions on at least these key areas would add a new dimension to the game. And some of big animals have goofy voices too. _childDocuments_.review: This game is very good, the vision is very strong, super charming. But I don't think it's for everyone.The magic of this game is the feeling of wonder and joy from trying something out with the tools you already have, in places you've already been, and discovering something new and exciting. But, as you progress through the game, the puzzles will get gradually harder and more opaque, and you will need to be more committed to get that feeling again.Unless you're a huge fan of puzzles, your playthrough of this game will range from 6-12 hours. This is a very high quality product, and I believe that its price is well-deserved. However, you're not getting a lot of playtime for what you're paying. It's some very polished playtime, but still not much playtime.If you don't mind that, go ahead and buy it. It's just that although I can appreciate that this is game is quite special for what it is, and how it is, it just didn't blow my mind, because it's not exactly for me.If you're the kind of person who can obsess over this game and find all of the subtle meticulous details sown in it by the amazing single developper, and get many tens of hours of fun out of it, then you will really love this game, I think.I'm glad I played it, but that's about it. I'd rather watch videos of people solving the obscure puzzles in this game than try to solve them myself. This is a subjective thing. I can't imagine someone truly regretting trying this game, because it's very unique (in a great and refreshing way, I think), so I give it a thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: The atmosphere and music in this game are great, and I generally like the puzzles. This is very much a game where you have to go back and revisit the whole map every time you get a new item, though. Unfortunately, you continue to get new items even into the post-game, meaning that the game involves a lot of backtracking. To make matters worse fast travel is pretty limited meaning that most of the gameplay is walking through the same couple areas over and over again. Most of the items are really cool and well-integrated into the gameplay, and give you multiple ways to solve each puzzle. A few items are pretty bad, however, and are hard to control or else offer limited utility outside of one or two locations on the map. A few of the puzzles in the late game are quite esoteric which can get really annoying. I really liked the bosses, which are really well-integrated into the gameplay and in many cases feel fresh and creative. For the amount of content this game is overpriced, but since it's an indy dev I'm more inclined to overpay; this game has the amount of content of a really good flash game rather than a full-length game. Overall skip this one if you don't like backtracking or obscure puzzles, but it's a decent enough game if that's your sort of thing. 4/10
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty light recommendation with some caveats. The games about 5-10 hours long for a casual playthrough and may run you 15-20 hours for 100% with light guide usage for later sections. If your heart is set on 100% and never using any guides you'll likely get much more time out of it, exactly how much more I couldn't say. Just know if you are that person there is (atleast) one secret puzzle you will  to look up in order to solve it. I think the games main content seems kind of half baked, it feels like a lot of proper "game" content may have been sacrificed in order to make room for more meta indie postgame stuff.  Depending on what you discover and when, you're able to snap any semblance of difficulty in half like the worlds thinnest twig; which is a bit of a shame because the game has a lot of really cool mechanics it just never does much of anything with them.  It feels like there is very little proper level design that effectively utilizes the tools at your disposal, this is obviously in-part due to the non-linear nature of the game, but it definitely doesn't help matters that most of the late game areas are dedicated to one off gimmicky mechanics or meta puzzles leaving little room to properly develop your arsenal of items. As for the aforementioned meta puzzles I didn't really care for them and ended up using a guide to speed up most of the process. Your mileage on these sorts of puzzles will vary, personally I loved the meta stuff in games like Tunic (my personal fav of this "genre"), The Witness, and Baba is You, but wasnt really a fan of it in games like Environmental Station Alpha or Fez.  Consistency and clarity are key when it comes to these sorts of puzzles and ease of navigation goes a long way in helping me tolerate them.  I think Animal Well kind of flubs all three of these things to varying degrees.  Lets just say you're probably going to spend a lot of time running around aimlessly looking for vague things and hoping that your interpretation of other vaguer things is correct and yes, you will have to redo those puzzles, and do those jumps to get through those rooms again, tough luck buck o!Despite all this griping, I think the game is mechanically brilliant, controls excellently, looks gorgeous, sounds even better (not so much in the bangin soundtrack sense but more so in a "cool noises" sense) and has great replayability.  Not to mention there's plenty of unexpected highlight moments and lots of exciting player driven discovery; which is always great to see in an age where so many games are intent on shoving every potential cool thing they have to offer down your throat with as much emphasis as humanly possible.  I don't think it ever lives up to its own mechanical potential but if a level editor is ever implemented or people figure out how to make mods that problem could pretty quickly be fixed.  Also as a quick aside im not sure why so many negative reviews are complaining about difficulty?  I thought the whole game was a bit on the easier side, its more about thinking things through and mechanical discovery than tight platforming or extreme precision.  If you've played an indie platform/puzzler/metroidvania before and beaten it you can beat this!

_childDocuments_.review: This game felt like Hallow Knight but without any weapons. Instead of fighting, players will use items found throughout the map to solve puzzles. Just looking at this game I didn't think the puzzles would be that hard, but I found myself using the internet to solve basically all of the late game puzzles. I really wanted to try beat the game without the internet, but I would have never finished this game without looking up the answers. Yet looking up the answers didn't make solving them feel any less rewarding. It was fun seeing how much thought went into the puzzles and unlocking as much of the map as I could on my own. The art style make exploring such an enjoyable experience. Which was important since I spent a decent amount of time wondering all over the map. If you have a steam deck, I highly recommend giving this game as try.

_childDocuments_.review: ANIMAL WELL is a deeply intriguing game from start to finish. Every screen is not only a work of art, but also laden with secrets begging to be explored. Everything about this game shows the dedication and love it has received from its creator, but the thing that I like most about ANIMAL WELL is the unorthodox items the player unlocks as they explore the world. I cannot recommend this game enough; ANIMAL WELL will go down as a shining of achievement of creativity in game design.

_childDocuments_.review: For a game I enjoyed quite a bit, I find it surprisingly hard to start talking about Animal Well. Perhaps that's because I'm not sure it has a lot to say outside of an earnest desire to provide players with a string of lovely "aha!" moments, and perhaps a renewed and legitimate fear of kangaroos. In the small but prestigious pantheon of Puzzlevanias/Mystery-Box/ARGcore games (Fez, Tunic, Outer Wilds, Void Stranger, La-Mulana), Animal Well stands out as perhaps one of the most accessible. The initial campaign is a pleasant 6-8 hours that artfully introduces new mechanics and teaches the player vital skills through carefully considered level design and intuitive, relatable abilities (everyone knows how a yo-yo and a frisbee works!) without using a single word. The developer has outright stated that this, "Layer 1," is meant to be beaten by just about any player, and it is a tremendous success in how good of a teacher it is. This alone is remarkable in a genre that is often deliberately obtuse and hostile, making the game an excellent entry point for those new to the Flavour. But of course, true-blue sleutherheads know that the main campaign is only the beginning. There's a post-game. And a post-post-game. That's what the freaks are here for, and the game delivers on its promise of a world-spanning easter egg hunt, with secrets galore and bunnies to solve. Yet in the days after unpacking its most significant mysteries,  I find the game surprisingly slipping out of my mind in a way that other genre titles never did.The best in the genre essentializes its mysteries by making the *feelings* of Mystery -> Revelation core components of their grander narrative or thematic goals. Fez demands scientific rigor in its puzzles, and rewards you with cosmic awe/terror. Void Stranger frustrates and obfuscates information for the player at every turn, making them feel as lost as its protagonist.  The Outer Wilds uses "aha!" moments as daring twists in its murder mystery of the universe. While delightful, I fail to see how Animal Well's numerous revelations feed into any grander narrative. Who built this well?  What is it? What's the significance of the bunnies? What do the manticores represent? What does any of this mean? These are not even real questions since there are no answers to them in the text. Just before writing this I lurked the Animal Well discord lore channels to see if I'd missed something, but no. Any answer is either a joke, nonsense, or effectively fan-fiction. No wonder the channel is mostly quiet for such a high-profile indie release. That's not to say there's *no* meaning present. My initial point about kangaroos wasn't entirely facetious, Animal Well does an excellent job at imbuing the animals with a sense of, well, animal unknown! Sometimes they're helpful, sometimes they ignore you, sometimes they hunt you, sometimes they scare the crap out of you for no good reason. It comes across as refreshingly devoid of anthropocentrism, and Billy's carefully observed and reproduced depictions feel more truthful (and honest) to the natural world as a result. Additionally, its elegance in puzzle design is a powerful statement on its own. Smarter people than me can unpack it though, and I'm sure they will for years to come.All in all, I came away from Animal Well satisfied if a little empty. It's an extremely luxurious and supremely polished puzzle box that opens up surprise after surprise, layer after layer. Yet after cracking open the last one, there is no grand revelation of what any of it was for. Those "aha!" moments sure are thrilling though, delightful all on their own. And now I know origami a little better. Plus, the whole thing was made by one guy! He made his own engine and it runs like a dream, how cool isn't that? So, y'know, it's a pretty good time all-in-all.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game!!! Animal Well is a unique take on the Metroidvania genre, blending atmospheric puzzle-solving with deep exploration. The game's beautifully pixelated world captivates me with its eerie, interconnected labyrinth that's just teeming with secrets waiting to be uncovered. Each puzzle feels meaningful, designed to challenge and engage, making every discovery a reward in itself.What really sets Animal Well apart for me is its focus on non-combat interactions within a dense, multi-layered environment. The game avoids traditional combat and instead encourages a thoughtful approach to navigating its world, where the real challenge lies in solving puzzles and manipulating the environment in creative ways. This design resonates with me as it emphasizes exploration and interaction over action, providing a truly immersive experience. As well as being a visual treat, the game's audio design complements perfectly, enriching the overall atmosphere and drawing me deeper into its mysterious world.Lastly, I appreciate how the game is structured. It’s designed to keep unfolding secrets long after the initial playthrough, promising a long-lasting engagement. The developers' attention to detail and commitment to creating an evolving gameplay experience is something I deeply value.Animal Well is a must-play for anyone who loves games that combine meticulous puzzle design with expansive exploration, all set in a beautifully crafted pixel art world. I think it's a masterpiece that redefines what a Metroidvania should be.

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well is more of a puzzle-platformer than Metroidvania, and perhaps my expectations may have been misguided because of this. As such, I found myself surprised at many moments during my first playthrough, satisfied upon completion of the many exquisitely designed puzzles and immersed in the intricate design of the visuals and audio of this title. Like taking a step inside of a children's picture book (E.G., Where the Wild Things Are), Animal Well nails its presentation with beautiful, hand-crafted set pieces filled with many secrets and intricacies. These many secrets play a pivotal role in the game's Metroidvania-like approach; there's plenty to discover in the Well, so much so that one playthrough simply isn't enough to get the full experience. In my opinion however, this is also one of the game's weaknesses; I found that jumping back into the game after taking a break for several days was difficult. I lost track of where I was going or what my objective previously was, which made it frustrating to re-immerse myself in the world again in order to get a better grasp of where to go next. Even without taking a break for a lengthy time, I continued to have this issue across several segments in my first playthrough. The Well is large; it demands your attention to detail at every screen and your ability to chart your next path forward is crucial to making your exit. Perhaps to some this is a good thing, I'm sure many seek this kind of experience. But as an adult with little time to play games nowadays, I believe this kind of experience is simply not for me. The other elements of Animal Well are what sold me on this title; the platforming feels really solid, the tools you acquire are very interesting and provide a very unique experience, and the puzzles are so well crafted, like those of The Legend of Zelda series. There's a lot to enjoy in Animal Well, and if you're ready for the work that comes with the navigation, you're in for a good time. However, if you aren't an avid fan of puzzle-platformers or Metroidvanias, this probably won't be the title to sell you on the genre. Overall, I enjoyed my time with the title, but I'm hesitant to recommend this to everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: I was admittedly a little sceptical when dunkey announced he was going to start publishing games. I was more sceptical when, at launch, the game didn't ... launch. After the game actually booted up, and I was quite surprised to find therein the thing that makes all great games - atmosphere. Animal Well demonstrates this as you boot up the game, and keeps this energy throughout.Anyway, still sceptical big mode is gonna do well. What are the odds they publish two bangers in a row?

_childDocuments_.review: One of, if not the best, puzzle platformers I've ever played. Dunkey/Big Mode backed a good game and are off to a positive start. Dunkey is doing it right. Billy Basso did an amazing thing with this game. A passion project that makes a profit is always incredibly admirable. This game does not require pixel perfect techniques to finish the main campaign, get the "true" ending, or even solve 98% of the puzzles; there's only 2 puzzles that require platformer expertise, and they're super secret and not required for either ending. I've played highly puzzle dense platformers before, like Fez, but I don't think any of them were as well constructed in how they present hints while simultaneously making you feel smart. There's definitely a bit of challenge sometimes with the "bosses", but they're mostly really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool, one of the coolest implemented boss mechanics I've seen.The Well is beautiful and feels alive with animals, most of them friendly. The dozens of funny, quirky, and sometimes horrifying interactions with the animals are fantastic. How the world and character interact, whether through particle effects, interactions with various lighting elements, or shifting camera angles is wonderfully delightful. The use of kids toys as tools was clever and perhaps adds a powerful nostalgic effect. Special mention to the bubble wand for its supplanting of the classic double jump mechanic.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed Environmental Station Alpha, you will like this even more. It's a high quality Metroidvania that gives you an absolute boatload of unorthodox post-game puzzles.The base platforming is as simple as it can get (you can't even control the height of your jump), but it gets exponentially more interesting as you find items. Animal Well is at its absolute best when you're discovering niche side effects of the items and start applying them in ways you didn't previously think to.Because of its open nature, it's really exciting to theorycraft routes and think about different potential ways of beating the game. Most of the ways of acquiring items/flames quickly end up involving .If you're aiming for full completion, you will see the game at its weakest, as a good chunk of it just comes down to sweeping over the same areas without any new challenges and checking vacant pixels on the map.Out of everything, I found the eggs to be the least compelling part of the game - the enjoyment factor in collecting them comes from the stand-out examples where you gambol through a gargantuan gauntlet or piece together a particularly perplexing puzzle in order to obtain one. Unfortunately, the majority are just hidden behind a vine blocking sight.Generally, I would recommend this game to pretty much anybody except for completionists. If you like challenge runs, this game is for you. If you like experimenting with routing, this game is for you. If you like solving weird and ridiculous puzzles, this game is for you. If you just want a good Metroidvania to blast through, this game is for you. But if you want a game that is fun to 100% front-to-back, Animal Well is  not it.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to love this game.  It's right up my alley in so many ways!  It's a metroidvania, it's got great a great atmosphere and unique style, it uses sound effectively and with impact, and it doesn't hold your hand, but rather let's you figure things out through exploration and gameplay experimentation.  BUT, where the game get tedious is towards the late game when you have to do A LOT of backtracking, and not being able to zoom in much on the map makes it a little tiring trying to figure out where to go back to.  Yes, there is a fast travel method, but only taking you back to a hub connecting to different parts of the map.  I love being encouraged to explore, but I felt like it was a bit too much towards the end.  I still really like this game and would probably put it in my top 10 favorite metroidvanias I've played.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one for me, because ultimately the game is fine.  The platforming is fun and the tools are neat and satisfying.  I really enjoyed a lot of the map, the rooms are creative, and the exploration felt natural until the first ending of the game.  This is kind of where the fun for me stopped. SPOILERS AHEADThere are so many issues with the exploration as a whole that arise when you think about this as a puzzle game that is moonlighting as a metroidvania.  These two things tend to be at odds during the first several hours of the game.  You are often tasked with puzzle or moderately difficult platforming to progress, the problem is that often messing up punishes you with a min+ long run back just to try again.  Dying sucks because the checkpoints are just spread out way to far, but the longer you play you realize that there is decent reason to the spacing and it becomes less of an issue.  But this made me not really enjoy actually playing the game.  After you pass the first ending, the puzzles then become the problem.  Unless you are a Private I. or avid forum user, these puzzles are going to feel like if someone handed you an exam in a language you didn't know all while telling you that if you were EXCEPTIONALLY perceptive during the last several hours you *might* be able to solve them.  Like everything you see that might even seem remotely odd, you better right that down, because if you miss it then you will be searching for that needle in a very large haystack. That really sums up a lot of the puzzles for the latter half of the game.  You are either searching every wall for various holes to rooms, or you  are looking for that one thing that you missed 4 hours ago without realizing it. To completely finish the game you will need a guide, I don't mean that in a way that's like "its too hard without one" Which is also true, some of the puzzles are just unbelievable and I can't even fathom how they got discovered without it being purely an accident.  But there is actually one puzzle for one of the titular secret bunnies that you literally cannot solve in your game.  The solution was a community effort with details I don't fully understand, but you cannot do this without looking it up. Ultimately, with the fun being hampered less than ideal run-backs for puzzles and platforming I didn't enjoy the first part of the game.  And the shift the game takes into being ARG level solutions to puzzles that just don't respect your time outside of a haystack search in most puzzles just isn't fun.This is not a perfect game and it is not a game for everyone, clearly I am an outlier here since the reviews seem unanimous, but also I think a lot of that does have to do with the fact that it was published by Dunkey.  I don't want to belittle Basso's work, while the game is not for me it is still very impressive, but having it published by Dunkey is really making a lot of people treat it as the second coming of christ.  When ultimately it is a smart but rather unfun game to play.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to put in words how this game made me feel. Animal Well has something for everyone. It feels both difficult and fair, but never easy or punishing. The joy of finding secrets, discovering new ways to explore the well, and solving some of the most fun puzzles is around every single corner, and hidden in every nook and cranny. Controls feel tighter than possibly any game I've played in the last 10 years, every single room is a hand decorated work of art, met with a hauntingly beautiful soundtrack, topped off with some of the most enjoyable and creative puzzles I've ever solved. Moment after moment after moment of "How did they even come up with this?"

_childDocuments_.review: Usually I am not a fan of horror or anything horror adjacent, so I was hesitant based on a lot of the promotional stuff I had seen leading up to it coming out. The final trailer video showing it seemed to be mostly puzzles and such with a eerie vibe to the game, similar to many other metroidvania style games, made me want to give it a try though. And man oh man am I glad I did. This game does NOT hold your hand at all. Every puzzle in this game is for you to find, solve and figure out on your own. There's multiple routes, solutions, and all sorts of aspects that can leave any player from giddy with excitement from solutions, to scratching their head going "there's a way i am suppose to be able to get that?!" The eerie vibe is a little off putting at times for sure, though I chalk that up to not being super fond of eerie games, and also it definitely makes your skin crawl with some of the music as well here and there. There definitely is a few moments as well where I had to cool myself down to not panic and mess up puzzles while creepy weird stuff is happening all around me. The pixel like look with some of the crazy pixel physics in some moments just are insane, and provide everything from "That's just gorgeous" to "Holy cool that was insane! What just happened?!" All in all, for a game that I thought would haunt me in my dreams (which granted it likely still will, looking at you bosses) I have enjoyed it quite a lot, and the puzzles have been so refreshing and pleasant. The game truly feels like it is genuinely rewarding you for the challenges you complete, before it soon enough gives you a harder one to solve. Definitely recommend, and seriously hope people give this game a try, cause its very much worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll probably add to/change this review in the future if I see reason to.In short, I recommend this game when it's $15 or under, there's a lot here that makes it good, but not great.Some problems and gripes.Fast travel is almost perfect but ruined by the some of the entrances being in awkward spots for no apparent reason. I also find it weird there wasn't a save point inside the hub in case you want to save&exit there for easier resets.It's odd that all of the items were more kid themed than animal themed. I'm stuck in-between how important collecting randoms junk should be in a game. on one hand, I think it's a good thing to have a true ending locked behind doing more such as collecting every egg. on the other, having to collect more than half to do one particular puzzle was frustrating to say the least. In short, probably would of been better if they didn't have the top in the game and just lessened the amount of eggs to 50. The extra items are all basically one trick while the basic items have a bit more complexity.Hollow Knight probably has spoiled my taste in metroidvanias, but this game doesn't really give off the interconnected vibe that I was looking for. Outside of the 8 fast travel points, you have fish head tubes that can take you to different points on the map, but for the most part their just used to go to an isolated part of the map or as part of a dedicated puzzle. meaning you'll just be going from A to B in the same fashion of one square to the next. I'd say the "labyrinth" is more like a house with more locked doors than anything else. The items (with the exception of the bubble wand) barely change traversing the map. Dark parts of the map aren't charted down even if you've been there. I'm not sure what the intention of doing that is terms of game design because while I can understand not knowing details of a section when it's actually pitch black, the majority of the time it's just an annoying mechanic that makes you second guess if you've skipped a part of the map, travel all the way there, only to realize you haven't missed anything. It's really odd to because I think the simple solution that should of been in the game to start is to have an in-between of sorts, as in just a rough outline of a dark room on the map so players knows they've been there instead of the all or nothing map marking. Non-existent in-game lore for whatever is going on. I'm not asking for wikipedia article exposition but it'd be nice to know why some animals are in cages and others are just chilling.some of the good.Puzzles are neat and for the most part you can instantly understand what items to use to finish a puzzle.There are no loading screens, just you and the game.Basic items have more than one use which makes them come in handy in interesting ways.Plenty of secrets for a game that's 34 mb.Sound design and music are solid.Visuals are more hit than miss.Player freedom is high on which directions you can go. No invisible walls.Overall, a proper 6.5-7.5 out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: A charming and unique puzzle-focused Metroidvania. The power-ups are unorthodox, and the level and puzzle design are great. Interactions between you and the world feel natural, and the sense of discovery and wanderlust doesn't disappear for all 8~10 hours the "main" game will take you to complete. Animal Well might be the first game in the genre to actually try something very different from the norm to great success - coming from a single developer, that is all the more commendable.The game also has dozens of hours of extra post-game content, with many mysteries and obscure secrets for you to find and solve. I wasn't going to play this anymore, so I took a quick look, and multiple of them seem like completely random ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to me; however, I know a lot of people love this kind of thing, and if that is you it's your lucky day.As you might know, Animal Well is the first game published by Dunkey's publisher, BigMode; as a result, a lot of reviews are effectively worthless memes that ignore the developer and the game's merits entirely. Hopefully, this gave you a better idea of what you're getting, although this is an easy recommendation for pretty much anyone since the game is a short, well-polished experience.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well is an unconventional game, but absolutely amazing if you go into it with the right mindset. While technically it's a metroidvania platformer game, it's more of a game about secrets as described by the creator himself. This game is best played without a guide, trying to figure things out for yourself. The game is expertly crafted to give you well designed hints that lead you to a solution without outright telling you. It makes you feel smart. On top of the well designed mechanics, the game is just beautiful, the pixel artstyle and the different particle effects look great. While it might not be for the average player, Animal Well is a great experience that I can't recommend enough.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

Also it's an extremely small install size and should run on anything.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been on steam for more than 14 years, and never have I ever before beaten the game to such a degree to get all of the achievements (honestly never cared for it). Animal Well is the first one, and what a ride it was. Some of the late game stuff I've Googled since I do not have that much time on hand to do it on my own but still, this is not a game, this is an experience. Not for everyone though :D
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those experiences that you're best going into knowing as little as possible about the actual substance of the game. In short, if you like metroidvanias and puzzles, there's a ton of stuff to enjoy in Animal Well. Stop reading here and go buy it if you like the sound of that.In a little more detail, whilst trying to keep it as vague as possible; I loved every minute of Animal Well. It has kept me hooked for a good 15 hours or so thus far and I am sure I have plenty still to do and see in this wonderful, labyrinthine world.Every discovery, every "a-ha" moment, every little nugget of information felt well earned - and every one spurred me on to keep searching and pondering on the mounting pile of mysteries I'd been accumulating.Animal Well just spoke to me on a level that few games manage. I played in parallel to a friend: Comparing notes and sharing our discoveries brought back some wonderful nostalgia of poring over game manuals in the playground and swapping tips for whatever we were playing at the time (some combination of Final Fantasy, Pokemon and Zelda no doubt).It also helped of course that the art style and audio in Animal Well are beautiful in themselves and contribute to a palpable and (in the best way) dense atmosphere.All in all, one of the best games I've played for a good while and I will be playing more :)
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend, good game, the atmosphere is ominously perfect, overall game feel is great, and with impactful sound designboth a tight platforming experience and a great metroidvania even if you only play till the credits roll (which can be pretty early if you move fast).I'd say that every "main secret" to get all achievements are very fair, although I ended up looking up a few personally. If you're insane and you love torture there are tons of extra secrets which range from a cute puzzle to extremely frustrating. I would say that there are some that, under the right conditions, are literally impossible to solve without using the internet. If you're really playing to this extent, I would say not to be afraid of cross-checking things occasionally for your own enjoyment
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Its a neat little game. Took almost 7 hours to get to an ending, but I don't think I will continue, even though there is absolutely more to it.Its a pretty smart game, I liked the puzzles and the style it is going for, but the game starts to break its own rules pretty often especially towards the end. A game of this nature lives and dies by its consistency to it's obscure mechanics, and there are absolutely many spots where it doesn't stay true to that nature.It's a good puzzle game and a good metroidvania, but it had some annoying aspects to it that made me not want to do anything more with the game post credits, which I guess is fine, but I wish wasn't the case.

_childDocuments_.review: At first you think you're getting a regular little metroidvania. That's how they get you.Hoooo boy the secrets in this game are obtuse. Like La-Mulana meets ARG stuff. The game exists on a few different layers: Layer 1 is the metroidvania part, Layer 2 is a more conventional completionist sort of thing, and Layer 3 is when you start getting into really really bizzare stuff involving binary, printers, and so much more. If you get to Layer 3 I wouldn't feel bad at all about using a guide (and in fact I'm pretty sure it's not even possible to 100% the game without using a guide in some capacity!) but there's some really brilliant puzzle design here and I think people will be discovering stuff for years to come.Strong recommend, and a really solid start to Bigmode's roster.

_childDocuments_.review: A unique metroidvania, blending exploration, puzzles and multifaceted visuals in a brilliant way.Enter the Well, a mysterious place inhabited by animals, sometimes cute but not always friendly, where each corner could conceal a secret nook and many screens present layers of hints for you to uncover and unravel. In this journey, an inquisitive mind and an attentive eye will your most trusted allies which will allow you to proceed, find strange objects and discover all their applications. For each puzzle, its cleverness is equal to the joy of having solved it, and there will be plenty of them here! Often a room you thought you explored completely hides more spaces, to be unlocked in a creative way.Even if you are not the sharpest secret hunter, the base path required to reach your home is feasible by most players and still gives a rewarding satisfaction. Do not give up on this game, because you fear you cannot finish it without a guide, but instead play it savouring each accomplishment it can gift you.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s been a long while since I last played a game that was this satisfying to explore. Beyond giving you the basic controls, with 𝘈𝘯𝘪𝘮𝘢𝘭 𝘞𝘦𝘭𝘭 you’re left to figure things out on your own, but it’s never so opaque that I found myself lost or frustrated. It encourages experimentation and often rewards your curiosity. If there’s one thing I found occasionally cumbersome, it’s how progress is carried over after dying. There are these blocks that appear and disappear when you flip switches, but if you die the state of these blocks is what it was pre-death. This will result in paths being blocked and puzzles needing to be solved again to attempt certain areas again. This was never a BIG deal but it occasionally annoyed me. Then there’s the fact you need to restock firecrackers every time you die, which also was occasionally cumbersome.

_childDocuments_.review: For Big-modes first game, hell even for most publishers, this is a FANTASTIC entry. Much like hollow knight, its a modern take on a Metroidvania, and it does a phenomenal job allowing you to explore and understand at your own pace. The graphics, sound design, music, and game play are top notch. I have one complaint, that being the spikes in difficulty due to the incredible precision some areas may require. In particular I was getting very frustrated with a part where you must build velocity on a hanging cage. I spent nearly 20 minutes on that one single part. It's more than possible that its due to a lack of skill on my end, but it felt ridiculous. I love how the game doesn't hold your hand, but at the same time you can't expect people to figure things out 100% on their own. _childDocuments_.review: I was happy to show some support to dunkey and I really hope this first release proves to be a success for BigMode and the dev Billy Basso.This game has a very charming look and feel. The environments are beautiful. I'm unsure what the player character is. A blob? A goomba? A sentient rock? It's simple and it's cute. The game's palette is dark, so every splash of color really stands out and appear luminous. The vegetation, the water and the various decorations make the rooms look more lively and dynamic. Overall, the whole aesthetic makes the world mysterious and strange and invites the player to explore.The mechanics blend well with this mood. The first items I found were firecrackers, matches, a bubble blower and strange eggs. You're not a fearless one-woman-army like in Metroid. This game really makes you feel like a small blob conquering the odds. Acquiring the bubble blower felt especially good as the game introduces you to the bubble mechanic first so you already know how to use this item the moment you get it and you can see what new possibilities have opened up for you.The difficulty isn't too daunting, but the game offers you opportunities to test your skills. The first bubble room I found, I wanted to push what was possible with the mechanics and tried to climb to the top. Achieving that goal felt rewarding, and gave me an edge in the confrontation that would follow.The puzzles were nicely designed. They often push you to investigate first, but they feel intuitive enough. New puzzles and game mechanics are introduced at a rapid pace so every room feels fresh and nothing seems too repetitive.Even though there isn't any tutorial, the game explains itself very well. If you've seen Egoraptor's video on Megaman X, you'll surely appreciate how organically you come to learn the rules of Animal Well.Overall, my first impression was very positive. Animal Well is a nice addition to the Metroidvania genre with a beautiful atmosphere and creative mechanics. It's an impressive feat for a studio made up of only one small dog. Super Mario Bros. 2  Knack II.  guns /10

_childDocuments_.review: Will try to minimize spoilers, play this game! Puzzle-focused metroidvanias are an interesting twist on what metroidvania fans think of when they hear "exploration focused gameplay". Usually, the more combat focused games like Metroid and Castlevania are what draw me to the genre, but a puzzle focused one with good mechanics and gameplay can make for a really unique experience. I am really glad Animal Well delivered on this idea in style. Even though it strays from the titles we have come to know and love, it still gives nods to other games ().The game tosses you right in, and you are left to figure out the mechanics through experience and the subtle cues the game gives throughout. It can take some time to grasp what the game expects of you with certain mechanics, but usually it becomes evident when right path is forward, and you're left to think on a puzzle for a bit. The game has a pretty engaging learning curve, and you get choices, especially once you play around with items. The one annoyance I had was that the locked doors that require keys are the same colour as the closed gates that you unlock with buttons. From far away on the TV, it took me time to realize I could progress because I thought a key door was a button gate. Similarly, some areas look very cluttered with detail, so it can be hard to pick out platforms in some areas, but the detail is always stunning and it doesn't hinder gameplay much.The item names themselves don't sound like anything crazy, but in practice, the puzzles have a lot of variety and lead to some of the coolest "aha" moments I have ever seen in a game (). Encounters can sometimes feel "boss like", but the game is never setting the expectation of bosses, so the simple setups of some of them didn't bother me. Even the regular enemy encounters are often immersive, because the game's environment is more subtle and quiet, until animals break the silence and even jumpscare a little. It's cute, yet unsettling, and a sense of massive relief comes when the game finishes, because in each room, you question what's safe.This is probably the only puzzle focused metroidvania I can recommend right now, at least for a first play through () it's excellent and pushes the boundaries in a lot of ways with it's gameplay and vibes.

_childDocuments_.review: Games like this are why I roll my eyes when I hear people complain about the quality of games these days. There will always be an overwhelming number of low-quality titles in circulation, but developers like Billy Basso will always be working behind the scenes to deliver something memorable and worthy of passing on to your peers and loved ones.You won't find them yapping on Twitter or YouTube; you'll find them working hard to deliver an experience like the one you'll hopefully purchase after reading this review.'Animal Well' is a unique gem in the platformer/Metroidvania genre, offering a nonviolent gameplay experience peppered with rewarding puzzles. Its ability to balance charm and unease is a testament to Basso's design methodology.When you play this, go in blind, exercise your curiosity, and soak in all the magnificent details it offers.Thankful I purchased this; I hope you do too.

_childDocuments_.review: Very minor spoilers, just warning you because this game is best played blind. There's more to it than meets the eye.- - -Some of the coolest Metroidvania mechanics I've ever seen, married wonderfully with a slightly "Outer Wilds"-style sense of discovery that's very addicting. Unlike Outer Wilds, this is a game I could actually replay without being completely robbed of the experience, although I don't think any of the reveals here hit quite as hard as the kind of gameplay/narrative cohesion you get in Outer Wilds. Don't get me wrong though, there were several times my jaw hit the floor after shouting "no way!" when learning something new. You can bet I immediately attempted the equivalent of Metroid's bomb-jumping and shinesparking upon unlocking some of the movement-focused upgrades early on. The implementation of power-ups can so easily feel like a "lock and key" type of design, but most of the tools in Animal Well are so handy and multipurpose that you'll be using them constantly.Gorgeous artwork and atmosphere, I was consistently impressed by the volumetrics and reflections. The technical wizardry on display here is beyond my comprehension.This game runs deep. Every time you find something new, you peel back another layer. I've completed most of the "second layer", by which I mean I've gotten the second ending and already have 4 of the final late-game collectables required for what I can assume is the final "true" ending of the game. I'd like to keep going, but I think I'm a little burnt out. Hunting down all of the secret eggs took a lot out of me, as I was constantly searching the map over and over again to find a single clue towards the next bit of progression.The game flows wonderfully at the beginning, in the "first layer". Progression feels swift and very open-ended. The second layer has a lot of moments that feel much more arbitrary and unnatural. You get something that only has a few specific uses, unlike the early game items that feel so much more versatile.I really appreciate the lack of direction and heavy trust placed upon the player, it's probably this game's greatest overall strength. But that doesn't change the fact that hunting down some of these final secrets without any hints or minor guidance can get pretty boring and obtuse. I do want to uncover more, but after all that tedium in the final stretch, I'm not quite feeling it right now. Massive respect to the players who can invest the time into learning all this stuff, I don't know how much I want to see online at the risk of robbing myself of my own discoveries later down the line. Granted, once we reach some of this "third layer" stuff, I think I'm out by that point.Highly recommended overall, no question. It's commendable to see a modern title so focused on secrets and discovery, even in the age of the internet and instant access to spoilers and guides. Jump in blind, and see how deep you can go.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10Despite its mix of secrets, puzzles, and metroidvania level design, the open-endedness of the individual puzzles and overall direction, as well as the detailed map, make it surprisingly easy to find some way to continue forwards both quickly and satisfyingly.  I only ever found myself lost during post game, and there was only a couple times where it didn't just feel like I was being obtuse about specific puzzles I was already aware of.  The unique and memorable environments also make it much easier to find your way around, and the detailed map makes it very easy to get to these memorable areas efficiently.The music is pretty bare-bones, even considering the game's moody, atmospheric tone, but both the visuals and sound design are absolutely enchanting.  The pacing is fantastic, as rare as that often is, the post-game builds onto the core perfectly, and the replayability is fantastic with the many branching paths, skips, alternate solutions, and difficult extra tech. _childDocuments_.review: (SOME SPOILERS, also this is based on first playthrough where I only went to the first ending, I'll update this review once I dig deeper into the game if my thoughts change.) I've seen a lot of people who absolutely love this game, and the only the actual criticism I've seen directed at it is either people with huge skill issues, or people just complaining about the keyboard controls. I really enjoyed this game, but I don't think it's a masterpiece like many claim, at least not for me at this moment.The core metroidvania approach here is great, as it's main feature is the way that it foregoes combat, instead focusing entirely on it's exploration and puzzles to avoid and traverse around enemies. Out of all the metroidvania's I've played, this one reminds me the most of Super Metroid, and as great as that game is, I'd definetly argue that SM's combat is probably it's weakest element. So to take a similar approach but without combat is something that works quite well for this game. I got stuck a couple times and got a little bit frustrated, but that's the metroid formula at it's core, unless you really strip down the sense of exploration like with a game like Metroid Dread, it's inevitable that you'll get lost. I think this game is clearly well-designed enough that getting lost isn't a problem as I generally was able to figure out what to do after each pick-up or door unlocked, and the map is pretty easy to traverse through once you discover each area, so backtracking isn't tedious. Visually, the game is obviously very beautiful, such a sharp aesthetic with the scan lines which really help it feel unique and retro. However, something that might be controversial to say is that I wish the game had more visual variety. From what I played, I feel as if a lot of the areas look very similar, without too much distinction between them. There are some different shades of blue in different areas which is nice, but it dosen't have the same visual variety that a game like Hollow Knight, or even Super Metroid. For me, part of the fun of those games is the actual discovery of each area, and seeing the new theme and aesthetic of each new location. This game dosen't really have that, as the very most you'll see is a new shade of blue for each room and maybe a couple new background elements, for how much this game's visuals and exploration has been praised, It's weird to me I haven't seen more people talk about this. To summarize, the game has a timeless, memorable aesthetic, and the things in the areas like the puzzles and animals are memorable but the actual environments themselves just aren't memorable visually.Really, that right there is honestly my biggest criticism of the game, which shows just how good it is. The other closest thing I have to criticism is how the game's soundtrack is pretty limited, but It's very clear that the lack of music and the focus on the great sound design is a core design principle, so well I did sorta miss something like the masterpiece soundtrack of a game like Super Metroid, In this case, the game is fine with out it. That's pretty much my main thoughts on the game. I don't quite love it yet like many other seem to, as from what I played, it felt like a fun game that pays homage to a more classic style of game design. I think i'll be back though, as I imagine this game has so much more to offer through secrets, as the abrupt ending alongside cryptic final areas gives me a feeling that there's much more to see outside the main game. I've made a lot of comparisons to Super Metroid in this review, and that because not only are they very comparble, but Super Metroid is just straight up one of my favorite games of all time, and a big part of that game was that it literally got better on each playthrough for me, so who knows, maybe this game will work the same way for me.The last thing to note of is the price. Now for what this game offers, I think it's a very reasonable price, however in comparison to games like Hollow Knight or Terraria, it's on the pricer side of sprite-based indies. Really that's not because this game is overpriced, it's because those games are just so underpriced. If you've got the money, play this game. If you've already played those other games, play this game. However, if you are very strapped for cash and haven't played some of the other heavy-hitting indies, I would be lying if I said I wouldn't reccomend waiting for a bigger sale. TL;DR Great Game, worth the price, but dosen't feel like a masterpiece to me.

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well is a "puzzle" platformer with a focus on exploration and lots of "optional" content.This is a low/no combat game. There's no generic means of fighting everything that can kill you.Whatever narrative exists appears to be purely contextual. There's no dialogue or text boxes.Your character awakens, you explore the world finding a variety of tools along the way and eventually you reach the credits. After completion you're then left to continue exploring for any secrets you've missed.The game has a nice retro-style with a horror sheen that bleeds into both the sound and graphic design.This is well executed in that many areas are unsettling to be in. Whilst it's clearly the developer intent I do not know how well the exploration theme is served by this.Structurally the game is a metroidvania with a very novel set of abilities.I found the "puzzles"/progression locks fell in to one of three categories.1) I needed to understand some specific new interaction in the current room2) I needed an ability I hadn't found yet3) I had all the knowledge/tools and therefore the solution was obvious.This is where the game all falls apart for me and why I won't be exploring more. Animal Well is very good at teaching the use of the abilities you gain, with certain rooms acting as intentional blockers where if you've not understood a certain aspect of an ability you can't really fudge it with others. The problem with Animal well comes after you've been taught and acquired abilities. Usually games will ramp up complexity by requiring novel combinations of tools. Animal Well just shoves linear strings together and shoves a timer on top. The timers aren't particularly punishing but some parts of the game do require a surprising amount of setup after failure and on a couple of occasions and found myself quitting out to the menu and reloading because getting back from the nearest save point was faster than restarting the puzzle in game.Having hit the credits the game hasn't managed to sell me on continuing to scour the game for secrets so my time with it is over.Overall I think the game is going to be divisive. Many players like me are going to walk away wondering what the point was. Others are going to be digging for weeks at the secrets left on offer after the credits.Edit:Following watching a streamer check this game out I've thrown some more time at this. There are definitely better puzzles and secrets to find beyond the line to the credits. I'd say my opinion of the game is more positive than it was when I initially reviewed this. However the game is still no better at selling itself and I expect quite a few people will continue to be like me and bounce off when the credits roll.

_childDocuments_.review: There's more indie metroidvanias out there than you can shake a stick at. It's a very crowded genre, with some absolutely staggering titans like Hollow Knight, Guacamelee, and Blasphemous. There's a few mainstay mechanics that are pretty much mandatory, such as a large map with gated exploration, where getting new upgrades open up paths and backtracking to try old zones with new movement methods is encouraged. As a result, it's an intensely competitive game of both staying true to the roots of what people enjoy while at the same time standing out with your own unique elements. And in that regard, Animal Well succeeds. I think one of the biggest things to note is that this is a puzzle game. There are enemies and danger, but "combat" is nonexistent here. Even the most vicious beasties you fight are just another piece of the puzzle you have to maneuver around. The idea of removing combat from metroidvanias is strangely alien, but looking back it's obvious how well it works. The other being the progression methods and explorations, and Animal Well does some cool stuff with this regard as well.I don't want to spoil too much of the details - much of the fun of this game is figuring out how the puzzles work and what you can do and slowly uncovering stuff - but I can say that the actual items and mobility options are a fun spin on the usual, and each one has its own little secrets you can figure out that add fun dimensions to the gameplay. It's very good at making you feel smart when you run into something, and the enjoyment I've gotten out of solving these problems.And of course, the art style is top-notch. It's pixel stuff, but the atmosphere is immaculate - gloomy and wet and with a strange tinge of horror to things. It feels as if I'm just this lonely blob guy wandering through some animal-infested underground complex trying to connect these odd pieces together. Melancholic gloom is very popular in indie metroidvanias, and while nothing has ever topped seeing the City of Tears in Hollow Knight that first time for me, Animal Well certainly gives it an honest try.It's good. It's really good. And somehow it's only THIRTY FOUR MEGABYTES in size. Worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: there are these inherent "metroid like" instincts ive had since quite a young age, the way some of the 2d metroid collectibles challenged you to really use your resources, or break them through "exploits" was always one of the best joys i've found when playing the variety of games i've come across. ANIMAL WELL presents itself without introduction, and it enamored me the same way 2d metroids would throw you into the wild and leave you to figure it out. it would seriously quench that "i wanna try it my own way" urge to leap and bounce across rooms, and i loved how it would boost me to collect a ton of eggs early into the playthrough, but by extension this was also that double edged sword that would put me stuck in my own self manifested box of challenging myself to bubble myself through the longest gaps or thinnest holes. and i loved that, because there was always a way to solve the thing at all, the game had an ending after all, right? and that assurance made me appreciate the game 10 fold because you had to have designed this game so many times over to truly be able to call it Non Linear. it pratically BLEEDS passion and you can sense every drop of it. its amazingthe urge to solve something never really manifested itself in my mind as "oh i LOVE puzzle games", i always found that i squinted at the idea that people liked puzzles in this naive "ew rubics cubes SUCK LOL" mentality, but now i truly think i have a newfound appreciation for intricately designed puzzles meant to be solved in the context of its own tools. its ingenious what this single dev has been able to procure from his craft.i could have gone on to talk about the in♥♥♥♥ingCREDIBLE art of this game, or its size, or all of its other charms, but it really is that non linearity and ingenious design to be able to push each and every room of the game to the brim with passion and care. all i could really say is thank you for the treat, and congratulations for finally being able to put out a game you've been holding onto for so long, mr devalso the chinchila ears flop when you step on them LIKE WH- AOOUGH i absolutely ate this game up. its amazing please play itPS, i would really really love to see a GDC style talk of what you did for the rendering engine, and how you leveraged all the rendering tricks to run amazingly, please consider!

_childDocuments_.review: There's not much more I can say that hasn't been said before, but Animal Well is a master class in show-not-tell gameplay chock full of aha moments and more depth beyond your initial (of which there are many) credit screens than perhaps any other game. There are many stopping points at which players can choose to gracefully bow out of the game, but for those who enjoy increasingly obscure and esoteric mysteries, puzzles, and secrets Animal Well is the deepest I can recall. Some of the post-game puzzles start becoming SO mysterious you should not feel ashamed if you want to declare you've had your fill with Animal Well and move on or look up solutions on the internet, but I think that is a strength of the game and not a weakness; This well is, ironically, as deep as you want it to be. The innovative uses of the tools you find are always fun when you discover a new, unexpected use of something you've already been using for hours, and who knows what percentage of those secrets of the game have yet to be discovered.The style, the sound design, the fact that the entire game is literally only 33MB, you can just go on and on about this game. Suffice it to say, I would recommend every single gamer, whether they are specific fans of metroidvanias or not, to at least try this game at some point. Yes, it is that good.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game, but I think it's a bit oversold.I was never really captivated by it like some seem to be. It's a bit thin on content and extremely mild in difficulty. Should you not be the type interested in bumping into corners and crannies looking for collectibles, you'll barely need a few hours to beat  it. I don't do the dollar-per-hour calculus because I think it's a bit disingenuous, and for as short as this game is, it will still take up a night or two of your life for less than it costs to see a bad movie with no popcorn.Overall, it seems to be dedicated to maintaining the ambiance for better and worse. It wants you to chill and respects your ability to chill on your own. If you want to take the tools it gives you and find some other way to clear a room, it's fine with that - we're chill bro. It feels almost a bit TOO laid-back. There are maybe a handful of moments in the game with any sort of expectation of precision gameplay, and the majority of it is going to just be real easy, breezy puzzle platforming. Most of the puzzles felt, to me, too easy to gain much satisfaction out of, usually amounting to no more than "use the item we just gave you". To it's credit, every room in this game invited something new, but it never really caught me much off guard.I respect a game that respects me; the best thing about this game is how hands off it treats the player. No tutorials, no dialogue, no quest arrows, or anything of the sort. All of the learning is organic, all of the problem solving is left to the player respectfully. It takes a brave creator to allow their work to be interpreted (played, in this case) by the free will of the beholder (player) but it's a beautiful thing when it happens. I kept feeling like I had to bring up Outer Wilds in this regard, that's how hands off this game is - perhaps even more so. I think this may have factored into the overall difficulty though, and really it might feel too easy out of fear of someone missing out or getting stuck.On the whole, this game left me wanting for more of an experience, more of a work. As it stands, it feels a bit on the simple side and left me a bit unfulfilled. There's all this ambiance and environment but it never really builds to anything substantial. It's not really going to leave much of a lasting impression on me, is basically what I mean. Whether that's a reason to avoid it or not, I leave up to the reader. I think it's a worthy experience and if you LOVE metroidvania games or atmospheric self-driven experiences, it might really be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really fun and intuitive game. The design is excellent. It's really easy to tell where you can go or what you can do. But it does require a lot of experimentation. Note that you can use the bubble wand to place bubbles below you. Took me too long to realize that and I was sort of stuck for a while.The game has one glaring flaw for me and that's how enemies behave. They are incredibly annoying. It's exceedingly easy to get stuck in a spot and then just get instantly killed by the enemies. This issue is most prevalent with me with the dachshund dog. What an annoying area of the game.Genuinely frustrating. Still recommending the game, obviously, but this issue comes up way too often with other enemies such as the crane with the long neck.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: A gem in the platforming/metroidvania genre. Stunning pixel graphics & physics bring every level to life and the clever puzzles keep you hooked instantly. The soundtrack is an absolute delight, perfectly enhancing the experience.I can't believe that this game was created by a solo dev. Highly recommended. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: If you take a look at my profile, you'll see a bunch of  reviews for games that I love. It's because I like to get awards, and people generally don't really read these super long reviews. But forget it, even if no one reads this, I just need to get serious for a moment about Animal Well.I'm going to break this down into a few parts to keep my thoughts organized. But most of all,  for this work of art, .I'm going to borrow from Dunkey here when he said Animal Well is "the lasagna of video games... only once you peel back its layers can you understand why you enjoy it so much".It's a  game in every way, but most of all in its visual presentation and the seemingly hundreds of sounds you can hear at any given time. Every area, every creature, and every pixel is placed with intent, and I could stare at my monitor for eternity in awe of it all. I've spent hours so far just interacting with swinging lights and hanging flora. The Well isn't just an area in a game; it's a Techno-Sylvan world brimming with electrical animals of all sizes and formats. Speaking of the titular critters, let's talk about gameplay!I cannot stress enough how much fun it is to figure out the inner machinations of Animal Well . The decision to not add a tutorial or to offer any sort of help to the player is what makes it so magical. The player will find several objects throughout the game. Though their functionality appears to be very simple at first, you'll quickly realize just how much you can do with these secretly-sophisticated tools. Like when I learned you could  the .But the well runs deeper than that, pun intended. You play as a little blob who must navigate its way through a beautiful but treacherous environment. You may find yourself lost, confused, or even afraid sometimes. But if you just take a second to look around and enjoy the little things around you, you might feel refreshed and ready to take that next step.? Animal Well is a game that reflects life. At the end of the day, we are all really just small blobs of meat that tumble and fall through life. We make our own victories, and the decision to quit means you miss out on what the world has to offer. I cannot believe 34mb of storage on my computer has gotten me to contemplate so many things and compelled me to write this long-winded novel, but I digress.The gameplay is awesome. The puzzles never feel impossible, but you'll have to reach into that empty skull of yours every so often if you want to find all the secrets. Speaking of secrets...The developer has stated on several occasions that this game contains secrets that "may never be found". Excuse me, but ? You are presented very early on with the concept of "secret eggs" that you can find, which are aptly named as they are quite literally eggs that are secret. For most people, the hidden content will end there. But I have this gut feeling that there is so much more to this game than meets the eye. Not just other hidden easter eggs, but a whole world that once was. What's the story anyway? Every frame invites you to look around and guess. There are statues of animals EVERYWHERE, but why am I this little slime guy? Why are there  and ? Did people live in this world? Is the well underneath a whole different ecosystem and environment? Who are those blue ghost square guys? After my relatively short time played, I am left with so many more questions than answers. I cannot wait to keep playing, but more than that, I cannot wait to keep .10/10. I cannot see how anyone could play this and not enjoy it. Thank you again for this absolute gem, and thanks to  for still reading this, for some reason.P.S. thanks to my gf for the awardI STOPPED PLAYING HADES 2 TO PLAY THIS GAME, ENOUGH SAID. SERIOUSLY.
