_childDocuments_.review: Very engaging and interesting metroidvania with a few twists in gameplay and mechanics. The atmosphere, music and visuals make for a great experience that can be scary and startling at times (the kangaroo can eat a ****) but it´s also very beautiful and can make you feel a bunch of different ways. The bossfights are perfectly crafted and very different from each other, with deep puzzles and rewarding level design. I guess you can summarize my experience of the game by saying that I wanted to 100% it, I wanted to find every egg, secret room, tool, candle and rabbit (and I almost did).
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't been this sucked into a game in a very long time. The puzzles and mystery are so engaging and set within a wonderfully immersive atmosphere. To me, this is a masterpiece that gives me that same satisfaction as beating a difficult boss in Elden Ring after you uncover a hidden mystery. Meticulously following the little clues the dev cleverly placed throughout the world was very rewarding, and I still have many more to find.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Such an fun and inventive Metroidvania. The ambiance and air of mystery about everything made me want to keep exploring more to see more of this strange world. And the way the game handles ability unlocks and environment interaction is so unique and different from anything else I've played in the genre. Making a puzzle platformer Metroidvania is something I don't know if I've ever seen before and I doubt anyone has done it like this.Took me about 10 hours to see the credits but I know there's still a ton of mysteries hiding for me in this world.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Overhyped because of some silly youtuber (typical youtube culture like a bunch of brainless parrots all giving the same meme review instead of actual helpful analysis). But, still not a bad little game with beautiful graphics, hence the still positive recommendation.This is a "survival" game so to speak with metroidvania level design. Secrets are somewhat obvious if you are paying any sort of attention to your surroundings for the most part (remember that hilarious comment from said silly youtuber that the community would still be finding secrets years from now, instead of the 5 minutes it did take? That didn't age well). The story aspect is mostly fun to breeze through though I did not have the motivation to continue the end game content (more secret hunting with new tools and an extra "boss" from what I've heard) Bosses are essentially chase sequences or environmental puzzles while they shoot things at you with one in particular being extra obnoxious due to having to traverse a large chunk of the map while not being able to check the map because time does not pause for that.Atmosphere was nice, music had its moments, but mostly if you are playing this game it is because you are a sucker for incredible pixel graphics.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic puzzle platformer with unique set of tools. Animal Well has a fantastic seamless tutorial system reminiscent of games like Portal. You slowly unlock abilities and are required to figure out their use to proceed, but there is an extra layer of combining abilities together that gives incredible depth and tons of secrets to find.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: A good metroidvania packed with puzzles, secrets, and challenging platforming—and no combat. It has distinct visual and audio design and a quirky, mysterious atmosphere. There is no handholding and much of the fun is in discovering on your own how to use tools and navigate the environment.Difficulty is up to you ... kinda. You can "finish" the game with just moderately difficult puzzles, though note that you won't be able to avoid some challenging platforming, so if you hate that, then this game is not for you.The bottom line is that these "basic" puzzles are excellent and very satisfying. Even when they are not too hard, just solving them is fun and cool and delightful.But the optional secrets get much, much harder. Like, super extreme obscure detective work hard. People are still wondering whether we've discovered them all. And that's where the game gets less fun, at least for me. Combing the world for potential clues involves lots and lots of backtracking, basically trying every tool in your toolbox on every pixel on the screen. Actually, just getting to the "basic" ending will likely involve considerable tedium of this sort. After getting as far as I could, I turned to online guides and found that I had barely scratched the surface on my own. And even following the community-found solutions was tedious and frustrating.There's definitely a group of players who considers solving very hard puzzles to be rewarding enough to be worth the frustrations. Indeed, one puzzle is designed to be  solvable through the collaborative efforts of such a community. Those people clearly had an amazing, rewarding time with it. But I imagine that the vast majority players would be more like me: I find it annoying that cool game content is basically inaccessible without getting out of the game and into the forums. The dev is even on record saying that he didn't think people would  discover some of the solutions. This is just not what I was signing up for when I booted this combat-less metroidvania. I did not expect .OK, but still. If you are OK with not seeing everything, and/or looking things up, then there is so much to enjoy here. I had a good time with  and tip my hat to the dev for putting it together with so much passion and attention.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well effortlessly redefines the boundaries of exploration and puzzle-solving within its mesmerizing pixelated world. At its core, the game is a recursive journey, every discovery leads to a new layer of mystery, and every solution unravels further questions, pulling you deeper into its beautifully enigmatic loop.It’s a cerebral experience that rewards creativity, curiosity, and thought. Animal Well respects your intelligence, offering puzzles that make you pause and ponder. The joy of solving them is amplified by the realization that the solution was always within reach, hiding in plain sight.It's a game that makes you feel clever because it is so cleverly designed.As the honor guard of the emerging Metroidbrainia genre, Animal Well sits proudly at the top of the list, merging the interconnected exploration of Metroidvanias with the mind-bending complexity of puzzle games. The result is a game that doesn’t just encourage exploration, it demands it!A "Well" worth diving into.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well stands out as a 2D puzzle platformer that felt similar to playing Hollow Knight for the first time. Its an incredibly unique world, that rewards trying to solve puzzles in your own way. The soundtrack, and the looks of this game are amazing and the puzzles are constantly leaving me feeling proud to have solved without getting stuck too much. I'm excited to finish searching for all the secrets, as well as anything that comes from this game in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic puzzle metroidvania. Shares some ideas in common with ESA, La-Mulana, Tunic, Rain World, and others and is so much more than "just another" indie metroidvania. Absolutely give it a shot - the unconventional skills/items and the unique animal-based puzzle designs are fantastic. And there's still a bunch of extra fun puzzle stuff for me to solve..!
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Fun puzzle platformer/metroidvania with  an impressive interconnected and non-linear map. Playing through to the main ending was fun but not super long, about 5 or 6 hours of play time while being slow, but if you're a completionist there is a heck of a lot to find. Tons of small puzzles for eggs, lots of hidden secrets and areas to uncover; I don't even know if I got all the main tools, but a lot of rooms had a variety of ways to get through so you can solve things as you see fit.Overall just a really well designed game that was a fun, short experience that can keep going pretty much as long as you want it to.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This feels very much like Environmental Station Alpha x Knytt Underground. Just know that those who prefer combat heavy metroidvanias like Axiom Verge or Hollow knight may be disappointed as the puzzles are the star of the show and some of them are not for the dull of mind (COD fans may need to look elsewhere...)  I know nothing of Dunkey but I look forward to seeing more from Billy Basso. It's exceptionally well made and certainly a slap in face of triple A studios.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR – this game is !Aside from a couple of boss battles, the gameplay is very chill, which I love. The multi-layered progression (collecting eggs → collecting bunnies → ) is very thought-through. The metroidvania structure has well-placed shortcuts, so that backtracking doesn't feel like a chore. There is even an puzzle about the shortcuts!Platforming is great, it is decidedly  like in precision platformers. As far as I remember, there was exactly one (!) instance of requiring rapid input of just  button presses for collecting one of the bunnies. All other tricks require just two. The Disc and Bubble Wand items provide unique fun traversal methods.Most puzzles are easy to solve. The game has different ways of giving hints to solutions. Some puzzles are harder. Some of the end-game puzzles are extremely obscure. But using online tutorials and guides didn't feel like spoiling these puzzles, because some of them require additional external knowledge.The best way to describe the technical implementation is uncompromising. The installation is less than a hundred megabytes with . The game launches instantly. All the transitions in the game are instant. And the developer has added support for CPUs from 2000s. To me, as a software developer, this is very pleasing.Plays very well on Linux – I am currently using Proton Experimental. Full XBox controller support (Steam Input isn't needed). Originally, there , but it was fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not for everyone.I am in love with animal well, just today it made me lose track of time and for me, that is quite rare to find these days.I mainly bought the game because I want to support Bigmode as a company, but it just happened to be a game in one of my favourite genres, so I have bit to say.I am no where near completing this but the map is HUGE, it feels like it never ends and at the moment it's honestly feeling kind of overwhelming. Most areas you go to you can't "complete" until you progress further in the game, but because the game is so big it gets hard to remember where you've been and where you haven't. Combine that with the fact that the teleport system is very limited and that checkpoints can be quite harsh, and backtracking through the maze-like map can feel daunting.I do recomment the game to lovers of the genre, but I do not think it's a good first game for people getting introduced to it. My one recomendation is that you USE MAP MARKERS!!! I only found out about them 5 hours into the game and it feels like I could have a tighter grasp on it if I started using them sooner. Also, as soon as you get the pencil, write down why you couldnt' advance in an area, so you know exactly what you unlock when you get new items.I will update this review when I'm finished with the game with my thoughts then.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not typically a puzzle game person, I get frustrated too easily. I'd typically rather play a combat-focused game and die repeatedly than stop and think about a puzzle. That being said, I found the vast majority of these puzzles a lot of fun. I like how the game doesn't explain things to you, but instead encourages creative thinking. None of the puzzles are overly difficult, and when I found a creative solution to one, it felt incredibly fulfilling. Would recommend. Wish it was a bit longer, but it felt like it use its time very well.

Try your best to find secrets and do puzzles by yourself, but at a certain point, you do literally NEED to collaborate so don't feel guilty about googling.My ADHD went all-out on this game and I became absolutely obsessed. 10/10 would hyperfocus for 25 hours (in total) again.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: At time of writing I have completed the main game and intend to try the post game. Animal Well is stunning. the artwork and colours are breathtaking and the interactivity of the environment is a joy. I only wish for more music. Most of the rooms feel quite quiet even with the ambient soundtrack. (Additional note for those who may struggle with sound tracks such as Celeste due to it causing anxiety: I found a few of the songs in this game to have the same problem, there is a setting to turn off the music if you also have this issue). As for gameplay I loved the exploration in particular. If there is something this game excels at it is making sure you dont feel confined, I only had one spot that I really felt "stuck" where i couldnt just leave easily. The puzzles are challenging enough that they feel satisfying to solve but rarely hard (assuming you understand the tools available to you) enough that a guide is required. The world builds a lot of intrigue and lets you figure things out on your own, both the story and the mechanics. This may be a draw to some, which i totally understand but honestly i felt lost in both ways. I have no idea what the story is, if there is one. Hopefully someone makes a Mossbag-style video for this game because i haven't a clue what happened. As for my biggest issue with the game: it doesnt tell you what your abilities do. Or what buttons they are even mapped to. It took me 30 mins after picking up the map before i figured out how to use it. The game mechanics have many nuances, some of which are supposed to be a surprise, but i really struggled just getting the base functions understood as I was just expected to figure it out. As a newer gamer this sort of intuitive understanding of games is something I dont have and makes this game mildly inaccessible and often frustrating to me. Overall, Animal Well is a good game. But it is one designed for avid gamers and people very familiar with the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful little metroidvania full of mystery, intrigue, exploration and some incredibly fun and addictive puzzles. Easy to beat in a sitting if you're smarter than me, but the egg hunt will continue your explorations even further.I want to highlight the soundscape in particular. Mysterious, ephemeral and haunting are the only words I can use to describe it.So basically like Halo 2 and 3 combined.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This may be slightly controversial, but I think this is one of the best games of all time.The puzzles, the aesthetic, the sound, the polish... Everything is masterfully done here.As someone who loved ElecHead, this is the maximalist version of that genre of games (knowledgevania?).This is the best trend of games in a long time. Please, recommend me more games like these.10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: lots of exploration and puzzles, as a guy who hates metroidvania's exploring the map of animal well surprisingly fun. The game does nothing to even indicate that there is more hiding within each nook and crannie but the sense of exploration and scale that the map creates makes it fun to search for things on your own.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably in my top 3 of Metroidvania games i like. The "main quest" part of this game reminds me a lot of Super Metroid (which is my n1), although the gameplay itself is completely different. There's still a lot of experimenting with the tools you get, but the combat is basically completely removed (which for this game I like a lot). But the game really shines in the post-game where during my playthrough I started to focus on collecting everything and solving all the puzzles, which was by far my favorite part of the game. It reminded me a lot of playing FEZ. At this point of the year probably my favorite release of 2024.

_childDocuments_.review: Great Metroidvania with tons of cool secrets. I don't want to spoil where to go but I do want to say: this game isnt linear at all, you can go wherever you want to and you will be able to progress there. This is something I wish more metroidvanias did this. The game is also gorgeus, it looks absolutely amazing and the enviorment is so interactive. Also this game is 40 MEGABYTES LIKE HOW?!?!? Would highlt recommend this game, I wasn't the biggest fan of the post game content, but I think that's just a me thing. 8.8/10 highly recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: Came across this game while browsing the store and was immediately captured by it's pretty scenes of nature and stylized animation plus the dreamy music that accompanied it.This was the first game in a long time that I've purchased and played without having first heard about it online, and it was worth every penny. The soundtrack is surreal, and the music during exciting moments is top notch. I love the contrast of light and dark. The abilities are incredibly unique, each time I got a new item my expectations were subverted from that of generic movement in any other Metroidvania.10/10 Loved it!
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: A fine and good game... until the post-game. Play until you hit credits (6-ish good and fun hours), then put it down. Avoid the post-game. The glaring problem is the game makes promises it cannot deliver on that hurt the experience dramatically.Everything before you hit credits is good. However, when you hit credits, there are many unsolved mysteries to do. This makes the promise that there's cool and interesting and rewarding puzzles left to solve, or even that you're not even really done with the game yet. After all, it was only 6 hours, maybe there's a whole other area left to do..... That instinct is wrong. You're done with all the fun parts. Put the game down now. There are still puzzles left, but the solutions to these puzzles are obtuse to the point of farce. You've been seeing these unsolved puzzles all game, enticing you to try to solve them... but they will only lead you to waste hours of time. When you eventually look up the solutions, you'll discover that you'd never have gotten them in a million years, and you have had your time and energy wasted. This feels so supremely bad that it soured my experience with the main game retroactively. Don't make my mistake. Buy it on sale--hell, buy it full price!! Hit credits. Put it down.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: An impressive show of what a Metroidvania can be. With no combat whatsoever, you're tasked with solving countless puzzles using only four tools, but those four tools are so versatile that I found myself accidentally cheesing the game constantly. Super short, but this is an explorer's dream and feels like something akin to Tears of the Kingdom with how versatile your skills are. Plus, most importantly, it really makes you  like you're in an animal well.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I am few hours into the game and found my first flame and the journey to get it was truly magical. Interactions with the animals are the highlights of this game, finding clever ways to get around the animals or use them to get around sometimes never gets old. The tools provided are a work of genius, props to billy basso. The sheer amount of secrets in this game is baffling but finding them is so damn rewarding and shout out to dunkey cause if wasn't for him this game would have gone under the radar for many gamers. Now i know what halo 2 meets halo 3 feels like.(Overall- 4/5)

_childDocuments_.review: Tight play controls, evocative world building being a little blob. Gameplay loops explained naturally, but you're going to have to pay attention to collect the many hidden eggs. The music is very certainly a vibe.The game also looks good with CRT scanlines off. This small game has an options screen! 5/5 so far, i want to play more at 1:00am when the world is asleep and I am awake in this weird "animal well" filled with secrets and tight mechanics.edit:also otters.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: The exploration in this game made me lose track of time so badly, when exploring just having a goal and then doing other stuff because its just there at the time feels so enjoyable. Towards the end (credits ending), I often couldn't tell if I was not understanding the solution, or that I didnt have the tools to complete the puzzle. Resulting in retracing over and over the map, unsure what to do. This was my first metroidvania type game so it was probably just being unfamiliar, but it became a bit tedious.Going to keep playing to see how much I can get completed on my own.Overall the art style and vibes, incorporation of music and themes was extremely polished. I loved the atmosphere and I wouldnt have stuck around anywhere near as long as I did if the world wasnt so well made. Very happy with the game overall.Final notes, almost got the second ending by myself but needed a bit of help with a handful of things. Absolutely worth it. Payoff felt really good.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: After one hour of playing this is exactly what I hoped this game would be like. The first items you unlock already have a lot of depth to how you can use them, I have no idea how long it'll take me to reach full completion but if the amount of secret eggs is anything to go by, then probably a very long time.edit: after 10 hours of playing I gotta add a trigger warning for giant ghost dogs chasing you across the map while howling terrifyingly.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: As far as metroidvanias go, it's more frustrating than fun. I understand trial and error is important but this game is overly punishing for minor slip ups and it's just downright infuriating. I'd not care as much if save points were more frequent, or if puzzles stayed completed after leaving the area, but as it is currently it's just so bloody frustrating to try to progress OR backtrack. I imagine it's great for people who like rage games, but I don't fall into that category so I did not have a good time here.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This is almost exactly the metroidvania I'd been looking for: Fun, puzzle-oriented, and light in combat. There's a LOT of stuff to find and collect, which can be very rewarding. But I'll say there's a few things that, while cool, are a bit too obscure. Nothing critical to the gameplay, which is fantastic.  But as someone who passes through the metroidvania style games once-in-a-while rather than playing a lot of them, it felt like a little bit much.I do very highly recommend the game. It's not a huge undertaking, it's fun, and the environment is absolutely gorgeous, especially a few areas. They did some really cool things with this, and I'd love to see more games like this.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun and has a cute aesthetic, but has a couple of difficulty spikes that are extremely frustrating with bad checkpointing. There's also some areas which require you to do a sequence of button/switch presses in various rooms, while having instant kills which reset the entire area's state causing you to have to redo the whole sequence - why not just have the regular respawn mechanic that happens when you fall into water instead of resetting you several rooms back at your save?I feel like it could use another quality of life pass before I can recommend it
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: A truly exceptional puzzle game with platforming elements. A small amount of simple systems build off of each other in interesting ways, and while this is a short game, it genuinely belongs among the greats of puzzle games. With roughly 5 hours to reach the end credits, is an extremely enjoyable time. However, there is a lengthy, interesting post game which takes another 10 hours or so (I was quick on the uptake and marked every odd thing on the map during my first go around so returning with new tools was easy). There is a post-post game similar to Fez or Tunic that I enjoyed but people may be frustrated by, however the first, second, and third endings are incredibly satisfying. This game is worth your $25. You'll be hooked in the first 30 minutes, and stay hooked all the way to the end.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to review Animal Well without spoiling some aspect of Animal Well that I enjoyed discovering either on my own or with the guidance of a friend.If you like complex puzzle games with an insane amount of depth, you will enjoy Animal Well. The metroidvania foundation of the game rewards you with immediate feelings of progression while leading you through the puzzles and layers of the game. Every tool has multiple uses. You may discover one on complete accident and then scour the map trying to find all the places where you have seen that cue before.However: I did stop playing because there was a point where I ran out of steam on the map scouring... I knew what I was looking for but I could not find all of them. I would like to go back and complete this game someday. As for now, the 21 hours I spent on it was worth the money and time spent.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game. Despite being able to get "100%" of the steam achievements in only 13 hours, there are so many more secrets to find. This game goes above and beyond, from its clever puzzles down to its gorgeous art style. To discover the deeper secrets in this game, you have to be a special kind of someone. However, even if you don't meet that requirement, you can still find enjoyment in the game's countless puzzles and platforming. It is truly a masterpiece of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: So I wanna say i came into this experience incredibly skeptical. This game has been promoted like hell by a big youtuber since it's his first in his new gaming company. I will say that, without honestly a few minutes in. This game is pretty good. I think the price is a little steep for other experiences but I think that's just other devs giving a really solid price as opposed to this being overpriced. The gameplay is engaging and well placed. I dont like forgetting to save.I'll give a few review once I finish but so far the game is good and I reccomend giving it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This was a great experience!Animal Well wasn't afraid to do things differently. It stayed clear of the usual metroidvania power up tropes like double jump, ground slam, wall jumping and the like, which made it feel really fresh and exciting for me play. The puzzles were excellent and the game didn't outstay its welcome up until the ending.I know alot of people love the added puzzles after the ending and I did too for a while, but the backtracking and some things being undecipherable for my brain meant that I quit after 15 achievements.Small ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ aside I would highly recommend this game and would rate it a 9 out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Quite a unique Metroidvania. It's not focused on your typical upgrades, combat and boss fights. Instead, it's all about atmosphere and puzzle solving. Exploring the world was a relaxing experience, with some unexpected scary moments. Animal Well doesn't hold your hand and wants you to try things out. Because of that figuring out puzzles and understanding game mechanics felt very natural and rewarding. It took me around 7 hours to beat the game, but now it's all about finding every Egg there is.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well is a unique game that combines aspects of various different genres to create something special. This game takes the metroidvania style but uses it as a base for the main focus of secret-hunting, similar to FEZ. The game just throws you into it, as the player awakens from their pod and is set to venture into the different biomes of the well. As they explore, they find various different tools to use, different animals living within the well, and many, many secrets to find.I enjoyed my playthrough of the game thoroughly, as I loved the organic nature of learning the mechanics of the game. I'd get a new tool, mess with it a bit to understand it on the surface, and then use it in a new way accidentally hours later. While that may not be nice for some people, it fits the vision of this game perfectly. As a puzzle game, I also really appreciated the different "layers" of the well. It makes the game more accessible to people who aren't as keen on the puzzle-solving aspect, allowing them to choose how deep into the well they want to go. The spritework done for the game is very pleasing to look at, really giving off the proper vibes that each area of the well is trying to present, especially when working in tandem with the lighting engine. Overall, Animal Well is a great game, and if you enjoy solving puzzles with some light platforming, you'll probably enjoy it as well!
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: definitely a fun metroidvania experience, with a mysterious ambience, and quirky powerups.  you definitely feel small and powerless and yet wondering at this world even as you gain cool abilities.  it has atari adventure vibes imo, where you pick up new items and the animals react in unique ways.major nitpick: 25% of my deaths are due to switching to the wrong item, and that increases dramatically in certain time-sensitive sequences.  you can only use one item at a time, and switch with L/R (or in a pause menu with Y).  using L/R is super frustrating, especially as you get new items that change where your gotos are.  please allow users to rebind buttons to whatever items they want.  you don't need a dedicated button for "Use" (e.g., eat fruit), you can use up or down for it.  you'd have jump for A, you could rebind B, X, L-trigger, and R-trigger, and then keep Y for the remaining items that you can switch through with L/R .  things would feel a lot less frustrating in certain areas if you could build out your preferred control scheme.  i guess i'll have to practice using Y to open the menu to choose the current thing i need, but i don't usually like stopping time like that in video games to grab an item i need as it can break immersion/flow for me.minor nitpick: i'd love to have short hop (by not holding jump as long) and long hop (holding jump longer), but i understand having a single jump height gives a retro feel.puzzles are fun and platforming is great (apart from the nitpicks).  overall an awesome game.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This is a rather unusual Metroidvania. A lot of the time, developers fall back on a lot of the same kind of upgrade-paths for movement when it comes to the ways of traversing the world: doublejump, walljump, wallclimbs, swimming... so far, animal well has used none of those, all of the new abilitys I unlocked to get stuff done are either completly unique or so rare that I can't think of any examples of the top of my head.The visuals are also rather striking. It is a pixelart-game but the neoncolours rly give it a unique vibe(although I will warn you, if you are sensitive to flashing ligths, make sure if the firecrackers are ok for you to look at before buying the game, since u do need those somewhat frequently and they can be a bit intense for the eyes). The game also has a surprising amount of physics, grass and chains all move when you touch them, there are reflections in the water, weird mist-effects, it all looks very nice.The last and most important thing I wanna praise is the actual gameplay. the game uses basically no tutorials outside of a few short "press Button to X" effects at the start. the rest of the mechanics are taugth to you via actual gameplay in a very natural way, which I wish far more games would do. Instead of forcing you to sit around and read huge walls of text, the game has enough faith in the player to be able to figure out what to do through context-clues. The puzzles are engaging, which is surprising for me to say, since I am not the biggest fan of puzzles most of the time and overall its just a very good package. If you play a lot of metroidvanias and want to stick with the genre, but are longing for something new, this might be just the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: It's like Halo 2 meets Halo 3 made by one guy. Super atmospheric metroidvania and the artstyle is really well done. There's this sense of creeping dread as you explore more and more, and yet it feels like the more you unravel the mystery deepens. Tons of secrets and side content, all in a tiny <40MB package.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very pretty game that is just simple and good. I didn't like the final boss fight exclusively because I am bad at platforming, but the entrancing beginning and solid middle were great.I wish there was some kind of quiet, ambient music that wasn't just the music found in save rooms and with enemies. This is a good game with about 11 hours of content, and if you're used to this kind of game, you will have engaging content back-to-back.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: So I'm not super far into Animal Well, but HOLY HECK IS IT GOOD. It's not even tagged as a horror game but it has made me flinch from its immaculate atmosphere alone more than any other game I've ever played. The mechanics are simple yet enjoyable, and learning to use them in creative ways is required to make progress. Be warned however, the game seldom tells you anything. I keep a notepad file open to write down any new discoveries I make!
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: just when they said it couldn't be done they found a way to combine halo 2 and halo 3. The added well-like components make for an enjoyable platforming metroidvania. so far really enjoy the art style and unique atmosphere, tho can be difficult at times I intend to see this one through to the end bit by bit.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Going in to Animal Well, I wasn't sure what to expect; it didn't resemble many of the rogue-likes I was used to playing. I can tell you without reservation that any doubts I had were quickly discarded- this game is wonderful, whimsical fun. As I went through the colorful pixel art environments, hunted for collectibles, and solved some very clever and imaginative puzzles, I found myself totally hooked by the whole package offered here. The game plays excellent on the Steam Deck, making it even harder to put down during the day. Fans of pixel art platformers (like Fez) will find a lot to love here.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I put up some content on the YouTube, URL =  , but short version: I've been testing Animal Well on and off for nearly two years. I've seen how it's evolved. And I've seen teases of puzzles that may take months for the community to figure out. I strongly urge you to get through the first 8-10 hours spoiler-free, because you'll have plenty of excuses to look online for hints and help once you reach the game's first "ending."PC-specific notes:* DualSense works really well, as far as vibrations and second-speaker compatibility. If you own a DualSense, use it.* Ultrawide support doesn't exist, because the game blacks out rooms that you're not in anyway.* Runs great on Steam Deck with all settings maxed out.* I've seen at least one puzzle that seems to be easier to solve on PC than on other platforms. That's all I can say.

_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually review games that I refunded because it doesn't feel like I gave the game a fair shake, but maybe others will have a similar experience to mine. I bought the game to support the YouTuber I like even though this isn't exactly my go-to style of game; it still seemed interesting and fun so I figured I'd give it a shot.I had an alright time in the beginning but there were some frustrating design decisions like missing one jump sending you back not just to make jumps over again but also to solve puzzles you've already solved. That's not very fun and it's especially weird given the game already lets you respawn with no punishment when you miss a jump some of the time. There's a health bar but most of the time I died was due to something taking away all my health in one hit.I also found the game too quiet, maybe I should've played with headphones instead of speakers but pretty much all I ever heard was footsteps and the occasional roar. The graphics are actually where I had the most problems. They reminded me of old point & click games that had you searching the screen from top to bottom, leaving no pixel unturned. Everything blended together and made just seeing where to go more of a tedious chore than a genuine puzzle.Eventually I got stuck for a while, I couldn't even go back to where I started, I circled the same five or so rooms over and over again before I gave up. I looked up a YouTube guide and saw that the correct way was actually right in front of me the whole time, I thought I was misunderstanding a puzzle but actually the correct way just blended in so well with everything around it that I didn't even notice it.I looked at other players' reviews and saw a trend of people complaining that the more you play the more the game leans into that pixel hunting aspect and that pretty much settled it for me.  is probably going to be great for lots of people but I just couldn't jive with it at all and even when it wasn't frustrating me it wasn't really impressing me either.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, I know, you're gonna get butthurt that I'm giving this game a negative, but you ought to blame Steam for the binary review system. And, yes, I read the negative reviews and they all are a bunch of noobs complaining over stuff that only happened because of skill issue (that may include not knowing where they were getting themselves into for those who hate a reasonable amount of backtracking and paying attention).The only reason I'm giving this a negative is because of a simple thing that it will take me a while to get my point across. If you don't know this game, this review will depict a very accurate picture of this game so you'll know exactly what you're getting yourself into and, if you agree with me, you'll wait for a better discount which would make this game worth the money. This is best played without spoilers. It's all about the wonders of immersing yourself in an unknown universe with its own set of rules. If you have an OLED with HDR, you'll get to experience the amazing contrast between the darkness and the many sources of light. Sound design is charming and immersive as well. What you can expect is tons of puzzles and backtracking. You have a map and you can mark stuff so you don't get lost in the sense of where you need to explore and what you might wanna go back to in order to see if you can unravel a new pathway or a hidden chest. The thing is that you don't know what you have to mark, but on the surface of this game, you can manage fine. At least with my so so IQ I managed. I remember most of the stuff and everytime a new tool was introduced, I kinda knew what new concepts I had to mark on the map and backtrack again. New tools unlocked = more backtracking.Now... here's where the issue begins. The game is more than that. Much more. The dev went Mercury Rising, or for a more recent reference for the youngsters, although with less naunce, The Da Vinci Code. The quantity and depth of the codes for you to solve is crazy! There are even codes that needed the help of the community to jointly figure out how to get passed them. There should be a specified subgenre just so people know what they are getting themselves into, like Souls-like. When you hear Souls-like, you understand that it's an Action RPG based on iframes and bosses that clip walls and all that crap. If there aren't other games like Animal Well, future games like this should be called Animal-like.At this point you might be asking yourself 2 questions:1. Are these codes so overboard?2. Why did you give it a negative review?Yes, they are. If you want spoilers to get the exact picture, check the videos linked bellow. If you haven't played the game, you might not grasp how much more than the base game those are, but you'll get the level of difficulty. You'll also get that you wouldn't in a million years have the patience and probably the IQ points to go after these secret puzzles, so you'll be left with watching videos and, if you really want, copy every single thing that has been done, which you'll basically be turning yourself into a macro. Fun, right? But, speaking for me at least, I just wouldn't ever find this emotionally rewarding. Dopamine wouldn't ever be triggered by going after this. LOL. And there's the potential to leave a bad taste in your mouth after beating the game and learning that there's a whole other side to it that you'll never beat. According to the dev himself, it was even designed for it not to be beat, but people did beat it. Regardless, emotions happen regardless of reason. You'll beat the game and think: did I beat the game? Oh, well...And the negative review is because you gotta take into account that if the game didn't have that, it would probably be cheaper because that demanded a lot of work. If you like that kind of thing, it's worth it, but as this wasn't disclosed and I wasn't into that part of the game, it was wasted on me. If the game was just the base (first and second ending) with a cheaper price, it would be an instantly positive review, but given all the f'ing effort that was put to offer the third ending (and then some) with the expensive pricing on an indie game, I just can't endorse it. Wait for a better discount - 40 to 50% I'd say! (I wish I could get a partial refund...)In fact, that even reminded me of another movie that could be used as a reference to what I'm trying to say. Back To The Future. That scene when Marty McFly played guitar at the dancing club, people were enjoying and suddenly he changes the tune and everyone was like "WTF? That's crazy and I didn't sign up for this."How to Unlock Each of the Figurines in Animal WellPuzzles before the game was even released *Steam is misbehaving and not displaying the newly added videos here.P.S.: Thanks to FuryForged for the videos. Otherwise we wouldn't know about all of it.Final (maybe) edit: I voted it for Game of the Year and edited this review for TheSteam Awards.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: A great little indie. It manages to convey a lot of passion for how simple it looks. It's a Metroid game 100% (not to be confused with a metroidvania which has RPG elements, none of that here)! You'll find power-ups that allow you to enter new areas or complete puzzles. Here's some gameplay if interested What really impressed me is how almost every screen has some sort of secret or puzzle.There's no hand-holding, no tutorial, the game just says "go". It feels like going down a rabbit hole. Each zone has some new gimmick to keep gameplay fresh.. also boy this game feels good to play, the controls are SO tight.If you enjoy this type of game, you'll enjoy Animal Well. Great job Billy! And thanks Dunkey, I would've never heard of this game without you.EDIT: I finally beat it. My first run I did everything myself without looking online, and once I got to the ending it just hit me how special this game is. It felt oddly immersive considering the graphical style.When the credits rolled, I was still missing 5 hidden eggs, so I looked them up online and unlocked the secret ending.. by this point I felt satisfied! A little burnt out with how complicated those last few eggs were...then I saw there was another layer of secrests for the secret secret ending. Looking into it, it would be another few hours for me to complete the final challenges, and would require me to go step-by-step with an online guide. All-in-all the super ultra secret ending has a personal message from the developer and Dunkey (I just looked it up online, I ain't gonna bother with it myself).Still, this game was a surprise hit for me, I certainly didn't expect to cherish my time with it, but I'd recommend giving it a try. Keep in mind, it took me a while to get roped into it, but once I was man.. what an adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to describe the depth of this game, and I don't want to spoil it. Let's say it's an amazing Metroidvania with more complicated puzzles than you can imagine lurking under the surface. Keep your eyes and mind open; everything, and I mean EVERYTHING, could be a breadcrumb to another puzzle. I wish I could forget I played it so I could play again!
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: took me 19 hours to 100% it, and although many hours i was full of rage and confusion, and lots of the time aimlessly searching the same places over and over and over, this game is really a masterpiece and is just so beautiful.definitely feel welcome to use guides when youre stuck because it can be so confusing, and you might just need to backtrack to one tiny little stupid spot in order to progress30 aussie bucks is a tonne of money, but considering how masterfully this game is made, I'm fine with the cost

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of my favorite games of all time. The art and environments are beautiful, the sound design is amazing, and the puzzles are great. It felt like every time I acquired a new item, a problem that I was having was solved, and I was impressed by the multiple uses that each item has. While a lot of the game is a relaxing adventure, it also has riveting tense moments that keep you engaged. Overall, it's an amazing game and I couldn't recommend it more for people who like exploration and puzzles
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Platforming, aesthetics, and world design are the keystones of this endearing exploration game. Animal Well's puzzles, aside from the exceptionally obscured endgame on offer, are easily digestible and fun; particularly since the environments are a treat to circumnavigate as the well expands. There is no explicit invitation from the game: have a blast bounding into a new zone of puzzles or flee to an familiar room to triple-check for secrets and soak in the singular atmosphere while you do. This is an itch-scratching and must-have experience, regardless if it ends at 10 or 25 hours.Pro-tip: the bubble wand is infinitely more useful than it initially presents, get creative and play with it.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Dripping with atmosphere, this game is a wonderful puzzle platformer Metroidvania about a lil blob guy. Tons of secrets, amazing level design, fun gadgets. The entire enjoyment of this game comes from figuring out as much as possible completely blind. Only frustrations are some bothersome enemy encounters and lack of autosave, leaving to some annoying backtracking. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: A top 10 metroidvania experience with incredible exploration and puzzling. Great music and sound combined with a beautiful color palate and visual style to create a unique mood. Layers of depth that go beyond just beating the game. The tools you acquire are fun to use and really change how you approach obstacles. Lots of thought went into each aspect of Animal Well. A little frustrating at times, but overall, great fun to play.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Really, really, really good. Layers give away to even more layers, the game is so big. Well-hidden secrets open up entirely new portions of the map. Beautiful, pure game design. Literal hours passed by in an instant without me realizing. Once you hit a flow with uncovering secrets, it's incredibly difficult to put down. Not to mention the creativity and complexity behind some of these puzzles. Billy Basso is not human. How one man could put this together is absolutely mind boggling.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Animal well is a simple metroidvania collectathon. It has very hard platforming sections. There are few indicators of where to go in the game. Ultimately, the game is relatively short with 5ish areas bosses. While there isn’t combat technically, there are frustrating sections where the enemies can kill you causing you to need to redo 5-10 minutes each time. I’m happy I played it but ultimately disappointed in the value, the difficulty, the length, and the lack of direction.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well is a good metroidvania, and has extraordinary world design and phenomenal puzzle design, although several puzzles are quite difficult, and any completionists will unlikely be able to 100% the game without online assistance. The abilities and items gained through progression breaks the conventional bread and butter abilities of typical metroidvanias. Rather than the standard double jump, dash, and wall climbs present in some way, shape, or form, Animal Well presents an array of unorthodox toys such as a bubble wands, frisbees, and yoyo's as its means of progression, each with its own unique (sometimes hidden) uses.There are, however, aspects that may dissuade other metroidvania enjoyers from Animal Well. For one, the complete lack of combat may deter players who enjoy the fast-paced action of games such as Hollow Knight,  and its relaxed and simple movement may be contrary to what fans of the fluid movements in Ori and the Blind Forest are seeking. Animal Well is a game that is best played at a relaxed, leisurely pace.Nevertheless, if you like old-school metroidvanias where you truly feel like you have just been dropped into an unknown world free to be explored, Animal Well is a game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: It's like I'm experiencing FEZ for the first time in a completely different way. The joy of learning and figuring things out while nothing is said. It's beautiful. Everything about it.(In terms of beautiful visuals as well, you can turn the scanlines off if you don't like them.)Also only 33 MB with zero loading time for anything, the developer clearly knew what they were doing.10/10, this game feels like it was made for me. While it probably won't be for everyone, in my eyes it's perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Where do I even begin? Animal Well is an incredibly well-designed metroidvania with plenty to explore, collect, and just mess around with. This is genuinely the most fun I have had with a game in a while, especially with one that I was not anxiously anticipating for months until release. This game brings out your creativity a bit, solving various puzzles and even coming up with unique ways to get to certain places on the map (whether it was intended or not). I found myself just messing around with the different items you unlock for hours and I'm not even done with the game yet. If you love platformers, puzzles, and exploring in your games, then this is for you. I couldn't recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I can see why this game would appeal to certain players but I really can't get into it. There's no combat, which I now realize is probably a good 50% of why I play metroidvanias. The traversal is a bit too punishing for me; dying can set you back 5-10 screens and forces you to redo large sections of platforming. The art direction is interesting but I feel like I'm straining my eyes the entire time trying to figure out what I'm looking at. Most of the puzzles I've encountered are fine but I'm bouncing off everything else that my patience wears too thin to really enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: dunkey said he was only going to publish good games and then billy basso makes fez 2 my jaw is on the flooreven if you arent keen on the arg elements and esoteric postgame (which im always a fan of), the main campaign is a great deal of fun with countless fun puzzles that spin your tools on their heads each and every turn, with an atmospheric gripping environment crafted so well that not a single tile is left emptythis game is GOOD. like REALLY GOOD. as a fan of metroidvanias, puzzle games, and exploration, animal well is a beautiful experience and i hope it gets talked about in years to come
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: it's a good little game, although too short and sadly very little story (even environmental storytelling). would be elevated by some story context to the great atmosphere. feels a bit empty as is now. this is sadly the way with a lot of games nowadays, they tend to think graphics and atmosphere IS story, but they often fall short. however, fun puzzles but could be a 10/10 with some more work on telling a compelling narrative.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: There are so many great things about Animal Well. The puzzles are challenging and just the right level of difficulty to still be fun. The tools you get as you progress really open up the world in an exciting way. I also like the atmosphere and art style of Animal well. It has a haunting vibe that also feels like home in a way. I do think you'll have to be OK with zero direction/hand holding to enjoy this game, as well as understand there is no traditional "combat". If you're ok with those two things i think you'll enjoy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: A captivating and unique Metroidvania experience. As someone who doesn’t usually particularly enjoy Metroidvanias, I’m kinda shocked at how engrossed I am with this game. It just oozes atmosphere and begs to be explored, rewarding the player with fascinating puzzles and environments in every corner! There are also tons of secrets it seems like, and I’ve already stumbled into a few.This is just masterful game design. Each room is so well-tailored and designed that there have been a few times I’ve put my Steam Deck down and said, “Wow, well done.” The developer knows what he’s doing.Give it a try even if this isn’t usually your cup of tea! This is a special one.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well is a mechanically great game, with literally nothing else going for it outside of hype and meta-gaming. It should win 2024 GOTY, but only because it's been an abysmal year for games.It's also incredibly overhyped and a tad overrated. This is an amazing metroidvania, with gorgeous graphics and artistic style. The world building, atmosphere, and platforming are top tier.But it's difficult as hell, esoteric as ♥♥♥♥, and has literally zero story or lore. I wish there was something here, an overarching story, even if it was a simple one. But the game is just a bunch of un-connected, really fun, platformer challenges.Don't get me wrong, there is a GOAL. Get the four flames. But there is no explanation why, nor reason to do anything outside of "to do it."The "end-game" is also incredibly lame. It's frustrating and un-fun, and you would never be able to do any of it on your own without outside knowledge. This is a literal design choice, and I think it's a bad one. There are so many things that are just literally never explained to you, and unless you cheated, you would have no way of knowing about them. It's engagement bait for "lore youtubers".I would give the game an 8/10. It is good, but I personally have to dock points for the complete lack of narrative and some bad design choices.

_childDocuments_.review: Mfw Dunkey's studio published a metroidvania of all things as their first game.In reality, Animal Well is a lovely game. The tools are simple, but have an added layer of complexity that goes beyond just the immediate puzzle usage. I was certainly not expecting how much mobility the tools allow. But it's definitely fun to discover flying on the disk for the first time. The puzzles aren't too complex, but let the player feel accomplished that they figured it out on their own. There are a few "metroid moments" but exploring usually reveals the solution. If all else fails, internet.The atmosphere is thick in this game, from the wall-of-sound style music to the sample-esque sound effects. The addition of scan lines by default was actually genius and evokes the isolated feeling of playing in front of a CRT late at night (it can be disabled, too). Sometimes, however, some sections are TOO dark, and make it hard to see the solutions to the puzzle. On that note, it was also a little disorienting to move from screen to screen and have to find your little fella again.Overall, a stellar first game for Bigmode. Maybe the Dunk will provide was with a JRPG next.

_childDocuments_.review: is a really made game that has a really nice cadence of exploration and discovery if you allow yourself to go in blind. It's crazy this is the work of one person, but the strong vision and the level of detail in design is consistent throughout, so it was a worthwhile effort.Nostalgic-burdened outlook aside...While it's true that  is technically a , a kind of game that evokes a particular set of guidelines, I wouldn't say it's standard—at least in my experience.  felt like it focuses more on exploration in key areas that many  tend to relegate to combat challenges, equipment, spells and those sorts of collect-a-thon sort of things. Saying more feels like it would spoil the fun, though. It's good to see modern games come out with the same feeling of discovery, or the same density of secrets. That said, of all the games with twists, secrets, rewards and all the other dopamine-laced hits that are empowered with the tease of the "reveal",  is one of the few games where the effort to remain oblivious to the game was well worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: So I've beaten the game (at least I think I have), and I have mixed feelings. Sometimes people say they wish they had a sideways thumb for games they thought had a lot good, and a lot bad. At first I was thinking of making such a review, but thinking it over I realized it's overall good and that I could recommend it.But there were parts of the game I didn't like. The inventory management is bad: switching between objects is painful, you either have to circle through them or pause the game and select them in your inventory. 90% of the time this isn't a problem, because you aren't under any time pressure; but then, the game decides to throw you puzzles that requires both precise timing and quick item switching. The puzzle room to hit one of the switches to get into the manticore room is one such awful puzzle: It requires you to quickly switch between the slinky, frisbee, and bubble gun at break neck speeds while doing platforming. This was awful, and the game isn't designed to handle this.There were other sections of the game that required overly precise platforming, I'm thinking of the 4 box puzzle leading into the M. Disk Shrine, and this is made even worse by the fact that you'll be getting chased through this section of the map as you're trying to complete the game. I felt the designer could have introduced some more leniency here, as otherwise this game is accessible.That being said, I gave this game a positive review. I was able to get to the end with only a little assistance from the forums, and this in game that has zero dialogue, zero explanatory text. This game is a masterclass in showing and not telling. The aesthetics are amazing, the designer is a master of getting you to feel what he wants you to feel in a given scene. When he wanted the player to be calm, I breathed a sigh of relief, where he wanted the player to be shocked, I said a verbal, "OH ♥♥♥♥." The game fools you into thinking it's hands-off, but it's actually very carefully designed, and the magic you feel when you progress was hand-built by its creator.The items are all novel, if a bit janky. I felt like the designer almost flew too close to the sun with the bubble gun, which is difficult to use, but overall it all works. When you see a particular L shaped indent, you think, "Ah, yoyo." The slinky ended up being my favorite item, being used in a way that gave me a sense of childlike glee.The puzzles are generally reasonable, although some are frustrating as I already mentioned. My opinion is the designer could go back and tweak a few of them that are overly demanding on the player. The inventory management system should be redone, or the sections where you're in a time crunch to use them removed.My feelings about the final encounter in the game are a microcosm of my feelings towards the game generally. When it's introduced, I was pleased, being taken completely by surprise and enjoying the sudden introduction. Then, I became irritated as I had to juke the stupid thing to complete the puzzles, wondering when this part would finally be over. Finally, having got past him, I realized I was pretty satisfied with the whole thing.It has flaws, but Animal Well is WELL-worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: It cost $1 NZD per megabyte which sounds like a lot until you realise you get 1000 units of joy per kilobyte.It doesn't take long to conclude that this is an excellent game.The environment is stunning and the soundscape seriously elevates the whole experience. It's so immersive and enthralling that you'll probably play half the game in your first sitting (at least you think that's the case, in reality you've barely scratched the surface).The puzzles range from trivial to moderately challenging. Nothing is likely to stump you for long and mechanically challenging sections are few and far between (especially once infinite bubble jumping becomes second nature). You're unlikely to ever feel the need to look at a guide. What makes the puzzles so fantastic is the tools you use to solve them. I won't spoil anything but just know, the developer implemented some truly fresh ideas that ALL hit the mark beautifully.Last thing I will mention is the secrets: they're EVERYWHERE! The sense of exploration surpasses all games I've played besides Outer Wilds. I thought Hollow Knight would keep the title in this genre for some time but Animal Well is a constant flow of pleasant surprise and discovery.Also, the animals are fantastic. It's a weird thing to say but it's actually a big deal when it comes to making the world feel alive. Animations, audio and behaviour really shine. The dogs are my favourite. Our goofy little protagonist often ends up as a chew toy but it feels warranted given our spherical nature.10/10. Just play it.

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well is a video game that shows and doesn't tell.Nothing that occurs in this game will ever be explained.No one will talk to you, no one will guide you.Everything that occurs in the game you will uncover yourself.There's a always another secret around the corner.Every single thing that stands out in this game has a purpose. Every detailed minutia will eventually come full circle and you will be caught with your mouth agape at the ingenuity required not only to solve the puzzle, but to also understand what thought was put into the puzzle to create it.Animal Well is a masterclass of artistic expression. There are almost no songs in the game, and the rich atmosphere of The Well will capture you and bring emotion to you in the strangest of ways.Animal Well is nothing sort of a religious experience. It ignites a wild and boundless curiosity within itself.

_childDocuments_.review: Animal well is a fairly low tension puzzle platformer.  But, actually its more than that.  If you've played Tunic, Fez, and the like you'll understand very quickly what sort of game this is:  Secrets upon secrets, upon ARGs, upon secrets.  Every item you get has an additional use that you can figure out if you are clever enough.  Every animal can be interacted with in a different way than you'd expect.  Every room has niches and holes and walls that you can discover lead to other places that lead to others ad infinitum.  It can get a bit overwhelming but the chill atmosphere and the fun platforming generally make it an enjoyable run all the way through.  The aesthetic is great as well, with soft low tension atmospheric music, interspersed with chirps and animal sounds most of the time, but spiking up to a chiptuney pulsing beat any time you enter a dangerous room.   The 16bit-ish art style some how conveys all manner of lush environments with ease that makes it clear that so much of what you see was not just copied and pasted, but crafted very specifically for the room you were in.  I loved the little capybara restroom especially.  As for difficulty, the game isn't absurdly hard, though there is quite a bit of backtracking while you figure out how things work.  Beating the game is just the start though because there are all manner of collectibles spread throughout the world and some ease of progression is locked behind them.  So get those eggs fella you better get those eggs.

_childDocuments_.review: Score w/o Context: 60/64 EggsThe Context:I have a deep respect for movies that minimize their dialogue, leaving a lot of the narrative up to the director. A quickly exchanged look can convey just as much info as a monologue in a fraction of the time if done well. Similarly, leaving a player to their own devices in a game world and designing it in such a way as to be decipherable and explorable with minimal help can be mystifying. I think Animal Well largely succeeds at this goal, creating an easily navigated world with intuitive designs around every corner. Being a combat-less metroidvania lends an air of familiarity to the environments you are dropped into, but also a bit of helplessness. It isn't a danger-free game after all, you just can't really fight back. These two tones mix well together, with the pull of unexplored biomes contrasting with the fear of the unknown constantly during my 12 hour jaunt. It was always worth it to push through however, if only to find the next gorgeously animated creature or flexible puzzle solver (aka item).These items almost all had multiple uses throughout the journey, and all were unique in their form and function, controllable yo-yo being my personal favorite. The puzzles I mentioned before were vastly solvable with clever thinking or usage of your inventory, minus a couple beats near the end that I found a bit more unintuitive and esoteric. Exploration and backtracking also mostly hits the mark of this genre, with each journey back getting quicker and easier with practice. Good thing too, as this game has layers to its world rivalling only Tunic that I can remember recently, and you'll find yourself going back and forth a lot. This brings my to my final standout of the game, the map! It's incredibly helpful with gaps and highlighting possible new avenues to probe. Without it, I would've been lost many more times. Still, I never got tired of digging for new secrets, and that's a triumph of design.

_childDocuments_.review: So it's a Metroidvania. Fine, fair enough. It looks and sounds good in that charmingly retro sense- in the "intentionally retro, not because the guy who made it can't do anything better" way. But that's nothing that hasn't been done before. You need to go further to realize what makes this game great.So I did my first clear. Found many eggs, did the main story progression, all of that. Also find a weird [redacted by Logstar] by [redacted by Logstar] which raises some questions. Then there are all of the background features that get you thinking...that has to mean something.The thing that makes this game interesting is that it all does. Or at least I think. I'm not sure at this point. People talk about the layers. There's layer 1, which is what people will do for a completion, layer 2, which is the formal 100% layer, layer 3, which is a level where some truly strange, obscure puzzles come up that are a community effort and only for true completionists...and then there's layer 4. That's the thing. I can't say too much without spoiling but it feels like this game keeps going deeper. There's a solid Metroidvania that feels good including the 100% stuff. Then you go deeper and there are these obscure puzzles that it took a community to find. And the amazing part is it doesn't feel like we're done yet.In a certain sense that's both what's great and what's awful about Animal Well. The third layer is done. There is this sense of FOMO from when the community was solving these brutal puzzles since we won't be able to recreate that unless there are groups of many people going in blind together. The fourth layer may or may not be done...and that's what does it. Few games go this deep and still give the feeling that there's more we haven't found. I hope we haven't. I hope I didn't miss it.And no matter what you think of this specific game it feels like this is going to be a huge influence on the future of the genre. This is the beginning. It feels like, in the future, other developers, even big-budget ones, will start adding these deeper layers. I think this is the beginning of a new generation of Metroidvanias and that generation will do spectacular things.

_childDocuments_.review: Animal well is a very unique and fun puzzle/exploration game with lots of charm. It’s quite a simple game, although quite a bit of complexity is hiding in this simplicity. My first go at the game I had a good time exploring and interacting with all the environment and its animals using the quirky, funny items it has to offer.Everywhere you go there this charming cozy-ness to be found driving you forward to see more, get more, do more. There a puzzle and a secret every step you take yet they still surprise you in their inventiveness. “huh this is a fun new puzzle”, “wow cool concept”, “wow I had no idea this was here!” over and over again until you reach the enda nd its pride itself on you figuring this stuff out by yourself. The game will tell you absolutely nothing while simultaneously showing you everything, although a lot of the puzzles will be so clear and cleverly designed to the point of becoming trivial, at least the ones relevent for completion. Yet they are very often still fun to do and hard enough to be interesting.The ending was satisfying enough for me, even though its hard for anything to have a bigger impact when lacking any larger context for anything.The second go around was still good, getting the last eggs to be found is still fun because really you’re just doing more of the same, however at least to me its design started to get in the way a bit more here. It tells you so little that at some point I didn’t even know where to look anymore and even if I had seen some of the important stuff before it was often still not clear how it was important, or when, making you go back just to see if it’s important yet. A lot of it becomes easy to overlook. In the end getting the last couple eggs started feeling more like I was just going through every room desperately trying every item you can think of to find that hidden wall that I missed. Looking up at least the location of the last eggs made it doable but also way less satisfying.Needless to say I do not feel the need to dive deeper into its well of secret upon secret however I have a huge respect for the dev for going this far with it while still keeping the main experience very curated. And if you at all enjoy finding secret then you will LOVE animal well. The cute animals are a nice bonus.

Unlike a lot of metroidvanias, this one (more of a puzzlevania, there really isn't any combat to speak of) this one never made me groan at having to go "ALL THE WAY BACK THERE!?" because it is so densely packed full of stuff to do. _childDocuments_.review: A lovely, multi-layered experience. _childDocuments_.review: A beautifully crafted metroidvania. You'll be in for a puzzle/platforming experience that is satisfying for the eyes, the ears, and the brain. Animal Well is one of those games that you're better off not knowing anything else if you're curious about it and don't want to end up missing out on some of the amazing discoveries and aha moments it has to provide. Visuals are gorgeous, especially given the game's pixel art style, with vibrant and colorful sprites that react to the environment (and even to you shaking the game window!), breaks of light drawing the player's attention to the amazing backgrounds present throughout the vast map, and dynamic shadow, smoke and water effects that will delight you. Not everything that's important pops out, however, and for a good reason (more on that later).Similar praise can be given in the audio department. Background music is reserved for specific occasions, but sound is very much a big part of Animal Well. The world  alive, with dozens of animals, some of which cute, some of which less so, and others quite creepy. Sound enhances your experience throughout your journey, be it through SFX that complement your puzzle-platforming or music that sets the tone when you're being .Gameplay-wise, you're given very simple goals from the start, and it's up to you to decide how and when you'll be going for them. The developer has paid a great deal of attention to just about everything in this game, but specifically to the flow of the player's progression as well. You'll inevitably need to revisit some areas as you go around collecting items, which will allow you to further progress past some block that you previously encountered in a particular room and decided to leave it for later. Important routes are thoughtfully gated so that the player must have experienced enough of the game to be able to pass. Key items are accompanied by simple yet effective tutorials that teach the player mechanics very clearly with no need for text.In terms of puzzles, there are several layers of depth which are not all immediately apparent, but most of which will reveal themselves gradually through careful teasing of the player. Empty slots, suspicious shadows, strange gaps on the map will become more and more obvious with time. Curiosity and careful exploration are rewarded with secrets after secrets, ranging from extra consumables to very large sections of the map with extra puzzles, collectables, and/or items.As for some of my personal notes and slight criticisms, I must say that I thoroughly enjoyed the path to 100% achievements, although with some assistance from online guides which helped me get through the some looser clues or other items and collectables that I missed myself which would've been too tedious or time consuming to figure out compared to the enjoyment I would get from a pure solo experience. Some of the late-game items felt a tad redundant, too specific and not as well explained as the earlier ones. Also, due to some puzzles requiring a bit more creative thinking and quick platforming, sometimes I felt like it wasn't super obvious that a puzzle I was attempting was not yet solvable and I just needed a different item for it. A couple items required for 100% completion were in my opinion behind puzzles that were just a tad too cryptic. Finally, the quick switch system of inventory items, although super convenient, became a bit too crowded by the late game which made it annoying to manage sometimes.That being said, don't let any of these negative points dissuade you from trying out this amazing game. Dozens of hours of enjoyment will make you wonder how all of this content is able to fit in just 33 MB in 2024, which is just the first feat of art you'll experience when you install Animal Well. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I loved Animal Well. I went in totally blind and saw credits roll at just over 5 hours, and I recommend you go in blind too if you can help it. I like the game for the same reasons I like Super Metroid: it respects your intelligence and doesn't hand-hold you. It communicates a lot of mechanics to you just by trusting that you're a curious person that wants to figure it out, and you probably will. It's basically entirely puzzle-focused and there's really not "combat" like other Metroids and Vanias. The vibes are thick and overall it's a great experience. Maybe it's not the most accessible game if you're new to Metroidvanias or puzzle platformers but I don't think that'll stop you from appreciating everything this game has to offer.After I saw credits I was just casually running around collecting the things I missed and my friend tipped me off that the MAJORITY of the content is post-credits, which really piqued my curiosity. Not long after that I realized just what I was in for if I really wanted to 100% the game. The game definitely pivots here, there are some puzzles that you can't reasonably be expected to solve on your own with the tools the game gives you, and that felt kinda ♥♥♥♥♥♥ at first. But I stuck with it and tried to do as much as I could on my own. You will absolutely have to look stuff up in the post-game, but it didn't ruin the experience for me, it felt intended that you do. At this point I was so curious about what cryptic ♥♥♥♥ they shoved in the game so I kept pulling that thread until there was nothing (I think) left, and I'm glad I did.
