_childDocuments_.review: The sound design and visuals are beautiful. A lot of love went into this, I can tell. Unfortunately, right off the bat I was turned off by the backtracking. I also think the difficulty didn't scale appropriately for when you are first starting out. The bubble platforming mechanic created a punishing barrier to progression. For these types of mechanics, introducing a lower risk situation can train a player to advance to a more difficult version in the future. That is, if you want the game to be accessible to more people and not just an few folks that are very good at platforming. I prefer games that can be played by folks with many levels of abilities; games that help the player "get good" early in the game, rather than punishing them for not ALREADY being good. I am not requesting baby mode, I am asking for a warm up. Even World 1-1 lets you jump on a few mushrooms first before bullet bill hell. Celeste trains you how to use the double jump with low risk scenarios before asking you to traverse through spiky death corridors. You get my drift...I wish I could give this a neutral review as I don't think it is a bad game and obviously many people are already enjoying it. I hope to revisit it in the future when I have the time and patience to endlessly fall into a well.

_childDocuments_.review: Astonishingly incredible. The idea of a puzzle-metroidvania is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ genius. From the handful of experiences I’ve had with the genre, the combat has always been the worst part of the package. These games demonstrated engaging puzzles and encapsulating atmospheres, but dithered about with lacklustre combat; combat that is somehow presented as a third pillar of the game, as an equal to its atmospheric and puzzling counterparts. Neglecting this element to the extreme brings out the best part of metroidvanias (and is really, really fun to play). Becoming intimate with this huge web of puzzles, slowly unravelling it yourself, and reaching the bottom of the rabbit hole. It’s an incredible concept, yet is so simple and so naturally delivered that it's hard to conceive how new this game feels. As both a publisher and developer debut, this is an explosive arrival to the scene, and hopefully a sign of great things to come for both.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game! Loved the artstyle, audio and gameplay.Took me about 8h to complete the "main story", and about 20 to find all eggs - with a little aid by google.There are still things to do though.Definitely a controller game. I am a keyboard+mouse guy, and I was reluctant at first,but having played through it, I get why they recommend it.Most of the puzzles were quite intuitive and fun, and even if sometimes I thought"oh god, this will be annoying", most puzzles were pretty managable for me at least.It is quite a challenging game at times, as expected from a metroidvania-game,so be ready to die and try again many times. Sometimes the save points were a little annoying - I had to backtrack a lot of times after a death. I can't imagine what this game must be like if you don't understand how to use the flute...I did have to look up stuff on the internet, there is a certainchase sequence to do, and I didn't realize that was the way to go forward - and what to do with it. I also needed some guidance for the last 5-6 eggs, since I really didn't know what do do with one of the last items I got, or where to find the areas it is used in.I kinda wish there were ingame tools to narrow down where to look for certain things,because many things I only found by accident, very long scouting sessions or by looking it up online. On the other hand, it is a very good feeling to find out about things on your own, and it feels so much more rewarding than beeing led from one marker to another. There are a couple of tricks to aid with finding eggs,but certain stuff ist a little... random.Definitely recommend this game - it may not be everyones thing, but it is a fun journey for a good price with hours of entertainment.

_childDocuments_.review: this is what a videogame should be. looks great, plays great, sounds great. there is absolutely no handholding and it is scratching that itch for exploration, while giving you a lot of freedom. you can cheese stuff, you can "sequence break"  to find secrets from different entrances or to just skip a few rooms. here and there. whenever you get a new tool, a lot of new routes open up to you. nothing special for a metroidvania, but there are a lot of places that you think you can reach now and you actually still can´t. this creates a loop of "AHA!" moments and always keeps you looking for stuff you might have missed.studying the map is really fun and it helps you a lot when trying to find areas that you haven´t been to yet. the map stamps are extremely helpful as well, as long as you use them. they  can save you a lot of time that you would probably be spending by wandering around aimlessly instead. seriously, use them. as soon as you find something that you can´t deal with yet, or something that you just want to remember the location of, put a marker on it asap!secrets in a game like this are what drive me forward and i could not stop exploring the whole map, until i had all of these stupid little eggs. i got all the achievements (and a few more things) now and it still feels like i am missing a lot. speedrunning potential is really high and this might be the first game where i actually attempt to do some. for me, at least a 9.5/10. Thank you, Billy Basso, for making this game. I really hope to get an ANIMAL WELL 2 some day

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well is a good game. That said, it's not necessarily for everyone. There's very little handholding, and while the game does a decent job of generally indicating the directions you need to go for the critical path, you may end up lost at times. If that's an issue for you, consider giving this one a pass.Pros:* Basic movement is really well-polished and satisfying. Moment-to-moment the game is a joy to control.* The environment and atmosphere are really well-done. It generally feels very alive, and strikes a good balance between being threatening and oppressive.* There's a lot of cute bits in the game.* A lot of the puzzle mechanics, once you understand them, feel really rewarding.* The map unfolds in a particularly satisfying manner. There's several points where it loops back upon itself in neat ways.Cons:* Since there's so little combat for much of the game, it makes some of the parts where there _is_ combat somewhat more difficult than they'd probably be otherwise. This makes for some weird spikes in difficulty at certain parts, where you'll end up having to die a lot to a boss because there's not really a lot of great other spots to practice the same skills.* There's some optional puzzles that have extremely difficult solutions with early-game items, and trivial solutions with later-game ones (sometimes to the point that they're no longer puzzles). This feels like it cheats out a little bit of the reward for completing them early, since it's with some frequency a collectable that doesn't really impact things until you have all of them.* Better in-game tooling to allow the player to mark points of interest on their map would be helpful. The existing map marking is a bit rudimentary, which is an issue when you can't easily distinguish if an element on-screen is an interactive element that you can't/don't know how to use yet, or just flavor art.* There's some difficult optional sections that require a lot of precision and are very deadly and just a long, painful walk away from the respawn point, or failing a jump drops you to somewhere you can't easily return from. Some sort of late-game item or technique to let you set a better respawn/recall point would be very nice.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a metroidvania puzzle platformer with a lot of very unique ideas. I would say it is more or a platformer than a puzzle game and the puzzles are not very hard, but they are satisfying enough to solve. Interestingly it is possible to sequence break a little if you master the  but I get the feeling that the developer deliberately allowed this, as it is fun to feel like you are getting one over on the game a little bit. It is a similar feeling to the sequence breaking that is possible in antichamber. I can't speak for the developer but if I were to hazard a guess then it wouldn't surprise me if they were influenced by games such as Knytt, La Mulana, Toki Tori 2, and Vessel. If you like any of those games then you will likely love this. I'm not sure how much of the game I have completed but I have played for about 6 hours and it feels like I am down to finding the last few secrets now.

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well is a passion project by Billy Basso, an American solo-dev, in development since 2017. Another entry in the long-line of successful metroidvania-style indie games, Animal Well instead trades away any semblance of a combat system to double down on its puzzle solving elements. The tools available to the player are enthralling to use, with so many hidden tricks and interactions that the game slowly teaches throughout even the first few hours of its runtime. You feel like a genius as you experiment and discover how robust the mechanics truly are, and as you slowly unlock more of the game's world to explore.The world itself is enormous. Playing the game I found myself constantly remembering my experiences with Elden Ring, where no matter which direction you head there is such a vast swathe of stuff to do. Players will be hard pressed to find a screen that doesn't have secrets to find or puzzles to solve. Speaking of the puzzles, the puzzles are the very reason why its so hard to talk about how fantastic this game is. Everything I've described so far is available before you hit the credits the first time. The issue is, that is barely half of the game's content, and doesn't even scratch the surface on how deep the rabbit hole truly goes. In truth, everything above only serves to conceal , which give way to even more game than I ever could have understood at first. This hidden second half is why I can't say why Animal Well is truly my Game of the Year choice for 2024. Its something you have to experience for yourself.Animal Well has very little story, and despite that I still feel as though I'm accidentally hitting spoilers for content I haven't seen yet despite being 90% of the way through the game's content. If Animal Well looks interesting to you, you should play it sooner rather than later. The longer you wait, the more you open yourself up to spoilers, and Animal Well isn't a game you should take for granted.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes cozy, sometimes unnerving, always mysterious. The game really lets you figure everything out by yourself, but the level design is clever enough to point you in the right direction without holding your hand. The art is beautiful, details are cleverly crafted, and the puzzles are very fun to figure out! Every item you aquire has at least two things it can be used for, so expand your mind to the possibilities of what you can accomplish. The map is absolutely crammed full of secrets, so make sure to look at your map from time to time to see if there are any empty spaces or holes in walls. I beat the game in 9 hours and am currently filling my time with all the post game puzzles. There are lots and lots of things to do!
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: I have some letdowns with this game, but overall it's an extremely positive experience.The game is an excellent metroidvania with a lot of collectibles, a really fun power-up system that is a lot less linear than you'd expect and requires more free thinking with how they help you solve problems. There is no direct combat, it's mostly platforming and puzzle solving, but both of those are very well designed and super tight. Honestly, this is peak for its genre.My mistake was assuming the genre was moreso related to games like Rain World, Void Stranger, and Tunic where the progression is "knowledge-based" and the secrets are more of mystery, intrigue, and moments where you're like "omg I could do that the whole time??? that was right under my nose???". Instead, this game takes a much more linear approach. If I see a new mechanic I can't interact with, I can safely just give up and leave until I find a powerup that addresses the issue; the thrill of experimenting and theorycrafting vanished after about an hour once I realized there is simply nothing I can do without a powerup to address a problem.Again, this is normal for the genre of metroidvanias, but it's a lot simpler and not as fun of an experience compared to games like Void Stranger, Rain World and to an extent Tunic. The "secrets" are mostly just countless holes in the wall that give collectibles, or slightly obscured markings that depict solutions to other puzzles. I think it's a "me" thing that I got my hopes up that it had deeper secrets, and more mind bending experiences.Overall, the game is honestly very simple, but for its genre it has the most depth, polish, and entertaining mechanics I have ever experienced. I put this above any 2D Metroid game and even Hollow Knight, unless you like really deep lore, in which case you will not find that here. Only abstract, cutesy subliminal messages.Don't play it if you're expecting mind bending, enticing, thought provoking, game breaking secrets/mystery/experiences like Void Stranger, Rain World, and Tunic provide. If this is not something you're particularly expecting, you should have a great time. I still wish I got it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Fans of Noita will find Animal Well a similar game filled to the brim with secrets to uncover and puzzles to crack. Even having "finished" the game, I still have MANY loose ends to wrap up. As a Metroidvania, it gets the gold-star for me. Abilities are multipurpose and fun to use, regions pose unique challenges in their roster of hazards and creatures, and all in all its a visual treat as well, boasting impressive fluid-simulated smoke, great pixel-art, and a wonderful atmosphere. It strays away from the Hollow-Knight formula I've seen so popular in Metrodivania's lately, having no conventional combat mechanics, but still providing unique and challenging bosses to be surmounted. I implore you to buy this game and dive into the well. The ONLY con I have so far is accessibility, that being you cannot re-bind controls at this time. I will update my review if this changes.Say hi to the frog for me.

_childDocuments_.review: A 10/10 game that becomes a 8/10 when you hit an sudden "first ending". If all you play of this game is to the first credit sequence, it's a great experience. When you try to push past this into the next sequence of the game, it becomes a hunt for exhausting the game world of 64 literal easter eggs. While finding these eggs are fun, requiring these many secrets behind varying levels of obscurity becomes monotonous, unless you are using a guide or an extreme surplus of free time. You'll be spending too long wondering around the map, shining two different kinds of light on every background and using every item on every wall, floor and ceiling to get to the last 15-25% of the game.When the endgame becomes "To progress, make sure you check off every collectible in this list and then follow a guide for the answer to the ARG, etc.", you've lost me.Great game up until that point, got 8-9 hours by the time I hit the first ending. A bit overhyped imo but overall a welcome sight on Steam.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This really gave me strong original Metroid vibes when I played this as a kid (either 7 or 8 years old). While Animal Well has no combat, I felt isolated like in Metroid. It felt a little creepy, like Metroid sometimes could, and it had that same focus on exploration to find items, to then continue exploring. Animal Well has no combat, but has made its name from the exploration, puzzle-solving, and emphasis on finding secrets. I believe I read that the designer of Animal Well says that has 3 layers of deepness within. After looking more into the "post-game," I see that I only really consider myself yo have completed the first layer. As can be seen by my achievements, 16/20 is is most of them. There is so much more to the game. That said, as an older gentleman, I had a feeling that it wouldn't be worth my time investment to engage with these other layers and looked up information about what was missed. Turns out there is a lot there, and was correct that I'm glad I left the game where I did. I think this fist layer could be completed much more quickly than what I put into the game. Despite everything I've said, I personally feel that the first layer was worth the time and money to play through. I think the second layer is what a lot of people would end up striving for and is not unreasonable if you don't mind doing a lot of backtracking to find secrets. The third layer involves at least one challenge that flat-out require multiple people to solve and are, generally, a lot more esoteric.I think anyone that likes games that don't railroad you into exploring a particular direction and games that don't hold your hand in explaining what things "do" will really get a kick out of this. I don't want to really describe much more than this because Animal Well really invites a player into its unique world, but is particularly waiting for those small few that really want to delve deep.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely don't think I've had this unique and interactive of an experience in a video game in a long long time. Almost every room you explore has a new puzzle or visual effect that most of the time blow me away with creativity. The ample collectibles and slight backtracking only add to the game's fullness. This game really takes me back to the GameCube era where games didn't hold your hand through tutorials and let you rack your brain, but at the same time leaving plenty of subtle hints that still leave you feeling accomplished.  The price tag was daunting at first, but I was completely satisfied within the first 10 minutes and would even consider paying more for this much fun! Billy Basso is a genius and I can't believe he made every last resource that put this game together, and Dunkey was on the ball to invest in him.

_childDocuments_.review: What a crazy game. The design is fantastic, both in terms of mechanics and levels, where you learn to use everything you need in an intuitive way. But that’s not the only thing that makes this game a masterpiece.It has a stunning visual aesthetic and top-notch sound design. All of this compressed into just 30MB—an absolute technical feat. But on top of that, the game has a ton of layers. Secrets are hidden everywhere, and finding them is incredibly rewarding!It’s true that some puzzles are absolutely mind-blowing. I had to get a lot of help solving the final ones the game throws at you, but even with that, they felt like a wonderful discovery.It took me more than 20 hours to finish, but if I hadn’t searched for so many secrets, it could’ve been done in about 4 hours.Highly recommended, an amazing game. It’s definitely one of my favorite games. If you love exploration and puzzles, you’ve got to give this one a chance!

_childDocuments_.review: You may have seen multiple reviews stating this game has several layers. That’s true, and you’ll need to decide how far you want to go.The first layer is simply completing the game without focusing much on collectibles, just to see the basic ending. It’s fun, and the visuals are a real treat for the eyes (I’d even say it’s one of the most beautiful pixel art styles ever). Playing with all the instruments feels amazing. For most people, this is where you should stop, admire the game, and move on to something else.The second layer is finding all the  and witnessing the . At this point, the game might start to irritate you. With each new instrument, you’ll be forced to backtrack — A LOT. You may revisit almost every area 2, 3, or even 5 times, just to see if your latest tool reveals new secrets or collectibles. If you really want to continue here, I recommend using a guide or map to minimize aimless backtracking.The next layers are where I think you should stop unless you were absolutely thrilled by the previous two. This is where the hardest challenges lie, and they WILL take an enormous amount of your time, even with guides. The community collectively solved many of these puzzles, so the chances of figuring them out on your own are slim. If you’re still curious, I’d suggest watching some YouTube videos of the hardcore players who spent countless hours unlocking these "rewards."TL;DR: The game is amazing, but you should suppress your inner completionist.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is simply an extremely solid puzzle metroidvania game. No combat needed to explore a sprawling map full of puzzles and secrets. You play as a little guy in a interconnected environment surrounded by towering wolves, iguanas, and cranes that won't hesitate to eat you. It has all the good metroidvania qualities: nonlinear, absolutely no hand-holding, and upgrades that recontextualizes previous parts of a sprawling labyrinth. The puzzles also get pretty insane, with puzzles having mechanics I would have never seen coming. The game definitely has several layers, where a large chunk of the game is beyond the first ending. If you want to experience a great puzzle metroidvania, this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard game to describe. It’s a Metroidvana with a focus on puzzles. The puzzles are the best part of the game. A bunch of times I went “Man! That was so cool!” when I figured out how to do it. So many little hints and ideas. Even after 100% (all eggs, items, achievements and the true ending) there’s a lot of secrets to find. One I found (cause of a Reddit post I passed) had a room with grass. The grass was in binary and if you played that number using the other secret code you open a room with a cool looking thing. Another one I actually found was a bone fish boss. Nothing feels cheap or stupid. I can see why people were calling this a game of the year. There is no other game I’ve seen or played just like this. No dialogue at all. No 5 minute cutscene before you can move. You just start. I like how it is all gameplay. This game was really fun and a great time.

_childDocuments_.review: ANIMAL WELL is a 2D metroidvania brimming with trippy atmosphere and top notch gameplay. While story is typically one of my top reasons to pick up a given game, the story here is non-existent or so esoteric I could not make it out. What this game does exceptionally well is developing this surreal fever dream-esque atmosphere of a dungeon inhabited by neon glowing animals, some of which are friendly and others who definitely are not. It unsettling in the best way where you really have no idea what animal or obstacle you will encounter next. Given that description of facing the unknown  one would anticipate a polished combat system. However, there really is no combat in this game and other than a few aggressive animals, no real bosses. The real challenge and heart of this game lies in its puzzle platforming. In true metroidvania fashion you obtain new items to help you unlock new pathways through this bioluminescent gauntlet. However, the true sense of discovery comes not just from unlocking new pathways but figuring out alternate uses for the items you already have. Since the feeling of figuring out these alternative uses for items are such lovely "aha!" moments (especially since the game does not offer much in the way of tutorials), I will not divulge any here. My favorite moments in this game involved my character being dropped into a room with seemingly no way out only to realize that I already had everything I needed to escape with a bit of lateral thinking. The only other game that has evoked such wonderful moments was Return of the Obra Dinn,  one of the greatest puzzle games of all time.In closing, if you enjoy puzzle platformers and do not need combat in your metroidvania, you should stop reading this and immediately delve into ANIMAL WELL.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Had so much fun exploring this underground labyrinth filled to the brim with secrets. Some discoveries literally left me with my mouth open and I was so glad I was able to solve the first few layers of the game by myself. So yes, there are like 3 or even 4 layers to this game, but you only need to solve the first to see the credits. The real fun starts after that tho, as you try to find all 64 eggs scattered throughout the world. What I liked the most was finding a new item and it seeming kinda useless at first... until you find out what it does over time. Even though the chatter online is all about the secrets, the base game is very fun as well. Figuring out how to get past obstacles and experimenting with your items is well worth the asking price alone, then it's up to you how deep you venture into the rabbit hole, pun intended.

_childDocuments_.review: Spoiler warning"The puzzles were not designed for me" is what I heard at the end of the game.The main game was good, honestly besides the artstyle nothing too out of the ordinary. What left a sour taste was the optional puzzles were literally impossible (and I mean it, you cannot solve one of them on your own, physically), at which point I had to look up a guide which just removed any incentive for me to look further on my own because I've already "cheated". This may be the intended design choice, that does not make me like it more.Alot of the puzzles that are solvable on your own were just short of being good design. Some of them just felt cheap or had extra steps attached to them that were just not necessary. In the end it doesn't even matter because you need to solve every single puzzle regardless to get the "true ending" at which point you're forced into a guide.If you are a completionist: this game is not for you

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic puzzle-box of a game.  The items you find to unlock new ways to traverse are delightfully clever.If you're looking for something to contemplate and dig into the various layers of the setting, Animal Well will treat you right.There's also a lot of small programming flourishes within the game itself; try giving the game window a shake sometime.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible. I was starting to get skeptical of Dunkey's incessant praise of this game, you know, it's a YouTuber making a game publisher, it's their first game, it's gotta do well or he's in deep ♥♥♥♥, etc., but no, it's actually that good. It's got a delightfully ominous atmosphere and some of the most deviously well-designed puzzles and gameplay mechanics I've ever seen. The game has a very classic Nintendo-like feel to the puzzle design and overall gameplay, it feels a lot like a Zelda or Metroid game in those microscopic, subtle ways that most devs (understandably) fail to capture, and it even pushes far beyond that level with the endgame puzzles and secrets. It might be a little too cryptic at times, some of the main collectibles are really hard to find without some kind of walkthrough and the minimap doesn't do much to help, I will never complete the ultra-late game puzzles with the rabbits, and backtracking/secret hunting can get kind of tedious without finding certain items/secrets, but the overall quality is too strong for these issues to matter all that much.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful metroidvania with a slightly eerie vibe. What this one does best is provide you with more unique tools than many of its peers, forcing you to think about traversal puzzles more differently. Theres no generic double jump here.This is a layered game with many secrets. Games like Fez and Tunic are clearly big inspirations for how to unearth the mysteries of this world and will keep you playing well past the initial objective.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Animal well is a game I respect more for its purity of vision than the resulting gameplay experience.The game takes places in a well full of various animals that make up the characters and enemies of this metroidvania. There is no dialog, and no real story direction (save for a kind of brief introductory cutscene that shows the four "flames" that serve as the main goal of the game). Your character is fragile, and combat is de-emphasized in favor of puzzles, which are introduced through clever environment mechanics and context clues. All told, there is a 3-5 hour metroidvania here (depending on how many secrets you opt to chase), and by the end of my fairly leisurely 5 hour playthrough, I was ready for it to be over.On top of this, though, is a vast array of secrets ready for the curious and patient to find. These puzzles range from hunting for metroid-style breakable or passable walls to find secret eggs, bunnies, and chests with candles and matches, as well as other environmental puzzles and one puzzle that by most accounts requires the cooperation of a few dozen players split across multiple game copies. Good comparables include La Mulana or Fez. Your experience will depend a lot on how much you value that sort of thing, because by most accounts, they comprise the bulk of the game, and clearly the developer spent a lot of their energy there.It's also worth noting that at time of writing, achievement rates for any one of the games four "flames" (effectively the objectives of the 3-4 hour game) are sitting around 35%, even though they imply playtimes around 2 hours.If you are someone who values games as art, or has the patience and interest to dive really deeply into hunting for secrets, you will probably enjoy this game a lot.If you are someone looking for a pure entertainment product with some clever logic puzzles, there's still something for you here, but I wish I'd waited for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful game! If your favorite part of Metriod or Castlevania was the puzzle solving, exploring the world, and wonderful pixel art, then this is the game for you! If you like Metriod or Castlevania for any other reason, I would recommend passing this one up as there is little to no combat in this game.  I would say honestly calling it a metriodvania is a bit of a stretch.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well surpassed all my expectations in terms of depth and also just the general feel of the game. The puzzles are very unique and satisfying and the setting is very charming. It combines both platforming skills with puzzles that require a wide array of interesting and unique items that you find throughout the game and that you slowly get to master. Would definitely recommend anyone to check it out!
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Its alright.Its has quite unique, charming abilities that i rarely see in a Metroidvania. Theres tons of secrets to find, but it gets tedious in some areas, where you have to runs through 5+ screens just for another attempt. Its short, but has extra content to find after the end. You dont even need all abilities to beat the game.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: After beating the game I can say that this is a certified banger. A lot of people are playing because dunkey told them too but bro got a good eye for good games. I hate puzzle games but i beat this entire game in one sitting. A truly wondrous experience with amazing art direction and sound. Looking forward to animal well 2. BUY THIS GAME
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This was a very fresh breath of air for me regarding the metroidvania genre. Here are a few thoughts:+ Cool vfx and sfx+ Very well optimized+ Creative power ups (not the double jump, dash and ground pound you usually get in this genre)+ Universally lovable theme and no violence+ Unending amounts of secrets+ A massive rabbithole+ Most puzzles do not limit you to one solution+ Creative boss fight ideas+ Immersive player constraints and puzzle limitations+ Secret-driven convenience progression+ Solo-developer (in a good way lol, he's a real expert)- I found the places where you are supposed to use the hard to spot- Story and playtime on the shorter side- Respawn points can be very frustrating (pretty rare though)The game totally achieves what it is trying to be. Personally it's not my favourite genre, but for all metroidvania lovers out there it is a must-play. The price tag is absolutely fair, and I think Billy Basso deserves applause for what he created. A true gem!
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to blitz through the game it might take 5 hours - but how could you not get lost in the atmosphere along the way? This game has a serene, spooky atmosphere, every pixel carefully considered - and I mean every pixel, because there are so many rewarding secrets and every item is a quiet revelation that will make you think "that was there the whole time??" again and again. With vanishingly little dialogue, the game teaches you everything by example with brilliant design.It rewards out of the box thinking and curiosity, actively enjoys when you try to break it, and I can't remember a single frustrating puzzle.(It downloads and launches like instantly, too!)This game is up there with Portal or Outer Wilds as a brilliant example of what games can be and I can REALLY see this getting awards in the coming months.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, this game is just hands down fantastic. Atmospheric audio, great visuals, intriguing puzzles and somehow this game gave me greater moments of tension than 90% of the horror games I’ve played. Don’t pass on this, while it’s pricey, it’s covering 7 years of solo dev work. Do yourself a solid, experience this game, its quality can’t be ignored
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably one of the most beautiful games ever made, and that I have ever played. It is a masterpiece. I picked it up, and just could not stop playing. You are rewarded for every little thing in this game. The minimalistic sound design is perfect. I would recommend every person to play this, just for the experience of playing it. It plays so smoothly, the controls are easy to understand, and you will be rewarded for figuring things out.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: a beautifully crafted game ruined by its difficulty. I enjoyed the puzzles and the environments, the music established a really cool vibe, this game is a great metroidvania but HOLY ♥♥♥♥ this games bosses are TOUGH, while some people like to be tested and pushed to their limits, i do not. A difficulty option would have been nice, or something to ease the pain.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: The game is an interesting metroidvania where you slowly unlock more areas of the map not only by getting new gear, but also by learning new things you can do with your gear.It is also a deep rabbit hole of hidden stuff you can get into even after finishing the game... Kind of wish it was a bit less obtuse in places and helped you complete more of it rather than making you reliant on guides...
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: The game's mostly excellent, but I'll give one warning:  Some of the jumping puzzles, especially at the start, are really difficult and frustrating.  20 years ago I'd have loved that, today I'm a bit older, my reflexes a bit slower, and I'm left wishing the character jumped about half a block higher.But a few hours binge playing later I'm realizing I need to stop to eat, so if you can manage some fiddly 2d platforming I'd recommend it.  Lovely to play a metroidvania who's focus isn't combat.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game. I thoroughly enjoyed all the animals and puzzles. There are many secrets to discover and many ways to get to them. If you enjoy platformers with various ways of going faster and various ways of getting places this is the game for you. I hope all who play this game truly enjoy it for what it is.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Wow hats of to Billy Basso - this is a great puzzle game with an amazing art style. I cannot believe a single dev is capable of this! The style, the puzzles and the content and items are very imaginative and the whole thing is very well thought out so far (I am about 3 hours in).Cheers to Jason (videogamedunkey) and Big Mode for seeing the potential and helping getting this published - they have a good eye for good games and I am excited to see what they publish next.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well is a great mix of Metroidvania with Puzzle. Exploration and puzzle solving is the heart of this game. A HUGE amount of secrets, and a nice atmosphere. You can get the normal ending of the game, without any help from guides. But, to get every secret and the secret ending, I think, is another story. If you have A LOT of time, and patience. You can probably discover everything alone. But I think that's unlikely.The world is not massive, but is a pain in the ass to revisit areas to search for more secrets. You have only seven fast travel points, and if you die, you will return to the last save point. These two factors make the meticulous exploration for secrets a drag. I played 10h, and found 40/64 secret eggs. Those 24 left, will probably take me more 20h to find without a guide. And the eggs are not the only secrets to find.TD;DRGreat exploration puzzle game, that demands 3x more hours to get every secret on your on, or use a guide.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle themed metroidvania with stellar sound and art design. Platforming is certainly tricky in some spots, and depending on your level of patience, can be downright frustrating. However, there are so many clever moments and interactions with the creatures you come across that you tend to forget about said frustrations.  Glad to support small indie devs and games like these, we certainly need more of this in the industry.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well is an excellent love letter to traditional video games with the acknowledgment that the landscape of gaming has changed. It never holds your hand and allows you to explore the whole sandbox with the tools at your disposal. The collectibles don’t feel like a waste of time to collect due to the clever way they’re incorporated into the world you’re exploring. Animal Well was also created with a community in mind. Some secrets had to be solved together (even though they were all found pretty quickly) I highly recommend this game to ANYONE who enjoys just sitting down and playing a game. My only suggestion would be to play through the game for as long as you can before becoming genuinely stumped on what to do or where to go next. You experience will be way better imo
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most complex and deep metroidvanias I've ever played.Not sure what the story is (or if there's even a story) but this game is basically one huge puzzle. No guidance, no nothing - it's just you, your brain and your instincts. Really fun cracking this game open, and after 12 or so hours I still haven't found everything.I will say the game has too much content for its own good, and some of it isn't fun to find - just too well hidden. But I can see myself going back to find all the eggs (and maaaaybe all the bunnies). Not sure I'll ever replay it from scratch, though.The visuals are interesting and have a certain style and appeal. The sounds are also pretty good, though they do not stand out as much. Overall, a true indie gem and a fantastic game.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This is a gorgeous game.   Visually really stunning - dark and gloomy with neon blues and purples.  Imaginative, creepy.  Gameplay is a standard platformer with very non-standard power ups.  It subverts expectations in ways I can't say without spoiling the discovery process.  Careful exploration and observation is rewarded.  Some challenges were harder than I would like, but there are a lot of ways to make them easier with later exploration.  Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Completely unbiased review here. As much as I love Dunkey, I came into this game with skepticism. After I played the entire playthrough in one sitting (14 hours - don't judge me), I can say this game truly is like Halo 2 meets Halo 3. This game absolutely creams my jorts. This game's puzzles are intricate and make you think, the sound design is perfect for the atmospheres Billy Basso was trying to convey. The way you unlock new tools as you go makes exploration worth every second you spend failing skilljumps or having to redo puzzles to get to new places that you didn't even see before. The map is huge, the zones are creative, the enemies are interesting and have movesets that make you think outside the box. I love this game, and can confidently give it a 9.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Unbeatable atmosphere, and exploration. I would also dispute the fact that there is no "combat". Ye sure you never get a sword to swing and kill things but that doesn't mean its a walking simulator, there is plenty of things that can kill you. At its heart this is an atmospheric puzzle metroidvania and I think its worth a buy.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: BANGER - just rolled credits still with plenty to do. This game balances creative puzzles without being frustrating. I typically DO NOT LIKE Metroidvanias and was able to make it all the way through without assistance. Atmosphere puzzles and creativity are great. Game doesn’t overstay its welcome by any means but there are TONS of secrets and collectibles for anyone who doesn’t want the game to end at credits.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This game goes a few layers deep. Here's my recommendation (as spoiler free as possible)LAYER 1 - Yay! What a great game!The base game, credits roll. Everyone should play this. Great for any metroidvania fan. Slightly underwhelming ending, many secrets are saved for further layers.LAYER 2 - Man, that was tough but satisfying :)Great for completionists. You have to collect all the stuff. Highly recommend, adds answers to the somewhat open-ended initial ending!LAYER 3 - Skull emojiIf you want to dedicate a year of your life to finding all of the secrets on your own terms, go ahead. Otherwise, for everyone else, just follow a steam guide. Or watch FuryForged video "All of the Secret ______ in Animal Well" This was the most mind blowing and satisfying part of the game but the solutions are at times impossible to solve on your own.LAYER 4 - Pray to the animal gods before youThere's no reason you should waste your time on this unless you have a sick humiliation kink. This is the kind of ♥♥♥♥ that an entire team of discord operatives had to collaborate on solving, you on your own are ♥♥♥♥♥♥. But there are some neat easter eggs. Watch FuryForged video "Does Animal Well WANT Us to Cheat?".I myself completed Layer 1 on my own and it was amazing. I completed layer 2 with some assistance from the "Traveler's Guide to Animal Well" steam guide and was happy I did so. I completed Layer 3 with guides from around the internet and Fury Forged's video, I solved almost none of these on my own except for sheer luck. There's no point ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around with Layer 4. But insane to see what's there.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: First impressions very good!Any good platformer encourages players to break the game if they are creative enough.you can get quite a few collectables early and its so fun to have that "ohhhhh" moment when you end up exploring the way that gets you to the item normallyFinished this game at 16.5 hours after collecting all the secrets and collectables. I'd say this is a super fun platformer that turns way more puzzle focused the further into the game you go. You will think there is no way for you to explore further and then some new item comes along and you gotta check all again. If you dont want to spend a bunch of time running in circles I might suggest looking at a guide for where the puzzles are and then figure them out from there. Running in circles for 20 minutes just trying to find the puzzle is a bit annoying sometimes.Overall, I had a great experience with the game!
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: An actual masterpiece, and proof that graphics are never the best indicator of a games beauty or complexity. I am shocked and delighted by the amount of astonishment, terror, and curiosity this game managed to elicit from me throughout the entirety of the play through. There are ideas and mechanics presented in ANIMAL WELL that I have literally never experienced before in any other game. If you are looking for a game that slowly evolves into a masterpiece the further play, ANIMAL WELL is a must play.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that you can play for a bit then take a break. Whenever I was stumped I would leave the game come back and find new things to do. It's def not a typical Metroidventure, since a lot of the game is figuring out the puzzles. Even though you get items finding the eggs is pretty darn hard. I beat the game but I still have not 100% it. I am happy I did this w/o a guide, but it does help to watch others play. Once I beat it I saw some youtubers play and noticed all the stuff I missed, and how others use the items. All in all I enjoyed my romp through the game, and am happy to note there is more to do once you beat it, assuming you didn't use a guide. I beat it w/o collecting all the eggs and even w/o finding all the items.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: A very unique experience! Great vibes, unique puzzles and mechanics that will make you feel like a genius when you figure them out. There are also many optional puzzles that are so obscure/complicated that they'll make you feel like an idiot.The only negative parts for me were a couple sequences that were frustrating in terms of platforming under pressure.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Iz good. Vary big mode.So it's a very cool, cute, little game about solving puzzles, and those puzzles are really satisfying to solve.The art style is obviously peak brilliance.Tremendously, this game kind of taught me about how to make a boss more terrifying than pretty much all other bosses. There was a moment in the game where I could choose to overcome the boss (and likely fail), or I could run away and maybe come back later or find another way around. The game didn't force me to either fight (like most games) or run away (like most scary games). It gave me a choice, and as soon as I saw the boss, I literally noped out of the arena.I think there must be something going on psychologically where if a person chooses to flee from danger when they have the option to fight, it's way more impactful and visceral. Like fight-or-flight is going off, and my brain is feeling something sincere as if it's real danger. I need to think about that more. I think there's something to that.A lot of AAA games focus on breadth rather than depth. Like you have dozens of hours to do the exact same stuff again and again and again, and a lot of content is copy-pasted throughout the world or levels.It's awesome how many unique moments in this game had me go, "Oh, wow. Look at that." Or, "OMG. WHAT IS GOING ON?"There are so many rooms the character walks into where something completely novel is taking place or a unique challenge that must be overcome.My biggest complaint is kind of just that at about the last 15% of the game, I wasn't entirely sure what to do. Like I'd explored most of the map, and in some cases, there was a place I had to revisit, because (when I first went through that area) I didn't have the right tool to go down a particular route, and then once I got the right tool at a later point in the game, I had to go back and revisit those places, and that can kind of be easy to miss.There's also a Lastly, a puzzle is satisfying to solve. There were really only 3 or 4 puzzles I needed help solving. The game also implements a lot of backtracking where I'm having to resolve puzzles I already solved in order to get to a certain area. If the game implemented more one-way doors and shortcuts and ladders that can appear, then players won't have to expend their patience re-solving puzzles they already solved. I don't really get satisfaction solving the same puzzle a second or third time.Great game. Lots of fun. Can be frustrating at times. However, ultimately very satisfying and left me with a smile on my face at the end.Great job.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: The game art is amazing, sound, graphics, atmosphere in general, controls are fluid and it has a great vibe on it. I liked a lot backtracking for secret stuff.Discovering the secrets may be a chore for some players, there are puzzles like the 'speed' ones that felt cheap, more like luck than skill. Others felt like a chore, like finding all the eggs. This is those games where a single part can drive you more mental than the most punishing soulslike game and such, on the verge of really hating the game. But after lots of tries, you discover that a certain item has a 'secret' ability into it and your like will be much easier, and you will love the game again.I'd still recomend it because I've had so much fun discovering the secrets even though rage quitting like hell on latter parts. Just wait for a 20% sale or more and get it.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: Animal Well is like if someone jumped a magical smurf, robbed them, held them upside down to shake pixel art magic from their body. There is also a pinch of perplexing puzzles, and a whole lot of “What the heck am I doing?” into a pot and stirred vigorously. It’s not just the brain-bending puzzles that make this game stand out. It’s the atmosphere. The pixel art is good, and the sound design is immersive, you might find yourself hearing ambient animal noises long after you’ve turned off your brain and just sat there thinking "what do I even do". It took me 60 hours to 100% with no walk-through/guides and 10-12 hours just to find a flipping candle I needed. Yeah I definitely suck at games, but that’s Animal Well for you, an indie game that had myself questioning life choices, but in the most delightful way possible. Worth the 25$, can't wait to explore the deeper secrets that I still have yet to discover.
_childDocuments_.name: ANIMAL WELL

_childDocuments_.review: This game legitimately set a new standard for how good Puzzle games can really get. I'm probably a little more biased, because it's a Metroidvania with cool movement options and I love those types of games. However, I still feel like I'm underselling how good it really is and I can't exactly elaborate further, because of spoilers. All you need to know is that this game is 100% worth its price and does SO MUCH with SO LITTLE. Kudos to Billy and Bigmode!

_childDocuments_.review: Spoiler free.This game is good. It's like a more playable version of La Mulana.Animal Well is a game about puzzles, exploration, and secrets. You explore a genuinely massive and mazelike map, finding tools that help you navigate and solve puzzles. Every room has a puzzle, even the ones that don't look like they do- and every room has a secret, sometimes two, sometimes three. Secrets are one of my favorite things in video games, and Animal Well is full of them. There are secret areas, secret puzzles, secret items, secret gameplay mechanics. It's addictive. Every new room fills you with excitement; you can't help but imagine what it could be hiding.The developer says that the game is separated into three "layers" the first layer is the route required to beat the game. The second layer is the post-game and 100% completion. The third is apparently some kind of ARG that could take potentially years to solve. I have genuinely no idea what the third layer looks like, other than that I've been told that there are traps within the game's code designed to softlock dataminers. I have no idea if I even touched that part of the game at all during my playthrough.Most of the more interesting puzzles in the game come in the second layer, after you've probably already beaten the game, which I found disappointing. While there are a handful of really great puzzles necessary for completion; I found myself enjoying the side content a lot more than the main route. First layer puzzles are mainly just using one of your items to hit a few switches while you platform, post-game puzzles involve writing down information, following clues written on walls, connecting hints scattered across the map, etc. They require a level of attention and thought that first layer puzzles don't, and are much more engaging.The main route is just a little too easy, I was never stumped for more than a minute or two. In addition, I think that some of the puzzles and platforming sections are a little too unforgiving. The timing on some of the puzzles is brutal, and there are a few block puzzles that will instantly kill you if you fail them- with checkpoints just a little too far away to be tolerable. It really sucks to solve a puzzle and be doing it correctly, and then have to do it five more times anyways because the margin of error on the timing is a hair's width.Anyway, the exploration in the game is fun, the platforming is fun, the items are fun, the puzzles are fun. The graphics are great, the sound design is great, and the level and creature design is great. Animal Well is worth checking out if you like metroidvanias, puzzle games, secrets, and combinations of the three.

_childDocuments_.review: I have completed the game, including all of the achievements.  The following is my fair assessment of the game's strengths and weaknesses, and I trend towards the technical, especially when it comes to nitpicks.Short version: If you aren't a One Piece fan, you might want to give this one a miss.  Enjoyment of this game is extremely dependent on this factor.As a JRPG, this game is extremely laid back.  You will not find any real challenge until the very end, and then essentially only with the optional content outside of the story.  This was definitely one of my main gripes with the game.  But I eventually realized that this was done in order to keep the gameplay loop from interfering with the story progression.  By and large, the game is balanced so that as long as you defeat every map enemy you see exactly once, you're set.  Balanced both in terms of enemy difficulty and tolerable enjoyment.  By that I mean this game doesn't inspire a desire to grind for levels, nor does it require this from the player.The story is exactly what you would expect: A contrivance is conjured to provide an excuse for the Strawhats to relive the events of the story, just as generally occurs in the Pirate Warriors games.  There is a LOT of dialogue from just about everyone in the anime.  Enough to fill a season.  This helps considerably in selling the idea that you're taking part in the anime.The combat has a surprisingly functional gimmick that perpetually inspires the player to do more than hit attack—fights simply take too long to finish if one is literally that lazy.  And here is where the game's biggest strength shines: The character animations for various attacks are extremely well done.  Easily the highest tier of competence in the game was lavished right here.  This turns out to be important, since fighting ends up being about half of what they player does in this game.The music is serviceable with the occasional shining moment.  It's certainly not completely forgettable, but also not something you'd add to your playlist.  It's about as good as, say, the average Sakuraba OST—this is not praise, but not a condemnation.  It would have been surprising if the soundtrack had been amazing, but I wasn't expecting it to be.  As is tradition with anime-turned-game, there are ZERO references to the anime's music, front to back.Sound effects are about on par here.  Just like with the music, even when there were definitely certain sounds that are always used in the anime for certain moments—such as Sanji's air hop, or the sound of Law's Room ability—the game doesn't tap those sounds and instead just comes up with something of its own.  Disappointing, but entirely within precedent.This game uses an accessory system that has no meaningful balance.  In a game where difficulty simply does not come into play, it could be argued that a lack of balance doesn't matter.  Indeed, I just about ignored the accessories until I reached the end of the game and began grinding out the remainder of the levels, at which point I went about as ham as I could with making my characters overpowered... because the endgame/post-game is the only time when the content is actually truly balanced against those accessories.  This feels like the correct way to approach the accessory topic: Don't pay much attention to them until you reach the end, and then go crazy.  It's satisfying that the game DOES give the player a reason to grind out some powerful accessories, if only at the very end.Exploration is there, but not much rewarded.  Things are only rarely cleverly hidden.  Luffy gets a haki detection ability that's intended to find hidden items, but actually discovering anything with said ability is extremely rare and, if you will pardon the mild spoiler, almost entirely limited to moments when you've fought a new boss—you almost invariably locate their codex entry if you do a search.  Since there are no rewards or achievements tied to this, the only incentive is headcanon completionism.  The same thing goes for finding hidden items that only Sanji and Nami can see: They're there, at least, but you get nothing unique out of it, the game doesn't reward you, and it's all headcanon.  The exception to this is Robin, whose hidden items are required if one is interested in finishing the game's list of tasks.Small nitpick: This is the kind of game that will inexplicably hide food items and ingredients in chests.  Meaning you'd better be prepared not to treat this game as something immersive.  Treasure chests tucked away in dungeons for who knows how long will very frequently contain MEALS.  Meals which SHOULD have been something only Sanji could prepare for you.The graphics are better than I expected them to be.  With a 3080, the game can be played at a flat 4K 60fps from start to finish, and the only hiccups I ever saw were in the "strange place", possibly because the room is very busy and shows every crew member simultaneously.  Unfortunately, because the engine is UE4, one has very little choice but to use temporal anti-aliasing, which always causes afterimages on objects moving in contrast with the background.  Comically, the pre-rendered cutscenes, which always play at 30fps, were very clearly rendered in UE4 themselves, as they ALSO reveal the artifacting characteristic of TAA.My recommendation of this game is a bit like how I might recommend a One Piece movie: It's a spinoff, but it treats the property with respect and care, it uses the real voice cast fair and square, and it has a pretty high production value.  Fans of the anime are the target audience.  Pure JRPG fans should probably stay away unless you're out of options and need that blank filled.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I love One Piece to death, and i preordered the deluxe edition as there were many, many positive thoughts on the game and there still is, everybody is talking about the positives. Here are my thoughts so far.The game is, in my opinion, the best looking one piece game there is, all the artistic details can not go unnoticed. The sand, for example, has the style of a straw basket, making it look torn from the manga, with various other impressive visual details to boot.But to be frank, that's about where my praise ends. The combat has a very interesting idea, with multiple small battles happening at once in a turn based style. However i find the execution was rather poor, as for all the interesting ideas implemented, its really just using the best attack repeatedly. the auto battle shows this best, as even the AI simply uses the same attack over and over again. The fact that there is an auto battle system should show you already how repetitive the game can get, along with a speed multiplier which seems like it was ripped out of a mobile game. Continuing with the combat segments, where during game-play you spend most of your time, the UI is extremely cumbersome, with blinking lights everywhere, making it very hard to tell who you are targeting. One last thing for this section is the actual encounters. All random encounters seem to have three possible variations, randomly picked, and as such you can have the same fight multiple times in a row, making me personally at least avoid random encounters at all costs, as they just feel repetitive.Leaving combat, the other thing you are doing most is walking around. seeing all the characters in a three dimensional space is very fun, but the walking animations for most of them seem very static, after looking at each of them for a while, Zoro and Luffy just felt incomplete. for Luffy, the one you are likely to walk around with the most, while his general walking animation is decent, his main use is to zip to a point, not unlike the latest SpiderMan game, however there is little fluidity or  realistic momentum, and the second he get to where you "zip" to, all momentum is lost and he falls strait down. Continuing on, however, the story to the point i am, which i assume is little more than half way through the Alabasta arc, is consistently fetch quest after fetch quest. for example, a bird wants ten nuts, which all happen to be in birds nests throughout the town. however Luffy cant knock them down, even though they are all within reach of him, so to have the player use more characters, in this case Ussop, who is used to shoot them down. The world itself is also extremely linear, not allowing you to leave the path essentially ever, and from a game called "Odyssey" that is somewhat disheartening. there are invisible walls everywhere not allowing Luffy to jump down from the pillar hes on without first being dropped to the vines below. (said vines are on almost everything climbable as well) and if you attempt to jump down or walk off the edge of anything Luffy says the same line on repeat with absolutely no variation.For the final section id just like to point out the level system... during the first area of game-play, one fight is able to get you three or so levels at a time, with the stats each character has skyrocket. At the end of each fight, your characters will say something along the lines of, it wasn't my blades, it was me (not a direct quote), which can happen even after Zoro one shots the entire group of enemy's. in general, i love the idea of the game, but there are too many issues with the actual gamplay and story for me to recommend this to anybody, as playing this for any amount of time leaves me drained looking for the next checkpoint so i can quit. It seems I'm alone in this however, as all I've seen online has just been nothing besides praise. Either way, that's all I have to say.

_childDocuments_.review: Nami-swan and Robin-chan are just too beautiful and even more so with the "proper" mods, you know which ones i'm talking about. 10/10 game, get it nao! DO NOT BUY THIS GAME... unless you are a hardcore One Piece fan.I can already feel the stares full of hatred from the other franchise fans, but listen here - as a Monkey D. Luffy "imaginary nakama" for over 20 years now - I can't in a good conscience rope an unsuspecting passersby into playing this game. I honestly was going to downvote the Odyssey, but then Nami-sama has told me that she won't do the "happines punch" anymore, so you should understand - my hands were tied and I just had to upvote the game as her faithful slave. But at least i will explain here what are the game's problems and why you should probably avoid it, unless you are a fan yourself.First of all - the game does not explain NOTHING about it's setting to the player. From the very beginning the Odyssey expects you to know everything about the One Piece world, the Grand Line, the Luffy's crew composition, adventures and desires, about the devil fruits and their rules, about the world government and it's dirty secrets and many-many other things. Even though the game's story is tied to the world of memories, where Luffy and his friends will "re-live" some of their older adventures - those "arcs" are made with so many things cut off and unexplained, that a non-fan player will be as baffled about the stuff that happened there after finishing them, as he was before that. The game was made for the franchise fans first and foremost after all, so if you actually want to enjoy the plot there is only one advice i can give to you - read the manga  first (or watch the anime, but reading will be faster considering the lenght of the story).Second. Okay, maybe you don't care about the story or plot at all, and just want a basic gameplay satisfaction? At it's core the Odyssey is a typical party-based and turn-based j-rpg. The combat system by itself is okay, i don't have any major complains about it. Rock-paper-scissors vulnerability types, very well animated moves and attacks, an ability to change the team composition mid-fight - good stuff. The problem is what you are doing between fights... You are running. Back and fourth. In circles. Visiting and re-visiting the same locations again and again, grinding money, resources and exp, doing side-quests that require you to... yeah re-visit the locations you have thoroughly explored already. It's very tiresome. I literally felt how my will to play the game has been sucked out (and not in a "good" way) by this soulless gamedesign during the playthrough. If it was not the One Piece world, but some generic fantasy setting with the characters that i have no attachment to - i 100% guarantee you, that i would have abandoned the game half-way through. And judging by the steam achievements - many players actually did, because only the 10% of the game owners actually finished it.In my opinion confusing setting + tedious and boring gameplay are reasonable enough for the non-invested gamer to avoid the Odyssey. But what about the actual franchise fans?Well, yeah, in that case there is no other choice but to play it. Graphics are quite impressive, especially the characters. It's like a real-life anime, bruh! Suuuper! But even in that case i do have a few smaller complains to file.While the 3D models are really cool and the colors and environment are faithful to the original - the whole Odyssey world is just a dead and motionless decoration or stage backdrop if you will, there is no life in here. Take any good modern game now - there you will see a walking crowds, some simple events unfolding without the players interference, mechanisms moving, etc etc. Here? Everyone, aside from territory-patrolling enemies are just glued to the same spots, waiting for the player to come and interact. Nothing moves by it's own will, nothing lives. And it's really a shame because the world of One Piece is so vibrant, teeming with life and events! But not here, no. Welcome to the Madame Tussauds wax museum.Character outfits is my another complain. If you bought the basic edition - you will have the same outfits for the whole game's lenght. The travelling outfits dlc can unlock the pre time-skip versions of costumes. But this is all. WTF? If you follow Oda's work for long enough - you shall know that for every story arc characters have some special costumes and new outfits to match the mood of events. I was totally expecting, that after completing the Arabasta, Dressrosa or any other memory world/arc player would unlock the corresponding outfits, after all we even have a special tent specifically for the costume change. F**k you and your expectations says Bandai Namco. Thank God we are the PC master race crowd and unlike the console plebs we can use the mods to solve this issue. But still it's a very disappointing decision from the developer.And while we are on the topic of mods, there are 3 main ones that i have to recommend you to install, to make your overall expirience with the game better:1 better/alternative costumes for characters. this is self explanatory.2 jiggle physics. YES. THIS. IS. MANDATORY. you will not regret it.3 run speed increase. with the amount of running you will do from A to B to C in this game - it will save you a few hours of your time, otherwise spend on simple running back and fourth.While this game has a number of issues - it's still by far the best One Piece game in existance to date (yeah, previous were way worse imo). For a franchise admirer, even despite all my rant, it's worth a buy to at least enjoy the close-ups of the favourite characters and some of their banter. But for an outsider - it's a typical mediocre j-rpg and if you are into the j-rpg's there are better time sinks around, like the "trail" or "atelier" series, Tales of Arise or the soon to be released FF-XVI.So, in conclusion:One Piece fan? Buy it.Not a fan? Skip it, you won't lose much.

_childDocuments_.review: Super easy fights by mid game. Endless backtracking and bare minimum fast travel. Running speed is at a snail pace. Game has a function to change outfits, but there's only 1 other outfit in the game if you bought deluxe edition. So you gotta download mods to get any different outfits and those mods are usually just bikinis and nude mods for Robin and Nami. Chapter 6-9 are very underwhelming. At this point in the game you're so powerful you can just skip all mob fights except when you're forced to fight and it's more of a chore. Ending with really subpar bosses where you're at no point even close to being defeated. Adding to this you can just rush through those last chapters. Each chapter taking about 1 hour each. With 40minutes being dialogue and actual fights is 12 minutes of trash mobs and 8 minutes of boss battle (because the boss has dialogue and cutscenes too, the actual fight is around 4 minutes). I'd say the game has maybe some value for hardcore One Piece fans and I have to admit some of the humorous interactions gave me a few good chuckles. It's all brought down by the inexistent difficulty. The absolute slog that is backtracking to hide the fact the game is mostly empty of gameplay content. The game is about 80% dialogue really. If they make a similar game I hope they'll make one where we can make our own character. Choose our devil fruit or no devil fruit, instead being a swordsman, a kicker a la sanji or a god usuopp sniper. Add options instead of superhard railroad track story forcing you on a one way trip through every chapter. Give options on how to proceed and not just fighting like a real RPG. 5.5/10 for funny dialogue and cleavage. Gameplay and storywise: I will never play this game again.

The character interactions are great, especially if you're a fan. If you like One Piece's overused gags, you'll love seeing them here(gotta love em). Many good ideas in this game, such as smaller battles happening amidst a bigger brawl. The idea of a One Piece RPG is fantastic and they shouldn't give up on it. I love the idea I first mentioned in particular. Sadly, as others have said it just isn't executed that well so that is where the positives end. The negative: The story is fairly uninteresting. It has some moments of polish, but really ends up just being yet another bland One Piece filler arc instead of a believable part of the One Piece story. Most of the good ideas aren't implemented that well, in that the game's enemies are so weak that you don't need to devise any strategy or worry about type differences or any reason to not just use your strongest special attacks over and over. The game just tosses resources at you, so you'll never run out of HP or TP unless you impose restrictions on yourself. Even bosses are nothing more than a small irritation. The final boss is among the easiest in the game. Just spam Zoro's Black Rope Twister and any of Luffy's Gear 4th techniques and its done in very little time. The side content and post-game content is quite dull. The bounties in particular had a lot of potential, but all of the bounty pirates that you hunt aren't even worthy of being considered "filler". This game's areas may be pretty to look at, but only Alabasta had any real work put into them. The rest are very dull and short in comparison. On that subject, traversing the world with all of the various Straw Hat pirate abilities is a great idea, but in this game its just plain clunky and boring. Zipping around with Luffy feels stunted, and more than anything they make you switch to Chopper to get through a small hole or tunnel. You barely use the other Straw Hats, but their abilities aren't that great either. Nami finds money. Sanji finds ingredients. Robin finds research lore. Usopp shoots down bird nests. Franky builds bridges. Zoro cuts metal barriers, and the funny thing is I can't for the life of me remember if Brook does anything. That's how dull and rare it is to use most of the Straw Hats in the overworld. The music is fitting, but you're not going to be going back to any of this music to enjoy it on its own. One of the biggest issues is also the fact that the DLC offered for the game reuses so many assets and locations from the base game that it doesn't seem worth the purchase in the slightest, even when on sale. I don't see myself getting it.The gist of it is that I can't really recommend this game. It comes off as a horribly rushed game once you get past its surface. It was so dull that most of my playtime was idling on the pause menu. It took me nearly two years of off and on playing to finally get through it. I am a huge One Piece fan and I had hoped it would get better, but it didn't. Skip it and hope the next One Piece game is given more time and love.
