_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna be honest, I really wanted to like this game as a long time One Piece fan. I'll update this later on if my opinion changes throughout the game, but this is where I stand 4 hours in and roughly  EDIT: I have now finished the part mentioned previously completely (main story and revisit), and have around 12 and a half hours in the game. The review below stands true still, the only time I've used any consumable is to skip a character's turn because there's just no need to use any. I've done no grinding and I'm breezing through every encounter, even and especially the boss encounters - and for those of you saying I had not concluded the "tutorial" 4 hours into the game, get a grip. Nobody should have to suffer through 4 hours of bad game, and no tutorial should be 4 hours long.It's worth mentioning that the pacing does get slightly better though is still weird at times, and they do let you explore the map some more - there is just no incentive to besides the collector instinct for all of the ability upgrade cubes. And yes, I am saying this because I've looked through every nook and cranny for collectibles. I will return one final time when I finish the game, but until then, these is the only thing I have to note beside the main review below.EDIT 2: The game is now completely done from start to finish. I've 100%'ed it, including the collectibles and everything. Unfortunately I will be keeping this short as I'm sad to say not much as changed from what I've previously said, except that once you finally beat the game you have access to these special "challenge" fights which are revisiting the major bosses from the memories. There are 11 of them and you can do them all twice, the first being just as easy as when you fought them in the story, and the second FINALLY providing any sort of challenge if you don't want to grind for levels. I really wish they'd done something like this from the beginning, at least optionally. The story was pretty alright, very One Piece all the way to the end and I can't stress enough how much praise the art team deserves. As for the gameplay, I really don't have much else to say that I haven't said already so the final recommendation is: If you do not care about one piece that much and just expect a good game, you will not enjoy playing this. If you're a die hard One Piece fan like me, get it on sale. And, for everyone defending that I came into this wrong expectations because this is a JRPG, you are lunatics, and it is okay to be critical of the game and still like the series.The positives:- It actually looks pretty nice, the animations and the lighting are cool and the sound design is very good and faithful to the show.- Shamelessly, I bought this just to see the crew again, and I will include this as a positive because if you are a fan, there is quite a bit of fanservice in terms of all of the "cliches" of the crew being included (such as Chopper and Usopp's surprised faces/interjections and the rivalry between Zoro and Sanji).- The combat is pretty refreshing, I've never played a game like this (adds some FF aspects with a twist of different combat zones).- There's quite a lot of production value in the voice acting, they added a cool story that both introduces a new island and lets you revisit some of the previous arcs with new content.- PC adaptation actually pretty good in terms of graphical settings and optimization. The actual pre-rendered cutscenes feel like they run on 30 FPS sometimes but it didn't really take away from anything.And that's about it. As something that's kind of just in-between and mostly a note: as usual for these kinds of games, the keyboard controls are not the most intuitive and it's better to use a controller.Now for the negatives:- This is ESPECIALLY bad in the first part, or the new "island" but the flow of gameplay is  interrupted with "cutscenes" that have a fade to black transition before and after, and last like 20 seconds of reading dialogue. It really takes away from the experience.- This game is very easy. A lot of the other reviews mention it, but it legitimately feels like a 9 year old could beat this game, and maybe that's the point? But if this game was made for a younger audience, shouldn't it advertise itself as a rehash of the earlier events? I don't think a 12 year old has seen or read all of the content throughout the years to be able to appreciate the game. Also, there are a lot of neat systems such as a party to rest everyone and give you an EXP bonus for 10 battles, crafting for food and special ammo, an equipment system and a lot of strategy to the combat itself featuring a two layers deep "type" and "element" wheel for weakness/advantage - all of which lends itself to a lot of min/maxing or strategizing which is wasted when you have to use none of it to get through the combat. - Adding this as a segway from the previous points because it shoves all of the systems down your throat, but my god there are a LOT of tutorials for EVERYTHING. We did NOT need this much hand holding and it's very intrusive.- This is not an open world game and that is NOT the point of the negative, the point is that they try to put you in open areas with branching paths often, and instead of letting you go down the path, if you try to head towards the path that isn't the main story then you'll get a dialogue box along with ANOTHER fade to black and your character turns backwards. This makes the first negative point even worse, as both of these combined really soured the experience for me.Hopefully at least some of these things are resolved once I get through more of the game, but as it stands, I absolutely cannot recommend this at full price. If you're a die hard one piece fan like me and you will absolutely get this game, please just save some money and wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm still working on finishing the game but i'm currently about half way and honestly can't recommend it.I should start by saying i consider myself to be a pretty big One Piece fan so i'm definitely not biased in a negative way.The story, graphics, voice overs etc. Are all really great (seriously these graphics are top notch for an anime style game). During combat when you get to use your skills to beat down your enemies, it's a treat for the eyes. Especially the cinematics are really cool as well. It's also very nice to get to go back to some iconic scene's throughout One Piece's canon story (I'm not crying, you're crying, Vivi!).But that's about where the positive's end for me. I can see the potential of this game and i want it to be engaging and good, but it simply isn't. Combat is monotonous and i don't know why or how but, at the start of the game i received some very powerful artifacts which pretty much made combat super easy. It says the game is "open world" but it isn't true open world. Yes, i get to run around, but if i go anywhere too far away from my main objective, the game tells me to go back. Fast travel also often doesn't work until you've finished an objective. Quests are a drag because you go from point A to point B, ready to go to point C! BUT WAIT, we need a bird to navigate ... or we're missing something else so we need to MANUALLY RUN back to point A, to then go back to point B and now we can advance to point C. It's a lot of mindless running, which i could be ok with, except for that running feels slow, movement in general feels very limited. There's loads of invisible walls so you can't jump off ledges to take shortcuts, or if it's too high, the game won't let you drop down. Luffy can grapple and throw himself to certain places but every time you do so, you can't move until you land which really interrupts the flow of the game. Exploring isn't really rewarded. There's loads of chests around but they contain nothing really useful or necessary. There's a mechanic where switching to a different character can get you to open different kinds of boxes, or get through small places, or find ingredients or money ... but whenever you switch, you have a 2 second black screen to make the switch ... again interrupting gameplay.In a nutshell: The story, graphics, animation and voice overs are all top notch but they are combined with terribly slow, monotonous and braindead combat, slow and time wasting gameplay and a "closed" open world.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not a HARD RPG. It is NOT a Fully open world button masher. Nor is this a choose-your-own-adventure game. It is not dubbed in English but everything has subtitles. And the Art style is not for everyone. It seems to be fully controller supported (I say seems because I have not finished the game but have not run into any problems yet.)With all that being said, it is a very fun game to play. Though the combat is turn-based you still have many combat options thanks to the combat system. Although you can't have all of the Straw Hats on the battlefield at once, they can be switched in at the start of each turn of combat so you can change the team comp without losing any tempo in battle. Think old-school final fantasy combat, but not nearly as difficult. Exploration: Like I said this is not a fully open world, but there are lots of side passages and hidden corridors that you can go down to fight an extra enemy and get a little consumable. The main reason I explore is for the little magnifying glasses, they are little hud markers that you can inspect and a little blurb from the crew will come out. That is why I love One Piece for the Characters, and with Oda himself writing the story the Straw Hats feel like themselves. So when you see a magnifying glass next to an animal you can get a funny little outburst from Luffy telling Sanji to cook it for him. I'm not doing it justice in this description, but explore for the story and not the loot.The Story, I'm not far enough into the game to give an accurate overview of the story, but the setup seems solid. It's a little contrived, on how the Straw Hats turn into LVL 1 Characters, but that's just game balance and it could have been handled much worse. As I stated earlier, the Characters feel like themselves, which is super important to me.And those are the 3 pillars of this game, Combat, Exploration, and Story. So overall rating, I'd give this bad boy a 7.5/10Combat 7/10Exploration 5/10Story 10/10 (Based on Characters being themselves and the start of what could be an amazing story)I am extremely biased because I love One Piece. So if you are a fan of One Piece and want a chill RPG-style game where you can just sit back on autopilot and walk around with the Straw Hats, this game is 100% for you. If you want a challenge in an open sea pirate game with mortal combat button combos, this isn't your game. It is what it is, nothing more and nothing less. If you don't like this type of game, I doubt this will turn you on to the genre Hope this helps someone, I just answered the questions that I had and gave the info I wish I knew before I bought.Edit: Fixed spelling thanks to @Apatyte.

_childDocuments_.review: Would I recommend it to anyone? No. A JRPG fan, maybe. A One Piece fan, yes of course...but even that's a stretch. Pun intended.The battle system has allot of potential. I'm four hours into the game and the cinematic quality is one of the best parts. Everything feels good in combat, making me want more. Sadly it's everything else that tarnishes the game, and honestly any real One Piece fan is left confused at certain design choices and narrative elements.I personally dislike the story. It's a forced video game narrative that centers around the Straw Hats losing their strength and skill. It's terrible and moments with the new OC characters feel like pulling teeth. They get more highlight than certain characters of the actual series. Where the **** is Franky? Why does no one care about one of their best friends? Why am I now suddenly in memory version of Alabasta with OC girl that screwed us over in the first place? It honestly feels like someone went over footnotes of One Piece and was like "Ok stripe them down to the most basic tropes, and hard rail the player onto the story."*If you're here for a open world exploration adventure featuring the Straw Hats in incredibly detailed locations from throughout the story; this is half of that.I remember when DBZ games got allot of crap for repeating the story in every game. One Piece deserves a full fledged version of that. The next game NEEDS to be the journey from Foosha to at least Wano. The series deserves that kind of treatment.Odyssey is okay. Just okay. It certainly could be the best One Piece game out there, but it leaves much to be desired.

_childDocuments_.review: If I could, I would have given this game somewhere between a yes and a no on the recommendation. While I'm not going to completely condemn the game, there is a lot left to be desired. PROS: - The story is actually kind of fun. You get to go through some of the Straw Hats greatest adventures by reliving them as a memory. It's a way of going through past stories and not needing the stories to perfectly match the ones from the Manga/Anime.  - Interaction between the crew and with old allies is enjoyable as always.CONS: - Traveling around the world isn't too bad the first time, but after that it gets soooooooooooo boring. And you constantly have to travel back and forth because every quest seems to want you to go to the farthest place possible to pick something up and return it.  - Continuing the con about traveling is Fast Travel. It there but it is very limited on where you can fast travel too and each time you travel you have to sit there for 10 seconds as a yellow monkey waves at you before you can start moving.  - Combat is another issue. It was fun to watch the skill animations the first time around, but soon it felt like the animations were all too long and it just made combat drag on and on. Even with the fast forward option for combat, it takes forever to finish a move.  - Skills themselves. A few of the characters have quite a few skills for them to use, but honestly there's no reason to use 90% of them. Rarely do the different skills for a character have anything unique about them aside from the animation. Like two of Zoro's skills, they only hit 1 target, they do basically the same amount of damage, they don't add any additional status effects, the only different is the TP cost. If you're a fan of the show, you'll probably enjoy the story and the character interactions. However, if you're looking for a great game, then this isn't for you.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I imagine fans of One Piece will enjoy this game, regardless of its shortcomings. I enjoyed playing through the game with a completionist run, but I also couldn't help but notice many more minor issues since I did everything there was to do in the game. One Piece Odyssey is a long game. I finished my completionist run in about 60 hours (Steam tells me I've played for around 20 hours, but it doesn't consider offline time), with all optional content done, excluding the post-game content with higher-difficulty bosses from the One Piece universe. The game looks great. I imagine some people might have an issue with the art style they went for, but I think it looks excellent. The developers have paid great attention to detail, and the world sometimes looks gorgeous.The world-building is also top-notch. One of the negative reviews criticized the soundtrack for not being very good. And that's a fair opinion, but the soundtrack was composed by the guy behind the Dark Souls soundtrack and the "Tales of.." series, to mention a few. If you don't enjoy the music in this game, then you have pretty high standards :P Probably my biggest issue with One Piece Odyssey is its traversal. The traversal options in the game aren't bad; they're pretty decent. There are no mounts or anything, but there's the standard, fast travel option, and Luffy's iconic arm swinging is used a lot at specific points in the game.There's a second fast travel alternative that I hardly ever use because it's hardly ever available. But I have an issue with traversal, or rather, the side content in this game - primarily based around the age-old fetch quest design. Some of them aren't bad, but many are, in my opinion. The game in itself can start to feel quite repetitive after a while, likely due to the length of the game. If you're a completionist like me, you'll feel that repetitiveness in many of the fetch quests that require you to move from point A to point B and then point C before heading back to A and then to D. You get the point. I didn't enjoy some of those side missions at all. They felt like a chore, and most weren't worth it. Quite a few minor issues in the game bothered me at different times, but they might not be as much of a problem to everyone else. Quite frequently in the game, during story missions and side activities, the game locks you into a corridor of sorts. If you attempt to stray from the beaten path, the game will stop and inform you that you need to turn around before pausing to load the map and turning you around 180 degrees. I didn't mind it at first, but it got pretty annoying after a while, and I don't see any point in it being there when it's not preventing you from accessing areas you're not supposed to access. There are no sensitivity settings for the controller/camera, so be prepared for that. I initially felt like a snail, but I eventually got used to the camera being relatively slow. This likely won't feel like an issue to everyone. Several locked chests in the game contain some of the best combat items. For some reason, you won't be able to do the side mission that allows you to unlock these until really far into the game, and they don't get marked on the map when you find them - so, if you want to open these, you'll need to follow a Youtube video, as I did.. or backtrack to locate them all. This was an odd design choice, in my opinion. And it's not the only thing that doesn't become available until late in the game. Three of the playable characters don't become available until you've progressed far into the story, and these characters felt like they always lagged behind everyone else. Their upgrades roll out much later, and the skill upgrade cubes you'll randomly find seem to prioritize those three characters last for some reason.Again, it's an odd design choice. After finishing the game and working on the post-game content, I still haven't been able to upgrade Brook's abilities, while almost everyone else has had their abilities maxed out for tens of hours. All in all, One Piece Odyssey is a solid game with some cool features and plenty to like for fans of the series. The developers put a lot of love into creating the game, with lots of detail put into its world-building and character design. I appreciate that Robin has a different animation for opening chests, for example. Details like that always bring a smile to my face. It's not without its flaws; there are many minor ones, but I imagine most One Piece fans will love this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Possibly the best One Piece RPG you meet once in your life time.In this game, developer has nailed everything you could anticipate from one of the legendary JP animes in its history, while twisted a brand new story that fit the world of One Piece so perfectly. This game’s the real sight who has opened the curtain of gaming 2023, not SE’s Forspoken disaster.Before I start the review, I’d like to take a few lines thanking the community who had helped me successfully decide pre-ordering the game when I had doubts about it, otherwise I would have missed this master piece by my faulty assumption. Thank you very much.Pros+StoryJust like it’s anime, One Piece’s story will never disappoint you, this game’s the same. It combines real emotional moments from the anime with the story acting on its own. The purpose is clear: to help someone who never watched any anime of One Piece would still be able to know what have happened ‘in the past’ in order to enjoy the story as much as possible. For the fans, to review these memorable moments from the anime in the game, is a special treat. Not only have they opened sentimental feelings you had with the anime once more, but also gave you a new path towards ‘salvation’ which probably many of you wanted so badly when there was nothing you could do in its original ’place’, myself included. This is the furthest I can say about the story part, play the game to find all the secrets and eastern eggs within the game!+CombatWho said turn based combat can’t be fun? It’s glad to see the tradition of JRPG returns when the video game industry today totally shifted into ARPG a bit too much. Not only a fresh wind it is in the gap of mountains of ARPGs to me, but also it designed so well that leveling up don’t feel like grinding at all. Plus, not all the games need to be as hard as Dark Souls or Elder Rings to enjoy, OPO shows another route to enjoy the gameplay at its fullest by simply let you be ‘ invincible’ without cheating. +Semi-Open WorldDespite it isn’t completely a JRPG with open world, there are still plenty of things you can do in the game: Tons of side quests, collectables; cooking dishes; party to gain buffs before battles; make combat equipment...you can be pretty busy in the game depending on how you like to play the story out.+VAsAll from the original anime, wanted to emerge yourself in the world of the One Piece pirates one more time? They surely heard ya.Cons-Side QuestsThe issue with side quests mainly in the game is, after you accepted the missions, the mark of the NPCs who assigned the quests on your map will be vanished. You gotta have a real good memories about where they were located or only take a few in case you forgot whom was whom, and where were each one of them. Developers could have simply marked the quest- taken NPC with a grey symbol like any other open-world RPGs, then we would have less hard time to find the quests-givener while trying to do multiple missions at the same time. Also, another issue with side quests is: objective aren’t marked on your map, you will be given a rough idea about where to go by NPC lines or description, and...some of them could be pretty difficult to find at times. Either gives more hints when players couldn’t find the objectives for a long time, or mark them on the map, in my opinion would be a better design choice. It won’t destroy the fun to finish them, really. The legends of Heroes franchise marked all quests and exactly where I needed to go, I never got bored or thought they were too easy to complete :)-Collectables Again, for a completist(because I can’t love this game more) like me, it’s a nightmare to find out I’ve missed some of collectables after the journey’s end, when none of the ones I’ve collected are marked on my map. So there was no way to know which one I missed and where it could possibly be, all I could do becoming either running all maps all over again in hope of finding the missable ones I’ve left out which takes seriously time and effort or I had no choice but to look at a guide for help(facepalm). It could be much better if the map didn’t regenerate the empty jars, only left the ones I didn’t notice on my first walkthrough, or simply marked collectables’ location that I have gotten on my map, then I know where I need to search and where I don’t. OverallFew Cons, nothing related to the main story couldn’t possible ruin the bright sides of this game, and One Piece Odyssey has passed far from the bottom line of merely satisfaction. On the contrary, it’s easily one of my favorite games of all time, and it also becomes the first game I decided completing with 100% in 2023 to pay the respect that Bandai’s team had done a great job to craft this new pirates’ world, charming and unique for whom keeps calling me coming back once for more.P.S if this game would have a sequel, I will be glad to support it regardless. I love Adio, he’s my favorite character, his past is like what a grown man could have faced, and he had my sympathy

_childDocuments_.review: I love One Piece, watched the anime from episode 1 to current Wano arc including all fillers. Great show that keeps getting better. Through this game you get to relive some iconic moments.  in particular was very heartwarming. Characters both new and old are fantastically done, had no issues with any of them. Oh, and my goodness, getting to see them all in 3D and the animation being silky smooth, perfection.Felt great to use abilities from the show when I wanted to. With that said, I found myself using the same abilities over and over quite often as they were just simply stronger than others by a large margin for both single and multi target. The fact it was One Piece and to me, really well done, kept me going towards the last stretch because at that point, the actual gameplay was rather dull. Given the rock, paper scissors take on combat, the strength of abilities as you proceed through the main story and it being turn based, the game was bound to grow stale at some point. Might be a personal opinion, but something like Conquerors Haki shouldn't be spammable. Give it a turn or 2 to "recharge". Not the strongest AOE in the game, but an example of something I just don't think should happen.While most the game is replaying content we have already seen in the anime and/or manga already, which I enjoyed reliving it and somewhat at the helm so to speak, I will say it was kind of annoying to play content I already played once in the game again.I recommend this to any One Piece fan. New fans will have somewhat a hard time with it since they are reliving past events if you haven't gotten there or haven't seen these events yet so I could see it being confusing. I wouldn't dock it for this though as they have someone with them experiencing it all for the first time so new fans would be in their seat and the story takes care of you imo.Go in expecting a fun adventure with Luffy and the gang, but not GOTY quality in any area. I would rebuy at full price, but not everyone can do that. 100% worth on a good sale for One Piece fans.

_childDocuments_.review: As a One Piece fan myself, this game should have been a positive recommendation without a second thought, especially when taking into account the presentation. However, I can't recommend it because of how restrictive it is most of the time. To the point that if you try to wander off a little to grab a shiny on the ground, it stops you and yells at you using a text box "NOT THAT WAY!". The combat is turn based and it has several mechanics that in concept should engage the player in thinking about the next turn. But that design can be disregarded because the game is so easy. Most encounters, outside of boss fights, are trivial. Furthermore, most of the enemies lack basic amounts of stats, like health points and damage, to give any resistance against the player for longer than 2 turns. Bosses for the most part have lots of health points, so those fights drag out. Because of these issues, combat becomes mindless, with the best strategy to be using the attack with highest damage output possible to defeat them faster.The story is mostly a way to recap some of the most iconic story arcs in One Piece, while feeling like something is out of place because it's all framed as playing through memories and memories are unreliable.  Still the new original characters for this game fit great in the One Piece universe. I don't have any complaint about the presentation because it's great. Character models, every island and enemy monsters are all looking great and with a lot of details.One Piece Odyssey is a game that limits player agency to a big degree with a huge focus on guiding through players through its narrative. Making the experience of playing a game something mindless, linear and restrictive. Several quests are just going back and forth in the same area without even a fight in sight, because of arbitrary story reasons, and the moment you want to wander a little, you are stopped in place.  For anyone that wants more One Piece content, I would recommend to watch this game online instead of playing it. It's a disappointment how repetitive and restrictive the game is. Those are the reasons why I can't recommend it

_childDocuments_.review: Join Luffy and his crew on another grand adventure in One Piece Odyssey! As they are looking for their next adventure, they are caught in a storm and shipwrecked on a tropical island that is rocked by storms. Now, you must find your friends and escape this treacherous island. Now, with their powers taken away, they must engage in turn-based combat to squash anyone who stands in the way of getting their abilities back and making it off this island alive.One Piece Odyssey is the newest game in the One Piece series and switches from the real-time combat most of the other games are known for to turn-based, which serves it really well. Coupled with gorgeous graphics, great voice acting, and an interesting story (so far), Odyssey is a joy to play. We still have more to go in the story, but on the Steam Deck, I feel I found my favorite way to play already!Right off the bat, the game starts at 30 FPS, which is fine, but after the initial battles, it goes into areas that are more demanding on the system. With 30 FPS, max settings, and a TDP of 10, the game would dip a bit to 28-29. While this isn't really noticeable, it is concerning that 30 FPS is pushing the device so hard with the limited graphic options it has. It can be fixed, but if I am going to play 30 FPS, I want the visuals to be much more beautiful. I tried lowering all settings and without any caps, still found it to go around 38-39 FPS with 23W and above battery drain. This is when I decided to start trying for 40 FPS.Forcing the resolution through Steam to 1024x640, since the game doesn't have different resolution options, FSR with a Sharpness of 0, changing Shadows to medium, and a TDP of 11, this game runs beautifully so far at 40 FPS. The game still looks pretty great, feels much smoother, and tends to have lower battery drain in most areas as opposed to the 30 FPS counterpart. This is more than likely due to going from native resolution down, but this is incredible. And battles feel even smoother and drain less due to you going to a contained area for combat.With the upscaling in resolution, there wasn't much difference in overall visuals. Some menu text and character photos looked a little bit pixelated, but otherwise, I found it to look almost exactly the same as native resolution. I did also notice some minor stutters when going into some new areas when starting to use a skill in combat, but these went away almost immediately. Some cutscenes are also forced to run at 30 FPS no matter what. I have not experienced any bugs or issues during gameplay so far.Overall, I am having a blast playing One Piece Odyssey on the Steam Deck. I am surprised how stable it is running so far and being able to stick under 20W for 40 FPS with almost max settings. It would be great to have this playable at native resolution, but the sacrifices definitely don't outweigh the positives here. 40 FPS, decent battery life, and good-looking graphics all work together to make Odyssey a fun time on Deck. Hopefully this will continue as I keep going through the game, but I am optimistic it will!Our full review will have a quality and battery focused build. We will also see if pushing to 45 is possible, within reason, but 40 feels fantastic for a framerate focus. You can view all the screenshots and comparisons we have on our website.

_childDocuments_.review: This one is a weird one. I don't hate the game and it does have issues I think most people will not vibe with but it is a "try when it goes on sale" recommend from me. At full price? not a chance. -Decent game actually and pretty faithful to the characters/story. -There is way more voice acting in this game than I initially thought there was going to be. Half expected the game to be mostly text dumps but most of it is actually voiced over. There is a potential downside for some people on this point though below- Visuals are very good for the most part. Other than some weird things happening here and there with characters too close to the camera sometimes-Cue obligatory "feels very much like One Piece" the moves and characters/places deliver on the fanservice element very well. Like no lie they paid attention to all the details with the characters and their moves/voices/expressions/etc. That being said as you go through the game you will absolutely notice the absence of certain characters.- Obligatory "if you love turn based combat you will like this game" as that is the battle system-The battle system has a neat idea, along with the accessory "equipment" system. The shell is definitely there but this one is a bit of a plus and negative. The positive side is that you can customize the stats of your character pretty heavily with accessory/fusion system. The battle system itself has the rock/paper/scissors trinity but mixes things up with randomized battle areas and events during combat BUT there is a downside. Overall it is serviceable. See further below for explanation.  - Obligatory "if you don't like reading sub titles you will hate this game" as the game has only japanese audio. I don't mind this at all but I still have to list it.- Obligatory "if you hate turn based combat you will hate this game" as that is the battle system- Music is of "check the block" variety. This may be because the anime doesn't REALLY have memorable music outside intro/outro/major fights. So they went with pretty generic stuff. You probably won't care to look up the music outside the game to listen to it. -Camera. I don't know how they messed up a basic camera that has been figured out for decades at this point. The camera feels floaty and has this issue where it gets "stuck" on the ground and you kind of have to fight it to move it back. Really weird problem for a modern game to have.-Enemy variety. There are what like maybe 13 different enemies if you don't count the unique bosses? Really disappointing with the fact that they have so nonsensical stuff to pull from in the series. Maybe addressed in DLC but yeah its weak.-Story is like the music, nothing special but serves its purpose.-No quest markers after you finish a sidequest. This is a minor one but not having it marked on the map where you need to return to AFTER you finish a quest is kind of annoying.  -The combat. Ok the combat isn't bad. Its actually entertaining and has great ideas going..BUT there is definitely an issue with difficulty in combination with equipment system. Like I said above you can customize your character pretty heavily if you want, however there is no real reason to when you can just kind of stack attack. When you stack the attack stat as much as you can you end up just kind of steam rolling everything. Not really with just spamming regular attacks like other reviews, that only works for the tutorial area (obviously) and then the game starts throwing way more enemies at you on average. Its just the skills for the characters (the iconic ones from the show you know) are fairly overtuned at base. Towards the 2nd half of the game you kind of just wipe the entire field in one skill with Luffy or Franky. If they had spent more time fine tuning the character strength this could easily have been a very good combat system. There is a post game that starts to address this, but you know its post game so many people will stop playing at that point. -No real alternate outfits unless you bought the DLC. Really Bamco? So much missed potential. ConclusionThe game is very close to being a good game that I would recommend to non one piece fans, but it just misses the mark on that. I can really only suggest this to people who stan the show and even then only after it goes on discount or gets more DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: After multiple adaptations from the best-selling manga ever created by Eiichiro Oda, One Piece finally turns into a proper JRPG (perhaps for the first time in its history) and let me anticipate that is going to be one of the best to date. The plot of Odyssey can be considered like a sort of spin-off, meaning it has nothing to do with the events happening in the main series. While sailing across the New World, Luffy and his crew are shipwrecked on Waford, a legendary island surrounded by raging storms and populated by mysterious golems. Here the Straw Hat pirates are stripped of all their powers by two new interesting characters, Adio and Lim, who somehow have developed a deep hatred towards pirates. Lim has the special ability to make people forget about their powers and she uses it on the Straw Hat crew, thinking they are just like all other evil pirates. With their powers lost and the ship heavily damaged, Luffy and his friends are unable to leave the island, thus they accept Lim and Adio’s help to recover their powers by visiting “Memoria”, a dreamlike dimension in which our protagonists can relive their past adventures and remember how they gained those skills.Obviously, the story is just an expedient to make you relive the Straw Hat journey, starting from the Arabasta arc and moving forward, with Adio and Lim stories that are unfortunately overshadowed by the most memorable episodes of Luffy and his crew. Fans of the series who have already read or watched those might feel tired of re-living them again, just like in  before, although Bandai Namco was smart enough to include many new secondary events for each chapter. Those who are new to One Piece should know that there is a lot of fan service, such as references to other characters and events connected to the series, that newcomers wouldn’t be able to catch. Thankfully, each story arc has short recaps that give plenty of info on what happened in the canon storyline, so there isn’t any risk of being confused.Speaking about the gameplay, I’m not exaggerating when I say that Odyssey pretty much resembles  (the developer ILCA collaborated with Square Enix during its development). Not just the graphics, which are really great and perfectly in line with the anime art style, but also the narration, with its countless dialogues, the funny monsters’ design and the focus on exploration, gave me plenty of DQ vibes. Plus, it is possible to swap characters and use their abilities while exploring. For example, Luffy can use Gum-Gum Rocket to grab items or reach distant areas by stretching out his arms, Sanji can sense rare ingredients, Chopper can explore small tunnels, Nami can find hidden money and so on. This encourages swapping characters on the go and helps to diversify the gameplay during exploration. Each story arc accessed from the Memoria dimension can be freely explored through multiple maps that offer a great amount of secondary content, such as side quests, bounties and time-space fractures that will transport some of your characters into a new space called Hysteria, a corrupted memory that needs to be fixed to allow them to go back safely, increasing their bond level and unlocking powerful group attacks. There are also some greatly appreciated quality of life options, such as the ability to fast travel from any position (towards predefined locations), the option to increase the combat speed and even an auto-battle mode controlled by the AI, which can be helpful when facing low-level enemies that only need a few attacks to be defeated.Combat is turn-based, meaning you will have a party of four members taking turns to fight against small groups of enemies. Each character is initially positioned in a different area of the battlefield and must defeat all enemies on its front before moving to another area. All characters can be replaced at any time with the reserve crew, even if they have been knocked out (but one must still be alive). Replacing the team is recommended, as each one has a different type of attack based on a simple rock, paper, scissors scheme that defines strengths and weaknesses. Luffi, Sanji and Chopper belong to the Strength category, meaning they are more effective when facing enemies in the Speed category (such as Nami and Usop), who are more advantaged against enemies that use attacks based on Technique (like Zoro and Nico Robin), the latter being best suited when dealing with enemies of the Strength category. Other weaknesses and resistances are represented by Burn, Freeze and Lightning elements, so you always need to keep an eye on the enemies’ stats to understand how to deal heavy damage by exploiting their weak points. All members can also use special skills by spending tension points (TP), which can be accumulated with standard attacks. During the fight it is also possible to incur in “dramatic scenes”, which activate specific conditions such as “defeat the enemy before it unleashes a powerful attack” that grant additional experience if completed.While combat is satisfying enough, it can often be too simple and easy, perhaps to not scare off those One Piece fans who are new to RPG games. It makes sense, but on the other hand, veterans of the genre could be somewhat disappointed by the lack of challenge and customization (though camping and crafting accessories are also present). One Piece Odyssey is a great JRPG that shows this might be the best formula for adapting the series into a videogame, with a simple, but effective, turn-based combat and huge amount of content and variety. It’s a pity that the story only gives an excuse to revisit the story arcs from the series without adding much new content aside from Waford island. I think this was a missed opportunity for Bandai to build something different and completely untied from the series (more like  but with better gameplay), so I really hope to see their next RPG with a brand new original story offering a unique adventure that has never been seen before.

_childDocuments_.review: To be fair, I wish I could label this as something more neutral. This is a very 'meh' game. This is not a bad game, but a lot of the criticisms others have give it are quite fair and ones I hold as well. Personally, I think this is a game is better played if you are looking for something chill and positive. However, if you were hoping for something deeply entrenched in One Piece lore this isn't for you.PROS:Perhaps one of my favorite things about this game is its style. It's obviously not for everyone, but it does help keep the anime/cartoony feel of One Piece. It also meshes well when using powers, as something more realistic looking would have undoubtedly looked a bit off. While the lore for this is a bit all over the place, it does still manage to capture the spirit of it. You get to travel with most of the crew right off the bat and it absolutely nails their interactions and personalities. It also nails how other characters react to them. I generally played this game when I needed something relaxing and I feel like that is how it should be played.CONS:Unfortunately, I have a lot more things I dislike about this game. Right off the bat, I have to say I would not call this an open world game and I imagine most would agree with me. It is DESIGNED as it is supposed to be one, with areas that you will clearly be able to go to. However, if you stray too far from where you should be going in terms of the main quest, it will force you to turn around and not allow you to explore. That is the exact opposite of an open world. There's also the fact that a lot of the world just isn't interactive and the point of an open world is obviously to explore and interact. I have gotten far enough that the amount that you can wander is a bit wider because there are side quests but these facts still hold true.There is also the fact that you cannot play with all of the crew. While Franky joins up, he leaves before you can fight with him and Brook is basically a ghost for a good chunk (thus far I've barely even been able to interact with him). I'm not entirely sure why they didn't just split the crew up longer and allow us to regroup as a whole later on. However, it is annoying to be teased with characters and to barely even interact with them, let alone not even be able to fight with them.As others have stated, this is a non-canon story. I do not inherently have a problem with this, but frankly I do think it should have just kept to that. The game tries to "expand" on canon, but the manner in which it does that isn't really expanding and involves too much running around, doing nothing. The problem that I do have with the non-canon story though is that it doesn't really seem to follow the rules of the source material. One of the characters made for the game has powers, but they do not seem to be rooted in being a different species or having devil fruit powers. And if it plans on revealing that they ARE because of a devil fruit...well, I personally think it'd make even less sense since even the devil fruits have rules to them. She's effectively a plot device that breaks canon, in my book.The gameplay isn't bad. I actually like turn-based games, but I like them because when done right they can be challenging. As others have stated, this game is WAY too easy. You can go through a few turns and easily win, barely getting any HP taken off you. This is even true of bosses. Also, I've found during combat that there was a fair amount of lagging. Not sure if it is because my computer isn't the best out there, but considering what it CAN handle with no little to no lag, I am convinced that this is more of the game's fault than anything else.

Sure it can get repetitive, but I don't think that's enough to drive me from the game, but on that note I do juggle several different games at all times and usually reserve this game to my bed time game on my steamdeck. The game is very beautiful and it is functional. It has all of our favorite characters and the animations are superb. The voice acting is fantastic. Hardcore fans are usually pretty ruthless towards there favorite IPs if it isnt too their liking, but if you ask me, someone who rather enjoys One Piece but doesn't dedicate his life to it, the game is great and worth your time even at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just...not good. I'm not sure exactly what I was expecting especially as a One Piece fan but I was incredibly disappointed.To break the game into two halves, the OP stuff and the JRPG stuff it goes like this.As a JRPG it woefully fails, the combat is just not engaging, I basically met nothing that could survive more than 2 turns at the very max, even bosses. It's not so much that the game is incredibly easy (which it is) but the fact it's dull. You spend most of your time slowly walking through empty fields and avoiding enemies because it's not worth the time investment and not fun enough to be worth doing. There IS arguably variety in character building but I just equipped accessories with attack on them only for the entire game and never even came close to a game over.On the One Piece side of things we have frankly some embarrassing retellings. the supposed "what-if" scenarios mostly amount to "What if Alabasta but all the fun fights and memorable characters were gone.", "What if Water 7 but nothing mattered and most of CP9 were missing." So on and so forth. They have virtually nothing to offer to an existing fan but they aren't comprehensive or interesting enough for a non-fan to even get through. For some reason it seems like all their effort went into Dressrosa and Marineford exclusively because that's where most of the relevant characters and antagonists do all make appearances with some notable exceptions. On the other hand the original story is actually quite decent, Adio is okay and I really liked Lim. Lim is a charming addition and seeing her warm up to the Straw Hats and gradually get more interested in the plot as if she's becoming a One Piece fan herself was good. The original story is about on par with the original stories of most OP films, and I guess that's good enough.Overall, it's just a bad game, for JRPG fans and One Piece fans.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent game if you're a fan of the series. It does have some major flaws. Too easy, drags out too much. Positives: Easily the best parts are the visuals, music and animations. Gameplay is sorta interesting turn based with multiple zones in one fight with a basic rock paper scissor mechanic. And the Straw Hats never get old. It's always a fun time seeing their antics. Also, once you unlock the accessory fusions, you can really make some characters glass cannons. (Ex. Nami carried my playthrough due to her crazy AoE attacks and free dodges she can give anyone, and just buff the hell out of accessories that are linked to attack and tp/critical hits. Also make them more resistant to their weaknesses.) Playing around with these builds was easily the most fun part just seeing how busted you can make characters. The negatives: Alabasta drags on far too long. (Oddly it's one of my favorites arcs from the manga/anime!). The whole memory and reliving them is a trope I can't stand as much anymore. Wild since One Piece already has so many amazing arcs and world building. It falls flat here. Granted the twist that "memories can be difficult to remember or being fuzzy" could introduce fun changes for each major arc that was presented in somewhat different outcomes. Too easy. Story drags and picks up in the last chapter. Don't need a cutscene every step and also, please just give us everyone in the beginning. After I got everyone I ignored most of the side content cause I was feeling burnout and wanted to finish the game. Overall, there's a fun and interesting game under it. It's easily the most 3/5 game I've played in a while. If it didn't really have the crew, I wouldn't recommend it. But for a anime spin off game NOT being an arena fighter? Fun change but still plays it a bit safe. I'd like to see this in a bigger game! Got some fun foundations.

_childDocuments_.review: So originally I wanted to get this game because I read multiple comments saying "One Piece but Persona!". As a major fan of Atlus games and the Persona franchise, this was perfect because not only did it have my absolute love for Persona, but it was Oda senseis amazing story. Well let me tell you it was all a lie.Combat is persona-like in theme maybe, using a turn based formula of a party. However that is where the comparisons end. The game is a mess and quickly becomes repetitive with zero enemy variety to speak of. You will be facing off against the same 15 enemies the whole game through.Adventuring around the "open world" area can become a slog, most areas will be closed off due to story forcing you into a linear progression, which defeats the whole purpose of an open world game. You can't explore anywhere unless the game wants you to.The story itself is very lackluster and can be boring at times. If you add that on top of bad animations, it becomes painful to sit through. However I forced myself to do everything this game has to offer so I can give an honest review. Every achievement I could get, I got. Every corner I could explore, I explored. So trust me when I tell you the whole world feels empty and lazily put together at times.It takes roughly around 50 hours or so to do everything, but I think if you skip through all the collectables and achievements you are looking at probably 8-12 Hours of story. The last few achievements are also locked behind the DLC, which based on reviews and videos really isn't worth it.If you are a fan of One Piece, then only really get this game on a massive discount, otherwise give it a miss.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: This game is set right after Whole Cake Island so expect spoilers up to this point.+ Tons and tons of content+ Easy switching between characters+ Straw Hats dialogue and banter makes the game feel like you are watching the anime+ Combat is fun and fluid (albeit easy)+ Revisiting the memories is done in a way to keep things fresh (It is not a retelling of the same story)+ Well optimized and stable on desktop+ Easy mod support- No native ultrawide support- Could use more optimization on the Steam Deck- Movement speed is a bit slow- Combat is pretty easyIf you are a DQXI or One Piece fan, this game is at least a 7/10. If you are a fan of both, it's a 9/10. Even the flaws of the game are easily solved with mods. Difficulty doesn't both me too much so I'm running the faster movement mod, UUU for ultrawide and FOV fixes and a mod to remove the outlines to clean things up a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: I love one piece. Not just as a cartoon but for its genius adult themes. I love the nostalgia of playing a game based on my favorite show. It looks great, was well made, has fun dialogue, and the turn based battle system is a fun take. I just have one problem with the game, it is just…too… EASY!! I haven’t encountered one instance where I felt as if strategy or insight was needed to win a fight. The rock paper scissor battle mechanics only work if doing the wrong thing results in a loss. That said — I love the game and look forward to beating it, easily!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not worth playing if you are not a One Piece fan. While it does feature an original story by Oda, it mostly involves retreading old arcs from the anime (up to Dressrosa). Characters and events will be referenced who don't appear in-game, so if you don't know OP you won't know what they're talking about and the gameplay is pretty basic JRPG fare that doesn't make up for it.Even if you are an OP fan this is hard to recommend. The new original story isn't that good and mainly has you revisiting past arcs with slight alterations. The highlights are the graphics and full Japanese VA cast. They do a great job and help bring life and authenticity to the game (there's no English VA if this is an issue for you). The graphics aren't technically amazing but they do a good job translating a 2D anime into 3D, with characters and environments that match Oda's style. The gameplay itself is a pretty basic turn-based JRPG with some very light platforming mechanics. The game has a habit of making you backtrack and the movement speed is far too slow. There is an automatic run-mode and you can speed up battles but I consider them mandatory rather than a convenient speed-up - the game is far too slow-paced otherwise. There's not much to the battle system. There's a simple rock-paper-scissors style type system for strengths/weaknesses but the difficulty is very unbalanced. Most of the game is far too easy, except for the very end (+ the DLC) where suddenly bosses can instakill you even if you're near max level. There's nothing particularly strategic about battles, just deal damage when the boss is vulnerable and heal/buff otherwise.One Piece Odyssey is not a terrible game. I never experienced a crash and some of the scenes involving the crew were definite highlights but it's also just not a very good game. Bland battles and gameplay with a lot of slow backtracking really bring down the pace and overall enjoyment.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wasn't expecting much coming into this game, but Odyssey manages to be somewhat enjoyable, with its main draw being its story and faithfulness to the characters and previous arcs in the main series. Fans of the manga or anime should enjoy the many callbacks to Alabasta, Water 7, Marineford, and Dressrosa as you explore these locations and meet old friends yourself.While the overall story was decent, I did find the ending unfortunately rather rushed. But I can't complain, because IMO everything was still better than any One Piece movie I've ever seen. This could've been an actual canon arc within the main storyline and I don't think anyone would mind.The other main aspect of the game is its combat system and it's... okay... I guess? Combat is overall very simplistic and follows the rock paper scissors formula that's seen in many other turn-based games. I never found myself at any risk of losing fights, although there were some tedious side quests that required me to use revive items. The main "strategy" of combat really comes from your equipment. The game calls them "accessories", but without them, you're going to have a really bad time. So invest in defensive stats, dump everything else into attack, and you're good to go.I would recommend Odyssey to fans of One Piece. But if you know nothing about the manga/anime, I just don't see this game as worth playing over the countless other games out there. And definitely get this game on sale, because it is way too overpriced for what it offers.PS: Get the mod that speeds up running and camera movement, or you'll get sick of the tedium of running around real quick.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first steam review but I felt like I had to say something...Don't buy this game. I'm a huge fan of RPG's and I fancy myself a achievement hunter/trophy hunter.I thought I would get into the One Piece craze by starting this game and also starting the anime.First of all, lets start with the pros.Pros: Graphics, Music and some of the humor and writing.Cons: Linear as the straightest line ever drawn. The game holds your hand horribly. Once, I saw a treasure within my grasp and tried to get it, only to be turned around by my party and told to keep moving forward.It also has a stupidly hard jump in difficulty in the endgame. I was sometimes 30+ levels above where I should be with the best accessories equipped and I was doing scratch damage to the bosses while they were taking off chunks of 66% health per swipe.Sorry, I may be old school but when you are over leveled with the best gear, you should be gum-guming people to the moon.This game almost made me at one point think about never playing RPG's again. That's how fatiguing it was.Check my play time. I did 100% of the game. It took me about a month to get through.TLDR; Nice graphics good music but the game gets so boring and hard that you want to stop gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: I've always thought One Piece would lend itself incredibly well to a JRPG format. The anime/manga feels like a grand JRPG -- a protagonist goes on an epic adventure, exploring fantastical places, meeting party members along the way, leveling up their skills and abilities as they overcome incredible obstacles. IT COULD WORK SO WELL AS A JRPG! But we're given a poorly fleshed out clip-show-episode of a game instead of what One Piece deserves.Cons: The story is a literal clip-show that does little service to the few arcs it features; what little original story it does have develops slowly, hardly anything has happened in 20+ hours of gameplay so far; many of the map areas should be bigger with more to explore, but instead it feels like the game holds you back from exploration with its bad level design and it constantly pulls you out of the roleplaying when Luffy can't jump over a damn bench despite being able to jump twice as high, the worst is all the potential shortcuts that are blocked by a guardrail that you should be able to clear but then you're just forced to trek back the way you came, that's just bad level design -- give me some light platforming instead of these static pathways; the in-game currency is basically useless, you get all the crafting supplies you need from loot crates and such, I guess there's the accessory items to buy but I'm never excited to go spend berries on them; you can't buy or obtain new outfits despite this feature being built into the game, I read you can only get one (1) change of outfit only if you pre-ordered or buy DLC -- it's a $60 game, WHY WOULD YOU NOT INCLUDE THESE AND MORE IN THE BASE GAME? Most of the quests and objectives are just fetch quests and retracing your steps, and it's obnoxious how often it launches into another short cutscene, one cutscene will end and you'll take a few steps and another cutscene will play; there's no bounce physics.Pros: The environments we are provided are really nice, it's great to walk around the world of One Piece and see the goofy creatures and stuff; graphics are great and fit the anime's style perfectly; the battle mechanics are pretty good even if they are rather simplistic, the special attacks look great; the dialogue is fun and true to characters.In summary, this game has so much potential but it doesn't live up to hardly any of it.

Played ~5h, felt like 15. No one should spend a cent on this..

_childDocuments_.review: One Piece Odyssey is truly a slow burn game that you'll either love or hate, there is no middle ground.Unlike all previous OP games which were either action adventure or hack'n'slash beat em ups,this one took a wild turn and went pure turn based RPG!While the main target audience may be OP fans, the plot can be understood without prior knowledge of it's world& can be an enjoyable experience for all.The Story is from the man, Eiichiro Oda himself (the guy who writes the original for those who don't know)and is a unique take on revisiting older arcs, stories & situations from a new perspective. It drifts elegantly between canon & filler, but the soul, heart & morale of One Piece are here. All characters are voiced by their original voice actors,while dialogues & visual expression are grand & spot on with the show. There are a few new original characters which are more than befitting and of course, the whole Luffy gang!Cities & areas are all crowded in their most part with many interactable NPCs, either pointing ya in the right direction, giving you stuff or just sharing their tale. You can control any crew member at any time & you'll have too often swap between them as they have different abilities, to spot & collect stuff or progress through different areas.The Visuals on the other hand are truly outstanding & cinematics are a blast to watch! And by cinematics, I mean both the Story ones that are quite frequent without becoming much tiresome but the battle cinematics too. Each & all skills during turn based battles have their own choreographed video, with multiple angles taking place in few seconds making 'em eye-candilicious. There are super attacks, combination skill attacks and a few other neat mechanics with some Persona infuence if I may say so & that, in a good way. Battles unfortunately are quite too easy for the most parts with a few exception on Bosses & "elite" enemies. There is even an automated battle setting that lets the AI take care of things.There is no difficulty setting and there is no grind requirement (which may also be a good thing for some)to progress further, even while skipping all random encounter enemies & rushing the story.That, alongside the fetch quests even during the main story, which I was never a fan off, are the only negatives I can find about the game.To close it off, I'm giving it 7.5/10. It's a relaxing & easy game with good amount of nostalgia for the fans,a fine plot with many strong & few weak moments, decent pacing, the old-school & slow archetype of RPGand a Luffy that's always hungry.
_childDocuments_.name: ONE PIECE ODYSSEY

_childDocuments_.review: Short version:Even if you like One Piece, you will......hate the repetitive combat eventually...find out that the game is far from being open world...get bored with the cheap animations aside from skill animations...probably mod the game to have at least some fun...get sick of invisible walls and movement...get tired of the game swapping some your team members randomly...skip conversations and chitchat at some point...have to grind for materials and money...feel betrayed when they give you 30k instead of 3mil for a bounty...notice that they use the same models for lots of enemies...question life when you need all your crew mates to defeat one DLC bossLong version: TL;DR → Don't buy, and also tell everyone you know to not buy.I wish you could rate it "neutral" because that's what the game is for me. Not bad, but not good either. Just for the sake of preventing one person to regret buying the game, I'll give it a negative one. This game is far from being actual "open world". Don't get fooled by that.Is the intro video really necessary every time you start the game? Also, who the heck decided that return to the menu or quit the game in general has to be such a pain?As others already complained about is the unnecessary backtracking all the time. (Annoying) Fast travel won't get unlocked until at least 5h into the game.The game gets stretched so much, it's not even funny anymore. According to steam, only 25% of the players completed chapter 3. By a total of 8 + final chapter..This is not open world, it's linear levels with little options to explore, considering the game allows you to explore and not forces you to head to the current objective. Which is the case 90% of the whole game.Random endless chit-chat nonsense preventing you from opening the map and interacting with certain objects or NPCs.Same voice lines after every fight. You have to mash skip when entering and after the fight to skip the annoying chitchat after you heard it 50 times during the last hour of gameplay.,You have to interact with most NPCs or objects to get some "hidden" tasks done. Prepare yourself to run through every map at least twice (probably more) and interact with everything you see. Some chests that are accessible within the first hours can't even be opened, and you have to keep track of where they are to get them later on...Jumping exists but is useless 70% of the time since you can't jump most things - only the "intended" ways to go, especially in towns. Can't even jump a fence, has to run around. Whoever thought this was fine has to be fired.Fights are repetitive and get boring really quick. You'll notice that within the first couple fights.If a game offers "speed up" options in fights, you know that'll be quite the screen you're staring at. If you played Fairy Tail, you should be used to it, though.Didn't except a "new" story for this game, yet you'll go through all One Piece story again, which is a little bit altered. So, pretty much skip most backstory videos/cutscenes if you played any of the One Piece games.Crafting and character-lock for certain paths/collecting stuff is just dumb IMO. It doesn't even highlight unless you are on a certain character like Nami or Sanji. The only tells you that there is something when you're literally almost on top of it.Gearing up just with these artifacts is so boring. You have pretty much no real chance to play somewhat tactical. The game has some factor that isn't clear when enemies are plebs and when they suddenly do 3x the damage to what they used to do before.Either you steamroll everyone or get one shot by the next boss. Had to use food the first time to revive Zoro and Luffy 3 times because they got one shot by Sir Crocodile (once in first fight, two times in second) because the game replaced my Chopper with Usopp after the cutscene for some reason.Just slap HP & DEF on chopper, so he can heal everyone and never dies, all out ATK on all damage dealers (Zoro, Luffy, Nami), and you're set.  AOE everyone except bosses. Use attacks that reach or push enemies into another zone to prevent squishy attackers like Nami  from taking damage. I didn't bother with any other characters in my first 9h of game and it didn't change. Sanji is useless because he can't attack women. Franky and brook get unlocked way too late in order to really bother with them. Robin is alright but her skills are way too expensive in cost. So I stuck with Luffy, Zoro, Nami & Chopper for the whole game unless the game forced me to use others.3 different damage types and 2 different defense types are dumb. A mod that negates that pretty much underlines that statement by the community.Oh, and I modded the game to make it harder (1 level below max difficulty mod)Edit:  Changed my mind. The game pisses me off the more I play it. Definitely negative now. Especially when the game adjusts your formation and team members randomly at some point without any information.Grabbed the deluxe edition for around €30 and I still kinda regret it. If you paid more than that, congrats, you wasted money. The pricing is just all over the place, especially the deluxe edition and DLCs itself.Finished the game 100% (182 tasks) & steam achievements (excluding DLC) with modded 2nd highest difficulty in under 44h without guide except for the last 2 hours of collecting stuff I missed before.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing for a little while now and there are some small, but major things I find that really ruin the experience. There is I guess what you could call ambient dialogue that goes on as you get close to places and people, and that's great because it's usually something that adds to your understanding or at least fills the silence. Except 90% of the time it happens in the worst places, it triggers right by a group of bad guys, or as your running through a doorway to attack someone who you just waited 10 seconds for to turn around.  And once you exit battle the conversation doesn't trigger again. I just made it to the Sandy Oasis and Luffy said there's a perfect place to camp, right off to the side next to a save spot. So I talked to the people, saved, and turned it off for a bit. Came back a little bit ago and started the campfire that would normally trigger a cut scene but instead it didn't. Everyone in camp is now talking about events that haven't even happened yet, like I somehow am now further in the game and then backtracked to here again. I think it broke the prompt because I didn't camp right away before saving and quitting. It's set up very poorly in that regard unfortunately. But the rest of the game is fun, I'm not a real One Piece fan but everything is enjoyable so far, follows the format of the anime pretty well. There are places on ground as you explore with a magnify glass icon that you can have repeatable interactions with and it'd be much better if that were the case for the ambient dialogue as well. _childDocuments_.review: As someone who isn't a huge One Piece fan, I came into this game with extreme expectations in terms of an RPG as this game is published by Bandai Namco and developed by ILCA, the devs behind 2021's Pokemon Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl. How does this game stack up though? Well I've played about 7 1/2 hours of this game, and I have a list of pro's and cons that this game offers!PROS:-The game is truly beautiful and fully realized! The models, textures and sound design are all really good -The animations are really good for the attacks and cutscenes -Gameplay is really solid! Not everyone is into turn based games, but this game isn’t just attack attack attack, there’s a bit more to it! -The music is amazing, calling back to each arc this game explores from the One Piece series -Not every quest is a fetch quest or lame tackling a boss quest, and I really love that about this game -The costume choices are on POINT -This game has boobs... and lots of them. -Eiichiro Oda (the creator of One Piece) lead the writing for the story while still ACTIVELY writing the new chapters for the manga, and that’s really impressive -Exploration is fun and it’s nice to just get lost in the world CONS:-This game is WAY too easy. For this to be a JRPG, it’s offensively easy. I haven’t once had to revive a party member, and I’ve nearly clocked 8 hours of playtime. -There is no difficulty option which makes this JRPG suffer even harder. Pokémon is another offender of this HUGE problem with Role Playing Games. RPG’S NEED DIFFICULTY OPTIONS. -The story is nothing but filler and while it’s narratively inoffensive, it feels like there is ZERO weight to the story. I’m also extremely tired of every One Piece game covering the arcs of the manga/show and feels as if the devs of these games are too afraid to upset One Piece fans by doing something original. One Piece film: RED, while not official canon to the timeline, does enough to make it substantially different enough from everything else that the series has to offer. -The game only offers Japanese dialogue, which takes away about 85% of my attention from the game to look at whatever youtube video I’m watching on my 2nd monitor. No game that is released in the US/any other English-speaking country should be limited to only one specific language, even if the source is primarily Japanese. -This game has some technical issues with a LOT of screen tearing, frame rate isn’t consistent, and the game will sometimes just not respond to you. The camera is also kind of abysmal, especially when you do the gum gum rocket traversal option -While the exploration is nice, it doesn’t feel rewarding. The world while EXTREMELY beautiful, doesn’t have much to offer.  Overall while the Cons are substantial, this game does provide a seriously fun One Piece experience! As I said, I am not a huge One Piece fan, but I do respect the source material and realize how important it is that this anime is!

_childDocuments_.review: I wanna start the review of by saying, that even tho i do recommend the game, i also dont recommend it at the same time. Now let me clarify why.Story: The story is pretty much the same as it is with every One Piece Game which doesnt recreate the main plot of the Manga. Find Island, meet mysterious characters, find out the truth about the island, end. So far the story is nothing special, and i doubt it will become much more. There are certain things which try to make it interesting "Five Elders,Poneglyph like objects from another One Piece Game, and mentions of the old world etc", but im sure it wont have an interesting payoff if i consider the other games plots. Not bad not good. 5/10 so far.Combat: Now lets get into why i DONT recommend the game. The combat is insulting. Not because its too hard or too complicated. None of that, its just really really easy. Its so easy that i think a toddler could do it with no problems. So what is so easy about it you say? Well you one shot almost all enemies (even without abilities) and they deal like 2 Dmg to you. Some will now say "Dude thats just the beginning, it will get harder later on". And to that i say, i wish it did. Im now around 13 hours into the game, im at Alabasta, and its still the same, but now you 2 shot enemies. WOW so much harder...The only time i almost had problems was at a side quest, because the game throws 5 enemies at you which almost one shotted half my team. AND I LIKED THAT. I thought it finally gets more difficult, but nope. For some reason this fight is fairly difficult and the rest goes back to easy baby mode. WHY. I already handicap myself by not healing and using no equip items and its still way too easy. And the worst part is, the game doesnt let you decide the difficulty. The fact that an RPG from 2023 doesnt let you decide difficulty is baffling. This game is somehow easier than modern Pokemon. You need 0 strategy, 0 skill, just spam attack and it works. Worst part, the concept of battle is actually interesting. On the battlefield you have different zones. In each zone there are enemies and allies randomly put in, which means if Nami gets into battle its possible that she is surrounded by 5 enemies, and the other characters need to go to that zone to help her fight. This concept is really interesting, and could have amazing set ups for cool fights, but its useless because you one shot every enemie anyway. Funny enough the tutorial uses that mechanic very well, and it hasnt done that since. Its onestly pathetic and destroys the game for me.  2/10 Had potential, flushed down the drain because its actual game journalist difficulty.Other Gameplay: The other gameplay is just classic RPG stuff. Fetch quests, exploring, dialogue, farming etc. One thing i enjoy a lot is that every Strawhat is usable in combat and in the Open World, and they all do more or less unique things. Luffy can stretch, Chopper can fight into tight spaces, Sanji sees and gains more food objects etc. One thing i hate is the hand holding. I understand that the game sometimes goes "You cant go there yet because reasons", its annoying but its and RPG so its expected. What i hate is, if you explore the area, you will find things like small caves and openings. And if you think a bit, you can maybe come to the conclusion "Oh maybe Chopper can fit in there" And he does. Cool little "riddle" for exploration. The problem: If you approach any of these things, the game gives you a pop up which says "HEY IDIOT MAYBE CHOPPER CAN FIT IN THERE, I WONDER IF CHOPPER CAN FIT IN THERE, PICK CHOPPER, CHOPPER,C H OOOO PER." And it does that with every character which can do something like that W H Y.  You also sometimes need to find the right way and can even talk to NPCs to get tips, but that is useless because where you need to go is always marked on your map.Hand holding bs.  4/10Now the last thing:Charme:This game oozes charme and love for the OP world. You get so many funny scenes, sentences and references to older games, movies and of course the Manga/Anime itself. Its so cool and really adds to the immersion that that is THE ONE PIECE WORLD. If you are a One Piece fan the game will make you smile. It really respects the source material and mentions so many things from the past, without making it feel shoehorned or nostalgia bate. Just for that alone i recommend the game. Its also kinda interesting with its canon. The game mentions multiple non canon things like Shiki vs Strawhats, references to other games like Unlimited Cruise, and even has non canon characters in the game. So in a way this game just confirmed that all games, all filler all movies are canon inside this games universe, which is funny. 8/10 Truly feels One Piece. Makes you feel like a rubber man. I think the game is ok. If they ever decide to add a hard mode, i would recommend the game. But without its a "Only buy on sale thing".  It can be fun, but the hand holding is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, and the combat is insulting. It pains me because at its core, it feels like its made with passion and love. And it perfectly captures the One Piece humour and writing, but it just sucks as a game.  Overall 4/10. If no hard mode in future, get it on sale.
