_childDocuments_.review: Although i'd recommend this game, it has it's fair share of negatives.Before I get into them if you decide to play this game i'd recommend running a cheat engine and enabling 2X running speed, for some reason you run at a snails pace (genuinely annoying to explore) and can't escape any enemies as they're faster than you which i've not seen in a jrpg before. Not sure why the developers decided this as it feels awful. Firstly, it is very similar to the eastern only release of one piece romance dawn for psp, same basic gameplay loop, similar gear system, less grinding (which does make it better)Secondly, it reminds me of the fairy tail game released within the last couple years, great for fans of the series, however very clearly a cash grab that's slightly lazy. A limited skill-set, a limited num,ber of characters appearing, and a limited amount of content spread over wider areas and side quests which extends the playtime of the game. Lastly, a lack of a story, it neither goes fully into the one piece history, only using Alabasta, Water 7, A small chunk of Marineford, and Dressrossa. Yet only uses a pretty small area to explore for the new memoria story, with very basic jrpg inspired dungeons. It relies on the fandoms nostalgia without ever giving us what we want, and omitting Whole cake and Wano, which for fans had the coolest power ups and enemies. Please give us a game or series of games that goes through the entire one piece story, it would allow a consistant upgrade system as your crew gets better and recruits more people as they go through the world of one piece. Plus there's enough content to not have to throw a bunch of nameless enemies at you constantly and fill it with sooo many repetitive side quests that you cba to play through them anymore. (The bounties in this game are pitiful, random no name enemies they've powered up slightly and given a bounty (which you get between 1% & 10% of), and endgame you get new high level enemies in the form of yellow memoria cubes. I hoped for new enemies not used within the games story, but nope, just the same boss enemies from across the game powered up again. Which if you have decently levelled and upgraded your gear, were still no problem. Overall I've enjoyed the game for what it is, a nostalgia trip embracing some pretty slim JRPG mechanics, but it just needed more. Graphically it looks good, and suits the one piece world, the sound design fits as well, and i've not ran into any bugs so can't complain there.

_childDocuments_.review: I took time off of work to play this, I would say buy it BUT wait until its on sale. TLDR at bottom.I'm not a a huge fan of turn based games, well RPGs in general. There is NO Difficulty level in this game, and even being inept in the genre this game was a cakewalk.This also introduced something I have only ever seen in mobile games.......AUTO BATTLING?!?!?!!?!? WTFThis consists of having the computer use all of your highest TP costing moves, then playing like ♥♥♥♥.This game is not worth the $60 price, the fact that it was even more for extra outfits and money was a joke.By the end of the game I had 40 million berries, easily enough to go back and buy out the Yoisa shops in each level. There's plot holes, SO MANY INVISIBLE WALLS, you can't even jump over a railing to save 5 seconds just a invis wall so you have to run around and back to where you started. There's lighted windows inside destroyed buildings that are rubble laying sideways in the streets, but the warm inviting glow of hospitality remains because of poor design.Don't even get me started about the Breakable boxes and pots, my god. If i hadn't shaved my head prior to 20+ hours of gameplay I would have ripped all of my hair out in frustration. Once you break the boxes and pots and re enter the level, the pots are back BUT WITH NOTHING INSIDE. When looking for 99 YaYa cubes spread over 50 hrs of gameplay this becomes unbearable. In many other reviews people are referring to this as a cash grab, sadly I have to agree, the story could have been more thought out, Gameplay more polished, designs less rushed.  TLDR If you love One Piece this game is for you but NOT for full price, Half price is even pushing it, I'd say pick it up if its 50% to 80% off

_childDocuments_.review: The best One Piece game thus far, mostly due to the dev time given to it. The biggest issues however come from padding out quests that lead to the greater moments with backtracking, that poor quest design coupled with aggressively slow movement speed can hollow out the experience. The time spent running around CAN be fixed with a mod called "speed piece" making the experience far better.The only other gripe I can think of is that there are shops that sell clothes (ex. one located in the Water 7 area) hinting at the idea that in-game costume unlocks were going to be a thing, but probably got scrapped leaving the pre-order costumes as the only outfits in the game. Thankfully there are also a few costume mods to make up for it. All that aside its a great title that allows you to explore settings from the series, retaining the liveliness its known for in character interactions and enemy designs. But I don't see anyone picking this up unless they love the series enough to overlook the issues with quests and have access to mods.

_childDocuments_.review: Insanely easy with no difficulty setting. You could just press a over and over and would never notice a loss. Very boring, chapter 1 consisted of the same fight 15 times with the same monkey npcs. Combat is rock paper scissors but even if you attack with someone that you're supposed to be weak against you tend to one shot them anyway. I barely noticed i had even left the tutorial before they had me running inbetween npcs for the most useless dialogue you could ever imagine. Every object or scene you are able to interact with just gives you unvoiced filler dialogue like "What a pretty flower." or "Isnt that boat big?". Such a shame, ill continue to play and see if i can at least get some sort of satisfaction from the bigger scenes but as of right now i think its all going to fall short.Edit: After 17 hours I finally reached Crocodile and the fight took at the least an hour an a half. The cutscene was good and may be the sole reason i push to complete the game. It took 20 hours to complete chapter 2 while doing every sidequest and bounty that i could. The estimated 30 hour completion time given to us by the devs is looking a bit off. I would guess the game will take anywhere from 90-100+ hours to complete while doing side missions. If you dont do the side missions though i doubt you will be leveled enough to do the main missions. All in all im starting to enjoy the game now that they have given me some cool action cutscenes and finally a new set of skills for everyone. I am looking forward to seeing how the rest of of the game will hold up.TLDR: Game is very VERY VERY SLOW build up but the big moments are great for any One Piece fan.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is not worth $60, probably just watch all the cutscenes on YT, or if it ever goes on sale pick it up!NGL I love One Piece, but this game is not worth $60. Game play is super simple. Combat is rock paper scissors except you can still one shot scissors with paper. You can spam basic attacks to clear most fights. Enemies do not hit hard at all. The interactable magnifying glass areas are repetitive simple dialogue lines over and over. Not worth interacting with.(Luffy says he wants to eat every animal they find, and Robin comments something about rocks). You run from marker to marker which is just cutscene to cutscene basically.I am talking exiting a cutscene to walk forward 15 steps to enter another cutscene.It was cool using each of their unique abilities in the world, but it just felt really lackluster.This applies especially to Luffy's Gum Gum Rocket.You use Gum Gum rocket on specifically marked areas like a grapple hook, which is okay...but it literally sent him flying straight to the marked grapple spot, and he loses momentum and falls straight down from that spot. The last thing that bothered me is the movement.I don't normally play set path games like these, so these could be normal to most games in this genre, and I could just be super ignorant.There are tons of invisible walls.At the very beginning on the beach, there was a Pokemon-esque ledge I couldn't jump over.You could walk all the way down the path and go around the ledge, but you could not jump over the tiny rock border as it was just an invisible wall.I am not sure how long this next issue persist throughout the game, but sometimes when leaving the set path to grab an item I saw 20 feet away, it would have an NPC talk to me and tell me to come back, and then have a black loading screen appear just to teleport me closer to the set path. I prefer pokemons method of telling you that you can not go that way and having you turn around yourself, instead of being instantly sent to a black screen.This one is super picky but, there are also ladders everywhere, and you climb them particularly slow when you climb them up and down, which is strange for a rubber man who jumps high, rockets around everywhere, and is always falling from places.The only thing I enjoyed were the cutscenes.The cutscenes are great. The animation is beautiful! All their attacks are super well done. However, these cutscenes are easily found online and will satisfy any needs to know the story!

_childDocuments_.review: I'll just start by saying that i'm not a fan of One Piece, I have not watched or read it in years.I really did enjoy the game and a lot of the negative will be nitpicking more than anything. They need more explaining as to what is the problem which make it seems long but is not that much in reallity.I'll also avoid spoilers except a very very very minor one that doesn't reveal anything important.tldr : game is very fun but has a few missed opportunities and small issues.Really good if you like one piece.Might be nice if you know about it and are lightly interested in its world like myself.It look really nice and fits the artstyle of the anime very well.A unique story but still very tightly related to past stories of the manga played with a different perspective.I'm not a big JRPG player but the combat system was pretty unique and fun.Being able to walk around in important places is neat (although your characters are a bit slow).You can control most of the strawhats even outside of fights (has some issues i'll explain later).Lots of content if you don't ignore what's unnecessary but might get repetitive at some point.Had no issues at all playing with mouse and keyboard.I do not believe it to be any important spoiler as it is something you find out about very early on in the game and is core to it but, if you truly want to know nothing story wise then careful :In summary, the game misses the chance to create something fun and unique about the story of the game and manga and stays pretty uncreative in that regard overall. You can control almost every strawhat to explore the world and each have their own ability, which sounds pretty cool because you think you can just explore everything with your favorite character, but, you will find yourself playing as luffy most of the time since his ability to progress within areas is mandatory all the time and the quality of life of picking items from far away.You will also spend a lot of time switching between characters whenever you need zoro to cut something or chopper's size to enter new places for exemple.Meanwhile, characters like sanji, robin or nami have very little use and you'll explore most areas barely using them because each time you wanna swap character, you have to enter a menu, select the character you want and have a small fade to black while it switches, which isn't bad at first but gets boring very quickly.Exploring can also be a chore despite the few teleports you have access to considering the size of some areas (mostly the cities) compared to the speed at which you move.The game has a lot of sidequests, which seems like a good opportunity to have all you crew interact with all sorts of characters, but too many of them are about sanji being horny for the quest giver.Seriously, characters like zoro or robin barely interact with the rest of the world during those quest, while sanji is overpresent in so many of them.It corelates to the fact that each character is kind of stripped down to it's minimum.Sanji is horny for every female character, zoro only talks about being lost, nami about money ...The game focuses pretty hard on the core of the characters and not much else.To end this here, the game is really fun.The negative part of the review might seem long, but it's mostly a few things that need explaining as to why it's a "problem" as opposed to the good parts which is just basically explaining a few things I enjoyed and that made this game pretty good in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: When I got this, I was not expecting it to be as good as it is. It is by far the best One Piece game yet in my opinion and I'm not even past chapter two. The amount of care and love put into it is absurd by anime game standards and the combat is more entertaining than any turn based rpg I played. The story (so far) is also really good as expected since it was written by the original author. For downsides, the game isn't very challenging, although to be fair I have been fighting a lot of enemies I probably could've skipped and have been optimizing the accessory and memory fragment system. I can imagine it probably does get difficult towards late game and end game. I wouldn't recommend getting the deluxe edition until DLC comes out because let's all be honest, every game gets DLC nowadays. To sum this up, this is likely the best One Piece game by far, and is generally a really good experience. I most likely will update this after I beat it because this game is also ridiculously long as you'd expect from a One Piece rpg.(edit)So after 100% completing the game, my opinion more or less remains the same. The game's environments and move animations all look really high quality. The Dressrosa chapter is most likely my favorite with the Alabasta chapter coming in second. The story is better than I expected it to be especially towards the end and the final battle was a pretty strong conclusion. The game does remain pretty easy from start to finish thanks to the generous xp from battles, really strong food items, and accessories. That is until you try the post game challenges and the difficulty spike kicks you in the balls and Chopper is the only thing keeping you on life support. The gameplay is really entertaining even after the 100 hour mark, I never found myself getting bored. The game also isn't mean with their collectibles and they aren't too hard to all find. Ending off, although the game is a pretty casual experience, I think it sets a high standard of quality for all One Piece games going forward.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're the same then definitely check out this flawed-but-beautiful game, and if you just like turn-based JRPG's in general i think this is still an enjoyable experience.The story does take a minute to get going but I liked it overall, its non-canon but still an original story written by Oda himself. On the island of Waford you enter the memories of the Straw Hats' adventure to regain their lost power. You revisit locations and story arcs of OP(Alabasta, Water Seven, Marineford, and Dressrosa) but the characters are their present selves, so they interact with these storylines in different ways, which adds a little twist. The mysteries and history of Waford also kept me engaged. It feels like playing through another arc of OP and that's pretty cool. I really liked the new characters Adio and Lim, and the different ruins you get to explore on the island. This is a long game (90+ hours for me) but the story and crew interaction is what mainly kept me invested, this feels like One Piece.Similar to Dragon Quest, you explore open-map areas and begin combat by contacting enemies on the map. The main area is the island of Waford, which has branching pathways to the different ruins where you initially enter the different memories. You can explore the map with almost every Straw Hat in your party (not Franky or Brook :( ) and there are some character-specific actions for exploration and gathering loot, which there is a lot of. The turn-based-combat feels good, with the rock-paper-scissors mechanic allowing you to keep all the Straw Hats involved with their unique combat skills that fans will recognize. There's a bunch of accessories you can equip and level up, and the named combat skills can be leveled up as well.Clearly a lot of work was put into these systems and they are solid, but I do have some complaints. The main one being this game is mostly too easy, outside of a few of the bigger boss fights. I never really felt in danger with proper leveling and accessorizing, and all the items I had didn't really have to be used until the latter portions of the game. This game also holds your hand a little too much with the exploration, mostly telling you exactly where you need to go, even what platform to jump onto next sometimes. This was pretty annoying especially in the beginning. There's also a few moments of annoying backtracking I could have done without.This is a good-looking game. I loved exploring the different settings, the scale of the areas is bigger than I thought. I didn't know what to expect in the memory areas, but they put a lot of effort into recreating the look and feel of each unique island. I believe Alabasta is even bigger than the main area Waford. There are lots of NPC's to interact with and the Straw Hats have unique animations for climbing and opening chests. The animations in combat look awesome, the attacks are flashy and satisfying. There aren't a ton of animated story cutscenes but they looked good as well.The music and voice acting are great of course, this is OP. The main cast does a great job as always, making all the interactions feel genuine. This was a good game, and a great One Piece experience for me. There are definitely improvements that could be made but there's a ton of content here. You can tell the devs really put their heart into it and wanted to create an enjoyable experience for the gamer. Check it out dudes!

_childDocuments_.review: One Piece Odyssey is decent. It does not excel at anything but it's not bad either. Throughout the game you go between the game timeline and past arcs (being Alabasta, Water Seven, Marineford and Dressrosa), I think this game could've been much more if it was done more properly, considering you are going back to old arcs I expected more from the story content but majority of fights were skipped from each arc. I wasn't satisfied with side content, sidequest were boring and usually required finding something random or fighting enemies (most basic sidequests in every game), bounties were alright and I didn't care that much for memory links. World Exploration is alright. Arcs were paced finely in my opinion expect the Alabasta arc which overstayed it's welcome. Still after all the negatives this game has it's One Piece charm and made me a bit nostalgic going through old arcs. Also models for Nami and Robin were great. Overall I feel like it's an average game, has a lot of issues but when you compare pros and cons I think it's an enjoyable experience if you're a fan of One Piece, but getting it at full price is not worth it, at most 50% off and it's a good deal.

_childDocuments_.review: As a massive One Piece fan I really enjoyed this game. Good story, decent mechanics and overall good time. I have to admit I was a bit taken aback going from Pirate Warriors 3 and 4 to this due to those games being beat 'em ups and this being a turn based RPG, but after playing a bit you get the hang of it and get locked in. One gripe I have with this game is the pacing in some areas can be a bit weird and the turn based fights can drag on a bit, specifically towards the end. I also have to mention that the game sometimes has a bit of randomly crashing or freezing which can be a bit scary, especially if you forget, or neglect to save after a while -- I eventually become a paranoid and habitual saver every opportunity I had. (I had to redo the final base game boss fight twice before it stuck and I got the achievement.)The DLC is...more One Piece Odyssey, so if you liked the base game and its story, you'll like the DLC. Interesting 'extra' story and a nice opportunity to see fan favourites return for a fight or two, so that's nice. Overall, I'm looking forward to the next One Piece game. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Solid turn-based combat JRPG with interesting mechanics.The "gimmick" you'll find in this game is that you have to work around multiple individual fights occurring at once. Certain abilities can only target enemies directly around the character while other abilities can target enemies anywhere on the battlefield. If the enemies around one particular character are defeated then they can essentially "join" other fights that still going on. It provides an interesting strategy element that sets this game apart from most JRPGs. It blows my mind that there are a decent amount of negative reviews whining about the turn-based combat when that is one of the selling points of the game. Its like going to an Italian restaurant then screaming about there being no hot dogs available. Its honestly hard to believe that these people were able to even install the game. The graphics and art style are great (very much looks like Dragon Quest XI which is why people keep bringing it up), Nami and Robin's assets might even be larger than they are in the actual series, and also -- THE ONE PIECE IS REAL.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of the review, I'm at the Arabasta arc. Seems enough, as I've noticed the negatives about it at the very start of the game. By no means is this a perfect game, but it doesn't deserve some negative reviews, with others I agree and I will mention them here. Having played World Seeker, which is similar in it's gameplay ("Open World"), Odyssey is a massive improvement in all it's aspects. I had to make myself finish it, having it sit idle for like a year before playing it again: with Odyssey, I don't have that feeling and I really enjoy the world so far.With that being said, it looks absolutely gorgeous. There are bits that seem off, I have to mention that the Strawhats look exactly like they should, except Zoro. He's the only one that seems (to me atleast) rougher around the edges than the rest.Everyone is mostly animated (with that I mean moving in character due to lack of a better word) and the Strawhats act like their anime counterpart with the gesticulations and face expressions (they are also fully voiced by their original Japanese VA, except some minor dialogue). I have to mention that sometimes the audio doesn't seem like the same quality? I guess it's due to recording from different locations due to lockdown (or having to re-record some parts). Also, the mix is not balanced. They are engaged in conversations often, which gives them that "anime soul". They also communicate in combat, which also makes it more realistic and characteristic. The cutscenes use game models, so the transitions are smoother (I haven't tested this, but other reviews say they don't switch to their costumes in the cut scenes).The battles... yeah, they are easy, though it's a good practice to avoid battles wherever you can because you can get overwhelmed easily and could quit due to that. I avoid the term "walking simulator" but the game IS an One Piece scenery in itself, and you can engage with it with using your favourite character from the anime (if you watched it, if not, then the game is maybe not for you). You can switch between other members at all times, except when a quest uses specific characters. You won't be able to go where during gameplay since the quests won't let you, which is the biggest negative from me. It seems lazy, even if that should collide with the quest itself, I should be able to check the place out. Also there is a lot of double-backing, and the fast travel is unlocked after you get to half of Arabasta, where I am now.The skill animations are probably the best thing in the game (except Zoro's, I mentioned earlier that he seems off and skill animations are one of it). I won't spoil anything, but there are some great moments which, might not be usefull always, but give a comedic part, had happened in anime also. Overall, if you don't care that much about the combat (there are other games which excel at it - Persona 5 Royal e.g.) it's a great game and can be enjoyed if you give it a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: where to start. first of all the game has great character design, and has the original Japanese voice actors, but that's about where the great things come to an end (yes already)this game is plagued by one of the worst things in gaming, story padding, and when i say that it's plagued by padding, i really mean that it is infested, diseased, terminal, and quite frankly ruined by the amount of padding that the story has to make this game take around 30 hours to fully fully complete. one of the worst sections for this is the dressrosa arc and it never stops even after you finish with that arc, here's an example, the tower on waford (i'm trying really hard not to give any spoilers in case someone want to play it for themselves) the "puzzle" section is just full of cut-scenes showing what appears after standing on a button, even if it's directly in front of you, literally a 5-10 second cutscene showing a path appear, and it does this roughly 20 to 30 times if you want to grab all of the items in each area, and then there are cutscenes that start literally 3 seconds after one ends just for the characters to re-state what was said in the previous cutscene, at onje point there are 4 of these in a row. and my lord these add up fast, and makes the progression really drag on for longer than it should.the combat system SHOULD in all rights be good as a JRPG, but it falls apart quickly once a couple of your characters get their "full battle field one hit" moves, such as luffy with his Conqueror’s haki, which one hits' every single enemy in all of the battle zones that your other characters are in (even bosses get one hit). and also with the combat the accessories you can completely wipe the floor with any fight even without the one hit moves i already talked about. the combat is just far too easy to genuinely be fun, so after maybe the 10th fight it becomes very very boring and repetative, so you start avoiding fights like they're not even there and yet you still end up being over-leveled with most every other fight you get into. i'll give an example, the marineford battle, it's reccomended that you be level 35 to play it, by the time i got to that section i was already level 60 just from random battles and side quests through the other arcs beforhand. so basically the MANY MANY cutscenes before ever fighting anyone in marineford leads up to whats supposed to be a few "epic" battles, but after only a couple of your strongest attacks the main enemies, Kizaru, Akainu, and Aokiji fall really quickly. so what should technically be one of the longest arcs full of battles, is just 3-4 fights that take maybe 1 minute each, and half of that being the little cutscene that plays at the start of each fight.overall, this game has every right to be an amazing game, especially for fans of the anime, but it quickly falls apart into what seems like a cashgrab, riding on the back of the anime, and it begins to feel like they didn't really try seeing as they recycle story arcs from the anime and manga, even after saying that it's an original story, yes the 10% of the game that isn't in the recycled arcs is original, but the other 90% is just what i said, recycled story from the anime/manga. if this sounds good to you or you're just a huge One piece fan, then by all means buy it, but otherwise i would seriously recommend waiting for when this game is on sale, otherwise it isn't worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall very positive experience. You navigate through open areas and find items, food, and cubes to begin crafting, cooking and increasing the strengths of each of the Straw Hats. There is a level of fun to this because you can make them powerful enough to wipe enemies at a whim. _childDocuments_.review: Let's deal with the elephant in the room right away really, really, *really* fast: One Piece Odyssey is not a difficult game 99% of the time. Usage of all of the systems in the game will let you steamroll most encounters, and bosses can range from easy to a serious handful.Now that that's out of the way...this is actually one of the best One Piece games I've played, and probably ranks up there as one of my favorite RPGs in general at this point. Discarding the matter of difficulty, ILCA did a fantastic job with the end product. Their time working on DQ11 shows across the board, from a Mini-medal-esque 'smash boxes and the like' questline to combat giving strong DQ vibes. It doesn't reach the same quality as a polished Dragon Quest, but the atmosphere's there and it blends fantastically with the One Piece frame draped over it.Sakuraba's know-how is definitely noticeable throughout the soundtrack, with fields and dungeons having the appropriate atmosphere for a Straw Hat adventure, same as heavier moments. And thus far, Odyssey hasn't held back on the punches. If you were the sort to cry through the story of One Piece the first time through, Odyssey knows how to tap those same feelings.TL;DR: nothing groundbreaking, but it's a rock-solid RPG that leans heavily to the easier side, and that's nothing that can't be modded or patched out later. Worth full price if you're a One Piece fan, and worth looking into as a deal if you've ever been curious about One Piece and want some supplementary Cliff's Notes on the story as you read the manga or watch the anime.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't do enough research before buying the game.  The story is goes deeper into the history of the world of One Piece but since it's not canon, just like the movies, I don't see what's the point.  Although you're revisiting "the memories" of your adventures, the events that happen changes.  It doesn't even cover a lot of the arc, for example, once you get to Alabasta, you're already looking for Crocodile's hideout.  They just diluted the story and have these expositions in between chapters, that pretty much tells the player how they're supposed to be feeling.  With all the cuts they made in the story, it still took a long time to play because of all the running back and forth, solving puzzles in dungeons, switching characters because each possess a unique skill to gather specific items.  What really bothered me was when you can only fast travel when you have no need for it.  It also killed me that they can't jump over railings.  The battle system/skills/accessory build is a nightmare.  When I saw how they did accessories, I had a flashback to Valkyria Chronicles and how you outfit your tank.  The game also teases you with different costumes, but the only available costume to change into is from the preorder.  I'm sure that'll change later on but they should've done it before releasing the game.  I remember buying complete games back in the day.  I was hoping they did the game just like Dragonball Z Kakarot.  I'm a big One Piece fan, this was a real let down.  For what it's worth I didn't stop playing the game until I finished it.. so it's tolerable.  Just wait til it goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty much to Dragon Quest what Battle for Bikini Bottom is to Banjo Kazooie. That means it has some very obvious design flaws but if you like the characters and the world it might even that out for you. The main problem is the quest design, sometimes you do nothing but run to a certain point, get into a dead end, go back to the start to ask am npc for help, then go back to the dead end to finally continue. You'll see the same maps and groups of enemies over and over again. Really kills the pacing. You could probably cut out 10 hours of the game and still get the same experience. However it really nails the one piece feel. The animations, the banter between the characters and the art style really push you through it's low points. As for combat, it uses a Rock-Paper-Scissors system similar to the one at the core of Pokemon and Persona. While it's nothing ground breaking, challengeing or groundbreaking, it gets the job done. I guess that's what could be said about the game as a whole: It takes what works from the genre but doesn't really add anything new. But So yeah in the end if you didn't like one piece and turn based rpgs before this won't win you over.

_childDocuments_.review: While the story, world-building, characterization, and interactions between the Strawhats is wonderfully done and feels nearly canon (especially the Sanji and Nami shipping here and there.)There is a few things to say about the game play that I am not a big fan of.For an anime game that calls itself 'open world.' It is LIMITED.-For one, If the story wants you to go somewhere and you try to go off on your own, a character will say something and the screen will blacken and send you where you last were.-Two, while you can wander around when not having to do something, your area of wandering is locked to the map, if an area is on the map you can explore it. But to get to that area, or go anywhere else, you can't. Like if one area of the map has a path and you want to get to the path near that. You see that nice small row of rocks between you and it? You can't jump over them. This gets annoying after a while as you can't take any shortcuts to get places unless they're designated with an icon to use Luffy's swinging or jumping. If it doesn't have an icon or designated, no shortcut.-Three, you can play as any of the characters, but they all have overworld skills, so as much as you want to play as Sanji or Nami or others, Luffy is still the one that can swing up or the only one to use CoO (why?) and grab things from afar so he's the most useful to play as. It kind of railroads you into relying on him the most.-Four, EXP. Despite letting you limit your team to 4 characters and choosing who they are. Everyone will still receive EXP even your reserve crew. So if you had any plans of say having Sanji lvl max and Zoro lvl 1 (lmao), you can't. It divides it out evenly for them and for some odd reason Usopp keeps up with Luffy and gains levels the fastest..Despite that, if you like One Piece, love the characters, and follow the manga religiously and want that 'extra adventure.' It's still great for story and and a One Piece game. Treat it like a fanfic that you can play and you'll enjoy it. Just don't put any faith in its 'open world,' label.

_childDocuments_.review: In short: Nice graphics, nice dub, terrible pacing.I love One Piece, I've been consuming One Piece media for decades and decided to buy this game even though its expensive.The graphics are amazing and the dub is really good, the gameplay is cool and they inovate as much as they can since its hard to make turn-based jrpgs unique. However, this game has a massive flaw a HUGE disappointment that cant be ignored: terrible pacing.As soon as you finish the first stage that feels like a tutorial, you will be surprised by how big the map is, however, due to pacing you have little to no freedom in exploring anything. There are SO MUCH cutscenes that even novel-like games has more gameplay time than this game.It works like this: walk to a point - cutscene - defeat the enemy - cutscene - walk foward for 15 seconds - cutscene - enter a new room - loading time - cutscene - walk foward a little bit - cutsceneThe game is always stopping, it cuts your adrenaline, it really ruins your experience, there is no way to avoid it, you have almost no freedom when it comes to cutscenes ruining your experience, somtimes you want to walk all to the right to open a chest that you found but the area that triggers the cutscenes are so big that you most likely will not be able to, you will have to watch the cutscene.There are some little flaws that even though arent a big deal by itself, they still annoy you a little, for example, Luffy is not able to walk on small walls or jump from a sidewalk that is slighty above from the street. Even though the map gives you a "open map rpg" feeling, the invisible walls are everywhere, its so weird to see Luffy ignoring a 3 meter ladder by jumping to the top directly and then being stuck by a invisible wall when you try to jump fences; if you're on the sidewalk and want to go back to the street, you cant jump fences you have to walk back from where you came, its really weird.I dont recommend this game due to its price.

_childDocuments_.review: One Piece Odyssey is a great game for One Piece fans and does all the right things when it comes to fan service—delivering some (not all) of the truly iconic moments in the franchise! I constantly found myself holding back tears when playing through these moments through the Memoria system (think KH in terms of delivery). The game knows its audience and was definitely able to expertly repackage treasured experiences to hit all the right notes of nostalgia. In that regard, I am grateful for this game.As a JRPG, it's very middle of the line. I did not see any groundbreaking gameplay mechanics that were present in titles of a similar price range. The combat does not pose much of a challenge overall as you progress the story, but there does exist a "challenge mode" in the post-game. This would have been better inserted earlier in the game to encourage accessory fusion and more critical thinking in terms of upgrades.The collectibles in the game are also weirdly designed. It's a bit of a pain in the butt that breakable containers respawn even if they no longer contain anything for you to collect. Some do respawn the loot but these instances are few and far between. Additionally, the majority of the collectible types (character skill cubes) lull you into believing that the conditions to collect them all (or most) are not too tight, however, you are soon hit with the realization that there is 1 class of collectibles that are super precise and can be a pain to backtrack to complete (yaya cubes). If you combine this mixed messaging with the respawning crate/vase issue, then it's mildly annoying to track what you've picked up. Not the biggest issue, but an issue nonetheless if you care about collectibles.The game has flaws but it is better looked at as a filler arc that draws some of its strongest content from existing canon arcs. It's a story experience with casual elements of combat and exploration. Buy it if you are a One Piece fan, but shop around first if you are new to JRPGs, One Piece, or have a limited budget.

_childDocuments_.review: Mekel Kasanova's TLDR Reviews If you are a fan of the One Piece series, enjoy classic RPGs, and are looking for a well-polished and colorful game, then One Piece Odyssey is definitely worth considering. The game offers a unique story that ties in with the 25th anniversary of the series, and it has a turn-based combat system that is reminiscent of classic RPGs like Final Fantasy and Dragon Quest. The game also features beautiful graphics, an engaging story, and well-designed gameplay. On the other hand, if you are not a fan of the One Piece series, prefer modern RPGs over classic turn-based style, or may find repetitive fights tedious, then One Piece Odyssey may not be the game for you. The game heavily relies on the series' lore and character development, and the combat system is mainly turn-based, so it may not appeal to players who prefer action-based or real-time combat. In One Piece Odyssey, the gameplay is divided into two main sections: overworld exploration and combat encounters. The overworld exploration allows players to control one of the crew members and explore the game's world, switching between characters as needed, each of them have their own unique abilities. For example, as the main protagonist, Luffy has the ability to stretch his limbs and body like rubber, which allows him to reach high places, and also has an ability called observation Haki which allows him to see hidden items within a limited range. Similarly, other characters have their own abilities such as Roronoa Zoro, the crew's first mate, who has great strength and can cut down iron doors and boxes that block the path, Nami, the navigator, has the ability to sense and find hidden piles of cash, and Usopp, the ship's sniper, can use his slingshot to shoot down containers that contain useful items.In addition to the characters previously mentioned, Sanji, the cook of the ship, can use his "Cook's Nose" to find fresh and rare ingredients for cooking. The crew's doctor, Tony Tony Chopper, not only can heal his allies in battle but also can use his small size to fit through narrow and low passages while exploring the overworld. Nico Robin, the archaeologist of the crew, can use her knowledge to uncover information about the game's world and story. Franky, the cyborg shipwright, can use gathered items to create bridges to previously inaccessible areas, giving the game a metroidvania-like feel. Brook, the skeletal musician, is not yet known to have a specific role in the overworld exploration but will not be joining the crew until he gets his body back. Unfortunately, Jinbe, a fan favorite, is not included in the game.As players explore the overworld, they may encounter enemies or creatures that they must fight. Upon touching the enemy, players will be transported to a battle stage where they can use turn-based combat to defeat the enemy, similar to classic RPGs such as Final Fantasy and Dragon Quest. The game uses a triangle strategy of weapons, similar to Fire Emblem games, where power beats speed, speed beats technique, and technique beats power. Therefore, it's important to use the right crew member for the right fight, and players can switch between characters during battle as needed.One Piece Odyssey is a well-crafted game that is full of charm, and it was made with love and guidance from the series creator, Eiichiro Oda. The game is perfect for both long-time fans of the series and for those looking for a new RPG experience. The characters are well-portrayed, the story is engaging, and the gameplay is well-designed. The overworld is filled with vibrant scenery, while the combat is fast-paced and balanced. The game is polished to a high level and the developer did a great job in terms of bug fixing, I didn't find any bugs or glitches during my gameplay. Overall, One Piece Odyssey is a game that I can see myself playing for a long time, it's a game that was made with a lot of love and attention to detail.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr - If you really like One Piece, there's a good chance you'll enjoy this.  If you don't, you probably won't!I've never enjoyed a game so much and also felt that I had to NOT recommend it like I do with this game.  It's full of problems: far too easy with no adjustable difficulty controls; combat that you'll quickly master and that never really varies from beginning to end; annoying pacing of cutscenes that involve you watching, then taking a couple of steps forward only for a NEW cutscene to play; a strangely designed series of maps that are either too small or too large; a fairly simple story with a lot of sections that feel barely sketched out etc.But the thing is... it is absolutely filled to the brim with all the charm, humour and yes even strong emotional beats that One Piece itself has.  If you really, really like One Piece, that familiarity and charm carries things a looooong way.  I thoroughly enjoyed playing this game from start to finish, getting every achievement, making sure I'd done everything there was to do in the game before finally setting it aside.  But make no mistake, I only bought this because it was One Piece, and if I didn't know anything about that story and those characters then I'd have likely found the game a confused and somewhat disappointing experience.Luckily for me, I do know about that story and those characters, so I didn't have a boring adventure!

_childDocuments_.review: So after about six hours I think I've played long enough to write a review, or at least enough to talk about my first impressions and experience. First off I can say that I'm having fun, granted this is a typical turn-based RPG, so if you really aren't into turn based combat you probably won't like it. It is quite similar to a Dragon Quest game with a One Piece skin, not that I find anything wrong with  that, I like Dragon Quest. When the game begins you'll have access to a lot of techniques, and you'll start out at a high level, of course the Strawhats lose their strength reverting them back to level one. The player has to journey to collect their "techniques" basically unlocking new techniques, or I suppose techniques they forgot? You'll also have to grind as well. The biggest complaint I've seen of the game is that frankly it's too simplistic and easy. I must admit that for the first few hours everything was pretty easy, also the game at the beginning gives you INSANE experience, you'll level up after every fight and be overpowered. I have noticed that once I got into Alabasta, the enemies got stronger and I wasn't really doing as much damage to enemies as before. I will say it's still not difficult, but you can at least notice the game gives you stronger enemies to fight. Some of the bounty fights were kind of tough for me, I know one bounty fight the enemies did really good damage to me, but I might have been underleveled to fight them. Each Strawhat has their own "field skills" which some are basically generic skills, but others let them do unique things, which is kind of neat. Luffy can use Observation Haki to detect hidden items, Nami can find bonus money, Sanji can find rare ingredients, Frank can build bridges across gaps to reach new areas, Luffy also can use Gum Gum Rocket on certain terrain to traverse to new areas as well. The game isn't really "open world" as much as you might think, at first you won't be able to really go explore, the game will force you to go to a certain area to progress the main story, and THEN at some point you'll get the chance to explore areas you couldn't, but that also means a lot of backtracking. Backtracking does suck and most RPG's do this, you'll get a quest, go to an area, go back to town, then go BACK to the area, etc. It's a lot of back and forth, and the game I believe has a fast travel system but I have yet to unlock it, and I'm not sure how it exactly works. It appears you can eventually just fast travel to areas, which would make it easier to get around instead of going everywhere on foot. The game has an equipment system, but it's basically just for these accessories you'll find, which can raise stats like HP, attack power, defense, etc. You can equip multiple accessories though by placing them in this puzzle-like space, and each accessory has different shapes. The game's "mana" system is called TP, or tension points. The neat thing is you can get a lot of TP every time you do a basic attack, so by managing your TP you can essentially just spam skills over and over again, it's not very hard to accumulate TP in battle, and it carries over from battle to battle as well. The game overall does feel "too easy" there is no difficult slider, but as I said, it does seem like as you progress the game will get harder, though by that point you might be overpowered or just never really encounter anything that feels like a challenge. I can't say much about the story as I'm not very far, I can't really say how expansive the world is, nor how many arcs the game covers and how many characters from the series we see make an appearance. I can imagine it'll be pretty diverse though, I know you go to Alabasta, Water Seven, Enies Lobby, etc. You'll see characters from those arcs, and I've also seen Smoker and Tashigi make a brief appearance. As for visuals, the game looks really good, at least in my opinion, and I'm having not technical issues. I get a smooth 90 FPS, but you can unlock the frame rate to whatever you want. I gotta say that one major negative thing I dislike is CUTSCENES ARE LOCKED TO 30 FPS, so that is a bit annoying, I don't know if there is a way to bump the cutscene frame rate up to 60 FPS, but from what I can tell all the cutscenes run in 30 FPS for some reason. All in all I wouldn't say this is a "bad" game or would I give it a negative rating, combat can be a bit lackluster but if you're not into turn based combat then I can understand that, but looking at everything else presented here it's still an enjoyable game, I'd say it's certainly better than World Seeker. There is plenty to do in the game as well, lots of side quests and content, so you'll have plenty to do if you want to 100% the game. I'm not sure how long it'd take to beat the game in general, but I know if you do the side stuff you'll get a lot more playtime out of the game.PS: For those that care about censorship or make a big deal about it, well you don't have to worry because from what I can tell they didn't censor anything in terms of Robin and Nami's physique or appearance. I know a lot of people won't support or buy a game if the girl's are "censored" so just putting that out there.

_childDocuments_.review: To make a long story short One Piece Odyssey is a good game, but rather basic which might not interest a lot of people.StoryThe main premise of the story is going back through previous adventures that the Straw Hat Pirates went through to regain their strength after having been stranded on the island of Waford. The stories are basically remixes of the originals, so some characters are put in places that they wouldn't typically be. Such as Robin helping to fight Crocodile in Alubarna as an example. As far as my thoughts on the story(s) it's fine but very basic. It doesn't really reach any sort of twists or turns that would floor a person, certainly not me anyways. Additionally I'm not a big fan of the fact that the story tries to make certain scenes from the main story work. Such as having Robin be a stand in for Viola, it just feels forced. Beyond that the story for the side quests are pretty alright, usually very silly affairs and a couple of heartwarming ones.The main overarching story is very by the numbers and you'll see right through most of it. The story at the end of the day is the typical "New character doesn't like the preexisting cast due to preconceptions only to later enjoy their company".GameplayNow getting to the most controversial part of the game. That being it's gameplay and how easy it is. I would not hesitate to say this is one of the absolute easiest JRPG's that I've ever played. It rarely ever asks anything of you beyond what any other JRPG would and although that's not bad per se it doesn't have anything that makes it so unique that it would move past that easy stigma. Most of the fights in the game can be won by just making a pure strength build. Outfit your characters with enough strength and you can beat some bosses in about 2 hits.Now even though I said that Strength is the only stat that really matters, it doesn't mean that there's no build diversity at all, there's quite a bunch! You could make builds that are all about dealing elemental damage, builds where you go heavy on hp. Builds that make you super tanky with high DEF and GUTS. Builds that allow you to dodge. Builds that allow you to self sustain yourself with both HP and TP. To add onto that you can even make fuse accessories together to further diversify your builds. And for that I have nothing but praise for the game on that front. But as said before you can just get by in the game by having enough attack to knock out enemies in fewer turns.Moving slightly away from the combat of the game and onto the exploration, it leaves me mixed. The game consistently rewards players for exploring everywhere. Treasure chests are scattered all around the world. Materials and even items can be found on the ground. Finding memory cubes that can boost the attack power of special moves. Quests are scattered all over the game as well along with short stories called "Hysterias". Along with some other goodies which is yet again another genuine praise that I'll give the game. That said actually exploring around isn't nearly as fun as the rewards you find. Mainly due to the fact that the game has really large levels and you only get to go two set speeds. Slow as molasses or a sprint that isn't really all that much faster. And although the game allows you to freely jump whenever you want it's seldomly used in anything beyond some slightly tall platforms.PresentationTo quickly go through this one. The game overall looks really great and has a nice art style to it. And the animations for special moves is great to see, feeling like they have a certain weight/heft to them every single time. That said outside of combat the game uses a ton of canned and reused animations which can be a bit distracting. Additionally the game doesn't have an English dub so you're stuck with the Japanese voice cast which does remove some amount of gravitas when it comes to certain scenes.OverallThe game is fun and a super cushy adventure the whole way through. And although it is a One Piece game I feel that even non One Piece fans can still get some enjoyment out of it. I certainly hope that Bandai Namco starts to make more turn based games with their anime ip's since I find them to be more interesting then just mashing the light attack button for the 1000th time

_childDocuments_.review: Im a huge One Piece fan, as well as a huge JRPG fan, and want to start by saying the One Piece aspect of the game does most of the heavy lifting for my enjoyment of the game. The game is riddled with One Piece fan-service which is honestly great, as I love the IP and the world, so a large scale JRPG following the tale of our Straw Hat crew late in their journey is a joy to play through, but the game overall falls short as just a JRPG. With the exception of the combat, the overworld exploration feels like a JRPG from 2007.If you're a huge fan of the One Piece IP, and don't completely hate JRPGs, the game is definitely worth playing, but I'll start with my negatives.- The game is extremely easy. Im about 40ish hours in, and in this whole time, not only have I not once gotten a game over, but I've only had a party member faint a maximum of 4-5 times during my playthrough. - Most items you get in the overworld are just crafting for either Usopp's ball items, or ingredients for Sanji to use in cooking, but you get so many meals just throughout your playthrough, cooking as a necessity is really a rarity. It's disheartening to discover a secret area, open a chest, and just have raw fish to cook with in it.- While the prospect of freely switching between the Straw Hat crew in the overworld in order to use their own strengths to collect specific items (Usopp can shoot down nests, Zoro can cut iron boxes and doors, Chopper can go into small spaces), it feels more tedious than inventive to have to switch characters just for a slight mechanic, just to always switch right back to Luffy because he's the easiest to collect overworld items with. Switching to Chopper to go through a tunnel, just to switch to Luffy after, to turn a corner and realize you need to switch to Zoro to cut an unnecessary Iron door gets tedious.- The combat, while inventive, feels like a chore fairly early into the game. The idea is fun and great for the first 15 or so hours, but until you get late game field wiping abilites, the combat can at times feel sluggish and time consuming considering an enemy will almost always attack right after your party member does. It's not a complete deal breaker, but combat does eventually hit a slump that will make you want to avoid combat encounters.- Cutscenes seem poorly placed. There are many many times where you'll hit a point, play a cutscene, walk 10 feet, play another cutscene, walk 30 feet, play another cutscene. The cutscenes are animated greatly and I'm more of a narrative game player than a gameplay game player, but it does feel jarring and completely kill momentum when you can see the objective in the distance, only to be stopped over and over again by multiple cutscenes which in most case, just state the obvious of what you're supposed to do.Now if you've made it this far, Im sure you're surprised that I had all these gripes but still have a positive review of the game, and the easy answer is because yes, I do absolutely love this game, despite its many problems. As stated, Im a huge One Piece fan, as well as a huge JRPG fan, and while this isn't at all the best JRPG I've played, it's definitely the best One Piece game I've played. It has a great original story written by Oda-san, as well as the whole japanese VA cast coming together to voice the whole game. If you're someone who digs JRPGs, and honestly just loves the whole One Piece IP, no matter how slow it gets at times, I completely recommend picking up One Piece Odyssey. Stepping foot in Alabasta and Water Seven really hits the point of nostalgia that shows you truly how far the Straw Hat Pirates have come. Earning your abilities back at the same time the crew learned them at specific arc points feels great and gives you something to look forward to as you enter the next chapter of the game. Overall, I would probably give this game a 7/10. It doesn't stand next to some of the best JRPG's ever made, but as a One Piece game, its by far the best and most enjoyable to experience, and another arc to journey through given to us by Oda-san will always be worth the time.

_childDocuments_.review: An awesome traditional JRPG experience in the One Piece world.This game is a must have for One Piece fans. From having the cast doing the voice work, to the great writing, to the art style... it's everything you'd expect from One Piece.The JRPG mechanics are solid. Classic turn based combat system, with some nice depth to it. There are "zones" in combat, where your characters and the enemies can be split up between. Characters can melee people in their zone, or use ranged attacks against distant ones. If there's no one in your zone, you're able to jump into any other with a close range attack.It also uses a rock, paper, scissors approach, where characters are either power, skill or technical, each one being strong against one and weak to another. Makes you focus specific characters against specific enemies. Attacking enemies also builds up your TP, which is used to use your special attacks. So do some basic attacks and build up TP to use big finishers. TP also stays between battles, so you can build it up on weak enemies and save it for bosses.There will be little tasks in some battles, like having a buffed up enemy to kill before they take out one of your crew. Or to kill an enemy with a specific party member. All of these will offer extra XP, and sometimes bonus items and money.The game has a McGuffin that makes the crew lose their powers at the start, and as you progress you slowly regain more and more abilities. You also get pickups that let you strengthen various moves.There's a puzzle grid equipment system, where you can equip items that boost various stats (these can be enhanced). They will take up various amounts of space on the grid (so a 1x2, 2x2, 1x4, etc). You can equip whatever you can fit onto your character's grid. Giving you a lot of freedom on just how you want to buff up your characters. Focus on attack or defense or cheaper special moves, etc...The world itself is quite large. There's various hubs you travel between, from the starting island, to various main arc locations in each chapter, like Alabasta, Water 7, Marineford, etc... Each has lots of things to explore. Secret items, chests, powerups, etc... As well as your standard sub quests and a bounty system where you track down targets for money. Every location is wonderfully recreated from the show.If you're a One Piece fan, this is a must have. For those who play lots of JRPG's, this will feel a lot more like Dragon Quest over Final Fantasy. It's more "traditional" in style. Which is awesome.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is strange.It's definitely deviated from how typical One Piece games are with a RPG system; when you'd expect them to have something definitely more flashy and action packed. Whilst this game offers beautifully sculpted models and good locations.. it doesn't offer much else in terms of story and gameplay.The story becomes quite predictable when you've seen your fair share of One Piece movies and have read a couple of arcs. (Chapter 1072 at the time of writing.) Me and a friend I streamed it to even predicted some story beats as well as the dialogue the main villain of the story would say, and he did say those things. On the topic of story, you return to previous arcs (Alabasta, Water 7, Marineford and Dressrosa) and not much has changed besides one or two elements. The gameplay is fine. The special attacks are beautifully animated and are very faithful to the source material; however It becomes a chore to constantly switch out characters in order to fit the type advantage, and whilst it is good to not have the member switch cost a turn, it becomes bothersome to have to switch out party members constantly.On the topic of characters, Franky and Brook do not get to do much and not to mention that this game takes place before Wano, so Jimbei isn't in this game. Franky becomes playable halfway through the game and Brook only becomes playable in the final few chapters. While Franky is very powerful and his abilities are more focused on crowd control; Brook is very underpowered and even his animations feel lacking.  His most iconic move, the Hanauta Sancho: Yahazu Giri, is reduced to just a simple slash.Furthermore, to switch out the leader when out of battle seems aimless. Why give me the option to play as the other Straw Hats when majority of the time I'll be playing as Luffy to use the Gum-Gum Rocket to get around places, only to then switch to Zoro to cut down one iron door, and to switch back to Luffy again. Even more so, you cannot play as Franky or Brook in the open-world segments, which is highly disappointing.Despite the criticisms and harsh words I've given the game, I personally think that this game is just OK; the gameplay can become mindless when you learn you can break the game by just equipping characters with a lot of ATK+ accessories. Seeing the characters interact and talk about their past adventures is also fun; especially with Usopp and the Going Merry during the Memoria trip to Alabasta.For this game, if you're a One Piece fan and like JRPGS, you should play it but definitely wait for the price to drop. It is not worth the £60 price tag.6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite what people say about turn based style or difficulty, this is a very solid One Piece game and a decent JRPG.Do not be put off by the first chapter. The first chapter is essentially a tutorial, all of the enemies are extremely easy and you level up quite fast to introduce you to the combat, bonus EXP mechanics and the like. In similar JRPG fashion, the game gets a lot more difficult after Chapter 1, and beyond chapter 2 the combat and character building starts to get a lot more lush with the introduction of the crafting system.The party member rotation mechanic mixed with the Rock-Paper-Scissors weakness and field quadrant systems makes combat smooth and fun. Each character has their niches and uses without any Straw Hat being lackluster.My main complaints with the game are minor to me, but could be major to some. I wasn't a fan of the needless backtracking in the main story and lack of fulfilling sidequests and NPC interactions. The movement speed for sprint is also far too slow for a game with maps this large.Side quests themselves are typically fetch quests, bounty hunts, or backtracking related, and rewards aren't incredible. Admittedly I skipped most of them after the beginning so they likely get better, at least in the reward department.NPC dialogue is usually pretty bland but there are a few references and easter eggs super fans will like. The main story itself is really good, akin to the quality of a One Piece Movie in my opinion. Seeing how the crew interacts in situations theyve never been in (like the entire crew being with Luffy for Marineford and the half of the crew that was absent being present for Dressrosa, Etc), and getting to relive each arc with twists and alterations to canon is interesting. It's a nice deviation from the standard formula of just making the manga/anime's story into a game directly.Overall a 7/10 game, coming from a major One Piece fan. The game is worth playing to dip your toes into the One Piece universe and to get loosely acquainted with a few of its main story beats, and great for super fans like myself to have a nice 40 hour experience within the series.

I believe the overall story is solid so far and fits the theme of the show and the characters are all voiced correctly, are accurate to the show in their mannerisms, and the gameplay is solid as a turn-based RPG. _childDocuments_.review: The storyline of One Piece Odyssey revolves mainly around revisiting past memories, which is an interesting concept, but it is executed somewhat lacklusterly in terms of content. Players are thrown into the climax of the story arc, with previous events quickly summarized in cutscenes. The introduction of two new characters feels too brief. Overall, it's satisfactory for One Piece fans to play through once.The game features a turn-based battle system within confined zones, where your crew is separated at the start of combat, adding dynamism to battles. However, this novelty wears off after a few hours when your characters become overwhelmingly powerful, rendering battles too easy. The addition of an auto-battle feature feels unnecessary, and the lack of difficulty settings diminishes the challenge, making item usage during fights pointless.Exploration suffers from sluggish camera and movement speeds, discouraging thorough exploration. The world lacks enticing loot, with equipment limited to stat-boosting stones easily acquired through battle rewards or shops.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface by saying that I TRULY wanted to enjoy this game. I am a HUGE One Piece fan, and was extremely excited when I heard about this game being made. However, I was only able to slug through the first 2-3 hours before deciding to shelf the game for good. PROS---------- The graphics are easily the best looking you can get without going into realism, and the uncanny valley. I genuinely think that all One Piece games going forward should look like this, as every character and location was beautifully done in such a respectful way to the source material.- The story and dialogue are great, and I think this game truly shines in this department, however as I will cover in the Cons, this game is an experience best suited for a Youtube video with all the combat parts removed.CONS-------- The combat is a MAJOR part of the game and it is easily the biggest flaw. The combat is extremely boring, and the "Rock, Paper, Scissors" aspect of combat is extremely unengaging. I never felt like I couldn't use a "Paper" attack or ability on a "Scissors" enemy. There is no feeling of danger or urgency in any of the fights, and I never once sensed any outcome that resulted in me failing any combat encounter. - The beautiful locations you are able to "explore" are amazing, and I truly did enjoy exploring them. However, this game is horribly plagued with forced backtracking that is completely alienated from the story, and serves nothing but to halt progression for the means of inflating playtime. Having to run for 5-10 minutes just to pick up one item, and then another 5-10 minutes to return is insanely boring, and ruins the pacing and enjoyment for me. This repetitive backtracking is what ultimately made me quit the game. OVERALL:------------Overall, I would not reccomend this game unless you could get it for under $10-$15 dollars, and even then that might be too much. I appreciate the effort from Oda, and the developers. However, the combat and horrible progression and pacing make this game unbearable to slog through. Even the most dedicated One Piece fans like myself might have trouble finding enjoyment beyond the surface level when it comes to One Piece: Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: First of all: I'm a HUUUGE One Piece Fan. I watch every new Episode each Sunday, I already have played some other One Piece games and I just love it.BUT: This game seen as a game is just not good in my opinion. I pre-ordered it in like October or November 2022 and was hyped as hell. I barely spoiled myself with any kind of footage or something. I just wanted the whole new experience. I read something like "open world", "round based" and which parts of the OP story you participate in.I don't say, the story, animiations or whatsoever are bad, but the gameplay and the gameplay-mechanics: The combats are suuuper easy - like the enemies deal 50 damage while having like 2.000 HP - except for when there is one special event fight with one buffed standard enemy (one of those 50 damage dealers), who suddenly deals like 1.600 damage! Like... what the f*** is this?! Only these two extremes do exist and it's just way too unconsistent. Apropos special event fights: When normal fights give like 1.000-2.000 Exp, some special events additionally give like 12.000 Exp! Meanwhile some (Mini-)Bosses also give like 10.000 Exp at maximum. Also you can just freely swap characters in combat (except in special event fights sometimes), so you can position them best possible always. Even the characters, who already are in combat. Like what is all that combat-zone system about, when you can just swap them like your underwear?!Another annoying thing for me is the "exploring" of the "open world". Yeah, there are some sideways with loot and sometimes even chests in there, but... all of that is just ♥♥♥♥! Some stupid cooking material or I don't know. Often the chests contain worse stuff then the loot just chilling and blinking on the floor. It just doesn't feel good finding and opening chests. It's just "ah, another soup" or "ah, some other ingredients for some healing/buffing stuff" always.Then there are the skills, attacks and stuff: Yeah, they look pretty cool and nice and there is a lot of them, but... just why? I don't know, why all of zoros (single target-melee-)attacks do the same stuff, except for the damage numbers. I mean yeah of course they have different costs to activate, but... sometimes they're just too similar, even in numbers. Also why do some characters have like 15 attacks, when others have like 5? And the upgrade-cubes: Some characters (preferably those with more attacks) can upgrade more than the others. And the finding-rate of these cubes seems totally random and disproportionate. I believe, I got like 3 of zoros Skills upgraded before the first of Nami or Robin. Just why? Btw: This upgrade system just sucks in my opinion. Finding stuff to upgrade a limited amount of attacks just in numbers. To be fair: The thing with the stat-equpiment-items is kinda cool.**Spoiler-Alert**: The enemies are just super boring and repetetive. In the first real chapter (Alabasta) I hoped to fight against the Baroque-Agents (Mr. 1, Mr. 2...) and their companions, but the only fight like this was with Mr. 2... It was just so disappointing.I played some other One Piece games like Unlimited Adventure and Unlimited Cruise 1 + 2 (all on Wii) and I loved them. They were sooo great. You were able to individually train, buff and level your characters - instead of having no choice which to have in your party and level automatically. The combats were not round-based (not a bad thing per se) and action-loaded. You were rewarded doing combos in combat so you were not spamming the best attack or something like this. You were rewarded exploring and collecting stuff. My thoughts drifted away to those games while playing One Piece Odyssey and I wondered, why I play this and not these games. I really love One Piece, but this game is just so f****** boring. I'm really sorry to say that and I'm also really sorry paying 80,- € for this game (Pre-Order-Stuff).**Spoiler-Alert**: I'm currently at Enies Lobby in the Prison-Area while texting this and I think, I won't continue playing, because this game is just not worth my time... :(

_childDocuments_.review: The game is nice and runs well on PC, if you're a fan of One Piece you will most likely enjoy it (as long as you don't mind JRPGs and turn-based combat).Having just finished the first chapter, these are the complaints I have:Vsync doesn't seem to work, even though it's enabled I still see screen tearing from time to timeThe main cutscenes are prerendered and capped at 30 fps. This also means that if you change the outfits of the characters this won't be reflected in the cutscenesFor now, the game is extremely easy, to the point where I have been one-shotting enemies consistently (the upside of this is that all characters - even those not fighting - get the EXP and levelling seems relatively fast; I don't expect much grinding will be needed to complete the game, if any)Traversal is a bit too slow for my liking, but there does seem to be some fast travel mechanism which I have not unlocked yetOverall, I would recommend this to OP fans and JRPG fans alike, although I'd warn you that the game will spoil plenty of One Piece lore (Given the bounties that can be seen in the save screen, the game seems to be set between Whole Cake Island and Wano, so around episode ~900 of the anime and also chapter ~900 of the manga). If you're not interested in either this is most likely a game you can skip, as it doesn't seem to have any groundbreaking gameplay or storytelling (for now).

Stuff like "Kill the buffed enemy before a crewmate gets knocked out". Completing these challenges gives you extra exp, like a LOT of extra exp. Multiples of what you would normally get. The issue is that leveling up is really really slow without these challenges, so if you're unlucky it can be difficult to get levels. My other issue is that the game is a bit too easy. I can one shot most basic enemies when I have the type advantage, and sometimes even when I don't. I am still in the early game so maybe that's why. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: The game fails in two main categories, storyline and combat. Copy & Paste destroyed what could have been a great game.The problem with the storyline: it is boring and highly repetitive. Kill one elemental, travel one memory world, do that 3x, some final encounters, The End. Everything is predictable after the first 5 hours. Character development is non-existent; every character starts in the usual "happy leader", "grumpy", "slutty", "lone samurai", etc. clichés and does not move an inch until the credits roll.The problem with combat is that it offends the intelligence of even an 8-year-old child. As a result, there is hardly any motivation to use anything but the most potent available attack.As of today (game version 1.0.0), there is NO setting for any difficulty level. Therefore, everybody is forced to play on what can only be described as "super-easy / story" mode.Stats-boosting food is available in abundance, and should your resources run out, one of the overpowered meals corrects this problem immediately (for all party members) in one action and then repeat the same until any fight is won. Also, there is an endless recycling of enemies and bosses, with almost no new models in later stages of the game, up to the degree that would make even Square "colour swap" Enix jealous.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a One Piece fan, you will likely enjoy this game quite a bit. It has all of the charm of the One Piece universe wrapped up into a neat little JRPG bow. That said, I have played better JRPGs than this before, but I've also played WAYYYYY worse. This game is more than passable, especially if you're invested in this franchise. The writers have managed to maintain the lovable personalities of the beloved Strawhat crew & friends, and even bring back a lot of old jokes and characters that were surprising and welcome to see. (Kung-Fu Dugongs were a large standout)   The combat is a bit too easy on average, but there are a few boss fights throughout that will require a bit more forethought than many of the minion battles. The moves the crew has access to are a delight to use, however. The animations are crisp and it's always a blast to see Usopp's Rubber Band of Doom and to see Nico Robin squish somebody's nuts. The dual zones allow for a tiny bit of additional strategy that helps to spice up battles just enough to keep them interesting. Overall, you can see the inspiration from some of the more successful JRPGs of our era and that's definitely a good thing in this instance.   The story is actually decently interesting and most of the jokes land pretty well. Of course this is all under the assumption that you're already a fan of One Piece. But if you are, I'd argue that this title is a must-have for you. Especially if it ever goes on sale. Give it a shot!

_childDocuments_.review: I liked One Piece: Worldseeker, but this game blows it out of the water. The only thing I miss is using Gum-Gum Rocket as a means of travel, but in a JRPG where random encounters are an expected and necessary mechanic, it makes perfect sense to remove that.
