_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this is what Pokémon, Digimon and all those other Monster battlers should have evolved into. I've bought this game on sale out of boredom and been spending every free minute playing it since.It is that good.On the surface it's what you expect, you run around, get to collect monsters and battle with them.But it is also so much more; every creature has an ability you can use outside of battle and most of them are important to find secrets or progress in general. Those are the metroidvania elements mentioned everywhere. That's a nice touch, but for me, the game was always about the battles and building a team of creatures I liked.Adding new monsters to your team is always possible (and encouraged), as they'll only be two levels behind your highest monster when you get them. You can even get every single bossmonster you'll fight over the course of the game, some of which are simply badass.The difficulty I found very fair, it's not as easy as newer (or older, really) Pokémon generations by any means, but it's never hard just for the sake of it.If you lose a battle, it's usually easily solved by changing your strategy a bit or adding one monster. You will need team synergy; meaning someone who can heal, someone who can buff and/or tank etc. That's no big deal though, as every monster can be viable.Customisation is very deep as well, a big skilltree for EVERY SINGLE monster. Most can be used in lots of different ways to fill holes in your strategy. If you learn the battle system and build a balanced team, you'll never run into any issues. The postgame gets a bit more tactical, but by then you have enough monsters and experience to build a team for whatever you wanna beat.The story and characters are very basic, but the gameplay and overall battle system make up for it. That's what the game is about and there is a lot here if you like turn based combat. Having seen the trend with other games of the genre, it's a travesty this game is only 20 bucks, when you have to pay triple that to play a vastly inferior Pokémon game. No brainer to pick up on a sale, even full price I'd buy it again in a heartbeat.It truly is the best game of its genre.Oh, and there is FREE dlc coming out for this in 2022, making me very hopeful for more future content and/or a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: If you like turn based RPGs that are in the vein of Pokemon and want just a dash of Metroidvania elements, this will scratch both of those itches. Tons of monsters to catch, each with 3-4 skill trees with each monster having multiple niches that they can fill so no one monster has to do one thing and allows for a lot of variety in play style. For the Metroidvania elements, they're pretty bare bones. Puzzles aren't insanely hard, the areas aren't insanely difficult to traverse, but it is a refreshing take versus the generic top down view and I enjoyed those elements for what they were. Nothing groundbreaking, but not bad in execution by any means.I've seen in the comments a lot of people taking issue with the team building/strategies that they feel are forced on the player as you get through the game, specifically debuff teams. For probably the first 3-5 hours you can get away with not putting a ton of thought into team building, but the farther along you get into the game the more important the synergy between your monsters becomes. The easy thing to do is build debuff teams or ensure you always have someone that can remove debuffs, but again with the variety in each of the monsters the game will allow you to not be forced into debuff teams if you teambuild properly, but it becomes much harder to do so the farther you get along and it will be harder to do without hunting for certain pieces of equipment. It may feel like that debuff play style is being forced on the player, but I did not feel that way until almost the very end of the game and by then I had the means to put in the extra bit of legwork to build a team that didn't rely on debuffs.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has dabbled in a lot of monster raising and metroidvania games, I'll be up front and say this is really the ideal you could get when you cross the two. It's really similar to something like Dragon Quest Monsters, where you're more focused on 3 monster synergies vs each monster in a vacuum. The game starts out simple enough, you'll be introduced to very simple compositions and the game does a good job of leading you through new mechanics, new buffs/debuffs, and you naturally get a feel for what a good team should be as you navigate small chunks of dungeon and do puzzles here and there. As other reviews have noted, yes, the game does hit a significant difficulty spike near the end. For me personally, I had two spikes: one where my team was suddenly fully weak to all the monsters in the new area and underleveled, and one of the scripted fights near the end. The former was simply resolved by reconfiguring my team with more appropriate monsters and exploring to find some new ones, the latter by using a mechanic that I really didn't take advantage of because the AI's type of team wasn't really used until the end.From a monster raising game perspective, it's terrific, if you're in it only for that, you'll love it.(If the following complaints are actually options, I didn't see them in my time, which likely means they just need to be made more obvious in the UI)The metroidvania part is where things get a bit meh for me:The first thing is that you rely on monsters to get from point A to point B, the only base skill you really get is a double jump after a while. This is fine, and it requires really finding new monsters, but the thing is that it's hard to tell what monsters do what until you hatch them (which - keep in mind - all eggs are rare drops so you need to win fights well to have a chance at them), or really what's even available. An example of this is that there are small paths that your character can't go through, should you be looking for a transformation item? Should you be expecting a monster to carry the ability? And there are plenty of these tunnels scattered through the game - there's one in the first area. Just knowing what to expect would be nice, an example could be having a list of all the traversal skills in the game and then when you encounter the monster with it, you add that monster to that section, or something of the like to know what you need to hunt and what's functionally optional.My next point, and this is likely my biggest frustration (relatively speaking, it's rather minor in the grand scheme), there's no way to note these skill specific areas on the map, or any. So you go through the first area, go "yeah i need to jump higher, fly longer, etc" and keep going only to continue the game for 8 hours until you get the skill you need, forgetting the chest 3 areas back. The game really encourages a ton of exploration and re-exploration, but it can shoot itself in the foot by not showing what's where. You constantly get new skills even through the end of the game which means that every time you take a break to go re-explore an area, you're going to go in an incomplete / non-explored room, go "oh yeah I can't do anything about this" and leave, which can get a bit tiring after 20 or so hours and doing that multiple times because it's not realistic to memorize the whole map.Overall, the game really feels like a love letter to 3v3 monster games, and metroidvanias alike, and I love it for that. There is some QOL stuff that would elevate it for me, but that might just be me. It's definitely a great game and worth the time investment, so I'd recommend it highly.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh man, this game is so addicting!  At first I thought it was going to be kinda boring...the starter area is stupid easy.  Never used any healing or items.  But the difficulty ramps up fairly fast and the battles are rather enjoyable after that.  And it's just so much fun trying to collect all of the monsters to see what they do!I think my biggest complaint is the lack of unique abilities.  I haven't counted, but there are only about 50 or so abilities, including all of the attacks, passives, buffs, debuffs, etc.  That may sound like a lot, but ~3 hours into the game all I'm running across are monsters that just have a different combination of the same abilities my other monsters already have.    So it's just a matter of finding the 6 monsters that have the right combination of those abilities and you have all of your bases covered.  This is by no means bad enough to make me downvote the game, but it gets a bit boring as far as customization goes after a while.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not used to playing Metroidvania games. In fact, I tend to avoid platformers. But their idea of one that also has pokemon-like elements had me interested. And when they said they were going to be Linux compatible, I was intrigued, so I purchased the game.I was surprised at how many quality of life features they had. Large skill trees for each monster would have you want to try different builds, and the 'skill reset' item is fairly easy to get quite a few of. You don't have to go to a location to swap things in your team, you have them all with you (and if you don't like that, there's a place where you can stick them later). Got extras? Donate them and get rewards.The platforming itself is fairly easy, and though I fail some some jumps quite a bit, there's no lives system, and you restart at the beginning of the jump, so no worries about having to backtrack or reload to try again.I haven't fully finished the main storyline yet (need to catch them all) so I can't attest to that, but it doesn't seem bad so far. I'm not entirely gripped by it, but it hasn't thrown any super tired cliches at me either, which is nice.The artstyle is very good for the feel of the game, and the fact that creatures animate even when idle is a nice touch. So many games just decide to stretch or wobble the sprites, so it's nice to see the effort put in.The fact t hat there's several different paths to building a team, so you can play in a style YOU like vs just what is 'best' is also really nice. I mean, if you're going for certain goals, some monsters will be better then others, but there's still a few options.All in all, it's a very cute, very well put together game, and one I'd highly recommend, especially if you want to support smaller dev groups.

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Sanctuary contains a blend of pokemon, metroidvania, and JRPG elements; around 18 hours to beat, I'm guessing at least 10 more to 100%, although I'm not sure if I'll do that. Overall I'd score this game on the upper side of mid; it'd be better on handheld (although I don't know if steam deck is supported); I'd get it on sale for at least 50% off. The story is the tried and true 'evil darkness hidden for ages reappears to threaten our heroes and destroy the world.' The writing is very bland and if you're a fan of story in your games, this is not one for you. The metroidvania/pokemon elements are interesting, there're 2 non-monster powerups that you get fairly early on in the game, and then most of the other elements are tied to your monster's non-combat abilities. I'm enjoying that, although I really hate that getting the right egg is largely RNG. The latter part of the game was already starting to feel grindy, and having to grind extra to finish unlocking the abilities I needed to complete the platforming puzzles was frustrating. Overall I still enjoyed the game, it has a few unique points to it, and if you like creature collectors this is a decent option.

_childDocuments_.review: A smart and well-constructed mashup of two great genres. If you like exploration, turn based rpg combat, or deep levels of party customization, this game is absolutely worth playing.The world is heavily interconnected and fun to poke around. Your monsters provide most of the upgrades that allow you to access new areas, which allows you the opportunity for some light sequence breaking if you explore thoroughly. The visual tells for obstacles and hidden areas are generally pretty clear, so you can tell quickly whether or not you possess the correct ability to reach any given area. In the recent major patch, they also added a nice custom map marker system to help you keep track of which places you might want to revisit in the future. Alongside this, the game also provides a handy menu option that points you to your next main objective in case you get lost.The combat is easy to grasp but incredibly deep. You start off with very simple direct actions, and slowly throughout the game you unlock more actions and passive traits that create synergies between your monsters. By the end of the game, each of your actions is triggering multiple buffs, debuffs, heals, or extra attacks, which is incredibly satisfying to see play out. The UI is very well built to convey a lot of information that helps you predict the effectiveness of your actions so you don't get overwhelmed. The game also offers several optional challenges to really push your understanding of the system to its limits. My one personal grip with the combat is the battle scoring system, which tends to emphasize certain strategies over others.Monster customization is also very detailed. Each monster has its own skill tree, one of two major passive buffs, equipment, and even food. All of this allows you to very thoroughly control what a monster is good at. Though a lot of the skills are shared across multiple monsters, each monster's base stats and skill tree are unique, giving each of them a clear identity. To help encourage experimentation, the game provides a few ways to boost the level of your monsters to match your highest-level monster, which eliminates the tedious grinding you tend to experience in these kinds of games. It also lets you save and load multiple team setups so you can switch back and forth easily. The one major drawback here is that it can be fairly time consuming to look through the monster skill trees and equipment lists to figure out what things go well together.The game has solid art and character design. The monsters, which are mostly drawn from folklore, fantasy literature, and other games, have a great deal of charm and variety. The background art and music both do a solid job of conveying each region's atmosphere. The writing isn't the most sophisticated, but the main story is competently told, and the background world building (found mostly in the monster log) is pretty interesting.Overall, I found the game extremely enjoyable, and it is one of the few games I've chosen to 100%.

_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Like Metroidvania games? Like Pokemon? Wanna relive the feeling from the old Dragon Warrior Monster games?Seriously, imagine sitting with an SNES controller in one hand playing Super Metroid and a Gameboy in the other collecting monsters... And that's the game you get. I know this is only Early Access, but I'm SO excited for the full release of this game. The developers have created something here that I can pick up and enjoy without struggling or devoting a huge chunk of my life to.And just a small thing of note... When you start the game, it just... starts up so quickly. From the time you click the icon to the time you're playing the game, it's just so fast. Warping from one warp point to the next? Nearly continuous gameplay. This game has virtually no load times. Start the battle without a bunch of fanfare. Fight on the stage you were in in the first place. Finish and the battle is over, no reloading. Ready to call it quits for the night? Save and quit damn near instantly. I haven't seen a game run this smoothly EVER. _childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: For an early access title this game definitely shows potential and is already playable for a good while (at least for me). The core mechanics are simple enough to understand and the gameplay feels smooth. It can be a little frustrating in the exploration when you see something you can't currently reach or unlock because you don't have the required abilities and can make it a little frustrating when you must backtrack to get things.The combat is pretty decent overall, with lots of depth for each monster with its own skill trees and suck like. The rating system caters to both a very offensive playstyle and a more cunning playstyle - although currently it rewards winning in very few turns and having lots of health at the end of your turns. As a result of this, closer and more difficult battles are made to seem unrewarding while complete landslides are praised, which can be pretty demotivating at times.There are lots of items you can use with your monsters for a variety of purposes. Up to three pieces of equipment can be equipped for each monster and they can all also hold a weapon. There are skill resetters, potions, revival items, escape items that add lots of options both in and out of battle. I do like the inventory system in its way, but it is a little difficult to find what you are looking for at times since it all goes into a single category and you have to navigate it to find which item you want - maybe a sorting feature in the future could help this but right now it's a bit clunky to use.The trainer battles in their current state, however, seem quite unfair to me. For one, all your healing, shield and damage effects are halved which can significantly change how well your team performs. In addition to this, if you go first (which is the case in all npc battles in the game as of writing this) you only get to use two monsters in your first turn as a 'balance' - something which became a huge issue in the sun palace fight because barriers aren't that effective and 3 aoe attacks can wipe out one or more of your monsters with ease. Overall I would recommend it - it's very fun and they've got a lot of things right - but at the same time there are definitely some improvements that could be made.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Monsters you obtain have abilities that you can use out of combat to explore more easily and unlock new areas that you previously couldn't reach, often unlocking extra monsters and rare equipment pieces (which you can still acquire otherwise, so don't stress about missing a couple of items).The game's got fun platforming, nothing unfair or crazy, there are some timed sections that can be frustrating, but use the tools you have available and you will prevail. The creatures are cute and the skill trees of each one allow for a great degree of customisation for your team's strategy. There are 111 creatures to collect and they can all be used to support more than one play style, so, use whatever you think is more fun and enjoyable!The story is alright, nothing amazing, but pretty solid. If I have one complaint, that would be the ending. It felt extremely lacklustre. The final boss was a little too easy, I think. Or maybe I just happened to have a good party composition for it, I don't know.The music and pixel art in this game are pretty damn good. Kudos to the artists behind both.If you are a fan of platformers and creature collectors and/or like team building rpgs with interesting skill choices, I think you will like this one. It also scratches that completionist's itch you might be suffering from. Getting 100% in the game will take you a decent amount of time, probably over 40 hours, unless you look up spoilers.Definitely buy on sale, or even full price. It's a good game that offers good replayability value.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: A strange case.This is a really good monster catcher. Incredibly in-depth with skilltrees for each mon that, while repetitive, allow you to build your team with far more diversity than most games of the genre.This is also a somewhat basic metroidvania.The two genres are not used in a way that compliment each other, and that's a real damn shame. This could have been more than just a "really good game that is also a metroidvania for some reason". It's certainly not enough to ruin the game, I just can't help but wonder what it would have been like if it'd gone in a different direction.Still, I can't help but sing this game's praises. I want to repeat this for those in the back: this is a REALLY GOOD MONSTER CATCHER. The metroidvania elements are just there to frame progression locks in a way that just feels like it was tacked on there.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely *loved* it.Really well-made and polishedThere is tons of freedom in the game, and unlike some other monster-keeping games (namely ones with "pocket monsters"), there really isn't a single monster that is useless, as far as I could see.Which means there's an exorbitant amount of combinations for teams that you can make.I just finished the game, and I'll definitely be playing this again in the future with different setups.Hoping for a New Game+ option that would make that even more interesting (non-existent as of December 2020).But even for a single playthrough, it's really good.Definitely recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Not gonna lie, as a fedora wearing neckbeard, the musketeer hats on the characters are the only reason I considered getting this game at first. Did you know that hatching a chicken and then forcing it to fight other chickens is both illegal and immoral? Monster Sanctuary takes place in a world where that is a legal and a respectable way of living, only that instead of chickens it’s mouthless, bipedal, one-eyed beast that sets things on fire with its mind.Monster Sanctuary feels like a grown up Pokemon. Specially now that Pokemon has become so bloated and un-innovative. This is one of my favorite games. Saved me when I was in a huge depression after finding out my wife had a new boyfriend. Pokémon was like that for my wife & I once. We’ve been through the most horrific amount of stress/depression/anxiety in this last couple of years. Life has been unbearable. Monster Sanctuary was a ray of light and such a wonderful distraction. I honestly don’t know where we’d be without it. It's absolutely perfect for disenfranchised Pokemon fans like myself. It scratches the same itch as a monster trainer, but with an unbelievable amount of thought and care put into it by the developers. Tying the typical metroidvania upgrades to the monsters you catch is such a natural fit I can't believe it hasn't been done before. The strategy is a perfect balance of being easy enough for casual players, but having an insane cap for anyone who wants to minmax.It's not often you find a game that is SO good with such little fanfare. Monster Sanctuary is close to one of my favourite games of the genre, it's a fun mix of Metroidvania-style platforming and monster collecting and battling like Pokemon. But calling it Pokemon-like its unfair. The combat is nuanced and framed around team building. In three-on-three battles, particularly towards the end game, you frankly will not win without thinking about your tactics and your team. And there's not one tactic that is objectively better than the other, whether you like to buff, debuff, stack, brute force, shut down teams with defense, there are so many options to succeed and it depends on your playthrough.Perhaps my favourite aspect of Monster Sanctuary is that every monster in the game is viable. Even the Monsters you pick up in the first area can take you through to the end of the game. It's all about how you use their unique set of skills to your advantage.The game is challenging, particularly the end game and post-game, but you can adjust the difficulty settings depending on how you like to enjoy games. I cannot recommend this game more highly. The devs are all lovely and very active in the community. Selfishly, I want this game to become wildly popular so that we get a sequel in the future, but also because I think anyone who picks this really well balanced game up will enjoy it, particularly Pokemon fans, RPG fans, Metroidvania fans, and more. If this game sounds remotely interesting to you, buy it. It's one of the best value games for it's price.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Sanctuary is a pixel art platform-monstertaming-rpg that may seems similar to Pokémon at first sight, but has very few in common in the end. The game start with you being a Monster Sanctuary guardian from a guardians' family and you'll get the starter from your father. So this is how a great story begin. You're gonna catch a lot of different monsters and combat a lot of them. What make Monster Sanctuary unique Is the usage of your monsters' ability outside of the combact: some of them will let you fly, others will let you swim, see in the dark, remove big rocks, jump higher, you can even ride them. It's not like Pokémon HM cause here you'll have to do the platform parts on your own using monsters'ability.-Monster Sanctuary has a good story. Not awesome, but at least good. -you Will carry all of your monsters with you, not only 6-monsters have a Skill tree. Every time they level up, you're going to pick up a Skill from there. So same monster can have totally different skill trees.-Monsters have weapons and other equipments. You will have to buy or gather resources to improve them-Monsters can eat food that increase their stats. The last 3 foods they eat are the only that matter-Monsters have more than 4 moves and they don't have to forget moves to learn others. Moves have levels and need mana to be cast-The combat is always 3vs3 and is actually very strategical. There are various types with their strength and weakness and a lot of conditions. -there Is no thing like Pokeball: there is a combat valutation instead. If you win a fight against Monster in few time, using lesser moves and causing high damages, you'll have an higher rate in the final valutation of the fight. A 100% means you'll going to find rare items. You can find eggs of monsters after the combat and it's how you obtain them. --combat system Is very good-nice pixel art-nice music-nice variety of maps and byomes-challenging -a lot of updates even in 2022-great monsters-gather resources and crafting feels satisfying, wish I had it in Pokémon-There are few evolutions. A solid 8.5/10 to me. Follow for more reviews

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sure that there are plenty who will be happy with this game, but I'm not. I think the best way to summarize why I don't like it is that I felt like my time was being wasted by the  system which gives you more or less loot depending on how well you do in an encounter. All of my annoyances boil down to the fact I don't get to see all the game unless I get 5 star ratings. And while I could just look up a guide, having to farm out all the mats/monsters/G is a big no.I don't like the story: I think it's made for kids and is extremely naive.I don't care for the sound design or music: It's just more acceptable than anything.The controls are good for what that's worth.The combat starts off ok, but eventually becomes tedious, grindy and boring.The exploration would be good cause I really like jumping puzzles, but some elements are LOCKED OFF if you don't get 5 star rating on one of the hidden bosses.The collecting would be good except 5 star rating yadda yadda.Seriously, this rating system just did it in for me. _childDocuments_.review: Monster Sanctuary is an absolute indie gem. I never thought a Pokemon metroidvania would work, but Moi Rai found a great balance and it works well. Great things:- Combat takes place in the overworld, so you don't feel disoriented when combat ends. Turn-based games tend suffer from cut away combat disorientation, but not here which is a huge boon to the metroidvania aspect.- Monsters are what open up the world. Rather than reach for skills and abilities that help you traverse the world and backtrack, the monsters you find in later areas just might have what you need to traverse further. Your monster manual will tell you what a monster's overworld ability is as soon as you fight it!- There's usually two places available to go at one time, and you can even venture into new zones if you find the right entrance. I probably took one of the stranger routes in the game, but I loved it for that!- The Story actually affects gameplay at a particular point. Really shakes things up.- When you "level up" at the level cap, it gives you a level increasing item instead, which is beyond amazing QoL for making new teams in the post game.- The synergies and builds you can make are awe-inspiring. The community has taken and ran with these so well!Not as good:- Parkour can be pretty drifty. Most notably when using mounts in tight corridors.- Your starter familiar doesn't get better overworld abilities, so their overworld utility is overshadowed at some point no matter which you choose- Most of the extra outfits kinda suck imo. The starter one is the best, followed by the winter one.- ~~You can't pet the dog~~

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a great game! Highly recommend it if you want a pixel art Pokémon feel with a nice spin on it in terms of strategy, team building and combat. I feel like debuff comps need a slight nerf - especially when it comes to armour break, weakness and poison.2. The inventory system feels a bit chaotic - I would say implementing some technique of using obsolete accessories/weapons beside selling them would be great. A disenchanting for mats or something else might do wonders.3. I would recommend introducing shiny monsters. The light/dark ones should substitute them in a way, but I feel that the drop rate is so high, and the overall idea of the mechanic is totally different. And let us be honest here - the main people buying the game, would be the ones wanting to revisit their Pokémon experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Ever wondered what the lovechild of Metroid and Pokemon would look like? Well, look no further. Monster Sanctuary is definitely a very fun game.You do have a team of 6 Monsters that will fight for you in a turn based fashion, while only 3 of them can be active in the fight. Each monster generally has one weakness (and of course something they are strong against), and at the start of the match, you get to choose who of your 6 active Monsters you will send in to fight. If you selected your team properly, you will be able to exploit the enemies weaknesses or you will build on the combo system to do a finally killing blow on the enemy.The combat features a combo system, in which the first two monsters will build combo points for the third monster to really exploit. Each hit the monsters will do, increases the damage on subsequent attacks for a turn. Some monsters do have “finishing” moves, which are single hit, high power attacks, designed to be used last in your list of monsters.Passive abilities also give you more hits, add debuffs, allow the exploitation of debuffs and so on. Quite a nice system.The game also features some limited ability to evolve some of the monsters, and I would have loved to see Breeding and Evolving to be a bigger thing than they are. Then again, it's an Indi game and maybe Monster Sanctuary 2 will feature that.Still there is a way to evolve some monsters. Like turning a caterpillar into a butterfly. This ability will be unlocked later in the game.Also, while only your active 6 monsters gain XP (and this is some downside of the game in my opinion), you can bring a bunch of other monsters along for their “traversal” powers. So you will be able to be levitated by some flying monsters, or turned into a slime to squeeze through tight passages or activate orbs with their elemental powers and so on.The downside of the game is the inability to have your monsters grow without being in the active team. Yes, you can go farm new eggs, to spawn monsters (which will spawn 2 levels below your highest monsters) but at the end of the day you will end up grinding a lot. Not that different from pokemon, but still worth mentioning because it discourages swapping out your team for new monsters, in my opinion.Overall i find the game quite enjoyable and even without a sale well worth the purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to give this a negative review, really. The art, the story, the uniqueness of every monster, everything is so fun... until it isn't. (TL;DR at the end)I had a blast for the first few hours playing this game. I thought this would be the one, the best monster collecting game. My only issue early game was the way you obtain monsters. Every combat has a rating at the end, going from 1 to 5 stars. This rating is based on turns taken, combos done, buffs, health, debuffs on the enemy etc. It's hard to go above 3 stars in the beginning, which is a 40% rare drop chance. Even 4 stars is only 60%. This rare drop is not guaranteed to be the egg, it could even be any other rare drop. No one tells you how enemy respawn works (by doing 3 other encounters btw), so you might just get stuck trying to obtain a specific egg for AGES, not knowing how to respawn monsters and not getting the egg drop every time you do manage reset it. Early game when you want to catch as much as possible and gain new abilities, it can be annoying (and also makes speedruns very RNG heavy). This gets easier later on when you have access to an item that respawns monster automatically. Minor issue solved, everything is fine. Then they introduce 6 vs 6 combat. Normal combat is 3 vs 3 or 3 vs 1 for boss fights (Which are great, I love the different gimmicks of them and I enjoyed beating all of them). The new ones are similar, but now you have 3 other monsters on the bench that will switch in when one of your first 3 dies. The first 6 vs 6 fight is against your rival. First time I lost a fight in the game. I upgrade my equipment, assign my skill points and manage to win eventually. I always criticize Pokemon for being too easy, so this was a welcome change. But throughout the game these battles became PAINFUL. Sometimes they were fine and actually enjoyable, just requiring you to upgrade your gear, no big deal. The other ones have ridiculous meta teams and require you to change your team up more and more, just to progress. They'll start with buffs that heal the party every turn, possibly outhealing your damage passively. I change up my team and do the same. Then they start stacking buffs. None of my monsters could do that, time to replace them again, I guess. Then they start removing your buffs every turn while stacking their own, it goes on and on. One of the final 6 vs 6 encounters has a team that just stacks shield, heal and buffs passively while removing your own buffs every turn. Who thought this was a balanced fight? I played some JRPGs that are known for being very difficult (such as Etrian Odyssey and SMT), but they rarely ever made me think "that's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥". This fight and the final one did.It feels like you need a spreadsheet to just keep up with enemy teams. Catch everything, analyze, calculate, replace. Don't get attached to your team, you'll probably replace them once you find the next monster that does the same thing, but better.I wanted to play with a party that I like, imo that is the point of monster collecting games: bonding with cute animals and training them to be strong, but the game actively shows you that you need to have a perfect meta team, if you want to have a chance. That includes replacing your starter. I eventually beat the final boss after replacing half of my team, giving them all maxed gear and then losing 7 more times due to bad luck (3 misses in a row despite the enemy having no buffs and my character not being blinded. That kind of bad luck) Additionally I also managed to get stuck more than once for not having certain abilities yet. Remember to always carry teleport items, you might just maneuver yourself into a stream of water and never get out.I went ahead and got every achievement of the game, because apart from the atrocious 6 vs 6 battles in the story and the amount of grinding needed to upgrade equipment, the game can actually be fun. But for how fun the game can be, the negative heavily outweigh the positive and unless the devs decide to rebalance (or add a "normal" and "easy" mode which you can switch between during the adventure), I just can't recommend the game.TL;DR: - Luck based mechanics are a bit annoying early game- Story battles have a ridiculous difficulty curve, you will constantly have to switch up your party, even replacing your starter. No bonding with certain monsters like you would in something like Pokemon or Nexomon- Some of the last battles were pure frustration- You can get stuck by not having certain abilities, which shouldn't happen in a metroidvania
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great. The battles are thought provoking, but not mentally draining or overly time consuming. Collecting new monsters is fun, and using their abilities to progress through the game is super exciting. You could have 2 of the same monster and they could be used for completely different situations due to the diverse skill tree and equipment options. The movement and occasional puzzle-esc parts of the sanctuary keep the game fun and refreshing, instead of just walking forward to progress through the game. The story progression is also fun and interesting, as what starts as a simple journey unfolds into many quests, some of those quests being very important!Overall, I would recommend this game to all who enjoy team-builders and turn-based combat, along with those who love quests, strategy, skill trees, and optimizing items.

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Sanctuary is a good game. I enjoyed it way more than Pokémon's more recent game and will compare it to that game often as I used to love that franchise.Story is alright, it works but it's nothing too special. The most disappointing part of it is how quickly they just glance over light and darkness considering it's a pretty important gameplay mechanic once it's introduced.I am glad they let you tackle story moments out of order because it's a metroidvania so you have some freedom in your progression. The only thing stopping you from going in certain areas is your level but if you're good, you can be levels behind an area and be able to explore most of it. Only bosses can halt your progress then but it's not an issue encountering something too powerful as you can come back later after doing a different story moment. There's usually something else in the story to do if you're having a hard time in 1 area.In terms of monster design, it's alright but game stands no chance against Pokémon in this regards. There are a couple I do enjoy like Mogwai, Shockhopper, Glowdra and Aazerach.While areas you explore aren't too unique, they are at least pretty interesting to explore with secrets, branching paths and puzzles...something Pokémon doesn't seem to do these days.The pixel art is good, nothing impressive but good enough that it all looks charming.Music at first was meh but I grew to like it over time. The default battle theme and monster champion theme weren't good to me but later battle songs and the variation of the default battle theme you can pick are all good, I really like the Alchemist theme. Area music is decent but nothing too special.The game's a metroidvania so it's a big map with a lot to do. Your monsters are basically your power ups, the more you collect, the more you can explore. This alone is a great reason to get as many monsters as possible as you never know if a new monster will have an essential ability or not.Almost every monster is viable in battle too, while there aren’t as many monsters as in a Pokémon game, at least they’re all useful. I changed my team up from time to time, but some of my earliest monsters were still viable in the end. Mogwai being my trump card the entire game, capable of deleting health bars...at the cost of being pretty fragile.Anyway, the battles are so much more interesting than Pokémon. By default, battles are 3v3 which already increases the strategy by a ton. You also choose the order of actions in your team which is a mechanic I adored in Epic Battle Fantasy so it’s great it’s here too, funny it’s also with a team of 3.Random reference aside, the order of actions is very important as there’s also a combo mechanic. Every buff, heal or attack fills a combo meter. The higher the combo, the higher your damage boost. So it’s best to do all the buffs, healing and multi-hit attacks first and then end it on a big WHAM. So satisfying to completely destroy a health bar after a set-up.What makes it even more deep is that every monster has a skill tree that lets you choose their role in the battle. Some monsters can take on 2 different roles depending on how you picked everything on the skill tree. The skill tree is also your only way to learn new moves. The amount of moves aren’t that much as you’ll find monsters with similar attacks quite often, but at least every attack has a use. In Pokémon, like 75% of all moves are completely worthless and even in that game moves are shared between many Pokémon.Every move also consumes mana which restores a certain amount each turn, that way you can’t spam your strongest attacks all the time and status effects that increase or decrease mana restoration can really affect your options.Evolution feels like it was forced into the game. Not many monsters can evolve and you have to use a specific catalyst in a special area to evolve a monster but the game doesn’t tell you what catalyst evolves which monster so it’s not really worth the effort to evolve. The game could have gone without this mechanic.What isn’t a forced mechanic is the light/dark mechanic. At a certain point in the story, monsters will be affected by light and darkness which makes wild monsters more powerful. You can also shift your monsters to light or darkness to strengthen them and it’s pretty interesting. Shifting to a side gives a boost in stats and a powerful ability but how your stats are boosted and which ability you get depends on the side, so you have to make a choice. Light generally is more defensive and supportive while darkness is more aggressive and disruptive. If you regret your choice, the game at least is kind enough to let you find items that let you change this.I am very thankful for how much they try to mitigate grinding in the game, at least, when you’re changing your team. Monsters you collect will always be near the level of your highest level monster and there is an item that lets you level up monsters that are 2 levels below the highest level. That little restriction for the level up item allows them to give you plenty of these without breaking the balance.Using max leveled monsters isn’t a waste of EXP too. They still have an EXP bar and each time you fill that up, you get an item that lets you max out other monsters.That being said, if you don’t fight every monster you see, you’ll likely be underleveled. While this wasn’t an issue for me as I went in area’s underleveled all the time, I can see this being an issue for less skilled players who will feel the need to grind in order to progress.This goes nicely into the difficulty. This game is no cakewalk and will trash your team if it’s bad. I welcome this difficulty as I like a good challenge and Pokémon was so easy that it was boring so I much rather have this than spamming A ‘till I win. I actually had to make major changes to my team from time to time to have more focus so I could win certain tough battles. I really liked having to strategize how to beat certain teams.Even if I like the challenge, I think a difficulty option would be neat. Not necessarily lower the level of monsters, but make their strategies less focussed. Bosses will have legit good teams with dangerous strategies and making those strategies more tame might help less experienced players.Because mine sucks, I pay special attention to how games use luck. I can safely say the game uses luck a lot better than Pokémon. In Pokémon, 1 unlucky moment can cost you the battle while in this game it's less frustrating.It helps that most attacks are multi-hit so missing 1 hit of a 6-hit move isn’t a big deal.The map could use some improvements, it’s a basic gridded map which does the job but not being able to pin locations so you know where to return to later is a bit annoying. I probably missed a few secrets because I forgot some areas had a secret in them I couldn’t access yet.You can inspect your opponent’s stats in battle but it would be neat to inspect your own team too, it can sometimes happen that I forget stats and weaknesses of my monsters.Shops strangely do not show you how much you own of items, so you have to check your inventory to know how much you have of something. Not that you’d use the shop too often as healing items are not really the most useful. You’re better off having a healing monster in your team or using health-stealing attacks.The game has some rough edges it could improve on but in general, it was fun and good and the team seems to be aware of them. It was a lot more fun to play than Pokémon’s more recent games and isn’t short on content, around 30+ hours so it's definitely worth €20.

_childDocuments_.review: The art and music and style bring me back to an older generation of games that I look fondly upon, while letting me collect and customize a variety of different monsters with cool equipment and meaningful stats, as well as interesting and unique challenges presented between the champion boss fights. If you told me that this was a big budget Nintendo release from the 2011~2014 era of 3ds games, I would not bat an eye, and that is a compliment of very high praise. Fantastic job and very well executed. While the game is not perfect in some regards, (like showing the tower rise with each level pull while the the first section stays at the first, second at the second, instead of rising, with the top being filled in with the section below it), and not a lot of ways to help bring up the power of weaker, earlier game, evolutionless monsters in line with later game ones with better abilites, skill trees, and base stats, the variety as well as the genius of the shift system for further customization as well as the great diversity of accessories makes up for that in a big way. My only real gameplay complaint is that later game rare weapons like the restoring wand come unupgraded, meaning I have to invest thousands of gold to bring it up to a comparable level to weapons I'm already using, and that the price of materials and availability of gold is a little sparse. As someone who used no combat consumables, opting to sell them for gold, selling excess equipment and never buying food or non-rare equipment, I found myself at a gold deficit frequently while trying new accessories and rare weapons to experiment with.  Maybe gold sense could be a larger increase, as even with an aurumtail with those skills assigned, I still had to spend a couple hours grinding gold and selling items to buy the materials to upgrade all the different unique weapons and accessories to +4, as I am still unable to buy gold or rubies from the material shop even post credits. All in all a great game, with satisfying and fun combat, a lot of player agency and customization, which are very important to me, and a great style with cool and cute monster designs.

_childDocuments_.review: It's sort of like a 2D sidescroller version of Pokemon with exploration, platforming, RPG, and puzzle elements, but actually fun... oh, and an actual story and side quests that isn't just "collecting" all the monsters or playing errand boy.I'll start off with the good.The 3v3 (sometimes 6v6) battles are pretty neat, as is how every single monster actually feels varied, unique, and useful at almost every stage of the game. They all have their own strengths, weaknesses, types, and so on. It's a little more complex than a "rock, paper, scissors" kind of thing. For instance, there can be a monster that's only weak to a magical fire based attack, and either neutral to or strong against all others. An interesting aspect to the battles is that you're scored and given a rating at the end which affects what drops you get, and it shows how many points you get for different things (bufss/debuffs you use, number of turns taken, synergy with attacks, combo rating, exploiting weaknesses, etc). In addition, there's a combo mechanic where the more times you hit an enemy on your turn the higher the counter rises, and the higher it rises the more damage you do, so it can pay off to do weaker attacks that deal more hits with your first two monsters, then deliver a damaging blow with your third monster. The counter resets at the end of each turn.Every monster has it's own RPG-like skill tree, gains XP in battle (or by being part of the "active" group) which gives a skill point upon leveling up, and tiers of skills are locked behind levels. It's possible to unlock every skill for a monster by continuing to "level" it past max level where it just gains skill points.There's a variety of equipment, levels for equipment, different kinds of food, and so on to equip or affect your monsters with, along with an option that comes up mid-game that can wildly change stats and other things.There's just as much emphasis on active skills as there is on passive skills, and builds relying on either or a mix of both are all valid. Speaking of which, synergy not only between skills but between different monsters is set up very well. For instance I can have one monster grant a shield to all three members at the start of each round, which in turn may trigger an effect of another monster that activates upon receiving a shield.One of my favorite things is how, unlike other games this may be compared to, your monsters actually matter outside of combat. In fact, they're absolutely essential for exploration and getting around. There's monsters that can pick you up and fly for a short time, ones that you can ride for better speed and higher jump, ones that can break open walls, ones that can cut or burn vines away, ones that help you swim, and so on and so forth. The way this works is that you have a monster following you at all times which you can use the exploration ability of (i.e. flying, destroying obstacles, etc), and you can freely swap them out for any monster you have obtained at any time without restriction.Side note, there's also an online PvP mode you can enter once you have it unlocked. If that's not your thing, that's fine. The rest of the game is offline single player and you're not punished or miss out on rewards for not partaking in it, nor is it required to enter PvP at any time.Now for what I don't like.There are a couple jumps that require nearly pixel perfect precision. I don't mind challenge, but some parts are straight up ridiculous. There could also be more explanation of your monster's exploration abilities. It's touched upon once, but only for one thing for your starter. That's pretty much it. I hate sounding like a fanboy, and I'm sitting here trying to think of what else I don't like... but that's pretty much all I can think of.

_childDocuments_.review: It was quite a fun game., it has a nice art style and some good music., it's quite simple but does have some very nice characters and was interesting to unravel the mystery and plot of the game., it's great, the combat is nice and not random, and you actually see the monsters that you have to touch. Each monster having its own ability is especially nice, you gotta keep hoping to get their eggs on each new monster so you can see if it has some nice new ability you need to explore the map. Not all of them will be useful, but it's still nice. Speaking of the map, it's also pretty good, varied places, decent size, all pretty nice, with some light puzzling as well at times. Marking stuff on the map is also fantastic so you can remember places to come back to.There's basically no limit to the amount of monsters you can hold at once, as well as no limit to their moves since it's skill-based, which I do like. At least there's level ups you can easily get and buy, so it's just *fine*.I feel like there were some typos, like 1 or 2. I think I saw them towards the end of the story, I don't quite remember where, but yeah., a fun game that has some pretty good design, good combat, and a simple story.

_childDocuments_.review: What would a Pokemon game feel like if it was a metroidvania? That is roughly what Monster Sanctuary is.You collect, level up, evolve and battle (in 3v3 or 6v6 duel formats) with monsters. However, the overworld plays like a 2D metroidvania with environmental hazards, platforming, secrets, etc. There are also weapons and accessories to collect and upgrade as well as skill trees unique to each monster. All this variety gives a lot of freedom to switch around teams to use and counter different strategies your enemy might use. All in all it is a really satisfying blend of both genres.I would describe the story, music, and graphics as good enough. They did not have anything that stood out to me but they were enjoyable. The game's main plot had a conclusive end but leaves a very clear path to a sequel.One other thing worth pointing out is that the game has a lot of player friendly gameplay mechanics which I really appreciated. For example, even though only your active party (6) gains experience, there are items you can buy or get as drops or rewards which let you level up monsters. Once a monster hits the level cap (42 at the time of writing this review) it continues gaining experience and each "level up" grants one of these items to level up another monster. There are various other examples of similar design choices that seem minor but allow players to have fun with the game's mechanics as opposed to worrying about farming or grinding in order to fully make use of them.Overall: it's a solid, fun game, especially for any fan of Pokemon or metroidvanias!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Either go into this game with no expectations or set them accordingly:This game  an excellent metroidvaniaThis game  an excellent monster battlerThe metroidvania mechanics are superficial and mostly appear in the form of exploration, finding obvious keys for obvious doors, and a handful of puzzles.The actual monster battler mechanics though are excellent. Each monster has its own skill tree and each monster feels like it has some kind of niche. _childDocuments_.review: This review is based on the Early Access version and   for the Full Version (In case people read it after the full release).Pros and Cons (A more detailed review is further down):Tags: Retro Platformer, Turn-based, monster collecting. + Good controls+ Decent variety of monsters+ Evolution of monsters (Light/Dark and Evolution are nice options to utilize the various types of monsters in even more different ways.)+ Good music+ Riddles are not too difficult and not too many (Some you can simply skip, if you don't really need the item)+ Balancing is okay, though slightly favoured towards heavy Physical Crit Builds (That was my experience after some hours) - 13h of gameplay (Remember, it is EA. They will add more.)- Economy is pointless. You earn gold but can't really spend it, because it is pretty easy to get the top gear without spending money- Item variety is too smallThis game is a retro style platformer with turn based monster fights. And as such it works pretty well. The platforming part is solid. The controls work well, even for someone like me, who is not used to controller gameplay.The fights are very fun and interesting. You collect various monsters with varying abilities. It is the usual rock, paper, scissors style where you counter your opponent with the specific element or ability to gain the advantage. And in that regard it works pretty good. You don't just have the usual 3 or 4 elements, but instead they are also split into physical and magical attacks. So if you want to make absolutely sure to have the upper hand, you can choose from a variety of 50 Monsters to counter your opponents weaknesses. In this stage of the development, you can play through 6 or 7 areas with are filled with riddles which are sometimes challenging, but definitely doable. I am usually someone who googles riddles quickly, if i spend too much time on them, but this game has found a good balance in difficulty. Of course because the game is still in EA, some things are lacking a little bit, like e.g. the skillsystem needs a bit of balancing. I was able to build a: Healer/Buffer; Magical/Nuker; Physical/Mass Crit Team which carried me through the last 4 hourse by nearly onehitting every enemy team without a sweat. People who want to rely on a core-team will see that it is not advised to just stick to your favourite 3 monster party, but you should always keep at least some monsters up to speed with your main team, in case you run into a fight where you are heavily disadvantaged. The game adds a lot of variety with options to additionally evolve your monsters to either light or dark which opens up further actives skills and passives. Also you can evolve your monsters with certain items, though this is really late in the game and thus not really relevant yet.Also the game offers some challenging Bossfights, as well as a very basic infinity mode. Also PVP seems to be an option, if they ever think about adding Multiplayer. PVP fights against the AI in the game are not really challenging and thus i hope i'll be able to duel with real Players in the future.The games economy is very basic. Your items have preset effects which do not differ to items of the same type. The is no rarity element involved. You got a weapon, it deals certain damage, you can up it +1,+2,+3 and thats it. Money is pointless. I literally didn't need to spend a single gold coin. You can only buy items like gear, potions (which you do not need to use at all, because it is easier to heal with skills and the HP resets after evey fight.) and food. Upgrade materials can be found and not bought, but you find lots of those so no problem there.It would be interesting to see rarity added. You slay a Boss and have the chance to drop some nice weapons. Definitely something i would love to see.Overall i can to recommend this game in its current state. For the price you get at least 12h of gameplay and in the future i can see a lot of content being added which might even double or triple the time. This game as a lot of potential. So if you are into the turn-based fighting and don't mind some platforming in the meantime, this game is a safe bet.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice selection for April and I highly recommend that everyone, Pokémon fan or not, should get it. It has enough going for it to stand on its own without the comparison. Monster Sanctuary is a wonderful blend of creature collecting, TBS, and oh so light amounts of platforming -- just enough to keep an adventurer paying attention. The game has a wonderful story that builds just enough curiosity to make the player wonder why the world is designed the way it is. While finishing the story did leave me feeling a bit confined in the Sanctuary (I want more), it was all because the game did such a great job of giving me such a rich experience within the confines of the world that I was given to explore and the monsters I was able to hatch. I love that you can't just power through all the content with the same team (without experiencing diminishing returns). Combos and team roles (healer/shield/damage/etc) are a thing and slowly become a wall you need to overcome in order to learn how to efficiently win battles without simply using brute force (until you figure out a team that can use said force efficiently).I love that in this game, equipment and food buffs are an actual thing to signify progression instead of just being tacked on. I also experienced a lot of freedom in swapping around monsters for my various teams as I worked my way through the post-game content. The game allows you to invest resources, within reason, towards new monsters so that you can try out various builds without experiencing buyer's remorse. It's a game that wants you to try everything and really think about various builds within each extensive skill tree to make the most of your experience.It was just an awesome experience overall and Monster Sanctuary definitely filled a void created by my disappointment in newer Pokémon games. I'm glad that this game was one of the few I chose to pick up again after a long hiatus from Steam. Money well spent!

_childDocuments_.review: This game proved to be quite a pleasant surprise for me!Basically this is an RPG where you're a monster trainer who runs around in a 2D landscape that looks like a graphically improved Terraria and is laid out in the style of a Metroid style game. You have to figure out various jumping puzzles on each screen, sometimes requiring the use of the monsters you've acquired on your journey to reach tricky treasure chests that were once impossible for you to obtain. As an example, the vaero monster (which looks like a bird) can pick you up and carry you across large gaps. Another monster, the monk, can bash walls on command and sometimes reveal hidden passageways leading to treasure.The assortment of monsters you can collect is where the game really shines. Battles play out in a standard turn-based JRPG fashion with each of your monsters having an elemental strength and weakness, and a plethora of elemental attacks and support skills to use. At the end of any given fight, you may acquire an "egg" that, when hatched, gives you a type of the monster you just defeated. Each monster can be equipped with a weapon and three accessories that are very heavy on stat modifiers, all of which can be upgraded at a blacksmith. All monsters also have skill trees that you can sink points into when you level them up from fighting. The skill trees in this game are super satisfying and allow you to learn stronger versions of existing attacks, brand new abilities, and all sorts of cool passive modifiers that do things like drastically increase your critical hit chance if the selected monster has a buff on it, or leeching hit points whenever the monster deals damage, and these two examples are just the tip of the iceberg.I expected this to just be a cute little game that I'd put a little bit of time into, but I'm approaching 10 hours just over a day after I first played the game. I'm seriously hooked on Monster Sanctuary. There's so much customization, battles are surprisingly strategic, and exploring the various 2D platformer-esque "biomes" of the game's world and finding secret routes and treasures is so much fun.This game is early access, but it genuinely does not feel it at all. Don't let the simplistic and retro look throw you off, this game has a lot of depth and is super polished already. I cannot recommend this game enough.

_childDocuments_.review: As one of the long time fans of the Pokemon franchise who is bitter about the decline in the  quality of the games and the whole "Dexit" affair, I'm really glad I stumbled upon Monster Sanctuary. While it is in the same genre as Pokemon, but does a bunch of things that makes it unique and isn't simply trying to ape what Pokemon does. Not only do you have a large cast of monsters to pick from to add to your team, you can customize them all with unique skill trees, food slots and equipment. Each of these bits of customization are meaningful strategic decisions that can drastically alter the way your monster performs in combat. The fact that most battles are 3v3 means that you'll almost always have 3 of your monsters out of the field at once, allowing you to further customize your team by creating synergies within your team to amplify their effectiveness. While still in early access, I have yet to encounter any bugs, glitches, crashes or instances of gross game balance issues. The platforming metroidvania element of the game is probably its weakest point, but even that doesn't really detract from my enjoyment of the game and I can appreciate that the devs are trying to do something unique. Some of the puzzles can be a little frustrating, not because they're hard but because they're fussy. However, the treasure hunting element that this mode brings can be enjoyable as you probe the nooks and crannies for hidden treasure chests. Overall, this game is worth your time and money even at this stage at its development and as it progresses to a 1.0 release will become even more of a good deal. I have no regrets buying it.

_childDocuments_.review: Hey, you got some Pokémon in my Metroidvania!What? You got some Metroidvania in my Pokémon!Mmmm... mysteriously delicious!No seriously, this is one of those combos that had never occurred to me before, but now that I've sampled it, I suddenly realize that they go together perfectly. Kind of like 'Disney characters + Final Fantasy' was a joke before Kingdom Hearts became a bestselling blockbuster series.So, you've got a bit ol' Metroidvania-style map to explore, with various biomes that each carry a distinct atmosphere, look, and selection of enemies. But instead of accessing new areas by finding upgrades, you do it by battling and catching monsters who can assist you with new abilities. Instead of finding a grappling-hook in a chest somewhere, you catch a giant spider who can web you to where you need to go. Instead of finding scuba-gear, you catch a giant fish that can pull you swiftly through the water. Instead of finding double-jump boots, you... well, actually, you still find double-jump boots, but frankly, for a Metroidvania, double-jumping is so utterly basic that it'd be silly to tie that to any particular monster.The combat-system, meanwhile, is remarkably deep and varried, featuring a variety of potent buffs and status-ailments that gradually ratchet up the challenge and complexity as you progress through the game. Early on you can get by easily enough just targeting enemies' elemental weaknesses, but carry on doing that, and you'll hit a wall in the late-game, where instead you have to focus on stacking buffs and shields on your own party, while loading the enemies up with crippling ailments and grinding down their own attempts to buff up high. Just don't forget to still keep an eye on the elemental lineups, or your key buffer/healer might just get suddenly one-shot by a heavily-boosted 'Super Effective' attack! There's also an intriguing combo-system that takes some getting used to, and a somewhat arcane 'grade' system that gives you various rewards from each battle based on how well you performed.What I'm getting at is that this game is DEEP, and neither pulls punches nor holds your hand all the way through. You get some mild tutorializing at the start, introducing you to the basic systems, but it's up to YOU to actually figure out how to apply them effectively, and if you fail to keep up, things can get pretty frustrating pretty fast. You have to be ready to revise your approach, switch out your monsters, change your gear, and try new things if you want to make it through the adventure - and, more importantly, hatch 'em all!If I have to give it ONE serious criticism, it's the frustrating way the 'shift' system intersects with this game's version of 'evolutions'. Without going into too much detail, the shift-system is enabled around or past the halfway-point of the game, depending on exactly what kind of path you take, and causes new, more powerful variants of every available monster to start randomly spawning. You can turn regular monsters into shifted variants using an item, but this item has highly limited availability and cannot be bought. Meanwhile, the 'evolution' system allows you to use certain special items to transform a small number of monsters into different, usually more powerful, monsters that invariably can ONLY be obtained in this way. Some of these special items are simply dropped by the 'evolved' form of the monster when encountered in the wild, but others can be obtained only ONCE, in treasure-chests or from NPC's. Additional copies of these evolution-items can only be gained randomly from 'reward-boxes', which means spinning a really big wheel-o-fortune and crossing your fingers. Do you see the problem? By the time you unlock 'shifting', you're liable to have already wasted several semi-unique evolution-items on regular, unshifted versions of those monsters. If you want a shifted version of the evolved monster, you'll thus have to either pray for another evolution-item to drop from a reward-box, or expend an equally rare and valuable 'shifting-stone'. It's really more of a nitpick, but it's something I feel could really have been handled better. Consider it a warning, also, and a reward for having read all the way down here!So yeah, apart from that one niggling annoyance, an excellent game that combines two genres in a remarkably entertaining fashion. Definitely worth recommending!

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: 100%'d the game aside from NG+, and had a great time.  Two thumbs up. I beat the BBEG and there's more game to play!  I don't know if I have DLC or what, but I'm happy about it.  Been having tons of fun with this game.  Metroidvania with plenty of map-exploration abilities to collect, and a few difficult platforming areas.  The combat is not platforming, it's like a JRPG, 3 vs 3 or 3 vs 1 (boss) or 6 vs 6.  When you finish a fight with a high enough rating, or if you just get lucky, you can get an egg for one of the monsters you killed, and hatch it as your own!  Each monster has a different selection of attacks/skills (many are repeated on multiple monsters) to be unlocked as they level up.  It's up to you to build an effective, synergizing team, and there are lots of things you could focus on!  There are 2 attack types: physical and magicThere are at least 5 damage types: neutral, air/wind, fire, earth, water/iceThere are attacks that only hit 1 monster or AoE all 3There are attacks with different quantities of hits, which affects your combo counter, and whether it got dodged etcThere are healing and shield skillsThere are a ton of buffs / debuffs You can also equip them with a weapon and 3 accessories, which all do different things and can also be upgraded. Lots to play with, especially once you get into the high levels and can fully spec out your monsters.  That has a lot of COOL factor, but it takes a lot of TIME so I tended to build 1 team and use it until I got stuck, then try to build something new.  Currently $23CAD on Steam, but I got it <5 on a Fanatical Bundle, and it's well worth that.  Having a great time!

_childDocuments_.review: If you like monster tamers, buy this game.Nearly every other monster tamer relies on the Pokemon formula of 1v1s and one-shots. Monster Sanctuary finally brings monster tamers into the world of modern RPGs, rethinking all of the cliches and conventions to make a game worth more than just sum of your nostalgia. It's simply fun to play.There are no bad monsters. Every monster has a purpose (or multiple), and every monster can be strong in the right party comp. Want to try something different? Reset the skill tree with a common item. Having a hard time with a late-game fight? Hatch a monster at near-max level, and slot it into your party with 0 grind. No other monster tamer is this detailed, this strategic, or this flexible.I've been a fan since the original demo that ended with the Steam Golem fight, and I've been waiting a long time for the full release. There are some things I'd like to see improved, like the writing, and the early areas could be improved by applying the design skills learned from 5 years of development, but I have absolutely no hesitation in recommending this game right now.It's just fun to play, start to finish.

_childDocuments_.review: Early game is a lot of fun but then it becomes a chore. They've implemented level scaling (very odd scaling based on how many rooms you explored and monsters in rooms set to your strongest current ones, so in theory you could meta-game that if you really want to), a level cap at level 40 (which means enemies set close to your level cap, especially random encounters become a chore as you can't out-level them anymore) and contradictorily core gameplay loops.You have wild encounters and bosses where you fight 3-vs-3 (or 3-vs-1 for most bosses) and you tailor your party usually around that, but then there are party fights of 6-vs-6 (though only 3-vs-3 in the fight, if one of your monsters dies you have to select a replacement from the remaining ones). The party fights are an absolute chore, usually about having the right buffs/debuffs and don't allow much flexibility to overcome. Either you have the right monsters or you're dead.Now, the monsters come in egg form. If you hatch them they usually have a level around what your highest level is, but only the 6 main monsters gain experience from fights. So if you later need one of the other monsters for a specific talent, yeah, you have to grind that up, which happens quite often later in the game. It's really tiresome.All this does is make the early game rather exciting with lots of stuff to explore and get but later due to all the mechanics described fighting becomes more and more tiresome.

_childDocuments_.review: The PVE is an incredibly fun metroidvania RPG, but I feel more inclined to talk on the PVP for this review. The fun of PVP comes in designing a team strategy and having that strategy play out against your opponents. Now of course, the first few tries (first 20, if you're me), the strategy is gonna crash and burn, especially if you're trying something new. However, making adjustments to your team is incredibly quick and easy. Thanks to the egg mechanic, all monsters you catch will be just below pvp level, and without any grinding I had hundreds of level badges to get them to max level instantly. Since early game mons can be PVP powerhouses (the very first mon you encounter, blob, is a solid PVP healer/debuff applier), having them instantly be up to level is incredibly convenient. Also, each mon has skill trees, so two people running the same mon could have them doing totally different things. Thanatos, for example, could be a carry sweeper or a nutty support. This game deserves more players, and the community is incredibly welcoming and willing to help you in the learning process of team making. Definitely check this game out

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Sanctuary is essentially a Castlevania: SotN metroidvania with Pokemon style monster capture and old school JRPG turned based party combat.    Each creature has a unique skill tree and can be further enhanced by light/dark shifts, upgradable equipment, and perma food buffs.  The game progresses at a nice rate and exploring the map feels natural without too many road bumps.  You will likely need to retool your team several times to focus on intra-monster synergies and opponent weaknesses throughout the course of the game to meet the demands of stronger challenges or boss fights.  Absolutely recommend for the aspects mentioned above as well as the enjoyable drop in game play, great pacing and difficulty ramping, sense of exploration, and the endearing pixel art.  The free DLC "The Forgotten World" adds a new area with additional monsters and challenges that add on to the already great experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Sanctuary is a monster battler with a metrovania overworld and turn based 3 on 3 battles. I've played through the game 4 times now (once with each starter) at various points through early development and once again when it was released lovingly into the wild (60 hours in the last 2 weeks). And I'm still finding new combinations to try.Do you want a physical based team that smacks down your opponents, you can do it. Do you want to debuff the opposing team to oblivion and watch them helpless die to fire, poison, and ice, this game lets you do it. Do you want a cute frog, adorable fluffy one eyed monster, and a caterpillar facing down the odds, yup, you can do it. The freedom is yours. Each monster has different skill tress you flesh out that lets them do what you want them to. You can be a dedicated healer or a direct damage beast, or an aura sharing support, the flexibility is yours. And every monster is viable. In my current playthrough 1 on the monsters from the first area traveled with me literally to the last zone. It's biggest strength can also be a weakness however. There are 101 monsters each with varying skills and putting together a synergistic team is important. There's a lot to take in and its easy to get overwhelmed. Fortunately, the community is extremely helpful and the dedicated community liaison actually liaison so help is only a discord or forum post away.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: If you like metroidvanias and monster collecting-battler/tactical games, this game is for you. I like the former better, but I also like to get lost in skilltrees, combining creatures, and equip them with stuff that makes them stronger. This game is seriously good, I like it a lot. I don't really go for achievements with steam games, but I unlocked all 34, just for fun. Even if you go through the vast map and storyline, the game still proveides things to do.There are many pros:- I love the pixelart, the animations are not many in frames or types, but the existing ones are made well.- Many retro tunes to listen to- The monsters are cool as hell, some are cute, or funny, some are noble and majestic, some are terifying and horrendous. And there are a LOT of them. You can modify them to light or dark, (upgrades to base stats, and a new skill) tripling the creature number. Some even can be evolved to a new monster.- Interestingly both the platforming and the tactical battling made really well (with small hickups).- The metroidvania part include the monsters too: all creatures have an ability that helps in exploring and progressing on the map.- Worms!There are some cons:- The map is not a big help, it's very basic, not giving any information whatsoever (no ability gates, not even the area names).- If you look for a specific thing (a monster, a crafting material etc) it could take a long time to find it.- To max out everything, you probably have to look for some guides as I did. Some secrets are hard to find (wich is fine, I just mentioning what I used some guides to), most of the champions are hard to defeat to 5 stars. Some of the puzzles are hard to solve (the timered ones especially). To find and build a team for defeating a specific champion could take a long time, as they probably need some equipment you don't have, and maxed out. And the skilltrees, as I mentioned I love to mess around with them, I'm just not good at it. :)But, despite the cons there is so much to love, this game is worth it's cost, and if you are on a budget, wait for a sale, and then buy it, you won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent monster battler. The story and "metroidvania" aspects are pretty simple but the combat is really enjoyable.
