_childDocuments_.review: quick note: my playtime is inaccurate, add +20 hours to the time of review. I mostly played and beat the game over one weekend I didn't have internet, so it didn't sync playtime. A complex, party-based RPG with a pokemon-like coat of paint and metroidvania world gameplay. Each 'monster' has an extensive skill tree and the name of the game is building synergies with your team. Every action affects your whole team in some way, leading to lots of emergent complexity and synergy. Instead of 1v1 being the standard, battles are 3v3 opening much more possibility for teamplay. But, skill tree resets are very easy to get your hands on, so you don't need to be afraid of investing a dud skill point or going down the wrong path - you can reset and try different things as the monsters unlock new skills, and you rotate in new picks for your team. You can re-skill your entire team after a boss battle to take advantage of a different approach. For me, the real fun in the game comes from optimizing my team so I can beat most battles in 2-3 turns. When wild encounters start lasting more then 3 turns, I know my team isn't keeping up and I need to optimize their skills and equipment. On the other hand, Trainer and Boss battles provide a longer form battle where synergies really shine. Spending 3 turns of set-up and defense to allow your Sweeper to spend the next turn bulldozing an entire team is incredibly satisfying, or setting up a stall + dots team and watching the enemy slowly dots themselves to death.  The great thing is that wild, trainer, and boss battles are all so emergent different. Wild battles, you get the most rewards for beating them fast so you want some good all-out attack to do these quickly.  Bosses are typically incredibly strong but fairly narrow in scope, so you need to build a counter that really focuses on their strengths and weakness in particular.  20% damage reduction against all kinds of damage won't do you much help on a boss buffed itself to 500% fire damage, so you really need to prepare for exactly what you're fighting, after a few failed attacks to scout out their moveset and weaknesses.  Keeper duels are different again, with a 6v6 style that are highly varied where the Keepers have all the same mechanics and options that you do. All these kinds of battles require different approaches so you never get stuck in a routine and are constantly on your toes, thinking about how you can leverage the skills and abilities to you have to build a plan against the enemy infront of you. It is difficult to stress just how important team synergy is in this game. You can't just build each monster individually to fit a predefined role, their role will change fluidly depending on the match-up of allies and enemies. My tank in one battle is my DPS in another is my support in another. All monsters can, and should, do all depending on the situation.  Trying to play most monsters 1-1 matching a role or ignoring synergies with allies (and against enemies) will lead to severe under-performance (and long battles), but the game is very forgiving and you have easy access to re-skills to fix things or just try something new.Built in new game+ and options for randomized and nuzlocke-style  ('Brave') runs with or without permadeath give this lots of replayability that I'll be sure to keep coming back to.

_childDocuments_.review: One may be tempted to say that at first this is a pretty cute-and-dry Pokemonlike, but where it excels it turns the game into a whole new, and much better, form.Here, the monsters you can tame have skill trees, and that makes all the difference. Suddenly, instead of simply having one team that maximizes type coverage, you have a set of builds you can make, and this set is huge. Every monster has many different ways you can stat them out in these trees, and there are many other points of customization as well. This adds incredible, fascinating depth both in and out of combat. It makes combat a dizzying whirl of effects, both active and passive, being applied in a turn, and it really is a joy to experience.It also bills itself as a metroidvania. This is true! Monsters grant out of combat abilities that allow you to access new areas. I was never good at combat in metroidvanias, so replacing action combat with real-time combat is a really genius move, if you ask me. I will say that the original Pokemon has metroidvania elements too, what with HMs and all, so this isn't exactly revolutionary, but I do love platforming and discovering things on the world map in this game.The writing is... Nothing to write home about. A little too inspired by Pokemon in that regard. Another (admittedly weird and minor) gripe I have is that there are no game over screens when you fail a plot-required battle, but instead when you lose, you're instantly and unceremoniously teleported back to before the fight. It breaks my immersion, honestly, and I'd at least like to have a game over screen I need to press "continue" on to get teleported backwards.Overall, do I recommend this game? Absolutely! The actual battles are far and away much better than its inspriation, and the builds I can make will have me thinking for a very long time.

_childDocuments_.review: So if you're looking for a new Pokemon this isn't it. It was mildly fun, but the game keeps freezing on me. At times this makes it unplayable. Adding to that, I recently found out that only a handful of the 101 monsters can evolve. For me, like 60% of the fun in Pokemon was evolving your pokemon. It gave the game a nice progression and made me feel more invested in my team. Well, all of these monsters look like level 1 starter pokemon, and they don't get any better. The skill tree would be cool if there were a greater variety of moves. Half of my monsters share essentially the exact same skill tree, and the other half have another version of the exact same skill tree. So essentially it doesn't matter in the least if I pick one or the other of my grass-type monsters. None of these monsters so far have anything unique or special about them.The level design is confusing and not in a good way. I spent a good deal of time trying to find my way back to a certain part of the map on the first level, and the map was no help at all in trying to do that. It's just nondescript green blocks, and they don't give you really any idea of whether one way is a dead-end or whether it was a soft dead-end that I needed a certain monster's special skill to get through. The level design is also pretty boring so far. Everything looks the same.The monster special abilities would be cool, but they don't really do anything except help you get to chests which have seemingly pretty common/underwhelming items. Would be cooler if you had to use them to get through certain parts of the level, or if there was a better payoff to using them to find treasure. There is not a lot of surprise in this aspect.The story so far also seems weak. I was not invested. You live in a monster sanctuary. You and everyone else hatch and train monsters. That seems to be the extent of it. I really wanted to like this game. I think it has potential, but I would have to see a lot of changes before reconsidering. Including:- (actual) Monster evolution - More interesting level design with better maps- More engaging storyline and characters- More variety in skill tree/monsters have unique abilities that would make me choose them over another monster in battle- Fix the constant freezing (I know this isn't an issue for everyone but I have never run into this issue before on this computer)Pass.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing this since the game's early alpha builds before it made it onto Steam and I love it. I first found it on a pokemon fansite, as like pokemon it is a monster collection RPG, but thats where the similarities end. The game takes place in a sort of hidden lost world within our own, one where the culture of the humans inhabiting it remained unchanged since the middle ages (just without the senseless bloodshed). The action starts fairly quickly and each monster has a unique skill tree. And also like pokemon many of these monsters evolve too (though every evolution uses an item and they can be hard to find) My only complaints are in relation to the difficulty curve. I say this because while an RPG does sort of expect one to do some amount of grinding, often you have to go to some pretty far lengths to get the EXP needed to level up and even then  a tough battle can still wipe you out due to the rules of tamer battles not letting you use items (which makes sense, as you can heal/revive with certain monsters all you please) but the real problem comes in when we factor that in each new area the difficulty curve spikes to a level forcing you to grind like mad and at a certain point the EXP gain for the previous area becomes abysmal, forcing you to waste money on items against wild monsters and the item shop doesnt appear to get stronger healing items making it somewhat difficult to get a good handle on progressing unless you are that determined to waste hours training against significantly less EXP yield than what you actually need.Overall I give it a 8/10. If the developers can rectify the issue of how grindy the game is I might rate it higher but for all I know I could be just asking for too much.

_childDocuments_.review: There are a number of games which claim to be Pokemon adjacent or somehow threaten to usurp the Pokemon throne- we all know them! Temtem, Yokai watch, they all generally get tripped up on one or more fronts that really fail to capture what it is that truly makes Pokemon such a beloved franchise! It's not necessarily some epic world-saving quest, it's not necessarily just collecting monsters, it's not necessarily the cute designs- it's a game that somehow manages to be simple to understand but surprisingly deep in the mechanics and capacity for creativity, it's a game that manages to be straightforward but full of mysteries, it's a game that rewards you for however you decide you want to play it. As someone who grew up with Pokemon since I was a kid, I've really wanted to find something that catches that same level of amazement and wonder that I felt back then- and finally, I've found one! Monster sanctuary is incredible in every single way I could think to describe it. I'm more of a Pokemon casual, but a great friend of mine does competitive battling and she's blown past my current progress and rants and raves about the game and its balance, its catering to many different play-styles or strategies, and how it remains a really engaging game all the way into the endgame! In fact, she's already plotting a second, or even third play-through- which should be evidence of just how in-depth the mechanics are for this game!Important to note however, is that these many mechanics are expertly introduced, a slow trickle of complexity that actively gets used and expanded upon over time, without ever becoming too much at once! Unlike Pokemon, as well, the game itself is designed from the ground up to teach you about these mechanics and to encourage you to use them- so what seems like a vast array of potential avenues to explore always feels just one step removed from what you just got comfortable doing- and that slow trickle of interesting, engaging ways to play the game continues well into the end-game!Another incredible thing to note is that none of the Mons end up getting outclassed- no arbitrary tier system because some Mons are just statistically so much better than others- it does a really, really good job of giving a huge variety of valid strategies and making every Monster good in their own way, even the humble monsters you start off with! The sheer diversity of monsters composing the highest ranking teams for the online battling (That's right, online competitive multiplayer!) is baffling to the extreme- and mind you this isn't just because nobody knows what they're doing, these are the truly competitive teams that have fought their way to the top.I feel like I could go on and on, but this is already an extremely long review, so for the sake of brevity! Play it, it's incredible, the graphics are cute, the monsters are amazing, the battling is so well paced and balanced that it boggles the mind, the mechanics are incredibly fun, the story even goes crazy places, this is just some of the most fun I've had with a game in a long time and I simply couldn't recommend it more. Worth every penny!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great, although it took a while to really show it. Combat and mechanics are all awesome, with slight nitpicks here and there. No persistent health and not being allowed to switch monsters mid-fight makes having 6 of them somewhat redundant, at least until the game gets hard enough where you have to start abusing type advantages hardcore. These issues don't apply to the master-vs-master battles, though, which are great.The skill trees are awesome in general. Not much else to be said there.I said the game is great, but it took a while to show it. I said this because the game has a lot of issues that oddly get better or stop appearing later on into the game. For one, the aesthetics and level design at the start of the game are pretty poor. Enemies that don't particularly follow or attack you at all, so you can run right past them. Treasure chests strewn about haphazardly. The layout of the level doesn't really make for interesting platform challenges, and there aren't many puzzles or anything to keep you busy. I understand the reason for some of this. You have 6 monsters with 4 equip slots each, so there has to be a boatload of equipment right off the start to fill those slots. That said, it would greatly serve the game to give context to all those items: receive them through puzzles, receive 'starter kits' from an npc, change the sprites to something other than just chests (big red gemstone for red gems, etc.), maybe have some monsters come pre-equipped with an item or two, etc.The start of the game needs a lot of work, and honestly it really gives the wrong impression. Later on chests start appearing mostly behind platforming challenges, puzzles, hidden walls, or unavoidable enemies, and they really don't spam them the way they do at the start.The visuals of the levels later on also improve immensely. It seems like the further you get in the game, the better the levels start looking. The enemies still have fairly passive ai, which I'm not a huge fan of, but they at least start putting them in positions where they're difficult to avoid.Here's a couple more gameplay nitpicks: the player character's physics are honestly pretty bizarre. You rocket up when you jump and can turn instantly, but your max horizontal speed is kind of low, which feels really weird. I also wish there were more applications for the monster overworld skills, and also wish they would be more responsive to use (imagine enemy shoots attack at you, you dodge, then use your monster skill to hit the enemy and get to start the fight with some kind of bonus.)Ultimately the game is more rpg than metroidvania, so it's not the biggest deal in the world, but at the moment the metroidvania half of the game could use a bit of work.The final big issue I have with the game is the music. Similar to the level design, it generally improves over the course of the game. The music in the first couple areas as well as the battle theme are honestly just not very good. I'm not sure if it's the instruments or the mixing, but it's pretty rough. From around the 3rd area or so and onwards, the area music becomes far more bearable. The music in the snow area in particular is fantastic. I don't know what the difference was, but the snow area really nailed it.Main thing is the game could really use different battle themes based on the area. There's only 1 battle theme for the entire game, besides boss fights as far as I can tell, and it gets old pretty quickly. If there were different themes for each area, that would be perfect.It may seem like I'm really bashing on the game, but I actually really do like it. It kind of nails the 'Pokemon, but with skill-trees and also it's 3v3' idea. It just has some work to be done in the aesthetics and metroidvania department. The story isn't anything to write home about, but people don't really play these types of games for the story anyway.I'm just nitpicking it pretty hard since it's early access and all this stuff has a chance to get fixed. I think the game really does have a lot of potential, and that it could be something truly special when it's finished. Even if you want to wait on it a bit, it's definitely worth your time. Good game.

_childDocuments_.review: The map progression in the game is somewhat linear. You can explore zones outside the main story to an extent, but as the story advances, new zones with new monsters become available. Each monster has a special skill that can be used outside of combat, such as gliding, breaking blocks, and more.These skills are used to solve the game's puzzles, which are generally quite simple. They also allow you to reach certain areas through platforming. However, platforming isn’t the main focus of the game, as the jumps aren't pixel-perfect or difficult, and there are no hard platforming puzzles.The zones and monsters are beautifully designed, and the monsters are quite unique—you'll likely end up with some personal favorites. Each monster has a unique combination of passive and combat skills, which you unlock as they level up. Some skills are shared between monsters, but since the combination of abilities is different for each one, every monster remains useful in various situations, even if they share some skills with others. Monsters' abilities often revolve around specific themes, such as debuffing, buffing, or dealing damage.The combat is the best part of the game. Damage-dealing attacks are divided between physical and magical types, and each falls into one of five elemental categories. In addition, some attacks come with secondary effects, like buffs or debuffs. The buff/debuff system is extensive and becomes increasingly important as the game progresses.Combat is 3v3, but your team consists of six monsters, allowing you to build a team of your favorites or monsters that complement specific combat strategies, such as a debuff-focused team or a buff-heavy team. This system allows for deep strategy, with a lot of variety and viable setups.Regular enemy encounters are fast-paced and not particularly difficult, but battles against other characters with their own teams of six monsters are much more challenging. There's also an online mode where you can challenge other players.The story isn’t very deep, with a simple "good vs. evil" narrative.In summary, if you enjoy monster-taming, building synergies and strategies in combat, and customization with a bit of challenge, I would recommend this game. However, if you're looking for a deep story or challenging platforming elements, this game may not be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing fun for anyone who likes pokemon or Dragon Warrior Monsters from back in the day. However, it does need a little work. The power curve never feels quite right, so you have to grind a lot to get up to the next tier of abilities (I set a macro to autocomplete battles and set the speed to x4 in cheat engine and it still took 1.5 hours to go from level 25 to 30) A lot of the abilities feel like copies of each other with a different coat of paint.[Abilities]The abilities boil down to:-Do damage (usually one big finishing move or a multi attack chip damage)- Damage over time (fire, poison, chill effects. All pretty much the same)-Heal-Shield (adds a second health bar)-Buffs and debuffs (just change percents on damage or chance to hit)[Combat]The combat is super fun to start out, but once you get into it, you'll realize the best way to win battles is just stacking damage over time effects while healing your own monsters. Damage dealing moves are still relevant, but just don't pack a punch. They usually do (with buffs) about 20-40% of a normal enemy's health and you don't get that same anticipation and reward as say a 3x sword danced pokemon one shotting anything in its path (which I feel is pretty comparable.) [Story]There definitely is a story and it's similar in quality if not better than old monster fighting rpgs like pokemon or DWM. [Final Thoughts]This game is fun. It is very fun for the first several hours, but it desperately needs more variety. Everything begins to feel the same and you find yourself mindlessly completing encounters or skipping them all together. Definitely give it a try if you like similar games.[Note to the Devs]Please, please, please add breeding mechanics to this game. They would make collecting monsters so much more fun, especially if there were powerful monsters you could only obtain through breeding. An online breeding feature would be even more fun.

_childDocuments_.review: i absolutely adore this game and everything about itexcellent visual style, monster mechanics that make you have to think about how to build your team and large build diversity for each monster.also one of the few games i've played where damage over time effects have felt Goodcan't recommend it enough

_childDocuments_.review: This is everything I love about pokemon with the fat stripped away. Allow me to just list what I like about it:- New monsters are introduced constantly.- Each monster has multiple skill trees.- There's a hard level cap for every monster , normally reachable by the final boss.- Instead of many elements to track, there's only 4 elements (fire,water,earth,wind) and neutral attacks- There's physical vs magical attacks (in each of the 5 element types), but a single defense stat; there are magic-focused tanks that can heal- Monster evolution is present, but underplayed to the point where you can beat the game without it- Hatching new monsters immediately sets their level to roughly the average level of your current party- You can respec any monster's skill tree if you make a mistake- EVERY monster has a field ability for navigating the environment; flying, lighting up dark areas, activating switches. There's a bit of overlap, but the fact that no matter what your favorite monster is, it can be used in the overworld brings out the kid in me- Combat is based more on your understanding of what each monster can do, rather than just putting out the right monster. You can have one of the best monsters in the game, but dumping skill points into revival skills instead of a special attack can be the difference between winning or losing a battle. - One of the monsters is basically , and another one is basically . If you like Pokemon and Metroidvanias, this could be the game for you. Look up some gameplay first, the tutorial does a pretty good job of establishing what's to come. Plot isn't super important or noteworthy, plays it fairly safe - not bad though. As a heads up, there's a MASSIVE difficulty spike near the end of the game that a lot of people apparently got hung up on, it really demands you understand the mechanics and have been leveling up equipment. Devs are super responsive and polite, if there's something you don't like, don't be afraid to give them a shout on Discord or something.

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Sanctuary is been a very unique take on the monster collector genre.The metroidvania aspect with platforming and exploration gives it a bit of that hunting feel, looking for new frontiers and monsters to add to your own ranks.Combat being fully 3 vs 3 all the way through not only adds a lot of combinations but the skilltrees each monster has also means the specializations really feeds into it, giving things a lot more depth and complexity which I personally tend to look for in the genre.For those interested there is also PVP, though I have not tested that personally.If you enjoy exploring a beautiful world and more complexity in combat this game is an absolute steal at any price.

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid turn-based battle system, monsters are varied and interesting, and more importantly, late-game monsters are not automatically stronger than the monsters you found early on; that's not just "you CAN beat the game with a butterfree and a raticate, but it's a dumb idea", that's "You can genuinely make solid endgame teams with early-game monsters".Out-of-battle RNG can be compensated for and overcome; there is no RNG in monster stat distribution, and no items are RNG-only or wholly-missable thanks to various systems in place.Story is forgettable but doesn't get in the way of gameplay and isn't bad.Map exploration is good, use of monsters as metroidvania exploration powers is a fun quirk.Looking forward to NG+ mode soon to be implemented, which will allow you to replay with your full monster collection from lv1, on a higher difficulty. Edit: NG+ mode is as good as expected.Not just a good game, but a game where the devs have put in various anti-frustration features without making the game too easy or exploitable. Solid recommendation if it looks like your kind of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a LOT OF FUN, but definitely not for the casual gamer even with the "casual" mode option. Once you get about half-way through the game it really pushes you to make proper builds and take the time to understand all the synergies between the monsters. That alone kind of pushes things a bit above casual game-play, then near end-game the difficulty imo gets BROKEN. There is a lot of creative stacks you have to do to actually BEAT the game, this isn't like an optional boss or anything, the last two to three bosses and even leading up to the final boss get exceptionally difficult for the average gamer. I had a lot of fun, but to me it kind of ruined the experience. Game plays basically like a metroidvania game, but you have monsters you collect up and fight other monsters in turn-based combat. The game itself is fun, learning curve majorly ramps up though. Lots of fun optional things you can do. Biggest gripe I think I have with this game is the weird imbalance towards end-game, and the annoyance of getting 100% of achievements requires a lot of tweaking of builds. If you're an achievement seeker though, 100%'ing this game will be REALLY satisfying.In short, worthwhile on sale but be ready for a brutal experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I try to keep abrest of various Pokemon-Alikes on Steam, as a fan of the genre, and that's how I got recommended this one by a friend. This game... I don't know if I'd agree with calling it a Pokemon-alike exactly, but I do like it, and I like it a lot, and I think that willingness to be its own thing with its own identity is a big part of why I like it a lot.The Turn-based combat system seems solid, I'm looking forward to it really kicking my ass as the game does on, because it looks like it's gonna get ready to, and I like the abilities to customise my monsters. I like the idea of having actual builds for my monsters, that's not something I've really seen from the genre, and it's interesting, though this system I do feel like I'm dreading screwing it up more than I'm excited to make something synergistic and fun, but hopefully that's just the early levels where I have fewer choices.I was also not expecting to enjoy the Metroidvania world design as much as I am, but it's neat, and I like exploring for secrets and loot and monsters, and I feel like the best endorsement I can give this game is that in typing that, I just realized a spot on the map where I think I can go back now and find a rare monster to add to my team, and now I'm totally gonna go do that.Game is good, and this being steam, you'll get an opportunity to buy it for cheap.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. It may not be perfect, but it's extremely well done. Growing up, two of my favorite games were Super Metroid and the original Pokemon; this is a beautiful marriage of both of those and well worth playing.The combat system is surprisingly robust and the game will definitely challenge you at times. Getting wiped by a boss later on in the game can be a real bummer, as these battles with other trainers get to be very long. But it is so rewarding to come back with a better strategy/lineup and take them down. Really love the battle system here, it's the highlight of the game for sure.The Metroidvania aspect is also pretty well fleshed out. It isn't full on Super Metroid level of exploration(of course,) but it's fun to get the power-up to finally unlock a new area. The idea of your pets giving you these abilities is awesome too and it does call to mind both Pokemon and even Golden Sun as well as the aforementioned Super Metroid. Graphics are great, the game has a lot of charm. I love the visual designs of the levels and areas and most of the monsters also look awesome. The story is respectable and does at least give a fresh take on the formula. It isn't overly dialogue heavy like some similar games tend to be, but there's enough story there to keep you on track and engaged.It isn't perfect though and there are some faults, but I consider them all to be pretty minor. It took me a while to get used to the floaty controls. But the platforming here is pretty tame and you do adapt to it just fine. But there was definitely a period where I had to adjust to it. And while the story is fine, it's certainly a weaker point of the game. But outside of these two things, I can't really complain.With all that said, highly recommend this game and I think if you are the type of person(like me) who sees a preview/trailer for this game and thinks that it looks up their alley. You should totally get it, I feel pretty confident that you will enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I was so inebriated when I wrote the last review I decided to rewrite it into something comprehensible.This is hands down the best monster catcher game.Every single monster from start to finish serves a unique purpose in combat, there's no monster that's functionally worthless until it evolves and you don't find another monster later that invalidates one you've been using for a while. Rather you will find a monster who trades off a couple of good passives or attacks for a few others and it's all set up specifically so that there's always a scenario where your best choice is your favourite or that a particular support can make a monster that otherwise seems bad into the best for a few particular fights.Combat is actually fun, it's strategy team based combat where you don't win by just playing rock paper scissors which is refreshing for the genre, bosses and rival trainers will regularly flatten your team not because you aren't high enough level or you didn't get the right element on your monster but because they have a strategy that forces a swap. The first rival trainer fight that beat me was spamming buff removal attacks and I was trying to stack defensive buffs at the time.The game regularly rewards you with cool ♥♥♥♥ that changes how you evaluate your monsters for combat. After the first third or so of the game you unlock "shifting" which is shinies. Except that each monster has 2 shiny variants that are functionally different from the base colors with unique stats and abilities. Also you can change the shiny variants you have so no need to grind endlessly, the spawn rate for them is 1/4 so even if you did want to grind it's bearable. There are others as well I won't mention to avoid spoilers for those who don't want to know everything the game has before starting.The campaign of the game genuinely does last about 30 hours and is a ton of fun start to finish with a story that's actually interesting at times, something I can't say about any other catcher game.The only complaint I can even make is that there's two monster designs I don't like. That's pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome, I can safely say this is the best game I own.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. Reminds me of Paper Mario 64 with more detailed builds.There are a lot of things that I really like about Monster Sanctuary:- The Variety. Monster, skills, items, levels.- The Skills. Each monster had unique talent trees.- The Artwork. Pristine pixelart.- The Adventure abilities. Monster's aren't just for battle. Use them to fly you around, run fast with mount, etc. - The Minimap. Very clear boundaries. Great for the one who wants to be 100% in exploration.- Completionist. I 100% (all monsters tamed, all map discovered). Super satisfying and attainable.- Boss fights. Get ranked based on how you fight the boss. Do well, get a boss monster yourself!- Combat system. More hits in a turn, the more damage is done. First monster hits 6 times? 30% bonus damage for the next attacks that turn.- New monsters. Hatch an egg for a new monster- it's only 2 levels behind your highest. Easy to swap new for old. There are things I am not crazy about.- Grind. Didn't feel it till level 30 (Max is 40). Not a super downfall, worth mentioning.- Overwhelming. Between all the choices- monsters, skills, team comps, and items. Tutorial helped- not all inclusive.- Walls. Your first team won't beat the game. Get new monsters that work. That won't beat the game either.- Progression speed. It felt very slow at times. (finding a new monster with a new ability to help explore- running back to gather what wasn't accessible before). Beat this (100%) in less than 50 hours. Worth the money I grabbed it for on sale. I'd pay full price as well. Had to look up builds about 3/4 of the way through to actually progress. I couldn't use my Wolf, Catzerker, and Tengu the whole game =(

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and solid game that's brought down by a small number of issues.The game progression (as of writing this review) feels very formulaic as you enter a new biome, catch all monsters, defeat the boss, go to next area. I am currently in the fifth or sixth biome and have uncovered half the map. Due to monster variety, and their exploration skills, comes dyslexia as you wander around the world while carrying several pokeboxes worth of monsters with you (while in Pokemon you would find those boxes in the Pokecenter). This freedom is welcome as you always have all skills with you but you slowly realize that it makes menuing needlessly complex. There are options to leave monster behind or at day care but the UI is visible straining because on that screen you do not know which monster has which skills so you go back and forth from main menu to day care deposit. Overworld battles are dmg over everything and you are motivated into doing the monotonous skill rotation combo until the enemies are defeated. For bosses however, you are punished for not building defensively. So either you have specific boss-only monsters that are permanently benched while on overworld, or you build some weird mix-builds which makes the overworld monsters needlessly hard. Exploration is nice and the metroidvania effect is wonderfully settled in but the platforming is made by platforming experts (sometimes we need pixelperfect jumps and hover application for those chests), and the switch puzzles are merciless and not fun. The minimap needs some more QoL like the ability to place markers. It's hard to keep track if a maptile is fully explored or waiting for a specific monster's exploration ability. Lastly, if your monster is not part of the 6-unit team, they do not earn exp. But only 3 of them are constantly fighting while the other 3 are benched, that's why it's uncommon to really care for equipment for inactive monsters outside of squad battles (6v6, very rare occurence). It becomes apparent that from the vast roster of available monsters, you never actually have a need to switch and just try them out. They need to be skill levelled and they also require equipment, and if you split your exp on too many units, you will be forced to grind to make up for it. Remember specific pokemon from the first generations, the one that you only carry around because they learned HMs? Monster Sanctuary embraced this mindset.In the end, this game feels nice to play and there is always a small excitement of getting new eggs, checking their skill trees and also their exploration skill. Although transparency in regard to monster roster is not well thought out, this game is definitely worth it if you ever see it on discount.

_childDocuments_.review: ep combat system where you have fairly standard stuff like weaknesses and resistances, various attack elements (like fire, air...), attack types (physical, magical), and debuffs (like weakness or poison), but all of this is then juggled on top of a combo system where each hit adds to the next hits effectiveness. There are some Metroidvania elements present; when you collect monsters they can be "equipped" to follow you and each one gives you an extra power like 'break through walls', 'glide', 'burn vines', etc. that allow you to progress to other areas. The world feels large and the zones feel unique. The story is pretty basic and the dialog is weak, but it keeps everything moving along nicely while giving me a reason to catch 'em all. My only gripe is the imbalance of 3-4 of the encounters; they are WAY harder than the rest of the game and end up making the final boss look like a pushover.

_childDocuments_.review: Intro and Combat: I've spent a lot of time playing this game. Far more than I originally thought I would upon first purchasing it. If you're looking for a breath of fresh air to the monster taming genre then right here is where you can get it. As a big fan of the genre itself I've found myself quite disheartened that so many monster taming games tend to take so much inspiration from Pokemon when it comes to the combat Well rest assured, this game feels unique when it comes to it's combat. Bosses and other big fights feel decently challenging, but not unfair. Also while it is indeed turn based their is a big emphasis on team building since you fight with 3 monsters at a time. It is extremely enjoyable if you like to look through skill trees (Each monster has them with 3 or more trees) and see what builds you can make for a monster that may compliment others. Monster collection and grading system: Monsters themselves are collected via eggs awarded through the grading system after battle. It's fun tightening up your team comp so you can aim for higher grades for collection of more materials and eggs. Oh and did I mention that any egg you hatch is only a few levels behind your highest level? This saves so much time on grind and lets you focus more on team combinations. My only nitpick with the grading system is the execution rating. It's not always clear why it sometimes turns out low. You can stomp through a fight and still end up with a low execution rating and be left scratching your head as to what the game wishes you to do.World and platforming: As for the world layout itself, if you are familiar with metroidvania style then you got a good idea of how the world is laid out. Monsters come with abilities that you can use in the overworld that will let you access areas you previously couldn't get to. It is fun going back to previously inaccessible areas and possibly finding new monsters or a new boss. However often times double back to an area I couldn't get access to and end up with a piece a gear I had already collected at some point. The platforming itself can feel a little finicky in my experience, but I should state I played this mostly on keyboard. Lots of backtracking can eventually wear your patience admittedly a little thin, and unfortunately when you back track through areas it's not going to necessarily surprise you with something new. If there is ever a sequel I think this area of the game can be improved quite a bit. One way could be by making weather patterns for certain areas and making monsters appear that normally don't when certain weather conditions are present, giving the player some level of excitement when it comes to backtracking and running into something new possibly.STORY: Story in this was unfortunately for me, largely forgettable. It's not a point of contention however. I enjoyed myself immensely just playing the game and was happy that I didn't have massive amounts of plot dumped on me. ART/Art direction: I'll say this first. The pixel art in this game is pretty clean and on point. Only a couple monsters would I consider to look rough in this department. However monster design is a bit all over the place. In fact it was the one thing that nearly made me skip buying this game and really missing out on a good time. You have monsters like Targoat and Shocktrooper that look great, and absolutely look like they belong to the same game.  They look unique enough you could remember what game they came from if you seen them a few years later, but then you have monsters like Akhlut (Slap some legs on a killer whale.) Catzerker (Cat with boots and a sword.) and Specter (Spooky flaming skeletons) that are very uninspired. My problem with these is they are generic and thus forgettable to the point where I had to pull them up on the wiki to remember the names of them. Some monsters like the Promethean don't even look like they belong with how jarring they contrast to some of the others. I hope this area improves a good bit if there is ever a sequel.TLDR; If you like monster taming games with a dash of metroidvania, and an emphasis on team building with skill allocation, that's not afraid to be different from others in it's genre then get this game. 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice blend of monster trainer and metroidvania, with a pinch of puzzles. The story plot is fairly predictable and main caracters like charisma, but the game is great regardless.It almost does Pokemon better than Pokemon itself. You can really build great synergies within teams, and have separate teams ready to fight,Fans of Min-Maxing will have a blast. Fans of cheese mechanics will have tons of fun (looking at you Brutus).People that mention hitting a difficulty wall towards the end game are tpically people that didnt think their comp thru and just made do with whatever they had. While you can breeze thru most of the game with about any set of monster, the last few challenges (the Alchemists, the Mad Lord and the Spectrals) will require to work your comp up a little. Overall I highly recommend it. At a normal pace, it took me about 40h to complete, which (to me) makes it a bargain even at full retail (20$).Then of course you can redo other "fun runs" (blobs only, birds only, goblins only, etc) and even get in on the PvP action for more challenges. _childDocuments_.review: I hated Pokemon for a lot of reasons, I also loved Pokemon for a lot of reasons. This game has so many unique and wonderful aspects that make it the best of any monster capture game I've ever played.So much to explore, so much to learn, and not a moment of it feels like work. It's just the desire to keep going and keep growing. Every new zone an amazing surprise of discovery. Every new ability unlocking even more fun and possibilities. The story has amazing flow. Monsters have skills trees, equipment, passives, exploration abilities, and an enormous amount of configurations that are just fun to play with.Monster aren't caught, but hatched, and they hatch only a couple levels under your highest level monster, so there's no having to grind up your monsters or teams. There are cheap consumables for leveling any monster that's a bit behind.Then there's the team saver, saves skills, loadouts, and everything. You can have SO MANY TEAMS. It just makes it so easy to switch to a different teams for different challenges.This game is so incredibly worth the money and the time, Having beat the storyline over 80 hours, I'd love to see this game grow even more, there's quite a bit of endgame, but I can see where it'll peter off once I complete the things I want to complete.There's also PvP, which could add more endgame, but PvP isn't my cup of tea.

_childDocuments_.review: This is great pokemonesqe, 2-d ,side-scrolling, plat former! I bought this for my 70 year old dad as it looked like something he could learn with ease and he would enjoy it and he did. He currently has 163 hours on record and has beaten most the game. When I saw how much he liked it I bought it too!! The controls are intuitive and easy to master the battles are engaging and require thought and strategy to beat. The difficulty scaling is steep  so be prepared but if my 70 year old Dad can do it i'm sure you can too.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best games I've ever played, and probably the best monster-catching game you'll find in the genre, let alone Steam. The games simplistic style and comparatively small monster count (111 at the time of writing this) betray it's complex but fun leveling and skill system. Because of this, the game can be VERY challenging, especially once you hit late game where if you don't know what you're doing you'll get your butt kicked by just about anything you bump into. However, this game does an excellent job of easing you into the different mechanics of the game, and by the time you reach the third or fourth area you should have a good grasp of how the game works if you have good reading comprehension, unlike me.        Now since this game is difficult, I've put a mini-guide below if you want it. However, if you do not, then all you'll need to take from me is that this game is VERY much worth $20 and I cannot recommend it enough, it's a good 30 hours of fun and I think most people will enjoy it, including you.        Each monster has its strengths, weaknesses, and one to three areas of profession; healer, support, tank, buffer, debuffer, and of course the magic/physical DPS, and its your job to balance them out and create teams that synergize with each other based on their passives, abilities, stats. And the cherry on top? If you ever make a mistake and put a skill point somewhere that you don't want that messes up your strategy, the game has you covered by giving you access to infinite skill reset items VERY early on in the game at the stronghold shop at the cost of a handful of gold, meaning if you wanted you could just mix and match skills till you can come up with an unstoppable monster child of death and destruction that even the gods themselves fear.        This game is VERY akin to Metroid in its platforming, and different monsters have different explore abilities. You'll want to keep tabs on which monster does what as the game doesn't tell you on their status screen, it only tells you when you try to switch your active explore monster. (A + D on Keyboard, L + R on Xbox controller) Another thing about exploring: The map. Or more specifically, the marker tool for that map (Spacebar for PC, A for controller) which allows you to keep notes on things you find but don't have access to, like elemental switches and unbreakable walls. If this was explained in game, then I either missed an NPC I didn't talk to or I wasn't paying attention in one of the cutscenes dialogues, which is unlikely but I've done dumber things. Its very important you keep tabs because these inaccessible spots lead to optional bosses, unique equipment, and items that can 'permanently' buff your monsters like rare food, or items that actually permanently upgrade your monsters like skill potions.        And that's it! Thanks for reading, and I hope this review was helpful in one way or another. Happy hunting!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game, it just isn't for me. THE GOOD: + Very good and likeable pixel graphics. + Relaxing soundtrack. + Wolf as a starter. + Lots of different critters to get later in the game. + Platforming is very easy. + If you customize the controls right, you can play with just one hand. + Your character can be male or female. + Turn based combat. + Progress seamlessly transfers from the demo to the full game and I encountered no bugs in the process. + Monsters have abilities to help you explore or beat simplistic puzzles and it's easy to switch between them on the fly. + You get monster eggs as part of the loot system (which itself is a big minus form me), so you don't need do it with some catching mechanic like Pokemon where the creatures need to have some health left for you to catch it. + The game has a demo you can try for free - given I jumped the gun and bought the full game before seeing how repetitive it was, I'd advise you to take your time with the demo. + Whenever you hatch a new monster, it will have the same level as the weakest of your existing monsters and will receive the appropriate amount of skill points right of the bat. THE BAD: - The demo does not reflect the final game because it uses an old build of the game - e.g. the final game will correctly display buttons you've reassigned to say changing the monster traveling with you, but the demo will only display the default controls regardless of how you've customized the controls and skills at the end of the monsters' skill trees won't be shown in the demo. - Very repetitive terrain - I didn't have the patience to reach a new area. - Lack of enemy variety and battles that grow boring and stale (in the first area at least, you'll quickly feel like you've seen every foe there is and then the battles begin to drag and not longer feel interesting). - Likeable, but very simplistic story. - Monsters don't evolve (a few do according to the Journal PDF - DLC). - Weird loot system: each battle can be ranked from 1 to 5 stars, but the ranking feels arbitrary and doesn't encourage strategic combat, you are given a % for what you'll get based on this arbitrary score (e.g. 30% chance to get a rare item). - There might be crafting of some kind in the game, but while I got plenty of items that seemed like they had something to do with crafting, the game never told me what the crafting is like or what does it do. - The tutorial is there, but it doesn't tell you anything beyond very basic and intuitive mechanics, but it doesn't offer insight into any complexity the game might offer later (and I'm too bored by the repetitive elements to keep playing and find out on my own in some distant area of the game). - Lots of features are there, but you'll find out about them in the forum and not the game itself - e.g. supposedly you can sell monsters you don't need somewhere, but it's in some distant area. - You can't use numbers in monster names and if you have 2 monsters of the same species you won't be able to tell which is which. - When managing equipment, you don't see the stats you should - e.g. when you pick what you'll feed a monster you can only see what you've already fed it and what you can still give it, but not its stats, you'll only see that under the "Equipment" tab. - How equipment is structured is weird: your monster can equip 1 weapon, 3 accessories (mage items or armor to improve various stats) and 3 items you can feed it - it would make more sense for feeding to be consumable items and you could feed any monster any feeding item as many times as you'd like. - Monsters' skills upgrading makes you feel like you're thrown in without an adequate explanation. E.g. increasing attack by one increases you damage by what? A fixed amount a percentage? It isn't stated anywhere. - Given the loot system, the game can feel grindy in terms of loot and getting new monster eggs. FINAL VERDICT: The game might appeal to some people, but it quickly became too repetitive for me despite its initial charm and since I've only played for an hour I've refunded the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The battle mechanics are really fun and the leveling and means of obtaining new monsters allow for experimentation with different strategies, which really escalates as the game goes along. Strategies that work against some teams and monsters do not work against others, and the game promotes trying new things because penalties for losses are almost nonexistent. The exploration and platforming aspects of the game aren't the most fun in my opinion, since the story is somewhat basic, which makes the world building lacking in immersion. But the story does what it needs to and makes a world for you to play around with. The pixel art is genuinely incredible, which makes the backgrounds and battle animations pleasant to look at too. The soundtrack is pretty nice and gets a bop going but nothing special to me. Overall, Monster Sanctuary is a really fun game with great replayability value if you like turn-based strategy similar to Final Fantasy and Pokemon.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? Not yet, but certainly on it's way to become one when it is finished. You get a platformer combined with strategic turn-based combat.Explore the captivating fantasy land, find treasure in chests, meet cute monsters, and kill them in turn based 3v3 combat. Actually, you let your monsters (familiars) do the fighting, you just stand behind and watch. Nice job, being a Monster Keeper.You play an aspiring Monster Keeper and are sent on the Keepers' Trail to advance your training with Old Buran. Soon you discover something that needs a real hero to solve, though...The platformer starts not too difficult, the jumps are easy, the puzzles simple. It gets more difficult later on, when a simple jump is not enough anymore and you have to use the powers of your familiars to overcome obstacles, like tearing down a thorn bush or shattering a stone wall. Took me some time to find out that the block building ability of my first familiar was useful to reach higher platforms... When you die during platforming, you are just reset to the same screen.When you find monster eggs, you can hatch them and add them to your party. Greets from Pokemon! Adding them is only a first step, though, you have to name, feed, equip and train them. And then you let them fight for you. The upgrade tree of each monster is rather unique and mildly complex, there are different skills you can unlock and upgrade. Use your collected weapons & items to improve your familiars... although it is a bit strange to equip a dog with an axe or a blob with a bandana...The strategic combat is the heart of the gameplay. You choose 3 familiars that will fight for you, giving orders to them jRPG-style. They can use the skills you have unlocked for them before, cast buffs & debuffs and chain combos to enhance efficiency. Every monster has certain weaknesses and invulnerabilities, so you should think about how to attack them. Your party starts every fight fully healed.Enjoy the wonderful pixel art while listining to the relaxing soundtrack and playing the game via gamepad. Can't wait to see this game finished!Collect monsters and let them fight for you in turn-based combat while exploring a world in classic platformer style.

_childDocuments_.review: 9.5/10, super satisfying and highly recommended for RPG lovers.Someone amazing introduced me to the game and asked if they could watch me play. We said we'd play for an hour so I could get a taste of it and then we'd move on to something else. I got hooked right off the bat and played for 7 hours straight. The other person stayed up way later than they should've in order to continue watching. They told me I could continue playing on my own as long as I shared about my progress with them every now and then. One week later, after 58 hours (with some AFK time), I've 100% completed the game along with all the steam achievements. The only 0.5 point deduction is for slightly lackluster background art, somewhat uninteresting story writing, and inconsistent music quality (most of it is pretty good, a few tracks are amazing, and some just sound like a Casio keyboard backing track), but honestly these barely even matter in the grand scheme of things. The aspects that truly matter to me were done phenomenally in my opinion: The variety of monsters is impressive, everything (from monsters to items) feels very well balanced, the game feels constantly rewarding, the world map is a joy to explore and clear over time, and the difficulty progression feels just right throughout the entire game - never too boring, never frustratingly impossible.My hat is off to the developers.

_childDocuments_.review: Well then! I don't usually write reviews. But this game is so incredibly *vexing* in what it could be but veers away from that the frustration pretty much forces me to!Monster Sanctuary is a game about Metroidvania-ing around raising Pokeymans in all but name. They're strong\weak to different things and each creature has 3-5 skill trees it can invest in so you can tailor a party to your liking. Sounds neat?! It kind of is. At  first.Unfortunately, the game 24\7 scales enemies to your level. As soon as you enter a new screen, it locks that screen in to what it was when you entered : Those LV 7 enemies will always be LV 7, and so forth. This is okay for backtracking but a nightmare for feeling any sort of accomplishment when the challenge is constant. Which is a lie, it's worse as you play more. Early on you aren't expected to pinpoint-build monsters perfectly, but later on you absolutely are.So the main problem with this game comes from this scaling. You can't just train a bit and get past a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fight - of which the last 5-15% is *full* of - and handle a fight as it deserves to be handled ,with brute force and contempt. No, you take your strongest creatures in, your max leveled, well equipped ones and you watch as 1, maybe 2 enemies attack and *delete* one of yours without any chance to interfere in a meaningful way. Neat, so in a "Keeper" (Trainer) battle, you're permanently down one creature. Lovely :-\.Oh but don't worry, your entire team is likely to get deleted too because it isn't set up so you can *figure out* what to do. Oh no no no it's heavy-duty trial and error. If, like me, you are faced with a brick wall at max level, there is no dealing with that. You look at your other, lower levelled creatures and realize "Well ♥♥♥♥, I have to raise these guys over 1-3+ hours to MAYBE get past this *one* opponent".And yes you do. Yes. You. Do.This doesn't even mention the individual insufferability of some opponents like the Stolby - an owl on long Flamingo legs who looks at a 20% health bar ally (IE, enemy) and not only heals is harshly up to around 75% , but also applies a shield (bonus health, essentially) of 25-45% in value. On top of the health the monster just got back.  Leveling is slow and tedious, as only the 6 "main team" creatures get exp. I am literally sitting on over 50 other ones that gain precisely 0 exp as they aren't in that six person main team. So when the game thinks it's being smart and encourages strategy, it encourages trial-and-error, padding, and luck-based gameplay by forcing you to not proceed even harder, but to do go back and spend your time on these creatures. MAYBE These will work?I have to stress one thing though. The game *starts* amazingly. It's really fun and enjoyable, and that joy lasts at least 12 hours, 18-24 properly until you get to where I am (5th Sanctuary Token Keeper Duel :-\) Training itself is handled oddly - enemies only respawn after you've fought 2 (3?) other enemies *after* the group you want to respawn. Or you can buy\find and use instant respawn items. From a menu that gets really bulky once you have FOUR PAGES worth of monster eggs padding in the way :-P. This is very much a Mass Effect 3 sort of game. Starts with a lot of flare and promise, and the gameplay is *mostly*very solid. But that last little bit just sours it out of nowhere, and so extremely. Expect to play it and like it for the first 80%~ or so and *hate* the last 20% I wish the devs leaned into the skill trees more and the "Let's make it challenging hur hur" a bit less. Like, a *lot* bit less. By the way, Boss enemies called Champions only drop their eggs - so you can play around with them - if you 5 star them. IF you meet the first one at level 5 and can't do it, you can refight them all later in a specific location....and they all scale to your level. *Always*.  So no boss for you unless you construct a team specifically for the enemy you're facing - and good luck with the amount of effort that takes. SEE A PATTERN YET?!At this current point in time, I literally don't have the energy to launch the game ever again. I'm not playing it, I'm certainly not beating it and it's just...really, really irritating. But I have to recommend it anyway because the sheer amount of gameplay before all the bad design decisions hit you - as I said, 12-18 hours avg - is still very good, especially for the price.

_childDocuments_.review: This is actually hard for me to do.  Most of this game is great.  It's Metroid meets Final Fantasy meets Pokemon.  The world is platformer exploration, with monsters that you catch taking the place of most exploration powers that you would normally earn.  Battling with monsters isn't just the end, you get to equip and feed your monsters to boost their abilities.  It all comes together rather nicely... if it followed its own rules.The big downside I've found to this game is that opposing monsters, wild, champion, or owned by another, all exceed what your own monsters can achieve.  Want a tanky monster that can't go down in a single round?  You can build it, but the wild monsters a level lower than yours, with a lower vitality rank, and (theoretically) no equipment will still be healthier than your monster.  Better watch those affinities too.  Monsters gain the ability to damage equal to yours as if they had the appropriate affinity even when it's a neutral damage type.  Pray that they don't actually hit the right affinity.  Even a tanky team will go down in two rounds if they manage that.This isn't just guesswork either.  I've tracked monsters and their growth potential by certain levels and tried to get one of mine to match the opposing ones... they never do.  This seems like a small thing, but it makes typing and synergies an absolute chore to manage, and that's before you take rng into account for how likely are the monsters to crit or miss.  I really wish they just followed their own rules.

_childDocuments_.review: So what's the best way I can describe my experience with Monster Sanctuary overall? I had a blast. Genuinely, I had an extremely fun time with it, picking and choosing the monsters I like and finding fun combinations to pair them together and steamroll through battles in the way I liked doing! So why am I giving this a negative review?Because the developers decided to throw all that fun and creativity completely out the window for the final stretch of the game's story. Now, what exactly do I mean by, 'they threw it away'?Throughout the entirety of the game it never really mattered what monsters I brought to each battle- some fights may be tougher than others because I didn't have a fire elemental monster and some might be easier because I used a lot of water based attacks, etc.; Though those are just examples. No fight was ever 'unwinnable' because I didn't bring the specific monster or the specific synergy that the developers wanted me to have, they were just tougher than average at most. And I had fun with that, because it meant I could keep using MY party, the party of creatures that I had been using for a long time because I liked them, the party I gave nice little names because the names were funny.(Minor Spoilers Ahead)But the final stretch of the game says no to ALL of that. The best example is this- the fight with Eric. This was, without a doubt, the worst fight I had in the whole game. Eric has a lot of tanky monsters that buff alot, shield well, debuff the living daylights out of you, oh and did I mention most of his monsters will just straight up one tap you? Because they will. A lot.This fight felt so poorly designed that I couldn't help but wonder how in the heck it got into the game at all- because I was getting steamrolled despite being OVERLEVELED for the fight. Now, why was this the worst fight for me?Because I chose the Wolf pet instead of the Toad pet. The wolf pet is weak to pretty much everything that Eric throws at you, which means it gets one tapped fairly easily, and the wolf was by far my strongest monster at the time. Not strong enough to one tap or avoid getting one tapped by one of Eric's roided out freak beasts I guess.And that was the most disheartening moment, when I realized that I wasn't allowed to use the one Monster that has been with me for my whole journey, that I used for my entire quest up till that point, because it can't survive the first turn. No other encounter up to that point was able to one shot ANY of my monsters, but suddenly this guy's can? Awful. A very awful final difficulty curve meant for the most hardcore of players for no reason at all.A wonderful journey with a pile of disappointment waiting at the end, with the journey not being worth the heartbreak. Do not buy.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I 100%'d it, and I wish I could play more. A superb 3v3 monster raising game with a good metroidvania tacked on for traversal. Fully recommend, hope they make a sequel.The best way to summarize Monster Sanctuary is to break it into its component parts. It is important to note though, every part of this game is well done. The story you can take or leave, its serviceable, but the amount of love and care put into descriptions of the monsters is enough to make up for it.Metroidvania: The traversal mechanics are simple enough, with the uniqueness of most of your actual unlocks are monsters themselves. Sometimes this does mean you need to get a monster ability to progress, and that requires a few fights, but this is minimal. You do get a double jump, but most of the standard new mechanics are monster based. A monster will break walls, allow a glide, swim, burn vines, etc. The only negative here is I wish you could mark areas, as when finishing things up I would forget where the new ability I got could be used in older areas.Monster Raising: Every monster has a skill tree. It isn't fully unique, a lot of skills are shared between monsters, but the exact layout and amount of abilities differs. There is enough difference and a hard cap on skill points that you could ostensibly build two monsters of the same type differently. In addition, there is gear, some with unique bonuses other than stats, and a later mechanic introduces a choice of two unique bonus options. Some of these are -major- and you build a team around them (Bleed stacks not going away for example, letting you stack up hundreds to slowly murder a defensive monster). Further in addition, if you make a mistake in a build, or want to change things out, there are items to reset skills, level up lower monsters and the like. I never felt like a bad choice locked me out of any potentials, and I could easily reconfigure my team. Lastly, every monster gets 1 of 3 unique 'ultimate' skills, which you can change between fights without an item. All of this adds up to a superb experience making unique teams and trying out new combinations.Combat: The 3v3 style, along with the raising detailed above, means that you have a lot of opportunity for fun combat challenges. Some fights will be against one huge monster that acts multiple times, but often you will be facing a team of three. If it is an opponent trainer, you will 6v6, with three out at a time. Buffs and debuffs are very important, and some monsters are entirely built around healing when buffing, getting free buffs, spreading debuffs, super-stacking them, etc. You also heal to full after every fight, but there is a grading system based on buff/debuffs, rounds taken, damage, how 'efficient' you are that makes you want to do every fight well. The higher the grade, the better chance of getting rare items (including eggs for monsters to raise).In summary, an amazing game, fully worth 100%'ng, and doesn't deserve to be compared to Pokemon. Its better.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I've ever been so pleasantly surprised by a game in the steam discovery queue. It checked all the right boxes for me. If you're a theorycrafter grab this! _childDocuments_.review: the game follows a really advanced story line that keeps you wanting to push and play more. however i find that there are some uneasy areas that might need a slight fix. some of the champions that you come across are a bit over powered and since they get to act twice it makes it a bit hard to attack them and inflict damage of any type whether its direct or indirect (damage taken from an effect) and that makes it difficult even at high levels, your monsters tend to be slightly weaker and many of your attacks and abilities don't really make a dent in there health. i know that they are made to be a challenge and that they are bosses, but could the dev's give a look in to some of or all of the champions attacks and abilities and maybe make them a bit less O.P. and difficult  ??  i'm not asking to make them weaker or less of a boss, but just a slight tweak to make them a bit less impossible to get by and or deal with on a scale. i do love the fact that many of the regular monsters scale with your current monster's level, that makes it fun to be able to improve your current groups levels and abilities. over all the game is great and i see much improvement and add on's in the future and i would recommend it to my friends. please keep in mind that i know that its still early access and there is much being done to add and tweak so i'm just seeing if there is any changes or knowledge of this happening to others during there battles with the champions and bosses. thanks for making a great game and cant wait to see if there will be a M.S.2!!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: This is what I'd always wanted Pokemon to be ever since Red vs Blue.  Very in depth team building, where every monster has its own skill trees, 3v3 regular battles, and 6v6 trainer duels where the combat is quite tactical.  You also don't have to worry about stupid things like EVs forcing you to grind 100s of geodudes.  Respeccing is as simple as using an item, and new monsters are hatched just 2 levels under your max, so it's easy to try new things.  And as the game goes on, and the difficulty ramps up, you'll want to be trying new things.It's also a fun Metroidvania-esque world to explore on top of everything else.  So yeah, fun exploration, strategic combat, and in depth theory crafting with no risk of wasting time and resources on a build idea that doesn't pan out, makes this one highly recommended.  If you've always wanted to like Pokemon, but never really liked Pokemon, check this out.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like turn-based RPG and metroidvania exploration then you'll probably love this game, definitely one of the best indie game that i've played. Finished the main story within around the first 40 hours, got the 100% steam achievements at the 65 hours mark. Gameplay basically revolves around building up your best lineup of monsters while min-maxing their stats and skillpoint distributions for its 3v3 fights. The story is just enough to keep me interested but the unique gameplay is its main charm. The amount of content that this game provides is just worth so much more given its price, when you think game seems like its over you'll just soon realise that there's still a lot more to do, even for the post main story content. I personally dont play RPG games often but this one is definitely an easy 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: at launch it was kind of meh, but as of right now it is *chef's kiss.*Long version:I backed this game on Kickstarter and played it at launch. It was okay, but I got bored after like 20 hours. It wasn't very well balanced yet and overall just wasn't that fun.With the recent release of the Forgotten World DLC, I decided to give it another try. I was quite frankly blown away. The game balance was much improved, but on top of that combat just FELT more fun; it's hard to describe. I was especially impressed by some of the Quality of Life changes, like being able to add markers to the map. Plus the massive amount of new content is impressive.The bottom line is that this is a must-purchase game for any fans of either mon-raising games or metroid-vania games. Even for players who aren't fans of either of those genres, it's still worth picking up if you can get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having a ton of fun with this game. The combination of monster raising with Metroidvania gameplay is excellent and I like how your monster team has an out-of-combat purpose. That alone can make you want to capture new monsters you see (especially on Randomizer mode), even if you have a favorite combat team. The skill trees provide a choice of molding your monster and your team. Most monsters I've come across can be adapted to different roles or at least nudged in certain directions. A monster good at physical attacking might have a bit of healing or magic attack. A tank monster could be a defensive tank or a heal tank, with some support on the side, etc.The battles are animated well as are the monster movements and your character's movements. The story is interesting so far and combat can be rather challenging. Having a built in randomizer is wonderful and throws another interesting wrinkle into the game. Of the extra modes, it's by far my favorite. There is also an online play mode where you can battle other players' monster teams, but I've not fooled around much with that yet. In all a very enjoyable game, especially for the monster trainer gamers out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, i'm sorry for the size of this review. Had a lot to go over :)Aesthetics and Soundtrack:Right off the bat I will say that the landscape and colour-grading of the game is wonderful. They achieved the full fantasia effect that increases the atmosphere surrounding the game very well, also reinforcing the emotion of the story line, going from what seems like a happy adventure game to focusing on the importance of stopping a certain evil force which I won't mention in case of spoilers. The soundtrack does its job emphasising these point miraculously as well. The tracks they have used really fit each area. My only qualm is perhaps the monotony of hearing the battle music over and over after a few hours in, however in the options there is a setting for alternate battle music would helps with this. Just means switching back and forth every now and then.Battle:The feel of the battles can be pretty slow overall. In the first zone it teaches basic combat features quite well, type advantages, status effects, boss battles (champions) and basic functions for players (skills, equipment, etc.). What I found is that the battles will be consistently slow-ish even with the 2x battle speed when you are in an area with an even level with your team. This does help with allowing players to learn the functions of equipment bonus' and buffs. So if you're looking to one hit enemies you'll have to be a bit over levelled or you'll find it happens when backtracking to previous zones. There is a slight difficulty curve once you get to the 15-20 level part of the game. Learning how to stack buffs, and taking out enemies which can de-buff and remove buffs from you first helped in my case. Be sure to study your monsters' skills and find the synergy that helps them. For example, I am still using a green slime from the first zone (i'm around level 25) focusing on unlocking the healing abilities and buffs/de-buffs, equipping it with weapons and armour that improve healing and mana regeneration.Note~ The Battle/ Pvp tower is extremely helpful for getting used to the 6v6 combat. Use it when it becomes available :)Gameplay:The player movement is fluid and easy to grasp for the most part. I found that some of the puzzles or obstacles can be a little confusing when you have no knowledge on required external monster skills (Levitation, Ground Switch Activation, Lighting Dark Rooms, etc.) This can be figured out with progress and hatching new monsters, though in my case I wasted an hour or two total of some of the puzzles. In my opinion having a sign or some dialogue explaining what abilities are necessary for certain obstacles would help players that are casually exploring, not focusing on main progress.Conclusion / Overall Opinion / Suggested ImprovementI love this games tried and true fantasy environment. The concept is nowadays quite overdone, but the developers have managed to make it feel refreshing by using very familiar combat systems and puzzles to many who have played games like pokemon, final fantasy, KoH, etc. I feel that giving some visual guidance to players would not be a bad idea. I like the concept of talking to your familiar as a form of a vague quest log and doesn't leave much to be desired in that department. The puzzles need some direction in my opinion, or something to give an indication of the prerequisites.Overall... I love the game and the direction it's heading in. The challenge of the game is satisfying, not being difficult enough to rage quit when you lose a 20 minute battle (They can go for that long if you are as bad as me). Some tweaks in guiding the player and maybe some more information of stats and their importance might be nice.That's my thoughts on the game roughly 13 hours in. Hope this helps anyone window shopping wondering if this is for them. Give it a shot if your not sure.Thanks for reading,Your Average Filthy Casual.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: There have been many Pokémon clones and other creature collector type games over the years, and perhaps because they knew they never stood a chance against the behemoth franchise, they rarely bothered trying their own spin on the genre and predictably vanished soon after their release. on the other hand not only tried, but absolutely succeeded in creating its own unique metroidvania inspired world with many innovative, highly customizable monster systems that offer countless possible strategies and synergies, massive improvements on decades old genre-wide gameplay elements, as well as actually challenging battles for people above the age of 10, all neatly packaged with some classic medieval fantasy aesthetic and awesome soundtrack.Even the loathed HMs were turned into a fun varied explore mechanic.8.2/10
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: I had so much fun playing this game. The way I describe it to my friends is that it's like Pokemon but less grindy & less monotonous. Most battles are varied and engaging, requiring a certain level of strategy (but no guesswork because all the information is displayed right there). The best part is that it is so easy to change your team up at anytime, thanks to the skill trees and the skillpoints you are automatically rewarded based on the time you obtain your new monster. The story and the monsters are cute. The soundtrack is amazing. My only real complaint would be the lack of markers for the map, but if your memory isn't crap (like mine) it shouldn't be that big of an issue.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

The story is kept basic, but what really pushes this game over the edge in terms of enjoyment is the addition of metroidvania-like world exploration.
