_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: This is already something special, a unique mix of turn based team building strategy and platforming build on a foundation of cute monster buddies. If this is all the game they planned to release I still would have been glad of my time with it. _childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: After bouncing off the game early on, I came back and became thoroughly addicted. _childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: It starts out fun and promising but over time becomes mind numbingly tedious. Every battle takes ages to complete, enemies love to full heal or fully replace barriers every turn, and most of the combat boils down to who has the most buffs and debuffs, making the buffs and debuffs themselves feel entirely meaningless beyond trying to stack up as many as possible. Every new area spikes the difficulty in a jarring manner and seems to rely on you getting good RNG to grab the most broken monsters from that zone in order to continue. Worst of all, the big progression points are almost always marked by Keeper Duels, which exemplify every issue with combat that the game has, tenfold. They're truly miserable.It's a shame overall since the art is lovely, the music is very nice and exploring the world/collecting monsters is pretty fun overall, but there's little drive to continue doing so when the game seems dead set on bogging down your progress at every turn.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: One of a kind game, monster collection combined with metroidvania! It is so simple and yet so complex, it lures you in and gets deceptively challenging. Once you get the hang of it, its a lot of fun. The monster sanctuary world, music, characters, story, even inventory management are all nicely done. The depth in combat is simply brilliant. Absolute must buy!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: As an adult and a game designer, it's hard for me to love the original pokemon anymore. It seriously lacks depth even though there's plenty of room for itThis game is like a cure for that.Each monster is like a unique hero with a skill tree to build uponEvery 3v3 battle makes me think about the best team combinationI hope this game can release some kind of paid DLC to expand the game even bigger like pokemon HG/SS and like Monster Hunter did.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Man, what a surprise this game was!Pros: - Incredibly FUN combat system with tons of synergies between monsters- metroidvania with monster taming, very cool and working idea- Huge pool of monsters- evolving the monsters is cool, and has tons of freedoom in the skill-tree of each monsta- Funky little world with secrets that can be found out by switching between escorting monsters- No punishing progression (if u lose a combat, u lose some money, but money is not even an issue in this game)Cons: - There is only one big con: The WALL. The difficulty WALL. So lets start at the beginning: Some good stuff should be addressed, before we delve into examining the problem. First, in Monster Sanctuary EVERY monster can be a LATE GAME monster. That means, even the first little mudcrap can be an endgame warrior, becouse its all about building up your little team, and choosing the best lineups. And thats the thing, i really liked about the game: that i dont have to switch my monsters constantly.......then the endgame came. And suddenly you hit a brick wall. The difficulty went from calm and medium to HELLISH within a minute. The endgame fights simply cannot be fought without abandoning your old team, and mathing out the best monster lineups against every single sideboss fight (and there is about 4-5 at the end). There is a good thing, and a bad one here:The good decision from the dev was that you cannot outlevel endgame bosses to just harvest them blindly. Thats okay and cool, makes the endgame really strategic... HOWEVER! The game is very different at the end, than before... I really enjoyed most of my playtime, i built up my little team, i geared them, it was a really fun time - then they just disappeared within a sec. So... after 30 hours of build up u have to trash ur team, and play with some meta lineup against those bosses. Totally ruined the endgame for me... i lost that sensation which came from achieving a high level with ur heroes and enjoying that power. Here u get frustrated at the end, u doing math with stats, looking for best lineups against X and Y bosses on the forums but definitely not playing the way u did before. Iam so sorry about the endgame, which was a drag, a wall. Anyway, the game is insanely good, i have never seen such a cute wombo-combo synergie monster tamer like this. But be prepared for the endgame, its not friendly.BUT I DEFINITELY RECOMMEND IT TO EVERY SINGLE HUMANOID. If u want to have fun, also a challenge, thats it. Oh... and man, trust me: get over the pixel art... if its not ur thing, that game will work anyway. It has DEPTH.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: It's a bit like pokemon meets a metroidvania a pokemetroidvania as it were.The game shows great potential and very interesting mechanics. _childDocuments_.review: I am still in the process of progression in this game. I think I will have 1 or 2 areas to explore and several to backtrack to. The hours you get for the cost is very good. Not sure about replayability, but there is dueling with other players I read.Pet collector, similar to pokemon, with RNG aspects to getting eggs (you don't just catch things, you get eggs to drop and hatch).Evolution of some monsters is possible, but require certain items used in certain places to happen.Some basic crafting and equipment updating systems. Using the right stat equipment per monster helps a ton.Area exploration, with places unlocked through certain monsters innate abilities.World of Warcraft (vanilla) talent system for each monster to explore. Unique to each monster as well.Party of 3, so you can mix and match for fun and interesting combos.Combat gets more complex as you play. Having a strategy and synergy in your party is key.Only downside is some monsters are completely useless mid to late game. Some monsters you can get right away and use at end game. There are few teleporting stones so sometimes you backtrack a bit.This is really NOT a big deal, and does not take away from how close this game is from being an absolute masterpiece in my humble opinion.

Love the retro SNES graphics, skill trees, combat combos, story, etc.  Alot of work went into the uniqueness of each monster skill tree.  I wouldn't change anything about this game. _childDocuments_.review: I thought I could kill a couple hours here and there. You know play this game when I have some time. _childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this by saying, a game that has drawn me in like this I haven't seen in over half a year. This game feels like everything is thought out. You might ask "Is this a Pokemon competitor?" Far from it, this game surpasses Pokemon games in practically every way possible. This is from someone who is a big fan of Pokemon.If you like monster training and catching games, pick this up. It is worth the full price, and you'll be sucked in so quickly to the extremely customizable creatures. The uniqueness of every creature's build and what they specialize in. I trained for a long time to keep all my monsters the same level. However I had to give up midway through the game, to the point where I was getting so many monsters that customizing them all at that point would be insane. The endgame even has so much thought and care put into it. The tiny things, such as you using a final level party they give you a free level up item for any other monster if you have their xp reach the cap. then allowing them to gain another one. Something that games of all sorts never implemented. This is just such a small example of how much thought and care have gone in this game.This has only been me judging it on a single player game. The game adds even more with competitive multiplayer vs modes. Allowing you to build your own teams with so many customizable options for each monster. I have been more focused on training the monsters for myself, I'm certainly going to need many more copies of each one for different builds. This game looks simple at first glance, but upon playing it you are given more and more customizable options that make the game so much harder to dissect. They are revealed to you in a fair and not overwhelming progression.Seriously, if you like Pokemon, other monster catching games, and you like to "collect them all." Buy this game now, for sale, for full price, it's simply the best monster catching game I've played.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Sanctuary's world is surprisingly large and filled with a lot of things to do and see. I kept getting surprised by how much more was hidden up to the end of the game. The combat is pretty strategic and I appreciate that the outcomes of most actions are predictable so you don't have to leave stuff up to chance. There are also some pretty great monster designs and there are a lot of potential ways to build each monster which can be overwhelming at first but the game is very forgiving in letting you tinker around and try different builds and team comps. The game has some extremely difficult late/post-game challenges for people who get really invested in team building which is also a plus. There is a late game difficulty spike, but I think a lot of other reviews exaggerate how rough it is (outside of ). If you're a fan of monster tamer games I wager you'd really enjoy this one, I know I did.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like:* Metroidvania style side-scrolling exploration games with plenty of backtracking as you unlock new abilities?* Gotta-catch-em-all monster trainers* In-depth multi-branching skill trees for character customization* Team building to maximize synergies in 3v3 combatThen this is THE game for you! Each monster, instead of simply getting skills as they level, or as you collect items to teach them, has their own unique skill tree selection, generally containing 3-4 separate skill trees with passive and active skills that gives each monster the ability to fill multiple roles. Out of combat, you're a side-scrolling Metroidvania game where each monster has their own out-of-combat utility. From lighting obstacles to crushing them to even making them, adding to the number of places you could potentially backtrack to with new abilities to find new stuff. You collect monster eggs to hatch them so you can train them, you get them not by throwing some consumable at them, but by defeating them and having them drop their egg as a Rare drop. But don't worry, the better you do with your combat, the higher the score for that combat, the more likely they are to drop the eggs. And there's a rematch system for Champion (legendary) monsters, so you really *can* catch 'em all in one game. As a criticism, there will be timed platforming puzzles that are pretty silly hard. Some chests I simply gave up on bothering to get, because the controls aren't really responsive enough to justify those tight timings. However, these chests are invariably consumables you can find elsewhere anyway, so missing them isn't a huge loss. One thing I do greatly approve of is how easy it is to swap monsters out. Level Badges increase monster's level by one, to a maximum of one level below the highest level monster you have. In exchange, they're available in unlimited quantities from a vendor. There are also Skill Reset items that are also available in unlimited quantities from vendors. So it is trivial to try out a new monster and see how they work with your heavy hitters. tl;dr: If you like the strategy and tactical depth offered by a team of three, each with multiple skill trees, and you like Metroidvania style exploration with a whole host of movement options you can obtain, and you enjoy games where you can catch 'em all... you need this game in your life.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Just played this at PAX. Had to force myself to put the controller down - I could have sat there for hours playing it. Its...pokemon...crossed with a sidescrolling metroidvania? That doesn't do it justice, though. You go around, fighting monsters in turn based (but fast) gameplay, with opposing elements and various skills you can choose on levelling up.Do good enough and you may get the rare drop of a monster egg, which you can then put that monster in your party (and name it!). Every level, monsters get as point to unlock a skill on a skill tree so you can build your monsters how you want within their skillset. Theres also equipment you can give them that does various things. When youre exploring in sidescrolling mode, you can have a monster follow you (which you can easily switch with LB/RB)- each monster has different skills they can use (IE - flying monsters can give you a levitation boost to reach high up platforms, fire monsters can burn things etc. Its really interesting and unique. The pixel art is great, and so is the music. I love pixel art, so this fits the bill perfectly - kind of that "16 bit with modern DPI look" that can add a lot of character to a game. There's also an awesome bestiary with a detailed large pixel drawing of the monster, in addition to 3 pages of flavor text to provide more lore and background of the gameworld, as well as the monster's stats. My only complaint is its in Early Access - which I normally dont buy. But I wanted to support Monster Sanctuary. I'm hoping it turns into something great, it has amazing potential. I'm not going to play it until its done.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: I was going to pirate this game. I really was. I actually downloaded it. But I played it for about 15 minutes before realizing these guys deserve my money and my time, and so I bought it with no hesitation and I have 0 regrets.This is amazing. Absolutely amazing. The graphics are on point, the monster variety is just right, the writing isn't awful and cringy as is the case in most monster keeping games. You actually get to use most monsters in useful ways, the bosses are a lot of fun, the process of coming up with decent team composition and builds for each monster (that can actually be very different from each other, especially when taking into account the dark and light shifting for each species)So far, for an early access, the game is perfect and this is the game I've been dreaming of for years now, it has absolutely everything needed for an engaging monster taming game. Pokémon and Digimon's most recent entries could use a lesson from these developers.Onto the "cons":The music can use more work.The game is obviously not complete yet.

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Sanctuary is a fantastic, addicting mix of platforming and turn-based combat. Lots of monsters to fight and collect, lots of items to equip, lots of team and monster builds to consider. The game gets considerably harder as you progress - especially toward the endgame. Monsters each have their own combat and platforming abilities, skills, and strengths. Every monster can be used effectively in a high tier team, it just depends how you utilize them. Highly recommend. Easily one of the best indie games I've ever played. I wish it had DLCs or a sequel in the works. I'll definitely come back to play through this one again. One testament to how good this game is - my 66 hours are over the course of just 11 days, all while working a full time job.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool JRPG with some neat combat mechanics and a lot of variety. You can approach every encounter differently, and there are a ton of strategic options. All new team recruits are just a few levels below your highest regardless of where you pick them up, which lets you try out a ton of strats without a big investment. I never got bored through my entire 55+ hour playthrough (counting postgame cleanup).There's a neat rating system after every battle, so if you want to optimize your play, you can, but you don't have to. It's a neat way to bake in difficulty and reward players for engaging with the game systems.Just stick with the game for an hour and a half or so; the first area is a little slow, but you get a lot more variety once you get through it.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: A very very good game that is worth its price for sure. Of course it depends on what games you like, but this combination of a metroidvania and classic rpg makes this a game that should attract a large audience. As in 'it should'. This game is criminally underrated, and deserves way more love. It has a very addicting gameplay loop, which differs from regular critter collectors, because instead of just gaining more stats upon leveling, they gain a new skill point which can be used on a diverse but at the same time cohesive skill tree. This can range from new attacks, passive debuff inflicting or extra damage. They manage to make these skill trees very fitting to each monster, despite the fact lots of attacks overlap. Also the monsters all have great design which really conveys how they act in battleNow for the Metroidvania part. The world is designed for you to explore it, with secrets containing held items or other goodies all over the map. Each monster additionally comes with its own overworld power, which gives access to even more secrets and goodies. Some areas even require certain monsters to access in the first place.For the last part i really wanted to talk about the difficulty, because this game gets really hard towards the end. Personally, i really enjoy a bit of difficulty in most of my games, but i see why this may scare some people from buying the game. The thing is, in this game its incredibly easy to add new monsters to your team. Certain items will allow you to instantly level up any monster to the level of the rest of your party, and there is no downside to it whatsoever. This game wants you to experiment, and not stick with one team for the whole game. Each major boss has a team with strengths and weaknesses and its up to you to build a team that can deal with these factors. Don't get me wrong though, it is very much possible to beat the game with the same team from start to finish, but some fights will be brutally hard if your team just so manages to have a weakness to the enemies strengths. Also the music is fantastic, with absolute bangers for most bosses to extremely relaxing and thematic themes for most areas. All in all this game is worth buying for sure. I haven't even mentioned half the things that makes this game good, but I emplore you to experiment and have fun with this game. Extremely underrated but oh so good regardless.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: I got a good eight or nine hours of fun out of Monster Sanctuary, so I can't say I hated it. But I also can't recommend it. I really like the idea of a Pokemon battler metroidvania, and the monsters and their abilities are visually very well designed. The art looks great and I could see the powers capturing one's imagination like Pokemon did for me all those years ago.But I don't think the platformer completely works. The puzzles aren't great, and the length of battles makes the exploration a bit of a lurching experience. There's a very odd difficulty spike where I went from never having lost a fight to getting absolutely shredded by a boss trainer. I think I would need to rebuild a new team and get really strategic about builds that will specifically deal with this one guy, and I just don't want to do all that grinding, the regular game has been grindy enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: The biggest hook to this game is that is supposed to be like Pokemon. While it is true that there are elements of Pokemon in this game, it is unfair to say they are alike. Monster Sanctuary is more akin to a Metroid RPG that borrows elements of Pokemon. That is not necessarily a bad thing, but it can be disappointing to players who were expecting Pokemon's level of game play and mechanics. The positives to this game are:+Skill branches allow for variability and customization options for different monsters.+Obtaining monsters you want doubles as a way to grind and strengthen your team.+Different options for strategy and combat makes different gimmicks and mechanics viable to the player. +The world feels vast and it is satisfying when you are able to access new areas. +If your strategy works, you are able to take down monsters well above your level. The negatives to this game are:- The game can be very challenging at times and force players to either grind or fine tune their team strategy.  - The vast amount of monsters in the game paired with the 6 member team limit makes keeping alternative teams the same level difficult.- You can only bring 3 monsters into combat at a time, this can be frustrating when trying to decide which monster is better suited to fulfilling certain rolls.- You will need to constantly refine your strategy to keep up with new challenges. This means monsters may have a one-time-only use, or need to periodically be left behind and re-integrated into your team.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: If Pokémon and Metroid had a child, it would be Monster Sanctuary. A great game that combines combat, training, and monster collecting in the style of Pokémon with metroidvania mechanics and pixel art. The game takes place in a 2D map where you encounter monsters that, when defeated, drop eggs that hatch into your own monsters. The combat is very similar to Pokémon, with 3 vs 3 battles and monsters weak or strong against specific types of attacks such as fire, water, or physical strength. The innovation lies in the exploration of the map and the metroidvania mechanics. The skill system for monsters is well-designed, following a tree structure. You can equip monsters with weapons and items, and feed them to enhance certain aspects. Not as inspired as Cassette Beasts, but still quite entertaining.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: It was cute, it's basically if Pokemon turned into an *actual* RPG and cranked up the difficulty a bit, since you do have to think about what you're doing not just this element beats this, etc, (esp towards cap level cause you cant use level as an advantage). It also has different New Game+ things for replay ability, and the pixel art is just beautiful.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: This game might just do Pokemon better than Pokemon.It has everything you'd want in a monster battling game: a wide variety of cute and charming creatures, a battle system that's easy to learn but has a lot of depth, and a character progression/leveling system that has a lot of meaningful choices. The ability to buy items that let you retrain your monsters' skills for a reasonable price saves a lot of grinding and allows you retool your monsters' abilities as you get a better grasp on strategy.You capture monsters by getting their eggs, which they randomly drop upon defeat. Your performance in every battle is ranked (depending on how much damage you've taken, how quickly you won, etc.) and higher ranks give better rewards. Do well enough and you're guaranteed a rare drop, making it quite likely that you'll get an egg (and if not, it's because you got a different rare drop instead).I was skeptical of the Metroidvania elements at first, but they ended up making the overworld a joy to explore. Enemies appear on the map, so you can fight or avoid them at your discretion, and capturing monsters gives you access to their abilities in overworld navigation: for example, a steam golem can bash down walls to open up new areas. Don't think this is like the horrible HM system in the early Pokemon games; your monsters' navigation abilities are available from the moment you capture them and are completely separated from their combat abilities. You can also use the navigation abilities of any monsters you've captured (though only six monsters at a time can be "active", i.e. available for use in battle).My only criticism is that the equipment and item crafting feels a bit bolted on and out-of-place (why does holding a shuriken make my pet phoenix better at setting things on fire with their mind?), but while it doesn't seem to add much to the experience, it doesn't really make it noticeably worse either.EDIT:Coming back to this having beaten the game. After reading other reviews, I'd been dreading the final section of the game, seeing many reviews calling it a horrible difficulty spike. All I can say is, your mileage may vary on this. While I did experiment with a few different team setups, I didn't spend a huge amount of time grinding, and I was able to finish it on my first try. I pretty easily beat the water monster user a lot of people complain about (while using a monster weak to water!). The only times I've had to use hyper-optimized team builds were to max rank against certain bosses, which is not required to complete the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I was having a blast at the start but a couple hours in I started running into battles that effectively punished me and made me not want to play unless I min maxed everything when I just wanted to enjoy playing a little monster battle game with platforming absolutely turned me off and left me pretty disappointed. It's like Pokemon if you are forced to EV and IV train your pokemon and min max all your attacks you can't really choose monsters you like and stick with them without being punished for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Super chill and well designed game overall.Cons:- Got so addicted that i had to catch'em all and complete every achiev.Pros and considerations:  - As your probably already know its a metroidvania exploration game with Final Fantasy/pokemon kind of combat, where you can capture tons of monsters, level them up and build them as you wish (as all of them have their own skill tree and combos).- Unlike other negative reviews, i didnt really grind at all and made all the way to the end game using almost same team (with some minor changes when i found some really cool/powerfull creature on my way), at the end i had to face some REALLY challenging stuff and had to proper build a team.. and had even more fun trying out every build. (charge for big numbers, bleed, burn, poison teams..)- The combat itself is very tactical and makes you use every resource your monster may have. Yeah, thats what people kinda dislike, you are not just entering a battle and spam thunder like a pokemon battle, you need to buff, shield, set a healer, spam debuffs on enemies or spam buffs to hit hard, it depends on your team playstyle.With all this in mind, have fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: fun game, a friend of mine convinced me to get it and I enjoyed it way more then I thought. I came across no glitches but there is still areas to access well before your meant to. During combat I was able to feel the gears clicking when my team was coming together. My only negatives is that for my first play through I found frost builds to be insanely strong for most of the game. The other downside is that the story is not the focus of the game in the slightest, not a big complaint but the story can just pull some bull here and there.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: worth the price, there is some fun rpg mob killing to be had here...saying that, its pretty limited? there are platforming action type stuff you need certain monsters for which seemingly would make the game more fun? in the end, it just makes the maps annoying. everything is placed in a weird way that is just awkward to look at and traverse and you know you cant reach some pointless chest filled with nothing until you get the right monster..... it just feels like the first 3-5 hours is the BEST fun you will have. it's worth the low cost though. enjoy
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: It's a mix between an Metroidvania, Monster Collector and some RPG elements.I hit 40 hours in 4 days and I'm now in my New Game+ run in which I'm trying to get the last achievement on the hardest difficulty.The only thing I wanted from the game was more!      10/10 Tip: The "Save Team" function also saves the equipment of the current team, unequipping and loading the saved team puts the items back on, so you don't really need that much duplicate equipment if any.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very nice refresh on the monster catching genre, battles are faster, but there are a lot and it is quite grindy.The exploring quickly becomes tedious, as the puzzes are quite simple to blaze trough, unless you have to backtrack with a certain ability or item... But other than that variation of it is not innovative at all. All you ever do is jump.Stacking damaging Debuffs is also quite fast in terms of just clearing the trash mobs. But nothing can beat catzerker in terms of destroying everything so far.Leveling your party is impossible, you are locked to some variation of 6 monsters. It made me not even hatch the champion monsters, because I know there is only one egg ever. If I wanted to change my party and use a champion monster, I would rather hatch it later when I need it... or never at all. Hatching a monster makes it about the level of your party - 2.The skill trees are really nice and so far I have not found a single "full combo" monster, but rather you have to take 2 for a good combination of skills. Like when you go for debuffs, you have one debuffer and one that makes debuffs stronger or stack higher.Personally I feel like there sould be more monster keeper duels, because the wild monsters are just pure grind and 99% of the time pushovers.Which brings up another point: Pacing.It happens that you just rush into a chamption monster by accident, as it was a very unexpected one. Some fights have no buildup at all. And then there is the monologue of the bad guys, but you never know if there will be a fight or not.It is not like you go into a gym and challenge the leader, it just randomly happens.Sometimes you unlock stuff at the keepers home and sometimes not, but you never know why.So what makes the game good?Item managment and equipment is done very well, you do find your special yellow marked item every one in a while and they have nice extra effects.Skill trees as mentioned before are very well balanced. They might be a big confusing at first, but you do know the skills soon enough. and you still have to figure out if your monster is a tank + healer, or tank + debuffer or whatever else.Most monsters can perfom several roles, or maybe when you get enough skillpoints it does not matter? I have not reached that far yet.Animations are very cool and the combat speed is nice without having to press or read everything that just happened (Like in Siralim). Almost every attack has a different effect.Every monster has a info and lore page with additional artwork, but it is done a lot better than in other games.Monsters are very pleasing in design. You may see the occasional bird or kangaroo, but other than that they are indeed monsters and not household items.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best examples of monster catching genre, tied with Monster Hunter Stories. I'd give this game a 10/10 if not for the brutal difficulty spike at the end, which made me lower it to 9/10. Still, an amazing mix of metroidvania and turn based rpgs. It's a wonder that a small dev team can make the best offering of the genre while AAA developers can't even get close to it. If you're into either metroidvanias or monster catching games, this is a must play. It also has PVP, but I've struck strictly to PVE. Got into Keeper Master rank with %97.5 of the map discovered within my playtime. And there were still stuff to do, if you are into it.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Although nothing about this game is particularly groundbreaking, what it does manage to deliver is a complete package which is enjoyable, fun, and challenging from start to finish. A metroidvania-style game with turn-based elements and skill trees centered around monster combat akin to Pokemon and sidescroller platforming, this game has enough depth to keep you on your toes while also allowing you to customize, experiment and fail without losing too much time or progress. At around 50 hours of playtime I was able to 100% the game and do it on my own terms with a team of monsters I actually liked and connected with. It was a refreshing experience to play a game that felt finished, had a decent storyline, above average art and music, and had no discernible bugs. Ultimately, it is wholly worth it's entry price if any of these aspects sound appealing to you as it's definitely one of the best games I've played this year.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: A simple, quaint and enjoyable experience for anyone who likes turn-based battling or creature collector games (i.e: pokemon-ish). Don't look to it for story, it's very very linear. Everything good about this game is it's game-play / battle system. It's dynamic enough that you'll need to spend a bit of time strategizing, but not complex to the point of doing rocket-science.Get it on sale and it'll be more than worth your money.Didn't expect to sink these many hours in and plat-ing (unlock all achievements) it.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: I am very into RPG Turn-Based games like Pokemon, and I played competitively for a long time. The game is fantastic and as fun as Pokemon despite the limited visual aspect. I played this on a different Platform, and enjoyed it so much that I got it on steam.Pros:Easy to learn, hard to masterAll monsters serve a unique purpose in and out of battlePUZZLES!CompetitiveExplorationFun Team BuildingBalanced (most of the time)Cons:Gameplay can feel slow and repetitive early onGrindy
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Metroidvania style exploration meets Pokémon monster capture, you get 101 eggs to hatch which become your monster army, each monster has a diverse skill tree and can be built to fill different roles. game offers PVP functionality so you can challenge others. Good story, nice visuals, enjoyable game play.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: love. there's exploring and creature collection and you can grind for as long as you need if you're bad at the duel function (me). i'm so bad at strategy!!! but i grind for long enough, i'll have the level advantage!!!! i don't think that's how it's gonna work later in the game, but for now, i'm doing FINE. i love collecting my little guys.edit: HOHOHOHO I HAVE FIGURED OUT STRATEGY. I LOVE MY DOT TEAM. DAMAGE OVER TIME FOREVER. it's really bad against vodinoy though!!! so back to the drawing board!!!! _childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: A solid critter-catcher with charming art, fun battle mechanics and a thought-out leveling system. I've already sunk several hours into this game and catching all the little monsters is really fun! There's a diverse set of skills and types so you can really mix up your team however you want. However, when I saw there was a frog as a starter choice, I knew I would be sold. My only complaint is that the platforming can occasionally be pretty frustrating, but it's not terribly punishing most of the time and there have only been a few items I've had to leave behind. From an accessibility standpoint, this can make for a feeling of slow progress as timing jumps isn't always easy for disabled players, but I found I have been able to get through most areas without too much difficulty. I love the art and the creatures; you can tell a lot of love was put into their design. Being able to unlock different types makes it all the better, with different skillsets and colors to choose from! The game also does a good job of not dumping it all on you at once so you have time to learn the mechanics. Creatures also have other utilities on the map, like being able to solve puzzles, float the player or swim, and I found that made a lot of the platforming feel more fun and less like a slog through a level. Plus, it's really cute to see your little monster friend follow you around the map! While I can't say anything about the end game story, I like the one that's been presented so far. The game does a good job of making you feel connected to the world and invested in what happens to the monsters and the keep, and I'm looking forward to seeing where it goes! I think this game is polished enough to warrant full price, it seems very reasonable for the amount of content and I think it's very promising that the devs seem committed to releasing free DLC so as to keep the PVP aspect of the game (which seems entirely optional) balanced and fun for all players. Definitely a thumbs up from me!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Promising potential, lovely pixel art and a little challenging, I'm looking forward to future updates. Some platforming sections are difficult if you don't have awesome reflexes and there are some nasty difficulty spikes but the community guides can help with team planning to get around these. All around a solid early access indie title with about 10-15 hours of story content so far!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful game for children who want to get into rpg's. Colorful pixel art, charming music and easy to understand instruction make this a pleasant game to entice young minds. That being said, there is nothing here for anyone over the age of 15 as the aesthetic, dialogue and difficulty is for a much younger audience. Having played 3 hours (I bought the game twice) I quickly realized this is Pokemon except three units fight at once. Like most turn-based games there is very little in terms of decision making and even the most minor encounter is a 3-5 minute slog of hitting the same abilities over and over with the game littering you with equipment constantly. Provided there could be harder challenges far deeper into the game which require more thinking involved but if the majority of the game can be completely with little effort I fail to see the point. If you are a parent wanting to get your children into a simple but lush pokemon style game I highly recommend this. Great work by Mon Rai Games.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: + Extensive variety of monster; visuals, skill sets, abilities on the map+ Fluid movement/exploration on the overworld+ Varied areas although within the relative norm of fantasy games (e.g., forest, cold area, etc.)+ Optimized UI makes the frequent menu browsing a pleasant experience+ Swapping between monsters for exploration skills on the metroidvania map is smooth, considering how often you're doing it+ Intricate combat system revolving around combos, synergies, buffs/dots, and much moreEach monster has its own drawing and multi-page biography. I can't stop playing. There is so much to do!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely fun game. A combination of Pokemon and Metroidvania. What's I like most about this game is the team building. It is not about getting the strongest monster or grinding their level to MAX. It's about creating team with synergy that supporting each other. With good team, you can tackle bosses or teams with higher stats than you.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Really, really nice game. Not stressful yet engaging, with a good deal of strategic thinking in battles.The feature that gets me the most is the skill trees : each monster has a unique one. You can really make your team and your strategy, with 101 monsters to collect and adapt to your gameplay. Then the rating system of each combat gives a nice objective and keeps you focused on your fights : your loot depends on it. You can't use the same monsters and abilities over and over if you want to get the most of the fights.There are a few game modes to unlock when leveling up, like online combat with a leaderboard. Or fighting the previous champions again and try to improve your score. It allows for a nice change of pace from time to time.The weakest feature is the exploration part. There are lots to explore and unlock on the map, you can gain abilities and come back to get previously hidden or unaccessible loot and explore new areas. Not bad, but not feeling quite as awesome as the combats and team management.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: 4 out of 5 starsSteams rating-system kinda sucks for nuance, I highly recommend this game although it isnt perfect.Good Game. its not hard by any stretch, and I 100% this game at the time of writing this review. It offers really interesting Team-building variety, and as far as i can tell every monster is viable in the right context, yes even the basic slime. While the Post-game does leave some challenge to be desired, if you like team-building or just monster collecting, than this is probably a good pick. In general I would say pick it up if its on sale if you arent sure you like it, but if you enjoy the collecting or team-building aspect of games like tem-tem or pokemon, then this is probably always a solid pick.A warning: There are several puzzle-chests in the game where you can accidentally soft-lock yourself if you dont have a teleport item, so always stock up on those in case of emergency.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: This game definitely is not just a metroidvania pokemon, it's so much more. Of course there is elements of both games, but they have complemented each other really well and I think it makes for a really awesome experience in general. If you like metroidvania style games and some monster collecting this is definitely for you.Edit: this game just got better nd better with the updates, highly recomended.

_childDocuments_.review: A very tentative thumbs up, and if a "neutral" option were available I would pick that. I had fun making it to the end, but I don't think I will finish this one to spare myself the headaches.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Cheap graphics, cheap animations, cheap story, cheap music, cheap controls.What the designers probably thought:How much can you copy from Pokemon before getting sued?Something platformkemon.I am srsly dissapointed.This isnt anything close to a metroidvania, its a cheap jump and run with uninspired round based battles that take way too long and repeat themselves over and over.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game in Early Access but didn't put much time into it. I just wrapped up the main story and I have to say this game is really well done and fun to play. All monsters having their own skill trees makes for a fun time. I also like that evolving a monster doesn't strictly make it better like in other monster catching games. If you can deal with Metroidvania like progression, there's a lot to like here. Can't wait to dive into the post game and the Forgotten World!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game so much. It brings so much promise. I'm 5 hours in and I'm still going to give it a few more to see if anything suddenly improves.The problem: as stated by another recent negative review: it gets repetitive. Run around, fight monsters that stay the same level as you (never have a hard/easy battle, everything is medium), battles are too long, use the same combination of attacks... I can tell there is an "evolve" function of some of the monsters but I have yet to evolve anything.  The game seems extremely linear as well... even though you can explore a bit off the direct path, the most you get out of it are some cheap items that will soon be replaced.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, TO BE CLEAR, I do NOT recommend this game if you are interested in a good metriodvania with great level design. I do NOT recommend this game if you want a compelling story. I DO recommend this game if you like turn based combat with a lot of depth.The level design is incredibly bland, the story is about as compelling as a Pokemon mainline game story (not that compelling), but I'm somewhat impressed with how much effort went into the combat. The game plays with a lot of interesting ideas that I don't see other games do much with. It has its problems, but the strategy needed is pretty deep. Each battle is pretty dang long too. The plain old wild battles can take like 10 minutes. This isn't like Pokemon where you one shot or two shot people, there's a lot more that goes into it.In short, get the game if you like turned based combat. It wasn't compelling enough for me, and it didn't hold my attention, but you might like it.EDIT: The 10 minutes for wild battles thing was an exaggeration. I'm trying to draw attention to the fact that most battles you go through aren't going to be like pokemon battles were you find the weakness and one/two shot it. There's a lot of people saying I was bad at the game, and that's why I didn't like it. But as my review says, I didn't like it because I'm not super into turn based combat. If you like turn based combat, you'll love this game.Also, 13 hours is plenty of time to figure out if I like a game or not. If it's not enough time that's a failure on the game, not on me.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this game - it took about 35 hours to finish completely, with the last few achievements requiring some research on the internet (I didn't research or look up anything until after the final fight in the post-game). However, compared to other games you can mark *most* of the areas to return to when you have the appropriate ability with the ingame map which was amazing.Recommended to turn battle speed to 3x, the animations are nice but combat is much quicker with that speed.The combat was fun and challenging with plenty of options for experimentation, the in game tips were actually useful for recommending how to build a party. If you've played any of the Pokemon games, this will be a comfy game for you.Platforming was both difficult but fair and you definitely felt skilled after performing some of the harder jumps or navigations.Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, engaging game that combines monster-raising with platforming. The monster designs are cute and inventive, and the gameplay is smooth with the right level of challenge. The 'shifting' and skill trees are nice touches for a monster-raising game as well, meaning you can really play around with different monster builds.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest, when I purchased this game I binged it for 6 hours straight. And it's important to remember that I really enjoyed those 6 hours. This game scratched a few itches, some of which I wasn't even aware of. But then I realized I really hadn't done much in those 6 hours. The combat sequences take a long time and are a majority of the game. As other users have pointed out, the Scoring System is self defeating and doesn't reward players for using some of the complex mechanics that are built into each monster's varrying development. The game rewards fast, quick combat--using supports, tanks, and healers is not as heavily weighted as simply smashing your way through monsters. Boss encounters are more fun and challenging, but punish you for even attempting supportive play to your team. The rest of the game--map exploration--is very basic classic Mario-style jump puzzles. There is a really promising monster ability mechanic that could add a lot more depth to the map puzzles, but it is vastly under utilized. Promising, but a chore to play. It requires a decent time commitment, but doesn't feel very rewarding. Map puzzles are pretty straight forward, but have a bit of a skill cap that may frustrate some players. It lacks real depth to satisfy the urge to play the genres the game is based off of--I ended up just going to play Pokemon and Crash Bandicoot.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Sanctuary fills me with a joy similar to when i first played Pokemon but has the fun elements of a metroidvania. The leveling/skill system is really deep and allows for tons of different ways to play and experiment and you can equip a variety of weapons and accessories on your monsters to further tweak them for combat. Each monster seems pretty unique and they have different ways to be played based on the skills you choose. All in all this is a solid game, and you can see the devs put a lot of thought into it's creation and still remain active in the community with players. Happy gaming!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: It's metroid and it's pokemon and it works. They told me that in the description, but I had to see it to believe it. I don't think there's a single monster, including the unevolved ones, that isn't viable with the right team composition. There's so much nuance and attention to detail. I LOVE finding all the secret areas! Music is repetitive but at least they're good tracks. Overall, 9/10, amazing
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game with way more depth to the combat than it seems. It is definitely metroidvania Pokemon with tons of homages while still being wholly original. I might actually like this team building system more than anything I've played before. Any monster is truly viable and can be top tier depending on how you build them and synergize with the rest of the party.I read some complaints about the difficulty curve before they added a casual mode. I played on normal and it kept challenging me enough that I stayed invested instead of mindless mashing through combat after the first few areas like most games. I'm going to try master difficulty on new game+ next. Usually when I play a game I tend to list things in my head that I'd improve, but I struggled to find any this time. I could say minor quality of life things like adding a win counter to the Infinity Battles so you know how far you are after each round. Really what I want is a sequel with more monsters and new areas.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a hidden gem, truly amazing underrated monster game! If you like metroidvanias, you may not like this game, simply because it is not a pure action game, but a turn based combat rpg; the only thing it does have in common with metroidvanias are the exploration and platforming (which is not challenging in any way, and it isn't supposed to be, since that is not the focus of the game).Buy this game if you love monster collecting games like digimon or pokemon, you will not regret it. The combat is really fun and strategic, and every monster on the field is a fundamental building block of your team, you can't just power through everything with only one monster, a good team composition is key to victory. So if you don't like to rebuild or rethink your strategy, but just mindless crush everything  (like most rpgs), you may feel frustrated by this game, since some battles can be really tough.Another positive thing about this game is the community, on discord the players are always helping each other. There so many fun strategies and game mechanics to discuss about. Also, the devs are always updating, balancing and adding new things in the game! This game deserve to be way more popular!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Hunter is a nice adventure with a lot of content due to the great amount of creatures in the game. Following a simple storyline, you explore a simple world with monster that have abilities in and out of combat. The amount of monsters and the variety of abilities is whats makes the game interesting. The lore is rich, but you can go through the game without paying to much attention to it, because it's very intuitive and there are just a few sidequests. It's clearly a well-done game, but I hope it gets a sequel with better graphics.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Something different and it's great!Think Pokemon/World of Final Fantasy combat meets metroidvania. I was a little worried there wouldn't be much content in it's current early access, but I was mislead by a negative review by someone whom didn't have many hours played.I adore this game. BravoWould love to know when the full release is.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: This game is much better then it has any right to be. At it's core it's a pokemon like monster collector/battles, with  better combat, but an (even) more forgettable story.The art is lovely and the OST's are great.The best thing about it in my mind though is the insane amount of possible teams that can be build, for somehow the devs made every single mon both viable and strong in their own team.While it's certainly not required to finish this game, this allows for so much experimenting. This game is truly haven for those who love to theorycraft.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: The comparison must be made... and the others are right. This is pokemon if it actually had any depth and respected your intelligence. I'm thoroughly impressed with how much this improves on the dry uninspired classic pokemon formula. Sorry - I really like insulting pokemon and this is a great opportunity.You now actually have deep customization via skill trees and having three character on the field at once, plus 3 backups. They all also have 3 equipment slots. This alone turns baby's first rpg into something that requires contemplation. And if you don't come up with a proper group you aren't going to have a good time. You could probably get away with whatever on casual difficulty though. The middle difficulty is harder than most rpgs already and you will definitely lose or have a rough time if you don't think about your composition. There is also an online pvp where you battle other players.Most of my complaints are minor to medium-level nitpicks. There are too many secret walls suggesting I change my monster constantly and hit all the walls, often with no real visual hint that I can see. You can't see all the buffs and debuffs without pressing a toggle button and then backing out afterwards. Battles can feel a bit samey because the way teams work together, you're going to using the same sequence of skills most of the time unless an emergency comes up. Sometimes feels a little grindy because battles are long. I don't care about the storytelling in the slightest. There are some other small/meh issues I'm forgetting about.Pokemon wishes it was this good.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: I went to give it a try and ended up playing for 9 hours straight. I enjoyed every minute. The collecting and progression are really addicting and make for very engaging game play. I can tell it will scratch the completionist itch for a long time. The Monsters are used in really interesting ways impeding them in the metroidvania style game play. The customization options available have a good level of complexity and create a challenging battle system. Looking forward to playing some more!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of the best creature collector games I've played on Steam. The only other game that comes close for me is Coromon, but the game play here is just so captivating I love it, and I love the pixel art so much. This is probably the only game I'll ever write a review for, just because I'd want anyone on the edge of getting this game to absolutely get it. I was really sad to hear we won't be getting any major updates, but even as is the game is super replayable, and there are endless things to do so don't be afraid to try it out!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was unsure if the genres that this game mixes would be a good mix, but all of them are done well.For the metroidvania style, you'll be revisiting old areas to collect chests and hidden monsters, if that's not for you, it's not required.For team battles, there are great synergies between certain monsters due to them having 1-3  types, but for the story optimization isn't as required either.Monsters have their normal versions, as well as light and dark shifts, so teams can be altered to suit your play style a bit more. Monster evolutions are not a huge part of the game, creating new monsters, not necessarily better than the base form, but suited to different roles.Overall, pixel art is well done, and the game seems to be well put together.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. The story is very much like Pokemon, kinda cheesy and nonsensical but still fun. The 3v3 battles lead you to come up with builds and strategies that can involve monsters you previously disregarded because you ran into another monster that opens up a completely different play style. The music is extremely good. I was vibing with every background and battle OST.My only gripe with it is there exists sudden difficulty cliffs. You could have a team that wipes the previous bosses/trainer fights and suddenly run into a hard counter that decimates yours. It could be very hard to figure out how to proceed and grinding for materials to upgrade equipment can be a chore. When this happens, the path of least resistance is to radically change your play style to accommodate the fight. It's definitely a game that forces you to adapt.Overall, a very satisfying strategy RPG. It reminded me of playing Pokemon as a kid but with infinitely more depth in monster builds.

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted this to be a short review. Kinda failed.Grinding works differently in this game. Monsters you hatch from eggs are 2 levels below your highest-leveled monster, and you can get them up 1 level pretty easily with how they give away level badges like candy (even being able to buy them at some point in the game), though said badges only allow you to level them up if they're 2 levels below the monster.Much like Metroidvania games, expect backtracking. Backtracking is rewarded, however, with being able to get eggs a lot easier from low-leveled monsters, and being able to use beefed up versions of them. All monsters in this game are actually, really viable with the right set up and team synergy. Even the Blob you get in the beginning of the game. As you gain more monsters, you'll also have more abilities to use which can unlock treasure chests you couldn't quite get earlier, or even unlock new areas and monsters in some occasions.However, don't get too attached to your monsters, this is where this game can be compared with SMT a little bit. With minimal grinding, Monster Sanctuary starts becoming more of a strategy RPG, especially since pretty early-on, a huge can of worms is released in the "Light/Dark" variations of monsters with special passive abilities, and there's overall no reason not to have them all be one or the other for the most part. Items to change "neutral" monsters into light/dark variations, or shift to one variation or the other are overall pretty rare too, so this further encourages the backtracking aspect of Metroidvania games to collect more monsters.Getting back on the topic of comparing this game to SMT though; your team should ideally be easily rearranged to focus on surviving the area and the bosses at hand, exploiting their weaknesses to defeat them as quick as possible.Every normal/mini-boss "Champion Monster" encounter has a rating system. Your team should ideally be focusing on getting 5 stars consistently for normal encounters at the very least (and you can always rematch the mini-bosses later in a special arena), so that you can have an easier time collecting their eggs, meaning more abilities and an easier time making teams to fight the situation.The reason why I'm warning you of this now in the review is because if you aren't, you're gonna be REALLY struggling come the real boss battles: Keeper Battles.I won't say much, but this easily doubled the difficulty in my playthrough, especially with a certain underwater battle. Well, actually, that's where I have a small gripe with it, and I'm not afraid to spoiler it either.Still, though, I really can't recommend this game enough for anyone who wants a challenging monster collector RPG. It's pretty short without being TOO short, and there's some VERY challenging post game content too; with potentially more on the way.Really, the only reason why I compared this to Digimon too was because, well, it's certainly not Pokemon. There's evolving in this game, but what it really does is shift a monster's role in the team. That's not Digimon either, but it's probably a closer comparison than Pokemon, since Cyber Sleuth had those 3-on-3 fights.Also, the alternate themes you can toggle on in-game are incredibly catchy to me, though I think the Champion Monster theme could use a similar touch-up.Finally, if you're interested in the PvP scene, there's actually a save file out there that's endorsed by the devs and community that completely removes any grinding needed. Please, please, actually finish the game before you get it though, the single player is incredibly solid and fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game so much.  It does so much almost right.  The non-linear game, the team building, the battle system...they're all so close to working in a way that's truly enjoyable.But every one of them falls flat in a way that doesn't seem like it's improving but is rather getting worse as I go on.  I'm going to go from most frustrating to least frustrating here to help prioritize.The biggest gripe I have is that wild battles/guardian fights and fighting other keepers are fundamentally different to the point it's become extremely frustrating because they take different teams.  Wild battles and guardian fights focus on a star rating system.  The faster you kill them and the more health your team has left when you succeed, the better your star rating, and more stars equals more rewards (5* a guardian fight for an egg of that guardian).  This encourages building a team that hits hard, fast, and often, and is where I think the game is at its best - many monsters cover this well, and allows for the flexibility the game boasts to shine through.Keeper fights though...the farther you get in the game, the more these require a very specific kind of team, and that is very inflexible.  Usually a team that cleanses debuffs well and applies their own rather than focusing on the damage.  They become fights of attrition where hitting hard and fast is just straight up not a strategy.  So what this means for you is you'll have a team of monsters that you go through the overworld with and try to build around the star system, only to get stonewalled by a keeper fight and need to go grind up a different team that can out-attrition them.  It's a jarring shift and is my biggest gripe with the game - I did not like needing to bench the roughly dozen monsters I had built up to handle different kinds of fights under the star system to grind up a handful of goblins which out-sustained the keeper at the top of the Sun Tower, for example.  It goes against the "build what you like" model and the two types of battles don't mesh at all.  If they had picked one and stuck with it, it would be so much better, even if that meant not having as many "viable" monsters.  As is it feels like they made all the monsters, made one battle style, then decided they needed variety for the sake of the monsters that didn't work well under system 1 and made system 2.Next up on the frustration is the RNG gatekeeping.  The exploration side of a metroidvania is to find the one room with the new powerup you need and then go use it wherever you can.  This is still the case sometimes in Monster Sanctuary and it works well when that's the roadblock.  Just as often though, it's a monster ability you're lacking, and in that case you're now subject to RNG.  Farm the monster fights, hope you did well enough in the star system for decent drops, and then hope you get the egg you need to get the next ability to move on.  It brings the game to a grinding halt, quite literally, especially since monsters only respawn when you clear four other rooms or use a consumable to bring them back.  So if there's 3 rooms with the correct kind of monster, that means, travel time between rooms excluded, you're not actively working on your goal 25% of the time.  (Also I understand that they didn't want to give the starters amazing abilities but it feels really contrived that the Eagle familiar can't figure out how to use greater fly when it's supposed to be the embodiment of the air).Finally, a minor gripe, but one that seems to be mirrored in other reviews, the platforming is fairly minimal, which feels off for a metroidvania title.  It's a minor thing and I'm not giving the review its thumbs down for that, but I would like to note it.Overall, Monster Sanctuary is a ton of fun early on.  I really like the character designs, the monsters are more classic JRPG monsters than something like Pokemon or TemTem, but they're charming and I like them on the whole.  Music is solid if really really loud (even when turning it most of the way down in the settings) and the plot has been genuinely interesting if fairly bare bones.  The non-linearity is amazingly well done too, with monsters' levels being set based on how much of the map you've explored rather than area C being level 15 all the time, in case you go and do areas D E and F first.  But the core gameplay loops struggle to be consistent and ultimately causes a lot more frustration than enjoyment...I've tried to play this three times now, and two of the times I've stopped was because of frustration with the core loops not being consistent.  It's so close to being a great game, but the lack of consistency in what battles gauge as being "successful" and the forced RNG drop grinding for some of your powerups just keeps making me put it down after a fairly short time playing it.  I'm making progress each time, but not having much fun doing it, so I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game for those who are into the monster taming (creature collector), or just like a really good turn-based rpg.Some quick aspects I wanted to point out about the game:- Deep strategic battle with high sinergy tactics. So pick well your monsters, look for combinations on your team, work on your strenghts and oversee the weeknesses, use well not only the skill points, but equipments and food. Recommendations for end game: ~50% damage absorption for every monster, 4k hp. Some monsters can get away with less, but they sure have their protections.- Nice metroidvania exploration with a lot of backtracking. But here you use your monsters field abilities as exploration tools, like flying, mount, wall break etc. Pay attention to your surroundings, there's a lot of secrets in this game. :D- The game can be fairly complex. But now there's difficulty in the options menu for those who want a more casual experience, or harder. Also in the options menu, you can set the speed of combat from x1 up to x3. So feel free to adapt the speed of the animations. I personally use it on 1.75x because I find 1 painfuly slow but faster than that I lose track of things happening.- For those more hardcore the game has a lot of end game content, post campaign and also for the pvp people there's pvp battles with ranking and seasons.- The story is sufficient to serve its purpose. Not too deep, but interesting enough. I personally like it but the game is not all about it, the thing of this game is the combat, exploration and monsters.- Now, have I said that this game can be complex and hard (specially at the end, as you can see some people say here at other reviews)? The majority of the complexity lay on the monsters skill trees. So, I recommend you to read it all. Every monster you catch, read  it. Don't let to read after you have 50 monsters already. If you read it along your gameplay, you gonna understand the game mechanics well while you progress and can learn and adapt your strategy and gameplay. The basis of the game is not that hard, but you must understand what is happening first. And remember, every monster you hatch will be 3 levels lower than your highest level monster. If you want to use some monster that is way under level, just go where you found one and drop a new egg to hatch (remember that the number of stars you get from a battle says the chance of dropping rare itens and eggs). There's no need to arduosly level them all up. For those remaining levels you can use level up badge (like rare candy, but only level up until it's 1 level lower than your high level).- At last, but no less important, this game have really cool creatures. I love the monster aesthetics so much. It's really really cool. Vertraag and Draconoir, my favorites. Not perfect though, but I love it. I expect great acomplishments from these devs in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I have purchased this game on Steam, as well as on my Switch (Where I currently hold an additional 15+ hours). My short review would be simply "If you're considering trying this game, you absolutely should", however there's a lot else to dig into when it comes to my overall thoughts on the experience.I would have to probably label this game as a sort of "greatest hits tribute" to games which came before, and inspired Monster Sanctuary, which may sound like I see it as a stigma, but it's done so brilliantly it becomes a huge strength - a rare thing to achieve, and man is this an enjoyable game, with or without appreciation for it's inspirations.The leveling system for your monsters is incredibly elaborate, yet completely intuitive and easy to understand, and it becomes addictive very quickly, and drives you even more to continue playing through the story. The battle system is equally as intuitive, but as with any RPG, may take you some time to come up with an appropriate strategy for how to handle each of the 'baddies' you encounter, and the game is frequently showing you stronger and stronger foes, so it becomes necessary to do a bit of grinding from time to time.I will say it was kind of a shame, for such a strategic and fun battle system, I found myself wanting to play other real people with it, and I gathered in game that you CAN do so, but it requires completion of the story first. It should be a more obvious option which you have much earlier on - that is literally the only complaint I have, and it's not a huge one.Lastly, as a composer it kills me to see brilliant soundtracks go unacknowledged, this game has an amazing soundtrack, I've pulled it up on Youtube to listen to it casually a few times. If you're an audiophile with a taste for 16-bit RPG tunes, I would recommend this soundtrack with or without playing the game.Congrats on the 3000 reviews, I would love to see more of this game in the future <3

_childDocuments_.review: If you saw this game and though, well this looks fun? Buy it now.I saw this game a long while ago on 9gag. I wasn’t sure when about the early access release.I generally like the Devs to have time to fix things before I give it a go. But boy oh boyYou collect monsters, unlock new abilities that help you in the metroidvania map sort of style, fight battles with your beloved pets and uncover a dark plot (dun dun duuun)The combat plays out on the "worldmap". One team attack first followed by the other. The twist is that every attack, buff/debuff, spell or heal stacks a combo meter. The last monster on your turn deals extra damage depending on how well you stacked. This resets every turn and the enemy utilize the same function. Which mean that even if you shield or heal, its still all counts for the final blow. Each action cost mana which you only generate between turns, so you cant get too reckless either.  Great system that awards many different play styles!Each monster can be captured and used in combat. Instead of using pokeballs or hoping for a percentage change of capture (I’m looking at you Ni no kuni) The game drops  egg as rear loot. The better you perform in combat the higher the ranking you get (between 1-5 stars). Every action during combat counts for a higher ranking. Overkill, how many turns it took, their level, combos or even the amount of buffing and healing. Great system which also helps with backtracking through the game, because killing low level monsters can earn you some sweet loot!Cute music. Amazing artwork. Leveling up your monsters. Engaging combat. Evolving story.In overall if you’re reading this, you should buy it. Because this is a great game. Which will just get better with more updates rolling out soon!
