_childDocuments_.review: Learned about this game through Twitter, even won one of their giveaways and thus got the bookguide for free. Bought it during the winter sale and honestly? For 7€, it's not bad at all! But as with any games, it does have flaws. So as I usually do, I'll start with the review with the stuff that could've done better and go up from there.First and foremost, the difficulty. It felt weird that during the 30 hours it took me to beat the game, I kept on going and didn't find most of a challenge. The game is reasonably easy... Up to the endgame. Once you reach the final dungeon, the last three bosses suddenly go ballistic in difficulty. The game has a level cap of 40 and since I don't like skipping encounters in games like these, I reached them at lvl 38. I had to go up to the level cap for them, min-max to hell and back, evolve two of the monsters on my team and I STILL couldn't beat the blue alchemist. Felt kinda dissapointed that all I could do up to that point was to try and brute-force my way through it and took me up to 15 attempts despite me only struggling with another encounter before (a lvl40 boss). On my honest opinion, I would've increased the difficulty on the game itself and tried to not be AS brutal at the very end.There was also another thing related to the difficulty that felt off, and that's the amount of experience you get from encounters. As I said before, I avoided skipping fights as I usually do, and I noticed something really off. Normal encounters and bosses give pretty much the same amount of experience, which is not a lot. May I ask why, though? The way the loot system works in here is that you gotta rank high on a fight to get anything that valuable, and as it is, only by completely demolishing a boss you'll ever get any reward that's worth your time, as in terms of experience, you're better off just fighting normal enemies.One more note: of the 30 and a half hours of playtime I have, you might be surprised to know that around 80% to 90% of that time was just fighting. It's a shame, as while encounters are fun and engaging, I actually found the exploration, puzzles and platforming stuff to be more enticing. It's always great to balance things out, and the amount of encounters kinda ruin that concept. On my opinion, if the game ever gets a sequel (which I hope it does), I would hope more attention is brought to other stuff that ain't just fighting. More attention about the story for example, or making the areas have even more details and hidden stuff.Lastly, something that even the game will warn you on start-up: please, play it with a controller. I tried it with a keyboard, but it really doesn't feel right and when it comes to puzzles and platforming, you'll need to be fast and precise. If you play the game, play it on a controller. If I'm honest, I can see the game being perfect for a platform like the Switch or that Portable Steam thing that was being shown not too long ago.With that stuff out of the way, what do we have left? A surprisingly fun RPG, which while at a simple glance seems to be "Pokemon but 2d", it feels closer to "Pokemon with more emphasis on classic RPG mechanics, metroidvania platforming and nice pixelated graphics".The combat mechanics are surprisingly good and engaging, well balanced and fun. Instead of using Pokemon's system of "level up and learn an already set lot of skills and evolutions", the game goes for multiple skill-trees for each monster. This means that you can build your monsters however you feel like, and there's indeed items to reset all points and try out different styles. Further more, some monsters can evolve, which changes the skill-trees dramatically. Does it mean that you should evolve every monster? Shockingly, not really. Given skill trees are different, you might even find usefulness on keeping any of them un-evolved. And furthermore, each monster has a basic style and two variants (a light side and a dark side, lets call 'em). The planet gets all the freedom they could ever want to build their team as they like.Platforming and the whole metroidvania style here is executed quite well! If I could throw any complaint about it is that I would like the world to be even bigger as I had a blast exploring places and coming back once I had the monsters and skills needed to open ways previously sealed. Plenty of secrets too, which is great.While not something directly related to the game itself, the book was fun to read before actually playing, even checked it through the playthrough a couple times for information. The artwork on it is just as beautiful as the one on display on the game itself, and only thing I could ever ask is that a future sequel might find it great to use that beautiful art on the game too in some way.Animations, ambience, music and landscapes are well drawn, played and done, with my only complain that it is odd some stuff seems to be missing. Victory animations for example, there aren't any along with no music cue or anything when you win on a fight. There are no sounds or fun stuff on the background related to the place you're in, like snow falling on the peaks or sparks of fire near the magma pools. Feels great, and can surely be improved.Lastly, while I haven't touched on it, it is great that the devs added a multiplayer option. I was expecting it to be avoided entirely and leave the game as a singleplayer experience only - and I'm glad I was wrong.In the end, this is a well-crafted RPG done by devs I've never heard off and published by a well-known company that most around-20-year olds out there will have fond memories of. I payed around 7 bucks for it, and for that price it'd say it's well worth it. That being said, if you have a Switch, perhaps think of picking it once it releases on it, which as far as I know will be out on physical format very soon. Just remember, use a controller.TL-DR Edition: A game somewhat similar to Pokemon, but with a fighting style more closely related to classic RPGs, 3 vs 3 with HP, mana and stuff. Game is great and fun, but has some small problems that hopefully, might be fixed in the future via DLC or sequels. On a same, it's a good purchase that might last you around 28-34 hours. Big difficulty spikes by the very end, though.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to write a fair reveiw of this game. So I have to start with price. I got this for 10% off plus an additional 20% with escapists coupon. Now I do know what I'm in for with free access games (and these guys give you a huge disclaimer props for that! Still waiting on a pinned suggestions disscussion!) Anyways I got 30% off and what I got was..... pretty damn cool and very inventive, a lil grindy and drove me insane (till I remembered it was supposed to be like POKEMON as well as metroidvainia then finally I settled down looked for a good combo and grineded a few lvl's. If those two combinations don't sound neat to you then do avoid until a bigger sale. If one is meh to you...watch the promos and if still meh, wait for a bigger sale. but if those sound like super wonky fun well they are (though a bit grindy and mid game rewards much more diversity thanks to resets that FULLY reset skills, no starters!). TLDR; It's unpolished, rough and needs work. But the devs knew it, but they also knew one other thing. You'd have fun playing it even now and it helps them make it better! It's a much more...HM world Pokemon.PS: if a developer see's this, tell the team to get on more varied food for all stats!!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: I have really enjoyed playing this game. The monsters are cute, and the game play is interesting. The leveling system for the monsters allows you to customize your team in really fun and interesting ways, and I like that you can level up all the monsters on your team during combat instead of only leveling the three that fought. I only intended to play for ten minutes the other day and ended up playing for over an hour. Will keep playing, I want to see how many more monsters I can catch!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Monster sanctuary is brilliant in some places, and clearly needed more time in others.As a metroidvania the platforming controls feel good, but the map design is rather boring. I'm not saying It's bad, but It's very obvious the game was made with limited resources. i recon so much art time went into all the monsters which look great, that the terrain and map design was sort of left behind.The combat is fantastic, imagine if Pokemon had RPG skill trees and equippable items. The skill trees create synergies between monsters, where one might poison opponents, and another allows that poison to spread or double stack. This combat can also make the game -MUCH MUCH- harder than pokemon. And as someone who usually plays games on easy/normal, it frustrated me from time to time.if you enjoy minmaxing and looking for the best combos this game has what you're looking for - If you want to spam your strongest attack and do nothing else.. Thats not going to work out. The game has a fantastic sense of progression, your creatures get more powerful every level, and your character unlocks new ways of moving like double jumps, creature assisted swimming or flight.All in all, while the end of the game was frustratingly difficult for a casual like me, this was a thoroughly enjoyable experience that i would've gladly paid double the price for. Pokemon and Temtem could learn a lot from this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Great game so far!  It's like a combination of the art style of Terraria and the collection and combat of Pokemon.  I would highly recommend this game (even at full price!) to anyone that is a fan of monster collecting and turn-based battles.  Even though it's early access, I'm really looking forward to seeing where the devs take this game.  Would like to see  an even larger variety of creatures to tame (like 200!)  :)
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game to be incredibly fun. I first heard about this game about a week ago. _childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Nice GameTook me like 40h to finish it (beat the last Boss), but you can explore more after the credits.If u like Pokemon and Metrovania games, then this is a game u will enjoy.After some hours i had to read some guides cause the difficulty level raises kinda after the first 2 areas.There is a online (pvp) arena but i didnt tested it. Like in pokemon you can use your different Monsters to advance in the Areas f. e. by abilities like shrinking, swimming or flying. _childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this on Kickstarter and I have to say the final release is excellent. I actually dropped it during EA because it was pretty incomplete, so returning to this after 1.0 has been a blast. It's a monster collector/battler (ie, Pokemon-like) in a metroidvania setting with some key differences.- All battles are triple battles - It is pure turn-based combat (ie, no speed stat to affect turn order)- Only 1 defense stat for both magic and physical damage reduction - You need to make use of the combo system effectively to actually clear content- There is no random encounters, all enemies are visible on the overworld- You 'capture' monsters by defeating them and obtaining their egg, which you can use to hatch into the said monster- Only certain monsters evolve, and pre-evolved monsters are no less viable than post-evolved mons - their skill sets are different. You can think of evolved monsters as different 'versions' of a monster rather than direct 'upgrades'.- You teach your monsters skills via their individual skill trees- No limit to how many monsters you can carry on your person, because...- Every monster has an exploration skill that helps you navigate the overworldThere's a good deal more to the game than just the above, but IMO playing it is going to be more helpful than reading a description.One thing I will note though, maximizing your party's effectiveness feels like you're playing competitive Pokemon, because of the battle score system. For some people this is going to be a big plus, but for others it might feel overwhelming. If you're in the latter group I'd recommend looking up some party builds other people have found useful and copy them until you find what feels good for you. Personally not a big fan of the battle score system because you get basically nothing if you don't consistently 5* battles, which usually requires a fairly well-optimized party. Regardless, exploration is satisfying, and leveling your mons doesn't feel like a grind. The EXP scaling/balance  feels excellent. There's plenty of metroidvania in here for people who want that, and there's plenty of Pokemon in here for people who want that.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: I generally had a good time with this game.  The monsters all have fun designs and the fundamental gameplay is pretty engaging (I generally don't enjoy turn based party combat.)  The exploration and team building are also enjoyable and I encountered no bugs or technical issues.  With that said, some fights get annoying or drag on a bit, even with the built in system to prevent that.  Regardless, I certainly got my money's worth out of it and feel comfortable recommending it.For context, I approached the game (on normal difficulty) by making one generalist team to handle every challenge without using consumables.  This was doable, and I'm glad I didn't have to build separate teams for each champion or keeper duels (essentially two variations of boss battles).  That said, I put a lot of thought into my team's skill trees to have answers for most weaknesses, damage types, and especially debuffs.  I also didn't like keeper duels enough to do the post game duels or several of the side objective duels and I only got 5 star ratings on a handful of champions.  So if you want to do literally everything the game has to offer, your mileage may vary.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game because it seemed super cute and fun, and I've always enjoyed games where you can raise creatures. RPG games are my favorite, by far. This game has a decent bit of content so far. There are plenty of monsters, lots of abilities, a decent chunk of map to explore, and more. However, there were a few sections of the map that were not yet implemented and I'm eager to see what you can do with them, as well as evolving the monsters with certain items and access to the tree needed to do this at. I've heard about a dragon monster and I'm REALLY eager to get that one. If you enjoy turn based strategy games that are more faster paced with cool pixel graphics and side-scrolling type behavior, this is definitely worth the buy. Especially considering it's not finished and they're going to add even more of what this game is so great at.

_childDocuments_.review: This game should have an Overwhelmingly Positive score so I'm gonna help try to get it there, it has a ton of great content and they just released a free DLC with even more. _childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Sanctuary is a mix of a Metroidvania and a JRPG (a JRPG very inspired by Pokémon) that shows how much a few twists can make and old formula feel great.I'll start with the most interesting and enjoyable feature of the game: the monster battle. The game, as I said before, feels inspired by Pokémon but I think it goes the extra mile and it isn't a "copy & paste". The first thing you will notice is that all the battles you use 3 monsters, this makes SO much sense because this allows the player to build a party that have sinergy and each mon can play a different role in the combat. This is the reason why Pokémon tournaments are 2v2 and not just 1v1 where you almost always avoid support or tank abilities in favor a damage ones. So... having 3 mons allows you to build a team, with different roles, but that its just half of the combat, the other half are the skills. The skills system is complex enough to make you feel that you are choosing how you want to build each mon, but it is simple to understand what each skill will do and how it will combine with each other. Each monster have between 3 and 5 skill tree to allocate points with different focuses (magic damage, physical damage, healing, shielding, buffing, debuffing, aoe, single target, etc etc etc).Ok, so I've discussed how the "JRPG part is" but how about the Metroidvania or the story? First lets talk about the exploration and platforming part. This part is really straight foward, playing you will face obstacles where you will need to acquire one of two things: a new power up for the character (as double jumping) OR a new mon that has an explore ability that you need (flying, swimming, mounting, etc.). The latter is what I think makes this game excel without making a game changing innovation in the classic metroidvania formula, it just let you choose (and see in action) what monster of your collection you want to help you and in what scenario, I think that this makes so much sense and makes you feel more engage on the game.Finally, the story. I must say that it isn't a story that shake my world and will keep it in my mind forever. It's simple, but it fulfills it's role to push you through the game.I want to give a shout out to the art style that, although being simple, it's beautiful. I love pixel art. PSA: If you want to have a full image of the monster, remember to go to the monster journal.100% Recommended. You like Metroidvania? Go for it. You like Pokémon-like games? Go for it.Also... it's a freaking perfect game to play via steam link on your phone.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Meaty math, good monsters, controls wellThe platforming/metroidvania aspect is a bit flat but if you look at it as a compliment or accessory to the core game (teambuilding) its fine. Story is barebones but unobtrusive which i appreciate. Levelling/acquisition/respeccing etc. is convenient so you can focus on building and not grinding.Music was largely forgettable with a few good piecesIf you like mathing out builds and combos from a diverse pool of skills, passives, and monsters you will adore this game
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: The game really grows on you.  The difficulty is subtle at first, feels like an older style RPG style.  There are however a ton of ways to optimize your monsters and be able to create unique teams.  Some of those are not really understood until you put enough time into the game.  If you wanted you could go through the entire game and not really get super deep into the strategy, but it really does reward you if you spend the time to construct a party that is optimal.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: That's a short, but good game. Probably around 10h of "discovering" (new creature, area, leveling for new attack...) before you really need to start grinding and testing new party composition (the game encourage you to do some sort of perfect combo, by giving you more stuff each fight if you do so).Since you get better loot if you find a better way to fight (each fight have a 5 (6 hidden) star rank), and the level max is limited, the grinding isn't that bad.The game is enjoyable, doesn't overstays his welcome and ask you to try new things often (while giving you new tools to do so - new monster mostly).Some QOL addition are here, like cheap item to reset your spec, or experience shared with backup party.The low pixel count can be annoying for some people but the game actually looks nice for this style (when you are into it), and the animations, even if always very short, are well done.The platforming is simple and average - not a problem by itself. The story and map layout is somewhat linear, some little secret here and here are a nice addition (and you need different type of monster to get them).Overall it's a good short game. I'd like to find game like this more often.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who used to love the Pokemon games, Monster Sanctuary really hits that sweet spot of strategic monster battling. It starts off simple, but as you learn more and more about the complexity of the game, you start to see how crazy battles can get. For me, the very *first* trainer battle against Will was harder than any entire Elite Four! But I learned a lot from it, and was excited to tackle even crazier stuff afterward.I'm not usually a fan of all the backtracking in Medroidvania-like games, but this one has a great teleporting system and an easy to use customizable map so you're not running around for hours aimlessly. Also love the fact that your familiar can remind you of what you're supposed to do at any point, which is super helpful when you come back to the game after a few days break.Tons of quality of life stuff, great post-game content, and huge depth of battle strategy/monster customization make nearly any monster viable in some way. My only negative is the actual story itself, which felt needlessly complicated, but the gameplay was so good I didn't even care.Also when in doubt... Magmapillar them out!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: I was a little skeptical going in. A pixel art metroidvania with creature collector mechanics? I like a good creature collector but platformers and metroidvanias are not really my cup of tea. I Generally hate backtracking and especially in metroidvanias, trying to remember where that one place was that had the one thing i couldn't do at the time. Luckily for me though, this game is fantastic.The Metroidvania stuff did kind of annoy me occasionally, however falling off a platform or hitting spikes or whatever was never much of a detriment as you just pop up on the last safe ground you were on with no repercussions, allowing you to retry as many times as you need to very quickly with no downside. The map also has a handy little marker you can set as well, so anytime i found something i couldn't do yet, i would just mark it on the map, label it what it was that was stopping me from going that way, and when i found the thing that let me pass it, it was easy enough to get back there and go do the thing.Where this game REALLY hooked me though was the amazing creature collector side of the gameplay. There are SO many build options for your team and strategies you can do. And because your monsters have skill trees, you can even make multiple teams with the same monsters work completely differently. The synergies you could line up between your monsters attacks and even what position you placed them on your team could really make a difference. There is so much more to the strategy than just "Hit the enemy with the element it's weak to" that so many other creature collector games pretty much completely revolve around.Since you hatch new monsters just a couple levels below the level of the ones in your party, switching out your monsters and your team strategy was quick and easy and the game showers you with level badges that you can give to your underleveled monsters and get them to just one level below your team as well so even if you want to try out that one monster that you have had in your inventory for a while and neglected, it's a trivial matter to get them into fighting shape again and play around with your build. You can also carry ALL of your monsters with you at all times instead of having to go back to a PC or some stupid garbage to switch out your team. All these quality of life decisions just make experimentation and build testing that much more fun and doable.All in all, this game hooked me so hard that even though i'm not typically the kind of person to replay games over and over again, I can't stop thinking about this game even after i have done everything. Seriously considering doing a new game+ run.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Yes this game is good.  The monster customization is compelling, and fielding a diverse team is really satisfying, and I'm a dude who loves squad customization and turn-based tactics.There are two things that suck about this game.  1 - As a metroidvania, it's really weak.  The platforming is more frustrating than anything, it adds nothing to the game besides being a nuisance, because it's never quite certain if you didn't make a jump because of the clumsy platforming or because you aren't SUPPOSED to yet.  This is the heart of why this game sucks as a metroidvania, is that ambiguity I mentioned where sometimes it isn't clear if you are missing something because you overlooked it or because you aren't *supposed* to be able to get to it yet.  The second thing that really stinks are the weird difficulty spikes.  I have been BREEZING through the Sun Palace area, and then when I get to the major encounter at the end of it, I am getting trounced.  Also happened with the first trainer duel.  Otherwise though its an excellent game and I suggest you pick it up if you enjoy the pokemon rock-paper-scissors counter team-building elements.  I'm having a blast despite my two qualms.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and cute. People mentioned the obvious link with pokemon but I think it's much closer to the early FF games (up to 6), as a party tactical RPG. Each monster has archetypes that you unlock via a skill-tree (damage dealer, healer, booster,etc or some combination ) and equip items and consumables. Each monster being some combinations of archetypes you need to mix and match them to have the perfect party.It's fun and quite addictive to try to find the perfect partners and combos, especially since almost any monster is viable. The game is easy up to the end where there is a big synergy check on your party via trainer battles that are in general more fun and challenging than monster or boss battles. If you like monster collection and/or turn&party based tactics you'll have fun with this.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write many reviews, but this game absolutely deserves it. I may be biased as a huge fan of monster training games, but this game is such a gem and truly masterfully made. Traversing the world feels good, and the music is excellent so the somewhat slow movement is made up for by being a generally relaxing experience. I love using the monsters outside of battle to interact with the environment, it reminds me of the pokemon ranger series. The game difficulty scales well, and you absolutely must use 5+ different monsters on your team, as the encounters are varied enough that you can't lean into a single team comp to carry you through the entire game. I have truly been captivated by this game, so I highly recommend getting it to anyone who is on the fence.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Such an amazing game. I played 100 hours on the Xbox version and this is one of my favourite games ever. The soundtrack is one i listen to regularly and the gameplay is really well made and very enjoyable. Just like Pokemon but different enough. Very chill mechanics and good difficulty that keeps you wanting to beat the next areas and bosses. The skill trees and mechanics can get quite deep, and despite the retro styling it feels like a modern game
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Great Creature Collection + Metroidvania game. Nice aesthetics, nice music, great selection of monsters to capture and use for combat and exploration. It doesn't hold your hand but it's only really difficult towards the end of the game. For its cost, it's a little gem. Really looking forward to see what more can this people do in their future projects.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: The battling system is quite fun, with skilltrees for each unit that can be customized to your playstyle or team setup.But there are several underlying issues:- Story is incredibly linear  - Because of the linear story, many monsters cannot be unlocked until you've progressed areas    - By the time you unlock the monsters lategame, the partylevel will be at a point where it's not really worth grinding- Getting stuck in areas due to the vague indications on what the player has to do next is frustrating- Majority of the time the player will be walking from zone-to-zone. There are very few fast-travel locations but the player has the option to use an item to fast-travel. There are a finite amount of those.- The artstyle is fun, but it gets boring since the game uses zones/areas to seperate parts of the story. Meaning that the player will be looking at the same style and facing the same monsters for long periods of time which feels very tedious and grindy.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: The game is all in all entertaining. The difficulty is alright. Random battles against monsters are fast enough, and the bosses typically require some amount of tactics to make it through.The balance is fairly good, though it varies quite a bit which abillities are good/satisfying to use. Catzerkers f.ex. gain random buffs when critting. You can get their crit chance high enough that they get basically every buff when they use a multi-hit area-of-effect attack. Other minions just heal, which isn't fantastic when some enemies will one-shot you. I get the impression that the developers are trying to balance everything, so that might improve. It is currently "good enough" to reccomend, especially to fans of monster-collector games.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Sanctuary is one of the best, if not the best, game of its genre I have ever played. The artwork and music are an easy 10/10. The developers are also very active in the community and their passion for this game is apparent. I think the biggest change from a game like Pokemon is that in Monster Sanctuary, every monster is viable. There are some that are better, but thanks to the complex battle system, different monsters can shine with the correct synergies. The gameplay itself would take an entire article to accurately describe how in depth it is, however, it is not too difficult that only hardcore gamers can really enjoy all the game has to offer. There is a fairly active PVP scene, albeit mainly for Steam. I have purchased this game initially for switch, then for xbox so I could play with some of my friends, and finally I purchased for Steam solely for the PVP.  There is also a tournament youtube channel that showcases top tier gameplay.The game does have some replayability , but I burnt out after the 6th new game. That being said, I am still playing this game very frequently, the teams you can make seem to be endless.I cannot recommend this game enough. There is also free DLC coming later this year, with a substantial amount of content coming as well as changes to existing monsters both in appearance and gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a wonderful game, if you're not having fun playing this game I don't know what to tell you. Each monster feels unique, random encounters have a decent difficulty, NPCs battles are really good, All Boss fights are amazing, they really make you think on how to build your team around almost each fight as they are really hard to do if you're going for a perfect score, story is decent enough, it does it's job. There are certain really cute and great moments, exploring feels great when you're in a new place, the game makes you feel good when you solve a puzzle, my only complain about exploring is back tracking, sometimes it feels the teleports are too far apart and you have to walk way too much in low leveled areas. Don't remember saying this and I'm too lazy to read over this whole thin but, ALL monsters feel unique and there are so many ways in which you can choose to play each one of them (I played with 2 Blobs (slimes) in my main team and we killed god together 10/10, if anyone is curious their names are Bob (regular slime) and Bobce (Ice slime) ), I still have to finish a lot of optional challenge bosses and NPC fights, have to catch 5 more monsters before having full journal and I got a say, this game brings me joy 10/10 in everything it does.If you did read all of that, I salute to you o7
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: For $8.99, this is the best pokemon game I've played so far! Especially better than the last like 10 years of pokemon. It's fun, the art is good, the use of creature abilities to interact with the world is awesome, and you can customize your creatures skill trees too??? Brilliant game, and, frankly, worth it at full price too!
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent spin on the monster battler genre. Each monster having its own skill tree is really cool. Add that to monsters having a weapon and 3 accessories, plus 'EV training' with food and you have a LOT of customization available. Tying loot to combat performance means you're always encouraged to perform well. Fully healing after each battle means fights can be independently challenging instead of just existing to grind down your HP until you get to the next pokemon center. As somebody who burnt out on the stale gameplay of Pokemon over a decade ago, this is a glimpse into what Pokemon could be if Gamefreak/Nintendo gave a ♥♥♥♥ enough to innovate a little bit. An absolute steal when on sale, and great for Steam Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: I gave it a good shot but not for me. Capture monsters and have them fight reminds me of pokemon. Each monster has a good amount of options to choose how to build. As well as feeding and gearing them up. I couldn't get a good team going. I did some poison and fire build but then that stopped working so needed to change the team and it was just annoying to me. Lots of options in this game but that just made it more confusing for me to choose and in the end felt like i needed to grind more than I wanted to.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Much better than it looks at first glance. Surprisingly in depth combat system, and can feel quite rewarding to put together a strong monster composition together that compliments each other well.Monster design, story, and dialogue can feel a bit underwhelming compared to its obvious competitors, but the execution on game mechanics is strong enough to make up for those short falls.Doesnt reinvent the wheel, just does what its trying to do well.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Almost 46 hours to complete all achievements.Very fun turn based game. You only get a small handful of evolutions in the game and they aren't all that game changing but what you get instead is a large skill tree on every monster that you can spec through manually as they level up. This makes building your own team a lot more fun than most of the turn based games I've played.You also deck out your monsters with an assortment of attachments and weapons that further adds to building your own team of monsters.I never felt crippled from bad choices with choosing team members that didn't fit my team because it gives you items to bring other monsters up to your max monster level and future monsters you obtain scale up to your highest monsters level so you can experiment throughout the game mostly freely. I replaced my entire team at least 4 times throughout the game to try different playstyles. I never had to grind any levels.Respecing the monster skill trees are simple to do.Monsters offer a large variety of skills to be used outside of fights for traversal, it feels a lot like getting a new powerup in super metroid that unlocks new areas i've passed.Difficulty is solidly balanced. I had trouble with a few legendary fights after beating the game but it was great, it really made me dig in to build the best team I could to win the fight in the final stretch of the games content.Biomes feel very different from each other which is a nice change of pace. It didn't feel samey.The pixel art is very well done. Monsters feel consistent in art style.Music is fitting.Monster variety is varied. Story is alright. It isn't bad and it isn't world changing. You're the hero so do the hero thing. The one and only problem I had with the game was completing the map for a achievement. There is a false ceiling you can pass through in the beach biome, there are no other false ceilings in the game so I had no idea that was even a thing. There is no reason to believe you can jump through the solid rock. Either make it consistent through the game or give me a reason to believe that there is a false ceiling. This only really matters to people wanting the achievement as the hidden room doesn't server a purpose except for 100%ing and getting a sword you can just get through a crate somewhere else.Very fun and awesome game.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best monster taming game on the market, with a generous amount of metroidvania in the mix. The artstyle is cute and all the monsters feel unique and alive with their animations. The gameplay is dangerously addicting, with an incredible amount of customization and quality of life improvements that other games in the same genre haven't achieved yet. All the monsters are viable and feel powerful with the right set up, and even if there's only 100 monsters the team building experience, the equip system and the shifting give a lot of variety and replayability to the game. You can easily break the game with the right team composition, but it's not required unless you play the higher difficulties or aim for the 5 star champions. There's even light platform mechanics and some enigmas that break up the pace of the fights. I loved the ost, it's really really well done. Can't say the same for the plot, it's just basic, nothing breathtaking, it's simply all right. If you're fan of Pokemon/other monster taming games and want a really balanced, addictive gameplay, buy this one. It's often on sale, 6 bucks it's even too little for this gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: Metroidvania meets Monster Collecting.  This is an easy to learn, difficult to master turn based RPG.   Since three monsters fight at a time, the team compositions and synergies come with a great deal of customization.  In addition, resources needed to re-spec your monsters and improve gear are plentiful and easy to locate, which is good because without a solid team strategy, fights become very difficult.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't a bad game in terms of Metroidvania.  The abilities you get are pretty bland, such as .  It's sort of a mix of Metroidvania and Pokemon in a sense.  When you encounter enemies, you go into an RPG-style monster battle.  Sometimes wild monsters drop an egg item you can use to get that monster.  Each monster has its own level, strengths and weaknesses, various attack types, and a semi-unique skill tree.  As you progress through different areas, you have to figure out what monsters to put in your party that are strong against the monsters found in that area.The story isn't half bad and has a fair amount of dialog, although plot twists are few.The game does have some good quality of life features.  For example, when a monster is max level, you continue to "level up" with that monster.  Each time you fill the exp bar again, you instead get an item that allows you to give that level to a different monster, so you aren't throwing exp in the garbage by using your best monsters.  It would be a shame to feel like you were wasting exp by using them right after they .One sharp criticism I do have of the game is that the difficulty curve turns into a rather sharp spike with "RNG" written on it.  Up until you get to that point, the difficulty is pretty mild.  48 hours in and nearly at the end, I called it out of frustration from losing constantly.  I decided to go back and give it another try because I really hate to lave a game unfinished like that, and guess what?  RNG is a fickle thing.  I blasted through the last several bosses with the same party I was already using without losing once.  It does have a difficulty setting you can adjust, but the RNG toward the end is lethal on any setting.All in all, I enjoyed the game except for getting frustrated with the RNG near the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Are you the kind of person who gets super attached to their monsters/units and is constantly anxious that they'll have to leave them behind when they become obsolete? Well, here it's entirely possible to beat the final boss with the very first blob you've hatched in the tutorial . In fact, I'd say that every single monster is viable - as long as you play into its strengths. No need to worry about IV, EV, no endless grinding; just team building and strategy.The game almost feels more like Monster Train than Pokemon; it's less about having the perfect monster with just the right moves and exploiting weaknesses - rather, it's about creating those cascading synergies of destruction which hopefully will end your opponent before they end you. Yes, exploiting weaknesses is a thing here as well, but it's just one piece of the strategic puzzle - one that sometimes is better discarded in favour of a more synergic course of action.Alas, this is also something that can be seen by many as bad; You see, for a big chunk of the game you can get away with playing Monster Sanctuary as if it was Pokemon. Buffs, debuffs and synergies are just nice-to-haves, but we know it's all about that "super effective" raw crit damage. Right? Well, at a certain moment - which, sadly, is in the final stretch of the game - you're being told: Stop. You're playing the game wrong. Here's an opponent that actually uses buffs and debuffs strategically, and they will  you if you don't have a properly built team. If you explore a lot, you'll probably run into one of the super champions before then - and they'll teach you this lesson a little earlier; but you'll still have to get down to it, read the skill descriptions and make a team that's got good synergy.That said, the team building is as streamlined as possible. Each monster has 3-5 separate skill trees which usually focus on different possible roles; you can immediately see all of them and plan ahead. You can also very easily respec your monster, or hatch a new one which will be only slightly behind your strongest level. And no worries; you can save teams for later use - and there's more slots than you can possibly need.There's a lot more to say about the battles, but enough is enough. You get the idea. It's great, and generally grindless. Let's talk about the aesthetic for a bit.It looks great, that's plain to see. Every monster is fully animated - walking, jumping, attacking. And the monster compendium has wonderful, detailed pictures of each and every single monster. On a Cute/Cool scale, they tend to fall towards Cute, but that doesn't prevent many of them from being cool as well. Areas are varied and each of them has their own unique feel, even if from a pure level design perspective they're more or less the same. And the music? It's a bit of a mixed bag in my opinion. Some early game pieces feel... I don't know, uninspired? But as you keep going, the music gets better and better, all the way to the end. One piece in particular has a very specific feel - it's meticulously made to sound like it's from Terranigma, an old SNES classic which happens to be a favourite of mine. It's so spot on that I refuse to believe it's a coincidence - and why would it be? Monster Sanctuary is a German game, and the biggest fan community of Terranigma is also in Germany.The story is also a little weird. There's nothing wrong with it per se - I enjoyed it, and there's a lot of interesting lore everywhere. Something about the way the characters speak is... unusual. And the story itself is very plain, not many twists and no real structure... in a way, it feels less like a story and more like something that's actually happening. That's a good thing? Maybe? Unusual, like I said.All in all, the game is fantastic. I enjoyed it greatly, and towards the end I simply couldn't put it down. I'd even go so far to call this game a masterwork - at least as far as its general design and individual systems are concerned. If we lived in a fair, meritocratic world, Monster Sanctuary would be death knell of Pokemon; kids would wear Blob backpacks to school and we'd have a Hollywood release of Detective Catzerker. Instead we live in a world ruled by marketing budgets and trend-driven design; luckily, you can escape this world at least a little bit and play Monster Sanctuary.And remember, love your Blobs, and they will love you back!

_childDocuments_.review: Concept sounds amazing, but the game disappoints.It feels like a chore early on and fails to hit that metroidvania vibe pretty hard. I feel like if either one of the issues was fixed the game would be amazing.Turn based combat heavily relies on balance to feel fun. If you can mow through the enemies without paying attention or cannot beat the enemies without some meta build and strategy (outside of hardest fights) it's like a death sentence to a turn based combat game. This game hits both ends of balancing problems, because the start is tediously easy and people claim the end is too hard.The monsters have elements and elemental weaknesses. There's little to no reason to exploit those weaknesses early in game, because neutral (non-elemental) skills consistently outperform the elemental ones that the enemy is weak to. This is a recipe for boring combat.I tried using different monsters and all of them feel identical because incentive to use weaknesses is just not there and early buffs are 100% useless. I literally spammed my highest damage skills at everything and only switching when my the enemy had resistances against my element (not often). That resulted in new monster acquisitions not feeling as exciting as they could be. Think about the last metroidvania you enjoyed. It likely had 1 of 2 things: really fun action combat (clearly not in this game) or really fun exploration. This game looks like a metroidvania, with it's map design, (monster) ability gated "secrets" and 2d side-scrolling, but it doesn't feel like one, because it fails to make exploration feel exciting. Since the first area of the game you are showered with generic stat-stick gear. When you have all that gear, unlocking a "secret" door and getting another piece of generic stat-stick gear you don't even pay attention to it. As a result, visiting an optional area feels more like something you HAVE to do for completion rather than something you WANT to do for a chance of an exciting reward.For what its worth this indie studio had a vision of something that hasn't been done before and followed through and I respect that. With that said I expect core aspects of any game to be polished to the point they are engaging. In this game's case I feel like proper balance (from start to finish) would be the biggest priority, because it's the boring fights, where I just waited for animations to finish, that made me quit. I doubt many people will enjoy it enough to finish it, so I won't recommend it until something changes.

_childDocuments_.review: A great game even in it's current unfinished state. My only gripe is the timed puzzles, which can be frustrating. Other than that it's a solid, fun and addictive game. You play as a monster keeper. Killing monsters in the wild gives you a chance to obtain an egg from them. The egg can be hatched instantly from inventory and be used right away if you want. You have an active team of 6 monsters which all gain xp from your fights, even though you can only actively use 3 at a time. All 6 can potentially be used against Champion monsters, but no more than 3 at a time. A great mechanic allowing you to experiment with different monsters. There are no set classes as such, but some monsters have skill trees which let them either be better at buffing and healing, AoE og single target dps. You can do damage with any monster, but where the game really shines is the syngery between monsters. For example - some do more damage the more buffs they have, regardless of what the buff itself actually enhances. The fights themselves makes me thing of old JRPG's and I love it. Actions are selected from drop down menus and is easy to get started with. You can also upgrade your monsters gear, but I wish they would add in actual crafting as well. There are many monsters in game already and it feels very fleshed out. I've done all the available areas, but still enjoy the game. I try out new teams or play endless mode, which is quite fun. You can also challennge any Champions again as much as you like in the Sanctuary. So to summarize; Timed puzzles are pure stress and frustration in pixel form, everything else works. Thankfully there aren't many timed puzzles and almost all of them can be skipped if you don't mind missing out on a little bit of treasure.

_childDocuments_.review: Gifted to me by my friend Indraw as a christmas present.I would say i am currently halfway through the story of the game as of writing this review.Do i recommend Monster Sanctuary? YES! Without a single doubt. This is by far the best metroidvania i have played made post-2010, the level of polish is through the roof and everything just... Works! You can really tell this is a labour of love, and I have yet to encounter a single bug or glitch - so far NO playstyles seem "unviable". From a lighthearted yet extremely detailed lore to the fun, casual yet incredibly complex skill and combat system, the gameplay of Monster Sanctuary is something i haven't really experienced anywhere else. It's casual and fun, but at the same time very intelligent. The visuals resemble Starbound, while the general platforming, puzzles and world progression pacing is akin to Castlevania itself. Combat plays out like Final Fantasy, while the primary gameplay element is more akin to a Pokemon or Digimon game.Looking at the gameplay system itself in more detail, it LOOKS deceptively simple - if you have played games like Final Fantasy, you'll be familiar with it already. However, the degree of customization over your team compositions, what they can do and all the myriad ways every individual monster interacts with all the others you can put together in a team is outright staggering. Despite how relaxing the overall tone of the game is and the gameplay itself, composing a trio of monsters is an activity that can make you think HARD to properly optimize everything. And so far, i am not anywhere near running out of content, nor does the game feel grindy in the least - for a game with an on-rails story like this, i expected it to last perhaps 20 hours at most. Yet here i am 40 hours later, and i THINK i have only reached the halfway point.The music is charming but the earlier tracks can quickly get a little repetitive. The later soundtracks do not have this issue - as you get further into the game and unravel more of it's story, the music always suiting newer areas well will only get you further immersed. If there is any complaint i can think of, it's that i know the game will end eventually. I'll definitely want more! If you enjoy Metroidvanias, RPGs (whether combo-oriented or not), super cute pixel-art games or just a very well-developed fictional world, Monster Sanctuary is certain to get you HOOKED. There is no real "wrong" way to play, though it certainly helps to be quick to grasp complex mechanics and numbers!

_childDocuments_.review: I think that when reviewing games, it's always important to give a frame of reference for where your opinions are coming from.  Hi, I'm Zantoma.  I usually stick to multiplayer games.  I don't have much experience with RPGs or Metroidvania-style games, but I have played several, though mostly many years ago.  (Paper Mario 64, Golden Sun 1 + 2, Darkest Dungeon, Metroid Fusion + Zero Mission + Prime 1/2 are the most notable examples.) I do love me some Pokemon though, so the idea of a monster collecting game with elements of the exploration of a Metroid game seemed interesting to me. When it eventually made it to the front of my backlog, I could barely pull myself away from it.  I may only have 32 hours played listed as of this review, but it's worth noting that that playtime was put in across three days total.  I only stopped because I ran out of game to play.  As of this writing, I have completed all of the Steam achievements and optional challenge fights.  I found it to be pretty delightful all things considered.  A few elements in no particular order; Exploration - Pretty fun experience, I accidentally wandered my way into areas considerably more advanced than I was a few times and found the backtracking with new abilities interesting.  Each of the monsters having their own exploration ability gave me more of a reason to collect all of them, and I very nearly caught 'em all by the end of my playthrough because I didn't want to miss any of the exploration abilities.  The game could communicate some of the required tools a little better.  I went through most of the game wondering if I was doing something wrong with a certain interactable but it turned out to just require a late game exclusive ability.  The exploration abilities remind me of like a map psynergy from Golden Sun  or a partner ability from Paper Mario or a Pokemon HM, except it also encouraged me to snap up every monster I could find to look for new toys.Story - don't care lol, did its job, not much to say about it, not particularly interesting.  That's fine with me.Combat - Heavily buff/debuff/dot focused system.  Not really much Pokemon inspiration here imo, but like I said at the top, I haven't played many RPGs.  There seemed to be a variety of viable strategies from poisoning and burning enemies to boosting up allies for massive crits to infinitely stacking bleeds.  There is a combo system where the monsters that act later in your turn will have stronger attacks, so it encourages you to run at least one buff or heal focused monster which helps avoid the ingame Pokemon strategy of "hit it until it dies".  I found the unique equipment effects to be generally pretty interesting, and enjoyed checking out each monster's semi-unique skillset each time I snagged one for their exploration ability.  Battles occasionally got stalled out for fairly long periods of time, but I didn't mind that aspect too much, since it was mostly because I wasn't utilizing good counters to what opponent lineups were doing.  There was a mass buff "critical mass" sort of gameplay in those endgame fights, where I just had to build up enough power to eventually shatter my opponent's buffed up monsters, and then the reinforcements were immediately put down the following turn.  I know of at least two ways I could've avoided most of this through teambuilding, so I'm going to chalk that one up to possible user error. On the topic of those semi-unique skillsets, in addition to each monster having its exploration ability, they also each have a customizeable skill tree that lets you choose what active and passive skills each monsters have.  Many of the abilities are shared between similar monsters, but each of the game's 101 species (as of this writing) has a different combination of the four trees that they can fill out.  As an example, a basic Blob (slime) can focus on lowering enemy damage output, dealing extra hits to set up combos with unaspected or water damage, healing allies, or poisoning and otherwise inconveniencing enemies.  Mine served me well until it was replaced with an upgraded version toward the end of the game.  Difficulty - Felt like a pretty smooth experience.  The 6v6 battles against NPCs were significantly harder than the open-world 3v3s, but I didn't have to adapt my strategy too terribly much beyond adding a second party for backup or situational counters.  I see the other reviews talking about a late game difficulty spike, but I didn't really feel that too much, so it may have been changed in a patch.  I think throughout the story and all optional content, there were only 2-3 battles I had to try more than once or change my team for, and that includes 5*ing all of the graded fights.  I'd say that overall I felt like the difficulty was "pleasant" playing on "normal" for the first time, not too easy, not too hard.  I probably would've set it to be on "Master" difficulty if it had been an option at the start of the game rather than set mid-game, and that may have suited my tastes a bit better as a Darkest Dungeon enjoyer.There didn't seem to be very much grinding - I almost hit level cap by the final boss, and just had to do a couple of random encounters to ding max level before taking a crack at it.  Future monsters were very easy to train up thanks to the generous amount of "rare candies" you get, plus the high starting level newly hatched eggs came at.  Getting a new Monster battle-ready for me at this point in the game is as simple as equipping held items, leveling it up a few times with consumables I have laying around in piles, and then filling out its skill tree.  Very accessible and easy to flex new party members in.  Overall, I quite enjoyed this game.  It isn't something I'd play for thousands of hours like Dota, but it's just a nice little game, and the world needs more nice little games.  Heavy recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: I can say without exaggeration that this is one of the most fun games I’ve played.Monster Sanctuary never crossed my radar for whatever reason, despite my enjoyment of Metroid-vania games and monster battle games. I might never have noticed it if it wasn’t for my brother who gifted me a copy.This game is about half Metroid-vania – a 2D platformer where you explore a world and gradually open up new areas by finding new exploration powers and weapons. The other half is a monster battle game like Pokémon or Temtem where you capture and build up a team of monsters that do your fighting for you and frequently battle other monster trainers. What makes this game great is the blending of the two elements. The monsters provide the exploration abilities as well as the fighting team.Just that description isn’t the whole story, however. The game is far more deep than most monster battlers as each monster has three or more talent trees and not enough points to max them all out. You might have one green slime built to poison enemies, another copy of the exact same monster built to heal your party, and a third specialized into direct damage. The 100+ monsters in the game give you a complex web of buffs, debuffs, attacks, heals, and combination abilities that blur the categories. You can maximize the power of a monster with gear, food, and talent choices, but the real fun is in building teams that synergize.I have a problem with finishing games. I will often get close to the end and my interest will wander for six months or so. This is one of the few games where I got my copy and played straight through to the end non-stop. I stopped right before the final boss to collect the last few items and write this review. There isn’t much else to say. This game is incredibly fun with a cool story, fun mechanics, huge amounts of replay-ability, and a lot of fun things to do after beating the main quest.
_childDocuments_.name: Monster Sanctuary

_childDocuments_.review: The Main Game:Combat is incredibly deep with many many factors at play at any given time but the best part is you can actually learn how to use these to your advantage and make the most out of a team. A core part of this game is that every monster is entirely viable, from the common Blob to the mysterious G'rulu, you just have to learn what their strengths are and how to amplify them through synergy and combo counters. There are both trainer battles and Champions, extremely powerful individual monsters who serve as a test of your strength who can be obtained if you receive 5 stars on the combat evaluation. A final note on combat is the existence of a mechanic called Shifting, where any monster can be given a special consumable and gains a buff to their stats, an ability and a colour change just for the shiny hunters out there. That combined with the immense options provided through the skill trees lets a single monster have the choice of almost any role in some cases.Additionally, the exploration side of the game is vast, even at 64 hours the one achievement I'm missing is to explore the entire map - there are secret rooms and passages everywhere with progression locked behind discovering new types of monsters who can aid you should you obtain them. Lastly, the plot isn't exactly thrilling but it makes sense and gives structure to the game which I can appreciate.Post-game and PVP:In the post-game you can find all the remaining Champions and even Elite Champions who can prove to be challenging if you aren't prepared but by that point you should have a solid grasp of how to win fights of attrition, debuffs such as poison and burn are welcomed. One last note is there's a gamemode called Infinity Arena which is pretty much how it sounds, each battle makes the enemies rise in levels whilst you struggle against them and get rewarded handsomely based on your performance.I personally have not done much PVP yet, 7 battles and I only won 2 of the 7 but because of a steam exploit someone basically gained a win by forfeiting but it somehow counting as a win for themselves and a loss for me which was a bit annoying. There is also no matchmaking currently so you'll be thrown against max level teams even when you're at level 10 and there isn't a way to directly challenge your friends yet but these are both fixes planned for the near future on the dev teams roadmap along with many other enhancements to look forward to.Conclusion:It's Pokemon but with far more depth, exploration, no stupid mechanics like EVs or IVs that will make you waste hours or days to make a team whereas in monster sanctuary it takes about an hour at most to make a team from scratch ready for PVP or Infinity Arena. Plus meme teams like goblins only or blobs only are actually viable.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game after I saw I had a coupon for it due to another game in my library. BEST COUPON EVER. Like I don't even know where to start in recommending this to someone but DAMMIT I WILL TRY.    So let's start with the visuals. Honestly, they are nothing special. Now, don't get me wrong, they look great in the sprite-work and the monsters are both simple yet creative for the most part (the starting monsters are a little basic but do work nicely to kickoff the rest of the game). It's just that it looks like I can do all of the terrain in gamemaker within a day no problem - but hey, it looks good so I'm not complaining.    The story as of right now is barebones. Clearly they're setting it up and from what we know it is a nice story premise for sure. The only main issue with it is that it doesn't really gain traction until a little bit later in the game and even then it is nothing big story defining. I will say though it is nice to play the first few hours of the game at your own pace without the game making you feel like you should follow a storyline to get more out of your experience. I have high hopes for the story aspect of this game.   Controls are simple and tight. Excellent since this is a platformer in addition to being an rpg.   Okay time for the gameplay talk. I noticed people are comparing this to pokemon and while I agree there are similarities, this game not only does them differently but also shakes up the combat entirely. Easily the best aspect of this game is the way you get monsters. Each monster has an egg (including bosses) that require you to get a high rating after you win the battle. Based on how well you stacked your moves, how little damage you took and how many turns it took to win, you can get as high as a 5 star rating which basically guarantees you get the monster egg. I LOVE this system. No longer is it really a matter of if you win but a matter of how WELL you can win. This makes every fight as you progress become engaging as you need to develop a strategy on how to make the most effective win happen. As for the monsters, they all have a few sets of skill trees that allow you to really customize the role of that monster. This helps make getting the same monsters still fresh and exciting since now you can really alter what this new one does for the team. And the difficulty is bliss. Never did I feel like I deserved to lose and even being WAY underleveled for the hardest difficulty battle in the tower, I still barely managed to pull out a W by playing it with a perfect strategy and correct enemy focusing to ensure they can't use their extremely tough strategy. Another aspect MS shares with pokemon is having a party of monsters that need experience from battling in order to get stronger and learn new abilities. However, MS makes the exp share between all of them make sense, meaning that the ones who did not fight only get a little while the ones in the battle get way more (as they should). Type effectiveness is crucial in all fights unlike in pokemon and monsters evolving is something that happens but in my time with the game it only became a thing to do after the 10 hour mark or so for me. I like this as it means I don't have to grind out monsters just so they are usable and I can enjoy their base forms a lot more before they change entirely.    Overall, this game is an absolute gem. Its exploration - which I just realized I did not mention - is intriguing and feels like metriod. The music has its charm rooted in the simple yet pleasing visuals. The gameplay is superb and I wish this was done in more games. If you do not have this game yet and are interested in literally anything I said BUY IT! It's worth trust! I cannot wait for when this game is fully complete!

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't written a review for a while, but felt like this game deserved it. It's basically a metroidvania-esque pokemon type game. _childDocuments_.review: I played through the demo twice already, probably putting ~16 hours into it. Just the demo.This game is so good, so satisfying to play, I actually went to try and beat every challenge, get every rare monster, search out and find every single possible corner to explore, maxed most monsters and tried multiple builds on my favorites.This game is an absolute masterpiece.I dont even like pokemon but this game just hits the nail on the head.The music is nostalgic and catchy, the monsters have multiple very theme fitting skill trees to mix and match. If you dont like physical damage on your spectral wolf, make him a ice nuker, if you dont like magic damage on your slime, turn him into a healing machine.Every time I feel like I have 'the team' I want for the rest of the game, some cool new monster comes around with a different mechanic that makes me want to try them out. I remember trying shield stacking for supporting and sustain, trying to get as many buffs as possible to be spammed in one single turn, trying to burst down enemies before they can act, debuffing them so they basically cant act. And now that I'm returning to the game, all of the above has been retouched, rebalanced and expanded upon. With only more to come. The game had an astounding amount of build variety with just 2 tiers of skills during the demo phase of the game, now there's 3 tiers of skills with a 4th one on the way. The amount of builds to try is growing and it was already large before. Like I said I spent most of my demo time trying out different possibilities on all the monsters. Unless this genre just doesnt seem appealing to you, this game basically will satisfy you. The combat starts a little basic, but the higher level you go the more complicated it can get. I'm not sure how the balance pans out because the ceiling of power is higher than before so I'll have to update this if I run into any problems when I get there.But man... This game is just great...

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Sanctuary does a LOT of stuff very, very well:Plenty of Monsters with a large mix of 2-4 attacks, heals, shielding, buffing, inflicting status effects.Good amount of status effects, how good they are depends on your passive abilities and the enemy monsters.Good amount of buffs, infinite duration during a battle! Yes, no more "refresh every 3 turns" monsters necessary! But buffs can be removed by other monsters with special abilities, so you'd have to recast them.Very good equipment system: All Monsters get equipped with weapons+accessories which boost certain stats. You might make a tank with high defense and shielding abilities, a critical hit buffer, a magic nuker etc.Each Monster has mana, but it also regenerates mana each turn. You can use equipment to boost regeneration. You can use status effects to decrease enemy mana regeneration. You can decrease mana cost or have special passive skills which regenerate mana. Very well made!Minimal grinding required, "catching" new Monsters will always be near your level, even from low level areas. You also get enough "rare candy"You can buy "skill resetters" for cheap, letting you completely change Monster builds whenever you wantNo limit on Monsters you can carry around. Battles are 3v3 with +3 backup, meaning you use 3-Monster combos. Save/Load option for teams, you can switch out whenever you want. Monsters can be traded for rewards, if you want to clean out. Or you can store them away.Metroidvania platforming, but the abilities you unlock are actually Monster abilities. Cool! A buyable return-to-home item. A few fast travel spots.Leveling is very fast. Reaching max level on any Monster will earn you a "rare candy".Multiple special miniboss monsters. You can catch them too, but only if you beat them effectively. You can also rebattle them as often as you like and get the max reward later. They will be at your level too.Fairly difficult trainer fights! Losing a battle does not screw you over - you get reset to where you were standing before the battle, no loss of progress. You can then try again, or change your team, or leave and come back later.I spent half my time playing just thinking and planning of new teams - teams which use a ton of buffs, teams which stack multiple status effects, teams which keep charging up one nuker and one shot minibosses, there are TONS of ways to build teams.ABSOLUTELY RECOMMENDED!

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Sanctuary is a really fun pokemon-like metroidvania. The skill system is easy to grasp but can be quite versatile. _childDocuments_.review: It's an excellent team battler with lots of flexibility when it comes to team comp and tactics, but is held back in certain areas via execution.Pros:+ Diverse monster pool, even enemies that look like reskins can have very different skill trees and may in fact form a solid combination with each variety of the species fulfilling a different role on the team, from damage to debuffing to healing and more+ Excellent art which continues to be improved, it's great to see a game like this getting so much focus on it's core such as NPC design and areas instead of rapidly spreading too thin+ Many opportunities to respec teams to demo new strategies. While resets aren't immediately available, you get a very generous amount of the items for it throughout the game and by the time you are in late-game getting more is still easy unless you are resetting a truly obscene amount+ While you get the option to specialize your team members through the light/dark system, attempts are made to also promote keeping a creature neutral with neutral-exclusive items+ Monster evolution isn't the end-all decision for species. While evolved forms DO often have more powerful abilities, their pre-evolutions tend to have more support focused skills and can be excellent support without ever being evolved+ The shops stay relevant throughout the game, while often giving you options a tier below the absolute best available through exploration, I never felt like the shops became totally irrelevantCons:- Leveling can become extremely slow come late-game. You will be fighting the same end-game enemies many times over if you want to level monsters to the cap. These monsters appearing in teams of three and often specializing in tactics to drag fights out can make this particularly frustrating if your preferred monsters do poorly against stalling tactics.- Unlocking boss monsters requires getting a high score on their fights, but refights with bosses let them scale to your team's level, often outpacing your ability to actually kill them fast enough for any sort of time bonus, since time bonuses do not factor fight level, it is strictly based on number of actions. Using stall and debuffs on a boss instead of nuking damage? Too bad, your bonus from buff usage will not bridge the gap on points you are losing for not blitzing the fight, which can feel very punishing for a game with wide team selection. Maybe an even more powered-up form that guarantees a drop would be a middle-ground? Normally I would just take the hint and build a team to specialize in boss fights, but teams of that nature are often horrendous in trainer fights where survivability and crippling the other team's sweepers is much more essential. As is, I just think it would be a lot of grinding for creatures I wouldn't want to bring to a trainer fight- Small methods of the scoring can be bothersome such as your health rating ONLY caring about what your health is at the end of each turn cycle. It doesn't matter if you have a buff/debuff/regen system up that makes you virtually immortal, if an enemy gets a critical combo on you and drains one of your monsters for a turn, you just took a big hit to your health score.Final Status: Strongly recommendThe game continues to be improved and the developer is releasing content that addresses issues reliably (not many monsters available for construct buffs? Release a new area about constructs!) For the price I think it gives a good diversion and will only become more rewarding in the future. I look forward to more evolution options and a larger beastiary
