_childDocuments_.review: At the time of early access launch I feel in love with the game even though limited to what you do it has so much potential and I happily stayed to watch it grow and develop and I don't regret it one bit! Sure the game has had it's fair share of bugs but it's one single developer and Robert that solo developer is amazing, he speaks with his community and goes out his way to try and deal with these bugs and issues as quickly as he can. The way he always listens to the feedback and suggestions from the official suggestion forms for the game, and more just really shows inside the game itself as it's developed. The old tutorial that was difficult and didn't explain really anything at all have been remade completely, the old one is out the window and a brand new one is near perfect for newer players. The way the tutorials now work I can't help but adore the new tutorial that even gives the characters more life and personality than before as you go through it. The design tool/bench to create your own custom designs, items and furniture is really great, it really is the best feature in the game and now for those who don't like or still practising with the bench/tool can now use pre-built designs (only limited ones so far but have heard more could be coming!) using a brown book icon.  Though with the tutorial you do need to actually read all the prompts and such, I know many don't seem to for some reason haha.Many compare the game to animal crossing, even more so at the launch of early access and back then it was easy to see it that way but since then, will all the major updates like farming, mayor merits, narrative and so many more it really can stand on it's own two feet. This how I strongly feel myself for the game. It has areas where you can relate to animal crossing but at the same time it can also feeling like a different game as you play it yourself compared to seeing gameplay/watching it. With more updates hinted that are yet to come I can't wait to see what else is coming, seeing this game grow since early access until now has just been an amazing experience to really see it become it's own game that can stand on it's own feet if given the chance.Then there's the community. The official discord server is a great place filled with so many amazing and kind people who are willing to help answer questions, help you deal with bugs and to fill out a actual bug report form so that the bug can be dealt with. The steam forms slowly and surely have been growing with more life along side the screenshots and the "artwork" page for the game growing. I personally highly recommend the game if you want a relaxing game with the same genre as animal crossing but has more to it, more to do and a feeling of going somewhere more than it. If you love to get creative the design bench/tool, the art easel for creating clothing, wallpaper and flooring is perfect for you, the tools to express yourself are amazing in the game once you get the hang of the controls and way to do so. BUT I don't recommend the game at its current state to players who don't want to deal with bugs, who refuse to make backups of their saves, who don't want to bother filling out an official bug report form or understand that an early access game isn't complete and still is in the making. Those things can be stressful to people and ruin the game experience for them but sadly it's early access, bugs tend to happen making backups of your saves regularly can massively help you when you encounter a major bug. But the choice is fully up to the person, the feeling of a good game and the game going into a good direction is up to the person, the art style of the characters not everyone may agree or enjoy it can really depend on preference but I like to say give it a try if the genre and creativity are your thing but only do so if you can handle what comes with an early access game.Once past that tutorial stage it can feel slow slightly but once past it you are free to do whatever you'd like. You are have freedom to create, build and control the town to your own design. I happily do giveaways for the game and will always fall in love with it and it's community that love to help each other and share their creations, thoughts and feedback! If have discord please do join the games official server. It honestly is a great place and hub for the community where the solo developer reads feedback and can find the links for bugs reports and suggestion forms, community help and more.

_childDocuments_.review: I have physical and cognitive disabilities that limit the types of games I can play. My reaction time is very slow, and I'm easily fatigued, so I thought this slow-paced game would be just right for me. It's true that the pace of the game is slow, and it's nice that you can't be killed by monsters (I never encountered any enemies, and I made it to the second-to-last mine level, the silver level). I talked to all the visitors to the island, and asked them all to move in, and they all said they would... but they never did. And then the visitors stopped coming. I had many vacant houses, but they never moved in. Later, I learned that you're supposed to walk up to the house and click on it to make them move in,  but I had to learn that from Google. I never got around to trying it. The main feature of the game is building furniture, which is not something I have the cognitive energy to do. I didn't realize it would be such an integral part of the game. I would only recommend this game if you're interested in building furniture. Farming was a grind. (I didn't get far enough to craft sprinklers). Mining was boring after the first couple times, since there are no enemies. The whole game is about collecting resources, like tufts of grass, to build furniture. The villagers are creepy looking and devoid of personality. And there's no story. No potential for friendship with the villagers (as far as I was able to figure out).

_childDocuments_.review: So far Hokko Life has been fulfilling my Animal Crossing needs as a person who isn't going to buy a Nintendo Switch for one game I really want to play. It is very much still in early access and it shows. At times the lack of directions can catch you off guard but the community over on the Hokko Life Discord has been great for assistance and feedback from what I have found. If you are looking for a game like Animal Crossing this is very much a game to give a try if you don't mind the bugs while in Early Access. _childDocuments_.review: On par with a lot of the reviews: lots of promise, needs lots of work.I can do pros of course, but its an early access game prone to change, and the only real pro you can have is this is a pretty decent AC-like life sim with heavy emphasis on designing/creating. I've played around 7 hours and still haven't progressed as far as you currently can so far, so the game concept is there and sorta finished. But it will need a LOT of polish!My suggestions (and I guess this is the cons too):- More bugs/fish/creatures. There's a very limited amount.- Adjust prices. Fish and bugs shouldn't cost around 2g in this game, especially when that's all you can mostly do on a day to day basis for a while. -  I see what they want and it sorta works at first, but the moment you can move people in it all crashes. Bugs and exploits allow you to access further areas you shouldn't be at yet; you can take and sell any villagers items, including the main town shop furniture.There's a big push on villager requests, and the game does a terrible job atm of explaining that you need certain villagers and their quests to unlock certain recipes to help you progress your exploration. That would be fine, but then to move villagers *in* you need to have materials that are at places you shouldn't be accessing until you've already moved X amount of people in. The gameplay loop and the ideal path you're supposed to take to progress is heavily flawed, and also doesn't mesh well with the  sandbox of the game. - Tutorials: game has virtually no good tutorials or organic interactions that help you understand how things work/how to do things/how to progress correctly. You'll progress the "story" but then once you finish the current objective its like you hit a brick wall until you can find out from some other players what you're supposed to do next.- UI: The UI is not very good. Inventory screen is usable but lacks personality and ease of use.- Bugs: I don't need to really include this one. Its early access so it is a given. -  Overall, the game is an exhilarating new step for this genre on PC finally, but the amazement lasts for about an hour or two. Once the gameplay loop does kick in, the devs seemed to have overlooked many of the gameplay flow details which has made my experience confusing and drawn out so far. But even so, when you aren't taking part in the story progression of the game, you see just how less of life and personality this project holds in comparison to its Nintendo IP inspiration. It's early access and I don't mean to sound rude, I do still love what we have here, but it is obviously flawed in a lot of places. There's a strong lack of presence and identity outside of the general ideas they try to develop on. I feel if they get a good budget/community support and more time in the oven, and they reapproach a lot of the core ideas and mechanics, they can turn Hokko Life into a casual PC staple!Besides that, if you like these types of games and REALLY enjoy building and decorating with items, than yes I can recommend this! But only for veterans of this genre itching to try out new things. Elsewise: kindly wait until the game is finished.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like it.  It all feels pretty hollow.  The thing that got me to finally say 'no' was the designing of items.  The camera is obnoxious to control, there's no snapping to grid lines for item placement so that things are aligned.  There's no 'mirror' duplicate option either so that again, what you have on the right/left side is done to the other.  Rotation should probably have different settings like 30 degree, 45 degree, and then free-form rotation rather than only having one free-form rotation.  It's also not very intuitive on if you have an item selected.  Sometimes it's hard to tell if a button select worked on an item.  I like the idea, but it needs more attention and love and to have more streamline-user friendly customization.  The customize section feels like regular Blender with built in assets, and Blender, while an amazing tool, is not intuitive and user friendly off the get-go. You have to watch tutorial after tutorial.  So the bar of satisfying entry here in Hokko Life is...a bit too high when the general focus of the game seems to be customization.

_childDocuments_.review: A somewhat bias review: Not my kind of game. I very much enjoy Rune Factory, Stardew Valley, Harvest Moon, Drago Noka and the like, but I don't enjoy this game. This game is VERY much animal crossing in all the ways I dislike.The game-play loop of crafting consists mostly of gather resources->build stuff->sell excess->repeat. The issue herein lies in the fact that material gathering is painfully bare-bones, and it doesn't help that the hit detection imo isn't great (I have frequently missed the first hit on an object because I was one step away or facing the wrong direction). Additionally, the variety of things to collect is very limited, and the game doesn't give you agency to progress very well. What I mean by this is that you are painfully held back by the story arbitrarily deciding when to unlock what feature and this railroading in a  mostly sandbox style game is constraining and chokes the experience.The focus of the game isn't crafting, and building, it's wholly set on designing your own town and beautifying your environment. You can design furniture, decals, and outfits, if that's what you're into, but the crafting aspect of the game is limited to 'collect base materials to allow you to customize something'.This is a very casual game I feel would fit on the switch, 3ds, or even a mobile aspect since it's probably best enjoyed in bite sized amounts, but if you're into making efficient farms and watching big numbers get bigger, this isn't the kind of game for you.PS: I have had to sleep through multiple days without doing anything just to progress the story so that I can have something new to do. Quite painful to be frank.

_childDocuments_.review: Uncanny valley vibes.A lot of the reviews make mention of the odd art direction for this game and it's for good reason. This gametook heavy inspiration from Animal Crossing and it shows in the music, villagers, dialogue, and mechanics.This isn't a bad thing as it makes a lot of strides in doing certain things better, but unfortunately all the charm from Animal Crossing is not present here.The villagers are all animal based and meant to be cute, but they are so anthropomorphic that it just comes offas creepy. The dialogue with them is so stiff and their expressions so limited that they all just seem solifeless. Pair this with the fact that the animations reset during conversations and it just becomesunsettling interacting with them.The dialogue for this game is so one sided that even when you are given a choice to answer it's onlyever one answer. Seriously, in the three hours I played they kept asking me a question and prompting a response,but you only ever get one choice. It comes off as lazy and insulting. Why try to prompt the player to respondif you don't really get to decide? It could have been written in a manner that didn't require asking one to answer.Crafting, collecting, and decorating is miles better than Animal Crossing. The amount of customization you haveis absolutely stellar and truly allows you to go all out, but the villagers and NPCs just drag this game so down.There's a reason why the video focuses so little on them.If you like Animal Crossing New Horizon and are fine with the look of the NPCs you'll enjoy the game. If thescreenshots of the game are off putting then take it at face value as it doesn't get any better.

_childDocuments_.review: Pro'sDesign your own itemsCheapDeveloper still working on updatesCon'sSeriously lacking contentCreator codes holds back one of its best game mechanicsBuggyThis should still be considered >early access<I initially purchased Hokko Life last year when it was still well into early access and refunded as it offered virtually no content and was buggy,  after giving it a second chance it hasn't really grown that much beyond that.   It still feels like early access and lacking in content, the fact that I'm on the 22nd of Spring in the first year and more or less discovered most of what the game has too offer and feels like the developer basically stopped adding content altogether. The reason for this feeling comes from mining,  you can craft up to a silver axe and nothing beyond that to mine gold and diamonds which, honestly have very little purpose beyond just extra parts for furniture building, the entire pace of the game is slow with limited options throughout, shops carry limited clothing, limited furniture etc...and the only real end-game is to beautify the town you are slowing building up which often ends up just heading to the mines to collect resources, teleporting back to  your home sleep until morning and then repeat.Even the mining doesn't make much sense with Iron ore being rarer than Diamonds or Gold???  Even unlocking the mining hat serves no purpose at all, because its a late merit unlock which requires 10 steel bars which requires a bucket load of iron, but right at the start of mining you unlock mining lanterns which you can quickly and cheaply build to light the mines anyway, it serves no real purpose except for an extra item to craft, because why not?Item creating and design is interesting, but once again ultimately lacking because instead of doing something like steam workshop integration, they opted for a creator codes which are fine...but that forces you to hunt for codes online for something you might like for your town, its a convoluted system which sours perhaps its best and only worthy mechanic. Bugs and glitches still exist,  I encountered a very annoying bug which seems to have no fix and that is the game is no longer informing me what items I've picked up, or items I've received from completing tasks so I have to hunt through my bag for anything new...if anything at all. Overall, Hokko Life is okay for about 10 - 15 hours then after that, the average player will move into something else as you have pretty much explored the vast majority of what the game has to offer,  the mayor marks vary from easy to boring and annoying, which hold back some of the more interesting content.  The fishing mini-game is fine, but once again - don't expect anything spectacular either.   At the end of the day, Hokko Life is basically a sandbox furniture crafting game, its' not a farming game or a life sim and if the idea of designing and building your own furniture doesn't sound appealing then this game isn't for you.Now, after all the updates, bug fixes and more content added - the world shrines update for instance sounds like a step in the right direction,  but this game needs more much much more before I could change my review to a positive.   Right now, if I had to rate this game - its a 5/10.   It's got promise, and some people will find it charming but its limited content and creator code system hold it back.  Hokko Life needs pretty much double or triple the amount of content, more clothing options, more hairstyles, more furniture, more areas, deeper mines, more mayor merits, more crafting, more in-game events, deeper farming system and much housing options.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a game like Animal Crossing that isn't Animal Crossing, this is a pretty good pick, but with a few caveats.Hokko Life captures the concept pretty well with cute characters, slow pacing, and low-pressure, repetitive gameplay.  It's the kind of thing you play when you're trying to calm yourself down and lull yourself to sleep.  You're never in a hurry to get anywhere.The unique gimmick here is that instead of the large assortment of collectible furniture in the series it's emulating, Hokko Life offers an object editor that lets you build your very own furniture.  The editor is kind of clunky, but it's flexible.  I'm no artist, but I'm sure someone who is could make something really impressive out of it.  Perhaps the biggest flaw in the editor is that materials are required for each part added and you can't JUST design an object, so I keep getting stuck one piece shy of my artistic vision and having to save, gather 1 piece, then come back to edit.  Weird design decision.On the flip side, the drawback to having a game rely on community content is that if there's no community, there's no content.  In-game discoverability is low and I assume that I'm expected to go dabble in some online forums or discords to find friend codes, but I can't be arsed.  I just want to chill and play home decorator.  Without furniture to browse, I can't do that.It's also worth noting that with the flexibility of user content creation, you give up the interaction that would make furniture really interesting.  I can't put tapes in my tape deck.  I can't pretend to play my SNES knockoff.  I can't play my instruments.If you're looking for an escape from your endless debt to Nook, this might be a good place to find it.  Ultimately though, this just makes me want to dust off my Switch.

_childDocuments_.review: Game seems fun so far, and we have to keep in mind it is an early access game. Therefore, not recommended *yet*, it will need a lot of work before it can be officially released. Basically what I think it's like early game: In a nutshell, collecting butterflies, cashing them in, growing trees, and designing furniture in the designer tool. Basically its a designer tool with a world surrounding it. Things that make the game suboptimal: - Incentive based gameplay is completely non-existent; there is no notification of quests completed, not even coins visually going into your backpack when getting rewarded, no cheerful reward bells chiming when you turn something in.. No "feel-goods" about achievements or missions finished. - The camera is not movable and your character goes in all directions, there is no third person toggle possible sadly. This means it's hard to see things, or the really be immersed in the game. It can be nauseating when you are used to third person view. - It's early access so on bugs: There are glitches with non-working ramps, bridges and stairs. It's the only design i've tried so I don't know how many other designs bug out. So far ONE design that a certain player made (their tutorial is in the forum) works, but for a game that is all about design, its sad that all other creations seem to float in the air and become unmovable... I had to delete my save and start over again with the river full of floating bridge-designs I had tried. What would be *really* helpful is a way to access the game's Settings while being in the game, not forcing you to quit first to find the settings in the main menu.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for January 2023, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before February 7th, 2023, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.A take on Animal Crossing. Hokko Life screams its inspiration.  You have animal characters, arriving in a town on a train, and people just walking up to you and making demands of your time.  But that’s also exactly what Animal Crossing is.  This isn’t trying to create a new genre, it’s taking what is successful and finding its audience, and doing that well enough after a few minutes to get comfortable with the game.Hokko Life is focused on a laid-back style of game, where players build a town for characters, add new citizens to their town, and just have a simple existence.  It gets into the meat of the game quickly but this is a slow raft ride down a lazy river rather than whitewater rafting.  It’s not going to appeal to everyone but it’s a game you can boot up every couple of days and play for thirty minutes just enjoying the atmosphere. Pick this up if you enjoy Animal Crossing.  I stress this because this isn’t attempting to be something completely new, it knows what it wants to deliver to players and does it successfully.  This is the comfortable shoe for players who want to experience Animal Crossing on a different platform, and the fact it’s not tied to a set internal clock means players can play on their schedule. _childDocuments_.review: Imagine a child running around with their arms outstretched like an airplane, possibly making "vroom-vroom" noises, and then running up to you with a "really cool" bug that they think you'd like to have. Now imagine your town elders getting inebriated one evening and saying, "We're tired of running this dump. Let's let the kid do it!"That's the basic premise of this game (minus the inebriation part - I'm not really sure what their motivation is). If it doesn't make you run away screaming, you'll probably love it! I confess, I wasn't impressed with it when it was first released. I found the muted colors depressing, and there really didn't seem like there was much to do. After a short time, I got bored and uninstalled. But I went back recently and found it much improved. The beginning is still kind of slow. You arrive on the train, having no idea where you came from or why you're there, and you're given free room and board at the hotel in town. Then you're asked to do some simple tasks, but you run out of them quickly. NOW, however, there are a couple of broken down houses in town, and you're asked to fix them up. Then you're allowed to take one for yourself, and the game takes off.It's similar to many of the Harvest Moon-style games, though farming doesn't come into the picture for a long time. Instead, you do chores for people and learn how to build things and collect butterflies and fish, in exchange for cash. The creator wanted it to be similar to Animal Crossing, and it definitely evokes that game. When you catch a butterfly or fish, the camera zooms in and you display your catch. If you've played Animal Crossing, that will be very familiar. So will many other elements, including the animals moving into town. (Fortunately, I don't have to endure them asking for wardrobe changes and strutting around on the runway. Ugh.)It isn't Animal Crossing. It's a similar, but unique game, and after several hours of gameplay, I haven't even come close to running out of things to do. On the contrary, there seems to be more to do, as the game move along. I haven't even opened up some of the areas yet! So it's definitely fun and engrossing. The muted colors are a stylistic choice I don't really agree with, but at least there is a lot of variation in weather and the time of day. I recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: After 14 hours and still progressing through the game, I can say I recommend it. I've unlocked a ton of stuff because I tried to optimize my playstyle while still playing at my pace. Please try and set your expectations when you compare it to any other life sim game. Its not a randomized or generated map. It's a static one. Dont just like "animal crossing" or "stardew" or both, think about other games... like MySims. I'm not kidding, my boyfriend mentioned MySims, and that made a lot more sense for the visual feel, how items go flying, the way all the characters individualized designs feel a bit eclectic. But most of all, the crafting system opens itself up slowly but surely into an individualized make just about whatever you might want to. I've seen foodtruck decor pieces, I've seen final fantasy mounts as chairs. The creation contests allow community approved submissions to become canonized objects you can buy from the main stores rather than downloaded. It can be slow rolling at first, and like many games these days there can be a risk of tutorial slog. I dont mind that, as I can still get to doing what I want. And if you're patient, "it doesnt matter which house I choose as mine", yeah because you can move them later, and you can move into a bigger house you build later. I do wish there was an easier way to find other players' creator stores, but we live in an age where the answer to your question is on a discord server. RipperoniI look forward to seeing how this progresses past this stage of early access at July 1st 2023

I think they're kind of cute, in a semi-horrifying way. Sure they have dead zombie eyes with weirdly dilated pupils, but at least they're colorful. I guess.- You can design your own furniture, which on the surface is what I was looking forward to and I still think it's a great idea.. unfortunately the controls to do this are SO fiddly and obnoxious that I almost ragequit the game trying to put legs on a table. Please let me use the arrow keys to nudge objects around by a couple of pixels. Why can I not do this? Why is there not a "snap" option for basic things like PUTTING LEGS ON FURNITUREplease- The mines are a cute idea but the amount of lamps you need to put down so that you're not constantly getting "IT'S TOO DARK PLEASE SAVE ME" messages is obnoxious. You can have two lamps on the same screen, but if there's a 100-pixel wide area of darkness in between them, your character for some reason gets lost in the abyss and a huge message pops up on your screen telling you it's "too dark". _childDocuments_.review: If I could give this game a neutral review I would. It's okay, it feels like an attempt to create Animal Crossing for PC, but of course it's nowhere near as good and there isn't that much to do. The characters are a bit weird looking, not as cute as I would have liked and they don't have much depth.I enjoyed my first few hours catching bugs, relaxing and fishing but I really hated the crafting. It's pretty complex, especially when it comes to making original designs. I couldn't design anything that didn't look really, really bad. This is an issue as making original items and uploading them to the world is part of the games merit system if you want to complete 100%, I didn't find this cosy or relaxing at all. Another issue is the inventory system. It's just bad, even with max upgrades. Every time you want to craft something you need to take out each crafting material and put them in your backpack, then return them all to storage when you're finished. The storage sucks too, it's huge, and makes your world look really ugly.Hokko life is okay for a few hours, but there's not a great deal to it unless you love crafting.

_childDocuments_.review: I know what you’re thinking, Animal Crossing but the animals are emojis. That my sound like criticism but it’s far from that. The truth is that imitation is the sincerest form of flattery. And while obviously inspired by AC the game has a charm of its own that make it super fun and worth your while.I love that the concept of the narrative is basically animals who kidnapped you to make their town pretty by holding you hostage in a fever dream.It’s such a wholesome game… trusting a mysterious stranger with unrestricted use of your spare room and giving them an axe. What could go wrong?The game looks great, and although the anatomy of the animals is a bit wonky at times it doesn’t take away from the experience. The truth is I’ve been desperate for a game that combines Animal Crossing and Farm sims, and it has so much potential for improvements. I can’t wait to see how this game evolves.Finally, I absolutely adore how completely British all the characters sound.  That alone makes it a 10/10 experience for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to love this game but so far it's very.... lacking. The Very Slow start is frustrating and will lead players to getting bored Very quickly. It takes ~4 in game days before you can start fishing or catching bugs, which for a while it seems will be your primary source of income. The crafting system inspired by My Sims is pretty rough around the edges and needs a lot of work. There also seems to be no real tutorials on things so you're left with only really vague ideas on what to do.Slightly less vague if you've played a certain Other life sim involving animals. However where that game succeeds, this game is struggling to find it's footing. In AC you can start making money pretty quickly without any hassle, in this one though? Things you find around the world sell for very low, while items you need like crafting recipes, tools, & backpack upgrades cost Quite A Bit of money. It's just too grindy for its own good.One area of the map seems to be locked off by a Very small height difference you could easily climb or jump...but you can't. So because of that, for the early game you're going to be locked to 3 areas with very little to do in any of them. I'm going to cut this game some slack since it's only a single person developer on top of early access, But as of right now I can't really recommend it. If you're a fan of life sims & animal crossing in particular, maybe keep on eye on this one. But while it certainly has potential, I'd definitely wait awhile before dropping $20 on it

_childDocuments_.review: is an indie version of  without time flow in real time. It recently released into Early Access with core mechanics in place but still needing a lot more work. Despite that, the game is quite fun and I look forward to seeing what the final product will shape up to be. It's a good game to dive into now so that you can hop on the forums and Discord channel in order to give input to somewhat contribute to the further development of this game. Please keep in mind that this game is primarily created by a single developer who is very responsive to suggestions and is working on frequent updates to help fashion the game into a better experience.There's a minimalist story, in which you, the protagonist human character, falls asleep on the train and wakes up in the rural town inhabited by bipedal humanoid animals who you can befriend. (If it's sounding familiar by now, I think it's intentional.) Without a place to stay, the innkeeper offers you a small room to stay and keep some of your belongings, in hopes that you will stay and help make the town better. The game starts with only two neighbors/villagers, and it's up to you to slowly expand and invite more villagers to settle. The gameplay is focused on several different elements, all of which are casual and essentially stress free.1.  play a huge part in this game. You can practically design and create anything you would like, from utility items to decorate pieces, using the crafting materials that can be found in-game. The in-game designer/creator tool doesn't have the best UI so it's hard to see what you are doing at times. Nevertheless, this will get most of the players to spend hours trying to create some cool-looking pieces. You can also create paints and fabric dyes, wallpaper, etc. to fully personalize how the town appears to you inside and out--from interior design in the homes to external decorations and statues.2.  is also something that you carry out bit by bit. Now keeping in mind that this is limited in function at this time, as you can build 4 different houses and each one can only house one resident. The biggest limitation is that the houses cannot be moved once they are built and only face forward at this time.3.  given by the villagers will come along, especially when more of them move into town. This is usually something fairly straight forward, such as giving an item to another individual or obtaining an item that's easy to get to. Other times you will have to provide a quantity of a craftable supply. And from time to time, you will also be asked to design and to place a piece of furniture in their home. This last bit sometimes can get a bit time consuming if you start pouring in creative juices in trying to design the next best thing. These tasks often have a number of days limit attached to them, but there is no penalty for not making the deadline, the quest/task just cycles out and will come back again later. Sometimes you are just unable to get the supplies needed in time, and that's okay.4.  are inevitably linked together, as when you start, your area of movement is very limited and you have to use those resources to explore more and expand the available locations that you can visit. With more regions progressively opening up, you will have more materials and more land to use. Ultimately the resources go back to materials needed for mostly the designs and crafts that you will do.5.  is also to be expected, as you will be fishing for a number of fish and catching insects (butterflies) also. The butterfly catching is easy and effortless, and the fishing is probably the only aspect of the game right now that involves any kind of reflexive button presses in its mini-game format that's fairly easy once you get used to playing it.Easy to use a keyboard and mouse, the controls that you might want to use are displayed on screen when it comes to that, so it's easy to figure out what to do. Controller works well for the most part, including the item design, but there are times when you will need a mouse and keyboard and the game will tell you. I imagine that full controller support will be an eventual goal.The game has adorable design, and you can create almost anything if you put your mind to it and have the resources.Seeing as you will likely end up spending many hours playing, the music can become a bit repetitive. It's not difficult to turn off the music if you so desire and play other music in the background.Almost everyone who is remotely interested should be able to play this game. It's casual and adorable, with a heavy emphasis on personal design.Current Early Access price is $19.99 base, which I think is reasonable for the game overall. Currently it needs some work still, so only buy in if you want to try it now and maybe contribute to the game's on-going development. The core mechanics are there, but the developer is making frequent updates both in planned content and also to fix problems and implement suggestions from players.1. It would be great to be able to generate blueprints to save for the items that you design instead of only being able to copy/edit from created items in the inventory.2. Villager identification for quests/tasks. It is very tedious to run around and talk to each one of them just to see if they have something for you to do that day.3. In addition, a quick map to show where each villager is would be awesome, since they are always wandering around and sometimes are difficult to find to trigger/continue/finish a task.4. Hopefully this comes around soon, but currently the houses that you build are permanent, and when they are put in, they cannot be rotated. So everything in town has the same directional orientation and I had misplaced a couple of houses so as to block off chunks of land that I could otherwise use. It would be great to be able to more customize the housing locations. This is going to be especially important when the planned farming update comes in.5. There's a way to share with other players your designs, and that's in the works. It currently only allows sharing of 5 designs so it would be nice to eventually get Workshop support and people can create and share whatever they wish instead of having the heavy restrictions.6. Craftable storage units or allowing users to maybe put clothing and other supplies away would be so much appreciated. Currently when I don't use something I toss it all over, and fortunately the game saves whatever you toss on the ground, so it's a big deal. The backpack inventory is all you have, and even fully upgraded, is not nearly enough slots for what you might want to hold.My very first play session is recorded here: is an impressive indie game made mostly by one person. It has some rough edges but has enough core mechanics for people to play it as a casual game and also to spend many hours with the designing tool. The game is rather shallow in terms of other content right now but hopefully that will change. Nevertheless, it is fun and will likely only get better from here. Definitely check it out some time!Score: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really good game with lots of potential. It follows the Animal Crossing formula, new kid in town earning money, decorating homes, and expanding the town.My favorite aspect of the game is the ability to customize craftable furniture. The world is your oyster. If you check out creator's custom content, you'll find amazing things. This is a huge plus in my book.You can decorate your villager's homes manually. You can take out and put in whatever you like, something that took Animal Crossing forever to do.It's not based on a real time system, which is great because I'm not time traveling or stressing about the passage of time. I spend each day how I want and can skip to the next day if I really want to.This game is STILL very buggy. If that's something you're not into or feel skeptical about, then you might want to wait on the game. I could make a list of bugs I've found. _childDocuments_.review: I am a big Animal Crossing fan and I have always wished for Animal Crossing, or an Animal Crossing-like game for PC, well here it is. However, this game still has a long way to go before it gets there. I totally understand that it is Early Access and still in development, so I am not going to go off the rails and say that I don't like the game and won't play it, because in good time, I believe that this game will reach my expectations. My biggest complaint with this game currently, is that it lacks direction. There are very few quests that relate to any sort of story progression that are constantly active. There are a few in the tutorial of the game, but then you're on your own. The only quests that do exist, are if you talk to a villager and they ask for you to make them an item. This gets boring and repetitive after awhile. Similarly to Animal Crossing, it would be nice if the villagers grabbed your attention on their own, like displayed something above their head if they have a quest for you. The more villagers there are, the tougher it is to have to talk to everyone and find who needs something. I just need something that points me in any sort of direction with story progression, villager requests, etc.My next big issue is crafting using the blueprints. The blueprints, are hardly blueprints. An actual blueprint would show me exactly what I need to put where and guide me through HOW to build "a bed", or "a dresser", etc. Currently, all the blueprints do is help with size. I'm not that creative, I need a lot more guidance. How about making one general blueprint, like what is already available, for those who are creative and can make furniture from their own brains, and then have an option for those of us who struggle with this type of thing that guides us through how to make something.I also agree with many of the other reviews here that the animal villagers look a bit lanky and weird with the human-like bodies. That's one of the things AC does nicely with their game, is they make the villages cute, short, and chunky, or whatever qualities might relate to that animal. Another thing I would also really like to see is more of the furniture and items be interactive for both my own character, and the villagers. Like, I placed some musical instruments in my town center, but all they do is sit there. It would be cool to see the villagers wandering around sit at the drum set and start playing, or have them interact with the beach balls that I placed on the beach!So, overall, the game is a great start, but it has a ways to go! I would love to see it have these features I just listed, as well as many of the features that other reviewers have suggested. I do plan to stick around and hopefully see them through!

_childDocuments_.review: This game leaves one wanting. It is clearly an Animal Crossing dupe and it isn't following the top rule of borrowing someone else's idea: they didn't improve it or make it their own at all. This game is thin and surfacey. Hokko Life lacks complexity at every turn. This is made worse by the fact that the devs did not bother to explain roughly 50% of the game principles/mechanics to the player. I believe it is this lack of transparency that makes Hokko Life appear to be more than it truly is, which is not worth more than $10.Gameplay:The pinnacle, #1 problem with this game is that it is one of targeting tiles (to use tools, to farm, to build) and the movement is clunky. The fact you can't change perspective adds to the dilemma. Oftentimes, I will mysteriously look past the next square, and have to walk back two spaces and forward again to target correctly. I don't like that the animations for watering/digging still happen if it is impossible, or you've already done it (in the case of watering). It's difficult to fish when you can't see the rive well, when you can't angle your pole, and catching butterflies can sometimes be vexing. I think it is because of the clunky, unpolished movement that they were kind enough to make your tools infinite. This game would be unplayable if the tools needed replaced after missing the same darn butterfly six times in a row. Since they weren't going to improve the visibility/character movement I guess it was the least they could do!Crafting:Do you like to make cute stuff? Do you check for balloons every 4 minutes? Don't worry, the crafting is completely untenable in this game! You receive maybe a dozen "recipes" and buy the rest, but they are really just ingredients. Then you can toil and suffer through their in-game building system. It does not follow any system I have used before. Every item I made was wonky and unfortunate. In the city, after taking the train, you can download all sorts of items for free. They are free! How cool. If there was not a community, though, this game would be ugly and boring, as the creators made Hokko Life an aesthetics desert.Farming:First off, the flowers. They are ugly. There are 5 kinds that you can grow. There are some one the island, and I dug them up to replant, but they don't spread and it was very tedious. The island plants are the best, but you can't grow them. Unreal. PS, my red flowers have just cropped up all over in one area, as they are spreading? Do I need fences? Why are no other flowers spreading? I hate the weeds. They are everywhere and sometimes you'll stand two squares away before the dialog to pull will appear. Movement, people! Fix this!!Next, the crops. There are so many and watering is OBNOXIOUS. It is so fury inducing I must use CAPITAL LETTERS. Okay? It's so bad! I have a real life garden and it takes the same amount of time to work for real food as it does to get you watering done in Hokko Life. Please tell me how an entire watering can only waters 7 plants? They don't tell you the water must be refilled so make sure you place your garden beside the pond! Or you'll want to drop dead :) Water every other day! Be smarter than me.Now, you may want to know, understandably, why is there farming and fishing etc. if the crafting is undeveloped and sort of nonexistent in the state they left it in? Exactly, I guess there had to be a game somehow, you know? You catch fish to sell them for 10 in game gold that you don't need to buy anything. You can grow them to fulfill food requests from Oma. By the way, did you know you need to keep seeing Oma to move the game forward, like, at all? Explains the otherwise pointless Inn, I suppose.Fishing:I prefer this method to the AC style, as it is very stressfree and easy to have prompts help you along as much as Hokko Life tries to help a fisherwoman out. On the flip side, it has to be this way because the vision/movement issues make it so that you'd really never have any hope of catching a fish without it telling you E! The river and pond are the worst offenders for visibility concerns. The fish are boring, though, and pointless. The challenges are okay. The boots are annoying. The baits matter, not that they explain that at all. Another time that the community made the game playable. In fact, fishing was very unrewarding until I looked it up online: you can get a treasure chest of basic crafting items/money you don't need if you hit E during the orange/blue section of the timer bar. Some fish are available during certain weather events, seasons, and require baits types. This is probably the most developed and nuanced portion of the game, but to no end. There's no clam bake on the books, kids, I fished for steam achievements.The 10 fish in 10 minutes challenge is painful. Getting a boot during a challenge is gutting.The fish Tournaments are a CROCK OF SPIT. Okay?!?!:?! I played for the last 10 hours because I wanted my blue ribbon. My good girl ribbon from Steam for getting all my achievements is not coming. The achievement says "COMPETE" in fishing tournaments. I don't enjoy fishing, really. I don't fish in real life. I don't like fishing and catching boots. I don't like it, Sam I am, and I tried it, alright? So I took part in the fishing tournament and it went quick, I caught enough to get bronze and laughed all the way to the bank. The second tourney I took part in but it was catching river fish and you know how I feel about that, so I caught one and got on the leaderboard. I checked, there I was, with one. The game didn't count it, though, because I guess I didn't get a medal? It isn't 1st, 2nd, 3rd, either- they say you need to catch 10 of the particular fish to get a gold, 8 and 6 for the others, respectively. This is OBSCENE. Compete does not meet place. It does not mean "meet an arbitrary number of fish caught" marker. It means take part, try, show up and give it a go. I am fuming. I told myself I'd stop at 23 achievements. 78% is enough, I thought. Then I was like, no, I'm so close, but I have to go to sleep another 90 times to attempt this achievement. Are you joking? It's not even a game anymore, it's a chore.Outfits/Character:I liked how much I could customize my character, but the outfit options are nonexistent. There is a tailor's knock off shop that has 4-6 unfashionable, plain things in one color each and the shop is only open 8 hours a day, and doesn't open when the day starts. I have been twice. I have gotten clothing as a reward from villagers. I have duplicates. Unreal.Villagers/Town:The villagers are boring and superfluous. I would take or leave them. The houses can be customized, but it's sort of buried in the one shop option a day and the dsigns take different items/money. I just built the same basic house for everyone because all the work for the others didn't make sense for how little I enjoyed the so-called improvements. There's not much to do with them, though the game wants to insist there's stuff to do. I'd say everything about this game is the appearance of substance but it's a cut out.Quests and Challenges:The mayor merits of the game are stupid, okay? I have unlocked whole rows of them but they unlock linearly, so since I haven't built 50 known recipes (50 chairs?) I have half a dozen "locked" things in the game. I'd realize, oh, I need to blah blah, make 20 custom things and then it'd be like UNLOCKED, UNLOCKED, UNLOCKED. How annoying to be held back that way. I have beaten this game and attempted to get 100% completion, and I still have dozens of locked mayor merits. That just doesn't make sense to me. May it also be mentioned that in my attempt to get 100% completion I saw that the most basic achievement is at 56% and most others are less than 10, 5, even 1%. People do not buy this game and play it, full stop.All this to say, nah. Play something  like Polyville Canyon or Kingdom and Castles. Love you, bye!

_childDocuments_.review: It doesn't bode well when the achievement completion rate for a game is this low, for the kind of game it is.It is a game heavily inspired by Animal Crossing. It does things better than Animal Crossing, it does things worse. The one thing it gets rid of is having to play the game in real-time to progress. And with that said it's incredibly strange that most players stop playing the game after building their first house which is about a couple hours into the game at most. The progression makes sense for the most part, but certain things are overpowered compared to how you would obtain certain resources otherwise. Fishing gives you a lot of basic resources like wood, stone, and coal. And it even replenishes your bait used for the most part. But having to manually go around an crop trees is quite tedious, but that's a gimmie compared to other games where you harvest trees for resources.It's just that this game gives you a very free way of obtaining wood as well as making money. Money isn't an issue like most other Animal Crossing like games. The main issue I mainly had was storage. As well as placing items being quite honestly annoying because of the different shapes of items, as well as not being able to place items even if there is space to place it, as well as being able to place items when there isn't space to place them. It's very inconsistent and makes creating certain layouts either tedious or impossible. If you want to place an item behind another, most likely you won't be able to because the interaction hitbox is the physical model of said item rather than the tile outline that item occupies for whatever reason. This game very much embraces the psychotic ideologies or theories people sumize about Animal Crossing. You cannot say no to anything. If you are tasked with something you will have to do it. You cannot overfish, you cannot over catch bugs, they are an infinite resource that respawns constantly. You will always be able to get a treasure snag on each cast. You will always be able to catch a butterfly even if you miss the first swing. You can dig holes, and not fall in them. You can magically teleport to each load zone even if the teleporter is literally right next to the load zone you want to go to making it utterly useless. There is a subtle, yet underlying, unhinged quality to this game. Maybe it's the fact you can dye yourself a neon red and stand out like a cherry red tomato as you stand ominously in a bush. Maybe its the fact the villagers don't react to being pushed around or you barging into their house in the dead of night and sleeping in their bed without permission. Maybe it's the fact if you get the angle just right you can shove a villager partway into the floor. Maybe it's the fact you can plant trees clipping into the rock walls enclosing your encampment. There is a lot of liminal qualities that I cannot decide is the result of lack of features or pure intent. The achievements aren't all that difficult either. You just wait three days and harvest minerals to upgrade your tools and then buy more houses. This isn't the most ambitious game, but there is very little to mess up. This is very much a game meant for children.

It felt very odd, and half the villagers being plushies did not help the setting. Maybe that's the point? The Mayor Merits system is just weird to me. PC is not the mayor, never said anything about being the mayor, and you have to complete them to unlock things like running. And the meh gameplay and clunky controls did not help at all in endearing this mildly creepy game to me. It's a good idea, needs a bit more development time to really shine.

_childDocuments_.review: super cute game and I am sooo happy I bought it. It is kinda like a bootleg ACNH, but at the same time it has features ACtwt is still crying and wishing the "original" would have. It definitely offers it's very own spin and seems like I can actually play it for a few years.POSITIVE+ create your own furniture (feels like modding)+ trees/houses become see-through when you stand behind them + place objects everywhere!+ rotate the objects however you like+ everyone is they/them. you don't need to choose a gender and you can just express it by hairstyle and clothes. all the villagers are genderless, too (in English at least. I played in German for a while and there they used gender pronouns)+ place things in different areas. put a house on top of the mountain, decorate the special farming area, build a fish shop. the possibilities, omg+ the town is kinda small-ish, but because of the different areas you don't have to include a farm in that space which gives more opportunities to create your dream town+ online feature / hokko creator shop: download community items and place them freely around your town.+ move the villagers houses without paying in-game currency. just pick it up and move it (even rotate it)+ decide who moves in and into which house+ you can move into another house as well+ there is so much to do! farm, fish, catch insects, visit the island, mine, decorate, build things, ..... it has so much content! NEUTRAL / HALF-HALFo I know many people think the villagers look creepy and I remember the first look/trailer, but in the final product I honestly don't think they are that creepy? Some of them are weird, but there are some really cute ones too. I love the detail each villager has. Instead of offering hundreds villagers with the same personalities each one has their own story and character, which is really cool.o the town is created newly in each save file and can differ. the first town on switch was not good because the workshop was so far away from the exits. with my pc file, it's almost next to the teleporter AND I have a freaking mini-waterfall in the middle of my town. so cute, didn't know that was possible. If I had known, I would have restarted the game more often until I had gotten the perfect layoutNEGATIVE- sometimes a bit buggy (game flickers while running)- the start is super slow and you basically have to go to sleep at 2 pm to skip for the next day- then, boom. five quests in one day and you feel crazy busy. I wish they would lock some of the things more behind quests and guide the player more.- some things take quite some time to figure out and there could be more explanations from Oma or other characters- I played on the switch first and building mode was basically unusable. It is only for PC. For switch, it is absolute hell- creator shop only allows 8 items on display. there are mind-blowingly amazing objects by the community, but they can't be downloaded anymore because the creator updated their shop- the amount of downloaded and created objects is very limited. I hadn't downloaded much and it still said "limit reached" (AFTER I was trying to save a selfmade creation and it got lost. which sucked)- game often crashes when using the online feature- downloading one creator object multiple times can result in data loss / game destruction Even though I do have some negative points, I think these could be fixed in future updates as the creator is apparently listening to the community well and some bug fixes are already in the works. But, the positive outweighs the negative by sooo much and I am really happy with the game. Heck, I bought it two times already haha. I moved to PC because I want to create my own objects, but I will still play on my switch from time to time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a fun and cute game.  The crafting and designing is amazing! I'm so bummed though because when I first bought this game, I couldn't get it to start.  It kept giving me error messages.  I looked online in discussions and forums for answers.  I tried to add it to the exceptions on my firewall which didn't work the way the instructions told me to because it wasn't on the list to add and I couldn't add it by selecting files. It was frustrating. I tried restarting, clearing the cache, and restoring files. Then I just kept trying to log onto the game. It would seem to work and then the screen would go dark and close out.  I got a few different error messages each time, but I kept hitting play and trying. Then, suddenly it let me play.  I was able to play for a few other sessions this way, but it always made me try several times before working.  Now this morning I've tried the same as before, but now it's not working at all.  I don't understand the inconsistency.  It doesn't make sense.  I hope others don't have the same issue.  I recommend the game, but want others to know that this could happen to you.  Sad that I can't play, but hoping for a fix.UPDATE: I just decided to uninstall the game and reinstall it and that fixed it! Thought I'd leave the original message in case anyone else needs help.  We'll see if this is a permanent fix, but so far it loads up just fine now.  YAY! Okay, so for my complete review after playing for 19 hours:  I'm so excited for this game to be fully complete because I'm loving the early access game play so much.  It's a vibrantly colorful world with beautiful graphics and so much to do.  If you enjoy Animal Crossing and farming games like Stardew Valley this is going to be such a treat for you.  If you aren't sure what to do at first, talk to the NPCs in your town.  If they don't give you hints or quests you can work on catching butterflies by buying a net from the store and just focus on earning money by selling the butterflies at first and then go to bed and see what the next day offers.  Each day you'll have more things to work on as you unlock more things and get more villagers.  Fishing is a little tricky at first, but follow the prompts on the screen and you'll get it down. The design table can be a bit tricky too, but same as fishing, follow the control guide and you'll eventually get a feel for it with more practice. You can also look for guides (see my suggestion below in the last paragraph)  It's the kind of game that just keeps getting better and better the more deep you get into it.  There are some really great tutorials online if you just google or search on YouTube.  I found a great YouTube channel called Satoshi Gaming and she does some very helpful tutorials and relaxing game play.

Oh...and i still haven't figured out how I'm supposed to make bait to fish with yet.You could go back to learn Design 101:-Put a bulletin board up for getting / returning quests.-Make a storage solution available right at the start so you have somewhere to put stuff.-Give players the ingredients you need to craft stuff to get through the entire tutorial.-Break tutorials into smaller pieces as you 'discover new areas', don't force it back to back.  -No tutorial event should take place over a day span.

_childDocuments_.review: A game similar to Animal Crossing, but with farming sim stuff too.    • This game is mostly comparable to Animal Crossing, but additionally, there are farming sim mechanics as well.     • Gameplay includes: placing houses & recruiting villagers, villager quests, planting trees/flowers, foraging, crafting, mining, fishing, bug catching, artifact seeking, collecting, and eventually, farming.     • Initial character customization is choosing hair, eyes, and skin pigment. Your character is, by default, non-binary and characters in the game will use “they/them” pronouns on the rare occasion that they refer to your character.     • Further customizing your character with clothes happens after the game has started. Eventually, a character that runs both a clothing shop and hair salon sets up in the village square. Items that can change appearance are: tops, bottoms, shoes, glasses/masks, and hats.    • Merits Rewards are rewards granted for doing a certain number of tasks. Some rewards unlock objects or functions that make the game easier.     • No combat.     • Several afro-textured hairstyles. Most games have, like, 2 (feminine & masculine) or none at all. Additionally, the player can make their skin pigment whatever they want.    • Rainbow-themed clothes and at least one Trans Pride top.    • A decent amount of areas to unlock and discover.     • It’s fun to choose where houses are built and to decorate the town.     • Fishing and bug catching is fun.     • The controller works well for the most part.     • Tedious crop watering. The watering can only holds enough for watering 6 crops. Watering is one-by-one. There’s only one pond on the farm land, so the crops planted further away are particularly annoying to go back and forth for. It takes a long-a$$ time to unlock sprinklers or the weather device; the prerequisites for unlocking these are things you’d accomplish toward the end of the game. (Btw, why do devs do this sh!t? Why would you make something extremely useful available toward the end of the game when the player is about to be finished with the game? Devs do this way too often in games.)    • I absolutely hate the furniture designer. It’s frustrating regardless of whether I’m using the controller or mouse. The mouse is marginally better, but it takes a lot of patience to actually make a good design. I just don’t have said patience. Sadly, to unlock Merit Rewards, the game requires you to use the furniture designer a lot. Ugh.    • House exterior roofs and siding (to buy) in the real estate office don’t alternate often enough and don’t have nearly enough variety. The whole time I played the game, sidings were only ever yellow, green, and blue. Roofs were only pink and variations of brown.     • Lack of personality. The devs just took a lot of gameplay ideas from Animal Crossing (which is fine), but didn’t really do anything special with them. What makes AC so successful is both gameplay  it’s cute/quirky/upbeat personality.     • Game locked up after the first new resident event. My character was supposed to spawn in front of Rosa and the new resident, but I placed the house near the river, so my character couldn’t spawn in the river and it kept spawning across, where it’d get stuck. Had to restart a few times to get my character to spawn in the right place for it not to lock up, and by right place, I mean right in Rosa and the resident’s faces.     • During a Merit Reward unlock, the game locked up. Couldn’t exit the menu from any tab. Had to shut down and restart. Thanks to autosave, I didn’t lose too much time, but it was still annoying.    • Fish shadows occasionally show up out of water. It doesn’t even come close to being as fun as Animal Crossing,  there was some fun to be had. It’s not as expensive as AC, so if you don’t have a Switch or money for AC, this technically is an alternative. It also often goes on sale, so there’s that too. It’s usually $20, but I got it for $6-something. Ultimately, the game wasn’t anything special, but it was fun  for me to not hate it. If there was a “neutral” option for reviews, this would be in it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes away all of the annoying things about ACNH, retains what people love and expands on that. Sure there is no terraforming, but I personally don't care about that. I'd rather have had the key elements of Animal Crossings of the past just better. This game is developed primarily by one person I believe, and I'm convinced now more than ever that people should have higher expectations of Nintendo. They have the money and a large team, they can do so much more for the $60 they charge. This game is early access and is lacking a bit in polish that you'd find in a AAA game such as NPCs getting stuck behind furniture and items sometimes falling where they shouldn't but for the most part it's been a wonderful experience. If you're like me and often wait for a sale, I'd say just get it at the $20 (I did) it's more than worth it for hours of enjoyment you'd get out of it and I'm happy to support a game where the developer put obvious passion and hard work into.Some minor details that may be helpful to some people, this game has good controller support and works well with remote play (i've been using the Razer Kishi). So basically you can play handheld like Animal Crossing. One tip i'd give is to make sure you never turn in a quest or loot with your inventory full, very rarely you can run into an issue where you can lose the item. Looking forward to the finished product!

_childDocuments_.review: My pros and cons.Pros> Really promising game.> It's cheap, well atleast here in my country the game is only 13 bucks. Animal crossing was like 60 to 70 bucks when it came out here. > Runs technically well for an early access game and I didn't encounter any game breaking bugs.> Beautiful graphics and it doesn't look like a cheaply made game.> Music is great and really sets the theme of the game.> Villagers are cute and beautifully designed.> Crafting is amazing and you can build or design anything to your hearts desire. Crafting is where I would say hokko life has an edge over animal crossing.> Lots of items to build and collect.> It has its own day and night cycle so you will never have to wait in real time or cheat the timer just to finish certain activities.> There's mp integration like being able share your crafted items online while also being able to download other players crafted items and use it in your village .Cons > Map is quite small and it already feels crowded after building a few houses. I also wish the beach/lake area was bigger. > Still a bit buggy and rough around the edges. Characters easily clipped, get stuck, and it also easy to pass through objects. > Some exploitable stuffs that needed to be fixed, like being able to steal villagers belongings and then selling them for easy money.> Some objects/stuffs still has missing pics or texts.> Quests are limited to fetching or delivering items to villagers. Some quest are also a bit annoying like a villager asking you to build stuffs for him/her and would then ask you to put it inside their house after that to complete the quest. (Damn these lazy villagers!)> Game progression can be quite a bit confusing.> Character customization is still lacking and no facial feature options right now. Clothes are also pretty limited.> The villagers kinda feels the same.> Although crafting is amazing it can also be quite overwhelming and complicated for some.> No object interactions like watching tv, opening the ref, turning on the stove, toggling the lights, etc...The things you buy are mostly decorations right now.> Day and night is kinda weird at times. Sometimes morning is pretty dark while night is too bright.> No storage as of now which is pretty important since this game requires a lot of collecting and crafting.> No options to move houses. > Only a few fishes or insects to collect.> No seasonal celebrations or festivals. Other than the fishing contest there's really not much of activities in game.If I would recommend this game to anyone? Yes and aIso no, it really depends on your tolerance with early access game.Although the game is really enjoyable at this state but I also feel like the game is just 60 to 70% complete right now with a lot of stuffs still missing or lacking. Since I've gotten the silver pick and opened the last locked area of the game I feel like I have already hit a wall and there's really nothing to do anymore, well atleast for the meantime. So do some research first and watch some let's play before deciding to buy the game. For now I would give the game a 6/10, a promising game but with still a long way to go.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Manages to be both boring and fiddly at the same time. I am very impressed by a lot of the user created content, but that's not a good reason to play a game like this, IMO.I was looking for a game that had minimal to no time pressure while still providing something to look forward to as I played. What I got was a game that managed to put its most annoying mechanics front-and-center while what I would have originally thought was the main gameplay zipped by in tiny bursts. I gave this game thirteen hours to impress me, and at the end of that time, I realized all I was actually impressed with was the ingenuity of the community in building custom items.Main game progression is gated behind use of the most normal-sounding and yet most frustrating sprint mechanic I have ever put up with; you sprint with left-shift, but you have to start sprinting after you start moving, which I have never seen before, and your character gets winded very quickly. Have fun sprinting for 400 seconds about three seconds at a time to get the essential unlock, let alone the 1800 for the unlock that seems to be there to celebrate how long you have been thoroughly playing the game.Main game progression is gated behind grinding treasure chests via fishing, which manages to be both easy (hold WAD keys as indicated) and a pain in the rear (you can't control your cast distance other than choosing where to stand, you have to get the hook very close to the fish for them to care, and they move around quite a bit). I got treasure rarely enough that I managed 4/10 treasure despite having caught over 100 fish. This is where I noped out.As far as the character interaction, the visuals are cute, and yes, I would be able to identify specific characters by their dialogue, but that's about it. At least one character is actively obnoxious, and most of them are just meh. The tasks they want you to do are basic and don't seem particularly tied to the character, and none of them are actually endearing.If you, like I, got this from Humble Choice recently, I found Grow: Song of the Evertree to be a much better game. Doesn't have the Animal Crossing vibe quite as strongly, but at least it hasn't left me feeling like I got scammed out of my time and energy.Edit: I decided that so I don't get constant news about the building contests and so on, I am removing this game from my account. I am so sure I will never play it again that I don't even want it languishing in my backlog.

_childDocuments_.review: Review UpdateI don't know if Hokko Life will become a different game than it is now, if it will be story rich action packed multiplayer or whatever dreams you might have about it, but in its current state it is A GAME FOR CREATIVE PEOPLE.If you consider yourself not very creative, if you prefer to follow a story told, if you are at a loss what to do because nobody told you, if you find games where nothing happens just boring, if you have no patience with an Early Access, if you want action, goals, entertainment, fun, then Hokko Life is DEFINATELY NOT the right game for you.But if you just need a blank piece of paper to get entertained by your own imagination, if you are into designing things, if you like crafting stuff but don't want a game holding your hand, THEN THIS IS definately THE RIGHT GAME FOR YOU.On top you will meet other creative people who share their creations with each other. Hokko's welcoming community is waiting for you.- - -If you've ever played My Sims on PC then you'll recognize the similarities. I wished for years someone would remake the concept & this dev, Robert Tatnell aka Wonderscope has succeeded in doing so.The game is structured very similarly to what i played as My Sims. One starts in a run down town & the main endevour of the game is to make it attractive enough, so that new people want to settle there. The world is disected in smaller parts, which load on entrance, it is filled with different ressources & those are used to build & create. Oc Hokko Life is not a complete carbon copy of My Sims from then, which drew itself inspiration strongly from another game, Harvest Moon & in the meantime there were similar & very popular games, like Stardew Valley or My Time at Portia & the residents of Hokko are actually fable like animals & thus the game reminds many players of the also very popular game, Animal Crossing. Why i mention My Sims is because it had a very unique ingredient not to be found in any other game afaik, a workshop where players can do more than just rebuild predefined items. Hokko Life contains a very similar workshop, filled with building parts, textures & paints, which are assambled by the player in the workshop with atmost freedom, with the only restriction, the objects must be functional along few points, every other design is up to the player's imagination & skill. Hokko Life is in its current state in Early Access, it is a pretty far developed but not at all finished game. It is unpolished, it has bugs, it has dead ends & is unbalanced. I would still very much recommend it, it is already now a very fine peaceful & charming game & it looks like the dev is quite experienced, dedicated & updates the game often. The game shows a great promiss & i am very excited to see it grow.
