_childDocuments_.review: Game  didn't seem that bad at first, but wow is it a headache... And i'm QUITE patient with early access games.Wasn't expecting much, as I went in with the impression that this game is basically in alpha. I expected bugs, but hoped for none too major. Found my first game breaking bug just now, and it pretty much did me in--my character is stuck in the fence because I was trying to catch a butterfly by the workshop and as I pressed E, the dialogue box to "enter" came in.Big mistake.See, this game has no logical pathing. My character didn't run into an object and immediately script, "oh, I'm stuck. better WALK AROUND THIS SOLID THING IN THE WAY UNTIL NO COLLISION". It didn't even just automatically teleport me in. *sigh*Would have been forgivable if I could manually save without quitting the game, but as far as I can tell, that's not a thing. So I basically am going to lose an in-game week and over 2 hours of progress over this tiny oversight. I'm not sure why the devs even allow you to walk indoors with something equipped. Considering the butterflies clip through and SIT INSIDE the buildings, did they not foresee this issue? Or is it something they just decided to work on later? It's a pretty obvious bug and pretty irritating with no unstuck commands or ways around it (such as reloading). You can't open the menu nor control the character when they are attempting to enter a building, btw. everything on the screen goes away and no button presses work, (except maybe Alt+F4). Other issues are usually simple stuff like you have to be basically directly on a character to talk to them, using MK to play doesn't set the aiming up right--it is very clunky and games like this need a controller, (hardly any support for that atm but there is some, so I'm sure they'll add more later), when talking to characters they slide over to you when turning and, if they are seated, they basically are just floating and sitting in midair. Very Strange. Speaking of interaction distance, the entrance bug was unexpected because the distance in order to enter a building is quite small. It was, (presumably), significantly smaller than the distance i was when trying to catch the butterfly, so that vacuum effect was quite strange.In terms of money, the economy feels fine and well balanced. No complaints there. The fishing is not worth it, however. It is an absolute waste of time and probably the biggest headache in the game. If you have played games like My Time At Portia, the fishing system won't be hard for you to catch hold of (ha). However, casting your line and getting a bite? LOL good luck. Even if you cast and it lands directly in front of their faces, the fish will swim past the bobber and go about their business. It's like you're so unlucky you manage to find the only blind fish in existence. Now, the fishing minigame itself is challenging, I admit that, but what do you expect to catch with a rod made of sticks and grass? It'll likely be easier with upgrades, (logically speaking), In terms of money (again), fishing is a massive waste of time because you'll probably not get anything worth more than 6 coins. Add in the time consumption of spending maybe around a minute+ just trying to get the fish to SEE the line and then another 30-45sec of minigame... Yeah. SUPER not worth it. You could probably catch at least 5 butterflies worth 23 coins each in the time it takes you to catch 1 fish. Don't bother with it. Also, there's some mention of bait, which I'm saving worms for, but we shall see how that develops. Also there isn't  any snapping in placing anything, so you might end up with some furniture ghost floating around that you can't get back down. The "Move" prompt just doesn't show for it. Another bug, but not a huge deal. I'll just be more careful in the future so my future house isn't hideous.That being said, if you have epilepsy or any photosensitivity, DO NOT PLAY THIS GAME. There is a BIG flash when you catch insects, and I really don't know why they don't give a warning?? That's a huge safety issue, and you could probably get sued over it. Yeah, sure, people don't have to play the game, but what if they don't know there's flashing BECAUSE YOU DON'T TELL THEM and they catch a bug and immediately have a seizure?  Some people are sensitive enough that 1 flash can trigger them, some others are triggered by repetitive flashing. Better safe than sorry, just don't play at all if you're photosensitive. Seriously. The only way to make money for the most part is bug catching. You might be able to get something for the items you craft, but that takes blueprints. Which cost money. So unless you're fishing 24/7, good luck with that. The game will ridiculously grindy, but somewhat possible. It just wouldn't be worth the time as of right now.Speaking of money (again), I think the biggest pro here is designing everyone else's homes. Seriously. 10/10. I sold all of Oleander's stuff for being a bad boi and kept what I wanted from it. Sold the purple elephant's amps because I don't want noisy neighbors. Lots of money, lots of free furniture for me, and bad boi has to sleep on the cold floor in the corner. (Next time he gets the can of pennies.)Overall, in its current state, I would not recommend. I was actually quite disappointed given how long I've been waiting to see this game, but I am grateful to be able to at least play! I'm definitely going to keep playing, but realistically, I would say wait at least a good 6 months from now when they have more updates done, and see if content-wise it's worth playing. Hopefully we'll have a decent amount of bug fixes then as well.Edit: Updating to recommended because this game actually has an autosave feature. Wasn't sure if it did or not because it doesn't tell you, and I don't expect early beta/alpha games to have such a feature. I logged back in and was reset to the bedroom starting point, but it was the same time and I still had my money/items. The game breaking bug was thwarted without my knowledge... Just wary of something different in the futureEdit 2: There's other good stuff to the game I never mentioned, and I feel that's a tad unfair. The first that came to mind was ETHNIC HAIR. YES. You read that correctly!!! They actually have DECENT ethnic hairstyles!!! They have twists and cornrows, and either could really pass for dreads, as well as lovely fluffy ponytails/pigtails! More than just the standard boring Afro for anyone who isn't european or asian. Anyone with curly/kinky hair knows how hard that is to find in a game, let alone having it look decent.Another pro: YOU CAN EVICT RESIDENTS. I didn't like one particular resident, so I gave him the boot. Brought in someone else I convinced and I love my town A LOT more!!! That level of customization I always wanted in Animal Crossing, but they never implemented anything like that. Quite silly, really...I would also say the furniture designing platform is both great and awful. It's hard to understand until you get it right for the first time, and then you get what you're looking at. You can eventually unlock a computer that shares users' creations (current WIP?) and it's looking similar to the workshop in Sims. Basically you can share your creations and use others'. However, the creations they have on there I suspect are just stock creations by the devs, but I could definitely be wrong! There's challenges for furniture themes on there, so it's quite believable that it is indeed creations by other users. Add the fact that the interface and creation scheme is incredibly in-depth, and I'd say I like it more than I hate it now that I've gotten used to it. I will say, however, bring in PLENTY of materials. Seriously. I do it in the hundreds. I never know how much Im gonna need of each material, so i try to bring 200-300 each time i want to be creative on the bench. It would seriously suck to spend hours and then have to start over again because you're short a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: I actually really enjoy Hokko Life. It's a cozy and relaxing game. Yes, we all know it's an AC clone, but it has some differences: some good and some bad. Being able to craft furniture from basically scratch is super neat. Unlocking new areas is exciting, and being able to activate shrines for fast travel is very very useful. Villagers don't seem to have as much personality as in AC, and the UI isn't as friendly. Don't go into this expecting AC and you will be pleasantly surprised. There are enough differences to make it its OWN game in my opinion. I have currently played 15 hours and feel as though I have barely scratched the surface, so I don't understand the reviews that say there isn't much to do. Yes, overall the game is a bit watered down compared to other big name sim games, but there's still enough to keep you busy. There's mining, fishing, bug catching, crafting, etc. Hokko Life draws heavy inspiration from Animal Crossing, but I feel as though it stands on its own and was created with love by a dev who really put their heart into it.

_childDocuments_.review: I knew it was an early access and I knew what I was getting into. It's not finished or polished and it's made by one person. I knew what this meant and I wanted to support them and try the game. THERE IS A TON TO DO and work towards in the game, I'm never bored. This is an enjoyable and casual game with a very unique and complex crafting/building system. I've been playing for days straight and will continue to. The game has never felt slow and boring yet and I still have a ton of things to unlock.FUN THINGS You Can Do In The Game:- Craft furniture from absolute scratch. Buy paint and a couple square cubes and manipulate shapes into furniture and usable objects. Allows for insane creativity. If you're bad at this, you can download other peoples designed furniture or buy furniture from the shop.- A farming update is coming soon, so says the Dev.- Seasonal changes. Bugs and fish change depending on time and season and location. Collecting!- Unlock new areas. Later in the game you can unlock more locations to find new resources. More locations will be added in the future.- Recruit villagers and decorate their homes. Each evening a new villager will arrive whom you can ask to move in. Make unique furniture for them or buy furniture and decorate their house!- Minority friendly. The single-studio developer goes by he/they pronouns. There are a good chunk of afro hair styles. Once you pick your skin tone, ranging from ivory to deep brown, you can then adjust sliders for undertones.- NO energy drain! We love not passing out at the beach because we wasted all our energy for the day.Once you join the discord or ASK OTHER PLAYERS questions when you're lost, you'll keep playing. If you never seek out solutions, you'll stop playing. The game should provide this help to players, but it doesn't currently which is why most people stop. I just look in the Steam discussions and ask questions in the Discord (for quicker replies) and I'm set.XNEEDS IMPROVING Or Adding: (not gonna touch on bugs because, duh, it's an EA)- A crafting tutorial. It is so hard to do if you're not into model-engineering-stuff and aren't an art major! Even if you are those things, the game doesn't tell you how to do anything it just sort of happens.- A better introduction. You're on a train, wake up, and you're just here. I do not have a problem with this, Animal Crossing is very similar in this respect, but I don't have a problem with people saying they would like more narrative.- The only things you can do at the moment are craft and decorate, but these take up A HUGE amount of your time and resources so I don't see how you can get bored with it, unless you don't like creating artistic pieces and decorating. If so, maybe don't get it YET. I say yet because more content and activities WILL be added in the future.To people who say the game shouldn't have been released in the state that it's in, ... it's an early access. It's kind of like a Kickstarter. Finding interest and supporting the developer(s) (financially and with constructive feedback) allows them to create the finished product they know they can make and that you know you want. With peace and love, if you don't want to play an unfinished game, don't.p.s I've experienced NO game breaking bugs so far. Only one small duplication bug. Im absolutely able to play the game fully with little to no issues. That doesn't mean you won't have any, but thought I'd add that.

_childDocuments_.review: A cute, charming little game similar to Animal Crossing. There's farming, crafting, fishing, mining, etc. You get villagers, do requests, etc. pros: you can save anywhere and at anytime. I hate games where you can only save when you sleep and it pushes the game time forward. This means I can stop what I'm doing, take care of rl, and come back to any tasks I need to do.you're not limited by stamina to only a few tasks per day. all the villagers can fit on your island (once you open up all the places)once you get the catalog, any item that appears in the store, you can order. no waiting endless days for the shop to rotate items. it's very chill, over all. lots of little things to do.cons:there's not a terrible amount of variety in how the exterior of your home looks like.crafting is fun, generally, but you're very limited in the shapes of things to build with. Would like more variety. It can also be a bit fiddly. Like, crafting could be great with a few improvements.watering crops takes way too long. I assume there might eventually be an upgrade. But having only six "waters" in your watering can means watering takes forever.you can go to an island, but there's only one island and it doesn't change. wish there was a bit more variety there.It's not always easy to tell which stones/trees/etc you can interact with your tools. Anyhow, overall, the game is fun, if you like this sort of game, but could be improved. Not sure if the devs are done working on it, but I think with a few enhancements, it could be great.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not a replacement for any possibly related game you might see a resemblance to (ex. Animal Crossing, Harvest Moon/Rune Factory, Stardew, Ooblets or the like). My current recommendation is to play those games if you haven't already. If you need something new and you’re okay with a different animal crossing-like experience(one focused more on design than connections or story advancement), I think Hokko Life mostly delivers. It takes some of what those games have offered and delivers in a semi-unpolished way with a focus on creation. (The unpolished parts of this game lead to a lifeless or unfinished feeling.) For the price offered, I think that's a deal. Even more so at a discount. (I picked it up for 13$ after its post-EA release.) I recommend it if you're looking for a town design simulator with a few extra moving parts.I haven't seen all Hokko Life has to offer, but I plan to spend more time in it. I was really struggling to find a review post-early access with the information I wanted, so wrote this and I will add-on when I have more to say.I'd like to expand on why I think Hokko Life is a good experience, and also on what I feel is missing from this now complete game. Why I like Hokko Life:- the biggest asset the game has is the furniture customization process, so if that isn't interesting for you then the game might fall flat; being able to share these is really great- there are settings for audio, display, and controller/keybind remapping; bonus points for separating the music and sound effects (nintendo pls take notes)- inventory stacking is great! I specifically love that bugs stack which brings me to....- money is easy to get, bugs are quick to catch and easier to sell- the environment looks nice (though I still prefer to use reshade for additional fine-tuning)- the controls are easy to use, tried both, prefer controller for easier bug catching- the loading screens are fast, but there are a few of them between some important tasks (like selling or crafting at first)- the characters have a bit of personality to them, in design and dialogue (though the game maintains a quaint happy-go-lucky village vibe. pro/con)- Mayor Merits are diverse and provide very real buffs (ex. endless watering can, plants growing faster, shopping catalogs, SPRINTING)- the furniture customization is in-depth enough that it feels unique and fun (with multiplayer sharing)- NO TOOL DURABILITY, thank you.- Uses game time instead of real time, so you can progress at your own pace- the ability to freely move and edit housing & furniture (including neighbors)- so far at least one villager wants for something/has a task for me,  which i personally enjoy- biased but fishing is a plus, i love a good fish catalog - havn't used yet but multiple save slots is always a plus- ongrid and offgrid furniture placement with full rotation is lovely!What is missing:- 1440p resolution support at least, widescreen support would be a great bonus (playing on a 3440x1440 monitor)- It locks my mouse in the window and the game freezes when not in focus. (playing in windowed mode)- there are no text display/speed options- character models feel weirdly squashed flat on the sides, most notably on the pigs (Rosa & Poa), and are stylized in ways that make them love/hate; plus their outfits not editable (can't wear your designs)- being dropped into the game without direction or controls (took me a second to figure out which building to enter and how to do so, and then how and where to 'sit' for the intro.) was jarring.- Mayor Merits are too obscure. We need to see what is being unlocked, and some of it should not need to be 'unlocked' in the first place like sprinting. (also sprinting does not need stamina, this is not a survival game)- there should be a basic set of things we learn to build immediately from Sally instead of just a planter box; a storage box should be one of them (you acquire the storage box way too late)- the current player dialogue feels... meaningless. There is no personality in the options, and never an option to refuse or postpone things.- there are currently no hairstyles that I personally think look good in game, nor does the character's face look 'right' to me (I'd love the ability to choose another face type or something.)- in standard directionless fashion for these kinds of games, there is no guidance on unlocking specific tools or buildings which is only made worse by the obscure mayor merits (I don’t want a wiki to play the game please)- not having a space or anything to really show off our ‘collections’ in game feels odd. (bugs/fish)- most of the furniture has no interactions, a tv doesn't turn on a picnic table cannot be sat at. this leaves the world feeling a bit lifeless- for the mine area, a wearable lantern should be the first available option to deal with the darkness, crafting a ton of light posts seems excessive and expensiveA running list of what is NOT in the game for people coming from similar games: multiplayer of any kind, swimming/diving, cooking(?), any sort of combat or enemies, an in-depth story, friend ‘connections’/heart events or gifting, player owned businesses, a museumIn honesty: I think this game is decent. From a one person studio. I'm interested in designing a town stylistically, but returning to or staying with the game long-term is probably off the table.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to give Hokko Life... a timid recommend.Don't get me wrong on the timid. It's a great game and I am going to have many more hours in it I'm sure. There are just some things about the game that keep it from being an outstanding game to me.The biggest one is the character designs. I don't know why they seemed less uncanny valley in the trailer, but they did. A lot of the characters are very very strange looking, especially the elephants (other than Paula whose design is great). You also get friendship points with NPC's but thus far I don't see a point to talking to them? Their personalities are pretty bland, a lot of repeated dialogue, and there's (thankfully) no romance option.There's also somehow, at the same time, too much to do and nothing to do. The days are super long which gives you plenty of time to do things and if you do everything you need to in a day you'll likely use up all that time. Go to the mines. Gather seashells. Pick all the flowers. Chop and replant all the trees. Check the shops. Then when you get far enough, water your crops and go to the island. The thing is that once I have done all those things... there's really only so much to DO.That brings us to the coolest part of this game. The creative designing of furniture. You get various shapes to work with that you can resize and reshape to just about anything you want and put together to make pretty much anything your brain can come up with. I built a 90s easy bake oven and a Stanley red standing tool box for storage in Sally's shop. It's honesty so much fun to sit down and build something cool. It does have it's problems though.1) There's not nearly enough prefabricated furniture. Sometimes I want to just be able to build something without having to go into the creator and make it from scratch.2) For as many shapes as there are, there just isn't enough. There's A LOT of things I wish were in the game. A big one? An equalateral triangle piece. The only triangle piece has uneven sides and it's practically impossible to make one. I made a pair of kitty ear headphones for the gaming set up I want to make my character in my game and I had to use the heart piece and flip it upside down to get something anywhere near a cat ear. Also getting a "leg" type piece that is square with round corners would be nice. I have many things that would make this review mostly suggestions for the rest of this review. More things that are fabric. Ability to add water to something. So many.3) Being able to save a design to be used on another design. Like I can save any design I make, but I can add that design to another design. Like if I take the time to make a latch. I'd like to be able to save that as something I can use in another design instead of having to remake the latch on any new design I try to make.4) There's a way to share your designs with other creators and that's so freaking cool. I love it. I just wish that I could go in and search for items by name instead of needing a creator code. Let me search "table" and then if I see a cool one go to that creator's store. Having to have creator codes makes it hard to find stuff you want that you don't want to try to create yourself. There are contests though where you can make themed items and enter them and then there is community voting which is really freaking cool (my easy bake got into the voting for the toy theme and I was stoked).5) The last thing is honestly no fault of the dev.... and that is that if you aren't into the idea of creating items to decorate your town FROM SCRATCH.... you probably won't get much out of this game and I don't recommend it. The creating of stuff is such an important part of the game. Even if you just want to decorate your areas and NPC houses. You will have to either struggle to find specific furniture you want that is community made or struggle to find the furniture you want/need from the general store. The game will be very slow with very little for you to actually do if you aren't going to design your own stuff along with doing the other stuff. So if you don't think you are creative enough to make your own items... you probably won't get much out of this game.Overall. I recommend the game to people who are creative types who enjoyed animal crossing but wished there was more furniture and that you had more creative freedom. Do keep in mind tho that this game is not Animal Crossing. If you disliked the lack of personality in the AC villagers you'll HATE it here. If you want an insane range of creative freedom though in a game that scratches a bit of that AC itch and enjoy life sim games. This is a pretty good one.Edit: I did want to edit to add one additional thought.... ♥♥♥♥... the... net.... There's a learning curve to catching bugs in this game but you will miss a bug FAR more than actually catching it. I don't know what the dev could do to improve this, but catching bugs is the most frustrating thing in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: **NOTE:** This review is part of my steam curator review and is the extended version. Check my steam curator page at  . Follow appreciated!--- Hokko Life is a rather unique game. While adhering to a farming/sim game, it is obvious that it is somewhat influenced by Animal crossing. Some people claim it to be a full copy,  while some merely believe it got inspired by it. My knowledge on Animal Crossing is minimal, having never played it, but from what I have seen is that yes, there is some influence here and there but the game is also greatly different. It's nowhere to being a copycat. In Hokko Life you wander upon a small village after having fallen asleep on the train. And so our story begins. You slowly start integrating into the society of the village, helping others with their personal tasks and attempts at making the town a better place. Everyone, including you, wants the place to be more lively and get outsiders to come over and visit - perhaps move there too. The game follows a story which helps you get started with the basics but also introduces you to intermediate aspects. Of course you are under no obligation to follow the story - but you kind of have too. Without a story you don't unlock the new stuff and so forth. But it's all worth it, because before you realize it the town is thriving and you can build whatever you like, buy whatever you like. Have your own house designed your way. The possibilities are endless! The game runs on beautiful graphics that even a potato can run. The colouring of the game is perfect. I'm in love with the bright colors, and the characters are amazing too. Talking animals and a talking human. What a twist of events. You could compare the graphics and tone the game sets to Animal crossing. It's the same style. Hence this game is amazing for those that played Animal crossing and want the same type of experience regarding game style. The game is also amazing in not having common in games ‘invisible walls’. You know when there are multiple objects close to each other but there's a gap but you still can't walk into it because the game wont let you? This game has none of that, which impressed me the most. You can walk virtually everywhere, there are no invisible restrictions or alike. Lastly, as I'm sure some will still be hesitant over this game, I'll summarize the above one last time in asking, is it worth it? Is the game worth its price or not? Simply: Yes. It's worth it. The price might be somewhat steep for some who view this as an Animal Crossing copy, but it's not. The game comes with an amazing story, child-friendly of course, that can span on forever it feels like. Above that, the game also comes with endless possibilities for those that love designing their own objects, home or town in general. I can't stress enough on how you can virtually do what you want here. Build a fence to trap the inhabitants? You got it. Design your own house? Go for it. Steal stuff from other houses? Oh yea. However, like all games there will be a problem here or there (which won't mean the games are bad, just some people can be picky). One of them is that some non moveables aren't fully solid. They are in a sense transparent in that you can slightly walk into them or NPCs do. One of these are some chairs in the Inn (the place you start your journey!). Another is that in some areas the game wont let you place an item a certain way despite there being no obstacle. Other than that, I saw no other glitches. Also, the latter rarely happens so don't worry. All in all, having summarized the aspect and feel of the game, including potential issues, I still stand to my opinion that you should go and get the game. It's a perfect game for a calm evening and basically let your imagination do its thing.

_childDocuments_.review: Charming little game. I played a tonne of Animal Crossing on Switch, and I've been eagerly awaiting this game for a while. Look, real talk... It's Animal Crossing - there's little that separates it from it's progenitor, even the interface bears resemblance. However, I'm judging this game on its own merits. Overall, I enjoy this game. It's calm, chilled and charming. It's exactly what I want out of an Animal Crossing game, and has some unique little tweaks to make this experience even better. Things like deep customisation on furniture, rotation of objects more than just 90 degrees, and the 'grid' of the game being altogether smaller makes this feel more of a simulation. Despite it being a clone of Animal Crossing, I'm looking forward to seeing what this game brings that's different over time. It feels as though they've built the foundation of the game on Animal Crossing's shoulders, but I hold out hope that from this foundation it'll blossom into its own beast.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an updated review. The original review is at the bottom.=======================================================================So. Version 1.0, eh?Well, point to the devs: they did fix the bugs I encountered during my previous attempt to play, so there's that.It's not completely without its charm, either. There's some interesting ideas, and a vague sense of a specific direction. However, it feels very hollow.I have been playing for a solid 6 hours now, and I have not once stopped to think, "Oh, that's such a cool touch!"Furniture doesn't do anything — a TV can't have a screen to turn on, even with like three still animations. There's no music played by radios. You can't sit at a table with a bench unless it's designed specifically as a chair — things that are tables only let you put stuff on them.It's interesting you can design your own furniture, but it's pretty limiting. You need a lot of resources for each item, as every board of wood costs an actual plank from your inventory — so your creativity is very limited at the start. You also need to purchase crafting recipes, and can't go straight to painting in a color you like without growing the plants necessary to make the dye. This causes a single furniture item to be a multi-day affair. However, it *does* allow for crafting multiple items at a time, and it doesn't make you wait for multiple bars to complete the job.The character designs remind me of the old Teddy Ruxpin dolls. They're fine, but I can't say they look particularly endearing. They also don't have particularly interesting, or charming, dialogue. From what I've looked into it, it also sounds like there's a very small selection of possible villagers, and they have unlock requirements.There are perks you can unlock by doing normal activities. This is a neat idea. Unfortunately, none of the perks (that I've come into so far, at least) are particularly polished. The mini-map is designed with a color scheme that reminds me of sitting in an elementary school room with everyone's houses pinned on it. Still, it is functional, and as a bonus it does show where the villagers are.You can redesign the interior of a house. This was a unique concept at the time the Early Access started, and had ACNH not launched their sole DLC, it would have no comparison on that front. However, having played both, there's just no way for that feature to carry the game even close to the amount of cool stuff possible in that expansion.There's butterflies to catch and fish to fish up. I didn't manage to find a way to unlock fishing in the six hours I played. When you catch them, it adds them to a scrapbook page in your menu. The menu art isn't particularly stunning, but it does represent the butterflies adequately. Additionally, the butterflies can clip through trees and rocks indiscriminately. It's unclear exactly how to best aim the net — it seemed somewhat random if a swing would work or not at any given distance.On top of that, there are some UX choices that were annoying — the top of my list being that pressing A will simply skip to the next panel instead of speeding up the current one. It didn't really matter since most of the text was pretty drab, but it doesn't make sense to skip text that scrolls so incredibly slowly. Other small things cropped up as well — using a controller to design items is a slow process, placing bridges is finicky at best, and there's a lot of back and forth involved in mining at first (since you must place your own lighting, which requires materials from within the mine, and it's not close to town and there's seemingly no way to fast travel).It's... fine. Absolutely fine. However, between ACNH and Disney Dreamlight Valley, I can't see a reason to recommend this game over the others. One is way more polished and has a massive amount of content beyond what this can provide, while the other has various Disney IP at a bare minimum.The timing is rough. If this game had come out before DDV, or been a bit more robust (or polished), my recommendation might be different.=======================================================================Original Review=======================================================================This is a mess still. While it's expected Early Access would have unimplemented sections of code, this is a bit beyond that. I'm not expecting a perfectly polished statue at this point... but whatever pebbles exist should not look like chunks of asphalt. The new character creation screen isn't even polished, and that's first impressions type stuff.It was too immersion breaking to bother with. I'll probably come back to this later, but I would highly recommend waiting on it for now.

_childDocuments_.review: It's really fun but it has some Quality of Life issues I wish they would re-work.  Such as tools, you can only use one tool at a time.  You have to open your bag, pick a new item and then you can interact with it.  You have to do this with everything, if it is multiple items, such as seeds, then you have to open the bag *every single time* to pick the seeds.  This is obnoxious.  The numbers 1-0 do nothing in the game so there is no reason why you should not be able to work with an entire bar rather then one key for one item.  Once you unlock sprint, it is very fast to deplete.  It's annoying and your character doesn't get very far before you have to stop all together.The textures in the game are beautiful but the UI is horrible to look at.  The buttons look like cheap, glossy plastic.  It looks like a mobile game user interface.  It could be much, *much* more stylized to fit the game.  The logo for the game alone is a great direction to start with, if you were to consider actually designing a real UI for your game, rather then a flat, bad-looking copy & paste UI.Atmospheric sounds should be a setting all on their own.  A big point of these types of craft/farm games is the atmosphere.  Being able to silence the music and turn up the sounds of nature are almost key to any game, but especially in a game where the player is going to be spending so much time just hanging around either while fishing, catching bugs, farming, whatever.  It needs to have a beautiful, natural soundtrack.  Very slow progression for an already slow genre.  You need to wait days, sometimes even up to over a week in-game, for some things to happen such as trees growing.  IMO this is asking too much of the player.  You are already expecting to have a very casual, slower-paced session when you go to play a game like this.  But literally spreading this out over such a huge amount of time while giving the player literally nothing to do other then sleeping the days away (unless you *really* just love walking around catching bugs & fishing all day, every day, while waiting) is not how the average player is wanting to experience the game and I feel like this was somehow a huge oversight in development.  Four days for a tree, trees are finite in the game unless you catch bugs & fish constantly to pay for the seeds to grow trees to cut for logs in order to make planks for crafting.  But you are waiting SO LONG for the trees to grow while you are waiting.  It feels like you are always waiting in the game, something I particularly hate in my day to day interactions, and I despise seeing it in my games. I have a lot of negative things to say but basically, it really is a fun little game.  It doesn't break any new ground.  It isn't going to win awards for changing the genre or anything.  It's incredibly cute, the quests are easy to understand & carry out.  The UI shows everything without being too intrusive.  There are many little interactive piece of furniture you can craft and/or buy.  There's real customization in the game, which is very rare to see still even after all the fuss everyone made when Sims 3 came out.  The animals are charming and easily discernible from one another making them easier to remember.  When you need to talk to a villager you will see a visual effect around that NPC.  This is a super kid friendly game as well as a great way to just have a calm night in with a cup of coffee.  You can even move many of the items in the town as well as picking out exactly where your next villager will build their house & what kind of house they will have.  Later on in the game you can further customize all of the houses.  Merits are things you can earn by completing tasks in your journal such as cutting down a certain number of trees, catching # of bugs/fish, etc. The Golden merits will give you buffs or you will get 100g in the mail for helping finish requests.  Tons of great things about the game.  Nothing game breaking or so annoying that it stops you from wanting to progress.  But things that could definitely be worked on or looked at.

The game loop is pretty much, gather materials so you can make really cool things and in the process do doing that gain achievements that help you unlock more cool things. I'm not really into creating items, I tend to want to design things as an end game thing when I play games like these. So I don't find this game very compelling, I also don't think unlocks should be hidden behind achievements as a result because like I don't want to design 25 things or 50 things or whatever. But I understand their are people out there who may want that and their wonderful community of creators is proof of that.And the game as it is functions is quite good. Any bugs that may have existed at launch I did not experience. Yes the villagers can be more life like, but frankly as far as dialogue and interaction goes they could be far worse. They were interesting character designs, some I liked more than others. The fact you can put the houses anywhere in the world is lovely. I had wanted to put a cottage in the Red Woods until I decided that I couldn't be bothered to continue the game.So just be aware of what you're asking for when you buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Super cute game. As many others have said, I am also a long-time player of animal crossing. It is a little clunky in areas, but nothing as unforgivable and dramatic as other reviews have made it out to be. I think there is only one dude working on this game, and it is going to take a little more time than a huge dev. SDV was also clunky in places when it first released, and look where it is now. It is important not to review bomb early access games just because they did not meet your extremely high expectations of the genre.. this is how you stop sales, stop the dev's income and then subsequent good updates and content do not get done. You can tell that the dev of this title put a lot of love into it, with the many systems that are in place and the pretty cute story. The only thing I would change, is the art style of the animals, and that probably would not even be possible at this point in time. I'd like them to look a little less Fisher Price and more chibi cute.. but that is just my personal preference. Everything else looks great. The furniture is also extremely adorable. 7/10 at this point in time!

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★☆☆I cannot honestly in my opinion tell you to buy this.NOTE: I did not back this game on kickstarter/patreon, wherever. I didnt even know about it until literally today.Starting with... oh crap. - The character designs are ok. The designs have had some polish, you can tell. It's all clean, stylised, nice. The humans are kinda creepy. They just smile.  - The animals seem cute enough. I don't know if each village has randomised villagers, maybe I got thrown literally two elephants because I'm boring. Or maybe that's just the pre-determined villagers.- Why am I allowed to just run into people's houses, the shops, and just...move their ♥♥♥♥? I can just take it? Why is that a thing? Nobody has explained/talked to me as to why this is a thing. It seems kind of ...weird?- The bugs. Oh boy! The first thing that happened was that I booted up the game and pressed the start button on my controller while my character was on the train. Apparently that breaks the game! I was not able to move out of the screen. Don't do that. I had to force quit and start again.- , I had a rabbit fall off a chair and float while I was talking to him. When you wake up, you can run around the room before your screen loads, and you can get stuck in the corner of the doorway. Oops. - If people say stuff to you, they wont repeat it generally, so you better hope you didn't ram that A button. _childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game.The grapics are cute, the music is ambient. The artstyle used on various decor, nature, animals etc etc. are very nice with a ton of details.Character customization is charming, and there are a ton of outfits to collect.But I still find it lacking. The tutorials are either too short or simply not there.The grind to unlock features is massive. I would not mind that so much, if I actually know where I'm going, but I do not.Yes there is a tech tree, that lists things you have to do to get a bigger backpack etc.One achievement says "visited the small wood" - yes sure but where is that forest?I have unlocked the map, and level 2 in the mine, the bronze pickaxe, leveled up fishing, an  island etc etc, have even started farming. But I have still to see that forest, unless I'm looking for a tree or something?...edit... to the above: I have now unlocked that "visit the small wood" - but only because I'm  extremely stubborn AND was willing to again grind massively.I'd love a bigger house for my character. I can build it, but what about customization, other colors etc etc. That I cannot do... yet. I suppose I need more unlocking of features. So ok - what if I build a bigger house with the default settings. How do I move my character to the new house? There is no move house feature. Yes there is an evict button on all houses including my own. So what happens if I click that button? Am I kicked out of the town, or will I be able to grab the new house?On several occations I found, I had once again sold items I need to either complete a quest, or needed to craft X item. Once unable to find X items again, so I deleted the save game and started over.The lack of storage is a massive issue, that quickly becomes an annoyance, until you figure out how to get around it.The character interaction feels hollow.I'm puzzled as to why you cannot interact with the other NPC's if you hold something in you hand.I am normally fairly creative, but the design tool drives me up walls. How some players can create the wonderful art they do, simply evades me. What can I say besides I'm in awe.I have created various items. But once I have used those items, where do I find them again, if I want to create more of X item?If I have to take the train and then go "to my store"... then just NO that needs to be changed.Another example, I had unlocked how to craft a bulb, but no matter what I did I could not figure out how to use said bulb to create an actual lamp.After wasting a ton of raw materials and like close to an hour getting nowhere, I decided it was enough...... edit to the light bulb issue - again after grinding some more, I can now use the bulbs when crafting something.I'm all for heureka moments and like playing games where I have to figure out how everything works. But constantly going blindfolded is not my idea of fun.The game has massive potential, but needs a lot more development before it's something I'll really enjoy to play. As it it now it holds too many frustrating moments.I will continue to spend more hours playing, hoping for more updates. If/when they do I hope I'll be able to change my review.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is interesting for those who attached more importance on design and crafting in ACNH. Mines also play a role here. My focus was on conversations with the villagers, drinking coffee and fishing - in other words, relaxing. So at first I dismissed it as a bad buy, but somehow I do have some fun in the game, even if it's not normally one of the games I would enjoy. And that means a lot. You can have a lot of fun with this game. Give the game some time, even if you're skeptical at first, and you'll get used to the walking animation. I promise.
_childDocuments_.name: Hokko Life

_childDocuments_.review: I really tried to like this game, but as it is now, it's still lacking in a lot of areas. After a certain amount of progression in the game, you'll find yourself just repeating the same thing again and again until the next thing is unlocked, which was supposed to make your previous chores easier, but at that point it'll be too late for it since you've already finished grinding up the things you desperately needed a while ago. Things that I think could be improved on: - Make requirements for important game mechanics to be unlocked more obvious to the player, mechanics like farming, fishing, cooking, should be unlocked relatively early in the beginning for the game to feel busy, as of now everything is unlocking too slow, which leaves the players feeling bored easily. - Either balance out the rewards for villagers requests, or give a long term goal for actually completing villager's requests. There are crafting, produce or food requests that actually makes the player lose profit if they were to complete them. In fact, there's actually not much reason to complete them besides completing the mayor's merits. - If the main goal is to complete mayor's merits, look, I love to grind in games, but some of the requirements are too ridiculous and slow. Food requests only spawns once per season for me, and you need to complete 20 food requests to unlock all the mayor's merit. Fishing tournaments are super rigged since the fish that are required to be caught either only starts spawning around 5pm, or you'll need fish gut bait to catch them (which in itself is quite troublesome to grind). - The villagers houses are so empty, and it's not worth decorating their interiors with my ugly builds since in the end of the day, the villagers don't care what's being placed in their house.  The first two villager's house was so full of personalities, it would be great if the other villagers get to have requests that asks the players to help decorate their houses based on their own unique personalities. - When a mechanic is designed, usually players would like to do it for a purpose, to unlock better upgrades, to increase skills or relationships. So far a lot of things in this game are just placed there so you could just do it, for funsies : / Maybe it's fun for some folks and I'm not the targeted audience for it, but that's just my own two cents.- Maybe have a different music theme for different seasons? As of now the music is kind of limited, but fixing the pacing of the game should always be prioritized.I can see a lot of potential for this game to be a great cozy game, and I hope to see more from this developer improving in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Got a code for the game, tried it out on stream and it was a lot of fun - On day 1 there were a few bugs but nothing game breaking and from then there has been frequent patches and updates to make the game more enjoyable!The discord community is really great too and help with any issues, ideas for designs and how to help report bugs etc. They also keep that discord up to date with what they're working on for patches which is really nice to see.Music is relaxing, controls are easy and fishing is fun! It's like a more crafty version of Animal Crossing, with relatable animal villagers - one which seems to be constantly having an existential crisis.Very excited for the farming update too!

_childDocuments_.review: You can tell that this game is in Early access. It's rough around the edges, although visually it's a real nice style. Gameplay is pretty typical of an AC-like game, although my biggest gripe is the "story" so far. I'm not expecting a masterpiece, but being a kid that falls asleep on a train and is then just kinda ASSUMED to be staying in the town they end up in forever just because there's not many trains back out again is a bit... Weird. Your character doesn't even protest when the villagers just auto assume you're moving in after being there for one night. The beginning just possibly needs rethinking to be a little less... Creepy. The first people you talk to literally put you to work RIGHT away to make their town a better place as if you haven't got a train to catch and somewhere you were originally going. Gameplay-wise it's fine though so far, especially for an early access game so I'll recommend! If that changes as I play more I'll be sure to edit this.

_childDocuments_.review: Summary:- Good try for an AC wannabe- Villagers lack personality- Lack of bugs and fish- Focused on building and resource gathering instead of making money- Gameplay mechanics locked behind a grind fest called merits.Good try to scratch the Animal Crossing itch, but it's just not it.The cute animals are all there including fishing, bug catching and your small village you can decorate however you like with stuff you can even make yourself!But the villagers lack personality, they don't have much to say outside of giving you certain quests to give an item to another villager or craft furniture for them.There aren't many bugs and fish to catch and the variety of bugs is low, it's mostly butterflies flying around.And  the one thing i missed the most... CAPITALISM.Where in AC I personally focused on getting as much money as possible, this game just isn't focused on that. It is focused on gathering resources, building stuff for yourself and the villagers and explore a bit of the area.Now I hear you thinking:" There is a farm however! I can have my own little farm!"You are not completely wrong. However, you need to unlock this farm with doing grindy tasks called merits, which may differ to running x meters, waving x times to a villager, fishing x fish, chopping x trees etc.At the moment of writing I have 6 hours in this game and guess what, no farm yet.They actually locked a lot of the gameplay behind these merits, some are easy to obtain others are a lot harder and I am not a fan of this system.

_childDocuments_.review: This game plays a lot like a happy medium between Animal Crossing and, when you unlock the farm element, Stardew Valley but doesn't really match up to the quality of either. I would recommend this game for people who have played a lot of AC or SV who just want a change of scenery but if  this is going to your first community / farming sim you might be better trying those first.

_childDocuments_.review: 5 hours in and I think it's a great game! SO cute. The town is nice, I see there's lots of potential. The townspeople and the visitors are adorable! I love doing errands for them, it keeps me occupied and they give you clothing items. It's EARLY ACCESS, give it some time! The items you'll be able to create with the design table seem ENDLESS. I cannot believe how many options there are. I can't seem to figure out how to build a bridge though? So it'll take some practice. I've invited 3 people to move to my town but each house is 400 coins so it'll be awhile until I get some more houses down. Seems like a lot of hustling for now, hoping to see more story content in the future. I'll put some more time into the game this weekend and see what else I can do to improve my town! I'll add more to my review later. I am a little lost what to do sometimes, which is the same way I felt about Animal Crossing and there's still people 1 year later rearranging their island for the 800th time. Money is slow so you'll catch bugs (which also had no intro) or fish... which I hate fishing. You get used to the mechanics, clicking left and right... it's a lot for a fish. I just avoid fishing because it's not something I look forward to. A few things I noticed: I had to google how to use the axe, there wasn't an intro?I'm not the only one complaining about the difficult equip and unequip idea. Can't figure out how to attach bait to my fishing pole... the explanation isn't thorough enough.Is there a way to pause? I figured the menu you get with clicking ESC would be a way to pause the game. It's not.The guidelines for building a bridge? Not a good enough walk-through. I'm lost on how that works. Also it froze up. Moss explains how to plant items AFTER I've done 3 jobs on digging holes and planting/growing flowers & trees."English Screen Missing" pops up in the top left while at the design table. Derris also says "Good Morning English Screen Missing".

_childDocuments_.review: This game has so much potential but it isn't worth my time at it's current stage. You have to be 4 or 5 days into the game before you can really do anything and then when you can you have to use a horrible design interface to make things like bridges, furniture, etc. You need a blueprint to make an item but the blueprint doesn't tell you what pieces you need, where they go, what size they have to be- nothing. _childDocuments_.review: I never leave reviews but I feel the mixed rating on this game is a shame so Im tossing this out there. Lots of content if youre willing to actually play for a while or if you need to give it another try post-early access to see it more polished (the route I went).Its a gradual upgrade/unlock of features as you play to get to everything, similar to AC as people have mentioned, but it has its own unique elements that make it a standout imo. Freeform item creation is huge (I havent seen such a funky open-ended design element in a game since Amazing Island on the gamecube). As for general gameplay, if youre wondering why you cant do a certain thing....just keep playing (work toward the merit rewards).It has some qol features that not every game in the cozy life/farming/crafting genre has or does well: unlockable fast travel spots, free movement of storage items without having to take everything out, free movement/re-placing of houses once the ability is unlocked, optional snap to grid when placing things (opens up so many creative decorating options when off!), easy tool switching, apparently unlimited item stacking (even the critters. ♥♥♥♥ your non-stackable wildlife AC), plenty of time in the day, etc. Lots of things I have suffered through in other games, this game does really well to get you to the fun part of designing, crafting, and decorating. That said, there are some things that could be tweaked or polished for better user experience (like the sorting of some purchase menus, let me sort the catalog by item type pls), but for me the minor inconveniences are far outweighed by the positives. Again, the ultimate freedom with item creation and then placement without a grid is is the showstopper (and really fun if you're like me and played more sims build mode than the actual game growing up). 4 bucks on sale? 20 bucks full price? Either way I'd say go for it.Fun game, good job to the team that made it!

_childDocuments_.review: So, first impressions : Some of the 3D models are horrendous, especially the hair, they're atrocious. But the lighting and colors are pretty good, so it manages to make most of it pass (most...). Animations are jerky (and please stop with those repetitive arms movements while characters are talking, they look... weird at best...). As for the first characters you meet : I don't want some cute baby-faced girafe to talk to me with some ol'redneck accent... Pick a lane. Either you choose full force cuteness, or you make the contrast over the top and humouristic. Here it's just uncanny. All those cute animals talking to you like your senior neighbours... I don't feel the magic.Will update this evaluation once I get a bit more into the actual gameplay.Edit : Okay, so still a lot of problems for the look & feel as well as the UI and controls. But, a lot of great ideas too. That custom furniture design tool could be awesome for example, great great idea, but a lack in UI / tooltips right now, and a bit limiting (few pieces available, most pieces can't be resized by much, which is very limiting, and the rules for other characters recognizing certain objects are too strict, like a chair seems to really need four legs and nothing a tad bit more original).Edit 2 : Game left early access and everything that was horrible is still horrible. Instead of making vital updates, like most "indie developpers" the dev just added more "stuff" and called it a day. Don't bother.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Hokko Life for about 50 hours, since I got access on May 28th.I honestly can't believe this game is being developed by a solo developer, with only a little outside support, like music and art. _childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game and am optimistic that the developers will continue to flesh it out into something worthy of your time, but at this time I simply can't.Pros: - the art style. This is of paramount importance for these types of games, and thankfully it's pretty good, but the player character needs more customization options beyond just the hair. The art style makes for very pleasing graphics overall.- the music. It's great. Simple, but relaxing.- the creative freedom. There's a good amount of freedom in customizing things, both in where to place furniture and how to customize the furniture itself.Cons:- the writing. It's bad enough to ruin the entire game for me, but this is something that sticks out more to me than perhaps it will to others so take it with a grain of salt. The characters are very bland and lifeless, and get used to reading "Haha" as its own chat bubble after each sentence every single time you speak with the town NPC's. Every character uses a "they" pronoun as well, which while that may seem heroically inclusive, it paints every interaction in the same shade of gray. It's pedantic and tiring.- the content. This is in Early Access as of this review, so I don't want to harp on this too much as I'm sure that much more is coming. That being said, the gameplay loop is just too flat. The days are very long, which may seem nice at first, but then you realize that the relief that comes when you manage to get that last chore done before the sun goes down is very much a rewarding part of games like this. There is of course a balance, but this game does not even try to find it. Much of the time you've done everything you care to do that day and it's only noon. It makes the experience feel more empty than perhaps it deserves.Overall, for me the initial charm has worn off after 6 hours, and once that's gone you're really not left with much. I believe that, eventually, this will be a game worth your time, but in its current state that is not the case. I wish the developers the best and encourage them to keep at it as it certainly has potential, and I will be looking forward to seeing how far the game comes as it progresses towards full release.

_childDocuments_.review: Hokko Life is a cute little game, similar to Animal Crossing.It has everything; mining, farming, fishing and foraging! You even have a workshop where you can use little pieces to design furniture that you don't have the blueprint for or you cant find in the shop. The villagers are similar to ones from Animal Crossing but besides their requests, I don't really see much interaction with them.The progression for the game can be quite slow, and it's not always clear on what you need to do to progress further. It's a game where the merits really come into play, forcing you to do the tasks to get the merits in order to progress and unlock items. For example, I didn't realise I needed to unlock the bomb through merits to progress further in the mines and then be able to get to the red forest. Sprinting in the game is quite useless as I think the walk speed is enough and there's areas where you can teleport to from basically anywhere, but sprinting is useful for merits. The sprint speed is quite quick but doesn't last long, making the merits harder and grindier to get. The regrowth of trees is infinite unless you shovel the stumps out of the ground, and they don't take too long to regrow, the flowers and the grass take the same time to regrow. The stones/rocks in the mines spawn back in the next day which makes it easier to grind for stone, coal, etc. The game can be quite misleading when it comes to using emotes (waving at villagers), I looked at the merits and found that I needed to wave at villagers, so I went to the settings and was told the emote wheel was F. I pressed/held F and nothing happened, leading me to believe I just hadn't progressed through the game enough, like how it is in Animal Crossing. I then researched it on google, just to find out the actual key was C.I'd give this game an 8/10, but I wouldn't buy it at full price and rather when it's on a sale between 50-75%. It's not worth the full price, but it is a fun, enjoyable small game nonetheless.

_childDocuments_.review: Hokko Life is an Animal Crossing clone arriving on Steam Early Access the June 2nd. This is a title that clearly tries to exploit the absence of Animal Crossing on the PC gaming landscape, similarly to how Temtem used the absence of a Pokémon game. But Hokko Life doesn’t only try to copy the mechanics of the brand, adding instead interesting feature that will please a lot of Animal Crossing’s fans!Sleeping on a TrainHokko Life makes a very short introduction on how we got the little dusty city in the middle of nowhere that we will call home: we overslept on the train and ended up there! And, how! How unfortunate! The next train will take days to come! Luckily, the little bar that we find ourselves in is filled with two very kind gentlemen (can an elephant be a gentleman?) that offer us a place to stay for a few nights. Obviously, in order to repay them, we will offer our help to make this little forgotten town a little bit more welcoming to new visitors!This quick introduction, while not particularly original, allows us to put our hands on the game immediately, without the need to wait for long dialogues that could’ve been boring. After that, we start off immediately with a place to sleep and our trusty axe: the latter will be particularly useful in the first two hours of the game, since most of the quests will involve gathering wood to build a bunch of items. In these first two hours we are also introduced to new characters, all different animals following Animal Crossing’s tradition, and complete a bunch of quests for them, culminating in the building of the first home for a new citizen.As for its current state, the very first hours of the game leave little freedom to the player in terms of activities: we will in fact work for the various NPCs that inhabit the village, gathering resource, crafting items and placing them, all according to their requests. In terms of gameplay, this quickly becomes a checklist of things to do: – go to Oma to get the quest – gather x resources – go to Moss to deliver them – Moss crafts something and asks us to place it wherever we want. I certainly would’ve appreciated to have more choices during this first part, in order to break the otherwise serrated rhythm of the initial quests.After the first bunch of quests, you’ll get access to the more advanced features that Hokko Life offers to its players: besides having items to craft, like in Animal Crossing, you will also have the possibility to design completely new items. This is done by starting from smaller, craftable parts, like a wooden leg of a chair or a plank of wood: by using for leg and one plank, for example, we could create a small table to decorate our home or, if we are willing to share, also the entire village by putting it outside. This system gives an incredible degree of freedom to the players, allowing them to create incredible items to display in their villages, with some limitations: the first one is that complex objects will obviously use more items to craft, plus the designed object must fit inside a bounding box that limits the size of the final result. In this case, bigger objects can designed by talking to Sallie, the carpenter, who sells both bigger bounding boxes and new item pieces to merge together.Obviously all this freedom in the hand of the internet could be a little dangerous, and I honestly expect to see tons of peni… tentiaries filling a lot of players’ villages. Luckily though, since this a game that will also be played by little kids, Hokko Life will only be singleplayer, with no plans for multiplayer or cooperative sessions: the only way to visit other player’s villages will be via the screenshots on Steam I fear.Similarly to Animal Crossing, we won’t have an entire house at our disposal from the very beginning, which means that we will have to work hard to earn one. After that, we will have complete liberty and customize it however we want. The customization of our home allows players to create really nice interiors, given that they have the right items to decorate them, and this can also be seen from the start by looking at the cozy little houses where the first few NPCs live in.Speaking of NPCs, we will start with just a couple of them, randomized at the start. On my second savegame (the first got corrupted after an update, something that the developer said won’t happen during the EA period) I started playing with a really rude dog called Oleander and a cute pink elephant called Mei. While the villagers are initially random, once you expand your town you will get new ones, eventually gathering them all to your friendly neighbourhood: in total there are 24 of them, with the possibility that more will be added during the Early Access period.Hokko Life is an interesting Animal Crossing clone: while it doesn’t add new groundbreaking features, it also puts the foundations for a title that could potentially be the one filling the void in the PC gaming landscape, similarly to what Temtem did for Pokémon games. Unfortunately, seasoned Animal Crossing players won’t find a whole lot of new stuff in the game, but PC players that never experienced this kind of title could be in for a surprise!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is something special! Yes, at first it might look like another Animal Crossing clone...but what makes this game really cool is that there is an awesome community mechanic to it! You're given a huge variety of pieces (think building blocks) which you can resize, color, rotate, and basically use to make just about ANYTHING! From chairs, to lights, to storage, to any kind of furniture you can imagine! And once or twice a month, there is a contest with a theme for you to create something and submit it, and the community votes on it, along with what the next theme will be!Now here's the most awesome part! You can upload your item you create to your "shop," where others can see it and download the item into their world! For totally free! And there are some REALLY creative people out there who make some AMAZING stuff!So that's what I believe is the main selling point of this game...and the discord community is AWESOME! There's also the rest of the game: farming, fishing, moving NPCs in to your town, butterfly collecting, resource collecting, etc. It's really like what Animal Crossing SHOULD be. Your tools don't wear out, items stack pretty much infinitely, and there's a fast travel system. Time flows at its own pace (it's not real time), but it doesn't seem rushed, like other games like Stardew Valley, Garden Paws, etc. It's just right! Also, there's no stamina system! Bottom line, THIS GAME IS PERFECT!

_childDocuments_.review: I've played just about every life sim out there. Life-long Animal Crossing stan. This game holds up among the best.  If you like games like that (and Cozy Grove, Stardew Valley, etc) you will like this. It has a great balance overall with resources and money that it never feels like a grind.Pros:- The building feature is so much fun. I'm not as talented as some others, but it's extremely fun- Piggybacking off the last point, being able to download things other creators have made FOR FREE- The freedom to move villagers in and out and move houses around at will- Like Animal Crossing, you can design your own wallpaper, flooring and clothes, but there's more option in the clothing such as shoes and hats- This has the best fishing minigame of all similar games I've played.  It's not as difficult to pick up as Stardew nor as simple as Cozy Grove or Animal Crossing. Cozy Grove has way better aiming though, something similar here would been great. I don't even mind that the shadow doesn't change per type of fish.- Great loading times- Adorable and interesting villagers- Fun Archeological minigame (the ones with the blue gemstone shovel are probably the most difficult part of the game)- Resources don't ever feel too constraining/hard to have enough of. Not grindy, especially with errands and the villager donation box that can be unlocked pretty easilyCons:- Limited house exterior/roof options- Depending on which hairstyle, the hats look sort of off/cuts into hair at weird spots.- Flooring is pretty difficult to make nice with the way the pattern repeats- Repetitive, but easy requests from villagers- Stores don't refresh daily, more like every other day- You can accidentally waste water in the watering can. Should have been like when you try and plant something without a hole dug or sow seeds without an open tilled soil spot/overtop already sowed seeds. Pretty frustrating until you get the unlimited watering can (which I still don't have yet at 70hrs in)Pick it up, you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is in early access so some bugs here and there are inevitable, but the team is responsive and helpful and the updates and patches are plentiful. It's REALLY CUTE, there's many items in the game, it's not too grindy, the villagers are sweet. The crafting is very open ended but that just means i end up spending way too much time making absolutely eye-searing furniture. A dealbreaker for me in games like this is the day cycle - which in my opinion is great here. You don't drop dead in the middle of the caves at a random hour, you don't have to manage stamina, and you can take naps to advance time or skip to the next day. It has a gameplay cycle that keeps me hooked without ever being frustrating or tedious. From posts in the forums I understand item management was a big problem before the storage update, but I started after it and while sometimes I DO run out of space, i haven't hit stack limits on anything which is really important to make inventory management alright and not a chore. All in all, a lovely little game.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Review edited to reflect recent updates - several of my problems were fixed!It's early days still and there is a lot of bug-squashing and such to do, but Hokko Life is already a lot of fun. However, only buy it in early access if you're prepared to deal with bugs and unfinished bits - otherwise, wait till it's finished.Check out my first 15 days in the game with commentary: Also, although the game is clearly influenced by Animal Crossing, it is NOT a clone of the game and there are significant differences. If you come into it expecting "Animal Crossing on PC" you might be disappointed. Great Stuff:+Beautiful graphics and sound+Cute characters+Design system lets you make unique furniture and art which you can then share online with others+All controls are rebindable+Slow-paced with no pressure, but not linked to real time, so you don't need to wait real life days for progress+Devs are listening to feedback and making changes/updates just about every dayNeeds Work (These things may be fixed during early access):-Fishing minigame is tedious and complex for no real reward-Gamepad support is still only partial-When you interact with someone/something while holding a tool, it puts your tool away (minor annoyance)-Limited stamina for running which seems very out of place in a game like this (annoying)-Can't manually reorganize inventory-Only one save file and it can't be deleted without finding the folder on your hard drive and deleting it-Design editor is still fairly clumsy to use and in particular, there are issues making functional bridges and ramps (often takes several tries to get a design that works and is placeable)-General bugs typical of early access (prompts and graphics not showing correctly, NPCs glitching through the landscape, and rarely, save-breaking bugs that require you to start over)Overall, I found Hokko Life worth playing and I will continue playing it through early access, but you should only get it now if you are okay with unfinished bits and bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: The first impressions are beyond terrible and continue to feel so throughout the entire start of the game. I recommend speed-running your way through the game and ignore 98% of the dialog. You'll eventually discover that the game opens up and that there is a lot to do and can be done at a relatively short time as well. You can essentially make the town and the residents living spaces look however you want too if you're interested in that sort of gameplay style or even go beyond and literally hand craft your own original interactable 3D models. I guess this is why they decided to make the town feel very bland and give you a blank canvas to work with. Luckily there are plenty of incredible community made creations that will cover most if not all your needs to decorate the bland town. These can be browsed and downloaded in-game. Why am I recommending it ? Well, there is no middle ground in these ratings on here and the pros do out weight the cons BUT only if you keep digging. I seriously recommend blazing through the beginning portion of the game which can last up to 3-4 hours depending on your understanding and navigation. This is NOT Animal Crossing so I don't understand why the devs thought that their audience are willing to be just as patient when they haven't gathered any reputation yet. Yes, this game is just as slow as Animal Crossing with uncovering its mechanics and overall goals of the game and they seriously need to change that as no sane player would enjoy going through such a first impression for the sake of their immersion and drop the game real fast. There is still a lot that has to be improved and changed. Recommend getting it on sale and only if you have the time to dig through the beginning portion of the game.
