_childDocuments_.review: While the Story told here is nothing special and very much in line with other Japanese games like BNE's very own timeline-fixing adventure Xenoverse 2, I suspect the sheer amount of fanservice will be enough to keep most fans of the franchise engaged. Short VN sections - that are notably absent when playing in coop - connect the missions with each other while lengthy and near permanent chatter between characters during gameplay further advances the plot.Visually, the game offers a clean look, with little post processing and high resolution assets in gameplay while leveraging it's anime roots during VN sections and in it's extensive use of 2D character popups.While explosions, weapon and skill effects are pretty to look at, they can at times obscure the playfield and cause an overwhelming amount of visual clutter that can make it difficult to see enemies and their attacks. The soundtrack is little surprising but constantly of high quality with a varied selection of tracks from all iterations of the Gundam anime mixed with some original music.Weapons and explosions are punchy, only the voicework stands out negatively at times. The constant barrage of chatter during missions is exclusively available in Japanese language with subtitles and can not be turned off or muted fully. Especially during more difficult missions this makes following the in-mission story nigh impossible.The gameplay is very reminiscent of other Gundam titles such as SDGO or Gundam Breaker and consists of a healthy mix of cooldown driven skills, light and hard attack combos, powerful specials and last but not least dodges and parries.The mission and grind based structure of the game creates plenty of opportunities for replayability and the vast amount of Mobile Suits from all timelines of the show offer a wide variety of style mixups, even after a few dozen hours of playtime.Of note is the abysmal Keyboard & Mouse support which seemingly does nothing more than emulate a controller, which makes camera control feel painfully unresponsive. Performance on PC is good if not fantastic and the game offers a plethora of settings one would expect from a modern PC port. Only the missing FOV slider stands out negatively in an otherwise solid release.In Summary, SD Gundam Battle Alliance is an enjoyable if sometimes grindy game and with plenty of fanservice to enjoy and several DLC Packs including missions and new Mobile Suits on the way, it certainly will be for the foreseeable future.

_childDocuments_.review: Battle Alliance is a game that is in conflict with itself and it is tough to recommend it if you aren't already a big Gundam fan, because that's the only likely reason I can find for overlooking its flaws.As you play through the game, you are constantly unlocking new mobile suits, which is cool, but you are strongly discouraged from trying them out as you get them.  In order to make progress, you need to spend funds to upgrade mobile suits to get them up to a decent level to take on increasingly harder missions, but you are given nowhere near enough money to keep more than one or two in a competitive state, so consequently, you are strongly encouraged to pick just one unit to upgrade as you play through the game.  It doesn't feel good to see your rewards for progress go to waste since you need to stay economical.It's especially disappointing, given how Artdink had the perfect unlock and customisation system in their earlier Gundam Battle games on the PSP.  There, as you fought through the One Year War you'd start with a basic GM, then get a slightly better custom GM, Guncannon, Gundam, Full Armour Gundam, G-3 and so on.  Each one would earn its own pool of custom points that could tune it up in many different ways, but it didn't boost them so much that it ever felt like starting over on a new mobile suit was a setback to recover from.  It couldn't work exactly the same in Battle Alliance, since this game bounces you from one timeline to another erratically, but that's still no excuse for coming up with something worse than what they were doing fifteen years ago.Missions aren't particularly exciting, slash your way through a bunch of mobile suits that are barely capable of fighting back in order to get to a boss that is either a mess or a pushover.  If you're an appropriate level (Or less because you've been spending your money on multiple mobile suits), you get to experience the frustration of an enemy with no hitstun, that you can't easily read because there are four of you showering it in particle effects, and that will dash across the arena to slap you down twice as fast as you can move.  Mobile armour battles get especially bad when one of your partners goes down, the other attempts to revive him, gets targeted by the boss and repeatedly knocked down by wide, sweeping attacks, and you are ultimately left alone to fight the thing, with no chance at all of getting even five seconds to help one of them back up on their feet because the enemy is utterly relentless.If you are above the recommended level, however, you'll just melt the boss without a sweat because level scaling is really strong.Half way through Battle Alliance you'll start unlocking Confused missions, which are just old stages with a new battle appearing inside.  So you're fighting the same old level 5 enemies from the first time you completed it, but with the addition of a level 25 mobile suit fight.  It's not meaningful content and the disparity in challenge within the stage just highlights what an awful idea the levelling mechanics are.I haven't mentioned the story yet because there's very little to say.  You play as some guy who gets brought to video game world with his operator for the sake of looking at a few random episodes of Gundam.  That's about it.  Combat is almost as shallow, it's just auto-lockon, pew pew, slash slash, repeat.  You get a few moves like a launcher and a wide slash, but they aren't much more than a little mixup to keep yourself entertained against fodder and they aren't very practical against relentless bosses that take no hitstun.Even with my criticism, I hope this game is enough of a success for Artdink to get another shot at this.  They put in plenty of effort into making plenty of high quality Gundam assets and if they don't get put to use in another, better game, it'll be a real waste.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game. Extremely clunky.If you love Mobile Suits, then there's a decent chance you'll have a good time with this game. If not, this probably isn't for you.SD Gundam Battle Alliance is a game that doesn't put its best foot forward immediately. Most action games will make it fun and satisfying to just mash buttons (to an extent). Generally your basic moves will flow together and you'll be able to do relatively cool and fun things just by going wild. This makes the games fun even for beginners, even if the games actually have incredibly deep, complex, systems under the surface. SD Gundam Battle Alliance isn't like this.SD Gundam Battle Alliance is built with clearly intentionally incredibly clunky combat systems with relatively long recoveries after pretty much every action you take, where there's a short animation cancel window that allows you to chain actions together in a short queue. This is actually a lot more fun than it sounds like, if you're willing to dig into the game systems (not saying that they're particularly complex, just that you have to harness them). The problem is that the game feels like total garbage to play if you don't dig into the systems. The game, thus, gives an incredibly bad impression from the start.Once you get into it the game is actually a lot of fun. It still has its problems, and clearly needed more time in the oven (the Bawoo literally T-posed instead of having a proper shooting animation when the game released), but its a good time.One of the major issues you may have is the boss design. All of the bosses are designed around super armor. This is, was, always has been, and always will be a lazy and cheap way to add difficulty. Instead of being able to go in and do fun melee combos on bosses you first have to break their armor, otherwise they can just trade you and slap you in the face for deciding to attack. The super armor break window isn't very long either, so you get a single combo in, and then go back to poking out their armor. Even worse are the Mobile Armors. Forget super armor, you're just not going to stagger them (aside from occasionally being able to render them inactive for a short period). Meanwhile the Mobile Armors are incredibly fast, and hit in incredibly wide areas. Hashmal is by far the biggest offender with its tail sweeping attacks that hit an absurdly wide area with high speed for high damage. This might be more manageable in multiplayer, but in singleplayer where you've got AI companions, this renders your AI even more useless than you'd normally be used to them being, since they get slapped around even while the boss is almost inevitably focusing you down.If bosses had longer telegraphs, like in other action games that focus on large bosses that you can't stagger, then this would be fine, but Battle Alliance is content with having enemies that have the same sort of movements as player units, while having incredibly buffed up stats and super armor layered on top, which just feels cheap, even if it's manageable.Compounded on this is the fact that blocking only reduces damage, rather than completely stopping it (unless you perfectly time your block), and a lot of damage still gets though. This means, unless you get the incredibly strict perfect block timing down, blocking still ends up with your eating so much damage that a boss can take you down relatively quickly, Not to mention a block gauge on top of this, so even though your blocking still has you eating a bunch of damage, your guard can be broken (relatively easily) having you eat full damage after a few hits.Referring back to the AI you can take in singleplayer: The game is relatively driven by your stats. If you're not upgrading your suits, you  going to be slapped around. Your AI has its own levels. Each one gains some XP, even if they don't participate in a mission, but the only ones that are going to keep up with you are the ones you take with you. This discourages experimentation and taking different companions for different situations, since they may simply be underpowered. A patch addressed this by upping the amount of capital dropped by a fairly significant amount. You may just rush down upgrading a suit, sure, but this allows fore much more balanced experimentation.Still, despite the questionable design choices, the combat is still pretty fun. Trying to avoid and mitigate damage while getting in pokes can be a good time, assuming you accept the design for what it is and it doesn't frustrate you.Other than the gameplay elements, the story, while not amazing, is fun. It also appears to perhaps, but not definitively, position itself as related to some of the older G Generation games (particularly Overworld). Some of the original designs and character names seem to point to that, but the game is so incredibly self-contained that it may not actually be related at all.It would be fun to see the characters from this show up in a G Generation game. Including your currently faceless MC, who has his own background, voice, and default name. I want to see him fleshed out.The fanservice is also fun. One mission has you fighting aside Amuro in Nu Gundam, as a bunch of different Gundams from different timelines show up, and he has short dialogues with them that can be interesting, like his shock (dismay?) at Uso's age as a pilot, or his confusion over Knight Gundam's interaction with him. Furthermore, your AI companions may have a short exchange with each other when you start a mission, such as Amuro reassuring Chris if you take both the original Gundam and the Alex into a mission, or Kira commenting on how flashy the Hyaku Shiki is if you take him and Quatro into a mission together. It's stuff like this that didn't have to be done at all, but are appreciated touches.Overall, I actually really like SD Gundam Battle Alliance. Honestly, it's not a great game, there's too many problems to consider it one, but it's still a lot of fun for the right kind of person - the kind  of person that's willing to dig into its clunky systems, and loves Mobile Suits.Seriously though, screw Hashmal. That fight sucks.

_childDocuments_.review: Game's not perfect but after having put enough time into it I think I can definitely recommend it if you're a Gundam fan or just like seeing mechas fighting in generalGoing over some points by people who have criticized this game:1) Lock on is broken -> Correct, even if you turn auto lock on off (which you SHOULD, particularly if you play on mouse + keyboard) any movement of the mouse will cause your lock on to swap to another target which will severely cripple your ability to actually fight properly.However, because there is a soft lock on that is always on, you are able to play without manually locking on outside of boss battles which you might need to use to see their break barI would hope they fix this down the line but even if they do not, it's a matter of getting used to not locking on when facing hordes of enemies (or occasionally using it to correct your camera orientation)2) Combat is broken -> Incorrect, majority of people who complain about the combat being slow in this game or not being able to button mash their way through the enemies are suffering from Pilot Skill Issue. Combat definitely has a decent flow to it and the combo system is very fluid as you can easily cancel one move into another, similar to fighting games.This is in fact encouraged as a higher combo count yields higher returns on the cooldown cut of your special attacks. Figuring out each Gundam's ideal combo is pretty fun and you have plenty of leeway to try your own combos and attacks to approach each fight. Once you figure out how to do so you will be able to fight enemy Gundams without breaking a sweat as you can essentially do absurd 60++ hit combos while juggling the enemy in the airWith that said, combat against Mobile Armors (AKA giant mecha bosses) are definitely much harder in solo and require you to actually pay attention to what the boss is doing as they cannot be simply juggled to death. The fights against MA are basically extremely punishing and I recommend playing ranged units in order to maintain distance against them and keep pressure off of yourself by dodging whenever your ranged artillery is on cooldown3) There is no EN dub for this game -> This is true, but let's be real I don't think this justifies a negative review. It's Gundam, it's anime mechas, as long as subtitles exist (and they do), I am okay with it4) There is too much grinding in this game -> Find the missions that allow you to farm easy money, then leveling becomes a breeze. Consider handling your finances in the game better if you constantly find yourself out of money - if you spread yourself out too thin because you invested in too many Gundams then you can't really blame the game for that.Also this is game about Gundams fighting other Gundams, that's literally the gameplay loop, I do not understand people complaining about the grind.To finish up, I highly recommend playing the advanced tutorials of the game as the game only puts you through a basic gameplay tutorial before letting you do whatever you want. The advanced tutorials introduce gameplay mechanics that will allow you to have a MUCH easier time understanding gameplay flowAll in all:An excellent action game that's held back by the absurd difficulty spikes of the MA bosses and janky lock on. If you're able to look past that, I would say this game is incredibly satisfying to play.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very specific kind of game and you're either going to love it or hate it. It's an action rpg/hack n slash kind of gundam game and its an absolute blast to play! Sometimes combat reminds me of the Breaker 3 combat....Sometimes...(I miss that game)A lot of the reviews seem to be bombing it over not realizing the type of game it is, or the style it is which is SD (chibi) style. I've noticed a lot suggesting sluggish game play but I never thought it was supposed to be insanely fast, since you have to balance cooldowns heavily early on until you get better parts for your build. A lot of Gundam games aside from the Breaker series tend to run like this. Runs just fine on PC. No issues aside from it has a slightly horrid targeting system. I play this with controller since it's a hack n slash and it is comfy. Like Breaker games though, be ready for a grind. While not as grindy as those games, unlocking some Gundams will take some luck and multiple plays of certain missions. Surprisingly it has a fun and slightly deep system to customize suits to your gameplay. It's an absolutely fun romp, if repetitive at times but sometimes, that's ok! You can take friends with you!That is the bonus of this game: it's co-op! Up to two others can join you on these missions which help with the replaying of missions honestly. I wouldn't have nearly as much fun solo. Difficulty seems fair on normal with some bosses pushing the envelope of what you and your teammates can accomplish in your Gundams. Side note: Don't focus on leveling just one Gundam. It will be good to have a couple to swap between, esp one of each role since some boss fights are very specific on the set up you'll need to be successful. Money is hard to comeby, but is easier to earn higher up the missions you go, also you can sell parts so don't forget to sell what you're not using!I can't wait for further content from this!

_childDocuments_.review: Fun Game, a lot of Gundams and Mobile Suits to choose from but it doesn't have every suit you can imagine like SD Gundam Cross Rays, but if you ever wanted a Gundam Xenoverse game this is it.A lot of people are comparing or confusing this game with Capsule Fighters but there is no PVP it's pure Single Player and Co-Op.The Gameplay, Mission and Story System is a like Xenoverse.You're going through time/missions to fix historyYou get Parts, which get better in rarity and stats further into the game you go you can equip up to 5 but you need to uncap your Gundam to equip more then 1 Part, you also unlock Gundams from Blueprints you get from Missions this can range from needing to do a mission 1-4 times, and/or having to do another mission to get out half of blueprints needed, and from my experience you are at least guaranteed 1 blueprint on doing runs again on normal so it’s not as RNG heavy as XenoverseGameplay is similar to Xenoverse in terms of fighting and dealing with enemies you will have a bunch of weak chaff enemies you deal with pretty easily, then you have bosses who are the real threats you have to deal with as some have health and boost/balancer gauge that when broken allows you to stun them with attacks and combo them moment the combo ends they are no longer broken. You can use various of Melee attacks, Special attacks, Ranged, and 2 Sub-Weapons/Abilities to do damage and for some character can be used to extend or do different combos based on your playstyle, there’s All-Rounders, Infighters (Melee focused), and Sharpshooters (Ranged and Semi-Mage characters), and diffirent Gundams have diffirent combos and combo routes you can do so expirementing can show you some new things to do on a stunned/weakened boss.The Graphics honestly I like them they have an Art style and I don't really mind SD Style Gundams, but for some it's a turn off.Controls: Right now KB/M isn't the greatest it's playable but it would be easier if side buttons and middle mouse button and scroll wheel (They are looking into it), but it's not awful just not the best so controller would probably be better for some. Performance: I'm getting a constant 60FPS, besides certain cutscene that happens where the game really struggle and makes my PC struggle.Some are having issue where they can't launch the game, others are having issues playingI have a Windows 10 Pro, 1080ti, I7-8700K, 64GB 3.2MHZ(Profile Enabled) DDR3  (I do animating on this PC, you don't need this much)TLDR: If you ever wanted a Gundam Style Xenoverse game this is the game for you, it's fun and you can customize your favorite Gundams to be stronger or do certain actions easier or more often

_childDocuments_.review: If you're expecting this game to be the next big Gundam game, you will be disappointed. While it is definitely better than New Gundam Breaker, that's a low bar and not very indicative of the mediocrity of this title. What's Good:What's Bad:The Verdict:It's playable, but don't expect a whole lot out of it. Frankly, older titles like Gundam Musou 3 fare far better despite their age. Ultimately, I think many will agree that Gundam Breaker 3 was the apex of the non-VS Gundam titles, and we're now in a quality decline where the only Gundam games getting the bulk of development time and effort are the Arcade titles. Buy it if you're jonesing for a Gundam game, or if you simply want to pad the sales numbers a bit so Bandai still remembers there's a PC market, but if you've still got a PS4 around, Gundam Breaker 3 and Gundam Musou 3 will treat you much better.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's an actual honest review that has given the game an actual chance and long playthrough unlike the crybabies who quit without even playing an hour of the game.Ignore reviews good or bad that have less than 3 hours in. To do the tutorial missions take about 5-10 min to complete after the main tutorial mission and there are about 5 of them. You don't start fighting big bosses until like an hour in and that's not including setting up you mobile suits, custom music you can import and deciding whether you like infighter, all-around or sharpshooter class. Many of the negative reviews are crybabies not playing more than an hour or two without even experiencing the game, especially the ones complaining about the lock-on....which you CAN turn off and change. So those "reviewers" aren't really credible. The cons I do have about the game are that sometimes the camera is annoying especially in really close quarter areas of maps or locked in corner. Many games have that boo-hoo. The AI teammates could be better in single player, but they are not trash. I wish flying could be faster. The over-arcing story is forgettable. Environments is lack-luster.  Can be frustrating to get lowbies in your co-op lobby who can't do the mission you set and then the mission gets unselected which means you have to kick lowbie and reselect mission. Pros:talking about forgettable over-arcing but missions that are labeled "true stories" are missions like in the anime and cut-scenes like in the anime which is awesome. Lots of mobile suits. I enjoy the customization of using parts and pilot skills. Really cool boss fights. Doing multiplayer is 100% more fun than going in single player. Executing 50 plus combos is satisfying and so is getting your favorite mobile suit. The sounds of the mobile suits are true to each anime and not generic. Visuals of the mobile suits are really really good. The ability to import songs is great and the game already has a good music list. Combat is fun and engaging especially when using role abilities and break abilities along with combo extender skills. The combat is simplistic, but deceptively high skill ceiling cap for doing massive damage and big combos. Counter attacks for the win! Ultimate moves are satisfying to pull off. Big boss battles are always great and can be challenging. What the game needs to be better experience: A pvp similar to SD Gundam Capsule Fighter. A better match making system to get into online co-op. More vibrant environment. Fly faster.VERDICT: I would recommend the game to people who like mech anime games and gundam fans. People who like hack n slash games that are simplistic with deceptive high skill ceiling and to a lesser extend of dynasty warrior enjoyers (but much smaller scale)

_childDocuments_.review: As a lover of the SD Gundam Capsule Fighter I have to say this game is a welcome replacement at long last. This is exactly what I had wanted co-op missions to be like back then. With the addition of a stamina meter in the form of a boost gauge that controls how long you can run or attack, I'd say this game is the Dark Souls of the Gundam franchise. As you begin to notice enemies telegraphing attacks you will inevitably begin to pick up on concepts like "perfect blocking" and even parrying. My only issue is the mobile suit roster is a bit smaller than I initially anticipated, so I'd urge the devs not to abandon this game and flesh it out by making all the mobile suits, currently modeled in the game already, playable and offer some updates that add more of the obscure mechs that the fanbase loves.

_childDocuments_.review: As a game that is Mixed, Its worth playing, and that's coming from a SDGO player.Best:Battle Alliance is a hack n slash goodness with a sprinkle of RPG into it. Know that like RPGs, you will be grinding for blueprints and cash for upgrades to raise you MS lv, along with your supports. With a strong single player mode and a good multi-player mode, it brings a good standard Gundam experience that fans of Gundam will love, and newcomers will be intrigue by its simple gameplay.ConsLike RPGs you need to grind completed missions to get yourself ready for harder missions. Story mode is very GUNDAM anime (take it or leave it) and it kills it a bit with no English dub, Which can make it hard to follow while you play and try to read in the missions. New players to the gundam lore will be a bit lost, but the game will give a rundown on whats happening in the lore.ClosingThis game has the DNA of the old SDGO game and for a starter, this game is worth a play. It shows that the developers wanted to show a simple game with Gundam that is easy for newcomers and for returning fans to enjoy.  If you are new to gundam, this game will be a great starter. As for Gundam fans, you wont be disappointed. SDGO fans, The DNA is there and while not exactly the same, its still worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice entry in the Gundam Universe, weren't it for the heavy grind nature of the game (which is fine, it's an rpg), accompanied by the gear grinding (lol) countinuous and repeated dialogues in game, I don't get it why even after retrying an already done mission, you have to hear characters talks overlapping to the in game audio over and over, wish there was an option to turn in game dialogues off. _childDocuments_.review: First impression: Great for Gundam fans, ehhhhh for people like me that are casual/new with the series. I only know stuff about 0079 and even then, quite little.The game has 3 different types of suits. Ranged, melee, and mixed types. Ranged excels at ranged weapons which have reload (cooldown) timers. Melee excels at well...melee. Mixed types do both at a decent level but don't necessarily excel in either. I've played around with about 7-8 different suits and at first glance, they seem like gameplay reskins, but they all have different weapons and ultimates. Ranged type units get the most out of the variety of weapons in the game that certain suits come with. It's a shame you can't change weapons in the hanger.And that's something this game fails at. You can't change weapons or the look of your suits. Why??? It's a tad of a letdown. The only customization there is...is equipping simple (at least at the point I'm at) parts to your suits, and upgrading them. Wow. "Play the game more" I will, but I can tell that this game is super repeatative, and that's where I'm going next. This game is insanely repeatative. Even if you switch mechs every new mission, which I'm intending to do from now on, it still gets kinda dull. Enemies are samey as well. This game would've been better if missions had mixed enemy types. Enemies with pure range that rarely use melee, and enemies with pure melee that rarely or never use ranged. Instead, every enemy is the same hybrid tactic. Bosses are a whole other can of worms. Bullet sponges that are best poked from range while dodging their engage attacks and hoping they go for your allies. The bosses look cool but that's about all they really accomplish. I guess the arenas are cool?Unlocking new mechs is interesting. You don't just buy them. You collect blueprints from crates and boss kills. I prefer this over having to spend a fkton of credits on a new suit. I can instantly field it and that's great! +1. The way you unlock certain mechs can require you to replay missions to get more blueprints. I like this. It's padding but optional padding that rewards you with some cool toys. Bosses are horribly designed. They feel rng heavy. Sometimes they jerk off and only attack your allies, allowing you to freely attack them at range and even with melee attacks. Other times, they target you from across the battlefield with perfect accuracy and drain a third of your health (more if you're squishy). Certain bosses such as the giant armored Zeon suit can go die. Super armor, immunity to beam weapons, all of its attacks are area of effect, huge health bar, and if your only means of doing damage is getting close, have fun! It almost always resorts to stomping or charging you, which is ding ding ding AN AREA OF EFFECT ATTACK. If you want to unlock the classic Gundam suit (might be able to unlock the blueprints later on who knows), you have to beat him at least twice. In my case, I got 2 blueprints the first time I beat him, and 1 or 2 the second time. At least the other bosses had smaller hitbox attacks and smaller health bars. Keep in mind I grinded and beefed up the melee suits, and they did nothing to him. Remember how I said he's immune to beam weapons? This means that your only way of "cheesing" him (in massive air quotes) is to use weak ranged weapons on melee and mixed suits, or use a ranged suit and hope he doesn't charge you from across the arena and destroy your health bar. It's like a rhinoceros playtested it. It smashed the controller before the testing even began. Are the other bosses just as bad? Ehh not really. Some of them were much easier, and much more fun. Shout out to the one dual wielding axe suit in the city (Can't remember the name and I'm not a super fan sorry). That was a fun fight. A shame most of them are just inflated health bars that hunt you down way too ferociously. This game is really hard to rate. On one hand, the game is riddled with repetition, simple mission design, and mechs that mostly feel the same apart from their sub weapons. On another hand, the game looks and sounds great, plays well and is full of fantastic fanservice for fans. The price in my opinion is outrageous. There's a game on 3DS called Little Battlers Experience (or LBX) and it goes for about half of the price and has similar gameplay and aesthetics, BUT IT HAS CUSTOMIZATION. You can strip and swap almost everything with those mechs.Ah fk it. I'll give it a thumbs up. The mechs look awesome, the visual effects make me orgasm and I'm feeling a little chaotic. The game isn't a super grind either (at least where I'm at), which is a massive thumbs up. Now can all of you weebs cool it? Learn to take criticism on your games. Instead of just clown awarding reviews you disagree with, engage with the critic and refute their points. Yeah yeah sit quietly in your corner with all the money you wasted on Gundam kits, while we criticize repetitious cash grabby Japanese games. Cuz yeah, this game is a cash grab. 100%. Full price for a game like this is outrageous, but thankfully lots of people like me can make a lot out of the game. Co-op is nice too although I'll have to play with randos more than likely.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun Gundam game that's almost a little mix of the PS3 era Gundam 1v1 games and Dynasty warriors, but with a slower paced combat. Melee, guns, abilities, and supers on each suit, as well as role (class) abilities that also come in handy. Combine that with the role boosts your friends/NPC friends give you, items on each suit, and pilot skills you can swap around and there is a bunch of load out customization you can work with. The actual combat is fun, in my opinion, though I can see why some people would say its repetitive. It is a grind focused game.I would have loved to see a bit of a deeper melee system where standard -> special attacks do different things depending on where you are in the combo. That's not to say the melee system is plain, everyone has combos, some have more hits than others, and everyone can do a circle slash and an upward/downward MS smash depending on if you're on the ground or in the air, respectively. There's also a combo break ability to get you out of enemy attacks, perfect guards (which turn into counters if you PG a melee attack), and a shield system that works, but you can't just sit behind both because of chip damage on regular guards and the chance the shield bar will break. It's just missing a little something to take the melee combat from good to great. As well, the Mobile Suits having different weapons to choose from would also make each suit feel just a bit more like it was actually "mine." There are, however, a lot of MS's in this game as in tradition with the G Universe at this point, and I could see how both the above point and this could become little nightmares balancing wise.I don't expect this, but honestly I'd love to be able to recolor my MS's at some point. I haven't seen this feature in the game, and have to assume it's not there at this point. Little things like that can go a long way for players.Over all, if you're looking for an action Gundam game, at least for PC, this is the best one. New Gundam Breakers was a wash, and this game is a better direction then where NGB  was taking the franchise. This game is fun, a bit flashy, and time just slipped right past as a buddy and I played it for hours. If you're unsure, save it and wait for a sale, but I highly recommend giving this game an honest try.Now, if Bandai could just get Battle Operations 2 working on PC I'd be ecstatic about Gundam games right now.As a side note, I see a lot of people upset with the lock on system. I just want to point out you can turn auto-lock off if you want and change whether the lock focuses enemies by distance or center of the screen. The lock on system isn't great, but I didn't feel it was enough of an issue to list. For me, anyways.

_childDocuments_.review: My Gundam fandom extends almost solely to the hero shooter, Gundam Evolution, (rest in peace; you were gone before your time), and by extension, the RG Sazabi kit it inspired me to buy, build, and display. This might be a hot take, but I quickly came to the conclusion that mechs = cool, and when I started looking into more kits, designs, and even some of the shows, it was only a matter of time before I'd seek out video games. SD Gundam Battle Alliance seemed to be the perfect pickup for me simply because of the sheer size of the roster; it contained all of the models that I'd come to know and love from Evolution on top of dozens of others. This game's roster covers the entire series of shows and movies that Gundam has spawned, so if you like a suit, odds are you can play as it. For someone whose interest was narrowly focused on the few models Evolution provided, which were from several different series, it was a boon to see something that encompassed all of them and more.Though the roster is impressive, obtaining your favorite Gundam may be easier said than done. Unlocking Gundams requires finding their blueprints, which are found as drops in missions- typically you will have to replay several missions per blueprint, (some suits requiring 3 or 4 complete sets of prints), and you have to be sure you play the mission in a way that spawns the enemy that drops your print. Sound confusing? Well, it's not... with a guide. Even with a guide though, playing through 3 missions 2 or 3 times apiece to unlock a single Gunpla was tedious and unrewarding. I went through the effort for my top handful of suits, but beyond that, I couldn't be bothered. You are awarded some for just playing the story mode, but the vast majority are not.Replaying a mission was tedious for the simple fact that the gameplay is simple. You have some projectiles to shoot on cooldown, an ultimate ability, and a melee combo, but there's not a ton that goes into the combat beyond reading a boss's moves and figuring out your best rotation of abilities based on the suit you choose. The bosses also come with an industrial-sized health bar a lot of the time, so the rhythm you find may result in a several-minute-long standoff with you dodging, using a cooldown, dodging, using the other one, dodging, take a swing or two, dodging, ult, repeat. It's very similar to the Dynasty Warriors-style games that pop up here and there, but I personally found it a little more mundane and dumbed-down, with my buttons mindlessly mashed just a tad more than I'd like.I'll be blunt; I wasn't a huge fan of the story. It seemed like the same story that everyone and their mom is using these days as an excuse to do crossovers with every version of every character- the multiverse is being breached and you have to fix the timelines! I couldn't be bothered to care about it in the least truthfully, however I will fully concede that as a non-fan of the shows and movies from which these timelines were brought, none of the fan service had an effect on me, and that's a huge draw to these storylines. Obviously the game isn't at fault for this at all, and longtime fans may have loved it for all I know. I just prefer when these games use something like this as an excuse to make an original story that isn't something you'd see from the canon, something like Dissidia Final Fantasy.Honestly though, gripes aside, the characterization and life brought to both the suits and pilots was great to see- the models were brought to life in stunning detail, the pilots had plenty of contextual voice lines to spice up different character interactions, and anyone who's seen a single Gundam clip would be impressed by the sound design and how true it was to its source. Love it or hate it, this game does an excellent job of putting you in the Gundam universe and letting you live your power fantasy in your favorite models.Cards on the table: this game wasn't for me. The gameplay loop didn't engage me, the fan service was lost on me, I'd prefer non-SD models in a similar game, but guess what? It's not a bad game, and I still had fun with it. The fact that I was able to beat the game despite my complaints AND enjoy doing so just tells me that people who are really into the genre are gonna love it. I had just the most glancing interest, so I have to imagine that super-fans were messing their pants over this, and I love that for them.Cinematic playthrough:

_childDocuments_.review: With the recent patch, this game is a lot less grindy & feels a bit more fluid. You're not going to mistake it for Devil May Cry, but it's fun to play & the counter mechanic adds a decent skill ceiling. I can't recommend it to anybody who isn't a Gundam fan, because the story is visual novel nonsense that only remotely makes sense even if you are aware of all the different canon storylines in Gundam. That said, it's a fun & competent third person action game, especially with friends.If you're a Gundam fan, I think it's an easy recommendation. There are tons of mobile suits, all feel unique & have unique movesets. The graphics aren't mindblowing, but the suits look nice & the visual style is clean. You can add & import your own custom music, so if you want to get all the series soundtracks to use them as background music, you can. The game has a good amount of content, as well: ~20 hours to complete the story, with unlockable hard difficulty & more unlockable suits after you do so. The DLC is costly & doesn't really seem worth it to me, but the base game is fairly meaty.Some bad reviews of the game complain about the SD visual style, but considering SD Gundam games & media are probably older than most reviewers, I don't think complaining that the style is a bad fit, or childish, or not what players expected, is too legitimate.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Not a masterpiece, but a solid game with a few flaws. If you are a fan of the franchise there's a good chance you will like this product.I just decided to post this review because I don't think the average rating depicts a fair image of this game. SD Gundam B.A. is clearly a game made for Gundam fans, or at least for people who like eastern-style mecha. If you are not in these two categories, I understand that the gameplay alone might not be enough to capture your interest.Reading the game's title, I too was thinking that this game might have been a "sequel" to SDGO. However, it was very clear since the first trailer that this was not the case. The game delivered what has been promised. A side node: I played SDGO back in the day and the PVE mission weren't anything to write home about, almost felt like a chore.The SD art style is a matter of preference. I don't mind it, but I can see why some players are not happy with it.Graphics are alright in my opinion. The game runs smoothly on my machine, it's pretty light on the GPU and honestly I never got an FPS drop even with multiple enemies on screen. Yes, the poly count and the texture quality are not up to standards; it doesn't bother me that much because the suits' animations are well done.The sounds department is solid. There's a lot of voice acting inside and outside the missions. There's a large collection of remastered tracks from the various anime, very nice.The story is serviceable. The "breaks" are an interesting concept to justify what's happening in the game. The plot is very simple though and it feels cheesy at times. I don't think the main selling point of this game was the story anyway.Honestly, I like the gameplay. You can do combos, mix melee combat and shooting from afar quite nicely. Also, every Mobile Suit feels unique and there are more than 70 of them to collect. On the negative side, I didn't like a few boss battles against mobile armors: they felt too agile for their size which coupled with the non stellar AI makes the stage a bit tedious. Controls could have been better, especially when using keyboard & mouse. The fact you can't bind the mouse side buttons in 2022 it's simply sad. The lock-on mechanism doesn't work well and if you use a mouse like myself I suggest to disable the auto lock-on entirely.

After the launch, I could say other than the two factors above, the mechanic actually has quite potential, but everything was destroyed by unoptimized lock-on function, not to mention its repetitive and grindy. _childDocuments_.review: First things first, I love this game.  Not just because I'm a Gundam fan, but because it just clicks with me.  I'll admit the combat is kinda simplistic, and the difficulty is basically just "higher levels = more hitpoints", but that doesn't stop this game from being a fun lil' beat 'em up.  I've maxed out a few of my Gundams, so at this point I'm just grinding for slightly better upgrades (upgrade parts definitely suffer from RNG shenanigans, so you just have to keep trying until you get something really good).  In short, I get why some people rate this game poorly.  I still enjoy it though, so I'll try to be fair with it.One thing I'd like to touch on is Steam Deck compatibility.  I've played this game exclusively on my Deck, with almost no issues.  It's Unsupported because apparently the Graphics Settings can't be configured to run well on Deck, but I haven't changed the settings at all and it runs fine.  Occasionally, on certain levels, the scene get just a bit too complex and it starts to chug.  This doesn't happen often, though, unless you replay the same mission over and over to get Uncapping Materials or Upgrade Parts.  Yes, I've done that...  Keep in mind that since this game is pretty demanding, your battery will not last long.  I've spun this into a positive, however.  I play for an hour, then build Gunpla while my Steam Deck recharges.  This way, I don't get bored of either activity too quickly!For many people, one major issue is this game's cheap difficulty.  Basically everyone you fight is a bullet sponge, and the bosses are even tankier.  This gets exponentially worse when you replay missions on Hard Mode (to unlock the EX Missions), and then the EX Missions await as yet another realm of pain and suffering.  However, once you reach level 80 (Character level, not MS level, it's kinda confusing), you unlock the greatest skill in the game.  Medic.  This allows you to regenerate 1 Repair Kit (up to your carry limit) whenever you use your Role Action.  I hardly ever used Role Actions until I equipped this skill, and then nearly all my woes disappeared.  This is the secret to becoming overpowered in this game.  As long as you smack the tanky bois often enough to refill your Skill Meter (separate from your SPA meter, again it's kinda confusing), you can effectively have infinite Repair Kits.  That is how you beat the overpowered bullet sponges in the EX Stages.  By becoming overpowered yourself.As I mentioned before, the combat isn't the most sophisticated.  You essentially have 3 Classes to Choose From: Infighters, All-Rounders, and Sharpshooters.  Infighters excel at Melee, Sharpshooters excel at Ranged, and All-Rounders are for people who can't decide if they want to be Punchy Bois or Shooty Bois.  I played through almost the entire game with All-Rounders, but now I swear by Infighters (Specifically Burning Gundam, because Muh Childhood) because I realized that once I deplete my beam rifle, I have to use Melee anyway.  And since I spend most of the fight smacking the enemies, I might as well specialize in that.  Coupled with Medic, a well-equipped Infighter can help you delete almost any boss's healthbar at lightning speed.  Still haven't dove deep into Sharpshooters, because they might not run out of ammo as quick as All-Rounders, but they still run out fairly easily.  Apparently their Role Action has something to do with instantly reloading the main weapon, but I never paid too much attention to that.Bosses in this game come in 3 flavors: SD Gundams that look somewhat like you and your posse (and could potentially be the exact same MS if you've unlocked it and are playing with it), Unplayable Mobile Armors that are absolutely humongous, have annoying grab moves, but get staggered and sit still for 30 seconds if you hit them hard enough (so you can hit them even harder), and SD Gundams who spawn an infinite goon squad to pummel your AI Partners and make your gameplay experience a nightmarishly drawn-out sequence of desperately attempting to dodge their attacks as well as the boss's attacks.  In short, if you want to grind for Materials and Parts, avoid missions with the third category of boss.  However, if you want to get blueprint drops to complete your MS collection, tough luck, you'll just have to deal with it.A side note about Mobile Armor Bossfights vs. Mobile Suit Bossfights.  You can juggle MS, but not Mobile Armors.  This means that certain SPA Attacks, such as Turn A's Moonlight Butterfly, are woefully underpowered against Mobile Armors, since you go right through them instead of picking them up and dragging you with them.Speaking of SPA's, they're your ultimate attacks, available every 2 minutes.  Some SPA's function as buffs, while others are your typical Anime Mega Particle Beam cannons, and some are a combination of the two.  They play an important role in grinding for Capital (Upgrade Points) because enemies hit by SPA's drop more Capital when killed.  Your SPA doesn't even have to deal the final blow.  As long as your SPA damages an enemy by even 1 point, they'll drop mega bucks when you or your partner lays the final blow.  To this end, the Alex Gundam is one of your bread and butter grinders.  It's got a Buff-Type SPA that temporarily changes it to an Infighter moveset.  Everyone you punch turns into a moneybag.All in all, you don't necessarily have to be a Gundam fanatic to love this game, but it definitely helps.  While it's doomed to be overshadowed by Gundam Evolution, I hope this game is successful enough to show Bandai that the Western Market is hungrier for Gundam media than they realize.  While I can't overlook this game's flaws, they're not bad enough to destroy my enjoyment of this game.  I recommend this game to anyone who wants a fun lil' beat 'em up.  Maybe not at full price, but it should go on sale regularly.And to those of you Gundam fans who shun this game due to a dislike of the SD Art Style, consider this:If you hate SD Gundams so much, think of how many of them you'll beat the snot out of while playing this game!10/10 will keep grinding.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-Combat is enjoyable-Designs look pretty nice especially with all that added texture-Boss Fights are challenging-UI Is pretty straight forward-Game is simple and straight forwardCons:-Not really worth the $60 price tag-A few bugs-CAN get repetitive-Not enough suits-Not enough missions-Boss fights while challenging can also be a ♥♥♥♥♥ and a half to fight-Really bad camera control but can be rectified with switching off Auto Locking and using Soft Locking-The amount of diversity when it comes to combat in this game-Movement FEELS slow but it is not too slow-Capped at 60FPSOverall Summary:Objectively, this game is pretty mid and not really worth its price tag. It's a hack and slash Gundam game. It can get repetitive but it's not to the point where you're having to run missions any more than 5 times. The bugs when this game came out were pretty bad as some of them were game breaking mainly the UE-4 Fatal Error but after the first update, I haven't experienced it since then. You can't go over 60 FPS which is a letdown as I feel there are those who have some nutty computers out there and they can easily play with over that. The combat can get repetitive but this is a game where you can basically turn your brain off and just have fun whacking grunt suits. I honestly wish there were more units to pilot - mainly grunt suits and some other iconic suits in the franchise. The roster feels small for how BIG the Gundam Universe is which is a real shame.Subjectively, I personally enjoy the game. I would honestly recommend it to anyone who enjoys hack and slash games. I like how a lot of the suits operate and how combat is. The boss fights are actually challenging and some more than others to an infuriating degree but I managed to get through them. They're not impossible to beat. This game allows you to turn your brain off and just have fun. The combat is actually pretty nice and in a way, I can see some aspects of SDGO in here which hits the nostalgia bone in the right places. The graphics are nice and the suits are nice to look at.Rating: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I was super hyped when I saw this game: finally a real gundam game coming out on steam (I mean there's New Gundam Breakers but honestly, that game is not a great time). Not another tactical rpg/strategy game, but an honest to god gundam fighting game. And while it is that, and better than New Gundam Breakers, that's about where the good ends. Now I'm probably still going to play through it, at least put several more hours in due to being a die-hard gundam game fan, but I would never recommend this game to anyone.Holy crap the grind in this game. Want to unlock new suits? better play the mission you get it from 1-3 times (probably more later on, I've seen some mobile suits that require 5 of a particular blueprint) because you get a random number of blueprints instead of the fixed amount you need. Want to actually use some of the suits you just unlocked? you're either starting back from the beginning or grinding in place with your current suit for a while 'cause if you don't upgrade it up to your current main you functionally can't use it. Get late enough and they'll introduce you to limited time missions to get blueprints, so want to finish that one suit? better go to a level that won't give you practically anything in rewards 'cause it's three directories back just so you can get one blueprint where you need five, and then you get to WAIT for the mission to open up again. It's been quite some time since I've been so blatantly told to go ♥♥♥♥ myself by a developer.They hit you with mobile armors in this game early and frequently, and unfortunately they're not fun here either. I've yet to find a gundam game where my first reaction to seeing a mobile armor on screen isn't a loud groan of annoyance. Games run the gauntlet from making them a boring slog with 8million times your hp, to being absolute monsters that'll run your ♥♥♥♥ while you do barely any damage because every developer seems to agree that whatever health mobile suits have armors should have exponentially higher pools. and of course, like everything else in the game, they have hyper-armor.Did I not mention that part yet? literally every enemy in the game from the biggest mobile armor to the smallest support unit has hyper armor: they can't be knocked out of their combos and if they start winding up congrats you better block or dodge 'cause it's going through. The melee focused ms for the pc have a class ability that gives them temporary hyper armor, but other than that /you don't have any./ That's right, despite being the "chosen commander" of the story, you need to use an ability from a specific subsection of your ms options to be on the same playing field as the bog standard enemies from level /one/.And all this would be fine if there was /any/ variability in the enemies, every mission will always have the exact same enemies in the exact same spots: making doing the same mission four times to unlock a ms /feel/ like the slog it is. I want to love this game, really I do, but in its current state I'd say stay well clear. I haven't addressed the story 'cause I honestly don't care about it: it could be the stupidest thing in the world and I'd forgive it because it gave me an excuse to fight robots. That said nothing about the story is surprising as long as you remember standard japanese tropes and it's... fine? i guess, but yeah nothing to write home about.Edit: So in my desperate thirst for gundam on pc I've continued playing this game and my complaints have only gotten worse. I've made it to directory six so if you don't want spoilers to that point then don't read aheadSomeone on the development team has a fetish for mobile armors and took their relative uselessness in the shows personally. That's the only explanation I can come up with for why there are so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ many of them and they are so bs. They can turn on a dime, have perfect tracking regardless of distance or angle, and all of them have at least on attack that hits 80% of the arena and is more luck and rng than skill to avoid. After every attack they hop back far enough to dodge melee supers (yes even if you're kissing them when you start the super) so if you have one it's really only useful to dodge some damage, which becomes necessary when the mobile armor has missiles. If you aren't far enough away to circle juke them than you're looking at 20% of your health in damage /if you guard/. Their accuracy is made even more frustrating by my choice of the musha gundam, who's second subsystem weapon gets dodged by the aforementioned hop back, and first subsystem has such garbage tracking that I'll whiff with most of it (incidentally getting hit by another of their perfect tracking attacks while I'm stuck in animation hell for a while, which is oh so fun). And for hitting directory six I get rewarded with chaos missions where I get to fight an EXTRA, STRONGER MOBILE ARMOR ON A MISSION THAT ALREADY HAD A MOBILE ARMOR BOSS. I can't even say "wow so much fun" sarcastically it's so irritating.The grind is exponential, so now if I wanted a second suit up to my musha's level I'd basically need to double my playtime so swapping away isn't even remotely viable (and as mentioned some of my gripes would be less egregious if I were in a different suit). Now I'm no stranger to grind? but typically there's SOME variation to spice things up and not beat you over the head with the fact that you're doing the same mission over and over and over again. A great example of the grind done /right/ would be dynasty warriors gundam 2, where the pilot relationship grind was probably just as bad as the capital (money) grind in this one but it didn't feel like it, because there was that variation. Even if you picked the same mission ten times the map was randomized, the enemies were randomized, and even the friendlies were randomized (out of the available pool). Here however, thanks to the blueprint grind I've heard the dialogue of Archangel's escape from Alaska base and Kira warning everyone about the cyclops system seven times. Twice on the true mission for the freedom gundam and five more for the chaos mission to get the Sinaju III blueprints. Each and every time killing the exact same enemies in the exact same places hearing the exact same dialogue.Now a "seems feasible" fix for someone with limited coding experience would be just tone down either the frequency or overpoweredness of the mobile armors (I'd like the hp bloat of enemies reduced too but that's a very minor gripe compared to my others: it's just very odd going back to fight an ace half my level, use my super, watch it do enough damage to kill me twice over, and the man half my level only lost about 10% of their hp. It just feels off is all) and to make the chaos missions actually chaotic. _childDocuments_.review: Not sure if SD Gundam Battle Alliance is a lazy console port, but it sure plays like one. Terrible UI. Can't turn any audio completely off, only down to ten percent. Reviving a teammate has a very small  "hit box" causing the player to kind of hunt around next to the downed teammate. Revive key-binding is the same as heal-self binding, so it's easy to waste a medkit instead of reviving a teammate. Activating special ability requires the player to press both secondary ability buttons at the same time. This causes the player to frequently waste special abilities while trying to chain secondary abilities.Projectiles are very slow. The player can dodge incoming fire by casually stepping to the left or right. In some cases enemies are able to dodge the players bullets by running in a straight line away from the player. Targeting system is bad. Switching targets seems to use an invisible list, meaning you can hit a "dead end" while scrolling one direction. Switching away from a 0hp (dead) enemy automatically is an option in the settings, without this enabled the player will shoot 0hp (dead) enemies until they disappear. The enemies will not disappear until you stop shooting them. The option is not enabled by default.Graphics are as good as an SD Gundam game needs to be. The mecha textures look like an angry girlfriend took a set of keys to them. Audio is pulled straight from Gundam, so sound is good, music is great. Fun game if you're a starving Gundam fan, but needs the kind of love(updates) lazy console ports never get. No, paid DLCs don't count.

_childDocuments_.review: After a non-serious and abrasive review I'd put out minutes after experiencing the title, I've decided to scrap it and instead go for a more serious approach as far as reviewing this game goes. Normally I would try to be excited for the release of a new Gundam game on Steam, but this release is certainly underwhelming and severely overpriced, especially upon the consideration that you can buy a Deluxe Edition of the game for 85 USD. I feel like even with all the content, the production values alone on the game do not warrant such serious spending. This game would be worth it were the price halved and that's only because they're selling you the Gundam I.P., and in such an underwhelming state at that.Ultimately my gripes with this game come down to the presentation first and foremost, and of course then the gameplay itself which is bogged down by the presentation itself if you can believe that. For starters, the menus look so cheaply thrown together. It's all static imagery, it's all very low effort in general. It doesn't say "sci-fi," it just says "cheap mobile game menu execution." Nothing glows, nothing pulses, it doesn't quite establish the mood necessary that comes with a game that's billed as being an awesome Gundam robot showdown beat-'em-up.This carries over to the game's completely unskippable cutscenes:Do you remember those really stupid YouTube videos of some game reviewer or some other kind of garbage where a poorly-drawn cartoon voiced by a cynical snarky-voiced tryhard would appear over a video's content? That's pretty much what we're left with when it comes to these boring bits of exposition that spend so much time explaining the obvious to you insofar as the plot is concerned; the story unfolds around boring characters explaining obvious stuff and they're just near-static images with mouth movements that are reminiscent of games like . Just so very little effort involved with these moments of, again, unbearable and unskippable hand-holdy exposition. This kind of hand-holding even extends to when the game is trying to tell you how to navigate the menus: The game will not tell you how to access specific areas, it will take you to them, then it will do the task it is trying to educate you on for you, and then send you on your way.More damning about this hand-holding behavior is something I found extremely obnoxious during the tutorial level:The game sets you in the tutorial level. Great. And then tells you how to attack. Now, most games developed by sane individuals would simply show you a button prompt and you'd be put in a scenario where you could experience consequence but you'd still be safe to try the move out yourself. Instead of this, the game will interrupt you mid-attack, will cut to black and show the attack being done in a pre-rendered video of the steps it shows you. This happens  times, so of course this creates some pacing issues when trying to even get started. Rather than just let me figure it out for myself the game keeps trying to hold my hand with this over-designed means of butting in and establishing what are .Speaking of over-design, in stark contrast to the game's bland menus, we have on-screen during any given moment of gameplay the following when it comes to this game's in-game user interface:- At the top left, meters involving your teammates' health. Okay, great.- At the top, dead center when applicable: Boss health. Fair.- At the top right: A huge radar that takes up an obscene amount of screen real-estate. Not sure why we need this considering we can use our eyes to gain situational awareness. We already have to do this when picking up capital or items from the map, why can we not simply scout our enemies and allies out with our own eyes rather than this cumbersome interface, complete with its mission clock helping take up further space?- On each side of the screen, left and right: Oftentimes two portraits of two characters talking, which eats up an even more obscene amount of screen space. When characters are talking, you - At the bottom center: , which is flanked by- Your health at the bottom left and your ammunition count at the bottom right. Both oversized. Non-negotiably static in presentation.By now you can imagine that all of these things going on takes away from the action, and that's because they do. You have meters depleting depicting ammunition and health all over the place, the characters talking, and all the other stuff while you have a battle to fight straight ahead at the center of your screen. Remember when I brought up situational awareness? That's even more important now because you have enemies coming at you from all sides while a lot of this is going on, and you're going to be taking damage because you didn't see an enemy lurking behind someone's portrait or something.To show you how attached these developers were to this awful idea of having character portraits and exposition at every last turn, take a look at this image for a moment:Completely obfuscating one of the team members in an establishing shot to show off this generic anime girl who speaks way too much, when this could have easily been solved with:- A smaller subtitle box with- A smaller portrait or even THAT portrait completely downsized to fit said smaller subtitle box or- Them just doing what Super Robot Wars does, allowing us to see both a character talking and all the good robot action on-screen.There, now hire me to help you design a better U.I. because this is too much. Guys. There is too much on-screen. This is just like that Touhou game, : It also had too much going on on-screen, and it ended up doing far more harm than good. Simplicity . You're putting all the spectacle in the wrong places and your game is suffering for it.Speaking of spectacle, so many effects obfuscate the combat involved. Most damning was close to the beginning when you , and the Beam Sword it has just goes nuts and you really can't tell the beginning of the attack, whether it's contacted you, how many times it's contacted you, and so much gets lost in the spectacle that reading combat can be made difficult because there are too many effects. Especially when multiple units converge to beat up on the same guy. The only true indicator is the damage numbers, which strangely were the only things you could toggle on and off when it comes to the user interface. You  be taking hits because there are some parts in combat that are not communicated cleanly and effectively.The gameplay itself is actually pretty okay for the most part. It comes down to blocking effectively, striking effectively, dashing which works as a dodge, leveling up your pilots and your mech suits (whose levels don't carry over so you'll have to level them up one by one, which is acceptable enough although annoying in some respects). Yet at the same time I could definitely see how the gameplay loop itself could get very old and very fast, which is what is so amazing to me when you realize that this game is as expensive as it is. Overall, it's such a plain experience that happens to get in the way of itself when it decides to self-sabotage by being boring where it needs to get you excited, and being too overstimulated when you need to channel that excitement into focus to actually play the game. is really only good for the hardcore fans of the series, I feel like they could overlook these gripes of mine. I personally like the gameplay and everything but despise the design of it.It's 30$ good, and even then I'm not going to go to my computer and be hyped to play more Battle Alliance.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, this is a rather fun game. It at first appears to be on the "simple" side of a hack-and-slash, but it has quite a lot of depth to it. The more deep techs that can be utilized to achieve victory--even when under the level recommendation--gives a sense of accomplishment when you can consistently utilize these techniques. Be warned: these techniques are either barely explained in the tutorials or not even mentioned at all; there is quite a learning curve for them. It is really enjoyable, especially with friends. If you want all of the achievements though, you'll need to play alone with AI companions and level them up as well. Regardless, this game is best with friends.The story starts off seeming like it is "Xenoverse, but gundam;" however, as the story progresses, the plot takes a very interesting turn and gains a lot of depth (even the SD style is explained when the first cinematic is realistic). Not having a localized dub is a little disappointing, but anyone who doesn't recommend simply because of not having a localized dub has some serious issues with entitlement. The biggest issue with not having the dub is that there are exposition and dialogue dumps during fights, and you will not be able to get all of the interactions unless you pull away from fights to read. End-mission debriefs are similar to Phoenix Wright Ace Attorney discussions, though many times much more tedious and longer in length.Be warned, like many other SD Gundam games, this requires grinding and replay of levels for either currency or to unlock mobile suits. For me, it usually only takes 1 or 2 replays to achieve an unlock, so it is not horrible. The biggest grinding hurdle is the currency for leveling. Many later suits are much better overall than the earlier suits (obviously), but since all of them start at level 1, it makes leveling a chore at times.That's the end of the review. If you want some early-game advice, read below.****SPOILERS****(Assuming you did not have the pre-order bonus or digital deluxe edition)1. For a good early-game Infighter MS, get the Norris Packard Gouf Custom.2. For a good early-game All-Rounder, stick with the Zaku II until you find one that you like. Alex is a good choice because the Special Attack currency bonus counts for the entire time that you use the Alex's armor special attack (see #10 for more info).3. For a good early-game Sharpshooter MS, the Kampfer is a MUST.4. Advice with bosses: for larger bosses like mobile armors, use the Kampfer (or a non-beam sharpshooter of your choice). Many mobile armors have beam fields, and the Kampfer uses all physical damage besides its beam saber. If it is a normal MS/gundam, use the Zaku or Gouf.5. In solo-play, you do not need to level up the MS that an AI uses. Its stats are tethered to your player level.6. Do the practical tutorials in Directory 0 as soon as possible. They give helpful information early and currency for completing.7. Use the "Free Tutorial" to try out different mobile suits and find ones that are good with your play style.8. If you are grinding and leveling up a mobile suit, have it as an AI companion (if playing solo) so that you can gain friendship with the pilot for the achievements.9. Combos are your friend! For every 10 hits in a combo, your Special Attack's cooldown is reduced by an additional 1 second AND it stacks (50 hit combo will net a 15 second reduction: 1/10, 2/20, 3/30, 4/40, 5/50). This is another reason why the Kampfer is a must-have MS. Each pellet from the shotgun nets as 1 single hit, so 3 blasts (if all the pellets hit) nets a 27 hit combo (3 sec off cooldown). 10. Special attacks, if you are close enough to the target, will lock them in place. Special attacks will also lock nearby enemies within the same range. Enemies that are stunned by the initiation of the special attack will net higher currency rewards, so don't just hold onto it for boss fights, use it in a group of grunts too (this will make grinding go a little faster by netting you higher rewards).

_childDocuments_.review: I was really looking forward to this, but unfortunately it was very disappointing, especially considering the price.2 hours in, and you've basically seen everything gameplay wise - basic repetitive stage grinding.If you've played previous games like:Playstation Portable - Mobile Suit Gundam SEED: Federation vs. Z.A.F.T. PortablePlaystation 2 - Mobile Suit Gundam Seed Destiny: Rengou vs. Z.A.F.T. IIPlaystation 2 - Mobile Suit Gundam: Federation vs. ZeonYou will be greatly disappointed by the "feel" of this one.The only enjoyment would be the roster available for you to unlock/collect (and tediously grind to make them even usable).The core action game play is very weak in multiple ways:- Melee is objectively stronger; ranged is merely a suggestion, even on the class that focuses on it - the illusion of choice.- Ranged attacks are just spam attacks until they go on cooldown - they lack any sort of meaningful weight or threat.- Melee is just basic combo, special (heavy) attack, sweep (heavy 2) attack, or launch + aerial combo - you will only use 2 of these really.- Enemy mobs are just sandbags, the stage Boss is just a sandbag with an (annoying) anti-flinch shield that can recover halfway, and some have insane move sets that can stun lock you.- The camera angle/controls can be real nuisance; sometimes it feels too far, in close combat it can get blocked by other objects especially in urban areas - you will struggle with it.These to just name a few of the major ones.All of these just compound to a core game play loop that feels really bad to play and is unsatisfying.But hey, at least you have nice Mobile Suit models to look at... right?

_childDocuments_.review: [Intro]This game is a must have if you are a Gundam fan, or even a mecha fan. This game is action packed and will most likely have your favourite MS in it. Yes, this game can be a grind, but it is not that bad and I quite enjoy every moment of it. Personally, this game reminds me of the good old days playing online Co-op on the PS3 with Gundam Senki 0081. [Pros]- Great graphics for Gundam standard- Beautifully replicated stages of each respective Gundam timeline- True co-op focused game- Combos and controls are quite fluid and not overly complicated- Every MS feels different and has great animation- Enough MS to choose from all different series (at least the popular/main ones) [Cons]- Dialogues can be quite lengthy if you are not into these type of things- Could have been better if including 4-6p co-op for certain maps/stages- Can be a grind if you are a perfectionist (you probably don't mind if you are one)- Camera lock-on/reset can be annoying sometimes  [Final Notes]This game doesn't have PvP, though I didn't listed as a con because personally I find PvP might start to introduce Pay-2-Win elements into the game. Then it will be no different to any other cash-grab PvP titles. I'm happy the focus is Co-op and SP with a not-to-bad storyline (though I skip them all lol). I do hope they release more DLC packs and new mission packs in the future to continue to support the game (rather than a version 2). Also, please increase the number of players both SP and Co-op, happy even if its map-dependent, would've loved to rollout the full 00 team. To buy or not to buy,If you are a Gundam fan and can afford it -> Buy it now.If you are a fan of co-op and likes Mecha -> Buy it now.Any other reasons, just wait for price drop or avoid.

_childDocuments_.review: Like the top review said, a lot is missing here. I didn't try the demo since it was only on console, when the opening started and I got excited that maybe I get to create my own character and customize like Battle Universe series or SD gundam G generation series. HAHA how naive of me, nope you just input a name for multiplayer and that's it. You are literally just some dude who's mute the entire time and get used like a cog in this ♥♥♥♥♥♥ story plot. Okay I get it, it's fan-service and cross-overs, I did not expect the story to be good. The gameplay is grindy and I can also accept that. The lack of progression and customization is pretty bad tho... I'm currently on chapter 3 and I've already pretty much played everything that this game has to offered. Go do missions, unlock suits, upgrade with money, collect bonus parts, level up bonds, etc etc. Suits you just upgrade all 4 of its stats there is 0 build variety.I will say that some suits are more fun than others for having different cancel routes and combos, the combat I will actually give it a passable grade. When you play a fast suit and it feels good. There is just guard and just dodge system which is cool. However, imagine if we had our own pilot stats and progression on top of that... Too bad we don't live in that world because bamco always like to cut back and still sell the game with full $60 price tag... The lock-on system I'm actually fine with since I play GVG and EXVS series, I'm used to manually changing target. The best part about this game is the fan-service and cross-over dialogues obviously, its remix themes, and being able to use custom soundtrack. Graphic looks nice, the iconic scenes from the shows and presentation is good. I'm sure once I get to co-op with my friends it'd be a lot more fun than just soloing through story. In conclusion, buy this on at least 50% sale at 30 dollar price tag. I can see this game being aimed at a younger/casual audience but that doesn't excuse how barebone it is, when they've done better before and could've easily copy pasta some system from older games. I'm disappointed to say the least, and I doubt DLC will fix the core design issues we all have with this game.Edit:I've beaten the game and did lots of ng+ content. The negative review remains... There is so much potential with this game but everything feels incomplete. Only like 2/3 of the series actually has a story part in this game, the rest are just filled into "chaotic misson" where you farm the same exact mission again, but with 1 extra break in/invade. A lot of the story scenario will get you hyped up then cut off in weird spots then it cuts to the two character in original story mode explains what happened after, why? Later stage design are absolute garbage (especially the one gundam wing stage), there is somewhat of a challenge in terms of difficulty where you have to master the combat system again hard MA and MS bosses, however it feels like no one play tested this  to the fullest, you resort to cheesing some of them rather than having a exciting boss fight. I've spent about 15+ hours in co-op with my one other friend who is pretty good at the game, it's a lot harder if you do not have a 3rd player and you cannot add AI to vacant spot, there is also no spliscreen co-op for local play. Another big oversight is, doing any mission on hard mode does not count clears toward normal/easy mode, while if you clear it on normal it counts for both normal and easy? It just makes 100%ing the game a lot more tedious, a lot of the mission you are waiting for the character to say the same dialogues for the 100th times and cannot skip them... some suits are just straight up way better than others, and it is not based on how hard it is to unlock them, it feels like suit balancing is also really bad...
