_childDocuments_.review: Another game getting a lot of hate it doesn't deserve, mostly due to people not reading or ignoring the SD part of the title or wanting it to be something it isn't.SD Gundam Battle Alliance is a pretty fun beat em up action game that plays more akin to a fighting game where it's best to look for openings to punish and break the balance on boss mobile suits to string together you're combos to ramp up that damage, or punish the mobile armors after their string of attacks get a few hits in and get out.The difficulty is pretty solid requiring a decent amount of skill and attention not found in a lot of games today and depending on your skill level the difficulty might seem to spike every now and then, just know guarding is very important and the auto guard part it gives you at the beginning of the game is a trap that I wouldn't recommend using as it could lead to bad habits during game play and could make some fights harder. Learn how to guard yourself and learn the attack patterns and if you do fail just learn from it.The big negative I have for this game is the lock on switching for keyboard and mouse, as if you are locked on switching lock to another target is moving the mouse and it is "very sensitive" often leaving you missing attacks or turning your back when you don't want to. An easy fix would be to just let us change it to another key, this isn't much of an issue on controller.All an all It's a pretty fun game alone or with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: If you love SD Gundam as a whole, then playing this game is worth your while since it consists the core game play of RPG based action and the idea of collecting all Gundams that are yet to be unlocked. The thrill of the game is that it challanges the player to grind and basically develop skills, items, stats,and equipment that may vary on its effect or rarity. As a casual player/gamer this game will not disappoint, yet if you seek the competitive side of things, the game wont cover much on its multiplayer lore. The story and content was well done yet if you are leaning towards the long span of the game, I'm afraid you'd wish there's more added story lines within the SD Gundam franchise. Furthermore on those whom loved watching various gundam anime series, the game is very straight forward in showing the sense of nostalgia along with its music themes that straight came from known series such as the cosmic era of seed, 00 series, UC, etc. It is indeed notable that the developers did their homework in having each series to coexist all in one, while reminiscing familiar classic Gundam franchises together at a deformed chibi sized gundam that most gunpla collectors or fans alike love and enjoy aesthetically. The only disappointing part about the game is that It has lackluster features on multiplayer and missing things you may find known to specific gundam units that lack abilities seen on anime or other similar games you've played in the past. However, the presentation on the graphics design and combat mechanics are superb or should I dare to say very satisfying enough to cover a bit of its flaws. Overall its a solid game that resembles past classic and modern Gundam series with a heartfelt care in developing the game and how it shows passion to show attention to details. Somehow at the end of playing SD battle Alliance, players would probably tend to question additional contents and additional features that may somewhat be seen in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: A decent game, held back by odd decisions.The story mode is decent, and serve the premise of the gameplay pretty well. The switch from regular Gundam models to the SD one is honestly top notch. The music choice and the series included are also great. They don't overly focus on a singular timeline, which is something I was worried about, as many Gundam games seem hell bent on focusing on the SEED/Unicorn Timelines. The choice of units that are actually in here, is also really nice, some good suits that I genuinely didn't expect to see as an inclusion (such as the GM Sniper II, The Reginlaze Julietta, etc). However, the game also falters pretty badly in these same areas. While the gameplay is fun, it's grindy at times. And playing as a ranged unit is just hellish at times. Your AI companions are mostly worthless unless you get their friendship to max rating, at which point they become somewhat useful. Mobile Armor bosses are by and far the worst part of the game, fighting the Psycho Gundam, any of the Garbage Space MAs, and even Devil Gundam and the first fight with the Zeong are just ridiculously unfair. You're expected to hit them in their weak points for increased damage, which is almost exclusively their heads. However, that requires flying, which consumes boost and reduces your ability to fight for extended periods without using chain bursts. Flying also reduces your ability to avoid incoming attacks if you're fighting, because again, boost is required.The choice of suits, while I do praise them for including some lesser seen mobile suits, is also baffling. They omitted basically anything from Wing aside from Wing Zero and Epyon. This wouldn't be a huge concern, but you fight Leos, Taurus and Virgos, and you interact with Wings timeline 4 times. Meaning each time you go there, the boss will be one of those two gundams. If they'd added say, Tallgeese or the Mercurius and Vayate, it'd be less repetitive to fight in this time line. Wing isn't the only timeline to suffer from this, as G Fighter also suffers from the same issue, as does CCA. Progressing isn't nearly as difficult as some people make it sound, just play the game on Easy mode, get to mission 7-2b and grind it out once or twice with Alex Gundam, God/Master Gundam, any of the 00 Gundams, or the Lupus Rex, and you'll have more than enough to get a mobile suit up to level 50 (the cap before beating the game), that said, early game it IS a struggle if you want to play a specific suit and don't have it unlocked yet, and since most of the suits are unlocked through either playing a mission or clearing a chaos mission (an additional break in during a mission you've already completed), it makes getting a suit you want, and also leveling it up  before the end game tedious at times.Overall, with how much I've complained here, you might be wondering why I still recommended this game. Frankly, it IS a fun game, especially with friends. The core game play loop is fun and the moments they chose from Gundams 40+ years history really do feel great to play through... when they don't involve Mobile Armors. So yeah, I'd say get the game, preferably on sale, as 60 USD is a bit much for the content we're offered here. If the game DOES eventually get the support that Xenoverse 2 gets, I'd recommend it even more.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr I'd give it an 8/10. An above average, excellent game, with only a few downsides, but to get into it...SDGBA is a gundam hack-n-slash game with a fairly wide pool of SD Gundams to choose from, including an SD Gundam which was given a regular Gundam design which was then given a new SD Gundam design based on that... for reasons.Anyways, the pool is a little slanted, with most series only have 1 or 2, and a few series like IBO having 4 or more, so this is definitely a game where you'll want to look up what it has on offer before purchasing.I want to dispel a rumor before going further: THIS GAME HAS  TO DO WITH SD GUNDAM CAPSULE FIGHTER ONLINE. This is part of ARTDINK's series Gundam Battle, which was not released out of Japan until now, hence "Battle" Alliance.As I said, it's a hack-n-slash, but that may have been a bit misleading. The game's difficulty rises quickly as you play through, with several chapters being considered "player filters", which seems almost specifically designed to force you to get good at the game. While you can see for yourself the combos are very simple and nothing in the button layout should be particularly confusing, but this is like saying Dark Souls is a hack-n-slash because its combos are just R1>R1, You'll find as you get further that you either need to strategize, learn how to perfect guard or dodge, or play as a much easier mobile suit (sharpshooters work for many people). While the mooks are easy to kill, the bosses are the meat and potatoes, and they are very well designed. They have a limited moveset, usually 3-4, with a powerup phase that introduces a couple new moves. There's exactly enough to learn and master; there's not too much to become overwhelmed or too little that it becomes simple. There's also a wide variety of bosses and boss types, that play very differently. Unfortunately, all of this means you won't really know if you like the game until you're 10+ hours in and far past the refund limit, so spend cautiously.This is where I get into the negatives, of which there are few and they're mostly nitpicks.My first is there isn't enough of the game. You have the story mode and co-op and that's it. No other modes. No boss rush or timed trials or challenge missions. At most you can say Chaos Missions are a little extra because they add a boss to a level where they don't belong, but that feels like more Story Mission in my opinion.On the note of story missions, I really wish they had translated the dialogue into English, as it stands this is by and away the worst part of the game, and this is the only negative I wouldn't call a nitpick. I can't fight and read the them talking at the same time, and it's frustrating and overwhelming as an autistic person to listen to them speaking a language I don't understand with text boxes in the middle of boss fights. I know there's a mute, but that doesn't fix the text boxes, so short of translating it to English, I wish they'd give the option to turn it off entirely.Next, capital is required to upgrade your gundams, but they don't give you a lot of capital and you get a LOT of gundams, so you're forced to pick 1-3 gundams and focus only on them. What happens if you don't? The game actually has an underlevel mechanic where you deal significantly less damage than you should because your gundam level is too low, so you must keep up to date throughout the story. 1-3 is more or less okay, especially because you CAN drop gundams and move to others by just not upgrading old gundams anymore, but it does take away from the variety until endgame.Additionally, certain gundams do not feel like they were given very much attention, as they have skills which many wouldn't consider important or accurate, such as Arche having ranged funnels. Arche does have these in the show, but many would consider the beam fangs mode to be more appropriate. Additionally, other gundams have a class which doesn't make too much sense to me, such as Dom being In-Fighter, but this issue is much rarer. In both cases, however, a non-gundam fan would never notice or care, so it doesn't matter much.Finally, there are some rare bugs in the game. I had some issue using .mp3's for music. They would start and stop at odd times and occasionally crash, so I removed them. And on one mission a blueprint wouldn't drop for non-host players, which was very annoying, but all-in-all bugs were rare for me.I know I referred to all mobile suits as gundams, and that is not accurate, but I felt it would be the least confusing term for non-gundam fans, as I imagine most gundam fans have already settled on if they like or hate this gameI did not cover music because you can change the music in-game and beyond that you can hear the music for yourself and/or see the song list online. I also did not cover graphics for a similar reason: you have eyes and can see for yourself. I wouldn't want to disrespect your intelligence by implying you can't see or hear if you like something on your own.Finally, I'm a huge gundam fan, and as a result this review is pretty biased, but I sincerely hope it's also informative nonetheless, and I did my best to approach it from a perspective of someone who isn't a gundam fan because I'm confident gundam fans have already made up their mind about this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I am providing my review of this game now that I've gotten 100% achievements for this game. The game is totally worth its price. This game does have its pros and cons and for all its worth, can be incredibly difficult and frustrating at times but can be well worth it once you figure out the nuances to the game. This is a looter-shooter type game where you enter a stage, experience the story if you wish and gain loot in the form of Parts to enhance aspects of your Mobile Suits/Gundams and blueprints to get expand your pool of usage units. The game feels much like an action-fighting game; you go in and cut things down with your GN sword or duke it out with your beam rifles and guns until you face the Mobile Armors. As with all Gundam games, fighting Mobile Armors is an absolute pain in the ass especially when playing solo. Most mobile armors in this game has I-Fields which you need to break by consistently shooting Beam ranged weapons. Your AI partners are extremely dull when it comes to attacking so you'll need Parts and maybe the Pilot Skill Piercer to deal increased damage vs I-Fields. You can of course opt to use a physical attacker but the game developers made it so that if you are able to take down the I-Field, your beam attacks do increased damage to off-set the time you may have wasted breaking the I-Field. I learned how to Perfect Guard really well with most Mobile Armor enemies. You can Guard and Side Step in this game but Side Stepping isn't really that good because the game's tracking AI is really stupid. Unless you perform a Perfect Side Step which is pressing the button at the correct time, you're going to get smashed so I went with Guarding for most of the time since if you perform a Perfect Guard against enemy melee attacks, you can perform a Counter that destroys their Balance meter allowing you to put in more hits while they're staggered.. That said though, some enemies can be Side Stepped easier than others.The Target Acquisition/Lock on system in this game is a pain in the ass to deal with when playing on Mouse and Keyboard. Using a controller is fine and a lot more manageable. I still don't understand what way to shake my mouse to change the lock on target. The reason for the problem is when fighting bosses, sometimes add spawn and you just want to stick on the boss but you may accidentally move your mouse a bit as you press Mouse 1/2 and game goes, oh you want to target that dood instead and switch off the boss. Then you struggle switching from add to add trying to lock onto the boss again and die miserably. I really enjoyed the dialogue in this game. The overall story is meh but the character interactions in this game is amazing. It's like on the level of Super Robot Wars where some characters actually have lines related to characters from other series. There was one particular mission where Amuro joins as a ally in this mission and there are characters from different series that pop in and Amuro would have some dialogue expressing his thoughts on those people and their timelines. The cutscene animations the game developers placed into the game are also very nice too. That is also to say that the Gundam models and animations in this game are amazing. Using weapons whether it be ranged or melee weapons you can actually see the full animation of the Gundam doing the action including pulling the beam saber out to attack and returning it place after finishing unless you animation cancel. Oh yeah, SDGO players would love to know MCA is in this game although not as easy. Now the one thing I dislike the most in this game are Special Attacks (SPA). Ranged SPA aren't that bad but melee SPAs are absolutely horrendous to the point that it's useless in some situations. Against Mobile Armors you can pretty much kiss your melee SPA good bye because unlike non-Mobile Armor enemies which get stunned if you SPA close enough, Mobile Armors couldn't care any less that you used it and just does whatever they want to do and which is usually jump out of the way. Like I mentioned earlier, non-Mobile Armor enemies get stunned but they are not locked in place which means if someone knocks them out of your way, then your melee SPA is S.O.L. I don't understand this design idea.Ranged SPA also has its fair share of problems. If you lose track of your target when you use your SPA, you would miss the SPA entirely as well. Half the time that both melee and ranged SPA miss is because of the cut-in animation that prompts when you SPA. It's like a whole 2-3 seconds before you actually start attacking and so many things can happen in that time frame. On the subject of SPA, I also don't understand the design concept for some of them. SPA damage can be beam, physical, or both (hybrid) and can be ranged, melee, or both (hybrid). So you build your Sharpshooter with Ranged damage but its SPA is melee like why? Same goes for In-fighters which you build melee but its SPA is ranged. The game definitely has annoying game designs that makes no sense and some artificial difficulty because of said game designs but the game is fun to play. Playing with friends make it more enjoyable of course but there is multiplayer so if you're faced with a difficult mission, just create a room or join a room and play with others. Now I just want more Gundam variety added to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: A really enjoyable game, but fair warning, there are hitches along the way.  The plot is nothing to write home about, but many of the character interactions between those who normally wouldn't see eachother are pretty charming.  Music is pretty good, and like most Gundam games it includes a means to introduce your own custom tracks, along with the ability to have it cut in certain songs when you activate your Special Attack.The big thing though is that this game feels INCREDIBLY inspired by an old Gundam F2P game named SD Gundam Capsule Fighter Online(Or SDGO).  Back attacks, movement, sub-weapons, parts, the "trio-category" system for organizing unit playstyles, it's all incredibly familiar, just improved, while also adding their own dash to make the game unique, of course.The game also has a pretty satisfying combat loop against normal-sized bosses:  Bait out attacks, and hit them with your Subweapons while their stamina gauge is lowered to force a "Break", then do your best to rack up a large combo to do as much damage as possible.  It's simple, but intuitive and with a surprising depth that encourages players to figure out how to play the units they like the most.The difficulty can be a bit of an issue.  The best way I've seen it described is that instead of difficulty "spikes", there are moreso difficulty "steps".  Nothing really feels "insurmountable" or like a massive jump, but there are definitely moments where the game gets more difficult, and it feels frustrating until you adjust.The best thing I can recommend is that you get used to guarding.  Perfect Guards will ensure that you take no damage and lose no guard gauge, but even if you're unable to, it's still far preferable to block than eat a hit.  In a game where early units can end up with 500-900 HP, blocking will easily take off over a hundred damage from each hit.The main complaint I really have with the game is how grindy it is.  Not for blueprints to unlock units, that's fine, not even for parts, that's cool too.  But instead, I hate the Capital grind.  You just get too little money for how much the game expects you to have a variety of units.  As an example:  If you focus on a unit that specializes in ranged beam attacks, you're probably going to not be happy when you start fighting enemies with I-Fields.  Not just that, but it really encourages sticking to one unit, and that just feels wasteful in such a great game where all the units feel pretty unique and fun.  Not to mention the stats are already capped by the, well, "Uncap" system, making sure that you stay at a pretty reasonable stat spread for each section of the game.Another small issue is that the AI is..really, REALLY bad.  If you have friends, this isn't a big deal, because you can play with them.  But single player can certainly be a little frustrating with how much these guys get in the way.  But it's not the end of the world, the game is still absolutely playable in single player mode.All in all, I do think the game is a hearty recommend on my part.  I'll admit there's some nostalgia bias on my part because SDGO was how I got into Gundam in the first place, but it's been an incredibly fun time.

_childDocuments_.review: For someone who's been starving for a good gundam base game. This game actually scratches the itch. On that matter the battle itself feels good it makes up for the chibi style graphics they opted in this game. just don't use keyboard and mouse coz its more enjoyable in a controller. The only thing lacking on this game is space battle. There are alot of stages in this game and its all fighting in flat surface. We also need under water battles coz if you are familiar with gundam games there were battles fought under water and above water. On the other side this game lacks costumization I really wish that you can create your own Gundam or even pick your loadout to bring into battle. There is alot of Gundam that you can choose from. All the way from the very first anime Mobile Suite Gundam all the way to the most current one which is Gundam: Iron Blood Orphans. You can pilot iconic all iconic gundams or even choose to bring 2 of them on your solo mission along with their pilots. The Multiplayer can be a little toxic coz alot of them will kick you out of their lobby if you are too low level like i was. This game is really repetitive coz you will spend alot of your time grinding "capital" ingame currency to upgrade your gundam. Also you have to unlock all gundams using blue prints which you can find in each mission. some of the Blueprints can be easy to obtain and would usually be unlock by doing one mission and some can be unlock by doing the mission multiple times. All in all I find this game really enjoyable to play not just solo but multiplayer aswell. They also need to Implement a PVP arena for this game and man oh man this game will explode.

_childDocuments_.review: Battle Alliance was a great game to play. It was extremely fun, and up'd it's difficulty as you progressed making it extremely challenging, but rewarding, as you continued. It has been the best 40-ish hours I've ever put into any game. The different MS (Mobile Suits) were very cool, and despite what others have said, I didn't have much trouble upgrading random suits and going into the next available mission that I had. I found myself trying to do so many combos, and move through all enemy attacks with dodge it was funny and fun.In terms of problems, there were a couple. The lock-on system is not that great. At times, it will lock on to an enemy that is behind everyone else for some reason. The system also tends to re-lock on to something that you locked off of. The camera does not move fast enough either to even really count as a lock-on, causing you to have no idea what the enemy is doing or missing attacks on the enemy as a result of not being able to see them. I managed this somewhat by turning off Auto-lock, and quickly locking onto my targets myself, and manually moving my camera to compensate for the slow moving lock-on.Problem two : the AI companions. These things are the dumbest things on earth. Sometimes they will only heal you when the enemy is hitting them (god knows why), preventing them from healing in the first place. Many times, they will just not attack for a good while until you force them to use their ultamites/SPAs. I feel there would be a benefit if you would set options on the AIs such as :  "Heal down'd ally when x. Only heal x ally..." and so on. Being able to set these features and designate roles for these helpers would go a long way, especially for players who are completing the story alone.Tips : Use role-actions and combo cancel/reversal. Role actions give many benefits and help boost stats, attack faster, stop you from being staggered, or allow you to reload and utilize your abilities again. Reversals are very useful when fighting MS bosses that grab you, or put you into a combo that you want to quickly break out of. (can even stagger or lower their shield by a lot). I found that for the MA (mobile armors) that are really annoying (those guys hit hard and it is hard to see their attacks :/), using the "reversal" can help stop damage of one attack that is incoming. Use that info as you will.Now this game is extremely fun, with it's own faults, but I still like it. It has a souls-like feel to it, meaning at some point guarding, perfect guarding, or countering can feel very important, or simply dodging. If you like fast, challenging games (very fun with friends), this is for you. If you just want to sit back and relax, either play on easy mode, or this game may not be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Mouse and Keyboard mapping sucks, does not recognize mouse thumb buttons when attempting to remap. It does not register thumb buttons even after their 'fix' to include thumb buttons and, when it does, they are still unresponsive. Restarting the game or returning to the game after fixing thumb buttons and setting them up doesn't undo the keybindings, but outright refuses to recognize them again. In addition, mouse movements, and non-mouse movements randomly switch lock-on targets. While controlling mouse-and-keyboard, your camera is locked to the enemy you're locked onto, so you end up bouncing around attacking the wrong target wildly to a stomach-churning degree. At least you can remap lock-on to Tab or Q, but it's still useless on mouse and keyboardOverall, not a great port control-wise. At least I have yet to suffer a crash or game-breaking glitch.

The upgrade system is pretty grindy, but i suppose it could be worse. voice acting is great, plot is pretty complex but i admittedly haven't been paying much attention besides missions involving UC or AC characters. _childDocuments_.review: Solid hack-and-slash for fans of the series and newcomers alike.The charming SD graphics and bright cast of familiar characters from all across the MSG franchise will pull you in, and the satisfying combo-based combat will keep you there for quite a while. Juggle opponents, utilize your universal parry for some clutch counterattacks, or expertly dodge attacks while keeping your offense going with your mobile suit of choice's abilities.Unfortunately the game suffers from being quite frustrating - many attacks have very little wind-up and often require you to be on your toes to dodge them, and the visual noise of characters speaking, explosions coming from both sides, and little visual feedback can cause players to get disoriented and lost easily in the thick of it.I still think this game is worth a try though, and while the price is a bit steep, I think it's reasonable to say you'll get your money's worth if you're interested in the game's combat.

_childDocuments_.review: This is pleasure surprised from Bandai. As SD Gundam series (not to be confused with SD Gundam Capsule Fighter Online: SDGO which was Gacha South Korean game) has never been more than casual grindy turn based game with much for eye candy fan service until now. SD Gundam Battle Alliance is an action RPG game that focuses on reaction, with most interactive gameplay involving choosing good approaching to deal as much damage as possible, while avoid an attack from enemy. The game is allowed coop in familiar fashion to online game where up to 3 players can join in a mission and tackle the odds together.It's also a first time that they expand a story behind the simulator of G universe in full lore and fully voice original casts that actually involved in the coming plot, something that rarely happen in G Generation counterpart.For SD Gundam fan, you maybe are familiar with the purpose of the G universe simulator. Story itself narration is a welcome one as it has never been once before that the story of the Universe is cooperated with original series and is explained in this scale. Though in this review I will not point out to that but instead there's one feature I need to explain about how they narrate/carry out a story and lore in this game. Every time they brief you something about an event or plotpoint, the respective topic will be added to the cutscene replay under the library option. Inside Briefing Scene will contains said briefing cutscene. As it turns out that everytime you reach a "lore" or "plotpoint" briefing including a briefing about story of respective gundam series will never be played in a main story cutscene but instead the popup show up and said the briefing scene is added to said library, maybe they do that in order to avoid turning cutscene into unnecessary too long one and break the gaming flow. However due to this feature some people find a first impression of story to become disconnected as they found out that the casts are unusual adapt to the situation too fast. First few optional briefing scenes are, to me is actually very important introduction to the beginning of the story, which explain the cause and reason why they're here for.In this game, player gets to choose a suit which each of them has different moveset they wish to control and use then jump into mission. Mobile Suit can be tuned to increase level and performance with capital such as HP, boost, melee and ranged stat. Player can obtain more mobile suit throughout drop or reward from clearing battle and defeating boss enemy therefore it encores to play a stages few more times. Mobile Suit can be equipped with part that give additional stat and passive effect like more boost more attack dmg etc. When player clear a stage, they gain increased exp and level up which grant them a new pilot skill when it reaches certain level, which will give player an edge to compete against a new and stronger enemy in later state of the game.In additional to player, two partners can be brought into battlefield for support. They give out passive friendship ability depending on role of the suit they're in. They also can revive player should they be shot down during combat and vice versa. Partners are unlocked throughout the same way player unlock MS, by unlocking the MS, respective and original pilot of that suit will also be unlocked. Partner is not allowed in coop session.For the first time that the selling point is in gameplay mechanic. Unlike the simple standard turn based game where you can approach at each own pace in the counterpart titles. There's quite in-depth flow in how the game is played going on, and will have largely impacted an experience the player will be going to have throughout the entire length of game should player beware of it.On very first mission, they introduce you to a game with hack/slash grunt enemy that's barely a threat to you in order to introduce a button string, hate line and basic movement, then soon after that they blow a player away with an actual boss fight right away, such as the important of keeping a boss in constant fighting to the balancer meter system that all bosses have possessed. This is core feature of the game, boss fight will be toughest thing the game will throw at player, and will be a constant pressure that challenge player skill throughout the game each with different approach and how player can deal with them. For starter the tutorial will make sure you know there're three different type or role of suit in game. All Rounder, Infighter and Sharpshooter. Each will have near completely different mechanic and each perform depending on said roles.Next, the game tutorial makes sure that a player will be aware of necessary basic combo string, bonus damage depending on action, and that creating an opening for massive damage is important, including avoid damage taken as much as possible with Perfect Sidestep, Perfect Guard and Counter. And tutorial lives to it value as every boss fight is punishing for misplay and extremely reward when perform correctly. Sometimes, a simple jump, hold guard then rapid descent can dodge quick range attack from boss altogether. While an action seems sluggish and unresponsive, there're canceling mechanic and advance maneuver that increase overall performance, DPS and largely how smooth the flow of gameplay will have become. For example by closing in melee from the front, by input the cancel attack animation after first attack, and quickly jump then boost, the suit you control will immediately fly itself toward the back of the locked on enemy and from that point you can deal bonus damage and inflict greater stagger on enemy with following combo. The shooter can shorten their delay/ recoil after using the weapon by shooting a following up different range one, this deal greater DPS and can deplete balancer meter on boss much faster, by linking into range weapon with less recoil, it allows quick evasive maneuver after. Those fanservices never really change. You can see your boi Zaku changing mag, does ironic move kick and some. Top it off with rearrange of all those ironic soundtrack, except now in action game. Ironic sound effect of white base, beam rifle and so on. The battlefield design are quite good, there's elevate point in mountain, buildings in the city, a lot of turning and corner in space fortress etc, the design choice helps making map feel less repetitive. The downside is that there's no actual space battle, mostly when it's a space battle, you're fighting on space fortress or outskirt body of colony which played exactly like when playing on earth/gravitational environmental. I'm very much enjoying this game flow. I have always dreamed about a good action gundam game and this is definitely one of them. Mainly because it highly emphasizes the pilot skill as it always has been in SD Gundam G Generation, except now player is a pilot themselves. Fully story narration with all of them have been voiced with ironic line from respective series. It's nothing like SD Gundam Capsule Fighter Online, which was release by South Korean, gacha based, grindy and powercreep gaming experience player vs player environment which I dare say there're way more love being poured into this one than that gacha game. If you wish it to be that kind of game, this game will be near exact opposite of what you expect.The downside is there's no real space battle and lack of a many ironic suits but if this is their goal with a game, I will welcome more sequel or DLC additional of more suit, more stages and so on.

_childDocuments_.review: As the other comments stated, game is extremely grindy. There are only 4 things you can change in the game, (1)your gundam, (2)runes that give the unit extra stats, (3)pilot skills, (4)AI teammates' gundams.(1)Each unit has only 4 stats which u can upgrade, some are practically useless to some unit (melee for range focused unit, vice versa). At the current point of my game 1 mission yields about 2000 to 3000g, while upgrading a single point of stat (like +10 melee, not even a level) after 1st limit break cost 2000g+. The grind part makes it so you will have to replay missions, Missions plays out the same every time, same spawn, same enemies, same map. If upgrade isn't this costly I might have the tiny bits of fun replaying using different upgraded units but nope.It is hilarious to see so many reviews saying that you just have to pick a favourite unit then only upgrades and plays it. What's the point of having so many units if you can only play one.(2)The runes gives like +stats and some effects, for example +70hp and dash cost 2% less boost meter.(3)Pilot skills are passives that gives u minimum effects that are unnoticeable and I do not feel it has impacted my game at the slightest (Combo time increase, dash cost less). Also, 15 pilot levels lets u equip 1, max 3.(4)If you play with friends (which you should), you do not get to have AI Teammates. If you play alone, AI teammates are pacifist. They don't seem to do much except for trying their best to revive you when u are down, even when there are enemies that are knocking them down and disrupting the process constantly.The game was designed to make you have to replay it but also made it extremely unfun to do so.

_childDocuments_.review: SD Gundam Battle Alliance" is a challenging and intense action game that is reminiscent of the "Dark Souls" franchise, but with an even greater level of difficulty. The game, which is a SD Gundam version of Dark Souls, features a deep and complex action mechanism that requires precise timing and skill to master. Despite its casual appearance, the game is anything but easy, with a challenging I-frame system and fast-paced boss attack patterns. The game also includes a cancel system, similar to those found in fighting games, which allows players to increase their damage output and create new combo possibilities.The game offers players the option to play with two AI partners, which can make the gameplay slightly easier. Additionally, players can grind and level up their MS to progress more smoothly through the game, although it will still be challenging even with a fully leveled MS. However, playing solo on hard mode provides a truly challenging and intense experience for players who enjoy this type of gameplay.The game can be played with a controller on PC, but some players have criticized the lock-on system. However, this can be overcome by manually moving the camera, similar to the older Dark Souls series or the old Armored Core series.It is worth noting that some knowledge about the Gundam series is required to fully understand and enjoy the game. Some of the missions in the game are based on non-UC related series, such as Seed, and players who are not familiar with the series may have difficulty understanding these missions. However, even players who are not familiar with the series can still enjoy the game and its intense action and deep mechanics. Overall, I highly recommend this game to fans of intense and challenging action games.

_childDocuments_.review: A generic Hack and Slash Episodic JRPG wrapped in a SD Gundam Skin...What it does well as telling of the Gundam narrative through  "Distorted" Events that bring other series of Gundam into the timeline that that pilot or model did not take part in... The storyline takes a bit to pan out... after say chapter 2 it starts to make sense as a typical JRPG all the features get explained over the first few chapters and there are a ton of quests and missions...There are a lot of Gundams that are playable from all the series listed on the page and in the guides. With the highlight being on the everyday mass produced soldier units like the Zako 2 and Commando units... Literally the 1st chapter is about how powerful the Zako 2 is... Gundams are unlocked through a system of random dropped blueprints across the chapters which seems to be pretty low... Alot of the combat is around basic light and heavy attacks and dancing around your units abilities. Seems to be based around gamepad/ controller usage. Overall it is a nostalgic trip down the Gundam Anime Storyline wrapped in convolution of systems, loot and upgrades that make no massive difference except to make it a grind. Missing customization and personalizing beyond picking your commands name. So who is this game for: Those who like a simple game with no real controls or combos, Gundam Anime and have a desire to take part in the critical moments of the multitude of the anime. Those who like a JRPG Hack and Slash...Those who dont mind a grind for limited customization for the sake of enjoying a large Anime IP.Personally, this is not a game I would pay the asking price for simply for its lack of features. Not for the lack of time investment as it is a JRPG so i expect there is well over 60 hours of gameplay in it and even more post the main campaign.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not an ARPG. Please do not go into this thinking it's an ARPG. This is a beat em up. You will enjoy this game A LOT MORE if you realize that *it is not an ARPG it is a beat em up*. Also, I'm sorry to say, but the bigger of a gundam anime fan that you are, the less you will like this game. Yes, all your favorite characters, and least favorite, are here. Their mobile suits are here. However, the various mobile suits are not balanced how they would or should be in comparison to each other. More importantly, you might be a little miffed that your favorite gundam is put into a "class" that you don't want to play which means it's stat array and scaling are pushed into a certain direction. This is a good game for beat em ups. This is an okay game for gundam fans. This is a bad game for ARPG fans. You will find zero role playing here. The "loot grind" is not your typical loot grind for ARPGs.

_childDocuments_.review: Giving this a thumbs up only because I'm a die hard Gundam fan and it has been a huge part in my childhood.SD Gundam Battle Alliance, been eyeing this since the moment it was announced, didn't get to play the demo as I do not own any of the consoles other than PC, looks like review is pretty good for the demo, but that's just for the demo. Holding off pre-ordering it as Cyberpunk 2077 has given me a good lesson not to pre-order any games before release. And now that its out, is it really good? I would say it is a tough one to decide, but let's start with the good ones The Good:- Graphic is awesome, by far the best I have seen in a Gundam game, models are detailed, environment is good, everything is just nice to look at- Cutscenes is really well done and sweet to look at, a lot of iconic scenes in the Gundam series is really well enacted, gives me a good nostalgia.- Story is good and well explained, even if you didn't watch a particular Gundam the game does a good job of summarizing key moments in the story without dragging too much nonsense, so newcomer won't feel lost in the story.- Gameplay for each MS is unique, MS in the game can be classified into 3 classes: Fighter, Shapshooter and All Rounder. Class name pretty much tells you what this MS is good at, each MS has their own unique skills and moves and no copy paste, devs really put a lot of effort into this.- Voice acting and BGM in this game is really well done, lot of their originals VAs reprise their roles in this game, the classic BGMs is also recomposed to fit modern audience without losing their originality.And now to the Bad:- Controls, by far the most complain I have seen so far. This game clearly was meant to play by gamepad/controller, controls in KB&M feels weird and out of place to me, and not to mention the game auto locks on for you makes it even weird. For those thinking this will be a shoot em up game you will end up disappointing, to me this is more like Soulslike.- The Grind, another frequent complain in the community. For those who have played games like Monster Hunter will feel at home. To unlock a MS you simply need to clear the respective missions to collect its blueprint, sometimes you will need to collect up to 5 blueprints for it to unlock and upon unlocking it you will need to spent credits to level up, and not to mention all new unlocks starts with level 1, this is where the grind fest starts.- Difficulty, the game starts off fairly easy but gets harder as you progress and the level requirement is increased for each mission, and even if you match the level requirement you will still have a hard time fighting bosses and MAs, want to get better? start grinding- Immersions, I've seen people complaining why there's no english dub for the game, after playing the game myself I begin to understand why, don't get me wrong I am more of a sub than a dub guy, but with how constantly the characters are talking to each other in the game and with all the actions going on you barely had the time to read the subtitles unless your understanding of Japanese language is good, at this rate I will honestly ask for a English dub just so I don't feel lost with whats going on for the story, the dialogues will just randomly cut off the moment you reached certain stages, leaving a huge huh? - Unit variety, compared to older SD Gundam titles unit in SDGBA feels lackluster, even know most of the iconinc units is in the game but I feel like more can be added, maybe they will be added through DLCsAbove is my thoughts of the game so far, by far the best SD Gundam I have played so far after the closure of SDGO years ago. Only get this if you are a diehard Gundam fan and have the time to grind, otherwise just get it on a sale, not worth at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: SD GUNDAM BATTLE ALLIANCE

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly a bit disappointing when compared to Artdink's previous efforts. The Artdink Gundam and Macross games were very loreful content collection games that boasted gigantic mecha lists, missions, secrets and characters. This is a fundamentally different game, and just not as good...but it is modern, and for what it is, isn't so bad. Pros: The game is slick, fast and fairly fun. There is a decent list of mecha, though no where near what I was hoping. The game balances shooting and melee fairly well, and feels Dynasty Gundam-like, except the shooting is actually effective. The parts add some customization to the game, and depending on how you feel about the combat, the missions will either be fun to grind...or a grind. Cons: There's a lot, though most of it in relation to Artdinks previous efforts and what a downgrade this is. At the same time, I don't think the downgrade warrants a thumbs down.    - The mecha list: It's too small, and considering Artdink went Chibi, it's hard to believe they got so few MS in. Sure, it's the ones everyone likes, but the joy of the older games was running around in almost anything Gundam related...Even a Psycho Gundam, Elmeth or Ga-Zowmn (WTF is that?!). They would have been better off going with the design efforts of their previous games (with better controls) then some of the decisions they made. GBO2 has models of almost the entire Gundam franchise, even those with obscurity, I think Bandai should share those resources among their game teams. Capsule fighter, that influenced this as well, had more mecha too.   - Multiplayer: I think this was a bad idea. I know everyone bugs about it, but it's responsible for the some of the game's more ridiculous attributes. There's no pause...because the game was originally conceived as a matchmaking multiplayer only game. The pvp'ers, coops, etc are all unsatisfied, and all it did was create bad reviews. It should have been focused on single player, and effort/money into expanding the content.    - "Roles" and other assorted MMO/RPG Bullcrap: I hate this in GBO even. It makes more sense there than here, but I'd like the whole thing rolled up into a ball and thrown away. It's stupid that a Dom Giant Bazooka does little damage because it's a melee role suit. It's an ok effort that should have been much better. The upcoming DLC doesn't seem to offer much (2-3 mechs per release means they are not going to fill the roster, I've never seen Bandai support a retail release long term...though the free GBO2 has been), and Artdink, which has made the "content" games for Gundam in the past has made an SD game with a limited SD roster compared to G Generation. It can't help but be a disappointment to a hardcore Gundam game fan, though I think casual Gundam fans will get something out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: The animations although flashy take little to no consideration to the character models, this may look fun in a 1v1 but in a group fight, which happen more often than not, it becomes an epileptic's worst nightmare exaserbated by the terrible lock-on system. You will find yourself in instances firing or slashing blindly at the wrong target and won't even know it.SPA attacks animations take around 2 second to deploy so your target will be in the next zip code by the time you get back to the game.The AI in single player is brought to you by any game developed circa 2001, it is incredibly daft, in normal missions you may miss out the technological marvel of reverting back time due to the flashy attacks, but wait for a boss fight, if you're downed, the game will pick one of your companions and designate it as the "reviver" and the other the "spectator". Best of lucks getting that revive.Oh by the way, there is no pause button. Yeah, not even in single player. Let that sink in! a game with instanced missions, missions with timers, and a visual novel for a plot driver does not have a pause button.If you have 2 buddies you can push through the myriads of flaws in the game, if you are a Gundam fan you too could brush off some of the flaws in the name of fandom; However, I in good conscience cannot recommend this game in its current state, much less with the price tag of a triple A game. If this was $29.99 I'd tell you to go bananas and wager wether this game would be finished or collect digital dust in your library steam style, but for $60?! ($85 for the delixe edition) nope. PS. The tutorial phase takes more than 2 hours. I will play this game in an attempt to justify my purchase.

The constant automatic switching of targets is just beyond frustrating. It's so bad you might as close your eyes and button mash your controller or keyboard. You'd probably do better at this game by button mashing like a 5 year old.

_childDocuments_.review: Mechanically this game is a lot deeper than a lot of people are giving this game credit for. It's quite fun and varied in terms of what the suits can do in terms of combos. Yes, the melee attacks consist of two buttons and it seems simplistic on the surface but, like a fighting game, those buttons and combinations of them do wildly different things depending on the suit you're using. Boss fights are fun and will challenge you to play them strategically instead of just mashing into them, some requiring different lineups than your usual sortie. The levels can get a bit grindy but since the missions are over in about 5 minutes nothing has felt bad to go through multiple times thus far. If you're unlocking suits and selling off junk parts leveling suits really hasn't been a pain to me, either. Been having a lot of fun with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say about this game?Simple answer: I like it, I like it alot. It's enjoyable with a new formula with the Gundam Franchise. I see the future potential where if Bandai decides NOT to can this attempt. And I mean it.Long Answer: A lot of potential, Bandai should have had more confidence in the development of this game.I say this mainly because I mainly have experience in some of the Japan Only Gundam games back during the PS2 era. It's got a hack and slash feel that has areas where you can cancel your moves to make it more 'awesome or cool'.Simplistic style Devil May Cry gameplay, think DMC 1, not the later installments.Missions have about a time limit of 30 minutes so they're fairly short and can play quickly.Somewhat Grindy but you can increase gains long as you play the harder missions, Higher missions give more rewards.Minimal Upgrade system: Think 'spend points to increase stats'.Interesting and fun Pilot Interactions. Setsuna F Seiei and Kira Yamato has an interesting hypocritical condemnation intro at the beginning. And EZ8 + Gouf has a 'Impress the Father-in-Law' interaction for example. lmao.My Issues are more along the lines of believing this as it could have been more. Make the combat system more intricate, increase the ammunition count and give every MS more subweapon options. Use every button on the controller if you use a controller.... etc.My Basis of this is Another Century Episode. It's a JP only game but every MS/Mech has what..... 15 weapons all tried to button combinations on your controller. Increase Boosting, Workable flight mechanics, huge battles between ships, fortresses and more mechs. Attack combos that really makes you think you're in a Wacky Woohoo Pizza man Mobile Suit. And this was in the PS2 era!Every MS in this game canonically has minimum loadout of 8 weapons, and that's outside iconic attack animations in the shows. The game has RB and LB tied to subweapons. ACE has those tied to AXYB with Triggers, which gave every MS a WHOPPING 18 weapon specific animations!Did the Devs not have the confidence to make this game a standout? One can only hope this has enough attention and sales to warrant Bandai to make an actual game of this type to hit a homerun.Aesthetically, SD style isn't my tea, but I'll take it. There's no Character Customization aside from giving them a name and they're locked to a male voiceline (You can hear some of the combat screams). _childDocuments_.review: SD Gundam Action RPG with plenty of Mobile Suits to level up and equip items to enhance their abilities. The MC can also equip items that offer various features like less boost gage consumption or quicker repairs. The combat is deceptively simple and you can pull off some nice long combos once you learn the mechanics. Short replayable stages that change depending on the mission type. Some going to different areas. For example a Break mission will have you fighting inside the asteroid base A Baoa Qu. And when you revisit during a True mission you fight Big Zam on top of it. These stages are basically retellings of key moments during the various series but the characters are out of place. You get a what if story of what would happen if Amuro wasn't there to defend White Base and fight Ramba Ral? Or if Bernie didn't get hamburger.Somehow your favorite Mobile Suit is always missing. Some of the grunt types are just AI enemies. But you can of course pilot the famous GM, Guntank, and Guncannon. The Mobile Suits you unlock can also be used as AI partners with their series protagonist piloting. Even if you use that Mobile Suit yourself. Sometime the AI kind of just stands there. But they are good for reviving you in a pinch. Speaking of reviving you can emergency revive with a repair kit but they are better used to heal than revive. The AI partners can also be revived by you or the other AI but they will not self revive. Even guest AI characters can be revived in this manner so there are ways to stay in the fight even if it looks grim.Performance is fine. Locked 60 FPS. If you use SSAA it tends to drop the framerate at times so it is better just to super sample.I didn't have high expectations for this game but I am surprised at how good it is. Everything else is on hold till I finish it.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like most of the negative reviews are from people who were expecting a different game, which isn't the game's fault.Graphics [6/10] are whatever, they're fine considering it was definitely made with Switch in mind, and since it doesn't take much horsepower it runs great on PC.  As it's a console port from Bamco I have to assume m+k controls are mediocre at best, but this is a game meant for a controller, so go get something wired for ten bucks at your local GameStop or whatever.Gameplay [7/10] isn't exactly groundbreaking, but it's got more depth than it seems to (the tutorials are short, and new ones are unlocked as you go, so make sure to play them as they pop up), and chaining together attacking, dodging, blocking, and reversals is satisfying.  I'm seeing this game compared unfavorably to the Gundam Battle games for the PSP/Vita, but it's simply a different game.  I definitely feel like the lack of pilot customization is a huge disappointment, same with the lack of visual customization for mobile suits, but the gameplay is at least a little bit deeper than it looks and it's satisfying once you get in the groove.Story [6/10] is...well it's there!  I didn't expect much and that's what I got.  It's the same "world's collided and now we gotta fix it" plot you've seen in a bunch of other Gundam/mecha games, and the tiny twist they put on the formula doesn't really change that.  I've seen some reviews say the cutscenes are unskippable but that's incorrect, you can skip cutscenes and you can skip lines of dialogue during conversation scenes, so it's extremely easy to breeze on through if you just don't care.  The English translation has a few amusing puns/references ("gouf troop" lol) so it's at least worth skimming for the sensible chuckles, but so far I haven't had anything make me overly interested in the overall plot.  Sure, sure, we're repairing history (again), just tell me what I need to shoot and/or beam saber and let's roll.  Also there are dialogue options but I don't think they actually change anything, so whatever.Music [7/10] is fine, it's yet another Gundam game that uses covers of Gundam songs, but at least it's decent, and some of the remixes are actually pretty good.  Nothing really to write home about, though, except for the fact that you can import mp3s of your own music.  Always love this feature in a Gundam game like this, though it does remind me just how annoying it is that they didn't put in character customization.Overall [7.5/10] I'd say it's better than the sum of its parts.  Watch some gameplay videos of someone who actually knows how to use the combat system (perfect blocks/dodges, reversals, that kinda stuff) and see if it looks interesting, you'll be able to tell pretty easily whether the game interests you or not.  And if you don't feel like looking for videos, use Steam's return policy!  You should be able to figure out if you're interested or not within two hours.Use a controller, play the tutorials, watch videos first or just try the thing.  This is exactly what I expected based on the initial announcement, and I think I'm gonna be enjoying it for a while.  Though if I'm honest, any game that lets me keep using a basic GM effectively against mobile suits that should wreck it gets a recommend from me!

_childDocuments_.review: SD Gundam Battle Alliance is an interesting game to review. Although I had some fun with it, I can't in all honestly say it was all rosy. SDBA has its faults. Now, the question is to determine whether those are sufficient to deter you from purchasing it.Although this game is decribed as an "Action RPG" in the store description, let's say this game is as much an action RPG as a musou/warrior game can be. I would rather describe it as an hack a slash game, with a bit of customization.Before talking about the more technical sides of the game, I would like to mention the story. After 10 hours of play, I understood that this is a game about mending different stories. Whether all of it takes place in reality or in a virtual world, I'm not sure. But the thing is, unless you're already familiar with the different gundam series present in the game, it's possible you'll feel overwhelmed because of the non linear structure of the story.There are essentialy two types of missions, Broken and True. For example, first you do a broken Gundam mission, then you do an Iron Orphan one, then a Wing one, then you're back to Gundam, but now it's a true mission. So, if you're new to Gudnam, you'll probably be lost. And the fact that characters from differents series will appear  in a broken mission make the story more chaotic for someone not familiar with Gundam. (By the way, you can't skip the visual novel sections and you can't disable the story lines while in a mission.)There are 3 types of mobile suits in SDGBA: All-rounders, Infighters and Sharpshooters. Each type has a different Role Action that you can use while playing: All-rounders will attack faster and be able to cancel moves more, Infighters will gain super-armor and Sharpshooters will refill all their ammo. When doing a mission, you're accompanied by two AI partners. Depending of the type of MS they are, they will give you some passive effects and the closer you are with the pilots, the stronger those effects are.You can customize each MS with parts that you can obtain after each mission and their effects are randomly generated. Each MS gain level and you level them up by paying, allowing you to raise their stats and to unlock more slots for new parts, to up to 4 slots max. I have to add that you, as a player, can also equip skills. But you can't equip a lot of them (3 max). And that's it for the "RPG" part of the game.To unlock a particular mobile suits will require you to obtain one or more bluprints, sometimes more than once, adn the more you progress thtough the game, the more blueprint are needed to unlock new MS. Each new MS you obtain will always be at level 1, which means you'll have to grind & pay - because you level up by using "capital", the money of the game. On the other hand, the pilot that come with it will have the same level as yours; their level determines the level of the MS they're piloting. About the pilots, you can only use them as companions and each one is tied to their own MS.A mission drops you on a map with your two partners and depending on the nature of the mission (Broken/True), you will either see a twisted version of an event or the canon one. The game plays like a hack & slash, you have normal attacks, special attacks (=strong attack), a ranged weapon and 2 sub-weapons. You can also use a SPA (Special Attack) after some time. You can dash, dodge, block, do a perfect dodge, a perfect block and do some limited combos and most of your moves use a bit of your boost gauge.All MS have the same basic combos. Depending on the MS used, you will do something between 2 or 4 normal attacks, followed by what you want next. But I guess your most useful tool there would be a launcher (by holding the special attack button), or maybe a sub weapon. There's also the Chain Breaker, a move that allows you to either push back an enemy when you're being attacked, or to refill your boost gauge, at the cost of half your skill meter.The enemies are pretty inoffensive but the bosses are an entirely different story. They have a huge pool of health and they also have super armor. When they attack, they will deplete their "balancer meter" and you can also deplete it by using a sub weapon. So, the best way to fight them is to wait for them to attack, then use a sub weapon to deplete their balancer meter. Once it's empty, they're in a broken state and lose their super armor. It's pretty simple, but unfortunately sometimes it will be hard or even impossible to break them because their balancer meter is too huge, their attacks doesn't empty it enough or your sub-weapons doesn't do enough damage to their balancer meter. Even when you wait for them to attack and chain 2 sub-weapons, that won't be enough to break them; and when you can't, fighting them becomes much more harder.And there are the Mobile Armors. They hit hard, are fast, move a lot, their attacks have ridiculous hit boxes, some can even hit you while moving, you can't do aerial or back damage to them, sometimes you don't have enough time to predict/react to some of their moves and they have a weak point that is pretty hard and dangerous to approach. And some of them even have a barrier to protect them against beam ranged attacks. Your AI partner will also quickly go down against them and when that happens you have pretty much lost the fight. I know you can make them vulnerable for a short amount of time but I don't know how to do it consistently; unless it's just a scripted event. Fortunately, you don't encounter them very often but as it stands now, the bosses are the worst part of the game. Alas, defeating them is how you obtain blueprints.The game is heavily criticized. I've read some of the negative reviews and I'll be honest, I agree with most of them, especially the most reasonable ones. Indeed, this game has its faults. It is grindy, the combats are simple, bosses are a chore and have too much super armor, the camera can be bad, the customization is limited and it's possible that the roster could be also limited (Wing lacks a lot of MS). It has some other flaws though, like being guard broken giving damage, or gaining nothing except money when you fail a mission, there's not enough sub weapons, ranged MS lack the tools to be as agressive as the close-range MS, you should be able to heal your partners, your partners are often useless even when over-leveled and the only useful role action might be the Sharpshooter's one. It has some good points though. I don't like the SD style but you forget it with time. I like how the different environments feel "dense" and some of them even have destructible parts, it makes the game feels more alive. I also like the fact that you can do some exploring to find some hidden chests. But, more importantly, I do find it fun.I tried to explain most of the shortcomings of SD Gundam Battle Alliance and how it works. Should I recommend it to a Gundam fan? To a non Gundam fan? Though choice... I would advise either to try the demo on console if you can or to watch some streams first, and long enough to see some boss fights. Most of the time, I had fun with SDGBA but I wouldn't give it more than a 5,5/10. In the end, it's a competent enough game but with some glaring flaws.1. Update 1 (doing Lv. 23 missions): After having played it for 29 hours, I feel like the difficulty has gone up and right now I have to retry some mission 5 or 6 times. There is a balancing issue: some bosses move very quickly and are difficult to block/dodge, some others are slower and more predictible.2. Update 2: the game was patched and some MA were nerfed and you also gain more currency now, but I don't want to play it anymore. I guess this game was a disappointment for me.

_childDocuments_.review: So first off, for those of you looking for the next SD Gundam Capsule Fighter or SD Gundam Online game, just keep on moving and stop with your review bombing because the game isn't what you expected.Now onto the actual review. So far here is what I have to say based on the time I've put in so far.The Good:-Smooth combat that is easy to learn, but a little difficult to master mainly because you have to know when to time your special abilities.-The game looks great. The environment and mobile suits are all nicely detailed, better than I thought they would be seeing this is an SD Gundam game.-Fairly decent sized roster of mobile suits to use.The Meh/Bad:-After a while it feels a bit repetitive, but that is to be expected of a hack and slash action RPG.-The game does get a bit grindy at times when trying to unlock some mobile suits for use. The same goes for upgrading your suits.-The camera can be a little frustrating in narrow spaces like canyons.I really wish I could leave a neutral thumb on the review, BUT I'll recommend the game because personally I enjoy it. If you are on the fence, turn to youtube and watch some gameplay videos or watch a stream or two on twitch before buying (You know, the research any gamer should do). But this is a really solid entry and I can't wait to play through it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is AWESOME! It is mindless fun, tons of mobile suits to pick from. Not sure why it has mixed reviews, other than that we live in an age of unhappy people that no matter what a game company does, it does not please them. If you are a Gundam fan like me, ignore the bad reviews and just buy the game, it is awesome! It is worth every single dollar. I was curious and read some of the bad reviews and most of it comes down to the player being bad at the game. The game is solid, easy controls that feel super smooth. The bosses are challenging but fair. There are so many missions, and secret mobile suits that you can unlock later in the game. I have played by myself and with a friend and every bit of it has been laughs and overall fun. I cannot wait to see what the DLC has to offer.P.S. If someone is complaining about "optimization" they are just poor and cannot afford anything more than a toaster. The game runs perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: SD GUNDAM BATTLE ALLIANCE

_childDocuments_.review: cons:- The bosses feel "spongy". Even a fully upgraded Freedom Gundam will chew on a Kämpfer for two minutes if the Kämpfer has the boss tag. I suppose they did this so all the voice lines can play? :D- As with roughly 95% of all games that have a 3rd person view: The camera at times can be "unhelpful"- The landscapes don't look amazing.- story-relevant voice lines play in Japanese with subtitles ... during combat; I personally don't mind since I understand Japanese well enough and don't have to read the subtitles, but if this does not apply to you it might be annoying.pros:- the most important aspect: To me at least the gameplay is genuinely fun and the different suits do feel and play differently. For example, when you switch over from a Musha Gundam to a Freedom Gundam you don't just switch stats and animations, but also get a different playstyle. (both suits are labeled as "allrounders" in the game.)- the story is engaging- the character portraits shown during the visual-novel-style story scenes look nice- can collect all my favorite Gundams- the mobile suits (in contrast to the surrounding landscape) look really goodBottom line: I really like this game and highly recommend it.===========================Update after 35 hours of playtime:The game still is a lot of fun!Also: On the one hand there are those people who tell you, that the combat here is braindead button mashing (mostly people who quit the game after two hours) and on the other hand there are those who tell you, that you absolutely have to "git good" and be an amazing fighting game player to survive in this game.Well: They are both wrong. The game starts super-easy, but gets much harder later on. However: You can still get through the game with average reaction times and no fighting-game-controller-skills .. maybe by switching some stages to easy mode until you level your MS a bit more.The only thing where you need to be an absolutely amazing player is, when you don't want to get kicked from the co-op lobbies of over-ambitious, super-competitive people.Apart from that: The game delivers just the right challenge for my taste and has difficulty settings that allow you to scale it to your own preferences.About my initial pros and cons:Even after 35 hours the camera isn't great especially in tight spaces. Disabling auto-lockon helps with some issues, but certainly not all. The story in the end was good enough to keep me engaged, but not amazing by any standards. The collection-aspect of unlocking and trying new suits is a lot of fun, since many suits offer genuinely different playstyles. Some people on the forums complain, that leveling up new suits is "too much of a grind", but honestly: When you reach late game you get so much capital that it's easy to level a new suit to a point, where you can try it out in interesting missions and then decide whether you want to actually invest some time on maxing it. It's most definitely NOT an "all or nothing" decision where you cannot even pilot a new thing without throwing hours of playtime at it.
_childDocuments_.name: SD GUNDAM BATTLE ALLIANCE

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to get this game because it looked fun, I'm not a mega fan of Gundam but i have seen little bits of anime & remember SD in my childhood. Some of what the negative reviews are correct, the game is kinda clunky with the auto lock-on and the PC controls are "ok". I do however own a controller, which made it a much better experience. Yes the game is a bit slow on the combos & deviates from button mashing, so setting up your attacks and learning the Gundams is handy. The tutorial tells you to use your sub attacks to dwindle their "balance" so if you just go running into a boss fight trying to melee in like samurai jack, you're going to pay for it. Stun locking a boss and getting a combo over 20 feels great. This game is an RPG, so you will be leveling each Gundam individually. If one of those Gundams catches your eye, then you will go back to the earlier stages so you dont get wiped, or you can just use your beefed up one and continue the story and use the credits to spend onto the next  Gundam you want to level. The game is not too too difficult, but if you dont gear up the Gundam you want, youll get destroyed quickly. This game is an overall blast, the music is great, you can change the battle music to however you like. You can also import your own music into the game via MP3 file. I have not played with other players yet in multiplayer, but the single player aspect is 100% for me.Hope this review helps, if you want a full on Gundam game with Bigger Mechs then this is not for you. This is just a cool Chibi version of Gundam with a DBZ XENOVERSE vibe.
_childDocuments_.name: SD GUNDAM BATTLE ALLIANCE

_childDocuments_.review: it honestly took a little to grow on me. feels like its coming from a gundam build fighters series POV for the story. 3 hours in tho and im starting to enjoy the story more. the gameplay is actually pretty well fleshed out for the type of game it is. for a gundam game on PC i think its not bad.  would definitly pay maybe like 30 or 40 usd for it though not the full price.
_childDocuments_.name: SD GUNDAM BATTLE ALLIANCE

_childDocuments_.review: i used to play SD Gundam Capsule Fighter before it went offline in the US, and seeing this was going to come out had me very excited. So far from what i've played i am very happy with the game, and im happy you can still collect and play with the mass production suits, and they can still compete with the gundams. Only disappointed with how you collect the mobile suits so far, and i'm unsure if all my favorites are in the game yet. But two of my favorites are received early game, so that makes me very optimistic. And i'm sure they'll add more playable mass produced MS later on in packs or updates.Also, the partner system is nice so far, so even if you don't have friends to currently play with, you can still partner up with your favorite characters when you unlock their mobile suits, or you can team up with generic zeon/federation soldiers piloting mass produced suits you unlock. So far the maps are kind of small, but grow as you advance. And they are decently open, allowing for exploration for resource crates. So thats a nice little aside.

_childDocuments_.review:
In SD Gundam Battle Alliance, Mobile Suits and characters from across Mobile Suit Gundam history take center stage in this all-new action RPG.

 A Battle Alliance to Correct a False World
The story takes place in G: Universe, a world where Gundam canon twists and turns in ways no one can predict. To correct this world's distorted history, the player leads a 3-unit squadron consisting of Mobile Suits and pilots from across Gundam history - a true Battle Alliance.What Awaits Beyond False History...

 Combo action with stunning visuals and dynamic animation
Indulge in a wide array of Mobile Suit weaponry to crush many foes with! Control Mobile Suits portrayed with realistic weathering that showcases them as weapons of war as they tear across the battlefield with dynamic animations.

 Strange phenomena known as Breaks are twisting legendary moments from Gundam history, and you're in charge to fix them.
Experience Gundam history's most famous scenes as you develop new Mobile Suits to add to your arsenal. Gather Capital and expansion parts to transform your favorite machine into the ultimate MS.

 Tackle missions with friends in multiplayer!
Launch into battle with 2 partners to back you up. In multiplayer, you can play through the game with up to 2 other players in a 3-person team. Enjoy this new SD Gundam action RPG solo, or with friends.

name: Kine
detailed_description: 🔥 Kine Now Available! 🔥 Please check out the game and leave a review. Our team is tiny and every review helps <3 About the Game Kine is a charming 3D puzzle game about three musical machines hoping to find their big break. Guide these dreamers through a delightful tale of love, labor, and loss as they struggle to form a band and find success on the main stage. Manipulate and maneuver each character by taking advantage of their unique abilities. Navigate a stunningly beautiful world filled with a wide variety of 3D puzzles while listening to an award-winning original soundtrack. Award-winning soundtrack! Over 120 unique puzzles! Quirky yellow robots!
