_childDocuments_.review: Looking great so far, deserves much more attention. Whats there is a very polished and atmospheric experience.I really like the enemy variety, there is quite a lot of them, all appropriately creepy. Shooting the baddies is satisfying, but sound effects could use a bit more punch.While the 50 shades of brown aesthetic might not be for everyone, it creates a heavy, oppressive feeling of dread. I love it.I live close to what was previously known as Czechoslovakia and I'm a sucker for this depticion of dystopian Soviet past. Guaranteed extra points from me for that.HROT is surprisingly interactive, with many destructible objects, switches and gibbing enemies. Good stuff, makes the levels a lot of fun to explore.Amazingly HROT is being developed by one developer. Thats very impressive given the results. Keep up the fantastic work Spytihněv.While the game is still far from finished, its definitely on the right track. If you like Quake and Dusk, then HROT is right up your alley.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This game is indescribable.When it started, I thought it was just some indie-shooter.And though I was right, it was so much more than that.The atmosphere tells the story of sorrow, pestilence, perseverance and humility, a lovingly crafted, if low poly recreation of many Czech landmarks and sights, sprinkled with culture and love.The combat is exhilerating, as to be expected of a boomer-shooter, but with a level of depth that many modern triple-A titles lack. The feeling of discovering that you can kick the Kejdovec's bombs back at them, both disarming them and setting them on fire for a slow but ammo efficient death is a feeling of discovery and joy I haven't felt since I was a child picking up my first controller.And the bossfights. Dear God the bossfights are awesome.There'S at least 1 per level and every single one has a unique design and aesthetic. My only complaint would be that they only have 1 or 2 attacks to their name, which may get tiring over the course of a bossfight, but the spectable these fights present in tandem with their quantity leads to nigh unforgettable experiences in numerous succession each chapter.I am only 28 hours into the game, having just completed episode 3, but this game has suprised, confused, shocked, and intrigued me to my very core. I will return to it again, searching for achievements and exploring the newly added bits of content, hungry for more. And I'd like to thank the developers for making this game as much as a particular friend of mine, who blessed me with its presence.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is a genuinely old school FPS with a very strong 'You Are Empty' vibe to it. Not just because of the retro looking graphics either. The gameplay is decidedly yesteryear with secret areas, numerous enemies, labyrinthian levels, and sometimes obscure pathways on maps that can lead to running around in circles until you figure out which grate you didn't break or what turn was the wrong turn in the maze of corridors,HROT's simplicity is what makes the game so engaging and enjoyable. If you really enjoyed this type of run and gun shooter from the late 90's and early 00's you'll likely find yourself wondering where the time went when you sit down to play it.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT works for me on two layers. For one, it's a lovingly crafted throwback 90's fps shooter, with fast, fluid and satisfying combat, bonus points for running on a custom engine witten in Pascal. And for two, as a proud slav living in Prague, I can't appreciate enough the attention to detail in regards to the actual locations recreated in the game, as well soviet era signs, statues, appliances, cars etc... Not to mention a lot of little interactive easter eggs.In my opinion, that attention to detail is what separates HROT from other modern "boomer shooters".Can't wait for more updates/episodes.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: So far it's only 2 episodes in its development and it just keeps getting better, the recent 2nd episode blows the 1st one out of the water in terms of pacing , fantastic creepy thick atmosphere, great level design and just variety that keeps it from becoming dull.Visually it's like an even more brown Quake 1, yeah that's possible to achieve apparently but it works to set the mood I'd say. The gameplay is not really fully Quak-y and it even has some blood/duke nukem 3d injected into its style too, it has kind of a slower pace to it though and you can't jump all that high as you usually can in most old school shoot games. Ammo is also far more scarce in this game compared to other boom shots, it at times can very much feels more like a horror game almost but it's still more into classic boom shooting old school action than spookiness, granted this recent 2nd episode def. leaned more into horror than the 1st episode and i loved it.Only thing that's lacking in Hrot are a fair share of the gun sound effects I'd say, They're fairly weak sounding and could use improvements, especially the SMG and Pistol sound effects.But yeah give it a go, if you want a more spooky old school shooter it's worth checking this out.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I don't recommend this at $20. The game is fully functional, but there is nothing particularly unique or innovative about this game. It's pretty much the same as every other modern retro-styled FPS game. The sound design is a huge disappointment and the gameplay and level design are very standard and repetitive. The monster designs are just extremely weird and this is another one of those games that thinks it's innovative by being weird, but it's not. It's the same in terms of gameplay and level design as every other Quake clone.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is a very fun game. I think it would be fair to call this a "DOOMlike", which I find exciting given how most shooters operate these days. You wake up in a Soviet Replublic (I believe Czechoslovakia) and your mission is to start killing the invaders in your country. But really your mission is to kill whatever you find and get through the level. The setting and aesthetic are both very cool, and the gameplay is on par if not better than classic DOOM games, although I'm not sure it has the same enemy variety DOOM2. I've really enjoyed my time in the game and there's not really much more to say.8/10 Best beef stroganoff recipe I could find.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT's greatest strengths are its compelling level design, it's frenetic combat, and its oddball charm and humour. Levels are meticulously crafted to nudge the player along while still providing a sense of exploration and creativity. Combat is meaty and satisfying, with a unique arsenal of weapons and a very creative spread of enemies. The game's tone and sense of humour is very eclectic and may not be to everyone's tastes, but I found its political satirization and ridiculous style extremely funny. A fantastic retro FPS that shouldn't be missed.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a huge fan of retro FPS games for quite a few years now. I'm certainly not the only one as there's been a real renaissance of these types of titles. However, I've grown tired of it due to a huge amount of Unity engine retro FPS games. So I was genuinely surprised when I picked this game up and found myself genuinely enjoying it.HROT is a retro FPS game with an engine made from scratch, as such it avoids feeling too much like other games. The shooting feels great with a solid and orthodox weapon selection. The movement is well implemented and it reminds me a lot of Unreal for the most part. The character has a very weak jump however and relatively slow movement. The levels are well made. They consistently loop around to where you need to go and are in general very easy to navigate without using the game's map system. Plus, there are a lot of well hidden secrets so far. The enemy variety starts off typical but quickly introduces some very unique enemies into its roster.Overall, even if you are tired of retro FPS games, I'd still recommend trying this one. It's quite special and it's been very good so far.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is the perfect blend of horror and dark humour in many ways. While it may not be the most original boomer shooter, it generally does what it does pretty well to the point where it really is one of the better ones currently available on Steam.  I highly recommend this to anyone that likes boomer shooters. This is especially a must have if it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Out of all the new wave of retro shooter revivals this (and DUSK) stand at the very apex above the rest. From the authentic custom engine with polygon jitter to the impeccable gunplay, this game understands and executes on what made classic shooters from the 90s so great.The level design and combat in this game is fantastic. The varied enemies are dynamic to fight and the weapons are well balanced and a joy to use. It's one of those shooters that just "feels" right to play. While only one episode out of three is playable at the moment, the game shows great promise for what's to come. There has already been an update just a few days after launch that's added two new weapons and some tweaks based on player feedback.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is a "Boomer Shooter" FPS developed by Spytihněv; developed in the vein of older FPS games like Quake and the like. Recently it came out of Early Access, I had it sitting in my library for a while (shout to Sabwones for the game!) but I wanted to wait until it fully came out to truly give it a spin.I'll start with the story since there isn't too much in the way; you're in 1986 (according to the steam page) Soviet Union (specifically the Czech Republic as multiple mentions of Prague were in the game) as you find your socialist country surrounded by invaders. You decide to go out and kill these invaders and that's kind of it that I was able to find  as well as mentions of how  Other than that, for the most part any lore is kind of spread apart, which is fine cause I was mostly focused on the gameplay and atmosphere. The Gameplay was great, more throwback shooter gameplay with secrets, boss battles, and the such. Truth be told, I don't really have much to say here that the likes of DUSK, Quake and other shooters like this haven't already done. What I can tell you are some of the more noticeable things that popped in my mind; some of the levels in the first episode when ramping up can be on the confusing side in terms of layout but the more the episodes go on the better it gets, shift is a giant kick which you can use to both kick enemies and enemy grenades back and when timed right it feels amazing. I think Episode 3 is my favorite just from how insane it really gets, from fighting Salamanders or Otters with giant guns to the ability to save adorable dogs from cages to murder attacking enemies (which was my favorite part of the game, you can indeed pet the dog in this game). Other things to mention is that driving around the motorcycle is a lot of fun running people over, and also to keep an eye on your environment because this game will surprise the hell out of you real quick with enemies (mainly static vehicles coming to life to try to run you over). The double barreled shotgun will be your best friend along with the grenade launcher; and I guess the final note I can throw down is that you can interact your environment like opening cabinets to find ammo and in some levels keys, of which like other old school first person shooters you need to open doors that leads to the end of the level. For the last stage of Episode 3,  Last thing, I tried with everything but no rocket jump that I could find, so unless I'm dumb as s h i t don't even bother to do it cause it won't work.The Atmosphere/Art Design/Everything else for the most part was solid; at first the drab tone kind of got on my nerves a bit, especially with the sewer levels in Episode 1 (titled Kiss Me Gustav) but the more I played (mostly from Episode 2 and 3), the better it got and the more variation it had in it's environments. Keep in mind, I love oppressive atmospheres, It just took a while for me to get adjusted. Graphics look like Quake and other old shooters and as a simp for old throwback games I love it, the enemy designs are great environments whilst samey looking for the most part change up later on. The only criticism I have in this part is that two of the weapons, the Pistol and Machine Gun, feel under powered like a pea shooter; while I understand the pistol is supposed to be a weak weapon you have as a backup I don't really like it as a weapon mainly due to the fact that even if it's weak that it should still pack some sort of feeling. Otherwise, honestly this section is the strongest part of the game; it has it's identity in the sea of browns and blacks and it's not afraid to really get the Soviet aesthetic down.To finish off my thoughts, if you like old school throwback shooters than I feel like most people would like HROT; it's gameplay of finding keys and opening doors, interacting with the environment in small but interesting ways, shooting your way through strange creatures, etc. I enjoyed my time playing HROT, it has a unique personality with it's own inside jokes that I don't totally understand (like getting a recipe for food at the end of each Episode? Strange but made me chuckle) but I appreciate the hell out of, it grew on me the more I played and to me was it's best at Episode 3 . Is it worth your time and money? I thought it was good enough to get my money's worth but I guess 6 hours for 20 dollars depends on what you really find to be worth the price. It's unique and it deserves it's place in the Boomer Shooter pantheon, and a must play for the h o e s like me that love retro stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is a fantastic boomer shooter that channels the spirit of classic FPS games like Quake, Doom, and Wolfenstein. Set in a small socialist country neighbouring the Soviet Union after an unspecified disaster in 1986, the game oozes nostalgia and immerses you in a unique and intriguing setting, felling nostalgic even though it's new.The enemies are great, offering challenging encounters, the level design is top-notch, providing a perfect mix of open spaces and tight corridors to keep you engaged and exploring for secrets.HROT strikes the right balance between old-school aesthetics and modern elements, making it a must-play for fans of classic shooters and newcomers alike.If you love the golden age of first-person shooters, don't miss out on HROT - it's a well-crafted retro FPS with a unique twist!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Hrot really grew on me. I came for the boom-shoot, stayed for the Czech.Every level is absolutely stuffed with references to Czech culture and history, and it's wonderful.Gameplay is totally solid and enjoyable, but nothing groundbreaking. The real highlight of the game are the levels. In spite of the depressing color palette there is a big variety of real life locations, enemies, and fun stuff to do. I highly recommend reading up even a little bit of lore on the fandom wiki, it will enrich your experience.Two thumbs up for the music, fits very well. Sound effects are good, some weapons sound anemic, enemies are often funny (Zabít!).Graphics are authentically retro, no Unity plugins here.I will definitely have to visit Czechia one day.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know much about Czechoslovakia (even though I may be part Czech) but this is Czech DUSK and is just as much fun if not more-so.It is in early access, with its first two chapters available now and a third to come out some time in the future. I hope the final chapter will come alongside some refinements, like the railings that aren't actually real, or the weird paths the enemy likes to take as they approach you.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: is as if 's first episode was an entire game, along with if S.T.A.L.K.E.R. was made in the '90s as a Quake-esque episodic shooter, all set in dystopic late '80's soviet Czechoslovakia. It is a simple yet intriguing and a brilliant FPS, with a setting, style, atmosphere and gameplay that make it well-worth many hours of playtime. Also the fact that the game has its own custom engine that is written in Pascal (!) makes this game all the more unique and in a way meta regarding the time and place its story and world are trying to convey.The progression of the episodes feel smooth and fluid, the many details throughout the levels are impressive, enjoyable, notably funny and memorable, and the game has one insane final boss fight that no other boomer shooter could match and it will drop your jaw - for one reason or another.The final release is amazing and HROT is a gem.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is yet another in the seemingly endless line of modern retro FPS games. Made by a single developer it takes you on a monochromatic journey through Czechoslovakia where an "unspecified" disaster populated the area with hostiles, including flying Lenin heads and horses with gasmasks. And no, those are not the weirdest enemies in the game.If you've played any other game like that then you know what to expect. Neatly designed levels inspired by the classics, lots of secrets, lots of shooting and blowing things up, end-level stats and toilets. It's a little bit of Quake1 (visuals), a little bit of Dusk (combat), a little bit of Rise of the Triad (ludicrousness). Not a bad mix, if you ask me.A while ago I played Prodeus and I still maintain that in terms of combat and the overall gameplay flow it's the best modern retro shooter out there. However what Prodeus lacked was immersion. Levels comprised almost entirely of industrial facilities and caves and I didn't get a very strong sense of place there. HROT is kind of the opposite. The combat is just sort of there - it's not bad, it's not amazing. But the environments feel a lot more immersive. I don't want to say "realistic" because that's not the right word for this game. But the places you visit feel like they're actual places rather than some semi-abstract gameplay areas. The atmosphere is surprisingly strong.Of course a big part of that is the interactivity and all the random stuff you can do. I really appreciate the fact that the developer of HROT has spent time working on all those seemingly pointless little details and interactions that do not affect the gameplay at all but make the game world feel more immersive. I won't spoil them because part of the fun is discovering all those fun optional things but they're all cool and endearing. They certainly add a lot of personality to the game. And there are A LOT of them.The same goes for a number of features that are unique to certain levels. Some things only appear once in the entire game which not only makes them more interesting but also shows the developer's commitment. It takes time and effort to create something that only shows up once and not all devs would bother to do that. I mean, this game has a fully functional astronomical clock simulator that exists just because. I think that settles it.HROT is also unique amongst all the other retro shooters in that it runs on a completely custom engine. There's just something special about that fact, even if you could probably achieve the same effect using Unity or Unreal. And on that note, I want to commend the author for sticking to his guns and keeping the game's monochromatic look. I mean sure, HROT is brown. All brown all day every day. But that's fine. It's fine to sometimes have a game with a very limited color palette.So what's bad about this game? Well, there are some things to nitpick. Most people probably agree that the sounds, especially gun sounds are kind of unremarkable (to say the least). Many secrets rely on pixel hunting, like finding a wall that's literally one pixel deeper than the others. You have probably the lowest jump I've ever seen in an FPS. There's absolutely no story... and I know that this is not that important in a retro shooter but even Quake had a background story. It'd be nice to have some sort of context other than "something happened, kill the bad guys". I mean, the game gives you recipes at the end of each episode, instead of anything related to the game, come on. It's kinda funny... but still. The higher difficulty levels feel rather unbalanced. They're playable but not very fun.However I have very much enjoyed my time with HROT. It's endearing, clunky, campy and silly while maintaining the depressing atmosphere. Very much a labour of love and that alone makes it worth playing. If you don't mind the monochromatic look and can forgive the weak sound design, that is.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing special, just one of the best "boomer-shooters" of the recent years. On the surface it has great level design with quick and intense gameplay, but below it is so much more. There's loads of enemies and mechanics in the game, it breaks up the simple quake-like gameplay loop constantly with totally unexpected things. It's somewhat scary, but it is much much grotesquely funnier than that. Pummel Horse miniboss? Sure. Boulder that chases you up the stairs? Its just genius. I don't want to give off to much spoilers, this game is very funny, discover it for yourself.Visually its also very distinct, all the levels are very unique, each with its own visual quirks or details. As someone who grew up in Hungary the little details are everything in this game, whether the little cloth on the television, the exact washing machine my grandmother had, or just generally the vibe of a gym. Great stuff all around, I don't think you'll ever find a retro-style fps as unique as this ever again.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: PLAY IT. Excellent mechanics. Unexpectedly heartfelt and raw representation of life under communism. The music is dope. The pewpew is rewarding as hell. The weapons feel brutal enough. Give this guy your money now. Dev is an ultrachad too, fantastic message with the ending overall. ČESKÁ STRONK. Also thank you for the little frendos, both because they are adorable and helpful and also because they probably pissed off a bunch of edgy 13 year olds from the steam discussion forum and that's priceless to me.Can't wait for the next boomer shooter from you.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: In terms of gameplay, it is like Quake but set in Czechoslovakia and you're under influence of mushrooms and alcohol. Very solid retro-style shooter with good gunplay and decent level variety. Full playthrough should take around 3-4h, add extra hour or two to that if you are checking every corner for secrets and Easter eggs of which there are many.Strong recommendation if you like "boomer-shooters" and don't mind very brown colour palette, this game is absolutely worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Hrot's setting is grounded heavily in socialism era Czechoslovakia. The campaigns are tours of real-world places around Czechia during around 80's. It even makes sense geographically, the way they lead into each other. The castle levels, for instance, are various famous Czech castles. The wagon boss-fight is a callback to Hussite war wagons from the 14th century who resided in the location that level takes place in. The horse legs you fight at the gym are a gymnastics prop you leap over or onto during PE to this day. Bumper cars, carnival rides with swan seats and a random gorilla in the middle, gas mask drills to prepare for American nuclear attacks, the random socialist slogans, the crappy mass produced furniture, milk sold in plastic bags, etc. Every inch of this world is oozing with callbacks to things the previous generation grew up surrounded by.One more cool bit. Apparently the name Hrot means "Spike" in Czech, but it can also be used figuratively as "escalating a situation" or "picking a fight" something akin to "having a bone to pick with someone". I thought that was really neat.★★★★☆ 4/5
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: While people call it "Czechsolvakian Quake", it is more akin to Chasm: The Rift. Which is in no way diminishing it - the level of interactivity and finely crafted environments is more than welcome. The brownish palette and the overall aesthetics might not be appealing at first but they very much reflect the brown-gray days of 1980s communist era in Central Europe. Once you're immersed into the game, you start seeing it more like a treat rather than a disadvantage Plus the game itself provides a heafty challenge for anyone willing to go beyond Normal difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: In almost every map I thought "there could be more to explore instead of a few tunnels": train tracks to follow somewhere, see something new, a forest to enter, traverse a mountain, maybe a space station, some open spaces between the cities. Instead throughout the game you only get really densely packed maps around historical buildings.The reason for these historical buildings to exist is only there immediate reference. The 'build engine' games always made sure  to tell a story just by the different landscapes you'd traverse, a story of going somewhere, of getting deeper into the chaos or further away from it.Together with a lackluster third expisode and a meme endboss, the experience is over the line into the boring silly where it could be more immersive.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: You'll either love this game, or you'll hate it.Hrot is a love letter to original Quake, but with some of the rougher edges smoothed out and replaced with some Quake II and Duke Nukem 3D style.     It must be remembered that Quakes 1 and 2 were *all over the place* thematically.  They didn't bother you with tonnes of exposition, or cut scenes. They didn't have long procedurally-generated open-world areas. They were tight, focussed action, with an emphasis on keeping the player moving.So, if you like your graphics spangly, and your levels looking like they were rendered on a Cray supercomputer, Hrot isn't for you.  If you want to have lots of high-paced fun in the original Quake style (yes, including the brown-ness), then play this game.  It's not incredibly long, but even on 'normal', it's quite a challenge. You're a little more vulnerable through most of the game than you are in Quake.    Sprinkled throughout the game are loads of funny references to Czech TV shows, little historical events, personalities, authors. There's also amusing setups, and recipes keep popping up.   It's definitely the work of a fevered imagination.  I loved it, but then, I'm an OG Quake fan :)
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic retro FPS! It is all so stylistic and atmospheric! I love the dystopian setting with the communist Russian overtones. The graphics and the gameplay are so reminiscent of those games we played all through the 90's. The creatures and the enemies have this wondrous mystery and creep factor that only add to the experience. The fact that all of the prospective "humans" are in gasmasks really gives that unsettling quality that only adds to everything. Is this game perfect? Well, no. The biggest problem I have with this game is the boss battles and mini-bosses. They are either underwhelming or just boss minion battles. Their character designs are just not especially creative or inspired. The best one out of the bunch needs to be the horse with the gasmask. But only because he is a horse with a gasmask. Other than that, the levels are beautifully designed and smartly arranged where it keeps you wanting for ammo and health. They only reward you when you use your assets wisely. As rare as health items are, they are not impossible to obtain. It was also nice that they added the wine to the mix when you needed it most. I just wish they would have made the whole "getting drunk" part more of an obstacle than a gimmick. The weapons are possibly one of the best parts of the game. As mundane as they might appear, they are fitting of the time period and are great callback to Doom weapons. They even brought in the Quake lightning gun! It's rare to find, but wow, it is so much fun to use! This game is a standout in its field, and I can't wait for them to release the third episode! The first two were a lot of fun, despite a few of the more frustrating parts. If this gets a sequel, I will be first in line to snatch it up. Until then, though, give this game a try!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: As a game it can only be recommended to someone who is addicted to the genre or has not played a shooter recently (or has never played one at all). It is very purist in its approach to core mechanics - they are made up of shooting and searching the walls for secrets. There is a dedicated kick button for returning a grenade to sender or redirecting it towards some other unfortunate recipient; there is also jumping, but it is not possible to crouch - not that it is needed. Enemies are chunky and sometimes spawn out of thin air, but they do not track the player or compensate for a moving target, so continuous strafing keeps one relatively safe. The weapons include the electric gun that can do chain damage to up to three targets if they are close to each other, and a healing wine bottle that doubles as a molotov, but the rest of the guns are tried-and-true staples of the genre. Enemy design is decent; some enemies may look pretty amusing, but they do not really have any defining characteristics to remember them by - other than appearance, the gun they use, and the amount of shots they can tank before going down (I believe there are no headshots here). Enemy "tactics" are fairly simplistic - they do make the player strafe, but at least they do not just charge to overwhelm with their beefy health pools.As a joke it can be a source of some silly fun, as it does have quite a few details which may remind the target demographic of their childhoods, and some levels build up quite an atmosphere. However, the amount of detail varies from level to level (some of them may feel pretty empty), and there is no story to speak of, only a common "brown, socialist theme". The game's description appears pretty honest and contains examples of the game's distinctive brand of humour - consider looking through it before making your decision.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10If you're simply looking for another good Quake-like boomer shooter, HROT is for you. Complete with Slav influences.+ Good atmosphere.+ Good level design.+ Great replay value.+ Good enemy variety.+ Good weapon variety.- Weapons lack impact.- Certain enemies lead their shots too well.- The visuals are too brown. Before you tell me that Quake was too brown as well, just take a look at several screenshots of Quake and HROT and you'll agree that the latter is actually too brown.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: id give hrot roughly a 7.5/10 from what ive played so far (edit: ive now completed the game up to the end of the second episode which is all that is available at this time) . its still a very fun retro shooter with some unique enemies and a very moody atmosphere that rides the line nicely between all out action and tension. There is also a decent amount of tongue in cheek humor that helps offset the complete lack of narrative (the plot is even more sparse then doom or quake for reference) my biggest complaint and what i think holds it back the most is its overly strict adherence to retro fps dogma. i think it could benefit from distinguishing itself a little more from the likes of quake or dusk. nothing wrong with sticking to a formula that works but i think especially in the weapons department its a bit bland. overall however id recommend picking it up if you enjoy retro shooters, especially if its ever on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Discover interactive vodka and Russian nesting dolls all within the first five minutes while skulling down cans of blood and fat to keep you in the fight. The moodiest of the retro shooter revival and the only title, outside of Ion Fury, of course, to feel, look and play like a long lost 90's gem that Action Forms might've put out. Essential!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Comparisons with Quake, with which HROT’s user reviews apparently abound, are somewhat unfortunate. Outside its surface level visual similarities, or some of its weapons or enemies that evoke their analogues from Quake, this is a somewhat different sort of FPS. One certainly won’t find Quake’s movement or verticality here. Rather, HROT is closer to Chasm: The Rift if latter offered more variations in height within maps. Take away Chasm’s dismemberments and sprinkle the maps with some cute Buildesque interactivity, and you’ll have some image of what HROT is as a game. And as the sort of FPS it is trying to be, it is very good indeed: weapons are satisfying in their functionality and visual feedback (audio leaves something to be desired but this is something the dev is actively working on improving), and most of them play useful roles rather than being gimmicks or feeling obsolete after one finds shinier piece latter on. Enemies are varied in their looks and behaviour, and none of them are bullet-spongey. Maps are well designed, with character, with semi Build-style realistic-locales as opposed to Quake’s abstractions.All this is set in this gray concrete nightmare, the world of Soviet brutalist tenements and industrial spaces, of smoke-covered skies, of deformed life. The world wherefrom everything natural and beautiful is exiled. Such environment is violence on its own so that explosions of orgiastic violence of which game such as this consists can feel only fitting.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: It's good, like really good. The only reason people stopped playing shooters like this after the 90s is because people stopped making them. I for one am glad they're coming back. HROT has nailed every bit of 90s shooter aesthetic and the custom engine handles it so well. The lighting, textures and sound design are a particular treat. The soundtrack is a great mix of 80s synth/early industrial and really fits well. The enemies are varied and the models are period appropriate and look awesome. The boss battles are on the easy side but the bosses themselves are crazy and often hilarious. If you've played any game inspired by Romero then the weapons will seem familiar and comfortable with no one gun ever truly replacing another, just fitting the situation better.Only episode 1 is available right now with more on the way, it feels like the shareware version before ordering the diskette in the mail. It still has replay-ability in this state though, lots of secrets to find in the levels and an endless wave mode to round it out. The asking price could seem steep for 2-3 hours of current content but I was happy to help get this game realized. I can't wait for episode 2.Edit: Just a reminder that you can nomiate Hrot for categories during The Steam Awards.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome retro shooter!First chapter is really cool and cant wait for the rest to come.If you like games like Dusk or any type of retro shooters, you will absolutely love this as well.Only thing i didnt enjoy were a couple of balancing issues, especially with ammo. I kept running out of ammo several times and  healing items are really rare. (Played only on hard mode)But the game just came out on early access, so im sure these kind of issues will be fixed.cant wait for more!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished this game couple of minutes ago and I gotta say...HOLY S**T THIS GAME WAS F*****G AWSOME ! I've had so much fun playing this game and it was a pleasure to play this game. The sound was pretty good, the models were pretty good, the maps were pretty good, everything about this game was awsome.Is it worth buying it? Yes its abso-f*****g-lutely worth buying it.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I'd say it's a 7/10. It's enjoyable for fans of old school FPS games, but doesn't offer much. The action and guns are ok. The music design is great; all except for the sound effects for the weapons. Almost all the guns have no oomph or bass to the sound, so they all sound like pea shooters and it really detracts from the experience. It's one of those things where you're so used to things sounding good in other games that when it's missing you really notice it. Something else that's odd to me is that this game seems a bit confused about it's identity. It has a really creepy vibe and sound to it, there are even jump scares, but there's also a lot of weird comedy that seems out of place to me. I dunno maybe it's just me. In particular that final level just had me scratching my head. It's also very short, I finished it in about 7 hours.Overall I'd recommend this game on a sale; maybe I just don't get the hype but if you're looking for an old school shooter and haven't played Dusk, Amid Evil, or Ion Fury yet then I'd recommend those over this.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Hrot is a very charming and memorable game, with many entertaining references and easter eggs. The bleak aesthetic is very striking, but at times too bleak - it can be hard to spot essential switches in such a muted grey and brown environment. This is a fairly minor issue in most levels, but did bother me more than once. Overall, I enjoyed my time with this game, but considering how short the campaign is, I would recommend to get it on sale - a complete playthrough will take about 7 hours, 8 at an absolute maximum.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: The level design is exceptional; distinct, complex, but intuitive and easy to traverse. The weapons are varied and all have great feedback to them.The enemies and bosses are extremely unique and mechanically different, and the aesthetic and atmosphere while bleak, gets balanced by the game’s humour present in references andinteractable environments throughout the levels.It’s fairly short, but it is highly repayable thanks to how rewarding the core gameplay loop is, the game has multiple secrets, including levels, as well as a multitude of difficulty settings that are all well balanced, easy is easy, hard is hard, etc.Definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: At times it feels like "You are empty" if it was de-made in the quake enginebutIts just so much more than any of thattreading a fine line between bleak skav flavored horror and a weird satire of the tail end of Soviet rule and influencefun, grimy ugly and beautiful.solid retro gameplay creepy music and creepier enemiesalso there is an option to turn spiders off they are that creepy.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Its a very well made retro fps shooter with great movement,weapons and new ideas that makes this fps stand out a little.Its challenging on the hardest difficulty and the secrets are really well made. Some secrets are really visible and makes newbies to this retro fps genre a little bit more welcoming than other titles
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Atmospheric, fast-paced FPS heavily inspired by Chasm: The Rift and Quake, set in an alternate 1980s soviet-controlled Czechoslovakia. Challenging gameplay is the name of the game, but eeriness and uneasy feelings add much needed immersion. If you are even remotely interested in old school shooters, check it out.Pros:- Awesome level design;- Good controls;- Great optimization;- Pixelated retro aesthetic;- Interactive environments;- A lots of options;- Varied enemies;- Great soundtrack;- Good arsenal;- Fun gunplay;- Humorous elements;Cons:- Hit-and-miss sound design;- Lots of monster closets;- Some enemies are too tanky;
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Synchronicity: Today, on 24-JUN-2023, I finished this game,slaying the end-boss that has a striking resemblence to the PM of Russia...He is in big trouble today, and deservedly so!I found HROT to be a very fun retro game, definitely a hommage to Quake.Gameplay is fast, enemies and weapons are diverse and there are a lot op traps to get out of.The cold-war humor keeps things light.Impressive that this game was made mostly by one guy with community support.To finish it on normal difficulty, I did have to give myself a full load of weapons a few times.because I simply ran out of ammo, not knowning all secret staches.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most clear focused games to come out of the retro styled fps wave, everything feels fantastic, the world design is simultaneously beautiful and oppressive. Atmosphere is a highlight: the ambient sounds, lore, music, level design and enemy design all create a cohesive narrative of CSSR post Chernobyl Czech misery and accurately expresses a wide stretch of Czechoslovakian culture -to my knowledge-. Whether you're the type to get lost in a virtual world or just want to blow chunks out of vile creatures with a fantastically satisfying armoury, this game ~will~ be for you.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played much, but what I've played its a pretty good game. I will be playing more and uploading a video on my YouTube channel. Just to put in mine its in early access and not finished, so if you look at the description it tells you how many levels are currently in the game, so its a work in progress. Thank you devs!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I love HROT. It's great to just walk around in. I love the mystery and Soviet gloom of the first episode. The software-rendered aesthetic is just so perfect. It is beautiful just like Quake.I really enjoy the levels and their secrets. The encounters with larger groups of enemies in episode 1 are very exciting.I think it's a very special game. Thank you hrotdev.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't have much expectation for this game on seeing it from other YouTube reviewers and screen shots. But I just finished playing through the first chapter in one sitting and BOY was I wrong! This is so well crafted and the atmosphere is one I could really get into. It's so mysterious and unique.If you like 90's shooters and/or Slav culture, get this game, this has so much potential
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fascinating as a retro FPS.It has a really brown, dark and horror atmosphere with music that compliments it yet at the same time it has alot of really goofy,silly moments that you'd never expect which you'd think would pull you out of the moment but it strangely adds to the horror so much that it'll make you wanna keep playing to see what other interesting ideas it has in mind.If you love retro FPS's such as Chasm The Rift, Quake and or DUSK then this game would fit in perfectly with what you're looking for.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Beef StroganoffEdit:Absurdness of the boss fight aside, I think this game's high point is episode 2. Its very clear the creator of this game wants to play with horror effects and I'm all for it. Episode 1 is great as well. Episode 3 is fine but it kinda feels like the interesting level design gave way to arenas with absurd amounts of enemies towards the end. Regardless of episode 3's shortcomings I think this is a solid game. Easily one of the most stylistically distinct games under the boomer shooter umbrella that isn't shovelware.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing this review episode 3 is still in development.I had initially brushed this game off as yet another in a long line of by the numbers retro throwbacks to the days of Quake. In hindsight I wish I would have not judged this book by it's cover as HROT has shaped up to be one of the most enjoyable FPS experiences I have had in ages. Carefully crafted, well balanced and chocked full of secrets this game had surprised me at every turn with it's dedication to innovating it's own wheel. Though coated with drab art direction HROT makes every effort to make you see the beauty in it's browns, greys and beige walls.Episode 2 definitely takes some bold steps forward in terms of it's level design and outside of the box ideas, and I can't wait to see what more is brought to the table in Episode 3 in the coming year.I would strongly recommend this game even in this current state to both fans of the genre and newcomers wanting to dip their toes into the retro FPS sphere. 9/10 Legies
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Now I know what you're thinking... I thought the same when I first saw this game in the Store."Someone's ripped off Quake again".But this is actually a completely fresh game that has been written using a new engine (apparently in Pascal). While it is very Quake like in appearance and feel, it's actually a completely new story set in Soviet era Czechoslovakia.This game is Early Access, so you may want to wait until the completed game is developed before committing to a purchase, but if you like games like Quake, Half - Life, etc. then this is definitely worth a look.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Do note this game is not fully complete yet, this may be a deciding factor in your purchase. Only Episode 1 and half of Episode 2 are finished at the time of writing this review.Gonna be straight to the point, HROT is a game that doesn't do anything new but still is a great game. If want a game that's an enjoyable experience with great levels and classic FPS gameplay, then absolutely pick this up! If you want a game that'll reinvent the genre, you might need to look elsewhere.I don't really have any complaints to list other then I'd like to have more story, I know that sounds dumb in a classic FPS but I love the premise and atmosphere of this game, I feel like the story should be shown more weather it be through end texts or environmental means.A great game to add to a retro FPS library!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: play this game if you really want beef stroganoff.in all seriousness, the atmosphere in this shooter is so palpable despite how brown and dark everything is.strongly recommended to any fan of Quake, Blood, Dusk, Doom, whatever. excellent shooter.the first campaign (comprised of 8 levels) is very polished, intuitive level design and great enemy placement.all of the weapons feel amazing to use, especially the super shotgun (of course), the crossbow and i have particular love for the lightning gun.i've only played on normal difficulty but found it challenging but never frustrating or annoying. will have to play the harder difficulties soon. the dev is also continually adding and polishing more and more levels to play through as well for a second campaign.i bought this on sale for $15, the first campaign alone is definitely enough to justify that price tag.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay-wise, HROT is a good game that should be a blast for anyone into retro shooters. One of the most enjoyable parts of the game for me was the bleak atmosphere and mysterious setting but sad part with that is that for me it doesn't really see a satisfying payoff. There's a lot of interesting and quirky moments in HROT but it never really reaches the heights that DUSK, one of its inspirations does.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This is a narrow recommendation.  I was interested enough to play through it, though this is easily one of the more skippable Boomer shooters.  It's very drab, sometimes sparse.  It most reminds me of Dusk, Return to Castle Wolfenstein and Quake.  For a game that looks so serious and ugly, it gives you some stupid bosses at times that don't fit.  The idea is to be amusing I think, but it came off to me as ill-fitting/dumb.Levels, guns, shooting were all ..fine.   Aside from it's ugly brown colour all the time which plays a part in its lack of area variety, the other thing is that there just isn't much going for it to make it standout.  No grapple, no bullet time, no dodge, no double jump, no bright colours, nothing fancy or interesting really going on whatsoever.  It's a decent FPS, just.. far from great.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: All the weapons feel weighty and punchy and effective. I do wish the weapon sounds had a more punchy sound design but other than that, no real issues gameplay wise.I'm not sure what other old-school boomer shooters drip with this kind of atmosphere. There's some cool Eastern Bloc eldritch horror thing going on. I've heard/seen people complain about the lack of a thumping soundtrack and I think they're incredibly misguided. The game has an ambient soundtrack that suits the mood and atmosphere, I think asking for a dynamic open string Djent riffage in this game is a mistake and not at all what the game is going for.I had one, pretty major bug. The level that has the end button behind two turrets? I had zero health//zero ammo, so i dodged and weaved passed their projectiles to end the level. However, this is where it would bug to all hell. The next level starts and my character is like stuck, sunk into the raising platform. As soon as i moved or clicked my mouse it would restart me back at my last save in level before, where i had quick saved in the hall way. I had to retry ending the level... 9 times before it finally allowed me to start the next level.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: When something is amiss in a Soviet satellite state, the proper response is to go in guns blazing. The levels alone add an air of mystery and leaves a few hints as to what happened prior to you stepping in to clean up the mess, and the gunplay is solid. The difficulty? Challenging, especially since ammo, health, and armor are very rare in this game unless you start looking for secrets or just go in hacking enemies' limbs off with a sickle. Plus a few hints here and there that is guaranteed to make history nuts chuckle. Worth checking out.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Seems promising so far. I really enjoyed what there currently is of the campaign. Endless mode is enjoyable too, but everything seems a little barebones given the early access state of course.Some things I'm a little turned off by- Some of the guns feel boring and week. I found myself mainly using the pump-shotgun the entire game because it seems to be the best weapon for good damage and the ammo is everywhere.- Boss fights are pretty dull. They all followed the same pattern of chase, jump around, and shoot at you. - Enemies are very same-y feeling too. There's very little telegraphing from enemy attacks which makes it pretty hard to dodge attacks.- I often found myself low on health in most missions, which wasn't really a problem, but there's a constant heartbeat sound that plays and gets very annoying.I overall really enjoyed the experience, despite how short it was. I wish it was a little cheaper, but as long as more content is planned then I should hopefully change my mind about that bit.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I kinda love it? The atmosphere is easily the best part, each level had me on edge and nervous throughout. The level design in particular feels great, maps have a nice flow and shortcuts open periodically. I would recommend playing on normal for a first run. The game isn't hard per say, but you will be running low on ammo. I'd almost call it survival horror if the emphasis wasn't on the action. Anyway, buy it, play it, and check back in for the upcoming episodes and updates.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: The aesthetic and level  design is amazing, but matched by Dusk's - the only thing that's superior about Hrot is its Soviet aesthetic (I love said aesthetic), which is subjective anyway. However, the game-play is so shallow it actually takes away from the aesthetics and level design.This game is certainly over-hyped, and overpriced considering how poor the game-play is.Maybe that's just me and my game-play oriented brain?
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Low playtime for the review I know, but I played the Demo to death! HROT's fun to play, has really unique atmosphere to keep the player on edge, and delivers some really surreal vibes. This is an indie FPS worthy of spotlighting and supporting. If you like Quake, Dusk, and Soviet-era spookstuff, this is the shooter for you!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: It's a super fast, super satisfying Quake-like FPS with a really unique look. It's incredibly grim, even scary at times, but also the funniest game I have ever played. Hrot trolls you, tricks you, and plays with your expectations in a way that had me hooting at my desk. Also, it's only getting better. The first act was great, got me hooked on the game, but episode 2 was almost entirely dingers, memorable, knockout levels that really stick with you.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: No-nonsense FPS with an incredibly atmospheric art style. Enemies, weapons, environments, and especially lighting are spot on and set a perfect tone. Looking forward to the additional campaigns. Also I really appreciate the ability to adjust the position/scale of your weapon on-screen.So far really enjoying projects released by this Dev, this and LEGIE are easily in the Pandemic top 10.My one request; give us an open level centred around using the motorbike, its too cool to stay a sideline gimmick!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most fun I've had of the recent batch of retro shooters that have been coming out lately. Even though Dusk and the like were excellent, there's just something very satisfying about the game that's hard to put my finger on. The idea alone is brilliant. A late Soviet-era Quake with gasmasked horses and cybernetic Lenin heads as enemies, set against a menacing backdrop of unspecified disaster which seems to have zombified the populace and left a swirling black void in the heavens. It sounds dumb, but it holds together very well, and while the primary mood is one of horror the little touches of humour are really well-integrated and constantly surprising.Of course a game like this lives or dies on its gameplay, and in this regard it doesn't disappoint. The map design is particularly excellent, focusing on tight maze-like environments that double back on themselves at key points to avoid backtracking or aimless wandering. Music is also very highly polished and fits the atmosphere perfectly, transitioning from creepy background synths that set a unsettling mood to more driving pieces that get the blood pumping whenever certain key moments are triggered. Weapons generally feel tight and and enemies and environments are varied enough that you'll find yourself adapting your tactics on the fly. Things aren't perfect in this regard (shotgun ammo is a little too plentiful right now, and a couple of the enemies need tweaking to make them more of a challenge) but hopefully these things will be improved in the final version. At higher difficulties the game can feel challenging but thanks to a lack of hitscan enemies it never feels cheap or unfair. I have no idea what the final two episodes will be like, but if they continue to develop in this vein while developing the nightmarish atmosphere so effectively built up in this first episode we're going to be in for a treat.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: 5/10 The positives :- the atmosphere is good- enemy variety is good- neat niche features- lots of unexpected behavior from the enemiesThe Cons :- Dogs are enemies- only 2 of the weapons are actually useful in combat- the pitiful jump- enemy teleports are nearly silent and hard to hear- enemies hit a bit too hard (I played on normal) - health is scarce and barely heals anything- too many secrets that are hard to find (I know they're called secrets but they're hidden too well in my opinion)- I feel like there was more work put into the niche features (the functioning clock, the game and watch mini-game, the soccer field, etc) rather than the feel of the gameplay- levels feel like labyrinths and are a bit large for this kind of game- armor feels like it does nothing or at the very least barely anythingIn conclusion this isn't really a bad game. I just don't find it to be my cup of tea and wouldn't recommend it outright. Also a lot of the ideas this game has are fine. I personally think they were done better in other games.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really good shooter, possessing thick atmosphere and a surreal vibe. A game that combines low poly 3D models with a strong mostly monochromatic color scheme and an ambient, droning soundtrack to help theme the levels and build suspense for combat encounters and other surprises. This game is absolutely worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the old graphics fool you, the motion of the ocean is very modern, a very unapologetic shooter, comfortable with its own existence and cocksure about its target market, much less than be said by much bigger projects!  Trigger Warning: Communism and Lenin and his bros etc but I think the protagonist might be insane.9/10 good game also this walking meme of a developer wrote this in Pascal, haha.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: 8.5/10 game, very tightly madethe best way i can describe hrot is effecient: 200 megabytes storage, loading screens are minimal and only really occur to when booting up the game, doors open fast, levels are around 6-10 minutes long, and the level design is tight and compact.i liked it when i nuked a level
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: The brutalist architecture and bleak run down industrial environments of HROT's former socialist Czechoslovakia meshes incredibly well with the boomer shooter format. Maze-like levels, tons of secrets, and enemies crawling out of the walls had me appreciating a genre that I never had much direct exposure to. Much like other recent indie darlings, HROT serves as both an immensely accessible entry point into its genre while poking fun at some of its more dated tropes.Beef Stroganoff/10
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty dang awesome!  If Doom were set in Silent Hill, and if Silent Hill was located in some Soviet puppet regime in Eastern Europe, THIS would be that game!  I mean that in the best possible way.  Not really a horror game so much a throw-back retro FPS with an unsettling atmosphere and a few moments that constitute jump scares, usually baddies busting through walls to surprise you or opening a door to find a monsters waiting to shoot you.  And some genuinely unnerving bosses based off of communist motifs.You are a nameless citizen of some Commie Despotism or another.  With no clear motivation except to lock horns with the monsters.  The main bad-guys look like a cross between diesel-punk soldiers and Silent Hill's Order cultists of Silent Hill: Homecoming.  Uniformed goons with gas masks who shoot you on sight.  Later variants can teleport away from you at will and try to ambush you.  Giant floating heads that bear a striking resemblance to Valdmir Lenin fire projectiles at you.  Occasionally Hind attack choppers of Rambo 3 fame show up but somehow seem to bleed when you shoot them with shotguns (which are the best weapon against them).  And it wouldn't be that creepy without giant spindly spiders, so they're in it too.My favorite part is at the end where the final boss is a four-legged Joseph Stalin!  I have been a staunch anti-communist since freshmen year of High School when I read The Red Scarf Girl (highly recommended for anyone who actually THINKS communism is a good idea...lol) .  Even on normal difficulty it can be pretty unforgiving but very gratifying.Hats off to another indie developer who has managed to succeed where triple A developers often fail!  Here's hoping the developers keep at updating it and maybe give us some exposition.  But even as it is it's still a pretty darn good game.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game with extremely cool aesthetics and political satire, like being able to kiss pictures of politicians the main character likes. Very cheeky and I love that you can also do a variety of things in the game world, such as riding motorbikes through the levels, swim and fight horses with gas masks. Sometimes I got lost in the levels, but that's probably my fault for having a terrible sense of direction rather than the game's. Overall, absolutely recommended, though the price is a bit high considering how short it is so far, but I mean, it's still early access
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Hrot is a very good boomer-shooter, with a good soundtrack, cool graphics and well hidden secrets. The fights are dynamic and the bestiary is varied enough. Each level will take you around 10-20 minutes depending on whether you try to get all the secrets or not. This is not a horror game, but there are a few jump scares here and there, so if you don't like those but intend to play the game, get informed on when those happen so that you don't get too scared. Overall a great game, cannot recommend enough.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is an amazing "boomer shooter" made with lots of love, humor and wine. Mixing the styles of Quake, Chasm and Build Engine games like Duke 3D in a Slav-themed world full of gun wielding mad men, horses with gas masks, floating heads and the occasional bear. Definitely one of my new favorites in the retro-modern FPS genre. With a focus on pure fps gameplay, finding secret rooms, interactive props, silly jokes and cute puppers that will be your friend till the end! Just make sure you like the color brown, but that should be obvious based on the store page media.Highly recommend if you want to play a very solid and smooth retro-modern FPS and spend hours looking for that one secret you missed.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: All right i have played 3 hours so far and i have to say it's totally worth it game feels great and plays great. Movement is fast, shooting is satisfactory, enemies are dangerous and nothing is given to you for free. Atmosphere is crushing you can feel comunism leaking through your screen but its amazing at the same time. I am sure i am going to play more but i feel obligated to say to all fans of old school FPS just buy it and enjoy because this is a great game worth every cent.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I did love the setting, the almost universal shades of brown color pallet, the claustrophobic feeling. The game is also honestly quite fun. I love that it seems to draw from Czech culture, politics and legends as well. And the game manages to feel gritty, grimy, claustrophobic and oppressive. A hidden gem.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Big fan already - been following this one for a while (mostly due to other people's connecting it to DUSK, probably my favorite shooter of recent years). Played through the demo a couple days before release, and pretty solidly went through episode one when I could get my hands on it. Most of my issues are relatively small, and carry over from playing the demo: I find certain levels to play much better than others - I certainly found myself lost often, often looking for a single stray powerbox (keep your eyes open, seriously), and the sound needs some work (a lot of the guns lack any real sort of punch, imo). I also, at points, found enemy placement could be a bit frustrating - But these were relatively minor criticisms/problems for me. I am excited to play more. The game is dripping with atmosphere, from the general aesthetic of the locations to the enemy designs, and its hard to not get sucked in and go through the whole chapter immediately. Would recommend a play through the demo - if it seems like it's up your alley, the first episode will not disappoint.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is the funniest and most original game that came out within the new retro shooter wave.It constantly throws curve balls at you and adds new elements. Has such weird things that happen that it feels like a pipe dream.Apart from those though, what makes it even more special is how solid the level designs and the core gameplay feels.Its washed out colors might deceive you into thinking that the navigation would be hard but surprisingly its the exact opposite. Levels are masterfully interconnected, differentiated by uniquely designed rooms that are easy to navigate.There are tons of great things to say about HROT but rather than reading about it, you should experience it first hand.Absolute must play for everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: (EARLY ACCESS REVIEW FOR 12/07/2022)SYNOPSISHROT is a first-person-shooter set in the wonderfully grim and bleak 1986 Czechoslovakia. You have no name and your only goal is to destroy the hostiles that reside there.GAMEPLAYIt's traditional FPS goodness with some thriller elements thrown in. Run, shoot, find secrets and kill enemies as you explore various locations. Weapons are your usual pistols, shotguns, submachine guns to the explosive grenade launchers and lightning canons. Your enemy variety is quite expansive, from the Soldiers, Mutated Animals, Cultists and a horrific combination of all 3 thrown together. PRESENTATIONDon't be put off by the all brown / grey style, it actually works REALLY well for this kind of game. The feeling of dread, despair and grim shines through in the best way as the feeling of "something horrible happened here" starts to creep in. MISCIf you've finished the story and want more to do, you always have secret hunting, endless levels and of course Steam Achievements to work through.This game also doesn't demand much in terms of hardware. I was able to play the demo relatively smoothly on my laptop without having to alter any settings.Overall I recommend this game if you're in the mood for a suspenseful shooter.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is the Datura-induced lucid fever nightmare you wake up from whilst chained to a derelict basement under an abandoned laundromat somewhere along the steppes of Belarus after answering a deep web ad for volunteer work in developing communities. Creeks bellow out from an unseen stairwell, sending plumes of disintegrated drywall airborne. The clouds of dehydrated plaster glimmer and dance along the numerous beams of light penetrating through the loosely assembled wooden rafters above. The silhouettes of two men peak through the shadows of obscured shelving and cargo pallets. Your heart drops, you feel a rise of bile in your throat as the unimaginable reality of this situation begins to dawn on your now fully conscious mind. The echo of footsteps begin to penetrate through the deafening blare of antiquated air conditioning units, as the two shadows approach you from behind. You're helpless, immobile, confused, and entirely violated. They're getting closer. The shadows grow to absurd heights, easily breaching 6 feet each. They're getting closer. Tears well up in your eyes. They're almost here. You blink away your tears, violently opening and shutting your eyes in a desperate bid to wake up from this all-too realistic nightmare. They're almost here. No, you already woke up, this may be a nightmare, but it's certainly not a creation of nocturnal fiction, this is real, This is happening.They're here. You instinctively close your eyes.That's HROT.This game is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ radical, I've never felt more pride to be an an early-adopter and support this cause. Paying 17 bucks for this game in it's infancy felt like sending a check to sponsor disenfranchised Tanzanian youth seeking higher education.I've been following this game since around mid-2019, and I'm so fully funked out to see it in such a fully realized state with an actual functioning Steam page. So often these projects fall into the collective void where all promising Indie-Game-Twitter projects go when their devs grow apathetic or go back to the Arby's register in an effort to keep a roof over their heads without also keeping a ♥♥♥♥ in their mouths. (No disrespect toward sex-workers, you folks are amazing and your profession is valid).Obviously the tone and atmosphere are completely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ off the wall and utterly incredible, weaving this horrific web of art design, soundtrack, subtle-lore, and liminal-horror that fully leans into the strength of retro aesthetics in a horror setting and leaves you almost immobilized in many areas. All with this really unique, and largely unexplored within the retro/PSX aesthetic, Eastern European lens.We all got this from the demo and years of peaks through the dev's Twitter. But what seriously took me off guard was just how much the gameplay measured up. The combat opens up in a ton of areas, and the weapon dynamic and enemy balance seem seriously toned and well-tested. Combined with clever arena design, wonderful sense of level progression that carries through from the best of retro FPS, and episode 1 of HROT seriously ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crushes that 100% proof Boomer-shooter gooey goodness.There's been murmurs about the weapons, their impact and lack of "GA-GOOSH"ey-ness. But ech, blech, bloacch, bloackh. Don't listen to them Mr. Spythinev, I absolutely love the weapons and their sound design. They feel much lighter compared to the heavy, bassey tones in other contemporary titles of the Retro FPS Renaissance. HROT's weapons feel very utilitarian, and every-man. Fitting the tone of the setting, and the role of the character as just another soldier in the motherland's armies, not a stand-alone death god of boom and shoot. Keepa da noises.Where I feel HROT *might* falter a tad, is simply in its scale and sense of progression? It is only the first episode, and with it being such, there is a sense of same-eyness that starts to occur once you're over an hour in and you're still walking through the same sized narrow halls and eldritch demon-diarrhea soaked train station courtyards. As the game grows, I'd definitely love to see some larger maps alongside utilization of the game's driveable vehicles, perhaps in a Highway-17-esque extended section. Although I am absolutely certain beyond doubt we'll see the game's scale open up as the following episodes progress.To close, HROT is easily worth the $20 asking price, and supporting it's growth is something I feel a genuine sense of pride in doing.Support the arts and the Slavs.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, my time with this game has been marred by constant audio issues. Most of the time I have a constant popping sound that I have never had with any other game. Other times I try to boot up the game only to have no audio at all, forcing me to restart. As you can guess, trying to play a game with constant audio crackling in the background is not the optimal experience. It may very well be an issue on my end, but regardless it saps all fun out of playing. As for the game play, that is another area I was disappointed in. Guns don't feel as punchy and satisfying as they should, and movement felt too sluggish and limited. Enemy variety was ok in the short amount of game time I was able to stand. Unlike some other reviewers I actually don't mind the color palette, map design, and aesthetics; I love the soviet sci-fi/ Stalker vibes I get from the game, which is why it's so much more painful to observe it's issues. It all comes down to this--it just doesn't feel good to me. There is something missing from the gunplay and general gameplay loop that leaves me wanting. I do not think Hrot is a bad game, but maybe it just wasn't what I was looking for. Top comments are claiming this game is a communist Dusk, which I find very misleading. For those prepared to purchase Hrot, play the demo first, because it is really nothing like the fast-paced, frenetic boomer shooter you may be expecting. Again, this isn't a bad thing, it just leaves something to be desired in it's presentation.

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is a wonderfully idiosyncratic sojourn in Československo, or at least some fantasy version of it. HROT wears the trappings of a retro FPS, especially Quake and Chasm: The Rift, but its more than just killing. Like DUSK, you're completely enveloped into a world full of violence, but also many quiet moments of exploration and discovery. Most levels are long, intertwining mazes of corridors, secrets, sewers and exterior sections. A bit reminiscent of Heretic or HeXen. There are many well hidden secrets to be revealed by an inquisitive player. The score, by Sjellos, exponentially enhances the feelings of lurking danger, oppression and confusion evoked by the HROT and its visual identity. HROT is the complete package for those looking for a fun to play and unique FPS experience.

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is a thrilling homage to old first-person shooters, skillfully blending retro aesthetics with modern gameplay. The game's pixelated graphics and atmospheric pixel art evoke a nostalgic trip back in time, while its fast-paced gameplay, diverse weapons, and challenging enemies capture the essence of classic titles like DOOM and Quake. The well-crafted level design and haunting soundtrack further contribute to its appeal. HROT successfully resurrects the golden era of gaming, offering a satisfyingly nostalgic yet fresh and enjoyable experience for fans of old-school shooters. The game is truly a hidden masterpiece and a unique experience all around
