_childDocuments_.review: A "pretty good" Quake style game with a really unique vibe and setting.If you're into boomershooters, this is kind of a no-brainer, and one of the better efforts I've played in recent memory. However, I think from a raw gameplay perspective it plays its cards a little too safe to the "Quake" formula - the weapon selection is as you'd expect, and the combat encounters and level design challenges all feel very Quake, which is fine since that's one of the best shooters ever, but really I was hoping for a little of it's own unique flavour and it's own spin on proceedings. On more than one occasion it felt a little too much like Deja Vu for my tastes.One thing that is unique, however, is the setting. The comedy horror soviet vibes felt really original to me and I don't think I've seen this done in the same way anywhere else. It's part scary, part comedy - has a wicked sense of humour but also feels really grim and forboding. I love having to shoot flying lenin heads in a very brown soviet bloc.Overall, I recommend this shooter!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I love looking at this game. Right from the opening menu it immediately smashes you with this oppressive, industrial look and sound that create just the right feeling of bleakness. It unsettles you, even if only for a moment, which is enough to keep it in your mind so that whenever you interact with the world, you're just a little unsure.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: If you think Quake (the first one) is the best old-school FPS, play HROT.If you like shooters that focus on atmosphere and exploration, play HROT.If you think sewers and subways actually make for the best levels, play HROT.If brown isn't your favourite colour, play HROT to change your mind.HROT eschews the recent trends of boomer shooters becoming increasingly complex in the wake of Doom Eternal. There are no alternative fire modes. No upgrades or mods. There is a single move speed, a kick, and a jump. All enemy attacks can be dodged by strafing in and out of cover, or by circling around them.On the surface this might sound like a negative, but this mechanical restraint is part of what makes HROT so great. Old-school shooters weren't all about mowing down waves of enemies with complex movement/weapon combos. They were about exploring a hostile and mysterious environment. Enemies served as a way to make the levels feel alive, as well as a means to instil tension and dread in the player.HROT nails every aspect of this old-school philosophy. Its beautifully brown levels echo real locations in late-communist Czechoslovakia. Environmental storytelling is abundant and enemy designs are both humorous and terrifying. Most importantly, the game keeps you constantly excited (and slightly scared) for what comes next.HROT consists of 24 levels (each around 15 - 30 mins long) spread over three chapters. Each level is set in a distinct location, centred around the game's themes of industry, technology, transport, bureaucracy, and Czech history. Levels loop back on themselves in interesting ways (e.g. sometimes the exit is near the start, but you need a key), but are always well designed enough so that you never get lost (I didn't know there was a map until I finished the game). Most levels have several secrets to discover, and each of the three chapters have a sprinkling of set pieces and Easter eggs.Each level features around 60 to 70 enemies. Most of these are placed in small groups evenly along the level. There are often contextual clues as to when you'll encounter enemies, which is important as the skill in defeating them lies in anticipating (or reacting to) their presence, rather than long fights. Both the enemies and the player are reasonably squishy (even on normal difficulty).Some enemy types move in a slightly unpredictable manner, like they're a bit drunk. This makes them slightly harder to hit, but not frustratingly so (none of them are annoyingly fast).Enemy variety is also good, mostly from an aesthetic perspective, but there's also reasonable mechanical variety: enemy size, movement speed, projectile speed, damage, flying enemies, leaping enemies etc.Most levels also feature one section towards the end with a concentration of enemies in a big arena. If you found a bunch of secrets and didn't take much damage earlier in the level, it's a fun opportunity to use some of your powerful weapons. If you rushed through the rest of the level, it's usually a decent challenge to just scrape through this final wave.Other than one or two surprises, the weapons are all things you've seen before. But they all feel good to use, and each of them excel at dealing with different types of enemies.The brown crunchy graphics are perfection. The music is also excellent and the game does a good job of switching between atmospheric music, uptempo music, and silence depending on the situation.You should play HROT.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Give the demo a shot!Episode 1 out in EA with an endless mode, it's one of the best in the latest retro FPS craze, EP2 & 3 will eventually come out but solo dev with a family life in the middle of a pandemic so be patient and understanding!A ton of personality, charm, atmosphere and individuality despite the clear influences. A solo developer who put in so much effort into little details, both environmentally as well as in gameplay, interactive elements, making combat, movement, music, level design, all feel excellent.If you like Dusk, Half-Life, Quake, Chasm, old Build games, you should absolutely pick this up.I feel like the dreary brown really fits, it's done in a consistent deliberate fashion, with I think just enough shades here and there, which help with making the game easy on the eyes, you always know what you're looking at. Enemies, though also fittingly brownish, still stand out and don't blend in with the environment, making the gameplay feel like everything is easily signposted and critical information stands out at any given time. I was really surprised by how good the moody soundtrack is, just fits and sounds so wonderful, I wonder if even that is composed by the solo dev?Level design feels really satisfying, the way labyrinthine pathways loop back on some more central area where you need a key, the layers, not being just a flat plane, the secrets that are really rewarding to both figure out and what you usually get out of them.The 1986 Soviet controlled Czechoslovakia theme and setting also looks really good, the blocky brutalist buildings, the dirty concrete, the poverty of it all with no baroque extravaganza on display, just functional enough.It can get a bit samey; sewers, underground tunnels, some facilities, factories, streets and stores, but I don't know, somehow I don't mind it that much, maybe my opinion will change if 3 episodes will feel like this, but I'm not sure if I will get sick of it, as long as each episode does shake things up in some way, doesn't have to be environmentally.Weapons include a sickle that hits surprisingly well, even tiny rats! A reliable pistol that you can dual wield and feels great. Your workhorse shotgun that works at decent ranges, has a nice spread of a lot of pellets, feels strong and is strong in how it pushes enemies, knocks them down or straight up gibs them. A submachine gun which also is nifty, though ammo is scarce for that one at the start. An excellent rocket launcher which uses your grenade ammo, which are also handy in a pinch, detonating on impact, or good around corners. A really powerful nice super shotgun that knocks enemies really far. A lightning gun which is neat, could use maybe a bit more flare but gets the job done, and a BFG, a fun lightning ball launching device with a fun detonation effect.Some people complain about the sound effects of weapons, personally I like them, and even if they're muted, I just automatically excuse it subconsciously as fitting the theme of being these cheap knockoff soviet mass produced weapons that mainly get the job done.Still I think they feel really satisfying to use, many elements come together in making the combat feel rewarding, from movement, weapon animations, particle effects and muzzleflashes, ejected smoking shells,, hit feedback in knockback, slight stuns, blood spurts etc.Balance feels surprisingly good, normal feels like normal, still tense and at times challenging, but doable, ammo never at max (so far) but I usually have had enough for every single encounter, big and small, health pickups are just enough to keep me going and strafing will keep you alive for a long time.The game is fond of Doom 3 monster closets, but they haven't felt overly unfair, I expect them, I can see where usually enemies will pour in from, and, if I at all remember that I have them, I can place some land mines in preparation before picking up a key, triggering the enemies to come out.Special note for lovable goofy enemy designs, the game is a perfect balance of being spooky and not taking itself too seriously.Bosses were a bit on the easy side, but still fun, didn't take itself too seriously, silly yet threatening in behaviour, final boss felt like it had a really nice tense buildup to it, well scripted reveal in my opinion.Dev made their own custom Pascal engine from scratch, it runs silky smooth, takes only 100mbs of space on your harddrive, loading saves is instantaneous, looks surprisingly gorgeous despite the old-school feel it goes for; the architecture, enemy design, weapon design, little shaders for windows and metal, rain-fog-dust-particle effects, animated skybox, animated wobbly water texture with neat ripples, a rich audioscape filled with rainsounds, metro sounds, humming machinery etc to bring the world alive, fire that can spread a bit and linger and have dynamic lights, the smoke from fire, lovely grainy gradient to lighting and colors overall, ejected shell casings, the blood decals that can drip from the ceiling, the impact effects, enemies getting knocked back or even down, gore, breakable objects, AI that can zig and zag and not just mindlessly go straight for you, drivable little scooters...You get the idea, it's really feature rich, not much missing and has a lot we either take for granted or only expect in our pseudo-immersive shooters like Dusk, Ion Fury or Half-Life.A good options menu, some odd things like no numerical values for FOV or resolution, but at least those exist as options, alongside vsync, fps cap, fullscreen, brightness, gamma, renderer - Excellent Hud and gameplay settings, toggling all ammo counters, camera animation and strafe tilting, tweaking crosshairs, hud scale, weapon position & scale, message location, setting if switching to new weapon or always on pickup, a bunch of neat QoL stuff to customize, and good bindings as well.I've had no issues, the game feels really polished, haven't encountered bugs, and the game just looks, feels, sounds, is so good.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't say its for everyone but its the only game that's scratching my dusk itch as of recent. The very hard mode is challenging enough without being ridiculous like some other hard modes on these types of shooters. So my review is based solely on that mode (and its not really a real review just some points for any other nerd who wants to read this jumble..) - *The enemy balancing is pretty good but takes some getting used to. Each of them have their own strengths and weakness but you'll find that an up close shotgun blast pretty much takes care of any enemy.*Ammo is pretty scarce so you'll have to be accurate and plan your route.*The level design so far is intuitive enough to where you wont need to use your map, which is good to keep the flow of the game constant.*The enemy projectile speed is just fast enough that you can dodge it and be able to see it. *The sounds are satisfying and the music is done very well, its more ambient dark than anything else.*Game is more sedated in its presentation compared to dusk but will mess you up something awful if you think cero miedo was challenging. I just finished castle right now and really liked that level and the music on that level. Will update after I complete the game.

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty fun old school shooter. It's fairly short as of right now (about 3 hours to full clear the game on normal) but the gameplay is pretty tight.If you are a fan of old school Doom/Quake era shooters it is worth checking out. A good dose of nostalgia while also being newThat being said, there isn't much revolutionary about this game and it's fairly short in its current state. So if you're on the fence maybe wait for additional updates.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Phew, that was a tough game, a really good one but a really hard one as well.Played it on hard difficulty and finally a game that really was hard on that difficulty setting :-).Overall a very enjoyable expirience, the engine is great, the game plays fantastic and the leveldesign, oh my god, the leveldesing is on another level (pun indeed intended). The levels circle around to the places you need to be without you noticing it, so there is next to none backtracking, really impressive. And another thing that impressed me a lot is the atmosphere, to create such a deep atmosphere with such minimalistic devices is nothing but genius.If you like Quake or Dusk, this game is a must play, it is different in places but generally you can put theese three games in one basket, all awesome.Highly recommended to get this game, worthy at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: No thanks to David Oshry, I found this game, played the demo, and loved it. While the first episode is fairly short, this is going to be a new all time favorite shooter for me. If you think that possibly 5-6 hours of content isn't for you, then maybe wait for the creator to release more episodes. But for me, this is so fluid and fast and I love that. Cheers to you!8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Made of pure soul and takes direct inspiration from what one would call "Boomer Shooters", most notably Quake. What's not to love?Level design is for the most part great (and filled with plenty of interactive elements too) plus the weapons are satisfying to use.The soundtrack while pretty standard for this type of genre of FPS is still enjoyable to listen to and fits the game nicely.There's a good variety of enemies and they're pretty fair, not cheap by any means nor are they complete pushovers.Completed the campaign? Well there's an endless mode and a Bomberman mod made by the developer himself. I didn't expect any of this but hey, they're nice additions to give the game some replay value.Oh and there's a part where you can have dogs and they fight for you, you be the judge.My main complaint? This is more of a nitpick than anything else but the colour scheme that resembles my toilet after a vindaloo can get pretty old after a while.Overall the dev has done a really good job capturing the energy of an old school FPS and if you're into those types of games I'd definitely give this a spin. here's the obligatory wacky funni xd meme you were probably expecting: most normal holiday in prague, i rate it 8/10 neopets.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifully crafted FPS with the nuance of an expert.  This game is incredibly inspired and proudly wears it's influences yet never compromises it's unique style. Never once does an enemy, weapon, nor level feels like it is wearing down and becoming more of the same, nor does it feel like they overstep the boundary of the game's design. I truly, cannot overstate how much of an accomplishment it is to have this game stay true to style and world while also never feeling like more of the same. And to manage so with an intentionally duller, more laxxed audio and visual design is nothing short of master craft.   I hope all who play this, enjoy it or not, can at least see and appreciate how carefully and meticulously crafted this game is to deliver with a restrained design palette whilst never letting the boundaries of such tax the experience and give way to repetition.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Fun boomer shooter. Low poly, somewhat varied enemies. Wish there was more variety in weapons as you only use a few and they are just standard shotgun and submachine gun. The environments are varied, although not super interesting. But its fun, shooting and movement work well. The fact this was made by one guy is pretty awesome. I will say there are a lot of better boomer shooters out there. 7.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Beware! If you want to play this because you enjoyed playing classic DOOM, think again! HROT's normal mode is way harder than the hardest mode you could ever play in classic DOOM. Even the easy is no fooling around. You'll find yoursen restarting everytime you get hit for nothing, just to make sure you kill most of the enemies without getting hit. If you let yoursen get hit when you could clearly avoid it, you'll be paying for that later. DOOM had saves, so you could same mid-game and that was it, but forget that B.S.: You'll have none of these here. You die, you restart from the beginning.This game is for no amateurs! No sunday gaming! If you want to play it, you got to do FOR REAL.
