_childDocuments_.review: While I like the game, there was one issue that made the experience a lot worse for me. The game simply does not run smooth. Posting this negative review as a warning for others, since it really affected my time with this game. I also tried to contact the developer about the issue, but no response within a month. Here is what I sent to the developer:Hi,I really love HROT and I bought the game on Steam to support you and this awesome game!I want to report an issue that the game is not running smoothly on my beefy PC (AMD 5950X + RTX3080). My monitor is 120Hz and while the framerate counter is showing 120FPS all the time, the actual framerate is definitely lower and fluctuating. I am very sensitive to framerates and it's very easy for me to detect that issue.I tried various things in hope to resolve the issue: changing my desktop resolution to 4k, 1080p, 720p, running the game in a window with even lower resolutions by modifying config.cfg. It's definitely not an issue with rendering performance, I have super stable 120FPS reported all the times.I also tried to switch between raw mouse input on and off, but while that affects sensitivity, the smoothness was not fixed. Also experimented with GL_HROT setting, but smoothness issue is present in both on and off state.I also found a forum post stating that too high polling rate on a mouse could cause issues with HROT running smoothly. I tried lowering mouserate to 125Hz and that did not improve the smoothness, it only introduced a slight, but noticeable latency in responsiveness.Also tried disabling GSync and tried various VSync on/off and framerate cap in the settings to no avail.Running out of ideas on what could be tried next. It does remind me of the latest Amnesia installment which was locked to 60FPS and you could unlock the cap for rendering, but mouse polling was hardcoded to 60FPS in the engine which made the whole experience 60FPS even though I was able to run the game constantly at 120FPS.HROT real framerate is varying between 60 and 100 FPS for me. Again, the FPS counter is showing 120FPS all the time. The only time I could really feel it was 120FPS was right at the beginning of second level. That lasted only for a few seconds as moving forward to the next area made the framerate go down.I hope that you will find the info provided here useful as a bug report. If you want me to try some things, don't hesitate to ask. I am technically inclined, software developer too.  Keep up the good work!Thanks,Damian
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: It felt like I was back in 1996.Great atmosphere and tight gameplay. The story takes you for a ride without a single bit of forced exposition. You can see the dev's blood, sweat, and tears in every level. One of the most authentic feeling throwback shooters out there.  Highly recommend you give this game a try!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: A great retro shooter in the vein of Quake. Bland to the point of caricature, setting the theme of a drab and miserable soviet satellite state in the waning days of communist power. You have no action hero one-liners, no fancy dodges or skill trees, sound is muted, polygons have been rationed, and the whole world is brown with gray. Movement is so smooth though, shooting is so well balanced, it's such a well-distilled classic shooter experience. You are a simple man with simple weapons. Move and shoot. Save the Orloj and save Praque. And save the ratter dogs too.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I was eagerly anticipating this game and it did not disappoint me.Movement feels great, gunfights have good audiovisual feedback, music is excellent.*THIS IS NOT DOOM* don't expect a power fantasy, you will be near death often and ammo is scarce.Art style is bleak but not bland, comparisons to Quake or Chasm are unavoidable.A lot of people saying the weapons sound weak, it's an intentional aesthetic choice that I think works well. I definitely recommend this game if you are into classic 90s FPS or have ever watched a Civvie 11 video.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most promising throwback FPS games. It breathes (mostly) Quake and gets its inspirations just right. Bonus points if you actually lived during the infamous Eastern Bloc period, or at least are familiar with the daily realities of that time, which makes you appreciate the game even more.EDIT: Post-release update, game delivered as expected and is even more awesome, cannot recommend enough.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is another one of these boomer shooters but it's honestly one of the best in its genre. The quickest way to sum it up is that it's a goofy slavic take on Dusk or Quake. There are three episodes each with 8 levels that you can finish it in around 7 or so hours. Of course you can get many more hours out of it if you're looking for all the secrets on higher difficulties, but I was satisfied with halfheartedly looking for these on normal.The story doesn't really matter: you're some guy in the Soviet controlled Czech Republic and you have to kill a bunch of guys wearing gasmasks across very brown and depressing looking Eastern Bloc locales. It's got a good variety of weapons and a bunch of interesting enemies. The levels are definitely old school with their designs and key finding but rarely did I feel lost or unsure of where to go. It's just long enough to where you want more from it.There are a TON of historical references, figures, tidbits, and jokes that will be lost on the average Westerner. I had no clue what most of this stuff was referencing but it all came across as amusing and gives the game a fun, unique atmosphere somewhat reminiscent of STALKER and other 'Eurojank' games. There are two great Steam guides ("a guide to Symbolism in HROT (SPOILERS!!!)" and "Lost in Translation") that explains most of this stuff if you are interested.Even though it's kind of short for it's price I still had a great time with it. I got this from a Humble Bundle a while ago along with Ion Fury and more so I'm very happy with what I paid. $20 full price is kind of steep if you're the kind of person to one-and-done games, but it seems to hit $13.99 regularly on the big sales. It's a very well-done, competent, and funny old school throwback that I would wholeheartedly recommend to anyone who enjoys these kind of modern boomer shooters.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This game is oozing with atmosphere, and I love it. This FPS is a very well put together retro affair that is very by-the-book, but there is absolutely not an issue with that. The levels are well constructive, the enemies are well designed, and the load out does the job. I can't wait to see what the next episodes bring. I have a few constructive critiques that some others have said:1) Get those sound effects more punchy2) More lore in the levels! I love the atmosphere, so tell us what is happening in this world!3) More health and ammo in levels. I was always low on both, and it really hurt my boss fights and big enemy encounters. Not in a fun way. I was playing on normal, and was always desperately searching for pickups.I'm having a blast with this, and if you like retro FPS games, support an indie dev by picking this up. You won't be disappointed!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: When I first tried out HROT its second Episode was only half done and I went in with zero expectations as it was one of several games I got in a bundle. I was pleasantly surprised by just how good the game was and now that the game has fully released and I've had the chance to play through it I am glad to say the back half does not disappoint and it is probably one of my favorites of the boomer shooter genre.HROT is set in a Cold War era Soviet dystopia with some unique twists and weird ideas thrown in and doesn't take itself too seriously. The game is graphically reminiscent of early 3D shooters like the original Quake with its low-poly models, simple level architecture, and lots of brown, and really nails the retro aesthetic, feel, and vibes.The combat feels tight and well tuned with fast and fluid movement, a large arsenal of weapons that feel satisfying to use, with only one or two exceptions that don't have the impact or feel they should due to lackluster sound effects, and there is a pretty large variety of different enemy types with some rather creative and interesting designs as well as several unique bosses that'll keep you on your toes. I also love how you can kick grenades back at enemies. HROT can be challenging at times but overall skews toward being on the easy side so you may want to bump up the difficulty.The level design is solid and feels very old school with surprise ambushes, branching paths, and at times confusing layouts, but can sometimes feel flat as the maps don't always take enough advantage of the verticality of 3D level and encounter design. Some levels have notable and unique set pieces and landmarks but the levels often blur together because of the lack of color variety. Pops of color here and there would go a long way to add visual variety to break up the overwhelming brown and help to distinguish levels from one another.The music is generally pretty subdued and atmospheric to fit the dark and haunting vibes the game is going for but ramps up in intensity during the larger fights and is good to keep the blood pumping.Other boomer shooters might get more widespread recognition but HROT is great enough to stand right alongside them and is an excellent addition to the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Much like the Soviet Union, this is a game about rationing, but it's fun as ♥♥♥♥. Never have I been scurrying around sewers like a rat in desperate search for sweet sweet skim milk or another 4 shotgun shells just to survive my next firefight. Brush up on your sickle based combat if you ever find your bullets dry when fighting a gorilla, though.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for gameplay and an interesting artstyle; HROT isn't for you.i know people say this a lot but ill say it again, i wish steam had a mid review type because thats what i think this game is. I've played through a lot of boomer shooters and HROT just doesnt really impress me. Sure its not a bad game but it doesnt do much for the genre either. The combat isnt very good, the artstyle while i think is cohesive and looks good, starts to get bland after only a few levels in. It really ways down on the game as a whole as the combat and movement are already lackluster then on top of that there isnt much to look at. The game isn't terrible but there are much better boomer shooters out there.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: "Just the right amount of soviet era depression bleeding into my senses"-SsethzeentachVery neat little game, good level design, love the easter eggs here and there in the levels, really adds to the pacing. Absolutely worth the money, provided you like boomer shooters as much as anyone in the reviews section of this game. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: By turns this game is intense, creepy, nostalgic, funny, and always steeped in an atmosphere as thick as canned cream of mushroom soup (when the store has some, that is). Fantastic music.There is something otherworldly about this game: when you fight your way through a level full of surreal Chernobylesque abominations—sickle and shotgun in hand like a true pioneer of socialism—and then at the end, utter quiet as you flick a switch to open the next area, and an old film of dear Comrade Lenin begins to play… then I just don't know how to feel.A somewhat more abstract reading of the game yields the kind of paranoid fever dream that must have resulted from Soviet authorities' downplaying the disaster of 1986. When even the proletarian vanguard party has to admit that a  and  nuclear incident has occurred, that's the time to start being afraid. I will certainly be playing more of this.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I picked this up in a bundle of boomer shooters because I wanted to play Ion Fury and Dusk. Imagine my surprise when I loaded this unknown game up and enjoyed it more than either of those two.If there's one thing this game has in abundance its atmosphere. It is unsettling, creepy and weird. When you combine that with a well made fast paced shooter your in for a good time.It's a lot of fun and very unique. Give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Out of all the recent Boomer Shooters, HROT is probably the most authentic feeling one out there at the moment. The custom game engine really nails the feeling of a a long lost slav-jank FPS gem from '98 in the best way possible.Also, you can take a dump in the toilets. Can't wait for episode 3.10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: although I was born after the change of regime (1989) and not in Czechoslovakia (but in a Middle-European country close to it), there are countless things in this game, such as the different pickups and items in the gameworld that I instantly recognized, and they are absolutely wonderful, just full of charm and soulIf you are into boomer shooters and/or you are from an ex-communist or eastern bloc country, this game is a must-buy.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Calling HROT "Slavic Quake" honestly doesn't do it justice.It has an understated yet gripping atmosphere, with dark, off-beat humor that will appeal to Czech players first and foremost. With a large roster of monsters and a good selection of weapons, HROT deserves its high rating.Also, this is literally the only game I've ever seen that gives you recipes for beating chapters. Virgin DOOM with its surface-level plot ain't got nothing on Chad HROT and its recipes lemme tell yaMy only wish is that the first episode had a secret level like the other two, but hey the game has 26 levels + 4 survival maps.Buy HROTDrink semi-skimmed milkPraise Gustav
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: If you love classic FPS games or Dusk then you have to do yourself a favor and play this boomer shooter. It has everything a growing First Person Shooter boy needs. Epic guns, alots of enemies to shoot, humor, and most importantly more guns. Oh also there are boss fights. I loved every minute playing this fantastic game.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like it more than I did. Pros: -Gunplay is fun. -Level design is well done-atmosphere is great-exploration is rewardedCons:-bland art direction (makes areas confusing to navigate)-some weapons are practically useless-some game mechanics aren't explainedA fun play-through, if you're a fan of boomer shooters don't miss this one. Just wished for more varied environments, and more interesting weapons.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Hrot was an interesting game, an engine made by the developer, brown like in Quake, but set in a Soviet country in 1986.I played all of chapter one in about 2.2 hours on the medium difficulty, your mileage may vary.You, as the main character, don't know much, so you grab your pistol and your hammer and sickle, and start shooting anyone, or anything, on sight. There is probably more than what meets the eye.Movement speed is quick in a nice way, I don't go too fast or too slow, guns sound a little bit weak, but for this kind of game is perfectly fine.Gunplay is similar to another throwback shooter that we all are very likely to be familiar with, where the only hitscanner is you, with exception to your rockets, land mines and grenades, that'd be stupid.I haven't fully mastered the travel time of the grenade throw, it does have its dedicated throw button, RMB by default, which does what it does.What is very strange is why the button to reload the pistol is set to 2 by default than just R, not complaining when I can run it akimbo, does have a nice little reload then.Overall I found the gunplay quite good, enemies are relatively quick to kill on the medium difficulty, which is usually what I play at, feel free to try the harder difficulties if you're feeling masochistic.Here's to seeing chapter 2 and 3!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: A charming little shooter made by a single Czech developer, HROT feels reminiscent of days gone by with its Cold War-era setting, brutal difficulty, and limited graphics created by a custom Pascal-based game engine, but something about it just seems modern all the same, in a way that I just can't do justice. It has plenty of odd humor and interactivity, while counterbalancing that and the action with sprinklings of horror and suspense. I was admittedly hesitant when I first got this game, but it grew on me once I learned to appreciate the subtlety of it all.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing the full release i can confidently say this game is fantastic! Great retro shooter with an amazing art direction and gameplay. It's crazy that this was made by one dude in a custom engine and it came out so well. Happy to have been able to watch this game grow and get bigger better and more bizzare the entire way through!If you love a retro shooter in the vein of the Quake or Unreal I'd suggest you do yourself a favor and pick this bad boy up it has everything you want i swears it!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is a wonderful and very charming FPS shooter hearkening back to the days of DOOM and Quake with an infusion of life set in the cold war era. It manages to faithfully recreate the experience of the classics whilst being true to itself; it affectionately pays homage to what came before without being a duplicate re-textured clone. I love the monotonous dark brown and sad beige colors, they evoke a certain flavor of desperation whilst simultaneously providing a slight amount of hopeful warmth. It's a game that's so simple, it's fun.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: It's 1986 and something is rotten in the glorious peoples republic of Czechoslovakia. Your job is to gently reeducate the mutated citizens by showing them the error of their bourgeois ways. This education is vigorously applied using the barrel of a shotgun in the manner all great communist crusades should be.A short, bizarre and genuinely entertaining game.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR buy this game, is good. Okay, this is the first time I've felt compelled to write a review, and seeing as it's in Early Access and only has been out for a grand total of one day, I just have to recommend this game. If you're on the fence about it, don't be. The gunplay, the music, the tone, all of it pitch perfect. Obviously, there are some issues, specifically regarding framerate drops during some of the mid-Episode 1 levels. However, I fully believe the developer is hard at work solving these issues as they have not only kept releasing updates all day, but also used those updates to add and change secrets for those who've played the demo already. Another thing to consider, this game has been and will continue to see comparisons to Dusk (2018), which is fair. It clearly takes a lot of inspiration from that fantastic gem. However, HROT takes strides to not only distinguish itself, but set it's own form of atmosphere. Whereas the dark humor in Dusk can be, although cute, slightly cringy, HROT's humor is both dark, and oddly quirky. Random things will occur that are only elevated if you have an acute awareness of what it's satirizing especially the historical connections to real life. Sound is also really well designed, with each creature having it's own distinct idle noise for the player to identify and prepare for. The weapons are satisfying, while also reminding you to conserve ammo and to carefully choose how to approach combat scenarios. Overall, I am very excited for the future of HROT, and I eagerly await later episodes.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome! awesome and weird. There are tons of creative and interesting enemies, several of which made me stop and laugh. Why do the wheelchair guys do so much damage!? lol. The movement and combat are slick, fast, and fun. You have a veritable arsenal at your disposal to gib and massacre the bizarre hoards that fill each and every level. Dual pistols ftw! My one and only complaint stems from the weapons: they sound a little pathetic. C’mon gimmie some oomph. Otherwise this game is top tier.  It’s got so much atmosphere. Each level is oozing with intensity and a pervasive unsettling vibe. I got pretty spooked on some of the levels, leading to more than one moment of being startled but in a good way. There aren’t any cheap jumpscares save one, which totally got me. I shouted loud enough to startle my dogs too hahaha. I particularly enjoyed the part in episode 3 w/ the two dog companions. Overfeeding them till they puked had me laughing. This game is amazing and a mandatory purchase if you enjoy good games and don’t mind the low fidelity graphics. Another amazing boomershooter in a sea of amazing ones. I’m very, very happy to have played this. Can’t wait to see what the devs come up w/ next. It fascinates me how so many large developers are making and selling broken garbage for $70+ dollars and here in the indie scene amazing games are being made and sold for an oh so reasonable price. Idk, it’s a good time to be a gamer if you have half a brain.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This is a perfect game! Everything is perfect in it, design, weapons, sounds, maps, secrets. I have had the greatest joy playing the first two episodes and I cant wait for the 3rd one to come. I absolutely loved the game BLOOD back in the days and this comes extremely close to all that was good about the Blood and yet this is more - this is original, edgy, and fun.One secret I want to share - play this in "paper" "no blue light" mode of your monitor that makes the game even more brownish, its perfect that way and even more stylish ;-)
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I like hearing people calling it Slav-Quake but not being as jank as Slav-jank. Really fun weapon and enemies, even comes with a retro quality slider. I think a good improvement would be a weapon wheel but it's honestly fine with out it. HROT is very good at setting an atmosphere in this soviet russia dystopian nightmare with the perfect, light amount of comedy in it to make your playthroughs even more enjoyable without watering over the game's main tone it presents.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I can't quite say a lot has impressed me with HROT. Just another Quake clone around the block, but I give it an A for effort to try to be a little interesting with it's setting. There's way too much damn brown, it's literally like you're playing in a world of ♥♥♥♥. Granted, the setting is putting you in a world of ♥♥♥♥ but whatever.Don't care too much about it's setting, there just isn't a lot to grind your teeth over, it feels like. That's really all I can say about HROT. It is simply just a playable FPS that you could probably breeze through with FPS experience, but then forget about right after. Simply because it's just again, another Quake clone with a different theme painted over, which is about as impressive as making a few DOOM WADs, that everyone has done before.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: It is a genuinely scary game, off-putting atmosphere and convincingly bleak setting. Greatly assisted by authentic 90's era jittery polygons and crunchy textures. Very effective backdrop for what is, in fact, a silly game.Tight, polished boomer-shooter type gameplay. Moves fast, feels good to play. Lots of great twisty level design, key hunts, secrets, all that good good stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great Quake"esque" shooter that earns the title "brown", in that nearly everything in the game is brown to some degree.Which does not take anything away from the game, as it still is worth the purchase.Gameplay is solid and the array of weapons you get, all have a distinct usage, but the shotgun is 100% the one gun you're going to be using the most. As mentioned before, everything is more or less brown, but there's still variety in the level designs and takes inspiration from eastern european enviroments, specifically the Czech Republic, as iirc it was mentioned a couple of times throughout the game, that makes it so that while the color palette does not change immensly, the designs and variation of the levels do.I highly recommend this for anyone that loves "boomer shooters" or generally loves great shooters.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game! Enemies do not have hitscan, and as such hit way harder if they DO land a shot on you. Lots of running, lots of shooting, unapologetically brown (though more like Quake than the typical 2010s military shooter game) and you can get li'l rat-catcher dogs! Most of the game's writing is in Czech, but you CAN get English translations if you want some help with directions, plot, perhaps humour too. Does have SOME jumpscares, screen flashes, and spiders (though the game at least lets you convert those spiders into rats)Well worth the money for the time you can get out of it, even if the buffets never seem to be open.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Grimy and dirty and gross and icky but in a good way. I like the fast paced action and the gunplay is satisfying. The secrets are fun to collect and aren't too horribly hard to find/figure out (although you may need to look a few up, but such is the fate of a boomer shooter). I'd highly recommend playing this game on the highest difficulty. Excellent game.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Boomer shooters have definitely grown in popularity over the last several years, and as far as they go, I think that HROT is an excellent example of how to do them well.The gameplay is pretty standard for a boomer shooter; quick and fluid movement, simple yet enjoyable weapons, great maps, and a variety of enemies that offer unique challenges that can be conquered with the right weapons. Games don’t have to be revolutionary to be good, as long as you create an interesting premise and make sure that the core gameplay is up to snuff then you are good to go. HROT does that. I like the weapons, they feel well-balanced and hit the niches that are necessary for a game like this. I did want to see more weapons, but the roster they have is well done so that isn’t really an issue; a limited option of good weapons is better than a vast array of poorly built weapons. Level design can be a bit too maze-like for my taste, but there is a wonderful amount of variety and it always kept things interesting with unique mechanics regularly. There is a good variety of enemies that act in unique ways; they are not super smart, but for a game like this that is perfectly fine. Of note, to get one of the achievements I did have to beat some levels on the maximum difficulty and I must say that it didn’t really feel balanced at that level which kind of made it a drag and felt too punishing, but it was a challenge I will give it that. And as a final note, something that I was not expecting is that the horror is decent (particularly in acts 1 and 2). There was at least a time or two I got a bit of a chill through me, and there were two jump scares that were a bit cheap feeling (as I think most jump scares are), but they did get me. There is not a ton of horror in the sense of creating moments of fear, but the whole horror vibe is there.And speaking of the world and the vibes that it gave me I thought it was great. The game’s story is extremely strange and cryptic, which is a bit offputting, but fun nonetheless. But in contrast, the whole vibe and themes of the world though are really strong and dark and I just eat that ♥♥♥♥ up. The Soviet Union has interested me for a long time and this game shows it in a very interesting light as well, this grimy dingy world just oozes with character. All-in-all I found that the world is interesting and liked it even when it got quite wacky.As for the sound design, I think it is the weakest part of the game. Enemy sounds are fine, but guns do sound a bit weak to me. What is bad though is the positional audio, it is not aligned at all and feels like it needs an overhaul. I could see an argument that the sound design is that way because it is emulating an older era of games; however, I think that is a poor excuse. We can make better games while still keeping the spirit the same. The music does do better, it is quite atmospheric, though it is also nothing to be really praised either. One thing I will note is that there were a couple of times when enemy sounds rang out that were really creepy and gave me a bit of a chill, the first time I heard a bear but couldn’t see it got me a bit.Graphically this game is clearly stylized, the old chunky models, simple textures, and some flat objects all call to an older era and will completely be up to your taste on how you feel about that. I think that more than anything the drab brown colors only permeated with moments of actual color will turn off some people, but I think it really matches the setting and personally liked it. It is depressing, creepy, and dark and I like that. Your character's animations are fluid and I enjoy that, however, it does feel like enemies are a bit too stiff even given the era they are emulating. Overall though I liked how HROT looks and I think it enhances the game overall.To conclude I felt like HROT was a fun game, that kept me playing, had an interesting world, and did not overstay its welcome. The sale price is more than fair for the amount of fun I had with it, and I am glad to see that people agree that this game is great. If you are a fan of boomer shooters HROT is a must-play.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: OH YEAH...This game is already hittin' the spot. I tried to play with a controller at first but seems you can only adjust look sensitivity by integers (despite the decimal shown), but after abandoning the controller I feel much more at home anyway.At least once a year I get nostalgic for the original Half-Life. Even down to the obvious, blocky pixels when you hit stuff with the crowbar. This game is already scratching that itch. I'm impressed with the thrill evoked by this game, regardless of its graphical simplicity.  I enjoy the speed and camera tilt when you're moving around. Just using the pistol and melee is fun enough without the sub-machine gun or hand cannon. I haven't even tried the land mines. It's also pretty funny at times, and right out the gate there's a secret spot too, so, imo, it bodes well for how the player will be rewarded for attention to detail throughout the game. Great job Spytihněv.***I will say I managed to break all the boxes in a particular one room though and was surprised the most difficult-to-reach box had nothing in it... but hey, maybe there'll be a fix for that? 😉***
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: A very clever shooter. The visuals are extremely minimalist to the point of being regressive but the game world itself has an insane level of interaction to compensate. Destructible terrain, vehicles, playable pianos and there is even a fully functional Matryoshka doll lying around among many other surprises. While none of these things are integral to game play, the attention to detail is commendable, and used to great effect in the extremely odd and extremely uncomfortable pseudo-slavic setting. As far as the actual shooting goes the action here deviates between run-and-gun and slow-and-steady, depending on your current health and ammo. Spaces range from tiny to medium sized. There are no large arenas in the conventional sense, and enemy ambushes are almost always unexpected and rarely telegraphed. The music is perfectly moody and never overbearing; certain tracks trigger during scripted events. Great use of show-don't-tell throughout to establish the barest implication of a story and build tension.This is more than an FPS, this is art. One of the few titles I recommend in early access. I don't care if we have to wait another decade for a full release, the dude deserves the cash. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I am now a proud owner of a pack of prague ratters.Hrot might look like a visually bland game at first, but it is actually a very good quake like or "Boomer shooter" that has really good movement and gunplay. The visual style is dreary and takes place in a soviet era nation which is why every thing looks so bland and depressing, a common theme and artstyle among slavic devs or games inspired by slavic cultures. However despite taking inspiration from that sort of depressing and dreary style, the game is filled with a good amount of humor and silliness. The aesthetic never really gets old or jarring and works decently well, and despite the limited color palette it's easy to tell things apart from one another.The sound design is a bit of a mixed bag though. The music is very good and atmospheric, and the overall ambient noises work quite well. However some of the other sound design, particularly for some of the weapons sounds pretty weak, making them sound like airsoft guns. Enemy noises and grunts do a good job of letting you know when they're around, and mostly sound distinct from one another so just from sound you can tell what enemies are nearby or just spawned.For gameplay the game does a good mix of arena and exploration combat, there are plenty of secrets to be found and enemies to fight along the way. It does do the gameplay loop of having to find keys and usually you'll have new enemies spawn when you get to them to make sure the map isnt just empty while you're going to the proper door, ensuring you are reliably fighting enemies. This doesn't always work well however as there are several points where you'll press a button or get a key and enemies will spawn right next to you, which can feel a little cheap.Overall though for $20 as of this review, this is a very good game that's a lot of fun and feels pretty replayable.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This certainly was unique and had character. There's the 90's shooter nostalgic theme, but with modern game design principles, and more coherent/lucid level design than Quake (and the magical ability for things to rotate/spin from Quake 2). It doesn't take itself too seriously, which will be quickly evident, with lots of little Easter eggs, secrets and achievements.And brown. It's obligatory for a review to mention brown.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Every single enemy encounter in episode 2 is bound to ambushes or spawns after flicking a switch/picking keys up. On top of every enemy being too tanky. A snake takes 3 grenades, a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bat takes like 2 shotgun hits. Because of this tankiness, every weapon feels terrible and like a toy, the biggest crime in a FPS. Episode 1 was one of the biggest surprises. It had ambushes too, but at least it had some roaming enemies and gameplay that was more than keeping your finger over the quicksave button. Another janky Ivan set in an post-apocalyptic world. Nope.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant shooter with lots of heart poured into it, extremely atmospheric with everything from the guns to the flavour text of the news clippings matching the ex Soviet block setting that the game nails so effortlessly.Level design is brilliant, with looping levels returning to previously explored areas (usually with a new gimmick or some new enemies added in) and keyhunting that feels just like the good ol' days.Buy it, play it, get addicted to it. From Česko with love.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: They have just released episode 2, so in total it's a good 5 or 6 hours of play (included say half an hour on endless) hence there's already enough content to justify the purchase even if on Early Access. And the content, is spectacular. The level design is great, graphics are good, sound effects and music is top notch, mechanics are super - in my opinion it's one of the best retro shooters since Dusk (from which it borrows quite a bit, and it's not a bad thing).
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This game is impressive in how fluid it ended up being, adding such great mechanics that show mastery in design within classic boomer shooters like these. The developer adding random small goofy bits like a game-and-watch-like toy and random instruments shows me pure passion within developing this game, and I greatly respect such details which show care in development. The game? Incredibly fun and well made. It isn't a short game but playing it on Hard made it challenging and had me learn the mechanics and use all given weapons, even the mines which weren't that useful. The shotguns are very balanced, and plays very well despite being thrown towards the tanky enemies constantly. The constant switching between the normal combat shotgun for a slightly longer range and the double barrel for big damage has always been a staple, and this game doesn't sell short in utilizing that. The grenades are way too loose, but they are fun to use and the game makes them unbelievably accessible due to being able to right click to throw a grenade all the time and it can be used spectacularly in the middle of playing. The sickle and wine are straightforward, one increases HP and the other is fast melee. I think that if the grenades didn't take up a spot in the hotbar it would have been a little better since it's on your right click no matter what, but that's a small nitpick honestly. The map design is really good, very brown but that fits the theme it likes to give off. Secrets have been hidden well, and I feel very rewarded when finding any secrets despite never being able to find all secrets in a level. The bosses are just boomer shooter bosses, mostly shoot until death but that keeps them pretty fun though they aren't much to ride home about except how long and difficult the final boss was. I don't recommend playing this on anything higher than Normal, but since I love myself a challenge I went to Hard which made the enemies real tanked. All in all, this is an impressive game made within a specially made engine which had me excited from the start and still excited after finishing it, I recommend this game for those who usually like boomer shooters.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Even though only Episode 1 is complete, this is a completely awesome game. Plenty of references to Dusk and classic FPS games, but it creates a moody, spooky atmosphere that is uniquely its own. Like many of them, the story is minimalist, but after playing through a couple of times, you begin to see where it's heading. The Soviet-era world is convincingly portrayed (at least to these western eyes) with lots of cool unobtrusive details that never feel tacked-on or superfluous. The level design for E1 is very tight, and you will find yourself grabbing a key in proximity to the next point of progression, so it's not difficult to find your way around. Well worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Now at first glance, this game looks like a soviet Quake but its not. It reminds a lot of Quake in how ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ brown everything is, but it's so much more. This game is awesome, and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ weird. Possessed Excavators, cursed horses with gas masks, inanimate objects that shoot rockets as bosses, and the weirdest yet kind of fitting final boss, this game has it all.The weapons are pretty standard, you have you pistol(s), shotgun, machine gun, super shotgun, rocket launcher, and a BFG that is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ridiculous and makes the sky thunder when used. Both shotguns have weird and janky animations and are probably the two worst things in the whole game. (After the sewer level...) You'd think that a game this brown would end up being bad but it fits, because the best part of Hrot is its atmosphere. Instead of banging tunes hyping you up as you plough through the levels, you get an eerie atmospheric soundtrack - again, reminiscent of Quake - that is actually really effective. All enemies look cursed as hell with their gas masks and hazmat suits. Especially the horse, don't get me started on that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ horse...I can't wait to see what episode 2 holds, so support this game!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Game has finally come out of early access as a full release and is an easy recommend for anybody interested in 'boomer shooters'. The setting is very unique and the enemies are weird but memorable. Despite the lack of an actual plot being told, the overall experience makes up for it. Great stuff, I've recommended this since the early days with a single map and it's great to see the finished product.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Slav Quake is pretty great so far, looking forward to the rest of the episodes.First episode is roughly 1-3 hours give or take depending on how good you are and how much secret hunting you will do.Theres also a fun endless mode but its a bit slow going at the start for my taste.Pros:-Gunplay isnt explosive but it feels good overall-Once you get into the rhythm of how it plays it has rock solid pacing-Unique STALKER-esque setting really goes to show the game doesnt need to do anything crazy in its mechanics to be good-Atmosphere is fantastic, really has that horror feel a lot of more zaney and action packed boomer shooters are missing-Really solid music-While not super challenging (which is fine honestly) I love the variety and frequency of the boss fights-Fantastic enemy variety and pretty solid AI-Good amount of content for just an EACons:-You will be at low health often (or at least I was) which is fine but the heartbeat sound effect can get incredibly grating after awhile especially when you are trying to explore-Sometimes where to go is incredibly vague, albeit not ever frustratingly but it could stand to be slightly better communicated (good luck figuring out how that gorilla works)A+ Early Access so far!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I've ever played. Not just for the shooting, where the movement is fun, the weapons are well varied and the enemies are all fun to fight. But the atmosphere and setting of this game are second to none. Yes, there are games that are more intense or have punchier guns but I can't think of a time when I've been as open mouthed at what I'm seeing on the screen as in this game. Loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the game, but it's very top heavy in terms of quality. The first episode is very strong with a good theme and level design, but by the third episode the game has completely lost focus and starts throwing memes and movie references at you. It's all very strange.I would still recommend the game as the level design is still good and the first episode is well worth playing.  7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing 90's inspired FPS. Its immediately apparent how much love and care went into faithfully recreating the look and feel of a retro shooter, so much so that there were genuine moments that I felt like I was playing something that I somehow missed when I was growing up.From the get-go the game just oozes style. The quake-style low poly art paired with the dour post-apocalyptic setting is a match made in heaven and really goes a long way to evoke an oppressive and haunting feeling while playing. The gameplay is pure old school; you run and gun with no reloading, levels are labyrinthine and filled with enemies, and there are tons of secrets to uncover. There is even a respectable amount of interactivity with the environment, not unlike what you would find in Duke 3D.The game is in early access, but don't let that deter you. What is available to play is incredibly solid with the promise of more to come. With that I give this a high recommendation, if this is your style of game you wont be disappointed in the least.UPDATE: After now finishing the full release, I can say that the developers delivered an amazing experience, with each new episode topping the last. It was a joy to experience, so much so that I went back and got all the achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: If you ever wanted Quake to be set in an Eastern Block country, this game is definitely for you! In fact, I myself didn't know I wanted it, until I actually played it!The action is fast-paced, the weapons are satisfying, enemies are diverse and fun. Loved the secrets and references. The final level was freaking cool!I want more!!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Very competent retro FPS, there's really not much to say other than it's exactly what you think it is. If I had to offer some slightly esoteric praise then I'd say that I often pronounce a lot of films and games as not as smart as they think they are, however HROT is not only as smart as it thinks it is, I would say it's smarter.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty good old-school shooter in the vein of quake with a very specific (and to me, entertaining) sense of humor. It's not the best of the bunch, but it's solid. The enemy variety is good and keeps things fresh episode to episode (many staple enemies combined with various few level specific ones). The weapon variety is ok; it's perhaps too similar to quake and I wish it had one or two oddball weapons. The level design ranges from great to average in most cases, but a few levels feel like samey mazes. Also the secrets often suck, as while a lot of them are well thought out, equally as many of them feel very "original Wolfenstein" inspired (mash the use button on walls). I will say my time is mainly due to secret hunting and achievements, as otherwise the game isn't too long (though I think the price is appropriate to its length).Overall, if you liked quake or dusk, I don't think you can go wrong with this.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I went in expecting 'STALKER meets DOOM' and instead got a love-letter to Czechia and Czech culture. (I say Czech here as opposed to Czechoslovakian as most of the guides explaining the cultural references stated it was more Czech cultural references. Apologies for any offence).It's fun, most of the levels are enjoyable, but there's no real 'WOW' moment like in Dusk with the Escher labs. Really, the most interesting thing about the levels is that they are mostly based on real places which is neat.It doesn't take itself too seriously, level 2 you'll fight a gorilla with rocket launchers for hands and the games iconic enemy is a horse with a gas mask named after a Czech legend about a leaping horse.The weaponry is fine, most weapons are okay and have a purpose HOWEVER, the super shotgun is completely overpowered and really ruins the games difficulty curve (it one hit kills most enemies in the game and deals more damage than the rocket launcher). The game can be quite stingy with health, until it starts giving you so much wine (a portable medkit) it makes it kinda hard to die (I will add I played in Normal only, so maybe that's to be expected that is was kinda easy).The colour scheme is hard to discuss, it is mostly brown, but that drab colour scheme goes well for a game set in a Soviet republic. I can understand why some people might think it's ugly, but I think it works.Overall, a fun shooter, pick it up and enjoy being baffled by being attacked by medieval wagons, a pommel horse that shoots rockets or a statue of an old woman and then reading a guide to see what is going on and learning something about another country.EDIT: I should also mention this game allows you to poop in toilets then flush them.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Yet another Retro FPS. You would think I would tire of them, but I only Hunger for more. Game definitely needs some polish, but for the most part is a solid foundation. The atmosphere is great and is essentially 50 shades of brown with a dash of red . Guns are pretty standard, only missing a . Levels currently offer a balanced mix of close quarters, underground and surface areas, with some interiors. HROT currently has 1 Episode, containing 8 missions and 4 bosses. It took me about 4 hours to beat the game on Hard while goofing around and looking for secrets. Bosses are pretty easy and simple. HROT is somewhat of a key and button hunter, but most are located in pretty obvious and not maliciously hidden. My biggest gripe, which is personal preference, I despise monster closets and sudden hot drops of enemies. But when the rest of the game is solid, I cant let a personal preference stop me from playing this. Also, the game is really, really brown.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Boomer shooter. You know what you're getting. It's good. It's a little cheap sometimes with its jump-scares that make you take damage. Especially on the hardest difficulty. Small complaint though. Weird but cool soviet Czech aesthetic? Very brown, but it works to my eyes. Has some good atmosphere to it too because the music is good. There's a lot of different enemies, but not a whole lot of variety in how you handle them, I guess. I know that's somewhat typical, but still felt it was worth mentioning. Get it.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a real gem for 90's 'boomer shooter' people, with an atmosphere that will let you quickly understand you're lost in Nucular Apocalyptica. It plays and feels a lot like Quake or Chasm: The Rift (in the current stage of development, it's more like the latter), but it has its very own and unique background story, and it plays in our real world, in an alternate reality setting.There are frequent updates with new maps, features and bug-fixes by the game's developer, making for its own satisfying experience.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: While I fully intend to play the third episode when it comes out, I have to be honest. I have a lot of problems with this game in it's current state.-For one, your character feels simultaneously heavy and floaty. It's hard to explain. The jump is very weak and only seems to go 4 inches off the ground yet you're still able to make the landing or just float up to a slightly elevated platform. I'm not quite sure if it's bad or just strange and awkward . In regards to the shooting, many of the guns feel very soft and not impactful. With the exception of the explosive weapons I feel as though I'm shooting cotton balls at my target instead of hot lead whether it gibs them or not. The smg especially feels underpowered and the sound effects are quite weak.The enemies are cool and fit the setting extremely well (which is good too) they just seem pretty dumb. Sometimes, they'll kind of zig zag up to you for a couple seconds before deciding to shoot at you. Their attacks have little feedback so It does't always make it like I'm actually taking damage. Despite their attacks feeling weak when they connect, enemies just SHRED your armor and since armor is quite rare you'll spend most of the game unprotected. Healing via drinking wine is great, but I just wish there were more health and armor pickups in the levels so i'm not constantly smashed and staggering around. Enemies also have a very frustrating habit of spawning right on top of you during an arena battle, but that's for later. In addition to being dumb, most enemies are easy to kill so you'll only have trouble if you're fighting many at once or if the environment is working against you. -Which brings me to the level design. Hrot has an amazingly grimy and creepy setting, added to by the eerie ambiance. For the most part, the levels are real-world locations repurposed  into competently designed fps environments which feel lived in, but now abandoned. Issues arise when you and your enemies can just clip right through railings and other such obstacles. Enemies can also just shoot you from atop or below a grated floor, and compounded with the fast-paced shooting and (let's be honest) super-brown aesthetic, you're gonna have a hard time locating the target before you get a facefull of bullets and bombs. The game also relies far too much on traps. It feels like just breathing causes walls to lower and for you to get blindsided by some weak monsters that you had no way of seeing coming. This is especially egregious in episode 2 in which nearly every level is jam-pack with traps that just serve to take a chunk of your health off. -Arena combat is also poorly handled. Normally in a shooter with arena battles, the game waits until the player is inside the arena before filling it with monsters. And when new monsters are spawned in, there's clear audio and visual cues to indicate this has happened. Hrot spawns in monsters constantly with no such easily-recognizable cues. This is made worse by the fact that new monsters just spawn in out of nowhere once the first wave has been dispatched, which can cause the player to have monsters spawn right on top of them so that they take unavoidable damage. -There are some really frustrating/annoying design choices as well. I fell like the game uses collapsing floors a bit too often and it starts to loose it's impact and surprise after the fifth in the same episode. The underground levels especially were quite painful. There is an enemy in the bestiary that's literally just a boulder that will, without fail, instantly kill you on contact. Just run away, right? WRONG, bucko. I was running away from a boulder when i dove into a room on my right, thinking the boulder would roll past the doorway so I could proceed. But, much to my horror, the ROCK did a 90 degree turn INTO THE ROOM and UP THE STAIRS to splatter me. It was funny in retrospect, but it also felt like I was unfairly killed for no reason. On my second try I dove into the water below a metal bridge and the boulder was nice enough not to grow gills and swim after me. I can only conclude this was the intended way to do this sequence. Really just a boulder-shaped bruh moment. -Episode two did have one absolutely superb level. Granny's Valley was cool for a plethora of reasons. Giving the player a brief driving segment with other vehicles made the world feel more alive. The level leans heavily into the horror themes of the game by building up the boss with a book and a few notes scattered throughout. The jumpscare in the catacombs took me by surprise, and the way the statue stares at me through the window in the house was extra haunting. It goes to show that this game can take advantage of it's setting and mood to set up a daunting encounter. I just hope in the future the dev doesn't come to rely on jumpscares. one was enough. The final level was also amazing.-If nothing else, Hrot consistently finds new ways to surprise me and keep me guessing, which isn't something many games could do. Not since DUSK have exclaimed "WTF IS THAT". or "WTF IS GOING ON" with genuine interest. I hope this game gets better because there's a ton to like but it's being dragged down by so many issues. I will follow this game with great interest. I paid good money for it, after all.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I picked up this game seeing it was something I liked; which was a Quake/Hexen style retro shooter. The main issue I have with this game is really the tone it gives off; reading the description I expected something serious, with perhaps horror elements. And while it delivered that in the beginning, slowly the game stopped taking itself seriously, as if the devs got bored of the world they were making? It felt thematically similar to Stalker, and I figured with the screenshots and description this would be a horror shooter. What I got was a boss fight consisting of a playground gorilla and a living pommel horse. It began getting really stupid, especially since the armor consisted of wifebeaters. I thought this game was Polish, not Finnish. It just felt like clashing tones that you dont get from other retros. Even Duke Nukem in its humor atleast felt consistent. This felt like whiplash. Do not buy this if you're looking for a serious ambient experience like I was, but if you enjoy just shooting stuff, by all means the game is generally fine in that regard.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decent boomer shooter nothing too special. The setting is the standout of the game but the levels do blend together because of the color palette. The soundtrack is ok but basic. Enemy variety is pretty good. There should have been a lot more weapons there's only like 7 total and they are all pretty standard weapons with no uniqueness to them. One of the bosses is stupid because it needs to fall down stairs.6/10
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: A wholly unique experience among modern retro shooters! From the visuals (don't let the brownness scare you away), to the Czech setting and crazy gimmicks found in every level. It's most reminiscent of those janky but ambitious FPS titles you'd see from Eastern Europe, but infused with so much creativity and clear passion that you just can't help but love it! If you think Quake meets S.T.A.L.K.E.R. turned up to 11 on the goofy-scale sounds fun at all, then I simply can't recommend this enough!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun shooter with a good amount of challenge, cool aesthetic and brilliant atmosphere. The enemies are all unique and have cool designs. The guns are satisfying to use, despite them sounding a bit off. The level design is interesting, with each level being fun to go through and explore.Overall this a good game and considering it is in early access it should only get better.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Best Orloj Simulator on the market right know. The detail of simulation for the clock is amazing! Intricate animations, switching times, adjusting for moons and of course the most important bit - the apostle procession!  Good thing one can scare the pigeons off before they foul the grand square as well.10/10 clock experience.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic retro-inspired shooter, feeling reliably authentic to the era it is throwing back to. While the gunplay is good, the setting and aesthetic are what help elevate this game above it peers. If you enjoy Chasm or Dusk, this game will be very enjoyable.(Reviewed build as of 2/13/21, Episode 1 available)9/10 currently, would flee from gas mask horse all day
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Played through the first episode and for an early access title it definitely shows a lot of promise. The atmosphere and level design is pretty good with a lot of mystery to everything going on including the enemies which some are really odd, you'll see what I mean. The weapons are decent and satisfying to use, you can even run over enemies with a motorcycle. Its crazy that this game was written on such an old coding language as well but yet it seemed to work out really well as the game looks straight out of the 90s, no fancy unity filters this time. Even though there is one episode, I would recommend this if you are a fan of quake 1, chasm the rift, or half life as this game feels like a mash up of those titles, still overall another nice classic homage to 90s shooters. Also I learned how to make Beef Stroganoff because of this game :D Cheeki Breeki out of 10 Cyka Blyat rush B
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: So it's over. Finishing good games makes me sadge. HROT is quite something. Most games these days go for the abrasive, colorful look. This game is not afraid to be brown. I'm Polish and although I'm not familar with the history of Czechoslovakia, at times I felt at home. Mad respect for the custom engine written in Pascal - my slow computer appreciates that. All in all, a pleasant boomer shooter full of surprises, great level design, and sense of humor. Looking forward for the next one from the creator - whatever that may be!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of my favourite games to come out of the boomer shooter revival. The reason being that most new games in the genre tend to feel over-designed, having lots of fancy mechanics that create bloat without really stepping out of their predecessor's shadow. Hrot is a simple game with simple visuals, making it a very convincing throwback, and it's better for it. Despite looking like Quake, its gameplay has more in common with Doom, given the lack of vertical movement and abundance of traps. The levels are often cramped, which makes combat tense and exciting. Unlike Doom, however, the game is actually scary.From what I've played so far it doesn't seem to do anything groundbreaking, and there are some flaws, but what's there is really fun.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it from the moment I started playing it. It's tense, bleak, and downright claustrophobic in certain areas, but that's what keeps me coming back for more. Similar games have trouble with enemy placement when it comes to switching between open areas and tight corridors; they'll haphazardly fill a hallway with enemies strictly for the challenge of it while your arsenal is full to bursting. HROT focuses more on keeping you armed, but not comfortably so, sprinkling enough enemies in the appropriate environments to keep you on your toes. Cockiness is costly, especially on higher difficulties. The color palette and gunplay are very Quake-like, but unlike Quake, the world feels like it could actually exist (also, the shotgun is usually a make or break weapon for me when it comes to boomer shooters, and the shotgun in this game absolutely rocks).The only con for me would be the enemy jumping, which can be jarring at times. If an enemy is below you, and there is a platform of any height in front of them, they will continuously try to jump onto it, even if it's five or ten feet above them. Sometimes they make it, sometimes they don't, but either way it can be a little distracting in the middle of a fight.Overall great game. If you're into boomer shooters, this is a fine pick (I'd personally rate this above Wrath).
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: To the Point==========================Fantastic Boomer Shooter for any fan of the genre, blending horror and humor with tight controls.Good Stuff==================- Played the game on hard and it was extremely well balanced- A fast, responsive shooter that's very simple ( this could be seen as a negative to some). No leveling up weapons or skill trees, just get out there and start shooting- Unique and interesting atmosphere, the real and surreal blend quite wellBad Stuff====================- A little rough looking, not at the level of something like Wrath - Small roster of weapons even if the ones you have are all very solid- Some extremely well hidden secrets (some people might love this)- Took me 9 hours to finish on hard, that's a fine length of time but I wish there was more
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Visually it looks great, I really like the dark and gritty style. Game play is good too if you like old styled shooters, reminds me a bit of Unreal Tournament 2004. I had a few issues where the game constantly crashed on me for no reason but now it seems to be fixed.Beat the game at last, and gotta say the boss fights are real fun, and when you finally beat it, you will be rewarded with something incredible. Must play.Edit: The Beef Stroganoff, 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Did you ever want a slav quake? No? Well you do now. Solid and well priced. Boomer shooters tend to have fantasy or sci-fi elements to them but this is a more grounded and fresh take on the genre. Take that with a grain of salt, considering there's bulldozers that try to murder you and a chairmen from the Czechoslovakian communist party that comes back to life as the final boss.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best boomer shooters out there.The atmosphere is tight - both thanks to the great ambient soundtrack and well-designed locations (especially further into the game), weapons feel great to shoot and you're always low on ammo - which I see as a plus.HROT may feel a little underwhelming at first, but as you progress, the closer to DUSK-level quality it gets.Play it!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Nice, charming and fluid retro shooter game that has quite the appeal especially for Czech audience.+ Fluid, smooth gunplay and movement you would expect from a shooter like this.+ Excellent weapon variety. Not too many but those that are there are all useful.+ Graphics, artstyle and music is excellent.+ The biggest plus for me personally is all the communist Czechoslovakia imagery.+ Game is well priced for what it offers. Decent length, doesnt overstay its welcome.+ Runs very well on everything.+ I liked the interactivity. You can ride a bike, interact with many many things.- I felt like bossfights were all easy. I had more trouble with some enemy groups than with bosses.- Sometimes enemies can nuke you almost unfairly but its nothing major.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Hrot is weird, at least to my own Western sensibilities. Admittedly, a lot of what might be subtle jabs at the communist past of Czechoslovakia is missed by myself. Except for the kiss. The sounds could use some beefing up, save for the shotguns.However, there's no questioning the retro-shooter that Hrot has at its core. It's pretty damn good. The industrial communist locale combined with some pretty great horror elements and solid shooting mechanics make this one nothing revolutionary, but something tried, true, and dependable. It has a good arsenal of weapons that are pretty well balanced and weapon switching to save ammo will be a great way to maintain a leg up.  And yes, the pump action is pumping wrong, no one friggin' cares.Some will may take umbrage with the abundance of brown, but the game is setting a very particular atmosphere. It wants you to feel like you're in an industrial wasteland, with your surroundings feeling both alien and familiar. It does this with aplomb and you learn to love its dreary and washed out aesthetic for this reason. The ambiance is what really completes the experience. What would be otherwise ugly visuals are made appreciable with the music and sound design. It's like salt or vinegar in a video game, here. I've never seen the effect music and sound can have on a game so profoundly demonstrated before. Map design can feel a bit dated at times, but it's never too awful. It makes you want Spytihněv to further flesh out the world and what has happened to make it go so horribly wrong.UPDATE 10-15-2021, The first two levels of the new episode are showing off map design that is really good. Also, credit where it's absolutely due, this dude made an engine that's specifically designed to look like it's being rendered in 1990s software rendering. He has accomplished it and then some.Even MORE props, Spytihněv has a DEMO FOR YOU TO TRY. A demo. In 2021. The fact that he's released a demo in a day and age when developers (read PUBLISHERS) don't want you trying it until after you've parted with your money says a lot. Spytihněv clearly believes in his product and while it doesn't mean Hrot deserves a purchase, it should deserve a look.It's pretty great and it's worth the purchase.Voted GOTY because the industry should be ashamed with the crap it puts out, now.UPDATE: 5-16-2023The game is now finished. Is it worth it? Is it worth it after years of development?YES, IT'S AWESOME. GET IT. The last episode gets even more twisted and weird than the previous entries and it makes for a bizarre but fun time. Perhaps call this Spytihněv's Bizarre Adventure?Either way, it's complete and well worth getting. This is a quality FPS.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is a great game.The ambiance is weird and surreal, it doesn't take itself too seriously, and I like that.The Eastern European aesthetic clearly helps the surreal feeling of this universe.This is the first "boomer shooter" that felt like it was made back then.I love the unique enemies each episode has. Their designs are creepy and interesting, very recognizable, and sometimes a little silly. (I love horses though)All in all, I cannot exaggerate how much I recommend playing HROT. It was an incredible experience, and I will be getting all the achievements!I hope to one day be able to 3d model for a fun project like this :)Great job to the devs, well done :) <3 <3 <3

_childDocuments_.review: Pair this up with Cultic and you have a bundle of some genuinely awesome boomer shooters within the past year. Takes a lot of guts to try to design fun water segments in basically every level, and it succeeds on every front. I'm in love with the weird as hell enemies with gas masks that just get progressively weirder.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: IT'S OUT OF EARLY ACCESS, BABY!!! And it's better than ever! The last episode is soul-tearing, finger-licking good. All of them are, but these people just can't stop surpassing themselves with every iteration.When mosquitoes get sufficiently bloated with blood and turn into Party leaders, ghastly swamp lights, the stars of Kremlin, appear over the muddy waters. When these corrupt servants of tetanus drag enough gurgling victims down into the mass grave of black sludge, the palace of torture rises from the bog. With its bricks made of porous raw meat, and dark secrets weeping within its premises. The wandering graveyard flagellates the surrounding lands, grimacing on its defiling path. On the bones of the grieving, it feasts, distorting the nature of man, perverting the very concept of good intent, turning spring waters into vinegar to dip people in like dumplings. Rolling in loops of ruthless violation, the breaking wheel was created of rot, yet it never crumbles, only flakes. Nurtured on its mastitis milk, when someone hands you a loaded gun and points in any direction, you ask no questions. Tebe davno pohui.Here's HROT, an uncompromising mockery of the Soviet nomenclature and its exploits, a malicious parody based on disturbing authenticity, an absurdist hyper-reality of all overgrown socialistic establishments. Of their mercantile militarism, totalitarian autocracy, and imperialistic toxicity. Going through the Soviet underbelly guns blazing even just on Hard, not Very Hard, is an enterprise for the brave. I found it challenging yet not entirely masochistic. Time after time, I died in its hellish corpse mounds with a guilty hard-on, sipping on the noxious bile they secrete like it's Heaven's nectar.To highlight a couple of things before we go on, HROT has the coolest multi-layered skyboxes ever, the rest you can see on your own. But I gotta note that there's a world of difference between works that look like crap because an artist is a hack, and HROT, every stroke of brush in which reflects immaculate taste and truly cunningly expressed intent. The latter is the most important thing about art to me, I  don't care for "just pretty". Or "just ugly", for that matter. And however painstaking a vapid creation may be, something as resonant as the game wipes its hairy ass with it. The sounds have the oomph, but there's no music. It was replaced with static, dripping, droning, humming, and every little thing works as potent steroids, force-fed to the Herculean atmosphere of this rust golem.In terms of gameplay, it's a classic. You're a rat of many mazes, looking for doors and keys, oppressed by the resource scarcity... or deficit, to be more authentic. I think there were but a couple of moments since the first level when I had full health for a few seconds, and I could never afford to waste ammo. To fight for every crumb like a homeless man battles a stray dog for a rotten chicken leg is how I like it. This made discovering hidden stashes an alluring prospect, a necessity, not a mere completionist endeavor. And are they challenging to find in this game! Typically, I was able to uncover a third of secrets on any given level, seldom more. Unapparent buttons, fuse boxes in weird places, tricky acrobatics, you name it. HROT's developers come from the oldest of schools, especially when it comes to deviousness.The levels are all familiar places like a gymnasium, palace of culture, mausoleum, or a uranium mine. Try googling the latter, the sights are grim and morbidly fascinating. I keep hearing that something is industrial, was never quite sure what it meant. Now, I can say without a doubt, that I've witnessed the apogee of industrialism in every sense of the word. Even more so than Quake, Dusk, or You Are Empty. The level design reflects the claustrophobia of squeezing through the queues of the enormous Empire of Hostility. It always maintained the same rhetoric, sneeringly proclaiming World Peace through the clenched teeth. So, French-kiss your current Leader's portrait and enter the vile dimension, in which every elevator shaft leads to Hell, the only bar is perpetually out of beer, and where my childhood memories, doubling as my deepest fears, come to life. A life to shoot on sight.The enemies reflect the themes. Soldiers choking on vomit in their gas masks, bulky ogres in riot gear, bears to burn, БЕЗНОГNМ, demon horses, helicopters, ovcharki, homing Indiana Jones' boulders, and more. Spin on a carousel when it's not occupated by an occasional gorilla and watch out for that  in the school gym! Surrealism meets kitchen sink, an angry take on the kind of normalization that gives grotesque a run for its money. What's extremely commendable is that some foes are unique and only appear in certain levels, or are just very rare. You don't see it in your usual AAA titles anymore, where they always make an attempt to milk every asset, going as far as suggesting you push a button not to miss someone's carefully made set piece. HROT is the opposite of that approach, it doesn't care if its effort goes unseen since it's a bloody freight train of unstoppable inspiration.Except for being a gimmick for the pistols, there's no reloading. Finally! Some retro-shooters just get it, reloading was never a necessity in a world of uncanny artistic abstractions. The shotgun is great, the double-barrel is impeccable. Like the game's explosives, it leaves you soaked in clouds of blood and tushonka, drooling. Everything feels just right, just the way a grimy 90s shooter must be made. Like with that vomiting in a gas mask (sorry, no space for descriptions of tortures), there's a little story behind every piece. Take the Bolt Lightning Gun, the local BFG, for example. Bolt Lightning was a Soviet SCP of sorts, and it sure featured some grimdark lore to scare the kids! I remember being fascinated and horrified by tales about it hovering in through the window leaf and frying someone's ass. Some said it looked like a small Sun, some made up even stranger things. To have the legend in my hands, and with this context to boost, felt like bliss.So did this game, at large. Intentionally ugly, brutal, fast-paced, and containing so much raw, uncut emotion within, it presented me with a meaningful, inspiring experience, both in terms of its gameplay and setting. Despite being in Early Access, having 2 out of 3 episodes ready so far, it's a feature-full game. And it isn't janky at all! Not a single bug or glitch bothered me throughout. HROT isn't a mock-up, nor is it a mimicry, and it wasn't over-corrected to fit the present. It could've genuinely been a lost shooter from a bygone era, an actual cult hit in the 90s. But instead, it chose to be that now, when we need it the most. I award it as many medals as its sunken chest can hold.My curator
