_childDocuments_.review: Since I’m not trying to play every classic FPS of this new wave in the genre revival (especially since a lot of them are not good), I don’t pay attention to many of them as they pop up. HROT, though, had a curious style and a… “vibe”, I guess, that got me curious about the project back in 2021 when it was still in Early Access. Now that the full game is out and I had a chance to shotgun my way through it, I gave it a go and… Yeah, it’s quite odd, but mostly in a good way.While this title seems to draw most inspiration from Quake, there are plenty of identifiable other influences as well. The interactivity on the levels is closer to build engine games (specifically Duke Nukem 3D), there are a couple of Half-Life aspects here and there. But the visual style and overall feel of the combat is indeed closest to the original Quake, which is a great reference to stick with as it still feels great.But the game built on this clearly “influenced by” foundation is very different and… quite odd. In a way, it suffers from the classic shareware FPS issue of the first Episode (of three) being the most cohesive and well done. Not that the two remaining Episodes are bad, but they rather quickly stop giving a damn about any kind of logical connections and visual and “narrative” cohesion and become, at times, completely surreal. It starts as something like You Are EMPTY, but done well – a game with a clear style and theme, rather pure approach to classic level design, refined for the tastes of 2023 audience. But then turns into a mishmash of unfinished ideas, levels that are build as a one giant reference to something, levels that have a weird gimmick, sudden jumpscare-filled horror themed levels and whatever else that came to the developers’ minds. I can’t even begin to describe what state of confusion I was for the majority of Episode 3.It does play quite well most of the time. There are crappier (and usually, but sadly not always, one-off) enemy types, there are levels that get confusing and there are weapons that don’t feel as great as one would expect them to be (or they feel great but rarely get ammo pickups). But most of the time, it is full of fun combat encounters, cool shooting and exciting exploration. And it’s great that most (if not all) levels remain fully backtrackable right until you press a button to finish a level.Quite possibly, a lot of references, jokes and just things will be lost to many players who don’t know much about Czech history or didn’t live in the Eastern Europe when Soviet Union still existed. For me, being a Ukrainian born during that time, I did recognize a lot of things that were same or similar to my own experiences or were related to products or things that were imported from Czechoslovakia. But I also had to look up a lot of things afterwards just to understand what was that all about. Like one of the levels that’s based around a famous Karel Čapek novel that I haven’t read myself, or the nuances of the Hussite movement that I had only superficial knowledge of. It’s odd, honestly, how the game is chock-full of such things, but seemingly more just to have them instead of trying to share a story or give any kind of judgement to the era it references. It’s more about “vibes” and “member berries”. Apart from the bosses, I suppose, though even the game is more bizarre than pointed.HROT is not going to be a title I’d be recommending on the same level as DUSK or even AMID EVIL. It won’t have the same appeal as Prodeus either and, weirdly enough, even Chop Goblins might be easier to recommend because of how approachable and simple that game is. Already mentioned You Are EMPTY, for how poor its design was quite often, is also easier to understand, I feel, without a reference and strangeness overload that HROT might have. But nonetheless, I can easily recommend this game as for all its occasional poor decisions and for how surreal it becomes, not always in a good way, it’s a really fun game that understands the basics of a classic FPS design really well.

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is pretty unique in that it's an old-school FPS but unlike many of its kind, its level design is much more claustrophobic. Normally I wouldn't like such a thing but when the game opens up into wider open areas and spawns a bunch of enemies, those enemies already hit hard enough in close quarters that seeing so many in one area ramps up the tension by 10. The music is mostly ambient and lends itself greatly to the oppressive atmosphere, as everything is some shade of brown or grey. Secrets are challenging and rewarding to find, and the weapons are satisfyingly punchy and impactful. The boss fights are sufficiently weird and challenging, and HROT manages to have spider enemies that actually creep me out. I can't wait for further episodes. Buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: I think I can likely lengthen the review whenever there is a full release of the game, but for now I can already say that I'm recommending the game. ✅  (e.g., you can play the piano and organ on some levels. There is also a handheld game that you can play. It's difficult but fun!)✅  The enemy variation changes from episode 1 to 2. It feels palpable and like it's part of the same world, but this was an important feature. I felt like episode 1 and 2 were different enough to where I felt like I was playing BLOOD. This was valuable to me. ✅  - This is obviously something that's just fun that the developer added in. It was a great way to test the different weapons that the game had available, and it was in a familiar setting that felt like it was very much one of the levels. There was a particular level of a church, and it felt like it was this level and a couple of other levels put together, and the enemy variation was mixed with this. ✅ - one of the questions that I'm always wondering whenever I get an early access game or a game that has been produced by a developer that doesn't have a lot of games out is "how much content is here?" And if I'm able to play it for a few hours, lose my sense of time, and realize I could go much, much more in depth and find all the little details in a game, then I am happy. If I feel like I am playing a game and it's difficult for me to look at it from a perspective of feeling like there's plenty to do, then there's somewhat of an issue. ❌ - All I felt was brown or some variation throughout the entire game. You get used to it, but it wasn't... aesthetically pleasing. I understand this has to do with the theme of the game somewhat, but it was also a point of frustration for me. ❌ - This was a little bit frustrating because it felt like the bosses were mostly similar. However I don't think that the bosses are the primary part of the game. I will say, the one boss that I found to be clever was the tank boss where you had to figure something out about it to be effective to defeat it.My point with all of this being said, though, is that I recommend this game! It's great. I like it and I can't wait to see further updates.

_childDocuments_.review: It would be too easy to dismiss HROT as a Soviet themed total conversion of Quake, but the game, however, is so much more. The game and its levels ooze atmosphere, the game dev clearly has a vision they're going for. Almost a must buy for any fan of retro-revival shooters (boomer shooters). As is, the game only has a single chapter available and is in Early Access, but personally I am more than happy to support a single-man project with a vision this strong and a clear drive to make a game that actually has an identity. The game runs fine (the game engine is very light and the title regularly reaches 1,000-1,200 FPS even with a lot of action on the screen) and there are no major game-breaking kinks, some oddities like hostile vehicles bleeding or killed turrets making monster sounds, but all of this can easily be forgiven seeing how stellar the rest of the offering is and how this is the first launch version of the title into Early Access.Personally I can't recommend HROT highly enough to fans of retro-revival FPS'es and will be keeping an eye on future chapters of the story and updates to the title. One of the best titles to launch (into early access) in 2021 thusfar, without a doubt!

_childDocuments_.review: At the first glance, this is a proper Quake 1 sequel we've been waiting for. But despite having great aesthetics and weapon selection, the game totally falls short in the level design department.John Romero said, "I had a rule for the designers that if they created a room in Quake and it could be replicated in Doom then they had failed". And it describes the problem of level design in HROT perfectly: the game totally ignores verticality and 3D aspect of space, its levels feel flat and boxy, and look like something that could be easily recreated in Doom. Even more, some retro shooters using Doom and Build engines (like Ion Fury and Hedon Bloodrite) have significantly better level design than HROT.I am also not a fan of combat design since almost every monster attacks you with very fast projectiles. This makes constantly strafing around the best tactic, but it quickly becomes boring and dull. It seems like the game creator didn't really think of introducing enemies with various attack patterns and then mixing them in different combinations to create unique fights. So every battle here starts feeling the same in mere minutes, especially when the game keeps spawning enemies at you almost every time you press a switch or take a key.Furthermore, the game just loves locking you up in a large room or an arena (always rectangular!) and spawning mobs around you. And all boss fights also follow the same pattern: you fight one big dude who has tons of HP and spawns adds. You might call it retro, I just call it lazy and bad design. I would rather have one boss fight in Quake over several boss fights in HROT. Seriously, bosses in Wolfenstein 3D were more fun than here. I approve of this decision, but this doesn't make the game good, and I won't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is surreal. Off the rocker. Engaging and highly enjoyable.A very good retro style FPS. Level design is superb. While the game is reminiscent of Quake 1, it keeps subverting expectations. Here's a clever puzzle, here's a curiosity, a surprise, then maybe a jump scare, an inside joke, or something bizarre. It never gets dull. Good stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is a bespoke and fascinating piece of work. It's a fun and interesting shooter with lots of replay value and easter eggs to find. It's also a nostalgia trip that relies not on rote repetition of things you've seen before like so much in "nostalgic" games, but rather a masterful distillation of the qualities of those things and what made them special and interesting at the time. HROT's nostalgia respects your intelligence, in other words. Combined with a poignant and powerful political message at the heart of its latter chapter especially, HROT is a game that truly reaches the standard of what I would call "art" in the videogame space.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, let´s be honest, I first thought that HROT would be just another retro shooter like so many others. But after having played through all three episodes now, I have to state that this is THE BEST Quake-like retro shooter since DUST. It´s even better than Prodeus, Wrath or Ion Fury (have played them all). The gameplay is very fluid and satisfying, the level design is AMAZING and the setting is very atmospharic and kind of fresh. Some people say that this is a spiritual successor to Chasm: The Rift, but believe me, this one is MUCH better than Chasm (which is just a mediocre, overrated shooter from the 90s, in my view). On the technical side, the game runs perfectly well, graphics are amazing (if you like low poly late 90 shooters) and quickloading is very, very fast (which I think is an essential aspect in a good retro shooter). So do not hesitate, this is a MUST BUY for retro shooter fans! Support these devs, because they are able to deliver the quality standards that games came up with in the 90s. _childDocuments_.review: Hrot is a game I really, really wanted to like, but feel really short for me. _childDocuments_.review: This is a great game, but it's definitely rough around the edges and has potential to be really great.I love the atmosphere of the game. All of it was great to reflect its setting, and I hope the devs expand upon this more.I do think this, just in case the devs read through the reviews here:1. Guns need some better sound effects to make them punchier, especially the machine gun2. Add a bit more enemy variety to fights. A lot of the time you're fighting the same enemy a little too often, and putting several enemy types in one fight would keep players on their toes3. The secrets are a little to simplistic and depend too much on finding cracks in the walls4. This may just be me, but I played on hard mode and found some enemies to be a little too passive, such as the dudes with the barrels and the shotgunners.This is just off the top of my head. I'd love to see levels centered around the Soviet space program, Chernobyl, or Ukrainian farmlands or Moscow ballet. If the devs want to keep the game in Czechoslovakia that's totally cool too, because I'm sure they could bring in more interesting real-world locations and historical figures. _childDocuments_.review: It's a fun shooter with a unique (and weird) premise. As of writing, only the first episode is complete, with the second episode having a few levels completed, giving a nice taste of what to expect. That's roughly 4 hours long.The game feels like a Quake and Build Engine hybrid, with some fun interactivity with props and Quake-like atmosphere and graphics.I think my only gripe is that the levels could use a bit more decoration. Really looking forward to it being completed.

_childDocuments_.review: Calling HROT "Quake but Soviet" is selling it short. It's so smooth. The level design and atmosphere are so good. This is the type of retro FPS that should be supported and celebrated.Funny how another certain retro shooter (one that shall not be named) went into early access 4 years ago, 2 years before HROT. It charged more than HROT, and offered less. That game is still not out and has seen no updates in years unless you get excited seeing biweekly dev updates showcasing those epic upcoming new vase textures whoop-de-doo! (Yeah, you know which game it is. Well done.)Why was all this relevant? Because on the other side of early access... you have good developers who know what they're doing like Gloomwood's, DUSK's, and of course... . (Presumably) One gigathad fueled by nothing but actual player feedback and vodka, pumping out  improvements and level after level on a consistent basis throughout 28 months of early access. When people point to the aforementioned poopy game as a reason why you should never get games in Early Access, HROT is one of the few that prove the opposite by simply saying "Actually, yes it can work".Good on you, Spytihněv. Vashe zdorov'ye.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like a breath of fresh air in a sea of mediocre old-school FPS throwbacks. Really cool level design with some genuinely scary moments, a lot of which is credited to the games sound design. As of writing this Part 1 is only out, which feels a bit steep for $20, although development on the rest of the parts is coming along quickly. If you like boomer shooters you'll eat this up.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: It's 1986 and there are far worse things lurking in Czechoslovakia than British stag parties, moustache or pickled veg. A solid indie shooter that combines the muddy brown and black pallette of mid 90's FPS like quake, to a distinctive Central European horror (believe me you will jump at times).Exceptional detail and interactivity:-> press "E" to kiss a photo of the communist leader-> flush toilets-> get a translation of any Czech writing you can see (delightful!)-> authentic Czech weaponry CZ-25 submachine gun, duel wielded CZ-52 pistols, hammer and sickle.Worth price of admission and hopefully much more to come too. Czech yourself before you wreck yourself!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: : Soviet-era Czechoslovakia and medieval Czechia. Rust, dirt, blood, and a myriad of brown textures worked great to make me feel dread in one level and spook me in another. Jumpscares felt out-of-place, though.: Easy bunnyhopping. High player speed and no hitscanners -- you can do a no-damage run on the highest difficulty. No fall damage for you -- ridiculous fall damage for your enemies. Use the kick button (mouse2) to reposition them, kick Ogres' grenades back, and save ammo, which is scarce in the first few levels of each episode.: HROT is a competent Quake clone, but like with all Quake clones, Level 1 is really similar to Level 30, gameplay-wise, and HROT can't do much to surprise you.

_childDocuments_.review: Terse version: If you are expecting a great retro shooter on par with Dusk or anything on the old guard, you'll be disappointed. HROT is short, fairly easy, and doesn't play how you might think it does. However, this is an experience designed purely for fans of the boomer shooter genre, and if you are one, then this is a must have.Verbose version: HROT feels a hybrid of part retro shooter, part horror game, and part ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game. It's memorable if nothing else, and it feels both horribly antiquated in some areas while being genuinely clever in others. I think overall the game is good, but exactly how good might depend on who you are and how you look at it. It's either a casual, short run with some funny immersive interactions, or it's an interesting masterwork that subverts expectations in small but noticeable ways while expertly making use of its own self-imposed limitations. It's also heavily wrapped in Russian memes, so there's an entire second level of lore to this game if you are willing to look a little past the language barrier.As for the content, the store front pages aren't hiding any tricks. The entire game is bathed in browns and blacks. Every level feels like it takes place in a sewer, and more than a few levels are actually sewers. We aren't at Cruelty Squad levels of avant-garde, but this game is deliberately ugly and weird. Moreso than something like Dusk, this game likes to fashion itself as a horror game from time to time, so some areas are also completely black save for the flashlight. It has a purpose and sets the mood though, and there are lots of interactive elements and fine visual touches scattered throughout the game that might be easily missed if you don't look past it's colors. The mood is set with various industrial ambient tracks that rise and fall with different action scenes, and it all works really well.The weapons are well balanced with the traditional pistol, shotgun, super shotgun, rocket, plasma, etc, and every piece feels useful. Enemies hit very hard and react fast, but most go down fast too. You'll be fully loaded on firepower for most of the game, which can make things a bit of a cakewalk sometimes. HROT knows how to catch the player out too though. Some enemies are smarter than you might think, and sometimes it can be downright nasty with throwing out ambushes in tight spaces or spawning monsters behind the player to force them out of cover if they are being too patient. Quick trigger fingers are a must.Between little sequences like that and playing with the weapon balance in interesting ways, the sewage visuals are more to the game's detriment than not. There are no huge memorable levels, and even after just finishing the game before writing this, I could not tell you which levels go in which order. The game rarely uses elevation well, and almost every assault encounter with enemies spawning takes place on a flat plane that feels mostly the same as the others. People expecting more might be left with a bad impression going into these encounters again and again.Summary: Even its few drawbacks somehow serve a purpose with how it controls the player's combat strength or how it sets up tension afterwards. It's hard to put into words exactly how well HROT toys with boomer shooter traditions without playing it yourself. If you aren't a fan of this stuff, you may want to approach it with an open mind and the knowledge that it is steeped in hard-to-get memes. If you are, it's a fun experience. Solid recommend for retro shooter collectors.

_childDocuments_.review: This title is a masterpiece. I played the game when it only had one chapter and I already had a weakness for the game back then. But I didn't know what plans the developers had for the game and they brought the game to near perfection. This is a FPS retro shooter set in Czechoslovakia in 1986. The game contains 3 chapters, each chapter ends with a crazy boss fight, and that's not to mention the bonus content, which is also plenty. I can warmly recommend the game.10/10 .

_childDocuments_.review: Memorisation, not skill.Ultra hyper hardcore. Very Hard is unplayable on first walkthrough and it's unfair to saveload all the time. Otherwise it's atmospheric Doom-like shooter. If it's impossible to defeat enemies without knowing their locations and skills beforehand, why play it? It's not hardcore, it's grind and remember. Can't rate this difficulty mess for now. Enemies just hide all the time knowing player exact location and not making any noise. So it's hide and seek except everyone is against you. Enemies can jump much higher than player. Sometimes they just spawn and deal instant damage no matter how much you are bunnyhopping. This is memorisation hide-n-seek seeker simulator with guns... There always will be some surprise attacks that no one can predict and counter(damage is instant against 5 enemies). The only way to beat it is to know everything beforehand. Very often is too easy or too hard. Every wall can hide multiple enemies. I'm an ex-global elite in csgo and this makes me saveload because of not knowing what's ahead. It's impossible to play cautiously, enemies see through walls and will chase you down everywhere. In some cases downing monsters one by one isn't possible and there's no ammo. It feels random very often.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Great atmosphere. Interesting setting. Simultaneously funny and unsettling bosses.Cons: Lack of variety in enemy patterns leads to unengaging combat. Limited color palette makes levels difficult to navigate. The "puzzles" often involve endlessly walking around the map looking for the item you missed (either a valve, lever, or electrical box). Verdict: I look forward to seeing how the project turns out, and will play other episodes when they are released. With only the first lackluster episode currently available, there's not enough here to warrant a purchase yet.

_childDocuments_.review: I got  about a year ago from the Humble Best of Boomer Shooters Bundle. It left Early Access in May 2023 and that's when I got into it. Playing an unfinished game feels wrong to me and reviewing Early Access titles seems dishonest. So now that it finally released I can give my opinion on it.In HROT, whatever that may mean, you start your journey in a metro station turned bunker in the Czechoslovakian SSR. You soon discover that something horrible has happened as emaciated and alien-like creatures start attacking you. The game is divided into three episodes with eight levels each. Your arsenal is quite limited. There is only one weapon that I would put into the experimental category the rest are bog-standard guns. The same can be said for enemy variety. There are about ten or so different enemies whereas three types make up the majority. The boss fights are a mix of funny and trying-way-too-hard-to-be-funny. Endgame spoiler: . So that's what HROT is about.There are some amazing boomer shooters out there. I really liked Ion Fury and Forgive Me Father and I haven't even gotten into the neo-classics like DUSK and Amid Evil. HROT is an outlier in my opinion. The game is ugly. Looking at screenshots you'll notice that the whole game is just different shades of brown. It might be an homage to the original Quake but in 2023 you have to do better. The lack of graphic fidelity makes finding secrets very frustrating. Some walls are hidden doors but they blend in too much with the rest of the brown sludge. What's even worse is that there are no memorable levels because the design is the same repeated twenty-four times. Out of those I vividly remember two. One let's you ride a motorcycle and the other is set in a train yard. That's what sets them apart. Admittedly, the setting is unique but there is very little done with it. You'll find Soviet propaganda pieces and that's it. I'm sure the set pieces and props mean a lot to the developer if they grew up in the Czechoslovakian SSR but to me it does nothing.So, a quick but unfortunately negative summary of HROT: awful graphics, lack of enemies and weapons, bad level design. I'm baffled by the overwhelmingly positive reviews when there are dozens of better boomer shooters out there. Maybe they are all from Czechia and understand the significance of the . I do not.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is a great FPS with a brooding, dark tone. The color pallet is reminiscent of QUAKE, however the gameplay is not quite as fast, especially in the early game. It  also has alot of environmental story telling with no cutscenes. Each level makes you wanna find out what interesting stuff is coming next and learn more about whats going on through the levels. The gunplay is flawless. The music is very fitting dark ambient stuff. The sound effects are a bit odd and minimal, however you get used to them. The game has a sort of sarcastic and strange charm, a bit quirky. This also adds to the game. It feels strange and unique. Overall, I highly recommend playing this game because I'm really enjoying my way through the campaign. Recommended if you like old school FPS. I also think people who love the dark worlds of games like Let It Die and even Dark Souls may enjoy this if they like FPS games too, because they are tonally similar.

_childDocuments_.review: Really great game, recommend it to anyone who likes boomer shooters. One of the few I decided to 100%. Loved the aesthetic, gameplay, music, everything. Unlike a lot of Doom clones that have really ignorant "secrets" that amount to little more than guessing or just spamming Use, the secrets in this one were pretty well hidden but not in a frustrating way.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: After playing Episode 1 during its launch weekend (and having previously played the demo months ago), this game is already shaping up super well and I'm certainly looking forward to what the developer has in store. As of making this short review two new weapons were added and he has begun addressing one of the few complaints I had prior to the date of this review (namely he is updating the weapon sounds to be punchier, as previously weapons like the shotgun lacked a certain oomph one might expect, at least in the sound department).One of the biggest compliments I can give is the atmosphere alone is already quite stellar, with the game really nailing the oppressive feeling I'd expect from something set in 1980s Eastern Europe, and that air of mystery I got from games like Quake when I played them for the first time (though the levels in HROT are a little closer to something like Duke Nukem 3D in that they're clearly designed to have some level of realism, as opposed to the semi-abstract designs of Quake). Gameplay-wise the game may not deviate too much from what one might expect from a shooter that is following in the footsteps of games like Quake or Chasm: The Rift, but this is hardly a negative as I value fun and intrigue more than originality.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I dont understand the hype. The game lacks fun factor, and a clear-cut identity.Shooting mechanics are awkwardly slow paced but not fast-paced arcade goodness. There's no fun movement mechanics either. I say this as somebody who thought DUSK was pretty low-mid tier, but it hardly lives up to DUSK in the raw mechanics department. Health and ammo felt overly scarce as well, and my shotgun felt like it literally just did RNG damage. SMG also felt awful (even when the pistol felt like it did it's job better) but I'm willing to accept that I had scrub aim when I played it. but in total weapons felt like they lacked impact due to poor sound design, scarce ammo, and weird inaccuracies.This game is brown. Like, WAY too brown. This makes levels are extraordinarily bland and boring, they really crave a secondary color like red (which would still thematically support the aesthetic of dilapidating communist eastern europe). The enemy design also confuses me. The grunts are all fine, albiet quake clones (hey, don't fix what aint broke I guess). The bosses are dumb, however. It seems clear to me it's not really going for a "mystical"-type setting, so when objects like bulldozers and a gorilla statue become possessed/alive and start attacking you, it's just awkward. I really like the concept of the grotesque head-type enemies. They're white instead of purely gray which gives them an aesthetic that sticks out. The only issue is that I feel like the game doesn't lean HARD enough into this. I understand this is just episode 1, but give me more subtle storytelling a la HL1 about how and why these things exist and I would be a lot more interested in the game at large. I will at least say there were a few things I genuinly really enjoyed. I liked the translation feature as it really immerses you in the area without making it impossible to read everything. Being able to kiss portraits on the wall was pretty funny, and the cosmonaut part was also funny (you'll see it if you get there). And I think the game's setting has potential.And lastly, if you're genuinly reading this negative review, I want to you to really consider if you *enjoy* this game, or are just getting caught up in the hype circlejerk. If you look at the positive reviews, you'll see people who probably never even touched OG Quake 1 blindly worshiping the game as "le epic communist DUSK." I think this game has its fair share of very overt flaws, which makes it extraordinarily boring, and not worth purchasing.

_childDocuments_.review: I could talk about how the difficulty is as challenging as Blood even on Very Easy difficulty or how the brown art style succeeds where Quake fails or how the hazmat suits make the enemies look more monstrous or the good weapons or well done level design. Unfortunately, there is one massive sticking point that while it doesn't ruin the game, it well color your experience and that's the jarring shifts in tone.I think it mainly comes down a lack of context explain whats going on. Like you exploring these abandoned streets or spooky mines, enemies are puking like a plague hit with all the mutants and monsters around, everything feels oppressive and dire, helped with the games difficulty, and suddenly out of nowhere, you hear music and a clown is doing the macarena or some other dance and destroys the tone we were building up. The final boss is probably the worst offender of this since it's the final thing you fight. I won't spoiler it but it'll be a more fitting final boss for Postal: Brain Damaged.If only the episodes end with some context like DOOM or Duke Nukem to explain what I just did or where I'm going next but instead I'm just given a recipe for a tasty dish. I'm sure the devs thought it was a funny joke but you need to tell me the basics of what the F is going on! You're just breaking my immersion when you do that and I don't really care about immersion.

_childDocuments_.review: Hrot is a superb, brown game. It's a lot of fun to just tear around in, ripping and tearing, and if the obvious Quake inspiration is all you need to get circlestrafing then you won't be disappointed. The levels are fun, the enemies varied enough to keep the gameplay fresh with new combinations and the movement and shooting feel good. There's also an excellent sense of humour to the whole enterprise that revels in a very Czech-style dry wit combined with joyful surrealism. The episode bosses in particular are a real weird highlight and the final level peaks in the gag department in a series of superb bait-and-switch ploys that I won't spoil. An easy recommend just on the surface level.Going a little deeper, there're some very well-hidden secrets that can become fun to hunt down once you get a flavour of them and what to look for. There are also lots of achievements for odd behaviours and quirky little things unique to each level; having them pop up unexpectedly is a nice surprise and you can have more fun guessing what might trigger them.On the deepest level the game is full of cultural tidbits, hints and references that will provoke a more intellectually curious mind into learning some Czech/Czechoslovak cultural history simply for the sake of understanding some of the more oblique jokes. I know more of the history and also the national character of the Czechs than I did, because I played this game and it evoked a certain mood well enough for me to do a little web-searching. This is entirely parallel to the main experience of the game though: I was bunny-hopping and circlestrafing contentedly for the overwhelming majority of my playthrough and the intellectual stimulation didn't diminish that at all. This is after all a game for which someone somewhere took the time to record a silly noise to simulate the sound of an overfed terrier vomiting so you can imagine the cerebral side is not overpowering.It's a good game, at a good price. I don't regret a minute of my time with it. Big yes from me.

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful!  As someone who played Duke Nuk'em, Doom, and Blood through the '90's, this game is awesome.  I know all the levels on the games I mentioned.  This game plays like the ID engine with levels that at times seem familiar, but are unknown to me.  I could play this for days.There was that point in video games, and fps games that ID lead around the turn of the century.  This period where the graphics weren't great, but the games rocked.  These guys have captured this time in gaming wonderfully.  Congrats!

_childDocuments_.review: Updated at 1.0: Episode 1 and 2 are great, episode 3 is pretty bade, short epilogue/ending very unsatisfying. Unlike the game it emulates at the beginning, dusk, there is no clarity or pay off, just bunch of dull encounters with bullet sponge enemies. Overall worth the price for episodes 1 and 2 but  can't help but feel disapointed. Updated post completing episode 2: This game is fantastic! It is as atmospheric and fun to play as Dust, so far just as strong. Numerous quirky references to Czechoslovakian history give it a unique feel. Simple but fast, responsive controls (no dash, slide, etc, just normal movement), really good line-up of weapons which all have their uses. The boss fights are simply the best. Bosses are what I usually feel like are the biggest anticlimax in most classic and retro shooters, other than OG Doom, but these ones are great, super memorable. Still in early access, but lots of value here already. Can't wait for episode 3!PS I played the demo and really didn't like it! Not sure why, but if you like old school shooters would recommend giving the full release a go.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly quite wild. It goes from extremely entertaining humour to horror back to humour within minutes. The tonal whiplash at points is insane and that's great. It's a very entertaining ride. I learned a lot, I laughed and I was very afraid at times. I do not want to spoil anything else. To be very critical, the combat is alright. It works, its very serviceable. The enemies are fun and entertaining and as they're about to overstay their welcome and become stale the game is over. Some of the concepts seem extremely interesting and then vanish, or lead to nothing, or were just a throwaway joke. Some aren't and turns out you will see them again. I don't think I will ever play this game again having completing it, but the journey through it was extremely enjoyable and I do recommend this if you are interested.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the first episode. It feels like a combination between Quake and Chasm: The Rift. If you like that style of game play then I recommend this game.+ Cool atmosphere+ Motorcycle+ Interactive world a la Duke Nukem 3D (you can turn stuff on/off etc)++ Great level design.++ Good controls- Most of the enemy projectiles looks the same. For me it lessens the weird creepy atmosphere and makes the arcade-game vibe stronger. - One of the achievements is a mini game that has nothing to do with the rest of the game. It's entirely optional but if you want to 100% the game you need to slog through it.. Very boring and not a creative way to use achievements. -- Everything is the color brown all the time. This aesthetic without an equalizer becomes a bit uninspiring after a while.-- The sound effects are very thin and the weapon audio sounds like it's coming from toys. I would prefer punchier and rawer sound effects (Chasm: The Rift is a master of this)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic, I am waiting for the dev to take more levels and enjoy everything that you will make of this game, especially if you enjoy retro shooting games, or fast-paced shooting focused on movement, this game is for you, it is challenging enough in its difficulties and the designs of levels with secrets are fantastic!

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is an amazing Doom/Quake like FPS that is dripping with passion. The love for the genre and humor of the developer will not be lost on your play throughs. Every weapon is extremely fun to use and combo extremely well with one another. HROT has become one of my favorite gaming experiences in recent years. Buy it, play it, you will not be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels great! If you aren't sure about it, try out its free demo!The atmosphere is great, the enemies are varied and have good tells, and overall the gameplay feels pretty rewarding, the difficulties are well balanced, the guns are satisfying to use. Keep in mind though, this game takes maybe 3-4 hours to complete in one sitting on Normal. If you're going for the higher difficulties then it may take a few hours more. As of right now, it's a fairly short game but it's really well done so far for early access.There were a couple of hiccups with enemy AI (they would stand still while aiming a gun at me, but never shoot) maybe twice in the four and a half hours I played it. Aside from that, I encountered no bugs.If the dev keeps working with the great things that are currently in this game, I've got little doubt it'll be great once it's released from early access.

_childDocuments_.review: Reminiscent of classic doom, with it's own Slavic twist, HROT immerses you into an outlandish world without a plot- which I had only realized around 2/3rds into the game, after fighting the giant leninheads, carousels and horses, and hospital workers, and around the point of the bumper cars, where I realized there was no meaningful cohesion, despite that vague feeling of some sort of underlying idea behind it all. I think that describes part of what makes HROT so unique- absurdism underlying the concept of an idea, though with that addition of fundamental structure set up in its extremely interesting level designs. I never find myself bored with this game, yet there's something that prevents me from wanting to keep on playing it whenever it's turned off. This is perhaps more of an issue with myself, as I have far too many games inflicting with a choice paralysis, but part of me might just be unsure how to think about this game. I suppose thinking about it solely in the perspective as the absurd slavic FPS suddenly makes it a bit indistinguishable from all those other absurd FPS Doom-likes, like the recent Slayers X, Trepang2, or Incision. Despite this, I would say there's just a certain something that does still make HROT stand out. Perhaps intrigue. The fact is that even though the weapons are mostly your standard affair, they still stand out. I remember the mortar launcher much more than I do of any other grenadier weapons, the mines more than I do of Half-Life, the shotgun more than DUSK's, even the pistols too. Perhaps its for the same reasons that this game persists in my mind, despite conceptually being bland. If you haven't played many DOOM-like FPS games, I highly recommend this game. If you have, I still recommend this game, but see if you keep thinking about it when you aren't playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: I live in a post-soviet country and so much of the game feels familiar, using the same vehicles and architecture that I've grown up seeing. The setting is nailed. So is the atmosphere.It has funny things, creepy things, it's bizarre in a good way.The action is good (fast play movement, dodgeable but fast enemy attacks), but I very stronlgly recommend that you make frequent saving a habit in the game, at least for a first playthrough. There are some evil parts, especially on very hard. You can make a save without any slowdown, and loading a save is also  instantaneous.

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard for me to recommend this game in any other way than as curiosity due to its impressive custom engine, which hopefully someone will pick up in the future. Maybe I am missing something that fuels the hype on this game, but HROT is a far cry from the front row of actually good boomer shooters.It's not really bad or unfun, but as a whole experience, it's average at best, and really boring at worst. First and foremost, the episodes are really uneven, especially with their level design. It's not Dusk, sure, but even when not comparing to the best, there's a fatal flaw that runs as a main theme throughout the episodes. The engine tries to imitate Quake, but it's not utilized as the Quake engine was. Most levels are staggeringly horizontal, and feel like taken away from a Doom clone, not Quake. In this department, if comparision to Doom levels comes too far, Hrot is much closer to Chasm, than Quake. With a few exceptions, level layouts are simplistic and won't surprise you at all, especially with the enemy roster Hrot has to offer. Like others have mentioned, despite a huge bestiary the game has, the actual variety is minimal. They look and sound cool, right, but their behaviours and attack patterns are mostly the same. This devolves different combat encounters throughout the game, with an exception of bosses, into one same puddle of avoiding the same projectiles. Enemies that break out of this design are either harmless (the horse), or hurt the pacing (the teleporting soldier). This could be compensated with a smarter arena design and better spawning, but most of the combat takes place in static environments and follow the same layout: a rectangular arena and eventual spawns around the borders. Secrets are good, though, but I don't think I will be coming back to collect them all.There are exceptions from this rule, and some of the levels feel and play great. The second episode as a whole is much better than the remaining two and after almost dropping the game altogether after a pretty disappointing first episode, it hooked me to finish the game. The mines and the granny level are awesome. Some scripted events do create a great atmosphere people talk about. But these are exceptions that stand out in the sewer of the sameness that can be compared to a TV static running in a background. There's nothing memorable about the first episode after the initial novelty wears off. The great soundtrack and some imagery isn't followed by the actual gameplay or player's agenda. However, it was the third episode that let me down the most. It starts out strong with the newt level, but simultaneously separates itself from the theme the game was running along for two episodes. Basically, the game seems to turn into a meme, and I don't know whether it was intentional and just didn't work out for me in the end, or was it the creator hitting creative fatigue and just wanting to finally push Hrot out. The third episode is also a lot shorter than the previous two and abrubtly ends out of nowhere. Feels undercooked and rushed.The arsenal is standard, but it not utilized as it could be. Could hardly name any scenarios that would push the player into choosing a perticular weapon other than "it's close - shoot double barrel; it's far - shoot rocket or crossbow". The double barrel shotgun sounds great and has a great kick to it. Other weapons, on the other hand, feel underpowered even on the Normal difficulty setting, but can do their job. There's a well executed kick move that can bounce enemy granades to save your ammo.Other thing that connects to the mediocre level design with its horizontality that doesn't fit the intention of the engine (to imitate Quake) is the player movement, more precisely: the super weak jump that's virtually useless. It's barely utilized throughout the game. The crouch isn't implemented at all, and it does fit the Quake. However, it's disappointing that literally no other Quake movement design choice made it to the Hrot in the end.The game offers a horde mode, but the arenas are ok at most, and this mode doesn't come close to its counterparts even in games such as Forgive me Father.The game was fun to play through, but could use much more thought into gameplay systems and their refinement, because they are lacking and lag behind the impressive engine and audio. It's worth a playthrough if you like classic shooters, and played through the best, but I'd argue if it's worth its initial price tag. It's a mixed bag.

_childDocuments_.review: DISCLAIMER: I received the steam key for HROT for free in exchange for a detailed and honest review. My opinions and the contents of this review are my own.HROT is a retro-styled first-person action shooter game with horror themes, still in early access, developed by Spytihněv for a custom engine. Taking place in a desolate socialist city, the player must explore a series of public and industrial spaces dripping with a bleak monochromatic atmosphere. As the material of this review is incomplete, the review itself cannot be a holistic assessment of the game. When the full game is released this review will be updated.Out of all the current retro-styled shooters being pushed out, HROT feels to me to be the most authentic. A lot of this is owed to being built on a custom engine rather than trying to impose archaic impressions onto modern engines like Unity or Unreal. The custom-built lighting and shadows of HROT feel abstrusely arbitrated, reflecting the primitive lighting of early 3D attempts accurately, and there's a wobbliness to the polygons, especially those of your gun, that also evoke these older titles the game attempts to emulate. You could pick apart the visuals and find inconsistencies, for sure. Aesthetically, the weapon-models are slim and detailed, similar to (if not moreso than) those of DUSK, which doesn't feel accurate to the chunky, blocky weapon models from games like Quake. However, visually, HROT is worth more than the sum of its parts. The custom-built engine and grainy software rendering lend the game's graphics a broadly authentic impression which succeeds in transporting the player back to the mood and tone of those older games.What HROT does with that nostalgic mood and tone is the most impressive and fascinating thing about it. It isn't content to merely imitate the limitations of the past. In those archaic shortcomings, this game sees the seeds of potential for a unique and vivid atmosphere that can be best achieved in this technical style. Something sort of empty and monotone is turned vivid with implication, an unsettlingly quiet ghost-town of a gameworld which evokes economic decay and abandonment. The empty rooms of Quake, with its lonely torches and statues, were once crafted for the necessity of video memory. in those times, few decorative models could be afforded and so those that were present were iconic and evocative. But that same sense of a sparse environment populated by scarce decorations, which sit like low-poly monoliths in empty courtyards and office rooms, turns HROT into an eerie experience. The retro graphics allow the player's imagination to fill in the gaps, transforming the stark artifacts you find into relics from an almost timeless, instinctual age.There's a sort of reactive, spontaneous quality to these environments that give them an almost dream-like quality. Things feels ageless and meaningless, the arbitrary whims of classic shooters turned towards a mirror and made into something less bombastic. The enemies provoke this reaction too, unsettling in subtle ways that make them feel devoid of meaning or context. Yet their jumpiness and accuracy makes the player act as spontaneously and reactively as the gameworld does. HROT wants the player to shoot first and ask questions later, but it takes that impulsive action and uses it to instill a paranoid and dreary mood.These arcade-y sensibilities account for a good deal of HROT's immersion, despite the intuitive contradiction that implies. By making you submit to a "meaningless" gameplay experience, the campaign frees you to feel the full effect of its other influences, like the sound-design or environmental details. It's like a hypnotist's trick, lulling you into a passive state and then provoking you to feel or act in unexpected ways with additional stimuli. The music of HROT is especially fantastic at this, a rare and moody underscoring of modern-sounding strings and guitar that build out tense, ambient tracks.The gunplay of HROT itself is possibly the least interesting part to discuss. The guns all sound and feel distinct from each other and, I think, very pleasant to use, and there's a real sense of danger during every encounter due to the prohibitively limited health and armor resources. In my opinion, this sense of danger is too great, trapping the player in a number of unwinnable situations. It's not especially fun to have cleared the available level of health and still be in the 1-15% range, your only hope of progressing forward being a room of difficult to avoid shotgun-and-machine-gunners. If it were possible to outsmart the game with traps, like mines, or to dodge incoming fire more reliably, these moments would feel tense or thrilling. There's a real sensation of having your back up against the wall and having to dig your way out with gunfire or wits that classic shooters tended to evoke. Here, though, it more often than not feels cheap, and the weightless, empty atmosphere of the game at large distills you into a sense of passivity which makes these emotionally dire feelings hard to accumulate. I got through most encounters through save-scumming, and while it was never an impossible or frustrating challenge, I hardly felt tested so much as cheated. Some, if not all, of these criticisms are made sort of null when playing the endless mode, since death is essentially meaningless there. There is no objective other than killing enemies, and implicitly to survive as long as possible, which is tricky enough, but without the motivation of progressing forward in a level, and with the aforementioned weightlessness and cheapness, it's hard to devote much attention to it, at least for me.I should clarify I did like the gunplay the vast majority of the time, it's just that standing on its own without any of the game's other details to enhance it, it's fairly bland and can escalate to a degree of unfairness with the insanely limited health. Typically when a game limits health, the implication is that it expects you to avoid fire as much as possible, but with HROT, I've struggled to find a reliable way to do that. The guns feel great to use and all have unique and intuitive roles, and your movement speed and fire-rate for each gun feels just right. It's slick, but the implementation needs polishing, which it likely will receive as future updates come and go.Overall, while there are of course its modern touches, as there always are, HROT takes those qualities it needs from the past to form a compelling experience in the modern day. From the sound design to the game feel, it feels both forward looking and reflective, a somehow in-between game that rests on its own surreal ambitions. Of course the game is still in development, so the future is unwritten. Who knows where the developer will take this tone with the future episodes, or how the presentation and emotional framing will shift with future updates. As it stands, I'd recommend HROT to almost anybody. Even with just its one Early Access episode currently playable, it's an utterly unique and fascinating game which is a blast to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: Yes, this is only one episode, and - being a slow gamer - I spent 4 hours with it. So yes, the price might seem steep to you. But this is Early Access, meaning you pay for what you get and what you will be getting in the future, which is at least two more episodes and we'll see what else will be happening.As for what you can get right now: A good game. Check out the demo first, after that you'll know what you're getting into. It's brown. It's weird. It's also heaps of fun. The dev, who is active on the Steam forums and thankful for constructive criticism, shows great creativity (apart from the color palette) in enemy- and level design, and all this in a new, self-coded engine!Will it remind you of Quake? Sure. Will it feel like Dusk at times? You bet. Did the dev take inspiration from Chasm: The Rift? Most probably.But HROT is a good game all on its own, it's fun as is and shows a lot of promise for its future development.Again: Check out the demo. If you hate it, you will hate the game. If you like it,  get it while it's HROT.

_childDocuments_.review: Feb 3 2021: Like Quake and Dusk had a baby and raised that baby on a steady diet of vodka and communism.June 27 2023: Now that I've played through the entire game I'm really happy that I followed it from early access and got to see it get polished and improved. This game has now been fully released and it's worth every penny. Play it!

_childDocuments_.review: is an interesting retro shooter game that is set in Czechoslovakia, an eastern european soviet country at the time in an alternative timeline, where the country is filled to the brim with monsters.- Great 90's aesthetic, you can choose the resolution to your own liking to make it as pixelated or as crispy as you'd want.- The atmosphere is gritty and dark- Soundtrack that fits with the atmosphere- Maps are designed well and are fun to explore. According to the developer, some locations were inspired by real locations.- Everything is soviet, which makes the game ten times more interesting- Lot of historical stuff in the game, really makes the game more engaging- Guns feel great, not much to say- Endless gamemode, which is just a wave-based gamemode.- Steam achievements, trading cards, wallpapers, emoticons etc.- Enemy variety is great- Boss fights- Boss fights are a mixed bag from a challenge standpoint. Some of them are actually challenging, while some are just dumb easy- Maybe at times you will get stuck for a few minutes but that's it.- Right now it's really short, as not every map is finished yet.. I will rate the game when we'll get the full experience as the game at the moment is not yet finished. I can say however, that this game is fascinating and I can recommend it a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. Just finished Hrot ...and that was wild!If you've played Dusk or original Quake this will feel familiar but Hrot is a unique experience totally separate from anything else. The action is twitchy and brisk but not generally frenetic. With fewer monsters than either of the above games, it sometimes feels like a survival horror mixed with a Saw movie.Hrot also maintains an oddball sense of humour, leaning into its Soviet era theme with passionate detail and full of eccentric situational gags....And inanimate things suddenly lunging at you.Hrot is an intense boomer shooter dripping with character. It even drew me in enough to start researching 1980's Czechoslovakia just to understand some of the setting and references. Education!Play Hrot in a darkened room at night.

_childDocuments_.review: This is of course an early access game at the time of my writing this. It's possible the as yet unreleased levels will blow my mind (or suck).Initial impressions? It's good! The atmosphere is dark and compelling. It's definitely a solid Quake+ clone, but that isn't an insult in my book. The guns are from Quake, the monsters are from Quake with some later surprises, and the level design is Doom/Quake-ish.If you are just getting into this particular vein of retro-fps, then I will always recommend you play DUSK first (even before trying the nostalgic originals, DUSK is that good). But if you know what you like, and what you like is classic shooty-bang-bang, you can't go wrong with HROT.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best shooters I played.Weapons: 10/10. Not too many, each one powerful and useful in certain situations. Switching weapons is fast and easy.Levels: 9/10. Great level design, some backtracking but the game usually gives you shortcuts. I only got lost once or twice. Even though everything is quite brown, the episodes have a distinct look and feel.Enemies: 8/10. The AI isn't great, but the enemies are still very challenging. You gotta keep moving and play it smart. Health is rare and enemy projectiles or melee attacks hit you hard. The bosses are a bit cheesy but fun. The final boss battle was amazing.Story: 5/10. I didn't find much to discover. You can piece together some things by reading a sign here and there but it's not a game I would play for the story anyway. The level design and artwork gives you a good feeling of what's happening though.Given that this is a shooter, I am putting way more weight on the level design, the weapons, and the enemies than the story, so overall, I'd give it a 9/10. It felt a little bit like a mixture between Shadow Warrior (the original game) and Quake, but with its own unique style.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Before I review the game, here are my relevant biases: I'm a fan of HL but not many other 90's boomer shooters, and I'm not Czech. Hrot is outright the strongest "games-as-art" shooter I've ever played. It's also pretty hard and pulls no punches, mitigated by unlimited saves (at least in the difficulties I've played.) The entire play experience is best described as nightmarish (as in replicating the experience of being in a nightmare), pulling together cues from pop culture, motifs and styles completely alien to most players outside eastern europe, and incredibly strong sound design to create an atmosphere of dread. This spikes to terror when the game throws waves of enemies at you, coinciding with dramatic music and even lightning flashes. It's not clear if you're running away from something or towards something, but the fast-paced gameplay lends the whole experience a frantic vibe. All this is done with minimalist storytelling.Update: I wrote my review during early access. The third chapter is here, and the game is complete. I really can't find anything to nitpick about, since the final chapter is just as polished as the original two chapters.

_childDocuments_.review: HROT truly stands out from other titles in the Boomer-Shooter renaissance. HROT is built on a custom pseudo software-rendering engine that has been tweaked and honed to recreate the PERFECT classic FPS experience. Everything weapon sounds good and feels better to use, with nothing becoming truly irrelevant. The melee weapon is very useful for a specific type of pest enemy, and the starting pistol can become akimbo if you find another. There is a wide variety of fun weapons that are very powerful. While I wish the Ball-Lightning Launcher was in more levels than just E3M1 and Endless, it is still a neat addition. The Wine bottle serving as a portable heal kit AND special grenade is one of the coolest ideas ive seen in retro-FPS as well.HROT has atmosphere, you can really feel the soviet oppression through the whole thing. The level design is truly something else, there are many moments in the game that feel like the level designer is "setting up" the player for a trap, a la John Romero's DOOM levels, and I am here for it! After episode 1, the game suddenly takes itself much less seriously. Once this happens, and the goofy soul of HROT starts to really show itself, the game just becomes a joy to play. I got 100% achievements in under 24 hours playtime with some light usage of guides and playing on Hard difficulty for my main playthrough, so HROT delivers without overstaying it's welcome (something that many other Boomer-Shooters could learn from...). This game is seriously worth your time if you consider yourself a fan of DOOM, the first three Quake entries, DUSK, or if you're just a serious alcoholic and really want to make out with Gorbachev
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I don't know what to think lol It's like Quake meets Dusk meets Chasm? It has a lot of references to places, events and people that I'm unfamiliar with. Goes right over my head. I think if you're someone with a familiarity to the history of the Soviet Union you'll be able to appreciate the game even more. But that doesn't really interfere with the core game, which is awesome.The level design here is great. You're unlikely to get lost. You can move so quickly through these levels that I had to make myself stop playing at one point out of fear of finishing it in one sitting. The levels are tight, and have a lot of neat details to find and interact with.I've only played through it once, on normal, and I didn't get nearly all the secrets, and I haven't tried out the endless mode much. That took me ten hours, so there's definitely a good amount of game here because I don't believe I'm done with it.I would recommend going into the options and increase the "color" slider. It's still going to be brown, but it's much more saturated and generally looks better, I think.Overall, I don't have much to say about this game. Not because there isn't a lot to say, but because I think what's good about it is the same as what's good about every retro FPS game: great level design, fun combat encounters, interesting enemy variety, secrets, atmosphere, etc. The bosses range from wacky to insane and definitely got a big reaction out of me several times. If you like the demo, you'll like the game. If you've played a handful of the other retro FPS games and feel like you just can't get enough, this one is definitely worth picking up.

_childDocuments_.review: There are already tons of reviews about how great the game is so my review is about Linux support.The game runs fantastically on Linux with proton version 5.0. The only issue is that the audio is completely broken.This is because of an outdated OpenAl32 library. You can fix this by installing the OpenAl windows version on a vm and copying the OpenAl32.dll  file from windows into the games directory and replacing the old one. Alternatively you can use this  link to get that file.I'm hoping that the dev team of HROT would update this file so Linux users would have a much more plug and play experience in the future,

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game after pirating it at first, it was back when there was only the first episode. I was filled with the sorrow from the fact that the game made me to fall in love with it whilst having so little, played it several times on several difficulties opening all secrets, admiring quirky map design and great atmosphere, i could feel myself getting pulled into the Czechia, from soviet style apartment complexes to grand churches and castles. I decided to buy it without a slight doubt and never regretted it after. If you like Quake style gameplay with various enemies and weapons for any occasion, good level-design and not overly serious but convincing atmosphere i cannot stress enough how much id recommend this game. Also urge you to play any map with secrets at least twice, once without guides for secrets and other time with guide, secrets can be often tricky to find and to this day i cannot remember all of them. secrets, believe me or not often change the course of how you play the level, see it for yourself.Preferably the game should be played on hard/very hard if you enjoy a challenging game, though if you do not enjoy dying often Normal is completely fine difficulty to play on!I'm very grateful to devs for making this masterpiece, nothin' will ever replace this game, it will truly always stay in my heart as a dear memory that i might pick up from time to time. TLDR:just buy it, now.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: There are many retro-inspired FPS games out there these days, and yeah they're fun, but this game is on a different level for me, personally. The Slavic aesthetics & real historical references in Hrot gives it much more personality than the others. Simply put, this is just MY kind of game, and I can't wait for more. If you're not into any of that I would still suggest the game, as it does the classic FPS genre well, but with its own unique style & feel. Výborně!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is an experience. It's a curious blend of solid 90s FPS gameplay, eerie Soviet-era atmospheric horror, a loving expression of Czech history and culture, all while not being afraid to break up its sombre and foreboding atmosphere with some surreal and wacky encounters and gags. It's a bizarre but fantastic journey that you really need to play for yourself to appreciate. To the developers, I'd like to say Skvělá práce! (I hope I translated that right lol)
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Good:+ Nice aesthetics+ Ambiance and the music are alright so far+ Interesting enemy designsBad:- Placements for ammo and health don't feel like they were really designed around a pistol start on Hard. It's not uncommon to run out of ammo entirely even with smart management and not missing targets. Compare it to DUSK or Quake for how item placement should work.- Collision doesn't work in a lot of places. Ogres can shoot grenades through floors above you (why) and guard rails don't block you or enemies from walking through them.- Save for two weapons, the sound design and damage of the weapons are mediocre. Direct hitting a popcorn enemy with a rocket would gib them in any other game.- Since there's reloading there should be a button to manually do it, and an indicator for how much is left in the magazine. Why this isn't in to begin with is beyond me.Just play DUSK or Ultrakill honestly, HROT is overhyped. Even for an early access release this has a lot of problems that should have been ironed out before being listed.

_childDocuments_.review: It seems like "boomer shooters" are a dime-a-dozen these days, but not all of them get the "feel" right. HROT feels good. The weapons feel good. The balance feels good. The pacing feels good. And maybe most importantly the level design is good. They always seem to expertly loop you back around to that locked door after picking up the needed key, which cuts down on the wandering around factor some shooters suffer from. You also have a mini map if you get lost. Yes you have your key hunts and toggle switches. But even though the inevitable enemy spawns that result from these pickups or switch toggles may seem predictable by now, it's a staple of the genre, and HROT gets it right. The ambush arena battles are intense and fun. The boss battles are a little ridiculous, but that's also par for the course in this genre. I love the setting of HROT, taking place in old Soviet Czechoslovakia in the mid 1980's. It's dark, it's bleak, it's... brown. But supposedly that's what it looked like back then. I love all the little Soviet propaganda posters you see everywhere, written in Czeck (you can translate them by pressing "use" on them). It gives the levels a nice atmospheric touch. Additionally, the occasional Geiger counter clicking makes it feel like you're traversing areas you shouldn't be in. It's great. Very Chernobyl-like in some instances. (I love that the end level switches have A3-5 written on them. Which when translated to English letters means AZ-5....which was the Soviet RBMK nuclear reactor shutdown switch. The same one that kicked off the Chernobyl disaster. A nice little touch.)The enemies are varied enough to keep things interesting. And you'll discover which weapons in your varied arsenal are best for dispatching each enemy. Don't forget to hunt for secrets. Health, which comes in the form of strange Soviet styled food pickups, and medpacks seem quite rare. Which may be a nod to the 80's Soviet "Era Of Stagnation" and scarcity. So you'll want to look around for either breakable walls, or strange textured walls to find extra health and ammo pickups. Especially if you're playing on the harder difficulties. Some people call HROT Soviet DUSK, and I think that's a fair description. It is very DUSK-like, and that's ok! DUSK was freakin awesome. Overall If you like boomer shooters like DUSK, Doom and Quake, then you'll love HROT. Bonus points if you appreciate Soviet aesthetics. Give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty good and fun for the most part, but I recommend the hard difficulty or above for more intense fights. It's fast paced and has a variety of guns that are fun to switch around during fights. The pixelated style graphics and atmosphere go so well together, creating a haunting vibe. If you're into Quake, Doom, or Blood then I consider giving this game a chance. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: i know everyone is comparing this game to dusk, but I actually think they make a great contrast representing different ways of doing a modern quake-style FPS. while dusk is open, flowing, and fast, hrot feels considerably more claustrophobic and gritty. ammunition is scarce, health is even scarcer, and the silly big-tent-spooky aesthetic of something like dusk has been effectively replaced with a grim loneliness that gives the game an oppressive and apocalyptic atmosphere. i'm excited to see where this goes in future episodes especially, and what other types of levels feel like with this engine and atmosphere.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, I didn't enjoy HROT that much and playing the demo only cemented my worries on this game. It's definitely not a terrible game by any means but HROT is incredibly boring to look at and play as the only gun that's worth using and that is fun is the grenade launcher as all the other guns aren't satisfying to use in the slightest. The level design is also not very good consisting of muddy brown textures everywhere which makes it easy for you to get lost very easily. What I can give it credit for is HROT has excellent unsettling atmosphere that makes it very spooky and creepy to play even if it's not technically a horror game. However, HROT is really boring and just joyless and soulless to play. It seems with all these Boomer Shooters that have gotten Overwhelmingly Positive reviews that I've only loved maybe a couple of them. Maybe it's just my tastes in what I expect in a boomer shooter but HROT does not deliver the thrills of the 90's FPS and is really generic by today's standards even for a boomer shooter.Just buy Prodeus, which is also in Early Access and is 10 million times better than HROT. The guns feel actually good, the level design is awesome and so is the graphics and the game has modding!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome little retro shooter with a unique setting.While there isn't much content as of writing this review, what is here is soaking with a dreary soviet era atmosphere and i absolutely adore it.Ambience and music for the most part is really good and helps add tension, just like in Quake.Levels are nicely compact and are pretty well designed with plenty of secrets to find, and enemies to shoot.And if you love games like Quake, Dusk, Chasm, you'll feel right at home.The only serious negative i would say the game currently has, is the sound effects for a lot of the weapons themselves outside of maybe the rocket launcher sound a bit weak, and ofc, being an early access game, there isn't much to offer outside of 8 levels, a horde mode, and an interesting "NG+" mode (which randomizes the enemies and weapons, but you'll still be playing the same 8 levels again)But with time, i'm sure this'll be one of the top throwback shooters out there!If you are willing to support a single man dev team, and love these kind of games, definitely consider picking it up now! Otherwise, check back in a couple months once there is more content.

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool old school shooter. Looks perfect! Total dedication to a unique art style (has brown ever looked so good?). Episodes 2&3 are big improvements over episode 1. _childDocuments_.review: I never thought I'd use the word "charming" to describe a Quake-inspired FPS but here we are. HROT oozes personality, don't be fooled by the prevalence of the color brown. _childDocuments_.review: A fantastic classic FPS in most regards. The artistic direction is especially well done. The ambient is comprised of dark and oppressive music and sounds. The entirety of the game is brown and bleak, which works well in this weird communist zombie dystopia.The level design is simple enough that I didn't get lost, and it also features a few gimmicks to keep things fresh. Weapons are the best part. Here's a breakdown of the weapons I found:Pistol - Nothing fancy, generally well made but I don't understand why it has to reload. It's the only weapon in the game that has to do that.Single-barrel shotgun - Well paced and balanced weapon, although it becomes less useful after you get the super shotgunSuper shotgun - double-barreled boomstick - it seems like this weapon is better in every respect when compared to the previous shotgun, since it does double damage and shells are rarely scarceSMG - The fast-firing, ammo dump of this game. Works well against lower health enemies, like soldiersGrenade launcher - uses your grenades as ammo and deals more damage than just throwing them(I think?), but even if it doesn't, it's still very useful because the grenade thrown by it explode on impact and fly in a straight like.Mines - Almost never used them. They can be useful if you know where an enemy will come from. The one great use for them is in the last current level(E2M6), where a bunch of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ snakes appear out of the walls. I'll have to talk about the snakes too.Crossbow - Not bad, but I don't really see the point of it. It's kind of like a sniper, in the sense that it's great for killing enemies at a distance. Kind of like the rifle in Dusk. The problem is, Dusk has larger spaces, whereas in Hrot, 95% of the game is close quarters.Energy gun - This one's a secret which can be found on many maps - does a lot of damage and burns through ammo at the speed of light. Can be recharged by opening electric panels while holding it, though that damages you. Great at fighting bosses.I think there is at least one secret weapon that I haven't found. Something like the BFG from Doom.Enemies:Most enemies are fair, in my opinion. You start with soldiers, who run around and shoot one bullet at a time. They're easy, and a good first enemy.Then you get the biohazard shotgun dudes, who are kind of hard to deal with at first, because they require two shotgun blasts and they are also using shotguns.I think it's best that potential players find out the rest by themselves. It's quite a good roster of enemies... except one:The ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ snakes in E2M6 - They deal a ton of damage and they're the most resilient enemy, I think. They don't die from a grenade launcher shot. It takes one grenade and two super-shotgun blasts. What is this? Why can a snake survive a grenade or a shotgun blast? I don't understand what the purpose of this enemy is, besides frustrating players. Hopefully the get taken down a peg or two in the future.Overall, a great ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game which I will gladly revisit when more episodes get added. Great job guys, you nailed it.

_childDocuments_.review: HROT came to me as an absolute surprise. On the surface, it looks just like another boomer shooter which have lately kept being pumped out as if a conveyor belt has been spitting them out. Don't get me wrong - it is an amazing genre paying homage to beloved titles from 90s and early '00s, however, the boomer shooter market can sometimes feel oversatured and, frankly, uninspired. You've usually got two types of these games - ones directly adopting games they take inspirations from (such as the Build Engine holy trinity) or ones that include elements of generic fantasy (as if they were descendants from Heretic). Then came HROT and, well, you can tell that Spytihněv (the developer) did something REALLY right just from the Overwhelmingly Positive (almost a round 100%) reviews.HROT is a simply, unobstructed fun. It knows exactly what it wants to do and does not try to spread itself too thin. Yes, the brown-ish theme you see at the beginning will be present through the trio of episodes until the very end - but its not an issue since it is handled perfectly and sets the gritty, depressing undertone of the times of communism in a simply yet highly efficient manner. That being said, the true uniqueness of HROT lies in its setting - Czechoslovakia under socialist regime in the mid-to-late 20th century. It is rare enough to see a boomer shooter with a real, historical setting let alone one that would concentrate on such a small country (yes, I am biased since its my home country and yes, I know that the developer is from there as well but still - from what I've seen, foreigners find this setting fascinating just as much as we, the Czechs, do). Seeing all the references, communism-themed buildings, enemies and bosses gives HROT inexplicably fascinating flare - and I would not have it any other way.Between its unique theme, amazing level design, lovely hidden secrets and shooting model with amazing feel, it's not difficult to understand why I'd recommend HROT to anyone, especially fans of boomer shooters.
