_childDocuments_.review: SHORT VIDEO REVIEW:The premier in modern Slavjank FPS games! If you are a fan of the modern renaissance of old school FPS titles this could well be up your ally, but it is absolutely not something for the uninitiated and may well be a little too authentic for the general consumer.While many of the newer throwback FPS titles have tried their best to authentically recreate the feel of 90s shooters, there is an odd analogue to them all where despite their efforts it is somewhat clear that they are generally simplified Unity and Unreal engine titles, with any oddities coming from a lot of purposeful programming to recreate old exploits (strafejumping, physics objects bugs etc…), Hrot goes one further by having its own bespoke engine made in Pascal, an engine that seems to be running software rendering with its honorific ugly textures and weird lighting, plus its tinny, lightweight sounds give the impression the sound driver is badly made. Furthering this feel is the manner in which a lot of the items in game act in an extremely uncanny manner. While on the ground movement is predictable, jumping is odd. Vertical hops feel extremely anaemic, barely going 2 feet in the air, yet horizontally you can seemingly fly long distances, which creates a really odd sense of disconnection between the elements. To further this enemies sometimes do weird things like jump over walls or erratically bounce around, peddling the air as they go, all with very odd looking animations on models that just look so utterly off they would be the uncanny to the already uncanny. In this manner Hrot genuinely could be mistaken for a 1998 budget title that nobody paid any attention to, maybe bar a PC Gamer review that would give it 45% because of how much it lagged behind Quake 2 or Unreal, forever consigned to the budget DVD rack you found in hardware stores that nobody ever bought.This dedication to the warts-and-all feeling of an odd engine may make it sound like Hrot is a bad game. I would however argue against that though as its general combat design and level layouts say otherwise, meaning that it is less a lack of talent and more a pointer to where it’s inspiration lies. While titles like Dusk or Amid Evil were trying to recapture the mood of classics by Id, 3D Realms and Epic titles, Hrot is more an attempt to remake things like Chasm the Rift or capture the mood of Cryostasis: Really odd, slightly broken titles from Eastern Europe that likely did not have the time or budget to achieve their wants and ultimately got pushed out too soon. In this emulation of the feeling of these kinds of titles, Hrot excels without ever sinking into the mire of bad design: its quirky, not awful, and very purposefully so in its admirable dedication to jank. Sure, maybe the developer could have made it in a more powerful engine and ironed out all the oddities, but what is the fun in that?Here however is the issue: for the average consumer this is just a little bit too janky for most. It is well designed and the combat is a lot of fun, plus there are no bugs or badly designed moments where the player suddenly dies because of something cheap, but the dedication to jank will certainly put off many who would likely hope for a title to put Ion Fury through the ringer. If there was one element that seems a bit off it is the level design where it is a little hard to find the way forward from time to time, but those moments are limited to about 3 in the whole of the first chapter, and I cant help but wonder if they are purposefully being obtuse in their emulation of those older, more cult titles.If I could summarise it I would say Hrot is the perfect game for a slavjank fan. It smells so soviet that the game has constant references to the CCCP and the health packs are weird cartons of milk and the delicious sounding tins of “Blood & Fat”. In this if you love your weird European games Hrot is a bucket of fun! If you demand high quality across the board without any oddity to the game itself, be cautious as it may be a little bit too much for you.I am giving this a recommended rating over not recommended as it is good, just a very cautious recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom 2 is my all time favorite old school shooter. It blended horror, action, mystery, and exploration perfectly. There were times the game was terrifying, keeping you on edge, wondering if that next pickup is a trap (it always is). There were times you were strafe shooting around an arena, dodging fireballs and pumping shotgun shells. There were times you wanted to know what happened here, with the environment telling a story that in game logs never can. And you were rewarded for hunting for secrets, without them being mandatory nor too difficult to find at least a few of them. If all of this sounds amazing, you'll like HROT. It ticks all the same boxes of Doom 2, plus some additional humor thrown in from time to time. It's in early access, but there are a decent number of levels available at the time of this review. Get it, you won't be disappointed.

I wish there was more!

_childDocuments_.review: Calling this "Slavic Quake" certainly isn't a new & clever take, but the resemblance is uncanny. As is the game itself! This whole thing with an unspecified (nuclear?) catastrophe catapulting this game's world into another plane of existence goes strong all right. A horse with a gasmask is among the more normal things you'll get to encounter & send back to wherever they came from. Or forth into the otherworldly limbo this game takes place in.Just like Quake does. Another similarity is the (immensely satisfying) core gameplay loop. Avoiding damage through fast movement, killing stuff with simple, yet effective weaponry. The blocky looks certainly support this otherworldly vibe, as well as good old-fashioned Soviet brutalism.

The gameplay includes your typical range of weapons, Schyte (melee), Pistol, shotgun, smg, launcher etc. Although the gameplay is easy and staightforward to understand. The main enjoyment of this game is the atmophere and fast paced action. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: At this writing, I'm about nine hours in and enjoying it quite a bit! The controls are fluid, the game-play is challenging enough, the setting is great (I don't give it tops marks for atmosphere, but in terms of setting and the Soviet 'flavor', it's solid), and I have not yet encountered a single glitch.It's a pretty unforgiving shooter with enough hunt/seek puzzles (mainly how to get a door open), boss fights, and overall content to make it seem like far more than an Early Access game.The Dev is also quite active, which is always a plus for a game in development, and the updates/patches are frequent. I've also got to give a special notice to the excellent 'save' system (great stuff for the busy gamer) and the multiple difficulty options!It's definitely worth the cost of admission, and if you enjoy games like Blood West, Cultic, BABBDI, or, of course, Quake - then this one won't disappoint either. Also, there is a free demo, so you can try it out before spending your hard earned money.

_childDocuments_.review: HROTs quality is like, when you want to cook, but have barely any ingridients left in your kitchen and babushka comes over to help you out. With her help it becomes a decent meal. You think to yourself, if babushka had more spices and other ingridientns, it could've been an excellent dish. But before you lies a dish that is "Not great, not terrible" just decent.HROT knows overall what it wants to be as a "boomer"/classic shooter and it does what it has to do.- Gunplay feels nice for majority of the weapons roster (e.g. explosives, shotguns), but for the few other weapons (Pistol and smg), they felt a bit like peashooters and lack responsiveness. - Base mechanics are solid with strafing, kicking objects/Grenades and enemies, but imo it could've a bit more. Jumping and especially nade jumping lacks a bit of verticality and/or speed. I would've also liked it, if you could kick more projectiles of enemies back.- Secrets are hard to find without map and feel sometimes barely rewarding, Example: There are hidden buttons in form of bricks, that are barely noticeable due to the color palette of the entire game. You manage to get it open after 5 minutes of wallhugging and spamming e and what do you get? 5 hp.- The visual style, from its sick mutated, radioactive look of the enemies; and the titbits of the game world create an interesting setting. - Also the crude humor the game has, as what enemies you can encounter, made me first jump out of my chair and then laugh about it. Those oddballs in the enemy roster appear rarely throughout all 3 episodes.- I liked the overall level design, not too long not too short. The campaign structure is btw the typical 3 episodes with x levels in it,If I would rate it out of 10, it would be like a 6,5/10. Like above mentioned "Not great not terrible", there a couple of boomer shooters I played, I had more fun with, but this one is still recommendable.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: 8.5/10At a time when we are eagerly anticipating a new version of the Quake series, HROT has significantly quenched our thirst. HROT seems to have been created to take the place of Quake, which has also been successful. HROT performs very well in most parts, which is why it can be compared to Quake. The game's music was the only aspect where it could have performed better. Of course, absence of the music during the stages, due to the very good audio design of the game, has created a slight sense of fear in the game, which is in harmony with the atmosphere of HROT, but due to the fast rhythm of the game, lackness of the music is felt. But even with this problem, HROT is a close experience to Quake and also classic Doom.+:Fast gameplay that is extremely enjoyable with good gunplayEnemies and bosses with acceptable AI that make the game challengingGood level design like classic shooter gamesInteresting funny and scary elements that make the game specialStrange details that are truly amazing-:Lack of soundtracks to be played during the most stagesDespite the variety of enemies and environment, the game is visually repetitive
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game, generally the boomer shooter category when approached is either really good or flat out mediocre and this game was pretty great. I loved how over the top some of the enemy designs were and felt like they had pretty unique identities. The final boss was truly a sight to behold and stuck to the theme of being flat out ridiculous, fun, and over the top. This game to me was a title that really stood out to me as far as boomer shooters go and I would love some sort of sequel 8.5/10 I wish it was longer!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty dang good. Levels are big and varied with lots of one-time stuff you can interact with. This was made by one guy, on a custom engine he wrote, which is nuts. I love how personal it is, and how it embraces its country of origin.tldr: It's a good old shooter. Familiar, but just weird and personal enough to be interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is an acquired tasted.After watching Civvie's video on it, I decided to give it a swing and if you don't have nostalgia for the Quake era of gaming, I can't imagine this game as much to offer you. The gun play is very weak, your guns feel inaccurate and limp. As this game draws on nostalgia from the early 3D boomer shooters, the failure of the gunplay kind of unravels the rest of the game. Shotgun is probably your most impactful weapon but it's damage is inconsistent with the classic gaming shotgun with 5ft range. The grenade launcher is the runner up for impact but that's also lessened by it's really weak blast range and damage, and since you can only carry 30 at a time, unless the enemy numbers significant or packed together enough. You might as well just shotgun them.Secrets are interesting to hunt for, but it seems to be drawing on wolfenstein more than anything since alot of secrets are just press E on a wall, and the best way to find them are with your map so a viable strategy  is just to run around rubbing your face on a wall until you see an opening on the map.The game is kind of dull all round actually, it's so boring on the moment to moment that some of the more outlandish moments are met with a flat "Huh." You encounter a robot monkey or a sentient vaulting horse and it just doesn't electrify like the game seems to expect it will.I plan to push through and finish it, but it's very telling that the only time I really perked up and enjoyed myself in this game is when I found an old handheld on the floor and got the highscore.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This is a letter of love to the classic FPS games and especially Quake.  Now that's it's fully released I feel I can give it a hearty thumbs up as it's great fun, plays very well, and as a passion project with a reasonable price, you don't have to worry about any live service or microtransaction garbage. This is a great game and worth your time and money.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: A great retro shooter with all the elements of the classics; moody atmosphere, bleak color palette, disturbing enemies, a well rounded array of weaponry, WELL HIDDEN secrets, spooky music, hell yeah. I spent years playing quake and doom, as well as unreal. This game is highly reminiscent of the late nineties and is quite replayable as I need to find more secrets. Well worth 15 bucks.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Feels very good, even if the first episode just felt like the "Steamworks" map from DUSK but forever. Great atmosphere, great shades of brown, but Episode 3 is what really won me over. I love the sound effects, I love the Ratters, and I loved seeing the general design improve over the course of the game's three episodes. Has also helped bring me a newfound appreciation for my heritage.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Its true masterpiece in details, especialy if you are 90´ after soviet-era child. You can see box (building) with modeled cellar ventilations you exactly remember from your childhood, milk in bag,etc...There are also funny moments i can not spoil here.Middle difficulty is great. Game is challenging, you die, but there is progress every reload.I tried to think about constructive critics, but couldnt find anything i would like to add / improve.Just add more chapters and inspiration for my lunch :D
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This game is weird.It is extremely bland, quiet, even the weapons don't make much of a sound, everything looks bleak and grey, there is no joy in it.Perhaps it really wants to simulate what life was like in the USSR. But overall it is a good oldschool shooter. A big positive is that you actually find a use for every weapon and enemy variety is decent enough.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game to get an Early Access release for some time now. I see a lot of reviewers comparing this to DUSK which is likely inevitable, but I really think HROT is going to earn it's own respective place in the "boomer shooter" renaissance.I think nostalgia is a very powerful art design technique, and it is masterfully done here. It really does feel like you've just discovered an old unlabeled floppy disc under your bed that is truly haunted and possessed in it's own twisted lo-fi way. Some of these enemies really feel like they are straight out of the nightmarish paintings of Francis Bacon, existential, grisly, and complete abominations of nuclear disaster. Enemies will grunt and snarl from corners close by, background music will occasionally go quiet and you are left to the sound of your pounding heart and dripping (mysterious fluids?) nearby. I love this game. I'm so excited to see how it grows. I for one am glad New Blood isn't getting there paws on this one, I think it will be equally as acclaimed with this new dev team coming up to the spotlight. STRONGLY RECOMMEND.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this game is perfect considering how lackluster it seems to be at first: Great interconnected level design, enemies are surprisingly tough and unpredictable (they dodge ALOT), gunplay is satisfying, sound design is great (musics are good too!!), secrets are not too easy to find, and of course the glorious hammer and sickle.The gameplay itself is challenging even on normal difficulty because enemies are tough and they dodge alot. You also have to learn to preserve ammo and make every shot counts because ammos are a bit scarce. You also need to learn which weapons are effective against certain enemies (except when you find the  )cant wait to see more
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a cool vibe, it's a straight-up, no-nonsense shooter.  No gimmicks.  Very old-school game play and 'feel'.  HROT is one of the best retro shooters out there, very reminiscent of Quake.  There are frequent updates, and development seems to be progressing at a good pace.  I would definitely buy HROT again.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: We dont have S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2 yet but we do have this, the movement is fast the combat is hard yet satisfying, the atmosphere is unsettling and the whole games looks like brown poop, I dont mean that in it in the bad way, this game is the closest thing we have to Dusk 2, this game is clearly and heavily inspired by Dusk and the great example of this is the color scheme and the melee weapon which is a sickle, by no means im saying this is a copy of dusk this game just takes the elements of dusk and elevates it further and in a better way, there isnt a lot of sound variety but im happy with what little this game offers because its just perfect and it perfectly fits the theme of the game and the gun sounds are done greatly, though I really think the physics could use some work like how every object no matter the size or the wight just slides on the ground like butter, overall this is a great game, pls support the developer so that we can see more stuff like this in the future because this is a perfect start and its great to see the dev fixing bugs and supporting the game, and YES THERE IS ENOUGH VODKA AND KOMMUNISM FOR ALL OF US! YOU CAN KISS THE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ PICTURE OF THE PRESIDENT!! LIKE WHAT MORE DO YOU WANT ?!?!?
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Modern Czech Doom. 10/10 money not wasted.The game's very simple, run,shoot, and enjoy.The old czechoslovak setting is great, especially because I'm from the Czech republic and can relate to the various objects in the game. This might be a slight turndown for other people, because I dont believe many foreigners know enough about those times to get jokes and references.But otherwise, the game plays like a more moder version of Doom or Duke Nukem. It's fun purely gameplay wise, and the biggest plus I see it's indie made.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This game's levels so far an excellent, and I can't wait to see what the next episodes will bring!This game takes a lot of inspiration from ID Software's Quake, but the ways in which it's different are in equal parts distinct and imaginative. The Eastern Bloc aesthetics, interactable objects, and surprise enemies all make for a game that is able to have it's own identity.My only real complaint is the level design. Most of it is fine, but I would occasionally find myself unsure where I was supposed to go next. Aside from that: the game is easy to recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Dusk, Quake and Soviet-era references, you'll love this. The dev is very clever and creative with levels having horror elements, even laughing right at your face at certain points. If I'd improve one thing it would be the sound design which doesn't have the "oomph" that Dusk's had, but overall the game is exceptionally well-made.If you get this, definitely cap your FPS because my graphics didn't like it if I didn't, very stable and customizable otherwise.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Like others have alluded to, HROT is like DUSK with a Russian twist. I think the comparison is fair, but overlooks the fact that the game engine was built from the ground up supposedly. You can drive a moped in the second level which really activated my almonds. It is super impressive to see how optimized this game is and how much interactivity it allows through the custom engine. It does seem like it borrows inspiration from DUSK with the sickle and the quake-like graphics, but I think it's coincidental considering the soviet atmosphere and that destructible environments aren't uncommon. This game reminds me a lot of quake and the amazing atmosphere reminds me of S.T.A.L.K.E.R., but I think the fact that this game exists is a testament to the fact that there are amazingly talented devs out there with great insight into what makes gamers tic. This game in my opinion is superbly original where it needs to be and for the price at the moment (with the 15% discount) is a freakin' steal. Considering the amount of replayability and upcoming 2 episodes, I think this game deserves to be in the library of any gamer who enjoys oldschool FPS games. I am super excited to continue following the development of this game and in that respect it truly will be like experiencing DUSK again. I've played through the first two episodes so far and was thinking about what fixes or improvements would make this game better, but as I was typing the review, my nitpicks were so small that I forgot. The quality of this game overshadows many of the small issues that are pretty much non-existent, which is rare considering how games launch these days. This is a great use of early access listing and I cannot wait to see the improvements and updates made to the game. I think that there is so much room for this game to be G.O.T.Y. material truly. I would definitely recommend it currently.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the Worker and Parasite to DUSK's Itchy and Scratchy. If you like shooter what look kinda like Quake and go fast and shoot good, it's that. If you like bizarre Soviet era imagery and vibes, it's got that. If you want a video game where an oppressively brown color palette is a positive instead of a negative, it's got that.

The game can also switch between between scary and funny moments on a whim without breaking the immersion. It's pretty cheap and imo definitely worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Good difficulty curve for those looking for some challenge ala occasional moments of twitch shooting inside of some deeply brooding and atmospheric levels that have an unsettling horror to them. The player often has that "whats around the next corner" feeling as opposed to hordes of enemies assaulting you front and center (although that does happen from time to time and it balances in perfectly.)My only suggestions to the developer would be to add a manual reload function for all (or applicable) weapons for a bit more consistency. Highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: When evaluating a "retro" game there are various different criteria you can use, involving the hows and whys of using a retro aesthetic. In this case, HROT emulates EXACTLY what those late-90s "tech demos" felt and played like after the fall of the Soviet Union. Where some comp-sci grad student in Eastern Europe was finally able to play Quake and said "I could do that".Is it a great game? No. FPS gameplay has moved on in--jesus--30 years. Weapons and level design decidedly feel dated, for example.But I feel like the deficient gameplay is part of the point of this game. This is essentially a historical re-creation of late-90s "shareware" (i.e. indie/"please hire us" demos) FPSes coupled with a heavy dash of post-Communist irony and dark humor.Would I recommend this to everyone? Definitely not. Would I recommend this to anyone who was an active FPS gamer of the time or wants to experience what it was all like pre-Unreal? Yes.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is a great mix of speedy arena shooter styles with a setting not seen before in this genre of game. A hell of a lot of fun to play and is rewarding the better you get at it. What makes it different is that the developer has taken a lot of creative thought into each weapon, level & enemy and it creates a great unique experience. It's a blast to play.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, small confession; I'm more of a Build Engine man. I find Quake-style games overly floaty and the weapons consistently underwhelming (yeah, even you, Dusk). Whilst HROT definitely fits that mould, the weapons are at least fun to use, albeit not especially satisfying. Fortunately, it retains the excellent level design that is a staple of the genre, populates said levels with a varied and highly-entertaining cast of enemies, and coats the whole thing with a wicked sense of humour. I found it took me a lot longer to get through HROT than it probably should have done, simply because I was forever stopping to Google the myriad Czech cultural and historical references littered throughout  - so you're learning stuff too!If you're a Quake fan, I'm sure you'll love it. And if you're not a Quake fan, you can take it from me that HROT is still very much worth your time and money.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: A somewhat decent Quake/Dusk/Chasm: The Rift inspired indie shooter, with a bit of potential. Like most early access games, this one's a bit rough and severely lacking the materials of being a full release, alongside with needing to iron out a few issues.The enemies are ok and are fitting for the game's art-style at a certain extent, some of them felt underdeveloped and the boss encounters were rushed and underwhelming. Some of the enemy designs were a bit lazy and are more on the goofy side, than the intimidating end of the spectrum, they took me right out of the game whenever I was getting immersed. Granted a game doesn't have to be too serious, especially when it has slightly cartoon-ish graphics and very janky animations, but from how the game presents itself as being this bleak, lonely and oppressive scenario, sometimes putting in goofy additions like hostile, gas mask-wearing horses to such a world might not work as well as intended. Unless if everything were shown or explained to have been changed through mutation and technological experimentation. Also the snakes can take at least several times the amount of punishment a foot soldier can, for some reason.The music and ambience gets a thumbs up from me, they suit the game's dreary tone and loneliness pretty well, although the overall colour palette could use a little bit more variety - HROT is probably the brownest game in existence. I know it's a style choice to make the game look that way - However seeing nothing but brown environments for hours on end can get very tiring and monotonous.The level design is pretty solid, the secrets are 'well' hidden; if not a bit too convoluted and few and far between and you won't be able to find most of them if you aren't using the map. Most maps have a lot of thought and detail crafted into them, I would also say the same about the placement of their secrets. The issue that I have with these secrets, is that most of them have a tendency to reward far too little and aren't worth searching for most of the time, especially in more desperate scenarios.The game runs well and plays okay. There aren't any bugs that I have encountered so far, except for enemies clipping through grated floors, unless if that was intentional. Drowning can apparently damage your armour and you won't be getting that health back, when it should regenerate after getting damaged by the drowning. There were times that it felt like that the game was trying to be a fast paced shooter like Quake or Dusk, while at the same time, trying to be a Survival Horror; Health items are very scarce and seldom abundant, especially the armour. To some degree, that contradicts with the game's fast-pace oriented action. If the game is going to take the Survival Horror route, then being able to move slower and crouch behind cover would be nice. Enemies are also weird when it comes to trying to avoid their gunfire, it's as though they know where you are at all times and will instantly shoot if they see one pixel of your character out of cover, feels like their aim is tracking you from behind solid walls/cover and is quite cheap and frustrating, rather than challenging. It does add an element of unpredictability for the enemy encounters and happens to make the gameplay more dynamic. Personally I think a bit more fine-tuning may be needed, like enemies being unable to pin-point your exact location, after breaking out of their line of sight for a certain amount of time.My least preferable aspect of the game is the weapons, not only did they feel under-powered, but they also have some of the worst sound design I've heard in a while, even in an indie game. But I did like the shotgun and how satisfying it felt and sounded. The SMG is useless, the pistol being more accurate and useful than the sub-machine gun didn't really make sense to me - Since SMGs are supposed to be pistols on steroids. The only weapon I solely use in the majority of episode 1 is the shotgun (and the grenade launcher and sometimes the pistol), I could just hide behind a door and shoot at every enemy that tries to swagger in. You can get stronger weapons but they appear much later in episode 1, they were probably hidden in some secret I missed, considering how convoluted the said secrets are. The crossbow, of which I'm assuming is the rail gun equivalent of HROT, was pretty bare bones and boring design-wise, including the lightning gun. Like the enemies, I think they need a better introduction to the player and more depth into the game's universe, but that's just me.The game has flaws and I wasn't really impressed by it's dull and janky stature. But to the game's merit, there were a few aspects that I liked, such as the lonely bleak feeling, decent gameplay, music and level design. But beyond that, there's not really much that would make this game stand out from the rest and look less bare-bones than it already is. And I know the game is still in Early Access, but sheesh, this turkey really needs more time to cook in the oven. Lastly, I think the dev needs to present and catalogue his additions and updates to the game in a less subtle manner; I never noticed that these new levels even existed.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: The gunplay is just base quake, not much innovation there unfortunately.And unfortunately the movement is super dumbed down (no airstrafing) - so the combat is just running in circles and do damage. Monster AI is good, and has some funny interactions. Overall game has badass soundtrack and vibe, so definitely recommended at least for the czech commie era memes
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Rock Solid Brown Colored Quake-like Boomer Shooter. Lots of Brown Sewers, Brown Castles, Brown Caves, and Brown Corridors. Some Shake ups aesthetically might've been nice. This is the kinda game where all the little details make add up to something special. Like how every level takes direct inspiration a real place in Russia. When Duke Nukem 3D came out, gamers back then loved how levels felt like real places rather than abtract mazes. This is the natural evolution of that.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't go crazy hyping it up too far but it definitely delivers an immersive environment, has a one-of-a-kind look to it, and the shooting/combat aspect of the game works pretty well even using a controller.    It's just marked as Playable and not Verified but I'd say it's a solid game for Steam Deck too, with naming savegames and the game wanting you to use the on-screen keyboard during saving... that whole mess is the only time where playing on the Deck gets a little touchy and non-user friendly.    Other than that it's a unique FPS game with a decent single player campaign that's worth completing and its install size is really small so if you're looking for another game to cram on a shrinking Steam Deck card or drive, this would be a good pick.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Are you a fan of Quake 1/2 ? Do you miss the simple days of spending a rainy Saturday afternoon playing a game which you could just play a nice game without having to think about a million possible strategies to win? Do you like simple & fun Indie games?Then this is the perfect game for you! :DHROT is that kind of game which you can play, have fun, laugh a bit but still find incredibly smart aspects of the game. By using Q1 game engine, HROT will deliver a well spend afternoon playing a fun game. You will not find high resolution details or Hollywood scripted scenes, but you will laugh, scream and get frustrated about finding all the secret areas and fulfilling all the achievements!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent Quake-like retro FPS, if you're coming from the modern Quake mapping scene the level complexity doesn't stack up with the likes of Arcane Dimensions (but then does anything really?) but I would say they're a good step ahead of Quake's original maps, and there are a lot of visual and interactive flourishes as well as the overall CCCP aesthetic. Gameplay wise weapons are distinct and useful, the double barrel is if anything more satisfying than Quake's, the kick mechanic is a nice touch for zoning/clustering enemies for AOE and bouncing back the Hrogre's (heh) grenades. Finally there's an endless mode for going fast and listening to your own music in while you gib Semiks left right and centre. Basically if you like Quake, buy the game.Oh and in case you didn't notice there's a demo so you have no excuse to not at least try it out.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic little Slavic take on Quake.  Feels amazing and plays amazing--I originally had three complaints concerning this game but the Dev already knocked out two of them (reload issues and Sickle damage and speed). Now, the only complaint I have is the gun sounds.  Otherwise, it's a fast and dirty shooter that stands up there with Dusk.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT successfully captures the feel of Quake I, along with the dark and oppressive ambiance, with a Soviet-era Eastern European theme instead of Quake's Medieval/Lovecraftian one. That's actually a lot harder than it sounds to pull off.A LOT of indie retro homage games clearly show their limits even after 10-20 years of technological advancement. I.E. if you compare something like Them & Us or Fear the Dark Unknown (or, god forbid, the Outbreak series) with the first few Resident Evil games, graphics aside you can tangibly feel that the indie homages have much lower budgets despite the original big studio games having been made decades ago.A lot of Steam indie retro FPS games have this problem too, such as Crimson Metal, Monument, etc.HROT doesn't have this problem. Similar to Dusk, it really, genuinely feels like the games its paying homage to, and you can easily forget it was made by one self-taught dude in Czechoslovakia in his bedroom. It's smooth, fluid, and really captures the fun and feel of Quake I. My one gameplay caveat is that health and ammo seem to be a lot rarer than in Quake I or Doom 1 & 2; it's nothing that you can't handle with some experience, but it does make the game feel noticeably harder than Quake I even though everything else about the game (i.e. enemies and how it feels to fight them) is about on par with Quake I in terms of difficulty.My only issue with the game is that the ultrawide support isn't that great (the image is Vert-, you can increase the FOV to compensate but the weapon models will still be cut off).
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: First time playing a game of this genre, so I don't have any expectations for a boomer shooter. That being said, this game is great! Being to traipse through a long level, die pretty far in, and then realizing that once you know the enemy placements you can speedrun where you were once cowering behind every corner, it grants a feeling of instant gratification and mastery that is unlike anything else I've played. Now I truly understand my insane pace, me & Mark Rutzou.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Principally, this is a Slavic Quake with a very Soviet flare, but it's much more than that.  The attention to detail and interactivity of each level is impressive as is the atmosphere.  Thankfully, only special enemies are tanky due to the fact that we've long since overcome the technical limitations of Quake's era wherein you could only have so many polygonal enemies on screen without completely tanking memory so the combat loop is a lot more satisfying.  It is difficult, though.  On hard difficulty, you'll be terminally low on health and ammo.  You have to use your movement options and make good use of the terrain to isolate groups of enemies.  The level design is top notch, albeit...it's very brown.  Very dull.  Ugly.  Harsh.  Very bleak and Eastern European which is the tone, I guess.  It fits, but I'm a fan of a wider color palette than mud and diarrhea.  That said, the game is cheap, fun, and it plays well.  If you like movement shooters, there's no reason not to try this one.  Quake still plays alright, but it's showing its age.  Hrot takes up its mantle and expands on its gameplay, atmosphere, and interactivity.  There's also a gas mask horse and gorilla.  Don't ask.  You're better off finding out for yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I don't have any nostalgia for games like QUAKE, 'twas a bit before my time. So know that I'm not viewing this game through rose-colored glasses when I say you should play this for the atmosphere alone. I had my doubts when the color palette is mostly shades of brown, but the developers really make it work. The awesome combat and enemy designs are just gravy. This was worth every penny.Update: Upon completion of the finished product, my deep and profound love for this game cannot be expressed with words.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Outside of the wallhumping for secrets I think this game is wonderfully designed with an engrossing atmosphere. It is absolutely eerie and disconcerting to wander around a good number of the maps. Moment to moment gameplay feels nice with some fun enemies to fight and good guns. The hardest difficulty is frustrating on occasion but not more so than any other boomer shooter. I'm excited to see what gets added.

_childDocuments_.review: Average. The designers are really going for the bar minimum here. If this was designed back in the 90's it would've be tagged as a really crap Quake clone and left on the table. But because now, everyone is into the 90's fps resurgence with even a hint at old school ideals it's stickered with praise. Don't look into the hype this game is really sh*t. _childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game, it is a lot of fun and never gets boring. It is a bit short but that is because the game is in EA. The artstyle and gameplay are very good. The only issue I have is the gun sounds, they don't sound meaty but it isn't that big of a deal. The atmosphere is pretty good, there are a couple jumpscares but they are not loud or whatever, just when you open a door and there is an enemy right behind it.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: To keep it short. HROT is another game in the wave of recently popular "Boomer shooters". It takes place in Czechoslovakia of 1986, where something has gone terribly wrong. Like almost all shooters in this subgenre, the game doesn't hold the player hand and doesn't do much in terms of storytelling - instead relaying on level design, its enemies and occasional boss fights and jokes with some pieces of lore to carry it.Here some of the game's problems lay, as I don't think most enemies the game has are capable of enforcing different weapon usage and adoptive play style - there is literally one tactic that works on 90% of enemies, which is a shame, as it may make the experience somewhat stale at times. Bosses most of the times are too easy as well, but at least they are not bullet-spungy and each time they have very creative, absurd designs (although they are also most often based on Czech culture, so I don't fully understand them).However, what certainly manages to carry this game, especially in the second half is its settings and loads of absurdities based in Czech culture or further even soviet-block reality of 1986. And while - again - I don't think the gameplay is as good as it should be and the story and lore is so loose and obscure it's pretty much impossible to keep track of it, the gameplay is still solid enough, while the level design and settings successfully manage to carry it till the end. It is an impressive achievement - especially considering custom engine it is using and a game that slavs with interest in boomer shooters should definitely play.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Do you love Quake? Do you love brown? Are you sad you can't have absurd amounts of both in one package? Get ready to turn that frown upside-brown ladies and gentleman! HROT is the brownest Quake simulator money can buy! Or it's the Quakest brown simulator! You decide! Ready yourself for a thrilling night on the brown. You'll laugh. You'll cry. You'll make brown in your pants. Raise your anemic sounding weapons and paint the brown red! For the motherland!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is clearly one of the top 5 retro-styled / old-school-like first person shooter-games I played in the last years. Don't be afraid of the amount of brown-tones. There is no big variation in the colour palette, but this contributes to the whole atmosphere of the game. What I didn't expect was the amount of humour the developer put into HROT; this lead to a special twist in almost every map. And, dude,

Definitely browner, too, but that's okay because it's a good fit for the setting. _childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: What a strange game. This is a great game if your are an avid fan of the FPS Genre. It has solid fundamentals but neither the art or gameplay are going to be breathtaking. HROT has a suprising amount of world building everything works together well. Each level can take about 15 min and you are stung along by a morbid curiosity of what could possibly be around the next corner.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: After the first wave of the "new retro shooters" (Dusk, Amid Evil and Ion Fury), a million such games came out but very few of them I found to be actually enjoyable. HROT is one of the great ones. It's a tightly designed shooter, with incredibly slick level design, solid arsenal and gunplay and a profound sense of identity.Spytihněv crafted a deeply Eastern European game, written in a custom Pascal-based engine, if I understand it correctly. The visual experience is, technically speaking, quite faithful to games such as Quake or Chasm: The Rift, and even artistically HROT adopt much of that often ridiculed "brownness". The fact is, that the almost oppressive quasi-monochromy is claimed as an idiosyncratic identitary element. HROT is, and I quote, "set in a small socialist country neighboring Soviet Union (Czechoslovakia) after an unspecified disaster in 1986. Those times were dark and terrifying and so is the game". This Steam store presentation doesn't lie. The game does whatever it can to immerse you in a bleak and hopeless world, with ominous ambience, oppressive greys and browns, imposing, uncaring Brutalist architecture and more. If often feels suffocating and hopeless. All of this is amplified by the fact that yes, there are monsters roaming around, and supernatural elements, but HROT's world isn't really that much different from the reality that many people lived through in the URSS and neighboring countries during the Cold War. It's a brutal game world, but just one step outside the realm of harsh reality.The atmosphere is so strong that HROT could probably be considered even too oppressive and alienating to actually enjoy. Luckily, there are elements of levity and humour sprinkled throughout the levels, often completely absurd, surreal or otherwise distinct enough that they feed into the identity of the game without breaking its immersion.All the other elements like the shooting or further observations on the levels themselves, while integral in a shooter, almost take a backseat when discussing HROT. Suffice to say that those elements are indeed strong here.I would absolutely recommend the game to anyone that's looking for a competent, even excellent retro shooter, but if you are even remotely interested in this type of setting or you care about playing distinct experiences full of character just buy the game at full price. You won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I love these DOOM / QUAKE style games they are always super fun. And this game is no exception its very fun! The only complaint i have is that I got stuck on many parts of levels with 1 or 2 HP and i had to constantly reload my save and preform everything basically hit less for some sections.. But overall very good!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game because I like Quake. I was expecting some fun Quake-ish movement/shooting but with gas masks and soviet references and, yeah, that's what's here but HROT manages to be genuinely unsettling. There are some mild jump scare-like encounters but there is chiefly a lot of eerie atmosphere and times where you're thinking "oh ♥♥♥♥, what is going to jump me in this next room". There are clever uses of music, foley, lighting, and mechanics to convey mood... a spooky mood. Most of the time the game made me think of a world where S.T.A.L.K.E.R was a boomer shooter, which is high praise coming from a guy who loves both of these kind of games. The game has a very strong sense of atmosphere and a surprisingly large amount of environmental storytelling. You're able to read pretty much all of the text in the game and can interact with many objects (soccer balls, cans, old game & watch style toys). All the little stuff like that helps bring the world together and really convey the fact that the places you're moving through used to be lived in and aren't the carefully constructed videogame levels they really are. HROT is a very immersive experience despite it's aesthetic being that of a 90s shooter, which just goes to show that immersion is not about realism but rather drawing a player into the world you've created and it has certainly drawn me in.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a really amazing labor of love. It captures most of what made me fall in love with this genre of shooters. While the movement is a little rudimentary, the gun play is excellent and the atmosphere is very well-crafted. The game is both dark and hilarious, and it is an excellent vessel of Czech culture with a surrealist twist. It is one of the most memorable games I've played in a long time, and I find myself returning to it again and again to experience what it has to offer. Play it!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Like Quake and Chasm: The Rift had a mutant baby. The graphics capture the era quite well, and the soundtrack is fantastic so far. I like all the little sounds enemies make, the different interactions with decorative objects - it's like an old friend.11/25/21 - Episode 2 is shaping up to be fantastic as well, the levels more complex and more mechanics to make them interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: A Soviet themed Doom shooter.Everything works well and the secrets are quite unique in how they were hidden. It's pretty fulfilling when you sort of get a clue to what they are aiming for.Gameplay is tight and refined. Shotgun has always been king in these games and the enemies are interesting throughout the 3 episodes.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I don’t really write reviews for games much, but HROT is fun and unique. The atmosphere is surreal and so different from what I’m used to seeing any where, it makes me feel like a stranger trying to put together just what happened here, the music is creepy, and the enemy design vary so much, you have standard grunts, big dudes with grenades, submachine gun wizards, and the gas mask horses. The brutalist design of the city you walk around is different from the usually sci-fi setting of most other throwback shooter and come across and really makes you question anything that seems out of place. It makes me want to know more of what happened here. I’m looking forward to the rest of the game.Also, from a technical side of things, I think the dev made his own engine specifically for HROT which is pretty neat.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't impressed back when it was in Early Access, and although little has changed fundamentally, it has managed to win me over years later after hitting 1.0. The game's strength is found primarily in its level design. While a number of "old school" first-person shooters make the mistake of throwing you into arena after arena, HROT has the hallmarks of classic FPS level design that we all know and love. Secrets aplenty, consistent and logical progression through exploration and backtracking, and areas that feel like they attempted to be as realistic as possible with the technology they had at hand back in the day. Its setting and visuals don't gel with me as much as I feel like they should and the graphics are too rudimentary to really provide too much of an atmosphere, but on the gameplay side of things, it's terrific despite its imperfections (namely some off difficulty balancing and weak feeling weapons). It is short, though, so buy it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't particularly enjoy it. But it's cool. The gameplay is very reminiscent of Quake, but with a brown and gray pallete. The aspects i enjoyed the most are the scenarios, the references and some of the small details (the toilet, being able to kiss portraits, etc). I just didn't get a sense of satisfaction, something didn't click and it made me sad.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like it came off a relatively small magazine's CD filled with Quake 1 mods, maps, models. As you extract the mod from the CD, you read the readme file, where the author describes themself going to the science class to create levels for Quake, starting out with just leveling what they knew and then turning it into an art project. An art project to show the grimness of a dystopian presented as an utopia, but only for those who didn't ask questions. A society where the party men are talking about equality, yet showing immense corruption. Asking for complete obedience while looking down on everyone, who they say are their equals. It's a game that portrays everything through it's levels, the presentatation and the bleakness. It's not a graphical restriction, it's a choice that everything looks like it is rusting, like there is no colour in the world. And while the maps are a feat in of themselves, it just doesn't have a lot else going for it. If you loved the entry levels to Quake, where it presents it's monsters, architecture, scope and colour, you will enjoy this. It's atmosphere is insane for such a low fidelity game. If you want something more than that, it just isn't there. It's a feat, though, it's a statement and it is well done and I feel like that merits enough for a recommendation
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I am more satisfied with this purchase than I was with MW2. That isn't even to be a meme, it is the truth. This game is very well made and a lot of fun to play. It's only missing a multiplayer aspect for me.I love the graphics and the sounds. The enemies are awesome and some are funny. The achievements are pretty funny too. I enjoy the weapons a lot, they're fun and feel right in the game. I can't really think of anything to complain about. I just wish I could enjoy endless or the missions with a friend.This game clearly isn't for everyone. Some people want insanely realistic graphics that require the latest and greatest graphics cards... but I grew up in the 90's and this game is great. I believe the creator has proven that there is more to a game than beautiful scenery (although I find the scenery in this game appealing).9/10 game without multiplayer. Easily.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This is a true homage to classic first person shooters. The controls feel really polished. I love the guns. I love the sounds, the textures, the animations, the old-school feel. I love that it's pretty bare and yet contains everything I'd expect from such a game. Stemming from the country depicted by this awesome game, its atmosphere feels incredible. Incredibly accurate, funny and dark. All the tiny props and details funnily showing what wasn't fun back then.And yet, I believe it will be very attractive to the "western" audience as well! Just go play it -- I still haven't finished all of this EA but to my excuse, I played the non-public demos a few years back, so I have a headstart, of a kind :)
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: A very wonderful classic style FPS game, as many will put it it, in the style of Chasm: The Rift and Quake.Pretty much any description for the game will do: Slav Dusk, STALKER Quake, etc.The game currently in Early Access is 8 Levels totaling about 10 min each on the Normal difficulty, with 4 bosses, and 9 weapons. The weapons all feel great to use, even if the weapon sounds are slightly underwhelming. This isn't to say the sound is bad though. The sound is actually excellent. The level of ambiance is stellar, and the sound track is pretty banging.The sounds that enemies and the player make sound like they were directly recreated by the dev with Quake as a reference. The result is something different but very familiar to Quake fans.Right now, the game is only about 2-ish hours long, but it was well worth the price.This game is  in style and atmosphere, with pretty high octane gameplay that you could expect out of a classic styled FPS game. The custom engine is impressive, and very evocative of Chasm and Quake.On top of it all, once you beat the game, "Intruder Mode" unlocks. This, however, is not DUSK's Intruder Mode. This Intruder mode is an Item and Enemy Randomizer, which adds some really great replayability to the game. I started the game 3 different times on Intruder Mode and each time the first weapon you get after the pistol, as well as the enemies you face are all different. This is absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome in my opinion. This means that I will be much willing to replay the game in future runs, let alone the single Episode 1 we have right now. Along with this, there is a pisol only start mode like DUSK's Intruder Mode, so you still have that as well.There's also an Endless Mode where you hop around an arena sized version of a level and just endlessly kill enemy waves. It's fine.Overall, I give this game a 9/10. This game is  and I can't wait for the rest of it to release.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Did you play Dusk and wanted some more? Well HROT is basically Dusk's little brother. - The music doesn't have that same punch as Dusk does.- The weapons are cool and who doesn't love a super shotgun? But Dusk had more memorable weapons- The levels are okay but a bit repetitive. The scenery isn't as great as Dusk.- The story is barely there. Nothing like Dusk's and you don't get much resolution at the end of the game.- The game play is a bit slower than your standard boomer shooter. Almost like a mix between Serious Sam and Dusk.- The enemies are pretty generic, for the most part, with some standouts here and there.- Not very innovative in its game play except for the kick feature and some easter eggs. I really liked both those . Though, Dusk made me rethink how good a boomer shooter could be. This game merely solidified my love for them.- Difficultly spike between Hard and Very Hard is massive. So be aware of that when you start the game.With all that being said, the game is still a lot of fun. If you liked Dusk then you will probably like this since. I'd only pick it up when its on sale unless you just really want it since $20 is a bit steep for 5-6 hours of game play and a vague story.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: this game is great. I was not expecting some of the scares or how bizarre and weird it got. level design is top notch and the map works well. the movement and gunplay are tight. if I had one complaint it would be that the guns need to sound more boomy. otherwise this is an pretty good boomer shooter with excellent level design and some very memorable twists and turns. how do you pronounce hrot?
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: A very interesting boomer shooter, with a thick soviet - era atmosphere that will be instantly close to the hearts of those brought up in the former Eastern Bloc. Some interesting science - horror themes, solid shooter gameplay, with a slew of quirky weapons. Also a lot of interactive easter eggs. Constantly improved and expanded upon. Definitely recommended. This game brought me into the boomer shooter genre and I am oh so grateful for it.I really want it to hit 1.0.Velmi dobre to je, ano!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Followed since very early access and haven't been disappointed since. The brown-ness of this very very brown game is quite reminiscent of Quake and Czechoslovakia, the games main inspirations. Definitely a must-buy if you've enjoyed other games of the old-school fps "renaissance". Well worth the relatively small price tag. Note: Don't play the game in one long sitting; the game has episodes for a reason. Also, higher difficulties are actually difficult, so if you don't save-scum (as you shouldn't), be prepared to play some levels multiple times. The game has tricks up its sleeve to murder you when you're not looking, but they're not too punishing.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: If you take Quake, add some Duke Nukem 3D and Blood level design, you get something truly special. That is HROT in a nutshell! Tight gunplay, not a single useless weapon ( landmine, maybe ), fun details, plenty of hard-to-find secrets, and all wrapped in a delightful, eerie, surreal, and sometimes darkly comical package! Go get yourself a prague ratter today!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this one, though it's not without it's drawbacks.Pros:- super tight movement/controls- satisfying gun play- tons of secrets/Build Engine - esque interaction- level design/layout is very well thought out and tightly knit. - Super unique, sometimes funny enemy variety (horse man, bulldozer of death, etc)- immersive and comprehensive atmosphere/tone----------cons:- though it's effective at setting the vibe, frequently similar locations/textures/color schemes makes for a very "samey" experience, level to level. - Level design *is* really clever/solid, but the samey environments make it easier to lose thread of your goals than should otherwise be the case. -----------------------------------If you're looking for something with that Quake-feeling gameplay, this is gonna deliver. That said, it might rub you the wrong way if a lot of browns and rusty colors in the environment make you feel a bit dreary.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Hrot is a very atmospheric shooter similar to Quake.This game is still unfinished, so I'll provide only an opinion here.Pros:- great atmosphere - the first two levels feel like a horror genre, you don't know what's going on, yet it's scary and wicked enemies show up- good pacing - the pacing of the game is mostly OK, once you know where to go and what to do - you'll breeze through levels- music matches the levels - I mean, it's mostly dark ambient, but suits the game very wellCons:- some levels have convoluted design, but it's oldschool so it's ok- even at later levels one predominantly uses shotgun and the basic pistol, so arguably the item & ammo placement needs some review (for example SMG is only used tactically as to be honest I've never run out of shotgun shells)In general - I like this game and I'll play it more when more episodes are ready.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Currently, I think the game is too short to be worth it currently. The game is still in early access, so when the full thing releases it will probably be worth it. One thing I disliked was how lame jumping felt compared to a game like Quake, which this game is incredibly similar to. I wish there was B-hopping. I liked the new types of enemies that were exclusive to chapter 2, I hope chapter 3 adds some more cool enemies. All of the weapons feel nice to me and have a purpose other than the landmines and the crossbow imo, even the handgun and sickle have more use. Endless mode is fun but feels limited, I think more maps should be added to endless mode. I went to Prague in 2018, nothing like the game, except for the throwing up.

_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Very faithful to classic 90s FPS feel in terms of graphics, movement, and level design. Some additional highlights for me were the atmosphere, boss designs, and the music. HROT, somewhat surprisingly, manages to be extremely creepy and moody in spite of (or maybe ) the low res graphics. Ammo is not plentiful, so you need to be smart about how you approach combat.HROT has a strong start as an Early Access title which, in addition to new episodes, I would suspect will address some community requests and complaints (gun volume/sounds being one). If you liked any of the games mentioned up top, chances are you'll like this one too.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is a pretty unique retro FPS. Set in the Soviet Union, the game tries to do it's own original thing and if anyone told me this game came out 25 years ago I might even believe them. If I had to pick a classic game that looks similar to this game I probably would have picked Quake combined with a little of Wolfenstein, 'Blood' and a few others. I would not say this is the best retro FPS out there but because it's so weird (you are fighting horses with gasmasks....) it's worth checking out anyways. One thing to note though is that this game currently has 1 finished episode (out of 5 I think...?) and episode 2 which is 50% done. Even though the game may not be abandoned and there's probably only a small team (or 1 person even) working the game, it does not mean you can get away with everything. The normal price of this game is just way too steep, even if all 5 episodes were there (probably) plus the game has been out for over a year and at this rate all 5 episodes would be done in 4-5 years. If you do not care about any of this then give this game a try.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is a modern masterpiece. At turns weird, wild, and wonderous to behold and play, it never takes its foot off the gas, even during the most ominous and slow-paced sequences. Sometimes thrilling, sometimes terrifying, sometimes totally bonkers, HROT is a totally original and thoroughly unique tongue-in-cheek masterwork that stands tall amongst the best shooters of all time. Don't miss out on this one.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I'm up to the Uranium Mines on Hard, about two-thirds through the campaign, with enough gameplay experience to write this.There's no beating around it, this game's 3D textures, color palettes and sound design were clearly 'inspired' by Q1. Not that that's a bad thing though, this game definitely evokes the same fun atmosphere. There's inspired, and there's copying, and I'm gonna say that HROT lies on the borders of copying, as when I was picking up and scrolling through the weapons it did seem a little too close to Q1's system.The most noticeable divergence here lies in the location, which is somewhere in Communist Yugoslavia it seems(to my foreign eyes). A lot of references to Lenin(whose pictures you can kiss - wth), and the blocky buildings of the era are well-represented by the 90s graphics engine.Bosses have clear life meters, perhaps I'd enjoy more immersion if they had a more visual damage model(eg dropping limbs) instead to indicate failing health.My big gripe here is probably the level secret placements, which seem to use the 'odd textured hidden wall' method a lot of the time. I normally average half to 2/3rd of secrets found per level most FPSes, for this game I'd get only 1 or 2 out of the 9 they sprinkle around. Not that they're necessary to win the game because..Of the quicksave system. Which I abuse on a whim. Baby steps forward, if I feel like it. But hey I guess if you're gonna copy Q1, it's part of the package.All in all, feels like if a couple of Q1 devs decided to do a baby side project after returning to their home country, inspired by their native history. For us on the other side of the screen, something light and easy to pick up for a couple hours.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: If you have played Quake, Chasm, or Quake 2, you will find the gameplay very familiar. The story is minimal - you can draw some conclusions from the environment (My guess is an alien invasion that is corrupting the countryside), but the main focus is on gameplay.I found a first time playthrough on hard was quite challenging. The software performed well, with no lag or other interference.  I sort of felt the music was a bit on the repetitive side, especially between levels 4-6.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice, especially has great "feel" and controls; and clear graphics (in its style of course) and interesting levels with coherent themes. It has little interactive story elements which I like too. Look forward to the third campaign when it's ready!Few suggestions: Some of the secrets are very hidden, might be worth giving a little more in the way of in-game hints/visual nudges. I also never quite got a sense of ammo availability for the various weapons; also don't think I ever actually learned to recognise visually which ammo packs were for which weapon, which might have contributed to that. I'd also have liked a bit more "wind-up" for enemy attack animations, especially melee attacks - they feel instant now. It'd be a tiny bit easier but it didn't feel right to me.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game tbh! Great weapons, varied enemies, complex level design, satisfying shooting mechanics, and responsive controls. It reminds me of quake with less bunny hopping. The brown color palette seems bland at first, but it creates a surreal, eerie atmosphere and solidifies the horror elements of the game. 100% pick up if you like 90's shooters!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: For lack of a better phrase, HROT is a throwback FPS with a soul. That doesn't mean the game is a 10/10 masterpiece; The weapon feedback is a little lackluster, the level design is unpolished, and I can barely remember any of the music. But HROT makes up for those issues with how much it keeps the player on their toes. Enemies can be very lethal, to the point that only taking a few stray bullets will result in dying. That danger pairs really nicely with the level design, where the clearly Slavic urban inspirations get warped by all the key hunting and hidden nooks. The cherry on top is that HROT has an understated sense of humor, which makes the tense encounters and backtracking all the more enticing. This game isn't my go-to pick for anyone who wants a throwback FPS, but I will happily recommend it to anyone looking for something with a bit more flavor.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who misses Total Conversion Mods from the Quake/Half-Life era, this is an excellent game that captures the aesthetic of those shooters. Probably my favorite "retro"/"boomer shooter" inspired game of the recent resurgence.Definitely recommend it, as well it's still getting regular updates/patches to add features.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: A throwback FPS that does pretty much everything right (we aren't talking about that last boss though). Doesn't try to reinvent the wheel like most throwback FPS do and because of this, it shines a little brighter in my opinion. Enemy variety is great. They all look well-designed and are fairly well animated. Though there are some...Very strange ones in there that don't make a ton of sense, but I'll leave that for you guys to find if you playthrough the game.  There's quite a few that hit hard on higher difficulties, so they do a feel a bit tedious to fight sometimes, but that's not a bad thing. If anything, it adds that sense of dread that makes you take your time and contributes to the horrible situation you find yourself in. Weapons are nice. They pack a punch, although I only found some of them once or twice in my playthrough. Namely the "super weapons" in the game. That being said, there are quite a few weapons at your disposal and they're all pretty useful in their own ways. Level design is on par with what I expected, given the dev has only ever made 2 other games, neither of which were throwback FPS. It always felt like you knew the path to the next objective since enemies would respawn on the path behind you to lead you back to where you need to be. Though, there are a few, and I mean a FEW, parts where you'll be running around scratching your head. Overall, I think HROT is a must buy if you like retro FPS games. It's not perfect, but it's significantly better than most other games in the same genre.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Recently, I saw Civvie 11's YouTube video which was a roundup of retro styled first person shooers in early access and found out about HROT. Watching the footage of the demo, I immediately downloaded it and played the hell out of it until the game was released in early access on Friday and I spent the majority of the weekend playing it. After playing the entire first episode, I have to say, I thoroughly enjoyed the time I've spent playing HROT. It definitely nails that mid 90s era, Quake style first person shooter gameplay it strives to recreate. I know I've heard a few complaints about the drab, bleak color choices for the game, but honestly, I think they're fine and really fit that bleak visual style of Cold War era desolation in the Eastern Bloc. My only real complaints are that the ammo is a bit scarce, which could be a stylistic choice, leaning into a survival aspect due to being set in Soviet era Czechoslovakia, but I do feel there are quite a few portions of levels that would benefit from having a bit more ammo available. The only other complaint I have is the sound effects can leave a bit to be desired. The weapon sounds in particular to my ears lack a bit of punch. Some of the enemy sounds and the player death sound also leave a bit to be desired. They just seem a bit too subdued.  These are very minor gripes, however, in what is a very good throwback style First Person Shooter. If you are a fan of Quake, or Chasm:The Rift and want to scratch that itch to play something else like it, look no further than HROT, as I feel you will not be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good. Not entirely my favourite NewBlood FPS game, but I think it does definitely work both in terms of its shooting mechanics and its unique atmosphere that seems to capture this sort of bleak, urban decay like environment and at the same time existing as some sort of absurdity, surreal satire of sorts (weirdly evolving from a horror game into something that's strangely humorous honestly). Seems to take a lot out of Quake with regards to its visual design and overall is pretty satisfactory. Quite short as well, but then I guess that means it doesn't overstay its welcome way too much.(Note: Playtime was just way more playing on higher difficulties and repeating levels over and over again, as well as idle time.)
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best Quake-like boomer-shooter of recent memory. Edges out Amid Evil for me by a bit, and Dusk doesn't even come close. However, with the game's unique sense of humour and the unreasonably fun combat, my 15 hours with it went by very fast. If you enjoy Quake 1, this is a must-play and if you don't, you should still give it a go.

_childDocuments_.review: Very retro, very blocky, very browny, very slavic, very blasting. It's premise of decent, but not awesome, Quake-like FPS, but with slavic/soviet flavour. Shooting is pleasent and your arsenal are classics like shotguns or grenade launcher. Overall, not bad, it was quite nice few hours of shooting.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is a perfectly serviceable  old-school FPS who's main appeal is it's slavic-setting-turned-nightmare. HROT doesn't try to evolve the formula like Ultrakill or subtly tell a story like DUSK. Instead, everything - from the choice of weapons, to health and armor pickups, to enemies - are all drenched in whatever stage of Soviet decay Czechoslovakia was in in the late 80s. The levels are all "realistic" locations, much like Duke 3D, but have the Brutalist bent that's signature to the USSR. And much like Duke 3D, interactivity plays a huge part of the novelty of HROT, with an odd assortment of items that can be switched, flipped, or flushed, including Czech signage, which can be interacted with to get an English translation. Other than the very basic premise of some nuclear disaster  going awry, the story might as well not exist - it's an excuse to show increasingly strange enemies and a sense of unease. As a shooter, it's a solid lineup of weapons and enemies with suitably off-beat designs but nothing to exciting game play wise.HROT is sits comfortably in the middle of fun game and weird passion project who's primary audience is, presumably, people who have grown up in Czechoslovakia presumably in the 80s and 90s. It's cool to see that even with a flood of old-school FPS games on the market, developers can still find ways to distinguish them.

_childDocuments_.review: 3/10 got stuck on the first level. ran around in circles until i had killed opened and shot everything on the map i could. after 20 minutes of covering every inch for the 6th time, looked up cheats and gave myself a key to reach the next level. its ok gameplay wise, a ton of tiny things you can do. play pool, flush toilet, play piano. level design wise its a ton of backtracking, with no checkpoints and death reseting the entire level.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most minimalist games I've ever played. The music is mostly just basslines and drum beats, the animations are simple, the enemy designs are simple, the levels don't make large elaborate background set pieces a lot of the time and you can tell there's just an infinite void outside of the intended walls of the levels you explore, in general this game displays itself in a very very minimalistic manner, but it's not a problem to me. It managed to be fun, interesting, scary, silly, and just intriguing throughout it's entire experience, despite it mostly being brown. Like seriously this is the brownest game I've ever played. It also has no story at all, it's simply a Czech art piece about Czhechoslovak culture in the late 1980s. It's really worth checking out just for the unique strangeness and unseen cultural vision that this game lets you enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: The only way i can describe HROT in any capacity is imagine an unhinged 3 way mix between You are empty, that short lived period of early 3D games back when the highest possible environmental interactivity was the new big engine based marvel everyone wanted to 1 up each other with, And the kind of authentically crafted homemade experience you could only get from somebody living in the eastern bloc. Good open ended level design with lots of freedom to tackle something with more than 1 strict approach but will have you barely scraping by with regards to resources especially on higher difficulty levels unless you are some pro secret hunter but that's all part of the intended design & nothing is too spongy to come up short ammo wise against in HROT anyway, not even the boss fights
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is something special.This game has original quake style graphics and as brown as the game is the art style just works. You aren't here to be wowed by them but not once did I feel anything was out of place in this world.Even though this is not a narrative heavy game, there is world building going on as weird as it is. It'd be fun to see more of this.It plays like a standard shooter and honestly the gun play is nothing special. What is exceptional is the enemies, the arenas and the oddball situations the game keeps dropping you into. The game is not hard at all but it's solid fun. Every level there is something new happening that keeps you surprised and wanting to play more. The developer clearly had fun making the game and did not restrain themselves. Example, in most games player is drunk, wobble and blur the screen a little. HROT, nah do a full 360 turn while being chased by enemies cause why not? Every little thing they added was entertaining to me and I wish I could play the game all over without having memory of it.It's a short game about 7-8 hours so do yourself a favor and play it. Additional Notes:* Game has inconsistent performance on the steam deck at the time of this review. * Ultrawide works really well, did not feel like adjusting any settings to make it easier to play* I experienced a few performance drops but never really in combat, so there is something that needs fixing and it seemed very intermittent, like maybe once every few levels.* F6 is your friend.
