_childDocuments_.review: Quake had a baby and Dusk is its brother! Controls are really smooth and responsive. The guns feels nice and the gameplay got me chuckle a bunch of times, nice humor. The automap is a neat little feature and the amount of customization is pretty good for a new released early access. It still has another episode to release but I can already recommend the game to anyone that loved Dusk, Quake, DukeNukem and 1990's FPS shooters.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This game is browner than quake but an absolute masterpiece in its own right. While it starts with the bleak grey-brown atmosphere of an eastern bloc city you'll come across a variety of other environments throughout the game. The general color scheme will remain, but locations and atmospheres run the spectrum from oppressive to downright bizarre. And of course at the core lies a rock solid shooter of the boomer variety. You shoot the dudes, flip the switches, get the keys and progress through the level picking up weapons and power-ups along the way. 10/10 easy recommend for anyone who likes that sort of thing. For anyone else, it's cheap, try it, it's good stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: Overrated. Basically a reskin of every other boomer shooter you've played. Nothing about the gameplay makes it stand out in the oversaturated boomer-shooter market. Very generic weapons, level design (beyond the aesthetic), enemies, and key/lever-hunt gameplay. It's a competent game, but not deserving of the 98% positive score it currently holds.

_childDocuments_.review: A retro-style FPS with a real focus on creating a bleak and oppressive Soviet atmosphere (which it nails) and, at times, a feeling of worrying uncertainty as to what awaits you around the next corner. It’s hard to fully gauge the entire game as only one episode has been released to early access, but HROT shows promise to be something more than just your average shooter.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game for the atmosphere and visual design. The actual game mechanics are certainly enjoyable, but for me, the shooting is almost a sideshow. I enjoy it mainly for the various Czech national symbols and prominent locations, for the bleak Soviet landscapes and for the various Cold-war-era references. If you're the kind of person who enjoys that kind of stuff (urbex, urban decay, Soviet nostalgia etc.), you will not be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed my time playing this game for the most part. It's very satisfying to run through the post-apocalyptic Eastern Europe landscape and the humor is really on point (at least for the first two episodes (for me.)) You play as an unnamed soldier trying to reclaim his country from all sorts of nightmarish abominations. The environments have a lot of objects you can interact with which encourages you to explore. The game has a humorous side as I mentioned before but for the most part it takes a backseat to the horrors you face (until the third episode.) For me the guns are all satisfying to use, although I do prefer the grenade physics of Quake. The best compliment I can give this game is that it feels like a Quake mod, a very good Quake mod.Episode 3 is when the game drops in quality for me. The goofiness gets dialed up to 11 immediately. I won't even spoil the absurd things you encounter as I do think it's worth experiencing for yourself. It honestly turns into a joke .wad at this point. The level design falls off a cliff too with the only two design philosophies for this episode seem to be "haha so random" and "spawn a lot of enemies when you pick up a key or pull a lever." Now don't take this as me crapping on the game because I still love it and recommend it to anyone like me who grew up loving games like Quake, Unreal, and Half-Life. It's worth it even at full price. I would be interested in trying something else from the dev in more of the same vein of Episode 1 and 2 with more of an atmospheric horror theme.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is a fun, surprisingly funny (some player deaths left me laughing out loud), atmospheric game. Ticks all the right boxes for an older school shooter. The only thing I didn't like was the fact that it can be pretty stingy with ammo. Hence my switching to normal mode for the final episode. I'll definitely be returning to it for another playthrough at some point.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: COMRADE DUSK DUDE MUST FORCE WAY THROUGH CZECHOSLOVAKIA TO CRUSH EVIL GAS MASK WEARING HORSEAll kidding aside, the game really is excellent. A magnificent throwback boomer shooter that does not go easy on you and has more than a few tricks up its sleeve. The rodeo achievement is hilarious, the first boss genuinely surprised me (and bosses continue to be weird and inventive) , all of it is really finely polished. The only complaint I can see someone having is the limited color pallet, but it's very clear that the developer is going for a specific tone. I love looking for secrets (or "secred" as HROT calls them) in games like this and HROT does a better job than most hiding them. Excellent experience and I am genuinely excited for future chapters. Solid 9/10, definitely worth full price even now.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Despite it's dark, monochromatic and unwelcoming atmosphere, Hrot is a blessing of silliness and creativity amongst Boomer Shooters, and easily one of my top 5 of this genre. I have never seen something so creative in the most weird way possible. The developer poured their soul in every corner and every map and I have enjoyed anything that was thrown at me. Simply amazing!
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: First I would like to confess that before actually trying HROT I had a very negative impression of the game.The image I had in my mind was of a cheap copy of quake without 1/3 the quality of the original 90's Shooters.But luckily I was very much mistaken!HROT is a game with a fantastic ambience and solid gameplay.When I started playing I realized that it was not possible to use Bunny hops and that this would be a dramatic limitation of the gameplay as a whole, but that was not the case.The fact that we can't use bunny hops just makes the game more unique, the game's movement may not be as frantic as the other Retro FPS like Amid Evil, Dusk, or Prodeus, but it definitely fits the game's proposal.The level design of HROT is very interesting but also very repetitive.So my criticisms about how the game is now, early access, is only 3.Very limited color palette, which consequently affects the ambience in repetitive patterns, and a lack of good background music.I understand that the limited color palette can be an artistic decision to make the game more dark and tense, but I finished Episode 1 and it felt like I had never left the first map. But talking about the format of the maps themselves I admit that it was very interesting.Finally, a good background music is a crucial element for a game to be able to convey the same feeling of the 90's Shooters, I missed the songs during the progression, especially in the intense action parts.

_childDocuments_.review: this is actually a good game. if you like boomer shooters you should check this game out. although I find the jumpscares kinda cheap I prefer being creeped out by the ambient and the enemies designs rather then something jumpscaring me this isnt horror game. Other than that a really fun and cool looking game. it also made me wanted to learn more about my country. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT is both the creepiest and funniest boomer shooter to come out of this seemingly-never ending parade of throwback games. The utter lack of even the slightest CRUMB of story means that every level is completely unpredictable. Fighting a gorilla dual wielding rocket launchers or a possessed pommel horse? Cool. Rocking out with bipedal newts headbanging to trap music? Awesome. Exploring a crypt haunted by someone's dead grandmother? Why the ♥♥♥♥ not, I love it.Through all of that the developer shows this constant simultaneous love and disdain for his country. Some will get more from the social commentary than others, but even knowing very little it made me snort with amusement throughout. And let me just say...American developers? We need more games where every boss is a mutated and or superpowered version of our politicians. It would be very therapeutic to fight Mecha-Trump or Spider-Biden. Anyway, this is 10/10. Now please add workshop support so it can live forever.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice homage to times when shooters had little story but loads of guns, no reloads and no dumb regen life. A nice homebrewed Quake 1 made in slav-soviet-era styled Chekoslovakian temper and taste. Imagine Quake 1 but if it was released in one of USSR republics. Graphics are nice, enemies are weird and arsenal is just what needed.A nice mixture of humor, slav-specific boomershooter traits and feelings and nice gameplay that remain refined since first 3d shooters. Graphics - modest and nice. gameplay is something that i found very comfy in terms of speed and gunfights. Sound design is like homage to old days. And of course whole bunch of well hidden secrets, references and nice easterblock eggs to found. Hrot is very enjoyable game made of brown concrete of falling soviet stuff, nice taste of granny's kiflis, and good portion of liver dumpings made for dinner. It have no flaws,  i didn't found any. So i recommend this good found masterpiece. Enjoy your canned poultry tovarish! <3
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: HROT feels like a mixture of late build engine games like duke nukem, and quake, with environments that make some sense, relate to reality and have interactions scattered around like duke nukem while still mostly focusing the level design on encounters and movement and gunplay that feels closer to quake 1. HROT is not as good as Dusk but it feels like its trying something entirely different, and while not being as creative, still managing to be enjoyable.Also, I understand that checkpoints are a no no for oldschool games but, can we just get a mixture of checkpoints and manual saves? Please? Its infuriating to be tempted to either save scum or lose a lot of progress upon death.Edit:Also, also, please change/improve the weapon sounds. The weapons are very satisfying in their damage and usage but the sound effects for all guns sound extremely weak. I've heard nerf guns that sound more satisfying. Currently they sound like popcorn machines. This I think is the most important improvement the game needs.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: Finally got my recipe for stroganoff, can't wait for more to be added! Seriously good game tho, if you like the first quake you'll definitely enjoy this. The weapons are a bit more powerful so you kill more quickly than in quake which is really satisfying with the weapon options. The pump shotgun and smg in particular are really enjoyable for what they are. And I just love the setting, colors, and somewhat dry humor the game has. Overall, very epic
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of DUSK you'll likely enjoy this game. From DUSK, there's some notable differences: -The movement in this game is much simpler and limited. No crouching or sliding, jumps are small and dont effect your speed much, no explosive jumping, you really experience no vertical combat other than rare situations.-The weaponry and combat isnt as interesting; the game hands you a lot of shotgun shells, and then a decent amount of Grenades. This is good because both of these are the more satisfying weapons in the game. But thats it. I found myself not having much pistol, smg, and crossbow ammo when i wanted to deal with some arenas. The proximity mines are bad. Getting enemies to have to walk nearly directly onto them is a pain. And having such a short explosive range too. There's nothing really innovative. There is kicking which makes close quarter combat more interesting at least. I found it weird how you couldnt kick during some weapon animations like reloading.-Like DUSK with a spooky atmosphere, there are a few jump-scares. And along with it, there were some goofy events and jokes around that I really appreciated.No auto-saves/checkpoints was a bit frustrating, i prefer not to save scum but some parts of the level would kill me and having to restart to the beginning even near the end was a bit annoying on some levels. Despite all my negative points, HROT was a fun adventure. A must try for DUSK lovers.

_childDocuments_.review: The below is a mix of early access review edits. I'm leaving them there for posterity and because it shows passion, which is the foundation to the development of this game. This "review" is rough but I can't get rid of my thoughts from throughout development. I'm not being lazy - it's a time capsule. I'm leaving the edits be as this is my GOTY 2023. Therefore, my thoughts need to be preserved. This is one of the finest FPS games that I've played in years. It is S tier.------This review is out of date, because frankly, the game has moved from "early access" to "early access but it is already ****ing brilliant and I'm already very happy with my purchase." The developer is obviously a perfectionist, not that I'm complaining. He's also obviously a John Carmack level sort of genius, and loves to show off - he implements new achievements just to show off a cool thing he made in his custom engine, haha! Every new update blows me away. At time of writing, this is a very promising early access title inspired by Quake, Wolfenstein and Blood, with a hint of Dusk and Half-Life 1, in that order. Notice that I left Doom out there, although obviously that DNA is everywhere too. The soundtrack is amazing. With each (very regular) patch the game gets more polished and feedback is taken onboard. The developer cares. I cannot say more than that due to the game not being finished, but I encourage anyone who likes the above games to give it a shot. Also, it uses a custom engine written in pascal! That's cool! Super nerd cool! It's mighty impressive too.Edit: Still EA, but updates with some incredibly unique ideas come seemingly almost every week at the moment, and this game is shaping up to be one of the more unique doomer-shooters on the market. I usually avoid playing early access games until they're finished, but I'm enjoying following the evolution of this one.Edit 2 about 6 months later: This is how early access should be done. HROT is the definition of early access done right. Every single update brings quality and content to the game. I am incredibly hyped for the full release and I am honestly struggling to fault what is here. Even though it's only about two-thirds finished, I already consider HROT to be a masterpiece.V1.0 edit: There is a story if you pay attention, but don't take it *too* seriously. To say any more than that would involve spoilers for the ending. Episode 3 is WONDERFUL. The ending is EXTREMELY powerful.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a pure joy to play. Each episode is full of creepy, hilarious, and downright bizarre moments. If you are debating the purchase of this game, let me ask you: Have you ever battled a sentient, rocket-shooting gymnastics beam? A gas-mask-wearing horse? ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ KING KONG? I mean, you get an achievement for flushing poop down a toilet.Humor aside, the map design is incredible. Each map is a labyrinth of both open and claustrophobic spaces intertwining with one another, along with hidden rooms containing cool gear and weapons. As others have mentioned, games like DUSK have wide open areas with hordes of enemies. In contrast, this game swarms you with enemies in both open and tight space, something very unique within Quake-style games. For example, one of the boss fights takes place in a single small room.I cannot wait to see more episodes added, and highly recommend that you purchase this game if the demo even SLIGHTLY interested you. The demo is great, but I would check out some gameplay videos, as the full game has so much more to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: HROT

_childDocuments_.review: You know the basic formula - run and gun, grab the key, hit the switch, circle strafe your little heart out and try not to die to splash damage from your own rockets - we've all played QUAKE before, yes?We've all vacillated between moments of supreme confidence as you mow down monster after mindless monster, and moments of sheer terror as you realize that there are now TWO big bad guys chasing you and you're all out of the good ammo and you can't remember the last time you saw a health pickup (also, shoutout to furiously re-examining the entirety of the level so far, because you can't figure out where the key you just picked up goes.)Those were good times, weren't they? You want to do it all again, don't you? Of course you do.HROT is a much slavvier take on the tried and true formula, with a bit of extra silliness thrown in. The visual language of "things to interact with in the level" is slightly expanded, the enemies feel less and less like pushovers, and while your arsenal should feel entirely familiar, it's a *good* feeling. The double-barrel shotgun is appropriately kicky. The rocket launcher is clutch, though as usual you seem to take far more damage from explosions than your foes - rocket-jumping is not recommended. Hard mode is indeed hard. You'll have those quicksave/quickload buttons down to muscle memory by the time you make it to the second episode.That's my read of HROT, essentially - it's QUAKE-type gameplay (it even has zombies tossing projectiles at you from the middle of an underground water feature!) in a different setting, with a few new bits and bobs. What makes it work is that this isn't just a pastiche or a ripoff, it's true-blue oldschool gameplay, and clearly the developers approached the game with a thorough understanding of what makes a classic entry into the genre. It's a lot closer to the source than DUSK (though it can *look* a lot like DUSK desaturated sometimes) or Amid Evil, which are both excellent, but also stray farther afield than their predecessors. HROT mostly keeps to the old covenant, and it's a worthy shooter that's not afraid to quote its lineage.(PS - it's legitimately HARD on hard mode, but stick it out to the end of the third episode - things get WEIRD)

_childDocuments_.review: tldr: The game is brown and fun. Check the demo if it's your thing, then buy and play it. Edit: Important message! This game has SPIDERS! But you can DISABLE SPIDERS in the option menu) Amazing game, great aesthetics, great atmosphere, nice and fast gameplay, I am eager to play the rest of episode 2 and 3. My only gripes with it would be the weapon selection system, after playing black mesa recently having to press 3 two times to select the super shotgun, at the same time cycling to the normal shotgun just feels wrong. I use the mouse wheel to find weapons because they are organised in such a weird way. 1- sickle (okay)2- pistol (alright)3- shotgun 3- super shotgun (they use the same ammo and it feels like the Super shotgun replaces the normal shotgun completely, doesn't feel good to me)4- submachinegun (same ammo as pistol, more spread but faster fire-rate. Oddly enough, There seems to be a lot of shotgun ammo but very little pistol/submachinegun bullets)5- Hussite gun (A grenade launcher you will either get in level e1l5 or much later, so... it will be empty for a while)6- grenades (quite good, but with launching grenades bound to the right mouse button, a little redundant. I do love having it on right mouse button)7- Crossbow (Well, this is a weird one. A quite fast reloading single shot crossbow that kills most normal enemies in one hit, no zoom... in number 7. Don't try hotswapping to it in the middle of battle)8- Mines (alright, if you are using mines, you will most likely use them before a battle or when you are not being directly hit so being here isn't so bad)9- lighting gun (One of the two big hitters, it's number 9. again, good luck switching to that on the fly.)0- ball lighting launcher (shares ammo with lighting gun, it's the number 0. Just select 1 and scroll up).The game is in early access and a lot can and will change, but outside new and interesting levels (the three in episode 2 available already have me exited) I would like to see an overhaul or at least a refinement of the weapon selection system. I am sure the developer is aware of these things. Also, it would be nice if the sickle made a different sound when hitting things that it can break. like I said before, great stuff, great ambiance. Don't play if you hate the colour BROWN. For now, it's a nice 8/10 but if it keeps it's momentum it could be a SOLID 8/10 or hell, even a 9/10. Numbers are meaningless. It's fun.Edit: Oh! I was thinking, even while writing this "review" that a more "half-life"-esque weapon system would probably need a ui like in half life? name: Iron Harvest
detailed_description: Iron Harvest Deluxe Edition The Deluxe Edition includes the Rusviet Revolution and the Operation Eagle Addon, granting access to all new adventures in the alternative reality of 1920+. About the Game Iron Harvest is a real-time strategy game (RTS) set in the alternate reality of 1920+, just after the end of the Great War. The Game lets you control giant dieselpunk mechs, combining epic singleplayer and coop campaigns as well as skirmishes with intense action on the battlefield for multiplayer fans, Iron Harvest is the classic real-time strategy game fans have been waiting for. Tradition clashes with scientific and technological progress, while Europe is still recovering from the brutal battles of the World War. Cities are being rebuilt and in the countryside, the era of the Iron Harvest has begun. Farmers are uncovering the remains of the majestic walking machines that had fought on the battlefields of the Great War. In the midst of this chaos, a new threat appears that will put Europe’s very existence at risk. Secret forces are putting everything they can towards destabilization of entire countries, determined to set the world on fire once again and finally seize control. Lead dozens of different unit types into battle, carefully utilize cover and blast entire buildings to shreds. Take your time to come up with a plan which allows for a wide range of tactics, including a stealth approach. Mechs. We got mechs. Lots of them. Experience an epic overarching story, spanning more than 20 missions over three campaigns. Join nine charismatic heroes and their beastly companions in their adventures across Europe. Team-up with a friend and master all campaigns side-by-side in co-op. Command three diverse factions with over 40 unit types and 9 heroes with unique abilities. Setup skirmish and multiplayer matches any way you want. Configure your personal game interface and choose your favourite input controls. Competitive multiplayer with ladders, ranked matches & leagues. Choose from a vast selection of skirmish maps and challenge maps, available to play in singleplayer and coop. In addition expect regular free updates during the season, including new singleplayer challenges, multiplayer maps and more to look forward to. Conquer resource points, build your base and place fortifications to protect your unit production and research.

_childDocuments_.review: Good Points:+ Campaign - Well written, long, epic missions, and a ton of fun. It's very clear why this game took so many resources to make. The campaign is a war epic and it shows in every mission.+ Graphics - The game looks great. It runs very stable on my mid range system at high settings. The effects are amazing - buildings explode into pieces, smoke hangs in the air during chaotic firefights, tracers zip back and forth between frontlines, and the battle demolishes the landscape. It's extremely satisfying.+ Setting - The setting is extremely cool. Diesel-punk WW1 era settings are not new, but this is the most fleshed out take on one we've seen so far. The setting is also shared with the tabletop game Scythe which is a bonus if you're into tabletop gaming.+ The Action - If you've ever wondered what CoH would be like if it were more fast paced and action packed, just look at this game. The gameplay flow is extremely fun and gratifying.The bad points:- Balance - At this stage the faction and unit balance is very awkward. It doesn't matter very much for single player and coop play, but in PvP situations it quickly becomes clear that some units are close to useless and others can win you a match just by fielding a ton of them. - Counterplay - The game is very similar to company of heroes, but the counterplay in this game is not nearly as in-depth. Often you'll find yourself trying to balance your army between how many mechs you expect your enemy to have and how much infantry you expect your enemy to have. There are no tech trees at all, or commanders/doctrines like in CoH. So often you end up with similar army comps every match. This is not so terrible since the battles are still thrilling, but it's a point against the game.The Meh Points:~ Lacking Content in Some Areas (For Now) - There are not many multiplayer maps yet. These are going to be added over time, and the existing maps are pretty good. There are also challenge maps that are a ton of fun, and more of those will be added as well. The dev team seems to be fast-moving and updates frequently, so this point will not be an issue within a year. Additionally, there are additional factions in the setting for the dev team to explore. I'm not sure if they will ever add them, but the game is ripe for good old RTS expansions.~ Release Features - Not all features are here as promised on release. For one thing, coop on challenge maps and in campaign missions is missing. They are going to be adding this feature in the coming month, according to the road map. It does not feel good paying full price for a complete game and not getting the complete game. But, I have faith that the dev team will deliver their promises and more.~ The Price - $50 is a steep price to ask of anyone of an RTS game these days. With a years worth of content and an expansion bundled in, $50 would be completely fair. But at this stage the price is a little high. I am an RTS fan and wanted to support the dev team so they could keep making great games, so I paid the price. If you are a casual player, wait for a sale.Conclusion: Iron Harvest is worth your money as a promising RTS. The Singleplayer and Coop fun is here already, and PvP balance is being worked out. It's a good RTS that has potential to be great, and I have faith that the dev team will take it there over the next year.

_childDocuments_.review: I was pretty excited when I came across Iron Harvest before its release. A few of the game's qualities had me intrigued, but at least for me, the cons outweighed the pros.Other reviews definitely aren't kidding when they say the unit mapping is off, but my biggest gripe by far is cover. It just feels flat out busted. Your units don't really seem to know how to find cover or what to do with it, and neither does the AI. _childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that I want to love this game. I really do. You've got mechs with big dumb guns, you've got a cover system for infantry (it needs polish but it's there), and you've got some downright pretty maps. The game is stifled by a lack of variety, however. Sure, there are differences between the three factions you can play, but at the core of it all, they're the same unit with a different coat of paint. You build just two simple buildings back at HQ, which upgrade into an "advanced" form of itself, a barracks and a vehicle production facility and there is literally zero upgrading to customize your infantry/mechs. Infantry are versatile, able to swap weapons with that of their defeated adversary (for a limited time before the equipment despawns) should the need suit them, but mechs are doomed to be railroaded in their purpose. The flagship scout mech will always shoot that same big rifle and, because of this, the game suffers. I often found myself looking for units with more abilities, as well. Heroes have a couple at their disposal, some active or passive, but basic infantry have a simple "rally" ability and maybe a role-specific "throw the grenade" type ability.When attacked by mechs, I wanted my infantry to throw smokes or something to obscure vision, temporarily disable a mech by hitting it with an EMP, or try to cripple it with a well-placed shot to the backside.. but these options are just unavailable so I often find my infantry retreating once the armor arrives. I will say that AT fire feels super satisfying. Blasting the mechs with anything cannon related is pretty and feels like it HURTS.  Tl;dr - This game is the solid groundwork for something, but it feels unfinished. I like mechs but I also like options. The unit variety needs expanding and units need upgrades/more abilities.

_childDocuments_.review: Iron Harvest offers a unique perspective in a genre already rightly dominated by the likes of Company of Heroes. I've only played the skirmish mode to make the most of the free weekend. Some thoughts:Pros:Interesting take on the RTS genre.Very detailed models and graphics. From explosions kicking up dust to the screams of downed infantry men, the game is very visually appealing. It's also pretty stable and runs on all settings maxed out at around 70 FPS.Steampunk RTS is a very good addition to the genre.Some of the units are very creative: exploding travelling wheels? Check. Cons:-The lack of a true variety of units for each faction immediately becomes apparent. This is such a common feature for many RTS games. Even Red Alert decades ago gave you different units for allies and axis. -There are only 3 factions. For a game to charge you 70$ and to only offer 3 factions, this seems lacking. And then for each faction to share the same units? Lazy. I was under the impression each faction would have its own units and specialty units - it seems I was wrong. -Some of the units are ridiculously underbalanced or overwhelming. Flamethrowers are so underwhelming it is a joke, and even if you give AI a squirt of napalm. all they do is get in close and melee your units. This is ridiculous. - The base development options are SEVERELY LACKING. What's the point in upgrading if you can only do it once?- The upgrading is just awkward. You get an advanced barracks and an advanced workshop. Is this all? What about flying units? Most RTS games have a pretty decent variety of units AND buildings. Iron Harvest fails here big time.- The base expansion options are just awkward. By upgrading two buildings you apparently raise the unit cap. But I couldn't figure out how to get past 45 on one skirmish map which was ridiculously low. The game should make base expansion and upgrading way easier and clearer.- there is basically ZERO defense buildings offered. Its a joke. Other RTS offer you bunkers, pillboxes, tesla coils. In Iron Harvest you have ONE bunker that can be upgraded several times and they are all EASILY destroyed in game. You are simply relegated to pumping out units as fast as you can.-Some of the mech units are ridiculously overpowered, like the mech mortar unit. The range is ridiculous. All you are 3-4 of these along with some support units and you can pretty much destroy any base.-The starting units with shotguns are a joke. Shotguns are the wrong weapon. They are SUPPORT weapons, not main starting weapons. SMH.- Pathfinding for units who come to a chokepoint in a road is glaring: I had two mech units just bounce off one another as they couldn't just allow one to pass the other. This needs to be fixed.-The Line of Sight with some of the units is woefully inadequate and broken. I had a bunker with autocannon and the enemy AI had a bear and sniper 20 ft. Apparently sniper rounds along with a bear can destroy a bunker. The bear should have been mincemeat and the sniper suppressed. - The LOS of a bunker gets progressively narrower when you upgrade it. What the hell for? - Bunkers are underwhelmingly weak. Unless they are hit with medium mechs or explosives, they should be impervious to bullets. The devs need to increase the hitpoints of bunkers stats. Essentially they are a waste of time and materials to be built.- GET RID OF THE MELEE mechanics. I had 4 flamethrowing units who threw fire on a group of enemy AI. Somehow they rushed in past the flamers and melee'd my units to death. This is a game-breaking mechanic. When's the last time you rushed to melee a flamethrower? SMH.And the biggest con of all? The game does not have mechanics that allow it for traditional RTS military gameplay. In this game, you cannot plan, strategize, bunker down and defend. If you spend time building bunkers and collecting resources, the AI will destroy them all within minutes with overpowered infantry and underpowered bunkers. You will waste your time recapturing mines and defending against mechs. The game in the end plays like some hyped-up demo that relies on its art and visual styles, and nothing deeper. There are ZERO tactics involved. You just pump out units as fast as you can and recapture mines. For whatever reason, the game essentially is a race against who can rush you the fastest, and if you hold onto the first 10 minutes of the AI rush, you will have won. I have yet to play the campaign and will amend the review if I have time to play it. Overall, the game plays like a demo and there's a weighty feel of a lack of basic content. What's more, the price for a game like this is ridiculous. It isn't worth 70$, let alone 40$. Devs have justified the price for "upcoming material" that they plan to release - a super dubious business model based on inflating the price for anticipatory content later. I'll pass. The devs are taking a massive risk with charging 70$ for a game that has a third of the content it should have. It's also arrogant to charge this price and i hope the market reacts appropriately.Overall verdict: pretty to play, not worth the price to buy and to keep. The game has polish but just feels incomplete and hollow. The skirmish mode is broken by highly underbalanced asymmetrical gameplay that makes for unispiring and frustrating gameplay. Don't get me wrong: the game has A LOT of potential, but they first need DIRECTION. They should offer WAY MORE game modes, and allow for higher population caps, more defence options and deeper gameplay. You don't release a partially baked cake, and tell people as they eat half-raw batter that there's more cooked cake on the way. This game was badly handled from day 1.edit: I was going to use the remaining 4-5 hrs tonight to play the campaign, but it looks like someone is incompetent, advertised free weekend but shut the game down. I am unable to start it. Seriously, what a fail. Uninstalling this. Not really impressed.edit2: I noticed the constant teasers of upgrades and additional material. The devs are constantly chirping about how more content is on the way. You know what you call the game then? INCOMPLETE.

_childDocuments_.review: **Kickstarter Backer Review**Greetings!  Today I’ll be reviewing Iron Harvest; a spiritual successor of games in the vein of Company of Heroes (and DOW) which I played heavily and have returned to over the years.  Iron Harvest’s goals seem to be to implement an amazing new world into an RTS and in that regard it does very well.  It’s just the RTS in question feels like a beta for COH and not a reimagining of it.  Let’s discuss.Atmospheric Brilliance:  I want to start on one of the best qualities of this game, the atmosphere.  I include in this the overall inspiration of the setting, graphics, sound and animation. The premise (if you can’t tell) is WWI with gasoline powered mechs and thanks to the source material (mainly artwork and some short stories) this is done very well.  The world feels very lived in and believable as the only real ‘lie’ is that they now have mechs; everything else is easy because it leans so heavily on the real tragedy and war of WWI.  The details of the story itself are kind of forgettable but that just leans to the charm of it: it may be forgettable but it feels real.Imitation and Flattery:  The game starts out very strong with its heavy (very heavy) inspiration of the COH games; one might even mistake it as a mod.  If you like COH you will probably enjoy Iron Harvest’s core gameplay loop; though nowhere near as polished.  Infantry want to hug cover and capture locations and the death of a unit is a much bigger blow to the army than other RTS.  There is also a much less focus on base building and more on the slow grind of a tug of war style of gameplay.  Mechs take the place of tanks / vehicles and this causes some very satisfying changes like a mech walking through buildings or melee mechs fighting like Kaiju’s.  Alas, this is the beginning of the problems.Let them Fight:  The matches tends to quickly devolve into mech battles; I heard someone say ‘you basically build the biggest thing you can and march it to the enemy until you win’ and I feel this is very accurate overall.  I’m sure the game is very different at the high end of competition but I’m unashamedly a casual player who just happens to play RTS a lot.  Some units just feel a step above what they should (the infantry manned artillery are an example) and any weapon that is ‘anti-armor’ is basically anti-infantry as well; which makes sense and COH had a very elegant solution to this, accuracy and cover.  Neither of which seem to really be impactful on Iron Harvest.  This game uses armor grades: Unarmored, Light, Medium and Heavy.  But the sad thing is that it just doesn’t work; the power dynamics are just too extreme.  Light Arms tend to do too much damage to Medium and Light armor making many of these mechs less valuable but immediately upon building the end game big mechs everything else is washed away.  Ironically the issues with armor leaves this odd issue where smaller mechs feel useless, larger feel godlike and infantry quickly loose favor.War is hell…so is this game:  Okay, let’s talk about the unforgivable… Many of the levels are extremely frustrating, focusing around ‘gotcha mechanics’ designed (in my view) to cause a restart.  One mission has a massive army appear behind the lines without any form of notice and was well into my base before I could even get to them.  This may be a decent add for many faster RTS but this game is intentionally paced slowly and focuses on individual units.  The campaign forgets it is an RTS and tries to be a Stealth ARPG in some levels and set pieces that should just be a cutscene are turned into a mission and vice-versa.  This leaves the victory screen feeling exhausted and not accomplished.  The game also doesn’t seem to want you to learn anything; new unit unlocked?  No time to learn your base is being attacked right now and you have 5 minutes to capture the main objective.  It’s not necessarily hard…just frustrating.  The level design is just bad on the campaign, I tend to point to StarCraft 2 as having the best level design in the industry especially if you are trying to tell a good story.  Add to this the silly control changes and numerous bugs (invisible buildings, crashes, keyboard lighting issues, etc) the game just needs a lot of work to feel complete.Overall, like a mech with one leg broken and no ammo it’s not a bad game…just an incomplete one that needs a bit of repairs.  Mainly I can’t recommend a game that feels like an early access / beta game at full retail.  This game probably should have retailed for about ½ of what it is.   I don’t think the community will last and the single player has its moments but is too full of frustrating and un-fun missions just have little replay value.  I am a proud Kickstarter Backer for this game and would do so over again, the game has potential it just isn’t there yet.  There are achievements and unlocks and such but none of feels ready or gives a real reason to keep playing.  Regardless, as always; enoy!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has the most infuriating cover system I've ever encountered in an RTS. Even selecting individual units will still have them jumping to the opposite side as instructed, if not outright standing in the open. Worse still is how the cover is entirely irrational. Sometimes solid walls of stone can be used for cover, othertimes the exact same in-game model is entirely unusable for no reason at all. Constantly having to grapple with this cover system is more time consuming than any thing, and is a trial in your patience from start to end. The plot is laughably mediocre, and half the dialogue borders on being juvenile. It's as though half the script revolved around your hero being a woman. There are no less than twelve "But she's a girl!" lines from cutscenes within only an hour and a half. That seems to be a central plot point. This is only worsened by some of the worst voice acting I've seen in a game with a price tag over 20$ since the PS2 era. Its performance is also sub-optimal on a rig with 32gbs of ram, an RTX 2080, and an i9. Lagging in the first battle with more than 10 units is a rather paltry display of optimization.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy this game more than company heroes 1 or 2, dawn of war series, whole shebang, and I'm going to tell you why. It's simple. That's it. You don't need to worry about too many moving parts but the pace of everything will still keep you engaged. I just get into the flow of a match and forget about everything it feels so intuitive. You might lose your first match or two horribly, because it is different. I wanted to use a lot of infantry, but then realized that I absolutely have to focus on mechs and anti-mech guns. You can still use a lot of infantry, but you absolutely do need combined arms. It can be rough though fighting against certain factions depending on what your faction is. _childDocuments_.review: The world is on the precipice of a new war. Automachines, massive mechanical creations that move like beasts, have paved the way for an even bloodier conflict than the Great War before it. The Emperor of the Rusviets and the Kaiser of the Saxons are at each others throats, and powers unseen and unheard pull strings from shadowy corners. Between all this, a story a revolutionaries and rabblerousers, uncontent with spending their lives under someone else's boot. Iron Harvest is a wonderfully-crafted story that, although sometimes takes itself too serious, (or not-not-serious enough, perhaps?) it is an enjoyable singleplayer experience from start-to-finish (not to mention the multiplayer maps, of which are gorgeous!)

_childDocuments_.review: Is it perfect? I'm 5 hours in, how the hell do I know. I'm pretty sure I've spend more hours today wondering what I'm gonna eat for dinner than actually play the game.BUT! I did feel obligated to give a heads-up on anyone from my generation (Westwood was still alive) and expecting a RA/Tiberium Sun lookalike. So far it's pretty straight forward....make units, kill others and think the bear is cute.But the cut-scenes, my god they are something of a different class all together, I'm hoping its my computer but I'm pretty sure I've seen better animations in a game from 2010. The A.I. is also pretty messed up, one time they respond perfectly fine, other times they just let the enemy kill them and don't care about it. just like me at this point just wondering when it will end. And it's all over the place (at least in the campaign) and kinda gives the feeling of wanting to be an RTS and at the same time not really? It's throwing you a bone or 2 so you can move forward, but the pace is just the same as me waking up before I've had my coffee. Unbearably slow. Does this mean you shouldn't buy it? No clue. Come back when I've finished the game and follow me so you know when that happens. I want a bear medic. Who drinks. I shall call him Rasputin.

_childDocuments_.review: After 40h in the game and finishing the story, I feel that I can't recommend this game sadly.+ Love the setting!+ Some really cool units.- Missions in the story are way too long and too repatitive. A lot of missions either starts or end in a defense objective that just seems to go on for ever.- Bad RTS game mechanics, Mines takes up supply and that makes them almost useless since you can get units instead. - Units move at different speeds even when moved as a group and since the medics and engineers are the fastest units they run in first and die.- Bad story, the main story feels badly thought out and unpolished. It feels like none of the story-lines are fully finished and just left.- A lot of weapons has stangly short ranges.- The story tries to have "stealth" missions and these are the bane of the story, they are the worst stealth missions I have ever played in an RTS. You have no indication of how far enemy units can see and that together with a minimap that does a bad job at showing where you need to go. All this makes the stealth a chore and frustrating to play.Over all the game clearly draws inspiration from Company of Heroes in game mechanics wich would be great since I loved the gameplay in those games but sadly they failed in so many ways.In the end I hope the people who worked on it weren't expeirenced in making RTS games, because that would make me a bit more understanding.In the end and the most crucial problem is, that the game is not fun and that sucks since the setting is great.

_childDocuments_.review: Backed this because I wanted an alternative to coh2, which I still enjoy with friends in 4vs4 every other week. This looked very promising, but in the end, fell short.While the graphics are good, the core gameplay is not. In most aspects, it´s dumbed down compared to coh2.- cover mechanics not working well; only one cover instead of 3 like in coh- hand-2-hand combat breaks unit formations and is just stupid- time to kill often is too high; units are bullet sponges- crew weapons are way to slow; a pain to command them- no infantry unit diversity. every faction can just pick up a weapon on the ground and becomes this unit type- multyplayer fights are over in 20-30 minutes; you tech fast, then it´s all or nothing- campaign is cheesy; definitely not my kind of story. So, in the end, after several hours in different stages of beta and some after release, I just don´t play it anymore and went back to coh2, which is, despite being 7 years old, and with all it´s flaws and shortcomings, the better game, still. I am in no way mad at the guys at king art. I love some of the other games they made. But this one here had too big a pair of boots to fill.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good, not perfect but better than a lot of single player RTS games that have come out in recent years.  Review from the perspective of single player only.Pros:- Controls feel good- UI seemed untuitive- Graphics are well done- Polished presentation of story with nice cut scenes, etc- Level design is interesting- Story is unique- Allows for easy moddingCons:- Story gets a little overtly political or preachy, especially with the Operation Eagle.  A game about national warfare is going to obviously be political to a degree but sometimes it feels a little over the top.- Ran into a few freezes in the game when a campaign was finished but nothing that impactful- Base building mechanism is pretty shallow. _childDocuments_.review: The game really surprised me. When I started the game, I was a little bit skeptical. The first 2 hours I was comparing it with COH almost all the time. Besides that, the game is amazingly good in my opinion. The campaign had an interesting history. It keeps me from getting a good sleep sometimes because I wanted to continue playing to know what happened. I also like that while you progress in the story you unlock units a couple at a time (this is something normal in the RTS of old, but I have seen a lot in recent times that do not do this). The variety in units is not big but is just what I was needed. Sometimes you have a lot of unit’s variety and you do not even now what to do. This game gives you a good amount and I live the variety on mechs. You have your tanking Mechs and your light like snipers Mechs. I have not tried the multiplayer and I do not intent to do it too much in case I do it. I have to many games and little time and I and changing from game to game almost always. About the price I don not this is worth the 70 for the whole game and expansions. In a couple a year if they keep increasing the factions, then it will be worth it. I got the game during a 50% discount and got the whole game and expansions for 35$. At the time of this review the Ursonia faction was announced. This game is a buy but wait for a discount for now.

_childDocuments_.review: I stumbled across this game by falling in love with the works of the artist Jakub Różalski who created this world of 1920+. Bringing this unique world of inter-war dieselpunk/alternate history to life immediately hooked me so I gladly became Kickstarter backer for this game so I have greatly been looking forward to the game's release. I have to say I am personally very happy with what I have gotten so far, but I also recognize the reasons for disappointment that many players have been experiencing. While I wouldn't call this a "beta" release like some have (I was there for the beta, trust me it has improved), it is perfectly understandable that many backers (including myself) and non-backers were expecting more upon launch. The developers promised quite a bit, and as of right now, those promises have not been fulfilled. I would offer two things for any prospective buyer to consider before purchasing, first, is that one should keep in mind the small size of the developer and the obvious impact Covid had on the release of this game (they had to delay the console release to 2021 for crying out loud); and second, they have been pretty good with listening to their backers and players and making it clear what the roadmap is for the future. They haven't reneged on any of their promises, they just needed more time.With that said, you do have to ask if it is worth waiting (and spending your hard-earned money) for all the game's features to be fully implemented as promised. I think for most people it's better to wait at present. However, if you are really interested in the game's setting (Which includes the immersive option to play the game with native language voice acting with English subtitles), Iron Harvest offers enough content, runs well, and is fun enough to warrant a purchase. I personally feel there is enough there to tide one over while the developers round out the full experience.(I will be updating my review as I continue to play the game and as more content is released)

_childDocuments_.review: I have a lot to say about this game in the brief time that I owned it, and generally speaking, I did not enjoy it very much. I'll preface this review with stating: I am only reviewing the game on categories I felt strongly about. Graphics (other than art design) aren't something I care too much about (unless they're absolutely ♥♥♥♥, which they aren't in Iron Harvest). A few relatively specific categories will also be included, as I felt strongly about them for Iron Harvest. We'll start from the top:--- World Building ---Best part of this game, by far. A universe that throws these super neat looking mechs into a WW1/WW2 setting? Absolutely. And they look great. A lot of the pictures shown at the beginning of the campaign, the ones with the mechs photoshopped into the background of actual WW1 pictures, look awesome. It really sets the tone for the game you are about the be playing and man it gets you hype. Such a neat concept and it really allowed me to ignore the strangely renamed Poland, Germany, Russia and American factions because I was so excited to dive in. Unfortunately, this is basically all Iron Harvest had going for it in my opinion.--- Story ---Jesus. They dropped the ball so hard on the story. Like I said, it starts out super neat with the 'Great War' and the awesome photoshop jobs they did incorporating mechs into the WW1 photos. And then they have the audacity to throw the most cookie-cutter, bland, generic ♥♥♥♥ in your face with absolutely no parallels with the darker introduction of the game. I won't get into details, so you can play it for yourself, but everything about this story was just so fundamentally boring or eye-gougingly terrible that I never finished it. I'm sure there is an argument to be made that 'you shouldn't review the story before you finish the game', which I would typically agree with. However, I played 50% of the campaign, it was awful. If the first half of the campaign is so bad to the point that I cannot continue, it really isn't going to get above the 3/10 mark for me, even if the next half was a literal 10/10 (which I am doubting it is).This brings me to a subsection I want to discuss, which is the voice acting. I really don't comment on voice acting much unless we're talking about Joel from the Last of Us, or some other stand out job (Plenty of examples, won't list them here though, I'm sure you get the jist). Voice acting is something that, if done right, elevates the game, if not, it really doesn't leave an impact. Iron Harvest introduced me to a third perspective however. When the voice acting is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awful that I had to slam my head on my desk to get through cut scenes. It only carries over into the actual game play, whenever you select a unit, they spew a brutally awful accent and generic piece of dialogue (that has absolutely no variation, so I hear the same ♥♥♥♥ over and over from the same unit). I mean ♥♥♥♥ this game's voice acting is ♥♥♥♥. It hurts and it makes me angry.--- Gameplay ---After the difficult to bare with story, and the ♥♥♥♥ voice acting, I really was hoping the saving grace for this game would be its gameplay. Company of Heroes with mechs right? What could go wrong? I love Company of Heroes. But... it isn't. It is like a very watered down, janky version of Company of Heroes.Allow me to explain. In CoH, there is a distinct satisfaction to every unit you eliminate. The shots your units fire, be it a Sherman 76 or a standard infantry squad, feels unique and meaningful. I enjoy just... watching the combat between squads in CoH because it feels very much like (what I would imagine, at least) is a real firefight. Units are taken down when your squad loses health, etc.. So as your squad's health lowers, you know that maybe that next Kar98K shot could take out your AT guy, or your sergeant. It distinctly feels like there is a real firefight going on.Iron Harvest does the opposite of this. They took the pretty fun cover-based, squad-based RTS system that CoH has and just sort CTRL+C, CTRL+V'd it without understanding what makes it special. Bullets feel fake. Units will fire a constant stream of automatic bullets into a single unit, where he doesn't even look like he takes damage. Mechs do not feel good when the go up against infantry. They look great in game, sure, but they just entirely miss the marker unlike facing down a Panzer IV in CoH with infantry. I wish I could elaborate more on why this game misses the mark in terms of gameplay, but see for yourself if you still want to buy it. This was really the part I thought would redeem the... disaster of a story but nope. It was just more kindling on the dumpster fire that is Iron Harvest.--- Conclusion ---Kinda ♥♥♥♥ game, buy it ONLY on sale if you want to see for yourself. But if you end up enjoying it, that's cool too.P.S. If anyone tries to tell me that the ♥♥♥♥-awful Boston accent the give all the 'American' soldiers in this game is not "grab a .44 magnum and blow your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ brains out" levels of annoying, you're wrong. ♥♥♥♥ I hated hearing that ♥♥♥♥ and I am so happy I returned it. I have a Pavlovian reaction to the point if I hear "YEAH YEAH" in that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ accent one more time I will get KING Art and Prime Matter sent to the Hague for ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ war crimes. ♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: - Very cool art in unit models, maps, game atmosphere etc.- Challenging and replayable single player (skirmish matches vs AI)- Great campaign which on "hard" difficulty is a real trill- Overall good variety in the 4 races. They feel unique and play differently.- Plenty of Achievements and season rewards ingame- No micro transactions. Gold in game is earned only by playing the game.- More focus on tactic and less on strategy. Clicking fast saves lives here.- Only 2 resources and small 3 buildings base- Position and timely management of your units is everything. Even 2-3x times stronger unit can die from a basic cheap unit if not microed correctly- Map control is not that crucial as it may seem. You can still lose even with after controlling 60-70% of the map all game.- Not balanced. Some races have super clear easy advantages over others. Would be fatal in Multiplayer I assume.-Quite often units behave stupidly. Sometimes 5 clicks before a big mech unit starts moving.- The terrain behaves a bit differently sometimes. A giant mech unit cant cross a small wooden fence.- Harder AIs cheat like crazy with the resources, making map control vs them absolutely useless (in some modes)- Bunkers/Outpost could have been much more useful if cheaper and stronger. Absolutely no point in using them as they come of the price of giant end game mech and are effective only vs basic infantry units.

_childDocuments_.review: In any RTS, it's essential to be able to build a forward base. Not in this game. On the good side, the Polania and Rusviet campaign scenarios are well designed. in contrast, I hate the scenario with Saxony campaign. It's dumb and not fun. It's unfortunate really since the faction has interesting characters. The campaign should show case what the game is capable of doing, not overwhelm the player with scenarios that is too stupid no matter how you look at it. Whoever designed the campaign surely didn't playtest the game. The limit on the number of units I can create is laughable. It seems that they designed the campaign to literally tie one of the players hand, poke one eye, and cripple their leg to make it seem "difficult" -- which says a lot of how poor the scenarios are designed. Also NPCs able to see my units as if no fog of war makes tactical maneuvers impossible. They can snipe my structures across the map without any scouts. Yeah, AIs are bad. I bought this on sale and still feel ripped off.Do I recommend this game? Not at the full price. Wait until it's 60% off since to me that's how much it's worth.

The single player experience is fine but honestly this game lacks the depth of it's predecessors in the genre giving it near zero replayability with both the multiplayer and quick game vs ai being a mix of unbalanced and to be blunt unfun. _childDocuments_.review: I think the game is very good, I belief who liked Company of Heros, can also warm up to this game, but it is not quite as complex as COH, there are fewer skills and therefore less micromanagement. Also the cover system is a bit simplified, so a squad can't take cover in a blast crater. Also, a few more upgrade options for units and buildings would have been nice, but that may come with a DLC.  Iron Harvest is a good RTS and a great base to build on.I find the story very well done for an RTS, even without the bombast of a Star Craft, but the film/movie sequences are well done, the atmosphere comes across very well, the speakers do a good job. I especially like the option to have the nations speak their respective languages, I use it during my 2nd playthrough. It should be mentioned that there is the option to play the campaign in co-op as well.The graphics are also quite decent, the mechs are nicely animated, and when a TUR stomps through a building it just looks very satisfying, but why does the thing have to be as slow as a snail on sedatives?Away from the campaigns, I find the AI a bit weak, Medium is really a bit light, and Heavy was funnily enough, more eager to attack than the very difficult AI which was waiting to be wiped out - more or less.I hope that the above points will be improved in the future. However, download the Demo and try it out, it is worth it!Dear developers, now please bring a DLC and let us play as Togawa Shogunate.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Harvest

_childDocuments_.review: This game was... incredible. A true RTS, A fantastic campaign with a gripping story, Fantastic looking Mechs with unique playstyles and each mission feeling unique.  I know it follows the 1920+ universe so it already had a good base but Iron Harvest just adds and adds. this game is just so moreish and i... It saddens me it's going to be so long before i'll be able to get it for myself (free weekend).There are some drawbacks however, mainly technical in nature. The game looks fantastic but as expected beauty can chug out a pc. the second to last mission was just too much for my Victoria to handle more than 10 fps and there's no real way to reduce the graphical fidelity that much. the difference between high and low seemingly made very little difference. cutscenes would freeze and then jump forward often skipping entire lines of dialogue. it might just be an issue with midrange pc's however and the games gameplay more than makes up for the annoyances.Overall i know my reviews are always terrible but this game is an instant RTS classic and needs to be played by anyone who loves the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game. The slow pace of the lumbering mechs and infantry carted artillery really makes you strategize unlike any other RTS. Found myself drawing enemies into kill zones, and running distractions while sweeping around behind. The infantry system is well thought out how you can do battlefield pickups to turn any infantry unit into any other kind of unit you come across and a melee that sytem that lets you tie up ranged enemies so they can't shoot while you rain down shots from other nearby units. It's all a really fun and unique experience.  I like it more than C&C and maybe even more than Dawn of War.

_childDocuments_.review: Great concept and imaginations, these industrial ww1 looking mech units are great and the great war/interwar period theme are very unique, i love the theme of this game, remind me of Valkyria chronicles. A lot of people complained about the "repetitive" gameplay in the campagin which is kinda true but they are not bad, they are actually quite fun with big explosion, yes you will get tired of it after gaming it for like 3 or 4 hours none stop, but take a break and come back and you enjoy it again, the game remind me of command and conquer games's campaign where the fun is in watching lots of explosion and campy dialogue and cut-scenes. The gameplay itself is some what similar to game like company of heroes, i really love the detail on the units with varity of taking cover animations, but there is also a problem with microing the units as they don't exactly respond to your command due to these detailed animations, and the cover mechanic will make the units don't respond in time because you are trying to micro them and the unit ai are juggling between sticking to playing the cover animation and responding to your command so they won't fire their dam weapon lol. also there is very little incentive to build infantry eventually as you just want those mech, which a big problem in company of heroes 2 where tanks just dominate the game.The story of the game is fun, i can see that the devs poured a lot of hearts and soul into make them and for the effort i will give them A great compliment.  but it sometimes take some funny directions with alternative interpretations of history, take example of the Rosviet Revolution campaign, I thought you be playing as the revolutionaries and overthrown the tyrannical Tsar's government, but nah, you are playing as a counter revolutionary, and it's okay to be a reactionary cuz this reactionary leader is a strong independent woman, and the people's anger at the oppression they suffer and the lack of ability for the people to choose their leader is "worng" and "mob like" and should be stopped so "order" and "law" can be restored, I don't think a inbred who born into a postion of monarchy should even be a monarch in the first place, that maybe there shouldn't even be a monarchy in th first place?  The revolutionary people are framed as "misguided" and "mob like" by evil manipulator usurper like "rasputin" to upset the "order and law". but then again this game is made by people who are heavily influence by liberal politics so i am not too surprised by the story plot. But over all excpt for the funny story theme, the game is still fun.

_childDocuments_.review: "JuSt SpAm BiG mEkS aNd WiN GaMe! Inftry r useless" - every player who clearly never played online.The game has a great campaign compared to the standard for a strategy game these days. The multiplayer is being actively developed and they have made major release with a weekly cadence so far. Two patches alone were dedicated to unit attack responsiveness and cover responsiveness. Each faction is close enough to each other to feel fair, but different enough to feel like distinct factions (Each faction has 1 infantry only they can produce, their basic infantry has different starting weapons, and their vehicles are 100% unique) The beauty of infantry in this game is that they can level up and then equip any looted equipment on the field to change class. For instance, a medic can convert itself to a retreat and repair point, but are difficult to level. Level up some riflemen on unexpecting enemies, then switch into an available medic kit on the floor and boom - instant veteran medics. The same tactics apply to all preferred equipment & heavy weapons lying around.In the campaign it probably does make sense to lean on mechs, however the entire game is balanced differently for single player to enable the campaign to feel the way it should. Realize that campaign and multiplayer are different and the campaign is meant to be time consuming and challenging. I've replayed missions ive beaten for fun and some missions give you huge units caps, encouraging co-op with your friend.To all the fools talking about mech spam wins the game. Play someone online and try to build a mech without making 5+ infantry army first. I dare you to tell me infantry isn't effective. Dawn of war had turrets in your bases, in this game there is nothing to prevent the enemy infantry and reserve 1 from pushing you into your base and destroying you.If you're feeling like the game isn't balanced well or having trouble in MP, check out the online guides for this game. There is a lot of depth to the game that people just aren't exploring for whatever reason. For instance, people assume heavy mech for 700 beats two mechs for 350. If they stood and fought you are right. However this game isn't about direct stand-offs. A Gulyay-Gorod (final rusviet mech) will destroy a smialy (Polania scout mech), however 3 smialy's can run circles around gulyay and stop to shoot him for 10% minimum per volley. They reload in seconds, can run while reloading, and will pick that mega mech apart in 30-40 seconds. Those same smialy's will get evaporated by the newly buffed saxony artillery mech (Erlkonig) who has such range it can fire without being seen. Every faction has very interesting play & counter-play and there is actually A LOT to discover in that regard. A unit that isn't amazing on it's own operates well in packs, some operate well with a complimentary (Small hp, AP mech accompanying a hue HP, slow reload mech). Give it shot and look for resources online if you feel stuck. The community is active on discord and there's a ton of guide material out there.DLA POLANIA!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!Thanks,Dawn of War Retiree

_childDocuments_.review: Iron harvest has an amazing theme, great visual design, good audio... But the game itself is a bit of a mess, best described as "We have Company of Heroes at home". The infantry combat feels alright, with a cover system, flanking, a suppression mechanic that rarely comes into play, though cover gets destroyed easily and there aren't any craters left behind by ground pounding for them to hide in. There's also a discount retreat mechanic, though it doesn't help much.The mechs, the centrepiece of the game? Clunky, buggy garbage. Their pathfinding is awful and they get stuck on terrain, most of them are slow as molasses, and bringing their firepower to bear is an exercise in frustration. Sometimes they mess up for no reason, e.g. using Lech Kos's gorilla mech in the campaign, it started twitching and slowly sliding whenever I told him to slap a building. The mechs just feel bad to use, and this robs the game of its spectacle and leaves you wondering what the game would be like if it was more polished.

_childDocuments_.review: the art is gorgeous, the visuals are very impressive (i'm a real sucker for accurate destruction) and it does a very good job of convincing you that you're in an alt-history country! but from a technical standpoint, the game has many frayed edges which make it very hard to recommend at all. Pathing is awful, units will take insanely complicated paths (that often lead to their deaths if you're not careful) just to go from A to B even if it could be a straight line. the cover system is VERY hit or miss and will also very often get your units killed because things you'd THINK are cover just aren't usable at all. Performance isn't great either, can really tank if you have fights that get bigger than 6 units. Once these issues get ironed out (and the price drops a bit) i might reconsider, but the rough state of the game puts me off a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love Iron Harvest. It has a lot of qualities that I love and dearly miss from RTS games of the 2000s including base building, control point / resource capturing, but the game is utterly spoiled by a tremendous flaw with the AI.The AI are stupid, and a really special kind of stupid that I have not encountered in any RTS I've ever played (and I've played a lot of them since the 1990s). The AI will only attack a specific unit that you command them to attack. So the second you defeat that unit, they just stand there doing nothing. They get shot at, take damage etc and DO NOTHING?! What's worse, you cannot set an attack stance, so they can defend themselves or pursue enemies, or guard an area etc. Why is this not a feature? Instead you must micromanage absolutely every unit individually. This also goes for your engineers and medics. Want you're engineers to repair your army? Or want your medics to heal units? You must click every single unit one by one for them to bother to repair. This becomes a real pain and challenge when you have a number of units all the the same small area. You must try ti select your engineer / medic unit but it is so easy to accidentally click the wrong unit and try again in a clicking frenzy. All of this is happening while your army is just standing there taking damage from any attacker and not responding.For these tremendous flaws, I cannot recommend Iron Harvest. I was glad I was able to play it in a Steam free weekend. Saved myself throwing money away. It's really a shame as the multiplayer is fun, the story is great and the concept is excellent, but the retarded AI breaks the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Iron Harvest

_childDocuments_.review: Needs some better AI and pathfinding. Hands down. Enemy AI infantry need to not run straight into a cataclysm of mech death, just to take up cover directly opposite my own infantry. Attack-Move needs to be improved too. This makes any AI match a joke, even on higher difficulties and with handicaps.This is just a wish too but...I'd like some more cover options. I've noticed several areas on the map that would be great cover: ruined buildings, ditches, rocks and craters that just wouldn't give me the option to use them as cover. This turns the end of battles into a meat-grinder for infantry as they have no choice but to stand in the open. Sure, you can bring in Engineers and build sand-bags but that it takes FOREVER to set up even enough bags to protect one squad, they cost resources to build and are destroyed in an instant. Kinda difficulty to micro that along with an army of mechs too.Overall though, it's fantastic though. I'm a huge Company of Heroes fan and this is *exactly* that...just with mechs and amazeballs units. There's a sniper girl with a pet bear that heals units out of combat. A Russian (Rusviet) spy with a submachine and a f*cking tiger she can summon and RIDE INTO BATTLE. It's beyond awesome. Some of my favorite units in any strategy game I've ever played. And those are just the non-mech units.I hear some people gripe that the factions aren't distinct enough. I just...don't agree. The only similarities are with the special infantry units. All factions have flamethrowers, rocket launchers, machine gunners, medics and engineers. That's the extent of the similarities. Even the basic infantry units use different weapons. Thumbs up. Polonia FTW. Just work on that AI, please.

_childDocuments_.review: Looking at reviews online, I was expecting to have an experience that was mediocre, but fun enough to make getting the game on sale worth it. "A love letter to CoH with too small a budget" was the the impression I got from others before playing, but I found myself having a lot more fun than I expected, and I wholly recommend it.They really strove to follow CoH's footsteps in almost every way. Aside from the setting, where Iron Harvest differs from CoH is that it dials back on the micro, and added a little C&C spice with the heroes (a la commandos). It ends up being a more fast paced and arcadey take. The graphics are really good. Most impressive is the building destruction and damage on the battlefield. Mechs will stomp on walls and walk through buildings. An entire city will end up leveled, aftermath of explosions of a long battle coating the landscape. It's a satisfying feeling when you can't even see where the road used to be anymore, and that city block is a field now.I can't speak on the campaign--I haven't played it yet.There's a lot I love about IH, but because much of what I love is what I love about CoH, it'd be redundant to touch on those qualities. That strength is also a bit of a weakness. It practically ends up being another flavour of Coh, and while I do love CoH and how IH tastes, it could stand to deviate and expand on the formula some more. I hope this game is successful enough that they'll make a sequel, because I can really see it coming into its own and being one of the best RTS out there.I'm sure I'll spot new things further down the line when I've a more competent grasp of everything, but so far my complaints are few: Most can be split up by whether they're affective against infantry or armoured units. I guess this is a consequence of aiming for a more arcadey feeling and lack of unit abilities, but I wish there was more decision making and strategy in what you produce.  Each faction has the same two buildings: barracks and workshops. Nothing really there except which you decide to build first. This aspect definitely needs expanding on. There could easily be 2 more buildings as both the barracks and workshops can be upgraded to unlock a whole other set of units for production. Splitting them up would be an immediate improvement and allow for more meaningful choice and strategy.Outside of those two major things, all IH is missing is some polish, and polish goes a long way.They're not bad, but they leave more to be desired and don't leave a strong impression. Except the grunts you hear during melee bouts and deaths; those are kind of bad. Sometimes you have one or two models going a different route than the rest of the squad which can be... interesting. That said, being able to C+click to tell mechs to move in reverse to a destination is a much loved feature. Why CoH doesn't have this baffles me. To explain, you can go in for a melee attack to prevent squads from using their weapons to even the playing field. It's a great idea and can be fun, but it seems like a bit of an afterthought. You can be behind cover, firing on the enemy, but they will frequently just run up and vault them for a good ol' lengthy bout of fisticuffs. If it went faster and there were ways to avoid it, it'd be in a good spot. It needs expansion to add some depth. Perhaps adding an element of risk, increasing damage done to squads charging in, or units with different melee specialties. It's more of a graphical detail than a mechanic currently because it doesn't take them that long to get back up and shooting again. Now, with heroes it works as you would expect since they're a single unit, it's just with squads that it ends up being more visual flare.   A lot of things you'd expect to be able to position behind for cover, you can't. Where models position behind cover is questionable at times as well. Four might go up to the wall of sandbags, but another will be behind a crate 10 feet back.As I said in the beginning, as much as I love it, IH is little more than another flavour of CoH. Why is this? It's not just the shared mechanics, but also part of the delivery. I love Jakub Różalski's art, and the game could stand to embrace it more. Saying it needs to be gritty isn't quite it, but the atmosphere his artwork holds isn't quite there on the maps. It's there in the mechs, and it's there in the UI art, but not so much in the game itself. Let me ask you this, what do you see when you look at Jakub Różalski's art? Almost every work is from the perspective of the common folk, as towering and daunting machines of a wartorn world creep in the distance. IH has those machines, but that is half of what the art and world of Jakub Różalski is. What of the common folk? If you were to ask me how this game could embrace both aspects, it envision it being something like this:Don't just have fuel and ore resources, have food as well. The fields in the art of Jakub Różalski are those of farmers, of people trying to make it by. Imagine if there were farms that you had to capture, to feed your army lest they begin to starve. Not only that, imagine if you had to tread carefully on these farms. Bombing them to kingdom come while fighting the enemy might not be in your best interest, as it would kill the farms and farmers that feed your war. Perhaps you could do just that to farms under the enemy's control if you can't hold them for yourself? Now  would be true victory points. Iron Harvest has the Iron, but not the Harvest. It needs to divorce itself from CoH and really embrace its setting, to come into its own and stand amongst it's peers instead of in their shadow.
