_childDocuments_.review: I only played a bit plus what I played in the beta and so far I enjoy it. My main issue with the game is a lack of content and I feel like the core mechanics need a bit of refinement. I cant speak for everyone but I find the gameplay to be a bit to slow paced and while at first the company of heroes style of gameplay was enticing I think they failed to capture what made it work. I also do not think RTS was the best genre for this franchise to be adapted. A traditional 4x or perhaps paradox grand strategy kind of adaptation would have worked better in my opinion.I think the cut scenes are great and it was cool to see the effort they put into trying to bring sythe to life. Overall I think its an average to slightly above average RTS with a few unique features that's worth a try. While I appreciate the fact they arent charging full price for the game I still think 50 bucks is a bit much. There is simply not enough content but if price is not an issue than I think its worth a play.

_childDocuments_.review: Played for just over an hour during the free weekend. My review is only reflective of the single player campaign, as that's all I touched.GAMEPLAY:The gameplay is super basic and generic. Everything I saw in my first hour of play has already been done before, multiple times over, and this game certainly doesn't do any of it better than prior games. It has basic RTS mechanics with environmental cover systems which are immediately annoying and clunky to get your units into, especially when controlling more than one unit.STORY:Again very generic. The game takes place in an alternate/fictional history where "Polania" is at war with "Sovruski" (or something like that). You play a young girl, so OF COURSE you're a super-soldier who is a better shot, more brave, and a better strategist than the grown men around you. And, at the same time, you're also morally superior because you apologize to the enemy soldiers while you're killing them, and even chastise your own men for "getting good" at killing the enemy. I only got an hour into the game and can already tell where this story is going, and it's nowhere good.Maybe the game shines in multiplayer, but from what I saw of the gameplay and story in the campaign, I kind of doubt it. I cannot recommend the game to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: : The game is visually beautiful, with a great and well written single player campaign, and I would highly recommend it to any fans of Company of Heroes 2.Iron Harvest is a game that has its roots firmly in the 'new' type of RTS that was popularized by Company of Heroes 2. It has an emphasis on squad tactics and abilities with a unique visual design as mechanized walkers and tanks march across the map. I personally had a lot of fun watching the carnage of rockets tearing into infantry, the hefty anti-tank gun shots being fired, and buildings crumble to giant mechanized units. Although that being said this type of game is not for everyone, just as Company of Heroes 2 was not for everyone. Base building is limited to only three production buildings and an upgradeable bunker (standard, anti-infantry, and anti-vehicle). Sandbags and barbed wire are a fun addition in the campaign, but due to the fast pasted nature of skirmish play, they don't serve a purpose once mechs are on the field, which everyone, AI included, rush to produce. Don't go looking for an indepth Age of Empire, or the first Dawn of War/CoH style based building experience (Which I personally enjoy more). Defending your base is a must as there are only three buildings. However, bunkers soon become obsolete in the mid-late game, and fortifying a position with them, artillery and sandbags/barbed wire included, is often a waste. A good defense becomes a solid offense, trying to deny your opponent the resource nodes while pumping out units. Added to the 'offensive' game design, bunkers cost precious manpower points, which makes it really hard to justify their construction unfortunately - In the campaign I never built bunkers outside of the Saxony campaign for this reason alone, often destroying them anyway to free up manpower to use against the AI unit spam.The campaigns are really well done, and I applaud the writers for crafting interesting and likeable  characters. Broadly each mission is well crafted, but I also found it annoying to deal with the unending AI spam after I struggled to destroy their bases. The population cap made it difficult to defend as well as attack at the same time, especially when a large attack force spawns on top of your attacking units, or even behind them sometimes, causing you to lose all your units and scramble your defenses and pray they don't attack you in the area you had to draw defenders from. I prided myself on playing on hard throughout the campaign, but even after the reduced difficulty patch I could not finish the last Polania mission, as well as a few Rusviet and Saxony ones on any difficulty other than easy. Besides that, I enjoyed the story, and the banter between units on the field, commanders and common soldiers alike. This is the first review I've ever written and its quite lengthy, but I felt the need to share my thoughts on this game because I really enjoyed it. It isn't perfect, no game is, but it is a lot of fun, and you can clearly see that there was a passion behind designing this game. I've been following it's progress since the first days of its Kickstarter (never contributing to it for fear of a Cyberpunk type situation). But for what's there, it definitely shows that this game was a labor of love. I do have a few gripes, most of which is outlined above, but I felt that the experience I paid for is what I got. I really look forward to seeing what the team do in the future, especially with the story, and added factions (hoping for the Shogunate, and a Crimean Cavalry charge!). So to finish off here's a rapid fire of what I like and what I would like to see if possible:+ Greater faction diversity, I realize Saxony is all about turtling, Rusviet is cheap with flame units, and Polania is a mobile hit and run type faction, but let them own it! Think back in terms of Command and Conquer, each faction was unique and diverse and they totally owned it. From Soviet Kirovs and Desolator infantry, to Allied Mirage tanks and their aerial superiority. From G.D.I. turtling, to Nod's spam of cheap units. Give Saxony a reason to turtle, like Germany's free bunkers in Company of Heroes 2; And really drive home Rusviet's cheap industrial nature with weaker but cheaper units... because a Rusviet shotgunner should not be stronger than a Saxon stormtrooper at range, just as a Polanian mech shouldn't outgun a Rusviet mech from the front. Even just for Polania making cavalry an actual unit, with like grenade tipped lances would emphasize mobility and hit and run tactics.+ Added base building features. Upgrade buildings, wider ranging defenses (like trenches to make infantry actually useful mid-late game hiding from mechs) and maybe even stationary artillery like the British in Company of Heroes or Men of War 2. +Added mini campaigns for each new faction added, as well as, again, an emphasis on what makes them unique. Take for example Shogun units - you could make them tanky but because its all about glory to the emperor and what-not, make them unable to retreat. They'd be sitting ducks to Polania, but able to hold against even a Saxon artillery battery - like Protoss Immortals in Starcraft 2, able to tank siege artillery, but weak to a zerg swarm. It'd be touch and go to balance initially, but the players will let you know if they find things not working!- Less group spam in Campaign. I really enjoyed the game. And like I said before, I really look forward to see what the devs do next.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who grew up with the original C&C games, and has played almost every RTS under the sun (but never was that good at them) - I can comfortably say that Iron Harvest is indeed a good RTS game.Is it the next Red Alert, Dawn Of War, Starcraft or Company Of Heroes? Certainly not...but what is here is indeed fantastic.It's clear that this was made by a small studio, but it's equally clear that a healthy amount of heart was put behind it, from unit designs to mission structures. No unit nor mission feels the 'same', a feat that very few RTS games can attest to.There certainly is some jank here and there, along with some absurd difficulty spikes during the campaign (mid-mission spikes at that) but this just pushed me to rethink how I was playing the game and change my tactics on the fly - which I greatly appreciated. I will note that this review is based off of the Campaign and NOT the multiplayer - I have very limited experience with that mode, and only 1 skirmish A.I. match under my belt (which moves at a lot slower pace compared to Company Of Heroes, aka this games closest comparison).Each mech and each unit feels diverse enough that it's plausible that they exist within a cohesive universe - and most of the mechs have a decent amount of 'heft' and power behind them, where they're not a 'be all - end all' solution to combat in the game. You will need to use a diverse cast of characters for many encounters, and simply spamming one unit type will not work.This game mixes a fantastic athestic with very similar game play to  Company Of Heroes (I.E. smaller population caps, micro-managing units, cover and rock/paper/scissors unit types) that has an over all slower pace - that is filled with equally engaging highs at times.There are far less 'gridlock' moments (as in COH) where you're both just hammering each other in one spot - for what feels like forever - just to move an inch. This is down to personal play style though.I'd say that what you see (on the games store page) is exactly what you get - and the devs seem to be updating/fixing things (while providing a great season system for cosmetic rewards) at a decent pace, and will most likely support the game for a while to come.As long as you adjust your expectations - without expecting a masterpiece, and what you're seeing tickles your fancy...then Iron Harvest will certainly entertain you for a while to come.And if the developers continue building off of what is here, the game will certainly only become better with time.However, some balancing needs to be addressed in the campaign for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally wrote a very positive review for this game. Then a very negative one. I realize now that both were influenced by my own bias. This is a great RTS game, with a real emphasis on the strategy part. The worst thing about this game is the lack of a player base. Its hard to find games, i have so many hours in this game because i usually queue for match making and then go do something else. I have multiple pcs so sometimes i just forget the game is open for days on my secondary one. But the one thing that is motivating me to even write this now is the care that was put into this game by the developers. You can really tell they really really tried to make this a unique and highly detailed game. Every aspect from the modeling to the unit dialogue to the maps, you can tell they really cared about their end product. You can tell they had an idea first and worried about profits later. Even if the game isnt perfect, this is a dying breed of developer that needs to be supported, and i highly encourage you to buy this game

_childDocuments_.review: So, for me, i came in with an expectation and was thrown off by what i got. Is the game bad? no, i like the campaign, and the game play it self is fun when you get an idea for how things are going to go. But it was not the game i thought it was going to be. A reviewer said this game is just like Company of Heros, i don't know what that game is, but if you did play that game and are looking to get into this game. Apparently they are the same thing game play wise.When i first started this game i thought it would be a strategic military game involving long drawn out battles. With applications of military theory and resource management. Get a battle doctrine, crawl your forces up inch by inch while make your enemies pay for every inch they take. And what did i get instead?Paint ball with mechs. That's literally what it feels like. I'm not saying its not fun, again, But its a War themed strategy game. not a War based strategy game. you cannot apply large military maneuvers, the AI is to dumb to do anything complicated in the heat of a battle, and the anything the engineers build thats not a building can be run over by your own mechs. o and your base is just three buildings and that's it. In Multi player you don't even lose if they are destroyed. I play Battle Tech and i wanted to make a "battle of tukkyid" killing field. started with sand bags and barbed wire and had my units cover the engineers as they put down land mines. Hit the wrong button, and the bumbling walking tin can ran forward and broke all of my fortifications. I order a flank, the idiots take the longest way possible and get out flanked. I cant hold down a position, the number of units you can have at any given time is so small that you are unable to effectively hold the land you capture. And of you do it just feels wrong because of how limited you are with how many units you can have.I have not played multi player yet but i checked out a few videos online, and the strategies they use are more akin to a sports game of control points then military inguagments.This game is far to casual to be called a war game. And i would be okey if it was a small skirmished based game. i don't mind small scale strategy, But like i said, it feels more like you are playing a sport with guns then actual war. And the game is not presented as a skirmish style game. The ads, the art, all makes you think its a massive game with big mechs, and a lot of big brain energy to play it, and its just not.Finally, its clear the devs know nothing about warfare, and ya ya i know how that sound, But i don't mean they arnt military trained, i mean it seems like they didn't do any research on military doctrine and battle field theory, and just took other ideas from other games to make this one.This is especially clear in a cut seance where a Polania mech is shooting at a wall (not even joking, its just shooting at a random brick wall) as a squad of solders runs across a vary open field only to get gunned down. And its not even a trench rush. They are just random guys with guns standing in the open, i didn't even see any enemies so idk where TF they were going? The missions are not totally unbelievable, but things get bad in the Saxiony campaign where i have on several occasions vocalized to me self. "This battle makes no strategic or logistical sense! This is a huge waist of military racecourses and lives" And the camping plays the same way as my complaint! Its like the person who made the NCPs had more then a third grade education on military strategy and logistics, and the guy who worked on the players side of the game  just said "heck it i will just make it up as i go along"So Iron harvest, it's a sports game of Control points with a mech themed 1914 setting. Fun but not the hard core military game it presents it self as. im only giving it a thumbs down out of disappointment

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the game recently put in 42 hours played the campaign on the hardest difficulty and finished it because I paid 55 bucks for this so I was going to get my moneys worth, first almost full priced game I've bought this year. this game made me angry I had to take a break a few times because it kept putting me in a bad mood. Not because the game is bad it has a lot of strong points the story is alright I enjoy the mechs and the different armies in the campaign tho not sure why we didn't get a few missions where we got to play as the fourth army you come in to contact with in the campaign. The computer cheats like a lot which made it so infuriating playing on the hardest difficulty the computer doesn't have to follow the same rules as you do or at least it seemed to me in my play through to be the case one mission I was taking out the computers base and it spawned a giant army around me and wiped out all my mechs. In few missions I cut the computer off from all resources and it was still able to throw out a lot of big mechs in a short period of time. In the first train section mission the computers train gun can snipe you from half way across the map while in the second mission you get the same weapon and the range isn't anywhere near what the computer got I couldn't even attack mobs over a small forest with it so it was a pretty useless weapon that mission. The base building feels tacked on as there is only three unit producing structures one being your hq so meh. You have your defensive structures like bunkers which are kind of useless because they die so fast I didn't bother using them as in the harder difficulty early in the game you are scrounging for materials like yeah they help with infantry (still get melted) but really the computer is throwing a mix of infantry and mechs at you in quite a few of the missions from the get so I stopped using them quite quickly same with the razor wire and sand bags those are just a waste of resources cause they get destroyed so fast. The land mines are useless the enemies mines one shot your mechs but your mines only do like 1/5th the health of a medium enemy mech at 100 iron a mine they are expensive and useless so I didn't use them at all. The stealth missions brings the game to a grinding halt it was not enjoyable. _childDocuments_.review: I got this on the free weekend. Then I bought a copy of the deluxe version.Its just like Red Alert - same controls, resource gathering (limited), and base construction. Its set in an alternate Steam Punk version of 1920 (just as red alert was also set in alternate world, but via time travel). Its nothing like Company of Heroes like people have been saying here - I hated CoH. Iron Harvest is more a cross between Red Alert, and Panzers - my 2 favourite games of all time BTW... You can see why I bought it :). The art work is fab, it has an awesome single player campaign, and a great background story - 3 factions, with one campaign per faction - plus a DLC mini campaign.  I'm on the last chapter of the first campaign after 11 hours, which means (I'm guessing) I'll get 40+ hours of campaign play - plus there's single player challenges too. I dont play multiplayer, so I cant comment on that. Good value to the 30 odd quid I paid - but overpriced at full price IMHO.The main difference between this and red alert II is the resource management (here the troops gather metal and oil - you dont have a gatherer class, and there's no refinery). Building and repair cost resource, and there is a cap to the number of troops you can have (similar to C&C4) so you cant build thousands of troops and overwhelm your opponent with numbers. I have some minor complaints1) It plays great in ultrawide - but the cutscenes dont. Most games will show the cutscenes 1920x1080 and scale to fit no matter what size your screen, so you can see everything. Not so here - it zooms to fill the screen instead (with no option to turn it off) so in my ultrawide setup the top and bottom get cut off the cutscenes. Shame, because gameplay in ultrawide works great - the only RTS I have that does ..2) I paid the extra to get the deluxe version - all it has is the DLC included, and a promise a big update is coming, without telling you what. Its a promise thats a year old now (They were promising a "big add on" back in June 2020), with nothing coming as yet, and its May 2021. The DLC available now is under 2 quid, so why pay an extra £9 for that, and an empty promise? I'll repeat that to be clear - its a promise that you *might* get something in the future for free, that people without the deluxe version will be able to get as a DLC, but they will have to pay extra.3) controls dont seem precise - and sometimes a saved game will not be the same as when you saved it. Seems a bit buggy - one I observed - If you have troops in a building, theres a bug where when you restore the save, the troop will be missing from the display,(their icon will be blank/white) until you get them out of the building. 4) there are  fewer unit types than you might expect. Not a problem for me though, as I prefer it simple. But on the plus side, I LOVE the steam punk units!!All in all is a great game if you are a fan of RTS like me. And like alternate history ideas.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely not perfect with the expected jankiness and lack of optimization with a few bugs mixed in, but overall a excellent game. Maybe not a AAA game like the COH series, but its damn close and a sorely needed addition to a neglected genre of gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite not delivering some promised features at launch, still best tactical RTS since CoH2.The game is rather about the right tactic and strategy, than fast hitting keyboard.Right now you have:story mode for all 3 factions with 7 missions3 challenge maps, where you have to defend from waves of enemies3 maps for 1vs13 maps for 2vs22 maps for 3vs3PvPAll together you have by each faction not so much to build,just start with HQ and can build barrack and workshop for mechsdefence tower with 2 upgrades and minesthe 1 exo-suit-squad unit, 3 heroes and 6 mechs are very different,but the 3 weapon systems teams"mortat/anti-mech/mg" and 7 soldiers types are very similar,by each faction you can hire only 5 of 7, as some weapon types are exclusive for other factions, but can he harvested from killed enemy squads, like germany has doctors, poland MG and russia flame throwersThe Story is Ok, but mission design does have quite some hiccups, where you move handful of units over the map or enemy is spamming a lot of enemies. And it more takes time and patience to finish them, than making actual strategical decisions. The game is very good balanced for multiplayer, so far each unit has a functional counter unit.While the missions can be very challenging, the AI in skirmish is for skilled RTS player no problem.Gameplay wise it does have some neat impulses, mechs than break though buildings and obstacles, harvesting gear from killed enemies squads or collect resources from enemy killed mechs, with cover system and retreats do give quite good gameplay experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I love RTS games, I love the concept of this game but the execution is kinda clunky. Playing the game feels STIFF. Half of my enjoyment of this game was watching the cool mechs demolish each other - and oh god there's a lot of that. I remember my jaw dropping when i watched a mech WALK through a brick building, every brick toppling down and falling apart. The kid in me was havin a blast.The story is serviceable but didn't really blow my mind, I dont really feel compelled to want to finish it. You can probably tell if you'd enjoy this game just from the trailers, but veteran RTS players may be disappointed by this - a large part of me was. _childDocuments_.review: This is probably more of an early impressions than a review, but I will not be playing it any further and my last mission had such a sudden drop in my enjoyment that I want to give it a down before I leave it to most likely just sit in my library for the time being. So I actually enjoyed the game a lot for the three first missions. They got an interesting world, a decent enough story if kinda over-the-top in dialogue at times, and as a fan of C&C Red Alert I love that in my RTS games. The combat worked well enough to keep me interested, and I liked the massive and slow robots, and thought the protagonist of the Polania campaign was decent and fun. So what happened in the fourth map that absolutely KILLED my enjoyment of the game?Base building was introduced, and with it a beyond ridiculously low army size, which just made the map an absolute chore to get through, because you can't really build anything up. It made everything grind to a halt as I just saw the ressources keep rising and rising without anything to spend it on, and without the ability to make the battle feel big, and I constantly had to send my army back and forth over the open map, which felt like it was made for way for units than I was able to field and it felt so wrong and artificial to not be able to actually field an overwhelming army in an open map when you have a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of ressources. Or put up defences for anything I had taken because I didn't have any way to defend that didn't cut into the army size, even putting up mines and a bunker appeared to cut into it and I just... I really thought it was fun before, but I feel so incredibly limited once the army size gets introduced as a factor. It might work perfect in multiplayer, I don't know, but for the campaign it turns what is otherwise set up as a good or even great title into something that drains the fun out of me...

_childDocuments_.review: So, full disclosure everyone. Before I type anything else I feel obligated to tell you, I love mechs. I have ever since I was a kid. Not those skinny fast Gundam things the kids are always talking about. I'm talkin'  stompy abominations that sputter and are cobbled together with duck tape, zip ties and prayers. Guns booming and clattering as they push the enemy line, firing off one last barrage before shuddering under the weight of it all and collasping over onto a line of trenches, crushing the enemy infantry fleeing before it's terrible might.Iron Harvest looks and like what I imagined the army men and action figures I smashed together as a kid did. The effects and animations of all of the mechs and infantry are varied and wonderfully done, I have nothing but praise for KING Art as far as the models and sound design go. Plenty of variation between factions as well, each factions units are instantly identifiable which I love.That being said, this is not a spectacularly deep game and that bears mentioning as I know some people crave a high APM, extremely intense and in depth RTS. I don't think you'll find that here. The combat feels very much like Company of Heroes, insomuch that if you told me this was a mod for the first game I would believe you. The combat (more or less) boils down to take cover and shoot the other guys. Some things kill infantry well, and not mechs and other things the opposite. More or less anyway. I don't consider myself very good at RTS games, and I have been playing the AI at the hardest difficulty without any issue. The Computer isn't very smart, but i'm just here to smash my mechs against theirs anyways!Skirmish plays as you would imagine, and although i've only played the first 6 levels of the campaign I was very pleased with what I encountered. Very much reminds me of, if you'll humor me, the .It does have a little wonkyness, I've experienced a few times where a unit did not take the path I quite expected it to but nothing outside of acceptable parameter in my personal opinion.  There aren't a huge selection of maps out as of today for the skirmish mode, but the ones that are here are designed well and there are more coming down the pipeline according to the dev roadmap.Coop is as of the time of writing this NOT implemented but is slated to be released in the 2nd week after release. This was a huge deal breaker for some people but I am not so horribly offended that it has hampered my enjoyment of the game in any way.It's not perfect, but damn if I don't love mechs.TLDR: If you every wished Company of Heroes had mechs instead of tanks, do us both a favor and go ahead and click Add to Cart. It's worth it.If you are looking for the next Starcraft, a micro heavy or APM intensive game, I don't think you'll find what you're looking for.

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from someone who's more used to the 'BUILD BIG STRONG ARMY, OVERWHELM ENEMY" when it comes to RTS games, I'll be one to say that this RTS requires a brain. It's easy to fall into the habit of pumping out units with nigh unlimited resources or even semi limited production like the Halo Wars and games like it. Even with the largest  units in the game, a small group of well placed "lesser" units can seriously turn the tide of a game near immediately and make that "OP" unit you spent so much time staking out defensively to get make you look like an absolute tool. While defense is a key point in the game, I won't lie about that, if you sit on the defensive all game you're most likely going to get overwhelmed or pretty much made a joke out of at some point before the games end. Complacency is the easiest way to get screwed over in this game and frankly, complacency is pretty much inevitable if you rolled in from the games I'm used to. So FML on that one but I got used to it pretty quickly.Use your brain people, that Stalin syndrome thought of "I'll bury you under iron and steel" running through your head will get you screwed over really quick if you don't adapt well. Especially since sometimes, you don't have base placement advantage. At all.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't quite understand many of the negative reviews to be honest. It's almost exactly what I wanted from this game. A RTS game similar in style to CoH, later DoW, but within this new/old universe I know from the board game Scythe. And it didn't disappoint imho. At least the campaign, I can't speak for the multiplayer side, since I don't play multiplayer.What do you get? For around 30 bucks you will get 3 expansive campaigns for each of the initial factions: Polania, Rusviet and Saxony, all with their own stories, heroes, and individual missions. The story itself is quite good imho if not "mind-blowing", but it's well executed, especially for an RTS game. A more "engaging" story you'll only find in the likes of Starcraft 2.The Operation Eagle DLC adds a 4th faction, Usonia (America), and i imho perhaps overpriced compared to the rest of the game. 10 to 15 should have been enough. That DLC also continues the story from the main game (a bit). The Rusviet Revolution DLC is fairly priced, but you only play as Rusviet over 4 missions, no new units, nothing really new, just more story after the main campaign. That being said, the story is NOT resolved at all. Personally, I hope we'll get to see more faction and story DLCs, but that's just me.The 3/4 factions are all pretty much unique, at least when it comes to the Mechs, the OBVIOUS selling point of this game. Infantry is super boring, every faction has exactly the same with 1 noticeable difference for each one, but they're imho only ever useful to capture points, put into bunkers or man stationary weapons. Even anti armor gunners don't stand a chance against the bigger mechs. And this is where the game shines, from light scout mechs to artillery mechs that bombard entire areas to multi story walkers that lay waste to entire armies (and the surrounding city scape) or even airship carriers that attack with remote controlled bomb drones, it's just fun seeing them duke it out. If slow, methodical RTS games aren't to your liking though, you won't like this one either, especially since the AI isn't the brightest, and, at least in the campaign, will happily run into your meat grinder time and time again. They're only a threat, because they cheat, which is typical for campaign AI. I haven't tested it in skirmish to be honest.Added bonus: The factions are each voiced in their native tongue and in English, whatever you prefer. It does sound way better in the native versions, but it's a bit immersion breaking to see 4 different people talking to each other in a different language, and everyone just understands each other, but other than that that's really interesting.For the asking price imho it's well worth it. Especially during a sale of course.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing in the Alpha and Beta from the Kickstarter campaign this was everything I was looking for in a new RTS. I love alternate history theme titles. Set in an Alternate history in the 1920's we have the grueling nature of muddy ground combat this time with "Steam" style mechanized troops. You'll feel the pressure as a mech walks toward your troops undaunted by your rifle fire to suddenly feel the power as you trample your enemy in yours. A compelling campaign and plenty of variation between factions. If you're familiar with Real-Time Strategy titles the learning curve isn't that steep, you'll find the standard controls familiar enough to dive right in. Great mech models had me zooming in as close as I could get to look at them to the point I got distracted and surprised by enemy combatants more than once.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the best alt-history games produced in a long time, and a spiritual successor to CoH in many ways.The game is based on Unity, much like CoH2, but the gameplay is vastly superior.Key features are:- A narrative driven, length set of campaigns, 3 in total at launch.- Multiplayer Co-Op and Head to Head- Three distinct factions at launch, with more to comeOverall, the game reminds me of a mix between CoH 1's gameplay, and CoH 2's graphics and UI. The game still needs balancing: while early matches involve lots of infantry, later on matches devolve into mech slugfests, with no real reason to deploy infantry. Factions all play different and keeps the game exciting, but the campaign is where a lot of the shine is -- the cinematic effects where mechs are edited into WW1 footage, the music, and the story are great.Voice acting is good, especially considering you have the immersion option of hearing the voices in English or native Russian, German, or Polish. I think it will take some months for the multiplayer to be balanced, but this is worth a buy just for the campaigns and Co-Op alone for now if you enjoy RTSes of any type.

_childDocuments_.review: For those that pick this up, there's a huge chunk you have to suffer through in order to see the best parts. Really it just boils down to being forced to play the trash faction first, before you're allowed to play one of the 2 real ones. The Saxony and Rusvia factions to this game are extremely fun, featuring a very offense vs defense mentality. Mechs feel almost exactly like they look, and pack as much a punch as well. Unfortunately they added an absolutely abysmal 3rd faction that excels at nothing.That may sound like a joke, but the Polania faction in this game is absolute dumpster tier and quite easily the worst faction of any game I've ever played. Rusvia and Saxony are absolutely solid and feel great in combat, each with their own positives and negetives that complement their play style. Then there's Plolania, the absolute trash of this game. You're forced to suffer through an entire campaign of the weakest, slowest, most ineffective units of any RTS game ever made. Life a faction made of plywood and paper throwing pebbles at mountains. I don't know who designed this faction, but they desperately need an entire overhaul. 2 players of equal skill, Polania will lose every time simply because they have less health, and do far less damage. Their entire gimick is rifles, which are single shot pellet guns that do about as much damage as a pistol. Any other base unit could absolutely rush these units and obliterate them with minimal damage.The game itself can be a little slugish at times, and for some reason heavier units wont just auto fire at enemies, meaning looking away for a moment could get them killed. Other than the minor annoyances that could easily be patched soon, I would heavily advise new players to touch Polania as little as possible. Put their campaign on easy and just push through. Plus the co-op campaign is pretty damn solid. Looking forward to seeing what else this team makes, and hopefully overhaul

The complaints about pathing and unit responsiveness are valid but personally not nearly as distracting as they seem to be for some people (I rarely have any issues getting done what I want to get done). _childDocuments_.review: Let's start by mentioning I was rudely interrupted after finishing a mission by a pop up screen in game telling me "Hey if you liked the game, post a review, we need the free advertising!"Dear developers, be careful what you wish for. Because I'm a mischievous imp, and when you ask me to give my opinion, you can be bloody damn sure I'm going to give it.Like a lot of people have mentioned, Iron Harvest takes a relatively interesting setting which could have made the people engrossed by it, and turned it into a gameplay mess. It tries very very hard to be a company of heroes clone, but it fails to understand a lot of the core ideas and design choices made by Relic for Company of Heroes. RTS have a long history. And over time they evolved into certain directions for very good reasons. If you take recent RTS, or even more ancient ones such as Supreme Commander which keeps a very high place in people's heart, you see something quite important. The first pitfall such games avoid, is the tendency of RTS of old such as command&conquer or even Dune 2, to have the high end units such an upgrade over regular infantry that it's absolutely pointless to produce said infantry past a certain point. This was fixed in Red Alert 2, Starcraft 1 and 2, and Company of Heroes where units either have some particular skills/modes that make them valuable, or the capacity with the right positionning and equipement for infantry to take down armored units. Iron Harvest ignores this evolution and jump with both feet right in the pitfall by having the mechs being infantry wreckers, even when said infantry is supposed to take them down, and even when they are supposed to be anti-mechs themselves. The gun emplacements feel weak againt mechs. The anti tank infantry feels weak against mechs and way too squishy while being shredded by explosions. The game has a system of cover, but it doesn't seem to understand that infantry NEEDS to be able to pack up behind one, otherwise they will never have enough room for cover in a lot of situations. It leads to infantry models being out in the open and exposed when a cover isn't large enough for a whole squad. When you have 3 squads moving together, expect 2 of them to be out in the open because they can't take cover due to lack of room. It leads to further micro as you scramble to put every squad behind a cover. Said micro is further enhanced by a game which has a lot of difficulty grouping units by type, especially when they have skill to use, and kills ergonomy.As such, most of the missions feels like they were designed for units which worked way differently than the way they work in the game. Gun emplacements you need to go through without a possibility to flank them. Said flanking not working well enough. Absolutely idiotic and hard conditions to get the platinum medals which are neither fun nor interesting. For a RTS which has base building and unit production, a lot of missions have only predeployed units and no or little base building, focusing on heroes units... Your flexibility is as such very limited. Said missions rely a lot of foreknowledge to succeed in them. A grand total of 7 missions by campaign. This is very weak when compared to other RTS. Even more so when you consider some of them are quite short, or heroes focused, the long ones being long due to annoying gimmicks instead of fun(Escort missions, defense phases you can't skip with a poor terrain to setup defenses...). I will give the devs credits for making coop a possibility... But said coop is also poorly done, and you just are two people controlling the same units. Expect to have problems when one player give orders to some units, and the other decides he needs one of those units to do something else. A proper way to make coop would have been 2 players with 2 different bases or failing that, sets of units with different roles in the mission. Dawn of War 2 did that relatively well. Red Alert 3 did that even better. Of course that would have meant maybe to have different versions of the same missions for coop... But why not? Either you put effort and energy into your game, or you don't. And it's not a matter of finding excuses like "we are small indie devs" or "we don't have enough budget". The reality is the market. And when you have games which give better things than the one you're making, you need to match or surpass them, or lower your price. Players have no reasons to play mediocre games when good ones exist.Could the game be better? Certainly. A coherent balancing and quality of life additions would go a very long way. But it's not easy, and it takes time. Company of Heroes 2 is still trying to balance itself, and it's still not balanced properly even now. At some point it was even very much unbalanced. And let's not forget in many cases, balance changes made for multiplayer ruined key elements of the campaigns, making some missions quite a hassle to complete. And even this balancing won't save the terrible missions as they are right now. And for me, the campaigns are the main draw, as I don't care for competitive multiplayer. From what I heard, things such as early rushes exist at the moment, which is never a good sign.Don't claim you are the new sensation of RTS when you obviously don't have the skills and know-how to make such a game, because there will always be people waiting for you to eat your words if you brag. Just because you have an hairy arse doesn't mean you're a bear.

_childDocuments_.review: I typically buy strategy games like this in order to mostly play single player and have fun with friends, but I just can't recommend a game like this for that; I don't play competitive modes because I usually get too salty and I'm bad at RTS's, so it disappoints me to say that this game was transparently created for the competitive scene and nothing else.I've only played through the Polania campaign on Normal difficulty, and it just feels poorly designed. Even when I was doing well I wasn't having fun, because I was just cheesing combat because it resulted in the fewest casualties and fasted progress, and the final stage feels like it hasn't been playtested by the devs since launch. Your resources in the beginning are pathetic, and you simply don't have the resources to both capture points to gain more resources and fend of the increasingly monumental waves of enemies that are sent your way. Every combat encounter is against a group of units that has more population and resources then you can ever have, and the game demands you fight two of those groups at a time in order to progress at all. It's a shame, I never even got to see the Saxony faction, and now I just don't want to.I'm sure the competitive scene is fun, and if that's your thing, then I suppose you can check this game out, but for people like me who don't want such high-tension games, it's just not fun.

Perhaps a tip of the hat to C&C, we needed something like this. It's nice to see lots of solid FMV sequences too. I don't even ask for more quality because it delivers and fills a hole in the genre. I'm definitely buying this one.

_childDocuments_.review: If I was to be succinct, this is Company of Heroes in a world inspired by Scythe and Bioshock.It's fine for what it is. It is not as tuned or enjoyable as CoH2, but when compared to the circus that CoH3 is, the gap suddenly becomes much more narrow. Ultimately the aesthetic is what drew me here, and it delivers a solid B- performance. But I'm left feeling that while drawing inspiration from other sources, it really has no new ideas of its own.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the concept, and the unit design is fantastic.  You can pick up fallen units weapons to re-equip squads, which is a neat idea.  That being said the overall army size seems fairly small and for some reason defensive structures like pillboxes will bite into that number. The game is missing features that have been in RTS games for decades such as the ability to set a units behavior.   Some units I want to stand guard, some I want to be more aggressive and pursue enemy unit, but all units seems to normally just open fire but stay put if they decide to fire at all.  At it's best moments this game reminds me of Company of Heros but it just feels polished.

_childDocuments_.review: -50 FPS, sometimes 60 on an RTX 3080 at 3440x1440 / i7 8700K. Turn the graphics down to lowest and it doesnt change a thing. This isn't just me, it will be the same for you no matter your configuration or settings.-If you issue a command (left click on a unit then right click to make them move) then quickly issue another command to another unit the game will sometimes not actually register that 2nd command, but of course you don't notice this happened because youre clicking so fast. _childDocuments_.review: I would not recommend this game at it's current state, I may change my rating once they do something with the game to fix a lot of the Glaring issues, below will be the breakdown on the good and BAD sides of this game. I will be as detailed as can be to help those who might be interested in this game but also want to know more about this game. 1. Menu and Interface (start screen and game interface) Good:- looks niceThat's it!BAD:- clunky- too designed for looks rather than function- In game achievements (required for account cosmetics and other bonuses) soooooo messy (not optimized and time consuming) each achievement you have to unlock individually, no claim all button, and each one has to undergo an animation that adds to the time... that's time of your life wasted in none essential "FLUFF" PLEASE ADD A "CLAIM ALL" BUTTON you're needlessly wasting time. -too much loading between interfaces (due to the aesthetic nature of many of it's menu loading between each area moves between 3-5 seconds at least, this may not be big but it adds up Note: my unit is a mid tier gaming rig. compared to other titles this is a bit annoying, not to everyone but I added it here to inform those who may find this annoying)- no choice for static image (not everyone likes or needs animated background more often than not it's a waste of processing power)2. AI (both enemies and your units)Good:- AI CAN be challenging and fun to play with.again... THAT's it!BAD:- AI CHEATS A LOT (the AI seems to be able to produce units faster and cheaper than players) at first I thought it may be similar to other games that the AI teams just share resource unlike player teams BUT after one game where one of our friends disconnected near the end of the game (note: we all had little to no resources left at that point of the game) the AI managed to pull out several units within the span of a few seconds (not cheap units mind you) like MAGIC... - AI pathing is broken (your units) this is not always the case 100% of the time, but your units can sometimes be as DUMB as Bricks, choosing to go a longer path OR running into enemies despite having a clear path of choice nearby (more often than not this happens to infantry units) .- AI Logic is Broken (this may fall more into how the game has become with the expansion rather than a core issue) some units that can clearly hit targets (have line of sight and CAN hit those targets specifically (flying)) still move closer just to fire... this may be the case if the Game did not give is the attack range of the units... BUT it did, you have the option to show range, and more often than not this range means nothing (mostly on mech units and field guns/cannons/machine guns) even units having a clear shot... and have shot said target before (air unit) often needs to re-position often to a point they cannot fire (often the case with bigger mechs) - AI controlled unites seem to be stronger and more accurate than Player units (specially early game)  early game encounters even 1 on 1 will often end up with you being defeated (even without cover mechanics or such, even same unit types) AI seem to be more accurate than your own.3. Game-play and MechanicsGood:- Fresh take on some RTS mechanics.- unit movement is fluid does not feel too roboticBAD:- COVER MECHANIC IS A JOKE, I've played several games where the enemy has "Gone to cover" and i shot them from obvious openings (such as the back or sides of said cover) and they seem to sponge all the bullets off. I've played a lot of RTS that have cover mechanics and none are as BAD as this one, and I'm not talking about garrison cover either, this game can have units lean on the wall for cover BUT getting shot from the open area of said wall STILL provides cover, rather than how cover works in most games (cover reducing damage due to shots hitting the wall or missing) this games feels like it apples a damage reduction to units for just being IN cover even IF YOU"RE SHOOTING THEM IN THE BACK!- Unit models are oddly overlapping. several instances that I click one unit and send it forward only to see I GOT 2 squads from one click (Note: a drag selection just mouse click) 4. Units and Character design and functionalityGood:- Unique Base Units design per faction (base and not DLC units)- Unique Mech design per faction- Unique Base designs per faction- Each mech unit plays differently but close enough that you don't get confused or overwhelmed- limitation of certain infantry unit types per faction - good and varied unit roster (Base Game)BAD- Shared unit types on flyers (Expansion/DLC) only unique flyers are the new faction and even they have the same onld basic flyers added with the ones they have (sloppy work) - a lot of unit features are just aesthetic (guns that don't fire) (armor that does nothing) (does not have a good feel unlike games of the same genre) - Unite rank value Hardly means anything (for infantry it makes them tougher for mechs it's not noticeable) unlike other games where rank either gives improved range, damage, or armor, other than infantry ranks are hardly noticeable on other units (Example: rank 4 mech Hero can't survive a rank 2 anti armor infantry) - Unit value per feature greatly unused (melee units that should be tanky and tough for "MELEE" Are not, and die more often than not heading towards their target) while range units often share the simple weakness of back attacks (which arty units can exploit)

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent presentation but jank is just terrible to handle. Takes away from enjoying it too much. Missclicks, double clicks for single action waiting for it to eventually decide to respond, bad pathing, freezing bug. -Edit after completing campaign.I still finished it, but after playing Polonia on hard, last mission took me 4 hours straight with 4 retries. A 4 hour mission, apparently I needed it. After switching to easy I noticed how the game started running better. Because of the jank, you don't need to use your abilities as well and the game runs better. Basically, the issue is complete lack of focus on gameplay. It's just bad, there's potential there, but it's just not there. Minimal effort done on gameplay or balancing. The general idea is that infantry is quick, captures resources and is versatile, mechs are very slow and lumbering and do not fit through certain paths. It's great, I love watching when mech that is larger than a building crashes through it. Beautiful. However, what you need is that those mechs are centerpiece of battle - they're slow, but extremely heavy hitting should focus your effort around them, where mechs push the line, while infantry supports them, fights other infantry, and try to provide edge for your mechs to take down enemy. It's just not that. The mechs are powerful enough only in groups, but they're still squishy and don't have the weight. You just spam certain mechs and rush the enemy, overwhelming their build. Just not satisfying. Crewed weapons are pointless, only usable for base defence, mechs aren't powerful enough and are too cheap, infantry only builds run into hard counters - machine gun and then just get wiped out, meaning you need to have mechs to take out hard counters, and you need alot of them, so you might as well run mech only build, with infantry for capture only. The mission design is infuriating. Way too many no-base missions, which are tedious, because there's no interesting abilities to work with and they recharge at snail pace. Base missions are also bad, because sometimes you think you're fighting an opponent, but no it's just scripted spawns, which make your strategy completely irrelevant, just rush through, to the sometimes vague objectives and push on. Oh and the jank, is just tedious to deal with. There's no place for tactical game. The gameplay, clearly was not a priority. For instance, Usonia brought new type of units - airships, which are just mechs, but slower and can move through terrain. OK, maybe interesting. But the problem is, that every single Usonia mission has anti-air turrets, meaning your new type of unit is utterly useless. It's much more efficient to run infantry and light mech build to rush through. Oh and armor types - you have 4 armors - unarmored, light, medium and heavy. Weapon penetration is corresponding. You can still penetrate medium armor with unarmored weapons, but it's very hard. OK, there's potential here. Problem is, later heroes get medium-heavy weapons, which makes them significantly more efficient than any mech of any size, because armor penetration means that if you do 150 dmg against infantry you do 150 dmg against a mech, making infantry sometimes harder to kill than a mech. It's just unbalanced and poorly thought through gameplay. Clearly art department takes the priority and I think they're convinced their story is good, which it isn't. It starts promising, but very soon becomes standard vague conspiracy filled with cameo cliches. Nikola Tesla is in this, that should tell you level of storytelling. The American campaign is frankly insulting in it's formulaism and banality. Just boring. So much potential, great art, so wasted. Still gonna try world map and some missions before quitting. --after trying world map and a few skirmishing--The same issue with scripted events and forces just ruined fun in world map. It doesn't clearly explain or show what does reinforcing region mean, you get random and bewildering starting options and the army you get when you play, is just random. Sometimes you get partial infantry, reinforcements are whatever, sometimes you get partial mech support. The worst part was when I was assaulting Polish capital. There's a scripted mech unit inside a  camp you had to take out. I did, then pushed forward the line and a mech unit (pretty powerful) spawned right behind me. I had to build 5 bunkers surrounding their spawn point to deal with them because they respawned pretty regularly. This is just insulting design and those scripted spawns take away from enjoying the game, because you can't plan, it's just go all the time, which gets boring. As a comparison to say, Rise of Nations - no contest. Much better map game, much better RTS, still the only ones, that managed to make aircraft feel like aircraft. Tried multiplayer skirmishing, it's fine. I'm sure if I tried long enough I'd find some balancing issues, but at least there's no scripted spawning, so when you get snowballed, it's fair. There's a few creative modes and there's real creativity in this game, just all wasted.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game, even less so for the AAA price tag it has. Maybe during a big sale it's nice to get, but don't expect a polished game.EDIT: Regarding the sale, that's where I got the game myself. Just wanted to point out I wouldn't recommend buying for full price. Since you actually care about comments (and that's commendable because most devs don't), let me be a bit more specific about the issues I have, what I consider from most to least important:1. There are a lot of bugs. Solely playing the campaign, there have been plenty black screens that got me stuck where I had to Alt F4 out. There are also many instances where things disappear or fade out for no reason, such as the enemy mech boss disappearing during the cutscene after the 3rd wave in that defense mission, or some units' attacks don't even work, like the shotgun ability in the gorilla mech hero. This is my main reason to say the game isn't really polished.2. There are a lot of problems with the controls, even when I rebind the keys, the final result is a mess. If I opt for a grid-keys-based layout, buttons don't make sense as the QWER line uses all main commands when it should use special actions and viceversa. When I try to adapt it to a real, usable layout (A: Attack, S: Stop, QWER: Abilities, etc.) there's still no way to adapt the visuals to match the layout, resulting in the next problem, which I swear I don't understand why no RTS has ever thought that this is a big deal, when I think it's pretty much necessary and should have happened out of raw evolution of the genre, which is even more obvious when you look at MOBAs and they all use the same layout. Then again, even if you set keys perfectly and forget about the UI, whenever you want to build something o train a unit it suddenly becomes even more tedious as keys just seem to be randomized. This is also a big deal for me, and wouldn't disregard in an RTS from late 2019.3. During the course of the game, there's a lot of emphasis on using cover. When playing skirmish normal matches this works fine, and maps seem to have been designed with that in mind, but my experience after 10 hours in campaign mode is that most buildings can't be garrisoned, there's barely no cover at all, and the little pieces I've found are just positioned for enemy squads. This is just a problem for campaign mode of course, but still relevant.4. I can't get stable 60FPS in lowest settings with a 6 core CPU @4700MHz and a 1070. And I'm not even talking about massive battles, just 2 squads on screen shooting each other and it already dips.5. Sometimes the units don't feel responsive. moving a squad to a point, the squad goes somewhere else. Takes the wrong cover direction even when manually appointed to do so, some mechs also like to facebump each other and block themselves, and sometimes I've killed and lost mechs because they refuse to turn around and fight whomever is shooting them, and they just idle there and die. Not saying units should be super smart, but there's a minimum I would expect.I've noted all this in your Discord at one point or another, and also submitted some screenshots whenever I found a bug with a description of how to pop it up. I understand you are still working in fixing a lot of stuff, but so far my perception of the game has to be negative. If all these things are fixed in the future I'll change the review.Thanks for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: All I'm going to say is this: Great game set in a unique environment unfortunately plagued by heaps of drama-- be it about backers, pricing or bugs.I don't have a clue how IH attracted such groups of people where the entire community boils down to 4 subsections: -People who enjoy the game and don't care about the rest-- mostly single players.-People who are still asking about getting an aluminium figurine (which they should have already gotten ages ago). -People who want a partial refund despite being tens of hours of usage in. -People who somehow blindly hate it saying that first CoH is better, which it objectively isn't from gameplay to the technologies behind behind them both-- never-mind the campaign actually being good.Best way to play Iron Harvest? Stay away from the community and other players like they're the plague. They're just like League of Legends no-lives but if you replaced anger with salt.Overall recommend if you're into RTS games. Levelling is a great little system to keep you coming back. Also sound design and graphics are absolutely gorgeous. Campaign is great too, and skirmish can be tweaked to get different star ratings and challenges (that actually count to your levelling progression).Only thing that I'd really want to change about the game is so they included some sort of conquest mode, where you play a string of skirmish maps in a row, with each affecting how much progression you've made against an enemy. Like small campaigns almost, but all action.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following this project since 2018, and I really, really want to enjoy this game.  But I just cant because it isn't finished, and the devs should have pushed the release. My thoughts fall largely in alignment with the professional reviews you see online. The unit AI is ROUGH, and there just isn't as much content as you would expect, especially post campaign. I am having the same difficulty with unit AI & pathing, unit balance, and just plain having the units do what you click on them to do (they screw up, a lot). Enemy AI inconsistently ranges from terminator to potato, some will just stand in your line of fire, others will kite you from all directions like Che Guevara.Then to top it all off, they released(with the game) a 5 week road map full of content (like ranked matches and some direly needed maps- only 8 so far) that should have been included in the first place.The story and campaign are pretty good, with good voice acting. But only 20ish missions between the 3 campaigns.I miss the days when you got a full game on release.... seems like that is the exception instead of the norm now.tl;drStory= 9/10Game mechanics+ 3/10Content= 5/10Wait at least 3-6 months until the devs actually flesh out the game.

_childDocuments_.review: As cool as the setting is, sadly it's incredibly clunky to play and feels very unresponsive. Units are slugs - not just the mechs, but the soldiers too. Pathfinding is very basic. You use a unit ability and it takes ages for it to go off, if at all. Makes microing multiple battles difficult, because you can't fire-and-forget abilities, because you need to be constantly worried about whether the units do what you tell them and not something stupid. It's very difficult to get them to line up behind walls (on the correct side), especially if you have multiple squads grouped.Well, at least the game is very slow paced, so that kinda smooths things out a bit, but it's annoying to have to worry about your units doing something dumb. It's a shame too, because the unit abilities are fairly impactful, so microing them would be otherwise enjoyable (well placed grenade could blow up half a squad), but it's too unresponsive for that. If you send a squad into a building, you can't re-select them by pressing their control group, even though it shows their number above the house. You have to click the house... why?! Garrisoned houses seem to be bugged too. I can't really tell the units inside to focus any specific enemy. They just shoot whatever.The default control scheme is moronic too. Who tf thought camera controls were important enough to be put on WASD?!!??!?! Guys, this is a strategy game, helloooooo?! The unit hotkeys are like in Starcraft (personally am a fan of the DoTA standard)... Yeah, I pretty much rebound everything.Beyond that, this RTS just has a lot of mechanics I dislike (coming from C&C), starting with the unit cap. Base building is limited, there's no upgrade branching (as far as I'm aware).You can pick up new weapons with your soldiers from crates or take from enemies. This is really neat, but that's all there is in terms of upgrades. They feel more like side-grades, depending on what you need (machine-gun vs. soldiers, launchers vs. mechs, engineer for building/repair, medic for heals etc.). This just doesn't cut it for me.I suppose if you liked Company of Heroes you'll like this... maybe?

_childDocuments_.review: I...do not often review games. You can check my profile and see as much, I'm sure.But *this game*? I like this game. And after 40 hours I can certainly say I recommend it.Note that I have yet to play the multiplayer, so I can't accurately comment on that. This will be strictly for the single-player portions of the game, such as the campaign, skirmishes against AI, and challenge modes.In those 40 hours, I've played through more than half of the campaign, which is itself split into 4 separate campaigns telling an intertwined story from the perspective of 4 different factions. The final of the 4 was added in recent DLC, so I can't remark on whether it is as related to the over all story as the other 3. Regardless, the campaign as a whole is well worth the time and price. Lots of varied missions that keep things interesting beyond the simple build-a-base-and-take-over that you might expect, though there are some of those as well, but they never feel out of place or boring, I think.The mechanics of the game are sound, if nothing necessarily ground-breaking in that regard. In infantry play, it has the look and feel of a company of heroes, but without that level of tactical depth. There's a cover system and garrisoning, but tt's a bit more C&C in how it balances unit types and combat, which is to say a bit more rock-paper-scissors, as other reviewers have remarked. This is further augmented by a unit experience gain system that sees your units ranks up the longer they are kept alive fighting, capturing resources and objectives, or using abilities. This rewards keeping your units from being wiped out, as even if they are down to their last man and a sliver of health, they can retreat to base and be reinforced, all without losing their veteran status. And experienced units that are higher ranks are noticeably better than fresh ones, and you grow attached to them and feel the loss if and when they get destroyed. And this goes for more than infantry, which, if we're being honest, aren't the most important part of the gameplay. That is, of course...MECHSWhile each faction largely has the same infantry units available to them, with some slight variation; where they really differ - and where this game absolutely shines - is in the mechs. Sometimes called auto-machines in-game, these are arguably the best implementation of mechanized, walker-type combat units I've ever seen in an RTS or any other genre of game. They feel and play incredibly, some as raw and massive and lumbering as they appear. Others are smaller and quicker and maneuver not unlike infantry do and are often best paired with infantry to both augment your squads and protect the mechs that might be easily overwhelmed with enough small arms fire or anti-armor units and emplacements. Some feel like whole armies on their own, crashing through buildings and defensive lines like they weren't even there. As I mentioned before, unit experience also applies to mechs, but where infantry may only get bonuses to their damage and and defense, mechs gain special abilities as they rank up. Some abilities increase damage output, or allow a barrage at an area, or smoke screens, or even a bayonet charge! They truly do change how the mechs can play and really incentivize working to keep them alive; being willing to retreat them from battles they won't win, living to fight another day when they are stronger and better equipped. The mechs look great, sound great, and are awesome to play. The story the campaign tells is engaging and well-paced, I think. The cutscenes are exceptionally well done, with good writing and pretty fantastic direction, I'd say. I've only played the game on the "native" mode, which has all the dialogue and unit cries in the native language of their respective factions. While I don't speak Russian, Polish, or German; their voice actors do an outstanding job conveying meaning and feeling and, in truly tense moments, significant emotion. Hats are off to them, and, I'm sure, to the English voice actor as well.Skirmish and challenge modes are also well done, I've found. The maps are varied and interesting, and, while I've haven't played most of the available challenge modes, the ones I have played offered a decent, well...challenge!All in, this is a well-designed, well-thought-out and, I think, lovingly crafted RTS experience that we haven't seen in some time. I don't have prior experience with the Scythe or 1920+ worlds, but if this game is any indication of what they have on offer, then count me in for more. There are, I've noticed, occasional hick-ups with unit movement and I've encountered and odd quirk (maybe a bug?) in selecting units when they are at the edge of my screen, but none of it game-breaking or so frustrating that I want to stop playing. I have been, I will say, driven to frustration with the occasional campaign mission where the direction or objectives weren't as clear as they could otherwise be, and did cause me to stop playing for the day. I always came back, of course, because even with those occasional moments of difficulty and eye-rolling, I was still having a ton of fun most everywhere else. On a separate note, I've heard that the final 4th faction which I have yet to play may not be balanced quite as well as the original three, so keep that in mind.Seriously folks, I was fortunate to pick this up on discount, but even in just the single-player realm that I've played in 40 hours, this is absolutely, 100% worth the full price of admission. I do not think you will regret giving this a go if you're even mildly interested in an RTS. The world they've constructed is truly something to behold.For whatever it's worth, I will grant Iron Harvest my highest possible recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed Company of Heroes, I strongly suggest checking this out. Mechanically very similar with infantry squads able to take cover in color-coded spots indicated by your mouse, ability to garrison buildings, and pretty freeform defense fortifications like razor wire for infantry blocking or sandbags for on-demand cover. Base building is fairly limited, but that just means there's more room for defensive lines to guard them. The mech roster is the real star of the show, and each faction has a good blend of options with different specializations to feel unique.    The game isn't perfect by any means; the difficulty curve can be sharp for the less experienced in RTS games, and occasionally it seems like units need to be given certain orders twice for them to register, but it's a fairly uncommon issue. My biggest gripe, really, is the Veterancy system. Units can't use their special abilities unless they win enough fights to rank up twice, which many units simply won't get to do because people die in war. Losing veteran units to sudden reversals of fortune or bad circumstances feels disproportionately punishing, as you've not only lost a pillar of your forces, but even spending resources to make another immediately won't get you the same performance unless the replacement manages to win enough to get those promotions. And if you're on the back foot already, odds on that aren't great. I feel like unit abilities should have been traditionally researched upgrades, maybe with steeper costs to account for the benefits, but as a whole the Veterancy system just feels like a feature from Command & Conquer that should have stayed in the past.    That being said, I do really enjoy this game, flaws and all.  I'm still pushing through the campaign, which I admit has a somewhat annoying proportion of "Use this one hero character and two squads to fight a whole map" missions versus the usual "Build a base, get to know your army and units, learn how to use them well" structure. I get they wanted us to learn the ins and outs of hero characters, but I feel like the player suffers as a result of getting much faster-paced and unforgiving base management missions, as that's the kind of scenario they'll be dealing with in multiplayer.  It's not terrible by any means, and the actual story is pretty good so far with the twists and turns, but the pacing may put some off. All in all, if you're a fan of RTS games, especially the unit management-focused ones like Company of Heroes, I'd strongly suggest giving this a chance. Especially if you have friends to play with, if single player ends up not being to your liking.

_childDocuments_.review: I had this game on my wishlist for a very long time. I played it for the first time during the Free Weekend (May 2021), having put off the purchase for a long time based on the previous reviews I had seen.Pros:- Lovely theme and beautiful art. I love Steampunk style settings in games, and this one does it very nicely.- Variety of mech units. There is a nice balance of different ranged and close quarters mechs.- Decent maps. Whilst it would be nice to have community maps or an editor, the supplied maps are well thought through and I enjoyed playing them.Cons:- Clunky controls and path-finding. Moving unit around feels sluggish, orientation of units often end up with their weaker rear armour exposed because they won't turn around properly. Often have to babysit unit movements because they end up where I don't want them. Selecting units lacks the sense of confidence that other RTSes have as I'm often not 100% sure what has been selected.- Unit production limitations. I really don't like being constrained in how few units I can build, especially when I have fought to control resource production. I want to be able to lay down covering fire fields with multiple machine gun bunkers and acres of mines with razor wire around bridges so I can keep the AI at bay while I explore and experiment with advanced production. I can't do that with miserly army sizes.- AI. Playing skirmishes against the computer - it's either dumb as hell or Skynet-level aggression. No middle ground.I didn't get an opportunity to do a multiplayer match, but overall the single player element was fun. As it stands today it's not worth the full price at £47, so have declined the purchase and uninstalled it - if it pops up on sale for £15 then I'll buy it. As there's no middle ground ratings on Steam, I'm giving it a positive rather than a negative.

_childDocuments_.review: This review comes from multiplayer point of view mainly. I don't personally care about campaings in strategy games so I will not say anything about it. However I've played a couple of skirmishes against the computer and all I can say about that is that the ai in this game is extremely easy and simple even on the hardest difficulty.The game could be good and fun but in it's current state I just cannot recommend or play it. The community while being active and somewhat helpful if you ask the right questions, refuses completely to acknowledge any criticism towards the game and it's shortcomings.-Despite what some part of the community says, the game is quite literally a bare bone version of Company of Heroes. It has all the same mechanics, but just WAY less of them. For example there are currently only two different buildings that can be upgraded once and the hq.-There is currently three factions. They are identical to each others in the way how every unit is built, however the "small" differences between the factions units is what makes this game very unbalanced. Polanian (offensive faction) units are the powerful meta while Saxony (defensive faction) is pretty much worthless in the hands of equally skilled players. This leads to very little choice on what and how you should play.-The matches are too short, usually games last from 5 to 15 minutes at most. By the time you can afford to start producing your most expensive units, either your team is already rushing the enemy hq or the other way around and at that point the match is already decided. There is no way to recover if you've lost most of your units and the enemy is destroying your base.-On some maps the game is decided in the first 30 SECONDS, not even exaggerating. The maps feature weapon caches you can give your units and whoever gets their hands to these caches first, wins the game. The worst case being 2vs2 map called Crash Site. After getting the weapon caches you have the upper hand in the early game which allows you to also capture all of the resources, so the other team will get no resources and the already in the lead being one will start snowballing towards victory right away. There are not many maps in the game so you are bound to get the bad maps.-The game has many bugs, some smaller and some bigger. I will not list these since not all of them are game breaking and the developers listen to the community in some capacity on what should be fixed. The biggest annoyance to me however was the reverse command (hold C by default and click where to move unit) on mechs. First of all, the game does not list the command in the command toolbar for whatever reason, which makes most players oblivious that such an important thing even exists. Not only that but the reversing itself is buggy. Sometimes the mechs won't actually reverse despite the game even showing you are issuing said command, but will just turn around and walk normally to the chosen position. This can and will cost you valuable mechs because they turn their weak backs towards the enemy while moving and get destroyed.TL;DR:The game just isn't worth it in it's current state and I don't see it getting much better in the near future due to a small developer team and a backwards ass cult following of the game. I do hope to see the game and meta in a better state sometime and return to this otherwise very interesting game.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is solid and gives me some nostalgia for dawn of war the original one. The different factions feel fairly balanced and cover is pretty important which makes builders viable as they can build cover in the form of sanbag walls. HOWEVER. if you are the type who plays a game on easy to enjoy the story this game is NOT for you. The campaign is unforgivably hard. Even on easier difficulties. Im pretty decent at most rts but this one takes several hours and multiple attempts to beat 1 level. Some levels are easier then others. So far the 2 hardest was a train defense where you have to protect an entire train for 10 minutes under constant seige. The train will die from a single pistol shot from an engineer. So 10 minutes you can't let a single thing through. And the next one I've been stuck on for 3 days. On attempt 40. At least half my hours into this one level. Saxony campaign battle of 5 heroes. Its not hard because the ai is a brilliant traction. Its hard because the enemy has 3 bases and can field 4 armies of troops. Most of which start at max veterancy. You have an ai teammate who will capture 2 resource nodes and then stops playing and demands your help. If they get wiped out all 4 armies eill start to march in on your base. No ammount of troops or fortification will save you at this point as its effectively 4v1. If you turtle you'll never win. If you attack your base is destroyed if you split your army into 2 then everyone dies. Id argue the ai cheats are dialed up way to high and ive stopped having fun in the campaign as i have sweaty try hard on normal/standard for hours or days for 1 level. And to anyone who is all git gud i don't care about your opinions. If i wanted a sweaty try hard git gud experience I would have chosen a harder difficulty. As for mp idk havent played it yet. But skirmish with bots isn't that bad. But good god do you have to either a world class tactition or a masochist to beat the campaign. Overall still a good game. But thought i should warn those who wouldn't enjoy the campaign so theh don't regret it and not play. Art and mechanics are solid with no complaints aside from the one above. Overall good game.
