_childDocuments_.review: I played this game very shortly after release and while I had a few glitches, it wasn't game breaking and I think the devs have already patched those.  The second night I played/streamed the game it was much better.  This game has a really interesting mechanic that I haven't seen previously in other horror games where you actually have to hold your breath to prevent the enemies from hearing you.  It really adds a suspenseful element to this game and I really enjoyed it.  There is also a "weapon" so to speak in the game, but I honestly forgot about it after they introduced it and made it through the game without it.  I REALLY REALLY loved this game and the story.  There are at least 2 different endings.  The atmosphere is well done and very spooky, the music is great.I love the setting of the game.  The Mansion is beautifully creepy.I like the enemy design and the few different enemies are explained with the story.  I recommend if you are a fan of horror and scares, give this one a shot!

_childDocuments_.review: It's times like this that I wish I had a "middle thumb" button to recommend. Maid of Sker has a lot of things going for it. The story is interesting and it has an alluring atmosphere. However, it lacks in scare factor and edges on mildly creepy rather than the downright terrifying defined by successful giants in the horror genre. The enemy AI and design left a lot to be desired and with the help of the device gained at mid-game it was far too easy to avoid encounters with the wonderful burlap sack headed friends you make along the way. While I was initially ecstatic to find myself in a resident evil type of situation early in the game, puzzles and item combinations were exceptionally easy. Maid of Sker isn't a must play but it's a good way to satisfy a short craving for a macabre period piece. Definitely wait for this one to go on sale before buying, the positives of Maid of Sker understay their welcome, and you'll likely find yourself checking out of your room much sooner than you hoped.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll admit, I really liked the music, art of certain scenes, and general theme of it. The story was also good/decent for a short game. But unfortunately while I started liking it at the beginning, I got more and more annoyed as I progressed. If you find yourself in the unfortunate case of being found, good luck not dying. No place to hide or safe areas such as in a locker or under the bed. The moment one hears you, he pretty much has wall hacks and can track you down anywhere. Yea you can run, but you have to either get in an elevator or far enough away from his designated area. Running away and quickly going quiet and crouch walking somewhere else won't do it either, he'll know where you're at. Oh, this guy is blocking the hallway? I'll just move to the side so he doesn't run into me and I'll hold my breath so he can pass. Yea, no. Even if they don't touch you. If you're in a really close proximity, even when holding breath and not moving, the enemy will hit you. It just got more and more annoying over time and started dreading having to crouch walk everywhere, ever so slowly and making sure to social distance for covid. Also, the puzzles were brain dead easy.

_childDocuments_.review: Maid of Sker, is one of those games that doesn't have a great combat nor compelling story. But its atmosphere and enchanting music just drags you into the terrifying empty hotel full of beautiful set pieces. If you enjoy a short mini horror vibe with beautiful music/visuals. The game does so many things exceptionally well, the first 20 minutes have an atmosphere thick enough to make even Horror veterans sweat. When the enemies do show up it all falls down the stairs. I understand the "Not everybody is a fighter" mentality but the fact the enemies are blind men with bags on their head that just punch, kick or grab you completely destroys any tension the game had. At least give them a knife or something, any reason for them to be a bit scarier.The game does look gorgeous, the puzzles are fun and don't get repetitive and exploring the hotel is a treat. The story itself is predictable but still entertaining enough to want to see it through to the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Though certainly not a bad game,  fumbles the landing as it reaches its conclusion, making it legitimately difficult to recommend.I should be clear, however, that I really,  wish I liked the game more. With some strong opening notes, the game's melody really does feel like something special early out. Playing as a musician named Thomas, you've gone in search of your love, Elizabeth, who is being held in Sker by her nefarious family for some vague yet duplicitous ends; all you know is that you've been requested you produce a counter-melody to a song Elizabeth is being forced to sing. The rest, you will have to discover as you go. And in fact, for the first few hours of the game, piecing together the horrors of the Sker Hotel is fascinating. There's some strong environmental storytelling at play here, and the excellent art direction and sound design really elevate the experience. I think of equal note is how unique the game's narrative voice is. Developed by a Welsh studio (aptly named Wales Interactive),  is positively rife with allusions to Welsh folklore and culture. From the game's selection of music to the surrounding environments, you can feel the love and care put into the whole of the game's world. When I think about the positive elements of my experience with the game, it's this attention to detail that really resonates with me most.Mechanically, the game is  a proper survival horror experience. Initially appearing as if it's going to be a walking simulator,  gradually layers in a variety of stealth mechanics that the player uses to avoid conflict. These are... serviceable. I never found the moment to moment core loop of creeping around masked enemies while holding my breath terribly difficult, but the pacing of the game's first two acts does truly succeed at generating a sense of heightened tension. It even gives you a sort of sonic-weapon you can use to repel enemies, which was a surprising but welcome addition that introduced a wider array of mechanical options.But the lack of real, mechanical depth began to way on me after a while, feeling like the full extent of the mechanical skill set provided was fully explored after just a scant few hours; one of the game's selling points is its use of 3D sound used by both player and AI, while this is  impressive and certainly well-executed, it's worth noting that this is gameplay feature has been used off-and-on by stealth games since 1998's . This is when the game sprung its most unwelcome trap on me. See, past the halfway point of the game,  introduces Abraham, a hulking, nemesis-like figure who stalks you around the halls of the hotel with both dogged tenacity and point-perfect pathing, effectively rendering all of the previous hours of stealth play moot as a more -style of frantic fleeing replaces the central gameplay experience. It feels  and Abraham's ability to one-hit-kill the player only magnifies the frustration.It's certainly tense, but compare it to, say, 's Mr. X, who acts more as a constant pressure on the player to keep moving. Mr. X cannot one-hit kill the player, and the player is given ample opportunity to outrun and lose the stalker in the halls of the RPD. Erstwhile, Abraham can neither be shaken nor defeated, while he can dispatch the player in a single, frustrating hit. Contrary to popular belief, death in horror games is actually somewhat antithetical to good horror, cutting the cycle of tension build and relief, and Abraham represents a perfect case study as to why. Abraham is also introduced late enough into the game that  feels it worthwhile to begin narrowing its mechanical scope once again after, quickly shepherding the player through a linear sequence of scares that feel increasingly arbitrary in nature. Gone is the methodical exploration of the hotel, replaced with a coal chute directly down into spoopy, video-game-y nonsense, complete with a red-light/green-light boss fight that just... just feels awkward, even at the best of times.And look, again, I want to be clear and upfront that the game's initial hours were fantastic, really setting a solid and unnerving tone. If  continued along these lines, I think it'd be something really special, not unlike, say, . In practice, however, I found my patience and goodwill towards the game dwindling as it went on, eventually reaching a point of critical collapse. There  far worse horror games out there, but there are certainly far better ones as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Pleasant surprise. Short and sweet. Does not overstay its welcome. Good minimalistic HUD. Graphics are nice (for some reason I get Bioshock vibes). The story is good (and reminds me of another PS2 cult classic horror game in its theme, Forbidden Siren) even though nothing groundbreaking. Voice acting is good (though I wish the main protagonist also spoke). I like how the enemies roam the environment a bit, though I would have liked it to be even more like that, now they sort of follow a very limited route even though you can lure them a bit at times. The game is all about sound and not making sound since that alert the enemies, I wish this was a bit more consistent though, enemies does not seem to notice things like doors opening and closing and for some reason the protagonists way he exhales after holding a breath is way over the top like he is actually trying to get detected. The challange modes where also a bit fun even though a completely different style of gameplay (arcade) and the only time you actually get a weapon (at least on the hard diff on the game) Though I find it strange it is unlocked from the start. Definitely play through the main game before trying the challange mode since you will be running around in all the environments from the main game.

_childDocuments_.review: I put not recommended, but it's really closer to neutral. 4.5/10 maybe.Story is serviceable, and the atmosphere and sound design are well done. The enemies are just boring. From what I've seen they are also all the same. There are only two ways to engage with them: wait for them to pass, or (once you get the stun ball) sprint through them, gather them, and stun them all so you can accomplish whatever you need. They just feel lazily designed, which isn't a bad thing if they are filler around better designed or more interesting enemies. It also feels like the level and sound design are completely at odds with the "sprint and stun" meta that the game drives you toward.For the life of me, I cannot understand why throwing objects to draw enemies away from you was not put in the game. I'm sure it must have been discussed and shot down for one reason or another, but that one mechanic would have served the atmosphere and sound design so much better. On the one hand, you want players to experience this hotel with tons of visual storytelling and tense moments with music stings that trigger upon interactions between the player and enemies, but on the other hand, the most efficient way through the game forces players to engage with those things as little as possible. It just feels like the game doesn't know what it wants to be.
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: No fear, just frustration.Interesting premise and the game has a slightly unique take on the 'hide and seek' horror genre but in the end, it's just too frustrating for me to recommend.Why?The level design and mechanics are throw your PC out the window annoying. You cannot jump, you cannot push away any of the shambling goons that inhabit the hotel. You are on rails for all intents and purposes. You feel like a helpless ninny who can only defend himself with gadgets. By the way, if you use a gadget at the wrong time the level design will make it painfully clear. Add to this that the game only has save points and you spend more time yelling at your monitor than actually feeling the slightest bit frightened.The story is a bit interesting but the lead female is a tad too whiny for my taste. Not much mystery just contrived damsel in distress tropes here. If there is a twist ending or if the lead female character grows and becomes interesting, I didn't have the fortitude to stick it out so that should tell you something.The positives are the graphics and atmosphere. That's about it.Wait for this one to go on sale for under 5 bucks if you feel the need to satisfy your masochistic urges.
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: It's alright, I guess.A fairly short, simple stealth horror game. Simple story, simple gameplay mechanics, and a mostly alright execution.My two biggest issues with the game is character speed, I wish both the player and enemies moved a bit faster, and also the lack of enemy variety. There's one basic enemy type and only two bosses (thankfully they do differ from normal enemies). Wish the game would lean more into the supernatural aspect with the way enemies both look and work.One of the bosses can straight up teleport, give me more stuff like that. The basic enemies just don't look very scary, they're easy to avoid and they don't really do anything cool.Overall, Maid of Sker doesn't really do anything great, but it's not all bad, either. It's just kinda alright.
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: For me, the enemies aren't too scary but can be pretty annoying. They move slow, so whenever I'm in tight spaces or hiding from them, I just wait for them to pass. They are blind but can hear. Your breath, cough, footsteps, bumping into objects—they'll hear everything that makes noises (though this might depend on what difficulty). There are three types of enemies, including a big guy whose footsteps make my ears shake.I seriously enjoy this horror walking sim game a lot. Plenty of jumpscares that scared the hell outta me, I love it 'cause I miss getting a real jumpscare. The story is interesting, the world got the vibe, and the sound are incredible (I highly recommend playing with headphones at full volume to hear their steps). But the gameplay needs to be stealthy if you don't wanna get caught, so sometimes I rush and hell with it. Also, once you're in a safe place, the enemies won't come inside.I think one reason they made Sker Ritual is 'cause the Challenge mode in Maid of Sker. It's super satisfying to slice their heads off with an axe. I don't recommend this game if you're scared or don't wear headphones.

_childDocuments_.review: Chronic Disability Simulator.This game does not tell you much about the protagonist, but instead informs us of his character through pure gameplay. The first thing that we learn is that our man has a visual impairment of mid-severity, perhaps early cataracts. Everything is presented through a slight mistiness that is not unlike the result of smearing vaseline over the fronts of your own eyeballs. Merely making out the details of his environment can be more of a challenge than it should be, and certainly not a pleasant experience.The next thing we learn is of his severe asthma. Slowly jogging for more than 4 seconds at a time will result in a wheezing sound effect. Moving through a slightly dusty area with result in hacking and coughing, inhaling the tiniest bit of smoke will do the same. For reasons of historical accuracy, the developers of the game have chosen not to include an inhaler, which is more than reasonable, if unfortunate.The third and most severe disability on offer is the lead character's inability to lift his feet higher than 2cm from the floor, perhaps due to early-onset arthritis in his hips or legs, or some other injury. This turns low obstacles, of the type a toddler could gently step over, into completely impassible terrain. This tragic infliction transforms even the most open of areas into a maze of diabolical complexity.While I applaud the makers of this game for their efforts at inclusion, this does not make for a fun experience.

_childDocuments_.review: So after just completing all of the achievements for the game this is what I have to sayIt's definitely more polished then some of the recent horror games to come out. (Those Who Remain and Follia - Dear Father not that they are bad). I just feel this is the best indie horror game to come out in a whileAnimations and voice acting is great (although the other characters are voiced but the main isn't for some reason). Soundtrack is fantastic and helps with creating the eerie atmosphereAt first I thought graphics were washed out and had very low textures. but you get use to that after playing the game multiple times. The game also does a weird slight out of focus thing with the environment when you move, if you're using TAA, so swap that to something else.It's got some great mechanics that I haven't seen any any other horror games like being able to hold your breath, so the enemies can't hear you when they walk past. since they are blind and use their hearing to detect where you are. You also find a Phonic Modulator which puts out a frequency that hurts the enemies letting you escape without them noticing.It's not very scary once you've played it, as the enemies are that dangerous. Unless your going for the save once achievement. That makes some parts super tense and puts you on edge. P.S. one thing they fail to mention about this achievement is that you have to save to trigger the final boss sequence, so if you've already saved once, you can't get the achievement. You have to make it here without saving (luckily it can be done on easy)    Without any spoilers, the story is good and keeps you wanting to find out moreHard mode which has enemies show up earlier and are more sensitive to sound, isn't very good as they detect you way to easily. There's one section that you can't even go into without being detected. So your just running around trying to complete the objective. This defeats the purpose of being stealthy. There was an earlier section I ran straight through, which probably isn't what your supposed to do.One thing that makes the game easier if that there's safe rooms, where you can save and hide from enemies (if you're being chased). Since they can't enter these roomsYes, there's chase scenes, but you can completely ignore most of them if your stealthy enough, a couple of them are scripted. They aren't as good as Outlast but don't feel like btech versionsIt's definitely worth a buy since it's well priced.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is labeled as a horror, adventure and action on Steam, but it's more a walking sim with very few and easy puzzles. There's even a difficulty where you can disable monsters and just enjoy the story. Regardless, the game is short, about three hours, unless you want to get 100% achievements.On higher difficulties Maid of Sker does bear some similarities with Resident Evil: everything is happening in a mansion, a huge monster is chasing you, you use safe rooms with phonograph to manually save the game (there's no checkpoints). Other than that, it's a typical walking sim with some stealth sections here and there, but monsters are blind and are really easy to avoid.The story is not bad, the voice overs and visuals are ok for an indie game (I recommend disabling all post processing except ambient occlusion so the game is less blurry), and Victorian era setting is a nice touch, so generally it's a choice for an evening or even a couple. But don't expect too much, there are much better games in the genre (I recommend Apsulov and In Sound Mind in addition to obvious choices such as SOMA, Amnesia, and Layers of Fear).There's also a separate challenge mode where you have to escape the hotel navigating a linear path and killing enemies (unlike the story mode, you get weapons). It takes 20-30 minutes to complete on each difficulty, and there are 4 in total. So it can easily add another couple hours to your total gameplay time. Actually, Resident Evil 2 remake has a similar game mode, so the inspiration for this one is obvious.P.S. It's in October 2022 Humble Choice, so you can get it and a bunch of other good games for a dozen bucks.

_childDocuments_.review: If only I could give you one piece of advice: Be careful if you use headphones.Now then, do you want to talk a bit more about Maid of Sker? Okay...Is Maid of Sker a bad game? NoIs it a game for everyone? Not at all.I personally didn't enjoy maid of sker the vast majority of the time. Horror is a very personal thing and everyone has their tastes.In this sense what you can find is a great atmosphere. The hotel is spectacular and indeed the sound is a very important element in the game to which attention has been paid.As far as the main plot is concerned, it's average. The puzzles are few and extremely simple, the enemies barely exert any pressure. And worst of all, you'll soon lose respect for them, and that's where I think it really fails. _childDocuments_.review: This was an incredible experience for people who love great atmosphere in games.i saw in other reviews that it was difficult to deal with enemies...but...its not true. especially if playing on easy where they basically let you win....and then there is safe mode which enemies don't even exist! if you play correctly this is not a very hard game.at least not the main game.during the main story,the hardest thing for me to do. was figure out the puzzle at sker point. the hint is not really obvious.you may not even realize it is the clue to figure it out.and that was admittedly frustrating.the 2 boss fights the game offered was a nice breathe of fresh air for enemy encounters.i like that there are 2 endings to this,so the story while having some questions...was wrapped up good enough.so challenge mode...eh....i don't care for it. its the mode you go to to get weapons and kill stuff. and while i understand the appeal ....i also understand what it does to the atmosphere of the main game. as you get comfortable with enemies not being  as much of a threat since you can now defend yourself.for those who want to get all the achievements(i don't care myself...) you will likely going through each (there are 4) of these stages several times. and since each of them is the same path just with minor tweaks for challenge. its going to get REALLY tedious!No the game isn't perfect, but it shines in atmosphere. for those who like that and are fine with slow/mid paced thrills. i give this a recommend!examining things doesn't work well. hard to turn them how i want to.for long notes, the controller move the text too fast, have to use mouse wheel.on the store page there is a picture of Elizibeth sitting next to a grave, odd since this never happens. you don't even play as her. also another one with a group of people and someone in the middle apparently.being worshipped. never happens.in the Garden area, bottom left of map is a huge square, bottom left of that section going north. i walked into a tree and fell through the ground. i could not replicate this. might have to do with the poison trap around there and the timing it hit me.ignored Elizibeth asking whose there at the end. beta the game. and her dialog was playing on the main menu. _childDocuments_.review: I have to start this by saying I don't play a ton of horror games. I get talked into one from time to time to create with and this was one of those games. If that helps frame the mind of the reviewer for you :)Surprisingly, I did quite enjoy it. I say surprisingly cause most of the horror games I have played had a TON of really slow points that kinda made me not enjoy it. There are some slow moments here, but that's really on how much you wanna explore, how lost you get (super guilty of this), or if die a lot since you save only in certain rooms so you might repeat some things in this instance. I thought for the most part it kept a good pace (again, unless I got lost).I thought the mechanics of working with sound vs sight with enemies was interesting although, once figured out didn't really get in my way. (I played on normal mode if this helps)The sound design was really good. It kept me tense most of the time, even during moments where nothing is necessarily happening (You are looking through rooms, reading journal entries, etc) but kept me always feeling like something WAS going to happen. I hated that *insert smirking face*The controls were smooth and to the point. Minimal controls.The story was pretty intriguing, I would recommend finding everything you can read to really learn more of the lore.I did get a couple of stutters/frame rate from time to time. It happened through out, it wasn't non-stop, and wasn't enough to take me out of it. Obviously I played on PC :D I got a little layer of fears vibes in how it played with more interaction required of you. Plenty of little jump scares.The puzzles were pretty straightforward and enough to be a challenge but not so many it gets annoying,Game takes about 4 hours to complete.All in all I think it's a good horror game. There isn't combat, so if you like super fast paced games with lots of gore for your horror this ain't it. But if you like a linear, tense, first person survival horror games I think this would be worth a grab.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the one of those games where you take the role of a common guy and where you shall accomplish tasks by keeping a low profile rather than grabbing bull by the horns. Enemies in this game are wearing some scarf over their heads so they are effectively blind but they react to noise. What is good here is that developers tried to build a skill based experience, contrary to the luck based experience where enemy appearances and behavior are strictly scripted and where you shall die many times simply due to wrong guessing. If you are able to follow basic rules ie: sneak when enemies are near, don't scratch the furniture while moving, cover your mouth and nose when walking through dusty areas or space where purple gas appears you shall be fine. You are also tasked with gathering some items and solving some mostly not too difficult puzzles while avoiding guards. You shall also collect notes and listen to gramophone recording which shall introduce you to the dark story behind your fiancee's family wealth. So why negative review here?I almost ironmaned the game on my first playthrough on normal level. After first 30 mins in game I stopped worrying about guards as they are oblivious to my presence even if they walk next to me (but not bumping into me). The only area where guards functioned as they are supposed is a courtyard with electrical switches and passing that area was truly sweaty for me. Further into game developers break their own rules by introducing girl's uncle. This guy is somehow able to see through the scarf and is also constantly running after you - this is the only enemy that got me once and I had to reload my save. Rest of the game was again very generic and had a poor attempt on plot twist at the very end. Story was okay, hotel corridors and other areas were good, but sound was very poorly done - namely you shall hear guard's footsteps like they are walking next to you even if they are actually on the other end of the floor. I don't expect them to fix shortcomings with sound and enemy behavior since there were several patches that did nothing so at this point I don't recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this game is not worth full price. Only get it at a discount under $10 because it shouldn't really take you more than 3 or 4 hours to beat. This game excels at setting the mood and creating an atmosphere of horror. The graphics are beautiful and the environment pairs perfectly with the haunting music. The gameplay however, is pretty bad. It is essentially a watered down resident evil / outlast hybrid. You have a few RE style puzzles which are interesting, but very scarce. You also have enemies roaming the manor that you cannot kill, but they're blind (literally) which makes them extremely easy to avoid. I beat the entire game on normal difficulty in 3 hours without dying once (with minimal effort). Every enemy encounter is the same. Just wait for them to move out of the way so you can crouch walk past them. The enemies can't hear you if you're crouch walking which lets you freely roam the manor unless you bump into an enemy.There's so much missed potential here. The story is very unique and interesting which kept me crouch walking to the end, but there is so little to the gameplay that I felt totally unfulfilled once the credits rolled. This game is definitely worth a playthrough so I do recommend it, but considering how short the whole experience is, it is not worth $25.

_childDocuments_.review: To begin, I have been following the development of this game since its original preview. My thirst for a good survival horror game is like no other and I was hoping this would bring a satisfaction to that desire. So, in short, yes, it is a fine game and I recommend it if you casually play or are a die hard survival horror fan. I do not know if I set my expectations ridiculously high or if I am just chasing a nostalgia feeling in this genre, but I do leave this review with some amount of sadness. SPOILERS!!!!!This review is based a completed game on normal difficulty - The game begins slowly with a soft introduction to the main characters Thomas and Elisabeth. It is an exceptionally nice feeling stepping off the train as you begin to search for the hotel. The attention to sound detail is immediately noticed and the ambiance is thick. The OST starts out very strong as you approach the gate, but begins to become repetitive almost instantly. (yes it is a motif throughout the game, but it becomes almost annoying) The walk through the forest is serene and enchanting, but not entirely interesting. The game shows you where you need to go leaving a feeling of hand-holding to the player as you enter the hotel. Now, the hotel is, for the most part, the whole experience. The end mission becomes very clear very quickly and the survival aspect begins. Slowly you work your way through a basic understanding of enemy mechanics and what you need to do to not get caught. This idea of being silent and the enemies using echolocation to track you down is a fine idea, but so many missed opportunities with the inability to interact with the environment. You are either silent, holding your breath, or crouch walking through most of the game. You collect journal entries here and there that push the narrative forward (kind of), collectible items and game progress related items. Most of the puzzles can be solved by trial and error and just do not feel thought out. There are some great moments involving the mechanics and enemies, but its mainly just crouch walking around a hotel. There are boss-like "fights" that occur, but weren't very satisfying or unique. There are a couple different enemy types, but they do not have different AI patterns and feel the same. Eventually you collect all the key items and choose an ending to wrap the game up. I found maybe two endings.(there might be more) The sound is incredibly engaging and it always feels like you re being stalked. This is a success and possibly the main reward to the player in the ultimate experience, but so many missed opportunities that would make the player feel more in control. Using the environment to distract enemies while making escapes would have been such a great feature throughout the game. I never found myself worried too badly about bumping in to objects because I was already moving terribly slowly at crouch walk speed. If the enemies hear you however, you are basically on lock until you leave the rendered area entirely. This felt very strange. There are reoccurring large armoires and wardrobes that cannot be interacted with which felt missed as well during times of being chased.The graphics are decent, but the constant misty, dusty feeling made them feel more dated. This was a design choice to have the player immersed in a horror experience, but just made me squint the entire game. I, personally want to be able to clearly see or have my senses overloaded for a horror experience. All the hotel rooms blended together in a wash of brown and red and the times outdoors seemed to echo that in a green tint. Some rooms were very successful, clearly having received more attention (which is common in games), but they were rooms for items or story progression. This game is good and I recommend it to fans of the genre, but after playing other indie horror games such as Amnesia or Layers of Fear, I leave a bit underwhelmed.  5.7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: Maid of Sker feels like a fanfic for Resident Evil, but your enemies are not zombies, and you can't fight with them. They can hear you, but they can't see, meaning that you have to stay quiet, stop breathing if needed. That's a big difference in terms of how you survive in this game, mind you. But everything else is quite similar. There's a big mansion with closed doors, unlockable with keys you need to find; there are some simple puzzles; there is a big guy appearing from time to time to smash your head; there is also a safe room! I'd say Maid of Sker is a solid horror, short horror, worth for its money. The genre enjoyers are likely to love it.

_childDocuments_.review: TDLR: Small team and small price lowered my expectations and I got what it was was worth. Challenges are funner than the game itself but are very short and are near identical. It's like playing a less fun and definitely less scary version of RE 7, with way too much stealth involved.Story: As a composer named Thomas, you are summoned to Sker Hotel and are tasked to bring a new composition to your, I'd assume, lover. The reasoning behind it all tries to be obscure, but the main gist of it is about playing a specific song with a specific person bringing about a specific event. As you progress further in the story, you find more and more lore that will help you in your ultimate choice of how to play the song, backwards or not. So while there are 2 endings, it is very easy to just reload your last save and just choose the other dialogue to see the other ending. Gameplay: The gameplay, heck, even the game, was somewhat lackluster. At first, I really enjoyed exploring the mansion and felt it was gonna ramp up at some point, but it never did. 90% of the game consists of skulking around blind enemies that only react to sound, and, well, that's pretty much it. There is a bit of gunplay, but only on the ''challenges'' and while there are 4 of them, they are the same with few variables, like less health and the map being dark. It's also the same map as the main game, and they have no correlation with the main game. There are a couple of mechanics, such as holding your breath to traverse dusty areas so as not to cough and attract attention, crouching, to be less noisy when moving, and there is a device you can find to temporarily stun enemies... And I suppose healing items are also noteworthy. Very basic.The game is relatively short, spanning about 4-6 hours. 8 or so if you constantly get lost like I did O_oIt's also important to note that there is no autosave in the main campaign, everything is through manual saves, RE style, and while it may displease some, I found it just fine.Graphics: I enjoyed how everything looked at first, nature and colors were gentle and soft. It's too bad the vast majority of the game ends up inside the hotel and doesn't take full advantage of what it could. Still, graphics are good, at the very least, environments are.Audio: There isn't much to say here, dialogue is scarce, the chanting is nice, but that's pretty much all the game has.I'm not recommending it simply because its score is way too high. The game is short, very basic, not really fun and I don't think the game offered anything new, like at all. Outlast was better in every way. Still, if you really want to give this game a go, go ahead, it's not bad or anything. But it does not deserve a -very positive rating-, it's simply average, at best, at least get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally I finished Maid of Sker, another title on my backlog since quite some time. Overall, this was a decent horror walking simulator with a lot of stealth elements and some good old Resident Evil Eagle, Bird Key Puzzles.The game starts great within the first 20 minutes. You walk through an incredible lush forest up to the mansion. Then the main game begins. The next 1-2 hours are a bit confusing and even feel tedious. It is not really clear what to do. Why are you in the basement? Then in the garden and then back in the mansion. Well, it is good to learn the mechanics of the game. Mostly stealth. Try to push through. It is getting better.Within the next 2 hours the game starts then to grow on you. You will enjoy the puzzles, you feel the urge to open each door and even collect the items. You will open the map a lot. Put the map key handy, Just to look where to go next with your newly found key.One time I was running in the wrong direction, well took me 20 minutes backtracking. But I admit this was my fault. Overall there is however the feeling of too much backtracking, on the other hand always something new happens; meaning, you think you managed the path and then you fall in a trap and have to get out of it. Graphics are decent, however also a bit blurry. You do not have a gun, so stealth is the way to go. The game inspires itself a lot of the stealth and even Nemesis parts of Resident Evil. Better like this than inventing something completely new. The monsters are not really inspired.I really liked the sound effects and the audio, especially the voice acting is good. I liked the music in the game and the overall theme of Sirens and classical music. Well done. Beware of different endings and some cheap jumpscares. Damn I don't like jumpscares. Enough said, not spoiling the twist. No worries.A game that starts mediocre finishes good. Therefore I decided to not give it not only 5/10 but 6/10 instead. Hence a recommendation for fans of walking simulators, horror, stealth and mini-find-key-open-door-puzzles.(Finished it in two sessions only and wrote the review late in the night to keep the experience fresh; Steam Key received from developers for review purposes)

_childDocuments_.review: The color transitions are very good especially according to the environments you enter and the ambience in the game. I like the graphics. You are trying to save your lover who is locked in a hotel, but it belongs to your lover's father and uncle on time. These beings cannot see you, they can only hear you, so you usually have to bend over and close your mouth, moving quietly. This slows the flow of the game a little. _childDocuments_.review: Not too often are games made that are set in the late 1800s early 1900s, Maid of Sker falls right into that time period. It's not exactly what I'd call an ideal time period for a video game setting, however a horror survival game would be one of those genres that would work. I think for what Maid of Sker is, it pulls it off quite well. The main location is an old hotel and damn if it isn't creepy! I think it's best if I jumped into the pros and cons list and stopped myself from giving away any spoilers. FYI, I'm writing this review without having finished the game. I'd say I'm very close to the half way point maybe even a little over half way.   Pros* As I touched on already, it's set in a unique time period and that makes it pretty scary and creepy on its on. Not a lot of electronics, very little electricity so that makes everywhere that much darker. It's a slow burn, slow pace game, where you need to watch your step and stay quiet. In most circumstances, there is no running in this game without it punishing you for it.* I like the hold your breath mechanic. Not only have I never seen this done in a game, at least to this existent but it really feeds into the entire setting where something as basic as breathing could get you killed. * Graphics on the highest settings are wonderful. Now might I add, everything is dimly lit so that does ease the need for crisp graphics but again you are in a run down old hotel. So it fits. * Music & SFX, the best way for me to describe it is, you are Odysseus tied to his boat and being forced to listen to the Sirens. It's beautiful and it's down right creepy.  It's also exactly to the point in this game where without spoiling much, music is a major part of the plot.  As far as SFX, from bells dinging to a faint music box playing somewhere in the distance you'll need to keep your ears open to any and all footfalls in the neighboring areas. * I would say this game is a relaxing survivor horror and not a run and gun game, part of that is true. It's not a run in gun game, but it is far from relaxing. It's mostly about hiding and staying quiet. There really isn't much in the way of combat. It's similar to Alien Isolation, Condemned, Outlast and Amnesia. More on the story and problem solving, less on the fighting.Cons* I saw this complained about heavily, the saving aspect. The phonographs, those are your save points, where you also listen to a brief snippet of story or song. I do not like this part of the game at all. They are too few and far between at times. It's not fun to have to go back and do 20 minutes or more of game again because you are unable to find a save. ESPECIALLY, when the game is very unforgiving and enemies can't be removed only temporarily incapacitated or distracted. I know this will likely never change, but it should. * It's not scary. It's a horror game and it's not scary. It's creepy and maybe a little twisted that's for sure, but I haven't had a jump scare or anything that has truly made me take a moment and gather my thoughts. Which is very disappointing considering, as I mentioned before, you can get caught and killed for breathing. That's pretty damn scary, and somehow Maid of Sker doesn't capitalize on that very well. I should be sh***ing my pants like some moments in Visage, Outlast or Condemned. Instead, I'm almost falling asleep!* Besides the minor story notes and musical dolls you should look for, there isn't any reason to explore much because it's got a great atmosphere but very little to interact with or do in a large portion of the game besides sneak around. There should have been creative traps set for you or even to use on the enemies. Instead, you just want to find key items and continue with the story.* Too slow of pacing at times and too much time wasting! Unfortunately, since you aren't able to deal with the enemies in any meaningful way, you are left to crouch and wait for enemies to move along on their routes, which do change as you explore and discover new areas. I did say there are ways to distract but in most cases, those distractions are so far out of the way that they aren't helpful. Again, it would have been awesome to be able to trap enemies in rooms etc. I did list what some might think as damning negatives to a horror game. BUT, I think if you know what you are buying it's an easy game to like and appreciate. I like a lot of what Maid of Sker has to offer. I do wish they'd done several things different and that there was more to do than stealth around. However, with that being said I want to give the Wales Interactive team a thumbs up! I think this is the beginning for a team who could make even better games and I hope to see them do so. SO, feel free to buy the game a full price or on sale. If you've read this review and like what you've heard you'll enjoy Maid of Sker as well!

Let's be honest, it's cheap to do and this one feels particularly cheap right from the get go. This kind of games is actually really hard to nail right and this one misses almost all its marks.Gameplay is seriously boring. If you value your time, this isn't for you. It screams artificial difficulty (the levers mechanic is downright insulting). Exploration isn't a thing either. You will be treated to some really dreadful linear level designs instead. The supposed horror aspects are as often terribly uninspired (predictable jumpscares and cutscenes that takes control of your character). Graphics looks really strange too with color palettes quite reminiscent of those early 2010s days where everything was brownish and grayish shades.All in all, it feels to me like just a big and usual cliché. The only redeemable aspect I could find was maybe its premise. It looked interesting, but guess what... during the first big chunk without save points, I of course clipped through the floor in one of those lame rooms with levers and plunged into digital oblivion. Just the excuse I needed to shut down this game and never look back!

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, I've gotta go with "Nope" here.Price plays a huge factor in whether I "recommend" a game or not. And for the about 3 hours of actual gameplay you get, 25 bucks is just a hard pass. You can prolong that "experience" by tackling it at a higher difficulty or completing the 4 challenge modes, in which you have to escape the hotel under various conditions ... The funny thing about these challenges is that they actually give you weapons, so it's at least a completely different experience. No map, some unkillable enemies, straight forward affair, probably 30 minutes per challenge if you're so inclined.The base game though doesn't have much meat on its bones. Once you actually get the game running smoothly (for me it was TXAA that completely screwed with the FPS for some reason), have the correct mouse sensitivity (I had to go up to 50 out of 100. The game started me off at 5!) and survived the first shock of the game: The really bad graphics in overexposed sunlight ... You will trudge along linear paths until you actually reach the hotel.In here the game opens up slightly with various rooms to explore, a map that helps you navigate ... and enemies that make your life miserable, because you bloody well have no idea what triggers them and what doesn't. Since you don't have any weapons, your only choice is to ... stop breathing, because the enemies can't actually see you, only hear you. What they can hear I have no clue. Sometimes when you trigger an alarm or such they all come running, sometimes you can just walk by, almost touching them...as long as you hold your breath. Sometimes they chase you halfway through the hotel, other times they just give up after a second. That might all be difficulty related, but seriously, some consistency would be nice. For the most part on easy, and I guess on normal, you can just ignore them, walk or run past them, be on your merry way. But a few times they're just ridiculously irritating, for example when you have to figure out a sound-based puzzle surrounded by 3 dudes ...Well, and that's basically the game. There's a plot nobody cares about, because it's basically been spelled out for you very early on, so listening to the audiographs, talking to the girl or reading the letters you find doesn't really reveal much more to you. It didn't grip me in any way, shape or form.The "finale" of the game is you being chased around by a Mr. X wannabe, who can miraculously deduce your location, no matter where you are or how silent you are. In Resident Evil this was a cool concept, because the guy was constantly looking for you and there was an incentive to be quiet. Here, there isn't, because the dude will home in on you regardless, so the only choice you have is to rush through the corridors in hopes of finding what you need quickly.Puzzles and boss battles are tedious and irritating, not that there are a lot in the game. And the whole "you can only save at certain points in the game" is irritating. At least give us a save point next to every level transition, either an auto-save or a manual save station.The singing part of the game ... well, maybe you like it, maybe you don't. I wouldn't put it down as a unique selling point though.All in all Maid of Sker feels like a half-finished game, but at least it has an actual ending, two in fact. I wish there were more to it, something to actually uncover, a way to fight the enemies, actually EXPLORING the locations, instead of rather linear progression, voice acting for the protagonist, etc. But the game just screams B movie production value and that's a bit of a shame. The gameplay is just too 1-dimensional and boring.Also, whoever thought it was okay to have enemies hit a dog, has issues.

_childDocuments_.review: I just completed the game. I love the visuals and art direction. I think they are very interesting and overall the game creates a spooky atmosphere. There were moments where it legitimately spooked me and got a few jumps out of me as well. However I don't recommend this game for a few reasons.The main reason was because the enemy ai was so annoying that is made me curse! And I'm a person that rarely curses. In the game the main mechanic is that you hold your breath to avoid getting detected by enemies. However there were SO many times that I held my breath still while an enemy was far away and they still ended up detecting me and my character died.Another problem I ran into was that I ended up getting stuck at a dead end with an enemy or two attacking me until my character died again. And I was playing the game on the 'Easy" difficutly so it wasn't like the enemy AI was tuned up to detect me more. It frustrated me.Another issue I had was that to beat the game you have to get either all the cylinders or all the music sheets. If you aren't paying attention you will miss either the cylinders or the music sheets so you will have to backtrack a lot. Which wouldn't be a problem, however if you miss them and are on the last part of the game, the main area feels like a ghost town and punishes you for it. You can't use a lot of the main doors to access the mansion freely anymore so you have to go in an annoying maze-like pattern to go to areas you need to explore for items.I think including an ending that doesn't require either would've been a good choice for players who want to experience an ending but don't want to go through the hassle of finding all the collectibles of either type. So in all, there are things to like about the game. But when it comes to the actual gameplay, there are so many better options to choose from in this genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Maid of Sker is a first-person survival horror game that utilizes elements of stealth, puzzle-solving, backtracking, and no-weapon survival and is set in a remote derelict hotel. This game is heavily inspired by the popular British folklore legend of the Sker House and the original Maid of Sker. The original Sker House, still standing to this day, dates back to the 12th century, and has a reputation for being haunted by two ghosts: a captain of a shipwreck near Sker Point and Elizabeth Williams, the original Maid of Sker. The house was made popular by R. D. Blackmore’s book The Maid of Sker, written in 1872.In the 18th century, Sker House, actually located in Kenfig, South Wales, was owned by a farmer named Isaac Williams. His daughter, Elizabeth Williams, fell in love with a local harpist named Thomas Evans. However, Isaac forbade Elizabeth from seeing him and imprisoned her in a room in the house until she agreed to marry another man of “better” financial status. Even after the unwanted arranged marriage, Elizabeth still yearned for Thomas, so much that she eventually fell ill and died. Some claim that she died of a broken heart, others that she starved herself to death. Nonetheless, her spirit is said to haunt Sker House to this day. Perhaps she was coined the Maid of Sker because she was never truly married to the person she loved.The game Maid of Sker takes these real-life characters — Isaac Williams, Elizabeth Williams and Thomas Evans — as well as fictional characters and creates a tale of forbidden love and supernatural mystery that haunts the grounds of the Sker Hotel. You play as Thomas Evans, the musician, on a quest to save your lover Elizabeth, who is locked inside the confinements of the hotel. Though the initial premise of the story is based on real British folklore, there really isn’t much character development in terms of the main protagonist. You are silent across the entirety of the game. Maid of Sker possesses most of the tropes of a typical survival horror game. It has maze-like maps, locked areas that you need to come back to later, ominous ambience, and, of course, jump scares. The jump scares do not feel cheap but instead make the environment around you feel alive. There are also refreshing and unique elements including sonic weaponry, which stuns enemies using sound waves but does not kill them, and a particular entity that knows your exact location and stalks you relentlessly. Perhaps this particular entity, whom I will not name, is inspired by a popular tyrant from the Resident Evil series. Both elements contribute to the balance of hopelessness you feel in the game, a pivotal element in any horror game.The visuals for this game are quite appealing, as they pay much attention to detail and fit in with the theme of the story and lore. You are able to make out the descriptions on a wall, the facial features and words in a painting, and even the designs of a beer tap. This game has very little cutscenes, and facial features are nearly nonexistent, as the enemies are always wearing sack masks. Aurally speaking, the voice acting in the scenes containing phonographs and telephones is well-done and not awkward. Load times for this game were also very quick and seamless.This game offers 3 different difficulties: Easy, Normal, and Hard. I completed my playthrough first on Normal and am currently working my way through Hard. This game is by no means easy, nor is it unreasonably hard. I already thought Normal mode was decently challenging; I can only imagine how the difficulty would pick up on Hard! Though you are given enough healing items, ammunition and save points, you still can’t help but feel like you need to be strategic and smart with how you use them. Gameplay wise, the mechanics are simple to understand but hard to master. The gameplay is also very realistic and I admire the developers for that! The overall gist is that everything is sound-based. Enemies cannot see you but they can hear you. Running and bumping into things in your environment make noise. Coming too close to an enemy alerts them of your presence. You mitigate this by holding your breath while you walk. You cannot hold your breath while you run and sometimes you cannot hold your breath at all after running for a long time or holding it for a long time, as you need time to recover. There is an added element to this gameplay, which is coughing. You cough when you walk through dusty or cloudy areas, obviously making noise and alerting nearby enemies of your presence. The puzzles in this game are refreshing, quirky, and fun to complete, and a lot of them revolve around music, a major theme to this game. They aren’t simple to the point that you don’t need to think at all but they aren’t ridiculously tricky either. The uniqueness of each puzzle really picked at my deduction and memorization skills. There were many times in which I felt pressed for time while doing a puzzle in fear that an enemy would notice me or be alerted. Aside from all this, there are also diaries, letters, and notes to pick up that help provide insight to the events that led up to the current story.Though there are collectable items to look out for in the game, I am unsure whether there is enough incentive to collect all of them. As such, my outlook on the replayability of Maid of Sker is a little skeptical. The only reason to play through the game again is to challenge yourself with hard mode. The game markets itself as one that has multiple endings. Though this is true, it does not require you to replay the entire game again. Under certain conditions, you can just reload your save file and pick the other option. I had originally expected that there would be multiple dialogue options throughout the game that would work together to dictate what ending you get. I was a little disappointed that it was so easy to unlock the other ending. Another gripe that I have is that if you start a new game, it will overwrite your previous playthrough. Though this is not a big issue, I am not sure what the purpose of this is.My first playthrough of the game took around 6 hours. Given that I have played many survival horror games in the past, I will assume the average gamer would take around 7-8 hours to complete the game in their first playthrough. Since this is a survival horror game, I can definitely see this game being used by hardcore gamers to speed-run. However, during my playthrough of the game, I experienced frame drops during certain areas of the game. Fortunately, no bugs nor crashes occurred during my playthrough. For reference, my PC setup runs on a GTX1070.Maid of Sker is very big on audio cues and music. Heck, if you pre-order the game you get an entire soundtrack of folk hymns to listen to. Much of the story is driven by music sheets, instruments, and singing that are woven into the narrative. The music itself is tense, terrifying, immersive and beautiful. As you venture your way through the hotel, the floors creak, the winds chime, and the footsteps of nearby enemies can be heard, never making you feel truly safe. The only sort of solace you will find is in each phonograph room, always located behind a familiar green door. One thing I really enjoyed about each save point was that it takes the form of a phonograph, and plays a snippet of dialogue that adds to the overall development of the story. You will discover the truth behind all of this music after you play through the game for yourself!Maid of Sker was an overall delight to play, even more so considering that this game is not a Triple-A game and set at a very reasonable price. It is very much well worth the price tag if you are into stealthy survival horror, and enjoy figuring out the lore and mystery behind a well-known British folk legend. I greatly enjoyed the music, the narrative, and the unique gameplay elements that this game introduced.

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10, perhaps generously. Try it on massive discount as a niche experience. Not an incredible game by any means. A better walking sim for me is SOMA; but I've played worse. The graphics are very nice at times, although some things like character animations could be better, but they're okay too. The story keeps you engaged, but could have been more expansive. I don't want to spoiler too much about the gameplay, but it is fairly repetitive and you will be crouching around for hours avoiding the same enemies basically over and over. I was too lazy to solve most of the puzzles and just used a guide; there aren't that many. They seem like okay puzzles but nothing that would suddenly turn this into a AAA title. It seems influenced by games especially Resident Evil 7 and maybe even some Bioshock undertones (see what I mean in the challenge mode especially); but those games are vastly superior. I tried the challenge mode, but not too much. I was more interested in the campaign, which is where the main game should be; but I was surprised to find that the challenge mode has drastically different mechanics, and actually some very nice gun animations. But I got cheesed and Alt-F4. Like I said, more interested in the main story than challenges.

_childDocuments_.review: Maid of Sker was a good horror game with a story that I think is a bit different from typical horror. I don't want to give anything away but I liked it's blend of mythology mixed with some standard horror tropes. I think the thing that Maid of Sker does well is the immersion in its world with excellent visual design but even better sound design. Since the enemies are all attracted to sound then it definitely is a must for the sound feedback to be really good. Although, the music is what really drew me to the game. The hauntingly beautiful Welsh hymns were a treat and really added to the game's overall atmosphere.I think the shortcomings come from the enemies being way too easy to evade making them seem more comical than scary. Not to mention, it was fairly easy to determine where the enemies could go and couldn't go which made exploitation a bit too easy. Although, on the flip-side, I hated when I would open a door and an enemy would immediately be there ready to jump me. It didn't happen much but when it did, it felt a bit cheap. All of this is a very minor annoyance and didn't really detract too much from my enjoyment, but I think the short playtime helped with that.Overall, I recommend giving it a try if horror games are your thing. Currently for the month of October 2022, you can pick it up in the Humble Choice. If you'd like to see what other games are on offer and my thoughts on them then please feel free to check out my review below:

_childDocuments_.review: Well, the main character is quite obviously suffering from some evil long-covid-syndrome: You can run for like 5 meters when "Thomas" suddenly starts coughing and heavily breathing. Funny!"Maid of Sker" is in some way a "Resident Evil"-clone: You have to solve the story-line behind the spooky hotel and its former inhabitants (which wander though the rooms and halls, transformed into zombie-like creatures...only reacting to the sounds you make). Basically you have to proceed further and further into the huge building to uncover its secrets: Main level, a 1st, a 2nd floor, also a basement, a garden and a cemetary are waiting for being discovered. You´re mainly looking for keys which will allow you to unlock "special doors", also known from RE (Music Key, Crow Key, Skull Key etc).I´d give the game a 8/10.Its atmosphere is great, so is the soundtrack. The graphics are quite end-level but not photo realistic (maybe 8.5/10)The clues are very easy for RE-players.The monsters are deaf in some cases, others can hear you breathing even from the next room.The Tyrant-like "end-boss" seems to find you everywhere - no hiding possible here!Fazit: I liked "Maid of Sker" a lot. It was fun sneaking through the ancient hotel, looking for music paper-sheets, keys, old letters that let you dive deeper into the family-story.Bought it for 9,99 € and it was worth every cent.

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics: washed out and faded. The motion blur made me nauseous, so I turned it off, but there's no way to turn off the dusty yellow filtering or make the setting more vibrant. Everything looks faded, but not in a realistic or even artistic way. It's a very unpleasant environment that made looking at everything a chore rather than enjoyable.Content: I don't know, I played for 30 minutes so I only made it from the train station to the hotel. There's barely anything to interact with on that long walk. The landscape looks much the same, forces you on a specific path with nothing going on along the way, and I think the developers really missed an opportunity to deepen the lore by making it possible to flip through any of the dozens of books laying around, or investigate the papers or suitcases or any other number of objects. You basically just walk down a long path and open doors to rooms with maybe 1-2 things you can interact with. I was bored within the first five minutes, but I held on for 25 more minutes hoping it would start letting me interact with more and more things. It didn't.Summary: You want a game that will hook you right from the beginning, not make you feel like you're wasting your time. This felt like a big waste of time, and maybe the game gets a lot better later on, but I didn't want to run the risk of being unable to get a refund. In my opinion, this game is too tedious early in the game to be fun. At least it lets you sprint a bit, so you don't have to walk so slowly from one uninteresting point to the next. I really wanted this game to be good, it looked pretty great from the previews, but it's not worth the sale price of $12 to me.

_childDocuments_.review: Alrighty! Snowy paws on the keyboard, let's get this done. Kiba Snowpaw here with a review of the eerie Maid of Sker. As an old wolf in the gaming world and a devourer of anything that falls between the lines of suspense, horror and folklore, I'm more than excited to share my take on this game with you all.Maid of Sker is a captivating journey into a world that's been woven from the rich fabric of Welsh folklore. It's like diving headfirst into a beautifully illustrated book of ancient tales, only to find yourself surrounded by spine-chilling horror and desperately trying to find a way out. It's an experience akin to that time I fell into a snow drift. It was fluffy and inviting until I realized it was cold and couldn't find my way out. And, I'm pretty sure there was something moving under the snow...but let's not get into that.Let's start with the story. Inspired by the haunting tale of Elisabeth Williams, this game delivers a narrative as chilling as an Arctic breeze. You're thrown into a family saga soaked in torture, slavery, piracy and a supernatural mystery so thick it makes pea soup seem transparent. And who doesn't love a good mystery, right? It's like trying to figure out who stole the last slice of pizza at a furry con. Hint: it's always the raccoon.The gameplay is an interesting blend of survival and stealth mechanics. You're armed with a defensive sound device which, while not as satisfying as a good ol' shotgun, brings an innovative approach to the survival horror genre. Your primary strategy? Don't. Make. A. Sound. It's like trying to sneak into the house after a late-night gaming session without waking your mate. Trust me, the stakes are high.One of the things that stood out to me was the audio design. It's honestly some of the best I've heard, comparable to the sound of steak sizzling on a grill - crisp, enticing, and instantly attention-grabbing. Pair that with stunningly realistic visuals, and you've got a feast for your senses that will have you on the edge of your seat.Speaking of edge-of-your-seat moments, this game is rife with them, thanks to the AI enemies. They may be simple to bypass, but they add a layer of tension that's thicker than a polar bear's fur. And let's not forget about the alternate endings. Just like a choose-your-own-adventure book, the game offers different outcomes, adding a nice touch of replayability.In true furry fashion, I appreciate the attention to detail in this game. The developers at Wales Interactive clearly poured their hearts and souls into crafting this experience, just like a dedicated fursuiter painstakingly stitching their dream character to life.Maid of Sker does have its flaws, though. The story is somewhat predictable, like a dog who swears he won't chase the tennis ball this time, but we all know he will. And the stealth mechanics could use a little more complexity, like adding a few more threads to a simple knot.But overall, the game delivers an experience that's as engrossing as the latest manga or anime series. It's a well-crafted tale that beautifully blends elements of psychological, gothic and British horror.The Ice Wolf's verdict? Maid of Sker is a howling good time. It's a short but intense journey that leaves an impression. And remember, it's not about the size of the game in the fight; it's about the size of the fight in the game.Until next time, stay frosty, my furriends!

_childDocuments_.review: This is something in-between Resident Evil and Layers of Fear, but with lower budget. The story is mostly ok, I guess, although I am not sure I follow the logic of the last 2 choices (or rather how we the character would come to such a conclusion for the "good" ending).Unfortunately, there are quite a few things, that are a bit worse than story:1. It's a blurry mess even after tinkering with settings (turning off blur and TAA helps a bit, but not completely)2. Sound positioning is quite bad: sometimes it sounds as if someone is walking on your head, but they are not and vice versa.3. Sound of your own footsteps is exactly the same as that of the enemies, so it's extremely easy to mix the two and be on high alert, when you should not be. Although may be this is intentional.4. There are a couple of puzzles related to sound and enemies do not react to them. And generally they do not seem to react to most of the doors.5. Then there is a puzzle with insignias, which, when solved, summons all the enemies (due to loud sound), but they can find you even if you hide before they arrive. And they are supposed to be blind.6. Got a bug, where opening gates across an elevator works, but I can't go through, because of invisible wall, which forces to go around.7. There are a few gameplay elements, that are poorly (if at all) introduced: tripwires, sound device, violet mist. There are also no logical hints for boss fight(s). I mean those, that would make sense if the situation was in real life.So would I recommend the game? Well.. If you do like exploration similar to Resident Evil series (with similar puzzles) - probably. Preferably at a discount. Otherwise - probably not.

_childDocuments_.review: Review Copy Provided by Wales InteractiveIn summary: Maid of Sker is the next game from indie studio Wales Interactive, who have released previous titles such as Late Shift and Don’t Knock Twice. Delving into the horror genre, Maid of Sker aims to capture an audience with an unique premise, one that really hasn’t been attempted in the mainstream before (at least to my knowledge): Welsh Mythological Horror. At first, and to be fair by the end as well, they succeeded in this regard. The story had captured my full attention, littered with intriguing imagery, disturbing yet informative lore notes, compelling character dialogue, and eerie atmosphere. However, the impact of all of this is minimized, due unfortunately to some minor technical issues, abhorrently broken mechanics, and overly obtuse puzzle solving. Maid of Sker is a majorly mixed bag, with pros and cons engulfed in a never ending battle of tug of war; keeping the title from becoming either a flawless masterpiece or an abysmal failure. Overall Score: 6/10For the full review, visit

_childDocuments_.review: This is an "ok" horror game. It's fine, but I will give it a thumbs down to balance out all the good reviews, because it ain't that good.The first thing I noticed when I started playing this game is how over-designed and cluttered the environments are to the point of being unbelievable. It takes place in a hotel so every corridor has to be full of luggage and bags, more benches than you'll ever need, random piles of books on every bench, and of course nothing can be straight against the wall, everything has to be placed at an angle and in disarray because that's horror, right? Sure, to a degree. But when every area is so cluttered, and so over-designed, it starts to not make logical sense anymore. There's literally bags for 200 people in a hotel with 15 rooms. Why is there a random wooden crate in this toilet? Immersion is important in a horror game and if the environment isn't believable it is hard to get immersed. I dunno, I don't have this problem in other games but here I noticed it very quickly.Gameplay is fine. There's no combat, it's just about sneaking past enemies and there are a lot of them just roaming around. The fact that most enemies are blind makes it easier so the developers put lots of them in the areas. It plays kind of like Resident Evil in that you have a big building to explore with locked doors and themed keys to find, but it's still pretty linear. There's even a big stompy enemy like Mr. X in Resident Evil 2 who roams around freely at one point in the game. You just have to run from him, he actually can see. There's a couple of puzzles but they're all extremely simple.Sound effects, music, and voice acting is all good quality. But it's also bad, when it comes to gameplay. Most enemies are blind and only react to sounds, so you have to be quiet, there's even a button to hold your breath. If you make a loud sound they'll come running. Except some sounds they can't hear at all. A loud ringing telephone? Opening or closing doors? Can't hear it. You not sneaking? They hear it immediately. But even when you're sneaking your footsteps are quite loud. Ring the bell at the reception? They come running. But on the first floor there's a puzzle that involves ringing bells, and those they can't hear at all. It's all very inconsistent. What might sound loud to the player might be silent to the enemies.The story's premise is at least unique, but it's not told that well. There's not much of a mystery, you figure everything out pretty early, and there's nothing else going on. No surprises. And it's really not very scary. The atmosphere is good but the design of enemies isn't really scary, it's just dudes with bags on their heads.The graphics are good, but like I mentioned before every single area and room is so over-designed and cluttered, personally I thought it just looked odd. It also tends to look a bit blurry and filtered.There's also this bizarre challenge mode that reuses the maps and enemies for a first person shooter, makes it a completely different game. It's nothing more than the bare minimum for some extra content. I guess maybe that's good because the normal game isn't very long. I finished it in just under 5 hours, and I took my time and explored everywhere.That's it, a horror game that's just "ok". Nothing special, not terrible. One of those sideways thumbs for me.

_childDocuments_.review: The typical "we are making an indie game because we have purchased Unreal Engine 4 and the templates are fee/cheap" game where the trailer is the best part of it.AI is basically non-existent, the tension disappears after the first 5 mins when you realize how not to get caught or noticed, after that the game can be literally walked through without a single enemy encounter.Voice acting is good and the original idea behind the story was interesting, but the delivering was mediocre and the game itself is incredibly boring and repetitive.The most negative point in the game for me was when in a mission, you are dropped into a situation where you have 10-15 seconds to act and you have to choose between 10+ options to get out alive. It's random and if you die, you are basically back 5-10-15 mins (whenever you saved last time), because this sequence comes right after a scripted part of the game. _childDocuments_.review: Maid of Sker is an ok horror game that I don't really recommend. I was a bit nervous at first when at the beginning of the game there is a piano that's playable. I'm not musically inclined at all and this story heavily revolves around music and I thought I was going to have to be able to read music to solve the puzzles. Thankfully, there was only one real music related puzzle and it was easy to solve. All the puzzle boxes are pretty easy to solve. Figuring out how to access all the parts of a hotel is where the real game is.The game took just shy of 5 hours to finish and it would've been quite a bit shorter if it hadn't been for the monsters that shamble throughout the hotel and they're everywhere and it seemed like they were always blocking my way, slowing down my exploration. There was some back tracking in this game and it seems like the monsters are just there to pad out the game as all the back tracking had to be done in slow motion so I could stay quiet while crouch walking  around so the monsters wouldn't hear me. The main interaction with the enemies in this game is via sound. Running around will make the character breath heavy and bumping into things will make sound and alert the enemies to your presence. The player can hold his breath to avoid smokey areas that will make him cough and again alert the enemies. The problem with the implementation of the sound is that it's not clear at all what exactly can be heard. It seems like some sounds should have definitely be heard, but weren't. There are also some bells that can be wrung that will divert enemies from where you want to travel. The core dynamic with the enemies just wasn't implemented in any kind of substantive way at all. These abilities  were incorporated into the game with just no reason to use them, really. Maid of Sker is not scary. The atmosphere was decent. The graphics were just functional. There wasn't much interesting going, visually. The stage was set well enough for horror, the content just wasn't there for scares. When I started writing this review I was going give it a soft recommendation. When actually analyzing the different components of this game, I have give it thumbs down. This horror game is not scary, the main sound mechanic is poorly implemented, and the puzzles are way too easy.

_childDocuments_.review: Maid of Sker is a first-person survival horror game set in a creepy, remote hotel inspired by Welsh folklore. The game’s strong suit is its atmospheric tension, sound-based AI, and deeply unsettling story. However, while it has great potential, it suffers from occasional technical issues that detract from its overall experience.The game’s atmosphere is its strongest aspect. Set in a dark, foggy Welsh hotel, the eerie setting draws you in, making you feel as though you’ve entered a place cursed by both supernatural and human horrors. The sound design is exceptional – the Quiet Ones, enemies who react to noise, create a uniquely tense experience. The haunting renditions of Welsh hymns add a chilling touch that will stick with you long after playing.Maid of Sker blends exploration with stealth, as you try to navigate through the hotel, avoiding enemies using a sound-based defensive device. The game is at its best when you’re sneaking past the Quiet Ones, listening intently for their movements. However, the game suffers from some frustrating mechanics. There are instances where certain actions meant to distract enemies don’t trigger correctly, causing some aggravation. Additionally, the controls and game mechanics feel clunky at times, and the constant mist effect, though atmospheric, can strain your eyes.The second mode of the game, “Challenges,” presents a much more action-oriented experience with weapons and more difficult enemies. This mode shifts from a slow-paced mystery to more intense, survival-horror gameplay, akin to Resident Evil. Though this mode is more engaging and varied, it is still hindered by the same flaws present in the main game. Maid of Sker is an atmospheric and suspenseful horror game that will appeal to fans of psychological and gothic horror. It does an excellent job of creating tension and a sense of dread through sound design and environmental storytelling. However, it’s let down by some frustrating gameplay mechanics and technical issues. While it offers a unique experience, those expecting a more traditional, intense survival horror might be disappointed. Check out more of my game reviews on my curator page:
