_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: I changed it to thumbs up (but it is still mediocre) because I actually played one more playthrough on Easy (~2 hours) to tick off a few Achievements (No Hit Run, don't use a "thing", the good ending, all collectibles, everything explored...) which was way less frustrating than my first run on hard. BUT it was still not super enjoyable. So why did I have a change of heart? I guess because a) I played it again even though I didn't enjoy it that much and b) I also tried the "Challenges" (at least the first one; now I know why they made Sker Ritual...) and actually had a bit of fun. But this is it for me, I am not playing through the Game 1 or 2 more times to get the other Achievements.THIS IS A THUMB IN THE MIDDLE (leaning just a little more down since my experience was kind of frustrating) but it is also not bad.I just wanted to get that out of the way first.So I had Maid of Sker sitting in my library for a while. But since Sker Ritual came out and I wanted to buy that also (which I finally did because a friend of mine also bought it), I thought that this was the perfect opportunity to play Maid of Sker first.Now a WARNING: If you play this Game for the first time, DO NOT PLAY THIS GAME ON HARD FOR YOUR FIRST PLAYTHROUGH!I will elaborate on that later on but just trust me on this.So yeah, started up the Game, checked the Options and jumped right into it on Hard.Graphically this Game is decent looking, it is no masterpiece but it is good enough.What I noticed in the beginning - which was kind of annoying to look at - was a strange "blur" effect on everything (trees for example). Also there were some minor graphic glitches in some areas which was not really that bad.At first I found the breathing sound when you are running a bit annoying but I got used to it. Overall I'd say the Sound design is really good, in some areas even excellent. And the Music is fitting as well.Both let the tension rise and you feel uneasy most of the time.In the beginning you seem to be hearing footsteps all around you and I think the beginning is the best part.But later on, at least on hard, the Game became more of an annoyance.Now let me dive a bit deeper on why I was so frustrated and why I gave you the warning to NOT play it on Hard (on your first playthrough).You only have 10 Saves and you can save in set saverooms on a grammophone.Of course as a first time player, you don't know how long this Game is, how far apart the savepoints are and what will happen in the Game.You just don't know how the Game works yet. How will enemies behave, how many are there, can you find a weapon to deal with them (I think in the Options was the "Hint" that you can actually shoot, so I thought you might find a weapon) and what will happen in general?!Let me tell you one thing without spoiling it: On hard there is a TON of enemies around almost every corner. And many places are VERY narrow. For a long time you have no means to defend yourself apart from holding your breath when they get to close. Enemies only react to sound but they can't see.So you will sneak a LOT and this is slow. Sometimes you also get sandwiched between enemies and there are few options to escape them.Let me just tell you, in the end I had only one save left and when that was wasted (which I didn't know because it was my first playthrough) I had to play almost half of the Game in one go.No dying or your whole progress is gone and back to the last savepoint it is. And the last half was the most difficult part.Now that I know what happens, yes, of course, I wouldn't use up my saves like I did. But this is hindsight, my first experience was frustrating because I didn't know what to expect.That also meant that I didn't collect everything as I had actually planned. Because I couldn't afford to die, so I just tried a straight route to the end and missed out on a ton of collectibles and thus also lore.This is why: Play on an easier difficulty.Also the Game came out in 2020 (4 1/2 years ago) and the Achievement that I got for completing it on hard is still rare. Only 2.4% of Players have this.Still overall there is a lot to like. The atmosphere is pretty good, the music and sound design is good, it is easy to control and the locations are also quite nice.It is also pretty short. Steam says I played for 4.5 hours but ingame I was told it was 03:13:17hrs.This also means that there is a Chance that I maybe play this again someday on an easier difficulty to get another ending and collect more things and read a little more lore.But I also have to be honest to myself. Even though it is kind of my fault that I didn't enjoy the Game as much as I could have, well, I just didn't enjoy it as much... I think that I got this on sale and some people maybe got it for free on EGS but I don't think it is worth the 20€ asking price.Closing words: Not a bad Game but you can destroy your own experience with it...

_childDocuments_.review: A game that left me with moments of extreme tension, all while strung along an interesting and unique storyline. The use of mythology and the eeriness of the Welsh climate really adds to matters. I enjoyed this game quite a lot!However, I will say that there were definite sections that were frustrating more because of the mechanics of the game or controls than skill. Additionally, it could do with a bit less of the mist effect, as it created a constant sense that my eyes weren't focused that was distinctly unpleasant. Overall, 7/10 and worth playing, but would benefit from some extra polish.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun audio-based horror game! You play as Thomas, a composer invited to his lover's family hotel on the Welsh island of Sker to save her from some mysterious danger. You have to hold your breath and avoid blind enemies as you traverse the dark, haunted hotel.The story is a little weak in my opinion, but it unfolds very well nevertheless. Told mainly through notes and environmental clues, the tragic story of the Williams family unfolds. The ambience and audio are really good, providing a spooky atmosphere throughout the whole game. It also uses Resident Evil-style save mechanics, where you can only save when you come across a  phonograph in certain rooms. This game also offers a fair amount of replayability, as there are collectibles and challenge missions (eg complete the whole game in the dark with a gun). Overall, I thought this was a solid horror game, well worth picking up!

_childDocuments_.review: (SPOOKTOBER REVIEW) I went into Maid of Sker with low expectations, but I was pleasantly surprised by the experience. The game nails its late 1800s atmosphere, with the, and I dare say, eerie hotel layout feeling straight out of Resident Evil and some great music that really sets the tone(I didn't knew Welsh music could be so good). This isn't the best horror game out there and its clearly somewhat going for the RE experience so this might not scratch that itch, but it's enjoyable on its own,at least to me it was.While Maid of Sker is marketed as horror, it feels more like a stealth game once the enemies show up. Puzzles are simple but stretched out because of the sneaking required to avoid said enemies(well its only enemy type most of the game), which made things feel slower than they needed to be. Later, a second enemy, similar to guy from resident evil that hunts you down, can't remember its name, so everything you learned in the game so far, forget it when dealing with him. There were some jump scares, but nothing truly terrifying compared to other horror games (Outlast, I'm looking at you).On the downside, I ran into some camera glitches mid-game that forced me to reload my save a few times. Luckily, the issue disappeared after I avoided using a particular mechanic to hold my breath when enemies were near.Overall, I say Maid of Sker is a solid atmospheric game with a few bugs and a heavier focus on stealth than scares. Worth a play if you enjoy atmospheric games with a bit of a slower pace.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s neat to see enemies which are guided by sound alone, but when I found myself triggering one of those guys, I could not really hide. I tried to stand still and cover my mouth in secluded spot, but enemies just run towards your position and start hitting. The only way I found to escape is just to run away far away, to a saferoom (or save room) or in a room which triggers a loading screen. Also gotta say, for a game heavily based on sound, I would’ve expect it to have a surround sound option, the immersion would have been better.Speaking of sound, you can slam doors around and somehow the enemies do not hear that, but you breathing, they sure as heck hear that. And regarding those NPCs, the AI seems brain-dead, so apart from the hiding, they also have some chaotic patrol patterns, often times they just walk into rooms which you just barely unlocked, and heavens forbid you end up in a dead end room with one of those NPCs behind you.So yeah, I am not a fan on how the stealth is done. Another thing I was not a fan of are the enemies, you keep seeing the same ones all over the hotel, but here is the thing, there is a Challenge mode (will talk in brief next) which does have some variety of enemies, so why they aren’t in the main/story mode?Anyway, about challenge mode, I can say it is one of the most fun parts of the game. To put it short, you are given a bunch of weapons, you blaze your way through the hotel and it feels damn good going Resident Evil on those guys.So why I am giving this a recommend? Well because it builds up the atmosphere quite well, with both graphics and sounds done well, the story however just decent enough.

_childDocuments_.review: So, there's not much to say about this game. It's a good game overall. If you enjoy an horror game you probably will like this one. It's not jumpscare based, I think I got jumpscared 2 times the whole game, which took me 8h to complete in the normal difficulty. On the other hand, the ambience is REALLY good, and the game is a lot based on audio, play it with headphones for a better experience. The enemies are blind due to a story related thing that I won't spoil, so the sound is really important.It has 2 endings, a good one and a bad one, which totally deppends on a single choise, which I don't think is the better way to do this different ending stuff, even more when you can't save a checkpoint before your choise so you can see the other ending. I did the bad ending, not knowing about it, then went on Youtube to check the good ending and it's SO MUCH better than the bad one... I felt like I had so much work to finish the game for a mediocre ending to be honest, but it is what it is.I wouldn't count that has a con, but I do have some cons about the game, which I will mention:- There's a form of self defense, but in ANY part of the game I felt the need to use it, so it was useless. Maybe in the hardest difficulty it could be useful ?- There's a boss in the upper floor, which I think has bad programming, because anywhere you are he will follow you, even if you stay completely still.Also some pros I'd like to mention:- The boss fights are really well done for a game where you have no form of attacking the enemies directly;- There's a pacific difficulty option where you just explore what happened in the hotel without the enemies spawning, which is nice for people that enjoy exploring but don't enjoy horror games;- The puzzles are pretty simple but well done aswell. There was 1 or 2 that I didn't really understood but maybe because I was being dumb, which happens pretty often.To end this review, I got this game offered to me, and I do think it's a good game, but not for the full price they're asking, compared to the content they're delivering. There's like 4 or 5 extra mini games but it's always the same but with harder enemies and darker rooms.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished streaming and I'd say this has been a solid game that I'm glad to have played.StoryI feel Maid of Sker has a unique tale to be told, not necessarily that its plot beats are anything novel but the way the narrative is presented is as engaging as it is fascinating. Utilizing its Welsh setting and drawing from Greek mythology establishes a creative story that keeps the enterprising player intrigued right up to its conclusion, even culminating in a decision which feels genuinely difficult to make even after the lore discovered throughout the main character's foray through the hotel.Setting + SoundAn eerie atmosphere is established right out of the gates. From the moment the main character, Thomas, steps off the train that has brought him to the outskirts of Hotel Sker and through the entirety of the hotel itself, Maid of Sker is oppressive in ambience. Due to the nature of the game's cult antagonists abhorring sound the player becomes hyper aware of every sound in the hotel. Does the creak of floorboards come from old wood warped from age, or are those the tell-tale steps of a cultist shifting about? Thomas's steps seem to thunder in the hotel's quiet, the ruffle of shifting carpet is a din in the player's ears as you are acutely aware of every step forward you take.This quiet lends itself well to the setting as the sound-sensitive cult has ensured a brooding atmosphere that is remarkably broken by the songs of the Maid of Sker. Placed throughout the hotel in the form of collectible and objective items are "music boxes" which cut the silence. The music in Maid of Sker is as beautiful as it is haunting, thoroughly fitting the somber tone of the game while being excellent pieces in their own right. Finding the songs is as much part of the reason to play as is pushing through the story as the player feels compelled to seek out more of this tune whose presence remains a constant, yet seems never fully finished, so the player continues pushing onward to hear more.GameplayThe weakest element. Granted, Maid of Sker has 4 difficulty options and I chose to play on Normal. After my experience I feel like Hard would offer the best reactive tension to the game, but due to clunky pathing issues it's hard for me to suggest playing the game at its highest difficulty setting.Simply put, enemies in Maid of Sker are dumb. At the Normal option the game advises that enemies are attentive to the player and fairly aggressive should they be alerted. Though never pleasant, encountering a cultist in the hotel isn't a death sentence. More often than not (every time in my experience) after opening a door and coming face-to-face with a cultist the player can escape by covering their mouth & simply walking backward; even at a crouch Thomas moves faster than the lumbering cultists ensuring that, so long as your path ahead is clear, you will always be able to out-crawl the enemies around you - save for one terrifying monster later in the story. After a certain point most of the tension in the games comes from waiting for enemies to pass their patrols rather than whether they will actually find you. Even at Normal, which suggests enemies will give some chase, there was a moment I ran RIGHT past a grunt and, though alerted, the AI didn't bother to chase me around the corner despite it being close to the path I took.However, I can't recommend Hard because the pathing in Maid of Sker can be downright clunky. Generally moving isn't an issue, save that Thomas moves at a snail's pace unless he's running, and even that feels slow - the character in Outlast would run marathons around Maid's MC. The biggest crux is that Thomas will catch on the most random clutter on the ground and it completely disrupts his pace. Further, if this happens while you're actively holding spring to run Thomas will not automatically resume running even after you've freed yourself from whatever you bumped into. This can add some tension and frustration to encounters where the player is trying to be quick in their movements, only to have to move Thomas robotically over the floor terrain. On top of this, it's incredibly easy to become stuck in place if an enemy does catch you in a bad corner. There are locations in the game that appear meant to be obvious spots to step off the path while waiting for enemies to pass, but if one choosing to come into your vicinity then Thomas will get stuck between the environment and the enemy with no way to escape, even using the stunlock weapon eventually acquired will not save Thomas from this predicament as he simply hovers over the now cowering enemy waiting for them to recover and pound his face in.7/10Despite some glaring issues with the gameplay itself, I feel the story, setting, and sound of Maid of Sker do the title incredible justice. My favorite part of horror games is often the story and uncovering the mystery of whatever led to the events that are now so terrifying to experience, and Maid of Sker keeps that thread going strong right up until the end. Even once the plot is all but solved there are enough counter-clues within the clues that will leave the player speculating what to trust within the narrative as the final curtain comes to a close.

_childDocuments_.review: overall, this game is a fun experience, with some replay value for collectibles, and a relatively interesting concept. it feels a bit like the games that really took off in the 2012-2017 era of youtube let's plays, with a focus on stealth, mostly linear progression, and atmospheric environments and soundtracks.it evokes amnesia: the dark descent and skillfully wraps mythology into its main plotline. it's regrettable that some of the voice acting is not quite believable, and the plot overall is fairly thin. however, it's serviceable for the approximately 6 hours of gameplay you're likely to get out of it, and with two endings to see, it's a well-executed, if not revolutionary, atmospheric horror game to check out.

_childDocuments_.review: Positive review but only barely.The game does so many things exceptionally well, the first 20 minutes have an atmosphere thick enough to make even Horror veterans sweat. When the enemies do show up it all falls down the stairs. I understand the "Not everybody is a fighter" mentality but the fact the enemies are blind men with bags on their head that just punch, kick or grab you completely destroys any tension the game had. At least give them a knife or something, any reason for them to be a bit scarier. The game does look gorgeous, the puzzles are fun and don't get repetitive and exploring the hotel is a treat. The story itself is predictable but still entertaining enough to want to see it through to the end. This game could've easily been a cult classic if it put more work on making the enemies scary.

_childDocuments_.review: At the start I thought I was in for a treat - it looks immersive and has good ratings. It's a cool concept for enemies to not see you, but hear you. The immersion I thought would be there was just an illusion, because while it does look nice, I also feel like I'm dumped into the game with nothing to ground me, nothing to tie the player in with the game's world and make clear their place inside of it. You play as a bland sponge of a man. As for the enemies, I really felt like they were all too easy to run past, and I had no incentive to pretend they were scary or like sneaking past them was something I had to do. This is because they would lose me fairly easily, and if they did hit me? It felt like being hit by them had no true consequence because I knew I'd disappear by running far enough away. Once you're out of earshot for them, you've disappeared. Nothing about this game is scary, instead it feels like I'm going through a poorly constructed haunted house. The narrative is uninteresting, and the save feature is tied to in-game recordings of characters talking. The last thing I want when saving is to be stuck in a room listening for lore. If it were interesting lore, I could forgive it, but more often I find myself leaving the room as soon as I've saved. The character interactions feel shallow - the dialogue from Elizabeth felt more like she's being used as a mouthpiece by the writers, her words feeling meaningless. There is no sense of urgency, instead there is the sense that she isn't my first priority. This is strange because I was under the impression we're here to save her. Back to the enemies. After stumbling through what felt like random events I had no interest in going through, I'm given a device which can stun enemies? At least, I figure that's what it does, because I've never used it. The game is already too easy without it and I wanted to prove a point: I do not need something to make the game easier. In fact, I might not have even noticed there were enemies in the game if not for scripted sequences, so giving me something to combat them is meaningless to me. I need to finish this game sometime but I can't bring myself to do it. The thought makes me want to groan.

_childDocuments_.review: Inspired by an actual location with a dark history, Maid of Sker from Wales Interactive is a memorable, if imperfect, chapter in horror gaming. The player takes on the role of Thomas Evans, who has just arrived on Sker Island in search of his lover Elisabeth. Thomas soon learns that Elisabeth is being held against her will–and by her family no less–for sinister purposes that become more articulated as the game progresses.Arriving by train as so many horror story protagonists have in the past two centuries, Thomas makes his way to the decrepit Sker Hotel, which you can probably already picture. Opulent to a degree that seems economically untenable given its remote location, the Sker Hotel has recently undergone a revival for the ages, though that has all come apart by the time Thomas reaches its doors. Inside we find creaking halls, blood-stained floors, and eventually, a nefarious cult whose origins lie at the heart of Maid of Sker’s very solid story...Full Review:

It's a solid horror game that I think most people would enjoy, especially Resident Evil fans. It had a very similar feel to RE 7 and RE Village. _childDocuments_.review: "Maid of Sker" delivers a hauntingly atmospheric horror experience that stands out in the genre. Set in a remote Welsh hotel, the game immerses players in an eerie narrative inspired by Welsh folklore. The attention to detail in recreating the historical setting is commendable, contributing to the overall sense of immersion.The game's emphasis on audio-driven gameplay, using sound as a crucial element to navigate and survive, adds a unique and chilling layer to the horror. The strategic use of silence becomes as important as the unsettling soundtrack in building suspense.While the pacing may be deliberate, allowing players to soak in the unnerving atmosphere, it may not appeal to those seeking a fast-paced experience. Nevertheless, "Maid of Sker" excels in creating a spine-tingling ambiance, providing a memorable and atmospheric horror adventure for those who appreciate a slow burn and psychological tension.

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game. I'm a huge fan of survival horror, and love the Resident Evil and Silent Hill franchises. The story is great, the music is beautiful, the Sker Hotel is just absolutely stunning. The concept is fun and creative. The puzzles were pretty intuitive IMO. The only problem is that if you miss certain things, it can be a while/frustrating before you get to go back. The only bad thing I have to say about this game is that at least on Normal mode, the bad guys don't drop aggro. Ever. At all. So if you aggro even one dude by mistake (usually by being impatient), you're dead (unless you have modulator charges). They can open doors and go anywhere except safe rooms. They run as fast/faster than you, it seems. Which caused me to have to reset certain parts a ton of times, which was really frustrating. I ended up bumping the game down to Easy when I was in the basement just so I could get to the end.But overall, I highly recommend this game, especially on sale. For 5 hours of game play, it's worth 10-15 bucks. i wouldn't pay more than that though, just because of the length of content and lack of replayability imo (it's a story, so once you finish the story, there is really no incentive to go back unless you're an achievement hunter).

_childDocuments_.review: Length <4hrs‘Maid of Sker’ really creates a strange feeling while playing, visually impressive and an interesting story which does well of mixing a supernatural mythological story into the real world. Yet at the same time the game really felt unimpressive: there are no standout moments, no moments of fear, and the game just feels off. Like I am within a world that just does not feel like everything fits together.The problems with ‘Maid of Sker’ really come from the gameplay, enemies are abundant and will shuffle through the halls. The player will be avoiding them at all costs and will have to be quiet while holding their breath to not engage them. This leaves a lot of moments of the game as the player just waiting, and really becomes irritating when you are sitting waiting for the one enemy to move out the way. Sure you can just run for it, if you have a good understanding of the map you can get to safe zones before the enemies catch up to you. Most players will just be waiting and this really made parts of the game a slog to get through.Horror moments I felt were really weak, the problem is all the enemies look similar, the formless faced beings that chase the player really don't look scary. Visually they were not striking and instead the game relied on a mass of them to cause panic. While there were a few good animated scenes, they felt like they were put in just to show off the main enemy, and really were not striking to the character. Take ‘Outlast’ we see the traits of the core villains appear throughout the game, and understand the characters inclinations based on it. While in ‘Maid of Sker’ we really get the first moments then it’s just another enemy.The way the mansion was laid out was great, and it was designed in a way to open more as the player progresses, there was no one route given to my exploration and really made for a fun time being left to my own choices. Looking through different rooms as I pieced together what was going on was great.The story was really well done, while when playing the game the foreshadowing was easy to work out, the actual narrative beats were done well. Learning of what happened in the hotel and the history behind its successes really made for a convincing plot when you are wondering who the villain is. The mix of mythology and horror was really well done, while I wish there was more utilisation of the idea as gameplay mechanics, I still appreciate how unique the story was. The endings really offered two different choices, and rewarded the player for finding all of the needed items.Overall ‘Maid of Sker’ has an interesting story, some great visuals and is worth the experience. Although I really find the horror aspects disappointing as it just was not scary, with some tedious gameplay which drags on the game. It is worth the play but I have no desire to play through the game a second time.For those wanting a video to look at check below, it may be worth seeing what I mean by the sneak and wait gameplay mechanics. Looking for horror games check out my curator page, who knows what you may find:

_childDocuments_.review: A very pretty setting and some nice mythology/storytelling through documents helps to give tension to the game. The audio-based stealth actually makes for some scarier visuals, with the player able to hold their breath as enemies pass close by. It's not high-adrenaline terror, but it's a reasonably scary, tense experience set in a gorgeous Welsh hotel. I appreciated the actually correct portrayal of the creature involved, as well.I'm not a huge fan of the "collecting keys to advance" approach to games, but it is a classic and this is hardly the only game to use it so I wouldn't consider it a reason to mark it down. Personally, I find it more frustrating that the game seemed to have started off as storytelling and stealth, but then the challenge modes (and the spinoff combat game) seem to have gone in a wholly different direction that I find much more generic and therefore less interesting. I also had to turn down the graphics to the absolute minimum to be able to get this game to run, and it was still jerky enough that playing on Hard was simply impossible because I could not ring two bells or press two buttons in close succession, especially with the pressure of enemies. That said, my computer graphics are at the minimum for which the game called, and if you have a more powerful PC this will probably not be a problem for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: An immersive horror experience with great atmosphere and setting. The haunted hotel of Sker Island is a terrific place to explore. The environment design was the definite highlight of the game for me. Also, Abraham was really great, the short while he was around. Could've used more of him. The game features some very light puzzle solving and key item hunting- very light. All the puzzles are extremely straightforward and 99% of the key items happen to come across you as long as you keep your eyes on the screen.  The game's main mechanic around enemies is stealth coupled with a cool "Hold your breath" system. It works pretty well in favor of building tension- but after 4-5 hours, kind of starts to overstay its welcome. You'll rather take easy cuts around enemies and sprint whenever possible, because man do the enemies walk S-L-O-W in this game. They are slower than my 88yo grandma. Except Abraham. You'll know what I mean once you see him. Overall I do recommend this game, considering its relatively cheap price, and you do get good bang for your buck if you're looking for a good quality, modern looking horror game. (Looking at you, "PS1-Styled" horror games.)

_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: This game is... okay. But I can't really see myself recommending it to anyone.I think the biggest issue with this game is that first-person survival horror games are quite common and dominated by a few, much higher quality games.Maid of Sker doesn't bring anything new to the table and it does not excel in any aspect, it's mediocre all around.It's not very scary, the controls don't feel good, the story isn't very interesting or original, the environments aren't very interesting or diversified, the "enemies" aren't very scary or interesting and the "puzzles" are neither difficult or clever. It looks okay visually and the music is nice... But there are other games out there that are just better in all of those aspects.It's sad because I can tell a lot of effort went into it. But when you're competing with great games at a fraction of the budget... You really need to do something to stand out. Pretty much everything I've seen in this game I have seen in another game done better.The "Challenges" add gunplay which feels like it does not belong in this game at all. It makes the gameplay a lot more fun, considering the main story consists mostly of waiting and sneaking around... But as a FPS, it's very sub-par. It's very poorly put together, there's no feedback when you shoot enemies, enemies aren't very well animated and everything just feels very clunky overall.I finished the main story in a little less than 4 hours and kept playing to collect the remaining collectibles (notes and a single type of collectible that all look the same) and see the second ending. Exploring and collecting stuff was very tedious and frustrating. I played through the first challenge and I have no interest in playing the other ones.Seeing how they're developing "Sker Ritual" a spin-off that focuses on the gunplay aspect, it feels like the "Challenges" are basically just a prototype for their new game.I have to say, their promotional work is really good. The presentation is fantastic and all their trailers make the game look really good. Much better than it actually is. They massively oversells the game in those. For instance the second trailer advertises "Survival resources", shows a health pickup then the player interacting with an object that pops-up the menu. You then see EVERY SINGLE ITEM IN THE GAME. It doesn't even make sense progression wise (you'll have used and lost a few of these at that point in the game) and gives you the impression that there is way more items in the game than there actually is.There are health pickups and "cartridges" for a tool you can use in a portion of the game (also shown in the trailer). That's it, those are the only survival resources in the game. The rest are either puzzle items or items you need to complete the game. The main goal is to collect 4 cylinders and 4 music sheet for the "true ending", the trailer shows all of those items which you either cannot use or use once in the game to progress.Just keep that in mind. The game is mildly entertaining and not too expensive but it looks way better than it actually is. I think I would rather play through Resident Evil Village for the sixth time than play this game at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: On my quest to find another short horror game for the end of October, "Maid of Sker" was found in my library. Follow the weird occurrences in Hotel Sker in a nicely made story, which includes elements from Greek mythology to Welsh folklore.The game has an interesting story - Elisabeth, the daughter of the owners of Hotel Sker, faces the challenge to stop paranormal activities in the Hotel, which basically were not of natural origin. Yes, difficult to write a summary for this game without too many spoilers! Anyway, Thomas has to find some loot in the hotel, which would help Elisabeth to stop what is going on there. On his way through the hotel, he will have to avoid being detected by blind zombie-like creatures, who nevertheless have a very well tuned sense of hearing. This helps in keeping some form of lights int he game, which makes it easier for the player to navigate through it.The map is well made with enough places to hide and enough shortcuts to unlock. As a beginner, it was a good choice to play in easy mode - so many things are going on and/or could be missed otherwise. This includes the nice puzzles, which are solvable without any outside guidance. Well thought through!Only one small bug was encountered in the first playthrough on Win11, and even that one was helping the player :)But be aware: saving (if needed) is only possible in predefined locations!

_childDocuments_.review: The difficulty in Maid of Sker is what you want it to be. I played it on easy because I'm sick of survival horror games one-shotting you while you search for items. _childDocuments_.review: A nice and concise horror experience.The whole story is based on Welsh folklore and everything happens inside this haunted Sker Hotel. You can easily see the inspirations from games like resident evil and silent hill, but don't get fooled by the promotion video, the game mechanism is focusing on sneaking and the it doesn't really offer weapons to fight (except some sonic bomb for stuns) in the main game, the gun-fight scene is from the 'mercenary mode' of this game. Some might find this hide-and-seek playing style drying up pretty quickly, but it's a rather short story so for me this game ends before I start to feel bored, which is nice.Two fun facts in this game: 1. Multiple deadly traps in this hotel, but none of them tries to hurt you. 2. Pet the dog, it saves your life later.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a decent horror game with a neat little breath-holding mechanic that I haven't personally seen used to this effect. The way they incorporated it into the gameplay was well done. The story was good. It was pretty easy on normal, but had a couple challenges here and there. A few moments that made me jump. Plenty of collectables and puzzles too. FPS was locked at 144 FPS on my RTX 3080, which is to be expected as the textures in-game are pretty muddy overall. Still, I'd rather have great performance than amazing graphics. The results screen at the end of the story said it took me around 4 hours to complete, yet I've got 10 hours played according to steam. Either way, it is a very short game, but honestly, by the end it was just summed up really nicely and it didn't really leave me wanting more. Just a good "One and done" kinda game. I recommend this game for the $12.22 AUD price that I paid for it.

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Stunning visuals. The overall lighting is great and although the 3d graphics are not top of the notch they have managed with clever art direction and some tricks like image filters, fogs, volume lights, flares and floating particles to deliver a fantastic result. Wherever you look there is an amazing scenery to admire or take a screenshot.- Strong, creepy atmosphere. Right from the beginning you'll get immersed inside the loneliness and sickness of its world.- Great sound quality. Rich environmental design with lots of creepy sounds like footsteps, creaks, eerie noises and more that will make you shudder with fear. Protagonist's breaths give an extra touch of agony. Surround is also well built and enhances the gameplay experience, especially when you try to understand from where the enemies are coming.- It's a nice survival experience. It doesn't offer anything remarkably new at the gameplay department, but it's a well implemented "Resident Evil" inspired experience. Controls are simplistic, yet effective. You 'll get used of them almost immediately so you'll feel free to concentrate on the story right from the beginning.- Music is awesome. The main song is one of the most atmospheric and terrifying things I've ever heard in a video game. - Although there are some cliché parts like the stranded manor and the fearless, for some reason, protagonist, the story in general is interesting and manages to maintain your agony and curiosity till the very end.- Great direction. All the routes that the game forces you to follow are carefully selected, the framing between doors and windows is clever, there are everywhere amazing sceneries and the overall pace is really good. Also, the cut scenes are only few minutes but they are really good.- Although it is pretty linear, it gives you a feeling of exploration's satisfaction. The story is set in one building, but there are many different places to discover. The whole manor is a big puzzle and you have to search everywhere in order to collect the missing pieces.- Puzzles are simplistic and pretty easy to solve, but they are playful and give an extra dimension to the game.- It doesn't uses silly, needless jump scares like so many other horror games. It's mostly based on its well built atmosphere and story in order to give you the chills.- It has some, less stealthy, challenges to play after finishing the main game that involve weapons in order to kill more and hide less.The bad- Some stealth elements of the gameplay needed more polishing and variety. Also enemies' AI is pretty weak. They are just too dump. After a while you get used of them and begin to fear them less and less, so the frightening atmosphere slightly weakens too.- The survival element almost gets ruined by all these actions that stop the time. Each time you pick up the phone or an object or you open up the inventory and the map real time freezes even if there are three enemies around you ready to attack. It just looks like a cheat, like breaking the rules of reality.- Although there aren't silly jump scares, this sound that indicates danger tends to get triggered at random moments which is a pretty cheap trick if they wanted to scare you.- It would be nice if there was a bigger variety of enemies. These guys look a little bit generic.
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: Great atmosphere. You'll get a good heart attack when you turn a corner and see an unexpected enemy. The scripted scares weren't effective, though. Maid of Sker is very Resident Evil inspired, add stealth and subtract guns (the guns are in the challenge modes).However, it's exhausting to wait for the slow enemies to finish their patrols so you can pass them. You'll be cropdusted for minutes before you can progress. Also, I hate this game's puzzles. Here's a guide on how to complete a lever puzzle:1. Pull first lever2. Go to door, realize it won't open as it's not fully powered3. Pull second lever4. Go to door again to open it. If there's more than two levers, repeatYou cannot pull the two levers in one run and head for the door. The second lever will be unusable until you hit the door button. It's stupid and infuriating that the game is designed this way, especially for a game with speedrun potential. It's a major reason why I'm not recommending this.4/10

_childDocuments_.review: I have more positives than negatives of this game, and if I have to give it a rating out of 10, it would be around 7. I will start with what I did not like, and then end this review on a high note.Before you think my rating is too harsh, considering the ratings it got from professional gamers, I want to point out to the reader that this game is first of all short (you can play it through in under 5 hours). Secondly, the game's difficulty is not very intuitive. Harder difficulty just make the enemies tougher, the damage they inflict higher, and the likes. The game itself is not changing otherwise. The game's mechanics are a bit buggy from time to time (for example, sometimes your character will not run when you instructs it to) and it appears to be caused by objects in the game (a table that is in the way, but still a step ahead, seems to block the execution of the command occasionally). The peripheral vision of the camera movement was quite nauseating for me - looking at the screen a long time got me kind of like having a mild headache. This is not something I experienced with other recently played games of this kind.Now for the good part:This game had me at the end of my seat most of the time I was playing it. The story, although a bit short, was well developed, and the game was challenging enough to make me want to continue plying it until the end. It triggered my "completionist" nature, whereas a lesser game would've had me stopping whenever I got bored. I did not get bored with this game. The graphics are reasonable, and based on the credits, it is a relatively small development and graphics team that developed the game, and to me, being a developer myself, realized how much work they've put in as a team to get the game as smooth as it was.All in all, I am very positive about this game, and I will play it again at different levels to get all the achievements, which I have not managed to get during the original playthrough.I hope to see more games from this developer!
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: A really good game (especially the challenges) that had a few jarring moments, like the odd design choice behind the crushing walls "puzzle", enemies randomly swarming you after unlocking stuff, or the entirety of the second floor.. but despite all that, I still enjoyed the story and the game as a whole. I highly recommend it, especially if you like stealth games (I don't :P but the overall unique setting made me suck it up and finish it)

_childDocuments_.review: I would cautiously recommend this game for the story elements alone, which were strong enough to carry the game. It would have been nice to have some enemy variety in here. You had baghead and tubby shirtless baghead. That's it. The A.I was noticeably inconsistent at a few points in the game, namely the library. The sound design also didn't feel up to modern horror standards and I found it more difficult than it should have been to determine which direction footsteps were coming from and how far away they were. Failing at basic, important sound design elements, along with the inconsistent A.I, (Literally the only two things a good horror game has to nail down) the best I can do is recommend this game for the story and it's endings, which, I don't want to oversell, but were good enough to warrant the playtime. 5/10. At first I had thought the SOMA team had a hand in developing this game, which had me questioning how drunk they were when they made this, but it turns out that they merely recruited some of the writers or something, which checks out. Good writing, eh game. I'm still debating on whether or not to recommend this. Meh. It's your life. I don't know you so I don't care if I waste some of it. Recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this a positive score, but only barely. The game has many strengths, but also some glaring flaws.Let's begin with some good points: The art of this game, especially for the backgrounds is phenomenal. This game has the best depiction of a pine forest I have ever seen in a game and the old mansion that as the game takes place in the late 1800s has just been installing indoor plumbing and electricity in hideously unappealing ways if you were to live in it, but great way to add to the atmosphere. There are slight hints of steampunk in the main game, but I'd still call it a period piece.About half a year after release they added in some extra challenge modes that rearranges the mansion a bit and have you trying to escape it from top to bottom armed to the teeth. The main game includes no combat but this mode is filled with it, quite the contrast. The extra modes also includes some new enemy varieties which lean more heavily into the steampunk aesthetic.The action is pretty satisfying although some of the enemy death animations are a bit iffy.The voice acting in the game is quite good, and while there's not much in the way of character animation seeing as every enemy wears a hood over their faces, what's there is quite well done.As for negatives: The level design is quite good if you look at how the maps are built and the back and forth finding keys and backtracking together with solving some puzzles to progress. But it's a bit let down by the gameplay and how empty it often feels. Not empty from a visual standpoint, the place is cluttered and chaotic in a very realistic way. No, empty in stuff to do. Oftentimes a room will feel like it's just there to make the travel time between two other places longer. The room might look really good, but it'll be void of anything interactable or tricky encounters. The notes scattered around the place is also a bit oddly paced. The notes are often quite long, but there aren't that many of them. I think the games pacing would have benefited a lot from splitting up the notes and spreading them out more.Like I said before, the main game has no combat, it's purely stealth with the middle section of the game also having an item that can temporarily stun enemies around you for a few seconds. The stealth however seems a bit inconsistent. Although not quite as inconsistent as it seems at first. The game has a thing where bumping into furniture makes enemies nearby aware of you, but there's no sound to indicate you bumped into something so it isn't obvious. There's a loading screen tip that mentions this function of the game but I only saw this after getting an achievement for bumping into a ton of stuff which is when I realized that was even a thing.The stealth, once you really figure out how things work however isn't that great. All enemies are blind and hunt you based on sound and touch alone. But if you hold your breath, your footstep sounds apparently also doesn't reach their ears? And also, while you don't make any audible breathing noises (and thank god for that) as you hold your breath you make very loud inhalation and exhalation noises which they apparently can't hear. The game is also void of different materials that make different amount of noise and things like that. You can begin to cough if you walk into a dust cloud or near a burning fire, but just holding your breath completely stops any coughing from occurring. So the stealth ends up feeling very simplistic, and while there isn't a ton of health items in the game, I still never felt like I was close to running out of them either.And those are the two main problems, a beautiful world with too little to do and a stealth system that seems a little unfinished.I think adding in some combat into the main game could have varied it up a bit, or just stealth takedowns perhaps since you're trying to keep quiet. Spacing out the notes a bit more and perhaps splitting the health items into more, but less effective ones so that you'd have to explore more yo find them could have also made the world feel less empty.There are some other nitpicks of course, like in the extra modes some of the animations are not even close to as good as the stuff from the main game, like if you decapitate someone the head just disappears and the body ragdolls for like a tenth of a second before freezing stiff which sometimes results in some funky looking corpse poses. There's also some statues and paintings that get repeated in the mansion a bit too often and the weapons are a bit less detailed than most things in the game, but a lot of these problems are from the free bonus modes that were added in later and won't be encountered in the main game.The ending also lacked foreshadowing until very close to the end of the game so it felt a bit out of nowhere, but not in a mindblowing way, but rather in a "really?" kind of way.I hope these developers make more Survival Horror games in the future. This one has a really solid base, if they improved upon the stealth and pacing in a future game and put the combat into it rather than having it exclusively in bonus modes I think they could make something truly classic.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty cool game for horror fans, if you like Amnesia/Outlast you'll like this too probably.The Graphics are a solid 8.5/10, very good and stunning at times, but there's a pretty clear lack of graphics options in the video settings.The sound work for this game is GREAT, from the soundtrack to the actual sound fx, the team behind this game clearly put a lot of time and attention into making the sounds perfect and weaving them into the games atmosphere. Sound is also a very big part of the game so I'm very glad that they went all in on making sure that the sound is actually accurate and reliable. The gameplay is about what you'd expect from this kind of game, although it does have a challenge mode which is pretty cool, I haven't tried it yet but it looks interesting. Sometimes the stealth can be a bit buggy, and heals are VERY hard to come by which can make some parts of the game SUPER frustrating, but as long as you're conscious of where you save it isn't the biggest bother in the world on the normal difficulty at least. I will say though, if you don't like stealth games, especially stealth horror games, you won't be a fan of this.The story is actually very unique and I enjoyed it a lot. The late 1800's Welsh aesthetic mixed with a gruesome cult story, with a very cool twist that ties it all together in a way that I would never have expected by combining mythology with culture is very unique and something I would like to see more of. There's a lot to uncover, and its kind of hard to follow narrative wise since a lot of lore details are revealed to you by recordings of past events that are shown by the save point system, this makes it kind of difficult to follow at times and leaves the player to have to fill in blanks as they go because its possible that you could miss listening to one recording, and listen to another recording later on and be confused because you missed a detail. The premise is very very good, but the execution is kind of so-so depending on how flawless your gameplay is.The stability is pretty good, although I did encounter some annoying bugs, like once I phased through the floor of the map into an endless abyss and ended up having to restart from the last save spot I had. I'm 99% sure this is a bug, but if you're injured and use the pause menu to restart from the last save point you retain the same damage as you had before. But other than that the game ran flawlessly with no frame drops, sudden crashes, visual bugs, etc.Is it worth your money? I put a little under 7 hours which I do think is a little short for $24.99, but its worth it for the experience. If you want a game you can burn through in a night and aren't concerned about replayability, I'd say it's worth the full price. But if you don't feel like spending that much on a 7 hour stealth horror with minor design flaws, I'd say wait till its on sale.Overall - 8.5/10 would recommend buying this game on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Another one of those releases which make you ponder the world you are living in. Not because of the content or story per se, but rather because of a lot of the receptions you find about it in Real Life.But first things first: The actual game and its gameplay.Id say the game is OK. I have played my fair share of 3D (Horror) Games in my life, and I cannot say it stands out. That being said: I also don't think it is badly done. The environments are atmospheric and well detailed. The realistic horror plot is solid and well delivered (since its based on Folklore it doesn't have too many twists but is rather straightforward.. but why not?). And I certainly see what the devs tried to achieve here.There aren't a lot of "enemy types", true, and those enemies which you encounter are fairly straightforward. But that fits quite well. It is a game of one fragile human who is pitted against insanity. Not a game about some killing-machine supersoldier, special agent or whatever. I honestly believe the world needs more such games which also let you play those which might not easily go around and shoot whatever threatens them.Being that fragile human being, you will instead hide, sneak and try not to be found by the lurking danger.The games story is closely linked to the theme of "sound" and I think this is well delivered as well. Be it in the old phonographs or phone boots, be it by ambient sound or be it just by the ever looming threat of footsteps around the corner. It will make you very keen on listening for nearby danger.That being said: Reviews stating the enemies AI is fairly poor aren't exaggerating. I believe the game could've extended a lot on its system of "hearing enemies", like having enemies react a lot more sensible on opening doors, bumping in furniture or using mechanisms. Like the player having to mind the ground they are walking on or like having them try to obfuscate their own sound with nearby other sounds. Instead the enemies seem to ignore a lot of noise where the player would think "uhoh, that was way too loud" and avoiding them becomes fairly routine at some point. They couldve introduced gameplay where you actualy try to make some noise to lure enemies away (like the hotels early rooms suggest) and try to use your environment to your advantage... but sadly (played on hard difficulty) the game falls short on it and rather throws a larger amount of enemies at you to raise the difficulty.Now the interesting part about the public reception I mentioned earlier:Looking at reviews and the discussion board I found quite some opinions like "its like Resident Evil but without the guns".So what did the Devs do? They added Challenge Missions where you fight the enemies in good old gun-ho-style: Guns Blazing.They actualy did a good job doing that too, much like they wanted to say "alright, we can do THAT too". And for this they certainly got my respect. I only tried the first Challenge Mission, but they put quite some effort into it, with different "enemy types" whooting lasers, flinging fireballs and whatnot. It was quite a decent Challenge already.Still, to me, who actualy enjoys games which try their own approach, which try do things different, the whole situation is quite a pondersome thing with a bitter aftertaste.Anyhow.Bottom Line:Its a solid game for its current price tag (25€ at the time I write this), and I believe its well worth its price. But you really gotta be able to enjoy just a well crafted story with atmospheric surroundings to really appreciate it. Certainly a recommendation if you have an itch for another decent 3D Horror Story (and can be tolerant to the games shortcomings).

_childDocuments_.review: Solid horror game.It's nothing groundbreaking, but it is indeed competently made and I got an evening of fun out of it.  Everything about this game is really only slightly above average but it comes together to be greater than the sum of it's parts. It's obvious the game was completed on a small budget (the odd choice of only having half of telephone conversations voiced was a bit jarring I have to say), but they do make the most of what they have.  Voice acting, where it appears, is decent, the game does a grand job of keeping you immersed, and the sound and music and ambiance are all alright.The puzzles are pretty light and are mainly centered around navigating the map, avoiding enemies, to get to places to trigger switches and collecting items to enable access the next part of the house.  And thought the game is set entirely within a sprawling mansion and grounds that you have free roam over, by and large you'll find you're channeled into a fairly linear means of progressing through the game.There's a couple of interesting stealth mechanics included as well.  One is you have to hold your breath to avoid coughing when going through smokey/dusty zones to avoid drawing enemy attention.  But as long as you pay attention these are easy to spot so there's no real challenge to it.  And you also pick up a device that is basically an EMP grenade but for monsters.  Activating it sends out a sonic discharge which has every enemy within a fairly big range paralysed and clutching at their ears temporarily, giving you time to run away.  Useful when you've walked yourself into a corner.  But ammo is limited so you can't blast it constantly.  Beyond a couple of boss enemies, basically every enemy is just a reskin of every other one, and as long as you stay crouched and don't run, you can get ridiculously close to them without being detected.  A likely concession the developers had to take given the majority of the game takes place in crowded household environments.  Overall the game is easy enough.  I played it on the second hardest setting and, though i hobbled along on low health on a couple of occasions for an extended period, I never actually died.Finally, the game length is just about right.  Approaching four and a half hours of gameplay and winding up with what seems like the best ending is just about right for the asking price (I got it for ~9 euro).Overall it's a recommendation from me.

_childDocuments_.review: ((Spoilers included in review so ignore if you are thinking of buying the game, read the first bit ONLY))This game follows your usual D.I.D (Damsel in Distress) Plot story: - Lady gets involved in something potentially bad (In this case, her family does something traditional)- She gets in trouble.- You have to save her- You save her (Depending on the ending you choose)- Profit.Game was stellar from start to finish, it has you captured with very little defense (Like outlast) but instead of hiding, you are hidden from their "radar" by holding your breath. Sound is your enemy so you must use it to your advantage. The enemies are rather touchy with sound so to the point where you bump into things makes a sound? Enemies are alerted and the game does this really well. ((Spoilers from here on))Soundtrack: 10/10 The Music captures you from start to finish and lures you as the whole point of a Siren's song is explained or indented into you throughout this game, forcing you to follow it to key items but the soundtrack is nothing to complain about. From singing to the score used for this game? All is well balanced.Voice acting: 6/10For the soundtrack to be the forefront of the game, the game has a similar problem to outlast (But outlast did it better for sure) where the protagonist doesn't say much but screams most (if-not) all the time. The protagonist, "Thomas" doesn't really do much either than: - Scream (Pathetically and mostly lackluster considering the situation that occurs to make him scream) - Cough (Rather strongly compared to the scream so it's somewhat confusing)- Catch his breath after sprinting for 5-10 steps. (Someone's very unfit lol)Elisabeth on the other hand, was a perfect example of "less is more" where she played an amazing D.I.D (Damsel in Distress) but around the twists of where she begins to be somewhat "evil" she falls flat and almost deadpan to where her "evil laughs" are tough to listen to on a cringe level. Her Singing and her voice acting otherwise? Stellar.Environment: 10/10Absolutely gorgeous, from start to finish. Every single still if you were to run around blindly for 10 seconds and stop, could be a dynamic wallpaper for your computer. It was beautiful everywhere.Dog:10/10The Dog in here is a good girl and you will love her with all of your heart like how you did in Resident evil 4.Story:9/10The game has you captured from start to finish, but the ending gives a big crescendo with no climax (or if you're generous, there could be one but it's VERY lackluster) There's so much buildup and you are waiting to see what's next and even with the ending you chose, both are very much a letdown but the game makes up for that with a "breathtaking" (lol) journey from start to "final scene" not finish. Specifically said that way, because the final cut scene isn't something to write home about either than it was really cool to see the Siren for like 20 seconds before it flies away and "all is well"Bugs found:There are a few story-locked traps in the game you must go through but I was able to somewhat "Exploit them" by accident of course. One has you fall through a trap door but I was able to get out of the trap door area before it opened. Wonder if that's out of luck or not? Despite me not falling, the scream audio still played as if I did. Another was when I was trying to run away from the uncle through the gaps you can crawl through but he still managed to hit me when I was on the other side in another room but still crawling which made the death animation start and the both of us were clipping through the wall.Overall: 8/10Great game, above average voice acting, great story, great environment. Just wish it could've been a little better on those areas.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game, but I do think the price point is a bit too high for what you're getting. The main story is ~4-5 hours, and there's a new FPS mode that was recently added as well with a few different scenarios you can play through. The main story was cool and interesting, but a bit short and somewhat too linear for my preference. I also felt that there wasn't enough puzzle solving involved in the game -- I'm a huge fan of classic survival horror, so it wasn't the lack of action so much as just the general lack of things to do other than walk around the hotel. There were some puzzles, but I wish there were more, and just generally more interaction with the environment. It would've been nice to see the devs take a page out of the books of the devs behind Remothered and incorporate ways to distract enemies right into the environment. There is a small amount of that here, but you really only experience it in the first area of the hotel. Despite my qualms, I did have a lot of fun with this game. It was entertaining and creepy, and the story was awesome, I just wish there had been more there for what you're paying. I'd wait for a sale, but still pick it up.
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sorry but the AI is just broken. You get detected when you are not even moving and far from the enemy and sometimes you can go right past them and they don't react at all. Short game, good concept but way too linear for my taste and appart from random injuries from the broken AI, it's not really challenging and not a lot more than a walking simulator (ok a bit harder than those but still)
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: Survival Horror with a Twist. The game has an extremely interesting story based on a Welsh Novel from the same period, that will keep you hooked from start to finish. The AI is a nuisance sometimes but to tell you the truth it didn't bother me at all.If found at sale, it is an experience worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was going to vote it down because the dull gameplay but after a while you get into it and the graphics and audio are great, very atmospheric.You have to sneak past the monsters and the antiquated save system means if you screw up you might have to replay whole sections. It's a bit like old Resident Evil games (or their remakes) where the puzzles unlock different sections of a house and then you have to backtrack and can only save if you make it to a save room.So get it only if you like that type of game and with a good discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: The hotel is a gorgeous, dilapidated place of horror. The game oozes atmosphere and deserves to be experienced.The actual animations of the enemies are a bit stiff, as you'd perhaps expect from a minor studio, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ the surroundings are gorgeous. Just drinking in the sights is amazing.Oh, and it's also proper scary.
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: It isn't really scary, but still worth playing if you like first-person survivals. Pros:- Graphics are nice. - The music is wonderful. - The game is somewhat similar to Outlast, in that it relies on stealth/running to avoid enemies. - I particularly enjoyed exploring the 1st and 2nd floors of the hotel. Cons:- The game tends to get boring at times. It would have been better if the enemies could see a little bit, to make things more challenging.
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: This one was pretty good! I was so disappointed and angry with the Amnesia Rebirth I just wanted a new horror game. I really liked how much this kinda reminds a bit of Resident Evil 7 and Resident Evil 1 Remake with the atmosphere.Although this isn't so scary, it's still exciting and that works too! Actually the only bad thing I have to say about this is that it's pretty short after all. Maybe I shall try out The Dark Anthology next. Some day...8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this a thumbs up because it did suck me in, despite its problems. If you enjoy "cat and mouse" stealth gameplay, where you're relatively defenseless and have to avoid enemies, you'll probably like it. It's dripping with atmosphere. The stealth works well partly because ths game has such a strong sense of place - Sker Hotel is rendered in incredible, moody detail.The main issue with the gameplay is that it's too simple. For 85% of the game, you're avoiding stupid, slow moving enemies who can only detect you by sound. The sound mechanic could have been great but the desingers only added a few ways to be heard, like walking/running near an enemie, or coughing if the air quality is bad. If you crouch-walk near enemies and hold your breath in dirty air, you'll never have a problem. If wish they'd added more ways to make noise, like stepping on broken glass, bumping into furniture and whatnot. The game eevntually introduces new enemies but they're essentially boss firghts and are over quickly. When you return to old areas, the game usually chages up the patrol path of the enemies but they never add new dangers.  The original Resident Evil added hunters when you returned to the mansion and it was scary as ♥♥♥♥. But there's little tension as the game goes on because the enemies just aren't that threatening.And yet I had fun sneaking through the creepy old hotel, avoiding enemies and occassionally almost getting caught. Just wish there'd been more to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: An enchanting adventure through the myths of the "siren" song, the one making men losing their will. The darkness of the game is heavy to feel, like a night wave. You're in a mansion near to the ocean, but the trembling confined atmosphere evokes the inside of a sinking ship. The gameplay focuses on stealth : no weapons, your only friend is silence. The scenario touched me very much. Now I'm curious about the novel "Maid Of Sker".
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: The atmosphere, graphics, music and narrative elements are great but the gameplay can be somewhat tedious. The whole holding your breath mechanic is cool but you dont even need it on Normal mode, and enemies are predictable, you just crouch and let them walk past you, and even if they find you theyre not scary. Its more of a thriller than a horror, its just sad that the gameplay is so fundamentally flawed or else it would be amazing.Still a good one and done game though
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Absolutely beautiful graphics.- Dark, dreary, haunting atmosphere. You can almost feel the dread.- Excellent music selection (nothing that overwhelms or feels out of place).- Good story -- engaging, compelling, mysterious, and terrifying.- Blind enemies with excellent hearing adds an interesting dynamic to the gameplay.- The device that serves as a weapon for part of the game is rather unique. - The concept of music being either a saving grace or a curse is interesting in and of itself.- Having the phonographs not only serve as save points, but also play noteworthy dialogue for the plot.- Great sound design! Sometimes I thought I heard footsteps besides mine but it turns out it would just be other sounds in the environment. Other times, I’d hear loud creaks in the hotel, and I had to check to make sure something was coming after me.- Good ol’ doggos!Cons:- Why can’t the protagonist walk backwards? I thought this was very awkward, especially since looking behind you may be important in a horror game.- Elizabeth’s voice actress sounded kind of flat to me.- Why doesn’t Thomas speak? It seems a little strange.- The Uncle reminded me too much of Mr. X from “Resident Evil 2.” - It seems a bit too “gimmicky” that, to unlock certain doors, you must hit a switch, then go hit a button, then hit another switch, then hit the button again ...basically, you “run” back and forth for no real reason other than to draw out the game. Why not just flip all switches then hit the button? It still poses a challenge but a less tedious one.- Not sure if this is a con but the bad ending is pretty obvious if you’ve paid attention to notes throughout the game. Would have been nice if it were left more ambiguous so it would make it more challenging to make a final decision- Quite short -- maybe a few hours of gameplay at most.- Becomes less frightening the more you progress and become used to the mechanics. It's a good horror game, I think, but I don't see it being worth $25. When it's on sale, then yes, I'd say it's worth buying but otherwise, it's a bit much to ask for a game with many flaws.
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: Even though this game is a very short experience, it is well worth the price. This game is like if Amnesia The Dark Descent, Resident Evil 7 and Outlast 1 had a baby. The Atmosphere is almost always tense and eerie so that when scares do happen they don't feel cheap. The only thing that frustrated me about this game were the saves. at times i would be right near a save and because i made a little noise and got killed i had to replay 15-20 previous minutes of the game to finally get back to that save. Overall a very enjoyable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: This game was amazing! I was genuinely scared exploring the HUGE map. There's so much to explore and great storytelling in this game. To keep spoilers out of this, THERE IS MULTIPLE ENDINGS. I think it adds an element that other games don't have. This reminded me of Outlast with the different "Boss" people you see. And I found myself being super quiet myself. The sound mechanics are amazing and the fact that the enemies can't see you but can hear you adds a new element. Even though they couldn't see me It honestly felt like it lol. I was fully immersed in the story. The only thing I felt was wrong with it was the enemies, as soon as you mad a noise, it's like they instantly become unblind and just know exactly where you are lol. I really want either a 2nd part, or a prequel to dive into how this family ended up this way. I think it would be super interesting.  If you wanna pay and support the developers (which will be worth your time) I STRONGLY recommend to but if not, I'm uploading my whole playthrough on youtube.
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: Very aestetically pleasing game, amazing sound design and a somewhat unique story.The game doesn't reinvent the Horror genre, it sticks to the formula of older stealth and puzzle oriented games, like Amnesia, Outlast and other similar games. Still it's refreshing to see a Horror game finally be done right again.Unfortunately the voice acting didn't hold up to the rest of the sound design and with around 5h, it's a bit short for it's price.But for someone who is tired of the same old, same old indie Horror games, Maid of Sker is a great opportunity to finally play something good again.
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: With Wales Interactive being based in Pencoed Bridgend South Wales I thought Maid of Sker would be based on Sker house in Porthcawl I live 6 miles from Sker house.Anyway it turns out that it has absolutely nothing to do with Sker house in Porthcawl and looking at a map in the train station in the game Sker Hotel is somewhere of the Irish coast.I absolutely loved the game great suspence and atmasphere Wales Interactive have MAID a cracker and I hope there will be another or one like it.I enjoyed it so much that I have bought the game on the PS4 so now I can enjoy it on a 50 inch tv with surround sound.Its great to support a local business all the best for the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: Nice Indie Game, but I'd rather call it scary and gloomy instead of horror. This is based on atmosphere and setting instead of jump scares. The plot is interesting and based on mythology. Only aspect I really didn't like - or I'm rather fed up with by now- is a lot of hiding, sneaking and running from enemies similar to "Outlast" and countless others these days. I wish developers/ programmers would stop this "hide and sneak"-theme and start with psycho horror again (as in Lovecraft's works, Silent Hill, etc.). Otherwise it's getting a bit boring and predictable. Still, I recommend this game cause it's interesting and entertaining.
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: Maid of Sker is a thrilling first-person stealth-survival horror game set in 1898 and actually inspired by Welsh folklore that has already produced a well-known novel.  The main hook for the game are the sightless enemies that basically turns this into an interactive version of The Quiet Place.  Most of the game will be spent in darkness while trying to sneak around silently, even to the point of holding your breath when enemies are near.  Maid of Sker is beautiful; traditionally so during the opening train ride, as we see a stunning landscape sweep by from outside and inside the train as well as haunting beautiful once the train deposits us at the abandoned station.  Even the golden rays of sunshine can hide the fact that something is definitely wrong as we make the long trek to the hotel’s front door, and once the sun goes down all bets are off.  The audio is fantastic with an amazing soundtrack, truly terrifying sound effects, and some really good voice acting even if some of the conversation choices are a bit silly.   I had a terrifyingly good time with Maid of Sker.Full review at  and you can check out the first 80-mins of the game on our YouTube channel -
_childDocuments_.name: Maid of Sker

_childDocuments_.review: Wales Interactive delivers another solid Horror title I enjoyed this one for the most part.  Although It doesn't do anything innovative or genre defining it's presented in a fairly polished and immersive manner. Visually it's pretty stunning albeit a tad blurry and hard to see sometimes there is a good amount of details in the environments and nice lighting. Sound design wise once again holds up with some nice original music as well, the directional sound was quite good in my headphones which is super important during the stealthy bits. Story wise it's easy to follow and fits the overall sense of dread and unease throughout, I dug the mythology and Siren folklore stuff. Gameplay is the typical find some keys hide from the baddies ect nothing exciting which is the main issue with the game it's all same same ham sandwich kinda of stuff nothing us Horror fans havn't seen many times. I was hoping there was more complex elements(more survival/puzzles ect) but it's rather straight forward and easy game taking only about 4hrs for me to finish which at nearly 30 dollars CAD isn't great value. As a die hard Horror fanatic I purchase any new Horror titles I can get my hands on just to feed the itch but if this ins't you, you are probably best waiting for a sale or passing on this one. It's a solid experience but too safe and familiar. 7.2/10
