_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: It's a revival of the  (and therefore easier, for some) by the impecable level design and modern framerate. The levels have an amazing flow you can follow, everything is placed just at the right distance and with timing to keep you going forward. Collectibles are lined up as to teach mechanics and new movement skills. Challenge stages are well hidden and offer great training. . Of course, being like DKC, expect quite a lot of frustration while repeating parts of levels you aren't getting the gist of.The only downsides I see are: the soundtrack, while good, doesn't quite reach the DKC grade; the final chapter, levels and boss fight included, are a bit too brutal for my taste, I felt like the challenge was more about the movement flow being broken, to trick us, rather than like on previous chapters, where the difficulty was matching the skill level the devs demanded; and finally, while it only happened like 5 times in my 14 hours of playing, I swear I've gone through platforms I should've landed on, killing and angering me more than usual.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: I do believe I'm in the minority here, but I cannot recommend this game to people other than those who enjoy extremely long sections of trial and error (particularly in Original Mode). I was really excited to try Kaze, but before I even finished the first world I found the game to just be an endurance test. As of writing this I have just finished the third world. This is coming from someone who has played extremely little of the Donkey Kong Country titles, which this does seem reminiscent of, so it is likely just not my type of platformer. As a massive fan of Celeste, I picked this up wanting to experience more precision platformers but I just haven't enjoyed my time with Kaze. There's clearly a lot of care put into the aesthetics and deliberation in the level design, but I just can't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Kaze and the Wild Masks is a beautiful platformer game. Graphics, enemy design, main character everything looks fantastic. It really plays like the platformers from the 90's. Controls are fluid and responsive. Controlling Kaze is easy and super responsive. Level design is really good and it offers a lot of variety. Boss fights are cool. The game is not challenging but checkpoint placement can be cruel sometimes. It offers a lot of replay value as well. In order to complete a level %100 you have to collect gems, find 2 bonus levels, find the letters that spell KAZE, finish the level without getting hit and lastly finish it under a certain time to get the gold medal. You can spend a lot of time trying to achieve these in every level. Soundtrack is nice, there are some nice tunes. My only complaint with this game is that enemies don't pose a threat. Most of them just walk back and forth. When you die in this game, it isn't because of enemies, it is because of gravity. I think enemies could have been more aggressive and agile. Other than that it is an amazing game from start to finish. A must play for the platformer game fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Quite a fun little game. Great artwork. Controls are simple but tight. The music is wonderful (I especially loved the ice level theme!). Level design is good and I really enjoyed how it favoured boldness. Hesitating usually meant ending up struggling more than when you are just bold and keep pushing forward; once you tap into that flow, things just gel really nicely. While I personally didn´t care that much for one of the dragon mask levels, all the rest was top notch. Beat it in about 7-8 hours.I also quite enjoyed the added extra challenge of completing the three tokens for each level (I didn't get all of them yet though :D).All in all, a really nice little platformer that harkens back to the days of playing games on the SNES.Well done PIxelHive!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: A bit short, but fun 2D platformer romp.Seems to be channelling Donkey Kong Country and Rayman Origins/Legends for inspiration.Nice enough flow of movement in the game and the 4 different masks do provide some differences in gameplay.Not much to complain about. If you like old school platformers, and have 5-6 hours to kill, this is quite good.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This game has really creative bonus stages and level designs and gimmicks and just enough to set itself apart from Donkey Kong Country, especially the tiger mask . I'm really glad I put down Deedlit in Wonder Labyrinth before even finishing its third area and I think I'll finish this game rather than Alwa's Legacy which I put down earlier but picked back up.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very competently designed platforming game with 16bit-era mechanics and difficulty but coated in modern HD graphics. The game seems innocent enough at first but gets progressively more difficult with each level. For the most part it's a fair challenge with plenty of variety in its platforming mechanics, but it's also often pretty rage-inducing (just like games were back in the day!). There are also time-trial challenges, collectibles & such that add some replay value.I have two complaints. First, the auto-scroll levels (there are three, I think) represent a HUGE difficulty spike, as you have to rely on memorization and trial & error a bit too much. You'll probably die more times in these few levels than in the rest of the game combined. Second, while the boss fights are fair, they are of the kind that I don't really like whereby you have to wait for the boss to finish its move routine until you get a chance to hit it once.Anyway, if you're looking for a challenging and ultimately rewarding platformer with pleasant graphics and good mechanics, Kaze should be right up your alley. But you better have nerves of steel and a high tolerance for pain.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Kaze is a true homage to the Donkey Kong Country platformer games with a charming graphic style. It stays true to it in every way: enemies, masks that feel like animal companions, challenging bosses, hidden bonus levels in every main level and lots of bananas... uh... crystals to collect!The real surprise for me that Kaze held is that its level design is just as good as in your favorite entry in the DKC series!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! It's mainly inspired by the Donkey Kong Country games, with a bit of Rayman Origins/Legends involved and a . The main feature of Kaze is the masks, which are similar to the animal buddies of the Country games. I personally love 3 of the 4 masks, with the exception of the dragon mask which functions like the minecart levels of DKC, which I didn't adore either. So it's clearly a matter of personal taste, the dragon mask levels are still well designed.Overall it's a really fun platformer that you can nearly 100% in a little over 6 hours (I got everything but the complete speedrunning achievements and the complete no hit achievement). I wholeheartedly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful game with tight controls, great level design and satisfying platforming, and I absolutely recommend it to any Donkey Kong Country fan.There are some things it even does better than the modern offerings like Returns and Tropical Freeze; the titular masks with their unique controls and alternate playstyles are filling in wonderfully for the animal buddies from the SNES games, which were sorely missed in the recent DKC games. And in particular, Kaze's bonus rooms, which are all unique and clever challenges with their own goals and mechanics, eat Tropical Freeze's bland and repetitive bonus rooms for lunch.That said, the boss fights are the elephant in the room here. They're all terrible, I won't sugar-coat it. The bosses in DKC often left something to be desired even at their very best, it's true, but every last antagonist in Kaze is cut from the same cloth as Little Horn from Super Meat Boy, or Colonel Pluck from DKC Returns. You just have to survive and dodge their attacks for way too long, get in your one hit when you can, while they're briefly vulnerable, and repeat. It's miserable.But it's not enough to ruin an otherwise excellent game. If you like Donkey Kong Country, or sidescrollers in general, you should check this one out. Just be prepared for its lowest points.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: A bit above Mix. I don't find this game interesting most of the time.Good:(1) Good character development - rabbit glides using ears, grab ropes using ears... devs put in some effort.(2) Starts easy then increasingly goes harder, focus and keep a good rhythm, a lot of the time you need to jump on multiple enemies to proceed, timing is essential.(3) If you fail too many times the game allows you to skip and win, even for a boss level.Things to be improved:(1) Machines remain the same in different islands. A change in the background art is easy to get people bored.(2) Occasionally transform into a tiger, eagle and shark, but still run like a rabbit.(3) Could use more enemies, or more detailed graphics, add some animation or cutscenes. It is not exciting.Honetely for a similar price I'd pick Witcheye, Mighty Goose, Zool Redimensioned etc.

_childDocuments_.review: An hour in and I can easily say that the latest entry in the DKC franchise is really great so far! I love how Dixie is back, though, she looks a little weird honestly... and Diddy's... a floating head, or... something. Anyway, it feels just like the old games, and there's even some visual design reminiscent of another favorite of mine, Super Mario World (I swear, those slopes are the exact same angles).You know, thinking on it more it seems like they changed a LOT of things actually. The bananas look totally different (they're all crystallized or something?), the "KONG" letters (which I was glad to see are still here!) are... I think one or two of the letters might actually be wrong? It's just not like Nintendo to miss something like that... gosh, even the Kremlings, they're all in these weird vegetable costumes!Anyway, if you liked the other games you'll surely enjoy this one! And even if you've never played any of them before... if you enjoy challenging, quick platforming, delightful, fun visuals, and a lovely, energetic soundtrack then... just give it a go anyway; I don't think you'll regret it! 😊

_childDocuments_.review: Initial impressions had been to say it's a charming game and reminiscent of greats such as Donkey Kong Country on the SNES. Now at roughly 30 hours into this delightful platformer, I can say it brings much more to the table or rather, as much as you'd want a game to bring with the benefit of knowing the 90's greats from hindsight. The soundtrack is top tier--the theme in particular captures an honest, adventurer's spirit that I look forward to experiencing in all kinds of remixes. The narrative is uncomplicated but enriches the game. The bosses are better realized than any of the DK bosses, the masks bring a unique spread of experiences that add a compelling flavor but more than anything else--the level design is deceptively brilliant. First, you'll likely notice that the game has several achievements which favor time trials and speed running--each level is designed to be run smoothly from start to finish and once you've mastered the timing of your jumps and enemy placements, you'll find it satisfyingly silky smooth. Then, however, there is an entirely new version of each map for folks who master the speed running mechanic--the spin jump, where you press b at the edge of a platform to spin forward and propel your jumps further and faster. Once this move is in your arsenal, you will notice there is an entirely deeper level of design brilliance to be appreciated as the levels not only run smooth if you don't employ this, but run with devilish genius once you do. The end result will leave you feeling like you've expertly threaded a storm of needles to arrive at the end of the game (Jelly Dungeon and Scalding Gears are in particular, fantastic). It's like your own skill unlocks an entirely different version of the game. This degree of design finesse speaks to a care and love that went into crafting this game that I have not seen in any recent Triple A titles and reminds me of such hits as Hollow Knight or Celeste. A joy of a game that has something for a casual player and someone who really wants to get great at it. I cannot suggest it enough.

_childDocuments_.review: 1) Beautiful art style.2) Good level designs/music.3) Boss fights/music where my  thing in this game as they had the RIGHT balance of fun/challenging WITHOUT being frustrating to beat (along with hype music),  (see below).1)  The "ground pound" attack should've been given its  (like the "B button" on the XBox one controller) because I had many MANY  when I meant to "hover" instead of ground pounding, particularly in the "Free Fall" level where I wanted to drop down a rope and then immediately hover, but SO MANY times Kaze ended-up doing a "ground pound" instead which resulted in so many unnecessary deaths in this stage and many other stages too (Note to developers: please add a control option to give "ground pound" its own button instead of being the same button as the spin/hover button).2) Bouncing on enemies does NOT allow you to "hover" immediately after jumping on their heads and I really DISLIKED that aspect because that also led to many frustrating deaths (especially with how low Kaze bounces off their heads), not to mention the fact that bouncing really "kills the momentum" when you can't immediately hover after bouncing on the enemies heads. (Being able to "bounce+hover" would've made platforming feel so much smoother/better IMO)3) No dialogue/voice-acting during the story and no other characters that could've breathed more life into this game's universe (like for example 4) The game is very short, even after getting 100% collectibles, especially for its current asking price ($20 on PC and $30 on consoles). I feel the short length of this game and the fact that it doesn't have that much of replayability value, may not be worth that price (especially compared to  which costs $15 and has so much replayability value with 3 different characters and alternative story paths).5)  Unlike the earlier bosses in the game, the final boss in this game was a  To be more specific, my problems with the final boss fight can be summarized as follows:- The backstory of the final boss was told through "photos" you unlock in the gallery section rather than proper cutscenes, which really didn't give any "identity" to the final boss and made the final boss so forgettable and not really feel like a "true final boss" at all. Simply put, I just didn't get any sense of why should I consider this boss as the "final boss" at all without proper backstory-telling first IMO.- The final boss fight SHOULD'VE had their own "intro cutscene" before the final fight, but nope, the final fight immediately began without any context and that was both confusing as well as being very VERY anti-climactic/underwhelming for a "final battle".- Unlike the previous bosses who had awesome/hype boss music, the final boss music was TERRIBLE/BORING.- The final boss battle itself was not well-done at all and didn't utilize the power of masks very well at all (it was more "running/dodging" than actually using those masks to hit the final boss). The whole final fight felt frustrating rather than fun/epic (all previous boss fights were done way better IMO).- Even when the final boss is "dizzy" and is about to die, if you wait or don't proceed to deliver the final blow (and I wasn't even sure what to do at that point), you just "instantly die" for no reason whatsoever and I find that aspect to be quite stupid/punishing, especially after doing everything right all the way to the very end.This game is clearly inspired by the original "Donkey Kong Country" trilogy on the SNES and while this game has done well to follow in the footsteps of the Donkey Kong Country games, it honestly doesn't add or revolutionize those games using modern hardware/technology the same way  did to the "2D Sonic the Hedgehog" games which had voice-acting, great cutscenes, so many unique characters/villains, character abilities and so on. But nonetheless I think "Kaze and the Wild Masks" is a good starting point for this franchise and should this game get a sequel in the future, I hope it avoids all the "Cons" I listed above and that it should learn a few things from  when it comes to revolutionizing old beloved 2D platformers when creating a "spiritual successors" to those games in the modern era.

_childDocuments_.review: Kaze and the Wild Masks wants to hearken back to the '90s with its very DKC inspired design. From its two-hitpoint, one checkpoint, 2D-side-scrolling design to its moveset (spinning off a ledge gives you so much coyote time just like DK's roll, and you can pick up and throw some jars just like barrels) and masks (some definitely hearken back to the rideable characters in DKC), one might be forgiven for calling this game a "clone."Unfortunately, I can't say this game is nearly as fun as DKC.The big problem with this game is the level design: it quickly devolves into autoscroller after autoscroller where minor mistakes routinely give you no recourse but to simply die or lose your only precious hitpoint. Whether you're chased by a tornado or zipping down a long line of ziplines or climbing up rising ooze or stuck in that godawful autorunning mask (more on that one later), rarely after the game's halfway point do any of the levels give you a chance to simply stand still. And the sections get _so_ long after island two; dying and having to do 2 or 3 whole godforsaken minutes of the same platforming over and over and over and over and over and over and over and over because you keep hitting one in a long sequence of precise buttons a couple frames too late or accidentally got slowed down by a missed jump you think you can recover but nope there's the danger ready to autokill you... it just gets tedious. The fun disappears quick and if you truly want to stick with it, eventually it all feels like a waste of time.It becomes trial-and-error. There are some sections that genuinely require a specific set of inputs at specific times in order to get through - with literally no other way to move forward. Miss one input? You fell into a pit and have to restart the section again. This is especially the case with the autorunning mask. I genuinely don't know what they were thinking with that one; I must have died over 60 times in one of its levels just trying to figure out what it required me to do. And don't get me wrong, I do like the occasional minecart to break up the monotony. But the autoscroller gimmicks in this game are just way too excessive - and precise.I played through to the any% ending on original difficulty (and FYI my hours are messed up because I played it on deck in offline mode for a time), and I considered doing another playthrough on easy to better flesh out my opinion - because who knows, perhaps the increased health points and checkpoints would have made the game much more tolerable. And perhaps if I do end up going through with that, I'll edit my review, but for now I really don't want to touch this game again.Idk, if you really like trial-and-error, perhaps this is the game for you; but I really don't think it's fair to compare this game (or at least to compare it favorably) to DKC.

_childDocuments_.review: Game looked fun and bought it on sale without much expectations. After finishing the game 100% on original mode after 5 hours of playing I can say really enjoyed it (had some frustrating moments too).The art style was already appealing to me, small cinematics were also cool, the controls were quite tight and didn't expect the game would put up a challenge sometimes. _childDocuments_.review: At first I was a little disappointed because, at first, it feels like a reskin of Donkey Kong Country 3 and, while that's my favorite DKC game of the series, I wanted this game to have iterated upon the DKC formula and wanted to know what this game had to offer that was new.But boy did they deliver. This game is awesome, it has some new concepts and the challenge is pretty good. Also the final boss is amazing. It brings in everything that you've learned so far, even the powerups play a part in that fight. (It also has a casual mode, though I don't know how different the challenges are in that mode)The concept of the masks themselves are akin to the DKC3 animal barrels and are just as refreshing as those are in DKC3 - They break the monotony of the way you play the game and the levels are designed around them, keeping the challenge fair and fun. My favorite is the Dragon mask. It makes you feel like a badass in a rage without removing the challenge (the challenges with that revolve around platforming and smashing enemies to stay in the air).The music is great, the art is gorgeous. I wish there was more art in the game, but we get enough to get a grasp of the story and when art appears it feels like a treat.There are bonus levels (after completing in-levels bonus challenges) which are a fun extra challenge and definitely worth unlocking.The game is also great for speedrunning. I'm not a speedrunner, but when I tried going as fast as I could. things just seemed to fall into place to make speedrunning work. Also, no RNG from what I could tell. Unlike DKC bonus 'collect green bananas' barrels, green gems always spawn in the same location, so you can plan around that.Advice: Ground pounding gives you a little extra height. If you're going fast, you may just be able to reach things and platforms by adding groundpound to your jump, instead of going a bit further then backtracking and "losing time".

_childDocuments_.review: The comparisons to DKC are accurate for better and worse. The mechanics are almost identical, as are the objectives, enemies and the level design. It crashed at the end of the first level, then again when I entered a level and returned to the overworld. After it hung again when trying to quit the game, I decided to get a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: Donkey Kong Country 2 is still one of my favourite platformer ever to this day. I thought I could give Kaze and the Wild Masks a try and I did. Although I can't leave a good recommandation on it. Why ?Because even if it's clearly inspired by DKC (and especially Dixie's gameplay), the game feels really uninspired. This is like a 1:1 copy pasta of DKC with the same level design, but with a mix of good pixel art and wannabe Sonic (and I'm sorry, I hate Sonic Art style). Levels feel bland, the music doesn't sound catchy enough to keep me going. The parts I love about DKC 2 is how it feels surreal but still natural and smooth to play. The musics are on point and the gameplay is really responsive.In Kaze, sadly, not so much. Having the hovering option after a jump, but on the attack button... Really ? Air control feels really limited and why should it be bound to the attack button ? Also it would have been cool to have a running button but hey, after playing the first few levels and the "Parrot copy pasta level from you know which game" I felt demotivated to keep going.I still wanted a game that clearly takes inspiration from old school classics, but I never thought this would lead to a game that mimics everything from old games and does it worse, without really adding a fresh touch.

_childDocuments_.review: Allow me to cut to the chase this time. Things like graphics, music, collectibles, content etc are what you can expect when compared to other games in the genre. They’re done with care and they’re great. However, I believe that the game’s Steam page is misleading when it’s describing the gameplay and challenge. There is one mention of ‘but challenging platformer’. This is VERY underselling how challenging it is and whether it’s really a traditional platformer. It feels more like an auto-runner. You see, most levels (certainly after world 2) turn into either being A) chased by an enemy that one hit kills you B) same with a whirlwind C) moving camera that forces you to hurry up D) lava or toxic pool chasing you F) no solid ground so you have to jump on enemies to survive etc. Basically what it amounts to is you having to perfect a level, one mistake and it’s over. Levels have only one checkpoint which means you’re going to have to redo most of it regardless. The character also has to morph into one of the 4 different animals with their own moves depending on the level. One animal is a literal auto-runner, you can’t control its movement aside from jumping. Oh, and I hope you’re excited about the last boss having 4 phases with ‘platforming’ in between (aka chased by the enemy with one hit KO) and you can retry all the phases if you die, no checkpoints. It doesn’t make a difference if you do the last boss on casual except for taking one more hit I guess. I did the last 2 levels on casual and I’m not sure this is going to be enough for most people. Original difficulty feels too hardcore and I’m not sure if casual can be considered normal based on what I’ve seen. I don’t recommend Kaze even for lovers of platformers unless you’re looking for high challenge and an extreme form of trial and error. Make research about casual mode if you must. I can confirm that you can change the difficulty at any time (I wish I noticed this sooner). I won’t give Kaze 2 a try if it ever comes out. Seriously, what were they thinking.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an ambitious "Donkey Kong Country" clone that gets most of it right. Specifically, it feels the most like the second one. This game has a nice challenge, great art, and good music, though not something I would buy the soundtrack for. If you are looking for a well made, classic experience that is fairly challenging if you go for everything, I'd get this game.Kaze is a rabbit that is going on a journey to free her friend from a ring due to a mishap. The story is told through getting the equivalent of the "KONG" tokens, and as far as I can tell are optional. There are 4 worlds and you will go from stage to stage until you hit the boss. Much like Donkey Kong Country, there are hidden bonus levels you will need to beat if you want to complete the game. And much like Crash Bandicoot, there are also time trials you can complete as extra content, though I didn't do that.The masks are basically your animal buddies from Donkey Kong Country.If you ever wanted more Donkey Kong country this is more of it. I recommend those games if you like this one, even the gameboy ones are pretty ok.-     The sprites appear to be hand drawn with that "rough" look that makes the edges look pixelated, but not like those garbage games that make the art look, worse. Think "Jazz Jackrabbit 2" with a more detail. It looks good.-     If you are only trying to get to the final boss, the game offers a reasonable challenge on the non-easy difficulty. It's very refreshing, and encourages you to play it that way. You have no lives, so keep trying until you get it.-     Finally a modern game that lets me bind a different key for ground slam. Always make ground slam and dash on different buttons if you have room for them. Excellent use of controller space.    While the controls are not as tight as say, Dead Cells, I felt largely in control at all times, where any failures were mistakes I made. The platforming is also very forgiving. Just note, you will only be able to hover when descending, otherwise the animation won't trigger.-     I wanted more story and got it, and when I wanted to focus on getting 100%, I didn't need to worry about it getting in the way. Brevity is the soul of wit. -     There were a few times were it seemed like my character's speed and angle was set rather than carried over from a previous jump, but inconsistently. You will get over it, and learn when this changes during gameplay, but be careful when bouncing on enemies.-     I don't quite remember Donkey Kong Country bosses taking a literal age to finish, and then having to start over a 4 minute fight if I got hit. The final boss I can understand, but the second boss in the game is a huge slog, and it doesn't help that the flying mask controls were not designed for accuracy. Also the second boss has the Super Mario Bros. II wind physics. Once you get the gimmick of each boss you need to do it again, 2 more times, for every boss except the last one, which has new gimmicks each phase.    Thankfully the bosses are a very small part of the game. The weakest point of the game for sure.-     In order to get the best ending, you need to get 100 gems on every stage. In order to get 100 gems on every stage, you need to unlock the extra levels by completing all the bonus rooms in every stage. So at the bare minimum, you need the bonus rooms and gems. I don't think the KAZE coins are necessary, though I did get all of those.     Finding and doing the bonus rooms is fun, collecting 100 gems is not, except on the very short challenge stages that you unlock. I don't remember DCK requiring a banana total at the end. This seems more like the Crash Bandicoot box gem concept, except I did not enjoy collecting the gems in these stages. Thankfully the collection radius is quite generous, so it's only really frustrating in like 4/30 stages. You don't need to get every single gem as there are more than 100 in each stage, but you can only miss around 4.    If you didn't get all the bonus rooms and gems before you fight the final boss, you will need to beat the final boss again to see the better ending, which I did not enjoy having to do. That boss is long and requires a lot of memorization.    Needless to say my next playthrough will be a casual one.I had fun with this well put-together game. If a sequel is made, the bosses should take a lot, and I do mean A LOT less time to complete. Other than that, I am looking forward to another game from this developer if they want to make something else. If you like "classic" platformers, buy this game. You won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Kaze and the Wild Masks is a 2D platformer that goes straight to the point: the focus is not on the story, but rather on the gameplay, which is really well done and well complemented by the wonderful level design.The game takes heavy inspiration from the Donkey Kong Country franchise, so if you are a fan of that series, you should definitely check out Kaze and the Wild Masks. The gameplay feels quite similar, but Kaze still manages to be a great experience on its own right, although it is certainly a much shorter game.Kaze has a set of basic actions such as spinning to attack or using her long ears to extend her jumps, but there are also masks you can find in several levels that change up the gameplay, such as one that turns you into a bird that can fly freely, or one that turns you into a tiger, changing your normal spin attack into a lunging attack that clings to walls and lets you climb. The masks give the gameplay a good variety, and the level design itself is also great: the game is always throwing new concepts at you, making sure that things never grow stale. No level ever feels derivative or repetitive.The game also has a fairly nice soundtrack. The highlight is definitely the more ambient music that plays in certain levels and really helps complement the atmosphere. The art direction is also noteworthy; not only do the levels look great, but there is a huge variety of creative enemy designs based on vegetables, and the game keeps surprising you with them constantly up until the end. The animations are also very well done, really bringing to life all those great designs.All in all, Kaze and the Wild Masks is a great action 2D platformer that takes many cues from Donkey Kong Country and does a fantastic job at offering an experience that feels familiar while still staying fresh and doing its own thing. It may be a bit short, but it's still definitely worth checking out if you're a fan of platformers, especially DKC.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun platformer game with lots of potential, however it doesn't feel that long of a game.The game plays very well, feeling like the old Donkey Kong Country games, and even has mechanics close to the game, examples being attacking off a ledge and able to jump mid-air from it, even picking up the urns to throw at enemies.Gameplay is fairly simple to play, and good to master, you have your movement and jumps, you have a "Crash Bandicoot" spin attack, and your rabbit ears are useful for picking and throwing urns and hanging off ropes to cross areas also. Eventually you'll even earn powerups that'll give you some ability, changing how you play, from flight, swimming, wall climbing, and then for some reason, auto run. The game would also be fairy challenging, getting hit once will KO you and you respawn back at the previous checkpoint you found, there is however hearts around the map, grabbing one will give you a one hit shield of sorts, unless you get KO-ed to a one-hit KO situation. There is also a difficulty setting if the game is too tricky and can be changed on the fly mid-game. There are also collectables to find in game, yellow letters that spell out KAZE to earn some backstory, green gem pieces hidden away in challenge rooms, which can unlock a locked stage in each world hub, and lastly the red crystals, grabbing 100 each stage earns a gem which "may" have a effect on something, if you clear a stage without getting hit you'll earn a special medal for that stage, and lastly after clearing a stage for the first, if you play it again, there'll be a clock for a time trial, beat the time set for a medal for that. Again while the game is fairly challenging, its not that long of a game, there is 4 world hubs with their own end-boss and a locked gimmick stage, but even after that, it didn't take me long to beat the game casually and get all the collectables, minus not getting hit each stage and time trials, the speedrun achievement also points that out also since it can be beaten in less than 2 hours, so while its fun to play, the fun only lasts for so long, by the time you get the feeling for another stage, its near the time where your almost finished with the game.Would i recommend this game, yes, it shares alot of gameplay from Donkey Kong Country and has potential to be a great contender for platformers, but the lack of stages, or rather the length of the stages, means it can be completed quickly, but because of how fun it was, i wouldn't mind a sequel on it and hope for some future improvements should they decide to. If you are unsure about getting the game, wait for maybe a sale of 10-20%, since i had a blast playing it, and it deserves the love it can get.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly this is one of those games which baffles me with its steam score. Kaze belongs to 1980s with its terrible level design. It brought back to me those dark memories of playing and trying to beat the first stage of Back to the Future 3 on Sega Mega Drive (Genesis). After the first world you basically have to remember each enemy' attack pattern, then memorize where to jump and on what time you do that. If you fail, you go back to the beginning or to the only checkpoint if you were able to manage that (this is somewhere around the middle of every stage). It is highly stressful and not fun to beat a stage because in the end it feels more like passing a memory test rather than a skill based achievement.On the plus side they nailed the graphics and it plays really good on Steam Deck.

_childDocuments_.review: I beat this game in 7.5 hours on Normal mode.A very fun game reminiscent of Donkey Kong Country. You play a rabbit that inadvertently unleashes an evil doer and your bro gets their spirit trapped inside a jeweled ring. So it's now up to you to save Carrotland.There aren't many mechanics if any. Cept for maybe weighted platforms, which I didn't really care for. Oh, and the on and off light switches.My favorite moment was the level with air currents that blew you up and you can control your height with your hover.All the art is very nice to look at. The animations on Kaze and everything else is great, and gives plenty of silliness.While you go through 4 different lands that have a theme, they don't really. Once you enter the stages, they will vary. So if you enter the snow land, you won't encounter all snow or ice themed levels. You actually encounter lava filled landscapes, and dark ruins filled with brambles. I found it a little odd to be honest. They had the assets to create perhaps 2-3 more lands to actually make every land be it's own theme. I have a feeling they had to cut a lot of bosses, and thus we have this sort of mashup. I also hazard a guess that they also ran out of time or budget. I do miss a map screen to select your levels. Instead, you walk on a flat straight path to select the level with cute dioramas.The music can feel a bit...I don't know, generic? It has it's charm and it is not bad music but I wasn't jamming out to any particular track. The music is fine. I suppose I was spoiled by the legend, David Wise.A simple platformer but still great and plenty of challenge. Definitely pick this one up. I'm sure if the dev team had a bigger budget and more time, they would give you the full adventure with more lands, levels, mechanics, and bosses. Right now, it's a quick polished adventure.I recommend this game because there was a lot of love put into it. The quality of the controls, levels, and style is top notch. I feel calling it a clone is in poor taste because it stands to be the best DKC "clone". Who doesn't want more different flavors of DKC platforming in their life?
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best Indie Platformers I have ever played alongside Celeste, Shovel Knight, and A Hat in Time. Above all else, this is a love letter to classic Donkey Kong Country while also taking some inspiration from the new DKC games as well a dash of Rayman and Mega Man for it's heart mechanic and some level gimmicks respectively. While I don't have too much experience with the original DKC Trilogy, I still adored this game. The level themes were unique and interesting, the music was very solid, the controls were responsive, and Kaze's abilities are super fun to use. However, there isn't much content here. I've already gotten all the collectibles and achievements and I've only played for about 10 hours. I'd still highly recommend the purchase even for the full $20, especially for those hardcore DKC fans, but the shorter length may be a turn off for some.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: A must play game for any fans of the DKC series. It's pretty much every Donkey Kong Country game mashed together, with a little dash of Rayman Legends. Although it is an indie game after all, so don't expect the same level of quality or quantity of the games it was inspired by.  As of writing this review, I 100%'d the game, then played it again for a speedrun achievement. - The controls are super tight and responsive, probably the only time in my life I have ever   wished for more water levels because the controls are that good. - Level design is super fun. Mechanics and level gimmicks are well utilized and the difficulty   curve is perfect. The game never gets so frustrating that you want to rage quit, but there are   some parts that gave me a hard time.- Graphics are pleasing with a cute indie pixel aesthetic and great animations to match. - The music doesn't particularly stand out, but it's does a serviceable job. Kaze and the Wild Masks is a wonderful little platformer that more than satisfies my cravings for another DKC style game. I happily recommend this game to any fans of 2d platformers.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is visually very pretty and also has very good retro music. The problem and the reason why I can't recommend it is because of the gameplay: Levels are very straight forward, there is just no 2 ways of doing them, so it feels like a rythm game or a quick time event most of the time. That alone isn't necesairly bad but feels kind of cheap compared to other games that at least lets you see the threats on the screen before its too late to avoid them, so in the end it's trial and error and a memory game. Wouldn't be so critic yet just with that, but the game makes you believe you have these awesome power ups as mask: They are not power ups, they are sections of the game forcing you to change playstyles (imo this didn't need the fanfare the masks bring, since when they appear the level is specifically designed for you to use the new moveset, so you don't feel powered up at all). At least the boss fights are fun, but they are incredible easy compared to the real difficulty of the game which is learning the button sequence to beat each level.I made it all up until half of world 4, but absolutlely hate the dragon mask, since It just changes the way you naturally learn to play: You used muscle memory (something the game wants you to develop) to remember how to stay longer in the air spinning your ears? well too bad, now that same button will plunge yourself into the ground! :)

_childDocuments_.review: Gliding in air requires you to hold attack, instead of jump. You have to hold the attack button to hold onto a rock and release attack to throw, instead of just pick it up with attack and then press attack again to throw. Ground pound is down and attack and for some reason feels wrong to me. These feel terrible and there are no options to change them. It seems there was some sort of push to use only two buttons, even though they are copying a game that had 6 buttons main buttons available to it. Other than that, moving around feels good.Some of the levels are terrible. The game has an overworld where you pick what level to play, but it's linear. This means you have to play and beat the bad levels to continue. The game could benefit from a branching overworld where the more controversial levels could be optional paths.The art is great. However, the game feels a bit too much like a copy-paste of Donkey Kong Country, without anything new. The main character is replaced with a Sonic character and the enemies are replaced with fairly forgettable vegetables. It otherwise has extremely similar levels, game mechanics, enemy types/ai, etc. You spin instead of roll, you collect gems instead of bananas, you collect KAZE letters instead of KONG letters, you wear masks instead of ride on top of animals, you shoot around on sling shots instead of barrels, you throw rocks instead of barrels, you ground pound with your butt from the air instead of slapping the ground with your hands, etc. This would be fine if there was something unique about the game or if they just improved every aspect of the game, but the levels aren't better, the music is worse, and the story seems to have been thrown in as an after-thought. The art is really the only thing going for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly competent implementation of an uninspired game design.It might be exactly what it's supposed to be and that just happens to not be my cup of tea...After all, the game design seems mostly inspired by the Donkey Kong SNES games, which I find completely joyless. I'd rank this game well above DK, but still not really my thing.More specifically, I don't enjoy the movement mechanics and overall level design. It feels like it's a dozen or so tweaks away from actually feeling good to control.The levels have recurring readibility issues, like low contrast brambles and slippery walls that you can easily miss until it's too late.The whole game feels slow, to a sometimes frustrating degree, but sometimes you hardly have any time to react, such as when you get blindsided by offscreen projectiles whilst in a low-agility mode (swimming, flying). Other than that, I'd probably have chosen to play most of the game at about 125% speed.The main praise I have is for the polished presentation and flawless implementation.Overall, even though it's not bad or anything, I don't really recommend playing this game unless you're positive it's for you.If you don't really enjoy it at the start, you probably won't enjoy the rest either. It doesn't really pull an "it gets good" on you or anything later on.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't recommend  at all. At its best it's mediocre and inoffensive. It looks like she's trying to do a slow motion forwards moonwalk.While we're on the subject of "stiff", let's talk about Kaze's movement; it just feels overly clunky and... off... and considering that the game often requires precision platforming and pulling off specific moves and/or manoeuvres at a fairly brisk pace, there's a lack of both momentum and the feeling that I was fully in control. It just feels awkward and unpleasant to play.Speaking of unpleasant to play: the masks! None of the four masks that crop up at predetermined sections of the game are much fun to use. The worst one is the dragon(?) mask, which turns the game into a bad auto-runner.The levels are generally pretty decent looking from a technical standpoint, but they're kind of bland and boring. Lastly, due to the aforementioned stiffness and awkwardness of the movement and controls, the final boss is a seven-stage slog of everything I don't like about this game, all rolled into one level, culminating in .There isn't a shortage of great - or even just  - 2D platformers. _childDocuments_.review: // H // O // T // : // R // U // N //// R // E // V // I // E // W // S //Guest Review by GameGerryIt's 1994, you're 12 years old, you awaken, your sheets soaked with sweat, it's 4 AM. You're in your room, but it's not your room - is it? To find some semblance of comfort, you look for your poster for Super Mario 3, only to see a poster for a game called Extraordinary Merino now on the Nitro Enjoyment System. WHAT IS THAT? Oh well, who cares, Donkey Kong Country is coming out soon, you think. You go downstairs to find the VHS tape you got in the mail that was a Donkey Kong Country promo - it's gone. WHERE IS IT? You call your friend Bart, he answers the phone - "BART!" you say - he says "WHO? my name is BRANT!" Okay whatever. You ask Brant if he's still excited for Donkey Kong Country coming out. He says "What in the HELL is that???" You start describing it to him, the barrels, the bonus stages, the banana power ups. Brant quickly interrupts you - "Oh sounds like you are describing KAZE, we watched the promo for that last week when it was delivered to your house on Beta Max tape." WHAT IN THE HELL? You quickly hang up the phone and go to the entertainment center, digging though what you now realize are Beta tapes. You find a brightly colored one with the text "KAZE" emblazoned on the side - you insert the tape. Lo and behold there it is some BS knock-off of Donkey Kong Country with vegetables and some rabbit??, and for some reason the people in the video are really hyped for it. What system does it say it's for???? Sega? SEGA GENESIS? You look under the TV, and there it is - the only system you own, a Sega Genesis. How can this be???? You look for any sign of your NES or SNES - they aren't there, just some brick called Nitro Enjoyment System. What is that? You remember the poster, NO! It can't be. You run to the front door and open it, there is a newspaper on the ground. You look at the headline on the first page "NITRO ENJOYMENT OUT OF BUSINESS" - You scan the article - Nitro Enjoyment never recovered from the Extraodinary Merino flop they released 6 years ago and following the release of their Laserdisc attachment, they folded. Sega has reined supreme, Nintendo doesn't appear to exist. You run back into your room and slam the door, in bed you are upset, but then realize - at least you can still play Sonic! Then you look on the back of your door - a large poster looms with the title SANIC is back in SANIC THE BULLDOG 3 now with music from Vanilla Ice. You close your eyes, hoping to wake from this nightmare, but you never do - this is hell. TL:DR - Kaze Kong Country - do not recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Although not quite innovative per se, it does manage to excel at doing things.To start things off, the game just "feels" great from the get go. The controls feel great (What do you know? The devs already fixed Air Smash input just one day after my review!), the visuals are great, and the audio is great.I love how the levels were designed, it feels like every level has its own "gimmick" and with the Wild Masks, they never feel boring. I also love the devs' decision to remove Lives.The bosses are not that special, they are very "meh", but the final boss is really something, feels like a "final exam" where you need to master most of the games' fundamentals to beat. Although, it does feel like it depends on memorizing the pattern and does contradict the devs' philosophy behind removing Lives (to respect the player's time by not letting them repeat the same things over and over again).Main story is about 3-5 hours long, but it has decent replay-ability value that spans it more through Time Trials, Collectibles and Bonus level. Challenging game, in a good way - there is no "annoyingly" hidden Collectibles and more often than not, failure seems to be in the player's control and never feels frustrating but encourages you to learn and try something else, very addictive!Oh yeah, pretty cool narrative behind the story-telling too. Basically the story is told in pictures that you unlock when collecting a level's K-A-Z-E letters. Love the mystery feeling behind it and how it is open to interpretation.People who come in expecting a "Donkey Kong Country"-ish game will not be disappointed, however, there's much to Kaze and the Wild Masks than that and it certainly does have its unique identity. Definitely worth your time and money - there is no going wrong with this one.
