_childDocuments_.review: This game is a great well-rounded platformer that has tight controls for precision moves and unique mechanics to keep the experience interesting the whole way through.  There were some frustrating parts that made me put the controller down for a break, but I was always able to come back and overcome the challenges with persistence.  The level design gets tough, but not soul crushing kaizo hard, and the option to switch out to a more casual mode is a welcome one.  The story, art, and music all show a steady high standard of quality, it all left me very satisfied.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Dunno about this one. It strikes me as somewhat overrated. It's certainly fun in parts, but even the "casual mode" becomes annoyingly, grindingly hard after the initial world. (There are only four short worlds, though.) Graphics and music are okay (not amazing); there's no real storyline. And every enemy and mechanic in the game is borrowed (plagiarised) from Donkey Kong Country: it's truly shameless. So even if you like DKC you might find this rather too unoriginal to be interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun game! It has quickly become one of favorite platformers! :) The controls are really tight, every gamestyle really fun, the music's nice as well as the beautiful artstyle! There are several things you can collect, all of them really fun without ever being too frustrating.I also love the difficulty of the game. It's very challenging but never frustrating (well... two or three levels might be, but that's the smallest problem), absolute every level is fun in fact, and especially with the well-made controls (and I'm playing with the keyboard!)I'd absolutely love to see more from Kaze! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an extremely competent spiritual successor to Donkey Kong Country. The game starts out rather slow and simple, but gets really engaging a little ways in.I'm disappointed that the "Wild Masks" aren't incorporated more strongly. To continue the Donkey Kong Country reference, they're more like the dedicated animal buddy stages than the persistant upgrades I was hoping they would be.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on a whim, thinking for the longest time it was a Klonoa spiritual successor. Surprise to me: It's a Donkey Kong Country type game! It's clear there is a lot of wonderful art, animation, and effort in this game. I love it! The only issue is the game can rely a bit too much on trial and error, and the secret areas can be a bit too hidden at times. Do not feel ashamed if you are a seasoned platformer veteran and need to use casual mode!Bravo to the creators of this game! It is lovely!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Well worth getting on sale. A bit too short for a full cost purchase.Game has great music, lots of style- even though it's clearly DKC inspired (which is a good thing). Some levels can be a bit difficult but that comes with old school style platformers. Most importantly, the levels are fun to play through and the controls are tight enough for those levels.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: If you're tired of waiting for Ubisoft to make another Rayman game, Kaze is the answer to your prayers. While distinct enough to be its own property, it takes clear influence from the aforementioned neglected franchise as well as Crash Bandicoot and Donkey Kong Country. Kaze is a beautiful fusion of those series that's approachable to casual players while not being so easy as to bore a more experienced 2D platformer veteran. Completing all of the Time Trials, beating every level Hitless, and getting the achievement for beating the game in under 2 hours were all fair and satisfying challenges. It's also not too long, as a casual playthrough will only take 5 or 6 hours, and getting every achievement shouldn't take much longer than 10 - 15 hours.It's a good game. You should play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good challenging platformer with nostalgic elements resembling Donkey Kong and the 2D Sonic The Hedgehog games. I appreciated the sense of completion I got from collecting all the types of gems. It has the retro level of difficulty found in the SNES Donkey Kong games, which can be a positive or a negative depending on how you feel about it. The boss battles are three hit mechanics with three stages of challenging sequences, so I spent considerable time on them, but the repetition was not boring by any means. I also enjoyed the music and how well it fits the movement of the level. A speed run "mode" is built in for those who like that, but I've not tried it myself. I really appreciated the vibrant color choices and the hand drawn art and animation styles.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best 2D platformer available, it brings the good old 16bit feelings. A lot of negative reviews are complaining about the difficulty, but there's nothing wrong with it, the difficulty is on point, a good challenge if you want no-hit + time trials medals. It's a good game to have 100% of achievements.The only annoyance in this game is the huge amount of auto-scroller/auto-runner.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This game is bursting with charm and quality. It plays just like the classic Dkc games and i mean that in the best way possible. The sprite art is detailed and very expressive, and there are some nice tunes. I would say that 25 dollars is a little steep but I think if you are a big fan of challenging 2d platformers this is a must try.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: A game inspired by the Donkey Kong Country saga. It is really good and short. It will take a few hours if you want to 100% the game, but not a lot. Some levels are hard, but in general, the difficulty is not very high. The art and music are not to my taste. Overall, it's a great game, and I did not find any technical problems.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: It's not bad, like everyone said its a lot like Donkey Kong Country. The platforming and jumping is tight, although sometimes you'll go through platforms so the collision detection and hitboxes could be a bit better. Also the game really could use a double jump, and not being able to jump after landing on an enemy is kind of dumb as well. Its pretty fun, and some of the masks are cool, but later levels become stupid runner sections (laziest game design ever) and ziplines, rising lava, tornado chases, etc. Instead of good platforming its just following preset button pressing and its tons of stupid trial and error sections, especially with way too many instant death pits. There only being 1 checkpoint all levels could be better as although the levels aren't long some of the checkpoints and end of levels are far apart, forcing you to replay a decent amount. Only getting 2 hits total could have been better, should have been 3, although they do have casual thankfully so if you have to switch you can. The final boss is terribly designed, breaking the 3 attack rule and having no checkpoints but 5 different multi-part stages, forcing a ton of trial and error and repetition. The game is also pretty short, but it does have a great art and visual design. Collectibles are basically useless and theres almost no story at all. 7.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun DKC-alike! Quite short and sweet but has the extra collectables and stuff if you want more of a challenge! It's nice that it includes an easier mode for people who don't want to experience torture (like me!)Very nice sprite art and decent music. Quite an easy recommend if you're a fan of platformers!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Not even with rabbit ears you can shut your eyes hard enough to not see the homage this is to the Donkey Kong Country Series. You have a Stop&Go Station, Vulture Culture, Trick Track Trek, Target Terror, Toxic Tower and many many more. Add to this the perfection that is the music and level design and this is indeed modern DKC which lots of people like me loved back in the day. The worlds and levels look pixel sharp, almost all the music (especially boss music) is a instant banger and the namesake wild masks you play as all alter the gameplay significantly, causing each level to be something special. The game also impressively shows what happens to the greens your kids don't eat. Show them the enemy designs of this game if they won't eat their veggies ;-)It's not handholdy though, so you should be prepared to get your ass kicked by some levels. Especially if you want 100% and beat each level no-hit. The game does have some minor minor flaws, so this is some bickering on a very high level:All in all, if you look for a beautiful (for eyes and ears), fun and challenging 2D platformer, look no further.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Fair to say this is an homage to the Donkey Kong Country series that stands on its own. It's a platformer where you complete 8 stages per area while collecting crystals (>= 100), completing 2 challenge rooms or spell out the word KAZE by collecting its letters. There are transformative power ups that give you flight, swimming and wall climbing / dashing abilities that are used on a few stages. Heck, remember Bramble Blast and the barrel sections? Hehehe.... they're here too!I haven't encountered any mine cart sections yet... yet! They're probably here somewhere.It's been a good time so far. The bright visuals, mellow audio tracks and snappy controls make this an easy recommendation for people looking for something similar to DKC. Even if you're new to the DKC style games this one hasn't been demanding on my platforming skills so far so don't worry about it being overly difficult. Maybe it picks up later? I'll update the review once I'm done.Update - Completed the game in 6.4 hours including all collectibles and bonus stages. There were "mine cart" levels in the game! Looking forward to Pixel Hive's future work!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: I kind of wish there was more of this game. Played for just over 50 hours and i've gotten all but the speedrun trophy. By that i mean, i had a lot of fun playing it and wanted to do everything there was to do it the game. It's just a charming, if a little basic 2D platformer that really wants to give you the classic 16 bit experience. One criticism i'm willing to give is the hit boxes on the barrels are horrible. Expect to die a lot from phasing through the edges of barrels. All in all, fun game.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: If I could leave a "sideways" thumb here I would.One one hand, the overall game play, graphics and level design are enjoyable.On the other hand, most of this is ruined by an overabundant use of "run quickly from left to right through the entire level" mechanics. It got old quick back in the day and it's even more stupid now. One or two levels spread out over the entire game would be acceptable but the use of this game play becomes more frequent as you progress and one of the special "masks" you acquire also uses this mechanic.To the developers: Use this mechnic sparingly, if at all the next game. Let your players take their time and enjoy exploring your beautifully crafted levels.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun platformer game which nailed a lot, if not all aspects of a great platformer game. Lots of versatility with the masks which keeps the gaming experience fresh.It´s a pretty quick game to beat, even if you collect all the optional stuff. The difficulty is adjusted really nice (I played the harder recommended difficulty) and advancing to the next save point feels rewarding. Some of the hidden secrets we´re a bit annoying to find (I can imagine some people enjoy the finding experience) but most of the time they were positioned really well.Small spoiler: Also I would have enjoyed a hidden true final boss after collecting all the stuff, but that didn´t happen. :/Still, If you like platformers, you just can´t go wrong with this gem!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a solid platformer but it isn't particularly exceptional. I like the art style and art work but personally I'm not huge on any of the actual designs of the characters or enemies. There's nothing wrong with them it just isn't anything that really appeals to me. The music is nice but not overly memorable. There are four worlds with 6 main stages, a bonus stage and a boss level. To just play through any of these isn't very difficult, but trying to complete them will pose a minor challenge. I think it would be hard to recommend this game at $15 given how little content there really is but on sale for $5 or less it is worth your time if you are interested in platformers at all. I definitely had enough fun with this game that I'm not upset that I played it but there are also a lot of other things you could play that would be better overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Kaze is a beautiful love letter to Donkey Kong Country and well worth the price tag to platformer enthusiasts.  The music does an excellent job even when comparing it to the soundtracks from the DKC series.  The art is cute, fun, and well done.  It brings all the elements you’d expect with time attack mode, hidden bonus stages, 3 types of collection challenges per level, a challenge per level to take no damage, and challenging boss fights.  Many levels are challenging and give you a fulfilling sense of accomplishment when you overcomes them.  I look forward to going for 100%.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Nice platformer in really beautiful 16bit pixel art. The challenge is correct, the musics are groovy, and I really like the sounds, especially the very funny voices of the evil vegetables!A little too bad the mask transformations are just possible in some levels, levels that are especially designed for these forms, and of course the transformations can't be avoided. So, if you're looking for a Kid Chameleon vibe, it's not here.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: it follows Donkey Kong formula a lot, yet for some reason it s not as fun as Donkey Kong. Difficulty is not arranged properly some stages although late in game a breeze and some unnecessarily "challenging". I have no issues with challenge you can look at my profile and see but this game does not offer a good challenge IMHO.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: All in all, I definitely would recommend this to anyone looking for a cute, challenging platformer.  Sometimes I found some parts tediously difficult to repeat in their entirety, but the level design is great!  This game was so worth it on discount.  It's great to play on Steam Deck too!  Good short fun that doesn't overstay its welcome!  And you can always try to 100% it if you're looking for an even bigger challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very good platformer that really wants to be Donkey Kong Country. For the most part it does a really good job. It stumbles with a few things though. It would have been a solid B tier platformer if it came out back in the day.It's very tough, which is a good thing and it requires a lot of skill. Finding collectables takes the gameplay to the next level.Where it stumbles is there is a fair amount of trial and error and having to memorize levels. This isn't just for the collectables either. Sometimes just getting through a level feels more about knowing what to do and when than actually doing something difficult. The check points are also sometimes weirdly placed. You might spend a long time never seeing one, or you might stumble across one almost immediately. There seems to be no rhyme or reason to their placement sometimes.Still my gripes are minor. They're just things Donkey Kong Country did to a much lesser extent. Those games focused more on skill. But that's not to say this game doesn't require skill; it definitely does.Still trial and error gameplay was a big part of the genre back then, particularly B tier platformers and below, so I guess they nailed it if that's what they were going for. But I know some people might be disappointed. Still a good game though.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best 2D platformers I've played as a seasoned platformer player. The diificulty is just right (played on original difficulty), the level design is stellar and the controls, even if simple, feel really on point.This might be one of the few games where I've not only done but looked forward to doing the two things that I most hate in videogames in EVERY STAGE: time attacks and no-hits. I hope this is enough proof of how good it feels to play Kaze.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very much underrated 2D plat former game. Controls are tight and button input reaction are all immediate and precise. Throughout the game, you will able from time to time put on different mask that changes your entire game play.There are a total of four different masks namely the eagle mask, shark mask, tiger mask and the dragon mask. Each offering a different skill set to master when you don on the mask. A fun and challenging game out there. Definitely deserve much much more love from players out there that enjoys a decent platformer game. My only complaint is the last boss, which is freaking tough as hell. There are a lot of instant death with this boss and it is divided into four parts. One wrong move and you will report to heaven. If you think some of cuphead bosses are are tough, wait till you fight the last boss of this game. Nevertheless this game is still highly recommended...!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: I loved it until I got the dragon mask. Now I hate it. started off strong too. well others will feel differently and that's fine. I recommend because if your'e skills are sharper than mine then you will enjoy the fast,unfair and BS dragon auto scroll nonsense. it's a shame too because the game is gorgeous and looks amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: The developers clearly played a lot of the 16-bit era Donkey Kong Country games and it shows given how much this game was inspired by them, right down to nailing the feel of the tight precision controls and really good level design that compliment the controls. No two levels feel the same even if some of them do borrow elements from other levels. All that and more makes for some of the best side-scrolling platforming I've experienced in a very long time.Each level has four KAZE letters to grab and two bonus stages for those seeking to fully complete the game, the former unlocking bonus artwork and the latter unlocks extra bonus levels to play. Getting at least 100 small pink crystals in a level also grants a big pink crystal for that level and while not needed to finish the game, getting them all unlocks the true ending. Time trials are also present when replaying levels a second time with bronze, silver and gold times to beat similar to Crash 3.While the game can be quite difficult at times, limited lives are not a thing in this game so you will eventually beat it if you keep trying. If it still becomes too much for you, an optional Casual Mode adds extra checkpoints and allows one extra hit point to make things a little easier. Unlike other games that include a similar feature, the game never asks if you want to turn it on if you're having trouble nor does it completely break the entire game design when enabled.If you don't have a Switch but still want a game that plays and feels like Donkey Kong Country, or you're already a big fan of those games and are looking for other games like it, I'd strongly suggest giving this one a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous art, great sound design, fun levels... What's not to love?Personally, I found the difficulty just perfect (played on the original mode). The game offered some challenge, but it never made me feel frustrated. With some practice, all levels and achievements are doable. I guess "hardcore platformer gamers" might find the game too easy, but for a casual gamer like myself, it is well-balanced. Big thumbs-up!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: A 2d sidescrolling platformer of the same lineage as Donkey Kong Country that has just as much ingenuity and challenge. Kaze and the Wild Masks delivers a variety of levels and mechanics that do not overstay their welcome. In particular, I loved the auto-run levels that forced you to jump, double jump, and dive bomb through some truly hair-raising obstacles. I highly recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy platformers like Sonic and Mario, then you'll enjoy Kaze and the Wild Masks. Some levels are definitely more challenging than others if you consider finding all of the KAZE letters, secret portals, and Gems; I completed each of these tasks for every level. Overall, I wouldn't consider this game a difficult platformer given the target audience, but it is still fun to play. I got this game for my daughter and myself.I'd recommend this game to any platformer fan.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: There aren't many games i would deem perfect but Kaze and the Wild Masks is one of them.It is heavily inspired from Donkey Kong and has the same level of polish you would expect from a Nintendo game. While it doesn't hide its inspiration, it manages to be distinct by adding tons of unique mechanics.Every level is memorable and has its own theme going on. Collectibles, rushing through levels that flow like butter, unique boss fights and so on. From its artstyle to its gameplay, it is filled to the brim with charm and you can clearly see how much love and passion was put into making this game.Its criminal how little its known. Everyone should play this game.I will keep an eye on this developer for their future games. I strongly recommend you to play Kaze, you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Has a staggering amount in common with Donkey Kong Country, This works both in favor and against it. There are some cool ideas and mechanics explored with powers, the controls are tight and responsive and levels can be fun to playthrough. In a lot of ways it even improves on DK with instantly repeatable challenge stages. Something about it though doesn't feel the same to me and I found myself becoming uninterested in the levels and wondering how many I have left. It just lacks the cool environment changes, soundtrack quality and art design that made DK so good. Still, a solid experience if you want a platformer and it could just be me.6/10
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, engaging platformer that takes a clear inspiration from Donkey Kong Country while adding its own twists. Kaze is very fun to control, with a rather familiar helicopter twirling move and a downwards bounce that feels very satisfying to use, along with a forward attack that keeps your momentum which feels incredible to use. The masks also add fun new abilities - think of them like the Animal Barrels from DKC2/3 where you get transformed entirely for the rest of the level. This style works great for the game, it allows the levels to be hand-crafted around the mask's abilities and leads to much more interesting level designs than we would have otherwise.Not quite as unforgiving as some of the more sadistic challenges that the DKC series has to offer, but it's plenty difficult in its own right and should provide a decent but fair challenge for most players. I died plenty of times but generally checkpoints are well-placed and most challenges are able to be conquered after you realize your mistake. The game generally flows extremely well, which is something that matters a lot for a game that takes its influence from one of the greatest game series ever in terms of flow. Overall I'd definitely recommend this game, it's really fun and definitely scratches the DKC itch
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Now that i've completed it, it's time to review it. First off this game is a fast platformer, rarely does it make you wait too long. It's levels just like it's worlds, are short and sweet. Getting 100 gems, the two challenge pieces, not getting hit and the timer are all fun objectives.The only complaints that i have about this game are very small. The unlockable 7/7 levels shouldn't have a timer, they're more focused on being a test of skills, so not getting hit is enough. The timer achievment is weak and the speedrunner achievment is too hard, unless you know it beforehand. Lastly the last boss had good platforming, but the transformations segments were a little too easy(tiger was good tho).Now for the praises, the level variety is good, you don't tire yourself of playing this game. The masks are fun power ups, they change the pace of a level and none felt uneeded. The difficulty is just right, getting gold medals on all levels is very attainable, most levels i had at least 10 secs before gold expired. The dash jump out of platforms and dash comboing off enemies was excellent. The dash is very fluid and stops when you expect it to, the air movement is top notch as well. Backgrounds were pretty and fit the levels. The music was nice and i didn't get tired of it. The minimal story did more than enough. Overall if you like platformers, you'll love this game. It can be short, if you don't try to do everything it has to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Kaze and the Wild Masks is a really good old school styled platformer that not only captures the feel and look of old platformers, it also improves on it. Now what is the story. Two young adventurers Kaze and her friend/brother Hugo go to an old temple in search of a powerful relic, but the moment they find it tragedy happens. Hugo’s body and soul is sealed in the relic and an ancient evil that was trapped in it escapes, now it's up to Kaze to not only save her brother, but also stop the evil Typhoon from conquering the land with his vegetable army.So then the likes, the gameplay is really good it's hard but fair with the game starting off easy, but as you progress it introduces new challenges that makes it hard, the game also varies up the platforming not just with difficulty, but there are also these masks that give you certain powers like the ability to fly or the ability to cling to walls which help diversify the platforming.The pixel graphics are really good not only is it nice to look at and has a great use of color; it also has this nice cartoony feel that makes it feel like this would get a cartoon spin-off if this game was in the 90’s. The levels are really good each one quite diverse with plenty of interesting scenery that not only makes you want to stop and stare, but even explore. The enemy and bosses are really good each one with their own unique design, I also really love the fact that all the enemies are vegetable/ fruit /plant-based as they each one had some unique looks and animation.The story is good while it is your simple stop the bad guy story there's plenty of these little letters that if you get them all it unlocks a story that tells how all this came to be, I found it quite interesting as it had a Kung Fu Panda sort of vibe to it, especially with the main villain Typhoon. The characters are quite adorable looking, even those we don't really know much about them as this is a simple platformer, but there is still a little bit in the story that we get hints of their personality.The music is really good with plenty of great tracks to listen to that just really compliments the game. There is also plenty of challenges you can do which were are quite good, even if they are a little frustrating, it's hard but still fair. Also I like how all the achievements are quite easy to get it just takes time and practice even the hardest achievement the speedrunner can be completed if you played the game enough times.So then the dislikes, the game can be a little short if you're not going after any of the achievements and the price is a bit to high I mean practically $20, again if you're not going to go after all the achievements like I did the game and the price does seem a bit too much. I also would have liked that the game would have a few more bosses to fight instead of the four we have.Now then with all that done Kaze and the Wild Masks is a really good old school styled platformer that not only captures the feel and look of old platformers, it also improves on it, it has really good gameplay, really good graphics and a good story. So I highly recommend this game if you're a fan of old school Platformers this is definitely for you, I only recommend that you wait till it's on sale so you can save a couple of bucks.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun and enjoyable 2D side-scroller/platform game that fans of old school games like Sonic the Hedgehog would enjoy. You adventure through a variety of levels that include all kinds of different enemies and obstacles which Kaze navigates by using her two basic abilities - hovering (using her ears) and a spin-attack to defeat foes (many vegetable-type foes, like carrots!) You also get to use Wild Masks at points throughout the game (an eagle, tiger, shark, and some kind of dragon or lizard) all of which give you added and different abilities. The game world consists of 4 'worlds' (Forgotten Grove, Frozen Mountains, Toxic Tide, and Carrotland) each containing between 6-7 levels that are varied, colourful, and accompanied by a decent soundtrack. Within each level, there are a number of collectables for you to get which opens up 'bonus' stages throughout the game. There are two play modes - Casual and Regular. Casual gives you checkpoints and the option to pass a certain section if you are really struggling with it, but even this mode can be quite challenging. (You'll likely die plenty of times!) It has a good replay factor too, as you'll probably want to go back and get all of the items you missed first time around to try and 100% the game. There are also Time Trials available to test your speediness. This is a great game, if on the short side in terms of length, but I would definitely recommend it to anyone who loves a 2D platformer. It's fun to play, challenging but not frustrating, and is visually enjoyable. I give it a solid 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Everyone knows that this game takes a lot from the Donkey Kong Country series (it seems particularly from 3), and it plays a lot like the SNES trilogy.I like this game.  However, I feel like it's overshadowed by the games it borrows from so heavily.  This has the visual language of DKC.  It even has a few level ideas ripped straight from those games such as the Stop and Go Station-like level.  But it doesn't have the soul of DKC.  That's not to say this game has no soul, because it does, but it's not the same one that made me fall in love with those games a few years ago.The soundtrack is just not as good as that in any of the DKC games.  Those tracks, even from Evelyn Fischer, just have a certain atmosphere to them that give the musical identity of the series.  They can be catchy, melancholic, serene, atmospheric, even isolating.  For the miss of a track that Stilt Village SNES was, you have several other great tracks from DKC3 such as Northern Kremisphere, Treetop Tumble, Water World, Nuts and Bolts, and Rockface Rumble.  That's not even mentioning DKC1 and 2, both of which have stellar soundtracks.  Kaze's soundtrack just... it doesn't compare.  I don't remember or want to look up any of the tracks from this game.  It's not bad, it's just that there's nothing really special here.The minecart level standins are pretty bad.  I already didn't think well of them in the original trilogy, and the only reason I really like them in the Returns duology is because of the spectacle of the stages (Sawmill Thrill is one of my favorite stages from Tropical Freeze, but not for its gameplay).  I'm just not a big fan of auto levels to begin with, as I think they lead to unnecessary trial and error.  However, i can tolerate the minecart and toboggan levels from the original trilogy, as the mechanics are simple enough to make the margin of error relatively low.  It was just a jump, and that's all they needed.  On the other hand, Kaze decides to over-complicate the minecart by turning into a transformation.  You're now given a double jump and a downward dash, both of which allow the level design to become over-complicated for no good reason.  I just don't enjoy these levels where, if I miss one double jump or do a downward lunge just slightly too late, I just careen  into the bottomless pit and have to try again.  Most of the other levels in the game don't feel like this.The controls are pretty hit or miss.  Kaze controls pretty well, but the fact that the air twirl button is the same one as dropping from a rope without any option to change it is pretty bad.  The shark transformation plays pretty much like Dixie and DK underwater in Tropical Freeze, and it's amazing.  However, the base swimming is pretty bad, as all you can do is dive a short distance underwater, where the water forces you back to the surface.  It's not in the game very long, which is why I question its inclusion.  The bird transformation is exactly like Squawks from DKC2 and 3, but it's too slow for my liking, and firing a shot halts any momentum.  The tiger transformation is nice in how it allows you to air dash, but the wall jumping controls feel sticky (I've been playing 20XX lately, whose wall jumping controls like a dream).  I already went over the dragon (minecart) transformation.The bonus rooms are nice in that they take from the minigame-like bonus rooms from DKC2 and 3 (particularly 3), but they're not nice in that they all take place in the same cave.  One of my biggest problems with the Returns duology is that all the bonus rooms felt samey, which is due in part to how the environments didn't really change over the course of the game (especially in Tropical Freeze).  This game doesn't have it nearly as bad, as all the bonus minigames are unique.  However, the fact that every single one takes place in the same cave is a bit tiring.100% completion is just not worth it.  Completing all the bonus rooms is, as doing so unlocks the 4 bonus levels (which I think are mixed in quality, but still fun enough).  Getting all the KAZE letters does nothing as far as I can tell.  No it's the 100 fodder items per level you have to get per level that's not worth it.  Unlike giving you an extra life (which would be pointless in this game due to the lack of a lives system), now getting 100 gems in each level is required to get 100% completion.  All this gives you is a more complete ending.  It doesn't give you any extra levels to play, or even anything at all different during gameplay as far as I know.  I didn't actually get 100% completion, as I missed a few gems in the level that requires you to (afaik) get every single one to get 100, and upon seeing what happens I determined that it wasn't worth it for me to do that level again.The world map is boring.  DKC1 and 2 at least had interesting map background set pieces, and DKC3 had a genuinely interesting map in the Northern Kremisphere.  This world map is much like Super Mario 3D Land's: lifeless.The game looks good visually, but not memorable.  Casting aside the fact that the original games were pre-rendered while this game is fully sprite-based, I think those games just have more memorable graphics and animation.  Every single frame of those original games, especially 2 and 3, just ooze with life.  Something as simple as how the peg-legged Kremlings walk in 2 just oozes so much character, and there's a good reason that K Rool is such a beloved villain.  The visuals might not have aged the best, but I'd argue that the character designs and animations most certainly have.  Kaze sees fit to copy some of the enemies from the original trilogy with worse character design.  I get the whole thing that they're veggies, but they could have done more with the designs and animations.  Nothing about them stick out to me.  Not even the final boss.  It's not bad, just forgettable.So, with all that said, why do I still recommend this game?  I like the gameplay of DKC, and this game mostly delivers on that front.  The levels are mostly solid, and the controls are mostly solid as I've said before.  It's a well designed and polished game.  I like the lack of lives (and lost progress), I like most of the levels, the secrets are pretty straight-forward for the most part, the bosses aren't bad and the final one is really cool.  I can't hate this game, even if I think all 5 DKC games are better.  For $5 US, it's not bad at all.  For $20 US... I'm not so sure.

_childDocuments_.review: 2D Crash Bandicoot. Mechanics aren't very complex, but most levels have some gimmick, be it one of the 4 masks, that give you a different moveset, chase sequences, slingshots etc. Levels are also very linear. What annoyed me a bit though is how the game is centered around insta death bottomless pits that leave no room for mistakes.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute BLAST! If you like Donkey Kong Country you're going to love this gem. Do me a favor though: try and 100% the game. If you're going to blast through all of the levels you're not going to get the same fun experience as someone who tries to go for all of the achievements, trust me (and this is coming from someone who isn't into achievement hunting)Anyway, Kaze and the Wild Masks is a wonderful game that any fan of platformers should play!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely good. Clear inspiration from DKC 3, but it has more than enough originality to stand on its own. Level construction is TIGHT and the platforms / enemies are expertly placed to make it feel like a great quick-react kind of time in certain areas. HUGE props to the composer as well, the main theme is interwoven into so many other parts of the game, and it's an extremely good one. I knew from the moment I was flying through those slingshots and seeing how Kaze pulls them back with her ears that I was in for an amazing game.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: So, in case you were wondering if this game was just a copy of Donkey Kong Country, you'd be surprised to see that it isn't and by a good margin to have its own identity.Starting with the similarities, Kaze jumps on enemies at a curve, has to collect 4 letters on each level for a bonus, can pick up things to throw at enemies and can get an impulse in the air using crossbows much like barrels. Aaaand, that's about it. Seriously, even though one can mention that Kaze glides like Diddy Kong, she can go the whole distance. Plus, her ground spin is shorter in distance than Donkey Kong's roll. As a result, let's mention what this game does differently.For starters, there are no lives, so each level can be attempted multiple times without the risk of a game over. That's a relief as some can be a bit long with more or less checkpoints placed on them depending on which mode you're playing on (casual or original). Furthermore, this game features lots of enemies based on vegetables, well drawn backgrounds and platforms and a vibrant soundtrack with tracks reserved for different kinds of zones and bosses.Then, Kaze has masks that serve as power ups with various movesets which fit the level in question. Most are fine enough to control, but the bird one in particular shoots at a curve and flies up too slowly for my liking. We can also mention the constantly running dragon mask which is the closest this game has to minecart sections.As a whole, the game isn't that hard to complete. There are hidden green gem sections (some really well) that unlock challenging bonus levels, the fact that in every non-boss level you only need to collect 100 crystals and you can miss some to do so, and the time trial achievement does not require gold medals in every level, so you can make some mistakes. As you also can in the speedrun achievement which even though sets the finish limit in 2 hours, that's more than enough.In conclusion, in case you were in the crave for a 2D platformer that plays similarly to DKC in some aspects but has its own style in presentation, story, power ups and more, this is certainly it. Just take into account beforehand that the crossbows (the barrels equivalent) don't have a thick hitbox.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely knocked this one out of the park, great game. Really hoping for a sequel. Really have only 2 issues with this game. One, the running by itself mask is really annoying, and the 2nd issue is with the final boss. Just not a fan of the fight. However that is strictly a personal preference and not a reason not to buy this game, the game itself as a whole is awesome.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like a mix between good ol' Jazz Jackrabbit 2 and Bloody Trapland 2. Even though the level design is rather simple the game lasts just enough to not become boring. It is hard at times, but there is a possibility to change the difficulty level to a lower one.Beating the game took me ~7h, doing it 100% ~8,5h; the rest of the time I played was to beat every single level without taking damage (which was really fun, some levels were pretty challenging). There are also time challenges, but I personally don't like doing those in any game and this one was not an exception.The only thing that was really annoying are controls in Kaze's flying form; they are rather imprecise, which at times was frustrating, if not infuriating.But overall it was definitely money well spent :)
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Gave up in the second boss.  For a casual player like me, it´s annoying this kind of battle where you have to survive for minutes, avoiding obstacles, demading precision on the control and then having a few oportunities to hit the boss. Anyway, for those who have more patience and free time in life, maybe it worthes to play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Solid but short platformer with good music on the side as well. Bulk of my time was spent trying to do better on the time trials and not taking damage in the process. I will probably come back for the speedrun achievement at a later time since the game was fun to play. Hope that they are able to make a sequel in the future since they made a solid game.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, an enjoyable and simple plain nostalgic platformer.  No search for the holy graal of mechanic's originality, with awful an unnecessary complexity as a result. No fancy ultra realistic engines. No obsession for puzzle oriented level designs that make you feel lost most of the time. No dramatic and morally despairing plot. No pretension except to make a really FUN and enjoyable game. The visuals are beautiful and kinda relaxing, no ultra flashy visual pollution here, which is a bless. Music goes in the same directions as it does the sound effects, keeping the action going in elegant an enjoyable fashion. Gameplay wise, is a very well made mash up of the best thing from the best games from the genre's past. No kidding, you go Donkey, you go Sonic, you go Mario, you go MegaMan, and you feel like Chameleon Kid in doing so. The challenge is high but smooth, you never feel overly punished by the game and even the hardest parts are designed in a way  that seems achievable from the very beginning. If retro gaming is your thing, and you have a crush for the old style platformers with superb graphics, this game is the deal, dude. Go for it, it's a great fun that worth your time and the price asked for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: A nice little retro throwback to Donkey Kong Country. Controls are solid and levels are highly choreographed based on your movement + ideal jump patterns. It's a little on the short side (4 zones) with 100% achievements doable in ~15 hrs. Great on the Deck for living room/mobile play and  quick sessions between all of the other distractions in life.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: A great platformer with a lovely graphics style and fun movement!The story isn’t particularly deep, but perfectly fine for the genre of game. To be honest the album pictures are more intriguing than most the cutscenes are.Both the art and music are very colourful and energetic making it a delight to boot up the game just for the title music.The difficulty covers a good range, on the easier difficulty you can breeze through if you want, while the harder one gives a decent challenge. Additionally you can attempt to complete all levels without taking any damage, which if you decide to do it’s best to do this while having the time trial active as you can reset the level more easily should you get hit.Not all levels are the exact theme of the world, bringing a lot of variety to them despite there only being four worlds, some later levels even bringing back mechanics of earlier ones while building on them in some way.Bonus levels should rather be called bonus stages as they are small special segments accessible from within the levels. Often nicely themed after the mechanics of the level they are in.To conclude I really enjoyed this game, it has good variety and challenge while not overstaying it’s welcome. Very much recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: It's Donkey Kong Country 2, with:- a few twists, but mostly remixes of older ideas.- music that is pretty solid for the most part.- graphics which are okay but feel slightly off.- generally great handling of movement, slightly better than Tropical Freeze since you accelerate properly out of rolling through an enemy.- pretty much what you'd expect.  This is store brand DKC2, which sounds mean to say but they really just copied so directly in mechanics and otherwise it makes me wish they had done more novel things.I had a good time getting started with this, but not sure that I really feel motivated to play more of it.  I might, but it just... doesn't pull me along like an actual Mario or DKC game does.What I see here is something that does two things really well:- For anyone who is younger and who has not played the DKC games and doesn't have a switch for Tropical Freeze, then this is a great game -- get it!  The fact that this is "we have DKC at home" shouldn't matter in that case.- For those of us who grew up on DKC, my hope is that the developers have kind of established their mechanics and style and so forth, and can come out with a Kaze 2 which really takes things to the next level and makes it their own.  I would be watching any sequel with great interest, as they've certainly laid a huge groundwork here.Ultimately this gets a thumbs up from me, but it's a bit more neutral than anything.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a very fun and challenging homage to the Donkey Kong Country series. The level design it excellent, the mask power-ups are unique and fun to use, the controls are very tight and responsive, the music is great, and the graphics/art are crisp and vibrant. As someone who loves retro 2D platformers, this game really impressed me. The difficulty is just right in my opinion. Every time I die, it's always my fault. There are plenty of collectibles in each stage, and finding them makes revisiting levels more fun and challenging. Some of them are pretty tricky to find, so expect to replay some levels a few times. Overall, I highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a polished and mechanically solid 2D platformer.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Finished this game 100% including Steam Achievements in just under 8 hours. Got the game on sale for $5. I definitely feel like it was a good buy, as it was 8 hours of solid, good-old-fashioned fun, though I'm not sure it's spectacular enough to warrant the normal $20 price tag. _childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing! A beautiful tribute to Donkey Kong Country with a charming style all its own. The game play is smooth and simple. Levels are fun with collectibles and time trials for replay-ability. Bosses are unique and challenging. There is sort of a story, but as with DKC, it's not really necessary. My only complaint is that it's too short (less that 10 hours to 100% everything but the time trials.) It absolutely left me wanting more.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game. My biggest problem was that the person who told me about it sold it to me as if it was Donkey Kong Country 4. It is not. Far from it. Sure, the devs took a LOT of inspirations from Rare's and some from Retro's DK 2D platformers, but I think you will be disappointed if you're looking for DKC4. The game's also inspired by Crash, Rayman, Sonic and Banjo-Kazooie (or at least the composer is a bit inspired by Grant Kirkhope). And maybe, just maybe, Majora's Mask (because of the masks, of course).If you look at Kaze as it's own beast, you get enjoyment from it. Simple as that. So I'll try my best not to mention DK or other games in this review anymore.The art is beautiful. Bright and colorful once, dark and menacing then, but never tiresome. The artists can be proud of this whole game, everything looks fantastic. The cutscenes, particularly, which aren't pixel-art, but rather traditional comic/cartoon style, are something to behold. Gorgeous, gorgeous art.The music... while I'm not the biggest fan, it's good enough for me. The inspirations from Kirkhope are clear, but the music also stands on its own feet. Or sheet - sorry. Good work overall. Even better, no track from the game managed to annoy me. While that seems like something trivial, I find too many indie titles get to have at least one or two irritating tracks.The controls are hard to review because BOY this game is hard! Let me tell you: every time I died it was my fault and no one else's. But WOW, I wish some things were done a bit more like DKC - and I promise I won't mention other games after this: I wish Kaze floated more like 90s Dixie did. I wish her weight and mechanics worked more like any of the 90s Kongs than like hers. I feel like the game is a bit... "rigid" is an unfair term to use, the game flows nicely, but I wish it flowed BETTER. Of course that would require redesigning all the stages and bosses and enemies, so maybe in the next game we get luckier in this aspect.The idea of facing food is ADORABLE. And the artists once again can be VERY proud: I never thought I'd look at corn or watermelon and think "ugh, gross", but still be charmed by the things. Every single enemy, from beans to carrots and pumpkins, is extremely well designed and done so creatively. The bosses take a back seat to their fantastic minions, but they're still great.Finally, addressing difficulty, I think this is the game's Achilles's Heel. I started on the intended mode, getting every bonus, gem, K-A-Z-E letter, trying my best to take no damage, but WOW the game is hard. I came here for a good time, and the game delivered, the difficulty isn't that kind of "FINALLY" difficulty, it's very fair, but if you want something light, skip this one for a while. Come back when you want something a little more hardcore. I feel like this game is a speedrunner's dream, a completionist's fantasy, and in catering to these targets, they left other players behind. Sure, I thought "I'm dying mostly to bottomless pits, what difference will it make to change the difficulty to the easier one?" (btw, that's a very nice option), but I was wrong and not only did I die more than I thought to regular enemies, the extra hearts and extra checkpoints were more than welcome. Still I feel like the studio can learn to balance difficulty better for their next endeavors. I played the two last bosses in the easy difficulty and was offered the chance to skip the level. They shouldn't be that hard. Other games were hard mostly because of limitations from their times, and I feel Kaze goes out of its way to emulate that much unneeded difficulty.Overall, great game. I would say it's too short, but it's just the right lenght considering how hard it is. Maybe they could make a longer, easier game next time.Oh!, design a better world map next time! This one is good, does its task right, but it's basic considering what it could be. No need for 3D or anything that fancy, just a cute, walkable map that maybe changes a little as you progress through the current world, which is connected to other worlds.Score: 8.25/10
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game, gets a full recommendation. It's Donkey Kong Country 2.5: Dixie Kong goes Brazilian, with a good helping of Rayman. It honors those influences.If you understood that sentence, buy it right away. It is modest, don't get me wrong, but it is modest in the best way-- it puts all of its resources into the exact right places. The gamefeel, the aesthetics, the music, it's all so good. I wasn't a big fan of the final level where you have to boss rush in stages in one life, but that is par for the course for DKC and Rayman. My biggest complaint is simply that I wish there was more! More vegetables! More levels! More masks! More story! Animal buddies! A companion to trade out with Kaze! And to top it all off it's a wonderful Brazilian game! Viva o Brasil! My deepest love, respect, and admiration for all the developers in Porto Alegre. I really hope you've all been given a fair deal, and if nothing else can look at this work with pride as a good experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: "Kaze and the Wild Masks" is an extremely faithful re-imagination of the platforming gameplay from "Donkey Kong Country 2" (the main character "Kaze" controls exatly like "Dixie Kong") molded into a new setting, where animated vegetables took over the land and the folks got turned into crystals and you have to rescue your friend or whatever.They included many things from DKC, mainly the different animals that give you enhanced abilities (i.e. the masks that you obtain), the water sections, the mincart levels (where you put on a dragon mask and run like crazy) and even the "lightswitch-level" is in there.The style is very colorful, the pixelart is detailed and the level design is top notch, but the whole experience is very straightforward and there are not that many worlds and bosses to explore. 100%ing the game is sadly also not that rewarding, for there is no alternative ending, just a secret cutscene.It is challenging but more forgiving than the old-school-platformers and definetly worth a dive into the new-nostalgia genre!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game whether you're a DKC series veteran, or someone who wants to play a tightly designed platformer with a slightly frustrating, albeit forgiving difficulty. It's a level difficulty that hits the sweet spot of being challenging, but not unfair. (for the most part) I felt like I was actually improving with each challenge I had to face. Plus the controls are so tight that it's just fun jumping and running around in each level. Most of the time, it's the player's fault when they die, not the other way around. So when you come back from a checkpoint, or continue a different level, you start to get into a rhythm. Once you figure out how to traverse levels in a nearly perfect way, everything clicks. Visually speaking, most of the game is very appealing! From the levels, to the enemies, to Kaze herself! (The rabbit lady you play as.) The masks that you use from time to time also have a nice flair. Combined with the fact whenever Kaze wears a mask, she transforms, and certain parts of her body change visually to reinforce that they've become one with mask they're wearing. One gripe that I have is that some background elements feel very disjointed. Like some villagers of each Island looking like off-brand cereal mascots, no identity in the slightest. Another gripe is that while the music isn't bad, I also wouldn't say it's very memorable either. (outside of maybe the title screen music and a few certain levels) It's a shame too because almost every other aspect of this game is very memorable. Lastly, thematically speaking, every island's levels order wise feel very jumbled. Like I said earlier, I love the visuals, but in terms of context it's very awkward. Like one the second island, (the ice one) one level I'm in a ice level, the next I'm at a factory, and then immediately after that I'm in a Volcano. I almost felt like I was playing on different islands in different levels sometimes. The DKC series handles this a lot better. With each level you played,and each island you beat, It gave the impression that you were actually making progress traveling from point A, to point B and so on. Honestly, the gripes I have with this game are minuscule compared to how much I love from this game. I would love to see this game get the recognition it deserves. Some diehard nintendo fan labeling this game a "RiPoFf" is laughable. It's not a ripoff if it has enough identiy, and luckily, this game has plenty of it! Also, If you're one a diehard nintendo fan, sucks to be you ;3Final verdict: 9/10 BABY! THIS GAME IS A FUGGIN MASTERPIECE!!! EVERY SINGLE PERSON WHO WORKED ON THIS GAME SHOULD BE PROUD OF THEMSELVES!!I hope you have a very nice day/night :3

_childDocuments_.review: Donkey Kong Country with 1 rabbit instead of 2 monkeys. It does have a couple of new ideas, but it is heavily influenced by the DKC games, which is not a bad thing.
