_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This was a pleasant surprise. Kaze and the Wild Masks is a beautiful love letter to the 90s platformers, mainly the Donkey Kong series from the SNES days. I haven't played them religiously aside from the first one, but I can see all the similarities and I'm here for it!In Kaze, the Crystal Islands have been cursed and regular sweet vegetables have been corrupted and terrorizing the lands. On top of that, Kaze's close friend, Hogo, has been turned into a sprite that follows her around. She must journey through all of the lands using her skills and the powers that dwell in the ancient guardian masks to save the islands and her best friend.Kaze is a breath of fresh air. The colors are great, the music is cute and not annoying, and the controls are tight for the most part. Kaze can jump, spin attack, and do an air glide with her rabbit ears by holding the attack button. She can bounce off enemies for flips which helps keep the forward momentum going. Kaze definitely wants you to get into the flow of movement and speed running and it was a joy to feel it through the progression of levels.This game is also a collect-a-thon as each stage presents you with 4 challenges. Find the four letters that spell KAZE, collect 100 crystals, find and complete two hidden bonus stages (and some of them are very WELL hidden), and then complete a time trial once you complete the levels. Getting %100 will unlock the hidden ending and I found it worth the journey since it was a fun challenge. There was only one stage where I had to look up where the hidden stage was, but most of them just required me to really look hard and find them. The wild masks themselves are nice. They are relegated to stages and not something you have access to all the time. They give Kaze new abilities. The bird mask lets her fly, the shark mask lets her swim faster, the tiger mask lets her dash and scale walls, and the dragon mask makes her turn into an auto-runner with a double jump and dive. All of them controlled nicely and added some fun diversity to the levels. Add some fun game mechanics like the slingshots and the recipe is a delicious nostalgic blend.The game is not incredibly long which is refreshing. It took me about 15-17 hours to beat it, but a skilled player could probably 100% in 10-12 hours. The bosses were very challenging but, just the right amount of challenge. They tested you (especially the later ones and the LAST ONE), but it was never impossibly hard which I appreciated. If you feel the game is tough, you can change it to casual mode. You'll be able to take more hits and have more checkpoints. In regular mode, there is only one checkpoint and you can only gain one extra hit. I finished in original mode, but I always appreciate it when developers add modes like that for players who may struggle.As far as gripes go, I think I only have one. This is just a personal gripe, but I hate that when you bounce off an enemy, you can't glide afterward until you land. I had a lot of cheap deaths in where I bounced off an enemy and I grit my teeth saying, "If I could glide after that bounce, I would have lived." If they make a sequel, I hope that is something they add, as well as a dash button since time trials were VERY fun to complete in this game...well most of em at least.Final verdict? Do you like 2D platformers? Then you'd be doing yourself a disservice by not grabbing this game. It was incredibly fun and charming. It tapped into the nostalgic fun old school platformers and I was smiling the whole time while finishing it. Hats off to the developers for this masterpiece and I hope this is not the last we'll see of Kaze. Thanks for reading!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great modern addition to your collection if you enjoy playing side-scrolling platformers! Sprite and artwork is beautiful, music is awesome and the levels I've played so far have been really fun to explore while finding collectibles and secrets. The mask abilities you get in specific levels have been fun to play around with too. Think my favorite has been the one that helps with the underwater levels. Makes it fun to zip around and dodge projectiles with! It's on sale now as of the time of this posting it, so maybe consider picking this up! It's well worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: After completing the game 100% on original mode, I can safely say that this feels like a true sequel to the classic Donkey Kong Country games: The platforming is fast and tight, with the masks, which act as the animal companions in this game, providing a welcome variety in gameplay. Each level in Kaze and the Wild Masks feels notably different: With minecart levels (lizard mask), barrel shooting levels (slingshots), autoscrollers, classic platforming and escape levels.The music is also peppy and fun and later levels can become quite challenging, especially if you're trying to no-hit them, so that there is no lack of difficulty. I'd recommend this game to anyone who likes fast platformers. Since there is no puzzling involved, you can pretty much rush through all of the levels as fast as you want once/if you've got the necessary skills and that feels incredibly satisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big Donkey Kong Country fan and games that feel like DKC are really rare. This one pulls it off fantastically. The controls are snappy, the levels are just the right length and there are just the right amount of collectibles so the game doesn't become tedious.If you're a fan of classic SNES platformers, you have to plya Kaze, it's one of the best platformers out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a love letter to platformers, particularly the Donkey Kong Country series. Phenomenal level design with an extremely satisfying balance of challenge and variety. The mask abilities of (flappy bird-esque) flight, torpedo swimming, auto-run/double jump, and wall clinging kept each world unique and exciting. Visual design & music are 10/10. Can't recommend it enough!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Sooooo this is really fun. I highly recommend it if you're a fan of Donkey Kong Country or just platforming games in general. Art is beautiful, animations are charming, music is catchy, game starts out easy and ends up very challenging, but does have an easier difficulty for those who want it. Absolutely loved my 10 hours with this game, very much worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Like a lot of other reviews are already mentioning: This game borrows a lot of gameplay ideas from the Donkey Kong Country series. While it never reaches the hights of a DKC game and doesn't have many standout moments, it luckily avoids all of the pitfalls (e.g. awful bonus rooms in Tropical Freeze) as well. Everything is consistently good. The way the secrets are hidden, the level design, the graphics, the boss fights, the music, the bonus rooms. Never amazing, but never bad either.It's not a long game and probably not one that will stay in your memory for very long. But if you enjoy DKC and just want more of that gameplay, Kaze can easily be recommended (especially if it's 75% off like right now).
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. It strikes a fine balance between too easy and too hard, it's just right. The character design and animations are great and all unique in their own way. The levels are designed around certain gimmicks and are all quite different. The story is told in a way that add some mystery on the history of the world and masks.Basically a DKC clone, I'd give it a 10/10. Best 2D platformer I've played in a long while.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Super Tight controls and equally tightly designed levels. As the game progresses and becomes harder it really leaves less and less room for error and starts to resemble Geometry Dash in that you will retry stages dozens of times to get that perfect run where everything works perfectly. The powerups are creative, I love the Tiger levels especially, the dragon turns the game into an autorunner which are still cool. The Shark and Hawk.... eh, not a huge fan of those, but they are sparse anyway. There's also only 4 worlds in the game which makes the game end quite abruptly maybe 4-5 hours in. Bosses are all really cool. The collectibles can be a bit much but since there's so few levels anyway it's actually manageable. I 100%ed the first 3 island and got exhausted from it, the final island I just rushed for the end and I think that's all I wanna do. But you can invest a lot of time into this game 100%ing everything. Pixel Art, Music, all that's great too. The game does love to remind you to 100% every stage and that can put a lot of pressure on you psychologically. Collecting 99 pink gems when you need at least 100 is especially infuriating cause it amounts to nothing, you gotta repeat the level and get 100 for it to count. Not a big fan of that design. Just remember the collectibles are optional. 😅
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: I did expect more from this game considering all the extremely positive reviews I've read/watched, that said this was an enjoyable game, though it has some design decisions I'm not a fan of. It reminds me of Shovel Knight in that it doesn't try to emulate any one game of the era it's inspired by, but rather to capture the general feeling, which it certainly does (not always to its advantage). The story is more or less non-existent, consisting of a few still images, but you're here for the platforming. And it's generally good. For the type of experience they are going for they managed the difficulty well. The best levels are the ones where you'll use of of the titular wild masks and transform into a different animal which changes the way it plays, this is largely enjoyable, however the lizard suffers from no tutorialization. The other animals the game prompts you to attack to see their unique attack, but the lizard rather has a double-jump, which I had to go to youtube to find out as I had no reason to assume that (especially considering the game had given prompts for the others which was always tied to the attack button). My other gripe is stingy checkpointing. Even on casual which adds a few more checkpoints (from what I can tell that's all it does, I think maybe you get an extra hit point) the game is too stingy with checkpoints and it's rather annoying having to keep going through sections you've been, sometimes quite a while. The last issue is it has unlockable levels, tied to finding 2 secrets zones in each level and completing those challenges. Those are largely enjoyable though nothing that difficult, the problem is the levels while fun aren't fun enough to go through multiple times to find these portals if you've missed them. I would have liked to play the unlockable levels, but not enough to basically replay most of the game again (I found 1 zone on almost all levels, but only found both on maybe half or so) - the challenge mostly being to find them not the challenge in the zone.Other than that I mostly enjoyed my time with it. It's a good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: So I am a huge fan of Donkey Kong Country and this game does a really great job of incorporating elements from all of the games in that series as well as several others. I played all through the story and I'm working on 100% now. I like the spin jump mechanic which is similar to the roll jump from DKC, and I love the level design which has the ability to be difficult for newcomers but easy and even more fun as your skill increases. I don't feel like the art is very memorable though. It feels kind of generic and doesn't have as much charm as DK, Mario, or Sonic. This is especially apparent in the backgrounds and level assets. The music also doesn't have as much of an impact as those games either, which is unfortunate.Overall, I have really enjoyed playing this game and I am really hoping it gets a sequel considering there isn't another platform like DKC on the horizon.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: A love letter to platformers of old done right.Kaze and the Wild Masks draws heavily on the original Donkey Kong Country series and it shows. However that is not a bad thing at all and in some ways has improved upon an already incredible formula. As an avid fan of DKC and old school platformers this game gets a double thumbs up. If you've had the itch to play a game similar to DKC this is the game to get. Literally buy it right now as this is the closest thing that i have found.Pros:-------------------+Vibrant world and art direction.+Controls. The movement in this game has that "it" factor that is so commonly missed in some platform games. It has a very polished feel and a lot of time was put into how the movement flows throughout each level...which brings me to...+Great level design,  each level flows in way that allows you to zip through it once the pattern is learned. There are hardly any moments that feel stilted because you are required to take an abrupt stop. However you are also able to play in a more slow and deliberate approach which is very welcome. +Bonus "barrels" are back! And they are also well hidden. Every one is visable if you are looking in the right areas of the screen. More then once i found myself saying, "Wouldnt it be cool if they put one here? Oh wait, they did!" +Fun boss fights. I enjoyed each boss in this game, they follow the genre standard of learning the attack pattern of a wave and waiting for an opening to appear. Each boss feels fresh and I found the final boss fight to be especially enjoyable.+Difficulty. Everything felt fair. Each time i took a hit or made a mistake it always felt like it was my fault rather than poor game mechanics or design. It wasnt too hard or too frustrating and for players that struggle with this type of game; there is a casual play option that makes things a little easier to manage. Cons--------------- Overworld felt a bit boring. This mostly comes down to personal preference but I didnt enjoy how each world was presented. There is the themed island concept for each world which is fine, but once you "enter" the island it is consisted of 7-8 blocks in a straight line that make up each level. There is a harsh line between the environments of each level which tends to make the themed islands irrelevant. For instance, a sand/desert block in an ice world.- Length. Unfortunately it is a short game. I was able to beat the game twice in 10 hours. Once to collect everything and 100% each level and the second to speedrun through the game for the achievement.- Time challenge medals feel completely irrelevant. I've never been a big beat the level as fast as you can guy. However, i found it extremely easy to get gold in every single level, even beating the times by 20+ seconds at times. For reference each level is about 1 minute and 45 seconds to 2 minutes and 45 seconds long. This makes the gold, silver and bronze rankings feel unnecessary. At that point just give a single time limit to beat for each level - Cost. As much as it pains me to say it seeing how much polish and time went into this game it feels overpriced given the amount of content in the game. I feel like this game would have done much better at a $9.99 price point. As a die hard DKC fan and platform enthusiast, i found it worth it. I just someone that doesn't have the same passion finding it too pricey to justify.All in all a solid game that i'm very grateful is available to play9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent platformer. Clearly inspired by Donkey Kong Country, it captures a lot of the level design concepts that make that series great. Most levels have their own unique quirks that are satisfying to explore, and the collectibles and achievements are a great challenge that I instinctively wanted to complete.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Only played through the first world and I'm already enjoying it immensely. Fantastic Donkey Kong Country inspired/spiritual successor. Very similar controls and concepts. Great graphics, fun levels, absolutely recommend. The music isn't anything to write home about, but you can't really expect anything to compare to the DKC-series.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: At the point of this review I've about 80% of the game completed. There are only 3 levels left I have to do before the final showdown happens and at this point I'm torn about I like it or if I'm annoyed by it.I personally like to play plattformers at my own pace. From The last 7 levels were 6 of them chase-based designs. You can chose what is chasing you: A fish (this is the most interesting one), a tornado, lava, toxic water or you just have no control to stop. That's the main reason why I can't recommened it for everyone. Be aware of being chased in the late mid- and endgame.However the game makes clear that it wants you to play fast. The enemies and hazards are exactly so placed that you get over them easily if you are just fast enough. I like this idea. If you really want to be the fastest it gets a precision plattformer.For everyone else there is room for error, but not a lot. E.g. you get a collectable for 100 red crystals in each level after completion. In every level there are around 103-105 crystals. That means you are not allowed to miss many of them and you will find yourself trying to cling to any red crystal you can find.There are 2 challenges in each level. The entrances to them are hidden, but never unfairly. You can fnd them without help if you're looking closely and mind your surroundings. Doing all of them in each level unlocks a new, a bit harder level.Other collectables are the letters K-A-Z-E. Collecting all of them rewards you with a picture that explains a bit of background lore of the game. Neat.There are also different difficulties and time challenges. I haven't tested them yet.Animations are high quality. Enemies are hilarious. Boss fights are one of the bests I've seen so far in a 2D plattformer. The idle animations are adorable. The story is -I haven't finished it yet - weird.Summary: If you like to play fast and being chased in a plattformer, this might be for you.If you like to play in your own pace and want a wide variety of level types you might want to look elsewhere.Difficulty at "normal": Challenging, but doable.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Plays exactly like the old DKC games with the main character controlling like Dixie. The gameplay is refined in almost every way including greater feeling of control and more fair level design. It does lack the charm of the old DKC games though as well as the better level design seen in the newer DKC games. Plenty satisfying to play though and rather forgiving as far as platformers go. Pretty easy to get all achievements as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Kaze and the Wild Masks is an amazing platformer with excellent level design. It captures the essence and nostalgia of SNES classics. The game definitely takes a lot of inspiration from Donkey Kong Country, to the point that I would say multiple levels were blatant rip-offs, but it's so good that I don't even care. My only negative is that the game is a little on the short side. It took me just under 6 hours to beat the game and reach 100%. It's so good and I just wish there was more of it!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Nintendo should just sign a big check and give the DK franchise to them. Retro and Playtonic Games are doing a great job, however, theses guys nailed it.One of the greatest surprises in game for me. At first glance, this was another indie DKC clone, I must admit, the trailer didn't help me either. But once I started playing... this is perfection!The soundtrack makes me feel a kid playing DK on the Snes again, the gameplay is top notch, bouncing in enemies heads is as satisfaying as ever, hit boxes are precise (maybe even too generous for the player), level and enemy diversity is great, the story has something of a "Kung fu Panda", bonus stages are fun and challenging. I could go on and on, but you got the gist. Now I will find a a physical copy for 10 times the price, because this my friends, is the definition of a hidden gem, and what a gem we have here.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: If you love 2D platformers with movement that feels good, this game is for you. Spin attacks, jumping, bouncing, gliding, etc. I completed this game in under 8 hours. The game maybe short, but it's not shallow. If you're like me, I finished the game first, then consider if I really wanna complete the game or not (which I did and it's worth it). Nitpick: The story is nice and simple, but it's not very good in the execution of the sad parts. There aren't any text at all for exposition. I don't know anyone's name expect for Kaze (which I'm assuming is the protagonist's name.)
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Easy recommendation if you enjoy classic 2D platformers from the 16bit era (SNES and Mega Drive).Kaze and the Wild Masks looks fantastic and controls well. The power ups are fun. It is not difficult, but also not a cakewalk, especially if you want to 100% it. I mean, there is no game over and enemies/hazards are predictable and lenient, and in the off chance you find the game hard there is an easier difficulty setting that adds more checkpoints to each level.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best platformers I have played in a long time.A huge thank you to PixelHive and everyone else involved in making this gem!The flow of the levels and controlability of Kaze are amazing. For me, this game rivals anything along the lines of Donkey Kong Country Returns or Rayman Origins/Legends for bright fun but challenging levels. If you enjoyed those games (including the original DKC trilogy) then it would be a safe bet you would enjoy this.The atmosphere, the music, the level design, the change of play style thanks to the Wild Masks, and the controlled rise in challenge are near perfection. The only sore spot is the game's length, but with this quality in every aspect of the game I wasn't disappointed.I can see the devs doing a lot more with the skillset and challenges presented here, so here's hoping this is only the beginning, and we get some extra DLC or even a Kaze 2!!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This is basically a classic Donkey Kong Country game, it doesn't try to hide it's inspiration. While visually it is quite different from DKC, the gameplay is very DKC. It plays just like the SNES DKC games, it has roll jumping, rolling into enemies extends your roll, there are bonus stages, there are "KONG" letters to find, and even an equivalent to the animal buddies with the Masks. The character you play as even plays just like Dixie Kong. This is a DKC game, and that isn't a criticism, it's actually high praise from me. The DKC games are some of my favorite games, and this game is a worthy successor. Now there are some small criticisms I have for the game, unlike the SNES DKC games, you are only controlling 1 character, and I feel like the game loses a bit because of that. Aside from it just being cool controlling 2 characters, the ability to pick up and throw the other Kong did add a lot, and that's not here at all. It's not a big deal in the slightest, but it was something I missed having. Another thing is the way the story is presented. It doesn't really explain what is even happening, the intro shows the 2 main characters getting some kind of magic ring, which turns one of them into a floating head thing, and that's basically it. The only reason I know that the character you control is named Kaze is because of the name of the game, I don't even know who her friend is, or who the villain is or anything. You can unlock pieces of backstory which clears some stuff up, but it requires some interpretation, which isn't a bad thing, but I would have liked a little more clear context for what is going on, and who the characters are.But aside from those nitpicks, this game is fantastic, one of the best 2D platformers I've played. If you enjoyed those first 3 DKC games, this is an easy recommendation. Even if you just like platformers you should check this out.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Kaze and the Wild Masks is a gripping tale about the horrors of agriculture. Or it could be a fun platformer with heavy influence of Donkey Kong Country. The controls are great, the graphics are amazing, level design is mostly good and the music is downright magical. The only downside is that some on some of the later levels rely heavily on memorization as there is very little room to make mistakes. Yes, the difficulty can be very frustrating, but at the same time, there is a casual mode for us impatient babies, so it is not too bad. Overall a very well made game. But know what you are getting into. 4/5
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: A love letter to your favourite 2D platformer from your childhood - Rayman, Donkey Kong Country, Sonic etc.On the surface the concept of fighting through fruit and vegetables as a rabbit seems generic and doesn't pop out on first appearance, but it's creatively done enough that it grows on you and the tight controls and platforming gameplay makes up for it. The spritework is done well but the set pieces do feel a little repetitive at times, but the concept of the mask power ups does spice the levels up. It does get quite challenging especially if you like to 100% collect everything, it's no easy cruise if you give yourself a challenge. The flying sections were not a personal favourite as the tight controls you're used to are subverted by a button mashing style of flying mechanic and an attack that arcs, this makes it more challenging but not in the way you'd want.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Rayman, this one is for you. Right from the start I was thrown back to when I was a kid playing on the PS2. The controls are butter smooth and do what you tell them to. The levels are never repetitive and I loved how new abilities and levels were introduced. I never found myself grinding to get forward. Some levels are challenging in their own right, but I wouldn't say this is a particularly challenging platformer.One thing that took some getting used to was how "flying" was done with a different button than jump. I didn't understand why at first, but some of the mechanics introduced later made me realize why.The only downside is that you can't play locally with others. Otherwise, hats off to the developers. This is a well-made and fun game.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: It is astounding how the game implemeting only 3 basic movements with the help of brilliant game design, artwork and music manages to make every single stage feel differently. It may feel overwhelming to platinum this game because of speedrun and no hit runs achievements as you are bound to do what the game desingers exactly expects you to do. But all in all I am appreciated that the game teaches you how to play it, leaving you in the end with a feeling that you beat the game fair and squere completele. And that's something I haven't experienced for a while.If you are a fan of old-school precision platforms you definitely shoudn't demiss on this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful visuals; great, clever level design that rewards risk and exploration; simple, intuitive controls; gorgeous enemy design with clear weak points; beautifully designed main character with abilities that reference old platformers; and most importantly, main character’s control physics made just right. All of this comes together to create an amazing game that has obviously been made with love. Can’t wait to finish it and have my family try it as well. Thank you!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent platformer heavily inspired by donkey kong country series.Very pretty with nice music. 4 worlds in total, each with 1 boss and around 8 stages.It is challenging especially on the last worlds,especially the no hit runs.I had great fun with the game and recommend it except the final boss and final bonus stage in world 4,which i think needed more balancing.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: A simple retro yet effective sidescrolling platformer. Cute graphics and fitting music. The controls are very smooooth yet TIGHT!... But where the game shines is at it's level design and variation in levels and also in movement! The masks you use makes movement feel very different while the stages also makes you move in very different ways. It's super fun and comfy! Only thing against it might be that it is a little expensive for the kinda shorter game it is. But if you 100% the game it should take at least a decent amount of time. So it's all up to you baby! B)
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Rayman for furriesAt first glance I got more DKC vibes, but it's probably 70% Rayman / 30% Donkey Kong. Very straightforward and easy for platform vets (I cleared it 100% in 5 hours) but a good enough time. The newer Rayman titles are very clearly better versions of this idea, but you have to give the tiny team credit for the work they put into making that formula their own.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: I know nothing behind this game. It was on sale, had excellent reviews, so I bought it. Very similar to Donkey Kong Country on the Super Nintendo if you are old enough like me to remember the feel of that game. Some people really liked those games, and others didn't. I thought they where amazing platformers. Kaze and the Wild Masks is pretty straight forward when it comes to story, nothing overly complicated. The game gets right to the action. Looks really nice as well. The developers did a nice job with this game. Grab it if your a fan of side scrolling platformers. You will not be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy 2D platformers (especially Donkey Kong Country), you really can't go wrong with this one. Someone described it as "comfort food" which I find really accurate - the game just looks, feels and plays well. No major complaints but I found that the lizard mask segments had a huge difficulty spike and they seemed to rely more on just memorization rather than reflexes or skill.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic 2D platformer, easy to pick up but has plenty of challenges along the way.Very much a Donkey Kong Country / Rayman spiritual successor, so if you're into that kinda thing, this is 100% right up your alley.The mask power-ups look SO cool, and even though I get that some levels are designed around them, part of me wishes you could just switch between them on the fly to tackle various situations. If they ever make a sequel, they definitely need to go the route Rayman 3 did with that idea. It is very good but feels just a little restricted, and thus can definitely be improved upon.The game looks very pretty with fluid pixel art animation, and the soundtrack bangs.It does have some frustrating bits, but that's pretty much every video game ever so I can't really complain here.Just buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Kaze is a wonderfully crafted platformer that feels like playing the Donkey Kong Tropical Freeze (The best DK). It has that refined level design where things feel like they were planned there almost like a rhythm for playing quickly or at your own pace without impeding the natural challenge of the game.A+, contender for game of the year
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: From the videos and images, you would believe it is a bad interpretation of what made Donkey Kong Country special. That said, it is a good product that is definitely derivative... but which game isn't derivative these days? Comparing this game with DKC is unavoidable.The tight controls are something you can find in some of the more recent DKC titles. While it does have a smaller amount of levels than your average DKC game, they're all well-designed to an extent. I agree that the levels taking reference from the minecart are the most difficult... as the originals were in the 90's or even the 2010's if you played the Retro Studios titles. Once you get a better knowledge of these levels (which is par for the course for any platformer), you may be capable of appreciating the game as a whole. None of the deaths are cheap. Thankfully, it doesn't rely on a life system so don't expect a game over screen. What did disappointment are some of the bosses. That said, one of them was the most imaginative since King Zing from DKC2.The bonus levels are something that is improved from the modern DKC and you can find some of the influences across the entire progression in this product. The pixel art and parallax scrolling show the care and love that has been put into the art design. Kaze herself is well-animated, one of her animations being a direct reference to that Kong she's totally not stealing her moves from. The soundtrack is fine for what it is, but I won't blame you if you turn it off and try to listen to the classics themes of DKC. You'll see how much they understood it.Kaze and the Wild Masks is a wild ride, your typical 4-5 hours indie platformer that is well-paced, certainly made with passion and respect for the classics. If you're still unsure, waiting for a sale isn't a bad thing. Don't expect much of a story besides images for lore. Concept arts as unlockables would have been a better bonus.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: I had a blast playing this game, Kaze's design is adoable and the pixel art is just gorgeous. It gets hard towards de end but is still fair to the player.+Tight controls+amazing Level design+Imaginative scenariosWhat I dind't like about this game is:-Hover and attack on the same button-Themed levels all mixed up aroud the worlds (somehow)-Need 100% complision to get the good ending?The last one is a bummer because I rather have artwork and music as rewards than the NEED to replay all levels and challenges to get the true ending.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Donkey Kong Country 2, you will like this game. It's rather derivative, but also has enough unique content to enjoy. It's on the shorter side of things as well, but between time trials and 100%ing it, you'll get a solid 10 or so hours out of it. Looks great, the music is good-great, and I had fun full-clearing it (achievements and all).
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: To any DKC fan, this is a thrill. Controls feels very similar, and are very tight. One thing to get used to is the dixie-style helicopter activates automatically if the button is pressed, and there is no distinction between walking/running, although rolling gives a speed boost as expected.Very runnable, I enjoyed the first world right away and I already know I'll play this game to 100% (103%?)
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Best game 2021 ! Game was cute, and badass. Movement worked really well, I only had problems with the short, and long jump.The music was great, but I wish there would've been more tracks.Succeeding in this game felt awesome, and I really hope there's going to be a sequel.Overall this is a fantastic game, that everyone should play! Thank you PixelHive, and everyone else for making this masterpiece <3
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good platformer that manages to control really well and still present a considerable challenge. Nintendo and 90s Rare have made this combination look easy, but many of us have played enough games to know that it is anything but. All the other things like sound and visuals get a passing grade from me. I put very low weight on everything but gameplay when evaluating a game, so I will focus on that for the rest of this review.While I am completely comfortable giving this game a thumbs up for all that it did well, I must admit I personally was unsatisfied. The reason is that platformers are not my preferred genre, and I enjoy puzzles and exploration more. The DKC series from the SNES, which this game borrowed a lot from, hit my sweet spot with the rich variety of secrets that its levels had. Kaze borrowed the idea of secrets, to its credit. Every level has a green crystal, each half obtained by locating a warp to a timed bonus stage. Other reviews had let me know this aspect of DKC had made it in, so I decided to give the game a try.Where Kaze fell short is that whenever I had to revisit a level to find something I missed, the same approach worked every time: keep your eyes on the edges of the screen and look for warps poking out of scenery or a potential pathway leading offscreen. To be fair, most secrets in 2D platformers are found this way, but there's a big difference between Kaze where it was the solution 100% of the time and the old DKC series where it was the solution maybe 50-70% of the time. In Kaze, you never have to guess which walls can be smashed open. You're never shown in plain sight a cruel arrangement of the level's themed obstacles, with the obvious bonus letting you know that you can skip it if you want. You have no complex moves like throwing your partner to consider while searching. You never have to keep an enemy cannonball on screen long enough to hit a wall for you (!). You never have to find bonus stages inside bonus stages. You never have to think outside the box.In listing all of that out, I do not wish to claim that the developers failed to collect all the needed ingredients to make a modern DKC-style game. They certainly reworked several elements of that series, like throwing out the antiquated lives system, and most of these changes worked. It may have been their goal to simplify the experience and controls, hence no partner throwing, and to avoid some of the more bizarre requirements that make people reach for guides. (The enemy cannonball mentioned above is an actual solution from the DKC series, and it was as obtuse as it was unforgettable.) The reader whose tastes align more with pure platforming than mine may very well see all my complaints and think of them as positives rather than negatives, and I would accept that.But let me present myself as one example of a player whose favorite part of the DKC series was the creativity of its secrets. Kaze, while it has secrets, leaves that creativity out. The result was a game that did not meet my expectations for enjoyment.Don't let all the complaining above distract you from the fact that you will get a great platformer if you buy Kaze, and this alone is a praiseworthy achievement by the developers. If that is all you were looking for, this will be a good purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful tribute to Donkey Kong Country and other retro 2d platformers with pixel art so detailed I thought it was hand drawn at first from the screenshots. Very well animated as well with unique art direction that makes this one of the best looking indie games I've ever played with a charming soundtrack that goes well with the visuals. Character design is top notch, creative, and wouldn't be out of place for a mid 90s mascot platformer. However it doesn't end up feeling generic in the slightest nor a rip off and the game pays respects to the source material it's mechanics are lifted from while still managing to do its own thing. Controls are very responsive, jumping has a nice weight to it and levels are fun to traverse through whether I'm taking my time to collect every thing the first time or speedrunning a level I already beat. Well balanced difficulty and bosses and a lack of a lives system makes this alot more accessible than its contemporaries, (such as DKC Tropical Freeze for example, a much harder game) still it more than makes up for that with levels that don't hold your hand and provide a fair challenge with a bit of trail and error as well as optional bonus levels and time attack to get good a speedrunning levels you already beat. The game can be made easier or harder depending on your preferences but no where near as challenging as some balls to the wall precision platformers but still keeps you on your toes and a mastering of the jump, spin attack, and hover as well as the mask abilities will be necessary to get the most out of this game.The masks provide good variety such as one that you use to fly and avoid hazards as you fire a projectile, dive and dash underwater or climb walls and air dash. The only one I didn't really like turns the game into an auto runner where you run in place really fast and have the option to jump up or dive bomb downwards. I had a lot of trouble with this one and would have numerous game overs had there been a lives system implemented. Luckily the lack thereof makes difficult stages (precise platforming, bottomless pits, death spikes, etc.) and time attacks as well as bonus stages instantly and infinitely replayable. After dying you just spawn right back in, and this honestly is the best feature any tricky platformer can have. The whole experience is a very addicting "just one more try" gameplay loop whether overcoming challenges or trying to get a better time. No deaths are cheap and always felt like my fault and not bad level design with very few exceptions. The DKC inspirations are very apparent such as collecting 4 K-A-Z-E letter cards throughout the stage, being able to collect another character (that you can't play as to my knowledge, but I haven't beat the game yet) providing a shield that allows you to take an extra hit. The comparisons don't end there as there are two bonus rooms per stage that you have to either kill a set amount of enemies or collect a number of gems (this game's replacement for bananas) under a time limit. However these are not necessary for progression and only exist for completion's sake. I think despite a few minor complains I have with the one of the mask abilities and a handful of issues I had with the level design which is mostly superb, this game has tons of content and is well worth the 20 dollars. Do support this developer as it looks like this might be their first project and if it is then I'd love to see what else they create in the future cause this is easily one of the best 2d platformers out there and I don't think I've seen any games in a DKC style like this in particular. I will be buying the soundtrack also, it's a pretty good listen and gives the game a nice atmosphere. If you like platformers from the 16 bit era this is a must buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not exaggerating when I say that this is one of the best platforming games ever made.  Imagine the original Donkey Kong Country trilogy, but pared down to only the best levels.  You play as a blue rabbit who can use her hair to float (think Dixie Kong.)  You do not have a buddy in a traditional sense, but because of story reasons, your friend is stuck inside of a bracelet that will give you a shield for one hit, which can be regenerated by collecting a heart.You also have four different masks in different levels that give you different abilities.  A bird that allows you to fly and spit projectiles out of your beak, (think Squawks,) a Tiger that allows you to dash horizontally in mid-air and grip onto walls for a short time, a shark that allows you to dive underwater, breath underwater, accelerate underwater, and do a dash that damages enemies underwater, (think DKC Returns/Tropical Freeze swimming,) and a Dragon that turns the game into an instant runner, but you can double-jump and dash downward in mid-air.  This last mask is basically this game's version of mine cart levels.As far as story is concerned, it's fairly simple.  Your friend is taking a walk with you, and you encounter a statue.  Your friend accidentally lets out some collection of spirits, which turns all of the vegetables in the island into giant monsters (most of the enemies are this,) and turning your friend into a sprite in your bracelet.  You have to finish the game by defeating the four biggest, baddest spirits.The only real negatives are that the game is fairly unoriginal, which honestly I don't think of as much of a negative; it's more like this game wears its influences on its sleeve, but if you like DKC, you WILL like this game.  A real, genuine negative is that this game is very short.  I currently have 21 hours, but I've beaten the game 100%, collected all of the collectibles, did all of the bonuses, did all of the special levels, AND gotten a no-hit crown in each level, AND gotten gold times in every level, AND I've gotten every achievement, something I've genuinely never done in a game.  I've wrung as much content as possible from this game, and it's still only about 20 hours.  However, seeing as how this game is only $20, it's unquestionably worth it.  It would be worth $60, to be frank with you.Get this game IMMEDIATELY!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Only just started playing this, and it's extremely evocative of the DKC games, just like most of the reviews here mention. Demanding but fair platformer, where it's easy to screw up but the levels are individually short enough that it's not a hassle to get back to where you were. _childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: It's a retro, old-school style 2D platormer done in the "firm-but-fair" style;  challenging in all the right ways. The level-design and progress system is pitched just right in bite-sized chunks. Go for simple level completion, collect the set amount of gems or go for a speedrun... it's entirely up to you how you play it - you can even unlock a couple of mini-game hidden in each and every level. Universal icons that anyone can understand are used to keep you informed. There are no walls of text, no tedious story, no immersion-breaking loadscreens or cut-scenes to endure. Clean and crisp gameplay and graphics will keep you in the zone! Yeh, this should be in everyone's collection of action platformers. Thumbs-up all the way.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: So if you are into platformers, I highly recommend this game. Overall I think the levels in this game are all really fun levels. There are a couple ones that are alright, but with how short these levels are it isn't an issue at all. I have 100% this game steam achievements and all. I thought it was fairly simple for the most part. The not taking damage and under two hour are probably the hardest ones tbh. But to be honest this isn't the most difficult platformer by any means. It's pretty easy. World 1 is a breeze. World 2 has a couple levels but they aren't crazy. World 3 & 4 have a couple but it's nothing to bad. So if you are looking for a real hard platform you are barking up the wrong tree. But what this game does do well is bosses. Now most people know bosses in platformers are typically garbage or way to easy. Minus the first boss which is way to easy, the other ones provide a nice challenge. I enjoyed fighting them and there is a slight challenge to them, especailly going for no damage. The music in this game is also really solid. Really calming and fits the levels quite well. The best part of this game is it's a really good speed game. There is nothing more fun to me anyways to go on a level and try to get a good time. Really fun to get it faster and faster. A game I'll have to continue and speedrunning. The only thing I see as a flaw is the story isn't there enough which honestly for platforms is something that I don't care about to much and I wish it was just a touch harder, but those are really nitpicks. So I'd rate this game a 9/10.Also shout out to Snowman Gaming. He's the guy that recommended me playing this game after making a video on it. So if you are looking for a platformer to play I'd try this one, especially if you liked the Donkey Kong Country ganes.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: It's play with DKC, but with a bunneh. If you liked DKC, by all mean jump on that game right now!The platforming action is topnotch, Kaze controls super well, the 2d graphics and animation are fantastic, it looks great, the secrets are fun to hunt down...it's a perfect score all around!I wish the game was longer, but it's of a good length as it is. And when that's the only minus i can think of, it's a really good sign! ^^
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: An art style that I feel is heavily inspired by Rayman, the kinetic energy and fast-paced movement of Donkey Kong Country, and a moveset borrowed from other great platformers all combined into one fantastic platformer nets us this amazing game. It has only been out a short while, and I am so glad I did not skip over it in favor or something else when I was looking for a game to buy. The music is fantastic, the story is simple but charming, the artwork and designs are astonishingly well done, and every bit of gameplay feels extremely well polished. This game even has an accessible mode for beginner platformers as well as its normal mode being designed for platforming veterans!On the fence about this one? Don't be. This is game is a treat and well worth the pickup for a handful of hours for a full playthrough, and tons more doing speedruns and no-hit challenges afterward. Definitely an instant win as far as platformers go!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This game reminds me of the Donkey Kong Country series back on the SNES and quite honestly I like everything about that. Gameplay is quite easy to pick up and the first few levels do great to explain how to play the game. Level designs are cleverly done and have rich environments throughout the four islands.However, there are some complaints that I have. The levels where you don the lizard/dragon mask can be quite annoying, especially if you're trying to collect all KAZE letters and bonus gems (Speaking of which, these are placed quite well and you have to keep a very keen eye out for the portals). Story is also a tad on the weak side, especially the confusing back story that you get by collecting the KAZE letters in each level.All in all, if you're a fan of platformer games then I would highly suggest getting this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Polished is the keyword for this title. This is such a polished game, the levels, the pacing, the animations, the art, the music, the characters and the mechanics. Nothing bugs me and leaves me  asking "why did the devs do like this" i understood everything and i felt amazed by it. This game feels like looking at a clockwork, its skillfully made and all the small parts and pieces fit togheter like butter. The devs should pat themselves on the back and immediately go make another Kaze game because i want more!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. Just 100%ed it in about 10 hours. It takes a lot of ideas from DKC 1 and 2 and puts them in a precision platformer. The levels are linear, with secrets being just out of sight of the main path so don't expect DKC 2 or 3 levels of exploration. It has worse exposition methods than DKC, and art that is good, but it lacks character. The world map is somewhat weak, as each world is presented as an island completely divorced from the others and they don't do much to make you feel like this is a world rather than a simple string of levels. All that said, the gameplay is solid and tight. The masks are a cool idea, and they've been implemented pretty well. They offer a lot of variety to the gameplay as their move sets are quite different from one another. The masks are not like animal buddies from DKC. They are not optional, they are basically mandatory powerups that give you different movesets with levels custom tailored for those movesets. So you can think of the masks as different characters which you need to master in order to progress. Each mask gets used enough that the player gets to fully explore and utilize the abilities of each one. My only issue with the implementation was because the movement mode with the tiger mask was so similar to having no mask at all, after switching between them I'd frequently confuse the two movesets and that was a bit annoying. The game did start slow, but got batter as it went on. All in all, very enjoyable game.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing platformer, loved the art style, the catchy music and the absolutely precise controls! Kinda reminded me of Super Mario World and Yoshi's Island 2 for SNES, but with more variety and possibilities. Some levels include pretty interesting "rhythm action" which you can blast through (in some cases after dying a dozen times), but finally completing the level is very rewarding. The level design also is just superb, but I even more loved the design of the enemies (yes, you're facing and fighting vegetables!).It can get pretty hard sometimes, but there's an easier mode included if you're after a more relaxed gameplay. Definitely recommended if you like platformers!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: The devs set out to make something like Donkey Kong Country (maybe specifically 2) and they succeeded.  A lot of the game seems to be designed around doing what the inspiration did, for better or worse. The few things new (or at least new to me, maybe it's from other inspiration) they try work and set it apart. I do wish it was more difficult and was kind of surprised when the end snuck up on me. That said, this is a solid platformer I'd recommend to people looking for a breezy, not-that-difficult time.I hope this serves as a development springboard for a sequel where they try more unique ideas because they did do the base well.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: As an old platformer lover, I have become very picky with my games.I've grown up with Crash, Spyro, Rayman etc. and it's actually pretty rare to find that feeling again.Kaze and the Wild Masks hits all the right cords, and it does it in such a fesh way ! Retro-gaming has become synonymous with being old and thinking "gaming was better before". I don't think so, because games like Kaze offer lots and lots of new things to the plateforming genre, and it's great !From the fluid controls, to the stunning artstyle, everything is charming and works so well.Bonus points for the awesome Sound Track which honnestly gave me the chills on some levels.

_childDocuments_.review: Great straight-forward SNES-Style Platformer. If you played the first two Donkey Kong Country games, you know what to expect. A charming art-style. Short, straight-forward levels, that are designed to be beatable in about 2 minutes (with a time-trial-challenge to put that to the test). Masks, that change the gameplay of the stage for a change of pace. Diverse levels and solid run-and-jump gameplay that doesn't overstay its welcome.Highly recommended if you're in the mood for a simple side-scroller. I wish there was more.(Game-Length: My 100%-Playthrough took less than 8 hours, though I didn't try to go for the "no damage"-challenge on each level)
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful homage to platformers of old, but with it's own style.Controls are tight, and levels are varied to keep you entertained throughout.I put the difficulty at Intermediate for just beating levels, to Expert for 100% them.Overall I have been having a blast with the game, and is definitely worth picking up if you have a platformer itch but don't feel like playing through Donkey Kong Country 2 for the 100th time.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like Donkey Kong Country in the best possible ways. Like a love letter to that series, this game captures all the best elements from the precise platforming to the level variety. The art is colorful and eye catching.  The soundtrack is a joy to listen to as you romp through the levels.Certainly worth the modest asking price and truly deserves recognition and praise,
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a callback to the days of old-school, tough-but-fair precision platforming. While the main inspiration seems to be the Donkey Kong Country it also has elements of Yoshi's Island and even Megaman X. The levels are bite-sized and there aren't that many of them, but as short as it is, it's addictive. Even as frustrating as it can be at times it keeps pulling me back for more. Even when I have access to platforming giants like Crash 4 on this very same PC. The music is nice and relaxing, which is in stark contrast to the aforementioned difficulty. It's almost like it's meant to help keep you calm while you're in a dead panic. The art style pretty basic cartoony, which doesn't bother me in the slightest. I'm not a hundred percent sure what's going on with the story but there's an ancient civilization, mystical artifacts and evil sorcerers. It's definitely worth a look if you've got an itch to play a fresh side-scroller with a lot of life and a lot of challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Wow!What a fantastic game! If you love platformers you have to play this.  It clearly wears its inspirations on sleeve and there isn't much that is "new" here but its a fantastic love letter to old skool platform games.It eases you in, but the difficulty does ramp up pretty fast and there are some really challenging levels later on. A lot of the letters recreated the joy and frustration of Mario World, Special Levels such as Gnarly and Tubular
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This is Donkey Kong Country by way of Kung Fu Panda. Does that sound appealing? What if I told you that basic premise is polished to a mirror sheen: Incredibly expressive pixel art, evocative music, and levels that follow a refined difficulty curve. This was clearly a passion project for a small team, and that sort of thing deserves your support.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Challenging but fun, full of charm, and having that "one-more-level" feeling. Despite failing down or getting hit while trying to get the best possible score, I always felt satisfied and proud of myself for getting each medal and finding new shortcuts.The final boss would be my favourite part. Mixing all titular masks in the fight and finally beating the boss in one good try two times, this is the best feeling I had with game in a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the perfect example of how you don't need to reinvent the wheel or revolutionize the genre to have a successful game. You just need to execute the basics well, and polish polish polish.Kaze does this. The music and sound effects are good but not amazing. The animations are fluid. The character designs are cute. The platforming is clean and simple. The difficulty curve is smooth and in my opinion at least gentle. The story while  bland, is inoffensive and doesn't impose itself too much.The game is 20 dollars (I got it for 18), and I think it's a fair price. 30 would be too much, but I can recommend the game at 20 dollars. While Kaze might ultimately be forgettable, I'd much rather play a game like this than one that over reaches and leaves a bad aftertaste.EDIT: FYI 8.5 hours for me to 100% on original mode. YMMV
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: I am loving this as someone who enjoys retro throwbacks and I was a little worried at first about the difficulty but I have been extremely impressed and delighted by the curve. The level design is impeccable, I especially love the Dragon levels. It's already looking like one of my GOTYs. Kaze's design and the aesthetic alone really appeals in a way I can hardly describe but I am obsessed. This game is Sonic the way Sonic should have been done and a great way to experience Sonic as an adult or even if you just missed out. This game keeps me wanting more.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: If you like DKC and collectathon type of games you'll love this. It's got the level design and aesthetic/music of DKC and the combat reminds me of Crash with the spin attack. There are a few collectibles in each level to get including a crystal that you get in 2 pieces via Sonic esque bonus stages, letters of the main characters name lifted straight from DKC, collecting 100 gems, and time trials so there's plenty of fun stuff to go back and get after you beat the main game. Which is one of my few problems here, the game is very short, for a $20 indie platformer I usually want around 6-8 worlds and about a 4-6 hour single player and I beat this game in a little under 4 hours, but I still want to go back and 100% it sometime so with than included there should be plenty for the money's worth here I just think it would have been cool if there were a little more than 4 worlds. Great game overall though, controls feel smooth and the level design is good, bosses are fun, and the mask mechanic that alters how you play each stage is unique and great to use. This game is kind of a nice mish mash of other classic games in 1 and I recommend it highly, 8/10 from me
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: I still remember when I added this game to my wishlist. It was in 2018 and to be honest, I cannot remember how I learned about it. What drew me in was the art style, how colorful the presentation was and the concept of the masks seemed cool; also for my nostalgia, the copter ears reminded me of Jazz Jackrabbit 2 and it was another plus for that.The gameplay is very fluid, featuring tight and responsive controls. Not once was I feeling cheated when I messed up a jump or platforming section.The masks, as I said, are a cool concept which brings new, fun and engaging ways of playing/finishing the stages. (I have some feedback for this, down below).The stages are cool, fun and colorful. They don't focus on one mechanic, which is great, and thus they bring plenty of challenges to the table - especially in the last world.The characters are very well designed. It's clear that all the sprites (Kaze, enemies, game objects etc.) had a lot of love and care invested in them. Nothing seemed off, weird or of poor quality.The plot fits this kind of game. It's basic and easy to understand, which is told mostly through images and short animations.The SFX are clear, high quality and do their job well bringing the world around you to life.The music is alright. It has the role of being ambiental, rather than action inducing, or blood pumping - with small exceptions here and there.Yes, you will find lots of fun in this game, well worth your money. This is a quality product which delivers a smooth and challenging experience (or casual - the option is there).I encountered only a couple minor bugs during the whole game, like being stuck right besides the banana cannon after being hit, which happened under a very specific situation out of my control, which couldn't be replicated when I tried on my own. Other than that, this is a polished game (yeah, hard to believe in 2021).If anyone from the game's team is reading this, these are my 2 cents of what can be improved or added.1. The masks can be taken to a new level by having stages with multiple paths, which feature a type of mask (or more?) - thus bringing more variety and verticality to the game. Or only 1 path, which can be crossed with all the masks, but with which mask? Up to the player.2. Boss rush mode.3. A "New Game+" mode, if possible. The early stages can be harder, with a different design maybe - more traps, pits, enemies etc.4. This is gimmicky, but an in-game option to toggle between Xbox and PS4 button overlays would be neat.5. A skip intro option.Hope this review sheds some light for newcomers or people that were on the fence buying this title!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Everyone's been pointing out the similarities to DKC, and I have to agree - as a fan of that game, I can tell you in some cases which levels from DKC inspired certain boards in Kaze - but I've been having a great time, the momentum based platforming feels good, and the levels provide a satisfying challenge without overstaying their welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge platformer fan, so this was an obvious fit for me, but I'm enjoying it even more than I thought I would. The controls are great, with sharp response times and simple controls. There isn't as much enemy variety as you might expect, but there are a lot of neat little mechanics that are introduced (including some auto-runner sections that are really great) and the level design ramps up perfectly in difficulty. I'm about 60% done with the game right now, so it'll probably be ten or twelve hours to get a full 100%, which I think is a great length. Overall, really recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game and I'm so glad it exists for people who missed out on the majesty of Donkey Kong Country games and various other 90's platformers like Kid Chameleon. I'm happy to report this game belongs in the top tier of its genre, excelling in level design, art direction, memorable set pieces, tight controls, excellent music, the whole damn experience. Once I picked it up, I just could not put it down and I could immediately tell this is the sort of game that was made for me. It's challenging but fair, the secrets are hidden well enough without being obtuse, the masks are all fun to use in their unique ways. I can't say enough good things about this game. Probably the only issue I had was with the final boss fight being kind of tedious compared to the relatively quick bosses that came before it, but it's supposed to be "epic" and use everything you've learned up to this point, so I'll give it a pass.9.5/10, Just a truly fantastic platformer and I can't wait to see what this team makes next.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: My very first review here on steam and why? Because I think this game deserves it. Basically this game is Donkey Kong Country. It's not just inspired by it. It basically is Donkey Kong Country but with a rabbit - and a lot of angry vegetables.But in my opinion it's copying it so well, that it doesn't need to hide it, where it is coming from. Maybe it's not just that on point as its idol, but it is still a very, very well done platformer with a lot of fun level setups. It doesn't do anything new. Every gameplay mechanic you will find here was already used in a ton of platformer before that as well but it is doing it in such a thoughtful and fun way, that it is still one of the most enjoyable platformer you will find here on Steam. Especially for speedrunners! I bet this will be one of the best gems at the next GDQs.Kudos to the developer especially if you consider that you are such a small team. Nintendo probably couldn't do it better under these circumstances!The only thing which I did not like is the playtime. In my opinion it's a bit too short and I was hoping for more interesting and challenging bonus stages as a reward for collecting all the stuff in the levels.

_childDocuments_.review: Really good platformer inspired by the Donkey Kong Country series while giving it a lot of it's own personality and mechanics to make it it's own game, had a blast playing through this game, while my expectations weren't particularly high this game blew me away and it's probably one of my favorite games I have ever played, it also features some of the best swiming controls I have ever tried.Definitely recommended if you're a fan of platformers, this is a must play for sure!

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Rayman Origins and donkey Kong Country, this is a great game. The controls are smooth and responsive, the levels are creative and both difficult and not frustrating, and the game looks pretty and cute. It's not that long, I 100%ed it in under 9 hours, but i think it is definitely worth its price. Don't go in expecting much of a story, as while it is there, there's no dialog to fully explain everything, and I'd probably say that's my biggest problem... but it's a very small problem that didn't really distract from my enjoyment.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Style feels Rayman-like with whacky vegetable enemies.Stages are beautiful, varied and extremely detailed, while still staying readable when your character is in fast paced action flow mode.Gameplay is strongly inspired by Donkey Kong Country (minus the barrel mechanics), but has its own charming quirks.Difficulty is demanding, but always fair so far.Obviously a lot of love was put into this game, it is an easy recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: This game tries to tribute classic 90's platformers and especially Donkey Kong. I loved Donkey Kong as one of my favorite SNES games and also one of my best-of-all-time games.This game does the job, it's really fun to play and you get that nostalgic feeling.Played the Alpha/Beta a few times and bought it on day one and there's really nothing to regret.Get this game, they deserve your money :-)
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome precision platformer! The art is incredibly cozy, and the playstyle is just awesome. You get rewarded for both being curious and exploring the levels, and also for memorizing the map and also for having lightning quick reflexes! An incredible game that's worth the price and the time investment!!Platformer is by far the most clogged genre on steam, with at least a new platformer coming out every single day, but this one is actually awesome! You have very unique biomes, enemies, bosses, and forms!The story is told without any words and it works. The main protagonist, Kaze, is quite memorable, partly because you get to see her name every level.All in all, it's the most satisfying game I've bought in 2021!
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: With the original Donkey Kong Country trilogy on the Super Nintendo (specifically DKC2) being my favorite games of all time, I have waited a long time for a game to deliver that same type of game play.  This game is exactly what I have been waiting for.  The atmosphere, level design, and especially the controls were hitting all the right notes for me all the way through. The levels last for just the right amount of time, never overstaying their welcome.  I am so glad to see an indie game studio understand what made the original DKC games great for more than just the graphical fidelity.  I am very happy that the final product did not disappoint and would highly recommend this game to any 2-D platformer enthusiasts.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: Old school platformer.  Feels a lot like Donkey Kong Country even down to the levels being designed for speed runs so everything is timed for never letting go of right.  The graphics are really nice although the animated cutscenes make me wish the game used hand animated sprites instead of pixel.I really only have two small complaints:1) The music is a little lacking.  It's not bad, but I'm not in a rush to buy the OST.2) This is purely a personal pet peeve of mine but I can't stand rotating pixels.  If you're going to make a pixel game then you really need to upscale render your textures and use pixel snapping.  Rotating pixels always make me think of Flash animations and look cheap.
_childDocuments_.name: Kaze and the Wild Masks

_childDocuments_.review: (Note:- I have not completed this game yet so the review will  change at some point.)This game is beautifully handcrafted, and you can see the level of detail that has gone into this game.This is a definite must have for all those whom adore the 2D platformer styled game playWhen i played the demo teaser a while back the first things that sprung to my mind apart from nostalgia overload is how much it reminded me of my childhood favourite game Sparkster for the SNES or Rocket Knight depending where you are from :P and this is not a bad thing at all. It takes Elements and inspiration and owns every aspect of the 2D platform genre and owns the stage in being original and its own thingStory: The story is a simply story line nothing to extravagant which is certainly a nice call back to the games from the 90's and is a nice yet welcomed change of paceGraphics: Gorgeously crafted 2D sprite graphics and brightly colouredSize: This is quite a big game for the amount you are paying 30 levels + 4 Boss fights + 60 Bonus levels and then not to mention the dreaded time trials x_x but really good fun Difficulty: each level varies but this game starts nice and easy to get you used to the controls and then gets difficult very quickly and sometimes frustrating. Some of you may have no troubles from the get go, but from my own personal play through I have died quite a lot (Not for the faint hearted especially if you are not into the rage aspect of games)Pros:-Huge variety of levels and extras to keep you entertained Challenging Controls are snappy and very responsive (played with both keyboard and controller) although will say I my personal preference is playing with controllerCons:- Music will get annoying very quickly especially if you die a lot like I did xD (This is only cons really because of me not the game itself) The music is actually really well done.first two bosses are easy but like all boss battles once you learn their pattern it will be a breeze (Will update when I progress further through the game)For the price that this game is being sold at, I feel that this game is worth every penny and more I would say, and I honestly cannot wait to see where the game Developers go from here :)

name: Dolmen
detailed_description: Dolmen casts players onto a hostile alien world known as Revion Prime. Your job? Bring back samples of a crystal with particularly unique properties; the so-called 'Dolmen'. These crystals are capable of allowing interaction between realities, revolutionising space exploration and changing the known world forever. DYNAMIC COMBAT In Dolmen you will grow stronger with each battle! Experience a rich combat system with various weapons and moves at your disposal. Switch natively between melee and ranged combat to overcome the most challenging enemies Revion Prime has to offer. ENERGY MODE Energy management is key to victory in Dolmen. Energy is not only used for ranged weapons, but also for activating 'Energy Mode'. 'Energy Mode' imbues your melee weapons with elemental status effects, letting you take full advantage of your enemy's weaknesses. DISCOVER A MYSTERIOUS PLANET A devastated, darkly beautiful world is waiting to be explored. Will you find all the secrets that Revion Prime has to offer? Or will this cruel world push you to the brink of death? A CHALLENGE AWAITS Surviving is the last thing this world wants you to do. Will you see your timeline erased or will you overcome the challenge that awaits you? ENCOUNTER GRUESOME BOSSES Revion Prime offers a plethora of gruesome monstrosities that will put your skills to the test.
