_childDocuments_.review: A really nice one ! Platform without punishment, exploration with a markable map, XP and levelling up without the necessity of farming ennemies, puzzles to solve later when the understanding of the game mechanics gets better."Batbarian: Testament of the Primordials" is a spooky and groovy dive into a world full of fun and deconstruction of the myth of heroes and explorers, with its fair amount of plot twists. The difficulty is really progressive, you won't die easily, you'll get plenty of checkpoints and campfires to recover. You can play 10 minutes or 5 hours a day with the same enjoyment. The variety of ennemies is stunning, with them reacting differently wether they get approached, hit, and even hit harder as your character gets stronger. Even if the first boss seems like a classical one, what is next is very inventive, exploring other notions of what a level boss should look like.And the bat is not just a permanent companion for your charcacter, and your main tool to progress, it's the real hero there ! _childDocuments_.review: Batbarian is a delightful and rewarding pixel-art action platformer! It really brings me back to the golden age of the Metroidvania genre, while adding some modern gameplay mechanics and an engaging story. The environment art, character designs, and animations are crisp and beautiful, and you instantly feel it was made by passionate gamers who knew exactly what they wanted to create. Batbarian is brimming with witty humor and has an awesome soundtrack that will have you humming to yourself without even realizing it. In terms of difficulty, the game is tough and you will die a fair amount, but once you get the hang of the controls and timing it is super fun. Also, the dev added some assist options to make it a bit easier if needed.Overall, I'd say Batbarian is a fresh take on a beloved genre that stands up to many of the classics. I have a smile every time I play.

_childDocuments_.review: Really good game, does a lot of good things, got a bit long towards the end, but still very fun. Play the demo, it will give you a good idea if you will like the game.This game is a fun homage to Conan the Barbarian and the Sword and Sorcery fantasy genre from pulp novels of the 20's-60's. It has a good sense of humor that's not overbearing, and good puzzle-based gameplay, combat, and tough but fun boss fights. This game is the first non-RPG I've played in a while that feels like a proper dungeon crawl.The heart of the game are the puzzles. They are usually solved with a bag of rocks and various fruits that will have your bat companion fly towards or attack certain spots. Your bat starts off glowing light, which can stun certain enemies and light crystals. If you throw a berry, she will fly towards it and eat it, lighting distant crystals. Later you can also unlock fure and freezing powers for her as well. These are the only unlockable abilities in the game. There isn't an emphasis on backtracking as there are in other Metroidvanias, which is good because backtracking is a bit tedious in this game (more on that later.) There's a good variety to the puzzles and they provide a good challenge. Some can be really frustrating, and there are some trap rooms where I ended up just tanking my way through because I got frustrated with the precision needed to beat it "properly." But they're usually pretty clever and rewarding.The pacing is a lot slower than a lot of Metroidvanias. As the emphasis is on solving the various button and lever puzzles or platforming challenges in almost every room, traversal takes a while, even when backtracking. Compared to something like Hollow Knight where you can cross an entire biome in minutes, Batbarian can drag a bit. Sometimes you still need to hit switches, light crystals, or freeze clouds to get through a room you've already solved. It's just a bit clunky and tedious compared to other games.Story, art, and music are all great. Like I said, it's funny without screaming jokes in your face every 30 seconds.Although I did enjoy the game, I didn't finish it. The careful exploration room by room gets old. Without wishing to spoil too much, there is a moment near the end where you think you might be none but the game turns out to be longer. I player a little bit beyond that point, but I eventually got frustrated with running into yet another room full of traps and puzzles. I really like this game but wish it was about 15 hours long.Still very glad I picked it up when it first came out. Great game, and be sure to play the demo. If you like that, you'll like the game.

Explore hundreds of secret-filled rooms, fight big bosses, gather companions for your party and use the powers of Pip -your bat buddy- to solve puzzles and escape the eldritch abyss.

_childDocuments_.review: There are likely support groups for those personally victimised by geese out in the real world but with recent events, the ever-present threat of vicious waterfowl has all but fallen out of public consciousness. Untitled Goose Game is one of those rare golden eggs which crop up from time to time and gives the player the opportunity to fashion a feathery comeback.For those who have been sleeping under a rock for the past year, Untitled Goose Game gleefully burst onto the scene in September 2019 after a year of social media hype, with a PS4 and Xbox One release later in December. Initially an Epic store exclusive, Steam users are finally able to get their beaks into it as the release coincides with a nifty little local multiplayer update, but more on that later.The concept is simple, you are a horrible little goose out to terrorise a quaint British village in as many ways as possible. From the relatively simple act of dumping gardening tools into the local pond, to the complete victimisation of a particularly nervous and bespectacled young idiot, there are countless opportunities to cause mischief. A to-do list provides some necessary direction and completing tasks on the list allows progression through the linear level system, unlocking new areas to go and cause trouble in. And as far as gameplay goes, Untitled Goose Game is pretty straightforward. Your orange and white feathered menace has their versatile beak and raspy honk to use whatever objects can be found lying around, in order to achieve as much mayhem as possible. Sending villagers on —quite literally— a wild goose chase. Thinking outside of the box will often tick off secret objectives and unlock achievements, of which there are plenty.The graphics are simple, but that all adds to its charm. The most amazing thing about this game is in the detail. From the sounds your evil avian makes as he flip-flops his way across different surfaces, to the echoes that honk back at you from a well. The attention to the small things makes this game feel polished and solid. That’s not to say there aren’t small glitches, which is to be expected from a physics puzzle game, but they aren’t intrusive and end up being a barely noticeable hiccup in what would otherwise be an excellently developed game. The soundtrack is simple yet masterfully scored, making use of classical piano compositions from Debussy which dynamically change in mood and pace depending on the situation. It unobtrusively sits in the background providing flourish and support to the rest of the game.With the latest update, the game takes on the moniker of Untitled Geese Game allowing a second player to get in on the action locally. This opens up a ton of opportunity for collaborative scheming, and when working together seems too friendly, you can always make things difficult for your partner. You are, after all, a feathery menace to society. As an added bonus, the Steam version supports Remote Play Together, removing the requirement to be  sat next to your player two.From the first  to the last, House House have packed a ton of fun into a relatively lightweight game. The price of £15 may send some gamers into a bit of a flap as Untitled Goose Game sits in the higher price bracket for a year-old casual game, but the current introductory discount reduces it to just £11 which is more than reasonable. That said, this reviewer originally bought the game on the Switch last year and loved every second and having just purchased the Steam version, remote play with distant family is now possible. A welcome distraction in the current climate for little more than the cost of a couple of coffees.Overall, this game is definitely worth a gander. Because after all, who wouldn’t want to be a horrible little goose? 🦢

_childDocuments_.review: is an entertaining game that revolves around a goose terrorizing innocent civilians. Every couple years we get an indie gem like Goose Game that completely blows up out of nowhere, and I look forward to finding the next! It is a short experience that prioritizes player experimentation and never outstayed its welcome. This will be a shorter review as the game is short and relatively simple in itself, short and sweet (Just like a real goose).→ The gameplay itself is not the most innovative, but that is not the focal point to begin with. It can be simplified as picking up items, interacting with items, moving the goose around, and of course honking. Through your short playthrough of Untitled Goose Game you will be set in five unique areas that all have their own secrets for you to discover. → Once you’re set loose in these areas you will have a sort of ‘to-do list’ to complete. While that may sound like you’re going through the motions and just doing whatever the game is telling you to do, that is not the case. The game will set these absurd tasks like “having a picnic” or “lock the shopkeeper in the garage”. And the fun is not being told what to do, the fun is finding out how you are supposed to go about completing these tasks. This topic flows perfectly into the next section, that is the beauty of player experimentation and how well it is done in Untitled Goose Game.→ This is what makes Untitled Goose Game the gem that it is, the exploration and experimenting to see what outcome you get is an exciting time. You have you the goose and all the perks that come with being a goose (honk!), with that and the environment you are set on a mission of terror. The world here really is your oyster, given a list of vague objectives you are tasked about how you can get these scenarios to occur.→ The situations that occur are charming and unique, no two objectives are the same. This is really the main attribute that makes Untitled Goose Game worthy of a purchase. The game is essentially one big puzzle, and you must help the goose unravel these problems. → The visuals in this game are stylized and further enhance the ‘indie charm’ that is already so prevalent all throughout Untitled Goose Game. Instead of going for hyper-realistic goose 4k textures we get this beautifully cel-shaded art direction. The environments here are like the cartoons you used to watch as a child and being paired by playing as a goose, it does it’s best to bring your inner child.→ The sound direction perfectly compliments almost every aspect in Untitled Goose Game. The gameplay is wacky and cartoony, the art style is charming and cute, and is all tied together by the soundtrack. When you are exploring the town and not up to mischief the music that plays is delightful and happy, when up to no good the soundtrack quickly follows your lead and plays more intense sounds. → Another welcoming surprise is how well the sounds of the environment are. Everything from a retail store door chime to a water sprinkler all have their own appropriate sounds. This really enhances the world to the next level, as interacting with the environment is a major facet in this game. In conclusion Untitled Goose Game is a game that is perfect to play and forget about the stresses of the real world. The game offers a one of a kind experience of playing as a goose with only one thing on his mind, misbehavior. While Untitled Goose Game is an exciting and unique twist on the typical formula games feed us, I am not sure if it is a must play. The content provided is fun on its own, but what you get isn’t really worth full price. I heavily recommend that if you have interest in this game to pick it up on sale to live out your fantasies of being a goose.

_childDocuments_.review: Untitled Goose Game is a stealth puzzle game where you play as a goose whose mission in life is to be an absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.The controls are simple: you can honk, flap your wings, and pick stuff up with your beak. Instead of being open-ended, the game gives you a "to-do list"; most of the game is trying to figure out how to stealthily accomplish each of these tasks. The tasks are rather varied and take some critical thinking to parse out exactly what the game wants you to do.All in all, there are 4 areas which cumulate to roughly 2-3 hours of mainline content. After you reach the credits, extra tasks will be added to the to-do list, which bump up the playtime another couple hours, if you're willing to take them on. Most of the endgame content is pretty bland by comparison (5 of the tasks are to "speedrun" the original tasklist, which I found pretty easy and repetitive), so the main game is where most of the fun is at. I didn't find the playtime to be objectionable, like other reviewers did; a simple comedy game like this doesn't need to overstay its welcome. Having said that, if you're a gamer on a budget who wants something deep and involved for your money, well frankly, I don't know why you're looking at a freaking goose game homie.The game doesn't control well with a mouse + keyboard, so a gamepad is highly recommended. Not a big deal, but this can be annoying in multiplayer if you've only got one controller and want to use keyboard for your other player.The minimalist art fits the premise quite well. It uses classical music (Claude Debussy) for all of its music, and though in some ways I felt like that was "an easy way out" compared to making an original soundtrack, I can't deny that it fit here nicely.Truth be told, there's not much I can be critical about with this one. I got a few chuckles out of it, the premise never got old, and I left feeling pretty satisfied with what it gave me. I was thoroughly entertained, even if it's not the type of game that will stay in my memory for very long. Just a bit of silly fun as a goose.

_childDocuments_.review: ’s premise certainly captures my attention: play as an annoying goose, hell-bent on ruining the lives of normal civilians in a nearby village. Does this unique concept work out in the end? Let’s dive in.- Simplistic graphics that compliment the game’s tone- Almost every object can be interacted and toyed around with- Beautiful orchestral classical music- Non-linear objectives that can be completed in multiple ways- Awkward control scheme when using mouse + keyboard- Buggy AI makes the game frustratingPutting yourself in the shoes (feet?) of the eponymous goose, UGG can be described as a stealth-puzzle game. In each level/area, there will be at least one human NPC roaming around. You’ll be given a To-Do List: a series of tasks (usually annoying the NPC) that you must accomplish to progress to the next place. The difficulty of the task can range from a piece of cake to a pain in the butt. What I like is that the game does not hand-hold you at all. You have to figure out how to solve the tasks all by yourself, which understandably means a lot of trial and error. Most of them involve manipulating the objects around you. The goose can use its beak to grab (heavy ones can only be dragged) any object in the environment. Be careful though, the humans will not like it when you mess around with their stuff. The puzzles presented here are brilliant. I’ve never felt like the game had run out of creativity and become repetitive. This is helped by the NPCs having their unique quirks. For example, one area has a shy little boy that will always run away from you, thus the tasks are designed for you to scare the pants off of him. In another area, there is a burly man that will always shoo you away. Consequently, the tasks offered will encourage you to be stealthier.Unfortunately, UGG’s basic AI can hamper your planning once in a while. For instance, if you begin piling items in one corner, away from the NPC's reach, they will begin spazzing out indefinitely until you attract their attention. Another infuriating case: if one distracted NPC stands in the way of another, they will get pushed back which can ruin your game plan. The control scheme here could also use a tad more polishing. The default buttons for movement are the arrow keys instead of the more comfortable WASD. I also have to bind two different keys for zooming in/zooming out because the game will not accept mouse wheel scrolls for both of them. A small nitpick, but worth mentioning.The gist of the plot has the goose running amok, annoying the hell out of the villagers just because it can. By the end, the game reveals that there is a reason why the goose targets the place, but the story remains pretty basic. Which is okay, of course. The main selling point of UGG is the fun gameplay, not the story.The game has a feel-good feeling to it though, as I was grinning constantly when playing it. Pranking the poor townspeople even managed to get a laugh out of me now and then. I believe the game's light-hearted tone contributes a lot to this; from the diverse colour palette to the goofy NPCs' behavior, UGG always finds a way to make you smile jovially. I'd also like to highlight the classical music here ( by Claude Debussy, a 19th-century French composer). Every time you are pursued by someone, a piece of this music would accompany it. Surprisingly, this inclusion works wonderfully, as it makes me feel like I am in a cartoon chase scene straight out of a Looney Tunes' episode.  It took me around nine hours to complete the game twice, accomplishing every task and getting every achievement.  Good amount. UGG is a great stress-reliever whenever you feel tired or bored. The non-linear gameplay helps a ton. 25 of them. Most of them are acquired by simply playing the game. The ones that are slightly challenging are probably the 'Quickly' set of achievements, which are explained in the next part.Bizarre title aside, UGG is a fun comedy game that just wants to make you laugh. It did not overstay its welcome and the puzzles are cleverly designed. Some aspects could use more polishing, but the overall product remains enjoyable. It is the perfect game to unleash that chaotic evil in you. All in all, I recommend Untitled Goose Game.

_childDocuments_.review: I came into this game with very little expectations gameplay wise. From the few trailers that I saw, I thought that the game seemed to have a unique style, but I never thought it would be something that I would enjoy. However, when I began to play the game, I was pleasantly surprised.Untitled Goose Game is a fantastically structured puzzle game, charming in its nature and creative in this style. As soon as I started walking around as the goose in the first level, I immediately fell in love with this game. If you are looking for an intense game with a high level of difficulty, this isn’t the game for you because this game is very relaxed and humorous.Weirdly, the aspect that stood out to me the most about this game is how perfectly it makes you feel like a goose. There were a number of moment where I found myself genuinely laughing and having fun playing as this goose as it terrorizes this town for its own pleasure. From the tasks that the game gives you, to the way the NPC’s react to your presence, the game does a really good job of putting you into the mind of this mischievous bird. Additionally, the soundtrack of this game is really excellent. Instead of having a set score play over the duration of the game, the music changes depending on what situation you are in. For example, when you are gently gliding down a canal, the piano score is peaceful and subtle. Alternatively, when you are being chased by an angry ground’s keeper, the music becomes more sporadic and spontaneous. The result is that the atmosphere of the game is consistent to the actions of the player, which further immerses you in the game. Every aspect of this game contributes to forming a fun and entertaining experience for the player. Despite its short length (with the initial game being about 5 hours), it still feels like it reaches its full potential and explores a vast range of creativity within its level designs. There are so many memorable moments in this game, and it was an absolute pleasure for myself to experience. I would definitely recommend this game to other people, and I think it is something that everyone should try.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a delightful little puzzle game. You play the part of a goose, tasked with a list of mischief to perform. Steal the gardener's keys! Steal the little boy's eyeglasses, and then get him to find and put on a different pair that you've stolen from a shop. Steal a man's slippers off his feet as he reads his newspaper. Sneak into a TV shop and cause a commotion. Trap the shopkeeper in a garage. Honk at people right as they're in the middle of doing something delicate. Gather a list of items to make a picnic for yourself before people come to retrieve them.There's no score, no dying, no health bar, no dialogue. Nothing but you the (genderless) goose (who can honk, flap, and waddle), the hapless townspeople just trying to go about their business, and a neighborhood full of small items to pilfer and play with. The challenge is in figuring out how to get the people into a situation where you can take things from them - and then how you can evade them so you can keep your loot. Stealth and patience are the path to success here as you waddle around trying (usually, at least) to avoid being noticed. The action is punctuated by piano doodling, sounding like an episode of Mr. Rogers' Neighborhood.The main game, consisting of just four areas, can easily be completed in around two hours or less. Doing so will unlock more lists of mischief which require you to mix items between the areas and get the characters from different areas to interact, and there are also achievements for completing an area within a time limit. I can understand the complaint that $20 is too much for so little content, but the unlocked lists give it some replay value. It also supports cooperative two player mode; a friend can join you locally, or online with Steam Remote Play without having to own their own copy of the game (though when I tried this we had problems with lag). The game doesn't let the two geese wander very far away from each other, so it helps for both to work on one task at a time.It's a testament to Untitled Goose Game's simple game mechanics that some people on YouTube have decided to go find what additional mischief they can get into, beyond what's asked by the lists - such as painstakingly stealing every item in the game and dropping it into the lake. You'll get no credit or achievements for this, only the sense of satisfaction that someone, in some video game universe out there, is probably putting up more signs with a picture of a goose in a circle with a line through it.

_childDocuments_.review: You're a goose(or two geese if playing co-op) that run around and attempt to complete tasks with the primary goal of annoying the townspeople.  You are able to move about rather freely and interact with a variety of objects, many of which aren't necessary for you to complete your tasks, they're just there for fun.  It's innocent mischief, without violence or hurting people, nor do the people hurt you.  It's a nice semi-casual game that you can just explore and tinker with to see the townspeople's reactions.  The game has a pretty laid back feeling and has a calm, soothing piano soundtrack.You will spend a few hours completing this game.  Maybe 5 hours?  You could technically beat the game in under an hour but that would be a speed run if you already know how to complete the tasks.The game isn't too hard.  My 4 year old could handle the controls.  Granted, she needed my help figuring out the tasks, but she could perform them with instruction from me.The achievements are a nice balance between obtainable and challenging.  Don't worry about the mystery achievements until after you've completed the game.  Once you complete the game, the mystery achievements are unveiled and it's more obvious what you need to do for them.  In the end I was able to get all achievements without any outside help or internet searches.It's good as a "first game" for a 3 to 4 year old.  My daughter loves the game.  Although it can be a test of patience if youre playing together with a very young child.  All my daughter wants to do is run around and manipulate random objects, which is fine and many times I let her take the lead in just doing random things.  However, keep in mind both geese must stay in relatively close proximity to each other so if you both want to go and do two different things the game becomes a stalemate.  If you want to complete the game make sure your kid is old enough to have any interest in completing the tasks with you, hah!  I had to play some of parts of the game solo when my daughter wasn't around so that I could get the tasks done, opening up other areas for us to explore.There's a small amount of replayability for this one.  For me, once I got all the achievements I was done.  You've definitely seen everything the game can do at that point.  However, my daughter seemed to enjoy just running around and playing with the various objects, dumping them in the lake or making the townspeople chase her.  That's where a lot of the additional hours I put into the game came from.I didn't encounter any bugs when I played it.It was fun for both me and my daughter.  It's not too long but well worth the $10 I paid for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Untitled Goose Game is a game that gives you the full promise of its premise:  you're a goose, and your job is to that's it. . But how you go about making everybody miserable (but in a funny way) is what makes the game so much fun and hilarious. In fact, this might be one of the most original games I've played in a long time. I mean, what other game has a dedicated HONK button? Hold up, before I start showering the game with unbridled praise, it'd probably be best if I got my biggest problem out of the way (and it is kind of a deal breaker): . I beat the entire thing -including every single achievement- in about ten hours, in less than a week of owning it. I mean, the game very well knows this; as some of the achievements are basically “complete this level in six minutes or less”, and seeing how there's only five levels, it doesn't take a genius to put together and realize the game itself is saying you can beat the main campaign in less than half an hour. And all this for the price of $20?  I'd recommend waiting for a sale.Welcome to the town of... uhm... . guess it doesn't have a name. anyway, it's a lovely little place with a population of three hundred or so. It's surrounded by beautiful forests and glades of grass and flowers; the village buildings' simple but stunning architecture is gorgeous; and it's almost like time itself moves slower while you live here. Truly, ... oh, by the way, see that random goose over there? . yep, that's you! and your job is to make this perfect town, err... not perfect. just go out there and ruin everybody's day!  The controls shouldn't be a problem: your feathered friend will follow wherever your mouse cursor is when you left-click, while double clicking will make him run instead of walk. Right clicking next to things will either make you grab it (if it's smaller than you) or drag it (if it's your size or bigger), and right clicking again will drop whatever you're holding. Press the Ctrl key to (*ahem*), press X to spread out your wings, and -here we go!- press space to HONK! anyway, the controls are so simple that my four year old cousin plays this all the time; so surely YOU could wrap your head around all this. The town is a big open world, split into different “levels” like Park, Main Street, and Outdoor Restaurant. You have a To-Do list for each section, and each time you cross off everything on your list, you're allowed to explore the town further. Your jobs range from mild annoyances (steal that toilet paper! honk yeah!) to... (trap that kid in the phone booth! honk yeah!); but no matter what you do, somebody will be made big sad. In an idea similar to , you have to rely on NPCs in the later levels to unintentionally help you out with your tasks. You can only dress up the statue if you give the right accessories and stuff to the artist lady, for instance; and (one of) the only way to get into the pub is to hide in a box and wait for someone to unsuspectingly take you to the storage room. that's only two of many examples. There are also twenty or so special assignments on your list (that includes those time trials I mentioned before), and these can be a bit tricky. These extra jobs range from things like sailing a toy boat under a bridge, picking a bouquet of flowers, or . what the honk, goose? There was a particularly annoying part where you had to kick a soccer ball into a goal, but the goal was super far away AND on an uphill slope, so the ball always rolled away. I probably (*ahem*) should've called. anyway, Goose Game is one of those “easy to learn, difficult to master” kinds of games, but even the word “difficult” might be too much. “easy to learn, slightly less easy to master” would be more accurate.         When it comes to production value, it's honestly impressive how Goose Game can do so much with so little. Visually, this game looks fantastic. The bright, cartoony, and rather limited color palette really makes the graphics pop; and combined with some solid (but simple) 3D and a (*ahem*)  perspective, you'll be charmed in no time. Every person you meet shows tons on personality, despite having the most simplistic body features and very little voice acting (the goose is the only character with eyes and a mouth in the entire game); like how the shopkeeper is quick to anger and tries to chase you with a broom, or how the fancy man just wants to drink a cup of tea and read the paper, or how the groundskeeper is busy trying to pick vegetables. ordinary people trying to do ordinary things?  go ruin it for everyone, Goose!! The game has a massive variety of items you can find; slippers, candles, knives, toy cars, walkie-talkies, harmonicas, and cabbage just to name a few (THAT'S what's wrong with video games today: ). And if you don't feel like stealing stuff, you could always just waddle up to people and go HONK to see how they react. The game's soundtrack is also incredible: the only instrument is piano, but it's so energetic and zany; and the music fits so well with the action, that it's almost as if someone is watching the screen and playing the piano in real time. All of this adds up to a game with practically unlimited comedic potential; kind of feels like a classic kids cartoon forgotten by time, but then was rediscovered when everybody realized just how great and timeless the show really was. kinda gives me a fuzzy feeling, to be honest.Aside from being extremely short, Goose Game has a couple of other issues I want to point out. none of them are crazy bad, but they still bothered me. For one, you're a goose. Geese have wings and can fly and stuff, right? But, for some reason, our pal Goose doesn't know how to fly!! worthless!!... on a more serious note, the wings aren't really used in the game at all. The spreading wings feature just feels tacked on, like “geese have wings, so Goose needs to have wings!!”, but you're only asked to use the feature once during the game, and throughout my playtime I honestly almost forgot it was a thing. Another thing, if you're being chased by somebody, and you're pushed into a wall, the result looks a bit awkward; both visually and playability. The person and the goose kind of glitch and clip into each other for a few seconds before the game irons it out. It's like the game didn't know what to do or something. Finally, and this might actually be a bigger issue than the playtime,  like, what a missed opportunity!...no, that is straight up CRIMINAL!!I'm just about to wrap up, but while I still have your utmost attention, let me talk about something entirely different: . We, as people, should all strive to be more like Goose. Look at him: he doesn't judge people by superficial standards. Black or white, male or female, young or old, Goose doesn't care. . and you know what? there's something inspiring about that...wait wait wait, replace hate with love, and THEN that's a nice message. nailed it.Untitled Goose Game is an absolute joy to experience. With its unique premise, hilarious gameplay, attractive cartoon graphics, and a dedicated HONK button, it's a blast; and one of the most addicting games I've played in months. With that said, I can't deny the high price and the short playtime; but you know what? it's still worth it. well, so long... and honk honk HONK!!

_childDocuments_.review: A goose’s honk will trigger a fight or flight response in at least three people I know, freezing them where they stand, their fine neck hairs wispy little soldiers standing at attention, the calculus of escape crunching behind their long, glazed gazes. The story is the same: they were nine, at the lake with their sister and cousin, minding their business. A goose materializes from the hedge and charges, wild wings thunder like strong winds through sheets on a clothesline. Sister knocked down, shirt ripped, hair plucked out in clumps while she screams for help. Dad runs down lakeside, open-hand slaps the goose, grabs its neck, twirls thrice like a decorated discus thrower, and sends it sailing back to the hell it emerged from. The goose is not done, never done. It barrels back stronger. Dad fends it off with bows and backhands until they are up the hill to safety. In dreams, in perpetuity, dead beady black eyes strobe between jabs of an orange beak. God’s special little terrorist. What did we do to deserve this?But let’s rewind a bit, play that terrible tape back again, back to the turn of the 20th century. The Canadian Goose is almost extinct, ravaged by unregulated hunting and Industry’s merciless draining of wetland habitats. Entire goose lineages downed to scattershot ends, starving, searching for a safe place to lay eggs and raise young without the specter of nature’s greatest enemy appearing in a ghillie suit on a fishing boat and leveling death itself at the riverbank, the premonition of greasy goose meat dancing on their lips.Forward a little, conservationists and regulatory bodies acknowledge the horror we’ve wrought just at the brink of annihilation. The damage is done, but the goose is not done, never done. Federally protected, it heals quietly in what refuge it has left. In time, it will thrive again. Peace on the water, goose collectives re-emerge resolute. They will not flinch in the face of death; they will not bow before their hunter.Forward more, back to the lake of that fateful day, three nine-year-olds milling about before the unprovoked attack. What were they doing down by that lake, one with a fifteen-pound rock raised above his head by the hedge, one skipping stones, the little girl staring serenely across the water? The roosting goose knows the visage of destruction, the devastation of its past written into its own fight or flight response. The creature with the power of flight chooses to fight.If you were a goose, what would you call your genocide? What would you call your journey of healing? Untitled Goose Game puts the goose’s greatest tormentor into its webbed feet on a quest for reparations material and immaterial. Through a series of set-piece puzzles, you are tasked with unlocking doors of pastoral civilization using the only tools in your toolbox: a cumbersome waddle, a mighty HONK, and calculated mischief. Steal that farmer’s cabbage and hide his garden keys in the cabbage patch. Tie that snot-nosed kid’s shoelaces together, take his glasses, trip him face-first into a puddle. Steal that shopkeeper’s goods and sell them back to him at a premium. Stand on a grand stage and serenade picnic goers through the ancient majesty of goose song. Peck down the town until it crumbles and take what you came for.You deserve this. They deserve this. Decades of history led to this moment of petty mischief, where we expose the triviality of human civilization and our narcissistic preoccupations, the prioritizing of our creature comforts over all while inviting the annihilation of Earth itself to our doorstep.Set down the gun. Be the goose. Honk it out. Make humans rebuild over and again until we remember how fragile our little existence is. Apocalypse knocking, who will be left? The goose is not done, never done.

_childDocuments_.review: After many years, I finally bought Untitled Goose Game. To be honest, I wanted to wait until all the hype died and then I simply forgot about it.Fast forward to today and the game still holds up.It looks gorgeous and the sound design is fantastic with a lot of attention to details like the surface the goose is on. Story is super vague and it does not really matter. What's important here is to be a menace to everyone in the neighborhood and you do just that. The gameplay mechanics are both good and cute (honk, crouch, flap wings) and the levels are simple but fun.It's a short game that you can beat in two hours and after you do so, the game rewards you with more tasks to do on each level you already finished although I didn't bother. I had enough and I was happy with what I got. I played this on local co-op and it was a really fun experience.So yeah, one could say that the game is too short and that there's not enough content, but I think that if it had had more, I'd have gotten bored after a couple more levels. _childDocuments_.review: Let me fix the title for you: Annoying Goose Game.(That's not an insult on the game, you play as an annoying goose; the entire game is you just harassing people as a goose)---Functionally you just waddle around stealing peoples stuff and honking at them, making a mess of their area and checking off a list of tasks to move from one area to the next. (drop a rake in a lake, etc)Is it fun? Yes, but not for very long. After about an hour I'm kinda done with the whole thing. I enjoyed it but can't say that it improves at all from one list of tasks to the next. If you are good at (very simple) puzzle solving you don't have much more than an hour or two of content here and all of it repetitive.So, where does that leave me? I'd really like to be able to recommend the game. Unfortunately it's way over priced for what's here.What you see in the trailers and screenshots on the store is ultimately most of the game. Steal a few things, honk at some people, laugh as they get upset. Repeat that gameplay loop while finishing off a simple check list of tasks to annoy them and you're done almost as quickly as you started.Notice how the swamp of positive reviews (on day one) are all from people with like 10 minutes of play time with nothing better to say than "honk" ? If spending $20 to honk like a goose is what gets you excited, by all means, buy the game and enjoy.Those types of people could probably also just go stare at a door and bark like a dog and get the same entertainment for free.---Bottom line, this is $2 worth of fun with a $20 price tag. I could probably recommend it at $5 or less, but there's no way I can recommend it at $15 to $20.---EDIT (2 days later) for additional comment: I've now completed the game twice and have about 6 hours put into it. The achievements don't even trigger reliably. I'm still missing the first area achievement (while I have later achievements that would require the first to be done). I don't deny that I had a couple hours of fun, but that just confirms my original value assessment. Good game, bad price. And I feel no incentive to even try playing again until they fix the achievements to trigger reliably since it will just be the same very simple set of puzzles over and over again.---EDIT: I've now forced myself to replay this enough to get the achievements, it's more work than it's worth and stops being fun when so many of them are just doing the same things faster (speedrun) or painstakingly dragging something from one area to another which isn't hard, just tedious and pointlessly time wasting.---

_childDocuments_.review: When I first read about  back in 2019, I admit I was skeptical of its potential. Just how fun could a game about a malicious goose that pesters citizens of an idyllic English village be? Well, as it turns out, it’s a lot. didn’t capture my interest until I learned from watching a Let’s Play video from classical violinist/comedy duo, TwoSet Violin, that the game’s soundtrack features excerpts from Claude Debussy’s . Seeing the unexpected mix of anatine shenanigans and classical music, I knew I had to give this game a chance.Do I feel daft about my initial skepticism!  is a really good game! It’s surprisingly challenging, at times trying, unpredictably funny, and absolutely joyful. The traversable space of the village is divided into five major areas, with each having its own list of mischiefs to tackle. Figuring out how to carry out these shenanigans is the focus of the game.The village may be small, but it’s a well-designed setting for causing plenty of trouble. This makes discovering various ways of misbehaving extra fun. You may even pull off a trick that’s not on your to-do list by chance! As someone who identifies as lawful good, I did find some mischiefs rather mean-spirited and obnoxious. Nonetheless, I must admit that it was amusing and cathartic to play a character that is deliciously and unassumingly chaotic evil.The final task was simply surprising, for it explained the goose’s motivation for embarking on its quest. It’s exciting and nail-biting, and it gave me a great sense of accomplishment when I completed it. Although I still had a few items on my “to-do (as well)” list to cross off by the end of the game, I wished there would be an extra area or two in the village for me to explore.However, as a keyboard and mouse gamer, I found the default keys configuration uncomfortable. Mouse controls weren’t that great as well. Once I’ve remapped the keys so that I control the goose’s movement with WASD, and reassigned keys for zooming in/out, using the beak, and spreading wings to the arrow keys, the controls felt more natural. Or perhaps I could’ve just used my gaming controller. Oh, well.I didn’t bother with the game’s time trials, but I took me about 7 hours to complete all shenanigans. It’s a good length for a game with such a simple, entertaining premise. As for the soundtrack -- the thing that got me interested in the game in the first place -- I love how Debussy’s whimsical and lyrical melodies complemented the in-game events so well.So, don’t be a fool like I was and think little of . It’s a game that convinced me to embrace my inner chaotic evil side, taught me the malice that geese are capable of, and showed me that a goose has just as much star appeal as dogs, cats, ducks, rabbits and racoons.  has since become one of my favourite games, and it just may be one of the most entertaining one you’ll play as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Since my "Not Recommended" rating for "Untitled Goose Game" is based on my personal preference instead of anything intrinsic in the game, I'll start with that.  Simply put, I'm not recommending it because I just don't like games that are filled with fiddly, persnickety, tightly timed activities.  And, that's what this game is.  Now, if you happen to LIKE that kind of game, then this game's for you.  Technically, it's very well done with decent graphics (for what it is).  As long as you remember that you're just a goose whose sole ability is to move things to irritate people (and not a great, all-powerful gamer god), the tasks the game gives you and how they're done are fun and sensible.  And, just watching that goose do things is hilarious.  My only legitimate game complaints are that 1) the game is a bit short (9.8 hours to finish all but the last four (timed) Achievements - so, its list price of almost $20 is too high) and 2) some of the goals you're given aren't well defined (for instance, which character is the "burly man" or where's the "home" you need to take something to?).  Wait for it to go on sale for around $10, and, assuming you don't mind fiddly, timed tasks, then go for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Untitled Goose Game is a pandemic classic. The game was initially teased for the Nintendo Switch, but I held out for the PC release. Design wise, the graphics are charming and cute, with faceless characters that are expressive and visually interesting. I think that the designers nailed the rural, idyllic small town feel of the game. The sound effects are well designed and the music is similarly cute and charming to complement the graphics. Performance was great and likely will be for all but those playing on a Raspberry Pi. The puzzles are not overly challenging yet difficult enough to keep you engaged in the game. I played Untitled Goose Game over three 1 hour sessions with my younger sibling and we had a total blast figuring out the puzzles to complete the tasks. Each "scene" in the game is different enough to be interesting on its own. The movement of the goose is simple to manage and allows for perfect heists and acts of slight-of-hand. The game feels like you are playing through an episode of British children's television, and that is not a complaint. Certainly a fun game for anyone, I would recommend playing with a buddy via couch co-op.

_childDocuments_.review: "Honk!"Doris stuck her head out of the bush they had been sleeping in as the late summer morning sun came over the trees. Not far from where they slept, a boy with glasses was playing with a ball. "Wake up, Pontificus, you lazy ganger!" she honked. "There's  a boy having fun. That just won't do!""Sir Pontificus is awake, m'lady" he honked. For the strapping ganger he was, Pont was mostly a complete loon. They had been mates since she could lay eggs and never did he loose the dapper persona he had when she first met him on the lake. Some part of her was never sure how much of it was real. It did not matter. He was fun... and clever... and mischievous. "For love and seed and honor!"Her reverie was broken as he suddenly sped out of the bush, seemingly instantly reaching top speed, wings flapping wildly while honking the Ride Of The Valkyries.  "Nya-nya nyanyanya nya-nya nyanya nya nyaaaaaa!" "Hey wait for me!" She honked and sped after him. The boy had already started turning to see where the racket was coming from and Doris could see the boy's expression turning from confusion to shock. Shock to terror.  He turned to run. Stumbled. Tripped and landed roughly on the tarmac as Pontificus slammed into him, pecking at his legs. Doris had other ideas. With the boy now on the ground she went for his face. After a few pecks, the boy had already curled into the fetal position. His glasses had come loose and just then an idea came to her. "Pont! Come" she honked, grabbed the glasses in her beak and bolted around the corner. Pont was not far behind when she reached the well. "Sir Pontificus found that exhilirating!" he said as he sidled up to her. She already had the glasses held over the lip of the well. They always did this together. True love. Forever. The glasses dropped with a splosh deep into the water below. "Sir Pontificus suggests we get breakfast." he honked while still staring down at the rapidly sinking glasses. "Yes Pont. Let's go eat."

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I think the game is very charming, I would not buy this game at full price. I bought two copies of the game, one for myself and another for my friend so that we could play multiplayer, but I found out too late that there is no online multiplayer, only local. We played for 5 hours on my friend's copy, hence why my playtime is so low. We completed the main campaign and all but two of the bonus objectives ("score a goal" and "get tossed over the fence"), and didn't bother with any of the time challenges. Minor spoilers below (objects, locations, but not solutions to puzzles).The controls are not very responsive (although that could also be chalked up to being part of the goose simulation), which is why we could not bring ourselves to completing the game even though it is relatively short and enjoyable. Trying to get the goose to go in the right direction (without sprinting, since I am aware sprinting makes turning harder) is downright painful, and makes many of the challenges much more annoying to the player than the NPCs (when the whole point of the game is to cause trouble for the NPCs).I'm also not a fan of how object locations are not saved, because part of the fun my friend and I had made was collecting objects and bringing them back to the bell stash. We had collected all the flowers, all the anti-goose signs (except the chalk sign in the marketplace because that one is not draggable), and many other miscellaneous items from each area before we had to take a break, and upon reloading the save we found our stash was gone. I know this is probably to prevent the player from softlocking themselves out of an objective, but it did lead to us feeling like we were just checking boxes and not actually having an impact on the town. The best part of the mischief is leaving a lasting trail of carnage everywhere you go, and objects resetting destroys that feeling.I also didn't like how there was no splitscreen option for the multiplayer, but rather the two geese cannot be too far from each other. This may be a balancing issue, as being able to have one goose lure an NPC away while the other goose does mischief could make certain puzzles much easier, but still it was really annoying to be trying to sneak around an NPC only to be stuck in place because the other player is too far away. This was especially notable in the pub where the burly man can chase one goose out of the pub and force the two geese far apart, leading to lots of finagling to get the geese together so they can move again.

_childDocuments_.review: You play as a goose who is supposed to terrorise the local townspeople. Sadly however, due to the way that most of their AI works, you are forced into a more stealthy play style (personal pet peeve of mine when gaming, but whatever). You will really learn to hate said townsfolk too, as for the most part they easily outrun you and push you around on contact, which causes you to drop whatever item you're carrying in your beak. Depending on what goal you're trying to achieve, they can also just ♥♥♥♥ you up by standing in a certain spot for a period of time, forcing you to just stand still and wait for them to move on. The area based goals are put on the table as puzzles, but they ultimately come off more as a “learn how to follow the script” type affair. I like puzzles that give you some input to work with so that you can work towards an output, but a lot of these goals don't really give you any input to work with. It's very much a brute force learning experience – once you figure out how to get the gardener to bend over, you can probably figure out how to steal his keys for example – but even then it won't be easy because of how the AI works. You might be able to grab his keys, but getting away from him is another deal altogether.Somehow though, despite the play-style enforcing AI, the real villains of this game are the camera and the keyboard and mouse controls. Hold M1 to move and double click M1 to run? A camera that moves based on NPC location regardless of what goal you're aiming for? ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. I eventually found myself just holding A the whole time to be zoomed out because the close camera (default) was impossible to use. And speedrun based achievements? ight imma head out

_childDocuments_.review: Before I played this game, from what I saw in the videos on the store page, I thought Untitled Goose Game is like Goat Simulator that players just mess around and make pranks to hooman. Turned out it is actually a puzzle-solving game. I do think the tag puzzle needs to be the popular tag as now it is not, just to make things clear.Anyway, puzzles in Untitled Goose Game can be categorized as physical puzzles that require you to perform certain actions to crack them, as the opposite of the “traditional” puzzle that does not have action requirement. You really need some subtle and swift controls to proceed especially if you play alone. However, control of this game feels clumsy. On one hand, I think the dev made control in that way on purpose, just like Resident Evil 4 and 5 in order to make the game more intense. On the other hand, there might be some technical reasons as an indie developer. Such as hitbox is not very accurate, the end of objects can be trapped by some small obstacles etc. But I don’t think they are big issues.What I don’t like is the cumbersome default key biddings. Not sure why but it is completely unlike what PC players get used to. Also, originally developed as a console game, the game does not feel right using keyboard and mouse, although I made it through with mouse and keyboard as I don’t have a controller on my hand. Using a controller is highly recommended.As for the puzzles themselves, I don’t really like how the puzzles are designed to solve. Many of them are explicit, which are fine, but some are just reasonless. I mean, how to solve them doesn’t really have a clear logical connection with our common sense. They are something so unexpected that are just specific in this game. Plus, because there are so many items in one scene, it is hard to even find clues for them. I get that some people like this kind of puzzles for the unexpected solutions, as well as the funny reaction from the hooman NPC, but I will more appreciate logic-based puzzles that do not deviate much from our common sense.The game kind of reminds me of Gris that I think they both look really nice, but the actual experience is not that good. I recommend playing in duo mode and with kids might be an even better idea because I think they will be good audiences of the game, and remember to use controllers.

_childDocuments_.review: Honk honk! Welcome to Untitled Goose Game, where you play as a goose—a mean, scheming, hilarious goose—with one simple mission: ruin everyone’s day in the most delightfully annoying ways possible.Gameplay: Mischief in MotionIn Untitled Goose Game, you’re not just any bird; you’re a havoc-wreaking feathered fiend on a peaceful village. Armed with a checklist of pranks and absolutely no shame, you’ll honk, flap, and waddle your way through a series of delightful tasks, from stealing garden tools to locking a poor kid in a phone booth. Whether you’re dragging a rake into a lake or causing a gardener to faceplant over a well-placed trap, every “objective” feels like gleeful chaos that never gets old.The controls are honkingly simple but surprisingly strategic. Each task requires a mix of timing, cunning, and a deep, goose-like understanding of petty, feathery spite. Your tools of choice? An expertly timed honk, a sneaky waddle, and a fierce beak that can grab just about anything.Graphics and Sound: A Pastoral Prank ParadiseThe visuals? Picture book perfection! The colors are soft and cozy, with simple, hand-drawn characters that are all too easy to mess with. From the gentle blue of a pond to the warm bricks of a pub, it’s all charmingly designed to make your mischief feel oh-so-ironic. Add to that the delightfully subtle music, which swells up with each mischievous move, and you’ve got the perfect setting for goose-driven mayhem.But the real gem is the audio. That honk! It’s the sound of pure, undiluted mischief—both alarming and hilarious. Pair it with the villagers’ bewildered shouts as they chase you down, and you’ve got an audio experience fit for a comedy show.Honk-Worthy HighlightsUntitled Goose Game isn’t just a sandbox of slapstick; it’s a reminder of the power of simple pleasures (like stealing hats and causing general pandemonium). The freedom to creatively mess with the townsfolk is unlimited, and discovering new ways to complete tasks (or just make a mess) will keep you giggling all the way through.VerdictIf you’ve ever dreamed of living your life as a goose, honking and flapping around without a care, Untitled Goose Game is a must. It’s a short game, but each feathered prank is a treasure that’ll leave you laughing and looking over your shoulder for future goose troublemakers.Rating: HONK/10In the end, Untitled Goose Game is pure, feathery joy—a simple reminder that sometimes the best games are just about causing a bit of silly, harmless chaos.

_childDocuments_.review: Untitled Goose Game Review: A Quacking Good TimeIf you’ve ever dreamed of being a chaotic, feathered menace in a quaint English village, then Untitled Goose Game is your dream come true. This delightful indie gem lets you step into the webbed feet of a goose with an insatiable desire to wreak havoc. Who knew that flapping around and stealing people’s stuff could be so entertaining?From the moment you honk your first honk, you’ll feel a sense of purpose. Your mission? Cause as much mayhem as possible while the poor villagers scowl in confusion. Picture this: a peaceful gardener meticulously tending to his flowers, only for you to swoop in and steal his rake, leaving him to chase you around like a scene from a slapstick comedy. It’s pure gold.The graphics are charmingly simple, almost like a children’s storybook come to life. But don’t be fooled—behind that cute exterior lies a goose that takes joy in stealing glasses, turning on sprinklers, and dropping picnic blankets. You’ll find yourself devising elaborate plans, like a feathery mastermind plotting to trap unsuspecting villagers in your web of chaos.The controls are surprisingly intuitive, allowing you to glide through your villainous tasks with the grace of a ballet dancer and the subtlety of a bull in a china shop. But don't get too comfortable; the villagers will fight back! You’ll quickly learn that nothing ruins your day quite like a determined human wielding a broom.As for the soundtrack? Think of it as a delightful accompaniment to your mischief, with jaunty tunes that make you feel like a devious protagonist in a silent film. Every honk feels like a rallying cry for your fellow geese, urging you on in your quest for chaos.In conclusion, Untitled Goose Game is a whimsical reminder that sometimes, being a jerk is just plain fun. So grab your feathers, channel your inner honker, and prepare for some good old-fashioned goose antics. Just remember, what happens in the village stays in the village—unless you leave behind a trail of chaos and stolen goods. In that case, everyone will know it was you. 🦢

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little game, difficult to categorize; Stealth? Puzzle? Perhaps the most similar games would be the Neighbors From Hell series from so long ago. The next closest, oddly enough, would be the Hitman series. The town and its people is a Rube Goldberg machine to be disrupted by you, the annoying goose. Ever since I saw the trailer, I've already guessed that it would be a fun little game. The game feels absurd, in a good way. A few "a-ha" moments, some "wow, they thought of that" moments, and a lot of giggles. And yes, it's a little short, but IMHO making the game longer would overstay its welcome. Controller highly recommended. The default camera focusing may cause motion sickness if you're sensitive (as I am), but you can change it to focus on the goose only, which helps a lot. Not going to comment on exclusivity issues; as it is, with regional pricing and a day-one sale, I think it's worth a purchase. Honk.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a comedic game with surprisingly entertaining tasks for a game where one acts as a mischievous goose. The simple animation doesn't have expressions, and yet the plot line and goals of this goose gives the user the exact smug expression the goose would have if it were human in their mind. Even if it has been played multiple times it can be enjoyed by discovering different ways of doing things and become more time oriented- keeping that urgent feeling of an immediate challenge. Not to mention, the goose is an adorable goofball. Most humans innately find animals to be cute, beautiful, or elegant creatures. This sly jerk is all of them, and it is hilarious. Many smart choices of the developers.

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE untitled goose game. Untitled goose game is set in a small English town. You are a goose who needs to check-off his to-do list. The to-do list will have you doing things like getting the gardener wet, stealing his keys, trap someone in a telephone both, make someone spit out there tea, make a bucket fall on someone's head, breaking the vase, ect. The game is not that big map-wise, but I just love the little town so much! from it's market on the street corner, to the outdoor pub, to it's well. I just love how the game feels so open. On top of that you have the amazing instrumental piano music that gives the game that much more personality! Untitled goose game is also 2-player local co-op, so you and your friend can wreak havoc together! The controls are pretty simple. The only thing I found the slightest hard/frustrating is a couple of the tasks, but every time you complete that one hard one it feels so good! And the few that I did find hard were not impossible nor easy, it gave me just the right amount of challenge. The game itself is not that hard, but if your looking for something too have fun with and goof around, it is PERFECT for that. The controls are simple, but they aren't the best with keyboard and mouse. I suggest using a controller, or getting it on Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 4, or Xbox 1. Also when you "finish" the game you have a couple "to-do also" lists that add some replay ability. Overall I would say that this game is suitable for all ages, and I give this game a 10/10!
_childDocuments_.name: Untitled Goose Game

_childDocuments_.review: Untitled Goose Game is a charming and entertaining experience, perfect for anyone looking for a bit of whimsical fun. The premise is simple: you play as a mischievous goose causing all sorts of playful chaos in a quaint village.While the game is on the shorter side, it makes every moment count with clever puzzles and delightful interactions. The art style and soundtrack add to its quirky charm, making it a memorable experience despite its brief length.If you’re looking for a light-hearted game to brighten your day, Untitled Goose Game is definitely worth a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Untitled Goose Game

_childDocuments_.review: In Untitled Goose Game, you'll explore and use your goose's environment to complete silly tasks all while being a great nuisance to the denizens of a charming, little town.Overall, I loved that the game encourages players to explore and experiment with its sandbox's numerous objects and to study the routines of the townsfolk in order to figure out how to complete tasks and progress forward through the game.Also of note, I played this using an Xbox Controller and I can say that the controls worked perfectly fine and were easy to grasp upon starting the game.So go on and pick up this wonderful treat of a game! And you too can go honk and waddle your way to being the most mischievous goose in town.
_childDocuments_.name: Untitled Goose Game

_childDocuments_.review: Untitled Goose Game is an absolute gem that delivers pure joy from start to finish. Every moment spent as the mischievous goose is a delightful experience filled with laughter and satisfaction. The game’s charming, minimalist art style perfectly complements its whimsical nature, making it a visual treat.The game-play is brilliantly simple yet incredibly engaging. The tasks you undertake as the goose are hilariously creative, from  to . Each objective is a new opportunity for fun and chaos, and the freedom to approach them in various ways (for a better time) adds a layer of replayability.What truly sets this game apart is its humor. The goose’s antics are endlessly amusing, and the reactions of the villagers are priceless. The developers have masterfully captured the essence of being a playful troublemaker, and it’s impossible not to smile as you honk, flap, and waddle your way through the quaint village.The controls are intuitive and responsive, making it easy to immerse yourself in the role of the goose. The sound design is equally impressive, with the goose’s honks and the villagers’ exasperated sighs adding to the overall charm.In short, Untitled Goose Game is a must-play. It’s a unique, heartwarming, and utterly entertaining experience that will leave you grinning from ear to ear. I enjoyed every moment of it and can’t recommend it highly enough!

_childDocuments_.review: I give this game a rank B+ (80-85%)Cool game - definitely worth a try!See my profile for more details about my reviews.Well I am glad I gave this game a chance, years after it came out, when I had forgotten about it - I thought it was a typically pretentious-arty indie game all in the looks and style and not in the content... I was wrong.Instead of explaining why I came back to it, or giving a long review, I will just give back to Caesar what belongs to Caesar: do you guys know SovietWomble? This youtuber/twitcher hilarious man is mostly for his old CS/Arma funny videos (I recommend watching some), but he also has amazing insight on games (The Forest etc). He recently did a short video on this game: if you are ok with spoilers (and if you are not just watch like the first few minutes or so), watch his video, THEN you should know like me if you are intrigued by this game or not. For me, watching the pure joy and fun SovietWomble had while playing this game (admittedly, probably narrating to his chat) was enough to tell me I HAD to try this game too. And I am glad I did! This game is indeed a bit arty but not very pretentious and most of all it is totally meaningful and smart in its design. I LOVED every second of it.Be a naughty, silly, stubborn goose and mess around, discovering dozens of way to annoy people, to do cheeky, nasty tricks with their lives and their belongings... messing around just for fun could be enough for some, but I want more, and I am glad the devs added objectives, which, very ingenuously, unlock the path to the next area once completed! So smart.I am about to finish the game at 100% (my ruined hand won't allow me right now) just to say thank you to the devs, as their game is very witty and well written. The narrative, almost whimsical loop of the whole thing makes it even smarter and laudable. And most of all... that goose is so cheeky and adorable. is  on ,  on ,  on

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to the untitled goose game! Here you can be goose, goose around and don’t give a goose about the goosing problems of everygoose life!  No, you’re not a duck. You’re a goose. And that’s great! This “game” – though more so a simulation of the typical British small-town living circumstances – certainly will bring a smile to your heart and force a “HONK” from your lips. Being the silly bird you are, war is your option over piece by any length and trouble your choice of action when completing your quests. Lock people up, steal their keys, break their glasses and perform for an audience – do whatever a goose has to do!Short answer: No. Long answer: No, it isn’t.Unlike other “be an animal” games, like Goat Simulator, I am Fish or Deer Simulator, this game goes for a more literal understanding of being a goose. It is way less skewed towards the crazy and hyperbolic use of physics, action or extreme control-scheme challenges and much more aimed at a relaxing, but still sometimes intricate gameplay.Untitled Goose Game is a game about completing silly tasks in a fun, friendly setting and finding your way through unique and fun puzzles that are spelled out to you simply through a cutesy To-Do-List style quest-log. But don´t worry, you’re not grinding for useless cosmetic loot, hunting for the next achievement or fiddling with weird RNG to complete a quest. Sometimes you will have to show patience, sometimes it´s more about your motorskills of being a goose and some other times yet again it’s about using your brain to understand what is asked of you. But every task is light-hearted, fun and nicely integrated into the small, but cozy world around you. You’re a goose, you create harmless chaos and terrorize the neighbourhood just enough already. No need to also do backflips, hunt after a timer or raise your wanted level.The game runs very smooth, though the controls take a bit to get used to. While the controls overall are fine, easy to understand and easy to learn, they do feel a bit “unresponsive”, mainly due to the limited turning radius of your goose. But this all works in favour of the game, as you can shorten the turning radius by simply walking instead of running and other issues with the controls are also alleviated by simply playing. One frustrating thing this game sadly doesn’t really address is the way you’re pushed around by aggravated NPCs. While the interactions are wanted and needed for the gameplay to work, there can be instances where they push you into weird corner or where the hitboxes feel odd. There’s also moments where any and all control goes out of the window when your goose enters a brief “escape mode” from being pushed around. It’s generally fine, but can be a bit frustrating to play around with. You can get used to it and trick the NPCs AI into acting in your favour by manipulating their actions and pathing through your position or taking away another object from them, but the less of control never really starts feeling good.Overall though, the controls are good and the game does run even on weak hardware without hickups.This game is not for people who don’t like questing. BUT, there’s also secret tasks to complete, a speed-run mode, extra challenges for those wanting more and a superb local (and Steam-connect online) two-player mode that I can highly recommend.I see this game therefore as a game for couples, those who like to play silly little games, people who simply like to play something calm and on-the-side and those, who simply want to be a goose.It certainly comes highly recommended not just because of the setting, idea and execution, but also the very nice sound design, world design and especially recommended for those, who are into game design as a whole, as I can see this game doing a lot of small things very very good that other games struggle with a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: I recently had the immense pleasure of diving into the quirky world of the "Untitled Goose Game," and let me tell you, it's an absolute gem that will leave you grinning from ear to ear. This delightful masterpiece of mischief and mayhem is a testament to the creativity and wit of game developers. This game lets me channel my inner goose self and love for annoying people and stealing shoes.From the moment you waddle into the shoes (or should I say webbed feet?) of the mischievous goose, you're in for a treat. The game's charming visuals, coupled with its playful soundtrack of different piano notes, set the stage for an adventure that's as heartwarming as it is hilarious. The attention to detail in the game world is astounding; every nook and cranny is filled with opportunities for mischief, and you'll find yourself cackling with glee as you terrorize the unsuspecting villagers.What truly sets the Untitled Goose Game apart is its intuitive gameplay mechanics. Controlling the goose feels natural, and the puzzles are cleverly designed, encouraging you to think outside the box to achieve your feathered objectives. The joy of honking at just the right moment or stealing a villager's hat without them noticing is unparalleled.But beyond its gameplay brilliance, the game's real charm lies in its ability to evoke a genuine sense of happiness and amusement. It's impossible not to crack a smile as you watch the chaos unfold, and the interactions with the villagers are both endearing and comical. The game doesn't take itself too seriously, and that lighthearted approach is infectious.In conclusion, the Untitled Goose Game is a triumph of creativity, offering a joyful and refreshing experience that will leave you feeling elated. Whether you're a seasoned gamer or just looking for a fun way to unwind, this game is an absolute must-play. Prepare to embark on a feathered escapade like no other – one that will leave you laughing, honking, and thoroughly entertained. Bravo to the developers for crafting such a whimsical masterpiece!

_childDocuments_.review: I played through the game co-op with my sister. It was a loooooot of fun to be a couple of sassy geese going around ruining people's day. You can do plenty of things that have nothing to do with anything, which added an interesting element to co-op.The reason I add that it's "frustrating" at times is that the controls were not the smoothest (rounding corners quickly is not easy and we kept getting stuck on things). I wouldn't say that's a deal breaker - we just laughed about it or swore at the screen and moved on. While it can interrupt you from accomplishing a task, it just resets a bit and you can try again. Once you play through the main checklists, new tasks open up to you that bring the different areas together. It's also a different experience playing solo than with a friend, so you could have more than one run-through that way.Overall I definitely recommend! If there's a sequel or if this becomes a series of games, I will definitely be playing more!

_childDocuments_.review: one imagines the untitled goose game to be simple in nature, yet it is far from. as one continues throughout the adventure of this mischievous mallard, they gain a sort of appreciation for its complexities. coming from someone recently engrossing themselves in this journey, i can wholeheartedly back up this claim. whether its your first time through, just completing the core objectives and exploring the four diverse regions, or finding the secret tasks, ones much harder, its clear that untitled goose game is great.typical to many indie games, this treasure was clearly well polished and carefully designed. the way that they designed the game in a way that is obviously 3D, but cleverly put in a perspective of 2D style gameplay was a breath of fresh air from the usual one or the other. untitled goose game as a whole is lovely; the art style: magnificent, the soft piano music: beautiful, the interactions made with the npcs: hilarious at times.my only gripe with the final product is the achievements, more specifically, the "___, quickly" set. to complete these achievements and 100% the game, each area has to have its tasks done in less than seven minutes. for this to happen, you must find a route that allows for quick task-doing, while avoiding the finicky movement of npcs and grab mechanics. even then, it could be imperfect, and the tasks might be done right after the bell strikes. when this happens, its time to restart and try again. this, without a doubt, was the worst experience, especially the back gardens.in summary, the untitled goose simulator is not perfect, it can be at times one of the most frustrating things available on steam, and at others you feel like you are on top of the world. my time playing this was a mix of these things, and i overall had a wonderful time. house house made a masterpiece, but one not everyone can understand.

_childDocuments_.review: Mixing stealth with hilarity with the deep, often ignored, dark human lust for chaos and bullying small children. This game has a surprisingly beautiful ending and tells a charming tale while leaving much up to the players interpretation. It manages to have replayability while still having a good storyline that is satisfying every time. It also has a fun interactive soundtrack that gives cues and clues in game. The game is puzzling enough to be difficult but not impossible. The instructions are clear enough that you know exactly what you need to do, but vague enough you aren't sure how to do it. Each level has at least one difficult problem that you have to think outside the box for, and always you must look around for what to do. The bonus content (extra lists) at the end of the game offer even more replayability, during which I guarantee you will find easter eggs and little things you didn't notice before. The lists often have one clear way to do things, but you can always do it another way, so I strongly recommend looking outside the box for strange ways to do things when replaying, it almost always pays off. The NPC interactions are also something worth hunting for, so 100%ing this game still doesn't get you through all the content. All in all, a true masterpiece of gaming with a fun concept that they pulled of amazingly well. I strongly recommend buying this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Untitled Goose Game is the quirky indie game that AAA studios just can't make anymore. In this game you play as the titular goose running, honking, and flapping your wings through a suburban English village. The game sees you navigate through four scenarios, a garden, a street, two interconnected backyard gardens, and a pub. These four settings are seamlessly connected as you complete a "to-do list" of puzzles and tasks involving collecting or placing props in the interactive environment and having human NPCs react with them in fun and unique ways. One thing that should be noted is this is an extremely short game, about four hours in length, including the hidden "to-do list" and speed-run challenges, but even so I believe it's worth the $20 price tag.
