_childDocuments_.review: I got an advanced copy from the Devs so just saying that upfront. I really like the game, not too many rogue likes out there that give you as many second chances as this one does. The gameplay is simple, you're a parasite and you are weak so you need to hijack enemy bodies to borrow their powers. You go around room by room wiping out enemies and doing typical rogue like stuff but if your host is killed you go back to being a brittle parasite where you only have one life so you have to quickly find a new host. It's enjoyable, has co-op and is available on every major platform. My only complaint is it's a bit slower paced than what you're used with games like Isaac and Gungeon.
_childDocuments_.name: HyperParasite

_childDocuments_.review: I am just a few hours into this game but I love the art style and the gameplay. Each type of character you take over plays in a unique way and has a unique super move that charges slowly. The music for each full area and the cast of characters to unlock is unique which adds a lot of time and challenge to each zone.For improvements I would love to see more money drop so you have a chance to try the shop items, an increase in drop rate for the enemy brain drops so you can unlock them more often, 2-3 music tracks for each zone so that the music never gets repetitive, and at least 1 character type unlocked when you enter a new zone so you have a chance to survive when you lose your prior zone host.I think all of these improvements would help make the game flow better and allow players to progress at a reasonable pace while still getting to experience all of the fun and unique content.

_childDocuments_.review: HyperParasite is a great twinstick shooter and rogue-lite. I also own this game on the Nintendo Switch™, which I have heaps of hours on. It's challenging for sure and using the different characters makes it extra fun. This version is of course far better that the switch and is just fun to keep on playing for ages. _childDocuments_.review: High intensity twin stick action with a pumping synth wave soundtrack to help carry that along. Lots of 80's references that will have you saying "ohhh i know what you're doing there ;)" and a body-snatching mechanic that allows for some crazy action and strategy amidst the chaos. If you're a fan of any of the big hitters such as Enter the Gungeon and Binding of Isaac I would highly recommend you get on the HyperParasite train ASAP
_childDocuments_.name: HyperParasite

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty sweet. Crunchy and fluid, you play a slime who slurps into people and gives the rest of them a lickin'.There's actually quite a bit of content, lots of different enemies to kill or possess and zones to explore.Small objection though: while there's plenty of diversity in terms of the characters you can play as, when you fight thos same characters they feel pretty similar, where they all telegraph an attack and then expect you to get out of the way in more or less the same way.I also don't quite understand the unlock system, it seems like when you enter the zone after the first boss then all the enemies are locked so you have to beat a bunch of rooms without making any mistakes in order to make any progress.
_childDocuments_.name: HyperParasite

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best arcade rougelikes I've ever played. As an microscope hobbyist I love games where you can play as an amoeboid creature and this game does not let you down. The parasite itself is no push over when outside a host, and I particularly like that when you reach new areas it feels like you have to gain a foot hold on the inhabitants. The enemies are awesome as well and as you encounter new ones often time you think wow I really want to be able to control that guy, especially with the bosses so you better goal oriented grinding. Since it is early access there still are some bugs that can be annoying but never really seem to take away my enjoyment of the game at least. I got the game pretty early on and as each subsequent update is released the game just gets better and better.
_childDocuments_.name: HyperParasite

_childDocuments_.review: A bit frustrating a first when you don't have any characters unlocked, but chasing the unlocks is part of the fun.The gunplay is varied since you are constantly switching bodies, from melee characters that jump around to a shotgun to some massive boomerang, it's always about making the best of what you get.
_childDocuments_.name: HyperParasite

_childDocuments_.review: Thats a refund for me.The whole game is about dodging bullets, smashing trash cans for money, and collecting brains to give to some strange shopowner who wants to help you take over the world for some reason. I also don't know why an alien set on destroying the world needs money, but whatever.Not donna lie. I felt like i wanted to keep playing to figure out if there was anything else to the game. But it felt very shallow, and low on content. And i don't think the game has anything other than what i have already seen, to offer.This is what the game offers:1. Every shop has 3-4 glowing orbs to buy, but you won't know what does until you buy them. I guess you get to understand what they do after a few times. And they drop if the host you have infected with your alien dies. So its basically not worth every buying them. Because you also use money to unlock heroes.2. If you want to unlock new charecters you first need to collect the brain of the person, and give it to the shop owner. Then use trashcan dollars to buy them. I don't really get it, but that is how it works. 3. You once in a while collect a puddle of energy on the floor that gives your alien and host 1 of 3 powerups, they don't do you a whole lot of good unless you stack them a bunch. And even then, they don't do a whole lot of good.4. You keep on just going from room to room killing enemies and smashing trashcans.Thats about it. Have fun!
_childDocuments_.name: HyperParasite

_childDocuments_.review: Has potential to be very good, at the moment - it's a bit rough around the edges.You play as a slimey parasite - with 0 HP. One hit, and you're dead as a parasite. The game wants you to take over humans though, and they actually have HP.You can collect powerups throughout levels, and they can either give you an extra life for your parasite form ( so when you die,m you come back ) you can increase Attack stats, or Defense stats - and the stats affect both parasite and host body forms, however; your parasite NEVER GAINS HP - I really think that is a misstep.You start the game out with a few host bodies you can take over, here's the thing : you can't just tale over any body you want - you first have to get a brain drop from them, then bring it to the shop area ( to the left inside the shops ) and then you have to pay a certain amount of money - after you do that, you can take over the host body you unlocked when you find it in the map.here's my major issue with this system - when you get to level 2- there are NO host bodies unlocked, NONE to choose form, so you can't take over a thing when you first enter the place. The first level gives you three basic bodies to use.And, NONE of the enemies you unlocked from the previous level appear in the next one- making all the work you did to unlock them pointless past stage 1, that's a huge kick in the butt if you ask me.The difficulty ramps up insanely as well, and your parasite always dies in a single hit - so frustration is definitely on the menu for this game, be warned.The premise is very cool, the graphical style is unique - and the game is quite fun, but the negatives I pointed out are worth considering before you purchase.The game is still in Early Access, so this could all change at any point.Amoung the standard gameplay here, you can find secret areas ( with requirements to get to them, and certain rewards for doing so ) If you bring a certain host body to the shop, the shopkeep gives you a half-off discount - ( it's represented by a portrait in the left side of the shop ) This discount also applies to the brains being unlocked for your parasite to host.( kinda weird though, as you aren't allowed to buy stuff in the shop if you're a parasite, but the guy is clearly helping you somehow, idk ) I do recommend this game, if you can overlook the balancing issues it has atm, and one more important thing:
_childDocuments_.name: HyperParasite

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a good roguelike, my kinda game but lacks basic video features like changing resolutions or windowed mode which is a deal breaker for me. Even though it is 21:9 supported (in Fullscreen only) the game looks like its running in 1080p instead of 1440p on my Acer X34 monitor and there is no option to change resolutions currently.Refunding this, The game has potential but cant recommend it like this.
_childDocuments_.name: HyperParasite

_childDocuments_.review: After playing through the demo months ago and finally getting my hands on the final build of the game, I can definitely say this is triumph for the team.  HyperParasite is hard as hell.  It a also has a simple premise to it.  As a, alien parasite, attach yourself to a new host body and use their abilities to tackle each area.  It's roguelike bliss.  I always appreciate a developer who can find a fun and unique twist to an oversaturated genre.  Mastering the control scheme can be a bit tricky at first, especially when trying to find a new host body with waves of enemies surrounding you.  Like any rood roguelike, it's easy to adapt to after a couple playthroughs.  The soundtrack is my jam, with dark synth drenching every turn.  HyperParasite has been one more accolade for indie gaming this year, and definitely worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: HyperParasite

_childDocuments_.review: Crashed 6 times within the first 30 minutes, can't go into downtown (crashed 2 out of 2 times here), can't launch game, crashed 3 out of 5 times. Crashed when going into the area before downtown 1 time.Looked fun, was fun to play what was accessible before the unavoidable crashes, would be more fun and I wouldn't refund if it was a functional title.
_childDocuments_.name: HyperParasite

_childDocuments_.review: A great concept presented with awesome pixel art and a fun 80's style soundtrack.Quite challenging, as the game itself will tell you, but the controls are solid - responsive and easy to grasp.It's got that 'die-quick-learn-quick' feel akin to something like Miami Hotline, except this one has a fun dodge mechanic that's quite fun to put to use.Looking out for hosts to invade for new movesets is just great. It's like violent rogue-like Kirby....Also, the animation when you make your hosts explode is just hilarious.Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: HyperParasite

_childDocuments_.review: HyperParasite is one of the best rogue-lites I have played. Playing as multiple characters has never been so satisfying. You are randomly assigned a new body at the start of each run and there isn't one character type where I think "oh damn it".I'm always sceptical of indie games with the "difficult" tag. I've seen that tag thrown onto games with dodgy physics or unresponsive controls. HyperParasite has none of these issues. The game feels very polished and the game is initially hard but also feels very rewarding as you start to master it and unlock different characters. The graphics are clear and attacks are well telegraphed so you don't have many excuses when you die.I've only got as far as the second boss but I don't see myself stopping any time soon. Even though this is an early access game, I would totally recommend it to anyone who is a fan of twin stick shooters and action rogue-lites.
_childDocuments_.name: HyperParasite

_childDocuments_.review: The work here is great and really is one of the best roguelikes out there. You'll love the idea of possessing enemies to take advantage of their skills. Anytime this happens a shot of adrenaline will possess you changing the urgency of the run. The soundtrack is also sublime taking you straight back to the '80s.One of my favorite things about this game is that I keep coming back to play it simply because of the humor and addictive gameplay.Enemy attacks are great. It's easy to appreciate in a short time the difference between them, memorize strengths and weaknesses work out the best approach to take them down. The fun that the game provides you make the unlock mechanics and this makes HyperParasite not boring, but gloriously obsessive!
_childDocuments_.name: HyperParasite

_childDocuments_.review: The sheer amount of small details put into this game is just amazing! They created the perfect 80s atmosphere with all those cameos and references you find around in the game levels, from movie posters to character classes etc., plus the synthwave OST (even if it's incomplete) is top notch!I'm a huge fan of Enter the Gungeon (a title this game is clearly inspired to), I have several hours of game time on it on PlayStation 4, I really wanted to get this game for PS4 but just couldn't wait. I'm enjoying every single bit of it, can't wait for the final version!Keep up the good work!
_childDocuments_.name: HyperParasite

_childDocuments_.review: HyperParasite is a very solid and exquisite looking roguelite (or action roguelike). It differentiates itself from the horde of Binding of Isaac wannabees thanks to a novel mechanic that allows you to possess enemies: you play as a body-snatching alien parasite and while you can also deal damage in that form you're very vulnerable, this means that your main way of survival is jumping from one host to another while learning how all the different enemies work. The low-fi presentation complements beautifully the 80s inspired setting and you'll find many cameos and nods to movies and pop culture of that time. The soundtrack kicks major ass too. Overall this is an incredibly polished game for a very low price.
_childDocuments_.name: HyperParasite

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't had the chance to play very long yet, I just made it to the first boss and then died horribly.Even from the small amount of time played, i can tell that this game is quite challenging and a lot of fun.The ability of taking possession of different type of characters keeps the gameplay very fresh and fun on each run.Overall for being in Early Access, Hyper Parasite is already extremely polished and great to play, and the asking price is quite low for what you get.
_childDocuments_.name: HyperParasite

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, it's incredible how packed with stuff this is! I usually don't play many action games, but when I saw this one is set "in the roaring 80s" I couldn't help but give it a shot and I'm really enjoying it so far. Despite being still in Early Access, I see that the devs will add up to 60 (?!) different character classes, this is just plain crazy. It's also really, really hard, but in a good way! Can't wait to see where they take this.
_childDocuments_.name: HyperParasite

_childDocuments_.review: Happy to get to try this awesome game in early access, my first thoughts were of the awesome colors and detailed levels until i started moving around! Then I realized how unique the players powers were and the effects! It totally surprised me and upstaged the Incredible cyberpunk look. The game generated different levels when you play, and had extensive tutorials to follow so it was easy to get used to. (skip-able)
_childDocuments_.name: HyperParasite

_childDocuments_.review: Relentless rogue-lite shooter/brawler coming soon to a host near you. SNATCH, ZAP and REPEAT your way through a dystopian 1980's as a mysterious organism bent on world domination.
_childDocuments_.name: HyperParasite

name: Phoenix Point
detailed_description: Phoenix Point is the acclaimed strategy game from the creator of X-COM, now with Steam Workshop support! The Earth has been overrun. A mutating, alien menace threatens the last remnants of mankind. Only the Phoenix Project, a secret organization of the best minds and bravest soldiers left on earth, can repel the invasion and reverse the inevitable. The Phoenix Project looks to you for leadership. Research and develop new technologies, explore a ravaged globe, build your bases, manage resources, and dominate the battlefield. Just remember: you're not alone out there. Factions, including the corporatist New Jericho, the indecisive Synedrion, and the fanatical Disciples of Anu, as well as a variety of offshoot subfactions, have their own values, goals, and view of the Pandorans. Work with these factions via Phoenix Point's diplomacy system, use subterfuge to steal what you need from them, or simply crush all around you with military might. No matter what you choose, victory won't be easy. Phoenix Point Features: Tons of Content: Over two years of updates, upgrades, fixes, and new content suggested by our community, including Steam Workshop support for subscribing and enabling mods, tweaking existing mods, and setting up your game the way you want to play. Try our example 'Custom Campaign' mod to set up new unique campaigns. Mutating Alien Menace: Face down an ever-changing alien threat that adapts to your tactics and offers no respite even as your team becomes more powerful and technologically advanced. Uncover the Secrets of the Pandoravirus: Engage with a complex narrative, complete with multiple endings that the player can only uncover via several playthroughs. Explore, research, and discover a secret history, as you learn about the origins of the mutants, the Pandoravirus, and Phoenix Point itself. Manage Diplomatic Relations: The Phoenix Project is not the only organization trying to reclaim the Earth. The militaristic New Jericho, the mystical Disciples of Anu, and the technophiles of Synedrion all offer unique rewards for co-operation and threats for opposition. It is up to you to decide how, or even if, to deal with them. Take Aim on the Battlefield: In addition to equipping and commanding units, Phoenix Point lets you take direct control of your soldier's shots in combat, with a unique free-aiming system. Target enemy weakspots, weapons, or valuables, or just go for center mass. Next-Gen Tech with Classic Pedigree: Phoenix Point was designed by Julian Gollop, the creator of the X-COM series in the 1990s. Integrating the core ethos of X-COM while updating the visuals, technology, and systems to modern standards has made Phoenix Point best-in-class.

short_description: The acclaimed strategy game from the creator of X-COM. Fight tactical battles on procedural maps against a foe that adapts to your tactics. Manage diplomacy and economy on a global scale. Research, explore, overcome. Now includes Steam Workshop support for mods!

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a XCOM fan since the first came out, almost 20 years ago, and this game is very similar to  the last couple of XCOMs (enemy within and enemy unknown).The key difference, in my opinion, is the fact that the planet is split into 3 factions and you need to manage diplomacy between all (you can also steal tech and vehicles from these factions).During gameplay, you are presented once in a while with a sort of RPG choice that will affect your resources and your standing with other factions.As for units and weapons, it's the same recipe as XCOM: You start with standard and research and upgrade your way into some cool weapons and you can recruit from factions faction exclusive units, and you'll be able to upgrade, enhance or mutate your soldiers.It's fun to play, although and lengthy and the opponent's AI keeps trying to adapt. The true ballistic physics is great and you can take charge of the aiming. (that's also new!)The main drawback I find is that the interface needs a bit more work while working with inventory and manufacture, but nothing too serious. My review for this game is a solid 85%
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenix Point

_childDocuments_.review: It's a VERY basic XCOM 2. From all the footage and hype I expected a sleeker, more complex game to be honest, little disappointed, and already the game has crashed once (XCOM 2 hasn't so far after many hours)... Glad I got it in the 50% sale, would not pay full price. Feels like despite Beta and now Year 1, several years of development are needed to bring this up to its potential.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenix Point

_childDocuments_.review: Guys I think we all need to rethink our position on the Epic Exclusive deals. Games are released as unfinished husks nowadays and are not really playable until 2-5 DLC's and feedback from all that free bug testing they get. Not happy that they do this ♥♥♥♥ but its the industry norm now it would seem.So here comes Epic trying to make us use their ♥♥♥♥♥♥ storefront and pay essentially for the game to be released on Steam a year later bug tested and with a decent amount of content.Shouldnt be this way but I find it kind of funny that this probably would have sucked at launch a year ago. If you like Xcom but hate the horrible shooting rng this is the game for you
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenix Point

_childDocuments_.review: A good turn based strategy game, combat is intuitive, tactical, and over all fun. However, the base building and resource management might be a little too complicated as the most difficult part of the game about fairly early on is managing multiple bases, jets, alliances, attacks, soldier health, ammo replenishment, training new soldiers and more. That being said it's still fun. Recommended for more seasoned Tactical players
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenix Point

_childDocuments_.review: You have probably seen reviews spouting about the difficulty and how hard this game is. I've played since launch and THEN the game was hard. The developers have done a great job to bring this game to "normal" difficulty as far as casual gamers are concerned. THIS IS NOT A CASUAL GAME. If you love Xcom 2 or any tactical strategy game, this game is for you. They dont hold your hand, they dont make it easy, and you will feel better for it. Concurring missions and balancing teams is the key to this game. Knowing when to do certain missions or maybe just not, is a big part. This is gonna be an unpopular opinion but SAVE SCUM this game lol. If your an Ironman type of person, this is for you as well. Very indepth game, lots of combinations of classes, deciding which factions so side with and which to steal research from. Great game all around but not the faint of heart.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenix Point

_childDocuments_.review: In the realm of turn-based strategy games, Phoenix Point emerges as a true masterpiece, a creation that breathes new life into the genre. With the guiding hand of the visionary behind X-COM, it presents a narrative steeped in urgency and innovation. The Earth, ravaged by a relentless alien threat, finds itself at the mercy of the Phoenix Project, a beacon of hope amidst despair. As the commander, you are entrusted with the monumental task of leading humanity’s last stand.The depth of Phoenix Point lies not only in its gripping storyline but also in its rich gameplay mechanics. The incorporation of factions adds a layer of complexity, offering players the choice to navigate alliances, engage in diplomacy, or resort to cunning subterfuge. Each faction, from the militaristic New Jericho to the fervent Disciples of Anu, brings its own ethos and challenges, enriching the strategic experience.Moreover, the game’s flexibility is commendable. The Ballistics Model introduces a realistic approach to combat, where each shot matters, while the Disabling Body Parts feature adds a tactical dimension, allowing players to target enemies' vulnerabilities. The Action Point System ensures that every decision carries weight, forcing players to think critically and adapt swiftly.The expansive geoscape serves as a canvas for exploration and resource management, further immersing players in the world of Phoenix Point. This game has quickly ascended to the ranks of my all-time favorites, capturing the essence of strategic warfare in a way that is both engaging and thought-provoking. For those who appreciate a finely crafted tactical experience, Phoenix Point is a journey worth undertaking.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenix Point

_childDocuments_.review: Game is riddled with bugs, enemies getting into the walls, soldiers missing their target because there are obstacles that were unaccounted for. Along with the bugs there are so many QoL issues and lack of polish, missions start getting so repetitive it gets bothersome, saving havens and burning pandoran colonies turn this game into pure grind and you get penalised from not doing every single one of these, it isn't a matter of having soldiers/resources it is all about having the patience to keep doing the same missions 100 times. Enemies are unfun to play against, 80% of them have annoying shields and the variety doesn't really impress me either, guy with a shield but can spit venom is not really variety. Maps are too big sometimes and have you running around for a lot of time. The only saving grace are the technologies and weapons. It just gets too repetitive, most of the time I spent playing was grinding and grinding the very same missions, you are always under pressure to do them again and again. Characters and story aren't really interesting as well, spoilers ahead:The story starts out by introducing the pandoravirus and the creatures that it creates, which is very interesting and honestly it sets the game apart from XCOM, but then they had to come along and introduce aliens to the story. Characters had great potential, you honestly gave us soldiers at the tutorial that could have made a great part in the story and even had unique voicelines, but then they are silent for the rest of the game and if you choose not to take tutorial the game gives random soldiers at the start. Huge potential wasted, the turns out it was aliens all ago ruined the little potential the story had to begin with. I kept trying to finish this game because it always seemed so close, and I didn't want to waste all the grind that I had invested. Final mission had me go against hordes of enemies that respawned and an annoying final boss that kept forcing me to run around to be able to bypass its shields. Seriously, what is it with all the shields in this game? Anyways, boss does constant damage to your soldiers and nothing you can do about that, disabling body parts seemed to do nothing. Shield enemies kept spawning constantly. I just decided to give up and uninstall the game because honestly I was so tired of grinding, the only thing that kept me playing was the huge potential that this game wasted. It is a love and hate relationship but more inclined to the hate side unfortunately.Soldier voicelines are complete wack as well. Some of them are alright but nothing special, but there are some that are battlefield 2042 level of cringe.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenix Point

_childDocuments_.review: It's ok.  The Free AIM is a nice mechanic and the evolving enemies are cool but the rest of the game feels like a poor mans XCOM 2.  The UI can also be a bit cumbersome and the lack of Steam Workshop support is unfortunate.  I found myself enjoying the game but there was always a voice in the back of my head saying "Just reinstall XCOM already".
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenix Point

_childDocuments_.review: This game has plenty of little issues that nagged at me while I played. The progress is mind-numbingly slow, especially when you're just waiting for important story events to occur near the end. Many missions are same-y, with identical environments and limited variance in objectives. Factions are largely one-note, and what nuance they attempt to give them is largely lost with how goofy their personalities are. The story is plain and uninspired. Some enemies bordered on unfair and would kill my units before I had a chance to detect them. The overworld lacked some expected quality of life features. Sometimes enemies would hide in random corners and I'd spend several minutes looking for them after killing everything else. And many, many other things.Why then am I recommending Phoenix Point? Despite all of this, I was having fun.. The depth of the gameplay means there is a lot to master, and almost against my will I found myself thinking about this game all the time, what I could do better, how I would approach a new playthrough on a harder difficulty. I was playing this game in almost all of my free time for a bit, and I'm not sure if that means it's a good game, but it certainly clicked with the part of my brain that likes being good at things. Eventually I made it halfway through a playthrough on the hardest difficulty before deciding I had had enough of the bad RNG and frankly BS difficulty curve and putting the game down for good. And I don't recommend playing on that difficulty -- but the rest was a good time, to my surprise.Would recommend on sale if you're the type that likes X-COM but wishes it were a lot more complicated and perhaps wasn't quite as good.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenix Point

_childDocuments_.review: Great tactical game. A bit more complex than XCOM which is the closest comparison I can make. Some of the interface is a little obtuse and it's a bit difficult to find what you're in certain menus compared to something like XCOM 2, but once you get past the learning curve; there's a lot to like about this game. The difficulty level of this game is significantly higher than that of XCOM 2.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenix Point

_childDocuments_.review: After a relatively frought development period, the end result with Year One edition is great. It's nominally the "deluxe" XCOM experience. The Firaxis remakes dumbed it down, Xenonauts rebuilt it the same, Phoenix Point builds extra systems on top. It's not overcomplex, but there are a lot more subsystems in play. Difficulty is a bit weird at times, you very much go through feast and famine, and the final mission is ridiculously harder than everything preceding it. But I did like the various setpiece battles leading up to that point. Make sure you enable some (but not all) of the DLC to add spice to your playthrough.Also, while allying with all factions is probably a better strategy, I think you'll have more fun if you ally with only one or two.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenix Point

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, if you love turn-based tactical games, with the campaign management piece.  It is different enough from XCOM in many ways, but very similar.  The ability to move after shooting (move, shoot, move) give a lot of mobilty.  Keeping up with the meta events and not appearing to get behind can be disheartening.  There is still a lot to be learned but I'm enjoying it.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenix Point

_childDocuments_.review: a few things bug me about this game. first is the aiming while free aim is great the only class i can get to hit stuff seems to be the sniper. i have fired rounds that go though arm pits and between legs and a very close range, yet it seems the other team can snipe me with a pistol from across the map. i've started to use snipers and things that blow up to work around this. that being said most of the classes are useless because they cant hit anything! i end up cross classing to sniper or heavy. i will say playing vs the human factions is ok but vs the zombie crabs stuff is broken. talking zombie crab runs across the map and one shots my guy. that was no boss that was a normal dude. to be clear i will play a difficult game get my rear handed to me then try to improve change tactics etc. this game plainly has a feeling that no matter what i bring i will fail. the progression of the game has some neat systems the world will ramp up with you well to say the humans will stay a pace with you the zombie crabs will quick ramp up past the player. i spent alot of time raiding the factions for everything giving the game a pain grind.  things i would like to see in the game smoke bombs for cover well to say the smoke should work both ways. clearly i would like to be able to hit stuff like a buff to shooting while using cover maybe? i would like to change the weapons on the vehicles and they don't take up so much room on the aircraft. with more then 4 ish shots like let me pack more ammo maybe? 4 shots is not going to make up for the dps or tactics of 3 troops. gear is one more thing i would like to see some growth with a lack of tactical options in the leveling tree the gear could provide a fix to that gap mainly im looking at the armor and mounts(armor mods). alright i went on a bit of a rant so i will say if they fix a few things and you see it on sale might be worth your time to pick it up if your into tactical games as this. thank you for your time and take care!
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenix Point

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so ... The whole EPIC Games BS and their handling of it aside, Phoenix Point is interesting.  The story element is a whole lot more than XCOM2 which is nice, and its similar enough to XCOM2 in game play that learning how to play it is fairly easy.  Things to look out for include the fact that your reloads are not infinite, and that it takes time to fashion new armor and guns for recruits.  I like that you can have multiple aircraft to transport troops and the multiple bases is nice.  I did restart once after playing for a bit as I felt I had a better feel for the game and so far the second run is working well.  I'd recommend it but also part of me says get it on sale...  got it as I kickstarted it waaaay back.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenix Point

_childDocuments_.review: Reminds me a lot of XCOM---Adding more hours, I am totally hooked. The story is engrossing, the strategy of balancing skills and equipments between squads and bases is totally addictive. I find myself using second computer just to track the stats on Excel as I progress. And the tactical combats are just great. My last mission was won in extremis, with my soldiers on the edge of collapse, rushing thru the battlefield running or riding in the vehicle, like the ending scenes of Blackhawk Down. What a great holiday I get. Many thanks to Phoenix Point team and devs!

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: after some more playtime I've come to really appreciate some of the things that PP does different to the modern X:COM games. The Action- and Willpoint system, the bullet physics as well as the body part systems stand out to me in particular.  I want to elevate my recommendation to where I can confidently say that the game is worth even its full price.The original UFO, as well as and even more so X:COM Apocalypse where one of my most adored childhood games.And while I greatly enjoyed the modern Firaxis games, there was always a voice in the back of my head saying that this and that is lacking depth, is too streamlined or simply lacking the freedom of what you could do in the old games. It's hard to put into words, and in retrospect things like the political system of Apocalypse were also pretty basic, but at least it was there and and it had some consequences like not being able to buy weapons from hostile organisations.Well, if you go into PP looking for either a more faithful modern recreation of the spirit of the old games, or if you are hoping for an evolution to the genre, then you will most likely be disappointed.If however you are fine with a different take on Firaxis modern X-COM formula, with many parts of the game making it clear that this isn't exactly an AAA produced or funded game, then I'd say go for it. Once the price goes to 50€ I'm not so sure anymore... At that point for me personally it becomes difficult to stay objective and ignore the high hopes I had as a huge fan of the originals for the remake by the original creator.

_childDocuments_.review: I think overall the game is very good and fun. There is room for improvement and honestly it's not as bad as some of the early reviews made it seem. I will say though that I feel it lacks in items. I was under the impression that each faction had not only their own items such as armor and weapons but that those weapons and armor had upgrade tiers as well such as tier 1 anu assault rifle then tier 2 and tier 3 ect. It was disappointing to see it didn't. It definitely feels like the enemies get much stronger than you much faster while you basically stagnate like 10 hours in, I get this feeling like if you just progress through another mission you might unlock a new set of items to upgrade. I feel like that would of made the game more replayable if each factor had a multi tier upgrade weapons and armor tree. Also the game can be brutally difficult at times. Enemies continuasly get stronger while you basically just have to rely on your own strategy. This game is definitely good but it does feel like it could use just as many tools for yourself as it gives the enemies. Some of the skills also don't seem that useful. You can pretty much skip whole fights without ever using a certain skill. I would recommend trying to redo the skill system so that it feels like it has more meaning and more depth for each unit. There was another review that criticized the Heavy class being almost useless except for having a jet pack. This I feel is actually very much the case if you don't have a New Jericho flame thrower. I feel like the Jet pack should be an add on item to armor and not a whole armor piece in itself maybe it could be reworked or changed. There are other bugs that still persist that I have run into where in one example when your base gets attacked if you have a vehicle, the vehicle will sometimes spawn in a room that only has a ladder for exit meaning that basically it cannot be used in battle even though its on the map because of a bad spawning point. There are little things here and there that sometimes don't make sense but the game is by no means bad. Its still a great game Hopefully more content gets added and more options get implemented as far as items and research goes.

_childDocuments_.review: So before I say anything, I wanted to thank all the beta testers at Epic for this game. I also wanted to let everyone know that I was an original backer of this game but got a refund due to the unacceptable switch to EGS and the ensuing debacle.So for the review, it seems much more polished than some of the earlier builds. However, this is not to the level of XCOM 2, which many reviewers have compared it to. If you have gotten this far into the review and think this game looks fun to play and do not have XCOM 2, do yourself a favor and get that one instead. I like the free aim mechanic and how overwatch isn't an automatic win anymore. I like the different factions working with or against you and not at the player's whim like in other games. I also like the true to lore cutscenes and story. The research chains and technologies give you the incentive to work hard to be diplomatic with the other factions and balance your late game needs. Having the option to raid for tech or aircraft was a nice touch as well. There are many, many different ways you can play depending on how you balance these mechanics. This ensures no two games are the same. I think a number of the classes need to be rebalanced as a sniper/heavy or sniper/assault builds are much more useful than any of the other ones. I also think that the havens you need to defend should have buildable point defenses, so you don't have to keep fighting over and over and over. In my first game, I fought almost 70 haven defense battles within a 23-hour game. It felt needlessly tedious. Most of the maps are very similar, even the major story or faction missions. I'd like to see more variety there as well. I never felt compelled to care about any of my soldiers either, like XCOM.  More customization features are needed. Lastly, I think there has been a waste regarding some of the factions there. You fight the Pure and Forsaken, but have very little interaction otherwise. Similarly, the bandit and independent factions have such promise and have not been expanded on very much either. Why can you not choose to work with either? There could be special technologies and other consequences for relations with the main factions. If the developers read the reviews, they should use more of the very rich lore background. I hope the new DLCs fix these things. I'd give it a lukewarm thumbs-up, a 7/10. There is a lot that needs to be improved, but it is fun if you like XCOM, Xenonauts, or other games that are similar. I hope the developers step up and polish the game a bit more.  The 30 dollar price point should be kept as it is until it gets more polished.

_childDocuments_.review: 2/5 - not worth it unless on super saleI played this game enough to get my money's worth but it isn't very good. It's interesting but not very good. It works on a story level because you are earth's poorly funded best hope but maybe you should actually get help when you're allied with a faction.The most interesting part of the game is it's combat. Every bullet having it's own travel path is neat and at least feels better than a simple percentile to determine your shot. The issue is that your units cannot aim down and consider seeing the left eyelash of an enemy as having line of sight. Much like the rest of the game, there's something interesting here but it's flawed and really needs to be refined.

_childDocuments_.review: The return fire mechanic is simply broken. Whenever a character is taking a shot, he will step out of cover, fire, and then the enemy will return fire. Only then will your character move back into cover. (If he's not dead by then)Basically, the game is punishing you to fire at your opponent. In a game... where you have to kill your enemy... This mechanic, as it is implemented, has no place in a turn-based tactical game. It makes cover next to useless. Your characters will also sometimes destroy their own cover, while firing at the enemies. The line of sight and ability to free aim is a good idea, but unfortunately, it is, just like the return fire, not well implemented. Sometimes you can shoot your enemy, and they can't, sometimes the opposite. Why? The line of sight doesn't seem to work properly. The structures around you can be glitchy as well, and you can sometimes shoot through wall too.It is hard to believe the creator of XCOM made such a poorly designed game...It is a shame, because it has otherwise good ideas. I like the idea of managing the inventories of my soldier, of exploring the globe and building bases.But as it stands, Phoenix Point is barely playable because of these two issues.

_childDocuments_.review: A decent game that differentiates itself from xcom. It definitely takes getting used to since my soldiers for some reason can't lean over railing and shoot at enemies at a lower level. Taking cover at corners is weird as well. In Xcom my soldiers can step out and fire. Here, they transition to free shoot and I am staring at a wall. For any new players it is also useful to run up to an enemy shoot them and then run into high cover. I was so used to xcom ending turns after 2 actions that I did not think of it since this game uses a different action system.The most noticeable change is to how guns work. Each bullet has its own trajectory and damage which is interesting. Now you can target specific body parts of an enemy and each part has different armor so where you hit someone matters. This falls short because each weapon seems to have infinite range and the pistol somehow hits across the map. They should patch this by giving everything an effective range since gravity pulls on everything the same. They should also make mission important pathways or objectives indestructible. Having to restart because a single stray bullet or grenade spam destroyed the only way up can be frustrating.So far the factions are interesting but they don't really do much for me and could use some work. They are also pretty counter intuitive, for some reason when they go to war they destroy each other's havens. I would understand the disciples of anu doing that, but they should actually occupy and trade havens when at war. It is also not possible to create peace between them all because the game intentionally sabotages the relationship between them as tech progresses.The game is too micromanage-eee for my tastes. The cost for equipment to trooper ratio is so high. I struggle to afford even the most basic armor for my soldiers because i am always low on one of the two available game resources. The DLC with the ancients exacerbates this problem to the extreme. Now I have to find SEVERAL NEW resources and mine them. It becomes ridiculous because you have to fly a "manned ship" to get the resources. Apparently drones can't do that but they can scout the areas to find more mines. Oh, and you have to do that while having to defend them with your already thin ranks. On top of that to ensure you have resources you have to steal, defend havens, complete missions, and explore. Guess what that needs? You guessed it, another ship full of soldiers. This does not even include destroying pandoran nests. Then we add to the resources issue by having to buy ammo after every mission. Depending on the type of ammo it can be substantial. I have no idea why each resource has a + or - counter when you are incapable of producing your own resources. It's possible to get enough resources but it's a huge hassle that I don't want to deal with.The game requires multiple bases in multiple spots that all need multiple expensive upgrades for them to be remotely useful. Not to mention needing to activate each base to add to the resources issues.  it becomes a nightmare with everything else going on. Even then, the enemy can invade and destroy said bases so choose wisely. The ships need to be faster as well since late game none of my ships can make it to a haven before it explodes, especially when I am using a Disciple ship.I enjoyed the game at first. But nearing the end it feels like a slog because I am constantly having to fly ships to raid or fly ships to trade. Fly ships to defend, Fly ships to attack. Fly, Fly , Fly. That is literally the globescape. Xcom did a great job simplifying this by combining all resources into just one or two. Along with having resources automatically go into your account without extra effort. Aside from that I expected more since I was a backer on fig way back when. I also suggest reading the terms and services since this game has faced criticisms for broken promises along with going one year epic store exclusive. The game is not bad, but it is not good either. Hopefully Julian takes parts of the games that work and pitches it for xcom 3. I wouldn't mind a terror from the deep making it's way to xcom the same way the virus sread here.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I do have some problems with Phoenix Point - the busywork of maintenance, the comedy of mistakes from Festering Skies, small number of distinct enemies and the seeming absence of sustainable resource gathering (at least that I've seen so far)  - the gameplay and the storyline are really quite enjoyable.Basically: everything I have an issue with is stuff that can be easily added to the game over time and in some cases has been. The base game itself is excellent.Accuracy is based on a deviation from the central target and true LOS which, while annoying at times, ensures that every time you take a shot you're not relying on a percentage chance of hitting it. There's no 99% chance whiffs at point blank: if you shove your muzzle into a Pandoran head that head is going to quickly disappear. Destroying specific parts of the enemies can be a godsend as it will buy you more time, remove their best defenses/weapons/special abilities. Some enemies are even specifically designed to encourage you to flank them which I really enjoy.All enemies are on the map to begin with so you don't just run into a mob and they go "lol oh noes we got spotted" and scatter. Instead you have to hunt them down one by one or all at once as they try to swarm you. The factions you're trying to align with are, well, actually there on the map. You have to help keep those settlements safe and, y'know, protect humanity. There's no random mission generator to just create sporadic attacks - the enemies just invade the existing settlements and hopefully you get there in time to stop them (or the settlement's defenders can handle them... though they'll end up far weaker against the next attack if you do this) - creating the sense that you are actually the super secret organization dedicated to keeping humanity from getting wiped off the map.Finally a small part that is just cozy AF: You're the super secret not-quite government organization with cutting edge tech and the stuff you start with shows it. You kick off the game with probably the best tech available and your potential allies don't offer you dramatically better stuff - just different stuff. Overall the default equipment is really, really good and it further entrenches the feeling that you are, in fact, the secret organization that has been hoarding awesome tech all these years in preparation for saving humanity.... 'course it's also pretty expensive, but still. It really helps to reinforce the theme.All in all I give it a tentative recommendation. It's a flawed but fun game marred by a couple poor design choices that can be readily fixed with some attention. If the developers choose to fix them, then it would be truly great, IMO.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is really difficult.I love the "old" X-COM games and one can clearly see it is made by some of the developers / designers. The design is nice, the maps I find even more appealing (better map design, more complex paths) and the action point management is better (e.g. shooting does not end your turn)...However, some elements have been altered and it doesn't feel to the better.Most of my critic is the annoying usability. The management of equipment and soldiers becomes a chore. Especially finding a working combination of gun and ammo, comparing their stats or making a decision for the best armor becomes annoying - even more when the filters don't work again (e.g. you want to filter for assault stuff but see heavy weapons instead).Also annoying are some game decisions like having different looks for the same weapons and thus not stacking with the same type - therefore cluttering the list of weapons with no way of sorting them by damage etc.But also small things like selecting the best weapon becomes tedious when you need to move back and forth all the time comparing stats instead of having a comparison. And there is no info regarding damage but instead it shows  and the other weapon has . So you need to make a calculation whether it is better or not (or eventually the same). Don't get me wrong, this is not rocket science, but it requires some thoughts I would prefer to spend on the game.But it's not only the micro management of items, armor and vehicles which annoys me. Also the world map just is a mess. Filled with many icons - even the ones of missions you completed earlier you are using track of the important parts. Why not removing them and keeping the world map clean instead??Organizing your bases is also more complex than it should be. But also sometimes you have no real idea what you are actually doing right now.One difference to X-COM is also the "Pandemic Legacy" feeling where you discover new places on the globe and start "missions" or simply loot the place. Afterwards they are just dead spots on the map you have to fly by when refueling your plane. This is not only cluttering the map but also making it hard to focus on important aspects. Where in theory this sounds like a cool mechanic, it becomes annoying. Unlike X-COM where you have a budget every month, you need to scavenge places. And talking about budget and factions, I know this also sounds cool on paper but trust me, it becomes annoying in the game. Instead of being designated "world police" you are just a bunch of people who eventually save the world. But there are many factions in the game which are working with or against you. And you need to decide who to please because faction A also works against faction B. Where all factions eventually sound like stereotypical post-apocalyptic failed states. You basically need to decide if you want to work with the "true believers" or the "fanatical gun club" and betray the other faction because A wants you to loot shelter of faction B. This makes it annoying some times because I need to make decisions I don't want to, but someone thought a "diplomacy" function would be cool.Don't get me wrong, these elements are nice... mostly. It just has too many painfully rough edges where it gets annoying. So I usually play for 1-2 hours before something becomes boring or I wonder why the hell I have to do that now. Combined with cluttered UI so you sometimes just miss an important mission and you are loosing fun after that time.This sadly leads to a negative review. Even though I'm sure the game has some good parts in it.

_childDocuments_.review: Phoenix Point is what a squad –based strategy game should feel like. It is by no means perfect, but gives the player lots of different approaches for the same situation. The increased support for mods gives you the opportunity to customise your playthroughs even more, if you wish to alter certain aspects. But instead of writing long paragraphs of text, here are the most important pros and cons:PRO:+ No linear research resulting in the same loadouts. Different tools are better for certain situations.+ Reduction of RNG through manual aiming (if an enemy stands right in front of you, you are going to hit it!)+ Strategic fights (Disabling dangerous body parts/ weapons is far more effective than just shooting blindly)+ Different approaches to the global story (Help everyone or profit through sabotage and theft?)+ Difficulty increases over time (enemies grow stronger with you, making the endgame not a total cakewalk/ no one-man-armies that can handle an entire mission on their own.)+ Customisation (classes, vehicles, loadouts, even body parts - everything can be customised!)CONS:- Somewhat lacking soundtrack, mostly just ambient noise- Questionable handling of the DLCs (they can be turned on/ off, but the Pure & Ancient DLCs feel tacked on with no effort)- Attention to detail might be overwhelming (Not a problem for me, but some people might find the handling of the entire globe with invasions, scavenging sites, a dozen bases and a dozen aircrafts slightly overwhelming, but this is a matter of preference.)Overall I can highly recommend the game to people who like squad-based strategy games. This is especially true for people who like the XCOM series, but wanted to customise and control much more of the game than was previously possible.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenix Point

_childDocuments_.review: This game can be best summed up as “two steps forward, two steps backwards”.It looks very pretty. There is a lot of player agency. You can mutate or mechanically augment your soldiers, and there is a leveling system for each class. There is a “free aim” system which allows you to aim at specific enemy parts. And a lot of other cool stuff.The DLC that introduces air warfare is so poorly thought that it’s like it had no QA for balancing. There is a bug that makes opponents skip their turns in some instances when you load a tactical map from a save. Upgrades are not really upgrades, but they are more like “sidegrades”; which makes research very underwhelming most of the time. On maximum difficulty, the more successful you are, the game is designed to keep increasing the number of enemies on the tactical maps until the point you will become overwhelmed, which is an incredibly poorly thought mechanic.I hope mods will “fix” it and do another run in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: The stats say I've barely played this, but I was an early backer so I played it on the other games store plenty, and then got a Steam code for the Year One edition. Lots has been fixed since the initial release, but it still has bugs and flaws. The bottom line is that this game is both disappointing and good. It is from Julian Gollop, who is a legend at this sort of squad combat game all the way from Rebelstar Raiders in the 80s. However, it's hard to avoid the fact that this offers limited advancement on the ongoing XCOM model that's been going since the 1990s. Build a base, gain experience, go out and do missions with squads, research your tech and improve your equipment, juggle resources, face bigger, nastier enemies, etc. It all works, it's fun enough, it's got its unique character, the gameplay is smooth enough. For that alone it merits a thumbs up, because it is a competent and enjoyable game in its own right.The disappointment is that in the current state it never quite meets its early promise (e.g. the allegedly adaptive enemies don't feel like they adapt, but just level up), and it fails to really give much core novelty on an old format. It's a sort of "80%" kind of game: gets stuff right, but has nothing that elevates it to greatness.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly good for all fans of XCOM-like turn based tactics games. In my mind its on par with XCOM 2: the war of the chosen. I even prefer several aspects in Phoenix Project over XCOM 2. What PP lacks compared to XCOM 2 is the massive budget that makes everything more polished, so PP has had to make up for that with being creative. One aspect that is kinda a new player trap in PP is that it really doesn't hold your hand and it gives you total freedom in deciding how to approach the crisis. For a lot of new players this results in a very repetitive and bogged down late game, since the player will try to do everything and take every mission. The game gives you the freedom to do this, but the way that you are meant to play it is focus on your mission and focus on the bigger picture, rather than trying to be a global peacekeeper. Still there's so many right ways to play this game that trying to do everything in a single play through is not necessary.

The enemy just dance around while you're shooting for some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ reason. And because the spread mechanics is so simple, it's actually make it even more boring than XCOM chance mechanics. _childDocuments_.review: Update - Even with all the content now available, still gotten bored 2/3rds of the way into a run.I have researched several end games, but just cannot be arsed to actually enact them.Rated M for "meh".Yes I'm yet another Xcom fanatic kickstarter backer, who rolled their eyes and installed Epic for this game alone.The original release wasn't spectacular, especially with all the "DLC COMING SOON! TOTALLY NOT STUFF THAT SHOULD HAVE BEEN IN AT LAUNCH!" teasing us in the background.So, after grinding through some where between half and two thirds through, I got bored and decided to wait till the game was actually finished.All the development and platform issues/spectacles aside, it's basically just not that great.As other's have said, the soldier customisation options are weak and it's difficult to make them feel individual, hell even the colour choices are ugly.One of the biggest issues is basically in the faction gear, the differences are so minor that it's hard to care and almost pointless to get hold of anyone else's kit.You'll do just as well/badly with Phoenix Project guns and ammo as anyone else's.Sure, there are a few unique weapons and vehicles but they aren't anything great (maybe with the exception of the stun pistol)And the combat is just a bit dull and as the game goes on, feels more like a chore than anything.The economy is pretty unforgiving and you'll spend a lot of time scrabbling for resources, even just to keep your weapons loaded, forcing you into repetitive missions to scrape by.Story isn't too bad, nothing ground breaking but the cut scenes are okay and the fluff text for research & background is half decent.It does do some things right, the free aim location based shooting is pretty good (though free aim before side stepping from full cover will generally make you miss) and being able to disable body parts is a nice addition.And the big creatures do look pretty damned cool and make a big impression on first encountering.The enemy evolution mechanic is also quite cool, with the half dozen foes gaining variants and increasing in power.But, it's also quite fail in some ways, like I've seen 6 different evolution reports for one of the apex enemies, but have I ever met even the basic kind.Nope, not even once.Beats me how the heck they are evolving with nothing to trigger it...It might be worth getting on sale, but it's alas inferior to the recent Xcom games so don't bother getting it till it's discounted by at least half.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, this is a good game. But you can run into balancing problems, since a few tooltips are still missing in order to explain your possibilities. _childDocuments_.review: If you like XCOM style games and you don't have Pheonix Point then you seriously need to grab it now at its 50% discount.I have played the base game quite a bit via XBOX GamePass for PC where it was available freely to subscribers but did not include any of the DLC that are part of this Year One Edition.You should largely ignore earlier negative reviews because half of them were negative purely in reaction to its Epic Exclusive release. Whilst a small percentage of the remaining negative reviews had some merit I can happily report that PP has improved immeasurably since its initial release and what we have here with this YOE is a far more polished and well rounded game.I would go so far as to say that the political intrigues of interacting with the various factions together with greater variety in enemy units now makes Phoenix Point superior to, or at the very least as good as, the new series of XCOM games. Even should you not completely agree with that assessment PP remains an interesting and absorbing addition to the tactical turn based genre and an unmissable bargain at this price.

_childDocuments_.review: In many ways, Phoenix Point is inferior to XCOM-2. There is questionable gameplay balance, worse character customization, and just generally less of the magic that makes XCOM-2 so great.But I find myself returning to Phoenix Point far more often than XCOM-2 for a few reasons: the factions, the flexibility, and the larger scale. There are so many great moments of decision making that make you feel like you are actually strategizing a war against an enemy. Do you build bases near your allies to help defend them? Do you want larger aircraft that hold more troops but move significantly slower? Do you prioritize manufacturing or research?This game is honestly so, SO close to being the best of its genre. But the developer has a specific vision about what this game should be, and for better or worse, this is the Phoenix Point we get and maybe not the one we deserve. What this game needs is a general balance overhaul, clear weapon and armor tiers with a whole additional tier of equipment, vehicles  actually viable by dropping their squad slots to 2 (down from 3) and allowing them to reload, and giving factions more agency overall.As for the DLC, the Blood and Titanium DLC as well as the Kaos Engines DLC are decent. Legacy of the Ancients feels misplaced and I never engage with the content. Corrupted Horizons and Festering Skies actively make the game worse by adding completely unbalanced enemies and unwanted busywork, so I strongly recommend NOT buying these.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game a ton before it came to steam, while it was stand alone, and I have to say its definitely above the average. Its similar enough to games like XCOM that you can pick it up rather quickly, but different enough to make it still feel unique. Individual bullet trajectories makes weapons feel more worth firing when you have a half decent shot rather than abusing meta like previously mentioned titles. Having the option to shoot cover out of your way is also very helpful if not unrealistic at times, but who is playing this game for realism? Although this is about all the good I can say about the game, which is still the majority of my opinion at the moment. There are glaring balance issues involved with the game as well, but all of which are very specific and with enough time (like hours worth) you can find ways to deal with it. Unfortunately I have put this game down for a while due to one of these unbalances and I'm not sure if I will return to it. I love this game, and I love the story behind it, but when I face a stalker that can heal +100 damage from 1 melee attack in a single turn.. That's where I draw the line for what is fun.

_childDocuments_.review: PC SteamDuration: 94 hoursPhoenix Point is an X-Com style game.  Feels a lot like X-Com 1.5, mixing the old UFO Defence with the new reboot Enemy unknown.  Combat is challenging and exciting with a great ballistics system.  It's fun shooting out a leg to reduce movement or taking out an arm so the enemy can't use that two-handed weapon.  The world system is also very well implemented.  There are three other factions in the world who don't like each other.  You can side with one, none or all three.  They will end up attacking each other and "the clock" in this game is remaining human population.  So, you may (or may not) decide to defend them from one another.  Need a plane? Steal one from your enemy.  Want that research or resource, you can raid it.  In that way, it reminded me a little of X-Com Apocalypse.  "Terror" missions are lots of fun and nearly not as dreaded as in X-Com when you have 10 civilians transformed by headcrabs!  Instead you are set with protecting civilians or structures from the attacking force.  Again, a great improvement.  And mindsuckers can be shot off your soldiers head, so getting attacked doesn't mean your soldier is dead.  Just don't use a shotgun! Nice touch.  At 94 hours it got a little long for this old man.  But, overall, a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: Initially I was positively impressed with the game and its mechanics but unfortunately, as usual, the first impression was wrong. The game suffers a teeeeeerrible lack of balance if you ask me. It almost brags about the fact it's a game of choices and sacrifices that have to be made in order to procede but it then limits itself to throw at you situations that are simply impossible to solve without losing men. It's not like XCOM where bold decisions and good fortune could turn the tide in your favour. Here your men HAVE to die. Period. Gunfire is cool and I like the free aim system and the chance of friendly fire is also an interesting feature that adds some layer of strategy in the field but unfortunately your soldiers are so dumb that they simply cannot get down to free the line of fire. This translates in: are you shooting in the general direction of another of your soldier? Cool, you're going to have friendly fire on him/her. That is. You could have a single ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ soldier nail in the line of fire and you're going to hit it. Your soldiers won't even try to move away from the line of fire. Is this the way to make a game harder? My answer is no: in the current state this game is not as good as it could be. Also, the economy is completely broken. You will need an insane amount of resources to keep things running while your enemies get stronger and stronger right in front of your eyes. I believe the difficulty curve is too steep: at the very beginning of the game it seems like you can win fights blindfolded. After a few hours, when you are still learning all the many managing systems present in the game (with good potential but hey, give me the time to learn!) that are thrown at your face in a row, things change: a lot of superheavy armored enemies start to pop up and you're done. Even during ambushes! I was ambushed by these guys belonging to The Pure bunch and they where simply impossible to defeat. It was like fighting against heavy tanks using BBs.  The game has good potential but it needs to be completely rehauled for new players like me that feel frustrated by playing, not entertained. Since the game has good potential, I'm still waiting for the remaining DLCs that are to come (or at least I think so) but I won't hide the fact that, in the current state, I'll be looking for mods to better balance the experience.In the current state, I suggest to wait for the release of the remaining DLCs before buying the game.Behemoth Update: they added horse blinders to soldiers. Now they can shoot in a narrow cone only, making sniper and heavy unit's overwatch nearly useless. Feels like the authors hate they're own creation. Modders only can save this game, in my humble opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has so much potential. I backed it on Fig. I have the game (with all its expansion DLCs) on Epic and on Steam. But between the game play feeling a little "empty" (like something is missing but I can’t quite put my finger on what) and the bugs - it’s a thumbs down for me unfortunately. First thumbs down I've ever given - and i own nearly 1200 games on Steam alone...Played it when it first came out but stopped playing it because it lacked soul. Then got on Steam again – and all its expansions. Figured new content, patches and game play improved - lets try it again. So tried to play it again. But after random hours of playing the game just stops working. After I complete a mission (no specific mission in particular), the game refuses to load back to the geoscope and becomes unplayable. I scrubbed the game. Started fresh. Three times. Same thing – each time at different place in the story. after all that I finally got the game to progress further and discovered things just happen. There is no real cohesion, or motivation, or even just clear direction. Stuff just happens. Narrative cut scenes play, and more stuff to do just piles onto your to do list. Just soooooo much. It just piles it on.  All the time. More and more bases to unlock and build and repair, more and more and more things to research (most of which do not really matter). More repairs to be done. A never-ending queue of monotonous gear and items to be built. Mission after mission to do to collect more resources to continue to research more pointless things and build more stuff and recruit more soldiers. Soldiers whose ability and skill progression are pretty much all exactly the same. A heavy is a heavy is a heavy is a heavy. A sniper is a sniper is a sniper. Etc. So then you build more gear in hopes to try to make them different, which just take and more and more of go here, now go there, now there, now here, back to there… And things just happen. All the time. Most of the time there you have no idea what is going on or what to do. There is a big pink thing flying across the screen. What do I do with that? What is it. Can interact with it? How do I interact with it? Oh, look its destroying havens… so what? Still have no idea how to stop it. Can’t even target it.My soldiers have corruption. What now? Is that bad? Can I get rid of it? Is there anything to be done about it? Does anyone care? Is there a scientist somewhere trying find a cure? Can we help???? Does it even matter? What happens when they are completed corrupted???  I have list of 500 things I need to research. Which one do I prioritise? Will researching the random worm thing help me… oh look it didn't. Well, that was a waste of time and effort. Stuff just happens. Factions and peoples spewing things on screen to just add to the clutter that try to create a story by forcing you to make choices which ultimately just give +4 to one faction rating  and -4 to another… That’s all you do. No soul. just do stuff. There are no characters to connect with or care about. No personalities you love to hate, or to make your feel like the world matters or even what you do matters.  So, while tactical mission are initially fun, the constant grind just basically turns the game into a glorified “farming” sim. Its one off those that tries to do everything - and achieves that. But at the cost everything simply being more things for you do with no sense of achievement or meaning for doing them...

_childDocuments_.review: If you expect XCOM 3 or anything XCOM-like then you will hate it. They are both tactical strategy games, but that's where the similarities end. I myself am a huge fan of the XCOM franchise and though I feel like Phoenix Point didn't manage to capture the same feeling of grandeur and coolness that XCOM has, it undoubtedly does a lot of things better. Things Phoenix Point does better:-Chance to hit mechanic. You will never stand right in front of an enemy and miss.-It allows you to aim at and hit individual parts of an enemy, targeting weak spots and disabling limbs. In the words of a wise drill sergeant training recruits against the bugs, “The enemy can't press a button if you incapacitate their hand.”-Destructible environment. It exists in XCOM 2, but it is just done better here and enemies never see through walls to shoot at you.-It adds vehicles to the battlefield and it’s great fun.-It has minimal bugs.Things that might annoy XCOM players:-It has far less individual cosmetic customization of soldiers.-The game is slow paced. Every playthrough is like playing a Long War campaign.-In Phoenix Point you have multiple bases and it demands a bit of micro management.-Turns function as follows: you move all your soldiers, then they move all their soldiers.All in all I'd definitely recommend playing it. It has its flaws, but the developers have actually been awesome in adding additional content for free and even re-balancing and fixing things the community pointed out. If you start it up expecting it to be XCOM you will hate it, because it's not. It's Phoenix Point.
