_childDocuments_.review: After a glitchy, buggy, dull and monotonous start to life, Snapshot have worked hard and listened to the community to give Phoenix Point a chance to survive in what's becoming a genre over saturated with average or sub-par games. I was an early backer and played that first launch where the game was an unbalanced, needlessly difficult and boring mess, but I vowed to give them time to fix it and try again.Unfortunately, no amount of patches and hot fixes are going to fix this games core, underlying issue:It is slow. Dull. Boring. Uninteresting. It has no personality.Now, I'm not someone who needs a testosterone fuelled, explosion orgy in a whirlwind of death to enjoy a game. I play strategy games like Civilization, Stellaris, XCOM, Phantom Doctrine, King of Dragon's Pass, etc. But there is nothing in this game to get excited about or grip you. Even the music is this slow, constantly dragging, two tone snooze fest. I enter combat or go on a mission and have the exact same single music track as when I'm looking at the washed out 2D Base images or the dingy grey world map. The same dreary, monotonous music which literally sounds like a bored, depressed person halfheartedly playing an old piano for a boss they hate at a job they don't care about. Music sets the scene for media - it tells the audience how they should be feeling. Phoenix Point's music tells me I should be bored and depressed.Combat likewise seems to take an age. Maps are large and mobility is low, even when maxed out, and differs wildly between troops. The maps aren't particularly varied either and seem to either be open, sparse and poorly thought out or a poorly thought out maze of buildings and corners you have to creep through.Enemies die slowly. There's no sense of urgency and your tactical options are limited. In fact, the largest tactical option open to you is the free aim system, which allows you to selectively pick off body parts and take enemies apart piece by piece, which sounds like a great idea but again it just slows down what is already a fairly dragged out combat experience. You never feel like you've achieved anything when an enemy dies; they either meander towards you and die in a couple of shots, remain stationary and have to be ground down from a safe distance or take so long to wear down that it's relief when it's over and you can finally do something else.The story and lore, which could have been this game's saving grace, is again halfhearted and often feels like an teenage armature writer's club trying to show off how cool and edgy and dark they are. It's lazy and self-indulgent, mixing in so many elements that I wonder if a lot of it didn't come from other ideas the writers had, which they just crow-barred into Phoenix Point because they were the only ones willing to hire them.All of this makes Phoenix Point a game which is too simple and too complex in all the wrong places. It badly needs someone to strip out the story, speed up the combat, diversify the game in every area from aesthetics and music to game play and basically just pump some love and character into this game. There is a good game in here, but they need to rethink the core experience they're trying to offer. A slow, thoughtful game is all well and good but it can't be slow and thoughtful all.the.time. Especially when you're facing down a horde of monsters, or subduing a gargantuan mutant terror or defending your base or raiding another faction and in between doing these things the game and story needs to progress. There is potential in here, but the game needs to find another gear.Also, £46 for this game? lol, just no.

_childDocuments_.review: To sum it up: a good enough game, but not great.This is a tough review for me to write. I was an early backer for Phoenix Point, and felt it could be the next great TB tactics game. The potential is still there. But somewhere along the line, what could put PP as a reference in the genre got lost. It was first shown with a body horror, lovecraftian sci-fi setting (in the early days, there was even jokes being made by the community that The Fly's Brundefly could be an enemy in the game, and would mesh really well). But that was dropped for another post-apocalyptic seen so many times sci-fi world. The written lore was amazing and showed a lot of depth, and really, search for Phoenix Point's Briefings to have an idea of what was achieved by the writing team. But such a deeply researched, very well writen lore didn't make a difference in the game. Initial footage showed battles in oil rigs with huge monsters being hinted, but by the final game there were no huge monsters, just your regular troop soldiers. Comparisons with Firaxis X-Com's franchise will always be made, and rightly so, as Phoenix Point's developers didn't shy away from admiting the influence. Which it's just as well, seeing as Firaxis was highly influenced by the original XCom. If you played your War Of The Chosen to death, and can't stand to return to defeating those damned Chosen and their endless banter, Phoenix Point is a fine option. But do realize that it stands as one of those soccer players that show a huge potential at an early age, and by reasons unknow just end up playing in the lower leagues.

_childDocuments_.review: So.While I like this game, here's the problem I have: The basic player-engagement problem I had is that on a reward screen - you're almost always greeted with a big red penalty.Save a city? Well you sir can get F****d, we're going to start freezing your diplomatic overtures.They would literally prefer you allow thousands of civilians die than try to save humanity as a whole.And every faction is the same. You lose diplomatic standing for helping anyone that isn't them.I honestly stopped wanting to deal *with* them, and instead wanted to *overthrow* every one of the self-righteous prats - and force them to damn well cooperate until there was some population to spare in their internecine ♥♥♥♥-flinging.So yes. _childDocuments_.review: Post Hypnos Patch Edit. The game is much more manageable and puts you just shy of having an advantage in a lot of ways, the resource economy is much better but still harder, while you'll never stock up on all the bases, weapons, and people you want you can have enough, which is what this game is supposed to give you. you get access to more interesting weapons faster, and lets you deal with monsters that are just giant walking hitpoint containers easier. that said the updates moved this from a 3.5 out of 10 to probably a 6.5 out of ten. playable, solid, decent.there are still glaring issues, some classes are close to useless, or are useless, most weapons outside of assault rifle, grenade launcher, or sniper don't have clear roles, or limitations prevent effective or common use.  range or damage is often the biggest issue, weapons that should be the backbone of your squad such as cannons or sniper rifle still don't have the punch they need to feel like you are controlling the battlefield. and time is a huge factor, Steam says i put an extra 100 hours into this post update to beat it from start to finish, i'd say 60-70 was me actually playing, which let's be honest either feels excessively long or just outright is. i'd much rather it be tuned for about a 30-40 hour campaign, because at the end it felt like such a slog through mud and swamp i never really want to do it again. overall if you are into this sort of game and beat Gears Tactics then this isn't bad on sale but i can't recommend it at full price, and definitely can't recommend the Year 2 DLC.This game has some of the coolest mechanics of any squad based strategy game I know of. I love the targeting circle instead of the chance to hit. I love the classes. I love the chuthulu mythos inspired story and enemies. I love the art direction, I love map management.What I don't love massive disproportionate power scaling, developers nerfing any mechanic they feel is the player, playing the game wrong. (such as massively buffing the Scylla, to force you to bleed it to death. or nerfing two soldier weapons and the infilitrator completely.) the lack of armor, weapons, or crew. in order to win you basically have to be the scourge of heavens killing as many humans for tech and supply as you do enemies. otherwise you can't afford to match the enemy and even so it will still be insane with the difficulty of the enemies late game, many of whom can one shot a high level soldier. Many people have brought up these complaints and the devs have largely ignored it. instead releasing a DLC that is basically paying 10 dollars to make the game worse.  best case scenario you have a new rock paper scissors minigame that you have to research to use. worst case you lose multiple squads and transports for no good reason, and havens die out faster.  In a recent update Agrippa HX recently typed out something that I felt needed to be seen by more people, so I am quoting here."Considering this game has been out for about a year and a half and we're still talking about how Snapshot might one day fix its many problems and balance the game so that it will someday reach its potential, I think it's time to be realistic and admit that Phoenix Point will never be what we hoped it was going to become.I hope anyone coming to the game now is buying it because they like its current state rather than because they're still hoping it will become something different.I wonder what happened to this project behind the scenes. Much of what's wrong with the game seems to be at the design level. I find it hard to believe Gollop was the "creative lead" on this project. I thought he was a much better game designer than this. This never felt like a game from a designer with Gollop's pedigree. Was he really involved, or was his alleged role more a marketing angle and the real design work was done poorly by a subordinate with less experience and talent? Either he's overrated or he wasn't really as involved as the marketing said (i.e. he misled us). I don't know which it is, but neither makes me excited for any of his future projects"

_childDocuments_.review: First impressions: Just... just no. It's a busy, hysterical mess. It tries to do far too much and the end result is confusing blob of a game. We didn't need factions at all, and we certainly didn't need the tiresome chore of diplomacy with them. We didn't need a frankly bewildering array of enemies that come in about a billion different almost identical 'variations'. We certainly didn't need the frankly hilariously bad concept of a lovecraftian deep one who has found a gun somewhere. We didn't need an asinine resource management system that appears to have been designed specifically to keep you broke and desperate. If you want your game to be difficult, make it difficult. Don't just design it in a way that makes it not fun to play. That's not 'making it tough on the player'. That is making a design choice to make the game feel like a frustrating chore. I mean, I guess it's AN approach to game design, but it doesn't seem like the optimal one.Oh, and before anyone says 'oh but the game gets better' or 'the game just needs you to persevere and get used to it' - you have sort of missed the point of what a game actually is, there. This was hyped solely on Gollop's involvement. 'The creator of X-Com!'. It is not unreasonable, as a consumer, for someone to expect a similar experience. A game that can ONLY be enjoyed after you play it for 400 hours or whatever isn't actually a good game, is it? Would you watch a trilogy of three-hour long movies all the way through if you though that the first movie was bad after an hour or so? Time, and Life itself, is far too short. Sorry, folks, but no. I am not convinced by that argument. It's explicitly 'game-ist' and I'm not interested in racking up a thousand hours on Darksouls or whatever - I play games to have fun and relax. And this game is just annoying, and the sources of that annoyance are numerous and disappointing. It's hard to have fun when the game keeps pissing me off with it's tedious nonsense. To be brutally honest, this also feels like a naked attempt to sabotage future Firaxis games with the X-Com franchise, considering how 'Terror From The Deep' was teased at the end of that game. That's genuinely how I feel about it. It feels somehow... mean-spirited. Spiteful.Having played the original X-Com for possibly thousands of hours over the last nearly three decades, I had expected more from it's creator. It's a pity that what I got was something I can't wait to stop playing almost every time I am asked by the game to do something. It's a pity because the game is beautiful. I don't mean the derpy monsters or the baffling misama that is the world map, they look like absolute garbage apart from a small number of them - I mean the cutscenes that are shown as the tutorial progresses, the interactions (wholly unwelcome ones, mind) that you have with the other factions. The battlefields. Even the soldiers themselves. Lovely, and the voice acting is pretty good too.So, in summary: a confusing swamp of badly handled ideas, presumably designed by committee and badged up as 'X-Com, but better!' with the aesthetics of a far superior product drybrushed over the top of it.###EDIT###: So, don't let it be said that I don't give something a fair crack. I have now played an additional 110 hours. Do you know what that 110 hours consisted of?Shields. Shieldy-Shield-Shields. Shields with Shields on, with loads of Shields coming out of them. I wanted to see if the DLC did anything to really spruce up the miserable, grinding tedium of playing this game. They added two pieces of DLC that introduced a new enemy type, one of which I have already mentioned. Now... let me just say that Phoenix Point features Shields. A lot. There is a type of ubiquitous crab-man who has a shield. He appears a LOT. You will be dealing with shields a lot in this game. 'Hahaha!' Said the developer. 'I have designed an enemy that will force the player to adapt their strategy! THIS GUY HAS A SHIELD!'No, mate. What happens is, you force me to waste expensive ammo trying to chip the guy to death, because I cannot move my soldiers because if I do, I get shot immediately to death by a resident from Innsmouth wielding a sniper rifle in a way that would make anyone who ever fought in any modern war feel triggered. It's not challenging. It is tedious. I've already covered this. When you want a game to be challenging, you design it in such a way as to ensure that the player has to adapt their tactics on the fly and not rely on one Alpha-Team setup with a SOP. That's literally what combined arms is. That's literally how battles are fought. You don't just glue eighty pounds of calcium to someone's left arm and say 'Hah! Now they can't be shot at all!' and furthermore, if you DO do that, you don't make that type of enemy more common in the game than hydrogen is in the universe. This. Is. LAZY.'Never mind all that!' cried the developer. 'I'm not lazy and I'm most certainly not putting almost no effort whatsoever into this product that I am charging AAA prices for! I'll add two new types of enemies! And you know what? These enemies will be ROBOTS! Hahaha! You can't touch me now, I've added something with a bit of variety behind it, a bit of finesse and difference, and a new aesthetic!'Yes, mate. You certainly have. The Pure and the Ancient Defenders are indeed not crab-fish-cephalopod people.You know how you managed to balls it all up though? These new factions, that could have been so cool, so unlike anything else in the game?YOU GLUED SHIELDS ON THEM AGAIN.I swear to god, I am so BORED of dealing with enemies who stand still, lower their shield, fire a volley of godlike accurate machinegun fire that makes my maxed-out, hyper equipped and over-optimised snipers go green with envy, jiggle about with a weird animation and then put the shield back up in place.The other two bits of DLC are one where you can dress as a crab and you get a reasonable assault rifle and an absolutely dire machine gun, and one where you can lose a dogfight every few hours. Not going to lie, I am surprised that anyone would send an aircraft up to a dogfight with only a few rounds of ammunition; apparently that is exactly what the megaminds at Phoenix Point do. No wonder they lost the war.Finally, in this game you can build shields for your team. I have never done this because I find it almost offensive as an offer, considering the almost sexual fetish the developer seems to have for shields and I don't want to enable someone's addiction, because it's clearly impacting them. I also have no doubt that, based on my experiences of every other item in this game that you can build, it will be hugely unrewarding to use and massively overpriced for what it does. Rather like Phoenix Point itself, really.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I'm not sure why there are so many negative reviews for this. It's not a perfect game, by any means, but it's a lot of fun and quite similar to XCOM, which is highly reviewed. You probably already know the basics of how this work, so I'll just stick to other thoughts rather than describing the basic gameplay of it being turn-based and tactical with the strategy/resource management level.One thing I like about this game is the way shooting works. Rather than the XCOM style of giving you a percentage chance and you either hit or miss, this one gives you a circle that shows where all your shots will fall, and an inner circle where 50% of your shots will fall. You can just let the game auto-target for you, but the fun and tactics come from free aiming, where you enter a first-person view and aim your soldier's gun yourself. So even if it's a far off target or partially blocked by cover, if you can see any part of the enemy, you can normally get at least some damage on them, since it's not a hit/miss system if you're firing multiple bullets. For example, with assault rifles, you fire 6 rounds, so even with a bad shot you can still get a couple bullets on an enemy rather than missing completely with a low % chance or not taking a shot at all. It's up to you then to decide whether it's worth spending the 6 bullets for a bit of damage or saving them for a better shot, and I like getting to decide that a lot better than "Do I want to try a 30% shot and probably miss and waste my ammo completely?".Another aspect of shooting is that each body part on an enemy is individually targetable, letting you disable body parts for different effects. Maybe you shoot a leg to make them not be able to move as far, or you shoot their head to drop their willpower (if you or an enemy run out of willpowrer, that character panics for a turn). Or you shoot a part to disable a special power they might have, like disabling a torso to stop them from regenerating, or shooting their arm to make them drop a shield they're holding to open them up for shots from other characters who couldn't see around it. Disabling most body parts also causes bleeding, making the character take damage every turn. It adds more tactics than just "Put bullet in enemy, do damage."For negative things I've seen in other reviews, I haven't really had those experiences. The game hasn't been super hard or easy; it's pretty solidly in the middle for me. Just to tell what type of player I am, I'm a light save-scummer: I won't reload a game if I miss a shot or something, but if a character dies, I'll restart the whole mission (I won't just reload a quick-save or something). I've only restarted like 2 missions so far: one where I moved up and got swarmed by enemies who came out of an area I couldn't see, and another where a soldier got some lucky shots on them from a couple of enemies and died. I haven't been grinding; I've explored the map and done missions I've found, but just because I wanted to do them and they give resources and stuff, not to specifically get my soldiers to level up. I guess you might if you were just trying to do main stories, but why would you do that? And I haven't experienced any bugs; the closest I've come is that the overwatch system can occasionally be a little fiddly. If you're in full cover, your soldier can step out to the side to attack enemies, giving you much more of a view to aim at them, but in overwatch, sometimes it hasn't really done that, and my soldier will fire into a wall. But sometimes it does work, so who knows.Overall, this game is fun if you like turn-based tactical games. If you like XCOM, you'll like this. It's close enough so that it has all the same things that made XCOM fun but also has enough differences to keep things interesting rather than just being a plain re-skin.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my '1st run, Veteran (Normal) difficulty. 90h of gameplay. I think this deserves a review.My background: non hardcore gamer, aficcionado for tactical combat games (I grew up playing UFO: Enemy Unknown)If you like tactical combat games (XCOM style, mainly), and can afford to buy this with all the DLC's, go for it. The DLC's ramp up the difficulty even more, but add some (much needed) extra layers to the game. Even in normal mode, it is a difficult game. I recommend splitting your progress into 4-5 save files, because the game eventually likes to checkmate you, and if something like this happens, you'll have an older save file just some hours behind, instead of having to start from scratch again. Use only one save file and you're pretty much doomed (if you 're masochist, or enjoy a hardcore experience try using only 1 save file). What is checkmate looks like in this game? Well, if you somehow get stuck with very low tech resources, and have few vehicles/spare ammunition, and happens to be at war with 1-2 factions and having to deal with pandoran invasions also, you'll have not enough tech to replenish you ammunitions after each fight, and even worse, will have no tech to activate more bases, recruiting and producing (much needed) additional vehicles. If you're playing with the Festering Skies DLC and you only have 1 aircraft and it is blown up when you don't have enough resources to produce another, it's game over.Although the exploration sites add an enjoyable layer of roulette to the game, there are very few kinds of missions in the game, so it may drag forever from half to end. Basically you have scavenging missions (retrieve boxes with resources and evacuate), extermination missions (killing everyone on the map), rescue missions (rescuing something/someone then evacuating), and activating objectives missions (simply getting to a certain point and interacting with the object). The size limit of the map makes the rescue and objective activation missions not very much thrilling, because with enough speed your soldiers can quickly scan the whole map, locate themselves and trace a quick escape route. Almost never you'll need to split your party to search for anything (the exception would be scavenging missions, to finish the more quickly).From mid game to late game the enemies start to have A LOT of HP, so extermination missions drag forever. This, combined to the amount of missions of the same kind you'll have to complete in the game makes the second half of it drags on forever. Also, as the game progresses the factions start wars between themselves, so you'll frequently have to intervene to save their havens, and this add a lot more extermination missions in the second half of the game.I'm not a hardcore gamer, and as such I do not frequently come up with ways to cheese the games I play, but if you want to finish this game below the 100 hour mark I feel you'll have to cheese. There are a lot of class combinations and equipment/abilities interactions that are pure cheese. Also, in this game meelee damage is king. Your meelee fighters are your biggest DPS source (even with the most basic weapons they top most advanced ranged weapons), and they also save you A LOT of ammunition, so protect them well. I didn't like the Stealth mechanic (at least not for the player, bc the computer units always have high Perception values so they are able to detect your stealthed units easily)The A.I in the only difficulty I've played (Veteran - Normal) felt pretty good and not buggy at all. The enemies knew how to position themselves to enhance their DPS and hinder my advance. Maybe in higher difficulties they behave even better.The storyline is good, and the endgame is hard and sactisfatory. I cheesed hard in the last battle and I don't know how can someone can win it without cheesingIn my opinion this game looks like a more streamlined/simpler version of XCOM, which focuses more on combat itself than in managing resources/bases, so as such, I'll recommend it only for players that are already familiarized with XCOM style games.

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to XCom, this feels like a step down but a step up in some places. Being able to dedicate yourself to a faction that rewards you with unique technology or being able to go to war and raid factions is entertaining - Things like the Anu offering biological ascension and New Jericho offering mechanical augmentations makes for good roleplay and options.Overall, it definitely needs to be polished still - The aiming mechanic is good but there are still issues with it, with sometimes not a single bullet hitting a target. Some enemies are just way to easy to kill as well, and it feels like there wasn't much challenge fighting something like the Pandorans, who are supposed to be the thing that caused the end of human civilization once upon the time. In addition, the troops you control feel pretty static and you need to recruit ones that just have useful traits or something you can abuse like bonus accuracy - It doesn't feel too good to just min/max troops instead of having a rookie turn into a badass over time.I'd recommend it if you want a different experience than XCom, but if you were debating this or XCom first, go with XCom to ease yourself into the genre as it's generally more polished. _childDocuments_.review: # SummaryThis is it. This is the ultimate version of X-COM. # ReviewX-COM (originally titled UFO) was created in 1994 by Julian Gollop. It was a wildly successful combination of squad tactics and grand strategy games. There were two sequels which were not quite as good as the original, and a bunch of spin-offs. X-COM was re-made by different people in 2012 and 2016. The remakes had great modern graphics and introduced a lot of features to make gameplay more straightforward. They were successful, and deservedly so. However they were also massively dumbed down in order to appeal to console players and kids who hadn’t been born at the time of UFO. In 2019 Gollop returned to his creation and made the definitive X-COM game. It’s called Phoenix Point because he didn’t own the trademark, but don’t let that fool you into thinking it’s not X-COM. It incorporates the good parts from the remakes (e.g. streamlined gameplay, cover system, solider classes), and it introduces a new 3D aiming system that wasn’t possible in 1994. But underneath it is clearly a sequel to UFO, and is not dumbed down. # ConclusionIf you were a fan of UFO, you will like it. If you were a fan of the remakes, you may not. # Addressing common criticisms “The graphics are not as good as XCOM 2.”Do you play games for the gameplay or for how they look? The graphics are perfectly adequate. “All the weapons are the same; there are no upgrades.”This is not true. In the early game you will acquire access to weapons from four different factions. One set is worse than your starting weapons. The other three are slightly better. People are disappointed that they aren’t arranged in a hierarchy but are instead “side grades”, e.g. one will trade off increased accuracy for lower damage. By not providing a clear “better” weapon the strategic decision making required is increased. However, once you have played for about 50 hours you will begin to acquire unique weapons that are definite upgrades, and after 100 hours you will be able to mass produce upgraded weapons. I suspect many with short attention spans simply never reach this point. “The DLC is bad.”None of the DLC is bad.  The only criticism comes from people who enjoyed the initial (unfinished, I think) release of the game and didn’t like it changed. The ancients DLC does increase the length of the game to a degree that may become tedious. You may turn it off for a shorter game. The air combat DLC doesn’t add much so is a little pointless to buy separately. The corruption DLC makes the game more difficult so you may want to turn it off if you are poor player. But the game was clearly designed to include all the DLCs from the start: they were only split off and released separately for financial reasons because the game wasn’t finished in time.

_childDocuments_.review: I have tremendous fun playing this game.  It's not for everyone.  Anyone buying this expecting XCOM2 will be sorely disappointed.  There are differences that only devoted followers of tactical combat sims will find interesting.  For example, unlike in XCOM2, there is a system that actually upgrades the enemies you face as you progress through the game and even focuses their upgrades based on how you kill previous enemies.  If you like taking out their weapons first, good luck, because they'll add steadily-improving armor to their gun hands.  Like going for their head?  They can add armor to that too.  There's also a free aim feature so that you can decide where each attack your soldiers make targets, necessitating the aforementioned self-modifications.  That is hardly an exhaustive list, but it is two of the most intriguing to me.As I said, this game is not for everyone.  But for those who enjoy it, it will provide months of enjoyable gaming.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenix Point

_childDocuments_.review: If XCOM is paying for a 9.99$ item using two 5$ bills, then Phoenix Point is buying that same item with exact change. While the plethora of choices for every single action you take gives the user freedom to make unique decisions, in my experience it bogs down the game and feels like a chore. The game is very very slow if you want to play well. I'm talking slower than OW crawling in XCOM EU slow. Realistic ballistics is cool, having individual ammo types for guns is immersive, and choosing where to exactly fire your weapon is interesting, but all these added choices quickly cause choice anxiety and start to feel unfun rather quickly. This game, in my opinion, fails because it over complicates the XCOM formula, which it is clearly based on. For those who enjoy the Long War mod, maybe this is more your speed, but I personally think it's just too complicated for the wrong reasons.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. I only played it on the latest releases so I don't know about how the game developed, if it was buggy or badly balanced, as many say. But as it is, it is a very well-conceived experience. Sometimes the best games are not the ones that are universally praised, but the ones that appeal to a very specific kind of audience. This is no doubt that kind of game.

_childDocuments_.review: As I am writing this, I am trying to get a feel for what I would say...I didn't think I had so much to complain about, but once I started with one thing, it lead to another, and another, and another...I genuinly thought I was in the 50/50 weather to recommend it or not, but the more I think about game what it does good, what it does bad... I feel it does more bad than good.So I think the short answer for now is... No, I would not recommend you buy this.If you want to go into why... join me in the wall of text that follows.---------------------------------------Wasted time and directions:A general theme for this text will be, the amount of time they have had to improve the game and... and feel like they did the bare minimum with it, and how it almost feels like all they did for the game was add some DLC which... more or less are complete washes...After all of the time they had before the game was released, with the backing that they got, and then sidestepping their promises to their backers by accepting an Epic exclusivity deal for a year to get an even better cash-out, and then an additional 2 years later, they have sort of made a complete game... but it is still barebones when it comes to QoL fixes.And this game needs it's QoL fixes!!(Now, I wanna be clear, while I was one of the people dissapointed with the Epic exclusivity, I tried to not take it to hard. In my eyes, it was just 1 year more till the game released which would give it time to get bugs fixed and general improvments... Jokes on us I guess...)Unless you have a high tolerance for a game that does not respect your time - and I do not mean disrespect as in your entire squad got killed and you lost hours or days on a campaign, because that is Xcom - no I mean in sheer micromanagment of the systems that are not thought out correctly, or have been improved upon  with how long this game was in the making, and with how long it has been since the game has been released.That said, there are elements that makes the game compeling, but to the point I do not wish to play it because it is so tedious in all the other areas...My hope would be that there would be a Phoenix Point 2 where they would improve on a lot of these areas, but since they didn't bother to do so to until this point. I wonder if a sequal would improve...For example, as of this review, they not to long ago just announced that they are only now - NOW THREEE DAMN YEARS LATER - and only now are they working on making mod support for the game...(I know I am harping the time since this game released, but that is a lot of damn time for a game to have had to improve itself and not done that.)Just... wow... most people have played and forgotten this game - and you expect that people will only now want to get in on the action and mod it? *facepalm*As is, there are only a few mods that have been kept up to date over the years, some more seems to work despite not being updated. And then there are some that would have been lovely if they did work despite not being updated but do not.Like so many things with this game, things that should have been ironed out as the game came out, or at the very least within the first year of its release, then garnering a healthy mod community should have been on the top of your priority.I do HOPE that giving this game the proper workshop support will cause a resurgance of dedicated fans and modders to fix some of the areas that is wrong with this game.Sadly, I do not think this game has enough for that, judging by the not so impresive presence this game has on the modding scene as it is.-------------Design decisions:The positive.It does away with one of the most infuriating aspect of an Xcom game - point blank chances to miss are ALMOST eliminated with its intuative reticle-system for free aiming.It is still a decent amount of "chance" involved, depending on the size of the reticle/accuracy your soldier have. But it atleast make you feel more in control - it gives you a much better visual representation as to how you could miss or hit something, and the ability to specifically try to hit specific parts that are actually visable to you.The reticle system is absolutely the best design decision this game could come up with.On the other hand... EVERY OTHER SYSTEM really feels like a mess, with oversights and wierd design decisions. And I think there is almost atleast one "back breaking" visual glitch on atleast one of my soldiers EVERY SINGLE DAMN FIGHT!Or that there is a mod that have to fix a simple math formula for calculating grenade throw range...Again... 3 years and not fixed.For a game that is really trying to encurage you to have atleast 2 teams ready to patrol at any time - and more as you get later and want to cover more ground - it does an absolute piss poor job of minimizing clicks needed to do what you want to do!And having more than 1 airship to navigate the globe, just ends up being a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ PAIN as you constantly tell one ship to move, and because you asked it to move, it will activate the globe progression... never mind that you have another ship sitting and doing nothing while the clock starts ticking because you asked one thing to move...Thankfully there is a mod that tries to fix this issue the best it can. And it is a god send... I would have stopped playing this game way before if this little gem of a mod didn't exist!FURTHERMOREEquiping more than 1 team is nothing other than a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ chore you tell your parents you forgot about because you didn't want to do it... well here, it is a giant barrier for trying to have fun in the game!Save loadout!3 years, and still no way to set up loadout saves so you can more easily have atleast some core eqipment sets you want to field.There is also the suspension of disbelief that you can remove the gear of your team on one side of the planet, and equip it on the OTHER side of the planet...If anything, I wish the game was made so this was not a thing you could do, ofcourse with a compeltely different balance to cost/time to produce gear.As currently, it is really hard to build enough gear to properly equip multiple squads of soldiers without having to juggle their inventory around. Speaking of inventory... THE INVENTORY MANAGMENT IS HORRENDOUS!!!Holy guaccamole the inventory system sucks!First of, it still bugs out where it does not want to properly update whenever you try to select which class you want to filter out. 3 years people!Never mind that filtering by class is THE DUMBEST ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ way to sort ♥♥♥♥ out at! It still leaves you with an absolute crap ton of items to filter through. Not to mention the screen leaves a lot of real-estate that it could use to help filter out the items better.Some DLC's does not meld well with the game in my opinion.Addon like the Festering skies is thematicly fitting and interesting, but it feels like what it adds is almost just some variations of what is already there, it feels somewhat low effort.Except for the flight combat... with is the dullest, most boring, most unintuative ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ flight combat I have ever seen!!! Holy hell it is SO BORING AND BLAND!!!!! Like, you could just have done the original Xcom flight combat, and that would have been 10 times better. Sure, many people would have called that lazy, but it would at the very least be more fun and interesting than whatever this is... and Original Xcom was made 28 years ago... and their air combat was better.And sure, it wants to add this one custom made mission to kick start the ordeal, but it just ends up making the thing feel like it doesn't belong more than naturally intergrate in your campaign.That will have to do as there is no more space to write.Again, at first I was having a hard time recommending it, but after thinking about it, I would clearly not recommend it.You can not make a game on ONE good change alone... Which this game tried to do.

_childDocuments_.review: While I love the physically-modeled projectiles, this game is seriously flawed compared to the original 1994 game by this designer, and the Firaxis remakes. The maps are small and not varied, and what tactical options are afforded, if there are any, favor the enemies. (My favorite is the fortress map where you start on open ground against enemies with rocket launchers, because your troops are too stupid to approach through the buildings.) The constant onslaughts of ever-more-powerful aliens, while your troops stay unchanged except for higher damage numbers, quickly become tedious instead of fun. Play the 1994 original, or play XCOM2 with all the DLC, for more nuanced challenges.Oh, and turn off Legacy of the Ancients. It brings nothing but more tedium, with the prizes being weapons that, by the time you slog through to them, aren't *that* much better than what you ressearched without the grinds required.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, I've spent like 40 more hours playing this game. My original review (reproduced below) is no longer particularly accurate. The game is still pretty joyless, but it is... better. You'd still be better off playing any other XCOM-like.Here's the thing: this game is full to the brim with amazing ideas. Factions, varied playstyles and weaponry, interesting tactical layer. There are like 5 cool games in here.Except it's like they're playing all 5 series of The Wire at the same time. Maybe it'd still be enjoyable if you've seen The Wire a few times, but not as much as a focused approach.Cuz the DLC added a TON of cool fixes. But it's completely opaque what you're supposed to do with all these new things, or how they work together. Hell, I'm like 60 hours into this game and there are still VERY BASIC things I do not understand. Like how likely my soldier is to hit. They saw they had problems. They threw the kitchen sink at them. And now it feels like drowning in the sink.Maybe if you turn off the DLC it'd be more manageable, but I suspect it would be more anemic as well. There are just fundamental decisions that are faulty. Why are there dozens of kinds of weapons with different ammunition that are WORSE that your starting weapons? Why is constantly being out of equipment fun? What's the pacing on the human population destruction. Am I doing well? HAVE I EVEN HIT THE MIDGAME.Here's the wild thing: maybe I'd buy Phoenix Point 2. I sure wouldn't crowdfund it, but... I want this game to be good. And it's better. But now it's impenetrable instead of broken. It's joyless. I wanna love this. But I'm gonna see how Xenonauts 2 is. ORIGINAL REVIEW:Has it come to this?I was one of those foolish legion of kickstarter backers. I backed with confidence. I moved on. I was pissed when they decided to go Epic exclusive despite their promises. I didn't want to use their weird wire transfer service for a refund, so I got the Epic version. I played it a little, and there was a weird bug hunt mission where enemies kept coming and I could not find the nest or whatever and I was done.But then it finally came to steam, where I was told I could get it. And it had all these wild expansions or whatever. So I tried it, and it's fine I suppose but I don't know why the game feels so stingy. But I resolve to soldier on. But none of that matters when the game starts crashing on one of the earliest main plot missions.This game was a mistake from day one, and it's still a mistake now with years of development. This game is infuriating. This game is an utter failure. All I needed was a half decent tactics game that ran well enough. And you couldn't even provide that in your "year one edition."I want my money back, Julian Gollop.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy the game, but the amount of tactical combat, ironically, can be too high sometimes. I frequently find myself queuing for three encounters in a row, which quickly gets repetitive (especially in the end-game, when there are usually 3-5 pending haven defense events, so at some point I just stop bothering). With this amount of encounters, the game doesn't let me spend nearly enough time on the global map, which also slows down any research and construction, making the game to progress extremely slowly. I realize it's a bit unorthodox and maybe defats the core gameplay purpose, but having auto-revolve mechanic for some battles would be really helpful to deal with the sheer amount of repetitive encounters, such as clearing nests and defending havens.Other than that, there are some balance issues, especially related to the antediluvian weapons. In fact, the entire Legacy Of the Ancients DLC doesn't fit the plot too well, ending up in a situation where we're looking for a proof about antediluvian existence AFTER having excavated their artifacts and even manufacturing their weapons. The weapons themselves are too overpowered and more or less easily obtainable, so by mid-game I have most of my troops carrying end-game weapons that don't even require ammunition. Most of the advanced weapons tech comes way later, and by then it makes no sense to research or manufacture them, because they are weaker and need ammo.Despite the abovementioned flaws, I've had my share of fun with the game and would like to thank the developers for making it! Great work, guys! I especially enjoyed reading The Briefing volumes during the development, which was likely the main reason I was waiting for the game to finally come out on Steam.

_childDocuments_.review: I am pretty torn about this game (disclaimer: I'm an avid fan of Gollop's original X-Coms, the first one I literally played it for many summers during my childhood). And this really and truly feels like the spiritual of successor of those games in many areas. So why is the negative rating? As much as I enjoy it, I can't really recommend it. It's just simply... too ambivalent on so many levels.Every amazing feature comes with a huge blowback. Every DLC is a mixture of joy and pain. The quality of life is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ abysmal in this game. And last, but not least, there are still glitches and bugs in the game. Not major ones, but for the love of god, this stuff is on the market LITERALLY FOR YEARS.In it's core, it's really a modern X-Com, seems and feels that Gollop tried to pack everything in a neat package he ever wanted. On the surface looks and plays amazing, huge and wide range of customization, along with a vast sandbox world to play with. Then you start hitting the issues. The enemies scale up pretty fast and while your equipment improves, nowhere near to the enemies' capability. For example there is a single tier of armor upgrade and that's it. Which is manageable (larger teams, you learn the ins and outs of the game), but makes the long series of fights a tedious grind and takes away the joy of the original X-Coms of sending your troops in battle with new gear almost constantly.Then you suddenly start to realize that some of the essential gameplay stuff is locked behind DLCs (I'm talking about you, hibernation pods). Which aforementioned DLCs either bring frustation or (and) represent a serious sink of resources with barely any or minimal return. Talking about resources, it's super-essential here how you manage them. Then you suddenly realize that the game ♥♥♥♥♥ you over in many aspects. For example you can't scrap vehicles. God knows why. Just imagine that in the original X-Com you couldn't sell your Interceptors, Skyrangers, tanks and no, you can't manufacture stuff here to sell with profit (hello Laser Rifles from the original X-Com) to mitigate the dent on your budget.Then comes the quality of life. The overwatch feature seems nice at the beginning, then you realize that even your veteran soldiers will happily shoot their comrades in overwatch, because you didn't set up the reaction cone in a pixel-perfect way. Or, the grenade launcher trajectory and UI shows that you can hit something, but no, that grenade will explode by hitting something mid-air. Was it your last grande or last action in the turn? Tough luck!Or I could talk about the geoscape. Soon, you will have around a half dozen aircrafts flying around, which -if Festering Skies is enabled- will get even more bloated, as you will need aircrafts for intercepting enemy flyers and troop transporting ones to react to POIs, missions, haven defenses, etc. And transporting troops and vehicles between bases. Yes, the old system is gone, where you gave the transport order, now, you have to manually taxi the aforementioned troops and vehicles by aircraft. A ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ abysmal ♥♥♥♥, no idea how it went through the playtesting. To add injury to the insult, you can deploy 8 soldiers for a mission (have no illusions, you will need each and every one of them) and the single aircraft capable of transporting 8 troopers is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slow that the Pandorans can kill a half continent until it gets from A to B. Which means, that each of your teams (you need at least 2 separate task force, ideally 3) are loaded up in 2 separate aircrafts. Wait, did I mention that one of the DLCs require you to park a manned aircraft at POIs? So, have fun with managing 8-10 flying ♥♥♥♥ moving around and keeping track each one of them, responding to crisises, handling missions, intercepting flying ♥♥♥♥, trade runs, troop hiring, haven defense, clearing pandoran bases, etc, etc, etc.In all fairness and bottom line is... if you were a fan of the original X-Coms, go for it. Otherwise there is a fair chance you will be disappointed. It not only replicates the feeling of the original X-Coms, but also feels like -quality of life and difficulty- a game from the 90s. Not in a good sense.

_childDocuments_.review: The hate due to the EPIC Store choice is far over the top and has nothing to do with the quality of the game. I already played this for a while on EGS to have a tad more insight while didn't beat the full game (I was waiting for achievements on STEAM actually).Phoenix Point is the first game of this kind that is actually of the quality of the newer XCOM. It has some fresh ideas like adapting opponents and a slightly different approach in gameplay that reminds strongly to the Long War mod mechanics. The atmosphere is great and the strategic layer works quite well. On this regard it even has some more depth than the 201x XCOM games.Character development works nice too. It is a good mixture between the "build your godlike soldier squad" of XCOM new and the "soldiers are only cannon fodder" of the older games. I really like it Important to know is that this one is not as easy as the "overwatch trap and win" xcoms are. Especially in midgame this game can become brutal if you did wrong decisions hours before. This can actually lead to a loss in campaign which might be demotivating for some.Another plus is that this game gets still DLCs so development is still not finished and more content will be added.If you had fun with the new XCOMs and don't mind a challenge from time to time then you will most likely enjoy this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried really hard to like this game, as a big SRPG and X-com fan.Tried it on launch, found it too buggy so left it alone until this year with the year one edition. My main issues with the game didn't really change, some parts just feel incomplete/unpolished, I can think of a few times the enemy straight out cheated (such as running just outside your overwatch cone and attacking you from behind) and general frustration late game with a large amount of status debuffs and not enough mission variety on top of too many reinforcements.I've heard good things about the Terror from the Void mod which might fix my grievances, sadly that requires all of the DLC so I'm not willing to invest even more funds for the hope to find the game enjoyable again.The game definitely has potential, being able to target body parts and generally consistent damage helps you get around most of the RNG from other like games, so at least you'll be dealing some damage most of the time and some good QOL which give you more time to play and less organising your inventory or your squads.tl;dr The game still has a lot of room for improvement, buy the complete edition on sale if you are interested for the best experience with the new mod.

_childDocuments_.review: 5/10 game, story (World building, characters, lore etc) is the reason I rate it higher.Annoying design decisions or limitations on interface when trying to navigate between menus and transfer units, and find items and such.They should have included a search bar for text searching, and also should have made pop up selection windows instead of having a menu be an entirely new screen. Also should have put the Go To Base Location button on the main map for easier location of base when travelling with the ship to transfer units etc.Sloggish over-lengthy combat that did not need to be, especially when it feels like 80+% of missions are go to X point across the entire map and its a huge fight along the way, then have another non ending fight while trying to reach the opposite side of the map. Make some of these missions auto complete when you reach the item to collect instead of having them all extract on opposite side. In general the game is too lengthy during missions because of the amount of them you have to play in if you're trying to run a full length experience; this is made far worse when the difficulty ramping is ridiculous on the lowest difficulty that if you don't use a particular build or have a large enough team, or particular items, that could be the exact mistake along with other in game RNG that completely wrecks you and wastes hours upon hours.Outside of cheese builds, there are very specific options that allow you to do okay, but because of the nature of the largely area of effect enemy attacks or single target burst from the enemy, its extremely easy to lose a single well trained fully equipped unit with the best equipment and armor.The cover system and destructible environment is great, but also still doesn't solve the situation due to enemy position spawns or sparse cover which forces you to either clump and be vulnerable to area of effect; or spread out and not have sufficient cover to be taken down by burst strikes.With the length of combats and travel and wait times the game becomes extremely lengthy and NOT in a good way. Everything takes too long; especially towards the end game when everyone including the enemy constantly gets upgraded to match your upgrades. Which because of the constant death spiral (hard pressed resources even when trading and base attacks and various building goals it's difficult to keep everything going without feeling a constant crushing pressure and not in a good way that would bring to mind "Balanced" (Which TRUE BALANCE, is not what a player desires, and unfortunately this seems to deliver a truer balance) thus delivering the crushing pressure.)Now this wouldn't be an issue if it was on the normal or harder difficulties perhaps; but this is all on ROOKIE difficulty. If one is playing for the story, then this is a serious balancing problem. I've put far too many hours into this game without joy.Waiting for the next research unlock, awaiting the next grind, and avoiding the extreme difficulty mission because of soldiers had completed 1 or 2 already and need to heal before going back in because I'm not using the cheese build, which has lost potency since the updates from what I've been reading.So in their desire to "balance" the game, and remove cheese, they forgot their lower difficulties would need adjustment.Had some great mechanical ideas, and story seemed okay; but ultimately the game play balance leaves much to be desired, because one shouldn't be taking this long to progress in the game if they want to experience it all.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun game. Looks just like XCOM2, but feels a bit more like the old school X-Com games from the 90s. Rewards more cautious play. Less like a board game, more like a simulation. The AI seems not all that smart but it's still challenging because enemies have superior numbers and abilities. The game has changed a lot over time so check the date on user reviews.Parting thought: People always complain about missing from one tile away in XCOM games. Here they fixed it with bullet physics and direct aiming and people complain about that instead. Some people just like to complain. Usually those people are bad at the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like Phoenix Point. I prefer it over the new XCOM games, both the tactical combat and the geoscope strategy are better. The tactical combat is physical based, so it's not just about being behind cover or not, but the actual type of cover and any other types of cover even those that are farther away but between the target and the attcker, they all affect the chance to hit. You can aim manually which makes it even more interesting. The strategy layer gives you a lot of freedom - what you do, which bases you build, what you spend resources on, etc. It's still not as good as the original 90s XCOM, but it's definitely better than the remakes. All in all, it's a pretty fun game by its own merit.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Don't get this game if you want to play an XCOM-like game. You'll be disappointed.I've played all the Firaxis Games: XCOM Enemy Unknown, XCOM 2, XCOM Chimera Squad (side note, Chimera Squad isn't great in my opinion but is definitely an interesting take and could be worth the buy, try it out for the trial period, but it doesn't really feel like a full XCOM game, more like a short spin off with no character customization). XCOM:EU and XCOM 2 were great. Good story, good progression, amazing character customization, great mods, immersive story and as hard as you want it to be. You can basically make any play style work if you build for it. This just feels like a reskinned shell of an XCOM game. The cut scenes are just a slideshow with no animations, game doesn't look like it was made recently (graphics meh), the base management looks like a mobile game and literally a 1-1 rip off of the management from XCOM but way worse. It's just tiles on a screen instead of something that resembles a base at all. The things that are tedious, like grabbing resources from bins and avoiding the poison mist is just annoying rather than adding anything to the gameplay. I haven't played that long but I've tried it two times in the span of a year and both times I basically got through the tutorial and physically couldn't bring myself to play it. Unfortunately I waited too long to return it.It LOOKS like XCOM, but the important parts of XCOM'S soul are missing. Story, aesthetics, tedious in the wrong ways, etc. Not a buy from me especially if you are trying to scratch the XCOM itch.XCOM-like games that would be good to trial and see if you like are:1. Jagged Alliance 3, hire mercanaries and use ww2ish guns if you are looking for something fun that doesn't take itself too seriously.2. Battletech if you like mechs. There is no cover system so it's mostly based on armor, movement and over powering with weapons. Kinda cool, LOTS of management. If you are a min/max-er, you'll spend 80% of the game trying different mech builds and in the base/mech management screen. Jumpjets are SUPER fun to mess around with.3. Hard West Series if you like Westerns.4. Gears Tactics (Gears of War) is a classic at this point.5. I'm trying Othercide right now, haven't played enough to have an opinion on it.P.S. @MortismalGaming on YouTube has some great reviews on XCOM-like turn based games.

_childDocuments_.review: Hours on review are not quite accurate, played alot of this on the EGS as I was a backer and was fine with their reasoning of needing the cash from epic and I feel the results of it have been worth it. And they honored their word to give backers an additional key on the platform of their choice, so here I am. Now on to the actual review.Seen people comparing this to Xcom 2, which is of course fair in one regard as it is from the guys that made the originals, and not the most fair in another. For one thing they are on different engines, which means an entirely different feel. And for another one of the major differences is that Xcom 2 was directly following Xcom: Enemy Unknown (yes i know, duh, but there is a point here) and as such had a fairly set goal they were going for, where as Phoenix Point is going for their own thing.For example, the free aim system, and the real bullet trajectory, is a much better option than the 99% misses that xcom EU and 2 are famous for. Another major difference is while it does have a "doom clock" type system as Xcom 2 does, the real threat is the game has a system for the "Aliens" adapting to your combat style. So in Xcom 2, once you saw an enemy type you knew pretty much all you need to to fight it for the rest of the game; here, if you get too comfortable with easy headshots with free aim, they will mutate to get more armor on their head to make that less effective, or will be more resistant to explosions if you are very grenade happy, etc. For those of us that played Xcom 2: WotC, there was alot of talk of how the various factions didnt get along and were ready to attack each other as much as the Aliens, and then it was just resolved in like 2 and half missions and nothing really was different than 3 new unit types; this game has its three factions actually have agendas that conflict with each other, up to the point of the factions even going to war with each other over those agendas. Not to harp too much on the disappointing factions of WotC, but remember how, while cool and worked in the new system, the only real reward for improving relations with the factions was new cards, or sometimes another of their unique class unit, and otherwise you could just ignore them and not really impact the game much? Phoenix has different tech trees that are unique to each faction, and you can only get them by earning favor with that faction by doing quests for them, siding with that faction against the others, or by attempting to steal the tech at the cost of upsetting that faction.To finish comparing them, even though at the start i said it wasnt entirely fair but it is the best reference point, the tactical and strategic elements. For one thing instead of unlimited flight via the Avenger In Xcom 2, the manticore ships have set amounts of fuel per movement and have to able to link paths to be able to move to a location. Another difference is that, as opposed to Xcom 2 where you just sit waiting for something to happen that you go to, Phoenix requires you to actually preform scans of your area to find events and looting areas. Yet another serious difference is that in Xcom 2, the tactical was the heavy focus as the strategic just resulted in modifiers for the missions; Phoenix is a little more strategic minded. Yes it is still choices and popups on the global map that then influence what you can do in the tactical battles, but it is more than just "this enemy type now has armor" or "this mission is now available 3 turns earlier than previously". In this case it is down to choosing between helping this enclave to get favor for this faction which leads to new tech to increase your effectiveness attacking this Pandora base, or doing this time sensitive event over here for different faction thus angering the one faction but receiving a direct reward from the other that then can help you deal with this other Pandora base over here that has been causing issues for this third enclave that you are using for resources and recruitment. It is alot more dense and confusing that Xcom 2's method, which works well for how that game is structured, but overall pays off more, in my opinion, cause you are invested in each micro detail as opposed to just telling your troops which alien to shoot first to get resources for which ever tech you selected first this time around; which in turn adds to replayability more than the set events that are pulled from a fairly static pool.Overall, I feel this game is at least as good as Xcom 2, and WotC expansion, if not better in several/most regards; and well worth the purchase.For a more numerical label. Xcom 2 WotC is 7.7-8.9/10 for this type of game and Phoenix Point is at least the same if not a 8-9 /10

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game for fans of X-COM. It's long, difficult, with lots of customization options and multiple endings.The campaign feels much longer than the newer X-COM games, but there are a few quality of life features missing. For example: soldiers don't break glass before shooting through, so if you shoot through glass, the first bullet (or in the case of shotguns all of the pellets) won't make it through. At the same time, there are some welcome new features. The diplomacy systems are a nice addition, though the faction ideologies are a bit shallow and cartoonish.Some features, like secret weapons you can obtain, feel a bit undercooked (you need specific resources and processing sites, which can be frustrating because they very difficult encounters, but you don't have an easy way to tell what type of site you're assaulting beforehand). The mutation and augmentation features are great and add a lot of customization, but most of the options are basically slightly better versions of armour. I found a few combinations that worked really well for specific builds and basically never deviated. That said, between mutations, augmentations, combination classes, gear and unique items, and character-specific abilities, the character build variety is pretty good.Overall, it's really good! The tone feels more bleak, more desperate, than the X-COM games. It feels like the stakes are higher. It's a bit jankier, but ambitious games usually are.

_childDocuments_.review: The parts where Phoenix Point shines aren't enough to overshadow the parts where it lacks. 4/10The whole premise behind this game had me hooked from the start. A new take on the moderately done to death alien invasion made me think "Yeah, this one will be a good one!"... Then they went Epic Exclusive for a year, so I forgot about it. Was browsing my queue and it popped up and I decided to grab it. Now, it was 50% off, but still cost me $42.47 AUD (), would definitely not buy it at full price. I was expecting to get maybe 80 hours of fun out of this one, but I got to about 16 before it was just too much to bear.The Good- The combat is decent. The whole aim cone system is new and cool.- The body part targeting and health pools was fairly well done (though I feel like if you disable somebody's head it should kill them...)- The action points are good, both in design and utilisaion. Moving 1m only uses a portion of the action point bar, which was something I appreciated, compared to newCOM where you move a step and oops you only have 1AP left.The Bad- The aiming needs some sort of indicator (like for example, A PERCENTAGE), because just because I can see the tip of somebody's arm doesn't mean I should necessarily shoot at it. When the cover is blocking 95% of the enemy but the camera angle makes it look like its a good shot, I find myself always checking the free aim then being disappointed. Maybe putting a red tinge to obstacles in the aim cone or something might've helped.- Cover feels overpowered and useless at the same time. Full cover protects you from most attacks while half cover feels like it does nothing.- YOU CAN'T EQUIP A SHIELD AND A PISTOL AT THE SAME TIME LIKE WTFThe Good- The Pandorans (the main enemy) feel fresh and interesting, and the way they evolve is pretty cool.The Bad- The Geoscape map feels kinda clunky, and I don't really have an explanation as to why.- I had multiple instances of cinematics just failing to play, or just freezing mid way through.- I'm not a fan of the geopolitical shenanigans that are going on. I just want to be able to help humanity best as I can, but it feels like the game is forcing you to pick and choose between the factions, and I hate how the diplomacy missions are to attack the other factions. It feels like the game actively punishes you if you aren't attacking or stealing resources or aircraft from the different factions.- The inventory management. I feel like they decided for a simple design when they shouldn't have. Xenonauts did the inventory management really well imo, it had an infinite number of standard equipment - projectile firearms, grenades ect that you could just chuck on your new recruits. Oh whats that, you hired a new guy? Too bad you don't have any weapons/armor for him to use. That'll be 500 materials and 9 days to fully equip them.- The research felt more like a check list than progression. In Xenonauts and newCOM you started with projectile weapons, worked your way through to get laser and plasma weapons or whatever, but it doesn't seem like that's there for Phoenix Point. No, you gotta steal it from the factions or be allied with them to get access to research it. And half the time the newer stuff is barely an upgrade. Not a fan.- There's probably more I could add here but these were the main things that came to mind.At the end of the day, I probably over-hyped this game for myself and expected way too much. It honestly felt like I was playing an early access game. Maybe it gets better later into the game but it just ended up feeling like a chore that I didn't want to invest my time into. I'm sure there are plenty of people that are having a blast with this game, but I just couldn't get into it. Maybe I'll come back later and have a better time with it, who knows.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's star with positives. Shooting mechanics is fresh and interesting. You have to see target or its parts and aim at it. Damaging body parts disable them. this is especially useful against enemies with guns, as you can break arms so they cannot shoot you. Sadly, that works for you too and there is only on class (technician) that can fix broken arm. To make it worse, most common type of enemy, can regenerate. So disabling them has no effect.Other thing in tactical combat is continuous spawns. On some maps, you have to do the thing and retreat. This wit combination that you have to pay for ammo (this is main resource drain) makes it quite annoy.Overall, the game quality decrease over time. Early game, research has lots of flavor text, but longer you play, you get almost now extra info after you finish research. Also most research is irrelevant, it gives nothing interesting or better. Like having +15% damage on enemy that needs one shoot to kill. That is just lazy. You will also get most of the weapons and armor early game.Mid game, you found out, that nothing really matters. _childDocuments_.review: I’ll be keeping my original review below, but I’m changing this to a thumbs down due to a gamebreaking bug where loading a save causes the enemies to do nothing on their turn. It’s easy to reproduce and has been in the game since launch apparently. Shame on the developers for not fixing something this egregious for LITERAR YEARS. Also, the lategame balancing is horrendous. You either run a squad of mostly Sniper Infiltrators with Thief, Sniperist, or Farsighted (with maybe the token Heavy Technician or two for warcry, healing, turrets, and electric reinforcment support) or give an Assault/Berserker with the Strongman perk a heavy machine gun and watch him wipe the entire ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ map in one turn, maybe with a Priest to soften them up with mindcrushes. The game is a complete slog if you don’t at least employ one of these two strategies, and preferably you actually employ both at the same time. The game stopped producing flow state after the early game. It was much too hard in the midgame, and way way WAY too easy in the lategame with max level multiclassed soldiers. Additionally, because the perks you get with max level soldiers are what make the lategame so easy, this doesn’t make them difficult to replace, it makes them IRREPLACABLE. This is similar to Colonels in Firaxis XCOMs but in a game where new recruits and gear do not cost a small amount of resources. They cost a lot. Which is very strange consider this game is from the creator of the original X-COM, a game where losing soldiers was manageable so long as you had good logistics in place to replace them. So long as you had the resources to replace the soldiers you lost you could keep going after soldier deaths. The soldier leveling and perks being the factor that helps you scale with the aliens is honestly a dealbreaker. I don’t want a hero squad romp. I want a gritty, realistic campaign where my soldiers die but I push forward knowing I can replace them with someone who, while less capable, is still competent enough to face the alien threat so long as I give them the best gear I have available. I don’t want a game where I know that if I don’t reload/restart when one of my soldiers dies, the new soldier I replace them with will be very useless for a long time, and will probably never catch up to the same power level as the rest of my squad due to the incremental SP per mission system and the way SP converts into raw stats and unlocks abilities. Soldiers don’t max out when they reach max level, they max out after 50-150 missions depending on the difficulty. A soldier death should not be a permanent setback you can never recover from. It should be a temporary setback until you get a rookie through a dozen missions or so. I’m 100% ok with needing veteran soldiers to go toe to toe with the aliens. What I’m not ok with is how long it takes to train a rookie up to replace one of those veterans. Sure you can throw rookies into a base with loads of training centers to somewhat quickly get them to level 7, but because of the per mission SP system, those soliders will inevitably be too weak in terms of stats and/or number of unlocked abilities. Even in XCOM 2 WOTC, soldiers do not earn additional ability points when they are at max level! You only get extra for the shared pool, WHICH MAKES SO MUCH SENSE. Having a hard individual soldier cap means the enemies which also scale up to a hard cap can tailored precisely to the max power level of your soldiers to create an appropriate challenge. This doesn’t happen in Phoenix Point, because your soldiers individually scale in strength continuously over the entire campaign, which means it’s impossible to create enemies that will scale appropriately with any squad that loses members, because the replacements will ALWAYS be weaker than the rest of the squad, creating a permanent power reduction setback.My original review is below, but keep in mind it only really applies to the early game which, while fun, doesn’t last long:This game is cursed Firaxis XCOM. If you can look past the relatively low production values and unforgiving difficulty you'll find a worthy successor the original X-COM: UFO Defense that approaches the modern turn-based tactics genre in a way that doesn't devolve into killing everything before the enemy gets a turn. I would say this game is the geoscape of XCOM 2: War of the Chosen, but with much less linearity. The map is open for you to explore rather than simply making resistance contacts, completing routine missions, and choosing when to raid alien facilities. Instead of a single base you can restore a network of bases. There is not one set story mission progression, there are multiple objective paths with various outcomes. The tactical battles are much closer to XCOM: Enemy Within. No turn timers returns things to the slower paced long range combat that inevitably became much less common in XCOM 2: War of the Chosen. Overall the game is good, but don't expect the flair of Firaxis XCOM games, it's not here. This game is much more grim, cold, and apocalyptic, with factions that actually go to war with each other, and a narrative that is devoid of lightheartedness. In Phoenix Point, the only guarantees are death or save scumming. Lost soldiers are much more difficult to replace, and tech will not be enough in the absence of powerful veterans. Though if all else fails, you can bring an armored car with a missile launcher. Just keep in mind it has limited ammunition.

_childDocuments_.review: From all the Epic Store exclusives,  was one of the most anticipated by fans worldwide, who just like me, couldn’t wait for the Steam version. I had the pleasure to review it a year ago, so please take in consideration that my Steam play time does not reflect my experience with . In fact, my playtime of 120 hours on Epic, could barely justify this review, since the included content is just subliminally impressive and will give you at least 300 hours of solid gameplay.From the man himself, Mr. Julian Gollop, the mind behind X-COM, comes , a video game that borrows the elements that made his work so famous for, into a new generation of gamers, and classic fans such as myself. To better understand the importance of , try to imagine Star Wars classics, but made in today’s age, while still being the most epic movies you could imagine.Some say classics are classics due to their nostalgia and although they serve as inspiration, they cannot be replicated. However, in this particular case, the well known British producer and designer actually managed to create an instant classic, with all the gameplay, visuals and style we could only hope for.When the time came to create a universe and a solid story-line, Snapshot Games did what I always considered to be the best approach. Pick something real, and expand it using your own imagination, and thus here we are, with the Pandoravirus: originally discovered by scientists in Antarctica back in 2013, it serves as the main event behind .After the entire planet fell into obscurity by death, violence and monstrosity creatures, a special unit entitled  was created, to fight and contain such mutations. Now, with the full universe waiting for you, the goal is simple: Find, restore and equip fallen bases.As you expected,  is a turn-based strategy game, where you’ll control a unit composed of a certain number of soldiers. You take turns in exploring, attacking and if needed, cover other soldiers on the field. The gameplay is impeccable, allowing players to customize their soldiers from the ground up. Train their abilities, set their skills and put them to the test on the battlefield.Soldiers grow in skill and can become experts in specific weapon types, to further boost the inflicted damage. While in turns, you take control of each soldier, and you can even select what part of your enemy you want to shoot at. It reminds me of V.A.T.S, from the Fallout series. It works as intended, allowing for perfect head-shots or nailing that weak spot.While traversing the universe, you’ll come across three distinct factions that live by their own set of rules. The Disciples of Anu which are a strict religious group, New Jericho are the ones who firmly believe in purity of the human body, and in the end we have Synedrion, which are those who embraced technology and aim to become one with it.he game allows you to choose who you want to support, and while exploring the universe, several side-quests will pop-up. It’s impossible to be diplomatic with everyone, and sometimes one choice will benefit one group, above others. It’s also possible to try and scam these factions, as well as commit acts of thievery towards them.When it comes to performance,  is very well optimized, even for a game running on Unity. There have been several patches that considerably improved its performance and stability, which ended up reflecting on the visuals.I really like the visuals, it has a fantastic color palette, very alien-like, with a genuine touch and inspiration from its own story related events. I’m very happy with this decision since I have a tremendous passion for monsters that somehow resemble insects and sea life organisms. It’s absolutely amazing to see how beasts evolved into such colossus!With a solid presentation and a magnificent campaign, emphasizing exploration and player choices among factions, there is no doubt that  is one of the most important tactical turn-based strategy games out there, and the perfect Christmas present if you’re a fan of the genre.
