_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This game needs several mods to be even borderline playable.  And even then, I really just wanted to go back and play Xcom 2 with the Long War 2 mod.  Game starts out fine, but ends up getting worse and worse as you progress.Unlike Xcom, soldiers don't really progress stat wise as they level, and plateau hard.  Their power is almost entirely gated by equipment and/or augmentations, and even then, you will hit the performance cap relatively quickly as there aren't really any god tier capstone abilities when hitting the level cap.  Hell, their accuracy doesn't even improve!  Meanwhile, the enemy is constantly researching better tech that can take out troops (by surprise) in a single turn.  Classes are oversimplified and lack a lot of major unique abilities, and each soldier you recruit gets 3 random passives that may either be really strong for their class, or outright useless.  (Needs to be modded.)Enemies will spawn out of LOS almost randomly around the outside of the map during most missions, and may even be completely invisible unless you rush them thanks to humans having ridiculously low perception, even in sniper gear.  Some enemies can call in reinforcements once every other turn.  This is only compounded further by almost all enemies having nightvision, and therefore can see twice as far as you can at night.  Apparently, nightvision is not built in to hyper advanced suits of armor???  (Really needs to be a mod for built in nightvision.)Vehicles cannot be reloaded in combat, so they are straight up useless after a few turns.  Oh, and they take up 3 soldier's worth of space on dropships.  (Needs to be modded.)Advanced soldier customization like mechanical and biological augmentations are only slightly better (or outright worse at times) than just having a suit of armor, which is incredibly disappointing as they cost a lot of resources.  You are also only able to modify 2 out of 3 body components (head/torso/legs) for some reason?  Meanwhile, exoskeletons from Xcom2 let you mount advanced weapons on top of a heavy mobility/defense boost.  (Needs to be modded.)Bugs:  Here we are, years after release and there are still major gamebreaking bugs.  Some items like backback mounted weapons and some abilities like "Dash" and "Overwatch" can bug out if you use them and reload the save.  This bug prevents you from using them for the next turn.Enemies and allies also regularly don't get a turn for some reason.DLC: It's honestly kind of pathetic that I felt the DLCs subtracted from/did not add anything to the game.  Festering Skies sucks (seriously, don't enable that DLC), Legacy of the Ancients had incredibly repetitive missions all with the same reskinned and tedious enemies, Kaos Engines may as well not even be a DLC with how little impact it has on your gameplay thanks to how expensive its items are, the new "Muton" soldiers from Corrupted Horizons are only slightly better than base soldiers in specific areas, and straight up WORSE in others  (Similar to the advanced customization options mentioned earlier)  Corrupted Horizons also adds one of the most infuriating enemies that will show up in every single mission and call reinforcements until you kill it.  Since it can cross half the map in a single turn, sometimes you can't deal with them at all.  My advice: Avoid unless on sale, and browse the mods on NexusMods before you start your playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried really hard to like this game, and honestly there is a lot to like. My issue was that, unlike XCOM and similar titles, there was no significant feeling of progression. The late-game weapons and armour felt like the barest upgrade over the starting kit. There was never a feeling of progressing through a story, just an endless slog of disjointed missions until getting enough research to complete one of the 5 endings (spoiler alert: it's the same mission for all 5, all that changes is which colour doodad you insert into the final objective).Which brings me to the missions and maps: there was just very little diversity. The maps were all pretty much the same, with the same layouts repeated over and over. Even special operations rarely had unique maps, which was disappointing.Overall, it wasn't a *bad* game in spite of these issues, it has a lot to like. The class-blending was a fun touch that helped each operative feel unique. Having the ability to field multiple teams and aircraft definitely added an extra layer of strategy, as positioning became very important. But the reason I can't recommend the game is because everything started to feel like a chore about 1/3 of the way through. It might be worth checking out if you really like this kind of game, but I can't bring myself to give it a wholehearted recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: After I've read some negative comments I had to try it myself. Interesting story, seemingly strategic and all you'd expect from XCOM-like game, but soon after a dozen hours you start to see the game buggy aspects of it. At first, I really liked the aiming system, which felt way better than that of newer XCOM games, but that very quickly turned out to be just a fancier way to miss your target from even from close range. You'd think you'll make the shot if the whole cross-hair along with both circles is on an enemy's body, right? - wrong, it's the 99% shot missed case all over again, but this time you'll miss 3 of those shots in a row or miss them because of some idiotic hitbox or you won't be able to target an enemy because some horribly designed aiming angle that makes no sense - such as trying to aim down from a roof at an enemy that's standing 4 tiles away from a wall. Overwatch will very often seem useless as soldiers will face wrong direction while in cover, overwatch cone will be 50% of the time blocked by a wall where it absolutely should not as the soldier does not step-out from cover to make it viable. Some times shots will go through enemies. Snipers, unsurprisingly, feel like they're cross-eyed - they consistently miss targets - mid-range, long-range... Enemy assault will hit your sniper before your sniper will ever hit the enemy. Simply put, neither this nor any previous game of same type is genuinely difficult because of AI or the gameplay difficulty - no. It's the stupid bugs, moronic mechanics and bad design that makes the game difficult. Wish I could write more good things about the game but there cannot be any strategy when you are being robbed of important shots over and over again and you're just getting rigged into losing. I've endured similar experience in XCOM2 with around 1k hours, but hands down this game is something else.

_childDocuments_.review: All the most frustrating parts of XCOM with none of the heart.  This game seems great on paper but the execution is just not there.  PP:YOE's main selling point is essentially, "No XCOM rng madness, instead we give players grounded combat and realistic gun physics."  Cicada, cicada.  PP:YOE replaces "85% chance to hit" (XCOM translation = you're gonna miss) with two circles and your rounds will travel anywhere within the circles.  So the enemies, depending upon weapon and range, take up a certain... um... percentage of the circles.  Does it look like 85% of the enemy is in the circle, well you've got an 85% chance of hitting that enemy with each round.  For an assault rifle one round might hit where you intended, 4 might hit an arm, and the rest might miss all together.  Okay, I guess that's better and XCOM's approach?  But use a 3-rounder, like the heavy class' weapon, or a single round weapon like the sniper rifle... well, let XCOM translate  the result for you...  Last thing before wrapping up is the overwatch system: It is broken.  Enemy AI detects your overwatch cones before they "arrive" on the map and skirts the edges of the battlefields avoiding stepping into overwatch.  It makes it almost impossible to set up a decent, effective ambush.  Overwatch activates when you're able to paint enemies with the cones after encountering them, but mostly, the result is just random and janky.  PP:YOE utilizes the XCOM "slowdown" when overwatch is activated, but it seems you and the enemy are moving at two slightly, but consequential, different speeds.  The result more often than not is your unit firing too late (enemy dropping a level or, more frequently, running past cover) and missing.  Overwatch only seemed viable when an enemy is charging in for melee under 15 feet.  Its just not good, y'all.  This isn't a trash game, which makes PP:YOE all the more frustrating.  Take a look at what other reviews have to say about the core game and most of the DLC - especially Festering Skies.  The game feels rushed and unpolished; it feels like early access content.  But its not.  I realize I'm posting a review after only five hours, but really that's all it took to recognize what this is: diluted XCOM with smoke and mirrors marketing.  Also, this is just, like, my opinion, man.  Maybe you'll love it.  Maybe you won't.  I really suggest reading the reviews on this one.  I should have...

_childDocuments_.review: I did enjoy the game for a while until I hit a difficulty wall I couldn't beat without a mod to help me cheat; dead serious about this. The game has difficulty problems; and I can understand why the active XCOM community put it behind them. I'll go over what I see wrong with it; how the Devs could and should have fixed it, and My hope is that they don't make another Phoenix Point game...1. It has a steep learning curve even after the patching; this is a game where a mistake can actually cost you the game and it isn't forgiving. No the devs won't fix this either; they stated to me in an email the game is this hard on purpose. If you make any mistakes that cost you too many resources; too many soldiers or even lose a base defense mission, you can lose the game because you just can't fight anymore. Making matters worse with the pandorans is sometimes it isn't your fault a mistake happens or you lose something; sometimes the game will throw a fastball at you and you have no power to stop it period.2. There is no Haven diplomacy options to get the Havens to stop fighting and hating each other. If the factions get mad there is no chance of stopping them from killing each other off; and this has cost me games because too many people die and I lose every single time... It's a game reset every time the factions go to war. There could have been a lot of options and choices for haven diplomacy but because you can't make havens play nice and you can't interfere with them fighting without all of them getting irreparably angry with you, you have to let them fight each other into ruin and it removes a chunk of your population trying. If the pandorans are particularly aggressive this can make things worse with their already hard evolutions.3. The Pandoran Evolutions will outrun your ability to fight them; and in many instances even with enhanced units and somewhat better gear the pandorans will kill your squads and even with good unit combos there is a limit. If you have any DLC that adds new unit types; they will get harder and harder and will wipe your forces out. The Trident Varients are one of the worst because while the devs claimed they had the same number of actions as the player units, they have more than that and will use six or seven actions a turn instead of four.4. The Tech tree is complicated and linear in all the wrong ways and you have to go through the factions to get their gear and options. And if you come to blows with a faction they won't give you any of it and you have to steal it yourself... coupling this with the fact the game has scarce resources you risk spending resources to gain resources and a mistake will cost you and outweigh the benefits of what you stole or gained. Because there are no other research choices or options like XCOM or similar games; some of the equipment and gear you make is linear and predictable. While this can be great because you always know which directions to go to get certain things; you won't outrun the pandorans and you will rarely have enough resources to take advantage of these research options.5. Resources in the game are scarce and you have to spend resources to gain resources. You can trade resources; scavenge and gather things from battles but beyond that there is hardly any other way to gain additional materials and resources; this slows the game pace down a lot and if you are unlucky a bad mission can cost you and punish you badly even if it isn't your fault. (As mentioned the game has an unforgiving learning curve.) If you spend resources wrong or are trying to save resources the game will find a way to take them from you or force you to risk things to get more. For example ammo and throwables cost resources to make; and if you're low on anything, you're spending resources to make more ammo and that makes it hard to save enough to better things or trades or recruitment. Confounding this further is the fact that scavenger sites do not regenerate and there are no additional options to gain large volumes of resources without angering a faction. I know this game is post apocalyptic but explain to me how scientists with guns can't figure out farming; recycling and technology generation using the items on hand...(Spoiler Alert)6. There is no good ending; all of them are bad, if you somehow make it far enough to actually take on and beat the final bossm you will be rewarded with a bad ending of different severity depending on who you allied with and what choices you made to get as far as you did. Of all the endings the Phoenix Point ending is the worst; and so is the Disciples Ending. There is no option for a hopeful future and it's a terrible excuse to set the plot for a Phoenix Point II... Because in the end with how badly written the endings are and the choice paths leading to an end; there is literally no way Phoenix Point can stop a second invasion from Yuggoth without getting their rear ends kicked inside out again... Human Cooperation is how XCOM defeated Advent and in Phoenix Point there is no option for a human cooperation ending that actually suggests a good possible future outcome. While I love this game from time to time; I have my fair share of issues with it and ran into so many painful challenges in the short time i played it; that I can see why people didn't like it. A major downside to this is that the factions can go to war with each other in as little as two hours of game-play... and you can lose in less time than that.My recommendation to the devs to fix this issue was to tone down the difficulty and add more options for the players, they blew off my letter of recommendation and refused to address some of the major issues I had outlined from my game-play time. I hope there isn't going to be a Phoenix Point II because the shortcomings of this one and the fact the devs actively acknowledge the problems outlined and refuse to fix them; refuse to add additional content that could help ease and remedy the game's considerable difficulty challenges, refuse to address the difficulty curve and a myriad of other problems... I do not recommend this game to people looking for an XCOM style title.The game could literally be the way it is now; if it had more soldier classes, more tech trees and options on par with the original UFO defense, like customization options and maybe even weapon add-ons like XCOM II had to offer, additional vehicles (Come on... XCOM Enemy Unknown had a designated fast mover aircraft class... you're telling me New Jericho can't build fighter jets or VTOLs like the F-35?... or tanks?) The game could have had more random things like more pandoran structure types and challenges; more faction locations, like New Jericho refurbished and Aircraft Carrier or something... better diplomacy options, more research options that are linear and less confusing to use, and a learning curve that isn't so unforgiving that you can lose the game within two hours of playing it. It could even have randomly generated resource sites that have a timer like XCOM II and maybe just enough diplomacy to stop the factions from fighting even if they don't cooperate... It could remain the same game with so many additional fixes and add-ons; even with the high difficulty curve, but the devs in an email i sent them just said no...If you like a hard and unforgiving game this is for you; If you like an XCOM style game, play XCOM.

_childDocuments_.review: "Carcinisation (or carcinization) is an example of convergent evolution in which a crustacean evolves into a crab-like form from a non-crab-like form. The term was introduced into evolutionary biology by L. A. Borradaile, who described it as "one of the many attempts of Nature to evolve a crab".[2] Most carcinised crustaceans belong to the infraorder Anomura." -WikipediaIt's like XCOM: but not. Obvious, I know. It's made by the same people. But honestly? It's fun, despite its flaws. Aiming feels better than in XCOM, you now have some control over what you hit. Body damage is now a thing. A rifle takes two arms to hold, so if your sniper takes a burst to the shoulder, they're not sniping anymore.The different factions are neat too. Anarchists, radical militarists, and these new age hippy types. They're fun, if a bit flat. Game plays the same as xcom, there's a strategy and a tactics layer. In the tactics layer you control up to 6 soldiers, with the option for land vehicles. They take up 3 soldier slots on the dropship, so your options are a rover for 3 guys, and some of the land vehicles are quite nice. Rockets, healing, and a few other abilities.Something I don't like is how slow the snipers and heavies feel. They move noticably slower than assault classes, and their weapons require 3 actions to use, not the normal 2, making them even slower if you want to move and shoot. You can up their speed a little bit by changing their armor, but then you lose out on the sniper's extra accuracy, or the heavy's jump jets.Yeah, the heavy has a jetpack. It costs 3 actions to use, but lets you jump a decent distance. I've been using it in combination with assaults to pull the enemies into a frontline, then jumping over them to high ground.The strategy layer is a bit interesting too. You can have multiple bases you upgrade and fortify, which means you always have a safe place to heal nearby. Most of the time you're flying around in your dropship investigating unknown signals, which turn out to be events, havens, or missions.Overall I like it. It's not amazing or anything, but I got year 1 edition on sale for $25 and I'm happy.

_childDocuments_.review: Bit of a rant here.I picked up the game when it released on steam. I would have bought it the day it came out but they pulled the 1 year epic exclusive crap. I refuse to put that launcher on my pc. I've done about 2 play throughs but I have only beat it once on veteran. First one I lost bad because I was still learning. I am a die hard XCOM fan. I've played the original xcom on PS1 for gods sake. I had to download an emulator for terror from the deep because this was before steam had it. I have apoc but never got into it. I beat xcom reboot and put over 1k hours into XCOM 2+WOTC because of the awesome modding community. I have mixed feelings about Phoenix Point. I for one hated how the creator back stabbed the donators by selling his soul to EPIC. I'm glad I waited the year for the release because I heard the game was very buggy at launch. Which makes me question "Hey. All those millions of dollars EPIC paid you to release your game on their platform. If it's this broken at release just how much of that money went into the game?"The geoscape. Feels like it's more play your way instead of playing how the game wants you too. Keeping nations happy for supplies, no thanks. In PP(lol) your mostly left to your own devices. Which can feel overwhelming at first but is nice once you get the hang of it. The pit stop mechanic feels wrong though. There have been times where I didn't do missions because I couldn't get there. The Pure's fortress was in Australia for me and I had nothing near there. By the time I got a ship with a far enough range to raid the place the entire country was wasted.I love how you can aim at specific body parts instead of a hit %. I really hated in XCOM how you can fire a shotgun point blank into a muton with 98% and miss! I love shooting things in the arms to disable their weapons ect. I also love that I don't need a target to fire. If someone is hiding behind a wall I can try to punch a hole in the wall. I could do that in the original XCOM and I missed that feature.Their version of overwatch is better than XCOM and worse at the same time. It was good to be able to point where I wanted the soldier to shoot. However that wasn't enough. Several enemies crawl. Your soldiers will take shots at them even if it is impossible to connect a shot. My biggest issue with overwatch was the fact the enemies are still moving when a shot is taken. I've had 5 people pointing at one guy. When the first 2 finished their shots the little bastard had ran past the other 3 and killed someone. Forcing me to restart the mission. It would be nice if the enemy moved a bit slower when being shot at or my troops fired a bit faster.Not enough mission types. Mostly I'm protecting havens or doing a scavenging missions. Those got old real quick. I like the base defense missions but it would have been nice to actually have facilities to help you with those defenses. Eventually I ran out of points of interest and it felt like I was only doing haven defense missions majority of the game. When I completed the game I checked my stats and I had done over 6 scavenging missions, 2 soldier rescues, 6 base defense missions, 4 ancient ruin defense, 19 nests, 12 lairs, 5 citadels and over 60 haven defense missions. That gives you an idea of what you will be doing most of this game.Base layout was dull. There was no real reason to think about how you build your bases. No thought process on what to build or where to put it. Except for 1 base that was basically a farm, all my other bases where exactly the same. There is a reason to build multiple bases, which reminds me of the old xcom. However each base feels so dull and like it's there so you can reach other areas. In the old XCOM I had several defense facilities I could construct. If I had enough a UFO was destroyed before it landed. Preventing the need to defend the base at all.Not enough enemies. I do love how they evolve and adapt to what your doing but it just felt like there wasn't enough types. Their version of a heavy, assault and berserker was the exact same enemy. Just with different armor and weapons. Some enemies had really cheesy mechanics. I hated Umbras. I really disliked how a siren can walk a country mile, mind control someone then walk another mile to get behind a structure. Making it impossible to hit her.Classes. I like and hate the fact you can mix classes. Some combinations are amazing. Like snipers with rage burst or techs who can toss turrets straight from their inventory. However I felt the classes alone were not enough. It's like they knew you would combine 2 classes so they gave us 2 halves to make 1 whole. Some classes flat out need a specific sub class to function. Like the berserker. I felt I needed to train them in assault for dash so they could get into melee range. The Priest class was cool but it feels very weak compared to the Psi Operatives I'm used too from WOTC. Once a squad got maxed out I lost a little interest in battles because there was nothing more to learn.I like the 3 factions. Their backgrounds, the fact we can trade with them, share research, steal stuff from them. A nice touch. I did feel a little overwhelmed at times when multiple havens were being attacked at once. I like how we can appease to all of them but once they start fighting each other, it felt like being ashamed to be a human. Couldn't we at least wait till after we wiped out Pandora before turning on each other? If I start another play through I plan to raid them more so I can get a better start.The aircraft. I felt like the generic manticore is the best aircraft. Fits enough people and goes pretty fast. The New Jericho helicopter plane had more room but it's slower than manticore. The synedrion plane was quick but could only fit 5 people. The Anu blimp has the most space but it was so damn slow I regret stealing it. When I found out how slow it was I wanted to give it back. I had a starting position in South America. When I expanded to North America I moved my blimp up north. Some missions ended before it even got there. I had to send it back south and move the manticore up there.I liked the various research trees. Different weapons for different play styles. Certain factions offer different research. It didn't feel like a linear path compared to xcom. Unlock laser/gauss weapons first, get armor then go straight to plasma weapons. The story is gripping me. Similar to XCOM but different enough to be it's own thing and I love the lovecraftian take on it. I would have enjoyed some actual CG cut scenes instead of still pictures. The voice actors were average but they didn't have any names I recognized. My biggest issue with the story is multiple endings. I don't have a problem with that but how to get them. Making max research with a faction unlocks their final mission. Which is essentially the same as the final battle except the ending is different. Researching the Phoenix solution forces you to take their ending.I despise the ancients DLC. The hoplites are annoying as #@$% with their shields. I have multiple sites and I still can't find the one that lets me craft the weapons and it's more crap to protect. I couldn't find all the manufacturing sites.The cover system feels crappy. I felt despite being in cover enemies could still hit me pretty regularly. I had a heavy with a robotic augment that gave him a shield. They had zero trouble shooting him in the head -.- It almost reminded me of playing Gears of War 5. When playing horde on Master difficulty. Even if you are in cover they can still hit you. It's just flat out better to block line of sight then to be in actual cover.Last the final mission. First half is fun but the 2nd is really bad. You will know when you see it.Overall if you like xcom this game is alright. Has some things I wish xcom had and vice versa. Get it when it's on sale though.

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy spiritual successor to the original Microprose X-Com/UFO Defense, this game boasts a much deeper and realistic simulation model than the more recent Firaxis intepretations, while still providing a somewhat more streamlined and simple interface than more faithful remakes like Xenonauts. Getting better and deeper with each added update, this game deserves a deep dive by anyone who's a fan of the genre. Ability to think outside the box and look for new ways forward when frustration threatens to set in are critical in this game, though, as what at first glance very much seems like a clone or even ripoff of the Firaxis XCOMs in fact is in many ways quite different, and requires different ways of thinking to succeed.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd have a hard time recommending this game to someone when there are so many other games that do what it does better. It can be very difficult to find proper cover for a character because of the grid system limiting you to four sides of something and even if you do get full cover whether your character will lean out or have a proper angle is seemingly up to luck- In the base game the pandoran strength gain is directly tied to how often you win, so winning more makes the enemy stronger meaning that being good can inadvertently make the enemy outpace you.- The character customization is laughably simple to the point that it grew tedious to customize my FIRST squad much less my second or third. I don't know why they even included it.I could go on but honestly I'm not passionate enough about the game to do that. Instead I will take a moment to mention the mod Terror From The Void which makes the game much better and more fun. It doesn't address all the games problems, but it does make the game more enjoyable. Yet despite that I wouldn't say it makes the game worth playing. Even with the mod the game is still unwieldy

_childDocuments_.review: I sooo want to love this game. Cthulhu meets XCOM? Right in my wheelhouse (on both counts). Given I picked it up on EGS and played it a lot there and now paid actual money for another copy here, I must love it ... right? No. The potential for an amazing game is there, buried under some stupid design choices. Game balance issues are everywhere; from research to manufacturing to enemies ... everywhere and everything. The difficulty curve is ridiculous. While you're grinding away trying to level up your soldiers so they're actually useful and trying to research weapons that actually might do some damage, the Pandorans constantly leapfrog ahead. The lazy answer to increasing enemy difficulty is to add HP and/or armour and that's what the devs decided to do in PP.You very quickly and very easily find yourself in fights that can only be won in a brutal bloodbath that can cost you a fair chunk of your squad. That might be cool if it's a last stand against overwhelming odds, but not if it's because the enemy difficulty has just spiked up again and they've gained some ridiculous amount of HP and/or armour so your weapons barely scratch them. Oh, and don't believe the hype about 'true ballistics' (or whatever they call it). You'll miss. A lot. At critical times.If a fraction of the XCOM modding universe directed their attention to PP to iron out some of the gameplay issues, and to build on what's already there, we could have something approaching the game this could be ... maybe should have been. I get the sense, though, that modding won't be a thing for two reasons: because the devs want to offer the same experience everywhere (no mods on EGS, so ... tough luck) and because of the EGS exclusivity on first release. The moment to capture the attention and affection of modders is when the game first comes out and that opportunity was lost. You only get one chance to make a first impression.I could drone on longer. I haven't even touched on the random squaddie skill generation that produces usable soldiers or worthless cannon fodder. The thing is, all of these issues existed through its time on EGS without being addressed. While, in fairness, I actually like the new tutorial, it makes no difference if it's the lead-in to a unbalanced game. Same with adding new DLC content.Phoenix Point is a glass either half full or half empty, depending on your point of view. It could be good, but isn't. It could be bad, but isn't. It's a 'nearly' game. That's what makes it so frustrating. I'd give it a thumbs up and say "buy it at half-price".

_childDocuments_.review: Pros and cons:PROS:- The inherently organic nature of each play-through coupled with the abundance of available DLC really puts the replayability factor through the roof.- The game is still getting balance updates and new content regularly (2+ years after release)- The diplomacy management - there's a fine line to walk between the 3 major factions and they have great interactions with each other and the Phoenix(player) faction.- The adaptability of the pandorans(the enemy) makes for a great arms race. The challenge persists until the very end.- The ballistics' system- The vast variety of weapons, tech and soldier classes (and class-combos)- Great implementation of vehicles- Modular and randomly generated terrain elements, good interactivity and the destructibility- So much story(!) and it is served in bits and pieces throughout the game, the player gets to experience different bits depending on their actions.- Great enemy variety. A solid set of basic pandorans; augmented further by their constant evolution throughout the game.- probably more but this is from the top of my head  😄CONS:- No built-in Ironman mode- No multiplayer (skirmish mode)- Significantly longer playtime compared to other titles in the same genre. (?)Final thoughts:Other contemporary games in this genre do not even come close. but they might be more approachable and accessible for the uninitiated and curious players. There is seemingly no clear path ahead in mid-late game (other than just surviving and keep progressing tech/diplomacy etc). I suspect this is by design choice, since the game is somewhat open-ended, there are 4 or 5 possible endings I think. All in all Phoenix Point is the uncontested king of the "XCOM" genre.

And wwwaaayyy too long. Run from one end of the map to the mission objective on the other side. Then run all the way back across a cleared map to the only extraction zone... Why? Literally why? There is no threat after the mission objective has been cleared. 1 enemy spawns per turn, usually halfway across the map. And you have 6 soldiers to kill it with. It isn't challenging. It isn't immersive. It is just dumb. If there were better mechanics and interesting sit reps this could work. But there isn't. So this doesn't.Speaking of dumb. The people running these missions are mentally deficient. Why isn't your evac zone close to your mission objective? The farther it is away the more risk there is to your men in the field. It is pathetic tactical work from an op planning perspective. Cus there are no threats preventing you from doing this. Drive by landing, bolt out. Takes 2 minutes. Literally no risk. Why land 5 miles away from the objective? YOU HAVE SOLDIERS WITH JETPACKS!!! Are there artillery style enemies preventing a closer landing point? Nope, not at any point in the game. Is there a swarm of localized enemies waiting to tear your men apart? Nope they are evenly spread out across the map, making every area as safe as any other area. Seeing as you always move first, landing farther away from your enemies actually gives them a tactical advantage. As you have to move into their range of attack, to attack. But you won't have the A.P. to do so. So you have to play the game in s-l-o-w- -m-o-t-i-o-n. Bo. Ring. The people who made this game are absolutely useless at wargames and should turn their focus to making games like "Monster High." They are difficulty modifiers with parts of the base game they cut out specifically to cause holes that will nag at the player until filled. It is evil. 16 colors and 3 faces per race with 4(?) race's for customization when you'll have a roster of 70+ near endgame. Honestly, I'd take a gen 1 SPARK over a fully kitted Scarab any day. Ouch.Petty drama mixed into the game. In 'independence day' or another similar video game... cough, cough... or literally any other piece of media ever. When aliens attacked, humanity always shows its true colors. Under great crisis they come together to defeat the alien menace... You know. What would actually happen. Cus the alternative is an unwinnable position. Period. That is your job. Dumba $ $." There are ways you could make this concept work. These guys were clearly not interested. Generic, basic b ! tch drama.3rd party EULA. _childDocuments_.review: Having played the old Xcom games (1-3) and the remakes Xcom1 and Xcom2 I had high hopes for this game. Unfortunately the game feels like a weird mashup of old school Xcom and the newer Xcoms, but repeats some old design mistakes that makes it feel like the devs learned nothing along the way. For starters, I will admit the start of the game is interesting. The game is fun for a while. Then it turns into a boring crawl as you hope to just happen to get the missions you need to advance. To illustrate what I mean if you want to win on the Phoenix Path you need a lair to spawn. I never got one the entire game. It was always nests. Never a lair. So the RNG on what we found held me up on that route. So I decided to try another route, went down the Anu path and was softlocked by needing a live Siren. You'd think the devs would have learned from the Deep One folly of Terror of the Deep to not make the plot depend on a live capture of an alien that may never spawn or was never spawning anymore but nope. Days of trying to get one to spawn I finally cheated and used the console to automatically research it as I was bored of running around with nothing to do until I caught that Siren, but none were spawning in missions.Then other issues started to show. There are no good weapon upgrades. I was using starting weapons for the most part in the last mission. However aliens had like triple the HP of what they used to have, and combined with armor meant every fight was a slog now. Apparently these devs didn't pay attention to the outcry over the boss in FF12 that had 50 million HP. Higher HP =/= challenge. Oh and the final boss on the Anu route has 9600 HP and I was still doing 30 x 6 with assault rifles and 110 with sniper rifles and 50 x 3 with my heavy. I'll let you do the math on how long that took. Another issue I had though was how soiliders upgraded, or didn't. You get points to upgrade in skills and in a couple stats, but you can never improve a very vital stat, and that is your to hit. What you got for your ability to hit enemies is what you will have all game. If you get a sniper that can't hit the broadside of a barn at 5 paces, they are never going to get better. First Xcom type game I played where you couldn't improve your accuracy with training. Even the remakes you got some improvement with level ups at least. And finally, the ballistics system needs to be scrapped. I heard a lot of bragging about there's no random to hits and its all ballistics. Bull. What you get instead is a circle you still got a 50% chance to hit in the first and 100% to hit in the second. That's still random though, and is a random probability on your to hit. I found over the game I actually missed more than I did in the Xcom reboots. I know we may have all seen the meme of the point blank shot with 68% to hit from Xcom1 remake, but here you can do the exact same still, its just hidden and you don't see the numbers. I missed a point blank shot. So did aliens. And the free aim system is terrible. Fallout 4 has a better aim at body parts system, take a lesson from that please. Let me at least select which body part to aim at directly. Overall I feel the devs need to go back and really look hard at the older games. What they got here is not a fun overall mix. Make sure they learn what made the old games fun. Make sure they learn what people like about the reboots too. And also realize that players want to get more powerful. Gimping the players like they did here with no good weapon upgrades but aliens get 3x the hit points over the game is just not fun. Overall all playing this did was make me want to play Xcom2 again, and if I spend my entire playtime wishing I was playing a different type of game of this type, you failed somewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of great things going for it.  Unfortunately, there are a few very problematic design decisions that ruined it for me.The Good:-Compelling lore-Interesting alien species-Clever combat mechanics-Fun vehicles-THE AMAZING FREE-AIM MECHANIC (XCOM should adopt this!)-Excellent projectile physics.-Ability to build multiple bases-Fun exploration where you can meet factions, gather resources, learn lore, etc.-Interesting faction mechanics where you can steal, trade, ally, fight, etc.-Alien species evolve in interesting and logical ways, making you change how you have to fight them.The Bad-TERRIBLE IN-GAME ECONOMY (deal-breaker for me): you can't have monthly income without going out of your way to exploit a very specific and very tedious game element.-You usually can't explore outside your starting continent without specialized vehicles that cost more money than you're likely to have, and take forever to build.-Those fun exploration sites where you can get money?  Every time you go to one, enemy strength increases, and you start to need more and more tech/money to win missions.  If you want to take the time to research things, you basically can't explore.-RESEARCH HITS A WALL TOO SOON (deal-breaker for me): by the time you've explored everything you can, you'll have run out of things to research, and still not have effective equipment.  The tech tree is way too limited.-It's hard to find your bases on the map.  The icons are tiny.-FACTION TRADING IS BROKEN (deal-breaker for me): Most faction locations will never want to sell you the most important resources, and those few that do will only sell you around 100 per day (which is a pittance).  So, you basically have to have one of your precious air vehicles camped out on a single location's doorstep and trade food for something more useful every day in the hope that you might eventually be able to build something useful.-EVEN RAIDING FACTIONS DOESN'T GET YOU MANY RESOURCES (deal-breaker for me): So, you decided that trading is broken, and chose to raid a faction for their useful resources.  You fight a grueling mission that lasts an hour or more, costs a lot of ammo, and damages all your units.  At the end of it, you get...84 tech.  WTF?-THE IN-GAME STARVATION MECHANIC MAKES NO SENSE (deal-breaker for me): The game has this mechanic where the aliens are basically starving humanity into oblivion.  OK, that's fair.  However, food is, for some strange reason, the one resource that everyone has more than enough of, and nobody wants to accept your food in exchange for other resources.  WTF?  It feels like the game designers decided to ignore the lore, just to make the game harder in a way that doesn't make sense.-There are only a half-dozen alien species.  They do evolve in interesting ways, but fighting the same six (or so) aliens gets old, after a while.In conclusion, this is an almost-amazing game with a small number of fatal flaws.  I get that it isn't XCOM with a funding council, but having some reasonable way to get more resources is a basic element of this type of game, and regardless of how it happens, it needs to be possible without completely screwing yourself over.  Were it not for these few utterly perplexing design decisions, I would be giving this game a glowing review.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game so much , i love the genre .  Its an incredible fun game at the start , early game its pretty well balanced.However something happens in the mid games where it all falls apart - if your a min maxer , read reddit and tips sheets you might be able to dominate with over power class combinations or perfect starts on your resource spending, however if you don't if your a normal person or casual gamer not willing to dedicate the massive time sink of all that its going to be nearly an impossible game to enjoy.What happens early to mid game is the enemy escalates both in difficult and number , your will have tons of fights going on , you will be massively under equipped , if you didn't spend your resources and XP EXACTLY right you can lose an entire team in a turn to one shots.   If you don't have enough aircraft or teams and you lose or can't get to an important battle the game will fall apart.If you can't beat extremely stacked against story missions fast enough the game will fall apart, if you don't have the right classes with you on those mission or didn't min max , you will get dominated even on low difficulty settings.As the enemy expands you don't have the resources to keep up at all , you can't afford guns , team members and expanding bases.  If if you can do some of those your going to be way behind - attacks will be happening all over the place and you wont have the teams to fight them because you have based to detect the attacks or you will have the teams but you wont have the bases so your will never know about them.   Maybe your lucky and you have 2/3 and your sending teams out with no gear.The game could easily be made much better if you bases could produce resource or gear on their own for little or no cost .Soldiers are both treated as complete cannon fodder if you didn't min /max and make some cheezy exploit character class that a few soldiers might be OP but they can also be 1 -2 shot to instant death at anytime .Soldiers and gear are super expensive but they are also fodder and can easily die .  Materials are also super limited which leads to a bad combination.ITs a few steps away from being a better game then xcom - but right now its worse then most things in the genre from some glaring flaws - its a fun interesting game early on for the first 6-8 hours and worth while , once the enemy starts to really expand the mist the games becomes an repetative drag  or a slow painful death against enemies your a not ready to handle.The final nail in the coffin  for me is EVEN if you do things flawlessly follow guides ,get a great start you end up with highly level team well equipped , you will hit a point where the enemies become so strong only your best Min/ Maxed guys can win fights - when 2-3 fights are going on the same time in the world with over powered enemies you don't have the resources to take them all out and the imbalance is frustrating and annoying The game has made great strides but its just not there yet.Edit: Tried it again after the most recent update and while some of the DLC and reseach options has helped with the mid game end game is still horrible and tedious non fun grind.Also the festering skys dlc might just be one of the worse paid DLCs i have ever seen in a game.  It adds next to nothing for the player , add a few new OP enemies , and more rsources burn and grind to a game with too much grind and not enough resource as is.It creates a mid to late game grind /process where if you don't do everything just right - it leads to a death spiral that could take hours or days before it gives you a slow death.   yes there are ways to recover and turn around with Min Max and OP player builds .  But because their are OP player builds nerfing players then making enemies that can literally do everything - fly - high health - high damage - high armor - special attacks - hard to hit all in one is not the way to go.

_childDocuments_.review: If you don't care about controller support, like how the gameplay goes, and feel like it's a good bang for your buck, this is still a grab. This is a cautious negative, should be a neutral.Despite carrying the "XCOM" name on its description as means of comparison, it diverges heavily from modern XCOM, and not in a good or bad way. Problem is, sometimes it could've done better by diverging more. Story is about the same, even bugs feel like imported from the newest XCOM games. .(if you do, skip this part)Short answer is: XCOM is a tactical game where asset management is crucial, strategy is multilayered (long term plans are important, but instant execution is the bread and butter), and gameplay is divided in two equally important parts: real time strategy with base and resource management; and turn-based battles with units.XCOM reputation comes from the second part. A HUGE part of XCOM difficulty lays in the heavy randomness of battles, and how damage balancing can make a single enemy shot shift the whole battle (against or in favor of the player). When you see memes about "normal person seeing 95% *happy*, XCOM player seeing 95% *nervous sweating*", that ain't a joke. Even a unit that is on full cover can be critically hit by an alien, die, set the whole team in panic, and have everyone else killed because of that. In XCOM, any mistake can be a mission ending mistake. And when training human assets is a long and arduous job, that is the kind of commitment  you make on every mission. You are never safe from the Random Number Generator on XCOM, no matter how safe you play. And playing too safe is not only boring and bad for the player, but there are also mechanics that prevent or punish that.Now...Short answer is: way less luck-reliant on the turn-based battles with units.On XCOM finding an enemy triggers a cutscene, gives them a free-turn to prepare against you, and makes your regret ever advancing your team? Not on Phoenix Point! When moving, if a unit finds an enemy, they just stop. And on Phoenix Point, actions are divided into "Action Points" that have about nothing to do with "points", since they are not discrete. A 10 tile movement costs one action point? Then 5 tiles is 0.5 action points. And if you stop because you spotted an enemy, no action points are lost. Upon spotting, you can prepare yourself, or even retreat.The rest of the battle-related things are just as advertised. While the success of a strategy on XCOM can heavily be dictated on luck, on Phoenix Point a properly laid out plan is a definitive win.These two main differences aren't good or bad, these are what differentiates XCOM from Phoenix Point. If the dependence on RNG on XCOM early game has always turned you down, Phoenix Point might just become your best friend. Specially since damage is balanced in a way that even on early game, all units (yours and enemies) can soak more than a single bullet before dying.Similar to XCOM 2, your initial position is less of a "world savior" and more of the "underdog", with not only XCOM being the only faction fighting aliens. Except that in Phoenix Point they had the great writing and backstory to make the player even more of an underdog and make the factions more significant by portraying them as "as capable of being the solution against the aliens, as Phoenix Point might be", creating a more interesting world. BUT INSTEAD, you're appointed as "world savior" by the initial narration, and factions are very receptive of you. There is barely any animosity between them and you, unless you pick a fight. Huge missed opportunity here, to create an even wider difference from XCOM while ALSO making it stand better on itself. Also, the voice acting is kinda bad, and it's not the "so bad its good"-bad, it's the "bland"-bad. Some key persons have great VAs, but soldier barks are generically devoid of emotion. Actors seem fine, but VA direction seems incapable. These compounded problems (too much centralization on the player and bad VA) degraded the potential of having a more complex and more interesting story when compared to XCOM's "you're awesome Commander, now go save the world". Again, if Phoenix Point made this actually work, it wouldn't make it "better" than XCOM, it would've made it unique.The management side is slightly different from XCOM, being a little more straining and complex, with 3 main resource types (instead of just "Cash" and "Expropriated Alien Stuff"). Instead of randomly appearing missions, you have several places to visit and maybe find resources, battles, or just information. Weaving of the DLCs was improperly made, with time-limited-unique-do-now-or-never missions (or at least that how they appear to be) that appear on early game and pit you against enemies you barely have any chance against (praised be my two snipers, only two capable of damaging those dang missile-shooting heavies). Mission variety overall is actually very good, and layouts fluctuate from more open fields with few buildings to more cramped places. Except for alien nests. Artificially and unnecessarily cramped! Yay. Gonna leave a review on Yelp.OH YEAH. BAD CONTROLLER SUPPORT!If using a controller to play is important for you, and that  made you smile, STOP... I'm on a Dual Shock 4, forgot I had DS4Windows running, and when I saw the "You seem to be using a mapping software *yadda yadda yadda* 'you don't need it' *yadda* *yadda* *yadda*", it made me smile!Then, I closed the prompt, closed DS4Windows, opened the game again, and... controller unresponsive."Huh. Let's check options, sometimes you need to toggle controller use.". It was already toggled. Controller totally unresponsive."Well, sometimes you need to restart the PC. Shouldn't, but let's try". Nothing."Well, Steam Controller Configuration Support might be on, and it might need to be off (or the other way)". Nope."...back to what I know to use then." DS4Windows just works."Great, now let's see how well it's adapted to controller". BADLY.XCOM has a cursor bug where when changing characters, the cursor doesn't update the position, so when selecting another character and trying to move the cursor, camera whips back to the last position at full speed. That bug is also on Phoenix Point! They didn't bother to update cursor position on character change too (or messed the script the same way)! But wait, there new stuff too! Sometimes it warps outside the playing area, and you simply CAN'T bring it back because you can't move the cursor when its outside the play area! Also, there is no "floor selection", and the cursor doesn't "climb" walls, so trying to select a direction that is on another floor is an adventure in itself, since you need to position the cursor relative to the camera in a way that is targeting the tile on the upper floor you want to go, even if one tile to the "side" (camera relative) is completely off from the that upper floor tile. Trust me, it's BAD.Also, the rest of the UI+UX is AWFUL for controller. CAN'T use D-Pad for menus (worst part). Sometimes lacks UI helpers telling what button does what. And the cherry on top, is that the UI is heavily cursor-dependent. I cry in anger every time I see "Full Controller Support" and that actually means "you use your controller to badly mimic a mouse, because we couldn't bother doing better than that".Oh yeah, and the cursor is huge plus is always visible on cutscenes.Please, don't say your game has "Full Controller Support" if XInput isn't supported out-of-the-box. It makes the disappointment of dredging through bad UI+UX with a controller even worse.

_childDocuments_.review: This game does one thing right. The tactical layer is really good, involving and more strategic than most in its class. Combat is pleasingly difficult, in-depth and mid to late game has a few fun and interesting actions to spend your AP on. There is a 45 degree parabolic learning curve to be able to somewhat accurately predict what enemies might do next. They are very unpredictable and evolve faster than your team. This is really cool at first, but its not long at all before they simply start using guns along with all their other powers and abilities. That feels like cheap and artificial buffing instead of an actual planned or creative progression.  It's not inherently bad in a strategy game that the enemy levels faster than you, as long as the player has options that are reasonable and achievable to counter the growing threat. In this game, they really don't. And that's the problem. Options to keep up with the clock are insufficient to do so. Game content is mainly focused on combat and enemies over any other factor. Again, not necessarily a bad thing. But that means that meaningful options and overall game content for the player's team are very limited compared to other games in its class. There is very little customization of any kind, cosmetic or tangible. Rolls for classes and abilities make no sense at all, they are just random rolls. You could end up with a Heavy tank that rolls Sniper abilities. There are initially only three classes (Assault, Sniper, Heavy) and a couple others have to be unlocked through diplomacy with one of only three factions (Warlike, Scientific, Religious). But that happens late game, too late to matter really. You may adopt a new class and achieve the 2 or 3 abilities from both, but again this can only happen in late game when it's nearly a foregone conclusion. This isn't the only game where you will always be outclassed, outnumbered and outgunned, where the enemy will always be two or three steps ahead of you with more AP, faster and far more devastating abilities, with better armor and better weapons. Armor and weapons that are extremely expensive and time consuming to first reverse engineer, then to manufacture. With a doomsday clock ticking away, progression is crippled by the amount of time and resources it requires to keep up. Better games in the genre offer ways to overcome the initial difficulty curve rather than simply steepening the curve throughout. The only way to beat this game is to save-scum. The whole game. Continuously. But that's not fun for me, not an achievement of any kind. It's rather closer to work than fun. Work that costs money instead of being paid. If that sounds fun to you, then at least wait for it to be half off. $9.99 to $12.99 might be reasonable to try out the innovative aiming mechanic if you don't care about building a team and keeping them alive. But there are far better games to scratch that tactical turn-based itch. The lead developer on this team is a very talented and experienced individual who helped to bring us the original X-Com. He applied what he learned then and made a cool innovation with the aiming mechanic. I do hope that the team expands and grows and may yet bring us an amazing game worthy of them. And no, this is not what we got instead of X-Com 3. For that, you will have to look at Marvel's Midnight Suns, out in March 2022, by Firaxis and 2K. Perhaps the bell has tolled for X-Com, but hopefully we can look to smaller studios like Snapshot Games Inc. to keep the genre alive.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Difficulty heavily RNG dependent, most players will probably have to cheese the mechanics to win consistently, battles are repetitive, and enemies are not very interesting.  The story, most of the voice acting and campaign setup is pretty good.While this game seems to be way better than it was at launch, the difficulty level and the AI seem pretty broken, you have to really plan ahead and spend a minute or 2 on every single move since the AI seems to always know where your guys are.  If you leave any units out of cover for a turn, or they just get bad luck RNG in low cover, they'll probably get killed immediately, even on Rookie difficulty it's extremely unforgiving.I expected better enemies, but the mutant alien monster enemies basically just feel like any other faction that's been re-skinned for the most part, they get access to everything you get and more (shield guys, rifle guys, even snipers), but they also seem to get stuff faster than you can unlock and manufacture it sometimes, which is pretty frustrating and doesn't lend itself to interesting counter-play.  You pretty much have to fight all the enemies and factions using the same tactics to win without losses.I did think the story was more interesting than I expected, the factions have unique aesthetics, the voice acting is mostly pretty good (though some of the characters are pretty corny).  The world map campaign style is basically the same as XCom which I have always liked.One could argue I'm not very good at this game and that's why I don't like it (which is fair, I don't play many turn based games these days), but if 20+ hours of practice isn't enough to have fun and not feel like every mission is a slow frustrating slog unless I run one of the really specific cheesy builds, then I don't think it's really worth playing.  The animations and the terrain destruction also look pretty bad for a game at this price.I've had some fun between some of the more frustrating missions, but it still feels like a pretty average early access game in quality; if you're looking for a good turn based tactics game, XCom2, Battletech, and Phantom Doctrine are great.  I'd say only bother with Phoenix Point if you're really good at turn based tactics games and have already played the ones mentioned above, and are looking for a challenging experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember playing the original XCom (UFO Defense and then Terror from the Deep) nearly 20 years ago now and being blown away by it. It was just fantastic. Then the new XCom series came out and they were brilliant. So when I heard of Phoenix Point and Julian Gallop and so on, I was very excited. I had bought this and sank hours into it on another platform. Got it again on Steam as I saw a lot of DLC had been added hoping for an improvement, but was left disappointed.However, while the game is 'ok' as a turn based game, it is very poorly laid out. -It consists of countless and endless meaningless/repetitive grind missions over and over and over again. Missions become the exact same so fast-The diplomacy/loyalty mechanic between the three factions had huge potential, however its just boring and more grinding of repetitive missions-Weapon upgrades are non-existent-Personnel are completely impersonal; losing a soldier Id levelled up and invested in in XCom was nearly reason to start a new game. In this game I got no such connection. Soldier dies and you just carry on grinding-Rather than 'challenging', some enemies are just flat out annoying. Having half my squad mind controlled, or overwatch not triggering (overwatch mechanic becomes tediously annoying nearly immediately)Look, its not a bad game, but its not great either; 5.5/10. And not worth €50 (another thing the developers did was launch the game and immediately announce 5 DLCs that would be released over the year after release, as if the game wasnt finished when launched and thats the feeling you get playing it). The story behind it sounded so cool and gripping, but the narrative and story in game is rubbish. Doesnt grip or capture the imagination, literally just turn the speed timer to maximum and complete research/grind/level soldiers.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenix Point

_childDocuments_.review: If you buy this to scratch the itch of playing XCOM, but like me wanted something a little different as I've played through that series many a time; then I CANNOT recommend this game any less. So I did not play this on release and have only played it with all the DLC installed and it is possibly one of the worst strategy games I have ever played. The game starts tbh a little too easy imo. Many enemies are melee only and you can kind of just gun them down from range. But, after the introduction of corruption, acherons, chirons and the flyer events things start to change. 1) Corruption is a mechanic that reduces your max will, but gives you a small buff to DMG. Now I assume this was added as a DLC because the will point (WP) mechanic is core to the soldiers gameplay loop. I would say unlike XCOM, upgrading guns and equipment plays a lesser role to gaining new abilities via levelling (if you're more experience in PP you may disagree). This means your WP are crucial to a soldiers viability especially on later missions. To tell you the truth though, some of the WP mechanics are simply broken and allow you on soldier to permanently lockdown a troublesome enemy or give you immense mobility. So what did the devs decide to do to rebalance this? They decided to give you a condition that is at times unavoidable that hinders your WP. This means if you levelled into WP, well you're bang out of luck! You want to go deal with a lair, well that's going to corrupt you. Save these Synedrions who are in the mist, well that's going to corrupt you. There are then enemies that also can corrupt you as well as enemies that make all enemies corrupt you. Basically, you are going to be covered in vimto at some point. The worse part about it. THERE IS NO CURE BY DEFAULT WHEN YOU GET THIS! It's actually hidden behind a research of a Pandoran, with no clue really that, that is the case. Even when you do pick this up, it's so expensive that you probably cannot cure everyone. Overall, the mechanic just sucks. To tell you the truth though, this is because the WP mechanic is extremely ill conceived.2) Acherons and chirons - completely BS enemy. So these critters evolve to have a plethora of abilities, but I want to focus on two mainly here (I already talk about corruption which is meant to be their main gimmick, but it isn't). So the default acherons have a couple hundred HP and maybe like 50 WP. They have an ability that allows them to call reinforcements (like 2 units I think). I'm not sure exactly off the top of my head how much WP it costs them to do this, but I think it's about 5. This means that every turn, unless you hinder them in some way, or kill them; they are going to call for reinforcements EVERY SINGLE TURN! Comparing this to XCOM, I would say they are most like gatekeepers. But, unlike a gatekeeper, their abilities have no cooldowns. If you have the WP to pay for your ability, you can use it every turn. At least with gatekeepers, if they res, you can deal with the added enemy tempo, then kill the gatekeeper before it's ability comes up again. (i.d. also like to add, killing a gatekeeper in a single turn is much more reasonable than an acheron - especially later evolved forms). These big f'ers therefore call for reinforcements, then run away! If you finally exhaust them of their WP, they just use 1 recover and get back to business. The worst thing though and really what makes me think the Devs frankly didn't really care about the balance too much. These creatures in an early evolution cycle evolve to gain a resurrect ability. This now not only means they can call in 2 units. They can also resurrect in an AOE units you killed. Ofc it's a WP ability, hence they can do this every turn until they need to recover. This basically means, you need disruption, that being heavies with war cry or virus rifles or disorientation. However, 2 of these require you to have WP and the game mass corrupts you so you don't have them. See the issue? Chirons I have also included here are they artillery shell 3 worms from across the map basically every turn. If you have 2 acherons or an acheron plus a chiron on a mission, i hope your squad has some real cheddar of it's own; otherwise you are going to be ground down until you die. At least when chirons run out of juice though, they just leave the mission...3) The whack-a-mole behemoth flying mechanic. Honestly, completely stupidly incorporated into the game. I will say I actually like the aerial battles. They break up the monotony of fighting wave after wave of Pandorans. My main criticism is firstly, I didn't find it was particularly well explained how to initiate them. But I will concede, I think I was just dumb about this to start with. My main issue though is that they just go around the globe immediately destroying everything. This is another DLC FYI. I think it was introduced to stop people just loitering slowly in one continent and forcing you to expand. If you do this now, the behemoth will destroy settlements across the globe and you will lose the game. However, it is so hard to explosively expand to keep up with these flying flips. I started in central americas. The fliers are there. I bonk them. They move to east asia. I can see them destroying stuff. However, without a scan of the location, YOU CANNOT FIGHT THEM! Even though I know they are their. I flew past and pointed at them through the Gift's window. Look commander, the behemoth and it's flying entourage is heading to shanghai. _childDocuments_.review: I was going to not recommend this game, but then I realized it's not the game I dislike. It's the learning curve.This is why the following reads as a 'not recommend' :)My experience with this game has been bittersweet. Phoenix Point is entertaining and addictive and features innovations that I think improve upon the XCOM formula, but at the same time falls short of becoming anything resembling the 'XCOM killer'.Three things I dislike the most about this game:1) The overwatch system. It is completely unusable. On the one hand it's an essential tool to gain that always desperately needed edge in tactical fights, but on the other it leaves too much up to unknown chance and clunky mechanics. It's based on a visual targeting cone system that is way too limiting, confusing, expensive and unreliable to be practical.2) Difficulty scaling / balancing issues. You will need to have spent a lot of hours with this game before you begin to develop a feel for what you need to be doing on the campaign map a long time in advance. If you don't know that you should've already started preparing for something because you haven't had the displeasure of experiencing it yet, you may be slowly playing yourself into a hole you can't get out of. Then the only solution is to restart the whole campaign since it's become a slog-fest you're likely not going to win anymore. You'll know you're there when the game tells you there's gonna be an easy fight and when you enter tactical combat, you're immediately getting bent over and rammed against the edge of the map.3) Technology / Research presentation. The game does a poor job at providing you with the information you need to plan ahead. And in this game you need to plan ahead a very long time. On paper long term planning sounds like a great challenge for any strategy fan, but a lot of it is not intuitive at all and you only learn the ins and outs of the game either by spending well over a hundred hours on trial and error (preferably on low difficulty settings), or digging through Wikipedia articles and tutorials, which is not a good thing for any game and should never be expected of the player.Something I learned in my playthrough: if the RNG places the bulk of the alien activity on a different landmass you cannot reach anytime soon, just quit and start over.Did I mention bugs? Yeah there's bugs and you'll learn about them when you're in a life or death situation.( Note: I have only ever played with the TftV mod, mainly because allegedly the vanilla game is even more unbalanced and buggy )If you're taking this game on, I'd recommend committing to a full learning run where you play on the lowest or second lowest difficulty. It's stupid, but it seems to be the best way to get a grasp on how this game is going to play out.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. But I don't think I'll ever be able to finish a single playthrough.The intentions of Phoenix Point are never called into question. From the start, it is clear that it wants to take the foundations of XCOM, but to address some of its frustrations all the while giving players more control over how they advance through the game, from the tactical battles to the grand strategy. But in doing so, it also creates its own set of annoyances and frustrations; and regardless of whether these are born from a sloppy execution, too much ambition or inevitable to its design, the result means that invariably, PP will most likely end up feeling not as great as one would hope.First off, no more accuracy rolls! You can aim your shots, and shoot them wherever, and while there's still some probability involved, if your reticle is inside an enemy, it'll hit them. You will still get infuriating misses and even shoot half a burst through an enemy's armpit because they moved during their idle animation, but this really feels like a step forward for the genre. As is being able to perform actions without restrictions as long as you have the AP for it: you can move, shoot and move again, for example, and I cannot understate how good it feels to not being hamstrung by arbitrary rules on how you go around playing. The same can be said about class building: soldiers can wear pretty much any armor they want to, they can be cross-classed and augmented, resulting in a huge variety of possible combinations and roles. Hell, even planes are different sizes, so you can zip a small team around, or carry 7 dudes on a big lumbering quadcopter.On a strategic level, you are dropped in a random point of the geoscape and from there your mission will be to open up more bases, scan around, and deal with whatever you find. In this sense, dealing with the geoscape feels much more on rails, since most of the time you will have mostly just two directions to proceed in, and while you will have to deal with three other factions, each with their own identity and bevy of super well voiced little "choose your own adventure" conversations that you will encounter from time to time,  the strategic component is pretty straightforward and basically will boil down to allocating your resources and increasing your coverage, and open up more bases, and recruit more soldiers and-- this is where things get kind of ugly.While you will fight humans from time to time (and robots), the big bad of PP are the Pandorans. They will start with basic melee units, but as you complete missions, they will keep evolving into more dangerous ones, and will do so at a concerning speed, so from the moment you start, the pressure is on to constantly open more bases, and recruit more soldiers, and get planes to put them in, and now you're controlling 3 planes simultaneously, uh oh, the entire world is literally dying of starvation so you better get going! Uh oh, a Haven is under attack! Man your territory is getting kinda big, maybe you'd need to keep a team around to respond just in case huh? Hey you should do these missions on the other side of the globe, better open up more bases, oh hey this soldier you recruited has no ammo, you should probably look into that, UH OH ANOTHER HAVEN IS UNDER ATTACK. The timing is generous from what I can see, but you will be in constant fear of falling behind because by the time you realize, it will probably already be too late. But expanding will turn your game into an ADHD nightmare where you need to keep track of like 5 things at once, to the point that your eyes kinda glaze over and you question why you started to play this in the first place.The problem is that the game quickly gets way too big for its birches: for example, soldiers can only be upgraded from their character sheet, meaning that EVERY TIME you will need to go to "personnel", click on your soldier, check the amount of upgrade points they have, and then decide if and what you upgrade. Similarly, there isn't a unified inventory, either, so if you want to manage all the gear you have on the entire project, you will need to access a random soldier's inventory and do it from there. This only gets worse as you grow your teams, there is no easy way to track what squads have what weapons at a glance, and once you click on a particular Member, by the time you've finished sorting out through all the assorted armors and knick-knacks in their inventory, you'll have forgotten which of the 20 troops this guy was with, what does this unit carry overall, and what's the synergy of that soldier to the rest. And this is not one-time either, you're probably going to have to update inventories and level up every mission or every couple at least. Again and again and again.In general, I feel like PP doesn't let itself breathe out and have fun. And while I can deal with Pandorans somehow stacking two new mutations over the span of a single mission, the need to constantly be expanding your territory and microing your teams all while needing to keep track of multiple objectives, manufacturing, research and base expansion at once, uncooperative UI aside, is what really ends up exhausting my will to play it after a while. And while I get that feeling like you're teetering on a knife's edge while fighting impossible odds is kind of what these games shoot for, the fact is, this game becomes more unpleasant to play the longer you play it.I could talk about ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ enemies that can tank a full magazine to their face and still cut you up into chunks, or how locational damage can render one of your guys useless while almost every enemy will have the ability to regenerate their limbs, but to be honest, I think the tactical gameplay, while very different from XCOM, is mostly fine. But I feel like Phoenix Point should have either played its cards closer to the chest, or made sure that the game can be played at the pace it itself imposes in a more tolerable way. As it is, it's a bit of a shame that a game that does so much right still manages to feel wrong to play.6/10.
