_childDocuments_.review: Edited review after playing the game for a bit longer. I am now very confident that I would not recommend this game to anyone, XCOM fan or not. The things that made me dislike the game:- The tech tree    The tech tree is genuinely the worst I've ever experienced. In Phoenix Point you research things over time, but guess what? Most of these are literally meaningless and don't unlock anything. Probably 60% of them is just "get resources for researching this". Supposedly you have to ally/help the factions to get "interesting tech" (which is ♥♥♥♥♥♥ design by the way), but regardless anything you unlock is LITERALLY meaningless and mostly a question of preference, here's an example of some weapons / types:- A rifle that shreds more armor, a rifle that shoots longer (not a sniper), and a rifle  that pierces armor. That's literally it. That's all the difference I've had as of my playtime right now. Sure, the base stats are MINIMALLY better (we're talking range tradeoff for slight damage increase / piercing weapons (weapons??? why not ammo??????) which ignores armor but does less damage in the long run...Most of the tech is like this: minimal enhancement / just different "balance."And guess what makes all of this completely meaningless?The fact that as soon as I researched something, the enemy got the exact same upgrade. Multiple times. Acid / armor melting weapons? Oh, now your enemy has it too. Yay. Not even a single mission played without them having the exact same weapons / tech. I don't see why you put in a progressive research system if you're NEVER going to get an advantage tech-wise. It's literally idiotic.- The firing systemAnd god oh god the aiming system is the worst I've ever experienced. It's LITERALLY worse than ANYTHING in XCOM. For reference, you've got 2 circles, an inner-circle and outer-circle.  Supposedly 50% hit in the inner circle, 50% in the outer. Yep. That's all the reference you have for whether you're going to hit a shot or not. Mind you, if you're unlucky but have to take a gamble, that 50% could all end up in your teammate's head. Very fun and engaging gameplay.You can also just "shoot" instead of 'manually aiming.' But yeah. The only reference for whether or not that hits is a HUE OF COLOR on the enemy's health bar. That sometimes just doesn't update or show. Nice. I'd rather miss a 97% hit chance than this "realistic bullet-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥."- The factionsA couple of factions are in the game. I think around 4. They all HATE each other. Cus they have different ideals. So they HATE each other. Yep. No compromise. Probably. You need to ♥♥♥♥ some of them over to win the game. Probably? I lost. Cus I didn't wanna play unethically. So yeah that was fun. But regardless why help them if the tech you gain is virtually meaningless (see above). I dunno.- The squad system and recruitmentSo you can have multiple squads in this with multiple vehicles and stuff, so you can go on several missions at the same time -- I didn't do this because I never got the money to make a vehicle -- I could've stolen one from a faction, but I didn't want to. Regardless, the recruiting is horrible -- once you research (I don't know why you need to research the ability to hire people? Feels like they want to make EVERYTHING research) -- you get new recruits you can hire every ~3 days (you can also hire from factions but it's expensive), but often I experienced them being 3x heavy classes or 3x snipers (AKA no point in hiring them). Personally I don't like the whole "be everywhere at once with 7 squads of soldiers" because...... *drumroll* ...The missions are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ boring.- Missions and enemies!The missions are terrible! Not only that, the maps are mostly (I don't know if they're auto-generated or not) terrible because you'll rarely have decent cover and the cover system often doesn't even work! Terrible angles on every map combined with cover that seemingly doesn't exist (AKA high walls that just don't have cover, but clearly SHOULD have) makes for a great and fun time. The missions just aren't fun with the enemies. They're often just bullet sponges en masse, and most missions have infinite reinforcement so you can't even take your time to play the game. Nope, enemies just keep coming. The enemies also JUST might be invisible unless you get SUPER close because clearly they're all stealthy invisible ninjas! Some of the aliens even spit out mist that hide them so you can't kill them at all! And if you enter this mist your guys start panicking and fleeing, killing them all!I lost my entire lvl 6 squad (max level is 7/8?) to 8 invisible enemies that could shoot 4 shots with their weapons every turn! I couldn't move because they also had Overwatch on me so I had no choice but to die. And so I did. Sure, there might be tech at some point that helps against this, but I sure didn't discover it in my entire playtime.Most of the enemies are also just bullet sponges. Shoot them with your default attack probably around 10 times each to kill them. And that's just your average goon. Or nuke them with your heavy (but that's expensive!). Who's probably just gonna get mindcontrolled and run next to the "apex predator" (no spoilers here!) and get run over. And die. Permanently. No reviving or stabilizing by the way! Some times you'll also just come across literal boss monsters in the field. It's okay if it was balanced and there were less OP monsters too, but nah... You'll have the 3000 health boss running around killing all civilians while you're being ganked by 3 enemies who've all done mindcontrol on 3 of your squaddies. And next turn they'll get another, cus there's no limit on the mindcontrol! They can control as many as they want. Very balanced. Did I mention your squad's abilities? No?- Squad abilitiesIt's all based on your character's willpower! In other words, use it too much and your character flees and dies! Way to decentivize using abilities. And they're all lame too. They're literally all copies of the previous XCOM games, without the cool ones. [SPOILERS] We're talking about abilities such as dash, "not having to use action points to reload / use inventory" (more about the inventory below!), making your weapon use 1 less AP (so you can effectively shoot 4 times in 1 round, at the cost of 3 x 4 willpower = 12 WP (max WP is 20 at highest level). Mind you though this is basically not even enough to halve an enemy's health in the end game. Cus they're just bullet sponges.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game after sinking hundreds of hours into XCOM (the new ones, not the originals). I've heard Phoenix Point is much more like those original games, but I still really enjoyed it. It is definitely more difficult than new XCOM, and has a steep learning curve. However, the aiming system is vast improvement, and being able to do your combat actions in any order gives way more flexibility. I found there were far less combat situations where you lose for reasons outside of your control (thank god for no 95% chance, point blank misses)- the main ones being when a new enemy or status effect is introduced and you get caught out by lack of knowledge. The map is where the main difference comes in. It is definitely an adjustment to know you need to be acting at all times, and have events happening all over the world constantly. It is imperative to get multiple aircraft ASAP to stop yourself from falling behind. Also, make sure you research the humanity counter, you need to keep an eye on how quickly your population is dropping and open up new bases so you can see when colonies are being attacked. Food should be your most plentiful resource, trade it for everything else and get in the habit of doing so early and often.I recommend not sabotaging if you can avoid it, I managed to be friends with everyone and it gave me access to all the tech/research and far more resources than I would otherwise have. I definitely recommend not having all the DLC on for a first playthrough. Kaos Engines definitely seems broken though- better vehicles and weapons with no ammo? I abused those, not going to lie. If you get power through the learning curve, this is a lot of fun, good luck :)

_childDocuments_.review: This game technically delivers by checking all the right boxes, but I found myself getting more and more bored as I went through yet another mission set in yet another procedurally generated map using soldiers that were little more than numbers on the screen. Initially, the game has you struggling with resources but IF you can get past that, the mid-game has you swimming in resources but no worthwhile weapons or armor to spend it on because you already got the best the game has to offer. In short: The enemies still get progressively more powerful with time, but your own forces don't. Caveat: I played the vanilla game. Enabling DLCs might give more powerful armor/weapons but I found that starting out with DLCs enabled made the game too overwhelming. Even without DLCs, the difficulty would sometimes spike to insane levels and at one point I had to cheese my way past a mission that gated my progress towards the end of the story. Against the most powerful "boss" enemies I might as well have brought BB guns and wet paper armor. I finally hit a wall where the difficulty and the lack of fun simply wasn't worth whatever conclusion the storyline would come to.I still recommend trying it but I honestly can't see myself having another go. More of the same is exactly why I stopped playing.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I was a huge XCOM player over the years and really appreciate the revival of this game type.  After being part of the first releases, restarting numerous times to try different styles, I really love all the time and thought that has gone in to the game.  The diplomacy is actually very fun, the missions are typically centered well, and the base raiding is thoroughly enjoyable after that friend badmouths you.  ;)The animations are pretty legit showing some really neat interactions with the characters and their environment.  I still come across a new one every now and then that surprises me.  The only thing that drives me a bit nuts is when rotating the view with the keyboard it snaps into 4 directions and typically I get annoyed by mis-moving someone in close quarters.The main thing that is drawing me away is that I am a longer-style player.  I don't want to rush through the game, and it is not at all setup that way.  You can start out raiding like crazy on any level and win, but if you take your time the computer out-scales you pretty rapidly.  You can only utilize one crew per mission instead of letting you combine multiple transports on a single mission, so eventually you have your 8 person crew against massive armies of tank like creatures in which one (or multiple) just keeps summoning and resurrecting everything on the battlefield.  Drive me bonkers.  Just let me use the armies I have!  :)Outside of that, I have had a blast for a couple hundred ours so that says a lot for a single player game.  Maps are generated, but will find a lot of duplicates over time.  Utilizing all weapon types is great fun, and learning the willpower controls/defenses are a great aspect.  Hopefully, some day, I won't have to save 30 times a night to avoid outmatched random encounters(or encounters where my vehicles get stuck.  ;)  If you liked XCOM, give it a try.  It is totally worth the money.Thanks!

_childDocuments_.review: I was an initial backer who got burned by Julian Gollop reneging on his promise the game would be released on Epic and Steam at the same time. That said, I'm not going to fault the game itself for this. The tactical experience in this game is similar if not better than the XCOM series in that there aren't triggers that set waiting aliens in motion as there are in XCOM. Also, at four hours in, I find the types of missions more varied than they are in the XCOM series, without the artificial time constraints. The strategic experience offers more variety also than the XCOM series. You have deeper political considerations with warring human factions. This looks like it will offer better replay value than XCOM. Also, the voice acting for the faction leaders is fairly decent, imo.What XCOM does better is the personal touch for your characters. I grew attached to characters that I designed and named after friends. IN Phoenix Point, they seem kind of one-size fits all regardless of customization. That said, PP, like XCOM, has classes of fighters that you can tweak as you level up.Another thing I like better in XCOM is the feel of immediacy in combat (through amped music, closeups of aliens, louder sound effects). Combat is still fun in PP, just not quite as tense. Also, the base building is just butt-ugly imo in PP. A small thing, but I did like XCOM's side view with an animated base.Worth a buy? I'd say yes, especially as at its release on Steam it's on sale. If you like XCOM, you'll likely enjoy PP, angry backers gripes notwithstanding. PP's combat system is better than most of the XCOM clones out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's face it, easiest most obvious comparison to make with this game is to the Xcom series.  In many ways, they feel so much alike.  In some ways, Phoenix Point greatly improved on the Xcom series and in others I think they poorly implemented a good idea or two.  ie, the factions...  why does everyone have to have some dash of absolute crazy to them.  In the sense that no one is perfect, but you're trying to sell me on a huge chunk of the population believing something so ridiculous?  I don't want to spoil any of the story, but the writing for the factions "personalities" was poorly done.  Gameplay wise though, this is a solid buy if you find it on sale. Played through on Veteran which felt like the perfect challenge if you played the before mentioned series.  If not, start normal. You'll still enjoy the ride.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10 Game has a lot of positives. It's basically the new X-com with some of the old X-Com's stuff added in and a few new good ideas to help out.There are however 2 huge problems. It's not particularly user friendly, a lot of the ease of use things you'd expect from the X-Com franchise just aren't there, and this manifests in a bunch of ways from the graphics, to the UI, to issuing commands etc. As a whole it could be easier to play, without effecting the gameplay at all. The biggest offender is simply knowing if your troops will be able to see the enemy from where ever they move too. I cannot count how many times the UI will draw the line showing that my troop should be able to see an enemy from the new position, only to actually move and try to shoot and not be able to. It's frustrating and unnecessary.The other problem is the bugs. So many bugs. In just 7 hours of gameplay I've had to reload the game ~10 times because it gets stuck on one bug or another. _childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to recommend and like this. I love the genre, I really enjoyed my first 8 hours of it, but it just started to feel like a slog that became unfun.5/10Pros:- Aim and fire: Taking out the right parts of enemies limits their effectiveness, adding a great amount of strategy- Diplomacy: Help the right people to get more tech/gear/etc- Trading: The ability to buy/sell supplies (and with careful checking, even making a profit moving stuff from one to another)- The differences between factions, they're really interesting and well thought out, all three have their own unique takes on survival and their own tech; and the android people can be considered a sort-of fourth faction- You feel like you're losing; you're up against an unbeatable enemy and really trying to survive/thrive- Ammo system - having to carry ammo is great, and limited inventory. The missions where you grab gear are quite interesting too- Mission variety - from attacking cities to defending them, to attacking pandora lairs to rescuing people; there is a great variety of interesting missionsCons:- Story: 25 years after the virus hits the game starts, and you start with -nothing-. There are factions that manage to have global communication, and while it makes sense they don't work together, it's strange that they basically suck at existing.- Tech: Basic assault weaponry (but also rocket packs?) and basically useless armour. It's like taking army soldiers from now, but you forgot how to make shotguns or other basic gear of today, while having amazing vehicles. It's a weird juxtaposition of forgetting today's tech, but inventing a few less useful pieces. A lot of tech doesn't even tell you what you get, you just research things and hope you get something useful from it.- The Factions: To befriend them you have to babysit them. You're clearly just a small group of soldiers on a single airship yet they expect you to be everywhere and save all their cities. They have -lasers- and yet a few people with assault rifles are supposed to make this big difference? At least give me something for saving you, like some ammo for the laser guns I bought from you. What's more annoying is that as soon as you befriend them you get shown all their world conclaves and are expected to save them all, even if you're on the other side of the planet.  - Enemies: All the factions are rather unique, and fighting the three human factions is interesting. However the main enemy, the mist, basically just has everyone's abilities. You mostly fight the pandora, and it feels like fighting the humans is like fighting a weaker pandora. Especially once the pandora start generating unremoveable mist (except with explosives) in large areas around you, and cloaking every time they get hit while also healing when they shoot you. The pandora actually end up with better weapon tech before you do, and yet you can't steal the weapons back.- Cybernetics: Cybernetics are awesome, but apparently helping the androids means they automatically hate and want to murder you. Why aren't they just another faction like the other three?- The map: Everything is so spread out and you lack the resources early to easily outfit a single squad, no matter multiple. So you lose faction influence just for existing.- Aiming: Aiming is almost mandatory, as a lot of times you can fire at an enemy but have a 1% chance of hitting and as far as I could tell the game didn't tell you that unless you manually aim

_childDocuments_.review: It seems inevitable that a game which shares so much with XCOM (not the least of which being Julian Gollop, the lead developer) be compared to the modern XCOM games. Doubtless I am not the first and will not be the last to compare and contrast the two, but it is an important point to make, nonetheless.While the XCOM games of the modern day give you plenty of soldiers early on, you must train them and keep them alive as best you can, because talent is scarce. Phoenix Point takes an almost inverted approach, in that you start with a scant team that you can't really afford to lose in the early game, but as you progress and build training facilities, it becomes easier to replace those super-soldiers who have fallen in the line of duty. I prefer the Phoenix approach, because the former feels like building an ever taller house of cards that could crumble and leave you with nothing at the first major mistake, while the latter feels like building an aeroplane as you fly it; terrifying at first but gradually more and more stable.XCOM leaves whether or not shots connect with their target up to the big random number generator in the sky, while Phoenix lets you take matters into your own hands with manual aiming and a much, MUCH more robust movement system. The predictions that Phoenix provides, however, are not always as accurate as one would hope, leading to the awkward situation where you move your aiming reticle over an enemy's silhouette, and believe for all the world that your shot will end their life, only for the camera to pull back and reveal your bullet colliding with the tip of the stalagmite your soldier was using as half-cover, totally blocking the attack. Still, when it works, it's good.Character classes are far better in Phoenix, with a system that allows the mixing and matching of the seven classes to create horrifying amalgams that combine each class's five abilities in new and exciting ways. Still, a little annoying trait is that each soldier must spend ability points on their new abilities, often forcing you to choose which skills are worth using and which you'd never actually employ. You can get as many ability points per soldier as successful missions you have them survive, but this leads to a re-treading of the XCOM issue where the strongest soldiers are the ones you've had all game long, and losing one will nullify a lot of your forward momentum.My last comparison is regarding equipment. Grenades, the battle defining weapon of the XCOM games, are more or less useless in Phoenix, but replacing the XCOM Arc Thrower is Phoenix's Neurazer, not merely a tool for capturing enemies but a truly invaluable weapon in it's own right. There's no "basic kit" that you have an infinite supply of; each weapon and piece of armour is made to order, meaning four crafting projects are required to fully outfit a bare-naked soldier. Recruited soliders must be given guns on Hero difficulty and guns AND armour on Legend difficulty, or else the fresh meat becomes dead meat very quickly. This is offset by the fact that you can steal weapons (but not armour) from dead enemies in battle sometimes (it's random whether they drop them or not). So, swings and roundabouts.Going off of these comparisons alone, I believe Phoenix Point to not merely be a XCOM clone, but rather the superior game, with a lot more strategic depth and room for decision making. It's definitely rough around the edges, but I feel that adds to it's charm. Would recommend to strategy game lovers of every evolutionary subspecies.

Even the pentultimate weapons of the Ancients are a letdown and still do not have the killing power they should.Phoenix Point is also too forceful in its storyline.  There are many things the player may wish to do, such as visit havens, conduct raids, and acquire new soldiers from different havens but there is scarcely time to do so with all the Pandoran and other faction attacks. _childDocuments_.review: Phoenix Point is a weird one to review. There is so much to like about this game but also so much to hate. It is a good overall game if you can ignore the scads of blemishes that keep it from being a true gem. If you love the X-com series and tactical games like I do, it is absolutely worth picking up during a sale. Just understand that it will require some patience here and there.Pros:- I've been addicted to X-com since the original game (yeah, I'm old) and have played a number of X-com clones like this one so I don't say this flippantly... there are some mechanisms within PP that I believe outclass Firaxis's X-com series and I wouldn't be surprised if they are adopted in the next iteration of X-com. Those mechanisms:    o Overwatch - The way PP implements overwatch is with a narrow cone, which allows your soldiers to create overlapping fields of fire. There is nothing better than watching a larger enemy force bum-rush your kill-box only to be decimated.     o Focus fire and Line of Sight - Instead of relying on a 100% top-down set up and a Rng percentage roll for hit chance, as X-com does it, PP instead opts for a 3D FPS line of sight setup a kin to the Fallout series. Percentages to hit are based on distance from the target, weapon type and the ability of the soldier in question. The FPS aspect makes lining up a target much more intuitive while the focus fire mechanism adds a puzzle-like aspect to the gameplay as your Pandoran enemies often have specific vulnerabilities that need to be targeted for a successful kill. This makes positioning your troops to attack from various angles very important during combat.    o Skill Randomization - At first glance, the soldier level up mechanism is overly simplistic with soldier classes all going through the same skill trees. What can be easily overlooked, however, is that each soldier starts out with three random "specialties" within the tree that when combined within the right class can become the difference between them being cannon fodder or a killing machine. While there is certainly room for improvement in the soldier creation functionality, I found this randomization to be great for building out different fighting styles.- The story line of PP is great. Interwoven throughout with multiple endings, it drives you to your next fight in order to discover "what happens next?". Even after I tired of the combat, I found myself pushing through in order to unlock the ending.- Blood and Titanium, Corrupted Horizons and Living Weapons DLCs - Now I wouldn't advise picking up the DLCs individually but I do think that the reviews do them injustice for what they add to the base gameplay. When I picked up my game, all DLCs were included and at the advice of some forums, I disabled them my first play-through (which I think was the right call). Once I ran through the game a  couple of times, however, I found that the content they added was refreshing. I especially enjoy augmenting my soldiers with mechanical body parts (B&T) and have put together some great mechanized squads.Cons:- Global Map & Resource Balancing - There is no nice way to say this, the Phoenix Point meta-game is currently unfinishable (at least on higher levels) due to what are severe resource balancing issues. Now to be fair, I refused to play the game on anything but Hero (level 3 of 4)  due to combat on lower levels being ridiculously too easy. After restarting the base game some 10 different times using experience to make smarter choices, I found that I always ended up in the same dilemma around the same point. Eventually, (usually around the time scylla begins to appear), I ran out of resources as well as Points of Interest on the map which resulted in a sudden struggle to keep my team supplied with ammo. The solutions online recommended aircraft theft and farming/trading to trickle in cash but it felt like a subpar hack when I tried it. My solution - and one I would recommend once you've given the base game the college try - was to download a mod which gave me infinite resources from the start, taking that part of the gameplay completely out of the equation. Once I could actually fund my team as needed and Mutagen became the only resource I had to manage - the game became infinitely more enjoyable.- Combat AI - The combat AI in PP ranges from absolutely engaging to just plain ridiculous depending on the enemy you are encountering. The sad reality is that the combat AI is pretty dumb. Enemies rarely use cover effectively (often not using it at all), never move to flank your position, and regularly perform actions that are not in their best interest. Mostly, the enemy tactic is to simply bumrush you, allowing you to wipe out large hordes by setting up a defensive perimeter and picking them off one by one. Adjusting the difficulty level higher does not increase tactical difficulty but rather just adds more enemies to the screen. Now for the Pandorans (your main enemy), this AI tactic works fine as it lines up perfectly with the storyline. But watching human enemies regularly leave great cover and end their turns out in the open where they were easily picked off was painful to watch and I found many missions ruined as a result.- Combat Animation Bugs - While they weren't game breaking, several bugs in combat stole from the immersion. I noticed two primary animation bugs that regularly bothered me: 1) Often times a soldier (your own or an enemy) faced the wrong direction *away from the enemy* when crouching behind cover. This may seem small but compounded with the AI issues above was an immersion killer. 2) There exists (at least for my AMD video card) a dancing soldier bug where when one of my soldiers who was originally behind an upright wall was hit with return fire, they would get stuck while trying to move back into cover. This would cause them to jiggle back and forth for two full seconds before returning to place. - Character Randomization - The character randomizer algorithm is overly simplistic and it was rare that I didn't jump into the character screen after recruiting a soldier to fix what felt like an immersion breaking result. PP did a decent job of providing enough different names, faces and voices to create random characters but the tool used to randomize those options either (1) often overly used the same faces/names while ignoring others or (2) created ethnic/racial voice, name and hair combinations that felt pretty wacky.- Story Pacing - Despite the cons above, Phoenix Point really is a fun game but it is too d*#$ long! The amount of missions you need to complete in order to see just one ending let alone all of them is too much and the game ends up wearing out its welcome. As a completionist, I wanted to see the ending for the game but eventually I got sick of playing the same missions over and over.

_childDocuments_.review: A horrible execution of a few good ideas. When I saw this game I thought "wow, XCOM with the stuff that reboot missed, like bases, destructability and less randomized, ballistics based shooting". Oh boy, I was played like a fiddle.1. This game is ridiculously random. You see, every time you start a mission, all enemies and their positions are random. Spawning in the open field with a couple of snipers killing half of your operatives turn one? Check. Enemies spawning on your objective you must protect while you spawn in the opposite corner, so this mission is failed just from the start? Check! Getting a way too easy mission cause enemy spawned a lot of trash mobs or impossibly hard cause game spawned mostly elite? CHECK!2. Ballistics? Also random! You have 2 circles, 50/50 chances of hitting either a big one or a smaller one inside the big one. The problem - those circles are huge and are almost constant cause game has only a few options to improve accuracy. And even shooting point blank does not give you 100% chance of hitting simply cause most enemies have lots of gaps in their models where bullets will pass without doing any damage. Oh, and don't forget that all idle animations on enemies are affecting the shots, so if the enemy randomly ducks down behind cover, turns around or something else - you missed, even though both circles were on the enemy. And if you decide that you can demolish a piece of cover to shoot through it - once again, random! I have seen sniper rifles not demolishing small railings that handgun had no problems with, I have seen heavy weapon not doing any damage to a wall that is later destroyed by some stray AR shot.3. Enemies - completely imbalanced. Enemies that can oneshot you from another side of the map? Check. Enemies that oneshot you in melee AND are fast enough to cover the whole map in 2 turns? Check. Enemies that can paralize-lock or panic-lock an operative for the rest of combat? Check! Artillery units with oneshotting AOE attack? And they have this one too. "Well, at least they also can be killed in one shot, right?" - you may ask. Haha, nice joke - the weakest enemies take a complete turn for one operative to kill, elite ones may need 3-4 people to get dealt with in one turn, the biggest stuff needs about 18 operatives to be killed in one turn. A small problem tho: the most used squad size is 6 people. So yeah, good luck surviving 3 turns with no losses against an enemy that can oneshot TWO people in one turn. And you can guess that you will never fight only one enemy. Also remember that this problem is heavily amplified by points 1 and 2 from that review - and you will get the most ridiculously imbalanced turn-based combat you have ever seen.But lets leave the combat and move on a global screen and progression. So how did the devs ruin something that uses a long known formula?4. The bases. They are like in older XComs, you build stuff in them. The problem - their locations are ALSO randomised. So yeah, a bunch of bases put closely together, so they have no purpose and are not worth claiming? Check. Bases located in empty regions that are basically useless? Check. No bases near critical points - checked, once again. The amount of building on the base are also very basic and are not even worth mentioning.5. The techtree, or should I say - the lack of it. Yes, technically you have a tech tree. But in reality you have only ONE tier of armor that is available from the start, only TWO tiers of weapons, one of them your starting weapons. Most of the researches just give some trash rewards like resources or a few percents to damage against one specific enemy, or they are just plot researches that give you nothing but flavor text. Mutations and augumentations? Just a piece of armor you can't even take off, with slightly better stats but with a much bigger price tag. Not only the research options are trash, but they are also locked behind DIPLOMACY.6. Diplomacy, or should I say - lack of it. The most rudimentary system I have seen for a while, that has almost no purpose and you will not even remember it is there most of the time. Good lore-wise, but a missed opportunity on gameplay level.7. The class system for your operatives. The main problem - only 3 stats that only cover 2 bars (HP/morale) and speed. No accuracy, no special stuff like psy-ability, nothing. Perks - all pretty basic. "Oh, but they have a class fuse system, so you can make any of your operative a dual-class!" Yes, and they are mostly useless. You see, every class has only 7 abilities total. Most of them are stand-alone and only a few of them have some kind of synergy. I ended up taking something like passive invul to mind-control. And yes, if you thought that you will mix and match - bad luck, due to problems with game balancing you either go for meta builds or you loose your operatives, no other way around.I am sure there are things I've forgotten, but you got the idea - this game is just a downgraded XCOM with some nice reskins, and horribly broken everything else. Only take if you like savescumming, suffering or you have money you want to waste.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is excellent. Don't bother reading those negative reviews, they are all XCOM fanboys or disappointed backers and have too much expectation of this game (this game is made from the same people who made XCOM). In considering whether this game is for you, there are couple questions that you need to ask yourself: 1. Do you like turn-based combat where turns are determined by action points? 2. Do you like game with dark, sci-fi and post apocalyptic atmosphere? 3. Do you like a tactical game with RPG elements and a huge map with optional locations to explore? 4. Do you like resource management - managing your own base and watching it grows? If the answer is yes, then this game is for you. Ignore those XCOM fanboys, I played through both XCOM 1 & 2 and even the original ones released more than 20 years ago, those are different games that target different groups of players, there's no point trying to compare XCOM with Phoenix Point. _childDocuments_.review: Now this is a story all about how the Earth got flip-turned upside down. And I'd like to take a minute, just sit right there, I'll tell you all about how people were mutated by the air!Phoenix Point is the brainchild of Julian Gollop, creator of the original X-COM series. As such, it has many of the things that players of XCOM (And Xenonauts) will be familiar with - turn-based battles on tile maps, base building, recruiting soldiers for your squads, and the Geoscape, to name a few things.Where it differs is in its story, shooting in combat, havens and difficulty curve.Unlike the XCOM storylines, where earth is being invaded by extra-terrestrials, PP's enemies are the result of a mist-borne virus that causes people to lose their marbles, walk into the sea, and mutate into CRAB PEOPLE. CRAB PEOPLE. CRAB PEOPLE.Obviously, XCOM Terror from the Deep and HP Lovecraft inspired quite a bit of PP (To the point that Lovecraft is mentioned by name in-game). That said, I really wish the horror was better executed. Aside from narration over still images, there are no real cutscenes. This is a huge missed opportunity, especially considering the revamp of the tutorial introducing some named characters. Remember in Starcraft 2 the optional cutscene of Dr. Hanson becoming infested with Zerg DNA? Considering this is an entire game based around mutation and body-horror, you'd think they'd have fit some truly terrifying (Or at least suitably creepy) cutscenes in.The mission maps also lack any variety. There are all of 2 or 3 maps per setting, so you'll become familiar with them very quickly, and this makes the game feel somewhat bland and repetitive compared to XCOM 2 or Xenonauts.It's not a *bad* game though. The difficulty curve can be extremely unforgiving, and you should expect to fail or wipe on a few missions, maybe even lose a campaign or two until you get the swing. "Easy" is more like playing WOTC on "Normal" (or even "Hard" at times), but this makes those victories all the sweeter.Speaking of combat, I love the Free Aim feature and true bullet physics. It's much more satisfying to be able to see an estimate of where your shots will hit rather than missing an entire burst of shots on a stated 99% hit chance.Havens are nice, they work similarly to the factions in WOTC, with a bit more depth. They're a mix between that and an AI-Controlled PP equivalent. They're passive for most of the game, but near the end they may declare war on one another to mix things up.Ultimately the game is decent, and if you like TBT games you'll enjoy it. That said, it feels very half-arsed in a lot of places, or at least like you can see the seeds of a good idea that just fell flat.With only 1 DLC left to publish by the point of me writing this, I hope they're planning some free content updates to flavour the game a bit more, but I doubt it. Still, pick it up if you see it on sale. In some ways, it's better than XCOM 2 + WOTC. But in many more ways, it doesn't quite measure up. Still, a worthwhile addition, especially at a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: I've edited my response as I've now finished the game. I tried to find every node, etc so it took a long time:  You can waste a lot of resources bringing 19 bases back online.Quite simply this game isn't a good game. It isn't enjoyable, fun, interesting, well-developed, clever, innovative, ... anything. What it is is the converse of all of the above. At times I thought they'd just run off with the money and bought a bad alpha version of Firaxis' XCOM. It looks and plays like that but it isn't slick. It's still buggy and amateur. To develop a base, for example, you click a box, it fills up and then you get food. A spreadsheet would have more character. Talking of characters, the writing appears to have been done by a computer. A computer with no character.  It's dull, trite, bland and like a lot of things seems like an afterthought. It seems like they were too busy doing nothing (thank you, Prince) to realise that there might be something they could do with that which would make it better than ... I don't know. Like many I've played TFTD, Apocalypse etc. They were very basic games by today's standards yet they weren't repetitive grindfests. JA2 which I only discovered a few years ago when it was ancient history shows how you can make a brilliant game for nothing using crap (by today's standards) technology. The 'nothing' of course also being relative.The game seems to take all the cheesy, trite memes from bad games and throw them into one. Enemies that can one-shot you from (somewhere, you don't know where because they're invisible) , enemies that can somehow disable you in one go with a grenade whereas your grenades spend all their time missing the target. Resources that are so scarce that when someone destroys a weapon of yours, you re-load.  Enemy spam.  An incredibly tedious and stupidly-designed end-boss. There's nothing innovative here at all. Much of it seems designed to annoy you: it's not like you ever really feel that you've done something good as such and it's colourless, lifeless, re-re-re-repetitive.  I played on 'normal' aka 'veteran'. I tried to avoid conflict to slow down progression. Nope. And they don't progress so much as beef up. I tried to use stealth but of course they know where you are and can always find the exact right spot in order to hit you easily, but make it hard for you to hit them.  I tried to avoid politics but the factions will go to war and will just destroy your plans. This is a stupid mechanic as by the end even though I was clearing nest and lair and citadel after each as soon as they appeared (72 troops or so, 11 planes) another would pop up immediately afterwards. And you can't cover enough of the available area to stop them so as they wear you down that on its own is enough to mean you have to waste hours in the final mission. This was where I had to cross a large, open expanse and there was an invisible sniper on the other side. That took an hour to circumnavigate with new enemies (7 Sirens among them)  merrily popping up and ignoring the game rules of just appearing, but appearing and then shooting at your troops.  There are lots of things where the game does as it wants.And then there's crap design. You can have 8 troops for a mission, 9 for the last (but no one told me! And why 9, why not 10?) and that means you either take the buggy (Tiamat) that's so slow the world will have ended before its half-way there or you take 2 ships. Because that's such a clever thing to do ...I had hoped that the modders might be let loose on it and they could fix it. And it needs a lot of fixing, but it sounds like they won't really be allowed to get into it.If you've got money to burn and you're bored, I suggest you buy a nice metal dustbin, some wood and firelighters and burn it. It'll be more productive and you'll have more fun and feel better.

O boy I would love that! And, and, and an armory-building of a sort that allows you to mod weapons and upgrade armors, mix mutations and augments,- a leisure room that allows you to convert skills to skill pool when team mates hang out and interact,- that the swamp cats/independents were a bigger faction similar to the other 3 factions but one that specialises in guerilla warfare and, and, and perhaps they could train your melee oriented soldiers in counter-attacking enemies that move into or out of melee range of your soldier, a rush attack that allows you to run the full distance and take a swing,- that the driver in the vehicle levels up and gets skills just like soldiers, say, he could rotate vehicle when it's out of action points, mount different things, e.g. a fog of war cannon that conceals your soldiers when they exit, actually now that I come to think of it, the mechanic seems like an ideal candidate as a driver in a vehicle, perhaps something could be mixed here, he can also repair, etc, i don't know, just thinking aloud right now because I enjoyed this game so much,- oh, and generate a random world would be loveley! _childDocuments_.review: My two biggest frustrations with xcom1/2 was 1) that classic 99% hit chance shot missing, and 2) running into a group of aliens at a bad moment.1) Phoenix point fixes this. Basically each individual bullet is now considered one at a time. In xcom I would hardly ever consider taking a shot at <55% accuracy. For example, in xcom if an enemy is at very low health, but you have low accuracy, your turn is better spent repositioning or doing something else because most likely you will miss your shot. But with Phoenix Point, I would take that shot, because even though I have low accuracy, I just need one or two of my 9 bullets to hit the low HP target to kill it. It makes combat feel much more consistent than xcom.2) Your characters have 4 action points instead of 2. 2 action points of movement is comparable to one action point of movement in xcom in terms of distance, and shooting (for most weapons) takes 2 action points. What this means is that I can run out a short distance, shoot, then get back to cover. Running a small distance and shooting will leave you one additional action point to do something, which is nice since xcom would consider a movement of a few tiles and a full action points worth equivalent to each other. Even heavier weapons that cost three action points to move will allow a soldier some wiggle room to line up that shot. Movement does not fully consume an action point. That means I can move twice with a single action point. Ex: I have my sniper move one tile consuming ~.2 AP, take a shot consuming three AP, then move back into cover using another ~.2 AP. This used 3.4 of her 4 AP, which would not have been possible if movement consumed an entire action point (it would have cost 5 AP.) However actions such as melee, shooting, ect, all are measured in FULL action points, only movement can take advantage of fractions of an AP.Troops will stop moving if they spot a new enemy. So what does this mean? It means that if I tell a soldier to run into a building, but there's an alien in there, he will stop and let me decide what to do. In xcom the solider would just keep charging into the building until his order was finished and he was standing next to an alien. This small change compliments the other changes in the previous two paragraphs very well.TL;DR: combat feels much more consistent and flexible.

_childDocuments_.review: Developed and designed by the British producer Julian Gollop, Phoenix Point is a tactical game focused on strategy and turn-based combat, very similar to the famous X-COM game series. And that’s not a coincidence, as Julian was one of the main responsible for the franchise creation in mid-1993 when it was still called UFO: Enemy Unknown.Because of this, we can say that both games have the same identity, which resembles both their gameplay and their storytelling. So if you’re already an X-COM fan or already familiar with this genre, I seriously recommend you to play Phoenix Point. One of my biggest surprises from last month. And I know that this game is from 2019, but c'mon, Epic Games doesn't count.You can check my full review in

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid fan of the "X-COM"-Genre i really tried to like this game. And i did find a lot to like about it: The atmosphere (especially in the tutorial), some of the combat- and class mechanics. The voiceover.But, sadly, overall i cannot recommend it. There are just far too many aspects in which the game is insultingly bare-bones and - frankly - unfinished:- The UI outside of combat is 1 or 2 steps below minimalistic.- Finding and maintaining your bases+vehicles on the globe is a chore. If you have multiple squads ready for deployment and just want to find the closest one to a new incident on the globe, you have to visually look for them. Turning the globe near the poles is insultingly bad.- No way to trash vehicles or get rid of thm in ANY way. Cannot even rename them. There is simply a complete section of the UI just plain MISSING for them. And that despite there being a PAID DLC which focuses entirely on vehicles. WTF.- Filters for equipment/research are unreliable. Sometimes they work, sometimes they don't. Even if they were working 100% of the time they would be insufficient. Want to see a list of all the Handguns you know about? Though luck. Try to see a list of only head armor? Lol, who would even need THAT?!- The above makes comparing items/augments almost impossible inside the game. You are better off starting wordpad and wrinting the stats down yourself. This is just not good enough.- Loading a game inside a mission COMPLETELY breaks the AI. If you ever load a game during a mission you are automatically cheating. No way to avoid it. If there was an Ironman-Mode you could argue that's by design since the developers anticipated that anybody not using it would be a save-scummer automatically....but there is no Ironman-Mode!!!!Then there are some design dessisions which i simply don#t like but could be considered subjective:- I love to have more control over my soldiers and their equipment. Being able to chose Perks+Classes and enhance particular weapons/armor would have been nice.- The game simply assumes that everybody wants to mix+match different armor for stats and look like garbage. Sure, i like to min/max, too....but i would also like my Squad to have a certain visual appeal. In this game you can either look like the faction NPCs, look like your own faction but have bad stats (because the PP armor is simply worse than faction armor) or you can use augments but look like trash because the 2/3 limit means there is no "cohesive" look for them. Not my cup of choices, really.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are like: Great MOAR XCOM then it's ok, but it's not exactly what you are looking for.  Phoenix Point has much looser mechanics that lead to some moments that can't occur in XCOM but it also makes a "perfect mission" much more difficult - because things just go wrong sometimes in unpredictable ways.  The tactical flexibility is definitely a little bit more, but honestly that ends up being a downside at times.  The game becomes repetitive toward the mid and end game but this has gotten vastly better with patches and DLC. For me, as a 1000+ hour XCOM player and now pretty similar amounts for Phoenix Point (owned on EPIC and played Beta) I would give the overall edge to XCOM just because it is much a much more tightly ruled experience and the pacing is nearly perfect.  Phoenix Point is very good but even with many patches it is under-polished.  That is a result of its basic open-ended design for both strategy and tactical layers.  The model has tons of potential though and it is a worthwhile investment of both $$$ and time.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, one that will be keeping me entertained for many many play-throughs.10 JUL 2022 UpdateThe Infested Skies (IS) DLC ruined the game for me. I guess you can just play without it which is what I will have to do now. I have had a few re-playthroughs with the IS DLC now. Each time, no matter how many aircraft I team up with, the sudden emergence of BADDONS and insane enemy sky weapons just completely obliterates your game, instantly.So there is that, it is unbalanced. A broader point is that, unlike other really good strategy games, there is no attempt to build the DLC and especially the IS DLC into the story arc as you progress into the later game. It is guesswork trying to prioritise your builds in order to prepare for the late game IS DLC. All in all, I still think this is a great game. BUT it seems to need a Campaign Mode with a much better story arc and then a separate Challenge Mode. So hardcore elite gamers can muck about with impossible bloody air attacks and the rest of us can enjoy a balanced DLC that is sensibly integrated into the story arc and late game progression.

_childDocuments_.review: Terror from the void update: Mod improves a lot, but not enough for me to recommend the game. Despite their efforts, much of the original problems remain that make it infuriating to play.TLDRThis can be a fun game, especially if you like modded UFO-Defense Xcom. However, this game is also just as frustrating and buggy as modded UFO-Defense Xcom. If you’re looking at this because you like the modern Xcom, just don’t… Unless you’re a masochist and like frustrating slogs.More DetailsIt seems like this game is designed to only succeed after several playthrough of learning the hard way with significant functional inconsistencies in how systems and missions act, including some stuff that never seems to be explained.Some (among many) Examples of inconsistencies/bugs:•	Explosive UI indicators are often outright wrong, leading rockets to missing or hitting obstacles you couldn’t see.•	Mission objectives are inconsistent and update mid-mission. One mission you might activate an objective and auto-complete. Another will surprise you with extra objectives you really should have known going in, like “Kill all enemies” or “Evac all operatives”. •	Several times base missions will spawn a room locked off from the rest of the complex, making it impossible to kill anything inside the room making the mission impossible.•	Status conditions behave inconsistently: Fire for example seems to sometimes work, sometimes not, and may change which it’s doing while the enemy is standing in fire (and is not a fire proof enemy)•	Random difficulty spikes that require cheese-tactics and meta-knowledge to deal with since you research only ever gives horizontal upgrades.•	Sometimes you see no enemies and just have to sprint around, sometimes backtracking to find where the enemies or objectives are.•	Goo: Want to have your entire squad locked in place with no way out for the entire mission and just sit there? Yay. (Goo eventually decays, but if you don’t kill the enemy, they tend to reapply it liberally).•	Daze Mini-bosses: Goo wasn’t enough? Now you can have your entire team dazed infinitely until you quit the game.Random other commentsHorizontal Tech-Trees:I admit the game gives you tons of tools to deal with problems, but none of the tools are better than what you had, merely different (IE horizontal progression rather than upgrades). So, you never truly become powerful and just constantly struggle to the point of slogging through to the end. Random World Map:For better or worse this game is really random, both tactically and strategically. Each game is different, but there are a lot of fail states you can get into early. Start in South America and RNG no supplies missions? You’re stuck with nothing to do. Fail to unlock the proper sequence of bases in Australia? Entire place is locked off, in or out. Story, sort of:The plot develops, but nothing like the stories from the Archives on the main site (which are great and I recommend) and mostly is just a mess. Most events seem to be due to coincidence rather than any coherent plot reasons. Then we have the Ancients DLC where the civilization that had no evidence excepts scraps of legends left behind suddenly has mines and factories with active sentries lying around no one noticed for thousands of years and three world wars.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say I was disappointed with this game from before it came out. The creators of this game already lost all credibility for me when they screwed over the kickstarter backers in exchange for an exclusivity deal with epic despite the fact that they weren't exactly starved for money. A year after the game came out and very few people played it, we got it on steam with very little fanfare. I played the original X-Com games, as well as the newer ones and I have to say this game somehow manages to disappoint me on so many levels. Firstly, there's a very obvious lack of polish to the game. The "bullet based" shooting is terrible. It's a great concept, don't get me wrong, but it's implemented terribly. The RNG somehow manages to be more horrible than that of the newer X-com games, with shots 50% of the time shooting OUTSIDE OF THE OUTER CIRCLE IN DIRECT CONTRAST TO THE IN GAME TEXT. There is an RNG system at play that has NOTHING TO DO with the circles you shoot with. The damage is also completely RNG based but with absolutely no in game information displaying how. How do I know this? Because you do get information about how much damage a shot allegedly makes, and how much health the enemy has and whether or not it should kill them. So when it doesn't, and there's no apparent reason for it, it makes you scratch your head. A myrmidon taking 3 direct shots at point blank range from one of the hardest hitting heavy cannons in the game not dying makes sense to anyone? No, it doesn't. In contrast, the enemies absolutely cheat. I've seen cases of enemies exceeding their action points, shooting through walls, and even causing bleeding on a cybernetic part of one of my units. This is lack of polish, or the devs just mess around. The DLCs are nothing to speak of and not worth getting. They add very little to the game. In fact, there *is* very little to this game. This "X-Com" killer fails to deliver on a narrative level, a gameplay level and a satisfaction level. I don't feel like I'm saving the world, I don't get attached to my soldiers and the missions are so repetitive I got tired of this game (in my favorite videogame genre mind you) within 10 hours of playing it. I don't recommend ever buying from these jokers again. They obviously haven't been taking this as seriously as they've been letting on. I've had more fun playing the alpha demos on Kickstarter than the actual full game and that's a damn shame.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really just a mess. The original Epic release was unbelievably broken, and now over a year in the game has at least improved significantly but still has just so much more work to be done. As far as a game in the X-COM/XCOM genre goes, it's decently solid and I think is worth playing for dedicated fans of the series, but it can really be an exercise in tedium as the game goes on. Balance has been a consistent issue, and as the developers keep releasing patches to nerf certain abilities or equipment, or fix various exploits, the game just keeps getting less fun. A lot of abilities are just really weak and useless now, and so many weapons just have no place in the game. Snipers are just simply too inaccurate to be useful, and in general builds centered around mid-to-close range tend to work best. Enemies don't tend to have particularly varied strategies, they just ultimately stack armor as the game progresses, generally making fights against them more tedious than challenging. The three factions in the game will all hate each other no matter what, kinda making "diplomacy" pointless, but are at least capable enough at defending themselves that you don't really need to worry about protecting every single haven. Bugs, freezes, and crashes are everywhere: enemies will constantly loop animations for some reason, death animations don't play sometimes and an enemy's model will just be stuck after death, abilities will sometimes just be unusable even if you have the AP and WP for them, many bugged and broken achievements, the list goes on. Many bugs have been fixed since day one, so it does at least feel like the devs are continuing to work on the game, perhaps by "year two" we'll have more of a cohesive and finished product.Bonus round, so far the DLCs are all pretty bad. Granted, you get them for free with this version of the game, but they're just not good.Blood and Titanium adds yet another enemy type that just has absurd amounts of armor and little else in the way of strategy, and the augmentations it adds for your soldiers are mediocre at best, and generally not worth the cost to manufacture and repair. Living Weapons was originally a pre-order bonus, just adds a set of armor, a rifle, and an LMG. The armor is very durable but doesn't do much else for you, and the weapons, while better than your starting equipment, will fall out of use pretty quickly. Use them or don't, they don't really add or detract anything from the game.Legacy of the Ancients is pretty awful. Everything about it comes so late in the game that you'll have had your soldiers' builds and equipment locked in long ago, the new enemy types it adds, once again, just stack lots of armor and are also immune to almost every type of damage, leaving you with the strategy of "shoot it until it dies". The new equipment it adds is admittedly very powerful, but is just largely unnecessary, and since the enemies are just a chore to fight to even reach those weapons, I don't think it's really worth it.Festering Skies is not out yet, will be releasing in about a week as of writing this, and I believe it will require an additional purchase. Enemy UFOs and interceptions was something that was promised initially so this expansion screams of cut content, also bizarre to me that it took so long to get this one out, but from what I've been reading about it, it doesn't sound very promising. Instead of adding a detailed air game, it just seems to add weapons to the four transport aircraft that are in the game, and UFOs that will occasionally interfere with your craft. There's a large roaming base that you need to deal with, but it feels like the UFOs and interceptions, what should be the focus of the expansion, are more of an afterthought. I'll gladly eat my words on this, but I am just not impressed with what they've shown.I wanted this game to be Julian Gollop's prodigal return to the genre, and it came out as more of a wet fart. It really didn't break any ground in the genre, and while I usually don't care much about Epic v Steam drama, I do believe Snapshot Games taking the Epic deal for that first year of exclusivity really hurt this game, having it come out unfinished and then finally release to Steam a year later with very little fanfare. Perhaps a better mod scene could help this game, perhaps it just needs to cut its losses and start work on a sequel, but as it stands, I think this game turned out as a failure. I can only hope the team learned a lot from the work they've put into the game over the last few years and can improve for next time.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is ok, but falls short of many things.Coming from the X-Com series this game feels like a flat downgrade.The story seemed promising, an unkown virus transforming the planet and people.It reminded me of Frank Schätzing´s " The Swarm "So I was intruiged, and being a fan of X-Com and turn based Tactial games this game seemed like an obvious choice.However the game started to feel empty and meaningless somehow.The Lore / Flavor text sometimes is just missing, on gear especially it often says " A Faction XYZ Rifle "Yeah great, a little bit more love could have gone a long way here.Research was a complete disappointment, it all felt meaningless and lead to meaningless things.One of the main things I enjoyed in the X-Com style games is the research and development of new Armor and Weaponry.The Armor in this game is generic at best, uninspired with little to no differences.Same goes for the weapons, marginal differences.Using the Basic Phoenix Point Assault Rifle felt the same as using the Laser Assault Rifle of another faction.Research quickly became a checklist of things I had to research to move the plot along.There was no excitement about new gear that could improve your odds.The different Factions quickly became a nuisance as well. Bickering, whining and hating each other.The apocalypse is upon us, lets have a gigantic kindergarden fit and ♥♥♥♥ each other up, instead of focussing on the enemy.Which makes sense in a way, that´s human nature for you. Still I felt more like kindergarden Guardian than anything else.The combat is interesting, with the free aim system, but often your Soldiers seem to have no skill in combat at all.The leveling system of said Soldiers was ok, an open system where you can select every base class and combine them. It´s very flexible but also not very distinct. It just felt " Meh " like the rest of the game.The enemy evolves, countering your equipment and strategies.A normal Crabman who was meele only at the beginning, will evolve into having a machinegun incorperated into his arm. Or grows a thick Chitin Shield.That was extremely disappointing. You have this cool looking crustacean like enemies and suddenly they start to use human equipment. It looks dory and it feels dorky.I understand that you cant just have meele enemies because that would be horribly unbalanced, but it could have been done in a more elegant way, just make the weapons look more organic and give them a different description.For me it killed the immersion of an mutant / alien threat.Base building, which always was fun and important in X-com also seems uninsipired. The bases are just there on fixed location, and act more like " Gas Stations " so you can reach further away points of interest.All in all the game is ok, nothing special either way. If you are starved for turn based Strategy or an extremely hardcore X-com fan then this game can bring you some joy.Personally I expected a lot more, would give it a middle thumb ( neither up nor down ).

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game.  Worth the asking price.  A steal on sale.What are you getting for your money?   An enjoyable game with turn based battles and a decent story.What aren't you getting?  X-com.   THIS IS NOT X-COM.  I've played all the X-Coms, and while I enjoyed them, the big combat maps ( especially in X-com 2 ) could drag on and on.  Maps are smaller in Phoenix Point.  Enemies have their own agenda - sometimes they are gathering supplies,  sometimes destroying buildings, sometimes killing citizens. sometimes gathering intelligence. It gives a nice variety to the game.  And that's the area where Phoenix Point shines - in its variety.  Land on an "explore area" and you could wind up with a text encounter that yields supplies, faction, or moral choices.  Or you could get ambushed by raiders, or critters, or one of the three factions.  You can help the in game factions or choose to raid them yourself.  Why build an aircraft when you can steal it? In some ways the game improves on the X-com series.  You can always choose to "free aim" . This brings up a targeting ring with two areas - an inner area and an outer ring. Bullets will always land somewhere within the two ( unless they hit an object on the way to the target ). No more RNG miss madness.  If you aim center mass and both targeting areas are on the target, you are going to hit something.  You may not hit the little squishy body part that fills only part of the two rings - but you will hit something inside those two rings.  Specific body parts have specific functions.  Wound a leg and the enemy will move slower.  Blow off a giant, pointy arm and that hulking creature can no longer stab you with it.  The targeting and "real balistics" are a great improvement over X-com .  Even though it's not X-com, there are still some traditional X-com moments.  Don't have time to use the front door?  Blow a hole in the back wall and charge in to rescue a citizen from hot alien death.Tactically, your starting squad is fairly weak on skills and abilities.  As they level up, your combat options expand.  One great feature is that your heavy weapon user starts out with a jet pack.  Swoop down on an enemy and bash them to death with your auto cannon  ( this is pretty much a necessity because firing your auto cannon takes three of your four action points but bashing only takes one ) . A plus - or minus depending how you view such things - is the presence of a "doom timer".   If the human population falls under a certain percentage, it's game over.  If the "skull bar" fills up fully...  not sure what happens, hasn't happened yet, but probably nothing good.   What it boils down to is that time is not your friend.  Enemies continually get stronger and have improved skills.   A red fog of infection spreads inexorably over the map.   If a constant sense of doom or the unfairness of alien infestation excites you, then Phoenix Point is what you are looking for.Some players have experienced bugs.  I haven't come across any.  The game has been very stable for me.  Is Phoenix Point  X-com or X-com plus ?  No.  And that's not a bad thing.   Phoenix Point is a fun game with varied elements and enjoyable turn based battles.   Give it a go and see.

_childDocuments_.review: The realistic ballistics really sell this game to me. No longer do you get right on someone and have a 65% chance to hit. You can shoot the floor the enemy is standing on. _childDocuments_.review: Game feels patchy and incomplete. Nonsensical difficulty spikes once you reach a certain point in the campaign. Troop equipment organization and manufacturing is a mess. Way too much to do and you will never even get closing to doing it, so when bad things happen, it feels out of your control. _childDocuments_.review: Took me a while to finish my first campaign, but I can say it just clicked for me in a way XCOM2 never did.My biggest gripe with XCOM2 is that everything runs on countdowns which eventually put me off so much that I've never finished a campaign on that one.In PP however, countdowns are used sparingly and make more sense.The free aiming system, which some people dismiss as 'gimmick', is quite fun to use and has its uses beyond the 'cover as large an area as possible on the bad guy'. E.g if an enemy has no means to hurt you anymore, he's basically taken off the board. So if someone has just a 2-handed weapon and you shoot off one of his arms (or destroy the weapon), he's no threat anymore.It also gives more immersive feedback on your hitchance than a simple number; and since a lot of the weapons fire in bursts and each projectile is rolled seperately, it doesn't need to artificially roll a 'glance' or similar for you, you just hit with 3 out of 6 bullets on a bad shot and that's it.The 7 classes can be combined into 21 different 'cross-classes' (since Sniper/Heavy is the same as Heavy/Sniper) and while some combinations are more obvious than others, each ability has at the very least their niche where it comes handy. Each person also has up to 3 random perks which can make a difference in what class-combination and what combat role they'd be best suited for.Mutations and augments add additional variety and further abilities - I was quite surprised how much room for theorycrafting and experimentation is in this game.However, the UI is adequate at best:- there are no standard gear layouts or 'unequip all' buttons- the manufacture and equip screens lack sorting options (the default order of items is just a mess) ...- ... and are using not enough space on the screen which leads to way too much scrolling, especially if you don't know exactly what you're looking for while you haven't memorized the names or looks of items (and even if you know the names, there's no search function).All in all, 'twas fun and well worth the time.

_childDocuments_.review: It was difficult for me to decide whether I like this game or not.  I will put it this way: I recommend your second play through.  If you've got weeks to spare, you will enjoy your second or third run at this thing.Phoenix Point is very difficult and has a lot of balance issues. No play though is going to be the same, but the mechanics will be.  I realized about four hours after the world was lost in my first game, that Phoenix Point's difficulty is mainly due to overly complicated game mechanics that are poorly explained.In X-Com 2, you have a traveling military base and can deploy whatever combination of soldiers you need where ever they are needed, and there's often a binary choice with advantages and tradeoffs between optional missions.  Here, you have to coordinate intercontinental bases staffed with personnel, and manage your resources in a way that is arbitrary and leaves little room for experimentation.  X-Com 2 puts a lot of agency in the player's hands regarding how they want to advance through tech trees or what goals they want to prioritize.  Phoenix Point appears to do that as well, but it's largely an illusion - the enemies are constantly outpacing your organization's development, so if you waste resources building a facility with a limited scope of utilization or don't pursue a mission that would result in the relationship development you need to unlock some certain technology, you will be so far behind that whatever struggles you take on for the next several hours of gameplay will be for naught.In Phoenix Point, it's possible to do everything right, and still lose.  In fact, it's likely.  Some people enjoy having the cards stacked against them, but for me, I had the most fun with the game when I switched to the easiest difficulty, and fully understood how the game wanted me to play it, about 12 hours in.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenix Point

_childDocuments_.review: This game is trying to be the modern X-COM/Ufo Defense from the good old Microprose days. I so want it to succeed in that regard! Yes, I played those games from back in 1994 when I was a little kid and I finished it many times as well even on superhuman and it was fun! I would love to get that feeling back or even exceed that for this game. But, there are a lot of annoying nuances that prevent me on that. I'm recommending this game on hopes that more people voice out ideas and feedback for this game. I also played the newer variants of XCOM from Activision, the UFO games by Altar because I love the genre. You fight, you research, you fight some more and you win if you fight smart.Now for the game:It's definitely fun and enticing on your first 10-15 hours. Heck I lost a lot of sleep on this because I got hooked on it. Then I hit these walls:- I finished building the 1st land vehicle... ... ... how do I use it? do I ride it and go to POIs? or do I load it up on to my only aerial vehicle and end up with only 2 soldiers + that land vehicle? can I change the weapon mounted on it? I just couldn't figure it out. I was expecting it to behave like the soldiers screen but I'm clearly missing something here.- I've been grinding XP for my soldiers as best as I can to get them the skills they need but my research and resources are nowhere close to match that effort. - Then the Pandorans started getting stronger and get this... they're carrying more advanced weapons than you! How the heck did these mutants from the ocean learn how to manufacture beam weapons?! And nope, when you kill something (pandoran/mutant/human), your odds for winning the lottery are better when compared to the chances that you'll get any equipment from the kill.- Let's say you overcome the technology handicap above with sheer tactics and wit (or sticks and stones), then you meet a freaking oversized centipede that can mind control all your troops! Ok, ok, I'm exaggerating a little there but given you can't bring a lot of troops with you and this OP enemy can control more than 1 at a time is just too much. If you have a bigger stick to quash this bug that could make up for it but in reality you won't.- These pandorans are not aliens/ufos, they breathe the same air on the surface but for some reason, you need to research something way down the tech tree just so you can "capture" them for study. That's just ridiculous!- Yes, you have grenades but your new year or independence day celebration firecrackers probably pack more punch than these.- You worked hard to get more bases activated, even added more labs and workshops for increasing production and research capacity but you don't have anything to research on.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm on the border of not recommending, but overall It still won a thumbs up.This game heavily reminds me of another game I review, humankind. Both are supposed to be titan slayer (PP slays xcom, humankind slays civ), made with a developer that is very qualified, but fails. Nevertheless unlike humankind which misses almost entirely, PP plays its safer by incorporating most of xcom already familiar recipe with a few difference in combat that really polarize the game. The hit chance is replaced with ballistics system. Basically you fire your gun, and your buillet go to around your reticle. They can't go out from the reticle. The damage depends on how many projectile hit your enemy.The main deal breaker for me is the base management and geoscape. Xcom hits the perfect sweet spot of simplicity and complexity. Pheonix point cranks it up to the max to the point it becomes a chore. Almost a deal breaker, but the combat saves it. The resource management is fine, but the magazine system and some DLC unit maintenance really burns your resource. Yes, in this game you do not have unlimited ammo, instead you must craft/scavange magazines, If you have titanium DLC, your mechanical unit is almost not worth it. Tanky, but even the tiniest dent will burn your resource for maintenance. Overall 6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I came to this game after I absolutely loved every painful minute of playing xcom and xcom 2. _childDocuments_.review: I loved the Xcom games, spent literally 100s of hours in them and can see where some would consider this a worthy successor.  Sadly however, this game to me is simply not fun.  Even on the tamer 'Veteran' difficulty you will quickly get overwhelmed by either sheer numbers or because that one tech you didn't research or couldn't quite reach because your diplomacy wasn't up to snuff with a key ally.  As a player there is just too much you're in the dark about until it's too late.  You can point to it just being a learning curve but I've restarted my campaign 4 times now and it's just too unbalanced to be fun. _childDocuments_.review: I'm recommending this game, because it is by no means bad, and brings some interesting new mechanics to the table - a blend of the action point and turn based approaches, a new take on accuracy and manual aiming and a wide variety of enemy types and loadouts, which admittedly got a little confusing at the end.However, it pales to what XCOM2 and, even the XCOM EW, can be, and suffers from bloated systems with a bolt-on approach to DLC and expansions. There are too many small annoyances as well, such as incomplete documentation and guidance, anomalies in the aiming system and some interface challenges.If you really like the genre, and want something a bit closer to UFO than the more recent Firaxis titles, but find Xenonauts a bit *too* old-school, go for it. Otherwise, you might better enjoy XCOM:EW or XCOM2 with the respective longwar mod installed.
