_childDocuments_.review: Coming from the board and card games, this is a good adaptation while adding more videogame-focused combat.  Fans of Mansions of Madness should really enjoy this one.  Controls are a bit slow, but you have lots of options.  It has all the familiar characters with Full Voice!!!  That's something the MoM boardgame is really lacking, no voice.  It may be a little rigid for people looking for the typical videogame murder mystery, but again, it's quite seamless coming from the boardgames.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I commend the devs for trying something different rather than just a digital adaptation of any of the current board games on the market. However, I feel everything would have been a lot better if a digital version was what they had made. A good one at the very least. Arkham Horror: Mother’s Embrace isn’t a horrible time but I certainly prefer any of the board games over this any day.  I think many people would probably be left wishing things were more fleshed out. I said yes for recommending the game, but I only would suggest this if you’re a big fan of Lovecraftian stories and can get it on sale. Otherwise, I can’t see this as being worth it to that many people.If you'd like to see my full review then feel free to check it out here:
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game. The story was compelling, My  investigator was a Shakespeare spouting, stage loving grave digger. He was really entertaining. The art direction was really good. Some of the scene photos/artwork were just really pretty. The period pieces were on point. I dug it. The combat was janky(rough) but you can't have everything. I liked the party members you pick up on the maps. The spell system was fun. I do recommend if you like eldritch horror. Want to see more. Thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: It is unclear which board game this is even based on, as it seems to have grabbed all the worst parts of "Arkham Horror", "Arkham Horror the living card game" and "Mansions of Madness", and that's really saying something because all of those games are decent to great. Exploration is slow, with the "run" button increasing your character's movement speed by a blinding 5%. Camera angle is mostly downward and zoomed in, meaning that you can't see very far around you so that means a lot of extra walking to explore larger rooms. There are no meaningful choices to be made. You interact with objects, and are presented with 2 or more possible interactions. All but one is "wrong" and you are penalized for picking it. There is no indication of logic to which is the correct choice. For example: This time picking the lock on the drawer is correct, but for the other drawer across the room, with the same description, the correct response is to bash it open. There are no visible die rolls, character skills do not have an obvious impact on outcomes because there is no feedback outside of "WRONG, time to raise the doom track!"Combat is likewise so barren it might as well not exist. It's "tactical" in the sense that you move around and have action points, but there seems to be no such thing as cover, and units all move far enough that positioning doesn't make any difference. Attacks don't seem to ever miss, just do regular damage or a critical for more. I didn't experience any technical difficulties so I guess there is that.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who loves the Mansions of Madness and Arkham Horror board games, this is a let-down.  The controls are awkward.  There are no difficulty settings.  The inventory space is incredibly limited, resulting in leaving useful items behind.  Combat is incredibly tedious for the chapters I played - generally characters get one attack action and a bit of movement, and the movement is awkward.  For anyone reading this - just go play Mansions of Madness or Arkham Horror on tabletop simulator instead - you'll have a much better time.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of H.P. Lovecraft and Arkham Horror BG serie and everything related to Arkham Horror I'm really enjoyng the game. Gameplay is pretty simple but it works; it's a classic graphic adventure, so you move around finding and collecting clues and they added some combats in a quite simple TB system. The graphics is nothing special but TBH is not bad and it's really ok for this kind of game and the art style is really immersive, for a 15,99€ game (in preorder and till 24 of March) I have seen much worse. Technically there are some issues, graphical settings are not saved on game exit and there are a couple of issues during the tutorial, everything can be sorted and patched out, I hope that they will support the game both with patches and additional content.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: Simply weak at every level. I did not experience any bugs, and considering the cheap design of the game, the combats are fairly elaborated. But you can tell that it was done in a hurry. The story is completely linear and "discovering" clues is equal to pressing next. No challenge in understanding/discovering clues and mysteries. One bit that reflects the board game is that with the Mythos clock advancing, things get only more difficult and sometimes you can feel that you won't make it. But I have never been even near from loosing, making the game too easy and straightforward. And you probably will guess the entire story from the beginning. the main thing lacking from the board game is that investigators are basically interchangeable and differ only on their fighting ability, they do not have specific skills. I'd say they should return to their game and work more on it. Potentially good, but far from good.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: The voice acting is phenomenal and fun.  The story is well plotted and tight.  I'm not done but I am enjoying this a great deal. This is a great representation of the Cthulhu mythos and nice suspenseful mystery.That said, the camera angles are sometimes awkward and there is no looking up or down.  Every little thing you touch hurts your sanity! These are some of the most fragile human beings you'll ever meet and they never "get better" at not having an aneurysm over the same stimulus.  If someone comes at you the first time, yeah scary, but when you're fighting your 20th cultist maybe not as earthshaking?  I don't feel that my characters should be driven to multiple aneurysms simply by interacting with every single potential clue.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: Loving the way this game is currently playing out. The mood and setting is fantastic, the story intriguing, and the difficulty has a nice upward progression. Essentially this is like the board game and you need to treat it as such when coming into it. Very enjoyable gameplay so far and cannot wait to play more
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: Actually pretty good (especially for the price), if you are a fan of the Lore & Characters from the Fantasy Flight Board/Card games. It uses a lot of familiar Arkham Horror and Mansions of Madness ideas, but resembles Mansions of Madness most of all. **Unfortunately does not do the randomized layouts and items and encounters like Mansions of Madness--while there is freedom to explore and do some things in a different order (especially after the first few levels), the quests are static, with some optional sidequests. Do a quest, leave your most damaged folks behind to rest, do another, etc. Story is pretty good so far, only on the 5th mission though.***It's too bad, it looks like this was originally going to be a much more ambitious project, (Multiplayer, Procedural Mansions, item decks etc.) it has all the pieces to be a real Mansions of Madness game, but it looks like the new developers might have had to go into salvage mode with what was created and just get something out. Still, I'm enjoying it and giving a thumbs up. Recommend as long as your expectations aren't too high,
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game before release for 15€.Set it up with a controller after reading the negative reviews.-The camera only moves to the left and right, so not being able to move it up and down was a bit annoying, but I somehow quickly adapted to it.-The voice acting is done in a way that the characters mouth don't really move. Doesn't really bother me since it is not a graphically hyper realistic style.-The only infuriating thing is that for some reason the game does not save the graphics options I set. I have to go and set them all from scratch every time I launch the game. (Why do we have an "accept changes" and "reset to default" option if it is not going to work?)I'm gonna keep it, cause it seems okay for a 15€ game.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: I found that so much fighting with possessed asylum patients while reaping little to no reward was tiring.My lead character literally got stuck while questioning one of the college students early in the game, and I had to start over twice due to that glitch.The game had moments of interest that involved finding clues, but when my party kept dying and I didn't understand what the deal with the Mythos? clock was, I just wasn't having fun anymore. I did get at least 3 Achievements for the misuse of valuable inventory items...HA! I don't think I'll be coming back to try again.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the Arkham Files board games, I had high hopes for Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace, but it falls short in key areas. While the story and characters are true to the mythos, the gameplay itself feels slow and lacks depth. Team composition doesn’t matter, and the sanity mechanic, which should be critical in a Lovecraftian game, is practically irrelevant. You’ll just click around randomly, sometimes getting random sanity effects, but they have no real consequences. Characters move so slow around the map it makes you feel they did it on purpose to make the game longer... With no meaningful strategy or sense of progression, the game ends up being a shallow experience that doesn't do justice to the Arkham Files universe. Play it only if you are an Arkham Files fan for the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: This game probably is frustrating for most gamers. But I really recommend it for all people that enjoy playing the board games / table top games (Arkham Horror, Mansion of Madness) in the same universe. You already know all the investigators and much of the mechanics.I think the game really succeeds in  creating a very similar atmosphere to the board games which I always enjoyed. Also I like the story and all the mystery feeling. Of course it is not very long, so better get this in a sale or something. But I really hope that they will release more & similar games inin this great universe.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: I expected another board game PC port and I got lovecraftian Xcom. Yeah it is not as complex as Xcom, but I enjoyed it for what it is. My characters psyche got broken almost every minute, but it didnt prevent me from finishing the game. When you understand the system and got at least one great shooter in your team, the game is a breeze.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: Simply put, there are too many bugs to make this game enjoyable. Clunky gameplay and combat mechanics didn't help matters either. But the last nail in the coffin was having only one save game slot. Whoever came up with that shining idea should be strapped to a chair and forced to watch "Beyond The Wall Of Sleep" until they're carted off to Arkham. I was so looking forward to this game only to be very disappointed to the point of uninstalling it. This game wasn't released -- it escaped.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: I love the story and the turn-based play style. If you enjoy the board game Mansions of Madness and Arkham Horror The Card Game, you'll find the characters familiar and have a good time as long as the controls don't bug you too much. It was shorter than I expected, though - I play slow and it only took me 12.5 hours to get through the game my first time. The controls are pretty clunky, and there are a number of small glitches that sometimes interfere with immersion (like the investigation text for a cabinet describing a broken table on the other side of the house, or rooms where suddenly you can't rotate perspective at all). I'll likely play through again at some point with a different starting investigator, and see if there are any changes to the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: I am a fan of the stories of H.P. Lovecraft, and have enjoyed the app driven board game Mansions of Madness. I had this game on my wish list, because it was originally going to be a DCL for Mansions of Madness as far as I know. They stopped making Mansions of Madness early last year, and I figured that this game would never come out. I was surprised to see it on sale for pre-order when I did. I actually really enjoyed paying this game, and loved that some of the investigators that they used in Mansions of Madness were featured in this game. I think where the game falls short is in it's graphics and how you move through the world. Where it excels is in the story telling, and voice acting. They combat system is simple but enjoyable. I found it very fun to play. The developers have done a great job at creating a Lovecraftien type investigation/adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: OR How to make compelling game that requires you make a sanity check whenever touching the games GUISummary:If you think this is Mansion of Madness or a direct implementation of Arkham Horror you WILL be disappointed. However if you’ve been hankering for a turned based RPG/Squad based game that includes a interesting sanity mechanic with a strong Arkham Horror theme, this flawed gem is definitely worth a lookGameplay:You start the game choosing one of seven characters as your main protagonist but gather more investigators to assist you as you play. Each investigation has different stats, strength and weaknesses, different trait, and their own back storyThe gameplay switches between walking your team through adventure/investigate elements and turn-based battles with 5 action points. Both modes have issues, you walk around the maps looking for glowies that will either be clues, people, or equipment you can salvage. Sometimes you will find things that hurt you, that advance the doom clock or damage or hurt your sanity. They are interesting clue seeking tidbits, and clues you can read, but the log is NO help in summarizing that information which means you can run up the doom clock if you don’t have a great memory or don’t take notes. These kinds of issues are common throughout, and really can be annoying BUT somehow if you can accept them you will find a game that is well better than the sum of its parts, or flaws in this case.The adventure and turn based aspects are not well developed but neither are they that bad, the thing that makes this game unique is how you can lose sanity points along your mission, your sanity reaches zero, your character gets a trauma that will negatively affect the investigator, Their sanity then refills up, but you now have to deal with the trauma they’ve acquired. Between missions you can leave a traumatized Investigator at home so their trauma will be cleared. You can also use equipment you find to help you in your adventures. Cigarettes will cure sanity BUT damage the investigator, guns require bullets, and spell books can help you in fights, bandages can heal damage, and coffee can reset your action points.The interesting thing about this game, is that what is does well it does really well, and the thing it doesn’t, can be outright annoying.StoryThe story will begin including a little bit about the back story of you investigator, and the story is well told, BUT the narration is handled by Wilhelmina Tillinghast, who is the person you are to meet and goes missing, and the handling of it is a little jarring. Sure it results in some humorous dialogue at times, and other times unintentionally humorous dialogue, but seems like a odd choice you just get used and ultimately works if you can get over the odd choices the design team made.GUIOof! This one is a mess. You are constantly fighting things here. From an interface that doesn’t give you a clear indicator of how much moving cost in ap till you spent too much, or the clunky way you move in combat or the clunky way move inventory. This is a low light of the game design, it is definitely a hurdle, but if you can excuse it the game has lots to offer you.Sound All the investigators are voiced and have personality. The music is appropriate, this one is across the board pretty good, but not great.Graphics’ The graphics are good, but the animations and interactions are at times limited and clearly make it clear this was intended as a budget titles. They are decent though, some nice detail included throughout and it worksDifficultyModerately difficulty, turn based battle can be challenging sometimes includes puzzles or civilians you need to protect.ReplayabilityOther than the start with the unique back story beginning and the unique voice actors and skills for the 7 investigators, there is a lot of repeat the same adventure portions in replay, but I could see how combat could play differently.PriceWorth the price of $20 if you like the Arkham Horror theme and/or love turned based RPG/Squad based games!
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: If u love AH, Eldritch Horror or Mansions of Madness or either are a fan of Lovecraft and Cosmic Horror genre, this one is a must for u. Narration, fights and everything is drawn from FF board games and they are delivered nicely. It is a absolute pleasure to see ur favorite characters from games and AH files series in 3D digital format. But game has some performance issues such as frame drop that I hope get fixed soon by updates (thank Old Ones this is LH and Asmodee and not CDPR).
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the Arkham Horror table top game, his is a neat point and click adventure with some light but interesting srpg mechanics tacked on. It's not an adaptation of any of the 928 different board and card games in the setting, but I still find it fun enough for the price. The controls are awkward but in a way you can get used to after an hour, and the graphics aren't terribly special but they're also not the worst ever. I wouldn't suggest this for someone who wants something like the Gloomhaven computer adaptation, or to people who are sensitive to controls, but if you're a fan of the Cthulhu Mythos or the Arkham Horror characters and setting, this is a fun point and click adventure in the setting.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: It's what is says on the tin, a lovecraftian adventure using a turn based combat mechanic, and for the price it's worth it I'd say. I got about 6 hours out of it going through it at a steady pace, going in completely blind.The combat is enjoyable albeit not to difficult. With the real challenge being: "What gear/Investigators do we bring along today", It's nice to see the characters from the board-game making an appearance, with every character being fully voiced (in the cut scenes).Graphically it's not top of the line, but looks good enough, staying faithful to the hand drawn aesthetic.The story is engaging spreading over various locals but not something extremely original, although there where a few moment here and there. And the big-bad is something other than Cthulhu for a change, All and all I would recommend Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: I edit my review after 2 weeks +/- of playing - this game is really good! The first chapter on University was what confused me dearly, I didn't feel the Lovecraft atmosphere. Then in each next chapter the atmosphere just came with all strength, you can definitely feel the Lovecraft vibe and the horror. I recommend this game to everyone who likes board Arkham LCG games, Mansion of Madness and so on.But of course -- pros and cons:PROS:-The atmosphere is there!-Very pleasant graphics-Nice battle mode in my opinion -Nice voice acting - not perfect, but quite niceCONS:-The characters tend to block each other from time to time-The graphics are quite old now, they could be a little more suited for 2021 I count on DLCs and new scenarios!
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: So I'm 2hrs in and I'm enjoying this game. The atmosphere is good, its more of a lighter tone in looks compared to other lovecraftian games. The voice acting has been done well.  The graphics are bit basic but it maybe the style they were going for. The game play is simple but I'm not seeing that as a bad thing, people are comparing it to the board game which I've never played so I'm guessing people were expecting it to be more like that?It basically plays like a point and click game but this has added elements like combat and sanity checks. So if you like that kind of stuff this will be up your street. Its no Triple A game but that's why it costs only 15 moneys and not 30 - 40 odd.  If you're into Lovecraft like myself then I'd recommend this for the story and chill play.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of all things related to the Arkham Files, this is a huge disappointment.  Granted, I had very high hopes for this since I first heard about it, but it fell so short of the mark.  The interface is clunky and unwieldy, the dialog is terrible and conversations don't flow naturally at all, and it's just dull and lackluster.  It feels like this was created as a high school project for a game design class and it's completely unpolished.  I'm actually angry that Asmodee and Fantasy Flight would allow this to be release in it's current state.  So disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: So I'm not sure why some of the posted reviews so far are so negative. I really enjoyed what I have played so far. The voice acting didn't seem bad at all. I did notice the camera angle at the beginning wasn't great but you got used to it or it got better I can't decide which. The story so far also seems pretty awesome. The combat is turn based and is similar to Divinity Original Sin so I didn't have an issue with it other than the awkward death animation but nothing terrible. The inventory is small but haven't once been short on space. Maybe it's because I never played anything to do with Arkham other than this and it isn't living up to others expectations but I am having a great time playing. If you want to watch the first two missions you can watch my play through with the link below. Overall I would recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: Until they fix the sanity system in the game, I will be down voting this game and not recommending it.  Walk into a empty room, san loss.  Turn on a light, san loss.  Look out a window, san loss.  Wake up to start a new day, san loss.  Needs serious retooling considering the detrimental effects it has on your characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: I overall enjoyed the game. There are some bugs that need to be fixed, but I was able to work around most of them and it's only one scenario (The Herd of Algedy) that really annoyed me because the bugs were a major issue. It was fairly easy to play through the story and even the fights weren't actually challenging, but I liked the atmosphere and the 1920s feel of it all. It probably helps that I'm a huge fan of the board games though. The replayability of this game is limited - at least if they don't add more scenarios to the game in the future, which I kinda hope they will. I can still see myself playing this game again to collect the remaining Steam achievements. ;-)
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: I have never posted a review before but these negative posts are way off base. The price is MORE than reasonable for what you are getting. I absolutely love the art style! The theme is on point with lots of fantastic settings. The voice acting is great for some characters and mediocre for others (I suggest starting with the professor as your main for best theming). The combat system is basic turn based western RPG (or D&D 4th gen). Haven't encountered any bugs so far, but no game is perfect.If you are a fan of horror and lovecraft you'll have a blast.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Lovecraft's stories and setting this is worth a play if you can buy it on a LARGE discount.  It is somewhat atmospheric, and is well narrated (other voice acting is hit and miss).  Graphics and music are better than expected.  Game play is very simple, almost walking simulator simple, if that makes sense (but it isn't a walking simulator).What are you getting?  A weird combo b/w a very simple adventure game, and a poor xcom style tactical battle system.  However, as I said, if you like Lovecraftian stuff the adventure components are ok and the combat is tolerable for brief periods.  It isn't a hard game and is a good one to play if you just want to turn off your brain and chill.  I'd give it.... 5/10?  Really only worth it if you like the subject matter and are feeling a bit starved.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: I like it!  It isn't really a video game as much as it is game-ification of the mansions of madness app that accompanies that board game.  Imagine using that app, but instead of just clicking on the question marks or explore tokens to advance the app, you have characters that you can control running around the environment.  In a way, it is like a new board game has been created in the Arkham Horror universe, with many of the familiar faces, mechanics, and references, and this new board game is being presented to us in digital form.  When I started looking at the experience through that lens, I began to enjoy it a lot and will definitely be keeping this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: In brief, a good plot but ruined by bad game visuals, disgusting art, slow camera, clunky control, annoying narrative and lacks what made mansions of madness a great gameplay.I bought this as I wanted to play mansions of madness 2 but without spending time setting up the board game and playing dungeon master. But I guess the board game is so much more interesting that I am considering going back to it instead of playing this nuisance of a video game. Not gonna buy another game of this publisher.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: I do really like Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace, the game has an interesting story and a charismatic cast of characters set in the H.P. Lovecraft universe. It does have a few bugs though, a few issues with the controller I have had so far, hopefully this will be rectified soon. From a gameplay perspective, AH has turn based combat inter-spliced with the exploration of each scenario, from using pistols to melee weapons and also magic against otherworldly foes; one qualm I have with the gameplay is the insanity checks; when working through the levels reading documents and further clues to aid you lowers your sanity. Menial aspects affect this too much though, you will read a newspaper with a headline and lose sanity, a tad over-dramatic. This affects gameplay when you lose all your sanity points, this turns into a trauma, which decreases your skills such as range to attack an enemy. You can rest your investigators in-between scenarios as you'll have a wide range to choose from.Overall it is a solid and enjoyable game for the price of admission, there are some bugs but nothing too game breaking so far. If you are a fan of story and investigation games it is well worth checking out.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: Inspired to write when the game froze up. More on that later.First impression of game play, this looks and handles like a game from well over 10 years ago. I'm not a cutting edge gamer or anything but the basic look and control is substandard.The game flashed tips, for how to play games in general for some reason. Recommended checking the map if you're lost or whatever. Funny thing though, no matter where I move throughout the few levels I could before failure, the icon of my position on the map is always in the same location.Entering a level the map indicated that a door was locked (why is a map telling me that in advance?) so I went the other way to explore for a key or whatever. The game quickly had my character correct me and tell me that I needed to go to that locked room, and instantly placed me there. Where I "found out" the door was locked and then I was allowed to go back about my exploring. There are times for my character to state an exposition letting me know I'm trying something impossible or whatever. But short of that I expect to have the space to make mistakes. For my character to correct my action like that, it takes the role and the play out of a role playing game.Further on the level was a hall that was illustrated to have 2 doors and had a "this might be something" symbol on each, though the map showed they weren't really doors. Not that something secret is hidden behind a wall that is dressed up like a normal wall in a house, rather a programmer did a half @$$ job. I am betting the story will never go to those not rooms, but that for whatever reason that hall is just there serving no purpose and is visually misleading while the map shows its just worthless.Shortly after the game told me about new data in my ledger so I went to go through it to make the prompt go away, but I cannot close the ledger now. I can flip through pages. There is a row on the bottom of my screen telling me the controls, and telling me the same controls again, over and over.From my first impression up until the game refused to play I was disappointed. Don't see how it can be anything more than what it is now, except that glitches should be sorted out.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: the game felt shallow, capricious, and plodding.  Requested a refund.Long version:The "correct" decisions during Exploration/Deduction felt capricious and inscrutable.  It does seem that there were keywords related to some of the decisions and that there was a system for certain investigators being able to provide hints for those decisions, but for my choice of initial investigator I never benefited from this system in the opening act and what I played of the second act.  Sometimes the narration of the action taken didn't seem to me to match the name of the selection.  And you're punished for choosing the wrong option.In my (very limited) play I was never able to explore anywhere that wasn't absolutely critical to the plot.  There were interactions that were optional, but they all contained an item or delivered only a line or two of flavor text.  Everything was either directly on the main path or immediately adjacent to it.The dialog and plot felt weird.  For example, in the opening act (minor spoilers) very early on you're given a goal to get to a room on the second floor of the house you're in because you believe your friend is there.  You're in the foyer with stairs going up.  You cannot go up the stairs until you take the time to investigate a broken object on the floor first.  Why?  Because the plot says that while you're investigating the broken object you hear a scream from the person you came to see, who is in the room you were heading towards.  And you can't go up the stairs until you've armed yourself (with a letter opener?), which you can't do until after you hear the scream.Later, you find that person freshly sacrificed/murdered, with your only lead pointing to their place of work, ending the opening act.  The second act opens with you arriving at that place of work to access their office.  You approach a colleague to get the key to the office of your just-murdered friend.  The colleague berates you saying that they don't want to talk because they've already been badgered by police, reporters, and others. What?  Wait a minute?  Weren't we the ones to discover the murder?  How did the rest of the world find out about this and beat us there?  And by long enough that these other people were all gone by the time we got there.  It felt like a contrivance by the writer to avoid us having to break the news of the murder and also give the person a reason to not even want to talk to us, but it didn't make any narrative sense to me.The pace of combat felt plodding, even for a turn-based system, and yet somehow the controls are also still fiddly.  For example, during combat you can change what you have equipped for free as much as you want throughout your turn, and you can have both a melee weapon and a spell equipped at the same time, but if you change your melee option to your fist (the only way unequip a melee weapon) that sometimes will unequip your spell and sometimes it won't.I pre-ordered the game because of the discount.  I was disappointed and requested a refund.

At the start of the game you will enter a mansion where you can immediately go upstairs if you choose. _childDocuments_.review: This is a lukewarm recommendation; the game has little to offer.Not an RPG whatsoever, it's in essence a Point n' Click gameplay without much thinking, but with a dose of random choices and a copious serving of turn-based combat.Said combat is tactically lightweight, if not flyweight; minimal thinking required as well.The only connections with Lovecraft are the period, a visit to the Miskatonic University, and sanity checks (as introduced by the original Call of Cthulhu franchise.)The horror itself is run-of-the-mill witchcraft, not Lovecrafted.Said sanity checks occur every minute and for the most mundane reasons; not exactly immersive.Besides, in practice, the consequences of sanity losses are negligible.The interface is 2nd-rate.You can save and reload rather freely, but on one slot only; and unreliably so, because said slot is randomly overwritten by the auto-save (for a double dose of stupidity in reinventing the wheel.)The inventory is limited, tiny, yet a pain to manipulate; at least with a gamepad, as it seems to be designed for pocket phones.(Another sign that the game is a mobile port is the smallness of maps and the simplicity of the visuals.)In essence, you get  a decent, linear story with a decent presentation.There is nothing absolutely wrong with the game, but it's casual in every aspect, and certainly not worth the asked price.And if you're looking for excitement, try elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the Super Mario Bros. movie of video games. Growing up with the original Mario games had me so excited for the movie that even though it was TERRIBLE I watched it a million times and tried to focus on the enjoyable parts and forget the dumb stuff. The world and lore of Arkham Horror is amazing; and the new lore is what keeps me playing Mother's Embrace. Fans with a craving for the the lore of the Arkham Horror universe will be satiated but that's where the positives end. The combat is a less tactical XCom. The investigations are often clicking random dialogue options and hoping for the best, randomly picking the right party member at the onset of the adventure is the only way to get any clues as to the right answer. Focus on dancing elevator Goombas, forget the hobo Toad, and you might enjoy yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: I usually like Asmodee's games: they're simple but enjoyable, so I was very happy to know they were about to launch Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace.I can't explain the disappointment.The story may seem interesting, but IMO the gameplay is awful. - The combat system is extremely cumbersome, but that's the least, you can get used to it eventually- Weapons break in no time and you can't replace them since you don't find them easily - a thing you can expect to balance the gameplay since they break and you won't be able to combat but with your bare hands- Ammo is rare to find (!!!) even if you investigate everywhere taking the risk of losing precious sanity points in the meanwhile- The journal is extremely vague - you would expect to find there nearly everything you learned investigating, but this doesn't happen and you need to take notes- Most importantly, the Italian localization of the UI is a nightmare. I'm a game translator myself so I know what I'm talking about. I don't blame the translator(s) since it might have happened for several reasons, but the tips you get when interacting with an object are too often misleading, and your Mythos Clock ticks. In the third scenario, I even found two identical interaction UIs, which is simply unacceptable! Another time, one of my team suggested an action (investigate), I clicked the "Investigate" action and it wasn't the right option. I uploaded some screenshots for this reason. Many other actions were unclear or worse as well - like when you find two synonyms for two different actions (such as "Guardate velocemente" and "Date uno sguardo"). I don't know why the result was this catastrophic, but the localization needs to be fixed, and urgentlyAt the end of the second scenario, I gave this game a second chance and progressed to the third to see if it would get better, but it didn't. It even got worse and worse. When I ended up with 0 ammo and two broken guns in the middle of combat and had to use bare hands to fight, I decided to give up.I'm deeply sorry because this game has lot of potential, but it's poorly developed. I personally don't think a single patch will be able to fix all these issues any time soon. I will change my review as soon as Asmodee will do something and the reviews will start being positive, but for now, it's a huge NOPE.

_childDocuments_.review: , despite sharing a name with another boardgame, is an attempt to bring the  boardgame to the virtual environment. Even the main game folder is named "Mansions of Madness". If you are familiar with the board games by , you will be familiar with the setting. And, if you have previously played games like  or , you will be familiar with the turn-based combat.If I had to describe  in one word it would be "clumsy". It's inventory management is clumsy. And it's combat interface is clumsy. It also has a lot of useless clues that serve no purpose (just like in the  board games, but still).To move objects, you have to left click them, choose a right click context action "move" and select a destination slot. If you are moving stacked object, you also have to select how many of them you want to move. I think a simple drag and drop approach would have been better and Shift + left click could serve for dividing stacks.Inventory is severely limited, and you can't stack more than 5 items in a slot. It's annoying, but understandable, given that the  board games are also extremely punishing towards the players and the playable characters with the right equipment are much more powerful than the monsters. After each chapter, the equipment is transferred to the party chest; which is comfortable, if you want to choose different investigators, not so much, if you want to continue with the same team.True to the original material, there are a lot of sanity checks, and sanity is the most important stat. You check sanity/lose sanity, whenever the Mythos clock advances full cycle, whenever you encounter a monster or even when you examine a mildly disturbing clue. I would argue that the investigators would adapt to certain things with time and should not get scared every time they see blood or a dead body, but I guess, without the sanity checks and traumas, there wouldn't be any challenge at all. The sanity system serves as an approximation of the cosmic scale otherworldly horrors that the characters encountered in H. P. Lovecraft's stories, so that's the thing with these games. It's a rough approach, but I can live with it.Whereas the skill checks are on a whole different level of absurdity. You're lucky, if you have a character on your team with the right skill to tell which choice to make. However, if you don't, you have to make an educated guess, based on the key words. The problem is that not always those keywords are present, or several choices are equally logical or even the correct choice is not logical at all. So, on your first playthrough, you lose a lot of sanity points simply because of arbitrary skill checks. When it comes to combat, it's the same clunky interface as for inventory. You have to choose an action, then the target, then confirm it. If you are choosing to attack, you have to select a weapon to equip it and then you have to select it AGAIN to attack. Why one click was not enough is beyond my comprehension. A few chapters in the game, you also discover that, when it comes to weapons: firearms > melee weapons > spell books. Also, since attacking is usually the optimal action, in most of the situations, I didn't find spell casting or condition removal (Radithor) worth the action points.There are also some puzzles in the game linked to the investigation. The hints don't always make sense, but, at some point, I stopped caring. has many flaws. Another one that I haven't mentioned are the painted textures that really don't look good on a full HD monitor. And the first impressions are really bad. Oh, and the narration. The game is narrated by an old lady, who . The comic nature of her remarks breaks the immersion and strongly contrasts with the overall atmosphere of gloom and mystery.However, despite all of that, I do like this game. Because it succeeds in two things that matter to me the most: the story and the atmosphere. When I didn't have to listen to the narrator's remarks, I felt immersed in the spooky atmosphere. It was a similar level of immersion, as when playing the original boardgame with my buddies. And the overall story, pulp fiction that it is, is good. It's your typical Lovecraftian horror against the background of prohibition era New England and New Orleans. And, if that's something you're looking for, this game is worth a shot. Just be warned that the first two chapters are pretty bad. If you can get past the first impressions, there is some enjoyment to have. The gameplay is very linear, though. So there’s barely any replay value.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is serviceable, but unimpressive, and disappointing with the high quality experience that its name suggests.Within the first hour and a half, I felt no agency over my character, where no action that I took ever impacted the story in any meaningful way. Not only that, but there weren't options for me to explore other potential solutions or paths.You need to explore to gather resources and main story quest items, but the game arbitrarily punishes you for exploring that you have no way of mitigating or avoiding. Additionally, exploration doesn't feel fun as the exploration you do doesn't ever make you feel like you found a little hidden corner of the world.Combat is dull and ordinary, but functional. My characters in combat didn't feel different from eachother, and there was no strategic element to the combat  besides a meaty slugfest.Voice acting was fine, animations were functional, with all characters obviously having the same rig.The writing was stiff and awkward, especially with the decision to have a narrator, but that the narrator was the professor who was killed? It doesn't make any sense as to why you, the player, are hearing that character's voice.All in all a functional, but unimpressive and non-interesting game with weird decisions that don't live up to the quality that the Arkham Horror name suggests.

_childDocuments_.review: Very hard to get into game, in my opinion this game is only for serious Lovecraft world desiring fans, definitly not deserving full price of course.The problem with the game is that it is trying to hard to be like board game moved to the PC which honestly doesn't fit that well because let's put it plainly I found the game to be very frustrating. I will point out what I disliked and what I liked to make it easier for people to know (PS: I love Lovecraft, I play board games, got even few lovecraftian board games in my home).Let's start with what I liked:* the story - it was actually good* plenty characters to choose from* music, while not at epic level it really helped me to immerse myself* based on H.P. Lovecraft worksWhat I disliked:* although I liked the story the twist was very predictable* although we had plenty of characters to choose from we couldn't use lots of them from the start* pretty short story, 12h to beat the game and I really didn't hurry playing it* no quickload / quicksave* clunky controls for characters (frustrating)* clunky mechanics for insanity (if anyone is familiar with any Cthulhu/Arkham/Eldritch Horror board/card game you probably know this so skip to next point) any action that comes as shocking can 'cause our characters to lose sanity, when we lose enough points we go insane and have some kind of negative effect on our mental health (for example we need to smoke etc.), the thing is in this game we lose sanity points 2 much and 2 fast, we see dead body (not mangled, just somebody killed with weapon) we can lose sanity points, we read a note from some crazy guy we can lose sanity, we see crying student we can lose sanity, it's 2 much and 2 often to the point it is frustrating enough to save game and reload before any interaction so that you use your very limited sanity for what matters most (like meeting enemy), also gonna mention the fact that we meet and killed very early some kind of inhuman being and yet we get scared later on by notes and human corpses sigh... makes no sense* not enough ways to regain sanity during playthrough, we cannot take rest action or something similar we could in board/card games* cut scenes felt really bad* very few item slots per character, just 4 item slot per investigator is just so frustrating, I can find so many items throughout the game and yet I have just 4 slots* cannot revisit old save file after beating the game (for example replaying chapters with different investigators on same save file and keeping inventory) need to start new game after beating itTL:DR I would say that the game tried to hard to be like board game, it is very frustrating to play, I cannot recommend it the way it is to anyone except hardcore fans and people hungry for lovecraftian game. Even for fans I would say wait for a big discount like 80% or more but I can say that most of you will still be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Story 4/5Atmosphere 5/5Gameplay 3/5Mechanics 2/5 but get over it you didn’t expect Cyberpunkreplayability: yea maybeLet me start by saying I adore the Lovecraft Mythos, the original books the lore, the stories, the great old ones even the ttrpg games (personal fav.: CoC RPG,  Mansions of madness and, you guessed it Arkham Horror.) It is impossible to do this review unbiased but I’m willing to at least try.Story,: imo lovecraft was the worst author in the world, his writing style was atrocious but he did create an amazing mythos because he had an amazing fantasy and the developers picked this up, polished it, reimaged it to a more clear storyline and it’s solid although lacking some of the finer details. A lot of other games have better stories but it works. Key is this is a detective game so keep your wits about you. 4/5Atmosphere : It’s a quirky fun gritty that’s Arkham Horrors signature, Fun interactions sometimes silly but they managed to suck you in try to remember you never feel at ease in a Lovecraftian atmosphere but there is enough sense of urgency to keep on going, defy the odds and try to save the world without going Mad. 5/5Gameplay: These people make boardgames that are inherently difficult a lot of fun to play. The mechanics are a little wobbly and some controles are counter intuitive (x-com players beware) yes there are bugs (although few and far apart) but not gamecrashing. 3/5Overall: For the Arkham horror fans Yes, For the lovecraft fans Yes, For the Adventure game fans yes, You want high end graphics up the wazoo … not for you, speedy cool actions and snappy camera movements… also not for you.

_childDocuments_.review: The big caveat here is that this game is not worth the asking retail price -- and only really worthwhile if on sale & below the $10 line.What you get is a tactical turn-based story in the 'Arkham Horror' universe, a franchised world set in H.P.Lovecraft's ficitonal "Cthulhu Mythos".  You can start as one of 7 initial investigators, and will pick up more along the way -- from a total pool of 12.The scenarios, encounters, maps, and narrative are always the same, with variation in dialogue alone, based on your character choices.  You can also see the plot's "twist" coming from a playthrough away, if you have half a brain in your head.It's fun enough for what it is, but don't expect to get scared -- 'ARKHAM HORROR" is certainly not a horror game.  It does have a lot of visual flare and genre flavor, though.Sadly, it has seen only one update since its release, and is apparently ignored by the developers -- despite glaring flaws & typos in the game's text; and the need for simple quality of life fixes that the interface could desperately use to help smooth out gameplay.Let that inform your decision on whether or not to purchase.It certainly reflects poorly on franchise-owner, Fantasy Flight Games.

_childDocuments_.review: Before the review im a really big fan of both Arkham Horror and the Cthulhu mythos, and everything i will say will be from the point of view of a fan.Starting with the negatives, the game have clucky controllers, bad lip sync and in general not a lot of variety in terms of gameplay, in terms of graphs its not the best but not the worst, people shouls stop expectiv hyper realistic graphics in each new games, the art style is really good for this tipe of game, in general i can define it as a high quality low budget game.Now, for the positive aspects, for me this game captures the core of the lovecraft histories better than any other lovecraftian game i have played, the way the game tells story its just perfect for me, and the sound and music for each stage its just the best, i cant think of a better way of adapting this into a game, the best part are the puzzles, the main puzzles are not hard enough, but the side quest one are good, not because they are dfficult but because they make you search and read through the clues you find to solve them, and those optional puzzles make you feel really good after you solve them.Aside from the bad and the good, there is the gameplay itself, it is similar to divinity, but without the hundres of interactions and layers of complexity, its really simple, take your turn use your action points to cast a spell or use a weapon and repeat, but it is enough to maintain you entertained through the story.From my point of view and without finishing the game i think its worth the cost, its not a game that will give you hundreds of hours in gameplay, but it will give you some fun, a good story and if you are a lovecraft fan, a lot of fanservice.

_childDocuments_.review: Takes most of what was interesting from Mansions of Madness and throws it away.  This is very much of the "interactive story" genre where you just click on everything until you've clicked on everything.  At least in Mansions of Madness you have to decide which of your investigators will do what, and there are such things as skill checks and ways to manipulate them, and items that help with things other than combat.  In this, your group of investigators act as a gestalt entity and all real decision-making ends at the point where you choose which investigators should comprise the group for your scenario.  After that, everything is automatic and depends on whether you chose the right people or not.  Add in an overly-long and uninteresting combat system that isn't really what this game should be about, and the result is something that is almost entirely unlike Mansions of Madness.  A big disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a difficult "not recommend". I am really on the fence about this because I definitely don't think it's a good $20 game. But I also don't think it's the worst in the world. The story was interesting enough that I wanted to finish it- but in the last few chapters, I started to very much get annoyed by the fact that everything was very predictable. A lot of the time, you actually got hints and downright explanations for things in secret notes despite the fact that the reveal was coming only a few minutes later. It's about a 6-7 hour game experience, so it's definitely not overpriced game-length wise. I just don't know how many people will be driven to finish it. It doesn't have much replayability. There's a concept that if you reach insanity, which I think is getting 2+ mental afflictions, you get these "bad endings" for the chapters. I got one, it really sucked. We just decided to murder a dude in cold blood, which thematically made no sense. There are items in here that are just completely worthless. The dirty bandages heal you but they cost sanity. And you are NOT going to have enough sanity in this game to waste it on a healing item. There are books and bandages that heal everywhere, so I didn't use a single one. You get a ridiculous amount of items. It becomes a problem near the middle of most chapters that you can't even take your status items because you need to pile in all the new weapons you can handle because you don't want a weapon to break while you're in the middle of combat. So instead of being a survival horror, it's just an inventory organizer horror. At least in Resident Evil, you have a box to put stuff in. This is chapter-by-chapter, so you have to bring things back to your office at the end of the chapter. There's no way to access your inventory otherwise. The story was interesting at first and I really love the theme. But it got boring and predictable later, as I said. This is nothing like the board game. This was clearly inspired by Call of Cthulhu much more than it was inspired by Arkham Horror. A weird distinction to make, I know. But it felt like one of those Baldur's Gate's wannabe games set in the world of CoC. The only thing that was purely Arkham Horror were some of the named characters and the Mythos element. Obviously there are no "action points" in CoC but it's also not in the Akrham Horror board game, either. There were virtually no stakes in this game. I had no problem beating levels and only had to restart once or twice because I lost a battle. The mechanics of combat were fun and everything, but if that's all we're judging it on, you might as well just play Xcom because at least the story is better and there is much more involved mechanically. And the walking is half the game. You're very slow, and you're punished for exploring by the sanity checks that can be complete nonsense. You MUST play this with a controller. If you try to play it with a mouse and keyboard, it is obnoxious. I think it deserves the 6/10 it got. Not bad enough to completely fail, but not good enough to get unless it was on sale.

Everything is too linear. Basically you interact with everything you see, thats it. Most importantly there are not enough riddles and mysteries to clear.Other things are left unexplained. As cultits just appearing somewhere and doing things, and you dont find out why. It just happens. Of course you can make up story steps by yourself, various...Technical and Game design:There would have been potential to have more than only the sanity rolls as rng factor. Inventory is too small to use all the helpful stuff and you loot the same things over and over again. There seems to be no progression as you would expect from for instance the boardgames.Sanity drops not enough even if you touch everything you find. The characters could be way more deep and developed, or get a kind of development, where are permanent improvements and other basic stuff?The Interface is terrible, near the ending voiceover is no longer on par with dialogue texts or mixed and even spoilerlike if you pay attention. Characters get stuck somewhere, interaction gets clunky in some camer angles.The animations are just too blunt and some stuff that would have brought atmospere, such as smoking, is not animated. Having to pick the investigator you grab at the beginning, for every adventure does not make sense, as far as character switchting works here. I did not got the 3 insanity effects on 1 char, you would have to force it with misuse from interactions, i guess....Ranged combat weapons especially the 1911 look-a-like outperform everything else, movement is too slow, maigc damage too low, rifle dmg to low, etc, etc...Dialogues not autoplayed, why?This game is not the price it is tagged at. Point and Click as a genre would involve less control effort and would have been more fitting, walking around with WASD ads nothing to this game. _childDocuments_.review: A complete nightmare of a game that is entirely unplayable... the controls are clunky and not user-friendly at all, the horror checks are frustrating and combat is even worse. Just... play the board games. Some remarks before I end the review:- controls have to be a lot more user friendly- the BRIGHTNESS have to be improved by like a frickton. I had to adjust my monitor's brightness in order to be able to see ANYTHING so after that I had to adjust it again for normal daily use.- Stop it with the random horror checks. I know that it is an FF staple, but we have house rules that work around that to make the board games playable for people of varying experiences. Not so with this game and it is just frustrating. The exploration phase is horrible and the horror checks just make it worse!- RELAX the Mythos criteria. I just... the sanity checks are already driving me insane... the mythos is so unnecessary...- The combat... my God... I don't even know what to say about the combat. It is horrible. _childDocuments_.review: I'm two scenarios into the game so far, and I would recommend fans of the board games to try it out. Speaking of, I do notice some problems that I hope are patched away pretty soon:- The camera perspective is weird, as other reviews point out- The run function is not all that much faster than the normal walk function, so its weird to insist on holding the run button in. This should be a toggle instead. Running should be a bit faster as well.- It would be nice if the game had an auto-next for dialogue in cut scenes. When the voice actors takes so much time with each line, I get unnecessarily impatient when I'm tasked with pushing the button for continuing.And I have a last point that might be more off a pet peeve than constructive feedback, but why doesn't Jenny Barnes have the social skill? I first suspected that it could've made her unbalanced, but after recruiting the two first team members in the game, another skill would make her some more balanced, not less. Her social skill gives the character more personality in the board games, so it's a shame that it doesn't keep up in the video game.

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly I cannot recommend this game.  There is a severe lack of Lovecraftian games that are worth playing, despite the genre being (one would think) so suited to gaming.Graphically it looks like a PS4 launch title.  Surely not up to par with what one would expect in 2021.   I could overlook that if the game was fun though right?   Well no, it's not.   The camera angle is stuck at a Looking Down 3rd person perspective, which I found to be somewhat annoying.  You can move it back and forth but that's it, no way to properly look around like in Every Other Third Person Game.Voice acting is bland.   I'd liken it to new voice actors who don't understand how inflection and tone are so important in voice acting.   Think original RE1 poor voice acting.You can pick characters, but you don't get a lot of detail as to which can do what.  Saying this character is "average" at "physical" doesn't tell me much.  It's like the devs assumed  everyone had played the board game it's based on and didn't bother with details.It also doesn't have a lot of settings for video.  Seriously, just on/off for antialiasing?Refunded.  A good idea of a game poorly done.

_childDocuments_.review: The game certainly has issues. It's buggy - I encountered a major softlock in the Herd Mansion that required me to completely restart the mission, and multiple times I encountered dialogue subtitles that were completely wrong, or interactable descriptions that were outright broken.The game is also a complete pushover to anyone experienced with turn based strategy games - Not once in my playthrough did an Investigator go down, even though the game clearly expected it to happen with how many revive items it was giving me. Additionally certain combinations from about the mid-game can get hilarious powerful in comparison to the enemies (Give Roland a Shotgun and a few Bromo Caffeine pills and he will literally solo any boss fight in the game, or give any ranged character the Semi-Auto pistol and custom rounds and they will be putting out 15-22 damage per turn (depending on Overwatch)). A difficulty selection would be nice so I can properly challenge myself.However - If you're a fan of the Arkham Horror Franchise and want a quaint budget title (Yes - This is very clearly a budget title), it's worth a look, and certainly worth grabbing on a sale. The overall narrative was quite engaging for someone that likes to immerse themselves in game worlds (And no, the voice acting isn't nearly as bad as people were saying, I have no clue what's up with that), and while the gameplay was simple it was engaging enough to keep me through the game's 6-7 hour runtime.If I had to put a number on this game, I would give it a 7/10 - Very flawed, very jank, but if you're able to look past that, it's a nice time. I hope they're able to learn their lessons from this game and make an even better one in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: This is sort of a qualified thumbs-up.It's not a great game, or a super intricate game.  But if you like the Arkham Horror board games and the Lovecraft Mythos, it's a fun little story / campaign you play with familiar names and personalities from the board games.The combat is passable for what it is, the voice acting ranges from inoffensive to decent, although I was personally impressed that the game adapts with actual voice acting since you can bring any investigators on any mission and they'll still say lines.  It's basically about exploring scenes from the lovecraft mythos, fighting baddies in simple turn based combat, and piecing together a classic mythos mystery.So while I wouldn't give the game any awards, I had fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Light recommend. The developers being cycled out on this project, and redesign, was felt through the plot in that it felt strung together. The combat is turn-based, much like X-COM but without cover mechanics or any depth. There are perhaps a grand total of 4-5 enemy types, two of them just being variations of one another.So far as the writing, it is serviceable. Not excellent, but not terrible. I would say that the most bothersome aspect of both the plot (once you've figured it out) and the writing is the narrator. The narrator serves more to distract and take away from the atmosphere than to help build it. Speaking of atmosphere, there is not much here beyond the typical Lovecraft setup. One level in a mental ward, one level in a bayou, a few in mansions... But it does not capture that Mansions of Madness board feeling.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game with many reservations.1.) Give it a chance ONLY if you enjoy the Cthulhu mythos or universe. If you like HP Lovecraft and/or the Arkham Horror LCG or tapletop games, only then does this game have the *potential* to be worth your time.2.) The game is rough at a technical level. Even within an hour, I ran into a bug that required me to restart from the last checkpoint because the game refused to continue to the next phase of combat. Clearly, this is not an issue related to my OS / hardware, but rather just poor coding and testing. 3.) The UI / controls are rough too, though tolerable. They won't prevent you from enjoying the game if you like the universe, but yeah.. The devs clearly lacked the time, experience, and/or concern to polish the experience of playing the game..4.) The combat system is serviceable. It is turn-based tactical and a super light version of what you'd find in the modern X-Com games or Age of Wonders: Planetfall.  5.) The game oozes atmosphere and that is its sole saving grace. The voice acting is fantastic, the setting spot on for Cthulhu lovers, and the art, soundtrack, and writing are all fantastic. I find myself essentially playing for the story, and I hope that the franchise can get the true digital incarnation it deserves, whether that be in following the LCG format or continuing with what has been established with Mother's Embrace.

_childDocuments_.review: To start of I preordered this game since I love the board games (both 1st and 2nd edition) so my impression is of someone who got it for 15 euros.The story of the game is pretty standard for a Lovecraft game. There are somethings that feels a bit original but not much. However the atmosphere is very nice. The voice acting are very varying with most of the characters being pretty horrendous and the rest decent. The controls are sadly bad but since its a turnbased game it is managable. The graphics are dated but that was to be expected, just look at the screenshots. The music was really good in my opinion, suited the game really well.After playing it through I can safely say that, except for achievements if you are into that, there is pretty much no replay value. Sure, you could play it through with a different starting character but all that changes are a couple of voicelines and storybeats in the beginning.Overall the game feels true to what its based on. I would like to see more content for it like the board game does, maybe with DLC cases. It felt a bit short but if compare to other prices in society at the moment I feel like I got 6-7 hours of fun for 15 euros which is roughly the same prices as going to a movie. Speaking for myself I dont regret buying it.Can I recommend it?If you like Lovecraft stories and want to sit through a couple of hours of interactive story. - Yes.If you are a diehard fan of the board game that wants a faithful representation of it. - No.If you are neither and is just looking for a decent video game of the genre. - Maybe, but there sure are a lot of better titles out there.As another reviewer here said, I would leave a neutral review on this if I could.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed reading Lovecraft and playing the Arkham Horror board games, so I was really excited when I first heard of the game's release. It was a real treat seeing the players of the game come to life! The story is much more different than anything I've read in Lovecraft or played in the board game, and I think that it's really neat that Asmodee puts their spin into the Lovecraft universe.The game itself: Some of the voice acting was a little limited and the game itself had a number of bugs, but none were completely game-breaking. I'm expecting a later patch to fix the bugs. The mechanics of the game were tricky at times and the game seems a little rough, so I can see how it will disappoint some fans. For $20 USD, the price is a little high for what we get, and I would like to see it go down a bit. Gameplay: Guns are by far the most useful items in the game, but the game still offers some versatility with spellcasting. In my play through the game, I relied on a strong spellcaster to deal spells and had everyone else with guns in their inventory. A few things that I had an issue with during the game: Inventory space is pretty limited, so you really have to make decisions on which to keep throughout each scenario and which ones to bring into each scenario. Before each scenario, you don't really know what to expect, so preparation is a little tricky. Sanity plays a really interesting mechanic since it deals trauma to the investigators once their sanity reaches zero, and large trauma can alter the outcome of each scenario. Some sanity loss is unavoidable since you wouldn't know which interaction causes sanity checks, so it does give some replay value in the game to see how trauma level affects the investigator's decision throughout the game.Once you finish the game, your 'continue' option is wiped, so replay means starting a new game. This is a little annoying since there is no way to go back to previously beaten scenarios and inventory will still be limited in the next playthrough.Overall, I was excited by playing Arkham Horror as a videogame and seeing the story unfold, and I recommend anyone to pick it up when the game goes down to a more suitable price.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna preface this review by mentioning that "Mansions of Madness," the Lovecraft-inspired tabletop horror game on which Mother's Embrace is based, is probably my favorite. I'm one of those weirdos who collects each expansion, and hand paints all the miniatures. I've had this particular title on my wish list since 2019, and pre-ordered it as soon as it became available. All this to say, I can comfortably claim that I am amongst this game's target demographic. I was delighted to revisit familiar characters and settings from the games I love so much. So perhaps I'm biased, but I feel as though there's plenty here to like. Game play is surprisingly similar to the app-assisted "Mansions," with turn-based combat, punishments from the "Mythos" events, and frequent (sometimes arbitrary) sanity checks. The tone, atmosphere, and lore are all very true to the source material. I also think there's decent variety from chapter to chapter. Some chapters are more combat-based, some contain puzzles, some require interviewing witnesses or gathering clues, and others require a reasonable amount of strategy. The continuous narration of Wilhelmina Tillinghast, the protagonists' mysterious acquaintance, is a nice touch. (The voice acting in general, in my humble opinion, is perfectly competent.)As for the game's weaknesses... There's no way around it. The game seems to have suffered from its troubled development, and I encountered some pretty gnarly bugs during my play through. Some were easy fixes, requiring no more than a reload from my last saved checkpoint. But one bug in particular was significant enough to block any sort of progression in the game, and required a full restart. (I was five chapters in at this point. It sucked.)The tank controls are decidedly clunky, and feel even more so when you're trying to navigate the occasional room with a fixed camera angle. I also had to run the graphics on the absolute lowest setting, because game play was too choppy otherwise. All in all, however, I enjoyed myself. I look forward to eventually playing through the game again with a different primary investigator, once it's patched up a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: For full disclosure, I have to confess that I haven't played Arkham Horror the board game so this review is from the perspective of the computer game itself. Having said that, I have played Mansions of Madness and other board games in this genre and I've very familiar with the Lovecraftian universe too.On the whole this game is pretty good, but hopefully the sequels will be even better as it goes along. The premise of the game is simple - you take investigators to various sites to collect items, solve puzzles and defeat enemies. The story is interesting and the locations and variety of enemies is fine. The combat is turn based which works quite well, and the limiting inventory space and the number of investigators also works well.It does, however, get quite formulaic after a while. Turn based combat with a limit to the number of movement points means that you largely use the same tactics again and again. Also, by the end of the game I found that it was actually easier to kill enemies which were supposedly harder than those which were supposedly easier. Also, the characters don't seem to quite work for me. At least one of them you start with has significantly lower mental stats than others and then many seem to be much-of-a-muchness so there isn't quite the jeopardy there, and nor is there the co-operative play which makes the board games so interesting.I did like the feature of being able to vary my investigators from time to time as by leaving them behind for one mission they can get better health. Also it's possible there will be slightly greater variety if I choose a different starting investigator. However, the game could really have done with some sort of skill tree which would allow you to variegate your investigators further, and really build up your team so you felt you were progressing.On the whole it's a nice start but hopefully there will be further episodes with better features for greater challenge and replayability.
