_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game. I really, really want to. I completed it tonight. I saved the last level thinking it would be a good, long battle that would make all the slower stuff worth it. I was done in 15 minutes or less. So why a thumbs up?I'll start in the beginning. Be warned, this WILL HAVE SPOILERS.You begin the game with many choices of characters.  I chose the trumpet playing, Jim Culver. I liked his back story and thought that perhaps, since he had 75% Mental Resistance and was Moral Support with a trumpet icon beside his information, that perhaps he would be of great use in helping the mental stability of the group. Perhaps even that music in some form would be a boost of some sort, which doesn't exist. I didn't find that it to really be the case that any of that helped so in all honesty, just choose your investigator based on Combat and which ever one you think you can stomach listening to throughout the game. (Sorry, Jenny Barnes attitude makes me want to see what happens when the character loses repeatedly.) Backstory is nice but useless as they will only once, in the beginning, remark about their life to my knowledge. As Jim, you are requested to play music for Professor Tillinghast, Professor of Astronomy, so you are at her home wondering around her yard.  The door is locked. So you, as a good hearted, concerned, musically talented individual in the late 1920s, decide to smash the crap out of her window and crawl in, sift through her belongings and try to figure out where in the house this woman has gotten off to ... when you hear a scream and go upstairs  ... again, as someone who has just smashed their way into her home. Not a spoiler, the point of the game is she's dead and you, as a trumpet player, are now an investigator.I'm going to throw the pause button in here just to say that at this point, Prof Tillinghast is already speaking to your character as if they can hear her. However it is only you, the player, that can hear her speaking.  Now, as far as the vocal actors/actresses go most of them do fantastically at drawing you into the story. Some will say random weird things and you'll think "wait, what?" and move on. Within the first 10 minutes of the game I wanted to find Tillinghast to see if it was out of the realm of possibility to shut her the flip up. Being a southern gal, myself, and having lived around a great many older folk I can say with certainty her accent and "elderly voice" was an abomination. It was like being promised sweet tea and someone hands you a pop top Nestea. Wha ... Why ... I really saw no point at all in the ravings of Tillinghast in every single scene. I think only letting her speak when necessary to further the game would have actually immersed you, as the player, far more than her saying something and me yelling, "Girl ain't you dead?! STFU."And so the mystery begins.Gameplay :- The good news -- There are many levels that are fully walkable areas. -- There are SO MANY things to click on. There is never a room with absolutely nothing in it.-- You are joined by some really interesting characters that not only finish the level with you but are selectable characters for later missions.-- Some of the stories and explanations in the game are excellent and worth the read as you may find clues to puzzles.-- Mythos clock and lore are really good.-- Birthing Melee are in my opinion the best enemy because one shot takes them down and whatever is around them so if you can manage to hit them once they help you with some of the other enemies.- The bad news-- Every door has to be clicked at least twice to get through the first time. (Once actually opened you can just walk through them)-- Some of the dots for doors and item areas don't work the first click, or second.-- Some areas when you click the dots you end up just wondering around.-- At least once in a level but sometimes many times, you will click an item to have it attack your sanity or boost it. I'm leaving it in the bad news category because looking at a painting should not boost your sanity and reading a book should not attack your sanity.-- Sometimes you or the other characters get stuck in the corner somewhere on invisible walls and just when you think there's no way out you can click a dot and magically walk to where ever in the room that is as if nothing ever happened.-- On one occasion I had a very interesting professor join us and about half way through the game in the character select screen she was no longer there and a totally and completely different person had appeared in her place that we'd never met, seen or interacted with.-- Walking into some rooms or areas hit your sanity. Why? We're not paranormal investigators, mediums or anything so to have it hit your sanity just because you entered a hallway that had something hidden in a drawer is totally ridiculous.-- Some of the stories with clues to puzzles actually give you 6-7 clues to things that are for a puzzle that only requires you to figure out the first 3 and the rest is a waste of player time (moreso if you click something that hits your sanity when you could have solved the puzzle already.)-- When you click an object like a dresser, you receive 1-3 items that are good to have but you also lose 1 sanity. No idea why, you just do. -- Mythos clock sometimes sort of goes up but doesn't really. It makes the noise like it is but nothing has changed. Again, you take hits for random things to your sanity but nothing really brings that back down. Once you fill it up you get traumatized and you can't lose that unless you sit out a round. You can only bring it down with a Pocket Watch and I only found 3 in the game. (16 or so hours of gameplay)-- On certain items you are given a choice. Depending on your player's Investigation skill (search, manual, physical, etc) you may get a hint on which of the 2-3 choices will open a drawer or whatever. You have no idea which one is intended and you just random pick one because the choices are too similar. In two different areas they failed to put the full description in so you only see the name tag. That, I will put in bugs.-- I felt like the Notebook was useless. Never used it.Bugs :You'd expect this to have actually been a game that was Early Access while they worked out the bugs. - Point of contact dots are not very ... intuitive. You can click them and end up walking around them but not actually opening things or going out of the door.- After each level Prof Tillinghast has to go into her thoughts on why you should just do what she tells you. Every single one is cut off in the beginning and you are started 1/2 way through a word. Sometimes the audio is louder than the rest of the game when she's reading as well. Again you could cut all that out and just let us read it.- I caught at least two bugs that were graphical errors:---Piano at the Herd of Algedi says "A Piano objectInteraction/s3_piano_description" and you can choose Touch or Find Flaws. The Tip was No advice.---Boiler Room in the Asylum says "A Pile of Coal objectInteraction/s2B_coal_reach_description" and you can choose Pull or Stretch. Luckily I did have someone with Manual at this time and the Tip was It's just out of reach so I wasn't punished for a wrong answer.- In the Herd of Algedi there is a secret entry way that you can walk against and go through to the Attic. The items trigger, the fight and the exit do NOT and you have to reset the entire level.Hiring a team of 2-5 people to give the game a run through a few times with each character would have revealed all these bugs and they could have been fixed before release. I know, it's what I do. Or at least release as a work in progress. So why did I still give it a thumbs up with such a bad review? All in all, bugs and bs aside, it was really good. Mystery, murder, magic. The ending wasn't great, at all, but I may still play again. Get it on sale. Not worth $20.

_childDocuments_.review: So much of this game is shallow, incomplete, and buggy. It feels rushed, and lacking in polish or direction. The story is nothing new from the series and has no replay value. every choice is illusory and has zero impact on the game. The gamplay experience can be summed up like this. Walk up to something, press the interact button, read some text, repeat. Combat is somehow even more dull, and grows tiring before you're even finished with the second mission. all the enemies do is either walk and attack, just attack, or heal. That's it. Player options in combat are equally as dull.You have practically zero inventory space if you want to carry items with you, and the UI on PC is so clunky, that managing your inventory is the true nightmare in this game.  The color palette is nice and the game sounds decent, but the character models are dated, stiff, and cringey at times. The game also runs very poorly on PC, locking at 30fps causing tearing.The best parts of the game are the cutscenes that use the IP's original art assets, and it really makes you wonder what could have been had they decided to take a different approach. If you like H.P. Lovecraft, or the Arkham Horror Files, I implore you to spend your money elsewhere. This game is a stain on the franchise (along with final hour).

_childDocuments_.review: It was a interesting experience for me. Overall I give this game a 6.5 out of 10. Here is my reasoning why:Pro's  Neat story with a small plot twist that although obvious was also interesting. Lot of character variety to choose fromMusic is A+combat kept me glued and focused despite some repetition in how it was done. Now for the Mas o Menos or take it or leave it:Graphics are ok. Neither excellent, or horrible. Voice acting was fine. Now for the Con'sWaaaaaaaaay too short. I completed the game in 8 hours despite only having one game over. I don't think it is worth the price tag for the length. Now I would change my mind on this if they release DLC with new missions/stories. But if they are charging a motherload for said DLC I probably won't buy it. 5 bucks would be my max as the game was more expensive to begin with. Enemy variety is meh. It always drives me nuts when the same enemies keep appearing. Now in the context of the story this makes sense and with the length of the game as it is this isn't a huge problem. But if future DLC's use the same enemy models I would be very disgruntled.Camera is poor. Could have been better.Map is garbage. I couldn't really rely on the map except for determining where the exits were.The selector for healing a character could be more clear. There were a few times when I selected the wrong character and used the last of my bandages to heal.......Overall like I said, I give this game a 6.5 out of 10. By biggest take away's are the story was well done despite the shortness, and it drove me to finish the game. But unless they give us more stories and missions, I'm probably won't revisit this game. Keep in mind I love the Arkham Horror universe that FFG has come up with and was the driving force for me to pick up this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun little game. Not outstanding, but crafted with love. I recommend it to fans of the Cthulhu mythos who value story and athmosphere more than gameplay. The game is separated in scenarios, allowing for short play sessions. The exploration and combat are fun, but a bit simple and sometimes clunky. I am not familiar with the original board game, but it does feel like playing one of those rather than a video game.The graphics don't have the level of details we're used to nowadays. Nevertheless, I find them quite pleasant with a good art style. The locations are immersive and there are some interesting creature designs. It is more cartoonish and less dreary than other titles like Call of Cthulhu or Sinking City. Your investigation take you to a university, a dark asylum or a sunny New Orlean street. I felt like I was uncovering cosmic perils hidden below our mundane universe. The game is short (about 10h for me), but that's a decent length for this kind of game. The story is satisfying and well paced for the most part, although it ends a bit too abruptly with a very short final scenario. There's definitely some place for a DLC, hopefully.

_childDocuments_.review: Might come back and write a longer version of this review later but I just wanna say my quick thoughts now. It's not the game that I wanted, a lot of folks I think as well wanted basically Mansions of Madness in a video game. The old video preview for this game had talk about procedural generated mansions for re-playablity, and mentioned how that game was their inspiration. I'm certain that the folding of fantasy flight interactive caused this games radical transformation, although I haven't looked into it much. That said the game that we got....Is kinda good actually, it's not amazing but its basically Arkham Xcom lite. Fantasy Flight's Arkham flies franchise, is a love of mine it was actually my into to Lovecraft and I am sucker for the kinda pulpy gamified version of the mythos that it presents. I know all these investigators from my hours in the table top entries so it was very fun for me to have these characters in a video game. If you aren't already a fan of any Arkham file games then i would l say you might not enjoy the minimalism used in this game, and even I have to admit that the lack of variety in animations does make the game look kinda cheap. (All items are used in a weird 'video gamey' animation that always looks silly but works for gameplay) also the voice acting often feels 'first take' still none of this really distracts from the fun kinda campy story that feels very much like the thing other Arkham file games would do.Game play wise, this game is a mix of exploration and combat. The exploration has you walking around and interacting with icons that sometimes offer a choice. These "complex" interactions have similar sounding options often enough but you have to read carefully inorder to figure out which to use. Wrong answers advance the mythos clock which triggers effects when full. I like this system well enough especially since complex interactions have an associated skill which if your party has that skill will tell you what choice to make, however sometimes it did feel like the hint was too vague and that is frustrating. You also collect items to use in combat, inventory management is kinda important in this game or at least deciding what is important enough to make it into your precious few slots. Every weapon in the game will break over uses, which I dont really like in games but in this game it's kinda part of the challenge and I do think they give out the right items, you just dont always have room for them.Combat is like a xcom lit game with action points and overwatch, it seems pretty simple and easy but as the game goes on the fights get kinda hard, combined with the inventory system and I found by mission five it was becoming a real game. Magic is really good in this game which does feel odd for Lovecraft AND for Arkham file this is BY FAR the most powerful magic has ever been. It basically always does what you want and then 50% of the time ALSO does some other effect, half of the time just doing extra damage to a enemy or healing your teammate. Of course the time you except that extra damage it suddenly blinds your guy on over watch, but I still found myself SUPER EAGER to cast magic all the time. Not sure if that'sa good or a bad but certainly different. Also I found the controls a little finicky like it was needlessly hard to get the right consumable selected in battle using controller. Over all again I REALLY wanted and still want a MoM game but this game is a fun entry into the Arkham Horror franchise, I wish the story was less linear, I wish it was the board game, I wish it was multiplayer, but really for what it is and how it came to be, it's a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game campaign.I appreciated the courage of the developers, who did not limit themselves to transpose into digital format the board games from which this game is taken, but tried to create a mixture of point and click adventure, survival horror and tactical turn-based combat with customizable party.Unfortunately, the final product does not live up to the ambitions.None of the game mechanics is in fact sufficiently developed, with the result that the combat and survival are too easy, the customization is quite shallow and the point and click component is marred by a mechanism of almost totally random choices.A pity, because some things like the management of detectives and equipment could have worked very well with a little more care, because some of the puzzles are interesting and well structured, and because the graphics, although not up to a title double A, does his honest job.As it is, it is a game that I would only recommend to die-hard fans of board games related, and even to them I recommend buying it on sale because the duration of the campaign is quite low.I personally hope for future expansions and perhaps a robust overhaul of the game system.

_childDocuments_.review: I think many here went into this game with the wrong idea of what it actually is.This is a pretty well made translation of a Mansions of Madness boardgame campaign and it translates the mechanics of that game into a videogame: Find clues, fight simple turn based fights against monsters and the like and discover the mistery. I like the quirky characters that fit well with the board game and I've read that the Mmap tiles are randomly thrown together with each playthrough...which could increase the replay value, though I doubt that anyone would play this game twice as the story and the basics stay the same.For that and the 15€ I got it for as a pre-order, it's pretty good. There is just some little thing that didn't translate well: In the board game the players gather clues but with every turn there is a clock ticking in the background that makes the game harder, so you should think before running through every location and finding every clue. The videogame has that clock in the form of a mistake-wheel. You could investigate something and if you make a mistake, the clock ticks once. Unfortunately (and I believe this is what many criticize) this aspect is rather pointless. Either you have a character in your party that can give you a "hint" which is to say exactly what to do, or you don't, in which case you can only try and probably fail and advance the mystery clock. This would still be cool if it wasn't a choice between "patting down" a body, "taking a look at" a body or "examining" a body. This needs a rework, though I doubt that it will be changed.Also from the trailer I got the impression it would be something of a squad-based RPG, but considering the price this would have been absurd.Anyways, if you like quirky lovecraftian horror, somewhat of the humor from DoS mixed within and the sort of videogame-like board games, Arkham Horror, is a good pick.

_childDocuments_.review: i was one of the most exited for this game, had on wishlist since 2018.  the game company has other board game titles like gloomhaven, which i own and like.  i was exited for this one,  a lovecraftian theme paired with the solid game mechanics of one of the many tried and true board games that lovecraftian themes have successfully been attached too.  which one they attached it too honestly i could have cared less.  thats what this game was, when it was a project of lucky hammers, but what they did when that fell apart is create a one time played shell of a game.  its not a board game with a video game skin. its a play through of a short story, with the lovecraftian board game LOOK, but no replayability. no actual,, "game".  it was cheap, so i could care less about the money, or the graphics not getting any love.  i feel like a dissapointed parent, i just feel disappointment.  you had me in your grips,, making a narrative video game of a lovecraft boardgame that you can challenge yourself with when you get bored.  this is just what little you had the right to use of a failed project made into a game that looks like a boardgame.  woohoo.    i dont want my money back.. i just want you to go to your room and realize what youve done.and for anyone who says this is a cute adaption of a lovecraft boardgame, or that it "lacks polish".  your forgetting your dont play a board game once and then throw it away. its not at all about it lacking polish.and thinking about it more clearly, what i was expecting was an animated version of something like elder sign video game adaption,  an actual game.  you pick it up, play some rounds, get killed by some specific chaos god, or triumph.  the animation in that game was horrible, but it didnt matter because you were playing an actual game.  here they had the opportunity to make an animated version of such a game.  its just, why,,,?  why would you,,  just go to your room.

_childDocuments_.review: First know that you might get at top 30 min  of gameplay for each € spent when you buy it for 20 bucks. This is not a very long game. I finished it in about 10 hours. In the beginning the controls drove me crazy, but you get used to it after a while. Still I must say it feels like the development team thought: "We are game designers, ha!", but ignored that boardgame design and  videogame design differ... (No game designer in her/his right mind would map sprinting to the spacebar, while Shift opens some menu ... O_O!But, all in all, I enjoyed playing this game. To me it felt less like playing the boardgame version of Arkham Horror, but Mansions of Madness. It was nice to see the characters come to life. A lot of love went into their models... I also liked the atmosphere and the vibes of the environment you get to explore. It felt very true to the setting and made me long for a real round of MoM with my friends. The story is nice... nothing to deep, but with an OK twist. The choice of the great old one and her abominations payed off and kept me wanting  to see more. All in all: Do not expect an action game. Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace gameplay is slow paced. Interaction with the surroundings are limited. That is what makes it feel more like a boardgame,.... but if you are into that, grab it (best on the next sale if you are into a good price-performance ratio)! If you want an open world to explore and more agility, check out other Cthulhu inspired titles. I liked this game, but it can not compete with a Call of Cthulhu or - in a more similar genre - a gem like Stygian: Reign of the Old Ones (which is a bit buggy and sadly "unfinished", but delivers in it's own ways...

_childDocuments_.review: After playing throughout half the game, I can fully say I am enjoying this game. I don't usually play single-player games but Call of Cthulhu and Arkham Horror has always been an interest and hobby to me. Now I'm not saying this is a must buy, but for $20 this is a nice game to sit through and play, the clock and limited resources will make this game somewhat challenging and no easy feat but still enjoyable to run around on. One major problem I had was with the controls but after a while I got used to it, just move around with WASD and turn camera and select actions with right click. And I wish you could zoom out a bit more but it's whatever, moving items is as simple as dragging it into a slot and pressing an ok button. The graphics are a bit cartoonish besides environment but at least it is well designed and is consistent. The voice acting could be better on some characters but each scenario can be voiced by every investigator you bring into a mission. Combat is pretty simple, each character has 4 combat stats: Initiative, Melee, Ranged, and Magic. And each stat is either weak, average, or strong, which determines how much action points you use for that certain action. Now we get into story actions, the game is linear, with limited exploration where you can find a few side missions and some extra goods but spamming the wrong answers and not listening to clues will certainly be your downfall. The more actions you get wrong, the more problems will stack such as less movement or sanity checks. The story so far is pretty simple with the whole stopping an occult but so far it is enjoyable with your standard characters you'd find in one of your CoC campaigns. If you like a small story with some character/supply management based on eldritch horror and don't mind some of the voice acting I certainly think that $20 for this isn't bad, but if you are worried you could always watch a play through or wait for a sale. For now I will play more of it and I think people are blowing how bad this games is out of proportion just because it isn't like playing the tabletop version.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I begin its worthwhile to set context about this review. I'm a massive fan of Fantasy Flight Games' Arkham boardgame franchise, so this is very much from the perspective of a fan with preconceived expectations. For those of you familiar with those boardgames, this is based off of Mansions Of Madness rather than any of the Arkham Horror games. The game was originally titled after Mansions, but was changed during development to be in line with their current line-up of Arkham games (as Mansions Of Madness appears to have ended). I will also say to my fellow tabletop gamers, that seeing characters we have interacted with on the tabletop for years now, come alive on my screen was a joy in and of itself.Onto the game itself. This game's premise is you are completing a series of investigative scenarios, which compromise two forms of play, clue-gathering and turn-based combat. Clue gathering works in a similar way to how Telltale's Walking Dead games and other narrative based games operate. A series of icons will indicate where to explore. Most clues will have multiple ways to interact with them, one of which is the right way, the other having negative repercussions on your team of investigators. Investigators in your party sometimes provide hints on which is the best outcome. Movement in these sections can be a little tanky without significant camera control, but gives it a old-school Resident Evil vibe. Turn-based combat operates like XCOM-light and similar titles in that genre. Your Investigators can attack, trade, overwatch etc. This game can surprisingly be played with your keyboard alone, which was my optimum way to play. Something about the games design felt like it should have click-to-move, alas WSAD is the method here. Those unfamiliar with the board game may find the sanity system a little unfair - lots of ways to loose sanity but little way to regain it. Each non-tutorial scenario can take around 1-2 hours to complete, of which I believe there are 5. So definitely a 5-8 hours of play time (seems im about half way currently). Given the narrative nature of the game, there is little replayability - but the budget price point of entry factors into this. One issue I have is some of the dialogue choices. There's a narrator character who's dialogue sounds like she's talking to the characters, when they're infact talking to you the-player, but im not sure if she's intended to be talking to the-player? Other times characters will just repeat information you've just read in a diary entry etc. At least said-dialogue is well delivered by the voice cast!To cap off, those with a background in Arkham/Mansions should definitely give this a try. Those who don't, given the budget price i totally think its worth a shot if you like narrative based games and or lightweight tactical combat.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one to rate. Really.First of all: Look at my playtime. I finished the game. Let that speak for itself. And its not probable that I will play the game again just to check the voicelines of different lead investigators, since the whole game is quite linear.Ok, with that out of the way: I got the game on a whim, because I like the boardgame and wanted to see what the fuss is about. There are a lot of negative reviews, so I was hesitant, but in the end my positive experiences with the boardgame won me over.During the first few chapters though, I didnt regret it!No, really, the game got me curious from the first chapter and I was actualy quite hyped during chapters 2-4.While the graphic isnt AAA-worthy, it is "solid". Perhaps I am lenient though, because I was born in a time where the graphics were a lot worse and Im fine with overlooking graphical issues if the gamedesign is interesting.If you can stomach the cruder aspects of the graphics, it is actualy quite nice in the finer details, like the environments. Also I enjoyed the voice acting a lot (english language). Perhaps its because Im no native speaker, but I would actualy rate the voice acting especialy high. From my point of view the overall presentation managed to bring the world and the characters of the board game to live quite well, and I think thats one of the strongest aspects, if you are a fan.The story is overall quite well made too. It is nothing surprising and I found many story developments quite predictable ... BUT the game kept it interesting and atmospheric.The ironic thing is, that the "flaws" which are commonly critizised in the boards (and some reviews) are aspects of the game which I actualy like and rate positivly.First of all: collecting clues is mostly about guessing games. For example: You get a description of a container. Will you force it open, break the lock or lockpick? Take the wrong choice and you are slightly penalized. The only clue you have is a short description of said container. Some people consider those guessing games too arbitrary. I, on the other hand, like thinking about them and consider "alright, if they arent arbitrary, why did the devs decide for this choice as correct choice" if I go wrong. I think you CAN actualy figure out a lot of the correct choices by pondering the situation, the text of the object and sometimes the look of the object. Maybe Im "convincing myself" like someone said in the boards. But honestly: All that guesswork about the "why" of the correct answers was one of the most amusing aspects the whole game experience gave me. And I daresay it was quite a thing befitting to the investigative theme of the series. So I would actualy rate it as strength of the game and positive individual style which is a lot different to what you usualy get in games.Then we got the tactical battles and four other things which I found to be rated negativly quite often in the discussions: Mythos Wheel, Stress/Mind-Checks, Weapon Durability and a very constrained inventory.The Mythos Wheel is a stress-mechanic, which penalizes you for "bad" choices in the guessing games or prolonged fights. Basicaly its a counter, and if you get too many counts, you get a negative random effect impacting you for the chapter (or just one fight).You get the usual mind-checks whenever you see something (arguably) scary during the investigation scenes or if you fight. Aparently some people think fighting crazed cultists who want to stab you to death shouldn't test your psyche. Honestly: I think otherwise and dont mind that you also have those checks against human opponents. If you lose too much sanity, you wont die in this game. Instead you get a Trauma which is another penalty for your investigators. Each Investigator has 3 possible Traumas he can get. You can heal them by not taking that Investigator to a chapter (you will get more than enough investigators to alternate them), but the next time you get that Trauma it will be worse, even if it was healed for a time.Then you got weapon breaking. Dont know what else to say to it. Your weapons break, no matter if melee weapon, ranged weapon or spellbook. Is it realistic? Dunno, in all honesty I dont wanna go down that lane for a game like this. It does force you to alternate your weapons. Well... in theory.Then we got a limited inventory which could make you consider hard which items to take and to give to which character.Honestly: I LIKE all of those design choices, because they add the premise for some sort of challenge and unusual decision making in an unique style.However, my grief about this is: The game couldn't really deliver on its own game design premise!It has all those mechanics which I really liked on the get-go. It has a semi-interesting story and good atmosphere ... but in the later chapters it loses a lot of breath.In the first few chapters I saw those mechanics, saw interesting weapon choices with interesting modifiers, spellbooks which can wildcast, a weapon that might make you insane, etc and I thought "cool, Im so curious what else they will think of", but ... there wasnt much more. No, seriously, the game starts to repeat on the items you can find VERY soon. Same is true for the enemies. At first I thought the fights of the early chapters were just the warmup ... well, there wasnt much difference for most of the game and you had a few humans and monsters you encountered over and over again.It got a weapon break mechanic, but really: Weapons take AGES to break. I really had to make an effort to break some of them, and then you get so many new weapons and stuff anyways that you will always have something to replace them with. Especialy the last few chapters are extremly ridiculous in that regard.And the sanity/trauma penalities also never managed to hit me notably hard. It was more of an interesting side-thing in my experience.I think its one of those messes where the developers have great ideas, start focusing on them and realizing them, and then publishers or other important persons decide "nono, thats too hard/much. Keep it simple! Oh, and also the game has to be finished the day before yesterday.". The funny thing about it is, how many people still complain about those game mechanics, while people like me, which did appreciate them, will probably be disappointed by the wasted potential and the lack of content to build on those good roots that are there.But of course I am only speculating here.Anyhow. Im sill giving a thumbs up? Yes, but ONLY because there is no neutral-vote in Steam. Get the game if you like the franchise and the world and would enjoy a well crafted story in it, but be aware of the above points when you do, lest you be disappointed later on.

_childDocuments_.review: I had fun with it but it's a bit on the short side and simplistic. It kind of reminds of me if someone was doing a proof of concept for the game World of Horror or something. Where's there's a smattering of light elements from the Mansions of Madness board game, adventure games, Xcom styled turn based combat. None of it very deep.That said there were a few times I had to actually pay attention to what I was reading to solve the clues so it's not completely mindless.And if you're familiar to the Arkham board games in general. It's fun to actually see voiced (in some cases bad VO) of these consistent characters through those games.There were some bugs in my playthrough like missing descriptions but nothing gamebreaking. I also enjoyed the sort of cartoon graphics they were going for and overall the first playthrough even taking my time took about 6.5 hours. _childDocuments_.review: First things first - this game does not have features and graphics that modern gamers might have become used to and expect to see.  It is on rails somewhat and the graphics are certainly a bit cartoonish.  I also find that the various characters on offer seem to be too similar - they can all shoot guns and they can all cast spells for example...That said, after a few hours of playing, I am finding myself increasingly drawn into the tale.  A cast of familiar characters (from Fantasy Flight Games' excellent back catalogue of board games) must face down an unspeakable horror and it all seems to roll along quite nicely.  The themes are presented well, with a user friendly interface and there's very little time required to get to grips with how the game works.  The unsettling nature of the unfolding adventure is revealed bit by bit and we see our characters melt down under the weight of their various manias and insanity as they plot their course.  Excellent Lovecraftian fare.  I think I will enjoy seeing this one through.Update - After 4 hours play, I met my first bug.  The game froze up during combat.  Hopefully, the devs will get on this quick and fix it, as it is a shame to have to resort to last save position when you were otherwise doing well.  On the plus side, the third scenario is less 'on rails' and the investigators are left to figure out their own way through the chaos.  Still enjoying my play through though.  The story seems to be good and engaging and has me returning each day to play a little more.Finished the game.  Pretty solid in the main but with a few glitches - none of them game breaking.  The combat freeze bug happened again in the last battle, but it was easy enough to quit and reload - just a shame really.  Hopefully, the devs jump in and fix that.The turned based combat is quite engaging and requires tactical use of weapons, spells and action points to maximise chances of surviving.A thumbs up from me, but with a few caveats.

_childDocuments_.review: Reviewed after binge playing this on my Switch and going through the first three scenarios on PC.Likes:- Great atmosphere and music that captures the Lovecraftian mythos.- Interesting premise for the story that keeps you guessing almost until the end.- Strategic depth in the combat that relies on clever positioning and efficient use of items.- A diverse cast of characters that offers multiple gameplay options.Dislikes:- The environment design leaves a lot to be desired. Framerate capped at 30fps on the PC version, washed out textures on the Switch version.- Some of the voice lines are delivered in a stiff and dry manner breaking the immersion.- Throughout the game it is unclear what events can trigger sanity checks and which cannot. Why is an investigator's sanity tested when they read about everyday mishaps on a newspaper, but a dissected monster carcass does not make them flinch?Thoughts:For the price of 15 euros, you are not going to find Hollow Knight levels of quality from this indie studio. However, the game is overall a solid foundation for a sequel that can better reflect the ambitions of the development team. Well worth the price tag for fans of Lovecraft and early adopters of this adventure series.

_childDocuments_.review: I am  really enjoying this game! It's really neat seeing all the characters from the Arkham Horror franchise!The combat is quite good, I really like how you can undo movement, which I think should be a staple in Tactical RPGs. The game is also very smooth(Plays incredible on a controller) and I like the style. The voice acting is fantastic and even though they don't have mo-capped faces, it doesn't really matter because a character's face is never zoomed in upon.  The levels' set pieces are quite detailed and fun to explore. I think they did a really good job adapting the mechanics of the board games while still giving the game a unique feel. The story is also well written and interesting!I really hope they continue with more content for this game!

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think they bothered to test this game during development. Your character often gets stuck behind a person / desk / object, and there's no way to get unstuck without reverting to a previous checkpoint.Hopefully they'll patch it, but there's so many other issues with this game.- Graphics glitches.- Horrible UI choices.- Tedious movement mechanics and an ineffectual run button.Then the game play itself seems to suffer from some very not-fun mechanics. Constant penalties for no reason.I went in willing to overlook a lot of glitches to have a fun adventure and story... but this game is just tedious to play.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of the boardgame. I've played every edition, even the old first edition at Necronomicon in 2019. I love the setting.Not loving this game. I must just have the worst RNG because I failed every sanity "check". Ok, fine it's supposed to be punishing. whatever. The experience of it isn't rewarding, though. Then there's the actions choices out of combat. If you guess wrong, you advance the mythos. This would be fine, however sometimes the "right option" makes no sense: none of my characters have lockpicking, so why would they try to pick a lock? And why is it the fast action to pick *that* lock, but not the box where you find something by... "shaking it"?I'm just not into it. I'm unlikely to pick this up again even though it's only been like an hour? of actual play. meh.Also just FYI because it was really alarming to hear, Gew-Gaws is pronounced with hard Gs, as in Good, not soft Gs as in Giraffe. hearing "Jew-Jaws" was... something else.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the boardgame, you'll love this game, especially if you couldn't afford the board game (a la moi). CONS: - Right now, Sanity debuffs are CRAZY common. I didn't play the boardgame enough to know if this is true to the heart of the game, but right now I'm just used to the idea that my entire party of 3 investigators will end a scenario completely topped off on Loony tokens.  - More than a few times the game has locked up during combat, specifically when the Great Big Scary Timer goes down and one of my investigators gain a mythos effect. I've restarted to checkpoint to solve this issue of no buttons responding during combat that is the result to this bug. PROS: + The story, Voice Acting, and Action Scenes are wonderfully amazing to experience. I'm invested in the characters and the story from the start, so it makes up for some of the bugs. This should count as multiple pros, because it keeps me from getting too frustrated when having to reload checkpoints. It's so close to the board-game that I remember that maybe I'm desperate, but depending on how the deveolpers care for this puppy in the upcoming weeks will let me know.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay is pretty fun so far, combat reminds me of Shadowrun/fallout 1/2 though much faster paced, the story is entertaining and I'm genuinely enjoying the characters and their interactions with one another, I've encountered no bugs so far and the game has been pretty solid. If you like Lovecraft and video games chances are you'll find something to enjoy in this game and consider the price of entry being so low there's really not much of a reason to not get it.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review: Investigation is about going around the level clicking on highlighted stuff and if the characters you are using have the right skills it will let you know the best course of action. Combat plays like xcom lite. After every round of combat or every wrong investigation choice the mythos clock goes up and that effects your sanity. Loosing sanity sets off a trauma that is basically a debuf. Sound is alright, graphics are functional, so very surprised at a 30fps lock. It is not the Arkham Horror/ Mansions of Madness game we were wanting/demanding but at the low price there is a story to go through with very little replay. So in short there is fun to be had but most people will not like how it's been done and will probably get fed up and frustrated before the end... Heavy fans of the FF games check it out for yourselves everyone else who knows nothing of the FF/Lovecraft universe look elsewhere this game is not for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Arkham Horror: Mother's Embrace

_childDocuments_.review:
The year is 1926: a professor of astronomy is found dead in her mansion and everything indicates that she has been the victim of a heinous murder. Choose from 12 intrepid investigators from the Arkham Horror games, each with a unique set of skills, and assemble your team to shed the light over this mysterious death.

Find clues, perform interrogations and progress through nine chapters as the story unfolds. Your investigation will take you to visit shadowed institutions and mysterious locales, ranging from Miskatonic University, the Arkham Asylum, and the bayous of Louisiana. 

As you face off against Lovecraftian horrors, your investigators will descend deeper into the depths of madness, affecting their level of sanity and causing traumas that will impact the course of your investigation. Care about your sanity and make the right choices the Ancient Ones are preparing their return.

name: Spacebase Startopia
detailed_description: Feature List The 10-mission, fully dubbed single-player Campaign will require all your skills as Commander of the Spacebase Startopia as you strive to create one of the most attractive trade and tourism destinations in the known universe. Each of the three Decks will require your leadership skills, with the Sub Deck containing all of the Rooms vital to survival, while the Fun Deck focuses on your visitors and the flora and fauna found on the Bio Deck provides sufficient Resources for survival as well as a home to the graceful Dryads. Prevail against your competitors, for you are not alone on the Space Station. Sabotage your opponents' economy or attack them with your Mech Units, conduct trade and beware of Space Pirates eager to board your Station. The dynamic narrator AI “VAL” reacts to your decisions and is always at your side in both word and deed – and the occasional extremely unqualified comment. In addition to the extensive single player Campaign, an individually configurable sandbox mode as well as both a competitive and a cooperative multiplayer mode for up to four players awaits you. EXTENDED EDITION BONUS CONTENT EXTENDED EDITION contains the following extras: Spacebase Startopia Original Soundtrack Special Dungeon Lord alien hat Decorative statues for the 8 alien races Skins for the Fuzzy droids and Garbage Bots About the Game 'Help, we're all going to d... Wha... Oh, excuse me, it seems my system is no longer up-to-date – [old memory status deleted] – so, much better… WELCOME to the Spacebase Startopia ! I'm VAL, your helpful and efficient Space Station AI! According to my records, this Station hasn’t been used at all in the last 17 years! How very strange. Furthermore, it would appear that you are the only rational life form in this Sector. Well then, CONGRATULATIONS! I hereby officially pronounce you Commander of this Space Station! Hopefully you will enjoy more success than your predecessor who, according to the logbook, er… ran into some wormlike Aliens… Oh, nothing to worry about! To keep the same thing from happening to you, there's a lot you're going to have to do. Amongst others, there’s the development of further Sectors, maintenance of the three vital Main Decks as well as the customer acquisition and entertainment of our extraterrestrial visitors, who provide us with sufficient Energy for our plans for global improvement. Oh, and before I forget – it's probably just a bug in my security protocols anyway – but my sensors are showing just loads of enemy creatures in all of the other Sectors… So, what are we waiting for? Let's get to work! Let us join forces to conquer space.' Spacebase Startopia captivates with its original mixture of economic simulation and empire building strategy paired with classic RTS skirmishes and a good dose of humor. In addition to the challenging single player Campaign and the versatile battle mode, there are also competitive and cooperative multiplayer modes for up to four players. And as if maintaining the three Space Station Decks, entertaining the eight Alien races and defending against enemy invaders were not enough of a challenge, the dynamic narrator AI is not going to mince matters and commentates the events in a lovely but sharp-tongued manner.

_childDocuments_.review: Those five words are months and countless hours in the making. Testing the early access version, spending hours crafting feedback and having it all ignored by developers who apparently refused to listen to the many, many gamers who provided the identical, consistent feedback across all the forums.The developers and publishers do not deserve your money. And you deserve to spend your time on something that will actually bring you joy. Listen to the reviews and walk away - for this price you could buy a dozen books, a lot of ice cream, a Triple A title or a bunch of indie ones. None of those things will disappoint you like Spacebase Startopia, Realmforge Studios and Kalypso Media have today.I can't criticise the voice-acting because it's apparent there is none. For some strange reason they decided to use an actual fake voice that is worse than Google Translate, Siri or any other option on the market. You can tell because in a bunch of lines it actually misses the punctuation, making sentences run into each other. So the jokes don't land at all - not that they would, because it's actually just a collection of insults and put-downs.I cannot emphasise enough how bad the voice is. And they clearly didn't care enough about this aspect, because the 'dialogue' is highly repetitive. So over a one hour period of building your base you'll constantly hear the same badly-delivered put downs and insults.Sadly the developers were told this was a problem for months and they ignored it. The only solution they came up with was a button to turn the voice over off. That'd be like people spending a year complaining about bad graphics and then being given a button to turn the graphics off.The basic worker bots that you rely on also sucks. They're stuck in feedback loops, changing their form - constantly confused while your garbage piles up, keeping your residents stuck and angry until they leave. So that you're constantly super-micro-managing stuff that isn't your fault.The combat mechanics are broken. I've done a detailed breakdown in forum posts on exactly how and why it's fundamentally broken that I won't go into here. But trust me when I say combat will take up 5% of your actual time but influence 100% of your map. You will have to gouge wide avenues to make room for slow, massive crappy bots that you will almost never use.But if you don't get the slow, massive crappy bots then at some random point you will be invaded and suddenly die. It might happen in the first ten minutes, or the first three hours of a dozen times in between. But if and when it does, you'll be crapped on so fast that hours of gameplay is suddenly null and void.Again, the developers were told about this by loyal early access players and beta testers. Reviewers have left feedback and so have new players. None have been listened to.This is arguably the saddest point. There are so, so, so many other problems I haven't gone into because I just don't have the time or energy any more. Because I and others have provided constructive feedback, left messages and supported the development by buying it in early access only to be utterly ignored as the studio steamrolled on.To the developers, I have a simple message. Your customers believed in you. They trusted that you would do the right thing, listen to their feedback and deliver a good game. Instead - during a year of incredible hardship with job losses, family tragedy because of Covid and lockdowns happening - you refused to listen, you took their money and you let them down.I'm not going to exaggerate anything here - you didn't kill anyone and you're not deserving of punishment or any silliness like that.But you should feel just a little ashamed of yourselves. And I hope that in the quiet moments alone - when you're not on Slack talking big bravado with colleagues, and laughing at customers for posting feedback you never listened to - that you actually reflect on how you let real humans down. And try to be better one day.

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I wish reviews gave you a meh option. Because for every person who like this game, 10 more will get frustrated and leave before continuing playing.The first tutorial level for starters, assumes you already know how to play, and starts dumping visitors on you. In the first game you had to build your own port, meaning you could get your basics decked out before allowing people in. It's small things like this that make a game feel like you don't have to rush to get through things. The original, you could click around, figure out where stuff goes, play with settings... here you have an annoying AI reminding you to keep working.Biggest con :- The new VAL. The text feels like it was written by a former roommate of mine, a person who was permanently stuck with the mean high school humor that made her feel important because she could put others down. This VAL suggested using the air lock to get rid of carbon-based life forms, if it was possible I would rather shoot this robot into space.It's like the dev's looked at the original, which was occasionally snarky but overall rather supportive of the player, and decided that snark without substance was what we would love far more.- If there were voice actors involved for the new VAL, I feel bad for them. There is nothing positive to say about the robotic lack of humor or any form of self-awareness.- The shopping system. I don't have the time to check every two minutes to see what over-priced junk my assistant can give me. Give me a merchant with overpriced ♥♥♥♥ that comes by every x minutes and I'll decide then if I want to look.- The battle system is... yikes. The mechs are useless unless you actively plan for their use, you can't easily build security bots to aid in your efforts and even your security force won't help you fight pirates. What do I pay these guys for? I don't care if they aren't the super muscular body guards of old, but I want my hired muscle to do what I need them to do.- Stop with the joke that says "you achieved something... well, actually, your robots achieved the thing. All you did was maybe click a bit". Yah, I know, that's the point of the game. Find a different joke or shut up.The meh : - The Love nest was replaced with a cat cafe. I love the furry critters, but they did get rid of the love stat and replaced it with... relaxation, I guess? There are a few other buildings that are supposed to be pop culture shout-outs, if you love those is entirely a you thing. The sushi bar is cute for example.- Do we need those boosts? Like, really? I don't use them, I can't sell them, they usually take up space I could be using for other resources.- It's nice you tell me that from now on a certain class of visitor will be showing up, but really? It doesn't matter in the game play for as far as I can see.The good :- prefabs are a thing now, meaning you can choose to get a small, medium or large size built with a few clicks. You can even save your own settings for a room, if you have a design you love.- The bio deck is very pretty and looks a bit fuller. - The version doesn't crash on steam like the original does, at least on my old laptop. Like, this is probably all I have left of the original startopia. There's a few positives and you might end up liking it. I hope the devs make some twitches and revisit the biggest issues, which is the main reason for the thumbs-up. But if you're unsure about buying this game, try the original first. It's strange to think voice-acting would make or break this game, but it does.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really really reallly hyped about this game but was thoroughly disappointed. All I wanted was Startopia remastered but what was delivered was Startopia the mentally challenged edition.So let's get into the details.Graphics:The Graphics are decent but due to design choices it actually feels like a downgrade.Compare the Energy Cores of both games. New Startopia has this generic looking building on each deck, do not let it get destoryed, that is it.In the good Startopia your wealth is represented by a shining blop of reflective energy, seriously reflection in that old game, and the more energy you have the bigger the blop becomes giving you an ingame representation of your success.The graphics sure seems sharper and more detailed but everything gets lost in colors and the art style equivalent of comic sans. In the good Startopia the Station seemed dark and cold, which was fitting for a derelict station the player was tasked to restore. And the player actually made a difference, when you were done the Station was bustling with life, lights and colours.Now, lights and colours is the default.Everything is a shining neon coloured mess. Even the factory and the recycler look like a freaking carnival. Bascially everything is dripping rainbow juice, so it becomes really hard to distinguish what the different buildings are and what they do.I guess the final nail in the coffin of my enthusiasm was the fact that you can no longer leave the station.Before you could move through windows to the outside of the Station and have nice view of the Station exterior, it may sound like a trivial gimmick but it came very handy once you had access to the bio deck as that was a great way to spy on your opponnents.Now, an invisble wall is hindering you even from touching the station's wall but now the bulkheads become intangible the moment you start to open them.Sound:Again, sound is decent, however, we have to talk about the computer voice.Back in good Startopia you had this nice AI companion who was constantly annoyed by working with you because he would have been a much better administrator than you and due to his calculations your failure was very probable and your failure means he gets scrapped along with the station and you. So, there was this constant passive aggressive tone in his voice but he gave you praise when you did something good. In the course of the campaign he became even pretty friendly and the relationship between you and him was more like friends that have to do this ♥♥♥♥♥♥ job.In new Startopia you get 3 voices and from the two voices I tried out now they are actively aggressive, insulting you every step of the way. And on top of this, they do not even narrate events that pop-up. So it feels like they only ever talk to you to insult you. Fun...Gameplay:The controls feel off, like camera movement. When you hold the middle mouse button to turn the camera around the WASD keys start to function like a shooter, meaning you move towards the camera direction. Very uncomfortable when you are trying to look around your station.The interface is feels uninformative and clunky. For instance almost everything is icons, barely any text and personally I find those icons mostly not very iconic.Finally compared to the good Startopia everything feels dumbed down.Terraforming the Biodeck has become simply painting a texture. Research is gone but is now just a buy upgrades with a second currency. There are fewer alien races and they all need the same stuff, making them basically just all the same but different skins according to their job.And those are just a few examples.So, all things considered I really wanted this to be a good game but it is not. I could forgive most of those shortcomings if it were an original Title but it is not. Obviously this is a nichè genre but it seems the developers tried to broaden the audience by making the game more like a social platform time wasting game but this will probably misfire and disgruntle fans of the original.So, if you liked the original, steer clear or keep and eye on your playtime, so you can refund it.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all tyvm very much to Kalypso for the review key. But sadly I can't recommend this game. I never played the original so I'm unaware and thus unable to be upset by changes and such. So that isn't a factor. Overall I found the game fairly charming. The idea is novel and it's right up my alley. Sadly all of the stuff the game does well is rendered irrelevant by the simple fact that it doesn't really work.A quick rundown:You manage a space station, aliens will arrive and you have to hire some as well ass see to their needs, such as food, sleep and entertainment. That's all fine, that's what the game is about. The problem is the station takes a fair while to traverse, it's set up in this neat ring with three levels. When an an alien(or robot) decides it needs to do something it'll call dibs on that thing, and head for it. This means if a piece of trash is on the ground somewhere, the game will check who is available to pick it up, and then assign them to it. This can be someone on the other end of the station, and they'll then spend four years slowly walking over there, waiting in line for elevators, before finally getting there and doing the job.There might be someone else right next to said piece of trash picking up another piece of trash, and then not pick up the other one right next to them because it's suddenly been reserved by someone else far away. This is mitigated a tiny bit by some stations having queues in front of them, so more people can head to them at the time. Those are the exception though.It makes everything horribly inefficient. And there is very little you can do about it. Aliens will stand around and fail to fulfil their needs even if they're right next to a thing that could fix it. Workers will completely ignore buildings that need repairs because someone somewhere has already called dibs on that job. It's frustrating.You'll later have aliens that constantly quit their jobs or die because they fail to fulfil their needs. Despite the fact you put everything they need within very close range. They just won't use it. And then you'll have to hire and train a new one, until that one quits, for reasons you can't do anything about because the tools don't work.It's a shame because I think it could very easily be a fun game, if it worked as intended.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: Garbage. Absolute garbage.As someone who loved the original Startopia I really, really wanted to like this game. Sadly it has become clear that this was a cheap, lazy knockoff made to cash in on the name for fans like myself. Take the basic gameplay of the original then make them worse and suck out every ounce of wit and charm the old game had and that's what you get with Spacebase Startopia.Gone is VAL the helpful virtual assistant with his dry British butler mannerisms, now you get the personality devoid, cliche evil AI whose dialog consists entirely of being insulting to the player...and not even in an interesting or funny way. Gone is Arona Daal the shrewd but charming and reliable trader, replaced with a bland shop window you'll probably never even use. There is barely any story or dialog in the game and what little there is is simply awful, especially the ending.From a design and technical standpoint it's a mess. I won't bore with the details but for every minor improvement there are two big steps back. Worst of all is the combat/mechs. There is no nice way to put this...it's completely ****ing broken! Literally the mechs are so buggy and broken that it was almost impossible to complete the last two missions because they would randomly stop responding and just stand there helplessly until either the opposing side destroyed them or I did manually. Either way needlessly wasting time and resources to replace them every single time. I'd ask if they even tested this game but it's painfully obvious they didn't or simply didn't care.At first I was going to say wait till it's $20 or less, but no, save your money and dump this trash out the airlock.
