_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR Review: while the art direction is solid and it faithfully recreates the bones of what made Startopia great, it just doesn't do anything new or innovative with the concept, and like all Realmforge titles, the pacing is extremely slow without giving you enough to do to keep things interesting.Pros:-Fun, colorful, art and animations-Really really wants to do Startopia justice.Cons:-Sluggish UI-Terrible pacing-Audio fades in and out at random.-Combat is clunky and boring-Realmforge's humor is still tired and flat.I was pretty excited for this release, as someone who spend an embarrassing amount of time on the original Startopia. I don't typically play in betas so I went into this fresh. I enjoyed Realmforge's Dungeons titles, with some criticisms, and I was hoping that they'd learned some lessons to apply to Spacebase Startopia.It's obvious that the developers have a lot of love for the original. The art design is great, the aliens are colorful and expressive, and the fact that aliens of the same species come in different colors and outfits does a whole lot to make the station feel alive. The kitsch-y neon sci-fi aesthetic of the station and the buildings work well, and everything is immediately recognizable for what it is (with the possible exception of the recycler and factory).The good design doesn't extend to the UI, however. It's sluggish, and frequently obtuse. I can't tell you the number of times I've been building a room and accidentally cancelled it because I didn't press 'confirm' when clicking a popup. There is no energy-flow screen, so it's impossible to find out just where your energy is coming from or going, and often your energy will drop suddenly due to an inspector or other event, and you won't even know why until you click on the notification minutes later. On the Bio Deck, certain biomes might be grayed out, with no explanation as to why.Picking up items is easy enough, but dropping them is wonky as well. Instead of right-clicking to drop, you have to select an item from the buffer to drop, but once you finish dropping items of a given type, it moves to the next item, frequently leading you to drop items accidentally. You also cannot open crates directly from the buffer or the cargo bay. It's not terrible, but over time it makes doing things feel just a tad to laborious. Terraforming on the Biodeck is also finicky, with water being invisible if it touches a bulkhead at all.One problem Realmforge has always had with its games is the pacing. This was a gripe in Dungeons for me, and it's a gripe here, too. I am not opposed to leisurely pacing in games. The original Startopia did it as well. However, if gathering energy to build new rooms and progression through the tech tree is going to be so slow there needs to be enough to do to keep the player interested, and there just isn't.  The trading port is unlocked late, so manufacturing goods is pointless, and plants grow so slowly that it's a chore anyway. I cannot for the life of me fathom why they would give you the factory before giving you a way to profit off of it. In every scenario I played with a Factory available, it spend 90% of the game idle. Not to mention that building new Fuzzers and advanced goods costs precious energy that you need to save for rooms anyway. Micromanaging room settings and prices is also gone. At the same time, alien needs and population expand very quickly, leading to long queue times as you wait for the energy to expand your facilities. The bottleneck at the elevators between decks always looks like a violent mob with the rage indicators overhead as aliens wait to get to the Disco. Opening new sections on the Fun Deck is cost-prohibitive early on, so at best one can add a single extra elevator next to the first. So far, of my 5 hours playing this game (and finishing half the campaign plus some free play), half of that time has been spent picking up trash while waiting for the funds to build the next thing required to advance my research (the ridiculously expensive security station). The one new thing they've added from the old, the mechs, haven't come into play at all, and I honestly am not sure why they would choose that to add to a station management sim. WIth this pacing, the game could really have done with some customizability and optimization tools for us to fiddle, or ways to interact with the station visitors and residents while waiting for the various subsystems like trade and research to come into play. Let us schedule shifts for our employees, increase or decrease prices for services, cap the visitor count to prevent overcrowding, build rooms that aren't squares jam-packed with as many stations as possible.Or else just speed the pace up a bit.Aside from all that, the only other complaint I have is the persistent audio issues. The music fades in and out at random, as well as VAL's voice. In one case, the sound stopped entirely for several minutes, only to return all at once, with several of VALs lines playing simultaneously. I can't even adequately critique the sound track because of it. I also ran into one UI but where after looking at an alien's detail menu, the keyboard controls and camera button on the mouse locked up entirely, requiring me to close the game and restart it. As far as release bugs go, not egregious by the standards of the day, but annoying nonetheless.In the end, I'm not sure I can recommend this game based on my experience. The terrific art design can't make up for the fact that RF hasn't quite learned what makes for engaging management sim gameplay. Or how not to run a mediocre joke into the ground.  If, through patches, they shuffle the tech progression, pacing, give the player more granular control over the station, and add more interactivity, they'll possibly end up with a worthy successor to Startopia. As it is now, it's not.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not finished. Kalypso may think it is, but that is because they didn't QA test it at all. There are so many issues, such as scuzzers not being able to fight, and your employees seem to also be against it. But guess what is something you need to do! Kill enemies! This means you have to get your tech tree really high and research security stations and wait for them to give you police bots, and guess what. They're not very good! You also need a damn transporter to move them about floors, what?!As with the original, you can hire a single, yes SINGLE, species to help with the biodeck. They get annoyed over the smallest thing, so you're constantly losing them unless your starbase is the cleanest smoothest working thing ever, even at the start. Garbage also builds up stupidly often, and its now impossible(ish) to entirely get rid of it. They added far more micromanagement stuff without thought over the original. Your air? Can now get bad and you need to freshen it with lots of bought O2 boxes or produced on the biodeck. You also can promote your staff which does... things? It's not immediately obvious and i noticed no difference, it seems to cheer them up if they're feeling sad, which is often, but RIP energy/money.They tried to give the commentator and VAL the same level of humor as the original. However I can only assume they fed the old lines into a bad AI and it generated other 'fun' or 'comedy' things, badly.Pathfinding is bad, aliens often find their way around with only minor messups, but your scuzzers and big fighting mechs seem to think they can walk through walls and get stuck all the time.tldr: Bad game that is just nostalgia bait, go to Steam Shop or even GOG and buy the original. It's way more fun, actually works, and more importantly the developers cared, this is just a pump & dump game by Kalypso, which they're getting very good at doing from their previous games too. I hope in time we get a proper spiritual successor rather than this ridiculous expensive game that feels like a beta that got released as gold.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR if you are looking for your nostalgia fix this aint the game for you chief. But it is a good game especially if you haven't played the original.Being a reboot(?) of the original Startopia i will be making comparisons to that game. let me say that if i had to choose recommend that game over this one simply because the original has more character. That being said effort has been put in here and its not just a blatant cash grab so it has that going for it.Gameplay wise it plays much the same as the original game you start with one segment on each of the three decks on the station Maintenance, Entertainment and bio each deck has different things you can build (or teraform in the case of the bio deck) that allow you to keep your visitors and employees happy. Each race has a job they can perform for you as an employee, one race specialises in Medical stuff, another does the Garbage recycling etc. so you want to have a number of different races on hire to keep everything running smoothly. these aliens-when on staff-can level up and perform better as a result. each campaign mission has you do something different. From recycling a certain amount of energy, to healing a certain number of sick aliens to rehabilitating a certain number of criminals...The issue i have is these missions are carbon copies of the original game. The campaign does feel a bit lazy so far as a result and in the (at the time of this writing) 2 hours ive played i haven't seen any variation and its been almost identical level to level (with the ability to buy more segments in this game than the original)the main gameplay difference ive found so far is research, in the original, you would build a laboratory you would hire some Turrakens to work in it and you would drop crates of resources, buildings or droids in and they would research the next thing down the tech tree based on what item you put in the lab and then if you put an already researched item in the lab they would improve that item. In this game you have a menu, in this menu you have a number of options for research that you have to complete a prerequisite task, so for cargo holds you have to produce 5 resources, for a factory you have to store 5 things in a cargo bay, to unlock the tourism stuff you have to own one cafe etc. I Feel the old way was more interesting but this new one does have its merits as you can see what you want to unlock and how to unlock itA Definite downgrade from the original game is the Character the original had. Your AI assistant in the original would spout amusing anecdotes from time to time which so far appear to be missing. and Arona Dhall would ocasionally pop in to sell you some of his "Quality goods" that "Fell off the back of a trolley" neither makes a return. In this and for your AI assistant in this one you can choose from 3 voices one sounds like EVA from command and conquer, one sounds like GLADOS from portal or the other sounds like "we needed a male voice to balance things out lets just make Generic Male AI no 1". I picked "GLADOS" and the sass is entertaing but after a while it does feel a bit out of place due to the Cutesy art style which leads me to a gripe of mine. In the original Game i could picture all but one of the races doing the jobs they did (seriously the insects only do Comms work? they just didn't look very suited to the job to me) in this one i would say only one seems to make sense in their job (Dryad farmers) the worst offender is the security aliens...they are chubby,fluffy,almost always smiling and not very intimidating at all, one cutscene even shows them dancing in waterfalls on their home planet like some sort of cat thats enjoying a massage. the original had 8 foot tall, muscle born aliens with Red carapace for skin and stern expressions now THEY were who i would want for my security. there is one change i did appreciate though and that was the addition of uniforms, it used to be that your employees would have your faction symbol over them now they wear uniform clothing, which is a subtle but more immersive approach and one that i actually prefer over the original game (although having the option to have the faction icon might be nice, but i didn't go looking for it)I am also pleased that the soundtrack does seem to have taken a few cues from the original. The only track that seems to be missing a spiritual successor is the entertainment deck, but i think i know why they didnt put that in considering the cutesy art style, it might also might be the reason for the absence of the Siren race from the original. but all in all not a huge loss

_childDocuments_.review: It has some issues but it's not nearly as bad as some people are making it out to be. tl:dr at the endHalf of the issues people seem to have seems to me that they did not understand or are aware of game mechanics that are already there. This seems to be confirmed by the little total gametime of the reviewers. One might argue that if so many people didn't understand the mechanics then there is still an issue with the game, and that might be true, but one thing I don't think people get is that the 'tutorial' just teaches you the very basics, but the campaign itself is basically a tutorial too to prepare you for sandbox mode. Each chapter goes into detail on one feature, teaching you how that works, and then moving to a new one. I will make some examples of issues people highlighted in the reviews which make little sense to me:- Inhabitants complain that rooms aren't there when they are. They don't. If they do, it's because the room is closed as there are no workers in it. When you go check the workers might be there, but that's because they got back in the meanwhile. This is frustrating at the start, but I think it's actually the result of good simulation: Your workers only go back to work when they satisfied their needs, if the rooms they go to to do that are far away, or have massive queues, or also don't have workers it takes them longer to do so and get back to work. It's a cascade effect, where if one room doesn't work properly it can slow down everything else as a result. You can either hire more workers (and no, double the workers for number of shifts isn't enough: are you expecting these things to work 12 hours a day, you slavedriver?)- You can't buy more workers / other things whenever you want but have to wait for the rng shop. Yeah, you can't. Thing is, you aren't meant to use the shop as the primary way to obtain things. You are meant to build them in the factory. You can build anything you need in it as long as you have the resources (aka, a lot of dryads employees harvesting them for you and fuzzies going to pick them up and putting them in storage or you can periodically make a sweep and pick them up and deposit them yourself)- There's trash everywhere even though I put trashcans everywhere! You still need fuzzies to pick up the trash and drop it in the trashcan (so if they are busy doing other things they won't, you can assign some fuzzies to trash duty only too, but mine kept reverting back to automatic, probably a bug they'll hopefully resolve). Also, have you ever seen any place with a lot of people in it that hasn't trash everywhere? I like that when put into the role of an administrator I also have to deal with people (or aliens in this case) being dirty animals. Now moving to the actual issues (the other half):- The AI assistant is extremely annoying. People complained about the voice sounding about text to speech and about it trying to be some sort of GLADos rudeness but failing to be funny. I don't mind the text to speech, it's an AI, makes all the sense it'd sound like a robot. But it is just not funny. It keeps blabbing on and on about what bad job you are doing which, fair enough I guess, but then makes absolutely moronic examples and comparisons. 'I'd remove all the organics from the base, it'd give more energy and organics are so inefficient' oh, so you would remove organics from the project specifically designed to make the organics meet and reach agreements? That's literally the opposite of your job, and I'm the one doing it badly?- The menus being clunky and hard to navigate, and the UI being pretty bad in general. This is the biggest issue the game has, and probably the one from which misunderstanding about the game mechanics comes from. Too many clunky menus, a separate UI for the combat (why? there's three commands for the combat units in total), having some key information straight missing (like the energy breakdown. As far as I found there's no way to see what your ins and outs of energy are. You might have some massive wasters you can't address because you are unaware of them).- Lack of pause. I think this is an intended gameplay choice, I wouldn't mind it much if it didn't make it almost impossible to design rooms without the base going bonkers while you are busy doing that. I think designing rooms in single player should pause the game.- Combat is bad. Besides the nonsensical separate UI for combat, mentioned above, the combat is just lame. You get the unit, click on the enemy, that's it. Another thing people complained about was the Mechs needing two empty tiles to move around the base. I don't actually mind that one, it makes me design bases with wide avenues in the middle with decorations  and plants on the side which give the base a more organic look than a bunch of rooms all cramped together.- Camera lags sometimestl:dr The game is more like a rough gem than awful, like some people are putting it. Half the issues you see in the review aren't actually there, but some key ones are, which are: Bad UI and menus, annoying AI assistant, lame combat. If those three are a deal-breaker don't play it, otherwise give it a chance and play the tutorials and the campaign (basically an extra long tutorial) to learn the game before going into sandbox.

_childDocuments_.review: Until the last level, I would have considered this a "meh," but then the last level is such a deliberately terrible experience that it changed my mind to bad.  I loved the original Startopia.  I played it for hundreds of hours.  This is so much blander and worse.  The aliens are totally mute.  No cute little noises and voicelines like before.  Aliens all feel so samey.  I couldn't tell you a single thing one alien race prefers over another, if anything.  There's no charm.  The Eu'reka and the Bugs have cool designs, but everyone else is just boring.  Even now, I can tell you what the Sirens' or the Karmaramas' personality was.  Here?  I just played 32 hours of this game and I couldn't tell you what the Bugs like.  Researching new buildings is annoying.  You need so many visitors to be happy to unlock anything, and then you spend those points.  It can take forever just to get to security centers and jails.  So then what does your research center do?  It improves things, using buildings in crates.  Which means buildings have to be cheap to allow for you to research them five or six times, so producing buildings in your factory is ludicrously cheap, so buying and selling them to traders is also cheap, so trade is no longer useful or interesting, since the buildings you buy get researched instead of sold.  It also adds so many extra "utilities."  Bad air's now a thing, because buildings designed to be used on an enclosed space station just exhaust right into the air, so you need buildings to clear the air.  The fun deck isn't actually wired for electricity, so you need generators to power new sections.  The elevators are no longer instant, so you need lots of those to avoid long lines.  It's like they saw playtesters having too much room, money, and fun and decided they had to put a stop to that.I literally don't even know what the aliens are doing half the time.  You can hire 6 aliens and have no one working.  But then my fun deck is also mostly unused.  Casinos, sushi restaurants, cat cafes, arcades, they're all going unused.  So why is no one working?  I ended up hiring a dozen aliens just to ensure someone was working at all times.Combat's slow and terrible.  Do you have more mechs than the enemy?  You win.  Do you have fewer?  You lose.  That's it.  Not once did a battle turn out any other way.  No more employees fighting or contributing in any way.  No more taking over sections with Scuzzers.  You just blow up buildings until you win, or, to take over their main section, you spend 10 minutes shooting their energy core, even when they have nothing that can stop you.  Plus, you have to constantly send drones back, because whereas Memaus planting chestbursters was rare and avoidable in the original, here, everyone just gets facehugged, so you have constant people dying to chest parasites.  I could go on, but this is already a screed.There are some QoL improvements.  It's easier to hire, fire, and promote aliens.  It's easier to teleport goods.  Some of the new buildings are cute.  I like that it has premade templates, which apparently the AI doesn't use, so if you take over sections, it's still full of terribly designed monstrosities, just like in the original.  That's it.  It feels like someone described the original Startopia to someone who then tried to recreate it with better graphics.  So much is blatantly copied that they obviously were aware of the original, but so many things are worse that it doesn't feel like they played it, or if they did, they didn't enjoy it.TLDR;  It's bland, boring, and full of terrible design decisions.  It could just be blandly inoffensive, but the final level make it actively offensive.  Try it if you get it for free or in a bundle with better games.  Otherwise, avoid it.

Other than that the graphics are bright and happy (I prefer the graphics of the original). Everything else is a hollow letdown.I come from the original Startopia like most of the people that got this one. To be honest, I have a couple of hours worth of ranting about the issues and lacking content. One of my major issue is the number of bugs it has. For example I had 3 mechs attacking and winning vs another commander, mid fight they vanished from the game (deleted, removed, poof) and it lost me the game. They could redeem the game with updates in the future but not as DLC, they would have to be free and it would still be a lot of work to even come close to what the original Startopia is. I have 14 hours in this one because I forced myself to go as far as I could. I quit playing 2 times because of the bugs and how stupid the game is, I had to take a break.I finally stopped playing and loaded up the original Startopia, best choice I made.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: Welp, like the other reviews say. This game is a low quality cash grab.Tons of bugs in the game some of which make it unbearable to play like for example the sound cutting out, or after a long game being unable to click things anymore on the station, only the interface responds.Bad design decisions, such as VAL's bad voices and the badly written lines its been given some of which literally sound like they came from google translate. Another bad decision was the events and such, like every inspection results in a shutdown, no passable inspections, plus some exploits in battle between sectors, event spam, no cooperation with AI players..No updates in years, they abandoned the game as soon as they released it. No chance that anything here will ever be fixed. Seriously, don't even get this on discount like I did, it wasn't really worth it. I hated the gameplay, couldn't stand VAL, and realize that nothing will ever improve. I already went beyond the return policy play time because I wanted to be completely thorough and give the game a chance. It wasn't worth the 70% off I paid for it.The only good thing was that I liked the music. This game did have potential, had they stuck with it a little longer and worked towards fixing the problems. Just fixing the problems would have made it worth it, but fixing the bad decisions could have made this game a real hit.But, with their crappy launcher platform which I had to block with my hosts file as a method of displaying ads to people who launch the game and stuff, and as the company ditched it so fast, I will never get anything from Kalypso again. I've blacklisted the entire publisher now. The launcher is a very bad move that automatically earned the blacklist to begin with. Not bothering to fix anything, just proves further scummy-ness.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: Spacebase Startopia contains everything to be a good game but it fails to deliver. I don't feel the charm from the original game. The combat is horrendous, although there are a lot of buildings and aliens in my base it still doesn't feel alive at all. The sound bugs out all the time as well which is unacceptable for a so called finished game.I suggest buying the original game from GOG.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: I was initially looking forward to this game when it was announced in 2019, a spiritual successor to the legendary sci-fi management game by MuckyFoot in 2001.It skipped my mind when it released in 2021 due to other things going on in my life and now I decided to try and play it despite the mixed reviews and let's just say I should've thought something was up and it's readily apparent now. This game has terrible optimization issues where the whole game chugs trying to access your employee menu. The AI pathing is exceptionally bad and nobody seems to seek out the Sick Bay when needed. VAL is especially annoying as they're nothing like the snarky but by-your-side inorganic of the original with a grating text-to-speech voice.And good LORD the ending is such a copout whereas the original you were actually helping to make the galaxy better in the wake of intergalactic warfare and VAL even offers to toast with a bottle of champagne, I couldn't stand getting that far because while I could work through the slow process of building up my army in the penultimate mission, I couldn't stand the massive amount of chugging caused by navigating the menus.I don't like the additions of more needs for the aliens which means more things the game needs to keep track of and leads to an even greater strain when you're dealing with hundreds of visitors and Unity is *not* the kind of engine for agent-based sim gameplay as we've seen with both Cities: Skylines games. (For an example of a well-optimized game, see the first two RollerCoaster Tycoon games which are programmed in x86 Assembler with a bit of C++ to run on Windows, those games will run decent even on an old ThinkPad)Oxygen management is just another hassle. Having to build the lifts between floors rather than two coming with each segment.Energy distributors on the Fun Deck which replaces the more subtle Power Rating that limits your spending ability.Worse still is the complete lack of planning for any mod support at all which would've helped by, say, bringing back the feel of the original or even a total conversion mod of the original but nothing of that sort was planned or even considered.What are some of the things I *do* like about this game? Well some of the neat shortcuts for performing functions such as the item vacuum and the ability to instantly unpack with Shift+R.Research improves the performance of facilities rather than just simply making them cheaper to produce.A lot of actions can be performed more directly rather than the original's play-by-feel with the lack of numbers.Dryads can passively harvest from plants on the Bio-Deck without destroying them but you can harvest them directly if you need resources urgently.I'm not angry at this game, I'm just plain disappointed at the wasted potential of a sequel or successor to one of the defining games of my childhood
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: Edit on 8/26/2022: Swallowed my pride and repurchased the game since it has that kind of thing I am honestly looking for. Will give the review a proper do-over as I invest time in it.-----Original review on 8/23/2022.Decided to pick this up during the sale. Quickly refunded it due to the advisor, VAL, being a complete and utter a$$hole, enough so to make playing the game unenjoyable. I like management games, especially sci-fi related ones, but I'm there to play and have fun, not be mocked and insulted to the point of turning it away. This could have been an enjoyable game, but unless I missed something in my quickly established aversion to the 'advisor', I'm not gonna be returning to this just to be insulted for my troubles.That, and the devs have abandoned the game, so there's that.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: Having played a lot of Startopia back in the day, this just doesn't feel right at all. The ugly outlines, the overly colourful and cluttered buildings, structures and textures and the overall cartoony feel, the ugly alien redesigns and weird control scheme just isn't what I wanted from a spiritual successor...like, at all. Also there is this HORRENDOUS text-to-speech going on with the AI, which is atrocious...I miss the sarcastic VAL from Startopia while the devs here just didn't even bother with voice acting and didn't even quality control their translations!But there are a few good things! The new soundtrack, while it certainly isn't the moody and sci-fi music from Startopia, has a lot going for it. The new buildings are a great and innovative addition...but...that's about it!If you want a new Startopia, stay away from this game.If you only want a simple space station management game, get it on a fat discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, I still have the original on a disc at home and I played the Beta. But sadly it missed the mark and still feels like a beta product. The humor falls flat. The scripted dialogue is at times extremely hard to follow due to the weird robot voice they decided to go with. The interface is actually worse than the original game somehow, especially combat and conquering sections is needlessly overcomplicated in that you have to enter a special hud to order your units around.Lastly I can't listen to the game call me "Command-R" one more time. Who thought that was funny to hear a thousand times in the most annoying voice possible? They have added two other voices but non of them are especially pleasant to listen to. Where is Arona Dal when you need him?
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: I am quite disappointed about this game... considering the cost of it and technically being a remake I would have expected a bit more to begin with (or a cheaper product).If you're an old Startopia player...  the controls will absolutely confuse you. Simple stuff like "everything's done with right-click" - why?! It makes no sense. Clicking on an alien should be at least done with left-click, building stuff with right-click. Simple controls, why is everything on right-click. The left mouse button has no immediate use... makes no sense to me.Flying with the camera makes no sense, when using WASD the camera stays in the same height/position and moves around. As soon as you click the middle mouse button to see where you are going, the height baiscally changes and you fly to the point (down to the floor) that you are looking at. That again makes no sense to me. If I wanna fly and look around, I basically have to decide... either I look around and move the camera knowing i fly on the ground, have to look up again to fly up to then continue looking around. Or... I move with WASD only but then can't look around the station. Who the heck came up with that?One of the most "delightful" parts of the old game was the AI talking in the background, coming up with random facts and stories and sometimes being a bit smart-pantsy... the new AI is just a condescending annoying [enter word here]. I have no idea, why someone would think that AI is in any way funny whilst through the whole game play (and I haven't even played that much yet) it's just talking you down, how is that supposed to keep you entertained?Some of the essential game mechanics are also completely changed. Why does the berth have food AND cleaning in the same building? The berth was originally just sleeping quarters and you could move the foods elsewhere, forcing your aliens to discover the station. Now everything is just inside the berth. What'S the point? Apart from the fact that the berth is now constantly overrun because EVERYONE tries to get into it, whilst before the lavatory and the food station were elsewhere and the sleeping quarters too... so 3x as many aliens now try to get into the berth with an endless queue unless you build a huge amount of berths.The graphics are cute, I find some parts are just too interactive - don'T get me wrong, i don't mind the atmosphere cleanser to move and wiggle and blow clouds, but not EVERYTHING in that station has to move and wiggle and blink... even the doors of the lift keep wiggling... a bit much?!The factory is a bit confusing, but that might just be me being too used to other systems. I just find the interface a bit illogical, though the original's Startopia factory interface wasn't much better to be fair.I like the fact that "hired" aliens now where the stations uniform. That's a small little feature I quite enjoy. As silly as it may sound.I will update this review over time, but so far, I am not impressed. In German there is a word "verschlimmbessern" which roughly translates into worse-bettern... meaning... someone tried to improve the game play but actually broke it or made it worse. The new aliens are cute, but why did they have to change, what was wrong with the old ones? Focus should have been elsewhere...
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: Doesn't exactly scratch the same itches as the original Startopia. It just kinda scratches around the sweet spots.VAL is now voiced by Text-to-speech, is a little more demeaning, and is basically a weird mix of GLaDOS and the Original Startopia VAL.Building rooms and stuff kinda feel empty and lacking. Not much better gear put into 'em. You'll probably be using the blueprints a lot(Which is a neat feature).Combat System has changed though. You now use Drones and Mechas for battle. A pretty neat upgrade to the original's Employee VS Employee shootouts IMO.Overall, it's a different flavored Startopia that has it's charms. Not a sequel, but a side grade with different content and modernized graphics.Have fun, Command-Rs. ^^
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: This game has big shoes to fill. And it does that moderately well. Gameplay does feel like Startopia. Graphics is good. And all in all it's not a bad game.But there are issues. Many people mention the bad voice acting. Well it's not really voice acting, since it feels like an AI reading stuff. But that's not necessarily bad since the only voice you hear is supposed to be a cold hearted AI. I don't even mind the fun making an insulting jokes made about carbon-based life form's inefficiency. What a I would complain about is the humor and general writing of the voice acting. It's fine when the voice throws in an insult about non-artificial lifeforms now and again. But there is almost nothing else. Almost always the same punchline to everything. And that gets old and boring real quick. It's like someone keeps making the same your-mom-jokes every second sentence. Not very creative. On this topic the old Startopia is lightyears ahead of this one with Arona and the old VAL.Gameplaywise it's solid Startopia. I'd like some more chart and statistics. It feels like there wasn't much effort put in to make notable improvements though. It's pretty much a refurbished Startopia with a different combat system (although I personally don't care much about combat in Startopia) and worse voice acting/humor.So if you want a refurbished Startopia with better graphics and similar gameplay and don't care that much about the humor and voice acting aspect. Go ahead and buy it.I personally hope that they keep working on this game, listen to suggestions and improve it. It is in no way bad as many reviewers make it out to be. It just has lots of room for improvement.Right now I would only pick it up if it was like half price or so on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original and enjoyed it. While I didn't spend hundreds of hours on the original, but I did spend more than 30. However, something about this remake just feels... off. It is definitely missing some "je ne sais quoi".Maybe it's the "trying to be GlaDOS snark, but is actually just boringly mean" dialog. Maybe it's how the campaign feels "slow" or "too hand-holdie" after suggesting the tutorial that was, also, slow. Maybe it's the fact that all the aliens aren't as visually unique or striking as they were in the original. But something is "off" about this one and just isn't worth my time -- even when I got the game as part of a humble bundle for $15 with a ton of other content to sweeten the value.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: I ticked "yes" because the game works... But note that its not a perfect game. If you bought the original game, congrats, you bought this game. The aliens are more or less the same but their appearances and name was changed, there was no reason to do that. Strange is that one of the dialogues actually mentions the "Grey" aliens from the original. It felt like they intended to add some or all of the original aliens, but either because of licensing issues, a bright idea or just a cheap way of adding more races, they didn't. Anyway, since it plays the same as the original it acts as a modern version, but its still got some issues from the original. So it feels a bit... Lazy? Like they just took the original game and re-skinned it.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: I must admit, I have hundreds of hours in the original "Startopia" from when I was a kid and my dad bought me the original game from a charity shop. So I'm a big fan of the original game and was hoping this would largely be a re-texturing of the original game.I spent all of 8 minutes in a sandbox level and decided that I had seen enough. My major gripes:* The camera controls are utterly terrible.* It feels like the game needs a way higher FOV.* Some of the alien races have been completely changed (security race, the angel race, the religious race).* All of the races have been somewhat renamed.* Various core buildings have been removed.* Scuzzers are replaced with fuzzies (I can't overstate my disgust).* The fuzzies have 0 character, unlike the scuzzers who had such original movement and animations.* The bio deck looks really weird, I can't describe it.I have requested a refund, and will likely just buy the original (and clearly best) version of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: Spacebase Startopia is a playful attempt as a spiritual successor to Startopia. I did purchase the game the moment it was available on Steam and was able to see the 'pre-alpha' (or whatever it is called). There are several similar elements to its predecessor, but this game lacks many fundamental game elements that really made the older game 'sing'. Cons: - it's far too easy to lose, with the removal of Arona Daal. Without a fresh supply of trade, the game gets very difficult. - Research is completely restructured and now is not as critical of a process - No Security Scuzzers without a Security Station which takes up a LOT of room. This means if you don't land grab quickly, you can 'die on the vine' without having a military. That and Mechs need a LOT of room to move. - The UI is very dodgy. I either have to click multiple times to get an order issued, or I have to close out of the menu I'm in completely for it to register. - Research is very buggy. I have to 'deconstruct' and 'reconstruct my Research Station every few researches as it seems to get stuck. - The game has no soul. Startopia had custom 'voices' and personalities for each alien type. Here, I just can't give a care who has what problems.Maybe I'll revisit this game some other time, but this feels very unpolished. TBH, it makes me want to load up Startopia instead of playing this version anymore.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: Unlike most, I didn't play the original Startopia when I was younger, so I'm not bringing that to the table here. From a purely objective view as a fan of management-type games, I'm not at all satisfied with playing this game.Firstly, I agree with a lot of others when it comes to the notifications. There are way too many. I should never be yelling at a bunch of lines of code to shut up, but there wasn't a consecutive 3-minute span of time where I didn't literally get mad at this game's inability to shut up.I didn't complete the campaign. It was alright for some time, but the mission "Thunderdome" if I remember right, has you amass a 400,000 credits as its initial goal. Okay! No problem and I soundly beat the computer opponent to it...but wait! Now I need to defend my sectors and take over one of his...alright let me just build up and WHOA!? Here come not one, not two but four, FOUR, (4) mechs, plus a butt-ton of security drones. Meanwhile, I can barely build new ones because I can't get the medicine needed to make holo crystals to make more mechs. No plants in my Bio deck are dropping meds and no traders are selling them. Great game!I tried free play but without opponents there's really no challenge. I put on opponents and turned on the setting so that, instead of mech combat to take sectors you have a bidding war with your opponent, but it was taking stupid amounts of money to expand since the bids only go up in 10000 credit increments. Regardless, I got pissed off anyway because, for some reason, my security drones were refusing to fight the pirates that the game decided to not tell me were assaulting me. Or the multiple chest-bursters that were spawning every thirty seconds. Literally, they just wouldn't follow my commands. Great game!In brief, I just was not having fun, to such a degree, in fact, that I just don't believe someone could have possibly played this and said "Yeah! This a product we should release." Go somewhere else for your entertainment. This was painfully frustrating at worst and merely "okay" at even the best moments. Don't fart away your money on this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: You only launch once. Players only remember the release, not the fixes that came later.Starbase Startopia could have waited a bit.This game is an execution in failure; not by design nor concept, but by numerous bugs and balance issues. It is clear Realmforge Studios rushed a project they barely tested and might not have ever played. This is particularly evident as all the base game features work; but the AI routines and balance have significant issues. AI will sometimes bumble around lost, stuck, unable to reach their destination or perform a task. Buildings decay at such a fast rate, that it exhausts the workers and player in futile attempts to maintain them. These are issues that could have been caught with playing for more than 15 - 20 minutes at time. It is clear Realmforge Studios lacked the commitment to even play their finished product nor examine quality control.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to leave a good review, i really do. The game looks good and has that Startopia-vibe to it I've experienced for the last 20 years. Yet it has so many falws, bugs, bad design decisions, alien becoming mad for no apparent reason, garbage everywhere and fuzzies doing nothing.It's such a damn shame and I really hope this game gets better, but even after waiting for 4 patches before continuing playing, there are still way to many problems with it.Update: I have given up on this game after so many months I still get game-breaking bugs every time I play :(
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun and frustrating. I can't recommend it at this price.Combat is so broken and frustrating. Controlling the mechs and drones is a nightmare, they rarely do what you expect them to do. Making room for mech paths across the base means you'll waste precious space that could have been used for buildings.Trading is weird, even if you have the right stuff, sometimes the button to sell or buy them just doesn't work (and it isn't because of lack of energy).Variable building templates don't move between saves, making them pointless, specifically in the campaign where you would usually build 1-2 buildings of the same type.I didn't finish the campaign, as I reached the level that has 3 other computer players that I need to defeat, and it relies on the frustrating combat, keeps damaging your buildings and energy core every now and then (for fun, I guess?), and randomly gives some bonus to a random player (no idea what that bonus is).I'll probably jump in again for free play later, but this just looks unfinished to me, and for that price, and an original game to live up to, I expected more.UPDATE AFTER FREE PLAYSo, I jumped into Free Play, with no other players so I never bother with mechs and their paths, and no VAL bonuses. It starts off a bit better but later the whole thing collapses. Employees keep quitting for lack of nature in fun and sub decks (The game says placing plants in pots would help, which I already did, but there's no way to see whether it's working or not, there's no nature overlay or any feedback when employees go next to plants).Then visitors started dying, apparently only 1 or 2 medics bother with their job out of the 14 hired ones.The last research tiers are also disappointing, they unlock fancier buildings fulfilling the same needs, with much less visitor capacity and gigantic buildings that make viewing the base more annoying.I'll set the game aside for a while, maybe updates will improve things a bit.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: It's fine, but makes no improvements on the original while losing much of its charm. The writing isn't funny and the mechanics are poorly cobbled together. While it functions as a mediocre shadow of the original game, get the original if you can. The original shows its age, but it runs better and the design is better. The music, writing, and VO are terrible in this version. If you want a game like Startopia, but not as good, then this game is fine I guess
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: This is a sad game. It begins with the terrible writing, the grating voice delivery  -- it doesn't help that there are three voice tracks, all competently done, but they all use the same lame writing and terrible direction. I just switched voices off after a while. It continues with picking up the obvious trappings of Startopia and somehow making them worse than the first version (which wasn't amazing, but competent.) It ends with the sloppyness in game design and hostile user experience. Unpacking, item production, research, combat, vermin extermination, random pop-ups presenting you with bad choices, no way to see ingress and egress of energy, resources, people and so on.Yet the game is not very challenging, so you can win your missions anyway. Too bad that the "campaign story" sucks and there is no motivation left in me to continue playing. I don't know, I racked up 30 to 40h, often leaving the game running while doing something else (just make sure you have enough trash bots), so I guess I got enough out of it for my money. So sad.

_childDocuments_.review: As soon as I got it, I played it for 13 hours strait and I really enjoyed myself. _childDocuments_.review: So I don't do reviews, but I feel like I have to make one about this game because I am a huge fan of the first game and have even played what I would consider a fair amount (enough to test all the features and hit endgame a few times). So Startopia is one of my favourite strategy games I played as a child. It was humorous, strange and Sci-Fi all muddled into one. I loved it. I only wish I could say the same about this game. Lets start off with the base game play. This game is truly beautiful. From the overall graphics to the unique designs of the buildings, each designed uniquely for its purpose. That is unfortunately where the good points stop. This game had so much potential, but I had no idea that they'd remove so many themes from the first game. One of the issues they plagued this game with, was a heavy amount of micro management for the sake of micro management. You can only build so much before you are over-cumbered with soaring the floors with an eagle eye to call out every shot and pick up litter. Yes, you apparently are a part time bin man. This doesn't just affect litter though, you also have to micro manage every single building for when they need repairs because now in this game, they just lose durability over time (at a rather fast pace) leaving you flustered with so many tasks to do and you haven't even unlocked your third room for all your floors yet. This takes away the ability to be able to look at what you've crafted becoming slowly self sufficient. Now lets move on to other players (AI mainly). Not only do they advance and unlock rooms at an incredibly fast rate (leaving you feeling like you need to rush to expand your total space) but they also cause a lot of issues when you want to expand. The AI of the visitors/workers is actually broken, where any unique colour textures they have get instantly removed when you hire them because they only designed the uniform for that particular species with the one skin. Not only that, but they also have the tendency to leave their disease until it's gotten out of hand before getting treated, meaning that they are infecting more and more of the population. Now this will cause you a lot of issues, but because you're still trying to keep up with all the micro managing you do, you start to find it difficult to keep up. You cannot force them to get treated either, they have to go by their own choice. This often will leave you getting annoyed when people get mad when they're hungry etc, even though you have plenty of facilities to satisfy them, it's just the AI is ridiculously bad. Also P.s no matter how many workers you hire, the rooms they need to fill will never be full at once, so yeah, that's not annoying at all.Now on to war. One of the most fun attributes to the first game was being able to get an army of workers to fight the enemy to take their rooms and expand. This has been replaced with something that actually made me rage quit when I first discovered how the takeover process works. The workers do not arm themselves, not even the brutes. Nope, the brutes are just some fat Sci-Fi build-a-bear looking species that only operate machines via the station. So drones, sounds fun, right? Nope. The drones are actually awful. They will occasionally arrest criminals, but they aren't something you can just build on command, so you will find you are heavily limited. Not only that, but they added this war command table for you to control that is essentially completely useless and could be literally replaced with a right click. It is so awful to use that even when I was forcing myself to use it, it was just god awful. So verdict. As a whole, this game is just an unbelievable disappointment. Lacking in many areas it's first instalment thrived, removing the subtle humour and replacing it with a really cringe bot voice. I wouldn't recommend this to anyone. In fact, I'd honestly get my money back if I could. I honestly suggest the original Startopia as its far superior and while the graphics are certainly out of date, the game play is spot on and everything I wanted this game to be. Honestly devastated. Honestly, you could pay double the amount of this games value for the first instalment and you'd get more value out of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: Mixed is exactly right, that is the experience I got from this game. Building the base, taking care of various needs of aliens is fun and the reason you would probably get this game. On the other hand, graphics are average and game stutters and lags a lot. There are a lot of bugs, for example Startopia doubled the amount of goals I had in scenarios, when I managed to get one, I couldnt get the same goal second time, so I had to restart the whole level. Also fights with robots... building tycoon should not have any battles or combat, because it is clunky, unnecessary and no one is looking forward to it.

_childDocuments_.review: Dear god! Who tested this game? Apparently no-one!1. Main menu doesn't even work correctly. Highlighted option remain highlighted. Going into other options shows them over the top of the previous options so you can even read them!2. Tried different resolutions but instead of offering the usual 1920x1080 or other 16:9 resolutions I can only choose 100%, 90%, 80% etc resolution of my 32:9 5120x1440 screen. Bonkers!3. It's well documented how annoying VAL your ever present assistant/abuser is. Truly terrible!4. Managed to get through the 1st couple of tutorials but again the UI is all over the place often highlighting the wrong icon if I've accidentally gone into an area I wasn't supposed to.Think I'll stick to the original...
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: Badly broken, unplayable past midgame, and abandoned, unfortunately.The game is feature-complete but riddled with game-breaking bugs.UI stops working after a while -- clicking on things becomes only sporadically effective, often just stopping working for 10-60 seconds at a time.  The keyboard will sometimes stop working, and alt-F4 is the only solution to that.  Sound frequently just dies -- sometimes dropping to the main menu fixes it, other times it needs a restart (which particularly sucks because it's got a good soundtrack and that's a significant part of the appeal of the game).  UI elements disappear or stop working.  Sometimes going to menu will fix it, other times not.  It's a mess.The game doesn't quite work internally.  One of the biggest problem is that staffing is broken -- for each position, you're supposed to assign 3 aliens to fill all 3 day shifts, but for some reason they often just won't attend, and no amount of overstaffing can fix it.For example, on the mission where you have to keep the station free of criminals, you need to keep three security stations (4 positions per station) staffed -- that should be 36 aliens to cover all shifts, 48 if you're being careful.  I ended up assigning 85 aliens (!) to staff them, but they were always between 0 and 3 working at each station.  What are the other 70-something doing that whole time?  Makes it kind of hard to accomplish mission objectives.  The game does model needs (eating, restroom, etc.), but it's well beyond that.  Pretty frustrating.Another problem is everyone being mad at my station for boredom because there's no disco.  There's a big disco almost always at 0% usage.  Yeah, staffing problem for sure (in this case 24 staff to run 2 slots in the disco, so constantly not staffed), but even when they decide to work, no one uses it.  Nothing you can do except watch them fume.I see discussions on these and other bugs in reddit, etc., from a year ago, and none of it has been fixed.There's a fun game somewhere underneath the bugs, but this game is definitely not worth buying until it's fixed, and Kalypso has a reputation for not letting their developers bring their games up to solid prime-time playability.  It just never got finished.

_childDocuments_.review: I read the reviews before buying the game. Actually, I was a bit confused as I had never played this kind of game before. _childDocuments_.review: The original Startopia is a gem. A flawed gem, perhaps - many of the campaign missions are ridiculously hard until you know the correct, quick, painless, gamey way to brush through them. But a gem, nonetheless. Gorgeous, aged very well indeed. The new Startopia is... wrong. Sure, it looks flashy. Sure, it borrowed heavily from the original. But what was a huge, sprawling, empty canvas is now a tiny station. The deliciously sarcastic computer is now a choice of three bloody annoying soulless voices. Micromanagement is back with a vengeance. The graphics make my eyes hurt. I was looking forward to this for months. And the painful fact is still that the ancient (2001!!!) original looks, plays and feels so much better than this. Asked for refund. Will reconsider if, at some point in the future, VAL returns. Possibly. Meanwhile, my old starbase awaits.

_childDocuments_.review: I would not recommend this game in its current form. If you enjoyed Startopia, play Startopia, a great game that still stands up well today.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve been playing Startopia since the original and have always came back to it throughout the years.  This game is that game and more!  I’m very excited to spend hours in this game for sure as it has everything I loved about the original with a ton more content thrown on top of it. If you love sandbox and colony builders, then you’ll love this game!  They added a lot more customization to building blueprints too, which is a huge plus.  You can now make your Spacebase exactly how you want it with more fine detail.  The only thing that could be added to make it even more customization friendly is changing panel textures and flooring, but other then that customization is still very well done in this game, basically enough to let your imagination go wild.The thing I most loved about this game is taking care of your new tourist aliens almost as if your Spacebase is a theme-park.  You have to give them entertainment, give them places to sleep, hygiene fixes and more!  You also can craft and trade in this game with other space ships!  Not only that, there are also baddies that will come in and try to destroy your Spacebase, so you’ll need a good security as well.After putting a few hours into the released version of the game, I still haven't found the reason for so much hate on this game.  I still think it could use a bit of polishing with some things, but overall I still think it's a pretty solid game and am having a blast.  Most of my time spent in this game was in beta while making this review earlier.  Now having played the game in its release state, I haven't encountered anything that makes me want to change my thoughts on this game.  I do hope that the devs do take some notes on some of these reviews as I do agree with some of the things noted, but I still don't see why It's very close to mostly negative.  Could just be me, maybe I am good at finding the diamond in the rough, heh. I know words are just words… and aren’t the full picture, so I have some content for you to watch that will give you a better picture on how the game will play out.  You can check that out from the link below.  I can say that it was definitely worth my money.I’ll be doing more content on this game soon!

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like there's a potentially very solid game at its core - and I've definitely had a few genuine laugh-out-loud chuckles in the first three missions, but the game has a glaring issue that makes it impossible for me to enjoy the way I want to enjoy builders/colony management sims for any length of time.There is no pause button. It certainly looks like there's a built-in pause functionality as the engine keeps running but the simulation pauses when you pull up the Steam overlay, but I can't for the life of me figure out how to actually pause the game so I can tweak my rooms and builds without feeling rushed.I play this type of game to relax, and the lack of a transparent pausing functionality currently makes me unable to do that because any time spent tweaking rooms is time that my station might fall into shambles.Can't be hard to implement, but I will be waiting until that feature is added.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, it's not the OG Startopia, but it didn't need to be. In some ways it's better with more dynamic rooms. In some way's it's not... I still miss the sarcasm of your OG AI assistant and also Arona. The Presitige unlock system is interesting, and make sense. I like the updated Sabotage capabilities. _childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: With Spacebase, the devs have essentially done three things:1. Copy-pasted Startopia2. Re-skinned everything3. Turned the maturity level down from teen-adult to child-teen in hopes of attracting a younger demographic, which unfortunately grinds the gears of the mature demographicFans of Startopia will find only a few changes in Spacebase, and most of them make the game worse. People new to Startopia are paying fifty bucks for something that they can pay  for.The ten levels of the flaunted voiced campaign is nothing more than tutorial levels with voice-overs, unlocking one step higher tech per level. And the voice-overs is  most annoying pile of garbage you most likely ever have come across in a video game. Ten years from now people will be using Spacebase as a meme for horrible A.I. voice-overs.Outside of the campaign the game has very little replayability as you're building the same buildings in the same build-order every game and have very limited character control.If you can find this game for free, try it. Until then, get the original.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: *Updated* For nostalgia sake I really wanted to finish this game and be able to recommend it, but I absolutely can not.I battled through the campaign, I have no sense of achievement at having completed it, I'm actually just more annoyed at the anticlimactic ending to what was a level designed without much apparent thought.Overall, as a game this isn't fun to play, the difficulty spike and micromanagement are dreadful (especially since there's no pause to enable making the micro management less overwhelming when things get complex), it's riddled with bugs, a whole bunch of shockingly bad game design choices, mechanics, UX and UI abominations. This is a bag of flaming garbage that I regret having purchased even on sale that does a disservice to the fans of the original by downgrading the game play.It's bad enough for me to say this is probably the last game I ever buy from either Realmforge Studios and Kalypso Media as I don't trust they have a clue what they are doing and certainly don't think play testing is important (if they did, how could they possibly get this so horribly wrong)

_childDocuments_.review: Spacebase Startopia is a remake to the ancient game Startopia.I played the previous game an awful lot back in the day and was happy to see that this game is remade.Spacebase Startopia is a juggling simulator just like Startopia was where you have to make your citizens happy and give them proper things to keep them busy like a SCI-FI Disneyland.It unfortunately has a lot of content removed such as the Memau, Skrasher, Grekka Targ, Kasvagorian, Turraken, Zedem Monk, and Polvakian Gem Slugs. But the Dryads in game look exactly like the Karmarama did.Also the Greys are the same, and the Groulien Salt Hogs are the exact same as the version in this game.I personally liked the original names for most of them and species wish they included them as variants in this game or at least skins.For example: The new replacer for the Gem Slugs is definitely much cooler than it was, but I'd still like the Jabba The Hutt style slugs to be in the game for more variety.The siren replacer being giant fuzzy moths in hipster clothing is a welcome change though, I absolutely love their design.One of the main issues with the game is the obsession with the garbage script, if you don't take care of garbage at the beginning of each match it's already over due to the 30 Vermin spawning out of every single coke can. I get the mechanic but it's very annoying and takes away from the game's overall feel to it.The next issue is by far removing the Memaus, they were incredibly immersive and to have them completely taken away and the jumpscare of a giant Skrasher bursting out of an infected person who got bit by one that was sick is sad, because that added incredible urgency to curing sick people.Another thing like the original is the enemy CPU advancing way too fast and instant research glitch by them being able to research more than 4 things from a single science station, but that was in the original so that's true to the content.Also the lack of diversity in the races of the game which the original game also had is very jarring. I get the set amount of races but I wish there were at least 20-30 different races. That may be asking too much as mechanics change that, but it would make the game really warrant its 40$ Price Tag.As it stands it's got decent gameplay, very good for livestreamers and I wish that more people would pick it up.25$-20$ is a good price for it watch it when on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: If you expect this game to have any of the charm of the original Startopia, you will be disappointed. The original Startopia was not a perfect game but was still a masterpiece in terms of sound effects, narration, animation and atmosphere. Spacebase is not a masterpiece. It's basically a pig wearing lipstick.Back when Staropia was released it was a solid 9/10 for me, with a point deducted only for rather atrocious rival AI, it's still at least a 7/10 despite the dated graphics which honestly still work pretty well considering that "polygon" games are still popular.For Spacebase a 4/10 is more than generous, even without comparing it with the much superior original game, it's just not a well designed or implemented game. It's unfortunate because I thoroughly enjoyed Dungeons 3 by Realmsforge.So my verdict is, if you haven't played the original Staropia, do! And whether or not you've played the original don't bother with Spacebase unless you're a really big fan of colony builder type games.

_childDocuments_.review: It's really not as bad as the reviews make it seem. _childDocuments_.review: This is a fine successor of the old startopia, yes the game is a little different from the original one, less humor, some rooms work different, but it is very enjoyable for the fans of Startopia.People are crying because of the narrator, or some nonsense they can find, i honestly don't get it, this is a very faithful version of startopia, with great graphics and playability.We do need some quality of life upgrades, better path finding, smarter robots, zoom needs to go farther away. _childDocuments_.review: preliminary review 2 days after launch: after playing 4 hours in closed beta, 13 hours since release and over the years easily 200+ hours of the real  i can say with confidence: no.just no.i'll try to keep it fair here. at first i was not amused, by now i'm straight p#ssed off.at some point this game could end up being really good but that time feels months away. there are so many things in need of more polish, more refinement or plain fixing that it sucks the fun out of everything.the AI keeps talking without end in a cringy and unfunny way and often interrupts itself because its 20  seconds long pointless yada yada yada doesn't  end before the next pointless monologue starts. this way you easily miss the 20% of actually important notifications. you are busy manually removing bombs from your station every 75 seconds (i actually used my phone to stop the time) or dealing with any other "urgent disaster" forced on you  that playing the actual game and building & managing a space station gets basically impossible. you get Interrupted before you even remember what you were doing before you got Interrupted last time. it's actually insane. 30+ aliens waiting at the elevator getting hungry, tired, dirty, bored, ill and angry because the elevators only carry 1 person every 5 seconds. and your space inside the station is limited and expensive if not impossible to expand depending on the mission.GUI, usability and quality of life features are a straight F grade. you have messages and menus flooding the screen, menus hidden inside of menus, notifications that get overlooked or plain lost by the game since you get overwhelmed with all sorts of notifications all the time (remember the bombs every 75 seconds?). every action requires more clicks than it should and on top of that mouse clicks often don't register for some reason. you have lists of aliens and rooms but as soon as you click on one of them for details the list closes and all filters reset. it's utterly pointless to even try using.the flying trader arona daal is no more. back then he ripped you off but he had some useful things at the start of a mission. instead you get the VAL shop and it's completely useless. only single use items (!) or like  10x overpriced stuff. you learn to ignore it quickly. and even if you do need something specific it's usually not available thanks to the item rotation. horrific!the new research system is a hybrid of actual research and prestige points for making visitors happy. all that is neither easy nor fun to use. at one point i just stopped caring about the bonuses and just clicked all the buttons i could afford to click. worked just fine and didn't waste idle time you simply don't have during playing.after  playing for about 1 hour and owning a third of the station performance starts getting really bad. even with a 8c/16t cpu, 32gb ram, gtx 1080 and all my steam games on ssd.actually last game i was down to 20 fps after 3 hours of playing. that's amazingly terrible performance. i just played one of the later missions involving combat and getting rid of competing station administrators. let's just say the combat system is so clunky it's out of this world. beating that mission took me 4 hours. one time i had 15 minutes of combat straight. i needed to monitor every second of it and after that my station was totally f#cked up because i couldn't react to the constant messages & events and i was unable to adjust to changing demands and increased station size. i won the war but fixing up my station after that took me a full hour.oh and let's not forget: the single player missions are just an extended tutorial just like with the original startopia. sandbox and multiplayer are the real deal. if you don't care about that it's game over after 10 missions and about  20 hours. the amount of micro managing is off the charts. in fact building a nice station, making your visitors happy and rolling a profit turns to a side note when being bombarded with urgent emergencies all the time and the need to do absolutely everything yourself. want some potted plants to touch up your station, a pond on the bio deck for swimmers or just a single minute of peace and quiet? NOPE! you don't have time for any of that.did i mention? this game has no pause. brilliant!every mission i find myself thinking "i need to do this and build that" and 30 minutes later it's still not done! because bombs here, alien attack there, cringy AI speech in my ears and my attention getting trapped by bad interface or another random bug i just managed to find. i think i will stop here. with both complaining and actually playing. i think i made my points very clear.also it's massively overpriced. this game is not an original concept. it's 20 years old. they copied like 90% of it, made some changes and usually for the worse actually.with the clever use of discounts i paid 38€ for the extended edition and still i feel like i got tricked into paying  double what it's actually worth.if you want to start a starbase right now get the old startopia. it's 1/10th of the price but 10x better a  game.this game needs a lot more work to be enjoyable or even to hope to come close to the old one.don't tell me you tested this game 8 hours a day at the office when playing 30 minutes is enough to make me wanna smash my keyboard, torture the voice actors or just alt-f4 and forget i own this sad imitation.almost 9 months and a few updates later i finally managed to get the last achievement that was bugged before.and within the next second i quit and uninstalled.they fixed some stuff and added some quality of life features that should have been in the game from the start. but the game's performance is still terrible even on potent hardware and the problem of aliens being too stupid to fulfill their own needs is still there.to think that i paid 38€ on day 1 for this abomination makes me wanna hurl. worst deal of 2021 apart from corona.let's never talk about this game again.

_childDocuments_.review: Where to start...I played the beta and could see it was no where near complete then. So i waited until the final release of the game to see if any of the problems i had before were fixed... _childDocuments_.review: When I first found out that StarTopia was getting a modern remake/sequel, I was absolutely thrilled. I spent hundreds of hours playing the original as a kid. Oddly enough, despite its overall interesting gameplay and design, along with stellar writing and humour, the original game never really took off. I was sure it was going to die in obscurity.Spacebase Startopia lacks all of the above. The graphics have been bumped up, but simultaneously lost all their charm. The biggest offender is VAL. In StarTopia, VAL was a snarky AI with stellar voice acting and dry British humour. In Spacebase, you can choose three voices, or a fourth "no voice" option, and they're all bland. You might as well have just put a speech synthesizer in.I'm sure the developers poured a lot of love into this project, but it just feels like a soulless sequel to the original.

_childDocuments_.review: Review update: Can no longer recommend. The developer stopped updating the game three months after release. With the mentioned bugs in place, it disappoints.Original review, with hope removed:Not that bad in gameplay (I think the improvements in gameplay outweigh the downsides when compared to the original). But really bad in humor. Dull, repetitive - really embarassing. Still, not bad in gameplay!Not a highly optimized, sophisticated, large-scale RTS, but a fun playfield. I say it's enjoyable (ignoring the insulting jokes) and the later missions are a sufficient challenge.Some bad stuff:* Has performance issues. Building a large base, even with my 5900X, it blocks rendering half a second whenever a crate is put into storage.* Trading is obviously unbalanced and bugged.* Big bases are less attractive since aliens won't be super smart when it comes to route planning.* Hired aliens quit for lack of promotion (payment) when they already are fully promoted. Compared to the original, where you could just keep clicking the promotion button to fill them up with energy (money).Some good stuff:* Templates for rooms, yay!* Mechs. I was sceptic at first, but a new game mechanic should always be welcome.* The Biodeck is more important and easier to terraform (compared to original).It's hard to recommend at full price. But when on sale for half price, I'd say give it a try.
