_childDocuments_.review: Ninety-five percent of carbon-based lifeforms enjoy their time on Spacebase Startopia. Only five percent experience an unfortunate and surely accidental death.If you want to see gameplay and watch some of my second impressions as they happened, click on the video above. Spacebase Startopia is a delightful management sim where you run Space Disneyland. VAL, your sarcastic and dry humored AI is here to help... or maybe to watch you suffer. VAL always gets those two things mixed up. Prove yourself worthy as a spacebase manager by earning more energy than you spend. And don't worry: if you fail, you're easily replaced.The learning curve is steep, and despite the tutorial you're likely to miss a few things your first time. And maybe your second time too. (I certainly did.) But that's okay, because VAL is here with its three voice options to question your decisions even when you think you're doing the right thing. There's a bevy of aliens, structures, and even a splash of combat. You can min-max to optimize your building choices or take the more beginner-friendly pre-made structures as you're learning the game. The devs certainly tried to make things accessible even if at times you're left scratching your head about what to do. Or do the completely wrong thing despite your best efforts.But for those who can get past its learning curve, Spacebase Startopia shows its charm in the many aliens leaving reviews on your spacebase, just like other reviewers and I are doing on this game. #ConfusingButFun sums up my review, and maybe Kalypso will decide to hire me just like I hired my customers in-game. The tutorial isn't mandatory, but you'll need to play it to understand this game, and early missions continue to expand on your knowledge. But Startopia doesn't hold your hand either. In the second mission I mistakenly thought I needed to convert my food into better food via my factory instead of simply storing the food. And that was after I hired all of the dryads I possibly could while trying to figure out how to produce more food.If you can laugh off your mistakes and confusion along the way, there's a deep and sprawling game here to enjoy. Watching hapless aliens live their lives makes you feel like you're making a real difference as you extort their money for your corporate overlords. Did I say you were running Space Disneyland? Space Walmart might have been a better comparison.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: Decided to focus on mech production this time. Got one when the AI attacked me with 3. I was also forced to either make mys security drones blow themselves up or have 50% HP. That's on easy difficulty. Must be fun on higher difficulty levels.RTS wise: it's like Starcraft 2 with only 1 playable race with only 1 combat unit - the Thor. When you fight an enemy, whoever has more mechs will win. Security droids do nothing against mechs so it's just: you have 2, enemy has 3 = you lose. You have 3, enemy has 2 = you win. You have an aqual amount of mechs: usually you win because AI sucks at controling them. If you just pull out low hp mechs and repair them you should be fine. Remember how you could defend in the orginal startopia by hiring 20 workers provided you had enough cash? In this game your regular employees just do nothing and die. It's all down to mechs and nothing else. Only 3 types, melee, mid range, long range. Slow, sluggish, poorly animated. Just uninteresting overall.Sim wise: remember how dungeon 3 FPS dips hard when you pick up 20 creatures and drop them on the dungeon exit? This might be the same engine but as soon as you build up to 3 sectors, there's constantly more than 20 createures on screen. Ryzen 5 3600 + GTX 1060 6GB should not choke on this game yet I've heard even much stronger specs like 1080 Ti are also struggling here. Other than that it's just Startopia so if you really loved the original game, you should give this one a spin. Running a free play scenario with no oponnents is always an option. Though as soon as your base gets large performance will make it almost unplayable. Pathing also sucks. When I've got a full ring base employees kept quiting because they went for a drink to the other end of the station and while walking they got so thirsty that they quit. Room sizes make it impossible to have everything near everything so as your base grows, people will start quitting.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit to note: things are being patched - mostly Quality of Life things for now - but I will write a more comprehensive update when enough has changed to prompt another playthrough. Just highlighting that for now the below still applies, other than some of the pointless clicking has been eliminated through reduction in some activities and options to auto-resolve events and suppress notifications.Original review:There are some minor improvements over Startopia with multi-pickup, factory queues, and modern graphics.With some things your mileage might vary, like the different approach to research (doesn't work for me), resources and needs (it's messy and doesn't land as far as I'm concerned) and the bio deck terraforming (why is this just a dumbed down version of Startopia's system? Worse as far as I'm concerned).There are also serious problems with writing, pace, combat, glitches, and lack of understanding of what was good about the mechanics being cloned, or failing that a clear vision about the direction they were going to take with them this time. It's like Baby's First RTS, plus a bunch of pointless clicking and busywork that get in the way of what could be a solid builder/manager.Played 200 hours in beta, gave feedback about all these things and there was either no will or insufficient resources to make meaningful changes. No amount of UI and graphical polish can make up for it just not being much fun. Go play the original for £5 and have an actually good time - even with the old graphics.But the thing that tipped me into a firm negative is the unatmospheric, lazy, inept, nonsensical failure of a campaign. There isn't even boss fight music, and you have to click 'main menu' to get the entirely non sequitur ending "cinematic" that was animated in an afternoon by the work experience kid.The idea that this was allowed to be released without a total rewrite to at least make it make basic sense is absurd and insulting - all of these things could be fixed by someone with some basic skill and interest in the genre.For £50, it's obscene.Strong avoid.

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to the old Startopia, this game doesn't feel the same. Maybe it's just nostalgia talking but here's my main insights about the game:Pros:- Cutesy artstyle, cartoony and quality animations for just about everything.-Lots of avaible building.-Can decorate things in details.Cons:- Way, way, way too much busywork. The Biodeck barely harvest anything on its own because the Fuzzers only pick up one crate at a time most of the time. Cleaning up after garbage gets old quick.- Long wait time. Especially in early and even mid-game in Freeplay, you're going to WAIT. Wait until you have enough prestige to buy new buildings. Wait until you have enough money to buy anything. Wait until you get the event to clean up garbage or destroy your O2 to get money.- Alien AI is meant to have a lot of differents tastes and wants, but they move very slowly. You have to build multiple elevators for them to move around easily to the fun deck, but even then... After like 3 hours of freeplay in building and unlocking everything the aliens just swarms the discos and disregards almost every single other buildings. So I have just discos upon discos that works half the time because the employees take breaks very often to go eat and tend to their own needs.All in all. It may be more cute than the old Startopia, but it's swamped in busywork and tedious gameplay. You can't design the berth and bars the same way you could with old startopia, and the design of some aliens feels more "safe" and not as imaginative as the old Startopia.All in all, this is buyer's regrets at its peak.Also, VAL is insufferable. Funny quips and condescending comments gets old very, very, very quickly. About the moment you hear the same insulting jab about your thinking process or your slow gameplay twice.Get the old Startopia on GoG.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to recommend this game, but it - funnily enough, needs some more programming.- Trash is out of control. You'll spend the most of your time picking it up and squishing the vermin it attracts by clicking on them, even though I'm not sure if it really does any good. Building a crazy number of garbage cans help.- The worker fuzzies aren't programmed well and frequently stop working without any explanation. One way to help them work a little better is to build extra charging stations, but that isn't a fix all. It seems like they start to glitch when their batteries are low.- The tutorial is SEVERELY lacking. For example, I didn't know that repairs take crates from a factory, so when retrying a level, an hour in I failed the mission because I hadn't built a factory or produced any crates - ran out of energy due to most of my facilities failing at once, and not being able to repair them due to having no crates.- The pop-up events come in two versions - timed ones that pop up on the main screen, and smaller events that come through the message window. The problem is that the message window is really easy to miss.- Mission five glitched out so that after an hour of work, the boss didn't load in, even after reloading a save, making it impossible to win.- Having only ten campaign missions in a game this price isn't acceptable.This game could be great if given some more work. It obviously was released too soon.

_childDocuments_.review: NEWEST REVIEW:Update 1.2 introduced some small but important gameplay and UI tweaks that does enough to turn playing the game from a negative experience to a positive one: You can have fun with this game now as no single aspect of managing the station will now try and dominate your time.The game isn't perfect and it's not the Startopia of old. It completely lacks the wit and humour of the original. But from a gameplay and machcanics standpoint it's now playable and engaging.This is speaking from the perspective of if you enjoy playing long-form "Free Play" sessions where it takes 4-6 hours of play to complete the mission objectives. The single player campaign is fine up to the last final missions where it falls apart.If you want the gameplay experience of a Startopia reimagining then you'll get it. The artistic choices in terms of VO and Audio work is still quite bad though. I suggest you turn "VAL" off and put some of your own music on while you play.OLDER REVIEW:I've played through most of the campaign and played through a long free play game.For many like myself this game is to be compared to the original made back in the early 2000s.It has all the elements in place to be just as good as the original, but some heavy rebalancing of elements would be needed to make this game as enjoyable as the prior iteration in terms of game feel.I stress that if this game interests you. Keep an eye on it over the next upcoming months and let's see if the devs plan to address the balancing issues.It suffers from the following that is unlikely to be fixed:- A lack of wit and humour. The original leaned heavily towards Douglas Adams Hitchhikers guide to the galaxy. There's none of that here and it's replaced by a badly written GlaDOS style humour. Take my advise and turn the sound off for VAL. You're not missing anything.What can be fixed in later updates:The balancing of this game is well out of whack. Some elements are far too hard to control in the games later stage which leads to too much of your time focused on doing things you shouldn't need to. Namely:- Garbage management. In the original the concept was simple: Put bins around your base and garbage is managed. This game tries to over complicate it with bins that walk to recyclers’, bots that pick up trash and even employees that pick up trash. And all of this extra complexity is thrown away because the game can't manage garbage in the late game and can't communicate to you how you can fix it. Creating a very un-fun late stage where you spend 50% of your time collecting trash manually. Horrible. To the devs: You overthought this one. Scale it back and make it manageable. this system at it stands would need to clearly tell the player what they need to do to fix the problem, which it doesn't.Trading: Items you buy are not automatically put into the cargo hold. Why? Why add this extra step of needing fuzzers to carry it? Scale this complexity back.It's kept some things from the orignal game that didn't need to be there. Manually promoting your staff isn't a meaningful choice. You either remember to do it or they quit. That isn't any fun in the orignal game and it didn't need to be here either.Building more fuzzers is too complex for its own good. The game will almost effectively complete before you get the chance to craft what you need to upgrade your fuzzers to the amount and the tech level where they can manage the station well.The UI for this game is needlessly complicated. Combat has its own UI and it's not merited. Building rooms is a chore. Which is a shame because you can save blueprints of building designs which is smart and interesting.Overall:I can't recommend the game at this point due to its flaws with balancing. I really hope the devs care enough about this game to spend the time to rebalance the experience, dial back things that are not fun like waste management and focus on the aspects of the game that is fun like room design, layout optimisation and exploiting trade and manufacturing.My fingers are crossed for a rebalancing. This game can be fun with what it has in systems and assets. It just needs more work.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. Many people wanted a perfect Clone of Startopia, this game is not that. It has many resemblences to Startopia, while still having enough differences to feel different and that is ok.It is a decent game that deserves a chance. Best is tough that you watch a letsplay from someone you trust to decide if you want it.The Good.-C.R.A.T.E.S still exist and have been expanded. Some can even be used to grant buffs, such as faster workers, recharging bots etc. Otherwise its the same Food, Med, building crates like in Startopia.-The Stations are round and you got the 3 decks. (Inner, Entertainment and the Garden)-The early levels are pretty similiar to the 1st few Startopia levels. (level 1 collect Garbage and so forth)- You open a Door and the rooms are filled with Garbage, Vermin and Monsters.-Specific Aliens work in specific Buildings.-The 3rd Deck Gardening can be edited. You get more biomes now then in the Original Startopia.-Controls are almost the same with the exception of Hotkeys.-The Buildings are similiar to Startopia but got different names.-Diseases are dangerous unlike in startopia. If someone gets sick adn they decide they rather go to the Disco then the Doctor expect the Med bays to be overcrowded soon, tough it is a great money maker.-You can build Giant Mechs, they need space to navigate tough.-More research options, great for people like me who like games with research.The Bad and the Ugly-The Voice AI that assists you somehow does not feel like it belongs in the game. Could just be me tough.-The jokes early one are bad, they get kind of better later, but never reach Startopia levels of humour.-In Startopia Aliens in the Disco had awesome Dance moves, now we got Greys who twerk.-Startopia Disco music is great, here the Music is also Good it is more of techno style, still good tough.-The art style. Dont get me wrong it is ok. However Startopia got that Crisp Cartoon look this has got more of a.. I really do not know what to call it. Maybe "blobbish Cartoon Style" Look at screenshots from both games and you see what I mean.-The Music is Ok, a few songs etc really go well in the game, the others dio not.-In Startopia when you open a bulkhead door you hear that loud whirrling of gears and the sound of Air hissing as it fills the room. Here they open but they do not have that Audio that makes it feel like you are opening a massive door. It is not very impressive.

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, I found it more annoying than entertaining.The phrase "We were on the verge of greatness. We were this close." comes to mind. You can tell it's obviously made by people who loved or at least understood the old Startopia, which is more than I can say about other companies' attempts to replicate something, and it obviously did a lot of things right too... but...1. The UI seems to have this annoying habit of ignoring clicks. Like, it might literally take more than one click to get it to acknowledge that, yes, ffs, I really do want to switch from placing doors to placing beds, when I'm designing a berth. I don't know if it's my frame rate being too low to register brief clicks (I only have a RTX 2080 TI, after all;)) or I'm possibly dragging a bit when I click or what, but it's the only game doing that and it's annoying.2. Conversely, the UI lets you click right through dialogs. Like, let's say I'm designing a berth, I have a bed selected, and one of those timed events shows up where I must choose one bonus or another. Clicks to open it up and pick a choice will literally also place a bed, if it's within the berth blueprint. Or let's say the AI assistant started ranting at you again, and you want to click the little arrow to shut it up. Yep, same thing happens. Processing the click didn't stop when it hit the dialog, but basically continued straight through.At times, I find it easier to just cancel whatever room I'm designing or decorations I'm placing, and deal with those dialogs, then restart.3. Which, combined with the fact that I can't pause the game while designing someting, to avoid such interruptions, is really annoying AF.4. The fact that something as basic as being able to buy more worker robots is basically up to whether it was randomly available in the "VAL shop" at the moment. I might have to literally click that one every 2 minutes, and still get none. Imagine if you were playing Warcraft (the RTS, not "world of") and it was random if you can buy a peon right now or not. In some missions where you might need to do them in a fixed time for an achievement, so basically it's up to some dice rolls if that achievement's physically possible to do or not. Yeah, that's the experience here.5. The chatty robot assistant. Look, a snarky AI assistant who seems to exist just to insult you may even be funny the first time around. Now imagine playing the same mission half a dozen times because you want to get an achievement. Yeah, the experience is like being at a party and some drunk guy follows you around to tell you the same dad jokes half a dozen times. Better yet, if they weren't even as much jokes as some 'funny' way to insult you. And they're not even witty retorts or comments on the current situation, but lines that he memorized from somewhere else and is regurgitating verbatim, whether they fit or not, over and over and over again.I swear to the elder gods, a couple of times I actually found myself shouting "SHUT UP! JUST <bleep>ING SHUT UP ALREADY!" at the screen.6. But it's actually worse, because the game ranting and raving for minutes in a row is drowning actually useful information. I've watched even youtubers who play games as their day job, still miss important information, like that some crate is available, because it was buried in a 2-minute long lame attempt at the game doing a stand-up comedy audience take-down routine.Look, devs... the purpose of a UI -- whether it includes basically a glorified text-to-speech option or not -- is to make it EASIER to get the important information, not to drown it in a 2-minute long rant about how obviously you're too stupid to understand that you need to place the berth first.7. The pointless distractions like clicking space cockroaches (kind of like shooting the mice in Hospital Tycoon) to get rid of them before they infect everyone. I can understand why someone thought it would be a great gameplay addition to have something more for the player to do, but that is negated by its being repetitive and pointless. Those cockroaches will respawn in seconds, for example. It's literally easier and saner to just let them be, and just live with everyone taking trips to the doctor often.8. The camera... oh dear. Now I kind of understand why you can't scroll out too far without going through a ceiling or bulkhead, when you're inside a space station, so I'll give this the lowest priority. But... really, it's the only city builder kind of game in recent history, where I have to wrestle the camera (and I really mean wrestle) just to place some building.9. ... and at times moving the camera gives me a slight case of nausea. Which I don't remember getting in any other game. Not sure if it's the curved space or some blur they do or what, but yeah.10. Remember that talk about how I get interrupted while I'm trying to design a berth? Yeah, that's also because I get to design the same one over and over and over again every time. The game basically does let you "save" a design, but it's pretty much just a way to duplicate a room. (Which, granted, is already more than other games often.) You can only have one custom design per room type, and it isn't "saved" in any meaningful sense of the word. In the next mission, or even if you restart the current one, it's gone. So I have to recreate the same design I found to work well, every single mission. While wrestling the camera again, and being interrupted all over again.

_childDocuments_.review: Its basically a startopia with some updated graphics, modification of the combat system (In the old game, you put down static turrets and hired 4 types of aliens to serve as grunts, while in this one your security stations put out at max 8 drones plus a large mech unit to fight), some of the AI Stuff is a bit messed up (One major complaint on my end is the fact that Discos will have all their DJs quit at the same time effectively shutting down the berth), some bad tutorials (Most noticeable for me was figuring out what a "Hate Preacher" was and I just started ejecting any monks who did a red glowly thing on the fun deck).Its a bit too late, but I think they should've made the basic hygiene station (Which is part of a Berth) its own separate building or plannable room. Maybe let us set the prices on stuff.All in all, its a serviceable 'sequel' or whatever the word is. I do want to punt the AI Voice into space though, they're going GLaDOS or SHODAN on us, I can feel it.All in all, wait for a discount or for Kalypso to finish polishing it. 9/10 their games turn out pretty good after a short time, so I have faith they'll take any criticisms and patch it up

_childDocuments_.review: "Spacebase Startopia captivates with its original mixture of economic simulation and empire building strategy paired with classic RTS skirmishes and a good dose of humor."Translation: Starbase Startopia took a beautiful if old game and turned it into some kind of gimmick which doesn't have any of the charm or polish of the original. As for the humor, I suppose if you find an annoying robot telling you how much you suck whenever you do something right funny then you'll be rolling around the floor in no time. Personally I find the constant litany of insults just irritating. Asked for a refund, the original had it's faults but it was 10xs better than this turd with glitter sprinkled all over it.

_childDocuments_.review: Its hard not to play this without the rose tinted goggled of nostalgia and I guess its "okay" as a builder game, feels more like something you would play on a mobile phone rather than PC, certainly NOT worth the £40 price tag (Get it cheap from a KEY site)The lack of information when navigating can sometimes be infuriating, its almost like they knew fans of the first game would be playing so didn't bother telling anyone else what the buttons do.At 19 odd hours I've just completed the campaign and while I did enjoy some of it I cant really see why I would go back to it unless it received more missions and updates and a lot more tweaks to make it user friendly.Every mission can basically be won by building the barebones basics, getting the research lab unlocked and then AFK researching stuff until your so OP nothing else matters so not really a challenge, the last mission I just built 4 Security Stations with Mechs and steamrolled the whole thingOverall its "Cute" and I am glad I tried it but it just feels unfinished and lackluster which is a shame, people had high expectations and like a lot of games nowadays they were not deliveredProsNice style of graphics, aliens and buildings look good"okay" builder gameMakes you want to play the originalConsLack of Information on what things doVAL's voice is just terrible on anything other than the GlaDos clone and even that gets tediousOld VAL was smart, witty with dry humour, new VAL is just a D-bagNot much to do once you've finished the storyAI can be really stupid and take the most indirect routes or just stop moving entirelyYou can just sit in one area clicking build materials > promote staff > research > trade over and over and over and over until you winWhere are the tunes???No real challengePlot twist?? No its not, developers just copied Portal

_childDocuments_.review: Its pretty good y'all. I played/loved the original Startopia and still do on occasion because it holds up. Spacebase Startopia basically updates the original with different names and a few additional options. If I could I'd advocate for making the game a bit more complex than it is- the overall structure doesnt feel any different from the original but its a faithful remake/tribute. This would be a fine starting point for anyone new to the game and I'm really hoping that we can make a more sophisticated Spacebase Startopia 2 at some point in the future that takes things further and innovates some more. Glad the game got made- I'm truly enjoying playing it. Perhaps add a 4th deck in a new one sometime or make the aliens more detailed in their needs. Add crew quarters so there can be more of a relationship to your "employees" vs. tourists. idk. Good work. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Game is really impressive when it comes to visuals, animations, music and overall theme is well realized.It pains to see how this potential was not utilized. The main problem with the game is inbalanced progression  system, you can unlock everything on highest difficulty in like 3-4 hours. _childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really, really want to like this game. I want to LOVE this game, but unfortunately I don't. I find it... I don't know, disappointing, I suppose? More than that, it's a major let down. I loved the original Startopia game, I've sunk hundreds of hours into it, most of them prior to buying it on Steam. It's charming, and extremely replayable.This, however, is not. The biggest problem, IMO, is the writing, and the various voices behind VAL. VAL was the charm of the original game, as well as Arona Dahl. I only just got past the 'simulation' phase of the main game, so perhaps things liven up after that, but VAL definitely won't. All the voices sound dull and emotionless, a stark contrast to the humor and sarcasm of the original VAL. That VAL carried the game, while this one brings it down. It's not about the gender of the voice, for anyone worried about that. The original VAL had charisma, had a way with words, had inflection. This one sounds like, well, a robot. Even the 'male' voice is boring and not worth listening to. I'm half tempted to turn off VAL's voice and try and imagine their words spoken in a much more lively tone of voice.They really dropped the ball on the voice acting (or computer voice simulation), something that should have been one of the focal points of the game.I also find that they don't give me enough exposition about the base and the various aliens. Instead I find that VAL insults the player A LOT, and not much else. There's no real humor. The original Startopia was heavily inspired by Terry Pratchett (Cut Me Own Throat Dahl, anyone?) and Douglas Adams, this one has no inspiration behind it at all, except a sad attempt to copy and old, amazing game.Give the game a fresh coat of dialogue and a new voice actor/actress/charming computer voice simulation, I will definitely change my review in the future. But right now I can't recommend this to anyone, and that really makes me sad. I was waiting for this to come out for months, and now I'm just... filled with regret for something that could have been great.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: Full of nostalgia goodness, makes me feel 16 again! Id really firstly like to commend the Kalypso team, there has been some initial issues and bugs (Ive personally been helping test hotfixes) and theyve been squashing the bugs one after another (something youll be doing in game). So to a review. The game recreates the original pretty well, in addition to adding many features. It does have a little less scifi monty pythonesque references, and is replaced with a very sarcastic computer named Val. Some people have been hating on her, but I find it rather funny. The tutorial could use a little work as there are a few things that arent explained effectively, but anyone with half a brain will figure it out. The campaign is on the short side, which I do find a little lacking as the original was after all single player campaign and story driven. It also goes by rather quickly, but I think its fully serviceable. I find myself just using the room blueprints, as the items in them are never really gone over. Multiplayer I havent had a chance to play, but I could see it being fun and competitive.Graphics are all top notch, well polished with enough cheese left on to make it a true successor to the original. Sound effects are awesome, music is top notch and fitting.Games is getting ♥♥♥♥ on a little, and I dont think it is totally deserved. I would say have an open mind and give it a shot. I for one am loving it.

_childDocuments_.review: First let me make clear that I didn't try the campaign yet. I've always been into free play, so that's what I'm talking about here.In my opinion this is pretty much like old Startopia. I was actually surprised how similar it played, despite the looks. Of course people tend to focus on different aspects of the game, so your mileage may vary. Some things have been simplified a bit, but you still face the same problems and a lot of micromanagement as it was back in the days. And let's not forget that original Startopia made you do very annoying things... remember the terror of employee promotion? You browse the list for all aliens ripe for promotion, then you must select each of them individually (!) and each time the camera moves through the whole station to that guy, zooms in on him, he looks at you full of expectation, then you can finally click the promote button. Repeat that 20 times, knowing you'll have to do it again very soon.Now you browse the list for any (!) alien ripe for promotion, click and hold the button - all open promotions done at once! No zooming.Another thing I like is that you can choose complete rooms to be built without the need to first draw the walls, then add all the functional stuff etc. (which is still possible).However, there are more debatable changes - or things that rather should have changed - but I don't really have strong feelings towards any of those.If you're up for some beginner advice, here you are:Garbage handling is crucial! Get a recycler as soon as possible! Be aware that your garbage bins and cleaning fuzzies are useless without it! If there's no recycler both have no place to unload so they don't do anything. So until you have that infrastructure up and running focus on cleaning the station manually (until that point you won't have anything more important to do anyway). And if you see a bug, squash it.Disable automatic mode for all your fuzzies right from the start. The only way to keep track of your fuzzy performance is to know how many you have of each kind. If you leave them on auto they constantly change roles according to open tasks. This may sound reasonable, but I don't think it works very well (algorithms, you know...). You want to have sufficient robot power on standby for repairs at any time - the more buildings you have, the more important it becomes! Otherwise you may loose a building because you get a starquake just when everybody is busy hauling crates they couldn't even store because your warehouse is nearly full... Next most important thing is garbage disposal. If you see that your cleaning fuzzies leave too much junk behind, clean up the mess yourself and deploy more dedicated cleaning fuzzies until it balances out, then focus on something else. Crates are lower priority as you can quickly help with that manually. While we're at it: watch out for nuclear waste! As it comes in crates, cleaning fuzzies don't touch it. Only crate fuzzies will, so until you have enough of them you better make it a habit to collect those crates manually. Also: the only way to get rid of nuclear waste is to transform it in a factory and then recycle the product, and as you can't automate these steps anyway it's not a bad thing to have the waste in your inventory.Don't neglect general security! When you build a security station you get 4 security drones that detect and arrest criminals, but you want more. Many more, and you probably don't want to build that many security stations. A good solution is to buy them! I found that you can buy and deploy security drones before you even have a security station, and they work perfectly on their own. Frequently look at the trade offers and grab drones, they're quite affordable!About employees: check how many workplaces a building has, then hire more than that (about twice as much I'd say). Especially low-skilled employees spend a lot of time outside their workplace and you don't want people queueing up at your med bay because all the greys are chilling on the bio deck.Let's leave it at that. My overall verdict? It's a definitive "Why not?"

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this with some qualifiers. The short and sweet version is that this remake has a lot of flaws, but  can be fully enjoyable for newcomers and oldtimers alike, provided you temper your expectations somewhat. The latter group should also not be aggressively allergic to any changes to the source, because if that kinda thing makes you mad, the game will start rustling your jimmies 5 minutes into the first Tutorial.Onto a more detailed look:The original Startopia is a decades old game about managing a space station. You put down rooms where Aliens can fulfill their needs, trying to expand and turn a profit as more and more visitors come aboard. The game had some very basic combat as well, but achieved most of it's charm via missions that challenged you in different ways, and a witty sense of humour in the form of character interactions, and just watching your meeples be weird as they went about their daylie lifes.This new version does basically all of this, with some different spices. Some of it works, some of it does not. Strictly speaking I'd just tell anyone who doesn't massage their nipples to modern graphics to just play the old game. it's cheaper, on steam, and fairly stable (If not very resolution friendly) even on modern systems. But there is just enough here that you might still prefer this version.The good are a variety of Quality of Life changes, and obviously, the graphics. The game looks nice, has a range of charming animations, and although I feel like the races don't quite have the same weird appeal versus the older ones, watching your station get busy is still satisfying. You no longer have to click things you want to beam up individually, there is a race overview screen to help out with new hires and promotions (And getting an idea of problems that are present) and the new Biodeck not only looks really nice, it is now possible to harvest materials without half your farmers quitting every second week.The new research and combat will be up to taste. I prefer the former just for ease of use. The old research involved way too much waiting for certain techs, unless you were willing to splurge absurdly for multiple laboraties. The new one ties directly into your station happiness, with happy residents providing a currency used for unlocks. Each unlock also gives you some cash, which cuts down on the absurd amount of "waiting for cash inflow" the old game sometimes suffered from.The combat is a straight neutral for me. You now use bots to fight, instead of hiring 40 Aliens to do it for you. It cuts down on having to throw the 40 resulting corpses into the recycler afterwards, but there is still no strategy to it. Build a Mech or two, send them to the thing that needs killing, wait for completion. The bad is general congestion, the humour, and the games obsession with never shutting the fu*k up. Aliens seem a bit worse at getting their needs fulfilled. You can cut down on this by just overproviding rooms, but it's a tad annoying especially early on. Tubes in particular seem like a completely unnecessary addition. In the old game, they were present in each segment and had infinite capacity. Now elevators only send 1 peep at a time, including your bots. The fact that they have to line up across levels will infuriate you early on, until you learn to account for it from the start.The humour and "too much noise" tie into each other. VAL is breathtakingly unfunny and basically only has 1 joke, namely that you are bad at your job and slow and stupid. Every other review mentions this already, so I won't dwell on it: Turn VAL off, or at least make sure to turn down notifications. As for the noise: Learn to ignore it. The game will whine about stuff way before it is an issue, and you are completely free to take it slow most of the time. For some advice: You always need one berth more than you think you need. Plonk down food and hygiene services on the fun deck to cut down on elevator use. Always have at least 2 security stations. You generally need about 2 aliens per work slot to ensure they are manned sufficiently. Remember you can recycle crates for energy, and also make sure you terraform your biodeck to provide a bit of everything. If you feel like you are going to slow, build more airdocks.Overall, it's "okay" ranging to "meh". I got it on a sale for 10 bucks and for that it's about as much as you'd expect.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: The complete lack of communication on the developers' part makes buying this game inadvisable, in 2021. If you are intrigued by the concept, buy the original instead. I am a massive fan of the original Startopia, and I've probably put many hundreds more hours into that game from the time when I owned it on disk back in 2001 than are reflected in my Steam library. So, like many reviewers, I have a strong nostalgic attachment to the original, and in many ways Spacebase Startopia doesn't quite live up to that experience--even though it comes close in many respects.TL:DR: This is a solid management game with some RTS components that make it novel. If you like War for the Overworld or Two Point Hospital (or Dungeon Keeper 2 or Theme Hospital), you'll probably like this, too. If you're looking for a straight-up 2021 version of 2001's Startopia, you get that but with a substantial shift in tone.The original Startopia had humor based largely in the work of Douglas Adams. Your AI assistant, VAL, was dry and often critical, but never outright hostile to you, the player. The other major character, the trader Arona, was always trying to con you, but at least you know where you stood with him. There was a careful balance between optimism and cynicism in Startopia. This game is markedly different in tone, with the new version of VAL being much more aligned with GLaDOS from Portal--she roots for you to fail, a joke that quickly loses its novelty after the fourth or fifth jab, let alone the thirtieth or fortieth. It wouldn't be so bad if she weren't the only voiced character to interact with.The tool-tips have also largely lost the flavor they had in the Mucky Foot version; I appreciate being down-to-business, but it just makes the world feel more bland. The cultural references here feel forced somewhat more towards gamer culture--such as with the loot box lottery building--or towards pop culture in general with the cat cafe. It's clear that this game is mean to appeal to more than just SciFi fans, but it seems like a better balance could have been struck.Other than this lore issue, though, the gameplay itself is much improved over the original. (With the exception of trash, which seems to increase at a rate far beyond the player's realistic ability to keep up, over a certain population.) Research is better and more intuitive--rooms are unlocked through prestige and meeting certain milestones, and are *improved* through the lab, which means you can get all of the basic infrastructure well before you have scientists. Manufacturing is more interesting because resources are required to produce items now--though that does also make getting a sufficient level of robots harder. On that note, you don't get access to traders of any kind until very late into the tech tree compared to Startopia, and Arona is no longer around, so you're limited to what you can make and random items you can purchase for prestige from VAL.This is a solid game that struggles to live up to its legacy. I'm still finding it enjoyable even if it's not quite so revolutionary as it felt 20 years ago.

_childDocuments_.review: I was so excited for this having played the original over and over again to this day hundreds of times since release. It was always so relaxing and each level unique and full of just enough challenge to keep you in love with it's quaint simplicity.So even though this is (for now) a negative review thank you so much for breathing life back in to one of my all time favourite digital masterpieces. I'm just a little bit sore about how you've massacred this.. I think i'm about to attempt the last level of this new one but my Gods I honestly don't know if I can be bothered..Let me say first what this successor does well..1. It provides many more rooms than before  almost to the point it's a little overwhelming but glad to see such diversity. Even if they are just three+ different versions of the same buildings... fundeck *cough*2. It uh... Well I guess the graphics are fairly pleasant.3. It does feel like it has a lot more potential that 'could' be fixed.4. It loosely appeals to original fans.5. That's it..So what's wrong?1. Each level see's you building a base from scratch and the research levels set to zero. You don't get handed any rooms apart from one or two to help get started but if the theme of the level is trading well guess what? You gotta spend an hour or so building the exact same base you've already built a half dozen times before you get to the stage you can get a trade station which is the only new addition to this whole level, you then just have to fill one very short set of easily achieved trade objectives and that's it. Done. There's never any scenario specific buildings given to you to get the mission off to a nice start. It's the most shallow, boring excuse for a scenario theme and then you know you're gonna have to do the same next level with just a couple more buildings and lose shoe-horned reasons for them.2. Each level is a hint towards the levels of the original and almost copies their scenario theme in linearity so you kind of know what sort of 'story' theme you're gonna get for each level if you've played the original. However this is carried out atrociously because apart from an ever so slight change of winning conditions, nothing about the levels are different.. There might be the odd small surprise but they're so obvious that it's not a surprise at all. This game is just a chore rebuilding with no variation of reason other than cause VAL said so.3. VAL is replaced by three new voices which you can chose  between however VAL is the most unfunny, cringe, and annoying part of the whole game. She just constantly berates the player to the point you want to drive toothpicks in your ears because it is so boring and difficult to sit through. Seriously just mute her voice and read the subtitles. Not once has this entire game made me smile. Val in the original was tongue in cheek and made you smirk quite a few times. This is just.. awful and tacky.4. It is awful. Build something? Garbage appears. Build bins? Garbage piles up anywhere but the bins. More random litter? Scuzzers can never keep up, vermin spawn, everyone gets sick. This game may as well be called litter pick simulator 'cause in longer games it just gets out of control real fast even if you use these ridiculous cheat crates which clear up litter, sickness, or peoples mood in their AOE. Just... What? No thank you. Fix the damn garbage!!4 b) Having to supply oxygen filters and power relays everywhere.. really? You just didn't want this game to be fun at all did you RealmForge / Kalypso?5. Berths now contain basic sleeping pods, food, drink, and hygiene with no bins! Oh do you see where this is going??? And no social distancing means all your aliens get sick cause the berths are so full of people who should be going to sickbay but they don't they just wander everywhere else possible first! Seems a little too realistic actually.. Fair play.6. Alien designs are lame. Lose representations of the originals but nothing compares to Kasvagorians and Sirens. 7. Doesn't matter how many staff you hire it's never enough. Doesn't matter how much entertainment facilities you build, they're never enough. Doesn't matter what you do in this game, it will never be good enough. LITTER *cough* Staff happiness as well.. FUUUUUUUU !!!8. Combat.. You need to build security stations to house droids and a mech but you have to build the whole station with the width of mechs walking in mind. It is a damn chore! the system is boring and ridiculous. I once had 5 mechs get wiped out by 1 because their path-finding in enemy territory got slightly messed up. 9. The Biodeck is now just a mess, too many biomes, never enough Dryads to harvest plants fast enough. Temples seem pretty pointless too.10.  (Final thoughts) There's just very little fun or relaxation to be had. It's a chore to play and little things like not being able to zoom away from the station or staff becoming just numbers rather than troops to look after. Most aliens just walk through walls rather than doorways. Even the fact a lot of rooms pump out radioactive waste that takes so much room and time in your factories to deal with. As well as constantly having to research everything over again or build crates with existing resources.. It's all just far too much micro-managment and no fun.Please, please fix this game. It has so much potential for some DLC or patch updates but right now I'd be upset to have paid £20 for this.. My partner bought this for me at full price.. Ouch :/ :(

_childDocuments_.review: On the main menu screen, you’ll find Single and Multiplayer options. Choosing Single Player, you’ll find the games Campaign mode where you’ll have various objectives to complete as you complete the games story. Free Play game mode and the games Tutorial can be found under Single Player. You are also able to Jump to a Campaign Level or Load a previous game from here also. Selecting Multiplayer mode, you’ll have three options to choose from, Quick Game, Campaign and Free Play. Also here is Lobby where you can connect to others through Matchmaking or Join a game using a Game ID code. I haven’t tried any of the multiplayer game modes, I have only played the single player campaign and free play game modes currently.   I went through the tutorial to familiarise myself with how the game mechanic's work. There are five sections of the tutorial you’ll go over to learn how the game is played. After which I chose to play the single player campaign, the first campaign is the Garbage Empire. At the start of each campaign level there’s some information and the goals of the level which are read to you by Val, the AI who’ll help you throughout the game. There is also some information on Achievements which can be unlocked upon completing various goals along with New Rooms and Life Rooms which you’ll have use of.    The Garbage Empire starts you off with only one deck to ease you into the game. You will soon have to deal with three decks in your Startopia base but for now you only have to be concerned with, the Sub Deck. The Sub Deck contains the rooms which you’ll need for survival. The other two decks are the Fun Deck where your visitors can let their hair down, boogie on down in the space disco or for those thrill seekers take the Black Hole Drop. The final deck is the Bio Deck, this provides a home to the Dryads along with providing resources such as minerals, food and medicines.   Keeping your base clean is a must, garbage littered everywhere not only makes your base look and smell disgusting but it’s also going to attract vermin. To help you keep the place clean you can assign some Fuzzies but you’ll need somewhere to get rid of all the rubbish. Luckily you can build a Recycling Station to deal with all the garbage your visitors create, it will also transform the garbage into energy.   A clean and happy station means happy visitors however, it’ll take more than just a mop and bucket to keep the station ticking over nicely. You can create Berths where visitors can sleep, eat and drink and generally take care of themselves. Communication Centre will allow your visitors to communicate with the far reaches of the universe. Medical Stations will help take care of the sick and diseased and you don’t want them wandering around infecting others as that’ll just put a dampener on everyone’s day. The aliens spend energy while onboard your station, once they have spent all of the energy they’ll leave, hopefully they’ll have been pleased with your station.   Fuzzies your work droids will take care of any construction, cleaning and collecting of resources for you although you can manually do these as well. However, for the day to day running of the station's communications, recycling, medical stations etcetera, you have various alien species which perform certain jobs rather well. The Gresulurians work in the medical station, the Dryads work in the Bio Deck who not only live there but take care of the fauna and resources on that deck. The Telgor work in the recycling station and the Bugrathorians work in the communications station. These are a few to name, you’ll have to hire each of the races to work in their various fields. You’ll have to keep them happy in their work otherwise they’ll quit their jobs and that could cause problems.   Each deck is divided into a number of sections forming a donut shape with each having a bulkhead between them. You can unlock a bulkhead for an amount of energy, this will then give you more room to expand into. As your stations grows, you’ll have to deal with things like garbage bombs being planted, pirates invading your station, although sometimes they do ask politely if they can cause some trouble on the Fun Deck.    You can find out how well your station is performing by checking the Stations Rankings. Here you’ll find how each of the alien species feel about your base, their Satisfaction, Mood and their comments on the social media, SpaceSpitter. You can also find out if there are any problems the visitors are currently facing such as poor air quality and Val might be able to help sort the problem. Upon completing a successful campaign level your victory screen will detail your statistics, Game Duration, Number of Happy Visitors, Attractiveness (Min/Max) along with a whole bunch more statistics.              In the settings there’s options for Graphics (Resolution, Display Mode, V-Sync, Shadow Quality, Ambient Occlusion, Depth of View, Bloom and Station Rotation), Text & Audio (Main, Effects, Music and Dialog Volume Sliders, Text and Audio Language and Val Voice) and Controls (Scroll Speed, Camera Rotation Speed, Standard Camera Angle, Invert Y-Axis, Invert X-Axis, Orbital Camera, Vacuum Cleaner (Continuous), Additional Information, Creating Variable Rooms and Give Preference to Required Objects).  I’ve enjoyed playing Spacebase Startopia so far, I never played the original. I had played the beta version of the game although I did get a little bit stuck and it seems that it was a bug. However, upon playing the game on release I never had the problem happen again. I haven’t noticed any bugs so far on the fully released game as of yet. I have also only played the single player campaign (ten campaign levels) and the free play game modes. I like the graphics and the game runs smooth; however, I found the camera angles a little frustrating at times especially if I moved my cursor over the edge of the screen without realising. The one thing I did have some trouble with places crate down and trying to open them. I’d keep getting pick up and open wrong on my mouse when trying to use a crate, this could just be me though being useless (I know I agree with you I don’t think it’s that either).  Positives  +  Multiple game modes +  Nice graphics + Full controller support  + Steam achievements  + Has cards  + Steam cloud Negatives - Frustrating at times - Camera angles Create your perfect spacebase getaway for visiting aliens, create jobs, cure the infected, dance the night away, deal with pirates and more as Commander of the Spacebase Startopia. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: The original Startopia is one of my all time favourites. Played trough it multiple times over the last 20 years. Spacebase Startopia is a decent "copy" but it's obviously simplified compared to the original. But to be fair it is not as bad like with other "successors".  Graphics are decent but to colorful. The humor is sometimes  a bit off but it has its peaks. Controls work fine but i would prefer if the forward and backward movement would just move the camera just like in the original, instead of adjusting the camera height in addition.Yes, the (in my case German) narrators (2 female, 1 male) are weird but they'll do the job.Played 3 hours by now without any crashes. Performance is flawless but i encountered a few minor bugs like suspending music or sound effects. Overall i think it is a nice game as far as i can tell by now. What bothers me most is the price of 50€. Steam fees aside, that is way too much for the included content imho. And i guess there will be paied DLCs in the near future.Overall i would recommend Spacebase Startopia to anyone that likes the setting or enjoyed the original game from 2001 but don't expect it to be the better game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very rare thing that I talk badly or do negative reviews about anything, But I just need to say how it is and how I feel about the game. First of all I played the original Startopia for the second time only a year ago. And I loved playing that game from the first mission to the last. But Starbase Startopia is painful to play. As of this writing I'm on mission 4. I don't know if I will ever finish the game at this point. I feel like the positive reviews about the game are written by panicking employees trying to get paid. Secondly this is just a trend from Kalypso Media where their game releases keep getting worse. The game is just all over the place and there is no improvement on the first game in any way. it's even a step backwards when it comes to the interface. they did improve the camera from the early access. The paid early access was just to show how insecure they are about making the game, as they had the golden blueprint for the game in the original Startopia which is one of the greatest game I ever played. I do want to love this game because the first game was so good. but I can't. I regret every dollar I spent on this trash.Kalypso needs to get their act together as the new Tropico game was a total disappointment for me as well. They are so close to making good games but they keep missing the mark.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: If your on the fence about whether or not to pick up this game, watch some lets play clips on YT would be my best advice. You'll quickly get an idea of what to expect and whether or not the game is for you.I'm enjoying the game, its...exactly what it looks like, a management sim with plenty of player interaction, some combat and bright, vibrant and cute graphics.Navigating the UI isn't as clean and simple as it could be, but other than that it's a pick up and play friendly game to all sorts of people, including those who don't normally play management sim style games due to the complexity.That said I think there is enough depth that some seriously cutthroat multiplayer matches would be possible.I never played the original, so I don't have any nostalgia pangs modifying my views of this game, one way or another.The humour, well it feels like it's ten years old and would've been hilarious back when games like Portal were all the rage.It makes me chuckle, but I'm old (like the devs I assume) and relate to that era of gaming.Lots of others find the humour grating and are quite upset that the AI assistant routinely insults you and isn't a mega-busty waifu type character that is head over heels in love with the player.The game has clearly been made with some passion and love, particularly the animations, zoom in on the disco, you can just tell people had fun animating the dance moves of the assorted aliens.It's not a perfect game, there are a couple of bugs and it's also not an earth shattering 4th wall breaking masterpiece, but for what it is I'm enjoying it.The biggest negative for me, that I think will hurt the game, is it's price. It's clearly not a small budget game, the animation and visual quality alone would've been costly production, but it's Steam store price is quite high, especially when it boasts a neat multiplayer function yet no bundle purchase.High prices seems to be a continuing issue with the big publisher houses of old such as Slitherine or Kalypso, who still make good games but haven't yet realised that they were overtaken by EA and Blizzard and need to wind back the prices a tad.Luckily an easy way to get %30 off, is to buy it from the Kalypso website and sign up to the mailing list, which brings the price down to a much more reasonable $30-40 depending on your currency.With a discounted price, either through Steam sales or the Kalypso website, I wholeheartedly recommend the game if it looks appealing to you.The visuals are fantastic, its a lot of fun to zoom in and watch the aliens and critters walk around, pet cats or throw tantrums and hashtag about how my station is full of garbage.The gameplay is accessible to a wide audience, including more casual players who don't have the time, patience or interest in more detailed management sims.

_childDocuments_.review: So I loved the original, and I love this one, which makes sense, because the two are incredibly similar games. Anybody that is making complaints about it not being the same is absolutely bonkers, because if anything it's too similar. And why not, the original Startopia is one of my top games of all time, it was truly excellent.I love the addition of the mechs as well, and all the new designs are phenomenal and adorable. Overall it's a beautiful game and very engaging, with a lot of user friendliness upgrades from the original.My one complaint is pacing. Everything is too fast, the tutorials, everything. PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE turn down the rate of these random concern messages that absolutely require my attention. Is it that I'm playing on highest difficulty? At first it was fine, it wasn't too much, but by the time I get to the later missions, I simply have too much to do to be constantly saying no thank you pirates, I don't want you to climb aboard and ransack my space station, or to go yet again beam up bombs off the fun deck. I have no time to micromanage, to check if my potential hire is a criminal, to make a plan with my current resources to upgrade my fuzzies, to go put cute little plant pots in high traffic areas, to figure out why EVERYONES SO MAD ALL THE TIME. It's honestly stressful, which is the last thing you want a sim game to be. I haven't even had time to check if the aliens will wave at you when you click on them, it didn't occur to me till just now that I hadn't done that, but I literally have just not had a spare second to just sit with these cute lil guys.Am I just old, and the new generation is too distractible? I'm pretty sure I'm right and that it's overtuned. The game keeps telling me I should do things I have absolutely no time to do. Find 8 hate preachers? I didn't even find one before the mission was over.I only mention this because I'm hoping it can be changed by the developers, still recommending the game, love it, will be spending many more hours playing it, regardless!Edit: Holy crap, I just got to the first mission you actually need to do any combat and there is this game breaking bug where every time I go into a breached sector it just closes without warning and destroys any of my units past the wall, what is happening... Please fix this??

_childDocuments_.review: First off, let me say that I played this game on a M1 macbook and it took me a while to figure out how to even get the game to run (it will fail if u try to launch from Steam, so you need to launch it manually). Now on to the review:TLDR: Not as good as the original and confused about who the audience should be (children or adults). Still a decent game, just not as nostalgic as I hoped it would be - Starting by the elephant in the room: VAL's voice.  It is the most generic and bland voice I have ever heard, it almost puts you to sleep. Where is the sarcastic, condescending and yet endearing voice from the original Startopia game? Even if I switch to the "budget GLaDOS" voice, it's still not that great. - The races/droids have all been renamed to more whimsical sounding names probably to appeal to 8 year olds, e.g "Scuzzer" droids renamed to "Fuzzy" or Siren "brothels" have been replaced with cat cafes... wtf?!- In contrast to the above, the gameplay is still probably more suited for adults, since the micro/macro management is probably difficult for an 8 year old. So you end with a game that is annoying to look/hear for adults, but too complicated for children to play. Make your mind up, you can't have your (nostalgic) cake and eat it too!- Graphics are alright, if not a bit too detailed. I'm not sure if it was due to lack of graphics power or a design choice, but the simpler designs of the original, meant it was faster to distinguish and identify races/buildings/objects.- The music is alright, but I still prefer the original game's soundtrack.There's probably more things to like/dislike about this game, but I'll leave it at that. Regardless of my initial feelings, this is still a decent game and a great homage to the original, so I appreciate the work the developers did to bring back this iconic game.

_childDocuments_.review: Basically, the game is not intuitive.  There are many new concepts being thrown at you quickly and are barely glossed over in instruction.  The machine is there, but the levers are missing...  The spacing is wonky.  You mean to click this, but you click that and then you right click when you were supposed to left click.  Everything was sardines with miss-clicking menus.  I can immediately see why the reviews are meh whilst the foundation of the game is incredibly fun.  The original was spacious, slowly dosed, and grew into a tight-spaced complex mutli-level meta thinking game.  Here it's almost the same thing but more cluttered with the complex shot at higher dosages and administered very quickly.  Unfortunately, I think it ends the patient too soon.

I shouldn't have to look up how to use the factory in 2021, when I was able to figure out the 1990s game out as a teenager. What a step back.This LOOKS like Startopia, plays like an Idle game.

_childDocuments_.review: There is nothing I can add to the already excellent, complete, and accurate bad review that is, the day I write this, the first review on the page.  Received this as a gift from family who don't know to read the reviews first and jut knew I liked sci-fi and this type of game, but not which type of games, exactly.  The developers have the same problem.  What type of game, exactly, is this?  There is a poorly written G.L.A.D.O.S. narrator, which in retrospect should have told me to reach for the refund button right away.  There is one map. It is cut up into thirds.  Each third has only one set of buildings you will build over and over and over. Others have described the odd build restrictions, meaning little build creativity.  There is no unit variety.  It is too easy, until it becomes a save-spamming exercise in blind puzzle fiddling. When I start the game in 2021 I get a welcome mesage with developer news from a year ago, and they certainly were not leaving the game in a good place. I rarely write reviews, even more rarely write bad reviews.  This game deserves one.  If you can get it on sale, there is probably $5.99 worth of decent time-wasting in the first couple levels.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm several campaign missions in and here's my initial take...(EDIT)After some additional gameplay, I have more to add to my review.The campaign is boring and clearly exists to add "game time" to your playthrough.  It almost feels tacked on, as if it were an afterthought of something to "check a box" to say the game has it.Each level is you starting fresh and building the next unlockable building.    There are far more exciting things that could have been done with the campaign.  Spitballing here... perhaps one mission is you fending off waves of pirates?  Maybe another mission is you running the station successfully without being able to recycle garbage?  Or not being able to do 'x' and you relying on manufacturing boosters?The point is, the most exciting mission was the first mission where garbage was constantly showing up and it was difficult to control.  Every other mission was just "Okay, now you get to build the *next* building.  Have fun wasting another two hours of your life doing the exact same thing you just did, but unlocking another building!  Woo!" - such a bore!(END EDIT)Don't get me wrong; I want to like the game, love it even, because it's a nostalgia overload.  But holy, what an unbalanced and uninspiring mess.

_childDocuments_.review: I adored the original Startopia, and really wanted to like this game.I had the beta release, and was... well, I wasn't thrilled, but I wasn't horrified.  There were some things I hoped they'd work out, and some others that I really liked.The initial release was problematic for me, as in, did not run long enough to complete a single tutorial.  There was an update which has fixed that, and I can now play the game.I have not had a chance to play it exhaustively, but what I've seen so far is encouraging.  It seems to lack some of the original's charm - dry British wit replaced by someone who's trying too hard - but it runs well and seems to have many of the right features.I will happily update this when I have had more time to play but I wanted to note that the constant crashes have been fixed and it appears to be a good start so far.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really hyped about this. Unfortunately, playing this game is frustrating. There is just too much micromanagement, from bombs to garbage disposal to crate management. The fuzzies are pretty much worthless. Even with no bulkheads open 7 fuzzies cannot do anything. Station filled with trash and crates rotting in the biodeck. : you just have to spam the factory for fuzzies and get a bucketload of them to deal with biodeck creates (trash is still a problem)But what is pissing me off the most is the cargo management system. No cargo is registered if it is not in the cargohold. This is either a moronic game design choice or pure development laziness/incompetence. You buy something from a trader or construct something from the factory and you wanna build them right away? Sorry, no such crate exists. You have to wait for a fuzzie to get it to a cargo hold or find and open it yourself.No materials or anything else is registered unless in a cargo hold... so when you want to build something in the factory and you dont have enough materials (because of course you don't) you have to look for plants in the bio deck and harvest them yourself and then bring the stuff to the cargohold yourself. This is pure garbage.Also, what the hell is with the contrabands? Who thought it was a good idea to randomly spawn these trash from plants and then force you to pay fines if you are not constantly paying attention to the cargoholds and bio deck to find these garbage and recycle them? Why garbage you may ask? Because all they are used for is grenades. Are your aliens moody because your base is full of garbage (even though there is no garbage to be found anywhere)? Toss a mood grenade. Are they angry because they are too stupid to visit the cat cafe to relax? Toss a relax grenade or whatever it is called. Do you need to grow a type of plant faster to get a resource because the automated systems just let them rot? Toss a plant grenade. These kinds of things are not needed in a game like this, unless there is something inherently problematic about the game itself. Personally I (try to) toss all grenades and contrabant in the recycler. I want to actually play the game and the grenades are just a bandaid for a broken system.Next the combat.  Unfortunately combat is only possible with the security station and you need multiple of them for bigger army.Finally, a very minor pet peeve. The energy core is boring. One of the things I liked in the original is watching the energy collector blob grow (and the recycler actually shooting energy into it) and got kinda nervous when it was really small. This energy core is really unfortunate. It's more of a wall decoration than an actual important building. Buuuut I can live with that..... After building craploads of MkII and MkIII fuzzies, crates were a little more bearable.Edit: After finishing the campaign and playing a full sandbox game I must say that it is way more enjoyable than the campaign. Unfortunately, I enjoyed it way less than I should, mainly because of the (nonexistent) trading. The val shop is mostly irrelevant due to the insane prices and the fact that it rarely has anything useful in it. As for the other traders, their stock is more often than not worthless. They rarely have anything useful on there and their only usefulness is selling your radiation crates and buying stuff for research. While they have quite a few basic buildings in stock on really good prices it is completely irrelevant. After all, by the time you can build the trading dock, you have already built everything else other than the irrelevant luxury buildings. The rush of seeing that cool shiny thing you really needed on a trader is completely gone. Nonetheless, verdict remains the same. Game is not very fun to play. And while  val was funny for a while, I kinda miss the original semi-friendly val.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't know much about this game going in, except that the concept was intriguing and seemed like the type of game I enjoy. Five hours in and I'm shocked to discover that this was apparently in full release three years ago. Aside from constant bugs with graphics and audio, the gameplay mechanics are fundamentally broken. Pacing and balancing are so far from optimal that the game is painful to play - there were levels where I was literally just sitting there for half an hour waiting for something out of my direct control to tick over, with the occasional "Quick - click the bomb!" or something ridiculous like that to pass the time. Worst of all is the AI guide, which tries to be sarcastic in a humourous way but misses the mark completely and becomes unbearably obnoxious very quickly. I really thought I was playing an early beta. The animation and art style is cute, but if this is the quality three years after release, it will clearly never even reach the point of being "OK". This is a shameful product. It's a hard pass for me.

_childDocuments_.review: After having played this for a while, I quite like it. All in all I enjoy it so far, it has kinda the same flow of the old one (hectic at times, not much to do at others). The art style is somewhat subjective, but I think it works for the setting.IMHO, much of the criticism Spacebase Startopia gets is due to the (understandably) high expectations people had for it after the original game; which are difficult (maybe even impossible?) to meet.All in all: if you want to play old-school Startopia, get the orginal one on GoG; if you want something with more modern gfx and some additional gameplay improvements, get this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Twenty years ago, I was working for Gamestop, and this weird game called "Startopia" showed up on our shelves.  I just got paid, so I decided to pick it up.  Little did I know that I would play that game off and on for the next 15 or so years.  It was always installed, if not played, on my computer.For years, I enjoyed its silly humor, oddball graphics, and clunky gameplay... but little did I know that a remake of the game was being made.  When I found out my beloved Startopia was getting remade, at first I was leery... after all, remakes often fall flat.Well, I'm happy to report that "Spacebase Startopia" is a loving, well crafted remake of that little-known 20 year old bundle of fun.  The alien races are slightly different.  (I miss my Noble Space Slugs,) but other than that, the gameplay is deeper, the graphics are FAR better, and all the fun is still there!If you never got a chance to play the original, don't worry.  The remake has a MUCH better tutorial, and you will be hoovering up trash like a pro in no time!  VAL can now be tweaked to sound like a condescending, snarky female robot, a condescending, snarky GLaDOS type robot, or a condescending, snarky HAL 9000 type robot.  Joy!The scenarios do a good job of easing you into the game without ever becoming too punishing.  The research is a welcome addition.  Side space missions, aliens with different reasons for coming to your base... (Medical vacationers... space truckers... eco-tourists!)  This game just improves on the already wonderful original in every way!So, just buy it.  You'll love the hours and hours of abuse heaped upon you by your robotic master... uh... "Assistant."
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: Check out my full review here: Long story short, I was a fan of the original Startopia and sunk a lot of hours into it. Starbase Startopia is basically the same game with updated graphics, with not only a lot of minor frustrations but just feeling like the same game all over again. One thing I did not mention in my review was combat, which as in the original is abysmal and honestly there was no reason to bring it back. I also struggle to remember what's different from the original, because it basically feels like the same game.It might be worth a shot on discount (say 50%) if you are new to the series, but if you played the original I don't think it's worth it in the current state or price. I'll follow it along as development continues and DLC drop, but for now this is going to my "Not Interested" pile.

Using a real speech module instead of a voice actor would fit the theme pretty well, if it would be able to speak properly, without pronunciation mistakes, especially when having English words in the German text. The typos don't help either.And this constant slagging, demotivating and offending.. Getting constantly told how dumb and incapable you are and getting denigrated every single success is not only annoying, it almost hurts.So, Realmforge Studios, let me give you a review in the style of VAL:You managed to take an old classic and remake it, without using you carbon based brains to make it properly. When looking at other things you did, you are, again, not more than mediocre. But this was to except.

_childDocuments_.review: Spent hours of the launch day trying to remove the nausea/headache inducing Chromatic Aberration (+ forced blurry TAA or FXAA solution) that exists in-game as a radial Vignette. Sadly, unlike most other engines, Unity does not allow easy access to video settings, so we are stuck with the very limited graphic options given by the devs and any real modification requires more in-depth hacking of the game's DLL files.Its even ironic that the devs have a "motion-sickness" warning due to other game features, but seemly do not care for this ever present post processing "style choice".Really wanted to like this game, but playing it is not above my wellbeing/health. _childDocuments_.review: startopia was one of my favourites as a kid, and i was kind of expecting this one to just be a HD remaster of the original. the fact that this isn't is a mixed blessing. I am still playing it so I can't really pass final judgement yet but here are my opinions so far:pros:- some of the new alien designs are cool (brain guys with robot tentacles, the space pirates are little shark guys with reverse scuba outfits)- you can build mechs now- you start with some energy- you can vaccum up trash in a big aoe- theres little grenade crates you can drop that do stuff like cure disease in a radius, recycle trash in a radius, etc- your employees put on little uniforms- lots of cute little animations (the trash can robots waddle over to the recycler like that one star wars box robot, then puke their contents in there)- more biomes and purpose to the bio deck, instead of it just being to make the hippy aliens happy- more variety of buildings- interesting random upgrade events (stuff with pros and cons, like 'recycling is 100% faster but makes more pollution' or 'pesticides make plants grow faster but have a 5% chance to make visitors sick')cons:- the AI is trying way too hard to be mean and its like good god i get the joke. but as was already said the glados voice makes it better- the little trash aliens wear heart boxer shorts and i have had an extreme grudge against heart boxer shorts since childhood, to the extent that i have still never played ghouls and goblins because of it- the moods of your patrons are conveyed as tweets which is corny- i wish you could put trash cans in-room like in theme hospital/ twin peaks hospital, you have to put the trash robots outside the rooms and then your regular robots pick up the trash from the room and put it in the trash can- easy to miss your pre-packed crates because they are in a weird spot. idk why they arent just in your inventory at the start
