_childDocuments_.review: Its been so many years, since I was the Administrator last time...I remember Arona inviting me to Trade FederationRemember fun times, many stations expanded, battles, giant angry aliens...But then...something went off, my station went too far, gone offline, froze in space with me in itEveryone goneDont know how much time passed, but here I am, found by AI - VALBut this time - its not The VAL I knew, this one is different, more cruel, more feminine? and extremely annoyingAnyways, Trade Federation is no more, Space is filled with new species (I recognized only Grays), RFS is now controlling everythingStartopias been rebooted with new technologies...Yeap, its gonna be fun just like old times I thought but then...First of all, many of the old rooms and building were repurposed, eating and drinking stuff moved onto Sleeping room, gotchaThere's a lot of these changes so lets just move onScuzzers are no more - meet FuzziesWhich are basically the same, but now without the Security TypesThey were replaced by Drones, who are doing their job pretty badly - not very tough, not very smartI also was surprised, that none of the aliens are allowed with carrying guns with them (Except for pirates ofc)The reason for that is simple - MECHSGiant robots who are extremely powerful - so its pointless trying to blast them with yours outdated lighters so yeah...But battles are still the same as in the old timesBefore - in my days, we just stormed enemy territory with all we've got, giant army of idiots with lighters - trying to make as much damage as possible in the first attack - then just grind to the enemy core and bam - mission completedNow its the same - but now with Mechs killing as much mechs as possible in the first attack - then grinding to the core, before they build more of them.As for the missions She-VAL gave me - it was nostalgic as ♥♥♥♥ - with a little changes here and thereIn the end, she did what I feared the most back in the day - AI uprising.Turns out - I was just a mere executable program this whole time....eh ♥♥♥♥ it.Folks really hate this game for no reason at allEh, hello? Do you know HOW MANY YEARS passed since last Startopia game? be thankful - its their first attempt in this setting - since they had NO assets, and were forced to build game from the ground - yes, its not perfect, it SCREAMS CASUAL, its modenized and dumbed down as all hell but hey - at least we dont have buggy Slugs anymore.Less content? - yo, do you even expand and research bro?Too much needs that stack up on each other? - yo, let me see how YOU will need ONLY Food or ONLY water during 24/7 workAI is dumb - In the original game - AI Players had already hired workers from spaceport (along with scuzzers in it) in this game - the AI doing all stuff manually - and is pretty good at it - even on easy difficultyThe game is easy - tried hard difficulty yet? Aimed for achievments? - talk to me after 100 completing the gameGraphics are bad - now that is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ - sure it can be shiny much, but folks look at the bright colors first - then the other stuff. The real problem tho - is the optimization when you have TOO MANY ALIENS ONBOARD.Just like in the original - the game stutters then but at least - no more crashing.What is this game? - you are playing the role of a space station commander - aiming for creating a perfect place for various life forms - basically - DisnayLand for aliens. If you do not know ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ about the original - go play it now - its on Steam too.Is this game worth playing? - if you never played the original - you can try this and say your opinion. If you like City Builders but want something Unique - go for it. If you just wanted ANY game like OG Startopia - play it now and say your Very Imortant Carbon Life Form Opinion.Is the Remake perfect? - nah, something feels off. The music, the jokes, the designs of aliens...yes, its Startopia alright, but still needs much work to do to make it perfect - more species, various UI stuff to make gameplay more comfortable, more missions, DLCs etc,etc. Turn off VAL also.Is the game worth its money? - NO. I completed the game entirelty in less than 30 hours - and I hadnt enough still. This worth half of the price, or at least 1.5x of the price, but not the full price - need DLC or something.Is the gameplay smooth? - if you mean optimization - get ready for stutters on lategame. If you mean the tutorial and briefings - its bad. VAL is spamming you with jokes the whole time, whilst completley forgetting to tell how to do stuff properlyWas I satisfied? - actually yes. The game shines brightest when it lets you to play slowly and just relax - observing the aliens...the problem tho - are the achievments. These are hardcore as ♥♥♥♥. 6 (SIX!) timed achievments, CARL! But If do not aim for them - the game is fun and pretty addicting, once you stop comparing this game to the original and I MEAN IT.So yeah, 8/10 - good but far from perfectP.S. - online is just like in the old times. Basically NON EXISTENT.

_childDocuments_.review: Spacebase Startopia is a game developed by Realmforge Studios and published by Kalypso Media and is a spiritual successor/sequel to the original StartopiaOverall, if you were expecting a better and more built upon 'sequel' to the original game, then this isn't it. Actually, it doesn't even touch what made Startopia so unique and different and falters on many levels, however, as a standalone game and especially if you have never played the original Startopia game like I have, you may (emphasis on may) find something fun in this... I guess?The game offers some okay-ish graphics, although some incredibly ugly glitches here and there, it is okay to same the least but in terms of animations and such, it's incredibly poor and lazy and for a 40 EUR game that is not considered as an indie game, this is just sad...The voice-over work and music are incredibly poor and lazy, especially with the voice-overs. Badly acted with some cringey and horrendous jokes, it just didn't sit well with and my God does your AI assistant thing not shut up, thank the heavens above that Realmforge Studios actually added a no commentary option because I think they exactly knew how annoying the voices are during the betaSpacebase Startopia overall as a spiritual successor/sequel to the original 2001 is abysmal and pales in comparison to Startopia, so if you're looking for a better version to the classic... stick to the classic, especially right now as it is dirt cheap on Steam, however, as a standalone game not having nothing to do with the Startopia franchise, it is an okay-ish game to play, and it does get boring if being played for a long time, but is an okay-ish to meh strategy simulation game and to play in short bursts

_childDocuments_.review: So, I only played about 7 minutes of the game and I am thoroughly unimpressed. I really don't want to play anymore after this small amount of experience due to several factors.First off, the narrator really likes to be denigrating to the player. Not in some kind of funny, oh cute the AI voice over is really smart and is making a quip, but EVERY TIME it comes on it's like, "Hey, some slug was faster at this than you." Yeah, not my cup of tea, thanks. I do not want to be insulted while learning to play a game. Also, some of the narrations doesn't match the words in the narration boxes. Come on guys, really?Second, the voice over narration at the beginning of the campaign doesn't sync with the narration boxes, and even the voice over is cut off mid sentence when the end of the intro is done. Seriously, did NO ONE test this? It's piss-poor.Third, the controls are clunky and un-intuitive. You cannot, for an example, move the camera along the Y axis when placing a building. Really? I was building a berth and wanted a better angle, but it didn't work. I had to cancel the building, adjust the camera, then go back to building. This is just an awful way to do it.Fourth, continuing with the controls, Startopia the original game would drop anything in the buffer when clicking an empty space. This game forces you to select the item and then drop it. Granted, this is more a personal issue, but it's just too many clicks! Why not click and remove the last item in unless you click? No, you HAVE to click the items in the bar before being able to drop them.I do not recommend this game at all. Not until they have fixed the voice overs, reduced the insulting dialog, make navigation easier, and be more true to the original game in how it handles.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: This is Kalypso's attempt to steal the Startopia license by making "A generic, unrelated space game that HAPPENS to use the word Startopia in the title" as if there was no precedent for them appropriating older titles and injecting good ol german Kalypso humour into them. I hope you like getting called a carbon-based lifeform as an insult because it's the one joke in the game they repeat every mission.There is tutorial mode, campaign mode (which is just an extended tutorial), and the abandoned multiplayer mode. The campaign is, mission for mission, just a copy/paste of the original games missions; in the first mission you recycle, in the second you build a hospital, in the third you establish prisons, etc. In addition you can clearly tell which aliens are supposed to be their counterparts form the original. The one exception is the Gem Slugs, who are mysteriously absent. It's a fairly easy citybuilder, they want you to build in a very specific, linear way. This is because there is now a linear tech tree that is pretty much unrelated to the research lab. In the original, the research lab was a variable size room, so you had to invest in a good R&D department. That's gone. Here's how the game works, you unlock shuttle docks and then build five or six of them. The gigantic mass of new aliens will let you R O C K E T down the tech tree; this is because when you unlock a tech you get paid. This means that a lot of missions can be sped through by just spamming ports. Also there is no travelling salesman character so it's basically impossible to sell anything you produce unless you rush to the trade docks. The problem with this game is the fact they dumbed it down for their typical "My first Strategy Game" audiences. The way the tech tree is layed out makes the game feel like you are always in tutorial mode; new alien types are also unlocked with tech rather than being attracted by buildings they like. The Gem Slug being gone is big because they poop energy when they are happy, them being gone means who cares what your visitors think. You can just ignore the aliens entirely until they start to complain. Oh, and all the while you are being berated by a poorly written AI character that are VA'ed by the worst people they could possibly find. Bland and monotone performances all around. You never meet or interact with any other characters either. I miss Arona Daal so much. He had the best prices. It's Startopia, but with all the fun parts removed. You are doing yourself a favor by buying the original instead, it supports 1920x1080p and runs on win10+ and it's $7.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's start with: "Ok it's not the original Startopia, but it is good if it is considered as another title".Pros:- More dynamic rooms, compared to the old Startopia. Animations for recycler and factories are really well realized.- Combat system TUB involve only robots, not visitors or employees. In my opinion this is good. In old Startopia having your "minions" fight and die (so you loose all experienced workers) didn't make me so happy. In this way you have the economic and war part separated- Very funny robot guide voice, if you don't mind to b cinically insulted :-) I really love this, rarely I laugh playing games, but with this one I really laugh a lot. Here an example: "You've managed to complete all the tasks, despite the circumstances. And for circumstances I mean you! I had just to say it, to be sure that you don't miss even this dig..."Cons:- Some parts of the code should be optimized. The rooster sections takes seconds to update when you filter some aliens.- I would like a tool to pack and destroy rooms more easily, instead of selecting an object one by one if you want to reshape a sectionIn conclusion it is a good game. Not exceptional, not bad with some code to optimizes. Worth it a buy with a 40-50% discount in the state it is actually.

_childDocuments_.review: Cute litte Starbase Simulation based on 2001's "Startopia". Not everything has aged well since then. Worst thing for me is the inability to zoom out more, even though understandably it's limited by the station's roof. That could however have been avoided by just making the three decks higher.Another point of criticism is the narrator who just constantly blabbers on, makes you the center of many of her jokes, and yet fails with most of them. It feels like its trying way too hard.Last but not least there is no notification of BOMBs going off soon, should you have MUTED the narrator. They just explode. Fortunately that doesn't happen too often.That out of the way, you'll find an entertaining little base building strategy game, in which you do NOT directly control the units. Rather you set up buildings, give orders and watch chaos unfold. The station consists of THREE decks: the LOWER deck for industry, work, hygiene and security, the MIDDLE deck, mostly for entertainment and the TOP deck, which acts as a botanical garden where plants are grown and turned into components (such as food, o2, etc.).Overall its a fun game to play a few hours, then take a break. It can get repetitive if you go for several hours.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original Startopia when I was little, and was extremely excited when I saw the trailer for this sequel. It still keeps the same mechanics as the last game and adds some new fun ones! The attention to detail is amazing, just like the other game! I adore the cute squid mascot on the snack builds and the adorable slug races in the gambling buildings!One bug I did found: If you press Escape and press it again to go back to your game, the sounds and music will not restart, but rather leave the game silent. Quick fix is to go in and out of the Escape menu until the sounds and music return!Another part is the narrators. I loved both the French and English narrators in the original game. They were great talent, and was hoping that the original English voice actor would come back. 9/10!
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: It's Startopia with a visual upgrade. Which means it has the charm of the original, but also some problems.I for one like it!- The changes to the controls are 95% good ones, it's better to handle for sure.- The Aliens are cool updates or substitutions of the originals. Except for the Grey, they're basically the same.- They added some combat changes. Obviously still not complicated. But it doesn't have to be, because it's a tiny, negligable part of the game.- The changes to the research system are quite nice... researching upgrades that are meaningful gameplay-wise- I really like the updates to production in the factory. Using all the ressources from the bio deck and producing things out of them is very nice.1 or 2 things that probably need some fixing:- Garbage accumulation is slightly ridiculous. Even if you've plastered your decks with garbage-bots- Need for fun seems a bit broken. I had 1 medium and 1 huge Disco up and running for 10 sections open in total (4 sub, 3 fun, 3 bio) and it was still the main problem for most visitors.Other than that i'm extremely happy with this update of a classic

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is fine, and it's kind of cute. I love this studio's previous games (I have like 300 hours in Dungeons 3). The issue is this is not a finished product. _childDocuments_.review: I have been playing it for quite a while. Its fairly decent but leaves a lot to be desired, like a more efficient harvest system. The mechs need at least 2 tiles space to get around the decks, the visitors just drop their garbage and don't put them in the bins leaving the robots to waste time picking them up. Honestly, I would prefer to play the original game instead of this one, at least the comedy was much better than this one.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't quite the Startopia I remember from my youth, but it's close enough that I'm really enjoying it. The format is still more or less unchanged: You build a space station across three levels, fill it with facilities and equipment that will keep various alien races content. There are a lot of changes from the original, not all for the best, but some are definite quality-of-life improvements. The biggest improvement, to my mind, is with combat and strategy. In the original game, you brought your armies to designated points with beacons, and hoped that more of your people showed up before the enemy. This version feels like it's taken notes from RTS and squad-based games, and gives you a separate, tactical HUD for combat. Not as robust as other genres, perhaps, but definitely functional enough that you can get your units where they gotta go.Managing the biodeck feels streamlined compared to the original. There are fewer tools, and thus fewer variables that you need to manage. Some of the rooms that were variable-sized in the original are now fixed, which is a bit of an improvement to me: brigs could get huge, and now having them pre-defined is an improvement. The introduction of Blueprints is also a huge quality-of-life improvement: I almost never manually design rooms, I just use the small, medium, or large blueprint--making a berth by hand was fun the first dozen or so times, but after that? Just repetitive. My main complaint is that the writing and the humor aren't quite as sharp as the original. If the original game was Douglas Adams, this is more Eoin Colfer writing as Douglas Adams. Some of the writing is a bit try-hard, and not landing the jokes in quite the same way. It feels Startopia-ish, but isn't quite there. I think there are some bits of information that also didn't quite make it into the dialog which would definitely be helpful. Of the three voice options, I'm finding the GLaDOS-alike feels the closest to right (in some ways, it feels this game swapped out VAL for the Portal AI).Part of the reason I'm writing is that I'm disappointed with all the negative reviews this game is getting. It seems that a lot of folks were expecting more, and while I can see those complaints, I'm still having a lot of fun. While there are some things to complain about, I do think it's worth a try for anyone who really missed the original.Overall, this is hitting my nostalgia buttons enough that it's still Startopia--just that in smoothing out some of the rough edges from the previous game, it seems like they've added a few of their own.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first time on startopia and after a rocky start, im starting to love it This is a breakdown on my 14hours game timeFirst play – missions well they say missions its more like a tutorial as a lot of things are not explained also its limited access to items/buildings and aliens so the first few it makes the game seem really basic and well a bit boring like there is not much going on.  (took me about 3 hours to get onto mission5)Middle – mission 5 its starting to become a much better game its still limited and items still blocked you get your first battle but still new and learning the ropes this mission 5 and 6 took about 1.5 hours each as I still really had no idea what was going onEnd – after about 8 to 12 hours (as I left it running for about 4 hours while I was watching TV Saturday night, so just starting mission 7 a new alien race more new buildings and im finally getting to grasps with the biodeck checking have terraform a race or workers want and at the same time checking was resources I need for building its getting more and more in depth as I play so im looking forward to see what the final missions bring and then I will be ready to head out on my own and start a full on base without restrictions : So it was a shaky start and I thought what a hunk of junk but steady pace of the missions introducing new buildings and features the game is a 100% thumbs up from me and for anyone who loves base building

_childDocuments_.review: First I must qualify this by stating I loved the original I played it to death and wanted a sequel so bad, and instantly signed up for the beta, which I played all 4 tutorial missions then left wanting to enjoy the full game experience, Some of the annoying things about this game were also in the original, having to hire mass numbers of Staff so that you could have the 3 you need to run a building, I'm sad to say though that certain parts of this are much much worse, this becomes apparent in the first mission after the 4 excellent tutorial missions are over, you are on a station circling LV-426 with Aliens infesting the biodome. you also have to research advanced Tourism to unlock the research lab (yes that's as weird as it sounds).you are advised to build a mech, which infuriatingly despite building the transports, will not transport to the biodeck, also a solar storm knocked out the entire base, and despite putting all the buildings into repair mode it took over an hour for the fuzzies to repair most of the buildigs and some I just had to give up on. at somepoint when i'd unlocked a few bulkheads, the UI stopped allowing me to select and place anything without trying 5 times. they have removed some of the more adult humour and features, whilst i don't mind some of the race changes, the ai is now pretty terrible, this needs patching.the biodeck although looks pretty is clunky to do any real terraforming on which was one of the great features of the originalI loved and still love the original, its still in there somewhere though the magic is missing currently

_childDocuments_.review: Just like the old Startopia it basically stops being fun after the 4 campaigns are complete. The game and beta are basically exactly the same except in the beta you could easily invite your friends but now in the real game you having to find your game id and go to a lobby and have someone type that in. So in essence the real game is like the beta exactly except they took out one of the few things that made it fun to play with a friend. The AI voice is annoying and constantly insults you and calls you stupid. The old Startopia was much classier and cheaper and just as fun. The AI voice is much better. This game adds nothing to Startopia. Save your money and go buy the old game.Added - if you want to know how fun it is - it sits on me and my partners computers unplayed. Not eve enticing. Boring and horrible. Rip off and still mad that I can't get my money back for this garbage. Over priced.

_childDocuments_.review: Starbase Startopia is an RTS based game which is combined from Theme Park and Dungeon Keeper. The map is always the same in every mission which is divided into sectors and 3 decks or floors. Should you run out of space you buy out the next sector. You have the sub deck where you have basic infrastructure like recycler, factories, hospital, medbay, etc. Then you have the Fun Deck (Entertainment Deck in old Startopia) where you build restaurants, casinos etc. Last you have the Bio Deck whre you growth crops and plants for materials to process in your factory.What you do is to fufilly your customers or tourist  increasing needs, first only a bar and later on a 5 Star Hotel.You can play against AI where you cam contest a sector. The one who has last combat units standing in the contest sector wins it.The Campain of Startopia are chained narrative missions where you get introduced to the different aspects of the game, starting with recycling garbage then setting up med bays ans so on.So now my Oppinion. I didn't played Beta but I expected a Startopia and thats what you EXACTLY receive with little flawored changes here and there. So what actually changed in the game.* The combat has been redesigned. Back then you had your (some races didn't fight) employees and police droids who did the combat. The sector combat was basicly get your police droid alive to the sector door and hack it so it closes and you win it. Now you only have those tiny police robos and the big mechs- This is what i don't like the most, the combat feld clumsy in "Startopia Old" and now it feels even clumsier. The police robos deal almost no damage and the mechs fight each other. I like the mass battles from the past.--------* Resource System from Bio Deck has been simplified. You know have only 6 Resources (Air, Food, Minerals, Fabric, Medic thingies and Black Market Stuff). However now you factory processes this stuff into cuircuits or plastic etc.-/+ Dunno I guess this is OKish nothing that frustrates but nothing great.--------* Your "god hand" has been improved. You have mass grabs etc.+ Like it, back then it was cancer picking up each trashcan--------The campaign is still the same building you base, get money, finish mission. The narrative advisor is talking in Dungeons 3 manners.-/+ Difficult. I mean it is hard to bring an advanced campaign to a game where the map has to be the same each level. However all the levels feel very generic, like recycle trash in values of 10k bucks or heal 50 people, or earn money on Fund Deck, to destroy your opponents. I believe the game couldnt not be improved much this manner. At least the narrative is good ol Dungeons 3 humor :)----Conclusio---* Balance the resources, the pacing is not good, especially in O2 generation/consumption.* Combat ist way to clumsy and narrowed to those bots and police droids are trash.* Campaign is boring if you expect a good narrative.All in all it's not a Startopia 2.0 its rather more Startopia 1.4

_childDocuments_.review: I am head-over-heels in love!I have very fond memories of playing the original Startopia and was always saddened it may have been forgotten to time, and then Starbase Startopia materialised into my life!I am so impressed!It has all the charm of the original but has been beautifully refined. The graphics are absolutely stunning as is the animations of the creatures and buildings alike.VAL is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ funny, I'm constantly chuckling and on occasion, full on laughing out load because of an insult-compliment she's thrown my way. Although I love the insults, I do wonder if it is a tad overboard at times?The tutorial is also very well done. They make sure to cover as much as possible without spoiling everything you can unlock later and I'm also thankful that VAL speaks the tutorial (and everything else) out loud, making the learning process that much more pleasant to experience.The only issue I've noticed so far is the sound can sometimes stutter when surrounded by a lot of buildings/rooms that have clashing music etc but it doesn't particularly bother me at all.I'm so happy to see Startopia get the attention and upgrade it deserves, and then some!Truly wonderful work Spacebase Startopia team!!! 11/10

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, it's essentially the same game as the original. Better graphics and clearer guidance - I could never remember which aliens worked where, apart from the Grey doctors - and more help in the biodeck to chose your terrain and environment. There's some very nice additions - the blueprints for each room as an example, but you've still got the freedom to design your own if you want. The factory now makes more sense - you can use the crates from the biodeck to create other products rather than just burning energy, although I thought it strange that it doesn't seem to need workers?There seems to be more random events - the placing of different types of bombs that need to be dealt with quickly keeps your own toes.If you loved Startopia this is a worthy successor, in a similar way  that Two Point Hospital was a worthy successor to Theme Hospital.

The Multiplayer is like Anno 2070 - perfection!

_childDocuments_.review: I wrote a negative review about this game when it was released, that might've been rash on my part. I was looking at this game through the nostalgia glasses I had on for the original Startopia. At the time, I didn't play it very long  and did not give it a chance to grow on me. My gripes were that the game had been oversimplified, and the AI was so inferior to the original Startopia's HAL 9000. I demanded a refund and waited for a sale where maybe I'd give it another chance.The game went on sale recently, so I bought it again and played it some more. I also booted up the original to see if my gripes were founded. I now come to the conclusion that yes, some things have been simplified, but that's for the best because they were rather tedious in the original, and if you want, you can still design everything manually. The AI, well I suppose it is what it is, but there's a setting in the options that cuts down on it's chatter, and you phase it out after a while, in the end, it really isn't so bad.The detractors of this game say: play the original, you'll have a better time, I say, the original is ok, but 20+ years down the line, it's mechanics are clunky, it's graphics dated, it can be patched to run in 4k, which helps the visuals but makes it impossible to read text or use the interface. This new Startopia IS in the end Startopia, and it's a good looking, modern game.Don't judge this one too harshly, and don't put too much stock in all the negative reviews, play it a bit more, you'll see that it's Startopia fun afterall.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played the previous Spacebase so this is the first time for me. I am not that far in but so far I really it, the game has a quirky and cute art style with some pretty funky music especially when the fun deck gets going. I love all the little animations when the residents go about their business and do their jobs as well. Once you get a semi-stable setup going it's quite fun to watch all the stations and aliens interact and the unique animations that go with it, they all have neat endearing charms to them.I see in a few reviews people talk about the tutorial not being too good but I disagree. If you play the campaign it feels a little bit like a tutorial but with added challenge so it allows you to learn it a portion at a time. I would say some things could have been explained better in the tutorial. For example, I didn't realise I could upgrade security bots in the research tab (I still don't know how to upgrade the FUZZY bots) and it wasn't explained what the plant materials could do as I did not expect to get the mineral resource from them originally as it was not in my initial bio zone.I haven't experienced any fps problems on my rig and as far as bugs go I have only encountered a small few such as during a freeplay the music suddenly dropped but would occasionally come back as I went past certain areas and when I placed some benches in the fun deck they couldn't seem to sit and were rocking forth somewhat maniacally although I kinda found that funny.Lastly some reviews comment on the humour, I think it's pure taste to be honest. I am a very sarcastic person and I laugh at the deprecating humour the AI has although I do think sometimes the AI talks too much. I personally use the option to make it sound like Glad0s from portal as it suits the sarcasm and insults xD. As a whole I recommend this game, although perhaps not at the initial price. It has wonderful quirks and charms that I think will only be improved as bugs get fixed. If you love the art style, want a fairly chill game and don't mind sarcastic humour I would definitely give it a go.
_childDocuments_.name: Spacebase Startopia

_childDocuments_.review: SPACEBASE STARTOPIA is an original mix of economic simulation and empire building strategy paired with classic RTS fights. In addition to the single player Campaign and Skirmish mode, there’s also a competitive and co-op multiplayer mode for up to 4 players. And as if maintaining the 3 Space Station Decks, entertaining the 8 Alien races and defending against invaders were not enough of a challenge, the dynamic narrator AI is not going to mince matters and commentates the events.

name: Honey, I Joined a Cult
detailed_description: Honey, I Joined a Cult is a tycoon/management game where you must build and expand your base, supervise your cultists and resources, and increase your faith, funds and following! MANAGE YOUR CULT Effective management is at the heart of every money-making enterprise and your organisation is no exception! Being snappy dressers isn't enough, your cult must run like a well-oiled hypno wheel. Set schedules for your cultists, develop their skills, level them up and manage food and maintenance systems. Assign tasks to your cultists based on a priority system. So who said that micro-management doesn't work?! BUILD A BASE FOR YOUR CULT Every great cult needs great interior design. Place, design, and decorate rooms to keep your cultists happy. There is a whole host of weird and wonderful room options and objects, each with a vital role to play in your cult. From polygraph rooms, discombobulator, and spirit chambers to energy spas and the dreaded ministry of alteration. CUSTOMISE YOUR CULT A cult is only as good as its name (and its followers!). Choose yours wisely when picking for your cult, cult leader, the Divine Being that they worship, the Holy Room in which they prove their dedication and the followers that will become the cultists of tomorrow! Make your cult your own by deciding on: *A funky symbol *An epic uniform to impress would-be followers *An imposing hat to make other cults jealous *A strange relic to worship and adore CARE FOR YOUR CULT Cultists have needs too and you'll have to ensure that all of yours are fed, watered and having lots of fun! You must take care of your cult's physical and mental well-being to allow them to be the best cult members they can possibly be! It is as they say, cult is only as strong as the cultists! LEAD YOUR CULT Your cult leader can be very demanding. Whether it's recruiting specific followers or building certain rooms, be sure to bend to their every whim. Not fulfilling demands will lower their mood and a displeased leader won't be able to perform effective sermons. Cultists can be sent on missions in the local town. Whether it's gathering resources, unlocking new tech or just a demand from your leader, the Covert Ops room is the perfect place to plan! GROW YOUR CULT Use all your charms to recruit new followers, who will bring in resources and eventually climb through the ranks to become full cultists. Discontented followers will simply leave, so be sure to turn that frown upside down! Follow us, join the community and chat with the devs. Look in the external links to join our Twitter and Discord We're always listening – let’s achieve greatness together!!!

_childDocuments_.review: So i should confess i saw this game years ago and wishlisted it, Then it went quiet and nothing happened until fairly recently.Seeing it now in early access at this price i would argue that giving it a shot is worth it. - Has genuine soul and character- Easy to understand, due to clear and clean UI- Low price point (Currently 20 Euro without the 10% discount due to release)- Fun customization which is allowed even later in the game/cult encouraging evolving your cult- Feels slightly hollow in places because early access- Lack of detailed information sources when trying to get more details- More customisation of the ability to mod it in with more ease.(In other words more soul/character)- Some access to the statistics of the cult. As running it gives a very loose feeling about the details. (think a history of progress and average income)- An overview where you can see who does what tasks with priority and who isn't allowed on certain tasks. (Full cult overview)I liked what i saw before, I liked what i see in the game. I would like to see where they are going to go with this.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get me wrong, the game is fun. I played it non-stop for five hours after I bought it. After that time, however, you see a lot of issues. And I mean A LOT.First of all, I just got locked out of progress by a game-breaking bug. There are certain items in the game that are "one-per-base". After you buy them, you can't build another (which makes sense for balancing reasons). Sadly, one of those items just... disappeared after a police raid. The game registers it as still being present, so I can't buy it, but the room itself is completely useless, therefore pretty much blocking my progress.The progress feels very sluggish. I constantly play it on maximum speed, because there's just not much to do, other than waiting for money and building a room or placing an item. I thought the leader would have certains skills or abilities that would be useful in running the facility. But he only has like two and I rarely needed to use them. Basically, your input is minimal. There's no campaign, so no clear goal - you just unlock new stuff, build new stuff, for the purpose of getting more things, to unlock new stuff, to build new stuff... I know it's that type of game, but usually there's something more. Some stories, some tasks, sometimes even small choices. There are some options regarding the ending, but I got bored (or locked) before even reaching that point, going through the same, boring steps every time.Removing items, walls and such does not give you back even a small amount of money, so there's little incentive to redecorate/rebuild stuff. The best experience I had so far was wasting all money early on, building huge rooms and then waiting for the money to flow and just fill them in as you unlock new stuff. Building small and then trying to change things up takes too much resources (and is also buggy as hell, usually after removing a wall inside a building, the game does not register this particular place as being inside, so again, you have to waste money, remove all foundations and place them again).Early in the game, you unlock PR missions. Those missions, however, even if successful, will "reward" you with risk/heat points (which leads to protests and police raids). Missions that lower the heat are unlocked later on, usually after it's extremely high and hard to manage. And those raids and protests are just huge pain in the a**, with the sole purpose of just slowing down already extremely slow progress.Your minions will have various traits, some that will just add to their skills, but some, more annoying, like wanting their own room, taking care of their needs in private and all that. The problem is... Game just isn't designed in a way that would make it reasonable. I wanted to give all minions their own chambers, but it just resulted in a very low prestige rating for those rooms - it was much better to place them all together in a huge space full of stuff than give them smaller but private bedrooms. Same goes for toilets and pretty much everything else. Maybe those options are unlocked later on, that I don't know, but it's just annoying and unrealistic.Also, I felt that those traits will have some noticeable impact on gameplay, but halfway through I realised that one of my cultists doesn't like working with followers and yet he's been assigned to doing just that. I didn't figure it out earlier, because I saw no signs of that - he seemed fine. I didn't feel like I needed to check what they're thinking or what they want/don't want, because it didn't seem that important.Even the humor in the game didn't really work for me. I guess it may be the issue with translation (I've played mostly in Polish language), but some things (especially in newspapers and missions descriptions) were true head-scratchers. Sometimes I didn't even know what the hell was supposed to mean. Sure, there were a few fun easter eggs here and there, but nothing more.The most fun thing is creating your own cult, but even that was... well, disappointing. There aren't a lot of customization options. Good idea, bad experience. First few hours are fun, after that it's just watching the game at full speed, waiting for resources and then barely using them. It's only two steps above your typical idle game. And bugs are just icing on the cake.Sadly, I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Confusions... On the one hand its cute and quirky as advertised, providing hours of game-play for a decent price.On the other hand.. 30hrs in and feeling un-satisfied.- Build room, go on mission, upgrade room, go on mission. Occasionally read a funny piece of dialogue. Get bored - Go to the dark side hoping for some fun.- Build room, go on mission, upgrade room, go on mission. Sure there are different 'mission' types. The mini-stories in missions are great. But uh... A whole solid minute of amusing engagement? In between long periods of nothing-ness.It's simply not engaging enough. .. You keep upgrading and building thinking that some cool stuff is gonna happen. Or that the story-line will flesh out and captivate you. After-all - you're running a cult. But it's just so lack luster... I have 'followers' signing deals with the devil that are about as interesting as ordering the food in the kitchen.- The game has promise. It's at least worth the money if you are looking for a time waster. But after so many hours in I kind of feel 'led on' ...  I got all excited. Put extra time, and effort into this 'new thing' thinking there would be some kinda pay out at the end of the night. Some sort of 'wow' moment, or moments that would set this game apart. But instead I'm trying to decide if some sort of interesting 'promised end' - like your cult god destroying the world is even worth opening the game up for. Can I really handle more hours of this repetative un-rewarding game in order to see it to the end? I'm not sure yet. ..  ..

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to give this game a positive review however, I am going to be giving a lot of criticism as an avid enjoyer of management sims. Here is a summary overview with bullet points listed below for a quick read.Honey. I Joined a Cult is a uniquely crafted management simulator that uses a variety of different mechanics to create a cult simulator that adapts to create a nice pace of challenge at every stage. The game utilizes 6 different mechanics at varying stages of importance and introduction as the game continues onward. The balance between Public Relations, Heat, Influence, Money, Faith, and Divine Inspiration lead to different challenges hidden from the player from the tutorial. I felt the game was easy to learn as it was extremely similar to most other management sims like Prison Architect or RimWorld for example. Managing cultists through various selecting, altering, and manipulating as well as survival factors make it challenging to lead a successful cult, with a constant dilemma of balance between your resources. The game is aesthetically pleasing as well, with pleasing colour schemes, beautifully crafted environments, and unique characters. The satire in the game made me chuckle, with funny dialogue from the characters as well as hidden messages in the scroll chat. The music, while short in variety, was excellent in execution as well. Groovy and funky riffs that keep your head bobbing.With all of that said the game has some deep fundamental flaws both internally and externally. For one, the devs seem to have abandoned this game. I don't see any updates, there are various bugs that occur like when cultists are selected for a mission and then deselected they get stuck on the mission therefore making them unable to perform any other tasks. This can kill them/cause them to abandon because apparently it takes only 1 day for someone to starve and leave a cult they've been loyal to for the past 45 days. Features like the scheduling system are nice and intuitive but the priority system is extremely basic. High, low, or no priority which puts your sprites into a system where you can't have dedicated staff for rooms unless you devote dozens of hours meticulously crafting each of your 21 cultists (not counting the 3 bonus) on top of your other duties. As for the research, a staple in management sims nowadays, it couldn't be any more insulting. Researching on how to cook meat and vegetables as the premier option for your cultists is not only a slap in the face to players who've spent at minimum 15 hours getting it, its a slap to the little sprites as well. By the time you research the ability to run 2 missions at the same time, missions become obsolete besides for divine inspiration. A quick side not on the missions, while the side quests for the missions were fun, whats not fun is the game breaking bug that not only discourages you from doing them, but also reduces the chance for success further frustrating the player. The game felt like they wanted to include a main story after the tutorial but instead it's just the same ending. A placard with the flavor you chose at the beginning. You don't need to complete all three to know that. Just do one and you'll get it. There wasn't even anything truly unique about the mechanics of the rooms you were given, just a re-skin. I don't even want to get into the numerous grammatical and spelling errors that occur in the chat bubbles and tutorial menu messages. Did no one double check and read everything before releasing? Building in the game is pretty ok, but with a lack of ability to expand the lot you end up just making one mega structure for your cultists to live in with maybe a few other buildings for your followers. If the devs intentions were to be creative with limited horizontal space they should've given us vertical space like with bunkers for the doomsdayers or upstairs for growing the world tree. Just a quick quip back to the tutorial. Don't give us the impression that heat matters past 250, and even then it's laughable at best and doesn't impact gameplay minus cult debuffs. Also the music is good but please more than like 4 songs. Overall the game could use a major facelift and with the right TLC, it can shine and become one of the top management sims out there. Sadly, I feel this is a pipe dream and if you want to try this game, wait till it goes on sale for how I got it for like $8. PROS:*Unique Management Resources*Visually Appealing*Funny dialogue*Scaleable difficulty*Easy to learnCONS:*Unfinished*Absent developers*Bugs/glitches*Redundant mechanics*Lack of content

_childDocuments_.review: After playing for six hours, I can safely say that unfortunately, I cannot recommend the experience the game provides in its current state. I had a good amount of fun at the beginning, but my experience deteriorated rather quickly. Hence why I wanted to write this review and possibly make players think this purchase through a little more.-  The constant red exclammation marks that you cannot easily swat away, having to go through the entire "Objects" section to find which new items you can now purchase, the annoying and sort of cheap way these menu tabs are built in general,...the UI works against you, rather than in your favor.- There is so much . For one, we have the aforementioned UI. But that's by far not the end of it - I also had issues with mission assignments, the cult theme, building, or the "protest" mechanic.  The fact that you can just do one at time (for a rather long portion of the game) and have to keep constantly reassigning them for what feels like a small reward quickly became a frustrating loop I tried ignoring as much as possible. I reckon the random events that you encounter during these missions are supposed to be humorous and break the tedium a little bit, but to be entirely honest, I feel they only increased it due to their messy structure and humour which, at least for me, mostly misses the mark. Somewhere down the line, you have to choose a focus for your cult out of a few options. I chose the "Love & Peace" option and...it only added more of the same tedium. Just another progress bar that you fill by completing more missions (UGH!) and by your cult leader doing some research in their office. And that's like, kind of it? You get a few new rooms and customization options out of this. Cool, I guess. It's such a mess. It's buggy, and due to that and the UI it just feels like you're constantly at odds with the game. Besides, you get no refunds for rebuilding stuff, which is extremely questionable in a game where you should want to strive to make things look nice. There is also the prestige meter, which you can raise by filling rooms with decorations and more items, but you can never have really high prestige in small rooms (for example, single bedrooms). Thus, you're constantly incetivized to primarily build big, crowded rooms. Some reviews have gone into more detail about this, but tl;dr it's not only frustrating if you want to build multiple smaller bedrooms for design purposes, but it can also negatively affect some of your cultists who prefer their own spaces. But then if you build their own rooms, you can never get the prestige levels very high. Well, you get the point. Holy heck. The third protest of my playthrough was the straw that broke the camel's back. This "minigame" was making me lose my mind. Basically, a bunch of protesters show up at your cult and some of them start getting violent. You need to MANUALLY assign which cultist is going to go deal with whom based on who is likeliest to calm the protester down. You have to search your entire cult and *manually* find people who fit the requested criteria and *manually* click on the individual protesters every single time. Not only is this more tedium which (to make matters worse) interferes with your daily progress, but more violent protesters just keep popping up (with an - I am sorry, but - awful sound effect to boot) and the anger meter rises fast. I kept having to switch between pausing (to actually find cultists to fit the criteria) and x3 speed (because of course, swatting the protesters away takes loads of time).-  For some reason, you cannot even automate *ordering food for the kitchen*. Why? I really don't know. It does, however, make it so that your progress starts feeling rather pointless. Slow returns (mostly gatekept by the time it takes to research new things) for a whole lot of micromanagement. I know this is a part of the deal with resource management games, but this title kind of feels like playing Cookie Clicker, except you have to keep clicking on the cookie manually.- Quite a few things aren't well explained, and the tutorial itself is pretty poorly designed as well.- It just doesn't click, man. TL;DR: I am honestly just really sad, because this game is very much a shell of what it could be. It has this late alpha/early beta feel, except it's apparently a full release warranting a 22EUR price tag. And just, no -- I cannot in good faith recommend a title this clunky and unintuitive, at least not until this game gets some well-needed updates and bug fixes.

_childDocuments_.review: It really pains me to give a bad review. Since 2018 I looked monthly into my wishlist to check if the release date is announced or not. I waited and cheered…‘Honey, I Joined a Cult’ is a typical base-building and management game. Which is usually my favourite genre, but in this case I got bored pretty fast. I was very excited about starting a cult (something new and fresh for me), but it barely felt like one. It was a random game with some building and management features. For me it lacked SOMETHING, something special and charming. Features like communication with your upper-followers or ability to pursue people personally to join your cult. I wish I could do more with my cult owner or at least I would like to have more cultish features - something special, so this game stands out.I understand that this game is still in early access. Maybe I wouldn’t be so strict if it would be in early access back in 2018 or 2019. But I waited for almost four years (!!!) - in this time I graduated, got married, became a parent, moved to another country and came back. My expectations grew with every year.... I hope this game will get more charm and more personality. I have patience and I have time. I will check on this game monthly!4 of 10 – YB

_childDocuments_.review: It's basically like Cookie Clicker. You wait while numbers go up, and eventually you get to unlock things that make numbers go up faster and let you unlock more things.Now that can still be kind of addictive, but there isn't really any challenge to the game. It's way too "easy", there is no way to lose (or even suffer a major setback) unless you do it on purpose. You aren't really presented with any problems that need to be solved (as an example, think long queues in RollerCoaster Tycoon that make people complain, or bad traffic in Cities Skylines causing garbage trucks to not be able to get places and garbage to pile up, etc. - those kind of problems just don't exist here, everything seems to just work fine on its own without your input).The cult theme is also somewhat shallow and surface level, but that's not a big issue. I did eventually finish it, but it felt a bit like a chore towards the end. I played the second half of the game on 3x speed nonstop.

_childDocuments_.review: Honey, I Joined A Cult is an adorable game that I don't quite know whether or not to recommend. The in-game artwork and sprites are very cute, and the writing is funny and gets a reliable smile from me every time. The premise of the game is that you are a charlatan cult leader with an aesthetic straight out of the 1970s. Your goal is to cultivate a core group of cult "members" (i.e., free laborers) and "followers" (visitors who are milked for money by paying to use fraudulent "therapy" rooms) while you can live out the easy life as a fake spiritual leader. If you happen to establish World Peace or summon a Great Old One in the process of all this, well, whoop-si-doodle.The dark humor and cartoony graphics combine well if you're into that sort of thing (and I am). But the game suffers from a common problem that plagues many sims: once you have a good routine down, you're just grinding resources until you earn enough to cash in for an ending. My last game clocked a total of 14 hours, but I had most of the "therapy rooms" built at around 5 hours, and the remaining 9 hours was just letting the game run on autopilot in the background until I racked up enough resources to win the game. There are options to grind for upgrades to the therapy rooms, but they aren't very excited and just boil down to either "more decorations" or "more earned money" for each room. So a large portion of the game felt a bit of a slog, and I'm not seized with a desire to replay another cult flavor (the current options are Peace & Love, Aliens, and Darkness) because I can tell not much will be different in terms of core gameplay.I will say, the game author(s) seem very much aware of this problem, but I don't really like the solutions they're trying out to combat the issue. For example, every so often protesters will show up to picket your cult and you have to figure out which cultists are best to send out to talk them down. The problem is, the entire premise of the game is that you (the cult leader) see all your followers as interchangeable dupes, so it's a bit off-message to suddenly have to pour over which one appeals best to Logic and which one values Emotion in order to vibe best with the picketers. Another attempt to jazz up the game can be seen with random events that happen during missions; the problem with these is that I hate doing missions and the funny random events didn't really make them feel any less of a hated obligation. If I could make a wishlist for the game, I think it would be: - Give me a bigger compound to build in. Some of my members want private bedrooms, but there's no room for anything but big barracks-style housing and a huge privacy-free bathroom where everyone does their business out in the open. Maybe we could upgrade to a bigger compound over time, as that would give me something to do with this pile of money that I sleep on every night.- The "decor" category is huge and unwieldy to scroll through. It needs sub-categories for things like statues, tables, novelties, etc. They also start to feel pointless when all they do is increase the "status" of a room. Can you implement some kind of stat-boost for specific items in specific rooms: "important documents" speed up research, while the "teapot" speeds up cooking in the kitchen? Etc. Speaking of, give me fewer things that take up precious floor space and more things that I can hang on walls, please!- I cannot give a 5-star sermon to save my life. Adjust the requirements for this to be less unforgiving, please? Speaking of unreasonable standards: 100,000 Influence points for a Steam Achievement is insane. Did you mean 10,000? Because I spent 14 hours on my last play-through and got 26,000 Influence by the end. I didn't want to sink another 42 hours into that save file just to snag the achievement, you know? - The therapy rooms are interesting, but I want more of them! It feels very limiting that we only end up with half a dozen types of rooms. I wanted more rooms and (possibly) to have to choose which sorts of rooms my cult would specialize in. Picking my cult flavor only gave me one new room (the Maypole Dance room, which was admittedly VERY COOL, nice Wicker Man!) whereas I wanted so much more. There's so many flavors of 1970s chicanery to choose from--magnets, spoon bending, psychic card decks, blurry photographs, faith healing, and so forth--and it just feels very disappointing to be limited to maggot baths and yoga mats.- The writing in the random events is extremely strong and I enjoy them very much. I would perhaps expand that concept to occur outside the missions as well. Police could show up to tour the compound and the player's answers could affect whether your political Heat goes up or down. Family members could visit the cult members and that could affect Influence or Public Relations. - Speaking of public relations, I want to be able to throw events at the compound, even if it's just a text box on the Mission screen. I kept expecting the PR missions to evolve from more than just radio appearances. Admittedly I didn't do very many of those because they kept increasing my Heat for no good reason and Heat is hard enough to manage as is. I would balance that a little better; going on a radio show or throwing a charity event or hosting a gerbil-adoption day shouldn't increase political heat like that! - [Trigger Warning: Sexual Coercion] I was not planning to use the "Free Love" room at all and was a little annoyed to find that it was mandatory in order to receive the Peace & Love finale. It might seem silly that I'm cool with playing a game about exploiting free labor from victims of religious abuse, yet I draw the line at sexual coercion but I do. The room is a cool game mechanic (letting cult members share positive traits and stats after "learning" from each other... in bed) but I would *strongly* recommend implementing a statistical possibility wherein the chosen pair refuse to use the room because they're Just Not That Into Each Other; this would make me feel like they have a *choice* in the matter and are actively consenting when they do use the room. I have similar feelings about the incense room, for that matter. Anyway, I have rambled enough and this is getting long. I enjoyed the game a lot, but I enjoy the IDEA of the game more than the implementation right now, if that makes sense. I hope that future implementations feature a little more variety and a little less slog.

_childDocuments_.review: I am not recommending this game because it is not the game it should be.  The game mechanics are not about running a cult.  Control, loyalty, obedience, secrecy, faith, worship, sacrifice are all elements that go into a cult.  Theses are the things I thought I would be managing in the game.  The game does touch on some of these themes but only on the surface.  As an example the game has happiness instead of loyalty.  When running a cult loyalty is the top priority.  It is up to the followers to find happiness in being loyal, not in playing board games.  The game is fun if you like to manage little blips running around on the screen and all you have to worry about is keeping there meters full.  But there is so little in the game that has anything to do with running a real cult.

_childDocuments_.review: So far it's been fun. The dialogue is quite amusing to read and I appreciate the simplicity and ease of access of all the current features. As always with Early Access games there are and will be bugs, I've discovered one that is unfortunately mildly game breaking. During the tutorial, if your maintenance worker fixes your podium before the game prompts you to manually assign it to them, upon receiving said 'quest' the game becomes 'stuck' as you can no longer select the podium for repair and can not unfreeze time or progress until the 'action/quest' is completed.However, I simply just went to the menu and started a new game using what I learned already from the tutorial. I believe the game has real potential so I'll certainly be playing around it in more, just remember it's Early Access there will be bugs, but with bugs comes patches and fixes. Those who didn't believe in Santa -- merry be his name -- were on the "naughty list."My compound was called the North Pole, and the elves listened to me preach about keeping Christmas in your heart always in our hallowed halls of Santa's Workshop. _childDocuments_.review: Much in the same vein as Prison Architect; "Honey, I joined a Cult" is essentially a compound building sim. You can customize your cultists' robes etc... While showing a few glimmers of promise, it falls into the same repetitive pattern as most other titles in this sub-genre. After the initial construction, it's click, wait, rinse and repeat. The tech progression is the same tired approach that we see from other titles. Too many skills that end up netting you very little in the long run, essentially making the game "longer" whilst giving the player very little in terms of reward. Looking into the dev's "roadmap" leaves a lot to be desired. More akin to "Look at all this affectatious content we're planning on releasing!" as opposed to real game depth, this is a title that is best taken at surface value. It's schtick in a genre quickly becoming bereft of any originality. Good for an hour or two, but the $20 price tag makes this title one to avoid.

_childDocuments_.review: Honey, I Joined a Cult is an enjoyable game, as long as players know what to expect from this kind of management experience. The mechanics work well, there’s a constant sense of forward momentum, and the player is constantly busy contemplating how to increase experience and get the most out of his cult members. The game needs a higher top speed, as well as extra variety in the mission department. But the game does not deliver on any of the innovation and new ideas that the cult concept can support. The experience is well suited for newcomers to the genre but makes little effort to tweak its core ideas. Honey, I Joined a Cult makes it clear that Sole Survivor Games are good at creating a competent management title, but I really want to see them try to add a twist to the formula in coming projects.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: In Honey, I Joined a Cult, you’re tasked with building an “organisation” that extracts donations from its members. The veneer of being a genuine bona fide organisation is applied so paper thin, you’re really under no pretence. Whether you’re running the Cult of the Worm, the Lark of the Covenant or the Children of Saurus, your mission is to scam people for money, without drawing too much heat from the authorities, so you can totally get away with it.Talking of layers, this game is as simple as it is deep — there’s a vast amount of research you can conduct to help improve your ‘organisation’, from the basics of upgrading your toilets from simple buckets to actual genuine porcelain, to helping your glorious leader realise their grand plan, whatever that may be.This is just one aspect of the depth of each NPC — given the sheer amount of them and the various ways in which they view the world, it’s a genuinely impressive feat that it already looks and feels this polished.What we have at the moment is a charming, funny and well-balanced management sim that is as difficult as it is fun.- Solid structure after learning the basics- Successful aesthetics- Creates an atmosphere that feels very much on theme- Every bit as addictive as a management simulation can get- Long tutorial - Some obstacles in menu navigation- Overall the game brings very little by ways of innovation to the genreDISASTER | BAD | MEDIOCRE | OKAY | GOOD |  | AMAZING | MASTERPIECE

_childDocuments_.review: This could be a good game but it seems to be another game that was never played by the devs.There is so much to micromanage and QOL missing and it takes about 20-30mins to realize that:* no way to disable pause on ceremony* no way to mass dismiss followers* research stops when one project is finished even tho others are queued up. You have to micromanage* Members do not return from mission even tho the mission is done. You have to click complete just so you have something to micromanage* compound missions do not autocomplete when fulfilled. you have to micromanage* general editing of member skills/skilllevels through the room will always require you to reenter the member. Just let me mass remove skills.* The UI is oversized and overly complicated. It does not have to be. _childDocuments_.review: I wish i can give this a neutral rating. Its really fun to start but end game is empty. At a point it becomes just waiting for research to complete. The member/follower count cap is kinda dumb imo, staffing limitations are an annoying painful experience with this system. I'm towards the very end of the tech tree and have zero urge to keep going. It doesn't feel worth it.Also with the current recruitment system there is no urgency to maintain members. If they leave oh well, just recruit your followers. Followers are easy to get and bleeding them is almost beneficial because the fresh ones won't be bored with anything. At a point when i was mid game in my compound i wall off a huuuuge section of my base....for like 3 hr. My members kept dying except for 6 (the number of beds i hadn't walled off.). This was literally like a non-issue. I just kept recruiting followers and did heat missions to counter act the heat gained. Heat is the rating for police attention....no idea where it triggers but i stopped paying attention to this, it was at 300pts at a point. I didn't have any idea what was happening but it was such a non-issue i just kept building things until i realized what happened. Also something that really annoyed me is the lack of the ability to set hours of operation. I spent 1hr designing a perfect schedule for 24hr service because there are people walking around the streets 24/7.... no matter what followers only show up like 9am-9pm. Its a super fun game early on and if they develop out the recruitment system, and add a point to the end game i'll change my rating. In comments is a picture of my compound.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game through twice now and I still had to think really hard about whether I should review it positively or negatively. I particularly enjoyed:HOWEVER:Ultimately, there's definitely something special about this game that keeps me coming back. It's incredible for the first game made by a team of only two people, and they clearly put a TONNE of work into it. But I feel like the management sim genre is a really finnicky one and one annoying mechanic can throw off the whole game. In this case, there are quite a few annoying mechanics. Ultimately when I'm talking to others about management sims this never comes to mind as one to whole-heartedly recommend to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game at first. I had a lot of fun customizing my cult and watching them do their cute, little cult jobs. I put in 20 hours with my first cult and was getting close to the finale when I get a game crashing error. I restart the game, and get the error again. I ask about it in the forums and was told to send my game file over. I got a confirmation email that they received my report and have heard nothing in two weeks, except they sent me an email asking me how good of a job they did. So while I like the game itself, I would not recommend it because you might not make it to the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: Ignore the hours played I just let it run in the background while I chipped away at it. The early game is well fleshed out, by the middle game you have a good idea what is happening and if you pay attention won't have too many unpleasant surprises. End game needs serious work, it becomes super grindy and the last 50% of the game or so was me afking and clearing the popups so it would progress. The game forces you to keep improving your prestige but the lag is just a tad off. But beyond changing the architecture around periodically there isn't a whole lot to do while you grind out the special research and influence. Still, original rec holds but needs more work that I originally anticipated.  Iffy recommendation, the core game is there but there are some weird and rather frustrating bugs that require a level of micro that shouldn't be necessary. People dying from starvation and sleep deprivation when there is ample food and bed available for example, the scheduling UI also needs serious work.  I have only made it to about mid level and annoying mechanics/issues aside I am loving it, these types of games are my addiction (look at my Rimwold play time), the vibe of the game is great, art style wonderful and the humor just perfect. If you want a totally baked game, maybe wait a bit but if you want to support the Devs and financially comfortable with it I personally don't mind the purchase, as long as they keep improving and tweaking.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a cult management game where you never feel like you are managing one. Just changing a couple of names and a few aesthetic details, the game could be about managing a summer camp.Speaking of aesthetics, the game is a shameless copy of Prison Architect. VERY shameless. But without the challenge of having to build an optimized base.The building mechanics does not add anything to the game. The space to build the base is limited and cannot be increased, although it is not necessary. There are many types of rooms that can only be built once, thus limiting the potential of the game and making the gameplay unnecessarily long. In addition, the position and size of each building have little influence. The internal organization of the rooms does not matter at all. This mechanic is limited to building a room with four walls, putting a door on each wall and filling it with items randomly. No matter what you put or where, the cultists will walk over it with no problem.Forget about the micromanagement of space and infrastructure. The bigger and more cluttered a room is, the more prestige (more attractive) it will have. A communal sh¡thouse with a wall full of toilets works better than a system of individual toilets. A giant barracks works better than designing and building individual rooms.The gameplays are bland and boring. Most of the time I was playing at maximum speed to get the investigations developed faster, and to gather money more quickly.Having to wait for research development is the only thing that lengthens the game. For the rest, the management of the base is mostly absurd and bland.Most of the time is spent waiting, not playing. I have played almost the entire game at the highest speed. And, if there was an option to make time go by even faster, I would have used it.Again, this is not even a management game. It is a game of developing technologies. With a few small adjustments it is possible to have the base perfectly working with minimal modifications during the game.Most of the time consists of waiting to gather the necessary resources, and waiting for the investigations to develop. The best way to play it is having it minimized while watching a movie.The mission system, a key element of the game, is not well integrated. It does not make much sense with the rest of the gameplay. It seems like a forced obligation rather than an element that adds value to the experience.I could describe my entire gaming experience as slow, boring, and pointless. I see zero variability and zero repeatability.They have tried to mix many elements (building, resource management, RPG-style cultist stats, external missions, tech tree developments, etc.) without going too deep into any one. They are not developed or cohesive enough to fit well with each other and have internal coherence. It looks like a game with many independent elements put together.The ending is totally anticlimactic. So much effort... for nothing. A simple static final screen without any conclusion.In summary: Many ideas pushed together that do not fit well. They wanted to have in the same game several elements that they saw in other titles and found interesting, but without achieving internal coherence.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR: Game is fun but endgame is not because you're just waiting around until you can press the "win button" and unceremoniously get a still image as a victory screen after 30 hours of playtime.I like this game in concept and I want this game to do well. I hope that it becomes a game I revisit after a while of not playing after it gets more updates/DLC. The game was fun for probably half or two-thirds of my playtime but I feel like end-game needs a serious adjustment because it's pretty boring and unrewarding, resulting in me feeling like I wasted my time. I played at 1x speed in the beginning but eventually ended up leaving the game on 3x speed while pausing the game to make decisions. At endgame, I felt like even 3x speed was too slow and I wished there was a x6 or even x10 speed to make the waiting more bearable.I beat the game on day 130 and got the Darkness Hellfire ending on standard difficulty. Near the end, I was overflowing with cash so I just had to wait around for enough influence to alter my cultists. I played slowly and carefully so I never got heat above 200, never got a mood break, never got a single protest, and never got raided. It felt rewarding to "play well" and win without raising the public's suspicions at the time, until I looked at the achievements. For some reason, they actually want you to play in a way I thought was "playing poorly" because there are achievements for getting protested and even losing the game. Why? It seems so counter-intuitive.The research tree seems big but once you finish it, there ends up being a lack of meaningful progression. This is because everything on the research tree is just better than what came before so there's no reason not to use the best stuff you can afford (aka a lack of horizontal progression). The leader sanctum was interesting in concept but I felt like it took too long to get only for it to really just be another research tree despite the game hyping it up from the very beginning.As time passes, the game seems to get "harder" and I use that in quotes because it mostly just got more annoying to deal with. Your leader makes more and more demands and there's no way to get rid of or change these permanent demands so you're forced to use the best stuff anyway or your cultists will suffer mood penalties. I'm guessing these are completely random but I ended up getting a demand that made me create separate bathroom stalls for my entire compound or suffer a mood penalty for 6 hours while also later getting one that made it so each room needed to be at least prestige level 7 or my cultists would suffer a mood penalty for 1.5 hours. The issue is that small rooms can't hold enough decorations to make it to the higher levels so I ended up ignoring that last demand for the bathrooms because it wasn't worth renovating my entire compound just to negate a 1.5 hour mood penalty.The missions aren't very interesting and they don't feel all that rewarding and seem to give roughly the same rewards despite gradually increasing in difficulty over time. The "choose your own adventure-style" random events during missions are pretty interesting though and often full of references. Even though I researched the ability to go on multiple missions at a time, I never ended up doing more than one at a time because the missions requirements for success were so high that I needed to save my best people for them. Other than the random missions from newspaper deliveries, there's not much variation in the missions either. I would have liked to see a wider range of mission difficulties at a given time instead of it seemingly scaling linearly over time and I would like the more difficult missions to be fewer in number but give better rewards (e.g. difficulty 10 missions giving prestige level 7 decorations and up instead of prestige level 4 like all the other difficulties).The currencies the game needs you to manage are pretty hit and miss, imo. Money, influence, and maybe heat are fine as-is but I feel like faith and PR need adjustment. PR seems like it should do more than it does because what it seems like it does is just increase the probability of getting better followers. Reaching the max PR of 1000 was pretty easy, seemed kinda pointless other than getting to 700-800 for a chance at very good followers, and I rarely seemed to lose any PR so it was mostly just a straight line to the top. Faith wasn't really an issue for me until the endgame because the the maximum cap of 3000 felt too low. Doing research in the leader sanctum costs faith and cultists have faith upkeep which increases the higher level your cultists are. During the endgame, I dropped down to below 250 from the max of 3000 faith because I decided to do research in the leader sanctum. A cap that low disincentivizes having a bunch of high-level, good followers in the endgame despite the fact you need high-level, good followers in the endgame to complete any mission, which the game requires you to do in order to beat the game.Overall, I'd say this game is slightly above average but I'm looking forward to more updates to make it even better.

Also with continuing updates it is definitely keeping me engaged. Loving the new random events that you read in the papers.The tech tree is very straight forward to use and the ability to assign your cultists is super useful. Though I would like to have the ability to build more than 1 of certain room types.... Hypno just saying ;)Also a suggestion to the developers. Most Cults, at least on TV, seem to be self sustaining in regards to food. Maybe a future update include elements like crop growing, can buy seeds like we buy ingredients for the kitchen, and then harvest crops to make certain foods, from there we could have new skills for farming (Green Fingers) and maybe new techs that allow to start farming and then farm other crops.I'd totally recommend this game to others, a totally enjoyable game.
