_childDocuments_.review: I love the idea of the game, the humor is silly and the game has solved some typical management game issues in good ways (your cult members will get up in the night and get a snack if they're hungry, pretty smart little fellows). I firmly believe this is going to be a great game with some more work.But I have to say, right now it almost feels kind of empty. Don't get me wrong, there's quite a few rooms to research and build. But there's no fun objectives. The unspoken objective is to grow rich, which seems a bit too easy, and to grow your cult, which seems a bit pointless (since everything runs smoothly with just a few members and followers). Not even the slightest 'if you want to unlock this you need x amount of members/followers'. It even starts really nicely with an introduction story, but the story is abruptly cut off and the game basically says 'do whatever you want now'.There's a few things that still need to be ironed out and that's completely understandable for an early access game. There's a warning if a cult member is starving but if their health is declining for other reasons the game won't tell you. To change the sermon type you need an altar, yet the altar can neither be purchased nor researched. Moving, deleting and upgrading objects still feels a bit clunky. All completely fixable things.In short, the game is on a good way, it's just not there yet for me.

_childDocuments_.review: In Honey, I Joined a Cult, you play a Prison Architect-esque management-tycoon game where you're in charge of running a cult, managing its gradual expansion while trying to keep under the radar of both the general public and law enforcement. It largely plays the same as Prison Architect, but focuses more mood management; in that sense it plays more akin to Rimworld.I do not want to dissuade people or the devs too much as I enjoyed the game for what it is, but as it stands at the moment, there is a solid base for gameplay however there are some glaring concerns that affect my otherwise glowing review of the game.The first is that it seems a bit  sandboxy, in the sense that after you play for a bit, it ends up feeling samey. It's open-endedness with being able to "create your own cult" does not lend to its uniqueness from playthrough to playthrough. Perhaps having a campaign of some sort with unique scenarios will help in improving this aspect, as playing the standard sandbox mode ends up feeling repetitive with, to be fair, some changes depending on which "path" you take for divine inspirations (which could be thought of as overarching themes for your cult). Additionally, having more events or more dynamic pawns akin to Rimworld would make it more unique per playthrough, but perhaps that may be asking too much at the moment given the current state. Hopefully this will be improved in the future.The second is that the AI seems... absentminded? For example, the AI will wander around while working doing nothing as there is work to be done, then decide "Oh, this needs to be fixed" then walk over to it, and repeat. It was beginning to get annoying to see two of my maintenance Watchers idle around while there were 6-8 broken items that needed to be fixed, sometimes requiring manual intervention on my end to get them to fix something. I hope that this will be improved in future patches.My final complaint is how hygiene works. My understanding is that washing a pawn's hands after using the toilet only grants a  at cleaning the pawn. Which severely increases the likelihood of a Watcher getting injured from poor hygiene, especially in early game. It's really frustrating to see injuries created from eating without washing hands, akin to Rimworld's "ate without table" debuff. This should certainly be switched to a bar like Mood or Health, with the differing tiers of sinks offering faster filling of the hygiene, a higher maximum of the hygiene bar, or something similar. At least in this way, it puts some control back into the player's hands about how they should handle hygiene, rather than making it pure RNG about whether or not someone will get an illness from poor hygiene.Now, the final verdict. Is it worth ~20 USD/23 CAD off-sale? At this point, I would say yes. There's enough content to last a dedicated player about 12-15 hours per playthrough. Despite my grievances about the game, I did enjoy it for what it was and I am excited to see what they'll be able to do in the future, with my main hope being the implementation of a campaign mode. Unfortunately, I have not played Rimworld Ideology yet so I do not have a frame of reference to compare the two.

Every once and a while when trying to complete missions the menu for your characters would bug out and would not open up. Or what I usually like to do is send one on a mission then preselect characters for another mission I cannot open the window again even if i select the little pencil indicating to edit the characters chosen. The only viewable windows are the mission screen and the map. This will happen pretty frequently which is annoying because I can't get missions done for that day. I would try to save and quit and come back but it would only seem to reset when the next missions would load up for the next day.2.) If you have characters who have multiple jobs set to high priority your characters will bug out and run in circles bc they don't know where to go. Even trying to manually select the character and clicking on a job or action to override would not work. They would continue to cycle on a circle until the "calendar shift" you set for them would change. For example one of my characters was suppose to assign themselves a job. However, they were running around in circles as if they didn't know what job to do. Tried to select a job to override but it would not change anything. They finally stopped running around in circles once his "work time" on the calendar was changed to "free time" then they went to go do things like use the toilet and go to the rec room. Now this could hinge possibly hinge your gaming experience like causing a mood break for a character because I had this happen on a separate occasion. One of my characters was on break but then was circling around not knowing what to do first eat or toilet. I tried to select one and same thing happened -- could not override they finally shifted schedules on calendar by that time they had a mood break.3.) This just recently happened but all characters in my game are now bald. Which doesn't bother me or effects the game play experience in any way. However, being a visual learner I remember who my characters are and what skill sets they have based on their appearance first then I check the name (because some can look the same) But now that their physical differences are all bugged out and they all look like clones its difficult for me to differentiate who is who to, to send to a job that needs to be done so I would have to pull up the menu with the characters are go through the skill tree and figure it out that way.This isn't a bug but something for the developers to think about.1.) It's really annoying that selling objects and deleting walls does not give us a gain back in money. You basically just lose out on that money and it's really annoying when you're a beginner and starting off early. As you progress a little further money won't be an issue but before for the people playing the game for the first time I would wait to start building complex rooms too early on where you might have to modify later. Because if you decide you don't like the design or want to redo it deleting walls or redoing outdoor flooring will start tacking up if you don't know how to make money at first. Example: I started off building the bedroom and making little "cubicles" for all of my characters which I kept having to redesign because I didn't place the room in a good spot to begin with.All in all, this game is a pretty fun time waster but with especially the bugs that I've come across and the inconvenience of a few aspects of the game that you keep learning about as you go (obviously not talking about game challenges, but the user functions provided for you on the game) just makes it a little more less appealing to play the more progress I make.

_childDocuments_.review: As a management sim, the game is ok - it's fairly basic: you manage the well being of cultists and followers, working hours and jobs based on your cultists' skill points and quirks. You manage the overall fame and infamy of the cult. In time, you unlock research and rooms to progress down a major cult theme. For the first 1/2 of the game, it's quite fun learning the mechanics, unlocking new rooms.. but then the game grinds to a slow crawl to death as you realise there's not much more to the game. Once you have all the rooms unlocked, you realise the game just throws a bunch of the same things at you to gate your progress to slightly improve each room while you work towards finishing your cult. Firstly, the game really needs a x5, x10, x30 speed mode. Secondly, what's the reason for limiting the number of research rooms I can build? Thirdly, there needs more variety to earn unique cult points (sending 4 cultists on a 30 hour job to earn +5 Darkness is ridiculously slow progression).Unfortunately, despite the 3 cults having slightly different mechanics to each other - the difference and core feedback loop doesn't encourage me to continue to play this game. As you can see from Global Achievement Stats only 0.8% of players have completed the game on each of the major cults. It means that most players won't be bothered 100% achievement hunt this - it's a boring slog. Would be much better if they implemented higher fast-forwards.

_childDocuments_.review: Honey I Joined a Cult is a fun game in which you build a cult in the hopes of gaining faith, enlightenment, and of course copious amounts of money from your followers. The game has a minimalist artistic design in which characters are moving across a grid and not being directly controlled. Think of Rimworld or Prison Architect. The gameplay is engaging and the theme of cults makes it that much more fun to play with and watch play out before you.  The game intrigued me because it resembled Rimworld, one of my favorite games. The game has many similarities but is not as big of a sandbox in comparison. You have rooms that you can build and items that are associated with them directly. You can edit the schedules of each cultist, which is helpful, some missions come in the night. If you like Rimworld you will find a warm familiar feeling playing this.  I like the organization of the pop up screens and how things like missions and the building menu, as well as character details frame the screen when you need to look at them while still focusing on the center of the screen. This was great for building and trying to look at multiple people, moving around, etc. The UI in general is attractive and pleasing to the eyes. The filter menu really helps navigate and build rooms without having to scroll through pages of items. Very nice quality of life inclusion. The settings menu does not offer much control other than standard basic controls, but does have a night time performance mode in the graphics settings if that happens to be valuable to you. The game is quite funny and brilliant in design and scratches that itch of wanting more games in a similar vein of Rimworld. Building is simple and everything is well organized and the tutorial does a good job of setting you on the right path towards acquiring more followers to your cult. I enjoy that I can play this casually while listening to a podcast or music, being able to multitask adds value in management games for me. I absolutely love this game and I look forward to seeing it evolve with the roadmap the devs have planned. Dang good!

_childDocuments_.review: So far, I'm in love. The way you manage your members' needs is similar to that of the Sims, and the pixel art brings back memories of Stardew. I also adore the concept of trying to create a successful(?) cult in a humorous, self aware way.I will say, there's a few bugs I've noticed so far, and while they aren't game breaking, they're definitely a bit irritating when you have limited funds.1. When I tried to turn paths back into grass with a line, it spends the money but doesn't change. I had to do each individual square in order for it to work.2. At one point I attempted to create a new foundation that was rather large (around $300). Once again, it spent my money but there was no foundation to be seen. This was especially frustrating because it was about an hour and a half into gameplay, so I didn't have a whole lot of money to work with.3. Sometimes, when trying to change a follower's job, they'll just continue to do their current job and ignore the reassignment. I will say, however, it could have been my fault for accidentally assigning them to something I told them to ignore, but it's happened with three different followers from what I can recall.Like I said, these bugs aren't game breaking, and I'm only bringing them up for the benefit of the devs! I know you all are a small team, so I wanted to make you both aware in case you weren't. I look forward to future updates and many more hours of gameplay!

_childDocuments_.review: The game developer hates you. I don't know how else to explain some of the atrocious design decisions they've made here. It's essentially a simplified version of Rimworld, but somehow the devs have made the interface harder to use even though they have less systems. Rooms are a pain in the ass to manage because room specific furniture can't be placed anywhere except in that room, so if you want to do something like say switch the locations of two rooms, it's an absolute pain in the ass. First, you have to re-designate both rooms, and then, since each room is already filled to the brim with random crap, you're doing tetris to slowly switch the furniture of the two rooms when there's huge amounts of free space outside these rooms that you could use as a holding area but the game won't let you!Heat management is awful, there's only one real way to reduce heat which is heat reduction missions. The Ministry of Propaganda is counter-intuitive, you'd think that it reduces heat and increases PR, but no, it increases heat instead! This is so confusing that I've seen game guides claim you can use the Ministry of Propaganda to reduce heat.The game also doesn't autosave when you exit, and the sometimes prompts you to save first but if you say you want to save it doesn't create the save automatically, it just sends you back to the menu and you have to save manually and then try exiting the game again?? Have the devs played an actual video game before?It's clear the devs don't actually know what made Rimworld fun, they just re-skinned it while making the game more restrictive and removed all complexity from the game. Well, the more complex stuff was what made Rimworld good, without it the devs are struggling to come up with interesting game mechanics to keep the players interested in playing. Protests which are supposed to be this game's version of combat(?) I guess, are horrible and require way too much micro-management. Not to mention you don't even get rewarded after it! The heat reduction is minimal, you don't gain any influence from it, nor any items. It's just an annoying mechanic you're forced to interact with or be punished. At least Rimworld combat was both punishing and rewarding. A big raid also means lots of loot. Plus you could build your base to better manage raids, which places interesting design constraints in base building. In this game, which strips out the combat and only has base-building, you can't even design your base to better handle the negative events the game throws at you, heat management is literally a matter of not interacting with the game because all interesting game-play elements generate heat and the only way to reduce heat is one mission type that you only get one of a day, which for big cults is barely enough to manage the passive heat your cult generates.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest, the reason I picked up this game is because I loved Cult of the Lamb and I wanted to try some other management games like it. I was drawn to HIJAC because of the groovy artstyle and the base building aspect, as well as the more "realistic" modern-day depiction of the Cult that would be a neat contrast to CoTL's fantasy cult. I was surprised that I was not, in fact, playing as the leader of the cult, which in hindsight was foreshadowing how little control I would have over the game. There is so much ♥♥♥♥ to manage that it's humanely impossible to keep track of it all. You need to keep track of every single minute detail, down to the schedules of each individual cultist. Speaking of, every single NPC in the game has their own set of stats that you need to keep track of and level up, which happens at a snails pace and makes them effectively useless for anything. The UI is clunky and ugly as sin, and each menu acts like a pop-up add that you have to manually close when you're done using, and each one takes up at least a third of the screen, making the game feel claustrophobic.The customization of the game is severely limited too. You don't even get to choose the theme of your cult until you've researched at least a dozen prerequisites beforehand, and in that time you're stuck with the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ options for cult quality of life, the upgrades for which are locked behind grating waits for the research tree. This game is so unnecessarily complicated, with so many useless mechanics and micromanagement that it feels bloated and claustrophobic, with very little actually being accomplished, with incredibly long waits between stuff actually happening, even with in-game time being sped up. All in all, it's actually fitting that you don't get to play as the cult leader, because you're not the leader. You're not even the god. You're a grunt doing all the game's work for it, and seeing little to no returns for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game in its current early access state.  But like all early access titles, it suffers from balancing & technology progression issues (in terms of unlocking reasearch) as well as the lack of endgame content. For a few examples of lacking content: I can't see a use for the prison/cell doors than cosmetics, no upgrades for the canteen, people constantly getting sick from eating with "dirty hands", the cult being unable to grow their own food on the compound (become fully independent of society lol) or expand the compound to have more access to land to build on, etc...I hope it will mean something more in the future.  Fortunately, the clean aesthetically-pleasing UI and the core gameplay is so relaxing to play through and easy to get immersed in, it's given me all sorts of ideas and hopes for future updates.  Right now, I'm really keen on more missions/endgame content updates.  At the moment, the endgame is essentially a Doomsday cult but I hope to see some variance soon.  It would be pretty interesting for example, to build a cult before destroying the world and then continuing that cult in the post-apocalyptic wasteland.  Sigh...one can dream.

_childDocuments_.review: First 5 hours or so I had fun, maybe a bit longer than that then the boredom happened. I think it was around in game day 30 because I was around there when I went online to see how long this game was to decide if I was going to stick with it. The fast forwards isn't fast enough so I started watching something and playing this a bit in the background. I got to the point where I felt like I was progressing faster and it would make the game harder with little warning by adding new rules like walking into a room with less than a prestige level of 7 will give the characters negative stats... so I get to clutter up my Cult with a bunch of decorations to make it look stupid to improve the room levels. Some of the room levels refused to go up, do they count towards this? no idea, it's not explained. This is about the point where I slowly realized I do not like this game anymore. So later they impose negative modifier for my bedroom being below a comfy level. Well the bedroom is maxed at 50 prestige and no one likes it so I take it I should have unknowingly focused on the bedroom when researching stat upgrades long ago to improve the beds. Now it would be different if things progressively got harder or gradually these rule sets were put in and explained. Instead they were not, you are having an okay time then out of nowhere here is a permanent negative modifier to inconvenience you. So all my members started to leave the cult after that modifier. Played this game for 12 hours with no one leaving or issues, they throw in a random new rule with no warning and barely explained and I went from never having a cult member leave to all of them leaving over 3 days. Made it to day 85 before I closed the game. Was there something I could do different? That's why I give this a negative review, I didn't care enough to Google it to find out because I had just been going through the motions for an additional 5 hours and things never really got better after I started getting bored. It's not that old so maybe they will patch it to make me enjoy it more later. I didn't down right hate it but I would not recommend it as it is now.2 crashes, it has auto save. I don't think I lost too much progress when it did.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, this is the second time I changed this review and Steam really needs a "Mixed" button - I didn't hate this game and can see other people having fun with it, it just started to bore me after a few hours. However the end-game is plain bad so I went with "Thumbs Down" in the end.So I really liked the idea of the game - creating a cult in the 70s - and a lot of the basics are done well. The design is cool, cult creation is a lot of fun and watching the money roll in while your cultists treat followers with pseudo-scientific procedures is pretty great. That fact that the creators added a few mini games is cool too since it breaks up the monotony thats an issue for titles like this sometimes.And this is were things start to get less fun. It's an idle game and a lot of the tasks you have to repeat aren't challenging or interesting. Repairing toilets, assigning cultists to missions, picking underwhelming research options etc. Best case scenario: Your cult runs like a well oiled machine and you dont have to do anything. I tried the game on a harder difficulty too but that didn't make it more challenging, just more annoying. The game is also not as complex as similar titles which isn't a huge deal but adds to the monotony.Speaking of monotony: The music is pretty underwhelming. As far as I can tell there are only two rather similar songs included. I only played for a few hours and can't bear those tunes any longer. Thats kinda frustrating since the setting and various cult options scream for more variety here. (What's weird is that there are 5 songs on the DLC soundtrack - maybe it's a bug, maybe they play later in the game, I dont know...)My biggest issue is that story and main objective weren't enough to motivate me. Unlike in other games you are not fighting for survival so the things you do often feel pointless. I didn't really care for my individual cultists either, even though I am usually a sucker for that kind of thing. They have very little backstory and I've never seen them interact with one another. Thats kinda sad and a feature like that would have gone a long way.However, I was curious about the path my cult would take and that motivated me to keep playing. And while that wasn't ideal to begin with - I didnt keep playing because it was huge fun or I cared about my cult - the ending was just horrible. The game starts to throw annoying stuff at you and adds pointless tasks to prolong the finale. Whats even more annoying is that it doesn't play out on screen, there isnt even a cutscene. You just press a button and the game ends - what a letdown!In short: If you really dig the setting and enjoy idle games in general chances are you'll have some fun with this one too. _childDocuments_.review: 30h 2/10 1 if you save before choosing a "theme" and then play through the ending 3 times No, but you don't need a guide No Yes, but using the 4 save slots can help out with this. Save before you choose a theme Yes, the 100k influence is quite a grind No No No No No, you can play on the easiest difficulty NoHoney, I Joined a Cult is an awesome tycoon kinda game in which you run a cult and try to keep your inner circle believing in what you say, but also get more followers to get more money and influence. And if that isn't enough, you try to keep the heat as low as possible otherwise people will start to demonstrate before your building and that will not do any good for the mood of the people in your inner circle. I love this kind of unique theme. I enjoy building theme parks/ hospitals and things like that, but those more unusual ones just feel refreshing. It is nice to explore this kind of themes and what to do different. Here it made sense to send your people on missions to reduce the heat or get more pr so higher quality people want to join your cult. And having to hold ceremonies every 24h to keep your people believe in you made sense as well. It took me a bit to get used to the game, not everything was clear at once. The game does a good job of trying to explain everything but quite a lot is happening, so I didn't memorize everything from the tutorial at the beginning. I would recommend doing the tutorial at the beginning, as that also is an easy way to get the achievement for holding a 5-star Sermon. What I also liked was that the game told me how to get influence when it recognized that I struggled with that a bit.  A few things I would love to see in the game are a few more Quality of Life features. For example, you have to order ingredients for your cook to make food. I would love to see a button to just order everything to max capacity at the top o the screen, or the highest quality food at the top, now those are on the bottom, which means you have to scroll down every time you have to order food. Kinda the same thing with the followers, later on, you get options to see the quality of the followers, but those where you can see the information from in the followers menu are at the bottom, so again you have to scroll down. A way to be able to send away multiple people from your inner circle (aka Watchers) or followers without having to open their menu and send them away and then open the main menu again for the next one would also be a welcome addition. These are all small things but would make the game a lot more friendly in my opinion. The achievements are mostly what you expect in a management/tycoon kind of game like this. Get an X amount of all the different resources. Get good quality people, place decor items, and more things like that. There is an achievement for losing the game, this is easily done by turning off the vending food and don't make your Watchers any food. There are achievements for the ending with each theme and there are 3 themes in total. For those achievements I would highly recommend waiting with selecting a theme very late in the game so you have unlocked all the other stuff and have a nice cult, then make a save which you only use to restart and choose the other themes when done with one theme. The game only has a few save slots, so be very careful to not save over that one save slot you used for this.

_childDocuments_.review: So when I first heard about this game back in 2018 I was thinking it sounds like a right laugh, I was anticipating this release and couldn't wait. The dissapointment to see that even after 3 years of development that it comes to steam in "Early Access". After playing about an hour of this game I can see why it is in Early Access... what have the developers been doing those 3 years? I will not accept the pandemic being an excuse as this game was a year in development before that hit. With a publisher like Team17 behind them I would have thought they would have had a better time getting this out faster with some extra support? Obviously not.About the game itself...You build a base to house your cult, you keep the needs and wants up to make sure that all is well and you don't get caught by the police, you build rooms to provide services to get money and eventually recruit new members to your cult. Yeah.. pretty basic formula really.You can rename a lot of the bits and bobs, like the cult name, who they worship ect.. but thats really about it, its the same no matter which way you look at it. So "insert cult name here" is pretty much the only customisation you can do, the way you build the areas really doesn't seem to vary much, there seems to be only 1 way to play it. Build room A, bring in some money, research room B, build it, bring in some money, research room C... ect..ect...ectThis game needs more customisation, There needs to be an inbuilt editor to allow people to design their own idols, and/or at least Steam Workshop to allow modding. I don't know just doesn't seem as good as other games I have played that are like this before. Maybe I hyped it up in my mind too much thinking this was going to be the best "base builder management" game I have ever played, The fact it was cults gave it that comedic effect but it seems to have fallen short of actually being funny.Maybe wait for it to be discounted, I am sure it will feature on a Humble Bundle or Choice at some point - as a lot of these games seem to do - I got my copy through Humble with the 20% discount, and even then I still feel I have paid too much for this game.The plus side though from what I have seen of the game so far it seems well made, there doesn't seem to be many bugs or any real issues I have come across personally (not saying there isn't any just I havent seen them)I may give this another go when it is further in development, or when it comes out of Early Access, but if its taken 3 years to get here then I estimate I will see you all in another 3 years to update this review? But for now if you are after a game like this Prison Architect seems to have a lot more going for it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is kinda cool, but there are two things that really bug me about it.1. I dislike how foundations, walls, etc, just "magically appear" once you pay money to have them built, and it's all instant.  This game is similar closer to Prison Architect and RimWorld in the top-down art and genre, but even both those games required stuff to actually be built.  I'd really like to see them handle this better, but this in itself is not enough of a reason to not buy the game (it's early access, after all), but I guess I expected something better despite that).  Maybe they could hire workers who they pay with $$ until they can recruit enough workers who run on faith instead?  Who knows... but I don't like how it is right now.2. The influence mechanic makes no sense to me.  You use influence to research stuff (huh?).  And what can you research?  Well, more followers and members, sure... that part makes sense.  But that's less than 10% of the research tree.  I need influence just so I have the right to buy a toilet//bed/kitchen/whatever and until then, I have to sleep in a bag or poop in a bucket?  Really?  It's like the devs said "We need a tech tree cause all good games have tech trees" and yet couldn't figure out how to fit it in with a cult concept properly.  Considering this is such a significant part of the game, this is the main reason I can't recommend the game.Other than that, it's an okay game and you're getting what you think you're getting.Edit: So some dev said "hey... we've made some changes on our beta build..." so I went reading thru the patch notes, and see nothing related.  While some devs seem to really read reviews and take them to heart, I'm not sure these guys are one.  Maybe their discord community is better?

_childDocuments_.review: Really winds me up people leave a negative review on an early access game that has been out for literal days. Do you people not understand early access? One negative review starts with "Still needs a lot of work" - well done Sherlock. ITS EARLY ACCESS.Actual review - Really solid base to build off. Excited to see where this goes. Graphically it is a similar style to Prison Architect, a bit less similar to Rim World but in the same style as these games. Personally i'm quite a fan of this style. I would say so far it is most similar to Prison Architect in terms of gameplay. You build rooms, recruit followers & staff, and try to make money while keeping heat down. Buildings automatically appear when placed instead of any construction time. There are some great lines the followers speak when moving around. And they each have their own stats and traits too.Looking forward to seeing what is added. Depth is required across the gameplay loops. I agree with those who say they would like more "cult" related things. Very much a base simulator with a cult theme rather than being cult focused at the moment.I do like the missions and the "world" map, looking forward to more interaction and maybe more freedom to pick places on the map to send recruits with different outcomes, rather than being told the location?Some gameplay notes for the developers, should they read this:A softlock in the tutorial while placing down the 3 decor items in which I couldnt place the third one, but reloaded and worked fine after that. Sure that will be fixed in no time.Early game was good, lots to unlock and discover and was fun watching the followers use the rooms. Didnt find it too dificult though, just had to be patient for money. I would say that certain things break down far, far too quickly (bathroom objects) and the mechanics behind the janitors doesnt really make sense. They should be prioritising broken things. Because they go room to room cleaning, some days they dont have time to make it across the compound before running out of time and the broken items are not fixed and compound. Manually controlling the staff can fix this, but can be a pain.I would also say that there is balancing required around the number of followers you start with (less) and staff (more) to make the game a bit harder. I found I had not enough staff to operate all the therapies and modules, but i had over 100k in the bank come the mid game. Also, heat should be increased as i found it easy to hover around the 100 mark.

_childDocuments_.review: 2/5After several hours of managing the N.M.S.L. Communist Party (yes, that's the exact name I gave to my first cult) I am led to say that this game is too linear, doesn't give any incentive for finishing it (or playing it) and is essentially just a basebuilder with worse graphics than Evil Genius (yes, THAT version) and a few new ways to "end the world". Sure, it had its moments (viz, "send a cultist to lower Heat by performing an interpretative dance near the AG's office") but the surrealist humour infused in it (very reminiscent of Kingdom of Loathing or its single player successor games) or Theme Hospital can only go so far. Allowing for modding tools (new hats, new graphics for pawns, new cult symbols) might provide more longevity with regards to engagement and immersiveness but this game is not for everyone. _childDocuments_.review: I am 32 years old.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: As I sunk over 40 hours into this game I have to admit it's entertaining enough.tl;drBasically it should be in early-access. I really enjoyed the game but it has plenty of problems and even if it had any replayability (which it has not) I wouldn't put myself through it again unless there was a mayor QoL overhaul.**Review**It leaves almost no replayability after you did a run, besides "seeing" the different endings which is basically a matter of choosing button A or button B at one point.The game is clearly inspired by Prison Architect and Rimworld, and really does a great job mixing them.A severe lack of QoL components and the above mentioned issue of replayability make me believe this was barely tested and I constantly find myself fighting against the game trying to do what I would assume is natural tasks in this game.Your cultists have traits, and with these traits comes proficiency to work certain rooms. It's a nightmare trying to keep track of what cultist is set to work what room, what traits they need and sifting through possible followers to recruit as cultists that would complement which cultists I already have. All this information is available to you just not at the same time so there's a barrage of menu-swapping, hoovering for tool-tips and comparing in order to make any kind of decisions.Cultists are also very needy and want their rooms to have a certain standard. The way to do that is by decorating the rooms with items that you mostly find when out on missions. Here's one of the biggest QoL issues, there's a ton of categories of decoration, that makes sense from an actual decorators point of view ('rugs', 'lights', 'paintings' and the more confusing 'decor' and 'ornament'). But there's no easy way to find the "best" items without scrolling through each menu and there's hundreds of items.The game is not hard and I don't think you can actually loose without actively trying, there's some values to keep track of like "faith" that replenishes to a point each day but depletes during the course of the day depending on how good your cultists are. This is actually a neat mechanic to make sure the player is playing "the right way", I can't explain it better but it's a good  thing.Other values are there only to slow down the player and to rack up hours (as in my situation) namely "heat" that's something that adds up each time you do missions (which are needed to improve your cult in various ways) along with more sinister activites and you don't need much of it for things to go south so the heat have to be kept under control (there's ways to reduce it) but this limits what you can do each day greatly and most of it will be spent just fast forwarding and waiting.There's plenty of minor irks I have with this game all across the board but then this would turn into a bug report/feature request more than a review.

_childDocuments_.review: Honey I Joined a Cult is a delightful simulation game that stands out with its high replayability and charming graphics. It's a game where you take on the quirky and engaging task of running your own cult, complete with all the whimsical and bizarre elements you could imagine.The game's art style is immediately captivating, featuring cute and colorful graphics that bring a light-hearted and humorous tone to the otherwise eccentric concept of cult management. The visuals are not just pleasing to the eye but also add to the overall enjoyment of the game, making each interaction and development more engaging.What truly makes 'Honey I Joined a Cult' shine is its replayability. Each playthrough offers a new experience, as you can experiment with different cult doctrines, base layouts, and follower management strategies. This variety keeps the game fresh and exciting, inviting you to explore new ways to expand and maintain your cult.However, it's worth noting that the game can become a bit grindy towards the end. As your cult grows, the management aspects can become more demanding, requiring a bit more patience and time to progress. While this might be a slight drawback for some players, the game's charm and the satisfaction of seeing your cult flourish often outweigh the grind.

_childDocuments_.review: When I was a kid, me and my bestie started a cult. We had a bible, a doctrine, an origin story - the whole schtick. This game lets me pretend I have the charisma to actually follow through on my dreams and see the ninja pixies THRIVING, Honey, I Joined a Cult a resource management game in which you establish and grow a cult. There are loads of flavour decisions you can make along the way to really make it feel like your new home from home. I ran through a 'darkness' playthrough, but will almost certainly be back to try out one of the others - one must never simply settle for the first cult one comes across. Said flavour decisions also had me literally laughing out loud multiple times, the sense of humour really balances the bleakness of cults with the surrealness of the real world. I also really enjoyed the aesthetics as the cuteness is also a brilliant example of the kind of humour i've poorly described above. there are still some teeny tiny bugs/choices that are questionable (e.g. my cult leader thinks outside is a very poor room so they're never happy enough for a 5* sermon) but nothing game breaking, or even anything that took away from my absolute enjoyment of the game. I c an't wait to see what the devs do next because this was just so much fun to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Honey, I Joined a Cult is a unique and engaging game that offers a complex and intriguing experience for those willing to dive into its intricacies. While it may not be for everyone due to its steep learning curve, it delivers on several fronts that truly shine and make it a must-try for those who appreciate deep, immersive gameplay.The user interface (UI) of Honey, I Joined a Cult is undoubtedly complex, but that complexity is part of what makes it so captivating. It may take some time to grasp all the mechanics, but once you get the hang of it, it's a rewarding experience. The depth of the UI allows for in-depth control over your cult's activities, and this level of control is essential for the game's success.The storytelling in this game is nothing short of captivating. As you learn to create and manage your cult, you'll be drawn into a narrative filled with twists and turns. Deception, manipulation, and the pursuit of faith and wealth form the core of the storyline, making it an enticing journey that keeps you engaged from start to finish.The cartoon graphics in Honey, I Joined a Cult are visually appealing, with a unique and vibrant style that adds a lot to the overall atmosphere. The funky music accompanying the game adds charm and immersion, making it an enjoyable sensory experience.The game dynamics, while admittedly challenging, are part of what makes it stand out. It requires significant time and effort to understand and truly master, but the payoff is worth it. The need for careful management of your cultists, resources, and schedules adds a layer of strategy that will keep you coming back for more. The priority-based task assignment system is a clever addition, allowing you to make crucial decisions and see their impact on your cult's growth and success.In conclusion, Honey, I Joined a Cult is a game that may not be for the faint of heart, but for those who enjoy in-depth management and storytelling, it's a hidden gem waiting to be discovered. The complex UI, captivating storytelling, stylish graphics, and challenging game dynamics make it a game that offers a unique and rewarding gaming experience. _childDocuments_.review: Title: Honey, I Joined a Cult: A Hilariously Entertaining Misadventure!Rating: ★★★☆☆ (3/5)Attention all thrill-seekers and potential cult enthusiasts, get ready for a wild ride with "Honey, I Joined a Cult"! In this zany simulation game, you'll dive headfirst into the quirky world of cults, hilariously embracing your inner follower while trying not to lose your mind (or your sense of humor) in the process.The game starts with a bang as you accidentally find yourself caught up in the alluring and enigmatic world of cults. The graphics are charmingly retro, perfectly capturing the absurdity of the cult's rituals and activities. You'll find yourself laughing out loud as you witness fellow cult members wearing the quirkiest robes you've ever seen or performing the most outrageous dances to please the enigmatic leader.The gameplay mechanics are engaging, as you navigate the delicate balance between appeasing the charismatic cult leader and maintaining your sanity. It's a rollercoaster of emotions as you try to impress the leader with strange tasks, which sometimes involve odd chores like convincing trees to grow faster or chasing butterflies for their "spiritual energy."However, as fun as "Honey, I Joined a Cult" can be, it falls short in terms of depth and longevity. The novelty wears off after a while, and the repetitive nature of the tasks can leave you yearning for more substance. Although the game introduces different cult factions and leader personalities, the core gameplay loop remains relatively unchanged.And here's where the shadow of "Cult of the Lamb" looms large. Despite being released much later, "Cult of the Lamb" offers a refreshingly immersive experience, with its deep narrative, complex character development, and challenging gameplay mechanics. It takes the cult simulation genre to a whole new level, leaving "Honey, I Joined a Cult" feeling like a humorous but ultimately limited precursor.In conclusion, "Honey, I Joined a Cult" is an enjoyable mid-tier game that will undoubtedly tickle your funny bone. The hilarious scenarios and quirky cult antics provide a decent dose of entertainment. However, if you're in the market for a more robust and captivating cult simulation experience, "Cult of the Lamb" is the superior option to delve into the captivating world of charismatic leaders, devoted followers, and plenty of dark humor. So grab your sacrificial butter knife and embark on the journey of a lifetime – just remember to keep your wits about you!

_childDocuments_.review: (Got as part of June Humble Bundle) Feels to me like a more relaxed, if less complex Prison Architect. My main issues are the lack of a x4 or x5 speed, which makes days in late game where you're just waiting for timers to finish take forever, and I feel like the games writing could have used more flavor. _childDocuments_.review: At its core, this game is a very scaled down version of rimworld with a funny motive on top. I struggled with the recommendation because for me it sits exactly in the middleground....but if i have to chose it dibs slightly towards the negative.I did like the game overall, situations that i hated were few but when they came, they came in force, so here are my top-2-stinkers:1) Adding a strong requirement to have individual bathrooms in a game where you have ~20 pawns that all need to poop at the same time every day sucks. It just sucks. It would be fine if some other game mechanikcs spread the poop-times out more, so you would get along with ~1 room per 5 pawns....but since such mechanics are missing the game really asks you to build upwards of 10 exactly identical bathrooms and does not offer a function to just copy an existing room.2) Demonstrations. Man....what were they thinking with this? I like the basic idea....but this game lacks a quick bar for you pawns like rimworld has and during a demonstration you need to quickly assign individual pawns to individual protestors. This means you need to pause the game, bring up the pawn overview (which covers the entire screen!!), chose a pawn, close the window, assign the pawn to the protestor, unpause the game, wait for the next protestor, repeat. I fail to put in words how unfun this is. It is so disgustingly bad that every single time a day started with a demonstration i had to fight the urge to simply quit the game in frustration. This event/mechanic is less playable and fun than any other part of the game. Annoyingly, the "Tier 2" event of this type (Police raid) is FAR more playable than this....but most of the time you will get this Tier 1 version. It is with no doubt in my mind the single worst thing about this game. It just sucks. I would have enjoyed the game noticeably more if this event would not exist.---There were other, much more minor things that i found not that great...like room decorations that are available in unlimited quantities being too weak in the second half of the game and the ones available in limited quantities being too much of a hassle for still too little prestige. For example, if you sacrifice a very-good recruit (which is the best quality and they are not that common) ou get an object of prestige 7. Placing 12 such items in a room makes this room 6*7 + 6*3.5 = 63 prestige....but you need 75 to reach the highest rating. This is for EACH INDIVIDUAL ROOM. Maybe that explaines why i hate the requirement to have 10-15 bathrooms so much. Sure, you don't have to decorate each room - but this is pretty much the core idea of this game: Building rooms and putting objects in them.I also did not like the way the game-room works. I would have MUCH preferred if you could have just upgraded the items in each category when you get them....but since each individual item will start to bore your pawns and put them on cooldown you will have to keep all of them...so by the end of the game you need a giant game-room plastered with 3 tiers of entertainment in each category. Minor complaint, really, but did not like it.---Overall the game is good....but none of its good parts were as strong as its weakest parts (looking at you, demonstrations!) were frustrating.The part i enjoyed the most was optimising my pawns, eliminating their quirks and negative traits, trying to get the best positive traits. This is what this game does well, in my opinion. In some rooms you can actually see and "feel" an impact from adding a worker with really good traits for the job. But then you realise that in order to do that you simply have to sit out days, watching you screen as you do absolutely nothing because it costs so much influence to do and the only way to get influence is to watch the game play itself....that's why i diped towards not recommended in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: + The concept is fun+ Enjoyable at sections of the game + Humour can be good sometimes- You have to actually start "queued" research after research is done, its legit just pre paying for the research. - Dismissing followers is tedious and requires 3-4 clicks every time - Repetitive- UI is large and feels unhelpful - You have to manually order ingredients every single time - Tier 3 bathroom items and still 97% of the notifications were someone got sick cause they didnt wash their hands and now have a small bladder- The themes sound cool but the only use I found for them was to finish the game- There is no refunding for buildings so make sure to save in case you screw up- Global debuffs excluding events are permanent with no way to remove them- Doors are not considered part of any room and because they have a prestige of 0 your cultists will receive a mood decrease anytime they go through them- You have to close the sermon menu every single time - You can only do one mission at a time for a long portion of the game- The playable area is extremely limiting• Whenever I altered the sermon time followers would get stuck in the hospitality room and would not leave until they got so mad they left the cult and then suddenly had the ability to walk through doors again...• Randomly cultists cannot be unassinged from a mission until the mission expires or you start the mission and abandon it. The menu says 0/X when this happens despite clearly saying next to the cultist "currently assigned to this mission" • I've had a large room missing its floor randomly when not assigned. • Frequent red exclamation marks over followers/cultists with no rhyme or reason or even a way to clear/ignore it. • Player-forced actions can be overwritten by NPCs.• Despite being outlined with green you cannot force a cultists to the canteen serving station, it just tells you to use the table instead, either its not an option and shouldn't be select able or make it select able. also, 100k influence cumulative is insane.

_childDocuments_.review: No, I'm not going to stop playing this game, but no, I would also not suggest it in it's current state. While the game is entertaining from an external standpoint (and actually hilarious once you play), unless you're into doing a lot of research or suffering for the art (the tutorial is *terrible*. Awful. Teaches you nothing.), I suggest you play a better balanced base-builder/tycoon. Though the game is still in development, so if they patched some bugs (I've had saves glitch beyond return, but there are autosaves. I've also had issues with not being able to place objects or respond to mission prompts.), balanced influence and prestige better (influence is just... not what it could be in the game. You basically never have enough of it, until you do for one precious moment, and then it's all gone again. Unless you don't use it enough, and you progress too slow for the missions and end up spending all of your influence on room boosts because you don't have enough gaudy objects that cost 12000 dollars in each and every one of your rooms so your followers are depressed because everything is ugly but you can't afford anything better because you don't have enough influence to research the next therapy room. And then post game it's basically useless, so, you know.), and allowed for more control over the units (Giving them their own toilets/bathrooms, them actually *following* a command when you give them one and not just going back to their last priority, etc.), the game would be a lot cleaner. I would also really like a measuring tool so we could measure our spaces without risking laying the wrong amount of foundation. Thanks, okay, bye.

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable little game, I like the visuals and different thematic directions you can go with your cult. Perfect if you enjoy a game like Rimworld but really want to focus on managing your cult and get rid of some of the more tedious aspects of colony management. On the whole, it's a relaxing, somewhat grind-ey management experience but the visuals, progressive unlocking of loot/upgrades, and interactive mission dialogs kept me invested (though the latter can get repetitive quick as there's not that many different ones).

_childDocuments_.review: Really cute game with limited replayabilityI'm a fan of this game in general. The graphics are great, it's cute, funny, and generally pretty entertaining. There's almost no bugs,Unfortunately, after your cult is set up, there's just...not much to do gameplay wise. I reckon I got about 10-15 hours in before my cult just basically ran itself while I all but ignored it. The music is great, but it plays over and over again and got slightly maddening until I turned it off. When I started receiving higher level missions, none of my cultists even had the skills to do them, even with the covert ops 'pre-planning' stage.  I had one character who had amazing skills, and none of my other cultists ever got to go on a field trip. I essentially just stopped being able to do them, but it didn't really matter, so it was just another mechanism to ignore.The different rooms are cute, and the game has a good level of complexity, I'd say it's a little easier to manage a cult than it is to manage a prison. (prison architect) recommended, but buy it on sale, and don't expect too much replayability!

_childDocuments_.review: Really love the concept and art style.I got a solid ~20-30 hours of enjoyment out of it for sure & it scratches that base building itch that I really loved from games like Rimworld.  My one complaint is the pacing.. There's a period towards the end of most games where you're trying to get all the influence needed to get final researches & there's pretty much no way you could lose, but you've still got a couple months worth of in game time of waiting to get more influence. This is less of a problem on certain cult types, but on one in particular ("peace & love") it's pretty bad,As of December 2022, it's just a couple solid patches away from being a really good game. Would still recommend it in the mean time though!
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: The game seems like it wants to be a somewhat sandboxy game that lets your cult and compound/temple become whatever you envision and still be playable. However, there are feedback loops in the game balancing that makes it very easy to have your cult go into a negative spiral of self implosion if you don't play the game "right". I'm not just saying the game is too difficult, because it is quite possible to understand the rules of the game and then to try to play optimally to win. But that's a whole different game experience than what seems to be advertised. If the game really is aiming to be a challenging min/max-fest, then a lot of elements seem out of place. If the game instead is aiming for the whimsical sandboxy style, then it should be better at adapting the difficulty so that the player feels the challenge but generally overcomes it even when venturing outside of the mechanically optimal.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: Overall it's not a terrible game, but its just too similar to other games to the point where I thought it was made by the same people at first (its not). If you play these games I am sure you see the heavy borrowing.The issue is the game itself is very bare bones, it leans heavily on the cult idea for laughs but very little for game play. I more or less brute forced my way through the whole game and spent the majority of it in fast forward mode waiting for research to finish. You can basically ignore follower level it won't matter much. You can't make multiple of several rooms which dramatically slows the game down. Money is a joke very early on and serves little purpose. Followers are heavily restricted to slow the game down, research is heavily restricted to slow the game down...I am sure you get the point. Build one of each room, hit fast forward until you get another room, repeat until done.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: A cute resource-management game, with nice sense of humour. Graphically pleasant, quite balanced and in some moments challenging. For the first game of Developers this is a good start. Gave me about 17 hours of playing, and in total maybe there were two hours with little to do. The remaining time was interesting and always gave me a bit of satisfaction for solved issue. Please remember this is a micro-management game, so checking carefully most stats / effects / numbers is quite common. All such games are basically just a glorified excel and drills down to numbers crunching. Many negative reviews points out 'flaws' which doesn't exist, perhaps the reviewer didn't spend enough time or didn't look carefully. Examples like 'lack of job priorities', 'lack of overview' or 'too much heat' are simply wrong, maybe in the time those were written those functions didn't exist yet?All in all - solid position, worth trying.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has tons of potential. At the same time, there are flaws that still linger.Pros:- Customization in almost everything. The Cult? You can change the appearance, name, and even titles of your cult's leadership at any time. Compound? Well, with enough cash, anything is possible. Difficulty? Grindfest or quick and dirty, we got you. Location? Well...- The midgame is slightly varied. The paths the cult can go in do have a unique feel to them. After playing through all 3 (as of writing this) paths, I can say that the difference isn't as big as some might like, but it is noticeable.- The End Game scene is satisfying, as you get to see your grand plan for the cult come true.Cons:- Heat is hardly a threat even on the highest multipliers if you save money and research propaganda center. Unless you're trying to speedrun, you most likely aren't going to get a protest or a police raid if you take your time. Heck, you may not even get a police raid despite wanting to see what is like (like myself).- The End Game, while satisfying to reach, is very grindy. It takes a lot of research and cash to actually finish the final task. Adjusting modifiers can help with that, but it still takes a lot of time to finish final research.- You will always start in the same location, get the same events, and have the same grass covered compound. The events themselves are varied, don't get me wrong. However, you will get repeats if you are trying to accomplish all 3 pathways. I wasn't bothered by this, but I'm sure someone will be.Overall, I give it a 8.5/10.It does scratch the spot where you actually run a cult where the cultists actually know how to take care of themselves, but at the same time it can get bland and can screech to a grindfest if difficulty is adjusted poorly.

_childDocuments_.review: Funny, relaxing, and charming. A small amount of attention to detail will more or less ensure you have no problems running your cult on normal difficulty if you don't rush too hard. The main issue is there's too much waiting for bars to fill up and not enough ways to fill those bars. The Divine Inspiration meter is particularly bad in this regard, and it drags out the endgame to the point where it gets fairly boring because it's a series of 5 long researches with attached missions. There is a certain lack of depth to the game at this stage that makes it fun, but unfulfilling. Workshop would probably improve this game significantly. A solid 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is highly addictive if you enjoy other simulation games such as Prison Architect, or to a lesser degree Rimworld. You build a cult form the ground up starting with 3 cultists and a cult leader. It is your job to provided for their needs while recruiting Followers which can eventually become Cultists after they have hung out and been bled dry of their money for a bit.Cultists can take on tasks such as running the various cult rooms or researching, cleaning, cooking etc.Followers exist to be recruited as cultists/resource generation primarily and other options are made available later in the game.After a bit of research you get to decide the direction of your cult and currently there are 3 Paths to choose from. (Darkness, Futurology, Peace&Love)Each path opens up new rooms, cult goals,costume pieces, and even some special cultists to recruit.After Choosing your path and researching its tree with your leader further you are given even more choices in regards to the direction you want to take your cult in.The game does not currently have a true sandbox mode but allows you to continue playing after reaching an ending. With that said to reach the end of the game you have to actively accomplish goals and finally press a button that triggers the ending where you can see your stats, and choose if you would like to call it quits or go back and continue on your cult building way. Currently, according to the devs in the discussion section, there are no plans to implement a stand-alone sandbox mode or mod support. However, they are open to it if enough people express an interest in it!Updates are made regularly and so far have added in a lot of great content and ways to play.Get this game if you enjoy games like Prison Architect and are looking for something new to play!May your followers be many, and your cultist dreams realized!

_childDocuments_.review: Several among us are likely to have that one friend or relative, or we at least know someone who’s a teensy bit too much into alternative medicine or guided meditation. You can tell they’re not deepening a practice or applying the result of some research to a new topic, but rather they’re coasting on a rush of feel-good vibes that they only maintain in chasing the Next Great Thing. Sometimes, the Next Great Thing is a stand-up desk, or maybe a keto diet. At other times, it’s a cult.Honey, I Joined a Cult takes a subject matter that’s usually mired in uncomfortable bits of Pop Culture tidbits, like knowing about Marshall Applewhite’s desire to ride the tail of the Hale-Bopp comet to some perceived astral plane, or Japan’s Aum Shinrikyo and its infamous sarin gas attacks carried out in Tokyo’s subway system – and skirts right past all that grue to effectively poke at the simple truth behind most cultists; which is that these people are lost, in need of guidance – and sometimes given to a bit of the old word salad. That, at least, can make them funny. So you’re a quack and a scam artist – or a guru, naturally – and you’ve just hatched you next get-rich-reasonably-quick scheme; which is to start a cult. The basics are straightforward, seeing as a brainwashing routine couldn’t survive a constant immersion in the outside world. Your job is to see to every single need of your cultists and to arrange for the gradual expansion and eventual prominence of your ad-hoc bit of faux spirituality. It starts with the basics (food, rest, hygiene and a place to pray) and quickly expands with the need to not only draw in other faithful, but also maintain what you’ve built for yourself. You need to see to your followers’ crumbling mental health and also diversify your message, eventually figuring out if you’re more of the type to be coasting on the works of New Age ASMRtists or if awakening a few Great Old Ones is more your jam. Either way, you’ll need a media presence, influence in the wider world – and money. Lots of it. Mechanically, it’s all very close to Introversion Software’s Prison Architect – the one difference is you’re screaming about aliens and God giving you superpowers to keep your “inmates” happy. There’s a few recognizable quirks in the mechanics, from a Management screen that interfaces with each cultist’s individual quirks and foibles to a schedule that can be set on a per-hour basis. A lot like Planet Coaster or Planet Zoo, this is a game where a lot of the fun is in making minute adjustments over several hours. If you’re more the SimCity type and enjoy seeing how moving a decimal point can futz with your slime mold of an ecosystem, you’ll probably want to stay away. HIJaC is a game for the motherers and terminal optimizers but works on a scale that feels more like the later half of Netflix’s “Keep Sweet” documentary than, say, Scientology’s bafflingly meteoric rise.Of course, it’s all still in Early Access, and could use a little more variety. You’ll first love the very “Hippie Meets Shaft” vibes of the soundtrack, and then maybe start to think about muting it on occasion. The main loop is hard to break, and most events that alter everyday life on the compound are simple, from a toilet breaking down and needing a visit from the maintenance man to someone you’d sent on a mission ending up in the pokey for a few days. Fail to keep your followers’ mental stats in check, and you could find yourself with your elected Chosen One foaming at the mouth out by the complex’s main gates, screaming insult-filled gibberish at random passerbys. Early on, generating stable growth and keeping everyone debatably sane is a bit of an ordeal, so balancing issues can still pop up. As it stands, however, Honey I Joined a Cult is a fun and deeply satirical little ditty that isn’t likely to wow any Management Sim fan’s socks off, but that gets some laughs out of anyone with a bit of a history on what happens when a relative suddenly goes nuts about Celtic mythology and massive chunks of pyrite yanked out of old concrete slabs.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty good.  It feels like there's a lack of depth, like there could be more things added in.  The faith is slow to accumulate at the beginning, which slows your cult development.  Money is the issue, which relates to faith, which relates to prestige....  it's vicious circle that can really hamper your beginnings, making it feel kind of grindy.  These things could have been alleviated if there had been rich personalities added to the cult members, perhaps interpersonal relationship issues.  Or if there had been random issues that could occur, causing problems for the player to over come, therefore making them feel more vested in the cult.  But there are no real random events, and it is very easy to avoid the legal issues that you see in the trailer.The game is win-able.  It's a satisfying feeling to actually finish it, but at some point I wanted to finish it just for the accomplishment rather than because it was still fun to play.  There is probably some replay value if you want to try a different themed cult and perhaps try a speed run, but I can't imagine more than two play throughs.  All in all, a fun game if not too deep.  But worthy of playing if on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game on a whim, stayed for the flavor-aid. Its a fun game that reminds me of bullfrog's  theme hospital. Not so much the game play but the innovation. It's fun to run a company that isn't a theme park or a zoo.  Its a great game to play from time to time and worth its price. If you find it on sale even better for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: Now that the game is officially out, I want to say I am SO GLAD I put time into this game. It's clear the developers are passionate about what they do, know what they're doing, and listen to feedback. Any issues I had when the game was in beta got worked out. The skills/rooms tell you what coordinate, so you aren't developing skills blindly. The addition to doing things at night and just all around changes have all been positive in my opinion. Well worth it!!This game has a LOT of potential. And considering it's just two people, I am thoroughly impressed. However. there are quality of life fixes and just some things that need improved on before I can really sink hours into this. I'm finding that when I am building walls, when you place a new room where it shares a wall with an existing one, it's deleting the walls that already exist, along with forcing weird room shapes sometimes. The wall issues need fixed because while I don't have OCD, it bothers me when one room is sitting lower than the others, or that all of a sudden my walls are being deleted and it won't even let me replace them. You made a 'delete wall' button. DO NOT make adding walls also delete walls at the same time. counterproductive. The skills I feel could use better explanation as well. Since this is a micromanagement kind of game, I don't want to sink 20 hours in and realize I set up all my cultists wrong because I wasn't sure what the skills do.Other than those, the game seems really cool. I do enjoy the sandbox aspect of it. I definitely plan on keeping an eye on this game. I bought it knowing that once they finish it and it leaves early access, it's going to be a great game. Already on the way there.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: When first thrown into what I expected to be another average base building/management simulator for another group of people that just happened to be worshiping a long forgotten worm god, I wasn't expecting the level of control and complexity for a fresh off the shelf game that's still being heavily developed. There are a few things that I would add that could hopefully make the ride to being sent to another planet as a race of robots a little smoother, but overall the game has been developed nicely and it offers enough gameplay and intriguing interactions to keep the casual player interested and discovering new things throughout. From enjoying your basic group of friends who just happen to be helping you turn your favorite followers into food, to making sure your scheduling and futureproofing happen correctly, the game is definitely a 9/10 for games of it's genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and engaging, with a surprising level of micro-management options. Has a quaint retro feel and that quirky Team17 sense of humour. A must-have if you grew up in the 90's on Theme Park and the like. I forgot this game was early access because it's so smooth and stable. The team seems committed to adding more content and the game has a bright future as a cult classic.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: Really like the idea of this game from the get go!!  The design feels very similar to prison architect which made it simple to pick up but there are additional elements to it I definitely need to dive more into.  Only negative would be the follower number restrictions, seemed to be set really low and really hard to unlock more... would prefer higher numbers so more chaos ensues.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: I'm hesitant to review this one because I'm still on the fence about it, but it's undeniably charming. It feels like it goes *juuuust* on the side of overcomplicated though. Like it goes really into the weeds on stuff. And while that is a negative for me, I can definitely see where many others would enjoy so many options, hence the thumbs up. Maybe get it on sale like I did if you're unsure.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and addictive. Build a compound, manage & upgrade cultists, followers, and resources (money, faith, influence...). If you like building/management sims with a lot clicking around and observing AND have an interests in cults - this is for you.
