_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and interesting game. Definitely a fun and new take on the same style that Prison Architect uses. I'm a big fan so far and really love the direction the developers are going with the game so far. Updates have provided increased technology to research and new items to use in the game, which means the game will be fresh and new periodically throughout the early access development. Big thumbs up, cant wait to see what else comes to this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: Very well designed, a lot of humour lifted from Father Ted and Black Books with lovely cute graphics.  I don't find it particularly shallow, but the research tree is a bit harsh, although I guess not feeding them very well or giving them comfortable pews is intended to make the early game a bit of a grind.Could use some more flexibility about direction of the cult itself, as in you don't necessarily want to live a life of darkness until  a later sage and the ideas about alternative health are a bit questionable - some complimentary therapies are not actually ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crazy in reality.Might consider adding a bit of food growing and more grim menial labour for the less useful followers, and maybe some sort of study facility for their time off rather than constant board games and puggies.I think this is an extremely competent and fun start and I look forward to the point at which it will be getting DLC additions.  Is it value for money? It has certainly had a lot of thought and work put into it and it is very stylish, but I do think it is quite early.For most less serious game players it is more than good enough, on the other hand for your Project Zomboid or Banished players it is a good start and very nice to play. Not at all sorry I bought it.edit after 40 hours - there is a lot of hidden flexibility if you mess with the timeline, however I am seeing some coding issues in the later stages when it is a long game.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who enjoyed Prison Architect, I don't mind the familiar "feel" - actually the opposite. I found it easy to pick up and enjoyable. I think the game finds a good way to add some humor to a normally not-so-funny subject without being crass. I can't wait to see what else they will add as the game progresses through it's build
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! I'm hooked! Love at first sight! I knew this game was for me just by the title and the psychedelic 70's cover!! I'm really into this type of Sim game, but I was getting bored with the same kinda stuff over and over so this is a nice change. I love how you can be creative with your cult name and outfits especially the HATS!! :) I am really glad I bought this game and looking forward to future updates and more content!!
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: "Honey, I joined a cult." Is a cult.  I couldn't believe this is Early Access. It's well worth it and they update pretty regularly too! So many customization options, so many things you can do and play with. Amazing resource management and satire game. Okay yes, it's a bit upsetting that I put 40+ hours into a game and then an update came out that didn't get to load the new stuff to my old save. Eh, whatever. Cults come and go right? I've started to treat the restarts like my cult got "busted" in the last game and damn it... Okay lets take 3 folks! I love the narrative concept and the game is funny enough with enough content to keep you sated for hours. More so with all the amazing updates they add!Being a player of this game is being part of the Cult. Join us. We have punch and pie.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun at first and it's novelty is neat but once you get a good handle on the balance of resources and some patience it loses any fun for it and has no repayable value. It's fun to make your own cult, discover more outfit options and to start out build your own compound with neat rooms to focus on. Then when you eventually and inevitably spiral down a resource shortage and start failing, doing it again loses it's spark. It's very easy to cheese. Making a room prestigious is as simple as buying more stuff. More money is best done by getting more followers doing more stuff. It's hard at first but the further you go in the easier it is. Usually luck has a lot to do with how well you can do in a game like this. Sometimes you can't account for everything in a management game or have to choose the lesser of two options. Not really so in this game. It's simply increase output with no real sacrifice. After beating the game I found myself not really interested in doing it again. I summoned the great old one with half a million cash, all my cult members good quality or higher and 3 special characters. I maxed out on faith every night and didn't even bother researching any more because of the influence cost. Heat wasn't an issue, money wasn't an issue, nothing stood in my way except the time it took to discover and receive all the pieces to summon the great old one. By the time I did I was sick of the game. I would not want to play it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: I'll give it a thumbs up, for potential. It still has a long ways to go.I've heard comparisons to "prison architect", but outside of the graphics, that's where it stops. Prison architect is heavily focused on compound optimization, risk, etc, which is not a focus of HIJAC. I feel it's more similar to Roller Coaster Tycoon, or Two Point Hospital.A lot of the challenges in this game can be overcome just by waiting. It's very much an idle game, waiting for your cultists to accumulate enough resources for the next step, without any real risk involved. There's nothing wrong with an "idle" game style (if that's your thing), but there are hindrance. For example, every night your sermon will freeze the game with a popup. Additionally, certain rooms require micromanagement, and really don't produce what they cost.The early game can be a tricky balancing act. Getting your "faith" generation above the "faith" cost of your cultists can be a real issue. But once you're up and running, it's no problem. You can also easily lower your heat, so police will never be an issue (unless you want them to be). Additionally, the "therapy" rooms are almost functionally identical. The only incentive to have a variety, is because your followers will get "bored". What this game needs is not just "more content", but a rework of certain systems. Also, a campaign would be nice.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: Never been really into the idea of management games like Prison Architect and the like, but I think game has converted me into the Cult of Management.The funky and fitting music now plays in my head continually and I like it. The only issue I currently have is one I'm sure will be added in in the near future, and that's just to have more than one module room, or at least more than one hypnosis station and maybe a way to assign specific followers to use those module rooms since they are a one time deal.Overall, yes, love it, more please.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: This really has the trappings of a great game, however there are too many aspects to fix before I can recommend the game.+ Very nice artstyle+ No gamebreaking bugs that I've discovered+ Great Music+ A great format- A decently large amount of QL improvements need to be made- It is a very slow game, this combined with the lack of customisation in a run makes the game feel like it's not going anywhere- A lack of challenge, as soon as you know the mechanics you'll never have another issue for the rest of the game- Faith has no payable uses other than cult upkeep which is a non-issue, essentially a useless resource- There is a research tree but it is entirely linear, no choices cut off other options- Alongside the linear research tree there is no mechanical reason to have different styles of cults, I don't get benefits and disadvantages from different gods. This means once you beat the game, there is nothing else to do.- A minor thing is that the symbols for very poor and poor cultists need to be reversed. It should go copper, silver, gold not silver, copper, gold.- A lot of minor bugs, for example changing hairstyles while people are asleep will cause them to go bald until they wake up.All in all, I can see this becoming an amazing game it really has the potential, but at the current price with the current content I'd hold off buying. I'll change this review if we get to that stage.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: Its a good start. But it needs more.Games like this do GREAT with customization and random events. In particular I would like for the cult to have more interactions and feel a bit more alive. This game simply needs more to do and during down time (when you aren't building or doing missions) and it needs more simulation. Before it sounds like I am being too critical, I do want to point out this is early access. Do I like it? yes. Does it need work? yes.  Should you get it?If you are into rimworld or prison architect you will find this charming but a bit simple in it's current state. I would say yes but temper your expectations.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: This game is FUN! If you ever wanted to be a cult leader, this is the game for you. And even if you didn't, this is still the game for you. Yes, it is currently in early access and you can see that in the game play as in late game, it becomes a little repetitive but you will still have a great time playing this game. Right now, the variety of items you can use to decorate is a little lacking. My biggest wish for this game, is that we can join the avatars to the missions into town to retrieve objects, increase PR or any of the nefarious missions you can send your avatar on.Hopefully the developers are going to continue working on this as this is a promising game you can sink hours and hours into.

_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so far out there. I legitimately thought this was going to be a softcore idle game where you gather resources to do research. NOPE. You get to build rooms that can infuse your cultists with Demonic Energy (possibly turning them into a demon, though personally I haven't had that happen), you can yeet followers into a pit and offering a "sacrifice" to whatever Diving Being you decided to make fun on, Contract Rooms to make deals with demons, and least we not forget a room that has the capability of summon Eldritch horrors to take over the world.Play this game enough, do enough, and you get pleasantly greeted by a picture of some guy, chilling on a lawn chair with a drink, watching the world around him literely burn around him as you hear screams and, what I can only assume is ASMR that would have made H.P. Lovecraft swoon.It's a fantastic game that never, for a second, takes itself seriously, and it makes for rediculous antics, and some times very interesting situations. 10/10, would recommend to any one who can run anything on potato settings, can read, and wants to laugh themselves to the bathroom before any leakage happens.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: There's enough interesting and funny stuff going on in this early-access release to make me think there might be a really fun game here eventually, but at the moment, there's just too much waiting and not enough doing.Other than not enough to build/do, my biggest specific problem is with the "Heat" game mechanic, which is basically a measure of how closely the cops are watching your cult. It only goes down  on its own, and the missions that let you actively reduce it seem to stop being offered after a while. Since every other mission seems to increase Heat, there's a strong disincentive against doing anything interesting for much of the game, since you don't want to provoke a raid.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: When I saw the trailer, I got hooked. It looked like a fun strategy game, the art style is cute. Started playing it since yesterday. It takes a while to get a hang of what's actually happening and what needs to be done. Sometimes it gets a bit monotonous and frustrating but at the same time it's addicting! Been playing for hours :)
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of this review, this game is in "Early Access"; that said, for being an "Early Access" game, there's a whole lot of good going on!:- Fun to play for hours at a time- Runs really well even on the most potato computer- Lots of customization options to personalize your cult- The "preferred" skills for specific roles is SO INCREDIBLY HELPFUL when trying to figure out how to assign cultists or where to put their skill points when leveling them up (and to be fair, most of my bads are QoL fixes rather than actual issues):- Decor is so prohibitively expensive, especially early on, but a room lacking prestige from decor dents the quality/output of that room that you're pretty much going to need to spend all your money on decor instead of building facilities, which hampers your ability to generate more income- It would be nice to be able to "upgrade" room features, like beds or toilets, when a new tier is unlocked; as it stands now, you have to purchase the new item, then delete the old item- The Kitchen mechanic is a little annoying; it would be nice to set a recurring purchase order for food ingredients when it gets below a certain threshold or something similar.Overall I give it a 9/10. Great game if you like Two Point Hospital or Prison Architect!
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this with some appreciation for the idea, but ultimately, I just don't find this very good.* It's too grind-heavy to really feel enjoyable. Build room to meet $need or extort money from your followers. Watch them inevitably get dissatisfied with the room's equipment or purpose. Build more stuff. Continue.* The room choices are also fairly bland and feel very much same-same. This is especially disappointing given the wide range of possibilities that the theme allows for.* There's too much pointless micromanagement. Having to order ingredients for the kitchen or research hamburgers to make in there is pretty much just silly, for example.

_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, I really like it. Firstly - they get the basics absolutely spot on. Day length? Perfect. Speed of movement? Perfect. Priorities? Perfect. Pathing? Perfect. Whilst this might not seem like much, a base builder with all the good ideas in the world won't work without them. I'll even go as far as to say the basics here feel better than Prison Architect (PA), the next generation of basics, if you will.Cult stuff is funny and there's good humour throughout the game. The theme in general is a lot of fun, this feels more like a successor to Evil Genius than the actual crappy mobile-esque sequel. Research tree is huge and will keep you engaged for a while, there's also a secondary research resource as well which can lead to absolutely crazy upgrades (like a pit of doom)! Seeing as this secondary research is one of their key items on the road map I can see a lot of replayability in the future.So, here's some recommendations game devs:- Two new rooms;  - PR office - when manned, stops PR from ticking down;  - Attorney's office - when manned, slowly vents heat;- Room restrictions;  - Attorney's office and infirmary - average or higher quality only (this will drive people to replace cultists);  - others that you might think of;- Upgrades;  - Lobby or Recruitment office - let me filter out followers, after a certain point I no longer want very poor/poor;  - Give some skill boosts other than retail to the bartenders;- Research; - Increased PR limit - even better cultists/followers;- Followers;  - I would like to see a slightly upgraded system to the one the game has now. I'd like followers to be assigned a cult level and traverse my compound based on that level (all set by me). For example, a follower coming in at level one might be allowed to do the Meditation Chamber, level two they can then do the Energy Spa, level three it's time for the Hypno module. As a follower increases in level, you could also increase their base monetary and influence gains. You do see this in real life cults, pay £200 to move up to level two!!!! etc. The end of this circuit could then be aforementioned pit, or signing a contract and going back round.My last point is a big one, but important. The biggest thing the game lacks at the moment is complexity, especially around base design. As it stands now, your followers simply complete every exercise before getting bored, leaving and cursing your name. I don't like the open endedness of that, especially when everything else in the game is so polished.  So, to finish - brilliant game, unlimited potential - grab it now for a good 20/30 hours of fun with potentially hundreds of hours of it on the road map.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: First, the only simulation game I have played is Sims 4. That is my knowledge base. Clocking in at almost 7hrs, I have already destroyed my cult. You might wonder how could you ruin the cult***....but that's for the end of this review. Pros:+Good templates for your Cult, if you just want to dive into the game instead of agonizing over every detail. +A good laugh from the dialogue.+ Good mix between designing your camp and carrying out missions. Lots of decor and ways to earn more.+ Missions, divine inspirations, and research provide a good pace setting as your cult is building. I always found a balance between completing a mission, designing, and overall management. +Different jobs the cult members are assigned to. Have to keep them busy! Leveling them up and a template system is very nice!+An infuriating amount of undesirable cult members. I have to roll up my sleeves and whip them into shape. Yeah it's a positive because it mimics real life. I mean you would be a lazy cult member too, wouldn't you?Cons:+ The navigational interface is not intuitive for a player new to simulation games. My main sticking point is that in order to move an object or delete it, I have to click in multiple menus. For example, want to move a bed? You can't just click on the bed. Steps are Click on Room -> 2 menus pop up -> Click on "See Room Specific Objects" -> Click on "Move Object" -> Move the object. My question is why so many steps?+Typical bugs such as the maintenance worker not fixing the equipment, cult members standing idle, not feeding themselves.+Can be overwhelming for a new player. I do not see an easy to access "guide" or "journal" feature that compiles all the information as you go through developing your cult. For example, still figuring out once the kitchen ability is unlocked does the person assigned actually boost the kitchen stats and benefit every member? or is it individualized?  Another example is the covert operations. I unlocked that and built the room, but nothing seems to happen when selecting the Covert button. +The cult member traits are varied and randomized, but as updates go on would like to see some more higher quality followers at an earlier point in the game. +You will probably need to do a second play through (if you are dumb like me). There are some features such as giving pep talks to your members that I did not realize were available. It is a bit confusing. Overall, I would recommend and especially if the Cons of my review are addressed/implemented. **You would think after upgrading literal **** buckets to fine clean thrones and feeding the members hamburgers instead of candy bars from the vending machine they would be grateful, but nooooooooooooo...my star member who I built a separate bedroom for decided to up and croak. She was the true leader and it all went downhill from there...

_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game the first week of early access release. Honestly, I was expecting more from the full version. It's a competent simulator in that it runs well and the numbers can be balanced. It's cute. The concept is great. But it's about as deep as a puddle. If you're new to colony sims you will probably enjoy it. If you're a veteran, you'll likely be disappointed which is why I can't recommend it for the price. Without workshop support, which would mean fans could actually turn this into a worthy addition to the genre, there's just no reason to ever play it more than once. It's a $12 USD game at best and that may be a bit generous. It's like a well optimized Prison Architect with about 10% of the content of vanilla PA. With all of the competition in the base building/ colony sim market, I can name at least six games still in early access, at the same price or less, that have more content and more replay value than Honey, I Joined A Cult.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: love the game but it needs a lot of tweaks! missions in general get to difficult to quickly and rapidly become impossible  but because of low pr rating cant get better followers to recruit i stuck with poor or very poor, also pool of revelations only one or two followers ever use it . so still you have to get rid of most of your followers every time you want to recruit! its taking ages and ages to get a decent team together. other things like scrolling research screen and why does the research not pop up complete and then allow the researcher to carry on with out you having to go to research screen and scroll to where the item you research is on the tech tree? it doesn't make sense why be able to stack research if it wont start after the last one? i suggest a way of picking up followers or sending them to specific rooms eg pool of rev so you can make use of this facility more. maybe costing influence to do it? a more intuitive interface in general would be good improvement i found myself having to do things a bit awkwardly in daily stuff. moving rooms and changing stuff is a pain and awkward. also placing object direct to rooms from menu you cant see the prestige gain, please make it so you can! there's  lots more like that i look forward to seeing this grow!  i do love this game a few tweaks will make it a legend!
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: I was shocked to learn this was a two-person studio. So yes, I 100% recommend supporting this effort.There isn't a whole lot of content. 8 hours in and I feel as though I've stabilized the cult and am making so much money (with no real pressing need to spend any) that I could just sort of hang out and be fine basically forever. _childDocuments_.review: A really enjoyable game that I'm looking forward to seeing how it develops. As at Alpha release the game is fairly bare based on the developer's roadmap but it still gave me an enjoyable 20 hours to play through to the finale. The intro is very well threshed out with a decent cut scene but the finale is currently lacking with a single screen acknowledging you've completed the finale task (I suspect they will match the finale quality/cut scene to the intro in due course). I recommend purchasing if you want to support the developers and have an enjoyable, relaxing base building experience pending completion of game. Until more development is done there is limited replay value as many features that will provide variety aren't available yet.Largely bug free with some text missing which simply appears to be coded wrong/missing code e.g. dialogue box will have "%xxxxx%" where it might refer to an object. The only other bug is that some unique items will provide 2 in your inventory but can only be placed once. Neither of these affected my play through in a significant way. _childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this game a recommend because it's pretty good, even though what this game is about seems very unimportant to the game. Just to be sure i restarted a few times, with a few different cults, and sure enough, the Amazing cult of Bob Ross played exactly like the naked porn stars of Ron Jeremy. Not a single difference gameplay wise. Sure things looked a little different, different pictures, names of things and such, but the game was exactly the same, thankfully again the game was good although missing a lot of QOL stuff like making/saving blueprints, saving schedules, clear description of what items do (like drains, i haven't seen any water in the game so i'm guessing it's just decoration but...). So for now it gets a thumbs up from pappy, but just marginally as the game should be about your cult specifically not just some generic thing, atleast i hoped it was anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has great ideas and is fun at the start but it rapidly get repetitive. You just have to be patient and after a certain point, when you have enough different therapy rooms, you make enough money to max out everything.The evolution/size of your cult depends on research so it makes the game fairly easy. You can't really outgrown your cult. You are caps on the number of follower and cult members (both are quiet low) and the first upgrade for both doesn't add a lot so you end up having a lot of people leaving because the cult is full (which make the lobby job useless in some ways).At this point, the waiting game begins. You wait for your research to complete while piling cash and then, depending on the research, you build a room or unlock some other more or less relevant upgrade.Then the cycle continue... Wait-->Cash/Influence-->Research-->Room/Bonus-->Wait-->Cash/Influence....Doing mission can generate heat (which is not good, you want to avoid having too much) and at one point, I was kind of locked out of doing missions because people started leaving my cults for being bored at doing the same therapy rooms over and over and when people leave, it generate heat. To decrease heat, you have to passively wait (again) or unlock the mission to lower heat. And since you get caped out fast on cultist, you have to think about it before sending them on missions.Also, characters have different quality. You start with one moderate and all the others that you recruits for a while are very bad quality (at least for me). Even with the recruitment room and one moderate character maxed out on recruitment skills (speech and retail I think, I'm not sure for the skills names exactly), I wasn't able to recruit better ones. And from what I've seen, there is no way to know which followers are what quality unless you recruit them (unless I'm missing something). So from my understanding, if you want better cult members, you have to "cycle" through the followers that are ready to be recruited by recruiting them and then kicking them out if they are low quality? So that make them angry because they are kicked out and you loose one follower (which mean cash and influence income).Maybe that's one way to prevent people from leaving by themselves but I find it kind of weird and they end up leaving anyway.Starting Customization for your cult are fairly limited as well. If you want to "role-play" your cult and give them a certain flavor, it might be impossible for now. I know you unlock new item in game and you can customize your cult at any time but still, it be nice to have more options when you create your cult and then unlock more epic skins one in game instead of simply unlocking a new hat skin. It would be nice to have... I don't know... special cult member skins? Like a glowing skin or coloured auras.... flaming hairs (just random ideas on top of my head) but my point is that it would had some nice incentive to go fetch items in game and still make it possible to have more customization when creating your cult.Anyway, the game isn't bad and I haven't seen any bugs so far. The only thing I saw was the characters going through objects. Objects are kind of sprites with "standing points" for npcs, they can pass through with no problems and sometimes, it break the immersion of placing stuff in a room since it doesn't affect anything.I would wait a few updates and see where the game goes before buying it. There is a lot of research in the tree but really little incentive to go far in it or to keep playing.Longer review than expected but I hope it can give feedback to both players and devs. I'm open to comments if I've been missing out on stuff.

_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: A game that has a *.docx file that explains how to use Borlderless Windows API straight into the installation folder. Perhaps a memo for devs.I hadn't yet gived a try to an IL disassembler of choice, not even to know if it's feasible. And maybe I don't really want to disasm at all - given the preface, I think that the rest of the book is a theological mess to put it gently.Anyway.The game promise a management sim with weirdo faith theme.It delivers it.Gets boring fast - for me, I ALT+F4 the game without reaching half an hour of playtime.I recommend it because it has an original religion-related setting that can be very funny and engaging for the casual player.But also, I have to say that 18€ on sale is a bit too much.I'm pretty sure that I won't bought this if only I had a Demo to play with.Because my lamentations have nothing to do with Early Access - the path where the game is heading is clear, and the roadmap is useful, but it will add things, not revolutionize the existing mechanics, as far I can tell.The art (graphics + music) is pretty nice.The UX (mostly UI accessibility and ease of use) is overall good.So, buy this if you loved Prison Architect or similar games.I suggest to take it on sale only, tho.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has good bones, just a few issues:There is no way to tell a follower (member) to take care of their issues, ie) need sleep or food, they just die if it is not the scheduled time. This is especially bad if they die from sleep deprivation after being in the hospital because they were there overnight.The follower cap, not the members, starts too small. At only 15.Decor cost is too high for some objects and you'd have to fill up the room with decor to have a decent pristiege Goodwill missions should be a thing, to drop the heat score. Charity, etc.It has promise, but playing it right now is all about grinding. Getting enough points in whatever you need to level up is difficult. Money generation is ok, but maybe have an option for members to go out and work to bring in money.Thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good demo but not a good game. It absolutely has potential. I'm looking forward to some additional features as well as quality of life improvements. _childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of genuine potential, however there are a LOT of kinks to work out that they need to address to make it really good. There's a lot of spelling errors in the dialogue which I find quite irritating - it isn't very clear how to fix things when they break (it says to right click, but the assigned worker usually never goes there), you can't see the quality of workers until after you recruit them which is annoying (because apparently dismissing too many people at once will affect your reputation), there aren't many missions, and there's a dialogue box that keeps saying to upgrade and you can't even do that. It really has a great concept though - the music is fitting, the animation is funny, the objects are hilarious etc. This game, again, has a LOT of potential, but if you leave it like this, I would think you invested a lot of time and effort for nothing on developing, and wasted the time of users.
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun enough so far, but there are some issues that need to be fixed. namely; if you tell a character to do something, they prioritise basically everything else over that thing, it gets incredibly annoying... That and when a character needs to do a thing like eat when they're scheduled to sleep and they're not supposed to they go to that thing, but also try to sleep at the same time, which causes them to go into a break...TLDR; Game is fun, but there are bugs that need to be fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really fun game to get lost in for a while. _childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever wanted to be like L. Ron Hubbard, David Koresh, Jim Jones, ect and have people mindlessly follow you, living on your every word and giving you the last dollar they have in their pockets?In Honey I Joined a Cult, you are the divine leader of your very own cult, whose members (and money) are your livelihood.Build a compound. Send your flunkies on missions, while you sit at your desk counting the money they bring backBuild holy relics that will increase your prestige and status among the group, and go out and recruit new paychecks... _childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game. I really do. But as of now it just isn't all there. I know it is early access and I'm sure a lot of my issues with it may be fixed. At its current state I just can't recommend it.The first half hour was fun and I genuinely enjoyed it. But as I progressed a bit and did a bit of looking around (in game and online) on what sort of stuff I can do in it, I felt underwhelmed. The layout of the research tree wasn't to my liking. It felt like I had to follow a fairly linear path instead of just doing my own thing. Creating different rooms was also just missing a lot. I didn't feel like there were a ton of options for the objects to put into rooms and there was definitely a very limited selection of decor. I felt like the missions were all kind of the same.Don't get me wrong; it has great potential. But the key word is potential. Maybe if I had played it a little longer I would have stumbled across something that made it significantly more enjoyable but I didn't see that coming. It really feels like a lesser version of Rimworld and a lesser version of Prison Architect were put together and then they took even more features out. Realistically, the DLC in Rimworld that adds the Ideologies makes a better cult game in my mind. There feels like there are way more options in Rimworld with that DLC. I'm not saying I want this game to be a Rimworld clone. But I am saying that a game that wasn't really intended to be a cult focused game can be played more like a cult focused game than this one at this moment.I love the aesthetics. I love the theme. I love the setting. But I can't say that I love the game. Yet. My biggest hope is that they really revamp this game while it is in early access.3.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Honey, I Joined a Cult

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game so far and will continue to update this review as more content is added as well as when i have a few more hours under my belt. my only complaint so far is the lack of Cult customization, I would love to be able to have different pronouns used for both male and female member. For example having my male members be called Adams and the females be Eves

name: Vertigo 2
detailed_description: Vertigo 2 is a single-player adventure built from the ground up for VR. Deep underground in the reaches of Quantum Reactor VII, you awake to finish your journey home. You’ll have to face bizarre alien flora and fauna leaking from other universes - and deadly android security forces whose job is to purge the reactor of all life. Try to determine who to trust as sinister agents lurk just out of sight. Key features include: Huge, bespoke world design – an incredible range of environments makes Vertigo 2 much more of an adventure than Vertigo 1. Enemy variety – dozens of creatures and robots are waiting to be discovered. Hybrid locomotion – both smooth locomotion and teleportation are viable. State of the art VR weapons – carry an arsenal of 14 weapons, all with unique reload mechanics. Fully voiced characters – a diverse cast brings the many characters of Vertigo 2 to life. Original soundtrack – hours of original songs and scoring. Intense boss fights – Vertigo is notorious for its ambitious boss encounters, and Vertigo 2 brings 10 brand new bosses. Substantial campaign – 18 chapters long, Vertigo 2’s story has many times as much content as Vertigo 1.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a trend with VR games where they either don't take advantage of VR and feel like regular games that surround you, or they do take advantage of VR in some cool ways but don't full commit to certain aspects that would make them feel more complete. Half-Life Alyx is a bunch of pretty shooting galleries, Boneworks/Bonelab are cool physics sandboxes in simplistic environments, etc.Vertigo 2 is a whole video game.It fully uses VR in the way you would expect from an "experimental" game, but it also has all the staples of regular flat screen gaming that VR developers just haven't been able to get right yet. It doesn't feel like a tech demo, or a hardware showcase, or a port of a game you've already played. It feels like an actual, straight up, video game. And a pretty damn good one at that.The story lures you in with a joke-y tone that it never fully drops, but further inspection of the world around you and the encyclopedia reveals the rabbit hole goes a lot deeper than a Half-Life parody, with some well voice acted characters to boot. The environments are varied, from laboratory corridors to breathtakingly huge alien forests, and none of them bored me. The arsenal you amass is not only well balanced to utilize all the guns throughout the whole playthrough, but also contain some curve balls to make them more than just a regular game inventory (the long range "sniper" weapon is a revolver that only has iron sights until you pump multiple upgrades into it. It is rad). The music seriously goes hard, and much like all the other aspects of the game, only gets better as you go along. It's got some crazy secrets for immense replay value, along with a New Game + for the truly dedicated. And, to top it all off, you don't even have to play the (admittedly dated) Vertigo Remastered in order to understand this game thanks to a handy recap.A must have for any VR library.

_childDocuments_.review: The storytelling of Portal… The physical interactions of Boneworks… The weirdness of Willy Wonka… Wrap ‘em all together and you get Vertigo. A series made by… Wait, ONE PERSON?!That’s right, other than voice acting and some characters/world creation, the entirety of the playable games, [INCLUDING THE ENTIRE SOUNDTRACK], were made by Zach Tsiakalis-Brown. Even if this game wasn’t in VR, it would be a nonstop bop of a video game, but the fact that it IS in VR just speaks volumes to Zach’s love for the platform. The immersion of this series is astounding. There are boss battles, massive landscapes, eldritch horrors beyond human comprehension…The game really is an impressive feat in game development. The pacing is setup just right, and Zach knows exactly how to reward you as a player.Only wishes for changes really be for A) more interaction with dead enemies (picking them up to toss around), B) LEGS PLEASE?, and C) character animation. Everyone/everything else looks fine, but humans act kind of odd. On Zach's website he admits he's not great at character animation, but perhaps some full body-tracked motion capture could help there.Overall, get this game. If you're somehow disappointed, I'd reckon to say that your standards for games in general might be way too high. lolHere's my full video on Vertigo 1&2 if you want to hear my overly tedious thought:

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not one to write long-winded reviews but felled compelled to do so for this game for some reason.Story: Let me start of by saying that I have not played Vertigo 1 so I didn't necessarily understand everything the game had to offer, though it did a decent job catching me up to speed. Regardless, the story didn't really interest me too much. It was interesting enough to tie together the events of the game but I wasn't too invested in it. So don't expect too much from the story, though the gameplay makes up for that. I also wasn't really all that invested in any of the characters, most of them are quite one dimensional and uninteresting. Sometimes one would come through with a funny line or gag but most of them weren't anything to write home about.Gameplay: I'd have to say that the gameplay is one of Vertigo 2's biggest strengths. The movement is relatively responsive and customizable allowing for players to play any way they like. The guns the game has to offer are each quite unique especially when you take all of their upgrades into consideration which make them feel even more distinct. The guns are also really responsive and fun to use, I especially like their different reload functions. Speaking of the reload functions I quite liked how Vertigo 2 handles it's ammo system. You don't gather ammo like in most shooters, instead your ammo is manufactured at your waist and takes a certain amount of time to recharge. This means that you never have to stop using a gun for an extended period of time due to a lack of ammo, but you do have to switch weapons often during extended encounters keeping them feeling fresh. These encounters can sometimes be a bit too extended, going on for a bit too long in my opinion but I only felt that way about 3 or 4 times. Sometimes it does also feel like the gameplay falls into a bit of a loop just throwing encounter after encounter at the player but then shakes it up with the introduction of a new and unique enemy. Some chapters of the game also dragged on a bit too long for my liking whilst others were really short. Lastly I'll also mention the enemy variety which is quite impressive. There's quite a few different enemies which you'll want to tackle differently though some can definitely be too easy whilst some are unnecessarily tough. Ps. There's a reason Valve elected not to put runner zombies into Halve Life Alyx, you could have done the same and saved me a lot of trauma.The look: The game visually looks okay. The graphics aren't bad and most models look at least decent though some definitely look a bit less polished than others. It's something I can personally look past especially considering the relatively small team behind the models. One thing that did bother me a bit was how empty some of the environments looked. In a few sections the player is exposed to the outside world which looks very empty and bland except for the areas which are explorable which felt a bit odd. Maybe obstructing large open areas with mountains or buildings would have been better but who am I. Asides that the game also features a few scripted events/cutscenes in which the player is able to also move about. In these scenes npcs bounce right into each other and push one another around which definitely looks a bit goofy which can be a good or bad thing depending on the kind of person you are (I personally found it to be hilarious).Overall I had a good time with the game spending about 10 hours beating the entire story without getting every upgrade or secret weapon (which there's six of). The game seems to offer decent replayability with a chapter select and new game+ which I presume allows the player to experience the story again but with all their weapons available from the start.I would recommend this game to anyone who is in the mood for a fun VR shooter that you can just dip in and out of at ease. I'd give this game a 7.5~8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: I've played many VR games and I can say with confidence this is the best VR game ever made, I would even consider it to be in the top 5 best games EVER. It does right what so many VR games have got wrong.CLIMBING:It has the best climbing I've ever seen in a VR game, no instant snapping like Alyx, no shaky "realistic physics" system like in Boneworks, it just lerps to your hands creating a bit of drag and it feels weighty and works perfectly. A while ago Zach made a video called "I solved VR ladders maybe", he definitely did.WEAPONS:Guns are great too, there are SIXTEEN! (I think) They all have fantastic reloads, and all feel impactful, with the exception of the trident SMG which seems to do very little damage compared to the others.The gun upgrade system is great too, with many to find and very interesting upgrades that often change up the weapon's gameplay in meaningful ways.STORY:The story and lore are great, I'm yet to get the second ending, so I can't comment on that (at the very tail end of my NG+ run). The writing is really funny, but what kept me interested in the story is the fleshed out lore, it feels like you are in a fully thought-out universe,  All in all I loved the feeling of being in this world.COMBAT:Combat feels really good, super satisfying, when bullets connect you know. It can be pretty tough towards the end of the campaign, even on normal, but it forced me to really plan out how I was going to beat a certain encounter, which I liked. There's an enormous variety of enemies, and with your huge arsenal of weapons combat never gets old. The cubehead guys are my favourite, they're funny :)PHYSICS:Physics interactions are pretty important in VR games, and Vertigo 2 does better than most, the physics on held items and guns feel great. fantastically weighty. Something I noticed loosely related to physics is the fact there's no hand poses on bigger items, when you grab a big cube for example your hands just close, without looking like you're grabbing it. I'm sure this was probably done due to glitches with it, I know the annoyance of working with hand poses, but it takes me out a bit. Chairs are also pretty glitchy they tend to fling you around if you attempt to grab them. Don't try to hold a weapon in a moving vehicle, if it touches anything inside the vehicle it will do some cyberpunk 2077 style stuff with your arm flinging it around everywhere and sometimes making your arms fly off into the distance. It looks like an issue with unity physics, but since you don't ever need to use your weapons in vehicles, maybe disabling them once you enter could fix it.Unfortunately another physics issue is doors, if you push through them in the wrong way you do tend to get your arms stuck in them for a few seconds which happens really often on 90HZ, I turned my headset up to 120HZ and the issue was a lot less pronounced. Most people will likely be running the game on 90HZ though. This issue isn't brought up very much so maybe it isn't an issue for most people.I also want to note that the IK on the arms is fantastic, honestly the best I've ever seen, it's not really physics related but there's nowhere better to put it.GRAPHICS: Graphics are really good, enemy models look great, The environments are sprawling and look beautiful. The particle effects are really nice, I love some good particle effects, also loved them in Vertigo Remastered. Weapon models are masterfully done. One issue I do have though is the human animation, honestly, it's not great, Brian looks pretty goofy, both his animations and his character model, but the entire game is made by one person so it's unfair to be annoyed over what is a small aspect of an incredible game, plus the animations of other creatures look good.CAMPAIGN: To me, the campaign is the most impressive part of Vertigo 2, the entire thing made just by Zach, It is absolutely jawdropping, the best campaign I have ever seen in a VR game, maybe besides Alyx (which suffers from boring combat, unlike Vertigo 2). There's tons of variety here, there's even a level that has 2 separate paths and bossfights, I'm not gonna spoil anything, you should go play it. It took me what I would guess is 12 hours, and I didn't even look for the weapon mods or secret weapons on my first go, there is tons to do in this game, and with the coming level editor and workshop support, the content here will be near limitless.SOUND:The music is really good, like really really good, I've already put a few tracks from the game into my playlists, I'm still in shock after hearing that Zach also produced all the music. The sound effects are also very good, and react to your environment.PERFORMANCE:I was so happy with the performance here, I have a PC on the older side and have pretty bad performance issues with most VR games, areas of Boneworks drop down to <30FPS for me,  Alyx is really stuttery and I can't play Blade and Sorcery in anything other than 1v1 mode without my FPS dropping below 90. In Vertigo 2 on the other hand I can run the game at 120HZ 95% of the time!! I have NEVER been able to do that with any other VR game before, I can barely run the home menu at that lmao. There was clearly a lot of work put into optimisation and my PC (and me) are very grateful. FINAL NOTES:If I'm missing anything I'll update the review, there's a lot here to talk about here so sorry if the review seems a bit rambly. If you plan on taking in the story I recommend playing Vertigo Remastered first, the combat isn't as good, but it's very entertaining and still a fantastic game. My final verdict is if you own a VR headset, I can't stress enough that this is the first game you should be playing, you'll 100% enjoy it.Also side note, Zach, if you're somehow reading this, I wanted to say you're a huge inspiration to me. I've almost finished highschool now, and have been making games for years, and am just now trying to learn VR development. The fact you've made this incredible VR game, starting in HS, mainly on your own is just mind blowing. I'm sure I'll never be able to undertake a project as ambitious as this, but your work really inspires me :)10/10 Game

_childDocuments_.review: I had to check this game out due to all the youtubers raving about it, so I bought both Vertigo Remastered and Vertigo 2. Vertigo Remastered was ok fun, but super clunky and wonky, but I kind of forgave it for being an (in VR terms) old game. I was disappointed that a "remaster" was still kcunky though.Vertigo 2 is also quite clunky, but to a lesser extent. Maybe I am just getting old, but I had serious issues with defeating some of the bosses on easy level and found it rather difficult to reload guns, warp around while avoiding to get destroyed. The story is not very engaging and only serves as an excuse for the setpieces. At times the game is dragging and can feel like a chore, but when it was all said and done, it was a very imaginative and exciting journey with many different locales, monsters etc., making it a very enjoyable game overall and much better than Vertigo Remastered, which is not to degrade that game, but just to show how much better the developers have become in time.In the dry, dry, dry desert that is VR gaming (especially PCVR) this game is an Oasis.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This is a must buy and a fun first person VR adventure.As a game made by just one person, Vertigo 2 is quite impressive. The game flow smoothly along with various cruxes and bosses along the way. The plot was basically un-decipherable to me and I lost all interest in what was actually happening. I lament the "multi-verse" trend in games and movies as it gives too much latitude to give writers the chance to do anything and everything at any turn. I liked: - The weapons are all unique and fun. Leveling up weapons is interesting. And the secret weapons are a bonus. - The music is fair. Not annoying. Not spectacular. - The movement is very good, using a split between smooth locomotion and teleport which makes sense. - The art isn't AAA, but it's good enough and the creativity of level design and enemies is enjoyable.- The play time is long. I play kind of slow and I spent a whopping 23 hours to complete it. The not as good:- The plot is too convoluted and confusing. - The voice acting was "ok" but not great. I understand that's a limitation of being a solo developer and budget.- The difficulty, on "normal" was at times a little frustrating. I re-played one boss 20 times before beating it. I did enjoy the challenge, but it was just a couple boss fights that seemed too much. I only turned the difficulty down once, for Cyber-Joseph at the end.All in all it's at the top of the pile currently for indie VR action adventure games. While the VR industry continues to grow, this is what we have until AAA studios find it profitable to make VR specific games. And I salute the indie devs that put so much hard work in to these games so we have things to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: The first Vertigo game was great, especially for budget VR players, but the game fell a little flat compared to other games of it's genre such as Half Life: Alyx and Boneworks; however, this game does not. Everything from the gun play, to the mechanics, to even the world itself, this game far exceeds my expectations (and they were already high). As a final note, I'd like to touch on the length of the game, since it took me by surprise: my total hours on the first game are 7.6 hours, which is spanning over three full playthroughs, taking my time on each one. If you couldn't tell by my hours played while reviewing this, it took me 10.4 hours to beat this game, once. Adding that with the fact that every second in this game is far superior to that of the previous game, then I think you can get the gist. If you have any VR system, budget or high end, then this game is 100% worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: After having played the first game, Vertigo 2 feels like it's trying way too hard to be everything it isn't. _childDocuments_.review: The human mind may never comprehend how one person made this.Pros:The gun play is very smooth and fun. _childDocuments_.review: Vertigo 2 is an amazing VR experience. The fact that it was created by one individual makes it even more remarkable. However, there is one fatal flaw. More on that in a minute.I'm not sure what the average time is for a complete play-through. It took me 73 hours to complete the game. A lot of that time was spent in frustration because I could not progress through the game, thanks to several overly difficult boss battles.While some creatures you have to battle with seem overly simplistic in their design, you quickly get over that feeling when they start hurling objects at you. There are very few sequences where you get to explore an environment without first dispatching a number of attackers. While the game is heavily focused on gunplay and less on puzzle-solving, I did enjoy the times when I had to solve a puzzle to progress through the game.One feature that impressed me was the number of different environments. When I wasn't looking over my shoulder to see who was shooting at me, I enjoyed walking around in immersive worlds, most of which involved a perspective of height, thus the name Vertigo.Another impressive feature is the sound. It was never intrusive and almost always clued you into something that was or was not about to happen. This game also has a well-defined goal: to reach the core.This is not a game you can play without the assistance of a guide, or watching a walkthrough. In my case, I could not have made it through most of the boss battles without resorting to outside help. The whole idea of the boss battle was new to me. Apparently, it's a feature in a lot of 2D graphic games. My problem is that each time I had to confront a boss in an arena, gameplay came to a screeching halt. Even though I had the game set on easy, I found several of the boss battles to be nearly impossible. Some would argue that my problems with boss battles only point to my weakness as a player. I would argue that I am not alone in my complaint of overly difficult battles. This is born out by the fact that only a quarter of players who start the game actually finish it.Rather than appeal to the small number of players who appreciate a difficult challenge, the game would have been so much better had the boss battles been a little easier. Despite this one complaint, this is a game that should be on your list. Congratulations to the developer.

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe the best VR game of our time. The gameplay is simply phenomenal, the enemies don't stand around waiting to be killed. (often ended up wasting all of my meds on a bossfight, because i simply refused to use the teleport feature to dodge some of the attacks) i definitely do recommend this game, the story is great and the bossfights are very fun (most of the time), and the gunplay is GREAT, even though it's physics basedgame also likes to trigger your fears, most notably aracnophobia..thalassophobia..acrophobia..claustrophobia..agoraphobia..

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: One of the best and most polished VR games I've ever played. Must own.As far as sequels go, this game improves upon the first in so many ways. New and interesting characters to get invested in, unique branching story paths with multiple endings, expanded world building and higher stakes, all while maintaining its sense of identity from the first game. The arsenal of weaponry has been expanded and gunplay improved significantly - but with the caveat that none of the first game's tools and weaponry exist in the same form (except for one secret unlockable). Gone is dual-wielding, as now your off-hand is permanently assigned to the new teleporter. The new teleporter no longer acts as a portal that you can peek through before teleporting, which was a cool feature before but one that I didn't really miss once I got into the game. There is already more replayability out of the box, with an entire codex to fill out and complete, and an arsenal of weapons with unique upgrades hidden throughout all the levels - not to mention a 'New Game Plus' built right into the base game. The story overall was longer and well paced and kept me on my toes the whole time, introducing many new characters to interact with (as well as bringing back and fleshing out some of the originals), all with their own motivations and personalities. Level design is amazing all throughout, with so many unique locations and biomes to visit, and tons of new enemy variations lurking around each corner to test your reaction and put your new arsenal of weapons through their paces. Each of the weapons have unique reload mechanisms, and unlike the first game, ammo is now a thing - but its been implemented really well. Your ammo stores replenish over time, so if one gun runs dry you can just switch to another and let its magazines restore in the background. This forces you to rely on your entire arsenal, rather than just sticking to your favourite or best gun, which I found beneficial as it forces you become practiced with all of them. And you will need all of them by the end of the game. The bosses you must face are all very fun and unique, and often force you to use not just your arsenal of weapons, but also your surroundings to win against, forcing you to think quick in the moment. Overall I have very few complaints about this game, it is definitely one of the best singleplayer VR games to exist so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far the best VR game out there in my opinion. I have a bit of a VR addiction, and I do my best to buy or at least demo EVERY single VR game/experience that I possibly can. With that said - nothing else that I have found is as perfectly crafted for VR as Vertigo 2 is and I was extremely impressed from start to finish. This game was clearly crafted by someone that loves VR as much as I do and it shows at all times.  Every good virtual reality game mechanic that I have ever experienced can be found in this game, and on top of that, they even invented new ones that I had never ran into before. The story is fun, and at times hilarious but never anything less than interesting. It is the first VR game that I truly felt sad when I realized I was at the end of the game and I just wished it could keep going forever. Thankfully though  after you beat it you realize it kind of does go on forever thanks to all the cool replay-ability features the game has. There is a new game+ feature, different characters you can play through the game with all packing their own unique abilities/weaknesses and even a level creator feature Mario Maker style. The biggest highlight for me though is the graphics. This game is STUNNING and all of this is even more impressive when you learn it was pretty much all done by one guy. Just buy it, I can not wrap my head around a scenario where someone that truly loves VR would not absolutely LOVE this game from top to bottom. I wish every VR game could even be half as perfect as this one was in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, it's one of the most anticipated VR games of this year.The problem is, it is just not fun and it making VR look really bad. The main problem is the gunplay, all guns are clunky and uncomfortable, handles are at different angles just to piss you off, for reloading you have to grab ammo from a floating point like 30 cm from your body which is hard to do while walking around in gunfights.  All enemies are tanks, every fight is a real slogfest where you mostly have to reload at least once for every enemy, they also all have 100% pinpoint accuracy. To win you basically have to figure out how many seconds it takes for an enemy to go pew and you just hide around a corner and pop out between shots. To beat enemies that charge at you you just teleport onto something so it will just run into the object you are standing on, like they did in games 20 years back.You walk extremely slowly so to dodge you have to use the teleport all the time, also just traversing the map you will mostly use teleport to stave off boredom. If you cannot use stick locomotion this game is probably unplayable for you.Still I forced myself to keep going hoping for some kind of stockholm syndrome to kick in until a few hours in I noticed it is way easier to just run/teleport past enemies so you don't have to fight. This made me realize I was not having fun at all.From what I heard this game is done by a single person and it really shows.I seriously DO NOT understand why ratings for this game are so high. If this really is one of the best VR games of this year it does not bode well for VR in general.It's exactly what we don't need in VR games, it feels like a huge step back. If I tried this game before I bought my first headset I would probably never have rolled into VR gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: Like its predecessor, it's one of the best games in VR. For everyone who says, "There are no good VR games, everything is a tech demo," here you go. It is an actual, real game, made exclusively for VR, with competent, satisfying VR interactions, It took me 10 hours to complete, which, by VR standards, makes it an epic. Plus you get to save a robot society from commie robots! Or help them plunge robot society into a genocidal totalitarian nightmare if you want to be evil.And unlike most VR games that I finish once and am done with forever, I'm eager to do it all again in New Game+, so I can have all the guns from the beginning and get them fully upgraded. It's basically a Half-Life-style shooter with a cartoony Rick and Morty vibe. Lots of cool, bizarre alien environments to explore. Unbelievable that it was made by one guy. You're amazing! Please keep making VR games for us!Only complaints: Not much interaction with the environment. The character is painfully slow and there is no way to sprint/run. (Although I realize after I beat it that you can actually ready your teleport while moving by pressing down the stick.) Come on, stop coddling us. People will get used to VR. Once you get your VR legs, fast direct motion is fine .Been playing the HL2 mods, sprinting and strafing all over the place; it's fine.There were a few difficulty spikes that almost made me go "F this", especially where the checkpoints were too far apart, or where it saves 2 seconds from you getting killed. Had no shame in turning the difficulty down to Easy a few times, because even if I could get through it, it would have been more tedious than fun. And there weren't really any puzzles that I can think of...weren't there in the first one?So it's a great follow-up to the original, a completely new game, unlike some formerly great VR games where the sequel is a buggy unplayable mess consisting nothing but recycled content, cough cough WD:SaS:R cough cough, this is an all-new game, as good as the first. If you liked the original, absolutely play this. And if you haven't, get Vertigo Remastered right now.PS: WTF, upgrade stations don't reset on NG+? So I can never get any more than I already have unless I find any that I missed? What's the point of NG+ then? And there isn't even a console command to give all mods? >:-( PPS: Ok, there isn't a command, but if you use the command to enable to developer menu, there's a switch in the dev menu to give you all mods. Nice. Still, having all the mod benches reset while letting you keep the ones you have, so you collect them all again on NG+ until you have them all would have enhanced my enthusiasm and motivation for a second playthrough. Not doing that seems like a really weird choice that I don't understand the point of.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: You need to play this game, seriously, you need to play it. From the weapons to the enemy's you fight, everything feels really smooth. Just the fact that the game never really gets repetitive makes it better than most VR shooters nowadays. The amount content is insane, I've played for about 15 hours now and I haven't even done everything there is to do. Bottom line is, the game is fun and long.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a very tangible and immersive feel, genuinely one of the best VR games I've played so far.I love the gunplay, reloading, synthesizing upgrades. It all feels nicely polished, I'm astonished this wasn't made by a giant studio.Writing and plot are very solid, including choices. References to other franchises are the cherry on top for me.I'd say it's a must play for VR enthusiasts, but that's assuming people are like me (which they typically are not)
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: I thought Vertigo Remastered was an absolute hidden gem and this is an absolutely fantastic sequel.Improved in almost every way - better graphics, more action and faster paced, great acting/voice work ... A real feather in the cap of PC VR and probably one of the best new PC VR titles we are likely to see in 2023.Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; One of the best VR games I've ever played. The gameplay/fun factor is AAA level quality, but the graphics and voice acting are not.PROS:- Shooting feels great. There are multiple weapons that are unique and have their own reload mechanics. - The VR mechanics are very polished- The levels are unique and interesting. - Enemies are varied with different attacks, speed, health, etc. which makes each combat encounter feel fresh.- There are secrets to be found, exploration pays off- Bosses that are unique and not just bullet sponges. You need to learn their attacks to figure out how to defeat them.CONS (I had a tough time coming up with this list, meaning these cons that I listed are very minor in my opinion):- The voice acting is hit or miss. This game was mostly made by 1 person with help from a few others so this con gets a pass from me.- Some of the textures can be bland. - The dialogue is mostly funny but there were also lines that made me cringe.THIS GAME MAY NOT BE FOR YOU IF:- You're someone who needs realistic graphics. As you've probably already noticed the art style is more cartoony. For me this isn't much of a con as the art style fits the mood of the game. And I'm having so much fun that I'm immersed by the gameplay and well polished VR mechanics without needing realism.- You're looking for an easy game to just breeze through. The game can be very difficult in some spots, specifically bosses. It's not Elden Ring by any means but there are a few areas that I have died many times. You can easily access the dev console to cheat your way through if it's too much for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing gun-play, crafted with creativity and care, great jokes.Completed it and it is one of the fullest and greatest VR experiences today. In my opinion it is the best VR game experience to release thus far. It is high up on my list of greatest games of all time(in my personal opinion). If you're seeing this, play it without spoilers, it's amazing and you should grant yourself that privilege.Now it also comes with a free sandbox mode, the depth is amazing and there are so many custom levels to try.P.S Nani I wrote a positive review don't come to my house, why are all my loading screen tips saying "Nani has entered your home" please nani I have a family
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece, like on par with Half Life: Alyx levels of greatness. The level design is just really fantastic and varied. You'll find 0 repeated puzzles in here. The art style is just cartoon-ish enough where you'll be immersed in all of the landscapes but every texture doesn't need to be incredibly detailed to be convincing. The enemies and boss fights are all unique from each other and all have their own quirks. And the gunplay, y'all the gunplay is easily the best I've had in a VR game. Each weapon, and there's like over a dozen weapons, is unique yet has it's own strengths, weakness, and skill curves. And they are all fun to use, even the crappy starter pistol has cool animations and textures and all that. Then there's a few dozen upgrades, that are of course all unique, but they all somehow feel useful. Like each of the up-gradable weapons has up to 5 upgrades, and despite all the weapons being different, and all the upgrades also being different, they each feel unique and useful in some cases. Then there's the story and the lore, which are surprisingly developed for like a 10 hour linear story line game developed by one dude. No spoilers, but when picking which ending I really felt like my decision made a difference in the realms. Also there's this level of humor that's infused though out the whole game that I really appreciate and makes me smile, especially with the loading screen tips. Just easy 11/10, you should buy it at full price and play the whole thing. Honestly this game is so good, I beat the story, then immediately turned on New Game + to beat it again and find all the secrets I missed, which I NEVER do.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best VR experiences one could have.Vertigo Remastered was already a great game, although was lacking in variety and really leaning into the potential that VR gives. Vertigo 2 however does all of that, and then much much more.Weapons don't only have great designs, reloading them is both infinitely satisfying and greatly intuitive. There are plenty of puzzles that make full use of VR, even in small ways that help make doing them fun even when the concept is simple. But what surprised me most of all was all the hidden content.While vertigo remastered didn't have much in the way of extra content, Vertigo 2 has so much unique content to find, not just in terms of upgrades, which themselves are all unique and even upgrades with simple premises (i.e. faster fire rate) add more detail onto your weapons. Secrets could contain secret bosses, weapons, or even just jokes that were well worth the search.What really had me was that it felt that so much love was put into the game, into the reloading, the jokes, the overall atmosphere felt like there was fun had making it. On the main story, its generally simple and it makes one of the last choices you have in the game so much more impactful. Its fleshed out way more in 2 then 1, but still keeps you shooting your way through robots, aliens, and what not to get home.Its a very, very easy buy. even at full price, its unreasonable the price for this game with the level of content and fun which is present.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: I have only played 8 hours as of writing and there is so much that i still need to do it is not funny. This game is fun enough that i am going to play longer that bone lab (that is how much better this game is). BTW this game has done more than bone lab and it doesn't even have the best physics, but the physics are still good.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is now the best single player VR game. I think this game sets the bar for what a VR game should aim for.The main thing that has stuck out to me is how much spectacle is in the game. Every chapter is super memorable and has lots of crazy moments. I think this game benefits from its whacky setting which allows for quite a lot of variety between chapters which create real stand out moments. I think a lot of other games have played have more grounded settings which is fine, but in VR I kind of want to experience crazy surreal settings  and show me things I couldn't even imagine.Other great things: depth of story and interesting characters surprised me, great guns with really cool upgrades, bosses are a big highlight, voice acting great, music is amazing.Only negative for me is that whilst most things in the game look really nice (lighting and effects), quite a lot of the environment textures lack detail, but this maybe because a lot of the levels are quite large. Also the animation for Brian is quite wooden and awkward looking. But I'm really nitpicking here...

Every time I got to the Commander 13 part, nobody would continue the dialogue and i couldnt progress in the game any further.
