_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game and the previous game (Vertigo Remastered) are the only VR games I've played that come anywhere close to the quality of Half-Life: Alyx, which I consider to be the best VR game ever made. It combines the masterful level design of Half-Life with extra freedoms that HLA lacks, without going overboard and becoming a janky mess like Boneworks. It also has its own delightfully weird universe and sense of humor.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: It isn’t that often you get a story driven VR game that’s this good. I’ve played many vr games. Boneworks, Half-Life: Alyx, Saints & Sinners, Blade & Sorcery, just to name a few, and I honest to god think that Vertigo 2 is better than all of them.Buy this game. You will not regret it. Don’t wait for a sale. Just get it.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: It is a good game and it's absolutely insane that this was largely made by one person, but there's definitely some jank and rough edges in here. The worst was physics bugs during some sequences that made me die repeatedly. I also found the combat to be a slog at times. I'd attribute this to balancing issues and the enemy AI being pretty basic, but hey maybe that's a skill issue. Where the game shines is with the visuals and level design, it's often jaw-droppingly beautiful and it does a brilliant job of using the sense of scale you get in VR to it's fullest
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very enjoyable VR game and it is done right. The adventure feels like a half life game. I didn't find the story as deep or interesting but that's not an easy thing to do, but gameplay alone is good enough. I hope they will continue to improve more upon sequels if there is going to be one or two.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: A better, fantastic jaw dropping sequel to Vertigo Remastered. This game is the game that VR needed for a long time.Sure, it's not as polished as HL:Alyx. Some minor bugs there and there, but personally it's even better than HL:Alyx. Because Zach don't take you by the hand, he makes you, jumping, crouching, running,  travelling through a lot of incredible dangerous and amazing environement and with difficulty to maximum. Enemies are deadly and fights are life and death moment.The boss fights are amazing, I felt like I was fighting bosses in Zelda, the wrong side is there is no checkpoint during some phase 2 bosses, and some of them are very long, but, it's doable with a lot of sweat.Anyway, this is a special gem who need to be in everyone VR library ! I didn't even finish the game yet and for me, it's the GOTY.PS : The cinematic in a screen with 3D is an excellent idea !
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Not to be that guy, but this is one of those neutral but tending to negative reviews.The game itself would be fine, if it wasnt for some factors, which mainly are:Story/dialogues - This is more a personal thing, but I really am not a fan of the humor. I know its supposed to be very cliche with lots of inside jokes, but its just not for me. Most of the dialogues i really wish i could just skip to continue the game. Maybe its because I didnt play the first game, which is why im not going to weight it that much into my opinion.Difficulty - Most of the time im doing very okay with little to no health loss. Suddenly you are thrown into a combat sequence where 5 enemies surround you, and you have to take multiple hits in a short amount of time. Suddenly there is a raptor killing you in 3 attacks. Trying to dodge the attacks? Sometimes it works, sometimes the enemy has an aimbot like accuracy. If it mostly werent for the sudden "you are ♥♥♥♥♥♥" fights, i wouldnt complain, but especially around the gate segment early on i had to reload so many times because you just get mowed down in a second. It feels like you have little to no control over the flow of the fight.secrets (?) - I probably missed half of the secrets because the game is very bad at telling you which way is the one to progress, and which way lets you explore a bit more. So you go down a path, realize that might be the correct way, you turn around, follow a different path and now you are locked out of the actual side path. Idk, some indicator that tells you "this is a no return way, you sure?" would be great.The gunplay, the sound effects are great, the interactivity and the weapon system are also very spot on. Enemy variety is the same as the game difficulty. You have absolute useless bullet sponges that hit like a wet towel, you have enemies just taking 2 shots to kill you. Its very much all over the space.I will probably finish this game and then see if i actually put in a thumbs down, i got it on a big discount so it is okay for that price, but if i would have gotten it for full price, i would be probably very disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: now that the initial hype has worn off i feel i can write my actual review, this is THE best vr game out there, better than half life alyx too (too many's dismay) but i feel it deserves that title, as the slow paced alyx nature is rather boring on second and third playthroughs. this game has kept me entertained far longer than alyx ever will in its story and gameplay. you get MANY GUNS which are all situational, needing some real tactics to play through the game. SECOND: the game is pretty darn difficult especially for new players, (trust me my friend played on easy and still died a ton). Zulubo is a one man team and this stuff looks triple A (♥♥♥♥ you Medal Of Honor) and cant wait for more, as this game is getting sandbox and is going to have way more contentTLDR;buy the damn game, this ♥♥♥♥ is better than sex, and i know all about the sex and the wenor.

_childDocuments_.review: genuinely one of the best vr games out there right now, and i think for a very long time, and the Developer keeps putting out updates to make the game better and add more features to the game, like a level editor and character selector where the different characters actually have different abilities. Amazing Game, googoo ga ga
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Vertigo 2 is a roller-coaster indeed. It has a really good story with meticulously made environments to go with it. The weapons are also a joy to control and handle. Especially the shotgun where you can slam fire the thing with enough practice.However I have one major gripe with the game. Many of the bosses feel like bullet sponges. I played on Normal difficulty and I would consistantly have trouble with bosses for one reason. They all took too many hits to progress with almost zero indication for how much you've damaged them. Not to say all the bosses are bad but a lot just felt like a constant dragging on fight with no end.Another gripe I had were some checkpoints were spaced way too far apart. Mainly, again, during the bullet sponge bosses.Besides those two main gripes. The game is a solid 8/10 for me.Good story.Good environments.Good weapons.But (mostly) frustrating bosses.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: I'd say this is one of the best VR games out there, just under Alyx. If you're in the reviews section I'm sure you've already been astounded by the fact that this game was made almost entirely by a single person. The characters are great, the story is genuinely interesting but never overstays its welcome, and the weapons feel *good*. The graphics, environments, and characters look great, but more importantly, the OST is very well done, especially the end credits song. The only real complaint I have is that Brian (one of the 3 new playable characters in the recent free update!!) is very challenging on higher difficulties. Why haven't you purchased this game yet? You silly, silly person.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Half-life meets rick & Morty. Outstanding adventure overall. Only a few small suggestion for the future: - Default controls kinda suck. Would love to have more options. I'm always accidentally grabbing ammo and you can't put it back so it's wasted. Teleporting with the left stick gets pretty annoying. wish it was on the right hand, maybe the b button? - the Weapon wheel is pretty janky, difficult to switch weapons in battle. - Normal is very challenging toward the end, but easy is way too simple.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: one of the best vr games ever. it has a half-life like vibe witch I really love and the soundtrack is amazing. character desing is really nice with great personalities. the game also has a lot of references to other popular game titles and secrets. I dont know what else to say this game is amazing. 10/10 (personally better than hl:a)
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: I don't review games often but this game and it's prequel are truly masterpieces. It has a lengthy (about 10 - 12 hours) action packed campaign with some okay dialogue. Some good replayability as it has NewGame+ and a bunch of great secrets. This is the closest you will get to a Half-life like VR game. Absolutely get both Vertigo Remastered and this game, you will not be disappointed
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: From someone who's played Half Life: Alyx twice over, beaten the campaigns of both Walking Dead: Saints and Sinners and Bonelab. Someone who's put hundreds upon hundreds of hours into Boneworks, Beat Saber, Blade and Sorcery, VRChat, and Pavlov... I think Vertigo 2  just be the best VR game I've ever played.You should get this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute must have - in my top 3 vr games of all time.PROS: Extremely satisfying reloading (for the most part, more on that later)Very interesting storyActual funny momentsRuns perfectly on my end with no bugs encountered throughout my entire gameplay Beautiful varying settings on many different levelsInsane musicI have no mouth, and i must screamCONS:Sometimes its hard to grab the ammo from your side in the middle of a fight, its too offset to the side and it can take multiple tries to actually grab it.The game is pretty hard. I played on normal mode for 4/5 of the game but when the game started throwing in hordes of enemies it became too hard (some people may like it but i think it would be better to have 4 or 5 difficulties instead of 3).Despite me just talking about how hard the game is, some bosses are just too easy. E.g the last boss was one of the easiest ones, it would be harder to fight 15 robots than the boss.Things i would like to change:I really liked the AK-47 but i didnt like the fact that there was no indicator of how many bullets are left in the mag - i dont want a bullet counter however that would make it worse but i think you should be able to rack the slide slightly to see if there is a bullet inside or have it like halo where the shooting sound changes when the ammo is running out.I also think the bosses couldve been a lot better. A lot of them werent really unique in how youre supposed to kill them; just walk in circles and shoot. I wish that instead of the normal weak spots on a boss, there should be environmental ways to kill them. For example, the first boss couldve been different where its shield comes on straight away instead of after a certain amount of damage dealt to it. To get rid of the shield you do the same thing with the extinguisher grenades but instead of shooting it again, there couldve been large fire extinguishers/ CO2 tanks/ water tanks around the room that you shoot to slow down the boss so that you can then go for the killing blow in the end.Manual saves instead of relying on checkpointsIn conclusion, this is at least 10x better than bonelab, thats all i have to say.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: I played Vertigo Remastered just before the sequel and really enjoyed myself playing them back to back.The sequel builds upon the first game's foundation and reminded me of Half Life or even Bioshock at times. The atmosphere is great throughout and the mechanics leave nothing to be desired. I had an entirely bug and issue free experience that is all the more surprising seeing the credits roll by. Really impressive work I must say.Overall a really grand adventure that will surely be in many peoples list of favourites.Sidenote: The game can be quite scary at times. There are quite a few sections underwater or within sewers where I had to clinch my cheeks or else... Albeit, these sections never overstay their welcome and just work wonders for the suspense the game is building towards.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Look, Half Life: Alyx's cinematic moments, attention to detail and graphics are very very cool, I agree, I've played it four times. However, I just played this game for the first time, and holy hell it's amazing. First of all, the gunplay is amazing. There are 8 main weapons (The shotgun is just mwah) and idk how many 'hidden weapons' which I only managed to get two of, but will achieve all of them before I stop playing this game. The enemy variety in this game is brilliant, and the bosses were my first proper VR bosses, and for whatever reason reminded me of when I first played Splatoon 2's offline 'story' mode on my switch, this massive boss in an arena with tons of mobility, it was just perfect. I have crippling thalassophobia (fear of oceans) and there was a few points where I nearly through my very expensive headset into my very expensive PC. This game is a must buy and is genuinely my favourite VR game, knocking Alyx down to second place, and I'm considering buying Vertigo Remastered once I'm 100% finished - I might even go full achievement hunting for this game.PS:- I love the cameos in this game the portal references were absolutely beautiful.Edit: Just a couple things I missed/forgot to talk about - There are some choice making elements in this game that are pretty seamless and can result in you getting different guns and fighting different bosses on your travels, and as far as I'm aware, and I could be wrong, some choices can open up different endings.. maybe.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Hands down the best VR singleplayer game I've played to date. Bonelab and Half Life Alyx can't compete with this, they pale in comparison to this masterpiece. If you liked the first one, this makes Vertigo remastered seem like a demo.  The boss fights were 10/10. The enlightenment gun and sword are such cool weapons. If you haven't bought this game yet and you like VR, this is the one to get for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Not even finished with the game yet but can already say that this is one of the best VR games out there! I'm on Chapter 13 and I'm loving it. Couldn't recommend this game enough to anyone who enjoys VR shooters and has been looking for a great game to play. This is up there with Half Life Alyx IMO. Just buy it, skip the demo, you wont regret it
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Loved Vertigo 1. loving Vertigo 2 more.Pros:Lovely visual style. (stylized, cartoony etc etc but lovely)Good performanceEngaging and satisfying mechanics. Weapons are fun to shoot and reload. Teleporting, climbing, moving around feels good. Inventory is good.Environments, levels and puzzles are interesting and fun. Entering a new area and just taking in the strangeness is super enjoyable.Progression feels natural and engaging.Music is greatTremor-mitigation (weight/physics/friction to weapon movement) I have a tremor and this game makes it easier for me to aim well. Even "AAA" games like the tedious half life alyx don't have anything of the sort.Cons:Voice acting is serviceable. Not bad, not great. Mostly serviceable. Sometimes not so good. It's fine, but clearly not very professional. Lip smacking sounds in dialogue, attempts at characterized voices (which don't quite pan out) etcSound mixing is a bit sloppy at times. Sort of entwined with the voice acting quibbleBoss fights can be tedious and not quite clear in terms of player impact.No control configuration (I'd like to be able to change jump to forward on the right trackpad. Since clicking the right trackpad usually causes a snap turn as well)Game is a bit too hard - even on easy. Boss fights can be frustrating due to this. On easy (in my option) a good player shouldn't die several times before managing to defeat the boss. Just a feeling of wasted time. Easy mode (in my opinion) should be about moving through the game and enjoying it. Not "having a challenge" before needing to go to work. I have limited time. I just want to play the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun(ny) story game that always throws new scenarios at you. Good for people who already have experience with VR, beginners might struggle even on easy difficulty. Also I participated in a robot uprising against a fascist church with an AK-47 and Robot soldiers with russian accents and soviet uniforms.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Vertigo 2 added a hole lot of new and exciting developments to the game play and story. With the updated graphics, it make this game more modern go figure, but this change in graphics was achieved by one game developer which is amazing. The game play is more based around half life alyx, but the system came from vertigo 1 and still holds strong, I never found myself looking at my holster to find my gun taking me away from battle it's just one button and hand moment. The story is good not the best but i liked it, it had you figure out what was going on through the environment, which i will always liked. The reason why i said it's good is that there is a lot of reading and data logs to find. The enemy's are very varied and it feels like multiverseal madness, so much so, that it nearly crashed my game lol. There is indeed more endings to get which adds a sense of completion. when i first played i had no idea what i was doing but when i played again the story felt more clear but the only nit pick is that you have to read to fully understand what is going on. What this game developer did and accomplished is nothing short of extraordinary he took a long time to complete this game but i felt it was all worth it. goes to show that with time a game can be great so the next game he makes i wont rush him. I fully recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Buggy game, with dated graphics, cringe voice acting, bad jokes and cliche mechanics. Gameplay is frustrating and boring, with multiple glitches preventing progress. Gun handling is even worse. The fact that this game is getting positive reviews despite being so mediocre and poorly executed truly makes me concerned for the future of VR gaming.Comparing this game to Half-Life: Alyx is like adding a spoiler to a Prius and calling it a Formula 1 car. Sure it has a motor and four wheels, but it's definitely not anywhere close to being a race car.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Writing is obnoxiously corny at times, but aside from that a phenomenally well made and fun VR game. Highly, highly recommended. One downside, and one that you'll commonly see people mention, is the difficulty. This can be solved twofold; one, try and hit headshots, they reward you with ~3x damage per hit, which massively helps in fights. Aside from that, know your enemy. Running headfirst with a shotgun every time will get you killed.But if youre still finding the game too hard, just turn it down. I played through the game on Normal mode, but some bosses were still just a bit too much, and I turned it to Easy temporarily during the fight, then set it back. It's a minor annoyance, but makes the game much more enjoyable. Don't torment yourself, put it on Easy or Story if you need to.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic VR game. Great level design, and superb sound design. If a sound is supposed to be above my head, it really does sound like it is coming from that direction. Definitely a lot of effort put into this game. We need more like this.  Gunplay can be a bit wonky sometimes, but that might just be me. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Been looking forward to this ever since Vertigo 1 (2016 remastered) and boy oh boy does it deliver.I could write a lengthy review about this, but who cares about that anyway? Do you have a VR headset? Do you like original world building and shooting stuff? Great! Stop reading this and go play this game
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Jaw on the floow. That's how I would describe this game.Some people might dislike the humor and quirkiness (try the demo and you will know). And some people might only ever want to play multiplayer games. For everybody else, this is a no-brainer purchase recommendation. The game has been, and will probably be in the future, often compared to Half-Life Alyx, and I get it. While the graphics might not be quite up there, the interactions and polish are. And the creativity and environments might actually surpass it. _childDocuments_.review: I put off playing this for a long time because I honestly didn't expect much from the cartoony graphics and somewhat amateurish sounding voice acting, but WOW this is a fantastic game and perfect for anyone who is a fan of classic level-based first person shooters. First off, this game builds on everything the first game did well. It has a great arsenal of weapons, there is a wide variety of interesting enemies and areas to explore. I never got bored and the game moves along at a great pace, introducing new mechanics and scenarios. I also want to give a special call out to the bosses in this game as they are all really well done and creative. They also can put up quite a fight and some of them are HARD, but they keep you on your toes and aren't just artificially hard due to massive health pools like some of the bosses in the first game.Now, with all the praise, I do have some complaints. There are quite a few bugs and some of them are potentially progress halting such as your hands wigging out in the 2 flying sections of the game, making it near impossible to grab/aim the gatling gun. The story and writing/voice acting is also eh and didn't make a whole lot of sense to me, but there's enough charm there that I didn't care.Overall though, definitely worth a buy!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best recent VR games, but not without flaws. It is a zany, campy, sci-fi adventure that doesn't take itself seriously. It continues right after the first Vertigo game and actually fills in the gaps and explains many of the holes left by the first game's (mostly nonexistent) plot.Overall, I would rate this game in the same category as say Half-Life Alyx or Boneworks. It is a 10+ hour long narrative-driven shooter with some added features to give replay value. That sort of thing is unfortunately still rare in VR, and that alone makes it worth buying. In more detail:The Good:Gameplay - Vertigo 2 is *fun*. It is fast-paced (much more-so than Alyx) and features a variety of enemies with different abilities. The game gives the player a decent range of weapons, with upgrade trees for each. You can customize your loadout to fit different playstyles. There are also several somewhat hidden secret weapons you can obtain.Environments - Vertigo 2 takes the player through an assortment of bizarre and breathtaking environments. There was one moment where I was walking through a giant underground cave with large dinosaur-like creatures walking around. The music set the stage perfectly and all I could think to myself was "this is why I got a VR headset." There are some peak VR experiences in this game.The Mixed:Tone - As I said, this game REALLY doesn't take itself seriously, maybe to a fault. There are lots of overt references to other video games. There are lots of call-backs and cameos from previous parts of the game and the first game. There are lots of places where the internal logic of the game world bends to fit a particular gag or plot point. The loading screens are full of snarky jokes from the developer. Taken all together it's all a bit too ... self-indulgent? It kind of gives the vibe that the developer thinks they're really funny and wants us all to acknowledge it. Personally, I think the game overall is good enough to justify some self-indulgence, but it's cutting it really close. Also, the dev's political opinions do filter through pretty clearly in some parts. It's not a bad thing necessarily - calling video games art means that people should be allowed to express political opinions through them. But when combined with the above, I don't think it comes off too well. Through all of this, though, the game kept me entertained!Story - As would be expected from the above, the story is a constant stream of characters popping in and out of the story at random times. Sometimes they are friends. Sometimes they are enemies. Sometimes both! Sometimes they die. Sometimes they Deus Ex Machina the player out of a contrived situation. It works well as a device to keep the player moving through the many different environments and set-pieces. It's very fun in the moment, but upon reflecting back over the whole game, there isn't much stitching it all together. The plot is just a constant stream of "And then this thing happened!" without too much rhyme or reason.The Bad: Onboarding - The only really bad word I have to say about the game is about the first 10 minutes or so. Frankly, they suck. The opening cutscene has two characters that I couldn't understand without subtitles. (I had to skip it and restart the game with subtitles just to understand) Also, the first character you see is one of the worst modeled and voice-acted in my opinion. So I could see someone picking up this game and not being able to get past the first part.

_childDocuments_.review: Vertigo1 and Vertigo 2 are interesting games.Vertigo 1 I left on the backburner until I basically ran out of FPS VR games to play and so I just really got into it recently and the big thing I noticed was that although it was one of the first VR games I got 5 years later it was still one of the most solid vr games to play and it felt good to play and felt like quality.Vertigo 2 is the same thing again but with more experience and story elements. Again it all feels like quality.It doesn't have the freedom of Boneworks, but as a simple FPS shooter it is fantastic and fun.When badguys spit ink or fireballs at you feel free to smack the projectiles with your guns as well as dodging. A shotgun makes a pretty good baseball bat for that (the projectiles break apart on impact).UPDATE: I have been working through the campaign and it is really good. The story and characters pull you into the world and make you care about what you are doing and the best part is the bosses are creative, have personality, they are challenging, the game is challenging, but the game is difficult in a way that makes you want more and let's you learn how to be good at it. It's like an old Nintendo game where you have to learn the timing and the patterns, but it isn't so brutal that you feel like it is unfair (on normal difficulty anyway).It uses teleport but this game is a rare example of teleporting making the game more fun and not less fun.UPDATE 2: THis has been a great few months for VR first person shooters. Bonelabs was a bit of a let down, but then  we got a whole bunch of other FPS games that came out after. Some were Quest ports and some were from smaller developers, but most of them were actually really good and others at least had the right spirit. BUT VERTIGO 2 IS NOW KING OF THEM ALL.

_childDocuments_.review: The story is so long. It just kept going and going, and just when I think it ends, it keeps going even more. I had been at it for well over 12 hours in order to complete it, and the journey throughout was outstanding.Games nowadays often tend to have a few-hour-long campaign, especially with live service games that focus more on multiplayer. VR games are often even shorter than that. The fact this one went on for as long as it did, especially considering it was primarily developed by one guy, is hella impressive.I've never felt more stunned in a VR campaign since 's first debut. It was visually impressive throughout as well.The guns themselves, they all feel great. They all have some nice weight to them, they each have their own unique designs and traits. The reloads feel extra smooth as well, something that a lot of VR shooters don't focus on too terribly much, especially for games with more original, sci-fi designs, versus realistic guns like you see in  or . A personal favorite of mine is the Trident SMG, the way the magazine slots in feels so satisfying, not to mention the way it ejects slightly when pressing the eject button, and then you can either pull it out manually by hand or knock it out fully with a fresh mag.The ammo is virtually infinite, because while reloads are physical and you can reload endlessly, you can only have so many magazine slots per gun at a time, so every time you take a fresh magazine, a cool-down appears to regenerate an empty ammo slot. Empty slots regenerate one at a time until you're at max capacity again. If you use up all your ammo too quickly, you have to wait for at least one slot to finish regenerating a mag before you can reload. There's also a setting to have guns reload automatically in your inventory when not in use, so it's full when you pull it back out again.One of my favorite VR games of all time is , also known as  (come on, Early Access, over a hundred updates, an update every Friday for 7 years, made by one guy, what's not to like?), so as soon as I heard Anton Hand's voice (as well as spotted some sosigs later on), I squealed like a girl.Some sections reminded me visually of Black Mesa's Xen reimagining. It all looked pretty, the lighting and atmosphere helped set the tone.Something the game does that's interesting too, is frequently change the setting/location. Most games that do it often lead to mass confusion, and it's not very appealing. But  seems to pull it off successfully. Granted, it  get just a little confusing sometimes, but I enjoyed it all the same. Each location had its own style and theme to it. Its own colors and details. It was practically eye candy in most cases.As long as the campaign is, I will admit there was a level or two that I felt overstayed their welcome, and were a little too long for comfort. But the rest was right as rain, so 1 bad thing out of 100 other good things is impressive regardless.Can't wait to see the Sandbox update.  has significantly more in store compared to , so I bet plenty of people will have even more tools and toys to play with.I would also love to see some mutators like in the first game. Such as removing the cool-down for ammo regeneration, so you can reload as many times as you want without having to wait for a slot to finish after you've reloaded so many times in a short time span. Or a hit-scan option like in the original.Thanks for an amazing experience, regardless. Almost makes me wish Anton could port some of the guns to . I bet that Annihilator Shotgun would feel right-at-home in 's arsenal.

_childDocuments_.review: Really awesome game. It's awe inspiring how you're expected to multitask in this game and especially with the harder fights how there can be multiple mechanics being utilized while you're reloading, throwing grenades, teleporting around etc. You will have to use the teleport in this as there's no increased walking speed and though its not super comfortable having to move the left stick and hold it to teleport around, it does kinda feel like doom vfr. Playing this can be alot of work but it's more engaging than any VR game i've ever owned. You'll do a lot of shooting and a lot of walking and a few decent puzzles on the way to the core. If you struggle with VR controls this is going to be really challenging for your average player. I've never died as many times in VR as I have on here though I think it's reasonable overall.My only compaint is that instructions could be clearer... for example youre given a sword for a boss but no clarification or warm-up for it as if you'd just know immediately what to do and that youll pull the trigger when boss is in weakened state. _childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed HL:A, but found it lack luster, this is the game for you. _childDocuments_.review: Good:- Great sequel to a VR classic. - The physics interactions are great and the smoothing of the hands is really well balanced and make interacting with the environment fun. - The weapons are good and reloads especially feel fantastic even after 10 hours. - Some good fun 'hidden' features and easter eggs.- Some levels really mix up the gameplay to prevent it from getting stale- You can pet the blobBad:- Boss fights left a bit to be desired, difficulty for each is not consistent and some a boring bullet sponge grinds. - The environments are maybe a bit simple. - Some bugs here and there but nothing too bad or breaking.- Some frequently encountered quality issues that could have been addressedOverall a great experience and well worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. Guns are fun to shoot, reload and use. Enemies are fun, challenging and varied. Environments are visually impressive and fun to explore. _childDocuments_.review: IMO this may be the best FPS VR game. Amazing how many different worlds and enemy types you encounter, the level of creativity is impressive. Overall a totally unique and wonderful game. One of the best in VR!

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best VR game ive ever played, ♥♥♥♥ it, this is the best game i've ever played. Every VR game i've played feels like a tech demo compared to this. This game ruined boneworks for me and thats a compliment.From start to finish, I was immersed in the world completely. This is the most real VR has felt for me, not since HLA, EVER. The worldbuilding just makes it feel real, ever corner of every beautiful environment feels lived in, from the NPC's to the intricate layouts of every map, to the diverse and original enemies and bosses.The only thing i can compare this game to is when I first played Mario galaxy 2 as a kid. It was one of my first video games and all the beautiful and different worlds were unlike anything I had ever seen and though possible for a video games.This game really gave me THAT SAME FEELING. I feel like i’m in the world and it’s so unique and un-formulaic. The story is linear and yet it feels so exporable. Every 30 minutes it feels like i’m a completely new world just as beautiful as the last and yet it all transitions together smoothly. There were multiple NPC interactions where i straight up laughed, not like “oh this is kinda funny” but like “wtf am i in an episode of rick and morty rn ”.I have been so unenthusiatic about VR for at least a year now, I get on, play like 30 minutes of a multiplayer game or a simulator and then I get bored. I swear to god, I played this game 3 nights in a row for 5 hours at a time, i didn't take off my headset until my feet hurt from standing for so long.

_childDocuments_.review: Never even heard of Vertigo 1 which was apparently criminally underrated, and this right is AT LEAST the second best VR game ever made, possibly the very best depending on your taste. Because this is a very Half Life inspired game it's easy to compare to the other "best VR game ever": Half Life Alyx.  Cool setpieces and a focus on environments work very well for VR, as does shooting with interesting reload mechanics. This is the main element for Boneworks and Alyx as well. I think the enemies are appropriately paced and they are very varied, with hilarious designs. Game is not very serious and actually funny a lot of the time. Every second of this game introduces something new to keep it fresh all the way through.  The game has all the physics of other titles like Boneworks and Alyx, making the world feel very present. Breaking glass, having the spent magazine eject and become a physical item you can pick up, being able to throw and move most things in the world, having your gun collide with objects and walls. It all seems quite simple but it's a must for VR games, and here it's extremely well done. Unlike Alyx this game goes much further with VR, never shying from things that can cause extreme motion sickness (dude the boat), but that also makes it much more dynamic and interesting. Still criminally underrated buy now this is Alyx tier ong no cap

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the main story today, and I have to say, this is some of the most fun I've had in VR in a long time. The environments are unique and fun to explore, the weapons are absolutely amazing (especially when upgraded), and the boss fights, as weird as this sounds, remind me of Hollow Knight due to how challenging, yet fair they are. The characters are memorable, which seems to be quite rare in games nowadays, and the cut scenes are both well placed and entertaining. I'd also like to mention that this is without a doubt, the funniest game I've ever played. TLDR: 10/10 game, up there with Half-Life: Alyx and BONELAB / BONEWORKS, and the only reason I'm not playing it right now is because my VR headset is recharging.

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to put into words how much I enjoy this game. I mean, I figured it would be fun, but I didn't think it would become one of my favorites. Weapons feel weighty when they need to, but not overly cumbersome. The story is actually quite entertaining and original, and the soundtrack bops between a Sci-Fi/Space opera and whimsical storybook adventure.While it is a bit more challenging than expected, it is still one of the most well-made, and enjoyable experiences on the VR market today.

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased the full version of this game because I enjoyed the demo. It started off pretty well and then several issues became apparent. First of all, teleportation is pretty bad. With the Index controllers, you must push the left stick in to teleport. Then streaks of light flash at you every move you make. There are also several sections where you must enter water. You can't teleport through water so you must go into the options and change the setting to full locomotion to make it through the water then go back into the options to re-enable teleportation. The constant reloading is also a pain to deal with in my opinion. Each gun only fires a few shots and I was constantly getting overwhelmed by sections of numerous enemies while trying to reload. There is also no trainer or cheat code with a true no reload feature. The graphics in this game are also outdated and at times the animations are janky. There are also some pretty harsh frame rate drops every time the game auto-saves. I also did not enjoy the forced sections where you must fly in a helicopter and ride in a mine car, as experiences like that tend to cause me some nausea. Overall, I lost interest in playing so I cannot recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished Vertigo 2 last night and I must say, **WOW**! The game is stunning and unique from start to finish. The journey took a total of over 19 hours, which is looong considering the attention to detail and top notch gameplay. Each chapter is noticeably different than the previous and the level design is incredible. The brilliant design and drastically different levels offer a truly unique game with nothing else like it in all of VR. Each chapter also has hidden areas of the maps that keep you peaking in every corner (maybe even through what seems to be a closed door…).There are a huge variety of enemies, that have multiple different attacks and even enemies who fight other enemies. There are over 10 extremely fun and unique weapons, with 5 or 6 hidden weapons that you *really* need to be looking for the entire game to find. There are numerous upgrades to each weapon that adds something great. Upgrades can change the strategy for that weapon or it can make it go from maybe your least favorite to all of a sudden your go to.There is a solid story, beautiful visuals, tons of adjustable settings, top notch soundtrack and audio (one characters voice is the only thing that seemed off about the game), bHaptic support (thanks to @Florian Fahrenberger who not only did the bHaptics for the game but is also recognized in the credits! Twice!), smooth controls, lots of achievements, different paths you can take that changes the journey (and weapons) and a well polished VR experience that we are fortunate to play & will have you playing again & again.Vertigo 2, while not perfect, is as good as VR gets in 2023. I caught myself stunned on numerous occasions where I’d just stop and look around the environment. There was a psychedelic experience that was mind melting and a part of a level that legit felt like I was in another realm of life or fever dream.If you have a PC & VR, **buy Vertigo 2**. It’s games like this that make all the ups & downs of VR, well worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: You want a single player VR game with a full-length 10+ hour campaign in the vein of a Half-Life game? This is the game you want! Gunplay is really good, and it has this unique system where you don’t pick up ammo in the world, but instead, new magazines gradually re-spawn in your pocket. This means you don’t need to hunt around for ammo, but you still need to be conservative and alternate what guns you’re using. The balance can be a bit off for some of them. The AK shreds enemies, but the SMG feels like you need to dump an entire magazine into even basic enemies to kill them. Likewise, the shotgun also feels very under-powered, which is a blasphemy for a video game shotgun, especially for one named "Annihilator". The reloading is really satisfying, with many guns having a weird gimmick that make them unlike any other VR guns. It can be a bit finnicky sometimes. You can do a magazine reload with the AK, but the game is very fussy about how quickly or slowly you need to hit the magazine to knock it out. It seems like it only works half the time. There’s a big variety of enemies and worlds, there’s just a lot of content in general! It’s a very impressive effort for a one-man dev team.My biggest gripe with this game is the difficulty of the bosses. Overall, the game is challenging, but the bosses (save for 2 of them) cause the difficulty curve to take a sudden spike. A lot of their attacks do heavy damage and are very difficult to avoid. Which really isn’t helped by how damned slow your character is and how long you need to stand around waiting for the teleporter to reach maximum teleport distance. It’s honestly only really useful for dodging short-range attacks. One of them even commits the cardinal sin of having a swarm of quiet, tiny enemies who you can’t see unless you’re looking down. So while you’re fighting the boss, these little bastards have snuck up on you and are chipping away at your health. For pretty much all the bosses, I had to turn the difficulty down to easy, since I was sick of wasting my time. Thankfully, you can change the difficulty setting at any time.Overall, Vertigo 2 is an excellent fully-featured single player VR game that needs to be in the library of any Half-Life fans!

_childDocuments_.review: Well, that was amazing. I saw some footage beforehand (thanks habie247) and after a lot of drift issues, anxiety, fear, and almost refunding the game since it got so bad... Only fitting I give it 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: This, right 'ere is one of the best VR games ever made, if not the best one so far. For how much this game manages to cover in it's well paced gameplay, I'd kill for a third game. This game hits a mid point between some of the best vr games, and to me feels like a blend between something like Budget Cuts, experimental, and something like Half-Life: Alyx. Oh, and don't even get me started on the Rick and Morty-esc humor this game pulls at EVERY chance. The references don't stick out like a sore thumb, and really put a smile on the "all-around" gamers such as myself. This game feels like a VR game built by someone who loves the platform. Everything from the music, characters, environments, and gun-play make this game a killer experience, and should really be up there with the main titles people should recommend to new and veteran VR enthusiasts. The game has very little bugs, and it's largest down points are all thrown out the window with the game's charm. My only nit-picks are the middle to late game being a little draggy, and the animation. Even with that being said, I do believe this game is definitely my new favorite story-vr game. It's no boneworks, but it really doesn't need to be. This game manages to shine in ways most people may miss on their first playthrough, but it's little nods and secrets will really make you think and have a little laugh.In the great words of FUNKe, "Play it, then play it again, then play it again, and notice how hilariously overpowered you get compared to when you started."My point is, you've just wasted a bunch of time reading this, and should really just play the damn game.

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I really wanted to like this game. All the trappings are there - solid graphics, phenomenal optimization (runs great!) and art design that I can get behind. There's some tiny rough edges that aren't really worth discussing. Overall the presentation is great!But the guns... the guns :(First hour was fun, but something seemed a little *off*. I figured I'd get over it, but rounding the corner on hour two, I had to face it -  the guns in this game just don't feel good to me. The designs and everything are really imaginative. I'm not about to say the game should have mil-sim guns or anything like that. I don't mind that they aren't hitscan (I *love* Compound's guns).But they deal so little damage that combat - y'know, the main part of the game - starts to feel like a slog.Sidenote: The exception here is the revolver, that gun feels great. Unfortunately the ammo system doesn't really allow you to use a single gun for too long.Since the player has such little damage output, gunfight encounters all play out the same: Hide around a corner while robots walk towards you in a straight line and take them out 1-by-1 with revolver headshots. Its a shame, because the areas that you're clearly meant to fight in are, again, imaginative and well-crafted.Encounters with other creatures are at least interesting, but again marred by all the enemies feeling like damage sponges.Final straw for me was a sort of turret section - I'm riding on a platform moving along an orange lava river. Orange lava monsters that throw orange projectiles start spawning rapidly. They're too far away for the shotgun to be effective, and the revolver shoots too slowly to be viable here (you need to shoot down projectiles that are lobbed at you; the revolver has a very slow rate of fire) - and the weapon system is too slow for quick-swapping to be an option. But the pistol, the most best option here, takes about 1-1.5 mags to kill one enemy, and there's something like 8 on screen. Trying to aim at the tough-to-see damage sponges while dodging tough-to-see projectiles was just... boring. This section was then immediately followed up by another corner-camping gunfire battle. And that's where I quit out.I dunno, maybe the problem is me - it seems like other VR players are loving this game, and honestly that's a net positive for them *and* the dev. (Which, also, holy crap, this is a solo dev project, which is mind-blowing!) You love to see it! But its nuts to me that people are putting it in the same league as HL: Alyx, etc.That said, I won't refund it -- I feel like my core complaints are mostly addressable by tweaking weapons stats & damage values, maybe they'll do that. Or maybe they'll use the money to make the next game an absolute banger, which they're clearly capable of.PS - to all VR devs out there (I'm looking at you too, Boneworks/labs) - please hire voice actors if you're going to have extensive dialogue in your game, OR just don't write you game to have 2+ minute sections that's just being talked at by someone.

_childDocuments_.review: Its not very often that you come across a game that uses every single part of its medium to give you a great experience, especially nowadays. Vertigo 2 is so far above its peers that it actually assimilates them into its design. I counted no less than five games I had played before in VR that Vertigo had simply used as set pieces. Riding boats, shooting aliens and robots, taking a turret to enemy helicopters, what other games call their whole experience, Vertigo 2 calls a twenty minute stretch. And it goes on for over ten hours. The writing is hilarious. Every character is likable and I felt very sad when some of then were gone. The music was also fantastic. The wow moments keep coming one after the other like a machine gun and I promise it's like nothing you ever experienced in VR before. You'll be eaten by a fish, and then rocketed through its bloodstreams. You'll be hopping over lava waves while plugging a giant worm in the face with your shotgun. I don't want to ruin the best moments, but those were some of my favorites. Every single time I tried to guess what this game would do next, I was proven wrong with the biggest smile on my face. This is an extremely special experience that I am really thankful I was able to have and I can't wait to keep playing it over and over, though nothing will be as magical as the first. Now for what's not so great: The bosses are extremely tough. This is fun of course but one in particular, the church leader with the turban, is just too stressful for what you've got going on there. Even the brain boss, with a room you could barely stretch your arms in, was more manageable. They just stuffed too many enemies into the room at once, which all disappear when you defeat the boss anyway, so it was pretty unnecessary. Also I will echo other peoples sentiments that the SMG is a waste of a slot. It does hardly any damage and is the biggest and clunkiest gun, the worst part is that the spot to rip out your mag and the spot to lay your hand for stability are right next to each other and I don't need to tell you why that was problematic. I also wish the secret bow and arrow had better tracking with the pulling hand, so I felt better using it in more stressful and up close situations.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun. Kind of Half Life with a Rick & Morty vibe. Cool weapons, creative art, and a nice variety of environments, with some laughs along the way. The story is a bit head-scratchy, but serviceable. I like the ammo regeneration concept here; no need to constantly be scrounging for it. It ran pretty well on my system (Quest 2, RTX 3060ti, 8 core Ryzen, Win 11), with a few little goofs (like head popping through a wall) and one crash.When it comes to combat, I admit I'm not much of a soldier. Easy mode was plenty challenging for me. The boss battles I could mostly handle, except the lava monster, which was frustrating.  More competent players will have no problem.Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Vertigo 1, to the point of speedrunning it a few times. But V1, while very impressive, was a fairly short game which definitely had a wonky "indie dev" sort of vibe to it. But I loved the creativity, game play, and humor to play through it multiple times. So when I heard that Vertigo 2 was coming out, I knew I would buy it, expecting it to be very similar, though perhaps a bit polished. Especially as it's made by a sole dev. And hoooooly balls was I wrong! Vertigo 2 makes Vertigo 1, a good enough game in its own right, feel like a mere tech demo. The animations, game play, story, setting, landscapes, soundtrack, weapon optimization and variety, enemies, and levels all scream "AAA game". I'm about 10 hours in, and every level introduces new, well-thought-out, and (most importantly) fun mechanics, enemies, weapons, and concepts. This is an absolute must-buy, though make sure you play Vertigo 1 first, as the story is a continuation of that.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: My setup: Valve Index, RTX 3090, i9 10900K, 32GB, and Win10. It's not easy communicating the greatness of the game. Maybe better with an example. I had this issue of having about 20 soldiers to battle and one big alien monster. I ended up hiding under a desk, while the monster killed all the soldiers, lol. The monster did get badly hurt, and when meeting it I killed it with a single shot.This illustrates the way you have to think in Vertigo 2. There's no way you easily could take out that many soldiers or such a powerful alien monster. Well, you could shoot them all, but that would be difficult and time-consuming.In another place, I met a similar monster, and I fled - but found a platform and could shoot it from a long distance.The crazy content means you're constantly on the edge of your seat in Vertigo 2. There are aliens who only attack you, if you attack them - so do not shoot at them first. I'm doing a lot more thinking in this game than I anticipated, especially for the harder battles.AI is pretty good, had an alien friend following me, and it did so nicely. Then again, this is a first person shooter, you're not going to meet anything defeating you in chess ;-)Graphics are getting better later in the game, some of the first levels may suffer from being designed many years ago, while later levels look more fresh. There are several low-poly models looking like PS4 assets, and many low-res textures. But you also got high-res textures for guns, and textures look great when they are 10 feet away or more. You can find great dynamic shadows too, all in all graphics are great, animations too. Sound is excellent with the Index speakers.There are several combat situations which don't need to bow to Alyx, but generally Vertigo 2 is below the quality of Alyx, then again everything is. Vertigo 2 shines with its crazy universe, dark humor and semi-insane story - there's no other VR game just remotely close to it. Vertigo 2 is a surreal experience, and a perfect example of a virtual/alternate reality.My rating of the game would be 9.5/10. Alyx transcends the ordinary scale with 15/10.Btw, seems that Vertigo 2 only supports native SteamVR drivers, thus no OpenXR and no native Meta driver support. Of course no issue for Index users. Vertigo 2 supports Index finger tracking too.For left-handed users: note that currently left-handed controls are not working optimally - teleport has been assigned to left thumbstick, and I often teleport into enemies. Making custom controller bindings, I can't get teleport to work on the right Index controller - also you may need teleport to defeat the first boss and to jump correctly. Dev has promised to fix this March 31, but nothing has happened yet.Also not all parts of the game perform optimally, around the first boss some stutter is unavoidable, even reducing res to 20% (twenty!) the stutter was there, so it had nothing to do with needing a more powerful gpu - but no big deal, it was gone in the following level.With the Index res 280%, 4xMSAA and all other graphics settings maxed I get solid 90 fps - only dipping below near the first boss.PS. I did not like the playable demo - if you're considering buying this game try the full version instead, you can test it for up to 2 hours and refund if you don't like it.

_childDocuments_.review: While at work I watched a review from Habie147 on this game, since I was fishing around for new VR games at the time. I watched the review and was very impressed by what I saw, then bought and installed the game the very same night - boy am I glad I didI don't know what it is, but I  the 'infiltrate a top secret/high-tech facility' setting to bits.The story meanders away from that here and there, but does so in a way that makes sense and doesn't take you out of it.The gunplay is a little dated on some weapons: they have the movement sensitivity toned down to feel 'heavy', no two-handed weapons have a virtual stock (not a massive dealbreaker in this game), some weapons feel quite weak without damage upgradesOn the flip side, the movement feels good, all the weapons have the right amount of physics interactions to them without any jank. The game looks and sounds fantastic plus the soundtrack is pretty damn good. Oh and to top it all off there's an AKM in the game and it's probably one of the best guns in the entire game.Some of the boss fights were a little annoying to do, namely the Saplord and Cyber Joseph. Died LOTS during those fights. The pair of Centaurs was also quite annoying since they do massive damage and take a lot of it. I didn't like how some parts of the game NEEDED the teleport function since it felt kind of cheap.All in all, great game with a couple of relatively minor snags along the way. Definitely worth it though

_childDocuments_.review: Negatives: - The vehicle sections are currently a bit broken in the new update, but not gamebreakingly- Requires you to do a full click of the trigger to shoot and I feel like my knuckles (Index controllers) will break (it happened once before I got this game)- Not enough random ♥♥♥♥ like in remastered- Can't kill gentlehand- Replaying assembly is on the same level as sticking 23 rusty forks into my eyes (I've grown more fond of it over the hours)Positives: - Literally the best feeling gameplay in a VR game like this. BW and BL did great with realism, but in those games, jank felt really annoying. In Vertigo 2 the jank is a lot of fun most of the time (not vehicle sections). - Best loading screens in any game ever- Doesn't take itself too seriously but still takes itself seriously enough to be an immersive experience.- Story and worldbuilding is magnificent.- Best bossfights I've seen in VR games.- Indie game (I love indie games)- Hands down the third best OST in a VR game (1st and second are BW and BL)- H3VR reference in the game- Nani says trans rights (canon)- Insane ratio with performance and graphics, like this game is insanely beautiful and I ran it at a solid 90fps (besides the first boss which is currently broken CPU-usage-wise)- Only one real gun and yet getting it is an insane moment if you didn't know it was coming. - IN GAME LEVEL EDITOR WITH CUSTOM ASSET IMPLEMENTATIONS- Should've been GOTY 2023

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game is excellent and is deserving of every bit of praise. The game was very engaging throughout, with only a few parts of the game feeling truly frustrating. Unfortunately, these parts are all within the latter half of the game, leaving a great impression, but a bit of a frustrating near-end experience.I cannot see very well in VR, so I especially struggled with the stealth enemies. The fact that you had to face 6-8 of them and they only became fully visible when they were right in your face dogpiling you, it was really quite frustrating, and i ended up having to cheese the last confined room with all the stealth bots (not fun).I also struggle with being overwhelmed in VR and most players can. The sheer amount of enemies this game can throw at you, especially sniper enemies which make it impossible to move around some sparse environments, makes it a case of trial and error sometimes.Apart from these main issues (which ended up being quite a big two issues, but whatever) I absolutely loved Vertigo 2, and highly recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: You can view my review & gameplay here: This is a must buy for VR. If you loved Vertigo Remastered, then I'm sure you'll love this game as well. Fair warning though: this game is a lot more challenging than Vertigo Remastered with tough boss fights. However, you can turn down the difficulty as well as enable cheats from the console commands. So this game is accessible for all.I beat the game in about 14 hours on normal difficulty. I had a lot of fun along the way. However, the game is not perfect and with only one developer, I don't think you can expect perfection. However, it's simply boggles the mind that one developer can make one of the best games in VR and a game that should be a strong contender for VR GOTY 2023. Zach Tsiakalis-Brown deserves all the kudos, not just for bringing this great game for PCVR, but also for the more than reasonable price tag (if anything, it is on the low side).Game is running on the Unity Engine. On my RTX 3080, I was getting a steady 90 fps for the most part. I did experience some bugs, but the biggest one (Steam VR crashing) is one that I can't exactly say for sure is the game's fault so I'll just mention it, but without assigning blame. I do think the gun angle was too high by default for the Meta Quest 2 touch controllers. Lastly, there is some jank overall to some of the VR interactions. All the graphical, sound, & gameplay settings that you would expect are here. You can play comfortably seated.However, I will add that teleport is a necessary gameplay element in some of the boss fights. So if you don't like teleport, unfortunately, unless you cheat & use console commands, it is something you will have to do. I would have preferred a sprinting option. The gameplay, story, graphics, sounds, all come together to make for a great VR adventure. It's a can't miss VR experience. Honestly, you should stop reading this review and just buy the game. It's not perfect, but it's a great game that deserves a VR nomination for GOTY 2023 at the very least.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: 10/10Vertigo 2 isn't just a game; it's an unparalleled virtual reality experience that sets an unprecedented standard for immersive gameplay. From the moment you step into its virtual world, you're transported to a realm where innovation and creativity collide, resulting in a gaming masterpiece that earns a perfect 10.One of the most striking aspects of Vertigo 2 is its breathtaking visuals. The graphics are nothing short of stunning, with an attention to detail that makes every environment feel alive and dynamic. From futuristic cityscapes to alien landscapes, the game's artistry is a testament to the developers' commitment to pushing the boundaries of what's possible in virtual reality.The gameplay mechanics are a revelation, seamlessly blending traditional first-person shooter elements with mind-bending puzzles and gravity-defying challenges. The level design is a triumph, offering a perfect balance of exploration and action. Each stage feels like a carefully crafted work of art, encouraging players to think critically and adapt to ever-changing circumstances.The narrative is equally compelling, weaving an intricate and engaging story that keeps you hooked from start to finish. The character development is top-notch, and the voice acting is impeccable, adding layers of emotion and depth to the overall experience. As you progress through the game, you'll find yourself invested in the fate of the characters and the unfolding mysteries of the plot.Vertigo 2 truly shines in the realm of virtual reality. The level of immersion it achieves is unparalleled, making you forget the real world as you navigate through its rich environments. The attention to detail in the VR interactions, from gripping weapons to solving puzzles, is a testament to the developers' commitment to delivering a true VR masterpiece.Moreover, the soundtrack deserves special mention. The music perfectly complements the on-screen action, enhancing the emotional impact of key moments and contributing to the overall atmosphere of the game. It's a testament to the holistic approach taken by the developers to create an unforgettable gaming experience.In terms of replayability, Vertigo 2 offers a wealth of content. Whether you're a completionist aiming for 100% achievements or someone looking to explore different playstyles, the game caters to a wide range of preferences. The variety of weapons and abilities at your disposal adds an extra layer of depth, ensuring that each playthrough feels fresh and exciting.In conclusion, Vertigo 2 is a triumph in every sense. It pushes the boundaries of what's possible in virtual reality gaming, delivering a seamless blend of stunning visuals, engaging gameplay, and a compelling narrative. It's a testament to the potential of VR as a storytelling medium and sets a new standard for excellence in the gaming industry. If you own a VR headset, Vertigo 2 is not just a game you should play—it's an essential experience that showcases the true potential of virtual reality. A resounding 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a true exhibition of what VR is capable of. _childDocuments_.review: This is the one, this game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing.Oh my god IDK where to begin.I'll list the stuff that impressed me and the stuff that didn'tpros:Music is a vibeThere are many different locations and a lot a very uniqueThere is swimming and it feels really goodThere are vehicle rides and you can even use mounted weapons, oooOOoH mah gawdNPC's that are both friendly, provide lore, speak to you and follow you through locations sort of like Cpt. Price :D and ohh I wanted that so bad, companions in VR are really coolEnemy variety: Forget about soldiers and zombies, we've god DINOSAURS, big ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ robots, crabs, lil goblins, fire golems, cubes from minecraft, cacodemons and I'm sure a bunch more, haven't gotten there yet.Secret weapons♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ GORGEOUS CUTSCENES, not only did the devs figure out to make cutscenes work in VR, but they also look so good, with beautiful "camera" angles and establishing shots. Shots of the Earth in space literally made my jaw drop.Splash texts are full of ROFLSIf I find more cool stuff as I play further, I'll list them aboveNow for the meh parts.cons:The weapons are really floaty, the reloading feels solid and good, but in order to simulate weight, they used a similar mechanic to Saints and Sinners, where the gun just kinda wobbles around when it really shouldn't. And at Chapter 5 there's an "elevator" with a valve in a magma filled room that on my playthrough looses collision towards the end of the ride and sends me flying into death, thankfully you can use nearby pipes to teleport to the nexr location.Other than that, Holy ♥♥♥♥. Best game, at least for me personally. Step aside, Boneworks and Alyx.Finally, a game purchased in 2023 that doesn't leave me disappointed.Also sorry if my spelling sucks, English isn't my mothertongue.

The inventory system is awful especially when needing to move and grab at the same time during a firefight. It just doesn't work well at all. The weapons implementation feels very poor. _childDocuments_.review: I used to have a joke about how good this game is, but I just want to change it for any review crawlers in here. This is hands down, zero exaggeration, without a doubt, the absolute BEST vr game yet, in fact its one of the best games in general i have ever played. And to anyone who would like a bit of wisdom, here it is.We need to demand better. This game should be a beacon of quality for devs to reach. But we don't demand better. Ever. Because almost everyone will eat up any garbage that is given to them and we will never DARE criticize anything because of how hard we know game development is. Stop it. _childDocuments_.review: So - just finished the game.  I am leaving my original review below to show my state of mind after one of the bosses.This game is hard to describe.  I both loved and hated the game.  If I could go back in time I would show myself this review.  You will see amazing things that will leave you in awe.  You will laugh in delight and humour.  You will get this quirky little organic gun that is insanely fun to use.  So why did I also hate it?Imagine you are watching "The Godfather" for the first time.  Marvel at the loving detail the creator invested in this art.  You are captivated by the story, and immensely enjoying yourself.  Suddenly - for some reason, the creator splices in a sequence of someone running their nails down a chalkboard.  How long is this going to go on?  You don't know.  Eventually you suffer through it, and get back to loving the movie when suddenly it happens again ... and later again ... and again.These are the boss fights, and the combats with ridiculous difficulty spikes.  The bosses are all interesting and quite lethal.  They also frequently take place in a very small room with little to no cover.  I guess you are just supposed ... to be perfect?  I am playing a game, not training for the olympics!  One of the boss fights was literally "Oh, you know that boss that was giving you trouble before?  Well, here are two and now do it in a room with hardly any cover.  Have Fun!".  The game of course has a checkpoint system, and for the most part it is pretty good.  It was only one mega fight near the end where you would die, and you would restart right in the middle of your foes and die again in 4 seconds.  Wheeeeee!  It is absolutely INFURIATING because the rest of the game is SO GOOD!  WHY ARE YOU SABOTAGING THIS MASTERPIECE?Mercifully the game has difficulty levels that you can change on the fly (otherwise I wouldn't have progressed past 20% of the game).  Once it became clear that some of the difficulty cliffs were just stupidly difficult and unfair, I would just sigh, roll my eyes and lower the difficulty down to story to get past this chore.  I mean ... you will still die, just not as often.  Once the boss or insane combat was over and I was having fun again - I would put it back to normal, and I had to do this over and over again because the game was so wildly uneven.The weapons.  The weapons are various and you can get upgrades for them.  Many of them are so inaccurate that you couldn't hit a lake if you were standing at the bottom.  Once they are partially upgraded, you might be able to hit the broadside of a barn.  Seriously, the weapons seem to prefer to shoot around an enemy rather than at it.  None of this applies to the organic gun which is just pure fun.Now you know what is super not fun?  Being trapped in a small room with a lethal boss, fumbling with your weapons to reload.  Reloading of course takes two hands, which is kind of hard to do when you are running/teleporting constantly to avoid the bosses attacks.  However the game offers some advice.  It is easier to switch to another weapon which will be loaded, so do this a few times and then go back to your favourite weapon - and this works ... sometimes.  See - for some reason - even though you can see on the selection dial that there are mags available for that weapon - when you switch back to it - it remains empty.  I don't know why - but there you are - pointing an empty gun at a pissed off boss.  It is wall punchingly frustrating.So - yeah - you can get past the drudgery by changing the difficulty level.  However, there is one section that this WON'T help with.  It is in this lab with a bunch of puzzles (ugh) - one of which is a non-sequitur.  You can just look up the solution, right?  Yeah ... but not with one of them because everyone loves a JUMPING puzzle with clunky physics right?  Especially if there are a chained sequence of tasks and if you fail you get to do it all over again.  But wait ... there is more ... how about a really unforgiving TIME LIMIT, and if time runs out ... well, do it over again, and again, and again.  WHY?  WHY ARE YOU MAKING ME DO THIS?????????????So ... overall I am going to change my original review and give this a thumbs up ... but just BARELY.  I figure the good parts will linger in my memory more than the terrible boss design and clunky weapon loading.  Oh ... did I mention that there were like 11 or so bosses?  Yeah ... this is not a case of just suffering through one or two.  Anyway - if you don't mind difficulty cliffs and doing the same fight over and over and over again - then yeah, this game is great.  Except for that timed puzzle - that is just game cancer.------------------  Original Review ------------------------------------------------------I know it says I only played for 5 minutes.  Its because when I play PCVR I need to play disconnected from the internet.  I actually have about 3 hours in it and haven't finished the game yet.I was a huge fan of Vertio - but I am actually pretty disappointed with this.  Why?  Its the bloody bosses.  I thought the bosses in Vertigo were interesting and fun.  Someone somewhere must have complained because the bosses (while still interesting ) are wall punchingly frustrating.  Even on Story mode you will die again, and again and again *SapLord* - with no way to get past them.  And let me say - fighting a boss in a tiny arena in VR while fumbling with weapons and teleports is NOT fun. So it makes the game a chore.There really needs to be an option to bypass these black holes of fun in games.Just learned there is a cheat mode - so do yourself a favour - when you get to a boss - if you still can't get past it on story mode - just enact god mode and bypass the chore.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:-It'll take you about 10 hours to get through the story. -There are 6 secret weapons and lots of lore to collect, encouraging exploration.-Bosses are some of the best I've seen in a VR game.-I think there's multiple endings? I haven't replayed the final levels so I'm not 100% sure yet.-After you beat it, you unlock New Game Plus, allowing you to replay levels and upgrade your guns again (since upgrade stations can only be used once).Here's my review video if you'd prefer REVIEW:Changing my review. Originally it was a thumbs down for me due to poor balancing, and while I still think some areas need a nerf, the worst offender was the boat level, which the developer did nerf.. wish I knew a nerf was coming before I suffered through that level, but either way it shows the dev is listening, so let's talk about what this game does right.THE GOOD:Let me start by saying that the fact this game is made by a single developer is actually insane. There's just so much content, so many unique ideas all crammed into this game, it's truly a treat to play. Even the more annoying parts make up for it with every level delivering a unique experience.The best example I could give is that Vertigo 2 feels like the original Half-Life, but in VR. Not a VR port, but it's own game with idea after idea thrown at the player, with each area being something fresh just as you start getting bored of the last.The final levels in the game are really evocative of the original Half-Life, with you traveling through different dimensions at a breakneck speed, flying across jump pads while sniping enemies and being bombarded with all sorts of enemies.The highlight for me is the boss fights. These manage to actually be intense and difficult, which is something you don't see in VR. They've all got their own mechanics, their own special one-shot-kill move you need to dodge, and the last few fights end up being a true endurance test with you juggling all your weapons, desperately trying to reload them all while avoiding attacks. They're difficult, but very rarely did I feel cheated when I died, only frustrated.Guns feel intentionally sloppy. A few hours into the game and I was starting to get annoyed at how much the guns flop about, but I got used to it, and this is a good time to mention that you can upgrade all your weapons at weapon stations hidden throughout the game.The moment it all clicked for me was when I purchased stability, which is usually a useless upgrade on weapons, right? Not in Vertigo 2! Stability made the guns actually have a lot more control, so I think it was all intentionally annoying so the upgrades would feel meaningful.Another thing about the guns is there's unlimited ammo that's on a cooldown for each weapon, which is fine. I never felt like I had too much ammo to feel overpowered, but there are definitely some guns that shine more than others.THE BAD:There's not many things this game does wrong, but what it does do wrong almost made me quit playing.Around the middle of the game, you're thrown into a massive warzone map. The concept of it is great, but the execution is a bit frustrating. You have allies, but they're stupid and just get in the way, and enemies seem to always target me. Fighting your way through the streets is all well and good, but eventually you get to the enemy stronghold and are just barraged with wave after wave of enemies.. seriously, the fight takes like 10 minutes and if you die, you have to start again.I'm all for an epic battle, but it was more of a battle on my patience than difficult.One main complaint with this game is there's a couple areas like this that just have wayyy too many enemies, and it trivializes fights, forcing you to take cover, peak your head out to shoot, then hide until your ammo recharges.Worst of all, a handful of these battles barely have any cover at all, so if you have 1 hit when you get to these spots, good luck.Another issue I had was enemy variety.. okay let me start by saying there's a good amount of enemy types in this game ranging from all sorts of weirdo aliens, but overall there's a bit too many of the same copy-pasted robot enemies.There's even this one big robot that acts as a sort of mini boss. He's pretty difficult to beat, but near the end of the game he's a normal enemy.Personally I'd like to see some of these areas tweaked. I know Vertigo 2 is trying to be a difficult game, but less is more in this case. I'm pretty good at VR games, and even I was struggling with some areas.. mostly the boat area I mentioned above, which was thankfully nerfed.CONCLUSION:Vertigo 2 is one of those rare games that would be great even without being in VR. A lot of VR games are pretty mediocre if you take away the VR gimmick (like Saints and Sinners and even Boneworks). They're great games in VR, but without? Ehhh.I know this isn't a very good argument, but I'm just trying to say that even if Vertigo 2 wasn't in VR, it would still be a great game, but being in VR brings it to a whole other level that I highly recommend.
