_childDocuments_.review: I have to be completely honest, I mainly selected no just so this wouldn't get buried under all the other positive reviews that praise this game as the new leading standard for VR games and, keyword, experiences. For what it's worth, I think Vertigo 2 was a pretty fun VR game that, if you're a consistent VR user looking for something new or completely new to the genre itself than it'll likely scratch the itch, but I think there's a massive push to really herald this game as something it isn't; revolutionary.I'll start with what Vertigo 2 does right; being a game. I think it does a much better job out the gate actually interesting the player than Vertigo 1/Remastered did. I played and ultimately refunded Remastered because I felt it was far too arcade-y, sluggish, and failed to captivate me within the two hour refund window, which was disappointing after so many reviews for that game put it on par with Alyx, Boneworks, and TWD. Vertigo 2, as evidenced by my play hours, does a much better job out the gate getting the player involved. The weapons all, for the most part, feel unique to use and reload, but you'll find yourself really just quick cycling through your weapon wheel in the later stages of the game to maximize time shooting over time reloading, which I felt really trivialized the combat in the end game. I wouldn't even consider myself getting better or more in-tune with the game, I just found my entire arsenal of weaponry to literally overpower the waves of mobs you shoot. Whether or not you think that's a negative is up to you, I'm not entirely sure if this was conscious decision on the devs part to emulate DOOM or Half-Life, but it doesn't feel like the enemy design held up to the weapon power creep.On that note, the enemies are visually varied and visually unique, unfortunately the AI is on par with that of Bethesda enemies and, apart from a few exceptions, all just have some form of range attack to throw or shoot at you. I think the enemies work great as they're introduced throughout the story, as each time you find yourself fighting a new one you have to learn what's unique about it, but that starts to get predictable once you figure out their entire behavior model boils down to; Do they run at you or stand still, do they use cover or ignore it, and are their ranged attacks instant or projectiles? And even then, when there's just a massive group of them on screen, you just find yourself prioritizing which ones are closest since they don't meaningfully interact with each other apart from whether or not they hold position or charge at you.The environments are definitely varied and some setpieces are downright gorgeous, but I found exploring some areas to be confusing since it wasn't always clear which path was the way forward and which path was optional. I wouldn't say it really hampered my experience since I found all the secret weapons and most of the weapon upgrades and codex entries, but I did find it a little tedious to have to scour wide open areas on the off chance there was something hidden. On that note, I'm not sure if this was just an issue on my end or if it is intentional, but for some reason using smooth locomotion to go forward is slower than going sideways or backwards. Yes, you can teleport, but it bothered me that through my entire play through that my character moved slowest in the direction that you'd be able to move the quickest.The music is great, the voice acting is pretty good, and the animations are a little hit or miss. I think that about covers the game aspect, now for (in my opinion the most important part) the VR experience part of it.I do not know what identity Vertigo 2 has.I had a feeling once it was described by the creator as "Half-Like" that it would be overly influenced by Valve, and it definitely is, so much to the point that I think it was so focused on trying to be some Valve-esque game that it neither hits that mark or creates a unique VR experience. The most involved parts of the game are a helicopter turret section, which I found myself fighting the turret as much as I was fighting enemies with it, a boat section that all you really need to do is go full throttle and then turn every once in a while, and the reloading, which you do a lot. Apart from that, you don't interact with the environment like you can in Alyx, you don't have a reason to interact with it like you would Into the Radius or TWD, and it doesn't let you find creative ways to traverse it like you would in Boneworks. It's first and foremost a VR Shooter, which is fine, but apart from light exploration and upgrading that's all it really is. Despite how big the stages are you don't feel immersed in them apart from purely visuals, and that's if you don't mind some of the strange enemy designs.I don't understand what it does as a VR experience to earn some of the recognition that it's superior to Alyx; it has more guns and enemies and biomes but, at the end of the day, thats just more things to shoot at, with more things to shoot with, in more areas to shoot in.TWD has crafting progression and exploration. Into the Radius has exploration and gear progression. Boneworks has it's entire physics-focused playstyle and playgrounds. The one thing Vertigo 2 offers over those is boss fights, and those are so hit or miss that I honestly couldn't remember half of them off the top of my head.Look, I'm being overly critical because as much as I enjoyed it as a VR shooter, I didn't walk away from it thinking it brought something new to the VR table to advance it. If you want to make the argument that it presents the idea that VR levels can be big, enemies can be varied, and bosses can be incorporated you can, but Alyx presented that 3 years ago. Vertigo 2 could've, theoretically, been that advancement, but it's an indie game with I think just 1 dev. To expect that would be just asinine.I applaud what was done as a solo passion project for years, I think what's presented is a fun VR shooter with enough variety for things to feel fresh as you play through it's 8-12 hour campaign. But unless it's your first VR game do not go into it expecting something groundbreaking or the "new bar" for VR to hit. It's a fun game, but it's not a new VR experience.

_childDocuments_.review: So, i had 4 major issues with the original (despite the original also being fantastic btw)1. length of the game2. replay value3. cliffhanger ending4. lack of boss fightsand i can say that all 4 were addressed here, the main story easily took me 11 hours to beat (hard difficulty, but still very long game regardless)the game has hidden encyclopedia entries, hidden weapon upgrade cases, 2 endings, and even a split path near the middle that decides what weapons you get throughout the rest of the run with their own unique story and boss fights, and even secret (missable) weapons you can findthe game has a proper, beginning, middle and end story, that doesnt just suddenly end.and there are SO many bosses here, i think there are like like 14 easily of the top of my headand you get a newgame+ mode when you beat it, in case you were concerned about missing things.overall, extremely happy about how the game ended up, a must have for any vr owners and a very easy recommendation from me, highy suggest you .also buy Vertigo Remastered along side it if you dont already have the first game.I did have some minor nitpicks, but they are just that, nitpicks:1.when in seated mode, you can use the [right stick] up+down to go between crouched and standing, but its not done gradually, its either full standing or fully crouched, i wish it was done like boneworks where you can adjust your height with the right stick instead of it being a binary choice, there are many occasions (mostly elevator buttons/switches) where i was either too tall, or too low to use them.2. you can only teleport with the left touchpad with no way to rebind it (i played in smooth locomotion mode, right handed, seated) this was an issue throughout the entire game because most other games put the teleport feature on your dominant hand for quicker access, this left me with very bad reaction times when trying to dodge boss attacks (you cannot dodge some attacks without it). Might be because of the lack of buttons available to put it on, but i do hope there is a way to put it on the dominant hand somehow. (perhaps clicking in the stick, as its unused in the game)And thats it really, i had no other issues in the gameI do hope we get post launch support with this product as i simply want to play it even more. The original got a dlc for custom levels, and i do hope it returns along side some sort of endless wave based mode (some levels in the game are just begging to be arenas)

_childDocuments_.review: I'm just going to say it now, this game is 100 the best purchase I've made in months.but the main reason im posting this is because everyones goes "waahhh gun clunky :(((" with a bad review.so, from my research, the game is made in the Unity editor, i use the same.assuming that they are using Configurable joints (basically joints that can act as springs, hinges, etc. kind of like the constrainer from Bonelab.) i can say simply, on moving objects, they are horrible to work with.that "snappy movement" from guns when moving quickly is literally 99% unfixable. (from my research and use of unity / config joints for almost 2 years now.)they basically all types of joints, from configurable joints to spring joints (config joints are basically every single type in one component, but you can also have individual ones.) to hinge joints and so on, all require a rigidbody.rigidbodies are what basically give gravity, mass, and physics.the way i think the recoil in the game works, is it chooses two random values between two other values (how much should the recoil go up, and how much left or right should it go)-before adding forces to the tip of your current weapon upwards and either to the left or the right (depending on the other values.)so in the most simplistic way possible, there quite literally is ZERO fix without COMPLETELY scrapping the physics-based gun handling system, and replacing them with ones which will either just phase through walls making cheating easier, or contacting unity to get better with colliders. (im sure there are a few other ways but these are the main ones i found.)me personally as a developer, have ZERO issue with the clunky gun physics because i understand how displeased they must have been finding out that they cant give you a better experience, and that it would just feel less polished.they tried their best. that's all i can say.

_childDocuments_.review: I cry, knowing it will be years yet until I play a game of its caliber again. TLDR: buy, play, savor, regret you ran out, weep.I would advise you play the remaster of Vertigo 1 first, I played the first chapter and got annoyed at all the self referential humor going on, so I went back and played my copy of the first game. Correct decision. Several visual gags rely on the foreknowledge of the last game.Speaking of gags, the game has... a sense of humor? As the visual style and palette of voice actors may have clued you in, this game goes in for a cartoon-y art style (bright color, saturated, lots of good stuff like that) And honestly? It's feels good to look at. At times, especially in the wider open areas, the lack o small details are apparent, but fortunately in those areas you are usually distracted by the ass-wagon of enemies trying to murder youWhich brings me to combat. The combat is IMO the weakest part of this game. And that is not a criticism. I like the weapon designs they went with. They're wacky, variable, and give you capabilities you otherwise wouldn't have in the ways you least expected them. I love their enemy variety, it is wonderful and needs to be seen to be believed. Some of the weapons are pea-shooters, especially by endgame, but this is always compensated for by the ammo regen system. My railgun can 1 hit kill most enemies, but it has woeful regen times, so unless you hate that crab, you use the starter pistol. Certain enemies are also predisposed to weakness to certain weapon types, which rewards you for weapon switching. The combat style, with the teleporter bunnyhopping, is suited for fast pace combat with large groups of enemies in open areas with cover, slow methhodical corner hallway clearing ala Halflife, or big bosses with attack patterns. And the game has all three: well done. The shotgun is also OP as ♥♥♥♥ and I followed a friends advice to never upgrade to keep fair. Still used it time to time. It's a really nice shotgun tooMy only criticisms are thus 1. The cartoonishness of the of the weapons makes them feel mediocre (Looking at you Hammer and Sickle). 2. Not all weapons get the attention that they deserve because some of the situations they're good for are too... situational. You will be mainlining the one gun that is good versus android, because that's a majority of the enemies. 3. The difficulty scaling is brutal and somewhat random. Between group battles, hallway battles, and boss battles, the first is by far the most difficult, and turning a corner to be met by hells whole Xenos and robot buggery squadron is a bit jarring when 10 minutes ago I was doing healing drugs to RP being a heroine addict. The Bosses are at least always fair. As in slack off and die (they can and will 2-hit combo murder you), pay attention and use your brain and you can avoid most damage with easeYes this review was disproportionately about the combat, it's the central gameplay loop! GitsThe exploration parts are divine BTW. The open areas, vehicle sections (word to the wise, play this game AFTER acquiring VR legs) and scale they employ many, many times feels like I'm playing in a museum to other realities. It's great. The lore is great. The plot is great. If you are the kind of person who cares about science fiction and thematic elements, you're smart enough that I needn't opine about the quality: you will enjoy it. Off with you!In short: Weep. Because this game feels like what the world would be like if VR had AAA devs. I suppose they do. Good job Zach

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this game is legit super good. The original Vertigo was pretty good by itself, but this sequel does most things bigger and better. You actually have branching paths in the story, and the gunplay is decent in this game. its still not perfect, since shooting in VR really doesnt work very well if you dont have a larger space, and since you are unable to feel any real feedback for two handed weapons to really work well, but for what it is, its decently solid.One major complaint I have is unfortunately, the sponginess of the enemies. It often takes an inordinate amount of bullets to kill them, making all of your guns feel anemic. This was pretty bad in the original Vertigo as well. Weapon balancing is also not all that great either, as an example, the revolver feels a lot better to use than your starter pistol, but the ammo takes an age to regenerate, and it becomes relatively worthless in the mid game onwards due to how low your overall DPS is with it due to the very slow fire rate. Also, using the sights on some of the guns is not intuitive. The models are sometimes far too large/tall, so its awkward to use the sights. As examples, the starter pistol is VERY tall, the iron sights are barely useable, if you stick a reflex sight on it, it becomes impossible to aim, as its so high up compared to your hand, that it doesnt naturally come to your eyes when pointing it. the optic glass for the reflex sight is also a tiny little thing, so catching the dot in the sight is a pain. Every time I pull up the pistol to aim, I have to wave it around to find the dot. it was so bad that I unequipped the reflex sight shortly after getting it. The SMG iron sights are pure trash as well, I know it was to make it "unique feeling" by putting the middle blade back near your face, and the side blades in the front near the muzzle, but it doesnt work. It feels immensely awkward to try and use the iron sights on the SMG. If you have any training with actual firarms, you understand that you aim with irons by focusing on the middle blade, having it up close shortens the effective distance of your sights, making aiming accurately more difficult, as it is like getting normal sights and pulling them all the way near your face. the first thing you want to get for the SMG is the reflex sight, the glass on that is actually decently large, so you can catch the dot and use it to aim without much trouble. Its better to just hipfire the SMG for close range use till you get optics for it. With that said, I do have to point to the shotgun having good irons. I actually like the iron sights for the shotgun. Its a ghost ring sight, but with the full sight image being an aiming cross. Its natural and easy to use, which is what makes good iron sights.One final nitpick: The loading tips are really insulting. It feels like most of them are mean-spirited, unless its supposed to be a joke. If they are supposed to be a joke, it's a very bad joke.The overall package as a game is very very good though, for sure, this is one of the best VR games out there right now IMO. It really does feel like its near the same level as Half Life: Alyx.If you are new to VR, you will want to get this game (along with the original Vertigo Remastered), but dont play it as one of your first games, it will ruin most other experiences because your bar will be set far too high. Most of the other popular VR titles out there are usually much more limited in scope, or are very early generation VR games, where they are still figuring out good ways to do things. Play around with some other smaller popular titles to get a feeling for VR and get used to your setup and play space, then you can give games like the Vertigo series and HL:A a play to see the true potential of VR.Just a heads up: there is a short event in the game that might trigger thalassophobia if you have it. I noped through that in about a minute thankfully.

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolute triumph this game is, Easily one of the best VR games ever.Thius has my vote for VR Game of the year!This is an adventure that is fun all the way through, it has a ton of unique and cool weapons, lots of diferent enemies, locations, witty dialogue, good story... most if not everything feels polished and high quality, honestly it has it all...Usually i go more deep in my reviews but this is easily the best single player action adventure game since Alyx, cant praise it enough.Absolutely must play so, obviously very recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: This puts every other VR game to shame. I could not recommend this more. Phenomenal, so much thought and care into every asset and detail and mechanic and enemy and boss fight and sound and particle and everything in between. I love this game, and cannot believe how underrated it is right now. Fully recommend.Just to warn however, this is a long game. And although it has the most variety of any VR game to date, and probably most flatscreen games (yes, really), there are sections of copy paste hallway and robot fights, which can tedious and frustrating. If I were to have my way, I would remove and streamline some of these parts (e.g. spoilers: fetching the purple quantum key things was super boring and felt like a waste of time. _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible world, designs, story, humor. Feels good to play. Also the most challenging VR game I've ever played for sure. Absolutely AAA feeling work for a single dev. Worth the price I promise. One of the best VR campaigns out there. ...but I am not short on complaints.The controls are just really very bad, but I really feel like this is all very easily fixable. I'm curious why the guns/hands feel super floaty in comparison to any other VR games. It's not a dealbreaker, but if it's a stylistic thing... it doesn't feel good. I would like to be able to dual wield and that would make a lot of sequences feel better, even if I had to put something away to reload. The game could just be ambidextrous rather than having to set handedness in the menu. It also sucks that my storage has to be on the opposite arm from my shooting hand. It feels very old school in a very bad way that I have to put my gun away to use a grenade or heal. Seeing as I'm left handed, the mirror'd controls are a pain. I want to be able to shoot with my left hand, and still control all motion with that hand too because that's how every game works with a regular controller where my left thumb controls motion. The mirroring sort of works but I mostly prefer teleportation which is stuck on the right. Also if I do try to throw a grenade with my right hand, I hit B (Quest 2 controller) to pop the pin... and it pauses the game. Also, in left handed mode every weapon in the game is held by my left hand while auxiliary actions (mainly reloading) is done by my right hand... until you pick up the aether bow. Then it switches for some reason. I just cannot imagine why this behaves this way. Maybe it's only programmed for right-handed mode or something, I didn't actually try switching the commands because...I didn't get the chance to use the aether bow. After I finished the challenge (which was frustrating for the controls and other reason that I'll get to), nothing happened. I lost access to the bow. It was no longer in the chest but it also wasn't in my inventory. Based on the backward feeling controls, I wonder if this is a bug with the handedness.I also feel like the game wasn't really tested for users who would prefer to teleport most of the time. Smooth motion makes me a little sick after not too long so I was really happy to see that the game supports dash teleportation which is my favorite alternative! Buuuuuuut, any range enemy seems to pin on you perfectly when you are only teleporting. This was really frustrating to figure out for how to fight the aetherbacks. It took me way too long to realize that they only really miss if you're strafing when they fire. With teleportation you would have to perfectly let go of the button after their arrow is in the air. This really sucks because it makes it so that not only am I forced to use smooth motion but I'm also wobbling back and forth the whole time which makes me extra ill./rAgain, I want to be clear that this game is not just great for something built by one person, but it just is a great game that's worth your time and money. But there are a handful of times where where the fact that it really was built by one person starts to show, especially in lack of testing. I really think making the game truly ambidextrous by attaching guns to the player body would be the way to go. I realize that this is an "arsenal shooter" (e.g. like Doom or Metal Gear Solid) and that may be tough so I'd say do something like what Resident Evil 4 VR does and just allow the player to assign weapons to body locations in a menu (live action menu or not). This allows the VR experience to flourish, feel less limiting, and keep the action moving. I realize my smooth motion complains are far more fundamental in the gameplay and tougher to make an easy for.

_childDocuments_.review: The developer clearly LOVES the Half Life series and Portal.Vertigo is excellently weird, in a lot of novel ways.  It acts as a linear corridor shooter in the same way as Alyx, but in a charming low-budget way.  It reminded me very strongly of Half Life 1 in a lot of places. Vertigo's story is its strong suit.  Things are strange, but the story stays within its established bounds and lets you learn the space.  The story branches in a couple places, and I haven't seen that executed well in VR before.The game is not perfect, notably in its gun selection.  A lot of guns feel a little bit awkward to use, and only a couple of them are truly exciting.  Some of them were simply outclassed by later ones.  The secret weapons feel like a punishment; when you pick one up, you're locked into a difficult encounter which you can only use the inferior secret weapon in.  Unlocking the bow in particular took like half an hour to escape from.  The map design is also sometimes a little awkward, especially in dark areas.Overall, one of the best shooters available on VR as a platform.  It doesn't exceed Alyx, but that makes sense because it's a small operation up against Valve.  Vertigo is a pretty great second, and far ahead of Boneworks.  I'm going to go hit up NG+ and see if I can't find more secrets.

_childDocuments_.review: I am usually very critical and easily find things to complain about. This game is amazing in that it only really has one flaw, the quite prominent and annoying hand movement smoothing. Most of the time it can be ignored but the faster the action gets the more it breaks immersion and, in a way, makes you lose track of your hands and weapons. Unfortunately, this feature can't be turned off or adjusted.That being said, Vertigo 2 is incredible, one of the very best VR adventure shooters available. The story is compelling, the characters are interesting and the game keeps suprising you all the way through. It's a good mix of funny, scary, difficult, easy, fast and slow all in one. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished the game yet because my controllers are dead and its late but like... THIS GAME IS SO GOOD. It is a linear story game which is heavily inspired by Half-Life 1, Alyx, and BONEWORKS (maybe a little bit of DOOM too). THIS IS A VR GAME DONE RIGHT.Although I haven't really been following the story, I feel like the storytelling is very much reminiscent of Half-Life storytelling as characters interact and talk to you and seamlessly flow from talking to gameplay. The story doesn't drag down this game at all, it clearly isn't taking itself too seriously and the humor has made me snicker a couple times.I absolutely love the gameplay, it doesn't feel like its in VR just to be in VR; that is an issue I have with a lot of other VR titles. If you have played Alyx before, the gunplay, healing system, and weapon upgrading system are all very very familiar. The enemies do offer a challenge and require you to be precise and take cover. There are a lot of really engaging boss fights in this game which all vary from each other in unique ways.Also just like, wow, its clear a lot of effort was poured into making the assets in this game. Every single model appears to be made for this game, not store bought (although there isn't anything wrong with store bought assets). It brings a lot of life to the environment when the assets look purpose built and made with lots of care and passion.There are plenty of other things which I can praise about this game too. There are so many moments which are nowhere short of the word EPIC. I am also surprised at how well vehicles are done in this game, they don't feel clunky and make for really intense moments. I wont spoil what you will be doing with vehicles but just know, its much better than BONELAB's vehicles.PLEASE PLEASE buy this game. Give the people who made this game money, this is clearly a labor of love for VR and gaming which deserves endless praise. I am probably over-hyping this, but if you are someone like me who has been a PCVR enthusiast for nearly a decade now, this is one of those games which scratches the right itches in all the right places.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's unbelievable that a small dev like this is able to develop such a great, polished game, while much bigger studios cannot even get to 50% of Vertigo 2's production quality.Some people may not like the humor or may not like the art style, I get that. But if you're a VR enthusiast, please do yourself and the developer a favor and buy this game (which, by the way, is very reasonably priced imho).One word of warning, though: This probably isn't the most suitable game if you're new to VR, because I think it could lead to motion sickness if you're not used to heights and rapid movement in VR.

_childDocuments_.review: This is truly the a next level paradigm shift for gaming. I've just come back to this game after playing Remnant 2 for a while. Within 10 minute of playing it all clicked again. The freedom of expression and of play style choice cannot be matched. Just Imagine for a second, replacing grindy repetitive task with genuinely challenging complex encounters with sly round about solutions. I haven't beat the game yet but coming back mid-game I cannot help but be floored by the ease of interaction and weapon swapping. I feel so "animation locked" in 2D games. A lot of games feel so formulaic and are overtly numbers, and RNG driven. This results in gaming most often feeling like a part time job. Vertigo 2 is just fun, visually stunning, poetic and an all around really good time. I cannot believe gaming has made it this far. I feel lucky to be able to experience this game, and am really excited to recommend it to anyone who may be interested in trying out VR gaming. I originally got into VR with the intentions of Sim Racing, but I'm glad I was able to take a nice detour into a more creative side.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best single-player VR game I've ever played.The game utilizes VR almost to its fullest, especially on the Index.I have never played a game that uses the click on the Index controllers as a hair trigger before, which lets you use the trigger's pull for abilities on your guns.I love the quirky character design, the enemies are so gross and funny.The movement uses both teleporting and locomotion to create really interesting fights with enemies and bosses, where you have to dodge by teleporting away from some attacks or to retrieve to cover.Small details like being able to crush cans in your hands and certain NPCs reacting to your hands are very nice touches and make it fun to mess around to see what happens.

_childDocuments_.review: Simply calling this game amazing would be an insult for how well made this is. Vertigo 2 rivals, and even surpasses other VR games like HLA and Boneworks. The weapons are all creative, the humor is good, secrets are gold, and the pacing is a drug trip. having to prove yourself in a soviet fighting ring before doing Russian Revolution 2: Electric Boogaloo, or having to take LSD before fighting off said revolution has to be the most fun I've had in any VR title to date.In short, get this game.

Where Vertigo established the SCP-like nature of its world, this game drives home the concept with fully fleshed out lore for its denizens, including how each manage to survive and coexist in this facility. My only nitpick would be that there might be a bit too much information at first, and it can be hard to first get into the thick data entries, which you somewhat need to if you really want to learn about the world. But after the first chapter or so, you start to gather them at a much more reasonable pace, making it much easier to keep track. Overall, I came for the guns and stayed for the LORE.

_childDocuments_.review: A truly expansive, native VR experience that took me over 12 hours to complete!  The environments were beautiful, the music and voice acting were excellent, and the story was humorous, nicely vague, and kept you guessing and engaged throughout.  The variety of weapons along with some of the missions to specifically use the secret weapons were fun, and I ultimately found that almost every weapon had a good use in the game.  In many cases, learning how to defeat certain classes of enemy by learning their timings and attacks was engaging and rewarding.  However, I do have quite a few strong criticisms for the game (EDIT:  many of these have been resolved but I'm leaving my original comments in followed by edits...this is definitely my second favorite VR game to date after HLA).  Taken as a whole, I'd have to say that I enjoyed the overall experience of Vertigo Remastered over this.  Although the minigun finale of that game was a bit lackluster, and it ended a bit too suddenly, I felt it was a tighter experience where you felt satisfied from beginning to end.  For Vertigo 2, the creator was far more ambitious but missed the mark in some areas.  I will list my criticisms in order of importance to me:1.  You cannot win the boss battles (at least on Hard difficulty) without using teleport and there is no sprint option - I have a rule in HLA and VR in general where I only use teleport to speed things along or do necessary platforming moves, but never during combat and as sparingly as possible to maintain immersion.  That's not possible in V2 where every boss battle require teleporting to survive, and this was a massive disappointment to me.  IMO, there should be a sprint option and you should be able to sprint/jump away from any dangers with the same results as teleporting.  EDIT:  I actually can beat a couple of the bosses without teleporting now that I understand their timings better, but I would still like to see a sprint option added to keep the tension high in boss battles and in general.  Not a fan of teleporting in general.2.  Several levels have significant stuttering, likely as a result of them being so huge - The lava and forest levels are where I noticed this the most, and lowering graphics settings didn't seem to help much at all.  In some areas, restarting the game seemed to clear it up but YMMV.  EDIT:  Recent updates seems to have fixed the forest level lag but I am still seeing it in the lava level to some extent.  Still, it seems much improved.3.  The combat can get tedious at times plus enemies respawn when loading an autosave - I especially noticed the tedious combat in the forest level, especially with so many saplings to kill who quickly become easy to figure out and dispatch.  In another forest section, I had killed all of the flies in a certain part, then died a bit later but when I loaded the autosave I was being swarmed by the flies who were already dead.  I don't think enemies should load back in after loading a save.4.  There was nothing overly creative or skilled as it pertains to how to defeat the bosses - In most cases, you just pummeled them with everything you had, evaded one of several of their scripted attacks, and then rinse and repeat until an obvious weakness would appear for you to exploit.  Some overt or environmental storytelling hinting to the player that certain areas might be the vulnerable ones to focus on would have made for more interesting combat moments.  EDIT:  Upon further review, the bosses do have some weak points to exploit, but in most cases the methods to defeat them don't require much creative thinking.I still enjoyed the game quite a bit, but the aforementioned criticisms will likely keep me from wanting to play it much in the future aside from my obligatory achievement grabbing that I'll be doing now.  However, if sprinting is added and some of the larger levels are better optimized, I would definitely give it another go after letting it breathe for a bit.  EDIT:  Well I ate my own words and have been playing the custom levels as well as replaying the game attempting to challenge myself in assorted ways, and with the new playable characters.  New content continues to fly in and this will be a heavily played game for me going forward.

_childDocuments_.review: A very solid Half-Like. You probably don't need to play the first game to fully appreciate this one, it improves on it in every way and there is a story recap cutscene.Creative and punchy weapons, upgraded shotgun especially, albeit with a lacklustre SMG. It bears mentioning how satisfying and tactile some of the reloads can be, once your ammo stocks have regenerated. Hunting down upgrade points and secret weapons provides some entertaining exploration, and you can toggle off any upgrades you want to disable.It has a very unique and stylised world and enemy design, with a mysterious story that shines in its exciting set-pieces, which can provide a decent challenge at times. An underrated element that serves to construct the universe-hopping setting is the colourful database that fills out with each creature, character and location you come across.It has its fair share of replay value too, given the number of ways to try another playthrough thanks to the update, plus some player-made levels to fiddle around in. I was compelled to go back through the game at least once more to find the stuff I missed.This sets the standard for single player action in VR. It's a rare case where it felt like playing a whole-ass game, rather than another experimental sandbox tech demo or the next 'Call of Duty but VR'.P.S. _childDocuments_.review: This game is FUN.It lives at a beautiful intersection between balls to the walls creativity and fast paced easy to learn fun to master gameplay.Its 10-14 hours full of many explosive set pieces, scary moments... and the pacing... *chefkiss*. It is only when you play a game with truly amazing level design that you realise how important level design is.I don't want my review to be too long and a lot of people have already talked about enemy variety, world building ecc.. but I want to speak briefly about the gameplay because it's not been talked enough IMO. The gunplay seems simple and I was slightly disappointed at first you could not dual wield like in Vertigo 1 however, when the difficulty started to ramp up, I realised how smart it was to introduce a manual recharge. Every gun has a different recharge mechanics and the more you use them the better you get with that particular gun.When you start to get the hang of it and understand that often the smart move is not to recharge but cycle to a different gun to create some space between you and the enemies... maybe teletransport behind cover, you take a breath, recharge a gun you were using before, you nail the recharge, shot in face the enemy that was almost getting to you ecc.. you start to feel like a real badass and the gameplay really clicks. Some of the encounters and bosses in which I had to cycle through almost all the guns and teletransport all around were true peak gaming moments for me. I already praised the pacing and level design in general terms but what really works about them, and for my money makes it a masterpiece, is that it strikes a very rare balance between making you feel scared and making feel a badass action hero. I would not characterize this as a horror game but there are plenty scary monsters, dark spaces, unknown dangers and thalassophobia inducing sections. What distinguishes it from a horror game in my opinion is that for every horror element there is an awe inducing one (sometimes at the same moment). This really an experience made for VR and VR elevates it to more of the sum of its parts and to the realm of Masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished this game, and I can't recommend it strongly enough!The art style is simple, but beautiful, and makes great use of scale.  There are some stunning sights in this game. The character models can be a bit clunky at times, and the animation is sometimes lacking, but the personality of each character comes through.  I appreciated that every level is populated with various creatures or robots, not all of which are hostile.  Some are just there, going about their day.The writing is very silly and doesn't take itself too seriously, but never in a lazy way.  The characters are interesting and varied, the world is well thought out, with a coherent lore and a deep backstory. Despite the general zaniness, the levels felt like places, not levels, which, to my mind, is the best thing you can say about a video game level.  I really enjoyed the in-game encyclopedia entries that unlocked during gameplay, and would always start each session by reading all the ones I had unlocked during the last one. There are are also some great Half-Life-style set pieces, which keep the narrative moving along, and are often quite funnyWhere the game really shines, though, is in the interactions.  The game has some physics, so your hands interact with the environment in a believable way, but doesn't go to extremes like Boneworks, where it feels like you're playing QWOP VR.  The haptic feedback for various interactions is really fine-tuned to perfection, and makes everything feel natural.  The guns (and there are a lot of guns) are varied, and all feel unique, each with it's own reloading method.  Speaking of reloading, the game's ammo system is a nice compromise between infinite ammo and ammo boxes.  Each gun takes magazines of some kind which have to be replaced when they run out, but the magazines regen over time. This means you have to think about ammo, but don't have to hoard it, or spend all your time searching for hidden ammo boxes.  The health system, likewise, is an interesting compromise.  You have regenerating health, but only up to 50%.  To get to 100%,  you have to consume health items or use first aid stations (which both feel great, by the way).  This made it so you had to worry about getting hit, but not so much that it wasn't fun.There's more to talk about, like the variety of enemies and bosses, or all the secrets, Easter eggs, and cameos, but the bottom line is that this is a great game and you should buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Previous game Vertigo Remastered i tried in vr arcade on a vive pro, best i could describe it "a boring boneworks", this one feels like a fleshed out game. Still prone to bugs, crashes steamvr on level transitions which leads to reusage of upgrade stations, breaking rendering on scripted teleport in chapter 11. Imagine crashing steamvr to get an upgrade to your arsenal... Still would prefer not crashing at all. Pacing also is quite weird. Some levels include two paths to the same goal, i ended up trying both paths and being softlocked on a scripted elevator, fixed by loading checkpoint 7mins ago. Some sections are brutal and will exaust all your resources, others are a cakewalk. Upgrade stations feel strange, sometimes you get alot of them throughout the same level and then you go without them for a long time. There are also weapons you dont get to keep which is weird. Bosses are not balanced equal, especially if you planned out your gun upgrades correctly. I still have not finished it due to another steamvr crash on level transition which drove me mad again. Oh well, it did crash before an upgrade station...Edit: Man, it did crash on final credits, please fix...

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard for me to find a VR game that makes me not want to put my controllers down, but this game managed to keep me enagaged with it to the point where I managed to complete it in 3 days.This game is a masterpiece with a great story, great gunplay, heart-throbing gameplay in general, detailed levels, some of the best music I've ever heard, a large number of secrets, metal gear level amount of world-building, multiple endings and great difficulty balancing with most fights feeling hard but mostly fair, it also features puzzles which aren't that great, in my opinion, but they are few and far between, so they don't break the pacing, one thing you shouldn't expect is Half Life:Alyx levels of interractivity, you won't be finding newspapars to read and you can't crush soda cans here, but you can break glass and some objects, you can also wear hats and take selfies which save as screenshots.A video game is supposed to be fun and should want to keep the player interested in what it has to offer and this game managed to do that spectacularly.10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Umm...holy crap was this so much better than I expected. At first it seemed like an Alyx kind of game, and while it has that Valve irreverence sorta baked into its writing, the farther in I went, the more I realized that I was traversing a, in a lot of ways literal, melting pot of several game/genre ideas. For some titles, this doesn't work, but in Vertigo 2, it's so deeply embedded in the plot that all the wild and wacky stuff you'll witness on your journey just fits together flawlessly. You'll go between many different environments and set pieces, each feeling quite different from the last, with nothing outstaying its welcome. The weapons, each serving fairly specific, but not required, purposes, all feel pretty good to shoot and reload, with some upgrades that I liked and some I feel I didn't really need.Overall, Vertigo 2 may very well be the best single player VR title I've ever had the pleasure of experiencing. Mr. Solo Dev, do me a favor, do ALL of us a favor.....make another game plz!

_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Hot damn that's a good VR videogame. Feels extremely half-lifey which is always great. Good voice acting; i kinda don't know what's going on but I'm invested. The weapons feel awesome and easy to use. Good physical interaction with the environment. No floating hands too, that's cool. The levels are brilliant if a bit linear, but that's not a bad thing, half-life is linear. There's a ton of valve references, and I mean a TON. I don't hate that, but they're a little everywhere. The art and design are good. Everything looks nice and is well optimized. Can run at almost max settings on a 3070ti with very solid framerate in headset. I think the weakest part of this game is probably the sound design, and that's the only thing I can really nitpick.It's a very, very good game overall. 8.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: the game is good and i genuinely do recommend getting it, possibly one of the best singleplayer VR experiences out there, if you look past the janky bits that is.the weapons are pretty eh until you upgrade them. I seriously cannot stress this enough, look for those upgrade stations. You can see if you missed any in the chapter select screen. the ones you cannot upgrade that you get from chapter 10 are pretty neat. with one having an overpowered weapon and underpowered melee, and the other having exactly the opposite.The levels are quite simply amazing, they're usually on an incredibly large scale and every environment is unique and usually quite good looking for a VR game. sadly though if you have to go through them a second time because something broke or perhaps you missed something, well there isn't a sprint button. you can however teleport to move slightly faster. so the levels with the size that they are can be annoying if you have to go through them a second time. thankfully that usually doesn't happen and they do flow fairly well. just keep in mind checkpoints can be kinda funky sometimes so make sure you are where you think you are in terms of level progression after getting shot in the head or restarting the game.The enemies are a big step up from remastered, going from moronic bot with a laser pew pew to basically being on-par with the half life 2 combine and beyond. The game gets hard, believe me. The progression of this difficulty however is fairly well-paced imo and the weapons you get are spaced apart just right to keep combat fresh as your arsenal and options in combat expand. I do wish the enemies moved a bit slower though or that there were less of them in certain situations (chapter 10, church side is practically unbeatable from the amount of hitscan enemies and how crappy your guns are in a fight like this), it can be quite easy to get overwhelmed since the combat and arenas seem like they were built for a flatscreen movement shooter and not a VR game. this does however slowly correct itself as you acquire more weapon upgrades and start dealing more damage. Most enemies are well designed and fun to fight with one hard to see exception called a stealth bot. you'll know what i mean when you get your ass handed to you by them.The polish is fairly well executed, i didn't really notice many issues throughout the game, just a few nitpicks but none of them are of note.the movement is quite standard and plays a lot like half life 2 but in vr. air strafe B-hops included! one thing i did notice though is that conveyors are slightly janky and tend to completely ♥♥♥♥ your movement up if they aren't going perfectly straight (like going up at a 45° angle or bending 90°). Your teleport however always works so you can rely on it if you manage to get yourself stuck like I have several times.The music is absolutely wonderful and its available on most streaming services, including some of the more obscure ones like TiDAL which I can always appreciate. Not everyone uses spotify (like the entire hi-fi community) and most companies dont seem to realize this when publishing their OST's.all in all i'd say its definitely worth the money and this will 100% keep me entertained for the next 20-30 hours or so as i strive to 100% this ♥♥♥♥♥.Played on Index w/ ASUS 3060 OC, Ryzen 7 3700x @~4.2ghz, 32gb ram, on maximum graphics. No real fps drops ever noticed, smooth all the way.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: What if I told you that this game is one of the best VR games? It really is! The gunplay is extremely fun, the game looks great with a stylish cartoony look with some of the most beautiful scenery in a VR game! Vertigo 2 improves on everything from the first game and is quite challenging and the campaign is pretty lengthy (took me Approx. 10 hours to complete). Plus, there is an upcoming update that gives access to a really neat in-VR level editor which is (as of now) is currently in beta! I have not yet seen something like this in VR! You seriously get a bang for your buck with this game!Okay, now keep all of that in mind. What if I also told you that this game was made by a solo developer? And yet, I do not lie. This game was seriously made by one individual. ONE PERSON made this and yet we have AAA studios struggling to even make a VR game that is even close to how polished this game is. This really gives a WTF?! moment lol.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: I have played everything that VR currently has to offer, and I mean, EVERYTHING. The itch.io games, the praydog and luke ross mods, the FLAT2VR ported games, the dolphin VR emulated games, every steamVR game, every PSVR2 game, nearly each and every quest game, and nothing, i mean NOTHING comes close to what I experienced playing this game. It takes everything else by the balls and goes "this is how its done". It has numerous endings, decisions that change the outcome of the game and how it plays out, easter eggs, spectacles, weapons, characters, the list goes on and on. New game + doesn't hurt either. I can not put into words how much I recommend experiencing this game blind, along with playing Vertigo Remastered prior if you get the chance. 11/10 You knocked it out the park.

_childDocuments_.review: Vertigo 2 is an action Sci-FI FPS mixed with minimal puzzles, exploration and a lot of hilarious humor.The game resumes the story after the already amazing VERTIGO (Remastered version strongly recommended).You are trapped in a different dimension an trying to go back home escaping from some Sci-Fi captors, there are some other interdimensional characters searching for you and some arcane artifacts. This gives you the premise for a great Half-LIke Action FPS in Virtual Reality that will blow your mind, several times, get ready !!Vertigo 2 is an absolute GEM for VR gaming and should be played entirely, and probably replay it with the added features and mutators.Also I have to say this game should be, and has my vote for being the VR GAME of the YEAR. I freaking love it hehehIt plays great, has great humor, great action parts, several smart and hilarious plot twists, great bosses and it looks incredible in VR. Specially on some specific crazy parts that I was absolutely "wooooow!!" for a millionth time in VR :)Here is some basic gameplay with a lot of pew pew : 9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Reviewed using the Index headset and VIVE pro (2.0) wands.Love the references to Halflife and other references in the game.  The action is nice.  Pistols are varied, most weapons are upgradeable with very rare printers for modification parts.  Ammo is "automatically produced" so you don't have to find and pick up ammo throughout the game.The cons:The later levels start getting punishing for no reason at all and harder to navigate rather than the streamlined and linear approach the game takes in the beginning.Some weapons require "both hands" to be attached in order to aim which is a ridiculous concept in VR that I really wish no game had ever started doing.  If I needed both hands to aim, I would do it in real life, not in the game where now I can't actually steady my aim because I can't touch my hands together and I'm not putting my plastic "gun" sleeve on just for the times I use a shotgun or need to snipe.Trying to grab the machine gun in the ATOL is almost impossible while it's movingThere seems to be no way to speed up ammo production and the better the weapon, the more you want to use it, the slower the regeneration is for the ammo so the more you CANNOT use it.Boats and other methods of automated transit are seriously flawed, like to bounce around when they hit loading areas, etc.Turning locomotion off (which is specifically using blink) is required in some areas, but it is also fundamentally flawed since more than once I found myself being "reset" into a wall or on top of nothing in the sky.  Don't try swimming without locomotion, that's even worse.The aiming angle of the shotgun is far different than the rest of the guns and really "off" in terms of the angle.I only made it about halfway (ish) through the game before I started seeing cut and paste areas like with the centaur camps.Overall:  I loved the game at first, but the longer you play it the more you're kinda ready for it to be over.  It's a great game that over plays its uniqueness and makes you end up  getting frustrated with some of its quirks like the voice acting that sounds like a couple kids from drama class in high school and the cutscenes that you can't understand at all.I'm clicking recommend, but if there was a neutral button I'd pick that.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: THIS is VR's Half Life, a fun shooter/puzzler with great humor and plot. The weapons are satisfying and fun to use, the secrets are well hidden but not impossible to find without a guide, and it's fun enough to justify replay after replay. This game was made by one guy and its better than whole studios in some cases. It's a love letter to people who's been in VR since 2016 and a great welcome to those new. If you haven't gotten this game and you have a headset what are you waiting for??? I promise you won't regret it!
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Vertigo was an amazing experience from the opening moments to the last moments. Weapons feel good to use, enemy variety expands over every chapter. Levels never feel boring. Levels feel huge and super fun to traverse through. One moment in the game you get to battle in this on going war, and at the beginning you get to choose which side you want to be on.  Anyways yeah, so which ever side you pick will depict which weapons you get and which characters you fight. This game is something that you will keep wanting more from after the end credits role. And I think it deserves to be in everyone's steam library.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Literally the best VR game I've played.An absolute joy from start to finish, and so full of creativity it makes every other game look empty in comparison, seriously it feels like every inch of this game had so much passion and creative ideas put into it. The characters and level designs are off the wall and i was constantly being left stunned by the kinds of locations and creatures around every corner. It's like the game gets better and better the deeper you get into it, the levels get more wild and the gameplay gets more chaotic. The final boss had me grinning from ear to ear.The VR mechanics and controls are the best ive seen in any VR game to date, everything feels excellent. The gunplay is spot on and the movement/interaction is so smooth and clean. Performance is excellent too, which is normally such a let down for most other VR games. This game looks VERY pretty, and a lot of care and attention was obviously put in to keeping the environments clean and deliberate, not full of clutter and turning it into a laggy mess. I really can't believe how polished and well put together everything in here is for an indie game, especially one made by essentially one person (Zach you're a master of your craft).People call this the "indie half life" and that's a pretty spot-on description. Though Vertigo 2 utterly surpassed it in creativity, soul, and pure spectacle.Buy this game, play the whole thing. It's one of (if not the) best VR experience on offer right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Vertigo 2 so far has been been bigger and better than Vertigo Remastered, which is high praise.  Every VR game should strive to be as good as Vertigo 2.  Its a smooth experience and the weapons feel great.  I won't go as far to say it feels AAA but its a blast to play.  Looking forward to playing the rest of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: A seriously impressive amount of imagination, variety and content packed into this VR shooter. I think the closest comparison is Half-Life 2 due how to this game throws so many different/new things at you in basically every chapter. The first 2-3 hours start off a little slow and are about on par with the previous game (Vertigo Remastered), but from there the game just ramps up in set pieces and craziness. Then, you throw in the post-game content like different playable characters, workshop level editor, NG+, etc. Definitely one of the greatest VR games to date and an incredible/monumental achievement by a mostly solo indie developer.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty amazing story and narrative for VR, really sucked me in and got me hooked at first. My only complaint was the combat is really off in some ways, like everything is made out of rubber including your hands, but if that frustrates you like it did me there is the option to turn down the combat difficulty so it's whatever. Seems like a lot of replay ability too, with NG+, new characters to play as, and alternate endings.Oh I also hated that you are forced to use the teleport function in order to get past certain areas in the game. It's fine but why not just have a bigger jump so you don't have to use it? I also hated how one of the main actors seemed to have a bad microphone but also very minor and I got used to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Must-buy.This is what I wanted Half-Life Alyx to feel like. This has so much charm and good gameplay.The world is cool and I love all the interesting character designs.Also love a game that has super satisfying reloads for guns. Every time I popped a canister into my shotgun I felt the happy chemicals in muh brain.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: A piece of art. If you haven't bought this, buy it. Has some jank as it was made by 1 guy over like 5 years using all the Unity assets he could. But the heart and soul put into it is so worth the experience. My play time is how long it took me to beat it on Hard mode. _childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing it has so much passion a polish put into it with well hidden weapon upgrade stations, lots of unique enemy types, memorable locations, a good story, secret weapons, the graphics are good in my opinion, good characters, challenging bosses and the puzzles can be a bit difficult but that's what puzzles a for.I also love the references to half, portal, some other vr games and vertigo remastered.10/10 go in blind and don't spoil the game
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: like a 7.5-8.5/10The game mechanics themself are really fun: the guns are all really cool, the enemies all have cool designs, the story is (so far) pretty good, and it can be really funny at times. However, there are some problems: the story is intriguing at the start, but once you get to the tree chapter, it kinda gets boring. I’m in the water monster chapter right now so hopefully it gets better again. The bosses are so bad. Their attacks are so annoying to dodge, and deal way to much damage. It makes you ask ‘how did that hit me?’ Instead of ‘why did I get hit by that?’ Also sometimes you suddenly meet a flood of enemies at once and can barely do anything. I’d say you should get it, but like, wait for it to go on sale. Then you’ll get your money’s worth. Still, one of the best story based tv games I’ve played.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Vertigo 2 has got to be my favourite vr game. Its unique game play and story had me captivated from the moment i started the game. The Easter eggs are hilarious, creepy and cool, they make you feel rewarded for exploring. One thing i give top props for is the way they make the secret weapons not feel like some random thing you found in a bin, but rather a whole optional area that has its own content that would more often than not be skipped over. The weapons are fun to use and not unbalanced, i still used the starting pistol all the way through to the final boss. The game offers a strong challenge for the veteran vr players, yet an inviting story to peek the interests of most gamers. I without hesitation give this game a 10/10, as there is nothing wrong with this game, cant wait for a 3rd instalment/ a new game from these developers. Love your work, keep it up.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Does it dethrone Alyx as the best VR game ever made? Maybe, if it doesn't it comes VERY close. Playing the first one and second side-by-side is like a demonstration in what VR game developers have learned in 6 years. Everything is taken into account when it comes to mechanics and worldbuilding. There are still some technical issues. Had a few glitches that were annoying but resolved quickly. Seems to be some issues with controller rebindings. One part (the boat) that tanked my performance no matter what I did. Things that will hopefully be fixed with updates.I was already planning my second playthrough before I beat it. Then when I did it unlocked New Game+.Vertigo 2 should be a household name in VR as long as VR exists. Anyone making AAA (or any) VR games, take note. This is how you make a good VR game.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: this is one of the games of all times. 10/10more finished/polished than most AAA VR games on launch, gameplay never gets boring, very good voice acting and some of the best gameplay/gunplay mechanics. very refreshing from the norm, and always keeps you on your toes. only vr story game that properly rewards you for exploring off the set path for the story, and the combat is fun, challenging, but not too hard. very few bugs, mostly visual but nothing game breaking.if you are dwelling on buying this game, just do yourself a favor and buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: I strongly believe the first Vertigo is one of the greatest VR games ever created. This game, however, is terrible. They tried to do far too much. I couldn't even keep playing it after the first 30 minutes. I couldn't figure out how to kill the creatures attacking me. If I have to put that much thought into a game it's not fun and definitely not worth playing. I wanted to love this game but I can't because It's awful. I may give it another shot, but for now, there are way better games out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Vertigo 2 is an amazing game in it's own. The closest you get to a Half-Life style one, without actually ripping it off. There is so much creativity in here... Like, that it uses your steam profile image in some areas. :D Comedy is gold too and then... there is the recent update which adds new player characters. And those essentially feel like a new game. And a map editor inside VR? What is going on? And most of it is done by a single person?One of the greatest achievements I've seen so far and worth every penny if not more!
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Games like these are the reason I fell in love with VR in the first place. Thank you Devs for this amazing experience that will surely go into the VR Hall-of-Fame.This is not a tech-demo, not a proof-of-concept nor a hastly put together generic VR shooter that relies solely on gun controls to be a good game. This is a real adventure, made with care and love by the Devs.If you want an experience at the same level of Half-Life:Alyx, grab this.What it lacks in technical polish and some minor performance issues, it makes up in all other aspects. Looking forward to a sequel or any extra content the Devs might put out!
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

Finished the game and enjoyed every second of it. Beautiful Visuals even on older Hardware and majestic Sound-Design. Haven't had this much fun at a game in a hot while. Worth every Cent.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: I only recently played Vertigo: Remastered and I absolutely loved it. Far more than I expected to. Such an underrated game. So I was very much looking forward to Vertigo 2.It is crazy to me how much this game exceeded my expectations and is easily one of my favourite VR games. The weapons, enemy variety, exploration, characters, secrets, references, boss battles, music, the story and lore. Everything for the sequel was drastically improved. Absolutely blood fantastic!I really hope we see more of Vertigo in the future. I'd be all over that for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m honestly speechless.For starters this shouldn’t be someone's first VR experience. But it definitely should be experienced eventually. Half-Life: Alyx spoiled me as my first real VR experience because most VR games that were “Acclaimed and considered the standard for VR” were ultimately destroyed when HL Alyx’s insane polish hit the scene and raised the bar even higher.This game . It may even exceed it in some areas. The first game proved more non-valve half-like games in VR can work. This game takes everything good about the first and cranks it up to 100. I’m not exaggeratingThis game is constantly throwing new, fun and exciting things at you. Every chapter and set piece feels unique and memorable. There’s tons of weapons to play with and tons of secrets scattered throughout the game. They really know when to balance comedy and horror appropriately. It’s just so, so good. I can gush on and on about everything I liked about this game but I think it’s best you just go in blind and have as much fun as I have.For a game on this big of a scale designed entirely by one person is absolutely insane. You deserve the highest praise.

_childDocuments_.review: (NO STORY SPECIFICS REVIEW)(this review doesn't mention the bottomless update - which added an entire level editor, modifiers and different characters to chose from)This is a MUST play PCVR title that's oozing with style.# storyThe story is great and follows on from Vertigo Remastered. It also features two branching paths that you can chose from, and you're free to load from an earlier save once you're done to check them both out.# visualsThis game's environments are beautiful and unique - you find yourself somewhere completely new before you get comfortable with your surroundings.# weaponsThis game's weapons feel *designed* for VR. A lot of games have you use real-world guns that are 'ported' over from reality - Vertigo's guns feel designed around your controllers. Love the designs and feel.Swinging melee weapons around felt a little sluggish at first. Took some getting used to, but you'll be shooting for 97% of the game anyway.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: The pinnacle of VR gaming. Unironically one of the greatest VR games made.Guns could use a bit more solid aiming, but in terms of music, gameplay, maps, voice acting, it's all so wonderful, and for 9 hours of content, content you can replay for 2 endings and 2 choices and different gameplay, I'll sing the praises all day and night.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: First Playthrough:This has instantly become my favourite game. Just finished my first playthrough and I cant help myself but want to jump straight back in. From a gameplay perspective everything just feels *right*. Weapons are all solid, fun to use and look incredible, enemies each have incredible design and killing them feels so satisfying. Boss fights are all unique and have heart racing moments. The story is so good, it's rare I play a game with a story and actually feel like i'm making actual world-altering decisions but everything in this game feels connected and the story had me hooked from the opening cutscene. Some moments in this game are actually jaw dropping-ly beautiful, I found myself taking moments just too look around at where I was and take it in. Sometimes I find it hard to truly imagine what a level *is* when playing games, in some games levels are just a web of interconnected hallways that make no sense but this game has a real sense of reality that really helps keep the player grounded and the sense of scale amplifies that. Going into my second playthrough soon, hope to find the rest of the secret weapons I missed!A game hasn't made me feel genuine excitement and happiness for a while but this really captured that and the fact it was developed by Zulubo alone has genuinely inspired me too. 10/10 will play many times in the future.36 Hours:This game still holds up as easily my favourite VR game. Everything I said above still holds true and the more I play the more I seem to enjoy it. As of the time of writing this there has been some major updates to the game, one that adds 3 whole new ways to play the main campaign, one turning it into essentially a VR boomer shooter! The love and care that is put into this game is immense and it really shines through. The beta sandbox mode is intuitive and fun and the community already has made some incredible stuff to keep me playing and I've loved my albeit quite little time messing with the sandbox tools. With the introduction of the sequel feature in sandbox there is also mini campaigns being build by the community which is just unheard of in the VR space right now and im really excited to see where it goes especially with the features this game provides. With PSVR 2 release on the horizon I'd imagine more people will be checking out the reviews of Steam before purchasing and if you're someone looking into this game at all I'd take the plunge. The Vertigo Universe feels lively and fun, the gameplay is fluid and intuitive and the design is nothing short of beautiful. Play Vertigo 2.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Hands down best VR game I played so far. Easily outshines Alyx or other titles. It's quirky, funny, challenging, and at times breathtaking. All mechanics work flawlessly. The atmosphere is amazing. The levels are really different and the scenery is varied (so many games get this wrong, this is one of the only VR games I played with nice level design). There is a nice variety of weapons. You can actually use your second hand with physical interaction to help aim with the grenade launcher. I can't wait to try community made content with the new update.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very well put-together game. Aside from fairly minor glitches, nothing caused me any problems. The enemies have good variety so encounters do not feel static as you progress. The weapons feel VERY solid. (I'm a big fan of the revolver) The fact that you can gib enemies or cause visible damage to their extremities adds a lot of flavour to how powerful each weapon in your arsenal feels. I have not yet had a chance to experiment with the secret weapons aside from one (and I was horrible at aiming it) but it still added variety and fun to my playthrough. I'm definitely going to be giving ng+ a shot. If you like vr games (and don't get too motion sick) I would absolutely recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: The game is alright, it's decent to playthrough but I think it's a lot harder than the last game. Boss fights are completely frustrating, you are given no hints as to what you need to do to the boss, given no cover and you get absolutely pummelled. It consists of dying repeatedly a dozen times and then quitting the game and searching for a tutorial, for every boss. This is even the case with a lot of scenarios in the game, where it's just not clear what exactly you are supposed to do in order to successfully proceed, you just end up dying repeatedly. I found the story to be too silly to really get into and I struggled to even follow what was going on in the actual story, some of the characters I can't even understand what they are saying, like Nani. The environments in some of the later sections of the game are very nice and interesting though. Guns are well enough but I found the larger weapons to be too finicky and ended up mainly using the revolver. I'd say it's worth playing just because of the lack of proper full campaign style games on VR, and most of the scenes in this game are pretty nice in VR too.

_childDocuments_.review: Vertigo 2 is an incredibly fun and engaging experience that touches on so many capabilities of current gen VR. V2 is truly enjoyable has been a wild ride. The challenge has definitely been ramped up since the first game so be prepared to use your noggin, your eyes, and your evasive maneuvers.

_childDocuments_.review: So much has been said about this game - but not by me! Yet. I can't believe I never bothered to start up this game after buying it. The guns are really fun and the loop of constantly switching weapons while healing is awesome. In the videos I didn't care too much for the cartoony visuals, but they look really great in VR. There's lots of detail on the guns and there are some breathtaking environmental compositions. Don't sleep on this one!

_childDocuments_.review: Not a AAA VR game, but damn is it close.At its core, it's another FPS with sci-fi background story, multiverse shenanigans and so on. But it's so well executed that it feels fresh again.It's a love letter to Portal and Half-Life,  with several influences mixed in including High on Life, Outer Wilds, Boneworks. The theme of the game varies wildly during gameplay, like Super Mario Galaxy would, going from gory zombie-escape thing to Banjo-Kazooie child friendly battles.It's varied, it's fun, it has a teensy tiny bit of jank left, but come on.In 2023, it's an absolute must-get if you want to get some really fun use of your VR headset again.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: First game was great! Second game has so many things that are annoying. Can't dual wield weapons anymore. Weapon accuracy is garbage. Constant crouching while trying to turn around... more than half of the range of my right thumbstick makes me crouch... this, coupled with the manual reloading change means that combat isn't difficult, it's just frustrating. I have looked up the comments and seen that others have had the crouching issue... which is unique to Seated Mode players.  It makes boss fights impossibly difficult; and I have the game set to Story difficulty! There are other game design elements that feel out of place. It makes me sad, as I really enjoyed the first game very much, but find that I am getting so frustrated by the gameplay flaws that I cannot finish the story of this sequel. This game needs more than just a remastering... it took everything that was great about the first game and threw it out the window.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute masterpiece and the best vr game of all time.
