_childDocuments_.review: This game has been so much fun! Laughter, angry, even a little sadness i've felt playing through this campaign I love all the extra dialogue in this one vs the original. The guns tho not real yes, are actually really fun to use and find myself using all of them for different scenarios not just sticking to one favorite, its a great balance! The story is really funny and interesting at the same time. I knew i would like this game but i didn't know id enjoy it this much! There is even a part where choice affects story outcome a little making me ready to replay when i finally beat it. i read the campaign is about 10 hours long i'm close to that and 2/3 of the way through and i know i missed some stuff (secrets! i love secrets!!) so i'm sure it'll take me longer than 10 hours and probably will for you too (if you aren't an expert that likes to rush their games) Its not a very difficult game, but i will say i've had some frustrating fights with several deaths making that victory all the sweeter. So far id give this game 9/10 and say its a game type ive been waiting for quite some time now and so glad i found it!! I love it thank you so much for making it and letting us play it!!
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best VR games I've played. Really good weapon handling, beautiful art design, funny characters and writing, a good story, and it's super well polished (only major bug I encountered was an issue interacting with buttons, but that can be solved by making the window fullscreen, so do that)A little short (my playthrough came in at a little under 9 hours) but there is a new game+ with some reasons to replay such as differing story choices and finding secrets (there's apparently 6 secret weapons and I found 2, so can replay to find more)Overall I definitely recommend to all VR gamers, and if you loved the first game you will not be dissapointed. Overall just a massive improvement compared to the (already great) orignal.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Everything a Shooter - VR or not - can do right, Vertigo 2 does right.Interesting and satisfying gunplay with a variety of weapons to choose from? Check.Singleplayer Campaign that does not feel short but also does not overstay its welcome? Check.Constantly changing up the gameplay with new settings, new enemies, slower moments as well as hectic fights? Check!Its also a very good example of what a VR shooter can be, if it wants its selling point to be more than "If you point your hand in real life, you also point your gun in game!". This game does its best to be fair, but combat speed is practically on par with Flatscreen shooters - compare to Alyx, which for all its perfection has a much slower combat pace compared to HL2. Did i mention it has a New Game + mode and unlockable secret weapons and characters (the latter of which change up the gameplay entirely)?If you have a VR headset and even a passing interest in FPS games, there is very little that should stop you from playing this gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Such a great game! Definitely not as fear inducing as Half-Life: Alyx. Only some rare areas are slightly emotionally uncomfortable (if you get finger gun you'll know what I mean), but overall the game is intentionally goofy and fun. It's surprisingly well optimized and looks really great on Meta Quest 2. The story is absurd in the best way possible, characters are likable and well voiced. Kudos to the developer who accomplished this (honestly no idea how).
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: I started playing (Quest 2 - wireless with Virtual Desktop) with a full battery and only stopped when the battery was empty. I haven't encountered a single hiccup, bug or crash. The weapons and shooting mechanics are great, the physics are good, and the writing made me laugh (in a good way). The environments are imaginative and full of surprises and scratch any exploring itch you may have. The in-game interfaces are cleverly designed and I love the fact that you can switch the position of the ammo from the typical (and height adjustable) belt, to your back(pack) so the game can be played perfectly while you're seated - something that most developers don't think about. And, of course, the graphics are very good, showing many and interesting details and I often caught myself just looking around, instead of continuing with the game and the story. Also excellent voice acting and alien sounds. A must have, if you're into VR, and especially if you think there are not enough quality, story-based, single-player campaigns in your library. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, and I did for the most part, but the decision to force you to use teleportation instead of having a free move sprinting option makes the boss fights atrociously annoying/frustrating. And yes, I've played through most of the game, but I'm at the last boss (I think), and even on easy I will probably never be able to finish the game due to this extremely odd design decision.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: So far, this is the best VR game I've ever played....even better than HL:Alyx. Vertigo 2 is what I would call a true AAA VR game because it feels like there is just more going on in the game than any other VR title. The world feels alive, responsive and eventful with much to look at, the story lore is easy to get into and understand and there is actually quite a bit of enemies and weapons to be found. I've played Vertigo Remastered and this is a huge improvement, making it one of the few sequels I've ever experienced that actually lives up to the hype and delivers. Weapon handling is straightforward and works well and the A.I. actually can put up a good fight and make for some epic battles. I haven't had any performance or bug issues with the game, so that's a huge plus. The chapters are long enough and provide quite a bit of game play compared to other games while the voice acting is good and dialogue/events in the game can be very funny. Vertigo 2 is the VR game that you want to get if you're looking for something that has more content like tradition pancake games and it's actually a shame that it took this long for something of this caliber to be released in VR. It proves that VR  games can have bigger scope and more content and hopefully will inspire developers to create similar experiences in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: The best VR story game. No joke. This well surpasses Half Life Alyx and Boneworks in gameplay, story, difficulty, and generally fun. As with the first game, and even more so now, it never got stale, every level made me think: 'wow, that was fun!!' Even after playing, I will totally replay to get all the secret guns / alternate ending(?).. All VR devs please take note :)
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: ABSOLUTE MINDBLOWING!A couple years ago I played the first Vertigo and thought to myself that the game was just a short demo that someone half-assed put out for money. Then as I dove deeper into the story I fell in love. It gave me the same nostalgia as playing Half Life 2 for the first time. I beat the game pretty fast and enjoyed all the quirkyness of the original style and put the ol' Oculus down for good until I heard a rumor. A wisp through the grapevine that hinted at the development of Vertigo 2. This was the perfect time for me to try it out and see if it could live up to my expectations that I set for a single developer. When I say that my mind was blown, I mean it. The art style and optimization made it feel seamless and the arcade style of weapons felt great! Every corner I rounded had me thinking that the game was going to end as the gameplay felt too good to be true. Oh! I can't forget the great voice acting either! Each and every single one of the voice actors in the game made me either chuckle from their comedic jokes or sink my heart with the seriousness in their voice. I'm glad I got to experience this and hope others can as well. This game hands down better win ALL the awards coming towards it and I wish Mr. Brown the best of luck on the next one!
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game. The old get through a level and get to the boss works very well here.  I thought I was done with these type of games but it works so well in VR.. Highly recommend. There is also a demo to try it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Great VR gameplay even though you don't have any legs. I love the visual style and storytelling as well. there are a few bugs here and there and certain areas aren't as polished as others, but that is really just due to this being made by a single person. Imo the gameplay was more enjoyable than HL:A even though HL:A is my favorite game.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: I am not sure where the praise for this game is coming from. The top review saying this is equivalent to Half Life: Alyx or Boneworks is a perfect embodiment of pure delusion. This games gun handling sucks. Everywhere I aim, my character acts like the guns are 100 pounds and there is what can only be described as an "input delay" in VR as my character swings his arms 2 seconds later to ACTUALLY match where I am aiming. The gun models and reloading are pretty cool, I'll give it that. The game is very very easy, and the combat is not engaging at all. I know it was made by one guy and by no means am I attempting to down talk his work here, but the blind praise in these reviews is extremely misleading. If you think this is ANYTHING like Boneworks or Half Life: Alyx you are probably referring to the extremely obvious HL:A inspired healing stations, or the extremely slow lackluster movement. Boneworks because.... guns? Not sure. For VR veterans, I would not recommend this game to you. If you're new to VR, maybe. Just know, there are so many better games to play, and especially for 30$?? Just go buy Boneworks.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Works on Reverb G2.Vertigo 2 is much bigger and better than the original. It stands out among other story-driven VR shooters thanks to intense pacing, creative designs and huge variety of everything.The game never gets old during it's 10+ hours campaign by constantly switching locations and adding new weapons and enemies, including a lot of bosses. Core gameplay gravitates towards old-school shooter, but it has a place for surprisingly well made turret section, simple machinery usage and many exploration/story bits. Sadly, there is also some pretty boring corridor shooting here and there, but it never lasts for too long.Gunplay is physical and responsive, weapons are creative and fun to use. Most enemies have satisfying damage indications and death animations. AI of humanoids is decent: they are a bit blind to nearby missed shots and friendly deaths, but at least they can take cover and never get stuck in the terrain.Visuals look really sharp and distinct, while performing reasonably well. There is some infrequent screen stuttering, but it seems that was introduced in one of the latest patches and is not linked to overall performance.Physics is also quite good, with only minor item interaction jank.Overall, Vertigo 2 is one of the best story-driven VR shooters and a breath of fresh air in terms of quality and polish after disappointing Saints & Sinners 2 and Hubris
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is a VERY fun, and surprisingly VERY long game. Of course there are plenty of difficulty levels to turn it down to if wanted, and definitely didnt let that spoil my experience playing.Word of warning though, the game has no chill in terms of movement via vehicle (not that its a bad thing) so make sure you strap yourself in tight for a bumpy ride!

_childDocuments_.review: ********* VOTE VERTIGO 2 FOR VR GAME OF THE YEAR!!! *********Don't pass this up!     Once again I'm blown away. Vertigo 2 is just as well designed and fun to play as the first but better in every way imaginable! Like the first game this one does an AMAZING job at being a VR shooter! Not just a shooter where you can move your hands around.  You can tell time was taken to really think about all the many ways you can interact with your hands and with the world around you.      Each weapon is unique to the others in terms of how and what it shoots (if it shoots) and how you operate it. So much more here than just reloading different magazines. In the game world(s) there are so many different mechanics and interactions. Levers, switches, knobs and dials, buttons, swipes, grabs, climbs and all sorts of things.     The levels and worlds are well designed and all different and interesting in their own ways just like the weapons. And the enemies are no different. Each enemy has its own strengths and weaknesses and the game does a great job of mixing things up. Just as you get used to an enemy type and its mechanics, BOOM, new enemies you've never seen before or even one of the many fun boss fights against all sorts of crazy bad guys!     But levels and enemies mean nothing without a good story, right? Well this game has it. I was always so excited to hop in and see how far i can get into it with each time i played. The whole story from the first is still going on. (don't worry though you don't NEED to play it before enjoying the second, however it will give you tons of insight into whats going on, who's who, and some of the references to the older game in this one) It picks up right were the first left off. however there's now a little twist in that some new factions are forming and [[[SPOILER ALERT]]] you may have to choose some sides.     I really could talk about these games and how much I like them and how well they are put together for hours, but to make a long review short I'll just say this:  If you've played the first Vertigo game you know everything I'm talking about. You can tell this game was made with love in every line of code. the characters, the story, the guns, its all so good! This is that x10! So many new locations and levels, way more weapons than the first, so many more new enemies (and friends), all the great mechanics and interactions, and tons of references to other great games (VR and not). Its hands down my FAVORITE VR game series and I can't wait to see what else this developer can cook up!

_childDocuments_.review: It's incredible that a game developed solely by one person is better than many action-adventures created by full teams, VR or otherwise. The amount of variety on display with regards to characters, weapons, enemies, environments, and level scenarios is simply remarkable. Not to be hyperbolic, but at times this game felt like I was playing something old school--in the sense that it delivers a true adventure through pure gameplay. There is conventional storytelling, however, and it's actually solid; a lot of the characters have nice voice acting, too. Being the ambitious, impressive work of a solo dev, I think there's inherent leeway to overlook some flaws. This game is quite polished, all things considered. Occasionally the enemies can feel too spongy, and encounters wavy, but much of that drag is mitigated by knowing your arsenal. Playing on Index, I never got the hang of keeping my thumb off the trackpad, which led to sweaty situations where instead of continuing to fire my weapon, I accidentally put away my weapon. Also, the vignette effect when at low health made certain parts very hard to see. But that's probably the definition of a skill issue. Now to wait 5-7 years for the next game.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow.  I just finished the game after 20 hours, and it was enjoyable all the way through.I ran it on an RTX 2060 and I didn't think the graphics were lacking.  My HMD is a Quest 2 and I played it entirely over AirLink with no issues noted stemming from using WiFi instead of a cord.I wouldn't say the game is perfect with some jank here and there, which I would expect from a VR game.  Considering I'm not actually holding anything other than a controller, pretending I'm grabbing and eating a healing fungus isn't going to be perfect.I love the exploratory aspects of going through an abandoned facility, and this had that while also providing a reasonable amount of difficulty with mobs and bosses.I would definitely recommend this to other VR players (and I have), and I am looking forward to playing through the NG+ (which I didn't realize there would be) and also playing through Vertigo Remastered.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really understand the hype for this game, and a part of me feels that it's a combination of a desperation people have for "content", and anything that remotely resembles half-life nostalgia. If there was a neutral rating I'd give it that, but I'm leaning more towards negative simply because I'm not finding it that fun but it's enough to hold my attention in short bursts between chapters.It's just very bland and very drawn out. Yes, it's a lengthy game, but only because it repeats the same fights, draws out combat sequences of repeated spawned enemies of the same model, and slogs through so much walking. It's just a basic shooting game with not much else to it. The environments are not that high quality; they're conceptually weird and unique, most of the time, but texture qualities are low and techniques like pop-in are very obvious even when maxed out. The gun models are higher quality, but then you look down at your character model in contrast which is noticeably lower.The gun play is okay although some weapons have more physics tied to them than others and sometimes glitch out (like the enlightened gun). The AI is rough at times, especially when NPCs are supposed to be on your side, chapter 10 was frustrating having a group of AI follow you in a circle but constantly bump into you, get in your way, knock your physics influenced gun to the side while you're aiming, etc.Movement is somewhat annoying as the environments are sometimes very large requiring you to walk a long distance across open landscapes, but the movement speed is slow with no sprint button and no way to increase it. That means most of the time I'm clicking in the left analogue stick to teleport walk forward but waiting for the teleport's cooldown just as it's quicker, but I'm always left wanting to move faster while my hand feels strained constantly clicking.I'd describe this game as a very large meal but one that isn't very tasty, there's little substance to this game unless you're a massive fan of the humour which dips in and out, but the story is incoherent and seems to just be an excuse to move the player forward. The boss fights are somewhat frustrating often requiring trial and error attempts with checkpoints sometimes well thought out and sometimes resetting entire fights, exposing you to the awful loading tip one-liners that are a mix between edgy and cringe-inducing.Again, if I could I would rate this neutrally, and overall I would temper your expectations unless you're for something to really pass the time, or you're looking for something a little weirder with less polish. This game tries to be many things, a story-driven game, a shooter, has upgrades, light-hearted humour, horror, but in trying to do so much it ends up being a jack of all trades with a lot of content but none of it particularly strong.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: one of the best VR games in recent memory. Vertigo 2 is probably the closest a developer has gotten to the sheer quality and scope of Half life Alyx which means to say that this game is no joke. The size of the game and wealth of content for a singleplayer VR experience is not to be understated and the amount of improvements it makes over the original vertigo is incredible.A larger world, a greater emphasis on story and characters, unique biomes and exploration with lots of secrets, a deeper and more engaging combat system with many cool and original weapons. cool and interesting enemy designs and bosses, vertigo 2 pushes boundaries much in the same way half life alyx did and in some ways it surpasses valves titular VR title.i cannot recommend the vertigo series (especially vertigo 2) enough for fans of VR, it is an incredibly good deal for the money and the games are incredible technical achievements for such a small team of developers.

_childDocuments_.review: Vertigo 2 is easily 2023's VR Game of The Year. The fact that it didn't win that award isn't surprising but it is disappointing.The fact that 1 man can make a better VR game than 95% of large VR studios is crazy. Then again this guy did contract work at Valve, he knows his stuff.If you're looking for a fantastic mostly linear, story driven singleplayer game, a half-like, or just another good VR game to play, do yourself a favor and play this game.Tons of weapons, branching story paths for slightly different playthroughs, lots of enemy types, tons of bosses, and lots of level diversity. New mechanics, weapons, set pieces, and other cool "things" you get to do (I don't want to spoil these moments for you) happen quite often and the game doesn't let you play for too long without introducing something new.But everything is just super polished. I ended up playing with the metal door on the healing station for like 10 minutes just because it was so satisfying to open and close. I don't know why it was, but it was.game good buy it

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, i highly suggest playing vertigo remastered before 2.aside from alyx, i have never seen a (relatively) cohesive story told in this way in a vr game before, and from about a quarter of the way through, i realized this game is my favorite single-player campaign ever.THE STORY/CAMPAIGNSure, boneworks has a great campaign, and a good story (albeit hidden deeply) However, vertigo takes the idea of a vr story, and expands upon it greatly, characters, factions with different motives, and non enemy npcs that give the game life.THE ENVIRONMENTSthis game looks stunning. where half-life Alyx put you into a beautiful yet dystopian city 17, it looked FANTASTIC, however only about when the game ends, is where we start to see a change in enviroment.Vertigo 2  starts in the halls of Planck industries' own QR-7 but after the first hour, you are suddenly shooting down airships, fighting your way through cave systems, fighting in a battlefield towards a castle, and so much more i don't want to spoil.  THE WEAPONSMany other vr games have tactical weaponry, and that is far from a bad thing.however, vertigo 2, while still functionally similar to your standard rifles and handguns, they look and feel so greatfully different. and there are also secret weapons that you can find hidden through the game. if you have a keen eye, you may also find weapon upgrade cases that function similar to the drones in doom 2016-eternal.i have never liked a vr game to THIS extent since boneworks, if you believe that anything i mentioned sounds interesting, GET THE DAMN GAME. you are in for one hell of a journey.EDIT:After the update this game went from amazing to straight up the BEST VR GAME. Not only did the gigantic campaign receive a few changes, but now you have 3 more unique characters to play as, each having their own fun spin on the way the game is played, as well as a bucket-load of mutators that make the game harder, easier or stranger depending on which ones you choose. as well as a fully fleshed out level editor with most of vertigo 2's props where you can make any level that you can think of. i think it is an absolute crime that this game is fairly unknown as of now, but hopefully many more people get to play this masterpiece when it comes out for PSVR 2 in the future, as Zach put so much effort and care into this game. in conclusion...BUY THE DAMN GAME NOW.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Vertigo 2 is an adventure in every sense of the word. _childDocuments_.review: I can not stress this enough.This game felt better then my first time ever playing Boneworks, a game I looked forward to playing for almost 4 years.This game felt better then Half-Life: Alyx.This game makes Bonelab feel like a tech demo.This game is well optimized.This game has a lot of content.This game has several weapons, endings, interesting character, and TONS of lore for you nerds that are into that.If you wanted a Sci-Fi story game that feels heavily Half-Life inspired, play this game.If you like VR at all even, just.. play this game.Took me 8.8 hours to complete.Suffered SteamVR errors a couple times, or the game itself crashing, but it was very minimal and did not take away from the game by any means.I never once had an FPS drop the entire time I played, it was a constant 120 FPS, no problems at all.Just.. please.Try it, maybe even just the demo.VR Game Of The Year, 2023.The 4 year wait was worth it.Love you Zulubo.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a downright comedy game, but you never have time to laugh because the action is always frantic. The environments, characters, dialogue, weapons, story, enemy types, NPCs, never cease to entertain. There are dramatic moments but those are mostly in service to the humorous ridiculousness of this world.A game where I didn't mind dying over and over again to the bosses because they were so awesome I wanted to replay them anyway. Great soundtrack as well.The thing that bothered me though is the motion sickness. I wish the game's teleport worked the same as in Half Life Alyx, where the screen fades to black for a split second as you teleport from one spot to another, masking the movement between the two spots. In this game, the teleport moves you very quickly between the two spots, which very slowly made me more and more dizzy. Also the part of the game where you drive the excavator really took me out, after that I dumped the headset and layed in bed for the rest of the day. Though, when replaying the game for achievements I found I was getting more and more used to it so perhaps it's just a matter of me getting my VR-legs.I may very well nominate this game for best VR Steam Award at the end of the year!

_childDocuments_.review: Vertigo 2 starts out interesting, but slowly devolves into genuinely frustrating, infuriating, and just outright awful gameplay as it progresses. The sheer number of times I got save-locked into nearly unwinable fights is just unforgiveable. The difficulty wildly and violently flails between "I have full healing and no reason to use it" to "I have no healing and must survive on only the natural 50% regen for the entirety of a 4 part boss fight."The game is utterly saturated with combat cheap shots. See a healing item? Sure there will be melee units who can each half-health damage you instantly spawning the moment you try to get it. Everything feels remarkably cheap, and almost everything devours your health, leaving you no choice but to be either full health, or living on a prayer hoping they miss long enough for you to deal damage. Combat is nothing short of either boring, or infuriatingly painful having to eat cheap shot after cheap shot or being just outright swarmed by suicidal enemies who just face tank you.Level design is often nonsensical, leading to a lot of painful back tracking and skyrim-esc self-looping rooms. Its not always apparent where you need to go, and the pacing drags on painfully long for some levels.The Lore is the only redeeming quality of the game, and the only reason I completed it. Which is strange to say that a game that is borderline "Rick and Morty non-serious" actually has a decent sub-plot when its not being perpetually self referential or just cheesy. And yea, I do not encourage you to play Vertigo 1. I made the mistake of playing it, and it is honestly this but shorter and even more riddled with the same problems.Worse is the game has some real potential, its just buried underneath agonizingly bad combat and level design. Absolutely reeks of "we ran out of ideas, so lets just, uh, THROW EVERYTHING AT THE SAME TIME! THAT'S ENGAGING RIGHT?" Only combat utterly falls apart when you have next to no cover and no means of defending yourself outside of healing item spam. Atleast Vertigo 1 had a laser sword you could cheekily use to defend yourself from projectiles, Vertigo 2 has nothing and expects you to "Doom 2016" the game only you don't have the health, speed, or mobility to do that. So you get stuck in a corner and relying exclusively on the one most broken gun in the game, the shotgun. (It's so broken they actually have to take it away from you at the very end.)

_childDocuments_.review: I want to join the choir of good reviews prising this game as one of the best VR experiences I've ever had.The gameplay and the sense of adventure are absolute gold. Graphics are cartoon-ish yet epic and immersive. Sound design and music are incredible and everything is very well directed, drowning you deeper and deeper the more you play, into the Vertigo world.I love that every step forward puts you in a new situation with different types of challenges to discover, new enemies and new, unique locations always so interesting to explore.The use of VR is outstanding, giving you so much freedom in setting up strategies to get out of trouble: brawling, sniping, running, hiding, trapping.. 100% pure fun.I also want to remark the fact that the game doesn't force you into repetitive, uninteresting activities (unlike many other games), such as grinding or search for ammunition or health potions. No, at all times, all you do, it's something exciting, interesting, fun. Congrats!

_childDocuments_.review: You see streams of this on youtube. You see screenshots. And you think.. "Looks like just another VR game". But it's not. I know there's a lot of hyperbole out there about this game. And I wouldn't go so far as to call this 'the savior of VR'. First of all I don't think it needs a savior in terms of software, it's the hardware that is still challenging for people, both the price and the use, depending on the person and their circumstances.But this is a very good VR game.. period.The story keeps you going and the graphics looks crispier than Vertigo Remastered. The gun and gameplay is fun and expanded upon compared to the first title. There's more choice and there's more fun to be had there. Pros- Beautiful environments to explore (if not a bit empty now and then, but much less so than the first one)- Fun guns and gunplay- Some basic story choices giving players more agency in the story and adding replay value- Lots of fun characters- Adventure!!!- New Game+- Lots of interactive environments- Fun puzzles, nothing too challenging- A very special friend from the first game is back and it made me tear up- It runs great while streaming it to Discord on my 2080 super. (unlike some other VR titles)- The game is much longer than Vertigo Remastered and I'm all in for it! (About halfway into it now I think?)Cons- The first (main) pistol feels like it's tilted upwards too much, forcing me to rotate my wrist downwards too much in order to 'get the shot'. I find myself switching to other weapons often because of that which is a shame. All the other guns seem fine on my Valve Index Controllers.- Like any other VR title there is some 'jank' but nothing too weird, and not more so than other benchmark titles like Boneworks and Alyx. Don't push your hands against the window while inside a train, just a thought.- The game endsPlayed on HTC Vive Pro with Index Controllers.

_childDocuments_.review: Waited a while for this one to come out and I'm 100% glad it's finally here! If you enjoyed playing HLA, then get this game and even the first one, you will have hours of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: Such a well made game. Seeing the credits roll and reading that the music, the art and the dev was the same person really put my jaw on the floor. This is the future of VR this game if phenomenal, I have never played anything like this before. There were moments where I stopped playing and just looked at the world around me because it was so immersive. The environments felt so alive, it didn't feel like a piece of code someone had created that I was walking through, it actually felt like i was in a foreign universe, the AI interact with one another, there are fights that don't require you, there are dinosaurs versus aliens vs robots and you're just in the middle of all of it. The use of scale is so good as well. I always wondered why not more VR devs use the power of scale to their advantage. Everything works so well in VR the bosses feel fresh and not like bullet sponges unlike other VR games. Boneworks, Alyx and vertigo are the big three of VR and i think vertigo 2 is the best one. Usually when games have things like secret bosses or secret weapons I don't usually bother to replay levels and search for secrets, but this game is just such a joy to play that I have started hunting for secrets. So satisfying. The game feels so tactile, the sound design even the healing pods are such a joy to use. Even though the ar gun you get is kinda ass the reload is just so nice...So I used it as many times as I could. The guns are creative, the enemies feel fair. It all feels like a nice challenge, I didn't really get frustrated, except the boat level...that one took me a couple of tries. The story is so well delivered and really does immerse you. One of the coolest bit of this game is the ability of choice, the whole story is centred on autonomy, the robots becoming sentient the overarching theme of faith, its simply a well written story let alone a VR story, and you really do feel like you're in control. This is a linear game but there are multiple endings you can get. Finding how to get the other ending was so fun. If you've bothered to read any reviews you're already interested. This game is an easy recommendation to ANYONE. I'm just so impressed by this game, it was so fun to play. I could go on about the whole game for days, but I do not want to spoil anything. YOU NEED to play this game. You will forget how much money you spent on it. You can always make that money back. Experiences like this are rare. This game is an absolute gem. 10/10 truly an epic journey.
_childDocuments_.name: Vertigo 2

_childDocuments_.review: just got done with the game and it was glorius, it was funny, good gameplay, good humor everything combined made it an awsome experience. _childDocuments_.review: This took me about 14 hours to beat compared to about 4 for Vertigo Remastered. They're both great games, and the original 2016 Vertigo was a very good game. Like the original Vertigo, Vertigo 2 has some major difficulty spikes. There are some bosses you're going to struggle beating, so be prepared to die over and over again. You might even feel like giving up. What makes it even harder is that you're not sure if you're even hurting some of the bosses. That might be my main gripe with the game. Some other gripes: your walk speed is too slow, teleport is too slow, teleport is required too often to progress or beat a boss, the controls require that you remap the steam vr bindings to avoid some annoyances, there are windowed cut scenes, your arms are too thin, and some of the levels are uninteresting or bland to look at. Other than that, it's great.

_childDocuments_.review: This game really surprised me - I had an absolute blast playing this - much better than many VR games costing the same or more.Firstly the game is huge - really good value for money. The story is quirky and fun - but the main star is the levels - I had some truly unique experiences (not just in VR - but from any shooter) and marvelled at some of the worlds this throws you into. The weapons are varied and mostly satisfying, and have lots of upgrade options. The ammo system is excellent, encouraging you to hide out from time to time while your ammo replenishes. You'll also meet some very bizarre enemies - many of which I guarantee you have never seen in a game before.There's really only a few minor grumbles - some of the early levels are a bit flat and grey, making you think you've bought an average indy game, but persevere  and you will be greatly rewarded. The teleportation is just a bit too slow for my liking (the target spot arcs away from you at a limited pace, so quick movements are tricky - but then perhaps that would have made it too easy to avoid enemies). But honestly these are minor complaints in an otherwise fantastic game.I can't recommend this enough - just brilliant.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic take on the half-life formula and a great sequel. Gameplay is on point, works great on a Quest 2. _childDocuments_.review: This is a must-play made-for-VR game; engaging and diverse environments; AAA-standard game play. And as many others have noted, its an extraordinary accomplishment from a small (one-person?) indie development team. It deserves the support of every VR-gamer.

_childDocuments_.review: Jumping in I really didn't expect much from this game. I did play the demo before hand and it was really good but I really didn't get a good feel for the game play and the story. When I first started playing I wasn't really "impressed" and I say that only because I've gotten used to small devs and stuff making really great games. After I got to where the demo ended and the  started I started to realise how insane this game actually is. From the awesome action sequences to the hype music and the stunning visuals everything just worked. This game has SO much to offer. Again, Stunning visuals, amazing environments and level design. Great voice acting, A ton of different and unique enemies, Great bosses, Incredible soundtrack (I'm listening to it as I write this) A story that actually makes sense and plays out really well. Weapons feel great and a good variety of them too  Oh and the game is very well optimised too. I mean like I'd lag out every now and then if there's alot on screen but that's mostly bc of my pc being a potato. But it ran wayyy better than any other VR game I've played so far. Everything about this game is just so good. This is my favourite VR title EVER. If you are just getting into VR and you like Half-Life or just need a VR game with a long campaign then I encourage you to   Um also one more thing, while playing my game I didn't really encounter many bugs which is great there are still these three that bugs me the most and I would greatly appreciate it if they were looked at.  but yeah other than that all good!

_childDocuments_.review: This has got to be one of the best VR games ever made, I love how there are many really unique and cool guns, and theres also secret guns which are fun to find and use.The guns work amazing and feel amazing to use, truly. The campaign is very long and well made, if you take your time having some fun or have some difficulty like me, it should take around 12 or so hours just to complete the base campaign, then new game + adds some extra fun to playing through the campaign.Truly a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: Best VR Game of the year by far. This game has such a great variety of locations, it's amazing. So many great features, weapons and ideas and all that from just one man.. it's just beyond crazy to me. And those Boss Fight.. MAN THEY WERE FUN!Some critique-points - While the locations have a great variety as mentioned earlier, some are a bit long and stretch out quite a bit. Too long and too laggy on my hardware (good enough for a very fluid experience of Half Life Alyx in case someone was wondering). _childDocuments_.review: Simply Magnificent. A new game from one of the, if not the best game vr developer out thereA roughly 12 hour experience by 1 developer is mind blowing. After playing Vertigo Remasterd at its release i was already stunned. But Vertigo 2 offers so much more. Tons of dialogue scenes, which you can walk away from. It is full of references to the previous game, and other games. The characters are fun, interesting, mysterious and sometimes even scary. The game is full of secrets, so exploring is key. After 12 hours i bet i still missed whole areas, weapons and siderooms. The soundtrack bangs, especially the one during the Autonica chapter. My god this game even has storyline braches. You can liturally alter the storyline based on your choises and paths you take. Which is something i did not come to expect from this game. And lastly, this game runs smooth. It can be nauseating for newcommers. But it is super smooth for me. The mechanics are super fluent. The gun animations are more then satisfying and reloading is just absolutely amazing.This game made me feel like a child, it was a real adventure that kept going, took you to all kinds of places. _childDocuments_.review: This is genuinely one of the greatest VR games... no.. VIDEO GAMES I have ever played. With references to portal, half life, H3VR, and so many more, there is so much in this game that comes together to genuinely make it one of the best VR games I have ever played. Fair warning though: It throws basically every phobia you could possibly have at you. Thalassophobia (fear of the ocean), Nyctophobia (fear of the dark), Automatonophobia (fear of mannequins), Entomophobia (fear of bugs), Aracnophobia (fear of spiders. To a lesser degree here. There are some eight legged enemies in this game but they aren't exactly spiders, more robotic... things with 8 legs), and so many more that I've lost track of but those are the major ones. name: Evergate
detailed_description: 'Welcome back to the Afterlife, Ki. Let's get you to the Evergate, and back to Earth' When a lost soul named 'Ki' awakens in the afterlife, her path back to earth is blocked by the ‘Evergate’. To return home, Ki must decipher her mysterious connection to kindred spirit as she navigates through memories of a time once past. Navigate through each new memory via 85 challenging stages. Harness the ‘Soulflame’ mechanic, unlock new abilities and find your own creative ways to reach each end gate. This ancient power of the Afterlife allows Ki to slow down time, take aim and fire a beam of energy at white surfaces known as 'The Source'. Use your Soulflame to smash through the mysterious crystals scattered throughout each memory. Unleash their power to soar to new heights, reach the unreachable and safely navigate perilous environments. Hit multiple crystals at once to combined their energies and find new creative ways to reach the end gate. Rise to the challenge and collect 'Essences' by reaching all the areas within each memory. Use them to unlock ancient artefacts and boost Ki's attributes. Move faster, jump higher and harness even greater powers! Gorgeous hand-drawn visuals and an elegantly orchestrated soundtrack - recorded by a live orchestra - immerse players in the Afterlife and bring dreams, nightmares and spirits alive in stunning detail. Stone Lantern Games is a Boston-based studio comprised of 4 MIT graduates. Like a gamer choosing a character class, each engineer on the team specializes in one of four proficiencies: Visual Effects, Art, Music, or Narrative.

_childDocuments_.review: Evergate is sadly going to be a game that is going to be overlooked by a majority of people. It gives off the impression that it's similar to Ori and the Blind Forest from a visual standpoint, and it's a small indie platformer that may not have that extra oompf that forces you to look at it. Yet, if you actually dig into a game, you'll find a fresh take on the platforming puzzle genre that forces you to keep on thinking creatively, while still forcing you to have a semi-precision in order to execute your puzzle plan. Needless to say, there's not a lot wrong here on the surface, and my entire first two hours with the game was basically me having fun on stream while really appreciating the eye for game design.Dividing levels into three objectives that don't run concurrently all the time was smart, to force replayability but to allow for experimentation with the actual path that you're going to travel, and there's enough leeway in most of these elements in order to scoot by even when a plan falls apart at first attempts. I really enjoyed the subtle layers of teaching: forcing you to think about new obstacles in a different way, and not just use each tool like you had used before hand. The artifacts is a nice touch to help out the game too for those who may have difficulty, although I do believe at times it can be a little bit too forgiving with those aritfacts (ice one in particular).The presentation, while feeling similar, is definitely its own thing: and I was really surprised with the level of detail in the environments in particular. Storytelling is left to be there for people to enjoy if they want, and let's you fill in the holes with your own interpretation without feeling hopelessly lost. Honestly, I'm actually somewhat sad, because I know this game is going to get overlooked in the big picture, but it's a real enjoyable romp that you should take a look at.  list]

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful looking game with an art style reminiscent of Ori and a great soundtrack, but wildly different gameplay.  Here you’ll find a precision trial and error puzzle platformer.  The game is split into different worlds each made of a collection of levels.  The main goal is to get to the end using the special jumping mechanic wherein you slow down time and jump off of some part of the level onto another.  The game requires extreme precision.  Most of the platforming will require a restart of the entire level if you fail one piece of it.  This part deterred me from continuing.  The levels don’t allow for much creativity as it’s clear there is one correct path and it must be done with extreme precision.  The levels quickly become very complicated and tedious to complete.  I would’ve preferred more dynamism in the level design.

_childDocuments_.review: It looks as if Ori and Dandara had a love child, but with its own unique twists. This is a wonderful puzzle platformer. It's tough, but incredibly satisfying when everything lines up correctly. I actually think it feels a lot like Celeste in its gameplay, in that it has very intuitive abilities, and you'll die again and again, but that makes victory feel all the sweeter. It's smooth, intuitive, and getting all the extra rewards for every level is utterly mindbending from the start.Don't listen to anyone saying it's an Ori clone. Those people have no idea what this game is, or possibly no idea what Ori is. Evergate is not a Metroidvania, it is a tough but satisfying puzzle platformer that's a ton of fun.It puzzles me that using a similar visual style leads to so much criticism. These games are beloved for their art styles as well as gameplay/story. If another dev adopts a similar style and makes a good game, what’s the problem? This is how anything artistic works: something that has a distinct style inspires other creators. It’s the same with game mechanics, and the piece they draw on is always only a tiny part of what makes or breaks the game.So if you feel on the fence about getting it because you're worried it's just a rip off, know that it isn't. Evergate is a fun little game with a lot of heart and its own identity.   It's got 5-8 hours of content, and it is absolutely worth it. I really hope more people get to enjoy this gem of a game.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Evergate is a well polished Platformer-Puzzle game with speedrunning elements.Longer:Evergate is a traditional side-scrolling platformer in the way of games like DCK2, where instead of a team-up mechanic you have the ability to fire your "soul-flame" through a crystal and gain its effects. There are 10 total chapters + epilogue, and bonus levels. The story is well-woven into the game, as is the music, atmosphere and worldbuilding.Every book builds on the main premise of the game, leading to a few antagonist encounters.  As you progress by gaining essence through completion goals or speedrunning, you'll be able to equip artifacts which are both speedrunning tactics for the advanced platformer and a way to help out someone who's struggling with different areas of the game. The puzzle element comes from the crystals. The first 3 books are exciting but not too tantalizing. After book there there starts to be ramp up in puzzles which take some time, thinking, and experimentation to figure out. This culminates in significant puzzles in the last 4 books of the game.Disclosure: I kickstarted & played the game through the whole life cycle

_childDocuments_.review: Evergate. This game is a puzzle platformer developed by Stone Lantern Games and published by PQube. Introduced at the Nintendo Indie Game Showcase, it was enough to grab the attention of the crowd. Perhaps for users who did not know Evergate until now, it may be a hidden gem-like game. Really? Let's take a look at it with Nyanco-chan! (ฅ'ω'ฅ) After playing the game, it is even better than expected. It's one of the best examples of its genre. You guide the child-like soul, Ki that is probably inspired by the mana (soul) concept in the East, on her journey through the Afterlife. As wielding the soulflame to boost to new heights, you will have an adventure with her. As the game progresses, you encounter Ki's past memories across lifetimes. The story itself is mediocre, but the essence of this game lies in the puzzle platformer mechanics and how is it presented to the player.It's a soulflame mechanic. Basically you can slow down time, take aim, and unleash the mysterious power. What really makes Evergate great is the way that it adds new ideas and gameplay mechanics constantly to provide a fresh sense to the player. With 10 worlds where they have beautiful hand-drawn artwork and admiring soundtrack, each offer clever and various levels that you play through. There is a collecting element added here, which can affect puzzle solving. It means that you can enjoy amazing open-ended puzzles that the dev team really put a lot of effort into it.Evergate. It's a well-made puzzle-platformer with gorgeous design and an astonishing soundtrack. With the various gameplay mechanics, every new world you meet adds the cleverly designed levels gradually. If you are looking for a good puzzle platformer where you can experience indie spirit, definitely Evergate is for you. Highly Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like platformers? Buy Evergate. It is as simple as that. You can't find a better platformer at any price by any developer. The level design is ingenious, the controls are tight, the music is lovely, and more than anything, it's really fun to play! I can't remember the last time a game gripped me like this. I just couldn't put it down. Every new chapter in the game (there are 10) adds new mechanics and totally changes the way you navigate the levels. The final bits of the game are a beautiful culmination of everything you have learned. You can play this game casually and get through every level in a few minutes, or you can try to beat insanely fast speedrun times and learn perfect precision to get every collectible. Play this game any way you want to...but do yourself a favor, and PLAY THIS GAME.

_childDocuments_.review: As other reviewers have noted, Evergate is a beautiful, finely-tuned platformer with deep and unique mechanics. But I want to call out a particular aspect of the game that I find especially impressive: more than almost any other game I've played, it makes room for players of a wide range of skill levels.The levels in Evergate can be completed just by getting to the exit, which ranges from fairly easy to moderately difficult, depending on the level. Each level also has three optional goals, some of which are very difficult (or at least they were for me). Completing the the optional goals unlocks powerups; collecting and playing around with them provides replay value for completionists, while players having trouble can go back to gather powerups from earlier worlds to help them through the later ones. Even beyond the game's explicit goals and rewards, it's extremely satisfying to get "in the groove" and blaze through a level with precision jumps, and I get the feeling Evergate would be a lot of fun to speedrun.I played through a beta version of Evergate on PC and then 100%-ed the final version on Switch, and I felt nicely challenged but not frustrated throughout the entirety of both playthroughs. That's impressive, and it makes me think that a broad range of other players would enjoy it just as much as I did. If you have any interest in platformers, give Evergate a try.

_childDocuments_.review: This game doesn't have many reviews, so I thought I'd leave one. Evergate is a lite puzzle platformer (the puzzles are far from mind-bending) with some Ori vibes. However, the similarities to Ori are mostly in the graphical style and presentation, which are both great. The soundtrack is pleasing to listen to as well. It is definitely a fun game, and you're looking at at least 10hrs of quality fun if you decide to go for some of the challenges offered by the achievement set. The achievements in this game are a nice mix of challenges, exploring different ideas like beating x levels without jumping, and just general misc stuff. They were quite fun even to just figure them out.There is quite a bit of replayability if you're a speedrunner, as there are a variety of strategies for going faster due to the artifact system. There are 30 artifacts in the game, each giving you a modifier such as burning things whenever you fire, or an increased jump height or speed, all the way to creating a vortex when you fire your first shot for a level. If you're not a speedrunner though, you're looking at a solid 10hr experience here.One thing I quite enjoyed about Evergate is its progression. There are 10 worlds which are divided into books and chapters (4 books each with 2-3 chapters), and each book introduces a new use for the soulflame and focuses on this new use for the remainder of the world. This keeps the gameplay fresh throughout the game without ever feeling like you've seen a certain mechanic too much.Overall a nice lightly challenging game with a nice atmosphere, music, and unique gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely beautiful and amazing 2D Puzzle-Platformer that I highly recommend and will now explain why I think that way.The Music in this game is gorgeous, it just hits you emotionally at all the right moments throughout the game and its sweet story. Or you are an achievement hungry completionist looking for some interesting challenges, or maybe you love just seeing how fast you can beat each level, using the in-game time to be able to track your bests on each stage, Evergate's open-ended puzzle design and optional collectables gives each of these playstyles something to enjoy.The game is incredibly well optimized ( I was getting 300-500 FPS, and have heard even on lower end PC's it preforms excellently) and coming from someone who got to play this game in beta, even this games beta had less glitches than a lot of modern games full releases do. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR:  Evergate is a puzzle platformer with a polished gameplay, unique artstyle, an amazing soundtrack and a cute story. It follow Ki and her journey through the afterlife as trouble stirs. If you enjoy speedrunning you'll love this game. If you don't, there still is plenty to enjoy.Length: My first playthrough of the game took about 6 hours. Each level has 3 challenges to it. First is using all of the available tools. Second is reaching 3 specific areas on each level. This is finishing the level under a time limit. My first playthrough consisted of doing the first two challenges through each level. Speedrunning through each level afterwards took me about two hours. Level Design: It's very cleverly design. You can go through each level multiple ways, especially once you get more abilities. I found the puzzles to be a bit challenging, but not frustrating. Story: It's nice and cute. It's a little confusing at first, but I believe that's intended as your character is learning as you do about the afterlife. Artsyle: Very unique, beautiful, enhances gameplay and never interferes with it. Soundtrack: Great soundtrack. I found myself humming the songs outside of the game. I'd put it just below the tier of ori and hollow knight. Replay Value: It has decent replay value. Because of the different ways you can do each level, it doesn't get too repetitive. Saying this, there isn't necesarily anything too unique through each playthrough. If you enjoy speedrunning, it has a lot of replay value though. Performance: I had no performance issues and only one minor bug throughout the whole game.Cons: I found once I got all the skills and abilities, the only way to truly utilize them was to just speed up your time in previous levels. I would've enjoyed something like B side on Celeste where it's similar map, but you really gotta platform and think differently. Wishlist: I have no idea if there are any plans, but workshop support for community made maps would be really cool.

_childDocuments_.review: Evergate is a gorgeous puzzle platformer with some of the most unique and interesting mechanics I've seen in years. The puzzles offer a balanced challenge in terms of both problem-solving and mechanical execution, and mastering the controls to fly through the levels feels incredibly satisfying. The fantastic level design also gives the player a lot of freedom to come up with unique and creative solutions to the puzzles, rewarding players who enjoy thinking outside the box.The settings menu includes the basic necessities (volume control and key rebindings) as well as a lot of other quality-of-life improvements, such as a speedrun mode that adds a timer for each stage.The next section might be going outside the scope of what you'd be looking for from a review, but this game means a lot to me. I've been following its journey to completion ever since the first public demo releases, and the developers are genuinely some of the most lovely people I've ever met in my entire life. So seriously, if any of this looks or sounds interesting to you, give it a try. You won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: While the aesthetics are surely inspired by Ori, the gameplay is pretty different. You make your way through levels by activating "crystals" placed around the map, and to do that you fire a beam at them — which only works if there's a white surface at the end of the beam. As a result, every level is a sort of puzzle. You also have artifacts which give you powerful upgrades and can break many levels (for example +30% jump height lets you reach many platforms you otherwise couldn't), however you can only equip one at a time, and this type of level-breaking is kinda part of the appeal. Changing your equipped artifact restarts the level.The crystals themselves grow in variety over the course of the game, so at first you're only working with one type in each "room", but at the end it's many more, significantly increasing complexity. Some of the later levels can be a b*tch to navigate the intended way, but the game never demands use of artifacts, and so you can usually, if not always, find a way to break them, should you need it.Movement is pretty fast, especially falling, but aiming your beam slows down time, and you can also hold Q to freeze it completely whenever and for as long as you want. So I wouldn't say the game requires much mechanical skill, it's all about figuring out how to get through.There's also a neat story and good BGM.

_childDocuments_.review: WOW. This game is so polished, you'd never believe it was made by such a small team! The visuals are some of the most gorgeous I've seen - as well as being adorable - and the music is FANTASTIC. I'm so glad I decided to buy the soundtrack with it! The gameplay is really sharp and tight, which is crucial in a precision platformer, and the pacing is perfect - the new abilities are introduced gradually enough that they never feel overwhelming, yet none of the mechanics outstay their welcome.When it comes to difficulty, Evergate is definitely not an easy game. There's an achievement for dying/resetting 100 times, which I got after about 2 hours. I really appreciated the option to simplify ability activation because I was having some coordination issues with my controller, and there's other options to change things or make them easier too! There are two elements to each level, figuring out what to do and then executing it, and most of the time, the former was a lot trickier. Some levels, I bummed around, totally lost, for 15-20 minutes, but usually it was quicker than that and there were only a few levels that I found truly frustrating (and only one where I had to cheat, because I somehow managed to miss ). When you throw artifacts into the mix, which convey various extra abilities suited to different playstyles, you open up some different ways to complete levels. In feel, it reminds me of games like Blue Fire, Unbound: Worlds Apart, Nihilumbra (the void part), and the White Palace section of Hollow Knight, but never as difficult or downright unfair as those games got at their worst (unlike Evergate, the White Palace's execution is WAY harder than figuring it out; it's an exercise in "You want me to do what now?"). There are also a couple of levels reminiscent of the escape sequences in Ori and the Blind Forest, which I've always enjoyed in a sort of masochistic way. In terms of replay value, the time trials and tons of tricky achievements will let you keep going if you want!Finally, I adore the story! It's so rare to see a game that focuses on platonic relationships, let alone a sibling one. I really enjoyed the lack of cliche in the story beats, and how it covered grounds from innocent joy to jaded heartbreak to redemption. It truly touched my heart, and I'm SO glad this isn't one of those games (*coughGuacameleecough*) that forces you collect a bunch of super difficult extras for the privilege of a non-tragic ending.If you enjoy precision platformers at all, I HIGHLY recommend picking this one up, and throw the soundtrack in as well! Though occasionally frustrating, Evergate is a beautiful and thoroughly enjoyable experience that will leave you with a smile. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, as everyone mentioned, similar to Celeste, so if you like Celeste you 99% would enjoy it.Few myth busted from negative reviews:- It's shorter that Celeste. Right, but you still need about 10 hours to complete. It's like getting through A-sides without berries, same, I think.- Need to be very precise on controls. Wrong. There more space for error, it's 'precise platformer', but you have wider margin, I'd say then Celeste. - Restarts are annoying. Wrong. No room takes more than 30 seconds, average 10-15 seconds, restarts are instant (no animation delay/fade), I could not imagine less punishment for death.- Puzzles are repetitive - also wrong, you never applying same two tricks in a row, if you repeat something - only in the middle of combination of new mechanics, so it's always fresh. Only first world, maybe, as you only get access to 1 puzzle element, but even then I did not felt bored.- Missing tutorial. Dunno maybe who wrote that was blind. There is a tutorial. And you need to repeat basic game actions several times. Game literally have 4 controls - left, right, jump, and activate (with aim). WTH you need more tutorial for? It's just - aim the crystal with mouse and click, that's all the controls! For new puzzle elements in chapters you just activate them and see what it does, you don't need wall of text 'this triangle can break walls, activate to break a wall blah blah'.p.s. also there is some lore in the game, but you can skip-skip everything ang get concentrated puzzle experiense from 2nd minute to the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Evergate is a relaxing puzzle platformer that is mostly about strategy. Execution is typically not difficult due to time slowdown/stop but flying through the air chaining multiple crystals can be very satisfying.The puzzles stay interesting by introducing new mechanics in every world and gradually ramping the complexity. Additionally, each level has three optional objectives which are the main source of difficulty in the game. Completing these objectives will unlock power-ups that will help make levels easier or allow new strategies for speedrunning.The story is not interesting but that does not matter in such a gameplay-focused title.Overall, if you enjoy platformers and puzzles, pick this up!
_childDocuments_.name: Evergate

_childDocuments_.review: Genre:  -Puzzle Platformer Fit for me:-Not in my top 10 fav genre, so bad fit.  However, I love all other types of platformers, so maybe this one can win me over.Pros:-Gorgeous artistic style.  They clearly took inspiration from Ori, as this game has a similar aesthetic and the main character resembles Ori.  They are creative enough to make it their own unique experience while paying tribute to one of the most beautiful games ever made.-Perfect tranquil soundtrack w/ spot on sound effects.  Everything sounds really good and fits well w/i the Evergate world.-Extremely responsive and fluid controls.  They nailed the most basic part of this game.  This entire game centers around chaining multiple mechanics while in mid-air, so the controls need to feel silky smooth, and they do.-Fun movement, jumping, and the main juggling/slow down time mechanic.  Another clear inspiration from Ori but they expanded upon it big time.  They created an entire game centering around this one mechanic but added 10 different environmental mechanics that interact w/ this chaining/slow down time mechanic.  It's executed perfectly, and is fun, engaging, and intuitive to use.-This is a true puzzle platformer that really combines some of the best elements of puzzle games and the best elements of precision platformers.  I would play a lot more puzzle platformers if they all had this type of gameplay.-Adorable, heart warming story that works really well w/ the gameplay experienceCons:-Some of the mechanics at the end are bit complicated and it would have been nice to have some form of tutorial on how to use them.  I eventually figured them out, but they sometimes took a good amount of trial and error.-There are a ton of upgrades that you can unlock, but I found myself mostly using the 30% jump increase and 20% boost increase.  A lot of the other upgrades seemed fun, but felt very situational, mostly meant to be used in the world that you gained access to those upgrades.  It would have been nice if all of the upgrades were a bit more applicable.-No level editor.  I think a level editor would be a really cool idea, so maybe it's a possibility in a sequel.Thoughts:-Evergate is my new favorite puzzle platformer.  If all puzzle platformers had a similar focus on fluid, precise platforming sections; I'd play a lot more of them.  This is a great option for ppl that like precision platformers but would prefer a slower, more methodical approach.  I really enjoyed my experience w/ this one and will be on the lookout for any future games by these devs.Consensus:-Excellent Game (Tier 2 and makes up 25% of my reviews).  This is hands down my new favorite puzzle platformer.  It knows exactly what it is, and doesn't try to do too much.  With a gorgeous aesthetic, excellent fundamental mechanics, and a heart warming story, Evergate is a great game and one of my bigger surprises of 2020.  I love when I play a game that gets me excited to try other similar games in that genre.  Here's hoping that I can find some more puzzle platformer hidden gems!

_childDocuments_.review: If you're into puzzle-platformers, buy this. Just do it. Evergate is a fun game with smooth gameplay. _childDocuments_.review: There's something about ethereal gameplay and orchestral music that gets me every time.If you want to see some Evergate gameplay for yourself, watch my first impressions gameplay above. Evergate is a puzzle platformer that's kind to newbies and rewards good players with a satisfying gameplay experience. Each stage is fairly straightforward, but if you're going for 100% there's enough uncertainty and enough precision required to take a few goes. Plus, when you're just starting out, it's going to take a hot minute to get used to it. You jump, you shoot Soulflame, and as long as your Soulflame passed through a crystal you'll get a boost on your jump. Pass it through multiple crystals and you'll get an even bigger boost.If that all sounds a bit pedestrian, it's because Evergate has to be seen or experienced. The art style is beautiful. The orchestral music is so good that I'm disappointed it's not available to buy separately. And once you start playing, you understand how much fun this game would look if it was done as a speedrun. Failure is frequent but doesn't feel punishing because you just respawn instantly with the level reset. The lack of downtime is huge. There's also a bit of a mystery at work, told beautifully through images and sound effects that leaves so much to the imagination. This team knew what they were doing, and they executed it well.Either buy Evergate now or add it to your wishlist. It's a fantastic game that isn't receiving near the attention it deserves.

_childDocuments_.review: Video Review: Curator Page: Evergate a 2d puzzle game set in a wonderful hand drawn vision of the afterlife, where you play as Ki who wakes up and is greeted by the grounds keeper,  who helps you wield and use your soulflame (your main mechanic in the game) and tells KI, if she is to  return to earth she must go through the Evergate, But it seems the gate has more in store for her when it presents a memory book to her, uncommon for the gate to do, going through these memory books you find out that the memories are not Ki’s and it's up to you to progress the levels to learn the reason. Evergate Is a wonderful 2d platform that will bring speed runner flocking to it just because of its technical way that people could finish each level quickly and the game encourage it. With 3 different objectives during each stage that unlock ancient artifacts to boos Ki’s attributes like move faster, jump higher, and many more to help you along the way. The 3 objectives are  1. Collect all essence in the stage which are like small collectibles scattered on each stage. 2. Destroy every special crystal in the stage (I’ll go over them more in a second) 3. Beating the stage within a set amount of time. Each giving you one point to help you unlock the 3 unlocks in each memory book. Now the Special crystals I talked about. These crystals are the ones that help you traverse the stages. Activated by your soulflame only while you are aligned with a white section on the ground. Thats the best I can explain it but you should be able to see what I mean in the gameplay. Each memory book adds a new crystal to list. First being a simple launch crystal that sends you in the opposite direction you aim your soulflame. Others being platforms, flames, item swap and many more. Making later levels complex with multiple ways to complete. Other obstacles will dot your adventure as well, many death traps on each stage like thorns, a strange osculating star fall or whatever it is, and then my distain. The crows that will aim for you after each special crystal you destroy. They are used in some stages to help you reach the summit but are a real pain in the ass.  Now of course the graphics and sound design. The wonderful hand drawn elements in this game give the wonderful personality it has. I love how a good bit of games are going in this direction and gives the individuality to each title I play. Sound design is not too bad in this game the music I am in love with. The score that they gave this game works perfectly and is very uplifting and floaty. But, the sound effects at time that can be bothersome. The gem destroying gets repetitive and back again to the crows their howl is not my most favorite especial when you are speed running through the level and may need to retry the level because you made a mistake. But other than that, Evergate is a fun and beautiful game with a wonderful story. That I think most people will enjoy with its level design. I would recommend this game if you think it looks good and you think the game looks fun because, it is and you won't be disappointed. With 85 stages for 19.99 it well worth its price point.

_childDocuments_.review: Like many of you I collect stand-out indie games despite an eternal backlog. The art and puzzle-platforming of Evergate caught my eye a couple years back, and now finally playing it, it's everything I hoped for. The art's lovely and blends into responsive, thoughtful gameplay, as the other reviews say. It has several chapters and several levels per chapter, plus bonus challenge levels, each with three tiers of challenge -- clearing, getting bonus coins, and then meeting a speed-run goal. Just clearing is sufficient to progress, the coins achievable just by trying things out, the speed runs requiring precision and practice but not to the point of frustration (so far!).As for music, it hasn't gotten tedious to listen to on the tougher levels yet, if anything it's a bit catchy as I swing back through the parts of the level I've solved. The levels being designed with speed-run in mind, it's not slow or exhausting to get back to where I was after resetting to try another solution. Admittedly haven't played long, but no complaints after 100%'ing the first chapter for sure. Go for it!

_childDocuments_.review: Evergate was recommended to me as the newest indie platformer for people who enjoy games like Celeste and Hollow Knight. :-)I really liked it and can definitely recommend it. The goal of the game is basically to connect a number of level "items" in the correct order and way to reach the goal. The "items" you activate with your beam will give your character varying abilities (e.g. they launch you up or give you a double jump) and the underlying mechanics are all interesting and feel satisfying to use. It is not only about solving the puzzles, but you also have to time and execute your solution in the right way. This is where the game becomes a platformer. I would say the platforming feels pretty well overall: it is relatively slow paced and allows you to even slow down time which fits the puzzle character of the game. This makes the gameplay feel pretty chill. You can chain moves pretty fast once you get good at the game, but it never feels like you're in a rush. Both puzzle and platforming gameplay wise, the game provides a challenge, but is not super hard either.For each level you have three extra goals: reach the goal under a certain time limit, collect collectibles that are spread throughout the level and use all the "items" in the level. Especially the last one is a breath of fresh air that feels weird at first, but will grow into something you enjoy. You are probably used to the convention that basically the more things you skip in a level (let's say a health pickup), the better you play. This is how you should play to reach the time goal, but if you're going for the "use all items" goal, you have to play the levels in a different way. You could say you have to dance with the level. :-) Sometimes it's also much harder to include all the items in your combination of moves than ignoring some. The three goals that you don't have to complete all at the same time provide an opportunity to play each level in multiple different ways and see it in a different light each time.I found most of the levels pretty good and satisfying to figure out. Some levels were very intuitive and I could improvise the solution while flying through the air while others took a while to think about different options. A few levels go a little overboard in my opinion with putting a huge number of items in the level where you only really need a fraction of them. Some people like having a lot of different options, but I prefer levels that have a more specific solution. Other levels are exactly like that though and you need to use all items in a clever way to be able to reach the goal. So in general, the level design is really nice and probably has something for everyone.The game comes with nice graphics, a relaxing soundtrack and a cute little story for setting the mood. I found the mechanics very polished and I didn't really find any glitches even though I played it at launch. It seems like a miracle that the game even runs on my laptop at all which can run Celeste and Super Meat Boy, but not Hollow Knight. Evergate - like Hollow Knight - has lots of particle and lighting effects, but it always ran fluently for me.

_childDocuments_.review: been following this game since 2019 when i saw it at PAX East, drawn in by the elegant visuals. i'm not the biggest fan of platformers, but this game had a certain magnetism about it that i couldn't ignore.now that the game is released, i was very pleased with my experience. fortunately, Evergate is not just a "pretty face" - it's a damn good puzzle platformer too. it's clever and well paced - just as soon as you get the hang of one mechanic, they introduce a new one, and it feels rewarding to learn how to combine the new mechanics with the old ones.i appreciate that its "campaign" doesn't overstay its welcome, however if you really enjoy these types of games, there are lots of challenges to go back and complete, as well as several bonus levels. i beat the game in ~6hrs, but i bet there's another 3-4hrs of content there if you want it.the storytelling does a lot with a little, which makes it a great accessory to the gameplay - it's easy to follow, it delivers a nice message without ever distracting from the gameplay.in my opinion this game was well worth the 1.5yr wait, especially if you're a fan of these types of games. please buy the game if you think you'd be interested, as this is one of those studios that we should support!

_childDocuments_.review: Disclosure: I'm a kickstarter backer, beta tester, and contributorEvergate is a tight and tricky 2D puzzle platformer that combines the otherworldly art style of Ori and Child of Light with the tough-but-fair, die-til-you-get-it, stage-based platforming of Celeste and Super Meat Boy. On top of this foundation is a unique puzzle mechanic in the form of memory crystals that the protagonist Ki must shoot with her soulflame to unleash their powers. Crystals must be used with wit and precision to reach the gate at the end of each level, and to unlock playstyle-boosting artifacts via optional achievements.A charming and affecting story about second chances enhanced by a magnificent fully orchestral soundtrack round out this impressive first release from four-person indie outfit Stone Lantern Games.Fully supports both controller and KBM play, and is a bast for both heady, deliberate play and speed-running.
