_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent puzzle platformer, rewarding both careful planning and skillful play. The puzzles and mechanics are really well designed, with the different crystals offering a really solid variety of challenges for the different worlds/levels. The straightforward path is often discovered after a bit of experimentation or thinking, but often levels with have surprising shortcuts or tricks to the layout you can abuse to blaze through an otherwise tough room.Besides the gameplay, the art and the music (especially the music!) is excellent! The vibe is really beautiful and dream-like, with the jump in settings translating over to the aesthetics in a fun way. Definitely can recommend if you're into either puzzle platformers or more skill-based ones like Celeste.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice gem of a game with great level design, music, visuals and an interesting story. The Artifacts were also a great incentive to replay levels and complete objectives/gain the essence required to unlock them. Some of the artifacts did feel a bit cheap but you can play the whole game without using any of them. I'm glad most of them are fun to use since it actually felt worth unlocking them and spiced up the way in which you completed a level.The objectives are completely optional so you can finish the whole game quite easily if you were to play it that way. For the best experience, I recommend trying to complete the "collect the petals" and "destroy the crystals" objectives at the same time. It makes completing a level much trickier and provides a very enjoyable challenge.For a puzzle platformer with no combat, the game had a good amount of story which I personally found interesting and felt that it enhanced the experience. Though it was mostly told through a few seconds of visuals and a bit of dialogue whenever your reached a new area/level, it was still enough to make it feel like you'd been through a meaningful journey once you reached the end of the game.The visuals were quite charming and the music blended quite well with them. It great soundtrack that set the mood perfectly for each level, especially during the final area. Overall it's a fun, charming game with a good amount of replayability and an interesting story that has a nice message. It's definitely worth checking out, especially if you're into puzzle platformers or indie games in general.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT 2: No further updates or communications from Eko since my last message. The game is left in an awkward state. The rucks are too easy to win and the AI is tactically awful and will happily kick the ball out of the full, kick the ball when there's space ahead, or try and play from behind their goal line. I can still recommend the game because of the hours I've put into it but it's still not worth it at full price, especially with no further updates coming.EDIT: Eko are listening to feedback and have already added some much needed improvements to the game! I would keep an eye on the game because if they keep this up, I could eventually be recommending it at full price.I'm in an awkward position where I can't truly say whether I recommend this game or not. This is the first rugby game since Rugby 08 that has intrigued me enough not only to pick it up, but to pick it upon release.The main takeaway is that firstly, it's a rugby game and secondly, I've actually had fun playing it! I wouldn't say at this point it's worth it at full price but it's a really step in the right direction and if Eko Software and Bigben keep moving in that same direction, we can expect a good rugby game by the next world cup.- The game is actually fun. I've enjoyed my time playing it.- There's a nice amount of tactical fidelity and room to play around with it. Each tactic feels different enough to another.- A decent number of licensed teams and players. Probably the best we can get until the game is big and popular enough to include the lower divisions and full licensing from around the world.- The controls (that I've figured out) feel like they work. I've not been left scratching my head asking why a player has done X when I asked him to do Y.- A proper build-a-team career mode called "Solo mode". I really like the FIFA-style cards!- The menu interface is visually good and easy to use.- Substitution suggestions works really well.- Mechanically, as a game, a lot of it works. It doesn't quite have the fun and polish of FIFA and it doesn't feel like it quite represents a real rugby match yet but it's closing in on both.- The cost of the game for what you get. It's not worth full price.- Breakdowns against the AI are too easy. As long as you have one or two players nearby, you'll win it with ease.- The pacing of the game could be improved. Tackling feels fast and responsive but everything else feels slow and clunky. It makes any tactics outside of ridiculous offloads and constantly passing it wide to the winger very difficult. EDIT: Pacing has been improved and is on the right track!- Sprints down the wing are difficult as the typical winger has enough stamina to take them around 10 metres before they slow down to toddler-pace. Same with grubbering it past - it seems defenders always have an advantage. EDIT: This isn't as bad as it was before with the newer patch! Much improved!- Stamina in general is quite confusing. Being hit by a tackle takes away half of a player's stamina?- Player and team ratings don't match up or are misleading. Looking at my build-a-team with mostly players from Leicester Tigers for example: England star Manu Tuilagi 68, single capped Noel Reid 78. England international George Ford has a rating of 71, Jarrod Evans has 77. I assume this takes into account team performance as well as individual (struggling Leicester).- 40 metre offloads from props are still a thing. I understand this is a fun vs realism thing but it's laughable at times.- The AI commits way too many fouls and there aren't red cards. I've seen a match with 7 yellow cards, 2 of which were the same player (no red). EDIT: This has been patched out and is no longer a problem.- EDIT: A fair amount of bugs. Crashing right at the end of matches and the AI refusing to use the ball after a maul are the two gamebreaking ones.- EDIT: The game is a bit too easy now, even on Pro. The AI has some real blunder moments like kicking the ball out on the full.- Player representations on the pitch aren't great. This is purely a visual/graphical thing and hasn't impacted my enjoyment of the game.- Commentary team audio sync doesn't match the game. "Taking forever to take this restart!" after 10 minutes of open-play. "The referee has called an advantage after a foul" after a simple knock-on.- The tutorials leave a lot to be desired and I felt like I didn't gain anything from using them. Is there even a page to show me which button does what? What do the flashing buttons mean during the lineout?- It's clunky and cumbersome to organise your squad on the team management screen. The option to filter by position (sort isn't that great) or a "best-in-slot" quick selection option would help a lot.- Broken field play is still too organised. I want turnovers to feel as manic and disorganised as they do in a real match and make opportunist tries from them more of an option.- The attacking line is usually so flat, even at its deepest, that kicking is quite difficult. I can get off 1 in 10 drop goals or crossfield kicks without being tackled first.- EDIT: A few laws are inconsistent, e.g. Knock-ons are given for a chargedown and sometimes I get the line-out throw-in for a ball I kicked out.- A career/manager mode with full seasons, progression and proper transfers. I'd even be happy with a random player generator to add some bulk around the licensed players.- Southern Hemisphere rugby, lower division teams.- Missing tournaments like the Six Nations.- No real graphics options.- No build-a-player option.- If there's a way to name my custom team, I have no idea how to. I've been playing as "My Team 1" for the past 2/3 seasons.- No option to select your kicker.- EDIT: The option to make custom leagues. There's no licensing for an English Premiership league but we could get around that by making it ourselves.

_childDocuments_.review: BIGBEN are a Promoter I admire because they deliver games that I Actually Want to See & they have been behind some of the Greatest Game releases in the last few years too; o Dacar Rally, o AO Tennis 2 (with all its faults),o WRC 8 (an absolute Masterpiece).BUT, they have also been involved in some of the worst games ever released, I'm of course talking about RUGBY 18.THANKFULLY RUGBY 20 is huge leaps ahead of RUGBY 18 and a totally new approach, control system and mechanics lead RUGBY 20 into an unassailable lead over its predecessor.Certainly RUBGY 20 does not appear to offer the perfect rugby experience, but I would argue that this is the direction the gaming community were PLEADING for & it certainly does do a great job of delivering a relatively Realistic RUGBY experience and sets a decent foundation where improvement WILL be needed and hopefully will come.I have already changed this review from Not Recommended To Recommended and back again TWICE!  So I really am on the fence here.o NEW Mechanics – many of which I adore. Lineouts – Scrum – Tactics - Goal Kicking!o Graphics are acceptable; Not much of an improvement over RUGBY 18 TBH, but lots of nice cut-scenes and animations.o Tackling is pretty good in all honesty, I like it a lot (Area for enhancement but AOK as is).o LEAGUE option is OK, I like how you can set a favourite and it auto defaults to it (NICE TOUCH).o Some licensed players are really well recreated.o Some BIG NASTY & Illegal Tackles + resulting Injuries (thank goodness!).o MY TEAM (Almost Career) - Similar to FIFA's UT, but without the micro-transaction BS.o Gameplay I have had a game that was REALLY fun to play!  So sometimes it all works (which is why I say it has the potential).o Commentary - limited & stuttery but OK.o I think I counted 10 stadiums, they're OK.o Tutorials are ESSENTIAL in this game and what's there is good (some missing see below).o League Mode - start from French Div 3 get promoted through the divisions.o Challenges are NOT what they sound like (They are in-game weekly challenges) I was kind of expecting scenarios.o Passing is SLOW & Laborious. Passes happen Really late.o Slow gameplay, tackling seems a fast paced affair, but running, kicking and passing all seems too slow.o Licensing - if there is Modding then OK this can be bypassed, but without it, it is a problem. o No Single player career.o Online MP just doesn't seem to work.  I find a player, then sit waiting for that player endlessly...to do what? You already said player found?o Audio - Just quite poor and audio is SO Important to immersion.o Missing Tutorials.  Tackling (when the circle around your feet appears) Kick-off.Look this is a £30 game & for that sort of money I expect to be able to play happily for a long time & I am not sure this game is ready to deliver that.  Jonah Lomu Rugby was a game I played with my brothers over and over and over again, and if we had the chance we would probably play it today too, but this is NOT that game, it is nothing like that game.I am glad that the game has received WAY MORE Depth & revised motion capture animations do make the game feel more authentic.  Where this game REALLY delivers is on the Tactics & Set-Plays, `some` of the Mechanics (Tackling, Goal Kicking, lineouts etc..). Sadly it lacks in the most important areas (Passing, Player Movements, Responsiveness, AI Intelligence), it evens says in the trailer you can pass before or after tackle contact (but not during & this IS another problem).The issues in this game are not issues that cannot be resolved, a few tweaks to the arrangement of the algorithm & passes will be enacted when the player calls for them (not a second or two later) and the AI is something that will always be under constant scrutiny and tweaking.It's probably the BEST Rugby UNION game available, ATM, but I wouldn't say it was the best Rugby game available ATM.For me...Right now I do JUST about recommend this game...No I don't...Honestly I am RIGHT ON The FENCE!With a FEW Tweaks and IMPROVEMENTS I do recommend this game...but it needs tweaking.In all honesty I should NOT recommend the game, until these improvements have arrived, but I am so close to giving this a thumbs up!The issues will annoy me too much, BUT I think (hope) they will be improved??? This has the potential to be a great RUGBY game & I really hope they will improve the game. _childDocuments_.review: Huge strides forward from Rugby 18, and more tactical gameplay on the field than Rugby Challenge 3, but suffers from clunky player movement, suspect AI, and the lack of an in-depth franchise mode (one of my favorite aspects of sports games). _childDocuments_.review: Before i start know that i have lived and breathed rugby for 30 years, i know more than enough to give a verdict on this game so here goes...GRAPHICS  6/10Not great, could and prob should be a lot better than they are in 2020 for a £31 gameANIMATIONS 5/10just watch a replay of a player sprinting down the wing, the movements are laughable and poorly implementedDIFFICULTY  3/10This is where the game falls flat on its face, you have 3 levels...amateur, semi pro and pro.  With amateur and semi pro you can easily win every ruck and force turn over after turn over, with pro you will struggle to make one turnover per match, not that this makes the game hard..it doesn't.  The game is easy even at pro level, i have yet to lose a single game in my first 3 seasons and i'm no games wizard.A.I,  4/10The A.I. will constantly trunk the ball up thru the middle of the park and only rarely throw it wide, this just makes it easy to knock em back time and time again.  On the rare occasion they do throw it wide it feels a lot better but like i said its a rare occasion, 90% of the time they are as dumb as rocks.FEATURES 6/10The modes of play are not too bad, you have various leagues and nations, i did not expect a full license so im ok with certain teams and players missing.  What im not ok with is the solo mode where you create a team with card style players and run them thru a season.  Whats the first thing you do when you create your own team?  That's right you give them a cool name, but wait!  in this game your team name is called "myteam1"  and you have no control to rename it .... ARE THEY ♥♥♥ SERIOUS!   Why in gods name would they think that this is ok!  how detached from reality are the developers to think that a simple omission like this is acceptable, it may not appear to be a massive deal but it is, i'm lost for words at the total stupidity on display here...just wow!BOTTOM LINEAfter 17 hrs i am totally bored of this game, it presents zero challenge to keep me engaged and playing, i have gone thru 3 seasons unbeaten with "myteam1"  sigh!  who are rated 68, along the way i have easily beaten teams rated up to 82 all on pro difficulty, the AI are predictable and clueless and rarely pose a threat.   For a game that costs £31 this is not even close to being value for money, its fun for 10 mins the you start seeing all the cracks, The devs do not respond to comments and suggestions, gone are the days when developers had pride in their products, this has been dumped on steam and left to rot.  Do yourself a favour, keep your money and kick this into touch.Update:  Devs dropped an update out of the blue, poor communication still,  this update does go some way to making this game better BUT STILL NO WAY TO NAME YOUR TEAM, so annoying.   The AI will now offload more which makes them more dangerous and therefore more interesting, the game though is still too easy at pro level, only the very best teams will give you a good game...i'm still yet to lose a game, this gets boring!Getting better but still some way to go imo.  I really want to recommend this but i have to be honest, for the price its not quite where it should be, really hope they keep improving it.Update 2My final match on this poor game saw me run out 117-0 winners.  The A.I. are possibly the worst of any game i have ever played, oh and forget multiplayer because no one plays the game, if you do have a mate to play with you will experience chronic rubber banding issues that just sour the whole experience, as if its not bad enough already!  Zero updates forth coming and covid -19 is no excuse because plenty of devs are still working on games.  Rugby 20 is a con of a game that should be removed from steam...DO NOT BUY!

_childDocuments_.review: So, after about 16 hours in Rugby 18 and a few in this one, I think I can review this pretty objectively as I know what my expectations were. This will be an unnecessary long review.I'm only recommending this game if you buy it on a big sale and are very passionate about rugby. If you're not, it's a high red flagged NO.I want to start by saying that the only reason someone would buy or recommend this game is that they're a huge fan of the sport and, driven by melancholy, they still miss the good old Rugby 08 days and search for modern alternatives and rosters as updated as possible. As we all know, this rugby games market is not that great overall and we have a very specific and narrow list of games to chose from. Some better than others. This is clearly better than others, so this is why I'll recommend it. I really want to believe that at some point the Rugby games by Eko would be the new 'gold standard' of Rugby games, as there is a lot of potential. However, at this point, while there is are some great improvements compared to Rugby 18 (and also some downgrades, which we'll discuss at the cons), it's still hard to recommend this game (especially at the price tag it's got). This is, unfortunately, where the pros kind of stop...This would be a dream if it was more mod friendly. I, personally, could've gotten over the clunkiness of the game, over the AI and all that, as I know what the expectations should be for a rugby game, if it would at least let you do your own stuff. I'd highly recommend for future releases that at least a edit national squads option to be implemented, so you can select which people you'd want in your national squad, as a workaround for licensing. The booster thing also has to go - there was only one thing really fun about 18 and that's no more available.

_childDocuments_.review: Bit buggy at launch, but with the new updates being released in the public development beta earlier this week, this is becoming a brilliant rugby game! I feel that this game gets an unfair amount of criticism. Some of the reviews I've read don't appear to have explored the game fully, complaining about features not being there which are present or comparisons to the likes of FIFA football games. A series that have DECADES of development behind them and 1000x the budget. Played mostly on "semi pro" difficultyPositives - Large selection of licensed teams to choose from - play through top leagues with your favourite team- "My team" lets you create your own team from the players you have collected from booster packs. You can then play and manage your created team to success in Solo mode- Kicking system is brilliant- Lineout system is great- Scrum system is good, intuitive enough not to just be mashing buttons and not so labourious it slows the game down too much - Tutorials are good, but without the beta they lacked a control list (this has been added in the beta, thank you!)Notable Features improved in the beta - rucks which were previously too easy are now much more competitive, more difficult to turn over the opposite team allowing the AI to string more phases in attack- AI are much smarter in attack, making for some interesting moments defending cross field kicks, pick and go's and set plays - yellow cards are reduced, game flows alot better. - Control list in pause menu! (I'd previously been scoring trys by purposefully getting tackled over the line!)All the beta updates are detailed in the patch notes but I thought I'd note down the main ones Multiplayer- haven't tried it yet, may update when I do Minor issues - licences for some international teams and SH competitions are not available. This is understandable, licenses are very expensive - player models are a mixed bag, I suspect this is linked to licenses(player likeness) and/or development cost- Team/Player Rating system is off, the DEVS HAVE ADDRESSED THIS and are looking into it. This is due to their suppliers' system. Rugby fans who know of a certain supplier's database will probably agree that it's not accurate at all. - occasional odd bug where the controls will lock up after a scrum, player will make a tackle from 20 meters away, minor things that can be patched All in all, until the beta release I was on the fence about recommending this game. But with the fixes they're bringing through, this game is brilliant to play now and shows that the Devs are dedicated to bringing the game up to the standard fans are asking for. I'd probably say this is the best rugby game.you can buy right now

_childDocuments_.review: General consensus is that if you want to play a half decent rugby game prior to the release of Rugby 20, you needed to play games that are ten years old or so. Even the developers of this game made an awful rugby game (Rugby 18).This is not an awful rugby game.Is it a great rugby game? No. Licences are missing with no ability to edit your own teams (which would inevitably let you add people in). Half of the mechanics in the game are not intuitive and the tutorial does a poor job of letting you know exactly how they work. On Semi-Pro difficulty, your entire team are turnover kings, easily winning rucks from the opposition. That all being said, it does have more licences than PES ever had when it was first released, and some of the mechanics are really good. I've played this for two hours so far, a couple of times as my preferred teams and a couple of times as "MyTeam" which I'm sure I'd enjoy more if I actually understood how it all worked.Fifa 2020 is about £45, and this game is £30. It needs improvements for sure, but I think really for £30 if you're a rugby fan you should get this game. If you have no idea about how to play rugby and have just been interested, or you like sports team management sims, do not buy this game. It will either not explain literally anything to you including the rules of the game, or will not include the depth you want to see.

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, it's not bad at all!Given we haven't had a properly 'great' rugby game probably since Rugby 08, this isn't bad at all! Some slightly dodgy character models of famous players here and there but doesn't ruin anything, and although all the Southern Hemisphere national sides plus England and Super Rugby are missing, there's still a solid set of players and teams.Gameplay is ok, still very easy to whitewash the AI even on the maximum difficulty. Playing with your own squad through tournaments is great, even if I can't figure out how to change the name of the team though, and there's no options for setting Captain, kickers etc - seems to always be the fly half even if other players might usually kick. Some funniness with default team rosters having substitutes lined up oddly (e.g. scrum half at 16 not 21, hooker at 19 not 16 etc) but nothing that bad.Can tell the game is made by people that love the sport, great attention to detail with squad building, and tactical adjustment. _childDocuments_.review: This is the best rugby game available, with the worst tutorial ;) They just didn't explain how to attack.  You can adjust tactics in the menu though, and here's a quick primer:Start with "Classic" mode.  This is old school rugby where the skillful backs attack, and the big forwards stay out of the way.  If you played some schools rugby, or just played a while back (like me), this is what you're used to!  Tapping RS will do a side step and a long press a hand off.Then try a 2-4-2.  This means the big forwards do most of the early ball carrying.  2 are on one wing, 2 on the other with 4 in the middle.  Focus on using the group of four in the middle to get the ball moving upfield for a few phases, before spreading it wide.  For set plays, try giving your line more depth so you have more time to execute.1-3-3-1.  This is the hardest and unfortunately the default for a lot of teams.  Now you have 2 groups of 3 forwards to use in the middle of the field.  You can play the ball much faster b/c there is always a second pod available.  Once you've played a few phases, look for smaller backs hanging out behind the forwards.  Try passing the ball straight backwards to them by hitting both pass buttons before spreading the ball wide.  Pass chain 1-3-3-1, type B with diamond pod shapes works well.With the recent patches the game plays really well.  Still a few rough edges for sure and you'll want to turn the commentary off.Bottom line if you love rugby or want to learn the game, pick this up.

_childDocuments_.review: Mixed feelings on this one. I don't expect football level investment into a rugby game and the effort to add tactical nuance for the first time in a Rugby game is great but this is very rough around the edges and i'd go as far as to say unfinished in places. I'm OK with the lack of polish - god awful stock images, inconsistent and sometimes entirely missing player pictures, dated graphics corny music etc. - but there are a lot of bugs that i'm sure the devs must have known about:- Commentary isn't coded properly. They pick out the wrong players (sometimes ones not playing) or comment on things that haven't happened etc.  The worst example is that there doesn't seem to be commentary for a draw, the commentators just pick an arbitrary winner - There is no explanation of the controls or remapping. There are a handful of training tutorials but the set moves training doesn't work at all- You can't set a resolution over 1080p in game-your selected player will wander offside automatically unless you switch players quickly after the ruck- As far as I can tell, you can't name your team in solo mode - it's just "my team 1"- Sometimes the ball flies off at great speed in a random direction (usually as part of a line out)- I seem to have mysterious a enormous long number in the top right of my screen!?My biggest gripe is that we can't create our own competitions or teams to fill in the gaps from licenses. I understand not all license will be possible but when I can't create an England team, World Cup, European Cup or Six Nations, this becomes a hard one to recommend.The core gameplay here is good. Unfortunately the lack of polish/attention to detail is dragging it down. If there is continued development to iron out the kinks - this could be worth a look later.

_childDocuments_.review: I was hesitant to buy this after hearing and seeing the dismal attempts of the previous instalments. However this is much improved. I am lead to believe the devs are actually working on fixes and improvements. If that's the case then that's great because this game is full of potential...Some great bits, the game play feels rewarding to an extent, although this may be down to how challenging some aspects of the game are. For example actually scoring a try half the length of the pitch after stringing a few passes together is extremely rewarding. But, perhaps only because there seems to be a pass delay and off loading is actually 50/50. Conversions and pens are brilliant, scrums are challenging but a fun skill based concept exists. Line outs are great, although some delay tweaks needed. Tackling isn't amazing, but it works its simple and does the job well. Some bad bits, STAMINA depletes far to quickly, especially for a winger like Jonny May. i don't expect to see him running out of gas after a 20 meter sprint... There needs to be a control layout in settings so we can actually see what buttons do what. Took my a while to work out how to drop goal... Plus i've no idea how ball skills work. It seems a small chance that you actually side step or spin anyone! Let alone doing it intentionally. It seems ball skills only work with good timing, although no tutorial on this. Maybe the control scheme would be to look at how FIFA or Rugby challenge works and use the same model in giving us freedom. In league mode it seems a massive B**** ache to rotate the team after every game just to keep stamina levels up.Passing can be clunky, seems delayed. Hard to draw in players and pass due to the tackle animation stopping the pass chance. Opportunity to change kit before matches in league and solo need to be added!Player positioning in defence isn't ideal. The ai also doesn't make many tackles leaving you frantically changing players and mashing B.Also the opposing team make far to many high tackles quite often when you're on a break. Having said all that I have had fun! Although perhaps £30 is a bit much in its current state.. If you do buy it. Play the tutorials. It will give you a good feel for the mechanics of the game.

The commentators will say something when the entirely opposite thing is occurring, like "they've kicked the ball for possession behind the enemy line" when in reality I've booted the ball a mile out of the stadium because I want to end the half. Or, "he's definitely going to score here!" when I'm about 10 meters out with 3 players on top of the guy with the ball. Or, when missing a sideline conversion because it bounces off of the posts, the commentators say "he really should be getting those, that's a really basic kick"....uhhh is it? It just really ruins the ambience of the entire thing. However, you'd think it's something that would be relatively easy to sort out...right? So why haven't they done it yet? At least it's not like Rugby Challenge where I feel like they've gotten the entire mechanics for the players wrong. The mechanics....I'm not sure if I'm even using this word correctly, but the mechanics for this game are in my opinion....quite good. If you compare (which I am going to quite a lot) to the Rugby Challenge 'series' (said sarcastically because they're all basically the same game) the movement of the players and the way in which they pass the ball is somewhat satisfying and fluent, sure, it's not perfect, but it's way better than anything I've witnessed in the past 10 years of rugby games. The ONE THING that REALLY BUGS ME however, which is something that truly annoyed me in Rugby Challenge and I don't know why they seem to have done the same here, is the motion/way that they score tries. It's like...you've pressed 'A' to score, and then they take about 3 seconds to actually put it down, meanwhile they're doing some stupid Ashton-esque dive into the air (BTW DEVELOPERS LIKE 10% OF RUGBY PLAYERS WILL ACTUALLY ATTEMPT A SWAN DIVE OVER THE TRY LINE). It's not needed, just put the damn ball down, take a note out of Rugby 08, look at the ways in which they score, look how fluent it is, it's SATISFYING to score tries in Rugby 08 because they just put the ball down straight away and players behind them in motion don't catch up with the try scorer (which just looks utterly stupid) before he's actually put the ball down. However, this game above all its flaws, is fun. The lineouts are done really well, the scrummaging is good enough, the set piece and rucks are good in general I think. Something key for me, which Rugby Challenge failed to do, was giving the player the ability to build phases and not just whip it wide every time, because in this game it won't work. You genuinely have to build phases to suck the defence in, and it feels great when you've been knocking on the opposition try line phase after phase for you to finally sneak your winger in at the corner, it's satisfying. Another thing done really well for me is the kicking, both the restarts and kicking at goal feel relatively realistic, when you nail a touch line conversion, you feel as though you've earned those 2 points, whereas in other games (YEAH MAINLY RUGBY CHALLENGE), you could just bop over a touch line conversion as easily as you could in front of the posts. I've written enough and to summarise, I would recommend this game, mainly because I got it on ♥♥♥ for £16, mixed with the fact that it is a lot of fun AND MAINLY (I CANNOT STRESS THIS ENOUGH) THE DEVS ARE STILL BRINGING OUT UPDATES AND TAKING IN FEEDBACK AND CONTINUOUSLY BRINGING OUT PATCHES TO IMPROVE THE GAME.6/10 no where near perfect BUT....it has the potential to be the best rugby game in the past 10 years.

_childDocuments_.review: Been playing rugby games since EA Rugby 2004. In terms of game play, this game is the best ever. Why?Because it actually plays like a real rugby game. The minigames work very well for simulating the finer points of the sport that previous rugby games have lacked.As well, the tactical options the game presents are reflective of a real rugby match. Kicking is critically important as is putting players in to space and creating overlaps.I really credit the developers who seem to actually have an understanding of how rugby is actually played.What the game has in gameplay though, it lacks in features. The multiplayer system would be far better if there were actual rankings and it could use some additional licensing. Overall though, this is a great game system that should be built on and developed further.Some people will unfairly give this game a negative review, most likely because they don't actually understand how the sport of rugby is played or the tactics that actually allow you to win.  They are more than likely looking for an arcade experience where they can button mash their way to victory.  If that is the case, I suggest they look elsewhere.

This is by far the best rugby game made by Eko, and far, far better than previous rugby games made in this series like Rugby 15 and Rugby 18. I much prefer Rugby 20 to EA Sports Rugby 08. I played 08 myself and I very much disliked the gameplay, it is very outdated, and it is not very similar to modern day rugby (set plays etc). Not a lot of details have been put in to the lineouts, scrums (intentionally). Some prefer this however. I respect those who much prefer Rugby 08, however I just can't play it. I deleted it in fact, I found it boring and not very good. It will be great to have a new rugby game published by EA Sports. I don't know if it will happen though, as former, old EA Rugby games did not get a lot of sales back in the day, hence the lack of profit for the company. A new EA Sports Rugby game will have better graphics and better features overall I am sure, considering old rugby games published by EA.Although being a great rugby game, Rugby 20 has a few cons. Here are my improvements for the game, which could drastically make the game better and more enjoyable.  No, not all international teams are licensed. However, there are many licences on this game, including international teams.Yes.Yes, by far. _childDocuments_.review: Rugby 20, There are some great features at lot of people will have expanded on the points I will make. I hope the developers look at the feedback and do some updates. I think it's really hard to make a rugby game firstly, due to a lot of complex or dynamic phases in the game. Overall rugby 20 has done a good job, not the finished article by any means. ProsTactics, set plays love them the main thing I want is for backs to be backs and forwards to be forwards. So the moves you can do is a fantastic pro. The pod systems all tactics from real games and certainly much better than rugby challenge, where it feels much more like league, where players are interchangeable. Kicking different types of kicking freely avaliable, plus challenging. Lineouts, rucks and scrums are great take some time to learn and perfect, im still learning. Passing is mostly good, again some people already comment about passing in the tackle there is still a bit of a delay, making drawing the man a bit harder can allow the 2 on 1 situation to go wrong. But if you can pass b4 during and after the tackle it may become a bit too op for the attacker. Tackling is great great fun enough animations and different types. overall smooth game play. Decent commentary not necessarily fluid and a few mistakes with players here and there. Scored a try with 12trees and it said atkinson. Improvements tutorials probably a few more needed, or better explanations, Lineout tutorial was one that sticks out that wasn't obvious initially. Nor how you aim the ball in the goal kick.  set plays and other little bits, that I struggled in my first game to do. Have yet to explore solo or my squad much, but certainly a proper career (league, internation, europe, transfers) or solo player mode fifa esq would be great and if you did a dlc i would buy it.  really hope you update the squads, missing some key 2020 players, and their points/overall like rees zammit isnt 51 and is speed is much higher than 71. SUPER RUGBY the best league in the world and im european, i guess due to licensing but missing super rugby is such a shame, and a disappointment again if later adding a dlc of super rugby I would buy. graphics are decent as anyother sports game, some players look great some look knock off e.g. cips is a hairy beast. Running/ speedsters: my wingers should be outpacing in one on ones, yet they get caught by forwards. Skills are quite hard to use, and cant use when sprinting. Pods/crash ball: not great usually go backwards, and players struggle to get over the gain line, need a break tackle button or something. I think this could be improved, but equally this is a balance the defence needs a chance and you dont want a break tackle then he is through all the time. but more he gets a bit further forward than the previous ruck. this leads tois kicking too op or becomes too op, territory is important and it that sense this game fits rugby perfectly and i really like it for that, pressured on your 22 kicking is the option like it is in real life but you can kick successfully almost up to their 22/5m line seems a lil wrong. Ultimate team esq, in game purchases money etc just not a fan off. passing already covered. Kicking goal kicking hard to direct but suppose get the hang of it. This game has a lot of potential, and is certainly enjoyable certainly beats rugby challenge so far. If they added content with dlcs or just in updates I would be keen and would buy. Some tweaks and things to work or to play around with to see what works.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, it's a rugby game. If you like rugby, it's your only choice, and so I recommend it. It plays like rugby if you try to make it play like rugby.Downsides: (Not going to name them all, it's too much)Too easy (Can beat the all blacks with my 70 overall team on hardest difficulty "pro" Only 3 difficulties)Settings don't stick (Sometimes I'll play a game and realize it's super easy, then check settings and notice that since last game it turned from pro to semi-pro despite always winning)Set plays are awkward and slow, end up working only because they're programmed to work on the cpu sometimes.LIneouts are, as far as I can tell, a simple minigame followed by button mashing. I win against the throw more often than not on the hardest difficulty.It's also really easy to win scrums against the head on proKicking a ball that's already on the ground works like 10% of the times, mashing the button, pressing it right when the prompt comes up, doesn't matter, it almost never works.Crashes a decent amountNo rolling mauls, just button mashing games that almost always result in the same yardage gainIf you play aerial ping pong, eventually the opp team fullback or wing or whoever received your kick will just kick it out on the full even if they're not behind the 22, or otherwise kick a big lateral kick to a teammate that you can just wait on and get a turnover in the ruck.Rucks are pretty good though. Best ruck mechanics I've seen, though jackaling really only ever wins you possession, you never really get a "not releasing" call or anything, which would have been cool.

name: Subnautica: Below Zero
detailed_description: Below Zero is an underwater adventure game set on an alien ocean world. It is the next chapter in the Subnautica universe and is developed by Unknown Worlds. Return to planet 4546B Submerge yourself in an all-new, sub-zero expedition in an arctic region of Planet 4546B. Arriving with little more than your wits and some survival equipment, you set out to investigate what happened to your sister... Uncover the truth Alterra left in a hurry after a mysterious incident. Abandoned research stations dot the region. What happened to the scientists who lived and worked here? Logs, items, and databanks scattered among the debris paint a new picture of the incident. With limited resources, you must improvise to survive on your own. Discover uncharted biomes Swim beneath the blue-lit, arching expanses of Twisty Bridges. Become mesmerized by the glittering, mammoth crystals of the Crystal Caverns. Clamber up snow covered peaks and venture into the icy caves of Glacial Basin. Maneuver between erupting Thermal Vents to discover ancient alien artifacts. Below Zero presents entirely new environments for you to survive, study, and explore. Construct habitats and vehicles Survive the harsh climate by constructing extensive habitats, scavenging for resources, and crafting equipment. Blast across the snowy tundra on a Snowfox hoverbike. Cruise through enchanting and perilous biomes in your modular Seatruck. Research alien lifeforms Something undiscovered lurks around every corner. Swim through the giant Titan Holefish, encounter the haunting Shadow Leviathan, and visit the adorable Pengwings. Keep your wits about you. Not all creatures in this strange world are friendly. Survive the chilly temperatures Jump in, the water’s warm. The below zero temperatures of this arctic region pose a new threat. New weather conditions blanket above-ground habitats. Craft a toasty cold suit, sip on piping hot coffee, and warm up next to Thermal Lilies to stave off the chill. An ocean of intrigue What really happened to your sister? Who were the aliens who came here before? Why were they on this planet? Can we find solace from grief in truth? Below Zero extends the story of the Subnautica universe, diving deep into the mystery introduced in the original game. About the development team Below Zero is created by Unknown Worlds, a small studio that traces its roots back to the 2002 Half-Life mod Natural Selection. It is the same studio that created the original Subnautica. The team is scattered around the globe, from the United States to the United Kingdom, France, Russia, Austria, Australia, Canada, and many more places. Warning This game contains flashing lights that may make it unsuitable for people with photosensitive epilepsy or other photosensitive conditions. Player discretion is advised.

_childDocuments_.review: When playing this games predecessor, I didn't have to constantly read guides, walkthroughs and reddit threads just to find out what I'm supposed to be doing, where I'm supposed to be going, where I am, and where do I find pretty much every material I need. I constantly felt lost with the confusing layout of the environments especially Delta Island. It took me 20 mins to get to the summit because it's so loopy. This game is direction-less, poorly mapped, frustrating and confusing more often than it is fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Subnautica Below Zero is a fantastic game. It would be a perfect masterpiece, if it's predecessor didn't exist.But first off, Below Zero is nonetheless a great addition to the lore of Planet 4546B. It shows a completely different region and shows just how beautifully crafted this world is. New Creatures, related to some Fish of the tropics, Plant life you think you know, but still differs ever so slightly. The map design is beautiful, each and every biome is a sight for sore eye. (This will come back to bite tho.) The game has an amazing soundtrack which definitely exceeds the one from the first game but this is also a bit of a critique as I personally feel the tracks are a bit too persistent. For example in a biome of crystal caves the soundtrack is blasting your ears nonstop which really hurts the atmosphere. If you compare it to the Lost River of Subnautica for example, the soundtrack for that biome plays every now and then but mostly, the ambience is what fills you with immersion. Absolute Perfection. This game sadly did suffer a bit because of it's otherwise amazing soundtrack.The story of this game is neat. It's a good main storyline with some really forgettable sideplots. I don't remember anything about the Sister's subplot but the main storyline is really cool and gets a lot deeper into the cosmic aspect of Subnautica's general story which I really like. The characters are sympathetic and interesting, especially the main two. Their dynamic is really fun.This game is a lot more story driven than Subnautica which yes, is a rather negative point in comparison of the two games but honestly, it's just cool. I don't really mind it. Now we get into the territory of the negative.The map is sadly way too small. It is really beautiful and I admire the effort put into designing all of it. But it's really small and you'll get the feeling of having seen everything very quickly basically. The beautifully designed biomes are beautiful yes but that is not what the ocean is as a whole. It has it's beautiful sceneries, but it also has dunes of nothing. Subnautica excelled at that. Below Zero not so much. And another sad part about it, most of the really wonderful and interesting places just feel very... "unnecessary". This game was very enthusiastic about featuring a lot more land than the first one. But you honestly only go there for the story a few times and you have no reason to go there otherwise really. A lot of materials and ressources just feel like they have no purpose. Kyanite which was essential for survival in the endgame of Subnautica was basically just there to be there. The jellyfish biome was really cool. But you only go there for one ressource and just go back not exploring it any further. Because you have no reason to. There is nothing there except marvelous design.This game is 100% a downgrade from the first. Is it still worth checking out?Absolutely. It's a wonderful addition to the lore of Subnautica and I loved my time playing it.If you loved Subnautica, you'll like Below Zero.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is based on 100% completion and 32.9 hours of gameplay.Would I recommend the game? Yes, this is a decent game, but it is a step back from the original Subnautica in every way, in my opinion, so if you haven't played it yet, I recommend doing so first because it's a much more amazing experience and develops the world of Subnautica amazingly.As was previously said, the game is still decent and includes many of the same features as the first, such as base building, resource gathering, and exploration, but the atmosphere is noticeably lacking in comparison to the first. There are some cool things in this game, but they are not more than that; they are simply cool. While this game will keep you entertained for a few hours, I would wait until there is a good sale before purchasing it.    For people with  this may not be a game for you. There are large, deep bodies of water, and the atmosphere the game creates may be too much, so please do your own research before buying.All achievements can be completed in a single playthrough; simply ensure that you have almost all of them before finishing the game. Almost all of the achievements are story-related, so simply playing the game and finishing the story will earn you the majority of the achievements. And the remaining few miscellaneous achievements are very simple to obtain. You should have no problems with the achievements in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: (No spoilers) Below Zero falls within that curious case of being too short be a true full length game, but long enough to not be able to be considered DLC. Does that take away from the experience? No, it doesn't. Much. This game still produces a great open world with many interesting ideas, removing a few from the original and replacing them. A few of these design choices I can understand, but the fact that they removed the stasis rifle is a bit disappointing. The campaign took me 30ish hours doing just about everything there is to offer. The isolation and vast emptiness that was portrayed in the original is crushed by a few factors in this iteration, such as the fact the protagonist is ALWAYS talking to either herself or the other main character. It's a much more kid friendly version due to its more lighthearted nature, but is still very enjoyable nonetheless. VERDICT: Below Zero is more Subnautica, and how can you go wrong with that? The gripes I have with this game are only what I've stated, and other than those, the game is still one of my favorites this year and I'm so happy the devs decided to put it out there. 8/10

Recommend to anyone who enjoyed the original. I do think it takes some steps backwards though...After doing an early run of the game I was excited to play on release and experience the newly written story. Unfortunately, I enjoyed the first iteration way more and knowing that soured the story for me for my full run.  Also, I know they had updates between alpha and release but honestly I didn't notice anything different other than the story beats. Fantastic game and just a few things that keep it from being a perfect sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: If you loved Subnautica, you will like Subnautica: Below Zero.I must preface this with a fact: Subnautica is one of my favorite games I've played in the past five years. It contains everything I enjoy about survival games, while also blending in elements of marine biology and sci-fi. Somewhere in the endless fabric of time, I created Subnautica so that my present self could enjoy it today.The dialogue was fine. I haven't seen many reviews, but I can imagine many gamers probably hate the dialogue in this game. At times, it seems forced, but honestly, I didn’t really mind. Some might say it was cringey, but I scoff at that idea.The quality of life improvements with the Prawn suit were amazing. Going from Subnautica to Below Zero, interacting with the Prawn Suit is night and day—you get in and out almost instantly. When I inevitably return to Subnautica, I suspect I will miss these enhancements from Below Zero.Leviathans were okay. Subnautica still has the most iconic leviathans, but Below Zero doesn’t hold back either. The Shadow Leviathan and Ventgardens are awesome, especially since they are designed with their biomes in mind. The Shadow Leviathan, resembling a centipede, fits through the tight spaces of the Crystal Caves, which enhances the challenge. The other leviathans, however, were less remarkable.The giant jellyfish tree, aka Ventgardens, was a true spectacle the first time I saw it. Discovering that you could enter them to gather resources blew me away. Unknown Worlds Entertainment must have some insanely passionate biologists on their team because they consistently excel at creating intriguing creatures.The Crystal Cave was a phenomenal biome. It’s not only a beautiful biome, but the progression from purple to red crystals as you go deeper is great. The Shadow Leviathan really makes this biome terrifying to navigate. In my first playthrough, these creatures constantly chased me from 600 meters to 950. I always had at least one near me, heightening the tension compared to the end-game biome of Subnautica.The Sea Monkeys were a creature that kept on giving. Not only adorable, they also gifted you items and their nests contained important blueprints. Being able to visually identify the blueprints in the Sea Monkey nests was a godsend improvement.Al-an was cool. I really enjoyed the lore dumps from him (I’m not kidding). It was interesting to get more context about the Kharaa Bacterium and to learn at the end that he was the reason it escaped in the first place. The sequence where you finally build his body and travel off of Planet 4546B, presumably to his home planet, left me wanting more.Marguerit Maida was the second most memorable character, right next to Al-an. If other crew members had survived and been given a body to their voices, perhaps there would have been more impact. But Marguerit is a stone-cold badass, and the first time you enter her base and see the huge reaper leviathan head on her wall, you just KNOW she’s built different. I also have to mention her custom Prawn Suit and how much I wish we, as players, could do what she did with hers. Maybe in the future.Flora and fauna were obviously amazing—100% blew it out of the park. This is the selling point of every Subnautica game. If they lose sight of that, I think the series will die off. Creating whimsical, yet believable flora and fauna from an alien planet goes hand in hand with Subnautica. Some of my favorites were the Ventgardens, Shadow Leviathans, Sea Monkeys, Lily Paddler, Spinner Fish, Eye Jelly, Grand Cotton Anemone, and Thermal Lily.If you loved Subnautica like I do, then you will enjoy Below Zero. It still hits many of the same notes that made Subnautica so enjoyable, although not as many as you might expect.The majority of the land-based gameplay. I’m just not interested in the cold mechanics and traversing the glacial tundra, especially at night. When I think of Subnautica, I think OCEAN, not jogging around a giant glacier.The Snowfox was a buggy mess. I learned about the Snowfox, gathered all resources for the Snowfox hoverpad and the Snowfox itself, went back to base and built it all. Finally going back to the arctic spires and using the Snowfox, it fell through the floor. I kid you not, this happened three more times throughout my playthrough. The first time, I literally quit the game for a month because I just didn't want to deal with the hassle. The controls for the Snowfox were strange, clunky, and weird. Having this constant worry that unpacking my Snowfox might cause it to glitch through the ground and force me to go back home and make another was just exhausting.The giant glacier was extremely confusing to traverse (maybe a skill issue). The Arctic Spires and Glacial Bay were extremely confusing for me to navigate. I often got lost, to the point where I just looked up where the key pieces were and went there directly instead of circling around the island another ten times.For me, the reason why Subnautica: Below Zero doesn’t live up to Subnautica is because of the heavy reliance on land-based gameplay. If they focused more on ocean-related stuff and less on land, I guarantee this game would be better. But I do respect them for branching out and trying something new; I find that to be a refreshing quality of this game.The Seatruck. Throughout my whole playthrough, I wrestled with the fact that we don’t have a Cyclops anymore. I loved the Cyclops—it was such a cool and giant ship, essentially a moving base. The Seatruck is their evolution of that, but I am unsure if it actually is an evolution or a devolution. The modules that the Seatruck supports are epic. Being able to customize it however you want and put whatever modules you need is great. My setup was the Fabricator, storage, teleport, and docking module. But I still can't shake off the fact that the Cyclops was just so cool. I am all for having more customization, but I want my Cyclops back.Having a protagonist that talks. A character with a backstory and a purpose for coming to Planet 4546B is good, right? Well, I don’t know. For me personally, unless the character has a genuinely compelling story that can be told, having a faceless, mute protagonist is much more fun. I like being able to transport myself into the world and experience it like I am really there. Having a character just makes it feel a little less immersive, and a little more divisive. It was an alright choice, and obviously necessary for the interactions between Al-an and Marguerit and everything else to happen, but I’m still unsure about it.Subnautica: Below Zero is a good game. If you loved Subnautica, you will like Below Zero. There will be moments when you love the game and think, "Man, give me more of that!" Then those moments will swiftly end, and you will be met with ham-fisted mechanics that don't really fit into the game you know and love. Ultimately, I respect Unknown Worlds Entertainment for trying something different with their game. Even if it doesn't land properly, they at least have the balls to innovate or die trying.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to cry.I loved the first Subnautica.  It was the ocean exploration game I'd always dreamed of.  The creatures were beautiful in sound and in design.  The story unfolded through your exploration.  The world felt so big and alive.  It was an immersive (lol) experience near perfection, especially for an aquatic science nerd like me.Then they decided to make Below Zero.  And somehow - either through incompetence or spite, because there's no way this was done through ignorance - they took everything that people loved and replaced it with the parts that people hated.Namely, the biggest change: instead of exploration driving the story, story drives the exploration.  This sounds great on paper, but is terrible in execution.  Mainly because the game utilizes Forspoken-style dialogue long before Forspoken made it noticeable.  You know the reveal in Subnautica when ?  How the player is given that much information and then gives them time to realize the situation?  If it were this game's writers,   That's the game.   don't get to decide how you feel about the situation you are in.  The game will tell you what you need to feel.  It will tell you where to go next.  And it will rip you out of your immersion every time.  Creature design is a step down.  They don't look or act like beings adapted to their environment, as the critters in the first game did.  They look and act like beings adapted to be in a videogame.  The predators have looks and sounds that demand the audience be scared of them.  Its the same effect as a man in costume chasing you in a haunted house screaming "OOGA BOOGA BOOGA."  The Leviathans don't deliver the same awe or terror as the ones in the first game; again, the designs try to hard to be spooky.  Honestly, the only design I encountered that I liked were the sea monkeys.  And even then, they're overanimated to the point of parody.  The only thing this game did better than the first was base building options.  You can build a huge underwater house with rooms, rather than a bunch of circular modules.  These options lead to a much more homier base that looks more refined.  But they added a lot of that back to Subnautica, so there is really absolutely no reason to get this game.If I sound unusually harsh, its because this is a franchise I care about.  I bought this game day one of Early Access.  I remember when Robin was a researcher sending samples to her sister Sam up on a satellite , and when  was a prick who warmed up to life .  It was cozy and a great base line for an unfolding story set in a growing frozen world.  It was all about research and exploration, just like what I wanted.  And they THREW IT ALL OUT THE WINDOW BECAUSE I DONT KNOW.  I genuinely do NOT know what they were going for.  And the final result is such an obnoxious, hand-holdy, unimmersive experience.Here's hoping the true Subnautica 2 will be a return to form.  I shudder to think of the result if they decide to do the whole "throw out the parts people liked and buckle down on what they didnt" cycle again.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna start this review by fully admitting that I have my problems with this game. Yes I absolutely still recommend it, but I feel it's only fair to start with my problems and then talk about what I like.I will admit I'm a little sad this game isn't as unsettling as the original Subnautica. Subnautica was really good at building a tense, unsettling or even downright frightening atmosphere, and that is almost non-existent in Below Zero. I can also get a bit frustrated at times running back and forth to places over and over again, but after a few playthroughs/with some foresight you learn to pick things up ahead of time, so I suppose that's technically a matter of experience/patience. I'm almost hesitant to admit this, but I'll go ahead and say it: the fact that leviathans can't grab you or attack your seatruck so long as you are standing in it by having at least one module attached is absolutely busted. I'm very nearly fearless charging into areas with leviathans in them knowing full well that if I pay attention they basically can't hurt me. Even in the end game, where you would expect your prawn suit to be a necessity, you can get by perfectly smoothly with your seatruck so long as there's at least one module on it. I HATE the ice worm section of the game. I think it was completely unnecessary to have such an obnoxious enemy in here. The fact that the worm can force you to dismount your snowfox when you're literally nowhere near it so they can try to force you to use the thumpers is ridiculous. I will openly admit to having cheated once or twice just to get through that section faster. I genuinely cannot stand it. The other thing is the story feeling a bit rushed at the end, but I fully understand why/what happened with the writing team, so I feel it's unfair to be harsh about that. I will say that it feels like the plot with Sam ended incredibly abruptly even WITH the story changes. I really expected her to have been murdered by Alterra in secret, not for her to have genuinely made a mistake, especially with how much other characters kept hyping up how careful and calculated she usually was. Oh well. On to the good! I enjoy the gameplay more in this game overall than I do in base Subnautica, even if it can get repetitive going to the same place over and over. It feels good when things line up and you can do one task after another, and things feel overall a bit smoother in this game when it all comes together. I also appreciate how pretty the game is, again with everything feeling a bit smoother and more polished than in OG Subnautica. It's nice to sit back and take in the sights every now and then, even if I feel there aren't as many pretty biomes in Below Zero. I really liked what they did with Marguerite in this game, it was fun to check in with her and see how she was making a life for herself the best she could after everything that happened. I took a liking to her almost immediately, and was glad to see her hanging around.!!! SPOILER WARNING FOR THIS PART! DO NOT READ THIS SECTION IF YOU DO NOT WANT SPOILERS !!!I adore our new friend Al-An. Their relationship with Robin is easily my favorite part of the game. I love hearing them talk to each other, and listening to Al-An explain their point of view on things. Their conversation about how it feels to be connected to the network always strikes me as deeply lonely and sad. I also appreciate that (while Al-An may have been cranky and rude in pre-release versions) our Al-An is curious and overall courteous, usually only being blunt in their questioning due to a genuine desire to understand. Trading information openly and honestly is the fastest way to learn, and I feel it's more realistic for them to be genuine than mean if they want to learn new things. I won't spoil the whole ending just in case someone read this and didn't heed the spoiler warning, but I will just say that the details and emotions put in to the performance of the big reveal with Al-An always leaves me a bit emotional myself. As I said, Al-An and Robin are easily my favorite part of this game, and it's a big part of the reason I recommend it. tl;dr while I have my gripes with the atmosphere/repetitiveness/certain story bits, it is outweighed by my overall appreciation for the gameplay/aesthetic/friendship between Robin and Al-An. I would definitely recommend this game to someone looking for a unique and fun survival game with an interesting enough story and wonderful character moments. But you'll probably want to play the OG Subnautica first, to make sure you have full context for the big reveal at the end of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The current direction doesn't cut it for me.While I wished for some actual npc conversations in the original, the voiced protagonist and support character doesn't do anything for me. It's the old debate about inconvenience being a valid way of adding difficulty.Edit: I don't care if it's Early Access, Pre-Early Access or Pre-Alpha-Early Access. _childDocuments_.review: This is a "Yes, but..." kind of review.  The core gameplay loop is solid, the extra stuff for bases was nice.  The overall story was interesting.  Having a more developed land side of things was pretty neat, and temperature gave being out of the water a fun sense of urgency.BUT.  The last three hours were frustration upon frustration upon frustrated cursing.  I had trouble finding the arctic spires fragment, then I got zero hints as to where the fabricator would be, eventually resorting to a quick peek at the zone it was in and where to find said zone.  The crystal caves ate an hour of my time and required a full youtube video to find - maybe have the crystal hue go redder the closer it is to the entrance?I went down in the Prawn suit, prior experience from Subnautica indicating parking outside the final structure is a terrible idea.  There's an invisible wall stopping you taking it inside the facility before getting out.  Parking outside the facility is a terrible idea, there was no Prawn suit where I left it.  So I ended the game by deathwarping back to my base and jaunting over to the teleporter.The final sequence was nice eye candy, but the choice of where to go hadn't been telegraphed at all up to that point, and there was some other dialogue that suggested inter-character development that just hadn't occurred.  The sister story arc had a similar feel that I was missing large chunks of something too.It was fun, I felt I got my money's worth, but I don't feel any sense of closure with any of the story arcs.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanna start by saying that i played and finished both Subnautica and Subnautica BZ and the first one is one of my favorites if not my favorite single player game, so i was really excited about BZ but now that i'm done i feel like it was a 'meh' experience and i'll explain why.-----------------------------------------•  The thing that any Subnautica player remembers is the fear of going deeper. Exploration felt insanely unsafe and life-threatening, which built up anxiety and kept you on the edge of your seat up until you were back safe in your base. The most anxious or scared i felt in BZ was because of anticipation. I thought that if Reaper Leviathans were one of the first threats you found in the first game, you'd have to bump into something similarly scary here as well, but that moment never happened (at all). Once you learn what the threats are, it feels underwhelmingly safe to explore.• , which is far less than before. In order to finish the first game, you had to go as deep as 1500m or so, you had to fight or elude huge threats and risk losing everything you had, including your submarine, which at that point was your secondary base. Here, you go near 900m deep once and that's it, there's no huge threats, only Shadow Leviathans, which you can scare off with your perimeter defense and that's it.•  In Subnautica, the reapers were one of the first and scariest creatures to find in early game, but then you'd run into crabsquids and warpers and even bigger and scarier leviathans, but in BZ, all the "scary creatures" look like different types of sharks and there's only one type of "big scary leviathan" which is still not as scary as the reapers. Then you have ground threats, which you don't have to face more than once or twice and you can just outrun honestly.•  Your character talks a lot, there's another human on the planet as well, and then you have the company of AL-AN, commenting on everything you do. It used to feel like you were completely alone on this planet, surrounded by hostile creatures, but now you are not truly alone and creatures are not that bad. Your character also has a personal mission (so she went there willingly), finding out what happened to her sister, which imo gets overshadowed by AL-AN's mission.•  They replaced the seamoth for the seatruck, and instead of having a submarine, you have seatruck modules that you can attach to your seatruck, which allows you to have more storage room and a fabricator and some other stuff, but you don't actually need any of those to finish the game, same as the prawnsuit, i don't know if it was necessary in the first game but i do remember using it to get into complicated spots for rare minerals, here? i didn't even build it.•  I don't know if it's actually smaller or if it's because of all the ground areas and the icebergs but there's far less to explore and you end up going to the same places over and over again.-----------------------------------------There's still a lot to like about this game, like the addition of new friendly creatures such as sea monkeys and penglings & new cool biomes. The fact that they kept most of the og recipes which made building things and looking for basic resources easier for people that played the first game. And most of all, you get closure when it comes to the first game's story.The art and design are amazing, the gameplay is still good, the cinematics and animation are great, even the game trailers got better. The game on it's own is not bad, but the first one was really really good and it makes this one feel rushed. I still enjoyed playing it and getting to see what's new, but this could've been a DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: A conditional Thumbs Up -- The game is fun, but at a few places it can be extremely infuriating to play. The map in places is janky af, you can get stuck or get out of bounds, some caverns underwater are too small and can be hard to explore. Large parts of the tech tree seem unnecessary or obsolete, it's fine if you have them, it's also fine if you skip them. The story is rather okay, albeit somewhat limited, it was probably made that way to keep the playtime below ~30hrs. There are a few moments when you kinda have to google what to do because it's not at all obvious how to reach certain artefacts. The game should have made that more clear through logs or other pointers. The weather on the surface is annoying af. They've really missed the mark with that one. Most of the time you get either rain, fog or dangerous weather, you rarely get sun. And on top of that, "dangerous weather" isn't really dangerous, it's just annoying and it reduces visibility. This makes the game extremely irritating to play when you have to find the last part of the Alan's body with the worms jumping all around you; I had to turn off the weather in order to do this. Overall, it's a fun game, its performance is great, and it doesn't have a lot of bugs, but some of its problems strongly detract from the gameplay. Hopefully they will get addressed in a future update.

_childDocuments_.review: While I did enjoy the game for all the beauty and the horrors it had at precisely the right times for them it did feel like I was feeling a little disappointed overall. _childDocuments_.review: Review will contain minor spoilers.It's tough to review this game when you can just give a thumbs up or down. Ultimately, you can see where I landed- I think this game is competently made and well put together. However, I can't deny that the sum of its parts is less than Subnautica 1.This game has a much tighter focus on plot, which I appreciate- but it doesn't quite stick the landing. The game is much smaller than the original. The biomes are smaller, the threats are smaller, the tech tree progresses at breakneck speed. Unfortunately, this means that the plot doesn't really have the time or space to develop its characters much. Your protagonist, Robin, has a backstory and motivations which are clear but never particularly relevant to the plot besides telling you why she's on the planet. I don't feel like the game took advantage of the opportunity it had to expand on the Subnautica universe- we get told in the broadest, most general terms that Alterra is evil, but they don't give them any teeth. They never feel particularly threatening- all of their evil deeds are done offscreen, all of their facilities save a single satellite transmission tower are in ruins. Why should I care about what they were maybe trying to do at some point in the past, but demonstrably failed? They should be more of a clear and present danger here.You also get an alien companion who lives in your brain. I was really excited about this at first- we get to find out more about the architects! But you don't, like, get to chat with him. He doesn't comment on things you do as you explore, or places you visit besides a few scripted architect base locations, and those are mostly just "you're getting close to a base". It was a serious missed opportunity to both trickle out interesting lore for people who care about that, and to just get us to care about this pivotal plot character. Boggles my mind there isn't more idle chat here to fill the exploration time. It feels like you get an alien downloaded into your brain and then you can just kinda forget about it for hours and hours at a time. (Marguerit is a gem, though, and I wish she was in a lot more of the game than she is- she makes a very few, very scant appearances)That said, due to the smaller biomes, there is a lot less time spent exploring in this game than the previous. Smaller doesn't mean worse, to be clear- but I do think they didn't quite strike the balance here. I could not, for the life of me, find a place to put my base that felt convenient- everywhere felt equally like it was either inconvenient or already occupied, due to the smaller scale of the world.I agree with everyone about the Seatruck being a very poor substitute for the Cyclops and Seamoth. A modular vehicle sounds amazing on paper- but not when it's incredibly frustrating to drive, and when the modules are all so underwhelming.Ultimately, this still plays like Subnautica, and Subnautica is good as hell- it's a good game. But it's a sequel that tried to experiment with the formula of the first game and, to my mind, wasn't bold or clear-eyed enough to QUITE make it work. Maybe this had something ot do with the story getting rewritten entirely halfway thoguh- perhaps there was a budget or time crunch on getting the new story complete, I'm not sure- but there's still plenty of promise here, and it's still worth a play if you liked the first one.

_childDocuments_.review: Once again, Unknown Worlds delivered an enthralling gaming experience. Like the original Subnautica, Subnautica: Below Zero leaves you stranded and left to your own devices. You have complete freedom to explore whatever you want, design a most impressive base, focus on the story, or a little bit of each. Despite being more story driven and a little more objective-oriented, this game still gives you the freedom to explore and overcome obstacles in your own way. It’s very likely you and your best friend will have approached a task in VERY different way. There’s also several quality of life improvements made in this game when it comes to crafting and exploration. The game is gorgeous with slightly longer draw distances and improved textures and lighting. Though veterans of the series will, by default, not experience the same level of foreboding as they did in the first game, BZ will still manage to scare you from time to time!Despite BZ’s quality of life improvements, streamlining, and overall polish, I still find myself preferring the original. This sequel still has several fatal glitches that force you to use the debug console to fix, resulting in making your game file ineligible for Achievements. I had a piece of equipment somehow transport from right in front of me to INSIDE AN ICEBERG half a kilometer away. I got stuck inside my vehicle several times and couldn’t move it or my avatar. Fatal glitches like these that were excusable in the first game become an annoyance for a sequel using the same engine. I also prefered the way the story was delivered in the first one. Start with nothing more than, “well, you crash landed. Here are the blueprints to a scanner. Go nuts.” And before long, you end up realizing your part of a much bigger picture. In the sequel, a lot of that bigger-picture narrative is just told to your character at predetermined points in the game. Not a detriment. I just personally prefer the former. My one real complaint is the map and design of the biomes from this game. I feel I might have spent more time on land than in water. Because of the way objectives were handled, I spent less time aimlessly exploring and more time focusing on getting to an objective, and then coming back to base. I left one biome completely unexplored and two or three barely explored. This was mostly due to those biomes being very uninteresting to look at. They were mostly just space between me and my objective rather than a place I wanted to dive into. But the biomes is did like, they really nailed!All in all, this game is a lot of fun and a worthy sequel to Subnautica. It’s not without its shortcomings. But what games are? It very much still *feels* like Subnautica, and fans of the first game will definitely uncover some things in this one that will make them smile. The team at Unknown Worlds have really created a very special universe with these games. Play them both. A lot of fun!
