_childDocuments_.review: I really tried to get into Below Zero. I love the original game and was extremely excited to get back into the terrifying depths. However, Below Zero just doesn't live up to it's predecessor. The original Subnautica created an amazing atmosphere of isolation and fear, while also being funny and engaging. Most of all, it was fun to explore. I can't say the same for Below Zero.The voice acting is fine, but really takes away from that feeling of isolation. The story is... There. However it seems forced, like they had a couple directions they could go and just couldn't stick to one. The map is also smaller, which is unfortunate. It does have some AMAZING creature and biome design. I love the various critters and places, and each feels unique and well thought out. Overall this is by far the strongest aspect of the game. The exploration aspect of the game however is severely hampered for me by the new vehicle: the Seatruck. Ohh how I loathe it. It drives like the Seamoth's overweight cousin, a problem that is only exacerbated by adding on various modules, which is supposed to improve your experience right? Nope. Each new added module makes the truck slower and more difficult to maneuver. It's a frustrating and overall, joyless experience to drive. Spoiler ahead regarding vehicle progression:  I don't know who was making some of this games design choices, but they have some explaining to do. It's so sad to see them take what seems like a big step backward. I like several things about this game, but almost everything was done better by the first. While it does have some cool unique touches, I just cant get over how they completely dropped the ball on one of the main aspects of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is stupidly underated.First off, i see everyone's points. It doesn't live up to subnautica which is kinda sad, but you know what? I think its a much different experience. Contrary to subnautica, this game has a lot of story, which i can see why drives some people away. The original was kinda a sandbox game where you only had one goal; survive and get off the planet. But i think the reason why people don't like this one, is because so different. I think its very nostalgia fueled. I for one got both games at the same time. I had already seen a letsplay on the original (which i kinda regret) and wanted to try it out. Then i discovered this sequel. I bought it asap and luckily it was on sale. I enjoyed (mostly) it all. I think its very beautiful. I want to say that i had a much different experience with it than most others. For one i was exploring in the early game and didnt know what i was doing. So i was swimming on the surface of the water because that feels more comforting. And then i look down in the water, and saw the silhouette of a chelicerate. That sold me on the game. I was so fascinated by something that was a complete coincidence. I will also say that the base building in the game is much better. For one you can put alot more decorations in your base, and the large room and control room are great additions. I also think the prawn suit feels much better to use. Am i rambling? yeah... _childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to enjoy Below Zero. It has so much going for it; great gameplay, a breathtaking world that you can get lost in, but it feels a little empty. If you're looking for a Subnautica 2, look somewhere else. The gameplay features and world are there, but it still feels very different from the original. My main problem with this game was the story. It felt bland. In my opinion, the characters are not very likable, and the two warring storylines makes both feel underdeveloped.A lot of people have talked about how the arctic gameplay isn't really there. I have to agree. Movement feels clunky, and there are much more land-based survival games that do it better. I have done two playthroughs of this game, one during Early Access and one after release. In the first, I used the snowfox extensively to explore the arctic wilderness (which is what you're meant to do). But in the second playthorugh, I gave up and just used the prawn suit. I explored the area pretty late in the game, I had access to some nice things like the prawn grappling arm. , and the prawn suit coupled with the grappling arm means you actually move faster and more effectively than the snowfox. The seatruck is clunky and slow and hard to maneuver. The idea of a modular submarine is really cool, but for whatever reason, it doesn't really work here. I just found myself using the prawn suit for everything, which was the only vehicle from the original that made it in here. Now I want to talk about the good. The biomes and world is absolutely stunning. The bizarreness of the world (which made the original so interesting), made it in here, better. The colors are more vibrant, and it is way more visually pleasing (simply due to the fact that this game was released later). The leviathans aren't as scary, but that may be because I'm used to them from the original. Basebuilding also got an upgrade too. I found it very fun to build a massive base, as collecting materials isn't that much of a chore as the original. Though I didn't like many of the main characters, the PDAs detailing the story of 4546b are wonderfully put together. Some of the characters are very well written and voice acted, which was a scarce thing in the original.I know that towards the beginning, I said a lot of things that I didn't like about Below Zero. Compared to the original, yes, I didn't enjoy it as much as I wanted to. But considering the fact that it is the one of very few underwater survival games, the others don't come close to this quality. Overall, a well put together game that had some major flaws that tired me out towards the end of my playthrough. If you really enjoyed the original, get this game. If you didn't really like it, you won't get anything new out of this one.

It doesn't mean that its bad - its just the almost the same thing. Pretty much the only notable difference are  one new vehicle, the map and the story of course. Oh yeah, and also a temperature meter I guess, but its basically only works on land anyway which is like 15% of the game. The game felt a bit shorter and the map felt smaller, but maybe it is because I've already played first Subnautica and some stuff is the same. Also the map is a bit more vertical than the first one, so maybe it compensates in that regard. Honestly, I am a bit disappointed, not because the game is bad, but because it could've been much better, especially, since they've ported a lot of assets from the first game and had more resources and room for improvements (especially with feedback from the first game). But it seems they've either wasted a lot of time on the map, or were afraid to deviate too much from the original game. Some stuff seems to be added just for the sake of adding something new:  Honestly, the game felt a bit shallow, but again, maybe it is because I expected much more. Overall if you liked first Subnautica and want to experience the game again, but with a different story - it will sate this desire, if you expect something more - this game is not for you.

_childDocuments_.review: It does a few things better than Subnautica and a few things worse. I love the sea truck. The sea truck is mainly why I've put more hours into this one over OG Subnautica. I love how you can craft it in parts and then attach and detach those parts at will, based on whatever you plan to do. Need to just farm some metals for awhile? Just attach the storage and fabricator modules and go. Plan to go on a long haul to find the perfect base building spot? Might as well slap the bed, scanner, and aquarium modules on there too and bam, you got yourself a submarine that's still easier to pilot than the Cyclops. The story here is a little better too in terms of detail, even with some of the sappy cringey characters and dialogue, I was surprised to actually find my character interacting regularly with other sentient beings. The world feels just a tad less isolated and empty because of that. The biggest downside for me was that there just wasn't as much to explore and fewer options for base building. The map certainly feels smaller and I get that the addition of land mass and building on land mass probably factored into that. I honestly just didn't care as much about building above the water so it took away from the vast underwater exploration and building experience. Also the leviathans are nowhere near as scary. I mean don't get me wrong, I still got plenty spooked going into deeper water and hearing those noises but once I got my prawn suit I was practically looking for leviathans to mine. They just weren't as terrifying as the monsters from the original. Aside from that though Below Zero is pretty solid and kept to the overall themes of the original. I've enjoyed over 300 hours and plan to sink in a bit more before Subnautica 2 gets here.

_childDocuments_.review: After spending 38 hours immersed in the icy depths of Subnautica: Below Zero, I can confidently say that this sequel is a worthy continuation of the Subnautica legacy, deserving a solid 8/10.One of the aspects I adored in the original Subnautica was the building mechanics. Constructing my underwater base and expanding it to include various modules and decorations was incredibly satisfying. Below Zero not only retains this beloved feature but enhances it with more customisation options and a variety of new, intriguing modules that seamlessly blend with the game's arctic setting. The thrill of building and managing an underwater habitat remains one of the game's strongest points.However, I did encounter a notable challenge when trying to pick up the game after a break. The game lacks clear indications or reminders of what you were doing, making it difficult to regain your bearings. While this wasn't a deal-breaker, it did lead to some initial confusion and aimless wandering as I tried to recall my objectives and reorient myself within the game world.Despite this minor setback, Below Zero excels in several areas. The narrative is compelling, with deeper lore and intriguing mysteries that drive you to explore further. The new biomes are beautifully crafted, teeming with life and secrets to uncover. The sense of wonder and discovery that defined the first game is very much present here, enhanced by the game's stunning visuals and atmospheric sound design.The survival mechanics remain engaging, balancing resource management and exploration in a way that keeps you on your toes without becoming overly punishing. The addition of new tools and vehicles adds variety to the game-play, making the process of gathering resources and navigating the treacherous underwater terrain both exciting and efficient.In summary, Subnautica: Below Zero is a fantastic sequel that builds on the strengths of its predecessor while introducing new elements that keep the experience fresh and engaging. Despite the minor inconvenience of picking up the game after a break, it offers a rich, immersive experience that fans of the series will undoubtedly enjoy. An 8/10 feels like a fair score for a game that successfully captures the magic of underwater exploration and base building, with only a few hiccups along the way.

_childDocuments_.review: I picked up this game a few days ago after watching Jacksepticeye play it on his channel. Its an early access build so of course its buggy and broken in certain areas, and the game has substantial frame rate drops in certain areas...Yet somehow, despite all the bugs, this game still manages to blow Subnautica clean out of the water with almost laughable ease. Unknown Worlds has taken everything the learned while developing Subnautica and used it to create an enticing new world for us to explore! The only DLC i can remember enjoying more is Fallout 3's Mothership Zeta which is arguably one of the best DLC's ever created.Bottom line: Subnautica: Below Zero is a promising sequel to the original game. So much so that i believe we should all support and encourage the Unknown Worlds team to work towards turning Below Zero into a fully fleshed out game instead of DLCIf you loved Subnautica, then you will almost certainly enjoy this game despite it still being early access. Below Zero is well worth the money, if only to help support a truly brilliant development team as they craft another stunning chapter in the Subnautica universe :) PS;The bone sharks are back and just as scary as they were before. Unfortunately for us however, there are also several new, almost prehistoric looking creatures stalking the waters deeper down.I won't spoil anything, but lets just sat that the new creatures are just as terrifying and compelling as the creatures fellow Subnautica veterans are familiar with.

_childDocuments_.review: While this game is not as good as the original, it's definitely worth spending time in. Some biomes are not fleshed out well and can be boring/lack luster. They are also not as easy to navigate as land masses/ice bergs can get in the way. Base building is not as fun, as finding a great place to build under or above water is not easy. Most of the time, the places I wanted or would have built a base were already occupied. The biomes often feel claustrophobic, very easy to get lost and turned around in. I expected some huge cavernous areas like in the original, haven't found anything like it. The original Subnautica is in my top 10 games of all time. It's great to have MORE Subnautica, but I wish they had spent more time on certain areas and had less land exploration. 70% Subnautica 30% land exploration.  The land exploration is also... not great in my opinion. Full price at $29.99 --- Only for devoted Subnautica fans$20 or less, strong buy/must have unless you have claustrophobia (in which case avoid).

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this game is great, it fixed a few problems that I had with Subnautica. It also introduced a few bigger problems though. As a TL;DR for the review: buy Subnautica first, it's the overall better game and the story will make more sense, if you enjoy Subnautica, buy this game. For the people interested in my more in depth review, I've tried my best to write the review without spoiling anything, but there will inevitably be some minor spoilers.Also any positives in the original game I mention in my Subnautica review that I don't mention in this review are still positives in this game, I just didn't have enough room to write them all out.Let's start off with the positives, the game looks absolutely beautiful, it was even nominated for outstanding visual style for the steam awards. Whilst there are less biomes (we'll get into that later), they mostly feel more fleshed out, and nearly all of them look amazing. A much higher portion of the map looks beautiful (though there are some relatively boring biomes like the sparse reef in the original game, there are fewer of them). The textures look a lot nicer as well, compare the starting area of this game, the shallow twisty bridges, to the safe shallows, and the difference is night and day. This makes the exploration in this game far better than the original in my opinion.The game makes a lot of quality of life improvements as well (this might be outdated in a few months, the devs have said they will be backporting some of these to the original), the game adds pins for recipes, showing how many ingredients you have and the ones you still need, along with how many of the recipe you could make, which is amazing. There's also some accessibility features, like hightlighting nearby items and being able to change the size of the UI. When it comes to sound design, this game still checks all the boxes, it's brilliant, the music is also great, sounding just as good as the first game's, Ben Prunty did an excellent job filling in for Simon. There is one issue with the music, but I'll get into that in the negatives. Base building has been improved upon, there's some new base pieces as well as improvements to old ones, overall a better experience.There are some new items that are great as well, such as the recycler which is an endgame item that lets you break items into their components (for example changing a powercell into two batteries + silicone) and he mineral detector, a portable scanner room with smaller range.The ending is awesome, won't get into it anymore to not spoil it, but it's brilliant.Ore veins, these are a very welcome addition. In certain caves you can find bunched up ores and metals, which is a very fast way to get some of the rarer resources. To balance this they're usually somewhat deep down / hard to get to without a vehicle, protected by something dangerous, or require certain tools to access. But once you find them it's so nice filling up your inventory with things like magnetite and gold.The dialogue is well written and quite interesting to listen to, I loved the lifepod and degasi logs in the first game, and this game's dialogue is even better. The dialogue between your character and a certain other one is especially well written, though I can't get into it too much without spoiling the twist.Finally, the optimisation is a lot better, along with there being much less pop in. I get better fps at the same graphics settings, and there's barely any noticeable pop in (I do get lag spikes near some structures, but that's the same as the original game).Now let's get into the negatives:The mood of the game is very different. This isn't necessarily a bad thing but what I and many other people loved about the original Subnautica was it's atmosphere of loneliness, and this game doesn't have that. There's a lot more dialogue and your character even gets to speak to other characters. The game goes for a more exploratory feel, and isn't as scary either. The music ties in with this, whilst not being up-beat it's not as sad or creepy. The seatruck, this is both a negative and a positive really, it's a cool concept merging the cyclops and the seamoth, but I miss the seamoth, it was a lot smaller and more nimble, and in my opinion more fun. However it does do an adequate job replacing the cyclops.The prawn suit grappling has also been changed a bit and isn't as funThe land sections, whilst these are cool the snowfox has really awful handling, and just isn't as fun as exploring the beautiful underwater areas the team created. The land areas are also a bit more bland and less fleshed out, it's all just white, and there are very few creatures. However the new leviathan there is quite cool. The leviathans aren't as good as the original, especially the one that spawns in the shallower areas. In conclusion, it's still an amazing game, and worth the buy, I love the exploration and the dialogue is great, the gameplay has been improved upon in most areas. However the vehicles and land areas aren't anywhere near as fun (though I do still enjoy most of the land biomes). The mood is also drastically different, and not as unique.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Subnautica, you'll probably like this too. It's not *quite* as good but what is? Below Zero does a great job at encouraging exploration and giving you enough hints to not be stuck. There's something worth finding practically everywhere. In some cases, the something is a terrifying sea monster. But you gradually get more comfortable in your exploration, between learning how things react and equipment upgrades, so you can gradually proceed further & deeper, returning to base to drop off collected supplies and craft new tools & base parts.  And the environment is wonderful throughout, mysterious and beautiful and alien. The story is pretty good, but it has some linear-ness built into it that's easy to skip over: for example, there was one early clue I only got right at the very end of the game, and it only told me what I'd already figured out). The end result was that I wasn't entirely sure when that subplot was "finished" since I got the proper ending to my initial quest midway through. The other main plot thread is clearer, and ends the game properly.

_childDocuments_.review: [Warning - There be spoilers ahead] First off - as a huge fan of the original, I was looking forward to another underwater stint with Subnautica Below Zero.  Everything started off familiar enough.  Crashed pod, lost communications, unfamiliar surroundings... This time however, has a more personal story.  Unlike others, I didn't have a problem with this aspect, but rather enjoyed being part of a bit of a detective mission.  Maybe for immersion sake they could have allowed the player to choose your character's gender, but not really a dealbreaker for me.  The mechanics were familiar so I jumped right in and started surviving, and the game directs you to your first POI, kicking off the exploration.  This is also about when things kind of go off the rails for me.  I put 40 hours of play into BZ, but only because I was stuck in quarantine with covid.  I'd get frustrated or bored and quit, only to come back to it after having studied a walkthrough to figure out how to proceed.  I had no problem with the original in this regard.  I always seemed to know where I was supposed to generally go.  BZ gives you the barest little in the way of story, direction, or help.  [spoiler-ish alert] You have someone very able to give you more guidance right there with you and it is barely used.  As for the story itself, it is mostly a continuation on the story in the OG, which is fine, if not predictable.  There's not much else to see or do really besides the two 'main' quests. Many ideas are half baked - overland mechanics and vehicles for instance.  Not much was actually required to complete the game.  In fact, a game-breaking bug right at the end necessitated I use the console to warp back and forth as the game did not allow me to proceed until I reloaded for some reason and at that point I just wanted it to be over.  Read on for spoilers on the above.[spoily] As for crafting, gone are the seamoth and cyclops, replaced instead by more inferior vehicles (the 'sea truck' and the 'snowfox' that never get fully realized.  The sea truck allows you to connect modules and get all ice truck simulator across BZ if you want to.  Storage modules, crafting modules, sleeper cab, etc.  But you'll find them unweildy.  The storage module barely holds anything. Maneuvering the bus can be difficult - there are no cameras as on the cyclops.   You can build a prawn suit, as in subnautica, which I did.  And I never had to use it.  Literally never.  In SN, you HAD to use it to gather certain resources, but not so here.There is also a necessary bit of overland exploration in the arctic, which is a frustrating wasteland with not much to do but eat hot peppers to stay warm and constantly get lost.  You can build the snowfox, which is essentially an uncontrollable hoverbike made from tin foil.  It takes constant damage, doesn't go very fast, and the terrain design makes it largely useless and unnecessary.  When I first saw it, I thought it would make a cool ice speeder to cross a vast glacier, but the map is so small and bumpy that it never becomes useful.  Further, the giant ice worms which pop up every 20 feet simply knock you off of it and make it even more pointless.  I wound up abandoning it and handled the land section on foot.   You do need to make use of a ridiculous robot 'pengling' however for mostly stupid reasons.  At some point, you'll need to craft a 'cold suit' to stay warm and you need snowstalker fur from one of the numerous carnivores roaming the snow.  After savagely murdering several of them and unable to retrieve their hides, I had to turn to the internet, where I learned I needed to use my robot penguin to surreptitiously pull fur off their bodies.  Yep, totally obvious, that.  Apparently dead snowstalker fur becomes permanently attached to their bodies.  You also need to use the robobird to go into tunnels that any human with a crouch key could get into to retrieve ONE item. It kind of dawned on me, at the end of the game, that there was very little actual story or necessary tasks to complete.  BZ is more of a sandbox arctic survival simulator with a thin smear of story laid on top.  For those players who really want to stay there and build a giant Ice Planet Hoth base, it is totally possible.  There are resources aplenty to gather and do so.  It just doesn't seem like an interesting enough place for me to want to stay in it.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's my initial thoughts on BZ after a few hours of game play.Subnautica is one of the greatest games ever made and so BZ has a lot to live up to. It's inenevitable that for some people, at least, the sequel will be a let down, even if it's a great game in its own right. Because BZ is so familiar - it's the same balls of titanium falling out of limestone outcrops, the same bladderfish water, etc - it's extremely difficult to recapture the sense of wonder, danger and discovery that we all felt when we first played Subnautica.BZ is instead for me a chance to play Subnautica again with some fresh content, creatures and ideas. Yes, it's very familiar when the first game was all about novelty. But this is no bad thing. I feel just as excited to build and explore as I used to be. What a nice feeling that is. I can't wait to get home and go looking for rubies.The complaints about plot, voice acting, being spoon-fed etc seem a bit misplaced to me. I don't feel it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is going to be one of those "I wish there was a recommend BUT score" review.Below Zero is a solid addition to Subnautica. You get new biomes to explore, new toys to play with and a whole new set of options to build your base. And yet a quick look at the steam charts will reveal that there are a lot more players playing the original Subnautica than the sequel. There are just so many people asking for mods that import the Below Zero assets into the original game. Why?The truth is that this game, experience wise, is a step back. The new toys are fun, but they are just toys. The new biomes are pretty, but small. The map as a whole is rather tiny. You will get to the "that's it?" moment very quickly. Worst of all, a good chunk of it is above sea level. Which should add variety but is actually a chore to explore. Subnautica shines when you are in the water, not on solid ground.The worst thing is this new map does not feel intimidating in the slightest. Gone is the terror constantly accompanying your deep dives in the first game. Gone is the overwhelming sense of isolation you felt as you were trapped in this alien world. Even the leviathans feel more like a nuisance than any real danger.The idea of turning robin into an actual character rather than simply our avatar was also an unhappy decision. We are no longer living our story, but someone else's. As it happens this new story is rather boring when compared to the small but effective cast of characters from the first game. They told a better story in just a few audiologs than the whole below zero fully voiced, fully designed cast.The final nail in the coffin is the introduction of a character that actually interacts and accompanies you for 80% of your journey. Somehow it manages to have less personality than the PDA from the first game. Again these characters are not that bad per-se, but their presence takes away a lot and adds very little.All things considered: nothing can change the fact that playing Subnautica was mindblowing, playing Below Zero was just mildly fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Subnautica and Subnautica Below Zero are two of the very best survival games in existence. The artwork behind the graphics is quite beautiful, this is the only game that has even tempted me to consider paying big bucks for VR. There is the perfect amount of mining, exploration, story and building alongside moments of tension and 'jump'. They are different enough to be unique and similar enough so that you can seamlessly move from the first game to the second. I am FAR more excited by the possibility of a third in the series than I am about almost any other franchise (possible exception of a new Witcher game), It would be interesting to include small RPG elements about decision making and skillsets but other than that, I am not sure this developer could do much more to make these games better. They both score high 90s/100 for me and my 7 year old son who loves them very much, especially creative mode, scores them 100/100.

_childDocuments_.review: As a standalone game, this is a fun experience and a solid 8/10 from an indy dev team. However (as I'm sure everyone saw coming), this game was following one of the few games, in Subnautica (Original), that I hold as a legendary status 10/10 game (okay maybe 9.9/10). Due to this, Below Zero does not live up to it's predecessor, and comes off more as a 6/10. The environments, while initially pretty, and the fauna, while initially interesting and frightening - end up feeling rather bland and leave you wanting more once you realize that quickly, you've seen all there is to offer. The further dive into story elements with this sequel is nice, but seems to shift the focus from the original's survival horror feel. This sequel simply didn't feel nearly as tense and scary as the first. The two enemy leviathans that are supposed to be the biggest and scariest, fail to scare, as they barely do any damage to your two vehicles. And when they do, you can simply hop out, and use a repair tool on it... directly in front of the leviathan. Additionally, the map feels large at first, but upon exploring anywhere further than perhaps 500m from your initial drop pod location, you will find the environments desolate and boring. I fell off the edge of the map in a prawn suit, and was shocked when I realized that that was the entire map... I walked the edge of the map and realized that outside of the 4 or 5 underwater areas that are interesting, the rest of the map is just barren - even lacking leviathans or anything to threaten. Perhaps they wished to hit a wider market with this game, and so toned down the 'spooks' and tension, but in my opinion, any 3rd sequel needs to up those factors greatly. Overall, I would recommend this game to anyone who has played the first and wishes for more, but to anyone new to the IP, I'd much much much rather recommend they just play the first game instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Subnautica: Below Zero is a good game. While in early access, improved controls, game-play mechanics and vehicles help turn the experience of exploring 4546B into a smooth and enjoyable one. It's story is linear when compared to Subnautica's and doesn't tie all of its sub-plots together nearly as well. The map is smaller, both horizontally and vertically, with about 1/2 being unexplorable due to ice and the max depth stopped at 1100 meters. Why did I recommend the game then when I have so many critiques? Because Subnautica is a beloved game. It was unique and incredible! Lots of people look forward to the game's official release and they should know what they're getting into. That being said, if you go into this game with the right expectations you'll have a blast. Rather than the mysterious horror which permeated the first installment in the series, Below Zero is meant to be more light-hearted, adventurous and funny while still remaining bits of mystery and suspense. Simply put, don't go into this as seriously as the first game! The biomes are beautiful, many more so than the first game! Bases are way more customizable and efficient and there's a wide cast of characters. It will be fun, just love it for what it is!

A lot less of those 'wow' moments where you're in awe and just a lacking of biomes to explore.The progression system is ridiculously poorly done. Some of the things that are the big unlocks later in the game would be very useful in the early game but by then are completely useless.Base-building is a huge improvement over the original. _childDocuments_.review: **SPOILERS**Definitely a step-down from the original Subnuatica but a great game nonetheless. The creatures in this game are far less terror-inducing, aside from the shadow leviathan of course. The base building was a huge step up in my opinion with the addition of the large room, which gave the player a huge jump in creativity. As for gameplay, the beginning of exploring the world is much in the same where you feel helpless. This is quickly shut down when you find out you aren't alone on this planet, unlike the first game. The quests feel justified and you are rewarded for your efforts which moves the game along quickly. To my disappointment at the end of the game, I found that I never even used my prawn suit as it wasn't needed in any aspect, all of the resources can be found by hand which creates no need for the prawn drill. The sea truck can go as deep as you need it to go for the whole game, which also made the prawn suit useless. Lastly, the perimeter defense system on the sea truck makes going past shadow leviathans super easy and unsatisfying. Also, the ice worm is so overdone I think they really missed this one it's such a good creature, and the idea of there being a land leviathan is super cool but it just gets super annoying that it knocks you off the snow fox every single time. Now for the story, I feel like they needed to pick a story and run with it. There seems to be three mini-stories with each of them fighting for your attention throughout the game, those being Marguerit, Al-An, and Sam. Also, Robin talking during the whole game was a good addition it gave character as opposed to Ryley in the first game being silent. Furthermore, The story of Marguerit being tied back to the first game through the Degasi crew was nice to get some closure on what happened to that crew. But at the end of the game she feels useless you learn a few things about her and just leave her there without saying goodbye or anything right after you gain her trust. I think her story should have been told in the form of PDA's with the remnants of her base being left behind. The main reason you come to this planet is to find Sam your sister, but halfway through the game, it feels like we are in the full force of finding Al-An a new body so Sams's arc gets pushed to the side. I think the way they handled Sam at the end was well done with PDA's of her being throughout the map giving you the reasons she died why she was on 4546B. Then completing her work by giving the cure to the frozen leviathan was a nice ending to her story. Now for the main story of getting Al-An's body was really well done, throughout the game you aren't totally sure to trust him or not cause he resist answering some of your questions, and his people shot down the Aurora in the first game for gosh sake. It was cool to get some insight on him and his people through the whole game as they were a huge question in the first game. Finding the parts and building his body progressed the game nicely and was a lot like building the rocket which I really enjoyed. Learning that Al-An was one of the reasons that the Kharaa got out was really fulfilling after playing the first game. Without dragging this on much longer the ending of going home with Al-An was awesome, seeing the tech that Precursors have was super cool, in my opinion, this sets up another game perfectly there is so much about the Precursors that we don't know that I'm dying the learn about them. After all, I would give this game an 8/10 with the first game being at 9/10.

The story is ok and there's more direction than the first but that kinda defeats the object really.2) The vehicles... boy o boy can I not stand the sea truck >> The sub (cyclops) wins hands down: they are more maneuverable, you can use camaras to see where the back end is, you can build inside the sub to build your own little base, and they just look and feel so much better.The sea truck has none of the above: you can't build or customise it so if you want a bed that's "X" speed reduced, storage is another; want that prawn suit? that's yet more reduction in speed, agility, ability to drive the damn thing.. ?>>  You just have no choice with regards to "customisation" if you want that mobile base you'll need at least 4/5 modules so you are just pathetically slow, you can't see your back end so you're constantly getting stuck and it just feels cheap and sluggish...3) It's still pretty buggy: There's even a bug where you glitch into the door when you open it as you run, this is a bug I reported in pre-launch but they were too focused on the minority characters. The game crashes randomly so you (should be anyway) find yourself saving every 10 seconds and the game 'sticks' a lot too - even on reduced graphics which aren't amazing anyway.4) The constant political opinions of the dev's are so in your face it's unreal. I don't mean subtle digs but blatent and outright statements that make me roll my eyes so hard.. I played in small amounts but they distract from the game play too much.5) I can't stress enough how flat, boring and painful the main character is - she deserves this special mention. I don't care which of the 2 genders the toon is, what colour he or she is or what they believe in, this is a badly written character. Plus side is that I could still play without the sound on ;)Overall?There's some pro's - more blueprints for base building, more story to follow, I like the arctic feel but it kinda fell flat.There's wayy too many cons - if you play just prepare yourself for the underwhelming sea truck, the politics from RL in the game, the main toon being obnoxious etcThanks for the offer to change my review but I'll stick to it thanks ;)"An extremely poor ending to a previously great game - I'll be going back to the first one"

_childDocuments_.review: It's not as good as the original game, but you were probably expecting that already since so much of what made it good was about discovery, and a lot of the core gameplay loop is the same as in the original so it can't be rediscovered.  I'm not mad, I'm just a bit disappointed, and this will be a long one. I knew it wouldn't blow me away like the original game, but almost everything that made the original game good feels like a scaled down version of it. feels more linear. I get that it's arctic waters so it's not going to be as vibrant as lush equatorial waters, but both the east and the west side are basically empty. I had a bit of a similar problem with Skyrim, I'm from the north so snow is nothing new and as much as I love mountains it was a little dull compared to the weird Morrowind and vibrant Oblivion, until they released the Dawnguard DLC with its Forgotten Vale. It felt magical! Subnautica is not fantasy but it should still feel magical! But it's just sand and a few icebergs.Where the original game was absolutely brilliant in gently nudging the player in the right direction, this mostly just points you straight there. A part of it is just fetch quests, which I thought was particularly dull. It literally just tells you to "go there and scan this". Disappointing. aren't really very interesting either, it's just a few leviathans and just absurd amount of resources to mine, I'me talking about kyanite on the ground and in big mineable blocks when you need like ten of it in the entire game. This time you won't be running out of copper, but wouldn't it be nice if there was something more there? The blood kelp forest, the lost river and the tree are awesome locations in the original game, this doesn't really have them. The lily pads are kind of cool but serve no other purpose than to have a crashed ship with blueprints in there. is mostly boring. There isn't a whole lot there apart from snow, and you can't even get seeds for the plants to grow in your base for decoration apart from the food plants. The hostile animals make it kind of annoying, but carry a flare and they are irrelevant. But apparently a flashlight isn't good enough, has to be a flare. There isn't much lore or reason to thoroughly explore in there, the robo pengling is literally needed for one thing, otherwise it's for resources you can get in a million other ways. went through an extensive rewrite during development, but I'm afraid it doesn't really show. The original game used the Half Life formula of a random nobody who just happens to be there to great success. This time they went for a more personal take. I like the character, but most of the plot is still in writing or voice logs. The most baffling thing is that they introduce a character into the game in a great way, and... don't use her. Almost at all. I went to see her when I was about to leave and there wasn't even a voice line for that. No "hey I'm about to go" "ok bye!". NOTHING. WTF is that about!?Al-An as a character was likeable, and I wish there was more of him. The ending to the story is pretty cool and clearly inspired by a certain movie based on a certain novel, I liked that. But really it only adds a footnote to the plot of the original game.They landed in a weird in-between of a proper plot and something else. I played the early access early on when it was released and I wonder if it would've been better to go the way it went, where the main character's sister was still alive and a big part of the plot. And don't worry, her death is literally the first thing that is brought out in the game. Overall finding out why she did what she did left me a little empty, it was just kind of "ok that happened"., I played it on a laptop with a Ryzen 5 4500U with 16 gigs of dual channel RAM and integrated graphics. Given that it did very well, not great but quite playable. As for bugs, yes, it's not great. There's a hoverbike for moving around on land, which would run over all sorts of boulders and ledges and obstacles just fine. But on perfectly flat ice, like the kind that is shaved to mm perfection? It would ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ randomly stop, like 100-0 instantly. That is spectacular. But nothing game breaking. where the original game is a 10/10 for me (disregarding the bugs and performance), this is just a solid 7.5/10. It's not bad, but let me put it this way: I liked the original game so much I instantly bought the early access for Below Zero knowing that this game could be an absolute turd and I would still be happy giving the devs my money considering how much joy the og game gave me. Well this game wasn't a turd, not at all, but as for their next game I will not be buying early access.

_childDocuments_.review: It really pains me to give this game a negative review.  I really loved the original Subnautica and have over 400 hours invested in the game.  Below Zero has its good points but I feel the negatives make the game not worth the full price cost.  If you loved the first and just need to play it wait for a sail.  Here are my Negatives from beating the game:  1)  The map is small and very cluttered.  You can't see more then 20m in any direction and most of the map is between 20m and 50m deep.  The vast majority of underwater gameplay all takes place in caves you can barely squeeze your vehicles into.2)  The surface areas are a frustrating pain to explore.  Constant bad weather both lowers your temp and prevents you from seeing your surroundings.  Hostile mobs are a constant threat you have way of avoiding or fighting.  3)  "Gamey" feel.  In the first game you progressed the story by using real world thinking.  In Below Zero you need 'game' thinking.  This is hard to explain without story spoilers but basically you need to complete a task purely for the games sake with no real indication of why your character would think to do it.4)  The Stories.  Below Zero has 2 main stories.  Normally I would call one the main story and the other a subplot but in this game it is the 'subplot' that leads to an actual ending while the main story just stops leaving you wondering if there was something else you should have done or waiting for some other hint or clue to show you what to do next.5)  The vehicles.  There are some nice changes to the vehicles... except they are almost all completely useless.  Out of the 3 vehicles the only one you need is the SeaTruck, and out of all its secondary attachments you can safely ignore ALL of them.    Because so much of the game takes place in areas the expanded SeaTruck can't easily go you are basically either leaving part of it outside of a cave in hopes it doesn't get destroyed or just leaving it back at your base.  The Prawn has no point other then gathering resources for you if base building is your goal and even then it just saves time.  The Snow bike or whaterver its called is way to fast for the small map and you constantly get attacked by hostile mobs that knock you off.Now for the Positives and there are a few.1)  Some good quality of life upgrades like being able to pin recipes as well as being able to recycle items back down to retrieve component parts.2)  The base building has been improved dramatically and it really makes me wish I had these upgrades in the original game.  Having a larger room, a control room and being able to make dividers and glass roofs is amazing.  Unfortunately you don't have any really nice places to build a great base in Below Zero.3)  The Story.  While I didn't like how the main story just faded away, I really did enjoy both it and the subplot.  The main story brings back a character from the original game that I really love and the new subplot introduces a great new character.  If you read all of this, thank you, and I hope it helped you make a choice.  I have 36 hours in game at the time I wrote this, having completed the game in about 27 hours and the rest is just base building.  I expect my time in this game wont exceed 50 hours.  If I didn't have the first game to compare this to maybe I would have been more inclined to recommend it as you do get your moneys worth on average with other games of this type.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, it's an undersea adventure on an alien planet alright. Some of the story and dialog is atrocious, but the atmosphere and gameplay more than make up for it.Most of the story lore is in the form of "found PDAs". If a game is going to use this method of storytelling, the content in those randomly found recordings need to be awesome- they usually are not worth reading IMO. The AI jokes are out of place and kinda destroy the professionally built immersion. I feel there are some discordant themes in BELOW ZERO.Lots of confusion on how to proceed sometimes. Be ready for a lot of backtracking and searching. (Which can be both rewarding and frustrating.)The story seemed more subdued for Subnautiaca 1, and I think this developer should move back in that direction. I would love a new Subnautica style game that captured the isolated tranquility of the first one. Go play the first Subnautica first. It's a near masterpiece. If you enjoy(ed) it, you will want to play BELOW ZERO after some time passes as they are quite similar.

_childDocuments_.review: Subnautica Below Zero is kind of an ambivalent game. The loop of exploring, finding new blueprints, buidling new equipment and using it to explore further works great and is as addicitive as in the first Subnautica game. Unfortunately, Below Zero had some points that really hampered the experience for me. The biggest issue are the land areas. They are simply too big and confusing. I kept circling around the same spots all the time because I was totally. As much as I liked the parts under water, the land parts of Below Zero are an immense pain in the ass. These parts really ruined the game for me. What I also found to be very annoying is that the game doesn't give you proper clues as to where you should go next. That made the story feel like a guessing game. The game world itself is much smaller than in the first game. But it is as colorful and interesting as one would expect. But the constant sense of horror isn't nearly as present as in the first game. For some reason, I found the encounters with Leviathans rather annoying, whereas in the first game they really scared me. The new story is rather interesting, albeit it takes away the constant feeling of loneliness you had in the first Subnautica. To sum it up: Subnautica Below Zero is a decent game, but in my opinion can't hold up with its predecessor.

_childDocuments_.review: These games are truly works of art, if there is one game you NEED to buy and try, it is Subnautica. It is an underwater survival/role-playing game with a truly intriguing and deep story-line to unfold. It is not your typical game where you must kill to survive, but one where you must use intelligence and cleverness to survive the horrors that await you in the deep. This game uses realistic terror and stress unlike most typical horror/jump-scare type games. Most of us have a very rational fear of the ocean and what lurks in the open water and this game plays on those fears and puts you in some truly terrifying situations when you leave the safe shallows. The ambient music paired with this terror-inducing game-play is truly an experience like no other. Many times I found myself truly scared and feeling as though I was stranded on an alien ocean planet with carnivorous leviathan sea monsters hunting me. The roars of these beasts are spine-chilling/pants-wetting level terrifying. The atmosphere, the fauna, the flora, are absolutely stunning, like nothing I've ever seen before for such an animated-style game. The graphics are truly beautiful and terrifying in parts. I've put over 300 hours into this game and I don't regret a single second. It has potential for multiple play-throughs as you discover new things you missed the last time. There are many secrets to uncover and many biomes to explore as you try to survive and solve the mystery of this planet and find a way home. I don't want to spoil too much, so I will end it by saying that the many positive reviews on this game are 100% accurate and Subnautica has made a mark in gaming history. It's incredibly immersive, They've created a unique survival experience that even casual gamers can play, understand and enjoy. Unknown Worlds has gone above and beyond any expectations I have and I am truly excited for the new game and what awaits us in the icy depths. I will happily play and aid in the development process and I hope my feedback I send in via in-game can be of use to the team at Unknown Worlds in creating another unique masterpiece for us to spend hours of our life immersed in.

_childDocuments_.review: After the first game, this one looked promising, and it failed to deliver.Some positives remained from the original game - beautiful biomes, atmosphere, exploration.But exploration requires fear and uncertainty. In Below Zero, there are no extreme depths, no unbeatable predators, no fear. It doesn't come close to the lost river and lava zone in the original. Exploration starts nicely but quickly runs out of space. Those deep caves beneath the twisted passages? - Tight, small, and nothing below them. Caves under kelp forests? Tight, small, etc. Caves under lily pads? Tight, small... you get the trend. Are there grand canyons and plateus? No.The entire underwater map is undersized and lacks depth (literally). Large predators are annoying, not scary. There are too many of them constantly making noises, but they lack the bite to matter. Nothing as terrifying as reaper leviathan howling from the deep.So exploring is fun for a time but soon gets old.Land portion, on the other hand, is blown out of proportion and made too extensive. Also annoying. Getting lost on the ground because of the weather is not fun - it is tiresome. The land is mostly empty and lacks visual impact to keep players entertained - all that distance serves no purpose. For a game named Subnautica, it was questionable, to begin with, to make so many quest locations out of water. The story itself sucks. I don't mind the SJW ♥♥♥♥ all that much, though it was kind of blown out of proportion. But the story is not logical and fails to motivate the player. It would be better if they made it about survival again. On top of that, the character talks too much and is an idiot at that. "Philosophical" discussions with the alien AI were horrible - the MC responded to complex questions from an alien with a kindergarten level of logic and depth. It was incredibly frustrating because it was technically forcing that idiocy on us. I WOULDN'T answer like that, yet I had to listen how MY character is making an idiot out of herself (and by extension me) in front of an alien. Supposedly a scientist - she was reasoning at the level of a 10-year-old child at best.To begin with, if I were to summarize the first Subnautica in two words - it would be "Underwater Exploration". The story in the first game was just an excuse to get us exploring. It was simple, logical, engaging, and not distracting. We were shot down, had to survive and escape, thus exploring and going deeper — simple yet effective motivation. The plot met simple criteria:- Makes sense- Not over-complicated- Motivates to explore-Doesn't distract from explorationBelow Zero violates that. The plot now:- Makes no sense; plot holes everywhere- While simple, even primitive, it piles on you with over-exposition and useless drivel- Doesn't promote much exploration, it mainly forces you to go on empty land or to a marker location- Constantly distracts you from the world around you with info dumps and meaningless dialoguesPlot holes were so blatant that it was hard to ignore them, and even when you try - the story FORCES you into plot holes face first. The first minute in the game bears the question - since we aren't stranded and deliberately came to the planet knowing the conditions - WHY the hell aren't we wearing a cold-resistant suit? WHY no weapons? WHY no tools? WHY NO FREAKING SCHEMATICS? WHY not even scuba diving equipment?The "sister's" story also pictures a strange situation. Allegedly she SUSPECTED Alterra of making bioweapons out of the Caraar bacteria they found. No evidence whatsoever. Still, she conspired with the psycho Margarett, they performed a terrorist attack. Sam eventually caused a lethal accident and died with a colleague. I doubt that Alterra was making weapons or anything bad really - no private security or armed forces at all were spotted throughout the entire game. Even the voice log of Sam's last moment wasn't an armed stand-off, but just a colleague asking what the hell she was doing. One would think that "evil corporation" would guard their secret evil lab with armed forces and try to silence witnesses. Alterra, however, is merely a toothless bunch of incompetent cowards. Sam was a paranoid psycho, and our character is not much better.The alien part of the story is dull, dumb, and irrational. No choices are provided; the alien constantly contradicts himself and doesn't even sound sufficiently alien. The entire thing is like low-quality fanfic.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had this game since it first released in Early Access, and I was so, so excited for it's full release. I love almost everything about this game, to be honest. From the new creatures to discover, to the new characters to learn about, to the main story. And the soundtrack! I love the OST so much. It's a lot different than Subnautica's, which isn't a bad thing. In fact, I'd say it's a good thing as it makes the game even more of it's own thing. And the jukebox music is awesome, too! Now I'll go on to talk about what I really liked and such.Disclaimer: This review will probably contain spoilers, read at your own risk!I have to admit that one part of the story felt a little lacking to me. Your main objective when you start the game is to find out what really happened to your sister, Sam. I like this aspect of the story, but the resolution of it did feel lackluster to me, and I wish there could've been something more to it. That was really my only problem with it, to be honest. The rest of the story, in which you help a lone Architect, Al-An, was one of my favorite parts of the game. I absolutely love Al-An and their interactions with Robin. And the ending . . . I really loved it, but it definitely left me desiring more.Loved most of them, to be honest! They definitely did not disappoint with the designs of the fauna, especially the leviathans. Although, the way they look isn't everything. As much as I love the way the Cryptosuchus looks, the sound design and the way they behave was just so  They share a biome with an aggressive leviathan, and yet the leviathan sounds less imposing than they do. I'm more scared of their sounds than the Chelicerate's. Not that the Chelicerates don't scare me; they definitely do, I just wish the sounds were more appropriate for them.Ice Worms also fall under the category of annoying. They're really cool in concept, but the way they knock you off the Snowfox every time they emerge is just so :/ And for the late game leviathan, they are definitely scary looking, but fall flat as you can just stop piloting your Seatruck and they leave you alone. On a more positive note, I love the design of the Vent Gardens and Glow Whales. I love them so much. And the Titan Holefish are my absolute  I also adore the Squidsharks and Snow Stalkers. Everything, really. I love them all.Instead of having the Seamoth and Cyclops in this game, you have the Seatruck. It functions as both, pretty much, except you can't build in it like you can the Cyclops. Throughout the game, you unlock more modules for it, which allows you to hold more stuff, have a fabricator on the go, etc. The only downside to having more modules is that it makes your Seatruck slower (and a little harder to navigate, as you don't have cameras like on the Cyclops). I liked the Seatruck, although I admit I wish I had the Cyclops back. The Prawn Suit is still there, but I literally never used it lol.Now for the Snowfox, the land vehicle. It's cool, that's for sure, but also makes me feel kinda motion sick. The movement is just really odd, I guess, but I guess it makes sense since it hovers instead of rolls. The modules you can get for it also feel kinda useless imo, since by the time you get them, there's not much of a reason to go back. Maybe that one is just me, though.Overall, I really did enjoy this game. I beat it in around 13 hours, and that was with prior knowledge due to Early Access play. I enjoyed the exploration, and the mystery, and how I felt happy when I made progress in the story. I'm already in the middle of replaying it; that's how much I loved it. I can only hope that we'll see more of Al-An and Robin in the future, although I don't think we will :(

_childDocuments_.review: Too large to be considered an expansion pack or DLC, but simply borrows too many things from the original subnautica to be considered a standalone game or sequel, either. The gameplay remains largely unchanged from the original, with the exception of the added body heat mechanic, which mostly applies in the dry land segments. Two of the three vehicles from the original have been removed, with only the PRAWN suit reappering. The cyclops and Seamoth have had their functions combined into the more customisable Seatruck, which can fulfill the roles of both aforementioned vehicles. A land vehicle has also been added, though it's usefulness is limited. A lot of the thalassophobic horror from the original is missing, with the many memorable and terrifying carnivores from the original being replaced with fairly standard stalker and ghost leviathan copies. Nothing that'll give you the feeling of dread that hearing a Reaper Leviathan's roar for the first time did. The game world feels much smaller than the original, and the weather effects above water limit the visibility of the player to the point that landmarks can no longer be used to navigate, in contrast with the original where the Aurora could be used to pinpoint the player's location very accurately. Perhaps this was intended to make the compass upgrade seem more enticing, but it felt more irritating than anything.I'm conflicted on the story. It's told much more directly than the original, with a voiced protagonist engaging in dialogue with other characters and discussing plot elements with them, though portions of the story are still told through audio- and text logs as they were in the original. There is also a much clearer artistic message in this game, with themes regarding the inevitability of death and the "never play god" lesson so common to Sci-Fi featuring megacorporations. in Subnautica 1, the story was largely an excuse to have the player dive around in increasingly dangerous environments collecting things, which was fine because it wasn't trying to be deep. The story unfortunately sort of ignores the two most interesting characters in favor of a cliched "trying to find out what happened to your sibling" plotline, and there isn't as much worldbuilding on the precursor aliens as I had hoped, and what is there is pretty weak. The plot is still fairly strong by video game plot standards, but it's no SOMA.Overall, it's more of the same. If you really liked Subnautica and wanted more of it, this could be right up your alley. In any case i would recommend playing the original first, as while gameplay mechanics may be explained for new players, story elements are not.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game and nice successor to the original with some updated quality of life improvements. I'd recommend to anyone to try out these games, both the original and Below Zero (BZ). That being said, I think the late game suffered in BZ (spoilers ahead). Some of the deeper biomes (deep thermal, crystal, red zone) felt like they were just "there" and didn't really have anything worth doing in them above a task in the story. I really didn't need any resources from them and there was really only the fabricator quest. I might have spent 30 minutes or so in the crystal and red zone...felt very underwhelming unfortunately. Compared to the first game, where the deeper parts of the map felt very large and open...like there was a shallow map, a mid-depth map, and a really expansive deep map. Where in BZ, there's deeper areas but not much reason to be down there. I mined some Kyanite and Nickel but only used 4-5 piece each and that was done. Also, I could have used more deadly enemies, not because I want to die and lose my stuff, but because it would add more gameplay to it. I had a seatruck with a perimeter defense mod...I just scooted right through 4 Shadow leviathans without issue...if one aggro'd on me, I'd blast it, take 5 dmg or so, and keep going like it was nothing. I made the torpedo arm on the prawn but never even had to use it for anything. Lastly, I could have done without the surface zones. Delta island was fine and good, but the glacial basin part was just silly...hard to navigate, rough weather, leviathans that knock you off your mount. I don't mind the occasional land-based activity in subnautica, but I'd ask the devs to limit it in the future. Let's stay underwater for most of the game.Anyway, gripes aside, Subnautica 1 was one of my favorite games of all time. BZ was a happy successor that I enjoyed and played. I hope that the studio keeps making games in this series...the alien environments are incredible to explore. Well done and looking forward to more.

_childDocuments_.review: Although the game has not been fully released, I don't suppose much will be added or changed. If they won't decide to redo the entire game, there is very little room for improvement.And so, as it stands, Subnautica Below Zero (let's call it BZ) lacks in so much compared to the original.• Danger and Horror - unlike the first game, BZ's creatures aren't scary whatsoever. Their design is poor and uninspired. The Chelicerate spawns in 1-2 locations far out where you don't even need to travel. Not only that but it makes grumpy noises at a mere Peeper so you'll know its exact position while hugging the sea floor. And as many pointed out, it is just a humongous lobster. Shadow Leviathan has proven to be more annoying than scary. Apart from its territory patrolling, it resembles a black anvil. Take notes from Vsauce, or actual studies, on what makes things actually scary. The areas themselves aren't particularly creepy, the deepest one being situated at ~900 meters below, they all lack the proper atmosphere. The only one scary enough was the edge of the world. Even though I already expected to be killed by a scripted leviathan, the fact that the part was so murky made that the scariest experience of the entire game.Not to mention the ordinary fish. Previously, there were Warpers and Squidcrabs to worry about too. In BZ, there is literally no creature - including leviathans - that could pose any threat to me while I was in my Seatruck or Prawn suit.• Biomes - this is continuation of what I was talking before; there are no interesting biomes. Admittedly, I was kind of excited about the fact that there was gonna be ice and snow and ice. But due to how much smaller the map is, the glaciers stole much of the spotlight and opportunity for some amazing areas to shine. It's called Subnautica. There was no need for walking. There could've been some iceberg cavities which would lead to caches and laboratories guarded by the most dangerous monsters. The strongest defender of the Glacial Bay was the boredom I didn't want to face when I had to go there to fetch something.• Resources - I have to say, that I'm not the biggest fan of grinding for resources. It was very tiring in the first game, that's true. But on the other hand, I think majority of the players don't want to have basically everything handed to them. Which is exactly how it was; I had basically everything handed to me. This is a huge problem when you don't innovate the resources and reuse most of the blueprints from the original: everybody who played the original will know what to search for. I had all the materials needed for the endgame prepared in the first few expeditions.• Sound design - It'd be super lazy to reuse the roars of the Reapers or use the same music, but honestly, the fish sounded pretty bland. Again, even the Squidcrabs had their terrifying charging sounds. I will give props to the voice acting; both the main character and AL-AN sound good enough - although I'm not a native speaker. There is a track that was a bliss to listen to - Permafrost. And the Jukebox is something I always like to turn on. However, as if to compliment the completely unexpected chill atmosphere, there is no tension that the music could provide. I remember stumbling upon the Blood Kelp zone and hearing the Lava lakes track. Those were moments I felt absolutely uneasy. Maybe the music could be more like that or it could just fade into nothingness when exploring the deepest parts - but then again, there aren't that many.• The story and gameplay - It feels really short. Obviously, it isn't finished, but the story is pretty linear and fed to the player. There is also not much of mystery behind anything, because once you acquire AL-AN, you just go from one cache to another, hunting for the parts you are told to hunt for. And even though I do like the interaction you can have with him, I find  very cliche.• Bottom (1000 m) line - The best word to describe the game is 'lacking'. It just feels empty and shallow. Surprisingly even more so than the first game where I didn't have a companion with me at all times. I would personally prefer if they scratched the whole 'surface' gameplay idea and focused entirely on the underwater world. I would welcome deeper parts of the ocean to explore. I wouldn't mind more dangerous creatures. I wouldn't be against waiting for another year or two if it meant the game would go in such direction.

_childDocuments_.review: It's unavoidable to compare BZ to the first Subnautica. It definitely fixed a lot of bugs and improved resource collection; I never fell through the floor of my seatruck or got stuck in the prawn suit like in the first game. It's a lot easier and less grindy to find resources, though the mineral detector has a *uselessly* short range. There are more sections where you want to / need to be out of your seatruck, which can add to the experience. Oxygen plants and cave systems are cool; the seaglide's map is actually functional now. You still need mods to remove annoyances (hotbar expansion, map, and easycrafting were my go-tos) but overall the game is more polished than Subnautica 1.*Unfortunately,* it lost some things too. For starters, the game isn't scary. None of the leviathans are, and the normal critters are just annoying. Subnautica 1 was terrifying; BZ just... isn't. The game world feels smaller and shallower; there's so much less *depth* to explore besides occasional caves that take the place of the objectively-cooler Lost River. The story focus means it's more handhold-y and "go here, do this" than free-exploring. The above ground sections just aren't very fun, and the snowfox is just bad. Too slow, controls terribly, way too fragile, and you fall off every time a worm shows up. Use the prawn instead.BZ is... fine. There are good moments in the underwater sections and I got over 20 hours of play out of a game I got for $20. That's fair, honestly. But it's just not as good, or as large, as the first one. Take the polish and some of the new basebuilding stuff from BZ and combine it with Subnautica 1's better world and creatures, and you'd have an excellent game. As is, it's just okay.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not recommending this game for three main reasons.A: It's super unfinished at the momentB: The protagonist is voiced and has an unbearable personality.C. Storyline is inferior in what has been developed so farSo the first part is pretty basic. Huge portions of the map are literally not made, features are buggy, the story isn't even done yet. The game simply isn't finished and I don't mean not fleshed out I mean you're literally buying half a game. If you want to spend money to support the devs and test what they have at the moment that's great, but don't buy the game under the prerogative that you are buying a full game it's not even close.The second part is what really motivated me to not recommend the game. So in the first subnautica your protagonist is unvoiced and generally devoid of personality ext. Voiced protagonists rarely bother me (i.g. fallout 4's voicing didn't bother me), however the way it was executed ruined the game for me and it's not really fixable. You play a female, which I'm fine with, but she is so ARROGANT. In subnautica I was always checking over my shoulder suspicious of any fish in the ocean because half of them could kill you. It really felt like I was fighting to survive and I felt my character experienced the same fear I did. However this protagonist's dialogue and voice convey that she is utterly unafraid of the terrors of the deep, and the mysterious alien race you re-encounter, and it frankly just comes off as both fake and annoying. Furthermore she comes off as some super eco warrior type, which I'm not really into. It probably would have been fine if the other bits of her personality weren't so toxic, but this really just killed any empathy I might have had for the character. This resulted in me almost enjoying below zero, but every time my character opened her mouth it completely broke immersion and I just wanted to play something else, anything else.Finally I found the story mediocre. Let me preface that the is story is not *bad*, but despite the voice acting added to it, it simply falls short of the first, at least with what is in it. For starters you are not alone you have constant radio communication with your sister who is in orbit, which greatly removes the fear and unknown from the story. In the first one you you were frantically searching for the other survivors, while trying to find out what happened and what is going on. It was full of twists and turns and I never knew what was going to happen next. However, in this the story comes off more of a grocery list of instructions. Part of this can once again be accredited to the deplorable protagonist, but even without that the mystique of the first story just seems absent.Ultimately the game will eventually be fleshed out solving the first problem and that might lead to the story getting more interesting as the game is finished. However, there's no way to get around a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ protagonist and that same protagonist will remove any joy I might get from the story or gameplay so it with a heavy heart I can't recommend this game despite how much I enjoyed the first one.

_childDocuments_.review: At the moment, which is March 7, 2021. The game is still one month away from official launch. This review is based on the pre-launch condition of the game, and I'll try and update it when the game officially launches.For the most part, what you're getting with Below Zero is exactly what you got in the original Subnautica. The time spent under the ocean, exploring the biomes and uncovering secrets is effectively unchanged mechanically from the first game. This is great, and I loved the first game. So why the negative review?The time spent on LAND is big change from the original subnautica and is, for the most part frustrating, or wholly negative. Because the game is set in the Arctic, land areas are mostly white ice broken up by caves and the like between cliffs and glaciers. Visually its distinct and looks good. For navigation in a game that specifically eschews a traditional video game map with a "you are here" marker, its awful. The devs even seem to have noticed this and there are 2 static maps available of specific areas. Both don't help much, because the areas are both convoluted and lack good, non-repeating landmarks. Underwater navigation, comparatively, is the same as the first game, with lots of useful landmarks to use to orient yourself. Beacons help with both, and can be used on land, but are distinctly less useful on land, due to the convoluted cave systems that connect areas.The other big issue on Land is the Ice Worm, a new enemy that only appears in a certain area of land. These act like you would expect, popping out of the ice to attack you as you traverse. Unfortunately they are, at the moment, very poorly  implemented. They don't do a great deal of damage to the player personally, and the vehicle you're given to navigate the Land sections takes damage but will never die in one shot. The worms will knock you off your vehicle, apparently regardless of distance as they breach the ice. So traversal of the area becomes, rather than tense, just tedious. As you're knocked off your bike every 30 seconds or so, repair it, then continue on your way. There are items to convince the worms to stay away from you for a time, but they, if anything add the tedium of setting them up. The animations involving the worms are also need a lot of work, as they can appear in odd places, based on their size, and leave nothing behind. The whole creature is just not very well done at this time. I'm hoping they do a lot of improvements with them.Bugs:-The most common bug I've experienced, and it can be frustrating, is to do with the main vehicle in the game. Very frequently you'll find yourself "swimming" in the air of the vehicle, either on entry or getting out of the driver's seat. Sometimes this is fixed by opening the PDA or pausing, often not. The only way to fix it if the above doesn't work is somehow getting out of the vehicle. Another issue to do with the Seatruck is that, unlike the Cyclops, you can "park" it in such a way it isn't level. Leaving all your modules inaccessible.-I've had multiple sound bugs, where sounds will overlap each other in odd ways, including cutting off dialog.If you absolutely loved the first game you can probably overlook the above and end up enjoying it anyway. The Land sections are relatively limited and once you're done with them you never have to go back as far as I know. If the Ice Worms and the issues to do with the Seatruck are fixed on release I can definitely recommend this game to anyone. But as it stands, I can only recommend it to someone who wants more Subnautica and has some patience to deal with jank. Most of the new additions to the game are great, especially the new base pieces and the new biomes are stunning as always. Really hoping I can amend this review come May.
