_childDocuments_.review: To anyone who wants to buy the game:This game is a five out of ten because the deliver is astonishing; the script on the other hand is half-bake and feels unfinished. I really enjoyed the animations, the art style, the world design, and the voice acting as they are all very well done and something to be proud about. However, it feels exactly like the first game but with snow. If you enjoy survive mode in the first game and want to explore some new biomes then it might be worth it, but the game play mechanics, the farming, and story format are all the same as the original game. To anyone who wants to hear me rant about the story: (Warning: I will be harsh with my words)Honestly, what upsets me the most is how the writers threw out the original script of the beta release to basically repeat the script of the first game where you're uncovering what happened on the planet instead of the main story taking place in the present. When I played the first release in beta, I absolute loved the characters and the direction of the story. It was so cool and so different and I was so excited to see that story unfold. I waited for the final game to come out so I could uncover the story as a whole and then was met with complete disappointment. The main character is so watered down and flat, but at least the character now matches the plot. There is nothing unique about the main plot that really made me want to play the game. Actually, the section with the Architect and completing his missions were very well done script and delivery-wise, but the larger portion of the script with the sister and Marguerit do not add any value to the game; if anything, they cheapened it. The rewritten story with the virus and the antidote basically felt like I was repeating the first game.  I really REALLY WISHED they stuck with the originally idea for the story, and I am extremely disappointed that instead of working on that story for two years, the writers threw it out for a script that felt like it took one month to make and was made with no care or attention put into it. The script is so full of holes and it's so repetitive that it makes me question whether the writers actually worked on the script or just wrote a first draft and said done. If Unknown worlds remade the game with the original beta script, I would honestly buy the game again just to see that original script unfold because that's how good the original script and characters were. But because they released the game with a story that is so empty and followed the virus idea of the first game, I honestly have considered getting a refund. Of course what I say is harsh, a lot of people worked on the game, and that I don't know why they changed the script, however that doesn't change my disappointment in the final story. To developers:If any developers stumble onto this review, I want to say the physical world you built for this game is amazing and very well done. However, I was so invest and very much admired the original story and characters that it actually inspired me and influenced some of my own character designs and stories, and in the end, I am genuinely heart-broken that the original story and characters are sitting in the trash. I know it's late, but I beg you to please please please remake the game to bring back the original story with Sam alive and on the Vesper and Robin in the ocean hiding Al-an from them. I will pay for that story to be made and I know a lot of other people will too.  Please consider.P.S. If anyone wants to tell me off in the comments or add to my discussion, have fun:)

_childDocuments_.review: Below Zero takes the original Subnautica, and subtracts the reapers and good writing, and fills in the void with a linear plot, more cave diving, and a generous dose of Amnesia-style walking simulation. If the above sounds appealing, or you're an absolute Subnautica fanatic, then this game might be for you.For me, this game is absolutely murdered by it's terrible level design. Everything is confusing and misleading. Key areas are carefully hidden using obscuring terrain, weather effects, or misleading pathing. Again, I'm not talking about hiding bonuses or easter eggs; these are core plot points. In some areas, it wasn't enough to watch a youtube walkthrough. I had to have the video open on a separate screen, and then play it a few seconds at a time while copying each twist and turn.This Byzantine level design somehow coexists with an extremely linear plot. There is exactly one order in which events should occur, and if you do them differently the dialog won't make sense or you won't have any indication of what to do next. I got things out of order and solved all of my problems (sister's death solved, finished her work). I then had to wander around randomly to figure out what unstated plot point was keeping me on the planet.Speaking of plot: the overall plot of the original Subnautica didn't make a ton of sense, but it was functional. And it was carried by the dry, dystopian humor of the PDA and other audio logs. Below Zero started ok, but the bottom falls out remarkably quickly. At times the dialog is so sparse and blatantly functional that it sounds like the voice actors are reading from a plot outline. Special mention to the PDA lines for being particularly awful. No idea what happened there.The original Subnautica had fantastic visuals and atmosphere. There were a bunch of colorful, visually distinct biomes, each with their own soundscapes and fauna. Below Zero is just... muddled. In some places, everything is crammed together, and in others there's huge stretches of absolutely nothing. The biomes aren't very interesting or distinct. They all seem to offer some of every resource, so it's hard to remember which is which. You're constantly under threat from small predators, but hardly ever see proper Leviathans. Bottom line, I've put a ton of time into Subnautica, and I don't think I'm going to bother finishing this. I don't know if this is COVID-19 and remote work killing the magic, or if someone's ego got out of check, but this game is not good on its own merits, and is particularly bad as a sequel to a game as good as Subnautica.

_childDocuments_.review: *Spoiler Warning*The gameplay isn't too bad bad but after the first couple hours it just becomes a bore. Upgrades are limited and most of them are straight-up useless since the only vehicle you need is the prawn-suit(unless you're some kind of base builder that must have a base in every biome, then the sea-truck storage would seem compelling).Danger-wise there is only 1 sea-level leviathan with the rest of the big-ones just being a double-sized version of the normal monsters. The ice-worm is just an annoyance that gets you off the hover-bike if you don't time your speed boost.The land game-play is poorly done, the hover-bike is a down-grade from just straight-up using the prawn to traverse land. Food just fills you up with water and nutrients plus the land peppers give you heat too(making managing your heat redundant since you find them in every cave).The story is a mess, your main objective for going into this planet is tossed aside completely and getting the alien out of your head becomes the priority. You can straight-up ignore any if not all of the search for your sister because it affects nothing.The *side* objective of helping the other woman on the planet has no further interactions, no goodbyes when it comes to the end to leave the planet or when you discover and complete your sister's retarded quest of curing the infection.Depth exploration is useless, you can get the most important material around 500-600 depth and return when your alien buddy needs his body. The whole game can just be spent in your prawn suit 24/7.Compared to the Original game, this one is a HOT mess of a poorly written story, uninteresting mc(making the protag a*strong**angry**female* with no other notable characteristics with a retarded goal that gets tossed aside isn't something that will make anyone remember Robin), exploration is just look for the upgrade and never look back at that biome unless it has one material you can't find in the other ones and vehicle progression is non-existent as all you need is the prawn which can be aquirred in the first 2 hours of gameplay.Overall a 5/10, boring land content, less aquatic content and bad story. Just buy it on sale if you really wanna play but it's not worth the £25 price. If you haven't played the OG Subnautica then buy that one and never look at this mess.

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable game and I liked the experience. There's a lot of complaints from people about the game not making you feel the same way as Subnautica did as the protagonist in this isn't silent anymore and isn't stranded on the planet by accident and arrives there by choice, but I personally feel that just copy-pasting everything from the original wouldn't have been the right way to go. The changes make this game feel distinct enough. The precursor quest was by far my favourite one. Overall, this is a a decent experience but Subnautica is still the better game.

Also for the jukebox thanks for allowing players to add their own music to it, I loved jamming to night of nights as I evade a shadow leviathan. Negatives:However, The game feels significantly shorter if I remove all the time I spent making my base look cool. The safe area you begin in is straight in the middle of all the content you need to get to making it easy to go to one side of the map and refuel in the safe area then go to a new place. The land area, while I enjoy its addition I cannot help but feel it takes away from the initial feel of subnautica, stuck in the ocean with things that wanna tear your face off. The last major negative I wanna touch on is the sea truck module that allows you to just zap a leviathan and move on, it’s busted and I felt no danger anymore if this easy to find module could literally make this game a baby game. _childDocuments_.review: This game is just as good as the previous one.They are however quite different. Subnautica: Below Zero focuses on different things than the original game. In Subnautica the focus was a lot more on the survival aspect, it was carefully curated so that you progress in a much slower pace, it was scary and the narration was something that was there to grab your attention and nudge you along to explore. But before anything it was supposed to make you feel alone, struggling to survive.In this second adventure the focus isn't as much on the survival, because honestly I would have lost my mind if I had to run around collecting stalker teeth and such so that I can make shiny glass. The survival elements are still strong, the story still pushes you to go to places and explore, but the main difference is that there is so much story, I couldn't really imagine what else they could put in terms of technology. The main focus is quite the opposite, you aren't alone, you're there to explore, and uncover all the secrets you can. And there's plenty of secrets.The world may not be as big, but it's definitely as rich, beautiful and in places terrifying. I've played through both games and I've thoroughly enjoyed them both. P. S. Make sure you play on Hardcore difficulty as this is the only thing in my opinion that the Subnautica series handles poorly: death.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't exactly call this game worse to the original Subnautica just "different".Where as the OG had its strength in exploration and horror, below zero puts more of an emphasis on Storytelling.Lets start with the cons:The new vehicle has a certain charm to it as you slowly expand and upgrade, but once maxed out the Seatruck essentially just becomes a slower Cyclops with no Seamoth to spare. The lack of a fast smaller submarine to compensate for the Seatrucks tardiness makes diving in the late game caves tedious, the only saving grace is that you still get the prawn suit and have the possibility to eject the containers of the Seatruck to gain speed and use it as a "seamoth replacement"This brings me to my next point, the map size is smaller. While some may believe it to be to the games detriment i think this is for the best because it means you have to spent less time travelling with the Seatruck and the games strong suit isn't exploration to begin with.My next issue is the atmosphere, you feel a lot less lonely and scared, this is because the player character talks, there are a couple of characters to meet on the map along, coupled with the new sountrack.The new soundtrack doesn't stand out, with the only exception that stuck with me being the crystal cave soundtrack. All these contribute to atmosphere that is a lot less scary and unnervingLast on my list of cons was the new land zone/gameplay.I was really excited for that part of the game. The game provides you with more in depth temperature mechanics compared to the OG, drink and food to keep warm as well as interesting flora that provides warmth.Seeing all these new mechanics i expected that the land portion of the game would entail a dangerous trek through frozen waste and tundra, huddling for warmth while trying to avoid packs of alien polar bears and Iceworms all in the hopes of reaching a distant research station far out in the arctic plains!Instead i was met with a maze canyon with a few snowstalkers scattered about and the occasional iceworm attack. All these supplies i gathered were useless as you can reach the arctic station with the snowfox with minimal effort.It is clear that gameplay and atmosphere isn't the games strength. What this game instead excels at is the storytelling, they made some nice quality of life improvements, imnproved building and built upon the voice log storytelling of the OG.While the story isn't without flaw,  It does provide an interesting and compelling relationship between the player character and one of the people you later meet in the game. As they both struggle to find out what happened on the planet and form a bond over the course of the journey.To conclude, I would recommend to only buy this game when it is on sale or something. The gameplay makes the 30 euro price hardly worth it, it feels more akin to a story focused dlc that expands on the lore of the original, instead of a standalone sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Subnautica 1 was such an impeccable masterpiece in every facet. The story, gameplay, immersion, and fear factor have held up so well since its release back in 2014. What subnautica did best, Below Zero has done exponentially better. During the first couple months of this game, you followed Samantha Ayou, a researcher for Altera, trying to find more about the Architects, and the Karah virus. That story line didn't last long, which at first, was disorienting. Since the last big update, the new story follows Sam's older sister, Robin Ayou, finding what happened to Sam. On Robins adventure, she stumbles upon an Aecherect named Ai-an. Without giving too much of the story away, these two characters traverse the frosty land of 4546B, searching for Altera research facilities to reveal Sams fate, along with giving Aian a new body. To a newcomer just now purchasing this game, it's fantastic. The story is rich, it has many critical thinking moments, and it questions the morality of man-kind, a lot like SOMA. While giving you this, it also delivers a great gameplay experience where you can forge your own path and do the story, for the most part, in however you deem fit. They're still a lot of bugs in the game, some more annoying than others, but they're mostly very minor. Purchase this game if you enjoy narrative drivin, survival horror, strategy, and/or psychological horror games. Games similar to this - SOMA, Subnautica 1, Observation, Observer, Amnesia, Narcosis, Bioshock; 1&2.

_childDocuments_.review: Still a great game, but just not as good as the first.A lot of unnecessarily added mechanics, things that are added to the game just to make it feel more full.  There are some pretty cool moments that are reminiscent of the first game, but mostly it just seems like they are trying to replicate a formula and not doing the best job at it.There is no need to have a fully voiced character or show the faces of so many others that are never really shown at all throughout the rest of the story.Overall, I would give it a 7.5/10.  Enough good parts to outweigh the bad parts, but still very much Subnautica. Get it while it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazingly fun game. It feels smaller than the prequel but there is a lot to do to spend your time. The surface gameplay has been greatly expanded and the modular sea truck is a smart addition. Base-building is as awesome as always.I wish the game was more upfront about what you have to do at some point though. Exploration and discovery is fun but at points it feels like you're stuck. The log is not a big help when that happens. The payoff is great when you finally figure out where to go to but the devs could have killed a lot of dead time in the making.The only real downside I see is the missing multiplayer. This game would be ten times as fun if you could play it with 1 to 7 other friends and really build a giant home for your squad. The singleplayer experience is fine but everyone who played a base-building game with friends knows the difference.To me Subnautica: Below Zero is a great sequel and I recommend you buy it if you liked the first one or base-building, exploration games in general.

_childDocuments_.review: Original Subnautica is certainly better. This one isn't really an open-world Sandbox like the last one; they took a different direction and this is a campaign game. The main character is much more prominent in the story and even has a voice. You also aren't alone on the planet, there are some other quite silly borderlands-inspired characters.Can't say I really like the change but there are some new things in the arctic environment that are nice to explore. This game could have been really good if they built on the original formula and just added more stuff. But, as is, you're kind of forced through a generic, poorly scripted story if you want to see the new things they added to the world. If you're okay with that and pick the game up on a discount after enjoying the original, then good.

_childDocuments_.review: Spoiler freeAn amazing "Wtf was that noise" simulator. Just like the first game.First and foremost, if you are reading this and you loved Subnautica, then you will love Subnautica Below Zero. I've seen some negativity saying this game "stripped the spirit" of the original Subnautica by adding/removing the features listed below (Like traversing land or having a smaller world). This is false. The spirit of the first game is not only intact, but it's even stronger due to some of the changes made. Differences listed below:Differences:+ Much bigger focus on the narrative, with actual characters to learn about and cooperate with. This doesn't change the core of the game, which is basically swim around discovering things at your own leisure in whatever direction or fashion you decide to do it in, just like the first game. You slowly uncover what happened/is happening as you progress. Each new area presents new dangers which you will have to find ways to equip yourself for.+ The new characters are great, especially Robin, our Protagonist. She is witty and isn't afraid to ask hard questions even if her life is in direct danger. + Solid voice acting all around. Their personalities are brought to life as you learn about them and maybe even what happened to them.+ The soundtrack is still great.+ New Items+ New Enemies+ There are landmasses to traverse in this one and specific items utilized for these landmasses+ This game is longer than the first (First being ~20 hours. This one being ~25-30 hours depending on your playstyle).+/- I honestly don't remember if the world itself is smaller than the first game, but it doesn't even matter. There is still a big rich and deep world out there with more content than the first game, and you will love it all the same. Quality > Quantity in this instance.+/- The Cyclops is gone. If that is the game breaker for you, as I see in so many reviews on here (and wow), then yeah, you can dodge this game. It's been replaced with the Seatruck which has overall better utilization since you can attach/detach the components you want or need.The rest is mostly identical. Solid gameplay with smooth optimization and plenty of (new) fish to run away from.If you are still reading by this point, then do yourself a favor and PLAY SUBNAUTICA FIRST, then come play this game. Both are absolutely fantastic experiences.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Super entertaining game, although the last ~10% sucks. Just like in the original Subnautica, the survival, exploration and craft appeal of the game sticks with you as you go throughout the story, until all of the sudden, it disappears. The writing of the ending is fine and seeing it unfold through the cinematic type stuff is okay. It's just the in-game requirements to get the story completed which feel underwhelming and tedious. Up until the latter part of the game, there's always new exploration, enhancements, items, etc. to keep you hooked, all while the main story progresses. This is what keeps the game compelling. Toward the end, that excitement was gone and I only kept with it to see how the story would end. Like finishing up a delicious meal with a bland dessert, the ending somewhat spoils what would be an otherwise perfect game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an excellent follow up to the first game.  Telling more stories in the world of SubNautica is exactly what I was hoping for and they delivered perfectly. I highly recommend this game to anyone who liked the first SubNautica game and I look forward to what this studio produces in the future.

Also there's some nice little details linking it to the first game. The only thing this game lacks is that glorious seamoth purring sound.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Now I'm gonna be honest with this review, I really think Subnautica Below Zero is bad, I've played the hell out the first Subnautica, time and time again. While the game had issues, it was fantastic regardless. Story was simple, progression was straight forward, get seaglide, get seamoth, then Prawn or Cyclops then the other. Then head deeper and deeper underwater. This game is a mess. The beginning was fantastic, beautiful and I was in love with the idea of having a sentient ai being stuck inside your head. But the interactions sounds so forced, like dialogue you'd expect rather than being what would feel natural. Progression is a mess, I've had so much trouble with trying to progress that it just put me off. Get seaglide, get seatruck next. And from there well you need to upgrade the seatruck up, more modules, get a prawn spot. But the problem is, that from there its a mess. You can go either on land to where those ice worms or whatever are. Even that wasn't done well as I just took my prawn suit there and was able to go up on top of the cliffs to avoid it. Or you can go deep to the Prawn suit lady, Maiter or something I forget. She tasks you with disabling the comm tower, you could also go to the old ship. This is as far as I got. They screwed up with this game, like I understand they ran into so many problems while making this game. But it just doesn't have the same feel of the first Subnautica, it isn't the same type of terror in this game. You don't get the same sense of terror and loneliness that you experienced in the first game, being the sole survivor of a ship wreck, finding out your crew was picked off one by one from an unknown creature. You don't feel the sense of horror that you are alone, on an ocean world plagued by giant sea monsters and a deadly alien virus.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Subnautica, you'll probably enjoy this one well enough. Silent Protagonist is gone, replaced by someone else. There's a lot more dialogue and 'plot' given to you through PDAs. My biggest gripes were holdovers from the original and slightly worsened. I find it absolutely impossible to navigate and build a mental map of either game. Exploration is therefore fairly annoying for me. Below Zero has the issue of a much wider progression, with the result that I did the plot almost completely backwards.Don't go into this expecting anything new or better. It's more of the original but slightly different.

_childDocuments_.review: It's nowhere near as fun as the first game - the above-ground sections are an absolute mess, the vehicle is kinda clunky compared to the Seamoth and nowhere near as cool as the Cyclops, a lot of the biomes are a bit bland and self-repeating, the story is janky and not as cohesive as the original (despite being fed to you more), there's no Hoverfish, no Cuddlefish and barely any cool Leviathans, and the game lacks direction when exploring - but it's still a damn good game, had a great time with it, love the new base-building pieces, and still shed a tear when I had to say goodbye.

_childDocuments_.review: Even in early release, as of Jan 2021 this game is pretty awesome. Two serious crashes over 52 hours, and those were fixed by using the public Beta (definitely improved graphics over the official early access version - go fo the public Beta at this point)  It has "atmosphere" similar to the original Subnautica, except now you're in an Arctic biome rather than a tropical one. A "survival" game without weapons, you start off digging into the suspect circumstances of your sister's "accidental" death at a research facility. But it's abandoned, so you have to find your way around based on diaries and notes. The outdoor environment is mildly hostile - you're either under water (and tethered to oxygen) or in freezing air (and needing warmth). There are references to events in the original Subnautica, but I'm pretty sure you don't have to have played the original to enjoy the current one (hard for me to tell, having played through the original at least twice).But this game and its cousin excels at creating an environment that's simply fun to hang out in and explore. I've been in no hurry to "solve" the problem I originally set out for (and when I did solve it, I was in the middle of, um, larger quests) - I look forward to spending a few hours just learning the lay of the land & sea, and seeing what I might discover.
_childDocuments_.name: Subnautica: Below Zero

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. It takes what Subnautica did great and improves upon it, while also adding more interesting things, such as larger landmasses, temperature, as well as a much better and more present story and characters. The gameplay is very similar to Subnautica, so if someone wanted to play one of them, I'd recommend this one, since it's such an improvement. Although, I played Subnautica a lot before playing Below Zero and none of the gameplay felt old or repetitive. Definitely a must buy. Also using the wiki was necessary for me, as a few materials were in places I didn't know the location of.

_childDocuments_.review: Yea.. So I had some hard time with deciding whether to recommend this game or not. It's definitely got its moments, but most of the time you feel like playing one of these "bigger DLCs" where you get a reskin of the base game.!!!!!!All right, so there is some fresh content that ALSO fits in nicely - I liked how the devs made the game to "kindly persuade" you into using fins rather than vehicles- Oxygen fauna/flora is a nice addition and require you to cleverly plan your next moves in the  or in open water. It also makes it less stressful when you know that there might be another "bubble" just round the corner.There are some nice visuals like   or  - these are the top of the topFrom the good things, The facelifted Prawn Suit is also worth mentioning, as it finally feels more robust and versatile, than the old one which was basically a walking brick. Even the Seatruck , despite its bulkiness and lack of maneuverability.I liked the quick entry in the plot, without the "oh boy here we go again- a fresh start" moments, where you are basically taking classes in "the game 101".Some fauna was nice, some was funny, but I didn't feel overwhelmed by it, for the most time.Despite all the above fancy biomes, a bunch of new items and few clever tweaks, the game feels mostly like Subnautica 1.0, but with other assets. I don't say its bad- its in fact good, cause why change something that works?But when it comes to exploring, you see this damn fog for most of the time - I mean it, player's range of view is seriously limited and won't let you see the beauty of most biomes.NAY, most of the "surface" biomes feel small if not cramped and repetitive- you basically see one of 4- creepvine, vents, bald, black plains and some twisted tentacle-like bridges. I assume that because of their size, devs tried to hide it behind some fake fog and muddy water - OK, it could work, if it wasn't enabled basically everywhere. I swear to God, you saw further in Sub1's Lost River than in most of Sub:BZ's biomes. Lillypads might be great, but I simply can't see much of them.When it comes to cave biomes- well it gets better, but its simply because you usually expect caves to be small, but at least here you get to see something new and totally fresh. Notice how often I used the word  in the above part? It's cause like 75% of this game takes action in caves- you won't see the sun very often. And despite all the work put into making them easier to navigate.. they're still caves - if you won't mark some POIs, you'll get lost and frustrated.I won't even mention the DEPTHS in this game, where the deepest biome ENDS @  meters- you don't get that "oh boi, we are reeeaaaallyyy deep now" feel. Instead you just keep thinking "when it'll get deeper its gonna be fun!", until you realize you've hit the bottom and its time to swim up.Also the WORLD EDGE biome is all bad - where in Sub1 you knew you gotta stop swimming and turn back, in here you wake up @ 600-800 meters just walking down the easy peasy slope, and some strange sharko-shrimps start attacking you outta nowhere.Now, the infamous Seatruck...Ok, I see the point- traveling on map where most of it is in caves can prove difficult when you have to backtrack for every single thing, so why not just haul it all? In that field, Seatruck really does its job- as a freight mule and huge portable storage. When it comes to actual traveling, well... Remember when I said about the game "persuading" you into using fins and Seaglide? Well there you have it- no more quick touch and go in lightweight vehicle with unlimited supply of oxygen- now you pretend to be a snail, hauling all the cargo with you, exiting only when you need to collect something.So, to close this bulby boi (cause of its front window :B1:) topic - it feels like flying a brick, but at least you don't have to go back for most of things.All right, now the plot.THE PLOT IS MEH, one of the MEH'est in recent time. Either I did ♥♥♥♥♥♥ something up, or there was basically no closure- just . Tadaa, nothing else. Meeting with Sea Emperor in Sub1, or even leaving scene was more climatic than any of Sub:BZ parts.Where in Sub1 you felt the need to continue searching for clues, in Sub:BZ you simply end the game and feel like you wasted at least half of the time.Yep, that's what I said - paying full price for it feels like scam, cause it simply doesn't add that much content, that much plot and that much biomes, as the first one.But getting it on like 40-50% promo? Go for it- it has its moments of "aww", some fun parts and even if you take into account quite the long list of "nays" above, its still worth giving it a go.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, please don't hate me, I already left a review for Subnautica and talk about Below Zero at the end of it, so it is attached after I say a little bit more about this "take two" on Subnautica. First of all, if you LOVED Subnautica from start to finish you may like Below Zero (anything's possible right?). But if you were starting to get worn out by the end, or if it ever felt tedious, do yourself a favor and skip Below Zero! Seriously, this could ruin both games for you!Everything that made Subnautica a slog just seems worse in Below Zero, and that despite obvious attempts to streamline this second chapter. If you love swimming around in disorientating caves searching for blueprints that may, or may not, have spawned so you can get the gear that you (think) you need to proceed in the game, then -look no further-! This is the game for you, you can waste countless hours wandering in circles while fretting over you o2, thirst and hunger levels! Yes, all the things that make your daily life a frustrating challenge without any of the reward (sorry, as much as it's reassuring to hear the player take that big gasp of air after nearly drowning, or crunch crunch crunch on some salted fish, I am not vicariously enjoying any of these experiences).But that's not the best of it. The best is that Below Zero is buggy! Yup, get off your hoverbike and fall -through- the glacier into the ocean below. Did I mention that this is a very large glacier? Good luck swimming to the edge before you drown... dummy, why didn't you plan for that? Okay, you used the "unstuck" feature to survive that death trap... now you're in the middle of the glacial ice fields, and the only way you can survive is by using your hoverbike to stay warm. Now there are ice worms that knock you off your bike periodically, no problem, but whoops, meant to get back on your bike but you picked it up and put it in your inventory instead. No problem, I'll redeploy this vehicle and escape this frozen hellscape lickity split... except the hoverbike just clipped through the glacier to the ocean below... okay, how are you gunna survive that one dummy? To be fair, I didn't notice a lot of penalties to dying, actually got me back to my seatruck faster... maybe I missed a valuable game mechanic... just get the components I need, then die... voila! Like free teleportation. Gotta love it.Another gripe, and I'll lose some of you here. But I think this game might be woke... No seriously, I read comments about the new player character being a BIPOC female, but that didn’t throw me, she’s completely normal throughout the game. But the new PDA voice has a thick Indian accent (google it, I’m not the only one scratching their head)? Okay, that's a little off putting (and difficult to understand sometimes), but the commentary is bizarre. “In the control room, you can change base lighting and colors, rename your base, and see information about power and structural integrity. But not the integrity of societal power structures.” Wait, what?! That one stuck with me, but there are some other strange “jokes.” Then there’s this alien database where they’re talking about their “replication,” because they can “copy themselves as many times as they want,” and “perpetuate themselves forever,” or something like that, but “that would be shameful, and any architect inclined to do that should just delete themselves.” Wait, what?!?! I’m taking it these guys aren’t pro-life…Okay, obviously I didn’t like that game. Below is the review I wrote for Subnautica, if you’ve played Subnautica you’ll probably get an idea from it as to whether you will agree with me about Below Zero.Okay, nevermind... My review is too long, Steam won't let me post it. You can probably find my review for Subnautica if you look for it. My guess is that no one will care enough to do so (my guess is very few people are still reading now, but if you are, thank you. You are very patient, you might actually like this game). I will try to clip the part about Below Zero from the other review and paste it here (please excuse the repeated story):"It got way worse in Below Zero though. They added a bit more "quest prompts" and some other characters to interact with too, but the game is way buggier than the original subnautica. And now we have freezing to add to the survival mix (I turned hunger and thirst off, no way I was going to play through that again). So on one occasion I deploy my hoverbike (which keeps you warm) and whoops... it just fell through the earth. I don't have a hoverbike anymore... Please excuse me while I run around wildly and freeze to death. Or the blueprints for the quest item that don't appear Margeurite's desk after she tells you to pick them up. I didn't know anything was wrong until I spent 3 hours wandering the world trying to figure out what I missed. Then I googled it, found out this was a common bug, submitted a bug report, then went back to Margeurite's and... okay, they're on the table now? They weren't there before, and that's not the desk where she told me to pick them up... but cool... I guess? At least I finished the quest. Then I started searching for the leviathan cure. Spent a few hours wandering around the glacier with a map that looked like it was drawn by a child (in the future everyone is far less competent than they are today... I didn't know that was possible...) and finally I got so bored I just looked it up on youtube, Oh... I have to swim under the glacier... Well THAT wasn't on the map. After that I got fed up and looked the rest of the quests up on youtube. 20 hours was WAY TOO MUCH time to give that game.What a waste. I wouldn't call this a game. But if you don't have a real life that needs attending to I suppose you can engage with a very frustrating "alien planet survival simulator."

_childDocuments_.review: Not really an improvement over the first game. Besides a few new base buildings, new items and one or two UI changes most of the game is and plays the same.  The new items and base building possibilities are great additions. The pinning of recipes is a great idea.Only if they didn't remove one of the best parts of the predecessor, the seamoth and the cyclops. Their replacement in the seatruck is just an abomination. It's designed to be a middle ground between the agile and fast seamoth and the cyclops, as a mobile base. But it fails on both ends. It's cumbersome to move around, slow, once a few compartments are attached, and even with all the compartments attached it doesn't come close to being a cyclops replacement. No more travelling around in the cyclops and the finding an interesting spot, exploring further with the seamoth, no more transporting the Prawn suit to mining locations or intense resource gathering without worrying about inventory space.  So a big step back in every possible way.  So why on earth did they keep the Prawnsuit and removed these two? The other vehicle, the snow fox, is not really great either. It's clumsy and unresponsive to use, and in all the small canyons and labyrinths it's only slightly faster than walking. This leads to another big disappointment, the overwater stuff. I don't know why they decided to focus more on that, but, as it was in the first game, it is still the weakest part of the game. While the underwater world feels interesting, very atmospheric and alien, the land part is just one boring glacial canyon after the other. No real diversity or interesting level design. In contrast to the amazing world underwater, the land just can't keep up. In the end you have an amazing water world to explore, a kinda interesting story to follow (still preferred the storytelling method of the first game), and good item crafting and base building.  But inventory management becomes so horrible and frustrating that base building and resource gathering is more work than fun.  So that leaves only the underwater world. And that was already amazing in the first game...

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish there was a "Meh" button.Unfortunately though for BZ there isn't and even more unfortunately I have played my fair share of the original Subnautica. As a result there are certain expectations as to BZs potential and where it fails spectacularly.Story:BZ is much more focussed on story than it's predecessor. The main protagonists seems to be talking pretty much nonstop, there's PDAs and lore everywhere and there's even a real, living  person you get to meet and interact with. All of this sounds great at first but for a survial game it really isn't. You don't really get any sense of "Robin(son) Crusoe in Space" when there's a grumpy old lady living just 400 meters next to you. BZ also makes the mistake of overexplainign the alien architects, robbing them of most of their mystery while simultaneously not fleshing them out enough where it counts. For example, AL-AN referring to themselves as basically a hivemind makes no logical sense when they later take blame for the Kaara outbreak like an indivudal would. But the idea of an alien that identifies as "we"sounded good on paper I guess so why think about the deeper implications of that concept. It also doesn't help that the main protagonist can pretty much be summed up as "Looking for her sister, hates Alterra, is always sassy"...Visuals:BZ is a noticeable improvement compared to its predecessor. The creature design is mostly fantastic, biomes feel very unique and different compared to anything the basegame has to offer and there's less empty space with endlessly repeating textures. Instead of sculpting pretty much everything from a blob of terrain like in the basegame the devs went back to more commonly used methods of building a map which allows for more realistic and diverse environments. Overall the visuals are a vast improvement even though you'll still occasionally find some necgelcted areas that are mostly barren with nothing but repeating textures and a handful of stones here and there.Sound:It's okay I would say but inferior to the original in pretty much every aspect. Whenever you hear a great soundfile like "Welcome aboard captain" you can be pretty sure it was lifted from the original. The loading screen music doesn't stand a chance vs the original and so do most other tracks but at least it's not to distracting. And the jukebox has everything from "makes my ears bleed" to catchy earworms. Still can't close my eyes wihtout hearing "swim up swim up" in the back of my head.Leveldesign:The original had a lot of open areas whereas BZ is more focussed on a smaller scale combined with a higher density of content and for the most part, this new formula works. A new form of oxygen plants that give you a one time air boost allows the player to explore areas without beeing to dependent on a fixed air supply. The result is a freer but also riskier exploration that's very fun to play. There are also more environmental hazards that will incapacitate you for a certain amount of time adding another layer to the "running out of time" aspect exlporation in Subnautica has always had. I do however see three big issues with BZs leveldesign. 1. lack of  depth (literally). At its deepest point BZ is about 900 m deep, That's half of the original. Diving down into the abyss is what made fun in the original and there's very little of that in BZ. 2. The Map feels to small. Sure the original had a lot of empty space but in BZ you feel like swimming in a pond rather than an ocean and the fear of the unknown that might lurk out there suffers tremendously as a result. 3. The land sections are a pain in the butt. Horrible visibility, clunky movement, almost no interactivity, annoying enemies and the complete loss of vertical movement make these sections a chore. I don't mind exploring small icebergs and such but the larger landsections almost made me quit the game more than once.Building.There are lots of cool new ways to customize your base such as a control center, that allows to change the color and powerusage of your base, glass ceilings and a giant sized multipurpose room that is highly customizeable. Unfortunately in terms of gameplay these new building options don't change much though. If you were waiting for say a defense system against leviathans, more interesting flooding mechanics or some other evolutionary tech like a teleportation station you'll be dissapointed.Tools:Mostly the same as in SN. There's a mineral finder which I rarely used and that's pretty much it. Vehicles. I wont be talking about land vehicles in this section since I'm not ready yet to relive the utter madness that is handling the snowfox in a snowstorm. I also won't talk about the Prawn suit since it's pretty much identical to the original. I do however mourn the loss of the Seamoth (its speed would have made the map look even smaller I guess). The newly introduced seatruck is an interesting concept though which I quite liked. It offers a lot of comfort and customization while being clunky and slow which I thought was a fair tradeoff. Overall the selection of vehicles in the original is clearly better.Creatures.I'm a big fan of Alex "Abiogenesis" Ries and his designs. I've followed his various social media for years and seeing his influences in designs like the squidshark was fantastic. But also in terms of gameplay BZ has made some steps forward. There's giant holefish sending swarms of parasites after you, fish that can freeze you if you get to close, plants that drag you down and adorable little f*ckers named "sea monkeys" which will steal your tools if you don't hide them quick enough. I still whish there was more meaningful interaction with the local wildlive but it's definitely a big step forward.ProgressionThis one is probably the biggest failure of the entire game. In the original the design was simple. You basically start on top of an underwater mountain and your goal is to get to the bottom of it. Along the way you'll find new tech and plot elements. Have fun! In BZ the entire pacing is a mess. Visiting a base on the surface will shower you in blueprints which takes away the joy finding a better solution to insufficient tech you've previously had to deal with. When unlocking a vehicle it also unlocks all depth modules meaning you can build a fully geared uo prawnsuit in no time if you want to. Navigating the surface early in the game, which requires barely any equipment, is more dangerous than anything even the deepest trenches BZ have to offer. Oh and once you can dive past 400 meters you've pretty much seen every creature and ressource thats in the game with one or two exceptions. But there's a bunch of neat looking crystal formations down there so yay I guess. Just thinking about all the fantastic wildife, ressources and environments you would encounter for the first time when reaching the lost river biome in the original for the first time makes BZ pale in comparison. Performance:Noticeably better than in the original but still a far cry from good. There's a lot of popins and textures loading slowly. But at least you can now enter vehicles and buildings without microfreezes.Verdict.There are a few moments when BZ almost reaches the levels of quality the original had but all too often it is quite obvious the devs didn't really understand what made the original a surprise hit. At the end of the day BZ is only worth the money if you are desperate for a worse version of Subnautica. One thing is for sure, I will no longer throw my money at UWE in early access.

_childDocuments_.review: Following on from the hundreds of hours I sunk into Subnautica, the idea of a sequel terrified me as much as it excited me. If you came to the reviews to see if Below Zero was like the first Subnautica, I'll make it quick: Below Zero's narrative shifts tightens its focus on Robin, your avatar in this frozen hellscape. Unlike Ryley, Robin has thoughts and feelings and desires. She exhibits fear and responds to the world, often without your input. The more I played, the more I found that it didn't diminish the experience at all. It was just different to what I was expecting after the first Subnautica. Let it get its hooks in you and there's a personal story within Below Zero. In Subnautica, I always wondered about the lives and exploits of the voices we hear over the many PDAs we find. The lifepod survivors and the Degasi crew. In Below Zero, I felt like I was living one of those smaller stories.Can you still slack off and built amazing bases? Absolutely! The base building feels even more satisfying in Below Zero; with so many more options for customising your base to your liking. Even the above ground bases are worthwhile in many areas!My return to 4546b was incredible. I felt like I was coming home, but someone had redecorated while I was gone.

_childDocuments_.review: This game misses the point of the original Subnautica. What really made the original Subnautica so incredible was the world. It was mysterious, scary and dangerous. You were thrown into it without a clue of where to go, surrounded by monsters far bigger than you, whom could swim way faster than you. The waters were deep, seeing the floor of the ocean from the surface was almost always an unlikely thing - everything felt more visceral compared to Below ZeroBelow Zero strangely feels as though it's the first game in the series, and the original Subnautica is the sequel, it's simply "less" of a game compared to the original. Every aspect BZ tries to improve on is something no one asked for, or makes the game less endearing. The world is shallower, literally. It isn't nearly as deep, not that this is typically an issue, but that sense of depth is less refined here, you feel 'safer' which in this game, is actually a bad thing. The vehicles are less interesting, the 'sea truck' is fine, but it doesn't live up to the first games selection of unique vehicles. The cyclops was amazing, it was huge and impressive, could hold your smaller vehicle and it felt like a moving base. Below zero is a worse game without it. Perhaps the biggest issue with Below Zero is the narrative. I'm not even here to discuss the quality of the story, I just think this kind of game is worse as a result of having a main character that speaks and there being people (person) out in the open world. The sense of total isolation and mystery is gone as a result of a more personable story line and it brings context to situations that would have been better off with the players left wondering. Lots of unnecessary personification.I do think our main character is incredibly hard to relate to as well. We know she's a zoologist, we know she hates the corporation Altera, we know she loves her sister, but she's already established before the game starts, and she doesn't really have enough going on, at all, for me to care about her in this story. At most she is a nuisance, at the worst, she actually totally draws you away from the atmosphere and sense of isolation you should be feeling in this game. Overall, there are dozens of small things that make this game feel worse than it's predecessor, I'd simply suggest buying the first game.

_childDocuments_.review: 5/10 - Good game but vastly inferior to the amazing original for the following reasons:-The smaller map (what were they thinking?)-Much less danger - both in terms of drowning risk and hostile creatures (what were they thinking?)-The PDA voice is *REALLY* annoying in BZ.  I want the old one back.  (what were they thinking?)-The silent protagonist of the first game was more immersive.  Robin is annoying.  -The story is not as good  -I miss the Cyclops, which was more fun and more capable than the modular Sea Truck -The sea is too safe.  There are some aggressive creatures but they are more annoying than dangerous.  Air plants are way too plentiful.  -The land portions are ok but nothing special.  Too bad this is such a large portion of the map.-The new vehicles are not particularly great - especially the hoverbike, which handles awkwardly.-No major changes to the formula, only "fixes" things that weren't broken in the first place-No major quality of life changes - stacking inventory would be very nice for instance.In spite of the above, it's an ok game .  The environments are beautiful (just kind of small and not dangerous), the music is great, the engine runs a bit better, and it's fun.  It does not live up to the epic original though.  I have to give it a negative review because it was so disappointing, and I was recently reminded of how bad that awful PDA voice is.  The PDA voice is a microcosm of the game design here.  Take a perfect original, change it just to change it, and end up with something annoying in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Keeping true to the magic of the ocean, and giving more reason to explore above land makes this game a must-have. Developers clearly put the time in making an already beautiful game more amazing. Collecting resources is a bit different and could still evolve after the final game release. The story was very good, but I don't think it reached the epic level that the first version had with its deep philosophical under tone. Below Zero doesn't disappoint as you try to figure out what happened to your sister. Some great enhancements for this version: More customizations (base color) and a new vehicle. I am not sure the necessity of having a Control Room for a base as I didn't have a need for it. On that note, the Prawn suit is not as useful as it was in the first version. You might not even need it at all as resources are spread around in rocks so drilling is not as laboresque. This isn't necessarily a bad thing. As much as I wish there was more storage on the "Sea Truck," you don't need to load up on materials as you did in #1 because materials are balanced and mostly near by or close enough to not have to dedicated an hour to one particular task. Without giving too much more away, the game is a lot of fun with an equal amount of exploring. Some biomes are breathtaking. There are more predators that aren't as casual as the first game, so you will be on your toes... fins.My only hope is that they bring back Time Capsules. One of my favorite post-game time killers. I also miss the stasis rifle for the big guys, especially the annoying ice worm. The game has never been about fighting and that is what helps make it unique.

_childDocuments_.review: Subnautica below zero is… certainly a game.As an early access player who has watched this game improve over time, and a massive subnautica fan, this game really let me down. But I don’t like to be a negative person, so let’s go over the things that this game does right first.1. The fauna designs are very unique. I was pleasantly surprised by the variety of new creatures, it’s definitely worthy of subnautica.2. I loved the expansion on base creation and decorations, as someone who likes to spend way too much time decorating my bases in games, this part definitely was an improvement over the original.3. I really liked the elaboration on architects/precursors. I found them extremely interesting in the original, and the fact that this game expands on them as much as it does made me very happy.4. A colorful cast of characters made the abandoned PDA data fun to find. Recurring characters made me want to seek out the PDAs more than the original, similar to how the degasi crew fascinated me in the original.5. Well.. it’s a subnautica game. It draws a lot of inspiration from the original. And it helped scratch that itch for more content, but it just doesn’t feel rightAnd that leads me into the next part, what I disliked about the game. There is a reason I’m not recommending it, after all.1. Progression and distance. While everything in below zero was roughly the same size as the original, including the map… this game felt smaller. WAY smaller. Unlike the original subnautica, I never felt the need to make separate bases. Whereas in the original subnautica, late-game areas are massive, expansive, and just feel grand and amazing to navigate, in below zero.. these areas are all small, they feel cramped. And they all feel like they’re just a hop, skip, and a jump away from my base near delta station, one of the earliest parts of the game.2. Leviathan population. No, this isn’t a “game too scary!” Situation where I have to git gud, but the leviathan population just feels wrong. I’ve played the original subnautica for hundreds of hours at least, across different platforms. The reaper leviathan still gives me the shivers, I find myself avoiding them at all costs, mostly because of how uncommon they are. Seeing a leviathan in the distance in the middle of a blue void triggers my fear of the ocean in the best way. They feel TERRIFYING.. below zero was like that for a bit too, I got jumped a bit, but with the ridiculous amount of squidsharks and chelicerate that just get hurled at you in areas I commonly passed through for progression… I adjusted fast. Now whenever a Chelicerate attacks me, it’s prompted with a “oh, there you are.” Followed by a sigh of annoyance and a press of the perimeter defense button. They feel more like annoyances than actual scary threats.3. Depth. One of the scariest parts of subnautica for me was going deeper, descending into the void and seeing the environment change around you, from peaceful sandy shallows to creepy bloodkelp areas. In below zero.. I feel I barely notice the change from surface caves to deeper ones, except for the crystal areas, of course. It didn’t feel as nerve-wracking as the original. In this one, you just navigate through tight caves, the only thing that made me notice how deep I actually was were the crush depth notifications.4. Atmosphere, the atmosphere of the original subnautica is perfect, hearing the cry of an unknown creature in the distance sends a shiver down my spine, I have to gather my courage to continue as I inch closer to it, hearing the sounds grow louder as I approach a deep pit. In below zero, near the surface, or everywhere really… it feels like you hear caprosuchus or anything else screaming nearly nonstop. This is scary at first, but it gets old fast. Hearing enemies just fill the ocean with near constant screeching that sounds WAY disproportionate to their size desensitizes you fast. I no longer even see those sounds as a threat, just an annoying background noise that’s nearly constantly playing. These weak enemies have such a powerful roar that it’s almost laughable sometimes. Really ruins the mood.5. The surface. I was excited that we were getting more surface exploration in this game, but it doesn’t deliver at all. The original subnautica has islands with structures that are super fun to explore. In this one, I never used thumpers, I only used the snowfox for like, 5 minutes, barely even used the coldsuit, and completed most of the story content of the surface in nearly 20 minutes. And yes, I do know the surface had very little story content in the original, but this version just felt so barren. The original had fun environments, it was small, but used its space and time wisely to become a pretty cool and memorable part of the game. In below zero the surface was big, boring and bland, just snow, snow, snow. It didn’t feel rewarding to explore at all, and I barely ever felt threatened by ice worms. They’re easily evaded even with just the prawn suit, and I never found myself using the thumpers as a distraction to drill there, because I NEVER drilled there. I found all of the resources I needed underwater, close to the surface, at that. I never had to return there after completing the story content. I was really expecting the surface to be exciting, seeing as SO much content and even a temperature feature and a ton of technology was planned for it. What did I get? A boring landscape and wasted resources for something that took up a minuscule part of the game, one with so many items, and a few awesome creatures attached to it ended up being unmemorable and a total dud. Thank god for the recycler, at least.6. The main point to the story. In the original subnautica we were dumped into an unknown ocean, the objectives felt extremely rewarding and satisfying, exploring the aurora, curing yourself, building the rocket, writing a heartfelt (or not…) message in the time capsule? All of it felt great. In below zero I struggled to find a purpose to keep playing, it just boiled down to basically three components. It didn’t feel rewarding, it didn’t feel time consuming, and the information for this things being withheld just felt boring. Something that could’ve been over way sooner felt like it was just panning for playtime. I wish there was more to it. But that’s about it.

_childDocuments_.review: The positive:  I think if you're at all tempted, you should play this game.  It's beautiful, exploration is compelling, and it feels like a nice extension and expansion of the first game.  When you're getting into new areas and seeing new things, this game can be exhilarating.  And while a lot of the items and mechanics are similar to the first game, it changes up enough that it doesn't just feel like a rehash.  Also, I appreciate that I don't feel blind 80% of the time walking around in the prawn suit like I did in the first game.  I don't know if that's because the headlamp on the prawn suit are better, or if the lighting in general is friendlier, but I like it.As for the negatives:  This won't be a surprise if you've played the first game, but it can be incredibly frustrating when you're lost and looking for something specific.  This is especially true in the large above ground section which has multiple important locations, but they're separated by sections that look almost identical.  It is so easy to get turned around and go in circles.Also, the plot stuff is a little too hands-off at times, despite the game having a more active plot than the first game.  There were a few times while playing where I had something I needed to do, and for every other situation there would be a signal to follow that would nudge me in the right direction, but for whatever reason I had no signal or no guidance to get me there, so I ended up looking it up.And that's the thing.  I get the design choice to not have a map or minimap in these games.  But ultimately it ends up sending me to wikis and guides to try to find things after spending hours searching and getting frustrated.  I think I'd like it more if the game had internal ways to track this sort of thing.All that being said, this game, along with the original, were a really fun time.  Very engrossing.  And I very much look forward to any follow-up on this series.

_childDocuments_.review: Following up Subnautica is a tall order, but Subnautica: Below Zero does a solid job. However, this isn't a "Subnautica 2," it has a significantly different style and feel than its precursor. Firstly, if you haven't played Subnautica, go play it first. Ideally, go into it blind, the element of discovery in that game is truly magical if you aren't aware of what you're going to find, and Below Zero spoils a handful of things that somebody going into the first game blind wouldn't know. Below Zero also has a much bigger focus on story over exploration, and the game pretty explicitly tells you where you need to go most of the time, which honestly in many ways is an improvement, seeing as in the original Subnautica, the map was so enormous you could easily miss the next area you are supposed to expand to, and there isn't as many clues as to where you need to go, although I think in many ways Below Zero tells you a little too explicitly. To get down to the exact differences between the two, firstly the player character in Below Zero is voiced, and there is even a human NPC, which is something I very much was not expecting when I first ran across her. Your character also has an objective, which the game didn't fully sell me on but did well enough that I wanted to progress. As for the real meat of Subnautica the original, the exploration, Below Zero is very different in that a lot of the exploring you do is looking for man made structures which you are vaguely aware of from the start. Because of this, the scale of the things you find is a fair bit smaller, and the map itself is smaller as well. With a more focused objective, I don't see an issue with this, although I did find it very difficult to justify building multiple bases when it would take me 10 minutes tops to get back to my main base (In the cotton anemone caves, probably my favorite biome in either game), so that could be seen as a pro or a con. Below Zero also lacks a submarine of the scale that the Cyclops fills, which I am slightly saddened by, but I also fully understand why: the zones are smaller. In exchange, they are absolutely packed with hand crafted details, and I think almost every biome from Below Zero was ultimately cooler than the biomes from the original Subnautica. However, the set pieces (Think the brine river or the black castle) in the original game were much more impressive in my opinion. Basically, there was cooler spots on Subnautica, but the biomes as a whole were truly majestic by comparison in Below Zero. I also think the music for Below Zero was a lot better, in particular I truly fell in love with the music in the tree spires area. The cold mechanic was also a little dissapointing, it never truly felt like a threat, especially when I could just hop on my snowfox or into my prawn to warm up (by the way, walk diagonally with the prawn, it's way faster for some reason).As for the creatures, I think both games had advantages and disadvantages. Spoilers ahead for creatures, so watch out if you don't want spoilers!Regardless, I highly recommend Below Zero, and enjoyed it immensely!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a mixed bag. Like Subnautica, the early-game is very strong, and it's a treat to explore the new world and discover the map. After that... well, this game has much less interesting and memorable locations as the first game. The leviathans are much less of a threat, to the point where I was almost never actually on-edge while playing. The ending is... well it's a mess, and a massive disappointment. It feels as if there should be multiple endings, but a major storyline in the game is completely optional and doesn't result in anything significant at all besides a bit of dialogue.I am a bit bewildered how the devs didn't learn from their mistakes in the first game, and actually made some of the issues worse. Still recommending it because I enjoyed the majority of the game, but yikes I would definitely play the first over this, just for the more interesting and compelling gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Can't recommend it yet. I like the idea of exploring a new world and there are a lot of new creatures and things to discover, but some changes I just don't think feel right. My biggest hurdle is the new vehicles. The Seatruck is sort of like a modular mash-up of the Seamoth and the Cyclops, but ends up feeling like a lesser version of both. When it's disengaged from its "trailer", it handles pretty familiarly to the Seamoth, but it's odd shape feels cumbersome; the engines sometimes get caught on things in tight spaces and can take bits of damage along the way. The fully stocked "truckin" mode is a far cry from the Cyclops and its repertoire of tools and gadgets. I think the biggest difference is in the visibility and maneuverability. The Cyclops has a wide front view with access to all of your controls, including three external cameras. I spent at least half my time looking through one of those cameras, lining up a tight turn in a cave or keeping an eye on nearby leviathans, always ready to switch back to hit the shields or launch a decoy. I felt powerful by the end of the game in the Cyclops, taking risks and venturing into the bowels of the sea in my giant submarine.The Seatruck by comparison feels much weaker and more awkward to control. It's basically still just a Seamoth, but with a bunch of stuff stuck on the back end, slowing things down. You can't look around without swinging the whole thing around with you and you only have the straight ahead view and a small "backup camera". I felt basically blind trying to get around, especially when there were any particularly large predators in the area. The best you can hope to do is hit the key for boost whenever you hear one roar at you and hope it gives up quick. I would never want this thing anywhere near a leviathan.Everything else so far has been hit or miss. I like some of the new areas, creatures and blueprints, but there seems to be a lot of empty space, especially on land. I assume there are plans to flesh these places out a bit more, but right now it seems like there's a lot of trekking from point A to point B and straight back after you do the story thing, with maybe a hidden cache or two on the side. The new subs are a big miss for me, which is very much taking me out of the game having just come out on such a high note after the first Subnautica. I might wait for the full release to come back and see if it can win me back, but I don't think I'll be touching this one for a while.

_childDocuments_.review: The sequel to Subnautica, although you might also think of it as stand-alone DLC.It's certainly large enough to be thought of as a sequel, clocking in at around 20-30 hours depending on how lost you get and how much exploration you want to do, but I certainly think I got my monies worth. The area of planet 4546B you explore is a bit smaller than the first game, but there's still tons to explore and find.The Buildings are mostly the same as before, but with a few new additions. The Cyclops submarine and Seamoth are both gone, replaced by the modular Seatruck instead. It's a nifty idea that works well enough for the region you're in. I miss the Cyclops a bit but it really wouldn't fit through all the small passages here anyway, so it's not a big loss.Speaking of... prepare to go free-swimming through loads of tight caves this time around, the 3D-map of the Seaglide is actually useful now. While navigating without it is doable, you're bound to miss stuff if you always keep it off. Fortunately, oxygen during these free-diving jaunts is much less of an issue than in the original with the addition of oxygen producing flora conveniently scattered around the caves.There is a bigger focus on story this time around as well, with the protagonist speaking both to herself and others. While you're heavily incentivized to do your own exploring to push the story forward, you also rather quickly find a map you help you navigate. While it's only a PDA entry and not an automap feature, you'll still find yourself referencing it repeatedly.As many have said, it's not quite as good as the original, but that's more a testament to that game's greatness than anything else. Below Zero is still very good, and if you enjoyed the first one then you'll probably enjoy this one as well.

_childDocuments_.review: The original Subnautica was probably my favorite game of the last ten years, and that's from someone who typically hasn't much enjoyed other survival sims. The art, the progression, the FEAR, the story, the base building, the gear crafting, the exploration of the completely beautiful aquatic world, the FEAR, and oh did I mention the FEAR?  Like others have mentioned, I never knew what thalassophobia was until Subnautica showed me I had it.This sequel gave me tastes and thrills of the original, all over again. There are many QOL improvements I appreciated, and I suspect I would have loved Below Zero just as much as the original if I could have wiped the first one from my brain so it was all new again. As it is, I still love BZ, it just couldn't possibly surprise me as much, just by being the second game in the series.  My only quibble is that I didn't really enjoy the land-based biomes as much as I do the underwater portions.One more note: I think that my ideal game -- like, of all time -- might be a procedurally generated Subnautica. Something like a single-world No Man's Sky in a 4546B water world, making sure to keep the base building and FEAR alive. I don't even know if this would be possible, but I really really hope they're working on it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a step up in every technical way. It seems to run better, the visuals are crisper and the use of colour is stunning. Base building has been improved upon and there are many great QoL changes that makes playability significantly better than the original.The problem with this game comes from direction.It's much smaller than the original in every way, the world, the biomes, the caves, the creatures, the vehicles.Subnautica is best served as a small player in a large ocean, not a puddle and not dry land.I had a great time, in the first game, building my secondary base in the deep caves and yet there isn't really much point in building a single base outside of a single multipurpose room for upgrades and storage.The story is...fine, it's not great and I feel it's playing too hard into the comedy, especially with the silly charicatures in the corner of the screen, but it's not too offensive or off putting to ruin the experience. It's just, eh. The first game did it much better, less is more and all that.What's there is mostly good, but the scope for this game was too limited. I would love to see a third subnautica game, using everything they've learnt and the tools they've created but done properly with much more development time and budget to allow for a game of a much greater scale but the third game is very rarely the best in a series so I wouldn't have much hopeEither way, this is not worth the price

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game in itself, but intensely disappointing compared to the first. Some of it was inevitable, of course: we've already done this once, so it's harder to surprise us. But really, the game seems to promise much that it doesn't deliver on. There are some fascinating biomes, but mostly the world is repetitive and boring. There's almost no reason to visit most locations more than once. Without the intelligent threat posed by some of the creatures in the first game (and these new creatures are also AI stupid)  and the time limit implied by the plot, there's very little tension here. Once the mystery of what happened to your sister is resolved, and it's not much of a mystery, you're left wondering why there's still any game to wade through. The Architect part of the plot blows. The above-water segments are treated exactly the same as underwater segments through the use of heat-loss rather than oxygen-loss time limits, but it's still very little threat and they're a complete chore to hoof through. You are drowning in resources. You have a massive collection of vehicles and vehicle parts, most of which are little use and the rest of which remove any tension or need for movement planning, so I was vastly overprepared for all the situations I encountered. Subnautica caused terror, confusion, and sadness through judicious use of atmosphere, environment and set-pieces, but this game doesn't have many equivalent moments. Subnautica used the crushing drive for survival as plot, and office politics for brief moments of levity; Below Zero has office politics for plot and occasionally remembers being 600m underwater in an alien ocean might also be interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: Too much differed beyond what made Subnautica great. Lots of gameplay bugs still, lot of cut content (things like the backup camera for the janky Seatruck, or the stasis rifle), story is pretty weak (probably from completely overhauling the story 3/4ths of the way through development which only made it marginally better) and the voiced protagonist detracts rather than adds to the overall game quality.Fauna AI seems to have lost a lot of aggressiveness in the bigbois, never once did I feel threatened besides the Ghost Leviathans in the Crystal caverns. And then those were ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ due to constant locking on to you if they see you from 200 meters away, not moving, no lights, nothing to draw attention to you.The playable area without including the boring, buggy, and annoying gigantic land section, is really bland and small. Solid 1/3rd to 1/2 is just boring sparse generic arctic areas. Sea Monkeys tend to be all over the place too, due to the small underwater play area, greatly increasing their annoying presence.The overland section is entirely too large for how uninteresting it is. There just isn't really much of a reason to explore there, while constantly fighting either the Ice Worm, the terrain in a prawn, or the cold on foot. Requiring a special full suit just to not have to worry about the cold is also quite annoying. The Snowfox was pretty useless all things considered. Still deal with cold, but the terrain becomes even harder to deal with. The only real use for it would be dealing with the Ice Worm, but tbh the prawn does well enough with some buggy grapple-jumping at worst.I could go on for a bunch more but its honestly just not worth the effort. Just like this game isn't worth buying anywhere near full price. Might be worth 10, maybe could recommend it as just something to continue the subnautica feel a bit at 5.But overall, I'd say don't bother.Oh, and ♥♥♥♥ whoever decided to make the PDA voice so annoying and heavily accented. The original was great, no reason to change it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is better that the first Subnautica in some aspects, worse in others. Better in that you get more tech to play with and that there's new, more interesting environments to explore, worst in that the progression seems kind of... off. For example, in the whole game, there's only one Rebreather piece of tech. If you miss it, the rest of the game gets exponentially harder because you can't spend more than a few seconds outside when you go to depths below 100m. You also had more clues on where to find bases and alien facilities in the first game. In this one, the clues are very vague even when they give you a map. Then, there's the boring surface section where there's a weather event that forces you to seek shelter every 2 minutes. It is nuts!All in all, it is an okay game and if you liked the first Subnautica and want more of the same with some questionable design decisions, then get this.
