_childDocuments_.review: Subnautica: Below Zero is an epic adventure that will transport you to an icy and exotic world hidden beneath the ocean's surface. Developed by the awesome folks at Unknown Worlds Entertainment, this standalone expansion of the original Subnautica takes the excitement to the next level!Get ready to be blown away by the stunning graphics and immersive sound design that bring this world to life. With a gripping storyline that builds upon the original game and introduces new characters, plot twists, and exploration opportunities, you'll be hooked from the start! And the best part? The game's progression is perfectly balanced, so you'll never feel overwhelmed!But what really sets Subnautica: Below Zero apart is the amazing world-building. You'll dive into an immersive underwater ecosystem, encountering weird and wonderful creatures as you explore a variety of new biomes, like icebergs and frozen caves. And with a range of cool tools and vehicles at your disposal, you'll be able to navigate this mysterious world like a pro!The crafting system is also super impressive, allowing you to create all sorts of awesome tools, vehicles, and equipment using resources you gather from the environment. With so much to discover and explore, you'll never want to leave this captivating world!In a nutshell, Subnautica: Below Zero is an incredible survival game that takes the original to new heights. _childDocuments_.review: It´s not a bad game, not at all BUT it is just a downgraded Subnautica and smaller/less in quite every aspect. So, taking into account that the "original" huge Subnautica has the identical price tag (2022) than this "dlc-sized" game, I simply cannot give a thumb up.With "smaller/less" not (only) referring to the map which is much smaller (in area and depth) with less biomes - but also almost all other aspects of the game. Some examples:- While in Subnautica you could build a submarine (with sonar and stuff), place things inside - here you have just a "seatruck" with prebuild modules, lacking most of the features, noise-mechanics completely missing, no speed-steps, no sensors, no customization, nothing. - While in Subnautica I was really horrified by the Reapers, the Chelicerates are somehow much less terrifying, as other said, they are looking like huge shrimps. Overall the game feels much less frigthening and dramatic. The world is shallower, brighter, no huge endless caves (can be positive or negative).- While in Subnautice one felt really alone and desperate, stranded on an alien planet, trying to survive completely alone - here you fly to the planet on purpose, have allies to talk with, human bases everywhere. Overall, much less "dramatic".- Subnautica had two stories which where intertwined (the alien thing and the escape thing), while the alien-thing was not expected from the beginning but discovered - here, one story is just the centuries-old "search for your sister/brother/mother/child"-thing and the other one some sci-fi stuff without any connection to the first story.- While in Subnautica you were alone in the wide ocean (only two tiny islands), seeing over hours nothing but water - now about 1/3 of the (in comparison tiny) map is above sealevel, dry land (not sub nautica). That takes a lot of the desperation-feeling as you can just leave the ocean and take a walk whenever you want.Overall, its just a heavily downgraded and smaller version of Subnautica with less features. Would be a perfect DLC (maybe with option to travel between the "main"-word and the "arctic"-world), but in this form, its a major step backwards. Play Subnautica first and see this like a standalone-DLC of the main-game. Still reasonable but compared to Subnautica, really underwhelming.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: The game is good enough now.This rating is a temporary one until the extension gets out of Early Access. I LOVE the original SubNautica, but I don't like this extension. Some mechanics have been WORSE... but the team has really improved the game and story in the last month. The game is already worth the money as it is. The devs have shown that they care. As soon as they add SOME KIND OF map, I am going to change my review to positive.Positive:+ [FIX] They are working on fixing the story and took out the bad voice acting and story+ [FIX] They have added a new voice actor who is awesome, calm, professional and not acting like a schoolkid on a classtrip.+ [FIX] They deactivated the mini-bases that made your own base pointless+ [FIX] Bigger base room has been added additonally to the multipurpose room+ [FIX] They have made the route to the inside of the ice biome more visible by adding A LOT of really awesome-looking jellyfish.+[FIX] They made the resource grind a bit more enjoyable by adding a portable scanner. They also seem to have increased mineral density overall.+ [FIX] More unique animals and plants are added by the day and replace the older model bone sharks etc.+ Some new fish/plant designs+ Awesome new Leviathans (who actually hunt other animals)+ New setting+ New vehicles+ Better story integration (multiple npc characters, cutscenes, storytelling, humor (Al-An))+ Voiceacting+ More base parts+ CUSTOM PORTALS+ Jukebox?+ November updateNegative:- The new vehicles aren't better. If I hated anything about the first game then it was the damn waiting time with the "VRRRRR" in the background when you needed to get from point A to B with your relatively slow vehicles. Especially the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Cyclopse. Turn up the speed, please (or add a "boost mode"). The sea truck is not any better, it is even slower. - Still no mod-switching. If a vehicle has mods, there is still just a limited amount. It would be better if you could install 8, but only use 4 and switch between them from the outside if necessary). That inventory management is boring.- [FIX] Some of the animals are just copies from the first game with a few changes like the arctic peeper.- Same for some of the plants.- THERE IS STILL NO DAMN ACCESSIBLE MAP. You STILL have to rely on those scanning rooms that slow down the game and only give you a temporary perspective on a small part of the map. Please add a constant map plugin to the PDA that you can expand by building scan rooms or something. Sometimes you just don't find anything, because you lose orientation in the game. Beacons are not enough.- Scan rooms should be bigger so that you can see the information better. Would also be more visually impressive. You should also use more colours to make different depths of the ocean floor more visible (light green - dark green - yellow - red - violet - purple). It is just a big blue mesh mess at the moment. Add options to manipulate the map in direction and angle.- Make scanner room cameras return by themselves to charge.- [kinda fixed] THE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ RESOURCE GRIND! It is fun to poke at some rocks at the beginning, but it gets more awful over time when you have to build more mods, structures, EVERYTHING. You have to poke at hundreds of rocks and it is annoying, boring and frustrating. It would be way more fun if you would add filter plants to the game that you can find and collect in different depths or hidden caves that you can plant and which "filter" out some minerals from the water over time. It would be great to have some progression in the game from "Hunter & Gatherer" to "alien crop farmer". Maybe let certain plants only grow in certain depths?- Let us scan different types of sea grass ;)- [FIXED] make the multipurpose rooms bigger by default, please.- [FIXED] Why would you integrate ice biomes like that? I had to find a hidden tunnel under the ice to get there which took very long. - I still can't produce "better nutrition" items like food bars from plants or fish.- No laboratory: You still can scan everything in an instant. I would really enjoy to have a laboratory to research certain materials, eggs or animals for longer. Like putting them under a long-time scanner that gives you extensive information about the animal after some time instead of a short summary.- [FIXED] Bases have become useless, because there are bases everywhere now. And emergency mini bases. Great. Why don't you continue to wipe speedrunner's ass?- [FIXED] You can just leave the planet when you want, but want to stay? What the hell?- Alien ruins still look like empty art museums. Did they live there or...? Develope some lore, please.- What is the purpose of those land-areas? I thought Subnautica was about the ocean in the first place? Moving on land is very slow, boring and clunky to be honest. The snow fox bugs out everywhere at the moment.- [FIXED] PLEASE deactivate the story part for now. I accidentally start to trigger major spoilers and events in the story ("its a secret...") without wanting to. It would make way more sense to activate the triggers when the world is finished in terms of design.- [FIXED] Character is very annoying and talking ♥♥♥♥ with her sister (Subnautica character was silent). I don't like the voice actor either, because she doesn't fit the setting. She is like: "Oh, hey it is -40° Celsius under water, I am basically out of food, get hunted by giant sharks and squids (or both) and I think this is hilarious AHAHAHAHAHAHA - I WANNA STAAAAAAAAAAAAY!!!"Jesus. Why. Get a grip.- No audio wiki entries. It would be great if you wouldn't have to read all the entries. I love them, but it would be great if you could listen to them on the go. Let a dude read them out in English and add the vocal version to the PDA. If you can scan something, just give us an optional button to press ("press O to listen to the new wiki entry") so that we can keep swimming and listen to the beautiful, beautiful details of the world and creatures you built in subnautica without disrupting the game flow.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I'm a bit disappointed with this sequel. The original story to this game was great; it has a reason for other people not to be down there (a meteor storm), it had an eye catching story, and I wish we could've seen it. This new story is just... lackluster. We have no reason why Alterra abandoned the planet, and the Sam story line is just lame. The first part of the game had us wondering why she really died, and if there was more to the story, only to learn that she just... died from her own mistakes. Everything is so much more confusing, too. I had to look stuff up on the Wiki to find things, despite getting all PDA's and story elements, including Sam's Kharrar cure that wasn't explained whatsoever, and it didn't even explain why I needed it. Definitely disappointing for a game I spent $30 on. Original Subnautica had a fantastic story and took much longer to complete, and it was just satisfying. This new game was meh, but the new story vs the original is just ten times worse. I loved the first game, and it hurts me to say this.

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't finished yet and had a more story driven narrative as opposed to very little story drive in Subnautica. Im not sure if I like it more or less though. I know they want to make an exploration game and the terror stuff is secondary but they shouldn't discount creating a world where you are never quite sure what will happen. One thing that would help this game is if there were roving bands of creatures that "randomly" swam through the shallows and attack the player and or the base. Otherwise Subnautica fans are going to love this game when it is done.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved everything about the first game, and I will say the second holds up. My only issue with the game is i feel that some of the out of water experiences weren't that strong. It didn't seem to have as much story around it and only a little discovery other then a couple bases and a lot of tunnels. The glaciers all around are cool but its hard to tell if its a unique glacier with anything on it or just some random glacier. The seatruck not sitting high on the water makes that an issue. But with these small issues the game is still really awesome. Great story, very varied biomes and discoverables, and awesome base building and vehicles.
